I was astounded at the size of the conference spaces, which span three levels and includes a Starbucks. However, the layout is not super intuitive and even with a map, I had to ask for directions. For example, the first floor of the conference space is not accessible via the first floor hotel lobby; you have to go up to second floor, over and down on an escalator.

It is well-equipped to host large meetings and conferences. However, the Starbucks could use some speedier staff to keep the line moving...

There aren't very many dining options within quick walking distance of the JW (particularly for breakfast) but High Velocity on the first floor is okay; I've heard better things about Osteria Pronto. 

*Note that parking costs an arm and a leg - it's about $40 for a full day in the JW garage, but that's the same as the White River garage across the street. Pick your poison, I suppose.

Burgers are varied and interesting, boozy shakes are delicious! Atmosphere is comfortable and fun, with servers to match. On occasion my medium rare comes to the table medium, but otherwise I've always had good experiences here. Fried pickles are yummy too!

Very personable staff!!! Nikki is a wonderful asset to the restaurant!! Excellent food!! We thought we were going in for just coffee and left with our bellies pleasantly full:) and a to go box!!! C u next year.....

Cool ambiance, great food! Definitely order the Yakitori, we had chicken thigh, very tender and moist. The duck fried rice was yummy too.  The Japanese beer, Orion, was really good too, never had it before but good drinking beer.

Steak and shrimp is greatly delicious, big size, and thick. The sides are a pretty big size too. That's why the prices aren't marked on their daily-changed menus. Just for the 2 of us was $70. I went with a Groupon though. Nice scene
I love that this place is close to work and they have a drive through.  The service has been nice, to me.  Sometimes it can be busy, but what do you expect on McCarran?

If you read the reviews of Hickory Hollow Mall from oldest to latest, you'll see its staggering decline. I went here recently for the arcade, and it's really the only thing left worth visiting. Seriously, about 1/3 or more of the mall is closed and the stores left have the vaguest names you'd probably think I made up on the spot - Today's Fashions, Streetville, etc. I can't recommend this place unless you're already in the Antioch area and want to walk around for its defunct bizareness.

Love the concept...and apparently so does half the city. Long lines, competing music, and general chaos rule here. Bring cash and a crap load of patience and maybe you can find the few diamonds in the rough.

Came here with my husband one night after he could not stop raving about the food here. Had kabobs, mango chicken, and something else. Excellent excellent! Price was beyond reasonable, esp for the food that was so delicious. Place is BYOB which we did not know before we went but that's even more of a reason to go back again. Definitely recommend if you are in a mood for some good Kabob!!

The place looked interesting enough, the live music was pleasant enough, the food and drink were over priced and marginal at best, but the coupe de grace was delivered when I received the check. I had asked for an additional portion of herbed mayonaise that accompanied my Cuban sandwich, upon examination of the check, I found a $1 charge for a table spoon of mayo. Unbeliebvable. I said something to the manager who did nothing but say "that's how it is."
Don't be lured by the interesting exterior......this place is not worth your time or money and the management is completely tone deaf on customer perception of value; $8 for a 10oz glass of common IPA, $18 for lack luster fish tacos plus mayo for $1. There are much better options in that town or accross the river.

Camille has been cutting my hair for awhile now and she always does an amazing job! She listens to what you want, and is very talented... I have a fairly specific look (stacked in the back, extreme angle, side bangs) and she always does it perfectly.  In fact, now both of my roommates are going to her as well!  Plus, it's a great value.  Ask for Camille when you go in!

LOVE Schlafly! It was always a must-do when I came to visit my boy's fam, and now that I've moved here (from first Milwaukee, then Chicago), I am grateful to have such a wonderful place to go get good beer! It's really nice in the summer, as they have live music and a nice patio area. They also have a farmer's market here in the summer, supplying the area with fresh, local produce! They also make note of where your meal came from, which is always cool to see - because for most things, it's out of the midwest - go local! 

I like all their beers, but my two faves are the Coffee Stout and the Raspberry Heffe. Definitely staples in the appropriate season. You can easily sample a bunch of their beers if you go for a tour, I think between my boyfriend and I we tried them all and then some! (We also made good with the bartender, who was cool giving us a few extra - hah!) If tours bore you, they are also more than willing to give you a free taste of whatever you'd like to try up at the bar to help you decide.

If you're looking for a laid back place to go get some good food and excellent beer, definitely give Schlafly a try.

Great nail salon!  My boss was in town and wanted to get a manicure/pedicure with me. I work by Valley Forge but live in NJ, so I went to Yelp for assistance finding a good nail salon. She said it was the best manicure/pedicure she's had in years. They are very professional and courteous. It was a great experience!

Beer and pizza, done right.

BEER
I was already a fan of this place before stepping foot inside because they post their upcoming specialty kegs on twitter (http://twitter.com/thegoodpiestl). What an awesome idea from a group of people who clearly love what they do. Great ever-changing beer selection

PIZZA
Delicious Napoletana-style pizzas with fresh ingredients. "The Good Pie" is the classic margherita, and the chefs even use the correct type of cheese: buffalo mozzarella. Great attention to detail- if you like this style of pizza (who wouldn't?), you can't miss this place.
Got a small Kilauea this time. It's sooo good! Nice decent amount of BBQ sauce, onions, chicken, pineapple and some bacon crumbles. Yum!

Consistently decent customer service.  I've seen it get rowdy in there with the Penn crowd and staff handles themselves with finesse. 

As always, great ice cream.

hotel was good, pillows were kinda small, beds were comfy, shower had body wash, shampoo and conditioner dispensers, flat screen tv. cleanliness was 4.5 out of 5 (found a empty cup next to one of my beds). front desk lady was very helpful with checking us in and answering all of our questions even when it was 1AM in the morning. self parking was 12 a day and they have shuttle services every 20 mins for guest to the airport.

I ate here 2 years ago for breakfast based off the suggestion from a local. I ordered a Bloody Mary and omelette. The omelette was stuffed full of hair. I'm talking pube sandwich. I'm only writing this review now because I have a friend visiting soon and I had to search this place out to ensure he didn't go! Worst food experience (nightmare) I've ever had.
Doesn't taste anything like it used to the meat taste awful he fries are less thick and taste like cardboard really was the best fast food burger 17 years ago

As a vegetarian who prefers to eat gluten-free, I know I'm not the easiest customer for a restaurant to please. Still, this place has a little room for improvement, so I thought I'd mention my experiences here.

Not wanting to eat meat, fish, or gluten, I made a meal out of half an app and a small entree. My food was tasty: the grilled avocado app was very good, though it definitely needed a light sprinkle of salt, and there was none on the table. Our server disappeared for such long stretches of time that I didn't want to wait and just ate it sans salt. My small (read: very small) salad entree was listed as beets, arugula, cheese, and almonds. I got an unexpected upgrade to pine nuts instead of almonds. I'm not complaining, but it would have been nice to be notified of changes to the dish I was ordering. 

A word of advice to gluten-free customers: After ordering I later learned that there was a risotto dish under the "pasta" section of the menu. Since I avoid most gluten, I didn't even look at the pasta. Strange that they would put a risotto dish there. Also, the dessert menu has many (three I think?) gluten-free options including a gluten-free brownie sundae. It clearly mentions gluten-free on the dessert menu. However their main menu never once mentions gluten-free options or uses GF icons or anything. 

My boyfriend's trout meal was disappointing. It was served skin side up (a bit unusual?) and said it came with potatoes and a pea puree. His peas were whole, not pureed, and the potatoes were nearly raw. Not just al dente. Basically just off-raw.

The server was very sweet, but not quite as present as he could have been, as our water glasses went unfilled for long stretches.
Really good sandwiches.  The sides are way to expensive for the amount you get. But the sandwiches are priced well and taste great!  The staff is very nice and professional.

Incredible donuts and fresh, well cooked sliders. The bar appearance is deceiving... no alcohol unless you bring it (get it next door at Steins and use the chiller at District). Haven't tried the coffee yet but it looks great! The slider features are continuously rotating and are creative. Great atmosphere and a compliment to the area of Magazine Street. Had the cheeseburger sliders, duck slider and BLT with 1/2 inch thick bacon. Yum!

#chifoodie #NOLAtourism #foodtourism #blackownedbusiness #blackbiz Highest rating.  Eating at this cafe in the middle of the flea market was the most pleasant surprise of our trip.  We had a Thanksgiving breakfast.  We sat at the counter-- 5 of us including 2 kids.  The staff was loving, called everybody darlin'.  I ordered vegetarian red beans and rice and cornbread.  My cousin had the greens.  Becuase she was sitting next two me I had both.  Delicious does not describe this place.  It felt like each plate was made with love.  The red beans and rice were simple and flavorful.  The counter offers a variety of hot sauces to chose from.  I chose the Chipotle with was a perfect paring.  The greens were tender, but not mushy filled garlic and spices.  The cornbread was my dessert.  It was a big hunk, soft and not too sweet.  Afterwards we shopped in the spice emporium and came away with the chipotle and the scotch bonnet hot sauces.  Our only regret of our trip is not returning to this place.  Highly, highly recommend.

Great establishment. Travel a lot and have visited multiple BL locations and this is by far the best. Always great service and food is always brought timely and as requested. Bartenders are very professional, friendly and always smiling. Props goes out to Brandy who always does a great job behind the bar.

I LOVE MY HAIRCUT!!!!  For years I have gone to hairdressers who although they do a great job, I never feel get exactly what I'm saying.  I'm in an artistic feild and always lean towards a less conservative haircut, but I feel like no one ever does this for me until today.. Jenny just cut my hair and it looks so awesome.  She flat ironed it which i love the way it looks!
I brought in a picture and she suggested i leave more of my length, which was such a good call.  
I love my haircut!!  Jenny is a rock star.

We are regulars. Its one of our places for sushi rolls. Very clean place. I think they need to change up the menu a little more often. I personally dont care for much of the hot foods. Just dont like the sauce. Soups are GREAT. I would tell you to go.

Deep Sea is the choicest place to end up after a wine-soaked afternoon in the Funk Zone. It is the only tasting room on the wharf and the view is unbeatable. Perched on the pier overlooking the marina, it is a great place to enjoy a bottle of wine whilst surveying the ocean for marine life and enjoying the briny ocean breeze. There is indoor and outdoor seating.

They do offer tastings, but you get more bang for your buck if you just purchase a bottle. Be sure to ask to sample the wine before you buy a bottle. The servers are happy to oblige. Bottles are priced handsomely and one can enjoy a fine white for under $20. I would recommend the grenache.

I love Thai food, and this place does not disappoint. Their lunch special is ridiculously awesome: $10 for soup, an appetizer (or, if you are soup averse like my husband, two appetizers) and an entree that is only slightly smaller than the regular entree. I, two opted for two apps and no soup, and the fresh spring rolls and dumplings were yummy. My husband's tofu satay was also good and came with some delicious sauce. The place is a bit small, but the food is great and the price is right.

This review is specific to the Mother's Day Brunch.  

We always enjoyed this restaurant previously.  The food is always great & was very good on this occasion. 

However, we were really disappointed with the Mother's Day Brunch.  I understand brunch isn't usually part of your offerings, but to not have a kids' menu at 10:15am on Mother's Day (aside from the lunch/dinner) was a huge miss for us. 

I am sure this is a very busy day but instead of enjoying a leisurely brunch we were in & out in less than 40 minutes.  Our bread had barely cooled off before we were served our entrees.  Well, almost all the entrees. My food showed up about five minutes after everyone else's. 

When you are heading out for a special day & open to spending a bit more than usual for a Sunday brunch, I guess I just expected a bit more effort.

Mediocre bbq and service. Lukewarm food. The way they bring food out is like this: one person gets their plate, another person gets their plate in about 10 min, and the third person gets theirs in about 5 min after that. Portions of the actual meat are pretty small. Bbq sauce is given if requested but they don't volunteer it. It is given in a small plate so you have a limit.

1st visit. New to Springfield/Greenbrier area. Tried the brisket sandwich, small sandwich Is 3 oz sliced meat cut fresh when ordered. Served on a bun. Was very tender and well flavored with smoke. Side chosen was baked sweet potato. Comes with cinnamon sugar butter. Was a real "baked" potato, not steamed! Probably cooked with the brisket judging from the crisp skin. Overall pretty good eats. I'll be back! They also serve pork and chicken with several sides to choose from. Closed Monday and Tuesday.

I went in to try on and order a bridesmaid dress a few months ago, and was told to come back a month before when I need it for alterations. I have 6 weeks before my friend's wedding in another state, so I figured I would go in and have it taken care of. All was fine until I went in to get it adjusted.

I made an appointment a few days prior, and when I arrived, I got a "Well, you're not listed on here, but that's okay, we have time." Way to make me sound like an inconvenience; I could tell this was going to be an awesome experience.  After lecturing me on making sure I had shoes on because they "drastically change your posture" I told the woman I would be taking care of the hemming myself once I decided on a 2.5 inch heel or a 3 inch heel and it wouldn't be enough of a difference to affect the bodice section. After getting into the dress and walking out, I made a comment about having to buy 2 sizes bigger for it to fit my butt (bottom heavy), so I needed to have a bit over 3 inches taken out of the top. One of the employees decided to make a fantastic remark - "You either have to pay to have the dress altered or pay to have surgery." Excuse me? When is that ever appropriate? I kind of like my ass, and I can't really do a whole lot about it. The Puerto Rican side of my genes leaves me with more butt than I know what to do with. But back to my complaint.

I decided to go through with having it pinned and getting the tally to have the proper bust alterations. $195. Pre-tax. Not including hemming (which would have been a minimum of $30 as per the chart in the dressing room). That also included a "rush fee" because I didn't want to wait until the day I get on a plane to go to a wedding out of state (Who does that? What if there's a colossal f-up?). Apparently wanting it done in anything less than 5 weeks is considered a rush job, even though the sales associate said I should come back a month before I needed it (remember, I gave myself 6 weeks just to be safe). I paid around $180 for the dress to begin with. I told her it was ridiculous and I wanted my dress back. Sorry. Paying $400 by the time it's all said and done for a bridesmaid dress made out of polyester? I'll pass. And I'll pass on piss-poor customer service too. Those women need a trip back to training and I would personally classify it as firing material if I was their boss.

So yeah, avoid alterations there like the plague. I took someone's recommendation to check out the Burlington Coat Factory's tailor/alterations woman (Bernadette) just a little bit up the road from this location. She was appalled at what I told her and wrote up the same alterations PLUS the hemming for a little over $100. So yeah, it's obvious where my business went to.

This place is the definition of hidden gem! Don't be put off by its location inside a hotel - this was some of the best BBQ I've eaten. Plump, juicy smoked chicken. Killer, lean but tender coffee rubbed brisket. Perfect pulled pork. Each platter is only around $11 and comes with hush puppies AND three sides. The kids meal would be a healthy portion for a grown up - we got the pulled pork (came on a bun) with sweet potato fries and our toddler loved it. The four BBQ sauces on the table are distinct and awesome. And the beer list! Incredible craft beers at just $4 a pint. Coming from NYC that is an amazing bargain. Dinner for three people with two beers was only $40. So worth it. Julie, the waitress, is friendly and instantly learns everyone's names. We learned they have smokers in the back and everything is cooked on site. So happy to have found this place!!

My GF and I went up to Santa Barbara for a vacation and some wine tasting.  I found the Santa Barbara Adventure Company online and booked the Cupcake and Wine tour because my GF really likes cupcakes.

We had never been to Santa Barbara before, and the SB Adventure Company tour was great.  They picked us up at our hotel promptly and we drove around to get 2 more couples.  The driver, Adam, took us to the Santa Ynez valley and 3 different wineries.  Adam took care of all of the arrangements once we arrived, and after the second tasting we had a delicious lunch.  

The cupcake tasting was actually paired with the third wine tasting.  While I enjoyed the cupcakes, it was a little hard to focus on both the cupcakes and the wine (as the previous tastings were have some accumulated effects).  That being said, I would definitely recommend this tour and getting some extra cupcakes for the drive home.
Best theater in town. Love the seats and love that I can put extra butter on my popcorn.
Our waitress Erika was fantastic! Very helpful, on top of everything and always smiling.

The girl in the drive thru had an attitude with me when I asked about the puppy cup. She wasn't friendly at all. When I got the puppy cup it had one dollop of whip cream.... so then I ask if I could have some more and she barely gives me anything and says sure..like that's not cool. If it's such a problem and hassle I'll pay, that's not the issue. I go to this Starbucks all the time. I don't know what her issue is but she needs to fix it

Got a groupon for the lady Jane package for me and my mom to go. It came with a soup and salad, the soup was so watered down and had no flavor. And the salad was about 3 pieces of baby spinach and about 2 grape tomatoes and came with an apple vinaigrette. They didn't let you pick your own dressing. It also came with a tower of sandwiches and 2 scones for each person, out of about 6 different sandwiches on the platter there were only about 2 that were edible. The rest were absolutely horrible. The tea was good and the scones were alright. But that's all I could ever see anyone going there for. If you are planning on a meal I would eat somewhere before and just go for tea and scones. Was not pleased with what they had to offer. I am very happy I just had a groupon and did not pay the full price for this. I would have been very disappointed and tried to ask for money back because it was just very horrible. I would not recommend it to anyone unless they just wanted to have tea. I would not get anything else from there.

My car was hit while it was parked in a parking lot. I brought it in to Philadelphia Auto Body and the whole process was seamless as they worked with my insurance company. At the end, they figured out a cheaper way to fix my car and gave me a refund off of what my insurance company paid them. They also detailed my car and fixed a few other scratches that had been caused previously without charging me. Overall, I had a great experience and would highly recommend this shop to anyone who needs body work.
Service is awesome friendly knowledgable, selection of hats range from the best to the more best lol. Cost is just about right

Service was not that great.  Slow to fill drinks.  One meal in our party came out after some of us were done eating.  Apology was give and we were told it was delivered to another table. Probably should have been comped.  Water taste like baking soda.  Food mediocre.  Decor and atmosphere was excellent.

We just moved to the area and after meeting someone who quickly recognized my son's love of trains she recommended that we pay a visit to the Frisco Train Store.  We spent two full hours at the store where both my son (4) and daughter (14 months) enjoyed playing at the train tables, especially the large multilevel one in the middle of the store. The place opened at 10 and quickly filled with children and parents. By noon it was starting to quiet down, but a few more families were coming in as we were leaving. The store has a charming atmosphere and provided great fun for young train enthusiasts.  For parents there are plenty of places to sit, free Wi-Fi and snacks and coffee to purchase.  There is a sign upon entering with a polite request for a donation, which I did feel was appropriate as the place offers a wonderful indoor play space on a hot or rainy day.
Great luncheon buffet, lots of veggies and salads..

My wife and I had dinner at Uncle Maddio's tonight, and I had them make me a pesto chicken pizza, with pesto as the base sauce, mozzarella, chicken, and then a pesto drizzle and fresh basil to finish it off. It was honestly one of the best pizzas I've ever had. The fact that they have beer and wine is just another plus for them, we will be having friends in town in a month and we'll definitely be bringing them by!
Out of lager and serving Jagerschnitzel that was way too salty and covered in salad dressing. This is German food? Nein Danke. Portions are appropriate for a German stomach.

Very mediocre. Service was disappointing, the food is nothing special and the place was pretty dirty. We tried this place as one of our first dinners out after moving to Tampa and will unfortunately not being going back anytime soon.

My best restaurant experience in Tucson by far.  I haven't dined for dinner in a  while and just got on Yelp, but after I had seen some of the awful reviews, I had to do Maynards justice. 

I went for dinner a couple months ago, before a show.  We had a reservation and were seated promptly.   We started off the meal with a few cocktails, the Martini Caprese and the  Tarte Aux Pommes.  The Tarte Aux Pommes was a little sweet for my taste, but these cocktails were outstanding.  

Our server was friendly and attentive, and he really new his stuff.  We had all his recommendations.  Our first course consisted of the mussels in the classic white wine broth, house frites (AMAZING) and the charcuterie: three pieces of toast, one with mortadella shmear, one with anchovies, and one with duck rillettes.  The duck charcuterie was my favorite but all were the perfect start to the meal.

For the main course, I had the filet with brussels and bacon.  The filet was cooked to perfection, and as for the brussel sprouts - I guess it's true that everythings better with bacon! My guests had the bouillabaise - fresh seafood in a delicious broth (my favorite) - and the fresh fish of the evening.  No complaints.  We completely cleaned all of our plates.  We had moved on to wine for our entrees, and went by our server's recommendations, which were impeccable but I have unfortunately forgotten which wines by now.

Though we were fairly full, I am never one to pass on dessert, so we shared the chaud froid and the lemon tart. The chaud froid was a selection of cheesecake, biscotti, fruit, and other goodies to dip in a very rich semi sweet chocolate fondue of sorts.  Amazing for anybody thats a chocolate lover! The lemon tart was perfectin.  (and the lemon tart dipped in the chocolate fondue was good too :)  ).  One guest finished with a digestif and one a glass of sparkling wine, we had a fabulous evening and definitely enjoyed our show!

Maynards is what good restaurants should all strive to be.  I've been back to the bar several times since my divine meal, and the menu has changed several times.  But definitely give this place a chance!  I promise you will not be disappointed.

The restaurant was very cute. The staff was friendly and helpful. The food that we had was good. Nothing overly special, but solid. We were perhaps disappointed because we had heard it was great.

Drinks were made with fresh ingredients and were very good.

Excellent seafood! The fried catfish was like being at someone's house for a fish fry and the stuffed crab had lots of crab meat. The boiled shrimp was the best I've ever had (really large shrimp with lots of seasoning. The place has been there since forever and is a very relaxed atmosphere. Love it!

I know there's that other Greek Festival every May out in Des Peres, but this remains my favorite Greek Festival in the city. 

Every Labor Day weekend, St. Nicholas opens up its doors, and Barnes opens up one of their garages, and the entire area around Kingshighway and Forest Park is inundated with all things Greek.  

The food is AMAZING and you can fill up for under $10 easily.  Buy a bottle of wine or a few Greek beers, sit back and enjoy the music.  The pastries are the best.  I could eat my weight in this baklava.  Quite frankly, as much as I love Olympia, I can't help but admit, this Greek food is better and the atmosphere certainly cannot be beat. 

This festival runs for the entire Labor Day weekend, and is filled with dancing, music, (as I said and couldn't shut up about before) amazing food, and plenty of OOOOPAAAAAAAs.  You can also buy plenty of items at the Flea Market of Athens such as T-shirts, olive oil, and other Greek goodies.  Certainly something to put on your calendar next Labor Day weekend.

As a poor college student, what is more attractive than 1.50 tacos just a mile away? I came in at around 11 am on a Saturday and the place was already starting to fill up. They have fun decorations and place is incredibly clean.

I had the carne asada tacos and asada caramelo. I would only recommend the carmelo if you're a huge fan of plain quesadillas - not much flavor in them even with the meat, but lots of gooey melty cheese between toasty tortilla if you are into that (I know some of you do). The caramelo was ok, but the big winner for me was the carne asada tacos. Although the carne asada comes out looking more like hamburger helper meat rather than freshly chopped chunks of steak, it was pretty darn delicious. Topped with the unlimited salsa verde, fresh cilantro and limes,  fresh guac and pico de gallo, I'm pretty much all set.

Although it's not the best ever I've ever had, it's pretty darn good, cheap, spotlessly clean, and close to campus. Delicious $1.50 well spent!
The Residence Inn was pretty much what I expected. The rooms are spacious & clean, there is a good selection of chairs & couches to spread out on, and the bed was comfy.

I was really iffy about coming here in the beginning... I just wasn't sure... but there hummus appetizer is really good 

I don't really think I had a great meal but overall the experience was a lot of fun I came here for reunion with two of my friends from college and we were able to sit and drink in and just have a blast in and have good service which is something that I really look for!

I tried Dream Tea House for the first time last night when practically dying of thirst at West Edmonton Mall, and can't wait to visit again. I ordered 'Smile,' a strawberry-rose slush with lychee jelly, and found it perfectly sweet and flowery, with tons of lychee floating around the bottom of the cup. My boyfriend, who's been wishing for watermelon juice all summer long, had his dreams come true with a fresh watermelon juice, avec plenty of tapioca, on special that day. Our drinks both came in at under $5, good value considering the size.

The definition of a 5 star restaurant.  (I know I grade easy, but if I was a food critic from the New York Times, I would still call this place 5 star).  It's not cheap so bring your money, but the food is WORTH it.  Oh and also, there's an in-house ghost.  Yeah that's right, dinner and a ghost.

I'm sort of disappointed in the flowers we purchased for our Mom. She absolutely loved them & in the end that's all that matters. However, I feel like an $85 bouquet of flowers should look more like the picture on the website & include less fill in the arrangement. There really shouldn't be a good side, all sides should look great when spending good money on flowers. I will consider using Mayfield next time we send flowers, but they only get one more shot to prove they're the best in town.

First off, I am not a tourist to New Orleans so when I make a reservation I expect to not be rushed through my meal when the restaurant is 1/2 empty and I know they aren't waiting to turn over the table to another customer. Second, I was appalled when the singing trio came to our table and placed thier carafe to put tips into right in front of me. Most restaurants have the entertainment located in one area and people can go up and request them to come to their table personally to entertain with a song or two and they can pay them. I understand the restaurant may have thought it was a nice touch to have them go table to table but lose the jar.  If people enjoy it and want to tip them, they will. I felt like a fool after they had come to my table because my guest and I only had credit cards, do they take that? No, and they looked at us like we had 10 heads when we didn't reach down into our purses to hand them cash. Third, my guests dinner was great, mine not so much. I had fish that tasted like it would have been excellent if it wasn't drowned in salt and spices. I am used to the New Orleans spices but this was too much. I wish I  had just ordered another Crabmeat Broussards appetizer (which was delicious) and a side. Last but not least, we had the profitterols for desert. They were very good and highly recommended by our server. But then as we were eating it, my guest realized that she was chewing on a wrapper. Mine did not have a wrapper underneath it so we assumed they weren't supposed to have them and we brought it to our servers attention and just got a 'sorry' from him. After the experience I had, I don't think I will be going back there any time soon, maybe just for drinks on the patio.

I came here with a group of six friends excited to try something new. We were not very excited about it by the time we got done with our meal. To start off, the lighting at our table made it very hard to see the menu and our food. Once we ordered, the good came quickly which was great. However, the waitress told us the appetizers were family style which to mean means bigger than usual portions that you can share. This was not the case. The portions of the appetizers were just enough to get a small taste. Unless you are a mouse, it will not be enough food. By the time we ordered our food, it was after 9:00, aka "late night", which means the portion sizes are smaller. The waiters failed to tell us this before we ordered. I ordered the gnocchi for my main meal. While it was tasty, it was not worth the price. The meals did not come with any sides and if you did want sides they were about $10.00. All-in-all the food tasted good but was overpriced for what you get.

After reading the reviews, we had high expectations.  We arrived at 5pm on Saturday evening to a packed brewery.   We were told the wait was an hour.  There were tables in the bar and we waited until we were able to snag one. Unfortunately, the bar menu is not the same as the dining menu.  We ordered chips and stuff to munch on while we waited.   The chips, guacamole, and puréed bean salsa were actually the highlight of our meal.   I ordered a beer.  Beware, there are no traditional beers here.  They only sell what is made in the brewery.   They also do not sell soda.  My kids had ice tea which was extremely bitter.  Too bad the bartender has not mentioned this to me.   
The real disappointment was the fish tacos.  As previous people have stated, Where Is The Fish????  I felt like I was eating nothing but breading.   At $12 for two tacos, I expect more then fried batter.   I also expect red cabbage cole slaw on a fish taco.  Our waitress was nice and so was the host. Not a place I would ever eat at again.   I am actually surprised at the high ratings.   My daughter and her friend had the hummus appetizer which they said was pretty good.

Couldn't resist a ice cream cone shaped building...Treat yourself with a Twistee Treat You can't miss the building...the fiberglass cone building brings immediate recognition and awareness. It's as if your craving for ice cream came to life. The hardest part is trying to decide which yummy soft serve flavour you are going to get. The ice cream was delicious and the staff friendly and efficient. It takes a little while for each order to be made but its perfect on a hot sunny day. Its rich smooth flavors take you back to a simpler time. The menu indulges in ice cream, cones, cups and shakes. The banana splits are the best in the land. Twistee Treat also offers Malts, Shakes, Sundaes, and Slushes! The lines can be long and bring your own wet wipes because it can get messy...the ice cream is thick and creamy...Twistee Treat ice cream makes you smile.

Got take out yesterday and it was hands down the best I've had since moving to Apollo Beach. 
The Greek salad was on point and so was the mixed grill combo, would definitely recommend Pita Kabob

I just waited twenty minutes on an empty bed and had to leave because I had another appointment.  The bed was vacant but not clean.  One of the attendants cleaned it and then went  back to the register to wait on someone else.  This location is very well-maintained  and  the people working there are nice, but waiting for such a long time when they're only somewhat busy is annoying. I have a premium package that I would like to use.  I understand that I should expect a wait, but this was excessive. I waited a while last time too.  I'm not sure what the point of online check-in is or whether I will continue to visit this location/maintain my membership.

What a shame, they tend to make little mistakes here, but the food is so good. I really didn't like how the manager(?) treated the woman helping me like she was stupid. Small mistake, I ordered dark meat and they gave me mixed. They were out of thighs, she was tying to be creative and fix it, like give me back my order and give me 2 extra legs to make up for it, which I was fine with so I wouldn't have to wait 8 minutes for fast food. We were having a conversation and he just took the 8 piece box of chicken and threw it in the trash, saying the boss was watching him on the camera and he "can't give food away". But the real problem was how he didn't even talk to her or me, assumed the worst, and the proceeded to talk about it to another person as if me and the worker weren't listening to every word. That was rude and I felt really bad for her, she shouldn't be treated like that in front of customers, and I should be spoken to, not at. If you can't trust your employees to make your customers happy or fix their mistakes, then why would I want to come back?

Great customer service and super work. Came out on a Saturday to repair a broken hot water heater. Very honest and a pleasure to do business with. Will definitely use them as my plumber going forward. Highly recommended them for you plumbing needs.

I was in the mood for pizza, so I stopped in  at Mod Pizza, in Oro Valley, Az. and ordered a pizza for takeout. Wow the service was great from placing my order to the finish product. It was a great pizza for the money, Thanks to the entire staff, Great Job!

This place is adorable. The decor is "rustic modern" and incredibly cozy. There's a nice outdoor seating area. The bathrooms are clean. I got a Yerba Mate green tea and my hubby got a cappuccino. Both were delightful. We will definitely be back.
Great flavor! I sincerely enjoyed my chicken souvlaki! The baklava was the best too!!
Great food, love all their options! Just don't expect a quick in-and-out during lunchtime rush. This location is particularly busy around noon.

My boyfriend and I went to KUCHI because we were really were craving sushi. I got the KUCHI roll and it was delicious and really fresh. At the end of the meal they gave us free Saki and ice cream for dessert. The food is really fresh and the atmosphere is really relaxed. Recommend!

This place is relatively smaller than other pho places in Santa Barbara. The food in general is tasty although I think they probably include MSG in it. I love their beef sandwich and the chicken one too. However, their boba is slightly pricy.
I love the ice cream here. Great place to get some ice cream and just relax. They play music that's cool too

Yassss! I knew that whenever I got the chance to head over to NOLA I would have to make a pit stop here. After watching Justin Duncan (the owner) on Big Brother Over the Top, I was curious to try out his restaurant. 

My family and I stopped by J's Seafood for lunch today and we absolutely loved everything we got. I got the Fried Crawfish tails and practically inhaled them because they were so good. My sister got the Crawfish Beignets and said they were very tasty. My mother got a shrimp boat, and could not stop praising how much she enjoyed the fried shrimp. We are from South Florida, but she told me that these were the best fried shrimp she had ever eaten. My Aunt got the Shrimp and grits that were also very good. 

The only negative thing I will say is that the time for the food coming out was a bit sporadic. There was probably a ten to fifteen-minute interval for each of our items coming out. This is a great place to stop by for lunch and I would recommend it to anybody heading into French Market.

This place is great, I will be back without question. 1/2 & 1/2 Alligator was better than I expected. Seafood platter included oysters, catfish, shrimp and stuffed crab and 2 sides. The entire staff was friendly and extremely attentive.

This is a wonderful pizza place and is true to its roots. Great restaurant to stop in before a concert or Lightning game. Only complaint is that the service is lacking. Waited nearly two hours to get our meal after they realized they screwed up a calzone.

BOISE, ID:  I like this Hampton almost as well as the Hilton Garden Inn across the street.  It is mostly updated, clean and spacious, the rooms are nice and it is right off the freeway.  I like the location in walking distance to the movie theater and several restaurants; you don't even have to leave the parking lot to get there.  Book early; they fill up fast.

This Meijer has a very nice atmosphere and it's huge. I've had a very good experience with staff members throughout various parts of the store- from the Starbucks, to the Deli as well as the cashiers.  Everyone always greets with a smile and a warm welcome.  This Meijer is also open 24/7 which is convenient.  If I need to do some work on my laptop, I can go to the Starbucks section and not have to worry about it closing.  No one has ever disturbed me either.
I've tried their freshly made sushi and it has never disappointed. I have also tried their pizza chicken, salads, mashed potatoes, mac n cheese and literally always came back every week for more. 
The only thing I wish this Meijer had was more of a variety of fruits like some other Meijers I've been to.
Other than that, I highly recommend shopping at this Meijer!

Silver Peak is my go to. Unlike other restaurants/bars in the area, Silver Peak keeps their kitchen open until they close. I love their happy hour nachos but my favorite is the salmon fish and chips, you will not disappointed. I usually have great service but every now and then they get a new server or they have one bartender that ignores everyone else when he's having a conversation with a customer. For the most part the staff is great and when it's slow will take a genuine interest in chatting with customers.

They have a great beer selection and are always mixing it up. The pub menu is fitting and it's great for large groups and parties as they have a back rooms 

Bring your garage ticket with you because they do validate.

Lots of TV's for your viewing pleasure, good place to go shoot some games of pool and if you are a smoker then there is smoking in the pool area.  They have excellent "bar"  food  and the beer is priced pretty well.  Just be sure to go with the small or large pitcher.  ;)  

I am a little biased to this bar, being that it is my neighborhood bar.  However I will admit that the service at times can be rather.........slow.  It' even aggravates me at times.  Have fun and be sure to stay too late!

I don't think I could say enough good things about Lüke. We were originally trying to grab lunch at another place in New Orleans that ended up being completely full so we came into Lüke as a back up option and it was probably the best decision of my life. The meal was probably one of the best I've ever had and we came back twice during our six day stay. 

Must orders are the brussel sprouts, shrimp and grits, and the stuffed Bienville oysters. The brussel sprouts are charred perfectly and cooked in this delicious smoky sauce. The shrimp and grits were also sublime with an excellent balance of spices. The oysters were by far everyones favorite - they're cooked and served with a mix of shrimp and crab and a breadcrumb/cream topping. I would recommend going for lunch/dinner over breakfast as their breakfast menu isn't as extensive but if you do go for breakfast I'd recommend the fried chicken and biscuit. It comes with a tobasco honey sauce that is so delicious.

The prices are extremely reasonable and you can enjoy a nice cocktail while there as well. Couldn't recommend this place enough and it's generally pretty easy to get a table (we didn't have a reservation either time and only waited 10 mins max).
The steaks cannot be beat.  A bit expensive, but worth a try from everyone.  Their valet make it great to park.  The sides are huge and worth sharing

Went for a brunch on a sunday morning and wow didnt realize the wait would be so long for basic food. Heard from many people how good it was and was disapointed. Had the chicken and waffles and was a chicken strip with super dry syrup on a waffle. Expected more for the price

Pros:
They offer a great deal on your first wax if you're a new client. And you get a discount every time you refer a friend - awesome!
The prices are really reasonable - their package deals are even better.
They do an awesome job with the waxing (most of the time)
It's almost always possible to get a last minute or walk-in appointment - something that is practically unheard of in other salons I've been to.

Cons:
They're extremely pushy about selling additional products, future appointments, packages - EVERYTHING. And it starts the moment you walk in. I've experienced everything from being heavily pressured to schedule my next appointment immediately after I finished, to having a tech talk up several products during my appointment, and then grab them all and put them on the counter with the bill when I went to pay, as if I had already agreed to buy them. Very uncomfortable.

This is not the place to come if you're expecting a relaxing experience. They make no effort to hide the fact that they're basically just trying to get clients in and out as soon as possible. This means that if you're getting a brazilian, you'd better not be shy, because not only will you not get a towel to cover anything, but the tech will also expect you to "prepare" while she's in the room.

I'm sure this is true for every salon, but the quality of the techs varies a LOT here. They mostly seem inexperienced. I've had some really great ones, but one or two who were really awful as well. (The tech I had for my last appointment missed several spots and spent the entire time trash talking the rest of the staff. Awkward!) So if you get someone you like, be sure to remember her name for next time! (I'm really bad at that.)

I always recommend this place to my friends who are on a budget or need an appointment ASAP. Just remember.....sometimes you get what you pay for.
Great froyo spot! Lots of topping selections and the girl at the counter was incredibly nice. Would definitely go back!

Great drinks, fun atmosphere! Live music! I would love to eat and stay at the hotel sometime. My friend immediately made a reservation for a weekend when her friend was coming to NOLA. So, it pretty quickly impressed!

The line wraps around the back of the store but moves relatively quickly. The chewy pralines are delicious as we're the tourtes. They package up the candies for travel, which is a great option for tourists coming from afar. Friendly service too. Make sure you try a sample before you buy.
Great view on the upper level deck. Saw a dolphin! The Fish and Chips were great - huge portion and very fresh. The service was also good. Will be back!

We always like to support our local family owned business and share our experience, it was our first time here, and all around had a great experience, our server was helpful, we didn't wait to long to get our table and our complements to the chef all food was really good lots of flavor!!
First time costumer and i really enjoyed myself, good staff and very clean, great flavors but i still felt there could have been more, but that's me.

Quick Summary:  Slightly overpriced yet still great bourbon bar with a diverse blues entertainment lineup.

I've been to T3 five times and have eaten there on three occasions.  I've consistently had good food, though I struggle with the price for the value and portion size.  My most favorite foods there so far have been the fried tomatoes (on special), corn fritters, primal chili, crabcakes and blackened catfish.  Prices are too prohibitive on their charcoal menu offerings (with no sides?!?!) to entice me.  Service has always been quick and accomodating and all of my meals have always come out hot with the appropriate condiments.  Great bartending with special emphasis on liquor/cocktail knowledge AND food pairings.  I've never been bored with my bourbons there, and it never fails that I am offered something that I've not tried before.

The decor in the venue is simple yet interesting.  Whiskey barrels serve as seats and foundations for the tables and bar upstairs, though the hard bar seats are hell on the ass with little back support.  The lounge area has inviting couches, a fireplace and shuffleboard.  There's a distinct lack of scuzzy people hanging out and that's almost enough for me to give them an extra star!

Twisted Tail has become a hotspot in the Delaware Valley for blues performers.  House band Mikey Junior and the Stone Cold Blues Band (have competed several years at the International Blues Challenge in Memphis) rock the spot weekly and host the Open Jam on Sunday evenings.  Other local and regional acts have graced the stage, to include Roger Girke, Georgie Bonds and Deb Callahan.  My only whine is that acoustically, the band space is far from perfect. The narrow chamber limits the ability to get a substantial audience in to see the musicians; there are only two tables on the floor up in the front of the room.  The bands are backed by glass windows and surrounded by brick in the long, narrow room; sound vigorously jettisons around in the room.  It would be easy to put some stylish acoustic material in the clamshell where the bands play to control some of the harshness.

My other criticism?  My sense is that the chef and management is overthinking, coming close to ruining the simplicity of southern cooking with nouvelle techniques and ideas.  This isn't a BBQ joint an they should probably stop peddling themselves as such unless they truly change the menu and employ KISS priciples.  In turn, they'd be bringing in far more people and getting far better reviews with easier-to-deliver fare.

Restaurant Week '13

Drinks - Two flights of tequila supplied by greasy man hitting on us - AWESOME. The only issue was once we were done with the tequila our server was supposed to get us margaritas with our choice of tequila. She was so busy that we never got the chance to really flag her down. Not the end of the world, partially our fault. 

Moving on.

The quacamole was so buttery! We just ordered it sort of plain with jalapenos, cilantro and tomatoes. 

I got the empanada app which was very good. The chicken inside had a lot of flavor and the crust was perfectly crusty. I got the short ribs for my main and forgive me because I forget what it came with, but everything was good. Definitely a solid three for the dinner.

The dessert was just weird. I wanted to be adventurous. But I guess sweet/spicy sauce and chocolate just don't do it for me. I took one taste of the chocolate tart and instantly wanted to vomit. That has never happened to me before and I was embarassed by my poor choice!!! My dining companion chose the better dessert - the mango mousse cake something or other, and that was sweet!

I could go back for happy hour, but there are other Mexican places I need to try before.

The driving range is open till 10:00 p.m. The guys are unpretentious and eager to help. The "clubhouse" is a trailer with an awesome deck. This place reminds me of something out of Tin Cup...which is what makes it great. Go hit some balls or come on a Wed night in August and play night golf on their 9 hole course. 

Loved it! And I'll be back many times.

It's not expensive. There is always a wait on Sunday, but it tends to go fast. It is your best middle of the night drunk eatery choice. It's definitely a little piece of history. The food is definitely like home cooking. Many different omelette choices. Last time I tried the French toast and it was amazing. Some of the staff is awesome, and some could use better people skills.
Typical Sushi Chain, You should not expect anything special. Standard, boring quality.

In July 2014, I used G&G moving for a local move and had an amazing experience.  After shopping around prices, I chose to go with G&G.  Some alternatives had slightly cheaper rates but they were all on a "per hour" basis and had all sorts of additional fees.  G&G, on the other hand, had absolutely no hidden fees.  They quoted me a fair price (not on a per hour basis) and that is all i paid (except a tip for an excellent move).  

What more can you ask for:  Vernon and his employee arrived early, worked diligently and carefully, didn't damage anything, and were polite and friendly.  They even wrapped up furniture for protection during the move.

Vernon & Jessica run a great company.  I have already recommended them to a friend and highly recommend to all.

We just moved South from Pittsburgh. What we really miss are the ethnic food stores in Pittsburgh's Strip District; i.e., Italian, Greek, Polish, Spanish, Middle Eastern, spices, sausage store, fishmonger, etc. So when the cable guy gave us a list of craft beer bars, restaurants and the market he and his wife love (Mazzaro's) we decided to check them out. 

Yesterday was the Mazzaro excursion. What a pleasant surprise and fun adventure. We found all that we were looking for at the market plus more. The staff was friendly though very busy. A lot of the customer's weren't  sure what some of the products were and others were helping them and providing suggestions on what they like and how to use. (Of course there will always be those with carts banging into you and pushing others out of the way to get their ticket first. LOL, and yes, I was the recipient of the two overzealous customers.).

Next time we go we will have lunch on the patio. All of the tables were taken so we decided to go home and feast on the bounty we purchased. 

The next visit will also include me having the spumoni, which looked absolutely delicious, and a seat at the coffee bar. Can't wait till then.

First off this is a nice place to come an visit. If you have a voucher that cover your stay and give you 100 credit make sure that everything they said is in writing. I had a voucher that discounted me for two nights and gave me 100 credit to use at the resort. One of the employees said that I could use the credit to cover cover my stay.  When I checked out the manager said that we could not used the credit to pay for the hotel. Again this is got a great deal, I don't mind paying for my stay. What I do mind is being lie to.  Honestly is everything. If they were honest from the start I would be giving them 1 star.

I was visiting from Baltimore and staying at The Loews Hotel when we stumbled upon this place.. The bartender was very cool ( Brendon?), the drinks we good, and the food was cheap. Had a good time listening to karaoke as well. We had such a good time we came back the very next night. I highly suggest this place if you want to mingle with the locals!

I had a chance last evening to visit this place. I ordered a banana pie and a butter milk cheese biscuit with a lo colombe regular coffee. The food was ok , not very great, i found natural sweetnees or no sweetness in the bakery items i ordered which depends on a person's choice. The prices are high i supposed, the staff was very good. If you want to experience it for once or have enough money to spend, definitely go but it's not a place for daily evening visita especially when you are a student. Happy eating ....

-diwa
Wish the menu had more kid items but other then that the food was amazing! I am still thinking about those sweet potato fries  So far I have had the Bison burger. Can't wait to try more!

When I was planning my best friend's bachelorette party, I came across Linley with Music City Pub Crawl and decided to book a private tour with her. We had 14 girls and booked an afternoon tour with her. Linley texted me the night before tour and the morning of to check in which I appreciated and met us at a bar to start the tour. She was so welcoming to a group of people she had never met before and instantly became part of our crew. 

We toured 4 or 5 different bars and had an absolute BLAST. One of the girls in our group had recently had surgery and couldn't drink but Linley made it fun for the whole crew - sober or not! The trivia was fun and applicable to our group and we definitely got competitive. 

I would HIGHLY recommend this tour - it was the highlight of our trip to Nashville :)
Awesome place for a quick bite.... Loved the tuna melt sandwich and black bean soup!!! AAA+++

Horrible customer service!! I ordered my photos and the lady told me 8 minutes.. now I'm sitting here waiting to check out for 20min and one of their employees is sitting there printing her own photos on the machine! Literally 3 feet away from me and she won't even eat someone to ring me up. Not to mention there are about 2-3 other customers waiting behind me to checkout.

I've been coming here before the age of Netflix, Hulu, and during the era of Hollywood Videos and Blockbusters. Its been interesting seeing them constantly remodeling and rethinking the store layout and how to keep afloat in a digital age. I come here now for all my old classic movies with Cary Grant, Humphrey Bogart and Audrey Hepburn. The kind of movies you have to buy online to watch. I love that the classics are broken up by actor. It makes it super easy and fast to find or browse if you know an actor you want to see more of. Occasionally, I will rent a series like Game of Thrones as well. Shows that you have to buy into some plan to see their content (*cough* HBO *cough*). I love the new addition of the Casa Video Bar (see my review on their YELP page). You can grab a beer and browse the movies or just hangout there. It's all connected! I love that they have food trucks on different days (see their Facebook page for what food on what days). Casa Video has done wonderful things to get you to stay longer, spend more and make your experience overall enjoyable and relaxing. I believe they have the staying power and will be around for a lot longer. They've got growler filling capacity, beer/wine to buy, popcorn or a menus to order pizza from down the road if you plan to stick around for awhile. My only complaint, so minor but I am a poor girl and find their rental prices a bit expensive. They do offer 2-1s on Tuesday and Wednesdays, definitely helpful! Really, this place is a one-stop shop for all your movie needs and a must see at least once but I guarantee once you go you'll be hooked for life. You've been warned!

Great swamp tour...I would recommend driving there and save a few bucks if you have a vehicle.   It lasted a couple of hours which I think was a perfect amount of time.  Saw several alligators, a family of wild pigs and a couple of creepy spiders. The tour guys were friendly and funny.  The only irritate was a young girl that always had something to say...
The shrimp and grits for breakfast were outstanding -- just sad I discovered them on my last day in town.

The staff here is very friendly, but I beg to differ when it comes to the line in this store. I don't know what it is but the line is always long. I haven't waited for coffee so long at a store in Philadelphia or NYC. One of my chief complaints, I understand customer service but catching up on life, school, kids, is not a good when the lines are long.
Floor was dirty. Food lacked taste, not a lot of selection.  Service was good nice waitress. Glad it was only 15.95 only had half a plate and I was turned off.

For what it serves it is awesome.  I waited in line for about 45 minutes during the last Manayunk street food festival to get a taste of this food trucks.  I'm not privy to food trucks on a normal basis because of my work location so I considered it a special occasion to wait in line for this.

When I got to the front of the line I placed an order for a large deep fried curds and some sauce to go with it.  The fried cheese curds were absolute bliss.  Cooked to the right consistency, warm, gooey fried goodness.  The only thing that hampered my visit was the next time I was the truck there was absolutely no line.  Wish they could move faster for the big events.

For the price of the room we should of had better service and more perks. Free Wi-Fi would of been nice and they also blocked my hotspot from working not a good place.
I am glad the FCC found this out.

The restaurant looks closed from the outside. The windows have a peeling tint, and it is dark. The inside of the restaurant is also dark. This was strange at first, but ended up being good because it's harder to see the things you're forcing yourself to actually eat. Although there were five empty and prepared tables, we were not seated for about ten minutes. There was no apparent reason for this, but it seemed to be what happened to everyone who came in. The floors were also incredibly slippery and hard to walk on. When I placed my order, it was written down, however, three things didn't come at all. The sushi is low quality. They use entirely too much rice, and the fish does not taste or smell fresh. I couldn't eat it. The cooked food was not awful, but was not worth getting. The waitress for my table was polite, but rarely present. Overall, this was a disappointing and overall disgusting experience.

I remember when this place was new and fresh. It was worth the trip from Germantown.  Now, the quality of this place is akin to an expensive Pathmark.  Oh, how the mighty have fallen.

I've been disappointed with this place for a while.  But the kicker came when I came for a *simple* caesar salad.  All I wanted from the salad bar was - romaine, onion, dressing - 3 simple ingredients. What I realized as I stood there amazed there wasn't romaine, was that they've mistaken fancy for quality.  A salad bar with only spinach and mesclun? No iceberg or romaine...why? And the spinach and mesclun looked a little wilted anyway, so it wasn't even appealing. 

So trying to salvage my trip here, I peruse the rest of the bar.  It's totally Mediterranean influenced.  Meaning...I hate it. I don't like feta. I don't like stuffed olives. I don't like dolmades. I have to be in a mood for hummus, and it's damn sure not coming from a buffet. So I'm totally underwhelmed. And since my desired salad base is inexplicably missing, I can't just make a salad.

I go to look at the sushi...why, I haven't a clue. I know it's gross, but the allure of the Asian man cleaning the knives as if he's just freshly made all of those containers of sushi, gets me.  I look and then gag on the price.  

I'm starving though and have just had an incident involving the cops (funny story), so I just want to sit and eat something. I finally buy just a simple macaroni salad from the deli and get water. 

I sit down, come to Yelp and find the sushi restaurant 2 blocks down, get up and leave.

I don't think I'll bother stopping here again.
I love this place, my favorite item is New York Olive Bread and their home made potato. Staff are very friendly.

I clearly ordered UNSWEETENED iced tea. They came out with sweet tea. I just noticed in the reviews that they did the same exact same thing to another customer.

Anyway, when I pointed out the mistake my server said she could not take back or refund the drink.  My only recourse was to order and pay for a new drink. So I placed the order, waited 10 minutes, but it never came. I pushed the call button, but I was ignored for five more minutes. I finally gave up and drove away without the drink I wanted. I ended up paying full price for a drink that was poured into the bushes.

I headed over to McDonalds and got exactly what I wanted for half the price.

I will not be going to Sonic again.

Food at this eclectic, outdoor restaurant/bar was fine, and reasonably priced, but not only were cocktails ~$15, I was actually charged $2.50 for a cube of ice in my  Scotch! Really? $15 for a drink and another $2.50 for a single cube of ice??!! Maybe water is expensive in that part of town.

During my 90,000 mile service on March 6, 2013, Walker VW (Metairie, LA) recommended that I have my CV boots replaced. Since I was driving home to Virginia that weekend, the service manager agreed to complete the work on March 8, 2013.  I picked up my car on the morning of March 9th (I paid $724.68) and departed Metairie early on March 10th to head home to VA.  As I got on the highway, I noticed a little more road noise than usual and made a mental note to get it checked out when I got home.  As I continued driving, I noticed a knocking noise and pulled over at the nearest exit, which was in Mobile, AL.  I visually inspected the vehicle and noticed the engine under cover hanging from my car.  My assumption was that Walker VW hadn't properly secured it after servicing my vehicle.  Fortunately, I was able to find a mechanic open on a Sunday morning.  He removed the engine under cover and disposed of it, citing that it was beyond repair.  He opined that it likely hadn't been tightened enough, hence the initial increased road noise I had heard that morning.  He advised me to have the engine under cover replaced as soon as I got home.  I contacted Walker VW on Monday morning (March 11th) and explained the situation.  Francisco stated that he would look into it.  On March 12, I brought my car to my local VW (Sheehy VW, Springfield, VA) to order the new engine under cover.  During inspection, they identified that I was in need of new CV boots.  They physically showed me the faulty workmanship of my CV boot replacement from 4 days prior.  My Sheehy VW service advisor  called Walker VW and spoke to Francisco.  He explained the situation and Francisco said he would look into it and get back to either Ben or me.  Sheehy VW ordered my engine under cover and I agreed to come back the following day for the CV boot replacement and engine under cover installation.  When I dropped my car off on March 13, I asked Ben if Walker VW had called him the previous day.  He said no.  Ben contacted Francisco again.  Francisco requested an estimate and said he would get back to me later that day.  When my car was ready for pickup, I contacted Francisco to find out if/when Walker VW would compensate me for their obvious faulty workmanship.  He said he was waiting for the service manager to come in but that it would definitely be taken care of.  I picked up my car and paid $986.92, of which $220.21 was for the engine cover and $597.89 was for the new CV boots (the rest was for 4-wheel alignment and tax).  Sheehy VW service desk explained the extent and severity of the poor workmanship.  They stated that the job had been completely botched by Walker VW.  Not only were the CV boots not installed properly (connecters were loose and dangling), they had been packed with little to no grease.  I contacted Francisco again on March 14th, March 15th, and March 18th.  He continued to tell me that he had provided all the information to the service manager and he was waiting on a determination but he excepted everything to be taken care of.  Francisco called me on the evening of March 18th and requested that I fax my invoice from Sheehy VW.  I did so on March 19th and followed up with a phone call to Francisco.  He said that he received the fax and would provide it to the service manager.  Francisco has been consistently polite; however, I have now called at least 7 times and I feel I am no closer to getting a refund.  I have been beyond patient and reasonable, but Walker VW is without a doubt responsible for this.  I unknowingly drove 1300 miles with unlubricated CV boots.  I wasted time and money getting my car RE-repaired.  Not to mention the time and stress associated with repeatedly having to contact Walker VW about this situation.  Walker VW owes me $818.10 plus tax.

Look folks, bottom line here. If you want the best seafood, freshest seafood, most knowledgeable monger, their prices are low on the list as to why you shop here. Sure you can get seafood cheaper at Publix, Winn Dixie, or places similar. But you will not get anywhere near the quaility or taste. How about a whole  Grouper right off the boat? Got lucky when the fisherman came in, and it was in my belly that night. Please enjoy.

I will start with the fact that I've only been there once (last night) and will probably go back at least once more...to be fair. I like supporting the little guy...

My husband and I had the Pollo Asado taco - which was all chipotle. The Barbacoa taco - which was so salty you couldn't taste anything else. The Carne Asada taco - which had so much cheese on it, you couldn't taste the meat. And the Carnitas Bowl, which was probably the best thing we had. 

The chips had way too much cumin on them. Cumin does not make food authentic latin cuisine. The rice is definitely minute rice and the beans are canned and neither were seasoned. However, the tortillas themselves are pretty good and the guacamole and salsa were both very nice.

I don't care much about atmosphere, or the decor...since I am not eating either of those things. The place looked clean...which is very important to me.

Prices were reasonable - for what it is.

That being said, it was a nice try, and we will go back at least once more...maybe it was just a bad night. The staff was friendly enough, and we were comfortable there.

If you want decent Mexican food in St. Pete, this is probably your best bet - unless you fancy the Taco Bus which struck out three times with me.

However, If you want authentic Mexican food, try Miguel's in Tampa or Casa Tina's in Dunedin. It's a drive, but well worth it.

I went here for a New Year's Even dinner.

Good chinese/french fusion fare.  I'm not a fan of the stuffy atmosphere though and I probably won't go again because the food didn't wow me enough.

Love this place! The owner is a nuritionist and knows her stuff. She was very friendly and explain the menus and the concept of the restaurant to us. The place is aim towards healthy eating. I came in on Sunday and and ordered the Lemon grass soup and my boyfriend had a chili bowl. Both were delicious and fresh. I will be coming back for the salad on my next trip.

No matter what night we go....Service and food is always excellent. When you sign up to get their notifications but email....almost every 4-6 weeks you receive an email with a $20.00 off $50.00. Order.   Not good on the AYCE specials or $4.99 Monday might burger w/ fries.... Cooking classes monthy are also the best....we dine her @ least 1-2 times a week....

I just went to Mr. B's about an hr ago to see what all the commotion was about with their seafood gumbo.  First of all, the gumbo was such a small portion that I thought I was being pranked when the waiter served it.  Maybe it was small due to me being 6'3 225 lbs but still, it was more the size of an appetizer than an entree.  The roux was flavorful but that's where it stopped.  It had extremely small portions of seafood that was small in size as well, it felt as if they were measuring the seafood in each dish like they were going out of business.  The ambience was nice but for the prices they charge, I will not be going back.  I'm extremely disappointed as I had read the reviews and was excited about trying their gumbo so I'm still on the hunt for a better gumbo spot.

Best breakfast I had in New Orleans. I got their pancakes which were amazing and tried grits here for the first time. Of all the grits I tasted over the course of my trip these were the best. It's not a particularly fancy place and it is cluttered but that said for what it is- its great. Prices are very fair and the food is solid.

This is my very first yelp review. I feel this place deserves it.

As someone who is very familiar Chicago style deep dish pizza, I was fairly skeptical of how the pizza would turn out, due to the lack of deep dish pizza places in Nashville. The places that claim to have "deep dish" pizzas in the past have failed tremendously. Probably because they weren't actually deep dish pizzas. 

When our pie (the veggie) came out we jumped with joy because it was exactly what we were used to receiving in Chicago. Deep filled pie, with sauce on top and fresh veggies. The server cut into it with a spatula table side and lifted one massive piece on to a plate as the cheese followed in all it's stringy glory. I took my first bite and was in deep dish heaven. The sauce was on point. The cheese was thick. The veggies were not over cooked and and the crust was buttery, flaky and dense. Perfection!

I was so pleased with my experience. The owner was sitting next to our table and talked to us for a while. She says this is the first restaurant she's ever opened. And she owned it, pun intended. The staff was very friendly and the atmosphere and decor where very Chicago like. The price was great too. Especially with the sourcing of the ingredients. Local vendors and some organic ingredients. 

Good beer, good pizza. There's nothing else I could ask for in this place. Welcome to the 615, 312. We're glad to have you. Expect to see me often.

We fell victim to the "SECRET CLOSE".  That's where the server closes their station, usually unbeknownst to the management.

After checking the sign just to be sure they were open (till 10), we walked in with 45 min to spare.  

A large table was finishing up and there were no other patrons in the dining room.

The lone server asked if we were making an order for take out or dining in.  When we said dining in, she informed us that they were closing and that we could still eat, but in the bar.

I even mentioned "Funny, because your sign says you're open till 10" and got a blank stare reeking of "who gives a sh*t"

Sad thing is the bar had no table seating and the bar was full.  The only place you could sit was a lunch counter that faces the wall...the black, blank wall.

Anyway, if I'd wanted to eat at a bar, I would've gone to a bar.

And if you want to close earlier, just adjust the time.

If you don't want to work that late, find a job where you don't have to.

Continued down the street to that place where the sell pizzas by the "Slice"...pretty good stuff there, and open later and accepting guests right until the last second.
We stayed here on an overnight visit. We had a great time. Place was great, food was great. However make reservations in advance for the spa.. they book up fast

Fairly new to the area, I was eager to find a prenatal yoga studio that focused on the individual, in addition to the practice. A friend who worked at a local preschool, referred me to Then Comes Baby and after reading reviews and speaking directly to the owner, Sabrina, I decided to give it a try! 

The facility is clean, airy and inviting and it was really great to connect with the pregnant moms in addition to the instructor. During my first class, wendyEllen happened to be there to demonstrate some moves from her bellydance class. The next Saturday, I was back to attend that class. 

I feel that I finally found a community in Then Comes Baby and connected with a wonderful group of young women and educators.

Very good.... my daughter loved the food and thought the staff was very nice.  The owner or manager was at the table several times and delivered our food.  The seafood ravioli was excellent and so was the fresh tomato and basil sauce.  It was authentic and well done.  (Italians in the restaurant business- so not easily impressed)
Good brew and good food!  Have been there a couple of time and never disappointed.

I love marathon! I have been in here few times and every time, I never had trouble waiting for a table or not getting anything below perfect! The prices are super reasonable and the menu selection is very diverse!

Haven't had Ted Drewes in yrs, but I'm glad I made a stop by to relive my HS days of sitting in the opened trunk of my car to listen to tunes fit for an athlete who just finished up with my favorite summer sport like the good ol' days. 

I got my fav: 2 parts m&m, 1 part cookie dough, medley, and pineapple.  Even as it melted down quickly in the scorching heat, it tasted just as good as it always does, making me wish I had taken some to-go. Brought a NYer who compared it to Abbott's Frozen Custard in Upstate NY who also gives a raving review. 

Ted Drewes is known to provide Scholarships to kids and provide summer employment to high schoolers, so I completely understand a few small hiccups. We were overcharged $6 because of the accidental push of a button. She refunded us as soon as we made mention of the discrepancy, and apologized. It's not what you do, it's how it is handled after, so thank you, you get 5 STARS!

You have to rate a place based on what it is, and this is a hole-in-the-wall pan-Asian east-side dive -- and for what it is, it's pretty good.  Not quite 4 stars, but not 3.  Three and a half would've been a better fit.  The bump up to 4 stars was based on our love of their Hot Jalapeño Chicken Wings.  Now don't go there expecting bright orange wings glistening in sauce, accompanied by carrot and celery sticks, with ranch dressing on the side.  These are different and employ a Tucson favorite, the jalapeño.  The dish is basically little hunks of fried chicken topped with minced jalapeños and some other tiny pepper that looks like a chile pequin---awesome.  My husband usually gets the twiced cooked BBQ pork (not the regular pork, the BBQ one -- we got the wrong one once and it wasn't as good) and I look for something with broccoli in it.  I haven't found anything I like enough to order it twice.  But I like the appetizer enough to keep coming back to try again.  

Other Notes of Interest:
"Asian" in the title because they serve Vietnamese, Thai, Korean, Japanese and Chinese food. We've only had the Thai and Chinese.
The iced tea tastes funky--so if you're an iced tea freak, this may ruin the whole thing for you.
"Chips & Salsa"--when you first arrive you get a bowl of fried wonton strips with plum sauce.  Avoid this.
They serve brown rice (in addition to white)  to bring down the glycemic index of your meal.
Lots of regulars stop by for take out.
They deliver.

Been there, done that, won't be back. 
The food was horrible. Service was bad. And both my son and I left there feeling sick and stayed that way the rest of the day. 
It gets 1 star because, well I don't have an option to give anything less and also because it was very clean.

Overall I do like this place and have been coming here for years. They did a good job on the remodel but there are a few things that I do not like about Shephard's.   They do not have room service except for in the morning.  Their breakfast room service cuts off at 11 AM.  When you call their room service line before 11 AM most of the time they do not answer.  You are told to leave a message which they do not return.  The service inside of the restaurant is usually very slow.  They play the same songs just in a different order pretty much every day at the tiki bar.  There is no smoking on the outside patio.  It's a patio located outside....makes no sense.  The menu at the tiki bar is one of the worst menus I've seen at a hotel pool/tiki bar. They also carry Pepsi products instead of coke but only have like 3 options, Pepsi, Diet Pepsi or Sierra Mist. Pepsi is obsolete and they should update this.   I do love the live music, the private beach and the location of the hotel.  The daily live music is what keeps me coming back.

Yuck!! This place was horrible. Bland cafeteria style food thats luke warm with no flavor. I received ""kraft"" mac n cheese from a BOX..... lmao... wow!!! & green beans from a can. Didn't even doctor them up, just directly from.. the.. can... Never again. Even the hot chocolate was gross n made with WATER

Really cute place. Felt like I was on a beach somewhere in the Caribbean. I ordered a meatball sandwich and it was huge.  The meatballs were delicious.
