First time here I got the Cajun creole chicken it was good with the Cajun fries. Watermelon punch wasn't that good but if you mix it with the Oprah punch it tastes better will be back

This place has a great vibe and lots of energy! Being an out towner, we were recommended the tavern by our hotel staff at Hutton hotel. The tavern is in walking distance and has a very friendly wait staff. Their food was great and the wine made our night before walking downtown to enjoy the live music on the strip. And we are back for another round the next day! :)

Kameron just helped us tonight and he was rude and disrespectful to us. They got our order wrong when I ordered a ham and cheese sandwich but they put turkey so we pointed it out to him and he argued with us saying he read back the order to us but he didn't and didn't bother asking if there was anything else we would like to order when we wanted to add items to our order. When he gave the sandwich back to the girl making the food instead of remaking the sandwich we watched her just take the turkey off and put ham and cheese on the original sandwich she had made. I won't be coming back to this location because of the service we just revived. I will also be filing a formal complaint with corporate regarding the disrespect we recived. I have been in customer service for a very long time and would be fired on the spot if treated any clients the way we were treated tonight.

I don't order much take out, but when I do, I go to Salerno's. It is one of the nicer businesses on this forgotten strip of Rising Sun Avenue. They have also added a small restaurant to the pizzeria. The young girls who answer the phone to take your order are always polite and pleasant. Everything I have had here is delicious. Most recently I had a cup of the minestrone soup. It came with garlic bread. The soup was so fresh, so flavorful. Overflowing with vegetables and pasta shells. My boyfriend has the ham calzone and he devoured it. Another consistent favorite here are the clubs. The turkey club is delicious. Real turkey, crisp bacon and fresh lettuce. Comes with a ton of fries. Delivery is also quick!

Hai street kitchen's sushi burritos are hit or miss. The first time, the spicy salmon (slammin' salmon) had actual salmon Sashimi in it, albeit not enough to warrant the price tag. The second time however, there was not enough fish at all. The tuna was so sparse that it was hard to taste over the pickled radish and other vegetables wrapped up in the roll. I am far from satisfied and your money is definitely better spent somewhere where they provide more than a sushi gimmick.

Their food is ok. They give you plenty so that's good!! Also they have fair prices . And the atmosphere is good. Service is ok . Very friendly people!!! If you're in the neighbor hood stop by. Why not . Nothing to lose ... But also nothing to gain .. Keep in mind :)

I found this place through yelp figured this place would be great, but boy I was wrong ... ordered a boba milk tea they asked how sweet I wanted my drink I said really sweet please... got my drink and was highly dissatisfied, the drink wasn't sweet at all ..how do you mess up adding enough sugar! I'd rate the place a zero if I could.

I have been coming here for the last 3 months for the sauna, EVOX, and life vessel. I am so glad I found SB Life Vessel! Stephanie is so sweet and always makes me feel welcomed upon arrival and I always leave feeling much more relaxed! Some of the techniques may be a little interesting, but I promise it is worth it! I am a personal trainer in Santa Barbara and I recommend all my clients do the infrared sauna. It detoxes much deeper than a traditional sauna and I find it is great for my anxiety/depression. I am sooo relaxed after and you burn so many calories in the sauna! Make sure to bring a snack with you for after because you will be hungry. I will be  a long term client of Life Vessel SB!
Visiting from out of town. Decided to give it a try. Pizza and garlic knots were pretty good. We would eat it again.

I like this place. The spicy Asian steak wrap was tasty. I don't know what the "Steak" was, but the damn wrap was out of my hands in a matter of minutes - so that says something! It was filling. The vegetables were clearly fresh. They have a solid, hard working team and a good process to move people in and out - so don't be concerned about the line (lunch time) it will move quickly. Will check out some other stuff here. It's a worth check out again spot.

Sadly, I feel the need to update my review.  The last few times I've been to Gianna's they haven't had any dessert :(  No dessert makes the baby jesus cry.  The food is still good, but the last time I was there they completely forgot about the pizza I ordered.  Also, the place is usually packed, but it was a ghost town this time.  I swear I saw a tumbleweed roll by.  In my original review, I forgot to mention how gross the bathroom is.  Hold it if you can.

I don't think I'll be going back for awhile.  From the looks of the other review, Gianna's is been disappointing quite a few people lately.  Hopefully they'll sort things out and go back to being awesome again.

This place is awesome, hipsters included.  The music is awesome, even the sweating is awesome. They have PBR on the menu over and over (PBR $2, But Lite, $4, PBR $2, etc.)  This made it even better.  

Why yes, I think I'll have a PBR.

This is a huge restaurant right on the water off the causeway.   Excellent risotto and grouper.

The views are amazing from the restaurant (there are huge windows facing the water so it doesn't really matter where you sit).
Great selection of beer,great food, great entertainment and awesome service! You have to stop by to see the most beautiful girls in NOLA Nicole and Julie. They will take real good care of ya.
Go to Miller's Ale House down the street instead. It blows Brewster's out of the water. Better specials, better music, better bar, better crowd. This place is sliding downhill fast.

If you dine out at any other restaurant in Franklin other than Red Pony, you've made a titanic mistake- absolutely ridiculous in its attention to detail, as if it's scrumptious food were not enough.  I am a cynical jackass and can do nothing but rave about this place.   There is nothing  in Manhattan. Chicago,  Vegas or LA you'd rather be.

Best sushi I've had in a long time. Wait staff was very attentive and great all around. I'll be going back for sure. The lunch options they have are very reasonable and the presentation of the food was excellent.

Cheu is my favorite spot to get noodles in Center City! It is on the smaller side inside so at times I've had to wait for a table. Each time however it is worth the wait. Highlights at this place are the Miso Ramen and Brisket Ramen. The broths on both are so flavorful. This is the type of noodle place to play Blink 182 one day and Notorious BIG the next. They are really doing their own thing and I think that's what makes the place so unique. Plus they do serve alcohol. Reasonable price for great noodles!

my husband and I visited here on fri 6/9.  I think my expectations were way to high.  Donuts were not bad but certainly didn't live up to the hype.  We ordered 6 hots, 2 of each and each sugar mix and 2 of the fancys they had which where spicy pb and j.  My husband is crazy for chicken and couldn't wait to dive in.  He said it was ok

Good place to grab a quick bite or drink before a show at Union Transfer.

From the limited amount that I was able to try off the menu, I can certainly say that the food is tasty.  You've probably got a safe bet with most of the items available.  The beer and drinks list is quite extensive as well, so you will have little worry finding something you like.  It was fairly packed, but the food came out really quickly.

The place is crowded, so come prepared for a wait, ours was about 40 minutes. This is the worst part about the place.

On the other hand the other two components and look for, the food, and service, are both pretty good.

Let's start with the food.  It is pretty typical Taiwanese food, but it was done very well. Liked all the dishes that we had, suggest the beef pancake, that is usually a good measure for any Taiwanese restaurant. The ones here are pretty good, although I would say the portions are a little smaller than usual, it was still very well done.

What I would say differentiate this place from other Chinese restaurant is the service. I honestly expected to be ignored once we got seated, this is usually the norm for typical Chinese restaurant until you flag someone down. However, in this case the servers came around fairly frequently and water checking on how things are going.  I would say the attention that they give their customers in this place make it stand out other Chinese restaurants.

I would definitely recommend this place if you are visiting Reno.
Great food! The staff are really nice and the food comes out quickly. Look at how big the Nachitos appetizer is!!

Our first visit to this location, many great meals at his previous restaurant. All three of us had the halibut on the lunch menu..All agreed an excellent meal, excellent service!! Fish cooked perfect, tender and very tasty..The sauce & raviolis were perfect..  Just an excellent experience!!

I discovered about reYOU massage after purchasing their $40 groupon deal, which I easily scheduled via online for the next day. It was the best decision for the unrelenting back pain I was experiencing for days. Michael Vasta is an expert in shiatsu/thai massage, which is similar to deep tissue with pressure and stretching. He targeted pressure points and helped ease the tension on my back. He also included my arms and legs on his massage. After an hour, I came out feeling relaxed and pain-free. All in all, I was very satisfied and would definitely recommend anyone to try reYOU!

I ordered the meal deal with his six nuggets and fries and BBQ sauce and a large  sweet. Receive my order and I touch my fries and they was cold. Is be young guy in the window to your have any hot fries so I gave him my the cold fries and he hollered back to the person that was cooking. They said yes we have hot fries. So he went back to get them and when he was walking to the window he just hand me the hot fries in this hands. He should have put them in a bag or wrapped a napkin around them so I got another order of fries.

This place is horrendous at best. I thought that this place was for adults but yet I felt like I walked into a daycare. The whole place smelled like a port-a-potty. Had to use the bathroom real bad so did so before I left and went somewhere else and the bathroom smelled better than the establishment. Trust me don't waste your time with this place.

Walked to here during a 2 hr break from Vball tournament. Got in pretty quickly but didn't get out as quickly as I wanted. Julian gave us the rundown of what would transpire for our visit since we had 9 in a party (not sure we needed that). He did an efficient job managing our orders and kept up with all our refills. The bruschetta chicken salad was pretty goo but needed more tomatoes...yes I know it was a bruschetta salad with minimal tomatoes. Also blue cheese as one of the cheeses??? What about feta being a more delicious flavor choice.  How many people really like blue cheese?? I didn't time how long our entire visit took but ended up whoofing down my salad and dashing out so I could make our next matches start time.

The iced coffee is really good. I had the breakfast burrito, which was bad. It was wrapped in a mission tortilla and was tiny. They used jarred Tostito style salsa which ruined it. Get the coffee, stay away from the microwaved food
Best manicure I have had in a while! Excellent service, I would recommend this nail salon to anyone. I will definitely be back soon. :)

Super interesting concept. I'm a sushi lover myself, and chose the Spicy Tuna type item when I ordered.

It tasted great and was filling, though I have to remove a star for price. It takes about 30 seconds to make the roll and paying almost double an actual spicy tuna roll's cost at a sushi restaurant definitely stings.

If only this place were there when I went to Penn!

We drove from Effingham to take my brother out for his birthday. He is a chef and was interested in checking the place out. We made reservations and had no trouble getting seated even though it was very busy. Our server seemed inexperienced but was very nice and attentive. The management had her back when one of our entrees came out wrong and not only fixed the mistake but gave us the incorrect dish to take home. He even agreed to take my bro on a quick tour of the kitchen. 

All the food we tried was outstanding. The blue cheese chips and smoked salmon dip were both incredible. I personally didn't care for the truffle egg toast, but it wasn't terrible.  Our entrees were all cooked to perfection and very tasty. I could go on and on about the entrees, but dessert was my favorite part...the cheesecake...sweet Jesus...it was torched, meaning they set flame to sugar on top of it. The pie and ice cream are homemade, just as comfort food should be. It was a great evening. I will be going back!!
I enjoyed the entertainment and the food. Our waitress was excellent. I felt sorry for her, she had to walk so far. I don't think the restaurant is setup in mind of the servers.

Don't be fooled by the boring menu write up. The menu looks ordinary, but the food coming out of this kitchen is the work of an imaginative perfectionist.  He marries flavor combinations and textures so thoughtfully that we can only imagine the sleepless nights that have gone into each creation. If this guy was single I think my husband would leave me for him.  In our opinion this is the best food in philly right now.   You have to try this place. It is not to be missed. It is very reasonably priced for the quality and work that is obvious in each dish.  Please bring an open mind, he's trying the new, so don't be thrown off by an undercooked raw vegetable here and there.   Also make sure to compose your bites. Some dishes won't make sense unless you get each component on your fork. Cheers!!!

Stopped by for a quick coffee and snack and the Cumberland Island was wicked good, had an awesome refreshing after taste and still gave that great caffeinated coffee taste. Not from around here but definitely could be a chill study spot.

Also snagged a Ham and Cheese croissant that was also delic!

The food really was amazing.  Everything we had was executed to perfection.  It's a wonderful addition to the uptown nice-dinner-out scene--in-line with Clancy's, Patois, etc.  This, however, is a bit more inventive than your trusty New Orleans standards.  Inventive in the best way possible--completely delicious, solid food that you haven't seen on every menu in town.

The thing I can't get out of my mind, though, is the "chicken n' dumplins"--which is an amazingly fluffy and light gnocchi with shredded chicken and some sort of dark gravy/sauce situation.  I can't wait to go back and have this again.

Nice place to get your garments altered.  I stopped by to get a vest made and Kim (?) helped get me measured.  Picked up the vest today and fits just like it should.  No issues and service with a smile.

Location is easy to miss if going north on Rangeline.

Just bought a great box of fresh, organic produce: blood oranges, strawberries, frisee, lettuce, mushrooms, etc.

I love that they are trying to buy local and it's great service.  Wonderful use of the old Guilliot's nursery.  Check them out! 

Open every Saturday from 10-2.

Had breakfast here today. Service is very unattentive and we had to call the waiter multiple times for coffee refil and he also overcharged our check. I had the duck omelete, which was greasy and the waiter also misplaced my toast side order for french fries. For a 30 dollar breakfast I expected much more, would not go back.

Ahh-mazing! 
For a newly opened restaurant this place totally delivers; the space is modern and beautifully designed and service is friendly and expedient. 
This being our first visit, we started with the basics, which is pretty much a barometer on whether to dive in deeper.
Shrimp spring rolls were beautiful, Louisiana shrimp freshly cooked (still warm & luscious inside the roll); peanut sauce was rich. 

Shrimp vermicelli had gorgeous grilled shrimp &clean fresh flavors throughout. 

Beef pho was one of the best I've ever had; sultry, flavorful broth with amazing depth and gorgeous, balanced seasoning. Amount of beef was very generous; the only slight gripe is that the "fixings" (sprouts &herbs) we're a bit skimpy... I like lots with mine. Also, no jalapeño. Overall though, this wasn't enough to knock the rating down. 

Will definitely be back!
[this is a review of RFA's smog testing] This is an excellent place to go for smog testing.  In and out in 10-15 minutes, and reasonable prices.

I'm not sure why the negative reviews for this restaurant. It's very good. Nice selections on the menu. Everything we tried was good. They don't give their food away, but you get what you pay for and in my opinion it was well worth the price. During our one week stay in New Orleans, this ranked well above mid-range. Plus it's located right in the heart of the live jazz district of Frenchman. Eat a nice meal and listen to some awesome music just down the street. How cool is that?

The decor and the neighborhood were really nice, but the food was on the sweet side. I had beef kabobs with roasted potatoes, but they were soaked with some kind of sweet sauce that ruined it for me. The portions are smaller than usual. This place is probably more a bar than a restaurant.

Meh, expensive and uncomfortable seating. One family relocated to another table when one became available, the mother said she expected more than a stool as their bill was going to be $300.  They were sitting on metal stools like your Grandpa has in his garage. We ordered the Sunday fried chicken dinner for two. It was to be a whole chicken and sides. The fried chicken was good but we were served five legs and two wings, one strange bird. My husband said it was built for speed, lol.  We won't be back. Adding basil to everything doesn't make it italian.

Fresh falafel! clean and hip place around the area. Chipotle style assembly of falafel on the go, quick n healthy option with fresh ingredients.. my favorite is falafel bowl with pita. They fry fresh falafel balls when you order, spicy sauce and tahini are good too, other options include green mild sauce and mango!

Had a great experience with staff, I changed something half way through about one of the ingredients, and she was totally cool to change the ingredient and replace it with salad.. and a lot of seating space too if you're planning to go with a big group!
Very poor service, we ask for few extra things on our pizza and they forget and cook half way, they r doing again hoping this time come good.

We had a great time taking this tour! Michael is very knowledgeable about the city and kept us entertained. I was very impressed by the sites and ghost stories associated.  It was neat to stop into a couple of bars for a quick drink break.  The verdict is out on the bone lady, as she wasn't on the tour but did allow us to check out her shop. I expected more voodoo stories but enjoyed the ghost stories. The name of the tour is misleading. Definitely go if you like creepy historic stories.

Just got off the phone with Steve, very unfriendly, short  on the phone.  When I said Good morning..he mumbled something.  When I asked if he was having a good day, he replied back obnoxiously saying its a Monday, we are busy.. what do you need.   Here I was the one stranded needing tow service because of car issues and he was the one acting like he did not want to deal with having to provide the service.  Never again.

Wonderful French style bakery.  Stunning desserts that look like works of art.  Macaroons were splendid.  Simone delivers great tasting treats, but they will not be everyone's taste.  The mixed reviews are understandable.  St. Louis does not have the great bakeries as most other cities.  this place is fun and unique.  Worth a visit to experience something far better than grocery store gooey butter cake and the normal St. Louis fare.

My wife and I went here tonight as part of our anniversary.  As a man of a, ahem, certain age, I spent most of my childhood standing in front of video games.  I was glad to have heard about this place the other day.  I walked in, went straight to Paperboy, and was back to breaking up street fights and dodging careless drivers in no time.  Oh, how I still love that satisfying sound of breaking glass of non-subscribers' windows while tending dutifully to my devoted following of loyal Sun readers!!  And look out for that damn cat!!!  


But I digress.  This place is awesome.  It's like walking into 1985 all over again.  A couple dozen vintage games, all in emmaculate condition, and a few pinball machines as well.  Great bar.  Welcoming staff.    They even have a modern air hockey machine and a couple of VR games thrown into the mix.  Best of all, it's non-smoking!!!


And, just like in the 80's, there are wise guys who make dirty words using their initials on the high score board.  (I plead the fifth.)

Now, if they ever get "Spy Hunter," "Elevator Action," and "Hard Drivin'" I'll run down there to put my quarter up.

Great experience.  Although I'm on the record of not being a big fan of "counter service" (order at counter and find a place to sit on your own), it works for this casual breakfast place.  We went on a weekday about 10am and had many places to sit.  Tea is brought out in a French press which is cool and the well-steeped tea is great.  My build-your-own-hash was delicious and my friend raved about their "Prisoner Muffin" (which is an egg within a cornbread style muffin).  Service was excellent and friendly.  A must-go breakfast place in the main part of Downtown Santa Barbara.

I will first start by saying that the service here is some of the best I've ever had. Friendly, knowledgable and there for anything you ask for immediately without being over bearing.
Now to the food, we started off with the antipasto, a weekend special, and it was amazing. Prosciutto, mortadella, sharp provolone, stuffed peppers and many other things, marinated in a delicious oil, it was perfect. 
I got the porterhouse steak special next topped with Gorgonzola and an amazing steak sauce. Cooked veggies and mashed potatoes on the side, it was perfectly cooked and everything went perfect with the next thing. My girlfriend got the lasagna which had the best mozzarella cheese I've had, and the sauce was also amazing. 
We got the Tierra massou finally and that was perfect as well. 
Between the perfect food and the great service I would highly recommend this place to anyone.

Got the banana split, chocolate glaze and mocha donut. Chocolate glaze was very rich and I don't like too rich so it wasn't for me but the banana split was delicious. Didn't really taste like a banana split, more like a cream puff flavored with a lil banana but I liked it. It's about $2 per donut
So so so nothing special not a lot of vegetarian options and even the ones they have are not that good

Overall, my experience was quite positive. I was very impressed with Karis, the salesperson. He was very professional and knowledgeable as well as being a pleasure to talk to. He answered all of my questions and returned my calls and messages promptly. Similarly, the crew that did the actual installation was wonderful. They worked very hard, and were friendly, courteous, and respectful of my home. Also, the price was quite reasonable, and they had a variety of financing options available, which was very attractive. My only complaint is in regard to scheduling. It was hard to pin down a date for my installation, and even after it was agreed upon it had to be changed. In addition, the borough inspector found a problem that needed correcting and it took several weeks to get them out again to take care of it, and it required more than one phone call and follow up on my part. But this is a minor quibble overall. I would not hesitate to use them again.

Amazing food!! I ate here about 3 or 4 times and they constantly knocked the ball out the park! Everything I've gotten from here has been amazing. From the grilled cheesesteak to the blackened steak and shrimp quesadillas. I love this place and I definitely plan on becoming a regular.

Great authentic high quality and fresh tacos. Owner bet me that these would be the best I had ever had, and I  lost the bet they were that good. 

Better that the other popular taco shops in Indy. Definitely the best tacos on Keystone by far. And even better than the tacos I had in Mexico. 

Decor is simple, plenty of parking out front, and the menu is nicely priced. $2 per taco. And they come with fresh meat, 2 tortillas, and their salsa is made fresh daily too!

I truly believe New South Ocean is one of the better Chinese restaurants in a 5 mile radius of Flourtown.  I think some reviewers may mistake the lower sodium content, as less flavor.  I've never had their sushi, but after reading some of the other reviews, and seeing the amount going out the door while waiting for my order - I think I will in the near future!
I'm always on the hunt for a tasty dairy-free latte and theirs (almond/coconut milk blend) is definitely one of the best in Nashville! Will definitely be back.
Veggie pizza is the best. They have a lot of different choices to choose from . Olus if you want something different then what's on the menu they will make it no problem.  Best pizza in the area.

My husband and I stumbled on this place one night as we were driving around aimlessly looking for somewhere to eat. It looked slow and we were hungry so we popped in to check it out.

The place is pretty large with a bar area on one side and a dining room/sushi bar on the other. We were promptly seated in the dining room and shortly a waitress came to offer hot towels and take our order. We had appetizers (LOVE the gyosa here!) as well as a number of sushi rolls. 

It isn't the best sushi I've ever had but the service was quick and courteous and it definitely is at least an 8 out of 10. We've been back several times since then and Wasabi Lakeview is now our go-to sushi stop, at least on weeknights when we aren't looking to venture out of the neighborhood.

We've been waiting to try Livery for months now, but waited for the crowd to settle down first. Unfortunately they do not take reservations. We got lucky and arrived about 6 o'clock on a Saturday. We were sat immediately, however the people that joined us later overheard the hostess say it was an hour wait after we got there. I recommend going during the week or earlier in the evening. They had valet parking, which I would highly recommend so that you aren't wasting time finding parking and walking to the restaurant. Livery is stunning inside. There are a lot of different rooms and a ton of windows. However the one down side to Livery is that they only have ONE one-stalled bathroom! At 6pm on a Saturday night, that makes it pretty miserable. Our server was great and kept drinks refilled the entire time we were there. She greeted us quickly and took our order quickly as well. For appetizers, we got the Mexican street corn and the cauliflower. The street corn was absolutely amazing as well as the cauliflower. The sauces that came with the cauliflower were really well flavored and went well with the dish. My husband got their take on a Cuban sandwich and really loved it. Cubans are his favorite thing and he definitely was not disappointed. I got the Manchego salad and added chicken to it. The salad was big and had a ton of flavor. My brother got the queso empanadas for the table to share and OH MY GOSH. They are incredible. Stuffed with a ton of cheese and served with beans as well. So good. For dessert we also got churros. The churros came out warm and served with a caramel sauce which was delicious. The food all came out correctly and within a good amount of time. Definitely recommend! We'll be back!

Taste of Music City.   More like Taste of All the Mediocre Touristy Restaurants in Music City.

The wife and I arrived on time to receive our free our passes we won through Yelp, which was AWESOME and we are grateful to have won the passes.

On to the even itself.  

Lots of local vendors of all sorts of variety of foods (though most seemed to go cheap on the event with simple variations of lots of mexican type dishes etc) 

So I skipped the free chips and salsa for the most part and tried a variety of dishes from various places.

And sadly literally NOTHING stuck out to me.   I couldn't tell you the name of any of the food that was great (though I wanted to try Sopapilla's but the line was way too long the whole time and pregnant wifey was on a hunt for something in particular (Gelato))

Now the Drinks and Desserts are what did stick out. 

Nothing Bundt Cake.  Some lemony cakey thingy.  Damn good.

Legato Gelato.   Burnt Sugar gelato with some kind of bourbon brittle.  Damn good.

And then there was Popcorn Sutton's Whiskey and Lemonade (my friend for the day) as well as Heroes Vodka (surprisingly really good for a non vodka drinker here and I believe 40% of proceeds goto to Veterans, which is an awesome thing).

Some of the beers were pretty good, but didn't try but a few (AssKisser Stout was a good coffee-y tasting flavor).

Otherwise there isn't much special about the event.   If I had paid $50 a ticket I would have vowed to never go again because they literally grabbed all the touristy places a true FOODIE would never or rarely go to, for the most part.

The drinks and food made it a fun place to be for a random last minute event for us and we would go back, but not if we are paying for ourselves to go.

Thanks again Yelp for the tickets, I do appreciate the opportunity to go and don't want to sound ungrateful for free food and drinks.

My wife and I had dinner at Maynard's on NYE and were really impressed. While the service was a bit slow, the food more than made up for it. And although the dish we had (cassolette) was a bit strange--it was basically a big bowl of meat: duck leg, and sausage on a bed of pulled pork and beans--the individual ingredients were amazing. The HOUSE-MADE sausage provided several enjoyable burps throughout the evening. Overall, a great experience at a wonderful Tucson gem!
Dropped in late in the day to get a taillight bulb replaced. They squeezed me in and in less than an hour we were legally making left-hand turns with a functioning blinker. Cost was only $18.

Less than one star! This place lied and said we didn't answer the phone. It took 2hrs for them to tell us they were busy. I will not use this location again. Even if the manager tries to give us coupons, horrible customer service.

Leaving hungry. My fish was undercooked, floppy, gloppy and bloody. The Royal Street Salad with bacon, mild blue cheese and delectable herb vinaigrette was delicious - if overdressed. My husband's YaYa Gumbo underwhelmed with lack of spice. Our waitress was a tad snooty too. Cool old school dark wood decor and long bar. If I were you, I'd go somewhere else!

Revisited the Depot for a 5th time last night. The place was packed but we had a reservation so no worries. Once we were seated, it took about 15 minutes for our waiter to come over and take our drink order. This was after my husband went to the hostess stand to request a server. I was afraid the whole night was going to go that way but luckily I was wrong.

The food was excellent as usual. The menu had something for everyone in our group from the vegetarian to the meat eater. Food came out in a timely manner, hot and delicious.

The building is gorgeous. I highly recommend a reservation on weekend nights.

So this place was a great find. Service; quick and friendly. Food came warm and prompt. Environment; inviting, quaint, and fun. Very clean, and bright lit. 

Had a chance to speak with one of the owners. She was very nice and fun. This place goes the extra mile to give its customers fresh good food. No food is kept frozen, all fresh. The grind their own meat for burgers. The bake their own bread and all the baked related goods in house. The soup is made from scratch and I had the clam chowder and it was fantastic, like butter the clams where not over cooked. The sandwich was packed and very tasty. The bread was light, airy and soft, like biting into a cloud.

  The soup and half sandwich deal is a great value for lunch. 

The owner told me they would soon be changing the menu to add yet more choices. The menu was already huge, but I would love to come back and find out what gets added. If you are local to this area you must come here! I came from TX and am jealous to not to have such a place closer to me. You folks are lucky to have them!

Taste was decent. Nothing compared to the so philly tony Luke's.  Sandwiches are half the size of the original tony Luke's and priced higher. Love the so philly tony Luke's. Won't return to the maple shade location

This is one of my favorite restaurants in NOLA!  I come here Everytime I'm in town.  Such sweet people who work here and incredible food!  Best charbroiled oysters I've ever had!  Also on that list are the frog legs.  They don't take reservations but were able to seat our large group of 15 w/o any issues.  Thank you Katie's for always being a culinary highlight to my NOLA trips!

I used to love George's Wings. I ordered from them this weekend and it has gone downhill. Their boneless wings aren't good anymore. Giant pieces of chicken and the chicken is gross. Too much breading and drowned in sauce. The girl at the counter was extremely rude to us as well. I'm disappointed they were one of my favorite places but I will not order from them again.
Lots of fun... the MC was very funny and very inviting.  Not a karaoke bar that you have to be able to sing to fit in.  Mixed crowd but not uncomfortable

If you are looking for an amazing burger look no further than Burger joint! Best burgers in edmonton. I order the build your own burger with curly fries and the awesome sauce. It is our go to burger place. Awesome food!

I hate what I'm pleasantly surprised. I had excellent service, excellent food and a great time. Rodalee was my server. I got to learn her name she got to learn mine. Excellent experience. Pork Chop Heaven. Enjoy!

Another Thai place in SB?! We had to go try it.

We went on a Wednesday night and the store was adaquately packed. We were seated right away and the service throughout the night wasn't that bad. We ordered the creamy crab ragoons and the pad thai.

There are reviews here that were raving about the ragoons, and honestly, I liked them a lot! They're pretty good. However, I usually wouldn't order it because the meal itself was so big. 

The pad thai is good; not the best I've ever had in SB, but it tastes just right. Ask for a spice rack to spice it up. I really enjoyed it.

I also had the thai tea, which came in little mason jars, and was pretty inexpensive.

My items added up to ~$22 including tip but it was a good experience!

This is the go to place for your staff Christmas Party. Amazing, stellar service 5 stars and 5 stars for the great tasting food. The demi-glaze is so delicious. Our staff had the best time ever and we cannot thank you enough to the staff especially our ever so accommodating and very professional restaurant manager who went above and beyond to help us with the event. Our dental office's christmas party turned out to be a great success! Thank you to Seorak and team!!
This place is awesome. Try the black eyed peas. This is one of the nicest BBQ joints in the city. I can't wait to come back.

Although the name is super-corny, it's very fitting.  They do, indeed, sell More Than Just Ice Cream.  I've been here a bunch of times now for sit-down lunch and really enjoy it (the front is just a counter, but the sit-down part is in the back).  Very small, casual, laid-back dining area (but nice).  The servers are always really friendly.  The place always smells fabulous (obviously).  I'd say the prices are generally "reasonable."  Most of their food has a "home-made" taste to it.  Their hummus is very yummy, and I always get a grilled cheese sandwich, which sounds simple, right?  Oh no, my friend...  the bread they use, which i *think* is honey-wheat, is simply out of this world.  Maybe it's just me... but that there's a tastey sangwich.

OK, now about those desserts... Obviously, the ice cream is yummy.  duh.  Their apple pie looks horrific, but from what I've heard, it's amazingly good.  The main thing to know is that their portion sizes border on obnoxious.  So, either bring a friend and share, or make a dessert your main entree.  Cause ain't nobody gon' eat dat much.  It's kind of annoying, too, because it's not like you can take it home with you... (well, i guess you could... but wouldn't it get all runny and melty and gross?).  My fave is the brownie sundae.  Good God, ya'll... 

Two complaints:
1)  I noticed that the food (not the dessert food, just the foody food) tends to take forever to come out.  I know it's because everything is made to order and cooked right there in front of you in the kitchen, which is nice and all, but if you're in a bit of a hurry, as I am when I'm on my lunch break, you may get held up and a little annoyed.

2) Horrible music on the speakers.  Last time we went, it was a bunch of Cher techno-remixes, and the time before that, en entire CD of Jennifer Lopez.  Not that it's blasting or anything.... but still annoying.

Those two complaints may just be coincidental... things that only seem to happen when I'm there.

I use body cycle as part of my ClassPass.

This place is good for the beginner to mid-level spinners. 

However, if you are trying to get a hard workout in, I'd suggest Flywheel.

The instructors and staff are friendly and helpful especially when you first start out.

The equipment at BC is a bit dated as well as the sound system. I'm a spinner that really gets going based on the bass.

My wife and I spent a three day weekend in January at the Plaza Beach Hotel and could not have been more happy with both the location, right on the beach, or the hotel itself! The hotel is very clean and well cared for as was the room we had. The hotel staff was very helpful and friendly. The pool was beautiful and warm. Being right on the beach is a great plus because it make s going for morning walks and evening sunset watching so easy.  Every detail was just right and we will go back next year for more than just three days! 

Can't wait to go back!
Found this quaint diner looking brother breakfast.  I had the cinnamon swirls French toast and it was delicious!  My waitress Inga was awesome!   This place is worth a return trip!

Had lunch here the other day.  Not bad, but I've had better. The Makhani Chicken was a little on the tough side.  Loved the Chana Masala, Saag Paneer, and the salad was crisp and fresh. The naan was ok, but they didn't have mango OR tamarind chutney. This was a major disappointment for me. Nevertheless, the Ghulab Jamun, Kheer and Chai tea were all okay.

It was my first time here and it was pretty decent. I'm definitely a fan of sushi and I thought the sushi was super delicious! The rest of the food was just okay - the chicken I had was very hard and I only had a few bites of it before throwing it away.

The servers were very attentive and nice, but one server was bringing crab legs to a table, which I thought wasn't fair cause they got all the crab legs lol. But overall, it was a pleasant experience. They had a huge selection of food from sushi to desserts which was definitely pleasant.

The one thing, I would complain about is the lighting. First, my boyfriend and I were seated under an orange light which made the environment a super weird color, it was just plain weird to be eating in such strange lighting. The other thing would be the lack of lighting in the food area near the ice cream bar, it was just so dim. 

Overall, it was definitely a pleasant experience and we will probably make another trip in the future.

Once again, Charter has lied about when they would put in a new line so our TV could receive a good signal.

This company has no idea what customer service is.

I try to taste boba drinks every where I go because I'm a boba enthusiast, so when I saw that there was a boba place by the movie theaters I was going to, I was a little hesitant but was down to try it. 

Going into the store the girls where on their phone laughing and didnt even greet us for 5 minutes straight until we went up and started ordering. 

I got a jasmine green milktea while my friends got a matcha milk tea. When my friends got their drinks, the matcha green milk tea was a different green. It was like a candy apple green and the taste was even worse!!!! It had no matcha flavor at all! Just tasted like straight up candy. it was so sweet but the boba was chewy so thats at least the only good thing. 

the Jasmine milk tea, was already pre made and had a slight taste of jasmine but also, straight up sugar. All in all i dont think i'll ever come back to this place and you shouldn't either!

The best thing I had here was the red velvet ice cream cake...actually one of the best deserts I've had in a lonnnnng time :)
I had the BBQ shrimp which was good, but the shrimp was flavored as well as the shrimp rem. app that I shared.  That app was sooo flavorful.  The granny salad was perfect and the crawfish crepe was good too.  The service was really good, the chef came out and greeted our party.  I'd def recommend the red velvet and the BBQ shrimp if ya don't mind getting ur fingers dirty.

Two words, FALAFEL BUFFET.  I know that also sounds like thunder thighs buffet, but hey, some buffets you just have to try. Every Saturday there's an Iranian/Mediteranian buffet.  Falafel, Kabob, sometimes curry, Its awesome. During weekdays the food is always cooked and seasoned wonderfully and its a great experience every time. 

This family owned restaurant is such a good addition to our community.  Its hard to find a restaurant where you have contact with the owners in every experience. This place measures up as they have several times made special orders for me and comped delicious soups and appetizers. 

Its a must try for all Reno-ites.

Celebrating its 25th anniversary in 2015, Broad Ripple Brewpub is known as Indiana's first brewpub.  The Brewpub looks like a typical English pub on the inside with dark wood paneling, a tin ceiling, and even a fireplace.  Plus, it has a large patio that can seat up to seventy people during nice weather.  Broad Ripple Brewpub has a diverse menu and several of their own beers on tap to compliment nearly anything you choose.  They offer various starters, salads, sandwiches, burgers, pasta and classic pub entrees such as fish and chips and bangers and mash.  Thankfully I scanned the entire menu as the very last item on it happened to be pizza!  

Broad Ripple Brewpub has a few of their own pizza creations to choose from, but I ordered a more basic sausage and pepperoni one.  My pizza ended being much better than I expected for something listed last on their menu.  The thin crust was cooked in a way that it allowed it to be somewhat firm but not charred, and I liked that.  It had a good amount of cheese without me ordering extra, and I also liked the way it was cooked to a golden brown.  The sauce and meats didn't stand out as much, but there was nothing wrong with either of them.  If everything listed on Broad Ripple Brewpub's menu before the pizza is even better than it, then I need to have many more meals there and I recommend others do the same.  As a cheese lover, I had to sample their cheese curds in addition to my pizza and will say that they were pretty tasty, so I haven't found anything I don't like on their menu yet!

New Orleans is a fantastic food town. You'll find it hard to find bad food at any of the restaurants. 

We stopped here on a suggestion from a friend and I'm sure happy that we did. 

 I ordered a Po-Boy with sautéed shrimp, bacon, and jalapeño. Add. to this all of the great Po-Boy toppings and you have quite a sandwich. It was full of flavor and had a nice little bite with the jalapeños figuring prominently in the dish. 

My wife had a roast beef Po-Boy that was seasoned just right for that NOLA taste. 

The Creole House also had a fantastic and attentive waiter who kept checking on us and definitely deserved the tip that we gave him!

This is a great little diner....discovered it by luck...in a little strip mall...daily specials always....family business...nice customers all around...ive had breakfast twice and not disappointed
..my husband had a Rueben..cleaned his plate..

Came across this restaurant from my news feed on Yelp and bookmarked it for a later date. Well it was dinner night and my wife and I decided to choose this place for the night. The restaurant is kind of in the middle of nowhere but don't let it fool you- the food is great.

We were waited on by a new girl who had just started that was very sweet and nice. We both had a lobster roll but mine was cold and my wife had a hot one which were both excellent in their own way. I thought the price was high though for what you get. We also shared the chowda which was probably the best we have had and that was worth every penny!

We noticed another table having the twin sisters which were 2 lobsters with fixings which seemed great for the price which we will try next time. 

Don't know how often we will come here as the prices are high but you get quality food!

You can also purchase lobsters and other seafood here also if you would like to make it at home.

Last night me and my Pham went to Joey B's on the Hill to enjoy dinner together as a Pham.  So I walked in all buff and ripped and such, if I did not have a shirt on they will most definitely still serve me because I am so uber ripped and yesterday was abdomin day where I just worked on my abs.  I ordered a Caesar salad to start but the salad dressing was really strong so I did not eat all of it.  And frankly the salad itself was all that great, I should know I am vegan certified.  Then I ordered a pizza  with sausage and bacon  because I enjoy lots of meat on my pizza or za for short.  The za was perfect, it was thin crust with lots of meat, cheese, and never too much sauce hey.  That song too much sauce cannot be applied to me because I like to keep it saucy.  In conclusion the za was Gucci and the salad was meh.  So I give this place a 69 hams out of 75 peppermints to keep your mouth  fresh like my fashion game.

Wow, okay, so I pretty much fell in love with this place after having their chicken glass noodle soup as it is probably the best soup I've ever had ever. It's so flavorful, fresh, and hot and it makes me feel so right and healthy after eating it. They take such care cutting the carrots into cute shapes and they include so many fresh ingredients you can add like fried onion, jalapenos, bean sprouts, green onion, cilantro and oodles of glass noodles and more. It's an amazing dish, I have to have it at least once a month. Their bubble tea is good, but it has the consistency of a slushy and I prefer the smooth tea I get elsewhere, however I love bubble tea so I appreciate them having it. The woman that works mainly with customers isn't the nicest, but the food makes up for it.

Well, the good news is that NXNW is still here.  While they've scaled back considerably, there's still interesting live music here from time to time.  The food and service, unfortunately, can be inconsistent and when it's bad it's bad.  I hope it hangs in there!
I just received a valentines bouquet they are the prettiest flowers I have ever received.  The flowers are gorgeous.

We were referred for the cookie dough egg roll..we decided to try for brunch, although I was very skeptical after reading these reviews. So happy we did not wait on the ridiculous line outside pancake pantry!
There was no wait here at 11 am on a beautiful Sunday morning. The bloody Mary's have topping choices!  I went with bacon and olives, my husband added pickled okra!  Delicious!  While the food was not quick to come out, it was time for me to enjoy my drink!
Our food was hot and delicious- my husband and I had eggs and an omelet.  My boys LOVED the Reuben and French toast!!! The hash browns were good not great. The biscuits were awesome- sweet, and definitely not dry!
The mimosa- all 3 varieties were yummy!
Dessert - the cookie dough egg roll is unique and delicious. The butter cake was very good but very sweet and rich. So if you like that go for it.  I totally recommend this place for a great breakfast. Our server was extremely pleasant and attentive. This is my first trip to Nashville, and if I ever come back I would definitely revisit Jacksons.

I went to petsmart to buy dog food today. The dog food (blue buffalo freedom- adult large breed) was very easy to find. I also bought treats while I was there and they were easy to find as well. The store appeared to be clean. I checked out with no line and was able to use my $5 off coupon.

Solid brewery and a nice casual spot to drink a couple.  View of the production floor through a glass wall behind the bar.  Friendly bartenders and the food looked pretty good too.  Definitely worth a stop on the St Louis brewery circuit.

I was really looking forward to Luke, but ended up leaving disappointed. I had heard such good things so my husband and I came to dinner on a Monday night. We were seated at a table backing up to the bar, which wasn't ideal but we dealt with it. We had two servers who were friendly enough, but for some reason just seemed very overwhelmed and unable to handle the tables they had. I had a bubbly to start and my husband had a beer. Both were fine but not special. I moved to a red wine for my meal, and it wasn't very good, especially not for the price point.

To start my husband got the stuffed oysters with shrimp and blue crab. They were very bready and underwhelming. The only crab to be found was small slivers. For our mains I had a shrimp, crab, and cavatelli étouffée. I expected more of a shrimp dish with some pasta underneath, but it was more like a pasta dish with minimal seafood. The shrimp was small and tasted like typical frozen shrimp. Like the appetizer, there wasn't really any real crab meat, just small sliver here and there. The pasta was fine but felt a tad overcooked. It honestly tasted like a pasta dish I could make quickly at home. And for around $26, that's ridiculous. My husband had the jumbo Louisiana shrimp with jalapeño grits. Luckily, his shrimp were large and flavorful. But the rest of the dish fell flat. The grits had very little flavor. 

Toward the end of our meal a very large group came into the bar, it almost seemed like a post-wedding thing. They were very rude and kept backing into not only our chairs and table, but the people around us as well. A lot of us were getting frustrated and the staff couldn't have cared less. They did nothing to remedy the situation. We left as quickly as we could. All in all, the food was mediocre and this place felt like a tourist trap, which I hadn't been expecting. I'd go elsewhere while in New Orleans.

The Brussel Sprouts! These are must. The food is great and creative. The atmosphere, though...loud. I had to raise my voice to talk to my husband and strain my ears. We were seated right next to the bar and the noise was a little ridiculous. I wanted a fine dining experience and unfortunately the atmosphere killed it for. On a better note, the service was amazing. I'd go back but with a more casual mindset.

Beautiful hotel with a lot of food and entertainment options. I enjoyed Chi (the Asian restaurant) and Oceano (seafood).

The cassino is very clean with all of the table and slot games you need, plus a big sports book. They have a lot of HUGE TV's everywhere to keep you entertained with beautiful panoramic rotating pictures. A lot of bars all around and the cocktail waitresses are fast and attentive.

I went to Platinum based on Yelp reviews and wasn't disappointed. In fact, Kristy gave me the best haircut and style I have had in literally decades. She listened to me and is clearly an expert. Platinum is reasonably priced and the staff is friendly and professional. Rachel gave a great shampoo and scalp massage, too. I'll definitely be back.

Slow, forgettable food and high prices.  We stopped in for brunch, fairly busy: 1 hour and forty minutes, and no one even apologized for the wait.  My stuffed french toast was not cooked all the way through, and my fiance's breakfast sandwich was a mess.  I was also frustrated that my meal was served with imitation maple syrup in a plastic cup, considering our meal was $30 dollars before tip (you can add real maple syrup for $2, lol).  The hash browns were just terrible, they were slimy and tasted a month old.  The food was almost as good as a quality diner, but not quite.  The space is charming, but it seems like they have far more tables than the kitchen can keep up with.  We sat near the kitchen door and during our lengthy stay you could see the kitchen staff was barely keeping things together.  It's a shame to see a small kitchen working so hard with no hope of getting out of the weeds. The army of servers was very friendly and took our order promptly.  We had high hopes for Blue Plate, but have to say we won't return and wouldn't recommend it to others.

Not the best quality today in my arugula
Salad.  The avocado was bad (gray) and yet still served on top of the salad.  Usually much better.  Staff mis rung our order and changed it from salad to wrap.  While walking out, we were stopped and asked for $2 difference.  Not very professional nor customer friendly.

As a local, it takes a lot to get me to cross the causeway and to the beach.  However, my wife convinced me to try Basimo, and I'm certainly glad that we did.  The food is fresh, made-to-order, and unique, especially in an area filled with chains and comfort food.  I ordered the organic bagel and a smoothie, while my wife got poached eggs.  The flavor of the food was outstanding, especially the blend of pepper on the greens, which sparked my wife to comment how it'd be easier to get me to eat vegetables if they tasted like that all the time.  I couldn't argue!  The smoothie was delicious, and the cream cheese was a revelation, as was the blackberry jam, which took me back to my childhood and my aunt's orchard.

Beyond the delicious food, and a very passable cup of coffee, we were taken by the homey atmosphere.  It was like visiting a neighbor and sitting at the breakfast bar chatting while they fixed breakfast.  And they treated my young daughter very nicely, even giving her some tasty grapes on the house.  We lingered well beyond the time we would normally spend in a restaurant (especially with a 16-month old).  Who could want to rush out of such a nice place?

We had a fantastic experience, and are looking forward to our next meal at Basimo.  It is definitely worth crossing the causeway for a healthy, homemade breakfast, and Basimo delivers both with flying colors.
Place is Average Wasn't to bad felt a little uncomfortable there

I went in looking for a ipod which some how when I checked the availability on line said they have it but any how when I got there I walked around for 30 minutes without anyone approaching me finally I asked a older employee where were the ipods he pointed down a isle and said " down there"...ok how do I get it if the ipods are not on the shelf. so I waited near the counter 10 minutes with 3 other customers while several employees gathered around playing and talking about their personal phone cases. so I got the attention of on of the not so bright employees and he had me waiting while he looked in the back only to tell me they don't have the ipod...he began to walk away when I had to say to him well can you tell me where can I get one from, he told me that there wasn't a available computer for him to look it up, for him to only go to the one at the desk I been standing at for the past hour that no one used. while he was looking between his personal phone which another employee told him to do since he didn't know how to work the store computer mean while he was continuing his conversation with the other employees about phone covers they got from five below..best buy have went down the toilet...

I had both of my feet tattooed by Dave. Not only do I love the way my tattoos came out (I get compliments on them ALL the time) but Dave actually made the experience pleasurable. He is really funny and talked to me the whole time to distract me from the pain. He listened to what I wanted and made last minute changes without giving me a hard time, even when I respectfully disagreed with his artistic advice. I know this is how it should always be, the customer gets what THEY want, but I've visited several other shops in Philly that were significantly more pushy. I would not hesitate to go back if I ever decide to get more tattoos!

Had the pleasure of dining here with the parents, kids, and the wife this past Sunday. I enjoyed their brunch menu: leiper's fork, a delicious egg, tn country ham, smoked Gouda and sausage gravy opened face sandwich. It was fantastic. The side items were a bit cold (breakfast potatoes) and my mother's praline banana French toast was also cold (like they cooked hours ahead of time and topped the bananas and pralines when she ordered it). If not for this, I'd have given a five star. Also the she-crab soup that my step-father got was delicious. All in all a great little slice of heaven in the Bellevue area. Crumb de la Crumb does offer great bakery items and coffees as well. I highly recommend this place.

If I could give half stars, I'd want to give 3.5 here. It's definitely not yet at 4, but more than 3, no doubt. 

I was super excited when I found out about this restaurant. Being from Dallas, one of the big voids I felt here in St. Louis was the lack of proper crawfish, so when news broke of this place, I rejoiced. After having the crawfish, I remain cautiously optimistic. That having been said, I won't rave and say this place is amazing, because it isn't. Not yet. However, I see much potential here. I got 2 lbs of crawfish, corn, and Cajun fries. The corn was sweet and juicy and perfectly soaked up all the juice from my boil bag. The shoestring fries were crispy and seasoned just right. The crawfish was good. Not great, but good. I was disappointed at the flavor. I opted for the whole sha-bang (obvi the only way to go!) and went with mild on the spice level (my general spice tolerance is pretty low), afraid that anything higher that mild would make my nose leak and my lips burn. However, the mild was, in fact, extremely mild. I tried my fiancé's top level spicy crawfish, and even that was doable. I think they could probably afford to go more heavy handed with the spice on the flavor, and really kick it up a couple notches with the heat. I must admit, though, that the buggers that were sitting and marinating at the bottom of the bag were quite flavorful and succulent, so that was a plus. Also, mopping up each crawfish in the remaining juice also helped with the flavor. 

If crawfish isn't your thing, they have crab, oysters, shrimp, and other options. Shrimp basket was fantastic; one thing I generally dislike about fried food is all the breading. The shrimp here were crisp with minimal breading, and the flavor was spot on. Interior is nice and spacious, and there is ample spaces to park. Extra points for having sinks in the back of the restaurant, outside of the restroom area, so you can quickly wash all the crawfish juice from your hands. 

I remain highly optimistic for this place. Will I go back? 100%. Do I recommend it? Yes, definitely give it a try. I am hoping that with some time, the flavors will really develop and I will really, really be mad for the Mad Crab!

Ha, the breakfast was just okay. Granted I didn't go during breakfast time really. Except the french toast, unbelievably good for a tiny place like this. Our waitress seemed hurried.. I soon learned why. What made the experience memorable was the employees blatently discussing details of drug transactions in front of senile old customers in terms they were sure no one would understand. Apparently as soon as she was done with our table she would run home and pick it up. Wondering if customers can also score an eighth for the low, lol.

Another amazing Mexican place in Tennessee! We headed into Nashville from Kentucky, before heading back to California. Of course I needed to get another chimichanga covered in cheese dip before we headed back the next day! 
I searched on Yelp and we were close to Las Palmas! 
Once again the cheese dip covered chimichanga did not disappoint. As someone who is from a California, visits Mexico often, and has lived in Texas, I have had my fair share of Mexican food. From traditional to Tex Mex nothing beats the amazing cheese dip of Kentucky and Tennessee. 
I absolutely love the chimichangas but my younger cousins all love what many restaurants refer to as the the special. Here it is called the LP Special and is rice with meat covered in the cheese dip! I want to try this next time!
Check this place out if you're in Nashville!

My wife and I recently went to Red Mesa during a brief stop in St. Pete. Though it looks unassuming from the exterior, and the interior is nothing to write about, the food here is amazing. 

We tried the fried calamari as an appetizer, and I can't rave enough about the sauces which accompanied the  perfectly fried calamari; both the chipotle and curry dipping sauces were divine. 

My wife got some fried shrimp as her entree and I decided to go with a combination platter with a taco, enchilada, and empanada. Both our meals were PERFECT. The empanada crust could make anything taste good, it was simply delicious!

This restaurant is a must when stopping in St. Pete!

There's a lot of pizza around Drexel so I thought this place would be just like the others...it's not!  A friend convinced me to check it out and when I saw their 2 slices and a bottled soda for $5 I was drawn inside.  I had the Big Daddy Bacon, BBQ, Ranch pizza and it was one of the best pizzas I've had (and I've had a lot).  Today, I just went back to get some more and they were in the process of cooking the pizza I wanted so they took my name and number and said they'd call me when it was ready since I work close enough they're even going to bring it to me!  Service at it's FINEST!

Nice wash, but WATCH YOUR VALUABLES! While the price is reasonable, and the wash is good, there is a chance stuff will be missing. I lost $100 cash during their wash. Management response - won't be responsible for what they're employees do. 

So do a cleaning before you get a cleaning from Uptown Carwash.

Had a very nice first visit here. The owner Ted, was very friendly from the start and the restaurant was busy on a Friday night the beginning of Chinese New Year. We ordered the Pu-pu platter and crab Rangoon and for dinner chef specials with seafood instead of Chinese American regulars and some fried rice. Everything was well prepared. The shrimp large vegetables crisp. The chili sauce sweet and tangy. 

We will return. The owner made an effort to visit and learn our names and ask about our first visit.

I had been wanting to try Oakley's for months (since I read about it on Yelp, thank you, Yelpers!) and about three weeks before Max was born, we headed out the whole 2 miles from our house (yes, this little gem was hiding out just around the corner for the entire five years we have lived here!) to experience the fabulousness that is Oakley's Bistro.  Tucked in a small strip mall (I know, right?  Not ideal but...it works!), it doesn't have a ton of curb appeal, but once inside, the trendy, romantic atmosphere prevails.  Don't let the parking lot scare you away or trick you into thinking this is a cheap dining (as bistro might let on).

My husband and I were seated promptly on a Friday night on a cool summer evening in early August.  It was a great location with a view of the whole dining room AND the kitchen (like that!).  Our waiter (I can't remember his name but his girlfriend had just recently had a baby) was prompt, polite and recommended incredible choices from the menu.

I do remember arguing with hubs about which appetizer to get, but we settled (and by settled, I mean, I got my way) on the Lobster Waffle.  We had to try it, after all - who puts lobster in a waffle?  All I can say is ...wow.  Heaven in my mouth (I am writing this review SOLELY for the waffle, I won't lie - you MUST go there now and get it).  It came in a skillet, hot out of the oven, full of a deliciousness I cannot fully describe!  Large chunks of lobster, an incredible sauce all mixed together with some amazing veggies IN A WAFFLE!! Who knew?!?!  I certainly did not, but let me tell you, I could have eaten another for my entree.

My entree ...while good, was not as delectable as the lobster waffle (but I suppose, I may have blown the load on the appetizer!) :).  I got the Fettuccini with veal meatballs.  It was good, but a bit on the salty side and I am a HUGE fan of this particular spice, so I was a bit overwhelmed.  I thought the sauce lacked SOMETHING, though at the time, I could not place it.  I would not get it again.

My husband got the Duck and Duck and he thought it was great.  I went to try it and he nearly stabbed my pregnant paw with his fork before allowing me a (small) bite.  It was mouth-watery and delicious.  I was incredibly jealous of his meal.  

We skipped dessert.  Our bill was still out of our pre-baby budget at right over $100 with tip but I absolutely enjoyed my "last supper" and would definitely go back!!

I recommend Oakley's for anyone looking for something unique, original, small and intimate in Indy.  Great for a small group (maybe 4-8 people), a third (hello - home run, boys!) date, or a nice girls' night out.  They have a wine list that I did not partake in but was very interested, and I think that if you have the money, you should spend it here instead of a typical chain hell hole that encompasses the roads of Indianapolis.
This place gets how to do it. Online ordering, with tip included! They show up when they say they will. The food! Great sushi for a perfect price. Just love this place.

We made a reservation to go here with our children on Sunday evening solely based on the high Yelp rating. Disappointing is an understatement. The $13-15 price for three bites of pasta is absolutely ridiculous. They stated that they were meant for tasting. In that case, either lower the price or provide a somewhat larger portion. We were flabbergasted! The food overall had a good flavor but was consistently over salted.The waitress was friendly but mostly stood over by the kitchen and chatted with her cohorts. Getting her to get us a check or for more water was impossible. Definitely not going here again.
Love this place!! Amazing French toast with Caramelized bananas and great omelets as well. Very nice atmosphere and great service... Will be returning often.
Great place to bring a girlfriend, the view is pretty spectacular!

VERY disappointed in the service here  ! My daughter and I walked into the store and were ignored by the girls holding the little carry bags. As we walked around the store we passed many ladies holding the little carry bags and still were not offered one or even asked if we needed help. Alas, we actually didn't need a little carry bag after all because we walked out and headed straight for the MAC store.

I was craving sushi one night, but it was late in Chinatown.  My options were limited, and I opted to try Mixx Asian Bistro.  I called in an order for pick-up, including a spider roll, tamago nigiri, and a few more rolls to tally my bill to approximately $30.  To my chagrin, there were no other customers in the restaurant upon my arrival... despite Chinatown being alive and kickin' until upwards of 2 AM.

Well, it was the worst spider roll I have ever had.  In fact, all of the rolls were horrible.  I've had better "sushi" in pre-packaged containers from the grocery store.  The rice was dry and inconsistent, but boy was there ever a lot of it!  The tamago was also dry and lacking of any sweetness.  I should have just scrambled some eggs myself and slapped it on rice.  The remaining rolls aren't even worth mentioning.

I was left with a bloated rice stomach, an insulted palate, and a lingering feeling of regret for flushing $30 down the toilet.

I will never come back to this restaurant.

I had an enjoyable dinner her I sat at the bar to watch the Warriors win the NBA finals. The wild mushroom with balsamic was a great appetizer and it went well with a black butte porter. The bar staff were very attentive and made good recommendations. For my main course I kept it simple with a nice burger, some of the other entrees looked interesting too. I would not hesitate to eat her again.

Not happy. When I ordered a beer and chips and dip it took 20 min and I still had no chips and dip. Finally I told the waiter to refund my money. 5 more minutes to complete that. The entire time the manager, a short haired blonde females with glasses I could hear explained the entire thing. She never said a word to me. Poor management and organization.

I can't understand how this place has such rave reviews.

Maybe it is because I came in the middle of the day?

Maybe I have bad luck?

Maybe I checked into the wrong Spoon Me? GPS fail?

Anyway. The place looked so drab and actually dirty. The one girl who was working was nice, but not so apologetic when she told me they were out of fruit and a few other things.

There weren't many flavors to choose from, or toppings for that matter. I must say though that the quality of froyo was better than that of the place in my town, but the toppings were kind of sad. 

I will be back most likely since it is near my work. Expect to see better next time.

This place looks a lot nicer than it actually is, unfortunately. It's also priced as if it were a nicer restaurant.

I just ordered soup since I wasn't all that hungry to begin with, and it was just ok. My friend, however, ordered a full entree for $26 and she said it was subpar at best. The fries were soft and the schnitzel didn't have much flavor. It was a $30 fried meal basically. The staff also seemed inexperienced. They were nice though. 

I know we didn't have to order what we ordered. Maybe if we had ordered something else, our experience would have been better, but overall we weren't impressed.
Best breakfast in Indy. You always get something different as the menu is always changing. Go early since it can get busy. And it's the best orange juice I've ever had.

The food tastes like it was seasoned with water and the turkey may as well have been jerky. The food was well below subpar. I know this is a local hot spot but I cannot figure out why. . I usually don't mind waiting for excellent food and service, but never again will I wait 30 mins in the rain for pancake pantry. Do yourself a favor and skip it, especially if you're price conscious. Outrageously priced for the meager offerings.

Loved pretty much everything about this hotel. Our room was beautiful and huge - more than enough room for two friends crashing together for the weekend - and free wifi and bottled water were welcome perks. The daily buffet breakfast - also included in the rate - was actually really tasty: all the standard continental fare, such as yogurt, cereal, pastries, juices, coffee, tea, etc. PLUS eggs, bacon, sausage and grits. You can dine inside the buffet area or at one of the tables in the courtyard, which I recommend if weather permits. 

All in all, it was a terrific experience. Bar attached to the hotel is great - lovely little mini courtyard where you can sip drinks and watch the world meander down Bienville. 

For a location in the Quarter so close to Bourbon Street, you can't beat the quality, value or price. Plus, it was really, really quiet for being that close to Bourbon Street. Bonus for when we had worn ourselves out and really needed to crash. 

Oh, one more thing. Well, two. One: there is a small mini-fridge in the room for personal usage (not filled with anything already.) Loved this as we stocked up on extra water (don't get big bottles, they won't fit) and our morning (and evening) Red Bulls at a Walgreens just two blocks over. Also - there are quite a few electrical outlets scattered handily throughout the room, and even the ones in the lamps worked - a rarity, I find, in hotels. 

Lastly - there's a jar of fresh, delicious, chocolate-dipped madelines at the front desk. YUM.

One thing to watch out for: If you're staying in a room surrounding the courtyard, the staff tends to adjust/pull the metal tables into place for breakfast early - nothing major, but metal-on-brick screeches were a bit annoying at 6 AM. That said, it wasn't a big deal given every other positive - I will totally stay here again.

This thrift store is gross. Everything I saw was tattered and dirty. I saw a rack selling underwear...UNDERWEAR. I can only assume they were used because it's a thrift store. All the people looking through the racks were coughing, hacking and missing teeth. All the busted up furniture was over-priced like an employee was wanting to take it for themselves and knew nobody would pay those ridiculous prices. There was a glass table with fabric chairs with black stains all over it for $150. You could pick up better in a back alley somewhere. The only thing I might buy here are CDs or DVDs.

I had some electrical work done, a new garbage disposal installed and my Pella glass storm door which was locked in the closed position repaired. Lynch Maintenance Service did an amazing job, on time, professional and courteous. I will definitely use them again!

I found this place on Facebook. I love a good Cuban Sandwich so I figured why not try one that is "Authentic". Beautiful day when I went. Sat outside, ordered my sandwich and was super excited. Got my sandwich looked good, but tasted awful. The au jus or whatever it was, wasn't that great. The Sandwich was bland as well as the sauce. I have had a better Cuban Sandwich at 14 West. Sorry Tata but I won't return.

Epic fail.  15 minutes after we ordered, we received the smallest 13 dollar cheesesteak I could even imagine.  13 dollars you say?  Oh yes, they charge a dollar for exactly 3 pieces of long hots, and TWO dollars for sharp provalone.  And their "traditional" size is so cute and little.  Like it is a kid size.  
Now, mind you, we are Tony Luke Oregon Ave customers.  We go there instead of Pats and Genos.  
This sandwich went in the trash.  It was greasy.  The meat was cooked weird.  It was stacked weird.  The onions were disgusting.  Now, this was at 7pm, not 1:30 AM.   Clearly the grill was not hot enough, and the cooks were not good enough or didn't care enough to fix it.  The roll was bad.  I can't believe my wife and I had to toss this in the trash and look for other food.  But we did.
The worst part? OK, the sandwich was the worst part.  But the next worst part?  We talked to the manager.  He apologized and said he would keep an eye on the guys on the grill.  But didn't offer us a re-done sandwich or a refund or anything.  He saw us throw it in the trash and did not make it right.
Tony.  We have talked to you at your stand in South Philly, and the restaurant across the street.  If this is what you think of South Jersey, stay on your side of the river.  I can get a sandwich like this for a couple dollars at Wawa.

So there isnt much great to say about this location popeyes there is usually always an issue with condiments. Not enough ketchup NEVER any strawberry jelly (because yes not everyone loves grape). But the main reason that they get such a poor rating is because i dont think i have ever been there and the staff didnt have an attitude all the way up to the manager! If you are traveling and leaving out the city to head towards Ms then may suggest another popeyes because you may get hot fresh chicken or you may just get the wrong order as i have a few times. They get two stars instead of one because when the order is correct and fresh the food is good!

Good food. Indian in Bryn Mawr, yay! I had Malai Kofta, which didn't really seem to have much cheese for "cheese dumplings" but were nonetheless delicious. My girlfriend had mango chicken (on the special bryn mawr menu) and it was delicious as well. 

I've had better naan but this was perfectly acceptable. tamarind and mint chutneys served with it were good. 

decor is somewhat cheesy but that doesn't matter. service is just fine. 

lots of families with kids there when I went. 

They deliver! and there's no fee (according to the website) so a meal + tip is pretty much the same price whether you go to sit in or order delivery. Seeing as how I usually end up spending way more than I intend on delivery food I think I'll try this next time and get better quality food than pizza or bad chinese for probably a similar price.

Also I definitely plan to go to the 9? dollar lunch buffet sometime!

I was referred to Authorized by another mechanic who didn't have the expertise (or tools/time) to repair my car. That was two years ago and I've been coming to him ever since. Mike is an incredibly nice guy and is honest. I'll keep coming to him in the future.

Amazing!  Have tried Piezanos several times since their opening and have been consistently impressed with the quality of pizza and other food there.  The crust is chewy, the sauce is lovely with a nice spice to it, and prices are awesome.  They also have a good selection of nicely prepared salads to feast on prior to the carb over load.  This is a great new option in Tucson!  Keep up the great work.

PEPPERMILL RENO OVERBOOKS THEIR ROOMS AND THEN FORCES YOU TO ACCEPT A DOWNGRADE WHEN YOU CHECK IN!!!! YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED!!!!!
DO NOT STAY HERE UNLESS YOU WANT TO RISK IT!!!!!

I will try to explain just how bad the customer service is at Peppermill Reno. I have never been treated so terribly at a hotel before. I booked a Grand Spa Suite a few days before my stay for two nights. I had booked it online, but before I did I had called to confirm that I would get one of the remodeled rooms and non-smoking, and was told that the front desk was very good at accommodating me. Great, but not so fast. When I get there is when I get the slapped in the face by their hotel staff. Upon check in, the little fucktard does the whole typing on his computer really fast and you could tell he's up to no good. I was nervous I was about to get bad news, and I was right. He proceeds to bullshit me about how they don't have my requested room anymore and that he would offer me a $50 "discount" and put me in a much downgraded room. Nothing close to what I reserved and paid for. Not even a non-remodeled room, not even one that was a smoking room of what I reserved. The way he put it was like he was doing me a favor or something.
