One this to beware of is the bathroom situation, they have 2 unisex rooms, one in the front of the bar and one in the back.
The hibachi experience is amazing! The place get pretty crowded, expect long waits if you have no appointments on the weekend nights.

Marathon was ok, but nothing spectacular.  They have a nice $20 for a 3-course dinner deal, which made it extremely affordable.  However, I opted for Chicken Noodle Soup and the Buffalo Chicken Sandwich.  The veggies in the soup were cooked perfectly, as were the noodles and chicken.  However, the soup had no flavor and there was too little noodles, veggies and chicken to the amount of broth.  The chicken sandwich was delicious though.  I also had the spiked apple cider, warm, but it wasn't that great.  Service was ok, but I wanted to order my soup first so that the sandwich wouldn't come out too quickly.  My waiter assured me to put in my whole order and they would time it appropriately, but as I suspected I was only two spoonfuls into my soup when my sandwich came.  Overall, ok, but nothing more.

St Pete's beach was very nice. The sand for the most part is very smooth (there are some rocky areas). Parking was super hard, but I guess that's just how it is for most beaches. It was $2.25 an hour. The parking lot was around the 46th Ave cross street across from the Publix/Chase shopping center. DO NOT PARK THERE!  They will tow. We didn't park there but it was tempting. Then we saw the tow truck taking out cars and we knew to not even think about it. We got there around 2:30 pm that afternoon and the sun was still out for a few hours. Then we watch the sun set at around 6:23 pm and it was beautiful!  A view with no obstruction. It was absolutely stunning!  I was there with a friend who does acro yoga and was able to take a stunning photo of them with the sun setting behind them. It was awesome!
Food has always been delicious.  All of the food comes with a generous amount of meat and seafood, unlike some other places who fill the container with mostly vegetables. They are quick too.

I'm a fan of Nawlins Creole Cafe.

I loved the food, but found portions were on the small side.  I left feeling like I had a good representation of New Orleans cuisine and wished I had a tad more though.   This restaurant is family owned and spawned from a successful catering business.  Mama Nawlins is always on site with someone in the back working their voodoo that they do, which I've found to be consistent each time.

The fried oyster, shrimp, and catfish are always good and lightly breaded with the right zing to take you back to the french quarter.  I've also tried the shrimp po boy on a few occasions and found it to be very tasty as well.

Plenty of room to take the family or host a Mardi Gras party.  I recommend the sampler platter so you can decide how adventurous you want to be.  Menu is kid friendly.

They also offer Seafood Saturdays and from time to time, they offer all you can eat Catfish.  I would place them as good contenders with the contemporary Yatz or even the "new comer" Mud Bugs (Carmel), if you are familiar with these other cajun-style places.

Spicy Tuna Tostada and Black Garlic Wings.... YUM!! Definitely the best items under Small Plates.

Pork Pizza Dumplings were alright since I tasted more dough than the meat inside.

Brisket Ramen tasted okay too. I had high expectations because Brisket and Ramen are both on my top 5 but the broth needed to be hotter and noodles tasted like Top Ramen.

Impossible to reach anyone on the phone.  If you call to speak with a doctor you get told that a nurse will call back but when they do, they don't leave a message.  If you call them, prepare to be on hold for 45 minutes on the phone and for noone to answer at all.
Omg this is a great place! Donuts are soft & amazing. Lovely bread. Hope this place stays in business for a long time!!

I love this store but not as much at my dog.  It's his favorite spot for treat.  The selection of products are fantastic.  Most wonderful about Doggie Style would have to be the staff.  Everyone is professional and friendly, especially the manager Mike.   Mike is very knowledgable, friendly and helpful.  He was a great addition to the store.  I was sad to here he is leaving.  He will be missed

I'm sitting here eating breakfast. The orange juice tastes fresh squeezed - delicious! I ordered the eggs benedict with much hesitation. They are made with a sriaccha hollandaise and placed on Belgium waffles. I was fearful they would be too spicy. I can't stress enough how perfect they tasted! The breakfast potatoes were equally as delicious! I highly recommend this breakfast! The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because there were crumbs on the seat and the hostess wasn't friendly.
The wings were good. The loaded baked potato fries weren't. The fries were soft and the bacon was bland. I will go back for the wings, but next time I'll try the tots.

I preface this by saying I came in at 9:30pm which is 30 min before the place closed.  I had ordered the Jambalaya for 15.95.  It was very poor and tasted bad.  On the wall was a Zagat sign from 2004.  My guess is they have been slipping for past 12 years.
A bit pricey but delicious! I love the constant rotation of flavors and all the toppings. Oh so many toppings to choose from.

I recently used Pizza Mizza for a meeting I held in Santa Barbara.  The pizzas all 10 of them were delivered on time and were fantastic!  The manager told me exactly how many pizzas I needed and helped me pick a good variety to cover almost everyone's possible diet needs.  I will use them again for future meetings!

I like this place! The staff is always nice. They don't take to-go orders which is really inconvenient for people who work in the middle of the day and want to just stop by and pick up an order. They are kind of pricey compared to the HUB, which is a coffe place I love.

Other than that the coffee is good and so is the food.

So I had never tried Quinns and then my window cleaning company, Boise Window Cleaning, took them on as an account and then my wife and took some suggestions from their staff. 

my wife loves the Shrimp Fettuccine and I really that as well in addition to the Philly Cheesesteak sandwich - both excellent choices!

Great BBQ!  Just moved up from the States and heard about this place from my husband's co- workers. 
Definitely worth the drive from Edmonton. Everything was fresh, the meat was tender and moist.  Our big family had everything from ribs to brisket to pork sandwiches, and everything was great.  Super kid friendly and the owner and his daughter were wonderful. Glad we're moving to the area- this will be our go- to BBQ joint!

I feel bad for giving a small local place a bad review...but it was that bad :( I will say the guy at the window was super friendly and nice. But the taste of the meat was so foul I had to spit it out. I've never tasted anything like it. It wasn't a burnt or smoked taste...I honestly don't know what was going on. I ordered the BBQ nachos and it was cheap and a huge portion but I literally couldn't swallow it. Also I am pretty sure they use canned pork n beans or something very similar. I threw the entire container in the trash and made a sandwich for dinner :-/
Love this place. Simple food, really fast service. I just hope they open one up in Carmel so I don't have to drive so far!

This is a place for tofu soup. If you haven't tried it, this is the place to start. It equals the best in NYC (I have not been to Korea...) Sizzling hot and delicious. If you like soup, do not miss this place.

For under $10 a bowl, served with piping hot rice and pan chan (small side dishes the Koreans serve with most meals) it is an amazing value. My wife and I order two bowls and take home half of one most times. For $25 including tip you can have a dinner unrivaled anywhere. Plus this place is BYOB with no corkage fee.

The atmosphere here is quite sophisticated. The restaurant is decorated with primitive Korean farm implements -- most look like they belong in a museum. It is quite beautiful, yet very relaxed. What else at these prices.

They have Korean BBQ too, but I have not found these dishes up to the other places in the Korean section of North Philadelphia (see Seo Ra Bol)

I think this place is over priced and unless you have a coupon, it's not worth it.

Most times we call for take out and most often put on hold.  We use to try and get delivery, but the delivery time they quote is always outrageous so we now opt just for pick up.  

Last time I ordered a salad, which they put in the bag with other hot food.  I certainly didn't want to pay for an already overpriced side salad that was wilted and warm because it was sitting with the hot food.  

The hot wings were unimpressive, small and not worth the $$$ we paid.

The  bright spot is the pizza.  They have interesting toppings and I do love the BBT.

For the money I think there's better places to go.

I think I'm over Natural Cafe. The other day I ordered my usual SB Veggie Grill, and realized it no longer comes with the tahini sauce. It's just grilled veggies on brown rice. When I asked what happened to the sauce the employee said it now costs $2 extra.  It's already $11.50 for the plate (grilled veggies and tofu on a bed of brown rice). Unless there's something about tahini being super expensive that I don't know about, I don't get why you would take away a sauce from a menu item and then charge for it. I think that's bad business.

This is a great place to eat with family or friends. The restaurant is very attractive and they have a menu that should satisfy everyone. The only drawback is that were obvious: The restaurant is poorly lit which makes the menus difficult to read. And the wine list, while extensive, is overpriced for offering very common wines which could be purchased at Walgreens.

Wow, I can't believe I've been working in Brentwood this long and have failed to eat here.  I haven't really explored the full menu so I'm judging solely on the burritos.

You can choose from a 10", 12" or whopping 15" gargantuan burrito.  My wife ordered the adobo chicken and I tried the asada.  I have had so many mediocre meats from other burrito places, but the meat here was packed full of flavor and tender.  Also, I like how they throw the burritos on the grill and throw some type of cheese on the bottom that I've never seen in other places.  It was late, and I was in a hurry so I didn't take time to inquire.  One warning as far as toppings.  The chopped peppers are not jalapenos but fresh serranos.  If you don't have a high spice tolerance, be careful adding those to your burrito as they'll have your sinuses cleared pretty quick.

I can't say enough about the freshness and quality of the ingredients.  I was jaded by the whole burrito craze but Chile Burrito has got me craving those things again.

Visited this restaurant last night and Michelle served us and she was OUTSTANDING and please sit her section if you want great service because I will. I guess I need to mention that our dishes were really good as well. 

We visit this spot several times and it's always pretty good. Usually it is pretty busy and have to wait but this time we walked straight in and was seated but as we were leaving there were a wait. I highly recommend getting there prior to 7 pm especially on Friday.

Cheap and delicious food! You can't go wrong with that. The food is good, however they cook your eggs in a microwave. They don't really have a real functioning kitchen.  If it is busy, don't be in a hurry.
Couple of restaurants here, not enough though considering this is an EATING ASS TOWN!!!! Try again!  Maybe with the upcoming renovations they'll get MORE NICER EATERIES that represent N'AWLINS!!!!!

So happy my husband did some research and I didn't go somewhere else. I had a 2 chips in my windshield, 1 small but the other was rather big and when I took it to Safelite they told me there was absolutely no way it could be repaired and I would have to replace my entire windshield.  Shawn repaired my windshield that I was told would be impossible and it was about 4x cheaper than my quote from Safelite.  Very prompt on responding to my request and setting up the appointment and the whole repair took about 30 minutes or so.  Great business, trust all the 5 star reviews!

We really liked it here. The place isn't huge but it allows you to interact with the 25+ cats.  Super sweet and caring staff.  There was no kitty smells and comfortable for all.  They had people filing in and everyone was happy.

We look forward to going back.
Nothing about my Vesuvio pizza wasn't yummy and yet it failed to blow me away.  pizzeria Vetri is still the best at trying to make an amazing pizza, especially where the crust is concerned.

It's a fun place to eat. The food is yummy and the attitude is awesome. We used to just come in for the fish, but now it's just as much about listening to Brent make the customers laugh. A good time..

Yes,

I got it, the price tag might be a little on the higher end of thigns (especially being in Goodlettsville, TN - but it is worth its value 10 times over because the food is simply just beyond delicious.

I came here for a friendsgiving and I was wowed beyond belief. Everything from the best Turkey, best mashed potatoes, and best pumpkin cheesecake I have EVER HAD in my life is from here (don't tell my mother please... luckily she doesn't use yelp).

The decor can be a fancy cafetaria like if you want, OR it can be casual family dinner table away from the house, if you make some arrangements.
Once again a great meal. The biscuits & scones are fantastic. Turkey with curry chutney sandwich is a great sandwich.

Where to begin!? Kiel came highly recommended to me by another Santa Barbara photographer who was already booked, a blessing in disguise! I wanted to give my best friend and her husband photography for their wedding gift. Kiel was very wonderful to work with from the beginning! Photography is not just taking pictures, in my opinion, it is the essence of capturing a sequence of moments and memorializing them forever to retell a story. The angles and the lighting variations he captures really embody the essence of the variety of special moments in a wedding. Kiel is also kind, professional and easy to work with. He is prompt in his responses and turned amazing photos around in a relatively short period of time. To anyone who is looking for a photographer who really knows his art form, I would strongly recommend Kiel. Added plus?! He is fluent in Spanish as well!

I wrote a review on this place before about how the pho soup tasted inauthentic and very watered down. Well, after that review the owner of the place messaged me and said all type of things. She said I must be wrong because her pho is the best of the best, even better than all the places in Vietnam. I lived in Vietnam and I know what is a good, authentic bowl of pho is. Her garbage pho is nothing compare to the pho in Vietnam. So this owner needs to get over herself and a reality SLAP! LOL Secondly, based on the message, I can tell that this lady is very argumentative. I don't think her pho is good and my review reflects my opinion. There is nothing you can do to change my review. So stop messaging me and threaten me to change my review!

If COFFEE is  what you are after, this is the place. Real pure bean varieties well brewed and at the right temperature. I miss the old locations. Now you can find Passero's on the concourse at Suburban Station and in the Wanamaker Building. The service is quick and friendly.

Very friendly people and we were promptly seated for our 7 pm reservation.  It took a little while for someone to take our drink order but after that things started to hum right along.  The food is very good and the dining room is very attractive. I'd definitely return on a future trip to Tucson.

I took my car there Sunday and noticed new scrapes and rubbing off of the paint on the right side rear door the next day. This was not there before I took it in. The scrapes were long and indicative of a brush or a rock on a piece of towel.

Update to my original review: the Sparkling Image regional saw my review and was thoughtful enough to give me a call. He said he might be able to help me. I went back in and the crew waxed my car. The waxing and cleaning really helped reduce the appearance of the scrapes to the point they were hardly visible.

It's totally worth the hype! 2 things you need to know up front that I didn't find mentioned in hardly any reviews:
1. Cash Only, they do have an ATM
2. Parking, this is in a residential neighborhood, so parking is a challenge. We parked in front of Mojo's (great place to grab a cup of joe before or after).

Orange juice was fresh and delicious! Shrimp n grits were fantastic! I love the shrimp and grits at New Orleans Cake and Bakery, but these were incredible too! Totally different tastes, so they can't be compared. It's the rosemary that makes these so incredible. The hubster had Banana Foster french toast, which everyone talks about. He said it was really good. The kid had a side of scrambled egg. All the plates were cleaned. 

As for the decor, someone mentioned it scary the kids... That's crazy! The decor is really cute, in fact, I loved it! It reminded me of Dia de los Muertos decor. Totally innocent and colorful. I should've bought one of the little houses! I forgot about them while I was there.

Def recommend.

Amazing pizza- great casual atmosphere- awesome people!  Called ahead and our pitcher of beer was waiting for us on our table.  Pesto chicken and chucks special pizza where unique and wonderful!  Meat lovers  18inch was a highlight for our group of 12 as well.  Quick cab ride from the nugget!

Ate here a couple of weeks before Christmas after receiving a gift card.  I've been here a couple of times before.  Free pie Wednesday is good.  There's just a lot of restaurant choices so I don't eat here often.  We happened to be here on all you can eat chicken tenders night.  I didn't know they had that.  Anyway, my wife, son and I all got the tenders.  My wife ordered the regular, my son got chipotle and I requested the Nashville hot.  My son loved the taste of the chipotle.  My Nashville hot was okay, I just didn't like how it was soaked in sauce.  It made the breading soggy.  I should have asked for it on the side, but I didn't expect it to be like that.  I prefer Nashville hot to be more of a seasoning in the breading and not a wet sauce poured over the tenders.  I ate most of it, but some was just too soggy so I scrapped off the breading and ate the meat.  If you like very hot then O'Charley's Nashville hot really won't satisfy you.  It was spicy and had some heat but not really hot.  If you're familiar with Buffalo Wild Wings the heat level of O'Charley's "hot" would be in the range of BWW's Caribbean jerk.  The all you can eat tenders meal is a great deal.  With all of their specials throughout the week, and great coupons they mail, O'Charley's is a really good deal.  Good rolls and butter, good pie and a good deal.

I love this place! Christine gives me great pedicures and she's so personable! I brought my five year old to get a pedicure with me but instead she got a pedicure and her nails polished. I got here at 8:30 am (which is when they open on Saturdays)  and both of us were finished by 9:30 but I stayed a little longer to make sure that my toes were perfectly dry! This is only my second time coming but I recommend them to everyone. They've gotten busy every time I've come so make sure to come early. The wait doesn't seem long though because they have enough people working! Give them a try if you can!!!

I have a teething 8 month old that was keeping me up all night and I decide to get her a Baltic Amber Teething necklace!  Of all days to decide, it was a Sunday and the Nurturing Nest was closed.  :(.
These ladies went above and beyond to help me get a necklace that very same day, even though they were closed!  And my daughter has been her happy self ever since we put her necklace on!! 

My only complaint is that they're in Reno and not Carson! ;)


I look forward to  going back and checking out  all their other awesome  boutique items and maybe even attend a few classes!!

Really interesting and tasty pizza, but either they don't have enough help OR they have the wrong person on the phone. We needed delivery as we are sick and we live 10 minutes away. The woman on the phone said, "I'm not sure if I am supposed to take this order", so my husband got irritated and told her he would come and pick the pizza up. She hung up on him. When he called back, he simply placed an order and she took it. We will think twice about ordering here again. I must emphasize that the pizza is good, but nothing is good enough to put up with a grumpy rude order taker. Employees need training!

I have been here twice and was displeased both times. If you like cooked sushi swimming in too much mayo-based sauce, have at it. Neither time did it taste fresh, and more than half the rolls are deep fried or cooked in some way. The menu is enormous, and yet none of the signature rolls sound appealing. Don't bother.

The food was cold and disgusting.  The waitress was rude. We were supposed to get a glass of wine but we didn't.  The worse experience I ever had.  I would not recommend this tour even if it was free.

Had this pizza walking by on Frankford and Girard. The toppings were really fresh and the crust was amazing! The crust is really important and they do it right. I talked to the owners Ben and Lauren while I ate my slice and they really seem to care about making good quality pizza. It tastes like its from a restaurant but its quick and easy out of a truck. They have an awesome blue and red truck, you can't miss it.

I'm a beginner building an aquarium. The owner helped me get set up with some substrate for next to nothing. They had a ton of beautiful fish, and I'd like to go back when I start getting into saltwater/marine aquariums.

Vince is excellent, and I appreciate what's he's doing for this community. I recommend all my friends to go here, since the service industry can do a number on anyone's body. My results have been fantastic, and my lower back pain receded after one visit.

Leigh Anne makes the best cakes! I received one this year for a surprise birthday cake and she hand painted each detail. So beautiful!. I also buy my kids birthday cakes from her. She pays attention to detail always!

This was the worst dining experience of our entire trip to New Orleans.  The place is in a great location and looks fine from the outside, but the food quality is just NOT good.  Maybe it's because we had such great meals everywhere else while we were in Nola, but every single part of our meal was a disappointment.  The service was ok... a bit slow, and not terribly friendly.  I had a PoBoy which was just... lousy, and my wife doesn't even remember what she has (not because we had been drinking; he hadn't.  Just because it was terribly forgettable.)  

There are many other FAR-BETTER places to eat while you're in Nola, so please take your money there instead.  If you are considering Cafe Pontabla, INSTEAD, go down the street to 1109 Decatur and eat at Coop's Place, which is a much better restaurant with great food and great atmosphere!

Roundin' Third is awesome. It's a local bar where you can have decent conversations with people you either know, or know someone else who that person is related to. The bartenders are very friendly and people can actually carry a conversation here. There is a pool table here so you can shoot some pool with a few quarters. 

Since this is a Goleta bar the prices aren't so bad. I was shocked when I ordered two beers and I had to put money back in my wallet because I took out too much. This made me proud to grow up in Goleta. I will definitely be back sometime the next time I am in town. Thanks Roundin' Third!

-Tej

Um.  Okay.  I really don't understand the 1 star reviews.  I was just in there today helping my mom get a new phone to replace the relic she'd been using for god-only-knows-how-long.  

We went in and the music was a little too loud for her liking... so, I asked someone if they could turn it down, as my mom struggles with ambient noise, making it difficult for her to hear whoever is speaking to her.  The woman I asked smiled and, without hesitation, immediately went to the back to turn the music off for the duration of our visit in their store.

Then our guy came to help us and he was friendly, informative, and patient while we went back and forth over whether or not to get the iPhone or another basic phone for talking and texting.  Mom decided on the iPhone (yay!) and we were outta there shortly thereafter.  

Definitely a pleasant experience overall.  I mean... it's a phone store, folks.  They have to deal with needy, indecisive people all day, everyday.  Lighten up.

Wow!  Truly loved this place! We went before a show at the Fox, and had a wonderful spinach salad, Dillpickle soup, and sandwich. And the ice cream - - to die for. Thanks to Nathan for being such a great server! We will be back.
I sure wish buffalo shrimp was back on the menu, it was most definitely a 5 star item.  Please bring it back

A local favorite and food staple and I can see why!! I will be honest and go ahead and say that I am not a big fish spread fan, but this place has some very good fish spread!! I also partook of their cheeseburger and it was an excellent choice!!! The open air environment was very nice and I will make sure to come back here when I am in the area!

My fiancé and I were down here from NY for the week so I could go to a workshop for work. We ventured in early in the week (had to after seeing the menu) and has Jason as our server. He was awesome, Very engaging (we're used to colder folks back home), funny, and was an excellent server. The food was amazing (especially their prime rib!) And the beer (fiancé LOVED the PeckerWrecker) was incredible. Honestly, the service alone was enough for us to come back and tonight we did. This time we sat upstairs (the interior of this place is amazing) and had Rockett as our server. She was, of course, incredible. She was funny, attentive, and gave us each a big hug or two before we left. I digress, the service alone is enough to keep us coming back (next time we're in town!!) And the food and drink is just the cherry on top of a fantastic dining experience. 
Jane has definitely made Cool Springs Brewery a hidden gem for locals and out-of-towners alike.
We will most certainly be back and have already recommended it to others.
Y'all are just damn awesome. :)

This place takes hipster to whole new level.  It's just too over the top in terms of breakfast offerings (they don't honor any food exceptions and they don't even offer a standard eggs and bacon option).  Everything is overly complicated, and takes about 3 looks to actually understand the menu.  I ordered the tofu salad, which was just blah.  My friend ordered the chocolate waffle - he said it was very chocolatey, but didn't have much else to say.  The service was slow and inattentive, even though the place was only a quarter full.  While I appreciate the great environment and decor, this place is just too over the top for me.

This place was quite a surprise for being so close to the French quarter with a ton of tourists in the area.  The place is huge with a lot of seats so you shouldn't need a reservation unless its a special event in the area.  The prices were pretty reasonable and they had a 3 course menu for 35$ I believe.  There were some items we really wanted so we just decided to order off the regular menu.  We started with the duck pastrami sandwich and the alligator dish.  Both were really good but the duck was AMAZING! The sauce and flavors of this dish were out of this world delicious.  For my meal I had the duck breast and it was really really good.  The duck was cooked perfectly.  My husband got the redfish and he really liked that as well.  I tried it and the fish was super tender and flavored nicely.  
Overall I was pleasantly surprised with this place and may come again soon!

Some of the best sushi I've ever had. Loved the scallop roll, so creative. It was all delicious. Small restaurant, great atmosphere and not astronomically priced. If we come back to the area, we'll be back!

I used to come to this place all the time when i was in college. I loved it then, i love it now.
It has been remodeled and looks nice and new. I got the spicy tuna bento box. The sushi was fresh. The noodles and tea that they give to the table are sooooo good. My friend got the general tsos box which was also good.
The beds are comfortable. The motel is very clean.  The staff is very friendly.  The cook really has really done an amazing job.    He made us to feel very welcome.
Apparently some sort of miscommunication on the coffee thing, they have a new machine ready to go now I'm told
Great baked goods, especially their birthday cake! The dense, buttery frosting and cake w/ the fruity pebbles or whatever cereal it is embedded inside is so delicious.

Lee How Fook is certainly a hidden gem. It is located on the edge of Chinatown, surrounded by a number of good Asian restaurants. It is absolutely worth trying. The quality of the food is note worthy. Their General Tso is some of the best ive had in recent memory. It isn't greasy AND it tastes good.The atmosphere is very mom and pop. A good place to go for 2-4 people looking for good chinese cuisine. Keep in mind that the place literally only has like 5 tables. Its super small. Not the best chinese but definitely worth trying, its good!

I apparently left a review on my last visit. That was almost 6 months ago, and even though I remember my service being crappy the first go round, swearing I wouldn't return, we decided to give it another chance. My opinion of this place has not changed... A sunday night dinner, with only a couple of tables seated - service still sucked royally! I did notice a sign posting for employment but with the minimal amount of people in this establishment during tonight's attempt it cannot be that they are understaffed. My only recommendation for them would be to hire experienced waiters/waitresses.

We ordered a lot tonight and have a few suggestions:

Spicy Scallop roll - excellent!
Spicy Tuna roll - excellent
Shrimp Tempura roll - good; will ask for less fish eggs and substitute avocado instead of asparagus. 
White Dragon roll - very good, but I could have used some tempura crunch and it was too much fish!
Salmon sashimi - nice pieces, but pricey too, in my opinion...

All that being said, Nippon Tei rocks.

Visited here for the first time ever today, I really liked it alot! The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because it does not have near as much variety as Whole Foods. They had some awesome deals on meat for a Tuesday, I think they have these type of specials every Tuesday. I will definitely be back!

Went here yesterday with my wife and some friends. Nice Cold Beer. the Sauces are excellent and unique, we keep them in the house ;). Had the southern fries with cheese and pulled pork, they were excellent! Good smoke on the pork and fresh cut fries. I had the brisket sandwich and it was very good. One person had the Smoked Pulled Pork Reuben and raved about it all day and the girls had the smoked Chicken salad (I had the leftovers for breakfast :), it was excellent! I am glad to see some good QUE in our area! We have also had excellent results at the Collegeville store. give it a go, you will not be dissapointed! Keep it live and local!
PS. Phil and Robyn are really great and down to earth people!

Very hit or miss. Sometimes you get a good waiter who is nice, polite and gets everything right or replaces it immidiately.  Sometimes you get a terrible waiter who is rude, doesnt want to help and doesnt do his job properly.
In any case the food is decent and the two managers I have spoken to are rude and unhelpful.
If you want my opinion the one downtown is much better.
Great food and always fast. The place is always clean. Drinks are very strong. Salsa is fantastic. Highly recommend!

This is a great meat/seafood/specialty item market. Although I've never had the occasion to use their catering service, I'm sure it is top notch and would recommend trying it. 

Harr's seems to have the largest selection of quality meats in the immediate area. They are also one of the very few places to procure dry aged prime beef. Try their specialty kabobs for a treat. While there are several excellent seafood markets in Pinellas county, Harr's quality and selection make it a convenient stop, especially if meat is the primary reason for the trip. They will happily clean shrimp for $2/pound extra. Overall, their prices are extremely reasonable and comparable to the chain supermarkets.

They also have a full selection of wines and specialty items as well as deli and both fresh and frozen prepared foods (made on site). This is definitely not a place to go when hungry. Open the door and the aromas will beckon you to step in a little further. On initial glance, it might appear to be any small market. Once past the check stand, a whole foodie haven awaits. Warning: at this point, unless you are only one of five people in the place, walk directly to the meat counter and grab a number - note the crowd gathered here - it takes a while! 

Note: if you call in your order ahead of time, there is a place to pick it up and you don't have to wait in line. It will be prepared to order, wrapped and ready for you. 

My only "beef" is that the produce selection is very limited and not quite as fresh as one would expect. For that reason alone I rated them a 4 versus a 5. I've yet to find anyone that can rival the Fresh Market's when it comes to produce.

So, if you're in the neighborhood, drop in and check it out. As I said...don't go hungry (you could always run next door to Mecca for a nosh first), look beyond the check stand and take your time browsing. I guarantee you won't leave empty handed.

My wife and I have been here for dinner in the past so we decided to try their breakfast since we were in the area. Both of us really enjoyed what we got. The service was excellent as always. We had their signature blue duck fries as an app. They were just as good as we remember them being. I will tell you that it's a pretty large portion so it can be filling for two but is probably a great item to split 4 ways. I got the chicken and waffles and my wife got the short rib breakfast quesadillas. Both were excellent.
Absolutely loved this restaurant! The service was spectacular and the food was better than i could have ever expected. Super affordable for a good steak!!!

This is by far the worse Starbucks in the entire city. Terrible customer service. Lacks in consistency with both pricing and quality of beverages. I purchased the same coffee three days in a row and each day the price was different. Some days the price was 2.16 some days 6.56! That's a big difference and don't expect them to explain why. The quality of the coffee is just meh. Taste like it's been watered down. The chai tea latte has no spice some days. The one thing I can never understand is the total lack respect for customers at this location. I mean after being charged 6.56 for a cup of Americano I don't want to listen to you complain about customers dropping king cake on the floor and arguing about who should clean it up. Do your job. I mean if they put as much effort into their actual job instead of complaining this place could be bearable strictly because of location.   Wish I could give negative stars.

we definitely contributed to keeping them in business while we were in college, living around the corner! My typical order included the buffalo chicken wrap and mozzarella sticks, which are both great.
Some of the very best Thai I have had in this country. Food was excellent; service was superb. Highly recommend.
Love this store great healthy food and treats for all pets, and they do wonderful work for the rescue. And a friendly and helpful staff
American Spirits has a good selection but likely the least friendly staff you'll ever meet. I go here purely out of convenience.
The pizza was great and the meatball sub was very tasty. Service was fast and checked in on us often. It was nice to sit down somewhere and enjoy fresh food!!

I booked my stay with breakfast for two included ($10 more than base rate). However, breakfast is NOT included! The front desk only gave me a voucher for $20, but unfortunately, the CHEAPEST breakfast buffet for two is already above $20.
The breakfast is terrible. A $5 subway or McDonald would be better.
As a IHG Platinum member, I was offered two free drink vouchers when I checked in. I tried to order a cocktail from their menu, and the waiter told me that she could only give me the most basic cocktail for the voucher. Oh now I really regret for tipping her.
I stayed three holiday inn (or express) properties during my winter trip. This one was the most expensive but the least satisfactory.

Yes, small, crowded, you may feel rushed, but this place is also one of the top reasons I live in this neighborhood. I live in between both co-ops, but this is the one I go to. What grocery store can you get kombucha on  tap, work on a farm to get a discount, and take free classes on all kinds of interesting topics? The beating heart of Mt Airy..I guess you either get it or you don't.
I'll be back for our next convention. Great craft beer selection. The twist of this place is downstairs. Full of goodies.

Pretty average Mexican restaurant. The chips and salsa they give you when you sit down are not the best. The salSa tastes straight out of a can. I will say their portion sizes are generous though, as the salad was huge. The guacamole was not good and did not taste fresh either. The best part would have been the sangria or the queso blanco which you can really mess up.

This place has been such a great find!

I started off with bikini waxes here- I was nervous after a bad experience at another salon (I'd sworn off waxes for almost 2 years after it!) Salwa completely understood my anxiety, and made the procedure as quick and painless as possible.

After some scheduling constraints, I started seeing Phoebe. She is great! They recently started offering bikini sugaring, and Phoebe urged me to give it a try. She's a pro at it, it's (in my opinion) less painful than a wax, and leaves my super sensitive skin un-irritated and bump free! 

During waxing procedures Phoebe is great at chatting (she's very funny!) and she keeps me distracted from any discomfort. Then I had a facial with her, and she seamlessly transitioned me into a very calm, spa like environment. She seemed to really know her stuff when it came to the facial, and I left very happy!

I'd definitely recommend this place- I've never left disappointed, and I've been coming here for almost a year.

I love Nola Discount Pharmacy!  There prices are amazing and the customer service doesn't get any better. It feels like such a personal experience every time I go. Ross (owner/pharmacist) always takes the time to talk with me and expresses genuine concern, and Patrick (owner) is always so friendly also. Its such an at home feeling every time you are there.

A lovely little space that offers a big, delicious breakfast......I had eggs with ham and asparagus, all incorporated into this delicious omelet, accompanied with great hash browns and a butter biscuit.  A total gourmet delight!   And the coffee was good too.  Everything was reasonably priced and abundant.  Just watch out for the biscuits  and gravy and fried potatoes.  Share this one.

This will likely become a 5-star review when I have a taste of my 2nd, 3rd or ... well, we can stop counting after that, right?

I tried their Stout (Mastadon Stout brewed for the ISM/Yelp Paleo Party) and loved it. It wasn't as 'cofee' as I expected. Instead, it brought a lot to the party (no pun intended). I could tell they put a lot of thought and heart into the brew. 

I think we have a winner. Bring on the next pint!

AMAZING!! We come to The Wildflower frequently. Whether you come for breakfast or lunch, all of the menu choices are fantastic. Everything is fresh and flavorful. Don't forget to check out the bakery items before you leave.

I just left build a burger at Green Hills a few minutes ago I had some time to kill before a movie so I stopped in to get something to eat. There were 2 African American ladies at the grill and 2 customers in the restaurant. I waited at the register for a few minutes since it was my first time there and after no one greeting me and being ignored I left and still no one addressed me. I went to Jonathan's next door. What a terrible and sad experience. If you are losing money its because your staff is awful. I hope you correct it. I can't see myself going back.

Ninki has all the intentions of trying to serve Japanese food.  However, it falls short of that, amongst other things.

While its location is what brought me here, it is not AT ALL what you expect to see when you walk into a Japanese restaurant of any sort.  It looks like a late 80's, early 90's bachelor pad.  Kind of like black laquer threw up on Japan.  No bueno.

The service was less than decent, considering it was a fair 20 minutes between visits from our waitress, who was extremely hyper and difficult to understand because of it.  Needless to say, we finally chose our Hibachi bowls (shrimp for me, steak for JTR), and then waited our "alotted" 20 minutes for the food.  Did I mention we watched a table of four (who ordered before us) get their food 5-10 minutes before us?

The food smelled great.  I was extremely excited at the look of other people's plates, but when ours arrived, my hopes immediately dropped.  The veggies were covered in butter and oil, and my shrimp was sitting very lonely on the other side of the plate by itself.  A small heap of arugala made a nice wall between the veggies and the shrimp.  The steak looked fairly appetizing, but the plate was also pretty sparse and lonely looking.  At least serve this stuff in smaller plates so it doesn't look so pathetic!  JTRs fried rice tasted like a stick of melted butter.  Luckily, I found the silver lining on the menu: steamed rice.

Recap?  I won't be back.  Proverb of the day: A Japanese restaurant's ability to not screw up a bowl of steamed rice is no reason to return.

We visited Johnson's Corner Farm when we were in New Jersey for Christmas 2016.  It was super cute and festive during the holiday season and tons of cute little knick knacks like Christmas signs, pillows, and dolls.  We bought a blueberry pie to take for my in laws when we were there.  That pie was DELICIOUS!  I LOVE blueberry pies generally and really enjoyed how fresh and berry-licious that pie was.  I think this farm would be a fun place to go berry picking in the summer (I went berry picking in central Jersey with friends back during summer 2012).  I would definitely visit again if I happened to be in that area.  Their pies are delish, their service was very nice, and it's just very quintessentially Jersey.

Beer selection.  Beer club..do 85 beers and you get a 20oz serving vs. 16 or 16 vs. 12 depending on the pour once you finish the beer club.  I don't like sitting in the restaurant part and only really like sitting at the bar area because it has the TVs and the large windows.  They have one really stupid seat right behind where they take your name when you arrive (if you've been there and actually sat there you know what I'm talking about). Food is consistent (yes I've had better pizza), but this isn't bad at all.  Hoagies are pretty good and they're oven toasted.  They often give you surveys with your receipt for $5 off your bill on the next visit. Groupons are out there sometimes too.  Atmosphere is great in the bar area.

I went here with some coworkers while visiting Philly for business. It was pretty empty when we first arrived but could have been due to the weather. I had the chicken kabob with samosas. The samosas were pretty decent, had a nice flavor with the cilantro sauce. The chicken kabob came with rice and a side salad with a ranch dressing. I am personally not a fan of ranch but I guess this is the only option for salad dressing. The entree came with bread that was very good. As for the kabob, I would recommend asking for spicy. It gave it an added flavor that really made the chicken taste better without being overly hot. The rice was a bit dry like others have mentioned but they do add a tiny bit of sauce too. The kabob could have had more onions and peppers. I only got two small pieces for each kabob. Overall, if you are hungry and have no other choices give it a try.

I love the look of the restaurant, reminds me of San Francisco.  However, the food is just not that good, and it's pricey.  The service needs improvement and they the blast music so loudly you cannot hear anything.  Gave it another try since the open, unfortunately we won't be back.

I absolutely love this place. The customer service is incredible, the food... Omg. I've never had better cucumber sauce or falafel. The pita bread is just so soft and perfect. It's sit down quality with take out prices. I never leave feeling weighed down, just energized and satisfied. Soooo much love for blue fig!

horrible customer service. tried to buy live shrimp 2 dozens. already filled my bucket with shrimp and then told me that accept only cash. I was surprised and told him I know why so many bad reviews about that pier (not credit cards and expensive shrimps $5). The guy told me he not going to have business with me and took all shrimps from my bucket back :). Very bad experience. happened 9/6/2016 ~ 4pm.

BTW. I am living in 1 mile and won't back to this place any more.

good luck !

Old World Coffee - Reno, NV

We just dined at Peg's Glorified Eggs and walked over to Old World Coffee for a little caffeine. I was in need of a quick "pick me up" before we headed to Michael D Thompson Trailhead. I got their espresso and it was paired with a shot of H2O. I've never had a coffee house pair a small glass of water with my espresso. Stumptown doesn't even do this. This is saying a lot. Old World Coffee is basically telling me that their espresso is so strong that I will need to chase it with water. I took a sip of my espresso and was amazed on how fresh, bold, and strong it was. It only took a couple of sips to wake me up and get my groove back. Old World serves an awesome espresso.  

The cafe itself is small with a few tables/chairs. The entire place is clean and the staff is very knowledgeable about their drinks. I recommend Old World Coffee.

Technically there were 2 pianos, but they weren't dueling. This place is not what we thought it was going to be. To sum it up, we went on a Saturday and paid $10 cover to get in and were greeted by what sounded like live band karaoke and looked and smelled like a frat party. We couldn't even hear the pianos over all the other instruments. I've been to some amazing dueling piano bars in New Orleans and this wasn't even in the same category.
Also, it liked like wild animals tore the place up just before we got there. Shoes sick to the bar and dance floor and the bathroom was gross.
Excellent service and the hamburgers!!We highly recommend cocktails are also wonderful and Alexis was the best!!

I LOVE THIS PLACE. I would eat lunch here twice a week if I could. As it is I go out of my way to come here. The tofu bibimbap is my go to but the menu is so healthy, tasty, filling and affordable!! The owner is so sweet and there are 5 small tables (no server) for eating in. So convenient. Go here often :)

+1 star for the Phanatic, a pretty awesome mascot.
+1 star for the yummy philly cheesesteak I had
+1 star for the Liberty Bell, altho it did not ring when I was visiting
+1 star for the freakin cute Build-A-Bear Workshop
+1 star for the under-14 gift I got even tho I was 25 y.o. then (thanks asian genes)

-2 stars for being Philly.* Go on, hate my review.

------------------------------------
* Really though, this isn't a 5 star stadium.

Wonderful. Can't say one bad thing about this place. Went tonight. Second time here with the family. Service was exceptional. I have a 9 and 7 yr old. They love it. This place has an awesome kids menu. Rolls piping hot and plenty of them. Dinner was great. I ordered the sirloin and it was cooked perfectly.  Husband had burger with mushrooms. Kids got ribs and chicken baskets. Tons of food all of it delicious.  Can't wait to go back. Best place in town by far.

Have to admit that I was a little skeptical, but so happy we gave this place a try after reading the good reviews on Yelp. We chose to eat there. The restaurant was very clean, and so was the restroom (the first place I head when dining in an unfamiliar place. Clean means we can stay. This one was spotless and the soap even smelled nice. If you care about that sort of thing.)

Service was very attentive and fast. The owner greeted us warmly, and quickly brought everything we needed. We both had lamb dishes. The meat in each was tender and perfectly cooked. The sauces were delicious. The rice was fluffy, and again, perfectly cooked. 

We certainly will be back for more.
Went with a busload from our community. Good food, entertainment and great place to mingle and make new friends. A bit of a hike, tho from the Sun City area.

Priced us $500 dollars less than they ended up charging and blamed us for the misunderstanding. Horrible communication and service. You can tell they get commissioned for work they bring in because they pointed out every minute flaw in hopes you would let him fix it. Will not return.
Food is good, prices are good. Will definitely make this a regular stop. The cocktails are always in happy hour (2nd one half price).

Portions are HUGE and the apps were delicious. Service was good too, our waiter made us laugh and was popular with my Grandmom lol I definitely recommend it for a nice family dinner out for a graduation/birthday celebration.

Came here on a Friday night right before close. These guys have a ton of opinions between the Lassis and the chaats. It does get a little overwhelming to say the least but in a good way. Had a mango lassi which was good. Chaat wise had the crazy, papri and chicken tikka. All were good, the chicken tikka was probably the one in there that I raise the most questions about. But good stuff overall will def be back.

The food here is good, not great.  It is very busy during brunch, if you arrive around 1 pm you should have no problem getting a seat in short order.  I ordered the Monte Cristo sandwich, I did appreciate the french toast for the bread but the ham was a standard supermarket lunchmeat.  My dining partner had the breakfast sammy and was happy with his choice.
If you use the Yelp app to secure a place in line, you will check in with the hostess at the time requested and should still have another 20+ minute wait.  Not as reliable as an open table reservation but thankfully they have the option.

Some coworkers brought us lucnh from here the other day and everything was delicious! We tried all the meats, mashed potatoes,  and rolls! The meat was flavorful and spicy,  the mashed potatoes savory and chunky, and the rolls buttery and doughy! Loved them!
Fantastic food, gourmet burgers and shakes - all local and organic. Our only complaint is that it's not real kid-friendly - only 2 items on the kids menu. Over all, GREAT experience!

Yea its not the best ball park anymore (was at one time) in the majors but its still pretty damn good! Old school charm mixed with modern amenities. Best spot to see a sporting event in Philly by far! Easy, but pricey parking, and usually traffic waits to get in and out are tolerable. Staff that works there are usually courteous. (Just wish they would be a little faster to get rid of the foul mouth drunks at times) Plenty of great food options, although some might suggest pricey? Try McFadden's just outside the park or Tony Luke's, Bull's Barbecue inside, or maybe even Harry the K's for nicer venue inside. I find that no matter where you sit (except in a couple spots) are good seats. Especially worth the money are Hall of Fame seats, if you can get them for good price (under 40 bucks a pop) Some even don't mind the standing room only just to be there, but the place is half empty now, so they you can usually get seats cheap in the upper decks. Shame the product that plays there stinks, but once they start playing winning ball again, I expect this place to be rockin, and once again be the place to be seen on those hot Philly Summer evenings!

I have been been to Franklin's quite a bit since they opened, probably around once a week. This includes when they opened with a limited menu, while they now have a full menu. This is where I think Franklin's runs into trouble - it seems that they can't figure out what kind of restaurant they want to be. 

If you take a quick glance at their menu, you'll notice that the prices are slightly high when considering this is the same place that has among the cheapest (and longest) happy hours that I've seen in a while, in addition to $2 Miller bottles all the time. They have Skee-Ball, basketball, and a golf game in one half of the restaurant, then they have a "regular" sit down part with the menu that I mentioned above. 

The service is great, the manager is always friendly when I'm there, and the food is good....not great. I think they went overboard on the TV's, but that's just me. In addition, they have a good beer selection (including your usuals and some rotating micros/crafts). I think they need to decide, and pretty quickly, what kind of crowd they are going after and what kind of restaurant they are going to be. A combination of a sports bar and a nice sit-down restaurant just doesn't seem like it's going to work, especially considering where they are located (an out of the way location that's not going to get passerby traffic).

If I would have written this review a few years ago I would have given them 5 stars. Basically - for the weekend - I am 'too old' for this bar. During the week (after my favorite Wednesday at the Square) or during events (like the infamous Santa Crawl) Lucy's is great. Other times, not so much. 

The best deal here are the $3 mimosas. There is nothing that helps (starts) a Sunday hangover like cheap champagne and OJ.

I am a picky eater but once it is good I can't stop giving the compliments while I am enjoy eating. Here, Guido, is my most favorite so far for the pizza with an amazing paper thin crust. Which I could not imagine how they kneading, tossing, and flipping the dough in the kitchen. 

I am sure that many many time you will leave the crust behind when you start to getting full. But I always hesitate to do that here because I love their dough so much.

Please note; if you are thinking to come here for weekend' a dinner by 6pm. Be sure you make a reservation around at least an hour before you heading here. I used to be in the line in front of the restaurant sometime for over half an hour.

Hands down the best sandwich shop/one of the best lunch spots in the city. The whole menu is great, but good luck trying to pick just one sandwich. My go-to was always the Benton Park - that being said always check out the special board right above the register before you order.

Great little local joint with a great owner who, if you come by enough, will take the time to learn your name. Agree with the other Yelpers that seating is sparse (especially when outdoor seating is not an option), but worth it for the sandwiches.

Everything we tried was delicious!!!!
Dumplings, lamb, shrimp, beets, edamame. Wonderful. Every bit of it.

Cashed in my Mother's Day gift from hubby and went out to get some lobster last night (Saturday night) .Again we got a babysitter and were out to get away from the kids.

We didn't have to wait because I snagged a seat-yourself table for two in the bar area. No kids there!

Drinks:
Red Lobster is usually the only place I can count on before I walk in the door to have Parrot Bay coconut rum on hand for a piña colada. Well, wouldn't you know they were OUT of it this night. GRR. So I tried the Sunset Passion Colada with some Bacardi O and it wasn't that great. The strawberry garnish was overripe and I couldn't even eat it. I made up a drink and ordered Alizé Red Passion liqueur on the rocks with a splash of cranberry and ginger ale. The bartender didn't think I'd like the stuff but I did...it's made with passion fruit, of course I like it!
It was nice and strong, had her garnish with an orange wedge and that was old too...I advise they restock the fruits or not prepare so many before hand as I do like to eat them with my beverage.

Anyway....

The Food:
I just had to try the lobster nachos...I'd been craving Mexican food but had a gift card to Red Lobster, so it was perfect. They were delicious! I liked that and I'm a native Texan, so that's saying a lot.

I was starting to get full though so I didn't really eat much of my salad.
I had the Rock Lobster tail...HELL YEAH, that bad boy was perfectly cooked and delicious. The bartender/server cut it off the tail for me and tried to take away the shell but I told her to leave it cuz I wanted to pick off the little morsels LOL! I almost tried the live Maine Lobster but I didn't want to do the work and it only had about 6oz of meat in comparison to the amazing 12oz of Rock Lobster tail. 

My husband had the Ultimate Feast and he was quite happier with his Maine lobster tail, although smaller than mine of course hehe, and the fried shrimp was as expected (I like mine crunchier than they do it there, but I digress),  he substituted grilled shrimp for the scampi (less buttery saucey stuff) and they were really good. Unfortunately the mashed potatoes were instant. You can totally tell and what a shame. The seafood was consistent and good, but even Outback uses real potatoes...I was better off with my steamed broccolli (which was thankfully not coated in butter). 

The woman serving us (and the people behind the bar) was on her toes all night and she was very knowledgeable on the food (how I got my weight stats above) and super friendly in a non-annoying or fake manner. She was great and so we left a well-deserved tip. I had a great time sitting in the bar area and I didn't miss anything about the dining room area...we could even see the Phillies game on. :)

There's nothing great or bad about this place.  Airy, open dining room, decent menu of pizzas and sandwiches including some veggie options.  Their sandwiches come on french bread, and they are HUGE.  Seriously just get a box with your order, I can't imagine finishing one.  The downside is no sides are included, but the hummus plate and fries were definitely enough to share.

I wouldn't seek Cafe Roma out, but if it's convenient and you're hungry, it's a nice spot.

I found my puppy chewing on the heel of a pair of [gasp!] Ferragamo black suede boots. The damage was mostly on the bottom, but approximately 1/2" of the suede-covered heel had teeth marks. The owner of this shop was very friendly and suggested he cut 1/2" off of both heels and add a thicker replacement heel, to balance it out. Worked like a charm and saved my favorite boots (which I'm more careful to keep out of harms way, now). I have since taken all of my shoe repair business to this shop, with always excellent results. The shoe/boot shines are also very reasonable and make your shoes look better than the day you bought them.

Woooow!!!! I literally just watched a video on this style of ice cream, and I must say cold stone has nothing on this place!! We stopped here on a whim after eating a huge lunch, and were so impressed, not only entertaining to watch, but beautiful representation and delicious!!!!

Friendly service team. Good location. No appt required! Get the coupon from the Fast Lane web site so the price is VERY COMETITIVE. I had the smog check done and they met my expectations. The "sign" for the shop is too hidden because the gas station obscures the view from the street. I highly recommend them.

My fiancée and I had a bad experience - like, really, really bad experience - at the northside Harry and Izzy's location.  I mean, horrible - nasty hostess, multiple service mistakes, and a pretty horrendous fiasco involving a missing wallet.  I was willing to give them the benefit of the doubt for the most part, considering we ate there on New Year's Eve.  And good lord, the prime rib sandwich was incredible.  I contacted the management and we ended up getting the meal comped so we could try again.

Well, a few months later we decided to try again, at the downtown location.  They definitely made up for the previous experience.  The food was still excellent, for the most part.  The shrimp cocktail was sinus-obliterating as usual, but the seared tuna was slightly flavorless.  We shared the prime rib sandwich, which fed us both easily.  Throw in a pair of cocktails each, and we left happy with a bottle of the house cocktail sauce.

I like the interior of the restaurant, which feels like a place where powerful people spend lots of money on things (and not in a gaudy or over the top way).  I think the steaks are largely not worth it, though - the quality of the meat just isn't there, considering how expensive the cuts are.

I would absolutely recommend the downtown location over the northside location.  It wasn't nearly as loud or cave-like, and the atmosphere was more romantic than just dark.  It's definitely a restaurant worth going to, just avoid the steak in my opinion.

I came here on a beautiful Saturday after biking all around Forest Park and dug into the salted caramel ice cream. It was only $3 and it was divine.

TRY IT!

Came here again with visiting friends and they loved that Pi has $1.50 beer sampler options, since it's the perfect size for us girls. Also, I was ambivalent about the Berkley because of the olives but lucky for me, we swapped out olives with basil and now it's the best pizza ever!

I haven't been able to stop thinking about the ice cream OR the pizza all week. So. Good.

I also rather enjoy the cornmeal-y crust, and I'm one of those who doesn't ever eat the crust!

Overall this place is too cute to miss, and the food/drinks all match up to the great atmosphere/service/ambience. It's such a great StL hotspot and I love bringing visiting friends here!

This was one of our more memorable experience, date night for hubby and I.
Star Wars New Hope with symphony was awesome.Watching the movie and the Orchestra at the same time was so cool. If you enjoy these type of performances this is very good. The Orchestra was great, sounds were right on point,beautiful arrangement. The art of music and film was amazing to watch. Thank you Nashville Symphony 
We will return.
Very good dinner of Vietnamese and Thai dishes at a reasonable price. Flavorful and presented well.

Not the best street tacos in the city (that honor goes to Nada), or even the second-best (La Margarita), but they're still great. And for the price, they're hard to beat. The rest of their menu is also good, and the outdoor seating area is swell in the summer.

HORRIBLE & Did NOT make good on paying for new door.

We just moved in to our new house and I went to put on brand new locks and handles on my 3 exterior doors.  As soon as I began to try the front door I realized I was in over my head and called Anytime Locksmith.  The kid answered (not owner Shay), came out the next day and after 4 hours had messed up, ALL 3 DOORS!!!  To the point that my garage entry door had a hole in it.  After repeated calls to the owner 'Shay', who was always "Out of town" he finally called back and came out.  He acknowledged that the doors were bad, but told me that the new handles and locks I had were only to be put on 'new doors'.  I told him if his guy would have told me that I definitely would not have had him do it.  He fixed our front door and he then agreed to pay for a new garage entry door, because of the hole his guy had left in our door.  He said all I had to do was call him with the number of the door place and he would pay the bill over the phone.  THAT DID NOT HAPPEN.  After several calls and the owner Shay being "out of town", each person took my name and the number for my new door and promised to pay.  After 3 month . . . I have paid for the door and the installation of that door myself.  I decided to wait several months to see if he would pay for the door before actually writing this review . . .  but as you can see, I ended up having to write it.  NEVER, NEVER use these guys.

You could die waiting for a prescription to be filled, they are manipulative saying one thing and doing another.  This place is a travesty.

I would give them no stars if I could.

Love this place! my boyfriend and I were at an event on Columbus and wanted to check out some area places. He wasn't sure he wanted to go, but we were glad we did! The hot donuts are amazing and the chicken was fabulous! We got the chili-garlic glaze, awesome! Sure to be back soon!

Four stars for service! Excellent waiters and waitresses. They could definitely improve in the food/brunch department. $15 bottomless mimosas were a plus. My friend had a cup of gumbo......totally needs work....the roux was great color but lacked flavor....I've also never seen chopped carrots in gumbo but some include that as a part of the "trinity" of base ingredients. The Bywater Breakfast was tasty. I subbed the potatos for cheese grits. The grits were ok but kinda lumpy and they chopped up my bacon and scrambled it wth my eggs with out asking. I ate it anyways. Lol the Rasberry jam was a nice touch. I did however get some cracklings to go and they were DELICIOUS!!!!!! Next time I will try the boudin.
First time here and loved it. Plenty of food. Great service and free soup. Food was delicious!
We had valentines dinner here and it was excellent. The meals were prepared as ordered. Service staff is very professional. Nice quiet restaurant in the heart of Carrollwood.
This place is burger heaven! Everything was delicious! If you want a juicy burger this is the place to go!

Wahoo five stars!! This place is my favorite bar on bourbon for sure!!!! The Bartenders, DJ, and  MC are Awesome! It's super fun in the daytime! Get there early for amazing drink specials three beers for $5 and buy one get one free shots and watch it start to fill up as it gets later in the day! At night its soo packed and there's like a band and everybodys dancin! I go here everytime I'm in New Orleans!! Loovvve it!!!!;)

I try to go here once a week, the food is amazing and the price is right. Food is freshly prepared and it shows. They have an amazing awards program, please don't change a thing! 

If Chipotle/QDoba could be more authentic, they still could not compare!

Their chicken al pastor quesadilla is my favorite.

In summary: Best quick service Mexican food around.

Good Niu Ro Mien. very flavorful with an emphasis on balance. Noodle can be better but soup is very good. 
Rice with ground pork can use more fattier pork to further enhanced the flavor. But never the less it is good with flavor.
Siu Xiao Bing. The dough should be thinner. and a little bit too oily.
Crispy Chicken with basil is very good! very flavorful and juicy. 
Crispy Pork Cutlet has the right balance of salty and sweetness.

Overall very authentic in flavor and I like it.
Why 3 stars? because I am picky, and they can have improvements.

I'm not sure why this pho got 4 stars overall. Reading the other reviews, I thought this would be a good place to get some dinner but I thought wrong. The pho here isn't that great.  It still puzzles me how others think it's the best pho. Out of all the pho places I've tried, this is probably on the bottom list. There was nothing great about it.  I usually order the spring rolls and pho noodle soup. The spring rolls didn't stand out nor did the peanut sauce (and the sauce is always the best part!) The broth for the soup was ok- nothing outstanding about it either. The food was OK. That's pretty much it.  

The price for the amount of food I got was a little expensive for my taste. Two spring rolls and a small soup = $13.10. I've been to other pho places that were less costly with larger food proportions. It's sort of a rip off. 

The location isn't the best. It shares the same dining area with Port of Subs. Personally, I could care less for location. As long as the food is great, it doesn't matter. The best foods usually come from little hole-in-the-wall places. For this place, it isn't the case. 

If you're hungry and looking for a place to eat, it's an ok place- but not the greatest. If you're eating out to experience great food or a special occasion, I wouldn't really recommend this place.

It is not the best pho in Reno. If it is, that's pretty sad.

Sorry, I can only give it 2 stars.

We came with the meetup.com group and the service for our table was fast, very professional and courteous - they were swift with the small plates entrees and removal- the food was so so good! Try the scallops or the frogs legs! Oh my they're lovely ! The French onion soup was lovely and flavorful and lots of cheese! Please come to this place! It's mid priced- parking is very tight- come early or drive a small car!

We've been to Brixx three times in the last couple months. We really like the food, the people are friendly, they offer call to get in line which makes going convenient. There is also a parking garage next door so you can always find parking, 

I've been eating gluten free and I really like their crust, yummy and not weird at all.

The atmosphere is great! Drinks are unique. The reason I'm giving 3 stars is because I feel like the food quality had gone down hill. The last couple times I have eaten there the food has come out cold. I guess it's better to go during lunchtime instead of dinner.

I came here on Memorial Day for drinks and appetizers! I got few drinks and the hummus appetizer and it was all very good, also really reasonable prices. Jon's might have just became my favorite in south street.

Wow! Nearly a perfect meal.

Oysters were super fresh & cheap. Happy hour $.75 cent raw & $1.25 fried. Best raw we've ever tasted & we've had our fill over the years.

Tried a 1/2 price Sasarac for the hell of it. Not my thin, but worth a happy hour try.

But Ribeye brought me back to near perfection. Garlic butter & spices made the dish. Absolute perfect steak, medium, good char. Home made Steak sauce on the side was awesome. Still dreaming of the steak.

Shrimp & grits was by far the best we've ever had. Can't describe how incredible it was. Tons of flavors all meshed into a bowl of perfection. Still thinking of these grits too.

Bread pudding was very good. Solid dessert, but second to the entrees.

A Gay Sports Bar?  Hell yeah!    I went on St. Patrick's day.  I was impressed by the bar and the friendly staff.  The beer selection is--ok but it's definitely not a beer snob place.  Weird that there's no Yuengling on draft.   
I haven't been upstairs to the lounge part yet nor have I had a chance to sample the delicious looking menu.  I will definitely be back tho.

I'll start with the positives for this place: Customer service was fantastic, the area was fantastic, and it was located 3 mins walking distance to Sambo's for breakfast (awesome breakfast). 

The negatives: terribly overpriced for what seemed like a upgraded Motel 6, the parking sucks, and there are no hotel services (valet, bell desk, or room service).

This is a beautiful hotel with all the amenities. The bar is not to be missed, but get there early as it gets very crowded by mid-afternoon. The rooftop pool is beautiful and the exercise facilities good enough.

We had a problem with the safe in our room and the staff fixed it immediately. Our room was cleaned to perfection every day. And the pillows are just awesome!

The continental breakfast was excellent. Lots of fresh fruit, which was a good way to start each day of eating & drinking NOLA style. The only day there was a line was Saturday.

The location is excellent for walking the French Quarter. I'd stay there again in a heartbeat!

As a vegetarian, it is easy to take places like the Bottleworks for granted. Schlafly's has been workin' it out in the 'wood for a long time now. The food is always above-average and the place is large and usually easy to get a table in. So, I had to ask my GF recently, "why don't we wind up here more often?" So, we've decided to try to do just that. We want to support the local-focus and very vegetarian friendliness of places like this!

The good: pretty good beer, vegetarian options (including the ability, usually, to swap out match meat on many dishes), and pretty good service with a big big patio.

I guess my only quibbles is that it would be super cool to have some more vegetarian and vegan focus on the menu (without having to ask) and the decor. I sometimes feel like I'm eating in a warehouse (the tap room is far superior on this count for my money).
Came here for the first time for a launch party.  Very impressed with the room, the staff and the food.

Absolutely fantastic! Their Pad Thai was much better than any Pad Thai I've ever had because the noodles were excellent! The honey hibiscus tea was delicious as was the Thai tea with milk. The service was fast and exceptional. Also the owner was very friendly and it is always nice to see someone passionate about their food. My only complaint was parking was a little cramped, but we figured it out and it was worth it.

We got lucky to get two seats at the bar right away.  We got there around 10:30am. The place filled up very quickly.  Before we got our food a crowd began to form and it looked like it became about 20-30 min wait.  The food was hot and delicious.  The juice was fresh squeezed and amazing.  The service was impeccable as well but remember we were at the bar.  This was perfect for a very short walk from the hotel.

Don't listen to those two naysayers (especially one who prefers the institutionally horrid Olive Garden!).  I'm Italian, I've eaten in NYC and Boston and can assert that this is quality, southern Italy Italian-American food. I've ordered all over the menu and not once have I been disappointed. When you open the door you immediately leave the dreary Florida strip mall world behind, and you may as well be back up north at your favorite, cozy neighborhood restaurant that is so good, all your Italian friends eat there.

Made a reservation last week for a party of 30, we were accommodated on the second floor which was nice and roomy. We even had our own bar and the best part that its BYOTEQUILA. The food was fresh and delicious, the staff was friendly and very welcoming. We had some vegetarians in our party and we're very accommodating to their needs. Love you Las Cazuelas. We will definitely book another party there soon.

I experienced the 80-minute Nirvana Stress Relief Massage with Kat as my therapist. Between the deep tissue and Swedish massage styles (using just the right amount of pressure when and where needed), the treatment was deeply and profoundly relaxing to my body, and the blend of herbs, oils, and essences served to soothe my mind.

Will I go again? Count on it!

Finally got to try this place after a failed dinner attempt (we arrived before 5PM but were told it would be about a 90 minute wait).  It was 4 of us meeting for lunch and we met at 11:30 to make sure we could get a table.  The table we had was half booth and half high seats.  It wasn't full at that time but it filled up closer to noon.  Our server came out and offered up water to us as we waited for everyone to arrive.

There's was a daily special to go along with the regular menu.  Being lunch, everyone passed on the rotisserie but it looks like a great way to share a meal for dinner ($60 for a full chicken  served with Rosti-Papas, tortillas & salsa).  I decided on the rosti puerco for $16.

While waiting for our food, I noticed the volume of the music in the restaurant got louder but not as loud as a bar where I was yelling to my friends and I couldn't hear other conversations from the tables around us.

My sandwich arrived and was a large sandwich filled with sliced roasted pork, chimichurri, and pulled cheese, on top of a sesame seed bun, served along side roasted potatoes.  The pork was tasty and flavourful but with the bun being a little on the dry side, it could have used a little juice.  The potatoes were really good but I wasn't able to finish them after finishing off the sandwich.

Great place for lunch, but I would definitely come around 11:30 to ensure a table.

I'd give them a zero if I could. I hired this company for post construction cleaning. They are a bunch of crooks. The owner Larry will come to you first and give you a great presentation as if you'll be able to eat off your floors. Well let me tell you when I saw these 2 jokes walk into my moms condo I already knew this job was going to be a nightmare. They use the cheapest equipment. Stuff bought at Walmart or Target. No commercial cleaning equipment. They used one rag to dust the entire place. I kept telling them I feel a film on all the furniture. Their excuse was that it is post construction and it takes a few times. Well after they left I grabbed a bottle of windex and a paper towel and the film magically disappeared. Then they used a cheap little steamer machine to clean the floors. I looked at them after they dried and they still had debris and dirt on the tiles. Again they said it was hard after one cleaning to get all that perfectly clean. Then why did Larry the owner assure me it would be perfect. They charged me over $330 for a tiny one bedroom apt that I had to clean all over by myself. WASTE IF MONEY!!!!!

Went last week for dining under the stars with my bf. We had reservations and were seated right away by a very nice hostess. 

It's BYOB so we brought a bottle of wine. We got the "monkey brain" appetizer and it was so good! If you love avocado, GET IT. We also got the fried calamari and it was ok, very salty I couldn't eat much.. 

For sushi, we ordered one of the speciality rolls (the name escapes me) (8) and the eel roll (6). Both were delicious! I love sushi and Temaki was amazing. Would def go back!
Store has developed the feel of a chain coffee shop but quality of coffee is still high. Friendly staff, fast service.

We expected a more formal restaurant, but that was perhaps our lack of planning/research.  It's fairly casual with upscale cuisine.  A friend recommended it to me.  I was disappointed, but I had been to a fantastic dinner at Ralph's On the Park the night before, so this comparison was rather stark.  

The waiter was very casual and seemed to know little about the menu.  We ordered the boudin noir.  Having lived in Louisiana during graduate school, we know a thing or two about boudin and were looking forward to it.  Must be good -- it's a John Besh restaurant, right?  Wrong.  The waiter could have told us that this boudin is blood sausage that keeps it REAL.  By keepin' it real, I mean there must have been a gallon of blood cooked down to make this sausage.
