I know that some people like this, but come on, at least warn us.  It was inedible.  My husband asked for it to be removed from the table so that he could enjoy the rest of the food.

Fried oyster salad was very good, but it needed something to take it over the top.  Like a tangy bit of cheese, perhaps.  I'd still recommend it to you for a lunch.  Maybe you could ask for a little goat or bleu cheese with it!

Raw oysters were, well, raw oysters.  They were excellent.  It was a bit of a challenge getting the crackers and cocktail sauce all together from a server.

Etoufee of blue crab and brown shrimp on pasta was very good.  If you're expecting a normal etoufee, it's not that.  But I was not (I mean, it's on pasta and does not feature crawfish).  

We like to order mineral water at dinner.  This mineral water was keepin' it real, too.  It was drinkable, but I feel like they had something to prove with all this authentic, not-what-you'd-expect stuff.  Besh, I think that if you're going to surprise people with something they are not expecting, it should be fantastic and appealing to many people.

I recommend that you go here for a lunch.  Order a salad or a burger/sandwich -- I saw them coming out, and they looked delicious.  Your tab will also be less than mine was if you are disappointed.

Ok, so we went in at 2 am after the movies and coffee down the road. I must say the food is NOT quality I asked for bacon cheese Fry's. Close your eyes and imagine this. Onida Fry's, 2 strips of sandwich cheese and 2 strips of bacon. It was a sight and tasted terrible.

For those of you who have gave this restaurant a 3.5 rating..... Shame on you!

Now that we've got that out of the way, let me begin by saying this place was awesome. The Beignets made my breakfast amazing. Fluffy dough with a good consistency. I'm from Hawaii where we have what's called a Malasada. These two are very similar pastries. It brings me to deep sadness that Beignets may have just won my heart over. I really recommend that you consider just buying a single Beignet per person. These are very filling and if you've already ate your amazing meal, you may not have enough space in your stomach to fit it in. Take a break, finish a cigarette for those smokers and return for a delicious Beignet. So as I leave NOLA with great memories and experiences, I can gladly say "Beignet done that".

Was in New Orleans for work and happened to be there during Cinco de Mayo. Well I heard this is where the locals go and every year they have this great block party. Took the trolley there from the French Quarter and it drops you off pretty much right in front. Can we say best Margaritas around??? It was indeed the strongest drink I had in New Orleans, those drinks on Bourbon even with an extra shot or two of liquor is a scam. I would come all the way here and just get two 'double cups' and ride on back to the french quarter with them.  The block party was a great experience, they had a stage and later in the evening there was a concert. I got some quesadillas and they were pretty tasty, but it may have been the alcohol talking. Whatever the case I enjoyed my visit to Superior Grill and would definitely come back when I go to New Orleans.

I recently bought my car from Zano Cars and I have to say all has been great for me! Not only did I find the car I was looking for and with low miles but at a great price. I literally shopped around town and this is the place that I found with the best prices and selection. Ed, the owner made sure I was happy with the selection I made and also made sure all was 100% with my car. I will surely buy from Zano Cars again and send my friends and family here.

They moved out to Catalina and Tanque Verde. Eaten many times- from burger, broiled fish, to steak.
Consistently delicious ribeye! Fish (broiled) is delicious and the beer battered sandwich is great- a lot of food. Sides are good, except side salad is iceberg and tiny. My hubby loves the pineapple coleslaw!
Fair/ good service- in that department they have slipped some.
Prices are good for amount of food and comparable with other steak places. It's good for a family or friends dinner out.
Lunch specials are good.

We use to dine at this restaurant quite a bit when they had a better loyalty program, and better food, price combo.  They seem to have made a lot of changes which aren't for the better in my opinion.  Service is horrible at this location, always seem to be short staffed and kitchen is very slow.  The Plenti loyalty program has weakened the value as food is way overpriced for quality.  Many better dining options closer to the mall.

If you're looking for a quick bite for lunch or dinner and are in the mood for a pizza or sandwich, this is the place for you.   They have a vast variety of pizzas of assorted sizes and can also serve by the slice if that is your fancy.   I was a tad disappointed with their salad and/or low calorie menu selections as I have been calorie counting since the start of this year.  I will say however, that they were very accomodating to a special request I made to have a sandwich offerring they make served on a salad rather than bread.

Bitter melon and chicken congee, you and me were meant to be together...

...even if the waitress checked with me 3 times to make sure she got my order correct because white people don't generally eat such things I guess.  Same waitress who told my boyfriend that there was "no one here for him" (no other whities) when he arrived at the restaurant before I did.  LOL   Everything about this place screams legit Chinatown experience, in a good way mostly!

Cheap good food fast sums it up.  And the bathroom is clean enough to use, bonus!  A regular haunt of mine, any time I find myself in the vicinity around lunch time I'll find an excuse to hit the Garden Bakery.  As for the Bakery itself, I'm not sure, I kinda think that T&Ts does it better, but I'm not a huge pastry/baked goods fan.

I've been here to drink numerous times but this was my first experience with their food...

Waitress was not too attentive and seemed lost at times. I ordered one of the lunch specials which was an eggplant parm sandwich with spinach. It was HUGE and not too bad but lacked any kind of seasoning. The rest of my friends ordered chicken tenders which came only 3 to an order for over $7 (a bit steep to me).  They also charge for soda refills! (which i now only expect from high end restaurants or at least they tell you before you keep ordering)

There are better places to run to in a pinch in the area.

I had shrimp and grits 5 times in 5 days. Luke hands down had the best cheese grits! 

Luke's is an old school restaurant but worth it!!
Great place in New Orleans to catch some great bands and have some awesome fun!

Well, Conicelli isn't perfect. But they do take an interest in their business and customers. Thanks for reading and responding, Lori. I hope my comments are helpful in providing a fair evaluation and an honest customer perspective. And thanks, too, to Dan! I received the key ring and pen set. I love them! And the car is fantastic, too!

So plus one star kudos for the after-sale customer attention! It does make a difference and is important.

The food and drinks were top notch. I ordered the backspace burger, my husband ordered the roast beef sandwich. The burger was delicious, the bread was incredible, all of the flavors combined wonderfully. His roast beef sandwich was the best he's ever had, and he highly recommends pairing it with the fried oysters. We first ordered drinks off of the specialized menu, and the bartenders were fantastic and suggested we choose otherwise. We got long island iced teas, and wound up staying for two because their sour mix was freshly made and made the drinks delicious. We will be going back there by the end of our stay.

I have written a previous review on this establishment about the the lack of appreciation the management has for business. After submission of my review, I received a juvenile phone call from Mary, the owner herself. Instead of trying to clarify what happened at the salon that day, she TOLD me what happened and BLAMED me for taking the situation the wrong way. As an owner, she is going to defend her business but there is a difference from defending and not take responsibility for what happens in her salon. I would have gladly discussed if there was some type of miscommunication if she did not attack me over the medium of the phone about how I discouraged her business on the internet. I explained to her that as a yelp member, I have the freedom to write a real review on my experience and that  I did not have to speak to her first. Speaking to her about my review was out of common courtesy. She replied by saying that I was an angry, unprofessional, and a spoiled being. She immediately hung up afterwards.

Schlafly Bottleworks is one of my favorite places to go to in St. Louis.  For being a craft brewery, their food is also very good and you can tell they take great pride in it.  The atmosphere is very causal, but classy.  The facility is very large so there is a lot of room.  They have an outdoor covered patio which is very cool.  They also have live music several nights during the week.  Their beer has been a staple in St. Louis for over 20 years.  I would recommend Schlafly to anyone who is a craft beer fan.

There's a story below, but first, time to laud the man. 

He is perfect. Every time. PERFECT. Color? Perfect! His judgment is flawless. Cut? I actually say, "Whatever you want," and I mean it; I don't cross my fingers under the smock. PERFECTION. 

Plus, he does this amazing hair straightening thing that somehow makes my mother's hair look sexier and shinier than mine.  I once -- oh, God, it might be too painful to remember, too horrible to recount, no OK, here I go -- let my boyfriend's sister cut and color my hair. I figured that she was from Portland, OR, she'd be hip, she'd be with it (to borrow a phrase from Dr. Evil). NO.

So I returned to the ever-talented, in all ways perfect Mr. James Brown and his glorious (and gorgeous) Carol. I've been going to see him since my first hair cut. And I refuse to go anywhere else, ever. 

And he's funny too.

But if you book him up and take my slots, I'll cut a bitch. Know that.

Street is an excellent build-your-own burrito/taco/etc bar that also serves a wide variety of alcoholic beverages, all great complements to their food options. Its already been said, but Street reminds me of the perfect Chipotle-style restaurant I always envision, but have never been able find.. until now. 

Street shines not only because of the fresh quality of the food, but also because the food is legitimately Sonoran-style Mexican. Refried beans, spanish fried rice, street corn, al pastor, and queso fresco, all ingredients I've longed for in burrito-babies and bowls of yesteryear. 

The price is literally no different than Chipotle (actually cheaper depending on your choice), yet the food feels real, it feels like Tucson. $7 will get you any burrito with your choice of meat, beans, and rice along with accompanying garnishes.

Some of their drinks may be a little steep, but in my experience $7 for a good Michelada is not unheard of. The margaritas are excellent, and who doesn't like a good variety of beer with their tacos. Chips and salsa are also complimentary, self-serve as a matter of fact. 

Overall:
If you're looking for high quality, fast/casual Mexican food in the downtown area, look no further. In my humble opinion, it's worth parking for. Don't pass up Street, you won't be disappointed.

I'be been to this place twice now and I'm so unimpressed. My first visit I ordered shrimp taco, the crispy shell were very burned, complete inedible. I ordered a strawberry margarita on the rocks. Overloaded with sour mix. My second visit I order a shrimp taco salad with mango dressing. This dish was edible but over priced $8.95 taco salad+ $2.50 for shrimp+ 1.00 for guacamole ( a tablespoon serving size) and I ordered a reg margarita in the rocks no sour mix, it was disgusting, I asked them to remake the drink in which they did but I had to settle for an overly sweet/sour drink. The customer service was great. However we went on a Sunday evening at 5 so there was a long wait time and the waiters/waitresses were very busy

We arrived a little early sat at the bar and had a drink when it was time to sit at our table the bartender was too busy looking at pictures on her cell phone to see that we needed to settle our bill. We ordered a small plate they were out of the main ingredient.  The we were told the specials.  It was 630 pm.  Not crowded yet, and I ordered the Prime rib which was one of the specials.  The waiter came back to tell us they were out of the prime rib.  I think when you have a special, you need to have enough of it, especially when it wasn't that crowded yet.  Food was just ok.  Music was so loud, couldn't hear the person next to me.  Would not go back!

Marvelous . One of the most unique places in Indiana! It's every girls dream and for all you guys..treating a girl to this place..she'd be over the moon! It's a very professional, intimate atmosphere. For how many people were ordering to go, we received our order promptly. I will say, it was a bit confusing walking in the first time and figuring out how to order.

Sushi for days! I have been wanting to try this place since I moved here a year ago. My expectations were meant. The lunch specials are awesome and the sushi was absolutely delicious! 

$9.99 for 3 rolls and a salad or soup
$6.99 for 2 rolls and a salad or soup
$2 domestic and imported beer
Plus a ton of other dishes at great prices. 

I needed wifi and they gave me the password right away. The service was great and the servers were so friendly. This will be a regular spot for me now!

This resort is beautiful. There are Christmas lights everywhere. There's so many things to do and see. I won't have to leave for anything.  My room is breathtaking for the price. I don't know how my sister in law got these rooms so cheap but I am happy she got them. I will post some balcony pictures just so you can get a idea of what I'm talking about. 
Now the bad. I just ate at Fuse and it was disgusting. I hope it's not an indication of all the other restaurants here. Also figuring out how/where to park was crazy.
These people need to do something about their food. Really this whole situation has killed my experience.

This is my go-to place for great boba- the drinks are great, there's a ton of variety, and the atmosphere is bright and welcoming. The workers are pretty good at recommending things to try if you're new to the boba experience. Each drink comes out to a little more than $5 with boba, which isn't bad at all! They also do punch cards, and the price ends up cheaper if you use gift cards ($20 for 5 drinks, and you can use punch cards and gift cards on the same purchase.) I get the taro snow every time and it's awesome- but they have a ton of really good options, including chocolate and vanilla if you're not feeling adventurous!
Average food on this visit July 2015.  Good was bland and not very hot.  Service was excellent.

If I could give this place a negative 10 I would. Im not writing a review just to write a review so ill make this short. The food was completely disgusting. I went with my wife after hearing somewhat good reviews and decided to go. Wow was I surprised.  1) the food is way way way to expensive for the taste. 2) I ordered the short rib that was dry, bland, and honestly uneatable and oh btw it costs $34. 3) Wife ordered the salmon that was under cooked and bland. Way to much salt. 4) the waitress was rude and not knowledgeable about the menu. I am shocked that this place has remained open for this long. Save your money and buy the ingredients from public, watch youtube recipes and make a better meal then what cafe pontes  is offering. I think the chef should consider a career change

This is the closest panaderia to my apartment, so I went in hoping to like it enough to come back. Once you walk in, you can smell the pastries and sugar, which is a good sign of how fresh everything is. They have a lot of types of pastries to choose from, and they also have a small selection of snacks. They even sell tortas and other small Mexican treats. We picked up a various assortment of pastries and treats, and our total was about $7 for everything, a very great deal! The bread tasted great, no complaints or issues there. Glad to have a spot so close that can satisfy my cravings for pan. We'll be back!

It's an old time tradition in St. Louis that everyone goes to Ted Drewes Frozen Custard stand to get custard (ice cream) concrete, or order a sundae, milkshake, etc... 

They will turn the cup upside down before handing it to you just to show you how thick it is in the cup. LOTS of flavors and combinations to chose, or make up your own.  I like the chocolate-banana concrete myself :-)     At Christmas you can purchase your Christmas tree in their lot - really!

Pretty disappointing all around. 
They double charged my credit card. 
The Margaritas are not up to par. Not by a long shot. 
The food is ok, almost decent if you're looking for a quick lunch. 
I won't be going back anytime soon with so many other better options in town.

Came here for lunch on a weekday.  Ordered their lunch special of the day, which was a portabello spaghetti special.  Was angel hair pasta with chopped up portabello mushrooms and sundried tomatoes in an olive oil sauce with garlic.  Came with a garden salad.

What's hot
- Specials.  They have daily specials, which is cool.  Nice that they're working with the seasonal produce.
- Price.  Reasonable.  You pay for what you get.
- Service.  It looks like they're family owned and run.  Very nice wait staff.  Accommodating and attentive throughout the whole meal, which is nice.  No rush for you to get out.
- Their salad isn't iceberg lettuce.  It was romaine lettuce with some onions, tomatoes, and olives.  You could tell they don't just throw whatever on there.  If a restaurant is using iceberg lettuce for their salad, that means they're lazy and cheap.  Iceberg lettuce has no flavor and no nutritional value.

What's not
- Their bread.  Some may not care about this, but dudes, bread is always important, especially for an Italian restaurant.  Doesn't look like it's fresh.  
- Too much carbs.  I know, I know...  This is Italian food.  Dudes, my pasta dish had waay too much pasta.  The mushrooms and sun dried tomatoes were swimming in it.  A colleague's chicken sandwich had such thick bread.  He ended up putting aside most of the bread, because it was too much.  

Final Answer
Willing to come back, but not my first pick.  Doesn't stand out.

Tonight was our first visit to The Mason Jar. We'll never go back. The food was OK, but the experience wasn't worth what we paid. Just after filling our drinks, the ice ran out in the drink machine. And both iced teas (both sweet and unsweet) ran out as well. It took 50 minutes for our food to arrive. Tables around us were at no time cleared off/cleaned. We were in the restaurant for more than hour; at no time did they make an effort to replenish the drink machine station. My daughter ordered the fried shrimp platter--it was supposed to come with shrimp, fries, onion rings, hush puppies, and toast. The toast was burned (buried at the bottom of the platter) and there were no hush puppies. We requested the hush puppies--they never brought us any, even though it was part of our order. While were there other customers complained about the service and food. And some left before being served.

This was recommended by the valet guy and was the ONLY bad meal we had.  We waited for 15 minutes to get a table. They put us by the open door even though we asked to be inside because it was chilly out.  Waited 15 minutes before our waitress even came around. We should have walked out then, but we thought the food would make up for it. Wrong!  This waitress kept having her table's food and drinks being returned for being wrong.  She couldn't get anything right.  My friend and I ordered the try 3, which comes out of pots and placed in bowls, so we should have been served quickly. No, we waited an hour.  Every time I saw the waitress, which wasn't often, she said it was on it's way out. When it did come out, the jambalaya was cold and the crawfish etoffee was lukewarm and the gumbo had no meat in it. What a waste of our time. Tourist trap I'm sure because it's on Canal, so stay away.

I've wanted to love Butcher & Bee, but unfortunately I can't. I had dinner here only a few months after it opened, and it was pretty good. Food was tasty, but not very mind blowing or flavorful. 

I went back for brunch yesterday, and I was really disappointed. The food took forever to come out (And I'm a very patient person), even though the restaurant was half empty. My boyfriend's eggs with lamb was good, but my chicken biscuit came out completely dry and burnt. The serving size was very small for a $13 chicken biscuit. For that price, I would've easily gone to Barista Parlor for a biscuit sandwich instead.

Great Pho and excellent crispy tofu.  They have a large menu, a bar, great food, low prices, and they take credit cards.  What's not to love!

But the mung bean pennywort smoothie tastes like a lima bean slurpee.  Not sure why others seem to be enthralled with it.

A beautiful beach and perfect for lunch ages. 

Very busy here on a Saturday afternoon so be prepared to wait for a parking spot in the lot across from Chick Fil A. They charge $2.25 an hour and you pay at the machines. 

You can beach chairs for only $5 a day. Unfortunately you can't position them near the water, only in the back. 

The beach sand is light colored, fine, and fairly clean. No seaweed spotted at all here. The water was a bit cold, but it is February. Walking into it was easy. Not a lot of shells and it gradually goes down.
Very friendly staff and AMAZING candy.  My husband and I stopped by here on a recent trip to New Orleans and now that I've run out of pralines I'm thinking of ordering more from the website :)

My boyfriend and I went to this bar after leaving a show at House of Blues. It was a short walk and an easy decision to go into the bar. It looked so cozy and welcoming. There was a fireplace and not too many people. The bartender was conversational and respectable at once. I ordered the vegetable sandwich with no cheese. It came out with cheese (a common mistake) and the bartender was extremely accommodating and apologetic. We enjoyed Moscow Mules there all night by the fire and didn't want to leave.

I would have tolerated the frozen, square hash browns, discount orange juice, canned corned beef hash and over hard (when I ordered over easy) eggs...due to the fact that I saw the diner was understaffed and each staff was working very hard to get orders out in a timely manner (which still wasn't very timely), and the fact that many restaurants are cutting corners due to the economy...

HOWEVER, when I found a course gentleman's hair in my corned beef hash this morning while dining at Von's Diner, I had to draw the line. By-far the biggest waste of $25 (my husband and I both endured this)... and I will not be returning, and I highly suggest that no one else does.

The best part of eating here are the desserts! They are fantastic. The beer (of course) is tasty and fresh. A brew for everyone. The food is good with generous portions as well. Definitely a place to return to.

I dropped off my dry cleaning 3 weeks ago. Today go to pick up and am missing a pair of pants. I guess they needed to be sent to wet clean? I wasn't told it would take longer and I think 3 weeks would be plenty of time? So I agree to pick them up later. I was then informed I had to pay for them? even though they weren't in my possession?
The somewhat almost completely rude girl told me that that's how they did it. couldn't get the rest of my stuff with out paying for everything including missing pants. No manager to talk to, don't know if ill get them back? don't know what's wrong with them? If they needed to be sent out why wouldn't they have called and said that. Poor customer service and I think I just donated cash for missing pants. I will not bring my stuff to this very expensive I only go there cause they're green cleaners again..  Lets see if my pants come home.. Part 2..

The place is really nice and the staff was very friendly. The doctor took the time to talk with my son. I waited 3 hours to see the doctor which was frustrating. It seems the wait is a little ridiculous for an urgent care with only 4 people in front of us. Overall it was a good experience just wish it was faster.

Came here for twice. The Naan here is really delicious, thick, crispy and soft inside. However, it will no provide any sauce along with the Nann, so it is better to eat it with main dishes. The butter chicken is really great with creamy sauce. The Boti Kabob, which is lamb, is very crispy but a little bit dry. Definitely recommend this restaurant for people who love Indian food.

We had fish that was bland.  The waiter-recommended fried chicken was only average.  We had to flag down our waiter (Barry) a couple of times to remind him about things he forgot.  

Overall, on our second visit to Ralphs on the Park, we were disappointed.  The food should have been much better and the service was lacking.  For the prices and the Brennan's reputation, we expected much more.

Went about 30 minutes before their closing time, & it was fairly empty. Ordered 2 #5's (500 burgers & fries & drink) got 1 spicy & 1 non spicy fries, a black/white milkshake & a strawberry milkshake. The milkshakes were so tasty. Made with local Bassett's  ice cream, they hit the spot immediately. 

Had asked for the burgers to be cooked medium, ended up with an almost well done burger. The burger wasn't dry at all, sauce was good but not anything special. The burger looked pretty small, but it ended up being very filling. Fries were okay. The spicy fries tasted like Herr's hot chips. Food was better than expected, but on the pricier side for burgers. $27 for 2 burgers, fries & milkshakes. 

In all it was a good experience, pretty solid burger place. Good for a quick bite.
I love their chalupas and Tacos but I have to give them 3 stars bc they have gotten my order wrong numerous times.

I heard really good things about their Mac Mart truck that goes around. So I went to the restaurant when it opened up to try their Mac and Cheese. I got their grilled chicken pesto Mac and Cheese and I was actually pretty disappointed. I don't think I will be coming back here again.

Well I just don't know where to start!!!
2nd time here, and not impressed, the 1st time was not memorable either but not as bad as the 2nd time.

Should have known better then to go when a Groupon was active. We did not have a Groupon, mea culpa.

Got there at the right time, got a table, and waited, finally got water, no ice, took a while to get ice.
Took a while to get service, did I mention NO GROUPON!!!

Finally ordered apps, and drinks.
We got our apps way after other people that came after us got theirs; ours went to a different table, what we got was not even what we ordered.

After the apps, we finally placed our order; we got paper napkins (2 napkins for 2 people). Since our waitress was MIA most the time, got another server to give us more napkins, she gave us 2 more paper ones.
Napkins at an Ethiopian restaurant should flow like water.
Why we were not given cloth ones is a mystery, maybe it was a signal that we did not have a GROUPON!!!

Ordered 2 entrées, a lamd dish and a chicken dish
Served on a single platter over injera
A scoop of lamb, not well seasoned, and tough
Two small chicken drumsticks, excellent taste and cooked just right.
One ice cream scoop serving size each of, collards, cabbage and lentils, all three very good.

We finally asked for our check, since there was no sense in getting desert or coffee (or diner).

Left the place, when to another establishment, and got a couple of apps and desert, and at least we did not go home hungry.

Are Groupon customers more desirable than regular customers?
Not going to find out at this establishment, since it is very unlikely that we will be back for a third time.
Great sushi and Teppanyaki. Waitress was Ashley C. and took very good care of me and my wife. Get the ginger dressing to go.
Best Sushi and Chinese in all of Northern Nevada! I eat here as often as possible!  They always have fresh delicious food made just the way you like it. Great atmosphere and friendly staff.

Can't say much wrong with this place. They have many donut choices and are always making them fresh. They also tend to make the same ones everyday, so something you like is always there. I love the maple bars, and the old fashioned ones. Donut holes are also great! Grab a drink, milk, or some coffee and you've got a pretty amazing treat on your hands. Because they're fresh cooked, which tastes better anyway, you want to check this place early. After a certain time they stop making them to avoid a lot of "day old" donuts. The donuts are great and cheap, so pick up a few!

Was recently here for a conference and I would not come back. The guy who checked us in was professional but had no personality at all. The woman who checked us out was yelling- in front of customers- at a coworker for not working (The other woman was doing something on the computer and there was a long line the Sunday after the CMAs of folks departing). The walls were so incredibly thin I could hear everything from the hallway- I literally had to stuff Kleenex in my ears to sleep because I refused to spend $5 for a pair of earplugs from the on site store. Food is not great and way over priced and you get nothing for the resort fee( even self parking is extra). The room smelled like dirty feet and was old. The worst part was it took 20 mins to get from the front desk to the room. And this hotel is no where near downtown- not worth it at all!

Do not trust your reservation is reserved. I booked my room 8 months ago and found out by letter 3 days before my arrival that I was bumped to a lesser hotel, blocks away from hotel, and to a smaller room.  Emailed and called the General Manager, no response. Customer service offered the bare minimum by way of accommodations. 

I am sure they bumped us for a late reservation, higher rate. We were told absolutely nothing as to why we were bumped. Customer care stated, :yeah they do that". Who does that? In all my life, i have never been bumped from a hotel that has been reserved.

Do not trust them.

Best oil change of life! So I brought a book originally so I can read while I would wait for my oil change but boy was I wrong! The gentleman directed me to drive onto the dock and came to my window and asked if I have been to the original location and I said no I haven't, well he informed me that this is a family owned business and they recently just opened this one and they've been around for 30 years. I thought that was really cool, but it gets better I then ask if I get out of the car and the guy says you can but we'll be done in 5 minutes...I was blown away, from the time of me driving up to the point of paying and then leaving i spent 7 minutes and I learned how to reset my oil change indicator and it was very inexpensive! Basically if you haven't been to an Insta Quick Oil Change location you really need to because it's the best!

Forced to eat a dog in the French Quarter since we got back too late to avoid the long lines to the better restaurants.  I have to say that every hot dog I've ever had was better than the Lucky Dog.  There is basically nothing wrong with it, just tasteless, perhaps too fatty and definitely overpriced!  A soda and dog was $11.00.  Can you imagine how I felt after paying that much knowing that were hundreds of restaurants nearby where for about the same amount of money (okay a little more) I could have feasted?!  I was starved so I went with the dog.  Eeek!

The beer selection really is fabulous, but with Drafting Room up the road and Victory a few miles away, you have to have good food and equally good service to win over those competitors. 
After several visits, today was easily the most appalling service out family has ever received from any establishment, ever! From the level of irritation of us walking in as the staff was just setting up (we walked in at 10:45am, the restaurant opens at 10:30am as posted on the website), for brunch, to the series of unreal circumstances that took place over the next hour, I am still in a state of shock. We were ignored for the first ten minutes, despite my asking if we had somehow arrived "too early" and getting a simple "you're fine" in response, no eye contact, and no attempt to counter the whispering in each other's ears and rolling their eyes at us. 
Fast forward to the meal, we received our appetizers of tater tots and then our waitress, Katie, went back to drinking beer at the bar with the other servers while we sat in search of ketchup. I finally got up and went to the bar to ask the gentleman bartender for ketchup. Katie then retrieved two sides of ketchup for us. When I said thank you, her response was "sure". (Also, I can look past the blond hair that was inside our tots but it was adding insult to injury at this point.)
Our breakfast came, the food was indeed good but the service was soooo bad. My two boys eventually went to sit on the leather couch and play together, clearly disturbing the on-shift wait staff eating at the bar and chatting. When my boys walked back to the table they were saturated with the smell of body odor from the couch. I mentioned to one of the male members of the wait staff, that the leather sofa smelled and that they might want to wipe them down when the day was through. He said "oh, really, I can't tell, my sense of smell isn't all that good" and then "we'll make Katie take care of it" as he walked over to Katie and another female to openly mock me for making a comment on the couch. All of this in front of my children, the oldest of which was completely confused by why his mom was being made fun of. Not the example we set for our children. 
We will never, ever, ever be back to WOB Exton and I will recommend skipping this establishment to every person who will listen.

I'm trying to think of something I don't like about this place.... I'll work on that while I write this review. The Block is styled as a neighborhood restaurant/butcher shop. Granted, it's a pretty nice neighborhood. But The Block is always welcoming, never stuffy. As far as the butcher shop - they do have a nice, but not huge butcher case. Most of their butcher skills are shown off in the menu, where they do delicious things to mostly very local meats. Lots of pork - smoked, pulled, grilled, made into jam (yes, bacon jam). Beef is offered as a burger and a butcher's cut of the day. Chicken is a lovely roasted breast. But these folks know what they're doing with veggies, too. The flash-fried brussel sprouts will bring tears to your eyes. Their seasonal salads show off produce like gem-colored beets and tender asparagus.
And their bartenders know what they're doing - from the fancy-schmancy cocktails to the craft beers and a nice wine list. They are skilled and knowledgable. I love this place.

This is a great Italian BYOB, with quite the tasting menu deal. We paid $40 each for four well-portioned courses, and definitely did not leave hungry. I definitely recommend this place for a yummy meal at a reasonable price. Overall, we had very good food that I am still thinking about days later. That's a good sign!

We were in the mood for tacos and this place had great reviews so we headed over.  It is very hidden, but it helps to know its behind Thornton's.  We got 4 tacos, the campechana and a horchata..  The guy that was helping us was SUPER friendly and was happy to give suggestions and explain what the menu was (since it was all in Spanish).  They even split the tacos on two plates for us!  I got the chicken and steak and my husband got 2 barbacoa tacos.  I don't really have a lot of experience with these kind of tacos so I don't have a clear comparison of what would be considered amazing, but I wasn't aww stricken by these tacos.  I didn't feel like they had too much flavor.  There was this green salsa stuff on the table that helped bring out some flavor.  I liked that the meat was finely chopped so it was easy to eat.  I also liked the corn tortillas.  The campechana on the other hand was really really good!  It is the same idea as ceviche, but this has shrimp and octopus.  It was really refreshing and sweet.  It was a nice balance between the heat of the taco to the cooling of the campechana.  I really liked the feel of this place and how friendly the staff was.  I would come back again!

This is a great store and was where I ultimately purchased my engagement ring and our wedding bands.  I love working with the Pauls and everyone else at the store too.  I went in with some ideas and working with Paul, we came up with a great concept for my wedding band.  The only problem with it, is that I take it off too much, because I don't want to ruin it.  Other people told me I was a fool and should have gotten my rings from Amazon, so I could replace them if needed.  I made the right choice with Cozzi.  

A great selection and this new store really displays all of their incredible items.  We bring our rings in to be cleaned and inspected a few times a year.  Just a great group of people.

We recently stayed for the first time at the Monteleone. The Staff was very helpful and friendly. The bell guys were prompt and friendly. We enjoyed a few drinks at the carousel bar, which was really cool and the drinks were definitely worth the price. The room was clean and comfortable with a very comfy bed. The location is great, when you can go out and party, then come back to a quiet, peaceful place. 

When we checked out, we called the valet and bell station and within 10 minutes we were loaded and ready to leave. This will be the hotel I first consider when staying in New Orleans.

Tasty burgers. I had the NOLA burger topped with 2 fried green tomatoes. First bite burnt the S*#@ out of my mouth though. Literally blistered. They need a disclaimer on that particular one, similar to what you see on McDonald's coffee cups. I mentioned it to the server... no apology, just "oh it must have come right out of the fryer". Gee, ya think so! lol. It was good, and I would go back, but will definitely do a finger test of the temp before diving in.

As a former Philadelphia, my visits back to my old stomping grounds always bring me back to this little place. If you can get past the basement dining, this place is a great spot for lunch any day of the week. As a vegetarian, there are some great options. I know people speak highly of the kabobs, which are delicious, but I always get the same thing when I come. Qurma Cachalu is a potato and tomato dish which comes with rice and bread. It's the perfect portion and the bread comes with a spicy dipping sauce. Be aware though, the service is relatively slow. Don't go if you want to be in and out in 25 mins.
Was eating here yesterday with my friend and I order the BBQ tots and smoked pork chops. It was just absolutely delicious! Our waitress was great as well. Highly recommend eating here!
Love the mojo pork! Cafe Con Leche on Saturday morning is the best with cheese toast.

My quick summary of this place:
Location - Nice
Staff - friendly, and remember you... go out of way to make sure you are happy
Hotel - a little dated... 
Rooms - My god!!! I have yet to have a good room here.  The range from just a general musty smell and uncleanness... to a outright - holy#@)($*#@$ i am living in black mold stench.  Also, its not the best to come into a room and find that the cleaning was halfassed - pen caps on the floor, nail clippings on the floor.... just gross.

Again, the people here are good (not including the cleaning staff - at least my rooms) - but they are dealing with a facility that really just needs a massive overhaul.  There are other locations nearby (Hilton) that are much preferred.

Walked to District Donuts on my lunch break from work. I've been wanting to try that place for a while and I am so glad I did!
I did not put 5 stars because I was hoping to try their bacon donut but they did not have it at the time.
I bought 2 huge donuts (for less than $6 in total): mango & pink peppercorn and cuba libre. A perfect lunch on a cheating day!

Got the chance to make Sunday night dinner plans for my husband and some customers while we were in town for a convention. So happy that I chose Luke!! Spent weeks hoping the food was as amazing as I hoped.
Dinner on Sunday night started with the pate and crispy Brussels sprouts- both were outstanding. My husband had gumbo and the other three of us had the salad Luke with buttermilk dressing. This was the only less than part of the meal and it was simply 3 pieces of really rusty lettuce.
Two steaks ordered and totally enjoyed- one shrimp and grits with blue crab- and one crawfish etouffe.  Not much conversation and some fork passing was had- everything was incredible.
Our server (Melody/Melanie?) helped to make the entire evening very special. She is a gem. 
Thank you John Besh for an incredible meal that was not only supremely delicious but did not 'break our bank'.  We will be back the next time we are in from Kansas!

I wish I could give Anita Corbett negative stars, but unfortunately, Yelp doesn't allow that. I have attempted to contact her several times via voicemail as well as email and have yet to receive any contact from her. I consider that not only blatantly disrespectful, but also unprofessional on the part of a 'licensed' individual. She felt it appropriate to share about all her successes; however, did not feel the need to share how she was recently fired, after three months, as a couples' agent due to inability to even show their house. After hiring a new agent, within 10 days their house had sold. I would not only advise AGAINST using her as your agent, I would say stay as far away from any of the services she could potentially offer, she is nothing less than a wolf in sheep's clothing.
Trashy all over, customers, employees, the overall quality of the store. I learned my lesson and just pay 3xs more next door at Target.
Prep and Pastry is just okay... a lot of hype-- good food ( not great) We will have to give I a another try-- maybe picked the wrong day--noticed it was noisy to a fault

Really good food. We ordered the appetizer for four which would feed 8. Don't order the large one I'm afraid how big it would be. We then had stuffed crab with greens and Mac and cheese. Food was very good. Service was excellent

Once you eat here you will regret ever having gone anywhere else for a sub. The Yum Yum Club is my favorite and is made with bacon and turkey and I think one other meat. I would suggest any sub you order from them request "light mayonnaise" because they can be a little heavy handed. Don't know where they get their bread from but it's soooo good. Note they are cash only. Call in your order when you're 10-15 minutes away to avoid a long wait.
This place is awesome!!! Everything is fresh and the employees has great selections that they choose for customers!!!

Great food, the lettuce wraps are incredible, service was very good, our waiter Joe B. was fantastic...  Food comes very fast, all is freshly prepared and hot when it hits the table...  Sushi is excellent as well...
Make sure you check for unlimited mileage!!!  Otherwise it will be $0.40/mile.  Only says it in the fine print. Nobody will tell you.

I came in tonight and it was very busy but the manager had it running so smooth with a smile on his face. I noticed after the rush he went and patted the employees on the back. A little appreciation goes a long way. The food was excellent and the customer service is always amazing. I was here last week also and left my wallet and the sweet girl Elma that was wiping down tables came running out to give it to me. I can't say enough about this place I'm a forever customer.

great place. service was well above average. ambiance was low key and welcoming. cocktails were solid. but the food was was the most impressive facet of the experience. everyone at the table had a superb meal. if you eat meat, do yourself a HUGE favor and get the churchill burger. it's indescribably good. literally. i can't even put it into words.

Some of the best places are in the most unassuming locations. This is one of them. Geat old school Italian food. Awesome pizza. The bread is to die for. Great service. Reasonably priced. I've been going here for years. This is my in laws place to go when they are back in town. They are from Philly but have been out of the area for 40 plus years.
Great salon. Friendly and clean. A shoulder massage while you dry. Go here for mani and pedi!

How to even begin to describe the let total let down that was lunch today.  First, had to call back 3 times before we could place order, they just didn't seem to have any of the favorites.  Fine, so finally it became a conversation about "well, what do you have?" Please note, it's not like we called at 2:28 for lunch, it was a reasonable 11:45 or so.  Second, delivery was ridiculously late, maybe being from NYC I have higher expectations so I'll give them a pass on that...maybe.  Third and the final straw, the food was HORRIBLE!!!!! I don't even understand how they felt that what they sent out was acceptable.  How does a Dominican restaurant screw the most basic thing-Rice.  It was stale and crunchy...and not in a bibimbap way....which I love but not with my chicken stew that was void of everything but chicken.  The only redeeming item were the sweet plantains and I assume that was because it didn't require much intervention from the chef.  
Was this just an unusually bad day for a restaurant that thus far has been pretty good? I don't know but it will be quite a while before I return to find out.

I have not gotten the chance to eat the food there. And chances are, I never will! The service there was so terrible that I cancelled my order and left. I HIGHLY recommend going ANYWHERE else if you would like to be treated with any sort of respect.

To Good: The beer list. I like the good selection of beer that they had on the menu. 

The Bad: The service. We went in midweek prior to the dinner rush -- around 4:30 and our server had only like 2 tables. She kept disappearing into the back and took forever for things like refills. 

The Ugly: The food and the cost. We tried three different pies and only one of them was worth ordering a second time. Additionally, since this place is on the craft pizza bandwagon, their prices certainly reflect that and I'm not sure I'd visit again knowing that.

You should go to Guo Bin for one main reason: the POTSTICKERS. 

Seriously, Guo Bin's potstickers have set the standard against which I judge all other Chinese restaurant's. Their potstickers are definitely authentic and homemade and their strength can carry the entire restaurant.

Ask for vinegar, not soy sauce, to dip them in (or at least mix vinegar into your soy sauce). Why? It's what us Asians do with potstickers; the acid really brings out their flavor. 

Potstickers aside, I also love the friendly staff and atmosphere. The hostess/owner would ask me why I don't come by more often and the waiter would always try to give me life advice.

(I've moved out of STL 6 months ago. I wonder if they still remember me...)

Great ice cream and baked goods. Simple, traditional stuff only, but it's good. Nothing trendy about this place, though the prices are a little high. You can eat outside and overhear lots of family conversations.
Love this place! I was surprised how big this place was inside and they are very clean. Very friendly as well. Great prices too :-) defiantly my new favorite spot

Their food is average at best. Overpriced for what you get. 
I read other comments complaining about the service, well you get what you pay for. They have employees that work 12 hour shifts without a break. I would have a bad attitude myself. I can't say anything good about this place.

This place would've been more had it not been for the attentionless server we were unfortunate enough to receive.

Having just driven a few hours in a car from FI/Brooklyn/etc when we arrived at this place the only thing I really wanted right away was a glass of water.  Looking around every table had water, so I didn't expect that I needed to order glasses of water.  Instead we ordered glasses of Cava and a few cheeses...  Our wine and cheese came, but no water.  I finally asked him for some. What is this, Europe?  And it's not like every other table there didn't have their own glasses of water, they did, and I doubt even that half of them had to "order" water. 

Didn't try much of the food, just cheese.  It was good.

Our server seemed like a nice guy.. to others.  To us we were lucky to get a word in other than to add to our order.  I don't know where his too cool for you attitude came from, I think he had us pegged as tourists as soon as we sat down.  Which we were.  But that doesn't make us idiots.

It's a nice place. Parking is a pain. Drinks were good and the food was just ok. We had our work holiday party there. They were more interested in making the party starting after us happy. They just off our bowling lanes 40 minutes before our time was up and when we said something we just got a phony sorry. All this after they had us change the day and time.

What a gem of North Redington Beach a great hole in the wall with awesome pricing foods. You must try the Shubee Shack crab cakes and the crab balls, very yummilicious. 

Place your order at the little window and relax on one of the benches while Chef Pat makes your meal fresh and hot!!!
I had the crab balls -nicely crisp on the outside and crabby and soft on the inside. A fresh, delicious beachy experience.

I believe Perret's is the last army surplus store in the metropolitan area. 

If you have never been to a surplus store, you are truly missing out. Besides actual military surplus items, Perret's sells new clothing, boots, watches, sunglasses and other outdoor type items. 

My favorite thing to buy here are the ammo cans. The cans are waterproof and very sturdy. Besides storing ammunition, they can be used to store any valuables you don't want ruined in case of flooding. I recommend getting the SAW can as opposed to the more common .50 BMG can. The SAW can is slightly larger, but nowhere near as large as the mortar can. Everyone should have a few of these.

If you're one of those nuts who likes to bury stuff in their yard, you can find supplies at Perret's. They even have freeze dried food for backpacking or domesday preparedness.

To summarize, check out Perret's, it is cool.
The food is great. A good variety and very tasteful. I can't say the same about the staff. Rude not very friendly at the reception. If you get to pass that, enjoy the delicias!

Pros: professional staff, clean building, great atmosphere, I never feel pressured to buy anything. I love the use of essential oils and bottle of water at the end! Prices are fair. 

Cons: while the visits are extremely relaxing, I still have knots in my shoulders when I leave. My chiropractor has recommended that I find a new place to get massages, but it's so hard to find one that makes you feel comfortable! I've made it a point to ask at the beginning of the appointment for focus on my knots, but they're always still there after.
Very disappointed. Order was incorrect & no one seemed interested in helping to correct the problem by refunding the overcharge.  Will avoid this location in the future.

Today was my first day at this vet and it was a wonderful experience for me and my cat. The staff was so friendly and helpful. The exam room was very pet friendly. My cat has never been relaxed at the vet and he was completely calm and explored the whole time. Dr. Klapheke was wonderful with him and she was great at walking me through her exam, how she was making her clinical decision and answering all of my questions. She helped me feel like I had a voice in deciding on the best plan for my kitty and made everything so clear and convenient. I have never had such a wonderful experience at a vet. Now I just need to find a doctor for myself who offers such a high quality of care.
Fresh Dough, yummy 3 cheese blend, and plentiful toppings! Baked wings are delicious too!
Wacky environment, no restroom, not an original naan, curry is just ok, amount of food according to the price is not worthwhile.

06/16 update:  The new management company that took over last November took a few months to work through the outstanding issues.  I haven't seen piled up trash in the trash room since about February.  I'm revising my rating as a result.

Really enjoyed a St Pats dinner with the wife. It was an hour wait for a table for two with no reservations on a Saturday night but they had seating right away at the bar. 
Apps, drinks and meal was awesome. Definitely recommend for a nice meal on a date night.  Service was very good too.
Amazing tacos. Chimichanga. Menudo. Green sauce. Everything was so delish!!! And horchata so good!

This place somehow is always a miss for me. Thought I would give it a second chance with the chicken pad Thai and the Brian special banh mi sandwich but both were a miss. The pad Thai was spicy as I requested it, the taste was not as desire-able. The banh mi is very sad. They are open about getting their bread from the Publix down the street and that in itself tells a lot. Not every authentic or good. It's always a miss. Once a year kind of thing -- if that.

Paola is the sweetest, most friendly restaurant owner I've met! As soon as we walked in she greeted us with great attention... And the food is DELICIOUS! The calzone came out pipping hot and fresh, we will definitely be back!!
Just had my hair cut by Laura the other day. I'm a guy with a hard head to cut, in many ways. lol. But Laura got it right the first time. You can spend more but i doesn't get better.

Just gorgeous and on Thursday night they played all the 90s hip hip classics. Best place to celebrate my milestone birthday. Drinks are $$$ but delicious. Great Pimms cup. 15 dollars well spent but maybe you don't have 3 of them. Oops. Well you only live once right? The decor, vibe and people were just everything.

I survived opening day at 500 Degrees and came out very satisfied with our new addition to 15th and Sansom.

Burgers - 5.5oz burger on a tall brioche bun made to order (medium rare was juicy and delicious!)  It's not as good as the burger at Village Whiskey but it's about as good as the aged beef burger at Marathon Grill.  I was concerned about the size but between that and the plain fries (these truffle fries were overrated) I was wiping the plate and feeling great.

Goodbye Five Guys, Hello 500 Degrees.
Food was very good; however service is certainly not exceptional.  Overall good place for breakfast and lunch.

The first ever restaurant I have ever tried in the East Coast!

I got the crab cake appetizer that came with a small salad, a side of baked potato and lemonade.

Food's fresh, delish and really home cooked. Even the lemonade was freshly made! The crab cake had lumps and chunks of real crab meat...soooo good! 

The staff was casual, really nice and the service was fast. 
I love the restaurant ambiance, has a homey feel to it.

The desserts on their wall menu board sounded good but oh we were so full...

0.5 stars. 

On a truly sad day, an Indian friend and I (both of whom are from Tucson) decided we had an Indian restaurant craving (which would thus not be satisfied by our Tucson Indian moms' cooking). We literally walked into Sher-E-Punjab, were given a table, walked up to the buffet, looked at each other with agreeing shakes of the head, and walked straight out. The buffet presentation we looked at was simply not up to snuff. And this is despite our expectations being low to begin with, since I have eaten at Sher before and already know that it's a pretty underwhelming experience.

Be careful of your credit cards, people. I have never set foot in this location. Somebody working at this Red Robin location in September MANUALLY ENTERED - not one, but TWO - cash advances for $500 each using our company credit card number that was stolen from a retail location in Red Deer.
VISA and RCMP are working on the file, but, it's one thing to innocently take a fraudulent card, but when you process a "cash advance" at a place of business that doesn't deal in cash advances - either a staff member or a manager is crooked. Taking $500 cash from the float on two different occasions and then balancing the cash after doing so is no accident. That is something that should have been noticed at audit - and the fact that it wasn't, shows that the criminality is higher up the ladder than one would think...Shame on you Red Robin Sherwood Park!

What a nice surprise! When traveling from grandkids to another grandkids we thought we would stop and just get an average burger...Not HERE! This was amazing! The bun seemed fresh and homemade. I had the peanut butter and bacon cheeseburger just for kicks and what a fantastic flavor bomb! My husband had the hangover burger even though he didn't have a hangover. He loved his also. We also had the fried pickles that were served with a touch of class. Delicious dill flavor with chipotle ranch and a garnish of another pickle relish . Such presentation! And the French onion soup was at the top of the heap of most French onion soups. If we pass this way again, we'll be back.

I was impressed with the selection and fresh quality of the food choices.  The servers were very attentive and the staff were well trained in providing quality food and cleanliness to their guests.  Come hungry and enjoy a good quality meal at a reasonable price.  

For a buffet restaurant, I was very impressed.

I was very fortunate to have  a co-worker bring two of us  4 of the most beautiful soft tacos (beef) & it was soooo worth it.  I hadn't planned in eating tacos, namely cuz i forgot that he was bringing them in.  

Very very good. worth a trip if i happen to be around the Norristown area.. first impressions, so want more!!!

I'd heard good things about this place, but never eaten here, although my parents always stay in this Sheraton when they visit. I figured it would be an easy meal for us on their last night in town. 

Potentially one of the most underwhelming experiences I've ever had. The server gave the distinct impression that she'd rather be anywhere else in the world, and that we were sort of an annoying imposition on her time. The menu was short; there was very little to choose from, hardly anything for vegetarians. The enchiladas couldn't be be made vegetarian because they were "rolled in the morning." The children's menu was unavailable (although the server recited it for the kids), as was the pizza menu, because they were being reprinted. The server couldn't recite the available pizza toppings, but claimed they had "anything you'd put on a pizza." When my father asked for his favorite toppings, they were not available. 

I ordered the salmon which was middling, nothing special. It was a small piece of fish drowned in an overly sweet sauce. The rice was edible, but sort of looked like it had been sitting around. Neither of these foods gave the impression of being very fresh, although the grilled vegetables were. At $20, it felt WAY overpriced. 

My mother ordered sweet pototo rellenos and didn't like them at all. It was just chiles, cubed sweet potatoes, and a bit of cheese, not really a relleno at all. 

My father got the pizza, and if it wasn't the worst pizza I've ever tasted, it was pretty close. I've had better pizza at the bowling alley. The crust was like a piece of soft bread. The ingredients did not scream "high-quality." This pizza made me yearn for the frozen generic pizza in the grocery freezer case.

The kids liked their meals. My stepson had chicken fingers, which were pretty run-of-the-mill, and onion rings, which were probably the best item we ate that night. The onions were sliced to a good size and the breading was crispy, although it had a strange, bitter aftertaste. I'm guessing this food was frozen.

My stepdaughter loved her macaroni, which isn't saying much. It looked like last week's leftovers and when my stepson tasted it, he said it tasted like it had been in the microwave. She was told the fruit side would be watermelon and strawberries, but there wasn't much in the way of strawberries, and the whole dish had the taste and appearance of something that had been sitting in the back of the fridge all week with discolored watermelon chunks and tiny random bits of other fruit swimming in the juice at the bottom.

Basically, nothing looked or tasted fresh. This place isn't doing much for the reputation of southwestern cuisine.

Also, our waitress disappeared after checking in on us once. (She was most likely not busy with other tables, as we were the only people in the section, and possibly the restaurant by that time.) Ten minutes after we finished eating, my mother had to get up and hunt her down to ask her for the check. 

Might give the place another chance if/when they revamp their menu but at not running.

Great atmosphere and quality facilities. Very VERY happy we decided to try this place out. The movie was great, having no kids in the theater made it even better. 

However...

We did think the food was over priced and the service was a little slow. They definitely could use less staff at the front entrance and more at the bar.

None the less this just became our go to movie theater! Love seats and the beer.. haha

I agree with others who rated Citizens Bank one star. I had a bad experience recently when I tried to close my Dad's account there after he died. Since my name was on the account, I called one of their representatives and she told me what to do to close the account. Unfortunately, she didn't give me all the information I needed to know, and I ended up with over $200 in additional fees owed. A lady called me from their Recovery Department, and even though I explained what happened, in the midst of my grief, she said I should have known about things pertaining to my Dad's account because my name was on it. What made matters worse, my cousin referred me to his branch, and I spoke with the Branch Manager, Tamera James, and she said she'd help me by talking to the appropriate bank representative on my behalf. After our first conversation, she didn't return my phone calls. I resolved this matter today on my own. Avoid Citizens Bank if you can go to another one that is more customer service oriented.

While the ambience would've give. This a 5 star the sushi in here is good. Quality fish and I am picky coming from running a sushi bar at Disney. Limited beverage for sake but given it wasn't busy for lunch other than the local business clientele I understand. Shockingly affordable but I did recently move from Boston. I would come back regularly for the price and quality. Not much conversation at the sushi bar but to be fair I was on my phone nearly the entire time.

I was a bit torn on my rating for Penang. Could have gone 3 or 4. I went with 4 because of the roti canai. It was awesome. Outstanding flavor, very unique. I could have mopped up two or three bowls of it. 
The masak chicken was average. Not great, not bad. That is why the dispute between stars. I think I just ordered the wrong thing for my liking. 
Table next to me had the striped bass with black bean sauce and it looked amazing. I asked and they said it was. 
I look forward to coming back to try different dishes as I think you can find a variety of flavors to choose from and just have to learn what you like.

One of the best restaurants in Philly. They make all tortillas and chips on premises.  Lots of amazing dishes! Almost everything on the menu is gluten free. Friendly service and amazing food. Love this place!
I use SB airbus anytime I need to travel to and from LAX. This time I needed to cancel for a family emergency and the company was very accommodating. Thank you!

Okay so this is my favorite Mexican restaurant I've ever been to. It's so good, cheap, and fast. They have great deals all throughout the week, so check them out.

Now, here is the reason why it is my favorite Mexican restaurant: the queso (which is inherently not Mexican, and I understand that). It is so good and SO cheap. 3 bucks for a small bowl is all you need. The cheats are so tasty and dipping them in the queso is just heavenly. 

The decor of the restaurant is  so great. Lots of murals that have [actually] been featured in quite of few buzzfeed quizzes/articles regarding restaurants. 

The servers all walk around with 6+ plates in their hands--no trays. It's very impressive.

The drinks are stronger than the blood of Christ, I shit you not. 

Again, so good, so worth it, I wish I was there forever.


Do hot guys work there: several, sure.

For a palace, I expected a little more. The palace looks more like some well-off parents decided to put in a few tables and some video poker machines in a redone garage. I don't even think there was a throne.

We were greeted by a nice waitress. She told us we could sit anywhere and didn't need special dispensation from the king. We chose a center table, which delighted our waitress because we'd be "so close" to her only other table with patrons.

I'm not a fried chicken fan, but I'm not going to miss an opportunity to bask in royalty. My parents said the chicken could use more spice and the sweet potato fries were lacking flavor.

If you're wondering how the grilled chicken Caesar salad is, it's great. Our waitress, however, thought she'd warn me she was required to put tomatoes on it, and that I did not have to eat them. I don't know if they're not big fans of excess veggies at JB's or what, but it was a strange warning. I ate the tomatoes because I like tomatoes and not because I felt forced. 

Uh, in conclusion: if you like fried chicken and tomatoes with your Caesar, this is not a bad start. However, it's very cold in here.

The tire plus here is better than the one at new tampa. They are performed the tire change, balance, rotation or alignment better. I have come to here for my tire replacement.  I always find a 40,000 mile warranty tire here and change them almost every two year or more since tire do not last. What is the point to buy the good tire. The tire may be miss alignment once you hit the curb unintentionally. 

They tire plus here have the life time alignment and balance if you buy the tire here. I already got my money worth since I have been here for more than tree time due to their life time program.  I suggest you do the same. Right now they have the tire in 59 minutes or you are free program if you make appointment. A smart way to come here is to make appointment and there is less wait. 

They have wifi if you want to bring your computer while you wait for your car. Other than oil change, tire, and tune up please go to your dealer.

This place was excellent! Reservations are a must here. My wife and I had Sunday Jazz Brunch reservations for 12:30. We showed up early so the hostess directed us to the bar. This is where our experience started and We quickly fell in love. Beautiful bar in the back, just past an indoor courtyard area with ivy hanging all around. The Bloody Mary's were better than some of the other more famous ones in town

Once seated in the formal dining room, we were greeted by our waiter Travis and his assistant. They were very helpful and nice. The room was pretty with hardwood floors and old pictures on the walls. High ceilings of course, and lots of windows.

For an appetizer, we shared an order of the crawfish crepes. This item was actually one of the reasons I chose this place, and they met my expectations. My wife had the omelette, with potatoes and a biscuit. She was very pleased. I had the yellow fin tuna, which was the fish of the day. It came seared, on a bed of spinach. It was prepared perfect, and the portion was much more than expected. This wasn't some 2 bite piece of fish. I think a lot of people would have had a hard time finishing it. 

The band alternated between the 2 dining rooms, playing 2 or 3 songs before switching. Sound was awesome, not too loud, and they even took a few requests!

We finished our meal with an espresso, just enjoying the ambiance. All in all, a great experience. We will be back!

I eat at so co gyros about once a week and they never disappoint. Excellent gyros (my favorite in the city), but also really freaking good blackened chicken...   The blackened chicken wraps and salads are really tasty. Friendly staff, they appreciate your business and treat you like family. From time to time they offer coupons in various south county coupon mailings..., and they are nice enough to let you keep the coupon and reuse it until it expires! 

For paleo eaters... The gyro salad is top notch and I promise it will fill you up. Tough to find paleo options in this area, but the gyro salad is a nice stand by...,

My boyfriend and I have been shopping at this store since it opened a few years ago. We have never left empty handed. The prices are fair, the goods are high quality and the service is impeccable.  Like a previous post I wish I could keep this shop all to myself but it is so fun to explore, it's a must!

I typically don't get a  quesadilla at a Mexican restaurant for the desire to have something extraordinary, but this quesadilla was just that. Fantastic, like a party in my mouth. The gouda cheese, onions, and chicken mend together so well, then on the plate they add a sweet red sauce and a black bean and corn salsa, I literally don't think it could've been any better. As a chef's daughter I look for good flavor combos, and this was expertly crafted, and plated to perfection. Best chicken quesadilla I've ever had in my life. 
My husband got the chicken enchilada, without the Verde  (typically served with one Verde and one roja).... and he loved the amount of flavor in his dish as well... it's hard to make common things stand out to me, but this place has it down, from the difficult specialties to the commonly seen dishes. We will be back!

Good martini. Pleasant service. 

They list conch on the sushi menu which delighted me, only to be told after I ordered it that they stopped carrying it some time ago. 

Rice paper roll outstanding. Fresh and stuffed with vegetables. Yellow tail roll very tasty as well. 

Noisy bar blessedly separated from main dining room. Found the dining room too brightly lit, however. I don't know why this concerned me, but for a dinner after the sun has set one rather expects a less Shoney's-like ambience. 

But, it's a casual neighborhood joint so take it as it comes. I enjoyed my meal and look forward to wandering in again.

Was feeling lazy today so we ordered to go from here! I loved Connie at the front desk! She was pleasant from even the phone when I ordered. The seafood bisque is to die for! My lobster ravioli was amazing and everything is so fresh!

This is possibly my new favorite restaurant after only two visits.  I have gone for both lunch and brunch thus far, and both times the food was amazing.  My boyfriend, an avid omnivore and I, a pescatarian, enjoyed all of the dishes we received.  Each was extremely flavorful and did not try to imitate any meat filled dish.  Instead, the focus was on fresh ingredients and spices to create a completely satisfying meal.  The service is friendly and very accommodating.   I cannot wait to explore the dinner menu.

Oh. My. God.   The Canal St. Redfish.   Words cannot describe the flavor of this magnificent dish.  Panko crusted, pan seared redfish topped with a Cajun garlic sauce and topped with sautéed shrimp served with sautéed vegetables.   

Totally worth leaving my narrow-palleted wonderful hubby at Harrahs Casino to endure my tastebuds.

My husband and I had our first experience with Knuckle Busters just the other day and we are so overly pleased with this shop! I can't believe we haven't tried it sooner! I should've got the guy's name who helped us because he was so so so helpful and knowledgeable! I was jumping into the world of box mods and he throughly explained the pros and cons of the 2 that I had picked out so that was nice! The shop is awesome, they have a try before you buy on any juice. Speaking of juice, their selection is seriously so awesome! They have everything you could ever want and need lol. They have so many authentic items, it's amazing. And they have clones too, so you're free to choose whichever. They have everything you could ever want in the vape world lol. My husband and I will definitely, without a doubt be returning to this shop!

I remember when this use to be an abandoned Albertson's but no more. The parking lot is always packed on Sundays and pretty full for their mid-week service so I figured I would check it out. Whoever did the design of the facility itself did a really great job. Very open and nicely put together...kinda reminds me of the home goods aisle in Target but in a good way. Lots of space on the children side and a coffee/snack shack out front that seems to be the before service hangout. It's not your typical free coffee and doughnuts but they do advertise that the money goes towards the missionaries they support. The highlight of this place is their worship! This is play no games, professional quality, spirited, everybody out your seat time. The sanctuary is kept pretty dark so it's easy to focus and feels rather intimate even though there's a few hundred people around. The preaching was good and is more on the charismatic side of the church wheel.....and then there will be more worship lol. I can't say that I got a very welcoming experience where anybody bothered to know my name but I did get a free mug. 

Pros: Great worship, Modern church, Very diverse, Lots of options for people to get involved

Cons: Everyone seemed really busy doing something else
This place is sooo nice. The food is always fresh and the service is friendly and fast. The bier and the drinks are so good.

Ordered photai, just steak, and the broth is very very bland...had to add a lot of sriracha just to make it taste like anything.   Also, a large bowl is $10...stick to 777 unless you happen to be in the area...also ordered the pork sandwich which was was ok, but not enough meat.  I'm giving 3 stars just because of the service...

I have been coming here on and off for years and was excited to see how the owners of the Hook chain would do with a historically great place, wow was I disappointed. ... .....meh. Those guys should come and taste the food, nothing like the Hook chain, I would be embarrassed to put my name on this place after founding high quality places like Hook and The Habit.

There is some good. Great location, patio, places for kids to play, great vibe. Decent selection of tap beer. Too bad they had to serve food here. (at least what we had)

We both had Baja Fish Tacos. Non descript sauce,  fish smelled like they did not clean out the fryer, cabbage was flat, no other quality ingredients or flavors that came through. The salsa was watery no flavor, no onion or cilantro or pepper flavor, really really poor quality. After eating these fish tacos you really appreciate Spencer Mackenzie's in Ventura. 

We also had Cole slaw and it tasted like a pile of poor quality cabbage. No sauce or other flavors. I actually took it back and asked if they forgot to mix in anything with the slaw. Even after they "fixed it" it was horrible. 

I understand they have the Hook hamburgers here so will give it another shot one of these days.

My friend and I decided to have lunch at Mr. B's on Memorial Day. The atmosphere is moderately upscale. Fortunately for us, there was no long line or crowd, so we got seated immediately. 

For the most part the servers were nice, however our waitress could have improved her customer service etiquette.
 
My first issue with the waitress began after I asked her to clean the bread crumbs from the table ... (Side note: the bread is served from a bag, it's light and crispy on the outside and airy  on the inside... It tastes good but easily crumbles) 
The waitress wiped the table but left a considerable amount of crumbs on the table ... Afterward, the waitress called me a "neat freak" , not once but twice ... The neat freak comment was completely inappropriate. 

Second, the waitress was unfamiliar with the menu. She did not seem to know whether or not the shrimp in the various dishes was deveined. 

My third issue was with waiting 40 minutes for the crab cake appetizer. One crab cake is $18. The crab cake was actually good and savory, but it was disappointing waiting 40 minutes for one crab cake ... 

Our main course arrived about 15 minute after the crab cake. 

I ordered the shrimp and angel hair pasta. The buttery taste overwhelmed the dish. Since the dish lacked acidity, I requested lemons from the waitress. The taste of the pasta was not a big deal ... Nothing a little lemon juice couldn't fix. 

My fourth issue was with the waitress bringing the small cut lemons from the bar, instead of lemon wedges ... 

The lemon cuts were so small that I was unable to squeeze lemon juice from the lemons ...

Overall, I wanted to enjoy Mr. B's more than I did... I have no plans of returning.

Cool stuff available if you are buying for yourself. Things usually to expensive to flip on eBay or otherwise, and the 5-6 sellers we spoke with have ZERO INTEREST in bargaining, which is a buzz kill. I asked one guy about a lamp, and his response was, "Price is $55 but I won't take less than $5 so if you can't do that just out it back where you found it."

This is a place is great for take out. At work we tend to get it on paydays. Their Squid Salad is awesome and the specials are filling. Lunch time specials are at a great price most not more than $6. Sushi is a bit on the pricier side but to be able to bring it to work and eat it, it all hits the spot.

My girlfriend and I stopped by a week ago to eat.  We both got the teriyaki steak sandwich and two drinks.....the steak was raw in the middle....we too them back to the window and took the server that they were raw and he said it would be another 1/2 hour to get our lunch redone that he was backed up with orders.  Really? We should be first in line.....not impressed....everything about that place felt rushed, no quality control or customer service.

Old skool. This is another review of a place from the archive's. I literally grew up here. This was probably the first place I had a hoagie from. If you're from Philly, that's kinda a big deal. Memories of picking up a hoagie and holding it all the way down 95 to the Flyer's game, sticking it under my jersey, and tearing it open once we were in our seats. More memories of walking here from the jr high after school, getting wings and playing Galaga in the back. If I close my eyes, I can smell it. 

The service is "what the f yiz want?" and that's how it should be. The food is generous and fresh.
