The girl setting and clearing the table was a bit inexperienced, stacking up the entire flight of appetizer plates and bread plates in one fell swoop. But, very pleasant. 

I love the location here, its super close to home, and a great place for Italian food in Fishtown. Can't wait to go back again.

Had a good Monday date night here with the husband. Lucky for us, Mondays are Indiana Pint Night, so my pint of Taxman Blonde was $3. I had the BELT (bacon, egg, lettuce and tomato) and they let me be a PIA by customizing it with an over-easy egg and Texas toast. Soooo good. My husband had the Hangover burger and really enjoyed it. They make their potato chips in-house, and they are fantastic! It is a family-friendly place, which is great for us normally (as we have a tot), but on this particular date night, we should have sat in the bar--loud kiddos galore. Overall great food and service. We'll be back!

This place is so popular on the weekends. The line moves pretty fast but get here early for seating. The donuts are large, delicious, and made in-house from scratch. I will always be drawn to bourbon infused anything.

The sliders are good and the coffee is great for the area. It can get kind of smokey due to the open kitchen in the middle of the room and lack of ventilation. 

Flavors and items rotate so when you come in here, there's likely something new to try. They keep the menu simple, use quality ingredients, and provide tasty options.

Another starbucks review but seriously, this place is awesome! I am an addict of the Doppio Espresso, and for some reason this place makes it that much stronger and appropriate. Especially over ice, they simply know the way I like it which is not filled to the brim with ICE.

Their services are impeccable, and speedy. Their layout is better than most starbucks in the sense that there is actual parking, and you don't have to fight through hordes of people waiting for coffee to get to a seat. A great relaxing place for a good cup of joe.

My father was in the regional hospital in Brandon for 10 days and we were spending 14 hour days in his hospital room.  My husband has Celiac disease and is highly sensitive to gluten.  Having Outback nearby with a gluten-free menu meant that we could get at least one good, safe, solid meal every day on our way home to sleep.  The staff quickly started to recognize us, and even asked after my dad.  They were very helpful and sympathetic when I was too tired to be decisive. My husband had a fairly wide range of gluten-free choices, including the ever-delicious chocolate thunder.  Best of all, after a dozen meals (some during very busy rush times) my husband did not once get sick from gluten cross-contamination, which happens every now and then in less careful kitchens.  Even the curbside takeout was safe for him. I have nothing but good things to say about this restaurant and the people who work here.

I love this place. It may be my new favorite.  Very good and fresh. Everything we had was excellent. 
The staff is very friendly and it's super clean. 
On the quiet side so it's perfect for visiting as well.

Enjoyed brunch here with a coworker. Nice pub atmosphere, friendly staff, and tasty food. I had a concoction with eggs, sausage gravy, biscuit and cheeses and it was great. My friend had big, fluffy pancakes that I tasted and loved despite pancakes not being my first breakfast food choice. Reasonably priced too.
Had chicken tikka masala takeout. Delicious. Want to try something new next time but will be going back very soon!
Best New York type pizza in Tampa.
place was great! server was really nice and helpful. food was delicious and the price was just right! highly recommended!

Moon's is fantastic. Their breakfasts are great, as are their lunchs. Has a very eclectic ambiance which is perfect for downtown boise. The service is always great and on sundays (possibly other days, i just get breakfast there sundays) they have great musicians play which adds to the "north end" feeling of the place. The perfect play for a sunday morning.

The main feature- fried chicken, was not remarkable.  Many other places in town have better.  The mashed potatoes did not seem to be made from scratch, surprising for the price point of this place.  Apparently it is too much effort to have their bread basket for lunch, which is unfortunate, because it probably was their best item, had it been available.

The only thing more disgusting than the waiter's scabbed up hands was the food. Everything was cold and the biscuits & gravy arguably tasted worse than dog food. On top of all of this, the bathrooms were so filthy they resemble an underground abortion clinic.

Best place in town for great/affordable sushi. It really is the cheapest sushi in town and it is A LOT better than most other places in Nashville. The sushi is HUGE and Sam sets each plate perfectly: sushi, soy sauce, wasabi, ginger, orange. 

PAY CASH. He has a small article at the checkout counter stating how debit/credit cards are ruining small business. He doesn't accept tips too.

I'm impressed he runs the entire shop 7 days a week. He's a great guy and may pick on you time to time, but come on, it's Sam! And he'll remember your order too.

We ate here last night and have eaten here often over the past few years. It has been such a negative the last few times... it has really gone downhill.  The restaurant was dirty, none of tables were clean and the staff was disappointing.  The guy who made our burritos was yawning and stretching while taking our order, they were completely out of chips and utensils, overcharged us on our bill... it is obviously being mismanaged.
Check out FB under Madison .Taylor.  Posted pix of animal jaw found in fried rice from this place!   Ewwwwwww

Ready to head off to a movie in an hour, we sat at the bar for a beer and burger.  The $11 burger was dense and moist.  The beef is locally sourced.  The rosemary french fries were very good.  My friend Bill had the pulled pork and cheddar sanwdich with mustard fries.   We started with a grilled cheese and bread salad.   Staff was attentive and the food came out quickly.  

The owner (?) was behind the bar and gave us the low down on the renovations from the previous Cuban place.

We looked at the Noble menu around the corner, but I told my friend that I was not in the mood for $30 entrees.   I can see Slate as being a neighborhood, chill dinner place for locals.

The food and atmosphere were both great as usual. The only reason they get three stars this time around is the hostess that sat us. We had a 5:30 pm reservation on Sunday August 21st. We got there at 5:20 and they said it would be 5 min. At 5:40 we asked where things stood after he sat two other couples and he had clearly forgot about us. When he took us to our table he told us we would have to be through eating by a certain time. When we told him he was the reason we were getting seated late he told our server under his breath to watch out "we were troublemakers". Very rude!

I bought gift cards from Costco at a 20% discount.  Great right.  After two ridiculously terrible visits, including hard boiled eggs on our Benedict's (twice).  I gave the remaining gift cards away.   We did go on both Saturday and Sunday mornings, so you can read that either way.  Either my bad for picking a busy time or theirs for not being able to handle it.  No third strike for me, this place is way, way overrated.

I got this as delivery on Skip the Dishes. The delivery experience was great, but I thought the food was just ok. I got the yellow curry with chicken and the packaging leaked all over and the chicken was overdone and the potatoes underdone. The fried egg rolls were WAY too salty and were just not good. I really wouldn't recommend this place to anyone.

Ok, so I used to love Smashburger, but now I avoid it.  I went there about three months ago.  The morning after eating there I felt so weak and nauseous.  I had to cancel going into work.  I'm assuming it was food poisoning/ a bad batch of ground meat.  I have felt fine since then.

The actual tour was pretty interesting, and I enjoyed the swamp tour. GETTING there, however, was horrible. My companion and I spent 2 hours on the bus, riding around NOLA before we even left for the tour. The buses really need to be better coordinated.

The food here was good. We came for a late breakfast and waited a little longer than they initially said. The food took a long time to come which made lunch last 2.5 hours, but everything tasted good. The City Grits were especially fantastic! The coffee mugs were adorable and are a great gift (albeit a little expensive at $18 each). Overall a long but enjoyable breakfast.

Love it. Informal yet nice. Owner on hand. Food very good  osso bucco beautifully done. Artichokes were perfectly roasted. Will go again.
Ps....I am 1st generation Italian......and very picky about my Italian food.

Terrible. I had to get to church with a colored print that had details of a child with a fatal disease and their printer took 30 minutes to print 4 pages properly! Three different machines and three people had to get involved. They didn't charge me but I obviously missed my appointment! What's more their ladies room at 10:30 am is absolutely disgusting and no paper towels even though have have so many on sale outside.

Came in on a Saturday and was seen as soon as I completed the paperwork. The staff here is very friendly, approachable and professional. It made all the difference with my experience. Would trek over here again.

Penn Station, like DC's Union Station and other urban transportation hubs, is a wonderful example of early 20th century architecture. It is a beautiful structure, both inside and out. However, unlike Union Station, 30th Street Station doesn't seem to have kept up with the times as well.  There's a lot of unutilized space, and the waiting seats are the same wooden benches that have probably been there for the last 50 years. Sure, it adds to the historic charm. So does the old-school fully functional split flap display for arrivals and departures in the center terminal. But some additional and more comfortable seating would be greatly appreciated.

And 30th Street Station pales in comparison to Union Station or Grand Central when it comes to amenities. The wife and I debated whether or not to eat brunch at the hotel or the station, and opted for the hotel since we had a bit of time. It was a good call, as the dining options are very limited compared to what we are used to at Union Station. (Although they do have a Jersey Mike's, which is always good in my book.)

I'd probably still have given them 4-stars, but I had to ding them for having an entire men's restroom closed at 12N on a Sunday, causing a HUGE line at the facility on the other side of the concourse. Getting on the train seemed a bit more of a hassle here than in DC too. 

Overall, 30th Street Station serves its purpose as a transportation hub, but it isn't a true destination spot like its larger and more modern cousins to the north and south.

I used to love Red Lobster but last night will probably be the last time I go; especially to the Fairview Heights location.  

The wait was horrendous.  We were told it would be about 45 minutes.  We checked back with the hostess after it was getting close to an hour and we were told it would be about 10 more minutes. Okay, it is a Saturday, still not bad, right?  Finally after waiting one hour and 45 minutes we were finally seated . . . . and after numerous people that came in after us were seated.  Everywhere on the internet it says Red Lobster restaurants don't take reservations/call ahead seating so my bad for not actually calling to make sure as apparently they now do.  Most restaurants won't book large parties on a Friday or Saturday evening or at least keep them to a limited number, especially between the 5 pm - 7 pm rush time because . . . it's a Friday or Saturday evening and they are already extra busy.  Not here - there were probably 3 or 4 large parties which I guess was the reason one family of five had to wait almost 2 hours!!  If they would have just told us upfront that it would be well over an hour wait, we would have never stayed.  Apparently that is what they tell everyone that walks in because they continually told people that came in after us it would be 45 minutes to an hour wait (they did add fifteen more minutes on!). Maybe the hostesses just need more training in figuring out semi-accurate wait times but I recognized them from previous visits and they've all worked there for years. This would lead you to believe they are just not honest with people in hopes of not turning customers away.  I totally get that it was a Saturday and expected to wait but not for almost two hours and not one full hour longer than what you said when we walked in.  That is by far unreasonable.  There were actually smaller parties that came in right after us (not call aheads either) that were seated, ate, and left before we were seated.  I guess a party between 4-8 throws them into a conundrum but they can handle smaller groups and those with over 10 with no problems.  I guess we were really the fools because once we were seated, there was hardly anyone left still waiting (many had already given up and left).  Honestly, we sat there patiently and only asked once nicely where we were in the wait.  Funny how a few people that we are pretty sure came in well after we did, but loudly pitched a fit about the wait were seated right after they complained!    

Now to the food - menu selections seem smaller and prices are way too high for the size and quality of the food.  They've really just gone downhill over the years - the second biggest reason I won't go back.  The food was just average, if even that - let's face it, the Midwest typically overcooks seafood so it ends up tough and rubbery with little flavor.  The same can be said here.  The only thing that tasted excellent were the cheddar bay biscuits - still exceptional!     

The only saving grace to the evening was the great waiter.  I don't recall his name but he told us he was originally from Miami.  He was a very attentive waiter and was very friendly.  If I were only giving stars for his service, it would have been 4 or 5 stars for sure!

I could eat the blue cheese fondue on almost anything. I bet liver would taste good in that fondue. Fortunately I had some really good buffalo cauliflower to go along with and I hasten to say it was a top 5 all time appetizer ever.People rave about the fries and they were good but not the best I have had. The Tavern burger on the other-hand may be the best burger I have ever had. Made from ground rib-eye and filet makes me believe God made the burger lol The lobster sliders were really good but 22 bucks not that good. The mushroom soup had to be made by Angels it was amazing. Its a little pricey but you definitely get what you pay for, for the most part. As a whole it may be the best lunch ever. I give very few 5 stars on average and this was well earned. The place is nice and cozy and the staff were great. It was a religious experience involving food.

3 stars for a chain, is like 4-5 stars at another steakhouse. Compared to others in its class such as Outback, this place is great. Fresh baked bread and ability to pick your own steak make this place unique and worth the trip. This is the place I take the kids when we want a steak. You cannot compare this to a del friscos, capital grill or Morton's, but among it's class it's tops. The kids don't like the burgers as they are made on the same sweet homemade bread they put on the table. They really enjoy the atmosphere which includes stuffed armadillos and every table has peanuts for you to snack on.

I have only been there once and even though I really like the style, decor and everything, the food and choices offered definitely had some room for improvement. 
They did not have other options to whole milk and not many pastry options.

We have eaten here several times for breakfast.   Servers are nice and attentive.   The sweet potato pancakes are great.   A little dessert to start the day. 

The grilled chicken country breakfast plate is delicious.   The chicken is always tender and never over cooked. The potatoes are cooked perfectly, not over cooked and mushy.  I recommend their bbq sauce (spicy and regular) on the potatoes and chicken.

This place is fantastic! Came in from out of town expecting to deal with less-than-healthy pasta dishes as the only meal options for this vegetarian. Boy was I wrong, and I'm so glad! We found this place searching "vegetarian food" on Yelp and perused the menu. It all looked good and there were options for herbivores and carnivores so we were gonna give it a try but here's what really won me over: they have not only calorie information but macro information per serving too!!! As someone who counts macros this was just wonderful to see. Made it a no-brainer to try it and it did not disappoint. The food is delicious, healthy and well-proportioned. I wish there was a place like this back home! I didn't catch the guy working behind the counter's name but he was super nice and helpful as well. If you are in Reno looking for a healthy, macro-friendly or "special needs" diet option I really recommend stopping here.

Formerly Northstar Coffee Co, Zoma Cafe is my favorite coffee shop on State Street. They make a delicious white chocolate mocha and a variety of indulgent ice blended mochas (including peanut butter!) for the hot days, of which there are plenty in SB. If you're hankering for an AMAZING baked good, try the Tiger Bar. It's a half brownie, half chocolate chip cookie bar on top of a coconut crust. YUMMMM!

The place is very cozy. There is a great leather pair of chairs + couch, many low tables reconfigurable for groups, high tables perfect for studying or working alone, and plenty of plugs for laptop toters looking to use the free wi-fi. On top of all that, their playlist has impressed me repeatedly, including Devotchka, Owl City, Sigur Ros, Sam Sparro, and MANY more!

The staff is very friendly, talented, and accommodating. No custom creation request has stumped them. Oh, and there's a respectable discount when you use your own cup/mug/tumbler.

Stay classy, Cafe Zoma, and I'll continue to come back and sing your praises! :D

Really good pizza (really thin) but the rest of the menu is pretty average fair. They make a giant pizza you have to measure your front door to see if it will fit but most people only eat about a slice of it.

The beer and nachos are great here. However, the service that I experienced while ordering nachos on June 20 at about 4-5pm was horrible. The guy taking my order at the kitchen (wearing a mustache) obviously hated his job. I was extremely nice to him and he treated me like s***. This is my first time writing a Yelp review and he is the reason why. 

I would definitely go back but would not order any food if I saw him there.
Great sandwiches. My gf's was da bomb!! She got a mephis stax. My was good also. Very small place and packed! There is also outside seating. The staff was very friendly.

This is the walmart  closest to my house so I seem to always go there by default however, I might be finding a new one. The past few times I've been the meat selection hasn't been that great and last night the deli counter! whew! it took us 25 minutes to finish our order. The deli person was super slow had to ask her co worker a question about every single thing we asked for and oh before she even took our order we stood and watched her put away the meats from the other customer verrryyy slowly. It was super aggravating and ill tell you one thing, if we DO go back to this walmart for groceries we are definitely  skipping the lunch meat counter

Have been to Bliss Nails twice now, first for a peppermint pedicure and again yesterday for a dip nails manicure. Great experience both times. Pedicure was long, thorough and relaxing. They have different pedicure options. Manicure looks great! I love the dip nails and they last a long time. Had two different technicians both good. Very short wait time both trips, and the first my mom and I both got pedis at the same time. Will warn that it did get super busy while I was there (Friday around 4) and people did have to wait 30+ mins.

Came here while attending the Essence Festival food was so good we came 2 mornings in a row! I  would suggest getting the shrimp and grits. I Had that with the fried fish as well and asked for gravy on the side. The grits were nice and creamy, shrimp was tender and the fish was fried to perfection  with just the right amount of seasoning. The wait staff was also accommodating. The place is a bit small so get there early or there might be a wait.

If you need to buy in bulk or want quality products (I go here for the meats) or want cheap prescriptions or to refill ink cartridges and tons of other stuff. Its walmart but everything walmart isn't. They have good things not just junk. They pay people well. They care about customer service.
Props to being the first in St. Louis to serve Viet-Cajun!  Menu could be a little bigger but for what they do have they were all good.  The place was busy and the service was good.

My sister asked me if I was hungry at 10 PM and we were sitting in Grand Isle around 1030.  I think they close at 11 PM. You can imagine how annoying this might be to the staff, but we didn't detect a hint of annoyance. 

 I'm pretty sure our server's name was Michelle.  She was phenomenal.  Very kind and helpful.  My sister tends to ask 15 questions about one dish and then ends up ordering something completely different.  Michelle (if that was her name) wasn't even phased. 

 I started off with the crab cake, which was really great.  Someone remind me to take pictures next time.  Then I had the brisket.  It had a nice flavor and the presentation was cool.  They served it atop the lyonnaise potatoes with green beans.  It was moist and really tender.  Overall, it was well worth the money.  The entree was $18, I think.  

For desert I had the no flour chocolate cake.  It was really dense; almost a fudge consistency.  I'm a big fan of a flour-less cake.  I also had some french press coffee.  The coffee wasn't the best I had ever had, but it was very caffeinated and I do love that.

Appetizer, entree, desert, coffee and tip all came to $52 dollars for me. My sister and her husband were $86 for 2 alcoholic drinks, New York strip, a burger and desert. That's quite a bit of bang for your buck.  I will definitely be back.

This place is grand and is only about a 1 minute walk from my home.  I just moved here in January and ate breakfast at DeLuxe my very first full day in Reno.

The egg tacos were really yummy & original (French toast was just standard and more like a B-) and the hot almond chais have been really exceptional.  What I love most about the cafe, though, is the vibe.  Love the kind of folks it attracts, love the friendly owner, etc.  Moreover, DeLuxe let me camp out and use their free WiFi (while just ordering drinks and occasional desserts) when I first got here and was completely stranded without a phone or Internet connection.  

Thus, 5 stars!  Deluxe really rocks.  And another 10 points should be awarded for repurposing this old building.  I really dig that kind of urban planning.

Wish they were open for dinners!  I'd totally come here in the evenings.
Great bagels but the egg sandwiches are not good. They use a liquid egg solution and cook it in the microwave. The eggs taste pretty synthetic

It was my first time going to this place. The atmosphere is really laid back and relaxed, the building used to be an old school laundromat and you can still see some remnants of it, which I liked. The staff are super friendly and accommodating. The food is healthy and organic and they also have lots of vegan and vegetarian options. They are great with meeting your dietary needs. I had the cabbage hand salad which was a delicious salad wrap in rice paper. My only issue with the experience was finding a chicken bone in the wrap.

They do the coffee/tea right, the location is great and you have to like an open-air cafe that is low pressure. This place has the hipster vibe to it, with the laid back but friendly staff and a very chill environment compared to the vortex that is the French Market that lies just a block away.

The food at Sloppy Hoggs is good, even if it's overpriced by 30-50%.  Take advantage of the current Groupon specials to get the food at costs closer to what they should be if it were priced reasonably.  It can be a busy place, so don't be surprised if you have to wait awhile.  Call ahead if you intend to dine with friends.

Came here for a color correction. Jessica did an amazing job, better than I could ever imagine. Fast and efficient. Prices are not terrible. You have to pay for a blow dry. so if you don't want to pay $30 or $35, plan on leaving with a wet head. Overall, they do a great job there.

Go here! Food great, service great! Make a reservation so you don't have to wait! The first time I went I had the burger no bun with the truffle fries, oh my! Second time the short rib on polenta, delicious! You can't go wrong.

Their eggplant parm is terrible. Eggplant wasn't cooked right so it was chewy disgusting. Greek Caesar salad looked great except lettuce all wilted cause they didn't refrigerate. Too many other places to go before revisiting

I love Han. (Handy Nasty as I call it.)

I can't say too much more than others have said, but this location is the better of the two I've visited. 

Must: Dan Dan noodles & cucumbers. 
I love: The garlic style with pork or chicken, but I make it a level 7. I've had several other dishes, all adjusted to level 6 or 7 and I really haven't been disappointed ever. (Specifically, I have had the scallion style, hot sauce style, and crispy rice. But seriously, if you can't deal with hot food, this is not the place for you.)

The only thing I've had that I am not a fan of the cumin dish - my boyfriend LOVES it, but it's really dry and powdery to me. 

On the specials menu, the curry is seriously some of the best food I've ever had. It's not szechuan, though, so try that on your later visits if you really want the specialties. 

One day I will work up the courage for the level 10 dishes.

Came by this place after successfully completing an Escape room, and it definitely satisfies that carb craving on a cold day. The entrance is located down an alley, which is never appealing, but nothing ventured nothing gained. 

The cheesy garlic bread was on point, and their ranch was spot on. The BBQ chicken was the crowning moment for me. For one extra dollar, you can add smoked ghost pepper jack cheese, and let me tell you, it is 100% worth it. 

Also, clean bathroom. Always a plus.

First off let me start by saying this review doesn't reflect the taste by any means, because the burgers, tots and shakes are delicious. However, the service and the care for the customer are much less to be desired. This afternoon my wife took my two boys (3 and 17 months) out with a friend's family that's visiting from out of town. Naturally Burger Republic was the spot of choice since they wanted some great burgers. The trip quickly went downhill. My oldest has a pretty bad gluten allergy so they specifically requested the gluten free bun for his burger and let the waitress know. When the food came halfway through the bun they noticed that it was eerily similar to the rest of their regular buns. When they asked the waitress about it she then asked the kitchen staff and then informed my wife that the bun was in fact not gluten free and she was sorry about that. That to me is unacceptable. Although she apologized, nothing else was done after that to make the situation right. Now I have a son who's crying because his stomach isn't feeling well in between taking trips to the bathroom. If nothing else a manager should've been notified and/or the meal should've been comped. Luckily my son's allergy isn't as bad as some have it and he didn't have an immediate allergic reaction needing medical attention. Needless to say that supposedly great trip for out of town friends has now turned a days worth of fun activities into a day of back and forth bathroom visits and crying children. NOT COOL! Needless to say I can't in good conscience recommend Burger Republic any longer. Regardless of the great food, if they can't pay attention to the customer for something as easy as a gluten free bun request who's to say that the next time this happens there won't be serious consequences.

I ordered corned beef hash and was very disappointed. Prior to ordering, I asked our waitress if the cafe makes their own corned beef and she said No, they buy it, cut it in the kitchen and make corned beef hash out of it. So I assumed that I will get real corned beef hash. After 30mins or so, the waitress came out with my corned beef hash looking like it came from a can - unless they use a blender to cut the corned beef, anyone will know the difference. I just wished that the staff are knowledgeable with the food that they are serving. This is not cheap breakfast and I don't mind ordering other things on the menu if I was properly informed.

Just came back from our first visit to Mizu Sushi Bar.  What a great place for sushi.  Used a Groupon and they still honored happy hour prices on my husbands Sapporo and our appetizer.  We had six rolls and all were delicious.  Standouts being the Cardinal and Mizu Special.  Service was outstanding and cannot wait to return.

This restaurant is awful and the prices to match it are dreadful. Don't be fooled, because the restaurant looks beautiful from the outside. Unfortunately the sushi is not up to par with other places such as Mikado and Kobe.

Maybe i didn't order the right thing? I had a latte and it was decent but i couldn't taste as much of the espresso and tasted much of the cream from the latte art. My friends got the drafts and it was also just ok in my book. Perhaps i would appreciate the pour overs more but one would expect all the coffee drinks to be solid in a coffee house. It looked like their drink menu was limited to pour overs, espresso latte, and drafts so none of the pizzaz of Sbux. Drinks were kinda pricey for the size and quality imho.

The space was free and inviting. In fact most of the tables were filled. The large windows allowed for lots of light which was great on a sunny day like that day.

My family and I went over a show at the Walnut (5 minute walk which was awesome) and was recommended by two friends to try it out. Honestly thought the price was a little expensive for what you got, especially my meal of a Turkey Pot Pie which was $19 and that's all you got, no soup or salad or side. Don't get me wrong, everything that we had tasted really good, but for comfort food it wasn't comforting when I got the check. Definitely recommend the Chicken Parm, Mac & Cheese and if you don't mind the price the Turkey or Chicken Pot Pie (depending on what they have). Also I highly recommend getting a booth on the mezzanine over looking the whole restaurant, it was nice to be a little secluded from everyone else and had that sense of VIP. Only problem is that sometimes a server won't be right there when you need one and will have to wait for them to come back upstairs.  For an overall experience and the fact that it was a Stephen Starr restaurant it was good, just thought it could have been a little more for the price I paid.
Awesome food.  Tiki Masala was the best I've ever had.  Kids loved it, too.  Their delivery was very fast.  Not sure why this place doesn't have 5 stars.

Very good reviews and the hope of something different led me to this place. I was not impressed! Not enough drink specials. Cheapest margarita they have is about 8 oz. for S5.50 and that is their special.....c'mon. Tried the mongolian beef, the spicy shirmp, and the carnitas tacos. All were bland, dry and very uneventful. The cheese dip was good but not great. The atmosphere would get an A+ but that is about it. Not a bad place to hang out if you had no other options....................but you do.

Went here for lunch with some co-workers .. Service was decent and it was very busy.  I had the Chicken wings , which are huge and a decent portion for the price.   A cool spot to grab some lunch and reasonably priced.

Nice staff, but sometimes will really have to wait. 
There is only one women who mainly works there, and the rest are staff from the actual theater next door, so if your standing and waiting and saw that someone saw you, make sure you ask them to notify someone to help you, otherwise you will have to wait a bit longer.
Afterwards, great service-- quick and easy and pretty affordable

I actually work in the beauty field of Hair, skin and make up,(I was impressed) My boyfriend and I went in for massages on 1/4.... Can WE just say...... ERIC & VICTOR are ABSOLUTELY AMAZING, they will definitely be recommended for friends and family. We cannot wait to get back.... So if you have a chance amd you need to feel renewed amd revived!!! Those are the guys you MUST see
Really nice bakery beautiful selection friendly staff great place to sit and have a cuppa coffee and eat lots of wonderful pastries and cakes

First restaurant we are at while in New Orleans for my Birthday. We had reservations. It was great! Ordered the chicken and the dessert. I recommend!!! After a weekend at Nee Orleans, Luke's was on the top of the list.

The Meat Lovers Pizza was fabulous, good beer choice, great waitstaff and the four of us enjoyed the show immensely.  I haven't laughed this hard in a long time.  We're definitely coming back and bringing our friends.
The staff is friendly, the food is 7 courses and HUGE servings, great for a large group, and the belly dancer was a nice touch for a fun atmosphere.
What a special place. Comfortable and priced right. The food was excellent. The service was exceptional. I'll be back again and again.

Three stars, but that had a lot to do with service being good. As far as the food was concerned, I was pretty underwhelmed, if I'm being honest. Having rather recently dined at a different seafood boil establishment (The Shaking Crab in Norfolk VA), I had a pretty good comparison pretty fresh in my mind, and with that, The Boiling House under-delivered. 

Celebrating my mothers graduation, we decided to stop in and get a little messy on some seafood!.....or Vietnamese noodles. Apparently this place is both a seafood boil AND Asian noodle house. Ooook. After my mom threw the whole night into turmoil by ordering off the menu (which the staff WERE gracious enough to accommodate), we got on track and ordered. One vegan in our party went with just cajun fries. (Not many vegan options here, if thats a concern for you.) Another has an issue with seeing her food look like it looks before its food (why did we come here again?) so she went with some noodles, and my mother was playing fast and loose with the menu, so as far as the SEAFOOD BOIL goes, it was down to my sister and I to split a bucket. Snow crab legs, shrimp, potatoes, corn and a ciabatta roll; boiling house sauce, medium. 

First thing that was weird was that although everything has to be ordered by the pound, our crab legs had to be ordered in 1 1/4 pound increments. uh.....ok. Whatever. Second thing is that, the corn was mushy. Boiling corn must be a hard thing to do, as it was the same problem at the Shaking Crab. Third thing, and this is a big deal, were the shrimp. The shrimp were a good size, but they may as well have been made of pencil erasers. They were SOOOOOO chewy, and way more egregious than that, the shrimp weren't cleaned. Yuck. It took me 10 minutes before I could even start eating, because I had to clean every shrimp myself. 

The rest of the food was OKAY. The crab legs were fine, the potatoes were fine, but nothing blew me away. The sauce was.....ok. Decent flavor, decent heat....a little watery....I was just like, "meh," the whole meal. 

Our server was cool, and put up with a lot, (my mother is a handful) but he was polite throughout; asking the kitchen to make her special dish, and even pointing out to us that there is a military discount, so we got 10% off of the meal. 

The place was nice inside and its BYOB with no corkage, so they definitely have that going for them. 

I can't say for sure either way if I'd be back or not. Again, I wasn't thrilled with the meal, but aside from the shrimp, I wasn't put off by anything either. I guess we'll see.

Oh, the floor is like the Icecapades. We all almost broke our necks walking in, and our waiters assistant slipped and knocked over a bucket of ice. Wear something with some grip.

First time...had the bltb, bacon lettuce, tomato and Brie...it was good...although the bread was only lightly toasted...if it had been grilled it might have been superb! Who know... and chopped salad...salad was good...I had an old fashion with markers mark...told the wife it was the cleanest old fashion I ever saw...ingredients  weren't muddled as they say...and no ice...but don't get me wrong...I did like it...whatever it was!  When I order a second one the bar tender had changed and I got a traditional old fashion...almost missed the first one!  Dessert was the cookies and ice cream...which to our surprise turned out to be 2 servings of 2 large cookies with ice cream...I'll be back if only to try and recapture that first new fashion!?

Very good food, excellent wines, and great service. We had six dishes. The smoked duck over coleslaw with cherry chutney and the creamed mushrooms with a puff pastry cracker were the stars. The lamb meatballs were ok, and the beef skewers were disappointing---lacking flavor and salt, and a little dry. But the other dishes, the chocolate dessert, great wine, and service made up for this. Though it is about 10% overpriced, we will be back.
Super filling burgers that will leave you bursting at the end of your meal. Super yummy!

Yumioca is nestled in the same plaza as LETS Grill, Tropika and Syphay. I've been here one time previously but never realized that they're owned by the same people as Tropika. 

Both times that I've come it's been dead. We were the only ones there on a recent Monday evening. The inside is quite nice and several different areas to lounge around. They have a couple shelves of board games but some aren't in the best shape. Saw connect 4, monopoly, scrabble and jenga (the Asian coloured version). Selection isn't the greatest. 

Only one worker was manning the front. They were out of lychee pieces (huh?) and only had enough tapioca pearls for half a drink. I know it was near the end of the night but that's still pretty ghetto. 

- Vanilla bubble tea ($4.95) - L and Jboy shared a vanilla BBT. Tasted like vanilla ice cream in drink format. A little too sweet for my taste buds. 
- Mango slush ($5.15) - went with mango bear pieces. Slush was pretty good except  several sips had bits of ice that hadn't been crushed enough. 

Decent enough BBT here but I wouldn't be making a special trip out for it.

I love love love the small Italian cafe feel that this place radiates. Our waiter had an accent and was very generous, made us feel like family at the table. The food was even better than the service, both my husband and I devoured every thing - especially the garlic bread. So many delicious options from appetizers to entrees to wine!

Had lunch and drinks there while staying at the Guy Harvey. 

The chicken fajita wrap was very good and my wifes steak tacos were very good. 

But The atmosphere is really cool to have a drink in. 

It was pricey like everything on the resort but friendly staff and quick service. 
It has a nice breeze and you can see the gulf from inside.

I had been to Rembrandt's once before. I agree with the over pricing and the crowded atmosphere that other people have mentioned. Still, it's a neat venue and thought I would give it another try. 

The second time we were greeted with horrible customer service, so bad that we left without ordering. We arrived at 10:50 am for brunch. Apparently the kitchen closes at 11:00am. We were unaware. We stood in line behind about 10 people for close to 5 minutes. At 10:56 the cashier angrily came over and announced the kitchens closes at 11:00 and they are cutting us off. No apology, not even any eye contact. She pointed to the person standing directly in front of me and said you are the last to be served. There was only 2 of us left. She wouldn't even accommodate 2 more people 5 minutes before the kitchen was closing. She, Rae as we later asked for her name, does not understand customer service. We had been patiently waiting and had arrived before the closing of the kitchen and she didn't even have the decency to apologize. She stomped away and was abrupt to ever person that came to her register next. We left without even ordering coffee. We were not going to stand for horrible service and give these people our money.

I love this grocery store...I could spend hours in there shopping. Everything is so fresh!  So glad you came to our little neighborhood. I used to drive all the way to Tampa to visit the Fresh Market.

Asahi is small family owned business with its own unique charm. the service is very slow in the dining even on slow nights so i typically choose only to do take out due to the poor in house performance.  Even take out takes some time. However the sushi here is extremely fresh and worth the sometimes long wait. Asahi also has amazing prices with most of the rolls being between 5-10 dollars even for specialty rolls. This is the best sushi place in the Belle Meade area, lacks the atmosphere and number of speciality rolls of Ninki but the quality of sushi speaks for itself.

This place was exactly what I hoped it would be! Super cute, with good food and great desserts. We got there on Saturday around 11:15AM and had no wait at all, but there was a line out the door by the time we left an hour later. I had seen the pickle soup on the menu and was dying to try it, so of course I ordered that as my side to the roast beef sandwich. The soup was very pickle-y, not lightly pickle-y, but I loved it. Roast beef sandwich was good - simple and served on tons of crusty bread. For dessert, I had to try the pineapple cake in a cup with the Chocolate Almond Joy ice cream. It was a dream in a cup (a really really big cup). I would have eaten every bite if I didn't feel physically ill midway through from so much food. I would love to come back here and it was perfect for right before a matinee at the Fox.

So Nick was our driver...he. Is. Thee.BEST!! OMG! We had so much fun! I at first thought this would be like a cycling class at the gym because of course after sitting on a bike seat for so long begins to hurt, but the liquor was flowing so I didn't think about it. Nick was so much fun. He gave us the aux cord and let us DJ. He even danced and rapped which blew us away!  He helped make our ride a good time. I will be doing this again.

We stayed in the Hotel Indigo this past weekend for my wife and I's 15 year wedding anniversary.  We wanted to experience a bit of the nightlife downtown had to offer.  The hotel was good for that, being adjacent to the capital complex and just a very short cab ride down to all of the hustle and bustle on Broadway.  Valet parking was expensive at $28, but very quick and convenient.  We arrived about 20 minutes before check in time into a modern lobby with restaurant and bar.  Our room was not ready so we went for a drink at the bar.  We were pleased to find a full bar with several local beers on tap.  We had just raised our drinks when the manager came over just a couple minutes later saying they had a room for us and we were upgraded.  We were allowed to take our drinks with us so we headed up the brass elevator.  The room was small but nicely decorated.  I am not sure what the upgrade was, maybe since it was a corner room with two windows it was considered an upgrade?  No matter we were well treated and happy to have the room a few minutes early.  The bedding was nice.  An oversized flat screen TV was there for the viewing.  The hotel should score 4 stars.  The reason I gave it only three was because of some cleaning issues in the room.  One of the pillows had fuzz and hairs all over it where it was dropped on the floor by housekeeping when they made the bed.  There was one pubic and two long hairs that were plainly visible in the all white walk in shower, and the caulk joints were moldy.  We also found an alligator hair clip was on the tray left waiting for us on the bed with two hospitality waters and ice bucket.  If we had a cleaner room, it would get a four star review.  It was otherwise a nice place to stay.

This food tour was horrible, both the food and the tour guide.  We have been on numerous food tours in Philadelphia with other tour groups that far exceeded what Best Tours offered on this tour.  In addition, we went with another couple that was new to Philly and it was a complete let down all around.  First, the tour guide didn't speak to the entire group, he addressed only 1 person in the group; there were 20 people in our group. Second, he never gave the group a full description of the places we went to, or anything regarding the area we were going to.  Third, the pizza places were so so, but nothing that great.  There were only 3 stops on the tour, and again, I couldn't tell you why these 3 places were selected as the tour guide did not say.  The first place you had a choice of 2 types of cheese pizza, the second place you got half a slice of pizza, and third place you got a slice of either cheese or pepperoni; horrible selection for a "pizza tour".  We were very disappointed with the tour.   Stick with the other food tour groups such as Chew Philly and City Food Tours.  Much better experience, tour guides and food.

Upon entering the restaurant I was looking forward to enjoying some good company, food and music but shortly after sitting down I slowly was let down. While I did enjoy the music I was first informed they were out of mint so I could not order a mojito, mind you this was around  6:30pm on a Friday night. What kind of Mexican establishment doesn't stay stocked with fresh mint, especially on one of the biggest drinking days of the week. I sadly had to settle for another cocktail. I then proceeded to order the chicken tacos which were a huge disappointment from looking at other dishes served. It was literally dry chicken, rice and cheese. Overall first time dining experience was a major let down.

The service started out great and the food was good, then a shift change happened.  The bar was not busy, and the service was terrible.  Food that was ordered never came out, took 45 minutes to get a side salad before our meal.  May or may not try again.
Real Cuban/Puerto Rican food. Met with the owner and chef... Very nice! Well worth the money! Can't wait to go again!

This is one of the better Indian restaurants I've been to recently. Upon request, they can make the biryani rice wickedly spicy. The tandoori is a bit bland, but the vindaloo is worth the trip. Highly recommended with a mango or pomegranate lassie!

I don't know how I'd never had pizza from here before, but I don't think I'll ever have pizza anywhere else now! We ordered from Gourmet last night because it was on the UberEATS app. Without a doubt, the best pizza you will ever eat, including the gluten free options. The BLT pizza is incredible. The prices are very reasonable. A Tampa prize!!
I stopped in here this morning and the place was a bit dirty and shop worn.  The pharmacy was not open so I left without getting anything.  There was only one person staffing the place.

This is a must-go tiki bar. The bartender obviously cares about his craft of creating a fantastic tiki experience. Top notch drinks, excellent presentation, a fun atmosphere that makes you want to stay for another drink, and a playlist that completes the whole experience. This place will become a regular stop on our future trips to New Orleans.

Vegetarian/vegan/meat friendly tasty food, but I always feel mildly sick afterwards. Service is friendly. Very average espresso. This place gets very busy. The chai tea is famous, but too sweet for me. Actually, all non-meal food I've had from here has been too sweet, but that's my own fault--I don't like sweet food.

This place is popular for a reason, you can't go wrong with Remedy--although you wont see me there.

This is a place you could easily pass right by, without realizing what is tucked away on the side of the road. The studio grounds and chapel are all beautiful, nestled up against a backdrop of the Catalina mountains and all those stately saguaro cacti. You can't take a bad photo here. 
Visiting the little gallery/museum is very interesting. For anyone who has ever lived in Tucson, Ted DeGrazia is a legend so getting to see his work and discover more about his life is very interesting. Everything is very well done and maintained. My favorite part is that beautiful little chapel where you can go and just sit and reflect. Unfortunately, I read that the chapel was recently badly damaged by a fire. Here's hoping they're able to restore this charming little gem of the desert.
All the choices, easy in/out parking, always fresh, tastes amazing every time. My favorite is the Power Bowl. It's a must go.

The food is awesome,  huge side portions and wraps. My friend and I picked the first 2 wraps on the board to share. Forgot the names already, but one had pork, and the other had steak as the meat. Both had plenty of veggies, rice, and other goodies stuffed and rolled tight in their wraps. We picked 3 salads (the Greek, broccoli, and sweet potato) for sides to try. Each were good, but both of our favorites were the Greek. 

Layout and where you have to go to pay is a little confusing, but the staff is nice and helped us new-bees. Tall ceilings and open kitchen concept in a auto garage shell is fine with us. Walls were decorated in awesome graffiti art, and we enjoyed looking at the album covered tables, games, and local art. Staff had an eclectic look and were well trained- didn't act like corporate robots. Which is always a plus. I didn't see this place as "a wanna be hipster place", just a relaxed restaurant were anyone can come and enjoy good food. I've watched suit and tie guys, military in uniforms,  hippies,  college students, kids with parents and everyone in-between come in and eat. 

Bathroom was clean and had plenty of back up toilet paper and paper towels in a basket. 

Overall great food, great atmosphere, good music, awesome staff. So glad we stopped at Phat Bites to eat. This area needed a place like this.
Just went to hit some balls. A large bucket is $14, so I literally walked out. Plus, you can only hit off mats.

We have 6 ppl this time. Shared two pizzas, one salad and one pasta, which is pretty much enough for us.

We got the martini seasonal pizza and it was great! Definitely go with the white sauce pizza. To me, white sauce tastes better than red sauce.

We tried the blueberry and Greek salad too! It's amazing and the portion is pretty big too! Good for sharing among 4 or more people.

Servers are nice and food comes pretty quickly! Good place for hanging out.

Visit time/day: weekend lunch
Atmosphere: typical Chinese takeout

Yet another mediocre Chinese takeout place. Ordered the Chicken & Mixed Veg Diet Dish with Garlic Sauce lunch special. Veg were slightly overcooked (still had a little crunch but I prefer more), chicken breast sliced thin but very rubbery (likely due to steaming). Garlic sauce was very good - they should bottle this! BF ordered General Tsao with fried rice - nothing special and kind of made him feel ill afterwards (*not* implying anything about the food quality, think it was more the greasy + sugary + boogery meat combo that made him feel grose). 

Pro: lunch specials come with a can of soda and they have an interesting selection, well beyond Coke or Pepsi (Hawaiian Punch - yes!, Root Beer, etc.). Not being a huge soda drinker I would have preferred an egg roll, but kudos for the soda variety :)

Probably won't go back especially when Ivory is just a few blocks away. I prefer veg more al dente, tofu options, and in an idealistic world, soup and/or egg roll with a lunch special.
Love this place! Great patio area, great bartenders, and great drinks. My go to starter spot!
Nice quiet short walk in the woods on a cold day.  Look forward to seeing in the spring

Great, speedy service! The workers are very nice, and the place is very clean. I always bring my cat here for checkups and shots. I've never had a problem with anything here. The workers seem to genuinely care about my cat and put effort into making her visits comfortable.

After getting the shake down from the bartender ... he asked for IDs and credit cards to verify age/name, we were very well taken care of by the staff. 

For a Tuesday night, there was a good crown on hand.  Beers were well priced and had a number of options outside of your "normal" bud/coors selections. 

There's are a good number of TVs here and the Panasonic 60 inch TV is killa! 

Great place to watch a sporting event or even relax with brew in hand ... 

Not sure on the food as we didn't eat here ...

This store is so much larger than the Speedway Marsh. The vegetables and fruit are always fresh and I love the fresh flower selection. The meat department is extremely helpful so don't hesitate to ask a question. They will grind meat for you and butterfly pork chops if you ask. Customer service, cashiers and stock folks have always been courteous. The store isn't laid out as you would image so be prepared to ask for assistant or go insane wandering the store. Not sure if the layout was experimental but much wasted space with isle layout forcing you to waste time crossing the store.Worth the effort once your familiar with layout and isle since they carry more items than most Marsh stores on the Westside. They are great about opening extra cashier lines when the lines get long and they do during the normal crazy hours.

The food here was so delicious there is no doubt that i will be returning. There were four of us when we went here and next time i want to get two more to join because there was so much food i couldn't finish It all! They give you a towel for your lap and you can take as much bread as you want, the whole meal is eaten with the bread and your hands. If you split the bill with everyone the price isn't bad at all. Also amazing atmosphere can't wait to go back!
Always get a Sicilian pizza here and they never disappoint. The staff here feel like family!

Clearwater is one of the most beautiful places I have visited. We picked pier house 60 due to its great location and affordable rooms. Great size studio room but not great for noise. With the balcony closed you could still hear most of what was happening outside especially the pirate ship and beeping horns. Beds were fairly comfortable and a small but very clean continental breakfast included.

Now why I have only given 3 stars... We went to bed at 10pm our last night tucked in and by 10:30 crazy loud laughter, talking and music from the next room. I had to call at 10:30pm, 12:30am, 1:30am and 2:45am it would get quiet for a min then go right back. Finally fell asleep at 3:45 am and had to wake up for 6:30 to get out for our day. When I spoke with management they confirmed they had a 1 warning policy and we're sorry. No compensation what so ever, and the girl at the desk confirmed it was a bachelorette party. So I got less then three hours of sleep and a sorry. I'm sorry but that is unacceptable! There are plenty of hotels in the area with great and even better views that will get my business, not here!
If your looking for peace and quite you may want a different hotel
Oysters every way! Was great! Will be back. Music great. Just wished they had ginger beer for Moscow mules!

Rude, surly, and unhelpful! Service was not just slow, it was HOSTILE. These people act like you are crashing a private party at their home! Not only did they not apologize for fucking up my order, they acted like I should apologize for asking them to fix it. I spend plenty of time in dive bars with "relaxed" service. But these people were not "relaxed," they were pissed at customers for being there. No wonder we were some of the only people there on a Friday night. Plus, the bathrooms are nasty (even for a bar) and the whole place REEKS of old beer. I could get better food and service at a Quick Trip, and Quick Trip will give you FREE WATER.

There is never a traditional "wait" here, always a solid conversation to be had with a fellow patron or a barber. There's also USB ports for charging your devices if you need to stay working until you're the next on the list. They also hand out time appropriate beverages - walked in around 10AM & was instantly offered a fresh coffee even though there was no wait time. Music is always great too - indie-rock vein. Their haircut quality is excellent! they take the time to meet their [& your new] expectations. 

Note: you can call for anticipated next available barber times but you have to be physically present to write your name on the list - so, plan accordingly.
Wow! The hype surrounding this restaurant is certainly merited. Loved the conch, gazpacho, and roasted chicken. Looking forward to visiting again!
Nice place, the restaurant left something to be desired. Not located in a "fun" part of town. Its right next to the airports so makes sense for some.

This place is awesome. The owners are fantastic and so kind. The environment is relaxing and really upscale looking. If you're in the area you should definitely give this place a shot. I would definitely go again.

The last hot yoga class I went to was a Bikram class in Paris during the summer of 2013 so when my lululemon friend suggested that I join her for yoga and brunch, I was a little more than intimidated.  Not only was it Vinyasa flow, it was hot! 

I'm so glad I took the plunge and tried out Priya!!! The space is absolutely beautiful.  The clean lines and extra seating areas are great- no one wants to be squished in next to sweaty, warm bodies.  The colors are soothing and fresh as well.

I loved the instructor.  The class was challenging but not intimidating.  I like that the instructor also included a little ab work.  (Much needed after the holidays!)

Overall, the staff was super friendly, accommodating and helpful.  I am excited to go back again and again and again!  Fairmount is lucky to have Priya!

At first glance you see a small, log-cabinesque structure as you drive down main street in Imperial. Then it hits you what it is with the large sign in front of it and the cars in the lot. I cannot say enough about this place, it usually has super fresh veggies at a reasonable cost along with other items that you can use with the veggies and fruits! Fresh breads too, along with milk and dairy items! The owners are helpful as well as those who work there as well.

1st time visit after the remodeling which seemed to only be a Mexican motif on the walls. The menu retains some bar food (burgers, sandwiches) and adds Mexican items (enchiladas, fajitas, burritos). Wish they would have refinished the tables and renovate the bathrooms instead. The American Burger I had was a freshly made patty done perfectly and delicious. My friend had the open face roast beef which he loved. Although the food was good, I probably won't be going back due to lack of ambience. Seems to be a lost restaurant looking for an identity!
I got my tragus pierced by Theodore and he made me feel so comfortable and he was super nice and personable! if you're looking for a good piercer in tucson go here!

If you are someone who loves putting fancy toppings on their burger, Village Whiskey is your place. And if you are someone who loves over-the-top fries, even loading them up with cheese and meat, Village Whiskey is your place. If you are like me, and just want a simple cheeseburger with salted fries, Village Whiskey is NOT your place. 

Now, what I do really like about Village Whiskey is their pickles. They are the perfect combo of sharp, salty, and sweet. The pickles come with thick slices of bread, the most luxurious butter-like dairy product (It seems too good to be butter, yet it's obviously not margarine and is probably just really good butter), and tapenade. I especially love their beet pickles.

I have also gone to Village Whiskey a few times for cocktails. While I believe they are typically full on weekend evenings, I have never had a problem finding a seat on a weeknight or after dining hours on a weekend. The cocktails are well-crafted.

So to sum it up, over-the-top burgers and fries (good or bad depending on your preference), fantastic pickles, and solid cocktails!
I caught the review on 13 news a couple of months ago and I finally was in the neighborhood so I stoped by and I had the Barito and it was amazing. It was!!!

I enjoy a good tea, especially when I am about to get on the train or a plane and know I will be dehydrated for awhile.  The 30th Street Train Station has a variety of options for tea and other drinks, but I think this Cosi rates. The service is always good, the staff really is friendly and quick to serve (they realize, I think, that most of us are running for the train and time is of the essence), and they accommodate your desires.  I was able to buy a large sized tea with one tea bag and a little soy on the side. Now that is not something I can do at just any tea or coffee shop.  

I will continue to use Cosi when I am travelling through the train station!
excellent general gau's tofu/vegetable. Nice and spicy.  Exceptional service and attention to detail.  The owner is an absolute sweetheart, very nice woman.  Check this place out.
Great place for bagels.  One of the absolute best!  No puffy, air bagels, but good, chewy ones.

Plush is a MUCH needed addition to the Midtown neighborhood surrounding SLU. Located on Locust just west of Compton, Plush provides quality, but very affordable, breakfast, lunch and dinner. They've got 20 beers on tap and a huge room devoted to music acts.

I went for dinner  on a Friday night and had a great experience. The place has a good feel to it and a simple dinner menu and many beer options. We were given a drinks menu (unlike a previous reviewer). I had the crawfish roll w/fries for $9 that tasted great that was perfectly spiced. I washed it down with two Schlafly Hefs for $4.75 each. My buddy had big veggie burger with fries that he said was good for under $7. Overall, a great experience. I will definitely be back.

Probably one of the coolest experiences I had while dining in St. Louis. 

Right when we walked in I noticed it was a very welcoming and trendy atmosphere. I went on a Monday night so it wasn't too crowded either which made it nice. 

I ordered the Cock-a-Doodle Noodle calzone which came filled with mac n cheese, chicken, bacon and green onion. The very nice and helpful girl that was taking my order recommended getting queso as my sauce, I obliged, and was not disappointed. 

The calzone was perfectly crispy and the chicken and bacon really balanced out the creaminess of the mac n cheese. The queso was outstanding and had a lot of flavor. I also enjoyed that they had fountain soda that was not the traditional Pepsi or Coke products.

If you want a 5-star experience go to Sauce on the Side.

Great Thai food. We decided to go to Singha for lunch during the week. As we walked in we were seated immediately in the back. It appears that this was a patio at one time, since the roof looks like a tent, but it is a pretty interesting room. Even though it was warm outside the room felt air conditioned and comfortable.

I ordered chicken curry, Thai hot. This is the first dish I have ever ordered Thai hot that came this hot. It was incredibly spicy. They blend so many flavors together to excite all of your taste buds at once. It was very good. Even though it was incredibly spicy, it was still amazingly flavorful. I absolutely loved it.

Our other entree was cashew chicken. It was not hot, but was as flavorful as the chicken curry. It was great.

Singha has really great food and the total bill for two entrees and one drink was only $24 with the tip.

Although this was only my second trip to Singha, I will definitely be back.

Had to make a pit stop on 95 and spotted the Golden Eagle Diner sign.  It was a bit off the beaten track, but the food was good.  I particularly liked the steaming hot joe and German Chocolate cake. Big shreds of coconut, light cake, and frosting not too sweet.  

Our waitress, Linda, brought everything piping hot. She clearly worked hard to do her best for all her customers. Very efficient and diligent. 

It's open 24hours. Good to know.

Great hang out pizza place, dine in or take out. This place is so neat and usually busy. Sometimes there is a wait, but so worth it. The decor is all vintage, lots of it is from local Florida. Seating inside is all large wooden booths and there's outdoor courtyard seating as well. They have a variety of classic soda, a few beers on draft, and a good variety of bottled beer from micro breweries.

The food is delicious! If you go with a group (or even by yourself), I highly recommend ordering a large Greek salad to share. They have both New York and Chicago style pizza. I love the New York style, either make your own or the Cappy's is really good. Everything is made fresh to order, so if you're in a hurry call ahead. We like to chill out, have a few beers and salad while they make our pizza.

NOTE: They only take cash, but there is an ATM there if you forget.

This place had a long line, and we went on a Monday! Worth the wait, though. While there was parking behind the building we had to circle a few times bc it was still so busy!

While I don't have any other hot chicken to compare this to, I was impressed and found everything on my plate to be delicious. The brisket tacos were also very yummy! The sides weren't anything special.

After we ate we walked around this neighborhood, which was really fun.

Sometimes when you have a hangover, all that will cure it is biscuits from Cracker Barrel. So you drive to your local Cracker Barrel, hope there isn't too long of a line, and you get a table. You order chicken fried chicken and some of that hashbrown casserole and biscuits. You wash it all down with diabetes-inducing sweet tea. And you don't care that this is a chain, or that the food isn't that great (it's salty, it's greasy, it's processed). All that you care about is that you got food in your stomach ASAP. This Cracker Barrel is just like all the other Cracker Barrels. Mediocre chain food, mediocre chain service, mediocre chain atmosphere.
And as with ALL Cracker Barrels, try to get there early or at off-peak times.

I love Henpeck on Sundays! Their brunch is SO good! You can get any type of omelette and the buffet is a little different every weekend. I'm trying to watch my weight so I get an egg white omelette with veggies. The guys do a great job cooking them and the vegetable dishes are very tastefully done and the desserts are good as well. I splurge sometimes and get a dessert from time to time. My favorite is the banana pudding. Delicious!!

This place is fantastic. A family friend designed the interior of this historical site for Kevin Costner (the owner). 

The filet mignon was superb, the sea bass, melty, flaky, buttery and sublime. I was skeptical that cabbage soup could be put on a menu at a place like this, so I tried it and it was great; the heirloom tomato salad was a little on the sparse side, even for this type of fare. 

The service was excellent (I guess you have to be a sexy Australian dude to apply for a waiting position here) and the bartender even politely obliged my guest's request for 7up in his $20 glass of sauvignon blanc.
I thought Luke was pretty good, though I wasn't blown away.  We tried a selection of dishes that we all shared.  The pasta was great-really fresh. The grits were a bit too heavy for me.

Wow!! Compared to the run-of-the-mill markets out in southern Maine, this place rocks!! So much more selection than Shaw's; so many more brands than Hannafords; much much better wine selection than Market Basket; amazing grab-n-go section with both affordable, healthy, vegan, and more luxurious options; and this Dierbergs is not even considered particularly upscale!!  What a hoot, they have a  smoker outside selling barbecue, awesome!! In the three times I visited this place, I was never able to sample the que, but the idea warmed my heart. The coolest thing of all: they sell wine and beer, open, in the store, so that you can get drunk while you shop!! HOW COOL IS THAT!!!??  They say one should not shop on an empty stomach, imagine what you come home with on a drunken empty stomach!! Even better, it just gets better, plenty of parking, and BOTH Trader Joes and Whole Foods are in the next parking lot. Metro link is just around the corner too.... Makes me want to move to ST. LOUIS, who would have thunk it??

Our go to electrician since he added a whole bunch of outlets, lights and wiring to our old Mt. Airy home. Work is done on time and professionally at a very fair rate and Jack is always easy to contact by phone when you need him. We've recommended him to friends and they are just as happy as we are.

I was driving by this divey Mexican restaurant and thought I'd grab some food.  The server was nice and attentive.  I was expecting some delicious authentic Mexican food.  I got a few chili rellenos and a tamale.  The tamale was very tough and didn't have much flavor.  The chilli rellenos' batter was just egg on the outside.  Basically an omelet rapped pepper.  I didn't have a bad experience or anything and they are friendly.  The food was just subpar.  I wish them the best, but I wouldn't return.

Upscale restaurant with a wonderful view! Make reservations ahead of time and request a window seat. If you're not too hungry, they have a beautiful bar area for happy hour to view the sunset. Wonderful service and delicious food. Definitely try the lobster mac and cheese!

I'm so glad I found this place when pregnant and that I'm part of the community as a new parent! It's a really wonderful resource. They meet you where you are and help you on your journey. The space itself is so comfy and lovely. I've taken the childbirth prep class, a belly-dance for birth class, and the new mom's circle and will continue to take advantage of more offerings. The instructors are all highest quality and make the classes fun, while delivering detailed, balanced information and support with no judgment (no small thing when parenting advice can be so dogmatic). The owner and instructors are truly caring and will go the extra mile for you, such as when I needed more support around breastfeeding: I got great one-on-one help and the referral I didn't know I needed to fully problem-solve with a specialist. I also really enjoy the other people that come around Then Comes Baby, and my partner and I have made several new friends. It's great not only to meet parents in the same crazy stage of life, but also to connect with like-minded folk I'd want to be friends with anyway! All that I could have hoped - they are truly creating amazing new community and making us such better informed and skilled parents!

This is a really good little place, though the menu is REALLY confused. We both had the bibimbap, and I just wish they would focus on that instead of the ton of random salads. Stopped here while traveling from Tennessee to Michigan, and our food was ready in very little time.

The bibimbap was a good portion size, with plenty of addins and a good sauce. The waitress asked me if I really wanted to put that much sauce on - of course I did! Bubble tea (green) was good as well, and reasonably inexpensive for a large container.

I was introduced to this place while on a business trip.  It's located in a small town and seems to be one of the few big diners around there.  It's a nice family style restaurant which serves up a variety of dishes suitable to satisfy all palates.  The service is very friendly and fast, regardless of how packed they may be.  Try their many homemade dishes.

After years of hype, I've finally tried Federal Donuts! They're good as donuts go--not greasy, kind of cake-y but not dense.

We got one of each flavor and shared them as a group back at home. Without knowing which donut was which, it was honestly hard to tell what flavors they were on the ones dipped in flavored sugars. The flavors weren't terribly strong. I liked the chocolate donut best.

Next visit, I look forward to trying their chicken.
Excellent. Loved the fried chicken and beans. The shrimp and grits was phenomenal as well. Great atmosphere.

I ate lunch there today for the first time and it was fantastic! I will be back. The coffee is the best I have ever had. The man working at the time asked me how it was and I replied "Great, I've never been here!" I think he may have thought I said "I've had better." He seemed suprised that someone would say such a thing, now I feel bad. I just want to reiterate that I have not had better, this is the best Cuban food I have ever had.

I decided I had to do the touristy thing and stop at the St. Louis Gateway Arch when I was road tripping to KCMO. About a week prior to my trip, I pricelined a hotel for downtown St. Louis and found this hotel for a steal! I didn't arrive to the hotel til past 9pm so I didn't really get to check out the surroundings too much. Someone else said that the area seemed a bit dicey...it just seemed desolate to me. I wouldn't consider it dicey, but then again, I hang out in Detroit all the time, so dicey takes on a whole new meaning to me. 

The hotel itself was beautiful. Built in a historical train station, it still retains its original structure and features of a larger station. The staff was super nice and hospitable. My room which overlooked the indoor mall was pretty much your normal Marriott room...nice king sized bed, clean room and bathroom. Parking was very close by and at a decent rate. Overall, I was pretty happy with the hotel and its location as it was easy for me to grab the MetroLink train to the Arch so I could do my tourist thing in the am. I would definitely return if I'm in the area again.

Forget Pat's and Geno's.  This is authentic Philly sub's right here.  I love a provolone, onion cheese steak and  these guys know how to make it.  Bread is what makes this the best place i've been to.  Why wait in line for 30 minutes at the tourist traps when you can go to George's and get a real sandwich.  This place needs more credit, but I love that its tucked away in the Italian market which keeps it more accessible to the locals.

I recently woke up to no hot water and realized that my hot-water heater was leaking and was probably shot.  I called a few of the obvious companies, one of them being Hiller Plumbing, and they sent somebody out to give me an estimate. I met the technician at my home and he said right away that it would have to be replaced due to the leaking, which I told the lady when I first called in.  He was going to charge me to come out and tell me that ($65.00, if I remember correctly) and said that it would be $1,200 to replace the appliance.  I told him I didn't need the top of the line model, and he said that was what was available and that was the cost.  Due to my pointing out that his office should have known it was shot if he didn't even have to look at it to know that it was shot (the leaking), I didn't have to pay the service charge (a plus for Hiller).  I thought the price was very high, so I asked some friends at work if they had any suggestions.  They told me about Sullivan Plumbing, so I called and talked with them.  They were able to fit me into their very busy schedule the next day, which I thought was wonderful since I had already been a couple of days without hot water.  They came out and the end result was a new water heater for $850.  They were very gracious, kind, helpful and weren't out to rob me like I believe Hiller was.  They are a family business that have been in the area for a few generations, which says a lot to me.
Perfect place with great soups and everything what we have ! Food was delicious and also the sweets...

This is one of my favorite spots in STL. I love the atmosphere. The food is delightful, the lattes are all very good and the service is always friendly. Whether I am out with someone or just need quite place to work this place is a good fit for both!

At the top of my Christmas list this year is that someone would open a huge, friendly coffeehouse near my house with WiFi and plenty of outlets and a lot of room. It hasn't happened yet but someone opened one up in Washington West which is totally not fair since Good Karma is an easy walk from the awesomeness of Chapterhouse.

I'll forestall my bitterness for now and just be glad that I can stop walking a whole two blocks than before if I really must be at a coffeehouse that much sooner. Good Karma is BIG and bright and has a lot of outlets and WiFi. There's a large selection of baked good and drinks other than coffee and tea. That's cool. They have two nice bathrooms, too, and no one bothers you and they're open late. Could this be coffeehouse love?

The downsides are the food's not great. There's a sign telling you not to bring food from elsewhere which I must respect but I must admit to being a little sad inside when I have to bite into one of their moist, overly eggy scones knowing there are great ones out there made by our own Metropolitan Bakery. The coffee's fine, as far as a brew is concerned but as a fellow Yelper said, the lattes leave much to be desired. They're confused as to what makes a latte and what makes a cappuccino. I ordered one once and none since. 

But what can I say. I'll take the bad scones and indifferent coffee drinks for the genuine friendliness of the place and my face is as green as their mugs when I think about how spoiled that neighborhood is while my part of town is totally bereft of coffeehouse awesomeness.

Oh, cash only though there's an expensive ATM on the premises.

Hella's has been my go-to Greek restaurant in Tarpon. It never disappoints and the atmosphere is great. The saganaki aka the "flaming cheese" is by far my favorite thing on their menu, I could eat the whole thing to myself. Definitely a must try! Their mussels are also amazing and have great flavor (make sure to dip your bread in the sauce). Their gyros are also by far my favorite gyro in Tarpon, full of flavor and the toasted pita bread is delicious!
Amazing exoerience! Walked in for a full set with gel and a pedi. Great quality on both.less than $70 and about 95 minutes. Will DEFINITELY be back!!!

I returned to Paradise Bakery & Cafe to give them another shot and, boy, am I glad I did!

A colleague and I hopped on over to Paradise during our lunch break. We were greeted by an employee the moment we walked in the door, which made us feel quite welcomed! There were a few people in front of us in line, but the line moved very quickly! We placed our order and found a table (it was pretty crowed at lunch time, but there was still plenty of seating).
