It was my turn to pick up food for my monthly lunch with a group of coworkers and we went with Pita Jungle. Now I've eaten AT Pita Jungle before but never picked up food to go. I wasn't entirely sure their food would transport well but luckily it all arrived in tact and still quite pretty. 

When I arrived at Pita Jungle the food was freshly packaged and waiting at the front register. By the time I got it to my place of employment just a short 3 miles away the individual pizza was still hot, the wraps still toasty in their foil packaging and the salads....well, they're salads. They were still cold, OK?

Everyone seemed to enjoy their food and I can only review my meal which was the Yellowfin Tuna Honey Sesame Salad. Served on a bed of fresh greens, were pineapple, strawberries and mango topped with seared tuna. The dressing served with this dish is a flavorful honey sesame vinaigrette - loved it! The seared tuna was okay but didn't appear to be a high grade tuna. The texture of the meat wasn't what I expected but the flavor was still good. Maybe it was that I'm more used to sushi grade tuna and it isn't sliced as thick as the tuna at Pita Jungle.

But the baklawa  (baklawa? I guess it's both baklawa and baklava according to Wikipedia...hopefully I haven't offended anyone over the years with improper pronunciation) was amazingly flaky and delicious. When placing my phone order I told the girl I wanted baklawa for everyone. She told me it came 3 to an order. I replied that I just wanted everyone to have one piece. She then said, OK, so 7 then. Whooooweeee!! We had baklava coming out our ears. She gave me seven ORDERS, not seven pieces. Frankly, it didn't go to waste thank you very much. 

Pita Jungle - thumbs up!

Fun place in downtown st Pete. Drinks are fantastic. I always go with an old fashioned and it was very well made. My date had a whiskey sour which they made with actual egg white. A nice and pleasant change. The drink was very tasty. Great spot to go for a date, but it is rather cramped inside at times. I went on a Friday around 9 and it was packed, which is to be expected. Even with the business, it wasn't a terrible wait to get a drink

I stayed here for a conference of 10,000 + people. The hotel was sold out, which is awesome for them!

The analogy I'd use for this lodging experience is this: it's like when you meet a really ripped gorgeous dude, and you start talking with him, and there's really no personality there, but he's easy on the eyes, so you stick around to see the rest. When you finally get to the moment where his pants come off, and the lip balm in your purse is bigger than what he's packing, so the whole experience is just disappointing.

The place is visually stunning! It's an eternal climate controlled springtime full of gardens and rivers and waterfalls under an expansive glass ceiling! That's about all that's impressive about this place.

The food service is woefully understaffed and most of the many restaurants are closed most of the day. There are long lines and long waits for everything, and when you get a seat, the service is slow and the food quality ranges from terrible to mediocre and is definitely not worth the prices, and I'm someone who will shell out for quality and not think twice about it.

The linens are no better than you'd expect in a budget motel. Towels, sheets and blankets are clean but thin and scratchy. The beds are comfortable.

The room could have been cleaned more thoroughly. It wasn't obviously dirty, but finding a pair of socks left by a previous occupant hiding under the curtains didn't inspire my confidence in the housekeeping.

The location is far from everything, so it's a hike to try to get to other options for food, etcetera, so you're stuck with hour long waits for a cup of coffee or a frozen McDonald's quality burger and paying $6 for a box of 10 tampons in the gift shop.
Great food and atmosphere.  The Ruben spring rolls are excellent. Service was very good. Strongly  recommend this as a food stop for night of enjoying irish bars.

There were two occasions were I didn't see people working washing their hands.  Both were when I sat at the bar to sit, so I was there for about an hr each time.  One time, the cook with long, greasy hair and a small trimmed beard did not wash his hands ONCE.  He continually touched the sliders by the sides I guess to make sure they were warm.  But he did it with other sliders. My friends, that's called cross-contamination.  That was one example. They don't wear gloves. The cooks with long hair have their hair exposed.  

I wrote to district about it. They never responded.  Then, I wrote a review with a picture showing the people working putting their shoes on the counter (See Instagram).  However, the review was taken down.  This says a lot about the establishment.  They keep their griddle clean around the kitchen, but I'm sorry, that's not enough. Plus it's unprofessional. These people obviously don't care, because they have swarms of tourists visiting every weekend.  

If you're kitchen is exposed, you have to own up.  There's a number of health violations there.

If you don't believe me see Jenni C's report from DC.

My suggestion for locals is to take your money elsewhere to other, better establishments throughout the city. Tourists, ride with caution.

I was pretty disappointed. Got the hot and sour seafood noodle soup that was neither hot or sour. The spring roll was not much better. The service was good except they asked if I wanted a soda refill and then they charged me another $2 for a soda refill without telling me. I guess you stick to cheesesteak in Philly.

The food is awesome! The one thing that I complain about is the amount of time I have to wait. It's never consistent and realistic. For instance once I came and it took 5 minutes for my order and then there are times when I waited 30 minutes for 2 tacos and a side of guacamole. 
The irritating part is that a large party came before me and they were served 5 min after ordering. 

I love their food but things like this makes me not want to come back.

I love renting my books here because of the deferred payment. I'm in my senior year of undergrad and Jeff never fails on providing the best customer service. Every time I go he offers me something new for free. The other day I waited in line for 20 min with only a receipt proving I returned a book and he provided me with some store credit for the inconvenience. Keep it up, Staff!

We've been three or four times now,  so I figured it was time for a review. My husband won't stop ordering the steak and try anything new and I've yet to figure out if that's a good thing or a bad thing. He's in love with the "token steak dish" and I must admit, it's pretty amazing and I'm tired of the usual Alberta beef dishes. The five onion dip is something I crave at about 10 pm on a regular basis (not sure if it's always on the menu?) and I have been impressed every single time we've eaten there. It helps that it's only three minutes away from our house - thank the gods we finally have something decent in Summerside! - and we pop there for lunch once in a while. I've yet to try brunch, but it's on my to do list! A very welcome addition to the south side. The only thing I would change is amping up the cocktail menu a bit,  but I am sure that will come with time.

There is no better! Honest, motivated to keep trees alive and healthy, I knew when we had to take our tree down it was the right thing to do. Competitive prices and very professional. They also go the extra mile, moving a shade loving plant once the area became full sun.
Your standard variety Target. Plenty of parking, and the store wasn't crowded. Closer than the one in Metairie if you live downtown. One of the nicest grocery sections I've ever seen in a Target.
This is my go place I love everything it's quick easy to order prices are great and food is good. Steak Burrito is where it's at

This is definitely the worst Hibachi I've ever been to. My last review was a 2 and I decided to go back and try it but seriously NOT GOOD!. 
The quality of the meat is terrible, steak is chewy gross ness and the chicken is blah, almost not edible and i think mine wasn't cooked completely.  They cook everything super slow and one at a time so half your meal is either going to be cold or you'll be full by the time you get the other half of your meal and the service is meh too!
If they didn't have the free birthday meal thing going for them, i'd have to say they'd be going out of business based on the quality of the food and service. Their prices are also insanely expensive compared to others i've been to. Brandon didn't even finish his steak it was so terrible, when a man doesn't finish steak, you know it's bad!
Definitely won't be back again, so many other better options in the area for hibachi.

Very friendly waiter for our large and somewhat rowdy group.  Always love a BYOB! Sushi was very delicious.  Ordered the sushi for two for myself and one other- delicious assortment and unique presentation.
This is an awesome place to get a great meal, have an excellent brewski or both.

Thought you were looking for Japanese food? Do you like Korean food?  This place has both, not just Japanese plates. Full menu of fusion sushi rolls, Udon, sushi, and other Korean specialties, such as kal-bi and bul-go ki. Excellent Don Buri.  I had the salmon stone pot, which was loaded with fresh vegetables, brown rice, and salmon cooked perfectly.  I would highly recommend. Pricing very reasonable compared to other restaurants nearby. I will be back.

What a horrible experience. The food at chili's has never been great but this experience will be our last one with them.  We took my son to the New Tampa chili's for his birthday at his request.  We arrived early (before 6:00pm) in order to eat and see an 8:00pm movie. It took over an hour for our food to arrive an when it did, everything was over cooked and dry. We mentioned it to our server and she completely ignored the situation. I finally stopped our waitress after watching my husband chicken down the swill they served us and asked her to redo his meal.  At this point, we were running late, my husband was disgusted, and we were over the whole experience. The staff, from server to kitchen, to management completely ruined our dining experience.  We won't be back!  Wake up before you lose more customers?

I went back for another blow out during the week and had a great experience.  Holly did my hair and she was amazing.  She listened to exactly what I wanted and took her time to make sure she got the volume I asked for.  It looked great last night and still good today!

In general, I highly recommend H&T!

There are several aspects about this Target that have redirected my business here, rather then the Murfreesboro Target.
I always have quick and friendly customer service here, something that you rarely found at the other Target. The store is bright and clean, they have a large parking lot, there are always carts inside, the people at returns are quick and friendly, their mark downs are easy to find, they have a starbucks, and they have a full grocery store.  Which in my opinion, is what makes them a SUPER Target!!

A more conventional/formal seating layout in this restaurant, but the food is still reliably good seafood.  Just like the original in Indian Rocks Beach, this chain is the place to go for tasty and affordable seafood in a casual atmosphere.  What really sets this place apart from the others is that this location is across the street from Clearwater Beah so it's a nice place to retreat for lunch after a day on the beach.  And if you get a window seat you can get the view of the marina and a beautiful, sunny day typical of Florida :-)

Great Bahn Mi option and best Vietnamese food in the area. Quick service and helpful. Would recommend to all - especially after only other Bahn Mi option no longer in business in Goleta.

Definitely a great stop and a regular spot for a lot of locals.
Great food, reasonable prices, friendly service, clean place.  This is a little hidden gem.

So I read all the reviews and was having second thoughts about signing up for our second band event but decided to give them a try. We arrived along with 48 of our band alumni. There was absolutely NO parking. Very frustrating. Parked in someone's lot, didn't get towed. Phew!  Wa told to go to the back. Partly the fault of organizer since the room we were in held no more than 40.  I was squished and had no room to move. I was thinking Yelp had it wrong then the unthinkable happened. As I came to the buffet line, there was no food. I mean every hot plate was empty. This has never happened to me at a buffet, ever. It took a good 20 min for new food to arrive, meanwhile everyone was done eating. The food was OK and for $50 per person was overpriced. Hence the reason for 2 stars. The desserts were cookies and little brownie like things. Tasty but I was expecting more. Appetizers were tasty. Chairs were covered nicely and waitresses were nice. If not for the great acquaintances, I would had spent the $100 elsewhere. There are several people who may disagree but read all reviews.

The catfish is my favorite here.  It comes in swirls, at least the last time I ordered.  The food here consistently brings some heat and a feeling of southernness.  

I'm a fan of their cornbread and their chili.  Their sides are on the small side, but the food is pretty good.

Overall: 4.5

Moved to PA from England (... the spiritual home of Indian food....!... (as I know it)) 3 years ago. Have since endured a range of Indian restaurants, that all sit somewhere in-between mediocre and terrible. This is the first "traditional" Indian restaurant that I've been to around the Main Line that I've thought would hold it's own back home. I really enjoyed my Kadai Chicken, and I'm looking forward to my return to Ekta, for I shall take on the Vindaloo.

4 stars instead of 5 mainly due to the typical Indian restaurant stuff... minimal atmosphere, quiet wait staff & uninteresting decor.

Great little bar and restaurant. The bartender was beyond great, he was Superb. An artist. Go in and ask him for his favorite cocktail. You will not be disappointed. 

The food was uniformly good. Cajun Piutine wa probably the best of the bunch. Our entrees were both good  dessert was an afterthought, and probably best gotten elsewhere.

I'm visiting from out of town and figured why not same as home. Food is always great but the service here was no where near friendly. The first employee was great but the second was not friendly and looked bothered by my request for fresh veggies. She rolled her eyes and not once smiled. Sad for such a great food chain

I always like going to Chase. The food is pretty good (not great, but consistently pretty good), but my wife really likes the atmosphere here so we end up going here quite frequently. If you're wondering about the atomosphere, it's got the whole red booth thing going and 1000s of twinkle lights hanging from all areas of the restaurant. It's a romantic spot for the over 35 crowd. Full bar. Service is hit and miss. Sometimes when we go it's great, other times, it's terrible, but it's a unique looking local restaruant that's pretty good. We've been many times and will continue to go on a regular basis.

This location is close to our home. We don't go very often but have been there maybe a dozen times. 
The inside is clean, the tables are clean and the workers are always nice and respectful. 

The food is pretty good but their blizzards and moolatas are soooo very good!  Trey are always freshly made and always exactly what we order. 

It's a great stop on a hot day to cool down. The Orange Julius is so refreshing any time of the day.

Favorite place to get my sushi fix! Staff is great too! Love all the drink specials! Sushi rose knows what tastes good and they never skimp out on ingredients. I've gotten a hundred sunset hand rolls and they were all the same which is amazing for I can not say that about the other sushi places in town. They even make my favorite nigiri that isn't on the menu. When other places just look you straight in the eye with a sagging face and say no we don't do that. Sushi rose even has a vip program and you can win gift cards. Other places could learn something from sushi rose.
WAY too much money for what you get.  And it really isn't that good.  The lettuce in the salad was brown and the pizza is forgetful.

The wings are to die for. 
Artisan pizza is tasty, but small for the price.
Our waitress was kind but did not really seem to know what she was talking about when it came to knowing about the food itself.

This place is the best I've found in broad ripple!  Their prices are reasonable, good customer service, and the mani/pedi I got is great!!  Diane did a wonderful job and was very sweet. I'll definitely be going back all summer!  Better than lotus and city nails in my opinion.

Not a far walk from r hotel. Lots of carnivore dishes. I assumed it was a vegetarian restaurant....but o well
The costa rica & bannana foster was yum! Organic juices were great. Off the beaten track non tourist place. Good food and staff

Contrary to other reviews, I've shopped at this Aldi location multiple times with no problems. Produce is fresher than at other Aldi's I've been to, and they seem to keep things well stocked even when it's busy!

Pizza is pretty good, prices are reasonable, portions are decent, and they're open late on the weekends. Location is pretty convenient too - especially coming from one of the local bars. I think Frank's has better pizza, but they close much earlier.

I bought a new A4 last week and had a excellent experience with this Willow Grove. Jeff Rosen was my salesperson and he attentive to all my needs. He was very knowledgeable and spent a lot of time going over the advanced technology features when I picked up my car.

I probably order take out here, yes take out, at least once a month.  They handle the take out prep, which is usually a concern of mine, quite well. Ponzu pork is a must for us, very great combo of perfectly braised rich pork with the sweet chili and napa slaw on crunchy wonton.  

Campfire fettucini is actually one of my favorite pasta dishes anywhere.  Perfect heat, with andouille sausage, some chicken and two giant BBQ shrimp.  The sauce on that shrimp is phenomenal.  It is served in a red chili cream sauce, delightful.

actually a lot of the pastas are good and the salads.  Chili shrimp is high quality entree too.  Crab cakes were a miss the one time I tried them.

The only crime and it is a crime is that they no longer serve, nightly, the short ribs.  They were the best around, served with a risotto cake which was glorious.  I kid them everytime I order to bring it back. It appears on occasion as a special.  I had an osso buco there one night that was spot on.

Interior is indeed dark, and more dressy than you might think.  I'm not that high on the sandwich offerings.

I met a friend at the nearby mall, and we decided to have a late lunch.  We wandered into Taranova's, as we both felt that some pizza was in order.  Oddly enough, neither of us got pizza, but the meal far exceeded my expectations.  

The decorations were standard Italian restaurant fare complete with a large Mediterranean-style mural.  I ordered a steak Stromboli (something I would never think to order offhand), and my friend ordered a cheese steak.  I didn't expect the Stromboli to be as large as it turned out to be.  It was massive, and it supplied me not only with lunch, but with a late night dinner as well.  The bread encasing the delicious meat/cheese/veggie blend was freshly baked, and the filling was cooked to perfection.  I'm not a huge fan of Stromboli, but it was easily the best I've ever had, and it was only $7.50.  My friend's cheese steak was served in a freshly baked roll, and it looked pretty good.  As I recall, it only cost about $5.50, not bad considering that a lesser quality hoagie might run you about $6.00.  

The serving staff was exceptional.  Our waitress was constantly refilling our drinks, and she was very friendly.  

Conclusively, the food was great, the price was low, and the service was top notch.  I will definitely come back to Taranova's whenever I'm in the Neshaminy area.

After much anticipation, I was excited to see a beautiful restaurant being built on Haddon Ave. Hearthside went up and I was ready for it. The restaurant opened and I was shocked it was nearly impossible to get a reservation. Naturally, I checked the Yelp reviews to see what people had to say. I read nothing but incredible things and I was not disappointed leaving after our meal last night. 

First, I have to start by complimenting the owners on the decor of the space. It's absolutely gorgeous, inside and out! The menu is set up for sharing which is, in my opinion, the most rewarding way to experience a restaurant. My boyfriend and I decided to order one small, two medium, and one large dish. We picked the tuna tartare (small), octopus (medium), a featured rabbit ragu rigatoni (medium), and the skate wing (large). All of the dishes were so delicious and portioned to perfection. 

We couldn't decide on dessert so we asked our waitress to surprise us with either the carrot cake or the apple fritter. When I saw her come out with a dish in each hand I was like "This place is definitely getting a 5-star review" so here I am.

Thank you Hearthside for yummy, yummy food and wonderful dining experience! We will be back to enjoy it all over again!

I watch the food preparer cough up a lung over the pizza he was making and never covered his mouth. Absolutely mortified and will never order from here again.  STAY AWAY unless you like the saliva and germs from your food prepared baked into your pizza. The food is great though, but I won't be returning.

Came here today to try their wings and eggplant parm. Called in my order and she said it'd be ready in 20. I got there in 20 and it took another 15. I was kind of annoyed until I got home to devour my food. It was so good, I'm not even mad anymore. A million thumbs up to their wings!!!! Eggplant parm was great too!

One of the best brunch spots in town. Amazing pancakes, skillets, and coffee. The grilled cheese with tomato soup is really amazing too. The only thing that kind of sucks about this place is it's usually really packed and a long wait. If you go early or late it's usually not too bad though. The servers are also really nice and attentive which is a plus. Highly recommend prep and pastry

This place has a good location in Hillsboro Village and lots of well-positioned tv screens (had a good time watching some world cup matches here).  However, the food is fairly bad.  Service is all right, sometimes slow.  Eh.
The apartments are great, service is prompt (but a bit lacking in quality), cost is high, and the community is beautiful. There is a pretty artificial lake and perfect walking/running path around it.

Chef's Market is top shelf in my book. Kind of like the Puffy Muffin (in Brentwood and Franklin) but I actually like the Chef's Mkt menu better. More hearty fare that appeals to men. The iced tea is great (not to watery) and they have large lemon slices (excellent!) so i am happy to pay a little more. 

I've been in Nashville for a long time and I was late to the party on Chef's mkt. They should advertise more.

Based on the reviews from the customers, I ordered 2 hoagies trays for a party.  Everyone wanted to know where the hoagie trays came from....so Chris' Sandwich shop be prepared to increase your customer base because I gave out your information.   The hoagies were awesome, we even had some people fixing to-go plates and hiding their hoagies.  In other words, they became the hoagie-burglar, after taking a bite!  I'll definitely be back when I'm in the area.  Great gamble!

Ugh, what happened? This was always my favorite Food Truck and we'd drive an hour just for their amazing Cheese Curds! But I just had my first order of 2018 and they have definitely changed since last fall. The batter now has an overly pronounced cornmeal flavor and consistency and it really changes the crunch of the curd crust and overall taste. The cheese itself seemed a bit off too. There was always a mix of white and yellow cheddar curds in each order. This visit all the curds were yellow cheddar and had a "Velveeta" feel and taste to them, instead of the normal rich and stringy cheddar cheese. As a fan of the original version, I hope this was just a temporary change of the recipe or perhaps an off-day.

What a sweet girly girl place to go!
Pesto was the best I've had in years. Bright. Fresh. 
The desserts are just ridiculous! (In a great way) 
Sensory overload at first. But, as I sat back and watched every detail of the business it's just amazing. Even the cleaning solution they use to clean the tables is pink! Your attention to detail was not lost on me. The food & desserts were fantastic. 
The service was fantastic.

This place is not only affordable but delicious and fresh. I had the bob Marley wrap and it was amazing! Hands down one of the best wraps I have ever had. The hand cut fries on the side were cooked to perfection. This little gem is in an office building and am a little jealous of everyone that works near by.

The place is a joke. The two medium cooked burgers took over a half an hour to be prepared.

They have a strange bathroom where the doors are transparent until you lock them. Sounds cool. Until 5 minutes into the number two experience the door randomly becomes transparent again while I have toilet paper in my hand and my genitals fully exposed. Oh and yes, there just happened to be a person staring at me in shock. While I stood there in shock. It could have been a child. 

When I shared this disastrous experience with the bartender who was serving us, there was no apology of any sort. I was laughed at like it was a joke. I'm engaged to an attorney and will be looking into pursuing legal action. This simply is not okay.

I recently had my first sushirrito. To be clear, I wanted to give this place all the stars because I loved the idea! Obviously, it is pricey, but I was expecting that. Although I felt the ingredients were fresh and delicious, it was very hard to eat because it was falling apart which made me feel like they still haven't gotten the full swing of things. It was also frustrating because I ended up dropping more than I ate. For now, I would suggest going for the bowl since it still has all the great parts but just not the mess and waste!


Hope some of the links get worked out soon!
Great little cafe with quality food, and friendly service. Hidden Gem! Its never very busy here, but i think that will change when the word gets out.

Came here for lunch with a large group on a Saturday. They sat us quickly in the dining section. There's a separate entrance to the right for dining in. The place was much bigger than I realized!
I ordered an adult beverage, some sort of alcoholic strawberry lemonade. Delicious! I got the Vito panini: prosciutto, mozeralla, tomato. It was so good! Everyone's food looked good. No complaints. They have some interesting menu choices for pizza. I'd like to go back for the pizza.
The decor is fun. Murals on the walls and ceilings combining local and Italian history. Great neighborhood!
It felt a little crowded, but it could have been because they pushed tables together for out 10+ group.

My first taste of oysters did not disappoint. The wait wasn't too long - the staff kept the line moving by filling up the seats at the bar. When I think of "The Big Easy" I picture a place where you can relax and enjoy your meal, and this place delivered. I was craving some seafood, and the combo platter looked like it offered a taste of everything. The waitress kindly recommended it for 2, and I'm glad she did - the plate was stacked with food. My date and I were starving after a day of travel and wandering the Quarter, and that plate still defeated us. I've lived in the south for the majority of my life and I've had quite a few hush puppies, but I can safely say those were the best I've ever had. Can't offer any advice on dessert as there was no room for it. Definitely worth a return visit!
Great breakfast sandwiches and friendly service. Makes me look forward to getting my vehicle maintenance done just to have breakfast at this cafe.
Totally enjoyed. Even thou it's new they need to get the seating situation under control,the quality of the food was good.

Newk's Eatery feels more like a deli than a restaurant. You order up at the register and then the food is delivered to your table. Drinks are self serve and there is a complimentary add-on bar with things like hot sauce, pickles, peppers, etc. I wasn't disappointed with the food by any means but wasn't thrilled either. It had a lot of seating which is great for a group. A couple of my friends love Newks and I would definitely go again if I wanted a solid meal but do not expect your tastebuds to be really wowed.

I love duck. I tried the blue duck fries, which are cooked in duck fat and topped with duck confit and Gouda cheese sauce. The confit was a little tough, cubed rather than shredded/pulled. The flavors were awesome though. I also had the blue jawn burger, which is a beef/duck patty with red onion jam, blue cheese, and duck cracklins. It didn't come with a side, but it was a giant patty. Quite good. Ate too much, too fast, which is always a ringing endorsement.
The Peppermill is one of the nicer hotels in Reno. They have a good selection.of restaurants, however not happy with their high (almost $30) resort fee. Good gym.
This is the best Chinese in area!

This is definitely not the best goodwill I have ever been to. The clothing selection is...ok, I guess. Not a lot of good brand names to be found among the labels (J.crew, Ann Taylor, etc). Mostly stuff from target and Walmart. Also, terrible home wares selection.

Disclaimer: I was born in Vietnam, lived in Houston for 15 years, then moved to LA followed by Sacramento, all cities with a large Vietnamese population. So this was tough to rate; I'd say it's 3-star compared to all Vietnamese restaurants I've been to, but I'm new to Nashville and can't compare it to the other Vietnamese restaurants here yet.  

The spring rolls were decent; I agree with a prior review that they were a little smaller than usual but they were also cheaper (my advice - get one order per person if you're used to splitting an order of goi cuon at most Vietnamese places).  

The jellyfish salad (goi) was amazing - better than I've had at places elsewhere. Many places have way too much cabbage and very little of the other greens, like lotus root.  This salad had a little of everything and plenty of jellyfish as well as shrimp and pork (a nice bonus; many places don't add in the pork).  

My bun bo hue broth was too sweet.  Not my style, but I think some people like it that way.  Will update when I come back to try the pho.

Prices were good - comparable to larger cities and very cheap compared to restaurants in general ($7 for bun bo hue; we spent $20 for dinner for two).  Service was awful.  The waiter (an employee) was friendly and attentive, but the woman I assume was the owner was openly rude to another customer and unfriendly to me when I paid at the counter.  I don't go to Vietnamese restaurants for the service, so this won't stop me from going back; just be aware that if she's rude, it's her, not you.

Some of the best ice-cream I've eaten in St Louis. They have a sign explaining why their ice-cream is so good. Go for the ice-cream you will not be disappointed. This business is in a fun part of the city which makes it easy to add this to your schedule for the night!

Love this place! After moving to Philly from NJ, I changed nails salons. BIG MISTAKE.. I had a bad experience at the new place and decided that it was worth it for me to drive to NJ twice a month just to come to Hi-Tech. They are all extremely friendly, fast, reasonably priced, clean, and super accommodating. All of their nail techs are awesome. I've since moved to Philly burbs, and STILL travel all the way here just to get my nails done!

Just experienced probably the greatest tacos that I've ever tasted. The cashier was wonderful and gave me her recommendations which I followed The fish taco was so fresh and so delicious and complemented by the sauces provided, I literally sat there in a state of amazement. My second taco was the Carnita. Usually braised pork loses its flavor. Here it not only maintained its flavor, it was picked by the spices and accompaniments. Also, the other sauce provided on the table just took this to unbelievable Heights. I highly, highly recommend this restaurant

My husband and I had dinner at Mango once before.  This time we took our daughter.  

The plantain chips and green salsa were delish!  We devoured two baskets and ordered some for take-out.

My daughter ordered squid and loved it.  Since it's not in the normal form of fried calamari, I was surprised she liked it.  

My husband had the flank steak which could have been a little more tender but he still liked it.

I had the chicken skewers with the hot dipping sauce which was very good.  It came with large kernel corn and fried sweet potatoes which were also good.

My first time to Cameo was the Friday before Easter. I had read the reviews and chose Melissa to do my hair.  I was very pleased at the beautiful salon, the cleanliness of the salon and how friendly everyone was.   Melissa was great and color came out great.  I called yesterday, May 8th, and was told she could do May 9 ay 5 pm.  I thought that was rather quick because Melissa is always booked.   Someone had over booked her

I had a very good experience here on family fun night. We did one game of golf, which was enough.  The kids had an awesome time, from start to finish.  After that, we enjoyed a drinks and some sweet treats, quick sit down.. thumbs up

I'm not terribly picky about my basic pedicure but since it is a splurge for my budget, I like to feel like it was special. Nothing specific to complain about but nothing I can say that was better than average either. I've been twice and since I'm new to South Tampa, I'm going to try somewhere else where I can feel as special as the regulars here seem to feel without yet being a regular. I had 2 different technicians and wasn't overly impressed with either of them. I did like the hot stone but felt like the massage was almost non-existent it was so short. Lackluster and let down are descriptive words that I would use as a new client who will be trying a new nail salon tomorrow.
I love, love, love the Peppermill.  It is always a delight to stay there and we always have fun.  They know how to treat people so they feel special.

My family visited Tre Scalini this past December for my dad's birthday. We were upstairs in what looks like a party room, obviously geared towards larger groups. The upstairs lacks the quaintness of the lower level, but the food more than made up for it.

Our waiter knew his stuff. He made recommendations, we took the bait and were not disappointed.

The staff were very accommodating. My son is a picky eater (obsessed with chicken nuggets!) and while I was willing to be strict, my dad asked the waiter if the chef could prepare him a chicken cutlet (not on the menu) and some 'pasta with butter'.

I'm not sure they had any butter in this Italian kitchen, but this is the type of place that will make a Wawa run to go get butter so that the customer is happy. By the way, the custom-made chicken cutlet was outstanding :)

All in all it was a fantastic family-style meal. The food was authentic and brought me back to Italy. 

Parking is a bit of a problem, but a small price to pay. We were lucky enough though to get a spot right in front of the restaurant.

I give this restaurant like 100000 stars for the food. It was sooo delicious and a little something different. I loved the atmosphere, the music, the decor, the cocktails. LOOOVED it all. My only issue is I came in solo and sat at the bar. There was only one bartender on so he was swamped. He dropped my entree order so I sat there for an hour with no food after my app. Luckily, the app was a good size so I wasn't hungry but after waiting for so long, I just was ready to go. This will not deter me from going back again but I will probably grab a table with a waitress. The barkeep also did make it up to me in with a few comped items so it was a definite win overall.
Had a salad and small ceviche for only $13 - the salad came with a meat, avocado, onions, cilantro and lime, tomatoes, and avocado. Great deal, great food!!

Unbelievably loud, and freezing cold.
Not a place to talk to friends, food was average, and not at all interesting, service was poor.

The general tso chicken was good and so was the egg roll but the ribs were dry and did not have any sauce on them. The chicken wings were ok, I've had better. They are suppose to give you 8 chicken wings but they do not. They give you 4 and cut the wings off so that you have 4 drumsticks and 4 wings. Which is a rip off.

Brian was our tour guide and he was AMAZING!!! We had 4 teenagers and an 11year old. We all loved it!! Comments from the girls...
"He taught us sooo much history."  
"It was as funny as 10 episodes of drunk history!" (NOTE: He of course was not drunk. It is a hilarious show.) 
"Best story teller!!!" 
"He made it so interesting."
"Why can't our teachers be like Brian!"
"Oh so like Princess and the Frog like makes so much more sense now!" (From 11 yo ;))
We were worried that it was 2 hours of walking but it was more of a stroll and we stopped a lot to hear stories. We took a break in the middle and got sno-balls got in some air conditioning and went to the bathrooms. Don't worry about the walking part being too much, Brian is so interesting, you won't even realize how much time has gone by.
My gf brought me here all the way from GA for a snowball. We got the stuffed snowball with ice cream. Unlimited flavors and oh yea the nachos are on point.
Great food and atmosphere! I always do a create your own calzone, and it is always good! The service is friendly and quick!

So gotta give one star because we can't even rate the food, due to us not getting seated. We came in it was not busy at all. There was a well dressed man behind the bar, not sure if he was a manager or not, he didn't say a word to us. The sign at door said wait to be seated. Several servers past us without even a glance. Several servers stood in corner seeing us but still no contact. Servers saw us leave. Not good costumer serves.

Horrible service by Karen Forman. I went to drop off my dress shirts and i asked for a quote for press only. This employee named Andrew advised that it was 30% off of 2.60. When i went to pick up my clothes Karen (who says its the owner) she was trying to charge me almost 6 dlls per shirt. I advised her of the quote i received the day before and instead of apologizing and providing great customer service after this mistake she was incredible rude and condescending. I've never experience this from an "owner" at any place. Never going back!

Fantastic salsa bar! The carne asada and grilled chicken are great. Their Sonoran dogs aren't my favorite in town, but tasty as well. Beers and fun atmosphere for eating in. I grab burros or caramelos here on the regular!

First time at a John Besh restaurant. 
On our visit to New Orleans, bumped into friends and next thing we were on to Happy Hour for the oysters. I've never had oysters, let alone raw oysters but what better time to try?.?.Aanndd I was pleasantly surprised! And the oysters were HUGE! 
Since we were in New Orleans and there was too much food to eat, didn't want to stuff my face before dinner. The jalapeno shrimp was a complete YES! I did push the actual jalapenos to the side, but the flavor were definitely all UP in the grits. I did realize though, what mint julep REALLY is -a whole lot of bourbon with some mint leaves and a bit of sugar - so definitely lesson learned on that front! But the waiter was VERY knowledge about the entire Food & Drinks menu.
The real deal.  Outstanding!  A little chaotic on  Friday, but that's part of the charm.

Sheltered from a rainstorm here for lunch yesterday. Not bad my friends! My daughters fish was great and the Hawaii plate was a perfect beach lunch! Staff super friendly and place was clean and family friendly! A great little find!

There is something that will excite every child in this museum. A train, a 90 year old carousel, a water clock, art, science, dinosaurs, an indy car and so much more to explore. Playscape is great for those with infants and toddlers. Additionally, the Museum Guild does an amazing haunted house each fall with "lights on hours". During the holidays, they deck the halls with a fun yule slide!  There are so many additional activities year round. Kids of all ages will enjoy this place!  The cafe also has great options. Learn, explore and make memories. This is a great place to do all of it!

These are the BEST CHURROS I have ever eaten in my liiiiiife. Perfectly deep fried, hot and piping with a side of delicious dulce de leche dipping sauce. I am so happy that I went for dessert after my meal- though next time I don't think I will be sharing!
For our mains my friend and I shared a half a chicken with the sides of roasted carrots, roasted cauliflower and potatoes (which came with the chicken). The chicken was phenomenal. I can't say any more than what all the other reviewers already have, but only to affirm that it really is that great. We both agreed that the cauliflower wasn't the best we had ever tasted, but the carrots and the potatoes were excellent sides. Between the two of us there was enough for leftovers for one which was great. It is definitely a place where you want to take more people so you can sample a bit of everything. I think that while the main course was great, I still think the home run for me was the dessert! Simple, yet so delicious. The atmosphere is really fitting- love the decorations and the warehouse look and feel of the place. It is very inviting and there is lots of different seating options depending on a) how many people are in your party or b) what kind of meal you are there for. Whether it be just drinks and an appy or a full family style meal. Such a great place and unique dining experience in YEG using lots of great local ingredients.

Went here for Father's Day and I was hoping it would be really good b/c of the other reviews. Let's just say I came away disappointed. The food in general needs more seasoning. I got my kid the ahi tuna tacos kids meal and the fish came out really bland. There's no cream sauce to go along with the tacos. The fries tasted like it was deep fried in really old frying oil. The New York strip steak that I ordered was tough. I ordered the steak medium and it came out more medium well. The fat was tough to cut off, most likely been sitting on the grill for too long. The monitor I ordered was okay, nothing to write home about. My wife had the spinach salad with steak. Her meat was tough as well. In all, the food is way too pricey for the quality food you get.
Customer service needs improvement, but the woman sold me spoiled fried chicken, and I had to throw away the entire plate. Will never go back there again.

This place is awesome. Chef JJ and staff knows how to cook up great food . If you love food and love to cook this place it for you.This was my 2nd class and I loved it. Last night was Mexican Night. All the food is made with instruction by Chef JJ and then feed to the class. Key dishes were Braised Goat Tacos with Tomatillo Sofrito, Smoked Chicken Tamales, Carne Asada, and Chocoflan. 
I highly recommend this experience.

Brunch only review. Tavern has delicious brunch that belies its rather generic name. There are some really creative dishes, both sweet and savory. The Shanghai Stirfry is savory breakfast genius: bacon fried rice with an egg on top. So good. My group shared the red velvet pancakes and the cheddar cheese biscuits (with chorizo gravy). Both were pretty good, though I think the red velvet pancakes were a bit sweet. Everyone was happy with their food, and you can't really complain about a 2 for 1 Bloody Mary/Mimosa on a Sunday morning.

This place is to die for. My husband and I come in atleast once a week. The food comes out fast and the people are friendly for the most part. The chips and salsa are always warm and fresh. The food is amazing; its your typical Mexican restaurant food. We've had the golden enchiladas, fajitas, shrimp quesadillas, burrito boom. But the best is the fajita burrito. It's huge and covered in queso, which is always fantastic. Definitely go here to get your Mexican fix.
Took a long time for someone to come and seat us even though the restaurant wasn't that full. Wait staff was nice and fast once seated. Food was good and came out fast. Overall not bad.

Very good.. The 5 stars are for the food and proximity to my hotel( right across the street). Ordered the charboilied oysters, very flavorful and reasonably priced. Also, the calamari was nicely battered and not chewy. We also ordered a spider sushi roll that was to die for! ( expect to wait a bit for the for the food, fyi) Overall very good experience..
Nice little coffee and pastry shop. Pretty busy little place run by a sole proprietor. Food was good.

When I was living in the Philly suburbs I needed to get my car inspected. I had one of those coupons you get in the mail for Havertown Tire & Service, so I though I'd give it a try. They did find a few things that needed fixing on my 11 year old Jeep, but that was to be expected. Over the next few months, they did regular servicing on both my Jeep and my wife's 15 year old Toyota. They kept both running well. On one emergency repair for me, they were even to get the job done early for less than they estimated. If I still lived there, I would still have them do all my work. Good work at fair prices.

I was in from out of town and Deluxe is my sister in laws salon so she made an appt for me 12/30 And Jen was my stylist. I received a cut and color and I LOVE IT. She listened to what I had to say and price was less expensive than what I pay going to a Wmington, DE salon. Same day appt. too.

I love Chick-fil-A but this location was way too crowded. I didn't find that the tables were kept up or anyone walking around checking to see if we need refills. If I come back it'll probably be drive thru only.

Can't recommend this place.  Went with a group of 7. They were unorganized and really seemed to have a ton of trouble getting it together to even take our order. 

The place is very dark and even in the dark we could see how dirty it was. There was a leak from the ceiling causing the couch like seat we were seated at to become soaked. The staff didn't want to move us. They gave us towels to sit on..the towels didn't work so we moved ourselves. We really shouldn't have stayed, but we were really looking forward to the Moroccan experience. I don't think we got it.  The drinks were brought out in plastic cups. The food was subpar and the service was awful.

What a GREAT place.  Came into Philadelphia for a trade show . . first night we found Marmont - and liked it so well we came back for a 2nd night.  If you are a Pinot Noir fan, try the IRONY 2011.  Wonderful flavor of berries with just the right tannin.  TOP NOTCH.  The Crab Bisque is creamy and full of crab meat - with a hint of cherry sweetness.  The mussel's were PHENOMINAL - try them Latin Style ! Our group had a variety of steaks, and all of them were simply great.  The asparagus serving is LARGE . . . excellent flavor and perfectly done.

Marissa was our server and she was PHENOMINAL - Never hovering but always there when we needed her.

Overall, one of my all time favorites. When I get back to Philly, I will DEFINITLY come back to Marmont.

Love this Baskin Robbins! They have a drive thru so I can take the kids coning. Service with a smile every time, and a cheerful, helpful attitude. This company has excellent customer service, and the ice cream is always fresh and delicious. Pralines and Cream is still my all time favorite! With the drive-thru option, I am able to enjoy the frozen treats without getting out of my car and freezing.

Refreshing atmosphere. Excellent food! Fresh, delicious, flavorful, and a good quantity. I selected a duck confit with eggs lunch dish. The duck was tender and flavorful and the dollop of cabernet goat cheese was the, "icing on top" of a very creative dish. It also included potatoes, dried fig, and spinach.

I can say we have been coming to Han D. for the past 7 years or so and have been very happy with our meals .  We like the Americanized menu they serve and the food is better than the other Chinese restaurants in the area . They do not get a 5 as I agree with other posters that each of the few employees have way too many hats to wear. At times I have to get up to hail a waitstaff member rushing by to get their attention for a question or water refill. Hire more staff during busy times !

Well when your related to St. Elmo's and Dunaway's you've got to prove your a part of the family and Harry and Izzy's does. You have a great selection of decently priced lunch options, some moderately priced dinner options, amazing (but pricey) steak and seafood options and yes the infamous shrimp cocktails!! They have an amazing wine selection and a superb bar tending staff.
The only problem I have had with this downtown location is that they sometimes suffer in service when they get busy. I think they were understaffed at the time we were there, or may have just been the outdoor areas or maybe because we were down there for motoGP weekend wearing leather chaps but I won't let that keep me from coming back. Overall your going to be happy with your meal here and if you aren't downtown they have a new location in Castleton at 82nd & Dean Rd.

Great ambience. Upscale. Food is ehh. I've been twice and thought the second time might be better and it wasn't. I don't recommend the flatbread and the truffled Mac and cheese is just okay. Both very greasy. My stomach hurt both times that I've eaten here.

Stumbled across the Village Pub & Beer Garden on a busy Saturday night and decided the place looked hoppin' so why not give it a try? 

Walked into the busy bar and we were immediately greeted by a nice host who informed us that it was spot a seat, take a seat type seating. It brought a competitive edge to our dining experience. He also informed us that it was a smoking establishment outside on the patio. He was very nice explained to us some beers and offered to get us one while we waited for a table to open up. 

The ambiance was a little too college bar for me. Very crowded, loud, and smoke filled. We patiently waited for a table that we were stalking to open up and swooped in when we saw our chance. They were either under staffed or overwhelmed with the crowd because flagging down a server was a difficult task. Our server seemed too busy to explain to us anything on the menu or any beer we might want to try. That and it was almost too loud for me to hear my friend sitting just inches in front of me (this was on the patio)

When our food finally arrived it came out nice and hot. I had the bratwurst rueban and my partner in crime had the blackened chicken sandwich. All of their sandwiches come on pretzel bread (literally a pretzel cut in half as bread) which was a cool spin on a sandwich. They were both delicious and something different.  

Overall the Pub was fine, nothing special, and no place to take a date. Way too loud. If you are looking to get a few drinks and maybe it would be better not on a Saturday night it seems like a good place to grab a sandwich and beer.
A blend of European style cafe aesthetics with amazing Southern Comfort food. We loved their Creamy Crawfish Pasta and Lafayette Chicken. Their eggplant sandwich was also very good.
Interesting little place tucked off of Main. Service was friendly and professional. Food was nice.

It's clean, it's comfortable, you get cookies for free and every staff member I encountered was very welcoming and nice. 

The pool is kind of small though, but that's not a huge deal. The parking garage is an old city garage so it's not exactly nice but, again, I'm from a large city so I'm used to what it is. It's a garage, what do you expect!?

Overall I enjoyed the place a lot. Very pleasant.
the best Taiwanese food you can get in Reno. No comparison to larger cities with a bigger Asian population but in Reno, this is the best you can get.

After years of receiving mail from Express Scripts, telling me how much I would save by switching to them, I decided to call. I was quoted $10 for a 90 day supply of the generic nexium. Our insurance had started charging us $47 at a local pharmacy. I decided to allow them to fill the generic as they promised for $10......BIG MISTAKE! Without any prior consent, or communication from them, they withdrew $404.00 from my checking account!!!!!! They filled the prescription as name brand without authorization from me!!!!! We never would have agreed to that. Run far away from this deceitful, disrespectful company. They refuse to refund the full amount or accept the returned package if I refuse shipment.  Have NO tracking information..nothing. How is this company allowed to do this?? Why have they not been investigated?? I am devastated by this companies business tactics.....

Went here with much trepidation after reading the scathing reviews on yelp and google, but my 2012 diesel was begging for its 10k service and logistically I had to go.  Calling for service was very pleasant, the receptionist very polite and professional.  I arrived when instructed and declined shuttle service, opting to wait.  Loaners are not available sadly, but the waiting area was adequate if not plush with good coffee and vending machine for other tastes.  During the time I was there, I was kept up to date by the very pleasant service rep, and I had the opportunity to over hear numerous conversations of other reps talking with other customers.  The people at walkers were always very professional and courteous even in the face of the inevitable irate customer.  
My car was updated and serviced without problem or charge; I declined the free wash as I needed to leave.  Of note, I did not purchase my car from Walkers;  this was never mentioned during my visit and I did not feel any bias.  I'm very pleased and will return.
Wow! I just looked that their new website and it looks great, just like the work they do! Love the way they expertly explain how their product and service is so much better than the competitions.

Went for lunch and ordered carnitas tacos ($11).  Lunchmate had the shrimp.  Came on a plate with refried beans, rice, guacamole, sour cream, pico and a basket of corn tortillas on the side.  Serving size was enough for lunch (with a bit leftover).  My food seemed salty...maybe even too salty.  Not just the pork but the rice and beans too.   

Anyway, the guacamole was five-star.  Really, REALLY good.  Better than the other local places (Distrito, Gaucamole, etc...).  The presentation wasn't anything special (served in a clear glass bowl with chips around the side) but it was really fantastic.  I'd go back at happy hour for a margarita and some guac.  For lunch I think I'll continue going to Distrito for the $15 2-course lunch deal.

Doesn't anyone work in this city? If not, and they have a New York Times, a MacBook, and lots of black clothing, they're at La Colombe in the morning.

Generally, the line goes out the door. But the service by the 3-day-stubble beautiful boys is spot on. They make the orders lickety-split. And their full tip jar is testimony to how they rock and roll. 

Really great part? Real creme in a china creamer. Long spoons. Granular brown sugar. And a saucer even if you're getting a cup to go.

Get the cappuccino. Their froth is the best in Philly.

Met Jennifer E and her hubby here for dinner.  The place is small.  There were five us is and we sat at a table for four.  The restaurant has a bar, stage for the band, and different size tables and chairs.  The food was tapas style servings.  

I ordered the beef, kimchi, rice bowl and small order of tempura shrimp.  Others at the table had : lamb sliders, pork belly, scallops, and fish tacos.  We also had an assorted cheese & meat plate to start.  For desert we had a brownie with ice cream and a marshmallow pie.  Everything I tasted was really, really good.  The band we saw was great.

Went in looking for a used G37X. Salesman was brand new but helpful and pleasant. Manager who was helping him train was also great to deal with. Didn't end up buying the car as it didn't have all the accessories I was looking for but I will definitely go back and look. If future experience is as good would definitely buy there,

No Chinese restaurant around here is great, but this is better than most. They charge for water! The only restaurant to ever charge me for water. Most places do not have both good crab rangoon and fried dumplings, but here both are good.

Got the spinach dip as an appetizer and it was delicious! Salad was good as well as my entree. It was angel hair pomodore. Prices were surprisingly reasonable. Will probably be back if I'm back in Nashville.

Fast food is exactly what it says and implies. Their burgers are equal or better than the competition.  There new attempt at Mexican makes me want to ask for my money back, but breakfast, now that is where they excel and leave competition in their dust.
I am not a "bread" person and always watch the fat content.
But when it comes to their golden flakey, totally delicious biscuts or sweet rolls, forget it I am gone. GONE to Hardee's in a flash when I get that occasional, overwhelming urge to indulge in their breakfast. 
My favorite is bacon, egg& cheese biscuit. 2 slices of nice crisp bacon and for once the chese is always melted!  Don't order just 1, make sure you get 2 or you will be too far away when your tummy screams more.  Of course you can get them with other meats than bacon and cheese or not is your option.
Let's not forget those yummy sweet rolls, no not Tea House good, fast food great. Cinnamon,  spiced just right and not too sweet. Bread is soft and hard at the same time and in the right places.  Then drizzled with icing and always served warm. So yummy.You have to try them for yourself.
What's a girl to do? why are their so few Hardee's  around Tampa?

Excellent Mexican food. I typically get one of their Alambres specials, and have never been let down.I also throw in a couple of their Al Pastor Tacos, as the meat is served hot off the rotating spit, with some fresh corn tortillas, and a slice of Pineapple. Outside of the normal Tacos and Burritos, they serve quite a bit of other mexican cuisine like Gorditas, taquitos, sopes, and more. Also, don't be fooled by the Avocado green salsa, it's pretty darn spicy. They also make fresh horchata. Depending on time, parking can be difficult, however its worth the walk if you trekking there. An Excellent alternative to Lilly's tacos (whom is also closed on tuesdays as well)

I took the wife out last night for dinner. We stood up front waiting to be seated. Once we got seated they took our drink order the wife decided that she would get a Malibu bay breeze which was made well. We ordered an Appetizer combo of chicken fingers Mozzarella sticks and potato skins. The potato skins were horrible and you could tell we're heated in the microwave. We never got the bbq sauce that we asked for with the chicken. When our entree came out my chicken was terrible. The wife's steak was terrible and had a ton of fat on it. We did get desert and my wife said that the cheesecake was incredible and the mile high Boston cream pie was great. All and all the floor was dirty and the food was terrible minus desert.

Meatball sandwhich..sausage pepper and onion..cannolis...I am from Philly but I somehow found the best Italian sandwhiches ever down here in Largo, Florida. Great people, huge servings for a great price

The food was OK. We ordered mac n cheese which came with a salad and another salad with steak. 

The service was terrible. The waiter did not come to our table at all except for serving our food and asking if we were done. We didn't finish our food and asked to get our food wrapped up. For some reason, our waiter did NOT include the side salad and mixed the mac n cheese with the tomato topping it came with, which I took off and put on another plate. What right does a waiter have to mix someone's food? Why couldn't he just simply transfer the food from the plate to the styrofoam? Ugh.
What a fun spot for afternoon tea. Great location if you are staying downtown.  Tea selection is great and reasonably priced.

I was born and raised in Thailand so I know my Thai food. The Other Half and I shared an order of fried spring rolls (delicious) and he got the "Pad Med Ma-muang," which is chicken stir-fried with cashews, and I got the Panang chicken. Both dishes were lovely! I was surprised by how good the chicken in cashews were and the Panang had such a rich, creamy coconut flavor.  The server was lovely and the food arrived quickly. We were surprised to see how empty the restaurant was on a Sunday evening, but we went at about 5 pm so it was quite early. I wanted to try the sticky rice with Thai custard for dessert, but was simply too full. Maybe next time. And there will definitely be a next time. What a nice find.

Great market in Medford! Just purchased a fine porterhouse steak, grilled vegetables, stuffed long hots, Italian meatballs, eggplant parm, homemade soup. I'm set for the weekend! They also have deli meats and a ton more food. Good local shop. Happy they were open today in the snow storm. Can't wait to cook the steak tonight!

As firstimers to NOLA...we spent the day in the French Quarter drinking, shopping and seeing the sites...as evening drew near, this beautiful restaurant emerged from the craziness...so we walked in. This is a very elegant place but don't let that fool you. My wife and I each ordered off the 3 course meal. She had the Chicken and I had the flank steak. Gumbo was our appetizer and chocolate cake was our dessert. Erin our server was sweet and efficient. She made us California out of towers feel very welcomed. I'm sure this place has drunk stragglers role in all the time....The food was AMAZING! This was a PERFECT end to our day. I love this place. Their food and service are unmatched. I will come back here when I return next year. (also try the Perky Peach cocktail) it is tasty!    Well done Muriels!

I have been to the Taquiera Calpenas at the Camden and Columbus Flea Market locations.  The tacos are fresh, stuffed, reasonably priced and delicious.  My favorites ones are the steak, chicken, pastor and carnitas.

Romantic, with great food.  I love this place.  Good location, great bartenders.  Amazing menu that's not too big.  The posole is especially satisfying if you're looking for a small lunch.  But the tacos are also outstanding, especially nice with those little pickled carrots.  If you're there with friends, get the chicharones to start.  Also, they have this cool pineapple drink they make in house called tepache that's unique.  Great tequila selection--love that you can do a flight.  Great place for a date, but also a nice setting for lunch with someone you like.

Easily my favorite spot to eat in Philly.  Drinks are great, service is solid, and the food is unreal.  The only down side is there is typically a wait on weekends, and when I know I'll be heading to the Khyber I usually don't eat all day because their portion sizes are huge, so the last thing I wanna do is wait (not their fault).  I 
Highly recommend this place.

Definitely my go to when I'm planning a coffee date with a friend or have a full day of studying to do. I love the variety: coffee, sandwiches, quiche, gelato even beer or wine. My only complaint is that it gets so crowded, especially on weekends but I don't think that's a bad thing for the business. I am always pleased with the service and the beverages/food. Just a phenomenal business and a bit more unique than other coffee houses. I also love that they always have soccer on. Decent WiFi for free, could use a few more outlets, and it would be awesome if they could expand or open another location!

Went on a Saturday night, not too crowded but definitely busy. Ordered three different types of bruschetta. Still can't decide which one was best! Great wine selection also. Definitely one of my favorite restaurants for drinks and small plates!

Overpriced, but the food is not horrible. 

What's horrible is the fact that none of the food is prepared fresh. They often utilize microwaves to heat-up pre-portioned food that may have been cooked many hours, or even days, earlier.

They have a good selection of drinks, but don't expect good food. They're incredibly lazy and uncaring with that part of the business.

Great place! Before I even tried the italian veggie wrap or the southwestern chicken wraps I purchased I liked this place.

Outgoing people that work there. Super cool atmosphere. Not too much $$ and a LOT of food for the price. A little gem on the corner for sure.

Vegetarian options! I got the #7 vegetarian meal. About an 7 out 10 stars. I would suggest maybe looking at the other options. Rice noodles are incredibly sticky and it's not seasoned very much at all. Still, very edible. The woman taking the cash as everyone has said is not friendly at all, but I'm just going to say she's misunderstood. Probably the life of the party when she's not at work. Worth going to!

This Double Knot sushi satellite eatery is located in the new and posh Franklin Hall "food court". I went with a coworker over lunch to try it out. Though there was a small line, it went by quickly. The menu has a lot of sushi options but the "chef's box" seemed like the best deal. $16 for 2 pieces of salmon sashimi, salmon over rice, edamame, and 2 rolls. Definitely a splurge for lunch but I decided to treat myself.

The meal is packed neatly in a cute little DK box. All the sides (wasabi, ginger, soy sauce, a spicy sauce) are in their own labeled containers. VERY aesthetically pleasing, not very environmentally friendly. 

This is what really annoyed me: for that giant box of $16 sushi, you get one little pea size amount of wasabi (pictured). Granted, I am a wasabi fiend but how can they possibly think that small amount is enough for all that sushi? I kindly asked for more wasabi and was told it would be a 50 cent charge by the manager. I can *maybe* understand if I ordered one roll or a couple pieces of sashimi but that was just annoying and unacceptable. 

The sushi itself was unbelievable. The fish was so fresh and abundant and the rice was incredible. Definitely way too much food for one person but would be perfect to split with someone. My favorite was the salmon over rice with spicy sauce! 

Though I'll never spend $16 on a lunch again, would definitely come back and order salmon over rice on its own. Everything else was similarly pricey but worth a "once in a while" lunch time splurge for high quality sushi.

I have lived here for 3 years and love it! The management has changed a few times, but I've never had any issues. I'm not sure about some of the comments about being towed, but if you don't have the proper sticker on your car than its your fault! The people that live here are mainly a mix of young professionals and older people, not many families, which is good. The noise can be loud on the weekends, but never past midnight. Its downtown, don't we live here to be in the middle of everything? Lol. The maintaince  staff has always been quick and professional, and the common areas are cleaned regularly.

I grew up less than 10 minutes from GBC so I'm no stranger to this place. Not much has changed there in my 30+ years of memory. The decor and menu are exactly the same as was in the days when i was to small to carry my own tray. The phrase "If it's not broke, don't fix it" applies here. If you're not a meat eater this probably isn't your place (unless you're fine with filling up on sides). It's not uncommon for the line to be wrapped around the building on Sundays and holidays. Ever since I was a kid I thought the heat lights cast a strange/creepy light on the servers faces.

Warning: they do not stand behind their work nor will they do right by the customer. 

I've been going to their Westampton location since the previous owner, Mike ran it. Always found them to be the most honest and reliable mechanics I'd ever encountered and as a result I've sent a ton of business their way. Sadly I can't say this about the new owner, Tim. This guy definitely doesn't stand by his work. 

A year ago my car had an engine failure. After discussing with the mechanic we decided to replace the engine. That's when the nightmare started. A year later and after $5000 spent I'm still without the car. The mechanic admits they can't or don't know how to fix it but the owner refuses to give me a refund. I've been beyond patient giving them every opportunity to make good, but Tim can apparently care less about his clients. 

Fair warning, they DO NOT Guarantee they're work. If they screw up, you'll be eating the cost and may even be without a vehicle. Not worth the risk. Find another shop. I sadly have to now prepare a filing court one year after I have them my car to fix so I could pass it on to my daughter.

I remember this place from when it used to be Zena's. Recently, all I've stopped in for is coffee, but the staff is friendly and the atmosphere inviting. I do wish they'd pour the coffee for you instead of handing you an empty cup to put the drink together yourself (coffee, sugar, cream, etc), but still keeps me coming back!
Rode our cruiser bikes in 103 degree heat downtown. Rolled out bikes in to this AWESOME bar. This place is a Definite go-to for us now. Great barkeep. Great atmosphere. Great tap list.
Had take out, Rigatoni Bolognese and a personal pizza with Spinach and Mushrooms. The food was very good. Mary the bartender was friendly and engaging. I will definitely be back.
Best froyo Ive ever had, seriously. Great decor to boot. Would ditch the crappy music/top 40.

I have been searching for a good Moscow Mule (vodka, lime, ginger beer) ever since I was introduced to the drink last year by a friend in Denver, where they are apparently all the rage.  Village Pub is the first place I've been to in Nashville that seems to have caught the spirit of the spirit.  They use pewter mugs rather than the traditional copper mugs, but the metal still gets frigid right down to the handle, which makes it feel close enough to a proper Mule for my liking. At $6, it is a well-priced cocktail, and they have several different variations if vodka is not for you.  For the mules alone, I will be sure to come back to Village Pub.

Other things they have going for them: 
1) a nice assortment of local beers. It's hip to be local these days, I know, but these folks seem REALLY committed to local.  For example, on tap they have Czann's Brewery, which is a one-man operation here in Nashville from a fellow who brews, bottles, and distributes all of his own product.  
And 2) a really relaxed, welcoming atmosphere.  Both the indoor and the outdoor seating was cozy, and the staff was very warm.

The only thing that drags Village Pub down, I think, is the food.  They specialize in pretzel sandwiches, the notion of which I found really exciting, but the sandwich interior was only so-so, with a disappointingly dryish pretzel.  It is certainly nice to have access to some nibbles while at the bar, in any case, so no real harm done.  

Come for the Mule, stay for some local drafts, and try not to build up too many expectations for the food.

this is my favorite thai in the city. if there is better i don't know about it. i love this place because i have asked on several occasions if there is fish sauce or whatever in the curry and i always get a very clear answer as though my question was understood. the answer is always "oh no we don't use fish sauce, we use vinegar [or maybe salt, i forget now], and it's totally vegan if you get it with tofu." that's what i like to hear. no bewildered stare. no awkward pause and "let me go ask the chef" as though the question has never been posed before.

plus it's fucking good. the red curry with tofu and the basil with mock duck are my favorites.

I'd leave zero stars if it were possible. I called to order fried rice before my drive back to Chicago. Special fried rice with no pork. Simple right? Obviously not. There was diced ham in the rice and when I called back they told me ham is not the same as pork. Huh?!?!?! Then they don't apologize but accuse me of not being clear. DO NOT SUPPORT THIS HORRIBLE BUSINESS!!! I could've have an allergic reaction because of their ignorance. Unacceptable.

I recently used Salon Fiber's Prenup Service to style my hair and makeup for my Indian pre-wedding event.  My stylist, Emily, was AMAZING!!!  She arrived early and had all her supplies nicely organized, which allowed for her to work so efficiently.  She was very patient and flexible and really took the time to understand my vision for my look.  She even gave me an extra lip gloss to touch-up my make-up throughout the evening.  Emily additionally did hair for my mother and sister --- they were both very pleased with the level of service.  Emily was so patient and calming.  She helped us all feel very relaxed and confident.

For the Indian brides out there --- Emily also placed a matta patti tikka (headpiece) for me.  She did a fantastic job with the placement and the headpiece remained secure for the entire evening.

For anyone in the area looking for impeccable hair/make-up services, you absolutely must select Salon Fiber.

Beautiful nail salon! Very posh! Lan did an amazing job on my nails! She listened and gave me exactly what I wanted. I'm very happy with my nails and will be going back regularly! Definitely highly recommend this place!
This is an awesome place. Service was great and I highly recommend the Churrasco Hanger Steak with a side of Crispy Brussel Sprouts (substituted for the fries)!!
Yummy! Great flavor choices and a lot of different toppings for you to add.! At $ .40 per ounce I can see quite a few revisits!
ROACHES CRAWLING ON THE WALLS! Walk in and you'll slide all over the dirty, grease filled floors. OMG.

I've been to the Nudy's on Route 30 in Frazer and this new one in Chadds Ford doesn't seem to be as good. Service was scattershot and the food didn't seem as hot and fresh as I'm used to at Nudy's. I also think the prices are a bit steep for what is delivered. A breakfast sandwich on toast  for $6.00 seems high. Also a $2.00 surcharge for maple syrup is kinda lame. Paid $20 for a basic breakfast. Since this is a new location I'll give it another try.

I tend to stick with my favorite restaurants in this town when it comes to Indian cuisine. For a change I tried India Cafe, which was conveniently located for us. The two curries we ordered, one vegetarian and one chicken, were quite good. The naan was crisp and fresh and the rice well prepared. It was more than we could eat so we each have enough for a lunch this week. Service was good and the place was very busy, so I was impressed with the attention that was not over-hovering. While I probably should not give a five star rating on a first visit, given we only tried two dishes, I think this is a good choice and believe they will do well on whatever dish you choose.

The Eye Bar does a great job of bringing unique European lines to St. Louis.   They have the best selection of eyewear in St. Louis, hands down.

While I have never gotten glasses at The Eye Bar (I have family in the optical industry), I have stopped in to look a few times.  They are always nice and never pushy.  

This weekend we stopped in after my boyfriend's sunglasses lost a screw.  They were not purchased at The Eye Bar, but they very happily replaced the screw.  We really appreciated their fantastic customer service.

If you're looking for new glasses, The Eye Bar is definitely the best spot in St. Louis.
Great Food, Friendly service and good prices. The Hot link is one of my favorite items, but you cant go wrong with anything you get there.
Got right in on a Saturday night. Great burger, amazing salty caramel shake, and great service! We will be back!
Came at the busiest time on the busiest day but the service and food were very good and worth waiting for.

Came here to bowl after we couldn't bowl at the bowling stadium, it was slow when we first came in and really got busy from the pub crawl. We sat at the bar and Edgar helped us he was the first friendly face we came across in Reno. We ordered drinks and the bacon wrapped dates which by the way were bloody fantastic ! Try those suckers you won't be disappointed. 
Then we bowled two games and had a lot of fun. It was very expensive though 18 for one game 16 for the second but we wanted to bowl so we just paid it. 
My only  issue was the rude security guard at the front when we were coming in he said I'm guessing your here for the pub crawl and I said oh well actually we were hoping to bowl and he goes well actually cool and just stared at me and I had to walk around him to get in. Shitty attitude problem, just weird and all of Reno seemed to be this way with an attitude.
Also the lack of servers in the place when it got busy was irritating. We had to search people out to help us. 
Had a good time here overall though and the bowling was fun.

Dining at the bar with Jared as your bartender is a 5 star experience . He's an excellent craft cocktail maker and highly attentive. The food is pricey but excellent, and if you go on Wednesdays they give you a number of free appetizers at the bar.

My husband & I came here for dinner one evening.  The decor is nice & I like the blue Dolphins on the wall.  It's a new place on Golf links & we decided to give it a try.  We ordered the large egg drop soup, kung pao chicken, & barbecue lo mien.  The soup had hardly any taste to it.  It tasted like hot water seasoned with salt & pepper with bits of eggs & a few green peas thrown into it.  Kung pao chicken had too much oil in it & lots of peanuts, but only a few pieces of chicken & veggie.  Also, the barbecue lo mien was not good at all.  It was greasy & tasteless with a few pieces of barbecue meat & few strands of beansprouts.  The server was nice, but the food came out very quickly, which is not a good sign.  Food must have been precooked.   We are not sure if we want to give this another chance.

From the rude condescending tone of the front desk personnel upon arriving at the hotel to check in on our reservation, the unhelpful service personnel by phone as I entered our room and it reeked of smoke.  The random dirty socks that were left in the room, generally shabby room with exposed thermostat, or the difficultly getting the dog bowls from valet service.  This was an abhorrent experience from walking in to leaving.

I had heard good things about this brewpub and was excited to try it.  First of all it's very noisy so be prepared.  I was disappointed in the beer list.
