I love this local hang out! The patio has a great vibe. The food is fun and I enjoy each of my meals because they are large portions so I always share with my friends and have left overs. They have great local beer selection and I highly recommend for my friends that are visiting from out of town!

OMG YES!

This is currently our favorite restaurant.  Upscale and classy all the way, the entrees vary between el seafood es deliciouso and steak.  Fortunately  their food is way better than my Spanish.

You must get the escargot and bananas foster.  I recommend eating them seperately though.
Highly recommend the Kung Pao Chicken. Great service. My whole family loves this restaurant.

Great service,!  That itself is a five star.  Chefs were quick.  Price is awesome!!!  Minus one star only because not authentic sushi, but still outstanding.  Portions are to the pricing.  Fish was ok.  Come early because it gets packed quick.  Also, sit at counter if possible.  Much easier to order.

Queso Fundido, spinach & mushroom enchilada, 2 mini chimichangas and chicken tinga taco. To drink was a mango and a peach margarita. 

Service, food, and drinks were great! Immediately seated, owner came to greet us. Our order was taken promptly and the food came very soon after.

Fun atmosphere during busy happy hour on a Wednesday.

I read a lot of reviews on here and decided to give it a try. The bar close to our house (Risky Business on Kolb/Sunrise) had my Steelers on but they don't turn up the volume on the any games. Even one would be nice to get the feel and excitement of the game.
This place has the vibe and feel we wanted! 
The breakfast burger was excellent! Their beers were cold and the service was fantastic! 
It was worth the drive. I'll be back!
Great food, great atmosphere.  Be sure to make a reservation on a busy night.  Had a splendid experience here in Nashville for a convention, this for sure added to it.

I just had my first massage with Karen. She was absolutely amazing. The atmosphere was so relaxing. I added on the aromatherapy to my massage and she was extremely helpful finding the perfect oils to help relax and balance my experience. I definitely recommend Karen, she was great!

Frozen custard was another must have while visiting Saint Louis, and Ted Drewes was the obvious choice. It seems like the kind of place where there will be a perpetual line at any time of day, but luckily there are lots of windows and the lines move quick!

I ordered a "concrete" with cookie dough and peanut butter cups and it was delicious!  A quick google search told me that the difference between frozen custard and ice cream is the addition of egg yolks to custard. It definitely didn't taste eggy, but it did taste different than regular ice cream. A good different!

Some of the servers were flipping the ice cream cups upside down before handing it to the customers, hence the name concrete...what a trick! :)

Beer: Excellent. The only reason to go here. However, you can only get one beer at a time, even if it's a 4 oz. pour. The waitress gave me some baloney excuse about how they don't want the beer to sit out that long. If your beer goes bad that fast, you've got a problem. They also have a card that tells you that you should only order a pint of beer if you're really serious about drinking, and they suggest you use caution if you order a pint of beer with an abv of over 7%. Woah, a whole pint!?!

Food: mediocre at best. Everything we had could have been better in some way. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't good either. Ceviche was just a scoop of fish sitting in vinegar, street corn was overcooked, crab tacos were dry, burger was decent but small, donut was burnt on the outside. The burger came with a pint of beer (look out).  The waitress asked me what kind of beer I wanted. How am I supposed to answer that question when you won't bring me multiple small pours?  I'd have to sit there for two hours before I could make a decision. 

Service: below average. Hostess didn't say a word, I don't know my server's name, and it took too long to get our check. She would not budge on the multiple beers thing. I'm sure that's policy, but I've never been to a restaurant, especially a mediocre one, and been told no for any reason whatsoever. I'm a grown up. I think I can handle two four-ounce beers at once.

Overall, this is a pretty pretentious, disappointing restaurant with really good beer. If you've got a bunch of tattoos, a sick new haircut, and like being told how much you can drink at a bar, then this is the place for you. Otherwise, get a growler to go and order a pizza or something.

We have never eaten at an Indian restaurant and we decided to be adventurous.    Since we didn't know what we would like, we simply asked our waiter and he was very helpful in narrowing down our choices and deciding what to order.   We were pleasantly surprised and LOVED everything!   We ordered two main dishes:  Chicken Makhani and Lamb Korma and both were amazing.    I overheard a gentleman at the table next to us tell the waiter that he has eaten at many Indian restaurants but that this was, by far, his favorite so far.

This is a fantastic place for breakfast and lunch in the French Quarter. 

It's just honest, simple, good food for a great price.

I've had nearly everything from this little place. 

Pastries. Pancakes. Egg breakfasts. Chicken ceasar salads. Sandwiches. Mimosas... YES! They have mimosas!

Just know that it's a pretty small place, and can get packed pretty quickly. But be patient. The line usually goes pretty fast, though the tables don't always clear fast enough for my liking.

If you want something fast, delicious and of high quality for the price, I would definitely recommend this spot.

Went there on a Sunday for lunch at around noon.  It was a little difficult to get someone's attention to get seated.  However, once we did, It was easy to get outdoor seating, and the waitress nicely volunteered to get a high chair for our infant without us asking.  

The coffee was about average for a decent restaurant - not bad, but nothing special.  I ordered the salmon omelet and my wife ordered eggs, pancakes and sausage.  The salmon omelet was flavorful and the Old Bay sour cream was a nice touch that worked well.  My wife found her meal totally unremarkable - not bad, but nothing we couldn't have done at least as well at home.  The prices were pretty reasonable for a sit down restaurant on the Main Line ($9.50 for the salmon omelet).  

The service was pleasant enough, but a touch erratic - it was quite a while before I was offered a coffee refill, for example.  After we got the bill, we found that my wife had been charged incorrectly for her order, and when she asked to get it corrected, was briefly lectured on the confusing way in which she'd ordered before they agreed to change the bill.  

Overall, our experience wasn't bad - the high points were the salmon omelet and the outdoor seating on a beautiful day - but we'd be more inclined to keep looking for a really good brunch near Wynnewood than  to make a return visit.

This could be an entirely pointless review, but I really have no idea what their coffee tastes like. I went in midday for an iced coffee. I wanted to sit outside, but there is no outdoor seating, just a spattering of chairs and tall tables with stools inside. I decided to stand at the table while I waited for my iced coffee, which was supposed to be made using their roasted Rwandan blend.

Nobody gave me an indication of how long it would take, only that my name would be called. They were nice enough when they communicated that to me, but I still went in with the expectation that it could take up to 15 min. After 15 min, I started internally debating if I should make an inquiry about my $5 iced coffee. Then, I decided I'll wait a little longer because I don't think I could appreciate the taste of a beverage hastily made for someone who was starting to get agitated.

The waiting continued, and then I started to think that my name was whispered and someone stole my cup (or they just took my money and ignored my order completely). I stood there, coffeeless and waiting, for nearly 40 min. Then, I just came to the conclusion that one comes to when they realize they weren't really that invested in the first place, which is "fuck it". I didn't bother to even ask what happened or try to get a refund. Keep my money. I am too poor to be spending money on overpriced coffee anyway. That transaction will stand such that I just purchased a fresh batch of casual contempt.

Here is the massive problem with this joint - they really don't want to make money or sell you pizza.  This would not be a problem if they were a vacuum cleaner repair store, but this is a flippen pizza parlor.  If you want to see what I mean then try an experiment - try to use their awful online ordering system and wait for them to call and tell you they are "out" of whatever you were ordering.  There is some magical time of night (I'm guessing approximately whatever time you consider to be the dinner hour) that the place suddenly stops making new pizza and will only sell you whatever old junk they've had sitting around.  This is so unfortunate because really their pizza is superb.  I mean really really good.  THAT is the ONLY reason I have given them 4 chances to disappoint me.  No more, I'm done.

Been going here for 11years with no complaints. Their pizza is amazing the BBQ chicken is my favorite of their specialty pies. Excellent salads too with better ingredients then one would expect from a pizza place. I recommend the Molise Salad it's wonderful.
This place sucks what diner stops serving breakfast on Sunday at 11 o'clock You Are Not A Diner!

The owners are very friendly and made us feel welcome. We had the guacamole appetizer and it was so fresh and delicious. They have authentic Mexican dishes on the menu so if you're looking for 'Americanized' Tex-Mex type food you should go elsewhere. Both of our dinners were delicious and I enjoyed the spiciness of my chicken dish. My husband didn't order a spicy dish but it was still very good and flavorful.

We had the oysters, impossible burgers, and wine. All excellent and we can't wait to go back! Their bread's amazing too. It was an extra special experience because the weather was nice so we sat out on their beautiful patio. Really enjoyable atmosphere. Our waiter Wayne was super attentive and friendly. Great service! 5 stars overall for sure.

Over the last year, service seems to be declining along with food quality (the menu is still great, but the preparation is no longer spot-on).  I no longer consider Brio competition for St. Louis's authentic American-Italian restaurants, but rather a nicer alternative to Macaroni Grill.  I'm rating 4 stars only in the hope they can re-earn the fifth I once granted.

A coworker and I noticed the store hand changed hands and was under this new name today on a trip that started out with Neely's as out destination. We figured it was worth a quick drop in, since MetroCenter is devoid of food options.

The good... Super low prices. We weren't sure if it was by accident, by promotion, or what, but we both ate (with drinks) for around five bucks. Service was quick and friendly. Food was price-appropriate. Fries were excellent. Varied menu with pizza, burgers, calzones, etc... Ordinarily I'm not a fan of the shotgun restaurant approach, but in MetroCenter it almost makes sense.

The marginal... You self-serve your pizza from a heating unit. The pizza was clearly pre-made crust cardboard stock frozen pie. Bland, gooey cheese. Mixed buffet and menu like all other entities that have tried to co-exist with Neely's over the years...it didn't work for them, why keep trying? Extra unused buffet steam tray counter crammed into front of restaurant takes up space and raises cleaniness questions. Decor MetroCenter chic. 

Will I eat here again? Probably. Would I recommend it to a friend? Probably not. 

PS - Delivery with a minimum order of $10.

This place was incredible.  We daughter and I had so much fun painting and getting to know people.  I absolutely would recommend it to everyone.  We were traveling from the Bay Area to Sparks for a mini-vacation and came across it on the internet and they allow under 21 and even have a family day on Sundays.   Big plus !!!
Two takeout dishes, chicken tikka and palak lamb, both ordered extra spicy.  Lamb dish was very nice, but the chicken dish had zero spiciness.

Archway is an unassuming, if not a little scary looking sandwich joint underneath the parking garage on 8th street between Arch and Filbert.  This is NOT a place I would go to if I had not been taken there.  However, after 2 years working at 8th and Market it is my savior on a hungover morning.  This my friends is the home of the perfect bacon egg and cheese on a kaiser.  The perfect proportions of all three ingredients and the crispiest bacon....with a little hot sauce this sandwich rights all wrongs.  The staff knows there regulars and greets everyone with a "hey sweetie, what can I get for you today?" However, this question is mute because the grill guy, in my case already has my sandwich going since he got on it as soon as I walked in the door.  Apart from this I can also vouch for their Texas Tommys.  It's super inexpensive as well, the kind of place you feel well fed after having spent about 5 bucks.  Anyway, if you love Bacon Egg and cheese on a kaiser, I would seek this place out, if not, then it may not be worth the pilgrimage.

Bumped up a star. Went here again by default because there aren't many salon choices on Sunday's. 
   This time it was noticeable that my hair was curled & it held up pretty well. The stylist was very nice but seemed a bit inexperienced. Not used to having give instructions or ask for product. I still had to do some tweaking before I could go out. 
   Also, little side note, I wish they would ask if you'd like something to drink after you're in the salon & seated at the hair station. Instead it was mentioned as I was walking thru the door but after I was washed & having my hair done is when I would've liked one!;) 
Overall not a bad experience, I would consider coming again.
Delicious food... The tzatziki is fresh and the frappes are great. Great local spot but the service could be friendlier. Portions are a little small for the price.

I've gone here to get my husband and my car re-keyed (gotta love that Honda feature) and they are very reasonably priced and super friendly! They were able to fix it with the same keys- which Honda said they couldn't do at less than a third of what Honda quoted. 
And when my awesomely old school window crank fell out after getting my car re-keyed, I stopped back by and they had it fixed in less than 5 minutes, no charge. Awesome.

I planned a sushi social here for my Japanese Club at the University of South Florida. They were very friendly about it and reserved our area for us. So many people showed up and the waiters were friendly and quick to cater to people. They sat us around the grills and everyone got up and socialized since this was a sushi social. Most people liked their food, though some people said it wasn't to their liking, I personally liked my California Roll but was so busy walking around and conversing that I did not have the chance to have a bigger meal. The steakhouse has a nice layout and sushi prices are reasonable, grill prices are pretty standard. A nice sushi restaurant and a great place to have a social.
Comprehensive selection (sometimes a little discretion could be a good thing), but sure to find something for everyone. Decent prices for a store of this quality.

Had a dinner there with my family last night. Hibachi. The place is nice but loud, which is fine. The food was good. However, the service is the most horrible I have ever experienced. We were at the table at 7:40.  The waitress, who seemed to be serving about 6 hibachi tables by her self, didn't show up till 8.  Got the water and wine glasses and 8:15.  Soup at 8:30. Salads at 8:45.  Finally at 9:05 the chef showed up. The waitress seemed annoyed for most off the time.  Not helpfully with the menu. Not interested in her job and overworked.  The chef was not engaging with us and boring compare to some other hibachi Restaurants. At the end two people at our table were over charged had to argue with the manager. I think if this place won't change it's attitude about costumer service and do something about it they will go down very fast.
Chill bar, perfect for a quiet Monday night. Sidecar was great and chips with salt and pepper the perfect foil for a sweet drink. Wish we'd discovered it earlier in our trip.

The hubby and I had the CA burger and the teriyaki burger with a side of fries. Lots of kids there today - they have a nice little sand area for kids to play. They have lots of picnic tables to sit at and an adult only section that is raised about the grass area. Pretty good burgers. This is the second time we've been there and we think there burgers are slightly better than average. Not sure if we'd return for a third time. Parking was a bit hard to find.

Came here for dinner on Christmas Eve. It was super packed, but a good amount of tables. 

We ordered the Five Spice Chicken Wings for appetizer, Baked Chilean Sea Bass, Braised Tofu with Black Mushroom and Vegetable, and a Crab Meat Egg White Fried Rice.

The food was really good! Everything was flavorful without being over oily or salted. The Sea Bass was cooked perfectly. I love how they added real crab meat to the fried rice. I usually have the egg white fried rice at other restaurants and they don't add crab meat in there. Nice touch that elevates the dish. The chicken wings were very moist. And because it was so moist, to avoid overcooking, one of my pieces was actually undercooked. It was a tad bloody. But it was so juicy that I forgive them that one piece! 

Overall, this place is more fancy I would say. We will definitely come back for some good Chinese food when we're in Reno!

Small little korean fusion place in the Brentwood, business area. Limited menu (some items are only available certain days), but great food. hours can be tricky so plan accordingly. Staff was really nice and helpful. Food came out quickly, I'll definitely be back to try more things.

Had the Gyro sandwich special, the sandwich was well made, good portion and they used Lebanese flat bread that MADE the flavor and taste, only better I have ever had was in Cambridge MA on Mass Ave!!!  While there, I mentioned it was the first time we had been there and the gentleman behind the counter allowed me to sample the hummus and the rice and beans, and OMG, the olive oil used on the hummus set it apart from any I have EVER had and the freshness of the rice and beans was impressive, we will be back there many times from now on!!
I love Yats! The chili cheese étouffée is incredible! I haven't met anyone who doesn't like Yats. Beware, cash only! So come prepared. Definitely worth it. Such a gem of Indy!

Last night me and 24 others were visiting from Houston Texas and we had Jabari as a waiter and Mike and Billy cooking grilling our oysters. Our service was superb and the food was outstanding. Anyone going by ask for Jabari. You will not be disappointed.

Nice ambiance and great pizza! I ordered ham and pineapple pizza. Hubby got a trio of eggplant parmigiana, chicken parmesan, and ravioli. He said it was good but next time he would just stick with sharing a pizza with me. The waitress (Kat) was kind and was very informative with the menu. She said she really loved working there, and it showed! We will definitely go back!

Some friends took me here back in November. I would love to go back.  The Mango Shrimp was on point!  The sweet to spice ratio was just right.  And it was actually served inside of a mango which really turned me on.  For dessert we shared the fried ice cream...very very delicious.  Never had fried ice cream before.  Looking forward to that again.

It was a Friday night and the place was packed but we didin't wait that long to be seated (approx. 10-15 minutes).  The kitchen area is open for your viewing pleasure.  The food came quick enough.  They allow you to bring your own bottle and if you are celebrating a birthday or something you can bring your own cake.  Not sure if there is a cake cutting fee though.

Also I had a bite of my bff's Roti Canai...the reviews are accurate...very tasty.
This location drive thru is so slow, I've been waiting in line for ten minutes before is started writing this review. There are still two cars ahead of me...

On Friday, 1/29/16, my wife and I stopped by Sam's Brick Oven Pizza for a drink and pizza. We got the Short Rib Pizza, Allagash on tap for me and Chardonnay for my wife. The pizza was excellent, the beer cold and wine just right. It was very crowded because an 'after work' group was there, but the bartender, Claire; never left anyone waiting, kept everyone happy and never missed a beat. I'm glad we came here and we can't wait to come back!

Ever since the first day we moved here from Denver 2 months ago we have loved this pizza place. The staff is awesome and authentic and the pizza is so delicious. As long as we live within their delivery range we will be loyal to them :-)

I'd rate it 6 stars if I could. What an experience. Coming from the New York area it's not easy to find genuine Italian culture in Tennessee. I can tell you that I've never even experienced something so Italian (outside my family) even in NY! Go for the food, stay for the experience. Absolutely incredible.

I'm an old fashion girl that really appreciates good customer service. It's very hard to find now a days where a hostess actually does their job and welcomes you to an establishment. This Village Inn was no exception. I'm not really that picky just a simple hello and follow me and I will seat you will work. I should have let that be my que to just leave, but I chose to stay and eat. My food tasted like old grease. I got eggs, bacon and hash browns. My daughters food was cold. I can't complain about the waitress because she did her job. Nothing more, nothing less. I'm really disappointed to write this as I grew up going to Village Inn. I didn't buy a pie because I was afraid it was going to be horrible and the memory of a good Village Inn pie would be lost forever.

If I had our wedding day to do over, I would absolutely book the Riviera Mansion again in a heartbeat. After the beautiful experience we had holding our reception here this summer, I can't recommend the Riviera Mansion loudly, often, or enthusiastically enough.

Our guests have since remarked many times about how much they enjoyed the space and food. The staff helped direct the flow of the crowd and there were so many beautiful areas to celebrate. The staff made sure my husband and I ate (so many brides and grooms never get the chance!), let us serve the guests in the buffet line ourselves (this was very important to us, and ended up being my favorite part of the whole wedding), and took care of everything so we didn't have to worry about anything during the stress and excitement of the day.

Breanna is also a dream of a coordinator. She made me instantly feel like I was in good hands and my very particular vision was possible. When I started planning I was across the country for several months, and Breanna bent over backwards to help me create the wedding of my dreams long distance. 

This place has an alchemy to it that made for the best day of our lives, in the most beautiful setting.

This review is for Parkallen pizza; we've been enraptured and haven't yet ventured to the other parts of the menu, even though they look great.

A quick shout out to the staff, who have always been sweet and understanding as we navigate the relationship straits that is the picking of the toppings. There are few dilemmas as great, and as meaningful.

I guess it goes without saying that pizza tastes much better when eating it right from the kitchen; delivery is foodie insult we inflict when we are lazy and hungry. Parkallen pizza is still very good when delivered, but in-house it was sublime! It has the most tasty crust I've long tasted in a pizza. The contributions of each ingredient (we shared a half Hawaiian and half meat-lover) could be noticed and appreciated.

The hunnybunny's place is near-by, enough so that we've eaten in and picked up pie for transport home. More than once it's been an open question whether we can survive the seductive pizza smell filling the car or should we just pull over and dig in. You've been warned :-)

Antiques everywhere!

I've seen some pretty unique items here. There's a little something for everyone, and the prices are decent. I wouldn't advise bringing young children inside, though. This is a very small store, and even an adult like myself gets nervous about the chance of knocking something off of a shelf.

If you can keep your hands, and randomly flailing accessories, to yourself (that  heavy purse can turn into a wrecking ball real quick) then this is a neat place to visit.

My husband and I were passing through the city from a long road trip, and I have always wanted to try this place out. Well, I have no regrets! The place itself is super clean and chic. The ambience was very warming. And our waitress Laura was the best! She attended us instantly very friendly and with a smile on her face! The food, one word, AMAZING!!! The jambalaya had the perfect blend of flavor and the shrimp and grits were so creamy! I recommend going to Desire as soon as you get to the French quarter, and don't forget to ask for Laura; she will definitely make you feel at home!

Wow! The food is fantastic! You haven't lived until you've had the wild boar bolognese with the home made pasta !!
Also the octopus appetizer is wonderful

The shrimp and grits were amazing and the BEST I ever had in my life! I get this dish often when I dine out and hands down it's the BEST! Also, try it with the crab meat, which enhanced the dish and made it so much better!

I love having Yolklore as an option in our neighborhood. I especially love the Nest Egg, but have loved everything I've tried. Baked sweets are always delicious. I appreciate that the kid's menu has wider variety than many breakfast places. Coffee is great, decor enjoyable. Love Yolklore!

12:20 PM: 10 minutes to be seated-seated for 15 minutes and no server or acknowledgement that we exist. Restaurant 90% full and no staff. 12/21/15

Good past reviews! What happened?

I have truly enjoyed my stay here at the Double Tree. It has all of the clean rooms, amenities, and friendly service you would expect from a Hilton Brand Hotel. If you are a Hilton Honors Guest they even have 3 special floors just for you! Oh, and don't forget the warm cookies when you check in!

The hotel is close to the Amtrak station (about 6 blocks) and they have a free shuttle that will pick you up. My train arrived early and after going to baggage claim I called for the shuttle and was picked up in less than 5 minutes. In the lobby you will find a bar, restaurant, and lounge. I ate at the restaurant (but sat in the lunge area) and it was pretty good, albeit a little pricey. The bar has all the major beers you would expect and a pretty good wine list as well. I never did use the pool or fitness center but the hotel does have them. Over all I give it 5 stars and recommend it to anyone visiting Wilmington.

Had the filet mignon and it was so tender you could cut it with a fork! I was unsure about the food since it was different from my usual fare but wow, we will be back. The salad dressing was so creamy and good I got extra and put it on my potatoes. Glad we tried it, everything was delicious. We also ordered the apple strudel w/ice cream, yummy!

I recently moved back to Nashville, after treating my cat JuJu for kidney issues in Miami for 2 weeks after he consumed a lily. It seemed like he was getting worse, so I brought him to the closest Banfield as he already had a wellness plan. The staff was great. Upon arrival, I learned that the female vet was not in and they had a male vet filling in from another location. After letting them know that he does not do well with men, they offered to get us an appointment at a nearby location and promised us we would have a female vet tech, Jessica. They let us go into the room early, so I could let him out and he could roam. Jessica was fantastic and made us feel comfortable. After giving him a shot to calm his nausea, we went home where he was ok for about 36 hours, so we made another appointment. 

I called several times between appointments and was always greeted with compassion for my situation and was given helpful information, especially from Juan at the front desk. After a second appointment, we were sent home with additional medication to help him out. He had lost a lot of weight throughout this process, wasn't eating, was severely sick to his stomach and would not let us give him any medicine that night (a process he never liked, but would oblige). After much debate, I called in tears and told them we had to do something, so they made me an appointment that afternoon with Dr. Hamm. After much discussion, I made the most difficult decision to end his suffering. Dr. Hamm was wonderful and explained the entire process to me and allowed me to choose which parts I wanted to be a part of. She and Jessica gave me time with him and helped me through each step. I will forever be grateful to them for their support and compassion. A few days later, I received a card in the mail from the staff with heartfelt condolences. I cannot thank them enough.

My friends and I were looking for an inexpensive but good place for lunch, so we asked a ticket vendor for a recommendation. He suggested Brew Brothers, right in the hotel we were already in. 

We got there and there was no wait (although it was 3pm). However, I suppose that was the perfect time to go because the pizzas were two for one! (So about 9 bucks for 2 pizzas)  Pretty awesome deal. I wish I had gone in on that deal though. My ahi tuna sandwich + fries apparently gets sold out every night, but I thought it was pretty average. The tuna was not rare enough for me. Not rare at all, actually. I did try my friend's BBQ chicken pizza which was bomb.

Overall, nice restaurant and friendly servers. Try to come during happy hour.
Loved the iced mocha more than the quiche I ordered. The atmosphere and service is great. Better than Starbucks.

I'm really impressed with Bridgestone Arena and I like it a lot more than the YUM! Center that's here in Louisville. It's a huge venue with tons of options for beer, liquor, food and vendor souvenir shops. I came here to see the one and only Stevie Nicks, we didn't have floor seats because they were too expensive, but the seats we did have were close enough that we could see, get good pics and good video as well. 

The sound inside of the arena was loud and the acoustics were amazing. It was the escape from real life that I craved and not only did I lose my cherry to seeing one of my idols that night, but also my voice screaming (just ask Scott XD). 

The food smelled great, but we knew better than to get food at an arena because of the up sell on it, instead we had a few drinks. Honestly the beer prices weren't bad, I spent too much money, but for a 16oz craft beer from draft it was $11 and for a 25oz domestic canned beer it was also $11. All the bartenders were very knowledgeable about the products and spirits. Scott didn't think that his cocktails were worth it because we like ours strong, though. At $20 for a double is about the average for any sort of concert venue. The whole staff was extremely friendly and helpful in whatever questions we had when getting drinks, walking around or getting back to our seats. 

One of the major pluses to Bridgestone Arena is that they have a section for smokers & people who just want some fresh air to go outside and be able to re-enter at. This was excellent because between The Pretenders and Stevie Nicks there was about a 20 minute intermission that would have just been boring to sit through, so we were able to get a drink each and enjoy a cancer stick outside. 

Overall I would LOVE to see another one of my idols at Bridgestone Arena again, and soon because we weren't able to explore Nashville too much due to the next day being election day (gotta do my civic duty!), but I'm all. The. Way. Down. I'm blown away (tire pun intended) by this arena and you will be too!

My experience? Good...okay. It needed some flavoring. Too expensive for the size. 
The attitude? Horrible. We got there precisely at 5 pm. There was a "young man" who took the seat at the door to let us in at 5:05. That said, we were the first ones in there. They asked if we had reservations. Since we didn't they told us to sit at the bar. Mind you the whole time we wed there maybe 5 tables got seated. 
The red headed bartender had an attitude that should never have been in the service industry. She and the dude at the door blinded me to anything possible. She was snarky, show off, condescending and just plain old rude. She pranced around behind the bar like she knew everything. Yes, thus 30 something ruined my experience. 
If food is so so then the whole experience can be changed by the attitude of the staff. I guess I don't get the whole "hipster" thing. 
I'm not sure why it got all the fives. My experience echoed the other twos and threes.

I'm a huge fan of burgers so this only makes sense for me to do. Go and eat burgers. I heard that this place serves up hamburgers of cows that wear socks, listen to classical music and are petted a lot. great, lets see if this really makes a difference in the taste. 

Well it didn't seem to much different. The burgers were good...a little greasier then expected but good. The place was very crowded but we managed to get a table. Yeah its a burger place. I would go back back becasue it was better then McDonalds/Burger King if I'm looking for a fast food fix.
Great place!  Cheers to more options in Donelson.  Only thing is... it seems like the product keeps changing.  Quesadilla was nice and stringy cheesy last week but cheese was like velveeta this week.

While I will go into more detail, there is one word that describes my lunch there today: Amazing!

I went there for lunch this afternoon with a large group of coworkers.We were seated quickly in a large booth. I loved the atmosphere. Very laid back and comfortable. Service was also very quick. Our server greeted us within moments, bringing multiple bottles (literally, they were obviously previously booze bottles) of water and filling our glasses. We needed more time with the menu, but as soon as we were ready, he was there to take our order.

I got the Southern Classic (Pimento cheese, applewood smoked bacon, fried onions, bread and butter pickles) with a side of Zucchini Straws. This burger was amazing. It was cooked perfectly medium rare and the flavors blended together in a way I never thought was possible. The burger patty was also very well seasoned and had that nice little crisp on the edges. It is honestly one of the best burgers I have ever had. The Zucchini Straws were also very good and the sauce they serve with them took them up another notch.

The rest of the table got a variety of burgers including the Double Major, Freshman, Stanford, and the Going Greek. We also had fries and tots. Everyone was super happy with their food. The only complaint I heard was that the Going Greek was a bit on the small side compared to the rest of the options, but the person who ordered it was very happy with the flavor even with the smaller size.

I will be back for sure. The only downside I can think of is the cost. With the sides not being included in the price of the burgers, it can be a bit on the pricey side for a burger. That said, I feel like the quality and service make it very worth it.

La la loved Lüke's. Can't beat $0.75 raw oysters daily from 3-6pm. They were so good we ordered 5 dozen of them. Hands down one of my fav dishes of all time is the Louisiana rabbit and chicken liver pâté. You must order it if you dine in. The bread pudding was nice and warm and a great way to end a meal. Make a reservation and go!

Maybe it was too high expectations, but the woman who took our order  didn't know if the ribs were baby backs or not.  kale slaw was on menu but they didn't have. Instead we got rice and beans, which were highly bland and disappointing. The tacos were good, but just good. The duclaw beer was fabulous, and we ate outside on street (not a pretty street I might add) but it was less than $30 and it was satisfying, but not exciting or amazing by a long shot; not inclined to return.

This is the worst Steak n Shake I've ever been to. Waiting 5 minutes in the drive thru before they acknowledge that you're there is ridiculous. I've tried to give them the benefit of the doubt on their slowness a couple times now. Never again will I go there. Horrible!

We have there five times and have good food and great service but the sixth time not so good the food was good the service was terrible we got our food but nothing else.My wife had to get the saucers and silver ware and ice.
When we were finished we waited and waited then we
had to go to the hostess station and they had
To page our waitress. To get our bill She was on break. We will go back BUT will not have the same waitress  Other wise I would have given them five stars

The bulgogi here is stellar, and everything else is pretty delicious. I can't say its the best Korean in town, because, like that other reviewer said, each one does something better. However, it is the best place to gather around food with friends. In fact, I'm planning a birthday party gathering of Korean BBQ with friends around the grill tables, then a night of Karaoke in one of their special rooms.

You need to get at least 2 orders of bbq, so it can get a little on the expensive side, but it is well worth it.

These guys are great! Friendly service with a fresh brew and good prices! 

Ken is my go-to and always does a great job for a haircut/beard-trim. Recently, while he was away, I went to Nick who gave me one of the best fades I've ever had. I'm definitely a long-time customer. These guys are awesome!

Great little bike shop with can do attitude. I found them to be very knowledgeable and accommodating in fixing the problems with my Trek Bicycle. Service and Parts pricing was reasonable and they did their best to handle all of my issues and get me back on the road even though it was shortly before closing. Thanks guys

I've been here several times because I live close. I love the rewards program. I get $1 off almost every time I go. I use to think this was the best fro-yo until I tried a really good place off of Prytania. Now Orange Leafs flavors don't have enough flavor for me. I still go because its a quick fix for my craving. The staff is wishy washy and if you want to try something, they hold on to those little cups for dear life. My other spot gives you a handful and let you have at it! All in all... It's ok for what it is.
Emilio did a fantastic job on my '84 Maserati Biturbo; adjusting the carb and getting it through smog. Very talented guy (reasonable too!) He's hard to get ahold of but worth the wait. Thanks Emilio!

I finally found my Philadelphia Spa! Was very pleased with the services I had earlier this week.The front desk staff is attentive & efficient. Michelle is very nice & professional & talented. She re-shaped my brows & I haven't been happier with they way they look. It smells amazing in the Spa & its hard to walk out without a soap or candle for yourself. Their "beauty boutique" is surprisingly a great place for a hostess gift on the fly!
Matthew was funny and had great ghost stories to tell mixed in with some history. Very fun tour!

I had to check if the place I'm reviewing is the same place I had been to and I'm sure it is. The experience I had at the weekend buffet at Indias Kitchen was nowhere close to the reviews here. The food was Bland and stale, devoid of any taste or flavors!

But the food itself was mostly gone at 1:30. Considering they stay open until 3 pm, that was strange. They refilled it after some asking but then I wished I hadn't asked! 
I'm guessing the dinner maybe better, at least going by the reviews. But I would avoid the lunch buffet if this is how it normally is.
Good hotel. Very nice staff.  Too far from downtown.  Nasty breakfast!  Generic sausage patties that make McDonalds look like a 5-star restaurant.
Not good for delivery. Food was cold and soggy. I ordered the salmon bento and stir fry soft shell crab. Horrible. Threw most of it away. Now looking for something else for dinner.

My 8-year-old and I visited Street on a recent evening, having heard a ton of buzz about the high quality of the food.  We were not disappointed.  The presentation and choices were excellent.  My daughter chose carnitas tacos; quoting her, "this meat is so delicious and it's just falling apart in my mouth!"  I opted for one each of the pollo asado and carne asada.  The tortillas were super fresh, the portions generous, and the fixings more than adequate.  Bonus points for the salsa bar with a nice variety of options, from mild to nice and spicy.  Free chips?  BOOM.  The icing on the cake was the beer selection - being an obligate gluten-free diner (thanks a lot, celiac disease...), I usually have to skip beer in restaurants.  NOT AT STREET.  Omission Pilsener in the fridge.  There you have it.  Highly recommended.  Good for families.

In follow up of my previous review of 5/14;  I still tell people about food poisoning from Norovirus.  Of course no one in my family has ever gone back.  And we never will.  What we will do, though, is continue to tell anyone we can.

I came in on a Saturday morning for my little one who had been sick on and off all week. There was no wait and I was the only one in the lobby. 
A tech greeted us and was very sweet and patient with my little girl. He gave her a sticker and got down on her level. He weighed her and praised her for her good behavior. He was a young man and spoke Spanish and English which is great for us as I only speak to her in Spanish at home. 
Next came the nurse practitioner who was very professional and also had a sweet and patient demeanor. She checked baby's ears and temperature and told me they'd need to do a strep test and one of her ears was developing an ear infection. Strep test was positive so we have antibiotics now. 
The prescription was called in immediately and was ready for pick up on it way home. The total time for the whole visit was about 30 minutes. Can't beat that!
All in all, if you have to go to an urgent care clinic which is usually a nightmare; this was a fast, super clean and very caring environment. I highly recommend it!

Kudos to Buddy Brew and their roaster as well as their customer service - 5-star on both accounts.

I was so enamored by their collaboration beer with Cigar City Brewing, Cubano-Style Espresso Brown Ale, that when I went to find a way to purchase it online, I didn't even realize that I accidentally bought the sister coffee roast, Cubano-Espresso beans.

As a home roaster myself, I have a deep appreciation for properly roasted coffee, and these guys nailed it! The taste is slightly nutty forward, and has hints of cinnamon and nutmeg on the backend. Don't let the name fool you - this is nothing like the "espresso" roasts you are used to that are mostly charcoal-laden. This coffee is a nice city+ roast, which preserves the nuanced flavors by not over-roasting/burning the coffee.

Try them out, seriously; it will likely be some of the best coffee you've tasted. You can buy the beans in-store or online. They roast them the just before shipping, so you'll never receive stale coffee.

Between their service and quality, they have positioned themselves as my go-to coffee when I fall behind on my own roasting.

This cafe looks very nice from the outside and the interior is nice too.

I was pleasantly surprised by how good the bagel breakfast sandwich was. Very filling and felt healthy. 

Latte was also quite good, but the tea selection is lousy.
This was the first place I went for restaurant week and oh my god the food was delicious the space within the restaurant was small but cute
Better than your average Subway. I am extremely impressed with the service here. They are very efficient and friendly.
Super cute new breakfast spot!  Interesting menu and great vibe inside.  I look forward to trying more of the menu.

I walked into Coffeebar Reno to celebrate their One Year Anniversary (1/19/2015) today and was happily greeted with $1 drinks! I appreciate the locality that this coffee shop provides: the employees were excited to celebrate the anniversary and the ambiance of the coffee shop was great! 

One thing that I absolutely LOVED about this coffee shop was that it was spacious enough to get a lot done, visit for a long time, and I didn't leave the place smelling like stale coffee. I assume everyone has experienced that terrible smell on their clothes after leaving a coffee place after working or chatting for many hours. 

The outdoor and indoor seating options were excellent and the overall experience at Coffeebar Reno was pretty great. I ordered the Dirty Chai latte -- which usually, I love! However, this one left me kind of confused. I think they use more chai than I'm used to. Regardless, Coffeebar Reno knows quality coffee, friendly service, and they certainly know how to froth their milk the right way. 

I will definitely be supporting this local business again soon.
Mighty good chocolate, mint chocolate, and red velvet cupcakes and chocolate peanut butter pie. That's all we had on first trip, but plan to return to try many more treats.
My fiancé and I have been bringing our dogs here for the last 6 years. I highly recommend them and have always felt comfortable with the staff and their advice.

Had a great experience at this salon! Got a pedicure & gel manicure, and enjoyed a glass of wine during. The girl did an excellent job, and really took her time, and I was very impressed with how long both my mani & pedi lasted (looking good still). A little pricey, but it's definitely a more high end salon so it should be expected. I got endless compliments on my nails by all sorts of people. I'm definitely going back!!!

The owners have been known to blatantly over serve, then kick patrons outside to fend for themselves, serve minors, allow rampant drug use, and basically give zero f#cks. (I understand its a nightclub, but at least work to pretend you're not shady like the rest try)

Can't wait until AGLC shuts this place down - maybe Oil City will come back.

from the outside and their website, Makiman Sushi looks like a take-out place.

dimly lit, snappy decor. they were playing singles you would hear on xpn.

rolls are tasty and creative. the night we went, they had about 10 specials.

if you are accustomed to a traditional place where the chef serves your sashimi with the right drop of soy sauce, Makiman's fish may taste bland at first. 
  
the test: mackerel, eel, tako, uni, salmon roe - all fresh and excellent the night we went.

if our first night is a usual night at Makiman, we'll come here every other sushi night.

The food here is ok, but I've literally never recieved good service in my four visits. Taco Tuesday is pretty good, eat about four tacos and you'll get your money worth. 

The burritos are ok, they tend to be a bit light on the meat and heavy on the beans. The food is basically mediocre, and the service terrible. I'm pretty sure the location is what is keeping this place in the green.

Cafe Olivia is tucked in the back corner of the City Market. They have lots of sandwich options made with fresh, creative ingredients. 
When I was there, the staff was friendly and patient while I  figures out what to try. 

I had the spicy Cajun turkey with mozarella, LTO and aioli on ciabatta bread. The sandwich was excellent and the ingredients were very fresh. The food is fairly priced and very filling. 

I'll definitely be back.

This is delicious authentic Thai food with a wonderful range of vegan options. The thom yum soup tastes like my mom's. Incredible and bursting with fresh lemon grass flavor. The tofu larb was divine with little bits of mint in a bright lime marinade. Will definitely come back.

I am so happy with my tattoo. I got a touch up to an existing tattoo and added to it. My artist was amazing! She made me as comfortable as could be for a rib tattoo. My existing tattoo looks better than ever and the addition is exactly as I envisioned.

I ate the spicy soup and the seafood was undercooked and watery. The broth was flavorless and disgusting. I asked for another soup and they refused and only gave me half my money back. I am leaving unsatisfied and hungry...super bad experience...beware

Visited Tucson for the first time 4th of July weekend 2016 and went to Red Door at the Westin.  The signature facial was wonderful and included the BEST facial massage I have ever received and I have had hundreds of facials.  HATS off to Raquel for a fabulous job.  I would absolutely go and visit her again when next in Tucson.

This place is awesome. We've been here half a dozen times and gotten different sandwiches each time and they've all been amazing. The Korean wings are a must have. So good! I love the Thanksgiving and Bulgogi sandwiches. The grocery part is really great - lots of staples but even more organic items. Things that aren't easy to get in No Libs. This has become our favorite spot in te hood for sandwiches.

This place is delicious!!  I had a traditional margarita while my mom had the carriage house margarita.  Both were delicious!We started out with the barbacoa empanadas and the cauliflower shishito, which were both delicious!  My mom had the Pork Pastor and I had the Octopus.  All of the food is delicious, creative, and the presentation is beautiful.  

Our server was on it.  He really knew the dishes and gave accurate descriptions and recommendations based on what we mentioned liking.  

I also loved the ambiance here.  The Cunningham Restaurant group does a fantastic job with this.  My only semi-complaint is that the dishes are quite small for the price you pay.  With that said, it still wouldn't stop me from coming back.

A place that is not to be missed! Special venue to experience really good jazz music in NOLO!!  Loved the ambiance, very relaxing and there is a great selection of cheeses and wine.  I will definitely be coming back the next time I am in New Orleans!
Dope stir fry dishes.  You can make your own.  Quick.  Fresh.  Wholesome.  Easy.  Delicious!

I'm very torn about how to rate this place. I think we had a one off experience and it might have had something to do with it being during Devour Downtown. But, we met some friends here. Initially we sat upstairs outside in the lounge seating.  Our server was Justin and he was incredible. We ordered some appetizers of the empanadas and Brussels sprouts. Both very tasty. Our drinks were wonderful as well. We decided to grab a table and have dinner and Justin was able to remain our server which we were happy about. This was at about 6:30. We ordered our food around 7'ish. Two of us ordered from the Devour menu and two did not. I saw our server ring our food in. We didn't get our appetizers (included as part of Devour) until almost 8pm. We noticed not a lot of food was coming out- so assumed maybe there was an issue in the kitchen. Then as we were waiting for our entrees we noticed many tables who were sat after us getting their food. We were getting a little frustrated and quite frankly pretty hungry at this point. Our food finally arrived around 8:45!!!!! By the time we got it, it was too dark to even see my food. It tasted pretty good, but the look of the food is a big part of what appeals to my appetite. Dessert came with the Devour menu and we ordered the churros. So, all in all we left pretty disappointed, but I will try it again. They were good and took our entrees off our bill. Am I wrong for rating this as 3 stars? I think I have to because I feel like I missed out on really experiencing the food.

The food was decent, not like I expected from all the photos.  The actual restraunt itself is nice and clean but it was very warm in there making it uncomfortable to enjoy the food.  The eggs Benedict was pretty good but my boyfriend's biscuit and gravy was not so much.

I work in the area and have been to this location at least 6 times in the past 3 months. The good: food is delicious, full of great flavor and always fresh tasting. The pita bread is so fluffy and perfect. The bad: the workers here are the most unprofessional and unpleasant individuals I have ever encountered in the food industry. I've visited prior to the lunch rush, during lunch rush and even after.. All the same, miserable and almost like you are inconveniencing them just by walking in the door. So I started ordering online instead to skip the interaction only to find out the two times I have when I go to pick up (well after my designated pickup time) they haven't even started my order. No apologies, nothing just a "we are starting the order now" and this last time "you are going to have to wait I just noticed you're order"!! The woman that works there, mostly from 11-4 Monday through Friday is whom I encounter most and should be switched to food prep in the back or fired. My coworkers have all expressed the same complaints. I am certain this location will not stay open for long and I plan to take my business to Choolah around the corner instead! They are welcoming as soon as you enter the door and food is just as delicious!!! Their naan bread, way better!

I went from not being blown away to really respecting the food at Aldine. You can tell that there is a lot of thought put into every dish. This is not the place to go if you are looking for a glutinous cheat meal. All of the dishes are prepared in a clean and healthy manner. They truly respect the quality of their ingredients and they do very little to enhance them as far as salt, fat etc. You will leave here satisfied and not feeling poorly about what you just ate. I thought the carrots could have been a tad more tender and the zucchini soup a little more exciting. Other than that we were very pleased. Probably one of the cleanest meals I have had out aside from the top vegan restaurants in Philly.

Wait during dinner time:  at least 45 min or so
Food:  delicious

We were surprisingly happy to have found this gem in Reno.  This place serves good Taiwanese  food.  Our favorite were the beef noodle soup, garlic/basil chicken, and the popcorn chicken.  We will not order the oyster pancake again.  The fried tofu bok choy was average.   If I am in Reno again, I would definitely come back.
Digg this place! Funky vibe, clean, trendy, with a friendly and knowledgeable staff. Dominique rocks, and as far as I am concerned, the stylist to see!
This place is insanely good. It's very small but that didn't stop it from being amazing. The waitress was great and the cook knows what he's doing. The tesla burger is very good. It's a much try.

If you can not tolerate smoke, stay away from this casino. Cigar smoking is a big draw here too; not just cigarettes. You have to wade thru the smoke to get to a small smoke free room of machines. No smoke free table games for us. No smoke free eating area. No smoke free bar area either. Your health is a none issue, apparently. 

If you want to gamble in a casino that is 100% smoke free, come to MD my home state. As a state, MD wants you to spend your discretionary income in MD w/o jeopardizing your health or MD workers health. Gaming is not important enough to visit this casino more than once for me. 

Just keeping it real, folks. I stopped smoking 25 years ago, for the record.

I've been here three times, all to get pants hemmed.  It costs about $8 to get pants hemmed, and it takes about a week.

John L. H. mentioned in his review that the dressing room has a curtain that doesn't close all the way.  On my most recent visit, the small dressing room had an actual door that could be locked from the inside.

The staff are quick, polite, and professional, and I'm pleased with their work.  I will return to Alteration Center in the future.
I just used Mike's AC, he did a great job. He didn't charge me for thing I didn't really need, a first for me.  He was respectful of my schedule and explained what he was doing.

Amazing burritos! I stopped in here on a whim and was totally blown away! I had the carnitas burrito, and my dining companion had the Chile Verde burrito. Both were huge, and had great flavors.  The staff was friendly, and convinced us to try the tres leche cake, which was wonderful! I highly recommend this place :)

AWESOME food, good service, friendly staff. 

Prices a slight bit high - but I'll return.

We hit the buffet for Friday night seafood dinner. Line was reasonable and we were seated probably within ten minutes. 

Food I think needs to be kept in context of the price. It's not the Cosmo buffet but that's also about double the price. Given similarly priced casino buffets I think it's quite good. The brisket and ribs are winners for sure (great crust and tender), the hot crab was also quite good. If anything I'd say most food was good quality but underseasoned. On the desert side the gelato was icy, the cookie got rave reviews from friends, and the rest of the pastry was okay but nothing to rave about. 

If you're in downtown Reno this buffet is worth a visit. But if you're not downtown or don't mind a quick trip, the buffet at the Atlantis is better and only about $10 more.

I visited Presence Float Center for the first time yesterday. This was my second time floating and it was a great experience. You can tell that a lot of thought went into designing the space and ensuring a relaxing environment. The space is very clean and well maintained. Every little detail was perfect from the towels to the post-float tea. I highly recommend.

Considering it's located in a museum, I think they do a fairly good job.  All the food seems to be made to order.  You order at the counter and they give you a buzzer.  In the mean time you can look around the gallery.

Had the falafel and friend had the burger.   The falafel was pretty good.  The falafel was nice and crispy but the portion size was tiny and was served on a wrap rather than a pita bread.  Felt it was expensive considering the tiny size.  I was still feeling hungry after my meal.  Friend's burger was decent and the fries were nice and crispy but again small portion size on the fries.  

I did enjoy the lovely outdoor seating area.  Thought the tables could be wiped down a little more often.  Despite the slightly higher price and the small portion size I'm still giving it 4 stars because of the ambiance.  And elevated price is expected.

We went with another couple who suggested it and although the drinks were good, the service prompt, and the food was good, it was severely overpriced. I realize it's Rittenhouse but the food portion to the hanger steak was absolutely absurd. I ordered a hanger steak fully expecting a decent size steak but instead received a quarter of the size of a normal steak. It was almost insulting. My friend who had been here before and had ordered the steak previously, was shocked and disappointed how small they had made the portion. I don't mind more "European portions" but this was ridiculous. My friend had to end up eating half of his girlfriend's meal because he was still so hungry and he's not a huge portion eater by any means either. It was a Saturday night and the place was absolutely dead, which seemed a bit odd especially on a lovely summer night. Seems this place is hurting financially and has decided to try and cut back on the food costs to the customer's detriment. I have literally had more steak on a steak salad. Good food but just not worth the price.

This place is awesome. The fact that its in a truck may scare some away and that is their loss. This is possibly the best thai I have had. If you like spicy ask for Thai hot and let them take care of your taste buds. If you cant take hot food stay away from thai hot...it requires your big boy pants lol

A word to the wise ... proceed to Bruce's with CAUTION!

Took my old Ford Escort Wagon in for a radiator flush.  The work was done suitably however I was not told that there might be some air pockets which would trigger a warning of insufficient water in the radiator and cause me to need to fill the radiator a few days later.  Careless in not providing info.

Much worse, was returning a month later to have the spark plugs and wires replaced.   Bruce Jr. was friendly and helpful and even provided a ride home - 3 miles away.  I got a call just about an hour later that the job was complete. 
The bill came to just over $200.  It seemed high for the job involved, however I was in a hurry to get to an interview and did not dwell on the steep price.

I later reviewed the bill and discovered that I had been charged tax for the labor (illegal).  And double charged tax for the parts.  Also, the wires used were exhorbitantly expensive -especially considering that this is a 19 y.o. car.

Further research informed me that the standard charge for replacing the plugs and wires on this car - in Goleta - is $70-$100 total (including parts).

I sent them a letter giving them an opportunity to make things right, and at least refund the excess money charged for the tax.  No response.

Do I think Bruce Sr. and Jr. are competent mechanics?  Yes, they probably are.  Do I think they can be careless and cavalier with regard to parts, labor and billing - unfortunately the answer is  also YES.

Ya know, I love Don Pablos. I don't live in the area anymore & there isn't a Don Pablos remotely close to the area I live now, so I don't frequent often. Maybe once a year, instead, when I once lived near the Deptford location, I visited twice every other week at least. My sister & I joke, now, about the sodium bloat we get the following day from eating here, no matter how much water we drink w/our meal. Ha. Lotsa salt in their food, so beware. But daaaymn, it is yummmmmmmy!

There were 6 of us, so when we arrived at 645pm, we had a 15 minute wait while they cleaned up a party that just finished. No biggie. This place is always hoppin' it seems. Kid friendly, loud, very loud. Loud because of the high ceilings, warehouse style. You'd think after 15 years, they would attach some sound protection drop ceilings, but they never have. The place is starting to look a bit worn down, but still clean & cute decor.

Some things never change....and that is a good thing. The Queso Blanco is like crack. Dipping your tortilla chips in that cheese sauce is HIGHLY ADDICTIVE! They added a spicy one, w/chilies, so we ordered both. Good thing we did. I ordered the pick 2 combo, a beef enchilada & a cheese & onion enchilada, extra corn cake. That corn cake is also like crack too. I eat everyones. Omg. I think they use cream corn, that has got to be  the secret, but geez it is yummmmm!! I am a sucker for the Sangria - Margarita swirl. Sometimes the bartender does a crappy job of swirling it, & the ratio of sangria to margarita is waaaaaay off balance. That happened while we were there at this visit, but our server, Steven was very accommodating & fixed it. He was (is) a serious rockstar. Our service was on fleek. We keep raving at the service we received at our last visit because it was so good. Steven *I am pretty sure that is his name* was one of the best servers we ever had. He thought ahead, brought us refills w/out us having to ask; he was super efficent & didn't annoy us, coming over to our table & moving us along w/out feeling forced or pushy & was patient while we waited for my nephew & other sister arrive. Amazing server. Best server we had at Don Pablos. 5 stars for Steve. 

It was about to be my nephew's 8th birthday, so we surprised him w/a song & dessert. He was adamant that we not sing & embarass him, butttt, that is what Auntie's do, embarass & laugh. Boy, he was so surprised, embarassed & found it all really funny. Thank you for making that work Steve. 

Consistent food & service are why we return. I will definitely visit again when I am in the area.

Not bad for a local BBQ chain. Had the pork sandwich. Not a Carolina style with peppers and vinegar but mixed with your choice of hot or mild BBQ sauce. Not my favorite way to serve pork sandwiches but still pretty good. Loved the roll. Would try this place again.

Irony is a funny thing. My massage therapist said to me that she had been with the spa since they opened 15 years ago. A few days prior I had listened to a podcast on NPR about doctors debating the fairness of the pending new law in California requiring MDs to go through re-training every five years to keep them sharp. I really hope that includes all aspects of healthcare practitioners if said law makes it through. 

Having dated a masseuse at the Hilton spa in La Jolla, I consider myself a pretty good judge of what five star treatment should look like. There was a long list of things that made my experience less than acceptable. The most annoying part of the whole thing was that I specifically made it a point to describe exactly what I wanted to the receptionist on the phone before going in. I even said, "Are you sure? I only have time for one massage on my 3,000 mile, cross country road trip, so it is extra important that it is nothing short of epic." 

Not only was it not epic, I almost got up towards the end and walked out. All I wanted was a deep tissue back massage. Not full body, not swedish styles, not thai influence, dont want my hands rubbed. Just take your knuckles and pound on my trapezius. I even told the therapist, "I'm a surfer, so I only want my back worked on." For wich her reply was, "Oh, are you a runner?" ... um what.

So what did I get? 15 minutes of work on my back, where I immediately asked her to use more pressure, because in her words exactly, "I work on athletes and have a one to 10 scale of pressure so let me know if I should increase or decrease my force." 

"What pressure are you at now?" I asked.

"Four." I heard.

"Can you please just go a LOT harder, please?"

"Oh well im still warming you up because the warmer your muscles, the deeper I can go."

So I waited. And waited. Had she spent the whole time on my back, slowly increasing pressure and making me "hurt" like she had bragged about, there would be no issue.  Instead, I got 45 minutes of getting my knuckles cracked, wrists pulled out of socket, (wich has left me with arthritic type pain in my fingers for the last few days) calf squeezing,  elbows repeatedly pushing hardly on my spine, extra long fingernails digging deep, and most annoyingly,  my pecs focused on for far too long... like literally 10 minutes. That was the point where I almost walked out. I come in with a very specific need and get completely ignored and treated like I know nothing of the practice and should just lay down and let the expert work. 

Maybe I'm just too used to California where practice is competitive,  and customer service is everything. And if you suck at life, you starve. The downfall of people having seniority and comfort in a job that has a steady flow of tourism is that the customer is sacrificed.  People this sloppy and lazy would never last in my town. Now I know. 

I left feeling more stressed than when I went in, felt no reliefe in the tension in my back, and $200 poorer. Almost home to San Diego,  I will be visiting my regular massuse today or tomorrow, after a long four day road trip. 

Voodoo

Never again will I be staying here. The room was dirty, it took an hour and 15 mins to get my car from the valet, they double charged me for our room. The only saving grace to this entire terrible experience was a very helpful gentleman named Ryan at the front desk that ironed out all he could with the double charge. For $259 a night I will stay at a motel 6 before I stay here again.

I visited here after all the other salons in my area close early on Friday. I also waited to write the review after a few days just to make sure my nails didn't chip. 
I got a pedicure done by Leo, there wasn't much of a wait and he got right to work. Very relaxing. I do not put Acrylic on my nails so I can't speak for that. The place was clean, quiet atmosphere. Not very big though.  I was greeted by staff, very friendly, didn't talk amongst themselves when they did my nails. 
I did take some pictures hopeful that helps someone else. I give it 4 stars because my toes look great and the place was clean (from what I saw).
Some notes:
-Might want to bring your own polish, crappy selection and old
-The pedicure wasn't exactly speedy but I was in no rush
-It is on the small side...
-I did not visit the bathroom or backroom so I can't speak for that. 

Despite the lack of stars they're still getting a good stream of business.  ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

My boyfriend and I went to dinner there on a Thursday night. I had looked at the Yelp reviews prior to coming, but maintained optimistic despite the mixed reviews. First and foremost - the service was fantastic. Our waiter was quick at getting our drinks and was very friendly. The owner had made her way around to our table a few times asking how we were which I liked. However, the food was not close to what I expected and we left extremely disappointed. We got the fried crab balls as an appetizer and they were OK at best. We got the Jumbo Lump Crab to share... and when we got it - it could have easily been an appetizer. There was nothing "jumbo" about the meat and the portion was extremely small for a $25 entree meal. Overall, the service was great but the food was lacking.

Really wanted to like this based on the glowing reviews. But it took WAY too long and the food just wasn't up to New Orleans' standards.Shrimp and grits - Literally 3 little shrimp, no andouille. Compared with the picture of shrimp and grits from another review only 6 days before I'm not sure what happened here. Pork chop tough and flavorless. (Those glowing reviews were from Illinois, New York and California, nice places, but..... not New Orleans.) Sorry folks, can't recommend.

We've been here many times and have never been disappointed other than the fact that word has gotten out about it and it can be crowded at times. It quirky and cute, service is always decent, and has a good menu. Everything we've tried has been good but our favorites are the pickle soup, mixed salad sandwich, royal grille and dark and sinister dessert.

Was visiting from out of town and stopped in for coconut flavored milk tea with boba and lychee jelly -- it was delicious!  The facility was very clean and the staff member was quite and friendly and efficient.  If I lived in Tucson, and I would definitely be back.

Wait staff good. Always find a seat quickly but the last 2 times we were there it took nearly an hour for pancakes and an omelet.  That's  just ridiculous.  Maybe give it one more try and hopefully those were flukes.
Fast, great service, delicious! One of our favorite spots! The ingredients are fresh, and pizzas come out hot. A good bang for your buck too!

I came here for breakfast with my man and it was pretty good. It is a little weird because it is attached to maggianos. However, the building is so nice. We ordered to bacon, egg and cheese paninis, chocolate chip cookies and orange juice. A little bit on the pricy side, it was $17 for everything. However, it was very good.
Ann Marie in the bar area is wonderful. My son loves the cheese fries and mac and cheese. We enjoy steak and salads. The food is always consistently good.

This is my first review on yelp but I feel I should share my experience. I just moved to New Orleans and needed a new place for waxing and nails. It's always odd to find new places, Buff Beauty had so many great reviews I decided to give it a try. The place is really clean and the people are very friendly. I had a waxing and an eyelash tint by Courtney and she did a great job. I called the following day with a question about the eyelash tint and the owner personally called me from out of town with answers. We had a long chat. She was helpful, professional and even gave me tips on places to try in New Orleans. Hands down the best customer service ever! Moving to a new city can be overwhelming to find the right places, I'm glad I gave Buff Beauty a try.

This place is perfect if you are wanting to stay on Bourbon and the staff is very nice the man that came to get our bags (Coop) was great! They are in the middle of renovations which is needed our rooms was starting to show its age but was very clean and I had no problem with it. This place was just not my kind of hotel I prefer the smaller hotels away from Bourboun...had to stay here for work. This hotel is great if you want to party on Bourboun all night nad have your bed not that far away. I also found that even though there was a ton of noise outside the rooms were actually pretty quite.

If you are aimlessly staring at the menu, get the Ziggy Burger! I mean, how cool is that name? The sweet potato fries were yummy too. 

Space is limited but everyone is friendly and the overall atmosphere is nice.

My only complaint (if you can call it that) is that this is one of those places that carnivores tend to like more than actual vegetarians/vegans because they serve what I like to call "sex with your pants on" food. As in, lots of carbs and empty calories to make it agreeable to those who feel that healthy food is tasteless. If you are looking for clean and unprocessed ingredients and are turned off by a little grease...this may not be the spot for you. But if your only requirement is "meatless", or you want to try something new and different, this is definitely worth a try.

BUT...I think even the most health conscious palettes can appreciate the power of the Groothie. 

Love, peace, and veggies.

This place is just delightful.  I came here with my parents last Saturday for a light dinner and drinks.  Our main waitress was very attentive and polite.  We also had a few other staff members come by to check on us throughout the night -- which almost bordered on being annoying, but was ultimately quite useful when I needed to order another drink!  The place filled up quick but service never wavered.  Live music (a guitar player) was about to start at 9pm right as we left.

We ate:
--Fondue.  Warm and filling, wonderful mellow flavor that paired well with white wine.
--Crab Cakes.  Wasn't as impressed here.  They were a little thin for my taste, though you do get 3 of them.  The orange salsa and peppers helped.
--Fried Shrimp.  I'm allergic but I cheated and had one bite.  It was delicious!
--White Pizza.  This thing was fabulous.  It was loaded with cheese, chicken and tomatoes.  Definitely not a wimpy pizza.

I drank a pear martini that was absolutely to die for.  Perfect mix of sugar, citrus and alcohol.  I also had a melon spritzer that was very refreshing.  It would be perfect to order at the end of a hot summer day or night.  Oddly enough, I can't find either of these drinks listed on their website menu.  They must have updated the menu but not the site.  So be sure to look through the whole liquor book when you go!  The martini's and non-wine drinks were near the back, if I recall correctly.

Bottom line: Definitely coming back here, hopefully soon!

Thanks to Groupon I tried out this service for the first time Friday.  I love the fact you can sign up online at any time and in this case I got a last minute appointment.  Tracy was a little late but I was overall pleased with how well and fast she cleaned.  Attention to detail is very important to me so it's hard to find someone that can do a good job dusting behind the tv and in the corner of the room.  Tracy did a good job w/o much guidance.  I plan on using the service again for the convenience with booking and I think with a little feedback, Tracy will be a good fit.

The food is pretty good, and I like that they have the soup, rice, and bread with meal; but it would be nice to have more sauces to choose from. Not the best I've been to, but not disappointing either!

Nice rooms and modern decor but not really a full service hotel. The bathroom is small in our room. About 6 X 4 and with the door opening into the bathroom, it feels really small. For $300 / night I expected more space and a full service hotel.
Not very talkative but their complimentary massage is wonderful and the price for nails is the best around this city.

Blake Shelton sure knows how to grill a good burger. My friend and I went here after a full evening of drinking and enjoyed some awesome music and delicious melt-in-your-mouth cheeseburgers. The house-made tater tots are just about the best thing you can put in your mouth then you add in a little beer cheese to dip them in and it's a life changing experience. Totally recommend this bar for food and music entertainment. 

Only con is that it is more contemporary than a true honky tonk should be in my opinion. Perhaps Blake is letting Gwen have too much say.

Also I found it ironic that the band was singing Miranda Lambert covers.

I got the Stuffed Pepper, Shrimp Pasta & green beans. There was NO stuffing in the pepper. Only heavily seasoned ground beef. No shrimp in the pasta, just 3 on top. Green beans were too salty. I'll just stick to the Turkey necks. Been here several times and have only had 1 good plate.

We had Smooth Move come out and move our belongings from our old house to our new house. They were happy to stop by our storage unit on the way. They were very efficient, very fast, and very careful with all of our stuff. Highly recommend for anyone looking to move, they were awesome!

Ok for a 45 minute wait at the drive through at least the food was correct and hot. There was no apology for the wait time and the girl at the window was unfriendly.  It took 25 minutes to get to the box to order with only 4 cars in front of me. Corporate needs to visit this location because service this poor is a problem within management. I know the food is made to order but the max wait time for each car is 8 minutes, but needs to be done by at least 3 minutes.  I've worked at a Steak 'n Shake. This is unacceptable. What if someone has a health issue like diabetes? They could be in a coma by the time they get to them. Ridiculous.

Update: I went inside this time where there were maybe 3 tables sat and 3 people waiting on orders at the counter. It took 25 minutes to get 2 milkshakes and out of all the employees there, no one had any hustle or sense of urgency to get food out in a timely manner, and I never saw a manager. This location needs A LOT of help. I won't even mention the people ahead of me or their wait times. Also I'm surprised the cooks pants were still on since they were past his ass.

My amazing race try out partner and I had one of our regular lunches here on a sunny Saturday. This is a rather exciting place to have to lunch. Lots of nice comfortable couches with pop-art/earthy combo (yes I know it sounds strange - you have to see it to believe it). Ultimately, it makes it a really relaxing place to sit down and have a cat with friends.
