OR, if you are on a studio binge, you can go to the benches and get your study down with the Vandy and Belmont kids. 

Food wise its creative sandwichs (not just your typical bland stuff) with unique names. They are really well made with a unique flavor in it of itself and served in a very interesting dish. They are a bit pricey from what you expect of a sandwich place (a $12.50 for sandwich and chips).

The only thing that keeps me from giving it 5 stars is that parking can be a nightmare. You park up in this gravel lot that you pay 2 dollars for 2 hours. The parking vending machine is also rather annoying. You have been warned.

Oh and also...strangely, the bathroom is build into this old bank vault style entrance. I felt like I was in the movie Ocean's 11 (the original Frank Sinatra one) going to the bathroom...

I really wanted to like this place since there are no
Thai restaurants to speak of on the east side. The food wasn't bad, it was just okay. The spring rolls were average but the Pad Thai was disappointing.  The flavoring was on the bland side and very watery. If I were already at the mall I would give them another try but definitely not something I would go out of my way for.
Came here after a concert late night, waiter was very attentive and received the same service as if it was middle of the day. Love this spot

Raley's worked at it repeatedly and succeeded in driving me away. Nicely, a somewhat new Whole Foods to spend my money at instead. Anyway, I bought an item that turned out to be misrepresented so I brought it back. And amazingly, I got a full refund. And unlike other stores, they just gave me my money back without grilling me to force me to justify why I wasn't satisfied. So I wasn't happy that I was misled and had to return the next day, but I did get a full refund, no muss, no fuss, wow! Yeah, I know, Raley's could care less about my patronage but I still don't like turning over my money to a store that has contempt for me.

I found Bobbin Ventures through Yelp. Jayna, the business owner and a fellow UCSB Alumni, is a pleasure to work with and has a gift for tailoring. She shows great attention to detail and tailored my suit exactly to my liking. I will be using her services in the future.

Thanks again Jayna!

We stumbled upon Khyber Pass around 11:30pm on a Thursday night. We were starving after an evening of travel, and many area kitchens were closed. We were greeted by two friendly bartenders, a fantastic beer selection, and some comfy seats at the bar. YESssssssssssssssss (you know that feeling?)

I went for the vegan pulled pork sandwich, based on the bartender's recommendation, as well as some smoked cheddar cheese fries. It was JUST what I needed. The sauce on the sandwich was excellent in combination with slaw. The fries were delish. My boyfriend enjoyed his wings, too. Next time we're in Philly, we'll probably try get back.

Best bagels in the area by far.  No issues there, but the place is the worst run store I've ever been in.  Besides the lady behind the counter serving food while visibly sick ( coughing, sneezing, sniffling ) they have no concept of how to help more than one person at a time.  If they are cooking something forget it, you can't even talk to the people behind the counter.  Multitasking is not in their vocabulary so plan on a very frustrating wait if there is a line.

This is probably my favorite event in all of St. Louis. I wait in breathless anticipation for it all year. It's a dazzling showcase of all the best talent in the country. It's a juried competition, so the artists you see have been up against tons of other talented folks, all vying for a spot in the Fair.

According to the Web site, the Art Fair is consistently ranked one of the nation's top fine art fairs. Each year the Saint Louis Art Fair attracts over 150,000 art enthusiasts who purchase more than $2 million worth of art at the festival. 

That's pretty impressive! I'm always amazed by the creativity and originality displayed here. My favorites have been wax sculptures of people that look as if they're real. In fact, most people stand there forever trying to decide if they're fake or not. I also love the photography - some of the most beautiful I've ever seen, even crazy ones like nudes with fruit themes. 

There's a lovely food court area, showcasing many of the city's finer eating establishments, live music and lots of activities for the kids. It's a fantastic event, always held in early September. Not to be missed!

We came here by chance when a nearby restaurant was crowded. I would come
back again, although there were a few ways they fell short. Liked the comfortable atmosphere and fun menu. While the menu is heavy on meat, there are several nice salads, a fish special and vegetarian option. First, loved my glass of wine. The beet salad looked beautiful, but two of us agreed that it was too salty. Everyone enjoyed their main courses, but my friend's fish was undercooked and much smaller than the other fishes (mine was perfect). By the time she got a new piece, everyone else was done dinner and they did not offer to take it off or even a comp dessert. Speaking of dessert, the ice cream was amazing.

2 stars for good food that is cheap- but dirty and poor service.  AFTER eating nearly all of it, I asked for a to-go soup container and they gave me a used one that was dirty with a hair in it!!!  When I asked for a new one and showed them no sorry, nothing, just replaced it!  What the!  And then I noticed flies around our table.  Health inspectors might wanna check it out

We were woke up at 8:53 on a Saturday. Check out is not until 11. I went down and said something. I put a note in the door...do not disturb until 11 a.m...9:13...bang bang bang...I went down again. I was called a liar. 9:45...at this point, I'm down in my truck...I watch the maid go back and knock on the room again (my husband is still in the room)...I see them ..I grab my camera... she ran back into the room next door when she saw it.. Do not stay here unless you don't mind getting the bum's rush,or like being treated like cow dung and called names.

Quaint romantic spot with awesome food and a decent wine selection.  Expect French Mediterranean tapas and entrees that are quite different from almost any other restaurant in the Bay area.  The creme brulee is also very good.  Highly recommended if you enjoy great food.  But don't expect a happening scene, awesome decor or a great bar because you won't find any of that here.

Stumbled on this little tea room while out for a Sunday morning bike ride.  We were not able to get in for tea as you needed a reservation for Sunday, but we did order coffee and some chocolates and enjoyed them on the outdoor seating.  I look forward to going back to enjoy the rest of what they have to offer.

Went in for brunch with a friend, and loved it!  They have a rather impressive menu for a coffee shop.  Their offer generous, but not outrageous portions, and the food is freshly prepared.  The pesto potatoes are fabulous!  One of the highlights of my breakfast was the lemon curd that accompanied the scone that came with my meal-a fantastic little treat!  I'm not a huge coffee drinker, so I ordered a cafe au lait, which was good, but nothing special.  I am willing to shell out $ for good, freshly prepared food.  My meal came to about $12, which I think is a fair price.

As a native New Yorker, this is my favorite pizza place in the Philly suburbs.  Also, Paola and Mike are great people that show a genuine appreciation of your business.  If you're in the mood for good non-pizza Italian food, Paola makes a great dish of pasta.   Their non-pizza dishes are probably better than most sit down restaurants, and cheaper!   Highly recommend.

I tried Pomme Cafe last weekend as it's on my favorite street of restaurants in Clayton. To start, we had a great bottle of pinot noir recommended by the waiter and Caesar salad. The Caesar was excellent. Next, we had the burger which was probably the best I've had in St. Louis thus far and the cavatappi pasta. The cavatappi pasta was lighter than I pictured and the sauce seemed nonexistent. For a sausage pasta, it really didn't taste like much. If I go back, I would order the Caesar and burger again and try out the gnocchi. Overall, service was good and atmosphere is cute for a date on the quieter side.

Ordered chicken pad Thai and panang chicken curry. Chicken was very tender in both meals. The pad Thai was the better of the two but be aware the rice noodles are very long. The curry was good but the sauce was very thin and the only veggies were green and red peppers. It was missing something but I just cannot put my tongue on exactly what it was.

Was in the mood for a burger to smash with my sisters. We were in the area already so decided to give this place some play. We had no idea of what to do. Stand in line or plant at a table. Walked to the counter greeted by very busy cashiers and servers. Decisions, decisions decisions! Isn't this the beauty of America? In summary, I chose a baja spicy chicken burger. It was average. My sister got something more up my alley. The mushroom melt chicken burger with sweet potato fries. My french fries were not dazzling. They were not better than a fast food spot. I won't blame my bad decisions on my review. I plan on going back to sit ouside again and obviously copy off my sister's order.

I want to start by saying that Kanella still remains at the top of our list for one of our favorite local restaurants.

However, last Sunday we decided to try their meze-family style dining. I must say as much as we liked the foods offered on the preset menu, we enjoy the open menu much better. The portions were quite small and for the price fix of $35 I would much rather have my choice of some of the best dishes in town.
My friend bought an iced coffee and found gross gooey things in it. We will never buy another iced coffee from here again.
Great food and reasonable price. Loved being able to have burger in lettuce wrap. Also had grilled chicken club salad really good too!
yr so nashville if ... you wait in line for an hour to eat pancakes

Cutest little noodle shop in the city. The food is cooked right in front of you. Its fresh and the staff are great! Got the dumplings (which the filling changes depending on the day), the Black Garlic wings (which are AMAZING). 

I havent even tried the noodles here, but I cant wait to be back so i can!!!
We went here after learning about it on White Linen night.  We sat at the bar and really got the royal treatment.  EXCELLENT food.  Great bar and cocktails.  We will be back.

I always meant to stop here, but encouraged and intrigued by Scott W's experiences, I wanted to give it a go. I rented a Prius from WeCar, and asked my mother if she was up for the challenge. She said she used to stop there when she worked in Metairie for breakfast. So, we pull into the lot, and pray we're not hit by any of the 19 Crown Victorias cruising the lot. 

Upon entering, we decided to eat at the deli, because it looked like rain. I had the meatloaf, and Mama had the chicken livers. I should have selected the livers. The meatloaf had lots of veal - which is a plus - they used this quasi-canned milk mushroom gravy that made you wonder if it was going bad/sour. Besides, they make real mashed potatoes with evaporated milk. I'm not crazy about sweet mashed potatoes if they're not yams. 

Onto shopping. I picked up a pint of perhaps the best tasting grape tomatoes I've had in over a year. There's lots to choose from, a booze selection out of this world, and the meat looked great. What was disheartening was the line to see the butchers. It very surreal to see people clutching large slabs of meat, hoping one of those nice boys with great forearms would trim, slice and/or dice their selection into perfection.

I have to say, one thing that I have come to love about New Orleans is how passionate and proud the locals are of the beautiful city. Our tour guide, Dawn, is a perfect example of this. Her enthusiasm and adoration of the city and the Cemetery gave me a newfound love of this unique city. She was so excited to show us the beauty of the cemetery, with relevant snippets of history as backstory. We started off the St. Louis Cemetery No.1 Tour with Dawn at the corner of Royal St. and St. Louis St., where we assembled the group and proceeded to walk towards the cemetery. Our meeting spot was a few blocks from the entrance, so Dawn stopped us a few times in the shade to tell us more about the city and the cemetery. Right outside the cemetery, she very clearly instructed us what not to do and to stay close. Once inside, she gave a summary of the different types of plots that were in the cemetery and then proceeded to guide us through. 

As a first-timer in the city, I'd recommend taking one of these walking tours since you cannot enter without a tour guide. It felt a little creepy to be touring and walking around, but made me appreciate the history behind the cemetery itself. But really, if you end up going, please be respectful!!! You would think that would be common sense...

This was the second time we have eaten at Carrollton Market, once with a group of 5 and now a group of 6  and once again all had an excellent meal with excellent service. I personally find the menu slightly limited (not a fan of pork belly or pig tails) otherwise I would have rated 5 stars. 
If you haven't been, you need to go!!

I would never rent from these people again.  I had a great experience my first year and then the little things catch up with you and they say that "have it on file" that you discussed it.  The rent WILL go up and they do not work with you at all even if you have never had a late fee.  They are not people friendly and kind of have a well that sucks kind of attitude.  I had one of the manager tell me that she has not had a month to month rate under $1990 in the area...which is ridiculous.  Just not a good idea. More of a headache than its worth.
My favorite drinks place to imbibe before a show in Ybor. Kyle is spot on every time with what is seemingly the exact thing I want before I even know it. Also, the nachos. Trust me!

The flavor of our food was good and it came to me and my wife hot.
I got the crabcakes and salmon special. Instead of two crabcakes as pictured I got one crabcake cut in half and the piece of salmon was half th size as pictured (less than 6 oz, 1 inch high in the middle by 1 in wide by 6 in long).
The white linen napkins are so old that they left white lint all over our clothes.
I watched a woman, not in typical waitress clothes (maybe a manager of some sort) go to one table with only a single balled up cloth and proceed to wipe the tablet top, pushing the food bits to the bench seats. Next she wiped the seats, pushing the food bits to the floor. She then moved to the adjacent empty table and did the same procedures again. Talk about contamination. No soap was ever used.
The restaurant had a bad odor when we entered sort of like the carpeting had not been deep cleaned in a long time.
After seeing the woman's table "cleaning" method it all made sense.
I wish I had seen that before we ordered.
I gave it two stars because the food tasted fine even if the portions were abbreviated.
I didn't make a fuss, I'll act with my wallet - they won't ever see me again!
Clearly management needs to be re educated.
Eat there at your own risk.

As far as diners go, you will not find one in the city that does as good a job as The Please-U. I've been coming here for years and I can honestly say that it is my favorite breakfast spot in town. Although some might find its menu items unrefined, I find it quite comforting to have a simple American breakfast without all the bells and whistles. Besides, if you're looking for something along the lines of a duck confit corn muffin with yucca pancakes, try just about every other breakfast place in the city, not here. Along with having an unpretentious menu, affordable prices and extremely prompt service it seems that Pleas-u does "diner" better than any other diner in the area. So don't say that I didn't warn you when they say that they are all out of unpasteurized artisanal cheeses for your free-range eggs benedict w/ baby bok choi.

Great chicken biscuit and really Fast service too.
The only thing bad about this place is the amount of ice they fill into your drink... lol

Good place for a quick bite !! Do try the power ale as a drink instead of the regular coke

Live in the neighborhood for two years and yet I waited so long to try this place -- I am dumb! It is a really nice place with interesting and tasty dishes. 

We were seated in the solarium area which I must say is one of the nicest spots I've eaten in. Just nice to be tucked in A/C but still feel like you are eating outside. The lighting was great and the noise level was perfect too. The music was really good oldies...mamas and papas and that sort of stuff :).

GET THE SZECHUAN DUCK SPRING ROLLS. They are amazing!

My friend and I ordered London Burgers and they were pretty damn good. I got mine with Boursin and Peppers and it was overall fantastic. I don't remember what my friend ordered but he seemed to adore his burger. The fries were alright, a bit too salty for me, but he liked them a lot and finished mine along with his!

The service was pretty bad. I really felt like I had to flag the waiter down the entire time. It would be five stars if not for the waiter.

A good Quick healthy sit down fast foods sit down restaurant for the family.  ! I tried all their Asian food here like : Japanese pan noodles, Indonesian peanut sauté this was good,I also tried their pad Thai too it wasn't  bad at all !
Food is good. Good portion of food. It is a fusion restaurant so do not expect a distinct taste.
Love this gym. The staff is awesome, the members are nice, and it has all the equipment I need. It's a place I can work out and I would feel recommending it to my mom also. Great place.

Yum yum really good breakfast challah French toast so tender and scrambled eggs simple but done right 
Server forgot butter and jam for toast but otherwise ok 
Will return for lumch

Backspace Bar is a solid bar with some good food options.  It is a nice quiet vibe which is really nice opposite those loud Bourbon Street bars.  We wanted a snack and had the BLT which was very good and some drinks- I would say my margarita was little heavy on mixer but we liked the place over all.

I think this place is worse than Basil Leaf. 
This is the greasiest pad-thai, along with Thai Style Cafe on La Palco Blvd. My husband had basil chicken; he doesn't even remember because it was so bad. 
The service? I felt like the step child who asked for food. The only thing great about this place is that we walked to this restaurant from home to have bad Thai. 
This is another place I'd recommend to friends who never had Thai before.
Should have trusted the reviews.  Prices have gotten very high and they left spots and water all over the windows and car.  Never coming back again.

Ate here last night. We sat at the bar. Delicious! Got the baked oysters (half casino and half rockefeller), both were very good.  It was my first time eating turtle soup. I really liked it! I was expecting a clear broth but it was more like a stew or thin chili. Very good. My husband got the rib eye and he said it was AMAZING! Rib eyes tend to be on the fatty side but this had zero fat--a wonderful piece of prime meat. I got the crab cake and it was probably the best I've ever had! Chunks of crab! For dessert we had the ice cream. It was good but nothing special. It had a mix of vanilla ice cream and raspberry gelato with a jam and whipped cream on top.

Stopped in with some friends and has a great meal.  Like most, I was a little surprised by the counter style ordering.  Over all the service was great and the food was fantastic.  I got a couple of Tacos with Al Pastor and a couple Carne Asada.  Both were really good.  Grabbed some chips from the salsa bar and some salsa.  They certainly have a wide variety of salsa options.  The chips and a few of the salsas I had were very tasty as well.
Wilmington was in a dire need of place just like 8th and Union - a mid-priced, delicious pho place. Vibe is cool and they usually have good beers on tap.

Good food and very fast service.  The Shawny pawny and roasted red pepper soup are delicious, however, the soup wasn't piping hot (personal preference) and they lost a couple stars on portion size and value.  For an $8-$10 dollar lunch you can get a much healthier portion of food elsewhere within walking distance downtown.  

if you're in the mood for something light and not on a super tight budget, check it out.

This is a nice little family owned German restaurant that we visited for Oktoberfest this year.  The owners were incredible and accommodated our party of 25.  They were kind and service was great.  However ultimately, I am rating the food.  I ordered the chicken schnitzel  which is what I normally order annually for Oktoberfest.  They did not serve veal, only pork and chicken.  I felt like I was eating a chicken patty you would get from your grocers freezer.  The red cabbage was much like the red cabbage I find in jars at the grocery store and the spatzle could have been boxed mac n' cheese. My boyfriend ordered the hackbraten which tasted like a dried up meatloaf with tons of salt.  Several of our party ordered the bratwurst and knockwurst.  Everyone referred to these as hotdogs.  Not one good word came out of anyone's mouth when it came to the food.  The only positives people gave were from the service and kindness of the family.  When it came time to pay, their credit card machine was broken.  We were sent across the street to the gas station to get cash.  

In the end, I hate giving such a bad review to such kind people but there was nothing good or authentic about the cuisine.  Yes, they give two free beers with all meals which just lends to the hospitality of the owners.  We will not return.

Stopped in for a quick lunch order a chicken veggie wrap.  My wife ordered a salad.  At the risk of being redundant it was "so fresh"!  I thought it was a little pricey until the order came. Going to have to eat chicken wrap for dinner too. Help was attentive, and polite. A good value. I will come back!
Had the fajitas. Loved them!  Super busy Cinco de Mayo evening. Swamped. Had a Groupon for our meal and ended up buying a second one because we enjoyed our meal.  Will go back!

My wife and I were looking to get some take out Mexican and we remembered Pablanos was right around the corner from our new condo, so we stopped by. We couldn't be more pleased at the quality of the good and friendly service. 

Everything was fresh and tasty, zero complaints. Well be back.

So glad we opted for Burger Study instead of Hooters!  DELICIOUS, well planned hamburgers. We had the Prime Degree and Southern Classic. Roasted garlic-black pepper aioli with my zucchini straws could be eaten plain with a spoon. My son's chicken fingers were the best we've ever had. Caramel milkshake for dessert, we stopped back in for two more for the ride home. AJ the waiter was excellent. So friendly and knowledge. We will definitely be back again and again until we try everything on the menu. All ready recommended to friends and family. Good job, Burger Study and Thank you!

Solid beer selection, wild and interesting pizza options, large indoor and outdoor seating. Can't really ask for much more. We sat near the bar and the bartender took care of us, nice guy. Chicken on the pizza we chose was cooked and seasoned perfectly. Will definitely be back.

Not really sure what people expect from this place. It's a cheaper brand of hotels in not the greatest part of town. For what it is a CHEAP hotel located conveniently by the airport it's pretty good, it's attached to a 24 hour ihop and right next to a bar. Staff is nice, rooms are decent not great. As far as value for dollar this place is great.

So so good! Little tiny place with mostly 2-tops. The meal- we're suckers for a cheese board and got a very generous one for $12. They gave my son a bit of dough to make a mini pizza - a really cute diversion. Pizza is thin crust, chewy/crispy, spectacular sauce and premium toppings. We got a calzone and my son got a cheese pizza. Canned soda and some wines. Salads look delicious. Guess we'll have to come back!!!

I can't believe that I haven't reviewed this place yet!?!?!? 

IT IS GREAT 

Great LOCATION in the busy part of Center City right by Rittenhouse Square. I like to take their food out into this park and enjoy it outdoors in the warm season. 

They are very efficient and provide nice and quick SERVICE. 

The MENU has options between salads, wraps, burgers and fresh squeezed drinks.

Mr. Jung Park is a true professional at what he does. He treats each piece preciously, and you can tell just from spending a few minutes with him that he loves what he does. Who better to trust your art with than someone who truly values what's in his hands and in his store? 

I came to know Mr. Jung Park and his Frame & Art shop while looking for some artists who would be willing to donate some pieces to the Student National Medical Association at RowanSOM. We are medical students who spend our time outside of studying to raise scholarship funds for underprivileged students and host endless community service events throughout South Jersey. When we came to Mr. Park, we were holding a small art auction at school and hoping to get some donations. He not only gave us some great pieces, but also cleaned them and wired them for hanging, and even put the corners on each piece! He took his time and conversed with us while he prepared the pieces he would donate to our cause. Seriously, this man is a gem with a heart of gold. His contribution helped us raise money for scholarships that would go towards diversifying the face of medicine. God bless him and his family. 

I am not writing a good review simply because of his generosity, but because you can tell a lot about a man through the way he interacts with people and the way he handles his work. We were not purchasing anything from his store, but he spent time with us. We were getting donations, but he still prepared each piece like he made a ton of money off of it. Honestly, I wouldn't go to anyone else to have my art handled than Mr. Park. And if you're reading this Mr. Park, thank you SO much!

I've lived in the St Louis area for over 4 years now. How have I gone this long without having Caleco's Sicilian pan pizza? How does no one talk about this when it comes to deep dish pizza? Waaaaayyy better than Pi down the street. I'm from Chicago and, while it's no Lou Malnati's, it is probably the best deep dish pizza I've had in the area since I've lived here. Haven't had anything else here but solid choice for pizza if you're in the area!

I would kill for a place like this in Orlando!

This is a perfect example of a diner.  
-Kitschy ambiance that looks like it is direct from the 1950s
- A *huge* menu!
- Amazing people watching in the late evening. 
- Servers that are awesome and FAST!
- Really good food no matter what you order. 

This place is now a must visit everytime we come to Tampa from Orlando.  Can't wait to try more of the menu.

Excellent burger place and very creative with their menu. Staff is very friendly and accommodating, and knowledgeable. esp the slim guy up front ringing the orders , he makes some great suggestions. U ask why only 3/5? I love everything about the place but I have yet to give a restaurant a 5 and 4 are scarce too and also cant its a burger place. If we r looking at only bar food, this place is easily top 5 in my list.

In my opinion, one of Nashville's best spots. Love it. Love the casual vibe in the Farmer's Market. Love being able to taste creations by an amazing chef in a laid back spot. Everything I've had here has been exceptional. The menu is unique and always changing. I was lucky enough to have Chef Arnold cook my food right in front of me! He was very personable and fun to chat with. Can't wait to try his other 2 Nashville restaurants! Highly recommended!!!
Sarah is incredible at what she does. She is honest and tries her best to give you what you want, while trying to keep your hair healthy. Very reasonably priced. Love her!!
The tacos and ceviche were delicious and the price was great! Our favorite was the fish taco and ceviche. The ceviche had generous amounts of fish and shrimp!

this place took forever to get our food. we had a decent size party and they weren't even that busy and it took an hour to get seated. our table was crammed and we asked to send some of the kids we were with to a different booth that wasn't taken and Amber gave us a snotty answer just saying no. for the rest of the crammed time the food was below par and the booth wasn't taken the whole time we were dining.

I had the Pineapple Basil Lemonade which is absolutely delicious! I'm glad I got it at the happy hour price of $5 though, because I doubt there was more than a teaspoon of alcohol in it, so $9 would have been overpriced. I also had the fried chicken salad and was not at all impressed. For $14 the portion was small and it was nothing but the salad mix you buy in a bag at the grocery and a couple fried chicken strips with honey mustard dressing

I moved here in October 2016 and am very pleased to be here.  The grounds are kept in very good condition and when I've had a maintenance issue the fellas have been here to fix it immediately!  WOW!  Also I've found the ladies in the office to be very nice.  I travel a great deal so the fact that my packages are delivered to the office is a real bonus to me.  The complex (my building anyway) is quiet and the neighbors are respectful of one another.  My view is spectacular.  I've only good to say about this place I now call home.

Very good.  Food is not as refined as a top NYC place and a person could claim some dishes (ie: rabbit pot pie) fall short conceptually or that the wine pairings aren't that interesting, but....

For the price the kitchen puts out some great food. Though it sounds gimmicky, the foie gras soup is a must, as well as the Kentucky Fried Lobster.   Either of these is surprisingly worth the price of admission.  A big bonus is that the service staff.  All professionally trained and genuinely work to make customers happy.  For example, during our dinner the manager brought over  a brisket sample because we mentioned it sounded good.  

A great place that won't break the bank, like some other Philly restauranteurs are trying to do....;-)

Ted Drewes is awesome. Don't let the haters fool you. I'm from San Francisco, home of some of the most eclectic and best food. Ted Drewes is the best frozen custard period.
Lisa B's comment is from a pretentious snob that has no idea what good food is. Don't let a novice who thinks she's elite fool you.
I was visiting NOLA, and I checked Yelp for well-rated spas. So glad I found Aria. Andy is delightful. Wonderful massage. Fantastic service. First class.

Heard about this place on a previous trip and for a dinner recommendation but didn't get around to it. Just happened to be in the area again and decided to stop in for lunch... Definitely did not disappoint! The shrimp and grits breakfast entree was spectacular! My wife had an avocado chicken wrap and they were accommodating to make it into a salad for her as well. Service was also excellent. If you've not tried this place, I would highly recommend it!

Pizzeria Vetri is a welcome addition to Philadelphia's pizza scene and is a great lunch destination for those interested in grabbing a real high quality bite before or after a visit to the one of Parkway museums (it's only a stone's throw from the Barnes). 

I visited PV on the second day they were open which worried me a little because sometimes places need some time to get up to speed. Despite some harried chefs (don't have a heart attack, guys) ordering around the pizza makers now and then, everything else seemed to be working (and tasting) just fine. 

I was promptly greeted by the hostess and was escorted to a seat at the marble counter in front of the large wood burning pizza oven. This is the place to sit if you can swing it. Not only do you get to see all of the pies made right before your eyes, you also get to peek at some of the other pizzas on the menu so you will know what you want to try the next time (like the one with the different cheeses and the eggplant one). Other seating in the restaurant (which is pretty small and fills up quickly I might add) also includes a slightly smaller counter looking out onto the sidewalk and parking lot across the street as well as a few large tables with community style seating (a la Stella) in the center. It's very kid friendly and informal but very cramped when it gets crowded. Kids can (and did) spill stuff and there's no worry about making too much of a mess. And if you hate kids it's hard to hear them over the 80's rap music being blasted (think Village People and Salt 'N Pepa) in the background. Kind of strange atmosphere looking at pizzas, seeing big photos of Italy, looking at families with kids spilling all kinds of stuff and hearing "Aaaah, push it. Push it real good" in the background. Maybe a tactic to increase beer sales?

Anyway, my pleasant server quickly arrived and offered me either tap or sparking water. I chose the latter expecting Pellegrino or something like that, but PV has an in-house bubbler like Zavino so they can carbonate their own. 

The menu at PV is pretty straightforward. They offer about ten whole pizzas (each has six slices...good for one hungry person or two dieting people). They also have one daily special rectangular pizza sold by the big slice, calzones, rolled pizza dough with pistachio pesto, and a few salads.

Wanting to keep things simple, I opted for the Margherita pizza. It came out quickly and was top-notch. The crust was very thin (thinner than say Zavino and a lot like Pitruco). It was firm and not soggy (like Stella) nor did it taste like a salitine cracker (like Slice!). It was nicely charred in spots but not burned. The sauce was good, not very thick but not runny, as was the mozzarella and the fresh basil. I did notice that in the chaos that started to ensue behind the counter that one of the chefs mistakenly forgot to drizzle olive oil and did not sprinkle sea salt on my pie like the other Margherita ones being dished out, but it did not seem to affect the taste at all. It was clearly one of the two best (if not the best) Margheritas in Philly that I have downed.

I managed to save some room for dessert and tried the cookie jar, which is essentially eight small cookies in a small white paper bag. It included two good chocolate biscotti, two of the best pignoli cookies I have ever had (sorry Termini's), two confectioners sugar covered almond cookies, and two pistachio gnocchi. It was a nice ending to my lunch and not at all overwhelming. PV also has fried pizza dough with citrus fennel sugar and soft serve as well. 

My bill for lunch was $24 which was not bad. I was a little surprised that PV charges $5 for their sparkling water (it's free at Zavino), but I guess someone has to pay for the bubbler.(which is not cheap incidentally). 

All in all it was a great lunch and I am sure I will be rushing back in no time. The food was great. The service was excellent. Granted, near the end of the meal it was like having a front row seat in that Gordon Ramsey show on TV, but I am sure that things will calm down at PV and everything behind the counter will mirror the perfection being plated and served on the other side.

This place is great for a formal dinner out.  The service is top-notch.  Went with a bigger group for dinner and we all agreed that the BBQ shrimp is the dish to get.  It is incredibly flavorful!  It is a little pricey but worth it for a nice evening out.  If you are going to splurge, this is the place to try.

First meal in NOLA .. Went here cause it was the highest rated place that was open and in walking distance to the hotel.. The Brussels sprouts were awesome.. Definitely get these..  Ordered the shrimp n grits and crab bisque.  Very heavy on the salt.. Overwhelmed the delicate shrimp and crab flavor..  Ordered the Baked oyster .. It had a nice herb flavored in the crust but was over powered by the concentration of butter ..  Yeah, its New Orleans, yeah the food is supposed to be rich and decadent...  But our plates were a bit much..

Very cute shop with a lovely owner and adorable little dog. (There is a tiny dog so be prepared if you have allergies. Personally the puppy was a huge bonus for me, but I understand some people might have issues.) Leah had lots of amazing vintage things and her store was so much fun to explore. She was very accommodating and we felt so welcome there. We'd definitely go again!

I either had Migas or Huevos Rancheros, I honestly can't remember anything other than perfectly cooked eggs and creamy black beans. Refuel is delicious! Great breakfast place but has some limited seating.

Creative plates but left something to be desired. 

Went the Saturday before Valentine's Day, had a preset 4 course menu, with two options for each course.  Salad and soup were great, apps were OK, main course was ah..., then desert was very plain.  

Service was good.  They took care of us nicely.

This is a great place for creole soul food in the Marigny, right near all the clubs on Frenchman. A friend we were with who lived here for a while said their fried chicken is among the best in the city. I can testify to their collard greens--excellent--and their jambalaya is hands the down the best I've ever had. I'm used to jambalaya being mostly about the rice, seasonings, and meat, but they pack theirs with about 10 different kinds of fresh vegetables that keeps it lighter and keeps the rice from drying it out.
These were the best cocktails we had in all of our stay in NOLA, hands down - and the pork belly dish is absolutely to die for.

I have to preface this by saying that we only had breakfast sandwiches.  I had the turkey and egg on rye toast and my boyfriend had the cheese steak and egg on a roll.  I wasnt that impressed but I wasnt surprised either to be honest.  The turkey tasted like the cheapest cold cuts they could find with eggs and american cheese (they didnt have cheddar cheese which is a downfall in my opinion).  I specifically asked for Rye Toast (toasted....i made that clear) and when it came, it looked and felt and tasted as if they put it in the toaster over for about two seconds.  It was barely cripsy at all!  My boyfriends sandwich wasnt all that bad but we've had better.  I gave it two stars because it was exactly that...meh ive experienced better.  We had them deliver so I cant really comment on the actual establishment itself or if it's any good at all.  I will try other items on the menu and hopefully I can revise this review.

Writing this review before I've finished...it is that good. Here on business with a colleague and we ordered the Honey Nut Sweet Potato Fried, the Crawfish Spring Rolls, the Shrimp & FGT Remoulade Po'Boy and the Chicken & Waffles. All of it was absolutely incredible! Can not recommend this place enough. The staff and the food is amazing!

Cuban cuisine on the go at a very affordable price. The ambience is casual and trendy.

Food...Good
Decor...great
Ambience...Casual and mellow.

This place is beautiful. Do you want to know the best part? It's free!

The courthouse is open daily to the public, so expect crowds and tourists if you're heading there on the weekend. You can amble around the inside, checking out the paintings and beautiful tiles and various rooms, and then make your way to the top for awesome views. They have an elevator and stairs to the top. The observation "deck" is't huge but it has 360-degree views so you can see the ocean, downtown Santa Barbara and the mountains on the other side. Aside from the awesome view the grounds are absolutely gorgeous with lots of green grass and shady trees for a picnic. 

Note: You can park right across the street in Lot 7. Convenient!

Great time yesterday at the south Philadelphia location.  the hostesses seated us promptly and when I asked for a table rather than a booth they were very accommodating.  our waitress was very nice and the service is always fast.  Great place to go after a sporting event especially when your team wins!

i love the atmosphere here! they've got booths, high tables, televisions, a huge pizza oven and an overall good vibe. 

i was simple and ordered a garden salad and spaghettic with meatballs. i was actually carbing up for a race the next day and didn't want to over so it...i asked the waiter to please place half of the order in a to-go box which he gladly agreed to...so great!

my dad ordered the pesto chicken pasta which he swallowed up. mom got the chinese chicken salad which she loved. they don't serve garlic bread with pasta orders...something most pizza/pasta places do but i didn't mind.

recommend going here and seeing what they've got to offer!

This is the go to spot on a budget. I reccomend that you get their daily special that comes with a meat of the day, flour or corn tortilla, rice, salad and beans. You can literally eat on it for two days so the portions are large.         I also love their breakfast, which comes with eggs, a meat of your choice and Flour tortilla. I would like to add that it gets VERY crowded during peak times (around 5 for dinner and later) so don't be in a rush. Also be prepared if going through drive thru that you will have a longer wit time.

My buddies and I have been to Brother Paul's several times now. 

They have a great beer selection, plenty of TVs and reasonable prices. The bartenders and waitresses have always been friendly and attentive. 

I can't comment on the food because I've never eaten anything. 

Brother Paul's is a solid sports bar in the Collegeville/Eagleville area, head there if you want to watch the game and don't mind other fans cheering at the TV.

It should be noted that I'm very particular with my Mexican food.  Red Habanero has a great vibe and friendly, attentive staff.  The food, however was a little above average.  The retried beans were very good, but being the picky eater I am, I couldn't find anything other than tacos.

I have been crossing the (parish) border more and more to shop here.   The prices, quality, and selections are fantastic!   I have been a fan for years, but would only shop  here when in the area, or if I had other business nearby.  Now, with the crappy customer service I find elsewhere, through the roof prices ( especially on produce), and lackluster selection in ALL AREAS, I am shopping here more often. 


The meat section is amazing.  Excellent values and selection.  The produce OMFG!   Even when you cant find good looking/tasting produce, Dorignac's has it!     The cheese circle, amazing.  Bakery--very good!! The deli, yeah!  All good!   The sections I dont particularilly care for  are dairy and grocery, but that is OK.  I have other options for that.  Oh, and the liquor, wine, and beer!  The very best in the city, and in 2 parishes!  I will be doing all my Mardi Gras food and beverage shopping here.  The cashiers are all sweet and down home.  No attitudes, cell phone talkers, or unpleasant customer service.   The customer service is like a complete 180 of that of Wal Mart, Winn Dixie, or sometimes Rouses (ALL Uptown locations that I speak of here).   


The customer base is of an older lot, many "more experienced" adults shop here, so it goes to show they have a very loyal customer base.   I am happy to be amongst it.  I shall continue to praise Dorignac's to whomever will listen.

Best Apple Cider ever!
Why can nobody else make it this good? I grew up on Adrian cider, then moved to Michigan as an adult. Michigan folks are rightfully proud of their apple orchards, but their cider barely passes for apple juice! I've never found the perfect sweet/tart balance that Adrian has maintained forever. And if you can see through the cider then I don't want to drink it!

4 .75 /5  if you like want Italian food and don't like wet noodles and dry chicken this is the place.our server Kathy was great very knowledgeable  and attentive  but not pushy or bothering. They have great selection  of beer and wine and the food is great we chicken Parmesan and a calzone  for our entree. and a fried trio of ravioli, cheese, poppers with sauce  appetizer  all were great we had enough  left to take home for another  meal.pricing is very good also you can get a gumbo soup, breadsticks and entree for about 13$  . There is a small bar with TVs also only complaint  is the seating is on the cheaper/smaller side if your a bigger or taller man you will not be to comfy that's all that has this place back from being perfect v

Ive been meaning to review this place for a while. When I moved here, I was looking for a good hair salon. Found about Serendipity through Groupon. I got an appointment for a week later, which I think is pretty normal here. 

I got my hair cut and hair color done from Heidi. She was nice, polite and even offered me a drink :) My hair color and cut came out really nice. I love it. It seemed like a very healthy environment, all other stylist were really nice too. 

I will definitely recommend and go back myself. The only negative thing about it is, the hours arent that great. I had to take a break from work at 2pm to make it to this appointment. If I could get appointments for evenings or weekends that would have been awesome. 

Since appointments are hard to get, call a week or 2 in advance and you should be good. Also, i got my hair cut and color just for $65, look for the Groupon. If you mention it to them, they will honor the price and you dont even have to buy the Groupon :)

This place is terrible. The restaurant itself is very dirty and obviously not well maintained. The service was absolutely horrible, the waitress was unresponsive to anything we said. She was friendly with everyone else except for us. The food was pricey for the portions and was sub par. My eggs also came with hair in it! Delicious! When I informed my waitress she didn't apologize or even say a single thing, she just snatched my plate away and took it to the back. Darrell came back with a fresh plate of eggs and apologized to me, he was definitely a lot more friendly than his counterpart. I would not recommend this place and definitely will not be back.

As all Philadelphians are well aware, the "Great" Northeast is a post-apocalyptic culinary wasteland. If you've ever seen the film adaptation of Cormac McCarthy's 'The Road' starring a gaunt Viggo Mortensen, then you have a visual metaphor for the food scene of Northeast Philadelphia. Simply put, it sucks; so much so that when I do find an oasis amidst the despair, I have to spread the word as obnoxiously as possible.

It all began with a discussion with a friend and coworker about how theres almost no pizza worth ordering in the Northeast and the surrounding burbs' and he immediately went on a rant about how awesome Da Vinci's is. Yesterday, I found out he was right.

I wanted to try two different types of their fresh hot pizza pie so my first order consisted of half Mr. Angelo (thinly sliced Prosciutto, aged and shredded Parmesan, and ripe cherry tomatoes layered over mozzarella and then homemade sauce) and half standard Pepperoni. The Mr. Angelo half was exceptionally good. Every bite was bursting with flavor. The Prosciutto was perfectly cooked so that you could bite through it without pulling the entire piece off of the slice, which we all know is a comman concern with pizza toppings. The aged Parmesan had that fresh aroma and flavor to it that you only get from real cheese that isn't processed. Safe to say I was a BIG fan.

 It's difficult for a regular slice of Pepperoni to blow the doors off like the Mr. Angelo (who is this Mr. Angelo and how did he inspire such a tasty concoction?) did, but it was a damn fine slice of Pep. The sauce tastes like it was made in the kitchen of a 74 year old Italian woman known to her grandchildren as Nonna and the crust is reminiscent of homemade Italian garlic bread. Both slices were excellent but the Mr. Angelo is still the way to go.

Da Vinci's Brick Oven Pizzeria is one of those fabled gems of the NE. I'm ordering again today for a pick-up to try a few of the other options. They are nestled in a little cove off of Bustleton Ave between County Line and Street Road. Blink as you race by in your 02' Honda Civic hatchback with an airplane wing for a spoiler, and you'll miss them.

Wow. Had to get that out there. This place is literally a time machine. Just off Bourbon, Hall houses the most authentic jazz experience you can find. Seated on the floor of a cozy, dimly lit room dressed in 20's decor, you're serenaded by a 5 piece old school jazz band. They will take you to church, the jazz funeral, and back. Fan yourself, sway, and sip on your whiskey in a to-go cup as the husky melancholy in the lead's voice takes you into the last century. Thanks for that NOLA.
Amazing Coffee/Food, always cute local dogs hanging out, support local artists, great queens village jem!
Excellent food and very accommodating. This is a primarily gluten-free and solely vegan restaurant in Montecito. The service is great and food is delicious. Highly recommended

Go to Charlie's! 

You'll get a far superior burger and shake!

Bonus: You'll get treated with the courtesy a paying customer deserves.

They have a lot of ice cream options along with milkshakes, candy, and snow cones. Their ice cream is very good and rich along with their milkshakes. Although their snow cones are too icy and it is like you are eating ice with syrup at the bottom. They also have a pretty good amount of candy. The place is a little run down but that is what give the place character. It would also be nice if they added some music.
Loove the iced coffee. Especially from 2-6 when they are 99 cents. Don't usually get much else besides donuts. Which are good of course.

First, to get the bad out of the way.  NO RESERVATIONS!  This disturbing trend by some new restaurants: "We really don't give a **** if we inconvenience YOU, we just don't want to mess with reservations.." is particularly an issue at The Livery, as even at 5:30 the bar was already pretty much full.  So you can try to squeeze in around the bar, where the servers are looking annoyed because you're in their way (you are), or you can sit on a bench in the foyer not knowing if you'll get a table in 30 minutes or 4 hours.  Totally unacceptable in my book.

Now the good:   The food is awesome!  As is typical of the Cunningham group restaurants, the menu is well thought out with Latin American themed small plates and entrees.  We tried quite a few and they were all tasty with an interesting amalgamation of flavors and seasonings.  Service was good, with the servers well trained on the menu options.

So overall, a good experience, especially since we didn't have to wait too long, but I wouldn't try it on a weekend after 6 pm or so, unless your time is so unworthy that you want to sit around indefinitely for a table.
Drinks are strong and cheap but the DJ is terrible even outside at the tiki bar is better music. Smh they need a new dj

Got the $10 for $20 deal so we gave it a try. Mike had the Ronnie Pastrami special mile high and awesome. We also got the Ronnie classic combo the roast beef was incredible.
We will be back. (Chicken noodles not so much)

Would've given 2 stars for the service (4 hours wait for new stickers), but I am giving 3 stars because of the kind service desk employee that waited on us. 

We were in Pep Boys to get our state inspection stickers reinstated. We had an appointment at 12, but was told that they were backed up and it would be  until 2 PM until our car can be seen. We were told originally it would take 1-1.5 hours so we said okay, and waited in the waiting area. 

At 2, I went up to the young man at the desk to ask about the status of our car and he ran into the service deck to ask the technicians if they had gotten to our car yet. The man came back and said that the technicians were still working on a previous car which had a lot of emissions problems. 

By 3, I had become very annoyed and angsty. I was a bit rude to the young man this time, but he took it well and spoke to the technicians again. Finally! After another 45 mins, he came back and told me that they are finally able to get someone free to rewrite the stickers. Feeling terrible, I apologized of my earlier behavior and he was kind enough to understand.

All in all, 4 hours to get new stickers is ridiculous. If Pep Boys didn't have such well mannered service desk employees I would rated much lower.

Dude!!! This place has had my mind reeling for a few days. The works omelet with pancakes and strawberry orange juice was phenomenal and service from LaKeisha was ideal too. I couldn't have been happier with this Saturday morning meal. I can't wait to go back- this food was killing any breakfast

Great deli meats, produce, packaged foods (eg chicken salad) and candy....can be a bit pricey though...also the management tends to be a bit unkind and standoffish...the turnover rate for employees is quite alarming as well

The staff at the spa are incredibly friendly and professional, but the rest of the staff are sub-par. It's too big, I think, to provide good customer service. I got lost getting to my room as the front desk staff did not tell me the correct directions (he even gave me a map where he highlighted the wrong way!!) The food and service at the Conservatory Wine Bar are AWFUL! The Margherita pizza literally was a flatbread with tomato paste as the sauce (and burnt tomatoes!).  None of the housekeeping staff will say hi in the hallways...which is a sure sign they are not happy here! Too bad...what a gorgeous hotel to mess up!!!

Soooo we stumbled across this spot due to a recommendation by a local at a strip club. It's a smaller size bar, but its so quaint & has a speak easy feel once inside. 

Food: All I can say is DAAAMMMNNN. Hands down this is THE best burger & grilled cheese I have EVER had. My fiancee dragged the chef out the kitchen to praise him for the deliciousness we experienced. All imma say is whoever thought of brie cheese on a burger was simply brilliant! 

The staff was on point with service & made sure we were taken care of. Be warned though - do not expect your food to come out within minutes. The food here is made with love & care. It took us about 40mins to get our food for a table of two; but totally worth the wait. 

This will be a staple bar/restaurant to visit every time I visit this magical city! 

Thank you Back Space!

I went to dinner at Cafe Eau earlier this week and was not impressed by the food or the service. My friend and I decided to split the beef quesadilla appetizers and 10 minutes later the server brought out an appetizer platter instead - she looked like she was going to walk away before we spoke up about receiving the wrong order. Then she confessed that she typed in the wrong order and didn't have the heart to tell the kitchen. We ended up keeping the appetizer platter but only paying what we would have for the beef quesadilla. Nothing on the platter was spectacular or really even all that good. The meat in the pork pot stickers were grainy, the toasted ravioli was a lot of breading and not much filling and the buffalo chicken bites were just mediocre. 

I ordered a chicken Caesar salad for dinner while my friend ordered the fried tenderloin. My salad was OK and his beef was just OK as well (i thought the beef had a funny texture to it, almost like it had been steamed)...nothing to write home about. We asked for the check and the server gave it to us, only to come back 3 minutes later with the correct bill (she had handed us another table's check). 

Overall I wouldn't come back here to eat, I think i might come back for a couple of drinks at the bar. I just don think that the food is worth the price you pay for it.

We only had one day in Nashville and a Trolley tour is the way to go.  Our tour guide Brad, was wonderful  and very knowledgeable .  We hit the high points in Nashville and were able to hop on and off to do shopping, have lunch, etc.  I highly recommend the tour!!  Get the 2 day special if you can -- you can't see all Nashville has to offer in one day!

I go to this place every few weeks, and while it definitely has it's cons, it is right around the corner from my work and it is pretty cheap (including free airbrushes on certain days).  

Even though you call to make an appointment, they never write down any of your information or even ask for your name, and sometimes you still have to wait to go after walk-ins, they should probably stop saying they take appointments. 

It is pretty run down, but it seems pretty clean nonetheless.

Fabulous dinner. I'd been there for brunch, a few times and it was always very good but nothing amazing. However, my dinner on Friday night was absolutely delicious. I started with a small cyprus plate which had fabulous halloumi cheese, olives, sausage, and a great dip (forget what but remember it being delish) and it was really great. Then I had the chicken with a yogurt sauce and it was also fabulous. And huge. Can't wait to go back and to eat my leftovers!

Best breakfast/brunch in Pasco county! Their Grits are amazing...honestly the best I have ever had. My favorite breakfast item is the Spinach and Mozzarella Omelet. My favorite lunch item so far is the mushroom burger, but you can't go wrong! Everything is delicious and you won't regret going in for some good food!

I've been visiting Mood cafe for a while now. I only tell Mr. Hassan that I want lassie or chaat; he takes care of the rest. I don't even choose because I trust his choices. Right now I'm having a lassie made with mango, banana, strawberry and pineapple. If you forgot to eat your fruits any day, just go for this lassie.
This place is head and shoulders above Chic Fil a and Zaxbys.  Better quality chicken and a great experience every time

A lot can be said about the Home Depot staff---They are very helpful and very agreeable when customer service is needed, they excel. Amanda, Hardware associate, seems to have jewels of patience and is very pleasant to work with. Amanda has two years tenure and being a young person, sets her sights on The Home Depot stock option and salaried person programs. It is great to work with the Home Depot crew, they are the best because they really serve.

Shannon, Millwork Supervisor, answered a specific need and cut lexan plastic for a project in my home as wood-working and ceramics skills, are rebuilt, perhaps to help nursing home outreach and teenage boys and girls mentoring. Aithough, Shannon noted that he did not have the extensive equipment to satisfy my request, his efforts and results were much appreciated.

Lastly, it is always good to get a proper and courteous sendoff. Cashier, Toshira the Home Depot person at the door rang up my puschases skillfully with a smile that sent me on my way. Will I be back to shop at the Home Depot? Yes, Oh, yes!

The sandwiches are very mediocre. I realize it's a pizza joint, but I was completely underwhelmed by the steak and cheese hoagie I got there. I recommend the chicken calzone or the pizza. The pizza's are a little pricy but pretty good. 

The service is also pretty slow, even when there is no crowd to speak of. The staff is friendly, but they seem a little discombobulated at times.

It's kind of weird having chain restaurant on Oak Street but I suppose if you had to have one, Mellow is not a bad one to have.
Last two times I've gone here for dinner , it hasn't been very good. Service has been good but the food is so so. Use to be better

Not sure why there's tons of negative reviews. I love it every time I go. Now, I will say the only O'Charley's I'd never return to would be the Antioch location. The Hermitage location is amazing and the food comes out promptly each time. But..you can't please everyone no matter how hard you try.

My first review because it was THAT bad. Place seemed cute enough, reasonable  price. Went in for color, worst decision ever--terrible terrible job, sincerely. And to top it off, the hair stylist was defensive and condescending. I highly recommended you look else where. Worst hair experience I've ever had, unfortunately, I wanted to like this place but the service was so fake and ignored my request, I walked out with hair nothing like what I requested.
Do not go to Bridgette!!!!

I stopped in at Sunrise Cafe this morning, went to the counter, and ordered coffee and a bagel. I was told it would be "just a minute" while they toasted the bagel. I stood and waited there while the counter person kept telling it would only be "just a couple minutes more". After what seemed forever, one of the kitchen personnel walked out. I politely excused myself for interrupting her, but said that I had waited almost half an hour for a toasted bagel. She replied that they were busy. I said that I could understand that, but that it should not take thirty minutes to toast a bagel. Instead of going intro the kitchen to check on my order, she went to the cash register, pulled out the tape, and told me that I had ordered at 9:12 and had only been waiting ten minutes! Since it was past 9:30, I suggested to her that her math was wrong. She replied that I should feel free not to return, walked into the kitchen and returned with the wrapped bagel. The delay was annoying, but her rudeness was unacceptable. I will never go back there.

Yes, the food was brilliant. Yes, the cocktails were delicious. That should be self evident. What's more important is that I got excited reviewing the menu. Not just intrigued, but genuinely excited. There was gesticulation, outburst of "oh my lord, yes!", and conversations with other diners. It isn't just food, it's the warm glow of summer in the Mexican highlands squarely in the middle of Indy.

My favorite place on University. They'll bring food out to your table but its really a self service bar. I don't mind that a bit though,  I actually like that I never need to wait for a server to order. The staff are all really nice! This is my go to bar in Tucson. Try the Daytona sauce on wings or chicken fingers and the buffalo chicken pizza is the best!
Actually the friendliest people in a UPS store, or any shipping business for that matter. The employees seem to enjoy each other which makes for a friendly and helpful environment.

I had been here once, years ago, but didn't recall much about it. May have just had a drink or two at the sizeable bar. Was staying here for business this time and decided to give a try for the convenience and cuisine. Based on the recent reviews here my expectations weren't high.

In a nutshell it was a good experience. The service and teamwork was outstanding. The food was a little up and down.

Head through the bar area to the hostess stand. Bartender comes out and seats me immediately. This was just the first example of the excellent teamwork.

Probably 8-10 tables with diners. Initially I only saw one server which had me a little concerned. I was thinking to myself I might have been better off sitting at the bar, which was reasonably full. I sometimes find you get better service at a bar seat although you are cramped for space.

Silly me. Greeted promptly by the very pleasant and friendly Kathleen. Her and the rest of the staff were a well oiled machine. Between her, the food runners, and the bartender (the seating was not the last of when he came to my table) all food and drinks were delivered promptly the table was cleared and my check delivered and the credit card run promptly as well.

As a side note if you order a glass or water or a soft drink it comes in your own miniature pitcher. Plenty of ice and like getting a refill or two without delay.

As an appetizer I ordered the Brunswick Stew. Hadn't had any in many years. It was outstanding. For the entrée I ordered the Combination Platter. This was a little variable. The Memphis Pork Sandwich was a little dry. Sauced. I probably should have added some sauce but I did not try any of the 4 sauces on the table. The Sausage link was very good. I also found the Pork Ribs, with a dry rub, on the dry side. Surprising for ribs and again maybe I should have sauced them.

Left stuffed, I finished everything. Defiitely will stop back.

I took my group to Shoney's for breakfast based on the recommendations of several people. We were all disappointed.

When we walked in we were greeted by the overwhelming odor of grease. The host was pleasant though and we were quickly seated and didn't wait lobby for our server. Two people ordered off of the menu and two got the breakfast buffet. The menus orders were served with the wrong sides but the server apologized and quickly brought out what was ordered.

No one was impressed with the food. The omelette was made with very little cheese. The breakfast potatoes were just fried cubed potatoes, basically square French fries. Each person is given one packet of jelly for their two pieces of toast. The orange juice was so diluted that it had no flavor. The breakfast sandwich on Texas toast was enjoyed but that was really it.

Coming here with my chihuahua for breakfast outside. There is a water bowl out for the animals.the servers are all friendly..one even brings dog treats out.its a friendly cafe in a friendly envitonment about 3 blocks from the spa and water.nice area to walk and stop in while shopping in the small shops along the street..there is inside dining and cafe style..there are outside small tsbles on the sidewalk about 5..we usually order the countryfried steak eggs and biscuit gravy for $6,75 its a nice little day out..

Friends moved to Jenkintown recently so we tried out this place for breakfast. Wait was a little long but there were 5 of us and it was Sunday morning. Small place, close tables. Service was friendly, I think it was the owner greeting people. The food was pretty good, I got the wag eggs Benedict. Came with thick toast, Canadian bacon and poached eggs. Good spot to soak up the drinks from the night before. Didn't get to eat them today but pumpkin pancakes sound delicious. Will try to get back here and try more things.

Lovely beach spot opens in the Shoppes at Sand Key. Just south of the Sand Key Bridge to Clearwater Beach, this is a welcome addition to the local fare. All organic teas, coffees, juices, smoothies, breakfast and lunch. Splendid view of the intracoastal waterway. Open every day 8-4.

Ordered a cake for a birthday. I chose a 10" round half n' half cake which serves has about 20 servings. I ordered it about 5 days in advanced. The cake turned out perfectly and was ready when requested. It was moist, soft, and full of flavor. The buttercream was also well done--not too sweet and just right. The shaved chocolate on the sides was also a nice touch. 

They carry the 7" cakes on hand and some of the 9" as well so if that's the size you want, you can pick up right then and there. While I ordered a cake, I couldn't help but grab a chocolate peanut butter cupcake for the road. It was great. The lip of the cupcake was chewy similarly to the ends of a brownie. So good! 

The staff was also personable. They made sure to ask if I needed any help, answered any questions I had, and ensured I got what I wanted. 

They also have a counter in the window so if you grab a sweet you can eat it right there. Highly recommended bakery! I will definitely be back.
I like this place.  They leave the doors open so it seems bigger than it is.  Sometimes it's a little difficult on the weekends to get decent service.

Not enough granola on a $11 açaí bowl. I asked for more and only got a small sprinkle. That's all that was missing, a crunch. It was basically a smoothie you spooned :/ I'll go back to try some toast but not for a bowl

We decided to drive up from St. Pete to see Tarpon Springs for ourselves. We got the assorted appetizer that had humus, tzasiki, and feta dip with pita bread. It was $10 but there was so much my wife and I didn't finish it. The taste was excellent on all three. I also had the dolmades which were delicious as well. 

The only draw back was our waiter. We went the day that Greece played Costa Rica in the World Cup. When we walked in it had just gone to penalty kicks and he was in a good mood. When he came back Greece had lost and you could tell his demeanor had completely changed.

What's not to love at Honey's.  Friendly, attentive wait staff.  Quality food with variety.  Chill vibe.  Reasonable prices.

Having moved out to the 'burbs from the city three years ago, we take advantage of any chance to frequent the restaurant scene of Center City.  Honey's has been on my list for quite some time.  And let me tell you, it didn't disappoint.  

Freshest guacamole I've ever tasted.  The waitress said, "they don't crack the avocado until you order it."  I had the churassco platter.  Flank steak with refried beans, rice and salsa verde.  Swear to our Maker that the beans were the best to ever touch my lips!  Sounds like I am over-reacting, right?  Go try the refried beans and then tell me I'm lying.

The wife got the red and gold beet salad with baby spinach, shallots, parsley, chives, walnuts and goat cheese with tarragon vinaigrette.  She found it quite delicious.  My wife isn't a foodie like me but, as we were leaving, declared, "We need to come back here again."

You hear that?  It's a ringing endorsement.  

Eat at Honey's.  Thank me later.

Cold coffee, under cooked and under seasoned fries. No bathroom. Sent us outside to the restrooms which were locked. Rushed us out the door super quick. I have been wanting to try JR forever. Just super bummed that is wasn't good...or fun. The burger was mediocre  and that's because the brioche bun brought up the ranking. Shakes were good,  only saving grace.

Super greasy pizza which usually I don't mind but it was salty and greasy! I wanted to order their special 2 slices for 4.99 but they did not have any slices so my only choice was to order a whole pizza for just me. I also purchased tiramisu (my absolute favorite dessert that usually no one can mess up) but it was freezer burnt and hard!?!  I usually always enjoy trying mom and pop pizza places at places I visit on travel but this one is definitely one I would not go to again!  I should've driven the extra 10minutes and found a better spot!  Lesson learned!

Didn't have a great experience. We did the trial session and everything seems confusing and unorganized. No one came and talked to us and couldn't reach anyone to ask questions. Classes seem very overcrowded as if they're primary concern is profitability. 

Disappointed because I thought my daughter would love it here.
Tasty BBQ and good service that is family friendly. Also a full bar. Affordable prices and good selection

We loved our first visit to Morrow's which is new addition to the culinary offerings in our New Orleans neighborhood. The food was excellent -- we had red beans and rice and fried chicken. The red beans were just delicious -- Is say the best we've had (and we've had them all over the city). The fried chicken was very tender, subtly spiced and beautifully crisped. I admit I was a bit leery reading the poor reviews about the long waits for food and service, but as a new restaurant, they had some kinks to work out. At this point though the service is excellent. Kasii, our waitperson was very attentive, friendly, and helpful.

I am the mother to three girls. Girly-Girls. Made of glitter. And sunshine. 
And that is exactly what the Cake Bake shop is made of. 
The Key Lime pie is beyond amazing. So amazing, that I have indeed, paid the very high price for the whole pie. 
The sipping chocolate is divine. 
But what we continue to return for, is the atmosphere. It's precious. And pink. And decorated to the nines. 
It's magical. 
Gwen has an eye for the details. From the aprons, to the decorations, to the to go containers...she spares no expense. 
This place is worth a visit.

OMG - GO HERE.  I've taken spinning classes at a number of places, both in the city and elsewhere.  I've never been anywhere as amazing as Body Cycle.  Here's what you WON'T see:  broken bikes, out of towels, classes cancelled at the last minute, instructors getting subs you don't like at the last minute, stupid rules about how to sign up for a class, instructors half assing a class, or any kind of mess.  If the owner's goal was to find the very best instructors in the city and bring them all to one place, he has succeeded.  I love Monica, Rebecca, Russell, Barry and Erik, but I have no doubt the other instructors are crazy good as well.  These classes are well planned, and they are no joke.  The bikes are amazing.  The space is beautiful.  There isn't just a water cooler, but one that lets you choose the temperature of your water.  This place is nicer than my home.  And I feel as welcome here as I do in my home.  The instructors are always friendly and welcoming, and always helping people set up their bikes if they're new to the studio.  The patrons are lovely as well.  No weird cliques, no one judging you or making you feel out of place.  You sign up for your classes on line, and can do so up to two weeks in advance.  They have an app so you can accomplish this right on your phone.  The more classes you buy at once, the lower the price.  Also, your first ride is free, so check it out.  I have zero doubt you'll be glad you did.

I got the avocado toast and my friends got acai bowls. The avocado toast was just okay- the avocado did not seem fresh and it was just on regular wheat toast. I could have done something better myself for cheaper. Though I myself did not try the bowls, there was very little smoothie at the bottom (for the 8 oz) and they were very liquidy.  I would opt for the 16 oz, even though $10.99 for an acai bowl is pretty steep.  Ultimately it wasn't bad, but I probably would not come here again.
Awesome atmosphere! Food was great! Had Gus's pretzels for appetizers, frittata for main course. Other folks had pizza and steak salad

I went for a consultation for alterations to my wedding gown on Saturday. I met with Gabe and he did not seem to know how to alter my ball gown style wedding dress. He also complained about the fact that it had a corset back. I love my dress and was not happy with the way he acted towards me and it. He also wanted to just take up the bottom, which would lose all of the hat detail on the skirt. I asked for a quote and he said he couldn't give me one because he wouldn't know how long it would take, and his starting ball park figure was very high. I got so frustrated I didn't even mention the other alterations I wanted done to the dress.

I am sure Gabe is a wonderful tailor, but I did not get a warm fuzzy feeling about him altering my gown. I will be going somewhere else.

What a cool experience! We went to an Ethiopian restaurant when we lived in Cali and it was okay but this one was 10x better. I met the owner and his wife and they were extremely friendly. We bought a platter of various different foods at try at the waiters suggestion and everything was so flavorful. I'm glad we came and we will be back.

Have never had a better place for my 14 year old Cocker Spaniel who has some special needs and gets really stressed out during haircuts.  The kindness & gentleness that exudes from their doggie oasis is contagious.  Almost didn't want to share the love, but had to pay it forward.  XOXO, Madison & Deborah. Love y'all.

We've eaten with friends who introduced us to Modesto's twice now. The last time as recent as Saturday evening. We closed the place down and then some! Needless to say our meal and service was impeccable! 
If your in a hurry, don't enjoy spending the evening savoring a fine meal in a casual atmosphere with friends this place is not for you. If you enjoy fine dining, great conversation, being pampered and instructed in the art of culinary sciences I highly recommend Modesto's. Everything was more than we expected in a great dining experience.
As a musician myself I respect all art forms, no matter what the medium and Carlos at Modesto's is a true artist! We had exceptional service and a delicious meal. It will not be our last time there. In fact, it is now on our list of regulars!
I highly recommend Carlos, the staff and the great culinary experience we had to anyone.

So if I could break up my review my different categories this place would be all over the star scale. 

Location is awesome. Back in a neighborhood in an old style home in New Orleans. Great walk up appeal, just down the street from a park. Everything you could ask for in a location. 5 stars*****

Inside, still very original. Nice art work, felt very natural and open. 4 stars****

The food, not for me. I ordered the Surrey's Eggs. I wanted something not too heavy since we would be walking around NO all day for the final four festivities. The Banana's Fosters French Toast was screaming my name but I had to hold me self back. The service was very fast but the food was just bland. No seasoning, no butter, not even any jelly for my toast. Nothing on my plate between my eggs, potatoes, or toast made me want to eat anything again.Maybe on another day I can try out that French Toast but I don't have the highest of hopes. I  normally would  have given this more than 2 stars, but the definition of 2 stars is "meh, I've experienced better." Right on the money.

Great location! I noticed this gem when I visited Vincent Van Doughnuts this weekend. Such a spacious dining area and great layout for the space. I ordered the Figgy Piggy and as someone who hates onions, I'm glad I forgot to ask them to leave them off. The combination was great! Staff seemed friendly even though I got my order to-go. Took about 10 minutes to get my food and I was on my way!

Can't wait to come back and try some Seattle Cider on tap. I stared at it for almost the whole 10 minutes I waited wishing it was 5 o'clock instead of noon.

I'm only giving two stars for the awesome waitress we had . But other than that , thumbs down ! 
My sister and I both found a long piece of black hair in our omlets!! My other sister had many eggshells in her eggs ! My coffee cup still had lipstick stains on it, which I could still wipe off !! The toppings that I was supposed to have with my omlet didn't come with it , I had to ask ! Even though the chef offered to pay for the three messed up plates , we couldn't get over the fact that hair was in our food !!! Yuck !! 
The chefs need to wear gloves and the waitresses do not need to go by the food as it is cooking ! 
Sorry , but we won't be going back anytime soon !

I booked a 60min therapeutic massage with a RMT at Qubo Salon & Spa this weekend. Qubo is blocks from my house and I was excited at the possibility of finding a local salon and spa that I could transfer all of my massage  and hair business to.  I typically go for two therapeutic massages a month and have my hair cut and coloured every 6-8 weeks religiously. Unfortunately my experience with this business was very negative and disappointing and I would not recommend Qubo to anyone at this point.
