Thank you so much for not only making kickass drinks and pleasant conversation, but REALLY thank you for picking up my cues to stop serving my boyfriend so I can get the hell home in time for a decent shift. Girl, people skills are half of the job and you've got it on point. I'll be back.

Feeling slightly generous at the moment, but this really is a 2.5 star review. London Grille is a casual bar/restaurant with an older, quaint feel. It's decorated with frogs, which was very cute and different. My friends and I came during happy hour and the bar was packed, so we sat in the dining area. 

Happy hour specials were decent, and I noticed that they have a pretty extensive wine list. I ended up ordering a Chardonnay for $5-- can't complain about that. Other people in our group enjoyed Yuenglings and well drinks for $4.

Food-wise, I was not impressed. I ordered the Korean Fried Chicken ($13), along with a side of fries ($3) after being told that my dish would be on the smaller side. The Korean Fried Chicken was ultimately soggy popcorn chicken, drizzled in salty, chili sauce and sprinkled with sesame seeds. It tasted about as good as it sounds...So despite being a smaller dish, there was a lot of chicken left by the end of the dinner. Definitely avoid this item. On the other hand, the french fries were pretty tasty!-- crispy and well seasoned. 

My friends seemed to enjoy their food, so maybe I just got unlucky with my selection. The food took a little longer to prepare than expected, but service was quick and friendly otherwise. With so many other restaurant options available in Philly, I honestly don't think I would go out of my way to return.

If I could give more stars I would. I've been taking my car to Goodyear for quite some time and mr. Harold and his staff are always pleasant and always makes sure I am taken care of. I often get paranoid about my car breaking down so I'd bring it to them and they'll tell if I need to make adjustments or not. Most times it's nothing, but they've never insisted that I needed any work that was not necessary and have always been very professional! They would even tell me how long I have till certain repairs are needed so that I can afford it. I wouldn't go anywhere else before I have this Goodyear location check me out first because they're honest, trustworthy and reliable!

thank you PJ. 
this was a great afternoon, filled with fun food.   the salad to start with, then we moved on to boudin, then onto brunch.   lots of fun here.

I just thought it was a restaurant, then realized that you got a butcher here, and lots of cheese.  you can shop up in here and bring home a killer dinner.  OR you can eat here.  we did tons of sampling, and a great bloody mary to boot.

I can see bringing lots of friends here over the next few months.  so nice to find a new spot for breakfast/brunch.  we will be back for dinner next.

The typical coffee house. Coffee, pastries and such. Staff was OK. Somewhat unprofessional in that they stood behind the counter talking loudly to each other about things not related to work or the task at hand. I ordered a frozen coffee (what they call a Mochasippi) and a bagel. Overall a decent experience, nothing wrong. 

Just so anyone who may visit here knows, parking at this location is TERRIBLE! There are a total of approximately 12 spaces, and 2 of those are handicapped. Be prepared to hunt around or use the drive thru.

I've only had a few reasons to contact Sierra air.  They installed my AC about 5 years ago, and I only recently signed up for their home comfort club.  But they are always super friendly when I've called with questions about my furnace and the tech that came out this morning to service the heater was professional and friendly.  I've referred Sierra Air to multiple people over the years based on the AC service and after today's service will continue to recommend Sierra Air.

Ate here again on Friday, and as usual, my food was excellent!!!  I'm adding an extra star now because our waiter was kind enough to move our table outside so my bf and I could eat outside. Unfortunately, it started to rain, but I appreciated the effort!  

People who came here expecting glitz and glamour know very little about authentic Jamaican spots. Forget about the fact that it was in a movie.....if you want some fantasy dining experience, go eat at a Beaches resort or something or go eat at Bahama Breeze.

My food came within 15 minutes and the service was wonderful. Yah Mon....

BEWARE!!  My family and I decided to try this restaurant based on reviews posted here.  Being only 1 of 2 tables in the restaurant when we arrived, the service seemed to be very good.  Food was delivered to our table in a timely manner, but half of the order was forgotten and had to be made after 2 of the meals already came out.  After finishing our food, we gave our waitress a restaurant.com certificate we had purchased.  The certificate cost $10 and was good for $25 toward your purchase.  When the waitress saw the certificate, her attitude completely changed.  She took a long time to bring us our check and boxes for our food, no big deal to most, but I was with my 2 young children who were definitely ready to go.  When we finally got our check, I noticed an 18% gratuity added.  Now, the checks at this place consist of a calculator tape and that is it.  You would never know how much anything costs by looking at your check.  The 18% gratuity was added inconspicuously after I gave her the certificate.  My party consisted of 4 people, myself, my husband, and our 2 children under 4 years old.  I couldn't believe a tip was added to our check.  My husband had dined her before, and there was no tip added, so clearly it was not a restaurant policy, it was at the waitresses discretion.  Also, there was a sign outside of the restaurant when we walked in that stated that fajitas were the daily special at $6.99.  On our check, there was nothing for that price, so when I questioned the waitress, she said that was a lunch special only.  THEN TAKE THE SIGN DOWN!!  I will not be back to this restaurant based on service alone, but on top of that, the food was only average...try Dos Margaritas in Hendersonville, much better service and much better prices!!

Wow, this place has really gone downhill! I don't know if there is a change in management or what, but this restaurant is horrendous and I will never return. Service was the worst I've ever had in a restaurant. Our waitress would disappear for 20 minutes at a time. At one point I had to go to the hostess stand and request refills on our drinks because the waitress had been gone for so long! We also noticed similar complaints from other diners. The food quality has declined and I felt sick after eating it. They have changed the chips to an inedible form of disgustingness. The salsa is also served warm. Ewww, wonder how long it has been sitting out! I think the health dept needs to come in. Do not
Eat here!!!!

Meh.

Stayed here in a tiny room, and the food wasn't terrible. The service was excellent, though the valet's were kind of douches -- but they were busy, so I guess it's understandable. The hotel was moderately clean. The streets are so tight and narrow in the FQ. We definitely got a good deal (I think the rate was in the $80s). I guess I can't complain too much, though the way the tub was draining, you'd think the hotel were still flooded and under water from a hurricane. It was just kinda gross.

It was my first trip to New Orleans, and other than the historical component and awesomeness of being in the city, I think after the buzz wore off, it felt like just another tourist trap, so the hotel, though grand and stunning visually, left more to be desired.

I went here more than a year ago and still dream about it! Everything about it was great -- we had an inexpensive bottle of wine that the guys behind the counter recommended, the cheese plate, and a mushroom polenta dish that was probably the best meal I've ever had.

I would recommend going at night -- there were tiki torches and twinkling lights that made the atmosphere wonderful. 

I'd go back to New Orleans just for Bacchanal!

Had our first visit 2 weeks ago on a Thursday night.   Place is very nice.   Decor is not my style but I understand what they were going for and they pulled it off.  Place was full with only 1 bartender?  I felt bad for him.  Even though he was solo, he knocked out those cocktails and gave my wife and I great service.  I asked him if he was usually on by himself on Thursday night.   The other guy called out.  Well, full bar, still got good service, cocktails were great, and they were short handed.  That's 5 stars in my book.
I know it's not fancy, but the food is fantastic! Best marinara sauce ever. I order eggplant parm via Uber Eats weekly!

Not nearly 4 or 5 stars. Poor service and under average food. Served my wife who is allergic to bacon (asked for no bacon) soup with bacon in it. I got roast beef that tasted like floppy sandals (bad). Was expecting something similar to Panera but no. Now worth the stop

I've been having my hair cut and colored from Phil for almost 2 years now and I can't say enough wonderful things about him!  I've "never " had a bad cut or color, he's very professional has a great eye for color and keeps my style fresh and up to date and I get tons of compliments when I get a new style!  I always walk out feeling like a new woman.  He's very prompt about messaging me for my next appointment and I have a great time while I'm there.  Every one in the salon is also nice!

My wife and I visited for the first time. We got our menus and waited for 10+ minutes and nobody ever came to take our drink order. Other people that came in after us were being helped. Really bad impression for our first visit.

Fabulous food and fantastic service!  We had the Nola Bites, Mufaletta, Crawfish Etouffee, and a side of the cheese grits - I didn't want to stop eating!  Carl, our server, kept things lively and entertaining without being obnoxious.  I don't normally write reviews and tonight's meal made me take the time to say, "Kudos Creole House!  Best dinner we've had in a long time!"

Lovely hotel, amazing staff and excellent service! Definitely staying here again. Great location, Close to the excitement of the French Quarter however our room was exceptionally quiet and enjoyed tranquility in a beautifully decorated room. 
Great value with breakfast included, and the staff does a great job of catering to guests.  Would highly recommend!

Recently moved to the area and was needing a groomer for our Lab- so I googled and yelped and came across Wags to Riches. I pulled up the website and was a little skeptical since the website didn't offer much info- but decided to call based on yelp reviews- so glad I did! They were able to fit my dog in the same day! Sandy was great with our dog and he looks and smells so much better and the price is super reasonable. This will be my go to place for my labs grooming needs!!
Great service, very attentive even though they were busy. I love the Duck dish:)

I can't say enough wonderful things about this practice and the staff.  I rescued my dog and they were the vet the rescue sent me to.  I went in not knowing what to expect, as I was leaving Dr. Platts office I asked them to call and transfer my older dogs records to Colmar and never looked back.   Dr. Platt is amazing, the word amazing is not enough to explain how she treats her patients.   Her staff is the very best not only are they wonderful to the animals but they are caring and patient with the parents.  My boys love them and that is all I need to know, if you don't believe go see for yourself.

I was a little disappointed in Tim Horton's.  This review is for the doughnuts only.  They do have breakfast and lunch sandwiches also.  It is located in the Cortex area, so it is pretty dead on the weekend. Parking is a problem.  If you can find a place on the street, consider yourself lucky. Their parking lot is located caddy-corner from the shop and is fenced in so you have a bit of a walk ahead of you.  

We chose the glazed, maple glazed, cinnamon bun,  apple spiced jelly doughnut and a cherry Danish.  I hate to say it but we were wondering if the doughnuts at Schnuck's would have been better.  

Would I go back?  Not for the doughnuts but I would go to try one of their lunch sandwiches.

Friendly, delicious, romantic are the 3 words I would use to describe this place. The bread is O' so hot served with a roasted garlic hummus 
(don't fill up on bread!). I got to try the toasted ravioli, which are house made, and I had heard they were better than Lombardo's, but, they are not.. just as I suspected! They weren't horrible, but tasted almost like every other ravioli I ever had. I also tried the bruschetta - now that was fantastic but I do wish it had some fresh basil to go with. For my salad I had a spinach with a salmon bacon and potato straws(they were soggy), but the dressing was a pink vinaigrette that was just the right amount of sweetness with some red onions - it was quite tasty. For my entree, even tho I was full a long time before it ever arrived - I had the Trattoria Steak. I ordered it med. rare. When it arrived, it was probably about a 6 oz. portion of filet medallions finished in a demi glaze of I don't remember what, but oh... my... goodness... was it delicious! I have never had steak melt in my mouth before, and this did. It was more so on the rare side, which was actually quite perfect for me. Every bite I think i moaned! It was served with creamy mashed potatoes(not a lump in sight!) and asparagus. I took 1/2 my meal home and ate the rest in the middle of the night - cold .. and it was still fantastic. For dessert we had shared tiramisu - which normally I'm not a fan of but GOD was that good. I went home, more than satisfied and afraid I was going to have a food baby along with a real baby at the same time! The service was okay, but I would def. eat here again!

I went here for restaurant week because I live in the area and always pass by. I definetly considered it more of a hotel restaurant, but it was wonderful! I would absolutely go back. It was a different menu because of restaurant week, but my entree of salmon over quinoa and veggies was one of hte best I've ever had!! I was so full but I had to finish it. They were also running a special for restaurant week where bottles of wine were $35, which i pretty decent for a more upscale place. The staff was very friendly, only issue was we could not find hte hostess for awhile to get seated. But I think she had ran in the back, and they apologized. Overall great inventive take on traditional cuisine. Loved it and cant wait to go back.

This is the best Domino's location! I usually order via app and when my pizza tracker says "Jeff" is preparing your order then I know I'll have a great dinner. I would definitely recommend this location. Very fast delivery and always fresh/hot food. :)

I come here every weekend to relieve stress and do some line dancing. This place a has great atmosphere and welcomes all ages. If you're looking to have some fun and drinks I'd stop in and check their line dance classes every Friday night at 8:30pm dancing starts at 7pm until closing!

I've actually ordered something three times and the food is fantastic, the down side is service. First time they burnt my food, told me they'll fix it better next time. Second time I waited two and a half hours while dancing before getting my meal. The last time I ordered I had to hunt down a waiter and they forgot my fork and didn't bring me the check at the end of the night. Still though, I love to dance so I show up for that and have a great time!

Went with some of my family last week. Fantastic food, fantastic beer! Loved it and definitely will be back again. I had the shepherds pie and drunkin punkin. Dinner portions are large enough to carry out and have leftovers for the next meal.

Really only came for the ox tail pho. Would I come back for it, you bet your ass! There aren't many places I know that serve specifically ox tail pho, so I was really excited to try this place out. 

First off, the broth was nice and flavory, it had a lot of body, and had a nice rich deep color to it. As for the meat chunks, they definitely didn't skimp out on the ox tail. They loaded the bowl up with several pieces. So much, that it got in my way so I had to remove some of it and set it to the side. I'm not mad at about it, but it just took up space and hid my noodles.

This hip brunch spot is worth the wait. We had a group of three on a busy Sunday morning and only waited about 30 minutes. Everyone at the table ordered some sort of Dutch baby pancake and we were all blown away. I had the Dutch baby pancake with berries and lemon curd and it was divine!

Overpriced but pretty good food. If you can handle the heat, make sure you get the spicy meatball app! It's phenomenal! I expected a little more out of my entree however. I got the bone in ribeye and while it was well prepared and an excellent cut of meat it just didn't have any seasoning on it that I could taste. Yes the temperature was right through and through just didn't have the flavor I expect from bone in cuts.

This was our fifth time eating at Berlin's Donner.  Marie greeted us sat us down and started to explain but told her I've been here many times and now just bringing my sister.  She had the sausage plate which consisted of three different types of sausages German potato salad and sauerkraut.  Since she has been to Germany many times she said this is authentic and absolutely delicious.  I had my usual chicken Donner which is always delicious and usually enough for two meals.  After reviewing the 16 types of German beer that come in every 48 hours we selected one and it was unbelievably delicious.  With 16 beers available on tap it's also the best priced beer in the entire area and tastes like a microbrewery.  I was glad to see a steady stream of people coming in to eat and drink and the IHOP next door was totally empty.  We are so happy to have a delicious place to eat and drink in our neighborhood. Don't forget to order the apple strudel with homemade vanilla ice cream.  You will not believe how good it is.

I can't say it was a HORRIBLE experience, but it was a "C minus" grade at very best, and probably more like a D.  I am a premier member and use National every time, all over the USA.  Here are the reasons for my sub-par review of my experience at with National at the PHL airport:
1.  When I went outside to catch the shuttle, the driver of the National bus was pulling away.  He looked at me and saw me running to catch the bus, but did not stop.  Directly behind him was a driver of the Hertz shuttle bus.  He was beeping at the National Bus driver to try to get him to stop.  The Hertz driver open his doors and asked me if I needed a ride.  I told him I'm with National and not Hertz, and he told me he would drive me anyway, because he felt bad for what he just witnessed.  He had some not very nice (but very professional) comments about the National shuttle driver.
2.  When I got to the National lot, I picked out a car from the aisle.  When I got in, I noticed there was a GPS device in the car that should not have been there, and the "low tire pressure" light was also on.  Two signs that National did a very poor job of reviewing the car before putting it back on the lot for another rental.
3.  Getting out of the lot took forever.  I'm not sure why it was taking the car in front of me in line so long, but 4 or 5 cars in the exit next to me went through in the same amount of time.  No one made any attempt to accommodate my exit after the long wait, and the attendant did not say sorry for the long wait when the car in front of me finally exited.

Most of my rentals with National have been fantastic, and I highly recommend them overall.  But my experience at PHL airport was far below expectations and my usual experience with National.  Hopefully next time will be better.

A group of us went to this restaurant for the STL Restaurant Week. This was a wonderful 3 course meal for $25. I had calamari for an appetizer, crab cakes and shrimp for dinner, and bread pudding for desert. It was more than enough food for me to even have leftovers to take home. Everyone in our party enjoyed their selections also. I will definitely visit this location again in the future.

We had an issue with our heating on the coldest night of the year and they were professional, amazingly responsive, friendly and fixed the heat at 10pm for us - and all for less than $100. Would recommend them without hesitation.
We got 50 wings last night. We ate a few and just couldn't believe how small, over cooked and horrible they were. Trashed them! Never going back!

I absolutely love this bar.  Jason, the bartender, is exceptionally knowledgeable and makes terrific drinks.  

The sorbet special is out of this world.  Go to this place!

I grew up with one bakery in all of small-town, Virginia that was best known for their donuts.  Fast forward 24 years and I live down the block from the Zagat rated #1 Cannoli in Philly.  

Holy cow, these some good cannoli.  But you already knew that. So get these instead: 

1.) Tomato pie: served on Sundays and leftovers Monday morning.  My God, is it good. 
2.) Creme filled donut: I had one a day for about three days straight and then decided I should start working out again.  Forego the powdered sugar.  Unless you're wearing white pants. 
3.) Pignoli cookie: Was told by my regular bartender to get this specifically from Potitos.  I waited three weeks before I did.  And then I bought a pound of them to "share" with my husband. 

I had the cupcake and it was so-so... I like rich, creamy frosting, and this had more of a spongy texture.
Convenient and the sushi is so fresh! Love it and I will definitely be back. I've only been there twice since it has just recently opened.

My boyfriend and I tried The Love for the first time Saturday evening of Memorial Day Weekend. The city is usually pretty empty on holiday weekends - but Love was still packed. Nothing on the menu really spoke to me as something I just had to have, but he had really been wanting to try this place. I"m glad I listened! We started with the duck salad - fantastic! We had the lobster spaghetti and the crab pasta special as entrees - both good but the lobster spaghetti was the winner. We also finished with a cheese plate and the cookie tray - I was skeptical that a cheese plate could be $20 good, but it absolutely was! Definitely a pricier dinner - but all high quality ingredients and worth the money. Good service as well - paced the different courses well and check on us just enough. Will definitely be back!

What a fabulous restaurant!  Because it was a busy Saturday night, we waited and then ate in the cool lobby of an office building and I thought that made the experience super unique... Almost like something they do in Europe.  The service was fabulous.  The octopus, meatball and carpaccio apps were to die for.  Both beautiful and delicious.  I had the oxtail ravioli and it was amazing as well.  Can't wait to return.
Nice place to have close.  The employees are pretty friendly too.  The cookies on the counter kind of creep me out though.

I consider myself an eggs benedict aficionado, and Wildflower Cafe may have delivered some of the best I've ever had.

The croissant the EB was served on was as close to being as France as I've been. Anyone who has eaten out of a true French bakery knows the chase after a properly flaky on the outside and chewy on the inside croissant I'm talking about. 

The biscuits melt in your mouth and when paired with the wildflower honey butter, they cannot be beat. 

The service was warm and welcoming and the setting was just as fantastic. 

Wildflower is the ultimate brunch spot, save yourself the time of contemplating and go.

The last time we went, everything was excellent. I had the strata for Sunday brunch and it was superb. We haven't always been thrilled with everything we've had so we'll give it four stars and hopefully up it to 5 if we get a couple more consistently good meals.

Tavern has a great brunch situation if you are looking to have drinks. 2 for 1 mimosas, bellinis, bloody Mary's and sangria make for a great start to the day. Brunch can get very packed during peak hours so you want to get there early on Saturdays and Sundays.

My mom bought a groupon for archery lessons and lane rental.  The facility is nice however don't bother with their lessons.  It involved less than five minutes of instruction.  While I would visit the facility again I wouldn't bother with lessons.

Awesome Pho .. OMG it's Top notch..It's surprising to my experience that's a corner resturant could taste this good. No kidding its was worth it. The owner was nice and had great customer service skills despite communication barriers.

How can I give this less than 5 stars? Admission is FREE! (of course, they casually ask for a donation but no pressure at all). What a beautiful landmark. My wife and I were talking about how it would be awesome to have a wedding here. But not in the Fall/Winter when it's windy freezing cold. Such as how it was when we went. We went up to the 4th floor viewing tower to get a good view of town. So nice... made me want to live in SB for about 10 seconds. Then more of that freezing cold wind started up again. I'm sure it's not like that all year long :) Plus, we had to go because we were 5 minutes out from the end to our 75 mins of free parking.

I was introduced to this hole-in-the wall by a dear friend who spent time in Afghanistan, and I have no independent basis for comparison to "more authentic" Afghani cuisine.   My friend, however, assured me that the offerings were close to the real deal.

We began with the hummus, which was quite good.   As a veteran hummus eater (my mother fed hummus to me when I was an infant, which was sometime before last week), I will note the the texture was right but that it was not as lemony or garlicky as I prefer.   Few places make dishes that compare favorably with the family versions.   The hummus was served with what-seemed-to-be just baked bread (very fragrant).  

The chicken kebab platter was terrific.   The kebabs were moist and juicy yet perfectly charred.  I adored the salad, which was fresh and crisp with a tangy vinaigrette dressing.  The basmati rice was perfectly cooked, each grain was separate and fluffy.  Our fairly healthful lunch was a good value, too.   Looking forward to many return visits.

Fun selection of clothing 40s-80s to buy plus a huge rental section.  Keep it in mind if you're on the look out for fun vintage. Some items were pricey, but there were deals to be found including a great 80s sparkle dress for my hipster costume ($20), a 40s style cocktail dress ($25), and an irresistible-y ridiculous faux leather vest ($10).  

Good times were had.

I finally made it to In-N-Out! Now that's a burger. I got a double double with fries. Why oh why can't we have an In-N-Out in Boston? It's just not fair. I've been craving that super cheesy yumminess since I got back from vacation. I already know that when I go back to Cali In-N-Out will be one of my first stops.

I can't vouch for their prices vs. other body/paint places. It was just time to clean up my front bumper and some small dings here and there. I dropped my car off when they opened. I actually got there a few minutes before the owner and cuddled with the lump of chocolate lab inside while I waited. I got a call the following day around 2 or so saying I was good to go. The owner was very pleasant to deal with and they did a fantastic job on my paint. They also polished my headlights, which were disgustingly foggy, and they sparkle now. I also found a small plastic container with leftover paint and a brush (like those old school paste bottles) in my cupholder for if I need to touch anything up later. I really hope I don't need to make a visit again, but if I find myself needing work done, this place has my future business.

This place is a hidden gem on East Main Street in Moorestown! It is a small restaurant that is easy to miss, if you arent paying attention.

There are several eateries with outside bistro style dining on Main St. Look for people sitting outside eating and you wont miss this place.
They specialize in breakfast and brunch here.

The staff is really helpful and friendly. The crowd really seems to be at its peak from opening until around noon. You can dine in or take out. There arent a lot of tables in the main restaurant area, so you may have a short wait for a table to open up. 

My wife and I stopped in for brunch, she had the omelete with cheddar cheese, bacon, pancakes and potatoes and OJ. I had the Churro French Toast with glaze drizzle, whipped cream, bacon and potatoes and OJ. The Churro French Toast was awesome! The potato cubes were tender and seasoned perfectly!  There are no menus handed out, as the menu is artistically displayed on the wall and window. You can pay with cash/debit or credit. Parking is availble on Main St. If you cant find street parking, there are parking lots within close walking distance of this restaurant. Once you are finished the waitress will bring you your check.

We made reservations for the W Main Street location. The appetizer we ordered was okay... We ordered the veg samosa. We have definitely had better in Tiffin in Bryn Mawr, PA. 

However, we ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala and the Aloo Gonhi and they were very tasty. Although I asked for it to be a little spicy and it was not spicy at all. But still overall a great taste. 

We thought we had a great experience until we went to pay. We had a double take deal coupon from doubletakeoffers.com which was pay $15 for $30. So when we went to pay they were not really sure how this worked. The "MANAGER" wrote down the code and said she would process it. When she returned to our table we still owed too much when I asked what the original amount was compared to the balance she got very defensive and I tried to explain that the deal was 30$, the "MANAGER" said that I needed to calm down and she believed me. All I tried to do was show her the coupon so that she did not think we were trying to pull one over on her. She was not nice about it at all. She took the check back to fix and stated she would be right back, she had someone else bring us our corrected check. As we were walking out and passing her she ignored us until we were almost out the door, and then she decided to yell from inside the restaurant "have a great day"!!!  She was very unprofessional. I also heard her speaking about a "special non-alcoholic cocktail" she was going to make for a child at another table, she had mentioned that she just started doing this. I hope the owners are aware. 

Despite the "MANAGER", which I hope soon will have to take a managerial class, we would come back for the food again.

When I found out that a Panera was opening close to my house, I was so excited. I love panera and have for about 10 years, even worked at one when I lived in Florida. However, this location is subpar. I go in the morning and I'd say 9/10, my order is wrong. I don't change anything. I see it on the screen, I see it's on my receipt, but when I get handed the item, it's just not what I ordered. I don't make a big fuss of it, but there are somethings that I can't eat. So I have to turn around and return it. I hate looking at my food in the drive thru but now I have to because it's never right. I know how busy panera can get, so I go at non busy times and yet, I still have an issue with the service. I have tried to give this panera many chances, but I'm not sure I can anymore. This last time, the cashier interrupted me to talk to a coworker and closed the window of the drive thru on me speaking, told me the wrong total, gave me the wrong sandwich, and when I came back, she was adamant that she didn't. Even though I still had the receipt. She said I should just keep the sandwich, I said I couldn't because I can't eat what's on it. Please don't fail me panera! Work on your customer service.

Two Goats provided the most delicious brunch for my daughter's bachelorette weekend. Alicia and Philip were so friendly and went above and beyond to deliver the absolute perfect meal. Our brunch consisted of chicken and waffles, quiche with bacon and spinach vegetable frittata, homemade biscuits, fresh fruit, etc. and everything was absolutely fantastic. In addition to preparing the delicious food, they also cleaned up and left the kitchen spotless. 
I can't stress enough what a fantastic experience it was working with them.

Really a very nice museum with a lot to offer. We only had a few hours and had 3  little boys with us...even though they were good you can only stay in a museum so long with 3 kids. But, after every exhibit they did have small areas for children to interact and learn more about the exhibit they just saw...I am sure this is great for parents gives them a moment to rest. There is a ton of artwork we did not get to see but you could defiantly get lost in this place for a day...you could spend a day in the gardens alone very beautiful grounds. We did see the dream car and fashion exhibit which were both great I would highly recommend them both. We did have lunch here it was not a amazing but a lot better than what you would think, however as you would expect a little pricey especially if you have a group of kids with you....they do offer beer and I believe wine so if you do bring children just know there are adult beverages available in case you lose your mine or just need a break lol

Had a recent pleasure of visiting the hotel for a friend's wedding and came to the restaurant for lunch. 

Though forced valet was something that we did not really liked, it was a pleasant experience. 

The River's Edge restaurant was wonderful. Great staff and waitress. Food is also good. We had the calamari, turkey burger, and lobster mac-n-cheese, which the later 2 were delicious. We especially would like to recommend Kylie the waitress, who has greeted us with friendliness, attentiveness, and passion. She made sure that we had the greatest dinning experience by continued checking on our needs and asking if the food was up to our standards. 

Will definitely come back because of Kylie. She is exemplary and a great asset to the restaurant and hotel.
Still love this place. It is out of our way but it's worth the drive. We mostly get the massamun curry and chicken pad thai. It's one restaurant I never get sick of.

Been almost a year since I've eaten at this place, so an update is an order since we had an early dinner here last night.  

Happy hour on a wintry Sunday and the place was pretty busy.  It only took a few minutes to get our drinks, but the service after that went downhill.  It was a long wait for our nachos, wings and sandwich to arrive - were they worth the wait?  Not really.  The nachos were burned, the hot wings reeked more of vinegar than spice, and the chicken sandwich was bland.  

Took forever to flag down the waitress to get containers for the food we only ate half of, and another long wait to finally get the check.

Anyway, sorry but my hatred of too many loud TVs in a restaurant (sports bar or not) still stands.
Love this place! The service is outstanding, the food is excellent, and the crowd is always fun!

Thankful that we have a really good restaurant in Alton. The food is high quality, fresh and well prepared. I even liked it to a five star when they prepared the food with more delicious sauces as in the past. Don't go on wine Wednesdays, or save a table for me.

Yummy brunch spot. Service admittedly can be hit or miss. Wait staff are always pleasant but sometimes they can be forgetful. Today for instance, they forgot my coffee until the end of my meal. Wasn't a huge deal to me as I'm pretty lax but perusing other reviews, this could be a prelude to a s*fit to someone else. I think the menu prices are pretty reasonable and the food quality is pretty good. I've been a devotee of the avocado omelette for the past few weeks with fresh fruit (actually sweet and not from a can, thank goodness). It's the same price as the other omelettes. Other restaurants charge a premium for avocado anything. I've tried the French toast, which is seasoned with cinnamon and nutmeg and not just dipped in egg and fried. Potatoes would be more appealing to my palate if they had some crisp factor but that's my preference. If you haven't been, try it

The appetizer we tried was the roti canai and it was like watered down indian food with barely any chicken in it. I got the rice dish with ginger duck as my main meal. The duck was soggy and not flavorful. My fiancé got the spare ribs. They were also really bland and maybe needed some salt/spices. I'm not a picky eater at all and love all different types of dishes. The food here was actually just really bad.
Fusion!! Flavor!!! Fun!!! This place is the place to go for a great Mexican fusion dinner! They take Mexican food to another level!! Pineapple shrimp tacos and a peach margarita are a must!!

I priceline-ed a room in this hotel for $50 per night.  That was the best thing about our stay. 

Parking is very expensive for St. Louis.  If you don't have a car to park, this would be a good place to stay.  If you're traveling on a budget, stay elsewhere.
Their made to order jiice blends are fantastic as are their soups and salads.  Great tasting, healthy nutrition.  Never miss a visit when I am in or near Haddonfield.

My brother and I have eaten in and ordered take out from this place multiple times.  A few weeks ago, when we ordered 2 chicken on rice dishes to go, we were told that we couldn't have dark meat for both.  So, I opted to have dark meat on one and white meat on another.  We were told that the restaurant can have half white and half dark meat on each rice.  That would be fine, except, when I opened the box at home, I was pretty sure I got half portion of dark meat and no white meat on my rice.  I like their food, but this just makes me very unhappy...  I will probably go there a lot less often from now...

Went here for restaurant week and since I was traveling for work getting a 3 course meal for $35 was right up my alley. I'm writing this 2 months later and I still remember what I ate. Warm goat cheese salad, lamb lollipops, and cannolis. Outstanding! So was the service and the free WiFi. Loved and would love to go back.
AMAZING FOOD. Wait was long but so worth it. The fish was great and the BBQ even better. If you are in the area, try this place.
This place is the shit! Looove the food and the service is wonderful  Atmosphere and decor on point!!

I just moved to St. Louis and Mizu was the first restaurant I visited downtown. The hostess was friendly, engaging, and quite helpful with menu options, and the atmosphere is very inviting. Oh...and the Las Vegas roll is fantastic!!

I was very disappointed in my visit on Mother's Day. I've been to the Fellini's cafe in Newtown Square and it was wonderful. We had a very friendly, attentive waitress and the food was delicIous. However, for this location, we were seated right away, but our waiter was no where to be found for most of our meal. It wasn't that crowded for being a holiday. It took forever to get our drinks, and there were no apologies from the wait staff whatsoever. We weren't offered cheese, we had to ask for it, which is strange at an Italian restaurant. We were halfway done our meal before we found them to ask. To top it all off the food tasted odd (we had ordered the same dish) and were both sick the next day. I recommend steering clear of this location.

Great location! Happy hour with $3 drafts. Other than that, you may want to head over to the Columbia Cafe @ The History Center. Seriously! As a Channelside resident wanting more food locations nearby, very disappointed in Hablo Taco. Of course we will be back (it is across the street) but next time just beer or margaritas with an order of nachos. 
Food wise: salsa is flavorless and I don't know that tomatoes are even in the recipe. For the tacos,  best flavor I've tasted is the Southern. Do NOT get there steak or pork taco!! Southern is probably better option. Shrimp taco had 1-2 shrimp at best. 
Guacamole with cheese and bacon is decent. Chips are good. Overall, food lacks flavor and some dishes are about the heat and not the flavor. 
Won't mention a name, but there is one bartender there that offers friendly service and makes a great margarita.

The food is never consistently the same.  I guess they must be one of the busiest locations in St Louis so beware of a constant crowed and don't except to get the same quality you might get at your usual location. And the Internet connection is useless.

I agree with other reviewers that the place should be cleaner than it is, but I would call it more messy than dirty. Old School Italian bakeries can still maintain their feel/nostalgia/ambiance and be updated. 

My gelato was so terrible that I threw it away. I'm an ice cream-aholic, so you know it was bad if I couldn't bring myself to eat it. It was gritty and chewy, as if it had caramel in it. It was even hard to scoop with the plastic spoon because the scooped gelato wouldn't pull away from that still  in the bowl without effort. I took 2 bites and tossed it. If it hadn't been a night when I was super-tired, I would have taken it back & complained.

On the other hand, the cannoli rocked. I'm a cannoli aficionado and recognize a good thing when I taste it. 

I bought 2 cheesecake slices.  They were pretty good.
For a chain pizza place that delivers, we like it. Lots of options for sauce, crust, and toppings. My favorite thing about Papa John's is the garlic sauce though.

We decided to change our Sunday brunch plans at the last minute and we were so glad we did! Fortunately, when we arrived, it wasn't crowded and we were seated right away. The food was excellent and the staff was very attentive and friendly - especially Shaun. We highly recommend and will definitely go back the next time we are in NOLA!!

My family and I occupied two rooms during our stay at this hotel.
Pros:  This hotel is beautiful and it has character.  It is in the best location in the French Quarter.  It was a short walk to the river walk, the French Market, Canal
Street, and Bourbon Street.  The staff was very friendly and eager to help.  The music in the bar was great.   
Cons:  The t.v. in my mother-in-law and kid's room did not work.  She called the front desk and was told that someone would fix it soon.  No one arrived.  She called again the next day.  This time she was told that she was on the list to have someone check on it.  No one ever came.  So she was stuck in a room with kids without a t.v.  My son eventually figured out how to fix the t.v.  In a hotel which prides itself on providing exceptional service it was very disappointing that no one was ever sent to her room to fix the t.v.  

Overall it we really liked the hotel and we recommend it.
This is another great local business.  Our two hounds always get their pawdicures here.  The staff is always friendly and treat our fur babies as thier own.  Ziggy and Straty say so!

LOVE LOVE LOVE the Preservation Hall! My family and I went on a thursday night...we were warned to arrive early so we could actually find a seat but did not follow the warning.  Boy did we regret it!  Since this place does not have alot of room, there are not alot of space for furniture...as in, there were only a couple of benches.  

My family and I opted to stand in the back because we didn't want to squeeze onto the floor with some of the audience.  Although we were in the back, we still felt the energy of the band!  When they started playing their first set, I swear---everyone started getting into the groove!  
Even my dad, who never really dances, started jiving and snapping along to the beat!  

Although some may say that this venue is TOO intimate, I know I loved it!  I enjoyed being in close proximity with strangers because after about 5 minutes, it seemed as if we all became friends!  We would go back in a heartbeat!  Definitely worth the $12!

Suggestions: bring your own water, it gets kind of hot & sweaty inside due to the crowd and be prepared to have a good time!
Good food fast.  A bit pricey, but it is the Quarter.  Friendly staff, kinda off the beaten path.

They need to use ube ice cream on their halo halo and not vanilla.  They need to use fresh tapioca to use in their sago & gulaman because those hard balls were disgusting in my drink. It should be soft and not old.

Best complete meal of my life. The whole meal was lovely (my best complement for food). My boyfriend ordered from the prix fixe menu and I ordered from the a la carte. He got the turtle soup, pecan crusted drum, and bread pudding. I got the fried green tomato stack and steak. The turtle soup was just so good, it was comforting and delicious. The drum was wonderful and flakey. The sides of the fish were hands down the best item with the crawfish and nuts adding a meaty depth, and the sauce was a light lemon perfection.  My green tomato stack was a lovely array of flavors. I don't eat shrimp due to an unfortunate incident when I was a kid but I ate these without hesitation. My steak was nice (though definite not the best dish on the menu) the sides were so good though-the potatoes and charred carrots were perfect. The bread pudding was good and a nice way to end the meal, the pecan topping was the best part. Definitely a must for dinner while in New Orleans. (My first five star dinner)

The room was ready and cleaned nicely when we arrived.  Room was large and well supplied except short on TP.  Had to request more.  Parking fee is too high but normal for NO.  So much noise from the street we had difficulty getting to sleep.  And we were on the 17th floor.  Noise subsided about 
1:30 a.m. Bell service was excellent.

I showed up hungry and left incredibly happy! The bread is amazing. I had the mussels appetizer and it was really good! I took a risk and tried the egg lemon dish and boy was it good!! I cant wait to go back and try the cheese appetizer that they light on fire!!!

Had a great experience staying here for 3 nights for a work convention. Rooms were nice and the hotel is in a good location. The only downfall is that the hotel is huge so it was a long walk from my room to get to the convention center
Don't be cheated - this is an American restaurant. Too much salad dressing on every dish. The only good thing is the uni.

This is the best burger place!! You can have eat the peanuts while you wait. And if you want to eat the peanuts with the shells on, they won't even kick you out! There's so many toppings like mushrooms, catchup, and cheese. It's to die for. My mouth is watering just thinking about this place. If you run into a guy wearing spandex, be weary.

I am obsessed with this place! I have been to a lot of nail salons in the entire stl area and have not found one that I am dying to go back to, until now! Jeremy did an amazing job on my ombré powder dip and I cannot wait to go back for a pedicure!! I would put my reputation on this place, and that's coming from a salon snob!
When visiting New Orleans stop by Mena's Palace for some great food, delicious coffee. The prices are reasonable & the waitress are very friendly.

My dining companion and I ended up at Three Muses by complete accident. We've made it our mission to eat at some of the more "acclaimed" restaurants throughout the city, and after trying to get into Adolfo's and failing miserably, we walked down the street to Three Muses.

It was unusually busy for a Saturday night. It was nearly nine and every place was packed. We walked up to the door and explained to Candice, the nice woman working the door, that we didn't have reservations and that we had just been turned away from our "Plan A". She was completely understanding, and told us that they were fully booked, but she would see what she could do. Well, Candice totally came through and she lead us to a small but perfect table right in the front.

Looking over the menu, I was pretty excited. Three Muses is a "small plates" place, so that means sharing. I'm usually not a huge "hey let's share" kind of person, when it comes to food that isn't sushi, but I could get into this.

We decided on the lamb sliders, the fries topped with feta, the shells and cheese that comes topped with bacon and the steak and cake, which is a sliced steak on top of crab cake.

All of the food was amazing. I think that my favorite had to be the shells and cheese. I found the Three Muses version to be a nice twist on a childhood classic and the bacon was a nice touch. My second favorite was the lamb sliders that had a lot of flavor and of which I could have definitely eaten another order.

There was live music playing while we ate, and while I thought that the band was a little loud for the small space, I found that it was a nice touch.

I had a great time here and I will definitely be dining at Three Muses again.

Was that Mexican??? I think not.  No taste, no spice, and not even close to Mexican!!!
  My dogs would not eat it, when I could not get it down.

Actually really clean, affordable last minute rates if any rooms are available. Great location, confusing valet.
Rooms very modern, very clean even the bathrooms were stylish. The bar is trendy and convenient but they only ever have one person working and a lot of large group's coming through so check in can be annoying but staff is friendly.
 Very sensitive smoke alarms, I only did one dab and the darn thing was going off for like an hour. Such a hassle lol the girl at the front seat was kinda annoyed with me. They offer bliss spa brand beauty bathroom essentials which I think is super awesome

I've been to Kehoe a few times for repairs and I have never been unsatisfied.  They forgot to put my radiator cap on and it resulted in me spending more money but Thomas said that he'd reimburse me and give me an oil change on the house because of the mistake.  I was not expecting that, especially since I lost my receipt.  It was an honest mistake - we're all human - but the way one handles the mistakes is what counts and Kehoe came out golden.  I will definitely continue to have Kehoe service my car.  Thanks to Thomas and all at Kehoe.  It is refreshing to find a mechanic with outstanding customer service (and they know what they are doing).  :D

Some of the reviews here complain about quality going down over time.  I disagree.  We were there 11/28/14, and it was the best we've ever had there.  Maybe they have been reading Yelp and accepting constructive criticism.  I noticed some new items, and some details done a little differently and better than in the past.

Service has always been excellent.  I have never been disappointed.  They are probably my favorite dining experience in Tucson.

If you're in the area and like steak, go here. I was in Hyde Park and needed a place to eat for lunch. Happened upon this gem. I got the Peter Lawford (Petite Filet), and my partner got Frank Sinatra (Shrimp Cocktail). The filet was delicious. One of the best I've had. The portions were filling but small.  The sweet ending desserts were similar to that of Seasons 52, I believe, the cakes shots. Those were pretty good. 

Overall, definitely worth the time. Few people were inside for lunch (most were outside), so the noise level was pretty low. The price is a bit high, but if you're in the area, might as well.

We pretty much had one of everything on the menu.  Yes, we were fat.  Really fat.

We each had a signature drink. I cannot remember the name of mine but it had raspberry in it and it was amazing (sorry, not very helpful).

Everything was good.  Really.  There was no dog on the pile but that would only give it 3-stars for me.  So, why 5? Oyster Sliders, HOT Chicken and Banana pudding.  Truly, these things were perfect.  They are both fried dishes and fried to perfection with tastes that complimented and stood up to the frying.  I think the Hot Chicken may have been the best thing I have had in months.  Now, I have not been to Nashville, so I do not know about authentic Hot Chicken but this was amazing. The banana pudding won over the table, even people that said they do not like banana pudding.

If you need other good choices, the table also really liked the eggs&ham, The Board, fried lobster tail and mac n cheese.

The place is small but nice and the service was great.  We are so happy to have a place to go pre-World Cafe Live.
They do a good job, doesn't take forever, prices are reasonable, and they have a comfortable waiting room with wi-fi.

After the bartender told us he made awesome margaritas, we trusted him with our request for two. Watched him pour Montezuma triple sec and lime juice in a cup and fill the rest with soda. The result was something like sour dog piss and tequila. The salted rim was the only good part. Then he charged $8 when the menu said $6. Won't be coming here again.

Terrible service! :-( The waiters couldn't recommend anything from the menu. Just pick a number he said... ok.  My vegetarian friend came with me and they served her fried Toffu with fish flakes. When we told him he was trying to convince us those were not fish flakes... Really?  No greeting, no refills,  The food is ok nothing spectacular. The only thing is that they decorate their plates very nicely.  Drawings of a bambu tree with the soy sauce. But they need better Service!!!

Lots of really cool posters!  For some reason, it's not very well advertised so people aren't aware of them, but the Anderson Design Group is HUGE!! IMO, if you're a tourist in Nashville, this should be your first stop.  And if you live in Nashville (and love Nashville), well, this is your place!!  Definitely check out their website!  They do design logos and posters for all kinds of businesses and cities!  Really great stuff!

We had the most incredible experience at The Hub when shopping for a first bike for my 2yo.  Ron, the gentleman who worked with us, was so informative and patient and kind to our little guy and us.  He took the time to figure out what bike fit our needs the best and even custom cut down the bike seat we ended up getting because my kiddo is a shorty. We went in looking for one thing and after assessing our situation he steered us in a different direction which resulted in a better bike that we will get many more years of use out of.  He was so patient, and even fitted a helmet for a finicky 2yo.  Big thanks to The Hub, we will never ever ever get a bike anywhere else! I thought they would only have adult things but taking such a young guy and having the individualized attention resulted in a safer custom fit bike and a perfectly fitting helmet.  We would not have got that at any of the other big box stores.

I'll give it to them, papa Murphy's is one of my favorite places for pizza and their cookie dough is phenomenal. Take and bake pizza are a genius idea and normally I have five star service. However, I visited this location tonight to pick up my order and was left waiting at the pick up window for over six minutes. Meanwhile, I watched the staff, on their cell phones, genuinely ignore me at the window. I tried to get their attention but clearly they were preoccupied. I then parked my car to head inside and saw one of the workers clearly FaceTiming someone while the other worker hurried to look busy as I walked in. My pick up order was fast but I simply could not believe I was ignored at the pickup window. It's simply distasteful customer service and a reason to visit another location.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!! Best Pizza Joint Ever! My family was traveling back from spring break and we were looking for exactly this! We ordered 3 small pizzas (due to dietary requirements) and the four of us finished it all with full tummies! This place had it all: great pizza, great prices, great service, & who doesn't love supporting a local business! It was a little out off the interstate, but well worth the extra 2-3 min to get there!!

Saturday, Memorial Day weekend. A beautiful day to take a drive to find something to eat. Took myself to Cherry Hill to go to The Turning Point restaurant to get a late breakfast. I sat down outside to receive the nice weather that we got blessed with and a good meal. Emily was awesome with serving the food and drink I ordered. The food came out in a good time and it tasted great. And anyone who knows me know that if I get any food is bland, they will hear from me face to face. I really don't like to season my own food. I find it as an insult to person who cooked the food. So when I get freshly made food, I will get it made the right way. If it isn't made right the first time, the restaurant only get one more shot to get it right. I'm happy to say The Turning Point got it right on how I want my breakfast. Kudos Turning Point, kudos!

This place is great. All the bartenders are always friendly. Prices aren't NY but they aren't NO. They are open late which is a blessing in UPT. I can't complain about their slice either. Plus if you're a disheartened giants fan this is a good place to catch a game.
This place is amazing! Delicious mimosa's, food and pastries! Best place for breakfast in Tuscon, and you can join waitlist online! Try it, you won't be disappointed!

I had my first Pho experience circa 2005 in Saigon when it was truly a hole in the wall off Lafayette Rd. We ate there a few more times, before moving away in 2007. 

A few states, many bowls of Pho and what felt like a lifetime later, we found ourselves in Saigon's current and expanded location one gloomy Sunday night, driven there by a mix of nostalgia and curiosity while in town taking care of some business. 

I wasn't sure if it's still owned by the same family but upon entrance I recognized the Vietnamese guy who used to run the dining room all by himself and he greeted us as if he recognized us too. A few sentences later I believed he did remember us from almost 7 years ago. As much as I like to think me and my guy make an unforgettable couple, it's more likely he is uncannily unforgetful.

I wasn't in the mood for an 8-dollar bowl of Pho (it costs around $6-7 in our hood) so we went with Bun Bi Thit Nuong (#90). It had the succulent Vietnamese grilled pork we love (in fact some of the best) though I could do without the shredded pork. For spring rolls, you can't go wrong with the same grilled pork and the clear dipping sauce they serve (much better than the thick peanut sauce served in some Vietnamese places IMO). Fried fish cakes were not bad, especially drown in the sweet chili sauce. 

To my disappointment, they don't serve salted plum drink so I got a bubble tea in Thai tea flavor. I wish I had ordered one made from fresh fruits since it wasn't the brewed Thai tea in liquid form I expected but a mountain of blended ice and Thai tea flavored powders (hate those). The tapioca balls weren't good either. 

On that Sunday night, the former Bob Evans dining room was half full but less than one third of the patrons were Asians, quite a change from years ago at the old location, if memory serves me right. I guess Vietnamese food has finally caught on in Indy.

Still closed on Tuesdays after all these years.
This place is terrible. The bagel was not edible, which is hard to believe considering I think it came from a store bought package similar to a Thomas Bagel or something. Not worth it, don't go.
Surprisingly good pub food at a casino. Delicious fresh and inexpensive.  Very good, generous portions.  Only complaint-not many vegetarian options. Recommend this place for burgers and pizzas.
Love the food here. Get the same thing every time, Summer roles, pad see eww and chicken Penang.  Best Thai in town
Average food, great location, small portion sizes and slightly higher prices. Move on peeps.

We have been here for lunch about 5 times and have been pleasantly surprised every time.  First of all they share the same kitchen as Delicia and if you haven't been there put it on your bucket list.  The decor is simple and fun, the food is what really matters.

FOOD:
We got the guacamole today as a starter, it was very fresh and a little spicy (it is the same delicious guac as Delicia).  The first time I visited some recommended the Pork Milanesa Cemita and I have never ordered anything else.  It is basically a Mexican version of the fried tenderloin with a egg and other goodies.  My wife has ordered every taco and she loves each one.

Note:  Take a look at the pictures of the menu because items on the lunch menu are not on the dinner menu and vice versa.

Father's Day Brunch, this place was close to my hotel and not too packed for a big holiday.

Waitress at front asked me how she could help instead of how many in my party. Before I could ask her what else they offer besides food and drinks, her coworker saved her and took over. Quickly seated, ordered Haphazard drink from cocktail menu. 

Had shrimp & cheese grits. The grits are really cheesy, so much so you can't eat them without cutting the strings of cheese. The shrimp, sausage, onion gravy mix that it's covered in is VERY tasty and flavorful. The grits are bland but it works with the shrimp.

I liked it and will return. Service was good too.

This place needs to get it together! Ice cream machine is always "out of order" has happened at least 5 times. The worse part is getting stuck in the drive through just to find out the machine is broken again. Not going here again !

Mostly kids working that don't care about service. We waited over an hour for our pizza.  When we finally got it the pizza and potatoes were cold. The place is loud and full of drunks on a Saturday night. If you want to get drunk and eat cold pizza its a great place. I won't go back.

Love this place! Great Chinese and Japanese takeout.

It is consistent & reasonably priced.

Food quality very good and fast for take out.

Great experience to lighten up a cold-rainy day in New Orleans. 

We came in on a Saturday afternoon and were seated in less than 5 minutes. Our server was kind and attentive and the waitstaff were accommodating. 

I ordered the crawfish beignet with jalapeno aoili and a side caesar salad. The beignet was hot oozing with gooey cheese and warmed up my day. To drink decided to mix things up with an adult Arnold Palmer. I asked for regular jack instead of vodka but to my surprise, honey jack was added which made it my new favorite drink. 

The establishment itself has a pretty cozy fit which mainly allows for smaller parties in the front. I did not make it upstairs but there is upstairs seating. 

All in all this hidden gem is a great place to experience what New Orleans has to offer.

A must while in Nashville! Get there early to avoid long line! Staff very friendly. Food was delicious! I got the old fashioned pancakes with a side of bacon and eggs. My fiancé got the apple walnut pancakes with a side of hash browns and bacon. All very delicious and it's worth the wait if there's a line!!! Highly recommend and will return when in Nashville again!

So far the best tasting pizza place Ive found since I moved to AZ. The flavor, the cheese, the meats, all complement one another well. The crust is good also, however I was wondering if this place offers a thin crust because I would definitely like to try that out. I'm from CA and yea I'm a Straw Hat fan with their thinner crust but the similarities overall made me happier then a fat kid at hometown buffet in the dessert section  jk.  But I would highly recommend this place
They provided a room to me very late at night after my booked hotel bumped me. Mohamed at the front desk was very friendly
Everything was delicious!!  Generous servings!  Delicious homemade pasta. Anthony took great care of us!!
Best guac ever!!! Love this spot I come here all the time. Really good happy hour too.

Even though UF isn't where I went to school, I do live in Florida and see zero problem with a Florida business supporting a Florida university. In fact, Gators is one of the Tampa Bay area's classic beach spots everyone should visit. Sure, it's a little touristy at times, but this is the nation's tourism capital after all so what do we expect!? The bottom line is that the food at Gators is far better than the typical beach bar/restaurant and you can't beat the location/view/access. It's a great place to go just for drinks too since they have good live bands and other events on a regular basis.
Solid 4 start. Amazing bread. Good concept. Fast and tasty. I will go again. Their bowl is quite filling. Chicken is very tasty.

The ambiance was fantastic, the food was delicious. The service was great. The reason for the 4 stars is because, when they served the appetizers they did not give us plates or serving spoons. I thought maybe this was an oversight but we ordered 3 appetizers and they did it all 3 times. Please pay attention to this.

Love this place! When I moved here I tried 4 salons downtown where I live and had terrible experiences. This place has the happiest most excited staff, great prices and most importantly quality nails. My first full set lasted a little over a month and they were long coffin shaped and I'm hard on my nails which is the worst combination. They're very up to date with what's popular (foil designs, chrome, even marble!) would highly recommend especially Julie and Tom!

Have you ever gone to a restaurant, place your order and wonder whether or not what you just did was a good idea? Well, it happened to me at this place. Actually, it was after I used the restroom that I became concerned and questioned my decision.

Before I go further I should explain I (obviously) survived to tell the tale. :)

See, this used to be a Church's Fried Chicken restaurant. Therefore you can expect it to be a little run down. However, it appears they kept the old greasy everything for posterity. The walls and floors are covered in grease. There's grease on the plumbing at the urinal for the love of all that's holy. My guess is they moved in and didn't even clean the place.  How it passes inspection is beyond me. As they say, if you want to know how clean a restaurant is look at the bathroom. 

The people were very nice.  I showed up about 20 minutes before closing and ordered food to go. I learned something in that they premake their fried rice. I suppose they add the meat or whatever to it as they go, but they were all out so I had to go with white rice. Of course, it was bland as you'd expect.

I ordered sesame chicken but there was hardly any sauce and no sesame.  So, it was deep fried chicken nuggets with a little sauce. The portion was large so you get a fair amount at a decent price. The flavor of the sauce was OK but the meat itself is questionable. Every restaurant buys breaded nuggets so this place isn't unique. The chicken, though, didn't seem right. It was cooked thoroughly but seemed off like it was perhaps pressed something or the other. 

The crab Rangoon that came with it was inedible. They tasted of old grease, we're dry as a bone and definitely not a good choice. Maybe it's because it was the end of the night, I don't know. But they were horrible. Sorry folks. Skip these mm if you go here.

Perhaps my experience was an anomaly. Others seem to enjoy it. Maybe I've become spoiled or expect too much. I don't think so. A clean restaurant is expected at any cost. This place doesn't even come close. 

Don't take my word on it. Try for yourself. Who knows, it could be the best experience you've had.
Unbelievable food.  Best I've ever had and it's always almost empty.  Sure the ambiance isn't great, but oh the food is so amazing!!
Food was delicious!! The wait staff seemed a little confused but all in all, it was a good experience.

Not bad! I got a burrito with salmon and it was a yummy, salty mix of flavors. Sushi burritos have a collapsability about them that makes eating them a bit more challenging, which I find entertaining. 

The burrito a rather underwhelming size (compared to the giant logs of food you get from regular burrito places) and the flavor of the fish didn't blow me away (compared to the flavors you might experience at a serious sushi place, or an expensive piece you get from a good grocery store). 

It was acceptable and satiating, but it felt like most of my taste bud reactions were coming from how they spiced and/or marinated their ingredients, rather than the freshness of the ingredients themselves. For the $10+ price, which made me feel like I was splurging a bit on an extra-exotic burrito, it didn't feel like I got much more food value than a regular burrito. 

However, I had a really nice server ! It's always interesting when the people are both charismatic and attentive. Their bowls looked larger and more impressive, so I'll see how their bowls are next time!

One of those unexpected local restaurants you always hope to find. Great staff, ambiance and menu. Creative and unusual food combinations (the filet may be the best I've had. ever). The restaurant was full and the rooms are fairly open but surprisingly quiet enough for conversation. We'll be back

Pet Paradise took such good care of our baby. She came home exhausted, so I know she was occupied while we were gone. Everyone there from the manager to the receptionist knew her name, and genuinely cared about her. We'd never left her with anyone but family before, and they helped to ease our and our furbaby's anxiety. Our puppy is a picky eater, and they were proactive in using methods to help her eat, even being in the room with her while she ate. We will definitely be using Pet Paradise in the future and our baby can't wait to visit her friends there soon! I can't recommend them enough!

We found this place by searching yelp and it definitely is a good place to eat. We come here for breakfast all the time. We either eat in or get it to go. They always have specials. We've been here for dinner once and it was delicious! I got stuffed tilapia with crab meat and it was amazing! And only $10.50! The food always comes quickly so you're never waiting long for your food which is great when you go in there starving! It's decent pricing. Also, nothing too crazy here with the menus so Iif you're looking for a good home cooked meal This is definitely the place to go. All around its a good place! Definitely check it out!

A wonderful find thanks to yelp! I was on the pier the day before and wouldn't have thought to go up to the tasting room. However, I'm glad that I did! The views are awesome from the second floor deck and it is a great place to enjoy the views and a glass of wine. 

I had a glass of the Deep Sea Riesling which was sweet and delicious.
Suuuuuuper overpriced.  The kids love it, but they aren't paying $2000 to ride on a tractor and pick vegetables.  This place has become a complete moneypit.

Perfect place to watch the sunset over Philly. R2L is on the 37th floor with 2 sides of glass windows. There view is on West Philly where you can see the Schuylkill River, Penn/Drexel and University City and beyond. On the south side, you can see the Delaware River and beyond.

We only had drinks there so not much to comment on the quality. The beer was cold and was 5 bucks.

Service: the service was great. The server was very polite, had a smile on her face all the time and always catered to photo requests by the patrons. Well done management and staff.

They do live up to their name 'Deviate' by making brews with flavors that departs from the more institutional/traditional beer taste. The night we went, they have beers with flavors like cucumber, chipotle, cinnamon, green peppercorn, raspberry, and coconut. And I'm not talking like just hint of flavor or a mild after taste. Its a quite strong and in your face flavor sip after sip. The more conventional beer drinkers might not like it or find some of the beer taste weird, but it can be fun and you gotta appreciate what they are doing and I think that makes them unique and special, and an excellent addition to the list of breweries in the Indy area and certainly worth a try. Definitely the place to visit for the more adventurous beer drinkers.

The staff were very friendly. They serve beer flight which is a great start so you can try most if not all and then decide which you like the best. No food but there were free pretzel sticks and water, and I think they allow order in or even bring your own food.

This is not your typical review for the Children's Museum in the fact that:
1. I have no kids and can't speak to how kids react to the exhibits
2. When I go, I don't take kids and only during after hours adult only events

Yes, back in the day I remember the countless visits to the museum on school field trips and it being large and full or fun and exciting exhibits. Now, like other have mentioned, the exhibits are pretty lack luster and seem not as fascinating and exciting as I remember them being, but this is coming from an adult's view and old memories. 

Why might an Adult might find the museum interesting? 

The Children's Museum has lately been able to land some of the best traveling exhibits, including the Tutankhamun: The Golden King and the Great Pharoahs in 2009 and most recently the China's Terra Cotta Warriors. Plus, they have recently been offering Adult Only after hour events in which the 21+ crowd gets to explore a section of the museum or all of the museum depending upon the event which normally includes a drink and hors d'ouevres. Ticket prices also happen to be more than the regular prices, but you do get to see the exhibits without kids running around. 

Also, if you happen to be a Dale Chihuly fan, you can view his Fireworks of Glass exhibit. I would recommend going down to the bottom level to get an underside view of his work. It is beyond amazing the level of detail and work that went into making this piece.

Parking it is free, but you have to make sure that you come in off of the correct road, Illinois,  to access the parking as it is located off of a one way street and you might find yourself maneuvering side streets to flip around to enter in the correct way.
Bagels are okay a bit expensive but the sandwiches choices are really good!! Sure wish they had gluten free
This local dive would get 5 stars for menu and Sunday football if they didn't let losers smoke cigars inside.

I had a blast! Although I didn't see any gators... since it was winter. We did see a bunch of birds and wild pigs wich was awesome! The swamp was beautiful and was worth seeing. Wished the tour was longer :( also if you do it in winter dress warm!

I was looking for something different for lunch in the Old City area.  Let's say, I should have stuck with my cheesesteak wrap from Gianfrancos!  I found them on Grubhub and it sounded great!  I ordered a buffalo chicken wrap which had a "*" next to it indicating it was a restaurant favorite.  It also came with french fries.  Once you added the tip on, it ended up costing me $14 for delivery.  It arrived in fairly good time, but I am not sure when the french fries were hot, it was long before they arrived here.  They looked like had they been fresh, they would have tasted good, but they were cold and hard.  The wrap itself was so far from what I was hoping for.  When ordering, it gives you the option of hot or mild sauce.  I chose mild.  I cannot imagine what the hot choice was like since the mild made my mouth feel on fire!  It says it contains blue cheese and I requested extra blue cheese.  I got one small 1oz soufle cup, none was inside the wrap as I was anticpating.  This was about enough for 1/2 of 1/2 of the wrap.  I was definitely disappointed!
Definitely worth a short walk from city center to see historic and quaint homes.  Liked the old cobblestone street!

We went there after making a reservation for two. The menu does not have a lot of variety and the food is mediocre. I had high hopes but it did not meet my expectations. Service was good overall along with good ambiance.

I wish I could exaggerate the quality of food but I cannot the food tasted fresh and came out very swiftly I kept staring at the table next to me with this gigantic plate of pancakes... The waitress quickly informed me that most of their food is larger than normal.... The wait wasn't long they get very busy but handle it well if your impatient you can join the wait less on Yelp or call in advance

This food is dam good.  The sliders were amazing. I recommend getting the brown bag special (two sliders, fries and homemade soda). If you have a small appetite consider sharing.  Don't let the size of the sliders fool you they are filling. And don't you dare go without getting a donut.  They're the best donuts in New Orleans.

I used to travel to Japan 4 times a year and really love all the different styles of Japanese food. Sadly Reno is know for all you can eat sushi which  just based on economics drives down quality.  Japan is all about quality over quantity,  presentation and experience rule the day.   Enter Kauboi Izakaya - it's pushing the envelope in Reno's growing food scene.  

I love the creativity of the food, the flavors were spot on and the service was top notch.   We had the Poke which was the best in Reno IMO.  Sure it's a small portion for the money but again quality over quantity.  The spicy shrimp gyoza was amazing as was the pork Raman.  The Giant Squid was giant and squid, it was good but I reminded again that I am not a fan of squid regardless of how It's prepared.  
The bottom line is this is a great restaurant that is pushing the creative boundaries in Reno. It's not your cheapest option in town and it shouldn't be.  (In Japan it would have 3x the price.   ). My only suggestion is they stock the bar with different Japanese Shochu's and it will be like I am back in Tokyo.

Ice creamery outside of the Cobb theatres at Countryside.  I'm giving this a 3 because the girl who tended, Sarah, us was good but she was left to flounder due to poor scheduling. She was in the weeds. I felt bad for her. 

The ice cream was good, especially when she blended in the toppings I requested. But there was a line building up and there was only one girl, a new menu and she was new there. She kept her cool and di just fine with us.

I think capital beer is pretty ok to me. I dont have any complaints other than maybe price but that doesnt really bother me that much with this place. Ill go here once a week or anytime im craving sushi its always pretty good. Chinese food is standard. Great beer selection take your pick.

Wait here for lunch during the week Between Christmas and New Years with 6 elementary age Girl Scouts (!!).  Nonwait, great service and the server named Nico was very patient with the 6 Scouts... answering questions, bringing extra sauces, etc.  all 6 Scouts had ice cream and proclaimed Baileys Range to be their new favorite place.  This moms burger was delicious too.  Thx!
Thanks, Dan, for solving our issues. Now I can say I'm satisfied with the final outcome.
We got takeout from there tonight - a small pizza and some sides. We picked up the order and brought it home. The pizza was still piping hot and very tasty. Everything was great!
