It took me a few classes to get with an instructor I jived with but finally found my instant faves in Rachel and Kaycie. I took classes with Rachel at least 3 times a week and there was literally NEVER a dull moment. I love this place, I have recommended it to multiple people, and can't wait to start classes again next week! Also... never did I think that I would become addicted to $16 toe socks but I have a new obsession! Choosing my fave grippy socks that I bought at IMX, they have a great selection too! Do yourself a favor and at least try out a week, you will not be disappointed.

Room smelled of mold. Saw two cockroaches during my week stay.the room service menu was limited but the Cobb salad was excellent. The location is good. Walking distance to market street an bars. the staff was friendly and professional but I don't think I will return. Philly has great hotels this is not one.

Large outside venue with full coffee and alcohol bar. I noticed others eating food but we just ordered beignets. Beignets were good (not as good as Cafe du Monde) they are $3.99 for 3. Live musicians playing and was pretty packed every time we walked by. Nice place, we'll return!

Very cool restaurant with an enclosed courtyard. Our two waiters were very attentive the entire meal, which I would definitely expect dining at a restaurant like Muriel's.  The escargot was fantastic and the soft shell crab was delicious. We had a large group and were lucky to get same day reservations. (I would definitely recommend reserving a table a few days in advance.)
Lots of space and I love the song selection.  I can only speak to downstairs which is only country.  Rap music upstairs.

Sending props out to Ben, Rachel, Suzanne and the chefs that made last nights meal amazing! "Sunday Supper" menu items, whiskey offerings and service were outstanding. The portions were generous and the ambiance = F.U.N.!!! Be sure to make a resee and go hungry! 
 (Oh, and you are welcome!!!! )

I'm still trying to convince my mom to bring us back for dinner. We went here for lunch, it was pretty busy but they had room for us. The space is historic and seems like a cross between a 20s movie theatre/20s soda fountain/40s club. I had the Sunday special which was chicken salad on a fresh croissant and it was DE-LICIOUS - and I'm not even a huge fan of chicken salad. We got ice cream after that and it was awesome. Big sundaes that were definitely worth the price. 
The whole place was worth way more than the price. The meals were under $10. It was awesome. Me and the three kids meals + big ice cream desserts came out to $38 - not including tip.
My only complaints are that they don't have any burgers (they definitely seem like they should) and the service was a little slow. I think the service was just my waitress, however, because she seemed a little out of it.
Really, seriously, get food here.

Used to be a go to for me. Tried to hit this one in the Harrah's Casino and it's the worst ever. Taking an hour to get food and getting it wrong almost each time. You'd do better to go to a hotdog vendor on the street. Sad times for this place. The franchise as a whole has fallen far from grace but this one takes the cake.

I live close enough to walk to St Pete Bagel, which is good because parking is limited. I go on the weekends for a cup of coffee and something yummy, like a fresh bagel and house-made cream cheese. Bacon and garlic-chive are my two favorite flavors. If you want something sweet, the peach fritters are out of this world. The donuts are beautifully made; it's hard to decide on just one. Bonus deal, you get a free donut with the purchase of a latte. They recently started serving iced chai lattes, so I see a lot of free donuts in my future! Stopping in for lunch? I recommend the Cuban sandwich. But I don't think you can go wrong with anything on the menu. They are always busy, but the line usually moves pretty quick. It helps if you know what you want when you get to the counter. There are a few tables inside and outside, if you want to sit and eat. The staff is always friendly and it's obvious they get joy from seeing people enjoy the food. Visit St Pete Bagel Co and your mouth will thank you. Happy eating!

We went on Sunday noon time.  It was pretty packed, waited about 20 mins they accidentally lost our names so quickly gave us the next available table.  Overall service was great!  Food overall was really good not too greasy which most diners foods are.  Love the waffles and potato tots!  Although fried chicken was not crispy enough!

Went on a Friday night and man was it busy! We waited at least 45 min for our food and when it came it was mediocre at best. I ordered the GF crust pizza and hubby ordered a buffalo chicken sandwich which he said was solid. Server was friendly just seemed super understaffed for how crowded they were...

ANOTHER location of Bing's boba loated in the Lee Lee's market plaza

during summer shaved ice was ONLY $1.75 for the small!!
--Small lychee flavored shaved ice: Yummy and refreshing in the 100plus degree weather

They have a large selection of toppings for boba drinks that I'll have to come back to try

NOTE: Stamp card for regulars!

Kien Giang is pretty good (but not as good as Miss Saigon).  A good sign that its a  good Vietnamese restaurant is that its always packed solid.  Their Pho is a bit salty and has more taste than Miss Saigon (its better).  But I would say that just about everything else on the menu, though cheaper, is not as good as it is at Miss Saigon.  Their rice paper rolls and bubble tea (powder based) were huge disappointments.  The rolls' pork tasted off and you have to make a special request for the peanut sauce. And my vermicelli dish was just mediocre.

It drives me crazy that they don't take credit cards because I never carry cash on me and its a pain in the butt to have to make a special trip to the next door atm at Kroger's.

The staff are not very friendly (except for this one guy) and definitely not attentive.  It took them 5 minutes to get a menu to us, another 5-7 minutes to take our order, another 15 minutes to get our drinks and another 10 minutes to bring out the orders.  SO SLOW!!!  And it took the guy forever to come back with the peanut sauce which I asked for for the rolls and for a fork and they were so absent minded that when we went to pay for the bill, she took the money then started cleaning tables before she gave us back our change!

Its not fancy or anything, but the food is authentic, delicious and cheap.  Sometimes I wonder how clean the kitchen or backrooms are, but whatever...

Bottom line: food is mediocre/ pretty good but cheap, service is slow, staff is inattentive. Its too packed and noisy, which I think is the reason for the slow and inattentive service.  Attracts a lot of local Vietnamese and poor college students, but  for an extra 2 bucks, I'd rather go to Miss Saigon and have a close to perfect experience.
OMG!! If your anywhere near New Orleans, you CANNOT MISS THIS PLACE!! Custom flavors that are always changing served by enthusiastic employees. Worth the short trip from the Quarter.

I have worked with Yong's Alteration in the past and she is very professional and her customer service is amazing.  I don't understand why people would write a single negative review about her business.  This place, hands down, is one of the best alteration shops in Indianapolis!
Excellent selection of meat and great quality. A little pricey but you get what you pay for here. The southwest tritip sandwich is amazing and they have a wide variety of rare meats.

Stir fry and fruit are amazing. One of Bala's gems but definitely need to count calories when eating here. One plus is the charging lockers for cell phones. One downside is the noise. This is one very noisy spot and not optimal for dining in. The food is fresh, the staff are nice and I love the customer experience. Fruit and salads are good, a little pricey but good for kids. 

A favorite indeed.

Good unit for the price and location, but there were some serious problems that were ignored.

First, I was surprised at how difficult it was to coordinate getting Comcast installed. The property managers seemed to know nothing about where and how the hookups were needed. This seems like a really common task but it took more than two weeks before I had internet access.

The door bells weren't properly labelled which confused everyone. Not a big deal, but occasionally I would get strangers ring for me because they weren't sure which button to press.

The power outlets were placed in awkward positions and wires from the fridge were hanging from hooks in the wall. One outlet was painted over multiple times and completely unusable. 

There was an incident where the fire alarm went off in our building and we were never given any explanation whatsoever after it stopped. 

There was evidence of water damage in my unit from the start, and one day after heavy rain a hole opened in the ceiling and flooded my bathroom. I was never given an explanation and they never repaired that hole even after they tore it open further to inspect damages.

Ordered village burger and it was ok at best. Didn't blow my mind for a highly rated burger. Drinks were decent but normal priced for center city. Wouldn't go back, but overall wasn't too bad. Shake shack is close by! P.s. our waitress wasn't impressed by our shamrocks attire...lighten up!

Best people to work with. You will love their customer service.
These are just straight up, good honest people.
You won't find better.

Tiny little place off of williams, nearly right behind French Press Coffeehouse.   They offer some sandwiches and baked goods as well as some groceries.  Let's just say I've been to Norma's 3 times the past month since I've re-discovered it.  The cuban sandwich is worthy of a return, yes. But what keeps me coming back is the flan!!! Oh my god, it's absolutely delicious! Have not tried many other of the baked goods but I am looking forward to doing so in the future.. If I can stray away from the flan, that is.The staff is always VERY friendly when you walk in there, and every time I've been, there are locals hanging out on the porch people watching or enjoying a snack. Very reasonably priced.

Went there for lunch and got the ribs, baked beans and fried corn on the cob. The meat was tender and fall off the bone juicy and delicious. The baked beans excellent. The fried corn was good but I prefer boiled corn. The staff was friendly and the service fast. I'll be back to try more items.

The wait is long and it is crowded, even late at night. I came in past 8 and waited over 30 minutes for a seat when it was cold and windy out. I would give it 5 stars if not for that seat! The Rock Crab is worth it, however; fresh and sweet with Caesar salad and a cup of hot lobster bisque on the side. The crab cakes are OK and so was the shrimp and scallop pasta.  The server was friendly, fast and helpful. She substituted the regular soup for  the bisque! 5 stars for her! A little pricey but a nice place for fresh, simple seafood fare.

UPDATE as of 2/28/11: CLOSED permanently! 

Yum! Definitely try this place and you will not be disappointed!!!! It's also super fun to sit outside on their large patio and listen to the waves crash as you sip on a nice pitcher of cold beer and bite into your delicious pizza!!

My girlfriend and I stopped there around 11PM on a Saturday night. The place was completely dead and we were the only people in the restaurant, so we figured we would get a better than average meal and service, based on many of the yelp reviewers.

The server was somewhat prompt and friendly, quickly taking our drink and meal orders. We were pretty hungry, so we ordered the hummus right away. It came out with some warm pita bread and a bunch of raw vegetables; the presentation left a lot to be desired, but it was decent.

Then came our main course. We ordered a pepperoni pizza with roasted garlic to share; in addition I ordered a chicken Parmesan sandwich, and my girlfriend ordered the Cajun chicken pasta. And this is where positive remarks can no longer describe the experience.

The pizza had a Chuck E Cheese cardboard crust that was rather unpleasant to eat. The sauce could have been good but there was so little of it, we couldn't really tell you. Pepperoni was OK, but the roasted garlic was cold (probably from a jar), tasteless, and piled high. Absolutely disgusting and unacceptable for almost $20. 

Next, I tried the sandwich, which was not a chicken Parmesan sandwich at all, but rather some grilled chicken from the freezer section chopped up into squares on a giant French roll. Again, there was almost no marinara sauce and cheese was scarce. Another big disappointment.

Finally comes the Cajun chicken pasta. I only tried a bite of the strange substance, which appeared to be comprised of the same chicken from the sandwich, an attempt at Alfredo sauce, red onions, and pickled jalepenos. It looked like something that comes out of your body, rather than something you put into it. The almost room temperature, overcooked pasta and overwhelming taste of raw onions soured my palette enough to get the check and head out ASAP.

What really put the final nail in the coffin, however, was the fact that my girlfriend became sick for two days after eating there, spending a good portion of our vacation in the bathroom. I would not recommend this place to anyone who values good food or sanitation.
Excellent class variety and instruction. Great location! Really really friendly atmosphere. So glad I got a membership. One of the best things I've done for myself this year. :)

This is like the IKEA of baby stores, except it's pricy.  I cannot imagine there's a baby item out there that they do not have either in the store or online.  

It can be really overwhelming for a first time mom, which is why the have trained "personal concierges" who will walk the store with you helping you register for the essentials.  All of the people on the floor really know their stuff and can provide help, too.

The only reason I cannot give five stars is that everything is so expensive and there do not appear to be a lot of sales.

A good BBQ spot at an affordable price on Street Rd.  My wife and I decided to give this place a try after reading the rave reviews.  A few things to keep in mind before trying this restaurant out.  The restaurant is in the Best Western hotel, not even in the front, you need to awkwardly head to the back of the joint to find the place.  At first glance it looks like a little dive bar.  We visited at 8:30PM on a Saturday night so our experience may have been out of the norm.  We actually missed the turn because the sign is so small it's easy to miss.  Worse, if you miss the turn you need to drive at least a half mile if not further to turn around (if you're headed towards Feasterville-Trevose that is).  

We were greeted by Julie.  Our first thought as we watched her run both the bar and attend to the floor was, seriously?  This place with such great reviews is being run by one person?  Julie is actually a true gem, personable and went out of her way to get everyone's name that comes into the place.  If you do meet her ask about her trip to Chile but wait until after you've eaten already ;)

As for the food.  I really wanted to give this place 5 stars however there were just too many things that went wrong.  Keep in mind, we showed up 30 minutes before the kitchen closes so our experience may be different from others.  I will say, the coffee rubbed brisket was delicious!  My wife got the Kielbasa sandwich however unfortunately it was cold and just didn't look palatable.  We ordered the Pulled Pork spring rolls as an appetizer.  Unfortunately we only received 2 small rolls and they were cold on the inside.  The sides were good but not great although the hush puppies were also cold on the inside.  Like I said our timing may have been the biggest influencer there.  The portions of the meal were very fair.  I saw some reviews about the portions being small but the brisket was about as much as any healthy person would want in any one sitting.  

The service wasn't bad, Julie was very welcoming and did a good job being she was running things by herself but if the management is reading this having another employee would help give the place a more favorable appearance.  With all this said the brisket was good enough that I'd come back again but next time I'll try to come when the food probably hasn't been sitting out too long.  One last note I didn't try the ribs because to this day I haven't had better ribs than Chicken Holiday which is in Langhorne/Levittown near the Oxford Valley Mall.  I'll try these ribs at some point and hopefully will revise my rating upwards, overall the place is worth a try at the least.
We had fun.  First timers and an early Valentine's gift . The guys there are very patient & knowledgeable. Had the best time
Four stars for atmosphere, groove, great service, and Benton bacon.  Burger is very good.  Not the very best, but fresh bun, incredible bacon, and well cooked.  Big thumbs up.

I don't get all the good reviews!?? Everything was way over priced. Waiters snobby. Atmosphere....not casual. Everyone was dressy. The gumbo I got was meh. Shrimp and grits was ok. Nothing great though. Oh and the only refill we got was our water. Coke is in a bottle so I guess I should've expected no refills but on tea? Wasted $80. There are way better places to eat.

Food was sub par. Bland and boring. When we were going to send an item back  the waitress was argumentative and said that that's how it's supposed to taste. If you're going for flavorless  they hit the nail on the head. Was not happy with our overall experience. Would not recommend, there are much better options in Philadelphia
Whenever I visit my friend is S. Phila I go here. I always go for the Lemon. Then I leave my friends house and go back for seconds.

I love this place! Their rice bowl is my favorite, although they have a lot of other delicious foods. The owner is so nice and makes me feel welcomed every time I come to dine in. I would recommend this place to those who want good food and excellent customer service!

Like Adam L., I lived in Chicago as well and there are a lot of really nice old school barber shops that really know how to take care of you. When I moved here I tried to find something similar and I found 4:59 on Yelp. I made an appointment, got my cut and I was really happy with it. The stylist gave me her card and I will likely schedule with her again.

This place reminded me of my place in Chicago and I was really happy with the service. They even did something my place in Chi didn't do... Served Beer!

I met Amin (Bitar's owner). I returned the molded pita bread last week and got refunded for it. He apologize and I did appreciate that, since I always buy my pita bread from Bitar's! 
 I'm so happy that he could also help me do a bakesale at his store so that I can raise money for the Arthritis Foundation. I  and my team "CHEF CHERRYL" will be walking a 5k on Dec 4, 2011 in Metuchen, New Jersey.
If anyone is interested to join my team or want to support me on this great cause please visit my personal webpage:
www.jbrmetuchen.kintera.org/chefcherryl

Thank you for your time reading this!!
Che

Brianna provides the best service to me every night I see her. Kaela is one of the greatest, always look forward to seeing her. I keep coming back just because of them. NOBODY ELSE. Except for Jenna Boyd. I love jenna.

Really cute, cozy place. The chocolate gelato was good and it was nice enough to sit on the back patio. The gal at the counter wasn't exactly friendly, which was awkward. I appreciate the bin for the plastic cups and spoons to recycle them!

George is the BEST! Our dogs have always hated being groomed and get so scared/nervous. But the minute they see George he picks them up and they seem to calm down. They don't mind going here! He does a fantastic job and has a great way with the animals. Can't recommend this place enough!!!

This place was okay. The service was fast and good and the options pretty decent.., but while it tasted good ..hubby and I both had stomach issues after. Maybe just a fluke but I am weary to go back because of it. I would try this place again if in a pinch but it would not be my first choice.

There is usually quite the line for this car wash so I knew it had to be good. Despite the line they get cars in and out pretty quickly and the car wash prices are very reasonable. Plus.... FREE vaccum!!

I've been going here since i was a little kid, I used to go to Dr. Tischler but he retired a few years ago. The place is really nice, I like the fact that there are multiple ones because sometimes I can't make it down to Moorestown as quick as Columbus.

The staff is pretty friendly here, I've never had a problem with them making appointments or anything. I got contacts once and had to change my presciption a few months after that and they took the other boxes I had back.

I go to Dr. Miller now, younger guy, really nice and funny. I don't go anywhere else for my eye appointments, I used to use Wal-Mart but it's not as good as here, or seems as professional.

Worst wal-mart I have ever been to. Unfortuanately I live just up the road and go shopping here once a week. I hate my life afterwards and always have a complaint. Don't expect to price match easily here, the first time I tried it the lady made me show her where I got my coupons. when I reminded her that it was corporate policy that I didn't have to she told me "it's common courtesy to show us" Luckily I had an app on my phone and had to look up all the coupons. The next time I tried to price match the lady didn't know how and I had to guide her though the process, and again I was asked to show my ads.

Also there are dish people who sit in the main walk way and heckle you to buy their product. The girl yesterday yelled at me down the hall that I would save 500 a year in a "tone"  if I swiched over, I turned around and told her that was rude and she cut me off and told me to have a nice day.

I hate this place.

AWFUL!!!!   We requested a table without overhead lighting.   I have a vision disability and need to be careful of lighting.   We explained this to Dorothy the hostess, she took us to a table directly under the overhead lighting.  We again asked if we could be seated at a different table, (the restaurant was not crowded, plenty of tables were available). She snapped back at us  "this is only a restaurant"..... excuse me.... I couldn't believe how rude she was.  She snatched the menus off the table and walked away, we found our own table.  So Cracker Barrel obviously does not make it clear to their employees to 1) the customer is important. 2) It is ILLEGAL to mistreat those with disabilities.  

Go if you wish, but look out for rude hostess --- Dorothy!

Delicious!!!
Although kind of a long distance away from the city, it was well worth it. Located near all the korean businesses is this tofu house. Outside is not that appealing, but indoors looks very korean styled and old fashion. The staff was very attentive and we got our food fairly quick. Since it is known as a tofu house, I of course got the tofu dish. I got the seafood one which had shrimp and a good spice. The side dishes were pretty yummy, it was great with the tofu dish. I probably would come back here for more tofu dishes, although far... 15 minutes or so is paris baguette and h-mart. Highly recommended!

First time here and it was really good food. I had ceviche de pescado and it was very tasty. My son had lomo saltado which is beef strips, onions and tomatoes over French fries. He like this as well. I added all the spicy sauce they brought on the side for the ceviche and nearly burned my tongue out of my mouth but it was amazing. Finally I had lucuma ice cream to soothe the salsa pain and honestly it was the most delicious ice cream I've ever had, no exaggeration. If you try nothing else try this ice cream.
Pretty solid tourist trap type restaurant on the docks. A little bit overpriced for the food quality, but reasonable given the touristy surroundings.

Busy burger joint, juicy well prepared.  Service more than adequate, friendly and professional. Not a beer drinker myself but they looked to have a varied selection. Good place to go if you're craving a burger

Yummo!! Amazing! Delicious! Donut Breakfast Sandwich sooo
Good! French toast amazing! And Steak and Eggs so tasty! You won't be disappointed!

Lawn Love Lawn Care received a four because my initial booking wasn't correct. But Robert who was my Lawn pro, was amazing. He was flexible, friendly, and professional. He even returned to warn me about the pesticides and my pets. He was understanding because of the scheduling mix up and is willing to return next day! I would use lawn love just for their lawn pro! 

The customer service I dealt with the scheduling mix-up was awesome. I felt they tried their hardest to assist me.

The location and building isn't great...but the food was good. They allow smoking on the backside in the screened in porch. They also leave the door open to the inside dining room so the smoke permeates the entire place. But, again, the food was really good. 

If you are in the mood for something a little different and not totally foreign...check this place out.

Kalamata's makes the trip to Green Hills much more bearable. Their fresh take on Mediterranean food always hits the spot. I highly recommend their mixed kebab plate. It's a ton of food with a chicken kebab, filet kebab (SO GOOD), and lamb kafta kebab (also very tasty) over rice or potatoes with pita and Greek salad on the side. Their chicken gyro is also amazing. It's a pita that is stuffed with the good stuff to about the size of a large softball and really inexpensive. Their seafood special of the day is always tasty and a great way to stay on the lighter side of the menu. Their dolmades are also killer. 

It's also BYOB although I've never done it.

All in all, you will most likely leave happy regardless of what you order!
One of our best nights started out here! Make sure to grab a reservation! It's a great place for small plates, good drinks and great music in an intimate setting.

Definitely my go to store for all my pets needs! Every time I go there and I need help finding something, I am always asked if I need help before I ask them for it. The store is clean, organized, and the staff is always friendly and helpful. Can't ask for much more really!

We were really looking forward to what the new lighthouse restaurant was going to look like, considering SB doesn't have many places to eat on the water.  It's nice, but what a misuse of space overlooking the water.  The patio is a joke, luckily the bar does have a view, still not the best use of window space.
The food was OK.  Nothing that I would have to go back to visit.  
What I couldn't understand, is it was FREEZING at the bar, was an overcast day, but no employee cared that the AC was on full blast and as we sat at the bar, three people complained to the female bartender who was a little snobby about the LA bread- great, we're in SB, source local, but she ignored everyone who said it was freezing, so she probably lost at least $60 in tips for 3 couples leaving the bar, on a not busy day.
Great, simple food. My first food establishment in Philly and I left a happy camper. Very nice service too. Will definitely be back!
Crappy vibe when I came in but the guy realized it took forever to fix my tire and sent me on my way free of charge. You just never know. Saved me some money. Thank you.

Hungrawesome.

Honey's Sit and Eat makes my stomach happy. I wanted to eat everything on the menu. That's rare for me. Almost everything was beyond exceptional. I couldn't choose. Maybe it was because I had to wait 30 minutes to be seated. Make sure to go on a sunny day if it's busy just in case you wait outside.

The Latke is nice for a change. Latke is kind of a substitute for potatoes it's like a fried hash brown pieces in the shape of bread. Thank God for something different. Take notes other restaurants. You need at least one creative twist on the menu.

The coffee is local and fresh, from La Colombe, the best coffee in Philly. 

We had Chile Rilenos and a Breakfast Burrito with Gauc. The Guac was amazing. 

The deserts sound awesome though I haven't tried them yet. Fried Banana Split anyone?

Very relaxed environment not intimidating.

The Auto Care Center at this Walmart absolutely suck, the mechanics are lazy, they don't have castrol unless you buy it off the shelf.  The employees are rude, I had the worse experience here; don't ever take your auto to be services at this location!!

The service was really good, our food was served quick and fresh. My kids loved the kids burgers, and I loved the sweet potato fries. This place was clean and friendly, I would definitely recommend to try this place out.

They went out of their way to help (we worked with John, the retail manager).  The hours are great, and they have a giant selection of menswear.  They listen to what you are telling them and get you things based on how you like what they brought you previously (size up or down, different style, etc). If you are buying a tux or suit, they may even do some quick tailoring while you wait so you can walk out with everything you need all set to go (they did this for us as well as the person before us).  They are quite helpful on working within your budget as well, if you have one.  Worth a stop for sure!
Great food and service. I'll be going back soon. It's authentic Kurdish food for a reasonable price which makes a great establishment. Their kebobs were flavorful and compliments their side dishes.

My boyfriend & I stayed here for 3 nights last week. I picked the Prince Conti because of the location and the price - half a block off Bourbon Street and a great deal for 3 nights. 

For being so close to Bourbon, the hotel is pretty quiet when it comes to hearing street noise but we were in an interior room so that may have helped. Noises inside the hotel, however, were moderately loud. You could hear the conversations of the room next to you and clearly hear them talk as they walked down the halls.

The room was spacious - king bed, TV, desk & chair, lounge chair. And it was clean. Not the newest or most updated decor but not a big deal. We were disappointed in the "quality" of the bed though - the mattress had very little cushioning and was in need of replacing. 

The staff, however, was fantastic and the reason this review is 4-stars. After my bf checked us in, our room wasn't ready yet (we were early), and the valet came to the car, opened my door, greeted me by name (and impressively pronounced it correctly!!), suggested a restaurant to try while we waited for our room and proceeded to walk us down to the restaurant in the rain. They were always helpful and also conspired with my boyfriend to have flowers delivered to our room while we were out.
Amazing bread.  I plan my Sat and Sun around going by this place after 9:30.  Whatever you get will be delicious and fresh. Grab a loaf or two and a bap and a brownie.  You're welcome.
Great bar for locals! People here are very friendly. The wings are THE BEST!! Tater tots are really great too!!

My coworkers and I came here for a birthday gathering on a Friday night, and I was happily surprised at how everything turned out.

Slainte looks a little skeezy from the outside (it's opposite from 30th Street Station, a bit of a rough corner with all the hustle and bustle there) but on the inside, cozy Irish decor mingled with the typical pub fluorescent trimmings and sports bar atmosphere.  Plus, CLEAN.  Omg, was it ever clean, from the seats to the tables to even the bathrooms.  I didn't have a problem putting my elbows on the table, that's for sure!

They have a wide beer selection and a pretty decent food menu.  Though the food itself wasn't outstanding, it's a step above the usual deep-fry meals you find in lesser places.  Definitely get the shepherd's pie with the mixed vegetables on the side!  Our server was patient with our huge crowd and kept coming back to make sure we were settling in fine.

All in all, a great place to come and celebrate after a long day at work, without none of the grubbiness of a lowkey sports bar and all of the fun.  Whee!

I called to make an appointment and the receptionists were very accommodating. My insurance was from out of state and they all took the time to check my coverage for me. After finding out I was not covered I still proceeded to get an exam, and purchased a pair of glasses. All of the team members were incredibly helpful and patient. They also were sensitive about my financial situation and have me incredible deals. I would recommend this place to anyone, especially Temple students! Most of the employees are owls hoot hoot!

My girlfriend and I had an incredible time at Compere Lapin. Everything from the cocktails, wine, and sherry - all spectacular. The food was seasoned and cooked to absolute perfection. With that said, the all-star of our night was our waitress Clair with the cool hair. She was very kind and extremely well-knowledged in the menu. Can't wait to return for another unforgettable experience.

I read up the previous comments about The Depot, so I went there with a bit of trepidation.  My Girl Friend was having a rough week at work, so I told her to meet me there for drinks, dinner and for me to get my college football fix.

For being a sports bar during the championship weekend you'd expect it to be pretty busy.  There were maybe 4 guys up at the bar and a few patrons sitting in the main area.  The beer's were cold, served in ice cold glasses, and the cosmopolitans my date was sucking down were, in her words, good and strong.

We ordered off the menu, I having the shredded beef nachos and Trixie the Bacon and Egg burger.  Both were excellent.  The only hangup was that the nacho's were served with the sour cream in one of those small plastic cups, with a lid.  A big scoop on the side of the nachos would have been better.

Two thumbs up for The Depot.  I don't understand what people don't like about it.  I thought it was OK and will be back.
Parking is not the best but the service and food is a must visit. They don't serve pork so everything is turkey based. Order the favorites and you can't go wrong! Cheese grits are so good!

My order: 
2 mahi mahi fried tacos
chips n guac
prickly pear frozen margarita 

I am on a hunt for fish tacos that even just slightly resemble the tacos i had in san diego...i didn't find them here, but they were pretty good - I'm not a huge fan of fish tacos with flour tortillas though! The best part was the sauce- - believe it was a chipolte mayo... nice touch, i would probably ask for extra on the side next time bc it's that good.  

the margarita was a little watery, i like a nice thick frozen drink.  

The guac was nice and fresh - I especially love the chips - very nice and thick - seemed closer to authentic.  

I love the ambience, casual but trendy, bright and airy and great music.

Every time we are in town visiting family we HAVE to stop by Mr Ice Cream...usually multiple times. All the flavors we have tried have been excellent. Pricing is reasonable, and you get as many toppings as you like. If you want ice cream, this is THE place to go.

Love this store!  My sister and I came across the store and decided to check it out.  We were so thrilled to see the amazing selection of toys!  So many awesome and unique toys and games, many that I've never seen anywhere else or are otherwise hard to find!  I also found a huge selection of educational toys, and very high quality such as Melissa and Doug.  To make it even better, the prices were amazing and the customer service was excellent.  The owners (mother/daughter) were extremely friendly and helpful.  They even offered gift wrapping and helped me carry my purchases to my car!  Such a wonderful store and I also love knowing I'm supporting a local, family run business.  I will be a regular and highly recommend this boutique to anybody!

I can't stop talking about this place. It is FABULOUS. the servers are all individually wonderful. So far I've had tall blonde hair blue eye boy, short blonde peppy girl, short brunette lady, and another boy. All of them were so welcoming and nice. Constantly checking in me to make sure I had all I needed. Not to mention the food is wonderful. It's like going to a super cozy diner!

The place is beautiful to look at. The decor is simply stunning. The cake was very good. Like VERY good. However. I don't know that it was $26 for two slices (big slices) good. 

It is definitely worth a stop in, and certainly an experience, but I just don't know that with prices like that that I will be going back very frequently.

Nice outdoor area. It's basically a dirt track for walking. One trail goes around the fenced in off-leash dog area with a few trails cutting in the middle. People are friendly and the dogs have a great time running in packs. Some spots can be a bit muddy and people don't pick up their dog's poop so you need to watch where you walk and make sure the dogs don't jump up on you (unless you don't mind getting paw smudges on your clothes). Otherwise, it's a fantastic place for you and your dog(s) to get exercise and spend time outdoors. I imagine I will visit this park many times in the future.

I was told there are lots of trails outside of the off-leash area and a swimming area for dogs, but I didn't go there since it's too cold right now.

Went last night. Grumpy staff and pushy, wrong personality for the restaurant business.
 food not as good as we expected. Not hot and small portion of pasta with dinner. High price for soup. Italian bread best part of meal!
Won't return!

I really can't say enough positive things about these guys. Let me preface this by saying that I was originally opposed to adding HVAC to my 100-plus year old twin. We were told by a few companies that it was an extremely difficult job. One flat-out told us it was impossible. But, thanks to my wife's urging we decided to get the opinion of one more crew, and just under a month later I write this while sitting in constant 74 degree bliss...in mid-August.

Matt, the sales rep set the tone right away. Within five minutes of meeting me he had a price sheet in my hand and explained the different options. Matt preaches "total transparency" and he means it. I never had to worry about these guys holding something back or misrepresenting their price or service. Matt was always super easy to get a hold of and had no problem calling back late, stopping by after 7:00 in the evening if it was more convenient for us, and just generally going out of his way to be accessible as possible. He's the kind of no-BS, stand-up guy you dream about dealing with on projects this large and with this much money involved. 

The rest of the crew is great, too. We had the same three installer for all four days that it took to complete the job. They kept me apprised of (literally) every step of the process and got my sign-off on even the smallest details before going through with the work. They cleaned up as best they could (it was a messy job) and were consummate pros. The owner, Nate, even dropped by on the first day to check things out and make sure everything was copacetic. 

The job itself? Awesome. The HVAC unit is quiet and works like a charm. Although I was initially skeptical about how much we really "needed" HVAC, I'm happy we took the plunge, and happier still that we found Unique!

We came here because we'd heard they had great desserts, but that was not our experience.
Our entrees were quite good, I had the lemon chicken with asparagus that was very tasty, though a tad over-salted.  My husband enjoyed his burger, but he had to ask the waiter to bring the wine he'd ordered after we'd already started eating.
The desserts were so disappointing, I got the "crack pie" which was supposed to be ooey gooey butter cake in a pie crust, which was just sweet, there were no other discernible flavors, the butter wasn't even detectable.  My husband's key lime pie was better, but still disappointing.

This is the best...for fresh made to order great food! The service is exceptional and the owners care about their customers.  
Love the vegetarian options and brown rice. Try the Eggplant!

After I leave the subway, if I crave sushi, I go in here. Every time I've ordered, the person who takes my order is always nice. Waiting is reasonable. They have a couple tables to dine in but it's better to eat at work or home only because it's really small inside.
My go to orders are shrimp tempura roll, spicy tuna roll, which are on the small side but great for the price. And the chicken teriyaki is always good and hot.

I recently spent a few days in Philadelphia at the Rodeway Inn. Besides being a little hard to locate this place it was a great find for future visits. The staff was friendly and the location was perfect. Plenty of restaurants and stores around (Starbucks across the street!) and not too busy considering it's the middle of a major US city.

If only I could figure out how to get one of those comfy beds into my suitcase.

See you soon Philly!

I'll probably give any Village Inn 5 stars! I love them as a breakfast place since they have great skillets, but their French silk pie is really the 5 star winner here. I can't find one that tastes like it anywhere else. 

I wish they would open Village Inns in south Florida!! I think they would do well, especially since they have they have the best pies!!!

Anand, the general manager, runs a great hotel. He even picked us up in the shuttle at the airport. They have great live music in the lobby/bar area most nights. Convenient shuttle to many places, helpful staff, quality food and good value.

Wow. Easily the most original, and overlooked, restaurant in Reno. Right on Virginia is SoMid (South MidTown), great atmosphere, even better food, and fast and friendly service. Pumping music, good bar, Japanese tapas.  All kinds of awesome.

Food was not very good and speed of service is very slow. Our waitress was very friendly tho. Granted We cane here on a Friday night, but it shouldn't take 1hr and half to serve dinner for two.  Poor execution on food and speed of service. I will not be coming here again.
Was very disappointed with the flowers they were not fresh and then they had weird marks on them never will use again

Very nice establishment with pleasant food and EXCELLENT service. This is the kind of place that I would go to just to have apps, a drink and listen to the music just so I could experience the service. Warm, friendly no frills servers with genuine smiles and intentions. The food was pleasant and quite edible. We had a special which included seafood over a nice risotto and the ribeye from the menu. The ribeye, although prepared well, lacked the quality of other comparable restaurants, but still good for a ribeye at an affordable price. Overall, a nice meal complimented by some AWESOME service. We shall return.

I suppose it was good for the price, but I just felt so unhappy with both the color and the cut that I would've rather saved up a bit longer for a better hair cut. The highlights weren't evenly blended with the rest of my hair and the cut was uneven.

I really do like this Shop Rite.  The prices and hours are great, and the service is generally decent.  The deli has usually has a special, which is a nice surprise everytime (like turkey for $3.99/lb!), and I always get samples of meats and cheeses to snack on while I wait for my order.  The bakery is usually well-stocked although the donut selection is not as fantastic as Giant's; they do have the essentials, though.  The store itself isn't the most well-organized but it has everything at relatively low prices.  Plus, if you shop on a Sunday morning, they have complimentary coffee, danishes, bagels, and cookies, which is a really nice gesture, I think.  I've also noticed that service has gotten a lot better over the years.  They also have an entire aisle dedicated to Mexican groceries, too, which most other surrounding groceries stores don't have.
By far the best Italian market I've been to! It quite busy when you get inside and the sweets are amazing!

Just had some of their other food. The marinated steak tacos with jalepeno jam , red cabbage and their creamy cilantro sauce. Brought a tear to this Texan's eye :'). They have a couple of new beers on tap as well. The Bear Mace is quite exceptional. I can't wait for their Imperial IPA and Cuvée Diable. Hops, hops and wine!

I really enjoyed this "hipster" spot in Webster. I was happy and surprised to see grass fed beef on the menu, a rare occasion in STL. I had the burger which was one of the best I have had in STL. I also had the pear and cranberry cobbler with ice cream...SO good. The wine list was decent, but they should add additional options for wines by the glass since I think there were only six or seven. Service was great and atmosphere was cool, I just wish there were more people there on a Thursday night!

We stopped in for a drink last night after the Orchestra. The drink menu has some interesting choices. I decided to order a Martini priced at $11. Instead of gin i ordered Grey Goose. The server asked me if I wanted grapejuice. Huh? she then walked back to the bar. A couple minutes later she came back and asked if I wanted a vodka band lemonade. Huh? Next the bartender came over to our table and said that the Martini would only fill half of the class and that for $3 more I could have a full glass. I said that I would have the regular Martini. Several minutes later I received my half glass of Martini. It was mediocre at best. We asked for the tab after we finished our drinks. The charge for my half Martini was $16. At that point we were so turned off that we paid and left. With all of the great bars and restaurants in Rittenhouse I can't envision this amatuer hour lasting long.

Yes it is a little crowded, and good luck getting a seat on major game days, but the service is good, quick and the selection is great. There aren't too many options but just enough and they have a good selection of beer. 

It was not our choice of the evening but where we ended up and it was a good decision.

My son requested donuts for his kindergarten classroom party. I called and Strange they were able to do a custom order with a smaller sized donut, which was great. However, it wasn't so great when I arrived and the donuts were not glazed as I requested. Yet, the owner was great and made the situation as 'right' as was possible on such a short time window. He also gave a roll of stickers that all the kids enjoyed! The donuts were a huge hit...kids and teachers were making a point to tell us they were delicious and it made my son's day. I appreciate the awesomeness of the owner and would recommend Strange to anyone.

Never before, we have eaten Ethiopian food so we cannot compare it. Before we made the order, the owner explained what the dish is. She also told how to cook them. Food had very interesting flavors. Interesting, two dishes were serve on one plate separated by vegetables. The restaurant itself is very colorful with many Ethiopian accents. Good prices, good service.

We've eaten here four times and have really enjoyed the food, the service, the ambience, and the great French 75s!  It is really far for us, but good enough that we keep working on excuses to drive to this end of town, coming up with one right now.

Was kind of iffy about coming here because I have never had Puerto Rican food before, so it was either going to be a hit or miss for me. Ordered the crab meat turnover for an appetizer and a coquito to drink. Both were so delicious. Never tasted anything quite like it. I ordered the shrimp monfongo for my entree and my boyfriend got the steak monfongo. Let's just say I will definitely be coming back for round 2!!! Salsa exceeded my expectations. 
The venue is small. Wish the tables were a little more cozy but for the most part, I would recommend trying this place at least one time. I don't think you'll be disappointed
The music is absolutely lovely, but don't get the old New Orleans fashioned.... it's worse than cough syrup and I got it without the simple syrup

Just opened so staff not fully trained. Although it was busy, and they lost my pizza it was surprisingly good. Will return when they get the kinks out. A good addition and value to Reno's marginal pizza offerings.

WOW.
Seated by the nice hostess right away. The decor and ambiance is simple and understated. It sometimes can get a bit noisy because the space is not particularly large.
The waiter was attentive, friendly, and very knowledgeable. 
Bread had some tahini dip, which was good, but nothing to rave about.
There was a special eel appetizer (GET IT). Eel was supple with an amazing smokey flavor. The carrot slaw or whatever it was...delicious. Sauce was unique!
The octopus appetizer was delicious. Two octopus tentacles cooked to perfection with a neat side salad.
Rabbit leg entree was juicy and fall off the bone. The asparagus, lentil, carrot, onion, whatever it was...delicious.
The lamb kotka looked a lil dry, but was absolutely tender and moist! Solid dish with pita, okra, and etc.
The pig cheeks was the best! Amazing moist and flavorful. I could not get enough. You must order this!
The food was top notch as were the size of the entrees. The chef actually came out a few times and talked to us which made us feel so welcomed.
Assorted ice creams...there was a dill sorbet/ice cream and it blew my mind! This is a must try if they have it.
Pistachio creme brulee had great flavor!
Service is great. Food is amazing. Prices are incredible reasonable for the quantity, and most importantly, the quality. Plus it's BYO!
One of the best meals I have had in Philadelphia so far.

Here is another review on a great Barber shop. I travel the country every week and ever 2 or 3 weeks I try and find a barber shop to go a clean up and shave. I drove 20 miles to this shop and I wasn't disappointed at all! 

My barber was very dedicated and focused on giving me what I wanted and making it look good. Fresh fade, lined up, and straight razor shave. All for $20 bucks. You can't beat it. I'm not sure what the normal rate is but for what I got $20 was a great deal. I just had the same thing done 3 weeks ago at a shop in Dallas and it was $80. 

Very well done I'll be back next time I'm in town. Thanks.

I would give them 2 stars because they are a mom & pop and I think they deserve some benefit of the doubt but too many compounded problems.

Unprofessionalism - 1) website is outdated that you can only request 1 service even though there are drop down menus for up to 2.
2) I was confirmed for an appointment. Upon my arrival, they asked if I could come back an hour later. Could they not have called me before I drove down from Brentwood?
3) After rescheduling above appointment, they call me the day before my appt to ask if I can come 45 min later (grant it, a logistical issue of being a parent & a business owner).
4) Services offered are not always what you get. Website offers an array but only some are available on certain days such as the manicurist only works on Fridays.

Finally, I'm in the door and ready for my back purification. It was basic back facial (I should've asked what the service included ahead of time).

During the entire treatment time, if I was not receiving a hands-on service at that moment, Martha left the room. She did not check to see if the mask used on my back was ok - it was actually burning as there were also 2 towels on top of the mask trapping in heat and anything escaping my pores.

She stated the foot rehabilitation massage was good. I was robbed here. I can generate more force by walking on a tennis ball at home for FREE for a better foot massage.
WOW!!! My first time having Indian food and it was great!!! I would highly recommend Indian food and this is a place to have it in.
Great pizza place our whole family loves. You can create you own pizza and put as many toppings on as you want at no extra cost.

I am a fan of the original location and this one is right there on the awesome scale.  The location has an expanded menu with nachos and tacos.  The location is always packed and has community seating, so don't be shy and make some friends.  They are kid friendly and highly encouraged.  The feel of this location fits well within the community and has suck a large variety of people that come there.

A Haven in the Rough. I am so happy to discover The Haven. I had no idea that it was so cute and spacious on the inside. I expected some dark, dirty old dive, with a few bar food items, which would have been just fine by me. I was so wrong. 

The Haven is a perfect neighborhood bar by anyone's standards. It has a full menu including several nicer dinner specials. Lots of drink deals going on here, esp during sports games. Coincidentally I stopped by her for dinner on the way to the Guns and Hoses benefit for the Backstoppers, and was delighted to see that a buffalo chicken sandwich called the Stop Drop and Roll donates a dollar to the Backstoppers for each order!

For those fanatics out there, there is a Golden Tee, sadly no Big Buck Hunter. And on an even better note, older people were hanging out and drinking here. One of my favorite things about places in the city is to go where my elders go. Those places are almost guaranteed to be friendly and legit. While I also consider Nellie Glenn's a cool spot for my south side turf, I'm also now adding The Haven to that list. I'm sure it's going to be my go to place for hanging out with dudes, my volleyball friends, and even my parents.

The wife and I stopped in at Cyrano's for a late night drink and snack.  Although it was a pretty ugly night, the place was hopping.  We sat at a pub table back by the coffee bar and they were seriously cranking out some hot drinks and lots of whipped cream.   The biggest question about Cyrano's is "What the hell is it?"

When you drive by, and even when you walk in, you get the feeling your in a trendy, upscale restaurant.  Then they hand you a menu and on its owne it looks like you might be at a Waffle House or something - very casual looking.  Upon closer inspection, though, there are not a ton of items, but they are definitely way too interesting to be at any kind of chain restaurant.  There is also a pretty extensive menu for coffee drinks and desserts, which we just ignored, and a pretty decent wine list.  The bar looks like a counter, almost as if they are embarrassed to have a full bar.  The ambience, while having an upscale appearance, is still very lively.   We weren't sure if it was the acoustics, or what, but this was a very loud crowd.   For anyone who has been to the Benton Park Cafe, Cryano's is what they are trying to be and doing a much better job of it. 

We had a couple glasses of wine by the glass and spinach-artichoke dip.  All was very good.   We won't hesistate to come back for a date sometime and try the main courses.  If it was more convenient, I have a feeling we might become regulars.  Cool place.  Give it a try.

As a girl scout daisy mom, I thoroughly enjoyed seeing GS Cookies crafted into their full potential... alcoholic beverages. Seriously, I would probably buy more cookies from my daughter if I knew how to make drinks out of them! 

With all of the bites of food & drinks made out of the cookies, I kind of felt like I was on the verge of a diabetic coma by the end of it, but everything was SO GOOD.

I did feel like the event itself was a little... slow? I'm not sure if that's the right word. There just wasn't much to "do" after making our way around to all of the sampling stations, besides sit, chat, and enjoy the band. We left pretty early on. As enjoyable as the band was - and they had a great singer - there's only so much sitting around that I can do, especially while my stomach was full of sugar. 

Still, this was a great opportunity for an evening out, I got to sample some great items, and they had a nice silent auction.

A great home Greek experience with good food and great atmosphere by the sponge docks of Tarpon Springs.  To get the Greek experience, you must get their feta flamed (flambe'-ed?) with the ouzo - opa!

The pancakes were fantastic. Not a place to frequent for healthier choices (of course, you're getting pancakes, why would you). Who doesn't love desert for breakfast? The restaurant was accommodating for a large group (10 people) in the outdoor seating, which was very nice for the early brunch atmosphere.

On staff was a professional interior design specialist who reviewed our floor plans, calculated space and layout and helped us make design selections we really liked. Also helped us from making a poor decision in an alternate furniture selection.  We were very impressed. Another associate also stayed late to assure we were happy with everything.
If i could give less i would...this place was horrible. Order was wrong twice,always cold and extremely overpriced. I was so happy to hear the are closing

I really enjoy coming here.  While I have only been here two or three times, the wait staff is always super friendly, knowledgeable of the menu, and give great recommendations on what to order. It's a nice setting, the times I have been its very relaxed, and quiet.    The view is great - it is on the second floor with a lot of windows. Ask for a table by the window, when it is snowing it is absolutely gorgeous!

We came to NOLA for one night and chose to dine here. It was a great decision! I had looked on yelp through hundreds of restaurants because I wanted to find THE BEST. We discussed old school, new American, tapas, seafood, steaks, pretty much everything. Then we all agreed on Luke. 

We checked into our hotel, grabbed the shuttle and sped over to Luke just in time to catch the end of happy hour. Half price drinks including wine (my fave). We really wanted to make sure we got some of the fifty cent oysters. The hostess and our server made sure with only a few min left we were accommodated! We began with sparkling wine and 2 dozen oysters. Both were amazing. Oysters were full and so fresh. They were served with cocktail sauce, vinegar and enough horseradish to make our eyes water in delight. Our next course we switched to a really awesome white wine (sorry I don't recall the name) but it was suggested by our awesome server. His name is Christopher Doppenschmidt in case you would like to ask for him. I then asked if it would be possible to get the shrimp from the raw bar hot. His response: we can do that! As was his response the whole night. He served he shrimp with local clarified butter. The butter was so amazing. We then tried the blue crab bisque. It is making my mouth water remembering it now. For dinner we shared the ribeye and the jäger snitzel. both were great. There are no words to describe the homemade bernaise for the steak. 

One of the best parts of the night was meeting Brian Katz the General Manager. We all laughed and had fun and he made sure our experience was one not to ever be forgotten. 

This was our second time dining at Luke. It will be hard to go back to Cincy and miss out on the culinary treats of Chef John Besh. We will soon return!

I have been a client of Tiffany M (owner) for over 10 years. She runs her salon with the utmost pride and professionalism. You can see the pride she has in her business when you walk in the door. The salon is warm and inviting and very clean! The staff is very friendly and extremely professional. They are all trained on the most current trends, so ladies anything you see in a magazine can be done here!! They have the top products available for sale and stand behind them! I recommend this salon for all your beauty needs!

Came here a couple years ago & haven't been back since.  All I remember was that the bread was good, but other then that nothing really stood out to me to be outstanding, let alone much appetizing to me.  I was open to try new things and it was definitely a unique experience, and I suppose it was "fine dining" with the ambiance and specialty-type ingredients used..things I've never heard or tried, and of course the small portions.  

However, I do recall that they pride themselves in plating and presentation, I just wish flavor-wise that they were appealing to me.  Unfortunately, the biggest sour memory I have of the place is that our server instantly changed her demeanor and suddenly had a pretentious air towards us immediately after she realized we were using a groupon.  She snatched the standard menus out of our hands and replaced them with the cheap "groupon menu".  There wasn't much of a selection, so it's either you like the groupon-set menu or you don't.  I think most people use groupon to get a taste of new restaurants to see if it's to their liking and then decide to continue business sans groupon afterwards if things went well, at least that's what I do but honestly I don't see the groupon working out for this place from what I experienced.  And considering the high prices, I'm even more reluctant to role the dice on giving them a chance on the regular menu considering my past experience here.

Pool tables, darts, and karaoke which warrant a 5 star review. Some of the WORST bartenders I've ever experienced. I figure a 3 star review splits the difference. If you are ok with a great bar with slow, rude service and weak drinks once you complain, you'll be ok.

Spent 2 nights at the Peppermill while in Reno on government business. Government rate is excellent, and they don't charge the resort fee. 

Hotel is very dated, and rooms are a bit gaudy. But the room was comfortable, and the non-smoking floor did not at all smell of smoke. Most of the public spaces in the hotel are also relatively fresh-smelling. That truly shocked me given this is a smoking Casino. The staff are Ultra friendly and helpful. I asked a manager for directions and he went out of his way to walk me to my destination which was halfway across the enormous Hotel complex. There's a nice heated outdoor pool and hot tub, although the second pool and hot tub were closed for maintenance while I was visiting. One of the things I liked most, and I guess this is part of the course for a casino hotel, all of the shops and coffee shops in snack bars were open 24 hours. If you're bringing the kids, they have a nice kids arcade. Parking is  relatively convenient. Check-in lines were long, but they have a self check in that sped things up a lot. 

Don't be mistaken, internet, parking, is not free. Most Travelers pay a resort fee which is another way of charging for parking and internet.

Only major negative, the neighborhood is terrible. I went for a three block walk to get to a Walgreens and took my life into my hands. Meth addicts, heroin users, and hookers.

I couldn't find a single thing that was worth a second bite. All bland or tasted funny. Didn't look fresh. I am not kidding - did not like any of it. Very disappointed. Not sure why it has good reviews.
Great coffee, tasty food, cute patio. Perfect place to grab a quick breakfast on a sunny day!
This place is awesome. The pizza comes out thin but crispy and its authentic brick oven. Awesome craft beer selection and knowledgable bar tenders. I will be back a thousand times.

Absolutely amazing place. When you enter the front door, you get the feeling that this is a place frequented by the same friendly faces. A Cheers vibe, if you will. Or maybe not, but still, you know what I mean. It's great to have a spot in Fountain Square that's hip and different. I've tried a number of the ciders and meads and I don't think there's one on the tap that isn't worth drinking. Snap Dragon is my current favorite. Awesome.

You can tell the people that run this place are truly passionate about what they're doing, and they're incredibly knowledgeable. I've added New Day to my growler rounds on Fridays.

We purchased a sectional and ottoman and within a month it started showing wear, fabric stretched, pillow tore from cheaply sewn together. I called for a month and each time a rep took the info and said a repair person would call. To date no one has called. 
I would not recommend this furniture to anyone.

Ugh please... people, if you want to insult Koreans by tasting our food and saying, "like oh em gee, you Koreans have disgusting food" then go to Korea House -_-

Seriously, Korea House is an insult to Korean food. I'm super SERIAL guys gosh! 

The service in this place is horrible. I went here with a friend and the waitress just casually glances back at us then gets up and mumbles something (which weren't very pleasant - I understand Korean) then sat us at a table where it looked like the chairs were charred by fire started by the people who ever went to eat here.

My friend and I ordered a plate of seafood "pancakes" (as you Americans call it)... the seafood tasted like they came from a small plastic container that you buy at the store next door to the restaurant where the cook doesn't even cook it fully. Literally, it tasted slippery yet rubbery at the same time. I ordered food, not playtoys for my mouth (which sounds disgustingly kinky in some of your opinions, right?) 

I look over to another table and they have some squid thingy drowned in this sauce. Ok, first of all, I know we're in America and Americans love having their food drowned in gravy-ish sauce but come on, that's just not a Korean thing to do. And low and behold the bitter waitress looks at the group of people at the other table and talks to another waitress about them - openly. Though I have to admit, what the lady said was pretty funny. 

But what really turned me off was that this place didn't serve good food yet people go here in hopes to get good Korean food. It's really embarrassing because when I have some professors and friends say something like, "Korean food is pretty gross. I tried it at Korea House and I can't believe you people eat something like that." 

Seriously WTF. Those people are just horrible in cooking and most of all Korea House is mainly for those "type" of people who go there to gossip about others (really, that's what they do - they hardcore bitch about other people) NOT a place where they serve decent food. 

People, I am just trying to save you  from an upset stomach and a night which could be filled with fun NOT explosive diarrhea.

I drove past the Barn Attic yesterday and turned immediately around to go in and poke around:  I am SO glad that I did.  I spent 3+ hours exploring all 4 floors which are absolutely PACKED: mad props to the clothing selection, and a special shout out to  vintage greeting cards (Secretary Day FTW!), beautiful antique lamps, and stacks upon stacks of complete vintage dining sets.

I came away with 12 items for $95 (just clothing and jewelry, I wasn't furniture shopping).  As the owner told me, this is NOT a thrift store, and she is right: it is way better.  

I found the owner quirky, entirely pleasant, and exceedingly helpful and patient.  Other reviewers are correct, she will greet you and give you the rundown on what's available in her barn and try to give you an idea of the scope and volume of what she has (which is a lot ... I can think of only a few places that might rival the clothing options here, and I have never in all my days seen so much jewelry in one place, ever).  She came upon me in the lower level of the barn, where a huge selection of amazingly organized vintage clothes live.  

She let me know they measure and organize all dresses and skirts by the waist size and showed me where I could find the wall-mounted tape to get my measurements.  Being a bigger girl as far as vintage shopping goes (modern size 12, top to bottom) this way of organizing the pieces meant everything I picked to try on fit me.  Literally EVERYTHING.  All 18 pieces I tried on.  This was an unprecedented first for me.  

The items I came away with were reasonably priced (between $4 and $10 an item).  The more unique or on-trend the item, the more you'll pay.  I scored a tortoise statement necklace for $30, something we sell at the pricey retail store at which I  work at part-time in the city for a whopping $88.  Whoever says the clothing is overpriced simply has not yet taken the time to go through the considerable inventory carefully, I found a TON of reasonably priced and thoroughly unique items.  Perhaps this is because I'm used to shopping in Philadelphia where I pay more for items that are hand-picked, transported, and marked up from places like Barn Attic.  Not only are the clothes a total steal for how one-of-a-kind they are, they were not at all picked over like they are in the shops of Philadelphia or NYC.  

Some things you can find yourself, but the owner knows where absolutely everything is and will point you in the right direction with unfailing accuracy.  She assisted me with 10+ cases of jewelry, helped me shuffle and explore through trays upon trays of vintage and vintage-looking jewelry (organized by color, the perfect way to shop for costume jewelry in my opinion).  

I asked, and the owner isn't interested in selling her inventory online and shipping to customers and clearly enjoys interacting with anyone who wanders in.  If you can't handle this kind of old school personal service, shop vintage finds on eBay, which I have done many a time.  With online vintage shopping be prepared for things not to look like you thought they would or fit the way you'd hoped (or even fit at all).  

I defy you to find a vintage shop as organized, fairly priced, with a staff that's willing to actually assist you ANYWHERE in a metropolitan area.  

This is a one-of-a-kind, wondrous place to explore.  I will absolutely be back, and  soon, with as many city girls as will fit in my car.

We ate here on Mother's Day. (Party of 5 plus one munchkin) The restaurant was not busy by any means however our food took approx. an HOUR to arrive at our table after placing our orders. Other patrons dined and exited as we waited for our meals.  When our food finally arrived it did not include my meal. My family graciously waited until I received my food (Cuban sandwich which was very tasty, btw) before they ate and by then all of their meals were cold. Our waiter was very apologetic and swore up and down that he turned in my order with the others and blamed it on the kitchen. My sandwich ended up being comped which I felt was fair. However I was really worried about the fact that we had parked in a pay by the hour parking lot since we waited so long for our food to arrive. When we were finished with our meal we headed to the parking lot only t o find a $40.00 parking ticket. I returned to the restaurant and asked the manager if he would be so kind as to help me out with it since we had waited exceedingly long for our meals. He said there was nothing he could do and compared it to me expecting him to pay for a speeding ticket?! Thank you Margaritaville Nashville for making my Mother's Day one to remember.

My Updated Review: I've gone back a few more times and their consistency for good food it on point. I have to say that their fried rice is the best I've ever had, I really can't say what it is about it, but the first bite I instantly knew. I tried their Sesame Beef which is a new favorite item, the sauce is good and the texture was like chicken, not chewy or fatty.

The staff is always nice and friendly, and the service is quick. The price is a little high compared to cheaper places, but you get what you pay for, plus the servings are big.

My First Review: Very good! I just had the Kung Poa Chicken and was the best I've had. I tell like there should have been more chicken, cause there was just enough for me. I used the pepper sauce that was given, it was too oily but added a great kick.  The crab puffs seemed a little to salty but were still good. I ordered takeout, and it was ready in less than 5 minutes; I don't know if that's a good thing. The interior was very clean and the staff was friendly. I can't wait to go back to try something else.

The Peppermill is our home away from home!  We love it there!  The staff is wonderful - always a smile in passing, no matter what position they hold!  We LOVE our VIP Host, Ryan who tends to our every need with the utmost of professionalism.  We refer many friends & acquaintances to the Peppermill, knowing they will become frequent guests as we have been the past 9 years!

I love the selection of toppings and apps, but I have to say that the crust is always tough. It tastes like it was previously frozen, it's a sad contrast to the fresh ingredients on the top of the pizza. Worth a try for the cool atmosphere and good food.

First, I've only been a member for a few years now.  In my mind, it was "worth it" to be a member and see special exhibits and get member pricing and discounts long before the most recent change in admission policies. This place is a great escape.  There are a lot of things I could spend $55 on for an annual membership and not be as rewarding.

As an arts institution, it relies on membership, grants or donations to exist.  It can only be part of the community if someone contributes.  I do not believe it should be expected to be a free park.  It does host community days and free days so that everyone can enjoy its offerings.

What I love about the museum most isn't inside the building, though strolling the collections is always interesting.  I love the IMA for the gardens and outdoor spaces.  The horticultural society has done wonders with the unique flowers and plants and every nook and cranny has something of interest.  Sculptures and fountains add interest to the gardens.

I love the gift shop for their men's ties and for unique gifts, and the greenhouse has unique plants-though shop early in the season for the best selection of perennials.  I also enjoy the cafe, which is great quality and usually fairly quick.  

I've read other reviewers who say things are expensive.  Again, it's about the experience, and I know my membership, and what I spend while visiting helps to support the institution.  IMA is worth the visit and worth doing your duty to support is you are able.

I've been coming here for a few years now and the guys and gals who work here are all kind, helpful and do a good job. Conveniently located on route 130, the hours are convenient too. You can find coupons online to save a few bucks. I recommend and will continue coming here.

i love this place.
i love the atmosphere and decor of this restaurant. it's very Italian old-fashioned?
I got the ravioli and shared a pepperoni & sausage pizza with my friend.
the pizza was delicious and our waitress was good looking and good @ her job.
I would certainly come back again if I ever came back to St. Louis.
it's also close to the ARCH and Busch Stadium, 5-7 minutes walking?
Patricia Claire special was amazing!! The food was so yummy and not greasy at all. Great atmosphere and friendly staff!

I was out with my girlfriend. Although the food was good, the waitress was horrible We first ordered 1 soda   and 1 ice tea, and 2 waters she didn't bring us the water for another 15 minutes after we got the soda and ice tea.

When we asked for 2 minutes-, that turned into 16 minutes We actually had to wave down the Hostess and ask where our waitress went so we could order. When  the host asked the manager where she was, he got her. The waitress came over to take our order Nothing- not even an apology or smile.. Not a "Sorry for the wait"

We ordered the Zuccini Frities, Chicken,Veal Parm. Food was all good. Bread was good.  We order the small portions. she screwed up the order- She brought us the regular sized ones. I made sure she didn't charge us for the regular ones - She in fact did and didn't take it off till the last moment- probably trying to sneak it by us hoping we wouldn't see so she would get a bigger tip.

She never came over and asked how our meal was. she never looked over to our table ONCE.After i got my meal i needed a drink refill. once again she disappeared for almost 15 minutes

It was around 3pm on a Sunday- there were plenty of servers, waitresses on the floor that night The restaurant was NOT packed. There was NO wait for our table when we arrived.And it it wasn't dinner hour yet. Our waitress appeared to be working only 4 tables in total.If it was any other restaurant That waitress would be catering to our every needs quickly and professionally with a smile on their face.

I have been to many restaurants and 90% of them have better service than this.

The food was good but I would rather stay at home than deal with this sub par and rude service.

She messed up the order was late with the drinks, never apologized and disappeared alot 

Trust me guys, go to a better class area than Springfield or dont be surprised if you walk away disappointed with the service.

This is a little joint like Hatch Print Show where you kind of step back in time upon entry. If the place wasn't always so congested I'd love to just nestle into a corner and love my ice cream. And there's the rub: the line. Be aware you will wait, it doesn't really matter what time of year, but during the warm months especially. 

Just by stepping inside people seem to be transformed into yesteryear. A guy in line with us noticed my husband's camera and struck up a conversation with us about photography and showed us some of his pictures. Seriously, who does that anymore? 

The ice cream is out of this freaking world. Local or tourist, Mike's should be on your to do list.

I haven't been to this diner in years. (Many years) this place always and still has good service.  The food use to be very delicious. I'm not sure what happened. Didn't think an experienced cook could mess up a simple dish, 2 eggs over medium, soft bacon, hash browns and white toast! 

Well I got 2 over hard you could stand a fork up in them, x-crispy bacon with soft ends that tasted like it's been pre made and was sitting around, hash browns that tasted like pure grease like they cooked them and dropped them back in the fryer to heat them up.... But I ate the toast that was good! 

I'm so glad I didn't order my first choice, eggs Benedict. Afraid of what that would have been like, the cook can't cook an egg. Does this cook even know what a poached egg is??? 

From what i understand they have a new cook, did u check his references??? 

It's a shame the service was great!! But you don't just pay for service!!

It was our first time eating there and we ordered the buffalo chicken bites, chicken tacos, stuffed potato spring rolls and salmon three way! The food was mediocre and our server was really slow! Don't think we'll be going back there!

I love this place, since I moved down to Florida, I make a stop there once every month almost, We ordered the fish spread to start, Man clam chowder and Mahi Mahi while my wife ordered the Mullet meal with the 2 sides of potato salad and the cole slaw, the soup wasn't really hot and my fish was really dry, but with the help of the horse radish and mayo I manage to moist it, loved the potato salad, over all good experience.
