The food was actually excellent.  I had a filet that really was cooked perfectly.  The service was excellent as well although they could be more assertive in refilling water and coffee.   

For me, this place is terrific because they let our group sit even before everyone arrived.  You know how some restaurants have silly rules about the entire group being present?  They don't enforce this and while we were waiting at our table, the waitress was more than patient in serving us drinks while we waited for the rest of the group.  This is service!

Fun bar and a fun atmosphere.  It really is a cute place.  I'd go back.

I am on vacation in New Orleans while my boyfriend is here on business, and I wanted to treat myself to a mani-pedi. I found Riverside while walking around the French quarter, so I decided to pop in and have my nails done. I was a little hesitant after reading some of the Yelp reviews, but I had a great time and I would definitely come back here if I lived in the city! The shop is small, but the girls are are really sweet and did a great job. It's not a fancy uppity place, but that's just what I liked about it. Good, clean mani-pedi and good company from the employees. Thanks, ladies!

Just perfect. Great coffee ( far better than Starbucks), large airy space, friendly efficient service, delectable food. This is the place to meet a friend for a light lunch, kick back and read, work on your laptop, have a  casual business meeting.

Met my friend for lunch. We shared curried chicken salad on toasted ciabatta, and the summer salad  with feta, pecans, grapes, greens and excellent dressing. The curried chicken salad was so good, I will go tomorrow to share it again with my husband. And the iced coffee, next time will order a large. Had a wonderful grilled cheese sandwich here and they have great muffins and cinnamon rolls.

This is by far the best lunch spot in haddonfield (pretty good for a bagel breakfast too). GO!

Arlene A.

I have to give it to Nashville in this area. You have Memphis soundly beat on the gourmet, trendy burger. 

Burger Up is located in South Nashville on 12th Avenue South and as others have noted, it's not easy to find if you don't know where it is. My GPS had it 1/4 mile further up the road, and I luckily spotted it while looking for a spot to park. Parking is pretty limited as well, but I was fortunate to find a place on the street. If there is one thing I took soundly from the University of Tennessee at Knoxville, it is parallel parking skills. No problems for me in that area.

Going in the restaurant, I was pretty impressed. Memphis has a lot to offer in the world of culinary delight, but a trendy burger served by hipsters is not one of them. The service was what I expected. It was not very good at first (14 minutes until someone came up to me at the bar to take my drink order), but warmed up when the friendly barkeep realized I was not terrible, I guess.

The menu is what you expect in a burger-focused restaurant. Plenty of burgers, and I liked some of the options, e.g. one with pimento cheese; one made of bison; the standard mushroom and swiss; etc. Because it was my first time here, I went with the standard triple L classic. It's important when dining at a burger spot to try their standard burger to see what all the hype is about. 

Presentation was as expected. Trendy appearance, fries come in a fry holder; nice looking burger, too.

Wait time was decent. Again, it was entirely too long for someone to approach me at the bar on a Sunday night (it was not that busy). Food took about 15-20 minutes to arrive. Barkeep followed up a few times once my food arrived. 

The burger was pretty good. The bun was fresh. You could actually taste the meat. It was a bit overcooked, coming in around medium-well, and I prefer a medium. Interesting they did not even ask how I wanted it cooked. Maybe that's a Nashville thing. Something I was not expecting was the amount of yellow mustard. Yes, the menu proudly announces yellow mustard comes on the triple L, but there was too much in my opinion. If I come back, I'll likely ask to leave it off, or put it on the side. This was a minor thing. The mustard was not too strong that it inhibited in some way the flavor of the burger. But it was always there.

Fries = good. This is one area Memphis really needs help in learning to serve properly. Freshly cut, nicely fried, and plenty of salt. And to boot, a homemade maple ketchup. When I was debating a score, it was between 3 and 4, and the ketchup brought it up to a 4. It was a really nice condiment.

Full bar, with a nice supply of small batch and high quality vodkas, bourbons, etc. Excellent variety of local and other microbrews on tap. Wines, offered, as well. Water is served without asking. Price is reasonable, IMO.

So there you have it. I'll certainly come back and eat here again.

I went two separate times. One it was super packed everywhere with no where to sit ( which obviously means only good things ) and the second time it was definitely a lot less packed but still a great vibe. 

They have outdoor and indoor seating along with a little inside food restaurant type thing to order food along with your beers. The outdoor patio allows pets which only makes me like it so much more  
There is quite a few different beers on top along with a kombucha (which I didn't quite like) but they also have bottle beers (along with ciders for people like me lol). Super cool spot for sure

My wife and I had a great time on this tour. We both love history and this walking tour enables you to learn some great stories about the founding and city of Philadelphia. Our tour guide was animated and on top of his game! I would highly recommend this walking tour!

Limoncello is the first of many amazing restaurants to make it into WC.  I first went over 5 years ago well before the expansion and shared some amazing paella.  The menu and restaurant have since expanded and I continue to go regularly.  They have a great wine list and extensive menu options, almost too many.  They regularly change their specials to keep things fresh.  The veal steak was up there with one of the best I have ever had.  

Lunch is equally as amazing, sitting outside on a nice day, either ordering a la carte or using their lunch buffet.  The sandwich selection is always phenomenal.  The veal parm w/ vodka sauce was one of my all time favorites.

Only knock is that it can be very loud, but dont let that stop you, just be prepared!

My BF and I came here for dinner while we were visiting beautiful Santa Barbara. The Rock Crab was AMAZING! Its was so delicious and it went very well with the beer selection ;) We also had a few oyster shooters and raw oysters that were unbelievable! The customer service is fantastic, very attentive but not pushy at all. Its not as large as other restaurants but its cozy has a nice view of the water and you can sit outside if you want. We are definitely planning to come here for the crab and oysters the next time we're back in SB...If you want delicious seafood for a killer price go check this place out you'll be glad you did!

Craft beer, boutique wines, artisan cheese and a seasonal menu of small bites and heartier sandwiches all served by one of the best trained staff in the city (plus multiple locations). Seriously, what else do you need?!

My child was sick and she left here feeling better.

Not really much more to say.

I have always loved Landry's. The food is always good. Even this time it was very good however the portions are a joke. I ordered the seafood platter and substituted the fish for shrimp. I got 6 tiny shrimp 2 oysters 2 hush puppy's and 1 stuffed shrimp. Very tiny "platter " for $30. Usually very full of food. Now the biggest problem was the service! 25 min to be greeted by waitress and 10 more min to actually get the drinks. Refills were given if you were lucky enough to flag somebody down. Very disappointed! She even had a trainer. Three times drinks empty over 10 min. I'm sure they won't be there long if service does not improve!

With so many tasting rooms on the SB urban wine trail it can sometimes be difficult deciding which ones to put on the list, well corks n' crowns is a must stop.  One of the nice things about this tasting room is that they have different wine flights so you can pick a flight that caters to your personal taste rather than having to drink things you don't care so much for.  They also have beer flights so if you have friends who are not wine drinkers you can all come an still enjoy a tasting together.  The staff was fun and friendly which made for a great tasting atmosphere.  Also if you go to the SB visitors center before hand you can get a coupon for a free beer flight with the purchase of a wine flight, who doesn't like free booze?!
WARNING: No Longer Serving Brunch as of 8-14-16. Host said they stopped serving brunch eight months ago. A great place for lunch and dinner.

I hesitate to write this review because my husband and I love this place so much, it's like our secret.  Two for one Mexican draft beer and the buffet is fantastic.  There are plenty of gluten-free options, veggie toppings and homemade style sauces not to mention that you can drizzle the whole thing with queso if you want to.  The menu is also great but slightly more expensive than the lunch buffet which can't be beat for $5, ice-cream included!  We also like the fact that the place seems family-run.

Very friendly service, and clean welcoming atmosphere! I was looking for a new place to go for a haircut in the Sparks area, and I think I found it!
Katie did a great job cutting my hair, and knew exactly what I wanted when I described it to her. Looking forward to coming in soon for color!

A year later and the quality has declined. The service was very slow and it was a quiet night. I again ordered my favorite, the Ahi Tuna Bowl. I only ate the rice. The tuna was tough and stringy. It was over seasoned with a Mexican spice but the bowl is asian inspired. The manager comped my meal. I won't be going back.

Typically this was my favorite place for brunch. Anytime friends visit me - I'm adamant about coming here. After this visit I can say I won't be back. The level of service we received was mediocre at best. I was also watching a short video clip on my phone and the server (who wasn't my own) tapped our table and said "do you mind turning that down?" Actually it wasn't that loud considering a DJ is playing music. Then he proceeds to make a "snide" comment to the table he was serving, "I can't even remember what I was going to say." Lastly, I ventured out of my normal routine and had the pork belly - didn't enjoy at all. Its been real BB - can't say I'll ever "darken your doorstep again." Wouldn't want to distract your clients from the horrible service and poor attitudes of waitstaff.

The Boyfriend and I are huge fans of burritos and Japanese curry separately, but when we found that Maru Global makes a Japanese curry burrito, the opportunity was too irresistible to pass up.

The beef curry burrito was amazing to bite into -- a nice creamy, spiced curry with carrot and potato.  Who would've known a combination of burrito and Japanese curry was so delicious?  Apparently the chef here at Maru Global whom we had a chance to meet as he was flattered when we took photos of his work.
Completely ignoring how full we were, we also tried its namesake takoyaki.  The spicy shrimp tasted so good and completely melted in your mouth it almost seemed sinful.

Thai and tacos, who would've thought they'd make such a great combination?  There's a reason this place hidden in a Drexel alleyway has received so much attention as of late...it's THAT good!  I noticed that today their prices had gone up by $1 for the Chicken Satay Tacos, only about a month ago they were $5 and now they're $6.  Still worth it in my opinion but the $1 increase is just at the far end of what's affordable for me.  Also, avoid the lunch rush as much as possible, its line can be long and so can its wait!

The best!  I managed to get TWO tools (brushes) stuck into my dryer vent ducts trying to clean the lint out myself. These two guys John and Skip came to my rescue removed the brushes and cleared the ducts of lint!  Very reasonable also. Highly recommended

Tucked away off of South Grand at Wyoming and Spring is this little corner pub with a great Pizza.   I have to say the Pizza is well worth the wait.  Sometimes you have to wait 30 minutes, others 45, sometimes upwards of an hour but the pizza is always amazing.  

The bar area is great.  It kind of reminds me of the dives my grandfather would take me to so he could grab a beer really quick when he was out running errands for my grandmother.  Smokey, dimmely lit, but delightful and lots of character.  There's always music playing, the walls have all sorts of customer art and funny messages on them from the many visitors both in town and out of town.  I think I could spend hours just reading all of the messages in on the walls in the dining room and the bathroom.  Either way I doubt I'd stop laughing.   

Late night the place really comes alive. Each time I've been there after 9 I've always left with a great memory and a great story.  The bar always has cheap pitcher specials to take you into the night during those long shuffle board tournaments or Golden Tee rounds.  

If you're a first timer, just know that it is going to take awhile to get your pizza if you ordered it. Just sit back, have a cocktail or three, and enjoy the company you're with. That is what the Black Thorn pub is all about.

Great place in the neighborhood for a good family dinner. The menu is basic (which was nice for my elderly mother) and the red sauce was REALLY good (nice for the rest of us)! The service was lovely and accommodating of our party including my elderly mother and my toddler. I ordered the pork ricotta, and it was really yummy. Not fancy, but really tasty. The spumoni dessert was great. I thought the prices were just right, and we'll be back!

Food is amazing. Great quality, good service. Lovely atmosphere. I was hesitant to come because it's a little pricey but portions are good and the food is worth it. I had the sausage pizza and toasted ravioli. They have a weekend brunch that I'm going to try next

I was routing for LaScala's before I even arrived, thinking it the perfect spot to have lunch with an out of town cp-worker.  It's close (which was its main draw) and Italian (who doesn't like Italian food?); yes, LaScala's seemed like the "safe" choice.  The decor is fine.  However, with the restaurant barely at capacity, we were originally sat at a wobbly table near the kitchen.  When we asked to move to another location, the hostess looked at me like I had suddenly sprouted some uncontrollable boil smack in the middle of my forehead, uttering, "Uh, okay."  Seated at our new table, I barely had 10 seconds to review the menu before we were prompted to order.  Folks, order...or you'll be waiting 10 - 15 minutes until the server comes back again.  We started with the caesar salad and calamari.  Both were decent in taste and portion size.  Our main courses came just as quickly, with one very big exception.  The server put in my entree as raviolis, not veal parmesan with angel hair.  I waited another 15 - 20 minutes for my food.  By the time my food arrived (sans angel hair, just regular spaghetti noodles), my fellow diners were more than half way through their food.  My entree did not blow me away by any means.  The sauce didn't take my breath away (good or bad) either.  On the plus side, the server was extremely apologetic and nice.  Being in the service business myself through a better part of college, I can empathize with minor mishaps (we're all human).  At the end of the day, I probably won't return....unless someone else is footing the bill!

Hands down my favorite restaurant in university city. If you've never been to Han you have to try the Dan Dan noodles when you get there. It's out of this world. Sometimes I just get two Dan Dans and a beer or two for lunch. The place is decently spaced out, there's a bar where you can sit at. They have a good selection of brews. 

The food is pretty good too. The menu has spicy ratings next to each item but You can pick the level of spiciness on a scale of one to ten. The service gets slow if when it's busy, mostly kids from Penn and Drexel working there. I would definitely recommend anyone and everyone to try Han dynasty at least once if not many more times.

Great first experience! I love that this place has a neighborhood bar feel, but with a hipness to it. We came for dinner on Friday night, and our cravings for comfort food were satisfied!
We had to wait a bit until a spot at the bar opened, but we were greeted right away while we stood by the doorway. We ended up eating at the bar too, which was fine with us! We were nestled by the window at the end of the bar, very cozy! Even though we were at the end of the bar, the bartender was very attentive and nice.
They have a nice beer selection which my boyfriend enjoyed! My interest was mostly in the food (of course) so we started with the cheese plate! 
I thought the size of the plate was appropriate for the price, and I enjoyed all of the cheeses. One of the grainy mustards was delicious! The other mustard is more of a Worcestershire sauce which cleared my sinuses, so beware! I also enjoyed the pickled veggies served with the platter, and the bread was to die for! Toasted and lightly buttered.
I was totally pleased with my dinner plate, the Caesar salad with fried chicken! The chicken was so tender and had a sweetness to it. The food definitely exceeded my expectations when dining at a pub. 
Overall, a great place to grab a drink and snack, or full on dinner! It was nice for a date as well, however it was a bit loud with the music and actual bar crowd that made its way in as the night went on.

While visiting Santa Barbara for a wedding, we rented a beachfront house and I set out to find someone to do (touch up) my lash extensions. Everyone I called said to go to Roxanne Manders at Alston Face & Body. She made room for me on such short notice and the place is beautiful. She touched me up and I just loved her attitude, professionalism and cleanliness of the whole place. She even sent me off with a little gift bag.
Thank you Roxanne for making me beautiful!

One good experience here but the most recent experience was awful. Guy behind the desk was ok but mechanic was a jerk. I brought in the car to get the cabin air filter changed and they charged me $600 for other stuff that was apparently wrong with it (which I went for, gullibly, bc I wanted to pass the inspection the next month). They assured me over the phone the air filter was included in the $600. Then as I'm picking up the keys (after paying) they slip in that "By the way, we couldn't find the cabin air filter, we don't think there is one." Twenty seconds later I find a YouTube video on locating and changing it, something that I've just managed to do in less than 15 mins. I wouldn't have minded if they had said they weren't going to do it, but to lie and then rack up my bill to that degree is ridiculous. As a woman who doesn't know enough about cars I expect to be played to some degree - but this was disgusting. They've lost a good customer and although they're right around the corner, I will not be back. I suggest you avoid it too.

My go to spot for my caffeine fix. Great location because it's typically on my way to most places. Only bad thing is very little parking but I always do drive-thru. The drive-thru line moves along fairly quick so no big deal.

Came in with my fiancé for a drink and a snack. I ordered a frozen white chocolate almond shiver drink, and it was so good! My fiancé got an iced tea, which she also enjoyed.  We shared a spinach and artichoke dip with tortilla chips.  It was served hot and bubbly, with melted cheese and big chunks of artichoke.  It was quite tasty!  The place is cute and was pretty steadily busy the entire time we were there.

Visited here for the first time after reading the reviews.  The food was very good; however, the service was lacking and most of the tables were complaining about the length of time it took to get their food.  The table next to us waited about 1/2 hour just to get a server to take their order. I had that Spaghetti Carbonara, which was delicious.  My wife ordered Eggplant Parm, which she said was really tasty. Our water and bread was never refilled. The waiter seemed more concerned about the customers on the outdoor patio.  The thing that annoyed me most was when I asked for change from the bill, it took forever to bring the change.  I asked another server if we could get the change and she responded with "change is really hard to find around here."  And then they gave me change but not the correct amount.  Guess they didn't want to give coins back but every establishment I've ever visited gives you the full change. I am a very good tipper (20-25%) as my former career was in a gratuity based industry but nothing annoys me more than when a waiter doesn't want to give you change because they feel it should all be theirs for a tip.

Typical Petsmart. I haven't been much of one to frequent Petsmart because I think almost all the food/treats they sell aren't of good quality - read up on canine or feline nutrition and you'll see why. They do now sell one brand that I approve of, Wellness, which is a new thing. I don't feed my pets this brand of food but I do buy their chewy grain free treats, which my dogs (one toothless) enjoy and can eat with no problem. Their prices on toys are pretty good too, as well as supplies.

What sets this Petsmart apart is the cat room! I am impartial perhaps. One warm summer day, I wandered by and saw a cute little kitten named Audrey. I fell in love and texted her pic to my now husband. He agreed to come see her. Then I looked at the other kitties and noticed a black older cat rubbing against the bars of his cage trying to get me to pet him. Later on- we came by and they were letting the kitties out of their cages. We saw little Audrey- what a cutie! Then I asked to see the black kitty - Fillmore. They opened his cage and he JUMPED into my arms, nestling his face into my shoulder and purring like crazy. SOLD! Fillmore became my first cat ever. That was the first and last time he liked me to hold him but he still is the coolest cat in the world!

Yay Petsmart for bringing us together!

Great lunch, AYCE sushi and hibachi place. My son ate a ton and we are headed back for his birthday this weekend. I am not a huge diner and the endless food was lost on me but the deep fried banana was amazing! The soups and apps were great and we look forward to sharing some new menu items on our next visit.

So the ice cream here is really great. The service on the ice cream side is always excellent, and they are very kind to the baby I typically bring in. 

The food side, however, is fairly lackluster. Service is fine, and it's an alright place to stop in for a quick lunch. However, nothing to write home about. The burgers are alright, the fries are pretty good, the salads are okay. 

I am giving it a three for the ice cream... That keeps this boat floating. If the food matched the ice cream, this would be a GREAT spot.

What can I say, I am a total fan. 

When they first opened, there were a few missing touches with their drinks but they quickly found their mojo.

I have visited the Truckee location before and that's where I tried their Cheddar Scallion Scone and oh my, it was a-ma-zing. So when I found out that they were coming to Reno, I was ecstatic. The only downside was they stopped making this pastry maybe a month after they opened their Reno location. I was really bummed. The barista I asked said that it was just not selling. I told her they can just make it for me and I will buy them all -- wishful thinking. I soon tried the Raspberry Ricotta Scone and this has been my new fave. I still wish that one day they would bring my old-school favorite back.

All in all, they have great pastries and sandwiches. Their crepes are also very tasty and they are huge, at least for me. Make sure to try the Espresso Chocolate Bar -- I have never had anything like this before. Another suggestion is the Lemon Ricotta Cookie -- you can totally taste the fresh lemons that were used for this goodness. My favorite sandwich is the Milano. The chipotle sauce (I think that's whats in there) is quite tasty with a tangy, spicy after taste.

As for drinks, I have absolutely loved their mate lattes. I think they are they only one in town that serves mate lattes but I could be totally wrong. I don't really drink coffee and am more of a tea drinker, which makes the mate lattes the perfect drink for me.

If you are around the area, this is a must-try for sure. Their decor is very welcoming, they added a "community table" that is quite impressive. Lots of room for meetings and small gathering. Oh, they have gelato too. Nutella gelato of all else. One word - Yummy.
Rooms are very clean, complimentary wifi for guests, and nice setup for breakfast and coffee. This hotel was much cleaner than neighboring hotels. I recommend this for lodging .

Went there for the first time 2 nights ago, and had a great meal!  Had a couple of apps, including the vegetable sampler and the seekh kabab, all of which were very good. For entres two in the party got various types of chicken kababs, both of which were very good. One kabab had some sort of mint marinade, and so the chicken was green, but delicious.  I had a vegetarian entree, which was also very good. My son got butter chicken--also good. Serving sizes kind of small, but in keeping with other Indian restaurants that I've been to in the past.  We got a couple naan orders also--the best one was one that was stuffed with a raisin/nut mixture--delicious. Overall, the service was very good, and the establishment was clean. Would go again in future.

Ran in here last night because I had forgotten to pack dinner and I was working a 9 hour shift.  Very convenient because it was right across the street from work.  

I was impressed when I walked in to the cafe area.  It reminded me of Whole Foods and how you can sit and enjoy a meal while getting all your needs in one place.  

I went with the salad bar and was impressed by their various choices and numerous toppings.  I also recommend the soup bar as well.  They had a few choices and I went with the old standby, Chicken Noodle.  You also get a roll with soup!

They have salads, soups, pre-packed sandwiches, and anything else your heart desires.  I will definitely be going back since it is conveniently located across the street from work!

Best thrift store in Tucson! Lots of selection, and there's usually a particular color tag that's 50% off each day. The store is roomy and well-lit, though the last time I went it seemed a little dingy and chaotic. Overall, a great place to look for clothes you'll only use once (Halloween costumes, coats for trips out of town, etc.), rarely-used small appliances, and the like.

Terribly filthy! The trash bins were overflowing. There was trash and garbage in the theater. When we left there was no sign of anyone coming to clean. The trash bins were full in the restrooms as well and most of the soap dispensers were empty. For what they charge for admission this was unacceptable.

Primo-sized hoagies.  Ruby's diner-like burgers.  Nifty Fifty's-like milkshakes.

this place is the definition of a simple local shop that consistently puts out great food.
Would not recommend this place it was one of the worse meals I have eaten....very over priced the food had no flavor the coconut cake was very dry too..save your money.

good mall with lots of stores. mostly expensive stores like bebe, coach, michael korrs etc. but still a great mall with lots of stands and good food. it also has a target and barnes and noble which is awesome. lots of bathrooms too
Sat outside by the fountain and had a pleasant lunch. Fish sandwich was fresh and delicious and the potato chips were fresh and warm.  Cold beer, nice breeze, and what more could you ask for?

I have been here twice. Once for a beer before shooting pool at Buffalo Billiards and once just getting a 6 pack to go. First experience was not horrible-draft beer was ok but the place is dirty and dingy. The second experience was laughable-the bartender/manager was visibly intoxicated, was slurring her words and charged us for each beer bottle at individual bar prices. This place is a total joke designed specifically to rip off tourists.

I keep forgetting not to order from here. Nasty food.Delivery comes faster than expected.They always forget to add eating utensils.If you like hot mustard don't forget to ask for it because they never put that in the bag as well.

Introduced to this by a friend and fell in love with it. I always make it a point to try something different each time here, especially the donuts. I don't normally have a sweet tooth, but this place changes it for me.#nomnation

A friend took me to this place in search of pieces for a costume, and I was in awe of the selection.  Personally, I think this place is untapped by most of Philly's hipsters (due to being so far out of the way on Wolf street), and thank god for that.  Like the second mile in West Philly, which I reviewed earlier, you've got to DIG, but the finds are well worth the effort.  

They also have some really wacky housewares and toys.  It's definitely worth the trek for those in search of oddities.  In fact, that whole neighborhood is quite odd, so it's an interesting trip down there overall.

I want to say that I agree with Jaski, in my last experience at Sake House service was sub-par. The waitress was quick to neglect the table, M.I.A. when I needed things like a refill or a fork for my meal (seriously not everyone knows how to use chopsticks). The waitress almost seemed to give annoyed glances when she would be getting our order. She took forever to bring our check in an almost empty restaurant. We had to get up and walk to the register so we could pay because waiting for her was going to take forever. I almost didn't tip her, but I felt bad because I really liked this place last time...so I left her a small tip and hope the next time I come back won't be like this.

The sushi was still good, but I just had to update my review to reflect this service issue.

We could not have had a better experience here.  We stayed in the King Deluxe room this past weekend -- perfect ambiance for romance complete with fireplace and whirlpool en suite.  The location is terrific with both Stearns Wharf and State Street within walking distance, and it's right around the corner from a market, liquor store with a very nice wine selection, and a local brewpub.  The breakfast was lovely in the AM, and our stay came with a free wine tasting at a nearby place that is right on the Urban Wine Trail.  Very friendly staff that helped with all of our questions.  Would recommend this place to anyone looking for a fun little romantic weekend getaway.

Favorite, favorite, favorite place in Philly, hands down. Been there three different times now and each time has been pleasurable and cheap.

Bruschettas are hand-licking good - have tried the caramalized onion, truffled mushroom, garlic and pesto, pistachio + honey, and the brie + cherries ones. All are good but my faves are the garlic and pesto and the pistachio + honey.

I always get the Three Cheese and Tomato Panino to split which is a good sized portion if you're splitting between two people. It comes with a side salad as well. Finally, the sweets are to *die* for; try the banana and mascarpone panino -- it's different and surprisingly good.

I'll always be a fan of this place. Love.

Closest (and still far) Froyo place. Move closer please.

Expensive, delicious, DIY, individualized, tantalizing, fun, trendy, and easy. Not as healthy as they make it out to be, but oh well. I'll work it off later.

there are defiantely certain times of the day i will not frequent certain fast food places. this Rally's lunch is usually pretty solid. i really like the wings and fries. sometimes the buns can be stale and the meat overcooked. all and all not to bad for a fast food place.

First off... The menu says Caesar salad with croutons. A Caesar needs croutons. We had to ask for them after the salad was served to us. Some other girls at another table had the same problem. I thought perhaps it was a new chef or something but now seeing all these bad reviews, I'm not so sure. 

Secondly, they have this advertised deal on the board and the waiter told us all about 25¢ wings... The wings were ok, nothing special. But, here is the problem and we learned a lesson as we don't really look at bills for accuracy all the time. We had already had our card swiped and then I looked at the bill and thought it was pretty high for what we got. I saw that they had charged us 8.95 for the wings! I'd like to give them the benefit of the doubt that it was a simple mistake but something tells me this probably happens a lot. I'm glad I noticed. 

It was nice to be able to sit out on the sidewalk and they will probably still thrive with all the drunk idiots that frequent this area at night.

We love this Childcare Center! I would give it 5 stars if they had a check in app of some sort like more expensive schools. However for the price we pay of $100/wk I give it 4 1/2 stars! My son has attended from 6 mths to 3.5 yrs old. We deeply trust the manager (& her Mom helps too.) It is a diverse, multicultural school with socioeconomic & racial diversity (important to us.) They got a recent Governor's award. zThey have 3 Stars. They Accept childcare assistance. Their food quality (which they provide) is quite good (although I would like to see more fresh fruit & veggies for snacks & oatmeal or healthy alternatives for breakfast.) I have liked all of his teachers so far. They did a good job potty training which he was under 3. The manager is a cancer survivor & very proactive about this cause & supporting others in the fight. 

This week is fun back to school summer fun week. The kids made Sundaes one day, they're having slip and slides and water play day today with cotton candy and candy covered apples, tomorrow they're making fruit cups,  and they've had visits from magicians and the zoo.

This Center has been a blessing to our life.
awful inedible slop the pork was rancid just disgusting,egg rolls were decent

"Babies don't need a vacation, but I still see them at the beach... it pisses me off! I'll go over to a little baby and say 'What are you doing here? You haven't worked a day in your life!'"

-Steven Wright 

They also don't need to shop, but I still see them here, bossing their parents around. 

Alas, I will be one of those parents in two short months. 

I never realized an unborn baby could be so expensive. The little thing isn't even here yet and we have already dropped the equivalent of this year's allowable IRA contribution at this store and others.

The products and service here are OK. About average. Sign up for their rewards program and get 20% off coupons that you can't use on half of the products in the store.

Big City Subs was reliably basic and delicious.  Good quality ingredients and friendly staff.  UNFORTUNATELY, as I learned today the hard way, they have closed (gone out of business?) and been replaced by some Juice World B.S.  We cannot subsist on liquids alone!!

I have been here twice since it has opened. First of all, great signage. It is extremely clear what your options are: Lassi, fresh fruit juice, shaved ice, milk shakes, and ice cream amongst other options. There are a few interesting flavors that I have yet to try, including the salt lassi (buttermilk) and sandalwood. 

The owner is extremely nice. He takes time to talk to customers about what goes into each item that is ordered. He's also plied us with a few generous samples of milkshakes, lassi, and ice cream. 

I have had a strawberry and mango milkshake so far and have sampled lassi ordered by a few of my friends. Everything was tasty. You know when a milkshake is good and everything is where it needed to be. We also sampled the fresh watermelon juice. It was like drinking a watermelon. 

FYI, the shakes are lighter than the lassi, so if you want something on the lighter side go with one of those. 

It is really nice to see a shop akin to an ice cream parlor in West Philly, especially one as unique as Mood Cafe. Go order something!

By far, the worst company I have ever dealt with. I am ashamed an American company can be, and is, so incompetent. I have to make numerous calls, scream and cuss out managers, to get anything done. I have Tri-care health care coverage so I have no other mail order pharmacy options.
I lived in Camden Bay apartments when they were brand new!! I would recommend it. I rate it #2 on my list from a scale of 1-10. Me and my daughter loved it.

Love this spot!  It's our go-to for hibachi.  They are very consistent with their service and quality, and the lunch buffet is cheap with just the right proportions to leave you satisfied.  No food hangover when you're done.  Awful health score? Didn't know about that one... Never eaten their sushi either.  All I gotta say is double yum yum

Love byo's and this little addition to the neighborhood is exactly the right combo- great sushi + byob. The decor is similar to Fat Salmon, whom I love- trendy, back lit, with seating all along the wall to accommodate a large group, or just two. The service was quick and friendly. And if there was a rating for presentation, these guys get 5 stars! I expected some sashimi a la cart, arranged nicely on a plate, but what came out was a martini glass with my salmon & hamachi on a bed of ice, with a beautiful pink flower. next to it was a mushroom shaped carving from what i guess is some kind of root. and at the base of the plate where my mackerel sat was some food art from spicy mayo sauce. I know some may think this is gimmicky...(and maybe is is??) but the sashimi was fresh & tasty. and anyone who puts that much effort & care into presentation shows they care a lot about food.

Way overpriced and extremely rude.  Tried to call for reservation several times and nobody answered.  Mentioned this to the person I assumed to be Angelo when he asked why we didn't have a reservation, and to which he scoffed at me as if I was lying.  I would have left if it weren't for the groupon we needed to use.  As we sat at the bar we meet five other couples that experienced the same issue and same rude attitude.  While we disagreed as to whether the place was more over priced than it was medicore and rude, we all agreed that we won't be bothered when this place goes under.
I think that the pizza here was absolutely awful. It was also very overpriced. The service was incredibly slow. I do not recommend coming to this place.

Montecito is a small town. I mean it's not Perryville, Arkansas but a small town none the less. Elegant, ritzy, privileged, conservative might be words to describe this slightly hidden onclave.

So walking into Tre Lune restaurant it represented it's atypical demographic very nicely.....as it should.

The bar in the back makes generous strong drinks. Their wine list is well thought out. The service is very respectful and the food is real good. Pretty much everything I just mentioned is what a Montecito local would want and expect in their environment. 

My caesar salad was very good. My meatballs and spaghetti was great. My friends pasta bolognese was equally delicious. Our wives shared a branzino which they loved and our chosen Caberet was excellent. All done in a somewhat upper class, casual way. That might sound snooty, but it wasn't. I mean that in a good way.

Tre Lune was a very nice dinner, in this very nice small town, where there are very nice people.
Stopped by on our way through Nashville and we loved every bite. Great food, tasty frozen drinks, and super reasonable prices. Yum

I'm not originally from Indianapolis, so there isn't the nostalgia  for me others have mentioned. Also, I don't eat meat, so it did limit my choices. With that said, I tried the black bean and rice burrito. It was huge and the prices are very reasonable. All in all, I did think it was good, but just not great. If you are a meat eater, I would say check out Roscoe's, if in the area.

Looking for one of our last few happy hours to end the residency year, me and my co-residents found ourselves at Barrio Brewing. Luckily for us, Barrio Brewing ended up having a great selection of beer and finger foods. We all went through several rounds of beer and really enjoyed chatting away in the fun atmosphere. I am sad I was unable to come here more often before I left Tucson but I know for sure that I'll be looking for their beer in the future.

My eyes r still watering .. What the heck the smell of ammonia was overpowering at the bar .. Food service and ambience don't matter when u can not breathe ! Really this was bad . Can not imagine what happened to require that disinfecting ...

We came here last night for a few drinks and to check the place out.  My fiance has been trying to get me to go, and my New Years Resolution is to stop saying no to everything new.

We walked in, and weren't sure if you had to seat yourself or if there was a hostess, but nobody at the bar acknowledged us walking in, so we just sat ourselves.  We were very quickly approached by a guy who sat a huge white binder on our table and explained, to my horror, that it was karaoke night.  I have taken singing lessons, have had solos in choirs, and sing constantly at home, but there is something about karaoke that I just wont do.  We sat for a while before the waitress came up and apologized for the wait.

I ordered and Arizona Sunrise, and Richard got the Hurricane.  Before we got our drinks, Mr. Karaoke came up and asked us if we had picked a song.  Richard said he had, but was trying to get me to sing also.  Our drinks finally came out and we ordered the Depot Sampler.  The karaoke guy came up again.  Five minutes later, he came up again.

We tried to order different drinks, but when I flagged the waitress down and said I would like another drink, she took that to mean I wanted the same one and didn't even ask Richard if he wanted another one.  When she got back, he said he would like another Hurricane and two Jaeger bombs.  The Jaeger bombs were warm, even the energy drinks were room temperature.  (during which time, the karaoke guy came up AGAIN, and asked if I needed more "liquid courage")

Our appetizers came out after a while, and it wasn't horrible, but it wasn't amazing.  Actually, the mozzarella sticks, which I don't really like, were really tasty.  The breading on them was very flavourful.  Karaoke guy came up while we were eating.

Our waitress never came back after that.  I had been harassed enough by Richard(reminding me of my resolution) and the karaoke guy to sing Paradise By The Dashboard Light with Richard.  It was horrifying.  Nothing to do with the bar, or it's rating, but I did not want to do it, and it was just as humiliating as I had thought it would be.

We flagged down our waitress, who, when she was actually at our table, very pleasant and after another 10 minutes we got our check and left.  I think it was pretty expensive, after by myself having two Arizona Sunrises, two Jeager Bombs and a Blue Moon Beer to not feel any kind of buzz.  It doesn't take me a whole lot to get a little tipsy, and I sure didn't leave with that feeling.

In all, I am not sure I will be back, definitely not on karaoke night.

The gyros are great.  The tacos are great.
The staff are friendly and the prices are good.  

They are open late.

I love this place.

Not too long ago they announced that they got new ownership. That meant that the bar opened up again and the worn/torn booths were replaced with new fresh ones, yay!
Don't expect a fancy Asian cousin. But do expect to find "traditional Amercan/Asian" dishes served the way you like them. 
Fulin's is not an expert on the Chinese, Thai or Japanese kitchen, but the mix of dishes are perfect and they do each and every one of them with style.
I think we keep coming back because we know everyone in the company will find something they like here, that includes kids! 
Thai red curry dishes, Sushi roles made right in front of you, extra spicy General Tso's chicken (if you like real spicy, ask for it!) Sweet and sour prawns and egg roles. They got it all.

Every kind of hipster works here. Bearded leisure shirt, nautical sea captain, handlebar mustache, eggs on the elbows. 

This place is meant to savor. These people take their time to create a plate pleasing to both pallet and eyes. Talk, people watch, strike a convo with the person next to you. 

I went with the lamb patty melt and this fatty approves! I also had a chance to sample the ham and gruyere pancake and latke. So good! To drink, I had a latte, no sugar required, with foam treated like canvas.

I can't wait to revisit this place as the weather heats up and they begin to seat the patio and open those garage doors. 

5 stars across the sky!

My first experience with Jackson's was back in March, when I was traveling to Nashville for the first time with a bunch of friends who were Vandy grads. They love love love Jackson's from their time in college, and therefore it was literally our first stop of the weekend -- and it was wonderful. I wasn't sure what to expect, since it was a favorite from college days -- but the food was simply delicious.

It has a low-key easy vibe inside, with art from local artists for sale, and the Bistro description is perfect to describe the food. Not heaping portions, but I was stuffed at the end of the meal, and absolutely satisfied.   We started off with martinis which were delightfully strong and full of flavor, and headed for lunch at a table shortly thereafter. Since it was a celebratory weekend, we started with appetizers, and the spinach dip, and the pigs in blankets with the amazing spicy mustard went in seconds. All very flavorful, I just wish I could have had another bite -- and take gallons of the mustard home with me.

Heading to lunch, I got the Rio Panini, and since I do love the standard thick bread one would think of for a panini, I was slightly sad to see white sandwich bread. It was a great sandwich, as were the fries, and the chips that I tasted off my friends plate. I think next time I'll go with the Rio wrap instead -- had ordering envy of my friends who went with that selection. But was in no way dissatisfied with my choice.

I was back again in Nashville this weekend, and stopped again with a large group for lunch. I expected a wait, as the bistro was packed with World Cup fans, but they easily worked with us, and found us a table quickly. Again, each person in the group constantly remarked on the quality of the food, and each had a different drink -- mine, the misery & gin -- pear cider, st. germain ginger liquor, and Tanqueray, was light and refreshing -- perfect for a hot day.  This time, I got this shrimp wrap, and the chopped salad, and ate every morsel off my plate. The shrimp had a slight kick to it, and it had so many flavors in each bite, I savored it until the very end.

I can say without a doubt that every time I'm in Nashville, I will absolutely be back for another boozy lunch at Jackson's!

Wonderful music and interesting environment
I took my girlfriend here
she really liked it

Enjoyed our meal at Valentino's.  Greeted professionally ,  waitstaff on point.  Ole school decor.  Bib salad delicious.  Osso Bucco was really good and quite filling.  Went upstairs to enjoy Johnny on the piano. A treat !!!!

What do you do when you are extremely hungry, locked inside of a venue, and there is a food truck? You walk up to that food truck and you order the giant hot dog and you inhale it. This food truck is New Orleans and that's why I needed to give it a try.  The hot dog was massive and since I'm a boring person I got mine plain. There's not much to say about a food truck, the staff was nice and the food was delicious, give it a try!

Located on Lower State, Zen Yai is a cozy little restaurant that almost always has a wait. Although Santa Barbara is not known for fantastic Thai food, Zen Yai hits the spot when you're craving Thai food. I am particularly fond of their Panaang Curry with Chicken as its a nice and spicy dish. I've tried several other dishes as well, but the panaang curry is still my favorite. The curry is spicy but it also has depth and the green beans are still nice and crispy. I usually like Pad Thai, but I find that pad thai at zen yai can be a little inconsistent. Sometimes its great and other times the noodles are overcooked. I do, however enjoy the Spicy Fried Rice - big surprise! I LOVE spicy food! 

The ambiance is nice for a date and the service is usually pretty friendly :) Although there's Thai food in Goleta, I'll gladly make the drive downtown to visit Zen Yai :)

As far as animal shelters go this is best one I've ever visited. 

It is a no-kill shelter so off the bat that makes it more laudable than the typical county animal control office. I visited several times before I finally adopted and each time there were plenty of staff on hand to assist me and the other patrons around me. I also noticed that there was always someone constantly monitoring the animal areas to clean up accidents. There is a huge fenced area in back for socializing with the animals and also private fenced areas for interaction without a leash. 

Unfortunately the dog I adopted came from a puppy mill situation. I had a lot of questions about the challenges I would face socializing and training her. The staff got me in touch with one of their experts and he went into great detail explaining what to expect and how to overcome the issues. He also spent a great deal of time monitoring the potential dog's interaction with my existing dog. I've never been to a shelter that was willing to give so much attention to a single customer.  The employees truly seem to care about finding a good match for both the animal and the person. 

As an added bonus for your own peace of mind, I was informed that if you run into any issues after your adoption you can leverage one of the shelter's socialization experts who will even make a home visit for no charge. 

All in all I was extremely impressed by the level of service and conditions at this facility. Compared to other shelters I have visited it is almost like doggie adoption utopia. I can't stress enough that if you are looking to adopt an animal a visit here should be mandatory.

A must-do in STL! Absolutely love the great pumpkin and the Big Apple. They are concretes with a slice of pie blended in. You get these nice chunks of goodness in there and it's so delicious and fun to eat! 
I like the terramizzou as well. My dog gets a kiddie bowl of plain custard and he loves it so very much! Lines can be really long but don't let them scare you! It moves fast!!
Wouldn't say it's the best Indian food I had, but I suppose it's decent and cheap (for the lunch buffet anyways).  On the positive, they had a wide variety of food.

Finally, some really good Thai food! And when I say good, what I mean is spicy, fresh, spicy and nice and spicy. 

The Pad Thai with Tofu, lunch size portion, was good sized and even came with a spring roll. My guest and I got out for right around $25 total and he had the egg drop soup. I ordered my meal spicy, and boy did I get it! Just the way I like it: bite, chew, sweat. Bite, chew, sweat. :)

Service was good and the waitress was very pleasant. In fact, I really can't remember having a better experience at a Thai restaurant, lunch or dinner. 

It's right next to ANOTHER Thai place on S. Dale Mabry that I've never tried, so don't get them confused. This one is farther south.
Great local place that you can rely on each time for a quality meal.
Delicious and reminds me of authentic Brooklyn pizza. Will be going back to try other items for sure.

I needed a manicure for my wedding (I NEVER have my nails done either gels- I work with dogs, there's no point.) I had NO IDEA what I was doing, just that I wanted gel, and the tip color to match my dogs' bow ties for the wedding. I had a picture of the style/length/shape of nail I wanted. I picked a color and was seated to get started on immediately. My ONLY problem with how they operate- they kept switching technicians throughout your appointment. One did my cuticles (god bless her- it was a 20 min ordeal) and then another woman placed the acrylics on, while a third woman traded spots with her to apply the gel. Then they rotated again with painting and all the grinding tools they use to get the acrylic out when the gel is dry. If I was regular customer- and they knew what I wanted, it wouldn't have been any issue (and I'm sure they rotate so the customer receives each tech's best abilities) but since I'm not AT ALL a regular, with each new person, they didn't know what look they were going for (only the tech I started with saw the picture and didn't show/tell the other employees) 
I will say that despite my "pet peeve", they still get a raving 5 star review. My nails (which I'm about to go get ripped off) have been on for SIX WEEKS now! And if it wasn't for the fact that my nails are growing out too far, they'd still look awesome. NOTHING HAS CHIPPED! Not a damn thing! There's no moisture getting underneath, it's incredible. I guess they know what they're doing when they switch people around. The finished product...well, it's pretty much perfect. I would HIGHLY RECOMMEND this nail salon. 
I posted a picture of my nails from last weekend- so they're 5 weeks old and were just starting to loose that shiny top coat.

I booked this bus after reading the Yelp reviews. 

I loved the fact that you can personalize the bus with your own wording. It's something so different and personalized that allows your event to be unique. 

I rented the bus for a wine tour in the Santa Barbara area for my 30th birthday. I was having a Great Gatsby 1920s theme so it went perfect. 

Darin was extremely helpful and professional from when I initially sent out the e-mail inquiring for a price quote. He helped me pick out locations that would accommodate large groups as I had about 20 people joining us. He was extremely knowledgeable of the area and made wonderful suggestions. He took a lot of pressure of having to plan the whole day. He provided me with an itinerary that was perfect for my themed party. The contract portion was easy to follow through with and he updated any changes made. Once again he is just so helpful and friendly. 

Our driver LEVI was just AMAZING. From the get go he texted me his ETA that morning and was super professional and helpful. He kept us on track and updated us with times until we had to head out to the next stop. Honestly he is probably one of the most polite bus drivers I've met. He helped us at every stop and made sure that they were treating us well. He even volunteered to take pictures of our group and never hesitated when we would hand him one more phone. THE WHOLE group absolutely loved Levi! Couldn't have asked for a better driver. I loved the fact that the bus had an aux cable which made it easy to play our own music and also having the waters came in handy! 

I can't wait for any excuse to rent another bus form this company. I've been on plenty of party buses for my birthday and wine tours and this by far has been the VERY best!!!

Oh my deliciousness!!! Went here last night at the last minute with my friends...they had a reservation for 5, but the staff was very gracious to change it to 6 at the last minute!!  I have been dying to try this place after walking past it about 43 times.  FInally, I got my wish. 

The owner is such a sweet, friendly man and greeted my friend, who made the reservation, by name.  He sure knows how to run a restaurant.  

The food is seriously amazing.  Everything comes out seriously, piping hot! I couldn't decide what to get, so I made a split second decision and went for the Canelloni(sp?).  Oh. My. God. I honestly wanted to lick the plate. It was that good....everything about it is utter perfection: the portion size, the sauce, the cheese...oh so good!

As for the others: Diver Scallops - they looked SO good and I hear they were delicious! I'll be getting those next time!; Parpadella with lump crab meat - Looked amazing, and my friend, who is a bit of a foodie, said it was divine; Rigatoni with Sausage - my friend, Brian wanted to lick his plate, need I say more?!; Veal Medallions - I'm not into veal, but apparently it was seriously good stuff! 

I can't wait to go back!! It may be tiny, but it packs a serious punch! It's definitely in my top 2 Italian BYO's in the city!

Love this place! It's my husband's and I's favorite spot in Zionsville. Always friendly and attentive service. Excellent food. You have to try their scallops and filet mignon or applewood chicken salad: both are divine. Wish they would do the old version of the raspberry torte though, not a huge fan of the current nutella torte version. They do have a gluten free menu, hoping as they grow they will add and expand it, as well as offer more dairy free options (health issues).

The funky band drew us in as we were walking down Bourbon St. The band was great, but unfortunately, the rude bartenders and the really pushy shot girls drove us right out in less than 20 min. Drinks were expensive and we didn't even get limes for our gin and tonics. I hope this band finds a better place, because they were awesome and deserve a better venue.

We were tired, hungry and in no way able to make a decision upon arrival to the French Quarter... our hostess, Christina, said go to Mr B's...it's the best food I've had in the quarter!   Pliable and trusting, we stumbled down Royal Street and entered the best night of our lives with Michael the bartender and David our dining companion and numerous other jovial Saturday night folks. The food was heavenly (barbequed shrimp and the wedge salad with a delightful local October fest ale) and the companionship wonderful... it was a glorious entry into our New Orleans vacation

Seems that all drinks here are made with a gas station style machine.. ironic for a business called the human bean.  Iced coffee was bitter and the chai latte was about 3x as sweet as what you would get at Starbucks. Second star for nice, friendly service.
Very good but you need a reservation if you're doing the Hibachi.  Staff is very polite and professional.

I joined LA Fitness about 8 months ago. The facilities are nice and they seem to be kept clean. I love the fact that they have racquetball courts and a pool. I would love to play more basketball but the gym is always packed. It is always fairly busy when I go. 

Their sales staff is a little pushy and I was really excited on how they treated my sister-in-law when she went to use her 3 day trial. I think it is nice price for the facilities and options they have. My wife likes to go to the Zumba classes. I like that they offer different classes!

If you want a little taste of New Orleans this is the place to go. I am from the South and have visited NOLA many times. The Mufaletta here was as good as any I have had in New Orleans. Fried Mac and cheese were also good. Food was out in no time. Definitely worth a stop.

Yesterday I had the pleasure of being able to enjoy my first Picasso and Wine for my birthday. My boyfriend and i attended the 11:00 class to paint a Charlie Brown Christmas tree. It was over all a great experience. The mimosa and Moscow mule was great! The bartender was amazing. The teacher was great as well. But the assistant unfortunately turned both my boyfriend and I off. For starters she scolded us about not keeping paint on our brushes. And I understand that paint brushes are expensive and they want them taken care of. But it's all in the approach. She approached us as if we were children instead of grown adults. And honestly the paint brush didn't have paint on it. It had already been rinsed in the water and cleaned off with a paper towel. I think one thing to remember with these classes is your dealing with some people that have NEVER painted and this is a new experience for them. I think if she had approached us differently it would not have turned us off so much. But over all we had a great a experience!

Burger Up is incredible! The vibe is great, service is good, staff is friendly, and the food is AMAZING. Although I have only tried their veggie burgers, they are hands down the best veggie burgers I've ever had (I crave Burger Up multiple times a month). Figured after having five awesome experiences here, I'd write a review so people know what to expect when visiting this spot. Cheers!

Really cute place that is run by a husband and wife team. The Bibimbap in a stone pot was delicious and fairly priced. The portion size was solid and I left feeling completely satisfied. I agree that this is a hidden gem and worth going to, especially if you live in the area. Also, I like supporting nice small businesses like these. The owners were very friendly and nice and other than the Bibimbap, my wife really liked the Ginger Cinnamon Tea. 

Of note, they take Credit Cards. I think the yelp reviews previously had said cash only. 

4+ for the food, extra star for kindness.

Great employees, great products/selection, outstanding race/event managing ... I go to FF at least twice a week and have been doing so for the last 2 1/2 years. This is where I get my nutrition, my shoes, and most of my running clothes and accessories. FF also trained me for my first 1/2 marathon and will train me for my first full this upcoming fall. I love the social runs on Wednesday nights and Saturday mornings as well. FF can't be beat.

This place kicks ass !!!!!!!!!!!! Drinks are at a great price you can get drunk and still go home with money. People are nice food is real good for a pub style you can smoke out back the place looks sick too. Really nice job with it.

Great customer service. They let us bring our large Pomeranian up on the patio with us, where he stayed tucked away under our chairs.  They even brought a bowl of water out for him.

Our food was really good. The price is reasonable ($20 for two) for sit down cafe food.

Since I travel so much for my job. I have he rare opportunity to eat at so many different places. I chanced on this place. Parking isn't exactly the easiest. But where in Santa Barbara is easy for parking?! This place makes that all go away. Service is outstanding. I accidentally left my CC there for a week. They remembered who I was, and had it waiting for me. This just doesn't happen in today's service related establishments. I've since taken family and friends to experience this first hand. Funny that I haven't got to the best part. Their food is off the charts. I frequent this place for breakfast while I'm working in the city. I've had lunch here a couple times. Same as B-fast. Doesn't disappoint. Highly recommend the Santa Barbara local omelette, add try-tip. A lot of food but you have to try it. I could go on and on. One last thing. One of the waiters there asked me my name after my second visit. Several weeks later, ran into him. Remembered my name. Just great food with sincere friendly service.

Stayed here while in town for our anniversary. Parking was very expensive. Valet is $30+ and self-parking is $25. Check-in was very quick. The lady checking us in asked what the occasion was and we told her about our anniversary and she offered us a few amenities like chocolate covered strawberries and champagne, but we were unsure if they were complimentary or not, so we passed. We were placed on the 15th floor with a very poor view of the other side of the hotel and a sliver of a view of the river. The room was very clean and really modern. The lobby is a little confusing because it is so large, but very modern. 

However...the walls of our room were paper thin. We could hear a couple laughing and talking all night long between the wall. 

Checkout was as quick as check-in was. We had problems exiting the garage all night long so getting out was, once again, a pain. 

Overall, great night and very close to everything!

I absolutely loved the environment here! I work from home and am new to the area.  I have been wanting to explore local coffee shops versus the chains, and Bandit was awesome.

It's a very minimalist design, with big long tables to work alongside people, as well as smaller tables along the wall.  I do wish there was some outdoor seating, though.

I visited on a Tuesday afternoon and upon walking up, was thrilled to see several people with their laptops out as well.  It's definitely a working environment mid-week, and I really enjoyed that.  I had an iced espresso, which was so great!  

There is a lot attached as well as street parking.

This could easily become a staple for me!
For cocktails, try the "Kali". Bourbon, hibiscus, lillet, sparkling wine. Damned refreshing.

Awesome all the way around!

You expect a great atmosphere when you're on Frenchmen street, but Three Muses has a really cozy feel to it that just makes you want to come in and stay forever.  We had a great band when we were there and were able to grab a table right by the bar so all we had to do to place an order is turn around and say what we wanted - that made the experience even better (otherwise you would have to walk up to the bar to place your order).

The food is simply outstanding.  We had:

Steak and Cake - Nicely cooked slices of steak coupled with a PERFECTLY prepared crab cake (just enough crisp on the outside).

Pork Belly - Excellent.  Served on little pancakes with some apple slices.  Just a great dish.

Feta Fries - A must have.  Good fries, lots of feta, seriously you can't go wrong with this one.

We loved everything we ate here, and ran out of time before we could order desserts, I'm sure those would've been awesome as well.  The drinks here are nicely prepared as well and fairly creative as far as the combinations.

Just a great, great place.  Absolutely LOVED it.

This inn's only positive point is that it is on the streetcar line and free Wi-fi, which makes it easy to visit different places around town. Upon arrival, our room hadn't been cleaned. Honestly, it looked like only the sheets had ever been changed. Nasty dirty baseboards, a dusty fan, shower and sink covered with other people's hair, dirty mirrors,  and holey, stained sheets. I informed the cleaning staff, and they took care of some of it, but I still never felt clean and relaxed during our stay. And I brought my own Lysol wipes on our stay, which was a good move. 

Best part-- my boyfriend found a tick on him after our second night there. When we got back to the inn around 10pm, our room hadn't been cleaned up and we had no clean towels. Luckily someone was in the washroom downstairs and had some to give us. 

We booked last minute and will never do that again. I'd rather pay $300 a night to stay at a nicer hotel than be worried about prior guests' hair haunting me in my sleep. Stay at your own risk, and bring your flip flops and multiple towels from home. Then burn them  on your way out.

I've had gelato before, I've had water ice, icies, slurpies, slushies, Italian ices, ice creams, and really this place is definitely on my list of favorite frozen treats. If you've never had gelato and you like to savor your ice cream using small bites, this place is for you.

This gelato is delicious - very smooth and either rich or light depending on the flavor. I had the dark chocolate which was like eating chocolate cake batter. It was a little overwhelmingly sweet for my taste, but still very good. I have the coconut milk one as well which was creamy and was definitely the defining characteristic of gelato: smooth and refreshingly rich. The last and most surprising flavor was the grapefruit. It was my absolute favorite and I am very happy that I picked it. It was tangy, yet creamy and very smooth. I found it to be incredibly refreshing and light and definitely a worthy flavor. 

The flavors were reminiscent of European ice cream shop soft-serve flavors, which was very nostalgic. 

What I did not like: the price. It was just way too much. Sure they use quality ingredients and it is locally made, and it's trendy and a nice spot- but really? $7 for a medium (which is equivalent to about half a cup.) Not a place that I would go every day, that's for sure. Definitely much better quality than the over-priced LA-NYC chain Pinkberry (I'm only comparing the two because of price otherwise they really have nothing in common.)

What it is good for: If it's a hot night and you're with-in a five block radius and have a group of friends - everyone is destined to find something they like there.

The first time I pulled into the parking lot of this restaurant I stared at my co-worker asking him if it this was a joke. It is located adjacent to a sketchy looking Budget Inn that could easily be the set for the Bates Motel. The restaurant itself is very much a mom and pop gig with limited frills. However, the food is actually quite decent with a varied menu that includes chile rellenos, fajitas, chalupas, tacos, enchiladas and more. The chips come out hot the second you sit down and the salsa is fresh and there is an endless supply. 

The service is quick, friendly and efficient. Again with no frills--which I am ok with when I want to eat and get back to work. 

It is a great place to grab a quick bite. You will leave feeling satisfied. Just watch your back and your purse as you get into your car.
The coffee is so good and different, they I've picked some up and it's coming home with me.  The beignets are wonderful good.  The service is friendly and the style is vintage.
My suspicion about too-tough octopus being a regular problem has been confirmed...kinda disappointing.

I want to give this place a chance but so far my two experiences haven't been exactly great. I've only ordered to go and haven't actually dined so that may be another story. But the first time, they were rather busy but I felt like there was no attempt whatsoever at customer service. Food was decent-I get their tofu vegetable spring roll and it's cheap but also rather bland. It's just tofu, lettuce, and some vermicelli. The second time, I called it in and they got my order wrong. The lady who took the order doesn't  seem to understand English very well, which is fine but she didn't own up to the mistake, either. She insisted I ordered a veggie pho and shrimp spring rolls.

3.5/5 We stopped in for a quick bite and some drinks. We had the bagel + cream cheese, a bowl of fruit, and an English muffin... The food was delicious! Only complaint was the expense. One bottle of cider was $8 and it wasn't even that good. We might come back at a later time for brunch if we want to have a fancy meal.

I bought a living social deal here and with all the great reviews I thought I couldn't pass up the deal. I definitely should have. 
First off, I drove by the sketchy house turned nail salon and thought...there is no way I am getting my nails done here. It looks incredibly unprofessional from the outside. However, again, due to the good reviews and since I had already paid for the deal, I figured what the heck! The looks of the inside do make up for the outside, but the service did not. I received the worst pedicure I've ever gotten. The nail polish was literally poured onto my toes. I immediately drove up to Flagstaff after the appointment and even after the 4 hour drive there were spots that hadn't dried yet! I ended up just taking it all off at that point and painting them myself.
I also got the shellac manicure. This did come out better than the pedicure, however the color that I picked and the color that was put on my nails was definitely not the same. Usually shellac can last at least 2-3 weeks...this lasted about a week and a half before it started chipping off. 
Needless to say, I would never go back.

We were in NOLA for vacation and this place rocks!  Half price oysters during happy hour for 75 cents a piece is just unbeatable. Also, try the butter, it's delicious.  

We had the Pate Of Louisiana Rabbit & Chicken Livers as appetizer.  It was so good and huge, we had to lick our fingers.  

Stuffed P&J Oysters is ok.  

Crab Bisque - YUM!!!

Matzo Ball & Roast Chicken Soup - the Matzo Ball is as big as the cup itself.  So there is actually not much soup, but what we had was good.

Salad Luke - This one is a delight.  It's light and flavorful.

Fried Oyster Salad - It's good, but do not order if you are already having oysters for appetizers.

Chappapeela Pork Schnitzel - this is good too!

Shrimp Cavatelli Etouffee - Fresh pasta with the shrimp.  Very good sauce.  

Moules et Fritos - Mussels were fresh and the fries were crispy

For dessert - we had Steamed Chocolate, just because some of us are allergic to nuts.  So anything with pecans and almonds, we can't order.  Steamed chocolate is very good anyway.  

I am taking off one star, b/c when I called in for a reservation, they said I can either go in at 5:45 pm or 9:45 pm. First time, I chose 5:45 pm the next day.  All is good.  Another day, I called again, they gave me the same times.  I ignored them and walk there at 7:30 pm and found that there were actually a number of tables available at the back near the kitchen.  I am not sure if those times are actually for outside, but the I didn't get seated outside near the bar the 1st time anyway.  So I didn't like their reservation policy.  Don't know what that is for, but if I were you, I'll not make a reservation and walk right in there.
Freshest and most well thought out sushi. We got the tasting menu and were pleasantly surprised by every course.
Not worth the 300+ a night they were charging.  When up the street to the Kempton Hotel for same price and stayed in luxury.
Excellent customer service. One of the few places in the airport outside of the gates that serves alcohol. I didn't try the food. Drinks highly over-priced, but you really have no other choice

I really dislike leaving negative reviews and I normally have a pleasant experience here. But today my coworkers and I ordered delivery and one order was wrong and one order didn't come with the sauce. When I called to let them know they didn't apologize and sounded inconvenienced when I asked them to fix it. They weren't pleasant or apologetic. Now I get that mistakes happen but just apologize. It's a simple thing but goes a long way. I'm going to hold off on coming here for awhile.

I live down the street from this local gem. I'm a lover of this type of food and this is my go-to. Their prices are good! Their garlic salad dressing is my favorite and I always buy it for take-out. My favorite dish is the meat stuffed plate there. I will return many more times before the year finishes.

Horrible excuse for Latin food. The service is horrible and the black bean soup is watery and has no flavor. 
The person who brought us out food didn't even know what plate was what. 
The tortilla soup is supposed to have avocado and cilantro which it had none of. 
The waiter never came out to ask us how things were, he has rude and snatched our menus before we were even finished. 
Horrible! I'll never go back.

I used to think they provided great service - until I got my car fixed from an accident on 2/17. I didn't have problems with them until after I got my car back. Since February 27th, 2015, Conicelli has called me a total of 23 times for a "review of the services" at Conicelli. The first time, I gave them the review. Then they kept calling - as late at 9-10pm!!! Half of the time when they call, the person on the other end actually hangs up and doesn't say anything - I just hear them breathing! When I do talk to them, I ask that they take me off the list of people to call because at this point, it's just harassment. I just talked to a supervisor, who knows if she'll actually remove me from their call list and get their act together. 

Go there if you want to get your car serviced, but be prepared to be harassed 23 times over the course of a month and a half via phone

Update - Conicelli called me after seeing the review, and seemed very concerned about the company the contract out to do reviews on services. I appreciated that!

If I lived in Nola, this is where I'd want to hang out with friends. Cool easy going vibe, table seating and some great music. A fun 40s style trio the other night. One bartender was really lacking, all around bitchy, but maybe just a bad day. Would still go back since it's such a nice easy going vibe when Frenchmen is getting a little crazy outside.

CLOSED! How disappointing and upsetting. Always dropped in for some packaged coffee or an espresso. Loved the smell of roasting coffee. This was part of the flavor of Ybor and now it's gone. What a loss.
PS They opened in Wesley Chapel

We went on a night that wasn't busy. The place was closing about an hour after we arrived. We felt rushed and could hear the employees talking about leaving. The fish tank was cool, but we were left guessing what kinds of fish where in the tank. They had signs but we couldn't find some of them. Where's the shark? Where's Guy Harvey's biggest trout? Some fish don't have a sign. Food was overpriced. Ordered a pound of crab legs but hard to believe that was actually a full pound. Taste was okay on the crab legs. We also ordered the lobster ravioli and didn't like it at all. Waitress was mediocre. She was not enthusiastic and didn't smile. Seemed like she didn't want to be there.

This was a really nice restaurant! I like the design. The lady who took our order was really nice and friendly, and offered me a better deal on the item I ordered. When they called my name, I got up to go to the counter, but the guy was already coming to me! That was a nice touch. Sadly, they forgot one of my items in the deal I chose, but I didn't realize until I long after I had eaten (on the way home, ha). I did dine-in, and it was a pleasant experience. The restaurant was clean and tidy, which is always a good thing, lol. I'll definitely come back sometime!

Wow, where to begin? I was looking for a new barber ever since my old one of 10 years retired. I wasn't sure where I should go, but found the Moose and decided to give it a try. I was far from disappointed. First question after asking my name was, "would you like a drink?". I was more than happy to wait patiently with a glass of makers. Toni was my barber, and I couldn't give enough credit to him. He takes his work seriously and really cares that you look and feel great. Finally, I have never had a haircut where I walked out of the shop feeling as good as I did walking out of The Moose. It's not cheap, but for what you're getting, it's worth every penny.
Great date night place! I can't say enough about the fried green tomatoes and the beet salad
Yes it is a bit pricey but after several visits I can say I have yet to receive any questionable food.  Always tasty.
Horrible experience. Pasta was gummy. Shrimp was overdone. Pizza was bland. Bacon had too much sauce.

Great breakfast! 

She's a pretty harsh food critique, but swears this was "the BEST quiche she has ever had!"

Coffee was great, service was excellent as always.
