They appear to have a lot of teen bussers who stand around WAITING for tables to empty or working inefficiently during rush hours. Hand them a coffee pot or help run food and drinks. Very frustating when your coffee cup is empty and everyone swamped except the busser just standing there watching.

Large variety for everyone.  Breakfast, Burgers, Sandwiches, Panini, Greek, Home Style Manhattans or even Liver & Onions, and now a Healthy Menu with calorie count offered. BEWARE the warning at bottom of healthy menu, calorie count is HALF order. Regardless it's healthier options which we all appreciate.

Food recommendations: The Spinach, Swiss and Turkey Bacon Omelette is exceptional and comes with fresh fruit. Large omelet and always one of my favorites. 

My other favorite is their Oatmeal. Creamy and comes with all the toppings on the side. Full order is a huge bowl (they also offer tiny bowl). I prefer just cinnamon and touch of sub sugar. Delicious!

Monte Carlo with Ham & Swiss on French Toast comes with choice of soup, salad or coleslaw. If you're not watching your waist a must have. ALWAYS delicious and trust me, you will enjoy the sandwich on their french toast. OMG!

Gyro Sandwich has tender slices of gyro meat on pita with tomatoe, onions and cucumber sauce. Tasty and would order again if hungry for Gyro. Spinach Pie with Greek salad is also very popular and tasty.

Breakfast options I speak from friends comments. French Toast is the best in the world. MUST order!!! Monte Carlo experience told me he's right even though I've never had a full breakfast order. 

Pancakes are good, not exceptional, would order again. If you love pancake toppings know that their topping is pie filling. Some love..so I'm not hating just warning. Fresh fruit option needed even if they had to rasie the prices slightly. 

Last but not least my friend loves the Liver & Onions. This being his third time ordering. He enjoys the way its cooked then smothered with sautee onions. His 2 side choices are mashed potatoes and corn. Corn rather bland and not sweet though. His words are if you like Liver and Onions order it!!!

Something for everyone. Give it a try and if you're not happy speak up to the manager. We have and it's helped. As he said, it is the only way they can fix the problems.

Overpriced.  

That's the best way to describe it.  Everything was FINE.  Just fine.  But when our bar tab is $60 for a few drinks, and I felt like I needed to go over the menu about 8 times to find something exciting to try (I landed on the burger), I felt let down.  

All of the reviews of this place made me want to come visit.  I think these must all be Vandy kids or tourists who don't know where the better quality places are with better prices.  

I just felt, well... so meh about the whole thing.  

Again, everything was fine, decent, even.  But by the time to pay the bill came, my husband and I thought of at LEAST 5 or 6 different places we could have gone for BETTER drinks with CHEAPER prices and a much better menu.  

Obviously, this is probably for the hip crowd.  So, if you're hip, go for it.  If you were once hip, and you know better... be prepared to be underwhelmed.

The first time I came was in autumn 2012 and then I came back during Yelp Spring Break 2013 in May. I called before heading over to be sure they would have it this time...you know what...the macaroni and cheese. 

Then I walked myself over here for brunch on a nice warm May morning and I HAD THE MAC N CHEESE!!! Mmmmm delicious (cheese butter cream delicious). I had the brunch this time which was a little pricey but I did try all of their signature items. I just kept getting the mac n cheese though, over and over and over. The service isn't top notch but I got enough sweet tea refills to wash down all the calories that I ate. I basically had everything from the previous trip but came specifically for the M&C. The only reason why I said the buffet was pricey was because I can only eat so much buffet food in the double digits but it was made with love...

Glad it was a long walk because I stuffed myself with that mac n cheese.

The Fat Ham: where the food is delicious but you always leave hungry. 

That's how I feel, anyway. Don't get me wrong, I understand that this is a tapas/small plates restaurant. I have been to quite a few such places. It's the price to size ratio that gets me. For the money, I'd rather go somewhere else. 

Don't get me wrong the food is pretty good and the whiskey selection is wide and fun, but I'm just as happy somewhere else for more food for the same ( or even less) price.

You know, Superior Grill is one of those places I have a love hate relationship with. While I love going there with friends to get together for whatever celebratory reason we can make up and have some delicious margaritas, I really don't enjoy the food that much. The food is really just not that good. Considering the great Mexican options we have now in the city since the Big "K," I think that Superior Grill needs to make some recipe changes. They can keep the chips and salsa just the way they are, the guacamole is pretty good, but the queso could use some help, kinda tastes like they use a white version of Velveeta.  I mean I know there are some good melting Mexican cheeses out there that can help the queso situation they have going over there. Really I think the only good thing worth ordering in my opinion are the chicken or steak fajitas and sharing with someone. Now as for the beans and rice that come with the fajitas, that's where I think a recipe change needs to happen.  They have been serving those same rice and beans for as long as I can remember and boy are they boring and bland. They just don't have any flavor.  The tortillas they serve, while they may be homemade, they are just to heavy and greasy, you end up filling up on the tortilla and you still have tons meat left for the fajitas. The cheeseburgers are pretty good and huge, but they are kind of out of place at a Mexican restaurant, but my son isn't complaining about that. All the other things I have tried like the plain ole' cheese enchiladas or the tacos are nothing to rave about it all tastes so processed and fat laden, I'll go to Taqueria Corona for those. Like I said I am usually there not because I want a great meal but because I am with friends celebrating, and I think most people go for the same reason which is probably why the place does so well. Anyways, I know I will be back to Superior Grill many more times despite my giving it 3 stars, just kind of wish they could up the quality on their foods.

Don't be surprised if the manager makes you out to be a liar. Tried to get a table after a hockey game for a table of 4. Once we did not get seated, I asked why open seated began when we were on list. He said they seated everyone on the list and acted like I was lying. He then proceeded to walk away. I manage a business and that's not how you treat any customer. How about asking when we put our name in or who did we tell at the hostess stand??? Really surprised by how we were treated. Never been treated so poorly by any business!!
Second time coming and it won't be the last! Everything is super delicious @stephsequeirafit

Such a great hidden gem!  It's one of those places you wonder where in the hell you're driving, but then you're super glad you made the journey (albeit our drive was only from downtown St. Pete...lol). I had the Pabellón and my husband the Sifrina, and both were oh so fresh and tasty!  We would totally order both again!  You can tell a Venezuelan abuela is in the back making your meal when you order. I think the employees are mainly family, so you can tell they take pride in what they do and are really friendly. This really isn't a place you come for romantic ambience, as it's mainly a order-n-pay at the counter spot. But while you're at the counter, check out the desserts!  They all look amazing and most are made in house. We got Tres Leches and Flan for later!  Yay!

My friend and I stopped by on a road trip through Tucson and now we wish we lived a lot 
closer.  We stopped in to buy some Yarn Its (which we love) and found the most delightful and helpful people in this store.  We couldn't leave before looking at all the amazing yarn they have.  My friend found the perfect shawl pattern and I reluctantly left the angora behind..

We have been twice, once for drinks only and once for dinner. Great atmosphere and layout. Bryan at the bar was awesome. Good variety of beer and liquor...meaning thwy had IPA so I was happy. Appetizers were great...especially the grouper bites. 

Downside is the band and all other activities are over at 10. After that it is just a quiet bar on the water. Too bad because the band was fun and had people up dancing. They have a nive pool area and putt putt golf on the inside wakway. All closed. Otherwise we had a great time. 

It is a 2 minute walk to the beach and the rooms at the attached Holiday Inn were nice and very big. Overall we had a great weekend.

So I'll start with a couple of positives. I loved the bacon bucket, nice TV's, and ok beer.  That said, the service is pretty bad. In my opinion a place that has multiple beers should have a menu that people can look at and not a TV screen that scrolls through. I respect the conservation of paper and all put printing a few menus isn't a bad idea! Also note to Danny boy.. Maybe the service would be better if he staff didn't drink more than the patrons.

Amazing view! And it doesn't spin to where you feel like throwing up while dining. 
The only thing I would say is that they need to update their decor and have vegan options!

Ehh, just so-so.  Not a rave review, by any stretch.  But to be fair all I had was a salad, so there you go.  Service was mediocre.  Wouldn't go again and felt like I wasted an opportunity for a better restaurant.
This place is awesome. Great service and great food. Also the place has really good vibes. You can't beat a BYOB!

We heard a lot about this King Cake Burger and against my better judgment, we went on an adventure to find them last Sunday.  First of all, if you're unsure of where the truck is, be sure to check their Facebook page (just search Food Drunk Food Truck on Google and it's the first hit) and they update daily with where you can find them. 

Alright, so back to the burger. Despite there being a parade going on, there was no line at the truck, so it was easy in and out. $10 for a King Cake Burger, which I'll admit looked fantastic-- gooey cheese, piping hot, etc.

So, here's my criticism: man, a King Cake Burger tastes a lot like a King Cake Burger. I don't know what I was expecting, but yup, that's king cake and a burger. 

Don't get me wrong, the meat was fantastic, there was tons of delicious cheese, and completely separate from the burger, I guess the king cake wasn't bad. Together though? Man, I don't need sprinkles on my burger, ok?

I don't really know what could make this better for me. Maybe if they did some sort of sauce on the burger that married the two flavors, but as is, the whole thing is kind of jarring. Or maybe I'm just a boring eater. Who knows.
Best price and same day turnaround time.  Can't beat that.  Knowledgeable and friendly, and clarified any questions I had.  I would definitely recommend!

This place shouldn't even be in business - it's as if they took someone off the street and told them to give manicure and pedicure to customers - the young men they hire to offer these services have no clue what to do - they look like they are sleep walking thru everyting - - charge $40???  Save yor money and your heath - lack of cleanliness is another complaint

I went here twice & both times had excellent service. The food was great. I got the veggie wrap on time that was good. Second time I had pancakes & they were little to much flour in it to my liking the cakes were like 1/4" thick other than that it was good. I do see myself coming back here again.

We stopped in thinking we were at Superior Seafood.  We were confused but stayed regardless, it was happy hour so why not?  Jeremy, our bartender, was an absolute doll.  Best margarita I had during our entire vacation.  He did upsell us to the top shelf, but it was worth it.  

He helped us choose an app, and suggested we order the half order instead of full, knowing we were planning to eat elsewhere.  What bartender suggests the smaller, less expensive option?  He asked where we were planning to go and suggested the sister, Superior Seafood. I knew it existed somewhere!  Thanks, Jeremy! 

We got the chimichangas and they were good. Nothing overly exciting but they satisfied the very empty void in my belly. The guac was fantastic. Star of the plate for me.  

I'd come back. I'd have guac, margaritas, and come when Jeremy was working. He was just the best!

A savior from the madness that is lax. It's always nice after a long trip to be welcome by this little piece of home.Buses are nice and clean, there are plugs for your electronics, and wifi. It also has a bathroom which is nice.  It's a really smooth process and the drivers are always very nice. They always run on time, sometimes a little early

Great food, and super-friendly, considerate service. 
We hesitated going to this cafe since we were looking for a full breakfast venue. But we were pleasantly surprised to find a great mix of breakfast and brunch items. 
Worth dropping by!

Looked around for a quality tint shop, and decided on Orange Tint and Tunes because of the positive reviews.  I wasn't disappointed!  The business was very professional, but with a friendly family feel.  Everyone was very knowledgable, offered great suggestions.  They did a fantastic job tinting the windows and the sunroof of our brand new Audi Q5.  I drove 45 minutes from New Tampa and it was worth the trip.  If you desire quality products from a quality business, this is the place to go.  Will definitely be returning for future vehicles.

Recently stopped here to check the new brewery out. As we arrived, we found they only had 4 parking spaces and then signs that said to not park on the street next to the brewery. Found that odd but we luckily got one of the 4 spots in the lot. walked and found the place to be decorated nicely. We were greeted promptly and ordered a flight of everything they had. It was a mix of sours, ipa's, and stouts for the most part. All were at or above average, except on of the sours, The Carlton. It smelled like puke. Skip that one. I really enjoyed the industrial design of the place, but hated the chairs. I could not sit in them, but the ladies seemed to enjoy them. Overall, I look forward to coming back and sampling some more beers.

This restaurant located at Tampa Palm in a plaza  behind Olive Garden . The interior wasn't so fancy or big but it was clean and comfortable. It sits about 20 people.   I had the beef drunken noodles lunch special and shrimp roll appetizer (for 7.50). Both tasted very  good. Service was fast . If you like spicy, ethnic Thai food, this place is worth trying.
Yep. If you want high quality food for a discerning palate, then here's your place. Service adequate to good the 3 times I've been there. All about the food.

5 stars for a 5 star hotel. We were on the back side so we had total quiet. Nice pool, great bar.... GREAT LOCATION: 1 or 2 blocks to Deanies, Absinth House, Arnauds, K Pauls, Gallitoirs, Mr. B's, Felix's and a Lucky Dog.

This review is directed at Bully's as a whole rather than a specific restaurant.  My wife and I along with 4 friends went to our local Bully's to celebrate St. Patrick's Day.  Boy was I rudely surprised to find the special of the day to be Prime Rib.  When I asked the waitress about St. Patty Day specials or Corned Beef and Cabbage I was told that Bully's corporate will not allow Bully's restaurants to celebrate St. Patrick's Day...... What the hell?  The city of Chicago is dying their river green, the nation is celebrating and Bully's is too good to celebrate with the rest of the nation...  Well Bully's corporate, you are not the only game in town and I'll take my business elsewhere.
I don't know why there are so many bad reviews. The food is good. Get the Happy Family with just beef and shrimp. Thank Me later.

I had no expectations and got exactly that ; not much. The customer service was non existent and the merchandise was sparse and very picked over.  The inventory is a combination of big lots and other discount stores basement sales items. I guess if you don't want to shop with a crowd then this is the place to be.

Absolute perfection. Throwback to a bygone era. Great soft serve and hard ice cream. All your favorites are there. Super friendly service and fantastic prices.
Cash only!

Had the famous shrimp cocktail....it was spicy for sure, but just your typical shrimp cocktail covered in grated horseradish mixed with cocktail sauce....definitely cleared my sinuses! Drinks were strong, nice bar atmosphere, friendly service.

Christine is a great restaurateur. Nice vibe, drinks, food, and tunes. You may remember her venture Aubergine that she founded with Gil (now at LuLu's). Her menu has evolved. So have the drinks. Don't try to move the couches they will fall apart.

This 7 course meal restaurant is delicious! You really get the full Moroccan experience. The service is amazing (brings flatbread every 10-15 minutes), there is belly dancer, and great atmosphere!

It is a great place if you want to just experience outside of the 'norm'

This place makes, by far the best Greek Salad ever. I like their wraps, but I absolutely LOVE their salad and soups. The Fire Roasted Vegetable soup and the Asparagus soup are my two favorites. In over a few years of ordering from here, I only had one bad experience with someone that worked there and the manager was quick to correct it for me and he even bought me my next lunch!  The prices are low and the service is good. Plus, they deliver to a limited area in Metairie, so that's a big plus.

Penca has a lot going on. The ambiance is rustic and romantic. The wine list is respectable. The food offerings are enticing. The bartenders know what's what. It's fair to say that for a soft opening, Penca has done pretty well to convince me to be a regular.

As far as food goes, I was disappointed that most of the things I wanted to try were out of stock, and I was not wowed by my chile relleno, which was lacking cheese. However, on my third visit, while sitting at the bar and talking with the staff, I learned that they had been busier than expected the first couple nights and had been short on a lot of food items, including cheese. Everyone so far agrees, however, that they love the tacos, and the fresh chips and homemade salsas. I look forward to being able to update my review later with better information about their food offerings.

While Penca is still working out the kinks in their food menu, and the wait staff is becoming more experienced, I am already a fan of the bar side of things. Luke and Brian are both very knowledgeable, and were eager to make sure that I selected a wine or cocktail that I would like on all three occasions. While I was not a fan of the gin cocktail, I am a fan of their old world dominant wine list and suggest trying a sherry from their dessert list for something different.

I had a great experience at Golden Nails. Tammy was awesome. I walked in around 11:20 on a Thursday and was able to be helped right away. The basic pedicure was wonderful! I enjoyed light conversation with Tammy which was nice because I came alone. The salon was clean and staff was friendly. I got a French manicure on my nails and it looks great. I did not feel rushed or pressured at all. In fact, I felt very relaxed. I'm very pleased!

Fantastic food. Our party ordered crab dip, burgers, chicken sandwiches, a salad, and two kids meals. The portions were substantial and the food was delicious. The chicken sandwiches are fried with a flaky, crispy, yummy batter, and the burgers were cooked to juicy perfection. We went with the crab dip as an appetizer and weren't disappointed. It was busy but the service was quick and friendly.

Take a ride up on the Elevator of Doom to an amazing hidden tiki paradise right above the French Quarter! Or just take the entirely non terrifying stairs if you are feeling squeamish. Either way the drinks are a slice Tiki heaven and well worth the journey. My wife and I visited with a friend last week and tried several of their signature beverages including the Last Guinea Pig, the Seaward, the Painkiller, as well as their takes on the Aku Aku Zombie and the Mai Tai. We didn't get to try our luck on the Wheel of Drinks (winner gets a Scorpion Bowl which is a super value, the loser a malt liquorY Smirnoff Ice). The bartender, Brian is exceptionally knowledgable on his tiki drinks, and he even let us taste test a new secret concoction which was fantastic and aromatic which may soon make an appearance here. Great decor, great ambience, and great music (whether you dig surf or Slayer they got it all) compliment a selection of seriously delicious cocktails. Hope to come back soon.

TLDR: Delicious food at cheap prices. Get the goat stew, it's heavenly. No AC tho, maybe don't come on a hot day. 

I'm a Dominican food newbie, so I can't speak for the authenticity of this food. But it is delicious! I ordered a lunch special, which includes a protein, a huge bed of white or yellow rice, a side of black or red beans, 3 fried plantain slices, and a cabbage and tomato salad dressed with vinegar. The amount of protein isn't as generous as the amount of rice, but regardless you'll still end up pretty full ($8-$12).  If you're craving more protein, go with the "order" vs "lunch special". You will get significantly more protein for a couple extra bucks. I loved the goat stew, but the pork spare ribs were meh (a little too salty for my taste). 

My gripes with this place include that there is no AC, just some ceiling fans, and that they don't have all the different types of protein on hand (I tried ordering oxtail and they hadn't made it).

When I was a kid, any food without the suffix "burger" was gross to me. I didn't like anything Mexican, Chinese, or Italian unless it was plain and tasteless. Guo Bin changed my thinking on food in general, and Chinese food in specifics.

It seems antithetical that what I consider the best Chinese food in St. Louis isn't located on South Grand, or in the Asian-American part of Olive, but underneath a retirement home off of 170 and Delmar. The food here is the best Chinese food I've had outside of the three months I spent in China. The Szechuan Beef in particular is amazing, with a crispy outside, and an amazing sauce garnished with hot peppers. The General Tso's Chicken has enough garlic to ruin the evening of your significant other, and huge hunks of ginger that compliment the crispy chicken perfectly. Even their pot stickers are done well, and they come with a great sweet and sour sauce and a mustard/horseradish mix that will blow your sinuses away.

The cherry on top of the dining experience is the service. There is one waiter in particular who knows all the regulars, and if he doesn't know you, he treats you like one. Trust me; go here, and order something spicy. You won't be disappointed.

The Pancake Pantry is a Nashville institution. It took me almost four years to get there, but get there I did! My husband and I had breakfast here with some friends, who insisted we had to, and helped us out with our menu selections. My husband, ever the steak-and-eggs fan, opted for that along with some pancakes, and I went with the Tennessee country ham with, of course, a side of pancakes as well. We split a side of hash browns.

We're not big breakfast people, but I've gotta say this is one of the better breakfast spots I've been to. It ranks as well as West Egg in Chicago, M. Henry in Chicago, or Ann Sather (also in Chicago). The ham was perfectly salty, my eggs weren't too runny (I ordered them over medium), and the has browns were nice and crispy. And the pancakes? Oh, my! Light, fluffy, moist, and melt-in-your-mouth delicious. I almost wish I'd opted for the Swedish pancakes, which were calling my name. Maybe next time.

Stopped here for brunch with my family on the last day of our vacation to St. Louis. The service was terrible! The hostess was also the busser and the manager so she would disappear for 10-15 mins at a time. This is something that might work on a slower weekday morning, but not on a busy Saturday morning. Once we got a seat, it took over 10 mins to get the 2 chocolate milks that I ordered for my 2 toddlers. They also brought out my kids food about 15 minutes before they brought me and my husband's orders out. My kids were done with their pancakes before we even received our breakfast. 

As for the food, it was okay. My omelet was nothing special. My daughter's blueberry pancake was still a little doughy in the middle, but we didn't dare ask for a new one because it took so long to get it to begin with. 

The best part of the experience was the cute two block area in which this place was situated. If we are back in St. Louis anytime soon, we would probably pick another spot to stop.

A coffee house with an ambience of a hipster, Indian, and casual scene.  No pretentious vibe that you see with mega chains like starbucks, second  cup etc.....The Kashmir Chai was amazing. I am normally dubious about the staff of these hipster coffee houses, but the staff was very friendly and influenced my selection of the variety of beverages.  Although the food may not be fine dining experience, the samosa's provide adequate sustenance to tide one over until dinner.

Wonderful! That's the best description of this cool little spot that I stopped into for Sunday brunch.  I stopped in when it was nearly empty which was great for me because I had the chance to chit chat with the staff about football.  
But let's talk about the food!  I had the house omelette of spinach, bacon and fontina cheese, with a side of grits and toast.  They use the best quality stuff and you can taste it!  So yummy!  Service was fast, super friendly, and on point.  
If you are in Dunedin, you need to take the time to stop into this great cafe for a meal. You won't be disappointed!

These guys and gals that work here are awesome! They are super friendly and so honest! We had to take my husbands iphone in because it stopped charging and we were hoping to get it fixed at a low cost and they really came through! The gal who works on phones found that the charging area was just really dirty and wasn't able to connect. She cleaned it for us and made sure his phone would charge and wanted us to pass along how great they are to our friends! Phone fixed (cleaned!) for the low cost of a donation to their coffee fund. We left very happy and so thankful for another visit to the Computer Room! So seriously, give them a chance! You won't be sorry!
I don't recommend anyone to come here. Worst service EVER. Waiters were rude and lowsy. Didn't give us silverware and got mad when we asked. I could go on but it's not even worth my time.
It was ok, the service took a little long but it wasn't too bad. The food was good but nothing out of this world (taste wise). The bread pudding was really good though!

We went as a family to Bowl here based on a recommendation from a friend. Right away we were positively impacted by the Retro look and feel of the establishment. Even the benches were wonderfully restored. The service at the counter was prompt and very good humored. As we bowled we also were able to enjoy excellent craft beer. The people working at the bowling alley were very friendly. It turns out the bowling alley had been in the family for generations and there was a picture of their grandfather from back in the 60s that was on the wall. It was very cool. We enjoyed it very much and will return.

I was a patient here for about six months and in that time this office screwed up my records numerous times, lost appointments, double billed me 3 times and just about every other thing they could do to screw up. 
The doctors aren't any better, it took 5 months to get test results ( all they could tell me was it agreed with previous diagnosis. But I had never had a previous diagnosis to agree with). 
Every time I had a question I couldn't get a straight answer, the doctor would only say "I'll get you a printout." So at the end of the day I had no answers and an inch thick stack of papers printed off WebMD.

Love this place!  Located just outside of Nashville -- the location is charming and every thing you want in a bowling alley!  Good food, great staff, and fun music.  The prices are hard to beat too!  We enjoyed using an extra discount through Sharing Spree Nashville! (http://www.sharingspree.com/Deals/nashville)  Thanks for Sharing!

This is not a very relaxing place to go if you need to let off some steam. The room has no element of spa to it at all, it's just a bed in a tiny room. The therapist kept talking to me and sneezing during my massage which made it a little hard to relax, and the receptionist is so rude. She's miserable when she answers the phone and God forbid if you have to reschedule! She doesn't like that one bit and will charge you for it. Over all, it's not worth it. You get what you pay for on this one. It's a cheap massage and that's how it's played out. I'll keep looking because this place was not my cup of tea!
Great laid back place for our last night if vacation. Accommodated a gluten free request perfectly! Service was fantastic!

Usually pretty empty.  Easy to get in and out of.  Not a ton of pumps, but it's a small town gas station so you shouldn't be expecting a ton of them.  It's a solid place to fill up.

Mini mart selection is small and the people working there aren't the friendliest, but what can you expect?
The crawfish bisque was probably the best soup I've eaten.  It was a bit crowded and service was slow but really friendly.  All worth it for that bisque.  Highly recommend going there.

The food was pretty good but as soon as I walked into a restaurant it smelled like rotten fish. The smell was so bad we asked the hostess to seat us in the back.

I got the Southern Breakfast - $15 - which had two eggs, cane syrup sausage, biscuit and grits. We all wanted the chaMpagne au peche - $9.75 - champagne & fresh peach, but the restaurant ran out of peach.

After our meal, we had to walk back through the nasty fish smell, which then turned my stomach.

For a John Besh Restaurant I was VERY disappointed.

After having several issues related to sciatic nerve pain Dr. Welch has really helped me alleviate the pain and put me on a program to strengthen my core muscles to avoid future problems.  Very professional and I would highly recommend this office for your chiropractic needs.

Good Cuban sandwich with a mound of meat. It takes awhile, so don't be in a huge hurry. Husband and wife running the place are very nice. One large could easily feed 2 people in my opinion. It's my second favorite In the Bay area so far, and I have tried several. "SMILEYS" is my go to place, but this place is right up there on the top of the list. Try it... you won't be disappointed!

We've gotten barbecue from Smokin' Out a couple of times now. My husband and I are true Southerners, born in TN and graduates of the University of Alabama, so we are particular about our barbecue! This fits the bill - nice smoke taste, good sides, good sauce options (I like to mix the sweet sauce and the hot sauce together). My husband wants to try other things on the menu, but he loves the Porky Pie so much, he can't bring himself to order anything else! It is a pile of pulled pork, smothered in their garlic mashed potatoes, then covered in shredded cheddar cheese. True comfort food!

Honestly not sure what all the negative reviews are from but I've had nothing but professional service and a gorgeous ring much cheaper than anywhere else including Shane company. Direction get off on Page make left right before you get to Quiktrip, not sure why that's so hard.  Richard was our sales associate he was informative helpful friendly and mindful without being pushy, Most importantly and I do mean most importantly she's happy with the ring that she chose it just so happened that we found her ring here. Loved our experience..

Great vibe, with many locals and friendly service.  Mussels four different styles...try the Russian style with a rich vodka cream sauce...and only $12 for a huge portion! 

Its supposed to be a steak place and they do have a wide selection of steaks. The atmosphere is more of a local bar, and I didn't try the steaks although I just might come back for the steak and more mussels!

This place spawned my new love for donuts, cold brew coffee and double fried chicken! 

Everyone must try at least one of each. One made-to-order hot donut, one fancy donut, a dry seasoned and a glazed chicken as well as their cold brew and hot coffee. Also, each location has a slightly different selection of hot donuts. I can't say enough of how great this place is and how wonderful of an addition they have been in the Philadelphia food community. I frequented this place at least three times a week for the past year and the quality of the product as well as the service are very consistent. Also, the chef Matt is always coming up with new and yummy creations so you'll never get bored of the flavors, ever. 

What are you waiting for?! Go check em out, you won't regret it. 
-P.S- they did not pay me for this review, I just love them so gosh darn much. ;)

Working so close to this sandwich shop is certainly a perk of the job.  I frequently walk over to this place to grab a cuban, medianoche or hot meal.  I have yet to have a bad experience- the only thing that can be improved upon is the wait between ordering your food and actually receiving your food.  But, the prices cannot be beat and the food is authentic and delicious.  If you order ahead and aren't there when the food is ready, there is a shelf with heat lamps that they put it in to keep it warm for you.  Everything is prepared fresh and don't forget to order a deviled crap with hot sauce- fantastico!

All of those menu items above are under $5!
The waffles were delicious. I should have ordered more than one. Cheap too. Very quiet when we went during the week.

Range is one of the newer additions to downtown, and once again, the folks behind places like Bailey's Chocolate Bar, Bridge, and Rooster hit it out of the park. They are my favorite restaurateurs in the downtown STL area - even though each place is very different in niche, cuisine, hours, decor, each has the impression of being well thought-through for what it is.

So, what Range is - a modern update of the soda bar / roller-skate-wearing carhop burger joints of yore. No, you don't pull up in your car and get served by comely ladies in skates, but the food is pure americana: burgers, fries, shakes, and floats. Except did we mention: *boozy* shakes and *boozy* floats? Yes. I would put on my bobby socks for these.

The  interior is dominated by a large bar-height table that runs the length of the restaurant, with stools for seating (we should add: there is also a bar-height bar that runs the length of the restaurant, parallel to the table ;-). Perhaps a bit off-putting to the standard middle-american diner, who seems to prefer maintaining a certain distance from (gasp!) other people, but we found it charming. Came in on a super-busy Friday night but nonetheless had maybe a 10 minute wait for a spot for 2 (which was just right for ordering drinks at the bar).

The burger menu includes many inventive takes on the classic, and it seems you can substitute different kinds of patties (pork, chicken, bison, lamb, veggie) for the free-range cow patties if you so desire (some burgers appear to be crafted around the type of meat involved, so sub at your own risk). We went exotic with the PB&J (Bison with arugula Pesto, goat cheese, and tomato jam) and the smoking duck burgers - the former was just... do it. You will not be sad. The duck was OK - nothing wrong with it, but in comparison to the PB&J it was a little boring. You should just order two sides of fries rather than one large - costs less, plus you get to try more sauces. The rooster is the same spicy/creamy sauce served on top of the crepes at the Rooster, and the homemade catsup was just fine. Haven't tried the others yet.

The big winner, though, is the boozy horchata milkshake: an invention that should have come to be long before now. You will somehow make room for it, we promise.

They have a fun Survivor-style competition where each week, two burgers "face off" in a battle - the one that gets ordered more gets to stay on the menu. Should keep things interesting over time - great idea for nom longevity.

First of all, let me say this: Go early. Go on a weekday. Be prepared to get cozy with the others who've come early on a weekday.

From there, I'll talk a little about my meal in particular. We went for my birthday, as I've been reading and salivating over the menu for a while. I got the Ginger Rogers (diiiivine, spicy and not too sweet, just the way I like my gin drinks) and we started with the deviled eggs, which were clean and had a tart, almost mustard-y tang to them. Well worth it.

Skipping ahead to dessert: the smores milkshake is topped with a lovely caramelized HOMEMADE marshmallow, and, if you've never had a homemade marshmallow, well, go ahead and see what you're missing. You'll never go back to those storebought stale cylinders. 

The pulled pork is yummy, though not the best I've ever had. And I've got a little secret for you, though: it comes with a side of fried dill pickle chips. I'll say that again: Fried. Dill. Pickle. Chips. Here's where the secret comes in: you can order these as a side, though it doesn't say so anywhere on the menu. Our waitress tipped us off, saying she eats them all through her late night shifts. A ringing endorsement if ever I heard one.

Oh yeah, and the fries. With cheese sauce and shortribs. It's absurd, but it works.
The place is nice and the flavors of the donuts are okay, but the donut itself is bad. It's like eating paper or a po boy bread with sweet icing on it. Donuts here aren't good. Just eye catching.

My husband and I just happened to go here one night when Miss Saigon was closed. (Honestly, I never really cared for Miss Saigon but I knew my husband liked it) 

Kien Giang has totally changed my perspective on vietnamese food. Their Pho is INCREDIBLE! I have never tasted anything like it. After our first dining experience here, we will never go back to Miss Saigon. 

A few things to note before you go. Don't expect great service. They're usually very busy, and always under staffed. One or two servers will be running around to about 20-30 tables at a time. Also, not sure if its a culture thing, but they're very to the point. Don't try to make conversation. Just tell the waitress what you want and give her the menu back. done. 

We always get the vegetable spring rolls (in the rice paper, not the fried ones) and they're incredibly refreshing. Always a great appetizer. The only thing we ever get is the Beef Pho and the clear noodle vegetable broth soup. The beef Pho (which I get with Tofu) is amazing. I don't understand how beef broth can taste that good. It blows my mind every time. 

Oh, they only take cash or check. And the prices are stupid cheap.

Consider the bar home and all the patrons family. Great bartenders and cocktails. A local Cheers!  So If you are not nice and can't handle keeping a bathroom clean- please head to another bar :/  Pal's is a New Orleans gem!
All the food was great!!  Really enjoy this place and love supporting a local business who is trying as hard as they are.

We walked in without a reservation on Father's Day  Sunday at 11 in the morning. We had a flight to catch at 3, so didn't have time to wait and luckily were able to sit at the bar right away. Looking at the menu didn't see anything that looked intriguing or exciting. I was upset that we may have been stuck with some boring brunch on our last day in Nashville. Oh my, was I wrong or what? I ordered the big daddy omelette and my husband got the Huevos Rancheros. I got a big omelet and I couldn't finish it. My omelette  was flavorful and the white trash hash was out of this world. I got a fried egg on top of my omelette. What else can you ask for? They also had buy one get one mimosa. Not sure if that was a Father's Day promotion or they do that every Sunday. We also ordered the red velvet waffle for dessert which sounded and looked creative but wasn't that impressive. Overall a great experience and definitely recommend it!!!

Going to Sam's is always an adventure. You never know just what he is going to feel like adding to that roll you just ordered.  Which is mainly the reason I am not so much of a fan. I can be picky... especially when it comes to sushi. That and the fact that I have yet to be allowed to order miso soup with my meal. But the prices here are good especially if you are a quantity over quality kind of person. Sam's does take credit cards but just be sure that you don't leave him a tip. Unless of course you like to see a grown Japanese sushi chef flip his lid.

Normally this is our favorite restaurant.  this time, service wasn't great, took way too long for our entrees. Seen another table right next to us, get up and leave (pissed). Not much to brag about this time. Took forever to get a second beer. Very disappointed all the way around.
Chickies and Pete's is the spot. Nothin beats Crab Fries. No way you go to Philly and pass this spot up. Hit 'em up at the Linc as well.

I had a tremendous experience and finally got a great deal here! Andrew was a very professional, nice, and polite salesperson who made me and my husband really comfortable through the whole process. He's the best salesperson I've ever seen! I compared lots of websites and The Mattress Factory definitely had the best price ever! I cannot wait to get my lovely mattress set soon!

These people are so super friendly. I had breakfast here Friday and it was amazing. 
Then today went to get some water and the two workers there incredibly nice, yet again. Great service, great food, and very hospitable

This is becoming a go to place before events in downtown Indy. It is a way to get St. Elmo's food scaled down and a bit more efficiently. My go to's have become either the Shrimp Cocktail or the Calamari, a couple of steak sliders and a glass of wine. Just the right amount before a game or play.

Have been to this place a few times. The place is usually rather deserted. It's clean, and the servers are friendly. But the food sucked each time. We ordered vegetarian, Baigan Bartha, Allo Gobi, Aloo mutter and a couple of other dishes. It tasted watered down, amateurish. Very disappointed. I need to remember not to go there again

I can't even tell you how charming The Cake Bake Shop is. It's expertly decorated in all seasons - to see it at Christmas is seriously to witness a winter wonderland. The cake is perfect, of course, and I've tried their espresso - strong and rich and awesome. The only downside, of course is that it's a tad pricey - so it makes for a nice treat once in a while but maybe not every day. But I love it when I go!

Lots of inventory.  No ice scrapers, but lots of inventory and they have gotten a jump on Xmas decorations.. 
If you are going to an "ugly sweater" Xmas party, here is the place to get all those things to sew on your sweater!

Staff was busy stocking shelves, long line at the cashier, clean, decent isle space.
I will most certainly return, should I be on this side of town.

Pretty tasty food but the prices are outrageous and portion sizes small. Ordered the curried goat and there were 5 small pieces of goat and a lot of other stuff but little meat. it was delicious though.. I felt the value for what you got was little. loved the presentation and taste.
As others have said, great place to set up with your laptop or books. Spacious clean interior. Bubble tea never tasted so good...
We loved the food - Greek Salad, Greek stir fry were both great! They were very busy and got our food to us very quickly. We will definitely return !!

Get the cote de Rhone

This is an adorable little wine bar, with reasonable prices on some great wines. I chose to down two delicious glasses of the cote de rhone blend which more than satisfied my wine tooth. I would recommend stopping here for a mid shopping spree wine because it is a nice place to see and talk.

Food: 4
Decor: 2.5
Ambiance: 2.5
Service: 4.5
Value: 4

Not much atmosphere to speak of, but great Indian food for cheap. Also, BYOB.

I stopped in and made a reservation, but I am horrified by the service I received. First of all, they took over an hour to seat us after telling us the wait was 30 minutes or so. Then, they seated us and it took over 20 minutes for a waiter to bring us water, let alone take our order. Food was far below similar restaurants (with better service). And I am disappointed.

Just average. I gave it three because the staff were friendly and the place itself was interesting with the old decor and historic site marking. The pasta tasted like it was from a box and not made fresh as I was expecting (being the stores down the street were all selling fresh pasta and it being in the Italian market). The veal was too salty and chewy, but the sauce had a nice light flavor to balance the dish. In the end just disappointed in the overall quality as it does not fit the location in the Italian market... tasted more like Italian food that I would get in the Poconos or a small town in West Virginia.
If I could give lower rating I would. This is the worst dunkin ever absolutely awful mean old lady works there in evening. Good luck getting a correct order.
I got Senegalese twists and was out of the shop in 5 hours. Very comfortable & clean inside. Cash only. There's parking available right outside the shop. Would definitely recommend.

Wow, what a great shopping experience, Ryan and Paul really took time to get me what I needed. Never any pressure to buy!!! I went to the store first thing in the morning and got all the attention as I was the only one there. Prices were more than fair, furniture is of very good quality. Delivery was a breeze, came when promised, got a call prior to arrival, and the two gents that unloaded and set up the pieces were first class. True " white glove" service. We need a few more pieces and the team at Oak & More will be my first and only stop. Great to find a truly good honest company to do business with in this day and age. 


Needed to add a few more pieces to our house so I stopped by to see Ryan and Paul. Felt great to be greeted by first name on the way in the store. Both gents were on top of their game, fixed me right up with what I was looking for! Great place to do business, I'll be back again soon.

I certainly felt out of place not being from 'Nova and it wasn't even game day!  Still, once I got over I ain't preppy enough to be here feeling, I ended up having a really good time.

Like every bar in America, they have different drink specials on different nights of the week.  Since I had never been to Kelly's, I had no idea what was on special.  After ordering something that wasn't on special, the bartender was kind enough to let me know what I could get cheaper that taste nearly the same, despite the line forming behind me.  

Cheap drinks, three floors to dance, a DJ, and a good crowd.  I'm sold.

For our last dinner in NOLA we randomly picked a 4 star place that had crawfish étouffée. That was the only criteria. 

Ambiance was ok. It's Bourbon Street so the clientele is generally drunk. It was ok. Noise level average to above average. 

Service was slow but reasonably nice. 

BBQ shrimp - good as advertised but the best part is dipping the free bread in the sauce. 

Boiled shrimp - plain. Nothing of note. 

Raw oysters - no brine left, far too big. Tasteless. 

Roasted oysters - with parm, these were decent. I'd get them again. 

Hush puppies - good. 

Fried green tomatoes - disappointing. I've had enough of the NOLA style of cooking which seems to be "fry the damn thing up." I was told by 2 southerners with us that they are not supposed to be battered & fried. 

Sweet potato fries - good. Worth it. 

Crawfish étouffée - decent. Not the best thing in the world but I'd recommend the dish. This is what I came here for and it was decent/ok. 

Jambalaya - tasted like it was made with hot dogs. After going to Coop's it is almost inedible. 

Shrimp creole - absolute rubbish. Never get this unless you are in a dungeon and have nothing else to eat. 

Generic po boy - fairly mundane. I'm tired if these sandwiches but even at that this was not good. 

Overall you could do worse, but you certainly could do better. Not worth the trip but if you end up there by chance there is good, and bad, food on the menu. Make sure you know what to get and avoid the rubbish.

It's very expensive.  But it's worth it once in a while.  It's more of an 'expense account' kind of place - BUT - I LOVE it!!!  I come here for special occasions.  It's one of the few places where you can get that 'supper club' feel.  The food is OUTSTANDING.  The service is STELLAR.  So....I still manage to go there often without breaking the bank:  Sit at the BAR and ask for the BAR MENU!!!  And don't miss the potato skins!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

BBQ spare ribs is awesome. If you're thinking about getting the sweet potato , get it loaded! Its covered with marshmallow which makes it sweeter.  We  tried a couple of the steaks, sirloin was alright, best I think was the prime rib and the filet medallion.  We were stuffed afterwards!  
Call ahead for this place! You won't regret it!  The service was really attentive as well.    They noted down my table size incorrectly and fixed it right away giving me another table!  
Also you get to pick your own steaks right at the front.

Bruce, the guide, was amazing and very informative. The low rating is because the tour included only a few restaurants and the sample portions were very small. For the cost of the tour I would have expected more.

I recently got a cheesesteak and bag of chips from this place. Cheesesteak was gross. Literally tasted like bagged boiled cafeteria meat on a roll with ketchup and onions. 

I will never go here again and recommend that all follow suit.
Don't go here for ANYTHING! You've been warned. They price gouge like no other place and do the job WRONG.

i have been here at least 6 times now and tried probably 60-70% of the items on the menu. I love tapas and have been waiting for a good tapas place in Nashville for a long time. My favorite items on the menu are the brussel spriouts, spicy couliflower, steak tacos and fish tacos. 

One of the things i appreciate is that they have tapas portions but also entre sized portions which makes it a great place for lunch as well.

Location of the restaurant and the parking lot behind the restaurant are also very convenient. 

Overall, I really love this place and would highly recommend it to anyone looking for tapas in Nashville.

When I bought my house, many people warned me that for the first few months, Lowe's and Home Depot would become my second and third homes because I'd be there so much. 

I think they were right. I've already been there twice since last week! 

During my first visit, I just picked up a few extension cords. The store is insanely huge, and since I don't like wandering, I asked one of the workers where I could find extension cords. He didn't know. HE DIDN'T KNOW. Don't you work there?!? I finally found them after a lot of wandering. 

During my second visit, I needed a hammer, an adjustable wrench, and a few other odds and ends. I found the hammer pretty easily, but once again, I was having trouble finding an adjustable wrench. Again, I asked a worker where I could find an adjustable wrench, and she wasn't sure. A fellow customer ended up showing me where the adjustable wrenches were, and he helped me pick the right one for the job. 

Perhaps Lowe's should give their employees a tour of the store when they're hired so they can help the customers a little better? Geeez...

We came in on raceday so I'm wondering if they just really weren't expecting too much business. We got cuban sandwiches, rice, pastalitos (they were out of chicken) and fried plantains. The owner and staff were all really friendly and I like the location and atmosphere, but stopped there. The bread was obviously stale to begin with on the sandwiches and the pastalitos were both cold. The meat wasn't warm at all. Just disappointing that we spent $30+ for what seemed like leftovers from the day before and I'm still craving Cuban food

The food here is amazing. Had a great time with my girlfriend.  Price is right. You cant go wrong here if you love sushi.  You cant get any fresher then having them make it for you right then and there. Love this place. Can't wait for the one in Tampa to open.

My boyfriend and I stopped by for lunch after kayaking nearby on a Thursday. First off, from the outside, the restaurant is in a older looking strip mall and doesn't really grab your attention. But, inside is a nice, quiet, Thai infused dining area. The service was great, the food was excellent. We ordered chicken pad Thai, lemongrass hot n sour soup, curry puffs, and spring rolls. Everything was delicious. We also got Thai tea and Thai coffee, both of which were perfect, not too sweet like I've had at a lot of other Thai restaurants. Dee came over and greeted us even though she wasn't our server. I don't know how, but she remembers us from when we would come in to dine or order takeout when we lived in the area before moving to NC. We have dined here several times before but I realized I never made a recommendation! We stop by to eat here every time we're in the area!

Not good sushi. At all. The $5 Kani salad is literally a whole sliced cucumber with 6 strands of crab in it. $11 specialty roll was tiny as hell, and didn't taste great. Fish used for sushi was just okay, rice needed more vinegar as it was super bland. If you've ever been anywhere for good sushi, aka have ANY standards, don't waste your $ here!

Food: 2
Decor: 2.5
Ambiance: 3
Service: 3.5
Value: 2.5

I love the concept of a 50's diner. Far too often the execution falls short of expectations. This is one of those occasions. Nothing is done particularly well here. I'm not sure how they've lasted as long as they have at this location.
Walked in at 11 on a saturday. There were 10 open tables but was told they wouldnt take walk ins because their computer was down. Absurd. Will not try to come again.

Greek flavors meet Chipotle-style restaurant. I drove out to Largo to try Mo' Ziki and I'm happy I did. All of the available meats are flavorful and fresh, their vegetables are crisp, and their menu is varied. I got the chicken Greekadilla and was happy with my selection. I also had the opportunity to try every Ziki and hummus available and loved them all! They have a cheese dip called K-Zo that is out of this world- like super mac and cheese!

My friend and I were the only two stopping in a bit after Ralph's opened for lunch on a Monday. This would have alarmed me if Ralph's didn't have such a good reputation and if we weren't greeted so warmly upon entering. Not to worry, there were plenty of other diners by the time our bread basket arrived. My friend and I shared the Mediterranean salad (several jumbo shrimp, crab meat and greens with a light vinaigrette) and a pork sandwich with provolone. This sandwich has supplanted Dinic's as my new favorite and the salad was perfect for summer. Cash only but there is an ATM in the back.

This was the first meal on the first day of our visit to NOLA. We were prepared for a long wait but they had a table for us on a Friday evening as soon as our party of four got there! 

Took us a few minutes to figure out the system - order drinks and food at the bar, carry your drinks to the table, wait for the food to come out as it gets done. The Sazerac and Hurricane were obligatory on our first night. Didn't disappoint. 

The food. The menu is not too big, its all small plates with some good vegetarian, fish and meat selections. 

Falafel sliders were amazing. As were the lamb sliders. The Meyer lemon was not detectable in the Cesar salad but it was excellent. Grilled shrimp on polenta was very good with a dark sauce. 

Dessert - hazelnut cake with Nutella ice cream - was very dry and not on par with the food quality. 

The Royal Roses were playing that evening - couldn't have planned a better way to start off our NOLA visit.

I'm on an Atkins diet and I find the sausage and egg biscuit and the ultimate omelette biscuit at Hardee's to be a perfect pow carb option (excluding the biscuits of course). The ultimate omelette has eggs cheese sausage and bacon and it is tasty with a good consistency. The sausage and egg was good not great. I went through the drive up at 7 am on a Wednesday morning and had a 7 minute wait from my order. They were busy. The lady was nice who served me, Oder was correct although no thank you for the order.

Wish I could give it zero stars. We were there for two hours. The first one and a half were spent patiently waiting for food and a second round of drinks. During our wait, two other tables of diners left after not receiving their food. The general manager, Joe, has no idea what his staff is doing and doesnt seem to care. There were a total of three tables occupied in the entire restaurant...no one was being served. The food came out cold and dry. Terrible food and terrible service. General manager "sorry for the bad experience but please come back." TURN AROUND AND GO TO RUBY'S DINER!! It is worth the wait...there's a reason "Plate" has no line. I did not enjoy paying $60 for a lunch with terrible food and terrible service...will not do it again at Plate

First of all if you carry have it on you.
No parking and no handicap parking.
Got there and was crowded and could not get on a waiting list.
I tried to ask the waitress`s and just got ignored.
And as far as the customers that were all ready there I think if i waited any longer i would have seen some nose picking.
VERY, VERY NASTY place.
Overall, great food. The only downside is that there is a lot of flies swarming in there.

Note: We did not stay in this hotel as guests.

We'd heard for the longest time to make sure we made our way to Gaylord while in Nashville, and I'm happy to say that we did. However, we opted out of actually staying there, as we had read a lot of negativity about it, and it was way too pricey for our liking.

The inside really is a sight to behold. It looks like you've wandered into a well kept rainforest, complete with trees, gardens, waterfalls, bridges, and even a boat ride around the resort. Simply beautiful, and with none of the downsides of being in a jungle, like bugs and intense heat. 

So...yeah, that's about it. The restaurants in the middle are also nice to look at, but way overpriced and the food isn't all that great. Another complaint is that it's extremely easy to get lost in there. I'm still not entirely sure that we got to see everything, but once we found where we entered, we weren't about to take a chance of losing it again, and left.

It's really nice to go through here once, and get lots of nice pics, but I don't think I'd return.

Oh, and the gas explosion that happened the day after we were there was purely a coincidence.
CLEAN! They open all the equipment in from of you! Richard did a great job on our tattoos and will definitely recommend him to anyone. His shading work was on point.

Food was not good. It was bland and dry. 
They give you a tiny (probably 20 chips) cup with chips no refill and "salsa" haha it was pico!! it had chopped tomatoes, onions, and cilantro. 
We order chicken fajitas and nachos. The chicken was incredible dry, no flavor and orange! Nachos were ok. Nothing to rave but ok. 
The place was overprice for the casual dinning experience and quality of the food. We just moved to this area from Texas and I must say, this place is considered mediocre on the south and for similar quality places, you would expect lower prices.
Oh, and lets not forget the "we don't take credit cards" and if you want to pay with a debit card, you need to get to the counter to pay and get charged $0.99 for using the card! WTH!!! You can tell a restaurant is cheap when they don't want to pay the fees for using a credit card and they make you- the customer-  pay for using a debit card. 
Seriously, you will better off going to chili's and get their generic Mexican food that at least taste fresher!
Will not go back to this place nor will we recommend this place.

Food is excellent the only negative is every time we have been the wait to get the food has been realy long last time we waited close to a hour for our food but if you are willing to wait the food itself is good and the staff has always been very friendly

Really enjoyed the atmosphere!! Great place to watch us open golf and women's World Cup at same time. Drunken meat balls were awesome. Ladies at the bar introduced themselves and were very attentive for drinks and food. Beers were ok. I tried the local Florida brews so nobodies fault that they were average. Great time!! Highly recommended.

We came in for a large group dinner during our convention. Mr. Bubba and Charlie took such good care of us. The dinners were all so good! We got tri-tip, rotisserie, and tacos. The Mahi special is highly recommended!  Thank you guys!

I found Anna Marie thanks to Groupon! Sometimes you get what you pay for on Groupon but Anna Marie is amazing! I switched from my previous wax spot to Adam & Eve and I'm so happy that I did! She uses hard wax, which in my opinion, is far less painful than soft wax. She was pleasant to talk to, kept the conversation going to avoid those awkward moments, and made me feel comfortable.

My new favorite vegan restaurant in the SB and Montecito area. We are sorely lacking in high quality vegan food that is more than just salads- and now Olivers is helping mend that problem! My partner and I came here and had the avo toast, the potato wedges with AMAZING green garlic sauce, the squash ravioli, the mushroom taco plate, and the chocolate torte. It was all absolutely delish! 

Service was great and the decor/ambience is lovely. Beautiful patio and nice bar. 

We will definitely be back to Olivers! Thanks for making veganism an even easier choice!

I too had been auto billed due to my membership when I moved to SF, although I spoke to Sean, the co-owner, and he immediately refunded my money that was billed by the 3rd party company. Him and the rest of the team were extremely helpful with not only my refund, but also giving me the proper coaching and sense of direction during my BJJ and Kickboxing training. I loved how friendly and chill everyone was at Paragon...absolutely no discrimination. The sense of family and academy pride was palpable.

Started training at Paragon Summer of 2011 and ended in Dec 2012 to move to SF. Love the people, trainers, culture and atmosphere of Paragon. Jeff Glover a legendary  BJJ World Champion and one of the best all time American BJJ practitioners started here and received his black belt from Alliance BJJ Black Belt Ricardo Franjinha Miller, the owner and founder of Paragon. I took more of the Kickboxing and Muay Thai, as I have more of a stand up background than grappling.

Def recommend this to anyone...don't be shy. lol

Very massive hotel, a lot to look at. The biggest downside is the fact that the hotel is very business-centric in the sense that everything is monetized and pretty expensive. The restaurants in the hotel are great, but expensive. The room service is really good, but really expensive. You can tell that the biggest feature of this hotel is the hotel itself. The atrium rooms are amazing, but wondering if it was worth the premium we paid for them. Seeing as we paid more for a room here than we would have in New York City, I wish they were a little bigger. The bathrooms feel a bit dated compared to some of the more modern hotels.

I don't know what they put in these things,but you will crave them. Are they the best most authentic Mexican tacos ever? No. But who cares? Delicious,cheap and quick and the sauces are the thing. My favorite is the City Slicker.
Delivery was late, pizza and garlic knots were cold. It was very disappointing. And I love all pizza usually. So sad.

UPDATE - I am giving them a star back because it appears the owner keeps up with yelp comments and genuinely cares about reviews and customer satisfaction. This has impressed me enough to go back for another try (plus a craving for truffle fries that will not go away), hopefully, after my next visit i will be able to bump it up another star or two.  500, I will see you soon. Fellow yelpers, I will keep you posted.

I have friends with horror stories about being Peach's tenants, but we'll leave them to write their own reviews. 
This is about my experience being a neighbor of a Peach property, known on our block as the Peach Pit.
Peach treats our neighborhood like a slum. 
The back of the property, where the trash cans are, is on a small residential street.  Peach's tenants dump all kinds of garbage on the street: broken glass, stinky kitchen garbage, broken furniture, just to name what's out there at the moment. 
As I write this there are two busted sofas, and an armchair with a big pile of poo on the seat. Smells like Peach!
Their landscape guy was there two days ago and saw all this stuff, but he's only paid to rake the front, so he left it all for the neighbors to enjoy. 
I wouldn't recommend Peach to property owners, tenants, or neighbors.

One of the best spas Northside of Indy. Personalized service and they provide you comfy robes. At the relaxation room, you'll be asked for what drinks you want (wine, tea, etc) and they have some warm booties. 

The room's ambiance can be changed with their LED lighting. You will need to sign off on a waiver by using their iPads too. 

This place is just a nice, little, trendy spa. The customized service sets them apart from competition.

Been going here for years when it was Zena's. Always good food. Now it's Orange Blossom. Same feel, same food. Love the the Morning Glory Omelette but the Pancakes are too bread like and sweet or lite and fluffy. Love everything else!

The location and amenities were great. The hotel wasn't bad, but the room wasn't great. Warning: be very careful where your room is located. Our room was facing the street and by the restaurant. It felt like people were inside our room because it was so loud. We could hear the neighbors toilet flushing and showers running.
Amazing beef and tripe.  Order anything drypot for a kicked up spicy stirfry.  Always the best in town.  They are my default asian cuisine and above compare for spicy selections.

Wings were good, but I don't like the service.   4 teenagers worker without any adult it  The worker jockeying very loud and in their phone all the time I was there.  it was unprofessional.  If the owner really care about the business he need to be there or at least hire a manager

In a City of full of  insatiable foodies, ruthless critics, and 'hood after 'hood of too-cool-for-school eateries, all vying for fame, the London Grill has certainly slipped off the wagon.

No AC and it's 90+ degrees out?! There were fans all over blowing around the musty air.  All the poor servers were literally dripping in sweat, trying their best to accommodate an obviously unimpressed audience.  I felt bad they were forced to work under these conditions.  I didn't even want to imagine what the cooks looked like.  Needless to say my appetite was small, all things considered,  and I steered clear of the meat.  We were even told to avoid certain best sellers on the menu (ie: Lamb Sandwich) because the roasts were over cooked that day, and it wasn't going to be their best show.  Good to know....

They tried to seat our party of 8 in a room off the 'green house' before we questioned the heat so much that they prepared a table for us one floor down in a half furnished room that hadn't seen life since.... Eastern State Penitentiary had vacancies?  Just an observation.

Oh, the food? Honestly mediocre. The Cesar was good. 

It's been years since I've been here, and I don't put the blame for this on anyone other than owners/mgmt.  I just couldn't stop the word "dive" from scrolling through my brain.  Get it together, London Grill!

This was the worst experience I have ever had at an IHOP. I had to send my breakfast back 3 times. I ordered the 2x2x2 with the eggs over medium and the egg whites were runny,so my meal was replaced with cold pancakes and sausage. I sent it back again and the eggs were worse than the first. I told them to forget it that I would go elsewhere and the manager came out to tell us that that is the way the eggs were supposed to be. We had to
Pay $8.40 for 2 cups of coffee and an order of toast. 
Love New Orleans, but would never go back to another IHOP again

This is a great hidden sushi gem right on the main Bripple drag. I've eaten here twice and both times I was very impressed with the quality of fish and service. They are attentive and the food comes out very quickly. The last time I went we had 5 of us and we got one of the little private rooms in the back which was super fun. We ordered the big boat for everyone to sample off of then ordered more as needed. Beer and wine are very affordable and let me tell you about those vino pours, damn, value sized. Highly recommend the rolls and sashimi, only 4 stars because the atmosphere is just eh. If only based on the experience in the back room it would be a solid 5 all day.

I feel like I may be an outlier here because I was unimpressed by The Fat Ham. Since moving to Philadelphia from Atlanta, I've been missing southern food tremendously and especially good southern-style PORK dishes, so upon hearing about this place I could not wait to get there. And I'm really not so picky - I love all types of food, I'm eager to appreciate it.
 
So, the dishes really were tasty but somehow just didn't induce those "mmms" I expect from a great restaurant. The portions are way too small for the prices and the flavors aren't as complex as you'd hope. 

My best advice is if you're actually from the South, don't go here expecting to find the haven for damn good southern food that you've been waiting for. If you weren't raised on this kind of food, I'm guessing you'll feel a lot warmer toward the place.

Great beer and atmosphere. Good food. Good service. Friendly and accommodating. I would recommend and go back. If you go on Friday or Saturday go early as it fills fast. Poor parking is why only 4 stars.
Super quick, friendly, great service. Fixed my tire, and checked the rest of the car for me before my trip out of town.

Better prices than I was able to find online.  Kind of a cool place to visit and hang out for a bit.  I am not a smoker, but enjoy vaping once in a while.  This place has a ton of flavors and a pretty good variety of hardware.  The owner was really helpful and didn't try to up sell me when I explained that I'm not a hardcore user.  He showed me the lower end more novice stuff.  I felt like I was treated well and this will definitely be where I return for supplies.

The anticipation of Milk & Honey has been building for literally years, and they finally opened with a lackluster impression. 
We came in for lunch and they did an excellent job with the space. It's very pretty and open with great design. 
Our waitress seemed a bit spacey and knew hardly anything about the menu, but it was only their second day open so I try to give some slack for new restaurants. However, she really should have been able to speak to the menu. We started off with the pastrami poutine and it was good but very rich. However, it was a good dish if you are wanting something substantial. Unfortunately that's about where the good ended. 
I had the turkey and brie sandwich with kale salad, and my BF had the fried chicken sandwich with farro salad. 
My turkey sandwich was not good. It came with fig jam that was way too much jam and leaked onto the outside which made my hands extremely sticky. Overall it was heavy and the flavors didn't meld together at all. The kale salad had too much dressing on it and the fried chicken sandwich was bland. I enjoyed the farro salad at least. My latte was good, but small and the honey latte was way too sweet, but I guess that comes with the order. 
The menu was promising and I was so excited for this place to open, but it was a let down after two years of waiting.

I have tried many Vietnamese places but this is by far my favourite.  If you are looking for a cheap bowl of pho or a noodle bowl look no further.  No, the tables don't get cleared right away, but we are in and out of there in less than 45 mins (usually 30!) even if the place is  packed.  #11, 22 and 44 are our favourites and you can't go wrong with the green onion cakes. Never paid more than $30 for a meal for two of us, and the tea is free!

Food is decent. Service is awful. It takes about 15 min to get an order in and another 15+ min to get the food. If you come order as much as you can the first time around, otherwise you'll be here for hours waiting for food.

I wanted to order more but it takes so long, I just gave up and left. It's too bad because this place has potential. Servers weren't very kind or attentive either. 

Just as an example we waited 30 min for udon noodles. On top of waiting the 15+min to actually get the order in. 

If you come, plan on being here a couple hours.

While we've had okay experiences with this restaurant before, lately we've been having experiences that have been worse and worse.

Tonight we ordered our food at 5:00 knowing that it could take 45min or so and now the time is 6:34pm and still no food.

My girlfriend called to check the status. At first they didn't answer, so she called again and some guy answered with attitude "Hello?" She asked if this was New Saint Louis Wok and all he said was "Yeah." 

So, they're taking forever AND then rude about it. Plus, the last time this happened the food was cold as well. It's just getting ridiculous

They just lost a customer who ordered from them on a semi-regular basis.

We love to go here for half price appetizers and drinks after the movie. The portions are huge even during happy hour so you can easily share with a friend or two. The lavosh is one of my personal favorites but I also enjoy the fruit and cheese plate, chicken fingers, sonoran shrimp cocktail, and the nachos from time to time. There are two happy hours each day. One for early birds and a second one from 9 pm to closing.

Favorite new pizza place. NOW LOCATED IN THE TREME. i'm sure they will update this soon, if not, I will because I want this place around for a long time. Had the spinach artichoke tonite and was very pleased. Very close to my house, so I'll definitely be back!!

Friendly bakers and very cute treats! I would be in big trouble if I lived here  their treats are priced well and if you have questions, they're more than happy to explain the ingredients. 

We ordered: citrus bar (GF) and everything croissant. 

Everything croissant was just perfect! A little bit of crunch on exterior but soft on the inside with delicious cream cheese 

Citrus bar was light and refreshing for a dessert bar.
Ugh.. Too many unsupervised kids. I love  kids, I truly do. Being in this place reminds me why we need more community centers.
Great food, nice and knowledgeable staff and the food was reasonably priced. We got the rainbow acai bowl and it was very good
i am in heaven great nite to see billy joel in concert great seats cant wait to see him ! lots of food , drinks, frozen cocktails,  really impressive stadium.

Me and my girls had so much fun on 11/13/15. The bartender was very attentive, the teacher was fun and we all had a great time. Some of us had never painted, and it proved that anyone can paint! I will definitely be back!

Food is excellent!!! The grouper is ridiculously amazing!! Along with the crab cake!!!!!!! Delicious!!!! The service is not stellar and this place needs a serious update but if you want good food with a decent view... Sculleys is it!!!!

High praise for Samantha who has cut my hair twice and given me exactly everything I asked for each time. I had too much texture going on and she was able to cut layers with blunt ends to mitigate the overly chipped previous cut. She spends time getting the cut right rather than quickly mass producing the same cut on everyone. She also gave me full "Birkin" bangs. I loved it!

I live around the corner and this is my second visit here.  
I went there this past Friday night with 3 guests.   Place was crowded but we were seated right away.   Staff was professional and on the ball with taking our orders and refilling drinks.   I did not get our server's name but kudos for a job well done. 
Bar was crowded and there seemed to be a handful of managers out on the floor. 
Beers were cold.   Our food was cooked and tasted great.  Zingers , burgers , cheese steaks and fries.
 Napkins were restocked as needed without asking.
The facility overall is very clean.   

What I really like about Millers is that it is wide open even though its packed , you are not crammed in .  You can sit and relax without floor traffic being a bother or folks hitting you as they get up from the tables around you.     They play good music without being so loud that you cannot have a conversation at the table.
I've read some of the bad reviews but as the name states : ALE HOUSE.  If ya want fancy then go into the city.    I think if folks stick to the basics there should be no problems.

Please train your cook or get a new one. Third time now that i get take out and its all burned up. Went in the trash last 2 times and told the guy taking my order on the phone to please make sure food is not burned but nope, same story this time around as well

If I could give this place a zero, I would.

Decor: dull and tired.
Staff: barely knowledgeable at what they do, and also CREEPY.  
Overall experience: RUN!!

I went in here for a bikini wax and a massage.  First up, the wax.  I think since I had booked a groupon-type deal, the woman assumed I had never had a wax before and could half-effort it.  I've gotten them frequently, and this one was unacceptable.  A third of the hair, at least, was still left.

Next up, massage.  CREEPY, CREEPY man, who hurt my back/neck and also grabbed me inappropriately CONTINUOUSLY below the sheet.

Please avoid.  This place does not deserve your money or time.

The male bartender (not sure his name) is super friendly, super knowledgeable, and... super friendly. By the looks of the place we thought it would be bad... it was seriously awesome. We got the shrimp tacos and the steak and cheese.. there are no words to describe... maybe we are just tourists and any Nola food is 10x better than what we are used to ... but it was amazing... the steak came out piping hot and each bite was like butter. The shrimp were seasoned wonderfully and just tasted awesome. This review was written only two beers in....
