Of course I was very nervous at first because there are lots of hot dangerous things around, but our instructor was excellent at helping us through the process. We made paperweights (which is a little weird since I don't really have any papers to weigh down) but it is great introductory project. We got to pick our colors and do all the fun heating and turning stuff - with adult supervision of course - and we were able to pick up the final product a few days later. It was a very low-level introductory class, but if someone really wanted to get into it and turn it into a hobby, they could easily do that at the Third Degree Glass Factory. I hear it's really great for group outings and children's classes, too. On another note, it was extraordinarily hot in there - I'm not sure if that was the heat from the glass-blowing, or the fact that the instructor was blatantly hitting on one of the girls in our group the entire time.

Stayed here to go to a Rays game.   Great location with a shuttle to Tropicana Field.  The rooms were very clean and comfortable.   There was a living room type common area outside our room and a little down the hall.  The bar and restaurant were very nice with outside seating.  The food was very good.  The staff were super friendly and beyond belief.  The lobby had comfy chairs to lounge to read a book or work on my computer.  Everything about this hotel was designed around relaxation.   We will be staying here for every Rays game and any other event in St. Pete.

Went in for lunch today around 11:30,   they were not very busy.. the service was HORRIBLE and the food came out cold.. my order was wrong, I never got my ice tea and the server's response.. We only have 3 people working today.  So.. that is my problem... Everything we ordered was cold and horrible.    My conclusion after being here on several occasions.. they are ok for breakfast and their lunch is always horrible.   Not going back.   ** To top it off, I had a 2 yr old with me and we waited and waited and his mac n cheese came out COLD .. the server put it down and said be careful it is HOT.. really.. I touched it and it felt like it came out of the refrigerator.. the baby wouldn't eat it after one bite.    Go figure .  I won't be going back ..

A great local shop to spend an afternoon. Needed to spend time to finally get a bra to actually fit right. I had a bra fitting and a good consultation on what I was looking for. There are a lot of styles to try and many neutral colors to make it more practical.  Will be back in the new year when  corsets  come in and springtime to look at the bridal collection for my wedding.

Interested in lunch plans elsewhere but wanting to go on a steamboat, me and my parents purchased tickets for the steamboat only.

Pros:
-Plenty of seating
-Lots of time to walk around
-Good history of the buildings we passed

Cons:
-It was raining the day we went (which is inevitable yet nonetheless sad)
-I guess you can smoke anywhere. Some guy was smoking an extremely potent cigar next to us...and an entire elementary school class on a field trip. It got me a little peeved.

It's a good touristy thing to do all together though, most of what I didn't enjoy was not the boat's fault.

Got a pound of crawfish ($12/lb) and a dozen oysters ($17) recently and they were good but not great. The crawfishs were nicely boiled and seasoned nice and spicy. We got the first batch boiled that day and it took a long time for them to get ready. I also did see them dumped the previous day's leftover into the batch after the initial cook. I guess that's to be expected but hate to see it done. Anyway, what was dumped in wasn't that much, so it wasn't an issue, BUT that's probably not always the case. As for the oysters, they were actually a tad smaller than other places, e.g., Felix's. However, they also skimped on the lemon slices as well, going for quarter wedges, which was disappointing since it was barely enough. Anyway, service was slow as all heck (probably waited like 30 min between ordering and getting served) and certainly did not come with a smile either.
I have always enjoyed the food at Luke.  They have a wonderful happy hour with cheap oysters and drinks.  They also make one heck of a burger.  My only problem has been the inconsistent service.

A local gem!

Old school charm. Great menu. Accommodating staff. Most importantly - excellent food, without pretense.

There was a mistake on the check not in my favor, which I didn't notice. While driving back they called me and corrected the mistake. I wouldn't have even noticed, so they went out of their way.

Will definitely go again and tell all my friends.

I just moved to Indianapolis and my car started making a God awful noise. I decided to rely on yelp to decide where to take it which can be risky. I'm glad I took the risk and didn't just take it to some well known chain. I took it in, not really even knowing what was going on, and got it all fixed and back on the road same day. Kieth and Brian were tremendously helpful and even took the time to show and explain some things to me. I will definitely be back with any other problems. Trust this 5-star rating.

This place I must say was probably in my top 10 dining experiences ever !!  If you're reading this review do yourself a favor make reservations to visit this  restaurant.  They have a little jazz band set up in the corner by the front door.  Music was Very nice,the customer service was exceptional and the food was amazing !

I've been visiting Dr. Kasper at the Coleman Center for Women for about five (5) years, for my annual "ladies" appointment.  Dr. Kasper is straight-forward and down-to-earth, with a bit of a wry sense of humor (which one can appreciate in OBGYN situations).  My appointments always take less time than expected, the phlebotomist is a blood-drawing ninja, and the nurses' station has been helpful with calling in prescriptions with short notice. The office's decor is a little dated, but that really isn't important in the grand scheme of things.

I find the Coleman location convenient, in walking distance from my office.   For outside visitors, I recommend the $5 valet parking for patients off the University Hospital's main entrance off University Blvd.  Finding parking nearby can be...complicated, as you're competing with IUPUI students/staff and multiple hospital campuses for limited space. The valet parking is cheap and you can drop off your car right by the front entrance. If you're hungry, the University Hospital cafeteria is pretty meh (minus the pizza station), but there is a close-by Copper Moon where you can pick up a quick latte after your appointment.

Divine Designs Floral and Tropicals designed the lovely floral arrangements for my daughter's wedding. My daughter provided Rachel and Gary with a few images of flowers that she liked, and they ran with it! Allison wanted a wildflower look for a vintage themed wedding...and she got exactly what she wanted!

Rachel and Gary were a dream to work with. They were easy to contact and even invited us to the showroom a couple of times to "play" with flowers to make sure that we were happy with the designs. 

The wedding ceremony and reception were held at one location. All of the flowers were in place and ready in plenty of time prior to the ceremony. All I can say is that I was blown away when I walked into the reception room and saw how they had decorated everything! The centerpieces, the mantle arrangement, and the sweetheart table were stunning! I peeked into the courtyard where the ceremony took place to see the swags in place and all of the aisle chairs decorated beautifully. Then to the bride's room to see my girl and the gorgeous bridal and bridesmaid bouquets... just beautiful! 

The flowers all held up beautifully for over a week past the wedding. I would highly recommend Devine Design Floral for any event. Our guests kept commenting on how beautiful all of the flowers were. There is no substitute to real flowers. They added such a special touch to such a memorable day!

Thank you, Rachel and Gary!
 
Everything was simple elegance ~ just as Allison wished!

Best place to stay in Reno. Super friendly staff, and the rooms are always clean and ready at check in.  
Tip, call for a room rather than book online.  I've always gotten extra help/accommodations when speaking with the staff.  Keep up the good work Peppermill!

We started off with the mussels (Belgian),  it was good, but the mussels were very small. The filet mignon was cooked the way I liked it (MR), but it was not seasoned well, if at all and the outer side tasted burnt. The lump crab was minimal, and the mashed potatoes were not anything out of the ordinary, but the asparagus was cooked properly. The hollandaise sauce was gelatinous and looked to be left out for a while; I did not care for that. Everything is a la carte (which basically means eat less or pay more). We ordered mushroom risotto and the brussel sprouts with the dinner. It is very hard to find good risotto, but at Marmont, the risotto was well cooked and tasty. The brussel sprouts were good, but it would have been nice to have it seasoned, but I suppose that is what the bacon and shallots are for. If the prices were lowered or if the entrees included one side, I would try this place again.

I love Albasha.  I'm not sure where it started but I've been hooked on their food since about 2006 when I lived in Shreveport.  I've picked up twice from the one in Metairie.  Glad to see they  haven't lost their touch.

So when I go to pick up the food, the waitress is going over my order.  I accidentally ordered the gyro plate instead of sandwich.  I asked her how long it would take to whip one up.  Apparently, not long.  I had my gyro wrapped and ready to go in about 3 minutes.  That's pretty good pick-up service.

The food was delicious. It's not gourmet, but it is solid from top to bottom.  Our salads were great.  I completely finished mine off.  Then, I crushed that gyro sandwich.  I actually had to remove meat off the sandwich, because it was so packed.  The bread for hummus dipping was soft and doughy.  The hummus itself was excellent.  Good consistency.  

We were looking for a quick pick up to go along with a lazy college football afternoon, and Albasha was perfect.  The food was excellent and plentiful.  Well worth the drive.

Everything is amazing at El Limon. I love the al pastor & carnitas tacos as well as the huge burritos. The staff is great and always remember me and welcome me with a smile. The tortas are delicious as well.
A higher attention to detail is given here than other barbers in the area. Worth every penny in my opinion. Old school barbers who actually take pride in their work. Hard to find.

Great food.  Did I say great food.  Hardly any lines.  Great drinks.  Pours could be more generous.  Was not crowded at all.....maybe the heat kept people away.

Need better signs with directions from the parking garages, and more tables and chairs.

  The restaurants serving the grilled food in the middle of the park at 6pm and 7pm......amazing.  wings, chicken.  

Hope to see even more vendors next year.

I recently relocated from NYC to Nashville and was not sure what I was going to get when changing dentists. Dr Harris came highly recommended to me and even then exceeded my expectations. Starting from the moment I walked in I was greeted by a very friendly and professional front desk staff. The office itself is gorgeous  and very conveniently located in the Gulch. I was seen straight away and had one of the best cleanings. After the cleaning Dr Harris met with me and did a throurough inspection. He asked me about any concerns I had and we discussed some cosmetic work that I had been considering. Dr Harris was very professional and did not try and sell me anything that I did not need / was not looking for. He has vast knowledge and state of the art technology. I look forward to my next consultation visit.

Lather Hair Studio is easily the best salon I have  been to in Philadelphia. Not only are the employees warm and welcoming (offering coffee, water, wine!!!) but also incredibly knowledgable and talented about all things hair.  I went to Lather to get my dream hair color, PURPLE, and not only did Dena succeed in giving me this color but she also took the time to use the appropriate amounts of bleach and color removers in order to not damage my hair, which she told me is very important to Lather Hair Studio. I would recommend this salon to any and everyone, strangers and my own mother. Lather excels in alternative hair styles but will still give you the best and most beautiful traditional style of your choice, these ladies are professionals. Love you, ladies of lather!

Stopped in Slainte while we waited for our train headed to DC.  Its conveniently close to the train station (about a block or so away) so if you've got an hour or so between your connection its a better option than what is offered inside the station itself.  

I really wish we could give 1/2 stars on yelp (come on already w/ that!!!) because I really do think Slainte is a solid 3 1/2 stars!  Food was mostly very good and the portion sizes were large which was a bonus.  

We started w/ an order of the awesome fries...which were in fact awesome.  Nice and crisp w/ lots of cheesy bacony goodness!  It was a HUGE portion also.  So much that 3 of us could barely finish half of them!  For our lunch entrees two of us opted for the soup & sandwich special.  1/2 of a French Dip w/ a cup of their potato soup.  Honestly I wish I'd have just went w/ the entire French Dip because it was very good.  The soup...not so much.  It wasn't very good and had a weird spiced flavor that I couldn't quite distinguish but it definitely did not enhance the soup at all.  We also got the Rueben which I was told was excellent and much better than the Rueben he previously ordered the day before in New Jersey.  It also came w/ a heaping amount of fries.  All in all a really decent meal!  We'd definitely hit them up when in town again.

Service by Heather and hostess at time . 
I will write about the food which was great in another review later on  to balance the offset.

A- Atrocious 
R- Ratchet
B - Bizarre
Y - Yikes
S - Sad, sad, sad...

Ok, so it is totally our fault for eating at this ARBYs.  But after a long day of eating really good food (see review from Commanders Palace - AND, yes ... Commander's Palace to Arby's is a major fall from grace).  We didn't have the energy or stomach capacity to sit through another huge meal that day, but were afraid to head back to the hotel w/o having a little something for dinner.

We popped into Arby's after bypassing all of the scary looking dives along Bourbon Street.  In the distance we saw ARBY's which generally represents "safe" fast food.  Au contraire my N'Orleans frere.  

Upon arriving, the manager had to prompt one of his seven workers hanging out behind the counter to actually take our order.  After some prodding, I was waited on by a young lady who indicated that she was sluggish, b/c she had to work until 4AM - it was only 9PM at that point.  Ok, fine - I get it!  I tried to encourage her and proceeded with my order.  All I wanted was a classic BLT - which clearly many patrons don't order from this location as the prep cook repeatedly asked the cashier "she ordered a BLT?"  As if I had ordered caviar and quail eggs.  

Sit back, b/c it gets worse ... we noticed an interesting crock pot / slow cooker on the counter ... interesting b/c the handle on the lid was missing and they had it rigged up with some sort of wire.  When we asked what it was used for - they said it was used to keep the au jus sauce warm.  Surely, this rigged up crock pot cannot be a part of the customized / standardized Arby's franchise plan.  

Additionally, we waited nearly 10 minutes, while they fried an order of mozzarella sticks for my friend. I guess it was a slow night for the staff b/c the guy working the deep fryer thought it  would be cool to throw the mozz sticks to the prep cook who was waiting to place them in the bag ... of course, the bag slipped from the prep cook's hands and landed on the floor.  She then proceeded to ask my friend if she wanted the mozzarella sticks that had fallen on the floor (since, in her words, the actual mozzarella sticks hadn't hit the floor) or if we were willing to wait for them to fry up another batch!  Yep, you guessed it ... another 10 mins for them to fry another batch!

LESSON LEARNED.

Tonight I visited gateway to India with my girlfriend to pick up a menu. I am new to the area so I am exploring different restaurants to see what is good. In the five minutes it took us to go inside pick up a menu and read over it for a little I was treated better then about 80% of restaurants I have been to and actually sat down and had a meal in. I will be definitely revisiting this restaurant to have an actual meal and I look forward to it. Its restaurants like this but I love going to I am sure this is soon to be one of my favorite restaurants in all of St Pete. A simple gesture like saying please feel free to have a seat while reading our menu can go a long way

I'm really torn about La Mulita. The food is good and the atmosphere is pleasant but it's overpriced. I wish I could give half stars because I really feel a 3.5 on this place.

The guacamole was good however there was little guacamole served compared to other places, especially for $5. The chips and guac don't come with salsa which is fine, as there is a bottle of salsa on the table. Upon tasting the salsa though, it was odd and seemed like it would be better on wings than chips or tacos. You get more bang for your buck with the guacamole and salsa at Bakersfield. 

I ordered the "bring me a shrubbery" cocktail and was very disappointed. It was very bitter (which I usually enjoy), but the mix of flavors was just unpleasant. I would not recommend it. I ended up switching it for a margarita which was pretty good. Again, small for $9. I would say Bakersfield has better margaritas. My boyfriend got the Barbados drink which we both enjoyed. 

As for the tacos, I got the pork carnitas and split them with my boyfriend who got the steak & chorizo tacos. The pork tacos were good and pretty lean, but nothing crazy in my opinion. It may be better with the green sauce but that contains dairy so I could not use it. I did really enjoy the steak and chorizo tacos. They were unique and flavorful and I would recommend them. I liked both tacos better than ones I've had at Bakersfield. Since we couldn't eat the green sauce we requested salsa verde to put on our tacos instead. It was okay but I wouldn't rave about it. 

Again, I'm really torn. I don't think I will go back but I would probably recommend it if someone asked me about it.

My husband and I went here for the first time yesterday looking for a fairly inexpensive recliner. I didn't really know what to expect but was pleasantly surprised. The store was clean and well organized and we were greeted right away. Billy was the employee that helped us and he was very helpful without being pushy at all. All the employees were very laid back. 

They didn't have a lot of recliners in the store but he showed us what was also available online and in the catalog. We ended up buying a floor model that we liked and I feel like we got a good price for the product. 

I really liked the other furniture and brands they had there and plan on going back when we need more items.

Enjoyed dinner with the wife here on June 30, 2011.  Excellent Italian dinner with generous portions.  I can see why the locals love it so much.  Relaxed but semi-upscale atmosphere, excellent food and great location.

First al fresco dining day of the year - selected Tria over Varga for a late brunch.  Service, while a little slow, was overall fine, until 3/4 of the way through our meal, when some heavy metal clipboards were accidentally dumped onto my left shoulder from a shelf 3 feet in the air behind me (ouch), leaving me with swollen and bruised left shoulder.

Now, understandably, accidents will happen, and our server apologized several times. However, in my experience, if a paying customer is excessively spilled on or accidentally injured(!), it is typically good customer service for the manager to offer a small 'mea culpa' of sorts  - perhaps pick up my cup of coffee or my bottle of Pellegrino?  Nothing, which suprised me for a place I once considered a quality establishment.  

I found this to reflect very poorly on the 13th St. Tria and I probably won't return.  Its a shame because I've been going to the Rittenhouse location for years and loved it.
-----------------------------------------
Update: Upping to four stars.   Tria's very gracious owner saw my Yelp rewiew and made the kind offer of a gift card (which is actually way better than a coffee or Pellegrino  :-)  A lovely gesture in making things right.

I'm so glad to know that Tria is still the great place I've always loved.  Thank you Tria - we will be back!!

If you're near the French Market, stop by. Even if you're not, stop by. The fried green tomato po' boy is next level. Tomatoes aren't sliced too thick and cut like butter. Batter is nice and crispy. Definitely one of my favorite bites in New Orleans. Possibly one of my favorite bites ever.

Service was terrible staff was talking over the food. the food tasted horrible the rice was very undercooked and was so hard. I ordered a salad bowl . I picked up the food during my lunch break and I could not even eat half of the plate I had to throw it away I will never be coming back to this moes location

Just got home from my first cut and color from miss jo and the first thing my boyfriend said, with a big smile was, "you look younger!" I kid you not! Very good job Jo! Thank you for holding my hand through my second ever attempt at color. Plus a great blow dry which I always turn down due to past attempts at managing my wavy hair... Glad I said yes. 
The salon is small, intimate, easy. Come early and peruse the shop (Bon castor run by miss Amy) for fun ... Pet belle, the sweet pup who knows how to close doors... Laugh with Jo who truly can't be more personable and warm. A lovely evening and a very natural look for me, which is exactly what I wanted.

This is probably the in my top 3 for best burger I've ever had in my life.  In town from Texas for Spring Break.  We were pleased as a party of 6 everyone was pleased with there selections.  Would visit agIn whenever in town again.5 stars..... *****
Stopped by this little joint on the way into the convention center. Really fast service and the food was great!! Servers were quick to refill coffee and the grits were awesome!

My wife was attacked and bitten by a rabid raccoon as we exited the theater. Thousands of dollars and a long period of angst followed before she was in the clear from rabies.Staff was minimally helpful. The off duty police officer was kind enough to alert us as we waited for the EMS to arrive that they also had a gator that hung out under cars on the backside parking lot. We go elsewhere.

Wow what can I say about this beach!!!!!!! I lovedddddd it!!! They have public parking and it wasn't expensive. Came out to be about $4.50 for 3 hours. They have chairs you can rent for $5.00 which I thought was a steal. I have seen beach chairs for rent for$10.00!!! 

The first day we went the waves were small not a big deal at all. The water was calm the second day I visited. It reminded me of the beach in Aruba. Not as clear but clean enough!!! My girlfriend is funny with beach water but she didn't want to leave this place!!! The sand is clean and they have a tiki bar not to far from the public parking. So we visited them for some great wings and amazing drinks!!!!  

They do have one outside shower I saw but I chose not to use it because it's drain must have not been working and and u had to step in everyone else's previous water. 

All in all St. Pete Beach won me over and I will actually visit them again and this time instead of driving an hour to get there!!!!! I will stay at one of its resorts!!!!  See you soon!!!!

This is place is great for bad Thai. Not sure what these reviews are about. I ordered a simple clear noodle dish - that was bad. My husband ordered a fried rice dish and the rice was mush. All ingredients including the mushrooms and carrots were canned or frozen. If you want bad Thai come here! I will not come back here even if they paid me to eat here. The worst Thai I ever had.

This was fun! I thoroughly enjoyed myself. I felt comfortable and our instructor Jenny was very friendly and helpful. They're right next door to Napa-Sonoma who will bring your order from wine to food right to you.  All you simply have to do is bring yourself. They supply everything needed for the project you pick. This was the best use of my 3 hours in a long time. I will definitely be doing this again.

They have a pretty good but not outstanding buffet, with about 10-12 entrees (including vegetarian) and a reasonable variety of appetizers, side dishes, and vegetables (spring rolls, egg rolls, dim sum, sushi, crab puffs, string beans, french fries, etc.). The food isn't unusually good, but it's adequate. One area offers half a dozen types of fruit (which are generally from a can). Soft ice cream and fortune cookies are the desserts. You can also order from an extensive menu; they serve large portions of most items.

The decor is plain, not much above cafeteria level. Service (serving drinks, clearing dishes, etc.) is efficient and friendly. Note: the sweetened iced tea is VERY sweet!

BEER BEER and oh yeah BEER!

This was an impressive fun, and free tour. The staff was very knowledgeable and friendly for this large site tour. We went around Christmas when everything was decorated and dolled up. They have quite the light show and people come from miles around. It's always fun seeing their horses, too.

The best part? Drink as much as you want at their bar when you're at the end of the tour (just get a DD). Not a fan of Bud? Well, it tastes far better from their tap, TRUST ME. Also, you can taste all the Euro brews, now that they were bought up by a European Brewery.

I highly recommend this to any tourists in the STL area.
Wanted to try this place out for awhile, finally made it. Cocktails were great, I had a Cloverclub made with Plymouth gin. We had the hen, maple soy salmon, popcorn chicken. It was great!

I love BBQ, and since moving to Nashville I have tried to find BBQ that I love as much as Dreamland or Full Moon. Edley's comes close. I got the pork plate with mac and cheese and green beans. The pork was tender and flavorful. It had smokey flavor with out going over board. The sauce is a good blend of sweet and spicy. The mac and cheese was baked and was made w/ real cheese. The green beans were flavorful but nothing special. 

My friend got the BBQ nachos. Of course, I had to have a taste and they were awesome. First of all the chips were house made potato chips instead of corn chips--awesome. The portion was huge and the toppings were very fresh and flavorful. 

We were there at lunch on Wednesday. They were steadily busy but service was prompt and attentive. 

I will definitely be returning to Edley's. There are a lot of other things on the menu I can't wait to try.

I have finally tried all three of Steven Starr's restaurants in Philly (unless there are more I don't know about lol). I had a great dinner here last night for my friend's birthday party, but I do have to say it's my least favorite of the three (continental being my favorite by far). 

The atmosphere is a swanky, 70s ski lodge complete with the shaggy carpet. They were very accommodating for a party of 8 on a Saturday night. 

They have a great selection of creative cocktails. I order a blueberry vodka drink with mint. It was delicious. 

For dinner, I had to go with the grilled cheese and tomato soup. They have several comfort food options, but the grilled cheese was calling my name. I made a good decision because the cheese was perfectly gooey and the soup was creamy. I added avocado to my grilled cheese because, why not ? 

The service was great. The food was good. I'm giving this restaurant 4 stars because I know Steven Starr can do better.

First time stopping by this drive-thru coffee stand.  Coffee was full flavored, not watery like Dutch Bros.  I enjoyed it.

Also ordered a bacon,egg, potato, cheese breakfast burrito.  It was very good.  They owner makes them daily or every other day and heats them up when ordered.  They are well made and the green salsa is good, but pretty small in size.  I liked it a lot better than Los Betos, but would be happy if they offered a larger size burrito for an extra $1-2. 

Anyways, the total was around $6 for the medium coffee and small, but tasty burrito.  Not bad.  Ill be back for sure.  

I know its a lot to ask, but if they got a little griddle and made the burritos fresh the tortilla wouldn't be dry and the ingredients would be piping hot.  Plus, they could offer two sizes.

Good sized burger with a big patty of meat, but can't say it's the best burger in town.  We also had the veggie burger- definitely would not get that again...too dry.  We came for lunch on Sunday, and there was no wait.  If we were in the neighborhood again we would eat here again, but a place I would not crave to come.

I moved to Philly two years ago from NYC, and while I love my new city and most of what it has to offer, I've had a HORRIBLE time finding a hair stylist. I have been to FIVE hair salons and each visit was worse than the other. I can't begin to explain how horrible my hair has looked. But I finally found Daniel Iannelli, who was at another location, but recently relocated to 21M. I am not exaggerating when I say I've only had one other hair stylist color my hair as well (the other was a celebrity stylist in NY). He also gave me a great cut, though I'm growing my hair out now. So color has been my primary issue. He's so well versed in what works to make your hair look natural, and suited to your skin tone (very important for a blonde). His customer service is top notch and he really takes all the time he needs to get it right. So happy to have pretty hair again!

The food is always delicious here. We've come here a few times for dinner and tried brunch for the first time today. The service is always a little slow... Taking away a star for me. It's a smaller space with a cute atmosphere. Drink menus are in cute old kids books. 

Brunch -- My party got the confit pork belly and eggs, cinnamon roll pancakes, corned beef hash and eggs, and the huevos. The confit pork belly and eggs was good but not quite what I expected, I wouldn't order it again. The corned beef on the other hand was out of this world. Very salty and has a kick but not in a bad way. My friend said that the huevos were delicious. The pancakes were out of this world. The cinnamon and sugar on top was a crunchy caramelized texture that really added to the pancakes. Loved them 
Also side note. The biscuits were good but not nearly as delicious as other reviewers claimed (at least in my book!) 

Dinner -- their Mac and cheese is delicious. I make sure to always get a side no matter what I'm eating. 

Overall good food, good drinks, ok service.

Me and a friend stop by for happy hour today and I was extremely disappointed and will not be back.  We arrived around 3:45pm on a Wednesday; they were in no way busy and we figured this would go smoothly. I order a glass of Merlot from a new male waiter.  A female waitress comes by and says she's training him and they are out of merlot.  I say that's okay and request a Cab instead; she returns and says they are out of Cab, I request the Pinot Noir, she returns again and says they are out of the Pinot Noir, I end up with the Malbec (4th choice). My friend got the 2 for 1 beer; in 90 degree heat (seated inside, but it's warm) she brings both beers at the same time.  After the food was delivered and finished, no one had checked on us.  I had to go to the bar to request a second glass of wine.  At this point there was a max of 6 people there with 3 at the bar.  The food wasn't good enough to make up for the lack of service.  I brought the lack of service to the "bartenders" attention and no one seemed bothered.  I won't be back; there's many places in Nashville with better food, better wine selection, and MUCH better service.
Tiny place... Great pizza!!   Parking is tough, but it always is in historic Palm Harbor!

What a great time! This was definitely a 5 star tour and we'd highly recommend it to anyone.

Marcus is the owner and operator of this company and he is incredibly knowledgable about the city he clearly loves. I'm not a huge runner so I was a little afraid of doing a 10K without "training" much but honestly I didn't even really feel the distance until we finished, mostly due to the fact that our discussion and Marcus was so engaging and informative. The pace was moderate but certainly not intense and we stopped and talked enough that even modest runners can do this trip.

Marcus took us all around the French Quarter, the Garden District, a historic cemetery and other neighborhoods and had answers to literally every question we could think to ask. He knew history and landmarks and didn't shy away from talking in detail about the checkered past of New Orleans... prostitution, slavery and the like. We finished the tour after 90 minutes feeling like we had a great overview of the city's attractions and landmarks and could now decide what else to explore during the rest of our trip.

Highly recommended, and help support a local business!

Lovelovelovelove this place. Good coffee, great tea, and an awesome hipster ambience? Yes, please. 

I've run by this place several times in the last month or so in preparation for the RTO. Oddly enough, it was my book club meeting that actually brought me inside the place. 

To start off I had the Coconut Chai Latte and a quiche. The latte was decent, if a little weak in flavor. But the quiche was as tasty as can be. They have an interesting and yummy selection of eats and treats, so it's totally an acceptable place to meet for either breakfast or even lunch. 

I may have started off with a Coconut Chai, but I ended with a Lavender Latte. Twice over. What I mean to say is...I tried my mom's Lavender Latte, loved it so much that I chugged my Chai, got up and got my own Lavender Latte. Then I became a crazed Lavender maniac and bought a SECOND Lavender Latte. 

That's a lot of Lavender. 

But obviously it was delicious. So frothy. The lavender is light, but strong enough to leave a lasting impression, which is surprising considering the fact that it's an herbal tea. Either way, I will definitely be coming back for more.  

As far as the book club meeting went, I wouldn't always recommend meeting large groups here. There is absolutely enough seating to accommodate a large group, but the place seems to be perpetually packed. 

Overall, it was a nice experience. I look forward to coming back and having another Lavender Latte. And they have a bunch of other interesting tea blends as well! 

Happy Yelping.
Have been going there for several years now. They have really helped to keep my migraines under control. Nice and relaxing environment as well.

Well out to grab some quick Mexican food without having to wait, I searched through my bookmarks and being new in town and not an insider yet, saw a tremendous amount of traffic for the first two weeks it's been open. So up to SoBro I go!!

I arrived it what appeared as a shopping complex that's had better days. I think this shopping center may have been featured in Judgement Night featuring Denis Leary, but now I'm digressing. So I abscond from my car with my wallet and shuffle inside. My first impression of here was that it was new considering there was just a cloth sign covering the previous owners sign. The interior is not much to look at, but I was there for one thing.  Tacos!!

I said hi to the owner who was more than polite and decided on 4 tacos, one of each meat. I had a seat while my mouth watered. Before I knew it the food was in front of me and the CCTV captured me drooling. If you are unfamiliar with authentic Mexican tacos they consist of double wrapped corn shells with meat, white onion, and cilantro.  Here they are also served with lime, cucumber, and red and green sauces on the side, nice touch.  No cheese for you, and that suits me just fine. Now Indy tacos let me taste your wares!

The chicken -very juicy and flavorful, very spiced but not spicy. 5
The steak-insanely juicy and meaty. Strong taste of pepper. This was the best of the bunch. 5+
Chorizo- oh how I love you. Mexican sausage, spicy, full flavor. 5
Al pastor-I wasn't digging the pineapple flavor but I'd still give it a solid 4. 

When I come back I'll probably get it to go and take it to the park, because the inside of the restaurant makes me feel like I'm in a cubicle, but the food more than made up for the lack of quality ambiance. While I was eating, I say at least 15 pick-up orders came in and they're off to a rocket start. The next will be me. 
Customer service 5
Food plus 5
Ambiance 3. Solid 4+ overall. And once again if you see me in there, back off or I'll buy out their whole stock:)

Tucked in the corner of a strip mall, shared with a gym and harbor frieght, I found a delicious Cuban eatery. One could assume they are mainly a take out place by the way it was set up. This is exactly what my hubby and I did. There are tables and chairs to sit in if you feel like dinning out. I like options :)

After a long hard ponder at the amazing selections, I decided on the pulled pork roast, yellow rice and green beans.  The rice was exactly what I hoped for. Firm and flavorful, cooked perfectly. The green beans were good, nothing to write home about. The pork was the star. It melted in my mouth. It had that built in flavor only a slow cooked roast can achieve. It paired well with the Cuban bread which was warmed and buttered. Definetly a home cooked meal feel, but in the best possible way. 

I will definetly be back.

Haven't had much of their food but, this is one of the best boba places I've been to!  Can take a while during lunch hour which can suck.  If your crunched for time in the lunch hours just be aware.  Its worth the line in my opinion.

I come to Nashville a lot. probably around 6 times a year. 
This is the first time I was so disappointed with a hotel. Our room had a very moldy smell. There was a knocking noise every half hour in the walls. I couldn't get a good night's rest. The only positive thing I can say is that it is about 15 minutes and a $15 uber ride away from the main strip of downtown Nashville. The shuttle charges you $10 a head round trip so if you have more than 2 people uber it. That way you get picked up and dropped off at the exact location and you can get picked up whenever and wherever you'd like. 
Happy Travels!

This is the closest where I live, but I am not here that often. The Pizza is OK, not terrible but  even one of the 4 star reviews mention, there are better pizza joints in Philly.  So, if I don't feel like getting in my car to drive there and walking over, I'll come over here. Not to mention they are open way late, so if other pizza joints are closed, I'll come here. 

I met the owners, who are nice people and I never had a bad experience with the service and sometimes there are lunch specials for 2 slices and a soda.  But the biggest  problem is there are many pizza joints in Philly, its a competitive market and if there are better slices out there, I am going to go there.

We went on Easter. It was a beautiful day, and they had the entire front open. The service was great. Two lovely young ladies. It's a cute, small space. We got the Brussels sprouts, and the Brisket, and we loved it. We ended up sharing it because they've got big portions. The music was fantastic.
Great time, went with my best friend and it was our first visit.  Everything was delicious. A lovely outing!

This is by far the best lunch I have ever had in Philadelphia. I started to go down the street but per my friends choosing, we came here. #WIN!!!!! Kate our waitress was amazing. When I went to order, I asked her about my selection and she said "your making ALL the right choices" lol. Indeed #facts. The reuben sandwich was so thick and tasty. But the highlight was the oxtail fries. Life itself!!!! So juicy, so flavorful, soooooo delicious! If your coming to Philly, you better stop here or slap yourself for not doing it!
Great local Italian food. Went here a few weeks ago for a graduation dinner and food was outstanding. Ambience was good and food felt authentic and very tasty. Will definitely return!

The small plate apps were very good.  Didn't expect this high quality food coming from a restaurant right off of Kelly drive.  The crab tortelloni was my favorite, I would go back just to eat more of them.

Prices are higher than expected but food quality was also higher than expected so I would say they are priced fairly.  We were so distracted by all of the small plate foods that we didn't even really try the pizzas.  I'm hearing good things on that end too so looking forward to my next meal at In Riva.

Had a great first time experience here. Food was good we ordered the bronze salmon, steak, and two pizzas. We got Brussel sprouts and a little Dutch oven bread thing for appetizers, which were good but I felt the Brussels were a bit drenched in sauces, but everyone at my table loved them. The waitress was excellent, very friendly and attentive.

Dissapointing. Went towards the end of the day. Ordered chicken curry, garlic naan and chicken samosas. I am not too picky about food, but I took a bite of a samosa and had to spit it out. It was soggy with oil and tasted like the oil was reused for too long. 

I was hesitant but I tried the naan. Can't mess up naan right? They managed to- It was tough and not fresh and even though it had garlic on it you couldn't taste it. Just dissapointing. Won't ever go back.

It was the worst experience of my family and my life. The food was absolutely horrible. We had chicken; absolutely no flavor at all. BBQ ribs: it was smothered with sage. They should call it sage ribs. Greens: it had no flavor, not even salt. Corn bread: basic. Jiffy corn bread is better. Red beans and rice was just okay. Jambalaya: was the worst . My daughter threw up all night and early this morning . It is our worst nightmare. She can't keep anything down and she is very weak. She said the sausages were horrible in the Jambalaya and that contributed to her great food poisoning . The fish was extremely bland. No taste at all . Needless to say I was truly disappointed to say the least in every aspect of this resturant . I spoke to management and all they could tell me was that I was the only one complaining. Like my husband said: it's s waste of time to complain to them , just never go again and when someone ask us about the resturant, just tell them the truth. If you don't want to be sick and laid up on your back for a few days sick. Then stay away from this place for life!!!!!!  BEWARE !!!!!!!!



Hello Gloria, 
     This is Sonja, the evening that we ate at your resturant was August 3, 2015. Thank you for taking my comment seriously. God bless you.

This place is great!!! It has a neighborhood bar feel. The bartenders are excellent and know you, your drink, and your hookah by name!! Excellent service! Great food. Please try it...you will not be disappointed!

Great atmosphere, decent drinks.  However the management needs to train bartenders to look customers in the eye to see they want service.  The music is loud so they can't hear you and they interact well with each other which is great but when you have to get their attention by turning a finished drink upside down that sucks.  Then they get attitude and tell you that was disrespectful and this is your last drink.  Given it was my only drink of the night and first time there, it became my last.  Management can feel free to contact me I can explain more.  I had three restaurants I can help you save this new place is you care.

This place is a must when visiting New Orleans! The music was awesome and there is no better way to enjoy jazz music than sitting outside on a lovely patio sipping wine. 
 
The wine selection is awesome and the staff was very friendly and eager to help
us choose a bottle. In fact we challenged the waiter to find us the best bottle of wine for under $25, with the prettiest label. He was enthusiastic and gladly accepted the challenge. Our wine was great! 

But it gets better! Bacchanal serves cheese platters as well that look delicious. Sadly we were too full to try. But you get to choose your own cheeses and they plate it for you. 

Overall, great atmosphere, music, service and wine!

I came to Nashville for the weekend and wanted to eat sushi, this place had the best reviews so I came. Everything was delicious and really affordable. The service was excelent and what impressed me the most is how quickly my food came, less than 10 minutes!!

This little coffee shop is easy to miss, as it's not on a main thoroughfare and it's tucked into the first floor of a commercial building. I'm glad I found it on Yelp, though, because the coffee is delicious and it's a decent spot for working.

It's cute and modern inside, but I agree with some other Yelpers in that it's slightly lacking in atmosphere and personality. Not a big deal, but a good point I couldn't really put my finger on. It also didn't help that the female barista that day wasn't especially friendly.

In any case, the coffee is really good. I absolutely looooved my drink - so much that I wanted to get another (it was a pretty small drink). It's on the specialty menu, called Little Sweet Thing or something similar. It was to die for: a small rocks glass with espresso, half & half and vanilla, shaken with ice. It sounds simple but it was soooo good - more like a dessert than a coffee.

For a long time, Outback was my favorite restaurant.  I order the same thing every time I go there, the 9 oz. outback special (MW), with a baked potato (cheese, butter, bacon), and a Caesar salad.  Top it off with a Sam Adams and I always leave feeling WAY overfilled.  

There's nothing special about this specific location, though I have never had to wait long for a seat there, which is a nice change of pace for Outback.  The servers are always friendly, and unlike a lot of places in the area, I can't ever remember being annoyed with waiters taking to long here (my biggest pet peeve is waiting for a course or the bill).

I'm in St. Louis at least once or twice a month for work and this place is now on my "GO HERE EVERY TRIP" list.  It is sooo good! 

Portion sizes: The small bowl is usually more than enough food, but I've also gotten the regular size when I was super hungry.  I also like that you can mix your fish scoops. I like to do part salmon, part spicy tuna, with the SPICY poke sauce. 

Toppings:  Good variety, generous servings and also really fresh. I really love that mango is offered too and it is not an extra cost.  This is also where my only gripe comes, in, though:  I wish they'd bring back the fried garlic! It was one of my favorite toppings but when I went last week, the girl working told me they didn't have it anymore and she wasn't sure if it would be coming back :(  Pokedoke, please bring it back! The fried wontons just aren't the same.

Decent spot for beers and food. The burger is underwhelming, but some of their British fare will satiate you just fine.

This place certainly won't knock your proverbial socks off, though it is a locale to see and be seen.

I would give them more stars but we'd made a reservation for 3 when they opened. They took my dad first, but then took another couple before my boyfriend and I. My dad ended up finishing and having to wait a good 30 minutes before me. We had a reservation when they opened, so they should have taken us all first, and me before my dad and boyfriend, since I took the longest (my ties had to be painted, whereas theirs didn't).  My boyfriend and I have been here before, and it was good, except she cut his toe.

We finally had the opportunity to try Katie's and now I kick myself that I waited this long. The food was fantastic! Its seriously the closest thing to the pizza and pasta we had in Rome last year. 

I very much enjoyed my Ted's Meatball pizza, and my husband devoured his Spaghetti and Meatballs. I think its safe to say that we now have an obsession with the meatballs here. In addition to our delicious food we were able to enjoy it on their outside patio (LOVE) with live music playing in the background. The atmosphere was chill and entertaining and the house wine took the edge off from the work week. 

I seriously cannot wait to go back and try another pizza and maybe some meatballs on the side.

After it was updated several years ago I thought it changed for the better, but it's going down hill again.  Sad because it's a great location, great prices, food is decent & they are quick, BUT it seems like it's getting very dirty again.  We got sick after eating there 2 separate times. I am not taking a third chance @ this diner.

You guys gave me the worst pai gow hands EVER.  However, my cousin started with $5 and lasted over 2 hours.  Thank you for giving us a fun time and taking my money!  It was worth every penny just kicking it with my cousins.

If you've got kids, this casino has a great arcade.  It's been newly remodeled and has great air circulation.  seriously...You can't even smell the 2nd hand smoke.

Had supper about 5:00pm, 7/10/17, and was disappointed with what I had ordered.  Waitress was nice and was clean inside.  I ordered a fried chicken dinner that came with mash potatoes, salad and peas.  I ordered garlic toast and not charged.  Meal was $9.00 and not very tasty.  The chicken was breaded frozen and the peas tasted like frozen peas also.  Mashed potatoes were instant.  I'd value the dinner worth about $5.95 for what was received.  Thousand island dressing was sour and way too much mayo.   Still looking for that fresh cooked food instead of the quick and easy frozen.  Don't think I'll return again.

Our first time here and the place is slammed!  They need help at the front of the house to keep things better organized, but the staff is very friendly and works hard.  My chicken salad croissant and arugala salad was delicious!  Well worth the price....we'll be back!!

This was undoubtably the best meal I have had all year. We came in on a Friday evening around 8 PM without a reservation. There was a community table available so we sat right down. A live band was setting up and we had a front row view.

Our server Philip was extremely friendly and went out of his way throughout the night.

We started with the fried pickles which were phenomenal. Fried pickles are one of my favorite appetizers in the world of appetizers and I have had many a fried pickle in my day. These were delicious! You can tell they were made in house with a deliciously seasoned batter. Go easy on the dipping sauce though...it's spicy!!

I ordered the chicken fried chicken and it was delicious! So good. The mashed potatoes that came with it were a little spicy but still very tasty. The gravy that came on the chicken and potatoes was the best part of the entire meal. The only disappointing part of the meal were the green beans. I could tell they weren't fresh and my husband's meal came with fresh green beans. My only feedback would be to replace the green beans that come with this meal with fresh ones.

My husband had the smoked meatloaf and he loved it. It came with a mushroom gravy and he was in heaven.

The Pecan Skillet cake was highly recommended by our server and it did not disappoint. This was hands down the best dessert I have had in years. It was like a pecan pie with a cake with fresh ice cream in a cast iron skillet. It was amazing. It literally changed my life for the better and no other dessert will ever compare. I will continue to have dreams about that dessert until I have it again.

We will definitely be back next time we are in the area! We stayed for a couple of hours and watched the entire set performed by the band. It was a wonderful Friday night.

Amazing bakery and very reasonably priced!!! We first used them for my fiance's brother's rehearsal dinner. I was in charge of the dessert table so we ordered lemon bars, brownies and two 8inch round cakes with designs on them. Village bakehouse was so easy to work with. Everyone at the party raved about how great the cakes were. 

Fast forward a few months my fiance asked the head baker if they could make a vanilla rose water cake. My family is from Jamaica and we use a lot of rosewater in our desserts. They had never done this before but were willing to try. My fiance took over the rosewater he wanted to be used and left it in their hands. I was so surprised at how delicious it was. I think I must have had close to 10 pieces of cake that weekend. It was sooo delicious and extremely moist. The icing was vanilla buttercream and was to die for. Thank you Village Bakehouse

Don't go here on a Saturday night for drinks with friends unless you want slow service with an attitude. We always try to give this place a shot but it's become known as a clear stay-away. Save your money.

I got bitten by bed bugs all over my body at this hotel. When I went to the front desk to inform the gentlemen who were manning the desk, there were absolutely no apologies or the remotest sign of remorse. They did, however, transfer me to a new room, which thankfully had no bed bugs. I would advise anyone who is not a fan of pest infestation and poor customer service to stay as far away as they can from this hotel. I personally know there is no way I will willingly go back.

Went for the first time. Took my father for lunch. I'm not a big fan of Chinese food. I have to say the food here was good. Service was fast. No complaints. Waitress name Angela if I'm correct was very nice and did a great job. I would return if I'm in the area, but wouldn't take a long drive to go there.

This is authentic as you can get for a French bakery on St. Petersburg beach. A nice find in the sea of resorts. A calm atmosphere, employees speaking French and French music in the background. 
Croissants are perfect, at our table almond, chocolate and bacon and egg. Sweet is the way to go. Back and egg are scrambled. 
Free refills on coffee, very sweet employees. 
Just a great way to start a Sunday am before a or after a walk on the beach.
I visited last week. The food was delicious! I ordered the lemongrass soup and the pad thai. Very tasty and lovely presentation. I definitely would recommend it.

Cozy place, reasonable prices, decent crowd.  Outside area small but okay to stand around in (no tables, at least last time I was there).  Currently working on being redesigned (had a few beers and helped the owner paint some slabs - friendly staff!)

I used to live around the corner from the foodery, and after yesterday I will never go there again. 
If you want an expensive ass 6 pack (very close to what you'd spend if you got the same beer at a bar), old tastycakes, or to spend double what you should because the prices are so high, feel free to go waste your money here. I walked into the foodery and asked the guy behind the counter to use his phone to call a cab (my phone had died and at 11 am on a Sunday, cabs were not really around) because I had three massive bags of groceries and I couldn't carry them all the way home. Well needless to say the guy said well I'm using the phone, I offered to wait until he was done, but he just said there's cabs outside all the time and turned away. I had told him that I had already waited outside for 15 minutes and saw none available, And he just said no can't help you. Horrible customer service, and considering it's a neighborhood spot, I'm shocked at the total lack of class from this store owner, especially considering I've been shopping there for years.
I thought the yogurt was great with tons of toppings to choose from.  You can go healthy or go crazy with all of the choices.  Seating is very limited but service was great. I will be back.

We peeked in and were  really hungry and thought crepes would be great right now. Once seated I should have trusted my instincts and left. Even my 8 year old complained about the dinginess of the place. It needs a complete rehab to capture the once cute rattan chairs now with stained cushions. The floor even with a severely good mopping would never be clean enough. Our server yes flaky no real complaints, it was slow and my daughter noticed her chatting with the other server and then talking to the customers a different  voice. It was kind of funny, she should have her own Yelp page. I felt like we were in the Twilight Zone, talking about our weird server while two girls in the next table chatted so loudly making it impossible not to ease drop.
On to the food..The Iced Tea was painfully sweet, she said it was sweet but even diluted with water was just over bearing. AND $3.50 . The Caesar salad was just okay. The crepe was actually very good. But if I really want crepes again I will go to Beau Monde.
 I had my wallet out before my daughter was finished just to get out of there quicker. We decided to pass up a desert crepe and head over to Ben and Jerry's for a cone. see next review!
I love this place. The hibachi is amazing and the service has always been excellent. It's a little too expensive or else I'd give it 5 stars.

Love love love this place. They have specials for everyday of the week that are just amazing! 
The service is great and you can order ahead to go!!!

We were here on a slow Friday night. We arrived around 8:45 and were seated promptly. It looked like they were slowly getting ready to close, there was only one table that seemed to have finished their meals. Waiter told us the specials, opened our wine and so far we're good! We ordered our appetizers and asked to have an other min to think about main course when he advised we shouldn't think too long since the kitchen is about to close. Understandable. After being served the apps it only took about another 10-15 min for them to bring the main course out, while we were still working on the apps. Also the busboy started lifting up the chairs while we were still eating, and the waiter seemed to call him and asked him to not do that while cstms are in the dining room. We were asked once if everything was ok, which I like because in other places you cannot hold a conversation without being interrupted like 5 times. We felt a little rushed, understandably because we were the only ones left by now and we were holding them there. If we would have been there a tad earlier I'm sure our dining experience might have been much better. Food was good, our mussels app had sand in them, so either they were not washed good, or they had sand on the inside so once they were cooked got out
Fabulous!! Inventive choices, well prepared options. Even some gluten free options.  Locally owned. Can't beat it!

Absolutely LOVEEEE diners and Jewish deli's and this is a jew diner. 

Highly recommend the pastrami sandwiches. They put a lot of twists on them, I got it over Latkes and the latkes were perfectly crispy. This place is decently priced.

I would give it a 5 star except that the decor was still like the old ownerships, except for the Easter themed counter. And that it doesn't include a free salad bar or dessert.

Had lunch there on a Sunday afternoon.  Everything we ordered was excellent.  I had the mahi mahi taco & the fish was perfect.  Two others ordered the Favorito Combo & loved it.  We also ordered a side or salsa & chips & guacamole.  Both very good & fresh.

So I no refill on coffee no service poo , sad , everyone gone a MOTHERS DAY COOKIE , but not me ! No bill , had to get up and pay!! I how its mothers  day but there was enough servers around and bussers that this should not had happened

Really good brisket and the sweet potato waffle fries were great. Husband had the 3 Men in a Boat. The servings seemed a not on the small side but okay as we were eating just a light lunch.  Very crowded little place but clean. We will be back

What a heavenly girly delicious little haven tucked into a quiet street in Broad Ripple!  Everything you read in the other reviews is true -- very expensive and very delicious.  The ingredients taste high end, absolutely no gritty grainy chocolate here.  Everything was smooth, creamy, decadent.  And the service was impeccable.  I just can't bring myself to give it 5 stars when the bill was $40 (not including tip) for two slices of cake, a little brownie, an ice tea, and the smallest little cup of sipping chocolate (lukewarm super rich hot chocolate) you've ever seen.  Still, it was such a fun place to go with my mother and little daughter.  And there's something so wonderful about getting a dessert with edible glitter!

Definitely try the lemon blueberry cake.  It was our favorite item we tried.
Their tofu soup is the best.  They matched Tofu House in California, if not better.  The soup is very tasty and has the right flavoring.  However, their BBQ beef is not so good, a little too sweet.

This is a great place for lunch or dinner! My husband and I came for lunch and arrived just after opening. I'm glad we did because there were a nice string of customers that came in after us. We ordered the red snapper meal from the dinner menu  and it was really good! They also have a lunch menu.  Our server was really nice too! We will definitely be back!

I love coming here. It's kind of a dive but very welcoming. I've had quite a few things on the menu and I have not been disappointed yet. The staff has always been very helpful in recommending things to try. Coffee is very good. Definitely recommend checking it out and it is good for groups up to 6 with no problem.
It was a really good experience. Things are expensive as you can probably guess. Good beer, good entertainment, decent food. Try chickie and Pete's crab fries
Awesome take out, great local place in Bensalem. Food is hot and delicious, it hits the spot!

Ugh. The only thing keeping this place from a 1-star review was the food, which was actually pretty darn tasty. That and a nice outdoor seating area. Everything else about the experience was pretty mediocre. The place has potential, but needs several major improvements. Service was TERRIBLE. The waitress seemed irritated with my questions about the wine list, ignored our basic requests (like salt and pepper, water refils, etc.), and seemed to rush us out without even offering dessert (which i am pretty sure is what they are known for and what we originally came for, but I guess not tonight since she couldn't be bothered). I could bore you with all the nitty gritty details, but I was unimpressed from start to finish. Plus, their live music was pretty abysmal. With so many similar, better options in St. Louis, don't waste your time or money at blondies.

We stumbled in here on our way to the animal shelter and I'm so glad we did, this is now my new favorite place! The bartender Brittany was so helpful and informative, she is really a 10 in my book. She suggested several items on the menu and I'm so glad she did because they were amazing. Wonderful experience, great food and outstanding service, thanks Brittany and Granite City!
Excellent surprise out in the burbs. I had a great eggplant pirogue and place was packed at 2 in the afternoon which seemed like a very good sign.

Full disclosure - I'm not an artist.  I wandered in here looking for a Christmas gift for my buddy's daughter, as she has been displaying considerable talent in that area lately.

Also, I may have been feeling slightly guilty about last year's gift.  Who would have guessed that a drum set wasn't a good gift for a four year old?

In any case, DeSerres appeared to have everything an artist could want, and a few things that they didn't know they wanted, but would probably buy once they set foot in the store.

The staff were extremely helpful and friendly, and went out of their way to guide me towards the less expensive options.  That was a first.

I totally ignored their advice, but I still appreciated the effort.
The smoothies are ok, every time I get one they have some chunks of frozen fruit in it...which is annoying. It's just an ok place, nothing fantastic.

After reading the reviews, I had high expectations of this place. 

First, the location. Maybe it's the cheap rent, or the proximity to NAIT (students likes their ribs...?), but I find the location a bit of a turn off. It's located on a quiet  strip mall, by a comic book store and surrounded by constructions. The sign is maybe a little too humble.

Second, decor. Again, after reading the reviews, I was expecting a cute mix of cowboy/modern decor, but what I saw was poorly planned Ikea/cow skin galore.

Third, the food. The portions are MASSIVE! So, if you like to eat 3 lbs of overcooked, dry, tasteless meat on bones. This is the place to go. I had the ribs and I think they are under-marinated, and they are trying too hard to inject the "Southern" influence in the flavors, they don't mesh well together.

Utterly disappointed, maybe I should have expected less...or none at all.

This is my go to tex mex place in Stl.  My reasons being: it's close, reliable, and always good.  

Overall: Standard tex mex fare, insanely fast service

I get the California burrito- modified to be vegetarian, and they don't make a stink about me being picky/ vegetarian like some places do.  It is delicious and smothered in cheese sauce.  You should get it.

I took my nephews here and they really liked it. It was a little frustrating that I had to buy special socks when I arrived. I felt like they should had been included in the price. There are a good amount of areas for the kids to play in, however, the foam pit doesn't really allow you with enough time.

everything was good. eating on the end of the wharf is great of course, staff is cool. i could give another star if the food was exceptional. the steamed mussels were really good although the broth lacked some oomph. the clam chowder was ok, loaded with a lot of herbs which wasnt my style. king crab legs was probably a bad choice on my part, should have ordered local catch

Lord almighty. The burgers - they know how to do'em. 

Got here on a later side of a Thursday night - there were couples everywhere making out in the cozy booth seats. I wasn't having any of that - I just wanted me some good burger. And I had one so I was happy as a clam. I can't even get my thoughts organized to rave about the burgers. My mouth is salivating right now - to the point of droolage. The burger is cooked to perfection(got med-well because I was second-doubting the grill-man...should have trusted him and gotten med-rare! next time...)and the cheese, mushrooms, tomato, pickles, lettuce... I scarfed it down within minus 3 minutes, I believe. My friends who were not (wo)man enough to get a beautiful burger got a little dessert thingy that they were still working on when I looked up from licking the last bit of burger juice on my plate.

OH and they have raw oysters, too! I have unconditional love for places that has raw oysters. Done. I love you, Village Whiskey.

However, I didn't care for the duck fat fries but it's just me because everyone else liked it very much. But that's because they didn't have the burger, I'm assuming. 

Honorable mention...the hostess that was working last Thursday night(Feb 10th or Feb 3rd - I can't possibly remember) - you greeted me ever so nicely and you took me right to my table so I didn't have any in depth conversation with you but you were the most pleasant hostess I've seen in a very long while..even working in that little vestibule with cold air leaking in from the front door, you had a genuine smile on and very welcoming. Thank you!

We were told the wait would be 30 mins for brunch, so we decided to wait rather than move on to a different restaurant. But then they kept us waiting close to 2 hours without an apology or explanation. So much for southern hospitality.

Once we finally got a table, I was at least looking forward to some good food, but the menu was a bit hit or miss. The coffee tasted like instant coffee. My friend got a crawfish meal, which was good. But my eggs were a bit underwhelming, and the "steak" in the steak and eggs my friend ordered was basically a bland hamburger patty. The place had some good moments, including a friendly waiter, but the bad parts far outweighed the good for us. Seems like the only pull is their bottomless drink offer, but overall it was an underwhelming and disappointing $50 meal after a 2 hour wait.

I have eaten here three times and have found the sushi to be fresh and yummy.  The sushi chefs were friendly and attentive.   The hostess is less so; no "welcome" or "thank you for coming", very abrupt in her interactions on each visit; hence the 3-star rating.  There are plenty of good sushi places in town; that little extra customer service can make or break a restaurant.

I bought a Jeep from this dealership about a month ago and that whole process was fairly easy and pain free. Kenny was my cars salesman. He was patient with my family and I as we were there hours test driving cars, crunching numbers, etc. The paperwork process was painless and easy although I was at the dealership for about 2 1/2 hours doing paperwork. Before leaving the lot make sure you THOROUGHLY check the cleanliness of your car! It may be shiny on the outside and appear clean on the inside but they do not truly scrub down the interior. My car still had pen marks on the interior cloth, easy to remove dirt stains, etc. When I wiped down the interior myself, my disinfectant wipe turned jet black! That's not clean. So have them wipe it down in front of you. Otherwise, a good experience

Whether you will love or hate your experience at VW will depend on how well you plan for the kind of experience that will make YOU happy. Do you like to be in an "it" place? Are you OK with crowds and long waits?  If so, then you'll have a good experience braving VW at a prime time (weekend night, lunchtime). If not, there are plenty of times the bar is almost empty and you can enjoy a relaxing, delicious meal and chat with the bartenders - but you'll need to plan to go at an off-peak time. Some of my best VW experiences have been at 2:30 in the afternoon, stopping in for a late lunch and mid-afternoon drink. 

I've found the bartenders to be professional, knowledgeable, friendly and accommodating in the extreme. They're always happy to recommend a drink - or even craft one specially for me - based on nothing but the most vague suggestions or knowing what I'm having to eat. I am not a whiskey drinker, but even I can tell that the selection is extensive and the bartenders know their stuff. Whether you are a novice looking to explore or a seasoned whiskey drinker looking for a treat, I'm sure you'll find it here. 

The food is very good, although somewhat expensive. My favorite is the pork sammie, which comes with the most incredible fried pickle chips. Although they are only on the menu as an accompaniment for the sandwich, they *will* serve them to you alone if you ask! Which I highly recommend. The first time I ordered the sandwich I was a little disappointed - the meat was overly fatty, and the sauce was overwhelming the bun - but it's improved every time I've eaten it since. The burgers, as the other reviewers attest, are phenomenal. 

You should definitely leave some room to try something from the "pickles" menu. My favorite are the heirloom tomatoes - they have a wonderful texture and are bursting with flavor. The artichoke hearts were also delicious. All of the pickles are served with very good ricotta spread, tapenade, and bread. These are some of the best deals on the menu, if you're looking for a small bite, they're perfect.

You MUST try the Carmelized Cauliflower with tahini...Fabulous! I work across the street from this place, and I go for special treats. The Falafel is very good. I prefer to eat outside because it's quieter. The staff is OK. Very friendly. I had one problem when I pre ordered my lunch to be ready by 11:30 to eat in. I only get 30 min. for lunch. I was there on time, my table was ready but the food had not been started, and the waitress knew nothing about it. 20 minutes later my lunch came but I had to get it to go because my 30 minutes for lunch was almost over.  I have heard the Philly Steak is very good. Can't wait to try it.

I was in town for a week long conference and Carmine's was next door to my hotel. I left Carmine's as my last outing of the week... I was not disappointed!! The food was FANTASTIC and the service was impeccable! I had the toasted ravioli, amazing, the Cesar salad, blew my pants off, and the Italian pepperloin, WOW!!!! I topped off the night with their tiramisu, holy moly it was the best meal I had all week. Words cannot describe the amazing service and the food well... I can die happy now!!! If you are in downtown St. Louis stop by and give Carmine's a try you will be forever grateful you did.

My girlfriend and I stopped into Mudbugs on a cold, rainy Sunday for a quick lunch while we were out exploring the Carmel Arts and Design District.  This place hit the spot in several ways.  I have included a few highlights below to explain what we liked about this restaurant:

First and foremost, as should any soul food restaurant - it warmed us up in all the best ways!  The decor was cozy/engaging, the dining area was clean, the staff was friendly and the food was good and hot.  As a massive food addict, I look for and respect any restaurant that offers all of these comfort points.  

Second, the owner offered us a sizable sample platter (7 entree samples along with a split hush puppy) so that we could make an educated lunch decision.  This was a great touch, and gave us an opportunity to find their strong points while contrasting them to other local Cajun shoppes.  The items that stood out to me were their dirty rice, Crawfish casserole and the Shrimp Etouffee.   These flavors created a very enjoyable 'Pick 3' experience.  My partner went with a BBQ pork Po'Boy, which she was really happy with.  Plus, we topped off our dining experience with an extra order of hush puppies...we couldn't resist.  I would highly recommend any of these dishes. 

Last, the portions were very generous and the prices were reasonable.  For around $20.00, the two of us ate ourselves silly in the shop and had enough leftovers for lunch on Monday.  My girlfriend was so excited about the leftovers that, at one point while we were getting ready for work on Monday morning, she said something along the lines of "...you know what helps make today a little less dreadful?  The Cajun leftovers in the fridge."  True story.

All in all, my girlfriend and I had a good experience at Mudbugs which places them soundly on my 'Top 3 Cajun restaurant' podium alongside Yats and Papa Roux.   We will certainly return, and I hope this review will inspire you to stop in as well!

Do not come here! There is a counter inside Macys in Paseo Nuevo and those girls do better. The staff at this location was fooling around and unprofessional, and the lady that waxed me eyebrows did a horrible job. It was nothing that I had discussed with her.

Party of four, the female bartender had a HORRIBLE ATTITUDE. She complained openly how thin her patience was and complained to the other bartender about how people were getting on her nerves.  We ordered breakfast my order was the wrong meal, so our waiter re input my order. A hour later my party was finished with their meals and my food never came. I left upset and hungry!!!! Absolutely no way to run a business and no effort to fix the situation, highly dissatisfied and disappointed.

I have lost track of how many times I have eaten here.

They were having problems tonight.  AC was not working well, a longer wait than normal, out of foods on the chalkboard...

Tonight I had carry-out.  The food didn't look good when I got home.

The container of salsa I opened was partially frozen.

I grumped.

Then I took the first bite of my dinner.  WOW.

Over and over and over I can't say enough how fantastic the food is at Indy Taco!  Tonight was the single worst meal I've ever had at Indy Taco and it was still an amazing explosion of flavor!

Go!  Just Go!
Had them do state inspection only 1 month after maintenance, and they asked me to replace the brake and tires which cost around $700.... Took forever to finish the paper work

If I could only recommend to a visitor one place to stop, #Mazzaros would be it, hands down. If they could only get one thing . . . a loaf of their Italian bread. 
"If you were stuck on a desert island and could only have thing to eat every day what would it be?" #MazzarosBread. 
This is an experience! If you go, bring friends. Stay and relax on the patio with a sub or gelato. Go inside and recharge with a espresso. Then, unwind in the wine room.
Don't forget to go next door to the home goods store just for kitchens. Try to avoid the crowds at lunch and weekends.

enjoyed the atmosphere.  the cannabis infused drink was a bit toooooo strong.  Other than that, it was a great visit but not a place I would go monthly.  A bit overpriced and over hyped.  They didnt even have any desserts we wanted to try.  That was very disappointing.

I've been putting off getting a "real" haircut forever. This place was recommended by a friend and I loved it. I've had Maria cut my hair twice now and each time have been so impressed. After years of crappy cuts, it was nice to get a great one. They do take their time so don't plan to rush--but it is worth it

Went here with my fellers and boy did we sit and EAT!...Sorry, corny just slipped out....

Anyhoo, I had a tasty omelet, a somewhat dry biscuit made delicious by syrup, and an excellent variation on a potato latke. Only one in our party didn't really enjoy his meal and he got the chicken fried steak, which in my opinion is never delicious, so I blame him for ordering it. 

 The atmosphere is very casual without being unduly lax in the service department and the prices are pretty reasonable, especially if  you can get there for the $4 egg breakfast!  For 3 entrees, an order of pancake (just one), and some fresh squeezed juices it was $35. If I were a Philadelphian, this would certainly be a go to spot for me.

Where to begin? The cheesesteaks were amazing, better than philly IMO. The bread was primo, the steak was cooked perfectly and the provolone was the perfect topping. I always get it with onion. The cool thing is they have multiple types of cheesesteaks and they have different sizes if you're not too hungry. 

I love the beer options, and wine selection. They have multiple drafts and plenty of bottles to choose from. The inside is nice and school oriented. 

My wife had their oval and really enjoyed it. Oval = oval shaped pizzas. Overall everyone at the table enjoyed what they ordered and there was no need for a to go box.!
Favorite spot in Broad Ripple for catching up with friends. The bluegrass group is a blast and we rarely have trouble claiming a dartboard.

THE ABSOLUTE BEST BREAKFAST SPOT ON THE WESTBANK BY FAR!!
