Great house band kept us grooving till very late..............if you are in the mood for old school dancefloor fillers..............this is the place..........I had a immense experience.....................

Ohhhh where to start.  If you are looking to stay in a hotel that represents New Orleans, don't go here.  The entry and the rooms are cold and sterile.  The rooms are navy & white without a speck of color.  I asked the front desk if they had something more inviting and the kid told me "No..the owners planned the rooms that way". Really??? The bellmen were always too busy BSing outside to help.  The strange "techno style" in the hallways was bizarre.  Fire alarm went off on Sunday morning..false alarm...but no sleeping in as everyone was on the stairs before they announced a mistake.
They ask for a cc# when you check in even though my trip was billed through Expedia.  I checked at the desk when we left and there were no charges.  Ten days after we left there is a charge for $1300 on my cc that I know nothing about.  So now I get to dispute that. 
Just yuck.  There are no balconies, no jazz, no warm greeting, no "New Orleans" style, nothing to recommend this place.
If you are traveling with family...avoid this place. If you are looking for any warmth..avoid this place.

Scream-A-Geddon is absolutely a blast! It's in every way better than Howl-o-Scream and Horror nights. It's incredibly affordable, even with the fast passes. There's cozy little bonfires everywhere where you can make s'mores, too! The houses are so creative, and they only let your group in so you get the full experience of being scared! I definitely recommend this haunted experience to anyone.

I always thought that Italian did not exist in PA for the longest time, but Limoncello's is living proof that I was so wrong. I will keep this short because everything on the menu is delicious. I haven't had a bad meal and I try everything. I have been there probably 10 times and would say if you live or are near the area, treat yourself one night and enjoy Limoncello's!

Dining at Marrakesh was a wonderful, authentic experience. The atmosphere was cozy, with colorful tapestries and low couches and tables. As for the food, all the courses were good, but a few were great. The phyllo dough/egg pie was a highlight, as was the lamb with honey and almonds. The mint tea to finish is always a favorite; I can never quite get it to taste the same at home. Since there's no real menu to speak of, service is quick, and the host and waiters were friendly and helpful.

Great transportation company. Easy to work with. Prompt, polite, thorough, competitive pricing. My family has used every year and even when I have called last minute, they politely handle and if I have cancelled and not used, they still are extremely courteous. 
I've never met a bad driver either. Always early to pick up, cars are clean and water provided.

All three of my kids went to Wings daycare and loved it. We loved how active they were all day. And the teachers were great!  It was always fun for them when they could go to planet kid. Or the rock wall. Or swimming.  Or field trips. Great place!

With flavors like Buttermilk Drop, Doberge Cake and Red Velvet, Creole Creamery is amazing. Their Cafe au Lait is my favorite. The line might look long but they move it fast. Tip: don't park in the parking lot across the street that belongs to he drugstore or you will get hassled.

We love this place. On average, we eat there once per week. Highly recommend sitting at the bar and chatting up all the krewe. Our favorites are bacon and crab Rangoon's, sweet fried shrimp, shrimp and avocado egg rolls, kimchi burger and the wings. Basically, everything is amazing. Order a bunch of appetizers and share!

I ordered the blackened chicken flatbread and it was just disgusting! The cheese was congealed and the chicken was totally inedible. It tasted rubbery and gamey like it had been reheated in the microwave. I tried to eat around the chicken but the whole thing was awful. This was my first visit and I will never be back. There's only one chance to make a first impression and Ballyhoo has certainly left a lasting one, in the worst possible way.
The commercials are so annoying. I would never step foot at one of his dealerships. They must over charge so much in order to be giving away vacations and all that junk their always yelling about.

I love Wawa and this one is no exception.  Very conveniently located, near lots of stuff, on a trolley stop, at a major intersection.  Parking is tight and mostly impossible during the day, but this is a walking + transit area, and you can park near here with ease late at night.

I pick up odds and ends here regularly.

The employees at this particular location are also very nice. =)

I love coming to this show! The first time I went to it when it was much smaller at the Enjoy centre. But sometimes less is more  There are so many awesome vendors here, but being a self professed foodie, my favourites were the food vendors!! Oh and Soo many samples!!! I ended up with a bag of dumplings, bottle of infused vodka, 6 bottles of wine, 2 meat pies (we had these for dinner, so yummy!) A bag of dehydrated mushrooms, a bag of cookies...and I almost came home with a bag of kick ass caramels. But as you can see I was over my budget limit  I have to give some shout outs to the awesome Alberta vendors I bought from... Spirit Hills Winery, Black Diamond Distillery, Untamed Feast, South Island Pie Company. You guys rock!!

I loved the "love plate". We were staying at the Aloft and the front desk recommended Trident to us. We weren't disappointed. Great beer selection, friendly staff, enough TV's to watch whatever sports were on. Not too noisy, but it was late on a weeknight. And my friend said his steak was perfectly cooked and delicious.

Mostly clothes. I'm on the fence about this place, because it's basically just a goodwill with higher prices and smaller inventory....that said, it has the higher-end clothing that was donated from Goodwill, so I'm sure it's handy for some. I definitely think that calling it 'vintage' is a stretch. When I think vintage I think older goods, but their version just means used. If you aren't looking for used clothing, I wouldn't bother checking it out.
Excellent hidden comfort food brunch spot. Great for a "first date," or meet up with friends.

SCAMMER ALERT!!! This place participates in FRAUD.  Someone with just my debit card number (not the physical card itself) was able to charge over $250.  Go somewhere else.  This just happened in early January 2016, so please heed this warning and do not shop here.

If you are craving sysco crinkle cut french fries with old bay thrown on them then this place is for you. Service SUCKED this sunday at the S Philly location. Apparently they make all thier money off of suing any restaurant on the east coast that uses the words crab and fries to describe  a menu item.

ROTTEN RALPHS IS TRULY ROTTEN

I have visited Rotten Ralph's several times in the past because I thought they always made margaritas well and I enjoyed their lobster bisque. The most recent experience however, was so dreadful that I'd never return. We came in and were pleasantly greeted. There was no room at the bar so we had to go upstairs. It was uncomfortably quiet upstairs but no biggie. We were greeted soon after we settled and our drink orders were taken. 2 margaritas and 2 waters were ordered w/o ice. The server returns with one water full of ice. We questioned it after he ran downstairs but. I could wait for my water. My friend had to move her car before 10 and we had set a 15 min timer for her to leave. That's how I knew the drinks were taking a long time. On her way out my friend stopped by the bar  to get someone's attention and to ask why it was taking so long since hardly anyone was there. She just decided to leave since she saw our drinks just starting to be made. We got our drinks at 10:03. 

While we waited for our food the server was hovering . I get that we were the only ones upstairs but where was this attention when we ordered our drinks? The food came and I had to ask for clean cutlery and my friend had to ask for ketchup for her fries. Being someone who has worked in the service industry, I feel like there are certain things you shouldn't have to ask for. He asks us, "so do you want hot sauce too?" I thought that was odd because what is the implication? We just want ketchup and clean spoons. He returns with a clean spoon and we have to remind him about the ketchup. I order a second margarita and the server comes back with a martini glass the size of a shot glass. Their glasses were already on the smaller side. I find it funny that he tried to quickly take away my friends margarita which she wasn't even done with so I wouldn't see the difference but I did and took a picture. He apologized and surprisingly quickly came back with the rest of my drink. He proceeds to do more hovering and eventually drops the bill. We payed when we were ready and the he informed us after seeing more than one method of payment that we would have to tell him how much we wanted on the cards. Why in the world would we not tell him that? We hand him the payment and I ask to speak with a manager and this is when things went downhill. 

I had every intention of paying for my meal and tipping my server accordingly. But what I didn't know was that the manager was going to add fuel to very slow burning fire. I honestly just wanted to inform him that despite such positive experiences I've had here, this was the poorest. I brought two of my friends here and as first timers they said they wouldn't return. (They had increased their prices last I had been there. I thought it was slightly unreasonable because I don't think anything about the quality had improved) I try and tell him first about how it took about 20 minutes for our drinks to come and he was immediately on the defense. He tells me that he is personally responsible for making the drinks and he knows for a fact it didn't take 20 minutes. He says "I think you know margaritas aren't the easiest drink to make. It's not a quick pour like a beer; it's a cocktail". Excuse me? I know how long it takes to make a margarita and I know a margarita is a cocktail. Mind you he tells me this after cutting me off and with a pompous attitude. I was quite shocked. So I proceed to tell him my intentions like I previously stated. (Maybe he thought I was trying to get money off the bill or something) I didn't want anything from him, I just wanted to inform him of the unusual experience so they could do something about. He wasn't getting it as he continued to be on the defense and take the stance that they were right so I was automatically wrong. I tell him sir I've already paid and he says he knows, he has my money already. It seemed to be a lost cause so I tell him that he doesn't seem to care about my opinion so he got dismissed. He threatens to call the police on me and I welcomed it. I haven't done anything wrong and we were about to leave anyway. Of course more words were exchanged and even my friends tried to chime in but you get the gist. Long story short, I left no tip, I will never return, I will constantly demote them to anyone who will hear me, the "manager" was rude, arrogant, impatient, irrational, and a poor representation of Rotten Ralph's and the reason why I will NEVER RETURN.ps. I'm sorry to the server who didn't get a tip at all but I was mad as hell for the low class treatment...and you were a bit weird.

This was without a question, one of the best sales and delivery experience I have ever received in my life. Below I will explain why I say that and how it came to be.  What I want everyone who reads this review to understand is a few simple strategies. 1) Know what you want before you go to a RV dealership; 2) Do your due diligence on choosing Make, Model, Options and the Fair Price you will pay; 3) Order the coach so you have time to sell your own if possible; 4) Don't be in a rush; 5) Have all your communication in writing and if something is missing, take responsibility that you did not prepare prior to your commitment.  
All the above is what I did.  Why, because I read every blog I can find on the subject, watch every YouTube™ video I could and listen to folks who have been RVing for decades. Every single part of my requests to Tampa RV were fulfilled prior to me even setting foot in the dealership. My sales consultant, Stephen Weaver, communication with me consistently throughout the ordering process (three months).  Everyone from the General Manager to the PDI manager called me prior to delivery.  Even the dealer sent me an email after I took delivery.  
Folks, every aspect of my sale to delivery exceeded my expectation.  Thanks to the entire staff of Tampa RV for working so closely with me.  My hopes are everyone does their research and preparation prior to even thinking about the purchase of an RV from any dealership.  Bravo to all involved.  See my addition comments below for more information.
This not my first purchase of an RV/Coach.  Prior to every transaction, I do a level of due diligence that most people can't or are simply not willing to do. In the past I have been asked to speak on the subject at national conventions, pod casts, YouTube™ reviews including my own and my personal blog on the RV Industry.  My goal is to be a advocate for clients to have a seamless and transparent transition with most RV dealers in the United States. I am called the "RV Advocate".
On to my review. When I finally choose my brand (AirStream), model (Interstate Grand Tour) and option package (Tommy Bahama) it was time to choose my dealership.  Since I had purchased an AirStream Trailer prior, I had gone through this process before.  It seems my prior dealer did not communicate some critical facts to me on my potential new purchase, so we parted ways as friends. My money, so my choice. I knew every single Airstream dealer is a five-state radius.  I had visited most of them. I was referred to Tampa RV (A member of the RVone Group) by a trusted Airstream friend. Tampa RV's reviews were not stellar to say the least, but I studied them very closely.  It became clear to me the issues, not only with Tampa RV, all RV dealerships I dealt with was "professional communication" on both the client and the dealers side.  I created a process in writing to leave "no stone un-turn" and the result was OUTSTANDING.

My family has been going to Skippers for years in the valley and have always loved the food. When they started shutting down a lot of the locations, the only one that was left was the one on Fairview and it was pretty run down for a while. The new owners that took over cleaned the place up and added a lot of fun décor. Same great food but updated and clean!

Standard food, poor service. I went with my family (5 top) and we were one of 3 tables there for dinner (it was Memorial Day). Our server was not only slow, but her was unfriendly. I've been a server so I understand a slow kitchen may not be a server's fault, but he was very rude. He would drop off a drink or bread and not say a word. Multiple times we tried to ask him for something but he ran away from our table so quickly that he didn't hear (or acknowledge) us. The food is good--nothing so good that I would say the wait and poor service were worth it. The waiter didn't even say goodby to us. A bit disappointed.

We rented out the patio balcony through the website www.bourbonsbest.com. . We were celebrating a 30th Bday and it could not have been more perfect. Open bar for all our friends/family and very good food. They even did a cake for us and it was soooo good! The area was very private, they had decor and everything. We even had a private restroom. If your looking for something on Bourbon that's reasonable go with them!! Thanks again Sharon and Bourbon Cowboy and for making my brothers 30th a success!!

The restaurant is okay. Came here with a group on the school's wallet, so I can't comment on how much the food was. It seemed fairly reasonable. Nothing was all that memorable, service and portions were decent. It's a bit removed from the group of restaurants by Rittenhouse, so it's a bit unfortunate that it has a mediocre location. 

I do want to note that the banana bread pudding for dessert was very delicious! Would order that again if I ever come back!

I created a Yelp account just to give this place a review. Simply put, 3J's has everything you could look for in a deli. There is great food to be had at affordable prices (recommend the grilled cheeses, breakfast sandwiches, veggie cheesesteak and fruit smoothies). 

Customer service at 3J's is also among the best I have ever experienced. Everyone is genuinely courteous, nice, and attentive to the customer's tastes and preferences. Overall, the best deli I have been to in Philly.

We love Pizza Mizza. It is a wonderful place for the whole family. Also at least once a month I meet my girlfriends there for a glass of wine while our boys are playing basketball at the YMCA. Fast service & the staff is always friendly.

I'll echo the numerous reviews here that seem to agree that the food is pretty good if you can stomach the terrible service you're likely to get.

I think the NY style of taking a pie that's been sitting outside all day and reheating it upon order is disgusting, so I'll never order by the slice. However, their fresh pizza is great, and I love the chicken parmesan sandwich. The fries are the delicious crinkle-cut kind, and best of all, they have Diet Mountain Dew on the fountain (with flavor shots - get a cherry shot in it!).

But several times we've gone there, they've been busy and depressingly understaffed. Amber was our waitress two times recently, and should definitely consider employment in a different industry. 5 minutes to get acknowledged at the "hostess stand" (which employs no hostess - and servers dread going near, apparently), another 10 minutes once seated to get waited on.

After putting in our drink order, it took, no exaggeration, over 10 more minutes for her to get our drinks. We fortunately put in the food order when we ordered drinks (why not? We had enough time to look at the entire menu), and 45 minutes later when the food arrived, I was told another server took my sandwich, and mine would come later. My three tablemates finished their food before I got mine, with no apology whatsoever. Again, the food was delicious, but then it took another 15 minutes to get cashed out. A 75 minute "experience" for what amounted to be pizza and sandwiches. I won't blame the kitchen because they were busy, but the service is reliably terrible.

If you've got time to spare, or it doesn't look busy, I do recommend Precinct Pizza's delicious food. But always be ready to sit there way longer than you wanted to, with little to no attention paid to you by the staff. Four stars for the food, one star for the service, but I'll generously round up to 3 stars overall.
Very good and quick service. Highly recommend. Food was very good and fresh. Poepl behind the counter were helpful as well.
Clean, friendly, and delicious! Accommodating of our sons severe nut allergy. Highly recommend!

This is a pub.  Don't expect anything but good pub food on paper plates, cold beer, friendly staff and a great time.   It you want something fancy this is not for you.  If you want some fun come on in.

It's your local neighborhood dive bar. There really is no other way to describe it. Of course, you've got the nurses singing karaoke who just walked down the street from Centennial. There's the Vandy students who strayed a bit from campus. Lastly, the out-of-towners who walked down the sidewalk from the Exit/In who look lost.

The Corner Bar isn't the classiest joint in town but it gets the job done. Beer and liquor when you need it and that's about it. If you're in the area and something close by is more convenient, then swing by The Corner Bar and see some REAL characters.
Fresh thoughtful tacos.  The BBQ is a MUST try, slow cooked sweet tasty.  The slaw crunchy fresh.  Service quick and tables are proportioned correctly.

Everything about this place is horrible! From the workers to the food to the treatment of their customers. If u thrive for great service delicious food and courteous workers this is not the place to go!!!
Excellent food, even better service. Told Kevin (the owner's son) that he should keep him:). Best sorrel EVER!!!  Great music!!!
Good food reasonably priced. On our way home from Lompoc (watched SpaceX launch) to Los Angeles and found this gem thru the Yelp app.

I have only tried the drunken noodles and the pad thai but that alone makes me love this place--especially the pad thai. And the staff is very friendly, and patient as you ask questions, etc. They also make great suggestions. I am excited to try more.....I plan to be back often!

BFF Cafe is AMAZING!!! 

I would love to show you pictures of all of the goodies we ordered, but I can't because we all just dug in and I didn't think again about pictures until I was down to a couple of bites.  LOL  Just another excuse to return soon and often.  ;)

I love their menu and how it tells everything that is gluten free, diabetic-friendly, paleo, and a couple of other designations. Their item listings also show the amount of carbs, calories, etc. Most of their menu is gluten free and/or easily changed up to be gluten free.  There are SO many items I need to try ASAP.

I had been wanting to go there for quite awhile, but it took family coming in from out of town (one of which is watching his carbs) to finally get there. I'm kicking myself that it took so long to get there. 

I think this just may be my new favorite restaurant in the area.  It's so tasty while being really healthy. They say that their cafe is your body's best friend.  It definitely fits.

Today I ordered the Bison Burger with a side of Cauliflower Sticks (you can choose between several sides). My bison burger included blue cheese crumbles, spinach, balsamic reduction, heirloom tomato, and mushrooms! I chose the Cauliflower bun (one of at least 3 breads and two of them are gluten free). The whole thing was amazing! It was a bit messy because of the balsamic reduction, but nothing several napkins couldn't handle.   ;)

We also ordered the Cauliflower Pizza with chicken, red sauce, red pepper, red onion, goat cheese, mozzarella, and basil. We split this and everyone who tried it really enjoyed it.

Others ordered the Classic Cheeseburger and fries, and the following Zoodle plates: The BFF, The Clucker, and The Salmon Zoodles. They all really loved their food. All of the Zoodle items looked really tasty, but The Salmon looked the best to me out of the three. I also bought some of their Peanut Butter Balls (with chocolate chips) to share and took a loaf of Cauliflower Bread home with me.

They also have a tasty selection of drinks. Their soda machine was out of order today, but we all enjoyed a variety of specialty drinks (from bottles and cans). I had a Pomegranate Bai drink. 

The staff was SO friendly and on top of their responsibilities. There is even seating outside, but we chose inside today. One of our cousins also thanked me for finding and recommending such a great place.

I NEED to go back soon, because I definitely want to try their Salmon Tacos and several other dishes. This definitely feels like it will officially be named my favorite restaurant in the area really soon. I'm almost ready to declare it, but think after one more visit it will likely be official. I absolutely love how easy it is to eat gluten free there safely and have most of the menu available to me. It definitely doesn't hurt that you get some amazing tasting food there that is actually really healthy! You definitely do not find that every day!

I don't drink Buds! But this tour is a must if you are in STL. 
 Free tour with 2 free drafts! You can't skip it. There is a lot of history to this brewery,afterall, it's the nation's top notch brewery! or so we have been told.
They also have a VIP tour which cost money but it's almost the same. I imagine! Anyhow, it's a cool tour, I don't want to ruin it for you by describing what goes behind closed doors! Go check it out for yourself! And make sure to drink up!
Happy Touring!

This is the best takeout Thai I've ever had - simply because it tastes less like takeout and more like a dish I would have had at a nice sit-down place. I went safe on my first visit here and ordered Pad Thai. It blows away all of my perceptions of Pad Thai as often too greasy or just bland. This Pad Thai tasted so fresh. The egg was obviously cooked to order and it had a spice that made the peanut flavor a compliment rather than be overpowering. The staff is incredibly kind and they obviously do desserts and other baked goods very well. They sell homemade shrimp crackers, sugar rice treats and boba teas so needless to say- I'll be back for those.

After my initial review, the company contacted me. They apologized, but more importantly, I felt like my feedback was heard and considered, not just blown off. They are a young company going through growing pains, and they defiantly have some issues to work on but I was really impressed that they read the review and did everything they could to make it right, including reimbursing me the cost of the repair when I went to their competitor. At that point, they didn't have to do anything. It really speaks volumes towards their customer service that they would foot the bill for the repair because they made several mistakes with the situation. I can't in good conscious leave a GOOD review because the ordeal still sucked, but in the after-math of it, I got more then expected and I am happy with the outcome. Thank you Puls for stepping up, apologizing,  fixing what you could, and considering my feedback.

I highly recommend Jayna and The Dress as a perfectly lovely bridal shopping experience in Santa Barbara.

I was convinced I was going to wear vintage at my wedding. On my first outing to look at wedding dresses (a week after we got engaged) I made an appointment at The Dress on a whim to appease my mom and sister in law. Turns out it was the best decision.

As many other reviewers have mentioned, Jayna is a great human and her shop is amazing. The dress that ended up being my wedding dress was one of many different styles I tried on. I didn't know what I wanted but I knew I wanted straps. I even tried the skirt and top trend which I adore but didn't like on me. I'm one that didn't get that immediate "I'm a bride" gushy moment when I put on the dress. The whole day of dress shopping was fairly overwhelming. 

I was lucky enough to purchase a sample dress on sale. And we decided to shorten it to tea length for that vintage feel. We bought the dress in January and took it home thinking that the wedding wouldn't be until June 2017 so it was too early to alter. In February we decided "why wait" and changed the date to June 2016, to the 4 year anniversary of our blind date instead of the 5th. So my mom and I lugged the dress back to Jayna for the alterations and she was able to fit us in seamlessly for at least 2 fittings (its all a blur already) to get the length and poof just right. She was so patient during those evening fittings with my mom and I- there's a lot of intricacies to being a bride that constantly had me asking questions. The dress was done by mid-May and I finally felt bridal. There's a fitting room pic of my smiling ear to ear in my finished dress that says it all.

Thank you Jayna!

Boarding conditions are not great - tons of little yipey dogs crammed into one room in crates; not good for a larger, more relaxed dog. I left my dog with them for four days and he came come COVERED in fleas. Gross, and to make it worse, they didn't even notice he was going insane scratching.

Would have been better but overcrowded was not how I wanted to start the night.  Saying that we grabbed a seat at the bar, had a glass of wine each and shared a starter (crostini with goat cheese and a homemade pesto).  Very nice.  A good way to start the evening but nothing special.  

Special was my companion for the evening.  Sugar was on my arm yet again for another shot at best date ever.....read the other review from this night to see if we achieved it

Once upon a Child may have moved their location, updated the store to have more room for this expansion but it's still one of the worst stores from this company I have visited. I've been shopping at "OUAC" for over 11 yrs and have visited stores all over CA and NV my favorite was one in Fresno CA off of Shaw Ave. This store was beyond a recycled clothes store once you walked in you were treated like you were shopping in a high end baby boutique. They helped in any way, looked through clothes with you to find great matching outfits, looked through back stock to help find certain clothing and treated the kids the like it was their own grand kids or children. I expected all "OUAC" to be that friendly, clean organized and helpful but I was shocked when I first moved to Reno and went to the old store location. Tried it again at the new store location. My son was treated like he was an uncontrollable brat, he's a 3 year old just checking things out. They took a bike out of his hands he was trying out and I planned on buying, every time he was near the other kids in the store they would move to play in a different area they would snap that he got into new items and take it out of his hands. It wasn't him that opened the items either it was already like that or the other kids in the store did it? I have no idea but he asks before he opens anything in my home or at a store, he's not perfect but he does know not to open sealed items. The clothes in store had stains, rips and wore out elastic. For a company policy that states they don't buy items with any mentioned above that rule was not applied to this store, I was upset to get home to see questionable items and had to throw away 3-4 things because they were not fixable. The stores too crowded with stuff not even gently used things. The staff was rude in a child's thrift store, I expect better customer service for spending over $150  on clothes and a $30 bike. They need more training on pricing and what clothes they buy because that mark is way off. My last time shopping here I'm better off buying $2.50 shorts at Walmart it's brand new, my child isn't traumatized  about going into "child friendly" places and I really dislike Walmart but it's a better route then these questionable items!

The owners know how to make locals feel warm and welcomed from their previous establishments. The food is amazing, prices are just right even cheap in many cases. Huge selection of beers and the menu is never ending.

I was going to give them a better review but 2 of the things I was most looking forward to (the boudin balls and the grits) were 86'd. For those of you who never worked in the business that means they ran out.

Needless to say i was disappointed, but the BBQ Pork Tacos were the highlight of hte night. I got the Pork Sandwich which was average at best. The Mac-n-Cheese tastes like a bad mixture from a box.

Decided to patronize this restaurant. Chose to sit at the bar because it was quicker to sit down. Bad idea. The bartender didn't properly greet us. Took awhile to ask if we wanted drinks.asked for water with lemon-got no lemon  (not big deal) figured I would ask if we can order a appetizer at the same time. Felt like he looked at us with an annoyed look. It took so long for lettuce with chicken mixture I had to get up and look for manager. The manager graciously brought the appetizer and gave it to us for free. I had to tell him that we never even got to put in our dinner order. He took our order but it still took very long to get the meal- An hour after we sat down. When we did question the bartender about the appetizer. My boyfriend was very nice to ask when we could expect it and he gave us an attitude." My man I just put it in it still cooking "lettuce and diced chicken...smh... meanwhile the two people that sat down before us were only waiting for one salad. It took 40 minutes for their salad that came out wrong. I will say the manager was nice and professional. That bartender treated us like we were an annoyance I guess because we weren't going to sit there and get drunk?! Not sure but his customer service sucked
Pork Belly Tacos, Lemongrass Chicken Vermicelli, Spicy Beef Pho and a Bloody Sriracha. Do it. Thank me later.

I've been going to this Chilli's for 7-8 years now. The service can be spotty at times but has on the whole been far above average. The food is pretty great top to bottom of the menu. They keep the place pretty busy so there is a wait most of the times I've been here. Their bartenders in the bar area are absolutely top notch. I would absolutely recommend their happy hour.

I was skeptical when we first went in.  Lately, the sushi joints in town  have been less than... desirable and frankly a waste of money.

My husband and myself were VERY pleasantly surprised by Sushi Rose!  Overall, the sushi was fresh, and they were freakishly busy on a Monday evening.  The service was attentive, even at the table (the bar was full).  Their salmon was nice and buttery, the muscles were fresh tasting and not stale like they'd been sitting under a heat lamp, and my husband said that the Yakiton was excellent (I'll take his word as I'm lactose intolerant).

I only  have two complaints: 
1) The Unagi was more than a bit on the lean side, but I'll try it again next time we go to make sure it wasn't just a fluke.  It's normally a very naturally fatty fish, so I'm hoping next time will be better.
2) There's a lot of cream cheese on the menu.  I don't mind it so much as I prefer hand rolls and nigiri, however, for people who can't ingest any dairy it really limits the available food.  Yes, you can request that they not put the cream cheese in, but, I'm a firm believer that you eat the roll the way the Chef intended it.  It's there for a reason.
Rosendahl is the absolute best shoe repair store in the Boise area.  Their work is consistently excellent and their prices are fair.  I have used them for years and will continue to do so.

Stayed one night here in Dec '10 after getting "snowed in" in Nashville..yep, snowed in! This is a fun place to stay...kinda Vegas style accommodations. As someone who gets to Vegas a few times a year, I have to say I enjoyed staying downtown at The Hermitage...and it will be my choice again next time we head out to Nashville.
alex is the best! Very clean and polite. Definitely the place to enjoy complimentary wine with any service :)

Best escape room in Tucson!
After we finished the Zombie room, we immediately reserved the Bank room. The difficulty was just right and it did not require too much math to solve. We had so much fun there and we will definitely come back !

We came here for breakfast and had to wait a weirdly long time to get waited on, and then our food took forever to come, even though we were there early and the place wasn't very busy. And while this isn't relevant to my rating, it is important to note that this is a very family-friendly place. There were kids all over the place, and they were really loud. The restaurant is not large enough for how many families go there, so if you want a chill breakfast, I don't recommend! But if you're bringing kids to breakfast, it's perfect for that!

I was invited by my friend Chris Cohen to try this place, which doesn't officially open to the public until today and doesn't have any sort of grand opening event for a few weeks. Despite few wrinkles they are quickly ironing out, I could see this developing into a locale where foothills residents can assemble for happy hour, sporting events, dinner, socialize, drink, etc.

The atmosphere they are attempting to create is certainly unique to the Tucson area. The attire the employees sport is derived from the late 1800's / early 1900's type of feel (forgive me if I misfired with that analogy, but I that's what comes to mind). Button-up shirts with suspenders and bow ties for the male bartender. Females wear respectable outfits that resemble that era, but I have no idea how to articulate their style. Either way, it assists the unique feel that will definitely attract people to return here. 

Chris advised that I try a shot of this liquor, the name of which I cannot quite recall, but it tasted like mouthwash and when I swallowed it I could feel it journeying down my esophagus. It's certainly an acquired taste and I was told that most people either love it or hate it; very few fall in between. I supposed I am one of those few. Not sure I would order it again, but it certainly did the trick. 

I also consumed an order of Duck Fries which were absolutely fantastic and made the trip to the Foothills worthwhile. I admit, I had a drink over at Fleming's before coming to this event, and being a bit of a lightweight, I was already buzzed when I arrived at Nox. Then I had the 200 proof alcohol, so I my recollection of this may not be 100% correct, but I swear on those fries there was Parmesan cheese. The duck was cooked perfectly. It was a not-so-surprising combination that exceeded expectations. 

I also had some pork sliders and, to be honest, they were a little dry. The meat was a little overcooked. When I was able to locate a piece of pork that wasn't dry, it actually tasted perfect. So, it was obvious they are still ironing out some kinks with the food, which is fine for a young restaurant.

Would I suggest this place to friends? Absolutely. Aside from the small issue with the pork sliders, everything about Nox surpassed what I foresaw going in. The service was professional and entertaining, yet slightly dignified. The environment was inordinately appealing (I dug the type of music they played; I don't expect to find eclectic electronic and / or downtempo  music in a region like the foothills, but that's what I heard as the night progressed. There are also so many flat-screens in that place I couldn't even count. It's a nifty indoor / outdoor restaurant where dwellers of the foothills can watch Arizona basketball, NFL Football and various other events. 

Oh, and there are the duck fries. Did I mention those? Oh I did? Ok, well I mentioned them again. They were ridiculous (in a positive way).

After letting this review sit in my drafts for about a year, I've had more sleep and am able to more-fairly assess the Provincial.  I have stayed twice; once with a friend for a conference, and the next time with my husband for a concert.  My first visit was a pretty good stay which is why I went back the second time.  Our room during our first visit was facing the courtyard.  It was small and basic, a little noisy at times with the pool just outside our door, but clean and charming.  The continental breakfast was nothing to write home about, but we planned on eating elsewhere anyway.  We especially enjoyed the location in the Quarter and the stories about its haunted history.

Unfortunately, the next time was not nearly as pleasant, so as I lie awake with the feeling of dystopia that can only arise from sleep deprivation, I made a list of pros and cons.

Pros: 
-Proximity to French Quarter attractions & Frenchman Street; walking distance to Central Business District
-One-night reservations available
-Lovely courtyard
-Friendly valet
-Comfortable bed with pretty antique-style canopy
-Mostly clean bathroom 
-Tasteful decor
-Haunted?

Cons:
-NOISY at every hour 
    3:00-7:00 pm: check-ins, tourists & carriage rides on street
    7:00-11:00 pm: (not sure--gone to concert)
    11:00pm-12:00am: drunks screaming and yelling on the street 
    12:00-2:45am: (not sure--left again)
    2:45-??am: occasional random noisy drunks on street
    7:00am: garbage truck directly below window, idling, dumping, workers hollering, back-up beeping
    7:00 am- checkout: guests checking in and out, valet & cabbies hollering to guests and each other "we got a whole load of people from New York here!" and other random exchanges; children screaming & crying, breakfast guests in lobby below, horns honking, another trash truck at 10:00 with all of its associated noises
    10:00: we gave up attempt at resting in order to check out on time and make 8 hour driving trip home (thank goodness for caffeine!)
-Top bedspread had not been laundered- chocolate(?), I hope(??) smear near top edge
-Online price doesn't reflect/estimate the much higher actual price of stay
-Mold/mildew growing on bathroom ceiling
-Low water pressure in sink
-Lots of minor maintenance issues (shutter blinds, fan blade, a/c grate coming off wall, shower curtain partially unhung, headboard scratched up & needed wiped down)
-Haunted?

I am still undecided if I would stay here again, based on my experiences.  The location is perfect, the prices are lower than other hotels in the Quarter, and I much prefer supporting locally owned historic businesses, but I also like sleep from time to time, particularly in a clean bed. . .

Today we showed up at 10 am for three spa appointments and were told that our spots were taken because there was a problem with the computer.  It is NOT the computer that is at fault, it is the staff of women at the front desk who have no idea how to make appointments and run a book.
When I called two weeks ago, the woman who answered was flustered when I asked for an appointment and had to leave the phone to ask someone else about making it.
She called back and CONFIRMED THREE APPOINTMENTS.
If their computer was down, how come they were able to fill the time, or were we bounced in favor of their guests.
This has nothing to do with services which were good.
We will not return.
New trailer exceeds my expectations. It is well  built and fits like a glove. The staff are great. I highly recommend them.

Great food and service. When I went for my first time, the owner personally approached me and my friends to greet and seat us which I thought was very kind and welcoming. Definitely enjoyed the Shepards Pie a lot and nothing could ever beat the Chesapeake Fries they offer! Servers are really nice and really good at what they do. Definitely would come back and recommend anyone to visit for a nice pleasent meal.

I helped host a baby shower at Noble Crust last week, Bradley the coordinator was incredible!!! He was really easy to work with and was there hours ahead of time to help make sure everything was going smoothly and helped us set up. 

The event was perfect, the food was amazing, the service was spot on.(Crystal was a standout!)  We did a brunch shower- the deviled eggs, fruit salad, gnocchi, fried chicken and waffles, pizzas were all perfect. 

The mother to be was so happy and so were all the guests. I highly recommend this venue for an event!! (And a meal!)
The blandest of the fake Mexican chain restaurants. Even the queso was bland. Man I miss Arizona & real Mexican food.

Wow, I can't believe how much I miss this place.   I spent many an undergraduate day on the patio sipping cold beers and enjoying cheese dip (which is the best ever).   The location is amazing, and since I used to live at 20th and Grand I did not have far to go to enjoy the grub when coming back from campus. 
   One other thing that my buddy and I figured out, we always went right before they were closing and they always piled free food on us.   Every time we always walked away with our order plus a free bag of chips and bean dip or cheese dip or anything else they were just going to toss at the end of the day.   Thanks SATCO for all the good times and great food.

3.5? 

I feel bad for giving a free festival a low rating but I'm thinking there's room for growth here. I love food. The Greeks love food. Unfortunately, there was nothing else but "food going on" while we visited the festival which left our visit on the short side.

Take that back- there were church tours and a gift shop. It'd be cool to see some hands on elements that keep folks around longer. Maybe I should have tipped back on one of the affordable $20 bottles of wine? ;)

As for the food- I thought the pastry line was really neat (6-10 different Greek desserts that you could hand select for a take home option). The Greek salad dressing appeared to be quite popular. (The salad was delicious)

The good: The rolls were beautifully plated.
The not-so-good: We arrived just before 9 pm, about 1/2 hour in advance of closing. The place was fairly full. We informed the hostess that we were celebrating a birthday. After seating at the bar, we were told that last call for ordering was in ten minutes. No problem, we ordered a number of selections to try, both from the board and from the server's recommendations, along with some premium sake and beer. There was no eye contact from the chef. Suddenly there was the mop and its related chemical smell as we tried to eat the rolls they'd just brought us. It's fine to take down the fish case if the restaurant is closing, but spraying the glass as customers are eating on just the other side of that glass? The point is to enjoy the fused flavors in the rolls, not the chemical being sprayed. There was no birthday acknowledgment of any kind, not even a small piece of sushi to try from the chef. In the end, we were gulping down our meal and chugging our drinks just to get away from the chemical smell. 
You folks seated us and served us. If you wanted to close, then tell us before seating us. You knew it was a birthday--couldn't you have suggested we go elsewhere if you'd soon be mopping and spraying? 
My dining companion had never been to Sakana and I wanted to show off the charm of the small place. Instead we felt rushed and in the way--and worst of all, could not fully enjoy the flavors of the pricey meal.
I was sorry I'd chosen to go there.

As I said service sucked ordered my food got to drive thru the girl asked what did I order? That's never a good sign. Then I had to wait for my large sweet ice tea isn't that made first? 6 people in the drive thru not sure why I had to wait for my order m. I see one of the girls go up front I'm guessing to get the tea. Finally got my tea I'm on my way take a sip and it's regular ice tea. OMG! how hard is it to get a simple order right?

Took an afternoon tour on September 12th.  They take your picture as you get on, so you can purchase a photo, but we never saw where you get them as we spent most of the time on the open upstairs rear deck or ( bar while it was storming) watching the shorelines and sights as we passed by.  It was relaxing but nothing much special about it, as mostly just rusted hulks lining most of the Mississipi shore line or trees and vegetation.  Just the bucket list to ride on a paddlewheeler.

Excellent food, and excellent service. The drinks are awesome too. I got the Parmesan cauliflower, filet mignon steak bites, and the burger with Parmesan fries. The Barney shrubble drink is delicious, I had two . The atmosphere is very nice, good for a date night or girls night out ( what I did ) and Trevor is the best server! I would go back for sure.

Let start off and say we were seated at 5:50 pm and by 7:00 pm we still haven't had our orders brought out. Our orders were very simple my wife wanted a panini I ordered a chicken salad club and my son a grilled Cheese. The waitress was very rude when we decided to leave I payed for our drinks and we left. If it was possible to give no stars I would have
Best Bulgogi in Nashville.  Period.  Staff was very welcoming and the food was seriously amazing.

Best thai food ever!!!  Loved the green curry, and my husband had the red curry.  It was delicious. The service was great. Our waiter was very friendly, professional and informative and did a phenomenal job describing the dishes we had questions about.  If I could give this restaurant ten stars I would!!!

I meet my husband here several times a month after taking the train.  Easy to walk to from Market East and so warm and comfy!  Usually get a window booth and some special drink the waiter suggests.  I love the salmon with the thin potatoes and mushroom topping.  He always eats the meatloaf and mashed potatoes and peas...something I would never make at home!!  The service is fast and friendly.  The market salad is incredible...you pick whatever you want and it is fresh and chopped and hard to finish!  So yes, it is homey and comfort food....in a relaxed fun atmosphere!
Great location and value for the price.  The room was large and the entire property was well maintained.  Free breakfast and coffee.

Everything about Jong Ka Jib Soft Tofu rulez. Seriously.

Getting a bowl of pipping hot soft tofu, chalk full of at least 5 different types of mushrooms, and colored a bright, crimson red (...you know for 5 stars) is a real mouth opener, eye opener, smile inducer. 

You'll be so happy after eating here that you'll probably want to move to Korea...so much so that it wouldn't matter which one.

The food is not anything special.  What sets this place apart is its prime spot right there on the beach right next to the round about & the pier.  Go there when it's not too hot out (perhaps after sunset) and sit outside.  It's pretty relaxing yet in the center of the action too.
Delicious pizza and great delivery. They even brought their driver in a few minutes early on very short notice for me so pizzas could be delivered for my daughter's birthday party in time.

The plate was hotter than my steak had to pay a dollar $1.87 for ice for crown on the rocks my wife had to pay $2.80 for ice to have them make a martini Ketel One. I wanted Worcestershire sauce and they gave me barbecue sauce which does not go with steak.

Get the cheeseburger and smoked fish spread for your appetizer, then go back again and get the smoked mullet platter!   Everything here is wonderful!!!  Such a cool place and very kid friendly! Love it!  Oh if you are wondering why I suggested a cheeseburger at a fish place?... Just get one you'll see - soooooo yummy!

Ate my first donut from federal donuts loved it! Got the maple brown sugar one and an iced coffee..everything was awesome. The chicken smelled so good sad I couldn't try it, was too full from the donut ..but I'm not complaining:-)
Great location for the east falls neighborhood. They always seem to run out of vegetables by dinner time. I always recommend wawa. This place is the reason to live up north.
Would be nice if maybe the same person was  not writing all of the terrible reviews of this restaurant. It all sounds the same and then praising another as much.

Everything about this was just alright. The burger was meh. Not flavorful. Mac and cheese was fine (in a mediocre fine kinda way, not a good fine kinda way). Green beans were just okay. I probably won't try this again.

If you are coming from a big city or burb with lots of nail salon options then yes, this place is no big deal. But it's damn good for South Tampa and for being 5 min from my house. I am referring to pedi only, that's all I ever get here.

I came a long way to get here. 

Maybe ten whole minutes, but to people in Nashville that's a lot of walking. Being a New Yorker, I saw the town was not a walking city. The place is hidden on the edge of the Gulch, but that doesn't even explain half my adventure. There was a train stuck along the way, and blocking our path. After two minutes of waiting, we decided we had seen enough action films, hopped on the train and made it to the other side. Eat your heart out James Bond. 

Was it worth it? You better believe it. 

Upon entrance there was a band playing some tunes. Definitely something I had not seen in a brewery before. Kudos for that. The staff was super chill and friendly. Got us on a tour right away. Surprising because we heard how so many places sell out by the middle of the day. 

The beers were tasty and the tour was solid. Stayed around to school some people in Jenga, but ended up getting abused. I was trying too hard to make the really difficult moves. I need to stop trying to show off, never works. 

Split some food to refuel a bit, after lots and lots of drinking. Hit the spot. Much needed. 

Thanks Tennessee Brew Works, hopefully people find this gem.

This is the only place I went to get my hair cut when I lived in Nashville. Speedy and skilled service without any frills. I got cuts from all the barbers and never left disappointed. 

A regular cut is $20. They don't take reservations, walk ins only. The parking is a little confusing as it is within the Vanderbilt medical center but there are several 30 minute spots right out front. You can enter and exit on 21st.

It's been hard finding a place that compares where I live now.

Delicious shrimp and grits, and Crocque Monsieur. We thoroughly enjoyed this nice little spot adjacent to the Hilton for a Saturday afternoon lunch in the CBD. The service was great and we loved the food. Highly recommend stopping in here!

Though this place is no Taco Express (quod vide), I'd rather make the trip here than suffer through that far-overrated baja place on Thompson Lane. CB grills whole the burrito after building instead of steaming the tortilla beforehand, so it's warm and slightly crispy, not slimy and tepid like that other place. Make sure you are quick enough to say "no cheese slice" before he puts the cheese slice (triangle of muenster, wth?!) in your burrito. I think that's the non-mexican owner's input. Whatever you get, just ask the guy behind the glass how he likes it, and agree. This usually means onions and cilantro and hot sauce only. Ask for the green sauce, it's the best. Tuesdays are good for the fish taco special (ask for "everything" on it). The drinks include a good lemonade, a mild horchata, and some sort of fruit tea mixture. Jarritos are available from the cooler. Smiley-face cookies for dessert--never had em, but hey, they might be good. The downside to this place is that there's like three televisions so it's hard to find a not annoying place to sit.

A favorite in the neighborhood.   Can't go wrong with this byob.  Cold app sampler is an awesome starter and I haven't found a dish I don't like.  This place is also great for rehearsal dinners and events.

this is a great gym, but you can read more about that in the other reviews.

i'm just writing to respond to the previous reviewer who commented that the staff at the sporting club doesn't let you deadlift.  this is blatantly untrue -- i deadlift at this gym all the time, and i see a ton of others doing it as well.

Tonight I was dying for chicken wings so I ordered the 10-piece hot set. To meet the order minimum I added waffle fries. Fast friendly delivery. However, I was very disappointed in my food. Both things tasted burnt like they needed to change the fryer oil--GROSS. Clean your fryer, Spot. Didn't get very far into the meal, $16 down. Sucks.

Try's to have a cool hip vibe but doesn't deliver on anything else. Espresso was good but they are luckily they are in the food desert of donelson. Actual restaurant is dirty and looks rigged up by duck tape , ordering process is annoying, staff is all hipsters with no sense of urgency and with as many egg options on the menu they should really learn how to cook one.

There is much buzz about the Children's Museum and I will say that it is a valuable asset to Indianapolis. This is probably one of the most accommodating museums I have seen with ramps for strollers. They layout is impeccable. Nice open airy spaces. Wide easy to use halls. The workers seem well treated and eager to help yet they aren't in your face pushy like other museums. 

When I rate museums though, one measure that I include in my ratings is the accessibility to the community. And like other museums in Indianapolis, The Children's Museum needs to improve for people who are of lower socioeconomic levels. Many museums are able to improve socioeconomic accessibility by shifting their admission charge to parking costs. This would make the museum more affordable to people who rely on public transportation and incentivize environmentalism. Given that large sections of Marion County have fallen under harsh times, The Children's Museum can truly innovate by extending its services to cater more to lower income communities. Quite frankly, even the $245 family membership can be steep for even middle income families. They should at least allow for reciprocity agreements in that level of membership. 

Issues in pricing aside, as Children's Museum, the Indianapolis Children's Museum is among the best in the country. It is one of those rare museums that possesses something to interest every child. The bodily kinesthetic learner can enjoy the Toddler Play zone on the 3rd floor or the extensive sports park outside. My 16 month old loves the Dinosaur exhibit. I found that the history exhibit does a good job of explaining racial inequality and injustice in the world and is quite interactive for children of all ages. The China exhibit exposes children to multiculturalism. Quite often, many Children's and science museums have too much learn or too much play (and not enough learning) and the Indianapolis Children's Museum has done a nice job of balancing both. I think the Children's Museum was smart in their expansion efforts to build off of what they have rather than build completely new. This is a smart strategy because it doesn't alienate past clientele who flocked to different exhibits. 

An example of public-private collaboration that should be happening more in Indianapolis is the presence of a public library within the museum. Through this, my 16 month old can take home a bag of free books with her that she can return the next time she visits. 

Overall, the Children's Museum provides a magical experience for the children that it serves. It does not get my most elite rating, however, because its pricing structure keeps certain groups out. This seems to be an unfortunate trend with museums across Indy and there is room for the Children's Museum to reverse this trend and expand its hard but good work of educating children.

I have only lived here for about a year, but Han dynasty is my favorite restaurant in Philly. They have a 1-10 spice scale and in some dishes a 10 is actually very hot. Just how i like it. The food is also delicious in general. My favorites are the dan dan noodles (a must), the kung pao chicken (nothing like what you get at your avg Chinese restaurant) and the spicy cucumbers. I think I've tried just about everything on the menu and it's all great. Portions are huge. Two people with big appetites can leave stuffed, and with leftovers for less than $40. 

Also all of the servers I've had have been very nice and without mistakes despite how busy the place gets.

I had a full set of acrylic gel nails done on Friday Oct 16th. This is a pretty expensive service starting at $55 for a full set. In less than 24 hours, four of my nails had broken. I went back on Monday,October 19th to get them repaired. By Friday,October 23rd, two of the same nails had broken and five other nails began lifting. I am not going to bother returning to have them fixed again, because it is more than apparent that they lack the proper skills needed to apply this type of acryllic. In fact, all of my recent services have been subpar at best and I am thoroughly convinced that the nail techs don't  have a real desire to slow down and execute any service with excellence . I will not be visiting again. It's a shame because I used to be quite happy with the quality of their product and service. That's no longer the case.

Soul.  I have been craving that fried chicken for months!  Jazzy atmosphere, simple. Soulful and longing to come back.  The seafood platter will wow!  But I miss that plateful of fried chicken!  NOLA at its finest roots!  I will be back, guaranteed!

I walked in just looking for information because a friend highly recommended coming in. I've suffered from back problems for over 6 years and I'm only 24. I've had back surgery and been to almost every type of therapy and place in town and have never gotten anything from these places. However yesterday When I came in they said they could do a consult now and see if he could help with the intense pain I was in at that moment and hour later and I walked out with no pain!!!!! He is incredible and I can't thank him enough. I will be telling everyone I know to come here and I will be back over and over again!

Normally, I love this store. Today not so much and not for the past few months. I called to ask if they have fresh terragon bc I'm having a bernaise emergency and first there's no answer in any dept. then I get an answer, I'm placed on hold, then I'm hung up on and I'm sure this is intentional bc no one wants to go look. Hello, Whole Foods, I'm giving you my business.

Upon arriving I was told I had gotten a free upgrade to a jacuzzi suite. That was pretty unexpected, though I think I would still give the place 5 stars even if I hadn't gotten it. The room was quite large and in addition to the jacuzzi it had a gas fireplace. Room temperature was already set to perfect comfort and very clean. The only thing I could have asked for was a desk -- there was a loveseat and a comfy chair with hassock, but nothing appropriate for computer use. We were only staying 1 night so had limited interaction with the staff but they were very welcoming. The hotel has a basic tea & cookies around 4-6pm, and complimentary breakfast from 7-9. Breakfast has a waffle maker which was pretty cool, along with more typical things like instant oatmeal, yogurt, boiled eggs, toast.

Excellent beer on tap and I loved the decor. Some might think it's too loud, but I didn't mind. The food was good, but a little expensive for what one gets: three street size steak tacos for $14 and a 3 ounce piece of (well cooked, well seasoned) salmon on a large bed of salad greens for $16. Maybe the burgers and sandwiches are a better choice. The staff was very friendly. I would go back for the beer, but not for food.

This is some of the best soul good I have ever had in my life, second only to my great-Granny's cooking! Best meal in New Orleans by far! Great prices, fun atmosphere, great waitstaff and excellent food!  I will definitely visit here every time I goback to New Orleans!

I'm mostly reviewing for the garden center and nursery, which is a dream!  Plants for indoors and out, in all different sizes, shapes, and colors, at reasonable prices.  Although I mostly try to get my plants at Gardens of Babylon next to the farmers' market, Home Depot is a close second.  During my first trip here, I ended up with a big hanging fern and bunch of succulents, cacti, and exotic angel plants, for around $25. I was impressed by their variety and quality of vegetable and herb seedlings as well, and I'm considering going back soon to pick up some things for my garden.

As far as the rest of the store goes, my partner and I had to purchase a few items to make our 1950s home a bit more tech-friendly, and the man who helped us (Rob, I think?) was very knowledgeable.

I made an appointment to try on a Monique Lhuillier.  The ladies weren't welcoming when we came in.  They gave us the dress and put us in a dressing room.  We tried on a few dress ourselves...by ourselves because no one helped us.  In addition, the wedding dress samples looked super rough.  I get it.  Your dress is altered and looks nothing like the ones on the floor but if I was a bride I'm not sure I could have pictured some of these dresses on me. The Monique Lhullier was OK.  I'm just not a fan on all this chiffon in most of these bridesmaid dresses.

I've been here 3 times since it's opened, and every time it has been SO good. Consistent, healthy, delicious!  I love the chicken bowl. The potstickers are crispy and perfectly fried. The cup of miso soup is the perfect finishing touch.  I'll be back.
Great food.  We were pleasantly surprised.  The outside was misleading, but the inside was nice and the food was delicious.  Note to decorator , loose the Halloween  stickers on the window.

My husband and I went here for lunch, and I just loved the look! It's so cute! I'll definitely take advantage of the outside seating when the weather permits it.  The wait staff was very friendly.  They gave us a nice portion of food.  We didnt order anything special, but the food came out quickly.  I'm looking forward to trying dishes others have recommended!

Praise Jesus something that is not your typical brewery!  I hate beer but love cider.  We came to Fountain square for a date night and found this place.  We started w the $6 flight and then picked out beverage of choice.  Honestly they were hard to pick from.  The meads are honey based alcohol.  Different but delicious!  

We also ordered the meat and cheese plate that was good.

I love this place. Can't get enough. Favorites include Cold noodles with spicy sauce, Twice cooked pork, Chongquin spicy crispy chicken, Sautéed string bean, Eggplant with minced pork in spicy garlic sauce, and Diced fish with spicy pickles pepper. Awesome!

Pretty good food and drinks - would be happier if the prices were a bit better, but I guess that's what comes with a more "touristy" sort of place.. Our waiter was excellent the last time we were there. Service in the past has been okay / pretty good. We like to sit outside. I can't imagine wanting to eat here if I had to eat inside, actually, it just wouldn't be the same. We didn't have dessert - but this was actually because our waiter recommended that we not bother.  Boo for them that they don't have desserts their staff feels comfortable suggesting to the customers.

Horrible! With a name like Brixx Wood Fire Pizza I was expecting alot. I placed a pick up order and got the 4x4. The 4x4 is supposed to be a 4 cheese and 4 meat pizza with parmesan, mozzarella, gouda, goat cheese, pepperoni, sausage, bacon and prosciutto. Doesn't that sound awesome?!?!? I walked in and looked at their beer menu while I waited for my pizza. They actually have a really nice tap list. I think that's why I didn't look at my pizza before I left because I was distracted by the beer. When I got home I was very disappointed. The 4 cheese pizza barely had any cheese on it. The toppings were pretty scarce too. I called them and complained and they offered to remake my pizza. I went back 2 days later still anticipating a great pizza. I gave them the benefit of doubt on the 1st pizza and just assumed it was a mistake but the 2nd pizza wasn't any better. No cheese, no toppings, dry and really no taste. Indy has wayyyyyy to many good pizza spots for you to waste your time on Brixx. Bazbeaux, Jockamos, Napoles, Apezza, South of Chicago, Pizzology... the list goes on. Blaze Pizza is better than Brixx and its basically a fast food place.
Wonderful place with wonderful food. Service was fantastic. My grandmother and I had a great experience.

I quite agree with most of the reviews posted here about the owner of this terrible place. I feel the owner is mentally ill or normally high on weed. He is a racist bastard and I will not be surprised if someone's sues to this place/owner in future.

I don't want to go into the minute details about our conversation with the owner but I would suggest that you should only visit this place in case you are fine with being treated as shit.I would rather spend an extra $10 bucks and go to a better place with better customer service.

I would have given 0 or less rating had yelp provided me that option.

Good food, good location and usually kept pretty clean.

Service is not very good at all, in fact it is the main reason for the 3 stars.

For dine-in the servers really have no experience in serving.. you may get one meal before your friends do. I ordered a slice and some garlic knots while the rest of my party ordered 2 sandwiches. The waitress brought my slice and garlic knots together, then brought the other orders about 10 minutes later... She also asked if we wanted refills on our EMPTY glasses when she brought the slice, we didn't get our drinks until we were done eating our food. The place had a total of 5 patrons ( 3 at our table ). At the time they had 2 waitresses working, 1 lady working the cash register and 3 or 4 cooks.

My other complaint is when ordering over the phone for pickup. I have ordered at all times, late/early, lunch/dinner and have given them plenty of time to finish the order 20-30 mins before I show up and still end up waiting 20 minutes for my order. I have even tried paying by CC with hopes they would make the order before I showed up... Someone needs to teach them some urgency and they would get 4-5 stars.

Food is pretty good, pizza always consistent. Stromboli's are HUGE and tasty. Garlic knots are pretty good, cheese steaks are pretty good. Wings are average.

All my previous registries have been with Target and I decided, (for family purposes) Babies R Us would be an easier option. When my boyfriend and I went in to get our registry, we were greeted by an older lady, she helped us get started on our registry immediately-great! But then, as she started asking questions she said "how old are your other 2 kids" and we told her when she then replied "you look too young." Then, she proceeded to comment on a mother of 3 that was walking through the store and said "can you imagine what it's like at their house" which were about to have a 3rd baby ourselves.. she then looked at my boyfriend and said "Will helping scan things help wake you up?" It was numerous comments like this that felt unnecessary and rude. Overall decent experience but kind of unprofessional.

I'm starting this off by saying I am a part time vegan. It's very rare that I find restaurants that either cater to veganism or restaurants that have tasty vegan dishes. HOWEVER, this place right here is one of the best places I've been to. 

I ordered the Ziggy Burger and OMG if that smoked tempeh didn't taste like actual beef. Honestly it tasted better than actual beef. And the best part about the burger was that I didn't feel over stuffed. I also tried the Pumpkin milkshake and that too was very tasty and light. 

I wish they had this chain here in Jersey. But until then I don't mind driving an hour for good vegan food.

Best everything bagels in the area, in my opinion. They kick the crap out of Manhattan Bagel or any other place people foolishly go to. I love surprising my sisters early on a Sunday morning with a bag of freshly sliced everythings. The everything great grain with jalapeno-cheddar cream cheese is my go-to, and when I'm feeling extra lavish I splurge on the lox bagel (lox, choice of cream cheese, onion, tomato on choice of bagel). I could eat that every morning for the rest of my life. The girls behind the counter are always very friendly, even early on a Saturday morning when the line is nearly out the door. I really can't speak to anything else on the menu, though. The fresh-squeezed OJ is obviously delicious, but comes with a hefty price tag. They also have another location that just opened up in Oreland. Be sure to ask for freezer bags, and immediately freeze half of the bagels you get so they stay fresh for the week!

The restaurant has beautiful views of Tampa Bay and the worst food I've eaten in a long time! The location is it's only plus! Everything else is awful! The restaurant is freezing but they have fireplaces  going in different locations. It must make its money on weddings. The food was mediocre at best. Please don't waste your money!

I started my vacation with my side chick eating some shrooms, popping Molly's and drinking a lot. After a night like that and a hangover morning I thought about looking into a New Orleans fave. We read the reviews and bammies found Mr.B's. Started at the bar while walking in as the whole weekend was filled with reservations, no issues with that as after a glass of wine and some Titos n soda the amazing bartender Brett recommended some items on the menu. 20 min later we sat at our table. We had the crab cake for an app and the pork chop for the sexy lady and the bacon wrapped shrimp n grits for the playa. It was out of this world amazing.

Great place to go! Awesome selection of glasses frames and sunglasses too. They're always up to date on the latest and greatest technologies and eye care recommendations. Super friendly staff. And a parking lot out back so you don't have to park on the street.
This place is pretty darn good. Great staff and service. If we ever come back here, we will definitely eat here again.

I knew I wanted 3m Crystalline on my new Tesla, so I did my research and decided to take it to Orange. They were professional, prompt, pleasant, and had my car done when they said they would. I even got cleaner, a microfiber cloth and cleaning wipes in a little gift bag! Very nice touch, Orange Tint, and I'm very happy with the tint job!

I really love this place. I probably go here an average two times a month for the last ten years. I like that they carry vinyl records and rare import horror flicks (even though they're a bit pricey). The only thing I hate is how they have two stations playing music within the lower floor at the same time. You stand near the jazz section and you get blasted with two different crappy songs. I hate that. Anyway, for someone that hates Top 40 and is into B-Movies this place is as good as it gets.

Finally got a chance to check this place out! I highly recommend the chorizo, al pastor, barbacoa, and poblano steak tacos. The house green and red sauces are really good.. the green is refreshing and the red has some kick but not too spicy.

I always receive fantastic service at Serenity. They are always friendly and very punctual with my appointments. Lots of options for nail colors.Today Kim did my pedicure. I got the sugar scrub, it was Amazeballs!

(This post turns into a happy story in the end) I was originally ushered in by the pushy sales girls a few months ago. I felt like I was just another customer that was stuck on an assembly line of bad customer service. As I was escorted to a chair, I was introduced to a girl who had purple hair. She seemed hurried and a bit cold shouldered towards me. I was so uncomfortable that I left as soon as I could (after more aggressive attempts to make me buy products from the pushy girls). I got home and was horrified by my eyebrows. I had a lot raising where she had waxed. Luckily when I called back, I talked to the sweetest girl. She apologized so sincerely and encouraged me to come back in so she could help me out. She actually listened to what I had to say, and didn't make me feel like I was going to be eaten for lunch. Thank you Kelly!
I placed a pick up order and the turn around time was super quick, the staff was incredibly friendly and the pizza was really good! I will definitely be a repeat customer.

neighborhood grocery store that is a throwback place.  not a great selection and prices are higher, but the workers are friendly and the location is amazing.  wish more neighborhoods had spots like this.

Killer workout that works muscles that you didn't even know you had. Jennifer is the most motivating, challenging AND sweetest teacher. This is the hottest workout in LA, and I'm so glad that Novo brought it to Nashville!
The food always good I have no disappointment but I don't really like their pizza it taste like Boston style pizza not my favorite

Food was okay at best.
Waiter was Missing most of the time.
Dessert was disgusting.
Bar/Drinks are fun and hopping.

Go here!! We need more places like it in NOLA. Tons of options for various diets and intolerances. The salads are fresh and big. They have pre made entrees and snacks, but to-go orders are quick as well. They also have NOLA kombucha and other speciality beverages. Everything is under $10.

Bonus: all the to-go containers and cutlery are made with compostable materials. The planet thanks you!!

I've been here twice now and it keeps calling my name to come back for more.  I can just hear a pig and a cow in the back whispering, "Bernie come back."  The smell outside wafting from this restaurant is enough to make you stop in and want to dive in.  

The number #1 attribute of this place, the specials.  Every night something different, and every night 4 or 5 different specials, a daily meat cut, daily flatbread, daily soup, and some kind of daily fish.  Diverse menu is an understatement and while they are known for their meats, both their fish and poultry dishes are also fantastic.

Must have dish - The potted pig, appetizer with pulled pork confeit served cold amongst some pickles, apple raisin chutney, and some pickled radishes and onions.  Even if it sounds scary, just order it.  It's amazing.

The service was great very knowledgeable wait staff, timely and friendly, but between the menu and the drinks you forget about everything else.

The best part about this place, the value.  With a cocktail, a soup, and an entree you can get out of here with a 5 star meal for $40 after tip.  The beer menu is medium sized and their wine is list is good, but their cocktail menu is creative and original.

from the pulled pork, to the rib eye steak this place is delicious up and down.  Deciding what to order is the hardest thing about coming here.

I wanted to try a buffet while I was in town and this one was located in the casino I stayed at, El Dorado. The price was right at $12 a person and the menu was eclectic. They had pho, Italian, barbecue, some Chinese, and more! My first plate was mostly meat and it was pretty damn good! Brisket, pork spare ribs, fried chicken, roasted turkey, prime rib, Italian sausage AND bison sausage. The cut of brisket I got was a little fatty and the turkey was dry, but everything else was great! For sides I got potato wedges which I drizzled with nacho cheese, Mac and cheese and Spanish rice; all of which were also delicious. As far as the Italian section, I only got a slice of pepperoni pizza. Not the best pizza I've had, but nothing to turn your nose at. I'm not too big on sweets but I took a look at the dessert bar and it was pretty extensive as well, same for the salad bar.
Awesome sandwiches (you can't beat the thanksgiving sandwich) and the staff was really nice when I went.  It is a little cramped inside, but the tables outside make up for it.

Good TO GO Food ...I'm in! I was expecting a big fridge when you walked in, pick up your food and off you go. Instead I found a nice cozy lounge with about 5-6 tables and hot to order lunches. I would say if ordering to go just call ahead it will save you time. 

So I couldn't pass up a CL deal and it was great for a first timer. I ordered the Tampa Chicken sandwich with my dietary restrictions this sandwich was still very tasty... that doesn't happen often, probably the caramelized onions has a lot to do with it. I also ordered one of their chicken dinners, they all come with two sides and you have to reheat them at home. Both dishes were very good. The parking it's small and service may take a bit but if you are in the are you should definitely stop by.
I was visited for my first acupuncture session, honestly I was uneasy and skeptical.   Amy was great and I'm already scheduled for my second one.
Definitely recommended tour. Didn't think the swamp would be a beautiful place, but it was. Great tour guide. Was skeptical on paying $50 but it was worth it.
