They clearly close at 10:30, so I was obviously surprised, Especially because they had served the two ladies ahead of me.  I don't know what they ordered but I wasn't offered that either.
The food was delicious. The restaurant is very clean and the staff was quite friendly. The spinach dip is a must!! It was amazing! We had Joey as our waiter and he was great!

Straying in NJ for Memorial Day weekend and used the good Ol' yelp to find a Breakfast close by.  This place is in such a cute neighborhood and the service was fantastic! Wait was a little long, however the size of the restaurant is very tiny, the staff did a fantastic job.   Food and coffee were also delicious.
Had the fish tacos and mojo chicken. Both were mediocre. Not our top choice for the area.

I ordered a special drink at 11:56 ( been trying since 10 of) when my bartender finally gave me the drink he said its going to be full price because it's pass 12, I showed him the time on my phone and he immediately got upset and said "don't worry I'll pay for it because I know times are hard and you can't afford it." 

YUP you read that correctly. My bartender, not knowing anything about me, disrespected and insulted me, after I treated him with the upmost respect and thanked him after every service. 

I've never been so offended in my life. You need to seriously reconsider your staff.

Five stars, no question! When I arrived I was greeted by the manager, John and the guy at the front desk, David. They were both super friendly and accommodating. I had seen the reviews about the noise from the club and asked them about it. They didn't hesitate at all to secure me a room away from the club. So, if that concerns you, just mention it and they'll take care of you. Overall, checking in was fast, easy and enjoyable. 

Then I saw the room and my jaw dropped to the floor!  It was absolutely breathtaking!! We stayed in room 502, a King Deluxe corner room, and got a really good deal on it. The style of the room and the whole building is totally my kind of place. It feels historic, but is updated and modern. It is very clean and stately. 

The wifi is free, the breakfast is free, the gym (down the street) is free. I didn't have to ask for anything else because everything I needed was in the room, but I'm sure if I had needed something I would have been accommodated. 

Another bonus is the little Italian restaurant next door, Little Nonna's. It was super romantic and charming with yummy food. I definitely recommend eating there during your stay. 

I wouldn't hesitate to stay at the Independent again and will definitely recommend it to my friends and family!! Thanks again to John and David for making my stay so pleasant!

A very cute place to have breakfast or brunch with someone. It is not a large location so groups are limited to 5. They have a fresh made to order kitchen with specials that change often. 

The food is always fresh, the baked goods are tastey and I love all the varieties of French toast and pancakes they make! 

Fresh squeezed juices along with fresh brewed coffees. 

Highly recommend this place, nice vibe, and great service. 4 stars because it takes a while to get food and it's a bit pricey for the portion sizes. Besides that, big fan.

Let me start this review off by saying, after my research on this restaurant I would not have selected it for my Friday night dinner but since my son was celebrating a promotion (and he was footing the tab) Grand Lux it is. 
A step above the Cheesecake Factory with much nicer decor. Very spacious seating area and the open viewable kitchen is nice. 
Service was excellent as they even put up with me requesting to be moved twice. 
Now to the star of the show "The Food". 
Although I wasn't disappointed, neither was I impressed. Portions were big and food presentation was fair. Overall not bad but I've definetly had better.

Until this week, I never even know this place existed. That is about how much I know about camping, fishing, and hunting.

However, now that I have discovered it, I would highly recommend it to people into all things outdoors. Which is not me. However, I did find some useful things here like first aid supplies, pocket knives, and backpack accessories.

There are huge - HUGE - sections for tents, fishing gear, guns, and clothing. You can find Cabela's own lines of clothes as well as designer names like North Face. I loved the selection of hats, but I was so overwhelmed with the selection that I left hatless. 

The trophies that adorn the walls and the big game display area, as well as a the "gun library," add a museum-like quality to the store. However, for me, Mountain Equipment Coop is enough to suit my outdoor urban needs - and the prices are better too.
Jose is awesome! He is professional. Does a great job grooming in a timely manner. He is welcoming and sweet to the pups! Reasonable prices. Overall best groomer I have tried.

So the review is for the ballpark - not the team.  As an O's fan with a sibling (also an O's fan) living in Philly, we decided we would meet up in Philly when they played this spring.  The ballpark is very pretty and we had great sight lines (sitting in section 140 - I think).  The people working in the stadium were very friendly and eager to help out.  A+ to the ballpark staff!  I would have liked to have seen more options for picking up tickets day of.  The big downside to the park was the prices.  Their prices are very expensive and was hard to swallow when I compared the cost of like seats in Baltimore.  

They do allow you to bring in sealed water bottles (sadly, not all ballparks do) and my understanding is you can bring in a sandwich if it is in a clear bag.  Since I had just driven up from MD, I definitely didn't have time to pick up food to bring in.

All that being said, I will definitely return the next time the Phillies play the Orioles.
Excellent  sandwiches  and service.  The staff is always friendly and helpful.  If you are looking for a NY style deli, this is the place for you.

It's so exciting to have a beautiful little bake shop further down Germantown Avenue! We're very lacking of these types of businesses down at the Germantown end. I recently picked up cookies and a read-to-take red velvet cake with cream cheese icing for a meeting/event. Everyone thought the cookies were excellent! There were some mixed thoughts on the cake. The icing was perfect - not too sweet and not too heavy. The cake, however, seemed a bit dry and crumbly or coarse. I'm not sure how far in advance the inventory of cakes are prepared or if maybe the recipe needs a bit of tweaking. I may try cupcakes in the future instead. Very happy to support a new local business and hope they become a successful new addition to the neighborhood.

Hats off to Yats! They consistently deliver excellent food at great prices. In addition to delivering on their gastronomic and economic promise, they play a highly admirable role within their communities in Indianapolis and Bloomington.
 
 However, to see them rated as Indy's #1 restaurant would be misleading. If you're looking for a quick, inexpensive Cajun food meal - this is your place. If you're looking for the top dining experience in Indy, I'm going to guess that even Yats! owners would say that is NOT their niche

Decent place.  The food was pretty good & served reasonably quickly.  The selection was broad and the portions were on the large size.  Atmospherically it felt like a more traditional variation on Cheesecake Factory, but still it was okay.  Prices were a tad on the high side.

Of the five of us at the table, they messed up one of the orders, and didn't re-serve it until the rest of us, after waiting a bit, were nearly done.  Yes, we shared!
Bacon praline donut!! I literally stopped traffic it was so good!

Holy. Fricken. Crap.  This place deserves ten stars!!!

I had the baby rigatoni without mushrooms. The flavors were beyond on point. I could not believe what my mouth was tasting. The noodles were perfectly cooked. The sauce was creamy and delicious. The meat was a little crisp on the outside and juicy and tender on the inside, and tasted soooooo great!! I also ordered it with a salad. The salad was basically a quarter slice of lettuce with a ton of different fruits and nuts on top. Holy cow, I have NEVER enjoyed a salad like I had this one. I seriously could not stop eating it. 

I also drank a Rekorderlig strawberry-lime cider. I never had a cider that made me salivate for more after every sip. It was so great, that I am going to try to find it in libel liquor stores, because I need more of it in my life.

They also had live music being played by a very talented musician ushing electronic instruments. I never saw anything like it before, and he was phenomenal. The waiter was super friendly, and on top of everything. He was great. The atmosphere was intimate and a little romantic. I really loved it, and hope to come back.
Great nachos, specially the "nachos grande", chickpea soup is good. Customer service is okay, good environment.
Excellent menu across the board. Be sure to check out the daily specials for a great bargin.
I love this place, girls are nice and especially cute. Food is so good the hot Santa Cruz is out of this world. I have a beer and play old arcade games while I wait for my food to go.

So we decided to give this place a shot because it's around the corner. When we walked in the deserted yogurt bar that use to be underdogs, it appeared clean and I think it was clean because it was also empty. The owner/employee/disenchanted worker asked us if we had ever been, we said no. He explained the process and then mentioned the health content, which I had to chuckle at due to the nature of putting unhealthy toppings on a "healthy" frozen treat. He seemed sad. And then said if we filled up our cups it it would roughly be $7. So we tried several flavors of yogurt (all of them cohesive flavors). To put it bluntly it was some of the shittiest frozen yogurt I ever had. You know how most people complain about toppings? I'm telling you there was the most bizzare aftertaste ever. Kinda like feet and lemon being put into yogurt. I had the pumpkin cheesecake with chocolate and vanilla. Gross. All around gross. My friend had apple crisp and vanilla. That too was gross. The toppings were ok. Not the best, but I did think it was cool he had hot fudge. And quite a selection. Ours wound up being $19.
Great food, great price and a great host! I love eating local and have added this to my list. Thanks for the birthday dessert!

I truly need to go here more often. It is by far my favorite Edmonton Bubble Tea location. I adore the wide variety of flavours available! It's also quite awesome that they have board games to play and offer a little bit of snack food too (this has varied quite a bit since I started going here many years ago). The hardest part for me is picking a single flavour as there are so many options! I really love the fact that they have strawberry juice as an option!

My first visit back in February 2012, I had to have a crown placed. This was not a good experience at all. 

I was in the office for over 5 hours. The crown never fit right. I went back in the next day to have this crown adjusted. It was an awkward situation. I felt the dentist & staff were upset with me for coming back. I explained to the dentist that, the crown felt hollow and didn't fit well. His face turned red. I could tell he was angry. When he left the room, I didn't know he had finished, because he never said anything. One of the technicians told me about 20 minutes later, 'You can go now.' Needless to say, I left angry. Plus, I paid double for a low grade crown that I would have paid at my regular dentist.

This past July 22nd, 2014, I went back to Spanish Trail to replace that same crown. It had broken in half a couple of days earlier. This was the same crown that was supposed to be unbreakable. The original dentist no longer works there, so I was going to see someone else. I also noticed the reception staff was different...and nicer too.

I'll start by saying, this is the best dental visit I've ever had. After x-rays by a very 'metro' young gentleman, I was gracious greeted by Dr. Jenna Zonneveld and her Assistant, Jasmine. They were absolutely awesome! They were down to earth, and funny. Dr. Z, as she refers to herself, actually listens to you. She explained everything from top to bottoms. The best part, that I wasn't going to have to pay for another crown. It was covered under warranty. Whew!

I was in the chair for two hours. I checked in at 1:51 pm, and left at 3:53 pm. I even waited for about 5 minutes in the lobby. Dr. Z even fitted me with an upgraded crown. It felt great! This Ladies new exactly what to do. It was impressive to watch them work. They instructed me to call them if there were any issues, and sent me on my way. That is how its done! As of today, the crown feels like my own tooth. Thank you Dr. Z and Jasmine!

A couple of suggestions to Spanish Trail in General. Quit the 'up selling' routine. If it's needed, then recommend doing so. Otherwise your just a money machine to your patients; and it's obvious. Most importantly, always greet your patients (customers) right when they walk in, and when they leave. It makes us feel good.

Food for thought...

Thank you,

Frank F.

I had the best experience EVER here. The staff was absolutely amazing, my waitress Lindley sets the standard for all other waitresses.  She knew the menu was fun and even made us smiley faces in our ketchup bowls! We had a large group and she took care of all of us with no hick ups. We even got to dance and sing to a couple songs. Every time I visit reno,  Johnny Rockets will be my first stop!!!! Thank you!

Cheap and GOOD.

Their enchiladas are bangin' for $7 and it's so much food.
I accidentally ate all of it during my lunch break one day. That was a mistake. So full.

They usually make them with green sauce (which I'm still trying to figure out if it's tomatillo sauce. It's a little too spicy to be tomatillo, but I'm still not sure what it is). I had it with brown sauce one time, which I thought was mole, but again, apparently isn't. The brown sauce is not spicy, which I prefer.

I've never had the quesadillas, but I've only ever heard good things.

Their hours are strange, though. Sometimes they're open and if they don't feel like it, they're not.

I went in one day asking for a take out menu and the girl pointed to the wall where the menu was mounted so I said "No, I mean a take out menu that I can bring with me". She said "Online only".
This is not helpful for someone who does not have internet access at work.

Loved this breakfast place.  Day two of our vacation and my daughter is still talking about the bacon.  I had the french toast, daughter had the hash.  The variety of choice in the hash was the best, especially being able to use sweet potato.  Very clean and organized.  Loved the outdoor seating.  Suggest you get in early on weekends.  The line was long when we were leaving just before leaving.

I was in New Orleans for the French Quarter Festival. Took the Canal street car to Katie's. The roasted oysters served with slices of baguette was amazing. This was followed by a delicious fried green tomatoes and shrimp poboy. Sunday bottomless bloody Marys helped as well. Spent the rest of the day at Le Booze.

I went to Momo's on a Sunday night with some girlfriends for gossip, life updates, and of course, food. 

We arrived around 8pm, and the place was mostly empty. The atmosphere is gorgeous; it was so cozy and beautifully decorated. I immediately fell in love. 

We were seated and immediately attended to by our super friendly waitress. 

We started with the layered pita dip as an appetizer. It's not listed on their online menu, so I don't remember the description or what was in it. It was pretty tasty, even if the pita chips were a little too hard. 

For my entree, I went with the grilled lamb kabob. It came with lemon oregano roasted potatoes, and the whole dish was seasoned with what tasted a lot like balsamic vinegar. Don't get me wrong; I love balsamic. But it was a little overpowering. And while the flavor of the lamb was good, it was way too tough for me. I was literally chewing on each piece for at least a couple minutes before I could get it down.  

One huge complaint was the arrival time of the food. My friend's gyro arrived about 15 minutes before everyone else's food. And the layered pita dip, which was supposed to be the appetizer, arrived with the main course. 

Anyway, once the meal was complete, paying for it was a problem. The waitress refused to split the check, even though there were just 3 of us. Ugh. None of us had cash, so we handed her our cards and told her which items should go onto each card. Not too difficult, right? Well, somehow she managed to screw that up, and ended up double charging my friend's credit card. 

Anyway, despite the mediocre food and service headaches, I'll probably be back to Momo's at least one more time. They have peach bread pudding, which I was too full to partake in this time. But I'll certainly order it next time.
Excellent experience. The menu is packed with must-try's. The service was super friendly and helpful. Wish I lived nearby so I could go again!!

Hands. Down. FIVE. Stars!  This is the best little place off the road right on the beach Mature Palms in the garden courtyard give just the right amount of shade. Every plate I ever had was great- totally going to go here every time I'm in town!
Decided to eat here since it's so close to the airport. The waitress and staff was nice and the food was good. Good ole diner feel.
Absolutely fantastic menu. Fairly small menu, but all cooked to perfection. Service is speedy and friendly. One of my favorite spots!
Hola sou do Brasil trabalho com calhas e telhados procuro uma oportunidade como calheiro

Only one person in front of me -- waited for someone to help me. A guy walked right in front of me in front of the salad spot. The worker asked if he needed anything and got his order. And I'm still waiting for a good 5mins with no help! I will not be back to that location!!! 5 people behind the work station and not one person could help me!!!!

Lovely late lunch at Tre Luna yesterday after a drive up from LA.  We started with the Ellen Salad which was comprised of expertly seared scallops, shrimp and a small salmon filet over greens.  We then moved on to the Risotto Lucca -- tomato, parmigiano and roast chicken.  Flavors were highly complimentary and the dish was perfectly seasoned even if the arborio was a smidge undercooked.  We actually ordered each dish to share but the kitchen split them for us and essentially doubled the orders.  Much appreciated!  Same for the enjoyable pinot grigio which we ordered by the glass but our server just kept pouring.  Since our plans to eat light were dead on arrival, we ordered the Affogato for dessert.  Also delicious.  Did I mention the expertly pulled espresso?  Noting too that service was impeccable.  Our server was right with us the whole meal -- highly accommodating but not at all obtrusive.  What a gem in tiny Montecito.
i really enjoyed Tomo.  food quality and presentation was very good. Wait staff was too cute too. :) hey i am guy what can i say.
If it's good enough for the President it's good enough for me... DELICIOUS Vanilla Peanut butter ice cream and Lemon Water Ice... Under $5.00 for both. Awesome!

This is our favorite Mexican place and has been for some time.  If you come on a regular basis, you become part of the family.  

This is a locally owned place that doesn't pretend to be a flashy chain restaurant.  It can be hard to find, tucked back in a big plaza.  But, its worth finding.  The place is always full of locals.

The Mexican food may not be "authentic" (depends who you ask), but I love it.  If you want it hotter, just ask.  There is also a full bar and great Margaritas.

Some advice -- avoid Monday nights unless you go early or like crowds.  They have $1 tacos and cheap drinks and the place is crazy busy.  Also -- ask for Wil if he is working.

Place is so very bad!!!!  Use to live in area and remember why i did not shop at store often.  Was in yesterday and did shopping--alot of stuff not on shelf's and employees every place but register.  When we went to check out had 1 express open and 2 other register;s.  Place was packed and needed way more open.   I left a full cart of food  at register and left,  I use acme in Morton and other areas, In these other stores they always have more lanes open,  Acme lost out today here because i had a easy 250 dollars worth of food.  Went down the street to Giant and was in and out in now time.   Acme in Upper Darby will never have a good review if they stay like this!!!!!

I tried this place for dinner and it's simply delicious. 
The staff greeted me with a smile as I walked in past closing hours; Yes your read it right. I was driving across the country and was craving for Indian food and found this store fairly close to the freeway 84. I called in and ordered goat curry(delicious ever)for take away and I was an hour away when I ordered. I asked if they would still be open past closing hours and explained my situation. The guy at the front patiently listened to what I was talking and said it's fine, I could come pick up. 

Arrived 15 min past closing and guess what; they were still open. Picked up my order and thanked them for their service. 

Enjoyed my meal and all set to drive next morning to my destination!
In town on business. In the mood for Indian. Great find. Great food. I'd come back here for sure. Try the Rogan Josh.

Husband and I bought two sandwiches and a few bakery goodies. Not overly impressed. Sandwiches and goodies were ok. Nothing like OMG, lemme run out and get something from this place. I may give this place another try soon as I like to see small businesses succeed in hernando county.

Went to rent 16 foot truck to help move my Dad. Chris, Alicia, Dylan and Tyson were awesome. They were not only very helpful, but extremely professional. 
They are very reasonable in price and the truck ran great. 
I will be moving soon and there is no doubt in my mind that I will rent from them again.
If you are planning to rent a truck, check these guys out over anyone else before you make a decision.  
As for truck rentals places, these guys are tops.

As far as amenities go no pool or jacuzzi :(
However as far as customer service goes TOP NOTCH... front desk housekeeping and even engineering were superb
Rebecca was really cute and a lot of fun. She's doing graduate work in history and really knows her stuff. Love a free walking tour and I tip pretty well.

Biscuits is an quick service diner.  If you sit at the counter, you can watch the staff speak in English and Spanish and quickly serve up all sorts of yummy breakfast dishes.

I've eaten there a couple of times.  You can sit outside, but I don't suggest it.  The service outside is not as good.

I've ordered both the American breakfast and the breakfast quesadilla.  I like the American-style breakfast better, mostly because I'm not into spicy food.  The breakfast quesadilla was flavorful, and I would recommend it.

My friend always orders the chorizo scramble and loves it.

Overall it's a no-frills kind of place where you can get a quick meal.

Imagine movie theaters from the Golden Era, with a big neon marquee.  Shrink it down to half the size you imagine.  Now you've got the Broadway.  It's adorable and recently restored.  It began as a place for vaudeville performers.  It was also a movie house.  In the dark 80s it was a disgusting $1 theater where you got pelted with candy when the lights went down.

Now they show films on some nights and have plays on others.  It's a beautiful place that is worth a visit.

Moonshine me up, baby!

Stopped in with my friend for a quick drink since we had a few minutes to spare before meeting others down the street for dinner. Diablo's is very large would be a great place to go for some fun with a larger crowd maybe to catch a game or fight or even enjoy some live music.

The assortment of Moonshine caught our eye on this particular evening so I ordered a strawberry lemonade (strawberry moonshine) and M had a cherry coke (cherry moonshine). Both were actually really good and the alcohol was surprisingly tasty and not overpowering at all. But then our waitress gave us each a piece of fruit from our moonshine jars. Whoooeeeee! Definitely has a bite! 

I'd definitely come back to Diablo's. Looks like a fun spot!

I really want to love this place. They have a new store front & a food truck, plus this area needs a good bakery, but Sweetheart Cupcakes is kinda pricey for only so-so & mostly unoriginal cupcakes, plus inconvenient hours. Cupcakes are desert & my family & I always say we want cupcakes AFTER dinner (7 or 8:00 or so), but they close at 6:00 every weekday & earlier on weekends, so we go out for ice cream or I make baked goods at home. The normal flavors are things I could totally make at home, so they don't make me want to leave the house & spend $3 each on. I have gotten some interesting flavors on weekends when they have special order leftovers & I thought they were worth the price, but I just can't spend that much on a vanilla, chocolate, red velvet, etc. cupcake. I hope they continue to do well so they can make more unique flavors & have longer business hours.

I loved Muriel's! Great atmosphere, very attentive wait staff and the food was exceptional. I walked in and asked if they could accommodate a GLUTEN FREE dietary request and they not only said an emphatic "yes" but had a full gluten free menu. I had a delicious spinach salad ( feta cheese, bacon vinaigrette dressing) and the petit filet, shrimp, mash potatoes and green beans. All GF. I highly recommend Muriel's and go again.

Trying what ever we can in Reno.
The food was very good, kids loved the food here. The sea food Ravioli and smoked salmon were excellent. This made up for our visit yesterday at another buffet.

First let me say I never had Afghan food before therefore I have nothing to compare it to. All I have to say if this is what Afghan food is then I'm a big fan. 
I started with Sambosa and this was delicious. The pastry was very flaky and flavorful and the inside was filled with potatoes, chick peas and spices was the perfect combination.
For my entrée I had he chicken corma with basmatic rice. I was a little afraid to order this since I don't like spicy food but our waiter explain it wouldn't be spicy at all and he was right.
The chicken corma was so good, the sauce was great especially over the rice.
My dinner companion had the lamb and really enjoyed as well.
This restaurant is BYOB

I got a sticky bun. It was very stale. Not good. I expected good things since it was a city bakery. Very disappointed.

Edit* after my one star, Swiss Haus reached out to me and offered me to come in and choose something on the house. I appreciate that they care enough to do that. though i won't be taking them up on the offer, kudos to them. two more stars!

This was my favorite coffee place for many years due to the coffee (especially lattes) and convenience. With the previous owner there was a staff person who had a terrible attitude and I stopped going. Over the last year, everything is back to high quality. The last couple of times the iced lattes were exceptional and I was blown away by the friendliness of the newer staff.

This take out Chinese restaurant is same with all the other Chinese take out restaurants.  I always order the Seafood Soup and Two Shrimp Egg Rolls.  I didn't like their dumpings cuz the skin is too thick and not my style.  I haven't tried their General Tso's or Sesame but I am sure that those dishes must be good cuz those dishes are the staple of American Chinese take out restaurants.  Cheap prices.  Why not?  Oh yeah, they don't accept card.  Wack.

the weekend buffae is very special ....attractive here...they have variety of non veg and veg dishes
and now they introduced a new type of combo , it s name is " thalii"
it means you can have variety non veg and veg dishes in a big platter.....its so interestive...and very tastey

My boyfriend had his flowing locks cut off today and I am SO HAPPY we chose this place. His barber was Mike, he was very thorough, he spent over and hour carefully snipping, trimming, and fading my beau's hair. It looks amazing, I can't stop staring at it! Will absolutely be back!

Where are you going to go to get a solid sandwich while rocking out to Pentagram? Yellow Sub of course! It's seems to draw the alternative crowd and it's full of crazy things seemingly stacked throughout the years? Creepy baby dolls? A pic of young Selma Blair? The logo of Buena Vista the bar with the great Irish Coffee in SF? It's all here. Capocollo and provolone for the win. Oh and rock out too.

Ohhhh...   Where to begin?   This place is an American treasure.   It's like stepping back in time.  Warm, romantic and unique.   The food is as unique as the restaurant.  I have been to this Tavern for a meal during the day and night.  The only thing I would suggest but it's not the fault of the Tavern, is at night you might want to put some bug spray on if you want to linger outside.   After all you are out in the beautiful woods

Super great lunch - wagyu burger and drum were fantastic!
Fun atmosphere and great service. Lots of yummy options.  Don't skip dessert and tea!!!

My mom was in town visiting and needed to get her hair styled. Shawn did an amazing job and my mom was very satisfied with his work. He was very knowledgeable and cared about making my mom happy. My mom will definitely schedule with Shawn again when she comes to visit. Also she likes the hours your salon keeps!

I'm a huge fan of their meat lovers smoke stack.  I've eaten it many times and not been disappointed.  It's also enough for two people, so it's inexpensive if split.  I've also had their chili and really liked it.  Their other sides are not memorable, but the meats are always yum.  They do need to be sauced to your preference, so don't forget to pick up some of the sauces if getting this to go.

We tried Pizza Mizza because my hubby saw that they offer gluten-free crust in an ad somewhere. The 3 stars is for said gluten-free crust - the best I've had anywhere. They lose the other 2 stars for 1) the gluten-free crust is not on their menu, so you have to know to ask for it.  2) the staff was pretty lukewarm, didn't seem to want to be there. 3) we weren't told upon ordering that they charge an extra $2 for gluten-free. The bill for 2 personal size pies and 2 drinks was a whopping $29. Very overpriced, IMO, but I would definitely recommend them for those who want a good pizza and don't mind the price.

This place was crazy and crowded but everyone should experience it once. The interior was incredible and rooms were generous. Each room had a balcony to an interesting view of a one of a kind hotel. If funds were limitless this would be a great place to hang.

I used to live in Nashville and loved the tacos here but moved to LA for 5 years ago, all of my LA friends told me about different taco spots that were "the best" but nothing came close to the tacos at this place. I just moved back to Nashville with one of my LA buddies and we had their tacos today.... They were even better than I remember!!

I was debating between a 4 and 5 because I think the mac and cheese balls were overpriced, but it's unique enough to the area that it deserves a 5. I'll admit I've never had "authentic" Cajun food, but the gumbo was spicy but not overwhelming. The Train Wreck (sausage/salami po boy meeting a cheesesteak) is delicious; not as spicy as the gumbo but still enough heat to keep it interesting. Very warm and filling.

The staff is pretty nice and they do samples of the gumbo, so give it a shot.

Love this tiny little shop on Chippewa. I am a big fan of cake donuts, and DDI has some good ones. I love that people run it, get their donuts, then sit in their cars in the parking lot, eating and watching the world go by. And they're open late!

Visiting some friends in TN and read about this place. Got the spinach feta hummus and the black bean hummus...so yummy but the balsamic reduction took it to another level. Also got the maple sage latte, also a win. My friend  got the fat veggie which was good too. Then I moseyed over to the bar for my gin and tonic. Best way to end my night.

You could not possibly have a worse room service policy than this place.   The room service call goes to voicemail?   The front desk help sends you to voicemail.


In my many years of travel, I have never experienced a customer experience quite as bad as this place.   AVOID at all costs, so many better options near by for far less.

used to go to dinardo's in wilmington, DE before they closed down years ago.  have been meaning to try this one in philly to see the comparison.  i was psyched to see that the same dipping sauce is used (they told me they still make it in DE and send it up to philly daily) and that there are the same addictive garlic crabs on the menu.   the crabs we ordered were hot and fat, as promised, and fresh as can be.   we got 4 jumbos (regular) and 4 jumbos (garlic) and left completely full.   while somewhat pricey, i gladly paid for something i haven't eaten in over 15 years.   looking forward to returning in the near future.
Best bubble tea in Edmonton! Lady who runs the place is very friendly and remembers our orders even if we haven't been there in awhile. Definitely worth going there.

We arrived Sat around 12 pm. It was easy to get a table. We ordered the items we like from the menu. The food came out at a normal pace. They tasted fresh and good. I had red bean ice cream at the end and it was very good. Overall we liked this Saki better than the one on Dale Mabry which we have been there once and got disappointed. The food here were more tasty. The service was great.

I am surprised by the negative reviews of this place. My husband and I are here for the first time on a Tuesday night and were really pleased. The atmosphere is great, the service was good, the food really good and the prices reasonable. We eat at a lot of Mexican and Tex-Mex places and both said that we found our new favorite.

It took us years to try it because it looks like a dive bar from the outside. I wish I hadn't been so judgmental and had tried this place sooner.
Have only had the tacos but I recommend them highly, fresh ingredients and spicy.  Parking is a challenge specially at lunch time.

Indian food has become one of my favorites when I'm looking to spice up my typical pizza, sandwich, and pasta diet. Here at Tandoor & Tikka, I have the option of choosing from four styles of meals. Although I am not sure I fully endorse what I call the Cafeteria style (walk down a line of food options selecting all of the pieces you want) for every meal, this appears to be the current trend. The food was good and the servings were plenty. Just the meal filled me up so I brought home the sides I ordered. I will say I was taken back by all of the selections available and when it came to sauces, I couldn't decide. The person taking my order packaged 6 sauces for me to try out and that speaks to me about the kind of restaurant they are trying to run! I will certainly be back to try some more.

Sadly, I had a waiter serve me a dinner I was allergic to, despite me (1) telling him I had an allergy; (2) after I placed my order, I asked him to ask the chef whether my choices would be allergy-free; and (3) upon his serving the meal to me, I asked him whether he had asked the chef  whether it was free of the allergy I needed to avoid (dairy) and he told me yes, it was fine. Partly through the meal, I suspected there was butter in it, and when I asked a different waiter, he confirmed that it had butter. They then offered to bring me something else, but the rest of my family had already finished their meals so I said no. Lastly, to add insult to injury, when I asked the waiter why they were charging me for my meal, given that I couldn't eat it, he said that since my son (who does not share my allergy) was taking it home with him, they had to charge for it. 

I have been dealing with this allergy for a number of years now, and while it has presented issues at restaurants, never has it been as egregious as this. I went to talk to the maître d', who apologized and removed the item from our bill. But the damage had been done and I am suffering the consequences.

I had been wanting to try this presumably "elite" restaurant for many years, and I'm very sorry that I did. Apparently, the waiter thought I said cheese allergy, not dairy. The waiter himself was somewhat disturbing, in that he was sweating the entire time he was serving us, seemed to have laryngitis, and was coughing a bit.

Did not have a reservation on a Saturday night, but was told 15 min wait.   Sat at bar to wait.  Ordered a Jameson and ginger ale was told they had no ginger ale.  Half hour later we asked if out table was almost ready and was told they forgot to seat us.  They seated us immediately.  Waitress was very slow to come to our table.  Another served dropped off bread and the butter tipped over on table.  The server left it and did not leave a knife waited about 10 min for a knife.  Salad was just lettuce and red cabbage.  I ordered the meatballs and pasta.  The meatballs tasted like bread crumbs.  The pasta sauce had minimum flavor.  The manager came over because we did not really touch our meals.  We expressed our concerns to her.  She apologized and comped our meal, munis the alcohol.  I don't think we will go again regardless.

It's difficult to judge a restaurant after having just one dish but what I did have, I liked.  

I ordered the tuna tekka don, which is just slices of raw tuna on rice.  The fish was very good and came in nice thick slices.  My friend had what she said was a California roll but I couldn't see the crab.  I tried one and couldn't taste it either but I still thought it was good anyway.  I also had the house wine which was full of body and nice.

The service was fine.  Nothing really stands out.  I hope to try more things at this place.
Amazing Breakfast . Little neighborhood dinner.  But a hundred times better than a fancy restaurant in the FQ. Service was awesome  and the food was phenomenal.

Came back a second time, and I gotta say the place is definitely still a five star establishment. Despite Hampson Street getting crazy flooded, and there being a line nearly out the door, the line moved quick, the owner was super nice and accommodating, and despite having ordered the same thing, it seriously delivered. 

Tried my friend's Huevos, and while her dish was lacking on the salsa fresca/pico, the beans were spot on; really well seasoned. If nothing else, I love how clean this place is compared to other New Orleans establishments. Feels nice.

We had a great time for their Halloween theme weekend. We rented the rustic cabin and it was perfect for us and very clean. We brought a small space heater and sound machine so it was cozy. The staff was so friendly and the campers were so nice and into making Halloween special. Sand is through the walkways so the dust pan and broom they have in the cabin was welcome! Overall we recommend this place and look forward to coming to check out the water area in the summer!

We really loved the French fries. They were spectacular!  We also recommend the chicken tenders (really hand breaded ), the burgers,  and the belt sandwich.  We also love their beer selection and specials! We will definitely visit again when we're in the neighborhood.
An impressive display of trains and scenery. My two year old was in heaven. The only reason it gets a 4 is it wasn't all that kid friendly.

We had a pleasure to spent our spring break 2015 in the bungalow motel. What an amazing place! Room was perfectly clean with towels changed daily. Tatyana and Gordon were like family and made us feel so welcomed. I truly recommend their place because it was much better than some other 4 star hotels.  Great service and overall experience. Simply amazing. We will definitely be back all the way from NYC.

I love this Farmer's Market, mostly because I love Companion bakery (especially their brioche, perfect for bread pudding, french toast, sandwiches, etc)!
I also love Bittersweet Bakery that is always there... And Tower Grove Park in general is such a lovely setting for a farmer's market...

I generally don't buy any of the fruits and veggies, just because they're a bit out of my price range, but it's a fun place to check out and take photos at.

Also, there's a fountain nearby with tons of kids running through it which just makes the place cuter.

I like bringing visiting foodie friends here and they always love it too.... We always grab a snack and/or coffee... it's a pleasant atmosphere with lots of crisp white stalls with bright colored fresh fruits and veggies!

As soon as you walk into this place your greeted by some of the nicest staff! The service here is perfect from the people who greet you when you walk in, to your waiter, the manager, and even the person that delivered our food gave great service! The ambiance is great you over look the city while eating! And the food is AMAZING the salmon is perfect and the warm vanilla cake for dessert is ssooo yummy! I am definitely going back soon!

My first time here and I honestly think this was the worst experience I've had at a restaurant. I was really disappointed with the food. I was hoping it'll taste authentic, but I guess they made it more Americanized which is kind of understanding. I ordered the papaya salad (thum ma hoong) for appetizer, it tasted okay... Down side was that it was too plain for me, didn't really taste like the flavor I was hoping for.  The pad see ew was also so flavorless, I wanted to get a taste of toasty-ness from the noodles. Lastly, the desert. I ordered the sweet mango sticky rice which is my favorite Thai desert ever and I was really upset with this one. The sticky rice was more on the soggy side than sticky side. The coconut cream was just slapped on top of the sticky rice which I don't know why because it's suppose to be mixed together with the sticky rice. Also the mango wasn't ripe, it was hard & not as sweet as it should be. The only thing that pleased me was the beef jerky (seen hang), it was really chewy & flavorful with seasoning & a side of a sweet spicy tangy sauce which made it taste 10x better. Although, the food wasn't to my likings, the service & the environment was great & soothing. Which was the reason for the 3 stars. Friendly staff, but horrible food.

This place is wonderful.  If you do a special order, ask for Max.  I recently ordered a cake for my daughter's sweet 16 - Max did wonders, especially since I asked for a large cake, shaped like Tiffany & Co. boxes.  My one contingency was that I do NOT like fondant.  Max made a beautiful cake with turquoise buttercream icing (which is not easy because the icing slips).  The cake itself was the moistest chocolate cake I have ever had.

- Did Not Meet My Expectations -
Two of my daughters and I treated my mother to lunch on the patio at Upland yesterday. My mother is hearing impaired so we try to choose locations on the quieter side to enhance her dining experiences. We also checked the menu online first to ensure a variety of salad choices as that is my mother's go-to menu item.
My middle daughter and I visited Upland for a beverage just a couple of weeks prior; it was a Sunday afternoon and the patio was delightful and quiet. Unfortunately, this visit was anything but quiet or delightful. 
Upon arrival were seated on the patio -- there were other tables occupied with ladies having lunch (looked close to my age), young parents with a baby, and others. That said, I was confused by the rock music blaring from the patio speakers. I tried to let it go, but after 10 minutes had gone by and we're still challenged trying to have conversations at our table, I went inside and asked the bartender (only staff member I could find) to please turn down the patio music as it was difficult for us to hear our own conversations. He seemed agreeable, but I seriously doubt the music was modified; if it was, it was marginal at best. It's not like I'm not a fan of Def Leppard, but I don't want to hear it blaring at a group lunch.
As we perused the menu before ordering, we noticed it was very different than the menu Upland has posted online for lunch. Far fewer salad choices, fewer dressing choices, and fewer vegan options (all of my daughters are vegans). Mother and I both chose the Bibb salad; apparently, it's a new salad offering with large, leafy greens, strawberries, candied pecans and blue cheese crumbles for approximately $11.00. When my salad arrived, it was a shallow salad bowl with lots of large salad leaves and a meager amount of the other ingredients. Fortunately, my mother's salad had a few more ingredients in hers and she seemed to enjoy it, so I was pleased with that. We did both enjoy the salad dressings we chose; there are only 3 offered so not a lot of options.
While we were still eating our lunch, our server asks if it will all be on one check and then before we were done eating, casually dropped off the bill to me. I really do not appreciate it when my bill is dropped off before completing a meal and also before having the dishes cleared from our table. Am I being rushed to pay the bill, and if so, why? As a customer, I don't appreciate feeling rushed by servers. Yes, pet peeve of mine. 
I should also mention that I tried ordering the advertised Monday drink special, Helios Pale, but was told they were out of it. 
Will I return? Would likely only do so to pick up a carry out order of the Buffalo Chili as it is a favorite of my husband's. 
Will my 20-something daughters return? Perhaps for a beer, but not for food as Upland now has very limited vegan options.
What can I say besides that it's the best coffee in the area! Buddy is a roasting expert and every cup I taste is perfection.
The baked french toast with the honey butter and brown sugar maple syrup is the most delicious thing ever! One of my favorite places in Clearwater!

Best haircut EVER! I am officially naming Jesse as my new stylist. I am putting my trust and style in his capable hands. 

I called on a Thursday morning and was able to get in the same day in the afternoon. When I showed up, I was impressed with the open and fashionable space. I was offered water, tea, or wine. I went with a glass of wine. It was a great touch. They also had good music playing.

I was seen quickly and told Jesse all about what I was looking for, and my usual haircare practices. He offered a few ideas and they were all great. I decided not to stray too much since curly hair can often become a mess and it was our first time together. 

When he took me to shampoo, I was sold. He gave me the best head massage ever. He took his time and put all the right pressure in all the right places. He is not a head rubbing amateur. Those fingers were magic. For the conditioner, he gave me a hot towel to put over my face. I melted in all the best ways possible. 

Then on to the cut. He dove in and skillfully crafted a great cut all while having a good conversation and asking for input on length. It ended up great. I was very happy. I also learned of a few places in town that I need to check out.  

The best part of all this? Everything is vegan and organic! I feel like it was a match made in heaven. 

When I went to pay, I was shocked that I was only charged $30. I threw on a $10 tip and went on my happy way. I expected it to be much more. I have paid way more for much lower quality cuts.

The only improvement would be about the distinction of men's vs women's cuts. It is a big pet peeve of mine. I wish there could be a gender neutral way of delineating between the amount of time needed to cut hair. Short hair vs long? Everyone on the gender spectrum needs haircuts. 

In short, I had an amazing experience at Studio Green. I will be back in six weeks for my scheduled cut. You wil not go wrong here. They will treat you well. Your hair will look great. They even give facials and massages. That will happen at some point.

I've lived in Santa Barbara for over 3 years and have been a member at Paragon for over 2. The academy became a second home for my husband and I to train, learn the arts, and work on our fitness/wellness. The instructors are very knowledgeable, helpful, and truly spend the time to get to know you. The members are welcoming and before you know it, strangers turn into friends. Highly recommend and watch out, it gets addicting (in a good way, of course)!

massive margaritas.
don't remember much else
family-run, had some combination dinner that didn't stand out.
Great food... try the honey chicken and ask about their BBQ turkey necks.  Very generous w/ their portions.

Nolan is the man to see.. owner / operater the guy knows what he is doing ESPECIALLY with COLOR! I am a 40+ female who does blonde weaves and I was a salon jumper for years and years no one ever did my color just right- either made me too blonde or too dark.. Seriously Nolan nails it every time- even when it is time to add some low lights which is very hard to make right on a blond he gets it exactly how I like it. Yes it is nothing fancy, there will be no expresso machine brewing. Price is super reasonable.. everyone is just laid back- you dont feel silly sitting there with foil in your hair because it really doesnt matter! ha
Used wrong lift and severely damaged my undercarriage. In body shop now getting body work and paint, frame has deep gauges too
Very strong vegetarian menu.  Food had a lot of elements: flavor, presentation, composition, fairly priced... Will return.

This is one of the best sushi bars I've ever been to! It's small, cozy,  beautiful, and the waitresses are very attentive. I had the Combo A and it was very fresh and delicious. Then I finished off with the banana tempura and I was absolutely stuffed with tasty food. I would recommend this place to all sushi lovers!
Serves up great food. While Woodlands was closed, this place satisfied my dosa cravings. There were even a few more creative dosas on the menu, which is always nice to see. Can't wait to go again!

Pretty cool concept. Five Guys knockoff with organic ingredients and some other creative touches. Tried the double cheeseburger and the veggie burger.  Definitely good for the calories and stick with the cheeseburger. Very good but a bit greasy.  The french fries are excellent. Not oily and nice crispiness.  Also tried the milkshake, made with fresh scooped ice cream, organic milk and I had fresh strawberries blended in. Pretty good!

Finally some decent pizza in TN!!  Having lived in NY for 35+ years you just get spoiled.  Most pizza places around here are just bad.  And folks... Domino's is NOT good pizza. This is the closest thing to the real deal I've found in years of searching.  I've only eaten here just once but I'll definitely be going back for more!!!

Pros: fast casual, flavorful food
Cons: overpriced for the amount of food you get

For a quick lunch on a rainy Sunday, this was a good fit. The restaurant's vibe is casual and baja airy. You pay at the counter, take a number to your seat, the food is brought to you in plastic baskets, and at the end you bus your own table. We ordered chips with salsa roja ($4), two fried fish tacos ($4 each), one taco of the month ($4) featuring shrimp and meat, and one carne taco ($3.75). We were served within 5-10 min and everything was fresh and well-cooked. The fried fish tacos consisted of fresh flour tortillas cradling a laughably small amount of fish, maybe 1.5-2 oz, under a prodigious heap of pickled red cabbage. I appreciated the handmade tortilla and the fish hot out of the frier, but for the miniscule fish portion, they were just not worth $4 each. My boyfriend did not enjoy the flavoring of the taco of the month, though he noted that the shrimp was cooked very nicely. He really enjoyed the carne taco. However, two tacos and some chips for each of us, which came to a total of about $21 for lunch, felt like a scant meal and we had to snack a couple of hours later.

It's a rare weekend indeed when I get a chance to get out with friends for Dim Sum, but one such rare weekend popped up recently, and it was decided to try somewhere new. A friend suggested the Tasty Noodle on Calgary Trail and the consensus was "sure, what could it hurt?"

Answer: It did not hurt anything but our bellies after they were stuffed full of delicious food.

We arrived with a fairly large group and were handled very easily, the staff was friendly, and the cart service was prompt and excellent. There was an almost overwhelming stream of food constantly passing our table, and the tea was never empty.

The food was very good. Everything we tried was very tasty, and there was a lot of variety. In particular, I'm always on the lookout for a good BBQ pork bun - and Tasty Noodle didn't let me down there. One of the best I've had in Edmonton, and I went back for them a few times.

Language barrier remains a bit of an issue - but that's fairly common during all of my Dim Sum experiences. Fortunately, we also continue to bring our friend along who speaks "Chinese Menu," and that helps immeasurably.

I'd recommend getting there early on the weekend if you want to get in on the Dim Sum - we did and were seated promptly, but by the time we left the place was packed and there was a bit of a lineup to get in.

This place is clean, the staff is exceptionally friendly, and the food is delicious!  I had the chicken quesadilla and being from Los Angeles, I must say they know what they are doing at this place!!  It was awesome!!  I sampled the French Dip sandwich and it too was great!  The sandwich was served with fries that were hot, nicely salted and cooked perfectly.  I will be returning because the prices are reasonable.

I hate to leave bad reviews but it has to be done sometimes. My fav dish ever is pad see ew so I decided to try Green Basil since I'd never been here before. 

Unfortunately it was the worst I've ever tasted! I took 3 bites and had to throw it away, which infuriates me since I paid $12 for this just to be wasted. The noodles were way too over cooked and mushy. They were also super dry, I didn't taste any sauce at all. Way too much veggies, which were also dry. I've eaten A LOT of pad see ew before and this was not even close. Sadly I won't be coming back to this restaurant. 

The only saving grace is the woman who rang me up was a total sweetheart.

I love how I'm going to be that chick that reviews all the Enterprise Rent-A-Car. I can't be the only Yelper who doesn't have a car, right?! It's Philly!

Right now I'm a fan of Enterprise. I can hear you scoffing, but $9.99 weekends are heaven for me. I can rent a car for the whole weekend and do all the things I want to do like .... go car shopping so I can stop coming to freakin' Enterprise.  

The best part of the $9.99 weekends is that even if the Enterprise close to you isn't participating, you can RETURN the car at any Enterprise location. Awesome. So I returned mine here and this branch was nicer than the one I rented it from. It was warm, smelled clean, and didn't look depressing at all. The guy was a little too enthusiastic for a Monday morning. I think he saw me check-in on Yelp! because he held out his hand and was like "Please tell me you're a satisfied customer and we did everything we could for you today!" in this fake boisterous robotic voice. Scared the s*** out of me. Almost docked them one star for the ass-kissing, but realized quickly, it could have been worse. He could have "kept it real" and treated me like ass because it's early on a Monday morning, but he didn't. He put on his best fake smile. And you know what? Thanks guy. Firm handshake back!

Food: 2 / 5 Stars

The Breakfast Poutine: (4 / 5 Stars) The real highlight of today's brunch was my friend's Breakfast Poutine - I stole a few bites. The Poutine had a rich flavor and was very satisfying. 

The Duck Confit: (? / 5 Stars) Did not try but was told that the dish tasted great. 

Smoked Salmon Beni: (0 / 5 Stars) Although I was looking forward to my dish, the Smoked Salmon Beni was a huge disappointment. Not only was the salmon in small supply, it tasted like over-cooked frozen salmon rather than smoked salmon as advertised (definitely not a deal with the $12.00 price tag that comes along with it). Even though the eggs, potatoes, and other fixings of the dish tasted great, the core aspect of the dish was severely lacking - especially compared to the other items ordered at the restaurant. I was able to use hot sauce to mask the flavor of the fish. 

------------------------------------------------

Location: (Not a factor in the rating)

Prep & Pastry is a very nice and aesthetic looking restaurant. There are a lot of places to park even if the lot is full and we only waited about 30 min on a Holiday Sunday at noon. 

------------------------------------------------

Service: 5 / 5 Stars

The servers were very nice and accommodating at the restaurant. Additionally, they were thorough on ensuring that the kitchen staff was notified of my allergy to nuts. 

------------------------------------------------

Overall: 3.5 / 5 Stars 

Overall, I enjoyed my experience at Prep & Pastry and will most likely return to try some of their other food offerings; however, I will be avoiding their Smoked Salmon Beni.

I'm sad to report that it seems the quality here is slipping. At first, I thought it was a fluke, but I've been here several times now and it's definitely on the decline. The flavors aren't as tasty as they used to be, and the texture isn't as consistent (almost all have runny spots and many 'sputter' when coming out). I've tasted a few that would even be described as questionably fresh, and one that was definitely bad (they replaced it immediately after I brought it to their attention, but still...). In addition, their toppings have gone down in quality (& taste) too, namely the mochi, the cookie dough, and the brownies. Not sure if this was their choice or their suppliers', but it's not good. The Paninis they promised early in the season apparently didn't pan out. Plus, the spoons they use are not great for FroYo, and are even a little sharp and too deep, and not Eco-friendly (many better ones exist). It's still clean, but not the "sparkling clean" it used to be. The girls who work there are personable, but the really sweet manager, Allison, who made customers feel really welcomed, is no longer there.

They bring in a lot of different machine-dispensed frozen treats, in addition to the froyo. They started with old school frozen custard, and added gelato and lower fat/glycemic varieties, and now even have Italian ice. The ratio of frozen yogurt to these other items seems to be getting smaller. That's not necessarily bad, just a heads up. I actually think this is kinda cool, and if they were to expand on it a bit and offer really unique (high-quality) options, like soy/vegan FroYo or unusual flavors (maybe something spicy?) instead of 3 different meh vanillas and 3 different meh chocolates, they'd have something really cool (& worth driving farther for). In fairness, they do usually have a sea salt something-or-other, kahlua chocolates, and a banana-y/caramel-y option, but even those are pretty typical FroYo finds.

Also, they possibly used to have a sugar-free option? I only suppose this because the last time I was in there, several different customers asked about it, but the response was that they don't have a sugar-free flavor, just the lower glycemic flavors and a sugar-free chocolate sauce. Most customers who asked, just walked out disappointed. Another headsup, if you're in search of that.

These changes aren't enough to prevent me from going there at all (froyo's yummy), but they certainly have made me less excited about it and more inclined to look for other options. Unfortunately, there really aren't many in the area. I know I'm not the only person who's less happy with Berry Creamy than I used to be. I hope they heed constructive feedback from loyal customers and keep a check on their quality. It was one of the things that made this place so much better than the others I'd been to. Berry Creamy is still high-ish on my list, but I'm worried about their position in the future.

This restaurant is absolutely doomed to fail. It's had more menu changes and owners, than I shower.
The food is so different and foo,foo it unbelievable.
Why can't restaurants give a nice simple quality food.
I've been in here 4 times with the new owner, but I will not go back

One of the best independent bookstores I have visited. The space is inviting and the selection of books, especially fiction way better than usual. It's evident that the owners know what they are doing, love books, and understand what a bookstore can offer readers.

With so many great reviews, there was no doubt in my mind that this was the place would be a hit.  It was my first visit here and unfortunately my last.  Walking in the receptionist wss very nice and sat us right away.   Unfortunately the table was so small it left me wondering how we would fit any of our plates on it.  The devote was nice and had a rustic feel.  I ordered the fish tacos with a side of rice & beans. My s/o ordered the steak or perhaps the beef tacos ( I cant remember the name). The food presentation was very nice but there was very little food which would have been ok it it was offset by big flavor.   However, the food was bland and needed salt among other spices.  I grew up near the Mexican border and know my Mexican food.  If your looking for an authentic spot or at least food with flavor... this is not it

Great food...order the club sandwich. You won't be sorry, I promise! My husband is a huge fan of the pizza too.

My only negative comment is that they are sort of known to screw up the call-in orders. My employer actually refuses to go back, as they completely forgot to send the order back to the kitchen two times in a row (which the staff didn't notice until they came to pick up their order after the allotted 20 minutes). Two times, really? They've often messed up group call-in orders I have placed, and didn't seem that concerned about it when I called to complain.

I would suggest dining in only for that reason.
One of my most favorite places to stop by for a cup of coffee. The staff is beyond friendly & the environment is typically quiet, perfect for studying/reading.
Great food at a fair price. If your in a hurry, go to a fast food joint. If not this is the place to go. Simple creative menu and a great staff.
I came in to get acrylics twice and both times they made me bleed! Very painful, but the end result was okay.

A great sandwich shop, its chain-status notwithstanding.  No matter what time of day or night or late-night, I always get great service.  These guys know how to handle the college crowd well.  The price is right and hey, the smells are free!
We get breakfast from here often. He prices are very reasonable and I haven't had anything I didn't like!  The choices are really good (healthy and less so:)

This is probably the most "complete" farmer's market in the area.  The collection of vendors tucked in the middle of Tower Grove is really great way to start a morning with plenty of awesome lunch / picnic options in the area.  

With that said, I've come here quite often only to leave with nothing.

I'd like to point out that we have some pretty lame mushroom vendors in St. Louis.  The one at Soulard is definitely superior, but combination of price and variety and severely lacking.  All too often I end up going to Whole Foods after yet another disappointing round of trying to support the local guys.

Tower Grove farmer's market also suffers from stands serving the same stuff... after many years of trying practically every farmer's market in the area, I just overall disappointed that few compare to the one at Urbana, IL.  

Ok with all this bitching I'm going to have to say that this place is worth driving out of the way for, as they DO have a selection of cheeses, mushrooms, produce, and meat (Salume Beddu has a stand there!)

This is the second time I've come here and it will probably be the last. The nachos grande barely had any cheese and it wasn't even hot. They gave us the appetizer with no plates and it took almost 10 minutes to get plates from the waiter.  Then the food barely had any seasoning. This is one of the few times I didn't even want to take leftovers home.

The Nook is a good addition to the growing culture of Indy. 
My wife and I were pleasantly surprised and excited to try a new place. The Kombucha-Rita was a good way to start the evening. It was a refreshing twist to a traditional margarita. 
The bacon guacamole plate was very tasty also and probably my new favorite way to eat guacamole. Next I had the nook burger and my wife had the chicken strips, which she was very excited about b/c she never gets to eat things like this due to a gluten allergy. 
The burger was one of the best I have had in a while and that is saying a lot because I am usually not a fan of gf burger buns. The 100% grass fed beef was very lean and left you wanting more. My wife was surprised at how well she liked the chicken tenders. They had a crispy gf breading on them but she did say that as they cooled down the breading did get a little soggy on the inside but that is normal for gf breading. 
Overall we enjoyed Nook and will be eating here again.

Star Wars drink served with a glow stick! If you get another bartender other then the shorter fella with the long slicked back hair, who wears rigs on his fingers. He's usually there, every other bartender sucks!

Best Sonoran dog I've had so far! The Carne Asada Papancha is amazing! Only issue is the long wait for food. I will be back, although probably just for take-out in the summer because it's a food truck with a porch-like seating area.

With all the great choices that exist in Philly now, I believe that Vetri is the best fine dining experience in the city. I think the restaurant is moving to a chef's tasting menu-only option, and that is fine because that is the best way to experience the indulgence that is Marc Vetri's cooking. In conjunction with the wine pairing, this is a can't miss option. Been here a number of times now and have always left feeling as if the money paid was well worth it.

Everything is delicious. There's no point in telling you which dishes to order, because its a crapshoot what you'll get based on Vetri's mood and available ingredients for the evening. However, the wait staff will ask if you have dietary constraints and will take that information back to the kitchen. My wife will not eat seafood, and they worked around that for her.

A couple of things about the service: it is great. Hostesses, wait staff are uber-attentive and the sommelier is awesome! His name escapes me, but he is friendly, knowledgeable, and constantly available for all the dumb questions I wanted to ask about wine. He is a blast to chat with and adds to the total experience you get here. He makes me and my friends feel comfortable.

Last thing....the last time we were there, the staff recognized me and my friend and gave the ladies at our table that evening's tasting menu with Marc Vetri's autograph. That was a nice touch to end a special evening.

Can't say enough good things about Vetri...it is a place that you should go to at least once to say that you've had the experience. Chances are you'll go there again.

We ventured to Newtown to visit a local winery on our first wedding Anniversary. Found this amazing restaurant on Yelp and it felt like we were back in Italy where we had gone for our honeymoon.
The food was authentic and our server, Crescienzo, was amazing!
Even though we live over an hour away, we are definitely coming back!

I found V Vegaz on Yelp, after searching for stylists who will not butcher curly hair. Far too many stylists have given me a mullet, so I am skeptical when it's time for a new cut. The girls of V Vegaz were very friendly on the phone, easy to make an appointment with, and very sweet in person. The salon is hip & chic, and all of the girls have great style. I love the location in the Loop- directly across from the Moonrise Hotel and down from the Pageant, so it is convenient if you want to do a little shopping before or after. My stylist, Erin, was fun to chat with during the shampoo and cut. She took some time to evaluate the mess on my head, gave an awesome scalp massage, and excellent cut for the summer. She also gave some great styling pointers. With curly hair, I do not get haircuts too often, but I am looking forward to the next one!

This place is so freaking cute and the deserts are delicious. Their price-point is very reasonable and the service was fantastic. Try the pumpkin cheesecake and all of the mini cup cakes. 5 stars for sure!!!

Such a great experience staying at this hotel for my wedding.  Staff really went out of their way to accommodate my stay.  From the coordinators, housekeeping, front desk, security, and bell services all were attentive and genuinely wanted to make my stay great.  They say it's all in the details and I would say that lowes fulfilled that from the embroidered pillow cases with name and date, multiple welcome notes, complimentary chocolates/chocolate covered strawberries/root beer/chocolate covered pretzels, rose petals, and champagne.  Well recommend all my friends visiting Philly to stay here.

Stopped in for happy hour on a Wednesday evening. The oysters were .75 but not that great. The drinks, however were very delightful! I had the Silver Saint and the Chelsea. The Chelsea was my favorite and absolutely fabulous!! We came back on Friday evening right around 5:00 pm hoping to snag a seat at the bar but the whole place was packed and the next available reservation wasn't until 8:30 pm. Be sure to make a reservation ahead of time!

The service is excellent!!  Ask for Joe!  He gave me the advice to try the seafood Benedict for breakfast. So yummy!  The pancakes were good and the cheese grits were good.  The coffee is HOT!    The bathrooms are very clean. Highly recommend for breakfast!

Think twice before using this vendor. The pink veil policy is no exchange or refund. Therefore if you order out of their catalog, and you are not pleased with the product, you are stuck with the item. The gown I ordered was poorly made, and the material was cheap. The two layer of  material was so thin, I was advised to wear a slip, by the owner. They also don't take measurements, they order a large size, and alteration is $60. This happen to me in July 2014. I found a 2nd wedding attire at another local boutique, the wedding suit was beautiful! If you don't want to waste your money, think twice.

I was very skeptical at first - I am more used to a $10 haircut from a mega chain. I was very impressed by the staff and Gary did a great job on my hair as well as my son's. Love the atmosphere. I'll be back. 

Also they have a Kegerator in the waiting area.

Went to this place before the Opry last night. Amazing food with great entertainment. I recommend the brisket with the Memphis Sweet Sauce! If you go on a Saturday before the Opey plan to arrive EARLY and make reservations. We left at 630 and there was an hour and a half wait to sit down when we left. It is located right on the corner of a busy intersection as well and traffic gets really backed up on Saturday nights! Great place 5 Stars! Try their local beer too it was awsome

I got to visit Whitebox for lunch for the first time. I was in the mood for a sandwich with more than one kind of meat, so I went for the Italian. It had all the ham, cheese and salami I wanted! But I have to say that the veggies and dressing it was topped with was a bit too vinegar-y for my tastes, so I don't know that I'd get that one again. 

My father-in-law knows about my crazy sweet tooth, so he picked up a (guten-free) chocolate chocolate chip cookie for me. It was amazing!!! Definitely one of the better cookies I've ever had and probably the best I've found in St. Louis. It was warm, soft and the chocolate chips were all gooey. I was really nice and shared it with my husband. That was really hard for me...

I love this restaurant.  I wish I still lived in Philly, so I could go more often.  The service is quick and the food is really good.  I like that they serve hot tea and water to start.  I always get the roti canai, the nasi lemak, and the mee siam.  Another good dish is the shrimp and mango.  Their prices have gone up since I initially started going to this restaurant over a decade ago, but they are still very reasonable.

Four stars, primarily for the sushi. While there's no dearth of places to get sushi in the area (assuming you don't mind supermarket sushi), the sushi at Veekoo is currently damned fine. I've had some of their other Asian food, as well. The quality seems to depend on the dish. But the sushi is always top-notch.

Stopped by for the first time today as I was starving at lunch. It was so much more and better than I expected. I got a chicken salad which had strawberries, blue cheese and walnuts added to the greens and a scoop of chicken salad on top-- it was sooo good, I gobbled it up without adding the citrus dressing that accompanied it. A+. Then I picked up 4 8oz small salads including: Greek, southern potato, rice and kale salad for my family to sample. All thumbs up votes! We will definitely go back to try the other menu items like Poppyseed Chicken casserole and daily menus. I can't wait!
Almond horn was a pricey $5 compared to Swiss Haus, and just about as good.
My favorite pizza place, and my kids love it.  The soda's are great and unique, and I highly suggest the Sweet n Slow pizza for you meat lovers.

Really good pizza, nice staff. Prices ok. Salads are a little small and expensive for what they are. But can't go wrong with the pizza. Some of better pizza in area, not too big, thin, well seasoned and flavorful.

Casual place with quasi communal seating, but is very manageable. Can be crowded at peak times. Worth checking out! Enjoy
Good food, great service ( Joe it was our server ) drinks good, stop by a great place for friends and to bring your love one alone...

What?  This  place is amazing  and I live in county and drive in  just for the breaded cod sandwich.  The chili  mac and burgers are awesome.The portions and prices cant be beat--I wish there was a one out in the county.  Yes, the place is busy...because its good.  My waiter was as nice as can be, even  at his busiest.  *remember  to tip graciously...most of the staff appear to be young and tips are their livelihood ; )
Went here last night for the 1st time and loved it ! AMAZING customer service.  Walked out with a smile! Will for sure be back here! Please support this local business !

Had a surf lesson today for my 11 year old twins and their friend, Chris Keet owner.  He was terrific, kids attended surf camp last year (5 days) and said they learned nothing compared to what they learned in two hours from Chris.  He was funny, validating and informative!  I would love to come back to one of his camps! What a great guy and my kids are happily surfing!

He also loaned us his fabulous camera, I have 343 pictures of my kids surfing PRICELESS!

BORING. 

The food was ok  - jazz band was cool. 

Steamboats are lovely but this was not a highlight. It was too long (stayed in dock for first hour) and food is generic. New Orleans is so fun. This fell flat.

Sparkling clean, quiet and lovely atmosphere, good pour on drinks, food perfectly done, consistent menu with fish, pasta, meat...soup, my potato was perfect.
For a neighborhood place very low key upscale w/o pretense.

Love the food! Black spaghetti is amazing! Been to this location four times now.  Friday nights they are super packed and the service needed improvement. I have been multiple times during happy hour and our waitress Sarah was amazing! She knows the all the dishes and will help with selections.  You can tell that she really loves working there because she describes the dishes perfectly!

I've eaten here many many many times and sometimes the food is better than other times.

but.

two words: FRIED CHICKEN.  

eat this here and you will never go wrong.  It's crispy and tender and juicy and pretty much perfect. You can get it with side of red beans and rice or collard or mustard greens.  All meals come with corn bread.

Some other of my personal favorites: 
the fried catfish
the fried pickles ($5 gets you a heaping mound)
bread pudding
red beans and rice
collard or mustard greens

don't forget the FRIED CHICKEN!

FRIED
CHICKEN

(repeat for emphasis)

DO NOT BUY ANYTHING THERE
My wife bought garden tools and she didn't like them so I went to return them, apparently when the guy heard I want to return something he become all red.
I didn't have receipt but it said ACE on tools , they wouldn't even give a store credit.
Unproffesional and dilettante behavior.
Be warned.
Not a bad place. Salad bar is great and burgers are good too, all the other stuff is just OK. Dinner is a bit pricey for the quality of food.

I came here to have my hair done in an updo for a wedding.  Kadi was very nice and she did an amazing job with my long, thick, and typically unmanageable curly hair.  The facility itself has a great design with high ceilings and it was a pretty relaxing environment.  I don't do the salon thing very often but the price for what I had done was pretty comparable to what I saw advertised at other places in Manayunk.

What a great place! Natural soaps and sponges. All handmade. People were so friendly and helpful. Genuinely friendly. I would put off shopping in the "souther beach area" until you check this place out.

The Blu Fig is home to some great Mediterranean grub but has an odd set up. 

Pro: Blu Fig is home to probably the friendliest staff of any Mediterranean restaurant I've been to. 

Pro: A couple of Vegetarian options available, including homemade falafel. 

Pro: They have fruit tea! One of my favorite things about Nashville. 

Con: The overall set up and flow of the place was weird. We were half-way waited on and half-way on our own. You place your order at the register but then don't pay until you're done dinning. 

Con: There isn't much sitting room inside (will probably be difficult during the winter months to find a spot to sit).


Overall though, it was good enough that I would go back. The falafel alone was worth the trip there. Obed, the manager there, was extremely talkative and eager to share with you how the Blu Fig is different than other Mediterranean restaurants.
Best Italian in SB.  Warm atmosphere and great staff!  One of the only restaurants in the area with outside seating on State St.  A must try.

I had my small 1960 master bath updated with PermaCeram in March in lieu of a gut rehab I couldn't afford.  I updated my toilet, vanity, and fixtures on my own and had Myron and Co. glaze the tub and blue/black tile walls (all four).  Additionally, I had the old soap holders on both the tub and sink upgraded to something more modern and a shelf installed in the bath.
