She fielded phone calls from us late at night, on the weekends, and even while on vacation. As settlement approached, she guided us through the inspection and mortgage process. Throughout everything, she was professional, knowledgeable and friendly. If I buy another house, I would absolutely use Liz agai n. She is the best!

Had a great time tonight ! First time trying pole dancing for fitness and wow I think it's so fun ... Make you work those muscles not easy if you have not used these muscles in a while !!! But definitely will make your whole body tone up !
The teacher was very knowledgeable and super fun ! 
This would be a fun class to take with your sister or friends 
Lots of parking and good location 
Nice facility

Elaine is the best! She helped us with our wedding order, and even went to the extent of taking my call after she left work so I could place my order in time.  During the planning, Elaine gave me honest feedback that I was ordering way too much.  I ended up thinking I knew better :-P and only still ordered more than recommended...and Elaine was right.  We had plenty more than we needed.  BevMo was great to worked with, especially with the perk of them delivering for free on our order.

Went here last night after a concert for the first time hoping to use a coupon I had gotten for $1 off any yogurt creation over $3.75. As frozen yogurt is usually kind of expensive, especially when they charge by the ounce like Sweet Alley does, I thought this would be easy to do, but alas, even with gobs of froyo and toppings I only reached $3.15. Dagnabit. Well, let this serve as a testimony to how cheap Sweet Alley is; but don't think its cheapness means it isn't delicious! 

This was by far the best froyo place I've been to in the SB/IV/Goleta area. There are plenty of interesting flavors to choose from in the froyo (Red Velvet Cake, Green Apple, etc.) that are all either low fat or non fat. For those wanting actual ice cream, you can get a scoop of McConnell's Ice Cream instead. There are many great toppings ranging from fresh fruit, nuts, candy pieces, cereal, and different syrups (yay for Reese's syrup!). If you aren't satisfied with even that, there is a wide selection of bin candy to buy from. 

I didn't give the full 5 stars for two reasons: not very many places to sit inside, and the orange couches that were there were a little dingy. Also, the woman who rang me up was kind of rude (although maybe she was annoyed because I had used my sample cup to sample almost EVERY flavor teehee) and asked me "What do you want?" when I just wanted a napkin, Geez Louise. 

Would come back again...probably in two weeks!

Kitchen K was a nearby lunch option when in St. Louis on business.  I'm used to having a range of options for lunch being from DC, but this seemed to be "it" aside from an Irish pub and deli on the street.

The menu had lots of choices but nothing out of the ordinary.  I settled for the roast beef au jus and was satisfied.  Nothing out of the ordinary.  Others in my lunch party were satisfied just the same with their mahi sandwich and the pasta special, but not extraordinarily.

The decor is nice and I would imagine this place is more happening at night.

Not a bad place to see a game.  We bought our tickets kind of last minute so we had to sit one row from top in the nosebleed section but we still had a nice view.  Maybe this was because we were in the "cheap" seats but a lot of the folks near us were pretty rednecky with colorful vocabularies so it was "educational" for my 9-year old to say the least.  Perhaps it would have been different if it were a game the Preds played well in and weren't drawing so much ire from the local faithful.

Otherwise, I thought the arena was laid out fine and it's in a convenient location to all the downtown attractions.   Also, check out the specials they're offering before you go.  I met up with a friend there who had bought two lower bowl tickets, two hot dogs, two drinks, and a car flag for $99. That's a steal.

Burger Up was more like Burger Ok.  I like the atmosphere and the service, but I wasn't amazed by the food, it was ok at best.  

The atmosphere is rustic/modern.  I love the big huge chalkboard talking about what farms they source for food.  Very cool in my book.  The service was great.  The hostess was awesome with her greeting and our server Leah was pretty nice.

Now the food could use a little improvement.  I got the black bean and quinoa burger with the sweet potato fries.  The fries were soggy and at a lukewarm temperature.  My friend's truffle fries were of the same quality as far as temperature and texture go.  The burger was also a little on the lukewarm side too, not hot at all.  My friends did not oh and awe over their burgers either.  

I might be back for lunch at the least, but as for now, not my top choice.

We visit New Orleans often, as we have family living there and I am a member of a number of Carnival organizations.  This trip we chose Mr. B's over Commander's Palace because we were going to be in the French Quarter for Dirty Linen Night.  First time at Mr. B's.  

The first indication of trouble came from the attitude of the hostess when our party of 6 arrived.  Just a "come with me".  

Our server was adequate but not particularly well-trained. We were not made to feel particularly welcome.   Our drinks took 20 minutes to arrive.  After 40 minutes, we had to ask for bread.

While I enjoy lingering over drinks and a meal, the 2 1/2 hours required for our meal was too much.  And although I understand the concept of a team of servers, after about 1 1/2 hours our original server vanished without a word, handing us over to others .  I must say that the last server of the evening was really wonderful.

The food was good.  But the inattentive and indifferent treatment at the hands of the hostess and our original server put a damper on the meal.

Really, there are too many wonderful restaurants in New Orleans to put up with this one.  We will not be returning.
This place is delicious! My only complain is that they take an extremely long time to take orders, so don't go hungry. The food is really fresh and has a great variety for breakfast.

Let me start out by saying the food was excellent.  The restaurant has only been open for five weeks and has some kinks to work out. The have a very good looking seafood and meat menu and the food we had thus evening was very very good.  There was a huge problem with the waitress.  Took forever to even place a drink order and then once we recieved our wine she asked us what we would like.  Problem is we had not been given menus. Once we did order and recieved our food my wifes order of salmon came out as red snapper. The owner came over to our table and couldn't have been nicer. He apologized profusely and admitted to a problem with our server that he was going to address at the close of business. The owner made things right for us and was much appreciated. We will definitely return because of the quality of the food and the plesantness of the restaurant.  We appreciate the owner taking care of us and realize it will take some time to get the place running the way he wants.

Good wine; wonderful service; shockingly good pizza (I.e. flatbread). One of the most beautiful gardens of any place in town, w a towering tulip tree providing a canopy over a cozy space with/ a few tables and music piped in. 

Prices VERY fair. This place is such a surprising find. I feel lucky to have happened upon it.

Ahh... the smell of a bookstore!  This place is small and parking can be a challenge, but it does have a good selection of books and often has good authors who come to do signings. Also has autographed copies of books. 

You'll pay full price for these books (it's not exactly Amazon), but the staff are friendly and I love to buy books there so I have a bookstore in which to roam!
Love this place! Veggie friendly and affordable. Staff is always prompt & they take cards which is a major plus

The coffee in seven words: Mmmm, mm, yum, nice, yum, delicious, mmmmmmmmmmm.

The service: Down home and sweet. I'd call it neighborhoodly, especially for being in a hotel and on an otherwise desolate block.

The locals: Enough of them to enhance the homey feel

The food offerings: Non-existent. Don't let those dry, too-sweet muffins tempt you.

First impression not worth the hype of reviews. Waited for about 10minutes after I was seated before anyone came to even offer me a drink. Only person that did was the bartender. The tables on either side of me were served, but I was ignored. Bartender, she was very nice and attentive.
Food is meh. Not worth the prices

Okay, so its a public library.  And all public libraries are wonderful, simply because they are public libraries.  This branch of the Belleville Public Library, however, is less wonderful than the numerous other public libraries I have been to.  

I was happy to be allowed to use their computers while traveling from out of the area.. I was not happy though to be asked to share the 15 minutes the curt, male librarian gave us (locals get 30-60 minutes) on the computer terminal that my boyfriend was using, especially because there were other open terminals.  Their computers were incredibly slow.. running Windows 98, are you? Yes... but at least we could (s l o w l y) make use of the internet.  

In addition to plentiful slow computers, they also have two floors full of books and other good things in an air conditioned building right off the main drag.  And the bathrooms in the lobby are locked for my safety.  Woot.
Excellent everything!   We were there in December.  One day during our trip we ate breakfast and lunch here.  Charbroiled oysters!!!!

Great place to eat, and even better if you are a dog lover. They are extremely dog friendly. Wonderful breakfast selection and specials - like their fried green tomatoes BLT Sandwich & Cheese grits. Or, just their Southern Breakfast.

I don't always give four stars and it's rare that I get 5 but this restaurant had a great burger great fries and I believe the owner was the one that helped me because he was really really nice very professional definitely would come again.

Super delicious Ukranian restaurant! This was my first introduction to the cuisine.

I Had sausage, pierogi, cheese crepes and cabbage rolls (sweet and sour, both varieties) and would recommend this place to anyone! It was fantastic
Convenient location to French Quarter. Clean, spacious rooms. It's located in a building with shops, restaurants and a liquor store.

I have never had Thai food before and really wanted to try it and this place had good reviews so I tried and my god was it ever delicious!!! The portions are perfect, staff is very friendly they treat you like your a regular. I will definitely come back and highly recommend this place!! It's in a sketchy area and you have to park in the back alley and enter through the back door (which made me a little skeptical but the food totally made up for it) :) I had the peanut curry and it was soooo good!!
Wonderful find! Fantastic spinach salad and although a half is not on the menu- they added a half spinach alas to my meal !

Fun bar to drink beer in. Nice selection of drafts and bottles. They have das boot if you want to channel your inner Beerfest moment. They have have a special on Jager Bombs. They have live music which to me makes a bar even better.

I would give this 6 stars if I could. Where to begin?

The BRUNCH is off the hook, same price as Jeannine's but you're eating in an art museum with French tapestries, elegant flatware, beauty in every corner of the room. 

I don't know how ANYONE could give this less than 5 stars. Now, at dinner it's apparently pricey. Duh. This is a fine dining institution in Santa Barbara and it's French with a star LA chef and the owners spared no expense in the remodeling of the casual, not divey but not nice, State and A which managed to stay in business a couple decades in spite of the subpar food. 

It turns out the owners have grown daughters in NYC and I have so enjoyed my afternoon here. My iPhone 5 makes a hotspot so I'm blogging before I meet a friend at 4 and swim to work off the potato daphinois--don't ask about the fat content--a sinful tower of thinly sliced potatoes with cheese and oil and all manner of terrible things which taste wonderful. 

My scramble--a bargain at 12.95--included perfect carmelized onions, roasted peppers, spinach and a hint of goat cheese--and I will dream of this till my next brunch here after Chicago/Michigan trip. 

After 5 cups of coffee to wake me up from horrible asthmatic night, I had a glass of the Ballard Pinot for dessert Nice but no better than the cheaper--9/glass--Kenwood Cab which I think is quite a respectable Cab for the money. 

The coffee is good but if you're like my father who, due to his time in the military, requires coffee which scalds the tongue, you will need to pull a Dad and ask them to nuke it in the "radar oven." It's not hot but I don't really care as it tasted good and did the trick: that is, it enabled me to have two glasses of wine after a miserable night of wheezing, hacking and blowing my nose. 

I cannot say enough for Maggie's and am so happy it's here in SB. I will come before my next show at the Granada for dinner at the bar. I have a subscription (see Yelp) and come alone.

PS I haven't eaten here at dinner yet but every single person who brought me food or booze was fabulous and I got to chat at length with the spectacular, smart owner with whom it turns out I have quite a bit culturally in common. I have no clue what people are talking about re service. It's not crowded but it's not empty and they have taken magnificent care of me.
You can customize your guacamole. You have many choices of add ins. We added roasted garlic and tomato and crab. Muy muy bueno. Oh and the margaritas were perfect.

Note: the location of this food truck is next to the Thornton's gas station parking lot. Just drive up along Armenia and you should see the red truck tucked behind a small make shift white fence. I ordered the 4 tacos for $8 special, all dressed with raw onions and cilantro. The tacos were al pastor, steak, chorizo and fish. They were all tasty and freshly made (the fish tasted especially fresh; it didn't have the typical bland, watery taste of defrosted frozen fish). My wife, though, said all the tacos were too salty, except for the al pastor, which is normally sweeter than most fillings due to the pineapple. Our table mates, who were Mexican, said the red ceviche was most delicious. The lemonade was not "freshly made/squeezed" as the sign suggested. All in all, a solid place to try. The service was quick and friendly.
So thankful for Target.  Trips to this store are pleasing.  I know what I want, I know what I need and I'm in and out and home in time for dinner!  Great prices with great customer service.
This place is amazing! The fish is so fresh and their rolls aren't full of rice like most places. AND they have my favorite thing, hamachi kama! So good!!

I would never eat at this place if I was looking for good middle eastern food in New Orleans, BUT when looking for something to eat on Bourbon St. I would totally go again!  This is so much better than the tourist traps and the pizza places!  Great food considering the location!

This is our favorite mexican food (fast food or sit down).  the variety of food is plentiful (yum...cabeza tacos) and they have a condiment bar that is clean and flavorful.  This place beats its closest competitor, El Guero Canelo.

My family recently moved to Florida and we see these places all over the area so we thought we would give it a try. My wife and I went to watch UFC 156. We got there early and even though the place was still pretty empty we were seated near the door. This would not normally be an issue but it was a cold night and the waitresses kept holding the doors open to talk with the people outside allowing all the cold air and smoke to flow to our table.
As for the food it was mediocre. My wife ordered wings and informed me that they were nothing special. I ordered a chicken quesadilla and it was awful. It was just plain unseasoned chicken with cheese, definitely not worth $8. However, the drinks were strong which was surprising.
The service was not great either. Our waitress, Deborah, was unfriendly and not very attentive often passing us by multiple times without noticing our drinks were gone. There are definitely much better places to get wings and watch a fight or a game in the area.

I want breakfast ! 
I'll be stopping here for breakfast from now on.
The atmosphere was relaxed,clean and very quiet for a Sunday morning.
The food was very good plus the portions were insane.
Service was a little slow but the yelp app/Facebook solves that problem

Our hotel set us up with one of their cabs to get to the airport. It smelled horribly of alcohol, there was a drive thru smoothie cup in his cup holder, and he was on and off the phone with someone discussing how many drinks they've had and where they were going to watch the Saints game. We ignored it, we had a plane to catch. 

Realizing that what should have been a 20 minute ride was going on one hour and a half, my bf suggested a route that was a lot quicker on the GPS and he went off. He said he was from New Orleans and knew his way, that we had attitudes and called the same person on the phone to discuss it, said he had places to be, traffic wasn't his fault, etc. By the time we got there, we missed our flight. We're still stuck here a day later. 

We called customer service the next day to complain. All we wanted was a refund for the ride, all other experiences resulting from it we would handle separately, but they said he still got us there- so should we have gotten out the cab in the middle of nowhere then? The taxi is independently owned and all expenses go through the bureau. Conveniently it is closed on weekends. Had we had known it would be such an ordeal we shouldn't have paid at all. But we also did not have time to spare arguing either. 

If you allow drivers like these to drive your cab (regardless of independency), and choose not to help, your company will look bad.

I'm from Orlando so the only reason I found my way here was because of Yelp. Wanted to get some eats before hitting the Dali museum and was not disappointed by the brunch experience here. My girlfriend had a mimosa with her shrimp and grits and I opted for the crab cake Benedict. Both were excellent but the shrimp and grits were on another level. The man in the kitchen came out to ask us what we thought and he shared some of the ingredients with us which was pretty neat. 

Unfortunately we weren't able to try their highly recommended bread pudding but that just gives us a reason to come back. The place was empty while we ate but I'm going to chalk that up to it being barely passed noon on a Saturday. The bar was stocked and we were watching them make all their stuff fresh; cutting fruit, making sour mix. 

All in all, a must try while in St. Pete.

This place was ok. I like how they offer you something to drink and the music is spa like. Prices seem a bit extreme for the establishment. $2 charge to use a credit card is ridiculous. They have a variety of colors. It can get a little hectic since they are busy. I was not overly impressed as some of the reviews say.

decent thia food plus if you go during happy hour you can save some money

Avoid the dessert it was way too expensive for the serving they give you
I'm a coffee lover and this place has the BEST LATTE ever!!!! We had hot latte and my boyfriend had iced vanilla latte. He likes his vanilla latte and I LOVED my hot latte!

I tried here. I really, really tried to give them a chance but alas, this review HAS to be updated.

Little Caesars of Roslyn, you continue to disappointed me.

I'll start with what is positive: price and location. I can walk to your store. The $5 hot and ready is SUPER convenient for me to grab on my way to a girlfriend's house. That is, when you actually have them. Twice now, there were no pizzas "hot and ready".

I will tell you what your number one problem is and what is holding this business back: Employees.

Every time I go in there, I see a new face. I understand that the average age may be teenager and I don't disparage that. Hey, I washed dishes at that age too. However, these children are not properly trained; especially on the phone. They have zero communication skills.

For example, I called yesterday (12/04/16) around noon for a pizza. I gave the girl my order and the conversation had come to a natural close. I said "Ok, thank you". *CLICK* She hung up. No "thank you, goodbye, thanks for calling, etc". Nothing. Just a click. It was rude. Even the Greeks that don't speak perfect English across the street say "thank you, goodbye". It is just common courtesy (or at least it should be).

The other indecent I had was a few months ago. I kept calling and calling to place an order and all I got was a busy signal. This went on for over 15 minutes so I figured I'll just walk over there. I tell the girl behind the counter that I've been trying to call and their line is busy. There was no one else in the store. She tells me "Uh...we are busy". I was immediately suspicious. "Really?" I ask. "Is this your number?" I show the number of the pizzeria saved in my phone. She confirms it. I dial and put it on speakerphone. Busy signal. "Why isn't your landline ringing right now?" I ask. She just smiles and asks if I would like to order. 

This tells me either they took the phone off the hook or someone else working (not working?) there was using the phone out of my sight. I didn't see anyone else but the girl behind the counter.

There was a "Help Wanted" sign up yesterday when I went to pick up my pizza. I agree that this place does need some serious staffing help or else they aren't going to make it. This is a shame because once you get past the lousy employees, and wait, the pizza itself is good. But with the volume of turnover, the hassle with ordering, and inconsistent pizza-ready times I'm going to have to go somewhere else in the neighborhood. Luckily in my previous review, I listed how many there are in the neighborhood so we will not be without pizza.

Good luck, L.C. on getting some new, quality, staff members in there.

Li'l Dizzy's has all the hallmarks of a New Orleans must-try- really popular, great reviews, covered in cool art and visited or acknowledged by multiple presidents and other celebrities. I have no idea why. Service was terrible- they'd snap at us and were generally extremely slow. The food was pretty bad too. I got a po' boy and it barely had any meat in it and tasted bland. It's pretty hard to screw up a po' boy. Everyone else with me got eggs with grits which were pretty bland as well, and getting the waitress to bring us our toast was like pulling teeth.Their bread pudding was a gelatinous mess produced from some kind of banana flavor mix. I don't write many reviews but I felt pretty passionate about this one; I would avoid.
I ordered sushi roll with edamame as appertizer. I think the food is just a little bit average and price is not too high. Nothing really special about this place.

Many thanks to Dr. Brogan, Karen and their whole St. Mary's hospice team.  Our loved one received exceptional care by each and every care giver.  My family has used Saint Mary's Hospice on two occasions and I can recommend them without reservation.

Loved it for Sunday brunch, dinner was hit or miss at our table.

Wasn't impressed with the crawfish bisque, and some entrees can be pretty rich, a la the redfish court boullion. 

The craft beers are great, oysters (at least the ones we had) were small and not very impressive. Don't know if this is temporary considering the hit the oyster fishermen took, but we'll see.

I'd say all in all it was a nice dinner, but no real show stoppers. At least on this visit.

Atmosphere - 5 Stars
Very clean environment with simple, yet elegant historic pieces. Very laid back staff. 

Food - 5 Stars
I had the Steak and Egg Sandwich. It was an interesting list of ingredients that all complimented each other well. Arugula folded eggs with jalapeño jam, shaved tri tip all on a cheesy croissant with a side of potatoes. I also had the pumpkin cronought (croissant crossed with a doughnut). 

Drinks - 5 Stars
I had a Maya Tea (Green Sencha Rose) from the beloved local tea favorite Maya Tea Company while my wife enjoyed the exceptional EXO roasters drip coffee. For a drip coffee, it was great!

Price - 4 Stars
It was very fairly priced with exception to the doughnut. $4 is a little stiff for a pastry.

I went on a Friday around 7pm. I was impressed by the cleanliness and friendly staff. The ambiance is great and it is decorated classy, yet has a casual feel as it sits right on Bourbon  street. I would recommend  getting a table by the large open doors if you like to people watch. I ordered the Catfish Latiffe  and was very impressed. It was flavorful and worth every penny!

Keep St Pete local and check out this amazing shop! The groomers did a beautiful job on my long haired dachshund. My dog isn't the easiest dog to groom either. I'm very satisfied with my experience at One Lucky Dog. 
After having a bad experience at a different groomers off 4th St I was hesitant about having my dog groomed. One lucky dog made all my worries go away with the friendly staff and open grooming salon where the company doesn't try to hide the dogs. 
Fun boutique as well the custom ordered me a leash that arrived within a few days.
We tried the tequeños, empanadas, cachapa and pabellon. Everything was really good. The pabellon is big, but yummy. Nice people and nice place.

While the price (early bird, non-VIP) is good if you consider all of the restaurants, wineries, and distilleries you get to sample, the setting made this event less than stellar.

While I understand the needs of the benefit...to give more students the chance to attend NSCC, the use of space was very poorly managed. Myself and my fiancé attended, being foodies and noting that some of our favorite restaurants would be there. The venue was so crowded and tortuous, having so many different hallways, that it was really hard to figure out where you had and hadn't been.

The food was pretty ok (although a ton of sweets), but because there was so little space and so many bodies, it made every tasting feel rushed. We would essentially stuff our face with whatever, then move out of the way so as to not block those waiting behind us to sample stuff. While I guess we could've took our time at each vendor, I think we would have felt really rude and like we were holding up the line. We won't be coming back next year, unless they move it to a spot with some more elbow room or maybe some areas to sit down, and larger plates so you could get multiple samples; sit, rinse, repeat.

first time at Hendricks. I ordered the pulled pork, wife had the chicken and the kids had their kids meal. The meals are very generous in portion size. The pulled pork was good and the signature sauces were good as well. Wife and kids loved their meals. The atmosphere was great and service was good. Will eat there again and try other items on the menu. I would say this place is almost equal with sugar fire with a better atmosphere.

I arrived to a line of about 20 people waiting on cars. No cars were in sight. I am Emerald Club member and there were no cars in the Emerald Club section or any other. I was told they overbooked. After about a 40 minute wait I had a car, unfortunately I had to cancel a meeting and reschedule it for a future date.

In my travels the St. Louis National and the San Antonio National locations seem to be constantly overbooked and the cars are regularly dirty.

For perspective I travel 3 weeks out of the month and almost exclusively use National so I visit a substantial amount of their locations.

So glad we stumbled into this breakfast place that was a block from where we were staying.   Everything about it was great... location, ambiance, wait staff, and, oh..the food!  OK, so we had to wait a bit for a table, though it was worth it.  My friend was head-over-heals for the Savory bread pudding.  For me, it was the OMG worthy crawfish etouffee, served on top of grits.  Did I say OMG yet?   Really good coffee, and very friendly staff working there.  One warning, when they are busy as heck, service can be slow.  Go with patience, and all will be fine.

I LOVE THE WAFFLE HOUSE.

The staff is soo friendly, always calling you "sugar" or "honey".  I had the cheesy eggs which were amazing and the buttery grits.  Oh yum!  We shared the classic waffle which is always made from scratch and so warm and fresh.  Simple food prepared with love and care.  

A must for any road trip!!

Ok.  Normally I give very long and flowey reviews with lots of details but with Milktooth that crap ain't necessary.  Just get here.  Get your mind blown.

[drops mic]

Groupon helped me afford this place.

Baked eggplant was excellent but the steak failed badly. It was pretty much uncooked. Perhaps it could pass as rare but it was one hundred percent red and had the consistency of tuna tartare. I even asked for it well done. Aside from the terrible steak, the polenta on the side at least was great and I asked for a many a refill on bread to compensate for my loss. 

As far as other things go, the service was great, but the seating was a bit cramped. Avoid getting seated in the middle tables as you will pretty much have no privacy.

I've been using R & N for many years, Rob is great to work with and very professional.  He does excellent work and always make sure he leaves the place spotless when the work is complete.  Always arrives on time and finishes the job in a timely manner.  I highly recommend him to anyone needing flooring work.

As breweries go, this place is well set up. Great porch and a nice interior with views of the brewing area.  The music is good to listen to in some spots, but in others (like parts of the upstairs) the sound can get a little distorted. 

Beers are passable and there's generally a decent selection.  They're not going to win any major awards but by Nashville standards they at least brew clean beers.  Thankfully they don't offer a bakers dozen of "IPAs" and have some imagination when it comes to their recipes.  That said, I'd stick to their more hoppy beers and maybe their dark beers. Their more lightly hopped beers are their most drab, and I suspect the pressurized mash filter system they use is primarily to blame--it literally wrings out all the sugars from the grain thereby allowing them to use less grain per batch of beer (so malt *flavor* is lacking). 

So 4.0 stars for the brewery venue, 3.0 stars for their beers..

This used to be one of my favorite restaurant chains to eat at. The last three experiences left something to be desired.  The first of the three, the manager decided to hold a meeting with the wait staff and left us sitting for 25 minutes waiting for our waitress to take our order. She was so upset and flustered by the time the manager released her to do her job.  The second and third time, there were problems with the food.  The sticky toffee dessert had PAPER still on it.  The skinny fries were so hard they were inedible and would break.  I think they have cut costs recently and it hasn't done the restaurant any favors. I don't think I'll be back.

I took my mom here to see Frankenstein last night.  We enjoyed it.  They were great entertainers.  It was funny and they sounded good.  There was food there, too. So that was a plus.  I was surprised they did another small show after which was about Las Vegas.  If I ever come to Tucson in the future I will go back to this place again.

This used to be one of our "go to" places for reasonably priced, good dinners but yesterday and our previous visit before have changed our minds.  I guess the almost empty parking lot should have been the warning....our server was very nice but the food was just okay (my crabmeat tasted like it came out of a can ), not reasonably priced and they ran out of Australian beer before we got there (at 6pm)...
The cocktails are absolutely perfect with the entrees. Amazing flavor combinations and reasonably priced. This was our first time but definitely not our last. Our server Kara was wonderful.

Worth the drive from Orlando to Hudson. From the moment you walk in they make you feel so welcome!
We saw opening night "Give My Regards To Broadway" and the show was fabulous.

The buffet was a good typical small buffet and they have a full bar. Staff and owners take care to make sure you're having a great time. 
 
I've taken my 19 and 13 year old granddaughters to plays and they couldn't believe how much they actually enjoy live theater.  Unplug, take your family,  support the arts and you'll have an awesome evening! 
I would highly recommend the Show Palace to all ages.

My boyfriend brought me here for brunch on Easter Sunday. It was a bit difficult to find since it's not view-able from the main street. Atmosphere is quiet and nice with a small town neighborly feel even though the view is of a parking lot. They have indoor and outdoor seating. 
  
       Our food was delicious, I ordered the breakfast burger(done to your liking) which was on a thick slice of French toast topped w cheese, their caramelized peppered bacon, a fried egg(or however you want it) with maple syrup!!!  My bf got the Kennet mushroom omelette and it came w house potatoes, which were red skin potatoes (my fave!) and was so delicious didn't need salt or pepper as if it was seasoned w/ the ingredients in the omelet already. And we split a fruit platter which I was impressed the fruit was all fresh not a bruise and presented very nicely: it had cut up strawberries, blueberries and raspberries, sliced bananas, apple, pear & a beautifully sliced orange.

         Everything was great including police service who refilled our drinks many times. The best part about this place for me was the BACON: It was AMAZINGGGGGGGGGGGGGG!!! I can't wait to come back I think I will just order 2 orders of bacon just for myself.  We also received a little card advertising their dinner so we can't wait to try that! Oh....its BYOB!!!!

We are still waiting for our pictures to come back, but pending those, I couldn't wait to say how awesome Jump On The School Bus is.  We used the service for our wedding to transport guests from downtown Santa Barbara to Glen Annie Golf Club in Goleta.  Throughout the entire process, Darin and Sierra are just awesome people.  They are truly one of a kind and I wish I had words that adequately encompassed how sincere and rad they are.

They made planning fun and arranging the schedule with them was easy.  Darin and Sierra provided guidance where and when I needed it.  They also offered to pick up the wedding party separately from guests early - I can't say what a blessing that was to us.  On the day of our wedding, they had a text message chain with some of the wedding party to keep everyone posted.  Well organized and well orchestrated with so little stress involved.

The buses were fun, amped with music and lights, and clean.  Of all the wonderful things from our wedding weekend in Santa Barbara, we will always remember Jump On The School Bus as one of the best memories and investments.  If you are having any sort of event, I recommend getting to know Darin, Sierra, and their lovely chariot.

We made the biggest Valentine's faux pas which is, deciding last minute to go out for Valentine's Day. Luckily thanks to the Open Table app, we were able to secure a reservation Saturday night for a peak hour seating. The restaurant doesn't look like much from the outside as it is housed in a large, commercial style building, but the inside is fresh, brightly lit and minimally decorated. 
I award three stars for the experience, as service was friendly, accommodating, timely and food was executed to the best of their ability. Where I found it lacking, was taste and temperature, general atmosphere. Too picky?
We ordered the Blue Crab Dip with Parmesan Cream for our first course, second the Cream of Mushroom Soup and Complimentary Salad for the Special Entree, and Entrees were Eggplant Vincent and the Fish of the Day, Redfish, served whole with potatoes and vegetable of the day. 
The soup was served first, and was under seasoned and not very hot. Crab Dip came next and though gooey, bubbly and tasty, was slightly overshadowed by the pools of oil on top. 
The entrees were also good, my boyfriend loved the simplicity of his fish and it was cooked correctly. My Eggplant Vincent was  a cup of eggplant breaded and fried and stuffed with crab and shrimp, served over a butter cream sauce and angel hair. Again, slightly under seasoned, but over all a good, tasty dish.
Overall, not my pick for a romantic evening or food to write home about, but suitable for an affordable, seafood orientated craving.
Wonderful service.  Expansive menu.  Great atmosphere.  Pasta and fish very good. Great dessert cart.

City Limits is a cute little place with some healthy vegetarian options. This place offers sandwiches, salads, and a full espresso bar. However they seem to be trying way too hard to be trendy. But they are definitely better than Bread & Co.

Wow, found this place looking for brunch near Rittenhouse Square. The staff are friendly, the coffee amazing.  My friend mentioned their popcorn and we found out that they only serve it at lunch. I am from Massachusetts, so I won't be able to come back, but they brought some popcorn out!!! And the smoked salmon eggs Benedict were delicious!

4 meals, 3 gluten free, could not have been better! $1 mimosas!!  Glad this jewel is my special brunch place with no line but boy are you missing out!  I had the tostada with seared tuna and it was incredible!  We each had a different dish and every one was fantastically executed with really fresh ingredients.  Kudos, Santa Fe!

We chose From the Heart to come out and assess our 8 year old shar-pei whom we suspected had been bitten by another dog. Our dog is nervous in new environments and her current vet was out of town. 
We were so pleased with the treatment our dog received. The doctor was very gentle with her, and reassured my obvious nervousness. 

The doctor's exam was thorough and her treatment was respectful and loving to the animal. Her vet tech was awesome too. They genuinely cared for our dog and made that mobile fee worth it!!

Only con is that it is double a regular vet visit, but in a case where our dog would have been further traumatized, it was worth it. My husband didn't care for her curt attitude when he inquired about the dog's well-being, but she was so good with the dog, I didn't care and chalked it up to being distracted ;) 

Highly recommend!
LOVE le rendezvous! Such a great little gem in Tucson. Best escargot around! Also! They have EXCELLENT beef Wellington. My favorite.

Their customer service SUCKS. I seriously hate coming here but I like their ice cream too much. It's either them or go get a McFlurry. It's like a bunch of 16 year old run the place and they take their sweet time doing anything. Be prepared to wait forever to place an order because they are too busy worrying about who made homecoming court . OH they also close early even when you showed up 15 mins before they're supposed to. But don't worry because you might be lucky to get melted vanilla ice cream thrown at you just Incase you already didn't feel like an inconvenience.

After hearing a lot of hype over Bailey's Range from my friends, I decided to check it out for dinner one weekend with my girlfriend and her friends. I went in with high expectations, but was left just feeling "meh" at the end of the meal.

I ordered one of the burgers they were featuring for the week as a part of their "Burger Battles;" a turkey burger with a Korean twist. Right off the bat, I was disappointed that fries did not come with the burger and cost extra. Fine, whatever, I ordered some. When my meal came, it was a let down by all accounts. Both the bread and the burger were charred which gave every bite a bitter charcoal taste. The fries were limp and soggy, as if they were neglected at the pass.

The only upside was the desserts. We shared a strawberry sorbet and a pistachio / cookies & cream in a waffle bowl. Both were amazing. The sorbet was tangy and tasted of real fruit. The ice cream was creamy and rich on top of a freshly made waffle bowl (still warm!).

I will definitely come back in the future for their desserts, but their burgers leave much to be desired...

I was recently shopping in Pier One springfield for outdoor furniture and accessories. The staff was very helpful and friendly. One of the managers Trish was just great. She even helped me pull together some color schemes that I loved. I've been shopping here for years because I always have a great experience and their merchandise is just beautiful and unique. Go there! The spring collection is coming in and its gorgeous:)
Ridiculous ... the place is awful food that preys on poor college students nearby... anyone with a car and yelp ... go elsewhere.

I am not sure what to rate this place since the two times I ate there were vastly different.

1st visit:: 5 stars!  Ordered the vegan pulled pork with sweet potato fries and a side of mac & cheese.  Everything was delicious.  I was surprised how good the pulled pork was since I still cannot understand how seitan can be prepared to resemble pulled pork.  Delicious!

2nd visit: 2 stars.  Vegan fried chicken sandwich, seitan sausage sandwich, sweet potato fries and mac & cheese.  The sides were delicious just like the first time, but something was off with both of the sandwiches.  My BF thinks they were old, which is entirely possible since we were both in gastrointestinal hell shortly after our meal.  

Overall, if I were ever in Philly again I would definitely get that vegan pulled pork.  The best part: sweet potato creme brulee.   Straight up heaven in my mouth.

Great great great brunch at Jones.

I recommend the monkey bread (to be split among the table) and the chicken and waffles! The bloody mary bar offers a build your own bloody mary experience where you can order a bloody mary exactly the way you are feeling it that morning. 

On the weekends you may have to wait a bit to get a table.

Went there today to get a bagel and it said they closed at 3. It was around 1:50 and the door was locked and the girl working there was in there sweeping. An hour and ten minutes before closing you have the door locked and are cleaning up?? Called twice and she answered and said "sorry, were out of bagels" ???? When I went up to the door I saw several bagels on the rack.... idk if I'll be coming back

Great appetizers, pizza, dessert and service.  In the moment, I felt like I was dining at the best restaurant in America.  The fried artichokes with lemon yogurt were unique and delicious. The spinach pizza with garlic and balsalmic onions was unlike any pie I've ever eaten.  The smoky, puffy, crisp crust was sooo good.  The zeppole for desert ruined any fond memories of amusement park funnel cake forever.  Can't wait to return!

Two good things: price of 18 for gel polish and the girl had warm hands. 

Went here based on Yelp but are my experience was nothing like I read. 

Dirty & dingy place, all the gel & regular polishes mixed together, girl never introduced herself & was on phone majority of time, hurt me while filing & buffing, nothing was done w/ my cuticles, used both CND and OPI (totally different products), less than a dime sized bath & body moisturizer then spent 30 seconds rubbing each hand. 

We'll see how long these last, but I can tell you NOT heading back there!

What kind of a Mexican-themed restaurant doesn't have quesadillas? Answer: Chipotle.
I have visited this restaurant three times for tacos and burritos. But, they don't have a quesadilla on the menu. Once I asked for it, and a couple of employees thought over it, asked each other, and said they could make it, but it will only have meat and cheese, and will cost the same as a burrito! I wasn't willing to pay $7+ for a quesadilla with just a little meat and cheese. Any other toppings would cost extra! Not fair.
If you're looking for warm food like quesadilla or fajitas, this is not the right kind of Mexican restaurant for you.
I also feel that the employee at the register should put in some napkins and utensils in the carry-out bag. I often forget to stop and get some on my way out, because at almost every other restaurant (not Chipotle) they always put some napkins and utensils in.
Only once, I got bad service at this restaurant. It was late evening, around 9pm, and the employee preparing my tacos kept talking to another employee the entire time. That is rude, if you are going to talk the entire time, over my food, with your coworker. And, it was just some casual chitchat!

We hit Edley's this afternoon for lunch. I'm a BBQ lover and have tried pretty much every place in Nashville. I was hoping to get ribs, but they're not served at lunch so I went with a brisket plate with mac n' cheese and slaw. The brisket was a solid A, nice char on the outside (my sister let me have the coveted end-piece), with a smoky flavor and wasn't too dry. I also enjoyed the mac and vinegar-based slaw. We split an order of wings that everyone agreed on as top-notch. 

It's a cool place with plenty of tables, a bar, flat-screen tv's, and an outdoor patio for once the heat wave subsides.

We noticed we had water damage in the front room of our house and called Master Restoration. They provided immediate help and were very professional, honest, and affordable. I was worried about mold with having 2 small children but they went above and beyond to set up a containment and barrier to avoid any exposure. All the workers were great, esp Jon Goodman who came back out to our house and located the leak and problem which we were able to fix. I highly recommend!

If I could give this place no stars I would. This hotel is dirty, the staff is rude, and I actually cried dealing with the front desk....horrible!!!!!!!!! Priceline will put you in this crappy place so beware

My first bad experience involved an order of lettuce wraps.  The lettuce was soft, dry, rubbery, and nasty.  Oh well.  My next crappy visit involved getting ripped off on a drink special.  When I pointed out the error, the manager/bartender Gabe refused to correct it and asked "Is it really worth arguing about?".  Nope, won't be back.

Quick review as I only had a quick meal here. The food quality was good and there is definitely a wide selection of items. The restaurant is clean and the service is prompt. 

My only concern really is the price of each item. We only had chicken fried rice and a vegetarian dish between the two of us, yet the dinner came out to $38.00. 

That's a bit too much in my books for pretty basic Chinese dishes.

Local chain recently changed hands and new name. Huge menu. Food  was  so,so. Service same. Service was slow. Even though it was Mother's Day it was not packed seemed to take awhile to receive our order. Carne Asada, eh. Fatty. No real flavor. Vegie fajita tasty. Ordered guac- arrived with dinner after reminding the server. Salsa was okay.  Kid friendly. Dirty bathrooms. Nice atmosphere. Can dine alfresco, but was too warm for that. Huge margarita-good for 2 or 3!  Not a must come here kind of a place for me but would try it again.  Maybe  it was an off day. We all have them:) In all fairness, I eat Mexican food more than any other ethnic food and prefer to eat at a little store front or cart in Mexico or my families' table:)

My wife and I are celebrating our anniversary in St Pete, and decided to have dinner in a local place. After looking at Yelp and Urbanspoon, we decided to go here based on the great reviews....mind you we had no reservations. When we got there we noticed the place was small but cozy, and the parking is limited, but since they open at 5pm that shouldn't conflict with other shops. 

We went inside and asked the host Mallory if we could sit outside to avoid the 45 minute wait. She is simply OUTSTANDING, and made us feel very special by the attention she offered us. It was a bit cold outside and she went and got a coat for my wife, which she really appreciated. 

The manager Sam Andrews  came to take our order, and made some recommendations based on what we told him we liked. He was simply spot on, from the wine to the appetizers and entrees, everything was delicious. Sam is simply a rockstar!

This place rocks, from great people, nice atmosphere, and great food, we found our new favorite place in St Petersburg.

This has been my only sushi experience in (Philadelphia) Chinatown but I am interested to see if there is another place in the area that can beat it. The restaurant is dimly lit and gets an authentic feel with the big Buddha statue. We came on a Saturday afternoon and there were not many people there (which in the end was surprising).

We had the spring rolls for appetizer which were great and served with a decent dipping sauce. The sushi included a Philly Roll, Shrimp Tempura Roll and the White Tuna Roll. They were all delicious and not to mention affordable (appetizer and 3 rolls were about $31). The service was great.

If you are in Chinatown I would recommend checking out Mixx (especially if your looking for a BYOB restaurant in the area).

As an Indian woman from Chicago, I was worried I would never find a decent Indian restaurant in St Pete. I am SO happy that Deccan came to town! Authentic flavors, great menu, friendly service, not overly spicy, and a good value (happy hour even on Saturdays). So many Indian places around here water down their menu to cater to American palates...this place is not afraid to do it right! It's a big space and a difficult location, so I'm going to do my best to keep them in business:) Give it a try!

Prices went way up on most things, except the burgers. The food did get better, but not to warrant the price increases. The onion soup was a large bowl and was very good. The salad was pathetic looking and not very tasty.

Worst meal in New Orleans. Horrible service. This place looks like the 1970's threw up. 
Menu is outdated, and overpriced. Bread was stale and took forever to come out. Entree came out wrong, and the new entree was chef boyardee in a bowl for $17. 5 person dinner party and everyone hated their meals. Oh, and she charged the wrong amount to my cc and wouldn't fix it so I could tip her. So instead of having management re-ring my card, she said "just don't tip me." We specifically told her what to put on each card and the rest in cash but she took it upon herself to charge both cards whatever amount she felt like. Run away from this Restaurant!
OMG this is the nicest travel stop I've ever been too!!! Everything was clean, pleasant, and there were more baristas than customers at the sbux. Heaven.

5 stars for excellent service, perfectly cooked shrimp (fried and in the seafood wrap), and the nicely updated outside deck.  There was a great band on the summer Sunday afternoon we were there, and a merry crowd dancing to the 80s and 90s music.  The view is very nice, right on the channel and Gulf.  The service was fast and friendly.  A great place to eat or while away the afternoon.

MMMMmmmm mmmmm mmmm :)  Decided to try Indian Food for the first time and loved it!!  We ended up with Samosa's, Chicken Fried Rice, and the Lollypop Chicken.  The Lollypop Chicken was probably the best thing I have ever eaten ever!  The chicken was crunchy and full of flavor.  DELICIOUS small chopped raw onion surrounded the chicken bringing a second texture to the plate & the little lemon wedge was so cute and added even another dimension of flavor.

Walls are paper thin. Don't expect to sleep if there's a guest staying in the room next door. Also, don't expect to be moved - even after two phone calls and a trip to the front desk.  Lastly, Marriott status will also not be helpful at this hotel.

Staff is nice. If you are looking for travel clothing, Scottevest, q zip,pick pocket proof clothing, RFID wallets, not your store, although orvis on line states they have these items.  Trout fishing, yes. I'm going to REI.

I have only had the Sonoran style hot dogs but they are my favorite, even from their more famous competitor. They have a "condiment" bar for added toppings. When I am in or passing through Tucson I always try to come here.
Delicious beer, cool people (I'm talking the staff b/c they really are nice and down to earth) and a fresh place!
So happy to find this salon! Peter gave me an amazing highlight and blowout in record time. The prices are great and they have the most comfortable shampoo chairs.
Still great place. Made huge improvements since opening and getting better all the time !

Strange donuts is one of those places I go more for my dog than for myself...

I could take it or leave it, but my dog means a lot to me... So four stars it is.

The maple bacon is one of my dog's favorite things ever... She knows it by appearance and will bark trying to get me to give it to her she adores it so much. Personally, I prefer Vincent Van Doughnut's version... But Strange's is cheaper and since my dog loves it, I go with it. You can't deprive a dog named Moscato, right? So on special doggie days (her birthday, the day I brought her home, the day we reunited after she got lost, etc) she gets one.

I personally only get excited about the Campfire donut. And even then I think it's more nostalgia related than taste related. I certainly don't bark/gruff or dance on my hind legs at the sight of it. We can't all have the joys in our lives that dogs do though... But seeing it in their eyes is nearly as good

On Fat Tuesday you have a staff of 5. Are you serious?  You are on one of the most popular corner Poydras and St. Charles day of Mardi Gras and you don't properly staff your location. Come on Starbucks. They have one person on the register and on guy who looks like he is trying to look busy so he doesn't have to do work. This is ridiculous. 

The staff is moving slow as turtles no smiles no hi how are you. Heads down they have one door open and the line is out if the door. The only good thing was I got bathroom tickets. DO BETTER

I'm sorry but this place is a ghetto. For massages, you don't even get your own room, but are in a general area with only curtains separating each customer. The customer next to me fell asleep during her massage so I had to listen to her snoring during mine. The massage started half an hour late, which the staff didn't even apologize for or acknowledge, and lasted for 45 minutes rather than an hour. It was tepid and too light.

I have been looking for a new go-to nail place since I moved to the Carrollwood/Citrus Park area, but nothing has ever made me feel compelled to return until now. Love Nails is in a newer plaza (not so much "strip mall" as previously described) with other higher-end retailers. The interior is gorgeous, with ample pedicure chairs and nail stations.
As soon as you enter and specify what you would like, they are quick to offer you a drink (bottled water, sodas, teas, even wine) and seat you quickly without much wait. They offer a number of specialty pedicures but don't push you to upgrade from the regular (although the Cooling Seabreeze was to die for on a hot summer day!). They also offer gel/shellack in more colors than I've ever seen available at other salons.
Along with great service, comes a cost, however. For an upgraded pedicure and a gel manicure, I paid $60 before tip, but ti was worth every penny! 
If you're looking for a good, reliable nail salon -- this is it!
Went there tonight, great service and professional. Lots of added touches with a basic manicure such as paraffin wax, hot stones, and massage. Look forward to next visit

Ahh the simplicity. ReAnimator has a plentiful, diverse coffee/cream supply for all your pick me up needs. Get real work done here and fade far far away from the soul reaping city. I recommend mid day. Get a cozy outdoor seat. WiFi. Coffee subscription.
Street Tacos in Tucson all get their inspiration right here.  Best Black Beans and Cotija Cheese on the Planet.  If you come visit me, 100% chance I'm taking you here for the win.

The food is decent.  The habanero bowl is tasty, but don't be fooled as I was with the name HABANERO Bistro.....The hottest thing they have is a salsa that isn't very hot.  When I asked if they had anything hotter she said No.....You would think given the name that there would be spicier / hotter food.  Big disappointment.

Horrible business etiquette. I work at a business where Paradocx winery was booked as a vendor for an event we were hosting. After confirming in advance and even prepaying for the wine, they never showed up. They never called or even answered a phone call throughout the night. Talk about bad business, I would never spend my money here and would certainly never recommend anyone to give them their business.

I love this place! Amazing food and awesome service. The lunch  soups are incredible; I'll especially the chicken and duck ones. The staff is so friendly and always so warm in greeting you. The quality of the food is so fresh and the summer rolls are awesome. I also like how you can adjust the spice of any dish even if you're like me and want it to be ridiculously spicy. I eat here at least once a week

From scratch slow roasted corn beef is best I've ever had (and I don't even like it, but looked so good on my husbands plate)!  Great breakfasts. Always crowded on weekend. That's a good thing.....a sign the food is good and fresh!

I was so tempted to order from here, but I saw one of the staff members repeatedly grab a food item with the parchment paper (as she should) but her long lime green nails always touched the food. Then she handed utensils to a client and didn't grab them
By the handle but the part that goes in your mouth. Lastly as she ladles soup into container she grabbed the container from the inner part instead of the outer part. None of these I would have an issue with had she worn plastic gloves. I would work on these issues quickly.

I had Pho soup there. It was so very good that, since I knew I was having company for lunch the next day, that I bought two more servings for the next days lunch along with a couple of the Vietnamese sandwiches, as the person coming hadn't had them before. They enjoyed the food also!!!
This was a wonderful find. Great soul food breakfast at more than reasonable prices. Worth looking for it's little hard to find spot tucked away in a small strip mall.

My husband and I were looking for a place closer to our house other than Los Betos for some burritos. 

Nato's Mexican Food was amazing. The burritos are bigger than at the other place and also more affordable. We got a burrito an nachos and had plenty of food for our family of four. 

The staff was super friendly and fast. I was surprised how fast we got our food with a full restaurant and only two people working.

The Restaurant was extremely clean which is a huge bonus!

We have found our new burrito place!

Pretty impressed with the service.  Had a tricky financial situation that was hard for other dealers to work through but Hollywood made it work.  Had the vehicle inspected and they said it was good which is good to hear, that they sell cars that don't have major problems.  I'll update this if anything major happens but so far I would recommend them.
Ok I took a group of students to hot box for lunch. They loved it and do did I (it really is good pizza). All is forgiven.  My other experience was user error. Oops!

I was at knockouts recently and there was no cook on duty so I couldn't order anything to eat. All I could is order drinks. The place looked a little unclean so it's probably best that I didn't get anything. Overheard an offensive comment about a disabled person. I will not go back nor will I recommend this establishment based upon cleanliness and insensitive remarks.

This place is amazing.  I go quite often for the 25 cent oyster happy hour and the oysters are always ice cold and amazing!  Plus beer and wine is half priced, can't beat that!  Eat there for lunch every now and again and the last time I went I got the oyster salad.  Wow, soooo good! Oh, and they make a mean burger.  Can be on the pricey side, but nothing like some of Besh's other restaurants.  Even so, totally worth it!
Food was fantastic! The bananas foster was delicious! Would come back here to try more great food of the menu! Thanks for the great food and service!

I won't be coming back to this place again.  

My bf gets the all-you-can eat sushi and I ordered a noodle dish.  The first thing out of server's mouth is that there is no sharing or we will be charged a $1.00 per piece.  Ok, I understand.  I felt the WHOLE entire time the wait staff was just watching me.  It was really uncomfortable for me and I just wanted to leave.  

Also, for the all-you-can-eat you can only order a maximum of 20 pieces at one time.  Let's keep in mind a lot of special rolls have 8 pieces and if you order two special rolls that would be 16 rolls.  Then after that, you can't even get a regular roll like a California Roll because that is a 6 piece roll  and with the two special rolls  would give you a total of 22 pieces. So basically, you are two pieces over the limit which is pure bullshit.  You would have to order your next roll when you finish your plate.  They will not let you order more than 20 pieces at one time, so don't even try it because that rule is written in stone.  

The Malaysian noodle dish was a very big portion but the sushi was not so good.  My bf got the all-you-can-eat but he still sneaked some rolls on my plate.  I tried the Crunchy Kani roll and it was drenched in a sweet sauce on top.  It was disgusting like they were trying to hide the dryness of the rice with sauce.  The same goes for the Crunchy Whitefish Tempura roll  and the Dragon roll because it all had the same sweet sauce.  I felt like I was eating the same roll all over again.  

Then I get the bill and I find out that I was charged $2.00 for Green Tea.  Seriously, most sushi places offer Green Tea for FREE.  This place sucks.

I was here for the first time yesterday. I wanted to try pink acrylics for the first time but they came out too light and since they were busy last night I didn't ask them to put a polish on top of it. So I went back this morning and asked if they could put a color polish on top because the pink acrylics were too light and they did it without a problem and didn't even charge me for it! And they also did a fabulous job!! This will definitely be my go to nail salon from now on!
You know you'll be getting a great meal when the menu is one page. Or, at least, that's how it should be. And that's how it is here. Our party enjoyed everything, and you will, too!

Stayed here one night passing through town and got a decent rate at $174 for one night, and it worked out great. We have a dog and that's huge for us to be able to bring him too. 

The room was fine, clean and spacious, the grounds were clean, bed was fine, love the free wireless and great location next to the harbor and State St. BUT...my most memorable positive note about this place is the front desk guy Anthony who was just awesome. 

He's a SB local and helped us with anything from finding a dog-friendly beach, to telling us the best local ice cream parlor and then snuck us in with last-minute reservations for dinner at Bouchon, which ended up being one of the best meals I've ever had. He helped make our experience at the B&B, and in Santa Barbara so much better. Big ups to Anthony. 

One area I think this place could improve is the breakfast. It was pretty unimpressive. Not gross, just nothing to write home about, and it's more of a continental style affair, not served breakfast like some B&B's advertise.

Gorgeous hotel, beautiful gardens and well kept walk ways. However don't come here looking for any southern hospitality, the staff is incredibly rude and when you ask anyone for directions no one seems to understand how to give them. I wouldn't recommend this hotel for guests with smaller children. Much better for an adults getaway!

Finally a casino in Arizona that appreciates Blackjack players!!! 

With a Player's Club that is second to none, there is, in my opinion, no other hotel/casino combo in Arizona that can match Casino del Sol.  

The property itself is beautiful.  The hotel lobby is a welcome retreat from the casino floor.  Guest rooms are spacious and well-appointed.

I rarely play slots but from I could see walking around, they seem to have better than average payouts.

I love Blackjack and if you're willing to bet at the higher limit tables ($25 minimum) you will be rewarded with 3-deck shoes; which narrows the casino edge.

Restaurants are good.  I like Abuelita's (quick & tasty Mexican options.  Festa Buffet is great option.  Ume was decent as well.

Even though I live in Phoenix, I'd rather make the drive to Tucson and play in a casino that appreciates and rewards me for my play.

$75 for one hour is pretty steep to stay fully dressed and just be massaged over your clothes in an open room but my therapist was very thorough. We also did the $12 for 20 minute foot massage which the first few minutes were great but then she just kept rubbing the same spot over and over again and was starring out into the distance so I would say OK experience.

Food was delicious. I tried a bite off of other's plates - rosemary bread, squash soup, lobster waffle appetizer, prime rib dumplings, duck, short ribs. Wait service was great. Waiting to try desserts

Let's be real, who doesn't love cemeteries?!
Just me? Can't be! I'm a sucker for spooky places like this, and was determined to set foot inside its walls.

Itching to see the famous Voodoo Queen, Marie Laveau's tomb, marked with xxx's, and adorned with gifts brought by fans and admirers.
COME HERE!  (As she was a New Orleans hero - as she didn't practice "hoodoo", but good voodoo and helped to free lots of slaves! The most commonly left item left at her tomb - hair ties -which goes back to her days as a hair dresser.)

Interested in brushing up on your New Orleans history, learning of former plantation and slave days, and all about the archdiocese?
COME HERE! (Take a tour, which will fill your head with all the knowledge you need! Also stop by the visitor center, as it's filled to the brim with maps, pictures and artifacts!)

Wanting to feel like a VIP and have access not everyone has?
COME HERE! (The cemetery used to allow all visitors, but due to the amount of the vandalism, all visitors must be accompanied by a tour guide - unless you have family members inside the cemetery!)

Dying to see where Nicolas Cage will be buried?
COME HERE! (He purchased a plot of land for $250, featuring a HUGE white pyramid structure for his body to be laid to rest!)

Looking for a fun way to spend an afternoon and engross yourself with all things  tombs/cemeteries and voodoo.
COME HERE! (no really! people are dying to get in!) 

Let's face it, there is no better way to spend your afternoon!

Sunday brunch is where it's at!!! I came in wanting nachos and was a bit disappointed that I had to order from a pre-fixe brunch menu, that did not include nachos. But I was hungry, and open minded. $18 for a two course brunch, including a great coffee (which could be served hotter). 
I ordered the Cobb salad and breakfast burrito. Excellent portions, and of course always tasty, fresh food. These vegetarian meals never disappoint. I highly recommend for a non-typical brunch!

Great place to go during the day or night, as a couple or with a group of friends. The bar has a decent selection of beer (not everything is an IPA like most places in town). They have an ATM to grab cash and all machines accept quarters. Even on a crowded night you can find something to play. You can also rent out the place for $300/hr and they'll open up the machines. They allow you to bring in outside food as well. Great addition to the midtown area.

very nice breakfast. Try the Huevos Rancheros with chorizo. It is awesome! 
Btw, go others earlier, it seems popular in this area + the hotel residents.
Delicious street tacos! We had the Barbacoa, Pollo Tinga & the Pescado....all were yummy! Great selection of craft beers too! We will definitely be back.

It was ok. Nothing wowed me, but it wasn't horrible. It was a quick check in process, the employees were friendly the whole time of my stay. My floor smelled like smoke though and my living area did too. I didn't like that at all. The pool was nice & clean. It had a bbq area too. That was the best part of the stay honestly. I would probably stay here again for a better rate. I think $185 is a bit much a night. The furniture in the rooms are dated. They definitely need upgrades.

If you are looking for a place you can show up right from the beach and not be judged then this is your spot.  Super low key, we read the reviews on Yelp and couldn't wait to have some good smoked fish.  Upon pulling up you can see they are not looking for fancy, there are a bunch of picnic tables and some take out but they do have a full indoor restaurant if you want some AC.  We sat at the picnic table and we were served right away.  
Ordered a $2.99 draft Miller High Life served in a frosted glass, great on a nice hot day.  We got the smoked fish spread with saltines, cheeseburger, potato salad, and Cole slaw.  Smoked fish was ridiculously good, they make everything right there and you can take it home too!  The cheeseburger was really great, cooked perfectly.  The German potato salad had tons of bacon and was served warm, absolutely amazing!!  Skip the Cole slaw but otherwise this food was so good we have been talking about it for days!

I picked out a mattress and got it the same day for pretty cheap. Darrell was really helpful and they called in advance before delivering it so I knew when to expect it. I love the mattress, and I only spent $400 total.

My favorite place to eat and/or drink in Nashville.  

It's in midtown, which is local and away from the honky tonks.  The ambiance, food, drinks, and service is great.  And if anything, there is always good people watching.  I come to Tavern after church for brunch, out with my girlfriends for drinks, or out to a nice fun dinner with my boyfriend. 

My birthday was on a Wednesday last year, which is 2-for-1's night. I came with my girlfriends and had my favorite dessert, their S'mores!  So much fun!

When asked where do I want to go for brunch? Lunch? Dinner? or just a night out...I always pick Tavern.

I have been going to Bella Prana for 6 months and to hot yoga classes all over the world since 2010.  The instructors are excellent. I also miss Mallory because she brought a lot of energy to the room and also because of her upbeat music.

Like any other nail salon they really push you to upgrade, get add ons etc. like $5 extra for callous removal, do you want a mani with that pedi, how about an eyebrow wax? 

My mani pedi looks great although I spent way more than I had intended to. Also I wish that my toe nails had been cut back slightly more, I had asked them to cut them as short as they could! Overall not the best place I've been but not bad either.

Good food and a excellent atmosphere - price/value equation was out of line.

Drinks were very average.
I was a little nervous after reading some of the reviews, but we had great service and the food was good too.

These guys are awesome. I first used Wheel Tec November 2011, when I damaged my rims after riding into huge potholes. I called after hours and the owner, Jon told me to come on by and he waited for me to get there. It was dark out and he used my cell phone light to check out my wheels. Talk about dedication! We got a great deal on a new set of 22 inch rims for our SUV. 

I called back when I needed tires yesterday and one of the reps, Waldy was not only accommodating, but he also got me a great deal (my husband had already received quotes from several tire shops) on 4 tires. 

The honesty, customer service cleanliness and comfort of the waiting area at WheelTec is top notch and I highly recommend them!

Easily the closest hotel to Independence Hall. 20 yards to the IH security checkpoint. 100 yards from the Liberty Bell. Easy to walk almost everywhere. Scores of great restaurants and bars close by.
Perfect service. Had a king room over looking the "park" - which really means your room looks right at Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. Definitely pick that option! Xmas week prices under $200/night?? Easily worth double!
Their burger is top flight. So is the shrimp and grits. Highly recommend this place. Got to sit in the French Doors. Beautiful weather.  Mark the waiter is outstanding.

I paid for a room at the Peppermill 3 months before I arrived for 3 people, 2 double beds. On Arrival ( Thursday afternoon ) I was told they were very sorry but they only had rooms with 1 king-size bed, but I could have a rollaway. The first room was so small that the roll away could not be open. The second room was ok but a rollaway cot for an 11 night reservation. Finally on the 4th day they would try and move us. I went to the front desk to ask when the room would be available, a very nice women at reception said let me get my manager and see if we can do something for you? I did not ask for anything other than a room for myself and my family, one that we could all have at least a part of a bed. I was basically yelled at by the hotel manager, Sorry it was either Melinda, MaryAnn or Lori. Now I did not ask for compensation I just wanted the room I had paid for. Do yourself a favor DON'T STAY HERE!

Wish I could give it 0

Food order was delayed by almost two hours and didn't hear back from anyone to let me know about this issue.

Marathon is one of those occasionally unavoidable places for Center City kids.  It's true, their menu is much more interesting than their actual product, but Brunch is generally spot on.  Their Breakfast quesadilla is one of my favorite brunch entrees in the city.  However, it's rare you'll see me here for lunch or dinner.  While I love the variety of ingredients and creativity of salad/sandwich combinations (especially for vegetarians), I have yet to actually experience a Marathon salad/entree that has lived up to my expectations.

As far as this specific location, I've come to the upstairs bar a few times.  It's fair.  I like the exposed brick and variety of seating options.  I do not like the overcrowdedness, the long wait to order drinks, and the randomly indifferent staff.  I'll come back when I'm in the area and want to grab a random drink, but I don't see myself making plans to come anytime soon.

Best diner ever! I have been to many diners around the country and this probably tops them all!!
Our server Gina is awesome!! I feel like I'm at home.

Went for the lunch special on a weekday.  Got the Thai basil and drunken noodles.  Thai basil was not spicy at all even though it said it would be on the menu. The drunken noodles was spicier but not very good.  Everything had a soup broth and not thick like quality Thai.  They make everything with this canned tomato base that tastes so gross.  Even the lemon grass soup had a canned tomato sauce in it .... really gross! Do not recommend.

This was one of the last stops we made on our way to Black Rock City, NV. We ran inside to grab some postcards to send to ourselves at Burning Man, but only found a card aisle instead. We ended up buying several birthday cards and tearing off the backs to make them into a one-page postcard. We stood in a slow line and paid for the cards and stamps, but were then told they have no outgoing mail or nearby PO boxes. They also wouldn't let us leave the cards and put them in their own outgoing mail. (We luckily found a fitness equipment supply store nearby that was happy to mail our cards for us.) Service was friendly but it would have been nice to have a place to mail out the cards that they sell here.

I've been several times and everything I've tried has been better than average.  Two stars because they cannot control the customers. Go in after 7pm and you will need a megaphone to hear over the wild animals that sing at the top of their lungs,dance in the isle, and suck their gold teeth so loud that you can't hear yourself think. If you want to try this restaurant, go @ lunch.
Best sushi. Highly recommend. The sushi rolls were very good especially the crunch roll and the service was fast..one of the waiter looks like Jared Leto too!

First off, the name reminds me of a swim school not a restaurant and the decor is lacking and should be redone. With that said the food was ok - my steakhouse salmon was pretty tasty and my husbands Guinness fish and chips were also good. My son also had fish and chips and he liked it. There was nothing outstanding though and it was pretty over-priced. Not sure if I will be back but it was a pleasant enough dining experience and the service was good,

The food was amazing. I had the jerk chicken and coconut water. The jerk chicken is so flavorful. I loved every bite. The roasted plantains are delicious as well. The coconut water was amazing. So fresh. Defiantly give this place a try. Worth the wait. We will be coming back for sure. The owner was very friendly too.

This place is amazing!!! Everyone must try the matzo ball with brisket noodle soup. The brisket is super tender, the meat just falls apart after you put it in your mouth. The slightly spicy soup seeps into the matzo ball giving it the most flavorful taste. Lastly, the noodles were perfectly cooked. It was al dente and not too soft like most Asian noodle soups. (It was so good I forgot to take a photo!) 

We also had the dumplings in chili oil - reminded me more of a ravioli than a Chinese dumpling, but I loved it! Wasn't too spicy and the dumpling skin was nice and chewy.

Another dish we had and of course, loved, was the pork belly rice bowl. It's a katsu so the pork belly is slightly breaded and fried. Oh my, the pork was sooooo tender. The sushi rice they used paired perfectly with the pork and the katsu sauce they used. I'm drooling just thinking about it. If you get this dish, I'd recommend adding some of the hot chili oil they give you on the table. Gives the dish a little bit of a kick.

I'm definitely going back to this place!

Specifically chose the Good Cup because we wanted somewhere that was open later, where we could sit and work for the evening. Upon our arrival, we stood by the register and were not acknowledged for what seemed like forever. When the red headed barista finally took out order, she was totally rude. The hours online say they close at 8 pm, but she acted like she was inconvenienced by our presence (though the place was full of people). You'd think having business would be a good thing, but instead we were urged out with a loud and grumpy announcement of closing time every 5 min. 

Our coffee and tea were delicious as always, too bad the service was so horrible today. We'll be back, but we'll make sure we call ahead and ask about closing time first, in order to avoid the inhospitable barista.
