It's a shame because Tortugas has some things going for it in the food department.  However, with other choices quickly springing up around it, Tortugas needs to get with the program before I'll ever go back there (if ever).  For now, even though it's been months since I ate there, I think about finding that hair every time I think about Tortugas.  And seriously Tortugas, do something about your debit card purchasing system, it's pathetic!  You have to pay money to do debit!!

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I've always liked Tortuga's, they are okay.  I really enjoy their chicken taco's and the nacho chips that come with the orders are really very good.  

They are not a great place to order take out from, its better to go there and eat.  When I order the chicken tacos to go, I find that they are VERY water logged when I get them home and the once crispy shell falls apart right in my hands.  Generous amounts of chips and salsa are given and that is always appreciated.  I do agree that they are overpriced though.  

They really need to update their debit card system or something, it always takes longer than usual when I'm paying with a card and I think they even have a surcharge for using a card!

The bagels are very good and always fresh with lots of variety to pick from. The breakfast sandwiches are the real thing to try though: fluffy eggs on a hot, fresh, toasted bagel. One of the best breakfast options in the area.

Most definitely my favorite food in Tucson!

No Anchovies is a great local gem for some great pizza. I have been a No Anchovies regular for about a decade now and I love this place! The people they keep on staff here are always down-to-earth and real, while still providing great service. I have never met a cook or bartender that I didn't like. One great thing about No Anchovies is that it doesn't take long for the staff to remember you and your order! 

Bonus - If you frequent this lovely establishment enough, they thank you with a large self-decorated mug that gets you plenty of beer for cheap!

Food was pretty good and the atmosphere was nice as well. Just enough lighting to create a very cool ambiance. There are big windows which overlook a nice pond with koi fish swimming around and a pier to walk out on. Every hour or so, there are fire displays that shoot out from the pond which add to the unique vibe this place gives off. The servers here are also top notch and are so friendly. Aja and Christine are great employees; very friendly and hard working. I can't wait until Union Station gets its well deserved makeover and this place will definitely be a hot destination spot once again.

This is a fairly small YMCA then I am used to in my home state, but nonetheless it's a Y.  The staff are very friendly. The place is very clean. The pricing is YMCA standards so you can make your own judgements with that. Unless I find another activity. I plan to stay put for my son.

This is a great place to get a little work done, meet a friend, and sip a nice coffee! Note: you can get free refills on the coffee, which makes it great for a morning study session. Their sandwiches are quite yummy (my fav is the prosciutto one). I only wish I could get a few more chips on the side (it's a healthy little portion of chips). The staff is always friendly and I love the upstairs workspace! Definitely check it out!!
I love their burger options and duck fries.  Trouble is, it's always crowded.

I try not to judge harshly when it comes to sushi since the Bay Area is especially spoiled. Anyhow, I was looking to kick a sushi craving and was needing to try this place out. It is average and I would go as far to say it is a first time sushi eater place. 

Cons; it is SO loud in the restaurant. It is a hole in the wall with walls that won't absorb a single sound and this was when it wasn't jam packed.
I love shrimp, but goddamn half the stuff on their menu is shrimp and cream cheese (we didn't touch anything with cream cheese and I am glad we didn't). Also, they put or garnished a lot of stuff with lemons. Lastly, everything seemed to taste the same no matter what we ordered which made the AYCE experience more of a AYCS (all you can stomach). 

Again, it is okay. Service was reasonable and chefs and servers were nice. But I will def be looking at other options for sushi in the future.

words can not explain how much i love this store!

Living in saint louis now i don't go as much as i used to, but i make sure to visit every time i'm in town.

I probably have like 20 things from this store in my apartment, they always have new stuff and they do specialize in vintage clothes! They also sell local artists art and jewelry, even stuff from the stl area. 

Every one need to check this store out, even if you are from the st. louis area. It's only about 20 minutes from the city.

A few of my Facebook friends had went to Unusual Suspects in the Broad Ripple area about a week or two before. So I figured it was time to try somewhere new by having my own visit. I'm on a new diet so I could only have the chicken and fish meals. I decided to try the salmon. The salmon dish was actually pretty good and the serving size was very large. The dish comes with a very creamy rigatoni which was awesome! My mentor who went along with me for this visit said the rigatoni was so good that she could eat it all day. So much so that she could have a whole bowl of it and be so happy that she would eat it while swinging her feet. How cute! The space was nice, service was prompt and I can see myself going here again to try some of their meat selections.

Start with the food. 
It is good, not great and they offer small portions for a high dollar price. 
Service.
Horrendous. They actually have a waiter here that several different people that I know have had wait on them and ruin their meal. 

Not bad just not great or worth cash. Service really bad. Or at least the same person who is waiting on all the gulch locals.

Sat at the outside bar...ordered Logan Burger.
It took 30 minutes to get it, when I politely asked about taking long time, the bartender said its taking time because I ordered well done. It was a stupid reply. 
And the worst burger for $17, too dry and not even worth $3. I'm glad I retuned it. How can someone not make a simple burger when charging it $17. It should not be named Logan burger when there is no flavor and it's just a cheese burger.

I go here a lot for soccer matches which is a lot of fun, but visited for the first time at dinner with friends from Australia.  It didn't disappoint. Atmosphere is great, food is great, wait staff is good.  Suggest the wings with house sauce, garlic cheese fries, and fish and chips.
One of the best donair poutines in the city. The staff work efficiently, communicate well to make sure each order is correct, and are friendly.

**** We have been here roughly 8 times already and love it.  We brought friends here and they loved it also.  We've tried a variety of items off the menu and always seem to get the chips & cheese dip.  The tacos and enchiladas are our favorites.  

My boyfriend and I have been here 3 times already in the past two months and plan to go again tonight for dinner.  It's nice to sit at a table outside, enjoy a drink and eat some tasty Mexican food.  Every time we have gone, we've gotten the chips and cheese dip.  We've tried the tacos and the dinner specials and have not been disappointed.   There is a kick to the food that doesn't stay with you an hour later.  Which satisfies the both of us.  
The staff have been pleasant and quick.  If you go, I would recommend signing up for their emails.  I signed up to get the weekly specials email and everything usually sounds good.  We've tried things we wouldn't normally and it's nice knowing what the specials are for the week.

This is a quaint hotel in the quieter part of the French Quarter. Jackson Square, Bourbon Street, Rue Royal, and Frenchman Street are all a short (safe) walk away.  We were also able to walk to Canal Street to catch the Green Street Car (St. Charles) to the Garden District and Magazine Street. We walked just about everywhere in the city except the city park.  The location is perfect.  

The staff was very attentive and so nice we still talk about Terry. I was taken aback when they use old school hotel slips to record your information rather than using a computer program.
The hotel was relatively quiet, we did have a little noise from people coming off of the elevator, but our door was right beside the elevator exit.  
The room, bathroom, and common areas were clean and inviting.  We didn't use any of the amenities the hotel offered.  We really just stored our things there, slept, and showered there.

I would stay here again on my next trip to NOLA

OFF THE HOOK!!! So very cool. The place. Is just amazing in so many ways. The staff extraordinarily friendly, professional and attentive. We'll done! The vibe in the bar . Restaurant so cool and comfortable. The lighting perfect. The veranda? Who wouldn't want to hang there? Live music off the hook. Perfectly cool. Rooms are clean, charming, nice sheets and towels...... This place is perfectly charming. I would recommend to anyone!!
Snowballs stuffed with cheesecake? Really? Okay. The kid loved it and wanted it again. My traditional spearmint was the way to go for me!! Delicious and plenty of choices!

Listen, I hate to be the bearer of bad news, but excuse me Hotel Palomar...banners are for Science Museums and the like...not for Kimpton hotels. 

Rewind...

I was walking to a little meeting down 17th street and I look up and in my face I see "HOTEL PALOMAR" on a plastic banner vertically hanging from the hotel. EW. Guess what Hotel Palomar? People know you're there...or at the least the people who you want in your establishment know you are there! This isn't like "THE HUMAN BODY" at the Franklin Institute. How many hotels have you seen with a plastic banner? Probably zero (unless you include the days inn in portland maine, but honestly...) 

UGH. It made me so angry that I had to give it a demerit. Maybe they need a new marketing director. 

xo

MY GOODNESS this place is amazing! Every time I go it's always so great. Always consistence with the flavor & serving amount. My favorite are the shredded beef tacos. They are always so full of flavor and great with the Gringo Style condiments. Their salsa bar suits anybody's taste buds. It's like a Subway and Chipotle assembly. The workers there are just as great and welcoming. Their bar contains yummy adult beverages. It will always be a place I will go for as long as it is open!

My favorite brunch spot in Tucson! The service is attentive and the food is very good. My favorite is the egg and chile relleno made with mole sauce sourced from Native Seeds/SEARCH next door. It's only available on weekends, however.

I've also had their omelettes du jour; biscuits with duck fat gravy; and pastries. The best part, of course, is their signature mimosas and bloody mary's. 

If you go on the weekend, be prepared to wait. But they have water and coffee available to make the time pass a little faster. Or visit their East side location on Grant near Tanque Verde. I've never had to wait at that location and the food and service are just as good.

My co-workers and I always eat at Farmer's Market t on Friday afternoons. I pretty much ALWAYS get Leo's sushi. You can always rely on them for some good, basic sushi. I have tried some of their samplers and my favorite is their salmon, tuna and shrimp rolls. 

I also really like their miso soup but on warm days, you can ask them to substitute it out for their pot stickers. This is one of the only places at Farmer's Market that also carries Coke Zero which is a plus for me. Finally, they always offer delicious samples such as kimchi sushi, yum yum roll, etc. Of course, their sweet smiles always add the perfect touch to this great family owned restaurant. 

The only reason I take off a start is because I feel like their prices are a tad bit more than usual for some simple sushi rolls. 

Visit them and try some great sushi! :)
Wonderful views.  The NPS really did this one right.

Most comfortable bed I have ever slept in.  I was in town for a convention.  Hotel services were excellent.  Staff is stellar. Room amenities good, but room was small for 2 people.  I am subtracting a star for the really bad view from my room, so be sure and ask for a good view when you check in.
Very Authentic food with an amazing atmosphere to match! Swift service, zero hiccups and a very friendly professional staff! A must Bookmark!
My favorite local breakfast spot! The good is always well prepared, large portions and in expensive.

Love this place!

My girlfriend and I are both not very big fans of going to Jersey for ANY reason.  However, every 2 months or so, we'll cross the WW to restock our wine and beer supplies at Canal's.

The manager of the store is super friendly as well as the rest of the staff there.  It's pretty impressive that everyone knows exactly where specific wines can be found throughout the store.  There is a ton of a variety and they know where to find it, just ask!  Also, they usually give samples of different wines that are on sale.  

As for their craft beer selection, it is great as well and reasonably priced.  Yes, let me reiterate that in general their prices are extremely reasonable.  And, you can fill up on cheap gas while youre in NJ too!

Not sure about Mark P.'s review but I have had the exact opposite experience each time I've gone there.

Excellent food, ambiance as well. You might have to sit very close to the next table if the restaurant gets crowded , but we happened to have a friendly conversation with all other tables around us.highly recommended

Service was friendly.  Good wine pour.  I ordered simple apps in the spirit of time, of course, I'm at an airport.  It took forty, yes 40, minutes for a cup of gumbo (pre- made item, just needs to be scooped out and plopped in cup). I am sure no one reads airpprt reviews be a use you get what you get.  If this restaurant was outside an airport it wouldn't make it.  Nice people.  Good wine pour.  But that's it.

Found this gem while looking for the car.  I'm so glad we stopped in and grabbed some cupcakes! Probably the best cupcakes I've ever had in life! Had German chocolate cupcake and I don't remember the name of the other one. . but it was banana nut bread with chocolate in the middle and peanut butter icing!  Every bite was heavenly! We will definitely be back when we are in NOLA!

Here's the thing...I want so badly to give this place 5 stars. I would give it 4.5 if I could but you know how that is. I love the food, I loved the drinks when I drank and I love the staff. The thing is the first time I came here I was an out of towner. I was an out of stater to be honest. I think maybe it showed and the girl working there didn't seem so friendly. We talked a little bit but something seemed off. I had the bacon Mac and cheese and some good beers so the food and drink were 5 stars I was just a little annoyed by the service. Well a month later I moved to philly and came back. I got the same girl as a bartender and put my best foot forward to be friendly and it paid off. Probably also helped that I was now a "local." Every time I've gone since no matter who's working I have a great time! The draft selection is pretty nice and the can/bottle selection is pretty extensive. I had the shrimp etouffe and it was AMAZING. I will admit the menu is sort of small but it works for me. I love this place and my stomach is growing just thinking about that etouffe!

NOT SURE IF CAFE.......................................

..........................................OR APPLE STORE

When you walk by and look inside, you see a row of people by the window, and almost everyone is using a MacBook.  (Wow, did I really try to pull off a meme in a Yelp review?!)

Consistent with previous reviews that have complained about service, this café is hipster--unfortunately, the snobby and arrogant type of hipster.

Coffee is above average, but why people rave about store-made French press baffles me.  Althogh it does taste better because it is made to order, French press is the frickin easiest way to make your own coffee at home.

The bed was extremely comfortable, that's why I give it a star. I thought the pictures on their website looked great so we decided to stay there for NYE. WRONG CHOICE! Checking in was easy but the room itself was bad. They have a full wall that was a mirror that just looked so tacky! Also, we do not believe in having mirrors face the bed while we sleep, so it just didn't sit we'll with us. But the worst part was the PAPER THIN WALLS. We were on the second story and next to the stairway, so we could hear every footstep in the rooms above us and people going up and down the stairs. You can hear if anyone has a tv on or just a conversation. It had to be the loudest hotel I have ever stayed in. I do not recommend this hotel to anyone. Stay somewhere else!

The owners here are very dishonest. They made up some stuff about being fully booked because of some event, and I was charged over $200 for a dirty room. When I asked to leave one day earlier, they wanted to charge me for the full stay. I've never been to such a shady establishment, and will definitely not return here or recommend it to anyone.

First time visiting this place after my girlfriend went on about how amazing culverts is. The cheese curds were interesting but the bacon double cheese burger was over prized and burned. Not worth the time.

Sat Co. is probably the best thing to happen to Vanderbilt students, since the football team started winning games!  During dinner time, you usually can see a lot of college kids sitting on the deck and enjoying buckets of beer.  I have been to a lot of great Mexican restaurants in my day and I must say San Antonio Taco Co is decent (However, I am comparing it to Olamedni's Mexican Cuisine in Capistrano Beach, CA /Richard Nixon's favorite restaurant). 

Food is decently good in comparison to some of the other Mexican places I have been to. I like to order the chips and queso on a nice afternoon with a bucket of Coronas! Nothing like finishing 3 hour long poli-sci class and heading over to Sat-Co for some beers!
This place is wonderful, I just love the food and hospitality.I try to visit atleast three to four times a month.

Love this place. The price is right, the food is good and the tables are all set up for saki bombs! The waitresses are on point and chefs talented in showmanship and presentation. I recommend you make reservations and make a night of it.

Very clean, prices are reasonable, and Jose spent time with me to plan out exactly what I wanted for my dog.  I felt comfortable that he was taking great care of my dog.  Prices are reasonable, only a little higher than the big box stores ($45 for my small terrier, which is $5 more than PetsMart charges) but I am willing to pay it because I want to support a good business.  We will definitely return.

Nice place to stop and eat. We go just about every Sunday for breakfast. No matter which waitress we get they are always friendly and get our orders right. It is very clean and the customer service is excellent!
I had the Massuman Curry with chicken. It was spot on. My friend had the drunken noodles with tofu. He loved the dish as well. Great Thai food!

Went to Em J's with some colleagues recently and we really enjoyed it.  The owners are super nice and the food was wonderful... I had the most delicious veggie quesadillas - my mouth is watering just thinking about them.  It's a little far from where I work.  If it were closer, I'm pretty sure I would become a regular!

Nice neighborhood bar. Very friendly atmosphere. Definitely laid back and not fancy at all. When we came recently, we sat out on the back patio which was nice. They even turned on the heaters for us. This is more of a bar than a restaurant, but the food is still good. The front bar is smoking, btw. Typical menu of things you would find at a pub. Our waitress was great and very attentive. I had a cheeseburger which was really good and huge. Their sandwiches are also good. The food prices are reasonable, and I think the beers are too. However, the mixed drinks are pretty pricey. My simple cranberry & vodka was 7 or 8 dollars. Overall, i'm sure we will be back

My husband and I stayed here one night in January 2012. We found the Inn very comfortable and charming. Great location, good value. We would stay here again. For all you folks who like to read in bed: though there are no lamps on the bedside tables, there are dimmable down lights in the ceiling above each side of the bed (at least in our one-bed room), with switches reachable from bed. On the brightest setting, these were fine for reading.

I love good Mexican food .... something this place does not have. To start the guacamole was bland, tasted like avocado paste out of a bag. Then I got the steak tacos Medium which were extremely undercooked, and had a terrible flavor. My friend got the chicken wing tacos in buffalo sauce which tasted nothing like buffalo sauce we both each only ate one taco only because we were starving. I wouldn't recommend anyone come here which sucks because I was excited about this place and love the decor. Service wasn't the greatest either.
Modern laundry indeed! This is the nicest laundromat I've ever been in. Very clean and super helpful staff.

Checked this place out for lunch and had the steak chimichanga which came with rice, beans and lettuce/tomato then topped with red enchilada and ranchero sauce. The fried tortilla of the entire was very light and prepared very well. The steak was tender and had a great flavor to it. I requested the hottest sauce that they had which was delicious (tomato based salsa with fresh chopped jalapeño added in) but if you are craving a scorcher, wasn't quite up to the challenge. I would also recommend the fajitas (either chicken or steak) after seeing them come out sizzling hot on a full plate. Serving size about 6 small fajitas.

Definitely a good place for sushi on a budget. I love to get the bigger, fried rolls. Normally I get raw sushi at other restaurants, but it's either a hit or miss here with the raw selection. I'll get a couple of their sushi combos sometimes, but the rice doesn't taste as sticky and fresh. Again, can't go wrong with the fried rolls... they are huge!

I am giving them 4 stars (rather than maybe a more reasonable 3) strictly because they seemed to handle the sudden crowd from the  UYE very well and they deserve credit for that.  That may make little difference when you walk in, then maybe it's just your normal Chinese food place but there you go.  I did order the St. Paul sandwich, something I had been looking forward to since I clicked I'm in.  It had been years since I had my first and only one and while I remember it being just a blob of a sandwich, it was a good memory.  I loved this one ... messy, the mayo, pickles, all falling apart, filled the right spot that night.  I also ordered the pot stickers that were pretty good.  It seems like most others liked there food but I also have rarely been to any similar place that stands out.  Not worth a special trip but if you are nearby, why not.

Went to El Camino for brunch this weekend. It was not as good as my dinner was previously.

The huevos rancheros was served in a cast iron skillet, which is cool, but it really wasn't doing it for me. It kind of tasted bland and the refried beans were more like a soup than they were like a refried bean. Also, the breakfast burrito doesn't come with any type of sauce like guac or sour cream, and I think that's just weird.

Our waitress, while very pretty (Megan Fox look-alike), was pretty checked out. She didn't come over to check on us and only refilled our water glasses after my friend had to start drinking out of my glass. She also didn't ask if I wanted a refill of my coffee. When my friend asked for ketchup she brought the bottle to our table and slid it across the table. I don't know if it was intentional or not, but it was pretty rude.

I'll stick with Green Eggs or Cantina Dos Segundos for breakfast now on.

The stuffed French Toast is simply amazing. Phenomenal service coupled with exquisite food makes Sabrina's my number one restaurant destination in south Jersey. This is a must try for anyone who loves remarkable food and awesome service!!

I have heard so much about breakfast at Ghini's but not much on Tapas Tuesdays (yes, I know tapas is Spanish not French but ,whatever, just go with it), so I am here to talk about the wonderfulness that is Ghini's aperitifs.  Hubby and I LOVE appetizers, so a night like this was created for us.

I really only need one word to review my experience: YUM!  We were joined by another friend and, between the 3 of us, sampled pretty much the entire menu (except the soups; bread & oil; blackened salmon salad; and the mussels).  

I don't even know where to start because EVERYTHING was so delicious. The hot dishes were brought directly from the broiler, so they were warm and toasty.  The cold dishes were just that - cold.  Nothing was even remotely the wrong temperature.  Everything was so full of flavor.  But none of the flavors were overwhelming or excessive - each flavor was in just the right proportion to make a well rounded dish.  I have never tried pate before but if all pate is this good, I have a new favorite food.

My only complaint would be the portion size of some of the dishes.  The Mushroom, Basil & Brie Bruschetta consisted of only 2 slices of baguette w/ the toppings and we did run out of crostini for the Spinach-Artichoke dip (which they quickly rectified by bringing us more).  It did help, though, that many of the dishes were served with a side of greens - which were topped with a light vinaigrette and just as delicious as the main part of each dish.

Had a massage there. Got an appointment immediately and there is the advantage of being open late on weekdays. 

Massage was good, I will not say it was best, but it was good. Might go there again if I really really need it and have no other choice.

Had the massage in a private room. they do try to sell memberships everytime you go and am not sure how good those memberships are.

This was our last stop on the way home. The waitress greeted us, with menu in hand and drink special. Half the party decided on the 6 beers for $15. We also ordered a margarita and glass of white zin. We informed the waitress that we just wanted to have drinks and watch the basketball games. Fine, she would check on us from time to time. We decided that we need some food. We ordered wings, smothered buffalo chips and the new pretzels stiks. Much to our delight the pretzels stiks were from Gus's Pretzels. The wings had just the right amount of seasoning and spice, to be tasteful but not over powering. Finally, the smothered buffalo chips. I thought the buffalo was a little strong, but the rest of the party enjoyed them. 

This is a fun place. The restrooms were clean, except they had an extremely loud hand dryer.

This would have been a one star review had the manger not had the foresight to comp us a round of drinks.  We went here for center city sips last night and the place was busy but by no means filled to capacity so it was baffling that it took more than 30 minutes to get our first round of drinks.  Food came out a bit quicker but not much.  Then when we were ready for our second round of drinks they had run out of the ingredients to make both (yes both) of their special priced drinks.  So we were not able to get them at any price.  The drinks were not consistent. My friend and I had the same whiskey based drink and hers was three times as strong as mine.  The food was inventive and tasty but the portion size very very small. The zucchini that we ordered looked more like a garnish than tapas. With that said to be fair this was a $5 portion for Sips.  I don't think that I would go back here - despite a lot of hand holding from the manager and apologies which were appreciated I think there are enough restaurants bars in center city that have already worked out most of their kinks.

Bob was a fabulous tour guide!!! He had great information and was very entertaining. We made 4 stops and were able to try Gumbo, Muffuletta sandwiches, Jambalaya, and Brisket Po' Boys. Bob was chipper and kept us in good spirits even though it was pouring out!

Dr. Berger and his Staff are wonderful. The smaller practice seems more personal, he connects with his patients, and we have never had to wait more than a couple minutes to be seen. The rooms are comfortable and they are even expanding to make more rooms and a larger waiting room. Easy street parking out front makes it less stressful for getting small children and strollers into the office. Dr. Berger even went the extra distance and stayed late to see my child for a infection so I wouldn't have to wait till the next day.  I would definitely recommend them to anyone!

Now this is where I will visit everytime I come down to New Orleans. The drinks were great, the music was perfect, and the staff was incredible.  This is the bar for me in New Orleans.  Thank you Amanda, Chris, Kristen, & Sara ( If I misspelled or got your names wrong its because evrerytime I left your establishment I was in very good spirits).
Artichoke was amazing.  Shrimp was amazing and desert was fabulous.  I will definitely go back and recommend to my friends service was so friendly.

Had not tried any of the lounges at Peppermill so decided to try out this one during our last stay. Very cool ambience with the fire pit in the middle, though didn't get to sit there because it's a popular circle to sit. In any case, there were other booths to sit at which were cozy. Each one had a direct view of the center fire as well as a small TV that played music videos. We had a 2 for 1 coupon for drinks and so I got the Inferno (regular size) and my husband got the ultimate mudslide. I really liked the Inferno and wished I could have had more! There was one waitress serving the lounge and she was pretty nice and attentive. The lounge gave my husband and I a bit of time to just relax on our last night at Peppermill. That night though, the people sitting at the fire pit were pretty noisy. Would definitely go back again and hopefully get a chance to sit at the fire pit!

I don't think there are any outstanding restaurants near Union Station, but this one gets three stars for some fresh veggies and decent dishes.  I had the angel hair pasta with shrimp, scallops and mussels, and I wasn't looking for anything heavy in the hot weather, so it was about what I needed.  Also had a side of asparagus, which they rocked - it was perfect.  The shrimp and scallops were a little too chewy.  I should probably just consider scallops an advanced maneuver food that is only to be had at places that don't serve Beringer White Zinfandel and/or have children's menus.  The mushrooms were huge and slimy - reminded me of Pizza Hut.

The husband's red fish was good.

The server was stretched pretty thin.  I got annoyed when it took 15 minutes to place our order, then, upon a moment's hesitation while reading a line in the menu the server was urging us on ("Ok...whoever's ready...speak up now) as if he was doing us a favor by stopping at our table to take our order.

Overall?  Nah.

As pretty as the arrangement was, I just wouldn't consider it "premium" quality (which is what I paid for). In fact, it makes me wonder what a "standard" arrangement would even look like. The arrangement was sparse and lacked some of the flowers that should have been included. It also arrived in a smaller vase than what it was supposed to come in. The vase had a smaller opening than the one that was shown in the picture, which is why there were less flowers.  Though customer service did give me 20% off of my order because of the complaint, I probably won't shop here again.

No brainer...best dive bar in South Tampa. Kasey, Mike, Dave, and the rest of the staff are always entertaining and the beer is always cold. PBRs are only $2.50! 

Leave the credit cards at home because they only accept cash at this establishment. Also - it is only beer and wine here. 

Usually the perfect bar to end your night, but you will leave smelling like cigarettes so be prepared to take a shower when you get home.

Wow! So far my favorite place I've discovered since moving to New Orleans! The atmosphere was outstanding. I went one night with friends and we enjoyed a bottle of wine and delicious cheese plate sitting at night under the heat lamps while listening to an amazing jazz band. I needed the heat lamps as I'm Florida born and raised!
Loved the menu...and the unique flavor combinations. The atmosphere is nice, but a little loud!  The ketchup was one of my favorite items an I am not even a ketchup fan! d

They have Chinese, Vietnamese, and Thai dishes. Very delicious. I usually eat the pho when I go but I change it up sometimes. I recently had the triple dragon and my wife had the pork fried rice. Both were done very well.
Great rehab. Friendly barkeeps, cheap drink prices, good food, and lots of places to sit. Highly recommend.

This place is just great. I have yet to order something I wasn't thrilled with. 

I regularly order a gyro and a smoothie from here through online ordering, the delivery is usually quite fast and accurate. My wife is fond of the shwarma platter and fan of their hummus. 

We only had one incident recently where the food was an issue. We ordered gyros and the meat was overly spicy. My wife loves spicy food and she couldn't even finish it. It seems like someone dumped a bottle of pepper into the meat when it was cooking, For this reason we dropped a star, but we are hoping this was a isolated incident

This place is pretty good.  I went for my birthday with my birthday coupon (which is an AWESOME deal!) and had a fun time and even got a free ice cream!  The food was good and the chef was entertaining.  My only wish is that the fried rice was not an upcharge.  At many hibachi places, all hibachi meals automatically come with the fried rice and you do not have to pay more.  My boyfriend and I were slightly disappointed that we would have to pay more for fried rice and ended up deciding not to pay for it.  Maybe they can change this in the future like other hibachi places.  Overall though, I still had a great experience and really enjoyed the food.  Great kickoff to my birthday weekend!

This place is a joke. We waited 2 hours for cold food, gyro meat tasted like it was from the day before, Chicken was dry, no dressing for our food even after I requested extra. I called to see if they could bring the sauce and plasticware and he said we were too far and it wasn't his fault. I called grub hub to tell them what happened and he told them I was lying and refused to give me a refund. My fiance also put up a review and he sent a "compliment" saying ," I know you tried to get free food but not all the time you will." I even told him to come back and get it if he wanted. Rude, disrespectful, and doesn't need to be working with food or people in general. Steak plus pizza is a much better choice.

I eat at this restaurant as much as possible when I am in Saint Louis. 

The food is incredible. You just can't go wrong with anything. 

The wine program is so much fun. I love that you know that all the wines are good and so carefully curated that you can just ask them to give you a cool experience and they will just intro you to a bunch of cool and delicious new wines. Last visit I drank a sparkling, semi sweet orange wine from Greece, 100+ year old vine garnacha from South Africa and a surprisingly great local "port" style dessert wine.

I went to Luke for lunch yesterday - as usual, they have the best fries in town... 

Service was excellent and food was good. 

I had the croque monsieur... lotta meat and cream. It was a bit heavy for lunch so I only ate half. 

For those of you who love John Besh, you'll love this restaurant. I highly recommend. 

I work downtown and have only been for lunch. I'll have to try it for dinner one of these days!

Went there for lunch a few days ago with 18 other guys.  Not only were the ribs some of the best fall-off-the-bone ribs I've ever had, they were very reasonably priced. We had a great waitress who handled all 19 of our food and drink orders and nobody had to wait for a refill on their drink. 

One side note, the place had various sizes of pig statues in all the windows. I asked our waitress if the owner would consider selling me a small one.  She sent the owner over who asked me why in the world I wanted it. I told her my wife collects them and I thought she would like that one. She walked over, picked it up, and brought it to me. I told her I wanted to buy it but she insisted I take it at no charge. 

That's not the reason for the 5 star rating...those ribs are that darned good!

We have a contender for best wings in Ardmore. Went for late night get together not long ago, haven't been since it was a maloneys, it's hard to believe it is the same bar. Nice and updated restaurant. Haven't tried the pizza yet, but the wings were great. They had the crispy exterior I love in wings, no mushy skin on these.

My car insurance company referred me to Safelite. The technician that replaced my window (Israel Alvarez) left shattered class in the door and when he put the door frame back in it caused several outward dents along the outside of my door. Safelite is now responsible for the estimated $1000.00 bodywork plus my rental car for the week that my car is going to be in the body shop. I did not notice the body damage until the next day since I was not at home when they went out to repair the window. I contacted Safelite's executive team, who then had Michelle call me from the local Safelite shop and she acted like she hadn't already been informed of what happened. I had to explain the whole story to her and not once did she say sorry on behalf of Safelite. She placed me on hold and came back to tell me that since I was not home at the time their tech was repairing my window, I was not able to sign the pre inspection paper on my car.(I have a brand new 2013 car that had no prior damage and the tech knew someone else was home if he needed anything) Michelle was very rude and not understanding of the situation. I proceeded to ask for the manager and go figure he was off work till the following week. My entire experience with Safelite has been a complete NIGHTMARE. On top of all this, the representatives who I called to schedule my appointment got the service address completely wrong multiple times and I had to call back to fix it. When I asked about the tinting on the window  the representative gave me false information that they would tint the window before installing it (Safelite doesn't do window tinting at all.) I would highly recommend finding another auto glass company for your window needs.

First time there, unbelievably disappointed. We tried their "Suicide" wings and they do NOT live up to their name. Suicide flavor tastes like straight red chile powder... Nothing more.
To make it worse, they charged us one dollar extra for this flavor and no where on their menu board with pricing does it say  you will have to pay that. 
Buffalo Bell you really need to give me my dollar back. Completely disappointed and dissatisfied.

Second big let down is the fact they do not offer lemon pepper. If i could give less than one star I would.

Preservation hall started in 1961 and clock stopped ticking there ever since. The tables, fans, lights are still from back in the day and they add that old-time feel. 

The bands are absolutely amazing! This was the real jazz! well worth the 45 min wait for tickets

There are angels working in the kitchen because the food here is  heavenly AND DIVINE! I ordered the red beans and rice with sausage AND fried chicken. Both were demolished within minutes! LORDT, LORDT LORDT!!!

Awful. Sagging molded ceiling tiles, AC condensation dripping in our food. I actually called the health inspector from there and he said they had been cited several times for the same thing. Gross, gross, gross. Huge crowd there and I don't understand because the food was terrible. We were told they had the best tacos in Nashville. So wrong.
Best shrimp and grits!  The bread pudding is also a must try, I couldn't stop eating it.

I dropped off a bike to have two flats  fixed said I needed one tire when  I picked up the bike it had a new tire and a almost  new tire he said he had laying around ,no charge  I recommend  this local business

This was my 1st time here in years. The 1st thing I noticed was the prices. They have been raised WAY the hell up. Most entrees now cost between 16-22 dollars. That would be fine if the food was higher end Italian food. It isn't. 

We waited half an hour for our food and when it arrived a few entrees looked like they had been sitting under a heat lamp for awhile. 2 people in our party had fresh looking food and they remarked that it was delicious. Mine however had noodles stuck together and the clams smelled funny. 

Our waitress seemed overwhelmed by the amount of tables she had. Drink refills took awhile as well as salad refills. She was very attentive and accommodating at the meals end when she was giving us the check. Trying for the big tip no doubt. 

Overall the food was just ok. Nowhere near the quality you'd expect for a 20 dollar entree.  Save your money and go elsewhere.

Delicious, juicy, fried chicken. Thick crust. Biscuits are pretty good but can be dry. They go well with the chicken. 
Be warned the sauces aren't free. Sometimes the staff will talk like things are included in your purchase like "which sauce?" Instead of "would you like sauce" or "would you like to try our apple cider?" As if it's a sample.

I must say I was very disappointed I read the reviews and I had high hopes but I would not go back. I ordered 1/2 slab and 1/2bl of the brisket. When I got home to eat the ribs were so burnt that were bitter and impossible to eat. The brisket looked ok but had absolutely no flavor what so ever. I gave it one star for the service which are nice guys but my food was not what to expect

Been training here for 5 months and it's by far my favorite gym I've been to. Love training in Gus' kickboxing classes as he pushes everyone and really makes em dig deep and give it their all every class. Everyone here is super welcoming and accommodating to your skill level. Great vibe and great offering of classes. Highly recommended

Very attractive surroundings close to the harbor and downtown central area, smallish menu, we attended Sunday brunch and both ate ramen , chicken was rather bland and the broth was weak but the miso hamburger was very good. At the end of the day $15 for a bowl of ramen is expensive so it better be pretty damn good and 1/2 is not good enough , doubtful we will return

Wedding Customers of Skybox Event Center: Have recent events left you scrambling for a venue for your happy day? North Hills Country Club will provide Ceremony and Reception space to you at a DEEPLY DISCOUNTED Rate. (based on our availability and proof of your deposit payment to Sky Box). We have been in business for 110 years, and we are not going anywhere. Call Mark Walsh or contact me via our website

Stopped in after reading the reviews to give it a try. Restaurant had been opened for well over an hour. Heard and smelled someone cooking (Pans shuffling around) in back, said Hello several times but after 5 minutes gave it up. Started to worry after I got home that maybe the person was in trouble and drove back to find customers coming in and out so I relieved. Unfortunately I'd already eaten by that time. I'll try again in the near future.

I had a sushi burrito and I loved it! I was a little nervous. Would the seaweed wrap be chewy? Would it stay together? Would the flavors work? The sushi burrito anxiety was real and it took me awhile to try it. If you feel like this, don't worry. It is not that scary. 

The Spot is combined with Ha Long Bay. You can actually order Pho with your sushi burrito! Anyway, if you walk into "The Spot" side of the restaurant, you will see that you order your burrito like you would a certain fast food Mexican burrito.

First you pick burrito, bowl or salad. Then you pick your protein. You can pick two or three for a higher price. Then you pick sauce, veggies, and toppings. Then you watch your beauty be wrapped into a burrito. 

I ordered a burrito with salmon and tempura shrimp (I highly recommend both). I then asked about the sauce and was recommended the spicy sauce since I am a heat fiend. I added cucumber, carrots, and jalapenos. I then added sesame seeds and little crunch wontons for texture. 

Some of the things that you could also add that I remember were tuna, corn, cilantro, red onion, avocado (upcharge), asparagus (upcharge). There were a lot of other choices too, but that is what I can recall.  

I grabbed a drink, a container of soy and lots of napkins (note: grab extra! Burritos are a little messy if you are like me and dip in soy).

The first bite was magical. It was super fresh, delicious, salty and crunchy all at once. Each subsequent bite just reinforced my joy. I polished it off and left very happy. I will definitely return soon. It is a little pricey, but I think that it is worth it. You have to try a sushi burrito if you are a sushi fan. You will love it!

Simplicity and attention to ingredients is highlighted here.  Anything is delicious and expertly prepared.  The prosciutto lemon tagliatelli is the best southern Italian pasta I've had stateside.  Byob.  Not for the claustrophobic.

I have only been here late at night. (They stay open late on weekdays!)

I have only ordered the $5 pint and slice. (Bargain!)

I have only been served by fantastic bartenders. (!!)



Those three things deserve four stars in my humble opinion.....I guess I'm easy to please.  

It's the perfect low-key joint for a midnight snack.
Prompt & friendly service, attentive without being overwhelming.  Delicious sushi rolls & Nigiri.  The Hurricane roll is detectable!  A great experience!

This place was in the middle of nowhere.  Some random ass log cabin.

It literally is a log cabin - with separate rooms within the one restaurant.  Probably USED to be a house!

We ordered rabbit, elk, pork ribs, and stuffed chicken.  My personal order was split between elk/ribs, but I tried everything.  Everything was delicious.  Elk is lean and very juicy.  Rabbit is.. well, tasted somewhat like chicken.  I really liked the ribs.  Chicken was very good too.

Not sure if I will ever order elk or rabbit again, but I definitely enjoyed my sample.  I ordered the elk just to say that I've eaten it.

Free cheesecake for dessert (Birthday celebration).  Mango something cheesecake?  Wow!  Great!

I understand that reservations are necessary - probably busiest between 530pm-7pm.  We arrived at 7pm and it seemed like things were dying down.

Rightfully so because driving out of this mountain it is pitch black and you are driving around winding curves.  If you do not know where you are going or are not from the area, be prepared with a map.  I felt like our drive home was different than the route we took getting there.  Maybe because I couldn't see anything.

Perhaps I'm a bit jaded right now as I am applying to Grad Schools for my MBA, but IUPUI charges you $10 to send your transcripts to other schools. So every school I want to apply to, not only do I have to pay their application fee, but then I have to give IUPUI $10 for every transcript. As if I didn't give them enough money throughout my 4 years in undergrad, they want to gouge you for as much money as humanly possible. Many of my other colleagues that are applying to Grad Schools don'
t have this issue. Their colleges send their transcripts free of charge. Must be nice...

I love driving across the Ben Franklin Bridge. The view of Philadelphia is priceless. While riding across the bridge, you get a great view of the Philadelphia skyline. The bridge can become a little backed up during rush hour. The Ben Franklin Bridge is one of my favorite bridges to ride across.

So there was so much that could have been so good here, and it ended up going downhill.

So myself and three others stayed here for the past week. it is a great hotel it seems, and it is in a prime location on Bourbon Street. (in fact, it takes up teh whole 200 block)

Well designed, nice old school class. Tremendous lobby, great facilities, etc.. Beautiful Pool, Nice little garden area with Orange trees, etc.

If you are worried about noise, dont be. We were on the 5th floor,and could not hear a peep from Bourbon Street, even on a Saturday!

The Beds are comfortable, the rooms nice, and amenities everything you would want. 

I love the classy, old school feel in the lobby, with the message wall behind the front desk and more.


So if it was so comfortable, then why only the three stars?

Well, the first is the service. we had 3 incidents. Not 1,Not 2, but THREE (we stayed form Thursday - Thursday - 7 nights)

1. We got food on Saturday night. We called and asked for plates and flatware. They said " sure,we will be right up". They never showed. We called again. They still didnt show. No happy

2. Sunday- room cleaning never came. WE thought, maybe it was because of timing. We were up early to go to the Rock n Roll marathon, and got back around 1, and were in the room till 4. So we figured that maybe, we were in there when they came by... benefit of the doubt..

3. Tuesday - well, again. no house cleaning. But we left early int he morning. And came back in the afternoon. Not cleaned. SO when we left for dinner at 5, we went to the front desk to complain. They said they would have it cleaned so when we got back it would be all set.
Wel, we got back,and it still had not been cleaned. At least they brought us clean towels.

So three distinct service problems that soiled our opinion of an otherwise very nice hotel. It could have been great, t could have been the best, and it could have got me to come back more and more

But it seems they have luxury pretensions and decor without the service to match. I will have to think before staying there again, which is a disappointment.

I would not tell anyone to NOT look at it, but think of what you find important, and take it how you will

ps. twice during our stay the elevators were on the fritz as well. One was not working and the other was malfunctioning.

pps... if you want ot use the pool, and the temps are under 70 degrees, make sure to ask hours before. We were interested in going for a swim in the heated pool in 65 degree temps... but it wasnt on, and were told it would take 4-5 hours to get warmed up!

Went back a third time for 18 inches of the Big Baller, Saint Louis Style, at the end of last week and just enjoyed some leftovers for lunch! SO Good! As always it was a pleasure to chat with Big B about pizza, the SLNPC family, and future zaa plans. Next time, we are for sure going to get the Christine. Steak pizza, I can't wait to eat it and tell you all about it! Check out the new pics, we're 'rackin' em up! ;)

Very inexpensive you get what you pay for it's directly one street from Washington Avenue which is downtown St Louis and the pool is ice cold when you go in in the dryer does not dry you're clothes.. Almost a great location for the Rams in the Cardinal games.  I was here for 2&a half to 3 weeks because it's super close to where I was going to live in I am now... But no free buffets in the rooms walls are very thin so you hear everything above you in on the side view and its kinda weird

Loved their noodles in peanut sauce, a refreshing  change. I had the lamb shrimp and beef family pot special. It was seasoned perfectly(but beware, if you're averse to spicy dishes this restaurant is not for you. The spring rolls were also very nice but I wish there was more variety for the dipping sauce, soy really didn't do it for me. This is a nice family restaurant  and best of all, contrary to popular belief, you are not hungry an hour later after dining here!

Sometimes this place is spot on, like the time I had the tasting menu with morels and a cream sauce, others it's pretty horrendous. Took my dad there after raving about it, and he ordered their signature burger, and it came out luke warm despite the fact we were one of the only ones in there, and the rest of the meal was less than stellar as well. Service is also hit or miss; one day your server will be just the right amount of attentive, the next they are no where to be found.

Came with my sister after a day spent at San Xavier Mission. We were greeted as we walked in the door, our waitress was very sweet and friendly. My sister says "the soup was so good and I like how they put the water pitcher on your table". I had two tacos and I would get them again. Very good.

Bicycle revolutions is my designated neighborhood bike shop. With a somewhat limited selection, and slightly higher prices, they're not my all time favorite. But, time after time, I find myself coming here because they're just so damn friendly and convenient. Brian is really great. I bought my first new bike (all the previous ones were hand me downs) here. At the time I didn't know much about what I was looking for. Brian helped me find a bike that fit correctly and was pretty much exactly what I was looking for. 

Six months later, I've learned a lot more about bikes. I would avoid buying a complete bike again, and instead build one myself. And I'm sure that Bicycle Revolutions could help me do that. But all in all, they're a great shop, and are largely responsible for getting me into such a wonderful activity. Oh and I just bought my helmet here! Good selection and they helped me find one that fit. Get a helmet :)
Amazing pizza! Great flavoring and love their gluten free pizza.  My family and I will keep going here :)

Here for a wedding in the area and stopped over in Santa Barbara for some wine tasting and beach. We looked this place up online ahead of time and thought it was unique being at the end of the pier. We headed to the restaurant after trying out a few tasting rooms. 

Note, they do not accept reservations and are busy. It's a tiny indoor outdoor space. Their system is write your name on a sheet of paper at the front. If your luck, someone is there to tell you the length of a wait. What you don't know, are the people who are no shows due to the wait but their names are still on the list. It could be a short wait, but also pretty long, specially for an outdoor seat. 

Do what we did, if the line is short, order from the walk-up take-out window. I thought it was lovely and perfect for a wharf.  While in line you get to view the lobsters and giant crab in their tanks. View a menu as you wait so you're ready when you get to the window. They are in a hurry!  Order your grub, stake out a nearby picnic table and listen intently for them to holler your name. I love the whole action of it all. I would like to dine at the actual restaurant some day, but this was still fun!

We ordered the lobster bisque bread bowl, super yum, think and creamy. I ordered the lobster tacos. Holey lobster! They made sure it was lobster filled I wish there was more sauce or filling than what was provided. It's more food than you can finish with the rice included. My boyfriend thoroughly enjoyed the crab cakes. We also ordered an extra order of onion rings (even though the crab cakes come with some). We were not able to finish our extra order of onion rings. Manager your eyes, they may be larger than your stomach!

I am very picky about my stars and I only give 5 to exception dining experiences. Don't get me wrong, I'm not a yelp hater, but I think 4 stars is excellent. I would give'em 4,5 if It was possible!!
I had a dinner date with my husband today and it was awesome. Hands down best sushi in Santa Barbara so far (we've tried about 4 places downtown).
We got there (Saturday around 7:45pm), there was a line, but since it was only the 2 of us there was a table available right away.
The restaurant was packed but we still got excellent service! (Thanks, Sheena). The food came out in a timely manner and everything was delicious!!!
I def recommend the garlic soy edamames, the miso soup (devine) and the yellow tail melt press box. Btw, it was my first time having the so call pressed box roll and I loved it!!!!
Anyways, don't hesitate to come to Sakana, you won't regret it! I can't wait to have an excuse to go back again.

Ehhh, I'll give it 3 stars. Could've  be better, could've be worse... 

For starters, we were greeted & continued to get great service from our server, Jordan.

So we start with the  "specialty," $12.50 margaritas. Straight "heartburn" sour mix. So sad; I  thought I was buying a drink that'd give me an excuse to gamble funds at the nearest Craps table. Not exactly. 

Next, I ordered the Calamari as my entrée. Holy Slimy Tentacles, Batman! 
*&%$! 
 I hovered over my Hubby's $5.00, Happy Hour, Burger entrée. I barely touched my Calamari, and just followed his lead. 

Jordan, you rock. The Brew's Happy Hour FOOD rocks, just steer clear of the mixed drinks. and slimy tentacles. 
*sigh*

On any given night in NOLA, there is so much music going on that you may overlook checking what's on the schedule here but rest assured, this is a great venue and worthy of your time. It's easy to walk here from the FQ or CBD and there are quite a few bars/restaurants on the way so make an adventure of it. The sound is great and their staff are pretty cool.  Definitely have Howlin' Wolf on your radar when in NOLA.

Pro tip: they have an ATM but it doesn't always work so if you want to use cash, grab some before you get here.

I ordered their avocado shake and chicken bahn mi. Avocado shake was good and tasty. Chicken bahn mi was kind of tough and lack a bit of flavor. I would recommend their shakes or shaved ice desserts but not their sandwiches or hot entrees.

I brought my 9 year il daughter in to share a day of manis and pedis. They were fairly busy for a Sunday afternoon. We both received classic spa pedicures. My daughter had a manicure and chose designs for her fingers and nails. Everyone was friendly. We did have to wait about 10 mins but we were walk ins so we did not mind. The prices seems comparable to the area salons. The facility was clean and try did sterilize all the equipment before use. They do accept charge/debit but with a $15 minimum... And tips have to be cash only. I was satisfied with the pedicure but a little more care on cut downs would be nicer. I did get nicked 3 different places. We would most likely return.

I've seen this place multiple times and frequent crate all the time. I heard that the drinks can be to sweet but figured I should check it out for myself.  So the service is nice. I got the matcha green tea snow with grass jelly. I asked for lightly sweetened.  A very refreshing smooth drink! I recommend.  Will have to try other flavors next time I'm in the mood for something here

Came by to meet friends for some cocktails and light appetizers prior to dinner. Great ambiance. Love the interior and live piano. Very classy. Would be perfect for Date Night! Great service too. Shrimp spring roll and Lobster Tacos were delicious!

Our food was good but kitchen time was very slow. We tried calabacitas scramble, hamburger, and an eggs/sausage (cajun) plate. Cajun sausage was quite good with some kick. Eggs were fine along with potatoes and toast. Burger was good, as were refried beans. Other items were average.

The most notable thing about our 12:45 Sunday brunch was the cooking time, about 20 minutes. This seemed to be a factor of one cook doing all cooking with occasional waffle help from a server. 

I think the summary is: walk in, count the patrons, look into the kitchen. If two people are working the griddle or teaming up, or if there are fewer than 10-12 customers, sit down. If not, head elsewhere. There are plenty of good breakfasts in Tucson at similar or better prices and without long cooking delays.

Went there for breakfast this morning.  Drive-thru was quick.  

Had the chicken, egg and cheese on the multigrain bagel and hash browns.  

Food was delivered to me in less than 1 minute hot.  

Very good start to the morning with courteous people at the window.
Won't buy juice or batteries anywhere else. This place has the best quality. And they're always super helpful!

Absolutely delicious. First off, there were endless choices of appetizers and you can't go wrong with any of them. Filling and awesome! Then the entrees were even better - from the steak frites to the fried chicken. Has a full bar and everything. And it's right in the neighborhoods a little away from the downtown area of Philly.

Had to review this place after going for a friend's birthday and having the cous-cous. I've been to Morocco  (best friend is Moroccan) and the cous-cous tasted JUST like her grandmother's. It was moist (sometimes you find it too dry) - The half a chicken was also very delicious. We went on a Tuesday and it was slow so it was a great place for a party of 10 during the week. Good service, highly recommend.

Should be called the Yucky Duck. Never thought a place could have worse food the the prior tenant(Louis) . Well I was wrong about that....way wrong. Started with Nachos's . I thought Nachos were suppose to be hot when served. Not some luke warm  canned Sams club cheese sauce poured on top of chips. Then topped with cold shredded cheese and cold pulled pork. Next came my wifes nasty salad with frozen chicken parts. You could taste the freezer burn on the them. I got the Hot Horse Hamburger,  it was not hot of curse. I think they precook the meat and let it set . A burger that is brought out to the table should steam a little bit when you bite into it. Nothing, not a bit of heat came off it. It was sold cold the cheese did not even melt. No wonder the sign on the door , says "hiring all positions"   I give this place 6 months at best.


Wow, took less then 6 months to close.

Hands down the best fried chicken in saint louis!! Go now! You can order by the piece or by the bird. I loved the thigh. We also tried the deviled eggs which were dressed beautifully and loved the little pickles!! Try the bread basket the biscuits are as good as the chicken! Other sides include slaw, greens, amazing mashed potatoes, creamed corn. I had a great manhattan tonight.., full bar with great selection of bourbons and whiskey. Great vibe here with the intentional use of raw materials. Feels like a true road house. So impressed with bens ability to create such great restaurants! Next Italian perhaps? Please Ben?! : )

One of the nicest places in Belleville.  I'd been there to sample a few wines and beers before, but never got around to trying any of the food.  Took the wife Saturday night.  We had the pear/Gorgonzola/honey appetizer.  Honestly couldn't tell it contained any pear..and the honey drizzled on top seemed a bit odd, but it worked and was very good.  We each had a flatbread pizza and while my Margarete was very good the Chicken/spinach/feta that my wife had was awesome.  Even though the main front room was pretty crowded the service was outstanding.  While my taste leans more toward cheaper dives, the bill for food, three glasses of wine and a large beer, including tip. was "only" a little over $60.  Very good selection of both wine and beers - if they'd only get Rogue Shakespeare Stout on tap, I'd have a hard time staying away from the place.
I ordered presents for my staff. They were very reasonably priced and they were delivered to my office! The staff loved the gift. Thanks, HK NOLA!
Fast service.  Friendly waiter.  Good food.  Reasonable price :)

Unsanitary.  The woman giving my my manicure had a cold or the flu, and kept sneezing.  They don't swap out tubs in between customers, just swirl cleaner in the bath.  My girlfriend and I got pedicures there and both of us came away with athletes' foot.  I hesitated to write this, as it feels bad to tell a business this, but perhaps this is a chance to clean up their act.

We have been to numerous restaurants in Tarpon Spring.  This is our first choice every time.

It's a little pricier than most on the strip but it's worth a couple of extra dollars.   

It's clean and the food is very fresh!  

I love the view of the street because I'm a serous people watcher.

If you're ever in Tarpon Springs, give it a try, you won't be sorry!
My favorite Indian in the nashville area. Try the sweet and sour chicken soup the goat anything and the lassy. Just amazing food. Spice yet super flavorful.

Chain.  This was my first visit to a Ruth's Chris, and to be honest, I was pretty disappointed.  I've heard the hype over and over about how great this place is, blah blah blah, but it was 'good'.  Here's the story:

The steak was decent.  it's a plain peice of meat in the middle of a hot-ass plate that can burn your fingerprints off (speaking from experience).  My dinner was overcooked (medium well vs. medium rare), and it took long enough that I wasn't willing to send it back.  The sides we decent, but certainly nothing to write home about.  

The atmosphere was a bit stuffy.  Clearly I see what they are going for in their 'private-steakhouse' setting, but for what you pay, I was looking to be a little more imporessed.  

Perhaps my steak got a little too well-done while I was dipping my fingers in my water?  Perhaps ordering a vodka tonic v. a bottle of wine suggested I have no taste?  Any one of these things could be true, but all in all - marginal.

Upside: 
2 blocks from Bourbon and Canal.
Easy walking distance to the entire Quarter and canal
Trolley to the Garden District Right out front
Pleasant staff
good sized room
nice rate
sweet breakfast buffet (Hello, waffle maker!)

not so upside:
clearly an older property (talking to you, shower)
our room looked out on a brick wall
loud, frisky neighbors (NOLA is not an earthquake zone)

I'd stay there again, mostly because we didn't plan to spend much time in our hotel room (and didn't!).

When ever I walk into this restaurant, I'm reminded of the Brady Bunch house. Everything about this place spells "comfort." It's decorated beautifully, and the food is great. I had the "Thanksgiving Dinner" and loved it. Everyone in our group (5 of us) really enjoyed the rood and atmosphere.

Went in looking for Pete's Wicked Strawberry Blonde today, came out with Lancaster Strawberry Wheat and a sense of purpose that went far beyond cracking open my newfangled bottle o' beer.  The employees (er, dudes) are friendly, savvy, encouraging and let me leave my groceries in an out of the way corner while browsing the wide  selection. Rarely does it make fiscal sense for me to put together a miscellaneous 6 pack but it's nice to have the option and makes a killer birthday present for adventurous beer lovin' pals. Also, there's often a grey cat crashed out on a high shelf or wandering around the store. Nothing says cozy like a sleeping kitty and a store full of beer.

The food was fresh and wonderful! The staff was friendly and accommodating. You can tell everything is made from scratch and the flavors shine though:) 

Great find and happy we stumbled upon this restaurant.

January 2017:

This is one of those metal and wood modern restaurants. We ate breakfast here on a freezing morning between snow storms. So, forgiving me for saying that this place feels cold. On the other hand the wait staff is among the best I have experienced. The others in our party ordered typical egg, potatoes, meat, and toast breakfasts; I ordered the apricot granola pancakes. What I expected was granola and pieces of apricot baked into the pancakes. What I received was four beautiful, fluffy pancakes covered with baked apricot granola. The pancakes were delicious on their own. A little syrup made the pancakes better. Adding the granola pushed them over the top. My only regret was that I could only eat three of the four pancakes. (Our wait-person told me that they do not offer a short stack version.) I stole a piece of bacon from my wife. It was good but a little undercooked for my taste. I like my bacon crisp.

March 2018:

It was cold and windy outside so we retreated to the Roundabout Grill for dinner. I ordered tomato bisque soup and house-made rigatoni. The soup was so good that I was tempted to cancel the rigatoni and get a couple more cups of soup. I am glad I do not do that because the rigatoni was about the best I have ever enjoyed. The flavor balance was excellent with just the right amount of sausage. 

The next morning I ordered the apricot granola hot cakes that I had eaten in January 2017. They seemed a bit drier than the last time. Slightly over cooked? It took a bit more syrup to get them just right but they were as good as I remembered them.

Booked this tour through Groupon - took this tour on the first day - which I highly recommend that you do!! Learned some very interesting history and received tips on how to tour the French Quarter like a local!  Best tip - go to Rouse's (supermarket) for Crystal's hot sauce and Slap you Mama seasoning...save $$$$!!

I would agree with the review of it being old money and botox, romantic couples and everyday business men, a comfortable and fun mix. Food good, drinks good oveall good time. We were left alone to conduct our business and not rushed out the door. Pricey but, convienient so, I would return for certian occasions.
Pick your flavor, pick your toppings and watch your ice cream be made in front of you. $6.50 one size, unlimited toppings, great taste! We will definitely be back to try more combinations.

Restaurants in hotels give me pause, but this is certainly not the typical instance.

The space is not very large, but the tables are not cramped.  The service was very friendly and there was a good soundtrack of New Orleans classics playing.

The food was well-prepared and tasty. The brasserie trope consists of comfort foods, to a great extent, not haute cuisine, but the quality and prepartion are outstanding. There are daily specials, making it more affordable.  I had the rabbit stew, which was quite tasty, but a little short on meat content.  My wife had a burger, which was ok, but pricey.  My other table mates had chicken and schnitzel, which were both  quite good.  The fries were just about perfect.

This definitely goes on my favorites list.

Food was ok....nothing really to write home about.  Server was really friendly and attentive. Drinks were yummy.  Overall, not bad but we probably wouldn't go back. It was the first place we saw when we left our hotel.

I recently had my jeep throw an altenstor pulley on 476. had AAA tow it to Kings. Jay and Dennis Rock !!! they had my Jeep back to me the next day and i was 100 % impressed by the world class customer service experience as well as and more importanly the knowledge and mechanical skills this company provided. bottom line they treated my baby the way i treat her.. thanks Jay and Dennis
Fantastic pizza and  cold beer!  This is the best Chicago styled pizza in St. Louis!

If you have the choice between taco bus, Taco Bell or here ... Hands down: tacoson!!! The beef flautas were huge and delicious. I tried my husbands rice and it was perfect. Will definitely be back soon!
AMAZING!!! Got the chicken with baked beans and cole slaw. Lots of food, tasted amazing, and was pretty fast too.

Ok, I was super skeptical of this place. I work around this place, and this becomes the place to hit up after a long shift. I am from Texas, so when I walked up and it looked like a trashy Mexican restaurant...I knew it was going to be fabulous. The best Mexican places are like that!! 

Salsa is decent. They have a spicy salsa and if you mix that with the mild it's perfect. I got a frozen margarita and it was good. I am silly and thought it would need an extra floater but it did not haha! I didn't end up using my shot of tequila! I got some combo meal with a taco and enchilada. I thoroughly enjoyed my food. I am looking forward to many more after work happy hours here!!
Poor service. Bad quality chicken. Simply rude and not worth the southern fare chicken. I've had so much better.

This is a quiet quaint place hidden from the traffic. Madre is a clean modern looking restaurant. Tacos are the main food. Sandwichs, guaq and chips, beer and other drinks are available also. My wife had the Ensinada fish taco ( Baja style grilled). I had the Idaho Potato and chorizo, and mushroom tacos.  All were superb and unique with sauces and ingredients. I will gladly go there again and enjoy the quiet atmosphere and great food. Service was fantastic also. I love the incentive menu.

This place had always intrigued me. Saw a picture of the "spicy beef chow fun" and it looked amazingly savory and greasy so I ordered that today. 

The total came out to be 9.71 for the one entree which I thought was pricy but would be justified if they portion size was big enough. Unfortunately it wasn't. By the end of my meal wasn't nearly as full as I had wanted to be, especially since I paid $10. However, the noodles came out tasty and didn't disappoint- perfect amount of spiciness and the beef was yummy too. 

The place was busier than I expected considering the poor ratings on Yelp. I personally thought there was nothing wrong with service and that the menu was pretty big and impressive. Just had to dock two stars off for price & portion size.

Person at the bakery refused to write on a cake from their case and refused to call someone who would. 
Left and went to Acme. No problem there at all.

Very dissapointed!!!! I made a appointment over 2 weeks ago only to be called 30 mins before and having the appontment cancelled. No sorry offered and just a when would you like to rebook. I find it funny that I get told on 2 sepperate occasions that they will need 24 hours notice before i cancell yet they only give me 30 mins!!! Seems like they dont feel like my time is worth the same ammount as theirs. I will never go here and i will ensure that everyone i speak to knows about the experience i have had with this place. Horrible!!!!

This is the perfect restaurant you want to order from for your mother-in-law's birthday if she's single and has an expensive insurance policy. We ordered an order of sweet and sour (hopefully it's) chicken and it was more effective than any laxatives available.

ahhh, I love this place(: I crave it as I write this review. I love love love their hot & sour soup, Hawaiian bbq chicken, stir fry & sushi!  mmmm, idk what was going on with those other reviews, but the food is great. the servers don't speak English, but it's a buffet so you don't need them anyway! who cares, I just love getting down on this place it's soooo good. :)

I enjoy Ava for brunch and a large party/reservation. The food is prepared for softer palettes with not as much seasoning, but overall a fresh taste. The staff is friendly, but can be easily overwhelmed when there is a lot of guests. The drinks are my favorite.

Worst store. Customer service is the worst. Everyone knows it. I've given this store countless opportunities to make it up but they still seem to not care about their customers at all. Don't get me wrong - there are definitely employees there that are helpful but when it comes to honoring prices or making up for mistakes (damaged items or missing pieces) - they just assume the customer is lying or at fault. I'm done with the store on walnut. Sorry for those employees that seemed like they cared

So good! Been to Pizzeria Vetri twice so far since it's opening. Both times, i've been wowed. This is the closest to real italian pizza as you're going to get statewide. Nice charred crust, loaded with fresh, tasty toppings.
Drinks wise, make sure to get an Aperol Spritz. Aperol and Prosecco, what could be bad right? The wine is OK. I'd honestly prefer a better selection, knowing what Vetri serves at his other establishments, but I understand the point of keeping this place as a in and out Pizzeria. Seems like their focus is more on craft beers, similar to Alla Spina. 
First of all, you must start with a rotolo. Those things are insane! Little bundle of joy filled with mortadella, topped with pistachios. I could eat those as my meal alone. Their pizza specials are usually the best way to go. The most recent time we went we had a pizza with fresh peaches on it that was to die for. 
Make sure you save room for dessert though, because they are phenomenal. You'll have a tough time deciding which one to get, trust me ! (we usually end up ordering them all, and taking them home since we're just too stuffed). The Nutella pizza is awesome! (that basically speaks for itself, its Nutella pizza, people) The Affogato is a must. Espresso with a nice helping of Soft Serve Ice Cream. The Fried Pizza Dough is what gets me every time. Its got citrus fennel sugar on every single bite. MMmmmmm.
I see everyone's saying that Stephen Starr's pizza place is better than this place. I've never been to Stella, but honestly, I don't think I need to. Pizzeria Vetri is hands down the best in my eyes. Definitely give it a try !

I know there are so many fancy local places to get a good burger and I'm cool with all that, but my favorite burger in the city is still at Five Guys. I get my junior cheeseburger "all the way" and share a medium fry with my husband and feel like I've eaten enough food for days. Love the flavor, love the casual atmosphere, and love having such a basic, non-boring amazing burger. Sometimes simple is the way to go!

It definitely gets crowded, but NOLA is a destination. There's nothing we can do about it. But I love the window seats. Gets the breeze and you can people watch while seeping your coffee and eat your croissant.

Dips are AMAZING as are the beef fajitas.
I've tried the Mexican pizza, chicken flautas, and chicken chimichanga to my liking, as well. Service can range from average to superb - never bad.

Went there for the lunch buffet and it was very good. Lots of options both meat and vegetarian. More choices then other places I've been too. They had amazing deserts also in the buffet. Would definitely recommend.
Dr. Sandy is great, the staff is great and the waiting room is fun! My child actually looks forward to going.
Food is great and service is better. Good daily specials and plenty of tv's to watch any sporting event.

This is a gorgeous place to drive through, hike or picnic BUT shame on you park service for charging $15 for a day (it's actually a week) pass but really. We live local and like to take visitors but paying $15 for a day is ridiculous. I mean come on-- most visitors drive through and even if you offered a $10 day pass and $15 wrk pass but $15 for a day is too much!  Recently I was at a charity luncheon and a group of people (locals) started talking about this-- at LEAST offer a day pass for locals with a Tucson drivers license!!!

Literally the worst excuse for sushi I've ever eaten in my life.

First, the owners are not Japanese, and know next to nothing about Japanese food. If you are going to call yourself a Japanese restaurant, at least take cooking lessons or something.
