Second, the rice in the numerous rolls we ordered was overcooked goo, and not vinegared. The low quality soy sauce that came with the sushi was mixed with water - utterly vile.

We also ordered tempura, which was basically an oily, greasy mess - basically deep fried assorted vegetables. 

We ended up throwing everything away and cooking our own dinner. It really was that disgusting.

We went to Salute while visiting family in Spring Hill.  They had won Hernando's "Best Italian Restaurant" for the past two years and wanted to experience the food ourselves.  The ambiance is OK - nothing to write about. Is in a strip center located in Sprng Hill Drive/Mariner Boulevard. I believe the space used to be an Annie's Banana's...  it is not luxurious by any means but adequate.

 We visited on a Sunday night when the restaurant was not too busy.  The service was very attentive and timely.  There were several nightly specials that were also offered in addition to the regular menu.  There was a piano player - a nice touch and added ambiance.

The warm bread served is in three flavors - regular, olive and pepperoni and is to DIE FOR.  It is lightly toasted, warm and has a great flavor.  I personally could make a meal out of this and a salad.  Salad or soup is served with each meal,  There were choices for vegetarias (but the soup had bacon in it) with plenty of pasta, veal and seafood choices.  Portion size was larger than average and the food was very tasty - traitional Italia fare.  Everyone enjoyed their meals and some had to take portions home - they were too full to finish.

No entree (except specials) was priced higher than $20 so there is a good value for the meal and portion size. We will probably return on subsequent visits to Spring Hill.  The previous night we went to Brain's Place in Hernando Beach which I personally would recommend over Salute - just a personal preference.

The restaurant does offer nightly specials - 2 meals for $25.95 M/T/W and occasionally offers 6 course dinners with wine tastings for $75+ - a good value if you are a wine connoseur.

I'll start by saying that I'm not a coffee buff, but I certainly enjoy a nice cup of coffee. I have to say that I wasn't wowed by the cafe mocha or the Americano that I've had from there, but I'd still go back to grab & go, because it's in my neighborhood.

Grab and go is the way to go, in my opinion. Last time I stopped in, there were at least two dogs sitting obediently by their owners, who were on their laptops. And it was pretty full. I was never really the type to linger in a coffee shop alone, though.

I noticed the set of rules posted by the milk and sugar - they really made me feel welcome. Very inviting set of rules. Appreciative of their customers they are.

This place has quickly become my favorite local coffee shop.  The music is always unique, the staff seems genuinely happy to be there which easily translates to good service, and the cucumber and hummus sandwich is so good I've yet to try anything else. They serve lovely hand crafted lattes and such too. Although I'm not local to Wayne, it's so nice seeing the regulars get recognized by name by the staff; a true mark of a successful restaurant of the community. If you need a place where you can feel comfortable working solo on your laptop or catching up with a friend, this is a great place to do it!

What's up with quality here? Really bad. I got a small mac n cheese and it was cold! Salad box was half full - seriously like 1/2 cup of salad and 2 tiny wedges of tomato (Greek). Not up to quality of other Panera s. Maybe they are a victim of own success. They are swamped at lunch - which could explain the poor quality. Maybe check out sub depot or pie 5 - more Lunch restaurants are opening in the area. Time to try them.

This was hands down one of the best restaurants I've been to! The Hot chicken sandwich was amazing with a side of fried tomatoes it was delicious! And our waitress was so nice and personable! Would definitely come back here the next time I'm in Tennessee! Oh and make sure you try there sweet tea, it's some of the best

I shop there at least once a week and multiple times frequently on the weekends. I have moved a few times and have visited several Home Depot's in the country and like you all have spent thousands. This store is as good or bad as any other.  I noticed a couple of bad reviews on here which I don't think are really fair. I don't care to be sold solar panels while looking for a door knob but all the staff has been kind and helpful to me so I am satisfied thus far. I went to pick up a new mower that my wife ordered me online and I thought it was a nice touch to be given a bottle of water for each of us. I never have problems returning things at Home Depot in general and that is important when it comes to doing thing yourself which I really enjoy.

This is one of the best places to eat in St. Louis. It's pricey, but worth it. I would strongly suggest choosing this restaurant over anything in Clayton. Please, please get the butcher's plate.. so good.
The crab omelette is amazing along with the banana foster French toast! Very chill, comfortable place to eat breakfast. And yummy coffee! I will be back next time im in New Orleans!

Authentic Diner & Greasy Spoon! A great stop if you're in or around downtown Clearwater.

In summary, this place will take you back and the food is EXACTLY what you would want from a corner diner. The food is well executed and extremely well priced and the ambiance is diner-perfect...even down to the fixed counter stools. The staff is very friendly and it truly makes you feel as though you've come home to the corner restaurant your parents used to take you to.

This is a MUST for a great hangover breakfast cure or just to fill that craving for some good 'ole 'home cooking' that warms the heart. 

The philly-cheese & egg breakfast sandwich is superb! Biscuits and gravy are fresh and homemade. Egg omelettes are fluffy and loaded with fixings. 

Eat local and give this place a try!

They have parking on site so no meters to feed.
i haven't found a nordies i didn't love! i love the selection and the nordy buyers are doing a great job!

We have been living in the area for two years. I have watched the steady decline of this chipotle. 
We eat at chipotle at least two times a week because of our jobs.
This place has become the great guacamole nazis. Instead of the normal sized spoonful that everywhere else gives, this place taps the spoon until it's leveled off. Leaving one with about a 1/4 cup of guac on their burrito or bowl. . I should'nt have to pay $2 for that teeny bit!!!

Next situation I have had with this chipolte is that we stopped in fifteen min before closing. With people in line BEHIND me as well, the counter girl explained they were out of chicken and steak and sour cream and only had enough guac left for one serving .....I called them out "you mean u guys were too lazy to cook up more and restock?!" 
Shrugging her shoulders she replied "do I want something or not?"
The manager person came out after hearing my complaints about paying $10 for a bowl with nothing in it! Comped my bowl but still lazy. 

I've also ordered twice online. Both times they claimed they didn't see it and had to rush to complete once I got there. 

Whomever does the hiring for this chipolte needs to be fired. Their workers suck lately

Stopped in with friends for a quick bite. I ordered the Gator Burger - this was the BEST burger I have had in a long time. Our server was AMAZING - by far the best server we have had while in town - I believe his name was Brad
This is a MUST STOP while in the area

Great tour guide(Tom) with very interesting details along the way, nice samples, and above all, it as FUN!
Also we got lucky and saw a full hitch of Clydesdales and Bud the Dalmatian. We're experienced at brewery tours, but this one is the Holy Grail of brew tours!
What an amazing experience from the time we walked in to the last cosmo. Great service, awesome atmosphere, delightful food, strong tasty drinks, and finally one of the best creme brûlée!!!

Came here for Valentine's Day with another couple and we all loved it!  The food was excellent.  We shared the crawfish with goat cheese appetizer, I had the blackened redfish as my entree which was out of this world, and the red velvet ice cream sandwich for dessert - all-star lineup!  The ambiance is also nice for a real New Orleans style dining experience with very polite wait staff and antique-esque decor.  All around a great experience!

One of the best cupcakes I've ever had.  Been to many cities with cupcakes and some not even being in the USA.  This place lists expected prices along with a great product.  They have plenty of cupcakes to choose from which is always a enjoyable decision.

It's unacceptable to wait 2h30 to have a table, the welcome waitress said 45min at the beginning and then nothing, everything is closed after 10pm so we had to wait... the worst place to end our vacations in New Orleans !

I wouldn't think of calling any company but Family Air for our AC or heating needs. Our experience with them has been totally positive.The guys who work for Family Air are conscientious about doing their best for the customer, and I firmly believe this is at the direction of the owners of Family Air. We have never been pressured into buying a new unit. Charlie's and Kurt's efforts have been focused on making our AC  work, not on selling us something new. That said, when Family Air does suggest that it is time to purchase new HVAC, there is no question that we will have them do the job.

I'm a sucker for that gourmet burger place that every town has and claims to be the best. From Brooklyn to the Bay Area, everybody loves talking about their favorite burger joint, their ode to the Earl of Sandwich's industrialized counterpart. The sandwich, as well as the burger, has really come full circle this century. Once designed to be a quick, no-frills meal for the industrial era's worker, who had neither the time nor luxury to prepare much else, the burger has now evolved into a serious culinary contender, a gourmet choice for the open-minded foodie and traditional diner alike. 

In Philly, for example, you'll hear Center City locals rave about the Shake Shack, or if they're peering through a lace curtain, you might even hear a whisper about the burgers at Butcher & Singer, or Barclay Prime. I'm not going to lie, Stephen Starr knows how to make himself a burger. My friend lives near a burger place in Brooklyn that still drifts into my dreams on occasion. They've got this back patio, great vibe, but all I really remember is that juicy, insurmountable cheeseburger. 

That brings us to Baileys' Range, which now holds a deserving place atop my gourmet burger list. Not only was the Ozark burger one of the most absurdly delicious cheeseburgers I've ever tasted, but given the other options, it was a very difficult choice. The ABC with apples, bacon, and camembert - uh, yes please. The homemade ice cream and milkshakes, the root beer floats with Fitz's Root Beer, the fries with the rooster sauce: this place doesn't have a specialty, it has a dozen. For your 6 year-old or your 60 year-old, your straight-laced burger fan or your boozy friend that wants a cocktail with ice cream - the adult root beer float, for example - Baileys' Range has something for everyone.

In addition to all of this, the portions are small but satisfying and the service is friendly and fast. They really put elbow grease into the decor, a perfect blend of contemporary urban and classic diner. It's not just another Steak N' Shake; Baileys' is its own brand, its own product. I mean, I can't tell you how many burgers I've eaten in my life, so for one to stand out like this must mean its special. It deserves to be a St. Louis institution and I expect one day, it will be.

Great casual food when ever and which ever restaurant you stop in at.  Love their choices and quick, quirky service. I've never had a bad dish, or a bad time here. Not a great formal diner, but they know what and who they are and do a great job of it.  Keep it up.

Came here a few months ago and YIKES!  This place got crowded.  There's barely any room to move now.  I still enjoy the view of the fountain and the streets of Central West End from the patio, but that's about it.  If you reserve a couch spot, it's much better, but there's no room to dance at all anymore.  The crowd also leans towards the more pretentious types.  Phooey.

Went for cafe au lait and beignets and was not disappointed.  Favorite thing was the beignets come out plain and you get to put on your own powdered sugar.  Coffee was delicious and the perfect compliment to the beignets.

Okay, people are too hard on this place.

I had a burger, a few beers, and the brussel sprouts.  The burger was excellent (though it was too huge for me to finish) and the brussel sprouts were good (though not great).  I think the best part of this place might be the space.  Even though the restaurant is pretty big, the atmosphere is home-like and cozy.
employees are great, latte was amazing and had a design, the avocado toast was super good

I was passing through the area one evening, in search of Great Lakes, which I regrettably cannot get in North Jersey (come on, April 22!). After a failed stop at one of the zillion Canals in the area, someone recommended WineWorks.

These days, I am increasingly underwhelmed by the selection at many stores. The mantra of "throw a few Sierra Nevadas and Founders on the shelf so we can say we sell craft beer" doesn't really cut it for me. 

WineWorks, though, impressed me. There was an extensive aisle of refrigerated beer and three aisles of other craft. One aisle was devoted to random singles where you can make your own sixer (I love when places have this and wish more places did), one had big bottles, and another had international craft beers. And they had craft even I had never heard of, from places I'd never have expected like Costa Rica. They have Japanese craft - and not just all Hitachino. They had a very ample selection - the biggest I've seen to date aside from what's at Eataly - of beers from my favorite Italian brewery, Birra del Borgo. 

As the name suggests, the entire right half of the store is dedicated to wine. And I'm sure the selection is fantastic. However, I went in with the intention of grabbing that Great Lakes and walked out with $75 in my bank account. 

The store is clean, bright, and spacious. The cashier was nice. This place is definitely worth a stop if you are in the area and even if you aren't!

I took my 2 dogs today to be groomed and they came back looking great!  They were long over due since we just moved to the area and we didn't know where to take them.  I found this place here on Yelp and I'm glad I decided to give them a try.  I was a little hesitant when I realized it was a house but based on the good reviews I decided to give them a try.  My pups came out with wagging talks and looking great.  I found my dogs groomers! Hooray!  The price for 2 dogs,  even after tip ($75 + $25 for a job well done) was good as well.

I use to love this restaurant. It's close by to my house, has decent food and modest prices. But honestly these last two times I've visited I've come home to an upset stomach. Food tastes great so I'm guessing it's what in the food that's getting me sick? Staff are ok. Seem friendly and over worked. I won't be going back anytime soon. I'm not really a fan of running to the bathroom for 5 hours straight.

What a bargain! Just about 10 bucks a person for a three course lunch. Food was good and filling. Service was great. If you're ever in Phoenixville looking for a cheap meal, Thai Place is definitely worth a stop!
Excellent breakfast burrito and Al Pastor hole in the wall! The menu is different from a standard mexican restaurant - as it caters more to the local population.

My favorite museum by far. Wonderful artworks and revolving exhibits. Shop has tons of great gifts and helpful staff. The Indian market every summer is awesome with artists and handmade work from across the country.

As we are visitors from California we had some problems with our toy hauler and decided to pull off and visit this store. Glad we did! 

Thank you to eddy and billy for your help this morning. Very friendly service and this store has what your looking for. Appreciate the advise and service that was provided. 

Would highly recommend this store for people that are in need of service or repair.

The historic  appearance of the hotel in general, was fantastic.  Why only 3-Stars?  Well, our customer experience while checking in was very unorganized.  The staff was unhelpful.  There aren't many African Americans who stayed at this hotel, and the moment the guy at the front desk laid eyes on us, his attitude was curt, abrupt, unhelpful etc.  I felt as though others like me would have felt 80 years ago.  Months ago we booked a very nice room.  When we arrived, all this man could do was say, as he looked at his computer..I'm so sorry, over and over again.  When asked why he was apologizing so much, he said it was because this room wasn't reserved for us, despite the confirmation letter we received from them some time ago, and even presented to him!
I tried to tell him why we wanted this room, and he talked over me and simply walked away in mid-sentence.  As though I was invisible.  He finally got another employee to help him, and supposedly we got "the room, with a river view".  With no help, we dragged our luggage to our room, only to find out that it was substandard to my liking and expectation.  It was more me than husband, as we had just arrived from the airport, and he just wanted somewhere, anywhere to lay his head.  Half the time our key cards don't work, which means we have to spend our time waiting for an elevator to take us to the lobby to request a key card that works.  How inconvenient!   I am not crazy about the room.  Not crazy about the plumbing sounds coming from our bathroom late at night either.  Unfortunately there are no other hotels to make a new reservation at which means we  have to stay in room 1467  until May 17, 2013...  Mrs Perello wasnt happy about the poor service or the excuses they easily provided.  Nice hotel, horrible service.  We were'nt satisfied until one of the staff members responded to our email plea to them.


Much to my surprise, they did respond and were most helpful beyond our expectations.  Dave was the individual who directly assisted us.  He was personable, professional, realistic and helpful.

I am so happy that they turned this around for us.  On a few levels!
Wonderful food! Elevated and incredible flavors. Only thing I don't like is the loud atmosphere. I eat here any time I'm in Clearwater, and I will continue going back!

I have gone here twice with friends and sat by the var. Their fries and crab cakes are wonderful!! Great place to stop for cocktails. The bartenders are engaging. A must do if you are in the city. Parking garage suggested. Enjoy;;;

Service was decent, better than a lot of times i've been here, its usually awful, and for the poor service that plagues northern liberties, its not a list you wanna top.  but my burrito although it had good flavor, came out like it had been sitting for a while.  Please hold, dos segundos is calling.

Terrific! Fresh, fast, super -reasonable, authentic.  Taco Azteca  - perfect. 
Lunch for 4 - $30
Not many tables - but, other than that - 5 strong stars!
Great pizza! Love the atmosphere here too. It'll be tough but make sure you leave some room for the soft serve as dessert.

Our favorite BBQ place in Nashville! Really good meat, flavor, and sides. I highly recommend getting the mac and cheese as a side.

The line can take a while, but I've never waited long for my food.

Awesome location, perfect porch to chill on in the summer, and even better food!

Excellent food and service.  Breads are to die for.  All four entrees were well presented and scrumptious.   The Key Lime pie was okay.  Tasted more like plain cheesecake.  Fantastic atmosphere and low noise level.  Definitely a "must go to" place.

My barber is Steven G. and my review will be reflective of my experience with him. My family and I have been using him for a few years now with satisfactory results. My husband went to the same barber for almost 20 years and only switched allegience after seeing Steven's cuts on both my son and me. Steven is meticulous and takes a great deal of pride in his craft. He's skilled with various hair textures as well. He's never late to his appointments and does his best to accommodate most schedules.  We have a standing appointment to insure we get our preferred time slots.

We've been to the other location in Lenox Village many times.  Last week we took some friends out for early dinner at then a show at The Station Inn.  Burger Republic was handy (only had to park once) and we felt it was a safe food choice.  ( our friends are picky).  Ok, so this location is downtown and that makes for a different cast of characters than you get in Lenox.  However, the table sitting behind us was loud and very vulgar in their conversation.  One dude was particularly shit-faced.  I don't shock or offend easily and he was grossing me out.  Our friends have finer sensibilities than we and they were quite bothered.  To our server's credit she did apologize and explained that the manager was on it and the table should be leaving soon.  She did offer us the choice to move; our friends declined.  So that happened.  The food was good.  Tater tot fondue was delicious of course...wish it was somehow a healthy choice because YUM. I had a turkey burger with pineapple and avocado and a side salad.  It was all good but not "OMG" good.  A little less good than the Lenox location.  They screwed up my hub's order.  The server made a "voila" moment out of presenting him with his Jack Daniels burger...except he didn't order the JD burger, he ordered the Fenway.  she whisked it back to the kitchen and got him the correct order tout suite.  Everyone ate their food without complaint which is pretty amazing for this crew.  Overall a 3 star experience.

Sandwiches are great, I had the Best damned Turkey 6" with a small fry and a pint of IPa, - without checking price on the beer...the waitress, while efficient and pleasant suggested another beer.  Sure I said.  So $15.00 worth of beer later I was presented with a $24.00 bill - before tip.  $28.00 and change for lunch?  Good food, but this is Not the place you want to come for beers!
The burger was amazing, but the service felt a little rushed.  Won't go during the busy hours again but the burger was amazing.

I really want to love this place. I've been here several times and the experience has really gone down hill. The first few times I went after opening, each time was like going to a different restaurant because the food was so different each night. Too spicy one night, great the next. Too little sauce one night, but barely any meat or sauce on my taco the next. We went for lunch tacos and margaritas yesterday and that was my last trip. The fish in my fish tacos was bland, but not fishy. My husband's brisket taco and beef taco had a ridiculously small amount of meat and even less sauce. And the worst part? They don't have their liquor license currently so we couldn't even get margarita. It was a bummer.

We live on Harbor Island so going here the first time was mostly due to convenience, however even though the reviews are not all stellar, we had great service and good pizza. The following week we ordered delivery through their app, the pizza was delivered within the estimated time frame and our order was correct. All in all, not my favorite pizza ever, but if you're on Harbor Island or passing through the area, it's definitely worth a try.

What a lovely little place!  I went to Euro Grill earlier this week with a group of friends.  I was pleasantly surprised with my experience.  Driving up to the restaurant, which is a converted house across the street from an industrial park, I certainly didn't know what to expect.  When I came in, I was met with phenomenal customer service.  A member of our group couldn't find the restaurant, so the owner offered to drive to where she was and guide her back to the restaurant--how awesome is that?  The food was good and so was the service.  Our waitress even did some sort of entertaining psychic reading with the Turkish coffee--I can't really explain that one for you--just go check it out!

A gamblers paradise..well at least in the tampa bay area ;-)  (it's definently no las vegas).  The hotel and casino are very clean, and they have a great decor fun decor.  You can get a hard rock membership card (this card can be swiped when you walk into the establishment and you have the opportunity to win prizes.  Also when you swipe them at the machines it keeps track of your money and also gives you points that you can redeem for different items).  For those of you who live in the area if you sign up for the membership, which is free a lot of time they will send you coupons for free meals at their restaurants.  They have Floyd's which had a lunch buffet and serves regular meals at night.  There is also the Green Room that serves a little bit of everything.  The food is only okay.  Nothing spectacular.  But the Casino is a good time....but please don't lose your SHIRT!!!

Derek is amazing! I was referred to him by a friend having just moved to South Tampa. His process and technique is really impressive in that it's innovative, yet refined and simple. He is so dialed in to his craft. A true artist. Prices are extremely reasonable and I was out in 2 hours for consult, highlights, wash, cut, blow and style. I've never gotten out in under 3 hours with this head of hair.
Awesome experience, cannot wait for my next appointment!

Essene is a place I go to pick up some special items I either can not find elsewhere or I just prefer the quality I get here.  For example, they have the best organic carrots - big, sweet and always fresh.  I love them raw and they are a hummus dipper staple for me.  The homemade carob bars with brown rice crisp are delicious.  The Mediterranean Lentil chips are wonderful and I have not found another store in the city that carries them.  So, I make a trip to Essene every few weeks to pick up my must have carrots and snack food.  I agree they are pricy, but for a few special buys I just love the place.  Must also say the staff is knowledgeable and always very helpful and friendly.

Whatever you do, get the sweet potato fries! Delicious!!

This place also has the best tofu scramble in town. It's actually spiced, and not just plain with some random veggies thrown in. The sandwiches are big, and the service is always nice. 

Cash only!
Nice cut of prime rib with baked potato.  Enjoyed the beer menu.  The building is rustic and I felt at home.  Will return.

Love it!  Really, really loved it!!

Eclectic craft beer, coffee and eats in a converted gas station located in Seminole Heights.  The inside is rustic with warm wood tones. A garage door is rolled up to make inside connected and open to the outside.  Outside patio seating is nice and a portion is covered.  

It should feel busy right up against Florida Avenue, but somehow the layout makes you feel apart from the traffic and a part of an experience.   It does get busy after work and tables fill up but there is turn over and everyone is having a great, relaxed time. Order drinks and food at the bar and they will bring food out to your table when it is ready.

Really enjoyed everything about it!!!
The ribs are so flavorful and seasoned to perfection and almost fall off the bone! The brisket was melt in your mouth and tasted amazing. The staff was absolutely fantastic.

If there were an option for zero stars, they would have it. Stood at the door, three people said "We'll be right with you," then a waiter seated us by the window.  A full 15 minutes later, no staff contact. No water, no hello, no look in our general direction. We had to ask the family at the table being served two feet away if we were actually Invisible. Finally, we walked out, even trying to stop at the check-out desk to explain why we were leaving...still zero acknowledgement. Not very busy. Are we blacklisted? I guess we'll live without mediocre food and somewhat skunky beer.

Came here for brunch with some friends on Sunday because all of the other brunch places in Baltimore were booked or had a long waiting time. 

Walking in, it gives off a homey feels get local. It's also a bit cramped, not enough where you and your party are on top of each other, but you'd have to be mindful of moving around (or turning and making awkward eye contact). Our server was nice. She didn't check back on us that much until we got our food, at which point she'd come ever 7 min (not complaining). 

We were a little put off by the amount if flies that just seemed to be hovering in the vicinity, not sure if thats just common there or someone left the back door open... but again off putting.

Food wise, I got the chicken and waffles. It was suggested to me by a friend. It's pretty fricken great. The chicken is tender, really well seasoned, generous portion size and boneless (hate looking messy in public places). The waffle was underwhelming in that it was soggy 5 min into the meal, but really the chicken makes up for it. My other friends got the chicken and waffles, and the eggs benedict (it looked like that at least). They were all pretty satisfied (especially the friend who got the chicken and waffles). Curious to see how other breakfast/brunch places on Baltimore ave compare.

Mere words are not enough to express the delight and flavors this diner/cafe gives off from the moment you hit the front door and sample the bottomless drip to the second your seated before your meal.  It's homey and the staff inviting. Will definitely return and that's Huge praise from my New Yorker trained palate. Let the grubbing begin.
Awesome food. Note, a roast beef a combo means w cheese not w fries. Mmmm!

I really do love this place! Great location, great staff, affordable price! I come get the colon hydrotherapy  every few months when i feel bloated or gassy. It really does make me feel better and it boosts my energy. The ambiance in the room is so relaxing. I just play my music and browse the web while my colon gets flushed out. And making an appointment is so easy and quick with the online  tool.

The service was awesome! Great bartender named Aukje VERY friendly and very knowledgable about the area. Best bartender in the area so far. Great buffalo bites, margaritas and live music. Only thing missing is a good IPA. Will definitely recommend this restaurant.

My. Nails. Look. Great. 
I asked for an appt via yelp and received a response in less than an hour. I had to amend my scheduled appointment and I was accommodated. 
I arrived at the new scheduled time and I was greeted and seated. I received an overlay from scratch along with shaping and new polish in less than an hour. 
Excellent customer service!
I enjoyed my relaxing time here. The facial was excellent and she gave me great tips for products. The pedicure was also very relaxing and my toes were perfect.

I have been to skeptical of acupuncturist for different reasons, one being they say you have to go back 10-15 times to get full results. But found Dawna to be well trained, very sensitive to my needs, and well beyond my expectations.
I've had only 3 treatments for possible carpel tunnel Due to my 15 years as a massage therapist and am thrilled to say I may only have one or 2 more treatments to go. She knew exactly where all my spots of pain were all the way up to the back of my neck. I would highly recommend her to anyone.

Granted we know it's on E Washington, I thought it was going to be something akin to flapjacks, however flapjacks is actually ok. 

Wife and I ordered the skillets, I also got a side of biscuits and gravy, came with toast and pancakes. Hasbrowns underneath were not cooked through, corn beef hash was hardly noticeable, biscuits and gravy were already solidified. They didn't even split them. Waitress asked "sausage gravy?" I said yes and found no sausage. Took a few bites, biscuits were dry. Pancakes were flat, tasteless, took a few bites of those as well. 

If you want subpar industrial food or have no taste buds knock yourself out. Waitress sensed something was wrong, you just smile pay the check then yelp. Service was fine. Not recommended.

Good service & good food!

From the host to the waitress, all went well.  The food came out quickly and tasty.  My boys had wings, which I think they loved even more b/c of the mess!  That came w/ blue cheese, celery and carrots.  I had the spinach artichoke flatbread w/ chicken...mmm mmm mmm!  I lied and told myself it would be healthier.  LOL

The boys enjoyed the mango lemonade.  They have a ton of tvs of all different sizes, showing all different sports.  (Not that that interested me)

Oh, try their blue cheeseburger...to do for.  The fries are pretty good too.
Great quality , very timely . Awesome prices my girlfriend loved them ..will definitely be buying from there again!

Wow! What a great addition to Lansdale. Stopped in on Founders Day and so glad we did. Super friendly staff and an interactive manager, very impressive. Didn't order food so can not comment on that but had fun sampling beers. Loved that they give you a small sample to try before ordering. Great atmosphere, love the section for kids with games and sofa, just overall great addition for keeping Lansdale alive.

Nice variety of fresh steaks and seafood. Chicken was delicately seasoned and the grits were creamy, not over cooked. Salmon was very good, a bit undercooked. Fine selection of wine and beer. Slow service. Children's menu was unexpected. My son really enjoyed his quesadilla.

This place rules.  I didn't think anything could compare to Morning Glory around here, but I was sadly in a small South Philly bubble that I'm glad I got out of this afternoon.  The food was just as awesome and fun, but the wait is a lot shorter. More tables will give you that.

I had an omelet with turkey sausage, turkey bacon and provolone. It was incredible. As any omelet with those ingredients ought to be. However, the potatoes tasted like jambalaya and had peppers in em so they won by default over other potatoes.  The menu said latkes or grits - I was sad when I heard they didn't have regular potatoes but then boom, waiter says they got em! Boom! The challah was great too. 

Southern and Jewish combined. No wonder why this South Philly native with Jewish blood loved this place...
Love love this Place! Such a sweet environment surrounded by great people and awesome beer.

We ate at Jones again today, and I have to say,"No, No, NO, Jones!!!!!!!!!!  You do NOT serve Chicken and Waffles with a bland CHICKEN GRAVY!!!" IT does NOTHING to bring out the flavor of the chicken OR waffles. Terrible gravy. Luckily, the chicken didn't need it, and we ate the waffles with syrup.

While we're on the subject of waffles, what was up with the HALF of Belgian waffle you guys served us?  I have never been given a HALF of waffle at a restaurant before. Surely you guys can splurge a little and give us a WHOLE waffle.

This is a nice restaurant low key nice services and good food, We started with the three dips the pumpkin dip was such a surprise really amazing and flavorful, The carrot app with ramps was roasted carrots which were tender and sweet with a garlicky tender ramp again nice, the only app we had which i felt was over salted and rubbery was the octopus, and I really love octopus, I like mine tender not chewy although I have traveled in greece and had it the way they serve it so it could just be my personal preference.  Price wise it wasn't too bad but a byob has to make there money somehow so items 25 to 32 seems reasonable.  My entree was a Quial which was tender and flavorful and my companion had the stuffed pepper very tender light and flavorful, the only thing is you have to get an app if you get the stuffed pepper because it is served by itself even though its hearty.  I will come back

I found this place on Yelp when I searched for "brunch on the beach" and it was a decent find. We walked into a completely empty restaurant around noon on a Sunday and that can be alarming. On a Sunday by the beach, it was actually nice that we were able to sit down right away given most of these brunch restaurants are packed around this time. With an open mind, we sat down and found that the breakfast menu was pretty large and it all sounded appetizing. The restaurant itself is brightly colored, clean, and has some coastal decor scattered about the place. The restaurant must be owned by people from England because their was an "English specialties" section which I thought was pretty cool and something out of the ordinary. I ordered the corned beef hash with extra crispy home fries and it was definitely a good choice. The corned beef was fresh and not out of a can and the home fries were cooked to a perfect crisp. My only complaint would be that in a restaurant as slow as this the food should come out much faster. We were kept waiting for about 45-50 minutes for 4 seemingly quick meals. Luckily my "double" mimosa kept me content while we waited. I would have been a little annoyed if I was kept waiting for bad food but it honestly was delicious and definitely hit the spot. Our bill was only $26 too! I'm glad this place is an option when everywhere else is crowed!

These guys took me in when I really needed them. I had my donut spare on my car from a flat I got a few days prior. I had a temp rope plug in the original tire and just needed it swapped out. Another tire/muffler place had refused to do so and tried to sell me a brand new tire. (Different review for that place forthcoming)

So I called Havertown on my way to work on a morning with snow in the forecast. Asked if I brought it in, if they could do the switch. They said yes, come on in. While I waited I had coffee and watched tv on a comfortable couch in a relatively clean waiting room (for a mechanic--best I've seen). After about 15-20 mins they had looked at my temp plug and explained that it wasn't great for long-term use, and recommended a permanent plug for $30. I approved, they did it then and there, and I was out the door just as the snow began to fall. 

Everyone was friendly and I've been riding on my plugged tire, which has plenty of mileage left in it, for almost 2 months. No problems. Just passed state inspection. Thumbs up.

Everyone who eats here knows that they rock. Their catering is great too. Chicken and dressing, chicken fried steak, the mashed taters and green beans and the desserts. I gotta quit, it's 2am am i am making myself hungry! MMMM!
had the chicken and waffles! it was very good. i look forward to trying other dishes. and they deliver!!

I stopped by here Saturday night (07/26) for an ice cream dinner (what? It was hot and I wasn't hungry for a full-on meal, stop looking at me like that!) with my brother-in-law and sister and I decided to get cinnamon frozen yogurt with chocolate sprinkles on a regular cone. It was amazing. The yogurt was sweet with a slight tangy zest to it, and the cinnamon added a subtle tone of flavor. The servers were very friendly and careful in how they prepared our orders, which scored extra points with me.

I plan on coming back here very soon to try out more of their 52 flavors.

After reading the positive reviews on here, I decided to give Sam's a try.  We arrived shortly after 5 PM on a weekday, so we were the only people in the restaurant until the over 65 crowd started arriving.  The decor is interesting - light colored wood slats cover the walls up to the high ceilings and somewhat mismatched booths and tables below.  It is almost reminiscent of a ski lodge, albeit one with the tables a little too close together.

We were promptly greeted, seated, ordered our drinks (their fresh-brewed ice tea) and began to browse the sparse menu.  If you don't want a burger or some grilled chicken concoction, this place is likely not for you.  We ordered the Thanksgiving on a "French" roll (no sides included, I ordered onion rings) and the walnut chicken with fries, applesauce and some strange-looking honey dip with pepper flakes (it tasted a bit better than it looked).

Our food arrived ~15 mins later as other diners gradually began to fill the establishment.  We were fortunate enough to choose one of the few tables that had ketchup and as I began to create a pool on my plate, I noticed this bottle had seen better days.   In fact, all of the ketchup bottles out had - the labels were oddly faded in a way that suggested these bottles had been "washed" and re-filled.  Come to think of it, the ketchup didn't taste like Heinz either.  Give me a break.

It got better, my soft roll was crusty on the edges from being cut and left to sit around, the turkey dry (which is supposedly roasted on site) and the stuffing bland.  The only redeeming quality of my meal was the cranberry sauce and the pre-packaged onion rings.

The walnut chicken seemed like a good idea, but also lacked flavor and the mountain of shoestring fries were not evenly seasoned with what appeared to be a "Cajun" seasoning.  The clear pepper flake laced jelly on the side did not look appetizing, tasted ok, but could do little to salvage this meal.

Overall, we could have easily made a better meal at home for less money - the bill came to $33 with tip.  There is a simple lack of quality and attention to detail.  It is obvious they get their weekly order from the restaurant supplier, put things together with as little effort as possible and call it a "grill joint".  If you are in the area, you'd do better with the Applebee's or the Subway across the street.  Even better yet, fire up the grill at home - you can't do any worse.

Update: Closed - not a loss to real foodies.

I used Uber eats to get a Buckin bacon breakfast wrap. Holy cow!  This is the best breakfast burrito I've ever had!  The sauce is tangy and delicious!  It took less than 20 minutes to receive and arrived fresh and hot!  Will definitely be returning!

Great food! My husband stated the staff was also great as he was the one to pick up the order. The lady at the counter even said the owner likes to help keep the kitchen spotless as we are people of the food industry and admire clean spaces. Only downer was that they forgot my black olives on my pizza that I paid the 2$ for.
Wow, fantastic. Best Pizza I've had in Reno. Sorry it took me so long to eat there. Veggie Pizza, crust thin and light, fresh veggies. topped off with a shock top beer, yum. Can't wait to go back.

I come here a lot. That's an understatement. When anyone is like "LOL LET'S GO EAT" I'm basically always "LET'S GO TO SUSHIBAR." From the $2 Imported beer special, to the insanely filling combo meals, this is a great place to satisfy all of my JapanNEEDS. 

There should be a separate rating here for the service. They deserve 10 stars. I have never felt more welcomed in a restaurant than by the staff of SushiBar. I always have prompt service with a smile, and it almost makes me want to go there every day if it weren't for that pesky thing we call "being an adult and paying rent."

I almost always get roll combo 6, which comes with a yellowtail, salmon, cucumber, and california roll. I mean, come on, that's a lot of food AND a miso soup and salad. Save some room for dessert though, because the mochi ice cream is off the chain.

We bought a Groupon before checking reviews for this place.  Big mistake!  But we went there anyway last week.  My wife had a small pizza which she said was okay.  I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich which was the driest thing I've ever eaten.   Service was very slow...we asked for parmesan cheese with my wife's pizza and never saw our waitress again!  Finally we went into the kitchen to get our check.
Nope, not again...
LaScala is consistently good home style Italian. The chopped salad is great for low carb seekers.

I loved the food and drinks. I've had several dishes including their eggs Beni and duck confit. Both awesome. The misses however didn't like her donut, and the seating is uncomfortable noisy and a little to hipster for me. But overall, one of my favorite breakfast stops for Tucson. Be prepared to wait a while for a seat.
Quite possibly the best brunch I have had in over a year.  It will be packed on the weekends but it's worth the wait.

Phil and Lou good guys, my first time i think im in love.These guys were so nice You guys made my first visit Rock !!!! My sister and i had the best time,we ordered the chili nachos ,the chili had  a medium sweet taste it was delicious,needles to say, they earned a very good tip tonight. Smiley Face:).

The Shrimp Diavolo was yum so was the mama mandola's chicken soup. Felt so good to have these on a cold winter day. Lobster ravioli was ok but the  Mahi wulfe was amazing. Dont leave unless you try the deserts as well.

Wiregrass is a really nice outdoor mall, with a lot of activities year round. On the 1st and 3rd Saturday of the month they host an outdoor market. Lot of local different vendors come. On the 3rd of July they have a lot of activities for the 4th of July plus a really good fireworks show that they shoot from the parking garage. During the holidays they have the "Festival of Light Show" on the top of the hour. It's lighted Christmas trees in sync w/ music from the Trans-Siberian Orchestra. They have a lot of different restaurants depending too what you are in the mood for. Something simple and quick you can head to Moes or Panera Bread. They also have your full service restaurants too. A tip is to park near the back. A lot of people try the spots right around Panera & Red Robin. If you go towards the parking garage, or park behind the nail salon, you will have much easier luck and much less traffic!
Great location but the place is very tiny.   You sit arm to arm with your neighbors.  Food is ok and I love the view.

YUM! Yum. yum.

Yeah, I'm a little late on the bandwagon after the New York Times has written about this place. Regardless, it was so delicious. I went with Martha G and another friend, so I had the chance to try 3 types of chicken -- Honey Ginger glazed, Zatar and Coconut Curry dry. While I loved the Zatar spices best (made me nostalgic for my first zatar exposure in Israel years ago), I think the glazed chickens are just so much more delicious. I can't wait to go back to try the Chile-Garlic glazed or whatever else they have on the menu.

Also, this review would be incomplete if I didn't mention the donuts. I will say that I'm generally not a big donut person - I love them, they're fabulous, but to me however good they are, they're generally just not worth how bad they are for you. I'd rather have another piece of fried chicken. Ah, but here... the honey donut that comes with all the chicken is so good you can't not have it. And the Halvah donut I tried -- also delicious but nowhere near as good as the honey donut. I need to try the hot donuts which sound amazing -- or maybe I'll just have more chicken instead.
Oh my God I love this place!!!!!!!!! I just hate that its soooo far away from home..Great place to people watch and have great ice cream..
Super cute southern vibes. The crystal chandeliers are my favorite! Try the smoked pork sandwich and an Italian mule. Cheers!

Honesty hour, we went out in Nashville after 10pm. Apparently, there are limited options at that time, when it isn't the weekend. We decided to try out this place after walking to a couple of other places that were not like their descriptions. 
This place has a nice ambience, nice staff, and a ton of beers and ciders on tap. The prices weren't bad for the drinks or beer. Between 5-8 for the beer/cider. Around 10-12 for cocktails. Oh, and the kitchen closes at 11. 

Now on to the food, we got the burger and the chimichanga. We were splitting them so we went for something a little different with the chimichanga. We also got the cheesesteak egg rolls. Sounds fantastic, right? Unfortunately, the burger was the only highlight. Everything else got a HUGE FAIL! The chimichanga was super soggy. The rice and beans were ok. The cheesesteak egg rolls were just BAD! No taste at all.  

Now on to our drinks. We first ordered their take on a margarita. They used silver
Tequila so it had a very heavy tequila taste. It was ok.  He wound up with the punch. It was ok. Mind you, we were traveling all day and ate everything. So, it was edible. 

All and all, if you need somewhere to go late, then try it. Just  stick to very regular things. The staff is nice ,so, that is worth a visit based on that alone.

Last year I went to this company cause I needed a bed and I saw they had an add a on Craigslist for "cheap" beds. I called and the owner Russ answered his phone like a normal phone and acted as if he didn't have time to talk to me, being rushed and short for time. After asking questions I set up a time to meet with him to look at beds. I found a bed I liked and he sold it to me for 650.00. It's an amazingly comfortable bed, definitely the best bed I have ever had. After some time with that bed I moved and had to sell it. Recently I found his add on CL again so I called him. I knew it was him right when I called due to the lack of customer service and communication skills. I went to look at his new warehouse with the same bed I had purchased two years ago. I laid on it and knew immediately it was the bed I purchased before due to the fact it was so comfortable. I started talking to the new person and he said the best deal they could give me on the bed was 1,100.00 after I told him I purchased the SAME bed for 650. He said that wasn't true and said I was wrong, I didn't have the right bed. He said he would never charge that little for the bed and began to bicker with me. Extremely unprofessional. I got the make and model of the bed to make sure that I wasn't incorrect and went to my mom who I sold the bed to and sure enough, it was the same bed he was trying to charge me almost twice as much for. After being rude to me, not returning my calls or texts and again being extremely unprofessional I decided I would rather pay more for a bed through a large department store then be called a liar and have someone try to rip me off when I paid nearly half of what I was being charged now. I will not recommend Russ to anyone and unfortunately him and his company receive my first single star rating.

We live so close by its incredible. For 2 years we have driven by this place sometimes several times in a day and never went in till today. We had the carnival and a burrito. Food was fast, service friendly and the bill was 20 with tax. Salsa bar nice .  We will be walking over from now on. Nice little neighborhood cafe

We stayed here opening weekend and have stayed a couple more times in the six months since. Overall, this is a nice hotel. 

It really feels more like a typical nice convention hotel to me (which it is) than a luxury hotel. It just does not have the touches to put it in the latter category for me.

The service here, however, is on par with any hotel in the city. It is top notch. Anything you need, they are happy to help. 

The restaurants are a decent option but I'll do individual reviews for those. 

The rooms are a decent size but not as big as those in other JWs. They are clean and comfortable. I think the bathroom is small for a hotel of this caliber. They had to cram a thousand rooms in this joint, though, so maybe that's part of the reason. 

They have an indoor pool and hot tub. These are nice options, especially in the winter, but this is another area I thought could have been bigger. The fitness facility on the other hand is huge.  

My wife travels a lot for work and we are loyal Marriott customers so one of our favorite activities is comparing the concierge/executive lounges at the various properties. The lounge here is pretty damn nice. They also serve food on the weekends which is very rare, as these hotels tend to cater to the Monday-Thursday business crowd. 

I will certainly recommend this hotel to friends and family coming in from out of town. Because they do have so many rooms, rates are very reasonable when there is not a large event in town.

Very basic breakfast joint with good food.  I had a ham and cheddar omelet.  The ham was smoked hickory and gave the breakfast such a great flavor.  Light and fresh home fries.  No grease on the plate.  A very filling breakfast without being overly heavy.  Great start to the day.

I absolutely love this Massage Envy location. The office staff is especially sweet and friendly, both in person and on the phone. I began here a few months ago on the introductory price and decided to join up the next month. I work in a spa, but because of our busy schedules it is so hard to find time to trade out with our massage therapists. Massage Envy makes it affordable AND they have great LMT's that know what they are doing. They have flexible hours and are open 7 days a week which is great for people, like me, that work crazy hours! I have seen a few different therapists (depending on what days I go), all of which have been amazing! I would highly recommend Chris, Angel, Brandon and Holly. Something I noticed about each of them is that you can tell that they genuinely love what they do. They are so knowledgeable about the muscles and things you can do in between sessions to help limit the amount of pain and muscle tension you will have. Becoming a member here was such a great decision and I definitely plan to renew my membership!
Rude, makes nails bleed, rude, don't ask for nonprofit donations to local organizations after beibg faithful for over 5 years, will lie about ownership, & rude. Did I mention rude?
Best hot dogs i ever had. Very friendly staff, a fun atmosphere. They also have a Reserved Parking spot for reciepients of the Purple Heart, Combat Wounded Veterans. Great great place to eat.

I have been to Judge Bean's three times over the past year.  The restaurant is quite small and the dining area is really packed with too many tables and chairs.  If you don't like people sitting very close to your table while you eat with friends and family, then you should go somewhere else.  They usually play old school country music which kind of sets the mood of the place.  The staff is usually very young but friendly and fast.  This place is very casual so everyone was casually dressed.  Most of the waitresses were wearing daisy dukes.  Now, on to the food.  The BBQ beef brisket is excellent.  If you like beef brisket then you cannot go wrong here.  The chili is pretty good.  It has jalapeno peppers mixed in it for some spice.  My brother thought the chili was very hot but I found it to be pretty mild but flavorful.  However, I do have a high tolerance to hot foods.  I did not like the smoked sausage.  It was way too smoky for me and I felt queasy for the rest of the night after eating it.  The BBQ sauce is very good but I wish there was more sauces to choose from for variety.  Now for the sides.  Their cowboy beans are mixed with jalapeno peppers with some habenero pepper spice and it was very good.  The potato salad, bbq beans, and fried okra are also pretty good.  I will go back to Judge Bean's but I will certainly avoid their sausage in the future.
It's worth the drive from Minden!  My favorite long roll was The Hangover.  Atmosphere is perfect and price is good.  2 people ate great for  $50.
Great vibe buying a car here--both times. Finance person, Elise, is great. Sales manager, Wes, is fantastic.

Sooo... this place is awesome. You order at counter from limited yet exquisite comfort food. Chicken, fried catfish, ribs, roast beef and a special ofnthe day. Great sides for you meat n 3. I had the catfish with some corn bread, special (Adam Wainright) heirloom tomatoes and I got the soup of the day (smoky tomato). Everything was to die for awesome. Sometimes there is a line but it moves fast or you can eat at the bar. Owner is on sight and responsive. Eat Here Now!

As previously stated this place uses free-roaming, grass fed beef, olive oil soaked french fries, and all that good jazz. So i'm guessing that this all natural approach is better for you, I don't think it really makes a difference in the end however. You'll still clog your arteries if you eat enough of these just like any other fast food. Standard burger fare though, nothing special, I couldn't taste the grass or anything else different so there's that. The fries, however, were very perplexing, they tasted great, but they were greasy as anything. This place is just a mini caricature of the fast food industry, It's better for you but still bad for your health in general. Craig Laban 2 bells for sure.

Ate here for a friend's birthday and was not disappointed. I'm half Italian so I have pretty high standards when it comes to Italian food, but Ava was up to the challenge. I ordered a penne dish with sausage which was quite good, though I wish it came with a bit more sausage.

The service was very good as well. We were constantly attended to and both our appetizers and main courses came out fairly quickly. Our server didn't let me go thirsty either as she was there to get me another Maduro as I finished my previous one.

I've also been here for happy hour and that is definitely something I need to do again. They have drink specials though they admittedly aren't as good as some other happy hours. However, the star here are there $5 pizzas. They aren't huge or anything, but a decent size for the price. We tried 3 of them and they were all fantastic!

This place is amazing! Great food, wonderful atmosphere, and friendly staff.  We bring our family for dinner and then stay to play in the attached classic arcade.  The owners, Todd & Scott, are two amazing guys that make you feel like you're an instant friend!
5.40 for 4oz bean dip. (few tablespoons) I think not. Won't ever go back!!!!I  Friends and family were right.

I had the Korean Tacos which were ok. I really liked the Southern Taco which has fried chicken. They margaritas are standard and good. They have your basic beer selections and some wines available. The patio is cool. If you arrive and see a line going out of the door. ALWAYS enter though the patio then go inside the building and directly to the bar to beat the standing line.

Tasty takeout barbeque. I had the beef brisket sandwich, which has great flavor and a fantastic sauce. It doesn't hold up quite as well as a take out dish because the bun gets quite soft but the taste was still great. My husband loved his sides, especially the beans and Spanish rice. I found the Mac and cheese side fairly bland, I'd pass on that one in the future. I thought the food was comparable to Meat's and a couple of our friends actually thought it to be better.

My friends and I drove through the night from Texas and decided to make our breakfast stop here after 12 hours of driving. Man ohhhhh man, these pancakes were the perfect pit stop. I highly recommend the chocolate heaven that was the Swiss Chocolate Chip Pancakes. Our waitress was the perfect example of southern hospitality and took care of us well. We got there around 7 AM, so there was no line and we were seated right away. But like other reviews have mentioned, the line forms quickly soon after this time. When we had the left the restaurant by 7:45, the line had made its way around the corner. Still dreaming of the pancakes, will be back again!

This place has everything you need to cook any type of oriental dish. Seafood selection is adequate but freshness could be alot better. Great selection of asian vegetables and fruits. Store is clean and staff is friendly.

Do not waste your time. I had gone here on June 25, 2015. They are closed, & they appear to be out of business. No further information has been given. There is a recorded message at 615-255-7019. The Hotel Indigo's staff that I stayed at, didn't even know this.

Straight up tex-mex restaurant that I discovered when I moved here. I visit this place for convenience since Chipotle is too far. Anyway, their habanero salsa is pretty good and they serve beer. Their burritos are huge though and I can't get enough of black beans...maybe that's why I frequent this place?

Just ordered... meat lovers pizza, spinach salad and tiramisu. Salad and dessert on point!! Very tasty... pizza had good flavor,  lots of meat.. A little on the greasy greasy side. 1st time ordering. .will definitely do again! Also had very nice service by phone and when delivered! Today recommend

I would give this place half a star if it was possible. I went for the first time recently with my boyfriend and our dog. I walked into the restaurant to first ask if my dog would be allowed on the outside patio, they told me no since she is not a service dog. That was ok with me I understood so we walked across the street to figure out where we should try next. While across the street we saw a large family and their small dog be allowed onto the very same patio we were turned away from. I walked back over and asked a different gentleman why we were turned away and this dog was allowed? He told me they said it was a service dog. "Service dog?"  that dog was not a service dog, not in its wildest dreams. I asked the man to level with me since we both knew they had lied.
This poor excuse for a dog, not a service dog just poor excuse for a dog in general is making real service dogs be turned away because they choose to lie (SHAME ON YOU FAMILY.)
So long story short I was allowed to bring my dog to the patio after a lengthy Q & A and me promising my dog would not bark, fight, or be a nuisance. After sitting down the other "dog" cried and barked constantly while my dog was still and quite. The children at the same table were screaming and crying and making it not worth staying. We paid for our two cups of coffee we ordered and left. The coffee was the worst I have ever had...tasted burnt and it was $7 for it! 

Never EVER will I go there and I will never recommend it to another person and especially not to my food blogging parents. I cant wait to tell them about this place :/

This is the second time I have stayed here. Wasn't impressed the first time but wow this second time. You owe it to yourself to pay a little more to stay in the Tuscany Towers. Big room, big bathroom with a hot tub. You want peace and relaxation and silence. You will absolutely get it there. Not once did I here anything from next door and not once did I ever hear a door slam the three days I was there. Loved it. Will absolutely go back. The heated outdoor pool was great. The hot tub was good and the big shower stall was good. What wasn't good was doing the f-ing splits and slapping my balls on that italian marble floor when I stepped out from the hot tub. My fault should have put a towel there. I tell you this if you go this is the side of the casino to stay.

Excellent ambience and hang out spot!! Great place to catch some college football! Really enjoyed they're cheese platter. Excellent selections and for a no pork eater, I was super pleased they include only cheeses!! Didn't have to miss out. The toast was on point, and don't get me started on the candied nuts. Yum! Had a perfect Fall flair. Have it 4 stars because they beer was good, but nothing really stood out. Our favorite, by far, was the 1927 IPA. Really delicious, citrusy, dank flavor. I'm normally the imperial fan, but wasn't too impressed. Too boozy over malty. Live music was just a plus. Great place to hang for a little 30th celebration. Would come back, and just might, just wishing we were more in love with the brews!

This is my go to place for Sonoran Dogs and Carne Asada Tacos. It seems like the reviews here are either 5 stars, or 1-2. I don't know if there's a big inconsistency with what staff is working. All I know is the food is always good when I've eaten there. The service is sometimes a little slow, but I won't really hold that against then, as it only happens when they're slammed with customers. The staff have always been extremely friendly, and even when they're busy and the service is a little slow, it seems obvious to me that they're all really trying to do the best they can. For me, that's what makes me not so picky about the service.
So, excellent food, good prices, friendly staff, and decent service. I recommend BK's if you're looking for good Mexican food.

We just recently had our Company Holiday party at the Peppermill in the Tuscany Ballroom, and I am quite impressed with the accommodations this fine establishment has to offer. Excellent venue for parties and events. The Food was very tasty, especially the cheeseballs. The chocolate fountain was a magical touch as well. The only thing I can say about the Tuscany Ballroom is that it was HUGE. Lots of space in there, and for the amount of people we had, it was hard to walk around and see everyone. This was definitely not the Peppermill's fault though. On the way up to the Ballroom, I got to check out the casino floor, and everything seemed very well run and well kept. Beautiful Hotel, and I can't wait to go back to check out the rooms next time.

What a lovely lady! 
I've been getting a Brazilian wax for over a year and a half now and have some horror stories. I used to go down to hands and stones down the street from here but after two incidents where the waxer left a patch of hair, I refuse to go back. The women that work there are amazing and polite but after one waxer (who left) waxed a portion of my eyebrow off and another left too much hair down there, I couldn't risk it anymore. For $80 a Brazilian? I better be bare as the day I was born. 
Back to the review. I didn't know it was located IN the salon so I was driving around a bit before calling her. I didn't make an appointment, which I should've but thankful she was free. She doesn't take credit card but trusted me enough to come back with cash after the waxing because she didn't want to lose time for perfection. She taught me how to fill in my eyebrows (because of the last wax) and made them look better than ever. Now for the nitty gritty! For my Brazilian, she did not wear gloves but she did wash her hands. I was too busy on reddit to see wether or not she double dipped. Sanitation is a huge thing with waxing (hence why I refuse to go back to Pink ever again, they double dip hardcore and use the same stick for everyone). After the wax, I felt great. I had to go to work right after but there was no soreness or redness. I've only received compliments on my eyebrows! I highly recommend her. 
$15 for eyebrow and $55 for a Brazilian with a student discount coming together for an amazing $70! I spent more just getting a Brazilian before! I found my waxer! Never going anywhere else :)

Decided to go here on the recommendation of my sister after more than a year and a half without a haircut.  I used to be very paranoid about my hair and had the same stylist from childhood until I graduated from college.  However after a good experience with my salon in Boston and a brush with a bob after donating hair in 2009, I'm much more laid back.  Made an evening appointment with Adrienne, which I very much appreciate, because I'm a grad student and also work part time in Trenton, so I tend to be out of the house from the early am till at least 6:45 most days.

Love!  Adrienne was totally confident and knew what she wanted to do with my hair while keeping the length I wanted, so I let her do what she thought would look good, since she's the stylist after all.  I'm very happy with the cut, as well as the service.  She was super friendly and talkative; a great conversationalist.  Not to mention the great scalp massage...can I get just that all day long during finals, please?  And the prices and convenience are great for me as well.

I'll reserve my 5th star for appointment 2, but I'm pretty confident that it will be another great experience and I'll be going here as long as I'm in the area.
Amazing bar food!! Everything I have tried here is delicious!! The meatloaf is a must have, the mussels and the ahi tuna salad also!!
Such a great establishment.  Always consistent, accommodating with coupons and the customer service is on point.  They're always open and have delivery available rain, snow or shine!

It was hard to give 2 stars.  THe location is beautiful.  Very quaint and bright.  Workers are very pleasant and helpful.  I had a large party and the staff were extremely accomodating.  My issue is with the food itself.  I have to say "Tasty BUT....".   I had ordered the High Tea for One.  I was expecting the traditional look of high tea with 3 tiers.  What I got was a plate with 5 little finger sandwiches, a scone with lemon curd and clotted cream and a slice of cake cut in 2.  Sandwiches were kind of tasty but the fillings were extremely stingy.  Scone was lovely as well as the lemon curd and clotted cream.  The soup was a tomato basil and was very tasty but entirely too chunky for the portion.  It was more of a marinara in consistency.  I was disturbed to see into the kitchen and see them preparing their vegetable cheese soup and the cheese soup was actually a sauce by Ragu.  The desserts were a gyp.  It was billed to be 2 cakes and chocolates.  No chocolates and it was one slice of store bought loaf cake cut into 2 pieces.    The meal was tasty; don't get me wrong, it was just disappointing.

Final note...If you have allergies to certain foods in the finger sandwiches, they have a strict NO SUBSTITUTIONS policy.

I find myself continuously returning here. The food is great quality and the service is always top notch. One of my favorite things to order is the Phó. Since My move from Seattle, I found it difficult to find a place that could make great Phó. I have found it.

Was in the area and lucky to have found this place. About 150 years old. Nostalgic setting with some decent food. Waitstaff was nice and accommodating. Amor had the tiger shrimp with saffron linguini and I was looking for an entree salad with their famous tri tip. Both dishes did not disappoint. So yum. The Italian blue cheese dressing was on point! The horseradish both the house made with apples for a milder flavor and the fresh grated horseradish for sinus numbing spiciness were sooo good. Ambiance whisks you away to another time
The  gym is dirty. I have given up.  Locker room is totally dirty and the manager doesn' give a damn.  I'm going back to planet fitness.

'This is the first buffalo exchange I've been to, personally I'm not impressed.  The clothing while yes is all very cute is not sold for what I would call a bargain.  It may have been that I went when there was low inventory (after all there's not really a "bad/good" time to go to a thrift store/consignment store) there seemed to be a lot of blouses that were from their warehouse...I had asked one of the employees why there were so many of the same kind of (several) blouses, he stated that they often get over stock of brand new clothing in their warehouse and its put out for sale.  A part of me thinks that's awesome but at the same time it kind of turned me off, I'm not going to buy a top at a consignment store for twenty dollars just because it's new, especially if it feels like the material won't wash well and I can find similar items at ross for less than half the price!  There were some really cute tops that i found from brands like J Crew and Banana Republic but once again the price was anywhere from 15.00-17.00 mehh not really for me, I've found great stuff from great brands at good will for 4.20 (and half that depending on tag color) so maybe I'm just a little spoiled on thrift store prices.  They had a lot of great little dresses and costume pieces some were very reasonable but I didn't have luck with finding my size on the things that I did like (a part of the thrift store game my friend) and the rest was what I would call "granny chic".  On my sad way out I saw a jewelery stand full of cute things that I wish I would have taken the time to check out but I had to go catch a trolley and get back to my hotel "raises fists" oh well, better luck next time I suppose!

I recently "discovered" Henry's as Frank (Owner/Chef) doesn't really advertise. 

What a wonderful surprise. Understanding everyone's experience may be different, I cannot fathom anyone not enjoying Henry's.

Each dish is a unique blend of fresh ingredients (and I mean FRESH), very tasty blends of spices and a heavy dose of Franks personality. 

I was most recently there for the New Orleans themed night. A six course meal paired with wine.

Every dish was true to the theme. But the Alligator stole the show. 

It is clear that Frank knows seafood and you simply can't go wrong stepping through the front door and having Denise (host) show you to a table.

Things to know: It is small and when full, a little loud (but I welcome that environment). The local crowd is very friendly and that makes for a fun evening. You can consider certain tables a bit better suited for a romanic dinner, so just ask Denise, she'll take care of you. It's BYOB with a liquor store around the corner (state store has limited hours so be sure to check). Henry's is only open certain days and times, so CALL FIRST. Portions are generous, pricing is very good for the area. Oh, they only accept cash, no credit cards.

Henry's is a place that should be frequented by everyone in the area. Hey Frank, start advertising... oh actually, don't... I like this little secret!

IF YOU ENJOYED MY REVIEW, PLEASE RATE IT AND SEND ME A COMMENT!

Bueno Onda tacos are hands down my favorite tacos in Philly. I always get the glazed shrimp and glazed fish tacos with a side of chips and guac. The tacos are so fresh and flavorful, you can't go wrong with any from their wide selection. The guacamole has cheese on top, which is not necessarily my favorite, but it still tastes delicious. The nachos are topped with cheese, tomatoes, black beans, and all other goodies so I would highly recommend those as well. Although I haven't been here for happy hour, I have heard from friends that they have $3 sangria and margaritas. I look forward to coming here for happy hour in the future and will keep on raving about these tacos!

Friendly staff...but some of their folks need to learn how to work more expediently. The carpet on the 5th floor definitely seems like it's due for a renovation as it was warped and bunched up in the middle of the hallways. My bathroom had cracked tiles and torn curtains that never seemed to want to stay in place. BUT, you get what you pay for and this place was definitely a decent value for downtown STL.

The first Mizzou football game of the season was Pay Per View only and not that many bars were showing the game. After arriving at Corner Pub to find there were no tables, some friends and I ended up at Hotshots. Sure, there were plenty of places to sit but they quickly became full. We were just happy to be able to watch the game. But when the table behind us became chain-smokers we were all pretty shocked as this place was serving a lot of food - guess they've paid their way out of participating in the smoking ban. What became unbearable was the table of old men with beer bellies that lit up some huge stanky cigars - yup, Hotshots allows cigar smoking, as well.

With the Tigers pummeling Southeastern Lousiana big time, my friends and I were fed up with the smoke and left soon after half-time. I'd rather miss watching a football game than ever come back to this place.

Also, I really dislike any establishment that makes it's waitresses dress in such tight skimpy clothing. Hotshots seems to be the place for hoosiery smokers to watch a game.

Open 24 hours. Very large portions. Food quality is average to good. Surprisingly wide variety of selections on their menu. Cheap prices. Friendly wait staff; I've seen the same faces there for years. They need to give the place a facelift, and especially update their booths because of wear and tear; the inside probably looks exactly the same as it did when they opened the doors in 1984.

The mixed reviews here are appropriate.  While the food here is very good (authentic, though a little bit salty the day we tried it), the service is a let down.  We waited longer than expected and did not get everything that we ordered.  The front of the house is clearly quite disorganized t times, but the back knows how to cook!

This place is very good. A must visit in downtown St. Louis. It's so close to Busch Stadium and the Arch and all of the main downtown locations. It's within walking distance of most of the hotels, such as ours, hence the reason we tried it. 

It's a very family-oriented place and has a very laid back, casual atmosphere. There is something on the menu for everyone. They have everything from steak to seafood to pasta to burgers to sandwiches. 

I got the beef and veal tortellini in white sauce (sans mushrooms) and it was wonderful. They put the perfect amount of sauce on it, which you know when ordering pasta is always something to worry about. 

My husband got the chicken carbonara and he loved it. (I did not try it as I am not a fan of mushrooms, but I took his word for it.)

My mom got the soup of the day, my dad got a burger and my nephew got chicken tenders and french fries. They all enjoyed their meals as well. 

But the best part came after dinner... Dessert. We shared a famous St. Louis Gooey Butter Cake and it was fabulous. I'm sure this place isn't exclusive to having it, but it was fantastic so I wanted to share.

The food left a disgusting taste in my mouth. Everything is fake meat dishes. Not sure why vegan places can't have any creativity? But it's all tofu and smoky flavor a added to the foods. Leaves a nasty taste.

Ordered a breakfast smoothie here.  Got the Amazonian whey(?) -  came with banana, agave, cocoa, and whey.  For 7 bucks a smoothie, it's pretty damn pricey.  I think the other breakfast options (an actual meal) are a better value.

I love this hotel!! The staff is amazing, the location is perfect, and the beds are amazingly comfortable. I stayed for about a week for work and ran a conference here. This is my go to hotel when planning conferences. I loved every minute of it. The meeting space is perfect and it's really cool how they still have the old bank door in their big ballroom- added a nice touch to our meeting. The bar/lounge down stairs was very convenient especially after a long day at work. The food is food- really good!! The location was perfect- I went out one night and explored the city with a friend and he took me to about 5 different places- all walking distance- from a tapas place to a hookah bar ending at a French restaurant. 
All in all definitely check out this hotel for a meeting or some where to stay when visiting the city. I'm back in Philadelphia tomorrow so I look forward to stopping by the hotel bar/ lounge.

Honestly, if I'm going to pay $25 for pancakes, bacon, coffee, and a drink I want the food to knock me over.  I ordered one of the fancy fruit drinks they had listed (The Giant Peach) which was neither giant, nor peachy.

The best part of my brunch was the coffee and even then $2.50 for coffee? I should be able to steal the mug (I didn't) for that price.
