We loved the Avocado and Crispy Cuban varieties, were mixed on the Tex Mex, and didn't really care for the Firecracker Salmon.

I opted for the Kobe Burger as my entree, and my fiance got the Americana Cheeseburger. They were both cooked to the temperature requested, and pretty decent overall. The portions are huge, so we both took home half the burgers anyway. And we, of course, had to order some cheesecake to take home. The cheesecake is always fantastic. I've had a few different flavors and they're all great.

Three stars means "A-OK" and that's pretty much how I feel about Cheesecake Factory. There are lots of menu options, so you're pretty much guaranteed to find something you like. But it is fairly expensive. I think for our appetizer, 2 drinks, 2 entrees, and 2 pieces of cheesecake added up to $100 (or around there). Quite a bit considering we weren't blown away. I'll come back, but only for the cheesecake!

I took my AutoTrader Trade-In Marketplace price quote here, and they refuse to honor it (or even offer a price at all).  If they are this hard to deal with when I'm trying to use a program they are participating in, I'm not going to find out how they are when negotiating a price to buy a car.  I frequently buy and sell cars, but I won't be coming to the Auffenburg dealerships for my next car.  I also won't be bothering with AutoTrader's Trade-In program either.  One good part - the staff was friendly and made time to look at the Trade-In offer certificate.

Fantastic, great tasting dishes! The stewed goat and roast pork were better than delicious. The chicken soup was exceptional, except it was served luke warm - once they made it hot it was great. Rice and beans, plantains great too. Look forward to going back. Nice and pleasant ownership and servers too.
It's all good here!  Pumpkin pie ice cream was my favorite on their plain fresh and crunchy waffle cone!

Uggh, I wrote a long detailed review and then accidentally hit back space. No, I didn't not hit the save now button. 

I refuse to spend another 8 minutes writing this reviews so, please excuse the blunt sentence fragments that may appear below. 

Hostess asked if we had a reservation... said no, we were seated in the half empty restaurant two minutes later.

Seated near the rear, above a leaking a/c vent, but it wasn't a deal breaker and I didn't ask to be moved.

Happy hour....yay! Half off drinks and hor d'ourves. Tried the fried oysters(first time having oysters...not a fan) The sauce for the oysters was tasty with a hint of spiciness. I didn't care for the consistency of the oysters. 

My kid's burger was huge and she explained it was delightful. String fries were included.  I decided on the shrimp and pasta(can't remember the name of the dish). It was rather cajun/creoleish, but I wasn't impressed with the combo. The shrimp was great on it's own. In my opinion the pasta was too thick. 

There you go a 3 star based on the shrimp dish. Luke has an upscale feel, though causal wear is acceptable.

First of all what a beautiful salon it  has a very elegant feel. I had gotten a gift card for microblading which I never had and wasnt sure I even wanted it.  For some reason I was losing a lot of eyebrow hair for some time.  I had my proceedure with Annie Morris, she was recommended.  She took her time explained the procedure, was very gentle, and accommodated my schedule I went in on a Sunday.  My eyebrows make me look years younger I love them.  I will definitely be back Annie.  I love the freedom of being able to run out the door without any make up and still feel pretty.  That gift is priceless.

Honestly, I did not enjoy  the good pie...not my kinda pizza.  However, I really enjoyed the eating experience.  From the coffee, service and unique ambiance; I really enjoyed my overall experience.  I can't say I will return, because again, its just not my kinda pizza.  But, I do understand why it continues to receive good reviews.
Awesome tacos just like home. 15 for $15.00. Try a frybread with sugar for desert. Thanks I'll be back!!!!

Amazing live jazz!  But here's the inside scoop:

Do not purchase the "Big Shot" tickets (almost 30 bucks per person!!!)  You will be sitting behind the band and looking at their backs the entire time. Not cool.

Instead, get in line at 7:30 p.m. Doors open at 8pm and show starts at 8:15 p.m. Best part?  Front and center floor seating (again, arrive at 7:30 p.m.) and you can stay for each show at 8:15, 9:15 and then again 10:15 p.m. Only $12 entrance per person, and $1 water.  Band takes requests.  

Loved this place.

Love this place. Great food, quick service. Nice place to relax and have a slow-paced dinner with friends. Also able to drive here, grab a quick bite, and make it back to work during a 1-hour lunch break.

I just got a couch and chair. The couch was custom, and the chair was a floor model. I'm very happy with both. Even better in person than computer design. Most of what they do is custom, which is fantastic. There are so many more options in styles, materials, arm rests, types of legs, sizes than you'll see on the floor models. If you like something, definitely speak with one of the staff about your customizing options, which can substantially affect prices (my choices were lower than the designs they had out, but you can certainly spend more).

Yes, you'll have to wait a bit of time for the piece to be made. That's what custom means. Also got a couple of throw blankets, I heart them.

I had a great experience. Natalie (hope I'm spelling that correctly) worked with me on figuring out what to do with my oh-so-tiny space. She was helpful and responsive, and did not try to up-sell me. She came over to my house and we sorted out what pieces and colors would work. 

Couch and chair arrived yesterday, 3 weeks early. Delivery guys kept me up-to-date on the delivery time, and set everything up well.  

Their prices are what they are -either they're too expensive, within budget, or you want to spend more for something higher quality. That's all on you to figure out. For me, it's what I expected to spend on a custom sofa. Ditto with designs -it's to your taste or it's not. I like their style, so I bought stuff there. Prices and designs are all on their website and available in store, no mysteries. 

I can't speak for longevity, how pieces will wear over time, but they seem pretty solid. There is a stain protection spray that you can get -I did. Will see if that holds true for stain resistance. Cat and dogs like their new couch.

I eat a lot of fast food and this is not a top choice. The automated order machine was broken and it couldn't accept cash for payment so to the long line I go. Like my previous visit the order was wrong on more than one item including a "no tomato" burger having a big juicy red slice. 

The order had taken nearly 15 minutes to be prepared and the two of us came during non peak hours. We swear never to return

These guys took our second car, furniture and 100 boxes from our 3rd floor apartment with only stairs and no elevator from Lansdale PA to Louisville Kentucky in just 2 days. Everything arrived safely with nothing broken and we were treated like we were their only customer. The price quoted didn't change at the time of payment either.  These guys are very professional and a joy to work with in a very nervous time.

Great Place!!!  Good seclection of wine and cheeses.  Appetizers are to die for!

Really nice atmosphere...and the staff is very friendly.  

The back patio is really nice as well.

One of the owners can usually be spotted mingling with the guests, insuring everything is going well.  They are also very good at offering suggestions, should the wine list overwhelm you!

Can't wait to go back once they start serving brick oven pizzas.

Went here the other night with my buddies from Guys Night Out.

Everyone agreed the service, food, and ambiance were excellent.

Happy Hour, and I've been here several times for that, does get a bit loud as the evening moves along.

Our supper group dined at 6:00 on a Wednesday and noise was not a problem.



Another Excellent Happy Hour here this past Friday.

Great prices on delicious food and drinks.

What more could you ask for?

Had a wonderful dinner at the tavern I had the chicken skewers, they we're delicious, wish they had more veggies in them however. But still they were great! My girlfriend got the Mahi sandwich and said it was perfectly blackened a Cajun tater that paired well with a creamy cucumber garnish, it was all really delicious! I got the house made cocktail "Amerboire".  So good I got 2!! Natalie was our server and she was so helpful and great! Made us feel right at home in Nashville! Can't wait  to come back

Expected a larger burger for $11. Seasoned very well. Staff was friendly. I ordered a Sex on the Beach and the bartender faked her way through. Pretended she knew how to make one but it was no where close. LOL! Still good, but a totally different drink from what I ordered. Back to the burger...tasty, but not an $11 burger.
Hot donuts. Be careful. Its addictive. and yummy. I don't like the glazed ones though

Use to come here a lot, last two visits were not good, seated us next to the bus station and had to listen to the slaming of silver ware most of the night, food took forever for the two of us, while a table of eight who ordered after us got their food first. Food was cold and over cooked. Waitress looked about twelve and had the experience of that, She was very inattentive and looked as if she was heading to a keg party in IV. Promote the busboy, cause he was awesome. Next time we went to see my friends band play (to find out they had cancelled them) Staff appeared unhappy and stressed when we walked in, they were not very welcoming , bartender looked up and just kinda glared at us to the point we changed our mind about Dinner and left. If you are wanting to visit this place...come up for the tri tip sandwiches, they are worth the drive, but I do not recommend the food in the Restaurant...

This Qdoba is probably the worst place I have ever been to. I placed an online order and when I showed up to pick it up, no one had even started on my order. After they realized I was there, they could have cared less. It still took 15 minuets to get the order filled. There wasn't even anyone else waiting. And then I saw one of the employees cleaning the counter by brushing all the crumbs and spills onto the floor. The whole restaurant was filthy. If I hadn't paid, I would have left. You couldn't pay me to return to this location. One star is way too much!

Beautiful, tasteful and quaint. This b&b is paradise. The staff is friendly, the rooms are great and the entire experience is first class. If you want to experience some history and elegance this is a very nice place to stay.

PUMPKIN PANCAKES KEEPS THE PANTRY PACKED AND POPPIN

Another legendary restaurant in Nashville, the Pancake Pantry was on our shortlist during a trip I took to the city of country music with some friends. This place always has a line apparently, but we moved through it pretty quickly and got seated within about 20 minutes.

The wait staff was pretty no-nonsense, which was fine. They took our orders quickly, and quietly made sure our coffee and waters remained topped. The dining space looks more like a summer camp mess hall than a traditional restaurant, and I felt my inner child coming out as my eyes ran over the dozen or so pancake options on the menu. 

In the end, I decided to order a Medley and two chocolate chip pancakes. The medley is a cleverly named medley of all the good things you could ever think of putting in an omelet, baked together in a bed of potatoes so its just a little crispy and reminiscent of my dad's Sunday hash. I substituted American Cheese for swiss and added jalepenos, and it was fantastic. 

The true pièce de résistance were, of course, the chocolate chip pancakes that came on the side. These were the fluffiest bad boys I have ever had. These pancakes were like the weird stuffing you see in old attic walls. They were spongy without being dry, generously covered in hundreds of mini chocolate chips that melted together as I cut into the dough. My only disappointment is that I will probably never get to eat pancakes this good again. Pancake Pantry has ruined all Denny's, IHOPS, Waffle Houses, and even my dear old grandmother's homemade breakfast cakes for good. Do yourself a favor and make this place a priority while you're in Nashville.

This is my favorite bakery in Chinatown! I usually get a pineapple bao (bun), red bean bao, and pork bun. 

These buns are the cheapest and they also have bags of multiple buns, with and without filling. They have boba but I've never tried it, as well as custard tarts. I love the buns and that's what I go here for. 

The service is decent. They don't speak much English, which isn't out of the ordinary in Chinatown. There's lots of seating and it's decently clean. 

Come here for the cheapest priced buns and baked goods (which are yummy) in Chinatown!
My first REAL experience of a damn good cigar. Will, the salesperson was great, his recommendation for me was great. The Ashton was smooth, creamy all the way to the end. I'm coming back for sure.
Terrible. Wish I could give it zero stars. Ignorant worker wouldn't let me make multiple orders at the drive thru. Waste of time

Nice, quiet, romantic spot. The dim lighting sets the mood. I came here with a friend a while back and had a good time. It's very different from your typical bar - no TVs or music, but this makes for great, intimate conversation. I don't remember what drink I had, something with champagne and a strawberry but it was very good. I'd definitely come back if I find myself in the area again.

everything else is 4/5 or 5/5 stars. but the blizzards are around 1 to 2 stars. first it takes forever for the order, Second, when they give you a frozen treat.... you expected to be frozen. instead it's a milkshake. if I wanted a milkshake I would probably order a milkshake. remember those years when they used to smile and tip it upside down to show you it's frozen. not these days, if you press on the break too hard, it's all over your car.

This is a really good all-purpose location for events. Especially events with anything to do with skates (inline or quad).

It's pretty straightforward here.  They host sporting events, offer some concessions and a good time was had by all.

However, I do have to comment that I think every seat in the house is a good one. Especially from the balcony level, where you can pick up a snack or a beer while watching the show downstairs.

There's also a bar/club upstairs that is pretty decent. It doesn't have the personality of other area clubs, but they're new and establishing their own niche.

A bare-boned place, so don't expect a lot of ambiance, that being said....I don't need ambiance as long as the food is good. BAP has a nice short menu and the bibimbap was wonderfully prepared and delicious. 
I will be coming back for more!
I also saw they added pajeon (korean savory pancake) to the menu, and i'll definitely be trying that on my next visit.
the price is great too - compare it to Rice & Mix on Walnut (also a favorite of mine) and i think BAP can hold its own...price is more affordable too!
The proprietor is also a very friendly man, courteous and helpful too. The portions are large - so there was no mistaking it would keep you sated.

I enjoy the beer selection, beet salad and calamari. Not in love with the food over all. This is a good place if you're looking for a few beers and an appetizer or two...wouldn't suggest the burger- its served on an english muffin- its just mediocre.
With that said...its a great place to watch soccer games.

I booked the Riviera Mansion exactly one year before my wedding, and I never regret that decision. My husband and I live in Philadelphia and we decided to get married in Santa Barbara not only because of his family but also because it's one of the most romantic and beautiful cities in the US we've ever been to. There were so many good places for weddings in SB, but we chose the Riviera Mansion (University Club) not only because of its old spanish charm and elegance, but also because of their good wedding packages. I was close to booking another venue, but my heart was telling me to look for one more place. The day I spoke to Breanna about the mansion, I was sold immediately. I booked the venue right away. She was very pleasant to talk to, and she was very patient in answering all my questions. We communicated via email and phone for almost a year before the wedding, and she was very consistent and accommodating! I sent her numerous emails about my plans and inquiries, and her turnaround response time was very quick. When we flew to SB for our initial meeting, she was very sweet and friendly, and gave us a tour of the mansion. We fell in love with the place all over again. Before visiting, I relied on the photos in the website and on Facebook, but after seeing the place in person, it was much better, and I felt so happy that I followed my gut. And until our final meeting before the wedding, Breanna went through the wedding timeline thoroughly to make sure that everything was in place, and even came on the day of the wedding to check if everything was all set. All in all, our wedding experience with the Riviera Mansion was a beautiful experience we will never forget, and we're so happy that we chose to make beautiful lifetime memories here.
More vegan options than I expected. The collard green wrapped farmstead was hardier than expected.

This place is a little hit or miss.  There were three of us in our party, two really loved their food - however, my sandwich had obviously been under a heat lamp for a while.  The bread was dry and hard all of the way through. 

Pros:
Bloody Mary's -  spicy!!  So good!
Omelets were good 

Cons:
Incredibly slow service .. and when you got service.. it wasn't especially friendly
Inconsistent food quality, some good.. some not

Overall, OK here -  but I wouldn't go out of my way to go back.

I would give it zero stars if I could, but yelp obviously doesn't like that. First, if you want to call this dealership the operator acts like the secretary of the CEO, and doesn't want to connect you to talk to anyone. Then she gives you a lecture about how things are handled. She finally connected me, after telling her she can keep the car if this call doesn't get anywhere very soon. Working with Lance was a pleasure. When it came to pick up the car we were informed that due to internal commission problems we would have to receive the car from Tony now as he was the first point of contact even though he wasn't at work or had any part in the deal at any time. Turned out he didn't even know what car we bought. When voicing my displeasure about having to work with someone else, John Hartman, the assistant general manager, just gave a rude answer asking what car we were picking up. Dealing with Crown GMC was a pleasure in the past, but with Hyundai not so much, yet the price made me not walk away at this point. I can only suggest to take your business elsewhere if you expect to be treated with respect. Interestingly it turned out that after signing all paperwork the promised navigation system is non existent and the car supports navigation through Apple Car Play or Android Auto. Make sure you'll get everything in writing before signing.

The French onion soup is my new favorite food. So many places make it with Swiss cheese (gag) but Slainte does it right with provolone and garlic bread. Just amazing. Their potato soup is good too, but I had to have two bowls of the French onion.
The majestic place is my go-to for breakfast, just wish they were open for more hours.

We went to Farm & Fisherman a few days after it opened.  It was mid-March and still a bit cold, and the small dining room was a bit drafty (they'll definitely need a shelter around the door next winter because when you walk in, you're standing right among the tables).  It's pretty close quarters with nowhere to wait for your table if you're early for your reservation like we are, but the location is great, and we were able to grab a quick drink at Mixto across the street (where customer service is sometimes seriously lacking).  What's good about being in such a small and intimate space is that you get a good look at what everyone's ordering, and everything looked delicious.  You are, however, knocking elbows with adjacent tables and can't exactly have any quiet conversation.  Farm & Fisherman is not the place to go for a quick bite.  I don't know if they're going for the "slow food" thing, but there was a long time between courses (filled with rolls and amazing house-made butter).  The food was really outstanding though and one of the best meals I've had in a while.  The farro soup was impossibly smooth with juicy chicken and a bright bite of microgreens - I asked if there was any cream in it because of the consistency, but nope that's just pure vegetable goodness.  We also had the prosciutto wrapped egg and pigs ear salad with pine nuts and lardoons (fabulously crispy and beautifully dressed).  For my entrée I had chicken...it was amazing, but I can't remember much else about it because I lost myself in the best hen of the woods mushrooms I've ever tasted in my entire life.  Actually, probably best any mushroom prepared any way I've ever had in my entire life.  Servers were moderately attentive and very knowledgeable.  We'll definitely be back.  BYOB.

Was visiting from California and it was Tuesday, so naturally I was craving some tacos. Looked up this place which had $2 tacos and $4 margaritas during happy hour so that already deserves one star in itself. 

We were seated in the back patio which had really cute decor and lighting. Only drawback is that I feel like we were sometimes forgotten about back there. Not to mention the waiter seemed super flustered. Which, I get it, it's happy hour, but there's no shame in writing down our order to make sure you get it right. 

Ended up getting a few tacos and chips with guac and queso dip for the table. Carnitas was great but the tortillas were not top notch. Maybe I'm just a CA taco snob, idk. I heard the guy from the table next to me ask the waiter what carnitas was so maybe Mexican food isn't the specialty around here... The guac and queso dip were both top notch though so extra points for that.

Would definitely recommend this place to a fellow out of towner looking for some good Mexican food or for anyone looking for a solid happy hour.

Third time to Fermateria. I'm really trying to like it. The only reason I'm giving them 2 stars is because the beer is very good. 
  This was the first time I was seated at a table that wasn't in the bar area. It took over 15 mins for our server to stop by the table. She didn't introduce herself but asked if we needed more time. Really?  I don't need more than 15 mins to figure out that there isn't much I would bother ordering from the menu. I got the kale and egg salad which was totally bland. I waited 10 mins to flag someone for salt and pepper to add some flavor. Then it took 5 more mins to get it. There were plenty of empty tables so  not sure what the problem was other than our server was NEVER around and rarely checked in on us. It took over an hour to get a kale salad and for my dining partner to get his burger. 
  The original tired hands has been more attentive in general and at least they have really good bread and cheese.   I hope they work the kinks out because it is a really nice space and I really want it to be a success.
Went here for my 26th birthday and it was hands down the best meal I've ever had in Philly. Worth the money! The game hen?! Outta this world delicious.
I feel like hurting someone every time I pull into this parking lot. Complete MESS!!!!
Great place, caring and compassionate staff. They have always taken great care of our pets, I wouldn't go anywhere else,  & Dr.  Haskell is the best!

Tampa Shoe Repair's Rick and Allan are the best at fixing shoes and anything leather or faux-leather related!! I brought them several pairs of high-heeled pumps and boots and they made them look new again! The service was impeccable and they went above and beyond for me! I am a reporter for CBS and I run around all day long for hours in my heels and they get wrecked fast! So I go through shoes a lot! 
You can't go wrong dropping off your beautiful shoes here! Best place ever!!! I'm moving and I don't know what I am going to do without them! They are my favorite!!

A great local (regional chain) diner with friendly staff, serving up tasty comfort food in a clean and pleasant atmosphere.  The menu offers a wide selection of breakfast and sandwich items, all reasonably priced.

On a quest for a good meal from a non-chain restaurant, I searched Yelp and found Dot's.  I'd driven past Dot's several times and thought about trying it, and now I'm glad I did.

I found easy parking right on the corner, and was encouraged when I saw local law enforcement and taxi drivers dining here.  Greeted when I entered, I decided to sit at the classic diner counter.  The interior is nicely done in a semi-50's diner motif, with a fair amount of seating including booths and tables.  Flat-panel TVs with CNN and ESPN gave you something to watch if the local color didn't somehow maintain your interest.  The waitress promptly provided me with a menu and asked for my drink order, all the while greeting other diners as they came in, many by their first names (obviously a local favorite.)

After reading about the Crawfish Julie (thanks Meli E.), I decided to have the seafood omelet with hash browns.   Watching the cool looking cook whip up my omelet (she sure knew her way around the kitchen!), it was ready within a few minutes, and served with a buttermilk biscuit that was halved and then browned on the grill, a nice touch!  My omelet was delicious, as were the hash browns.  Despite my best efforts to limit how much I was going to eat, everything was so tasty I wound up eating it all.

I checked out using a major credit card for under $10, and left with a satisfied smile on my face.  I'll be back the next time I'm in the area!

This chipotle is absolute garbage!!  The staff at this location is absolutely incompetent.  They under stuff your burritos, forget items in your order, ask unbelievably stupid questions, do not clean up the mess they make after each burrito and then proceed to drag your food through it.  

By the time you make it to the check out, they top it off by incorrectly charging you for your order, and because of the idiocy at large, they ask you to just accept their mistakes and move along because they can't figure out how to fix it.  

Horrible, this is all over several visits.

Great sandwiches for a great price. The soup and sandwich combo is a great deal, I recommend the roast beef panini.
There is also free frozen yogurt when you dine in. I eat here multiple times when I travel to Tampa for business.

We were a party of four; we were told it would be a 30 minute wait, which was fine. We were called up earlier than expected but as a party of 2, and then told to wait. ....what? The hostess looked like an unwashed teenager who just rolled out of bed at 7 pm on a Tuesday night. As we stood there in front of the hostess station, awkwardly waiting, another waitress shoved past us without saying anything and then glared at us. Girl, I understand it's busy, but I've worked during the holidays before and being rude to customers didn't make my shift go by any faster. Just rude, rude, rude and unprofessional.

Food is decent. Slow but ok service. Asked to watch a golf tournament on one of the TVs and it took them 45 mins to change the channel (asked 3 times). We would have stayed longer and had more drinks etc if anyone bothered to accommodate paying customers.
We have come here two days in a row now. Great food both times and a great atmosphere. Definitely give it a try.

The restaurant is in the middle of the Italian Market on ninth st. The restaurant is old school, red sauce place.  If that's the type of place your looking for it's ok.  But if your looking for something more lighter, clean flavored Italian this is not your place.  It's busy and on the smaller side.
Great food and great selection! It's one of our regular spots. I love that their menu has a Vietnamese, Chinese and Japanese options. Every time we eat here, the food is always YUMMY!

Soooo.... We went on Veterans Day and it was a shit show in there... Looked like maybe one or two servers and if you took a look around you could tell it was a terrible shift. The manager was just chit chatting with the cooks while the server ran around crazy. Then an actual old veteran had to wait 8 minutes for a dang coke. The pizza was decent but how dirty the plates and cups were ruined it all. It was not a fun experience.

Love their burgers, the fries'll do.  but the REAL find here is the weird oatmeal cookie nuggets.  they've got a wacky consistency that i LOVE... like unbaked, or misshapen granola bars, or some other new culinary technique. seriously. check them out.

I was never really inspired to try Cuenelli's simply by walking past it, but I decided to try it after reading a very positive review on another site.  Now I have a new habit!  It is the best rotisserie chicken I have ever had, hands down...uber moist, slightly spicy and with perfect skin.  It comes with a selection of creamy, zippy sauces that add SUCH a different and delicious taste. Sides include fries and salad for the less adventurous taste buds, but also Latin flavors like cilantro rice (which is muy rico) served with a choice of black or spicy beans, tostones, fried plantains (the best I've ever had) and yuca, among others.  The food is really delicious...especially for the price.  It's not upscale in the least, but it gets five stars for what it is.

Not worth the wait... I've worked in several restaurants in touristy areas and believe me folks, it's hard to screw up breakfast in a place like this. They have a great view of the water.  It's a cozy "feels local" kind of place.  All they need to do is smile, be courteous, provide attentive service, and halfway decent breakfast food and it's a 5 star place. Unfortunately, our experience was lacking in all of the above.  I walked in to record my name, party and acceptable dining location. Done. Waited 20-25 minutes. No big deal. Was seated at the "counter" despite requesting to be seated at a table...wait, seriously? no backs on the stools, no counter service to speak of. We were essentially sitting at the server bus station surrounded by bins of creamers,butter, cartons of juice, extra ramikens.... After another 10 minutes, a server reluctantly asked us for our order... as we were listening to the wait staff be "cut" since there were open tables - why are we stuck here?  Another 15 minutes and our "food" arrived. Powdered eggs, store-bought bread, canned OJ, undercooked eggs, cold food, congealed cheese, plastic plates, plastic condiments... it was only edible to my 9 year old son.  There is a Dunkin Donuts in the same strip mall. Grab an egg and cheese bagel and pull up a chair along the water - trust me, it will be a better experience.  Hope the food and service was just a one-off today... if not, your regulars must not have any taste buds or self respect left... good luck.   I have pictures to back this up - just haven't figured out how to add to this post!!

Our second time in New Orleans was made even better by our stay at Drury's.  What makes this place shine is its staff - from all of the front desk folks to our housekeeper Thalia.  

Our room was very clean and updated - although on the smaller side. Our bed and pillow was comfortable. We were worried about noise since we got a room by the elevator and ice machine. But it didn't bother us.  We liked the paintings of New Orleans sights on the walls.  

Drury's is located away from the madness of the French Quarter but within easy walking distance to it as well as the St. Charles street car.

I had the Fleur De Lis Omelet and it was delicious. In town for a tech conference (SpringOne), I wanted to find an authenticy feeling place for breakfast, and this fit the bill. It was a casual, hole-in-the-wall atmosphere with a tiny kitchen and delicious food.

Awesome awesome awesome!
Don't think twice. Long lasting. Covered every inch. So surprised and happy. 
I was skeptical about an airbrush tan from a random place. Not only being from South Florida where a tan is accessible but an airbrush is even easier.. Awesome chick. Awesome tan.

In town for only a day we tried to find a good breakfast.  This place was not crowded, and I needed my coffee fix. So, we decided to try it. Service is super slow. My coffee tasted like sewer water. The  asparagus mushroom omelet was ok, but not worth the wait. The potatoes were soggy, a definite no-no for the roasted kind. The bagel with Lox was just average. But I can't get that sewer water memory out of my head!!!

Great food, great service, great price...  recommend the Buffalo dog, fries and maple soaked churros.. If you  like hot dogs ... This is dogs gone wild...  Good third date dinner... Stroll south street...  Grab a classy dog and right on to the next thing...  Just keeping real...  Lol

You go here for the nostalgia. Don't get me wrong, the food is delicious but it is one of those places you go once to say you have been there then don go again. Mainly for the hour plus wait for the same food I can get at waffle house (which I love). But you should definitley go there.

I haven't got my sandwich yet? So I can't review the food. I can tell you the service is the worst I've seen.  May I just got lucky with the worst waitress. For the first time in my long dining career, I may leave no tip.
Glad to see you guys are still around! I TRIED to go, but ended up in Surreys? Damn. Was too hungry to contiune the search, but am glad to have found Refuel! Will be in soon!

Ate lunch there during the week we had fish tacos n a grouper sandwich. Big portions and great food. I was afraid it would be pricey but for the quality n portion size it was worth it. I'll definitely go back.
Great gyros, family run, friendly staff, the owner is super personable and you can pick up a great lunch for under 10$ in just a few minutes. Highly recommend

This place is okay
Maybe I went on a bad night, my meal was nothing to write home about. My lobster was very small and very bland. The waiter was friendly and very attentive.

We've been looking for our go-to sushi spot in Reno for years and we just found it! Sushi is fresh, delicious, and unique. The service was over the top amazing~ our server John made the perfect sushi recommendations for our taste and left us feeling full and satisfied. Ambiance is chic, loungey, cool vibes. We will definitely be back for more!!!

I took my family to NY pizza last night. We were the only table in the restaurant on a Friday night. The service was terrible. Our waiter obviously hated his job and could care less about taking care of customers. We ordered a spinach dip for an appetizer and it took over 20 min for it to arrive. The pizza that we ordered was nothing to be excited about and last night will be the last time we visit this restaurant. Management should wake up and make some changes. If you want to be disappointed... Visit this place

I love this place called for quotes and they had the best price in town ! I stopped in that day to have a stained uniform done and it was done the next day at 4 ! I will be coming here to get all my dry cleaning .

Buffalo Exchange is a chain store which is kind of a bummer considering there are local joints like Funky Monkey down the street that get less attention, however, it still has a nice selection and I've always been able to score some cool finds here. I have been disappointed by the prices they offer for some of the clothing I've sold here ($20 for a once-worn $300 BCBG gown) but it eliminates the hassle from doing resale through Ebay and the like. I love their jewelry and more costume-like wares. Buffalo Exchange is A-OK.

We booked a private balcony party with Sharon Hart and it went even better than advertised. I was worried at first after reading misguided reviews and talk from some visitors but our experience couldn't have been better. We had two private rooms with excellent Cajun style food plus the balcony. I recommend this bar specifically Sharon when looking for balcony rentals on bourbon street

AJ, MJ and Josh B arrived right on time at 8AM. They were professional, hard working and took great pains to wrap all of the furniture. We had torrential rain in the middle of unloading at the new house, but that didn't stop them. Not one piece of furniture had a drop of rain on it because of their earlier efforts. I have to say in all of my many moves over the past forty years, many of which entailed moving my entire household overseas, have I ever been so impressed. AJ and crew get an A+ in my book.

The sandwiches are minuscule and have a ton of bread compared to sandwich ingredients! I had a chicken, zucchini (who puts zucchini on a sandwich anyhow). Anyhow, I ordered ir and this was a major disappointment. There was probably a couple tablespoons of chicken on 1/2 of what I ate. My husband had procuitto and hi was pretty much the same. 
  So I'd recommend ordering cafe and croissants 
here.

Meun Fan is nice because of its Goleta location. The food is average, but their major downside is their pricing. Highly overpriced for the portions and the Thai food market in general. Facility is clean and the staff is friendly.

Among the food trucks at Drexel University, Cucina Zapata is definitely in my top 3 favorite trucks on campus. What I like about the food trucks at Drexel is that they are priced to not interfere with students' tight food budget. They are priced not high or low, but definitely cheaper than a lot food vendors that is owned by the school or neighboring stores like Shake Shack, Cozara, and etc. Another thing I like about Cucinas is the friendly staff, creativity, and uniqueness of the food they make for the customers. 

Cucina Zapata features a fusion of Thai and Mexican, such as tacos, burrito, katsu, bubble tea, and much more. The first I recommend is the satay chicken soft tacos (1 for $3, 2 for $6, 3 for $8) because I know they can get me full. The lettuce, the peanut sauce, spicy mayo, chicken, and the soft taco; the combination is amazing and the taste when it enters in your mouth is so satisfying. The second thing I would recommend is the Captain Crunch Tilapia Burrito. I know right..just the name of the food gives you wonder and joy. The tilapia's crunchy coat (Captain Crunch cereal) is the key and what makes this burrito delicious. The third thing is the Chicken Katsu. For just $6, this dish is packed with so much flavor: spicy mayo and siracha. This is definitely a must get!

On top of this, the tea here is a bit better than other popular locations, such as Tea Do and Kung Fu Tea. I love the homemade thai tea or taro tea and definitely recommend others to get this if you love this curiously orange colored tea with bubbles. After ordering these food that Cucina offers, not only it tasted so good consistently, but also I was able to tell about the creativity: it's Cucina's strong suit. 

There are so many food trucks on campus, but Cucina Zapata is no doubt my top three most favorite food truck at Drexel University campus.

We found this place while traveling on Yelp. Thought we would try it due to high rating. Good food and friendly staff. Little confusing the first time you order. Opportunity exist to make it easier to order and prices. Otherwise, 5 stars.

It ain't easy trying to find a new mechanic when you're new to the area, that's for sure. I went with Pep Boys because I thought it was a brand I could trust. I figured it be more expensive than a local shop but I needed new brakes and rotors ASAP so I had to find a shop quick and I went with this Pep Boys on Broad.

The manager we talked to was friendly and fairly helpful.

The problem was when we got our car back. First off, it took about 4 hours which was fine, we hopped into the city to kill time but it was twice as long as they said it would be. When we got back they said we should also get new tires, which another mechanic later told me my tires were fine. Our brakes started having the same issues within 24 hours. We asked a few mechanics about the problem and they said our brakes still looked like they were in bad shape.

I don't what they Pep Boys guys did for 4 hours but it wasn't what I paid for and they maybe didn't do any work at all. I sure paid for it though. About twice as much as I should of according to a local mechanic.

It's worth it to do your research. Get a local recommendation and avoid this Pep Boys.

The BEST! Great after Cards & Blues games. I've been here many times. Always friendly fast service no matter how long the lines. I recommend the Dutchman concrete! A MUST visit if you're in St. Louis.

I'm not going to say that I enjoy my visits here, because I don't enjoy the process, but it's not all bad.

The staff here is friendly and gets the job done quickly and efficiently.  I've donated at the Blood Center and at a few different off site locations. My latest donation was at Lakeside Mall. I happened to be there and the giveaways were pretty cool. A Tricentennial TShirt?! I'll take it!  A box of Russell Stover's chocolates?!? Yep, that's me!

The brick and mortar location is sort of dingy looking, but it's clean. There are drinks and snacks for you after you donate. Take advantage and have some to ward off any lightheadedness. The phlebotomists here know what they're doing, so follow their instructions if you're a first time donor. They won't steer you wrong. 

I feel like I'm giving back when I make my donation and always hope that if i, or my family is in the situation to need blood that it will be available. 

Bravo to these folks for doing what they do and helping out the community.

Not bad just not the same.
The service was good and the Pizza was not bad,
the restaurant itself had seen better days.
Part of enjoying a good meal also includes
the vibe or general feel of my surroundings.
Godfathers was a fun place to eat 10+ years ago
and while re visiting Reno we thought we would pay a visit.
Thank you Godfathers for the memories, but unless time and money is put in
 it may be time  to move on.

I was in town for a convention and sat at the bar.  The bar staff was super friendly and attentive.  I had the 1-1-1 appetizer which was great.  For dinner, I had the BBQ Shrimp, which was also great (although super messy).  I'm looking forward to coming back again and trying the bacon wrapped shrimp and grits.

In short, these guys were great. I don't usually spend time writing reviews but I felt this experience warranted it. At the counter Sean and Kirk were cool and knowledgeable guys who saved me money everywhere they could. And the tech Christopher did a great job at the hands on part of taking care of my truck. I'll definitely be back for any further tire or mechanical needs.

I'm a mega horror fan, and the Voodoo Bone Lady delivered. She is FULL of knowledge (she's a fifth-generation voodoo priestess and a member of an organization that delves into the city's past and supernatural realm) and an incredibly skilled storyteller who can bring the streets (and their supernatural spirits) to life. We did this on our first night, and it was a great intro to NOLA.

Responded quickly when we had a leaky gas line... Right after a huge rain storm and other plumbers were saying it would be three days before they could even look at it! Obviously they didn't understand we can't go without hot water for three days! B&W came out the next day in the window they promised and made the repairs in about 3 hours. Dave explained all the repairs before he made them. we had our gas turned back on that evening thanks to an equally quick response from the gas company

While initially I was very disappointed in this location, the manager really knows customer satisfaction. 

Being Christmas Eve, I had previously contacted this location to find out their hours. We were driving through during the holidays and staying at the hotel on premises. When we arrived 30 mins prior to the closing time the doors were locked. This was obviously a big disappointment after an 8 hr drive when a beer would have hit the spot. 

I posted on Granite City's website and received a call from the manager within an hour apologizing. To make it up to us, he delivered a growler of my fav brew along with a gift card. And what a nice guy!  

Next year when passing through on our way to FL we will make it a point to patronize them. And when we return home, to our local GC.

If you are looking for a top notch, caring, professional,  and compassionate Veterinarian Animal Hospital then look no further North Star Vets is it! In Sept/Oct 2017 I brought my 10 year old male English Black lab Rocky in to see them for a toe nail injury that turned out to be cancer. The diagnosis was Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the toe. He needed to have his right middle toe on his right front leg amputated so that the cancer wouldn't spread and in return save his life. Id like to give a special shout out to the veterinarians and surgeons who assisted in providing excellent care to my dog Rocky. *Dr. Higgins (Veterinarian 1st  consult) and his also excellent surgeon *Dr. Arulpragasam (Surgeon whom did his surgery). You both did a fantastic job and thank you very much! The front desk people are super nice as well as all of the vet techs and veterinarians we dealt with when there. We also visited the Maple Shade location to have his sutures taken out. Dr. Sarowitz (Surgeon whom took his sutures out) You too did a fantastic job and thank you! Rocky even thanked you with several kisses. I thank you too! I just can't say enough good about North Star and their employees. Rocky is doing great thanks to North Star Vets and up and running around again as if nothing even happened to him. Thank you so much for all that you did for my dog Rocky and my family. I highly recommend them for all of your pets medical care needs. 5 Stars! Sincerely, Holly, Michael, and Anthony Sollecito AND Rocky says thank you too. Woof!  Xxoo Locations visited were Robbinsville, NJ and Maple Shade, NJ...***Their is not one thing that needs improvement nor your employees. They are all to be commended for providing exceptional top notch service across the board.

Boyfriend and I ordered the Pacific pre fixe meal. The first course was not very pleasant - there was way too much kick in the sauce, but our server was very nice and was able to switch that out for their popular cheddar sauce instead.

The main entree was delicious. I would recommend their curry sauce with the meal. (The Fondue Fusion)

The best part was the dessert. We ordered the Banana's Foster (sp?) and that sauce was delicious, like... omg. Maybe it's because both boyfriend and I like white chocolate, but it was definitely very yummy.

Despite the fact that we came in at 7:45 and they closed at 9, aaaand we stayed way past that time, we didn't feel rushed at all to leave.

It was a lot of food for the both of us - maybe if we ever come back, we'll come back for the dessert.

I showed up for a hungover lunch on Sunday afternoon. The place wasn't super crowded. We were seated a few tables over from the nearest patron so we could hear each other talk. I enjoyed the decor, open and light, particularly loved the green behind the bar. I also like the commitment to  sustainability. 

We ordered the lincoln park (thin crust) and it was delightful. The zucchini was a lovely touch on the pizza. It was pretty cheesy, much more focus on the cheese than the sauce. One of the better pizzas in StL. 

-1 star for blatantly criticizing a St.Louis tradition with "anti-provel" shirts. Do well on your own, not by knocking some friendly competition.

I would like to say that it is possible to really dislike NPR and love Trader Joe's.  I will also say that I was introduced to TJ's by someone who loves NPR.

Trader Joe's is awesome.  They are my favorite grocery store anywhere (I'd happily take them over the local choices Giant, Acme and national chains like Whole Foods, Wild Oats, Wegman's and specialty organic stores) and I love shopping here.

TJ's has really good stuff really, really cheap.  The tempeh, soy milk, tofu, and cereal (among so many other things) are super cheap.  Everything they sell is actually good food.  They have really great unique items (I love the frozen veggie combinations, pastas and frozen herbs!) and all sorts of great staple foods.

TJ's are small stores, usually 6-8 aisles in my experience.  They do not carry national brand stuff (you will not find Campbell's soup here thankfully) so it's not the best place to find household type stuff you'd get a regular grocery store.

The only thing I don't love about TJ's is that sometimes they will stop carrying certain things after you've fallen in love with them.  This is usually OK because you will find you're also in love with whatever is next to it on the shelf.

It's a restaurant and a store all in one - how cool is that? No, really, this place is really cool. Good food, very good prices, relaxed atmosphere ... AND you can look for cool little finds around the restaurant/store while eating. I'm always impressed with the mixture of color and patterns inside, it's almost like being in a museum. 

I would give this place five stars, but on a few occasions the food and tea were not warm enough for my taste. Otherwise, it's a great place for good Indian food on a budget, with a very authentic setting.

I recently worked with Menu Maker to cater a large corporate event in Nashville.  Given that I'm based in Austin, TX, I had to pick them without a face-to-face meeting or having sampled their food.  I had some issues with communication during the planning of my event, but I know they are making strides to improve this.  Make sure that you get written confirmation of all your requests.

The week before the event, I was trying to get in touch with them to confirm the final event details because I knew that once I arrived in Nashville, I would be very busy with work and hard to reach.  It took several phone calls and emails to hear back from them, although the manager explained they've been having some trouble with their phone system.  We went over all of my event details and I made a couple of small changes to the menu, including selecting a gluten-free and vegetarian entree, for those guests with special dietary needs.  I talked to her at length about which appetizers and entrees are gluten-free because I'm allergic to gluten, as are many other people, and we settled on some good choices.  Fast forward to a few days before my event when the event coordinator, a different woman, called me and proceeded to run down the whole thing with me again because she didn't have the notes from my call with the owner.  I again stressed the menu changes and the importance of having gluten-free items.  On the day of the event, I discovered that they had swapped out one of the entrees I specifically requested (and that was listed on the final menu invoice) for a red bell pepper stuffed with couscous, which is NOT gluten-free.  I received an apology from the owner and assurance that she is working to improve their service.  Other than the last-minute menu change, guests enjoyed the food.

Okay, wow.  Seriously.  Boutique donuts with crazy flavors, great coffee; I went here twice during a four day visit.  Not sure what my favorite flavor was: Mandarin Coffee?  Orange Creamsicle?  Good coffee.  I hear the chicken is wonderful but we were never there in the morning.  They sell out of flavors of donuts, supposedly, so get here early.  Unique, and a staple of any trip to South Philly for the rest of my life, so I'll be eating a ton of donuts.

I would definitely come back.  It was elegant and the service was excellent. The food was so tasty and enough for two. We had the redfish special and the softcrab special. The special comes with gumbo, salad, and bread pudding.  All were so very good. I cannot say enough about the service. Top quality

We stayed at the Hollander Fathers Day weekend. ( 4 nites). This is the coolest Boutique hotel we've ever stayed! The decor is 1930's Keywest meets Miami/Cuba, with all 21st century amenities.  The staff are all incredible....ABCD, Above and Beyond the Call of Duty.  The beds are extremely comfy.  The food is good....desserts are decadent....homemade.  Price is very reasonable.  Can't wait to go back!!
Ordered takeout from Aroma,  and I was extremely surprised at how fresh everything was.  I'm not well versed in Indian cuisine,  but I know what I like.  :)

This is strictly for the Pepos in the college of SPC! The only reason im giving 4 stars is because the food is great, but the woman that works the counter, is the most rudest woman in the service industry. I brought my own lunch but saw utensils on the outside counter for everyone, however there were only knives, so I nicely asked the woman if I could please have a fork, she responded, we ain't got none, so then I ordered some green beans, I then again asked her for her fork, she looked at me with the rudest face and said, I only got spoons, I said okay that's fine. I sat down to eat my food, next thing you know, there's a ton of people in line, and what's she giving out, forks to people. I can't even. I'm in the service industry, I don't care how much you hate your job but damn, lose the tude.

I stayed at the JW Marriott for a traditional foods conference. It's the kind of event that is challenging for any hosting facility, as the organization involved does not simply select menus from the regularly available event menus. Instead, food starts arriving a week or so in advance of the conference (thus requiring appropriate storage be available - ever asked a venue to clear a walk-in for you?) and a chef comes in to direct the kitchen staff in traditional foods preparations methods. There have been issues at past venues for this event; the Indianapolis Marriott did a great job. One of the best I've seen.

Now, on to the hotel stuff. I was in a regular room on the 9th floor. My room was pretty close to the elevators and I could hear them whooshing and dinging. It wasn't super-loud, though, and it didn't keep me awake. The room was clean and everything seemed to be in good repair. The linens were above-average for hotel linens (especially the towels, which were both large and soft). The water pressure in the bath was not great; the hot water was hot enough to poach me when I wasn't careful.

At first the tub didn't drain particularly well (probably hair in the drain - they never know to fix it if someone doesn't tell them); a maintenance person was sent up promptly to service it. And they left a chocolate-popcorn treat with a "sorry there was a problem" note. That was totally unexpected and unnecessary.

The friend I split the room with said the hotel exercise room was one of the better ones she's used. The pool is small but clean and nice. All ice is found in an "ice room" near the elevators on the 2nd floor, which puzzled me at first.

The hotel staff is excellent. Every one that I encountered was helpful and friendly. I would happily stay there again.

Really cute, cozy place. The chocolate gelato was good and it was nice enough to sit on the back patio. The gal at the counter wasn't exactly friendly, which was awkward. I appreciate the bin for the plastic cups and spoons to recycle them!

I think this business is engaging in unethical behaviors. I have a GMC terrain that got timeshare issues but people here pretended they knew how to repair it. Returning to the store three times, they finally told me to go to the dealer to fix it. My friend has a car that is one year old and they asked him to change battery. Another friend has a broken transmission system right after she did oil change with the store. Don't recommend anybody to go there.

Got my car detailed here on Saturday.  It was stolen from in front of my house on Sunday.... Just don't leave a spare key in your car next to anything with your address written on it and you should be fine.

I went to Mandarin for a private party.  I didn't get the whole experience, but the one that I did made me wanting to go back to check it out.

I say that because I hate trying new clubs!  As far as standards for Mandarin, I wanted to compliment the bartenders, and atmosphere, and bathroom!

The bartenders were super fast and friendly, that could be because we had a smaller group maybe than what they normally see.  Our party was probably 50 people.

The bathroom, clean, and I have seen this before, but I love it, the sink is open to the men's bathroom and th water just falls from the wall into the sink.  Love it!

The atmosphere was very, sophisticated, not a place I would normally go.  I loved the balcony and the variety of seating/tables.  There were pub tables along with alcoves for a little privacy and also more open couches.  My favorite was the balcony over looking the fountain.
12/28/13. Great greek food. You cannot go wrong with anything on the menu. Fast bottle service. BYOB.  Book in advance though, they are a small restaurant.

Do not hesitate to utilize this facility. We always receive excellent, professional, and polite service. They send us picture and text updates of our pups. Our dogs love staying here. They get to go swimming, eat ice cream, and play a lot. We also get them groomed and bathed before pick up. You can't do better than this place if you have to leave your puppies somewhere other than home.

Show up during business hours and they are not open, no sign indicating that they would be closed, and no one answered the phone. If a business is going to be closed at least leave your customers a note on the door.

Came here with a groupon tuesday night and it was mildy busy. We were seated quickly and we were recommended a party boat for it was our first time trying sushi. Everything was amazing!! To finish our night we had green tea tempura fried ice cream. Will definitly be back again. Our waiter alex was the best!!!

This cute little tasting room serves wine by glass, by bottle, or they offer 3 different wine flights with 5 different tastings each. It's located on the pier on the 2nd level of some other shops. The view overlooks the ocean and it's just beautiful. This would be a great spot for a date or a girl's day. 

My friend and I ordered the classic flight for $14. We really enjoyed the Chardonnay, which surprised me because I typically enjoy red wines more. The other four tastings on this flight were just ok, nothing memorable about them. We did order a full glass of the Chardonnay though.

Bottles of wine are available for purchase to take home, as well as these great smelling candles made with their wine bottles, and other merchandise. Seating is available both inside and outside and the place has a very intimate feel. 

My friend and I really liked this place and we will likely come back next time we're in Santa Barbara. My only complaint is that I wish they offered individual tastings of the wines, or at least a build your own flight option.

Terrible service. Good enough food. I've been here twice this week. Service is a mess. They overcharged me for my meal on Tuesday and today when I asked for the special advertised on the window I was told it wasn't a special. I had to get out of cue and go outside, take a picture of the special being advertised and show it to the clerk.  By the way I lost my place in cue and had to get in line again.  The clerk still didn't know how to process the order and called the manager who seemed just as confused. I'm not sure I'm coming back. There are other options in the strip mall with just as good or better food with great service that won't over charge you.

After about a week in STL, PCWB totally made my Fri since we couldn't get a flight out that night.  It was at the end of a rambling tour through downtown, past City Hall and Union Station, through Forest Park and the Art Museum  on the hill, skirting past the zoo (we made a point to stop at Turtle Park), through the fancy-pants residential section of Clayton - and it was fancy - into the semi-built up area of downtown Clayton.  All in all, St Louis has some great architecture, beautiful parks and gardens, and a few too many sports arenas, but I get the feeling the locals are sorta invested.

We skipped the tapas place (too noisy), pizza (too many carbs), Chinese and Japanese, and after a big loop, sat down at PCWB at an outside table (whew!).  I really liked their basic caesar to start; it has to do with aromatic cheese on crispy greens.  They put anchovies in the dressing, soooo good. For dinner, I went with the Ham and Cheese (Gruyere) which came out piping hot, nicely browned and totally buttery and salty.  It goes well with the steamed broccoli and oven roasted potatoes, simple stuff.  I really like this little place bec/ dessert was a tiny slice of chocolate cake with rum butter frosting, lordy.  Such a great little bistro.  

It's airy and casual with great food.  It's nice to think that Pomme Restaurant - the heavy hitter  two doors down - has lighter fare here.  The chef? some fellow in a white outfit would wander down to PCWB to visit with the couple sitting next to us and order his friends another glass of wine.  Ah, the quintessential St Louis regulars!  Next trip, I'm staying in Clayton and skipping Arch everything.

They don't have Jameson. Also, the golf channel
is on every tv and on speaker. Didn't eat, but I think you get it.

I tried to like this place. They have good ideas, just very poorly executed. I've made reservations that were ignored. I've tried many menu items. Everything was edible but not much more than that. The food just doesn't make it worthwhile to sit in this strip mall for an hour to wait for a table. Best restaurant in the area? I guess but that's no big accomplishment. All done with this joint!

My family has been patients of Plainfield Eye Care and Dr. Groninger for many years.  I have gone to other clinics due to my insurance but always keep coming back.  Their staff is friendly, well trained, and educated on the latest trends.  Their equipment is current and they are always ahead of others on technology.  Dr. Groninger is the best at what she does and always takes the time to get to know her patients and their needs.  My daughter had an eye infection that was treated by the local immediate care, we thought it had cleared up and was a non-issue.  Through the eye scans they do, Dr. Groninger found scar tissue that could be damaging to her eye so we monitor it annually now.  You only get one set of eyes and I only want the best taking care of mine and my family's.  Dr. Groninger and the staff at Plainfield Eye Care are truly the best at what they do and I highly recommend them.

Great place to kill time, watch football grab some cheap brews and good yet affordable bar food. Large friendly bar area. Seems to be a neighborhood hangout but all are welcome. Daily specials for example all you can eat wings 8.99 on monday, 1 dollar taco night on wednesdays, thursdays pasta nite, 2 dollar lunch specials Monday through Friday 11am to 4 pm.

Surprisingly good wine list. Food was good. Our server Steve was excellent and had great recommendations for the table. Don't miss the smoke salmon spread. Would have licked the bowl if I was not concerned about public perception. My colleague orders the Tuna and was not disappointed. I had the shrimp and grits. Grits were very buttery, shrimp and andouille sausage were excellent on top. The fish tanks and walk thru are not to be missed. Only thing I would add are years to the wines listed. I did need to ask about the Grigich Chardonnay we ordered, it was a 2014. DELICIOUS!

Met a friend for lunch.  Chips and salsa were fresh and good.  Each had a Margarita which was good as well.  I enjoyed the water pitcher with fresh limes or lemons.  I had a salad with some blackened chicken.  Was a nice meal, nice service.  There was not a wait for tables, so we were seated right away.  Can't remember the bill total, but for going out to a longer lunch it seemed on par with what we expected.

My husband and I came in on a Sunday night and caught a guest chef collaboration. We ordered all 16 of the items on the mezze menu and enjoyed all of the very well blended, interesting flavors...especially the turnips, everything beets salad, the pickled celery with sour cherries, and faint anise flavored corn. The feta dip was tangy, hot and sweet at the same time. The surprising crunch in the hummus and as the other reviews mention, the pickled shrimp was really delightful. The jalapeño melon salad was my favorite light and spicy and sweet.

The highlight of the meal was the grilled octopus with a light, lemony sauce and the CRAB BEIGNETS!!!! That's right, the guest chef was from New Orleans. Justin Devillier from The Petite Grocery. The flavor, the slight crunch of the corn sauce was the perfect end to a perfect meal. 

The service was excellent per Ruby.  Would strongly recommend.

Mediocre in terms of food and service.  My boyfriend and I stopped in here Saturday afternoon on a whim because there was a Groupon and we were hungry.  The $3 Guinness was a pleasant surprise.  I ordered a veggie burger and my boyfriend had some sort of chicken wrap.  He enjoyed his, but my veggie burger was pretty bland.  I opened up the bun and dumped a bunch of salt and pepper on it.  The server wasn't rude or anything, but she wasn't friendly or nice.  When my boyfriend asked for a water, she said okay but proceeded to clear two tables, wipe them down, go stand at the bar and check her phone, talk to the bartender, and then finally bring over a water.  There were at least 8 empty tables and not a lot of people coming in, so no need to do all that before grabbing a quick water.
I don't know.  It was just mediocre.  Not terrible, not good.

Horn's is a Marigny neighborhood gem. Friendly, professional staff, a relaxed environment, and very good food. I like their brunch but really enjoy having dinner at Horn's. Their meatloaf is to die for and I love their chicken piccata with pasta Alfredo. I've been a dozen times and never had anything less than a very good experience.

Came back for dinner and so glad I did. Again, the service was friendly and attentive. All of the sides are Delish. We shared the 1/2 baked chicken and peach cobbler. Do yourself a favor and order the peach cobbler.
Pretty darn good BBQ. We ordered some pickle chips with our food and it was well worth it. Prices are more than fair and the portions will fill you up.

Tucked in a cozy spot on Watson, Yolklore is the type of restaurant I wouldn't expect in Crestwood. Normally a place like this would be downtown or in Clayton. Curious to find a place like this close by my husband and I was excited to try it out.

The space and decor is like most breakfast places: tight and cozy. The kitchen is open faced and there are coffee mugs, the menu, and a listing of the specials to greet you right at the door. 

I ordered the Bread Pudding French Toast and my husband ordered a basic breakfast plate. The french toast was good, the eggs my husband had were extraordinary and I really liked the direction they took with the potatoes, using whole yukon gold potatoes instead of cubed potatoes. 

I had a smoothie and he had the orange juice. I liked the smoothie but felt it was missing something. 

I noticed the manager touching tables as I ate, checking to see how everyone was enjoying their meal.

I enjoyed eating here, however I felt it was on the pricey side ($28 for two people) for breakfast.

I recently rented a car at the Philly airport.  They had a good selection overall, but when I checked out two or three cars, they all smelled like smoke and were not very clean.  It was obvious that although these were non smoking cars that someone had been smoking in them.  One of them still had ashes in the cracks and crevices of the center console.  
The steering wheel was 'sticky' from what I assume was the cleaning solvent used.
Before I left the parking lot I pulled a cleansing/sanitizing wipe from my suitcase and cleaned the surfaces. Not really my best experience with National.  They typically do a good job.
The real teaser was that the car I selected had satellite radio, which was a pleasant surprise.  Unfortunately, on day three of my rental that was deactivated.

We've been here several times and have tried cake, cupcakes, cookies, rice crispy treats and other dessert items. Each and every item has been incredible. Baked perfectly. Better than anything I've tried downtown or otherwise. I would recommend this bakery to anyone. Also, it's owned by a husband and wife who work there full time. They both truly have a passion for what they do and it comes though in their product and customer service!

My husband and I enjoyed a quick trip to New Orleans and chose The Saint hotel. We loved the hotel decor; very chic and clean. The service was great from the valet to the front desk.  We only had trouble when  ordering room service. It was difficult getting through to place the order, only to be hung up on.  Then when it arrived, we had no utensils. Other than that, we thoroughly enjoyed our visit! On a side note...you must eat breakfast at the Ruby Slipper just next door. The Bam Bam Breakfast and shrimp grits were delish!

You wouldn't know this was a tequila cantina so I think they could do a MUCH better job of marketing it.  The servers should suggest types of tequila to try or at least some kind of mention of it.  Our server, Angela, was attentive and informative.  Very helpful when it came to the menu.  The salmon is great.

Convenient location, no lines, good service.  We got steaks, a bottle of Malbec and the firecracker shrimp app that was a free yelp offer.  All the food was prepared well and tasted fresh.  The carpet did look a little dingy , but we were seated in a lovely high backed round booth , which made up for any leanings toward "casual" vs fine dining. An all around good meal!

It is hard to believe that I ate at the same place that got all of these rave reviews.  I ordered the chicken tikka, which consisted of some microwaved morsels of chicken and rice, accompanied by a large quantity of yogurt.  The yogurt was cold and partially frozen.  I love frozen yogurt, the type that is supposed to be a substitute for ice cream, but this is not what we were dealing with here.  The dining area was clean but sterile, without decor or other touches that could have made it a comfortable place to hang out.  

But the big problem was that the food was simply disgusting.  I don't like paying at a dining establishment for chicken that has been reheated in the microwave.  And when you reheat chicken that has already been cut into small pieces, it quickly gets rubbery. Add the icy yogurt, and you get one big EWWWWWWW.  The best part of the meal was that the worker behind the counter gladly provided me with a large tap water on ice, at no charge.  I have noticed a trend, at other low end places, of refusing to provide tap water, charging for it, or giving it in an exceptionally small cup.  But when ice water is the best part of your meal, you know a place has problems.

i first ventured to The Rev during opening week and have almost been a weekly customer since.  The quality has never faltered and the beer selection remains top notch.  You have to check out the Tiki Bar out back (open most nights when it's nice outside).

I highly recommend the chicken tacos along with chips & guac.  The tacos rank right up there with any of the authentic Mexican joints around.

The atmosphere inside could almost fit into a from dusk till dawn type movie.  I really dig the art and masks.

I have nothing but good things to say about The Rev.  Top notch service, excellent beer selection (many local brews), and great grub.  I will continue to return here on a regular basis.

Spare rib is really good! But I think it's a bit of small amount for a price we paid. I went there with family and we are big fan of Pad Thai so we ordered it too. That was a bummer. It was red and taste different than the all other Pad Thai I've eaten in my life. I would go back there just to eat the spare rib dish and some tea.

I had a great experience with I Like to Move It. I hired them to move myself and my SO out of a house and an apartment and into one apartment. All three locations were within a few city blocks of  each other. 

The movers did show up later than our agreed start time but they more than made up for it with their efficiency and even finished the move before I expected them to based on the original start time. The movers were very professional and were actually fun to work with. I would hire them again for another move.

I finally visited Livery and it didn't disappoint! The food was full of robust flavors and Audrey (?), our waitress, was an exceptional guide at navigating the menu and offering her suggestions. Monday's are "Leg Day" where there is a special chicken leg menu option including 1 of 4 sides for only $9, it's a great value. The empanadas were also very good.

We ordered from the grumpy guy at the counter, who was repeatedly impatient with my indecisive toddlers. Once they did make up their minds and I told him their order, he said there was no way they could handle that order. If I'm paying, and that's what they want, then MAKE it! When I slightly modified their orders, he still didn't want to make them. We ended up walking away with no ice cream. We will not be going back. I'm guessing this grouch could end up costing them the business...
Love it here.  The food is consistantly good!  We really enjoy Monday Opera night!

Was there to use a coupon, and wanted to try some of the unusual things on the menu. When I got there it was a tacky hole-in-the-wall with one rickety table and chair. They didn't have several oI f the items I wanted to try, and it took forever to make what I finally did order. The cheesesteak I got was the worst I've had in a long time. Don't bother, and definitely don't be swayed by the printed menu.

Love the concept and luckily when we walked into this small, quaint little place on the pier, there was seating available at the bar.
We had great service and our waiter was busser and the bartender. The food was just OK. It meant a lot to me that it was fresh and cooked to order.
The clam chowder did not have a lot of flavor whatsoever. I had to add the crackers,salt, tobasco and luckily I carry my own little stash of cayenne pepper. I have had clam chowder all over the world and sadly, I cannot recommend this once. It needed some creaminess butt hat could be personal opinion. Get a cup if you are unsure like we did, a bowl of it is a big commitment. There were a lot of people working and things came out very quickly. 
Hubby had a local beer which he enjoyed and I had a glass of wine. A glass of wine here means a GLASS, loved it. No frills here, wine right to the top of a glass you would get at your granny's house.
We split the fried platter with calamari, shrimp and scallops for $13. Not a ton of food  (3 pieces of each maybe) but the coleslaw complete with raisins and pineapple was a treat and they also throw on about 3 large onion rings. This was a nice dish to split so we did not ingest TOO much fried food. There is also the option to have fried oysters on it which we skipped. I imagine the more you order on the plate, the less you get of each.
I would for sure come back here. Unpretentious and even a little gritty. Come as you are.
If you want fine dining, there are other options on the pier.
They will validate your parking if you park on the wharf.

Maybe great for breakfast, but lunch was a disappointment for me. Service was very nice. Friendly professionals working well together. My chicken gyro was almost completely unseasoned breast with cartilage included. Tzatzki was also bland. Other's in the party had soups, both of them enjoyed it. Price was okay. I'm sure there are better items on the menu.

The gentleman that picked us up was rude as all hell. I asked him how his day was to be polite and make casual conversation - he proceeded to bitch and complain about uber and background checks and drug checks and when he asked me what I thought of uber, I provided a very diplomatic response to which he tore me to shreds and told me i "think wrong" and that's the problem with today's youth. 

Dudes name is Salko Hasanovic and he shouldn't be in any sort of customer service role or customer facing industry.

Wow.what can I say ??went to the lunch"buffet"(and that I use that term loosely) the abundant pizza station had a whopping 2 yes 2 pizza choices????the salad bar had veggies that were screaming to be returned to the earth or the compost pile and the staff???was there one besides the guy who took the cash to "enjoy" this lunch?? It was not the godfathers of yesteryear .Remember when there was more than one and it was GOOD??? Not so much now. The interior was dark gloomy and not so clean the one employee looked like he was counting the hours till his shift was over.long story short this isn't the place for pizza anymore..

These guys helped me figure out a solution for fixing a spot in my yard where my dog digs under the fence, right around the time the shop was closing.  I went in thinking I was going to need one thing and they helped me figure out what I really needed, which was actually cheaper.  They also measure my car and loaded it up for me!
OMG people with their pathetically loud screaming kids make it impossible to enjoy this place!!!  BE CONSIDERATE OF OTHERS YOU SELF ABSORBED IDIOTS!!!!!

I have ordered from this place twice because it's one of the only appealing restaurants on ubereats to me. First time I ordered a cheesesteak and fries. The fries were not good at all to me and seemed a little rubbery like. The. Cheesesteak was pretty good and the bread was really fresh. Remembering the quality of the cheesesteak, I decided to order another one the second time around. This time it wasn't fresh and my bread was a lil hard, especially the ends. However, the mozzarella sticks were delicious. They were quite huge as well, I guess that's why you only get 4. The marinara sauce was chunky and complimented the sticks perfectly. While, I might not order a steak again, I found my go to mozarella sticks spot!

The food was absolutely amazing, which is enough reason to go back again and again.  

The Hummous was great, but the one starter we had was awesome; Fatar Meshwi (grilled wild mushrooms). I'm pretty sure I could eat that every day.  We also got two outstanding mains, the Kawarma (Lamb) and the Prawns.  My wife and basically fought to the death over each bite.  I can't say enough about the food, delicious.

Unfortunately there were a few negatives.  Not that it's a bad thing for everybody, but felt a bit too hip or New York for us.  But that's just a personal preference.  We're more salt of the earth Philly.  There was also the bar area, which we were told does not allow standing room.
