They basically move you to an area to enjoy cocktails and the bar is only populate by those sitting there.  I like the idea of it, but the practice didn't hold.  My wife and I were sat at a two top along the path to the bar, and a large group was allowed to stand there and get after it during our entire meal.  We had someone's butt in our face throughout the meal.  I'm not sure why, but the rule seems to apply to some but not others, pretty frustrating.

All in all, the food heavily outweighs any of the negatives and I strongly recommend you give it a chance.

Tried to go to the biscuit love gulch location and the wait was over an hour. Our uber driver recommended this location and no wait at all. We walked right in and sat at the bar. The bonuts are amazing! Tried the nasty princess (not on the menu but the server highly recommended) and it did not disappoint. A must for breakfast!
Absolutely phenomenal food, drinks, service and staff. My party of 3 and I had a wonderful evening and Constantine our server was so passionate towards our experience. Highly recommend!
Not bad.  Have had better experiences at other MM.  Still nice to be able to get a gourmet pizza and craft beer

After we couldn't get in the first night, we came even earlier to wait in line and get in.  It was $12 at the door, and we ended up standing in the back.  The music was good, and I enjoyed the band, but the place is small, not well ventilated, you can't have drinks, and there is no bathroom.  The show went on for maybe 45 minutes, and it was good while it lasted, since the musicians were pretty good showmen.  

Maybe I don't appreciate jazz as much as most people, or something, but I'm not sure I understand why this place is so legendary.  Still, a good time, and something to do if you can get in.

A rare find of Taiwanese restaurant out in Reno. I highly recommend this place if you enjoy Taiwanese cuisine. You will be surprised at how authentic the dishes are here. Business gets very good on weekends especially during ski season. I would raise to 5 stars only if they can improve the decor a little more and the overall cleanliness. Otherwise, this is a must stop in Reno if you are a Taiwanese or one who enjoys Taiwanese food.
The food was fresh but I don't like the idea of creating your own dish, there are too many sauces to figure out if you're making your dish too salty or sweet.
Not for anyone under the age of 50. Smells like old lady perfume. Everything is well worn and rather cheap. Nothing high end. I would imagine you could find the same items at Goodwill.

Was introduced to this nice restaurant by the concierge at the Sheraton Hotel where it came highly recommended.

The best quality by far here, was the fantastic food. Everything was absolutely delicious. The corn bread was to die for, and my roast beef Poboy was oversized and left me incredibly full. To top it all off I had a perfectly made Hurricane, that left me perfectally buzzed at the end of my meal. 

Service was decent and our waiter was very friendly. This restaurant has a quieter atmosphere for lunch.

Will come back next time I am in New Orleans.

I love this place. Always great food and quick service. It can be a little pricey, but well worth it. They use high quality ingredients. Would recommend to anyone. They also have a great selection of beer.
Tasty food, a bit local a bit gastro. Great drinks and wonderful service from a lovely lady

Dave is a great barber.  He's always good conversation, especially if you like Harleys and guitars.  Great haircut for a good price.  He and his staff are also good with my two boys.  The sitting area is nicely appointed and there are things for the kids to do.

I have been wanting to go to Honey's for a while but I never had a chance to until a few weeks ago. The wait is pretty long due to its small size, we waited about 25 minutes. The food was well worth the wait everything was fresh; and both my friend and I were delighted to find they had vegan options as well. 

We will be back soon it is a great spot for brunch and authentic home made food. The prices are very good as well.

Red Mesa is our go-to special occasion restaurant with the best creative Mexican food menu we have ever experienced. More often than not we skip other Mexican restaurants when trying to decide what to eat for lunch or dinner. If you like beef, try the chimayo skirt steak. Awesome! Mouth watering! The guys in the kitchen rock! For lunch try the carne asada tacos. 
Service? We have experienced great service each time we've dined there. If you are a needy "look at me, I'm the only person in the world who matters" type of person, then you won't like the service, or the service at any other restaurant. Please stay home. We have had the misfortune of being seated next to people who have this attitude which tends to make everyone elses dining experience less enjoyable.
Don't be afraid to try something new. My wife tasted the duck enchiladas and loved the flavor. Try the frijoles charros! It's a flavor you'll never forget.
The restaurant interior is pleasant and cozy.

Good ole black owned southern hospitality and the food to go along with it. Had the fish and grits and a wonderful time with the family after church. Everyone was accommodating and made sure our meal was excellent! The hour wait was well worth it
Great little local place.  Friendly atmosphere,  fun bartender, I forget his name.  Great beer selection and really good food.

I was impressed with the service at this location. The woman who cut my hair was very nice and skilled at her job. My haircut turned out great. This location also offers coupons a lot of the time, so you don't always have to pay full price.
We love this place.  Great chicken, ribs, brisket, pulled pork and sausage.  We can't wait to do this again.

The best thing about this is the jazz band. They are AMAZING and super entertaining. The boat is nice and the views of the city are exceptional. Its a relaxing ride. We didn't have the dinner so no idea how good that is.

Last night, my wife and I had a great meal at 39 West American Bistro in West Chester. It is a BYOB with a nice variety of offerings.

My wife had the Mushroom Soup and the Goat Cheese Stuffed Chicken Breast. I had the Tuna Tataki and the Bucatini & Clams. We loved each of the courses.

The owner is Anthony and his staff made it a very enjoyable experience. We will definitely be going back.

This place was better than I expected. Total dive but that's fine with me. Could tell it's a locals kind of bar by the awkward looks we got when we walked in. The décor was like a pizza place from the 80's. Thought the place was going to be a complete dump, but I've been in a lot worse than that. Decent drink specials.
Best BBQ in St Charles.  Don't believe the hype for Sugarfire,  this is better BBQ at a better price.

Paula and her daughter did a Fabulous job on my nails. I had a fill and a pedicure. The massage chairs also worked wonderfully. The place was clean and everyone very friendly.  I have just moved back to NO and it is my new nail salon.  
Martha

I am getting ready for our trip to New Orleans this Halloween and was just fantasizing about our last trip there and how we ate at Muriels and it was wonderful.

For a place in the quarter that is right in the center of tourist land, this restaurant is classy but not overly stuffy. The atmosphere is beautiful. The walls, a deep velvety maroon with a collection of antiques and gorgeous New Orleans decor. You can see the attention to detail. There are no spots on the water glasses or silver. The table cloths are immaculate.

There is nothing too complicated on the menu, just delicious Cajun & Creole food. There is a table d'hote option which I like because you get a full course meal for one price. The wine selection is broad and desserts are heavenly. The bread they bring to your table is unbelievably soft and warm and served with an herb butter. 

A reservation is recommended but there are times when you can walk in for lunch or dinner also. It is an expansive restaurant in a gorgeous french quarter building. Appropriate attire should be worn (no shorts and flip flops) but it does not require a sport coat. I like to wear a dress to dinner anyways, there is something about fancy New Orleans dining that calls for being dressed pretty. If you are wearing a ball cap they will ask you to remove it and I appreciate that. I like that they maintain their standards and hold strong to those policies. If you want to eat in your outside clothes, go to an oyster house. Please, have respect for yourself and the other diners. : )

We have had beautiful, consistent food, every time, with some of the best service we've ever had anywhere. The servers are never hurried or rushed or nervous, but work at a relaxed pace. The servers, runners and bussers work as a tight ship and you can see the quality in their work. Everything comes out at the right time. Dishes are cleared at the right time. Water is filled at the right time. It is 100% perfect service.

A warning..... this place is haunted by a man who lost his home in a gamble. The restaurant is the ghosts former home. I was in the ladies room alone and something had turned the lights off on me while I was in the loo. There was no one else in the room with me. Scary but interesting to say the least.

I really enjoyed this place and my boyfriend did too. I would recommend it time and again for anyone in the quarter who wants fine dining, but not too-fine of dining.

We made a reservation for 7:30. We arrived and were quickly seated. We were given menus and I selected a filet mignon while my husband selected a porterhouse steak. We also ordered sautéed mushrooms. We asked for the fried ravioli appetizer and it arrived in good time.  I took one bite and did not like it. I was expecting cheese filling and it was a meat filling. In fact it tasted like a meatball. My husband said they were very good. However I did not like the taste and did not eat any more of them.
My husband ordered ceasar salad and shared it with me.  It was delicious. We both felt it was the best ceasar salad we had ever had.
Next came our meals.  I had asked for rare with the butter sauce on the side. Instead it was poured over it.  It was very heavy on the garlic side.  Our waitress asked how I liked it and I told her.  She took it back to the kitchen. The owner or maybe his wife came by and apologized and asked if there was something else she could get me while I waited.  I said no because I had a beautiful baked potato in front of me.  I had maybe taken 2 bites of potato and my new steak arrived.  It was perfect.  My husband said his steak was very good. He also had the baked potato. We both ordered the potato with butter and sour cream as well as the bacon with cheese toppings.  All of this was very good.  The service was wonderful.  We ordered desert to go - tiramiso and whiskey cake. They look yummy. I could only find one very tiny flaw and that is some of the foods were a little too salty. One interesting item is the light in the middle of the room.  It is a Dale Chuhuly  piece according to management. Very beautiful.  There is also an extensive wine cellar, which we did not take advantage of. It was a nice touch to this restaurant. Overall, a very nice dinner.

I was presently surprised by both the food and the service here. I ordered the gorgonzola gnocchi and my date had the pollo osteria. Both dishes were delicious and the portions are huge! Our waiter was very friendly and attentive. The atmosphere is very nice as well... good date spot. I will definitely return!

This place is great. The food, the prices and the environment. The staff was very kind and helpful and the decor was beautiful. Usually 30 mins after eating chinese i feel sick but the food here never did. They have lunch specials and thai food as well. I will go back soon.

If you're not a food snob, but like good Mexican food, you'll still be sorry you came. 

The salsa is clearly canned stewed tomatoes with jarred diced jalapeños... Nothing authentic. That's your initial experience before the food arrives. 

It doesn't get better. I got shrimp tacos. It came as 4 tacos, two tortillas each. 8 tortillas for about 8 shrimp!? $15. Rice and beans were truly sub par.

I did not risk eating the guacamole because it was half bright green and half brownish black mixed together. The lettuce had old brown edges. The diced fresh tomatoes were barely ripe, and crunchy.

My favorite part was the Diet Coke. Seriously. Oh, and leaving.

Love Jcrew. This location is a great size and has lots of size options. Only downside is that some staff is VERY snobby. If I'm not dressed that nice I get ignored. Also at times when I go right to the sale section they also ignore me. I do have great things to say about their wedding department. I got my wedding dress here and have purchased several bridesmaid dresses. All positive experiences and I love the dresses.
Went to the ER today and the staff was attentive and lovely. I have never been to a hospital for myself, let alone the ER, and it was as lovely an experience as it could be.

We went to LaScala's for the first time last night for dinner.  They have a very nice ambiance and the hostess was pleasant - she seated us 20 minutes early for our reservation with no problem.  Unfortunately, we were seated right underneath a speaker where the stereotypical Italian restaurant music was blasting.  We asked the hostess twice and the waitress once to have it turned down, and were ready to walk out the door when it was finally done.  

The food was good, not great.  I had the chopped La Scala salad which was very nice, and the gnocchi with mozzarella, basil and tomato sauce.  The entree was very salty, but would have been 5 stars if it hadn't been for that.  They got the escarole soup and beet and goat cheese salad for appetizers, and lamb chops and pasta with pesto for the entrees.  The lamb was delicious, but the pesto was awful - it didn't taste like pesto, but instead a cream sauce that had some basil flakes added to it.  Our wine, for $50, was pretty bad as well. 

Overall, the place has potential, but unfortunately for the price the food fell a little short in our book.

Awesome Catering! 

My husband and I recently were married in the St. Pete Beach area. We were looking for a street style taco spot to cater our rehearsal dinner (approx. 85 people) and stumbled upon casita taqueria. Don was super friendly and extremely accommodating when we contacted them. They delivered the food to our location and everything was perfect. The food was fresh and everything was warm and ready to eat. So many of our guests commented on how much they loved the food. I would absolutely recommend them for any group events. They are great!!!

Never again. My co worker and I went to lunch there last week. First off, our silverware was dirty, we immediately told the server to bring us another set (that should have been a red flag). I ordered a turkey breast wrap and my friend ordered the seafood mix. We waited exactly 45 minutes for our food. My wrap was disgusting, it was soggy and the turkey smelled as if it were many days old. The seafood mix is a joke, we counted 5 pieces that consisted of small shrimp and scallops, it costs $19.99!! for only 5 pieces of mediocre "seafood". Too expensive. The server never bothered to check on us. Because we were in my lunch hour, I had to chase her down for my bill (I shouldn't have paid for this disgusting meal). When I went up to pay the $41.00 for this lunch,  the cashier asked how everything had been. I told her horrible. For the inconvenience, she gave us a $2 discount. Like I said, I should have walked out. I learned my lesson, Never again. I went back to work and told all my coworkers to stay away from this place. Also, this place  is dirty! if the eating area is dirty, can you imagine what the kitchen looks like?

Decided to make an appointment with Mrs Ken based on the awesome Yelp reviews. Was not disappointed. I'll keep this short and sweet since everything else here is spot on. Went for my first Brazilian and was super impressed with how little it actually hurt. Plus she's the cutest! I really thought it would be awkward dropping my trousers and splaying my legs on a table for a stranger, but I felt very comfortable the entire time. Now my go-to for keeping the hair down there bare.

There were four of us and we each got a separate dish. They were all delicious.  We were so very, very fortunate to have Claire as our waitress. She was the absolute best waitress that we had at a restaurant in NO the entire week. If you can get her just ask what she would suggest.  The lobster entrée was perhaps the best. The coconut desert was "to die for".

I wish this restaurant would move to Atlanta GA!
Best ice cream I've ever had! Highly recommend. Fresh ingredients, amazing staff, fun and friendly atmosphere.

Great spot for appetizers and beer, over 30 beers on tap. The newest menu items, Rueben and Patty Melt, were awesome. The dry rub ribs were tasty and spices were delicious without burn. Wednesday is live music night so check it out.

My boyfriend ordered wings to go for us for the first time and they were delicious he also ordered us chicken tenders and fries. The mild Wings were finger lickin good, great sauce and the chicken tenders were delicious, fried and battered to perfection. Giving wings over Broadway 4 stars for their fries, they were big and hot but lacking some seasoning, they were a little bland and I was hoping they would be a little more tasty!
We sat outside, they are pet friendly. It was the best breakfast we had and I'm very much a breakfast person. The device was great and the food original.

I like the location of the hotel, it's by a lot of food places, The Grand Ole Opry and shopping. The hotel has its own restaurant with live bands. The rooms are a little outdated and smell moldy. I think it was the air conditioning that smelt like mildew. Oh and good luck with getting sleep at night! It's so loud and it doesn't help with the atrium right in the middle of the hotel. They have posted 'quiet hours' but be prepared to put eat plugs in!

I recently switched my oldest here along with my newest addition. They have two very convenient locations, one Uptown and in Metairie. All of the doctors are friendly. Staff is also very helpful. Both my kids sees Dr Michael Heller and I always ask myself how did I not switch over sooner. It's hard to find doctors or anyone who you would feel comfortable with your kids. Napoleon Pediatrics are also partnered with Children's Hospital, which makes it even more available.  If you are looking for a pediatrician, give this place a try.

I really wanted to give this spot a good review but this place is a business before a classic men's barber shop. I don't mind paying a high premium for a premium haircut but I just didn't feel like thats what I got here. To me it seems like you come here for the aesthetics more than anything. Like I said Its business first.
This place has everything you think you may want.. lights, cameras, drones, etc... I get all my accessories from here for my Sony Rx10

I came here after a 3 day backpacking trip and received one of the best, most thoughtful massages of my life from Summer. I wish I lived in the Boise area so I could go back for another! I had asked for hot stone and aromatherapy and Summer suggested adding cupping-and it was SO worth it. The perfect trifecta. I would recommend Summer to anyone!

The best boxing gym in the city! I started boxing a year ago wanting to both get in better shape and learn the skills associated with boxing. I've tried a few places but ultimately settled at NOBC. The positive atmosphere is the first thing you notice about this gym, regardless of if you are a professional or a first time boxer everyone trains together and shares the same passion for boxing, wanting to better themselves through the sport. The gym has everything you need from a weight room, a full boxing ring/equipment, and a cardio/ab area. In a few short weeks training with the owner Chase I have become a better boxer. The gym is clean, friendly, and fun. I plan on training here for years to come.

I went here one night and was quite parched. Sat down at a high top table and got a cup of ice water. Very refreshing and exactly what I needed. Highly recommend. Haven't tried the food yet! I look forward to my next encounter with parilla!

Ever since the owner passed away the new management has been nothing but problems. Every deadline missed. The prices went up and wouldn't honor previous agreement. And now that we want to go else where we have to fight them for our art work.

Awesome classic barber shop, great haircut, and was able to give me a cut that rivals my hometown barber. Greatly skilled with the straight razor, professional, and just at the right price. Thanks George, I'll be back!

Daddy's choice for Father's Day! None of us had ever had this before. Lots of stewed meats. We had lamb, beef, and chicken (no pork as Ethiopia is Muslim). We are with our fingers and bread.

The food was quite flavorful but not spicy hot. We each enjoyed it. I would welcome dining on this again.

FWIW, this was a challenge I dug very deep for. I am well fed. There isn't much food I haven't tried. I traveled 1200 miles to find a cuisine I hadn't eaten before.

The French market in itself is a must for any NOLA visit, however, any visit without an order of mother nature's crawfish Mac and cheese would be incomplete. Some of the most comforting, gooey, delicious Mac and cheese I have had. Well worth the long line.

Shrimp and grits. Best food I have ever had in my life.   Lydia is wonderful.  Wow. My wife had the Migras breakfast and loved it. My son had the biscuits and gravy and my daughter hand the scramble eggs with lox. All great.  To get here from French Quarter, we took the St Charles tram to Garden District then short work.

Fantastic Italian BYO in Rittenhouse area.  Daniel, the Maitre d' and part owner, is extremely engaging and conversational and even had a special veal dish that was not on the menu made that was phenomenal.  A bit cozy and popular but I can see why after having the food.  Don't forget the creme pastry dessert...incredible.  Will be back for sure, and often!

this place reminds of camping. it is not a resort. we had a block of rooms reserved for 6 months and when we checked in two people were given rooms with no beds ! how could a marriot resort even think that is acceptable. management did not correct the issue after several requests. i checked out. there are several nice hotels near resort with shuttle service. a confirmed reservation means nothing - even if a marriot elite membet. i would have rated zero if possible.

Ordered the yard bird and my dining partner had the new York strip. The chicken was supposed to have jerk spices to it. It was flavorless and not very good. The jicama slaw was not like slaw at all. The roasted potatoes were okay. The new York strip was okay except it was obviously a cheaper quality meat. 
The server was good. 
No sense mentioning the displeasure, the food was across the board not very good. It seemed to be the theme. Not worth the $60 bill that's for sure. Will not be back.

Wow this place is bad. My first impression is that this would be a pleasant spot in an otherwise, what is in my opinion the most unpleasant street in the French Quarter.  They had live music that sounded more like entertainment at a nursing home, a really untalented guy (how they found him in the city of greats I have no idea), basically constantly asking for tips and in between hitting some notes on his keyboard. 
The food was the worst part, 35 minute wait time ended in terrible beignets that taste mostly like oil and an omelette that went straight to the dumpster where it belongs.  Poor quality and the worst part is that they don't even try.  In this city a place like this should not pass.
Worst nail place EVER. I ended up paying $65 for nails i didn't even like. Horrible experience first and last time ill be going there!!!
South RAC is an awesome gym. Lots of workout space and variety. The employees are great. I love their Body Pump and Grit group workout classes!

Made an account just to write this review:

Breakfast Culture Club serves my favorite espresso in Santa Barbara. In fact, it's some of the best espresso I've ever had (better than even the best I've found in LA/SF). It has a fruited sweetness to it, a hint of red fruit, perfect mouthfeel, and insane sweetness. Their beans are from Coava, which I'd never had until coming here, and the espresso blend is just brilliant. I think they used to use coffee from Handlebar, which also makes good espresso, but I'm very glad they switched because Coava makes a much more interesting espresso (Handlebar is good, but very typical--roasty toasty notes, caramelly, but definitely not fruity).

I like to get a Gibraltar, a Cappuccino, or just straight espresso. The Gibraltar and Cappuccino both bring out the strawberry notes of the espresso, and end up very sweet because the espresso is just great here. The texture they achieve on their milk is fantastic as well--exactly what I want in a Cappuccino. That said, if I want something with more punch I just go straight for the espresso.

Their toasts are also very good. I think they've changed how they do toasts since previous reviewers posted--they prepare the toast for you, so it actually is instagram ready if you're into that :)

As for ambiance, this place is perfect. The opened garage door makes the whole place feel very open and spacious. Strong hipster and surfer vibes around, you'll often see people barefoot. Also usually a couple people working on their laptops. There's about 4 or 5 power outlets available. Usually I've been able to get a spot with an outlet if I need it, but in the morning it can be so busy that it's hard to find a free table with an outlet.

Highly recommend stopping in here if you like fruitier espresso drinks.
The food is great and so is the all you can eat deal. Service is hit or miss, but not bad enough to stop me from coming.  ;)

Very nice facility everything's top notch. Why they have one real restaurant for breakfast is beyond belief. Only 1! You can drink Starbucks until your head explodes and eat that "food" but otherwise you wait in line forever. This place holds thousands of people and there are around a dozen restaurants open for lunch and dinner but breakfast..forget it!

Loved it they food was great i had this awsome salad called the center city it was so filling for a salad i was surprised plus fresh mozzarella and beefsteak tomatoes how can u go wrong i added the pesto chicken it was perfectly seasoned and moist.  the service was great and i think the price is reasonable definatly and good afterwork hot spot or a place to get a simple quick bit to eat in a nice relaxing atmostphere.

My family and I come to this restaurant quite a few times. Sometimes more than once a month. But this time probably has to be the worst experience we've had. The waitress brought out salads for everyone when we clearly reminded her twice that we wanted two soups. And the soup tasted a little watered down and bland. Our waitress took forever to refill our drinks. When she finally did, she refilled the other two people's drinks and completely skipped past us. The food wasn't uniformly cut so there were big chunks of meat and vegetables. And when it came time to pay, we had a coupon for buy three hibachi dinners get one dinner of equal or lesser value for free. And they wouldn't take the coupon. So they had to end up making us another hibachi dinner on top of all the food we ordered. It was just a big hassle instead of taking the coupon and having the manager explain to us instead of our waitress who clearly had an attitude by the time she brought our check back. Needless to say, we won't be back...

My car was part of the air bag recall.  I also needed some lights replaced.  Honda promised me a comparable rental from Avis while parts were on order, which they said could take one month or more.  It took four hours the first day to do paperwork, wait on Avis who drove me to their office downtown where there was not a comparable vehicle.  Avis then drove me back to Honda where I got my car and drove home.  I noticed the visor light had not been replaced as I had asked.

When I spoke with the Honda service rep, complaining that I was now driving my dangerous car, he blamed me for not accepting the car Avis offered.  The story goes on for four additional visits to Honda, countless hours, $30. payment to my assistant for one of those visits, $35. to Lyft for subsequent rides to and from Avis, never did get a rental.  

In the end, I was the first to get my airbag replaced and got a complimentary taillight.  I will not be returning to this location for service.

It's a beautiful shop that made me feel like I was on the set of Streetcar Named Desire, ie it had NOLA charm. The owner was very gracious and greeted us very warmly.  We just needed a dozen roses, and he took the time to prune them for us and arrange it in a lovely manner.

Just this weekend, I went to Jackson's twice in 12 hours... first for a late night drink with friends and then turned around the next morning for a nice brunch. That should tell you just how versatile this Bar & Bistro is...  

With a great patio in the heart of the hopping Hillsboro Village, it's hard to stay away from Jackson's. There's always an eclectic mix of people day or night. 

Most importantly for me, I am a huge fan of the food and the drink selection! The menu has something for everyone! The brunch options are simple, but delish. Some of my friends commented that the presentation of the food was something to be desired, but I didn't really mind because I felt the taste made up for the lack of presentation. If I may make a recommendation...  the ahi tuna sandwich was delightful! 

The bar menu offered at night is also pretty extensive, from sliders to different dips. Most of those items were great to share and under $10, including the Verde dip (some spinach, garlic, and cream cheese concoction) and the nachos! 

I hear the desserts are worth trying, so I can't wait til Jackson's and I meet again!
Takeout was basically thrown in my box, but  dining in was fine. It's outback, take it for what you will

Goodbye, boring Dairy Queen Blizzard with boring strawberries!  Hello, Yogoluv!

Don't get me wrong.  This Yelper loves Dairy Queen, but when I am trying to watch what I eat, Dairy Queen isn't always in the cards.  If I try to behave and eat a dessert that is low in calories (or in my case, Weight Watcher Points), I am restricted to keeping things simple (i.e. plain vanilla with a little fruit).

That is until I fell in luv with Yogoluv (see how I did that with the spelling of "luv"?  Brilliant)!

Yogoluv is a small 2-store chain.  It has its first location in Columbia, MO, as well as its recent installment in Creve Coeur.  This was my first time to visit a yogurt shop, so I was blown away by the choices available to me.  This particular location boasts about 14 self-serve options from cheesecake to acai berries to red velvet cake.  The yogurt here is not a blend of powder and water, but the real deal with live and active cultures.  If the awesome flavors need a little more flair, there is an outstanding topping bar that includes the sinfully sweet candies and syrups, or if you are trying to stay healthy, fresh fruits and nuts.  In my case, I got a big cup of peanut butter frozen yogurt alongside a portion of cheesecake yogurt, topped with fresh strawberries and kiwis.  AWESOME!

Now this format isn't anything new.  There are numerous frozen yogurt bars around town, but what really topped off my dessert was the friendly customer service, and the attention to cleanliness of this store.  Also, it was nice to have a complete nutritional guide available for those of us who are counting calories (by the way, 1/2 a cup of yogurt will run you about 3 WW points).

So thanks, Yogoluv, for providing me a place to go whacky with my dessert without having to regret my whackiness later on the scale.

I have been able to do two team building experiences here at Chef JJ and I can say both times exceeded my expectations. The Broad Ripple location has space for indoor and outdoor experiences. The patio overlooking the river was beautiful and the indoors was decorative. My team and I were able to make flatbreads, chicken, steak, sides, salads and more! Both times Chef JJ's provided the appetizer and dessert. It was so much fun! I think it would be great for corporate events and/or wedding parties! I never knew cooking and competing with friends on a Big Green Egg could be so much fun!

This is a great & cute little shop/antique store. The woman who recently bought the store is very friendly! I found an amazing set of canisters for my kitchen there, & they were truly vintage! I will continue to visit this store every once in awhile, as she gets new stuff in occasionally. She has a pretty decent selection of vintage clothes, accessories, furniture, home decor, antique kids toys, kitchen wares, and more! A fairly large selection of vintage Pyrex dishes as well, which I know is a fairly popular item! Definitely check this store out! The prices are fair & you will more than likely find at least one thing that you will want to buy!

First off, the restaurant is located in a great part of New Orleans!  The inside of the restaurant had a great atmosphere where two men were playing live music and it felt very "local".  The food consists of small "plates" so for 2 people we ordered 3 plates and that was plenty for us, plus a cocktail.  We ordered the pork belly, macaroni and cheese, and bulgogi rice bowl.  All 3 were delicious!  The pork belly was amazing - fatty but crisp that you could eat it, the mac and cheese was gooey (not my favorite of the three but was definitely very good) and the bulgogi bowl came with kimchi which was a nice touch because you can't usually get good korean food unless you go to an asian restaurant.  Would absolutely go back!

Nice cheap motel across the street from the beach. Nothing fancy or special but serves its purpose nonetheless. One problem with this motel was the employees. At night, they got a little noisy and we had to tell the female employee to keep it down while she was on her cell phone talking loudly right outside our room. Other than that, great location and great for the money's worth.
$40 for a mani/pedi! Facility was nice, staff was friendly and my nails look great. Will definitely be going back

Just an awesome place to have a beer and catch up with friends. The beer selection is great and hands down they have the best french dip roast beef sandwich!  It's the small town charm of the place that makes it cool.

I want to first state, that I was extremely happy to have this supermarket in town. However, lately the overall state of this store has recently let me down. The concept of having a kiosk for ordering deli items is perfect but the system does not work. The first thing I do is place my order and do my shopping, mind you with a 2 year old, then go pick it up and check out. The past few times I have done this and my order has not been ready. I get they are busy, obviously that is why I use the kiosk.  Then when I ask about my order they act like how dare I bother them. Recently I got a response that they where understaffed and busy, but really 30 minutes!! They would never make a person standing there wait that long! I take my time shopping due mostly to the fact I have a freakin toddler. Anyway, they just do not have a sense of urgency or even employees that care to be efficient. I truly hope that this store does not continue to let me down because overall there products and prices are good.

I've heard about Americano for some time, but we finally enjoyed dinner there last night. I knew the food would be good, but I was BLOWN AWAY. I recommend the Seafood Paella, Brussels Sprouts, and Veal Meatballs. The Spicy Tuna Guac is a great starter. 

Drinks are fun and inventive. Atmosphere is energetic yet casually warm and welcoming. Service, led by Araz, is and attentive and in-tune. 

Very well priced for the quality of our experience. I unreservedly recommend you try Americano.

There are a lot of places to grab coffee in Broad Ripple and many of them are warm inviting spaces that make you want to stay. This place really isn't that. It is cramped and has a lot going on. I had a smoothie my first time and a tea my second. Both were just okay. What really gets me are all of the signs that say "outlets are for paying customers only." There's just something about which I find off putting about that. Not really a place I want to meet someone.

This is one of many Sonoran dog stands that I'm sure are not listed in Yelp yet. This is on the corner of 1st Ave. and Prince in front of the carniceria. I've been passing by it now for several years and decided to try it today. Glad I did.

He does his Chipilon style, which means he toasts the bun. That's the way I like it. And of course, he uses Alejandro's buns. This is a very good Sonoran Dog. Well constructed, tasty, nothing overly done.

He also makes his own horchata and limonade. We had the horchata, Excellent. $1.50 for a medium and $3.00 for a "grande," which is gigantic.

Today was windy and he had the canopy set up over the tables. Made for more pleasant eating.

On Wednesdays he has a special of two dogs and a drink for $5.00. Good deal.

I highly recommend this food truck.

All I have to say is this place is a hidden gem!!! My first time here in Santa Barbara and was looking for a decent place to eat where it's not too expensive. Found!!! When I come back again to visit, I will definately come back!

I thought it was marginal given all the hype. I was under the impression that the burritos were relatively large - I guess mostly just full of rice. Also choosing steak was a mistake - it was all kinds of chewy and gristly. I'd go again if someone else wanted to and I'd probably get something else.

We had heard great things about Chill so we gave it a try early on a Saturday evening. It wasn't crowded when we arrived a little after 5. We almost left before we ate but were glad we didn't. We were seated by an older red headed hostess, the first seat she offered us we declined and she seemed very offended when we asked if could have a different one. As I said it wasn't busy so there were lots of seats available. She then proceeded to tell the other women that work there that we didn't like the seat she offered. We were 6 feet away from her; I really don't think that is very professional, I'm not sure why she was offended, we almost left at that point. Lucky the rest of the meal went much better. Our server Matt was great, very knowledge about the food and the wine. We had 3 small plates that were great, the layers of flavor in their foods is great, hats off to the chef. The only reason I didn't rate it 5 stars was the hostess's lack of professionalism. Other than that it was great.

BAILEYS DITCHED THE DUCK BURGER!!!! 

I am devastated :( It was one of the best burgers I've ever had. Sigh. 

Had a pumpkin bean veggie burger on their special list once with an apple relish type thing and it was kind of a flop- not well balanced and had too many competing flavors to taste any individual one. Not to mention I left the restaurant forgetting my leftovers, barely took 3 steps outside, and when I returned for my box it was already taken and lost :(

But their shakes are wonderful (recommend the salted caramel) and they have a solid local beer selection. 

why, baileys, why do you torment me so??

signed, 
             your duck burger lover
Great clean place, staff was very polite. Dr Cooley is a extremely knowledgeable doctor. They are available 7 days a week, I highly recommend them, and am going there for ALL my medical needs.

Love this place, great European street food, clean, fast and friendly staff.
Great selection of beers, authentic.
I have loved going to this church.  Pastor Danny gives a great sermon!  It is always inspiring and touches the heart.  I would highly recommend this church.

Ate during the lunch buffet. Not terribly impressed, the food was slightly below average and the goat curry was stringy and I found three bone shards. If you are hungry and want a lunch where you don't have to wait for service then you'll be fine. otherwise I would pass.

While visiting the area, we decided to stop in at the Cool Springs Brewery. Husband and I had the fish and chips and we loved it! Great place. Beer selection had a good variety. Will visit again when we are back in town.

I come the the Fairview Heights location all the time and order the same two rolls. The Washington avenue has been a favorite of mine for a long time and I have recently start getting the Wasabi special roll and  it is now my favorite roll.  This location offers great service  and a great mall employee discount! I definitely recommend Wasabi to all the sushi lovers out there!

Trattoria Marcella was a last minute decision to find a late evening Italian dinner without a wait in line. So I called 3 hours prior to make a reservation without any problems. When my wife and I arrived, we were seated within a few minutes. The waiter clearly went over the specials and provided some excellent suggestions for our meal. I ordered their Manhattan straight up which was surprisingly good; since I am more of a whiskey neat person.

For an appetizer, we ordered the mussels. The cream pesto was extraordinary with the garlic croutons. My wife had an arugula salad which she thoroughly enjoyed.

For the main entree, I had their (special) braised pork on risotto. My wife had the lasagna. We were both happy with our choices and enjoyed them very much.

Overall, everything was perfect from the service to the meal. When the check came, I thought it was going to be near $100 but it was actually around $65. I don't want to compare this restaurant to others on the Hill because I really think they are all unique in their own ways. This place was an experience you will just need to try for yourself.
Anthony's in Pike Creek is my go to any day of the week. You can't beat the food and the atmosphere. Wish them the best with the recent expansion.

Good atmosephere, solid food, great beer selection. I've been here several times and have always enjoyed the food and drink. This isn't your Friday or Saturday night place to be, unless you enjoy very small crowds. To me, it's more of a good place to come for a happy hour or if you're just looking to have a few drinks. Overall thought it's a great bar.

Great gym, a little on the small side but they have really nice people that work there and try to develop a community culture.  The smoothie bar is a lot of fun and they have a good variety of classes.  Of course, because it's a good gym, it's always packed.  

Could clean the machines a little more frequently, I would work out in the AM and there would be hairs all over the floor.  The maintenance could use some improvement, a lot of treadmills don't have functioning televisions.

So, we came here to watch Game 7 of the World Series.  And arrived sometime during the 3rd inning.  Our party of 4 wandered the streets trying to find a bar that wasn't wall to wall (what were we thinking?!) and settled on the bar room of this place.  However, I would hardly call it settling, because it was awesome!

We stood about the first half of our stay.  Even though the place was packed, the bartenders were very attentive and were constantly scanning the bar to make sure that people weren't waiting too long to place their drink orders.  The beer was flowing for us.  The hefeweizen is yummy.  I'm cautious of dark beers so my ole standby is wheat, and this did not disappoint.  However, after a couple of those I got ballsy and had the pumpkin ale.  THIS IS AWESOME BEER.  It tastes like cinnamon and clove, and I'm pretty sure even the pickiest of beer drinkers would at least enjoy a glass of this.  

Sometime during the 6th inning, a table actually got up and left.  I was shocked, considering the circumstances of why we were there.  We snatched the table up, as we needed some food to wash down all the beers we drank.  We got the pretzel stick/cheese dip appetizer, and the macaroni and cheese, all to share.  Delicious!  I would eat both again.

I really liked the environment of the place.  There were enough tvs for a night like this.  There was an outdoor patio with plenty of chairs and ashtrays for the smokers.  Plus, most of the people (both employees and patrons) were friendly and in high spirits, so it made the night very enjoyable.

I'm definitely curious to try this place again to try some of the other items on the menu and actually sit in the dining room to see how that aspect of service is.  I would also like to tour this place.  Overall, the experience I had here as a first-timer definitely would bring me back!

Decided to give Khyber Pass a try for dinner on a Sunday night. The service, beer selection, and food were all top notch. The vibe inside was laid back with an eclectic decor. I had the brisket. It was so tender I didn't need a knife. The portions were huge and left me stuffed. I will definitely be stopping back to try some other menu items that piqued my interest and recommend giving it a try!

Tony likes was good I order a chicken philly mushroom peppers American it was delicious they messed the first one up and fix me another and gave both too me I also ordered wings with no sauce and a philly steak mushrooms onions and sweet peppers I enjoyed the all mmmm my husband and I are from Memphis Tennessee and was just passing by nice dine and dash to
Very pleasant environment. Inside decoration is adorable. They treat people extremely nice and staff are very helpful.

We live down the street from here. It's so nice to have an old fashioned ice cream shop near by. We have a 2.5 yr old and I'm pregnant with our second and we frequent this place! They are CASH ONLY. We love the soft serve, sundaes and milkshakes!! They also have hot dogs and chips. Seating at old colorful picnic tables outside brings a nostalgic feel. Love to support this local business!!!

Not terrible, just not good.  Steak was pretty skinny cut, ordered medium, came super well-done (roadkill), and was over-seasoned, albeit acceptable.  Potato (baked) was standard fare and pretty hard to screw up.  Salad was not fresh, and mostly-all iceberg, with a sad little bit of tomato.  Glad I tried it (seen this place for years and curious about it).  Will not order from again.

Really good food. Friendly service and reasonalble prices. Four people in our group and we had a sampling of soups and noodle dishes.  Lot's of great aromas and flavors. 

Try it! It's great.
Small intimate place with a great vibe, good service, and amazing food. So excited places like this are popping up. Chicken soup gyoza and cold soba noodles are favs!

My Mom loves their steak salad here, so here is my review after 2 visits...

They do make a decent breakfast here.  Everything seemed fresh, but just standard fare with nothing really worth raving about.

On my second visit, I made a crucial mistake and ordered the meatloaf.

Obviously frozen, it was sadly served with a thick, gelatinous brown gravy and instant mashed potatoes.  I wasn't able to finish it.  A Stouffer's TV dinner is better.  Really...

So if you are satisfied with just heated frozen entrees, you make like this place.

If I get talked into coming back, I'll stick with the breakfast side of the menu...

Pay no attention to the name, which makes this place sound like a dollar-draft haven for douchebags. Savvy Jack's is a French bistro with homemade quiche and personal service, run by the owners, who drive down from Spring Hill every morning.

I had the "French omelette", which most Americans would call a "potato-garlic frittata with a side salad on top". It was soooo delicious and it filled first the plate and then mah belleh. Gourmandise for ten bucks. Can't beat it.

The owners cheerfully give no respect to American condiments, because why should they? You want *ketchup*? Ugh, if you must... here's some Hunt's. You want puckeringly sweet preserves on your toast? Fine... here's some no-name grape jelly. When it comes to respectable condiments, however, the little packets of butter do contain REAL butter and not the oil-whipped ooze served at most rural-themed chains. Butter is worth doing right.

This place was great!  Free refills on coffee.   Young professionals go and work on their laptops there.  It's great to do some work there and enjoy the atmosphere.  I will be trying the pastries next...

The pool is nothing like it is in the photos and to top it off no pool side service. The rooms are nice and the staff was accommodating. However you could stay at a Hilton garden inn for half the price and have the same experience. I vacation quite a bit and part of my enjoyment is pool side service. I only stayed one night and canceled the rest of my 4 night stay. I ended up at the Weston down the street. Corey was the manager and apologized for the inconvenience which was kind. If you are looking to relax by the pool do not choose this hotel!!! Other than that my stay was splendid.

The moment I saw the bridge I knew I wanted to run on it. I went around 9:30 in the morning and since the sun was scorching, there were barely any runners - around 7-10 others the entire hour I was there. But the shade by the bridge will keep you cool and since it's by the Delaware River, the breeze was wonderful.

My distance clocked in at around 4 km. It was a peaceful run and officers patrolled the bridge to make sure everyone is safe.

When we visited this location my daughter was being a typical 3 year old & refusing to eat lunch while wanting to scream at the top of her lungs. Frantically trying to calm her down I managed to spill my entire large lemonade. Not only did the staff help clean it up, they got me an entirely new drink without me even asking. Everyone knows the food is good here but the customer service is amazing!

I moved to the countryway neighborhood in June. I received a takeout/delivery menu on my porch and thought it was worth a try. Every place we live we find our favorite Chinese take out. I was excited to see they deliver to the house. I have ordered too many times to count and they always have my address in their system based on my number. They say 45 minutes but usually get it in 25. Everyone I have talked to is very friendly. I LOVE the food and we have lived in so many different states based on being military. One of the best. I just got a yelp account and I'm shocked to see all the negative reviews on here. I order the same stuff each time so maybe it's better than eat others are ordering but I've never had a bad experience with them. I have had some BAD Chinese food over the years and this is far from.

What would I do w/o K&S in Nashville?!?! As an Asian living out in not so diverse city, I need a place for me to satisfy my cravings. 

Not only do they have the things that I need, but they're pretty cheap. Yeah, some of their produce are not the freshest, but you'd have to expect that for that price, right? 

This place is one of my weekly grocery stores that I go to. I usually hit this spot up after going to Miss Saigon, next door,  for the best pho in town to relieve my hangover. hahaha

LOVED IT!!!!!

From the reviews below, your first huge tip? Drive out to the location - that'll save you having the shuttle issues that everyone below seems to have! 

We opted for the night-time tour as we had to head to Baton Rouge the next morning, but we really wanted to fit it in.  I was dying to hold a baby alligator, but I didn't get to, though I didn't really miss it either.

The night-time tour was two hours, and no amount of bug spray (oh yeah, bring bug spray) will save you from the skeeters.  You will see the occasional spider and roach on the boat as well.  It's a freakin' night time tour in to the swamp, so if you don't expect bugs and bites, you're an idiot! (There was a chick on our boat who shrieked every ten seconds!)

Our captain, Bishop was great, he was entertaining, informative and he knew exactly what to do to to get the alligators to show themselves!  We saw a LOT of gators, a bunch of adult/full size and some littler ones too.

It was definitely a highlight of our trip to NOLA and I can't recommend it highly enough!!

Visited here for breakfast before a trip to Busch gardens. It's a bit of a spin beyond Busch gardens from Orlando but it's worth it!!! 

Lovely atmosphere, pleasant staff, endless coffee and good food.

I had the French toast with bacon. It was fab.

One more thing, the view of the bay from the back door is beautiful!

Horrible experience, my lady and I went to this place for our first time and what we read in the reviews is totally truth, place is dirty, food was cold and terrible. The chairs were comfortable but disgusting dirty , there were spills everywhere and it look like they were never cleaned.

Best cappuccino served at any of the drive thru merchants in town. Orders are always right. Service is friendly. Dark chocolate espresso bark bar is killer good and no linger available 
Strange layout to the lot from all driveways. Accessible from 39th and 38th. 
Walkup window and casual outdoor seating available

I have been here twice and saw Lonisha both times, she was very professional and easy going. She made me feel really comfortable with my first time ever getting a wax, she is now on maternity leave and im going on Saturday i am so sad about this because i dont know who else i should go to. But this place gets 5 stars BECAUSE of Lonisha

They probably have the best fried chicken I have ever had.   That's no exaggeration either.  I just came back from Nashville (TN) and Mississippi and while I found great fried chicken there as well, Gray Brothers still has them beat.
Great selection of health foods and knowledgeable staff!!

This place is exactly what we need in the Art Museum/Fairmount area. It's small, quaint, really well priced. The staff are extremely friendly too. They'll let you in even before they open and they'll let you stay after they close.

There's also seating in the back, including a couch and some sofa chairs. So don't be deceived when you look through the window and see just a few tables in front. The staff is also adding more artwork and decor, so it's only getting better. If you're looking for a new spot to chill for an afternoon that's quiet, serves great coffee, and far enough away from the busy foot traffic of fairmount ave, come here.

Delicious! My fiancé and I went here a week or so ago and the food, service, and environment was superb! This may be a new favorite! I highly recommend this restaurant if you love Asian food! I didn't get a chance to order sushi yet, but I saw the chef making some and it looked amazing! We will definitely be making a trip back here soon!

Honestly, this place is the best sushi place EVER in St. Louis. 

Kampai will not let you down when it comes to taste and price. This place, in my opinion and so many of other people who experienced Kampai, knows what they're doing. 

The quality of the sushi is great along with the service and mostly the price. Everywhere in St. Louis sushi places are extremely expensive and the taste doesn't match up to the price. It's usually just an untrained (not even chef) who pretty much chops away at the fish when really sushi is an art. 

Well these people know what they're doing and know how to make people happy. I've had the jirashi here and it came with a very nice miso soup and salad with a very deliciously put jirashi. Honestly, I'm a huge fan!! Also the green tea icecream dessert is really something you must try. I think it's a perfect touch after some good sushi. 

Though I have to admit that I'm not a huge fan of parking, but really it's not something that you can blame them. I mean, come on - seriously? I see some posts on here giving these guys a hard time just because of parking. News Flash : it's not their fault so stop QQing over it, kthxbai. 

Overall, this place is awesome!
The place to go to get a great deal on a custom built aluminum trailer. They built 3 or 4 for me over the years. All functioned perfectly and they will maintain it for you also.
Somehow this carmalitas is not as good as the one up the street on east bay. Not quite as fresh and just seems dark in there.

My wife and I visited on July 20. It was our first time here. We live in the area and wanted to check out the wood fired pizza and the overall vibe of the place. The ambience is classy, not stuffy. We sat at the bar and started out with a bottle of Portuguese Vinho Verde Rose. It was very nice and not outrageously priced at $32. That was the best part of our visit.
My wife ordered the basic pizza - fresh Mozzarella and basil with some chunks of tomato. I ordered the small plate octopus. The octopus was OK but underwhelming. It was cooked well but could have benefited from a spritz of fresh lemon and a drizzle of olive oil and sea salt.......and maybe some fresh parsley. The cubes of fried polenta detracted from the dish.
The pizza was really just OK. With the Renato wood fired oven this place should be turning out the best pizzas in the entire Philadelphia metro and suburban area. The crust was too thick and had way too much cornmeal on the bottom. The pizza lacked flavor. My wife said it tasted like a Chipotle  pizza. I suggest a visit to Pizzeria Stella in PHL to see how thin crust is done well in a busy place. Basic ingredients, great equipment and a nailed down process.
We will visit again soon, as we are eager to see this place succeed.

I love this place, especially since it's a drive-thru.  Beignets vary in quality depending on when you go.  Sometimes they are better, sometimes they are worse, but whenever you go, you will be satisfied.

Hands down, the best chips in Indianapolis. Service here is consistently amazing and fast. Food is as good ir better than your local taquiera. Taco Tuesday's = $1 authentic tacos. Can't beat it. 
Come here, you won't be disappointed.

I was having a particularly hard time decided between the amazing menu items for dinner last night so I told the server just to surprise me out of the five or so suggestions he gave. He probably thought I was nuts but I was very pleased with what he chose for me. Coffee cocktails were amazing! Will be back!

Visited this location and the food was awesome. Very impressed with the manager named Dustin who made some great suggestions. Fried pickles were really great! Place reminds me of a bahama breeze for anyone who remembers that. Thanks Dustin for being so cool to my kids and making it a great visit

I'm honestly not really into classic rock but if I'm around my dad, this is what I go to.  MGK is a pretty good classic rock station. I don't really know what else there is for classic rock in Philly... I guess that's why they reserved the slogan "Philly's Classic rock station."
The place was not fancy but was quaint and the pizza was very good, probably the best I've had in this area. Will definitely try it again and looking forward to trying other menu items.

Great Shop.  Everyone does a great job there.  But you often have to wait a very long time unless you get there early.  Worth the wait (IMO) and I usually make a stop by P'unk burger or Chayya while I am waiting.  Great haircuts and good prices too.

Adam and his team is great.  On time, incredibly courteous, and great work.  All that and a great price- 60% less than I was quoted from a window repair company!  If you need new screens for your windows, call him.

Originally were headed to the Great American Pub. Got there at 9 and was told they closed the outside seating at 9. I'm so glad we found the Gypsy. Went here tonight with my girlfriend and my dog. They were very dog friendly and had a water bowl for Sam. I got the smokehouse burger that was perfectly cooked. It came with sweet potato fries that were good as well. My girlfriend got the all you can eat mussels and I might have tasted a few. They were also really good. The staff was friendly and very accommodating. Can't wait to go back for the lobster mac and cheese.
Had the Country platter - best sausage gravy over the lightest fluffiest biscuit. Hash browns and eggs were fabulous too. Yum!
This lil place was so DELICIOUS, Great Service,Friendly Chef too. All of the selections were served Hot & Harty Portions. The Entrees were Great Se lecttions..The Menu had so many choices...See pics
The best place to stay! I have lived there for over 1 year and I felt like I was at home. Warm and friendly people always willing to help you.

I will have to try this place again for a more accurate assessment. Stopped by for lunch on a Thursday and ordered the grilled chicken kale Cesar salad. When I dig into it, it was suburb!  Perfectly portioned and seasoned. But then a few bites into it I found a long hair in it. No big deal, gave the salad back and they made me a new one. The second salad tasted tasted like a distant version of the first. As if someone completely different and inexperienced made the second and the real chef made the first. The second salad did not have the shaved cheese, the kale was wet which really ruined the experience (but I was hungry so I ate and went), the proportions were off too, the "smoked" chicken had zero "smoke" to it. 

Not sure what happened, maybe the waiter made he second one?? 

Place had a cool old pub vibe to it. I will be back to give it another try only due to the first salad being spot on minus the hair.

Dr. Biscardi is the BEST.  My sister referred me to her, and I referred friends of mine to her as well. I like that she takes time and answers all my questions.  My sister now lives in SF, but when she's in town, she does try to get an appointment to see Dr. Biscardi since she's great. I wish more doctors were like Dr. Biscardi. Also, Brian is great too - he's adjustment my frames for me and on the fly!. Love everyone on staff for this office, they're super great.

Ordered a burger and salmon. The bill came out to $27.00 not complaining about that, but the salmon was over cooked and a very chewy. Plus not the most pleasant of experience with customer service. I got a very unpleasant stare. I probably won't be back.

I just had my second visit at this restaurant hoping it would be better than the last time I ate there and unfortunately it wasn't. Maybe a little worse. I only went there because it was the closest to my route heading home. Cornbread = dry; cabbage = too peppery (let folks add their own pepper if they want it instead of the whole batch); yams = not enough flavor; baked chicken = tasted like 3-day old food. I paid a whopping $15.00!  It's hard to find good soul food in Lou that's affordable. I wouldn't mind paying that amount if I enjoyed it, but the meal was totally not worth what I paid.

I've taken my kids to Dr. Bozic for nearly a decade. He knows his stuff and is very pleasant and down to earth. One of my kids used to be very anxious about going to the dentist. But he's gotten over it. I think the indoor basketball court helped with that.

Just ordered delivery from this location. I was a little worried because of the previous reviews, but, I also noticed they were pretty old. Ordering was easy using the app and the points for free pizza is great. Surprisingly, my pizza arrived hot and smelling delicious in a reasonable amount of time (45 min). The delivery driver was friendly. I tipped him well. My pizza was exactly what I ordered.
It was delicious. Perfect for 8:00 pm on a Sunday. I can't say how it would have turned out any other time or day but I'm satisfied.

I've gone here a few times for lunch. Always good. Today was even better. The young man working the cash register got me started on the Qdoba rewards card. He is the first one that has ever asked if I had a card. Then during my meal he was going around to all the tables and giving out free samples of chips and queso. Now talking about customer service!! This guy is awesome. I appreciate going into a place and experiencing workers like him. I just regret I did not get his name. I would like to give him all the kudos that he deserves. :) Keep up the good work and don't ever change.
The quality doesn't seem it's as good as it once was. Maybe it's the new ovens. We now prefer New York New York Pizza down the street off of Big Bend.

Saw the rave reviews and thought would give it a shot. The pizza we ordered (classic) was good but not great. It was the hand tossed -- the dough, sauce, cheese and toppings were good, but a bit too much bread vs other things. The price was way too high considering the size and product. The service was exceptional- we had our pie delivered in only 20 minutes and people were very friendly.  We may try again but since we are new to the area will likely try others first.

Tourist trap. The fudge tastes good and they give you samples. The employees were very pushy. They asked us 3 times to buy their buy 3 get 1 free combo. Our cashier visibly changed his attitude the last time we declined, we felt like we had done something wrong and got drawn into a conversation over why 2 people didn't need 2lbs of fudge. When we looked at the bill he charged us over $20 for one half pound slice of fudge, when he had quoted us $10.99 for a half pound.

Dined here for the second time last night. From the atmosphere to the service and especially the food, everything was spot on.

The tomato gazpacho soup was beyond excellent, the green salad about par with expectations of a restaurant of this caliper, the smoked drum appetizer incredible (we likened it to smoked tuna dip down in the Florida keys - just better!), and the entrees were memorable. 

My fiancée ordered the pork shank, which was a sizable portion of pork (which fell off of the bone with no effort), set atop a bed of mashed white beans (which were a perfect compliment to the pork). I ordered the snapper at our server's recommendation, and was not disappointed. While the filet wasn't large, it was cooked and flavored comparably to fish at the finest of fish houses. I was very impressed at both the fish as well as the coconut rice and green pairings.

For dessert we shared the milk chocolate and salted beignets, which was just the right combination of sweet and salty.

Long and short, we will be back again.
I love coming to this theater for its play productions. It's affordable, and the entertainers do a great job.

I love this place. The snoballs are delicious - so far my favorite is watermelon. The best part about it - no extra charge for sweetened condensed milk! They really don't need it but I have grown up eating my snoballs with cream and that's how I like it. 

Everyone should check this place out. Young, old - you will leave satisfied. This is a great addition to Freret St.

After raving about how wonderful Acme Oyster House on Iberville St was to our friends, we were very disappointed in the food at the Harrahs location.  We arrived in NOLA mid afternoon on Monday and were just too hungry to wait in the line.  Excited to see that they had another location in Harrahs so we went there.  Very, very disappointed.  My shrimp po boy was one of the worst I've ever had.  If a restaurant is going to have multiple branches, the owners should make sure the food is up to the primary location's standards.

Came here with my partner after a day of traveling. We had a Groupon deal for this place and it definitely exceeded my expectations (Groupon Now can be a bit of a crapshoot). It seemed like it could get pretty busy, but we were lucky to be seated outdoors right away. Tria has well-arranged sidewalk seating. Our server was attentive without being up my ass (which I hate). The wine and beer list are excellent and very reasonably priced. We had some bruschetta, a brie cheese, and a flourless chocolate cake, all of which were yummy (although the bruschetta is a bit overpriced for what you get). I will definitely be back here when I'm in town next. I know that if I lived in the nabe, it would be a staple.

Party City seeks to have shoppers visit and then go away pleased with purchases that satisfy from huge hanging balloons to napkins, plates to candy to quench the party hunger of the best  of party needs. Stop and shop at Party City to give every party participant the color and finest of sequence and design.


At the time of store our visit, Christen, Tech Super Salesman shared the joy and outreach of her job by turning us to learn about the altruism of the staff. The 'City' manifested itself as it collected for the Boys and Girls Clubs of America to help in its "think young" campaign. Moreover, the Party City folks would like to see customers enjoy the fun and games found in its confines to realize increased happy times during a time of brokenness in our country and in our world.

So come on by, and remember the good times and party on, whether these gatherings be for young or old.
Pretty good and consistent.  Can walk here from our house.  When in the mood for Thai it definitely satisfies

Had the smoked BBQ chicken wings and Pecan pie cobbler with vanilla bean ice cream along with a couple different local IPA beers.  The food was as good as the atmosphere.  They were probably the best smoked wings I've ever been able to purchase at a restaurant outside of me making them on my own smoker.  Highly recommend a visit to anyone.

I've been seeing Nikki Marshall as my new stylist for a few months now.  She has done exactly what I've wanted every time and is always friendly.  As a former hairstylist, I'm particular about who does my hair.  The staff are all very nice and the salon is clean and comfy.

I STILL love this place. Recently I had a reunion with past coworkers here. My friends are especially into hardcore gaming but the owner was real sweet about explaining. The workers will suggest games and teach you how to play. 

As usual, there are great things to buy that are geeky and homemade. My current favorites are lanyards with geeky shows and the Houses of Harry Potter (pick up one for your friend's favorite house!). If you go, they will give you a $5 coupon to give to a friend. There's also a points system which adds up - 1 point per dollar spent.
Good breakfast place with excellent pancakes.  Service was very good as well.  Fluffy scrambled eggs and nice corned beef and hash.   I will be back when on that side of town.

Light at the end of the tunnel! My boyfriend and I purchased a home in late 2015. The home was left unattended for many years. The pool was one huge eyesore - turned into a frog pond! After a disgraceful and unprofessional interaction with another pool company, we decided to check out Budd's who actually installed the pool originally. They have been nothing but helpful and accommodating with helping us get our pool up and running. We are happy that we have a company we can trust! Highly recommend!

Brought my old Ford Explorer here to have a recall service performed on it and to get the 'ol 120,000 mile checkup.  This is a huge place and it was a little tricky to figure out where to bring the car around, but once it was in place we were appreciative of the communicativeness of the mechanics-- the whole operation seemed very competent and solid.

With mechanics you never really know, but the price seemed reasonable for what I had done.  They called to alert me to some extra work I might have wanted to get done then or later, but I elected not to have it done and at no point felt uncomfortable or pressured as I talked about the issues with the fellow that was helping me.

Would consider coming here again if I have continuing problems with the vehicle.

I just came here to profess my love for the shrimp tacos. Seriously, they're delicious. Like the kind of good that makes you wonder how something so tasty can be only $3.  I also had a mahi mahi taco and it's no disappointment, but also no comparison.  Loved the free beer, and they kept the margaritas coming without us having to keep getting up to order more.  And now I'm off to dream about those delicious shrimp tacos. Yum.

Cool place if get lucky and get a parking spot and table, I have tried to come here 2 times before being successful place was slammed on week nights both times causing me to get frustrated and go somewhere else both times, I went on Wednesday even though still packed got lucky I guess cause up front parking and circling a few times and then only waited 5 minutes for a table.
Service was amazing young lady greeted us promptly and provided us with recommendations and didn't rush us either. Had a flight and pretzels to start really good. Ordered burgers and they were good not amazing but not to bad. Will likely try something else next time. There menu is really diverse so won't get bored with choices. 
Overall amazing service and clean establishment. Will try to come back if get lucky again.
The dirtiest Starbucks I've ever been in. They do seem super busy so hoping that they were just understaffed today.

We went there yesterday.  The KFC was good but the spicy version was not spicy enough.  The chicken was crispy.  I think Soho has better KFC.

We tried the best of Philly's bulgogi burger,  it was nice and juicy but again needed more of that Korean flavor profile to come out with the kochuchang sauce or Kim chi on it to add some crunch to the burger.  The fries were weak and tasted like they were dehydrated and very dry on the outside.

I would say the Butcher and Singer's burger  and Village Whiskey burgers are better.

The shrimp dumplings were excellent and had a nice miso glaze sauce to dip into on the plate.

The service was excellent since we went early but would go again.

Southgate,  please don't hold back on the Korean flavor profiles which make Korean food so delicious to eat to accommodate the Rittenhouse area.
Great Jersey pizza here....thin with a great chewy crust. Small space in an old stone building.
I enjoyed my meal with the excellent customer service and a terrific attitude from Adrianna, I would definitely come back and have her as our server. Thank you so much!
Sid Bookers have the best shrimp in Philly hands down ! Search their business on Instagram and follow them.

Came here for brunch with a friend of mine, we both didn't know what to expect as if was our first time. I was pleasantly surprised. I has the duck confit hash and she had french toast-both were superb. The wait staff were friendly and attentive. I'll definitely be back! This place knows what they are doing!

This is has been one of my favorite places in st. Charles the family is so sweet and the food is always what you expect. They always over stuff my bag with goodies and more rice then anyone could ever eat. Worth every dime.

Beautiful patio furniture, great service, free delivery, what more could you ask for?  Oh, great service they have that too.  The entire staff was very friendly and helpful, not pushy. 
I love my new furniture.

Can't go wrong with Jasmine's great selection of sushi. This was our N-th visit. (I have lost count because we love this place for sushi!) We went with some friends who were visiting. We ended up getting many rolls and crab fried rice! OMG the CRAB FRIED RICE. So yummy!! We asked to be surprised with a noodle dish and the sweet server brought us the Jasmine Noodles. Not a fan. But everything else was spot on and we had a great time!

Best egg whites and cheese in town!  Speedy, friendly service.  And for those of us that have to work while hungover on the weekends, this truck is a lifesaver.

The only problem I have with them is that they don't make coffee.  (This really only merits deduction of half a point but since that's not an option I have to round down).  But really, it's not difficult to make and it would bring in SOOOOO much more money.  This is a college campus  where all the undergrads and grad students are zombies without coffee...

Come on, Bui's, make coffee so I can give you that extra star.

Finally made it to this landmark that my husbands been trying to get us to every visit we have in Nashville. They were delicious pancakes - light and fluffy and simple. Really you wonder how special a pancake really could be- they're simple right? Well I was impressed with the down to earth, yet famous establishment and their perfected classic. These pancakes are buttery and so light. I also loved the portion sizes- substantial but not the comical Paul Bunyan style pancakes we see so often now days. 

We had friendly prompt service and the atmosphere was familiar. It was pleasant to see the establishment had stayed so true to its roots over the past 50 years.

What a crock.  My wife and I had two vehicles in need of safety and emission checks.  I, the husband, dropped my vehicle off for the emission check around 9:15am and was told that it would take around an hour.  No big deal.  My wife pulled in 30 minutes later and went in (I had already walked to a nearby store).  They told her they could not guarantee a time for the safety and emission check, but that it should be done by 5:00.  My vehicle was done within 30 minutes, and my wife's wasn't completed until around 3:30.  Now, maybe the safety check does take a bit longer- so that's fine.  That said, they said that her vehicle needed a new brake light and that one of the windshield wiper blades needed to be replaced in order to pass the safety inspection.  They quoted her $250.00 for the repairs.  TWO HUNDRED AND FIFTY DOLLARS.  I went to an auto parts store and bought the necessary bulbs and a wiper blade for a grand total of $37.89.  They told my wife the bulbs were LED- they aren't.  They were going to replace an entire tail light assembly when all that needed to be replaced were three bulbs.  Now, the kicker.  When I took the tail light assembly out to do the (easy) replacement- three of the five bulbs had been unsocketed and pushed back into the lens.  One bulb had been cracked.  Now, I have no proof that the tail light was functioning before.  But I have considerable doubts that the bulbs had been pushed in and broken before I dropped this thing off at Dobbs.

Long story short, this place will get the job done.  They'll just gladly charge you about SEVEN TIMES the cost of the actual repair.  Unbelievable.  Any reputable repair shop would never quote such an astronomical price for such easy and quick repairs.  I will NOT be returning.
Thanks for the previous reviews. Are they nuts? This place continues to be fantastic. Great burgers and wonderful Gumbo. And Babs the bartender is a real kick. Try this place, you'll love it!!!
The dill pickle soup and adult grilled cheese are to die for!

Report card 
Steak tacos --B 
Guacamole---B+
Tortilla Chips---C-
Service----B
Cleanliness ---B- 
Price ---A

I'm in St. Louis (from Louisville) to visit the City Museum and go to Cardinals opening day.  I had my son and his friend with me, so you can imaging my frustration and stress when I noticed something falling from underneath my car.
