The mint julep was stronger than I expected, you can really taste the whisky and hints of mint. The New York sour is sour on top of sour if you like that sort of thing and the Sansome Street Sangria was pretty good with a hint of fruity wines and, once again, the whisky shines through. The featured item fell short for me. My entree was the Burger w/crab slaw, sunny side egg, applewood bacon, tomato and lettuce. The burger to bun ratio was way off. The bun was way to thick and wide. I must have bit the burger about 3 times before I made a dent in the burger. I was unable to taste any of the ingredients on my burger because the bread was so over-powering and thick. The burger and the toppings were sliding off the bun. I had to eat the toppings separate in order to taste them. Our bill was $144.00. I could've saved $100.00 and ate at Bobby Flays. He has the best burgers that I've ever tasted in my life. People fail to understand that a good burger is about having a nice soft reasonably sized bun with well seasoned good quality beef. The burger and the bun should be the same size. I should be able to comfortable open my mouth and,  with the first bite, taste all of the ingredients and toppings. Some chef's get caught up in the prettiness of the bun and the bigger the burger the better it taste... No! That's not it at all... To be honest. I'd rather have a burger from Nifty Fifty than Village Whisky. But it depends on how you like your burgers and I, frankly, am not impressed by size and glazed over-sized shiny buns. IF I go back, it would be for the appetizers only.

I've been to NOLA several times but never had the opportunity to eat at a John Besh restaurant. This was my first time, and I'm in love! My husband and I went to Luke for a Friday lunch. The restaurant was bustling--so I recommend making a reservation. The ambiance is that of a French Bistro-unpretentious, even though the service is 5 star. The menu can be somewhat intimidating for those not familiar with French words--but the servers are willing to answer questions and give recommendations.

Here's what we tried:
-Bread: Classic, Crusty French Bread 
-Foie Gras Terrine: Rich--it's an acquired taste
-Matzo Ball Soup: The Matzo ball was absolutely scrumptious...would have liked more broth 
-Croque Madame: Fanciest Croque Madame I've ever had; brought out on a wooden cutting board; get it with the Fried Egg--you'll want to take a nap after this one
-Cochon de Lait: Absolutely the favorite on the menu--crunchy bread, pulled pork and ham, caramelized onions, and the cherry mustard complements it all beautifully

Food was great! I got chicken Tikka masala as well as spicy chicken on top of rice, samosas and pita bread. I also got a mango lassi which was great too! The food was good but I suggest you come here as soon as you get it so the foods the freshest because it's set up kinda like chipotle. The lady who worked here told me that the owner makes everything fresh in the morning which is great. When I went it wasn't that busy so I would recommend going during a slow time like I did if you don't want to wait that long.

Few of my friends ended up visiting this place because of the bar.  We got outdoor seating almost immediately which was really nice on a hot summer day.  We ordered three flights of beers, which was all the drafts they had.  It was amazing.  We did our own beer tasting event.  I ended up ordering the side order of Mac and Cheese, which was amazing. First of all, the side is almost the size of an entree.  It had the perfect consistency of cheese and butter.  I would go back just for the Mac and Cheese.

Normally, I would stay away from anything close to PYT like it had the plague, but I have been wanting to visit Emmanuelle ever since I heard about it. It sucks it's in the Piazza, but at least we can park in the lot nearby and technically, it's more like behind it? Anyway, there is outdoor seating on nicer days and the chalkboard drawing of Saruman and Lo Pan (Big Trouble in Little China) was enough to get my hopes up.

As typical of cocktail bars, it was dark dark dark so be prepared for the stark contrast of coming in when it's nice and bright outside (as in, they're just opening). Since we've only visited when they open for the night, it's rarely been packed so sitting at the bar was comfortable. The bartenders are very friendly and we enjoyed the awesome music.

The drinks are great and crafted with care! I haven't had anything I didn't like yet. I love the decor of this place, it's up there with Bardot Cafe.

We always like Safeway.  The store is smaller then the larger Fry's in the neighborhood and it is easier to find what you want with out all the crowds.  We also prefer there flower and balloon selection.  The employees are great and always friendly.  We also like the US Bank on the inside.

Had it delivered to local hotel. By accident, went to wrong hotel (little language barrier) but quickly resolved and brought right over. 

Ordered the General Tso Chicken, egg rolls and wanton soup. All was very good but soup was not was I was expecting. Too many vegetable. Like my wanton with just soup and dumplings. 

Would recommend. Good presentation and tasted good.

I had dinner here on a holiday evening but there were plenty of tables indoors, although the outdoor seating was limited to tables with high chairs.  We had grouper and hogfish and both were very good.  They serve alcoholic beverages.  Prices were average for Gulf Coast.  I recommend this restaurant if you are in the Johns Pass area.

Great service and really good food. The waiting staff was on top of everything and Bernadette was amazing. This is a great local place and we will return!  The owner/manager even visited our table during our visit.

I absolutely love stopping in here for a quick drink and socializing with friends and family. A friend kept mentioning events hosted here and I first visited with family from out of town. The layout is friendly for group outtings. The brewery floor is appealing with areas for guest to view the process without a formal tour. I have become hooked on there Kombucha. As a beer lover it's weird to say that I truly get excited about this place for their Kombucha, it's such a niche in Nashville. They're the only brewery that offers an alternative non-alcoholic beverage adding to the appeal. 
I have yet to try the menu but it's intriguing and unique. Offering a wide array and providing beer lovers a reason to stick around. I could see this as a great date spot for beer and food enthusiasts like me.
Had the combination fried rice and pork n seeds. I was really impressed. The rice was some of the best I've had. They pork was good. Cold but fine. Spicy yellow mustard looked home made.

The $10 down, $10 per month with no contract hooked me in.  The annual fee is like $20...no big deal.  The gym is in a great location for me meaning there is no excuse not to go. The facility is big with a lot of machines and TVs.  Locker room looked nice, bring your own towel and padlock, with private shower stalls.  Other $10 fitness places have a wait for equipment or people waiting for you to finish.   Not here.  The open 24 hours pitch and seeing hours of availability was a little confusing, however, they are 24 hours throughout the week with weekend limitations.  Staff was wonderful.   The front desk guy, Donald, that showed me around talked to me like an old friend.  Super nice and interactive.  Greets everyone as they enter and leave.   Zero sales pressure, provided a tour and I was sold.  I like the free wifi to stream pandora.  People that Ive seen are normal everyday people.  My last gym was expensive but this is inexpensive and has everything I need in a clean, modern facility in a great location with hours that meet my needs without the crowds.

Hands down my favorite restaurant in St. Louis. From the small plates to the cocktails, Reed's has never been a let down (with the exception of their Reuben sandwich that is no longer on the menu).

A few of my recent favorite small plates include:
1) Burrata from the cheese selection sid: creamy, subtle, and simply a phenomenal start to any meal
2) Pickled Vegetables: this remains my absolute favorite dish because of the pickled cauliflower and the curry underneath - texture, flavor, and aromatics all work brilliantly.
3) Mushroom on toast with bone marrow: rich, umami flavor and warm crusty bread - what's not to love!

I've skipped main courses the last few visits so I can't comment on the recent menu other than the pork loin with creamy spinach and pickled onions, which was well-balanced - subtle but flavorful. A solid choice.

Pastry Chef Summer Wright is always changing up the desserts, and on my last visit didn't have the fantastic panacotta from my previous dinner.  But it's ok! They still had the thyme ice cream, which on first bite might be a bit shocking especially if you aren't used to herby, savory ice creams.  Have a second and third spoonful and you'll thank me you did.

I also have to tip my hat to the always fantastic, friendly servers and to Andrei Ivanov, their beverage director who also helps front of house.  He is always welcoming and obviously extremely knowledgeable when it comes to the food and wine/cocktail pairings.  

I am and will be a regular as long as I remain in St. Louis.

Stumbled in here this morning while in Nashville, we were greeted with only soft opening but then owner swooped in and invited us to come in and try the breakfast! Ended up loving this place! Great owners super quality food. Beautiful pastries, fabulous coffee and homemade gelato. Finally they sent over complimentary warm fresh made cookies gelato and whole milk. Truly amazing! This place WILL do well!!!

i've been here a few times and i'm always surprised that they have a respectable assortment of vegan and vegetarian items on the dinner menu. i guess the vegan in me just notices the word ice cream. BUT IT'S MORE THAN JUST ICE CREAM !!

thanks you've been a great crowd!

Just moved to the area. We were cruising around for a place to have a coffee. We loved this place. The kids loved the donuts and I got to finally try Matcha ;) It was great! We recommend if you're in the area!

Beyond impressed our first trip to new Orleans and i must say i am a hardcore critic of food and how it tastes and how the people serving me are. And man o man i felt right at home layout is so homey and fun. The people here are amazing fun and just all around wondeful. The food is top notch it really brings me to a place in many books that you wish you could eat at. If you dont try it you're a fool.

This is a nice little indoor snowball spot where you can sit and eat at a table if you want.  They specialize in stuffing their snowballs with cheesecake here and have come up with some really interesting combinations.  They use a Snowizard machine so the ice isn't quite as fine as Hansen's but the cheesecake addition and the creative flavoring twists make this a worthy place to grab a treat at.

Great service, quick response, and fair pricing.  I called on a Friday about having locks changed on a condo  we just bought.  He offered to come out that night and I told him the morning would be fine.  Really nice guy, great communication via text and phone, informed me about my lock type and what he would do and even made some extra keys for me.  Cost for job was less that i thought I would have to pay.  Overall very satisfied! 

Highly recommended

food is good. service is not. We go there at least 2-3 times a week, because of their organic options and fresh juice. There were 3 of us and It was 32 degrees outside. they had tables open but they were 2 tops and one large table right by the door ( that is constantly being opened) and the bar seats were available. we asked if we could wait for a table away from the door since we would rather not be shivering our entire meal. She (the waitress with very short hair) could not have said this is a more rude manner. "well you're going to have to wait outside then" We all just stood there dumfounded that she would talk to us that way.there was no one else waiting - it was not busy- you want us to stand outside in 32 degree weather? really? we were hungry and looking forward to some fresh juice so we sat by the door. They were out of the juice. wonderful.  They definitely act like they're doing you a favor.

Have eaten here twice since they introduced a new menu, and so far it has been delicious. The new Gorgonzola and pear salad was awesome, even though the pears were over ripe and kind of mushy. Silver Peak needed a menu update and has knocked their new Shepard's Pie out of this world (it blows Great Basins out of the water). The Spicy Shredded Pork tacos were delicious, however they are not spicy but have a ton of delicious flavor. The craft beer selection is always great and their mixed drink menu is delicious. Overall, Silver Peak is back on my radar for frequent dining!

Beware of parking. This place is good and healthy. Now that I can walk here, I don't have to drive across town to get my Taziki's fix.

This location is always clean and I have never had an issue finding a table. The only issue is that I keep running into people I know and getting into really long conversations :/

What can I say about this magical place that hasn't already been said before?!

This is the single greatest place to eat in the history of food.
I travel from Houston, TX with the main goal being Pancake Pantry.
The wait is never not worth the food. I have never gone a weekend though so I am sure it is a lot longer at those times.

Worth it all.

Best food.

Great tattoo from Vanae. Wanted a tiny piece as a souvinir before heading back home to TX, and tried 2 other shops before making it to the end of State St.The other 2 shops weren't interested in doing any work that day it seemed, and were really cold and rude. Went into Golden Eagle and everyone was friendly. Clean shop with a lot of character. Van was able to fit me in within an hour after her appointment, and even stayed a little late for me. Super sweet and talented, highly recommend.

My sisters and I decided to try a local place off by our hotel. Place was packed when we got there and still a waiting list when we left. Portions are huge! One sister tried the Swamp platter, so much stuff on there she couldn't finish it. My other sister and I tried the crawfish, shrimp and sausage mirliton, so good. It was the special of the day. Sweet tea was refreshing and even though place was hopping that night, our service was still above and beyond.
Cute little place, nice atmosphere. I ordered a grilled pork vermicelli and the noodles were cold, no brownie points there. The pork and flavor were on point though. Overall, I wasn't impressed.

We went in for lunch and the food was tasty but our waitress ignored us the whole time we were there. We had to pull over other waitstaff to assist us while our waitress chatted with bar staff with her back to us for the entire hour we were there. We couldn't even get our drinks refilled. Even though we returned to many NOLA restaurants for a repeat visit this was not one of them.

Super swanky pad! Both me and hubby went "Wow. How much did we pay for this fancy suite??!" For only $109, we have a huge room with a king bed, luxury sheets, sitting area, desk, bar, kitchenette, fridge -- THIS HOTEL ROOM IS ACTUALLY BIGGER THAN OUR APARTMENT!

Whoa - I just figured it out! I mean, the word "Apartment". I was _meant_ to be _apart_ from my apartment, and in this awesome huge hotel room, where there's hot breakfast from 6:30 to 9:30 every day, and the pool's open til midnight! I'm going swimming now!!!!!!!!

Wow, I cannot say enough great things about this place.  I needed a flapper dress for a 20s party.  I called the store before I visited and asked if they had dresses to fit my size (I'm a size 12 and curvy--not great for 20s style clothing!)  When I got to the store, the lady had already pulled 6 dresses for me to try on.  One of them was this amazing sequin and beaded dress that she said was very flattering on curvy women.  I tried it on and it was beautiful.  It was a rental, so she was very helpful in walking me through the rental process and making sure I had all the right accessories to go with the dress (pearls and feathers!).  I got a million compliments on the dress and I felt like a million bucks the night of the event.  I can't say enough good things about this store and I highly recommend trying it if you have a themed event.  Give them a call and they would probably love to help you.  I have been recommending this store to everyone who asks me about the dress!
Have had the Po' Boy and the Tuna Tacos and both were outstanding as were the fish & shrimp that I've purchased for home consumption. Plus, Ant, the owner is cool

Went here twice for happy hour during my stay here. The oysters are $.75 now but that didn't prevent us from ordering! They oysters were quite large and very delicious. We also ordered the crispy brussel sprouts and they were hands down the best I've ever had! The crawfish bisque was also very good, the gumbo just ok. We ended our meal quite satisfied with their delicious bread pudding
I give them three stars on behalf of the staff, they are real cool, the que is not, real tough ribs

3rd time's a charm they say, but in my case, 1st/2nd/3rd times were/are all charming.

Can I say I love The Wine Loft?  Starting w/the warm plush decor to the Live Local Music Thursday Nights to the Wine Selection available.  Not too big, not too loud, not too quiet - just right.  Why not a 5 star?  I very rarely give 5 stars because I think most establishments have room to grow, but this place is my current Crush.

I love the comfortable atmosphere and the decor makes me feel at ease.  Maybe because it reminds me of my home decor?? hmmmm

The appetizers haven't let me down yet either, so I really don't have anything bad to say about this place.  I would frequent this place once or twice per month consistently on Thursday Nights.  Pricewise?  I mean it's in the Gulch....what do you expect?

Four friends got together to try out Ava - great night with friends, but so-so on the food.

We had reservations and were seated promptly. Ordered drinks (prosecco, holy sh*t batman, sprite and 1919 mule), warm ricotta app and margherita pizze. Friends enjoyed the warm ricotta and the margherita pizze had delicious crust - a tad burnt, but light, not dense. Main entrees were cavatelli Al Ragu (3 ordered this) and braised lamb shank. The Ragu dish was a typical pasta dish - nothing fancy, nothing spectacular. The lamb shank with brussel sprouts and lentils was salty - way too salty. The brussel sprouts weren't cooked all the way and were cold. Disappointing meals and didn't live up to the hype.

Tiramisu for dessert - friends found it a delight.

The ambiance and atmosphere were lovely, but no need to rush back to try more dishes. Also felt overpriced.

I love the Fiesta Pizza, It was very tasty and loaded with toppings. Salad Bar is like unique accessory to the location, it is the center of attention as soon as you walk in. What about those big screens TV's, you just need to say WOW!!!

When it comes to South Philly dining, Scannicchio's is a really great place to eat.  First off, it is BYOB which is nice, and the staff is very friendly and accommodating.  It is also right near the Broad and Oregon stop of SEPTA so you can take the train one stop and you are down at the stadiums, which is nice.  It's maybe a block from the entrance on the other side of the street. Also after 6 PM you can street park for free nearby so if you are going to a game, free parking and just have to pay for the Septa.  The service is fast and smooth and I have tried many different things.  The filet is solid, and the gnocchi is really good, but I recommend getting it not baked because I think it is better that way and the waiter actually told me that too.  Their spaghetti and meatballs are solid and their bread is really good.  The caesar dressing is good and their salad is as well.  They get you in and out at a nice rate, where you usually are not waiting forever but you don't feel rushed either.  It is family owned and run, so it's not a chain and it offers really good food at reasonable prices especially considering it's a BYOB.  The chicken picatta is also solid, I've had that a few times, they give you nice portions too so I've never left the restaurant hungry.  If you are looking to eat someplace before a game, I highly recommend Scannicchio's.  They are conveniently located with good food and quality service.  I go there almost every time I am going to a Flyers, Phillies, or 76ers game and always enjoy the meal.

Note: They don't take American Express in case you are planning on using it but do take the other credit cards.
Great service, great prices,  applicable fitting atmosphere and decor,  best of all the beers and food are awesome!

Came with a friend to do some studying on a Saturday morning. We ordered two chai lattes and sat right by the large window at the front, which lets in a lot of natural sunlight. There's seating at the front and also more downstairs so it's a great spot to bring a laptop and do some work (plus the staff were very sweet as well). 

The latte was made from the purple Oregon liquid chai mix (which a ton of people use). It's a little too sweet for me so next time I'll probably just go with a tea.
Food is consistently good and tasty.  Quizzo on Wednesday nights is typically a fun time too.

I love Tijuana Flats!! They have the best sauce and best TACOS!! I go just about every Tuesday for Tacos because you cannot beat the deals. The food fits a college kids budget and is super fresh, what more could you ask for. I reccommend this for anyone hungry and not looking to spend a lot on a Tuesday.

I am not even much of a coffee fan, but their coffee is great! It's clear that Old World puts more thought and care into creating truly gourmet coffee than anywhere else in town. I had the orange blossom latte, and enjoyed it. I've also enjoyed their other drinks (hot chocolate, tea) and pastries. Every employee that's served me has been very friendly and helpful. They really take their time to talk to you about what you like, and help you decide on a drink that's going to suit you best. It's nice to know that they really care about whether you enjoy your drink, particularly at a coffee shop that is new and has a lot of creative and higher end options that most customers will never have tried before. If you don't know what to get, just ask and they'll help you!

The decor is nice, very modern while also being inviting (especially the wall behind the bar, in a nice warm wood). The menu is nice and simple, and I love that they have specialty drinks which will change throughout the year. Parking is surprisingly easy thanks to the parking lot behind the building (off Plumas St.). If I could make any change to this place, it would just be to add more tables. There are only two real tables inside (the rest being bar-style seating along the wall, which is great for working or reading but not so much for conversation). Most of the time that I go in with a friend and want to be able to see their face as we chat, the two tables are already taken so we're out of luck. The outside seating is helpful in that regard, but it would also be great to have a couple more small tables inside as well. Overall though, a fantastic coffee shop and I will be back for sure!

This place is amazing!! What a great brunch. We ordered the bananas fosters pancakes and the French toast and we both agreed it was one of the best breakfasts we've ever had. We had hash browns as a side and they were perfectly seasoned in rosemary (with a mixture of sweet potatoes and potatoes!) Our server Jillian was very friendly and accommodating.

Well, we were seated on the mezzanine with an amazing view on the restaurant! Our host was so friendly, funny and gave us a lot of good suggestions!
We start with a good drink and 4 mezze: the muhammara was good, the Brussels sprouts was smoky and lovely! After, we had the eggplant plate with pine nuts! That is a must if you go there! Smoky, tasty and rich in flavors! I highly recommend it!

Not bad. Got my first weave ever at this spot. 
Things to remember - if you're a walk-in make sure to go as early as possible. So far I've been there twice and have had to wait at least 2 hours before I was attended to. 

I'll be back - the first stylist I used was V - she did a great job. Jeff was great too...6 weeks later and my friends are still complimenting me on the weave.

Superb and friendly service in this tiny cocktail lounge.  To me, Emmanuelle's is what a lounge should be, dark, comfortable seating, attention to detail while making strong drinks, and the quiet occasionally interrupted by an instrumental duo.  

The drinks are creative and well made.  I ordered an old fashioned (one of the better ones I've had) and the "worthy fucking adversary," which is a spicy drink designed to taste like cold pho.  While I can't see myself ordering round after round of these, it was pretty good.  If you like sriracha, then I would recommend trying it.

There are true bartenders here, evident in the care taken to make your drink.

Food was decent, if a bit pricey.   The home fries weren't fresh, but were the little frozen cubes.   The omelette was very good, but my "green" tea was some herbal concoction that was super strong.   If I was in the area again I would probably try something else.

Best Thai in Tampa. Their pad thai is honestly the best I've ever had at any thai restaurant. They're portions are big enough to share, so you can order two entrees and it becomes family style. Also, their thai tea is a must, and if you're feeling like something different, try the chicken satay. It comes out with it's own little fire.
Fair warning: when they ask for the heat you want, medium is more like super duper hot. If you don't like heat, and for plain. It still has a kick to it.

So, I work next door to this place and have thought plenty of times I would like to try it. Normally I'm a Subway consumer but finally I made the decision to go in and Check this place out. My final push to give it a shot was a Facebook post I saw on my feed reaching out to Sherwood Park patrons to support this local business (search for the post if you want the details).
It's not a fancy place. Very "cafeteria" like. The hours are pretty short as well (another reason I never seems to time it right to go in). They are Monday to Friday 8:30am only until 2:30pm.

I initially planned on trying out their tuna sandwich but the patron in front of me had ordered the roast beef and after seeing how much fresh roast beef they piled on his bread, I quickly changed my mind. I ordered a roast beef on white and a small baked potato soup. Everything was incredibly fresh. No processed deli meat crap here! Bread all baked fresh, soup homemade. It was delicious. Large portions and incredibly fresh veggies. They had lots of salad and dessert choices as well, I just didn't partake in those. It was about $11 for sandwich, soup and a bottle of water. First thought was that it seemed a bit pricey until I reminded myself I easily pay that at subway and don't get a soup with that!
You can stay in or take out. Not sure if you can call in an order to pick up but not really necessary because the steady stream of lunch time patrons were served quickly and accurately. Would definitely consider making a permanent switch from subway with the hours of operation being the only thing that would stop me.
Worth checking out. Go support local!
I gave (2) stars because for the price of dinner I've had much better.  The best thing is the service was great, the ambiance is awesome but the food not so much.  Very overrated.

I love the smell of this place! Any spice you need, they have it. The staff also makes great recommendations if you're unsure of what you're looking for. I have never gotten a "stale" spice here. I enjoy the smaller size portions- it keeps things fresh in your own kitchen.
Great for harder to find items, especially for Indian dishes. 
Cash only.

I found this business through Yelp and chose it because it's close to me and the high reviews. I am very happy I found this place. I needed a dress brought in for a event on the weekend. Dropped off Tuesday and picked it up Friday. A perfect fit. It was a fairly simple job but the results are great and professionally done. I will definitely recommend and use this business again.
Hey. Not too bad. The brew is great. Waitress should of checked on us more often though. If they step it up a little, then its a good 4 star spot.

My sister and I went here for lunch on a Saturday.  We were the only ones in the restaurant, which was fine.  The interior is beautiful, with carved wood all over the place, and authentic-looking (having never been to Thailand, I'm not sure) decor.  We had the papaya salad and the wheel of fortune as appetizers.  They were both delicious.  The peanut dipping sauce was very flavorful and unique.  The chicken satay was deliciously moist.  Then we split the pad kee mao.  I love fat rice noodles, and the dish was just spicy enough.  The vegetables were tender, and the chicken was delicious.  For dessert we had the sticky rice with mango.  There wasn't a drop of food left.  I'll definitely be returning.
SUPERB describes this establishment in one word for the food , ambience ,music and service HIGHLY RECOMMEND

Try the vegetarian pad see ew! It was super super yummy came with broad noodles that had the perfect amount of flavor and onions bell peppers, egg and broccoli and green beans. Also came with delicious tofu if you get the veggie version. Really really great food! Can't wait to go back.

On 06/09/17 my wife and I made reservations to celebrate our 13 year anniversary and we couldn't be more happier. As a revolving restaurant there really is not a bad seat but I felt we were given a great view overlooking the gulf just in time to watch the sun set. Our waitress Tracey was so helpful throughout the night. She made great suggestions, took my wife and I picture and constantly made sure we were comfortable.The food was pretty good although my mini pork shank was not what I expected. This was my wife and I second time dinning here and we would gladly do it again.

YUM!!!!!! The burgers are juicy and worth every calorie BUT the boozy shakes are the cats pajamas. I had the Nutella shake and it was mind blowing. Variety of really neat beers on tap at all times. Family friendly too! Epic place worth seeing while in Gulch.

We pass Sakura a lot while shopping and it always smells wonderful from the outside. We decided to stop in on a Monday evening and my 5 yr old was really excited to do the hibachi. Unfortunately we were told there would be a 20 minute wait and were given a long explanation about only having two cooks in and blah blah. I knew a 20 min wait probably meant 40, and with two small kids that wasn't ideal, so we sat at the regular tables. Needless to say the kids were disappointed. I watched a few more groups come in for hibachi who had to sit on the regular side because of the wait. Which, 10 mins after we sat down, was still "20 mins!"

The waitress was nice. We ordered beef dumplings for an appetizer. My 5 year old and husband were not fans. The waitress forgot my husbands wine but she was nowhere to be found after she took our order. We saw the wine sitting on the bar for a long time. The host, I believe, would bring us our soups and salads but then would run away so quickly we could barely ask him for the things we needed. 

I got filet and chicken with fried rice. I was pretty impressed and thought the food tasted great with a nice presentation on the plate. The rest of the meal went well until we got the bill. Very pricey! But the kicker was....$4 for a tiny plastic kids cup of apple juice??!?!? I thought I was seeing things. My husbands wine was only $2 more! Wow. 

Still undecided about this place. I think I will give the hibachi side a try soon, but will definitely call ahead first!!!

Sticky, licky, sucky, messy, dirty and wet.  There is something better than sex for sale in Port Richmond, and no, it's not heroin.

Bonk's crabs.  Blue crabs in insanely spicy  briny murky seawater were the best I've had in Philly.  They were delivered less than hot, which irked me straight off, but were so tasty I forgave it.

Fries were crisp and well-seasoned, with a side of melted white cheese that smoothed out the hot heat of the crab broth.

Wings were good,  of the well-done school.  Not the best thing on the table, but respectable.

Deep-fried beer battered crab nuggets were hot grease perfection, dipped in a side of tartar sauce.

Dinner for three with a beer each, four jumbo $8 crabs and many fried basket things was $23 each.    Better than sex, but you still need a shower afterwards.

1.  Disfunction with the hostesses to start the night. 
2.  Drinks took 15-20 mins to get.  
3.  The orders took a long time to receive.  
4.  One was wrong and the other was cold.  The waitress asked if I would like my meal reheated in the microwave!  Appetite lost!

This is really a Korean restaurant with salad and bubble tea on the side. I love that the Korean dishes do not have any MSG taste in them and the prices seem VERY reasonable compare to the other Korean restaurants near by.

Nice place to get a quick fix of Korean food during lunch.  You can't go wrong with the rolls or dolsot bibimbap!

Finally made it to the famed falafel truck.  I believe the official name is Christos's Falafel.  I'd heard the stories and knew that I should plan to wait and just trust in what he is serving.

Turns out you don't even order here.  Little was said to anyone during my visit.  "Gus" cooks, refills the charcoal in his grill, and serves up falafel, grilled chicken, and salads/sides.  There's no menu. Walk up to the truck, and he'll put together a styrofoam container of everything unless you specify that you want a sandwich.  Otherwise, you need not say a word.  He didn't even ask me for money, assuming I already knew the price (it's not posted anywhere).  

My plate was $10 and could easily feed two.  The chicken was flavorful, covered in spices. The salad was fine, with fresh green lettuce, a bean dish, and something tropical I couldn't identify (was that plantain?).  My palate was confused after all the Greek-style meat.

But the falafel...oh, the falafel.  It was unlike anything I've eaten.  It was so bright--there are a lot of fresh herbs in there.  It was light and airy yet crispy on the outside. The texture was unusual but excellent.  I can't for the life of me figure out what it is that makes it so different. Does he whip the bean mixture first?   Whatever it is, it works.
The Peppermill Reno is a very nice place to stay! It has excellent amenities and a huge selection for dining! the rooms are fabulous as well! We had a suite in the Tuscany Tower.
Went to a special event hosted here for dinner.  As good as it gets and all the acclaim is right on.   Want to come back for brunch soon!

Worst service I've encountered outside of Dick's Last Resort (where it's kind of expected).

Missed drink orders, topping off my Zin with a Cab (both bottles were very nice until the impromptu "blending").  Bread thrown onto the table as an afterthought.  Taking each person's order twice and then giving them to the wrong person.

I won't be back.  Food isn't worth reviewing as it was average at best.

After checking out a couple of places for new frames near where I live in the suburbs, I decided to venture out into the city in hopes for a wider selection.
I was so happy I decided to visit West Coast Optical first. In fact, I didn't even need to go anywhere else; I chose the perfect frames within 2 hours!  

Nancy and Mark have some of the most chic and edgy, fashion-forward frames that I've ever seen in stores. I was actually overwhelmed by the plethora of amazing choices! I liked a bunch of the frames and had some trouble deciding, but Nancy was very patient with me. She made sure to only show me frames that reflected what shape and style I wanted, and ones that were within my price range. I never felt pressured to go with something more expensive, and she helped me narrow down to a few frames that I really loved. Both Nancy and Mark gave me their honest opinions on which frames flattered me best, and with their help, I picked out the perfect frames! About three days later, one of their associates called to say my glasses were ready to be picked up. Talk about speedy service!

I highly recommend choosing West Coast Optical for your eyewear needs!

How have I not reviewed the Range yet? 

One of the few "Bailey's" restaurants you'll find around STL. The biggest thing I love about these places is the "Farm-to-table" food. Menus revolving around the season, locally sourced meats for the burgers, and heck, even the tap beer selection is local! I enjoy the selection of unique beef, bison or even goat burgers, as well as trying the variety of dipping sauces for your fries. You feel like you are dining in a cleaned up barn while here...and I mean that in a good way. The decor appears to have been salvaged parts of farm houses and barns. Adding to the home on the range feeling and something I've never seen anywhere else (other than an Amish family restaurant) is the long "family-style" table running through the middle of the building. It encourages sitting next to strangers and making new friends! I love it. 

Before arriving, they do not take reservations, so don't bother. Also, parking is on the street if you can find a spot. Otherwise there are plenty of lots and garages within walking distance.

Enjoy!

Teavana is a scam. Everywhere in the country from philly to LA, their sales people are trained to push their overpriced/low quality product to you anyway they can. What's even more amazing is the wording and tone that came out of every employees are absolutely idendical. Stay away!!!

We stumbled upon this gem while looking for a quick breakfast on a rainy Saturday morning. This small family-owned restaurant has delicious food, friendly service and a quaint atmosphere! Very unique spot in this busy town of ours!
This place was amazing. Fast service, great food and the price wasn't too bad for what we got. Will be back when we visit Indy again!

Came for breakfast with my wife. Everything was delicious! I got the daily special, which was banana bread pancakes with a salted caramel drizzle topped with candied walnuts and the wife got a spinach, onion, bacon, goat cheese omelet. Will be coming here again!

Went to the grill for Mother's Day I have always hated to go out on that day.  Our  experience was wonderful the food was great and service was exceptional.  Our waitress Nancy was so friendly and attentive.  We never had to ask for anything.  She made our night a great time.  Thanks.
Unique setting, very cozy atmosphere, great drinks.  Hidden gem.

We were able to get a reservation so we are lucky to avoid the lines. We ordered stuffed oyster, crab bisque, fried chicken&waffle, and brussels sprouts. All the dishes are great, and the sprouts is the best we ever have, I would say all these dishes are must try.

Good Cheesesteaks but HORRIBLE service. I had to call three times to place an order cause the girl answering kept hanging up on me. When I got there, I found the cashier had headphones on and was talking on her cell phone, probably why she couldn't concentrate on phone orders. She proceeded to talk on her cell while I paid and when the phone rang at the restaurant. Some of the worst customer service I've ever had.

Love this place! Cinnamon swirl pancakes are amazing. Great addition to CH. employees are super sweet and always nice to my toddler. The service is a little slow at times but I appreciate the care and thoughtfulness that goes into my order and into the service. I always come here when I want a real breakfast with a side of kindness.

Had a group of students with me, and we found this place by accident. The food was good (with many healthy choices), and the service was very good and efficient. We need one (or more) of these in the Pittsburgh area!

I want to give a HUGE Thank you to Apollo's Pizza.  I coach a local middle school basketball team and we had our end of the season celebration today.  They did us a giant favor helping us out and giving us a great deal on 8 pizzas.  They had them all ready to go and the pizzas were very fresh and delicious!  Since we had close to 30 mouths to feed it was great for a local business to come through so perfectly for us.  Thank you!

I've been in Tucson for 2 years now and since I moved here, I've been looking for a hair place that I can become a regular at. Unfortunately I don't think this one is it. While this place is a bit more upscale than the surround hair salons in the area and may be a great place for women's hair cuts I personally didn't like it for men. Pricing is a little more than average for a franchise hair salon running at about $15 bucks for a men's cut. I might try this place again after I try a few others in the area before i settle down and pick which ones I like the best. Even though I think its just an average hair salon, it is actually better than most of the other ones I've experienced.

First, I have a wet butt. Why because the first booth we sat in was wet. I look up and see a moldy vent dripping water. We go to the next booth and it was better. Although I don't think the floor has been swept in a while. So, the food was meh. Really meh. The eggs were not scrambled soft as we ordered. So, we didn't eat them. My daughter ordered Mac and cheese. It was thin and watery with a bread crumb topping. Tasted like a box meal. Then I ordered a sampler which comes with coffee and juice. She brings me a large juice. When I get the bill, I have a charge for a coffee and juice. The manager says, you got a large juice so I'll just give you an adjustment. No, you'll give me what I ordered. I didn't ask for a large. I asked for a juice with my sampler. I've never been here before and won't be back. How would I know this? She says if it's really a big deal for you I'll just take it off. No, it's not that it's a big deal for me. Doing what's right and not nickel and diming me is important. Hell, I'm still hungry. The fact you cleared our plates and two of us left 80% of our food on the plate should tell you something. The coffee was never hot. The pancakes were microwaved. And, so was the Mac and cheese. I only ate my bacon. My daughter had a club sandwich. We probably all should have went with the sandwich. My home fries were gross. I don't think they use seasonings at all in anything. Yuck! Yuck! Yuck! Love supporting mom and pop places but if your food sucks, your service should shine.

Outback is always a favorite place to patronize on a sporadic basis. My first visit at this particular location was very good overall, and our server was great. I typically order the Sweet Glazed Pork Tenderloin, which is always very tasty.

Some strengths and some weaknesses for our first visit.  Starting with the positives:
The breakfast burrito was one of the best I ever had.  You can fill it with options and they were stuffed with high quality cheese, bacon and sausage.  The sausage is to die for.  The iced coffee (nice option) is quite good as well.  My wife had the grilled cheese sandwich that was cooked to a perfect golden brown and again, the cheese was top notch and plentiful (3 different kinds)  The outdoor seating was quit nice, and the spacious.  
Weakness-  The service was terrible.   We waited forever to get seated, and then it went downhill from there.  They may have been shorthanded, but the staff seemed pretty unconcerned and annoyed that they had a lot of patrons which was a bit perplexing.  The biscuits and gravy where pretty crummy.  The gravy was way too thick and biscuits were dry. The tomato vegetable soup was more vegetable then tomato and the earthy flavor was a bit much.  I could see how some might find this wholesome, but for us it was a flavor that didn't sit right.  It is not tomato soup in any way IMO.
I stand behind my four stars in that when it was right, it was fantastic.  The service may have been off that day, so I'm not going to doc them as everybody has an off day.  I look forward to giving them another shot.  I hope I can get past the burrito and try something new...but i doubt it.
My daughter likes this place for her nails.  She gets acrylic and is always happy with the shape and designs.  Good location with plenty of lot parking.

I was kind of skeptical to try this nail place out, but I was in the area and thought I would give it a try.  When I walked in on a Monday afternoon, the place was empty, but immaculately clean.  I asked the staff what the difference between a regular pedi ($22) and a quick pedi ($15), and decided on the regular because I had time.

I sat down and began my pedicure.  I was very impressed the entire time.  All of the tools were clean, and they were very thorough with my feet.  I left with a perfect pedicure, that is still perfect 3 days later!

I would definitely recommend this place and would love to see their business go up!

I was having problems hooking up the digital converter, TV, DVD/VCR combo to my new signal-boosting flat antennae thingy! What to do? I tried hooking it up myself a bunch of times after I brought the antennae home from the Wal-Murrt, but it just devolved into a sad twisting of cables and I got more and more confused-ed. It came to the point where I actually had no TV at all. Hmmm. This was actually worse.

So, missing my good friend, TV, I was happy to find this guy on the internet; his name is Steve Sowell and he seemed to have some good recommendations. I hoped he wouldn't be a serial killer or anything, that he wouldn't charge too much, and that he would hook up all my ISH and get this show on the road. 

So, that dude Steve came over, unhooked all my sad twisty cables, and had my TV  hooked up in 5 minutes while he was talking to me. 

HAHAHAHAHAH!

Oh, I'm such a dork! Then, he spent about 30 minutes getting the rest of the job done with all the best reception and also hooking up the other TV upstairs for better reception, too, and all that.  

WHOO HOO!

Only $94!

This is my first time eating Moroccan food and it has to be one of my favorite foods (beside sushi). I love how everything wasn't too heavy. There was a lot of vegetables and really yummy meat. My favorite had to be the eggplant salad thing (even though eggplants are definitely not my favorite). It was sooooooooooooooo delicious!!! I've never had veggies taste like that. It went very well with the bread.

This kind of dining is definitely DIFFERENT. You're basically sitting down on the floor with a round table. I'm a stickler for proper table etiquette and this place breaks every rule, but it's their culture so I'm open to it. You eat with your HANDS. No utensils. You mix and drop the food with your bare hands onto the bread. But you can wash your hands in the rose water (which smells super intoxicating, i love it!).

There's not liquor there, but BYOB and you'll have a lovely time!

Came in for the first time to fix the band on my Cartier watch and replace the battery in my Balmain watch. The owner and assistant barely welcomed me and seemed to act like I couldn't afford to be in there (my Cartier watch is well over $15k). I asked if they could look at it before I dropped them off and seemed annoyed to walk away from a customer with a Breitling watch. They gave a quick answer that he couldn't fix the band and refused to give any recommendations on where to take it. His exact words were "I don't know any reputable jewelers, but I can't fix it". I allowed them to replace the battery in my Balmain watch but I most likely won't be back due to the poor customer service. I will take my watch to be repaired by a jeweler who can give me more than a minute of their time.

This was a great place to stop with friends and coworkers after work. Service is excellent and the menu is perfect and manageable. I'm pretty sure we've tried everything on the food and drink menu.  It's a can't miss kind of spot and only goes wrong when you fall in love with a particular dish and discover that they rotate things out.  Please bring back the smoked ricotta.

Beautiful setting but WAY overpriced for average Mexican food. Meat was dry and bland. Miguel's, Taco Bus and Poblanos are all better. The servers were quite friendly however my husbands drink order was incorrect as well as an entree ingredient.

I'd give 10 stars if the option existed. Got blown off by another rv service place on camino de la tierra who shall remain nameless. JD at National checked our tires and got us on our way in no time. Many thanks! Highly recommended.

I visited Blondies for brunch and had a great experience. For starters, the Cafe Latte was the most amazing latte I've ever had!! I ordered an omelet which was delicious although I wish there had been a bit more filling to it. The staff was extremely friendly and attentive. Great spot to relax and enjoy a morning coffee. I will say, if you're looking for somewhere to get in and out quickly, this is not the spot as it did take a bit.

I think 3 stars is generous. It's really a 2.5. The staff was really friendly, restaurant was clean, and food was fast. Thats just it. It's fast food. I went with a basic famous star burger and it was identical to a whopper from burger king. This was my first visit to a Carl's jr, and i was expecting a little better. A combo with onion rings cane to $11 and change. So, in par.with fast food.

I LOVE LOVE LOVE Surrey's!  I cannot wait to go there again.  I got the Huevos Rancheros with a side of avacado mash.  Everything was so fresh!  I also liked that they had healthy food along with traditional breakfast items such as french toast and hash browns. Works well for us because I like healthy and my husband likes sweet. I would recommend to anyone.  

Also, it is pretty small in there and they don't take CC.  So Just keep that in mind.
I had a fantastic time here. The food was fantastic and the atmosphere was great. Spent New Years Eve here with my wife, and it's an experience I will always remember.

Simple, homestyle and delicious. Our party tried four kinds of tacos (carne asada, pollo, pescado and camaron), two kinds of burros (bean and veggie), rice and beans, horchata and flan. Everything was fantastic. Don't miss the homemade corn tortillas.

WOW! Let me just start off by saying this place is packed or maybe it was just packed the Monday evening I was there. My husband and I were craving yummy pizza so we came across Pizzeria Vetri and decided to try it out. We had a choice of either waiting 30 minutes for a table that would basically be shared with other people or eating at the pizza bar right away. I didn't mind watching the food get made. It was pretty cool in fact! We were offered sparkling or "normal" water and we chose the latter. 
My husband and I couldn't find a pizza we both desired so we ordered two separate ones: the crudo and the salsiccia. We also ordered a Rotolo because every other table seemed to be ordering one and it looked delicious. To be honest, I think the Rotolo was my favorite perhaps because it was the first time I tried it. 
Now back on topic, the pizza's were edible. Were they delicious? Eh. My husband and I don't exactly like vegetables. We never crave vegetables to be exact. However, while eating the pizza's here, we were both wishing we ordered a salad. I'm not sure how to explain it but the food wasn't exactly greasy but it felt that way. I wish they offered some pizza's that had meat and vegetables on them. For example, a Prosciutto pizza with spinach and cherry tomatoes. Now that sounds delicious! 
The service was A-OK mostly due to being busy. We needed napkins but never got them. We also waited about five minutes for the check to come. The whole experience felt rushed because the restaurant was packed and busy. 
All in All, I don't think I will be going back as I didn't enjoy the experience or find the food worth $60 dollars.
Overpriced drinks, not enough staff, pretty much standard airport bar joint. Nothing to draw people except for alcoholism and the need to travel by air. I have both.

If you're traveling through the Indianapolis area (because, let's face it, why would you be traveling TO Indianapolis ;), plan on stopping here!  

I knew I'd be driving from Denver to Maryland and was scoping out some places to eat along the way.  Reviews on other websites convinced me that I HAD to eat here -- I wasn't disappointed!  The fried chicken was the best I've had, by far.  The mac and cheese wasn't but was still very good.  But if and when I come back, it will be for the desserts.  The selection is amazing!  About half of the entire line is devoted to various cakes, pies, puddings, ice cream, etc. I'm bummed that I only selected one (the butterscotch pie, which was really good).

Here's how it works: get in line and grab a tray and utensils.  Desserts are displayed first and since you can't actually see far enough down the display case to see all the desserts and make a proper decision, you'll probably want to select your favorite from the first half and then another favorite from the second half.  Next, you select your meat then sides (as many as you can handle).  Dinner rolls and drinks are last.  You pay on a per-item basis.  Waitresses refill your drinks.

I didn't see the hours posted on their website but I believe it was something like 11am to 9pm, 7-days a week.  Next time I'm passing through Indianapolis, I'll definitely be stopping here.  I might even plan on going TO Indianapolis just so I can eat here again...

Were there a lot of "elderly people"?  Who knows?  I was too busy enjoying my dessert!

Been wanting to try here since we moved back into the area.  We were the only customers in the place on a Saturday afternoon when college football is on the tvs there. Two guys sat at the bar as we were finishing. 

The place is clean and presentable. Typical sports bar decor with most of the tables being high stools seating. Pool tables take up a main area.  Tvs are clearly visible. 

Service wasnt good.  I wasnt presented with a beer selection.  There is a Leinenkugel sign when you walk in, but they didn't have any. The waitress was polite, but didn't come back to refill drinks or check how our meals were.  We waited almost 30 minutes for our food to come out.

The food was decent.  The bread on the pulled pork and pulled cuban (not authentic cuban but still tasty) sandwiches were fresh and good.  The fries are made there, but either the oil needs to be changed or everything fried was cooked too long. The chicken fingers could have been tasty but also had the same overcooked fried flavor.  The cheese quesadillas were good, and a little spicy.

I'm not excited to return there, but I would as long as I'm not in a rush.

Wow - what a major letdown. I was on business in Philly and decided to try this place based on Yelp reviews. Either I caught them on a really bad day, or Philadelphia is not the place to get sushi. 

The 'Volcano Bowl' sounded promising - tuna tartare in a bowl of avocado. I've had tuna tartare at many different places, and this was by far the worst. Tartare is supposed to be chunky and juicy from the flavors of soy, lime juice, ginger, etc. What I received was reddish pink paste with zero flavor. 

That was my appetizer, and I knew at that point I had made a mistake coming here instead of trying a burger at Village Whiskey. But I had 2 signature rolls coming so hoped the meal could be salvaged. Nope - the Paris roll was just OK at best, and my 2nd roll (forget the name) wrapped in cucumber was barely edible. 

Next time I'm in town I'll stick to cheesesteaks.

Look, it's a chain, and you're getting chain food, but realistically the burgers here are pretty damn good and can be as cheap as around seven bucks!

What really makes it for me is the staff though. Everyone here from management on down is really friendly and outgoing without being obnoxiously in your face.

Dropped to four stars instead of five because the donut tower dessert is just GROSS. Seriously seriously bad. :(
I've visited Landmark a couple times since my last review and have not had another bad experience with the service.  It's a chill bar to watch games and grab a drink.

There really isn't much to be said about The Children's Museum that hasn't been said here already. The overwhelming consensus is that this museum is one of the treasures of Indianapolis offering a fun and educational experience for kids and adults alike. I am in complete agreement with this verdict. 

I will however offer a few specific thoughts related to our recent visit. One thing that exceed my expectations was the suitability of the museum for a wide range of ages. We went mostly for our 4 year old son, and he was certainly pleased with the experience. But, we didn't think there would be much to do for our 18 month toddler. We were wrong. There is plenty of appropriate and engaging exhibits for the young toddler as well as for the 8 year old. 

As a parent, we also had plenty of fun during our visit. Even beyond watching our children enjoy themselves, it was also a wonderful museum for the adult-child as well. I highly recommend this museum for weekend tourist as well as the resident day visitor. Keep up the great work!
So Patriots fans give you so much business but you close out half the bar for Eagles fans during the Super Bowl. Lame dude. Lame.
Service was great and lunch specials were good and well priced.  But all pf changs seem to over salt their dishes.  I would return to try other dishes for sure.

This is the second time I've stayed at the Loews--great both times!  The customer service is amazing.  There's 24 hour in room dining and it is actually good and really fast. The rooms are quiet--no noise from other rooms. I got sick during my stay and the staff extended my reservation and made sure I had everything I needed.  I appreciated that they went the extra mile to make sure I was comfortable.  The only thing I didn't like is that the mini-fridge had no room in it for take out.  Also, the doors slam really loudly--it's the only noise I heard in my room.

Decent food. Came here for lunch. Most patrons order food from here to take home to cook, but I'm in town for business, so I decided to have the Bobby Chez fully cooked food. The mini crab cakes special was good but I've have had better crab cakes though.

I went here for dinner when I was town back in February when I was going to a concert in Downtown Boise. This Skipper's is hands down one of the best locations that still exists. The chowder was nice and thick as well as the food being cooked to perfection. The service was nice and I was very excited to eat here. I'll be sure to stop by every time I'm in Boise.

Be prepared to wait. I mean for everything.  The service is lethargic and uninspired.  The bartender looks lost and clueless. The prices are CRAZY and u don't mean that in a good way. $10 for a beef sandwich that pales in comparison to Johnnie's or Al's. The pizza is good, but shouldn't take over an hour for a small thin crust, yet it did. Go here if you just need to kill that craving you have for a little bit of Chicago,  but dont expect too much. It's more like a bit of Buffalo Grove/Libertyville.

Our concierge recommended this place for a late lunch.  We had huge po boys!  My catfish po boy was very flavorful.  The fries that came with it were "meh".  We were happy with what we ate, and we were so full for the rest of the day, we didn't have dinner!  We thought that the prices were okay.  One of the less expensive places we ate at in NOLA, but also more casual.  I would definitely pick this place over the food court at the Riverwalk if you're at the convention center.

BEST MEXICAN FOOD EVER!!  The best service in town. Silvia is the nicest person in the world.  She writes our name on the wrapper ever time we go there.  You can't buy that kind of service.  I get the bacon breakfast burrito every time.

Really bumbed at the service today.  The banker who helped me appeared to be on the phone and was upset we interupted her. When I asked a question she was very rude "is that a statement or a question", wow, I felt like she was my boss not a banker. I finally had to go home and do the work from home, but then the 1-800 number told me that I then needed to go back to the bank to do the work again. There was a line so I left. This branch seems to have a lot of turnover, I remember when they greeted you here by name here and were a 5 star bank, and now it's let me see your ID and I can't help you. I would have gotten real testy, but I need to do business ( for now)  in the future here. I remeber a millionaire friend of mine told me one time, he likes the tellers and will call them sir, but the bankers are like used car sales people. This banker was like that, only a used car sales person would be far kinder.

Visiting New Orleans again after several years, and wanted to visit the Bywater section of the city again. I was glad that I found this fine place again. It was taco night so had a great time with a few friends, and the owners were there. They were very friendly and nice. Good to be away of the craziness of downtown.

This place has excellent sandwiches. I love Italian sandwiches, and I'm native to an area that has mastered the craft of making them--Hartford, Connecticut home of Franklin Avenue Giant Grinder. Anyway, a coworker convinced me to try Mazzaro's via take-out lunch last week. I've already enjoyed their sandwiches on two other occasions since.

The Spicy Sausage and Peppers, the Meatball and the Muffuletta have been my three choices. All three sandwiches were outstanding. First of all, the bread they use is probably the best bread I've ever enjoyed on a sandwich. Moist, a perfect balance between dense and fluffy, and a delicious flaky, buttery crust. The sausage and the capicola are tops--totally authentic Italian-deli style. Their roasted peppers are delicious as well.

They only charge $5.50-$5.99 for all of their sandwiches, an insanely good deal given how good they are.

Went for the buffet lunch today, and it was just OK. Nothing was hot (temperature) and the flavors were mediocre.  For example the Dal Makhani had no spice whatsoever.  There were a few good dishes, Saag Paneer and Lamb Vindaloo (though not spicy).

There are very few Indian buffets in this area so it will fulfill your cravings, but is nothing special.

Another perfect albeit short stay here.

It's nice to come back and see familiar faces of happy employees that remember you and your preferences.

Stayed in the main hotel with a corner room this time so I had great views of the bay and the sunset.

Rooms are impeccably clean. Service  is spectacular.  

From AJ  at the lobby bar...to Melinda and dave at oystercatchers..to Joan. .Margot and amir at armanis...the service is always terrific ..friendly..and efficient.

There's absolutely  no need to leave this resort  once ur settled in. Anything u need is at your fingertips.

I would recommend this hyatt to anyone who appreciates upscale dining and a luxury  resort.
very clean, lots if carts, fast dryers, large washers, free wifi to get your work done. excellent wash and fold!

Best ice cream on earth. The end. How can something be so delicious? I don't understand it. The flavors are so unique and intensely accurate. Lavender honey, salted caramel, and petit four? Who is back there creating these amazing flavors? I can't handle it.

The evening staff woman at the front desk on July 4 was fantastic! She accommodated a request for my family and was friendly and efficient. The room was clean and quiet, with a nice kitchenette. Breakfast and coffee were just okay.

I found these guys on Amazon Local and called them.  They did a great job and were really nice people, too. The carpet was in pretty poor shape and I think it looks great now.  I strongly recommend this group.  Every bit as good as larger, corporate cleaners, and yet more reasonably priced.

Went here for a friends birthday and on a Friday night we were easily accomodated for a party of about nine without a reservation. While waiting for our guests to arrive, we got the bacon grease popcorn!! Spicy and fatty, it tasted just like fresh cooked bacon. I split a roasted chicken special with my friend and that was PLENTY of food. I also picked off a friends plate of the pulled pork and it was AMAZING. The three different BBQ sauces were all amazing (mustard base, ketchup base and a vinegar base). Prices were reasonable, beers were good and had I could, I would have kept stuffing my fat face. I hate going to the same place twice, but I WILL be back here!

Made it to Luke's for dinner and the crabmeat ravioli is AMAZING.  However I'm knocking off a star because the place was a zoo.  

The next table was a 50th birthday party of 9 adults; one of the women was literally yelling at the top of her voice.  With tile/hardwood floors and tin ceilings, the volume in the restaurant almost ruined our meal.  It was exceedingly difficult to carry on a conversation at our table of 5 in between the shrieks next to us.  

Other dishes at our table were the redfish (w/ the crabmeat), the vanilla duck, shrimp & grits, and the shrimp farci.  Everyone thought their food was lovely...if only the atmosphere had been as nice.

I sat for 30 minutes before being acknowledged. It was 15 minutes before close only because I sat at the ofallon store for 45 minutes before they sent me to a corporate store. People behind the desk were ducking heads. The people at the kiosks all avoided eye contact, one pretended to be on his phone, 3 cashed out. One was in the corner texting. There were only two customers in the store. This place doesn't know the first thing about customer service. I will try to upload the video of all this going on.

We went for first time today at 5pm 
1st host sat us down and nobody came for 15min as i asked a waiter to be our waiter we were seen talking to him when he was rushed off and told that shes got this then left to get a waitress who finally came to rush our order out of us then disappered again we were just about to get up when our drinks came so we said lets see how this goes 
apps good 
salads good cesaer great
Johnny ok steak good but chicken dry 
soup minastrone good but cold and waitress didn,t have cheese then disapeared again
we also had Italian trio, good  
So lets see food good but not handled correctly
We got our check before we were asked if we were finished or wanted desert witch we did, so when we said something to her she just said sorry so we just said forget it then she dissapeared for 20 min this time, really ,never got a refill yet so when we asked for teas to go she came and refilled our table glasses, really ,however now we were laughing 

Wait staff needs to be retrained or fired  

That said will I go back.   Yes but not untill I read better reviews on yelp. yep

I was really pulling for this place and wanted to like it because it's some what close to my house.
First, the good: The presentation of the food was appealing and made me excited to eat it. The variety and flavor of the salsas were complementing to our meals, and the carnitas were moist and fried to perfection.
Now for the opportunities for improvement: The chicken in my quesadilla was WAY TOO SALTY and the "fancy" sauces they added on top were overbearing with a sweet tangy flavor. Not to mention they were selfish with the guacamole. The burritos were alright but a little on the small side.
*Note to restaurants-If you're going to charge $10 for a simple chicken quesadilla then load up on the meat and guac.
Overall this place was just okay and I was disappointed by their menu.

Terrible.. asked for delivery, was told they would deliver but received a call 5 min before it was to arrive, saying they don't deliver and that I'd have to pick it up. Mind you, we can't just leave work (hence the delivery) and clearly the order had been made. Just seems like it would've made more sense to just go on with the delivery and advise us that we are out of their delivery zone even though we've receive deliveries numerous times. Apparent I'm located between 2 locations and neither want to deliver.

Both my wife and I ordered soup at the same time; our bowls came out 10 minutes apart.  My wife's soup came with a piece of aluminum foil in it.  She sent it back and requested another bowl of soup.  We were promtly charged for that second bowl for her...SERIOUSLY!!  My wife ordered linguini with meatballs.  The meatballs were passable but the linguini had not been drained properly so her sauce turned into soup.  First time in over 20 years I have not tipped at least 18%.  This place is in dire need of training and management.

So I made a run to Soulard's Spice shop on Valentines Day, to pick up some spicy goodness and was struck with the desire to eat something good.  And not some street fare meat on a stick for 4$ good food.  While there are times for that, this was not that time.  So being in a great foodie area I recalled a previous visit to Sage for my bday a few years back and remember having a sandwich that had pork, cheese and a fried egg. That was all I remembered and all of a sudden I was focused. So I made a mad dash to Sage with complete tunnel vision.  

So I walk in around 3pm and the place is fairly dead.  I pony up to the bar and the bartender gets me a menu. I already knew what I wanted, but thought I would at least ask for it by its proper name.  They hand me the menu and it's a dinner pre-fixe menu for Valentines Day!  My heart sunk as I sipped on a freshly poured Malbec, thinking my dream would be destroyed.  So I asked the bartender is this the only menu, and he responded yes as it was the holiday.  I responded with a "that sucks" and described my craving.  He responded with "I can't deny a man a cubano(sp?)!!  Let me ring that up for you".  Bless you my man... Bless you!!

Over all, the sandwich was all that I remembered and more.  Pretty much perfect.  The first bite was emotional to say the least.  You know when you have a taste for something and you get it in the exact way you dreamed it? This was that occasion.. The wait staff and bartenders were extremely friendly as I was the only one at the bar and they were very accommodating.
We had such a great time on the tour! You have to do it when visiting St. Louis it was informative and fun and a free beer at the end!

The bus was  comfortable and driver was really nice. But I couldn't get access to its internet. I told to the driver and he called to their office but they said there is no problem. I had counted on their Internet to do some of my works.

Bar and grill inside the Silver Legacy, but technically it's in the El Dorado (shrugs shoulders).  In any case a great place to grab some chow, be it a delicious burger (Try the Blue Cheese Burger), wings, or pizza to name a few options.  Large bar to sit at, and plenty of micro brews.  Happy hour from 2-5pm with $2.00 pints and special priced wings, nachos and others.  A number of flat screens to if you need to find your perfect sporting event.  Live bands are usually on tap for the evening around 7-8 pm. Unfortunately food service stops around 9pm even though the bar remains open til the wee hours.  If you're in the Silver Legacy and/or El Dorado in Reno - drop in.

We went here for Easter Brunch. This was one of the few places we could find online. The location on the northside was full for reservations. So we called the downtown location and they had openings. 
We arrived to a nearly empty restaurant at 12pm. The food was bland and not seasoned at all. The prime rib was dry. The best thing they had was the french toast. But they served one slice cut in half at a time. 
It was really disappointing. I ordered a mimosa. It was made pretty well that I didn't mind paying another $1 for a second one. The way the menu read (which was a special Easter menu) was refills were $1.
The waitress acted angry when we challenged the way the menu read and being charged full price for a second one. I watched her stand near the kicthen and aruge with the manager. She came back with some lame excuse and said she was not able to adjust the bill. At that point, we asked to speak with the manager. He came over and spoke with us. He stated the intent of the menu wording but that was not going to work. I would have not ordered another one at $6.50 but at $1 I would at least enjoy that. Because the food was less than ok.

Pricey? Yes.
Quality? Yes.
Knowledgeable Staff? Yes.
Great Customer Service?  Yes.

I don't necessarily go to buy clothes, but they have hard to find products for men that are really quality.

Good place if you can afford it and you know what you want.

B. Major Grade:  A
Tasty food and super friendly service! Stop here if u r looking for a cozy spot to chill!

I'd like to reiterate what the title of this business is. Lama dog tap room AND Bottle room. Your employee Alex is ridiculous and blew up on me because I bought a 6-pack with a paid sticker on it and was drinking the remainder of a beer. When I was drinking, he proceeded to tell me I was lucky I was with the another business, otherwise he'd confiscate my beer. That's what a bottle room is. When I order and buy, I can drink - whether a 6 pack or a bottle of bootchcraft. If you don't want to be a bottle room, change your policies and name.

Best jeweler in town!  My husband and I have been buying from precision diamonds for almost 15 years. Moses is awesome and really understands what you want and if you give him a little time you won't be disappointed with your repair or design. Great family and I recommend them to everyone!

My husband is from Philly and LOVES Italian so when we came up from DC for a  weekend of fun, where else would we go but South Street?! He selected the place and loved that it was the oldest family owned Italian restaurant in the country. We came to Ralphs with another couple and we all loved it. It was crowded and tight but the great service and delicious food made up for it. I had eggplant parmesan which was some of the best I've had in the U.S. The wine was great and our server was so funny and charming. Good food, great service, what else do you need? Oh but remember it's  cash only, which was a drag but we knew about it in advance so came prepared.

Run away! These are slumlords, slapping some marble counters and stainless steel appliances into old, rundown buildings so that they can cash in on the boom city money. 

--They tore out our bathroom sink without warning and then left it like that for over a month. Who knows if they ever fixed it -- our lease ran out and we moved out with it still unfixed.

--Our ceiling leaks poured water everywhere whenever it rained, for months. No fixes ever, just mold blooms everywhere.

--Our heater broke while I was due to give birth and they took a month to fix it. I had to wrap my newborn up in winter coats for weeks while huddled inside this awful apartment building.

--They are jacking up the rent by 33% long before the renovations are done, so if you must live here, avoid for a few years until they're done. Otherwise you'll be paying for amenities you're not getting. We had no pool this year and you have to dodge construction everywhere.

I stopped at Gelateria Del Leone on a Wednesday afternoon for a quick little afternoon pick me up.  I ordered a small cinnamon gelato.  It's a cute place and I have been before and enjoyed it but on this day I wasn't feeling it.  The cinnamon gelato had some ice crystals in it.  This led me to believe maybe it wasn't so fresh? 
It doesn't help that I have had the Vietnamese Cinnamon ice cream at Clementine's Creamery two times now and it blows me away.  This paled in comparison.  Sorry Gelateria.  I also felt like the selection looked a little sparse...

Go by the side to see the aquarium; the food is not worth it.
They seem to be understaffed; different people seem to have different functions and bringing and opening a bottle of wine was a bit ceremonial. Once things got going it was more or less fine. 
All the appetizers came but not the child plate ordered. We had to ask for it.
Then, in the middle of the entrees, a second order of the child's plate showed up.
Food appeared generic, buttery and heavy. Deserts were fine: molten lava chocolate and key lime pie.
Some bottles in the wine list looked interesting but did not have information on the vintage. We hit a good bottle of Burgundy, a minor consolation for a mediocre meal.

Stopped in for lunch - delicious! We had a wonderful waitress as well. Greek salad was excellent - maybe a little too much olive oil. We had the shrimp, spanakopita, tiropita, and a blt gyro. Everyone was very happy with their meal! Order the tzatziki to go with the spanikopita.

So new owners took over the place or new management. It's now called Que Pasa. Based on the name change and new sign I decided to give it ANOTHER try. This time I was not disappointed, food was good. Good prices and good service. Thank goodness whomever took over did. It's much better than before. It's not gourmet or anything but it's decent Mexican food. Under the new name it's already made vast improvement. Hopefully it will just get better:)

Mmmmmm...a unique rich and creamy  soft serve ice cream!

My friends and I had received a coupon from the Des Peres Movie Theater for 2for1 Dottie's Flavor Burst Cone.  The picture looked so delicious I had to try it.  My friends said no way would the product actually turn out like the picture on the business card.  Ye of little faith, I finally went to Dottie's with a friend and the soft serve flavor Burst was AWESOME!  I recommend the "Blue Goo" flavor.  It tastes like birthday cake!

Although I didn't try them, Dottie's also had hard ice cream, shakes, concretes, sundaes, ice cream cakes, etc....but seriously, try the Flavor Burst!

Another think I was curious about was that on their business card it read.."saving the planet, one scoop at a time".  I thought they were just trying to be vogue right now because everyone wants to "be green".  But they actually do practice what they preach, go check it out, talk to the Dottie's staff and see for yourself!
The food was great and the service was wonderful.  There food was made from scratch, tasteful , and made with great care. I would highly recommend them to anyone visiting NOLA.

Pat Borkowski of APEX was the apex of home inspectors!  I am a first time home buyer and don't know much about home construction.  Pat met me and my realtor at the house, he actually arrived early, ahead of us!  Super friendly, Pat walked us through the whole house as he conducted the inspection.  He explained everything as he went, pointing out all the things he was taking notes on and taking pictures of.  His report was thorough and detailed, providing careful and conservative estimates of needed and recommended repairs.  The other reviews here I can only reaffirm.  If you go with Pat Borkowski of Apex you cannot go wrong!

Ed's Rec Room is such as fun place. My friends and I come here to play bowling at least once a month.
