6. 3 pools...cold, warm, and warmer (lol) because it wasn't hot hot to me, because in jersey they have a pool so hot its playfully called the lobster pot! (when the Koreans and others of lighter skin complexion get out the lower half of them is red!) its also a steam room and a dry sauna, both have nice herbal woodsy smells.  The body scrub area is located in the back and is pretty private so that's a major plus, the one in Jersey is open air...they also have a shower that sprays water at you from all sides...be careful, the middle dial is temperature and the top dial turns it on!

All in all I had a good 1st experience, its small but not claustrophobic...I would say its adequate for the price point you pay.  Its not super modern but the showers were cool, locker room was very upscale to me, bathrooms were clean, facility was clean, staff was nice, uniforms were ok, variety of things to do was limited but again for $20 why complain! Once you get over the nudity your fine, just like any gym or anyplace like that you may get your trolls/ gawkers but I didn't really feel much of that kind of vibe.  The Koreans will pay you no attention, its the Americans that usually make these experiences awkward.  I had maybe 1 or 2 guys that kinda gave me the "I'm checking you out vibe" but nobody engaged me, nobody came trying to "talk" to me or be in my face, it was a respectful distance if that was the case.  I did think one guy was trying to flag me down but over time I just think he was very expressive with his hands because every time I thought I saw it, he was talking to somebody else....but I wasn't creeped out like its perv city or anything,I've been more uncomfortable at beach than at this place,  if you get the vibe just be aware and cover up and that's for anyplace!  I'd visit again, and soon...my skin is soft, I smelled good, I relaxed and I slept so friggin good that night!!!

Their tacos suck and really long wait for food which doesn't make sense to me because the meat taste like it was cooked last month and stored in the freezer. That being said they have a nice ambiance and the staff is really nice.

A perfect place to swoop in, have a brew, and feel just a little better on your way out to your next destination.  

Great ambience, ample bar and table seating, chill vibe, and an unreal beer selection.  

Something about this place screams come here for just a bit...move on and open seats for others.  I don't know what it is, but to stay here for too long is difficult because choosing a beer from their selection is exhausting.  Maybe i'm just weird but it is what it is.

Definitely worth checking out.

After two visits, I feel like a regular already. The waitress recognized me from my previous visit, and by the end of the evening the entire wait staff was playing board games with us. (They were diligent about taking care of other customers, of course.) The acoustics were great, which was important because we were there to enjoy the music. It's fun to order from the creative menu and it's hard not to buy one of each of the hilarious literary t-shirts. This is a great place for smart, friendly, and fun people to hang out!

Been here 2x. Last night 5 of us went. 4 doing wine flights. It was happy hour Friday which is $2.00 off a $9.00 glass of wine. Now if the pour was good this would be fine but when the pour is way less than a 1/2 glass of wine, ya feel ripped off. I pay $9 or more for my fav glass of Chardonnay @ a restaurant & get a full glass. Just a little clarity. The wine flights are $9.00-10.00 but u get 4 choices, not on the happy hour deal. My favorite was the white wash but the other peeps liked vignonier.  
Recently we have been doing some local wineries. I have to say this place by far was my favorite. The wine choices they have are impressive & taste pretty good. I have to add here that I am a wine snob. I would not buy a local wine @ the liquor store. But having said that, I think doing the local wine tours are fun!  You pick fun people to hang out with & the wine just tastes better while your there.

I am going to keep this short and sweet. If you are looking for the best shrimp and grits money can buy, look no further. Those beautiful, creamy grits layered under those plump, juicy shrimp with that BBQ-shrimp sauce should be illegal. A perfect combination of creamy, sweet and spicy. Magical. I call it, aptly, food that changes lives.
Coming from big city like Chicago with alot of froyo place,  this place isn't bad. I like the openness of the store and friendliness of the staffs.

Ok... The Doubletree Hotel Broad & Locust Center City Philadelphia was a very nice stay! (Not to mention I was there on holiday visiting family) any way we stayed in this hotel in March 2 011 for 2 weeks! First time at a double tree, every was very nice! The bell men very nice & helpful! Every time we were leaving or entering the hotel they would speak. & give a warm smile. The room was very nice , clean. Two big wonderful comfy queen size beds! The room was very spacious & the view I loved! (They did have a mouse trap hidden under the long desk/ dresser (nice size flat screen) oh back to the mouse trap freaked me out at first But, I did not see a mouse (the whole hotel would have know if I've seen 1) lol. The Merriam Theater across the street,  Mortans, The Grill not even a block away! The shopping was good! Oh & El Vez Mexican restaurant around the corner.  Oh yes &  quiet time starts at 11pm (security will come to your door & give a warning) after that they will put you out lol .. We saw them put a few girls out!! Lol (I'm giving this review from my cell which is tiny, my apologies if any mistakes)

My first time here was decent. It was a large cafe, but few tables. They had more bars than tables to sit at. The bars had an outlet which was handy. I got bulgogi bibimbab and miso soup came with my order. There is only one size, but it definitely fills you up. Like a traditional Korean bibimbab, there are plenty of veggies and rice. The type of meat is your choice. You don't even have to get meat. On the side, there are a few condiments. As a Korean, of course I got the spicy red pepper sauce. But I think it was mixed with something else because it didn't taste like a regular . It wasn't spicy really... more watered down taste and a little sweet. It was weird. Not what I was expecting. 

We had to try out the dessert! It's supposed to be this traditional Korean bingsoo, but it wasnt. The traditional Korean bingsoo does not have whip cream on it... they also mixed the red bean and condensed milk together. So when we asked for extra condensed milk, they just gave us more red bean. They also forgot to put milk in our dessert bowl. The ice was hard and chunky. I was chewing on ice most of the time. I hated it. The dessert is horrible. Highly do not recommend. 

You can tell Bab Cafe is Americanized and not a traditional Korean place. First thing is the music. They play American music at a Korean cafe. I love American music don't get me wrong, but it's a Korean place. You should place Korean music. Second, they charge you for kimchi!!! Korean places usually get FREE side dishes. That's how we Koreans eat!! I couldn't believe they charged for kimchi. Third, the dessert. The whip cream has got to go! The ice wasn't shaved enough, I guess you can say. 

I'd come back, but only for the bibimbab. Nothing else.

customer service is very bad on this place and they are very unprofessional ,arrogant and rude .They behave as if they do not need customers and keep manipulating these yelp bad  reviews left ,erasing it for a fee ..
stay away, it is a complete nightmare !

Allergy Alert!  On Tuesday around noon (half the restaurant was empty) I ordered my usual, Orange Peel Shrimp, which contains no nuts.  I informed the waiter that I had a peanut allergy.  He repeated back the order, including the allergy alert.  When my plate arrived, it was the PFChang allergy plate, so I dug my fork into the food, only to discover that the dish was completely full of peanuts that had been stir fried with the shrimp and were covered with sauce.  This was a dish that could kill me.  I notified the waiter, who removed the food.  When I requested a manager, he eventually showed up and issued a very quiet, and not heartfelt, apology, and comped my meal, then walked away.  I was very disturbed at the lack of sincerity or concern for my health and safety.  If you have food allergies, beware.

As a brand I really do like Holiday Inn and often they are in the mix of my top three brands I choose when traveling with the family. The location is what allures tourist to this awesome location across from Busch Gardens Tampa.

The check-in may have just been the highlight of the few days I stayed. Our family really needed an early check-in at around 10:30 AM and that can be tough to have granted. However, it was and helped out so much. I was not acknowledged as an IHG Reward member and given one, or two bottles of water which is customary. 

The room was accessed with no issues and we quickly unpacked to head out for a day at Busch Gardens. I was not doing a major inspection of the room, but stumbled on a hole in the top sheet and was shocked. We also noticed only two towels and asked a house keeper in the hall for a couple of more. There was also mold on the shower curtain and hair in the bottom of the tub. The A/C ended up struggling to get to a comfortable level. 

One of the best thing the room had going for it was the amount of outlets, there were more than enough even for a family with two iPad's, a laptop and two phone chargers. The room also came equipped with a mini frig and microwave which was great.

I discussed the issues with front desk that said they would look into them while we were out at the park. After exiting a nice man who drives the HIE Van offered to take us right to the gate of BG if we wish and pick up as well. Only caveat was no pick up from 1-4 PM. That really sounded great, but we did not wish to take them up on it with our preferred parking and flexibility needed.

Upon returned to the room the only issue addressed was the towels and they were just set on the sink... not the towel rack which I would expect after not being set up properly to begin with. Okay, they let us in early which was appreciated. But the room was signed off as ready by housekeeping. At this point it was way too late to have anything else done and we needed rest and would take it up with them in the AM.

Our family did partake in the breakfast which is 6:30-9:30 AM. The people manning this area were hard working women and they did the very best the could. But OMG the place was a mob scene as I am sure they were sold out the night before. The layout was BAD!!! Only one run may it difficult to maneuver around. The food was meh, definitely better than nothing... almost.

The issues were discussed with the front desk and we asked for the room to be made up at 10:30 AM to allow the kids time to sleep in and head out later. I ended up running into the GM in the lobby and had a talk with him about mainly housekeeping related items. He said that he was only on the job the last few months and is living at the hotel and working out problems. The Housekeeping Manager was just hired and only on the job three days. He apologized for my problems and took down the room number before departing.

Some how things just all feel apart when we departed the room at 10:30, even telling housekeepers on the floor we were out and it needed cleaning. They said that they were not responsible for our room, someone else was. I contacted the front desk after coming back and room not made up. At this point the Housekeeping Manager was involved and assisting to get it made up. A new shower curtain was put in and new sheets were put on both beds due to the hole, they never asked which bed.

Overall it probably was my worse HIE experience, but not bad enough for a 1 star. I can see that new management is trying. There is the possibility that they could slip, or improve who knows. A two is fitting because there were issues, but at no time did I not see them trying to provide great customer service. I asked and was given an allowance for one night. It was not for a full night as requested, but it was for $50 and additional reward points were given.

I would not come back to this hotel again and take a chance. Current Yelp reviews on this property are for the most part stale giving it a 3 to 4 stars.

3.5 Rating from me and the hubby. He had chicken we both had gumbo and I had bread pudding. My food was good we added a tab bit of salt. I thought I cracked my tooth on something My husband said his chicken was cold. The place was packed, so you will have a wait, they have lots of breakfast items and a $16.00 adult buffet on the weekends, think most came in for the buffet cause it was quicker. They are packed like I said so you may not get a refill if you need one. They had some nice tiles on the ceiling, that I liked.

Greek food! 

Came here for dinner. When you first walk in this place you might think its small but you are definitely greeted by the staff with a warm welcome and discover how cozy it is. The food is phenomenal. They bring out the bread with tahini sauce to every table. We ordered the dips of the day with warm pita bread to share wit the table. I ordered the winter ravioli stuffed with pumpkin. Delish and not too heavy. For desert I shared the chocolate date cake and bites of the pistachio cake as well. Our waiter highly recommended the pistachio cake but both were equally unique and delish in taste. The chef also came around and made sure we enjoyed our meals which also was a plus! You def need reservations for dining on weekends here.

Let's start off by saying how do you mess up a simple fountain drink. The Pepsi was flattttt! Also my meal was the safest thing I could think of since I haven't previously visited the establishment. The food was certainly not worth the money also how can you mess up a basic dish like onion rings, wings and mozzarella sticks. Also before anybody in the table was finish the waitress came with the bill. Nobody goes out to be rushed during their whole meal . That's unacceptable

You can't get much fuller for 4 dollars like you can at Bui's.

What to get- egg, cheese, and...
Steak if you're tryna do it up and be full (6 bucks)
bacon, sausage, or ham if youre happy with any meat (4 bucks)
mix veggie special if youre health conscious (4 bucks) ...but then maybe you shouldn't be eating here in the first place.

Also, get the Bui's sauce!!! Its definitely siracha plus some other ingredients that add to its somehow appealing glowing orange color.

Insider tip: this is the only food cart around UPenn where you can text in your order. Imagine this- sunday morning you wake up with a terrible headache from last night. All you can muster up is... steak, egg, and cheese with buis sauce and salt/pepper. Take a shower, walk over 15 mins later, and your sandwich is done for you. How heavenly does that sound?

I bought a groupon to check this out & once I tried it, ended up(no pun intended) buying a series of 3. It's been years since I had a colonic & the technology has come a long way. It's like taking a shower on the inside. Carol is the owner & is very helpful setting you up & then give you privacy to 'do your thing'
Highly recommend it! Carol is also a very knowledgeable astrologist, which to me, is fascinating as hell. Try this...

The food was typical of anything you'd find at a chain restaurant, which this is. My burger was delicious! All of my coworkers had the Cajun pasta and loved it. They also had bread pudding and loved it. The entertainment was amazing! Service was great. We really had a great evening here.

My new favorite breakfast spot! 

I typically find what I like and stick with it. Here, I order the eggs Benedict. There is nothing traditional about this dish. It is their version of a cuban eggs benedict merging with a spicy biscuits and gravy. It is great!! And it's $6, even better!!

And then I usually have something out of their pastry bin. Haven't had anything I didn't love yet out of it.
We order sushi from this place about twice a week. It always gets here within half an hour and tastes pretty good for sushi delivery! Good prices and fast service. Solid for late office food.

Great burgers and fries with solid bourbon collection. However, still a bit pricy for a Rittenhouse pub. 

That being said, the vibe is chill and the service is reliable. Never have had a problem with food or staff.

New to the area so we were strolling the strip for a place to grab a bite.  The menu looked decent and inexpensive so we'd figured we give it a go.

The interior isn't bad.  Bright colors on the walls and an arrangement of tall Thai dancer statues, flowers and a water fountain greet you at the door.  Dim lighting could be enhanced by some spotlights, but it's ok.  I felt like I was on the Lower East Side in NYC at an eatery that caters to NYU students.

The staff is friendly and the lunch menu extensive.  We ordered some of the specials and were very pleasantly surprised.  The portions were plentiful, fresh and very tasty.  So good we decided we'd definitely return for dinner soon.

We returned on a Friday evening for dinner, hungry and ready to go... keep in mind it is BYOB, but we decided to skip the alcohol.  The place was packed but we were seated immediately.  We then proceeded to order Spring Rolls, Ravioli Soup,the Deep Sea, the Cashew Nut, a Mango Drink and a Lemonade.

The Spring Rolls were savory, crispy on the outside and quite large.  The Ravioli Soup, oh the soup that I was teased with at lunch and had to order a dinner portion.  The broth is so light and seasoned perfectly, the 'ravioli', plump and delicious, with slices of carrots, scallions, broccoli and a little bok choy I believe.  My companion ordered the Deep Sea, a seafood combination which looked amazing.  He ate every last bit which says a lot considering the size of the serving and the fact that lately neither one of us can finish any meal when eating out.  I ordered the Cashew Nut, which as you may have guessed, is their version of Kung Pao Chicken.  Yum, Yum in my Tum.  This was so good I even ate all the bell peppers that came with it.  Not as 'hot' as the Chinese takeout versions I've eaten, but all the more delectable.  Again, very generous portions, service with jasmine rice, my mouth is watering right now.  The Mango drink is good, the Lemonade a little sweet for my taste, and seems to be sweetened with honey, which I do not like.  But it lets itself be consumed.

Overall I am looking forward to going back to Thai Chef and Noodle.  It's good, it's inexpensive, a relaxed atmosphere, not too loud where you can't hear yourself speak, and did I mention?  The food is GOOOOOD.

one of SB's best hole-in-the-wall mexican joints.
people rave on and on about lilly's tacos, and i enjoy them, but Rincon Alteno destroys lilly's taco game along with an entire menu of other yummy stuff. 
TACOS AL PASTOR... that's all i need to say. the same choice of meat in their super burrito is also a killer.
luckily my metabolism is fast as hell, because i just moved two blocks away from this place, and it's not looking good...
The Chile relleno burro is great, the red Chile plate with rice and beans with a sobaquera tortilla Mmmm delicious also de pollo asado and carne asada burros are sooo very good.

I've always wanted to try Snarf's and I came here for lunch during work. They had a special salad--the Snarf's steak salad--and I said what the hey. It was awesome! Like, real, juicy bits of steak, two different types of cheese, and cranberries for some contrasting sweetness. I'm still not hungry and its 8 pm. The location is nice and clean too, I sat outside in the sunshine. I want to try some sandwiches next.

This just happens to be my favorite pizza joint definitely in my top three here in Sparks Reno area! 
Five piece chicken An Rojo's! And then Order any of the pizzas (they don't add a lot of sauce you can taste the difference) And the crust of the pizza is definitely one of the best!

I like La Va for its vintage, laid back atmosphere and tasty treats. Coffee prices are a little on the high end, but I am supposing this is more to cater to the newly gentrified surrounding areas than the regular South Street indie crowd. My husband can't get enough of the Dark Side of the Moon chocolate cake, but I personally am more into the coffee and atmosphere than the chocolaty treats.

LaVa sits at a location still close enough to the small businesses of the area but far away enough that it's not filled with tourists with loud children. I typically see lots of people doing work on their laptops, although I hear they boot you out after a certain amount of modem time, which in a way is both fair and messed up at the same time. 

In general, though, they have a decent selection of food and pasties to tide you over and they're only the second coffee shop I've been in that serves Turkish coffee. So needless to say I'm sold.

American Social is one of the best restaurants I've been to in the Tampa area. Our bartender Cierra was amazing. Her knowledge of the food menu helped my buddy and I find the best burger and apps. Her drinks were on point too.

Been coming here for years... this place would be so good if they could only fix their wait staff.    The service here, while has been great at times, overall sucks.  The high school/college aged girls that seem to dominate the staff seem to be more interested in chatting it up with each other, texting, etc than seeing to their customers.

Very disappointed in this place. I had high hopes for this place. Food was decent ( FYI you dont put sauce on a filet mignon). Service was below average. The place is very eye appealing. Not worth the money.

We came here for lunch and decided to come back again for more delicious food!!! We were waiting at the bar for seats for the *infamous happy hour oysters" here. We got a little frustrated because there wasn't a waiting list...people had to stand around and basically ready to fight for seats whenever it got available! The manager stopped by and got a conversation with my Man... My Man shared his thoughts about how a waiting list could possibly make the guest experience better. The manager squirmed a lot, conceded the point, but couldn't promise to change their system... BUT... Then he came back, said they'd had a cancellation for a table, and gave that table to us :-) He even came back by later w a complimentary appetizer. That's New Orleans hospitality! It's not just the restaurant, it's not just the food, it's the people that make the experience so special!

Came for brunch with my family last Saturday. Americano has a great selection of brunch food and you can also order from the tapas menu. 

In short, hip atmosphere and tasty food. 

The 2 for 1 mimosas were nice, but they try to trick you on the pitcher - $30 for  "pitcher" (it's a carafe) of flavored mimosas. The serve told us that the carafe holds 6 mimosas. So that's roughly $5 per flavored mimosa. The 2 for 1 deal (all flavors included) is $7 which means $3.50 per mimosa. Never been to a restaurant where you are actually charged more per item for a pitcher. 

Ranking of items we ordered:
Chicken and waffles (must have!!! Mmm)
Nashville hot cauliflower with buttermilk blue cheese (wow! Not a huge cauliflower fan but these are great. Could eat every day)
Brussels sprouts (couldn't stop eating) 
Potato bravas (solid dish) 
Fried manchego cheese with blackberry jalapeño jam (food, but kind of bland. Jam should be more spicy) 
Croquettes (odd combination of flavors, wouldn't recommend)
Excellent tour company!!!  Very knowledgeable and helpful.  I took the cemetery no 1 and courtyard tour and learned a good deal of information.  Definitely recommended

La Va is having an identity crisis
WHY they would ever think that starting up their "late night table service" was a good idea is beyond me...   One of the main things I loved about this place is that it's open late (10pm) and other coffeeshops nearby usually aren't. I live around the block, so I've seen it full in there even late at night... especially since the Penn bus and SEPTA bus stops right outside.  Now, 5:30pm and later thursday through saturday there are lights dimmed, candles on all the tables, and a new mediterranean dinner menu. I can understand a willingness to try a new thing, and I appreciate their bravery in that respect, I just don't see a need for it in that location and, so far, I don't see clientele for it either...  whenever I walk by now at night it's pretty empty in there.  They are right across from a bar/restaurant, right next to a very nice little BYOB restaurant. I don't know.. I just feel like if you're a cafe, you should stay that way.   I want my late night espresso and I don't want to now have to sit down and tip a server to get it. 
Off to Good Karma I go (also open late)! Sorry La Va...    I still hold strong my belief that you make the best chai lattes, though. You just can't satisfy my late night cravings anymore and I have to take away a star for that.

Love this farmers market. Lots of kind vendors that care about their products. If you're in STL and like a good farmers market this is a must stop. I have too many favorites to list. Parking can be a bit annoying but it's well worth it.

Cash only seemed to be the theme around Orleans, so that part wasn't surprising.  
The presentation of the food was nice.
Flavor was just OK, nothing to brag, I think I'd go back.

They are as good as it gets. Charlie and his staff know cars but more importantly they know customer service. I have worked at foreign car repair shops and understand the difficulty it entails, especially on a 25 year old car.  They made sure it was fixed properly and that I was taken care of. Thanks!

one of the best burger joints in town. I've ordered multiple items on the menu and have yet to be disappointed. Their beet salad, fried Mac n cheese bites, fried pickles, and the Woodstock burger are all yummy and their honey mayo sauce will rock your socks. I'd put that sauce on anything, you could drink it with a straw. Not to mention they have amazing truffle and sweet potato fries! Only downfall is that they're pretty pricey for a burger and fries, however you will leave there stuffed and you can't say that about a lot of pricey restaurants in Nashville.

This is literally a one stop shop of some of the best Asian cuisines. Japanese? Korean? Thai? Yes. Yes. And yes. My sister and I sat at the bar and ordered the Korean fried chicken, hoedeopbap, titan roll and nemo roll. 

The Korean fried chicken are some of the best I've had. Though We got the spicy option,  it wasn't as spicy as I'd hope, however the owner said they could definitely make it spicier for us. Totally accommodating, I love it! Side note, if you plan to order these, be sure to order these first and early on bc they take a while to make. But it's worth the wait. The crispness of the skin and juiciness of the chicken is to die for. 

The hoedeopbap is a bowl of rice with assorted raw fish, cucumbers, lettuce, and carrots with a side of spicy sauce. Warning. The bowl is HUGE! This is definitely a meal in itself. It's a very light and refreshing bowl. We had to take most of this home since we were too stuffed on everything else. 

The titan roll and Nemo roll were both delicious rolls packed with flavors. Again, these rolls are also huge so be prepared to take two bites or stuff it all in one, either way, you won't be disappointed. 

Aside from the huge projected tv screen on the wall, one of the other many cool parts of this modern restaurant is that they have a sauce bar. All the sauces you can imagine. I'm a sucker for a good dipping sauce so instead of constantly bugging my waiter/waitress, I definitely do not mind being able to make my own concoction. 

The owner, Michelle, was a pleasure to talk to. Her suggestions were on point and I look forward to my many visits there. Dessert is a must the next time I come!

I would have loved to write a positive review about this restaurant, however, the hostess at the door did not give us the opportunity to do so. I have never been treated in such manner. She shoved us out the door and behaved very hostile towards me and my group of friends. As a client, I recommend that you treat your customers. If this were my restaurant I would not tolerate a staff member who rages at clients, instead of handling the situation in a discrete manner. Never coming back.
Great place for some yummy and authentic food. Service was great and the place was clean!

My absolute favorite place to go to for great drinks! They have a drive-thru and a sit in area, also an outdoor patio. Owned by a cute couple who knows the names of everybody who walks in and when they're not around they have the friendliest employees I've met! I've never once been greeted without a smile. They have great homemade goods like muffins, cake etc. I highly recommend the frozen matcha tea or frozen hot chocolate as for they're the two drinks I always order, but they can make about anything and I've heard everything is delicious!

No one speaks very much English and unless you order one of their set combos they have no Idea what you're saying. For what you're paying it's great. The chow mein is really filling. I like the sweet and sour chicken too.

Ashley is truly the best pet sitter we have ever had. She takes such great care of our babies. They are comfortable and well taken care of when we return from vacation. Its is so comforting to be able to go away and know that our family is in the best hands and being loved and treated well. Thank you so much we really appreciate all that you do.

Hotel is beautiful- like a Wes Anderson film. Had a lovely time until we received two noise complaints from our neighbors. It was 7:00pm. The hotel absolutely ruined our night and what a shame we apparently ruined someone else's. Then, in the morning we could literally hear our neighbors on their phone and make out the entire conversation through the adjoining door. There is no way we were that loud, it was just that you can hear everything through their terribly designed doors/walls. Don't stay in this hotel if you'd like to have a evening without disturbances. Will never recommend this hotel until they remedy their noise problem.

My boyfriend and I wanted to try out something new today and he told me this place just opened up!! We were greeted immediately when we walked in ;) Our waiter took the time to explain the Pho Options as this was the first time my boyfriend was getting the XLarge option! The waiter even brought the bowl out to show my boyfriend! I ended up changing my mind and getting the Pad Thai with chicken. It was delicious :) we definitely plan on coming back!!

I went last Friday night. Typically places in UCity I don't bother with until the college students go on break. So I snuck in for a margarita and something with beans...I know bad combo. Any who, way too much ice in my shaker ,which. They do bring to the table. I scooped out the ice with my fork, guess what! To be kind it was 1/3 full. Where was the 1800 tequila I paid for? Idk....but the sip I did have was tasty. 
I'm vegetarian so I went for the black bean tacos...beans were bland. Which is disrespectful to Goya. I bought an appetizer, some foolishness called bubble bread. Don't get caught up in the alliteration like I did. It's garlic bread with some shredded parmesan on it. If that's what you want, go for it, but it tasted like frozen bread that was popped in a toaster oven. 
Otherwise...the server was kind. 
This place is designed for college students. They will eat and drink anything. 
In closing...Copa = Tom Foolery
2 stars cause at least they bring the booze to you fast. Only waited 3 minutes for my drink.

I am sorry but a gyro is not a pretzel burger. Spent 22.00 for lunch and had 2 beers and 3 dry slices of meat, a lot of lettuce and a flavorless tomato. 

I was contacted by the owner who is going beyond my expectations to correct a bad experience. That in itself, gives reason to return and change my rating.

Authentic Philly pho. Some of the best food in general. I could eat this every day especially with that huge variety of food and drink. If you're the owner and reading this, open up a restaurant in NYC. Better yet, let's partner up. We'll take it all the way to the bank!

Was looking for something new around the W 86th Street area and found this slice of India! The staff at this establishment are very welcoming and extremely accommodating. The presentation of the entrees was great from the sizzling chicken to the traditional dishes. The portions are well sized as they come with Basmati rice. Slightly pricey, but well worth it!

The apartment was really nice. My friends and I opted for a two bedroom two bathroom and it was really spacious. Within walking distance to everything. Would stay at a Stay Alfred apartment again in the future.

Have been visiting Frescos for at least 5 years and have never had bad food. Used to live a couple miles away and yes delivery was slow needed to plan ahead. Most of the time we just picked it up. They have the best pepperoni and mushroom Pizza I've had in town, love the fresh mushrooms and the manicotti is wonderful. It's no longer on the menu but they still will make it up for you just ask. I ordered salad (chef) for the first time and it was excellent, very fresh! The only negative is they need one on the east side. You can't even compare to other franchise Pizza places they don't even come close to the freshness and taste.

The best parts of this restaurant are the atmosphere, both in and out on their covered patio. Unfortunately, it's not quite distracting enough to hide the numerous, tough pieces of meat in the entrees. It was as if the meat had been cooked twice as long as it should have been. I ordered the pulled pork sandwich, and I kept pulling strips of leather out of my mouth. My boyfriend ordered a half rack of ribs. There was almost no meat left to eat, as most appeared to had been dehydrated, and shriveled to near nothingness. The side items were ok, but nothing special.  If this place were half the price it is, I still would t recommend it. It just wasn't anything worth bragging about.
I have bought many fine used items in this place. The dress shirt and and slacks sleletion is great. On the other hand I am not found of the denim pants selection.

Momos has great service and good food with decent prices. There's also belly dancing most nights during the week! The menu has lots of variety so there are lots of options to choose from. The lamb kebobs are good. The shrimp and grits is also very good. The chocolate phyllo dessert is ok but a little too crunchy for my taste.  The chocolate creme brule' is very rich and delicious.
Note to jordyn, it's not very welcoming to address someone when they walk up with "what do you want" a smile and warm welcome will take you far in life!
AMAZING - best mediterranean / Greek in Philly.

fast and friendly service.

for the indecisive (read: me), there's a nifty little mini four scoop sampler option for $4. win.

there's a old-fashioned feeling when you walk in, and it's quite spacious. at 10PM on a friday night, it was hoppin'. they have the regular flavors, but that's not why i ventured all the way there. it's all about the specialty flavors!

my mini four scoop sampler was:: steen's molasses oatmeal cookie, brown butter pecan, red velvet, and lavender honey. everything was so rich and creamy, and i wasn't disappointed. i was apprehensive about the lavender honey, but it ended up being my favorite. i'm not the biggest red velvet lover, either, but the ice cream made me a believer. the molasses oatmeal cookie really tasted like a cookie in ice cream form, and i'm a little sad to report that the brown butter pecan was just okay--not disappointing, but not unique, either.

i also had the pleasure of trying the skyscraper: cookies and cream, chocolate, and vanilla ice cream layered with caramel, hot fudge, and crushed oreo cookies. served with whipped cream and a cherry on top. its name comes from the fact that it's creole creamery's tallest creation..and, i'd argue, probably one of the most delicious.

I attempted to go in here while waiting for a flight and the staff were incredibly rude. They claimed to be fully booked-up even while it was basically empty (1-2 customers) and most of the staff were just lounging around and continued to do so right up until I got on my plane, since my gate was right next door. They clearly had people available; I think they just didn't like the looks of me or something, which is, to be honest, pretty comical. Just for the record, I look like an unkempt redneck, but I'm super-loyal and tip heavily, so sucks to be you guys. 

Plus the prices are ridiculous. And I'm a New Yorker, I am well-accustomed to things being gratuitously expensive, but $55 for a 25-minute chair massage? Oh honey, no. The least expensive thing in there are the massage chairs--yeah, like the ones you pay a dollar for three minutes in at the mall. And even those were a dollar or more per minute. 

Also, when you're lucky enough to actually have shop space in an airport, it is just really bad planning to put the massage chairs right in the front window, where it's noisy and everyone is staring at you as they go by.

The French Press, Anacapa location. Hand crafted/Brewed coffee took less than 5 minutes and turned to be a bad one. Sorry guys but when you offer and Ethiopian, hand crafted coffee from a fancy pipe at market price I can only expect a great cup, instead a got a very weak one, even the color was off. i don't know if the barista used the wrong proportions or that is their style? I will never know because not going back. I was just visiting SB and "needed" coffee. That coffee + 1 croissant =$9.30 , i though that was too much too...isnt it? 
After this i went to try another relatively new place and that was plain drip coffee, but a lot better.

Second time coming in. A little quieter than last time but that's probably because its the week following a holiday. (We went the week after Thanksgiving) Food didn't disappoint and we had the pleasure or having the same server , John P. Super nice guy. Again, love the food love the service! If you haven't tried- goooo! What are you waiting for? :)))

GREAT FIND!!! We wanted to try something new and had always noticed this restaurant so we made reservations. When we arrived, we were expecting a bar atmosphere and were delighted to find a very inviting, intimate dining room. We were sat at a table right next to the large aquarium, which turned out to be designed by the creators of "Tanked"! It was mesmerizing to watch during our dinner. We loved it, and all the Guy Harvey artwork was beautiful. We will definitely go back!

Our wedding in Santa Barbara in early September was absolutely perfect!! Our ceremony was at the beautiful mural room in the Courthouse and then we hosted our reception at the Rivera Mansion University Club. We planned a small, out of town wedding so detail coordination was important to say the least; working with the mansion for the reception which included many additional items including linens and tables and silver and glasses, etc. helped eliminate several frustrations and time constraints. Communication with the mansion in the months preceding was very cordial and on the day of the event the staff was very attentive and friendly. The mansion staff, furthermore, as you would expect, is well acquainted with many wedding service providers around town - DJs, florists etc., - which can help assist in the booking process for outside vendors. The event space itself is very beautiful and perfect for a classic wedding setting. We opted for a cocktail hour on the grass (the patio was otherwise occupied for an internal event) and the dining room was warm and welcoming which can be made to fit a large or small attendee level.  We look forward to coming back to Santa Barbara and the mansion to revisit our wedding memories.

This place is amazing. Their prices are lower than Petsmart and Petco and the ladies who work here are insanely patient and kind with my animals. 

To address an older review, they required shot records and vet info when I brought mine in. They also required it over the phone when scheduling someone else while I was there, so I think it may have just slipped that time. 

They're very flexible with scheduling, good with cats, and one of their groomers is ISCC certified, which is rare in this area. (This means for those of you who like more than a shave down or want breed standard, you're going to get exactly what you want here). 

The shop is clean, there's lots of parking, and they always have really cute pet toys and treats. (Also, their antlers are the cheapest I've ever seen, pro tip for those with heavy chewers). 

They won't disappoint!

I was really looking forward to eating here and left fairly disappointed. Went with my cousin & his partner and did the the '4 courses for $45' menu option on a weeknight last week.  As expected, it was packed.

Besides the foie gras soup, there really wasn't a 'standout dish' which any of us ordered.  I had a sip of the foie gras soup.  Interesting initial taste with a subtle taste of the foie gras &  one of the better finishes to a soup I have tasted in quite a long time.  

What was disappointing was that so many of the dishes were underwhelming or even disappointing.  The claims with oriecchiette & fennel that I ordered had clams that were quite gritty.  Simply hadn't been cleaned sufficiently.  I wouldn't mind that if I ordered a bowl of steamers at a seafood place that had a few sandy clams.  Not a dish where you have several small neck clams where every one but one was gritty/semi-gritty.   

Chicken with brussel sprouts & sweet potatoes (overcooked and not well flavored), mascarpone with coffee granita & chocolate (too dry),  and lamb belly (again overlooked) were also underwhelming/disappointing.  

Seems like they are almost trying too hard at this point & working out the kinks especially in the kitchen.  Wouldn't be surprised if they won't have things working a bit better in the kitchen in another month or so. 

Wait staff was very professional and attentive.  Surprised though that our waiter recommended a bunch of the underwhelming dishes including the claims & oriecchiette.  

I also liked the layout & design.  It was loud but not overwhelmingly so.  Easy to hear dinner conservation at routine sounds levels.  It was nice not to have to yell or literally get right in the face of the person you wanted to speak with.  

If you want to try this restaurant, I would hold off a bit until they potentially work out of the kinks.  Maybe try it after Thanksgiving in early December.

FYI:  They close at 5:30pm Monday through Saturday and they close at 4:00pm on Sunday.

Sure, the quality isn't always top-notch, but I tend to look at what I pick out (at least the stuff on the self-serve tables) before I put it in my basket.  And at their prices, I have no problem throwing out some stuff that's gone bad.  Small onions are 5lb for $2, so if a few go bad before I can get through all 5lb, oh well.  Half the time anything that goes bad was good to start and I wasn't able to go through it all.

It's not just good prices, but it's also bulk produce!  It's like Costco, but just for produce!

I spent $45 there today.  My biggest complaint would be that they only take cash.  The whole lack of receipts thing bugs me, too.  They do have an ATM there, though, so it's not a huge problem.

Honestly, I don't think the traffic is a reason to knock off stars for PJ.  It's not their fault.  There is a light right there - if you're going to PJ, turn at the light and then go into the parking lot.  Or drive past, go downtown and turn around in one of the parking lots and come back from the other direction.

I like going to PJ.  I'm lucky that I'm also within walking distance.  It's worth the walk.

This place is beautiful.  They have everything from indoor/outdoor plants, gifts, home decor, toys for kids...even cute wine-in cans!  Emily was fantastic and helped my boys and I choose a gift for my daughter and a variety of plants for our new home.  She was knowledgeable and thoughtful-we appreciate your help Emily!  

We will be back in the spring for outdoor plants!

I've probably been here 15-20 times. EVERY SINGLE TIME the food is delicious, the service is stellar, the entire experience is spectacular.  All the servers work as a team and everybody takes care of you. They all make you feel like family. Even the owner, Hope gets involved and makes sure that everything is perfect. Sometimes I'm not sure why I go anywhere else. Everything else nearby pales in comparison - and believe me, I've been to them all!
This place is like going to your best friend's house where they take care of every little detail and you feel so at home and everything is so scrumptious - yet you don't have to do a single thing except show up, sit down and enjoy!
There's always something new offered as a special and the menu items are very reasonably priced. 
Sometimes I feel guilty that I'm not paying more for these delectable meals. And that's no exaggeration!

Great for Sun brunch as they have breakfast and lunch items and a decent kids selection.  It's from 9a-2p on Sun.  Not  as glitzy as its sister Cantina downtown but the food is amazing!  Huevos Rancheros is awesome.  Beer and wine only and they charge for chips/salsa - still worth it.  Enjoy!

Excellent, authentic Jamaican food in downtown Trenton. I almost always get the brown stew chicken and am blown away every time. You should also treat yourself to a beef patty or one of the tropical drinks they have behind the counter. I've also had the curry chicken and the jerk chicken. All delicious.

Only took off a star because service is a bit slow and it's not uncommon for them to run out of popular items after the lunch rush. Go early to avoid it.

The service is always great, the food is always really good, Beef O'Brady's is one of the best places around. Their appetizer sampler is really good if you want to try a bunch of different things, and if you like burgers, the OMG Burger is awesome!

What a great idea - attaching a craft cocktail bar to a music venue.  You can walk through from Marathon Music Works, grab a drink , go back hear some music and glide back again when that craft manhattan runs out.  Really nice, bar and high tops and a little patio..  Smashing!  nice friendly unpretentious bartending.
Great sushi and prices. BYOB is always a plus. My wife loves the hot & cold dessert (fried ice cream). Highly recommend.

great place to get keys made in philly.  neighborhood is a little sketchy to walk through but accessible by the very busy washington ave. cashier/clerk was really nice and made my key copies toute de suite.  only cost me around 3 usd and some change.  all-in-all, a very pleasant experience.

Indy is pretty flat so the nice thing about staying at the JW is that you can spot it miles away. It's a great point of reference as you wander around downtown because that massive blue structure is always within view. Apparently, it's the world's largest JW Marriott. It is a new (opened Feb '11), clean and very nice hotel that's connected to other Marriott owned hotels in the surrounding area as well as the Convention Center, Lucas Oil stadium and Circle Centre Mall. You also have a nice walking area near the White State River park. All the aforementioned places are about a 5-10 min walk from the hotel. There's a lot of sports bar type of establishments and steak houses a few blocks away - that seems to be the common theme in that area. 

Pros:
- very new and clean; nice design
- very friendly and attentive staff
- clean room and bathroom; decent bed and soft sheets and good temperature control
- great breakfast at Osteria Pronto
- quiet area near a running/walking trail at White State River Park

Cons:
- no mini bar or fridge (but complimentary bottled water, tea and coffee)
- pricey daily wifi but you can have up to 5 devices connected to it 

The main lobby here as two restaurants - one is a sports bar called High Velocity and the other is Osteria Pronto which is where you can have a $16 breakfast buffet (mine was included with my stay). The breakfast buffet is probably one of the better hotel breakfasts I've had. There's a waffle and omlette station, pastries, oatmeal, eggs, sausage (regular and turkey), the best crispy bacon ever, cereal, fresh fruit and even smoked salmon. Everything tasted fresh and I like that there were lots of healthy choices. The staff here are very attentive! 

There's a also a nice lounge outside of this restaurant with lots of comfy seating. You can also get free wifi in the lobby - I think the limit is 2 hours per day per guest, I think you have to get the password from the front desk. Otherwise wifi is not free and is kinda pricey. 

Oh, there is a Starbucks on the 2nd floor of the JW but the hours are brutal. It opens at 6 am but jeez, I am never up that early yet it closes so early! I think it was 4 or 5 pm...too bad. 

Seems like a safe location as I wandered around by myself and didn't see anything sketchy in the day or night. The area is just quiet. If I were coming back to Indy, I'd definitely stay here again. The hotel is about a  $35 cab ride from the airport (before tip) but there's also a shuttle that costs about $7 that's within walking distance from the hotel (just ask front desk staff about it). 

Overall great hotel!

My family and I have been going to Eats since it opened because it is convenient, clean, friendly, the food is good, and each time we go, we get airline miles because they participate in the AAdvantage Dining Program.  That is a hard combination to beat.  That said, I have rarely been surprised by anything at Eats, except perhaps (rarely) a bad choice in the hiring of a new server - and such people usually disappear pretty quickly.

This particular meal, however, clearly stands head and shoulders above EVERY meal I have had at Eats.  Either they have hired a new cook who understands seafood better than anyone ever has in the past, or they have invested funds in getting someone additional training in seafood preparation, and it has already started to pay off huge rewards.

When we arrived, we noticed two "specials" on the welcoming board that we had not seen before, and they immediately caught our eye.  First was: "Tuna, crusted with black and white sesame seeds, lightly covered with Guinness chili sauce."  That quickly caught my attention and caused me to pause in front of the sign, and then I immediately noticed the other special: "Swordfish, served with a blue crab creole sauce."  We ordered one of each.

When served, they were SPECTACULAR!  My wife's tuna was a sushi-grade slab that was cooked to perfection, almost charred on the outside, but a deep crimson red all the way through to the other side.  The Guinness chili sauce was delightful, with just enough chocolatey, roasted malt flavors to provide a nice counterpoint to the tuna.  This was melt-in-your-mouth good, and my wife was overjoyed (and was almost unwilling to share a bite).

I have always tended to shy away from swordfish in restaurants.  It is hard to find, usually over-priced, and so damn hard to cook that the difference between perfection and something resembling dry Thanksgiving turkey breast is often measured in seconds.  But this opportunity piqued my curiosity because it was only priced at $10.99, but could easily have been twice that.  Years ago, while in the Navy, I was stationed in New Orleans, and came to absolutely love Creole and Cajun foods, so I figured if the sauce was true to its roots, even if the fish was terrible, I'd get my money's worth.  I am very pleased to say this was one of the BEST examples of swordfish I have ever tasted.  The fish was cooked PERFECTLY, somehow managing to be both juicy and flaky, and at least a full inch thick.  The sauce was actually classic Creole - without the coarse spices that Cajun food blasts you with - but accompanied by just enough of its refined French heritage to make you close your eyes and focus on the variations of taste that were assaulting your taste buds.  I was in heaven.  

Our server, Megan, was attentive and prompt, and actually curious about how we liked the two dishes because they were so new she had not had a chance to try either one of them.

In summary, you have (finally) outdone yourselves, Eats.  I don't see how you managed to create two specials on the same night that were truly outstanding, nor do I see how you can surpass this, but I look forward to seeing what is next.  And, should either of these specials happen to be back on the menu again any time soon, I will be there with all my friends.  As my Cajun friends used to say, "You done good, Mon'Ami."

I dare you to find a better bakery and cafe!   This is a locally owned establishment that knows how to take care of it's clientele!  The sandwiches are stuffed full of meat and veggies.  The bread is made in house and is so delicious.  The pastries and cookies are fabulous.  You have to try the Blueberry Bread and the Mountain cookie!  You will be back!   The owner, Patrick, is always on hand to make sure everything is perfect and that the service is fast and friendly.

I've stayed at many Hotels and this one was "ok".  They had a bar service that would wheel in around 5:00 and setup shop.  No good food places near by, and it was very loud outside the Hotel.  Keep in mind this was 8 months after Katrina, so you have to factor that in.   I was just happy I had a nice room, clean, sweet smelling and didn't have to worry about "bumps in the night"
These guys are excellent. They went above and beyond with their service tech Jeromi to make sure we were taken care of. Outstanding service

We discovered this location several months ago.  The staff is incredibly friendly and always helpful.  That said, my review here is primarily targeted at how they label their sale merchandise in the stores.  My partner and I recently traveled here to purchase dog food...we buy Wellness.  Wellness brand is relatively expensive food, so savings are pretty important when you stumble upon them.  We usually buy the 55-60lb bags for three small pups.  When we recently ventured to the store to buy the food, my partner had a $2 off coupon, and we noted when arriving to the shelf housing the bags that there was another $2 off promotion.  Now, I will say this.  In general, when you are in a grocery store or any store that stocks shelves with like items and there is a sale, 9 times out of ten the store will paper the shelves with tags stating whatever the promotion may be.  For instance, in a freezer for Ben and Jerry's Ice Cream (there are at the very least 20 flavors) beneath each flavor is a tag reading some sort of promotion- 2 for $4.99 (you get the picture) and there are at the very least 20 tags denoting each item.   Well the same was the case for the dog food.  A tag about every 6 inches noting the sale...with the smaller bags and the larger bags.  So, in an instance like this we did not read the small print because quite simply, just about every square inch of the shelf was tagged with the promotion.  So, we thought- AWESOME SAUCE...coupon + additional savings equals $4.00 off! YAY.  Well we get to the counter only to find out that we were wrong,  the fine print only referred to the SMALL bags of food, but at the time, the sale tags were everywhere.  I guess the lesson in  all of this is for consumers to read the fine print,  and for stores to be forth coming and to be honest in their marketing,  you cannot always rely on that fact.  I would suggest that this store and others be more diligent in their practices and I will bring my reading glasses more often when shopping Pet Supermarket.

Food was excellent. We had a variety of entries including the the grouper, the scallops, the crab cakes which was all crab not filler. The clam chowder excellent. 
  Our waitress Lori was amazing. She got continuously filled our glasses,got our order correct, knew the answer to all our questions and was overall helpful and pleasant.
Great experience.

So glad Yelp reviews brought me here. Sat at the bar by myself hit dinner. Friendly, attentive bartender. Nice cocktail list. The shrimp risotto was perfection! Creamy, garlicky, perfectly cooked, fresh shrimp.  Would order again in a heartbeat. No outdoor seating but lovely views of the water. Would be a wonderful spot for date night.

Although a bit pricey, definitely worth it. I asked what the woman working would recommend, the plain or chocolate croissant. She suggested almond and when I told her I had never tried it she gave it to me along with the chocolate croissant (for free) in case I didn't like the almond one! Both were amazing!!
Absolutely awesome, thanks. First time here and I would come again, this is a great place. Service was fabulous, and food as well

Typical bait and switch you would expect from a fly by night corner dealership. Don't let the size and cleanliness of it fool you they are scam artists and I know because I've felt with them at park automall. I drove all the way over from pinellas with the intention of finding a newer car and a significantly lower payment that was my goal when MANNY approached me with an almost 600 credit rating and some negative equity in my car all they wanted to talk about was getting a consigner or my interest wouldn't change and neither would my payment.... I understand if someone with a 450 credit score has a 350 payment with a 12-15% interest but I worked very hard to fix and move that needle to where it's at and to sit there and tell me there was noting they could do is complete crap never go here I dealt with CROWN HONDA of pinellas park before and that's where I'm going g back to.

Awful.  Plenty of other places to order food from that have a more customer friendly staff.  First and only time i will ever order from this place.  I live just under 3 miles away from this place.  One night I ordered 2 large pizzas for my family and they didn't show up.  After an hour and fifteen minutes I called to ask if their driver had left and the girl's response was " I am glad you called, we wrote your phone number down wrong so we couldn't get a hold of you to tell you we are not going to deliver your food.  We don't deliver that far."  I asked her why they took my order in the first place and why they didn't just deliver the pizzas regardless and she responded by telling me it wasn't their mistake.  (Please keep in mind...I LIVE 7 MINUTES AWAY.)  I voiced my concern to the manager, informing him that my children are now very hungry because he refused to deliver to my house that is under 3 miles away and he told me that he would call me when they were less busy.  A BUSINESS WHO DENT PUT THE CUSTOMER FIRST AND TAKE RESPONSIBILITY FOR THEIR MISTAKES MIGHT NOT WANT TO BE ONE THAT HANDLES YOUR FOOD.

This place was really quaint however the food was far from first class. The toast was cold, the milk was warm, the pancakes looked barely cooked. The waitress spilled milk on the table and my phone and didn't even acknowledge it.
Food is good.  Bartenders are laid back but cool.  Can get crowded but it's a train station so deal with it.

They were awesome. Chicken in a biscuit was amazing! They made an honest mistake on our order which we weren't even mad about and they went out of there way to make it right! And we weren't even mad to begin with! All our food was delicious and the staff was extremely nice.

Absolutely love this place!  From the amazing pizza, Philly Cheese Steaks, Stromboli, and Calzones, to the excellent customer service (when they can get to you), this place is great!  I rated four stars because there usually is a little longer wait for service as the place always seems to be understaffed.  This in no way takes away from the customer service you receive once they have a chance to get to you though.

Pretty legit Mexican food. The salsas are extremely spicy but if you like that you're good to go. They don't have chips though:(. If you're like me and like gringo Mexican food then go somewhere else, but if you want some legit tacos with HOT salsa this is the place for you.

I'm glad I finally got the chance to stop by here on my last trip to STL and that it wasn't terribly crowded. The custard is very thick, and a mini concrete was enough to satisfy one (not overly greedy or gluttonous) person. I got a concrete with Heath bar bits, and it was delicious. While waiting for my order, I saw an adorable old man drop his custard, and I was overcome with sadness... until he picked it up without issue because the custard was thick enough not to spill. o_O; Can't wait to come here again!

When my bathroom ceiling fell in for the third time in my old apartment, I had a nice chat with the guy who came to fix it. Marc grew up in South Philly and gave me a ton of recommendations on where to get a good bite to eat in the 'hood. You guessed it: among his recommendations was Ricci's. I was eager to try their sandwiches, but they were closed both times I tried to go (their hours are kind of unfortunate). Yesterday, I finally made it there (after making a pit-stop at CVS to hit the ATM, since they're cash-only) with my two friends who were visiting from Jersey. 

The lines weren't too long; I'd say we waited for about three minutes to order. They have an assembly line of sorts behind the counter consisting of four or five Italian guys, a few of whom I'm assuming were Riccis. I ordered a Honey Turkey hoagie (I don't think you get to choose a size... they're all foot-longs) with lettuce, sweet peppers, onions, provolone, and it was assembled with lightning speed. They wrapped up my hoagie and my deli pickle (only $1 for the biggest pickle ever) and handed it to the cashier, where I was rung up promptly and with a smile. 

We took our hoagies and chips home and proceeded to eat them almost as quickly as they were made. We were not disappointed. Although I still prefer Salumeria hoagies, I will definitely be back for another visit in the near future.

We came in late on a Saturday night. Food was on point and I'm always happy to see Excel soda on the fountain. Nice space! One calzone came out first because the other had a production issue, but the delay wasn't long. Ok, here's the best part of the visit: since we were there right up to the last minute, the crew was beginning pre-close duties and were hustling to get it done. The manager, Tony, very professionally and tactfully told he crew to use care so as not to disturb the dining guests. He was so low key about it, but I heard him and it demonstrated that guest experience matters, even at 10:30 on Saturday night. Thanks, SoS!

We are family of newer and used cars with four vehicles among us. Finding a reliable and trustworthy mechanic these days is nothing short of impossible. But we have found such a person! Wensel's Auto is the first mechanic we have dealt with in the past 14+ years that completely puts us at ease and we have the comfort of knowing we are getting accurate information, and excellent job, and the best prices to boot! If you are searching for a mechanic in the area, search no more!!!
Great place, love the sushi burritos. The sandwich is amazing. Great music in the background, love the decor.

Hotels are in the business of hospitality and service. This hotel is OUTSTANDING! Everyone is professional and so NICE. That makes our travel and visit to Philadelphia wonderful after a long day of travel. 

There's a restaurant, bar, and deli which are in the hotel. Again, everyone is so NICE. Service is great! I loved their Cobb salad.

The elevator is tricky, but it prevents strangers and unwanted people from getting to your floor. Make sure that the front desk explains it. Otherwise, you are not going anywhere.

The room is good. The bed is nice. The WiFi is off and on, but the hardwire is great. The bathtub/shower is full but it doesn't match the small bathroom. Be careful! It's small.

I like the furnishings.

This hotel is mainly used by many serious business people. The executive host lounge is really nice. Quiet and have great wireless connection.

The pool is COLD, but great on a hot day. There is a laundry area on the 8th floor.

Close to the public transportation and Reading Terminal Market. We took the train down the street, because it was too hot to walk. We visited the Liberty Bell and the Constitution Center. We also visited the famous Benjamin Franklin home.

I really loved this hotel and will stay with them again!

However, do not stay here if you are expecting Four Seasons hotel.
Very good spot. Excellent food, excellent service. Historic building with plenty of room and things to see. We will definitely be back!
Great place, have been taking care of my family autos for over 10 years. Honest, reliable, and sincere work. Hands down our family mechanic and auto go to site !

I really wanted to like this place, but the food just didn't cut it (and for these prices?!). A very kind employee held the door open for us as we entered, but we were left standing at the host's desk for a bit before someone showed us to a table outside. I noticed immediately that there were crumbs on my plate and napkin. Odd. We were told Sarah would be our waitress, and we did speak to her once before our waiter suddenly changed without warning. I didn't catch his name.

While waiting for our orders, my bf noticed how high the armrests on the chairs were, which made them a little more uncomfortable. I marveled at the price of a milkshake ($7!) and all the other items on the menu.

The bf & I ordered the "blazing" wings, which were not at all blazing and actually quite bland. However, they were hot when brought out to us and had just the right level of crispiness. I thought they were on the greasy side though. These would have been really good wings if they had had any flavor.

We also got the East Loop thin crust pizza, which had a lot of pesto, chicken, mushroom, and red onions. It looked like it had a lot going on, so I was excited... and then put off by the strange texture and aftertaste of the pesto. I really wasn't expecting that. I ate the two smallest slices and was not at all tempted to eat more.

So I probably won't be back. Maybe I would have liked a different pizza or a salad instead of the wings, but eating here again would feel like a gamble. I'd rather stick to Papa John's or Domino's for pizza & wings.


They did play some good music though.
Prices are great and the food is flavorful.  5th Street Benedict was delish, however, the bread of our steak sandwich was literally sticky dough and the steak was tough and fatty.

We ordered from Melt last night though Waitr. There was a problem with our order. After a phone call to the restaurant, they went out of their way to remedy the situation. Sandwiches were delicious, fries crispy and tasty. Loved the Mac and cheese. But most of all the customer service was outstanding! Thanks, y'all!!!!

My boyfriend and his family have been going to Sloan Toyota for years. I have heard nothing but wonderful things about Mohamed and I finally met him today. 

It's true what the other reviews say. He is charming and knowledgable. Mohamed was able to make purchasing a car fear and stress-free. You can expect him to give you an honest opinion and will find the best automobile for your budget. I had one of the best customer service experience I've ever had today. 100% would recommend Mohamed at Sloan Toyota to anyone in the market for a new car.

Best ever. Very minimal waiting room time, fast, brilliant service, in room payment, all the latest technology (laser surgery, stem cell treatment, newest, best techniques and care). Fast, loving service with a smile. No rush, lots of information and advise. We take ALL our pets (except the horse) and have received exceptional treatment for all, including laser surgery for the guinea pig's ear polyp, practical treatment of one of our dog's sudden "run down" look and bad mood, a bird injury AND preventative well pet care. The staff is very friendly and professional. My dogs actually get excited when they realize where we are going... they think it's the house of cookies, petting and attention to them, not a place to be afraid of.

I feel bad here.  Maybe i missed something?  I live local and keep seeing all of the positive reviews.  My wife was in the mood for something new so we gave Andale a try.  Well, lets see, the portions are a 4 outta 5.  I think they are appropriate and certainly worth the pricing, 5 outta 5.  I did not get the same customer service feel as others on this forum.  I did order to pick up, but i am not sure if the guy on the other end of the phone understood the menu.  Although he was kinda nice, definitely not rude.  Going in the restaurant, cleanliness was a 3 outta 5.  I like the concept and appreciate the home made recipes, but the food was a bit bland.  Not super tasty, not bad, just average.  I am not compelled to go back but may give it one more chance based on all of these great reviews.  More to come.

Came here last night for my boyfriend's birthday. I've previously been here before and once again they were nothing short of great. We had the bucatini and beef short ribs. Everything was cooked to order tasted perfectly and was well-balanced. The service was exceptional. One of my favorite things about this place is the atmosphere.It's very intimate. I'm going to try to make this place one of Nashville top rated Italian restaurants the absolutely deserve it it. Side note I do not work for this place. I'm just another reviewer who can appreciate and recognize a quality place. So anyone who likes Italian food (and who doesn't) should come check this place out.

Best shoe store in Philadelphia, hands down. I LOVE this store, and the owner Elena is the sweetest most helpful lady you can find. The shoes are incredible, I have purchased many shoes here. I get compliments all the time and I have never been unsatisfied with a purchase. I am not a big spender and I usually don't have a lot of cash to blow, but it's worth every penny. 

Seriously, go here, you won't be disappointed and you will be supporting a local gem. 
Cheers!

pricey but convenient.  i live nearby and the market is a great place to pick up a quick drink or snack.  my curry chicken fix from dibruno's can be satisfied here and there's a great stand to pick up fresh fruit.  other than price, i really can't complain.  glad it's here!

Toooo expensive! 12.00 for a drink and a bowl of vegetable soup. At least serve dessert with it. Back home in Seattle I can get a large bowl of delicious vegetarian pho, a coke and cream puff for $9.00.This place is over priced. Won't go back

Truthfully, not sure what the hype is about. Certainly a solid variety of pancakes, but the quality is not above what you can throw together out of a store box mix. The sign outside boasts that they've offered 23 varieties since they opened 50 years ago, but waitress informed us that they no longer sell the potato pancakes. We ended up getting the Swiss chocolate (5 regular pancakes with a TON of chocolate chips dumped on top), Georgia Peach (3 regular pancakes rolled to cover a peach compote, and blintzes (3 small rolls). Glad we didn't have to wait longer than 10 min on a Tuesday morning. Would've been quite disappointed if we stood in one of those infamous lines only to taste mediocrity. Plenty of other great breakfast options in town. I recommend Loveless Cafe.

I really enjoyed the grilled oyster which has a nice smokey flavor.  Stopped in for a quick lunch, sat at the bar.  Was there 30 minutes in and out.  Went back 2 days later after eating oysters at Acme, and had their oysters again.  Had a better flavor than acme and the bread was awesome.

We had a great time chowing down at this little Italian/pizza joint. Be warned that while all of my friends tried their pizza and loved it, I did not partake. Also, there is technically parking available, but it gets filled up super quickly, so be prepared to wait awkwardly if you come during busy dinner time.

As a large group, we pretty much ordered all of the appetizers, including greco salad, the broccolini caesar salad, the roasted bronzino, crispy artichokes, meatball, chicken parm, asparagus, octopus, short ribs, and a multitude of pizzas including margherita, eggplant, mushroom and zucchii and cipolla. while I can't speak much about the pizza, but heard great things about the cipolla, I really enjoyed the two salads, especially the broccolini and the spicy chicken parm. The asparagus and artichokes were a bit too over-oiled or fried for my taste. The short ribs were decent but just also a bit too fatty. The octopus was a tad bit on the chewy side and given how much it cost with how little were on the plate, I'd likely not get it in the future. I think if you want to eat frugally, the pizza and salad combination is likely the way to go, as the antipasti can add up, but overall, it's a decent, but expensive little Italian joint.

Food: 3-4 stars
Service: 3-4 stars
Price: 2-3 stars
Ambiance: 3 stars

The corner room with large picture windows is fantastic! We have a view of the arch and a view of the river on the 11th floor. 

The staff was very helpful checking in and out. We walked to Busch Stadium for a great Cardinals win over the Cubs and ate in the Village last night!

Totally enjoyed this hotel!

I've been a fan of Malena's since she opened five years ago.  You can tell that she picks each of her pieces with care and experience.  In a store that sells 90% vintage merchandise (10% rockabilly apparel), you'll be hard-pressed to find anything below excellent condition.

The boutique also showcases local fashion design talent such as Nicole Ray Styer.

My favorite part about Malena's (and most other shops in West Chester) is their First Friday Event.  The first Friday of every month, the boutique stays open late, serves drinks and Hor D'oeuvres and has a big sale.  A great way to spend a friday!

The prices are reasonable also, so you can find your one-of-a-kind item without breaking the bank.

Oyesters were fresh and well priced. Service was good. I had the special with fried shrimp, crawfish etoufee and jumbolaya. It was good. Had a jalapeño Margarita,the Drink was OK...Nothing special. Overall I'd go there again.
Amazing staff, very courteous. Food was absolutely on point. Loved their Fantasy Duck
Love the place, but on the last visit saw one of the girls cut the fruit without gloves. Big no no... Please address this

I recently got a Buy One-Get One coupon for AYCE at Sushi Minato, but I was extremely hesitant to use it.  After all, Sushi Minato is located where the much maligned (and rightfully so) Woo Chon once called home, and I was concerned that the only thing new about the place was the name.  However, after a very pleasant dinner experience with my sister, I'm pleased to report that Sushi Minato is a brand new place with a brand new feel, and has excellent food and service. 

Sushi Minato is on par with the other "big name" sushi joints in town.  It has fresh fish, creative rolls, and quick, friendly service.  Every piece of sushi was refreshingly bite sized, and nothing we ordered was over-sauced.  We sat at a table and I appreciated that our order came out one or two plates at a time as opposed to having everything squished on to one enormous platter.  My sister and I left full and satisfied. 

The only reason I am giving Minato four stars as opposed to five is that its menu wasn't quite as expansive as those found at Hiroba or Tha Joint.  However, Minato is still new and has great potential for growth.  Great job reviving a dead location, guys.  We'll be back.

This is such a unique spa compared to anything else that I have been to. First, everyone is really nice, professional, and most of all....good at massaging. I like how they volunteer within the community and donate their time and talent across the Bay Area. I am a teacher and I was introduced to this small business because they came to my school and gave out free 15 minute massages to the staff. Since then, I have been in Twice and received a 45 minute massage, infrared treatment for my muscles, a facial, and a 60 minute massage. I had Amanda last time and her hands are magnets to knots. Trust me, if you need some specialized knot work done, she is your girl. Also, they give teachers a 20% discount (which I truly appreciate). The owner is super sweet and the decor is pleasant and relaxing. If you are looking for a consistently relaxing experience, give Divine Connections a try.

Pho is cheaper than everywhere else and you can still get a ton.  There is food challenge here and you can find my face on the wall of shame as I did not finish it, this was a few years back before they increased the price by 10 dollars.  

I will recommend the pho combo large, and its more authentic than all the bougie places.  If you are here just for good food and don't want to drive across the bridge, this is a solid place.  In standard NOLA style, this place looks like its inside of a house.  Find parking on one of the perpendiculars.  

[rating scale: 5 stars is my favorite of this type +/- an insane deal if the food is super cheap; 4 stars a normal haunt I revisit; 3 nice but once is enough; 2 I did not get food poisoning; 1 Damn I got staph here]

The meals were absolutely delicious, I enjoyed every bite of the experience!
We were the only people at the restaurant, but hopefully it's only because it had just stopped raining.

Horrible absolutely horrible service, I ordered, and told them I'm trying to see if you can deliver to my location, she checked and said yes, so then I placed my order, they call me back after 23 minutes and tell me they can't deliver to me.. I say okay, well when will my money be back on my card, they hang up on me, so I call and call again and the assistant manager Will gives me a fake corporate number, they are horrible workers, they need to shutdown this jimmy johns!! I have gone to multiple all over the city it's my favorite sub shop.. But after this, I will tell many people about this horrible service!!
Great service, great menu, great food.  It's a nice atmosphere that is rarely crowded, and definitely one of my favorite restaurants in Media.   I hope this place sticks around for a long time.

For my 100th review, I was fortunate to rent a movie from Casa Video and found another epic place that has served Tucson for many years.

Free family movie on Thursday, whether you rent another movie or not - how cool is that?  Fresh popcorn to snack on while you walk around the store.

Virtually every movie you could ever wish to see, and if you can't find what you're looking for, they have a wish list that you can request it on.

Although old, the store is kept as clean as possible.  They have many different incentive programs and it is clear that the owner is really into customer service.  Well done Casa - thanks for an epic 100th Yelp Review!
