Barry's Bootcamp will kick your ass. If you are serious about amping up your workout, this is your spot. Move past the model pictures on the wall and the loud music. Challenge yourself. Trainers here are great. Facility is nice and there is plenty of parking. I hit the early morning classes 3X  a week. Commit and you will see results. And, quit whining. It's all about what you are willing to do for yourself. Barry's will help you get there! I'm a fan. And, did I mention, I'm almost 47 years old? Get after it...

If you are looking for authentic Baja Mexican food, this is the place.  We had amazing food, freshly prepared, in huge portions.  The fried fish (grouper) tacos are the best that I have had in the area.  My wife had the chile rellenos bowl which was delicious.  My son enjoyed the al pastor xtreme burrito which had to weigh at least a pound, but was so good he finished the entire thing.  Mexican sodas and elotes (corn-on-the-cob) rounded out the meal.  The tortillas are hand made and the service is friendly and out standing.  Two gentlemen from Houston were there eating, and they commented to us that this place was the only Mexican food in the area that they enjoyed.  I can't wait to try other items on the menu.  Run don't walk...

Not very good, the bathrooms were sticky and the bathroom handles had something on them.  The Hand Grenade had some stuff floating in it and did not taste very good and I peed bright green for 2 days.  Music was not good and cheesy.  I would not go there.

Nice place but small rooms. The mini fridge is hidden in some cabinets (ours were by the bathroom). I liked that one of the walls was painted. The bed was super soft and comfy but the shower was small and slippery. We had free internet but got the higher up version for free as well because my dad booked the room with his points. It was fun and I would come again.

Most choices were really great (avoid the chickenparm - awful.) like my crab-stuffed ravioli, over broccoli rabe.  St. Louis Ribs were fall-off-the bone tender.

There is a slight "SYSCO" pre-fab element to the food - but for the most part we love a nice weekend lunch here.  Burgers (patty melts, southwest style) are a solid choice.  Upgrading to Sweet potato fries is a good idea!

i love don pablo's for what it is - chain east coast tex-mex. as far as this genre goes, don pablo's blows its competition out of the water.

great starters (i highly recommend the border dip) and filling, tasty entrees. nothing is perfectly done, and not even close to authentically done, but it all tastes pretty good and the portions are extremely large relative to the price.

margaritas and domestic drafts seem to always be on special, if that's your thing. dos equis amber on draft is a plus for me, even though it's not a "special."

decor is corny and a bit forced, but family-friendly and very large and open, so the waits never get too long.

servers can be spotty, but for the most part are friendly, quick and attentive. i often go with my parents who tend to make borderline creepy remarks (my dad once asked our waiter if he was on facebook) and make tons of messes (same father spills an entire glass of diet coke every other visit), and they're good-natured about everything for the most part.

all in all, don pablo's is a surprisingly above-average dining option in the chain store wasteland that is south jersey.
The Hurricanes were better than any other place I had visited in New Orleans. The food was absolutely exquisite and had a very tasteful sauce.

I shouldn't even give one star , waited to be seated , seen a table open (it was packed) went to walk to table , waitress stopped us said that seat is for someone else , I told her we been waiting , she said no you just walked in which was not true . I put the menu down and walked out . She then proceeded to say HAVE A SHITTY NIGHT!! I'm like are you serious ?!?! What kind of customer service is this . I will never set foot back in there and I will let people know not to honor this business. Wish I could give no stars you get a 0 from me

How did this restaurant disappoint, let me count the ways. First, they "lost" our name on the wait list. Not a good start. As we waiting to order, we pondered what this restaurant was trying to be. It's Sunday after 3, the sound system is blaring dance music. We can barely talk to each other. There are many tv's showing a variety of sports shows. The waitresses is revealing is her navel. What is this place trying to be? Not a destination location for fine food. My eggs benni was mediocre. The eggs and sauce were nice, the English muffin, not toasted and soggy. And the potatoes(?)' Savory white and mashed sweet potatoes. Not a good pairing for breakfast. All in all, I leave poorer, and still hungry. Seek alternate routes

Italian is my favorite food so I tend to judge harshly when I visit an Italian restaurant. At Limoncello I really had no complaints!

The ambiance was so romantic with the string of lights around the outside and the potted plants. I love the outdoor seating that was available with umbrellas just in case it rains. It was so pretty from the outside people would stop and take pictures of the building before passing by. We sat outside, which is first come first serve and it looks like you can bring your dogs to dine with you as well which is pretty cool! 

The food:
I ordered the sea food risotto (I'm not sure if that's what it is called... it was one of the dinner specials). I am gluten intolerant so it's hard to visit an Italian restaurant and get something that is yummy and not pasta... but they do have gluten free noodles if that's your cup of tea. 

My sister ordered the Vongole and those clams were cooked perfectly and seasoned so well!! I almost like it more than my dish!

My dad ordered the Pescatore and his only complaint was there was too much seafood.. said no one else EVER! 

My other sister ordered the lasagna and she loved it and her boyfriend ordered the fettuccine with GF noodles. 

Basically everything was delicious huge portions that even we couldn't finish! We all took dog bags home and I'm so excited to eat the left overs!

Just beware!! Parking is a little difficult, there is $5 parking across the st but it fills up fast. Also for a party of 6 or more it's an automatic 20% tip. 

The waitress we had looked like she was new and didn't pronounce the dishes properly... only knew this because my sister took 4 years of Italian. Just think its important to know how to say what you're serving. Also it would be nice to list that they have gluten free alternatives on the menu. 

Thanks for a delicious dinner and beautiful dining experience! I will have to come back when I'm back in town! :)

To be honest, I was a little worried to reside so close to Whole Foods.  Will I rationalize it as convenience to spend $15 on a "100% vegan, gluten-free, organically-harvested" (VGFOH) bag of chips? Oh my.

But, I am happy to report this is not the case. Yes, Whole Foods carries some outrageously expensive items (mainly those in the VGFOH category mentioned above), yet  they also carry all the basics--and for reasonable prices! (I've even found some things to be cheaper than superfresh/fresh grocer/acme etc.). 

Goodbye, VGFOH qualms. 

Plus, they have rotating Monday through Friday specials that generally last 3 months or so (check the board by the prepared foods section).  Some of my favorites include: Buy 1, get 1 free soups, $2 off any made to order sandwich, and $2 off all deli meats.

Extra perks are the exceptional service. There is always someone ready to help you.  The lady working at the bakery section actually tracked me down because she accidently charged me for a full loaf of bread instead a half.

Only complaint is that it smells funky over by the salad bar. I know, weird,  but true.  I have no idea what it is but it creeps me out.  Hence the reason for the star-dockage.

Now don't let the low score fool you.  This place is such an awesome bar and even better way to grab something to eat.  Most of the staff here is so awesome they could probably do what they do in their sleep.  However, one bad apple can always spoil the bunch, as the saying goes.  
So when you wait patiently for a bartender to finish speaking to a guest in any establishment, you as a patron always find the moment in between when there's a pause to get the bartenders attention for another round of drinks, food or even to pay out your tab.  That's just how this industry works.  Get it when you can because when you wait for some bartenders at some establishments, then you may never get served at all.  
Which is never the case with the veteran bartenders here at Piranhas.  Who know their locals and even get to know their tourist clientele.  But when one particular male bartender decides that being rude to anyone that is disturbing their personal conversation with a regular is just too much to deal with doing their job.  Well that is just horrible customer service.  Letting any customer know that they're just too busy socializing to be bothered by anything remotely close to customer service such as another drink or in this case, "Can I tab out?" after waiting patiently for their pause in conversation is probably one of the worst scenarios a person in the food/bev industry can do.  So because of this bartenders negligence of doing their job (rather lack of) and telling my friend they are speaking to someone when they should have just said that they would be right with them as any good bartender in the industry would have done if they were not ready to leave that titillating conversation.  So is it any surprise that my friend drops her money on the bar for her tab and leaves? Because let's face it, we all don't have time to wait on you when the world is passing us all by during your venture into the depths of what you find fascinating in conversation.  
But the best is yet to come.  When the money dropped on the bar to pay the tab is just not enough becomes apparent for this barkeep.  Why in the world would any self respecting person in this service industry 'refuse' to accept payment from any individual to pay the remaining balance of the tab mentioned? Because that is just what happened after my friend left. Another friend who stayed tried to pay the balance, 'try' being the key word here. I mean who in their right mind would take the cut in their pay that they're tipped out at the end of the night when a mutual friend tries to pay the remaining balance? Refusal of the payment justifies that this was personal and not 'professional' at all.  So what is this guys problem? Who knows.  But that's his problem since he wouldn't accept a payment on a tab.  Does this sound like a personal issue? Perhaps.  It's definitely not a professional act. 
So when I walk into this place tonight with my friend and six other people who are ready to order shots and more rounds of drinks and the bartender tells my friend she is not allowed in there anymore, well obviously we took everyone to another establishment that knows what it means to treat their customers, like Honky Tonk Central and The Stage. Because they like money and won't be rude about it.  Piranhas missed out on all the business we gave those two places because of the arrogance of one menial bartender with an attitude problem that wants to make his job personal.
So good job Piranhas for perpetuating this bartenders abstract view of what the service industry is.  I personally have been going to this establishment for years and have sent people there on recommendations.  Never again.  I will blatantly blacklist this establishment and steer future tourist and local patrons alike from ever walking in here because of his actions.  I work downtown and talk to most of the tourists and locals that come downtown always asking me where to go.  So thank you for being the douche that helped me decide to keep future business from my friends that work there.  Bravo!  You're in a class among your own down there.

This place is bomb!!! The serving is huge when you happen to be in Mt Juliet by Nashville area try to stop here. It's cheap and food quality is awesome.  Try spasanga spaghetti and lasagna together.  Our waiter name Ethan is cool very good in customer service.  He is an excellent waiter

Wow! They don't disappoint. The namesake dish is absolutely divine.  Melt in your mouth buttermilk pancakes, then the toppings are just the next level.  We had the plain and Austrian, both were out of this world. 

Needless to say, the capstone to my visit was this place as I head off to the east coast.  I'll be back.

This place has some very good steak and pretty good sides to go along with it. But you're gonna pay for them as this is not an inexpensive place to eat. I'd consider this place to be more of a "special occasion restaurant" rather than somewhere you'd go on a consistent basis. The cheapest steak they have is a 10 oz. "Carne Asada" steak for $23. That's what me and my wife ordered and it was very delicious, tender,  and was cooked perfectly. I also ordered the "Estillo Charro", which was basically melted cheese with some chilis. This was a good choice as it added some very good flavors and some heat, although the steak does not need any assistance with flavor. I definitely recommend this place but just be ready to pay up.

Pros
- The room's very impressive.  I stayed at The Tower Imperial Suite and it was a killer.  I originally booked a Tower room which was $60, but they upgraded us to this suite ($210/night) for free.  Find out how from frontdesktip.com.
- The casino in general is nice and clean.  The theme is somewhat old fashioned with major neon lights, but for some reason seems new.

Cons
- Service / Friendliness of staff - We requested a non-smoking room and got a smoking room, the front desk told me they are all booked for the day, which there's no way.  It's the middle of a weekday and the parking lot is empty, no one playing at the tables.
- Service / Friendliness of staff 2 - I just wanted water.  There are no soda machines / floor like in other hotels.  The bar in the room had a sign for us to go to front desk to get a key for the bar.  The front desk told me to go to the casino floor to get water.  Walked long ways from my room to get a small bottle of water from an unfriendly bar staff.
- Might have been just my room, but it was very noisy outside like at 8am.  It was terrible sleeping at 4am and having to wake up at 8am.
- Not really a con, but this place is like 2 miles away from downtown Reno.

HOW COULD ANYONE RATE LA COLOMBE LOWER THAN A 5??? I take pilgrimages here from NY just for a cappuccino!

Let's just say, they make the best coffee drinks on the east coast. Foam is like whipped cream and the espresso is perfectly rich and smooth. I am a cafe hopper and have conversed about La Colombe with people from all over the country, and it has been agreed upon my restaurant owners and friends alike, that it is THE BEST. 

I often buy the pound bags of coffee here to bring home. They just opened one in NY, so now I don't have to stock up, but this one in Philli still can't be beat.

Our  server was awesome and that is the good news. My scrambled eggs & fried bacon was less than desirable. I think the fried bacon was made of salt pork it was so salty(to me anyway). If you are a foodie that loves eating whatever just to be different than you may love it. I prefer just plain good whether it be  unique or plain & simple. The other issue for me was the noise level inside. Music blaring and nothing to muffle sounds so don't count on a romantic chat. Go when it's warm to sit outside.

We purchased a groupon to Yakuza and we were excited to check out a new sushi place.  The restaurant is pretty large, it has one big open dining space with a large sushi bar area as well.  There were a few people here on a Friday evening when we arrived, so we were seated right away.  Our waitress was very friendly and nice, great first impression.  We decided on a few specialty rolls and a few plain rolls (usually those are our favorites).  The yellowtail, salmon and tuna rolls were very good, but on the small side.  On the other hand, the specialty rolls were normal sized, some even massive.  We had the white tiger which was very good even though the color of the sauce on top scared me a little...and the volcano roll was HUGE, I mean, seriously huge.  You don't even know where to begin with this roll because it is a huge heaping pile of sushi.  It was very good, but almost too much sushi and too much going on for my liking.  All in all, the sushi was very good and we were happy with our experience.  The cons I would mention would be the cleanliness of the windows where the end tables are sitting as well as the prices.   I noticed spiderwebs on the baseboards next to our table which isn't exactly appetizing.  I thought this place was a little overpriced, we ended up spending an additional $50 on top of the groupon I had already purchased which got us $30 worth of sushi.  We only ordered six rolls, miso soup, side salad and one glass of wine.  Our usual sushi place costs about $50 total for about the same things.  We enjoyed coming here, but it didn't blow us away enough to come back on a regular basis, but we would definitely come by again if we were in the area.

Best Mexican Food I have had in 10+ years. Chile Relleno is a must. Service was excellent. The menu is extensive and has something for everyone. Food quality is exceptional. Went with three others who all agreed that this was a phenomenal experience.

I have gone to this restaurant many times in the past with some satisfactory results but the last two times I have gone I have been dissappointed.  I was trying to hurry on my way to work and ordered two spicy chicken burritos.  What I was hoping for did not arrive.  What I received was two poorly wrapped, tasetless, cold burritos.  This seems to be happening alot at this particular restaurant lately.  I would just skip this place next time or find another place to stop in at.

I first got into La Colombe coffee from the cans they sell at the supermarket but this was my first time at a store.  I tried the triple shot draft latte and it was so smooth and light and even better than the can when you drink it on tap.  I also tried the Black and Tan which is half latte and half black cold brew coffee and it was good too but I prefer the latte.  They have coffees and sell some pastries but I'm coming back for more lattes.

Don't know what to think of the place.  Are they really helping rescue the pups from a place that might otherwise kill them or helping further the puppy mill industry?  All I know is we got our puppy here years ago and, though he is a fantastic little dog, he was very sick.  He threw up in the car on the way home but his stomach was empty so he just threw up stomach acid.  After taking him to the vet, he was confirmed to have giardia, ear mites, and kennel cough.  It took over $1,000 and almost a year to get him healthy and with no diarrhea.   His stomach is so sensitive to this day because of the giardia he had that he can only eat one organic dog food we found that works for him.  

When we were waiting to visit with him, the floor in the room was very cold and I could hear the puppies barking below in the basement so they must have been cold too.  We love our dog so much but would never buy from here again.

If someone asked me what my last meal on earth would be, it would have to include Blue Corn Asparagus Tacos from Blue Sage. 
Blue Sage is a small, often driven past, vegetarian restaurant in Southampton, PA. It's tucked away along 2nd Street Pike in a little strip of shops (well, there are probably only 2 other store fronts).
I have been a veggie for 16 years and finding a veg restaurant that doesn't think all veggies want to eat salad all the time is hard to find. 
Blue Sage offers so much more than a  "salad and tofu sandwich" type of place. In fact, no tofu or seitan or tempeh is used at all! That is the amazing thing. No mock this or mock that. Pure, delicious vegetables, fruits and grains.  Owner/chef Mike Jackson is a wizard of veggies. The food is fresh, clean, crisp. The Cubano Supper is layers upon layers of explosive flavor.  The Wild Mushroom Risotto is creamy and soul-warming. 

Whether a veg or not, don't pass by this Bucks County wonder any longer. 
A few tips: 
Make a reservation. The restaurant is small.  Fridays and Saturdays are packed. 
Love what you eat!

I have to start by saying that they took three of the items off our bill ... But, I've never returned almost all of a meal before. Ever.  We started with the calamari appetizer.  I loved the tempura style batter, but the calamari was VERY tough and chewy.  We paid for it anyway since we had eaten more than just a bite.  The sizzling rice soup and the house (combo) fried rice were both too salty to eat - it tasted like they dumped the whole shaker in.  My entree was the Mongolian beef, and the beef was so soft and without texture I could barely chew it.  Disgusting. Needless to say, we're still searching for a GOOD Chinese restaurant other than RIM at the Grand Sierra.

I have never been so impressed with a massage in my life. This place is absolutely incredible! The rooms are themed which seems simple but I found it a super thoughtful touch. I had the couples massage and oh my gosh. So amazing. Noise canceling headphones with fabulous soothing music sync with the vibrations in the table and absolutely take you away. I mean cmon- it's insanely genius. The staff was also extremely friendly and professional and just amazing. We had Jackie and Rachel and both my boyfriend and I agreed that this was the best massage we've ever had.  I honestly can't recommend this place enough. I booked it to make up for a couples massage from hell at a different company and I'm almost happy I got tortured for 60 minutes at the other company because it led me to search for and find Sound Stone.  This will be the only place I go for any massages from now on. SO. HAPPY.

Picked up a groupon and saved $15 and then came in and had a great meal. Wife had the salmon and didn't talk the entire meal. Yep she liked it that much. I was just grabbing a sandwich and had the chicken club. I'd eat that again. Bread was great. Toss on top of the food the great service we got from Debbie and we are all smiles but then the live music broke out. Icing on the cake. Live music is always a hit when grabbing a dinner. We are grabbing another groupon and heading back sooner then later and hopefully we can play some pool or shuffle board.

This is a good place for bread and desserts but the sandwiches are just NOT so good.  I'm not a big carb person and prefer the protein parts of my meal the most with lots of veggies on the side so this place isn't my optimal feeding spot.  Better to grab some bread to go and work your own magic on it.  They also offer some traditional Jewish breads that you might not find anywhere else in the area.  I never tried any of the Jewish breads and don't have any point of comparison to know if they are good or not but they looked nice.  The desserts here look pretty tasty and I had a cherry mini-pie that was pretty decent.  Overall I just wasn't that impressed and haven't been back for a long while now.

I took my wife and son out for dinner and ended up at MudBugs. A pleasant meal was has by all.  The red beans  and rice were delicious. As well and the Shrimp Po Boy. But my favorite dish was the Chicken Courtboulion. Spiced just right with fantastic side of Hush Puppies. We will be going back soon- and with more people!

Went today with a group for brunch. We had no complaints. Great-cucumber Bloody Mary, coffee, lobster gumbo, grilled artichoke, white trash hash and service. The decor was tasteful and semi modern. I definitely felt like we left Nashville for a couple hours which was great! Will definitely be back!
There is no better place to stay in New Orleans and the French Quarter. First rate accommodations and location. Love it.

One place I'll miss, and will definitely make a point of stopping by when we visit SB. 
- Cash Only
- ATM (with fee) inside
- Huge soda & chip selection
- Baked goods & soups

Husband loves their panini. I always get the Italian; for lighter fare, their grilled chicken salad is HUGE and cheap (under $6)! Larry the owner is always there and his staff are super friendly local high-school kids.

Our waiter Jonathan Cupid made our experience of New Orleans perfect. Regardless of the rainy weather outside Jonathan was a ray of sunshine.  He shared his wonderful voice with us as well as his Southern gentlemen hospitality by making recommendations for our stay. 
Thank you for a great experience!
A must go to kinda place!

Great late night hang out spot for college students! You're served fast and given very generous portions as well. Although it does get a bit crowded and noisy, that is only to be expected given their location. 

I ordered wings and a side of fries. Both were very standard in taste, though they were not bland. Regardless of the flavor, they do give you a lot of food. If you ask for an order of fries, they fill an entire rectangular Styrofoam container full of them. In terms of drinks, (quite surprisingly)they have an extensive beer selection. 
I will definitely be back here and highly recommend this place to any Penn or Drexel student before and after the party!

Have become increasingly unimpressed with the Asian food on Delmar. Got the chengdu spicy chicken which tasted no different than chicken from a fried chicken place. Rice that came with it was incredibly boring even for rice. Servings were way too much. Server was not attentive to table enough and appeared there was only one server for full restaurant. The only thing justifying one stars was the inside of the restaurant was nice.

We bought "our first fish" and couldn't get much help or information about what we might need. We were willing to pay more for a nice filter, a hearty fish, etc, because it was my daughter's birthday and this was her special present. We didn't receive any info or help, they missed the fact that we would need a dechlorinator for example, sending us racing back to the store. So... end of story, first fish died 4 days later. Not blaming you, Petsmart, but you sure didn't help either. 
From now on we're sticking with independent stores, not big chains.

I was so happy with my service today that I decided to write a review! The girl who helped me at the drive through window was so nice and super accommodating. According to my receipt Qudriyah helped me. I would recommend this location for sure. My favorite thing to get at Popeyes is the red beans and rice!

I was surprised to see such low marks on this one... we had a great time! Food was amazing and service was quick/attentive. We sat down after a half-hour wait, and our meals were ready (no joke) in about ten minutes. We ordered appetizers but our main course was so quick, it beat it and the staff threw the appetizer in free. We couldn't be happier and would easily recommend this location for those wanting to get out.
I love this place food and service is alway spot on. Only thing I wish was if they did the add on lunch special where you get a side of chips and salsa and drink for a few extra bucks

We had a very nice visit to Nashville. The Hilton Garden Inn made my visit much more enjoyable. The staff were professional, courteous and friendly. The servers in the dinning area were also helpful and friendly. Hany, one of the servers there was very accommodating in helps us with our food and drinks.
The hotel was about one mile from the busy downtown party area which was great because there are many ways to get there besides walking. Shuttle, golf carts that will accommodate up to six people or Lyft and Uber.

Big dining area, very clean, nice atmosphere, friendly staff. 

The House Salad was GREAT! Highly recommend. It made me realize that thing I like best about salad was BACON! 

We got a large 1/2 cheese,1/2 pepperoni...cuz we roll gangster like that. It was super yummy in our tummy-tum-tumkins. Even our ankle bitters loved it. 

We'll be back!

I. LOVE. GELATO(& Frost).

My first gelato experience was at a Frost... not this location but I fell in love with the product. Being an "east-sider", when this location opened up, I was here weekly. It's that good. Now, I have come here whenever I am in town... the quality of the gelato has not changed, neither has the ambience of the store.

All the enticing flavors, with fruit, chocolate, and other goodies glare at me through the spotless glass case... all saying "pick me, pick me". I sample away then pick something I didn't sample...

Perfectly sized (3 to chose from), doesn't melt right away, and the flavors (cream or fruit based) are amazing!

Awful service, stood at host station for 10min before a single server helped us. Once our hostess artived we were greeted with, 'what do u want?" No line at all and about 2/3 of all the tables empty, was told it was a 25min wait.  Wait for what? Wouldn't u rather seat us and make money off of drinks? We waited 5min until some friends of our hostess came in and we're seated immediately. I politely asked if we could at least wait at one of 20 open tables.  Was told they have no tables available, which was ridiculous.  Watched about half a dozen servers standing around the main area talking and not doing anything for about 10minutes. Then we left.

I have to be honest but I am shocked to see such horrible reviews. I have frequented this restaurant for over four years now and I have not experienced a single time in which anyone in my group and/or family felt dissatisfied. 

Food breakdown

Appetizer: We typically order the Summer Garden Rolls and some variation of the Jasmine Rice soup. I can't recall the name of the soup we recently got about two-three weeks ago but it was a variation of the Jasmine Rice soup with shrimp and it was EXCELLENT! We have add the Lemongrass soup and Coconut soup and both were great. Have also tried the Chicken Satay and I thought they were good but I wish there was more.

Main Entrees: Pad Thai with Tofu or shrimp is my absolute favorite! They cook it to perfection and I LOVE that it is not very greasy. I usually have them spice my food via their star system from 0-4 with a 3. I ordered a 4 one time and the lady warned me it would be ridiculously spicy and I thought ah I can take it.....let me tell you they don't joke when they say 4 stars! We also love the Coco Thai Basil, Thai Green Curry and a variety of their fish dishes.

Drinks: We love the Thai ice tea! Made to perfection with just the right amount of sweetness and condensed milk (I could be wrong about the cream type). 

Employees: They are super friendly, talkative and open to suggestions. I love that they REALLY listen to your special requests and/or dietary needs.

Bottom Line: If you like authentic, healthy, FRESH food, then this is your place! If you're looking for a run of the mill Americanized location then maybe this place isnt for you.

The Pho was very good. The broth itself was fantastic- the chicken appeared to be lunchmeat. Maybe that's how all Pho is, I don't know, but I was expecting something better. But the soup itself made it alright. I'd absolutely go back.

This place does a thorough job cleaning. However, the staff there can be snippy and rude at times. A couple times I wanted to get a full detail and the ticket attendant snippily said "it's too late" the first time I said OK and just got a regular car wash; the second time I came about 1pm and he said the same thing, I asked him what a good time was and he just ignored me and asked what car wash I wanted to get, so the lady at the front desk tells me to come before 12 next time. So my last run in with this same ticket attendant was yesterday, I was pulling up to the car wash under the direction of his hand motion and once I got out he told me in snippy and rude tone not to watch the front of my car and to watch him, Which I don't understand, I'm not going to drive forward when there's a car in front of me under your direction and not look at what I'm doing. So I go to the manager because at this point I know this guy is a bit rude, the manager tells me "well he's been here 19 years and longer than me and I haven't had any complaints" I said "well that doesn't have anything to do with my experience and why I'm standing in your office at this moment and I'm coming to you because I'm giving you an opportunity to rectify it rather than just going to social media or writing a bad review" he says "well you can do that, we have thousands of people come through every day" So here I am! The managers attitude was an "I don't care about your experience because we have enough customers, we can lose one" That will be my last time giving them a chance, I'm sure there are other car washes with thorough work and great customer service skills as well.

Why did I do it? This one was totally my bad.

I guess I was feeling a little homesick and the idea of some good fried fish and good sushi was too tempting to pass up. I should have thought twice when I saw a gaijin behind the sushi bar. I should have ordered fish and chips, something nearly impossible to mess up. But no, I ordered chirashi. The fish, although definitely safe to eat, was probably the worst-cut mess I have ever seen. Just bad. It was all differently-sized chunks and totally not the right consistency. 

But that was nothing compared to M's buffalo grouper sandwich. Again, insane thing to order. But strips of grouper, deep fried and soaked in buffalo sauce, sounded like the perfect meal at the time. The combination of flavors was... gym socks. I'll leave it there.

That being said, the waiter was very nice and attentive. And they were open at 9:30 on a weeknight when we rolled into town. But please, if you can't make sushi, don't open a sushi bar inside your restaurant... and if buffalo grouper tastes like sweaty feet, don't put it on the menu.

I have high expectations since I grew up eating home-cooked Vietnamese food and for the past few months, I've been living in Hanoi. I was in the mood for a bowl of pho and my dad didn't want to stop off in Chinatown after picking me up from the airport, so we opted to stop here since it was close to their house. I got a bowl of the rare beef and meatball pho to go while my dad opted to try their asparagus and crab soup. Total for the two items, $16. Yikes! (A bowl of pho in Hanoi is about $1; a bowl of pho in D.C. is $6 - $8. They were charging $10 for theirs)

The broth was okay, a tad salty, but when I added bean sprouts to the broth, it evened out. The broth lacked the subtle aromatic flavor that I'm accustomed to in a bowl of pho. The noodles were a bit chewy, and the meat was a bit on the tough side.

Cafe Verdi is our go-to whenever my sister, Mom and I want to meet somewhere relatively inexpensive and always delicious for dinner. Located in Trolley Square, across from Catherine Rooney's bar and the Logan House, Cafe Verdi offers you the option to sit down and eat or just pop in for a slice of pizza or calzone. They moved a few suites down, which threw me off a bit last night. The ambience is different inside - less pizza in a strip mall and more, "Hey! I get it....this is supposed to look like an Italian grotto." The food is always amazing. I never stray from my chicken alla griglia - two huge breasts of chicken with steamed broccoli and spinach. Last night, we had the polenta and eggplant stack (cold eggplant with mozzarella and roasted peppers) appetizers. For three discerning Italian palates, we were very happy. I had a pizelle for dessert, which my Mom had in her purse from a trip to see her Italian first cousin this weekend. No, I am not joking.

Wishing a happy, healthy holiday season to the family and staff of this priceless Italian eatery located in Newtown PA.

Always greeted with a smile, always a great meal.

Nice to be recognized and know what your food likes or food needs/requirements include. 

Hands down a wonderful go to for self, for family and for entertaining of friends and family.

I have only been here for one visit since I don't make it up to this area of town often, but this will certainly be high on my list of places to go when I am in the area. 

My visit came on a Friday night, and it was packed. Parking was made very easy in the free parking garage just go north on 1st Ave from Main St. (the intersection of Pint Room), and you will see the garage on your left immediately. There was a hostess that said she could seat us in the dining area of the place, or we could have a look around the open-seating bar area. We got really lucky and grabbed a table as another group was leaving, but trying to get a table in the bar area on a Friday night looked like a game of chance, as it was busy the entire time. There wasn't really a lot of standing room, so if you don't get a seat you might just want to put your name on the list for a table in the dining area.

I wasn't there to get food, which is good because it took me long enough just to decide on a drink from their enormous beer list. They have it broken down into categories of beers, and they cover the majority of the spectrum. The majority of their beers are on the safe side of things, but there are certainly some adventurous options on the list as well.  Don't quote me on this, but I am fairly certain that the beer list includes the name of the beer, the price, what state it is from, and the ABV %. It'd be nice to have an IBU rating, but even I will admit that I think that might be pretty ambitious for a list that long. I love that the price of every beer is listed by it. I'm amazed at how many places just have long beer lists without ever showing a price until you get your bill.

Our waitress did a great job relative to how busy it was. The guy who came over to clean our table after the last group left was not so much in that category. We got beers filled quickly and our waters stayed full the whole night. Our server even knew a decent amount about the beers they served and she was able to remind someone at our table what they had they last time they were there by just the description alone. One thing that is really frustrating at a place like this is when you finally make a decision on the one beer you want the most, and then they server goes to get it only to come back and say they are out and need a second choice. I know with a place that likes to rotate taps and gets in limited quantities of some beers that it happens, but the waitress didn't even take the time to cross it off of the beer list on our menus so the next person who sees that option and orders it will also be faced with coming up with a second option with no time to think. 

It was a little loud in here just due to the number of people, but it wasn't so bad that you couldn't have an easy conversation with the people at your table. The majority of the people here were young professionals, and the crowd was that of people who wanted to go out and get some drinks and dinner to catch up with friends, rather than to just go out drinking and getting wild for a night. There are quite a few TVs in the bar area, so all of the games you could want to watch will likely be viewable here, although it is much more of an upscale bar than a sports pub. As I said before, I wasn't here for food but everything I saw at surrounding tables looked delicious and I would like to give the food a try sometime, which I will likely be back to do in the summer when longer bike rides take me up to the Carmel area and I need a pit stop along the way.

At 9:30am on a Saturday, when the rest of downtown Santa Barbara is pretty quiet, this spot is packed - and for good reason!

The line to order wasn't long, just a few people. We waited a few minutes and were able to get a table - meant for 4, but we got enough chairs to squeeze 6 chairs around it. 

THE COST: $29 for three small bowls.

Note: The "Small" is still a decent sized bowl! We were afraid what the "Large" would have looked like. If you want what would be, say a "Large" at Pinkberry, then get the "Kid's Size". The "Small" did keep us full for several hours!

* Island - 4 stars
This is more heavy on the berry/tart flavors, and the toasted coconut on top is a treat!

* Cocoa Almond - 3.5 stars
Definitely sweeter, between the chocolate base and the banana. This would've been too much sweet on its own if I weren't sharing the Island with my friend!
Food was delicious, some items came out cold but other than that everything was great!

5 stars for Doylestown Thai food.  If you're looking around for thai food in this area look no further.

I've lived in NYC and San Fran and have eaten quite a bit of great thai food.  This place is as good as thai food that you'd find in San Fran and NYC at a non-upscale thai restaurant.

The service is great and very child friendly.  Parking in downtown can be a little difficult at times but worth it after you've eaten the drunken noodle, chicken with green beans and the massaman curry.

The pineapple fried rice was delicious but the drunken noodles were the best.  All the right flavors with a touch of heat.  The pad thai was a little too heavy on the palm sugar and too sweet for me.  I prefer my pad thai with more fish sauce, chili powder and egg.

The massaman curry is quite nice and will be going back over and over again.

This place is a BYOB and I would recommend a bottle of Riesling and some beer.

They do take reservations if you want to call in advance.  After writing this review I've talked myself into going here tonight with my family.

I can't wait for Thai deliciousness in Doylestown of all places.

We rented a room over the weekend and while I enjoyed the hotel staff and room, the dining was less than desirable. We tried the Oceano and the Cafe Milano. The staff were fine but the food was just not at a level expected especially for the cost of the room and the cost of the hotel. Not sure if we'll be back based on the food experience.

I'm so happy Shannon moved to this new salon!  I got the tour and it's a really lovely place!!  Shannon's been doing my hair for over three years and she's the best.  I don't think I will let anyone else ever do my hair!  I met  the owners Allison and her mom and they are very nice and I could tell right away Allison is a genuine, down to earth person and I wish her all the luck with the new shop!  I can't afford a lot in the way of face care so she suggested a small kit of some of the products for eliminating those dark spots we get...I can't wait to get it. Thanks Allison and thanks Shannon!!  :). Laurie

Where else in the area can you visit a steampunk-decorated coffee shop? Nowhere as far as I know! We were in the area so I stopped here and got some coffee drinks to go. I enjoy Kahwa espresso so I was pleased to see that's what they serve at Grindhouse! They seemed to have a wide variety of desserts in the case and they looked scrumptious but I've been eating healthy lately so I managed to resist.

Speaking of resisting... I have to admit, the whole time, I looked around nervously, waiting for perhaps a Scientologist to attempt to assimilate me. This is downtown Clearwater after all. However, everyone here seemed OK and I've not joined a cult so life remains good. I look forward to returning!

AWRSOME breakfast place. Service. Food and prices..... suggestions  Montana plate, Bananas Foster French toast, cheese grits. 

Make sure you get here

Very happy with our service , Ben showed up early, explained to us in detail what he was going to do, and what our yearly contract entitled us to. He was very thorough and professional, did a fantastic job! 
 We highly recommend Natura to anyone needing pest control.

I had the grilled Mahi tacos and my husband had the Spinach Balsamic salad with Ahi Tuna. We also had the buffalo wing appetizer. Wow. I am blown away with our experience here. The food was smoked to perfect and beautiful plating. It was definitely a fine dining dinner for only about $16 per entree. And I also got their moscato that was delicious!

I love, love, love this store. Such amazing finds every time. This store is so dangerous for me to be in, because I want to buy everything!!!! I've found great clothing, home goods, books, etc here!!! 

I do wish that there were a little more customer service. I like my alone time to shop, but I feel awkward when I'm shopping so close to the register and there's no conversation between me and the cashier. But their wonderful selection of vintage stuff really makes up for that!

Will always go back.

Went back to HipCityVeg today for lunch. It was packed (weekday at 12:30pm) but they were quick to take orders and keep things moving. 

I just wanted to post on Yelp again to thank the manager (I believe) for such great service today. I ordered the udon noodle salad as I had read rave reviews. Unfortunately, the salad fell flat. It was tasteless and just bland. (My parents had the buffalo Bella and crispy HipCityVeg and both were so good! And sweet potato fries were soooo amazing - crispy on outside and soft on inside) 

I decided the udon salad wasn't worth eating, so I went up and asked if I could have something else instead. The manager honestly actually cared that I didn't enjoy my salad and BOTH replaced it with the philly steak (my choice) free of charge, but also remade the salad so I could give it a second try! He thought that perhaps the fake chicken hadn't been marinated well and the salad was light on the dressing. This second version was MUCH better - much more flavor. I think my first salad was missing the dressing. I still prefer the sandwiches and I think the salad was a bit oily (I know, you can't have it all!). However, that is just first class customer service and I applaud how the situation was handled. Thank you so much, can't wait to be back soon!
Great place! Really crowded at night! The service was excellent. They literally said "we can cook it however you like". The food was good and exotic. Would definitely go back!

Alright, just finished a basketball tourney and my daughter wanted ice cream and I wanted a hotdog, checked yelp and this place popped up, wasn't far so we thought we would try it, drove by and place was totally packed, out to the street, debated then decided to do the wait, took maybe 20 minutes to get thru the drive thru and get our food, was totally worth it! Peer pressure made me get the double cheese burger with everything on it my daughter got a Reece's extreme, the cheeseburger was very good, one of the better ones, her ice cream was HUGE and very good, we both split some fries which was awesome. If you are even remotely close you really should stop, it is well worth it
Excellent soul food. Everything was delicious well seasoned and cooked to perfection. Best greens and black eye peas I ever had.

I've been eating here since I was two years old! I learned how to use chopsticks here and I've seen the staff all grow up along with me. This place is by far the best Thai food I've ever had (and I've been to Simply Thai, Dusit Thai, Smiling Elephant and all those other places). 

For appetizers, the tiger tear salad, chicken satay, and tom yung koon are the bomb dot com and I never leave without having one of them.

They have the best pad thai and chicken panang, so be sure to try it sometime. The seafood curry, while pricey, is worth it for the large medley of seafood you get. Stay away from ordering native Thai hot unless you want a red ring in the morning! 

Please don't pass this hole in the wall up. You'll love every bite of whatever you decide to order. I've never had something I didn't like.

I'm not a Phillies fan, but I have to admit that this park is beautiful. There isn't a bad seat in the house, and you could spend hours just walking around the stadium. There is always a long line at Chickie's and Pete's, but trust me, the crab fries are worth it. Monday nights are dollar dog night, so be prepared to have a hot dog eating contest with your friends. Lastly, Philly fans get a bad rap for being terrible fans, but there are a lot of fathers and sons that come to this park, so I'd say that Phillies games are rather subdued compared to Flyers or Eagles games. So, no worries if you're not a Phillies fan.

Quite possibly the best Indian food I've ever had, certainly in the top 3 experiences. Food is spiced to order and met expectations perfectly, especially if you have a hard time finding real heat. Staff was friendly, helpful and attentive. Even the leftovers tasted great!

Try the sexy naan!

Best food, best atmosphere!  I will never pass by another Joe's Crab Shack! I could live on the Crazy Good Crab Dip.  Servers are very good, hostess station is friendly upon arriving and leaving.  Food came out in a timely manner and was delicious!

I've been sitting at the bar waiting for someone to ask me what I'm having. I waited a good 5 minutes and still no one asked, yet everyone else around me was being served. It wasn't busy at all.  I ordered the pineapple rice and sushi and it was the worst thing I had ever had. The service sucked and so did the food. The sake cafe on Magazine st. is much better.

Makiman is good, but a bit pricier than other sushi places in town if you don't have some kind of deal. I've had various fish and vegetable rolls, which have all been decent, and the vegetable tempura is good. Service is average.

So I grew up in a city with 342 bridges and over 100 islands. I am no stranger to bridges and I know good bridges and beautiful bridges.. well, you get the point...

I've always had a soft spot for a certain bridge while growing up, but over time, I could not help it - Ben Franklin became my favorite.

Perhaps it's not the most exciting or the most beautiful...
Perhaps there's always traffic and/or construction that pisses you off...
Perhaps the toll has become fairly ridiculous...

and yet, I can't help it - I love this little bridge... even if I could take an alternate sometimes, I would still take Ben Franklin, just to see it one more time...

I can't really explain it, but if you drive it, if you walk it, if you walk next to it and under it (on both sides) during the day and during the night, in the summer, fall, spring and winter - perhaps you'll understand...

Twice now, I've run from the cold to squeeze through the door of Pabbit. It's been a nice refuge these last couple of freezing cold nights. 

In short,
The burger is better than Monk's. 
The fries are a close second to Monk's. 
The gnocchi are way too salty. (I still need to try the pierogies.) 

I love having a large pint of cider and a burger so that's probably what I'll stick to if we return again. I might also work my way through all of the $3 bar munchies.

Top 10 Things About Nomad

10.) Exposed brick walls - They remind me of other red things I like; Tiger Woods' Sunday polo, red folders, red pens to mark up someone's errors, the American flag and of course period blood (aka the red flower).

9.) The bathrooms - A dual-level toilet?!? Say what? When taking care of business, you can choose to sit down with a backrest in the traditional posture and your feet on the floor, or sit up top with a place to dip your feet in the hot summer months. Although the second option requires removing the heavy porcelain lid to the toilet, so if you're a woman this might be a challenge.

8.) Yadda.

7.) Yadda.

6.) Yadda.

5.) Food choices - You can order food in from any other local food spot, because they don't have a kitchen. That's right, you can enjoy pizza, ceviche, chicken mcnuggets, caviar, black truffles, black mambas and even pork belly pancakes. All is within your reach with a quick phone call. Use your imagination!

4.) Blacked out windows - When I first walked by, I didn't even notice the bar. So I kept walking...and walking...and before I knew it I was playing a game of dominoes with some local gentleman on their front porch. It didn't last long - I thought slamming your fist on the table and yelling "dominoes bitches!" was standard, but it seems my timing was off. On my way back up Orange Street luckily I heard the music emitting from inside, which brings us to number 3.

3.) Live Jazz and Blues music - Loves it. I even got to wear my favorite "White People Fucked Up The Blues" t-shirt. This is the real draw at Nomad. It's cozy, has a great beer selection, friendly bartenders and great music soaring through the bar and out the door into the third-rate city Wilmington sky.

2.) Free Goldfish crackers - Confession - I like to get a lttle raw and raunchy sometimes. Maybe dress as a seagull and eat raw fish, flap my wings in public to piss people off, etc. And what is a seagull's second favorite food? Goldfish crackers. I know, because I used to empty whole large cartons onto the beach when I was younger, to draw in every seagull within a 10 block radius to create a diversion to get home. Maybe I upset a few families trying to enjoy the beach without the cackling, cawing and bird shit on their chests, but these are sacrifices you need to make.

1.) I leave number one up to you, the reader. Sometimes it's about the journey, not the destination, sucka.

Our server was wonderful! So polite and nice mannered. The food. Oh. My. Goodness. Enough said. Portions are a great size! Prices very affordable. I had the jambalaya and catfish bites and the food was moist and well seasoned. The bites were so light and flaky and hot!! The cornbread is sooo fluffy and warm still and moist. Visit this place!!!

I had a late dinner 9:30pm due to a last minute decision. The food was delicious and well seasoned. The only problem is while patrons are still eating the employees sweep around your table and feet. I understand you want to go home but this issue needs to be addressed. Other than that all went well

A hidden gem. Don't judge it by the location in a small strip mall or its appearance. The food was incredibly fresh and delicious and prices are very reasonable. Ate here for dinner based on other Yelp reviews and was very pleased. They even took great care to accommodate a dietary allergy. We will be back.

Just okay. It seems that the crab is all they know how to do as myself and others have tried other menu items just to be disappointed every time. The only decent appetizer is mozzarella sticks. The crab cakes are bland but somehow still overly black peppered flavored. I guess the French fries are the best non-crab food item they have.

We visited Eats! during Creative Loafing's Tampa Bay Burger Week to try their $5 Juicy Lucy Burger. This Wednesday evening was fairly busy, but we quickly found a table with a view of the World Series game on several televisions. But because this is a small restaurant, I imagine it does fill up at busier times.

Having enjoyed their Mac-N-Cheese at the annual Yelp event in April, I was delighted we could substitute that for fries on one of our orders at no additional charge. Because the burgers were delicious. I'll rave about them first. Mine was cooked more than my requested medium well, but was simply so good that I was able to completely ignore the overcooking. The fries were also very delicious. But the highlight of my meal was that homemade Mac-N-Cheese! The bowl was huge - more than plenty to share between the two of us. Piping-hot creamy pasta, covered with bacon & a thick layer of cheese - glorious. Sooo good!

Our server was very attentive but not over-bearing. She was friendly & helpful, sharing her opinion of a couple dishes that had caught our eye for future visits. But, we also appreciated that she wasn't terribly chatty. Later in the evening, we saw a sign on the ad board about 70¢ wings on Wednesdays, and hubs almost ordered a few to take home for his lunch, due to our server raving about them. Even though he ultimately didn't order any (only because he wasn't able to finish his burger), we are definitely returning for those wings, as well as a few other entrees... And that amazing Mac-N-Cheese.

The restaurant just reopened today from a 2 1/2 week renovation. The restaurant over went a complete transition. The look used to be casual dining with a very busy decor to a classy upscale looking restaurant. Don't worry about the prices, the restaurants is affordable. 

Great semi open kitchen so you can view the cooks in action. There is a glass to keep the noise from entering the dining room. 

Apps are around the $10 area and you can get many main course for $14 - $16. 

The food and service is top notch. There are many dishes to choose from. This has now become my wife and I favourite Italian restaurant in this price range. 

The reason I am giving it 4 out of 5 stars is because they spent the money on renovating the restaurant but our bread came in a broken wicker basket. One of our menus was very worn out around the edges. Not a big deal but don't cheap out on the little things.

A country town feel inside of New Jersey? Go figure! A gift shop full of knick knacs that your paddywhack cousins adorn their walls with at home. A solid breakfast menu that is perfect for a quick stop or a take out on the go. Enjoyed the service and the escape.

Yeah, it's really pretty bad... The folks who work there are nice, on the whole, so I'm giving it a second star.

I've been going here for years since my time in school. Unless you're willing to walk to 10th street, this is one of your few grocery store options in the area. Spruce Mart on 15-16th and, um, Spruce, is decent enough, but that's really a big corner store/bodega. DiBruno brothers is excellent, but up on Chestnut and 18th, and more of a specialty item store--not where you get your cereal and 2% milk. There's Sue's for produce also up 18th, but they just sell produce. So in the end, you're stuck with the "Shttenhouse," as I like to call it.

The produce here is poor to bad, and they make little effort to make it even look fresh. The green leafy veggies are often wilted, brown, and withered, and the fruit either way to early to put out or, more often, a bit rotted here and there. 

It's been a long time since I've bought meats there. I probably wouldn't, either.

And so not a huge selection, very poor produce, and an extremely high price point for what you get makes this place a bad choice unless you have no other option, which I guess is how they stay in business. Avoid it if you can get what you want somewhere else and it's convenient to you.

We stopped in this gallery while wandering around the streets in a Friday afternoon. I am glad we stopped in his art work is beautiful. The lady that was working the gallery was super helpful she showed us how all his paintings are layered, and when she turned down the lights in the painting it was like the whole thing changed...I loved it. I think we may stop back in a buying something these are very unique works of art.

Plush is a huge place, kind of gives a vibe of an college apartment party with all the different rooms/areas that different groups congregate to; with an added bonus of being a music venue.  Shuffleboard on the floor and ping pong tables upstairs.  Cool.  

The beer list is pretty long with a nice mix of microbrews and prices were very reasonable, pints topped out at $5, with cheaper 9oz options if you want to sample more of their beers.  

The kitchen is open late, and the food is tasty, although judging from the appetizers, food wouldn't be my main draw for coming.  The grilled cheese sandwiches are mini and good for sharing, the spinich/fig/blue cheese wontons were a great mix of flavor, but the wings were wimpy.  It was nice that the whole menu is served all day.

I hate knocking places on service if the goods deliver, but Plush seemed very understaffed.  They have 4 bars in the place, which were moderately crowded, but took way too long to get a drink, the orders would be wrong, and then the beer would be completely flat.  What?!  

It's a great space, I'd come here for a show, but without the music, Plush would have to tighten up its game for me to come back.

What can you say?  Typical Applebees that seemed to be well-run and had friendly staff.  Food is consistent and predictable.

The Tuesday night burger deal is a good one -- any burger on their menu for $6.99.

If there was a 12 step program for ice cream addictions, this place would probably distract me from completing the course... Anyplace that still serves Richman's Ice Cream has my business whenever I can get there. Although I never have tried any, there's a menu full of good from the fryer and grill. The cheese fries must be a favorite since I saw a few orders being eaten on my way in. 
The ice cream prices are a bargain, and the serving size is enough to make you stuffed and looking forward to your next visit. 
They've been around for awhile, so its good to see a quality business still in the area.

Well after reading that this is one of the Top 20 Italian Restaurants in the Country, we went with some rather high expectations. And let me say they far exceeded those high expectations. My wife Donna, whose is a much harsher critic than I am said "Best Meal I ever had in SJ" then added, "Maybe better then the meals we had in Italy"

The Fennel Sausage and Broccoli Rabe app along with the roasted artichoke hearts with Mozzarella and tomato were truly amazing. simple ingredients and amazing tastes. For our pasta course we had the Spinach Gnocchi that was delicious . and the Pesto, that was as good if not better than the pesto in Cinque Terra Italy. For entrees Donna had the Orata which she raved about and I had the Bistecca Enna which was amazing 

If you are looking for Chicken Parm or Meatballs or American Italian Food, than this is not for you. But if you want simple authentic Italian food like you would order in Italy then I say book a reservation right away because you will not be disappointed.
I've been going to Alex's for a long time. Just good ol' BBQ. Nothing wrong with that...

I like this place because you can go with your non vegan friends and they won't be like ewww. I go here every single time I visit philly and it's definitely my go to if I have a sweet tooth or am missing the flavor of chicken!

Here is the deal with this place: It's not the most luxurious or friendly place (it's Clearview y'all), but they are super efficient and they do get you in and out SUPER quick. So if you're just looking to get a quick manicure or pedicure and don't care about making best friends with anyone than I say this is an ideal place to go. I rarely have I had to wait for a service here but I also try to hit up the nail salons at really off hours to avoid waiting. I detest this whole new chic nail salon culture where all these salons have suddenly started demanding appointments and refuse walk-ins. I mean, ain't nobody got time for that! Also, they have a lot of gel polish colors and regular polish colors and I've always gotten a very thorough and great looking pedicure from them. And yes, they do have massage chairs :-)
Great job of adjusting glasses.

Bad service. I've eaten inside there a few times and one time they sat us near the back then left the patio door open the whole time except for 5 minutes after I asked them to close it then it was propped back open again. Another time just not attentive and never came to our table. I've attempted to get carry out from there twice. The first time they lot my order so I had to wait 20 minutes after my pickup time for them to actually make it. Second time I called them and was put on hold for literally fifteen minutes- they never answered again. I just went to restaurant (still on hold), asked to speak to the manager and showed him the call before I hung up. They had plenty of staff and only 3 tables besides 1 group of 3 at the bar. Eventually they found the phone muted by the bartender who acted like she had no idea. The manager apologized (not the bartender) but nothing was done- not even my appetizer comped. Very disappointing. There's plenty of other places in the area with great food and service I'll go instead.

Dominic's Trattoria was chosen as the destination for a special family celebration on a Saturday night in November. We had a party of 13 and they have a small semiprivate room which they sat us in. I ordered the Veal Fontina (sautéed in a white wine mushroom sauce) with a side of penne pasta with red sauce. My meal was tasty and well prepared but slightly cold. There were 12 other orders at the table and unfortunately not everyone got to eat at exactly the same time. Obviously this was the kitchen's fault and not the waiter. The waiter kept drinks filled and responded to requests as timely as possible. Our waiter was very good but I think he had a bit too much on his plate that evening. The room was a touch small for 13 people and I felt a little claustrophobic. Definitely an older crowd in here. I'm 41 and I think I was in the running for youngest person in the whole place! I think I'm at a 3.5 for this one but can't in good conscious round up so 3 stars it is.

Great place for lunch during the week.  Very cool little place to stop in in the middle of the day and have some good food and a drink.  Food is phenomenal.  I would definitely recommend the hot roast beef with roast beef gravy and horseradish on the side.  

I've been here a couple of times for lunch but never for dinner or the weekends but they have a very nice menu.  Can't wait till summer time comes so I can hang out on the deck bar.

The hostess, Chris, was a complete ass! I arrived and asked for a table for a party of 2 and was told I would have to wait until the 2nd person showed up. I told Chris I would like to go ahead and order, but nope he would not seat me at a table!
They are good. Maybe it's my preference to another favourite Thai place I have, but their tom yum or kah isn't as tasty as comparison. The pad Thai is great.

I am so sad to see this place is closed. Circa 2009 my wife and I were there three days staying just down the street and ate there for breakfast on the second and third mornings - and wished we'd found it the first morning and we would have made it a triple.

My wife loved whatever she ate enough to want to return and I had the crayfish benedict both mornings. I have ever since called it the best breakfast I've ever had and I have long wanted to return just to eat there again. 

The place was charming and it seemed like a hidden find/treasure (which, if true, might not be the best for keeping busy).

Alas, I guess I'll have to settle for my second best breakfast, eggs bennedict at http://www.yelp.com/biz/sneakers-bistro-and-cafe-winooski?
Delicious food and great service. This was our first time and we will definitely be back!

Great breakfast for a great price. This place is tucked away from the main streets here in Clearwater Beach, but only a short walk away from the Hilton where I'm staying. Definitely worth the extra half-block to walk. Their outdoor seating affords more sun and atmosphere than most places on Mandalay ave.

Their croissant breakfast sandwich was a meal enough by itself, with the perfect amount of egg and cheese plus thick-cut bacon. The homefries reminded me of a very home-cooked feel, but may need salt for some folks.
I found these guys on this website.  They did an excellent job moving my stuff and nothing was broken.  I highly recommend.

Insured, Licensed and Bonded with very reasonable rates.

Absolutely great service and I will never leave my pet at a kennel again!  Eric, Jennifer and Celia are great!  They email you with a personal report after every visit so you know your cherished pets are loved.  

No more kennel cough, stinky fur, diarreah or haunted dreams from the pooches after a lengthy or short trip.  They'll also retrieve your mail, water your plants and turn on/off lights while you're gone.  A complete red-carpet experience!
We are back what more can I say. Friendly good service  the home made (free) are addictive.

Look no further! This is where you want to get your alterations done! I have been here twice and both experiences have been so quick and easy. Not to mention, the people that work here are extremely friendly and understand exactly what you're looking to get done. I just brought an item in today and didn't realize they were going to be closed until after New Years and I had an outfit I needed for NYE. Without hesitation, she told me she would have it done the same day and she wouldn't charge me any extra for rush alterations. Boom- outfit done in LESS THAN THREE HOURS! I can't say enough good things. Just go see them if you need alterations done in the Nashville area!
Dr. Charbonnet is a great and thorough dermatologist. I have brought all of my kids to see her and she is great with them as well.

Cute place. Huevos Rancheros were prepared well, although it seems a bit overpriced at $12 a plate. I almost feel like I can walk to the 99 cent store down the street and buy a can of beans/bag of tostadas to make it myself. 

I did enjoy the salsas though; they all tasted very bright and fresh.

The Coffee Cake is fine, but a bit dry after I asked them to re-heat it. I probably wouldn't ask them to re-heat it again.

They don't use numbers for your orders; they use emojis. So you'll have waiters come up to your table and ask "Are you unicorn/moustache face/batman?" It's a little absurd; it almost feels like it should be a joke on Parks and Rec that parodies millennial culture.

But it's still a cute place to get brunch.

We always get great service and good food from Pinas.   We have been eating there for years.    They know all their customers by name which makes us feel special.   Love their pizza and steak sandwiches.

I'm slightly conflicted about this because I came here strictly for the chicken Marsala as it's one of my favorite dishes.  My date's dish, the lobster ravioli had delicious scallops, pretty good shrimp, and I really didn't care for the lobster ravioli.  The lobster seemed slightly rubbery and not all that flavorful.

Onto the Marsala, unless there is something I'm not very aware of as far as the potential differences between a Naples Marsala and a northern Marsala, I'm gonna go ahead and come out and say that this isn't Marsala - and this is coming from someone that generally likes a tradish Marsala, then add some heavy whipping cream to the sauce.  This one is just too creamy.  I could barely detect that the chicken itself was cooked in a little bit of Marsala wine, but the creamy mushroomy sauce just completely dominated.  

I still gave it 4 stars, though, because I love places like this, and really, all of the food was cooked very well - nothing burned, dry, etc., but unless they change the Marsala sauce, I won't be back.  Also, the service was very good, and the owner hugged almost every person that walked through the door.  I'm assuming all of the 5 star reviewers really like hugs.
Very good authentic Mexican food. Tamales are excellent and always fresh. I'm a regular at this place. Great prices and good service. Quick service nice atmosphere.

Great burgers at a great price.

I came to Spot for lunch with my coworker earlier, and we were both really impressed with the menu, the burgers, and the service. Spot offers a pretty unique menu (burgers with everything from blue cheese to pickled daikon and gochujung paste) which is definitely enough to bring people in, but it's the juicy burgers, toasted buns, fresh veggies, and great flavors that will keep them coming back. 

We got the cheese-fries (fresh and good but nothing that'll blow your mind), the spot burger, and the umami burger. 

The spot burger was classic with a twist: a beef burger with bacon and chedder, pickles, coleslaw, and spot sauce. The pickles and slaw kept the burger tasting really fresh/not overwhelmingly meaty. 

The umami burger was definitely a bit heavier, but also more flavorful: grilled onions, mushrooms, pickled diakon, cucumber, gochujung, teriyaki, lettuce. I thought it was really great, the flavors were definitely there, but it was a bit too heavy for me so I couldn't finish my half. Definitely not something to get if you're trying to find something light!

Overally I was impressed, and I'd definitely be willing to come back again on a day when I'm really craving a burger! 

*The guys sitting next to me said they come about 2-3 times per week, and they've yet to try something they don't like. I believe it.
Went to this Starbucks today, first visit. Everything ok.  One of their smaller facilities, but enough space where you could sit and do work on a laptop.

I always like the chill ambiance of this pub. It's nestled off on a quieter part of 17th street and you could actually miss the sign if you aren't paying attention. 
I ordered a dirty martini and the seared tuna salad with shaved celery and beets on Bibb lettuce and my friends had the black sheep burger with Gouda and a portabella mushroom... Both were very tasty. In fact my friend said that it was the best burger in the city!

I used to go to elavation. I really liked the grass fed burger, fries, and shakes. But over time, this place has turned into a dirty, greasy, grimy, place. 

You have to wonder, if a place doesn't keep the front of the house clean, what does the back look like. I'm going to stick with shake shack for my burger needs. EB needs to clean house.

Don't work here either. The people are ignorant.

Ah, U-Haul.  I love your sticky miserable aisles and interminable waits.  NOT!   I reserved a trailer and scheduled a hitch appointment online.  I paid for the hitch online.  In the store, they assured me I had not paid and charged me again for the hitch.  Come to find out they had double charged me.  Joke's on me!  It was very difficult to get my money refunded- 2 calls to corporate and no one could do anything.  Finally I got my money on the morning I picked up the trailer.  I can't blame the employees- they are a product of their environment.  I know when I move again I will have to use U-Haul.  But I will not enjoy it.
Wonderful, attentive service and amazing food.  I have never been disappointed with any of the appetizers, entrées or desserts that I have ordered here.

I called due to a dental emergency and was given a same day appt. Dr. Cabrera was excellent. He extracted two teeth for me and performed a bone graft. It was painless! The entire staff was very pleasant and helpful. I would recommend their practice to anyone.

Been to a couple Q'Doba locations and this is the best. Friendly and very helpful servers. Yummy food! Queso and guac..what more do you need. Speaking of guac, I LOVE theirs. Creamy and chunky. I'm gonna go get some now.

I'm really disappointed with this franchise Krispy Kreme. I've noticed that if you forget to tell them "fresh donuts" you'll get day old or two day old donuts. You know they're old when the icing is invisible and the donut looks plastic. I bought 3 dozen for work and they were happy at the thought and alot of them said "well we just pop them in the microwave." No, absolutely not!!! I paid full price for supposedly fresh donuts and you shouldn't have to "pop them in the microwave!" Always request "fresh made!" I hate I didn't look at them before I left, but you shouldn't have to. This was the second time this has happened and I thought I'd leave a review this time. So disappointed! If you're going to sell old donuts at least discount them first! Not sure if I'll go back to this location!

We were supposed to wait 45 minutes but it was only a 20 min wait. The service was quick, and the rustic environment was mixed with a sporty vibe. The food was very good, and moderately priced. The pickle chips were really good. Will definitely return.

They blend all of the Ingredients together on the bowl items. So essentially you are eating a smoothie with granola and honey.. I have had acai in San Diego and in the Gulf Coast area that was great and in my opinion how acai bowls should be. Acai base and then a multitude of toppings that you can eat, not a smoothie in a bowl. Not impressed. It's not horrible, but I wouldn't go there again. I asked why they blend it all and they said it is because the ingredients are frozen. Assuming they do this to cut down on costs. If you want to have toppings to eat that are not blended then it's a dollar a piece. Granola and honey are good.

The best apple cider donuts I have ever had! These are hands down my favorite and I have been coming here since I was a kid. Now this place has changed radically since then as it used to be an actual orchard with pick your own apples and pumpkins and hayrides, but the donuts at least have not changed. Where other apple cider donuts are heavy and greasy, these are light and airy. When you get them right out of the fryer and the cinnamon and sugar is on yours hands, perfection. 

They also do all you can eat nights and brunch. I have been to the pasta night on Thursdays, and it is a good bargain for your money, but it is not going to be the best pasta you have ever eaten. It is more of a get what you pay for situation. Again the same experience with brunch. It is consistently good food, but it isn't going to blow you away. Except the donut french toast is pretty neat. They cut the donut in half and cook it like it's french toast. That is pretty great. 

This place is also a BYOB which is always great. They have this one room upstairs which is hung with lights and branches and looks like a pinterest-worthy area to have a lady's brunch. Something I may have to convince my friends to try.

I stop in usually 2-3 times a month.  Good bar food...wings, pizza, burgers, mussels, etc...My one complaint is that the pint glasses for all of the great beer on tap are often warm since they come right out of the dishwasher.  I appreciate a clean glass, but you need to find a way to get the glasses chilled.

I have been living in Fountain Square for a couple years and always said there needs to be a deli or butcher. Alas, my prayers were answered with Turchetti's and was so excited to try out the deli when it opened up. My girlfriend got the gem salad and she said it was incredible! The dehydrated then rehydrated tomato based vinaigrette was top notch. I got the Risino sandwich and I only have one word: delectable. The meats were tasty and you could tell they were fresh and had some love out into the process. Definitely will be coming back again and buying as many meats as possible!
Loved the boat and the trip but the supper is trash. I mean come on - this is NOLA where the food is great everywhere... except on this boat. Do yourself a favor and skip the supper.
A great atmospheric place to take out-of-towners for brunch, and it's not a tourist trap.  Our meals were scrumptious.  This place is legit.

Oh yum.  I like the ambiance in here.  I had a couple Abitas and the roast beef, which was amazing- served on fresh bread with a gravy and also oysters.  I scarfed the whole thing down, practically in one bite.  

Aside from kicking myself for forgetting to pick up a matchbook to add to my collection, this was an A+ experience.

The food here is always wonderful. The flavors all seem fresh and detailed. No dish taste like the other and it comes out quickly. Please do not let the illusion of small portion sizes turn you away. In fact, it is properly serve were you wont leave hungry or sluggish. My only suggestion is that if you have a party more than 2, to call ahead.
