Meh. It's not New York quantity or quality, but has a New York price tag... I was charged to change from Swiss to provolone cheese, $13 for a lunchbox sized sandwich  ($7.50 for a half-sandwich!!!), overcooked corned beef, not worth the 'gasp' price.
They have a kaoroke area! So love this place. Food was amazing. Enjoyed myself in karaoke area. I will definitely come back.

While traveling on business to Philly we visited R2L. The view was spectacular but the decor was bizzare. Who cares though, when you have a steak like the 28-Day Dry Aged 20 oz. Bone-In Ribeye with steak fries, maitake mushroom, black garlic + bearnaise sauce. We ordered the lobster mac side. This dish was lovely and well worth the price tag. Tasty! WOuld highly recommend.

As far as neighborhood 'bodegas' go, Citi Market is as good as it gets. Clean, open, and airy, they have an ideal selection of everyday basics, fresh produce, and healthy (and not so healthy) snacks, with a focus on the organic. 

Amazing vegetarian/vegan options, including tofutti for bagels (halle-freakin'-lujah), and pre-packaged Singapore noodles that I crave on a biweekly basis. 

Citi Market has saved the day (or dinner) on many occasions, when I am just too exhausted or busy to cook. It's a bit pricey, but the convenience is worth it.

Excellent, excellent food. Beautiful decor. Service was very poor.
I had the lobster ravioli and it was different then any other, but near mouth watering. I finished the plate. She had the Cesar salad and salmon which was excellent!
As I mentioned the service as "catch as you can" with waiter's walking right by you with a full water pitcher yet not filling your empty glass. We had to flag down a person to order.
I would easily eat there again. And be prepared for ho-hum service.
With a snap and intuitive service team I would have given this place 4+ to 5-star. But as it is, 4-star is high s she goes.

I've been here twice and I have a bit of a mixed review.

A few months back I came in and had sushi-- the sushi is good, tasty, fresh, and well-prepared. I enjoyed it and thought the next time I'd try some of the fried offerings.

We went last night and started with calamari. They were a bit dense and the breading was relatively flavorless-- I didn't ask if they were frozen, but it tasted like they were. We had a pick two plattered and shared-- Haddock and Chicken. The portion size was great. The slaw and fries were delicious. The chicken fingers were from frozen and not that good. They were like dense little morsels of dried meat.  The Haddock was 10 ounces and was just like any other standard fried fish. One chicken finget and piece of fish in I was done, the fried quotient reached, the oil seeping through my pours. I don't plan to come back for the fried seafood. I know this is a beloved spot by many, but I was just not that impressed.

Horrible experience. The service was awful (it took our waitress 3 tries to get our order correct) and the bar had barely anything available beer wise. Making things worse, the pub forgot the food order and after our first round of drinks we never saw a server again. We won't be back.

Henry is the man. Zoe is the woman. Everyone stop complaining. I was only here for 24 hours, but I enjoyed the hospitality of Philly; especially Craft House and Victoria's Pizza, but maybe I'm easy to please :-p

Came here on a Wednesday night after work around 6pm or so. Grabbed a couple of seats at the bar. Very cool layout and design. Definitely doesn't feel like nashville in there and not your typical bar decor. Had a couple signature drinks with tequila. Both outstanding cocktails. Finished off with a beer from Blackberry Farm that they had which was also very good. We shared a plate of their fingerling potatoes and they were delicious! Highly recommended and we will be back again. Very attentive bartender too.

I'm so happy The Libertine is in Indy.  I think the Seelbach is my new favorite cocktail.  We sampled a number of their offerings including oysters, the warm mushrooms salad, the beet salad, deviled eggs (three different kinds!), and the lamb neck rillette.  Everything was very good but the lamb rillette was my favorite.  

As mentioned previously plates are small.  I personally love this about The Libertine as I got to try so many of their tasty dishes.

I can't wait to go back to try more cocktails and food.

Oh one other thing.  I think they are the only place in Indianapolis that offers Fernet at the bar.  For that alone, they get 5 stars.

This place looks like a real bagel place, but those hard round things were not real bagels.

No complaints about the service or the prices.

Sbraga is the man!  Every single dish we ordered was outstanding. We started off w a few drinks- Mezcal, apple brandy, honey and lemon (forget the name), the lil hillbilly which is a watermelon white whiskey drink and a flight of the Rittenhouse rye brewed right in Rittenhouse. They were all delicious. After that we got right to it!  Started off with the smoked ricotta tomato salad. The ricotta literally melts in your mouth. Amazing!  The next two dishes came out in a piping hot skillet, the cornbread and sweet potato casserole. Both equally delicious. Next up, the shrimp and grits which turned my non grits liking boyfriend into a fan haha so so good!  The pulled pork w grilled peaches was also very good, but finally the hot chicken made its grand entrance and holy hell I could eat this dish every single day for breakfast, lunch and dinner. The perfectly spiced chicken sits atop a piece of toast smothered in a buttermilk ranch dressing w pickles. My dream come true on a plate and my fav dish of the night. We also can't forget about the homemade hot sauce that sits on every table. I love hot sauce and don't get me wrong, this hot sauce is the bomb, but I found myself not wanting to use it bc the food was just that good. 

Finally, we had dessert. I called ahead and told them it was my boyfriends bday so they surprised him w the Mississippi mud pie and I of course had to try the red velvet cake. I mean everybody needs cake on their birthday, right?! 

This place is a southern lovin' dream come true and we had an overall great dining experience. Shout out to Amy (I think) our server who was excellent. We can't wait to come back!

Great drinks and great vibe! We went twice on our visit to New Orleans. It was recommended by a native to the city so it's close to Bourbon but it's got a local vibe. Two live bands every night, no cover, a great cocktails.

Birchtree made our wedding an incredible experience for all. They were a pleasure to work with, had an amazing eye for design, made a mean cocktail and best of all - cooked up a delicious menu! 

We had several people tell us that they've never had such fresh and tasty wedding food. Our menu was Pescetarian, and they didn't bat an eye coming up delicious with options for all guests. 

Best of all, they put my wife's mind at-ease, knowing that the wedding of her dreams/designs would be perfectly executed. They kept the wedding moving like clockwork the day of. We highly recommend Birchtree!

I'm all about the Mesquite Chicken Salad!  The honey-lime vinaigrette is very tasty with nicely seasoned veggies.  What I really love are the chips and salsa.  They bring the chips out nice and warm to your table.  If you catch this place at happy hour, however, you probably won't get to enjoy any food.  There are people for days.  Nonetheless, their company is great with flat screen TV's all over the place.
Absolutely delicious!! The service is perfect and the food is amazing! I had the bacon wrapped meatloaf before heading to the airport to go home, so worth a visit! Seriously, just go :)

Fantastic Bloody Mary.

I had to update my review to give them props on their Bloody Marys. I made my own at Gaspar's Grotto's Booze Cruise Brunch earlier that day, so maybe that's what made the difference so jarring. I have to admit, I enjoy drinking Bloody Marys, but I wouldn't say I'm adept at making them. When I found out they had a $5 special on Bloody Marys, I was sold. Boy, am I glad I tried it. It had the perfect amount of spice and they even had Bloody Mary spiced salt around the rim! That kicked it up a notch for me.   

I had a chance to appreciate the décor since it was the middle of the day. I really enjoy the bright colors of the tables. It reminds me of Key West. They also had live music playing on a Sunday. You can tip the guy and request a song. It's a very low key hang out spot that just screams Florida. This is one of those places you bring an out of state friend to on a boozy Sunday.

Overall very pleased with the service I got from Music City Optical. I was able to book an appointment without difficulty, and ended up lasting a little under an hour (even as a new patient). My prescriptions were quickly updated and I was sent away with a few trial contacts. Staff is friendly, they helped me navigate what my insurance covers (or doesn't). Finding the parking lot was a little tricky, as there are many one way streets.

Below average 12$ cheeseburger. Small and underseasoned. California BLT, probably decent but kitchen cheaped out and used the butt end of the loaf of bread. Out of first 3 beer choices I selected. Will not return.
The best taco I have ever had!  Seared Ahu Tuna Taco,  I can't wait to visit Tampa just for this place!

So, so, SO good, there aren't words to describe it! Great atmosphere, outstanding food (one of the best Chile Rellenos I've had the pleasure of having), and great happy hour specials on the wine. Our server was very friendly and spot-on with all of his recommendations, and I can't wait to go back with more room to try to desserts!

The food at Ralph's on The Park was good, buit its the location, the view and the atmosphere that makes this place so special. We liked it so much we decided to have our wedding reception here. 

Went for dinner on Friday night. We ordered the oyster appetizer which was dissapointing but they served a big hunk of french bread and whipped butter with it, so all was not lost. I ordered the BBQ shrimp at the reccomendaiton of our server. It was rich and delicious. My fiance ordered the lamb chop. He also enjoyed his. 

The room for or reception is just beautiful, and the private bar on the balcony really sealed the deal for me. I can't hardly wait till the big day.

This elegant yet plain bakery boasts some of the best baked goods I have EVER had bar none! 

You are greeted by a very clean store & friendly staff with minimal decor - none is needed - the beautiful baked choices are art in themselves! 

After oooh'ing and aah'ing, we decided on a Butterfingers brownie bar that was so decadent, a perfect giant slightly sugared peanut butter cookie and a mini densely delish cheese cake. 


Although I cannot frequent this gem too often as I 
Value fitting in my clothes, I will periodically treat myself here, spread the Devine word and surprise family at Thanksgiving with yumminess!!!!

    YOU HAVE TO TRY THIS BAKERY!!!

If I could I will give zero star for this place. The hostess was so rude. When we arrived there it was pouring rain and she asked us to step outside to think if we want to purchase the ticket to get in! No matter how good the music is, she ruined everything. $40 cover for is and she made us stand in rain to think about it, we walked and were so happy！

Their website doesn't lie, you really do wait in less of a line between 5-7pm Monday through Fridays. We went on a Tuesday evening around 6 once and drove right in. 
Also check out their website before you go, they now have a little map showing current wait times, pretty cool.

Dr. Berger and his staff have always been wonderful to us.  They have gotten busier in recent years but I appreciate their hard work and realize it is difficult to run a pediatric practice that is growing so quickly especially in this neighborhood.  They have a lot of parent classes where are helpful as well for parents to learn about all types of things.

Best diner in SJ IMHO. my girl and have been enjoying Sunday breakfast here 4 years. Dinners are awesome too, food is always fresh and the chefs are top shelf. Very tasty food. Watch Sunday after 8am tho, parking tends to overflow to the street. Clears up after the after church family brunches and breakfasts are done.
Always worth the trip. Enjoy!

Upon entering the now Eagleville Tavern, the sign said to seat yourself. The bartender never acknowledged us or anything.  We sat and sat and sat and sat and sat. Totally being ignored for at least 15 minutes. Had I been hungry I wouldn't have hesitated to walk out. I expected this based on other reviews. Apparently a server or hostess doesn't show up til 4:30. 

The menu is decent. I ordered the Cobb Salad. Once we got a server things improved. She took our order and the food came out in a reasonable amount of time. I thought the prices were fair and the portions seemed good. The Cobb salad was good w avocado, bacon, tomato, blue cheese crumbles and ranch on the side as requested. The server checked back w us after a while. I think it's ridiculous to charge 35 cents extra for honey-mustard sauce. 

I won't likely be back as I hate being ignored.

CASH ONLY, just a heads up.

With lots of diners to choose from around this area, I would have expected better service my first time here. I arrived excited, noting to my boyfriend that I think I had read good reviews for this diner. When we walked in I was surprised by the size, but I have been too much smaller diners. Walking by the register, I received no eye contact from the three waitresses crammed behind the counter. Not even so much as a "hello". I understand they may not want to be working on a Saturday morning, but at least the hello would be nice. One waitress seems to be annoyed by our presence, eyeing us up as we try to find our seats. We are obviously first timers to this establishment, but there is no help or sign that says to seat yourself or otherwise...very uncomfortable. We almost left. 

After sitting at the counter, I was unsure if we were going to be helped. the gentleman next to us was helped right away but yet again there was no eye contact given from waitress, even a simple "I'll be right with you" would've sufficed. We ended up getting a very nice waitress. The one working tables seemed to be having a bad day with all the whispering and eye dodging she was doing in front of us?...

The food was typical diner food, small portions as other ratings have mentioned. Unfortunately, my boyfriend did find a hair in his omelette. He did not mention this until we left as he steps lightly in those situations. Prices are far better at diners down the road.

We were supposed to stay at this hotel for two days this week for my husband's business trip.  In fact, he was the speaker for one of the conference events in the hotel, so the room was to be complimentary for us.  When we checked in, I was impressed by the look of the lobby, although the exterior of the hotel looks rather dated.  
After being given our room keys, we headed down a long hallway to our room, and I started to wonder if the carpet floors had recently been flooded because I thought I smelled water damage.  The smell got worse the further we walked, and after hearing a few dogs bark from behind closed room doors and seeing signs such as "Do not open door.  Chow inside", we realized that we were smelling dogs, and lots of them!

Now, I adore dogs, but I do not like sleeping in rooms that smell like a kennel, so we walked back to the front desk to asked to be placed in a room that is not one in which animals are kept, nor near the barking ones. On the way back down the hall, I saw tufts of dog hair on the carpet, and my eyes were watering by the time we made it to the lobby.  The front desk worker informed us that there were no rooms away from dogs, as 300 dogs were attending a "Chow Convention" in the hotel!  I said I was amazed that they did not warn guests who might have allergies, and that I could not believe that there were not rooms that are set aside for people who do not want to stay where a dog has stayed.  She said, "Well, we charge them a cleaning deposit".  My response was, "A lot of good that does us right now."
I next asked them to find us a room at a sister property, and she claimed that all king or queen-sized rooms were booked.  
So, we had to get on the Hilton site and find a room 10 miles away from this hotel where my husband had to work the next two days.
I just went in to see him at the hotel conference room here, and they have done a good job of trying to mask the kennel smell by spraying disinfectant or room deodorizer everywhere, but you can still get a whiff of the tell-tale sign of dogs.
Rest assured that if you stay in a room at this hotel, it is a room that a dog has stayed in, too.

Great find !!  I was in pain with my sciatica. My doctor didn't have any solution except for MRI's and pain meds. I was told that acupuncture was the only way to treat it by a friend. I finally went due to the severity of my pain. I'm so glad that I did!!! I'm completely out of pain and walking again! The school is a cozy little place with very friendly students and staff. From the moment that I walked in until the moment I left i felt that I was well taken care of. I was so surprised to find out that acupuncture can treat so many things. I'm going to use this resource for my health needs before I waste more time with my doctor. I learned that "well visits" are the way to go by practicing preventative medicine before things get out of control !!! ASAOM is a great place for acupuncture. Thanks ASAOM for healing me !!

Deciding to brave the sleet and icy weather, we ventured to Kampai. My expectations were high, as I took a final drag of my Seven Star Japanese cigarette. I stepped through the door tuggin' at my Buddhist bracelet I bought in Osaka not 10 days earlier. I immediately dived into the menu with Tako Yaki and gyoza flavors still lingering in my mind from recent travels abroad. The Tako Yaki was on point, it immediately took me back to a place of bliss. Followed by the gyoza which was astoundingly authentic. The portion size even resembled that of my previous actual japanese street vender order. I've had many a cup of miso, but none quite as delicious and exact to the flavor memory as this. I was beyond thrilled with the presentation of the Nigiri, from the Green onion garnish on my Otoro to the fine bits of ginger on my Ama Ebi, it was a perfect plate. The temperature of the fish was a little cold, but it was still amazing and honestly if it isn't the best sushi you've had in St. Louis, then you clearly have never eaten real Japanese food. I rounded out my order with a dish that is well known around my korean/japanese household, bulgogi. It was mixed with a lot more vegetable than I expected, but it was smoky and sweet and delicious. The vegetables themselves tasted like the food of gods. Overall I think this is hands down the best place for a sushi dining experience in St. Louis... And trust me I've been to them all, I mean all. The ambiance was stress free and the staff was very polite, so much so to the point We forgot what country we were in and started to speak Japanese to each other at the table. I will definitely be revisiting kampai weekly and it is getting moved to the top of my suggestion list to fellow sushi lovers.
One of the best Chinese food places around have been going here for years! Always fresh and well done!

Pretty decent spot for Sunday football watching. We couldn't make up where we wanted to sit [ended up on bar tables] and the hostess didn't mind. Our server [Mike?] was absolutely excellent - he had some type of 6th sense for knowing when we were ready to order drinks, food, and need refills. He gave us plenty of space since the 5 of us were knee-deep in football. Fried ravioli was shared by all - wish we ordered more! My body was needing carbs, deep-fried goodness and beer after waking up hungover. Thankfully the ravioli, HUGE bowl of tortellini and Schafly's had me feeling better. They don't have high-def TV's [downfall!!] so football game quality was poor, average at best. Surprised me that a restaurant doesn't have good tvs for being a sports-place. Definitely a place I want to revisit if I come back to St Louis. Hopefully they can fix up the TV's.

This food is really wonderful and authentic. They make a papaya salad (have to ask for, not on the menu) that is so good and fresh. This place is tiny, and seating can sometimes be an issue. The staff is very helpful and very friendly.

Great little hole-in-the-wall right next to the party area. One of the best burgers I've had nice juicy good tasting Burger. Fries are off-the-charts service was quick staff was awesome recommend this place for anybody that looking for a quick lunch going to try Philly cheesesteak next time

This hotel is walking distance from many major attractions in the French Quarters. Its close proximity to local hot spots was a huge plus for my family and I. My wife and I decided to bring our two young sons along and were very happy with how the employees helped us with directions, discount coupons and making the boys feel special... Shout out to 'D' he was a real class act! The hotel has a very unique style and has the feeling of a historic building. The beds were good and the room was comfy. This place is beautiful at night with their lighting and choices of outdoor decor. My only negative was the entry door to room 226 (my room) was hard to open and very noisy. I finally learned to pick up on the handle when closing the door. To be honest I would go back again in a heartbeat. Great staff, and great service. Just be prepared to pay for parking, sometimes that can be a surprise. It's around $27, plus tip if you're not stingy.

We normally have breakfast at Puckett's and it's usually quite good.   Tonight we went for dinner and that was not the case. Our food took over an hour to arrive while we enjoyed the terribly uncomfortable outdoor seating riddled with flies.  When our food did appear, our server made no mention of its tardiness.  My wife's food was hotter than the surface of the sun (microwave???) and mine was simply luke warm.  

I'm aware that everyone has a "off" night but we'll stick to breakfast at this establishment.

I want to just preface this review by saying, I'm so damn addicted to the pizza that I'm not sure if I have had anything else. 

I'm also reviewing delivery, since I only went in once for pickup. And you know what? It was freaking pleasant going in there, on a Friday, and they were so in tune with their customers that it didn't even feel busy. And when I stepped outside for a cigarette...they brought it out to me. Seriously? Chivalry is not dead. Points for you, Ciao's. 

So here's my review:

If I had known this place was in Trolley before I moved into the Square, I would have moved a month earlier. I love you, Ciao's. Did you get my Valentine's Day card?! My marriage proposal? I'm ready to move in and start a life together, Ciao's! 

Get their pizza.

Great little Italian bistro- casual attire solid Classic American Italian dishes at a fair price. I had the House Calzone and subbed the Genoa out for their homemade meatballs. My wife had the classic stuffed shells in sauce which came with a house salad & garlic knots. Both were prepared well & were generous portions. Our waitress, Kirsten, was helpful and took care of all our extra requests promptly.

OK, if you love trying food this is your place to go! The menu tasting is by far my favorite. I love that you can try so many different things. The chef does not disappoint with the selections. I will say my all time favorite dessert is the pistachio flan. That's a big deal coming from someone who loves chocolate.
Me and my cousin are traveling here. Love the decor, the one I had is too sweet for me, but I love the place.

The owners of Hotel Congress have just recently opened up this great restaurant and market located in the Historic Depot. They buy food locally when they can to serve in the restaurant & sell it in the market. The interior is beautifully restored! I really felt like I was taken to another place in time! I had a great lunch and the best soy latte I've ever had! A great addition to Tucson's growing downtown!

We drove the Trace today from Nashville to just past Corbett's Ferry....what a treasure.  SO quiet and beautiful.  Very little traffic and lots of wildlife sightings, including 4 dogs :(  Just being able to walk on the Trace for a short distance was so cool!  Everyone should do part or all of this drive sometime.

Easily one of my favorite bars in Philly.  The ultra-mod minimalist decor is very pleasing, and the fireplace makes it extremely cozy in cold weather.  The menu offers many delish entrees and snacks - my favorite is the mac 'n cheese.  I often come close to tears if I don't arrive before the kitchen closes at 1AM.

Another major plus to this relaxing spot is the friendly and attentive service.  Bartender Doug plays excellent tunes and will concoct a glorious cocktail upon request.  He recently fulfilled my request of mixing something inspired by George Michael.  Also, Ryan the server is extremely friendly and easy on the eyes.

You will catch me at Snack Bar at least once a week having a glass of wine with friends.
Amazing service  my drink was never empty my shrimp quesadilla was full of shrimp and the tortilla was homemade and was cooked perfectly
Top quality, fresh fish and flavorful ingredients. Generous portion for the price, too!

Let me start by saying.This place is awesome feels very futuristic.It feels like your in japan in a big city.The sushi is good.I have had really great sushi so it's not on that level.But for a quick clean healthy lunch it's great.Lots to choose from.Just for the experience alone it's worth visiting.

We went to Village Whiskey today after having waited outside until 12:15 for Frog Burger to not open *groan*.  I had been there once before for Dining Out For Life, and had enjoyed myself.  We ordered everything on the menu that time, and it was more a novelty dining experience than a real one (i.e. we were too drunk to notice anything).   

Today we told them we only had about half an hour, and they had our food out within 10 minutes.   Only downside is the price.  $5 for what are fairly run-of-the-mill fries is highway robbery.  However their burgers are quite tasty, and the service was friendly and accommodating.  If you're looking for a reliably good burger in Rittenhouse-- this would be the place to find it.
Cat fish poboy was full of fish and had ample filling-to-bread ratio. If only the fish was seasoned. At all. With anything. Bland and underwhelming :/

Urban Shabu is excellent. If you're a hot pot regular, you need to try this place.

The restaurant interior is clean and modern, with marble tabletops, contemporary plates and cutlery, new age chandeliers, and a "Bon Appetit" sign hovering over the sauces. The place is almost overrun with servers, who are ready to help you from the moment you enter the restaurant until you step outside the door.

We arrived around 7:15pm on a Thursday evening and were immediately seated. The restaurant, though fairly steady, wasn't nearly busy enough to be full. This is partly because the place is huge - similar to Kings - but also because weekend evenings are usually the most popular hot pot times.

We ordered our broth (HK Style Satay for myself; Tom Yum for Kylie) and a bottle of pinot noir (I love wine and hot pot). The servers checked on us a million times before we handed in our list of food items, but they weren't intrusive. They came by with an inquisitive look and could be sent off with a small shake of the head. At other restaurants, servers who come by too often can be annoying; at Urban Shabu, they're simply poised and ready to bring you what you need.

Once we got our food, though, they left us to it - hovering nearby just in case.
A note on the broth, before I get to the food: the satay soup is lovely. If you're allergic to peanuts, you're out of luck - it's as good as my favourite coconut satay broth from Bangkok Restaurant. The tom yum soup has a little more of a tangy taste, but it's delicious, too. With items like these on the menu, why would you even consider ordering the (boring) chicken broth?

We ordered way too much food, as I'm wont to do at hot pot. Everything was fresh and of a great quality, and they definitely don't skimp on the servings!

My favourites generally include the angus beef, marble beef, lobster balls, and crab sticks. I'm not too adventurous when it comes to hot pot, simply because I know what I like. I tried a mash, which wasn't to my tastes, and I had a few mussels, which (in my opinion) taste better when steamed in a red wine sauce. The fish balls were the same as everywhere else and the shrimp balls pleasantly reminded me of xia jiao (a dim sum dumpling).

Overall, I think I've found my new favourite hot pot joint. I still love Bangkok Restaurant's food and the owners there are lovely, but Urban Shabu has so much of the modern China feel and has many more items to choose from. Bangkok is a hidden gem; Urban Shabu is a well-known hotspot.

At $26 a person, it's pretty much the same price-wise as every other hot pot restaurant in the city. For two of us, with upgraded soup and a bottle of wine, it came to about $90. Not too shabby, Shabu. Not too shabby.

Nice breakfast spot where you can make your own hash! Our toast didn't come buttered, so you have to ask for butter or jam for your toast. We choose sausage, corn, spinach, pepper jack cheese, sweet potato and poached eggs with herb aioli. I didn't really taste the herb aioli, and regretted not getting the hollandaise. The place was cute, and relatively fast and some of the other food look really good, but our hash was just okay.

No more "shady car salesman" comments ... 

We just bought a used car at AMS Cars and we were totally and absolutely thrilled with the service and selection available at their lot. I know, I know. It's hard to believe, isn't it? We were amazed ourselves. We weren't rushed into anything, we had all our questions answered quickly, and we were allowed to test drive the car and take it in to our own mechanic before we purchased! We can't say anything bad about this place.

If you're in the market for a used car, check out AMS. You won't be sorry. You'll find something in their incredible inventory. Good luck!

This is one of my favorite restaurants in Nashville. The service is always amazing and the food is always fresh and perfectly cooked. The patio is perfect for an early dinner in spring or summer, while the dinning room is prefect lite for a later dinner. They have a great little bar down in the lobby if you get their early for your reservation and want to have a beer or drink. I have been here multiple times and have not been disappointed yet.

I came to Lao Bar on a Sunday night, so it was very relaxed. It was also one of the only places nearby open on a Sunday! What's up with that! People need to drink everyday of the week, especially right before returning to work on Monday. 

The bartender was nice and helpful. She recommend drinks off the cocktail menu to us, which was very helpful because I have never heard of over 50% of those ingredients. 

The drinks were good although a bit expensive. I really liked the way they decorated the place.
If I ever make it back to Tampa I will find a way to visit Naviera Coffee Mills again.  The coffee is that good.
I love the French toast, white Sangria is so refreshing, bartender is awesome and grill cheese was amazing.

Omg omg, I would marry the man that would bring me Captain Crunch Burrito, it is what I want on any special day. A friend of mine bought me one for my birthday, that was the best birthday present ever, my coworker use to get them for me. I left work early, I took personal time to go to this truck, but when I got there they were closing early, needless to say i was crushed.  Please open something next to the hospital of University, we need you.

I like this chain and its too bad we don't have it out East.  The burgers are satisfying, the shakes pretty darn good, the price is right, and you can't complain about their hours (they don't close!)

I'd prolly give them 5 stars after a good night out!

Was excited to see Marjie's open earlier this week! For my first meal, I tried the daily special (coal-grilled Sheepshead with citrus and dill) with three of their sides: sweet potatoes, crispy cabbage and radish salad, and braised greens. All were delicious. Fun casual atmosphere with a great beer selection. I'll be back to try more. Want to eat the whole menu.

Was there for a corporate boondoggle / dog and pony show / freebie.  Food was great.  Service absolutely the shits.  Sorry for the expletive, but there is no other way to describe the service.  We had this 40-something male waiter with a real attitude, acting like he was doing us a favor.  My filet mignon was really good, cooked just the way I ordered it.  Would have been a great night if the service was better. Would I go back?  Nahhh.  I'll try to find out how other steakhouses work before I spend my money in that establishment.

Today was my second massage at Indy Massage Co. and my first massage with Anna. She gave me a deep tissue massage which was out-of-this-world fantastic. You've heard the song, "Hurts so good." Well, I got a big dose of that. I walked in with a very sore back and several other pain points and walked out feeling like a new woman in the making. 

Thank you, Anna.
Crab cakes with poached eggs are so yummy!we got right in the view was beautiful looking at the st.louis cathedral and Jackson square ,everything was served in a timely manner

Here is all you need to know about Keri Ricci.  She sold our house, in Maple Shade. In less than 4 weeks.  In one of the coldest, snowiest Januaries on record. This is approximately 75% faster than the average days on market, and she negotiated an excellent price as well.  Keri set us up with a stager and professional photographer which I feel truly set our listing apart from others in our town.

Keri and everyone on her team are true professionals and experts in their field.  Over the course of selling our house and purchasing another, Keri gave us a lot of advice and suggestions, I will admit some of which I disagreed with at the time.  By the time we closed, I realized that every single piece of advice she gave us turned out to be 100% correct.

We are so happy with the service that Keri, Melissa, and everyone in her office has provided, and their results speak for themselves.  We give Keri our highest recommendation.

Spent a few days in Indy for work travel and happened to be walking by the Libertine... It was really cold and their street sign smartly said "warm up with whiskey" and that sounded like a pretty good idea....

It turned out to be a great idea!! I love great cocktails and appreciate the creativity, time and effort that goes into making them.  Barman Randy Gray was a my bartender and it's obvious that he takes his craft seriously. 

Talked about my whiskey and scotch likes and then he made a couple of phenomenal suggestions... Each drink seemed to be better than the last.... 

His own creation, Le Point du Jour was a bourbon masterpiece... Great spot for a chill evening, a date, or just to try to a new drink... Every time I head to Indy the Libertine will probably be my first stop for a cocktail....

Since I be been going to Cbq for the dancing and dinner I have made this establishment my home and have been telling everyone this is the place to be ,,and everyone that does come to experience this establishment they feel the same ,I wish they would allow more dancing on more nights and we can have a great place to dance more often ,,big thank you to the dj LJ and most of the management for doing this for us dancers

We were visiting St. Louis and looking for a place to eat and came across Calecos. 

Do. Not. Eat. Here.

The service was the worst service I have ever experienced. We got seated and it took 20 minutes after that before anyone even acknowledged us. One waiter came over and asked if anyone helped us and said he wasn't even sure who our server was but was great with noticing we were not being served and became our waiter that night. 
The potato skins appetizer was good. The wine was good. The salad was also very good. We thought despite the bad service, we'd be ok. It took another 15 mins before anyone took our food order and even longer before we got our main course. 
The entrees were horrible. Parts of it were inedible. My boyfriend asked for the cheesy vegetable option as his side but when it came it was pathetic, rubbery asparagus. We asked about it, the waiter said oh sorry, they ran out of cheesy vegetables. ...ok fine, but let us know that and ask  is if we want something else instead. 

The entire time it took about 45 minutes before we got our meals and 20 mins before we got the check. A couple of tables around is were also waiting a while and they were not that busy. 

What a waste of time and money. Truly horrendous and I will absolutely tell people to avoid this place.

Also, shortly after we left I spent my night with food poisoning.

I love Gray's.  I've been going for over 20 years and I still have enjoy is the same as my first time.

Meatloaf, baked tilapia, pork ribeye, and chicken parmesan are just a few of my favorites.

Their staff is great, they work with urgency and respect.

Chick-fil-A is open in Reno! As expected, the line for the drive through and to dine in was long, but surprisingly went fast. The service was great - the workers were courteous, and quick. I ordered the grilled chicken sandwich and nuggets for my kids. I was quite surprised how juicy and flavorful the grilled sandwich was. We've been to several Chick-fil-A restaurants in CA and Florida so my kids knew what to expect with the nuggets...and the nuggets did not disappoint. My 7 and 9 yr. old downed a 12 piece in a matter of minutes and raved about how good they were as they ate. For those who haven't been to Chick-fil-A, note that their sandwiches come without sauce, their classic chick-fil-a sandwich is a battered seasoned chicken breast on a bun with pickles. The cashier will ask you what sauce packets you want to go with it. They have various sauces, buffalo, honey mustard, ranch, siracha, barbecue, honey, and I think a few others. Kudos to the staff for making their grand opening a smooth one. Our Chick-Fil-A craving was fulfilled with our visit...I'm sure we'll be back.

These guys are awesome. I've been tattooed by PM and am currently getting something done by Andrew. I've been pierced by Josh and Johnny as well. My husband has a lot of work by PM and has had something done by John W. They're all really nice and reeeally good at what they do. They aren't cheap, but you're paying for quality work. If you're used to cheap work then...you probably have shi**y tattoos. Sorry.

I don't really like this place..I needed to find a place to fix my blood sugar with my boyfriend at the time.. and came across a Japanese restaurant in Santa Barbara..it felt like a sauna and I felt like I was at Bally's..ill totally gross..food not that great..and service slow..but Santa Barbara is a great place to shop and unwind..

Came in this morning with my girlfriend. We were seated quickly and our server John was excellent. He was very friendly and quick to serve us. He also made sure our coffee stayed full (and we had a lot). Food was very good as well. Look forward to coming back.
Excellent coffee, donuts, bagels, and sandwiches. Some of their best donuts run out quickly, but all delicious.  Gets quite busy in the weekends. Friendly staff.
Un maravilloso hotel tiene muchas comodidades.  Un buen personal. Las piscinas son limpias, el paisaje la comida todo muy rico. Tiene un buen olor.

First time in the door and the owner spoke to me like we were long time friends. His daughter was working that night and both were so friendly and welcoming. Their pizza is great! I got the Greek salad and a supreme pizza, enough food for two days! Thanks Slimms for the welcome to fishers

I just recently moved to the area and we had the Chinese food. I thought the vegetable lo main which is my absolute favorite was a little dry and not enough vegetables. The general tso's had more broccoli than chicken it should be the other way. I also tried the vegetable egg rolls and they weren't that tasty. So I usually give Chinese food places another chance so I will, please don't disappoint again. Thank you.

I love this place. I had a Groupon and tried 3 sandwiches: the goat, the craw gator and the mac n cheezy. The goat was the best! It had a sweetness to it that I loved and the mac n cheesy was my second favorite. The staff were all friendly and the place was very clean. I would say it's in the same category if a Chipotle or a Company Burger. It's a huge step up from fast food. I will be back, this is one of my new favorite places. Please build in metairie!
Iced Vanilla Latte, Vietnamese coffee, cold brew, chocolate chip cookie (sweet and salty) very good!

I usually visit Bks for lunch and did not realize it is a seated restaurant for dinner. A lively bar scene close to campus without the hassle of being on campus. 

The Sonoran dogs are a must try. The service was lacking. Our server, Lorena,  was rude and didn't refill our drinks once. Then at the end of the meal she asked if we needed anything else. My recommendation is to go for the food and not have expectations of good service for dinner time.

Good place to go for lunch.   The lunch special is great.   Give you a soup, appetizer and main dish for only $11.   All their curry dishes are above par and so are their vegetable dishes.   Had the coconut ice cream for dessert and it was fabulous.

I am not from Reno but had to drive in for business. The day I was due to give a presentation at a seminar, my car gave me an alert that my brakes were problematic. I pulled out the manual and concluded that this was nothing to take lightly, especially since I had to return the same day over the mountains. I called up Reno Vulcanizing Works and spoke to a gentleman. I wish I could state his name but if you get him on the phone, you'll know immediately it's him. He was very friendly, professional, and willing to accommodate my needs since I was on a very tight schedule with all I had going on that day. We worked things out, I led the first part of my presentation in the morning, dropped my car off at lunch and hitched a ride back to the seminar, and by the time I was done for the day, my brake pads had been replaced. During the afternoon, the mechanic left me a message asking to proceed with replacing the pads (they were down to 5%!!!) and I gave him the go ahead. When I got there to pick up the car, everyone was friendly. They  were very fair considering the predicament I was in. If I lived in Reno, I would definitely go back.

This is the best all you can eat because it is free on your birthday! We have come so many times just to bring friends on their birthday. Also includes appetizers in the all you can eat which not everybody does.

What an awesome place to see a show! My first show at marathon was a sold out James Bay show. The line went fast to get in, and it was very easy to get drinks. The bartenders are very friendly even during loud shows! 
The second show I saw was Jamie XX! Much different crowd than James Bay but an even better experience. It was the perfect venue for Jamie XX! Bathrooms were clean and the set up for the stage is perfect for viewing all around.
I won't skip an opportunity to see my favorite artists here.

I would say this hole in the wall in Cherry Hill serves the best Korean food in the area.  Food is consistent consistent!!
Even the owner's smile is consistent.  I would say I have tried just about all the dishes they serve and they are all good.  Soups and stews are the best and other dishes are well prepared as well.  Only thing I was not too crazy about was the wings.  KFC they prepare could use better seasoning.  Bit too over powering with oil (heavy) and sauce.  If they are frying a lot maybe they should use smaller portions of frying oil just for the wings and change it more frequently.  Also the batter on the soggy side.  Heavier (fresh) garlic would definitely help enhance the taste.  In Korea KFC is done in many variations but better places use very specific frying technique to leave a long lasting crunchy batter coating.  I don't think this place knows how to do that.  Overall seasoning and oil on the heavy side and that stops me from wanting another bite of the wings.
Can't really say because I didn't dine in. They seem to treat their take-out customers a bit less friendly. Maybe that's because they know they won't be getting a tip.
Breakfast.  Lunch. Brunch. With the girls or with the family.  The cutest place for tea and crumpets.   A must go to

Delicious! We got the roasted cauliflower (amazing) and the calamari to start, followed by the equally excellent Brussel sprouts Caesar, the black pepper spaghetti and the tuna bolognese. Everything was so fantastic and fresh, and our waitress was beyond helpful and friendly. A new place, and a great one. Cannot recommend more.

This Target is always clean and the staff is usually very helpful. 

What can I say, Target is my guilty pleasure and I live that I get 5% off with my Target Red Card! Love it!

Hey @Sloppy J ! I completely agree with you!
The main issue I have with this place is the crazy lady they having working as a manager. She cussed me out in front of the other customers for asking when my chicken flat bread would be ready. Why did I dare to ask when it would be ready ? I ordered two burger combo meals and the chicken flat bread. I asked if in addition to the buzzer for the burgers if I needed a number for the chicken flat bread. She said no I will put it all on the buzzer. Ok cool. The buzzer buzzes. On the counter is only the 2 burgers. Not wanting to let my wife watch us eat without any food, I asked about the chicken flat bread. That is when the manager started cussing and yelling at me telling me that one of her employees was in training. She slaps my food together and slams it on the counter. About 10 customers at two thirds of her staff watched her do this. 

This lady needs to be fired. The previous manager was a great guy. Always classy and polite. This lady clearly doesn't respect herself or her job.

I know in a beach tourist location that overpriced food comes with the territory but this lady is literally crazy. I would love for the owners to catch her behavior.
Even if you are a gold member your not going to get anything special.  Otherwise expect your bare basic!!

My family came to visit. The five of us ate here around 100pm. By 700pm we were all feeling ill, one by one. Three of us ended up in the hospital. Including my elderly mother. The other two were younger and were sick at home. In my opinion, we all ate a similar dish and shared. We ALL got sick. You decide....

First off, a great beer list. It's refreshing to see a restaurant that sees beer for what it is: an amazing complex beverage and not a poor man's wine. I greatly enjoyed pairing beers with appetizers, entree and dessert. It was no easy task with the limited but excellent tap selection and even more extensive bottled collection.

And I haven't even talked about the food yet. Crab cake and flatbread appetizers, excellent. Crispy duck, excellent. All three were well presented and cooked to perfection.

But most excellent, the cinnamon brioche bread pudding with caramelized bananas and banana creme freche. Even my wife who is usually not a fan of bread puddings absolutely loved the dessert. Save room for it.

My only complaint (and this should tell you how good the food was since I'm still giving it four stars) is that the staff is somewhat, shall we say, curt. Almost like they are too busy to care that much about what you want. I can put up with curt if the service is fast, but it wasn't fast enough to put up with curt. I have to knock off a star for service which is a shame because I REALLY wanted to give Alison Two five stars.

I came in and bought some flour tortillas. The gentlemen at the counter was very kind, and talkative which I appreciated. The tortillas were amazing! When I bought them they were still warm. I definitely want to come back and get a burrito. I've heard great things about them.

Brunch for the win! 
An order at the counter style resturant that offers brunch all day, this place serves a smaller menu which clearly ensures top quality and care. The food is delicious! My friend got biscuits and gravy with over-medium eggs and I got a traditional breakfast with scrambled eggs, toast, turkey sausage and two potatoes. 
The potatoes were served in a style I'd never had - small yellow potatoes served whole but crispy and so well seasoned on the outside. Similar to a breakfast baked potato. YUM. 

We also got lattes which are served in to-go cups so that you can take them with you. They have both dairy and soy milk. 

The smaller, intimate atmosphere is clean and well kept, the bathroom is large and offers a changing table, and the staff is very friendly. I would recommend this place to anyone who wants quality breakfast food!

We had less than a 5 minute wait on a Sunday morning   The atmosphere is cozy and quaint. The fresh squeezed oj is out of this works and I had the BEST eggs Benedict and mimosa I've ever had! The potatoes are light and perfectly cooked. Everything was seasoned to perfection.

Their menu was missing tons of things we are used to ordering from all u can eat sushi. The fish was not fresh and it seemed like they use frozen fish and thaw it or something. Low quality is what comes to mind. Unfortunately, they were so dead on the Saturday we went for lunch that all of the crystal shrimp was disgusting and soggy like cake batter... No mussels or green tea ice cream were offered. I explained how crappy the food was to the sushi chef who made it and all he had to share was laughing. So I would say if you wanted really funny bad sushi spend your 18$ and then hit Walmart for new chonies.... Avoid, there are other choices near by that take it a bit more serious.

This pizza place is tucked away next to Willa Jean. My sister brought me here a few days ago and I was pretty pleased with my experience. She ordered the signature BBQ chicken pizza with lemon basil beer and I ordered the green stripe pizza. After they fire up your pizza for 3 minutes you can add unlimited toppings all for $7.95! The portions were friendly and neither of us finished our pizza. These pizzas are fresh, thin, and light. 

Don't forget to check in to receive a free s'more which they also fire up to have it warm and melting for you.

We had a very attentive waiter. Service was good. 

Got the Yellowtail Roll and the Korean Spicy Wings for starters. The Yellowtail Roll was good - not amazing. I wouldn't come here just for sushi. I will be ordering the Korean Spicy Wings for take out! They were delicious - the executive chef does not send them with a dipping sauce (ranch for instance) which I get because he wants to showcase the Spicy Korean glaze sauce. However, I would have preferred a ranch sauce. 

We got the LB Burger and the Truck Stop burger. The LB Burger was a WOW. White TN Cheddar Cheese, Onion Jam and pork belly. The burger was also a perfect juicy medium/medium rare. A delightful combination of flavors. The Truck Stop burger is like a "West Coast" burger, 2 thin patties, "special sauce" (like big mac sauce) and big chunky pickles. This is was a good burger but I felt like since I was so used to the flavors I wasn't blown away. 

We got WAY too much food - it was all delicious and only around $60 dollars. Great value.
Lizzie is the best in the world. She loves humans. And all of them. I want her to be the American of the year. #america and #lizzie

Came here on an afternoon with my wife. The place was empty and the staff was standing around chit chatting yet it took nearly 5 mins for someone to come up to us and ask "do y'all need something?" Umm.. we came to eat? We ordered dumplings, some rib eye steak, and 2 bowls of ramen (pork belly and brisket). Dumplings was good, rib eye was tough. The ramens came out barely room temps and the broth was super super salty. Definitely will not be back.

A great local diner for those on the go. They take regular breakfast items and add a small bit of local flavor to it. While it won't be a memorable dining experience when I look back on my trip, it definitely got the job done.
Six North Turkey Club sweet potato chips and an ice tea! A great place to relax and have a good lunch!

Mark is very professional, competent, fair and a great communicator.

I am afraid to say this, but I trust him.

Pretty great little hipster place! We all loved our brunch, and the bloddy Mary's were definitely different, but sooo tasty! You better get there early and still be ready to wait. Absolutely worth it! Would highly recommend :)

I don't normally go to gimmicky/chain places but i had a gift card and figured I'd better use it. Service was very good. Which in my opinion can make sub par food better. The food was ok. The seafood did not taste like fresh seafood u would get in the quarter but it was not bad. Obviously the biscuits were great. Salads tasted very fresh and lobster was also very good. Again the food was ok. I could go get better seafood at a fraction of the price
My husband and I had the couples massage. It was awesome!  Very reasonably priced and excellent service!  Would highly recommend to anyone traveling to New Orleans or locals.

So fresh!!! Great family bakery, always smells WONDERFUL (who knew fresh loaf of wheat bread makes you want to use it as a pillow?!). Very PATIENT with my little ones who run around the store (they get bribed with cookies). The bread pudding is outstanding, very moist and comes with extra rum sauce on the side (not for the little ones). Because everything is made fresh, lots of stuff not always immediately available, best call ahead to make sure they have it. Additionally to sweets, lots of quiche, and my hubby's favorite sausage rolls croissants. Truly a hidden gem of the city.
OH my gosh!  I love mc Popsicle !  He was awesome!  Also the band was great!  For the first time in 13 years my husband danced with me!

I went to chickie and petes last night for dinner and it was the WORSE experience EVER.  Now don't get me wrong I have  been to chickie and petes on several occasions and it was a great experience BUT last night made me feel like I was on a bad episode of BAR RESCUE.

1.  when we walked in (party of 3) the women at the hostess booth were so busy in their own conversation to even acknowledge that someone walked in. we waited for about 1 minute before even being acknowledge (STRIKE ONE)

2.  after being seated the waitress came right over and asked us what were we drinking.  didn't give us a minute to even look at the menu.  after ordering the drinks (which came out very fast) we order our appetizers.  the appetizers came out very fast which was great.  but we finished the appetizers and waited a good 10 minutes before the waitress came over and took our ENTREE order (STRIKE TWO)

3.  Entrees come out  (which were pretty good) and we finished them.  the waitress never not once came over and asked us how are we, did we need anything, she basically never came to check on us.  when she finally came over we asked for boxes  because we couldn't eat the rest of the food.  she brought us the boxes and left.  for another 15 minutes before we flagged her down and asked her for the check.  (which she should of brought when she gave us the boxes).  (STRIKE THREE)

**oh did I mention that it wasn't crowded?  so there was no need for the POOR customer service.


bottom line -- the FOOD here is GREAT,  but the customer service SUCKS ASS BIG TIME.  The waitress we had was very lazy, unprofessional, and act like she was intimidated by us.  My company does a lot of business with sports bars in Philadelphia and because of last night I will have them reconsider their relationship with CHICKIE and PETES.

I will take GREAT customer service with mediocre food ANY DAY -- over POOR customer service and GREAT food..

You know, I was watching "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia" which I like to watch for nostalgic reasons and one character said something about another character having a crush on "That chick who works at Dirty Frank's." Seriously? I thought that was a dude.

Two things that are good about this place. Cheap, cheap, cheap lager and good jukebox.

Last time I was there, I heard "Bro Hymn" and five other people besides myself where singing the chorus. Good times, good times...

Good lunch menu and sushi is half of during lunch. 
The fish is tasty too. Can't complain. I was fortunate to have picked them. To have lunch.

AMAZING, You can't get these sauces anywhere else. The sushi is already great with out the sauces, but then they put that on top, you don't even need soy sauce. I have even seen people lick the plates! It is practically a whole in the wall, which makes it perfect for a cute date. I have tried sushi all over CA and you can't get better sushi than this. My personal favorite is the Hanabi roll. I suggest going with a group around 6:00 PM because after this the place gets very crowded due to their small space. I would suggest them to put 4 or 5 tables outside during the warm summer months.

Came here on points and was impressed by the entrance and lobby area. High vault d ceilings and water features as well as a very busy lobby lounge area. Checking in was quick and simple and were given an up grade to the 12th floor which has a spectacular view of Tampa Bay.
We went to our room to drop off our bags and were impressed with the rooms decor and amenities. Plenty of towels and supplies in bathroom as well as robes and slippers! Safe in room as well as refrigerator and coffee station. Wi-Fi information was no where to be found, had to call the front desk. 
We were hungry when we arrived free a day of traveling so we set out to find some dinner. The lobby lounge was packed with what must be a conference since some were on laptops. We ventured outside in the pleasant weather and described to take a walk on the Nature Path which leads to a connected resort. The pathway was clean and pretty offering a close up look at a mangrove as well as placards with the various birds and animals to be seen off the walk way. The path ends at the resort and the oystercatcher restaurant. We were taken in by the sunset and view from this location so we decided to stay for dinner.
We went in and were greeted by the backs of many people. We waited in line to find out the wait time and while waiting noticed the wire art work on the plain white walls, the birds Popped off the wall, very cool. The wait an hour and ten minutes even for one person! Not cool especially since across from the hostess stand there was a huge room with multiple tables all empty! So back to the hotel where there were plenty of tables we were greeted immediately and the prices were half the amount.
Drinks were perfect as was the service and food selection. Lots of build you own creations which was my selection. Grilled
Chicken, Boursin mashed potatoes and steamed asparagus. The chicken was well done with charred edges which made it dry on the edges, mashed potatoes were also a little on the dry side and the asparagus was perfect. Waitress was pleasant and ready to help if needed.
After dinner I had to get some Tylenol and had sticker SHOCK at the prices $6 for a small tube and $12 for a box. Captured audience for sure there is absolutely no where to go for necessary items such as this so they charge you astronomical prices. Shame on me for not packing some. 
Nice place but too pricey for a one night stay.

My boyfriend got my birthday cake here and it was such a treat. Everything there is SOO GOOD and it's constantly changing so you're always finding something new to like. my birthday is in August, and they had the best little arugula lemon salad. the only reason why I didn't give it 5 stars is because the staff are young kids who easily forget, or are not really quick. I do enjoy seeing young kids getting experience, but maybe a manager should show them a higher end service protocol, since the inside is definitely trying to channel it.
Amazing food! Service was fast and very sweet, if you're looking for some amazing breakfast in Nashville this is the place to go! Highly recommend!

This was a pleasant surprise.  Was totally expecting something else but decided to stick around and give it a try. The food was fresh, the service was awesome, and I will definitely be back.

I tried the honey and ricotta, then the 50 shades of lasagna and ended with a cupcake and champagne

This place is just a few streets away from my house (please don't stalk me!!) and somehow I managed to drive by without stopping for almost a year and a half! Well, No More! 

I have only been here for breakfast, but I have never been disappointed. I have enjoyed everything I've ordered there, and everything my boyfriend has ordered, for that matter. This includes: Omelets, fried eggs, hash browns, cream chipped beef, scrapple, bacon, and French toast. 

No one at Country House is that friendly, but who wants to be cheerfully yammered at when they are hungover on a Sunday morning, anyway? And I kind of wish they'd stop calling it a "Restaurant," when everything about it - decor, food, servers - screams, "DINER!!!!" 

If I ever go there for a meal other than breakfast, I'll update. For now: I'm a fan.

Omg hidden gem hole in the wall !!! Started off with the quesadillas which were amazing! And so was the salsa!  I had the fried chicken which was pretty decent!  taters and gravy was amazing too  great food great service ! Don't let the exterior fool you !

Just had a root canal done with Dr. Parrish a few weeks ago. I have had other root canals in the past, and none went as smoothly as this one. New to Philly, I was referred here by a friend and was not disappointed. The whole staff made me feel as comfortable as one can in a dentist's office, and I will definitely be getting all my teeth work done here in the future!

This place reminded me of a Bennigans.  Standard food but nothing special.  We stayed at a hotel downtown and besides the restaurant in the hotel, this looked like the only place open for lunch on a Sunday for blocks.  Very different from Chicago!  So we went into Calico's...

We were able to quickly get seats and the waitress was pretty attentive to our party of 7.  Appetizers and drinks came quickly.  Everyone ordered a sandwich or breakfast item which came pretty quickly after that and were nice and hot.  Prices are good for about $8 per item.

Really nice and quiet atmosphere with sweet and friendly owner who treated us and made us feel like we were dining in her home. It was pretty empty when we were there and I think opened not too long ago, which is part of why I felt compelled to write about how nice an experience I had to help grow word of mouth! Delicious and affordable food - try the massaman curry! Will definitely return and recommend to others :)

This place is great! A colleague and I went for lunch and were very impressed! Great service and Great food! The Vermont Burger i ordered immediately made this a "destination restaurant" for me. BUT,I also had a cup of the BEST cream of mushroom soup (I know, i cannot believe i am typing this). My colleague got the Ahi Tuna and he said it was VERY GOOD too. BTW - the prices are good too. The Vermont Burger and fries were only $11. Not too bad for a nice/higher end restaurant. Anyway, check this place out. It is great!

I've gotten two tattoos at Crimson. The first from Curt and the second from Jess. Both times I had a great experience and the tattoos were exactly what I wanted. Everyone at the shop was professional and helpful, one of the owners even called me a couple weeks after my first tattoo to check in and make sure I was happy. I highly recommend the artists at Crimson Empire and I'm sure I'll be back eventually.

Whether its a Sunday night or a Friday night, I expect service to be splendid. With the location being central downtown Tampa, my expectations were higher. Yes I'm not from around here but the value of any estate in downtown would mean the quality better be darn good to ensure customers to come back while having overvalued food.

First off the style of the place looks more like a coffee shop. Don't get me wrong the place looks great, but it's not a pizza parlor. To charge me for refill at the SAME cost when you own a fountain machine is ridiculous. To be cleaning while I'm cleaning right around me is a health hazard and that is just plain rude.

I'd be surprise to see this place up and running a year from now if they continue some of the things they do.

A very interesting replacement to the late night special LaPeniche. Horn's is a restaurant who's chef is one of my friends but on this occasion he was off and as I viewed the menu there were very few options. Saturday and Sunday are brunch days but I got there too late for that as they stop at 3pm. I did not want to order anything too outstanding since the head chef was not there so I got just a regular roast beef poboy featuring their house made beef daube. The sandwich was served on vietnamese style french bread and was very tasty but at $9 for just the sandwich and no side I thought that was a bit steep as the sandwich was not that big to stand alone. A great side would have been house made chips and then you could charge $10 with no problem. I assume that there are daily chef specials because the menu is a bit short and a tad over priced. Overall it seems that Horn's is one of these tweeners, white collar food in a blue collar style, but so far to be honest I long for the days of LaPaniche. I will be back for breakfast since that seems to be the most popular dishes served here or maybe a chef special or two.

The other reviews seem to say it all: the food just isn't that great.  Not to mention I came down with a terrible stomachache after eating here.  But, if you like your Indian food good and greasy - you're in the right place.

I think this restaurant could survive by my word-of-mouth alone ---but it's just that good!

We first showed up at The Workshop Eatery (Now known to us, simply as "Workshop") at the beginning of March to celebrate the successful end to my ESL teaching practicum before the coming of our little one. To say that I was utterly impressed would be an understatement! 

The meal was the best I'd had in months (yes, even as a pregnant lady), and needless to say we were back at Workshop within the week.... then again the next week two or three times, and the following week, same story..  And so it became that that by the time baby arrived, we were on a first name basis with the chef, hostess, and most of the wait staff, and we'd eaten our way through most of the menu. 

The good news is, the menu changes: It keeps a rhythm with what's growing outside (Literally, there's a garden on the other side of the window....and also, beehives on the roof!) and ingredients are fresh. 

The meals are wholesome, the portion sizes tend to be perfect, and they contain veggies - yummy amazing veggies! (A tip from the wise: you want a whole bowl of fried brussels sprouts. And you'll still be talking about them the following week too. You may even come back just for them!) 

Beyond the food, other things I like about Workshop:
- The service is incredibly attentive (I drink lots of water and they keep the glass full) 
- The setting is intimate. It can be the perfect place for a romantic date or a girl's night out (be sure to make reservations if you're planning either)
- The pricing is very reasonable.
- There's a chef's table option! (Talk to Chef Paul about organizing this, and be prepared to have your socks knocked off!) 

To conclude, the little one arrived later in March, and his first outing was Easter Brunch at Workshop. We've brought family along, recommended it to friends, and when we get out, it  still continues to be our favourite restaurant!

Cafe Ponte is a delightful alternative to lunch for the area. It's upscale, modern and really takes an inventive and edgy twist to their menu. You can tell a lot of TLC goes into creating a innovative menu that stands out from the rest and taste delicious to boot!  
Now, I've only gone for lunch but it's always packed with groups of business professionals, making it a great place for a work meeting or client meeting in an otherwise lacking industrial area. I met my girlfriend for lunch, and even though the patio and outside seating looked so enticing, the storm clouds were looming in the distance. Inside it has s bustling modern feel, open kitchen (so you. An see the freshness) and stocked with a full bar.  I do feel it necessary to mention that they do CLOSE AT 2, so plan to go earlier for lunch but they re-open for dinner around 5:30.
Their service is definitely not short of 5 stars....our waiter was prompt, precise, provided great input on menu items and had a super upbeat and happy attitude.  He made me feel like I was happy that he worked there, lol!  The manager was even on the floor, clearing tables, delivering food and chatting up the guests.  I got the fresh handmade goat cheese gnocchi with pistachio pesto and broccoli....light, fresh and DELICIOUS. And the mushroom soup is a MUST!!  The best soup I have probably ever had!!  My girlfriend got the mushroom soup as well (swoon ) and the lobster roll, which was filled to be brim with HUGE chunks of lobster....there had to be s whole lobster in it.  Not one of those tools that's all filler and breading!  Definitely worth the market price.

I've came here a few times and the last 2 times my order have been incorrect. I checked the receipt and the correct order was listed. I suggest to better train your staff and make sure they are paying attention to detail if not you will continue to lose customers. This is consistent trend.

Good Dining in a Strip Center

Five of us shared a lot of different menu items and, overall, it was very good.  The restaurant is small and fills up quickly.  The kitchen is right behind the bar.  Service is friendly and helpful.

This gastropub is beer and wine only and the selections are relatively good value.

For appetizers we started with the wonderful char siu pork ribs.  Then we moved on to the deviled eggs which were fine but the various individual elements didn't really come together.  Deviled egg capped with a piece of fried chicken thigh topped with some salmon roe didn't really work.  Much better deviled eggs at Z Grill in St Pete.  We also had an order of poutine.  The fries, served in a narrow basket, were good, but the gravy was only OK and the cheese curds were in large clumps that all melted into a bit of gooey mess.  It would have been better with the fries on an open bowl and, a better gravy, and crumbled cheese curds.

For entrees we had the fish special which was swordfish.  It was nicely cooked and the chimichurri sauce with it was delicious.  The short rib and the lamb shank were both quite nice and very heavy.  Very good was the farro risotto which was drier than a typical risotto and had a delightful nutty flavor.

For dessert we shared the pecan pie which was nice and the smore tart which was rich and delicious.

I had hoped that a few more things would be a home run like the pork rib appetizer.  Most everything was very good.

Let me say that right after dinner, I was going to give this place five stars... Now as I think back to dinner, there were a few things I would have liked to be different.  Let's call this 4.5 stars.

Our reservation was at 9:15, but the people at our table were taking their sweet time in leaving, so we had a drink at the bar -- the bartender was so much fun!  I normally just have gin & soda or a martini, but the cocktail menu was inviting -- not too much crap in the drinks, nothing sweet -- so I got the thing with gin and aperol.  It was really refreshing, but - as a guy - I was a little embarrassed by the rose petals on the top.

Anyway, we sat down around 9:30.  We didn't experience any of the service problems mentioned by other reviewers (and LaBan), but it was also later on in the evening, so who knows.  In any event, our servers were prompt, friendly, and knowledgeable.  I was a little annoyed, though, that no one came around with a crumb scraper.

So, the menu: prix fixe four courses, with five or six choices per course for $45 (+$30 for wine pairing), or prix fixe six course chef's tasting for $65 (+something for wine pairing).  The six courses that day were fish heavy, and didn't suit everyone at the table, so we didn't go for that.

I started with the (legendary?) foie gras soup -- it was great!  Creamy, but not heavy, with subtle flavors of the foie gras, lemongrass, and a little heat from chili peppers.  The soup was well paired with a sparkling rosé.

For the fish course, I had the black cod with miso glaze and kimchee.  The fish was perfectly seasoned and cooked, and the addition of apple slices to the kimchee was amazing.  The fish was paired with a Falanghina, which was ok, but didn't do it for me.

The meat course I chose was the lamb chop.  The chop was beautifully cooked, and was tender, juicy, and extremely flavorful.  This was paired with oatmeal (which the server addressed, and assured me it was cooked with lamb stock and tasted like a risotto) and pork belly.  Neither the oatmeal nor the pork belly had ANY flavor.  The consistency of the oatmeal did add something, but otherwise, I think the lamb could have been paired with something better.  I don't remember the wine this dish was paired with, but I remember it being just ok.

I had the mascarpone with coffee granita for dessert -- it was good, and was paired with a nice port.  I tasted someone else's hot chocolate mousse, though, and was really jealous.  The mousse was phenomenal, and I highly recommend it.

All in all, I highly recommend this place, and will definitely be back.  I think next time, though, I will choose my own wine.

Support your local bookstore! Fighting Hillsboro Road traffic can be a hassle, but Parnassus is totally worth stopping by when you're making your trek to Trader Joe's and Whole Foods anyway. Despite their size, their selection is pretty expansive and current and they're glad to special order a book for you. Another great thing about Parnassus? Guest speakers from both local and not-so-local writers on tour!
Pork sandwich was perfect, rice and beans was pretty good too. Its a hole in the wall, and the folks behind the counter were a bit confused, but all in all it hit the spot.

The drinks were cool and fun. The food was great. The service was a little slow though. One of the things we ordered was the creole pot. The waitress said stuff was meant to be shared. The creole pot was delicious, but soupy, and they only brought us the be spoon. It took a while to get more spoons. Other than that, it was good and I'd definitely go again!
Great pizza!  Great staff!  Just be sure that you are patient if you show up at dinner time, this place is always hopping!

Great food at affordable prices.  I thoroughly enjoyed my awesome tomato, basil, and mozzarella omelette with piping hot french fries at 1 pm in the middle of a busy day in downtown Philadelphia.

Loved the casual, welcoming ambiance.
Honestly I love this place but the music they play lately has gone downstream MAJOR!!! I don't want to hear the same bad 80s or Motown song on repeat ..... Seriously bad. GIVE ME SILENCE OVER THIS

What a great place.  The bar is the center piece, but the dining area is beautiful and quaint.  The food is memorizing, everything in pretty little packages.  The drinks are incredible.  The people are the best.  I will return!  Its in a line with a couple of the best places in south philly, great block!

My wife and I had a great time interacting with the cats here.  Most were very mellow and just relaxed around us.  One was adopted while we were there.  Worth the visit if you want to lower your own blood pressure.

Went there and we both ordered the combo steak and shrimp fajitas.  They were quite good and hit the spot.  Had not been to Chili's in awhile and noticed they revamped the menu.  Service was good and the place was pleasantly unpacked at 2:00 to 3:00 pm on a Sunday.
First time here...and whoa! Clam beignets!  That's right you heard me...clam beignets and they were good...this guy is unbelievable...laurel and ivt... omg! Go...go...go!

This place always has a DJ on the weekends so you have two problems:

1) Music that is too loud. I don't understand how people can stand around talking to each other.
2) You get to hear hip hop.

The crowd is a lot of 21 year old and early twenties people. Just not a place for this one.

When I moved to Ridley Park we tested a lot of places for good eats. China Wok is the best Chinese food around.  The order  is always right and the people couldn't be nicer. The food is great ever time.  Also very well priced. I say get food from here always.

Bab is a great place to go on your lunch break for something filling yet healthy! Although the bowl I got couldn't used some more flavor, I was so full after getting about halfway through, but didn't feel guilty at all since it was basically just vegetables. Definitely would recommend!

Just had dinner at Bluewater Grill, food was delicious I have to say what top it was the service all the staff there is great very attentive too your needs. Also Raul thank you for taking care of us great service.

The sales portion of the store is full of nice clothing with sales associates tending to you as if they are waiters at Antoine's, but everything is certainly overpriced. The rental portion of the store though is abyssmal. I have failed to ever have anything fit remotely correct; plus, the pricing reflects the clothing sales portion but without the service they provide "downstairs."

Luckily we went on a good day because the line wasn't too long, but we drove by yesterday and the line was insane. I had the Parisienne pancakes, they were soo good! My husband had the Swedish pancakes, they were not good at all, the filling had a bitter taste like the white part of a lemon skin. The fresh squeezed orange juice wasn't that good either. Since it came so highly recommended I also ordered one sweet potato pancake to try. I wasn't a big fan, but I also don't really like sweet potatoes so I may have a skewed opinion. The service was fast.
Service was excellent - cheerful, friendly  and prompt. But the cucumbers looked a little old.

This was awesome. I had never had Chicago style pizza before and I was super excited to try it. The restaurant was clean and nice the staff was super nice. The pizza was cooked perfectly with a crispy crust, lots of cheese and fresh sauce. The calamari was so crispy and a fun twist with the fried lemon and artichoke in there as well. We had a tiny mix up that we didn't even care about and yet the waitress and manager treated us so nicely. Thank you!

G.O.B. sale was a waste of time.
