but thankfully, places like square peg get the attention they deserve. it took be about ten minutes to get past the first six feet of the shop. i wanted to touch (and buy) everything i saw and was barely successful in buying more for those on my shopping list than i was for myself. i am not going to list my specific purchases (since the recipients may read this review), but to give you an idea of what the shop has....leather cuffs, awesome jewelry (including fresh fruit earrings. intrigued? go check em out. :D and cool pendants, buttons and bracelets/necklaces), small crafted keepsakes and magnets, knitted bits of prettiness, pleasantly pungent soy candles (i have never smelled candles this fragrant, in a good way for sure. and yes, the alliteration is a oblique reference to penny pingleton is permanently punished in case you were wondering...), bags/purses, baby onesies and assorted prints....i am sure there are tons of other perfect presents there, and i was able to finish up two people on my list and make headway on a third (and find something a little extra for my sister). i LOVE places like this, perfect for presents and goodies (or when you want to indulge yourself).....thank you yelp for the word.....

Dint like the food much..Left a lot.. chai was good.
Servers were good but despite of requesting for onions 3 times we didn't it till the end.
Red habanero is awesome! Very good food, great service, good price and great environment!

Great authentic food and excellent staff.Felt like a guest at there home.The dishes were more than enough and the bread is excellent.Kept my glass topped of too.I definitely recommend if your in the mood for Indian food.

Like any other chain, Famoso is very much a restaurant concept, ready to take over the world, or at least Canada. The atmosphere in the restaurant lends an air of sophistication that is much needed in big box land. I enjoy the decor and feel at this location more than the Jasper Ave one.

While Famoso makes sure to use "00" flour and accord to standards prescribed by some sort of pizza authority in Naples, it's very much the Edmonton equivalent of California Pizza Kitchen - right down to the Barbecue Chicken and Spicy Thai Pizzas. I also like how Famoso, while using authenticity as part of its branding, isn't above including Pineapple as a topping option.

And while the pizzas at CPK are considered sacrilege by ex-New Yorkers who happen to live in Los Angeles, I enjoy them. Comparing Famoso to CPK is a tremendous compliment. However, Famoso's crust is a bit fresher tasting - if a bit on the flimsy side for my tastes.

And considering the quality of the ingredients, the prices at Famoso are relatively reasonable. If you're looking to go out for a more-special-than-normal lunch, the $11.75 pizza and sandwich combo is a great value.

Also, make sure to take advantage of Famoso's Pizza-and-a-Movie deal if you ever go see movies at Cineplex Odeon theatres on weeknights. Essentially, Famoso will sell you a movie pass for $6, which you may use for any movie from Monday to Thursday. The passes apparently expire two years after you purchase them.

I'm looking forward to Famoso's arrival on Whyte Ave.

I made a reservation for about 10 for a birthday brunch. They don't normally take reservations but we're very accommodating for my party. When I got there I ended up waiting 35 minutes past my reservation time to get seated, which was not ideal. However once seated we were treated to some appetizers to compensate for the wait which was great of management! In addition, our service was very good and very accommodating even though the restaurant was super busy. The menu has a huge selection and everything is super tasty! The mimosa brunch was totally worth it and went great with the food!!

I am a native New Orleanian and don't drink much alcohol (any more).  However, on July 30, 2016 my wife and I attended the event "Hops for Hope" at the Urban South Brewery.  The event was organized by our neighbors & good friends the Chrestman's to support HIE (Hypoxic Ischemic Encephalopathy), an organization dedicated to helping kids with brain damage.

The brewery itself is a no frills open floor concept.  Basically it's a warehouse with a lot of family style picnic tables set up for eating socializing and most importantly, drinking.  My wife had a raspberry ale which was a little too fruity for me.  I tried the Charming Wit and was immediately smitten.  Well let's just say I liked it a lot.  This was a kid friendly event so there was plenty of cold water on tap for the kids.

Unfortunately, the warehouse was not air conditioned and the few fans that they had did little more than act like a convection oven as they circulated the superheated air throughout the venue.  However, we were there for a good cause and stayed 2 hours, at which time my kid was getting too hot; as were several other kids.

There was live music courtesy of artist Steve Wulff, and a Zydeco band whose name I cannot recall followed him.  There were two food trucks outside and "The Crepe Cart" inside with part of the proceeds going to HIE.  Unless this venue was being used for another charity event such as Hops for Hope, I would not recommend going here from the months of June through September as the heat was stifling.  However, during the months of March, April October and November; this place would be pretty cool to hang out.
Class schedule met my needs but the yoga studio is pretty noisy sometime ( from the sound of upstairs).

For all I'm about to say, I feel I have to mention again that this is an honest review and I'm not even embellishing much on my experience here. I'll give them two stars. 

One extra star because they did something I can appreciate out here in the middle of the USA. They didn't try to charge me $8 for a simple Vietnamese sandwich. You guys HAVE to understand that these bAnh mi sandwiches are a DOLLAR in Asia!!! They are $2-3 dollars in California but for some dang reason they are $5-8 in the heart of the USA. I ate it up gratefully and happily. It wasn't as good as the last bAnh mi I had which was in SE Asia (mystery meat and questionable cleanliness standards but soooo dang tasty and I felt fine after eating it), but it hit my craving spot like a hammer.

Along with a bAnh mi was an order of goi cuon (spring rolls). The rolls were pretty small and the dipping sauce was crap. I'm sorry for not sugar coating, but it was absolutely crap. Like I tasted it and was like, "dude wtf is this?!?!" It was bland, and the strangest color I've ever seen in a goi cuon dipping sauce. It was like a light grayish brown with a less than creamy little bit more watery than creamy diarrhea texture. It was a very stupid dipping sauce. If people in Indiana say, "I hate Vietnamese food." I would first blame this restaurant as the prime culprit. I would rebut with, "did you, by chance, eat at Saigon Restaurant?" If this was someone's sole venture into Vietnamese food, I plead for them to try somewhere better and give it another try.

The next dish up... hu tieu bo kho. Beef stew with noodles. The beef was nice and tender and there were some great bits of tendon and carrot, but seriously... no real bo kho looks like what we were served. The broth should be a rich dark brown with a bit of orange oil highlighting the surface. This just looked like very dirty Pho broth. This is not the beef stew you serve to dip bread in. I feel like I was being served counterfeit Vietnamese food. I think that's why I'm not happy writing this review. 

Fortunately there seems to be some competition in Indianapolis for viet restaurants though. I hope that puts some fire in the competition and makes for better quality authentic Viet grub. If restaurants like this one is killing the first impression to the Indiana market, there may be no coming back!

It gets worse. The viet iced coffee tasted like soap. I cannot explain it. Did they not rinse the glasses throughly? Perhaps it was the viet coffee press that still had dish soap in it? What happened there? It was nasty.

It gets worse. I've been around. I've lived in a single bedroom apartment with a family of six with a billion cockroaches as a child. I've lived in cheap motel rooms with roaches and the smell of bug spray in the sheets. I've eaten whole meals in other countries with cockroaches crawling up the wall. But for some reason this kinda irked me... I saw our waiter at the counter visually tracking a bug on the counter. Then swat at it with his hand. Then move things around a bit and try to kill it again. In my mind I imagined a cockroach was his victim. I watched and watched... but did not notice any washing of hands after that hunting trip. Why were there no towels drying off his hands within the next five minutes? Why did his hands not seem moist at any time between this occurring and him serving our food? Like I said, I'm used to bugs, I don't like them and they still gross me out, but I can convince myself some stuff is okay... but why not wash your hands bro? Take some of that extra soap that was in my coffee and give it a go... I'd really appreciate it a lot. I'm sure the health department would as would the customers! It wouldn't take much more time out of your day.

I came to Indianapolis in search of good Asian food that would solve a series of cravings. I'll keep looking. Louisville has some great solutions. Perhaps Ohio is where I'll look next...

I'm thinking of taking away that extra star... yeah...

I've been to Zoe's several times for lunch and dinner with my wife and the food is always tasty.  However, both my wife and I always leave the restaurant hungry. I don't consider us as heavy eaters and I do not want to order two entrées. However, I do expect that the dinner portions to be larger for the price. Also, the hummus is always good and fresh tasting, but why does Zoe's always serve it in such small portions?  Just very odd.

This is my 1st experience here at Kettle.  The staff was friendly. The most enjoyable part of our dining experience was Johnny, a prep cook.  While looking over the breakfast buffet he appeared & offered to serve eggs the special way my husband likes.  Needless to say,  he had seconds.  Lots of food choices at times it was hard picking.  Very satisfied with the food (buffets can be hit or miss) & the prices.  Will definitely come back.

I will echo the love for the Dan Dan noodles.  Wow, so good.  

Located on Route 70 in an unassuming strip mall, Han Dynasty is a shining star in the universe of chain restaurants in the Cherry Hill area.

After a very bad experience for my wife at the Han Dynasty in Olde City (spice level related), I was able to convince her to give it another try.  Boy am I glad that I did.  This is probably some of the most flavorful chinese food I've ever had.  

Just beware of the spice levels.  Maybe I'm weak, but anything over 5 is almost too much for me.  Anything over 2 for my wife and her head is ready to explode.  It's ok though, they will modify to a more reasonable level.

The room is simple and it appears to be a BYOB.  Our server was very friendly and very knowledgeable.  The lunch specials were cheap but appeared to be filling.

I could go on but... the Dan Dan noodles are all you really need to know.  

I'll be back.
A Christmas carol exceeded my expectations.  The set designs blew me away. Characters costumes and stage presence were excellent

The SHRIMP AND GRITS here = hands down, the best thing I ate in New Orleans. 

The sauce is so EXTREMELY tasty!! The bacon and rosemary add a lot of depth to the dish. Also, there were so many shrimps that I lost count!

The restaurant is quite small and gives off a charming hole-in-the-wall vibe. My group of 6 waited about 20 minutes on a Thursday morning around 11am - I'd imagine a weekend wait would be quite substantial. 

Doesn't matter to me - I'd wait for as long as I need to if it means I get those shrimp & grits again. Until then, I'll be dreaming about them in California.

Everytime my family is in the mood for take out we always go here. Never have we been disappointed. General Tso's and Sweet and Sour Chicken are a must and anything that you might try will be good. Definately a must if your in the area.

what a gem! CS Tavern is an excellent destination date or family outing. On a windy road above Santa Barbara, the tavern is an actual old stagecoach stop. The original buildings sit in a picturesque lush creek hollow. 

Our food was great, well cooked high quality cuts of beef and venison served with fresh bread, well cooked asparagus, great salads, and killer garlic potatoes. we're not experts, but it seemed like a good selection of wine and we enjoyed our bottle.

It was pretty hot on the June night we were there. So hot in fact, we corked our bottle early and took it outside to finish it. The service was fine but not amazing.

Definitely worth the effort to check out this bit of California history!

Food is ok, but the service was terrible. I sat without a refill on my drink for over 1/2 of my meal, and the price for the drink (tea) was over $2. I will never go back here. Not worth the money or my time.

My experience with this truck is mixed.  Veg couscous seemed healthy but was pretty bland. Smoked salmon sandwich (with egg, radish, caviar) was great.

Service can be very slow at times -- sometimes he chats for extended periods with certain people.
For our first time trying Rembrandt's we were blown away. Such a stunning place. The beermosas were delicious and the food was good. Can't wait to go back.
I loved everything I tried but the Bananas Foster French Toast made my day. The service was great too, very friendly. Love this place.

Came here to celebrate my nephew graduation.  However the piss poor service and lethargic oh hum attitude displayed by the staff  oddly reminiscent of Denny's.  Avoid this establishment like the plague.

My whole dinner was mind blowing! Some of the highs and lows of the meal:
* low turnips, the taste was a little flat, they were thinly sliced and blanched for a soft yet crunchy texture.... Weird.  
* high Brussels sprouts, these were so delicious! They roast them and crammed in crazy flavor. Turned around a life long hatred of the "gross" tiny  cabbages.  I wish I could have a bucket!
* high whipped feta. I took one bite and immediately went to Pinterest to find a recipe. Honestly though I don't think I'll be able to find one quite like it. It had amazing texture, smooth and light. Taste struck a great balance of salty feta and sweet honey. 
* high gnocchi. Whoa it's a bowl of tasty little pillows. I wanted to jump into the bowl!  The egg created created a great sauce for this dish. Highly recommended for your main course. 

I think the next time I want to try some of the classics. Hummus, maybe the pickled veggies.

While I love love love the Frenchie (turkey, brie, sprouts, honey mustard on crunchy bread), I'm generally disappointed when I stray. Great baked goods, try the granola bar and peanut butter cookies, but the sandwiches often sound better than they actually are. Also the service at the Ladue location is often underwhelming.
I had the spicy chicken sandwich and it was hot and delicious but my fries were barely lukewarm. Customer service at the counter was very friendly and restaurant was clean.

We have taken several tours here in NOLA and Ms. Bone Lady is simply the best!!!!!

She was so knowledgable and engaging with all of us!  She was very personable, answered all our questions and offered more history on the subject! 

You MUST MUST MUST book her tours!!!!!

She's the best in town!!!!

Everything good they say about this place is true, so saying anything else about it would be redundant.  Other than to say that their mul and bibim naeng myeon are the best I've ever had.

Also, you don't *need* a car to get there.  From Center City you can take the 47 bus and walk about 5 blocks, or the Broad Street Line to Fern Rock then take the 70 bus, which drops you right at the corner across from the restaurant.  Also, the Melrose Park regional rail line is close by.

I bought a 5 class promotion last April for body cycle and have been hooked since. I've tried at least 5 of their instructors and all are exceptional!! Morning classes and noon classes tend to be less crowded. My favorite instructors are Russel, Michelle, Jessica, and Ross.  Each push the limits and have great play lists. I've tried other cycling studios and this studio has great energy, machines, and awesome trainers!!

This place is OK.  The qualiy of the food is ok.  Lots of options...noodle bar, hibatchi bar, 10 soups (some are scary), sushi, and tons of buffet food. 

Lunch is $9 and with a coupon it is $7.50.  Anyone who posts on here about food quality....you get what you pay for.  Sushi is average, food is average....but really - what do you want for a $7.50 lunch.

Dinner - offers more options, lobster, scallops for @$16 and they have a $2.50 off coupon.  Once again...what kind of Lobster and buffet do you want for under $15.

Overall - food for value - worth it.  

I would go back.

Just wait the hour for a table.  The wait staff are so kind and the food is amazing!  Perfect place to stop at if you're visiting from out of town like we were.  Hands down the best brunch experience I've ever had
Excellent coffee. Everyone there made us feel welcomed and manager that day came by to ask us how things were. They care. Had eggs hubcap pancake and fruit cup-delicious. I will go back
Great beer list, wonderful bartenders who are friendly, bacon popcorn, incredible gumbo. yum.
Great authentic food. Looks sketchy from outside but great good inside. Only accepts cash or checks so be prepared for that. Well priced and lots of food.

Catelli is full of class, perfect for romance or a special celebration. The waiter/staff treated both my guest and I as if we were royalty. The setting is a sophisticated, elegant Italian-style.

Their $35 restaurant week menu had a wide selection of 4 courses. For the evening I chose: 1st~ Lobster Bisque with Crab Cake, 2nd ~ Short Rib Ravioli with Horseradish Cream Sauce, 3rd~ Herb Crusted Tilapia 4th ~Dessert Sampler of rice pudding, crepe and admittedly, something I can't remember. The 1st and 2nd courses were my favorite, although the crab cake was crispier than I would have liked, it was yummy along with the lobster bisque. My 3rd course, tilapia was served on a bed of arugula and was so-so. The side was yukon filled ravioli in tomato butter sauce and was the better part of the dish. Lastly, the 3 mini desserts were tasty but not memorable. The courses earned a 4.2 rating. 

The check came back armed with coupons--- clearly they want their patrons to come back and oddly enough the coupons were not strictly exclusive for Catelli and could be used other places.   

Side Notes:
-Coat check is available. 
-Unlike most places, they are open on Mondays AND run a byob special.

The Thai Iced Tea is delicious! Super sweet and creamy but still has a distinct tea taste. It was definitely the best part of the meal. I ordered Pad Kee Mao aka drunken noodles, but I'm pretty sure that's not what I got - no spice and no basil. It was still good, but not anything like what I wanted. I thought the waiter had gotten my order wrong. My fellow luncher ordered pork fried rice, it was missing basil and lemon grass. Maybe those things are hard to get in Nashville - I don't know, I'm new to Tennessee - but it was disappointing all the same. I'll definitley come back to try the Pad Kra Pao and Pad Thai sometime. I still have hope for this place!

Came here before an event at the Ryman. Took 15 minutes to get water. Asked for a napkin, had to get it myself. Food was fair but took forever. Horrible service, would never go back. Too bad since it's in a great location in downtown Nashville.

I stopped by with my family on a Sunday afternoon--middle of the day.  Perfect time to go if you don't want to wait for a table.  I really liked the casual atmosphere.

We were greeted right away and our server was quick to bring us our drinks.  I went with the Bear Creek Farm Classic Burger and a side salad to be just a wee bit healthy.  The burger was awesome.  I usually don't finish burgers but this one went down fast.  I tried some of the sweet potato fries that a family member got.  I can't say that I loved them.  The taste was good but the texture...not so much.  Too limp and undercooked for my taste.

But I did not go to Burger Up for the fries.  I went for a burger and will definitely be back.

We ordered the 2 large pizzas and breadsticks for $20.  We paid like a $1 extra to upgrade to cheese sticks instead.  I know it's only $1 but the breadsticks were burnt and they barely put any cheese on them and just sprinkled a little bit of Parmesan on them. The pizza was good.  We asked for some Parmesan and crushed red peppers.  We were given 3.   Like how cheap can they be?   We have 2 large pizzas, 3 tiny little packets aren't enough.

Best local spot! I honestly take anyone who is visiting from out of town here for lunch or dinner! There are a few menu favs you have to try! Duck fries and quack and cheese (obviously) and I am a big fan of the wings as well! Most times I am full by the time my dinner comes, so I bring it home for later or spit the meal or sandwich with my boyfriend.  I call ahead and make reservations every time just to be safe bc I would hate to show up and wait bc I am always super excited for their food!  I celebrate every occasion I can here, I love an excuse to visit!!!

The alligator appetizer is delicious! Order it half fried and half grilled. It's so good, you don't even need the dipping sauce....but, the sauce is also good.
The Voodoo Juice drink is one my favorite mixed drink in New Orleans.
I like the location, which is right on Jackson Square by the Cathedral. Plus, the people watching is pretty interesting.
We've enjoyed all the classics-gumbo, jambalaya, red beans & rice with sausage. 
We will definitely be back!

I really like the food here. Extremely fast delivery and good service anytime I've order. However, nothing is ever really flavorful or seasoned very well. I literally have to go home and add seasonings to whatever I buy because the flavor is so bland. So strange. But once again, the food is well made and fresh. So hey. Win some lose some.

The pizza and wing were fantastic, the waiter and service was great.
First time there, my husband and I will go back !!!!

Why have I not eaten here sooner? Oh yeah, cause the last couple of times I did make it over, I chose that awkward time that they were closed.

Anyway, move over Magasin, this place is so much better! Sure, it's not as trendy or stylish, it doesn't look half as busy, and the menu is not as extensive, but it's probably the most authentic Vietnamese restaurant I've been to on this side of the river. The prices may be slightly higher, but I guess gas and toll fees make up the difference.  Oh yeah, and helpful friendly service.

I had the Grilled Pork Bun and my girlfriend had the Grilled Beef Bun, we also ordered Egg Rolls. The portions for the Buns are large, except next time I would probably order the Egg Roll to go with the Bun, instead of a separate order, as the price actually comes out cheaper.

What's good about the Buns?  Well they add the usual that you should have in there, crushed peanuts, fried shallots, and perfect fish sauce, all three things that are missing from the Magasin Bun.  Oh, and of course, I do prefer the traditional iceberg lettuce.  OH wait, did I mention that they also give you a generous portion of meat, it's cut differently into slices, but it is a lot more than just 4 - 5 thicker slices of the grilled pork or beef you would get at other places.  The Eggs Rolls were also pretty standard and good, not rolled in so much wrapping that it's hard.

I'll definitely be coming back and I'll be getting the Pho next time.

After the classic coffeehouse Borsodi's closed in July of 1989 after 22 years in I.V., Javan's was the business that took over. They have lasted longer than Borsodi's did.

I'm sure they are a good place but it makes me sad every time I walk by and remember the great stuff at Borsodi's (shows with Sonic Youth, John Doe of "X", Camper Van Beethoven, Henry Rollins, all kinds of other bands and performers).....but that's the way it goes. Maybe if Borsodi's had served burgers and fries instead of trying to be fancy with shit like Blue Pasta they would still be around.  Wish they were.
Organized, clean, friendly and great classes. A great yoga studio space. I am looking forward to returning for another great class soon.

The Food: Amazing. We always get the breadsticks which I would argue are easily the best in Indianapolis (try all three sauces!!!), after that my husband loves the Steak Sandwich, it's an open-faced sandwich with a 4oz steak, a fried egg, pepper jack cheese and all the trimmings. Their chips are homemade and have Old Bay on them, and the seasoned fries are super yummy. I love the Apple Gouda sandwich that has cinnamon. Literally everything we have tried here has been phenomenal. They also have a fantastic beer selection featuring lots of local brews as well as a large selection on tap as well as a full bar.

The Atmosphere: PHENOMENAL. I always feel like I'm back in England at a pub watching the football games. They open super early for "soccer" games and serve breakfast during these hours which is amazing. It's a smaller bar and can get pretty packed during games but it is super fun! 

The Service: Has been unfortunately hit or miss. We have had good service and we had had pretty terrible service, thus only four stars. I understand that you open early, but if you open then your service should still be up to par. For example, we have had that waiter that is super attentive and eager to please and offer great food recommendations, and we have had waiters who practically forget about you, botch your order, eat in the corner during their shift while neglecting patrons, seem to be on drugs and are too busy watching the games rather than doing their jobs. 

All in all I absolutely love this place, I just wish their service would be more consistently good. For now it's the only real soccer bar in the city and the food is unbelievable so we will continue going until one of those things change.

I have been getting my hair done by Caitlin for many years now. She knows how antsy I get sitting in her chair so she accommodates how she takes care of my hair by alternating my highlights to every other visit. This saves on money as well. She puts me first!  Great color and cut every time. She also deals with my great idea of changing up my color (drastically) or cutting a lot off the length. You won't be disappointed! Great products as well!
4.5 stars for sure!  Puppies and pizzas makes my week.  The pizza crust is remarkable.

This is less than 5 minutes off of 295 - a good place to stop for lunch if traveling South.  It is close to the Delaware Memorial Bridge.

Italian Kitchen is kid friendly- has chicken fingers, pizza, grilled cheese and French fries.  

They have cold deli and hot deli foods, pizza and soup.

You can pick up soda and bottled water for the road.  They also have coffee to go.

The children voted.  They said we should stop here the next time we are going South.
Excellent food and service. Dine in BYOB, pick up or delivery. Classic dishes fresh and delicious. Very clean and authentic in a nice friendly town.
This place is historically significant, and the staff is very informative. This is where the 1st Continental Congress met as far back as 1724!

To answer Greg T's question, YES! I am totally into bowling alleys that haven't been renovated in 30 years. I am not a serious bowler--I go maybe once or twice a year, and I'm looking for a place that's not too crowded or too family friendly/corporatized. When I came here, there was no crowd, the jukebox was playing a lot of Rolling Stones, and there was a little old lady with a big blonde beehive behind the bar. In short, it was awesome, and I plan to return.

My favorite place to have chimichanga in town (so far). For $8, I had 2 medium size chimichangas with crispy wrap. It came with picco de gallo, guacamole, green salad and sour cream. It tastes much better than the food from a chain Mexican restaurant or even local Mexican restaurant in Indy area. I wish they can make it with chorizo...it could be more delicious (and fattening too). 

The kids meal has a standard menu for the price range of $4-$4.5. They offer chicken fingers, quesadilla, hot dogs, grilled cheese and few more. They all come with a soft drink and a bowl of fruit. According to them they taste pretty good. 

In conclusion, the restaurant offers good (and unique) meals for the museum. They offer many different southwestern inspired dishes such as buffalo chili, and they also serve shrimp po'boy sandwich. I will return and try different dishes next time I come back here. Or I will probably just come back here only to order my chimicanga. Yum yum...

We were here for dinner. Not busy at all. The server did not come to our table for 20 minutes. In the course of that time, we were greeted by a multitude of mice. There were 5 separate appearances. Including under our table and at our feet. We also watched them roam freely into and out from the kitchen.  I used to partake in Honey's brunch nearly every weekend. For YEARS. It is safe to say I will never dine or advertise for this establishment again. When the server was told about the mice issue, he was not only flippant in his response, but made excuses rather than apologize, and charged us for our 2 cups of coffee.

I've been to the Knitting Factory for several concerts, and most recently for a show, Avenue Q.  I do appreciate that Reno has a concert venue that draws well known performers and performances to the city.  Going to a concert here is a much different experience than a show.  The concerts are general admission and everyone packs into the concert hall, with no options for seating on the main floor.  Depending on where in the knit you are at, you may or may not have a good view and you may or may not be smothered by other attendees.  Seeing a show here, I was not sure what to expect.  I was pleasant surprised when I saw that a general admission ticket meant that you just grabbed a seat in one of the many rows of chairs.  The venue is narrow so there were many rows, but luckily we arrived early and sat close.  The sound during concerts is always pretty good, but the show could have been better.  Tickets are affordable but drinks are pricey - what you would expect at a music venue.

This place is pretty good for a couple of things, the Brussel sprouts and the cooked oysters. I've tried many other main courses that just didn't wow me and took off stars for that. Service was good at least!

Came here for lunch.

Pros: Great food, well prepared, fresh and full of flavor. The bread pudding and Fresh fish were beyond expectation. The bread pudding is just moist enough to be both soft and of good texture. The fish though was just listed as fresh fish on the menu but it came with a bed of nicely cooked vegetables (carrots, reddish, long beans squash and etc) with pesto underneath the pan "fried" fish. The service is good, though not the best I have seen. 

Cons: if I'm being picky, the table cloth is kinda wrinkled and a bit old. Also, the chair is so light that when my group were leaving, two of our chairs fell back to the floor due the weight of the coat alone and our coats were pushed right on the floor by the falling chair :(. Fortunately there weren't a toddler behind or many people around. (So be careful!).

Wow! It's wonderful to find a restaurant with a HomeTown feel these folks at Chill go out of their way to make your dining experience perfect. We feel like we made new friends! The food was delicious! They couldn't do enough for us to make sure that we were happy with our  meal and had everything that we needed. The atmosphere is  great and the entertainment was fabulous can't wait to go back!

Time for expansion! Ever since I moved to DC area, your restaurant is one of the things that I truly miss in Philly! It's frustrated that there's no true Cambodian restaurant rather than one fancy fusion place. Ok, speaking of the food at Khmer Kitchen, I'm a fan of everything. When I lived in Philly, I went there a few times a week. Probably gained a lot of weight just from that...everything is so flavorful. The spices are sort of familiar if you eat a lot of Asian food, but something that so unique and different from other cuisines. I don't want to recommend this place on yelp before because it's way too popular for me to get a table during regular hours! Yes, I'm being selfish when it comes to food. But now that I'm away and desperate to send a message to the owner that they need to open one in DC area, please believe me that this is the best Cambodian restaurant one of the best Asian restaurants in town!!
Great farmers market but they closed the parking lot adjacent? What the??

We stumbled upon Luke's on our way to Alabama via NOLA.  At first we thought we were under dressed because the place looks fancy (and it was) but they were very warm and welcoming, the food was delicious  and our server TRISTAN was very accommodating. He told us about some New Orleans history (French Quarter Festival and Nick Cage's cemetery plot). He was very professional  and the only reason for the four stars is because the didn't have flavored Vodka.

I am more impressed with this location each time I go! Maybe I am getting to understand the layout but it seems like the selection and stock are improving. 

Price checking is always a good option but sometimes Canadian Tire just drops their prices and that is when it is time to pounce. Momma likes her deals so I usually shop off season and have a pretty good personal inventory idea of what I need/want and what I don't. 

As far as Automotive goes I have asked a few ordering questions and as per usual with Canadian Tire this department does not receive great reviews from me...or anyone I know. If given the choice on that I may even consider running past the local high school shop class before I walk in here as a female.

This knit shop is FANTASTIC! I'm a dedicated knitter from California going to college in NOLA, and I was a little worried about not finding a good yarn shop- I'm addicted to Malabrigo. Not only did this store have all of the nice yarn brands (Malabrigo, Blue Sky, Noro!!!) but they had an amazing atmosphere and staff. Maybe it's the New Orleans friendliness and relaxation, but the store felt like a cozy yarn attic you could linger in for hours. The employees were kind and helpful, and really tried to get a feel for what you needed, rather than trying to upsell you. Additionally, the decor of the store was extremely warm- it felt like a giant yarn closet, rather than a retail store. I will definitely be visiting again, and I will probably miss it when I go back to California!

I don't drink coffee here. I've never had a glass of wine under this roof. 

Matcha Latte by Maffi gets 5 stars. Matcha Latte by remaining staff gets 4 stars. Maybe its the touch of agave, maybe its his genuine demeanor. 

Its easy to get lost in the wide selection of pastries, scones, cookies and the like but when I'm hungry I always go for a crepe. The serving size is just right and they are perfectly both sweet and savory. 

The atmosphere is superb having had both intense study sessions as well as productive meetings. Its a chill place to hang out and the music they play is diverse but not too far out there.
Best indian place ever! My fav is takka masala and the chicken makhni and chicken curry.. dont miss out on this!

3 words ... Off the chain .! I decided to give this place a try because I'm open to trying different places and trust I did not regret that decision to come here .  The chicken was unbelievably good and will be back

Wow, this is the best Marshalls I have ever shopped. It was clean, well organized and had stuff I actually wanted to buy. The other day I went shopping at The Rack, looking for a short sleeved linen shirt and had no luck. I found it here and for only $20. What a deal. I hope they can keep it up. If they can, I will be a repeat offender. I mean, I will be a repeat shopper. 

I only shopped the Men's Dept., but the shoe selection looked huge as did the home area. 

Deer Creek Plaza has been totally redone, I'm looking forward to shopping the other new stores as they open.

Fantastic haircut!! If you're a guy who cares about how they present themselves and don't want to break the bank this is the place for you. Great stylist and a very male
friendly environment.

Just made a purchase and the staff was awesome!  They also have the most beautiful cat in their store and I found that to be a warm touch.  I read some reviews about the staff being snobby.  That was not my experience at all. The staff was beyond nice and so helpful. They have beautiful jewelry and the prices range from low to high. There is really something for everyone in this store!

This was my second time coming here. The first time I had halo halo and it was pretty good and super big. Definitely a cool sweet vibrant colored treat to have on a warm humid florida day.

Today a was a bit different.  Our first cold front for the season. I had no interest in a halo halo. I just finished slurping up some pho next door at saigon deli. We needed something sweet to balance out all the saltiness from our delicious pho soup.

There's a huge menu on the wall for pho and Boba tea and smoothies. Again, not interested.

What's for dessert I ask? They bakery case was there but empty. Not a fun sight to see when I want a sweet treat.

They said here's the menu.  Well I am not versed on filipino desserts. Growing up my parents would just buy it, & say try it. Like it or don't like it. Don't know the names of things. Help me. The guy was helpful.

Picked out an ube or purple yam cake w cream cheese frosting. Hubby was already to pre-judge  it bc he hates purple but he ate it up before I got a couple bites.

Happy we tried something new and I could recommend that. But if you don't know what anything is, don't just order from the menu. Make sure sure they show you or check out yelp pics.

I am an exec level who pretty much uses national every week for business travel.   Last week I returned the car on Wednesday.   They forgot to check it in or something so they kept calling me every day asking when I was going to return the car.     They gave a phone number that didn't connect to the right people so I had to go through the telephone tag game.   Every day they called with a robo call despite me already working with their staff on the issue.   Finally on Monday they send an email saying they found the car but now want to charge me through Sunday, which is apparently when they found it.

I get mistakes happen.   But why keep calling me and why send me a bill thru Sunday when I was working with customer service?    

Normally I don't have issues, but customer care fell down on this one.

First time eating ethiopian food.  Went here for a birthday with a large group of people.  I ordered the Dor Wat.  It was simply put, delcious.  Everyone enjoyed the food.  It was a bit warm in the resturant for us and the service was a little slow.  There seemed to be only one person working and we did have a large group so that is very understandable.    I would 100% go back if another opoprtunity arises.

Recommended to me by a vet tech and professional animal care expert, the doctors here have a rare combination of great diagnostic skills and a pleasant, comforting manner. I drive a pretty good distance to take my animals to this clinic, and it's worth the trouble.

We were going to Splash for years and this was our first visit to Aquafinz. It was just as good if not better ! The new location is perfect for us, just by the exit and entrance of the Vets Expressway on 54.

Not impressed - ordered delivery, took over an hour to get here. Ordered a green smoothie, they forgot it (the restaurant did call me to inform me of this after the order had already left 20 minutes ago and they did refund me which was generous...but still. What was the point of ordering it at all??) Ordered the veggie sandwich on multigrain toast, came on ciabatta. Ordered extra avocado, definitely didn't have it. And on a $9 sandwich I just wish I had gotten what I had ordered. Long story short, don't think I'll be ordering from here again. Oh well!

Wowzers!! The food is so good at Cajun Kate's. It's extremely small so come before the lines form. It located at Booths Corner in Boothwyn, PA and its open on Friday and Saturday. Please check this place out if you like New Orleans style cuisine.

Very yummy authentic tacos! Owned by a hubby and waifu duo~

Visited and ate at this place when they weren't all the busy yet and I'm glad to see on my last visit that they blew up! 
Only proves that if you do and make good food, the people will come! I love eating at places like these and hope their business flourishes! Best of luck Indy Tacos. :)

I arrived around 1pm on a Sat.
Choices were glazed and sweet potato.    Bought both
Total was around $2.40
The dough/bread just melted in my mouth
Frosting tasty.   Careful it's sticky and messy.  Napkins
I live in Tower Grove so it will be special trips
Price was average or high if you compare it to a TG donut place.
Arrive early for more selection
I shall return
We've been going here for 10+ years. Never been disappointed with the food. The staff is always great and remember your name. The food is outstanding every time

The food is ok. I had Salmon Genovese and I literally had a hard time just finding the salmon on the plate. It was smothered with a large amount of sun dried tomatoes and onions. The flavor was okay, but the food is so heavy it will sit on your stomach for a few hours. The restaurant is a bit small and sitting near the front of the house (near the door and the cooking line) isn't the greatest atmosphere with the heat from the kitchen, waiting patrons, and take out orders going all around you. It's worth a visit, just make sure it's not on a weekend or you will wait forever to be seated.

We love this placed its the best decision we have made for our child thus far. Disregard that 2 star review couldn't be further from the truth. We were at a previous school and are so glad we changed him to Creative World. He has fantastic multiple teachers, they taught him how to count, add, write, and even read a book on his own before entering kindergarten. This credit is fully on the school, not us. All the kids are great and the school jumps on misbehavior making a positive fun environment for those that are good listeners. No problem children here, teachers goals are a great environment. They get to bring bikes on some days and ride, water guns on sprinkler day. Our son loves it. And, many of his classmates will be in his elementary school, making the transition flawless. This is a premier school in the area, so if you are thinking of joining in the future visit now, there is often a waiting list, visit it now. You'll be happy you put your child here.
Greatest Cicis I've been to. Still covered in shame and self loathing when you leave but it was clean in there.

Love the prices for movies here! I get to see the movies I wanted to see during their cinematic release but missed, for a super cheap price! Judging by how many people show up there,  I don't think that this place needs my endorsement, but it sure deserves it. We saw Cowboys and Aliens, loved the movie, thrilled that I got to see it on the big screen.

Just wish they'd ease up just a smidgen on concessions ($4 for a small soda....really??)

Went for lunch today. I had the rice bowl, half lamb with tikka masala and half shrimp with madras. Nice assortment of veggies to go on top, and the additional sauces were a tasty finish. Had to  have a couple of samosas too. Food was good, service was quick and very friendly. Will definitely add this place to the lunchtime rotation!

This place is great. The decor is all militarily themed without being jingoistic, the owner is a great guy who isn't hesitant to start up a conversation with anyone. The beer selection is very impressive, you can actually reserve a tap if you're having a group of people & don't feel like continuously ordering. 

My favorite part is the upstairs cubby hole. It's got couches & a pool table, very relaxing area.

Enough with the silliness. I bleed inside because all I see is 4 star reviews. This place is incredible, the buffet is quite good for $20 but clearly they put stuff from the previous day that did not sell... BUT LEFT OVERS TASTE BETTER!!&/?):& 

Besides the great wings, ribs and sausage, these guys make an incredible set of not-boring sauces and they are remarkably good. I can't wait to drive by again...

Let me start off first by saying I've loved Chinese food since I was little kid. From going with my dad to the old school Chinatown duck places back in the day, to ordering General Tso's from the local suburban delivery joints. Having said that, those places have nothing to do with Han Dynasty.

Of course, you *could* order something safe off of the "Americanized" portion of the extensive menu, but why would you? Although I imagine their take on the Americanized classics is probably well above par, you come here to taste "authentic" Chinese (Szechuan) flavors, or as close to authentic as you can get stateside.

I've wanted to try Han Dynasty for a while now, but I honestly had no idea what I was missing. So far I've already eaten here twice in the last week, and I see no signs of stopping until I try most of what looks good to me. My first visit I started with the Dan-Dan Noodles (not on the menu, ask). They most unctuous, pork-y, savory, spicy, delicious bowl of noodles this side of anywhere. Highly Recommended. For an entree, being in the mood for some famous Szechuan spice, I opted for the Chinese Bacon with Hot Peppers. Wow, was this hot. The dish consisted of uniquely flavorful Chinese bacon (yum) sauteed with sliced green hot (HOT) peppers. The oily pork fat balanced out the firey sliced peppers, seeds, stems and all. I enjoyed the meal so much, I got an order of Cumin Lamb to go (unlike anything I've ever tasted - great).

My next visit was strictly take-out, and I went with an order of the Chinese Meatballs and an order of the Pork Belly with Preserved Vegetables. The meatballs might be one of the best things I've ever eaten. Perfectly tender meat like an Italian grandmother would make, but with subtle, sweet spices and a broth that you could drink but I just soaked up with rice and hungrily scarfed down. Best dish I've eaten in a long time. The pork belly was very good also, but not on the same level as the meatballs. The luscious, fatty, tender pork was swimming in a sauce not unlike that which coats the Dan Dan  noodles. Savory, spicy, rich, gelatinous...the only thing I feel it could use is a hint of sweetness to balance out the salty, savory preserved vegetable sauce.

Overall, great dining experience. If you have a chance to get to any of Han's three restaurants, I would urge you to hurry up and go.

CASH ONLY!!!  Only went once but it was cheap and tasty! Not a sit-down place. They still have their vintage sign up. Fun to see, especially when you drive by at night. Close to the famous Ted Drewe's.

Wow!! We went for the first time tonight at 8:40 and they close at 9. We did not at all feel rushed or  unwelcome. Rather the opposite, the service was amazing, we had Erin as our server and she is GREAT! Food was amazing and so well priced. You could tell it was very fresh. They have some of the best staff, best food and atmospheres of any local restaurant. Thank you for the amazing service and laughs Erin-- and the entire staff for making our first but not last experiment great!

Will definitely be back!!!
While in the city trued something​new glad I did got the sasauge Stromboli way to much for one person .Great taste placed filled up at lunch time glad I walked in
Excellent breakfast , Fig and prosciutto toast. Staff is Also excellent  pastry's look awesome .
Great seafood platter. Gumbo was awesome. Worth the visit. Crispy Kale with the swordfish was unique and tasty. Fish very fresh. Bit pricey but great for a special meal

Love. LOVE! My husband and I are German food fans and while in Santa Barbara on our honeymoon we decided to try Brummis. 

This place totally reminds you of your grandmother's house. Cute, quaint and absolutely spotless. The owners are both adorable and efficient and make you feel instantly welcome. The food is AMAZING. My husband's sauerbraten was perfection and my jaeger schnitzel was absolutely spot on. Next time we are in SB, we will be back!
The best breakfast in New Orleans hands down. Go see Ruthie. She is the sweetest lady ever. Great service, excellent food. Definitely a must!

Quickly becoming one of our favorite restaurants in Indy! So clean, kind owners and servers and fantastic food! Also, homeade drinks that are so flavorful and HUGE! Try the ginger one if you are a ginger fan. Indy, show this place some love. Their new location is fantastic!

The food is good, beer is good. The waitress is friendly ... the place isn't very lively. It looks sad  maybe better music  or drink specials or food specials. It's not over priced, the just place needs SOMETHING. I ordered the BBQ pulled pork sliders, they are tasty. The beer is local, it's pretty good (if you like beer).

It's a huge place. There's P.O. boxes big enough to store Reticulated Boa Constrictors in..you know, the ones that aren't native to Florida? 
The A.C. is blowing cool, cool air and everyone seems
to move and little slower as to savor the chill.
What impressed me was they have a card display in the corner..Hallmark cards..for all the occasions. I have never seen this kind of display before and it makes perfect sense. One is rushed and hasn't gotten off that card for that special person and voila! Here is a whole rack of them.
Brilliant marketing strategy!

TJ Maxx stocks everything from Polo shirts to high end kitchenware. You can even find a limited selection of furniture at this location. My wife stops off at this TJ Maxx nearly every weekend. She loves their clothing and shoe selections. They also have decent offerings for us, gentlemen. 

They also have a toy section with prices lower than Walmart. During the holidays they greatly expand their toy offerings. 

Be sure to check out the clearance aisle for the best deals. Her latest great find was a high end cook pot, $60 for $300 cooper bottom pot. 

Brand name clothes at great prices. If you are looking for a deal, you will likely find one at TJ Maxx.

Along with great food, and an extensive beer list, they have Saint Lucifer Spice on the tables as a condiment option.  I thought only bars in Philly were carrying St. Lucifer, but I'm glad I'm wrong.  It's really that good. Thank you Brother Paul's for bringing some originality to the tables.

Great place. So friendly and clean. Services always top notch. Staff is great. Food is consistently great!!  Love this place!

Another great night at Los trojes. These guys know how to do this!!!

Creamy pralines were a little dry. Chewy pralines were soft, not chewy, but I put one in the fridge for a couple of hours and it tasted better. Peanut butter cups were delicious, even if they do fall apart when you cut them in half. 

Some great looking bark here, but I'm too busy buying pralines to try it.

This used to be my favorite praline place. I think I'm going to try out some other places.
I really was hoping this place would have good food at a fair price with good service.  The server was nice.....the rest...meh.

Will give 5 star if I stay in the 2nd floor.. But overall a good experience. Breakfast， free bike rental and easy parking and did I mention about the great location ....so even though a bit noise early on from the 2nd floor but after 9pm everything quiet down... Would come back again but stay on the 2nd floor!

Sam's used to be nice when my husband and I would go. But during our last visit, all we saw were miserable employees who were obviously overworked. Then, we got our meal... 45 minutes after we got there and it didn't seem worth the wait. Mediocre at best.

I am a vegetarian and I love the soup/salad or half sandwich/half salad mixture. My favorite is the oriental chicken salad (minus the chicken) with the Mediterranean sandwich (minus the feta). It has this avocado dressing on it that is tasty and even though the sandwich is all veggies, it's really yummy that way. Also the grilled cheese sandwich and tomato soup is my son's favorite and they make a good one. 

All in all, Panera bread is a very good place to eat. You can bring a large party, not have to tip, which is a plus. So if you are looking to save some money on that, it's the place to choose.
Ok so last night got there at 8:45. Not knowing they close at 9:00 on Sunday.  We were sitted. Had a wonderful waiter.

I walked into Burger Up expecting it to look kind of like the burger joint that was in the building before it.  Boy, was I surprised! The space looks totally different, in a good way. I was pretty much sold when I saw the chalkboard with the names of local vendors they use and I recognized most of them from the Franklin Farmer's Market. 

It was a great lunch for my family. I was able to get a bunless burger on a very nice salad of mixed greens. My husband got some burger all loaded up with toppings.  The fries are great!  I was trying to eat healthy, but couldn't resist them.

The fact that the kids meals come with fries AND apple slices AND they serve Hatcher Dairy Milk (the best milk in these parts, IMO) made me a happy mom.  Both my boys liked and ate their meals.

The service was just okay. I'm not sure what kind of vibe they are hoping for.  The hostess was VERY friendly. She welcomed everyone and asked about how their day was, etc.  Once we were seated, it seemed most of the servers were cool guys in skinny jeans.  They were getting the job done, but I kind of got the feeling we weren't quite hip enough for them. No warm fuzzies once we got to our table. 

As other reviewers have said, the seating is close together.  I wouldn't want to be there on a date night, but for a family lunch I loved it. Now, the people sitting next to us, who got an upclose and personal performance from my three year old, might have had a totally different experience. :)

Just thinking about the food, has me planning another visit to Burger Up. I've heard the quinoa burger is amazing and I want to try it for myself. Soon.

My company recently switched its preferred contract from HERTZ to National to save money. I see where the cost cutting went to. Only two cars available with little to no options, customer service is sub-par. My company saved money but I lost the value. I travel almost every week and if it were up to me....not National.
Amazing pizza!!! The corn bread crust is delicious. The staff was friendly and attentive. I will definitely be back

This is a small but well designed gallery displaying Ted DeGrazia's work. The building itself is interesting. It's wonderful to see the wide range of his work and the artistic depth. I've always enjoyed his art but now I appreciate him more as an artist.

OK so it's not much to look at on the outside or inside however the food is amazing.

They have Chicken and Ribs with Rice and Beans and salad. They do keep it simple but they DO IT RIGHT! There are a few small tables in the back with the groceries if you want to eat here but they are set up for carry out. My chicken and ribs was so good, flavorful and tender. I also got an Aqua Fresca hibiscus water. I love, love, love that stuff and the large is like a small JUG so I had plenty to share with my friend.

For about 12.00 I had an amazing lunch and enough to have it again the next day for lunch! They are now open 7 days a week and the staff is very nice. They do accept cash or credit here as well.

GO here if you love great BBQ grilled chicken and ribs!
Bus was only 15 minutes late due to traffic being blocked for a race. No wifi, tho. Load your own luggage.

Butcher & Bee is one of the best restaurants I've been to in Nashville. If you're a foodie and/or a hipster, forgo the meat and three and BBQ and meander over to East Nashville for a dining experience. Here's why I loved Butcher & Bee:

1) The food- It's a small plate concept with the majority of dishes being vegetable based (though they do have some meat options). My friend and I ordered four small plates and a dessert to share and we left content. A few stand outs: The whipped feta is their signature. It is good, but if you don't like feta to begin with, order something else. Avocado crispy rice- It's more salad with a whole avocado mixed in and crunch North Carolina rice. Butternut squash soup- Bold flavors with a pomegranate seed garnish. Meat balls- comes in a triad and has cheese and bread crumbs mixed in. The chocolate pot de creme with chili was good, but not sweet (In case you're obsessed with sugar like me).

2) The atmosphere- It's slick and the simple art around the restaurant is perfectly placed. We sat at the small table in front of their logo painted on the wall and several Instagrammers stopped by to snap a photo. Warning: The light is low so it doesn't make for the best photos.

3) The location- It's just off of Main Street in East Nashville within walking distance to other Nashville finds like Edley's BBQ and Family Wash. 

4) The service- It's the South so it was friendly, but not in a fake or annoying way.

If you want a good Nashville dining experience that's on the cutting edge of Nashville's food scene pivot, go to Butcher and Bee. Just don't Google it because you'll find it's NOT a local joint (It's from Charleston, South Carolina).

They have a healthy variety of burritos and smoothies for reasonable prices in a cute little place on King's highway.  The new location is a big improvement over the old place.  The seating is now in the front by the windows and isn't as narrow.  It is now located in the old Stone Cold Creamery location.
Innovative food on the pricey side but worth it .margaritas are awesome great service

I went here for lunch today and it was great. Their sandwiches are fantastic. My server was great and very attentive. It was hard to eat lunch because all I could smell was the bakery and I just wanted to eat dessert! The salad that came with my sandwich was just ok, but my main course was delicious! My cookie for dessert was so soft and chewy. I can't wait to try this place for breakfast. I'll definitely be going back.

The seasonal vegetables right now is the carrot. I'm sure there are multiple carrots involved in making the dish, however, that is hardly the plurality I was looking for. Oh and the pumpkin beer flight remains a grand idea lost in execution. The staff is fabulous!

I am a self-admitted hotel snob. So, I do my research before booking a hotel. This hotel did not disappoint. It is tucked away. It's quiet and clean. The customer service is AMAZING - everyone we encountered was very friendly and helpful. The breakfast was above and beyond for a free breakfast. There is cereal, juices, waffle maker, eggs, coffee, toast, muffins. The rooms were a nice size and the shower was hot and had great water pressure. I only have three gripes. (1)I left a tablet on the bed and housekeeping left a note saying they were not allowed to remove personal items from the bed they couldn't change the sheets. (2) They provide one small, sample-size shampoo, conditioner, and body wash. I have no doubt had I called to request more, I would've been promptly attended to. (3) The pull out couch is uncomfortable. The padding is much thiner and it's actually preferable to sleep on the actual couch. Otherwise, Publix, CVS, Olive Garden are all less than a five minute drive which is very helpful. Also, the hotel is right off I-75 so if you're going to Busch Gardens or downtown, it's all expressway (and about 20 minutes to each). I would recommend staying here and I would definetely stay here again.
First time here. I ordered my eggs over medium and they got it right the first time. That doesn't happen to me very often.

I just created a Yelp account because I'm so annoyed with HoneyGrow.  I continue to go there for a lunch about once a week because I like the salads despite the prices, noise, crowd, and the amount of time it takes to make food.  It's fresh and generally they really try to get your food as quickly as possible.  I just went to pick up lunch to eat back at work - I watched a worker prepare my salad and didn't see her include any cheese.  I looked closer as she packed it up and even asked "Excuse me, I'm sorry, is there cheese in this?" to which she indignantly muttered 'YES."  I took her word for it - must've missed her add it.  I pay $10 for my salad, drive back to work, AND THERE'S NO CHEESE ON MY SALAD.  If you have a few hours to kill and don't mind hovering about your food to make sure it's prepared correctly, HoneyGrow is great.  Unfortunately, this is the last straw with them.  I'm so disappointed.  Sweet Greens it is.
Breakfast sandwich was yummy but everything was different than the picture! Chopped bacon, why??
I love this place, the cupcakes are sooooooo moist and delicious, I always get David and Goliath! I would've given it 5 stars but $3.50 for a cupcake is ludicrous... I only go for special occasions.

I have no words for this place. Your jaw will drop when you step inside when you see the selection of baked treats in front of you. Everything is fresh and there's plenty of parking. I highly recommend this place and you can't beat the pricing either

While they usually do a nice job of my nails their COMMUNICATION skills are the absolute worse! They often ignore you after signing in on arrival not giving you any information about how long the wait will be -- I waited 15 mins today before somebody finally came up front so I could ask. I was told a few minutes abc it ended up being 30 more -- I would have gladly made an appointment and returned later that day. They need to learn to respect people's times and schedules and be much more efficient with customer service. This is not the first time this has happened and whenever I kindly remind them they need to offer this courtesy they just say "sorry, sorry." If you have a busy schedule as I do, call and make an appointment first.

We've had NO LEAKS in our bedroom after several heavy rain storms since Alston stucco repaired our chimney & roof.
My husband and I give a 5 out of 5 star rating to Zach and his team at Alston stucco. Simply put, he did exactly what he said he was going to do. He called to confirm our initial appointment, gave an honest assessment of our roof and chimney condition, and got the job done the next day at a reasonable price.

He also provided some preventative maintenance advice for areas around the exterior of our house. 

If we need any stucco work in the future we will contact him again for sure. Thanks again for outstanding service.

I don't know why you people are all here lying to people. I got the fish tacos, they are absolutely disgusting. Is the fish boiled? Who boils fish for tacos? Because that is literally what this tastes like. Irrelevant, it is still Bland and tasteless. Also, I asked for flour tortillas, and I still got corn so thank you for that. And then the tortilla completely disintegrates on contact: what the heck is happening here?? Biggest waste of money ever, and into the trash it goes. I guess the hunt for good taco spots in town continues.

The third time *is* a charm!

We recently moved within our apartment building on approximately one week's notice.  After sending a flurry of estimate requests to local movers, Tom from the Sultans was the first to respond -- within fifteen minutes, on a Sunday evening.

Lucky for us, the Sultans were available to work their moving magic for us once again, and, as anticipated, the movers were prompt, professional and super efficient.  

We don't plan to move again any time soon, but when that day does come, I know I'll hire the Sultans of Schlep.

This place is so amazing.  The food is to die for.  The corn cakes are by far, the best thing on the menu.  Corn tamale with pulled braised beef. So delicious!  Pork carnita tacos are awesome.  The churro is so good. You will love it here!

I really like this place. I went in not really knowing what to expect, but it was awesome. I get the fried butterfly shrimp, which are great, and the fries are also seasoned super good. My family got the fish special and they were big portions and they all loved it. If you're looking for a casual place to have some quality fried seafood in Nashville, this is definitely it. Parking can be a pain in the five points area but it's not too bad. Extra bonus the sweet tea!
Got 2 chicken tacos & chips & salsa for takeout. Best tacos I've ever had & they were very filling.

Fabulous food! Homemade toasted ravioli, pastas, risotto, veal were all delicious. $$ is a little deceiving as a special entree and salad can run $30. There are more economical dishes available and portions are good. Probably not much difference in price than many other restaurants on the Hill. Near the top of my Hill favorites (slightly off the Hill if you want to be technical).

Captain Jason was very knowledgeable. He actually lives in that area! What can be better than having a true local take you around? I admire his respect for the environment and the laws in certain areas. There are some zones that don't allow alligator feeding. Other tour company's tour guides don't care about those laws and were feeding the alligators in no feeding zones.

Horrible service. Rude staff. I was told when the dry cleaning would be ready when I dropped off my clothes. On the third time going to pick my clothes up, and needing to head out of town, it was finally available! The staff was apathetic. I'll be spending my hard earned dollars on a dry cleaner that meets the  expectations it sets. Will follow up with the quality of the product.

I wanted to like this place but it felt more like a mass chain than a great local find. The staff were great and no wait. The custom omelet was not done correctly (tomatoes inside when I asked for none and an onion or two that were not part of my order). Not terrible mistakes, but the worst was that the food came out luke warm. The complimentary corn muffins also seemed old. If you're looking for standard fare, no frills, this place is fine. That said, for the quality they are too expensive for brunch/breakfast in my opinion.

My boyfriend and I really like this place and we prefer it over the other Indian restaurants we have tried in Philly.  It is reasonably priced and the portions are very filling with lots of protein in the meat dishes (we almost never finish both our curries).  Their naan is good but not the best that I've had.  I like their eggplant vegetarian curry although some people may not like that there is no texture to it becuase the eggplant is mushed up.  The chicken tikka masala and biryani are good but we prefer the lamb korma and the house special Makhani chicken.  The saag is also very delicious and the chili chicken is very good but it tastes more like a Chinese dish because the chicken is fried and there isnt really a curry sauce.

Their buffet is reliable, cheap and good as well but the atmosphere is a bit dingy so I prefer delivery.  They usually take about 30-40 minutes to the Domus on 34th and Chestnut.

I live 6 blocks away and pass this business daily, so when I saw a $10 off for new customers deal it lured me in! 

I'm sold. They do a nice job. Their prices are right in line w/competitors.

Pros:
-Parking right in front of entrance
-Friendly staff
-Use the Spot On app (loyalty program and earn free dry cleaning)

Cons:
-Traffic on Illinois can be a bit daunting. 
-They advertise free delivery but don't offer it in my neighborhood

Question: Whey don't any dry cleaners post their prices? I'd love to walk in and see them in the way nail salons post theirs?
the food is excellent, but bums me out never open on Sunday, play area clean and well done for my sons safety.

there are some harsh reviews for this location on yelp - i don't think it is any different or any more or less expensive than any other whole foods.  the people who work at this location are nice and they validate parking in the lot for you at any register. 

people complaining about the price just do NOT know how to shop.  there are bargains hidden in the bulk bins, the 365 brand products, and frozen organic veggies and berries.

the bulk selection here is good. the snack food selection is also top notch. 

things i wouldn't buy here are vitamins (cheaper at vitamin shoppe) most produce  (cheaper at sook hee's or sue's produce) except fair trade bananas which are very competitively priced, and pre packaged or pre made microwave meals - just because i don't eat that anyway. 

pro tip:  check the whole deal either online or in the store for coupons.  often times things go on sale in the store while there is a coupon available.  for example yesterday i got a coupon in the "whole deal" for $1 off vegan mayo - AND the brand was also on sale 2/$6 - therefore what would have cost me $8 for two containers, cost me $5. 

also they price match trader joes now.  check out the 365 tofu for under $2 a package.

Authentic Thai food with some original flourishes.  My massaman curry was sweetened with pineapple - I really liked the taste it lent to the sauce but eating hot, mushy pineapple chunks themselves? Not so much.

Also, for all the reviewers complaining that the food isn't hot enough - there IS a spice caddy at your table, with two kinds of chili sauce, chili flake, and fish sauce, so you can add more heat.

Menu was limited, and the portions were on the small side, but I'd give Basil Spice another chance to really impress me.

Great neighborhood sports bar! Plenty of HDTV's within the establishment. Outside patio in the back for your smoking pleasure. Great selection of beer and liquor and the bar tenders are great. Plus a pool table! I love the locals here! However the bathrooms are always dirty.

What happened to this place???????It used to be so good!  Sat near a table with employees crap all over..... there were sneakers laying under the table, laptop and papers all over, vases, piñata......
We used to love this place.  The milkshakes are still really good.   Both my burger and my husbands burger were beyond well done when we asked for medium and medium well.   The onion rings were completely over cooked and the fries were not freshly made had been sitting and were cold.   My kiddos chicken tenders were sliced in half and dry as a bone.  Not sure if they slice them in half to make it look like you get more or what.   I even noticed the quality of the buns and produce wasn't as good.  And it was  even lettuce it was 3 scraps of ice burg core. 
We haven't been there for a long while and figured it would make a great treat for the family.  We won't be back.  So sad this place used to be great!  Maybe they were just having an off day.
Really no complaints. I never wait long to be seated and food is always our quickly and made just right. One of our top dining out places.

My IPad quit charging so I bought it to Fixit to be repaired and paid $30. They called to tell me it wasn't the battery or the charging port but, was the mother board and they couldn't fix it. I saw a video on line that showed how to install a jumper to bypass the motherboard and asked if they could do that, they declined.  I asked them to not put the IPad back together leave it apart put it in a bag and I will pick it up. When I picked it up they had put it back together I asked why and was told they didn't want to lose any parts. So I paid $30 for nothing because they don't have bags or don't listen to your wishes. 

I received a call From Kevin the manager of Fixit and he reviewed the repair ticket which showed I had asked for them not to reassemble my I pad. He asked me to bring it in so they could make things right. So they disassembled it at no charge as I waited. 

Kevin is an exception these days because he really cares about customer service and makes things right.

Does this place have some of the best donuts in the world? If they don't I am shocked.  I had a donut in here that I can only discribe as outstanding. Fantastic, fabulous. The second one I had was just Meh..... I was kind of disappointed. I have been here several times and I cannot seem to get a consistent product. A donut that is fresh and yummy one day is dry and bland another. 

The service moves at a moderate pace. The first visit, the place was packed and it took a while. The second time, the place was empty and the service took even longer. They were almost out of coffee and gave us three half filled cups of warm coffee. It tasted old. If you have brew, right on your sign, shouldn't you have fresh coffee at all times? Just saying.

I have tried the sliders, and they are very tasty with quality ingredients, but they are a bit pricey.  This place is often a madhouse with horrible parking, but I continue to go back. If you are ever walking down Magazine and want a little break, try it out.

We came here for lunch on a Monday and it was pretty empty. We had an awesome table in the back and there were not many tables near us. The décor is great and it had that clean fresh vibe. Parking was a little difficult as they share a small parking lot with other businesses and street parking was not readily available.

We got a handful of appetizers (all small and cheap so you can try many of them) and my favorite was the whipped feta. It was unlike anything I have had and was great to the mouth! For my entrée, I got the chicken shawarma, which was different, and fresh tasting, but didn't jive with my taste buds for some reason. The bathrooms are a must here and the soap is so great, we picked up a few bottles for home (they sell it there!). The service was great!

Oh my goodness I'm in love with this place. My first time here and I'll certain be back! EVERYTHING I tried on the menu was amazing. From drinks to salad and apps to the main course. The staff was very attentive, we never had to ask for a refill. On top  of it they all seemed happy to be here and we're eager to answers any questions about the restaurant and make recommendations. I indulged in the outside seating and loved the riverside view. I couldn't write a negative in this review if I tried. Can't wait to visit again!! Thank you for the great service Nikki!!

This place was great. It's hipster af and that can be annoying but I brought a couple friends and that made a big difference. The food and drink is sooo good. The cocktails are one of a kind and delicious. Spicy Louisiana spins on a few classic dishes. Brunch here is where it's at. So many places to eat in NEw Orleans that it's always a challenge to choose but you won't go wrong with a visit here.

When we were considering vendors for our November 2011 wedding, Birchtree immediately stood out. Not only were they the quickest to respond to our inquiry, instead of simply emailing us menu options, they first asked us questions about where we shopped and what kinds of restaurants we liked. By the time we met with Rasa for an initial consultation, we already had a feeling that they would be a perfect fit.

We tried to make very thoughtful decisions with our wedding budget and so it was important to us to support vendors we believed in. It is impossible for me to convey to the adequate degree how absolutely thrilled we were to work with Birchtree for this very reason. Every single person we interacted with was helpful, kind and amazingly talented. From the owners to the servers, everyone was lovely and clearly dedicated to making sure the event was a success. The food was delicious, perfect and literally everything we wanted. Multiple guests have told me that they have never had better wedding food and almost everyone commented that they loved the family-style dining option.

Throughout the planning process, Allegra was amazingly responsive and flexible. It was so incredibly helpful to know that she was just an email away. During our rehearsal and on the day of the wedding, Allegra made absolutely sure that everything went beautifully. It is not an exaggeration to say that we truly could not have pulled the day off without her coordination.

Working with Birchtree was probably the best decision we made during the entire wedding-planning process. The food was outstanding and the people were amazing. While we were on our honeymoon, my husband remarked that he wished we could have another party just so that we could enjoy the food all over again.

Eu daria 10 estrelas ,se fosse possível!
Um restaurante simples , no pier e que supera as expectativas!
Pra quem ama KING CRAB não pode deixar de vir! Recomendo com todas as forças!
Mas, tem que gostar de comer com a mão!

This place is terrible. Let's start with their service, or should I say lack of it. Waited over 10 minutes to get anyone to acknowledge us after we sat down. Had to continually ask for items that came with the meal, i.e. she never asked what salad dressing I wanted when I ordered. Had to ask for the bread too, which was supposed to come with the meal. Had I not asked for these items, I probably wouldn't have them served. I also had to ask for drink refills; this is a deal breaker for me since it tells me the server can't even pay attention to their customers. The food came, 35 minutes later, and it wasn't what I ordered. My wife's salad was mediocre at best. I ordered a pork chop and received a sandwich. I understand it was a busy Saturday night after Thanksgiving but great food and service should occur consistently. Not coming back.

Worst fried shrimp ever. The batter was so strange tasting. Almost like flour and water only was used to bread the shrimp. It was think, not crunchy and just tasted bad. The worst part was is that the manager new I disliked my meal and  just said sorry. Yuck I would never go back,

My husband & I enjoyed a delicious dinner at Maria's last night!!!  The hostess, waitress Colleen & all staff were so friendly & attentive!!!  We had eggplant involtini as an appetizer, salmon in a tomato sauce with mussels & clams & chicken parmesan.  I highly recommend all these dishes & Maria's!!

I had to mix my own drink. Let that sink in for a second....I. Had. To. Mix. My. Own. Drink. 

I checked out the menu in the lobby while I waited for friends. Saw that a regular frozen margarita was $6.75 and a flavored one was $8.50. Confirmed here on their website: http://neworleans.superiorgrill.com/drink-menu.html

When I asked the bartender what flavors of frozen margaritas they had, he rattled off a list: watermelon, peach, blackberry, and some others. I said I would like a blackberry frozen margarita.

The bartender served me a regular frozen margarita with a small glass of blackberry syrup on the side. "That'll be $11.75," he said. I said "I thought flavored margaritas were $8.50?" He said "That's only for strawberry."
