I said, "Why are you giving it to me like this? It's not mixed." He replied "So you can see what you are paying for."

I proceeded to pour the blackberry syrup into my tall margarita cup. It pooled on top of the drink and would not thoroughly blend with the rest of the drink. I asked the bartender if I could have a cup so I could mix the drink by pouring it back and forth between cups. Instead of offering to mix the drink himself, or providing me a spoon instead of a flimsy straw to mix my drink, he handed me a styrofoam cup.

There were two male customers on either side of me, they were audibly sympathizing with me and making comments about having to mix my own drink.

In retrospect, I should have asked to see the menu so I could point out that it said Flavored Margaritas were $8.50, and didn't say "Strawberry only." But at a crowded bar with people waiting behind me to be served, I didn't want to cause a scene.

Instead, I will vote with my feet and my wallet, and avoid Superior Grill and their lazy, apathetic, misinformed bartenders.

The staff is really helpful impatient especially when you don't know what title you need. It's great that they're spaces that you can review books and read a little bit of the book to see if you will truly enjoy it. The bathrooms are a little unkept.

We hired Kelly's limo for our daughter's senior prom. The driver was prompt and very courteous, there were sodas and snacks in the car. He drove them to dinner, to the prom and back home. It made her night extra special!! Thanks, Kelly!!

Great place in a great town. I come to the area on business one night a week and The Pint Room makes me look forward to my travels.  

A great, but limited, food menu complements the awesome selection of beer on tap.  99 handles of draft beer with a selection that should satisfy every beer palate.  The selections change frequently and often feature a mini tap takeover from a specific brewery.  I love that the selections are not the same old craft beers that I can get at any other craft beer bar.  They make it a point to feature local and other Indiana beers and I have had some awesome beers that I would probably have never come across. The beer prices are very reasonable in a world of inflated prices.  I always find myself taking advantage of the $1.75 samples so that I can taste a greater variety of beer.  

The food is not your typical pub grub.  The burgers are delicious with well thought out ingredients that make them unique. It would be hard to recommend just one burger as they have all been amazing.  I'm not sure how the cook their fries, but whatever they do makes them delicious.  

The staff has been amazing and their service beyond reproach.  I always sit at the bar when I dine there and have rarely had to wait very long before someone brings me a big glass of water and asks for my beer order.  And my beer glass does not remain empty for very long before I am asked if I would like another beer.  I have been very impressed with Zach behind the bar.  He provides great service, good beer recommendations and even remembers my name even though I am just in there one night a week.

Also, the clientele in the Pint Room is awesome.  I come here when I am on a business trip so I am eating alone.  There is always someone willing to chat about beer or life.  I have enjoyed that greatly.

Can you tell that I am a huge fan?  Wherever I have travel this is one of my favorite places to eat and drink.  Great beer, great food, great staff and a great atmosphere all at reasonable prices.  What more could you ask for?
The staff were extremely friendly and knowledgeable. The doctor was personable. I'm just sad I hadn't visited earlier!
I like this place!  They did a good job expanding.  I always get good service.  My friends and I have a good time here.

Nice cozy bar with magnificent cocktails and delicious bites in a trendy yet rustic atmosphere. The bar is narrow but it is a warm and inviting space. 

The cocktails are top-notch especially the Old Fashioned and the Manhattan made with cask-aged liquor. They use fresh ingredients in their cocktails. Everything I was able to try from their menus was just delicious. Happy hour is on weekdays from 4-7pm. Regular prices are not bad at all from 10$ to 13$ for fresh specialty cocktails. 

Bites are also delightful and reasonably priced. Some personal favorites are steamed buns, beef sliders, and beer poached shrimp. The bites menu usually runs from 6$ to 12$.

Although the place has a relaxed vibe it can get very busy and loud during weekend nights. Bartenders are knowledgeable and nicely dressed just adding to the great ambiance. 

 Cask and Ale is definitely an affordable gastronomic experience with mouthwatering bites and succulent craft cocktails.

As a big lover of BYO's, Porcini was on my list for restaurant week. You pick your app & entree, and they give a salad for the table and two desserts to share (for a table of two). It was satisfactory, but not sure if I'd elect to go back just because there are so many excellent BYO's around. 

I got brussels for my app and rigatoni salsiccia, my friend ordered burrata and the cheese raviolis. We both liked our appies, our salad wasn't a hit (it had pickles in it, and a lemony-briney dressing?), and she loved the ravs. My rigatoni was okay and the sausage was excellent. The desserts were also good, it was tiramisu and another type of creamy cake.

I love this place, have always went to this specific location for over 13 years. However I feel the quality of food is slowly going down. The staff on the other hand was amazing and couldn't ask for anyone better to help.

I'm not quite sure if these are in new customer relations handbook:

Rolling eyes when you walk into a empty restaurant because it forces you to work. Oh, and tell your co-worker "see?"

Slamming sandwiches on the table after you make them as fast as you possibly can

Make you wait five minutes to take your order (did I mention empty restaurant?)

Make you bag your own carry out (did I mention empty restaurant?) 

With love to see the appendix on the training guides at Jimmh Johns. Not what I recall in making the customer happy and retaining them.
Great Margaritas.   Fresh Guacamole is perfect.   The menu interesting and food well prepared.  Good service.  I need to come early because I can't stand the LOUD noise from the diners.
Fantastic service and for the price I do expect that. Eric is the best! And I won't go to anyone else, he always hits the right spot and is very professional.

Finally got around to eating here. Had been a huge fan of Daniel Stern at his Queen Village place (now closed) but had heard mixed things about R2L. Pleased to say I found it to be truly excellent. Shared an array of appetizers - all excellent: lobster Mac and cheese, steak tartare, mussels, truffle flatbread. My entree was the short rib, which was delicious. Plus, of course the unmatched view and a fine wine list. Will definitely be back!

Really terrific experience.  We brought a group of middle school students and split them up into the four different rooms that are offered.  Without exception, all the students (and the adult chaperones) had a fantastic time.  The puzzles were ingenious, and the person in the room with us was helpful but not TOO helpful - we definitely had to do a lot of problem solving.  Highly recommended!
I was dying to find a place like this. It's like a childhood dream came true. Really really awesome place. Best ice cream in Tampa IMAO.

A quick note: The Smile Shop for kids is in 475A on the left hand side... from the street it is hard to see the Smile Shop sign on the door. See my Frontage pic.

These folks are super professional in a brand new office they had custom built for their purposes.

They treat my children very well, and the staff seems organized if occasionally a little overwhelmed by the awesome newness of these new offices.

The dental hygienists were REALLY great with my 3-year old, and that's not always an easy trick. 
Dr. Melissa McCool was also wonderful to my child and the other family present.
http://www.smileshoponline.com/meet-us/

I'll be using this place for years and years.

I come to the peppermill often to Oceano for the Sushi.  I attended my first Yelp event at the Game Lab and had a blast.  It well very good and organized.  For the regular yelpers we got stuck with the left over food which was cold. But over all a great event. Thank you

As far as the Game Lab, the prices were average from what I seen around town. Good place to allow the kids to blow off steam while the parents do some gambling.  

P.S.  if you haven't had the all you can eat sushi at Oceano please do its awesome.  The atmosphere is to die for.  Try Oceano sushi and the BLTA Rolls.

Have done a lot of shoppig there at lunch time cause it's near my office.   Effective yesterday I will no longer patronize this store.   I found out that this store does not participate in the redeem points for gas program for use at Giant gas stations.   I can do same shop at Giants in Trooper or  or Limerick on my way home and redeem some points.  Also yesterday I stupidly did not pick up the $20 at the self check out that I had requested.  A few seconds after I realized I had not, I ran back.  The person who checked out immediately after me took it.   I know it's my fault but when I reported it to management, they said nothing they could do.  So I gave them my contact information in the event that the person who took it might turn it in, all they could say was 'good luck with that one'.      Since the person behind me had also requested cash back I thought maybe they didn't realize they took an extra 20 and might return it.  I think based on their credit card information the management would be able to identify and contact them and ask but they would not.   Since over the years I have spent 1000s of $ there and since they basically blew me off, plus no redeem points program I am done with them.

mmm, satco tastes like procrastination!

great for buckets of beer when you should be studying.  a la carte prices on taco toppings always pissed me off thought.  only place ive ever been to, and i do alot of tacos, that charges by the topping.  i guess youre supposed to order your tacos after the first bucket...

when it comes to walking distance (from vandy) tacos and beer , this is your place.  of course, i always wondered by faculty didnt install a webcam for attendance records.

I'll start by saying that mellow mushroom is my favorite pizza in the world, but the Brandon location is consistently inconsistent. I travel for a living and have eaten at Mellow Mushroom all over the country, the Brandon location has a different taste and look than anywhere else. It is always very sparse with the toppings, compared with all the other locations.  When you have four different toppings on a pizza and can take 2 to 3 bites without biting into any ingredient, then something is wrong! The jerk chicken barely has any spice on it,  to the point where you can't even taste the spice. The last three times I have gone they have completely gotten the order wrong. The last time was for my birthday and we live an hour away. When they got it wrong the waitress very reluctantly took it back and have them fix another one. It's like she made me feel guilty for them messing it up. Then I went today on the way home, and they didn't put the sun-dried tomato on it. The clock actually argued with me that it was on there when I told him to pointed out, he said it was under the cheese. So I then proceeded to peel all the cheese back and it was not there. He again gave me attitude for putting on something that I had already paid for. I am convinced that the owner of this location purposely scrimps on the ingredients to save money. On top of that customer service is terrible to the point where I don't even feel like ever coming back. And that says a lot for my favorite pizza.

The whole reason we drive out of the way and come to this Twistee Treat is because they have no sugar added/sugar free ice cream that is extremely hard to find. But today the machine was "broken", trip wasted. My not seem like a big deal to most people, but when sugar is an issue these places stand apart, but like I said, not today.

Pop took us out for his 87th birthday. After checking to see if this was a dog friendly facility, we brought our pooch, Millie Moonshine.  We were a party of 7 plus Millie. We were seated at a large table, a little enclosed by the parking lot, but still had a view of the gulf. We picked the table since this was our 1st dining experience with our adopted dog. We brought her water and food. We started out with appetizers of Southern Fried Pickles, Crisp Onion Straws, and Loaded Baked Potato Boats. All were excellent. Our entrees were cooked well and presented excellently. Everyone except me took half of their dinners home. I ate the whole thing. It was not loud, music was fine, people were having a good time. The view of the gulf is magnificent, especially at sunset. We hung around to watch the International Space Station emerge from the SW horizon over the gulf and fly directly over head departing to the NE.. 
Millie ate all her food and drank her water and slept under the table for the most part. She did really well.
Large crowds waited to get in as we were leaving.
I want to thank the staff for making it a great time for all.
Love this area! So many hikes..amazing flora and fauna. You can escape the crowds by choosing more obscure hikes or by going early.Definitely go early if you want to park in the main lot.

Really neat find in Dunedin.  Cute place, friendly service and Hawaiian food meets Mexican food.  Sounds weird but cool flavorful mashup.  

We had the veggies nacho starter.  Delicious chips tasted house made, lots of cheese and good mix of red bell pepper, squash & mango to name a few. The sauce drizzled over it was so good I thought they should add a little more;)

Husband had the tuna poke appetizer for his entree, really good & fresh tuna.  Would have been even more amazing with my Kilauea entree's sauce drizzled over it so he kept dipping from my plate.

I had the Kilauea warm shredded sweet pork, over a bed of fresh spinach and black rice.  The sauce knocked it out of the park.  I got the spicy lava sauce and it had a kick but didn't overwhelm the entree. Perfect.

Bar had some cool drink specials too.  The Hula Mary, their spin of the Bloody Mary (had bacon & cheddar stuffed olives).  Looked great.  All in all an excellent lunch.

This place is one of the best spots for locals and tourists in French Quarter.  The shrimp and grits are heaven on a plate.  Their Crab cake is the gold standard.  Lunch specials include ridiculously cheap drinks and a variety of delicious smaller plates.  

I like to sit at the bar to eat, nonsmoking thankfully.  You get a bit more caudal and friendly service there.

Our experience was great! The owner was very nice and recommend the best mattress for our kids and us. He was not pushy and never gave us any religion talk as the other review said. The prices are wonderful. If I had gone any where else I would of paid double for my king bed. I brought 3 kids into the store and he was very understanding when one of my son's started crying because we would not buy the gel bed for my son. Super fast delivery! We got our bed the same day. The bed is super comfy and I can say my experience was the best... Thank You

I absolutely love this Starbucks - servers are friendly, coffee is always well crafted and if you go during down times they're pretty quick. My only gripe with this starbucks is obviously the parking lot is ridiculously small - forget going there in the morning when it's work time. You will never get a parking spot and the drive thru will take forever. The longest I've ever waited in the drive thru is 20 minutes and the only reason I stayed is because I couldn't get out of the line due to the high curb. 

Now if you can go after the morning craziness the service is superb. Also the pastries and breakfast sandwiches are fresh. I've had the croissants, very berry coffee cake, banana bread, brownies, bacon & gouda breakfast sandwich (this was just okay), veggie & monterey jack breakfast sandwich, turkey bacon and white cheddar breakfast sandwich and never left there disappointed.

There is no problem a taco can't fix. 

Indy Tacos popped up in my neighborhood a few weeks ago, and during that time I had three people tell me I had to stop by. We went for an early dinner around 5:30 on a weekday.

The owners are super excited to finally start their businesses. You can tell because when you walk in they take the time to explain the menu to you and after you get your food, they ask you how much you enjoyed your meal. Everyone was all smiles - and so was I, especially after I bite into the chorizo taco.

All of the tacos are made with soft corn tortillas doubled up around four meat options: chicken, steak, chorizio and pork. We ordered one of each (about $2.50 per taco) to try. Every one of them was delicious but the flavors in the chorizo really made me close my eyes and think about how happy I was at that exact moment. The pork comes not shredded but chunks that are swimming in some kind of chili sauce. Nothing was too spicy - but that's OK because the green and red salsa that accompanied the meal can take care of your need for extra heat.

Chips and salsa are a must - especially the homemade guac. 

The elote is just what I wanted - corn on a cob with a little mayo, a little cheese and a unique blend of spices. 

Indy Tacos accepts cash and credit, is open every day 11-8 except Mondays when they are open 4-8 (at least at the time that I write this review). Order tacos to dine in or take them to go.

I came here for a rehearsal dinner on a Friday night.  The place is charming and the food and the service was very good.  The only complaint I have is the room on the second floor that held our party was rather tight.  Also, there are not enough chairs for guests to sit down to get a break from standing in high heels all day long.

I RECOMMEND  Getting Your Toyota From A More Trustworthy Dealership.
These Guys Seem to Exhibit Symptoms of Opportunists.  

The car alarm waves have been going pretty solid  since 8:45   My Mom is visiting and has MS which includes some brain pain.  (Hence my roof deck yelling frustration; also told employee, who thought I made it up or didn't care) Employee play acted like he was a customer at first, said we should do more about handling the sound in other ways, suggesting??  Phone calls we do have are pretense at us having bought a car with a faulty alarm. (This confusion twist only works as a "misunderstanding" the first time. After that we figured they were playing us for chumps on purpose. Especially when they add- "well I don't know who you would talk to about that...."  As if no person at Sloan has know-how or ability to handle this car alarm mayhem). Not just one car. Not just one day. The alarms are on and off all day after day, with many cars.  We had called the cops after a couple years of honk honk honk honk honk...shenanigans.  Officer wondered why they don't press unlock, and look for headlight flash.  Me too.  Especially on rainy days.  (Which it was when the officer came by). I mention this to the employee.. He says they need the honks to find the cars.  My honey says "chart".  Employee (straw blonde facial hair) says "no chart..." Any advice yelpers?? My honey got desperate and held up a Toyota sucks makeshift sign over the fence.  The guy told him "Toyota makes the best cars, too bad there's nothing you can do." (to deter, I assume).  But I would do this...I Recommend Getting Your Toyota From More Trustworthy Dealership.. I don't know what level these guys can be trusted at sales wise... but they are not "work With you", guys.. 

Last year I talked with a Scotts Honda dude, who told me that Sloan Toyota put a billboard for their dealership right at the exit to Scotts Dealership.  When I asked about similar tactics from them (Honda) they said nah.  We don't swing that way.  Good way to be Honda. Better man than me.  And definitely better than Sloane.

This place is great! Their drink specials always have fun names, their fried chicken and breaded mushrooms are addictive, and of course the pizza is the best. I have been eating here for about a year or so now, and I have tried a variety of their pizzas. Delicious!

The kids enjoy the games on the family friendly side, and the bar area is a lovely place to catch up with friends. I highly recommend this place!

We saw the reviews and decided to try this place out, since it was close. The decor of the restaurant is decent. The service was ok, nothing great but satisfactory. We ordered several items including a seaweed soup, speciality roll, sashimi, and a more basic roll. The soup was ok, lacked flavor but not too bad. The sashimi was decent, tasted like it had been sitting for a while. The sushi was not good -- tasted old and was actually somewhat dark in color. The other roll was actually difficult to eat -- it tasted stale and old. The menu said "tempura" style, but what we actually got was a fried piece of I don't know. 

I travel regularly on business and have experienced some excellent sushi in Seattle, San Francisco, Dallas, and even here in Philly there are some excellent spots in neighboring Chestnut Hill and even a 1/2 way decent buffet on the other side of 476 in Plymouth meeting. This sushi lacked freshness and flavor -- two important qualities that make sushi so great.

This place is in an unassuming location with but a few tables and nothing remarkable as far as wall hangings or decorations. My wife and I showed up at around five on a Saturday. We were the only ones there for about half an hour. Not knowing much about Indian food, we guessed through the menu, but each of our guesses turned out to be fantastic hits.

The naan is perfectly crafted, we has some great chaak as an appetizer, and I had some sizzling lamb kabob, which was definitely the highlight of the meal. Even if you have no experience with Indian food, this restaurant is a must if you live in the area. It's my understanding that this place is relatively new.

As a plus, the wait staff was very pleasant. My wife and I definitely plan to go again soon.

Not a bad place for regular diner fare. Friendly staff. A little cramped inside. Ceiling tiles were sagging. Seats and all felt cheap. Stupid cheap meals(a good thing). I don't really feel strongly about this place to continue writi

I've had Spice n Grill a few times more.  What a great place, and great staff.  Spice n Grill finally started making real naan!  However, I'm not sure if they're really making it on-site or not;  I saw the cook warming it on the stove on an upside-down wok rather than in a real tandoor, and it's flavor and texture still isn't as good as fresh-out-of-the-tandoor naan you can get elsewhere.  Weird but still satisfying.

The food here is still really, really good.  The ghee they use in the chicken tikka masala is outstanding in quality, and she uses a lot of it.  The only complaint I have is that everything is still just a little bit too salty sometimes.  They've also already raised the prices on their menu for some items, which is hopefully not going to happen for the rest of the menu.

That being said, please go.  Try the beef nihari, the chicken tikka masala, and the chicken biryani.  Really good food and excellent service by kind people.

Very creative food with perfect portion sizes.
For once I didn't feel like I was going to explode from over eating.
Great cocktail program.
Service was top notch with a nod towards comfort. (A very nice blend you don't see too often).
Will surely be back!

Had my brother in law's wedding reception here. My sis in law and I went here on the day of the reception and spoke to Danny (manager I believe?) We confirmed how the tables were going to be set up and also confirmed the food order. There were 42 people that attended and they set up a long table in the back of the restaurant. Food was delicious! Service was great!
This is my favorite St. Louis restaurant!!! I love the Pepperloin Tenderloin and the Athenian Broil is to die for! The staff is very attentive and the owner comes around to check on everyone.

I have a difficult-to-fit foot for dance shoes. Lauren and Sue made the whole process a pleasure. They kept coming out with different shoes and sizes until we found not one, but two, that were perfect. I highly recommend the selection, and wonderful owner and staff here.

I go to el camino on occasion and the service is usually great! There was one time the service was a little slow but the waitress was super nice and I saw that she was busy so I was pretty understanding. Their happy hour specials are a awesome. My friend and I went the other day for some drinks and the girl bartender that was working was very friendly! Half priced margarita pitchers for hh! Can't beat that :P

This place is one of the most amazing, delicious, and affordable places we have ever visited. Sean is friendly and knowledgeable about his drinks and the food here is absolutely delicious. Andrew the chef knows what he is doing. All the food is fresh and he makes everything from scratch. Definitely come here for brunch and get the pretzel bagel salmon. This place is so good. Everyone come here and drink with friends.

Pretty nice restaurant.Shrimp and Grits were awesome choice.The best thing they had on the menu.I also had a chance to taste their kids fried shrimp and that was good as well. Over all it was a good restaurant.

I love this place. I stop by every chance I get when passing through Nashville.  I have tried a few sandwiches and several of the hot entrees. My favorite sandwich is the muffuletta. It never disappoints. My favorite hot entree is the Jerusalem chicken. 
The way it works.. there is a cold salad area which has mixed salads and the fixings for a "tossed" salad. You tell the guy behind the counter what you want. The hot bar works similarly in that you tell the guy what you want. You can have the already prepared items from the hot bar or order sandwiches from the menu. You then take your ticket to the front of the store to pay. I can't close this review without mentioning the chili cornbread muffins... they are yummy. I always take a couple home!!!  Tonight I ate one while waiting on my sandwich and took one home.

Not impressed at all. Tiny rolls for a hefty price plus very bland. Ordered three specialty rolls among other things and paid over $100. So not worth it. Gave an extra star for nice staff. Won't be going back as there are other places that are much better.

A great ballpark! There's never a bad view, no matter how high up your seats are. The best stadium food ever (except the beers are a little pricey). 

Always a fun time, even when the Phillies are playing horribly. The Phanatic really makes the game. It's always entertaining! A definite must go for spring/summer fun!

The food was very good. We shared a stack of pancakes that were amazing.. hint of cinnamon in them. He had an omelette and I had eggs with potatoes. The inside is EXTREMELY small so we sat outside. Friendly staff.. food took about 30 minutes to come out and we were in a hurry but will definitely come back!

Had the shrimp lomein with fried rice and it was delicious, the portions were good  ...I'm very picky with food but this place was great and the service was too ...
Ps. They give you an egg roll on the side and it's bomb ! Love it love it love it !

Absolutely tasty food in a stylish atmosphere.
We enjoyed the Rittenhouse Benedict and the normal burger. Both presented a broad range of different flavors, all in perfect alignment with the bar style and the expectation of high quality food.
The place is rather small and can therefore require some waiting time.

Dude.  Brah.  This is the place for Breakfast.  It looks like lunch is covered review-wise so let me tell you about the most important meal of the day.  Bekfast!

I ordered the 2-2-2.  I didn't pay attention to what the other selections were, 3-3-3 & 4-4-4 and so on, but what I picked was what I needed! Man it was great!   Oh yeah I see omelettes on the menu. 

It came with 2 eggs, 2 sausages, 2 bacon.  So I guess it's not that hard to figure out the rest of the other breakfast selections above :).  The sides that it came with that wasn't mentioned was grits, oven roasted potatoes (!) and a bread. Toast or a biscuit. Take the biscuit!  All that for $5.50!! 

I didn't notice if there was pancakes in the menu, if so, they are neck and neck with Ruby Slipper, Buns and Biscuits on Banks and City Diner.  Not a cool decor or anything fancy. Typical Westbank style but Brah ...  It's good!

Grits was just right, potatoes were seriously on point and the rest was how it should be. Perfect.  

The inside of the business must of changed since last reviewers been here. There is plenty of booth tables and the food was served on heavy plates and real silverware.    The lady that was mentioned in the other reviews is still there. Very friendly and patient.   The food came out fairly quick. So it is totally doable to pull off the road and eat and leave in 10 mins.  Keeps the mess out of your car too.  

I was looking behind the counter and it's a really wide selection back there.  Like there is a sort of hidden fully stocked back there with 4 beers on tap.  Strange but I'm talking a lot of booze.  Not sure when that comes into play but they have it.  Also a jukebox and a video poker machine.  

If you are feeling tired of the same old fast food choices and want that full satisfied warm tummy feeling for breakfast, don't even hesitate to visit them!!

I pretend that I'm a refined film buff, but sometimes you just need to catch a double feature of two marginally decent movies while eating Twizzlers out of the center console. Tibbs is a blast from the past, and while it may not be in the greatest location, I always have a good time so long as I stay awake for the second movie.

Pro-tip: swing by Mug 'N Bun before you head over to stake out your parking spot. A tenderloin as big as your steering wheel is definitely worth the trip a few miles away in Speedway.

I heard a lot about the new location on Penn's campus but didn't get a chance to go until today. I was hesitant about the family style at first, but am pleasantly surprised with the portion-size. Our waiter, Anthony, is extremely helpful and knowledgeable and provided with very good service. 
I agree with the reviews that say to order one less dish than the party size. I went with a party of 7 around 7:00, and we haven't eaten anything all day. We order 7 dishes and were stuffed by the end and even had leftovers. 
I was expecting a relatively large bill but the final cost is less than what we estimated per person. 
Not everyone in my party eats spicy food, so we got mild (around 2 or 3 stars) for most dishes, and everyone seems to be okay with that level. Rice is included with the entrees and there are free refills which is helpful in helping wash the spiciness down. Our table really enjoy the Beef & Tripe in Chili Oil even though we kept it at 10 stars. I would definitely go back again and I could say that my experience would be even better now that I know what to expect from it!

It's great if you pay money to go on the nights that aren't free. The passes you can get are super reasonable, with my kids I would probably use it every week.  I mean this place is great when its not cram packed with people lol. I love that the first Thursday of the month is free but so does everyone else.  Still all in all it's a great place to learn with your kids, yes even the grown ones!!!

First time there on Friday night. Service is good but it took them a while to answer my gluten free questions. Then they took out their GF menu. That was helpful. I'd say on the expensive side though.

We tried Fat Elvis and Key Lime Pie...both are great. We were also there at 11pm on a Friday and they still had plenty of donuts...much better than other places I've been that usually only have crumbs by then.

It was awful, we won't be back. The server was unfriendly and impatient. My chicken piccata was tough. I joked that it could be chicken jerky. I thought that the portions were small for the price. My daughters pizza was decent but I would probably go to Gina's on Columbia road for better pizza and all together a better menu.

Family-run BYO with great food and a quirky charm. 

A little awkward in the service department, but cozy.

The decor is silly and fun but still retains it's small, romantic atmosphere anyhow.

Food is on fleek. Get the giant cold app platter to start and the giant grilled meat platter to share. You'll be so happily full of food. Such a good amount of flavor and char while still being juicy.

This is a great place to go for happy hour after work, or for a drink before going to a show, or just to hang out on the weekend before you go dancing somewhere.

They have a great selection of beers and wines. Great tapas, extensive list of cheeses, and really nice atmosphere. Also, servers are very attentive and helpful if you need to pair a tapa with a beer or a glass of wine.

They have an event calendar with wine tasting activities, wine classes and the Sunday school, where you get to try a different cheese, wine and beer.

Downside is that, because so many people like this place, it can get really crowded. There are two locations though, Rittenhouse and the one in Spruce. During the summer you can sit outdoors.
Need to dress up? This amazing seamstress, outfit designer has everything for dress up, Halloween whatever! Always find what I need and owner is so very nice!

I went here for drinks with a friend on a weekend night. The bar area was way too small for the amount of people. Because of the amazing view from the room and the classy atmosphere, I can see this as being a very popular place for drinks. However, like I said they need more room. 

The drinks themselves were pretty good, but the service was not. We were able to snatch a high table near the bar, but had a lot of trouble getting a waiter to take our order. 

This place has so much potential, and the view is amazing, but they need to expand.

The food was good, not going to lie about that, and for a fair price. Only reason why it got 2 stars. As long as I don't catch something from the people handling our food with their bare hands without washing once!!! 

Not to mention two times I've been here had very rude wait staff that seemed like the last thing they wanted to do at this moment was take my order and bring my food. Once may be a mistake, happening 2 times is a problem. There will not be a third time. Maybe eventually they will stop neglecting us and serve us our food so we can eat, go and never come back.  

My tip is to the people cooking food in the back. Pretty disgusted that person handling all the raw food and stuff going into my mouth is not wearing any gloves and didn't see her wash her hands once. Won't come here again, don't want to risk getting me and my family sick. The health inspector should pay this place a visit.

Have been coming here for years. Glad to finally see a decent cider on the list instead if woodchuck and magners. Good has always been fairly consistent,  and the new decor is a welcome change as they bring a little city atmosphere into the burbs similar to Nectar. 

Not to keen on seeing the prices increase beyond normal bar/pub type prices. Burgers/sandwiches easily reaching the teens is a bit much. Have had the same if not better food at Kelly's for less. Still some of the better fajitas in the area which is my GF go to,  minus the tortillas of course. And Angry Orchard cider is a welcome addition. Miss the Dara Estelle beer though. 

Still good for catching a bite during a game and the beer selection is always vast for the non-glutarded. Would love to see some back to back big screens in the main dining room. Would make for a nice divider and not have to wonder what people are cheering about. 

Would love to see Marathon Grill take Food Source's location and bring some nice competition to them.  Iron Hill will do the same when it opens in Ardmore.

Stopped at this diner because of all the great reviews, however, it didn't live up to the reviews I read, at least not for us. 

One, as soon as you walk in there was a bucket & newspapers because the roof was leaking. Now, this is not uncommon weather for it to constantly rain. If you looked up at the ceiling you could see how the tiles were holding on to water as if could fall at any second. 

Second, food was flavorless. However, food arrived promptly and the service was okay.
Great owners, even better staff, and even better still is the food. This is THE SPOT when you get the munchies downtown.
their spicy fried rice is amazing and pretty much anything else is good too. wish they were open on Sundays for lunch.

This restaurant is more Lebanese than Greek but none the less great tasting Mediterranean flavors. In the mood for some Greek food, found this spot on yelp and had some pretty good reviews as well as some yummy looking pictures! I had the shrimp kabob dinner which came with rice, salad, hummus, pita bread, and some large shrimp. It was just delicious and full of flavor! Good portions of food for the price. I also had the spinach pies, they were very fresh and crispy. The spinach inside was soft and creamy and seasoned lightly. My husband had the gyro meat platter. He did not care too much for the hummus so they substituted that for fries. It was a very large plate of salad and gyro meat on top. He said it was very good but he wished the pita bread were a bit more softer. Overall great place for some Mediterranean flavors! Great food and service!

Came for a brew tour, left with an addiction to their pumpkin ale. Food was great, beer was unbelievably tasty. I'd definitely recommend the Moose Milk. If you have the time, take the tour and ask for Cameron. Cameron was really patient, very informative, and really went out of his way to make the tour memorable.

Our room was amazing!  Very clean and big enough to comfortably fit 2 adults and 2 children. The hotel itself was very clean and quiet. Staff was always willing to help us out when needed. There is a free shuttle to provide transportation within the immediate area or they can help you get a cab. My only complaint was breakfast. I wish there were more kid friendly options aside from cereal or a waffle. Maybe plain eggs?  Sausage?  Not sure. All in all I was VERY pleased with my stay and will be back if ever in the area.
Absolutely fantastic! Must haves - pesto rotolos, quattro formaggi, and pepperonis!

After I found "the dress" at a local bridal boutique, I still wanted to do some price matching to see if I could get a better deal, as I had already raised the amount I was willing to spend for my wedding dress in order to get what I really wanted. I came across bestbridalprices.com but was skeptical about buying online due to horror stories I've read about. I did some research on the company and the designer of my dress (Sottero & Midgeley by Maggie Sottero) and found that the website was a "premier authorized dealer". The website is linked to the physical store called Frew's Bridal in Alton, IL. 

The price was the best that I found anywhere in the Chicago area by at least $400, not to mention they were running a deal to get a free veil up to $100 and free shoes up to $50 and free shipping (although there are restrictions on the designers to choose from). A pretty good deal that can save a decent amount of money! The ordering process was fairly easy as well, although I didn't have an area to provide comments or specify a hollow to hem size, which would have been nice since the dress fits perfectly except the length is way too long. The shipping was way faster than estimated!!! I ordered March 31st and it wasn't scheduled to be delivered until July, but it came at the beginning of June!! I know these have a lot to do with the designer, but the dress goes to the store first to be checked before being shipped to the customer, so still great turn-around time. When I received the dress, there were 2 small areas where the stitching was loose. I called the store in the required timeframe and they didn't hesitate to let me return it to have it fixed by the designer. I declined, opting to have my seamstress fix it when she shortens the dress, since it was very small fixes and my parents were visiting soon and I really wanted my mom to see the dress since it would be the only chance before the wedding next year. 

I have 2 complaints. First, the veil was delivered in a round plastic container and it was kind of folded in, so I'm going to have to mold it to shape to my head or it will be sticking out every which way. I wish they would ship them in a container where the whole thing can lay somewhat flat. Second, the shoes I ordered were 1/2 size too small (my big toes hung over the edge a bit). I tried to exchange them since I didn't wear them anywhere and they were still in the packaging in perfect condition, but they wouldn't do it. I even took extra time looking at similar shoes and sizes to try to get it right the first time, but you can never 100% get it right with different brands. I think this was completely unreasonable and stupid - so make sure to pick the right size. At least they were free, but I wouldn't order the right size from them since I don't want to chance that those could possibly still be the wrong size and not be able to exchange or return them.

Overall, great company to work with minus the whole shoe debacle.

Teetering between 3 and 3 1/2 stars. 1/2 star extra for the location and surprising lack of sit down restaurants within walking distance to Clearwater beach near the pier. Lots of fried options and a few broiled platters on the menu. 

Cute decor and live music on the downstairs. We sat upstairs and couldn't hear the music.

We ordered the spinach crab dip for starter. Served with extremely salty chips. It had a layer of unappetizing hardened cheese on the top but once u got that bad boy outta the way it was decent. Good deal during happy hour for beer. On to my lobster roll. I used to go out to montauk for my fix and this wasn't as good. A bit under seasoned but otherwise ok.  Hubs got the broiled seafood and I tasted the scallops. Worst I've ever tasted. 
Service was ok but kitchen must've been backed up even though it wasn't too crowded.

Have your event here!!  We recently had our wedding ceremony and reception here, and couldn't have been happier.  No joke.  First off, all of our guests keep saying, and rightly so, that is is absolutely the coolest and most unique venue they've ever seen.  From the very beginning Aliza and Samantha made the planning process easy and fun.  There's a real attention to detail, and you can tell they really enjoy what they do and that they're having fun.  Chef Aliza Green is incredible, and loves to cook interesting things.  If you're looking for a "chicken or fish" type of event, you're doing yourself a dis-service (though I'm sure it'd be delicious too).  We sat with her and she asked us about what foods we liked and grew up with from our families and our cultures, and she had an interesting take on each aspect of what we thought our "theme" might be.  People were raving.

Walking in on the day of our wedding, we had zero concerns that things would be setup and would run the way that we wanted them to, and honestly it was even better than we could have hoped.  We wanted to have not only a unique and really special event, but we wanted to throw a really great party, and from what our friends and family keep telling us, I know we succeeded.

Seriously they were so great here from start to finish (and after).  Flexible and creative, and easy-going while still professional.

Couldn't have asked for a better experience.

2.5 stars...

I would like to give you a better rating because you're close to being something pretty good but its really not there yet. Like others mention below, the atmosphere is fun and a good local spot but the food has no flavor. The ingredients are there - fresh and good quality, but my taste buds are left screaming for more every time!!

I went there for dinner while in the Tampa area and had a great meal.   They have multiple Vegan and Vegetarian options, while also having a full bar with Guinness.   Very unusual across the good ole USA.

The place is in an interesting area, which seems it could be a little rough in the dark, so if you go, I would recommend going during the light hours.

The bartenders are really nice, and helpful with picking a good dish.
First timer. I got chocolate coconut on bottom and coconut on top, then topped it with coconut & almonds! yummmm :)

Great happy hour featuring creative drinks.  Inexpensive, but quality cocktails.  Pictured are the jalapeño strawberry margarita and the black widow.  Easy to get to in the CBD and ample parking.  Huge bar and spacious seating area.  Small plates are perfect for sharing.  Tacos are $2 on Thursday Caliente Nights.
Kicked everyone out at 1:40, despite their door saying 2:00 am close. Clearly just wanted our money then wanted us to leave. Bartenders were not friendly and bouncer was a jerk. Do not go here.

The Pitch Back team made me a new design for my business cards and magnets for my vehicle. They came out great! It was no hassle at all; reasonably priced. If I would have know it was that easy I would have done this long ago. Thanks guys!
They have the best wings around! I really loved them. I'll def come here for my wing fix from now on.

Small place tucked away on lower state.  I really like the order first then sit down aspect.  We had the French toast and the Chorizo Hash Special.  You can't really go wrong with French toast.  The chorizo hash was disappointing and not an "off the chart" breakfast choice.  The coffee was just ok.  I probably need to try another menu item before abandoning this option.

Oh my gosh!  This is one of the finest musical instruments store I've ever visited. 

First, when you walk in you're greeted by one or more staff members.  Even the nearby customers greet you as they're happy to be in a happy place with more happy people coming in.  It's a vibe thing!  

The expertise is phenomenal and they're well-staffed so no one is rushed in helping customers.  From entering to being rung-up the experience is nothing but outstanding.

We had dinner there tonight for the first time. The inside has been remodeled with new tables, chairs, paint and decor. The tables and chairs look to have been carved and hand painted giving a feeling of being in Mexico. We did not see it before but it looks very nice and colorful. The service was fast and friendly. The menu was nice and not overwhelming with choices. The food was priced reasonably. There was four of us and all the meals were very good and looked nice enough to photograph and share. We will make this one of our regular stops for a good meal. It was hot out tonight but there was a nice seating area out front that would be good on a cooler night.

I am not sure what the previous reviews were referring to as the staff is always so nice and helpful! Sandra who is extremely knowledgable is attentive and never tried to push you. I actually went to her as a friend referred me when I explained my current dermatologist was horrible! If you don't want to wait book first thing in the am!!! I highly recommend

We randomly picked extreme tacos after noting the post reviews on yelp. We were at the Museum of science and industry and this was pretty close by. The service was awesome and the person that took her order was incredibly friendly and very helpful. My husband had the extreme burrito. It was very large and incredibly flavorful. I had to extreme chicken tacos. I make sure to add some of the mild salsa and lime. The tacos were bursting with flavor We also got two elites cups. One was the extreme and one was the traditional. They were both fabulous with just the right amount of spice. We will definitely come back when we were in Tampa.

This place isn't my favorite, but i can walk here, and i do end up here sometimes.
Last time i was there I got something that came on a skinny little cedar board, I think its supposed to infuse the salmon with a deep rich flavor, or something insane like that.
well, it was a nightmare to navigate, and a bunch of some sauce got all over me, and it was all i could do to not loose my mind.
Don't order the thing that comes on the board.

Great staff. 

Cool environment and a tequila trading board. 

Food was ok.  My order initially was cold and had to be re ordered.  Tacos lacked any real taste and seasoning. 

Cool place to chill but foods forgettable.

Solid brunch fare. 

Got the eggs in toast. How do they do that magic? Chickens, laying eggs that appear in bread? OMG. Anyway, it was delicious. The only downside was it cooled fast and I like my eggs as hot as poss. 

The restaurant itself was cute and the bathrooms were clean. The service was excellent and the fresh squeezed orange juice didn't appear to be a lie. It was pulpy and good. Mmm. 

This would be a good place for a smallish group to come, there looked like enough seating for up to 6 or 8 at once. So bring everyone you know! Have delicious bread eggs!
Went for breakfast and had the peppers n eggs on a roll.  Very good sandwich.   The service was also very good, very friendly.

This place has relentless security who think they are allowed to put their hands on women. I was basically RUSHED by the security here and their 6 ft tall security group of 7 men surrounded me a - 130 little girl, a guy grabbed my arm & told me they saw me on camera being offensive towards one of their employees in a parking lot - 

Might I elaborate on that "offensiveness" - one of their employees was driving about 30MPH inside a parking garage when I was crossing the roadway area they were coming down & refused to slow down or stop while I walked across their path... They were within feet of hitting and potentially killing me & after I made my way across and the employee passed they laid on their horn as if I should've gotten out of their way??? So yes I flipped them off because I do not know how anyone else learned to drive but Im pretty sure pedestrian no matter where they are - have the right away... Any how as I walked back into the casino a man grabbed my arm from behind me and scared me so I pulled my arm back and said "dont touch me" as any women would say being grabbed by someone from behind - this man then proceeded to tell me I am trespassing because I was obscene to an employee of theirs... I was baffled & confused as the moment of the actual incident that had happened in the parking garage an hour earlier had already passed... I asked what he was talking about and he said "You flipped off & said -Fuck off" to one of our employee's... I was soo confused as to what was going on - I asked to speak to a supervisor who was very unhelpful & just asked me to leave, after I had already had my room for three days without incident... 

They were asking me to leave because their employee refused to slow down for me in the parking garage and I felt I should flip them off as they were rude practically almost killing me - yet the employee who is so innocent in this situation must've had a bad day/night because he took the time to call his boss and have us escorted out... Anyhow the reason behind this is all because someone wouldn't slow down in a parking garage and almost hit one of their customers... I would say that the employee would need a disciplinary action as well but it seems as if this place ONLY thinks THEIR EMPLOYEE'S who run down customers are right... I mean I could understand their structure but I wasn't drunk nor exploitative... I was calm & scared shitless of the 7 security men hovering over me

This place is a rip off. Took my dog there for tooth extraction. They examined her and gave me a written estimate. For best case/worst case. The bill came out to 150. Over worst case. Call to complain because my wife was there not me. And told them i was only going to pay their worst case bill. The lady on the phone told me they would send the dog home without any pain medication. Are you kidding me. This is a complete rip off.

Great new asian restaurant in Kimberton area.  Combination Chinese/Japanese/Thai menu.  We tried the sushi and som Thai food and both were excellent.  There is only one other sushi place in the area I know of and this place is better and less expensive.  It remains to be seen if that is just to entice people to come back given they're a new business but they did a terrific job of quantity, quality and cost.

I was here a month ago when I was visiting from LA and left a little sad knowing that this little gem is in Santa Barbara.

The food was really amazing and the workers were super attentive, ensuring we were having a good experience. Don't let the simple interior deter you from coming - all the food was so light and delicious that we were dreading the end of the course! 

I would definitely come back if I pass by or visit SB again!

Set back in a Feasterville stip center between a UPS store and an ice cream parlor, my expectations were not too high. Boy was I wrong. The food here was fresh, hot and very tasty. The authentic Latin food, delivered in a fast food environment, was not only plentiful but more than fairly priced.

Gena was great as she talked us through the ordering process. My wife and I each had bowls. Hers was chipotle flavored chicken and I had the shredded pork. We customized our bowls and the added grilled veggies and pico maxed out the flavor.
We also had a side of chips and guacamole. The chips were hot and salty and the guac was fresh and chunky.

Mirna stopped by our table a few times to make sure everything was good.
It was and we can't wait to bring our posse and sample more of their fine fare.

Maybe 4.5 stars but my sandwich was fantastic. My thunderbird was basically a perfect mix of turkey and various porky bits on some fantastic bread. I'm also a big fan of provel and wish it was on more stuff. Wash it all down with a 90 shilling and you've got a great meal. It's a fine portion but it was so good I almost got another sandwich, which since I'm in a road trip and have no fridge, would have been a mistake.

Sometimes my stomach wants to feel the freedom of a Rock 'n Roll saxophone, so here I am on the Yelp again, here I go, another review, another page:

On a long and lonesome Friday
East of Illinois
You can listen to my stomach
Moanin' out his one note song
You can think about the succotash
Or the creole chicken at Yats
But your thoughts will soon be wandering
Oh, my God I have to pay with cash
When you're ridin' sixteen hours
And there's nothin' much to do
And you don't feel much like ridin',
You just wish the trip was through

Here I am
at Yats again
There I am
Creole up in my face
Here I go
Eatin cajun again
There I go
off to Yelp this place

We were very pleased with the initial call and our new heater installation.  The technicians were knowledgeable, prompt and professional.  They also cleaned the work area after finishing installation.  I highly recommend this company and would not hesitate to use their services again.

What can I say.... I paid 10$ to park then waited over 20 minutes for a server. Finally after flagging down two waitresses I got the managers attention and was informed it was shift change and a waitress would be over shortly. Needless to say I left. I can't imagine the service would get any better as the meal went on. The manager refused to refund my parking and offered nothing other than a pitiful explanation that it was shift change.
Excellent food. Very authentic taste. By far the best Mexican food I've ever had. Not the greatest "curb appeal" but worth the effort to find.

Where is the best CrossFit Gym in the Indianapolis Area? Right here at CrossFit Zionsville! It is the most diverse, friendly, motivating, and family oriented CrissFit Gym in Indy! You will see results if you are consistent! Highly recommend this CrossFit Gym, two thumbs up!

Benny is outstanding, kind and thorough in his approach. Massage was outstanding, so grateful to have found him.  A side note for anyone concerned about his being deaf- it made no difference - and communicating with him is super easy!  He is quite tuned in  and checks in often to ensure that all is well. Forget Soothing Palms he should be called Holy Hands Benny!

Mike's is the best remedy for scorching hot summer days in Nashville. I spent only two days in good ol' Nashville, my favorite city in the US... and there's not much you can do in downtown if you're not 21. Thank God for this place! The big ice cream cones attracted my inner child and was probably the only reason I decided to go inside. 

The decor is very charming! 50's, old fashioned ice cream parlor and old fashioned soda fountains!! :) I munched away on my savory strawberry ice cream and my boyfriend enjoyed his strawberry soda float.

If you're in downtown Nashville, definitely stop by Mike's for a quick ice cream fix!

Buff makes me wish I lived in New Orleans (among other reasons). I went to school here and discovered Buff on my last trip back. As you know, finding a good mani/pedi place in a another city is always a challenge. A friend recommended Buff and Kim. I went with some college friends and it is super cute and has a great decor and atmosphere. They started by offering wine or champagne (love that). We got settled in and they did an great job and we had so much fun. I will defiantly  be back on my next trip especially since they are starting to offer blow outs. If you are in NOLA go to Buff!

Hubby did the fast food deal for lunch and got us something at Culver's. He said the drive thru was ridiculously backed up so he chose to park and go inside. He couldn't believe how large the menu was. I had the butterburger with American cheese and French fries. The fries are crinkle cut and had a great taste , they were salted perfectly and were not greasy at all. Best fast food fries I have had in a long time. The burger on the other hand was just okay. Bun was fresh and had good taste but the beef patty was really thin and slightly overcooked. I didn't think it had that much flavor and just wasn't that special. 

My husband ordered the fried fish plate with French fries and coleslaw. I tried the fish and have to say it was actually really good. The fish was cooked perfectly and not greasy at all. The coleslaw had a little to much mayonnaise but all in all was pretty good. 

I would definitely eat there again and they deserve 4 stars for sure. Oh.. And I forgot to mention but I hate Pepsi and they should really switch to Coke!

After reviewing the many comments of this place, I decided to check it out for myself. Here is a recap:

Service: Nice,average. Breakfast in morning consists of a lot of carbs - bagels, danishes, etc. Don't expect anything really healthy. Although, management might want to rethink investing a few extra bucks for a better selection to be aligned with their updated look and service. The free wine/cheese and bfast options didnt seem to have much of a crowd.. either perhaps... not many visitors or highly likely cause the food didn't seem too pleasing to the eye.

Room: Queen room.  Nice and clean. Showers are a bit outdated. Otherwise, nice cozy room. However, bring some candles and air freshener to really add that extra something needed in the room.

Parking was close to room and ample on street or in car port. 

If you like the clean line look, this is a great place to stay. However, would recommend mgmt to include some desert succulants or plants in the room. No flowers were in room as pictured. 

Ambiance: Quiet, great walkway for pictures. 

Recommendation - Great place if you dont want to break the bank but want a decent place to stay. Call and ask for any last minute deals and get up to an extra 15% off. We did and got a discount and bring some candles.

Reading some of the complaints about this place while I was on the train heading to Tucson, got my kind of nervous. I had never been to Tucson and had already made a reservation at the Roadrunner, but was having second thoughts after reading about strange people roaming the premises, meth heads, and a rude staff.

1st, to the complaints about having to stay in an apartment blocks away from the hostel; this happened to us as well, but I fail to see what the problem was. We ended up getting an apartment (less than a block from the hostel) with a full kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, fenced in backyard, and front courtyard. I don't have any problem with that. So what if a lot of people living there were long term residents- aren't most people long term residents of somewhere?

2nd, I did see some crazy looking people lining up in front of the Plasma center early in the morning, but what city of 250,000+ doesn't have sketchy inhabitants? Overall, I felt just as safe as I have in most places I've been around the country.

Finally, the staff. One of the main complaints I read is that they were rude; I met three different staff members and they were all nothing but kind. One was a bit annoying about checking out - knocking on our door at 10:30 (this is why they only got 4 stars) - but was at least kind about it.

The only weird thing that happened was them knocking on our door in the middle of the afternoon and telling us that they needed to take the bunkbed. We weren't using it, but it made me wonder what they would have done had we not answered. Would they have let themselves in?

There is no doubt in my mind that I would (and will) stay there again.

The coffee alone makes Summit worth a visit!!! But once you get inside, you won't walk out with just coffee!  The strawberry shortcake might be my favorite but the sticky buns run a close second.  Added bonus?  I get to pick up speciality treats for my furry family members too!

If this place was closer to our house we'd go all the time but as it is we get there for special days and when we have visitors come into town.  One time we had a reservation but otherwise we generally don't.

I love the flavor of their rack of lamb but I usually get something else that's easier to eat.  My meal has never been bad.  My wife always gets the stuffed filet and then won't stop talking about it til the next day.  One of my favorite things is they allow wine corkage for $10 so you can bring a really good bottle from your cellar without going away with a huge bill.

Have yet to have any problems with service.  I see a few reviews recently on the downside so maybe eventually we'll have a problem because a restaurant is sometimes only as good as their most recent hire, but so far so good.

I don't usually write about non food related places but this places needs mentioning. The location is pretty nice near Penn's Landing. But unless you're getting a great price, forget it. The place is old, no internet and they WILL tack on unsuspecting charges to your final bill....avoid or at least throttle the manager to get your money back.

What a cool place!  It's a "nano" brewery or something like that ... small batches of locally brewed beer, with a menu that changes at least weekly.  Belly up to their bar and you can taste as many beers as you wish for free.  My husband and I have very different tastes in beers, and I love being able to choose our favorite styles.  Another great local business to support.

We were first timers (five of us).. finding Pinocchio's on Google due to their Beer Garden. Spent the day in Philly (from Baltimore) and decided to stop here for dinner on the way home. Great choice! Buffalo chicken pizza and pepperoni pizza were big hits with us and the kids, warm and tasty breadsticks served prior to the meal. Our waitress, Sue, was awesome - very attentive and extremely friendly! LOTS of beer on tap! I went with the Oskar Blues Momma's Little Yella Pils and glad I did. Sue also brought me a sample of Van Diest Früli Strawberry Beer which was very yummy! But much more a dessert beer. Very fruity. They don't make their own desserts, but they were good nonetheless - Hershey's chocolate pie, lemon meringue pie and milkshakes. After our great meal, we wandered next door to the beer garden to create our own 6-packs to take back home. Staff is extremely knowledgeable and will recommend new beers based on your current likes. I walked away with some English and Irish brews and ciders, all very reasonably priced. This establishment is a small neighborhood place, off the beaten path of the highway, but well worth the trip!

Use to be a great alternative for the top steak spots... it has since taken on new ownership and since then as taken a huge drop in quality and taste. To sum it up, this place is horrible when it comes to a real cheese steak. If your looking for authentic this is not it

I visit New Orleans often coming from New York and I can proudly say that their pizza is legit!!! You can't get any better with the prices and deals they offer. Extra kudos to the fully stocked bar and wonderful service in both the bar and restaurant.

PBs is my spot! Breakfast Lunch Dinner snack DRINKSSSS! Waitstaff are all so nice and the bartenders are a few of the best you'll find out there. Shout out to Ryan Janine Dom & Sam !! 

* not to mention the cook is amazing too & the owner is super sweet & personable. 

Love the outside patio in the summer! If you haven't been you're missing out!

In the 11 years living in this area, today marked the first time going to this place and I feel like I've arrived late to the party! This pizza has the least amount of grease (they use real cheese!) and a crust you can nearly compare to pizza from NYC. We called in the order with a 25 minute estimate. The pizzas were ready and hot. We look forward to trying their other menu items!

This place is so neat! It can get a little tight-squeezed, so avoid ANY weekend visits if you aren't comfortable with crowds. They are almost always busy when they are open, but trust me - its worth every minute you have to wait for the deli or food counter. The coffee bar and patio give you both a fun Italian-market shopping experience as well as a great place for a fresh hearty or rustic meal. My fav is the spicy italian sausage they make in house. The butcher has decent prices too.  Oh gosh - the cheese room is absolutely amazing too. Don't miss the olive bar or bakery either!

I love this place. The guys behind the counter are not only supper friendly but pros at there craft. If you are not set on the typical Reno sushi all you need to do is just ask. They have the ability to amaze. There is an all you can eat menu that is comprehensive.
Best juice-smoothie-fresh vegan food in Nashville. Period. We are lucky to have something like this in our city.  Truly amazing and Chad and his crew are delightful.
Always have fun here with my son!  Clean facility and friendly staff.  The pizza is good.  It would be great for a bday party or a fun night or day out.

Discovered this little establishment on Yelp looking for somewhere interesting to grab a bite before seeing a show at The Cannery. I wanted to try something new since we don't get down that way just to eat much these days.

This place is perfect location wise if you are seeing a show at Cannery/Mercy Lounge as it's across the side street from the main parking lot. The restaurant has reserved parking, so parking to eat at the restaurant was not a problem. We then just walked to the show afterwards.

My husband and I ordered the Sorullos de Maiz (sweet corn fritters) for an appetizer. They were good, but I was really expecting more. The corn was really finely pureed and was more pasty. I would have liked more chunky corn, but that's my preference. The batter was crispy, but not as cornmeal-like as I was expecting. But then again I don't eat too much Puero Rican food so I didn't know what to expect! They were served with a savory sauce.

For dinner I had the Pastelon de Amarillos y Vegetales (spinach lasagna made with plantains). I've eaten plantains at Cuban restaurants, so I was expecting this lasagna to have a bit of sweetness to it. It was delicious. Two plantains on top and bottom with plenty of creamed spinach to fill the middle, topped with a top on hot melted cheese. It was very delicious. For my side, I got the mofongo (mashed plantains with garlic). It was a bit dry. It could have used more garlic sauce, which I guess was the tiny bit of sauce drizzled on the plate next to it (there was no sauce on the dish or given to me on the side).

My husband had the Arroz con pollo (yellow rice with chicken). It was good, but I noticed he was always pulling small chicken bones out of his mouth. That would have made my experience with this dish annoying, but overall he enjoyed the dish.

I would say that this place is worth a try to get some good authenic Puero Rican food.
I'm shocked at the good reviews here. Service was good the staff is very nice. I can eat dried out chicken at home. Very bland. Overpriced. Not enough parking. Won't be back.

This is my favorite bar in Nashville, hands down (and I've been to nearly every bar there is, from dive bars and honky tonks all the way to Patterson House). From drinks to vibe, they own it. 

Let me list what I love most: 

1. I've only been on the nights Marathon is not having show, and on those nights, the place is quiet and intimate. Some might say too quiet at times, but if you bring your own group or if you're on a date, it's the perfect space. 

2. The bartenders are amazingly talented! Mark, the manager makes the best drinks in town, hands down, and Zak is new and eager to share his love of the art of mixology! Both love trying out new drinks on friendly and open customers (I love being a bartender's guinea pig). 

3. I love the decor; it's really chic and open and beautiful! 

4. Once we started to become regulars, the staff was beyond amazing. I hosted my boyfriend's surprise party there and they changed the menu so that all his favorite drinks included his name! 

Come check it out and make it your regular place. If you like great cocktails, friendly and creative bartenders, and a lovely space, you will absolutely love it.

Very nice romantic chill setting.  Beautiful decor.  Spacious seating.  They offer chairs with backs if you don't want to sit on the ottoman.  I came here back in November so I can't remember the name of the drink that I loved so much.  I think it was bourbon with cinnamon and ginger.  What ever it was it was strong as hell, my type of drink!  Had to have another.  

I had the Maryland Crab Cakes and the Crawfish Mac and Cheese.  Damn, damn, damn, finger linking good. My friend had the Grilled Shrimp, Brussel Sprouts (infused with bacon) and Corn bread in a skillet.  My bff had the chicken in a bag.  The only one complaint I remember is the Brussel Sprouts.  My friends don't eat pork.  Not sure if it said on the menu or not that it was infused in bacon but thankfully no one got sick.

Will come back the next time I'm in town.
Love the ambiance here. Wait staff is always courteous and attentive. Saganaki cheese is a must. Gyros never disappoint (pita bread is amazing) and the any platter you order is huge in portion size.
Amazing place. Food is simply delicious here. High quality ingredients in all of their dishes. This place is most certainly a diamond in the rough.

YUM! My introduction to fry bread was many many moons ago, at a Rendez-vous (which is basically a reenactment of trade gatherings between settlers and natives), where fry bread was cooked in oil over a campfire - and they were amazing.

This beat even the memory. I had an Indian taco with a bit of green chili added and it was seriously amazing. Their beans are so good. Their homemade salsa/hot sauce adds a nice, tart kick, and the fry bread? Yup. Manna from heaven is a good description. I will definitely be back, and next time will have to save room for a sweet fry bread.

This place was terrible!

I usually don't eat sushi at all, the only reason I went here is because the girl I was with thought it would be a good idea to go. Ugh just thinking about this place makes me shake my freaking head in disappointment.

The waiter we had wasn't very friendly. I felt like we were tolerated the whole time there.

The food wasn't that great either. The soup was okay and so were the noodles. the sushi on the other hand was awful. It wasn't very fresh, tasted really old to me. Old girl had no complaints at first, A couple of days later she told me that she got sick off of her food. I didn't have that problem but I guess I was lucky. But still I feel that eating here is almost like playing a game of Russian roulette.

In short your better off eating what comes out of a dogs hind end than what they serve in this place!!!!

The price point is extreme compared to retail chains. They offer sales through their email program but make sure you confirm details of the sale prior to being rung through.

One of the sales associates (Diane?) Is fantastic at helping you find the right fit, style and price point.

Came here the first time over the weekend, upon walking in the place was very clean and pleasant looking. The staff was very friendly including the owner who was working when I was there. I ordered 2 Gyros and they were fantastic. Plenty big and super fresh ingredients and I really liked their tzatziki sauce. They also have daily $5 specials, I will definitely be moving them into my rotation.
Web site was easy to use to place our order.  We are from out of town and found them on Yelp.  Our order was delivered in half the time what they indicated.  And, the pizza tasted great!

Donuts, Sliders, and Brews!!!

I don't drink much anymore, but 2 out of 3 is just fine with me.  During our stay in NOLA, the gf found this place through, what else, Yelp.  Located in the Garden District, District Donuts Sliders Brew is a combination a of cafe, bar, donut stop, and a restaurant that specializes in sliders.  Yum, Yum, and Yum!

So, here we go...

-Chicken Sliders:  This was one of my orders.  Review the pictures and you can tell right away that this is one tasty slider.  I'm old school, so my preference in a slider is red meat.  However, their chicken slider does not disappoint.  Tender, tasty, and the bun was perfect. Good choice if you looking for some pollo in your diet. (http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=k29T0YDWDnUAnAzmUaPLWA&userid=y3FcL4bLy0eLlkb0SDPnBQ)

-Cheeseburger Sliders:  I got two of these and expected more, especially since their chicken sliders were so good.  Don't get me wrong, the sliders weren't bad at all, but I do prefer a less greasy one.  Got two and still killed it. Remember...my mom didn't raise a quitter. (http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=ydoUJVwV4V9djKGUca1FpQ&userid=y3FcL4bLy0eLlkb0SDPnBQ)

-Waffle Fries:  For someone that doesn't enjoy french fries, I did enjoy these.  I prefer steak fries if I'm going to have a potato sliced and fried. Their waffle fries are pretty close.  Golden, not burned.  Fried, not too salty.  Just right!!(http://www.yelp.com/user_local_photos?select=xUPlvqixgLDiSDYGyBo_jg&userid=y3FcL4bLy0eLlkb0SDPnBQ)

Other items on their menu include a BLT, which pimps a huge piece of bacon.  And let's not forget about their donuts.  I didn't try any but they looked delicious,  especially their Peanut Butter Cup.

Ambiance and Service:
Place is small, but not tiny.  There's still plenty of room and with their tall ceilings, you don't feel too cramped.  There's also dining outside or you can choose to eat at their bar.  The line starts at the door and yes, there's a line.  Service was pretty good and the food is ready pretty quick.

YELP PERSONAL CHALLENGE - (032/366)

Theresa did amazing work on my wedding dress. I purchased an old sample at a wedding boutique and it was at least two sizes too big. The entire dress was beaded so the smallest alteration was going to be an ordeal. Teresa was able to expertly hem and take in the dress, making it couture. She added lingerie straps and even washed an area that had been soiled. With all of my family out of state, it was a wonderful experience to prepare my dress with such a warm and nurturing lady as Teresa.  

Teresa only accepts cash. So bring it with you or you visit the ATM in La Fortuna, the grocery store on the corner. Also be sure to bring your receipt with you and have Teresa annotate it with each payment. I had failed to bring my receipt and my final payment was not marked on Teresa's copy. This was a regretful and uncomfortable experience after such a positive interaction at Special Occasions. Just bring your receipt and make sure it's always up to date and you'll have a very pleasant experience working with Teresa.

A 4th generation Nelson has picked up the ball and is working hard to keep the factory outlet ice cream store open. Although he has some big shoes to fill, I'm sure he's up to the job. The ice cream is fresh and cold as ever.

This is our first time here and we were blown away by the experience. Our waiter, Andrew, was extremely professional, knowledgeable, and pleasant. He sat us down and prompted asked us for drink orders, as well as, explaining the menu and listing the popular dishes. 

An extra star that I gave this place is purely because of how clean the establishment and service is. Andrew took our complicated order without writing it down. When I checked into YELP I received a coupon for a free fresh lemonade worth ($3). 

I ordered 1lb of fresh crawfish ($9/lb) and 1lb of frozen crawfish ($14/lb) with mild boiling house sauce. I added two extra corn and potatoes. The sauce was delicious and there was a generous helping. I wanted to try out the difference between the frozen and fresh crawfish, and discovered there was a big difference in size. Next time, I'll get 2lbs of the fresh. 

My partner ordered the snow crab cluster with the same sauce. I do want to comment that we ordered it with sausages and that the kitchen forgot ir. Our waiter ended up removing the sausages from the bill, since we finished eating our entrees by the time they came out.
Worst hotel I ever lived. Had to take this because there wasn't anything else nearby, and we were unfamiliar of this city, and it was 9:00 at night to search another after 8 hours of driving :-(

The best thing this place has going for it are the beautiful people who eat there.  There is a very LA vibe.  The space inside is kind of cramped and hard to move through.  The patio is great.  The food is fine; unremarkable.  They once gave me an appetizer for free because it was the last one and didn't look as pretty as the rest.

I guess I'm in the minority here, but I didn't love Bandit coffee.  A coffee shop needs a few things to me - it needs good coffee, but it should also be comfortable with good work stations, wifi (obviously) so that if this is where you're going to sit and work or chill for a while, you don't feel like your tailbone is going through your neck.

Bandit has good coffee and if you're in a pinch and want a cup to go, then coming here is a great option.
