But if you're looking for a place to work, or read a book or newspaper (yes, some people still read those), then I don't think this is the place for you.  It is very modern and open, but their seating arrangements are bars or tables with these metal stools to sit on.  Basically the opposite of comfort.

I like the floor to ceiling windows, so you get a lot of natural light, and maybe this is the kind of layout millennials are looking for.  Maybe young adults in their 20s like this sterile environment and don't mind a** breaking chairs.  Perhaps they like metal stools because it's really frustrating when a bar fight breaks out and you hit someone with a wooden stool, and it shatters, leaving you without a weapon for the next drunk idiot.  But this is a coffee shop, not an english pub.  

I like my coffee shops being more homely - some comfortable couches and chairs around, and absent that, seating arrangements that make me able to sit and work or read for longer than 30 minutes.
High drama bar. I have never been to a bar where I felt so uncomfortable... Staff fighting, rude to customers and not to mention an extremely long wait for "the best wings in town". No thanks.
I have been going to the neptune location for almost 2 years now. Katrina is great! She really makes you feel relaxed and gets the job done quick.
I always came here growing up for hair cuts.  It's not too pricey and they do a great job.  I recently went back and as usual the haircut was great.  Just what I wanted.

This is my second experience with a chain cell phone repair facility, and these guys are top notch. Chris is absolutely fantastic! I though the battery needed to be replaced on my Galaxy S6, unfortunately it was not. Chris worked with me on several options, and kept me informed throughout. I was given very reasonable prices and extraordinary quality. These are goto guys for any of my cell phone needs. Thank you!

If you are on a diet, this place is certainly your doom.

The pastries are just amazing, this is honestly the first scone I've ever eaten that I actually enjoyed, and do not get me started on the eclairs.

The food is actually very good as well, the potatos are amazing, as well as the toast they give as part of most breakfast sets.

They also have high chairs for the little ones and great coffee.
Our waiter was wonderful!  Awesome service, and the Bubba's Eggs Benedict were outstanding. Great experience for our out of town visit

Great eating experience. Can't wait to bring my bffs for brunch. Food was good and server pleasant. Dishes were attractively presented. LOVE this place. Best kept secret, got to get the word out. Will be my favorite brunch place. Family enjoyed the ambience, too.

First time and really enjoyed it!  Our server was Shelby was super friendly. Owner got involved in the meal preparation for my wife when he heard of her allergies. Very nice bourbon selection as well. The steak was excellent too.

Stopped in after walking from the Rocky steps to the Mutter for lunch. Friendly if slightly boisterous local crowd watching the hockey game. Pretty reasonable draft beers and the menu was great for the comfort food & bar food lovers. We had crab dip, the liberty burger, caesar salad, and the club sandwich. It was a TON of food and we took leftovers back to the hotel. Bartender, who was also serving, was super friendly and accomodating to our requests despite being a bit overwhelmed. Only downside was the homemade chips for the dip were stale. Otherwise would gladly return!

The food is good. Wouldn't bother with the Menudo though. It taste like tripe with tomato sauce...weird taste. The staff is friendly but is not really SERVICE oriented. They don't always come around to refill you cup and you can wait a while before someone brings you menus or take your orders. Good thing we like their food because the service can use some tweaking.

The worst tour I have ever taken. Our guide,Noah, spent an hour after picked me up, driving to other hotels to pick up passengers. Apparently the other can broke, so he had to pick up two sets( the last couple he picked up had been waiting for two hours.they for off when they realized they could not sit together. 
I gave up part of a conference to go on the tour out of my interest for the Bras Pitt houses and rebuilding after Katrina. As we drove into the 9th wars, the driver announced that it was too late in the day to go out to see the houses. Instead, he drove back to town to drop off someone and then took us to the Garden District. We then drove around for over an hour....looking at one antebellum mansion after another.
I was so disappointed.My plane left early the next day- I will never get to see them.
When I got back to,the hotel the concierge told me this was the third complaint she had had recently. She never recommends this company:I know why!

I know nothing about bikes but I knew I needed one. I told them my budget and they had several different models for me. They had such patience with me because I knew I wanted something just right. It's an investment, ya know? Finally, I ended up with my perfect baby: a Specialized Crossroads in a deep purple. I haven't had any repair done on it just yet but I'm sure their repair department is just as good as their sales!

I expected something totally different in terms of atmosphere and display. The music was some poppy radio station and it did not have the elegance of Maple street but the cherry cobbler i purchased was delicious. 
I was irritated, nevertheless by no signage for the pastries. No prices. No idea what anything was.

I was here over super bowl weekend and loved this place!

you must try the shrimp quesadillas, hands down one of the best things ive ever eaten!!!!!

Downstairs there is a really cool bar with great music, so if you are tryin to dance after dinner, i suggest you head on down.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND!!!
Absolutely excellent wings (the mustard are my favorite), cheap beer on game days, and Maker's Mark behind the bar. One of the female bartenders cusses like a sailor, and I love it.

This is the worst Wendy's I have ever been to. Charged me for a large cup and gave me a medium because they were out of large. Wanted a medium cup of ice but got a small even though I paid for a medium. Total ripoff. Avoid this Wendy's.

I've had a great experience with United. All of the technicians were very friendly and knowledgeable. They always called prior to coming to my house to make sure it was a good time for me. I worked primarily with Brandon and Will...both really nice guys. They did their best to be unobtrusive and set the equipment up quickly. I would recommend United to friends.

Sushi and service was excellent! Couldn't ask for better sushi in the area and the prices were reasonable.  New and lean interior and the tables were all full upon arrival.  Will definitely go back again!

Come here every month for last 13 months straight for WWE Shows. Tonight was the worst service, horrible. Our waitress took 30 mins to ask us if we want anything, never got a menu had to ask a fellow customer for one. Took 50 mins (i kept track) for a bowl of chips. Another 40 mins on a chip refill. 
No excuse for that. My chicken was super burnt, to go along with my cold fries. Refills were no existant. I couldnt find my waitress for an hour and a half till at end of show she dropped off bill. This comes off the heels of a bad service last time, i figured it was just an off night but no, im done with this place.

I'm always a fan of BYOBs. We brought out out of town vendors here and everyone was pleasantly surprised.

Appetizers: Dips, Goat cheese and warm hummus
Dinner: Chicken and kebabs

Everyone was satisfied! I will definitely return!

I only really write reviews on here when I believe they're warranted.  I read a lot of the other reviews which seems mostly negative, but I bought a living social deal for here for micoderm abrasion and a super peel, now I understand that most of the negative reviews were regarding Botox, which I can not speak on but my experience was wonderful.  The staff was very friendly and knowledgeable (namely Hallie who preformed my procedure).  Everything was very organize and ran seamlessly.  I'm not sure who made the uneducated comment of front desk staff doing her procedure, but I can't imagine this ever being the case here.  Perhaps a doctor did not administer the procedure but a licensed esthetician did (which mind you is very common).   I will absolutely be back, my results were amazing as was my overall experience.  I will also be recommending this practice to others.

For the same price as everyone else ($45 plus 20% tip for a shave, bath, and nail cut $ grind for my 30-lb. terrier), Kevin, the owner, and his crew did a bang-up job on Maggie. She came out an hour earlier than expected sans nicks or emotional damage. It doesn't seem like any of her extraordinarily long talon quicks were cut, which all groomers - especially inexperienced people who work at places like PetSmart - tend to do, making Maggie nervous about future trips. She doesn't smell like a funeral parlor full of cheap flowers, and she's not itchy from cheap shampoo. The doggie hairdresser listened to my requests: chop the cute but snaggled beard but leave the undeniably cute eyebrows, which, while funny looking, is just what we need for our hiking lifestyle. I gotta say, I like to take her to my loyal Karabu or And Toto Too, but they were booked, and I'm glad we branched out.

I can't even describe how much we loved this place. The four of us shared one medium and one large pizza, one was the Islander and one was a custom pizza. We were able to sit outside, plenty of seating, and I liked that there was no wait service, it allowed us to pick our seat and relax. The pizza was thin crusted, but SO delicious. I loved the pesto sauce, not too much pesto but just right. We will definitely be back!

I love the location in the Factory. Acai bowls are delicious. The only bummer was my last visit a young woman with long brown hair was visibly rude to me and everyone behind me. It felt like she didn't like the amount of the tip I gave her but wow what a way to ruin a healthy delicious meal..
Its a great place to shop for produce but a lot of is not actually from local growers see the link to news article http://www.independent.com/news/2013/jan/31/farmers-market-harvests-discontent/
I've been there a couple times now. Pasta is very good, great servings and their pizzas are excellent. The guy at the counter, Dusty or Dustin, is very friendly.

I have never been there before until today. It was nice the sandwiches were awesome I had a meatball sub and very hardy and very filling. I got the 7 inch sub which was more than of her most people. The cookies were really good at being a butter is better than the chocolate chip in my opinion. The staff was very friendly and the Decour was awesome. I will be back next timeI am in St. Louis

At Schnucks looking at the damage done to my front bumper from one of their stupid shopping carts. This Schnucks just like all Schnucks are trashy grocery stores I'm never coming back - Dierberg's all the way.

Have been many times for lunch, and I'm always happy.  The latest visit, however, was for a banquet at the end of a conference (on Koreans in China), and the crowd I was with had an absolutely fabulous time.  The staff covered the lazy Susan on our table for 12 with dishes; we ate until stuffed--and then the waiter took off what was left (and packed it up for take-home) and announced that we had finished the APPETIZERS and they would shortly bring the main dishes!  So they covered the lazy Susan again, and we ate until stuffed again, and we all divided up leftovers to take home.  It was a stupendous evening.  Everything was delicious, but particularly memorable dishes included lobster stuffed with crab, tripe, lamb with black bean sauce, pork belly hot pot, dan dan noodles, cold noodles and more.

Got a sun-dried tomato bagel that was very flavorful! They really pile on the cream cheese, so if that's not your thing, ask for light cream cheese or ask for it on the side. 

Took an apple strudel home and had it for dinner dessert. It was absolutely amazing. 

The donuts looked really good and there was a wide variety available.

The staff was efficient and pleasant but not overly helpful. It was a busy morning and they were getting people through the line pretty quickly though. If you aren't sure what you want, stand back until you do. Take a chance and order something different. 

This place might not be the NY bagel
shop that everyone seems to want it to be, but it's seriously good. 

Oh, while you're there, get a coffee. I got a caramel mocha or latte (can't remember which), it was sooooo good.

I tried a couple of cocktails at this comfortable, estate sale furnished bar.  It was the third stop in our exploration of cocktail bars of Philly that night.  I appreciate that their cocktail menu (if you are looking for something abnormal) is sectioned off type of liquor, making it easy to try new things that you'll still enjoy.  Plenty of old school favorite drinks, as well and interesting creations that I had not seen before.

Pumpkin flip is a beer based cocktail, but you'd never guess it.  It tastes a bit like thin spiked egg nog.  It is a creamy drink, strong, and very tasty.  Though, I don't think I could drink many of these.

My barometer for this sort of cocktail bar has been the old fashioned.  Their's is definitely among the elite.  The server reported the drink was made with Buffalo Trace bourbon (which is the same used at Franklin Mortgage and Ranstead Room).  I'd rank Tippling's on par with Franklin Mortgage.

Il Posto is such a great neighborhood cafe - the food is top-notch and fresh, and the atmosphere is effortlessly bright and welcoming. The "hidden" back yard also is a perfect place to enjoy a couple of bottles of wine (yes, a couple because you won't want to leave once you get there). They do a great job catering to each time of day, so you can stop in in the morning for coffee and bagels/yogurt or swing by in the evening for a full meal. It's always hard to choose what to order, but my favorites are the bruschetta, grilled cheeses: the punch or the adventure, prosciutto panini, Italian tuna salad, shaved brussel sprout salad and any soup of the day. Such a gem for that neighborhood and well-worth a drive!

Checked out this place after seeing a post on uwishunu.com

Went with the 500 burger (lettuce, tomato, cheddar, bacon & special house sauce), truffle fries and a vanilla milkshake. I was starving by the time I'd gotten out of that line, almost a hour wait due to promos they were running with it being grand opening day and all, so I tasted a few of the fries as I walked back to the office, soooooo good! Wish I knew what the plain tasted like to compare not sure if I'm just in love with the truffle oil or if the fries as a whole are just that good either way the prices remain the same rather plain spicy or truffle. 

Then get back to my office and took a bite of the 500, it has bacon, real bacon on it!! Crispy salty in the right places chewy in the right places bacon. I don't know why but I have a hard time buying a good burger sandwich etc that has bacon on it and actually liking it so I was pleased. My burger was well done, and well seasoned, all around good burger. They did give me the wrong cheese however that may have been due to some order confusion so I let that slide and was still good. 

Lastly and my only real complaint is the milkshake. Very Very good no complaints there, the girl who made it however only filled my cup halfway and when I showed it to her, asking why it wasn't filled up she said because they don't have their correct cups yet so that is the actual serving. It looked like a serving for a kids meal so didn't sit right with me. Wasn't satisfied with that but walked away because I was hungry and needed to eat my food but saw that the guy in front of me was eating in and also ordered a milkshake so I asked to see his and there was a very small bit of space left at the very top, went back to let milkshake girl know this and asked the young lady next to me, also with a milkshake to be my witness LOL. She took my cup and put more in and don't think she was too happy about it but I got my reasonably portioned milkshake and it was goooood. And trust me I'm not that knit picky but  for money at that portion wasn't flying with me. Oh also with the milkshake it was more soupy than thick. I didn't mind that about it those that like shakes you need a spoon to actually eat not drink may not feel the same. 

They still get 5 stars from me for now because in the hustle of taking care of so many people, she may not have gotten a good look at my portion and she made up for it. AND they've filled a major burger void I'd been having so they're my new best friends right about now.

Pancake house by day, steakhouse by night!  If you have read any of the other reviews (particularly for Gaucho Steakhouse), then you will see there have been a number of bewildered guests that have dined here.  The family that owns this brunch restaurant closes the place at 3, cleans up, and then reopens as Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse at 5 pm.  Both restaurants use the same entrance and space, but the signs over the entrance make it look like the pancake house is on the left and the steakhouse is on the right.  Just go to the left, regardless of when you dine here.

Okay, so the space inside is not designed for clearing things up.  There are large murals on the walls celebrating breakfast and area sports teams.  And there are posters about steak as well.  The space is broken up into two shotgun style dining areas.  The one on the entrance side has a number of tables and a bar area towards the back.  The space to the right is divided by a mirrored wall that is lined with booth seating for the tables that are located there.  Pull out chairs sit on the opposite sides of the bench seating.   

Anyway, I ordered my brunch selection and a bottomless cup of coffee and was generally pleased.  The "Original Benny" came with two poached eggs, a buttery Hollandaise sauce, English muffin halves, and Canadian bacon.  Pretty well executed and tasty.  On the same plate, some crisped hash browns came with the order to help mop up any of the sauce left over.  On a side plate, a colorful fresh fruit plate offered melon, red grapes, and orange slices.

The service was okay....efficient comes to mind.  Not a lot of interaction or welcoming attitude.  I could understand if it was a busy day, but the room seemed less than half full.

Overall, if you are hungry, the food is good and you just have to trust the staff to lead you to seating.  Don't over think it.

Review #503
This restaurant is fantastic Paul is an excellent owner highly recommend this restaurant

Boy, how things have changed in a year since my first very positive review from last July.  The movie theater next door was condemned and Bailey's has followed suit.  The food is of poor quality and overpriced.  I ordered a specialty salad and it took 45 minutes and was missing the avocado, egg, and cheese when it finally arrived; items which they don't carry anymore but haven't updated the menu or told the waitresses about.  The chocolate cake with ice cream arrived after 45 minutes with the ice cream fully melted.  All still charged full premium price for.  The restaurant also sponsors Superbowl parties for which we reserved a $100 table, drink, and appetizer package which was not worth the price; a St. Patrick's Day party, and Cinco De Mayo celebration as well as many others at which you are encoured to drink, drink, and drink the specials.  However when you try to be responsible and need to get a taxi/cab home the Management and workers have said on more than one occassion that "it's not their problem and taxis won't come out to their location".  That's totally irresponsible.  Used to be a good place but now I'm ASHAMED to invite any friends there or take my wife out for dinner and drinks.  I'll spend my $100 a week elsewere.  The nearby Logan's Roadhouse O'Charleys, and Outback Steakhouse are much better choices and values and you won't have Coal Miner's lung after one night of the poor ventilation.

I've only eaten here 3 times and every time it was so good I nearly exploded.  Very accommodating,  price is very reasonable for the actual amount of food.  Flavors are great.  I've never gotten a burrito anywhere that was as good.  It's a bit far for me to go frequently,  but they'll get my business when I've got the time.  On Mondays they have mole (one of my personal favorites), they had no problem making it into a burrito,  so yummy.

Our FAVORITE breakfast/brunch spot around our house. The food is always perfect. It's the freshest and very consistent. The atmosphere is awesome too. Very bright, simple, clean, modernish. The prices are great. We have never had a bad meal or a bad experience here and we have been at least a dozen times. And we look forward to going to refuel at least a dozen more times. Best best best! Refuel will always have a special place in my heart.

The room didn't have enough towels or soap and hair products. We never find the tv remote. I looked at my door and someone open it i guess when they came to leave the receipt and left it open. Breakfast room was something else. One person for a lot of guests equals disaster. Everything gone in seconds. Pancake machine made like 3 pancakes and ask for another bag. So I never had my pancakes. When we check in ask for late check out and they said yes but the person in the morning said we weren't allowed. Oh and we tried to used our rewards points and they would not let us either. The pool was not clean and the equipment to clean it was there all broken. Of course no doubt I won't stay there again.

I'm actually really surprised that I had this
experience with the place. I had high expectations for this place based off the other reviews but I can't say I would give this 5 stars.. the only reason I gave 2 is because there is no half. I would have given this place 1 1/2 if I could. The sushi came fast despite the "30 minute" wait time I was told on the phone. However the delivery driver kinda looked frazzled and when I handed him $40 he said he had to get the change from his car so I had to wait a couple minutes for that.. I also noticed that he gave me a bag of trash along with my food (I didn't realize this until I got to my kitchen). The empty peanut wrapper, wasabi, and sushi carton filled trash bag was obviously his or from someone else. I was immediately grossed out by this and only reluctantly tasted my sushi since it was packaged and untouched. Aside from this the sushi was okay. I ordered the Philly Roll and the California Roll which were fresh, but I ordered the Samuari Tempura Rolla which were soggy from all the sauce on top and really chewy. My brother ate the Shrimp Tempura rolls and said they were fine. Overall I probably will never order from here again.

I had an excellent experience, Chef Timney made a personal appearance to our table to make sure everyone was satisfied!  And we were!  The St Louis pizza (aka Talaynas) was out of this world!  And Chef Timney's special pasta of the day was superb!  I want to go back for lunch and see the lighrter options...I would definitely do it again. Friendly staff!

Awesome show in a small intimate setting! The jazz band was spectacular, musicians ranged in age.

Paid $45 for a front row seat on a bench. Well worth it to bypass the hour long line for a guaranteed seat. Otherwise, $15 for standing room only or if you're lucky, a seat on the back benches.

There was a line for the prepaid seats during the 9 and 10pm shows but not for the 5pm show. No bathroom, so know before you go. Great experience, glad we stumbled on this joint!

Dang, I went the whole summer without doing this!  Good thing I got the last one of the season. 

This sort of event is always a lot of fun, as it really shows off the small but growing food truck scene present in our city.  It's a great chance to showcase what they've got and get exposure.  It is especially nice to have gatherings like this since it seems we rarely see the trucks just around town during the week, and I love the opportunity to browse the selections and grab some various random things to munch on.

If you've experienced Food Truck Fridays, then you know the drill.  A bunch of trucks parked together, you choose the ones that strike your fancy, and spend the rest of your time hanging out and enjoying yourselves.  Feed the Camel, occurring on Hump Days throughout the summer, is a much smaller-scale affair hosted down by the river at the McKinley Arts Center.  The trucks are parked under and around the Keystone Bridge, and attendees can grab their food and drinks then find a table or nice grassy spot on the lawn.  It's a nice way to break up the week, and let some other trucks who may not be at the Friday festivities show their stuff, too.  There tend to be far fewer people at this event than Food Truck Fridays, so parking access is easier, the lines are shorter, and the entire atmosphere is way more laid back and chill.  Occasionally there will be music or other activities here, as well.  Such as tonight, with Archie from the baseball team entertaining the kids.

The selections run the gamut of variety.  From hot dogs to brisket sandwiches, vegan to hot wings, tacos to corn dogs.  Even with only about a dozen trucks and stalls present, you get a really good range to choose from.  I ended up with some Latin-Asian fusion rice balls from a new truck, a great chorizo hot dog from Bam Dogs, washed it down with slushy drink from the Mr. Margarita, and topped it off with a scoop of gelato from Bibos.  It was certainly an eclectic evening, and browsing through the menus at each place is half the fun.  Prices range from a few bucks and go upwards from there depending on what you get and how much of it.  Most all places take cards, but bringing cash just makes things way faster and easier all around.

If you haven't been this year, put it on your calendar for next summer.  Everyone should definitely come and check it out for themselves.  Food and fun, can't argue with that.

Very small menu. Im mexican and there is nothing mexican about this restaurant. Its not decorated at all, and no mexican music is playing. 2 tacos for $13+ are u kidding me? I ordered a duck salad because I like duck and I rarely see it on a menu. The duck tasted like chicken, it looked fried, a little tough vs soft like im used to. The salad was overpriced in my opinion at $16. I did like the salad but not for that price. After we sat at our table our server took forever to wait on us and the salad took forever to come out which was surprising because the restaurant looked empty. I would never come here again. Its disappointing because i live close by and would like nice places to eat near my home. Huge bust

I have to say, this is the 1st review I have ever made for help, and I feel compelled to do so to save diners from getting ripped off the way I did. My girlfriend and I stopped by here on a Sunday night and were seated right away. Outside looked nice and was interesting being under the highway/road above us. Our server greeted us and asked if this was our first time here. We said yes and from that point it seemed like the scam was on. My gf ordered a glass a wine and he suggested getting a bottle because they offer it half off on Sunday. Seems like a great deal. So I ordered a margherita pizza(tasted good/ not great)and she ordered chicken meatballs. It was a bit cold and the sauce was runny.(and overpriced). So we get the bill and see the bottle was charged for 29 dollars. I ask him about this and he said the bottle costs 59 dollars! I am certainly not a wine know it all so I decided to check the average price of it. THE BOTTLE OF WINE THAT IN RIVA CHARGED US AND OTHER DINERS 58$$$ WAS 10$!!!!
Overall the outside does look nice but the food was mediocre at best and this place is a bunch of scammers. Factor in the smug beer bellied waiter we had and it makes this one of the worst dining experiences I've ever had....IF YOU DINE HERE CHECK THE AVERAGE COST OF WINE AND TELL THEM THEY'RE CHARGING 6 X THE COST. Hopefully this review will deter anybody from getting screwed the way I was.

Larry knows his stuff! Called Larry about a slow drain to my tub and a leaking sink. He was on time, went the extra step to make sure the issues were fixed and had some good recommendations to lessen the problems from reoccurring. Pleasure to be around.
Food was really good. One should come here for crab and atmosphere. If you come for something different prob be disappointed.

Paddy Whacks is located on South Street in an area which they could have a good business of getting customers in. But apparently, it seems that is not the case. I have been to their Northeast Philadelphia location, so I decided to try out this other location in South Street. It is metered street parking everyday up to 10pm, so make sure that you feed that meter during that time. It is not handicap accessible. Bathrooms are located down the stairs in the basement. I have to tell you though as you walk down the steps, you can't help but notice the stench of urine in the air. They really need to do a thorough cleaning of their bathrooms and hallways. Our server greeted us and was friendly when we arrived. The bartender also acknowledged us as we were seated in a booth. Seating is limited. I noticed though that the open floor area around the bar is very spacious. I presume that they prefer to accommodate the standing room only for bar patrons rather than dining in customers? It is impossible to have a conversation going with your group because they have the tv volume blasting out very loud and tuned  to the Phillies game going on. The Cheeseburger sliders had no dressing whatsoever. The bun was dry, the patty was dry and lacked flavor. Caesar Salad was so-so, nothing special. The Shepherd's Pie was very oily. Oil coming from the ground meat? Apparently, the type of ground meat they used had the ratio of more fat than lean? The Kilkenny Chocolate Cake with Vanilla ice cream was the only dish that is delicious. I am disappointed at our visit to this establishment. Sorry to say that this is our first and last visit to Paddy Whacks in South Street.

My wife and I ate here yesterday (March 18) with an elderly friend who lives in the Tucson area. The friend loves this place for their chicken tortilla soup, and she was not disappointed. 

I had the Cobb salad, which was perfectly acceptable, and better than a much more expensive one I'd had the day before. In particular, the quality and quantity of the meat was impressive. 

This review is mostly to recognize the efforts of our server and (especially) one of the managers - bearded chap, John?? - who took great care of my wife, who has numerous food sensitivities. They answered her questions patiently, and at one point, John (as we shall call him) came out to discuss in detail the ingredients of the salad dressing. Collaboratively, a good solution was found - and my wife enjoyed her meal very much. 

I have one primary suggestion for improvement: turn the music down. At least for the Sunday lunch crowd, the music seemed far louder than most customers likely wanted. 

We will definitely return next time we're in Tucson.

Cool tapas bar, but I don't know.  0.50 literal bites are just weird to me.  I can't complain about it, it tasted well, but something about ordering 10 of anything just feels gluttonous, wrong, and shameful.  

I couldn't do it.  I paid my bill after four (SHAME), a glass of wine, and out the door.

SHAME.  

Go there for dinner.  You'll be able to order one item and be content.
This is a St Louis icon. I have been visiting Ted Drewes since 1982. Don't be discouraged by the long lines in front of the building.. they move super fast and it will be well worth the wait!

I stayed at this hotel this past weekend. I honestly will never stay here again. Checking in was a breeze and the associate at the desk was extremely nice. When I entered the room which mind you is suppose to be a club room but was located outside the elevators on the second floor.  It was very small for a club room. Ever 20mins you had the pleasure of hearing the staircase door slam for all the impatient people who didn't want
to wait for the elevator. I have stayed in many hotels and this was an extreme disappointment. Looking out the window of our room we had a horrible view of the lobby which the curtains didn't even block out the light from coming in the room. After I got home I decided to read the description of the room I paid for online. Now realizing after reading the online description of the room that I was not giving the correct room I was charge for. I book a club room which is suppose to be approx. 479sq ft. The room I stayed in was no where near this size. They basically charge me for a premium room and gave me a standard king room with benefits of the club room. That is not OK. The heater in the room sounded like a nuclear weapon when it turned on in the middle of the night. Can't tell you how many times it woke me up. There website indicates there is a valet charge of $36 per day for in and out service. They forget to tell you they charge tax on this service. Therefore it really cost you $44. Which doesn't include the tip you have to give the guys when you go in and out. This is not self parking. You will have to wait at least 20 to 30 mins to get your vehicle from valet. This whole valet idea is horrible. You just end up wasting your trip/time waiting on your vehicle instead of being on your way. They provide you the option to call ahead. So I try that option. Apparently they never got the information so we waiting 30 mins for our vehicle. What a nightmare. I will definitely be filing a complaint with the corporate office for additional assistance.

Great tacos! Not your average Mexican restaurant. The chips and salsa are different than the usual Mexican restaurant. But they have a variety of different tacos and they are all really good and taste fresh.

This used to be an excellent local flavor for college students and the like. Ever since the move next door, it has lost all of its character and has been transformed into one of the most pretentious places in Edgehill. Wait to be seated at a coffee shop? Are you kidding me?!

We stayed here over the New Years weekend and I must say and was quite impressed with this Inn and everything it had to offer. The price was reasonable during the New Years (holiday) weekend and the owners were very nice and helpful. I have never been to Santa Barbara and they gave us directions to the best places to eat and tour around. The Inn is not too far from the main street which I completely forgot the name. but it's about a quick 10 minute walk by the beach to the pier. From there you can take the trolley up and down around the area for a quarter! Another great thing is the continental breakfast!!! Any place that serves food is my favorite place. :)

Room wise I was surprised to see a nice, clean, welcome feeling room. We had the double bed room on the second floor and it was huge and spacious. The bathroom was nice and well kept. Not dirty or yucky like some "Inns." My friends who are OCD even liked the rooms! The only two things I would complain about is that they only allow one parking spot per room because of the limited space. I understand, but it sucks to have the other couple look for street parking. Luckily there were spots, you just need to read the signs! Also, the shower heads were a pain. For some reason, the knob to turn the shower head on wouldn't stay on! We literally had hold it up in order to get the shower head to work.

I highly recommend this place to anyone!

The food here is phenomenal. There are so many unique menu options and knowing that all the food is organic makes it even better. I had the "Duck Duck Gouda," which I instinctively ordered because it had the word "Gouda" in its name. I had never heard of duck bacon before, but Bareburger opened my eyes to it. It was delicious.

I deducted one star because we sat for a long time without water refills and it took one person in our party a long tIme to receive her change.

I went to Mother Hubbards on a weekday with my toddler daughter.  I was the only customer at the time I got seated.  Our waitress told us to sit anywhere we liked, so we did. We were both super hungry and looking forward to eating here as I had read a good review in the Tucson Weekly.  Boy was I disappointed.  I ordered the eggs benedict and a kid breakfast for my daughter (scrambled eggs, potatoes, toast. ) When my dish came, I was horrified.  Hollandaise sauce should be fluffy and uniform.  This was a runny, separated soup that engulfed not only both halves of the sandwich, but the entire plate, it was just a big plate drenched in melted butter.  The meat was flavorless and appeared to have been boiled.  The english muffin was dense and had an odd flavor.  I would have told the waitress, but she never did check on us.  Finally I went to the front and simply requested another plate, we were in a hurry and I wanted to get out of there, I did not have high hopes that ordering something else would make me any happier.  I took the extra plate, wiped off the eggs best i could and literally tried to wring out my muffins.  The coffee, rather expensive for plain brewed coffee ( 2.75 I think) was just average, and overpriced to my way of thinking.  The descriptions on the menu sound enticing but I do not have faith in the cook that day, perhaps another one does better, he just looked like a disinterested disheveled hippie type and prepared our food with zero panache.  I will not go back

The BEST Tom Yum on the planet! 
Absolutely my favorite place to eat! 
And so far my friends have all agreed! They even send me pictures of my favorite dish the Tom Yum soup, with coconut milk and medium spicy! They have the most delicious rice cakes with a special sauce, Yum Yum! Preeda and the rest of her wonder staff even know us by name! 

They have a full vegan menu and a full non-vegan menu. Giving you so much to chose from! Every time I visit I notice everyone in the restaurant has a smile on their face!

My good friend the other day tried their chicken basil and could not believe how delicious it was! Our compliments to the chef :-)

Every city I visit  I compare the Thai restaurants to Thai Legacy and So far nothing has come close. So when you visit Preeda let her know Greg sent you and that you'll have the Tom Yum just like he has it LOL

But seriously, nothing compares to Thai Legacy!

The pizza was undercooked bottom line. I ordered a medium with bacon and pepperoni and I'm sorry to report that the toppings were very scarce. Not cool.

At least the employees were friendly.

The place is nice inside. Lots of room to sit and free wi-fi. It's very trendy industrial decor. Overall, everything is pretty clean, not spotless, but not gross. 

They serve a select amount of breakfast foods  and sandwiches. The food tastes great! We had poached eggs and bacon. They make a PERFECT poached egg. I was very impressed by that. 

I had iced tea and it was decent, not excellent, but worth it. 

I did have trouble communicating with the cashier. She asked the order several times, misunderstood my name several times and gave me coffee instead of tea. Not my worst experience, she wasn't rude, she just seemed to not understand the words coming out of my mouth ;). 

Overall this place is great. A lot of people come here and they seem to be regulars. The menu includes breakfast items, sandwiches, bakery items, coffee, tea and some alcohol (I didn't fully check as it was 7am, but I know they have wine).

TERRIBLE SERVICE
I had out of town guests and took them to Bareburger. We were a party of 4. When we entered, we were behind a party of 2. The party of 2 was immediately seated at a 4-person booth, while there were multiple tables for 2 available. Host told us they were just clearing another booth (and pointed to it) and said we would be seated there shortly. In the meantime a party of 5 came in after us. It took 10 minutes to clear the table and then another hostess came up to the original host to ask who was waiting for a table. He told her our party of 4 and a party of 5. She proceeded to seat the party of 5 at the booth, adding a chair to the end of the table. There were no other tables, let alone booths, available for 4. When we told her we were supposed to be seated first, she said there was no other place for the party of 5 and it was just logical to seat them there!?? In what world is that logical?  We walked out and will not go back. Went down the block to Barra Rossa, seated within 5 minutes, had excellent service!

Another annoyance at Bareburger, while we were waiting to not be seated, a hostess came and shouted at the several groups of people waiting to MOVE TO THE BACK OF THE RESTAURANT SO PEOPLE CAN GET THROUGH! Has management never heard of customer service training?

I again am not really a big fan of Red Lobster like when I was younger.  I feel like the portions just aren't what they used to be for the price. I used to get the fresh fish selections and know they price is so sky high, I don't feel like it is worth it.  It was like $30 for the small portion of salmon.  I am not a fan of fried shrimp and fish, so what are the alternatives? If i want grease fries fish, I'll go to the Captain. 

The service is usually good to ok. 

 I love the biscuits, I mean who wouldn't .  I like the chowder also.

I have a friend who loves Red Lobster so I know I will be back. This is not a place I think about going on my own.
Fantastic French pastries. The almond croissant vaporized and made me eat a second one.
Carne asada torta was very good.  Medium salsa was good but not nearly warm enough.  Horchata was decent, but different.  I'll be back.

I recently had a bridal shower at West Avenue Grille. Everything was perfect. All of the guests and the bride were happy. I mostly worked with Molly on menu suggestions and they even went off menu for some items we wanted. It was a wonderful afternoon. Both Molly and Angelina did a great job. Thank you to WAG once again for making us happy!!!

I love French food and I have been here several times with my brother and parents. This is a cute little place that is part of the Mercado San Augustin. I have had the French onion soup, the cheese plates, pate's, crab cakes and cassoulet all very good. We usually order a bunch of stuff and share. The pricing seems reasonable.

I recommend sitting in the courtyard outside. There is some construction going on in the area that is a little inconvenient.

We recently stayed at this hotel and it was a really good experience for the price. Its not the most convienent hotel to all the tucson attractions but we had a very early flight and its literally minutes away. The free breakfast was great with both hot and cold items. The hotel has free wireless and all the employees we encountered were friendly and helpful.
Some of the best tacos I've ever had. And believe me when I say I've had my fair share of tacos. Free salsa and chips bar. They have good happy hour specials. Treat yourself to a churro!

We loved it.  We seldom eat out and are even less likely to go to inexpensive chain restaurants, but decided to try it when my out-of-town parents visited on a work night.  Good selection of beers for a casual dining restaurant, as well as full bar.  (wine menu was limited, but aren't they always!?)  

We were told "35 minute wait," but turned out to be only 7-10 minutes.

We had Grilled Salmon, some type of tropical chicken salad, 1/2 slab of babyback ribs, and a monte cristo sandwich, along with sides that included broccoli, fries, baked potato, and corn-off-the-cob.   The shared onion ring appetizer was a good start .

Waiter was friendly and humorous, service was prompt and efficient.  Total tab without alcohol was $45, and we all were properly full; indeed, my wife had so much monte cristo that she left food on the plate.

Given that a nice restaurant is at last twice that much for two and consumes another hour or more of your evening, this was a very good deal.   We probably will go there again on our own sometime.

Perhaps my friend and I are too much of a traditionalist but the Vietnamese,  Japanese, and Mexican fusion wasn't happening for us. 
The seaweed wrap made the sushi burrito chewy and difficult to bite into. The tuna was cut into big chunks so it made us feel like we were biting into a hunk of raw fish. 
We also had a rice bowl. That was good but not good enough for me to want to order it again. 
I was really hoping to love it here and surprise my boyfriend with a sushi burrito, at his job nearby, but I didn't want to take the chance and order him one and he not like it either.  
Oh well. It was a unique experience with good company. 
All the ingredients were very fresh and the restraurant was clean.

We visited on Sunday, January 15th and we were excited to try out Philly's newest addition to the gayborhood. The atmosphere of the place is OK, if not a little sterile. In fact, sterile might be the best description of this place as a whole. There was no real culture or heart beat. The whole experience was a little drab. The drinks were basic and a touch over priced with a mild pour. The bar tenders weren't especially friendly and the time it took to get a drink while it was only moderately busy didn't bode well for what it would be like if the place was packed. 
The place could really benefit from something unique, rather that is a craft cocktail list, a look, an aesthetic...something. 
We didn't try the food, but even the menu was a bit of a yawn. The one bright spot of our visit was the greeter/ID checker at the door. They were very warm and energetic when we entered and upon leaving. We stayed for 1 drink and left, not sure we would go back.

Love WOB. I've been coming here for several years and have been a regular customer every week. They have the best wings in town. My fav is the six wing special. Medium is not too hot and the flavor rocks.
Get some- you'll be glad that you did!

Tho post was updated from a 2 to 3 stars...

Dinner night out with the family. First time to this Cheddar's. I had high expectations after eating at the Cheddar's in Columbia, MO. I should have lowered them. My wife's dinner came out cold and looked awful. (Shepherds Pie. She ordered the salmon as a replacement.) On my dinner they forgot the carrots (later to find they ran out). The place was so busy that our server didn't have time to remember the condiments we asked for more than twice. I feel this place has real potential but they really have to add more staff to match the workload. It's a very popular place but I feel if nothing happens they will wither as fast as they grew!


Update: They just brought the bill and did not charge for my wife's meal. Thanks... I'm impressed. As soon as I hit post on this she brought the updated bill. (Literally, within a minute!)

Love Los Jeffes!!!!!

The best Kids menu in town.    Chicken, Steak or Shrimp Fajitas / Tacos / Quesadilla served with rice and beans.   My kids love the roasted corn.  

Taco Tuesday is my favorite.  $1 land tacos.   Great choices.   Al Pastor & Carnitas are my favorite.  

Good Margarita and atmosphere.  

I'll be back!

Bulk it up, Bulk it up.....That's how we bulk out

This place is just like Costco, bulk shopping central, but they have more ethnic stuff that focuses but not limited to Asian and Mexican goodies.

Great meat and produce department, along with a solid nuts and spices area. Solid sweets area too for all the sugar fiends.

Items are easy to find and prices are good. They also do a good job keeping this place clean and well lit.

My girlfriend and I had reservations for 11:45 on Christmas day for Brunch.  We arrived 5 minutes late due to parking but had called ahead.  We arrived and not greeted.  The staff appeared frazzled.  After 10 minutes we were directed to the bar no one having taken our names.  The hostess said everyone had reservations and that there were perhaps 60 guests milling about "waiting to be seated"  My girlfriend eventually found the hostess and our names were added.   About an hour later our names were called.  I thought there might be a riot in the restaurant and out.  

The food was buffet, the carving station unattended and many of the food warming trays were empty and cold.  They quality of the food was mediocre at best, I threw out a good bit.  When they brought out char grilled oyster they were gone in a minute.  There was no fish with the exception of shrimp.  People were visibly angry and still the line remained.  The staff was embarrassed.

We spoke with patrons who had come for ten years and said the chef had quit, management changed and he was sure they were just taking walk ins when fully booked.The hostess was being constantly yelled at for taking credit cards which would be charged if you didn't choose to stay.

Everyone was complaining regulars were stating this was the last time after 10 years.

This was like a poorly done Wedding buffet where they totally misjudged the amount of food, gave out reservations (did not honor them) and had taken your credit card to charge you if you did not show.  I have never seen more unhappy patrons.  There were still 50 people waiting to be seated when the Brunch closed and they were starting to pck up the food....

Poor food, long waits, and insufficient food for the crowd they allowed in (all reservations according to them but we heard some patrons say they just came in..  Never again.

this is a must for everyone.
two ways to do it.
buy reserved seating in advance cause thats the best way to enjoy this show
general admission means standing room only
small, tight, intimate, and hot.
be prepared if its a hot night cause there are some fans but its the real deal up in here.
the musicians are stellar and have a wonderful sense of humor.  playing classics and they take requests so hit that tip jar.
tshirts and beyond for sale after the show.
be prepared to wait in line.
8, 9 and 10 pm shows.
we did the nine pm.
pat O's comes out and provides drinks while you wait, or hit up johnny whites for a better drink price.  also, they sell no drinks inside only water, so be prepared and know that the focus in this place is the preservation hall jazz band.

Can you at least put some meat on that cheesesteak! Not a good bang for your buck. But as someone said, it's the only gig in town. Gosh,  McDonald's gives you a bigger burger and more fries, at a cheaper price! Never use to be this way at Parkside.
Excellent real French food. Not typical for Doylestown. Beautiful restaurant. The Skate wing was like being in Paris. Lunch and dinner are both outstanding. This is an outing restaurant.
Great swamp tour the bus driver and boat were both knowledgable with great stories and information. Definitely would do this again.

From the state-of-the-art playgrounds, to the friendly farmers and staff- this place is amazing! Hayrides to pick sweet, fresh fruit, animals to feed, country store with yummy food- this place has it all! We loved the sprinkler and playgrounds! We will be back.

Alana is the best aesthetician I've experienced when it comes to leg and bikini waxing!  I've gone to other Aveda Salons in Reno like the Tangerine Salon at Summit and L'essence, and she outperforms the services I received at the other places BY FAR!  

A friend of mine who works at MAC in Meadowood Mall recommended her to me, and I decided to get my first Brazilian from her today because I heard such great things. Not only was it quick and barely hurt (she does it UBER quickly using only two strips of hard wax for each side), she's very experienced (worked for Aveda for over 5 years), is a diligent perfectionist (making sure to get every single stray and fine hair), and is a super sweet, funny, great conversationalist (which makes the time fly and puts you COMPLETELY at-ease even when you are totally spreading your legs at her like you're giving birth! I totally felt like I was chatting with a friend like normal LOL). 

She is also very knowledgable, and I trust that her other services will be just as excellent as her waxing. 

I'm excited to go back to her to get eye-lash extensions as she's advertising $125 for a full set right now. I already made my next appointment to get waxed again next month. I highly recommend Alana, and will probably make an appointment pretty soon for a facial as well (she got the "Best of Reno Magazine" 2011 for her facials)!

Sbraga was amazing. it was everything I wanted it to be. obviously if you're going here you're ok with spending some serious money on the tasting menu- and it's worth every penny.

I had the beets, the octopus, the pork and then the dirt w/ worms for dessert. YUM. 
My party sat at the counter so we could see everything being made and talk with the cooks- which was added fun. 
the beets were delicious, they have slices of makerel on top w/ radish. very flavorful and delicious.
the octopus was grilled and spicy- cool texture, but overall very light. 
the pork was to die for. seriously, it was so good I can still taste it if I think about it a week later. 
the dessert choices were the only things that seemed a little off to me. I had dirt and worms- which is basically mouse and cookie crumbles, so it all turned out ok in the end. but the choices weren't that extensive. my sister had apple crumble which was also delicious, but she commented that it would have been better warmed up. 

I would definitely recommend Sbraga- it's a great place with a great concept.

This location's staff is the best! Everyone's very nice and welcoming. They always ask if I need help finding anything, even though I never do because I go there so much. I hope this neighborhood pet supply store keeps up with booming mid city. I really loved the coupon I received in the mail a couple of weeks ago too! So thanks Jefferson feed.

My wife wanted a cheap date night, so we decided to catch a movie at the Keller. We've never been, so it was a new experience for us both. 

For what the theatre is, it's decent. 2 movie tickets for $10 and it showed movies that were only a couple weeks old. The sound and picture quality was great, and the prices are just unbeatable in a theatre. 

The lady taking the money and giving out the tickets lacked personality. I did not expect much, but she just stared at me waiting for me to tell her what I wanted. No biggie. The staff inside all seemed to be 16. They were very loud but again, no biggie. The seats were uncomfortable and the movie screen had what looked like stains on it, but again, for a $5 movie ticket it wasn't a big deal.

Overall, I'd definitely come back based on the affordability alone. It could use some improvements to make it more welcoming and friendly, but it doesn't need it because the prices will keep people coming back!

This restaurant is our go to place to watch sports in Franklin. Their pizzas are great and their calzones even better. I would recommend this restaurant for a good local spot. Going to chain places such as bww is good and all, but sometimes a local place makes the experience that much better.

Dive Bar basically off of the far end of Bourbon St. Came here to begin the Ghost Tour.  Hurricane Special Drink comes out of a Gatorade cooler..... interesting option. Did not try it. 
Took a while to get the bartender's attention. Started getting frustrated and we were about to leave.... but then the bartender came to us and I accepted his non-apology when he poured two overflowing Patron shots for us. Apology accepted.

Great clean and attached restaurants are amazing. The location is perfect being on bourbon and just a couple blocks from the street cars off Canal. Luckily you can't hear Bourbon St. from inside but you can hear your neighbors through the walls. In all I would recommend the Sonesta as a great clean centrally located stay.

Finally checked this relatively new place on Magazine Street out! Since I am almost always craving Vietnamese food on Sundays, and since most places are closed on Sundays, I was pleasantly surprised to find out they are open on Sundays! SundaY!

The inside of the restaraunt is clean and spacious, nothing fancy. There is also an outdoor patio that is nice to people watch from. I ordered a beef pho, a fried egg bahn mi, and some spring rolls. The pho was a generous portion, although the broth wasn't my favorite, it was still pretty good. I really enjoyed the bahn mi. The bread was super fresh!Very simple, with a fried egg, butter, carrots, cilantro. I like dipping the sandwich in the broth... The spring rolls were good as well, the peanut sauce served with them was on point.

I have now been here a few times, sometimes just to get their Thai Tea. If you're craving something sweet, they make a good one. (And give you a few inches of whipped cream on the top).

The best part of this place is the price! Probably some of the less expensive Vietnamese uptown. And the staff have always been very friendly. Definitely give this place a try if you are looking for good value and pretty decent food!

Yum!! The steak was perfect.  I got the prime rib. There was so much food with the meal,  I took half of it home with me. On Sundays they do a prime rib special, it will be a bit of a wait for a table but worth it! 2 for 1 drink specials and full bar. I'll be back.

Always jammed but the line moves quickly and the coffee is still the best I've ever tasted. The cappuccinos lattes are special. They really have it down pat - no wonder all of the top restaurants serve their coffee, it's THAT GOOD!

Have I written about Spasso before? Idk maybe, it's my fav of all the fabulous media eateries! Tonight I went with a friend for a girls night out and it didn't disappoint! I had a watermelon lemonade Martini and it was light and refreshing, Erika had another Martini I think it was the spasso martini she said it was sweet and strong, both wonderful things! To start we shared the antipasto appetizer and honestly how can you go wrong with meats, cheeses, marinated veggies and olives! For dinner I had linguine ponza full of giant chunks of crab meat and some huge shrimp in a light tomato sauce, it's pretty much my go to at this place, the pasta is fresh made and the taste brings me back to my childhood in my great grandmothers kitchen eating a bowl of "homemades"  Erika had the crabmeat ravioli in a pesto cream sauce w sun dried tomatoes and it was a-mazing! Honestly I've been here so many times for brunch, lunch and dinner and have never been disappointed. I'll be back again and again!
Incredible and knowledgeable customer service!! Sky rocked out our experience. Absolutely recommend this shop!! Will be my new go to. Thank you!!!

When it comes to great flavor the smoked fish has it all.
Woo hoo! The coleslaw was perfect the German potato salad was very tasty. 
Just remember to bring enough cash for the meal and the tip.

Don't go...Its a scam. Food is awful and is very very very expensive and they don't post their prices. Three other buffet style places within five miles much better and cheaper. They charge little kids big prices and depending upon day charge different.

After getting lost from my friend and roommate for the evening, the front desk woman would not let me check in without her consent since she was the 'account holder.' I got her to call the front desk on her way back and was told that there were computer issues and it would take at least another 15 minutes for them to access the computer. I asked 'So you would like me to just sleep in the lobby instead of in my room I paid for?" The front desk lady said yes. UNBELIEVABLE. Worst customer service EVER.
I really like London for the location and the bar, though I'm challenged by their menu,  and sometimes inconsistent schedule as a result of special catering events.

If you live in Philly, and you're still buying McCormick spices or any other similar brand at a grocery store, you are out of your mind. The Spice Corner has just about any herb and spice you could ever need for a fraction of the price you'll pay at your typical grocery store.

A quick example: Your standard bottle of McCormick basil leaves, which weighs in at a whopping 0.62 ounces, will cost you, at minimum, around $2.50. The Spice Corner will give you 2.00 ounces (more than three times as much) of much better quality basil leaves for $2.00. I could go on and on doing price comparisons, but it's easier to just look at their website for an idea of what everything costs.

Regarding the quality of their products, everything is top notch. Even after being stored for several months to over a year, I've never noticed any degradation in flavor or potency. And if you're unsure about what spices to get for a meal you're preparing, the staff is more than happy to help you find exactly what you need. Plus, most products have a description and guide letting you know what types of food they go best with (fish, poultry, meat, etc.).

Apart from herbs and spices, The Spice Corner also offers a large selection of teas and coffees. While I'm not a coffee drinker, I do dabble in drinking tea now and then, and I've yet to be disappointed with anything I've bought here. They even have free pamphlets telling you the best way to brew each type of tea.

The husband and I decided to take advantaged of our 3 day weekend and head up to Santa Barbara. Seeing as how we both have never done an official wine tasting tour, we figured this would be a great opportunity.

I looked at some different tours on Yelp and then decided to go with Wine Edventures. We didn't decide until the day before we wanted to go so I was hoping they would be able to fit us in. Sean, the owner was very polite and told us it was no problem. 

The next morning our guide (Hans) picked us up right on time in front of our hotel. We then started off on our scenic drive up towards the vineyards. We visited 4 wineries which were all very different, and served a sandwich lunch (which was pretty good), and also received a souvenir glass.

I loved all the information we learned about wine and Hans was awesome, I would definitely do another tour with Wine Edventures again!

On our way home to Indiana stopped here for lunch.  As always at Cracker Barrel, the menu had many choices, including healthy options.  The service was efficient and friendly: It took only 3 minutes for the salad to come out, and 7 minutes later our food was out.  Food was hot and tasted excellent.  Refills for drinks were frequent, with the waiter being attentive but not hovering.  The bill was ready as soon as we were done eating, with the waiter even offering to provide us beverages to go.  
Restrooms as well as other facilities were very clean.

Personally, I have yet to find a Chinese restaurant I didn't like. I enjoy authentic, along with the americanized kind of stuff. My meals almost always consist of sweet and sour chicken, fried/steamed rice, and crab rangoon. I rarely deviate from what I like at a Chinese place. 

Wei Hong doesn't disappoint in any way. They are definitely authentic, serving food "family style" as opposed to, say, Panda Pavillion (also love it!), who caters to the individual/take out kind of customer. 

The chicken is less fried and chewy, giving you the impression that it is in fact, much fresher. The sweet and sour sauce wasn't too sugary and had the perfect blend of sweet and sour. Go figure. 

The crab rangoon was sweet and fried to perfection. 

I walked in to meet a friend and the restaurant was nearly empty except for a few tables of large groups. I can only blame that on the rain and the fact that it was Monday evening, when most people tend to eat in. It certainly wasn't because this place isn't great!

Yet another treasured gem on South Grand, for which I'll return often.

Nice romantic setting with white table cloth, professional servers and elegance. This is one of many restaurants under the Brennan family restaurant group . I ordered the bbq shrimp and they were Big and succulent and peppery.  This dish reportedly takes 2 sticks of butter to make . So be aware and take caution Weber eating the sauce.  I only ate spittle but of sauce.  There was no soaking the bread for me. Bathroom is downstairs . After eating the shrimp they give you a hot whit cloth with lemons to get the shrimp dll out of your fingers
So scrumptious! I had the dark chocolate and blackberry. Attentive and friendly staff. Great little place.

Went there for bottomless bellinis over brunch as a party of two. There was a bit of wait despite making a reservation but nothing to write home about. 

Our waiter was attentive and polite without being overbearing. He kept the champagne and juice flowing as soon as prompted which was great. 

As for the food, we started with the monkey bread - which is basically a shareable, rippable cinnamon bread that comes with a sugary dipping sauce. Think cinnabon. Personally, I'm not a huge fan of desert foods in general, let alone at noon on a Sunday, but my friend seemed to enjoy it. 

For the entree, we both ordered juevos rancheros (I know, sue us). While not incredibly delicious, the juevos rancheros certainly weren't bad. I'd give them 3 out of 5 stars. The reason I gave Jones 4/5 stars was due to the good service and reasonable price - and the food wasn't bad at all!

Would definitely come back to try some of their other stuff on the menu and for bottomless bellinis.

This is a world class restaurant. We are so lucky to have a chef of Yoichi's calibre call our city home. My husband and I ate here last week and I have wanted to return every single night! We have told dozens of people about it. A part of me wants to keep it a secret so we can be assured of always getting a seat at this intimate, sublime restaurant. But a bigger part of me wants to spread the wealth. This is much more than a restaurant - it is a culinary celebration of a master chef at the top of his game. Yoichi obviously loves preparing his food as much as you will enjoy eating it. Expensive - but worth every penny.

When I landed at about 10am, Saint G. said "want to eat breakfast at the Cracker Barrel?" and I jumped at the chance! Where else can you get the Old Timer's Breakfast which comes with 2 eggs, scrambled well done with cheese, 2 turkey sausage patties, hash browns, grits, 2 biscuits, apple butter, real butter, sweet tea, and some kind of gravy stuff? Can you say food coma? If there was a Cracker Barrel near my house, let's just say I'd weigh 300 pounds. Wow!

I love this place!

I'd been to Sage once before, more than a year and a half ago.  I shouldn't have waited to come back.  I was with a party of 6 and had a reso that I made earlier in the day.  We were seated quickly; the hostess knew our reservation.  We ordered the calamari per the waiter's suggestion, and we were all impressed: this stuff is where it's at, no where else have I seen breaded and fried calamari that is tossed in the sauce (a sweet creamy sauce that complemented the squid well).  The wine list isn't extensive, but it's got everything you might want - and all bottles were approachable.  
I ended up having the ribeye with candied yams and green beans.  Everything had tremendous flavor.  My one complaint would be that the yams were legitimately covered in caramel, which seemed like a little much.  It didn't stop me from eating them, though.  
The portions are pretty big, regardless of what you get.  I tried a bit of the steak and shrimp penne which had a peppery heat that wasn't shy.  Everyone at the table was very pleased with their dishes.  Including the cedar plank salmon, the Seafood Cipellini and the crab cake sandwiches.  
They have some great dessert selections, too.  All for $2!  I had an apple cranberry crumble and tried the creme brule - both very good.

Our server was very friendly and attentive, though he also was good at knowing when to hang back.  He needs to be trained on bottle service (didn't present the bottle and vintage, first pour didn't go to the person who ordered the wine and he finished that pour before serving the rest of the table).  I appreciated his suggestions, his patience and helpfulness.  

Some guests from either the AB visitor center or upstairs came by the bar drunk and caused some distractions (falling off bar stools) and increased the volume of the place considerably.

Coming from the Bay Area, my wife and I have lofty expectations.  Ambiance was nice for an Indian restaurant, waitstaff was awkwardly inattentive.  Food really stood out for being bad - the marsala had too much tomato, and the Vindaloo was the exact same base without the cream.  Shrimp had unsavory taste of iodine.

I'll keep looking, or start having friends from SF freeze and overnight...

After eating here on Saturday night, I can't wait to go back. The atmosphere is amazing! The staff seemed to be having a great time and really enjoyed their job, especially Rich. He made the experience fantastic! He helped us with food recommendations and all were wonderful! The crispy brussel sprouts were better than any I've ever had. The squash blossoms with goat cheese were amazing, as was the crawfish  etouffee and steamed chocolate with salted caramel ice cream! We sat at a great table where we were able to see the food being made, which I loved! All in all, it was great experience and I can't wait to go back!

Was hungry for a great meal and a friend reminded me of this place.  Been way too long.  I got the chicken parm with meatballs.  It was amazing!  My friend got a pasta dish with hot Italian sausage.  That too was awesome.  Have to remember this place more often.

Quite possibly the worst service I've ever experienced when dining in Nashville, or perhaps anywhere.  From the moment we sat down we are not attended to. We waiting 20 minutes for our drinks to arrive. Appetizers took another 30-40 mins, 1 was forgotten. Then after an hour wait we checked in on the entrees.  Seems those were forgotten. We were assured they were coming out.  They didn't. Not until we asked for the bill to leave. But then even that took 15 minutes because the CC machine wasn't working.  They just weren't on tonight. With that said, 1 star because the food we had was actually fantastic. Sadly, never coming back.

Gave this place a second chance after my first experience was somewhat mediocre and very much tainted by a waiter with personal hygiene that would be frowned upon even in Parisian caffes.  
  The food was great, and I have frequented the bakery enough to say that most of the items there are very fresh and delicious.  Their signature tomato omelet is sublime.

The oysters are fresh and amazing. The best oysters I have tried. We searched and searched and found this lovely small stand. Def does not disappoint.  I recomend the Oyster Creole. Its to die for. Its a fried oyster on a bed of creamy spinach type sauce. Add a spladh of hot sauce for a kick and voilà AMAZING. Did I mention its also a resonable price. MUST TRY

Woohoo! Yes its that good, I am an avid simmer so the swimming facilities are perfect..the olympic pool is good, the issue could be during summer hours cause schools out and theres usually summer camps and such, so it can get pretty full. I have swam at other places like Millenium in the park, but Kinsmen is by far alot better. I have used the gym there also its smaller but gets the job done.
Terrible food. Took 25 minutes to get our food. We ordered blueberry pancakes with a side of 2 eggs. Pancakes were overdone and had almost no blueberries. Left with stomach aches and disappointment

NOLA in the heart of Boothwyn!  I've been to New Orleans a couple times, and I love the cajun/creole food!  Cajun Kate's is the closest you can get to real cajun food without hopping on a plane.

They have a featured po' bo sandwich every week; my favorite is the oyster po' boy.  So far, I haven't had a bad meal here, and the fun, engaging staff makes the experience that much better.  The only real downsides (which also makes this a hidden gem) is that they are located in the Booth's Corner Farmer's Market, they're only open 2 days a week, and the counter space is limited.  I'm not complaining, it's just the way it is.

Their Red Beans and Rice, Gumbo, and Jambalaya are fabulous!  You can't go wrong with Cajun Kate's!!

Excellent service and delicious, authentic Thai food. Our server/the owner was very helpful in describing the food and how it is made, when we asked. The Satay Chicken and Crispy Spring Rolls appetizers were amazing - especially the homemade sauces for each!  Entree size was a little smaller than at some other Thai places, but that may be because we ordered from the lunch menu. Reasonably priced, especially for the neighborhood. We will definitely return!

It's good enough.

It is very convenient to where I live, and they have a variety of products.  Not rude, but not nice either.  It's cool to just walk around and check out the stock.

My issue is that the ppl who work there, never seem to want to be there.  But if you are more into prodcut selection, than customer service...go for it, I do!
Really quite good for the price. Get the Truffle fries and don't be afraid to order it rare if that's what you like (some of the other reviews make it seem a little scary to do so).

Wow! I couldn't disagree with Tom G. more!  We tried Carson's for the first time on Sunday evening and we had great food, great service, and really fun entertainment. Its nice to sit outside on the deck and watch the water while listening to Ed? play the guitar. We even got to feed the ducks who were swimming around the deck. But there are other reasons to visit this restaurant besides the scenery.
Although the restaurant was rather busy our server, Andrea, greeted us promptly and opened our wine so we could a enjoy a drink while perusing the menu. A few moments later she brought over some nice Italian bread with a homemade butter that tasted sweet and herby. She offered us daily specials and then took our order. I am not going to describe every dish but I will remark on the crab cakes and porcini scallops. The crab cakes are LARGE. You get  two served with a delicious risotto and asparagus. We enjoyed the Parmesan risotto so much that Cindi ( the owner ) gave us two complimentary servings to go home with us! We also tried the porcini dusted scallops because the dish sounded like something we wouldn't find anywhere else. It was absolutely delicious! Diver scallops sauteed to perfection, with a truffle oil and blanc sauce (not too much, not too little) to die for! This was also accompanied with delicious asparagus and risotto. Two of our non- adventurous friends opted for the fried shrimp dinner  and the other ordered the linguine and clams-both looked and smelled so good-they loved them! No greasy shrimp or fries here!
I took one of the crab cakes (no filler) home and we decided to try a piece of the chocolate cake and the creme brulee cheese cake, which we shared four ways. Again-rich, creamy, delicious!
Next time we go back we are going to try the calamari appetizer and the mussels in red sauce. We'll just have to make room!

I've been a regular customer of Ame Salon and Spa for the past three years and I can say without a doubt that their level of professionalism and range of services is unparalleled.  As a male customer, I have never once felt uncomfortable in a business setting such as a salon that usually caters to female clients.  I have always felt welcomed and am always greeted by name upon walking through the door. 

I have had a number of massages by Nicole over the years and can say unequivocally that she is top notch.  Her skill set is such that you will want to return as often as possible.  I've had massages by a number of folks in the past and I can say that no one has come close to the quality of massage offered by Nicole.  She is respectful of your time and always ensues that she is addressing any areas of concern.  You will be hard pressed to find someone with her charm and intelligence.

Danielle has been cutting my hair since I've been a client at Ame.  The reason I continue going back to her is because she actually LISTENS to me.  I've had my hair cut at a number of salons and barbers over the years and regardless of what I ask of them, they usually just chop and chop until I'm completely displeased.  Danielle, from day one, took the time to ask where I wanted to go and what it specifically was I wanted to make happen.  Her personality allows me to feel at ease in the chair and our back and forth is always enjoyable.

Please know that I rarely write these types of reviews, but I felt compelled to write this after my last experience.  I highly recommend Nicole and Danielle- I can assure you that you won't be disappointed!

Cozy, affordable, nice staff, amazing coffee.

I had a salmon and bagel plate with a side of turkey bacon and a strong columbian coffee.  Everything was fresh, fast, and great.  Our server visited us every 5 minutes to make sure we were good and coffee topped off. Impressed how great the food was and how nice the staff was considering how cheap it is (most plates under $8).

You can not go wrong with this place!
Luxurious 
Affordable
impeccable service

I am somewhat a connoisseur of nail salons and this one hands down supersedes the rest.

I stopped in while downtown to check if by some miracle they had time for me without any appointment. I was impressed by their honesty. They could only do one of the requested services because they had scheduled appointments and wanted to be respectful to those clients since they took their time to make an appointment. This was RARE to hear! Many of you may know that hardly anyone recognizes nail appointments and when you schedule them you usually wait 30 minutes soaking your feet in a tub. Therefore, I greatly appreciated this. By the time my pedicure was finished (which was relaxing and perfectly done) they had an extra employee come into handle the appointments, just so I could finish the services I had initially wanted! 

All in all, I highly recommend. The atmosphere and service received was irreplaceable! I can not wait to bring everyone I know!

This place is great. Wine and cheese room, fresh mozzarella is to die for! We use their catering all of the time for our parties. Strongly recommend their food for your next catering. Lunch time does get busy but their food is just amazing. If I had to criticize anything, their deli/sandwich ordering process could use some improvement. It's so busy and there seems to be chaos in that area all the time.

This is the worst scrub store I have ever been to. Do not waste your time here and if they offer to order you your size, DO NOT. I have lived in reno for two years and have been wearing scrubs for 6 years. First they will tell you how scrubs fits and what size you should wear. After a long discussion of telling them I like my scrub pants to be long and not high waters, I got a lecture on how I am not a tall!

When you think you have found the perfect color, you will find they only have xs and Xxl in coordinating colors. They will have 7 medium pants, but not a single medium top in coordinating color.
