This happens all the time. What I was shocked to learn about was the process of ordering scrubs. I ordered a scrub top and was told that in two weeks it would be in, but the company is fast so probably one week. After 2.5 weeks of hearing nothing I called them. The response I got was "these are back ordered someone should have called you." Then she told me they were back ordered until the previous day and  shold have been there! She kindly explained she would call me back once she called her supplier. Four days later no call. I went to the store, returned the pants I had bought and will never step foot in this store again. 

The topper: my friend had them order a top. Didn't receive it. They said they would call her.. They didn't. She went to the store to return her pants, and wait...... They had hear top on the shelf for sale! 

WORST CUSTOMER SERVICE, WORST PROFESSIONALISM

A really great neighborhood bar that's great for a lot of different things. I've been here for dinner (the food, especially the fried chicken sandwich and burger is excellent), brunch, and drinks with friends (excellent beer selection) and it's been a hit every time. I like that the atmosphere is casual but not overly so. If you're in the area it's definitely worth checking out.

We've become regulars here and i cannot get enough of their coffee and breakfast. Hands down they have the best latte i've had in town. Lots of milk froth in a giant mug with raw sugar and cinnamon dusted on top,yum! Their eggs benedict are perfect everytime. The egg is always poached correctly and never over cooked like it often can be at other places. Their english muffins taste as though they are made in house as they are very dense and crisp. We ordered nutella amd creme crepes for my boyfriends son and they are to die for. It definitely isn't cheap food by any means but for the quality i think its worth every penny. The service is always friendly and attentive. I would say average breakfast or lunch plate is around $10-$12.

This place is OK the therapist my son has is wonderful. The lady at the front desk on the left to be clear cause there are 2 is less then nice and nice is an understatement. She always has some kind of scowl on her face like she hates her job and every encounter I have with her which is every week she is Rude!!! It makes me not want to take my son there cause I have to look @that every time it's exhausting. This is a place for children and the parents are going through enough. Give me a break it's the first thing you see and the first person you meet. Lighten up lady. I question if you like your job. Nevermind their both rude. They act like their so bz just to ignore you.

A hole in the wall you'll want to visit again and again. Found Please U on Yelp and decided to visit during my trip to New Orleans. We had wonderful waffles and the best biscuits. Walked out spending $12 for breakfast. Friendly staff and delicious food. Locals all around!

The food was wonderful, but the service was very slow. I was here at lunchtime, but there were only 8 other people there the entire time and at least 4 staff members. I was told that if I had a dog with me that I had to let them know I was there without entering either the bar or the cafe- this after at least 5 minutes of waiting outside and being seen by one of the staff members. After that service was still lacking. The turkey, apple, and Brie croissant with the side house salad was fabulous, however. I also got a peanut butter blonde, which was hard and crumbly, but tasty. I would come back for another try, but not again with just myself and my dog.

The pho is actually great. I took my parents here and they approved too. The broth is not too oily like some other places.  Slightly lacks the strong pho flavor/smell but the place is on Magazine St...  different crowd.

You probably know about the big hulabaloo that is INDIEana Handicraft Exchange in June - a giant indoor/outdoor shopping fair. But did you know they host a smaller version in December, which just so happens to (smartly) fall on First Friday?

The one in June can be very hot and very crowded, so I preferred the wintertime version, although there were not as many vendors. The crowd favorites were still there, like Newfangled Confections, Homespun, Crimson Tate, Farizula Designs, Silver Linings Jewelry, Hoosier Proud, USI, Revival Food Co...the list goes on. Don't forget to check out vendors down in the basement and explore the open studio spaces!

I love this bi-annual celebration of all things local and will put it on my calendar for 2016!

If you're looking for fast casual meal that is healthy and delicious, this place is the spot.

The prices are great and everything is cooked to order, so nothing is sitting around waiting for you to order.

The prices were great. Almost everything was $10 and that included hot chicken or tofu.

Lunch was crowded and I waited about 10 minutes to get my meal so I'd call ahead if you're on a time crunch.

Definitely using this place to drop a few pounds.

This little restaurant is always so good. It's perfect for a quick lunch or relaxing dinner. They have lunch deals to help you save money and there is always parking up and down the street. The boba is delicious and they have a ton of flavors. I recommend it for a cloudy day or mellow date night. Service is always decent, no real complaints there.

There's nothing fancy about this place, but you can expect great tasting comfort food at reasonable prices.  There is a different homemade soup every night, and they're all delicious. Meals include soup or salad, two sides and dessert. They also have daily and AYCE specials.

Overall, good food, friendly staff, and good value for your money. I highly recommend it.

So far so good..... I travel to Reno a lot for work but normally stay in Carson. First time I have stayed at this hotel and so far have enjoyed it.

Lobby is very clean and well decorated, it has a modern appeal and good vibe. Roma are nice and the temperature is set comfortably. 

The staff is very friendly and I have been greeting while entering and leaving the hotel.

I wanted to like this place!!  I live less than a mile away, and for months I've watched the construction with anticipation. When I heard it was a Blake's, I researched them on the interwebs and got even more excited. I was *so* excited, in fact, that on opening day, I arrived before they opened and was the third person in drive-thru. (on a side note, the trash folks arrived right after me, and couldn't get to the dumpster, so we all had to move out of their way, let them do their job, then go back in place.)

For this "getting to know you" phase, I ordered a bacon breakfast burrito, a Southwest burrito with red sauce, and a Lotaburger with no add-ins. Despite being the third person in drive-thru, it took quite a bit to get my food, but I figured it was due to just opening. I took the food home and cut it in half so my teenager and I could try it all. The bacon burrito was...just okay. The hash browns were a big white mush and the green chiles were too hot for me. I had to pick them out. Teenager agreed, except the chiles were fine for him. I took one bite of the Southwest burrito and actually yelped. My mouth was instantly on fire! They should warn people about the red chile sauce because it was way WAY too hot. My lips and tongue were throbbing, and I couldn't eat any more of it. Teenager liked the burrito, except he said it was too small for the price. The Lotaburger (thankfully, I didn't put chiles on it!) was just okay. It was like a poor hybrid of a Whataburger and an In-N-Out burger, and neither of us were overly impressed.  So...overall, my impressions were "just okay, but the chiles were too hot" while teenager thought it was "just okay, but too many onions used."

A week later, we gave it another shot. We arrived late in the afternoon, and were smart enough to park in the adjoining church parking lot, right behind the bus stop. Interestingly, there weren't any people in line to order, but there were many people waiting for food.

This time, we ordered chicken strips, the grilled chicken sandwich, regular fries, seasoned fries and onion rings to go. It took FOREVER to get our food! For most of our wait, there were several other people waiting for their food, and one of the crew members kept telling us to move out of the way. (Here's a tip...if too many people are in the way..maybe get the food out faster?) The kitchen was full of people, so I don't know what the deal was with getting food out.

Anyway, our order FINALLY arrived and we took it home. Like before, we divided everything in half so we could sample it all.  Once again, the food was just okay. The chicken strips seemed small, and were nothing special. The bun on the grilled chicken sandwich was a sodden mess because of the mayo-like sauce they used. It fell apart quickly and both of us wound up just eating the grilled chicken and leaving the rest of the sandwich. The fries were  just okay...nothing special. The seasoned fries weren't very seasoned, and the onion rings were decent but too greasy.

So, to recap, in our two visits we tried:

a Lotaburger
a bacon breakfast burrito
a southwest breakfast burrito
a chicken sandwich
chicken strips
french fries
seasoned fries
onion rings

The overwhelming result: nothing outright sucked (except for that wet bun), but none of it was really good. It was just one big MEH. Add the intolerable wait, and this is one place we won't be revisiting anytime soon.

I'm so disappointed.

ps...my mom texted this morning, and said she was the second person in drive thru at 6:21am, and she didn't get her food until 6:39am. She, too, said the burrito was just okay, and she'd not planning to go back either.
My favorite Indian restaurant.Food tastes fresh and yummy.Great staff.will be back again n again.

Tried the Wildflower after reading other Yelp reviews.  We enjoyed it very much!  Has a cozy, country cafe feel to it.  Prices for breakfast were a bit higher than other places in the area but it is obvious much is made on premises with good ingredients.  The honey butter served with their fluffy biscuits was delicious and the whipped cream that came with the waffles was the real deal!  Their cheesy grits were excellent and the deep dish quiche was gigantic and good.
The place was a busy and crowded on the day of our visit but it was rainy and impossible to take advantage of the outdoor seating (I'm thinking that might have helped the noise level a bit).  But it is a small restaurant. 
The service was quick and polite, and I hope to return!

I happen to live in the apartment building above Cosi and after eating several lunches at Cosi I have to say I find the previous reviews to be a little strange. I never found the place to be dirty and I like their coffee (much better than starbucks!) and the tomato soup. 
Yes - the staff is not the happiest bunch I ever met but they're fine. Prices are reasonable and the sandwiches are ok too.
If you want a nice lunch place for soup/salad - Cosi might be a good spot for you.

This place is horrible I watched them microwave all our food in the plastic containers and handle trash while cooking and handling food I didn't even eat the food I ordered I suggest you don't go here

Honestly, there's not much more I can say that hasn't already been said. I'm giving it 5 stars to help its overall rating.  It's a shame that it is 3 1/2 stars...

Short and sweet: I love it.  It's a great dive.  But not the kind of dive where I'm afraid I'll get stabbed or contract hepatits from a booth.  It feels like a brainy dive.

Awesome pizza.  Great deep dish.

The bar works.  The prices are good.

Parking is not a hassle (at least not that I've experienced).
It's great for large groups.

I really do like this place!  Even if I contracted hepatitis, the great pizza would balance it all out...

I only rate two stars because of how delicious the food and wine was. my in laws and I were very upset celebrating Father's Day and my partners birthday. As we sat waiting for the rest of our party, we had to ask for menus. my mother in law wanted a glass of wine but never received it. I found gel like goo on a piece of my broccoli and as my partner asked the staff what it was, they told him it was just the sauce. not ruling anything out, I looked all over my plate to see if maybe the sauce gels when cold; but nothing else was found. once we received the bill, my original dish I barely ate was on there. my partner asked if it could simply be removed, to which the manager responded with a snippy "no, everyone had that sauce." we paid tipped and left. we will not return.

We stopped in here for breakfast on a Saturday morning. It was busy, but not packed, and we were seated immediately.

The service was attentive and friendly, and the food was very good. I had eggs benedict, and the hollandaise sauce was really tasty. My wife tried the special of the day, which was a pumpkin omelet, and she enjoyed it.

My only complaint is that the food was a tad expensive and the portions a little small, but delicious nonetheless. We will definitely stop in again when we're in the area.

Mother of pearl! That was a greasy cheeseburger! Clogged arteries aside, the food here was yummy! You order your food and they bring it out you 5-10 mins later and enjoy! I had a cheeseburger and smash burger fries which have garlic and something else (can't remember what!) on them, but they were delicious- not soggy! We also had the fried onions which were really good as well. I got the smaller sized burger which filled me just fine (and I am a big eater), so I can't imagine how big the regular sized one is!

Oh New Orleans you always catch my attention with your voodoo ways.  This place has a pulse about it and you can feel it the moment you step in and it may be overwhelming while you are browsing.

This is an active voodoo practicing site so please be respectful to the alters and offerings.  They have all sorts of gris gris bags, charms, candles and stuff for sale so if you are looking for better luck, to attract the right love or to stop a hexing, this place is where you need to go.
I have been here twice in the last two times that I visited New Orleans and this place is definitely authentic.  I have had a reading here and you should make a reservation because we were all hoping to have readings here but, since we were just walk ins the first time they only had time for one of us.  If you are coming for a tarot reading you should be prepared with questions to ask; unfortunately I was not but, I still feel like I took a lot from what the guy said who was giving me my reading.  He was pretty accurate and I appreciated that.

The pricing on all of their stuff for sale as well as the reading price was comparable to other places but, I think this place is a lot more legit than most places.

Finally! A great Vietnamese place with great Pho thats not a far drive! This place is 4 minutes from my house and I'm very thankful for that because its very delicious and very quick. The place is a must of you are in the area and do not feel like driving all the way to upper darby or philly. Enjoy!!
This Panda Express is big and has nice decor.  There is nice big wood table for large group. Lots is seating and two big screen tvs.
Best breakfast I've ever had! Service, quality and ambiance are why people wait to get in. I get it now!

Hoping I have the right Schnucks but I'd have to say, I'm surprised!  Why are the Schnucks stores rated so low?  I really don't get it!  
First off:  It's just fun to say, "Schnucks"! "Schnucks, Schnucks, Schnucks"!
Second: This store is a combination of No-Cal's Safeway, Raley's & Whole Foods!  They've got so much to offer; a real grocery shopping adventure.
Third:  The folks that work here are friendly and helpful.
Kudo's Schnucks!  We love you!

This place was AMAZING! We initially were going to the restaurant next door which was super packed and closing in 30 min so we came to bayou bistro instead. So glad we did! Everyone's food was amazing, our party of 9 basically had some of everything. We arrived shortly before their closing hours and were happy to stay open to feed us! Brooke and everyone else here was super friendly! I highly recommend eating here!

Ate a delicious lunch here with my husband and our toddler. The service was very good and the food was wonderful. It is all Italian food but ranges from pizza and sandwiches to seafood pasta and rack of lamb. My husband and I ordered the Louie roast beef sandwich and the chicken meatball sub, which were great, and cannelloni for our kiddo. The cannelloni was excellent--tomato sauce was fresh and full of flavor. They also have a nice wine list. Cant wait to go back!
I am here i recommend the scallops and pinot noir. And wwe had the blue point oysters for appetizers. Ask for Ron for excellent service.

This is my first time at Fuzzy's and it's definitely an interesting addition to Temple Terrace. It reminds me of Tijuana Flats but more spacious and an actual bar (huge plus). I tried the $4 happy hour margarita and it was delicious as well as the chips and salsa (although wish it had more lime). I also tried the pork taco that was on sale for Taco Tuesday and the meat was excellent. It's a fun environment and was pretty busy today.

I loved their French toast flight, so I got to try all three of them. My favorite was the Valentine. The only thing I wish was different was their portion size. I had enough for me, but the guys in our group were still not full afterwards. Overall great environment and quality food!

My boyfriend and I went to Ron's last night and had a great time. Big menu to choose from but we got Stromboli and pasta dish. We would definitely go again. The best part of our experience was our server Chris. Very friendly, accommodating and knowledgeable!

So, the owner, Gina, was very rude to me upon dealing with an unhappy customer.  She took over a week to call me back, and in order to even get in touch with her, I had to call the salon more than a couple of times to remind her that I wanted a refund.  When she got me on the phone, she said that she couldn't offer me a refund because I refused to let anybody else in the salon "fix" my hair.  HELLO?!... After suffering quite a hackjob of a haircut like I experienced, who would want ANYBODY to cut MORE of their hair off, let alone from the SAME SALON!?... No.  I said that the only solution was to let it grow out.  And she lied and said Bridget had offered me a refund the day I went in to complain, which was not true.  What she said was that in two weeks, if I still didn't like my "haircut", that the owner could give me a refund.  So thankfully I did end up getting a refund.  And I better have, because there is no way anybody should have to pay $40 for Bridget to destroy their hair.  But it's a shame, because I'm sure Gina is a good hairstylist.  And that was the person my friend recommended to me.  But because she "doesn't take any more clients", I was stuck with Bridget.  So if you go here to get your hair cut, you are getting a young hairstylist fresh out of school who has no real idea what they are doing.
So, it's been about a month since my experience here, and it's finally growing out a bit.  I did just take a trip back home to see my normal hairstylist so that she could fix what Bridget did, and she gasped when she saw it.  I was like, "Don't be mad at me, I didn't touch it.  It was the last person who cut my hair right after the new year!"  She was like "I see that, where did all your hair go?!"  
She is an extremely talented hairstylist (hair genius) with decades of experience and her own salon, and the ways she described Bridget's cut are as follows:
"A sophomore haircut."
"Yeah, she just worked way too fast, SHAVING your hair down the strand."  
"She gave you a mullet."
Even the other hairstylist in the shop was like, "Wow, where did you go to get that piece of work?!"
It's been confirmed.  
It's not just my personal preference of why Plume's haircut sucked.  It did suck.  
DO NOT GO HERE!!!

Absolutely FANTASTIC! We hired 3 people from Swig- one as a bartender and 2 for servers and general help. They were all amazing! They jumped in where they were needed, always polite and curtious to our guests, and I did not have to worry about a thing! We had Kyle, Reba, and Jen and they were all amazing! If I or anyone I know is planning a party where help is needed, I will call them in a heartbeat! It was so great to be able to actually enjoy myself at our party.
I can't stress enough just how great they were!

I thought this place was going to be OK but really they are unorganized, not well trained and unprofessional. I spoke to the office manager and the dentist about it. The dentist is in complete denial that he has problems. The office manager hopes to get the problems fixed and make it a better place. Either way, we are finished there and I don't recommend that you visit this office.

The restaurant week menu was ok but they were out of most of the items on the list. The bread served at the table was cold. The service was mediocre. They are not accommodating for their short comings as far as the menu is concerned.

I tried their burger at the Yelp homegrown event and I enjoyed BUT that is a biased view because it was a free and with the atmosphere of the night everything would appear to be "good/great".

Anyway, I did go to the Wynnewood location today to eat unbiased and actually pay for the meal so I can really feel if my $3.59 was wasted. 
It's about 10mins from my gym so it was post workout meal/dinner. 

I go the regular burger (no cheese) PLUS I got free fries cause of some special. I got the usual topping (lettuce tomatoes caramelized onions)...I got it to go.

Fries- Nothing special but not bad. I guess I'm used to my BK crunchy fries. These were not crunchy but when you throw potatoes into hot oil they usually come out soggy..unless they are battered. I enjoyed them but wished they were a bit more crunchy.

Burger- this was good. It doesn't taste any different from my BK burger and what not but I did like that the actual burger is seasoned so i'm not soo focused on  dousing it with ketchup to mask the taste of the beef like I usually do.

It's not soo far from me and I would return here. i don't eat burgers much but I would come back for another burger. The place was actually sorta packed with folks...so happy to see that they are doing well.

On our early-morning drive up the coast from Orange County to Monterey, we decided to stop at Dawn Patrol in Santa Barbara for breakfast.  What can I say?  The two build-your-own hashes we ordered were both fantastic.  Loved the homemade jam that came with the toast.  It's not possible to choose what's best, as the number of combinations and permutations is...well, you do the math.  We enjoyed great service and the surfer look.  Plus the delicious scone we brought to eat in the car later on.  If Dawn Patrol ever comes up to Marin County where we live, we'll be first in line!

Definitely a great bar hang out!  When I went on a Thursday night, the bar was packed, even upon arriving around 5:30 pm.  

The atmophere is loud and airy with lots of big screen televisions.  We got seated in a very comfortable booth and had a friendly waitress greet us immediately.  She informed our party that drinks and appetizers were half price for happy hour.  Since we were there for dinner, we passed up this offer, but it's good to know for the future as there were a few nice selections offered.

I had a crabcake sandwich --- nothing to write home about as it was your typical bar food sandwich.  They did give you a choice of shoestring fries, tortilla chips, or vegetables with the sandwich.  I opted to get the tortilla chips, but had to ask for salsa to accompany them.  

I'd go back to try out happy hour at the bar!

I love everything about Tired Hands and look forward to going every time I am home. My Mom first noticed the long lines of people outside of the original location and we were curious about what could draw such a crowd. After going once we knew it would become a regular spot for our family. The beers are funky and flavorful. The original location is tiny while this new location is huge. I would recommend the original location for a small group and the new location for a larger party.

First time here. Was a little skeptical at first since the little one was with us. User reviews said it's not kid friendly but our 8 y/o was able to find something on the kids menu. 
Our server was knowledgeable, very kind and swift. Bread and butter are a indication to us if the appetizer & main course will be good (not sure how that came about with me & the hubby)- and both butters were good & the bread was warm, soft and flaky. Drinks are on point and the crab cake appetizer was delicious.
Now to wait on the main course- filet, potato & sautéed spinach.

Exceptional!!!

A great combination of good food and ambiance. 
And the staff/family is amazingly friendly.  Youll like it here.

We went here with our 2 kids and another couple and their 2 kids on a Sunday and the place was slamming crowded. The wait was going to be an hour but our other guest got there early and put our names in and we were seated almost immediately. It is brand new and fun. There are lots of beers on tap. The waitress was great. Funny give and take. Patient  with the kids, special ordering ect. They gave them coloring pads that kept them busy.  After dinner we went to the back bar and sat by the fire place. This is the best spot in the place. A nice large fireplace and a large flat screen above it. Great spot. We will be back.
One of the best donut shops I have ever been to. Fresh donuts with a great variety.

Let me start off by saying, I'm not a vegan. I gave this place a try because of how much I love vedge. Not only was it the best vegan cheesesteak I've ever had but it was one of the better cheesesteaks in the city period. Unbelievable and tastes cleaner than going to pats or jims for a pile of grease. It's a must try vegan of not !

I would like to give the review in 2 phases.
Phase 1: We were at Tampa Riverwalk. Searched a decent restart nearby. Checked the closing time - 11 pm. Walked 0.4 miles to get there. Reached at 10:20 pm. The attendant said, we close 1 hour before the actual time and keep open only for take-aways. First impression - 1 star.
Phase 2: The lady asked where we came from. The rating started changing from there. Hearing we came from a long distance, she offered to have dine in. Truly speaking, we thought that this half hearted offer will turn them being rude to us. But OMG! True professionals. Never thought that our experience will be so amazing. Served nice n hot food (oxtail, jerk chicken and goat curry were amazingly tasty). Gave us complimentary chicken n veggie patties. A perfect dine in with family n friends; n great hospitality. Will definitely go everytime I hit downtown. Jennis and Andrew, you guys are just awesome.

Went back to this place for the second time and were not let down. We were in town for a ball game and were cutting it close on time but wanted to eat before heading to the stadium. Our waitress noticed our cards shirts and asked if we were going to the game and let us know she would make sure we got out of there on time and sure enough she did, despite a huge rush midway through the meal.

I got the Cuban again which may be the best sandwich on the planet. Husband got a Blackhawk sandwich, which was good but it was a cold cut...maybe he just didn't read the menu but he was expecting it to be hot. Either way it was good, although probably won't order it again. He also got the dill pickle soup, which he says he would "travel to the end of the earth for", it's that good.

For dessert we had a Nutty Irishman. It was covered in HUGE pecans and a huge whipped topping. Could've eaten about 10 more if we had time.
Great food! Came out quickly with a lot of options including vegetarian choices. Loved the ricotta and honey! All made in house. Also enjoyed the portabella mushroom pasta.

Justin is the best. He's been taking care of my 92 gallon corner tank at home for years now, and works on my Co2 system at my office as well. Super responsive and can get livestock, plants, or anything else you want. He's always ready to answer my questions or take care of any problems I have.  He's my go to guy for all things aquarium and has made my life so much easier. I can't imagine him not taking care of my tanks.

When I first found out that I was spending a week working in the Warehouse District I was disappointed that I wouldn't have time to get to my favorite NOLA spots. Turns out it is just an opportunity to find some NEW FAVORITES! Lüke is definitely that. This was an awesome meal in a wonderful setting with top flight service. Shout out to our server Kenneth! 

Here's the long story. When I took the included photo my dining partner knocked his Martini to the floor shattering the glass and causing a minor scene. The waitstaff handled it perfectly. Then I said to Dan... here is the test... is this a good restaurant or a great one? Kennth had replaced the Martini within 3 minutes! That is a great restaurant. As he placed it on the table he said, "Usually when this happens the second one comes in a sip cup!" That's FUNNY!!  The oysters were perfect both raw and stuffed. My etoufee was spot on and i loved it served over pasta. This was a great night at a GREAT restaurant.
Go to the location in the Loop, the one on the SLU campus is not as personable. The premium sandwiches are pretty good but the normal deli sandwiches are not much to write home about.

First off I want to give kudos to all the amazing people that volunteer their time at Telus World Of Science :-) The place looks immaculate and you would be hard pressed to find somebody where if you stopped them to ask a question they wouldn't  have an answer for you.

With that being said however I just got back from my first visit to the Telus since they brought in this new concept of upcharging admission for their "feature exhibits" and I have to say I was really disappointed with the experience. We walked through the whole body works exhibit reading 90% of the informational plaques on the cases and walls in half an hour and I really don't feel that it justified adding an extra $10.00 to the price of the general admission.

There is two exhibits at the Telus "Mystery Avenue" and "The Body Fantastic" that have been there a number of years and when you walk through them you really feel that they have outlived their usefulness. Body Fantastic has a number of things in it that look worn out and need maintenance and Mystery Avenue amusingly enough has video footage with news personalities that haven't been on television in quite some time. I think it is also worth mentioning that the explorer gallery upstairs is currently sitting empty without an exhibit.

There are a number of great shows in the Imax right now and thankfully a healthy offering of 8 different shows playing in the Margaret Zeidler star theatre. The star theatre shows are included in the price of general admission and definetly worth a look.

It's a great place to take kids for fun and interactive learning but just not a venue in th city that promotes repeat visits I think. If the city was smart it would put some money into the Telus to breathe new life into it and stop spending money on stupid sculptures to put on the corner of Fox Drive and the Whytemud but that will never happen until we get rid of Stephen "WE NEED A NEW ARENA" Mandel.

Did hibachi Saturday night. Food was made quick and the product tasted well. Had nothing to complain about. We had a living social coupon. Would I come back. Sure. Sit down maybe a lil different experience. But the byob feature is good.

I like it, I think the concept is awesome. They wait kills me though. I'm sure give a bit more time and things will calm down some. I will definitely stop by once in a while but I also really like another local ice cream shop in Seminole heights area that makes unique flavors too. That one is still a favorite, time will tell if icesmiles will steal my heart. 
The ice cream is very creamy and the flavors do evolve, they say they add new flavors every 1-2 weeks. I like that they add toppings too.
The Mead is always delicious and the staff is fabulous and friendly. Lots of fun reasons to stop in, took advantage of nead and mead tonight!!
Great and fast customer service. I would definitely come back again

Went here to eat and we're very impressed. Had a harvest salad,which was excellent. We had a pizza that was half mushroom, the other was the Bronx bomber.They had a totally  different taste from one another,but that's what made it so good! The staff was quite friendly and our waitress was very knowledgeable on their product.We will definitely be back!!!!!

The bouncers are rude and disrespectful. The customer service in this place is an absolute ZERO! For someone in the customer service industry i was appalled by how myself and my group of 10 LADIES were treated. No wonder this club was dead. Nobody wants to spend the prices to be treated like your club is on 4th Street. Beautiful facility, but ruined by the bouncer. Let me tell you how It started, upon entering i decided not to coat check. No big deal but as a few minutes passed i changed my mind. I walked to the guy at the entrance who was too busy talking to his girlfriend to even actually assist me. He finally yelled at me and told me i would have to exit and RE PAY and re enter in order to coat check. What? What terrible customer service! I have been in hotel hospitality the past 10 years and i have never witnessed such terrible disrespect. When i asked him if he could assist me since coat check was right there he put his hand in my face and said "no" and his girlfriend snickered behind him. I just dropped $$ on drinks for all my girls and tipped the valet $200 i am not afraid to drop money where people have excellent customer service. I will NOT be back to this facility. It is over priced and ran by a bunch of trash. Welcome to reno, you can build a vegas night club but you can't take trash and put it in a suit and expect it to be as classy.
Delicious and cheap - adding bacon to a st. paul is genius. I would give it 5 stars if they added egg drop soup to thier menu since that's my kids favorite part of chinese takeout.

This place is classy and has excellent dinner options. I'm from the N.East, and we know our seafood. I was very surprised to see large, sweet sea scallops. Being where the majority of scallops come in to port (New Bedford, MA) I was skeptical of what I would get. I was proved otherwise. 

Some dishes can be on the pricey side, however; the atmosphere; knowledgeable staff; good cocktails does make up for it somewhat.

Bawarchi has become our go-to place for Indian food.  In our house, we get take-out every Friday, rotating through different types of food, and when it's time for Indian, it's always Bawarchi.  I adore their Chicken Tikka Masala and dip my Paneer Naan in the sauce (deeee-lightful).  I'm not a spice freak, and their mild version is spicy, but perfect for me.  My boyfriend is a hot-and-spicy kinda guy, and their American Spicy Chicken Vindaloo works for him.  They also do an Indian-spicy, which he doesn't have the nerve to try.

If you're going to get comfort food, why not get Stephen Starr comfort food? I've lost track of his proliferation of establishments since I moved away, but, as a random restaurant choice, this was a good one. The four of us all got drinks, entrees and desserts, and left happy. Everyone got different cocktails, and we were each pleased with our choices. We went poultry-heavy: two orders of chicken pot pie, one of chicken and waffles, and one of fried chicken (mine). The pot pie was deemed wanting salt, but was otherwise well-received. My fried chicken was delicious: perfectly crispy on the outside, succulent on the inside. The accompanying fries were well-done, too. 

As for dessert, I can say only this: S'MORES. Get the s'mores, everyone; they are amazing and perfect, and I would eat them every day without complaint, I think. So, overall, a good meal, and won't break the bank. Keep it up, Mr. Starr.

Bought online voucher for City and Cemetery tour and seemed like a great deal. Was excited and looking forward to it. Scheduled pickup was 2:30pm and was given a window of 30 mins for pickup. Bought the voucher 2 hrs before and asked if the 2:30 was open. I was told yes . I gave voucher number and pin and it was supposedly reserved. Well at 2:30 the bus came and got on only to find out that I wasn't on list.  The driver called dispatch and there was no record of me . So I called the company after being kicked off bus and they told me the bus was stuck in traffic and that it was coming . I called at 3:00 and again at 3:30 and got same answer. Finally at 4:15 I was told my reservation was cancelled. So I wasted 2 hours of my day for no reason!  Disappointed from start to finish. For others with vouchers, call the company as you board bus to make sure this doesn't happen to you!
Ask for Gerri. Gerri is awesome. Desire has a great happy hour. $6 for 6 oysters and $3 draft beer, Monday-Friday 3pm-6pm.

Food is four stars, traditional American fare.  But, the service was one star at the Southport Indiana location on the evening of Sunday, June 15, 2014.  I will gladly change my review to 3 stars if management responds to this review that they have made corrections.  Our kids' dance studio filled up the place with customers.  Studio staff called 4 months in advance and again 2 weeks in advance to let them know we were coming and for the restaurant to make arrangements to staff accordingly (since Sunday nights are normally quiet).  We arrived and were seated.  The staff seemed to have expected us by their comments.  Orders were wrong at our table from the beginning, and three people at our table waited over 1.5 hours for their food.  Drinks were served randomly, sometimes before food arrived and sometimes with the food.  When we flagged the waitress to explain that she needed to bring chips or something for the three people waiting over an hour for their food she ignored our request.  We spoke to the manager and asked for the same thing.  Request ignored.  After an hour and 20 minutes the waitress asked if she should bring some chips for these folks.  Yes!  20 minutes later she delivered the chips with the food that finally took an hour and 45 minutes.  We had repeatedly flagged the manager throughout this process.  His answer:  There are 150 people here!  Then, the person who waited the longest for her meal (she got it around 10:30 PM) was double charged for drinks, charged for the chips, and charged for the wrong meal that they had brought her at the 1 hour mark.  That's right, they brought her the wrong meal an hour into her wait.  When the manager came to correct her bill, he made it sound like he was doing her a favor by removing the errors.  I politely explained that he and his staff could have listened to our repeated request of, "please bring something for our three friends to munch on since it's been over an hour."  The manager cut me off with his new mantra, "there are 150 people here!"  I would say this to his upper management: Your manager on that night was unqualified to manage your restaurant.  If indeed your restaurant cannot serve a full house of customers, then you need to close down part of it and serve only a limited number.  Do not tell your customers they are an imposition.  The mistakes by staff were forgivable up to the point the manager made excuses.  When I compared notes with other customers from our kids' dance studio, they had similar experiences, and with the same excuse from the second manager on duty, "there are 150 people here!"  Well, there might have been 100 people in the restaurant at its peak.  When I got there early and it was practically empty, they managed to get my appetizer wrong.  So, clearly the staff and management are not properly trained to provide adequate service even with a few customers.

1999 Ford Expedition needed a timing chain replacement.  Parts including coolant, radiator cap, oil filter, 12 1/2quarts of oil (due to metal shavings), spark plug wire set and the cleaner was $628.94.  Labor for timing chain $925.10 and labor to change spark plug wires $117.00.  You have to take the whole front of the engine apart to change the parts and I'm not sure I could have attempted it myself.  I'm a do-it-yourselfer and I try when I can to avoid the hefty car repair bills.  They got the job done fast and the trucks runs great!  I appreciate them fixing our truck!

Worst dinner I have had in Nashville. Food was mediocre beer and wine selection horrible. Oh plus no glassware to speak of.  They did not have any beer glasses or wine glasses. No need to go back. Great opportunity for someone who wants to open a real Puerto Rican restaurant.

Although they do not stand out in the realm of Dim Sum, its still very enjoyable =). 

While located in the same plaza as Ho Ho Choy; Chopstix is much cleaner, friendlier, less chaos, nicely decorated, and offers a variety of HK style cuisine. I especially adore coming here due to the cleanliness and the friendly staff. The price is as the same many Chinese restaurants/Dim Sum but they they do have a lot of "Specials". 

X.O Seafood Fried Rice: I don't normally order fried rice when going out just because its one of the easiest dish to make at home but the technique and ingredients put into this is perfect! You'll definitely be licking your lips for more.

A-OK! because as a whole, it really is just an A-OK Chinese restaurant.

I've eaten here with colleagues over a dozen times. I've always loved their food! 

Sometimes the servers aren't too polite, but regardless the food's terrific.

It's hard to pick a favorite dish here, but I've always loved the Curried Chicken. One of their appetizers chicken skewers (I forgot the name.. It's the second on the list) is awesome.

I also like their cold coffee.

It's also open pretty late so can be a good place to get take out food.

My partner and I have been eyeing this place for awhile, and finally decided to try it today. Sad to say, its appealing aesthetic from the outside did not match its products inside. After waiting for roughly ten minutes in an atmosphere serving 3 whole customers and only one person actually making the drinks (we were not even acknowledged until 10 minutes into being present here and no one else in line...the 3 customers were sitting at tables), we ordered two honeydew bubble teas at a whopping $5.50 each (the honeydew blend here is a mix of fruit and powder based). Once we got them, I of course shook my drink first (as any bubble tea, or boba, aficionado would tell you, you should shake your drink first to have the tapioca "bubbles" evenly distributed). To my dismay, the drink broke through the seal and created a mess on my shorts and the floor. When my partner asked about resealing the drink and explained that in every other place we've gotten bubble tea the seal has never been a problem, the person helping us stated that the humidity was the reason for the poor seal and as far as the shaking the drink at all other bubble tea places we've been to? Her response: "apparently, not here." No apology, no apparent concern for their customers. And all of this would have been worth it if the drink consistency and taste was great - our drink was liquid cream and not a slush like consistency as it should be. We won't be back here.

Love this little Mexican joint. I love the tongue tacos. Make sure to ask because sometimes they don't serve them. Everything is always fresh and hot. Wash it down with a pineapple Mexican soda and you got your self a meal!

Unassuming outside, modern inside with consistently impressive dinner spreads. The rolls live up to the restaurant's name - I have never seen such creative and artistic displays (our four rolls were highlighted with a gorgeous butterfly drawn from various sauces on the plate and a glowing martini glass). The rolls are uniformly delicious - as would be expected from the generous dollops of house special sauce and spicy mayo. Recommend the bloomingdale, anything with eel/salmon. For a lighter fare - go with Banzai Tree roll or odessa roll (riceless). The variety on their menu will blow your mind. Great for a date or outing - a nice twist on the traditional predictable sushi.

Amazing care for my sick rabbit. Everyone was gentle, concerned and every question I had was answered genuinely. I was shown how to administer all medications and honestly for the area the price wasn't bad. I was expecting $300+ I paid $120. I felt very comfortable and I knew my rabbit was in great hands. I will be using this vet as my primary vet for my two bunnies. Oh yeah and the best part was that I called at 1:50pm and was given a 3:00 appointment!

This review is for the newly opened second location on Pine Street between 9th and 10th street.  i stopped in this morning to check out the coffee here.  The cafe options for good coffee are sparse between the Washington Square neighborhood and center city (and I had grown tired of looking at the empty Ethnics space), the Good Karma Cafe is a welcome addition to the neighborhood.  

I ordered an iced coffee - its good to know they come in two sizes - 16 and 20 oz, along with a shot of espresso (at no additional charge), and that they also carry soy milk.  I decided to sit down with a magazine and my coffee and take in the atmosphere of the new space- its very open and still feels a bit empty- somewhat lacking the cozy atmosphere that makes a cafe seem so inviting.  I went to take a seat in the side room towards the back of the space, but the air felt a bit stuffy there so moved towards the front.  The music added a nice chilled out vibe, and the large paintings added some color to the otherwise white walls.  

The space up front near the counter is a bit barren, with the exception of two not-so-pretty drink coolers- it would be nice to see more tables here, or a counter with some stools.  There is also an atm inside, nice I suppose if you need a bit of extra cash (not sure if the cafe takes cards)...however, it would be nicer if the sound on the machine could be turned off- it beeps loudly every time a button is pressed- kind of distracting if you are reading or studying. Additionally, with the size of the space, before they opened, I was expecting more of a cafe- the kind that serves soups and sandwiches, in addition to coffee, tea etc., maybe this will happen eventually?  It would really be nice to have a quick sandwich/snack option in the neighborhood.

All things aside, I know they've only been open for about a week and a half and are still getting used to the new space, so I'll definitely return.

The Cake Bake Shop a picturesque cake bakery.  You can get desserts (cakes) by the slice or a whole cake.  The store is tucked away in a neighborhood in Broad Ripple - off a side street, but still close to the action.  It has parking.

Once you go inside, it is pretty magical.  It is like you are being transported to another time in far away France.  The lights are bright, the desserts look amazing, the music is soothing, the atmosphere makes you just want to relax, drink a cup of coffee or tea and enjoy the cake.

Unfortunately, that is where it stops.  I have been here a few times.  My first visit was magical and rejuvenating.  Since then, it has changed.  I keep giving it one more chance hoping that magic will return.  But... it does not.  Overall my thoughts:

- the staff seems to be in a big hurry to get you served and move on to the next.  If you have a question about anything, it may be better just not to ask.  They seem like I am just interrupting something more important they have to do.  It is most unfortunate.  If the staff were friendly and could act as though they cared about the patrons, this place would be better.  

- the cakes are beautiful, but they have lost the moistness they use to have.  It makes me wonder if they are making them and keeping them refrigerated now where they use to be fresh.  (Refrigerating a cake will dry it out, and that is what it seems to me.)

Service was excellent and our server was very knowledgeable regarding preparation and contents. Starter of nachos (sweet potato chips) and a small cheese plate were acceptable but not exceptional. 

Shared two entree plates of "Breakfast" as well as day boat scallops. Breakfast was FABULOUS and potentially overshadowed the scallop plate.

For desert had the PB mousse had minimal Peanut butter flavor and the blueberry tart with ice cream was OK. 

Overall good but not great.

This is the best Chinese food in Reno. It's not Bay Area fair but, it's the best you'll get in Reno. Believe me. I've tried every Chinese restaurant in town. 
First off ask for the dim sum menu. Order a couple of the items. Then settle in for some good chow fun dry style. I always ask for chow fun without bean sprouts. The potstickers are done fresh. Unlike some restaurants that microwave them (Palais de Jade). This is not a place for ambience. It's a hole in the wall type. The kitchen is in plain sight and occasionally they will be rolling won tons in the dining room.
Service was slow. Thank goodness the food was great to make up for it. The gumbo has oysters in it and the burger was actually really really good.

Had one of best burgers in a while here the other day. Very original recipe, with baby kale, tomato jam, and a spicy aioli, and cooked perfectly. Today I tried a half order of French toast, to great satisfaction. Fresh fruit, lemon-whipped butter, and quality maple syrup, all on top of house-made Hawaiian bread. 

The rest of the menu looks fantastic as well. Prices are about average, but still a good deal, considering the quality. They also have a couple of items available in small or large portions.

Every single time our family comes to this location we are treated so well. Customer service strong and quality of food is perfect for this prices point. Thursday is family night so we bring our daughter then.

Had the Alligator Meatballs with marinara over pasta and it was delicious. Everyone I was with really enjoyed their meal. I would say a great New Orleans style meal at a reasonable price. Staff was fine also.

The wonton soup is my favorite, but I also love their fried wontons, egg rolls, boneless ribs, and the fried rice. The food isn't overly seasoned, but it's really good for sensitive stomachs because you can sauce your own food to taste. Beyond that, the service is amazing, with a friendly staff who recognize repeat customers!

So this review is all based on my personal experience as an adult.

We visited the Children's Museum awhile back when the Avatar exhibit was in town. I was excited about  finally visiting solely because of Avatar. The parking garage is across the street from the actual museum but they did build a skywalk so you don't have to try and cross busy Illinois St with small children. But if that is your sort of thing there is a crosswalk with a controlled light so you can safely get across.

At the ticket counter there is a big Bumble Bee from Transformers which is neat and gets you excited about what you'll find inside. The museum as a whole is 4 floors filled with stuff for kids to do. As an adult with no kids, a lot of the exhibits were boring and uninteresting (as they should be as they're geared towards kids).

There is a lots to look at and do. I will say that the Chihuly sculpture was pretty incredible and spans the entire 4 floors. Avatar was cool and was laid out in a nice way that really had a good flow. From my understanding that portion of the museum is where the "rolling" exhibits are held.

The museum as a whole does a very nice job of teaching kids about how things work and really gives them their own hands on experience. Most places kids aren't allowed to touch but they can go crazy in here. I personally don't see myself going back again since I don't have kids. BUT if you DO have kids then I'd recommend taking the little ones for an afternoon of fun and adventure.
Absolute joke. These people couldn't give a f*** about customer service. Pathetic. If I could give zero stars, I would.

Blondie's is definitely one of my favorite places for brunch in the city. The staff is incredible and the food is lovely. Every server I've had there is phenomenal. The perfect blend of attentive and friendly without being too uptight. There was a red headed barista there who made the best cup of coffee I've ever had. She also had a quirky charm that you can only find in coffee shops from the 90's. There's also a manager with brown hair who looks like an angel and is so friendly! All in all, I love Blondie's. Try the Mandie Sandie with potatoes! So good!

A cafeteria of my dreams - so many choices of coffee, cold drinks, sandwiches, prepared salads, treats, and even small portion of nuts and candy - it makes my head spin! There is a buffet of hot foods sold by weight, a sandwich bar for custom cold and pressed sandwiches, daily soups, pasta, and more. I had an egg salad wrap that was absolutely packed and so fresh. I even liked the lettuce, which I normally don't, but it was crisp and doesn't have that weird taste I sometimes notice at other sandwich places. And the prices can't be beat - if you can avoid the lunch rush, the service is reasonably fast.
Great neighborhood place, food is always consistently good. Great open bar to eat in or have a couple drinks. Highly recommended

Been coming to Ron's since the 90s and we love it! I can't tell you much about the menu because I always get an Oval. (Red white and Blue is my favorite.)They have a nice beer list and good bar specials. A bit loud when there is live music. But it's a nice place to meet with a friend for a drink or take the family for dinner. Ron's has grown imensly since the 90s but still has great food. 

We also order take-out, pizza and ovals on occasion. Their convenient take-out side makes pick up quick and easy, not to mention their nice beer selection.

Service can be a bit slow and I never go on Friday or Saturday night because I know the wait will be too long. But on off nights, a Ron's Oval is a treat!

First time I went here was pretty good, years ago. It was a nice break from the standard suburb sushi fair. Went there again couple days ago and was very disappointed. Most of the sushi roll menu contained seared or fried fish and very little raw fish. The sushi and sushimi menu was tiny and left a lot to be desired. We got a lobster bisque that was terrible. To the point that I wondered if the chef ever tasted it before putting it on the menu. A roll called mango passion didn't even have a mango taste, and had ingredients in it that were so incongruent that the taste was bizarre. The simple rolls were ok, but tasted like any other sushi place. Also ordered a fried green tea ice cream. Nope. Didn't have that. Only had chocolate, strawberry and vanilla fried ice cream. The crust fell apart instantly. It was cold. The ice cream should have been melting a bit on the outside from the outer crust being fried, but given that this desert was probably sitting in the freezer, it was rock solid. They're supposed to fry it quickly once ordered. 
Even lowering my high standards of culinary experience I cannot give this place more than 2 stars based on food alone. It's a popular place and people do seem to like it. In my opinion it's probably because they don't venture out past the burbs.

Well it's been a while since I wrote a review and that's partially because I went on vacation.  Now it's time to review the main vehicle of that vacation: Carnival Cruise Lines....

I have to say that I'm pretty disappointed in carnival.  There are a variety of reasons why and I'll attempt to illustrate them fully below:

1 - They charge you for Soda.   Yeah I know.  I mean seriously? Soda is like the cheapest thing in the world and you have the gall to charge me like 3 bucks for can of Coke?  Get off me.  Sure you have an "unlimited plan" but you'd need to drink soda like me in college to get your money's worth.

2 - Diamonds International. It's really sad to me that Carnival has either purchased land or worked with each of the ports to create an identical mall at each port that contains not 1, not 2, but 3 freaking Diamonds Internationals at each location.  Then they drop you off and effectively hold you hostage in these cookie cutter malls shoving "cheap" jewelry, souveniers and lots of other "americanized shit" into your face.  I didn't go Cozumel to get a t-shirt from Ron Jon Surf Shop, get a drink at Fat Tuesdays and buy diamonds.  I went to experience local culture and to lay on a beach.

3 - Shore Excursions. Much like above, the cruise line makes it difficult for you to do anything without the purchase of a "shore excursion".    This includes laying on the beach.  Shockingly, at every port we are far away from the beach and to get there you generally need to take local transportation and/or buy an "excursion".  The excursion costs like $50 a person.  For the beach.  I mean cmon.  I'd say that's a bit overkill.  Can I go to a local taxi and get there?  Generally yeah, but guess what?  Those dudes know that your only alternative is a $50 excursion and they price themselves accordingly.  Oh and most excursions start at 8 am. Totally not my thing.

4 - Food.  I'll be honest, I wasn't impressed.  They have a ton of variety and the buffets and main dining room have reasonable hours.  But the buffet wasn't as good as a nice Casino Buffet and the dining room food felt like food from an overly-produced wedding reception.  The steak house was "ok".  My jaunt over to Elways at Cherry Creek here in Denver with Ladyhawk for our anniversary was 10 times better on a pure food level.

So at this point you must be saying, "geez Nick, you didn't enjoy yourself on vacation!"  You'd be wrong.  I loved spending a week relaxing, playing cards, reading and exploring new places with my wonderful wife.  It was a blast.  I'll even try a cruise again someday, just not with Carnival.  

The hidden gem in our excursions and searching?  Isla Roatan in Honduras.  That place is very beautiful and Anthony's Key Resort on that island is a place I'll go back to sometime.  Gauranteed.

Cool atmosphere and delicious ice cream. I'm not a fan of the food but who cares when you can listen to a hilarious soap opera in a corner booth and enjoy unique ice creams and floats? Love this STL gem.

My experience at Sliced was just fine.  My reuben was really good.  The broccoli and cheese soup was not overly cheesy and had good consistency.  However, the soup lacked salt and was incredibly hot, making me believe it was re-heated in a microwave. 

I was expecting a larger selection of soups than the three they had on the menu.  I'll go back and see if the options are different, or if they are the standard.

Overall, a nice change of pace, but nothing exceptional from the other soup/salad/sandwich places in the area.

A home favorite- from a Friday night out listening to live music, to ordering out for a pizza movie night. Rons never disappoints! We have been regulars for a few years now, and do not plan on stopping anytime soon!

I appreciate this place for many reasons, but mostly because they will show a good PAC-10 football game.  Being from LA, I need to watch my USC football!  

I don't love that you can smoke in this bar, but it's a sports bar, I get it.  

The food is normal bar food, but I always order the pizza.  They're delicious - especially with the jalapenos!

I called today Sept 11th after Hurricane irma to help us out with recovering our store and feeding our team members. I didn't give them much notice. The love I felt from these guys was just down right amazing. Bless you guys and I can't wait to enjoy your offerings to us!!

This place is amazing but a little pricey. The decor is very chic and modern. You go up to the counter and order and they bring it out to you. I ordered a spicy chicken salad sandwich that rang up to be $9 if I remember right.

The food and drink that I had was amazing and I was actually quite disappointed that I had finished it all and had to leave! They also have really good smoothies. Just ask!

I have been running around like a crazy person trying to find a good falafel in the burbs for the past couple of years, but I no longer have to look. I have already been there several times and enjoyed my meal every time. The customer service is slightly lacking sometimes, but the food makes up for it.

I booked a massage here with a coupon . When I got there, it didn't even appear anyone was there. No one was in the building except a male massage therapist. I filled out the paperwork indicating I was having shoulder problems. At no time during the massage did the therapist do anything for my shoulders. It was only a back massage, and was the worst massage I've ever had. Would not go back there, or recommend. I've had better massages from students at massage schools. On a positive note, the place was clean, in the therapist didn't talk all thru the massage. That's the best I can say for it.

Yikes, yelpers. This place is nasty. There was a fly in my salad that has been there so long it was withered and may have been decomposing.  We let the manager know and showed her the fly, she apologized and quickly dashed in attempts to not alert other patrons.   After the fly in the salad "mishap", I couldn't enjoy the rest of my lunch obvi. Then management came back to say "Hi ladies, how did you enjoy your lunch" Lol. "Um, you mean the fly you dipped in ranch for me, it was terrible". She seemed shocked and offended. I said, "Welp, you asked!" No attempts in reducing the price, just quickly dashed. Stay away!

This place isn't half bad as far as local bars go, but the tourists kind of ruin it so make sure you get there at a descent time. The roof top bar is really nice. The staff is friendly. Overall not a bad spot if you're looking get some drinks and make friends with strangers

Small diner type feel with nice staff. The food is par at best. I consider this a greasy spoon type restaurant where the plates are greasy and done fast. Prices are ok but I have had better breakfast throughout Clearwater.
The house gumbo is just astonishingly good, as was the eggplant with Creole sauce. The jambalaya with fried catfish was dry and flavorless, though. Advice: go for appetizers.

Certainly one of the most amazing Middle Eastern cuisines I've ever been to in my life. The place is well-rounded from every aspect, the food is incredibly amazing with all the Middle Eastern spices / tastes in all the different menu items I tried. They have delicious mana2eesh, incredible kofta and very yummy hummus with lamb meat. The interior is very intelligently designed, combining both Middle Eastern classic ancient designs blending perfectly with modernization. I guarantee you will never regret being there.

Stopped by for drink and basically greeted by 3 hipster bartenders who made me wait 5 minutes to order at the empty bar, ordered a lite beer and after that was completely ignored until I waved down a bartender after another 5 minutes, could be gay bar which is fine, just don't treat straight customers badly.

I was so excited a little over a year ago when I joined this gym.  I usually go around 4 days per week depending on how busy I am.  
Things they do right:
-Hiring great spinning instructors (Carl, Steve, Diana.. amazing instructors and I can't say enough good things!)
Things they can't seem to figure out:
-That having a DJ and handing me a beer at the gym after my workout is absolutely obnoxious and exactly the opposite of promoting health and wellness
-Never having clean towels ready 
-The employees.   Dear lord - I can't even begin to describe how rude 90% of the employees are.   Absolutely downright disrespectful.  I'd like to personally thank Harly for being the rudest gym employee to date.
-The most disgusting locker room .. I couldn't even joke about showering here. (Spring Garden only).

And the biggest #1 reason to avoid this gym would be...
THEY HAVE HIDDEN FEE AFTER HIDDEN FEE in your membership.   Oh - and GOOD LUCK CANCELLING - if they made it any harder it wouldn't even be legal.  I can't wait to disassociate from this place!

My husband and I live in the area and we decided to try the Affton Diner.  It took a while to get seated.  We ordered our breakfast (pancakes for him and eggs and sausage for me).  The portions were huge and the taste was average.  

Throughout the entire meal we could hear the cook yelling at the other workers.  It made for an uncomfortable experience.  We did figure out later that the cook is the owner which makes the behavior even worse.  

I doubt I will go back.

Pretty good food. I'm not a huge fan of the whole standing in line and ordering every ingredient of my meal but I figured I'd try it! I got 2 drunken yardbird tacos and a side of chips and queso. I thought it was a little pricey-- $13 for everything with a drink. They do give you a huge portion of chips and queso  though, I'd need another person to actually finish them! Moe's still has better queso

My sister and I stayed here for a night so that we could attend a concert.  The location was close to the subway which was nice since we were able to ride the subway to and from the concert.  The room was clean and my sister enjoyed the cookie that was given to her when she checked in which is a nice touch I've received at other double trees.  The only complaint I really had was that the AC would get really cold and then seem like it shut off and we would be sweating in the middle of the night and then freezing again once it kicked back on.

I recently ordered the pork chops and was very disappointed with the meal.  There was more fat on the plate than meat.  The flavor was fine, but not very appetizing with all the fat left on the meat.  
My wife ordered a veggie pita and not much flavor.  
We were there a few weeks earlier and ordered the lamb kebob dinner and thought it was too spicy and just didn't like the flavor.
I'm not sure if we'll go back, but running out of Greek places in the area.

I have been here 3 different times.  The first visit (underarm). This visit was complimentary and my esthetician was Gwen. Why didn't anyone warn me?!?!.  I wasn't ready!!  The first rip...Oh...Lordt the pain was unbearable, but I was satisfied with her high attention to detail and perfectionism. She was thorough and efficient, making sure she got every single hair.

Second visit, (chin and upper lip). I believe her name was Celeste. She wasn't exactly warm and receptive, but rather matter-of-fact and about her business.She was thorough, detail oriented and efficient. She definitely knew her stuff and I was out in 15 minutes.  I think it was her last day or last week at this location before she moved on to a different location. 

Third visit (side burns). I believe I had Jenny.  She was warm, receptive, and very friendly. She was efficient and had me out in 15 minutes.  

Overall, I had a pretty good experience and I would definitely go back. The prices are reasonable and the attentiveness and attention to detail is bar none (I can only speak on the ladies who waxed me). The only suggestion I have for this location would be to improve their customer service/receptionist.  There were too many times where my appointment was scheduled for the wrong time/day, my name/appt couldn't be found in the system, and I was put on obscene hold times.

Portabello is my favorite restaurant in the Delaware County period. Also my father's favorite restaurant in the Delaware County.The foods consistently good/great and getting what you want is possible even if it is not on the menu. Not cheap but I will pay more happily if I can get my money's worth. BYOB but beer is on the next corner and the wine store is very close by. 
I will continue to eat there as often as I can!

3.5 stars! Good place with decent food. We ordered the chorizo arepa (which was very good) and the reina pepeada (avocado, chicken and mayo). The second one had way too much mayo. It would have tasted better with less mayo. We also ordered the chicken soup which was good. Service was ok but lady at the counter was not very friendly. We would come back and try other items.  The place was full and had people coming in and out throughout the time we were there.

My sweet husband and I ate at Village Inn this morning and we've been ill since lunchtime. Food poisoning for sure. And it's a sick so bad that even pepto-bismol is ineffective.  I think village inn is off the list....eat here at your own risk.

What a stupendous place! Coffee was great, service was friendly, and the food was spectacular! The chef is talented far beyond the ordinary looks of this place. The plating/presentation shows a dedication to food and attention to detail normally reserved for fine dining establishments. Don't miss this gem!

This place gives me what I need when I stay around this area - clean rooms, hot coffee in the morning, friendly enough staff.  The lobby seems awkward to me, but it's not the kind of hotel where you're hanging out in the lobby.  The workout room stinks, but I use that as an excuse to not use it, so it's not really a big negative.

Love Soho Cycling! Your website is fantastic, easy and quick to secure a bike with my favorite instructor Susan! Susan's playlist is always perfect, and she runs a fun and motivated class! I always look forward to spinning with her, I come away energized and happy!

Great place for fresh seafood and views of the pacific. Very small so be patient and make sure to write your name on the list just outside. Able to meet other diners since you are sitting at the same table that goes along the windows being able to take in the views or you can get one of the few tables outside. Go for the crab!  Clam chowder is tasty. Very fun atmosphere.

THANK YOU to Reno's South Valleys Library for hosting my 2017 SOLO art show " the mountains are calling and I must go."..j. Muir....14 of my contemporary oil paintings done "en pleinair' ..aka outdoors!  September 1st thru October 30,2017..
...This local library is a great gift to our community.   I've enjoyed working with Kathy Berndt and her staff who are always  helpful and caring.... A beautiful architectural  gem with beauties inside...a GOLDEN GIFT  to all who visit... appreciatively, Carol Grigus....artist!

I drive by this restaurant all the time and didn't realize it was new from the previous Teriyaki Restaurant until I saw the reviews on Yelp.  I thought, 5 stars seems high for a local bistro -- guess what, it is absolutely famulous.  No 5 because I reserve those for truly expectional dining experiences, so 4.5!
We ordered take-out Saturday afternoon after deciding not to go out for dinner downtown.  We ordered a number of menu items to get a feel for the variety and quality of the food.  The tacos, chicken teriyaki, spicy chicken bowl and soup/salad were all outstanding.  Friendly and courteous service was on point.  Yahoo! - we have one more great place to eat in Brentwood.

A nice little place in the FQ to stop in for a drink and a quick bite. You can't go wrong ordering the duck potstickers or the crab cake appetizers. Skip their "romain salad", the lettuce is not romaine, and take a pass on their gumbo, the shrimp are the smallest I've seen. Whatever you do, order their bread pudding, the best I've tasted in New Orleans.

Looks like Edwardo's is now closed.   We went by Wed - July 29th at 1:30 in afternoon and it was closed with paper covering the windows.   So sorry to see it.   Food was excellent.  Hopefully they will open in new location.

The service always seems to be slow or in different. The hostess was by the kitchen to keep warm
She asked if we wanted to sit at the bar, even though we said to seat us away from the door. 
While sitting, 4 tables were left dirty for 10-15 minutes by the time we left. 
The food was just placed on the table even though one person has a food allergy 
I've been to all of the Bailey concepts were great service 
Not sure if we will return

Ended up here on a whim. A waiter was outside and suggested we come in for some samples of what they have to offer. We did, and everything was really wonderful. If I didn't live so far away, I'd be back. The owner and waitstaff were very kind, and the food was delicious!

Slow, the food was so so. The gumbo was actually bad. I thought the fried shrimp were good but by the time they came to the table all i wanted to do was get the hell out of there. For the price we paid i expected far better which is why i left a one star.

Atmosphere was a little touristy vs a beach feel. Chicken plate was good. The grouper was a bit fishy but the sauce was tasty. Waitress was friendly and on time. Good but not great on the experience. The fish tanks were super!!

Very good place to eat! My wife and I had never tried Thai food before. After leaving the family video store we decided to give it a try. That was 3 years ago, we have been going there every since then. We have never had a bad meal out of this place and the workers are really great. It should be on everyone's list to go try.

One of the best parts about Mad Dogs is that they're open late.  So if you're out partying on State Street and you need a quite bite to eat, this is the perfect place.  I tried the chicken hot dog with cilantro and lime and it was SO TASTY, probably one of the best hot dogs I've ever had.  The dogs are a little pricy, but if you're hungry and don't want to eat at a sit down place and wait for your food, this is great late night spot to hit.

Looking  for a reasonable place to grab a small bite. Tried this place out. Got the special of the day. French onion soup. Oh my gosh! Soooo good!!! Cheesy melted goodness on top. Delish onions and wine infused soup underneath. Oh man!! My sister got the steak egg rolls served with sirrache sauce.  My daughter got the baked bri. The crust was light and flakey. The raspberry sauce sweet and gorgeous. 
Loved the soft and easy mix of music. Quiet and perfect for a bit a respite on a cold rainy day.
Great service! Conch fritters were delicious! Will visit when in town again! Beautiful view of the bay.
Good, but overpriced and portions are small.  Recommend Thip's if you are willing to drive a few miles away.

If you ask locals where to go for BBQ, this is what they'll all say.  Some even claim the hamburger is the best in town (although I think that's a stretch).  This is a quaint little dive that is almost always packed.  The servers are all hard working local gals who know the menu inside and out.  If you're looking for a country style meat and three with a lot of local character, this is the place.

A few warnings; there is no alcohol, so if you're dreaming of a beer with your pork sandwich, you're out of luck.  Also, they do not accept credit cards.  Remarkably, if you don't have cash on you, they'll give you an IOU.  This is that kind of place-they won't take your plastic but they'll let you return tomorrow and pay.  

They also have a robust take out business.  Put this on your list if you're driving through town or live nearby.

No offense to anyone but the curse of the inability for NOLA to have really good BBQ has reared its ugly head here again. Good portions and the sides were tasty but sides aren't really what people come to a BBQ place for. The ribs were tough with a distinct over charred flavor. The brisket had a good smoke flavor but maybe it had been cut too early because it was dry. No complaints on the sausage though. Sorry guys....I really wanted to like it.  I know they are new so I'll try again and keep my fingers crossed.

I stop in here occasionally and enjoy seeing what they have in stock. Some of their clothes for children are fun, and they have a good supply of clothes and bedding. They sometimes have 50% off sales, which is a good time to shop there. Other times their things are over-priced, especially their home goods and strollers, baby swings, etc. They would benefit from lowering their prices.

Number of issues with this hotel. First, it reeks of cigarettes when you walk in. The staff does not seem to care or greet you in any way. They sent us to a dirty room at first before having to be assigned a clean room. The "clean room" smelled of musty carpet deodorizer and the cable did not work. There were oily handprints all over the head boards and the lamps. The shower had hair balls in it and the floor tile had mold and soap scum in the grout. Needless to say, you should pay the extra $10 and get a hotel somewhere else!!!!

Wanted to love this place as we just moved from Portland and the Flying Pies are AMAZING. Totally different pizza and ingredients, this one was meh. Service was extremely slow but they were busy. Ordered breadsticks and waited 30 min, never came. Pizza took a bit longer. The Portland locations have amazing sausage with LOTS of it on the pizzas. This was very sparse and crust is totally differen,t being just ok. Will try the Fairview location but if you are expecting the best pizza like the Oregon locations have, dont.
I order to go tacos and they forgot the cheese. The manager wanted me to come back to the restaurant and I could not. Worst customer service. Won't be back!

The food here is delicious!  I just couldn't choose between the dishes so I got two.  I had an order of pancakes and a full omelet (which comes with pancakes).  Don't judge, I just ran a half marathon the day before.    The line was long to get in amounting to about an hour wait, but that was likely because the town was full of hungry runners.  The wait was worth it.

I'm definitely going back when I'm in Nashville again.

Not bad but not great. We arrived around 6 and went to the roof top. We were wanting a table outside and the waitress was pretty rude about letting us know where we could not sit. Funny thing is that when we left an hour later it was still empty. Not a great start Blake. Let's break it down:

Atmosphere 3 stars - nothing special about the interior or rooftop. The downstairs area has a nice stage but the entire restaurant has a commercial feel to it. I considered it average for Broadway. 

Service 4 Stars - our waitress was very pleasant. She was helpful and attentive. No issue here. 

Food 4 stars - it's bar food but pretty darn good. I consider it above average. I had the trio sliders. The pork was very tasty, the bologna sandwich (yes they still make these) a we really good and clever. Lastly, the hamburger was solid. My wife had the pimento cheese wrapped in mozzarella. Really well done. 

Value 3 Stars - for basically two appetizers and four beers we left with a $60 bill. Alittle high for what you get but considering it is in the heart of broadway, probably pretty typical. 

All in all, it was ok. I would give it 3.5 but yelp won't allow me to do that. It's definitely slightly above average and I would come back.
Our order was made quickly.  Pizza was good and hot when picked up, but I'm just not that big of a Domino's fan, therefore the 3 stars were given.
Best chile relleno I've had!! Specialty drinks a MUST! Very relaxing and excellent service. Definitely going back.
