Gross. The restaurant is dirty, and tables were allowed to sit forever with used trays and half-eaten food on them. The service was slow and it wasn't that crowded. I ordered a shrimp platter, an order of mozzarella sticks, and a root beer, which came up to $16. Steep!

My mozzarella sticks tasted awful--wayyy too salty, first of all, and they were just frozen sticks out of a box. There were five of them, so I paid a dollar a stick for frozen crap that was too salty to even eat. I ate one and ended up tossing the rest.

The shrimp were likewise cooked out of a box of frozen junk, and somehow they had managed to overcook them so they were kind of hard. The shrimp inside were super-small and it was mostly breading. Five shrimp came with soggy, mediocre fries, some bread, a small side salad, and cole slaw. I ate like six fries and by that time I had given up on my meal, so I can't report on the slaw, salad, or bread.
My can of soda was not even very cold, so they managed to screw that one up, too.

This place charges way too much to be serving such crappy food. From the dilapidated atmosphere, it is clear that no care or pride really goes into this restaurant. I'll certainly never be back.

We are here for a four day anniversary get away and I'm compelled to say that so far 1 day in and totally unimpressed. 50% of the staff is rude and unfriendly (thank you to the other 50%). Manicure and pedicure was OK but overpriced for the services and salon definitely needs an overhaul. The nail polish and gel selections were so small as well.  The place all in all is run down, shabby., smells of mold and definitely in need of some upgrades. The all inclusive has hidden costs that I didn't become aware of until I booked the services and only because I asked.  The booking process was long and it took me a few tries to reach them to book the services. I wasn't made aware of the fact that the Grille is under renovations so meals are served in a room that has the mood of a retirement home (this matters when you've purchased an all inclusive and your on a romantic getaway). If I had to keep it positive: the burger at the pool bar was delish, the beds are comfortable and some of the staff are really nice. I will have an overall picture by the end of the weekend.
Finally got to check out Melt, and it certainly did not disappoint! We got our food quickly, everything was hot and fresh, and everything was so, so good! I'll definitely be back!

Co-workers and I have been going to the lunch buffet once every month or two for years and love it!  Now, I'm not too well versed in Indian food, so don't have much to go on.  But, I am an experienced "eater", if you will, and this place has great eats!  Favs are the naan, chicken tikka masala and sagg paneer (equates to spiced creamed spinach in my book).  Also love the mango yogurt drink and milk tea.  I scoffed at the idea of a buffet at first, but this one is worth your while. It's a great way to try a lot of different types of Indian food without emptying your pocketbook or ordering something that you wish you had only sampled before committing. It's very busy here at lunch during the week- the service on plate clearings, water, and keeping the buffet well stocked is great.

This guy loves food....and cares
I might try this place again I think
This guy might have some good ideas
We will see....

Dude. 

I cannot believe we finally have a legit Greek restaurant in Nashville AND they have Heineken on draft. Like. Seriously. Two of my favorite things. 

The tzatziki sauce was everything it should be, rich, garlicky and not watered down. So freaking delicious. The fries were savory, my salad was delicious and fresh, my husbands lamb was awesome. But omg, draft Heineken!!!!! I'm half Dutch and haven't found one place in Nashville with draft Heineken (drinking it out of the bottle is just not the same) 

This place is a win win win! Cheap and absolutely fantastic. Yay! We will be back again and again!!!
The best bbq in middle Tennessee hands down. Better then anything you will find in Nashville it you are in the area you have to eat here.

2014 canfest what more than you can ask for over 100 beers with some micro breweries what I was most excited about was the breweries that I used to go to when I lived in  A.Z. Four Praks brewery, San Tan brewery.

Higher prices, yes.  Surly staff, probably.  Poor selection... I have to quibble with that one.  It's not the selection that's bad, it's the quality of what's available that's bad.  The last time I was there, I think I literally picked over twenty jalapenos before selecting three that seemed like they were in at least marginally acceptable condition.  But hey, at least they HAVE jalapenos.  This may be my fault for being from California, but if I can't get jalapenos, serranos, and anaheims in good condition in the same place... it's almost too much to bear.

Anyway, as a car-less shopper, this place has saved my poor-planning ass more than once.  If I need molasses, I know they have it.  If I want brussels sprouts, my odds of finding them here (questionable condition notwithstanding...) are better than any other place within a four block radius.  Sometimes, when it's 15 degrees out, that's just enough.  Tack on the additional half-star for carrying my beloved Method home cleaning products and I have a solid three-star experience.

Came with a friend for pedicures. Her pedicure came out great! her person was friendly and did a good job. They DONT offer gel pedicures. Which is what I normally get but it wasn't a big deal so I went ahead and chose regular polish. Here's where everything turns for the worst. Now came the time to get my pedicure, everything was going well in the beginning. We got through the massage and paint job and I looked over my feet and was very unsatisfied. I spoke with a short balding man about my concerns which was the dead skin that was still left on my feet and the horrible paint job. He suggested that he'd repaint and remove the dead skin for me. I told him to just remove the polish so that I could just go to my regular nail shop. He removes the polish and some of the dead skin. And proceeds to try and charge me full price as I am still unsatisfied. He was very rude and went over to other customers to MOCK me as I was still standing there. I remained calm and polite and asked to speak to someone else. So I spoke to the manager who offered me a discount and to repaint them for me. They both said I was lying because the lady "never gets complaints and they know that she's good" Meanwhile the rude man went upstairs to mock me some more with his colleagues. I do not recommend this place. HORRIBLE CUSTOMER SERVICE!

I loved loved loved this place. This is upscale, modern, Mexican with a twist of innovation, creative dishes, and expert preparation. Service was impeccable. The sangria was the best I've ever had anywhere. The appetizers guacamole, some type of taquito, and plantains were scrumptious. The steak dish was perfect and not too spicy.  The tres leche cake was out of this world delicious. Can't wait to come back. It wasn't too busy so I hope the place is making out ok, it's just terrific.

My boss had recommended this place for a nice dinner spot. I made a reservation for my fiance's birthday, but was still a little unsure of what to expect (mostly just b/c I had never heard of this place before). 

Needless to say, any concern I had was immediately wiped away after walking in. The atmosphere was amazing. Rather than one large dining room broken up, there are several small rooms with tables, each having it's own unique decor. Our server was amazingly friendly and helpful. Her recommendations were spot on. They have an amazing baked brie appetizer... I highly recommend it. It was so good I got it to go for Valentine's Day a few weeks ago. Our main courses were also delicious. 

Overall, I couldn't recommend this place more. Admittedly, it's a little pricey for a random night out, but well worth it when you do go.

Excellent, back to original standards. Roti Canai, Nasi Lemak, fish fried rice and golden fried squid a must. All about service as well and Indra is one of the best servers we have encountered on our numerous visits here, as usually this is what they lack the most with rather rude and unfriendly servers.

Arrived early at 10:30AM and found the best parking spot possible.  Right near the arts and crafts and not smashed between any other cars.  I was planning for a loooong walk, but luckily was less than a block away.

We hit up the Arts and Crafts first and I was impressed by the selection.  Lots of snacks (nuts, popcorn, sauces, candy, etc.), clothing, toys, decorations, etc.  I ended up buying a dutch oven pot, Angry Bird keychains and popcorn.  I could have gone crazy, but I resisted the urge!

We ate at the Checkered Pig first and had the Rib Sampler and 1/2 a dozen of Hush Puppies.  Loooove the sauce!  Great taste and doesn't taste store bought like some of the other ones did.  I'm actually planning on going back to buy the sauce.  And the Hush Puppies ... what can I say?  Pretty good flavor, but really though ... how can you go wrong with Hush Puppies?!

We also stopped by the Carson City rib booth and tried their Rib Sampler as well as a Chicken Kabob.  I was slightly disappointed with their sauce.  The ribs were tender and chicken was cooked good, but in my opinion, I think their sauce tasted store bought.  I apologize in advance because I'm sure there's some Carson City rib lovers on here that have now put a hit out on me.

Lastly, we ended up getting Fried Mushrooms and a Strawberry Funnel Cake.  Fried Mushrooms didn't have much flavor and they were what they were.  Just battered mushrooms deep fried.  At least we tried them, but we had high hopes and were slightly disappointed.  The Strawberry Funnel Cake was super filling!  It was cooked perfectly ... it was fresh and just crunchy enough.  

We also scored some "official gear" for this cook off with a mens t-shirt, pig beaded necklace and a rib cook offf pin.  We drove to Reno for this event, might as well remember it!

Overall, we loooved this festival.  Everyone would always talk about it and we fiiinally made it out.  I'm pretty impressed and now would like to see what the next years cook off will bring.  On that note, we're going back tomorrow to hit up some other booths we wanted to try but had no room in our bellys.

Helpful tip:  Bring an umbrella for shade when you walk/wait in lines and a chair to sit on.  Seating seemed to be very limited so racing for a seat once someone gets up is never fun.  Ribs and sides are hard to eat!  I'm surprised they didn't offer more tables/chairs.  That's the only downside.  Free event = can't complain.

This place is great! It's gotten me through my first semester of medical school. It's relatively quiet, depending on when you go. No tweens hanging around like in Starbucks down the street, and the table options are awesome. I rotate btwn high stools (with backs), regular tables and comfy sofa chairs.. (and im pregnant so im picky).  The 10 minimum sucks but if you buy yourself a gift card and are a frequent user, it's not an issue. The baked goods and soups are kind of lacking, but they make up for it in tea selection and hospitality. 

Overall-big fan.

I think enough has been said about the quality of their baked goods; I couldn't agree more! What I would like to add to that is some praise on their great customer service.  Whether ordering in person or online, these folks are the pinnacle in customer satisfaction.

Can I give this place 10 stars? The food, the service and the vibe are spot on.
Chef Jason and his crew really shine in this fresh StPete stand out. We started with the tuna tartare and the shrimp ajillo over white beans, then moved on to the black cod, oxtail with house made ravioli, and the grouper fresh catch. All were executed perfectly and devoured quickly. Our service was efficient and well timed. Nice selection of reasonably priced wine, and local brews. My only gripe... change from paper to linen napkins. :)   I simply cannot wait to return, and to spread the word about this real-deal eatery.  Bravo!

Great oyster but everything else was just meh. Below average BBQ shrimp (shrimp was way over cooked and sauce was bland). Extremely slow service. I had a feeling that I got a bit rick rolled by reviews on this one. Will not try again.

Really enjoyed Sierra Rose Sushi. Service was speedy and friendly. They were swamped but still took good care of us. I liked everything that we tried. The Hamachi was amazing. Quail egg shooters were also very tasty. We will definitely return.

Stopped in here for dinner while visiting Philly with some friends. Decent prices and tasty kabobs (I had the chicken). Between the kabobs, rice, bread and the potato scallion pancake app we split, everyone left sufficiently full. The place was not really packed when we were there but we were having a later dinner so maybe missed the dinner rush. It was nice to be able to sit and take out time with the meal, and we stayed for a while after chatting away without feeling rushed out the door the second we finished out plates. If I lived in the area I could definitely see this place becoming one of my regular spots.

Formerly Cadillac Ranch, this place preserves much of the country atmosphere and decor with the conspicuous absence of the mechanical bull.  But if you want a mechanical bull, you can drive to the Sparks Nugget soon and go to Gilley's.  The place is as huge as it was before including a patio area that will be nice when the weather improves.  Excellent service.  The chicken wings are awesome and fresh and succulent and they have extra BBQ in bottles (sweet, spicy, and a South Carolina style mustard sauce).  The bottles kinda reminded me of the old Tony Roma's at Sands a long time ago.  The tap didn't have any regional indie beers, the liquors are mostly corporate.  The BBQ ribs start off about $15 for a half-rack of beef ribs and $18 for pork baby back.  I would have liked to see a sampler or something or a larger appetizer list.  Good start though.  No country line dancing but they'll have live bands.

I went on a Sunday morning with my wife and daughter.  Place was busy. Wait was only 10 minutes so not bad.  You had better hope you get a booth.  We were sat at an undersized table which barely had enough room for the food.  It was so crowded I was hit 2 times by the tub the busboy was carrying.  I can tell how the crowd is turned over so quick.  The bulk of the food is prepared ahead of time.  The wife had waffles and bacon.  Waffles were good but bacon had been sitting for a while.  I had eggs benedict.  Home fries were good.  Eggs done nicely. English muffins hadn't been thoroughly cooked.  The sauce was a whole different story.  Absolutely horrible.  Looked like someone had melted butter and thrown some spice in it. One plus is the wait staff was friendly. I left my tip on the table and when paying the check I was asked if I was leaving a tip on the card. I said no and got a dirty look and snide remark. had read the reviews on here and my wife had been there before.  We will not be back.

BEST cheesesteaks around this town hands down. Why? Because of the fresh baked seeded roll baked right next door (connected to a bakery) with flavorful meat and cheese. This is my go to place for cheesesteaks around here (different story if you're in willow grove check out the steak and hoagie factory). More often than not, I can't get them since they close early (9 pm). Definitely check this place out and if you happen to go there, pick up some bread for the house. You won't regret it. Oh and they also have a deli meat counter (limited selection).

In terms of food, it's the Waffle House and exactly what you'd expect. In terms of service, staff, and overall customer satisfaction, my expectations were blown away. While passing through on a road trip to Florida I stopped here for breakfast. Upon leaving my car broke down and was stuck in their parking lot for the next several hours. Everyone working at this location was more than eager to lend a helping hand and go above and beyond to make sure I was ok. Stop here for a bite to eat and you'll leave with not only a full stomach, but your faith restored in humanity.

I've had the luxury of traveling all over this World and I've been to some really great places and I find it so interesting that I can't find anything as good as what's in my own back yard . F&T Longley is an outstanding example of what a pub should be like . Upon walking through the front door you'll be greeted with a friendly hello , fast friendly service , consistently good food and a guaranteed good time . The staff is wonderful , they all have great attitudes , they are very friendly and Johnny on the spot with their service . Kevin and Andrea are fun , engaging bartenders and their wait staff is over the top . My servers name was Amber and she was a rock star , first class all the way . Put this place on your speed dial ....you will not be disappointed !

I gotta say I was rather disappointed by our recent experience here. My sister was really looking forward to trying the T&T sandwich but they were out of tongue. Instead she ordered the regular tripe sandwich and it was quite bland. I tried some as well, and had to agreed it was bland. I ordered a cheesesteak and that was also a little bland, I think it would have been better if there was more cheese and grilled onions. Also they put the ketchup on top, instead of on the inside of the sandwich which made it really messy to eat, so If  I ever go again I would ask them to put it inside the sandwich. Staff were really friendly there and everything smelled really good.
The bbq beans were very delicious. The Tri-Pi with the chimichurri was seasoned well.

I want to take these dirty diaper burritos and rub them on my naked body. They remind me of a giant fly larva and if I could eat them everyday I would do so. PS you can scan old receipts and email them to corporate in order to get points toward your free burrito. Ill let u do what you want with that information. Gangsta!

I drive 20+ minutes just to come here! This is by far the best nail salon I've visited. I always get a gel manicure every 2-3 weeks because it lasts so well. Customer service is great, manicure always lasts forever, and they have such a great selection!

We had booked two tours, with two different companies for today. One earlier in the day and one night tour. The Voodoo one was the first one with New Orleans Secrets and that one was great! We got to go into a voodoo museum and temple among other places, the information was rich with voodoo religion and history and the tour guide was very personable. 

Then we had this tour...The Voodoo bone lady tours-
5 in 1 haunted tour. The guide Brian was a great guide so nothing wrong there but the tour itself was just ok if not slightly boring. Lots of information and haunted history but nothing all that interesting honestly. The stories we mostly boring and you lose some of the interest because your constantly being shuffled around due to other tours moving about. Tour guides have to scream just to tell the stories. I suppose we expected more from this tour with all the great reviews. If you're into walking and listening to somewhat boring haunted history that you could very well just look up online, then this might be good for you. Otherwise skip it and find something else to do like the tour we went on earlier today where you can actually go inside places. 
We actually left the 5 in 1 tour half way though because of the boredom.
This place is HORRIBLE.  1 cashier during winter break? Great planning management.... I have already been waiting in like for 25 MINUTES!!!

Me and husband went there to have dinner expecting to just have a normal dinner it was completely horrible service was terrible didn't even leave her a tip how bad she was the Appetizers came raw and cold and the stakes was over cooked and my  knife couldn't even go to my potato the worst part was the Manager didn't even care he was completely rude and horrible he said nothing and just left I'll never go back there again

DONT GO!!
I cracked my phone screen and ever since I got it fixed here, it hasn't been working the same. It glitches, and doesn't respond to my touch signals at times. I looked up my issue and it is called the touch disease. I asked a friend about who also fixes phones and he told me it sounds like there could be potential stolen parts because a lot of phone stores in philly steal parts. My dumb ass went back after cracking my phone again, hoping it was just a bad application. Wrong. I went there 2 more times explaining the problem. One day I was there and wasn't addressed for a half hour, just to be told afterwards that I should come back 3 days later when the manager was there. I came back, and convincing them it was something wrong with my phone, was a hassle. It was only glitching slightly the first half hour was there. But after that it started glitching like crazy. The worker had the nerve to tell me "wait 10 minutes it'll go away". BUT IVE BEEN IN AND OUT THE STORE FOR THE PAST WEEK TRYING TO FIX THE EXACT PROBLEM. Come on!The manager changed my screen for free, however, the long term damage was done. My phone was still not usable. My phone didn't do this before coming here, even when it was cracked. I now have a new phone and I will never go back.

Their screens maybe cheap but they are cheap for a reason. I go to Philly Wireless. Customer service is exceptional. They have a front and back screen protector with option of color & design for the same price this place has for a cheap, minimal protection, front only, screen saver. Philly wireless told me they were probably using bad screens. I'm not going to assume but I know I won't be back.

I don't usually go to Sonic. I'm not sure why, but I never think about it. It's currently nothing but snow and ice on the ground and Sonic is one of the few places open (along with my place of employment). I stopped buy for some breakfast and was happy to use the drive thru. One of the reasons I never think of Sonic is I don't like when they come out to your car. I find it awkward. I'm weird, I know this.

I ordered the breakfast burrito combo, with bacon. It comes with tater tots and a drink. I'm a sucker for a strawberry limeade. It was 5ish dollars, which seems a lot, but the burrito is huge. I was surprised to find actual bacon strips inside. A lot of places use that chopped up bacon in the breakfast burritos that taste like Bacon Bits for salads (Taco Bell, I'm looking at you). Hot eggs, cheese and fresh bacon in a burrito, along with hot tots?! I need to not make this an everyday thing or I'll be 350 pounds.

Santa Barbara: if you build it on the beach, they will come. They definitely built East Beach Grill on the beach, and -- especially on holidays -- people come. If you've got a thing for great expanses of water and sand, I can imagine no finer location for a restaurant, although this particular place combines their much-coveted location with a slightly harsh, utilitarian, almost food-service feel: plastic chairs and tables, ketchup splurted out of dispensers, order numbers constantly barked through a muddy P.A. system.

This makes The Habit look like The French Laundry, especially on crowded days when it feels like civilization might well come to an end then and there. But during quiet times, I've actually enjoyed this place; I think I want to come back soon some weekend morning, taking brief bike ride or longish stroll from downtown and grabbing a simple breakfast. I've enjoyed a fruit-and-yogurt bowl here, their fries taste well-seasoned, and their burritos look decent, given a context that really doesn't lead you to expect a decent burrito.

Word on the street says that East Beach Grill's real strength lies in its fruit pancakes, and I'll return for them, but man, a lot of those burgers and related sandwiches remind me of my junior high's cafeteria. I have a feeling that if I asked what the deal is with this, I'd get little more than a complacent shrug in return, like, "What do you want? We're on the beach" -- the very same attitude afflicts the rest of Santa Barbara, too.

Stopped here for a happy hour on a Saturday night and the bar was completely dead. I was the only one there from the hours of about 6 to 8:30, until another couple joined me. I'm not sure why it wasn't more crowded. The beer selection was small, but they had plenty of wines and an entire list full of Tequila to choose from. I didn't order any food, but had I been hungrier, there looked to be plenty of options from the menu I could pick from. It was clean inside and the bartender was pretty friendly. She put on a football game for me and checked back on me regularly. A manager was present, who also checked in on me during the stay. Everything was decently priced, as well. I'd definitely stop back for a drink or two. The only downfall would be, as I already mentioned, the small beer selection.

Great food amazing atmosphere! Absolutely loved this place. The menu isn't very long but everything on it is delicious. The price was very reasonable as well. It feels like it should be pricey but it isn't. It's more of a restaurant than a cafe. The entrance is a little hard to find but that's to ensure the privacy of everyone sitting outside.

Relaxing w/ Simple and Buttery Country Style.

This is a great place to eat if you are looking for a Country Style-made place with family and friends. Its casual, calm, and simple. There is a lot of butter going on, but just how a country style should be, and is perfect the way it is. I usually get steak and corn on the side when I am there because once I walk into the restaurant the steaks (medium well) are seriously calling my name. Its incredibly mouth-watering, and juicy with some A1 sauce! 

The place is not loud, even with little kids. I never had to wait for a seat. The service is great, and people there are really mellow. Never heard any customers complain,  always walking out happy and plumped.
Great service, great food and great bar. I found the French 75 to be a great brunch drink similar to that of a Bloody Mary or mamosa, although totally different.

Had dinner with a friend here, before going out shopping.  

The service was quick, efficient and friendly. I ordered a pick two of French Onion Soup and a 1/2 salad.  I asked for extra croutons and dressing on the side. My requests were easily made and cheerfully done.  My friend ordered a special sandwich on white bread.  They did that for her as well. We were quite pleased.
Soooo good. If you want amazing street tacos and AC this is the place to go. Good for lunch.

I love this place. Close to where I live, the people who work here are nice and does a good job with the services: manicure, pedicure and waxing. The nail polish they put on stays ridiculously long which I liked. Very satisfactory and affordable!  I love their massage chair too while getting my nails done. :)

The Budweiser campus is really quite spectacular. My 10 year old daughter enjoyed the Bud Light tour immensely with all of the extra details pointed out by our wonderful tour guide. She even got to stand with a Clydesdale for a picture. : ) There is walking inside and out of buildings but very doable. There was lots to see and learn! Buy tickets in advance; when we arrived lots of times were sold out.

Amazing brunch! Got the make your own sweet brunch this morning and it absolutely hit the spot, challah french toast topped with chocolate chips and a side of whipcream. French toast was cooked perfectly and the chocolate chips came out melted and perfect. Prices are great and parking is always easy to find before heading out to browse Jenkintown's shops.
Great food! Our server Nicole suggested club sandwich and we loved it! She was very attentive and personable! Make sure you ask for her,when you go there! We will be back!
One of my favorite spots in Nashville for brunch!! Their coffee is incredible also. So many options on the menu to try... will definitely have to come back to try more!

This French Press location has the killer combo of sleek atmosphere and delicious coffee which never fails to impress me. 

I think it's worth starting with the atmosphere: I remember going for the first time to their State St shop and being seriously impressed by the coffee... and equally disappointed by the lackluster decoration. But not here: the building looks like a futuristic gas station (which, had they one of those chalkboards things outside, would likely empower them to make "fuel" puns for days). On a nice day (most days here), the sunshine comes pouring in. 

More importantly, their coffee is great. I've been to both Handlebar & the Santa Barbara Roasting Company and I have to say this was my fave. Their cappuccino was not too foamy and instead really layered the milk in top of the espresso shot, providing a cool contrast between the two. Somehow it felt more suited to the hot weather while simultaneously being tastier than the competition (but, you know, that's only my personal opinion). 

It's a really cool spot. Try it.
I regularly visit Thailand however I live in Spring Hill. This place makes very authentic Thai food I'm so happy they are local, very friendly bunch as well. The food is all very delicious.

Perfectly reliable and lovely little breakfast place as you drive along the Gulf Coast Highway. You put your name on the list (my guess is there's always a list), and they call your name when it's your turn. You can sit inside or outside; we enjoyed sitting outside and looking out at the water and watching the pelicans diving for fish. The breakfast is nothing surprising, but everything is done well. They know how to poach eggs; the fresh fruit is actually fresh; and the service is terrific. We would definitely come back.

The beers are endless. Many good beers on tap. They also have many beers in a walk in cooler.
Lots of indoor and outdoor seating. They offer bar food.

The food is average. I ordered for my drink an horchata. To my disappointment it was made with horchata powder. Not a good sign.  I ordered the tampiquena steak and it was ok but the flavor not there. I don't consider this restaurant authentic.
Love the fresh roasted coffee!   And it's a great place to 'hang'.

Really good, really 'spensive, sriracha sauce was less than "mild." Overall, tastes like the best mozzarella sticks ever. Not actually sure why they're marketing team wishes to differentiate from sticks, other than obviously their shape. I guess mozz blobs just doesn't sound appealing.
Not good, I was expecting more for the price they charge. Don't trust this place

Solid Lee's. The employees are courteous, and the food comes out fast and hot. The bathroom was also relatively clean. Foodwise, the coleslaw was great. I also tried the spicy dippers but couldn't tell if they were spicy or not.

It's close to my office so I find myself here fairly often. The fact that you can order online and then pick up in-store is appealing.  Sometimes I just don't want to deal with people, you know? 

The best way I can describe La Madeleine's to people not from around here is that it's like Panera, but French-ier. So instead of soup you get soupe and instead of salad you order a salade. Lots of extra E's on things.  Calorie and nutritional information is available for just about everything. 

There are lunch specials which are reasonable and plenty of vegetarian options as well. Fresh baked breads and pastries (think tarts and cakes and cookies) and even a small wine selection. 

If you dine in, be sure to leave a buck or two at the table for the guy clearing away your dirty dishes.

Probably my favourite turkey burger I've ever had. So flavourful and delicious!

I'm lactose intolerant and took my lactose pills to have the milkshake. It was fantastic. I had the Nanaimo Square one. 

Left super full and very happy (with great Instagram pics to boot!)
Favorite dishes are the Grilled Asian Chicken Salad and the Grilled Chicken & Asparagus Linguini. The Sunday brunch is awesome as well with lots if choices. The Northern beer is a good choice.

Was hoping for a better experience, but I'll give them another try next time I'm in the area because I prefer to support local coffee shops. I really want to like this place.

First off, good luck finding the shop. I knew exactly where it was supposed to be based on GPS, but I overlooked the place twice due to poor signage and ended up driving around that same building twice and then wandered further around to a different section of Westhaven before finally seeing a sign for it!

I feel the drink menu (coffee and espresso) is a little limited. They do have different food options including baked goods, biscuits, and even ice cream. It was after I had ordered and paid for my mocha that I found the muffins wrapped and stored on a centerpiece server on the middle of the big table where patrons were sitting. So I went back and grabbed one and paid separately. My mocha was on par. The muffin was just not very appetizing. The service was fine, but they didn't go out of their way to smile or make you feel welcomed.

Oh yeah, my lid came off my drink twice, but fortunately it did not result in a major spill. I had trouble getting the lid to fit on my cup.

They also have tea and coffee by the bag for sale, as well as gifts.  The place is beautiful and rustic on the inside. I'm hoping next time I have a chance to stop in that I can upgrade my review.
Great location, walking distance to the beach, tucked away between Mandalay and Poinsettia Ave. Great service and manager. Great food!

This particular KFC gets one star only because I can't give it zero stars. How is it that the last three times I've been here over the last couple months there is no extra crispy chicken? YOU'RE A CHICKEN RESTAURANT! Also my container of green beans was mostly water this last time. Every time I come to this particular location it's always something and it's always disappointing and on top of that the customer service is always awful. It seems the employees are miserable and go out of their way to be rude. I kept going to this kfc because I love kfc and it's on the way home but never again. "Keyla" working the drive through window needs to learn some respect and some manners as well as some customer service.

I am hard to impress when it comes to service and food; but I can say that I was floored by the staff in this place! When I walked in I think they thought I was in a bad mood due to my contacts, but they seated me right away. Tiffany my server has been spot on amazing! A good server is a rarity in the restaurant game, and I commend her and the cooks highly with the response time to my food. I hadn't even finished making my coffee before my appetizer was in front of me. The nachos were decent, but the main thing I came for was the cheesesteak! Which again, the wait time was nonexistent. Tiffany checked up to make sure everything was okay throughout my meal, and I greatly appreciated it! I can't speak for everything on the menu, but from the things that I've had here, you really can't go wrong with any of the food...and if nothing else the coffee is exquisite!
The slowest at each stop in the drive thru. Fries soggy it was 630 they should have been fresh. Poor service. Like they had trouble counting at each stop too . Won't be back any time soon .

Our family's favorite pizza place. Our kids love it and so do we. Pizza is delicious, and their buffalo wings are awesome. This place doesn't even deliver and they are always packed, pizza must be great if everyone is willing to go pick it up  :)

Our service advisor, Katie, is fantastic. She is professional, friendly, knowledgeable and always follows up with us in a timely manner. There's also a young woman (dark haired brunette) who helped us with our loaner vehicle on 2 occasions and she is thorough, helpful, friendly and professional. I've been very impressed with the service standards and all of the staff members that I've encountered at this dealership from phone to in person. I really appreciate it.
These folks make an art of doing good and simple breakfast and lunch food exceedingly well.  It's a new fav for sure!

I came here after not having been adjusted in years--it was awesome! The doctor who saw me was even able to fix some knee pain I'd been having. Their rates are affordable and the staff is super friendly, especially their office manager, Jodie! Would definitely recommend to friends!

First, I like this museum because it's beautiful. 
And so is the art. 
So many modern art museums are based on this idea that unless something is disingenuously transgressive and ugly it isn't honest or with the "now". That is: it must exert a blunt force upon the viewer. 
Well, as Mason Cooley said: "A blunt statement can be as false as any other."

The three large gardens around this place are great. Get you in the right mood. And are worth visiting just for them. The collection ranges from African, to European, to some South Pacific art, and it goes on, it's a solid context. 

Anyway, there is much more; best to go and check it out for yourself. 
A wonderful way to spend a day and refresh the mind, spirit.

I think I've been to most of the Thai places in St. Louis, and this is my new favorite.  Their Pad Thai is the best I've had in years, maybe since I was in Thailand. 

This restaurant is owned by the same guy who owns most of the other places nearby - he owns 4 Thai restaurants in the Loop (Thai Guyang, Thai Country, Thai Cafe and Thai Pizza), plus Thai Nevis in Creve Coeur.

I think Thai Nevis actually has the best food, but it's often empty and very quiet in there, which is not a pleasant dining experience for me.  Thai Guyang, in the Loop, has pretty good food but the service is not very friendly, there's no atmosphere, and it often smells in there.  Actually, it always smells in there.

As for Thai Country Cafe... I don't know how I've lived here for 6 years and never tried this one.  The front room feels cozy and friendly.  There's a giant wagon wheel in the middle of the restaurant, which makes no sense, and the walls are lined with the most random assortment of items you could think of... garlic, golf clubs, thai carvings, teapots, tennis raquets, etc.  Strange.  But the food and service were great.

I didn't love the green chicken curry, which is why I am giving them 4 instead of 5 stars.  It was too spicy and not sweet enough for me... and the sauce was a little too runny.  The pad thai was fantastic. I asked for some ground peanut to put on top and it was just great.  That plus a Singha Thai beer and I was very happy.

I will definitely be back!

The various Tria locations are all great, and this one - perhaps the original Tria? - is perhaps my favorite, being a bit more roomy compared to the Tria West. Seating upstairs provides a somewhat quieter area. I recommend getting in a bit early, as the place does fill up. Incredible wines and beers, as well as the food (tapas size) selections. On a recent visit, our server, Jill, confidently recommended the Avec les bons Vœux de la brasserie Dupont - she was right! I'll try to get back while they still have it. For snacks, we enjoyed the white bean spread and a cheese selection. The very attentive staff brought more bread as we worked through what was first served. On a more recent visit, the mushroom with Fontina toast was excellent, very simple, yet really satisfying. And may I say that NOT having a TV was an excellent decision by the owners.

Wonderful restaurant!! Staff is friendly and efficient and the food was absolutely amazing!! We all enjoyed our meals and wished we had time to go back again!!! Would recommend Mr. B's for anyone wanting a truly great dining experience!!!

Food = I only wish Orlando burgers were as good as the burger here. Juicy and perfectly cooked with well thought out toppings.

Atmosphere = Nothing to write home about or special in any way. But you're here for the food. 

Drinks = impressive array, but to be honest, I just got a water.

I ate at Pizza Mizza for the first time this evening and I am quite impressed. The food, while not the best I have ever had, is very good. What made the experience though was the service. I picked food up for take-out and, I believe it was the manager, who gave me the food was very friendly. If you are looking for a good meal, and superb service, Pizza Mizza is the perfect place!

Worst experience ever! My boyfriend and I  came here for a quick lunch on Sunday. The waitress didn't acknowledge us until 15 minutes later and when she finally approached us, instead of apologizing she said we were last on the list that's why she waited this long. Very very bad beginning. We ordered wraps which they were terrible, my chicken wrap had two small pieces of chicken and a lot of lettuce, so basically filled with lettuce only, gross. And the waitress brought one water, and Said "I only had one clean glass" really? Is that what you say? 
Anyways, I'm never coming back. I wonder if the owners or managers of this place look at yelp and Facebook reviews? Maybe you should train your servers to be more polite? I worked in customer service for years so when it comes to these situations I know when something is wrong. 
This was the first time I ever tip less than 20%

The original Habit is truly the best. I've tried the Habit before in LA (USC campus center), and it was the most mediocre burger I've ever had . BUT this Habit changed my perception of this chain forever. I got the Charburger with the side of Onion Rings... and it was heavenly! The onion rings are golden and crispy, but doesn't feel ridiculously greasy. Would definitely come back while I'm in SB!
It's a diner which is exactly what you want for a good, big breakfast before a long day. Seems to be where a lot of locals go which is where I like to be. Great prices for a downtown restaurant.

We really enjoyed our experience here!  The past week they expanded their hours from just lunch to dinner.  They are new, so still on the "preview" menu, but the full menu should launch soon.  This place was developed by a James Beard nominee, so I had high expectations and they didn't disappoint.  We had the handmade chips and guacamole (big serving, so be prepared).  My favorites were the chicken tikka taco and the Idaho spud potato.  My husband liked the mushroom bacon taco and the "Chef's taco" of the night, which was a meatball taco.  It was a little bit more than we are used to spending ($4-$5 per taco), but I would say that is fair for the quality that you get!   This was definitely our #1 pick of the new taco places that just opened up in town.
I had the taco salad and it was great.  Good chips and salsa.  Good staff very friendly.
You can't beat the prices and the quality is pretty good. During the daytime counter person is very pleasant and polite.

To bust up the monotony of working from home occasionally, I like to stop in local coffee shops. Not as quaint or cozy as Calvin Fletcher's, but good coffee options and friendly staff. I have been forgotten about a time or two where I've ordered a drink and had to remind the barista a while later.

Found this place using yelp and it's great! I was hoping for a nicer atmosphere but the inside is pretty much the equivalent of eating at a Zaxbys. However, the food was awesome! Spent about 20$ on 2 ppl and you get tons of food. The gyro was great and Greek salad is huge. Had enough for a leftover meal. Check it out!
Large portions of good food at reasonable prices.  Solid value.  The chocolate chip pancakes are close to perfection.

I wanted a bowl with two items. The employee explained she would be happy to assist however was concerned it would not all fit in a bowl. She offered other suggestions as well as an attempt to have a bowl with 2 sides. She cared that I got value for my money. She showed true customer service.
Decided to try something different today.   And I am glad we did.   The food was excellent.   Tammy our server , couldn't do enough for us.  We will be back

Unquestionably my favorite tea, coffee, yummy healthier options treats spot in Wesley Chapel.  The must try's are the cinnamon sugar donuts & the banana nut bread.  
The teas, coffee, and espressos are freshly made to order.

Not so impressed. Nice facilities but staff wasn't super friendly or helpful. Asked for a wake up call & didn't get one. They sent someone up to BANG on our door & try to use a key to get in... No idea it was a hotel employee thought someone drunk was at wrong room. Lots & Lots of smokers everywhere & no nonsmoking Casino area.

I booked this for my group of 13 bachelor party. The bus picked us up from our hotel and we reserved a private boat for the tour. We brought 3 coolers of alcohol with us and a couple people in my group were rowdy drunks. We were drinking on the bus and the boat but Cajun Encounters was great to my group, we had a lot of fun and everyone loved it. I highly recommend the private boat swamp tour for bachelor parties.
Nigerian food that is very delicious. Egusi soup is my favorite, spicy greens with melon seed oil

Listen, I love burgers and I've also worked in food service for a long time, including food trucks. I usually give people a pass. I know it's hard work. But the experience with this truck was terrible. The burgers are small and not anything special and very expensive. $12 each I believe. We waited 30 minutes for our food and it wasn't busy. The guy on the truck totally ignored us for quite some time. When we finally got our food the fries were cold and soggy. Not going back. 

Like I said I get it, it's rough work but not an excuse for soggy fries and a burger that looked like it was stepped on.
Extremely dissatisfied. Server kept dissapearing. You should never leave a restaurant still hungry especially after ordering the bottomless soup and salad.

I was lucky enough to try some of this cupcakes when my boyfriend brought some home after the media preview. I tried the banana and fell in love with it. It's not an overly sweet cupcake but more of a rich flavor from the banana. Well, that was a few weeks ago and tonight we stopped by the location after dinner at Taqueria Del Sol. 12 South is really and up and coming place, isn't it? 

The store is located next to Dapper James (aka Reese Witherspoon's fancy store). The Sprinkles cupcake shop has the infamous cupcake ATM. Whoever came up with this creation is marketing genius. I remember when they came out with the first one in Beverly Hills and it was on all the news sites. Now Nashville is lucky enough to have one. And the people of Nashville must love using it, because I've seen tons of Instagram/Facebook/Twitter pictures of people using it. Funny enough, when we stopped by around 8pm on a Wednesday night, there was a line of people using the ATM, taking pictures, taking selfies. At one point, the line was LONGER to use the cupcake ATM than to order from the counter inside. At it was 37 degrees outside! 

Anyway, the inside of the store is pretty small. I think this part used to be an alleyway and they made it into the Sprinkles store. I was boring and ordered the banana cupcake again. I skimmed the counters and was only seeing chocolate stuff and this might sound crazy, but I'm not a huge fan of chocolate. Of course, after we ordered I saw the strawberry and the vanilla. I will have to try those next time. My friend (who is gluten free) was with us and got the gluten free red velvet cupcake and said it was very good for gluten free, nice and moist. Phillip got the captain crunch ice cream in a waffle cone. The cone was nearly falling apart and the girl making it behind the counter asked him if he wanted a different one, but it took it anyway. It take a little time for them to pack up the cupcakes. The presentation is worthy of the $3.75 price tag. I wished the bag had a couple napkins in it, however. 

This is a great addition to the neighborhood and Nashville. I think they'll have no problems bring in business from all the foot traffic along 12 South. I also think they aren't in competition with the other cupcake places, such as Gigi's because this isn't so focused on a huge blob of icing on top. The flavors here are more simple and clean, in my opinion. I might even try out that ATM (maybe with a selfie too!).

(PS- the cupcakes are more of a value compared to the ice cream. One scoop for $3.75 is pretty funny in my opinion.)

Reed's is one of my favorite restaurants in St. Louis. I've been there for brunch and dinner. The food, cocktails, and service are consistently amazing every time I visit. 

Definitely check out the three course prixe fixe option. My friends and I usually do that and share so we can get a little taste of everything on the menu.

Come early. They sell out fast! I got here around 1030am to get wings because they're usually ready by 11am. It was packed!! I got an order of the chili garlic wings. Delicious!!! I want to come back and try the buttermilk ranch wings before I give this place a 5. Service is friendly!

My eyebrows were in dire straits, but I've been super busy and didn't have time for a wax and the post-wax redness.  My sister had been talking up threading as the way to go and when I discovered Shanti did it and was around the corner and is only $12 I was sold.  I agree with others that its not a warm and fuzzy type of place.  When I got upstairs after some trouble with the door, I was told to go to the room on the left.  I sat down, and waited a few seconds.  I informed the woman (sorry forget who it was) that I had never been threaded before, and made it clear that I just wanted my eyebrows cleaned up.  I had to hold my hands in kind of awkward positions as she did it.  I think it was a little more painful than waxing, but it was super quick.  My brows seem a little thinner than I normally get, but all the hairs I wanted to get rid of are gone.  $12 is a lot cheaper than you'll pay for waxing at any of the Rittenhouse salons/spas, so I think I'll definitely be going back.  Bonus: they have a stamp card to get the 10th wax free.
Fantastic place! The drinks were great, all of the dishes were delish, and the atmosphere is perfect.

The food was excellent as usual but I called ahead and requested special service for my wife's 40th birthday and the staff promised to accommodate. Not only did they not accommodate, but when I noticed it wasn't happening I asked the manager who promised to take care of it. Still nothing. She didn't notice but I was severely disappointed. Not coming back.

My Honduran wife and I are in heaven as we sit after finishing a meal that took us back to her mom's kitchen. The food is quite authentic and very tasty for a fair price. The dining room is not large and as soon as a table is cleaned another patron walks in the door and sits down. We waited 20-25 minutes for our food as it was freshly prepared, with exception of the rice and beans. The food was well worth the wait. I wish they had jamaica as a beverage option. Overall a very pleasant experience!
Best best best best best best best ice cream I have ever had besides gelato in Italy!!  The staff is super friendly and the place have cute eclectic decor.

Excellent, food is cooked fresh and is delicious.
 It is a family restaurant. 
Portion size is huge.
They also have a vegan menu.
Excellent rooms and great customer service, we celebrated our aniversery in Santa Barbara, and the inn was awesome, definitely recomended.

The food here is top gear! Prices are a little high. The family that owns the place is very welcoming and hospitable. This is my daughters favorite restaurant. She always wants to have her birthday lunch here. One year the owners gave her some very nice birthday presents. It really feels and tastes like you are at someone's house having a home cooked meal. There are other Indian places out there where it seems "americanized". The Kormas are great. We are big fans of the Bhindi Masala. Samosas are good too.

The beer selection is excellent too. I also enjoy the filmi soundtrack coming from the large screen TV.

Adam at IDC was very helpful and informative when it came to get the ring for my fiancé. He help me to pick out the perfect ring for her. Thank you so much to Adam and the International diamond center.
Finally a great taco spot! I'll stop being a grump now.

(2.5 Stars) Photos: http://www.facebook.com/photo.php?fbid=10150353153361676&set=a.10150311275426676.332342.727646675&type=3&theater

I felt so conflicted after the meal. I walked out of Sbraga knowing full well that it has the potential to join the ranks of the great restaurants in Philadelphia, but it is just not there yet. I have to say though, considering that it is barely a few weeks old, it did well and i expect ratings for this place only to go up.

I went to Sbraga with a group of friends with great expectations despite the place being new. We wanted to try as many dishes as possible and since the tasting menu only starts the next week, we ordered as much dishes as the table can take and did it family style so I can do this review.

Service: The biggest letdown. The inexperience of the service is apparent despite their willingness. Service is frustratingly slow at the start (10 minutes to get water. 20 minutes to prepare my cocktail which came too late to be even called an apertif anymore), but improves as the courses arrive.

First Course:
Sweetbreads - decently good, like the idea of fleur de sel on top of it and the capers to go along
Blue Crab - nice and creamy, but still reeks of the "crabby" smell
Foie Gras Soup - I would say its an awesome soup if it was't called lemongrass cream soup. the lemongrass and other spices were so overpowering it killed the dish. nothing else makes sense afterwards. respect your ingredients please. modern cuisine for modernity sake is not the way to go.

Second Course:
Fish and Chips - nice take on the classic F&C, enjoyed it
Artic Char - I adored this dish despite my other companions calling it "just a salmon." balance of the cream and the fish is great.
Labne Ravioli - I couldnt understand this dish. Anchovies brought did not give the intended effect as the "fishiness" was too strong. tone it down and it would be great
Lobster Tail - executed to perfection. curry goes perfect with it as a complement. dump the dumpling and it would have been one of the best lobster dishes i ever had.

Third Course:
Lamb Belly - too much granola, other than that, its pretty amazing
Meatloaf - its great, i may be insulting it but it reminds me of Ikea meatballs when the sweet cuts the savory in the perfect balance.
Duck - average. really.
Top Sirloin - hands down worse dish of the night. soggy marrow crust, unevenly cooked. overdone top and medium bottom when i requested for medium rare. worst of all: IT WAS DRY. only dish i did not want to eat after a bite.

Desserts:
Singapore Sling - its disgraceful but im a Singaporean who hasnt tasted the Singapore Sling cocktail. its pretty good but needs to scale down on the lemongrass again.
Chocolate, Mascarpone - awesome richness and creaminess. choux provided the perfect textural contrast.
Apple Mille-Feuille - average at best despite the good creme chantilly
Pineapple Financier - a must order. pineapple crisp was so awesome.
Cheese Plate - brie was good but im just not a fan.

After my meal, I sent a pretty pointed email to the restaurant about my honest opinions and I appreciated that Chef Kevin took the effort to personally look into it. I hope this restaurant do shape up because i can really see its potential for greatness. I wish them all the best.

Not bad = finding parking, wait in line (before 10:30 mind you), $5 cover charge, layout that includes lots of open space & plenty of bars in both the inside & large outdoor patio, 2 different women's bathrooms (Thank the lord!) located in different areas of the club. 

DJ was a bit much at times but had a lot of fun props (glowsticks at the dj booth and even the wait staff did bottle service with glowsticks, glowing bottles, and even sparkler fireworks) and the music got a whole helluv alot better once 11:30 hit. 

Ran randomly into some girlfriends and they mentioned that this was the only joint popping on State Street. 

Tonic Nightclub was a fun place to go dancing post-wedding (not mine mind you!) and pretty easy to get to and get in despite it being Kardashian wedding weekend.  Congrats to friends M + N on your gorgeous wedding.
Do not let the outside deter you . This place is a gem. Authentic Mexican for very reasonable prices!  Service is pleasant and helpful. The restaurant seats 30.

Walked in for lunch about ten minutes after they opened and there was a bunch of tables already full and they kept rolling in. We ordered and split a sandwich, the Pan Con something, and it was awesome. It came with this green dipping liquid that I could have sipped and been set for the day. We then each had a small colada, which the retired barista accompanying me told me was espresso and sugar, but the coffee was Cuban and it was delicious. I will be bringing business lunches here, I might even just come for the morning cup of Joe.

Franklin such a great place with so much history! 
I'm so glad we went on this tour! Our guide was Jim, and he was very knowledgeable and informative. We learned so much! 
Story about Todd, who died pretty much in his dad's back yard was so touching. 
I enjoyed time I spent there, I just wish we could see more of the house!

Just walked in as we were headed to another area restaurant. Not only was I t
greeted by the hostess immediately, the manager came out from behind the bar and had a 10 minute conversation. They were actually in the process of closing yet they still offered me the menu! I didn't want to be the jerk who walks in at closing & makes everyone stay an hour later so I said I'd be back. They gave me the menu to home! The hostess & manager gave wonderful descriptions of their specialties & practically begged is to come back. Oh I'll be back!! Don't you worry about that. How can I possibly say no to people who are so kind & enthusiastic about what they do? Looking forward to a good meal!

I have always had a fantastic meal @ Modesto.  Atmosphere is quite good for just grabbing some early evening drinks as well.  I could eat the Salpicon De Mariscos 3 meals a day.  Specials are +++, but come early or you'll miss out.
They hooked it up with delivery like 10 minutes before closing!  Good food.  I got beef chow fun and dumplings.
Not many places serve lengua tacos so those alone make me a fan.

Burger was awesome.  Perfectly cooked, melted cheese, great ingredients, and bun.  Yes, a little expensive, but excellent for free-range and humanely treated animals.  I can't wait to try the chicken, as well.  I did take out, and the fries were soggy by the time I got home --- maybe cutting a whole in the corners of the to-go containers would have curbed this a little.  But, overall, great place for healthy meat-eaters and veggies, alike.

I checked this place out with a couple of buddies, and a guy that we met at the hotel who happened to be a Saints fan as well. This place was suggested by the guy we met, and I can see why. The place has a cool vibe, and a mix of different seating areas. *****

We ordered the Verde Dip... Spinach and Garlic. The dip was great! The chips were half crushed, and when I brought this up to the waiter he mentioned that they must have come from the bottom of the container. He acted as if that statement made it okay that we got the crumbs at the bottom of the bag, so I then told him that it was interesting that he didn't think we should get decent chips. We'd already ordered some wine/drinks, so I figured he'd be willing to give us some decent service in hopes of a decent tip. The guy returned 7 or so mins later with some chips. I guess the guy gave us something to talk about, and he did try and hustle a bit more later in the evening. ***

My boys tried a mixed variety from the menu. Their only complaint came from a wrap. It just didn't live up to the expectations. Chicken, Guac, MJ cheese, and tomato. All great ingredients, but under seasoned.***

I ordered the Shrimp and Grits. Part of my family is from NOLA, so I appreciated the good shrimp and sausage. The grits were good too. BUT it was over salted. It didn't ruin the meal, but I was hoping to finish on a high note. ***

I'd rate them 3 1/2, but will give them a 4 since the night would have been better if the waiter wasn't a dumb@$$ during the beginning of the meal. Good times for the most part.
Best tacos I've had I a long time. Ordered the shredded pork with everything. Yum!  Didn't go inside but can't wait to go back and try some more.

Friday May 11 was such a beautiful evening that my husband and i decided to go somewhere with outdoor seating.  We were both excited about coming here as we had been to the previous restaurant at this location and were very pleased.  We thought we would be WOWed after reading the menu.  What we found was a pleasant but inattentive server and bus boys that seemed to be clueless.  The food was mediocre at best.  I had the poached pear salad.  The flavor was very good on the pears but for $8.50 I wanted more than 4 thin slices.  it was supposed to have smoked Gouda.  I think there was 6 pieces that appeared to be box shredded.  I could not find the craisins or walnuts and the greens were starting to turn brown.  My husband had the wedge salad.  Again, over priced for the quality and amount.  I had, as an entree, the Jumbo Lump Crab Cakes.  They had no flavor.  The mashed potatoes had a lump of cheddar in the center and were overpowered by Old Bay seasoning.  My husband had the Seafood Pescatore which he said was OK.  I will say the desserts where beyond excellent.  We were told they were homemade so KUDOS to the baker.  We shared a Chocolate Mint Torte.  My mouth waters thinking about it.  The server, while she was pleasant, came over to take our order and then we did not see her again until she gave us our bill.  We asked for flatware as our food was served with no implements to eat it with.  Had we had the set ups at arrival we may have had a luke warm rather than cold meals.  When we asked for red wine glasses it too over 20 minutes for a bus boy to provide and when we asked for water you would have thought we had three heads each.  We will not be returning however, if the person who made the desserts opened a dessert eatery, we would frequent that establishment.

We have had the WORST experience with Comcast and we haven't even had our service setup yet! The representative was to have scheduled our service install for July 2nd and no one ever showed. So we log onto our account to find that it had been switched to July 8th without our request or approval to do so. We work from home and really needed the Internet to be setup by the 4th. We called Comcast and the representative said she saw how it showed we had it setup for the 2nd but that she didn't know who or why it was switched. We spent countless HOURS being transferred back and forth between customer representatives and had spoke with TWO supervisors. They didn't try to make it right or send anyone out so we've been at a disadvantage this entire week. Completely unacceptable. This experience alone, is reason enough to walk away. I would suggest going with AT&T U-Verse!! No customer wants to deal with the hassles and ignorance that we have throughout paying for a service for something that isn't cheap to begin with. Utterly disappointed and we will be posting reviews about this all over the place since people should know what they're getting themselves into before entering into a contract with an incompetent & problematic company.

Best Mexican food in PA. Tacos are excellent: al pastor is phenomenal- moist and flavorful. The service is humble but friendly. I have taken 10+ friends here and we all continue to go back whenever we can.

Went here recently for Mother's Day 2013 with my 10 month old and was surprised at how accomodating they were. Its in the Matrix Hotel, the decor was fabulous, wasn't too noisy so my daughter actually slept through dinner and the layout was well thought out for business meeting or an intimate setting. Free parking very close to the building always a plus downtown.

We were seated promptly, despite the fact they were busy. Our server was ALASTAIR who was very knowledgeable, fast and pleasant, he recommended everything we ate and he was spot on with his choices we enjoyed everything, he even took our pictures to commemorate the night, top notch service for sure.

The food was superb! We were given some a smoked salmon dish on a spoon which you'll see in some of the pics that was a nice tasting and was complimentary. The bread service was fantastic, tempts you to ask for more lol. We had  the feature risotto (pic included) for an appetizer, I actually started eating before taking a pic sorry about that but it was really good. It was a generous size so I would suggest sharing it with someone which we did. My husband had the lamb which he said was really good and I had the salmon dish which was very delightful in its presentation and taste. The shrimp and scallops were good and was enough food that you didn't feel like you were being overcharged for fish. My husband actually ended up eating some. We had the sticky toffee for desert which is caramelicious! and the chef sent some complimentary treat as well, needless to say we were stuffed :)

Considering all the food we ate the bill was less than we expected which is always a pleasant surprise. All in all a great night and a great choice I will be back!
Slow service, no checks for water, did not honor check-in discount. The food was okay, nothing impressive but the prices were decent.

I can't remember the last time I ate at the mall  let alone the last time I ate at a place I  perceived as fast food.  But I  am glad that I took a chance with Smee's.

The fish and chips were amazingly good.  I was in the mood for something fried with French fries.  The fish had a light batter and was fresh, seasoned with a subtle garlic seasoning.  The fries were fried just right and none of the meal was greasy.  The tartar sauce is really good as is the cole slaw that came with the meal.

Evidently Smee's had a restaurant somewhere in Reno and is considering building another one somewhere in our hometown.  At least this is what the server said and she was very nice.

This place was not crowded at 5:00 pm on a weekday.  I think everyone is back at school.  It's at the food court in Meadowood mall. 

Plenty of parking.

I will definitely be back!

My first experience with Sephora was in Paris... so that's not quite fair, but I have experienced Sephora in San Francisco and several places in New York City.  Why is it that many people in Philly just seem to give up,  I go to Sephora to spend money and each time I leave confused.  The staff seems sophomoric and at times I can't find a soul to wait on me.  Other times they are standing around having conversations and not real interested in helping me.  I am 60 years old and I am not just there to buy a lipstick.  The one in Cherry Hill is even worse.  Customer service is the name of the game.
Interesting and traditional decor but the food was just okay. We tried the sunday brunch.

Bad customer service. After driving there, filling out my paperwork, then waiting some more.. I was told the machines have been down all day and to reschedule. Shouldn't that have been communicated to me way before my appt was even scheduled?

really should separate out the restaurant reviews from the spa reviews.

restaurant.  used to be exquisite with one side of menu for calorie counting health conscious and other side for "just yummy gourmet".   New menu removes all calorie-counting and spa-conscious eating and puts little symbols by healthier selections-not nearly as helpful.  We ordered tarragon chicken salad and grilled grouper sandwiches for lunch.  Both meals (without health symbols) were fine but not "over the top".  Sweet potato fries (without health symbol) were yummy.  Mineral water from spring is always cold and delicious.  Service, view, fresh flowers, and ambience were excellent.  Reasonably priced, 2 people for about $20.  Front desk told us it opened at 11:30, but restaurant told us they started serving at 11.  Doesn't seem like total act is together here.  Don't post menu specials 'til late.  Restaurant closes 2 to 5.

Spa is lovely for exercise options, jacuzzi, pool work-outs.  They recently reinstated waiving the resort fee for FL residents.  Unfortunately, they don't tell you before booking, they now have a band playing til 11 p.m. Fri/Sat nites around the pool (audible from your room).
Everything here is amazing!!! Pulled pork, ribs, chicken, and all the sides! I haven't tried anything I didn't like.

I was condescended to in store when I came in for an oil change because my brakes needed obvious attention. I could clearly hear them joking about it in the workshop, and they could literally see me looking back at them through the glass. Not only that, but the kid who was taking care of the transaction, Michael, was holding back laughter, after I told him that clearly my brakes need attention, but that my dad does that type of maintenance on my car. 

They also offered me packages that were more than twice the price of the one I needed, but gave me the one I needed when I asked for it.

I also observed the same associate blowing off a customer before me when he said the name on his receipt was wrong. Manager Curt was more helpful.

This is a small little restaurant in a shopping center. Once you step inside the door, you can smell the garlic and feel the heat from the pizza oven. Service was good. Pizza was excellent. Best crust I have tasted! We will definitely return.

Great little bakery and coffee shop. Had we been in NO longer we would have tried the Belgian waffles. Next time. 

And thanks for the intro to Gold and the Rush. :)
Super cute, chic nail salon!  The products are all natural and smell wonderful.  The staff is super friendly, professional, knowledgeable and do an excellent job.  Will definitely return!

We went for lunch and there was no wait. The service was great and the food was excellent. My wife had the vegetarian pumpkin dish and it was amazing. We started with Bulani which was a great appetizer. I had a chicken dish, that I can't remember the name of, but it was also delicious. Their saffron rice that comes with the food is as good as it gets with rice. I highly recommend trying this place out.

I have been to many local nail salons and spend even more money sometimes. They were good But this was the best. Staff spent a Long time doing my manicure and pedicure without complaint and fix the color when i asked. the quality of place and service is great. I will go back again.

Boston Pizza Millennium location. This is pathetic. We just ordered a large pizza and a double order of wings and it cost $70.00!!!! The shrimp were soggy and water logged. There was a huge piece of onion skin in one slice of pizza. The wings were mediocre and very small On what planet is it reasonable to charge $40.00 for a large pizza and $23.00 for 16 wings. That's a $1.45 EACH!!! I will never order pizza from Boston Pizza again. 

For all those interested I highly recommend Nitza's pizza in Sherwood Park!

Not as good as I remember. The first time I went it was phenomenal. I went again and got the same thing to-go. Wasn't as flavorful and the sauce was something I'm allergic too. I didn't know that sauce came with it. Nevertheless, I may be willing to try again. We'll see.

The location is fantastic. Just far enough removed from the mess of Bourbon Street, but still close enough for you party people. Pretty much everything is within walking distance - even the conference center on the river front is only a 20 minute walk away. 

I enjoyed my stay here, and really appreciated the fact that they let me check-in at 8AM on the morning of my arrival even though check-in time is typically not until 4PM. I also loved the room that I was given (a corner room on one of the newly added floors). It was spacious and the bed was so, so comfortable. It was like sleeping on clouds, I kid you not. The only thing that kind of irked me was the separate elevator that was needed to access the top 3 floors - it made the whole commute up and down the building quite a hassle. 

All in all, I would highly recommend this Wyndham for either business or pleasure. They make things very convenient for you - with cab pickups, printing services at the front desk, etc.

Bella Vista is *amazing*. I can't believe others haven't yelped them! I worked with Trevor on my wedding and he was everything you hope a wedding vendor will be: Nice, Professional and 100% capable and dependable.  His prices (while not at all cheap) were reasonable, he worked with us to find good lighting within our very limited budget, he never tried to sell us things we didn't need, he was nice and helpful and totally competent. He threw some free cords and random  things we needed but didn't know where to find and when we couldn't decide if we needed a tent (every web site said it would rain) it was Trevor that gave us the best advice. (Not to get the tent. And he was right! We saved 5k and it was a beautiful clear day and night.) They are just total pros.

Can't believe I have lived so close to this place and not gained 500 pounds.  LOVE their coffee, pastries, and sandwiches made to order.  Fun to eat outside at picnic tables after ordering lunch.  I take all my out-of-town guests here.  Only four stars because I wish they were open later on Saturdays or open on Sundays-so many times have wanted to bring people here but can't because of limited week-end hours.

I walk by this place daily and I've been wanting to eat here for a long time.  My friend had mentioned that this place had one of her favorite burgers so I had to check it out.
It was DELICIOUS!  It may be on the saltier side as others have mentioned but I have a salty palate so I didn't really notice.  Something about the beef patties with the cheese and pickles made for a really delicious combo. 
The fries that came with it was good too.
service was good too
What a stinky, moldy store. It stinks and everything looks old and faded. It doesn't help when the employees are rude!

I special ordered a birthday cake with inscription. I arrived at the appointed time to pick it up only to see my name being scraped off and another name be inscribed. The man in front of me was sold my cake. The store offered no discount on a "rack" cake. My birthday party was ruined.

Capo De Monte is like an undiscovered treasure right in Seminole!  Unbelievable!  I was astonished by what I found in this place!  The sandwiches are absolutely gourmet, with prosciutto and sweet peppers and the soup is to die for!  I have also picked up lasagna and chicken Marsala for dinner and scored major points with the Mrs.!  Everything is tasty and fresh - a refreshing departure from all of the fast food joints.  I intend to try their catering for our next office party.  Everyone needs to discover Capo De Monte!

Kyoto represents that slice of Japanese cuisine which features misoshiru soup, sashimi, sushi & maki rolls, don buri (rice bowls), udon, bento, tonkatsu (a favorite), and a staggering number of appetizers (from gomae (a wilted spinach salad with sesame) to beef tataki to tako yaki (grilled Osaka-style octopus balls festooned with paper-thin bonito flakes).

What it offers it does very well, and the hunnybunny and I have visited numerous times (and done take-away even more) because it's very near to us. Their fare is satisfying and presented straightforwardly. Perhaps a touch pricey, but we don't walk away feeling cheated.

What I really like to do is start here and halfway through head across the street to Kabuki, which offers similar fare with a different take on the presentation. It's the best part of a soy sauce pub crawl :-) and makes for an interesting date night!

Jordan the hostess was very patient and helpful in taking care of things early on; took care of me while I waited for my (late) party to arrive. Outside seating is nice, and only suffers from all the dag gum noise (who knew 10th st. was THAT busy?). But you do live in the city, so suck it up, eh? Wide selection of beers that came quick and cold. I had the salmon entree which was the cats' ass (not the fishes). Overall awesome experience.

It's a bit pricey but I'll tell you what...that was the best dang panini I've ever had in my 27 years of life. Been talking about it all day. Nonstop. It was so good.

So yeah, I had half of the Bacon & Brie Panini and a cup of Bacon Corn Chowder. Both delicious! Again, do your mouth a flavor (Ha! Get it?) and get the panini.

What a fun place here in downtown Tucson. We decided to check out the Friday nights wine tasting. A nice band with a great outdoor setting. The wine was fantastic and the servers were knowledgeable. Plenty of people enjoying the atmosphere and the great wine. We also had a pepperoni pizza that was tasty. I hope to go back for dinner soon.

Stopped here for lunch and got their brick oven burger - and it was amazing!  The service was a bit slow during the lunch rush, but they only had one waitress, and she was very apologetic.  The atmosphere is really nice and classy.  They are BYOB, however with a $15 corking fee.

As far as a lunch spot I highly recommend, and will definitely go back soon!

Well, hello there Crazy Sushi. thank you for fulfilling your duty as a sushi restaurant and offering me delicious, fresh and affordable meals. 

As I explore Philadelphia and use yelp for guidance, I have been let down quite a few times. Crazy sushi however was an extremely awesome surprise. Sushi is one of those things that if you do wrong, there's no fixing and it leaves reminders like "you sure you want have sushi again, it was so gross last time". 

For lunch they offer a ton of specials! From bento boxes to roll specials. You can get two rolls with a soup or salad for 8 bucks or you can get three rolls with soup or salad for 12 bucks. Do yourself the favor and get three rolls. The sushi is always extremely fresh!!! The staff is beyond nice and welcoming. 

I wish they can open a location next to me in jersey. But in the meantime I'll continue to enjoy my lunch here. Thank you, crazy sushi- I appreciate that you did not ruin sushi for me.

Great place for any occasion. The services are always wonderful, and the food never disappoint. Some of my colleagues claim Cafe Ponte has best burger in Tampa Bay, and I definitely understand their argument. I have also try their tasting menu on several occasions, and always look forward to the next time.

Spent many days in the Original in New Jersey. Actually competed pagainst them for a while.  Good sub, decent service that used to be aces,  but as the franchisee has opened more stores, the thinning ranks of competent employees is obvious. Also, way too expensive for a sandwich. Two Giant meal 'deals will run you around $30.00 . This isn't the North East, and they are just sandwiches.
