For appetizer, we ordered the pork belly taco which is a seared pork belly served with pickled vegetables and fresh herbs atop a flat steamed bun.  Yum!!!  I would definitely order this again.

My sister and I each had the pho ga kho as our entree.  I LOVED the presentation of this meal.  The meal comes out on one large plate with the pho noodles and chicken in one bowl, the vinaigrette (I think?) dressing in a little dish, and the broth in another rice-sized bowl.  It was the first time I've ever eaten pho ga this way, and boy was it good!!  To eat, you toss the noodles and chicken with the dressing.  If you feel it is too dry like this on its own,  you can add some broth.  (I liked it as is).  A word of caution!!  After eating this dish, you may feel just the right amount of fullness, but after drinking water, the noodles will expand, and you will feel very very full!!

I didn't order anything from the bar, but they seemed to have a huge selection.  I'd definitely come here again if I were in the area.

Walked in for the first time today. The wait was not long and our waiter Nancy was courteous and gave us the right amount of attention we needed. I had stuffed French toast and turkey sausage and my husband had Belgian waffles combo. Coffee was good. Perfect breakfast to start off the weekend!
These cats have a great shop and the owners are assets to the Tampa Bay music community.  Go buy some records there!

The Depot is one of my favorite places to go eat.  The service is always good, friendly staff,
Excellent food. The cod and Brussel sprouts are amazing.

Got in for breakfast and OMG! I had banana French toast and my husband had pancakes. They were both just amazing! Quick service, gorgeous atmosphere! Definitely want to come here again when I am in the area!

Lazos has the best pizza in Philly. I think they are a little pricier than your average local pizza joint, but I still buy it. The honey barbecue wings are also pretty good. 

If I wasn't a Registered Dietitian, I would probably eat here once a week. I get a slice about once per month and the wings maybe once every 2-3 months. Both are a really good treat on a cook-free night.

The staff are also very nice. That's always a plus for me. I highly recommend Lazos.

Attended at wedding in the city Friday night.  We stayed one night at the Loews.  The hotel is very nice, the staff were very accommodating.   Check -in wasn't until 4:00 and the wedding was 4:30.  We were able to check in early enough to get ready without a lot of hassle.  The 3 star rating is for the $36 to park for less than 24 hours and the $12.95 they wanted for WI-FI.  Really?  I would have parked else where had I know what the charge for parking would be, and as for the WI-FI, went to a local coffee shop and got if for NOTHING!

There was a 45 min wait when we got there, but we were seated quicker than that. My first margarita was say too sour and not good at all, which is disappointing considering it was Margaritaville. The 2nd margarita, a more expensive one, was better. The food was good and I love the atmosphere. Our waitress was very nice and friendly. I'd go again.

Food was good.  Waitress was OK.  Manager is a pud.  After ordering an IPA I was brought a glass that was half foam.  Waitress said it would settle.  Ten minutes later asked to get it topped off after it settled to half a pour and still had an inch and a half head .  She was AFRAID to ask the bartender (no exaggeration - clearly nervous).  Asked to see a manager and she said he was the manager.  Me, not afraid, went to the bar and asked for a top-off.  Met with a condescending smirk to which I asked "is there a problem?" (If you're a pud to me I'll be a pud to you).  After a few pleasantries I walked away with a full beer.  Ordered my next one in a bottle for obvious reasons.  All over probably three ounces of beer.  Just give me a full pour and not make me wait 15 minutes for the suds to go down.  Any other place would have replaced it immediately.

I made reservations for a Tuesday evening at 7pm, but it was unnecessary as the restaurant was fairly empty. Our waiter forgot our green tea, and when we reminded him, he kindly made it on the house for the inconvenience. The food was delicious and fresh - my friend loved her Uni (which she had been craving) and Rock Shrimp, and I was delighted by the quantity and quality of fish in my Chirashi. After a great meal and good service, Izumi is now one of my top places for sushi in Philly.

This place is by far the best sushi place in SB! The press boxes are all amazing. The Montecito and the mozzarella red wine eel melt boxes are great! The sauces are all original, colorful and makes the quality sushi just that much better. Highly recommended

The best thing about this cinema: they have reclinable chairs that also elevate your legs...!! I loved that part! If youre're looking for wheelchair friendly seating...you can transfer easily into the chairs as well because the arm rests go up. It was awesome!

Another plus is that they serve food and alcoholic beverages at the cinema...that's a service you can't get everywhere. However! the food left a lot to be desired. I order the Blueburger. It was ok at best. I did not really taste the blue cheese. The burger tasted very bland, it had that cardboard taste frozen burgers have. My friend ordered the sangria...it was watered down wine with an orange floating in it. I was very disappointed with the food specially for the price, that was a 14 dollar burger. 

The service was great! The server that attended to us was very helpful and she checked on us appropriately. Everything we asked for was brought promptly to us. 

I would return, I have not found a more comfortable seat in all of Tampa. I don't know if I'll order a meal next time due to my experience. Maybe just one of their snacks or appetizers to munch on, something safe.

Speaking of addiction in my review of Dinic's I cannot walk out of the terminal without my cannoli fix from Termini Bros. You absolutely must eat one immediately right after it is filled by hand to order, there is also only one kind of cannoli, yes I know they offer Chocolate and Vanilla but Ricotta and Chocolate chip is the only one you need to order, fuhghetabbout the rest.

Hideaway is a great bar to relax at.  Cheap drinks, nice staff, and fun regulars.  My favorite weekend visits are when the regular seemingly blind piano guy is playing all the jams from the 50s-80s and the old couples are on the small floor dancing, chain-smoking and drinking away.  

This place can get really smokey, so be wary if that's not your thing.  Outside of the multiple paintings of the lady with her breast exposed, there isn't much about the bar itself that stands out.  It's just a fun, old-timey bar to chat, dance, and throw a few back.

A friend and I went for Sunday brunch. No wait for a table as there were only about a dozen people dining. Drinks and food were ordered. Drinks came out fairly quickly but biscuits & gravy with scrambled eggs and shrimp & grits took 45 minutes to be served. During this time the waitress never came to check on us or refill drinks (sweet tea & coffee). When food was served, my shrimp and grits were aweful. Grits were plain, 5 prawns laying on top and a dark gravy around the plate. I took 2 bites and motioned for the waitress to take it away. My friends wasnt much better. We both agreed that we wouldnt return.
Monica is the best manicurest in the world. The nicest and professional person ever. Use her and you will never leave her. I have used for over 20 years.

Been driving by this place for years and found that some folks from another restaurant took it over and some friends (locals) said it was a great find for a local place.    Greta beers on draft (even Guinness ) and wine.   Awesome burger, very good fish & chips, "Great" french fries and a shepherds pie that will fill you up.  Everyone loves the chili...but they always run out B/4 we get there!!!   Clean and friendly staff & owners.  There is occasional music, a juke box & a few video games.    A real neighborhood location for cold beer & good food.   Just don't tell too many people about it!
Flavorful food. Fast and friendly service. Can't ask for much more out of breakfast. The seafood Benedict was a win.

We came in for lunch to avoid the wait at another restaurant. It was Memorial Day so the usual lunch buffet was shut down and they used the dinner menu. That menu is expensive but the cook nicely suggested we purchase two entrees for the 3 of us, which worked out fine. On to the food. Chicken korma and lamb biryani were fine. I would have liked more meat in my biryani (after all, it did cost $19 for an admittedly very large portion).  There were a couple tiny patches of unseasoned rice in there but they did not detract from the dish at all. The korma was what you'd expect and plenty tasty. Naan was kind of thin and came out before the rest of the meal. Bummer, I'd hoped to eat it with the other dishes. My younger son ordered mango lassi which took forever to get there but was gigantic, tasted good, and served in a kind of volumetric flask that was cool to look at. I think the reason I'm giving Taj Mahal 3 stars is the timing of the meal (naan early, lassi late, everything took a long time despite the restaurant being pretty empty) and price-to-meat ratio of the biryani. I'd go back, though.

What in the bloody heck is this?  After reading some positive reviews on yelp, I decided to give phat bites a whirl. Upon walking in, I figured, okay, it's a hipster hippie kinda joint. Healthy, organic, vegan, inexpensive, right?  Nope. Dead wrong on all counts. Upon walking in, you just stand in a line. No menu. Nobody telling you what to do or where to go. And then when you finally order, you are told to order coffee separately. Wtf?  And then you have to wait in an endless line to pay. And then you have to wait at your table and wait for your name to be called. Then, to add insult to injury, the portions are TINY. I literally am on my phone looking for a place to eat breakfast... after having just finished breakfast at this joke of a place.  

So, if you are in the Nashville airport area and you are longing to pay ridiculous prices for mediocre service, mediocre decor, tiny portions and middling food, by all means come to this joint. Then we can talk about a bridge in Brooklyn I can sell to you for real cheap.

I decided to go and experience Blackfinn for lunch because I had heard mixed reviews about the restaurant. Well unfortunately, I have to go with the bad side of the reviews. While my food was decent, my service was terrible. I had a server named Lucy, who seemed very irritated and unhappy. I felt as though she rushed us and did not really want us to be there. When we sat down, we were greeted by a gentleman who was very friendly and took our drink order. He told told us that he would return with or drinks. He also gave us the day's specials. After awhile, Lucy came to our table and the experience went downhill from there. She approached the table with a "are you ready to order" Not a hello, how are you? Nothing. We asked her questions about the menu and she acted as though it was a problem to answer our questions. The story goes on and on about our rude rushed service experience. The food was good, and the gentleman the originally greeted us was friendly, so would I go back? Probably would give the restaurant another shot, but I would definitely ask them at the desk."DO NOT sit me with Lucy," and i suggest you do the same.
Usually a good quick wash, but no tire shine(armor all) or fragrance on their $18 "Supreme" wash is unacceptable - basically the same as their $13 one. Won't be going back unless I have a coupon.

Stanton's Gourmet Catering KNOCKED IT OUT OF THE PARK for our event in Santa Barbara!! When searching for a caterer, I found that everything was so expensive. Stanton's prices were so much more reasonable then any other place I found, and I cannot imagine that any other caterer would have topped what Stanton and his team created for us! Stanton made himself very available for the planning and when needed, offered guidance in a very friendly and helpful way. They went to the site three times before the event. The team was exceptional and attentive and genuinely cared about guests and our event. The food was absolutely out of this world! Everyone went nuts over it! I have been to so many events where the food was 'okay', but at our party, people were going back for seconds and thirds. As Stanton predicted, his potatoes rocked everyone's world! I have one friend who is a very picky eater and NEVER eats fish, but went and got seconds of the salmon! I did not have time to do a tasting or much planning - and with Stanton's Gourmet Catering, I didn't need to - I had full confidence in his team and his menu.

Service is great and the food is awesome! The tryst cocktail is amazing. I'm from Austin so whenever I can get austin liquor I'm trying it especially with deep eddy vodka! I will definitely come back!

What a fun place!!!  It's where everyone in town seemed to be!!   We had dinner and Keeli was phenomenal with her perfect recommendations!  She made it a fabulous food experience!   We wish were in town longer so that we could come back again!!  Don't miss this hit spot!  See if you can sit on Keeli's section because that gal knows the menu!!!!  So fun!!!
Been going here for a few years and still have had only excellent experiences. Give Paola a try and you'll love her work! Very clean and professional and always on time.
I normally don't like any type of coconut curry, but man the red curry here was on point. Yum!
Great place! A few different bar areas, cool sports pics on the walls. Loved that the bathrooms were central and clean. Good food. Decent service at the bar. Very cool place before a concert!

This ever-changing wall of art is really a gem.  If you are ever downtown and have some time to kill, take a gander.  Just drive East on Chouteau until you hit the Mississippi.  The wall is long... it's an actual flood wall... but it makes a great canvass for a can or two of spray paint.  Don't bring your own paint.  You're not going to be near as talented as the artist that created this mural.  Just bring a camera and and open mind.  Take a selfie or two and you'll have a unique backdrop photo for your Facebook page.

Oh... and you might want to visit during daylight hours.
Amazing amazing amazing amazing amazing.  The Ecuadorian fish stew (cant remember the name and it may very well be Peruvian...LOLOLOL) was everything that God designed it to be.
Real good well-priced cheesesteaks. The best ?? Probably not, but considering they "borrowed" a lot of ideas from the Steve's Prince of the worlds it's not too far off.

OMG What a great Gem!!! Me and My husband are really tired of the super-expensive not-so-good food scene in Santa Barbara and today we decided to give Carp a try. We were "late lunchers" and only had a few options open. Since we both love Thai food we decided to Try Siam Elephant. 
First things first: based on SB yelp's I am actually surprised this place is only 4 stars! it is definitely a 5 star in my opinion.
About our experience: We were greeted right  away by this really nice guy who gave us the option of seating outside. We decided on the lunch menu - WHAT A DEAL!!! - and my husband had a Thai Iced Tea.
The soup we got for "starter" was SO DELICIOUS that my husband ordered another one. Then  I had the pad thai per server recommendation and my husband had the spicy noodles (as warned on the menu: very spicy). All the food is REALLY fresh and AMAZINGLY DELICIOUS. Kudos to the Chef. And the portions are great (with the menu you get not only the soup and mais course but also rice, crispy won tons AND a spring roll - needless to say we needed to go boxes hehehe). And the service was AMAZING!!! From Winit, our server, to the ladies inside and even the new trainee, everyone was just so nice and welcoming and on point with everything.
Not only will we be coming back, but I already started spreading the word here in SB about this great Thai place in Carp. Well done, guys. Thanks for everything.
Been here twice and it was ok. Quaint little dining place in Woodbury. It used to be a train station, hence the name. They're great for serving beignets. Food was ok, nothing special.
You select your ingredients to do your own hash for breakfast..great idea and the coffee is very pleasant.

Great service, loved the decor, but most importantly can't wait to come back for the delicious food - honestly some of the best Szechuan I've ever had.  Some of my favorites were the SPICY CRISPY CUCUMBER, DAN DAN NOODLES and THREE CUP CHICKEN.  Would highly recommend.

I took my vintage Manolos in to have the rubber tips on the heels replaced. I had read all the negative reviews, but thought: "it's a simple repair, I'm optimistic." Big Mistake. When I went to pick up the shoes, I was told that there was a problem. I saw that the stilettos had been broken and re-glued. A glob of dried glue and the now warped lizard skin covered the bottom half of each heel. When I asked what had happened, I was told that when the nail was pulled out, the heel snapped, "which shouldn't happen, I don't know why it did " according the the man. He said he wasn't going to even attempt to do the original repair. When I asked why the second shoe had the same re-glue job on the heel, he said "that one broke too. I didn't think it would happen twice." He wasn't particularly kind about any of it. They refunded money that I paid upfront for the repair. I walked out with ruined shoes. Lesson learned, heed the reviews!

Came here late on a Monday night for a bite to eat. 
From the start, our hostess seemed miserable to be there and was quite rude, but nonetheless...
Our server was very sweet and attentive throughout the whole meal.
We ordered a Philly Cheesesteak and the Kobe Pizza. Both delicious and came out pretty quickly. The tater tots were bomb!
I would highly recommend this place for a quick easy meal.

Dumplings is a cute little restaurant located on Ellwood Drive. 
This is an Asian fusion restaurant owned by really nice Asian people. 
I tried there Sichuan Dan Dan noodle soup. It was not as good as I thought it would be. 
We ordered the spicy green beans and the Rice Dollar with Vegetables. 
There must be a different translation of English??? There was only one kind of vegetable and it was the cheapest kind of Chinese veggie they used. 
I found that the food lacked flavor and was slightly over priced for such small portions.
They only offer pork and beef dumplings even thought the restaurant is called Dumplings. It doesn't mean they have varieties.
The dumplings are homemade and taste pretty good. 
A lot of regulars come here for takeout. 
I wouldn't try the bubble tea here cause it's all made from powder and I'm don't usually order bubble tea from a Chinese restaurant unless I know 100% I can trust it.
I worked here for one day and because the restaurant is so tiny, you don't need more than one staff in the front.
Usually the owner can handle the entire floor. 
I feel like the owner has accomplish her dream of owning a restaurant where she can invite her friends to come over and she can cook good food for them.

Stopped in to Kitchen Kapers  behind Moorestown Mall while out doing some errands. First thing after walking in is that wonderful aroma of coffee that's in open small containers. Buy it by the pound or half pound. They will grind it while you wait. Picked up s half pound of coconut gourmet coffee for under $7. Pleasant staff can answer your questions. Large selection of kitchen gadgets, pots & pans, etc. they also sell Stonewall Kitchen specialty food. Picked up a jar of Wild Maine Blueberry Jam which is very good. Price is also comparable to online. Shop wisely as prices can be double compared to other stores like Walmart for the same items. Lots of made in China utensils which for me is a turn off. I try to stick with made in USA. Happy with 2 purchases and on my way.

Really good food. I got gnocchi with meatball, my girlfriend got spaghetti and clam sauce. Both really liked our meals. My meatball was fantastic, and the sauce was very homestyle - not sweet at all. Thoroughly enjoyed it. The portions are small, but we liked that about it.

I love this place! Excellent customer service, clean inside and out and  consistent product. They have a couple of sorbets available, but I usually go with the golden vanilla or chocolate. If you've never had a shiver you've got to try one. I get something called the Triple Threat (yes that's a proper noun). It's chocolate yogurt with brownies and Oreos. My wife gets them with "enrober" which we call crack sauce. There's a few reasons why it could be called that: it's addictive, it hardens and cracks when upon the fro yo, and well we'll stop there. My wife gets crack sauce and Reese's peanut butter cups in golden vanilla.  Get a large eat half and freeze the rest, you won't be sorry.
Great breakfast/lunch place.  Would come here every morning if I could!

On our road trip from Louisville to San Diego we stopped here. Great decision. I had half the meatball sandwich my boyfriend has the Cuban. Both delicious. I love that it was quick and affordable and great atmosphere. There was a line once we got there but it moved pretty fast and there was also live music. I would definitely return again. There were no tables inside available but we were happy to eat standing up since we had been seating in the car for hours! And for those girls that can't handle big portions the half portion was enough for myself. Loved it! Thanks Yelp for helping us find this St.Louis gem

We were here for an event honoring 9/11. I had the salad (surprise surprise) with grilled chicken. The chicken was salty I couldn't even touch it. My mouth watered after taking the first bite it was so strong. The fries were yummy though.

We also sampled their pizza. No flavor whatsoever, but we had to eat.

The actual venue and the servers are great! So two stars there.
Food was really good. Good customer service. I ordered the legume. My son and I enjoyed it.

The Good News: 

If you attend a happy hour and sign up to win a happy hour, odds are that you will win a happy hour every 4-6 months or so.  I signed up once and have won 4 happy hours so far.  Also, the female bartenders and girls that come here are pretty attractive.

The Bad News:  

This place gets way too crowded with former frat boys.

I dropped my dog off next door at the groomers and was about to head out for lunch. I noticed this place in the same shopping center. I love ethnic foods and coming from a Mediterranean background (Greek) I'm very picky about kabobs. It's one of our specialty foods that we share and I've eaten at some of the finest kabob restaurants throughout the country including at my friend's homes who are great cooks. My favorite kabob is Koobideh which is what I ordered and let me remind you again about how picky I am with this particular type of food. It was excellent. Flavors were spot on, perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned, and the portion was just the right size​. I cleaned my plate and was stuffed but I felt great. It's not too heavy. The price is right for quality food, and the service was excellent. You've earned my business.

Top-notch service and great food... you can't ask for more than that!

Came in on a Friday evening- actually, we had put our name down at a place across the street and after being told we would have an hour and a half wait, decided to wander around and see what our other options were. Checked out the menu at Moto Cucina, and decided maybe we would get a drink and a snack. This place is really deceiving- we walked in to a packed dining room and front bar area, and the hostess told us there was another bar in the back of the building, and we could order food there as well. 

When we entered the back bar, it was like another world. It was quiet, empty, perfect to sit with the girls and have conversation while enjoying cocktails. Thanks to the sweet hostess for the tip!

We were warmly greeted by Dominic at the bar, who guided us through the cocktail and food menus. We decided to just get a couple dishes and share. since we had plans after dinner that involved lots of alchohol. We shared the Wagyu Beef meatball and the cheese platter. The burrata and proscuitto on the cheese plate were favorites.

Since it was such a comfortable atmosphere and Dominic was taking such good care of us, we decided to continue our food and drinks at the bar. We ordered the sausage, onion, honey, fontina pizza (so good!), and the gnocchi with green apple. For some reason, we also decided we needed the olive oil tasting, which came with a mountain of foccacia and three different house-infused olive oils. Maybe all this was overkill for 4 people trying not to overeat, but it was well worth it!

The gnocchi was the stand-out dish of the night. The soft, salty potato pasta with the crunchy apple was the most perfect combination. Every time I said I was done I had to have another bite. The pizza was great as well, but the gnocchi will definitely bring us back!

The back bar area looks like a garden, with grass up the walls and mirrors that resemble windows. It was a very different vibe from the front area. There were a few larger parties that came in while we were dining at the bar, but it was still a more quiet, relaxed space, especially compared to the hustle and bustle up front. This is definitely a hidden gem, and I can't wait to come back!

Super excited to eat here... Love the outside seating.. This place is always super clean. The staff is way friendly and the treats here are all soooo good!!! The flavor variety of gelato is crazy... I ordered a Guinness flavor and  it was incredible ... Perfect place for the family after dinner somewhere!!!!

Last night was my visit time visiting Felicia's Pizza. The shop was just about to close but Tony waved us in and took our order. He even gave us some suggestions and pointed out the most popular pizzas. After we ordered he began to make our pizzas and the wait wasn't more than 10mins. During the whole time he talked with us about Ardmore and his renovations. Soon there will be rooftop seating above the pizza shop to accommodate more people.

Price: I thought the prices were very fair. $6 avg for a small individual pie which is more than enough. Around $10-11 for a medium and about $17-19 for a large pie. If you are with a group of people it's definitely worth getting a couple of different small pies and sharing.

Taste: I am not a pizza fanatic and I also do not care for thin crust pizzas. But I will say that this is a good exception. The ingredients tasted fresh and the sauce was just right.

I would recommend Felicia's to anyone. The only tips I can remember are 1. not expect to find seating (just yet) and 2. be aware of the hours as they close pretty earl (reason they lost a star).

I love you Texas Roadhouse. I want to be buried with a hot roll with cinnamon butter slathered on it. Their rolls are hot & yummy, almost like you're eating dessert. I love getting my steaks (medium rare) smothered with extra onions & a side of loaded mashed potatoes & a cup of their chili. So absofreakinglutely-delicious. A great place to come eat before you go to try your luck @ Parx or a great place to celebrate (or console yourself) after you try your hand with lady luck. I wish I could eat here everyday. It's delicious & it's cheap!

The server had cut her arm and had blood running down it and was serving ice cream. I saw that she had gotten blood on the ice in the case. While the ice crewman was creamy, the sanitary conditions I observed were abhorrent.

I'm constantly at the ballpark, as I'm a diehard Phillies fan (yes, even when they are in last place!). While nothing will ever compare to the perfection which was The Vet, this place is amazing. There's literally not a bad seat in the place, and even if you're in the nosebleed section, you most likely have the best seats in the place! 

They have a very large amount of bathrooms, which for me as a female is an excellent thing! What's not a excellent thing, is the fact that they've stuffed as many plastic seats together to get as much money out of the place as they can! I'm not an extra large person by any means, but I certainly fell cramped when sitting. 

The prices of food and drinks are of course astronomical, but that's anywhere you go for a game, and for an Eagles game it gets worse! Personally, I just tailgate and fill up outside, so when I go inside I'm not waiting to spend my money on a mini hot dog, that costs the price of a car loan payment. 

Another thing that's great is the super cheap cost of a Phillies tour. It's a great thing to do on a week day with a friend or your kids; when will you ever have the chance to go into the locker rooms or sit in the same seat as Harry K?

This was on my list of places to try in 2018. It was fine, but I expected more than just fine. The drinks were tasty but seemed really tiny. The corn dog appetizer was tasty. Not exactly what I was expecting but good. The entrees were good but seemed pricey for the portion and then discovering they come with no sides. My fault for assuming. But to add a side would definitely take it to too pricey for what it is. Was really surprised the jambalaya didn't even come with any sort of bread.

I've never been to nola before so I took a shot in the dark picking this hotel in the 11th hour before flying out after Hurricane Isaac.   I was so pleased upon our arrival.  It was blazing hot outside as we entered the perfectly chilled lobby.  Our petite King room wasn't ready so the very nice and helpful girl at the front desk, Katelyn,  immediately upgraded us to a premium King.   It faced the street but no noise due to it being just far enough off bourbon st.   Our room was lovely with a marble floor and the most comfy king bed ever!!  It's a great little boutique hotel.  No crazy emenities, but a terrific free breakfast, awesome location, great, helpful and courtious staff, clean, beautiful rooms and awesome air conditioning!!!   The bellman, Rene, was super helpful and came rushing to our aid when we needed help opening our rain swollen balcony doors.  I highly recommend and I will be returning here!

Pan D'olive is a big place and it was hoppin Friday night with the one-night break in the World Series.   We had a reservation, so we were a little surprised when we headed down to the basement dining room.  It's not a bad area, though.  The waitress said they rarely use it.  The bar area was absolutely packed.  We took a glance at their happy hour specials and they look really good, so I guess that explains why the bar crowd was all but gone when we left.

You get a bread basket to start out.  I wasn't crazy about the olive bread (tough and a little dry) or the olive oil on the table.   

The first thing we noticed are the prices are very reasonable here for a pretty classy restaurant.  For an appetizer, we tried our old favorite, calamari.  Although we both like the Trattoria Marcella and Bartolino's versions with flash fried spinach, this is a good one.  We shared the lobster ravioli and the Cappelini, which was a pasta I didn't know but was basically a vegetarian thin spaghetti.  Both were solid choices.  The ravioli was obviously made in house and you could definitely taste the lobster.   I didn't like it as much as the wife. I found it a bit too dense and a little fishy.  She thought it was very good.  

This month they offer half-off wines by the bottle (from the list, not the cheaper menu items).  The list is pretty impressive, although we're not experts.  We ended up with a Rosemount red blend and it was pretty good.  

Service was very slow at first, but one it got rolling, they were fine and did a good job.  Dogtown is a bit inconvenient for us, but  still we won't hesitate to go back and would definitely hit them up for happy hour given the chance.  

Three and a half stars.  Probably would have been three except for the low-priced apps and happy hour.

This was my first time eating at Yah Mon. The food is just as delicious as it looks in all of the pics posted. I started with a chicken patty that was crusty on the outside, moist and delicious on the inside. For my entree, I had the brown stew fish. I must say that this was the best brown stew fish I've ever had. It was perfectly fried (lightly), very fleshy and moist on the inside. I ordered the small dinner and the portions were very hearty and filling. The wait staff was very friendly and welcoming. The owner came out to check on us a couple of times. She was so sweet and friendly! The interior is well-appointed and very comfortable. I will definitely be back!

I got my coffee right away like after I placed my order in. The barista was making my drink as I was paying. The store was kind of packed but luckily I found a seat by the door. I got my usual drink, venti Carmel frapp and it was delicious as usual. 

I gave it 4 stars because the workers were talking among themselves and goofing around too much. They should be talking to their customers not amongst each other's regarding something that happened earlier in the day.

It's a pretty small Starbucks so just FYI try to get there early to avoid the lengthy lines. It is right across the Betsy Ross House.

My favorite place to eat. Go there at least once a week and the staff is always so nice and helpful. The dry pot style beef is by far the best thing ever. Would highly recommend to anyone in the area. I found that the Old City food is just as good but the service isn't.
Good ice cream and a variety of sundae options. They sometimes have music and you may catch some ice sculpting. Not impressed with their pizza or pretzels though.
Quality selections and decent prices for good vintage clothing.  The attendant was also very helpful!

We like this place, great ambiance & the food was good. But I also thought the food was a slightly on the "sweet" side. I understand the concept of balance, but everything had an underlying sweetness to it. I think of traditional Mex food to be spicy, this had zero. The food was flavorful but had no KICK - that's what I want! 

PS: if you're trying to eat low carb, this is not the place for you. It would be nice if they offered some low carb & healthy options though.

Even their house-made habanero sauce (which I had to ask for to help add some spice) had a weird sweet/vinegary/burnt taste. It was spicy but the flavors were definitely way off ......

Not a fancy sit down place where women make salsa table side, music and margaritas are flowing and food mediocre.....this is the real deal!!!! Best home made corn tortillas, best fish tacos, best beans, everything I have ever eaten here is amazing.....one of the BEST Mexican joints in this city. If you have not experienced this place, you are missing out big time!

I ordered the grown up griiled cheese today....roasted pork with provided cheese on Italian bread. The pork tasted like dirty grill and was very greasy. My husband had the chipolte brisket steak. He said it was OK. The bread fell apart and the brisket was in big chunks

The food and service were mediocre; nothing exceptional or out of this world. The decor of the place though is upscale and gives an air of luxury.

I had the fillet mignon with mashed potatoes. Both could have been better - the steak was medium rare on the inside as I asked but slightly burned on the outside. The mashed potatoes tasted good but lacked a bit of salt.

Still getting unwanted advertisements, sales pitches for life insurance, emails for their products.  Harassing your current customers with unwanted mailings and junk email has only one result. Will try contacting ICCU one more time...then I'm closing my account. Their marketing style is just too obviously aggressive for my tastes.
Excellent NY strip steaks, perfectly seasoned and cooked. The roasted salmon is also wonderful. Exceptional are the roasted mussels.

I had brunch here last weekend.  I started with the beet salad, which was very nice.  My friend got the potato pancakes and lox.  I tasted the pancakes, which were good, but could have been crisper on the outside.  I had the short ribs and eggs over easy.  My meat is sweet, it's cooked with some dried fruit, and I'm not a bug fan of sweet with my eggs.  
I'd go back, but I'd remember to bring some bubbly so I could have a mimosa (BYOB!), though there is a liquor store right next door which is super convenient.  

We had a weird experience at the end of our meal where we couldn't use the bathroom because out waiter had gone in and not come out (like at least 15 minutes).  It was a pretty uncomfortable situation.

We have transferred to St. Louis for work, and are staying here until our home sells. Thus far, this has been almost 3 months.  We have had great experiences 90% of the time.  Rob, Chris, Mickey, Jim, and Jessica are fantastic. Jackie and Roberta are always atrocious and rude, and have almost caused us to rethink staying here. However, the 5 mentioned above always remind us why we do. Rooms are cleaned daily if you are out of your room by noon. Price is extremely reasonable. Very secure parking, but their staff is terrible.  Don't think the garage is staffed by Ramada, though. Rooms could stand a few updates (TVs, etc).  But, overall great place for the price.

I've been looking for the best sub in st. Pete. And I found it here. I have lived down the street for 3 years. Now I'm moving to Las Vegas and I love the beach and st. Pete. Is the nices place I ever lived.  The second thing I'm going to miss Mazzaro's  I have had a lot of subs. This is the one. Best feeling I get is going on a off day that there not to pack. Then getting my number 20 in 15 minutes. But will wait for it. Never been over half hour.

Pretty cool modern gastro pub on St Pete downtown strip. Great spot for people watching. They offer an array of house specialty concocted drinks. I tried the Chop Top martini (Grey Goose Melon, Pear Vodka, Chili Ginger Rosemary, kungfu girl Riesling). It was prepped well, a little sweet for my taste but I enjoyed the different complexities. Then I ordered the New Orleans Style Blackened Shrimp Po Boy . OMG, I was impressed! The sandwich had generous amount of shrimp which had nice texture w/ snappy crunch. The marinate was on point too. Truffle fries were tasty as well. Good crunch and not limpy. Bartenders / servers were friendly. One of them explained to me the different ingredients of their most popular drinks.

I'm not sure the food rates a solid 3 star rating, but the overall experience probably does.

It's not great.  But, some of the dishes are pretty darn good.  The price is right, and it seems like they're constantly cleaning, which is a good think in a buffet style restaurant!

My favorites are the Coconut Chicken and the Peanut Chicken, they seem to be a cut above similar dishes at other Chinese Buffets.  The rest of the food?  It's hot, fresh, and filling, if a bit bland.

It's one of those places I stop when I'm hungry and don't want to spend a lot of money, but still get a good meal.  However, I wouldn't plan a special occasion here.

We moved into a new-for-us house and at first it appeared that the carpets were okay. We had painters come two days before our big move in day and when they were on the floor doing the trim they mentioned the carpets smelled like cats had peed on it. We do know the previous owners had cats so I called Brothers Carpet Busters and they were able to schedule me in the very next day. I spoke with Daniel who was very courteous and professional and he is also the one who came out to clean. He and his partner did an amazing job and my husband and I are extremely pleased. They were even able to remove dark blue paint left on the carpet the previous day by the painters!
a/c not working on hot days in summer of2011 !!! cockroaches on sidewalks going into rooms !!! manager was screaming at renters !!!

I don't believe the name is derived from the street name, since this is the second location of Berix in town...  

Anyway, I stopped in for lunch the other day and had the doner kebab.  Please note this has nothing to do with the more familiar shish kebab we all know.  It's a sandwich, plain and simple.  I have never had this dish in the US, only in Germany.  Over there it's callled doner kebap and there are lots of places that specialize in it.  It was always cut from a skewer and it had the look of stacked pork steaks.  The taste was much stronger there (not a surprise). Heavier on the garlic, I think.  The version here is pretty much a gyro on bread.   It was very good bread - billowy and soft, and the ingredients were all quite tasty.  It was big - probably enough for two to split due to the big roll.   The best part might have been the price at $4.79.  It's cheaper than a subway footlong!!!! Plus about 15 times more tasty.  

As noted in the other review, this place is probably the nicest fast food joint in town.  Beautiful stonework on the fireplace (yes fireplace).

Counter service was a little laid back, but okay I guess.  Not sure what would happen if I came when they were busy...  

Language barrier?   Well the first thing she said to me was...well I'm not sure, but it wasn't English.  I gave her my typical dumb look.  After that, we got along fine.  

Some of the other dishes looked pretty tasty.  Breakfast is served, although it starts at 9, which is kind of late, really.  I guess Bosnians like to sleep in more than my 4-yr-old daughter.

If you want to try bosnian in a familiar fast food setting, this is a good place to start.   Maybe do a little menu research before you arrive.

Good hamburgers and a great place to bring kids. Had the roasted chili burger one night, and the California burger another, and both were very good. The onion rings were fantastic, but I could have passed on the fries. It can definitely be a cluster f here, but the food is really good so I would definitely come back.

The staff of Soffiato Via did an amazing job getting my bridesmaids and myself looking amazing for my April 14th wedding! Everyone looked amazing and our hair and make-up lasted all day! Thanks for making us look amazing on my wedding day! It was the best day!

I am going to have to downgrade my rating of this place. It used to be a great place to take your animal. Not so much anymore. We have literally been a patient of this clinic since 1994. With every visit until recently I have felt that that we were a valued customer and the front desk has always been helpful and able to work us in. My cat has been having issues with her ears and I called in. I explained that I have to work and need an after hours (after 5) appointment. I tried to get 2 Saturdays in a row but they were full and unwilling to work us in. The latest they could give me was 530 on a weekday. Since I work until 5 and live 30 min away, that is not going to work. Old customers don't matter I guess. I am taking my business and my cat elsewhere.

One great physical therapy? Go here. Individual time and attention is taken to make sure that you get the best care options for your issues. All the employees are kind, considerate, and actually care about you and your health.
Super friendly staff, lots of sampling. All local beers worth the trip as its sorta off the beaten trail.

First time here today and my family and I had a pleasant experience. Meiling was our server and she was phenomenal. She would check on us, refilled our drinks and ask if we needed anything else. The food we ordered was delicious! We ordered the French toast with guava, Monte Cristo, Route 66 and the Huevos Avocado...every plate was very tasty and delicious! We will definitely be going back!

All i can say is HONEY CRISTO!!!!!........................
Wife had the breakfast bomb and said it was good. But F that.... 
HONEY CRISTO BABY BABYYYYYYY
( Biggie voice) 
Feel like Biggie right now tho. Full!

This little gem is hidden behind the old abandonded Joe O'Maila's Market at 56th and Fall Creek Parkway.  

Jane is the owner's wife (her husband's name escapes me, but he's always in the kitchen cooking away!) and they are both good people.  Ask her nicely and she'll show you a picture of her son, now a loveable toddler!  Plates are taken quickly, drinks filled when half gone, very awesome service!

The food is actually very good.  You have the typical Chinese buffet offerings, (chicken and broccoli, steamed dumplings, fried rice, lo mein noodles, sesame green beans, general tso's chicken, and more) and I like that the veggies are actually crispy and still have some color!  They also have a menu that you can order from if you wish.  From the menu I reccommend the Crispy Honey Chicken, a mixture of chicken, with slivers of carrot and green beans in a flavorful sauce, served with white rice.  It usually comes with hot peppers but my husband isn't a fan of hot so he orders it without them, they are always happy to accomodate!  They also have the standard ice cream machine.  No toppings to really speak of, just sprinkles and chocolate/carmel sauces.

All in all, this is the go-to place when my family and I want Chinese food.  We always get great service, great food and at a great price.  Highly reccommended!

My family and I went on the Steamboat Natchez tour on our first full day in New Orleans. We are from Connecticut so we hadn't really seen anything like it and we enjoyed ourselves a lot. We went on a Sunday early afternoon in May 2014.

I would say there are three groups of people on this boat.  People who came for the brunch buffet, people who came to learn about the area/pay attention to the tour, and those who came to lounge on a boat with drinks.  Whichever reason you're interested in it for-there's potential for a good time. 

I was on board for the tour part, we opted out of the brunch due to some mediocre reviews about it. I wanted to be able to see everything the tour guide was talking about. We were advised to board early to get a seat on the front left side--but there were plenty of seats even after everyone was aboard.  Even if you don't opt for the brunch there is still plenty of food you can buy at the bar/snack bar. I got a frozen margarita, that was pretty nice. 

We enjoyed the guided tour portion of the ride, learned a lot about the area (being Yankees, we knew absolutely nothing when we started) My mother especially liked the voice of the gentleman giving the tour over the loud speaker--she said it reminded her of Disney World. 

They play the calliope when its time to set sail. Try not to stand too close to it, its SUPER loud. I liked it a lot more when I was several blocks away in the French Quarter and the distance created a decibal buffer.  

Don't forget your sunscreen!

Final stop before we fly out! This place is always clean and the staff is very friendly, they always remember to double bag my order but that doesn't quiet the flavorful aroma as I slide through the security I'm all the envy!
#bestriceinthelou #lifeofaflygirl #ihadallthepeoeontheplaneaskingiFtheheavenlysmellwastheirfirstclassmeal #uhhhhnope

Visited St. Louis for an event within the Delmar Loop, Pi was the choice for lunch. The BLT Salad was great but a little too salty for me, the ingredients were fresh and the waiter spoke highly about partnering with local companies for products which was great. Delmar pizza was also great, fresh & hot. The "pickles" were also good however the cucumbers were not too fresh to be the pickles most expect.

Beautiful place, Excellent music, and friendly staff. The singer in the music trio had an angelic voice. The brandy punch and pork chop with greens tasted yummy. The service was too slow! One guy would bring out the food and sit it on the tray next to the table and it took the waiter too long to actually give us the food. For one dish the host ended up passing out our plates. So if you don't have any other plans for the day, this is an excellent place to experience.

They now carry Vincent Van Doughnuts!!!  I didn't think this place could get any better...but they're always intelligently experimenting!

Staff is knowledgeable, friendly, and accommodating.

My go-tos are the salmon tartine and the roasted chicken sandwich.

My ONLY regret about this place is that I work way outside their catering radius...

Hard to believe this place was under 20 feet of water just a year ago, 
Literally Under Water ! 

The Opry Mills Mall is still washed away, Bass Pro Shop is the only store open as of yet.

What tasty beverages at this otherwise tourist trap of a destination. 

Worth the drive and parking hassle. Try the IPA and chill with your friends or walk around outside. You can drink while you shop. I'm sure the Quakers are not happy about this loophole. 

Enjoy the day and grab a memorable cold one with the ones you love. 

Worth the line.
The bartenders here are really knowledgeable. The food is delicious. I'm giving it a 4 because it's a little expensive and, sometimes, the bartenders can be a little slow.

I was so delighted by my wedding services with Cassidy Rae Events that I am writing my first ever Yelp review.  Here are a few details to show you how amazing Cassidy really is: 

1. Cassidy is incredibly organized, patient, and professional.  She provided us detailed timelines and schedules that alleviated loads of stress from the pre-wedding and day-of planning.  Throughout the planning process she responded quickly to ideas or concerns, and was an extremely reliable guide.  Her attention to detail and knowledge of the industry helped us make the best decisions possible to have both the wedding we wanted and one that we could afford.  

2. Cassidy coordinated an amazing team of vendors who worked together seamlessly to create a perfect wedding day.  Every vendor Cassidy suggested was professional, within our budget and a delight to work with.  Both Cassidy and our photographer came to the wedding rehearsal to get acquainted with our family, and to discuss the set-up with the venue staff.  On the day-of she coordinated the set-up with all the vendors and put the finishing touches on our décor.  She was so dependable and did such a great job communicating with our vendors that it really allowed us to enjoy precious time with our friends and family before the wedding. 

3.  Cassidy's dependability and attentiveness are unmatched.  Every time I started to worry over something it turned out that she had already thought of it and had taken steps to either avoid or remedy it.  She even had an emergency cosmetics bag ready for me on the wedding day!  I really can't express how essential she was in helping us have a stress free wedding.                 

After working with Cassidy it is clear that she has an inherent passion for this industry and for making her clients happy.  She went well above and beyond to help us achieve our perfect wedding, and was truly excited to be a part of it.  It was SUCH a pleasure to work with her!  We got so many compliments on our wedding, and are beyond thankful to have been able to enjoy our special day thanks to the superb work of Cassidy Rae Events!

Great friendly service, being new to the area Jackie was a delight to have. We all had breakfast  for dinner, which was filling and good.   Will be back for something different, maybe even the scrapple, which I had never had before.  Tastes like sausage.

Cycling my way through coffee shops in Fishtown. I had a great latte here. Baristas were pleasant enough and knew their coffee well. Unfortunately there just isn't too much seating here due to the weird shape of the building so it gets crowded, but if you snag a spot it is a great place to do some work. Love the outdoor sidewalk seating when I want to read a book with my dog and relax.

With 1200+ reviews, and 4.5 stars it's pretty obvious that PnP is a beloved Tucson spot. I can see why - I loved it too!

The space is small and simple with a generous patio (which wasn't open on our visit because it was "cold"). Prepare to have a hard time making a food decision as everything on the menu looks great. I opted for biscuits and gravy with eggs and a side of turkey sausage. 

Can we talk about those biscuits? They're huge, like the size of my face huge, and perfectly fluffy and topped with oh-so-good sausage gravy.

Can we talk about my eggs? PERFECTLY cooked. PERFECTLY. 

Can we talk about their housemade sausage? The turkey is a little spicy and the pork version is wonderfully seasoned. If you eat meat and don't order one of these, I am sad for you. 

Finally, can we talk about Matt? If Matt has your table you're going to have a good time because he's pretty great. 

Two thumbs up!

Great move by B&N to take over the old Border's space.  This spot was meant to be an upscale retail bookstore.  This can only help them because there were people that did not even know that there was a B&N on the other side of the bridge and shopped here all the time.  Bad news for the little shops over on the other side, though.  However, if the River's Edge development is any indication, the right mix of national and local tenants, along with a pricy facelift, will bring back the old B&N strip.

Now to the new B&N!  It's clean, bright and organized.  It's also very roomy.  Not overcrowded like some bookstores are.  Maybe because they don't have much of a music selection (at least I did not see one) and that helped bring about space.  One thing that WILL keep them in business is the brilliant kids section.  It takes up the back third of the store!  It is so vibrant with colors and layout that it will definitely help kids start or continue their love of reading... and lead to future adult customers, who will be most likely buying their Nooks from here.

Need some new photos from Yelpers!

My first every fortune reading of any kind! Can't say I wasn't some what skeptical, still excited and curious regardless.

There are so many psychic reading being offered in New Orleans. I've always wanted to try it. So what's better place to have my first experience than here right? I had to depend on Yelp (again) to help me decide. Didn't have the time, or really wanted to pay hundreds of dollars for several different ones. 

We happened to walk by Earth Odyssey and I recognized the name from Yelp. Came in to make an appointment. They were fully booked for that day (we were leaving the next day), but said they'll take me in for the last appointment. Awesome!

The ladies here are all so nice and friendly. While waiting for my turn, I had some time to look around the store. They have so manyyyyyyy things that you can get here as far as jewelry, energy rocks, souvenirs, etc...

Overall, my reading went fairly well. She was able to tell me a few things about myself and my current situation that a complete strangers wouldn't know otherwise. At the same time, there wasn't much detail of anything about the future, but that wasn't surprising. The only down side is, because I was the last customer of the day, she did my reading a little too quick. It lasted maybe 15-20mins, compares to the one that went in before me, hers lasted close to 30-40mins. Lesson learned, I would definitely do another one, but would not schedule anything close to their closing time.

I have driven PAST Blake's in Deming, NM on my way out of Hatch so many times and always thought to myself, "Huh, I really should try them out." But I never do because I just want to get home to Tucson and to be honest, 9 times out of 10 I just put a Sparky's green chile cheeseburger in my belly so I wasn't hungry. When Blake's came to Tucson, I was really excited!!!

Don't believe the hype. The green chile cheeseburger at Blake's is a mediocre burger overall with the saving grace being the green chile. The green chile is delicious but not very hot, at least for my taste but that's not where I find fault with this burger. The actual burger is greasy and just a whatever burger. Mine was thrown together so sloppily that I had more onions and tomatoes off the bun than on it. I literally had to put my burger back together before I could eat it. And then the grease started dripping off my hands. Honestly, I would compare the "burger" part of my sandwich to any old fast food place but priced much higher. We also had seasoned fries which were good and onion rings which were not. The size of the order of onion rings for the price was NOT a bargain at all.

So I'm glad I finally tried Blake's but I really don't think I'll be back. Especially when the green chile double cheeseburger I had at Whataburger was actually better but then again, my judgement on that one may have been clouded by a hangover.

I needed a special order cupcake on short notice, customized for a special occasion, and Sugar Rush was awesome. While they weren't able to do exactly what I needed, they offered solutions that worked just as well. The red velvet cupcakes were great. The other options looked great, and we'll be back for more.

As there are several Mexican food joints around Tucson, this is my go to favorite, as I have found that I have several favorites this tops the list.  Great service, a great location and the decor is out of this world. If you have not tried this place yet you must.  It is the first place we take anyone wanting to try real Mexican food in Tucson.

Great breakfast spot and we went during the week so it was not crowded at all! Let me tell you, the grits, if you like grits, to die for! I would go back just for the grits! I had eggs, pancakes and sausage which were all good, the pancakes could have been brought out sooner, but that's just me being picky, I prefer my food brought out piping hot . Did I mention the grits were great?!!
Hosting a party here in June and was assisted by the lovely staff in planning the event. The samosas were heavenly!

So I came for lunch buffet around 12:30 pm. The food has not been replenished even after asking for. The tandoori chicken pan had one piece and another guest took it. Staff was more into watching Indian movies than to take care of the buffet line. It is now 12:55 the only items replenished were Naan an a cabbage dish. 
What I ate was good but I don't think the ownership pays attention
I called to set up an appointment and gather further information and received no follow up call. Definitely will not be giving them any business anytime soon.

I like the *idea* of Marathon more than I actually like going there. I have a weekly appt near this place and tried going here afterwards for some readin' and eatin' (aka "I have no friends and am by myself and hunnnngry"). I almost always order the chicken salad sandwich with a side salad and it's tasty, for sure. Everything is fresh and all that. But it's not food-gasmic, you know? Also, I know this shouldn't be a complaint, but the service is too fast. I like to sit and wait a while and here I feel rushed, which ruins the lazy late lunch vibe I'm trying to get going.

OTF is a great place for everyone of all fitness levels to workout. From just starting out to the elite athletes. They give a great variety of exercises, no same routine twice in a week. We use the treadmill and rowers all the time and it's always different. The coaches are awesome and will push you to be your best! Even if you don't feel like working out, still go and you'll feel better afterwards.

Love this place.. Atmosphere is amazing.. Every employee is polite, happy and very courteous.. it makes me happy to be here every single time..I never order burgers anyplace else.. but the burgers here are amazing!!! I highly recommend Islands to everybody!! Don't miss out

Service is awesome!!! I was greeted by an incredibly friendly man behind the counter, he then decided to walk us through the menu and give suggestions about what we should order. We had stopped by on Tuesday, which is taco night. The special is 2 tacos and rice. I got 1 shrimp and 1 beef and my friend got one chicken and 1 beef. Each taco is topped with a kimche inspired slaw and homemade sauce. I liked the beef taco the best, but they were all good. We decided to upgrade our rice to fried for an extra $1. I got the spicy rice and my friend got plain. The spicy rice is no joke it was full of hot goodness. I also got an order of dumplings. They were very good. 

After our meal the chef came out to make sure that we liked our dinner and ask how we heard about the restaurant. 

I will be back. Good prices, good good and good service.

Cate Zone is pretty authentic Dongbei Chinese food, and their skewers taste just like the ones found on the streets of Beijing. 

Other highlights include the crispy fried pork and the sauteed eggplant. The candied potatoes are good but messy. We also enjoyed the chicken mushroom soup with clear noodles. 

Downsides: small space, long waits.

I love this place! Been going to the brandon store since they opened..... Soooooo happy they are in south Tampa now! The store is so nice and clean and they have tons of great deals and everyone is very nice :)

Really enjoyed the Relax the Back class with Michelle! A lot of great information, warm friendly instruction and I left feeling empowered. What a peaceful atmosphere and helpful classes to get back on track with my yoga practice.

Solid beer and burger joint.  I'm giving it 4 stars since everybody I went with liked their grub and beers.  I had a beer that was soaked in a bourbon barrel that was too strong for my liking, so ask to taste it before you order it, they give samples!

More like 2.5.   I want to like this place

My Kiwi, pear, carrot, wheat grass juice drink was good....just not $12 good.
I get that its Doylestown and "healthy", but that sort of price point precludes repeat business.  

Ditch the corny lab coats

I really like In Riva! The atmosphere is great- especially if you can sit outside in the temperate months. As other reviewers have mentioned, the portion sizes are **really** small for what you get. Back when they had tortellini on the menu, I was shocked to be presented with approximately 8 little tortellinis in a bowl. Granted, they're some of the best pasta I've ever tasted, but damnit it was brunch and I was hungover and ready for a big bowl of pasta. Pizza definitely seems to be the way to go if you're looking for filling - and you could totally demolish one of those by yourself. You'll love the food but be prepared to order a lot of it!

Wonderful wings!  We got the Cajun Creole, Lemon Pepper, Cajun Ranch and 0017.  Totally delish!!  The ladies taking care of us made us feel right at home.  Why I haven't come in sooner is a mystery to me.  Don't make the same mistake!  Come in and get these delicious wings with friendly service.

helpful staff, never had a bad wait time;
normally i go in the evenings after work

This looks and feels like a zoo jail. The animals look like they are depressed and in not good health. Their food (raw meat) was thrown on the ground and the animals didn't even want to eat it. Flies everywhere, filthy water. There were 2 camels there and they both looked to be in very bad condition. I asked the worker in the gift shop about the camels and she told me that it was normal for the camel to look like he had a broken jaw because that's what the males do to attract a female. The lion looked emaciated and was very lethargic; granted he was old, but he just didn't look good at all. I left this place with a heavy heart for those poor animals.
Super crowded, staff are pretty good at being salesman. Don't believe that prices change daily and they will try to sell you a membership if you use a guest pass.
Mi Caribe is a place to go and have a decent Spanish, Caribbean foods. The portion was enough to enjoy desert.
Thanks for all the great sushi! We will definitely be back, great beer as well, I'll see you all there next time.
Great ice cream, all home made the day of. Limited lactose free ice cream, hopefully changes soon! Definitely recommend. This place is worth it!

I had gone a few times when they had first opened and it was rough. the service was rough, the food was different each time. I haven't sat at a table since then as, noted in other reviews, the service was very slooow. I've sat at the bar since, though, and continued to enjoy the bar, which has a number of t.v.s.
I think their menu is cool and trendy, different than regular bar food. I am way into the homemade truffle potato chips and the the white bean bruschetta. Those are under the $4 bar menu. i've also enjoyed the bacon dusted calamari, which was real tasty.
One time, my sister ordered the applesauce something or other wings...they were very bland and tasted like nothing other than warm applesauce. The sauce could've used some bbq sauce and brown sugar. 
My boyfriend had the steak sandwich at one point, which he described to be o.k.
That time we also ordered fried oreos. I love fried oreos, i did not love these. There was way too much batter and they were way overcooked. 
I think their drinks a little pricey and their missing an opportunity on their beer selection. I drink beer and seek out craft beer spots, and I am not alone...there are a lot of beers on tap but they  mostly include PBR, sam adams, guinness, coors, bud, yuengling. The best beers they have (or at least had, I haven't been in awhile) were goose island, victory and magic hat., which are still to me just okay and not unique. Definitely need to branch out and get some more craft beers to live up to their name. i understand the type of people that may patron this bar are your blue collar, budweiser type crowd for the most part...but what's to say doing fun beer tasting nights or food/beer dinners wouldn't open up a new world to those folks?
Still, it's better than it's competitor, Bung's. There! I said it.

This is a Manayunk summer staple. My sweet tooth is absolutely insatiable but Whirled Peace keeps it at bay. The selection of froyo is a little small but extremely tasty. I recommend the pineapple sorbet, surf-something. It's juicy and refreshing. I usually opt for classic tart which is creamy and not too icy. 

Good array of topping, I love the mochi balls and bursting boba, usually strawberry or mango flavored. The smoothies are definitely a great option. You select your yogurt and a juice, throw in whatever toppings float your boat, and it all gets blended into a nice glass of tastiness. 

Not the most impressive froyo joint but Manayunk really lacks dessert shops, so I am very thankful for Whirled Peace.

So glad this place opened in the neighborhood.  I have been here quite a few times now for lunch and dinner and it is consistently delicious. The best deal is to just get a whole bunch of all the delicious tacos.  The mahi mahi and carne are my favorite!

I really was not in this place long enough to say too much. I know right when we walked in I got a chain feel about this place, reminds me of a Disney Epcot Beer Garden or TGI Fridays stuff hanging from the wall...did not have the local bar feel. We stopped in to have drink after dinner. We grabbed a table and then to my delight I saw a whole shelf of games you can play at your table. So, after grabbing the last cards against humanity we played at the table for an hour laughing way to loud and making horrible card combinations. Since we stuck to sitting at a table we relied on a waitress and I have to say service was pretty slow and they were not super friendly. But, I do love the whole games aspect and would recommend this place for a group and of course a round of cards against humanity.

The food here is pretty delicious. The only thing I can complain about is the portion sizes... that seems to be more of an issue when we get take out, but maybe it is the illusion of the dishes when we dine in. And sometimes there is some inconsistency with the pizza thickness, since I always order a pizza, have noticed a couple of times! 
The whipped ricotta I do have to say is so delicious and despite the inconsistency of the thickness of the pizza, every pizza we have ever tried has been so good. The specialty cocktails are fun and I have enjoyed many of them. The salads are creative as well as the pastas. 
Love coming here! We will be back!

This is part of the gold course, so it was a very dead atmosphere when we went for dinner. The service was terribly slow. It was known for burgers and shakes, both were so rich and gross I could not eat them. Sadly, I would have preferred regular fast food. The shuttle system is extremely slow, so make sure you take your rental car or prepare for a long walk.

Great restaurant for breakfast or brunch! I started with a mango mimosa which was excellent! My boyfriend ordered the Bourbon Street Breakfast Platter mainly because it came with a shot of bourbon! Ha! I tried his pancakes and they were good. We both really LOVED the candied bacon. Since the bourbon came out in the same container as the syrup we were a little confused. Did we pour it over the pancakes? Take it like a shot? We just did both in the end and it was great. Good bourbon, lol. I ordered the shrimp & grits which were also super tasty and the grits were the star of the plate! BEST grits! I took off one star only because plating was kind of thrown together and not as pretty as the same dishes I've seen on Yelp.

Best beer store in Philly and then some.  The selection is huge and I've yet to go to the larger store up in Northern Liberties.

I enjoy the fact that I can pick up a good selection of the beers I used to drink back home (including my home town favourite Sam Smiths, the best bitter in England) as well as a lot of the beers I have discovered while doing fieldwork around the world (Coopers from Australia, to mention one great brew).

Sure, you occasionally get a dud (please don't drink the Hambleton Sugar Ale, it's made from Molasses and really was horrid, I should have payed more attention to the label) but that is only to be expected with a selection like this and I guess someone out there in Philly probably thinks my dud is the best bottle of fermented hops to ever run across their lips...

The selection of beer glasses from around the world (or stolen from the nearest pub with authentic glasses, who knows) are great and I always look forward to my birthday and a few more pieces of drinking paraphernalia .

I hear it also sells other things apart from beer, I've never noticed them though...

I was once a regular at Pho Hoa in South Philly until I moved to the North East. This restaurant is probably one of my favorite Vietnamese restaurants to eat at. They make their pho quickly and send it out to you asap. The servers are on point when you need anything at all and a few remember me and what I usually order. I also recommend trying the bubble tea here as well. Great place.

I wasn't expecting much of this place--I looks like one of those chains with mediocre Mexican food, and the fact that it's in a strip mall doesn't help the appearance. However, having been to Fiesta Maya twice now, I can say that his joint proves that looks can be deceiving. My husband has had the fish tacos both times we went, and he's a fan. I've had the taco salad (nothing miraculous, mind you, but a step above the standard issue taco salads available elsewhere) and none of their shockingly good beef mole tamales. My only gripe is that it's not possible to get a side of mole sauce to go with it (in fact, I'd up this to five stars if I could get a side of mole).

Chips were also good, with very fresh, well-spiced guacamole

I've been frequenting Pia's since 2011, both their Tampa and St. Pete locations. I don't trust anyone else for my waxing needs...their technicians have always been professional, and have done a great job! Love that they stay open late and you can book all services online.

Amazing diversity of sushi and other traditional Japanese foods, affordable, even more affordable during their happy-hour hours! everybody is like fireworks going off in your mouth, especially if you get the tempura spicy tuna rolls!!  5/5

This place place has some of the best spicy food I have ever tasted, we had cumin crusted lamb and chilled beef with tripe in a chilli oil which was out of this world. If you do not like spice stick to the Chinese side of the menu! The only reason I did not give it the full five star is the service was very slow and the interior is very plain.
But the food is worth the bad service!
Clean. Friendly staff. Well organized and easy to find your products. Grooming services is very good here. Returning items is super easy. This is my preferred and local store!

I had been waiting to go to Jazmine for what seemed like years, ever since we moved to the south meadows. My lovely wife straight up refuses to eat "Chinese food" and we take most meals together, therefore, no Jazmine. That was until I discovered that they have a sushi bar! Kristen loves sushi (as do I) so a date night (with no kids) finally came along and whammy!! Time for Jazmine. I had the Mongolian beef and crispy fried noodles with chicken, Kristen had all you can eat sushi. The food was good. Wasn't great, not revolutionary by any stretch, but if you dig Chinese food and sushi, you will not be disappointed with the food. The service however was weird. Basically we got a server who looked distraught, we asked, she said that she had messed a few things up at other tables and was in the "dog house" with the manager. (Your not supposed to use the "d" word at a Chinese restaurant). The rest of the night several servers and the head chef would come by and ask us  if everything was ok, as if the young lady couldn't handle taking care of us. She was great, and they treated her poorly right in front of us, it was just super awkward. Anyhow, there's not much good solid Chinese food in Reno, especially in the south meadows area. This place is pretty darn good. Also they have an all-you-can-eat sushi lunch that's pretty affordable.

Nestled in the best casino in Reno is the best lounge on the planet, The Fireside.  The atmosphere alone makes it a must-visit, but what really separates The Fireside from all other contenders is the world-class service I always....and I mean, always..receive when I take a seat at the bar.  Thank you, Vaugn!  Thank you, Caitlin!  Thank you, Mark!  Thank you Riana!  You all deserve a big, fat raise!  See you soon for another round (or three) of killer margaritas!

We are big take out people so decided to give this place a try, we never made it to the Clayton  location.  We got the blue ribbon burger, green chile burger, fries and onion rings.  The burgers were both good, we both agreed the fries were great and could have done without the onion rings. Our order was not quite done when I went in to pick it up but by the time I paid it was ready to go.  As soon as I got into the car I tried an onion ring and it was cold and hard so it wasn't the travel that did those in.  Burgers were cooked to the requested temp and my husband thought the pickles were delish.

The Cantina's mesquite chicken burrito is hands down the best Mexican food in Reno/Sparks. The margaritas are always good, as are the fajitas.
I've never had anything less than good service each time I've eaten there.
Best Mexican restaurant in the area.

Kung Fu Noodles, was a new and working out the kinks while, simultaneously, my lover and I were passing by on our way to an appointment, so we ordered quickly and indicated we were in a hurry.    

I received my lunch special in a reasonable time (7-10 minutes), however my lover ordered a noodle dish under the entree section and it took about 25 minutes to come out.  I had literally finished my entire lunch serving before her noodle dish arrived.  My lunch special vegetable assortment was tasty, but my wife's seafood noodles were bland and unremarkable.  Kung Fu Noodles did give us an extra portion of rice at no charge because of the long wait, but I am used to asian places giving unlimited amounts of rice, so it didn't quite compensate for the delay.  We made our appointment, but not comfortably. 

I would give this business 2 stars, except that they are new and working out the kinks, and I don't want to rain on their parade out of the gate, and I am their first reviewer, and I want new businesses to make it.

Was really impressed with my experience at Libertine Liquor Bar; definitely the total package. The space is tasteful, modern and upscale - the dim lighting helps create an intimate vibe and the noise level energetic but not overbearing. The staff we encountered were wonderful; friendly, efficient and helpful. The craft cocktails are thoughtful and creative with a vast, well laid out menu; they were on par with Chicago's top cocktail bars. The only oddity was it appeared all cocktails were shaken - even one's that were nearly pure booze, perhaps to put on a show. I particularly loved the rye based cocktail with Fernet Branca, coffee and Angostura bitters.The food is daring, modern and well executed; I strongly recommend the Deviled Eggs - such a cool presentation and phenomenal taste. Quality ingredients are utilized both for the cocktails (i.e. all house made mixers) and the cuisine. We chose to sit at the long bar and greatly enjoyed being able to watch and interact with the bartenders. Puck was our primary server and I loved all three of his cocktails (the name of the bartender who created each cocktail is listed on the menu; the first one of Puck's I tried was so wonderful I opted to keep choosing his creations). While Libertine is not inexpensive, it is well worth it considering the ambiance and quality. Definitely a place we look forward to returning to next time we are in town.

Worst customer service at rental counter! Never explained about surpass for tollway ended up paying twice for tolls. Agent was rude uncooperative caused a lot of anxiety renting POS vehicle! Must work in conjunction with allegiant another poor excuse for a airline! Nickel & dime you!!!!!!

Hands down the best bbq brisket and gelato a buffet has to offer. The meat is succulent with a great smokey flavor. The gelato is made in-house and has plenty of selections such as coffee, strawberry, blueberry, lemon sorbet, mango etc. 

Prime rib is okay. If you go on Fridays,  there's crab and prime rib night. Dungeon crab and snow crab is served and is very fresh. The rest of the food is okay. Overall experience was one of the better in Reno. The downside is that they do not offer membership discount. 

Our server was th best! Was attentive, friendly, and took our plates often. 

Will definitely go back.

A late night visit with an old friend on my last night there, brought us to Brewsters for a sampling of some different beers and a few good laughs.

A very modern style restaurant greets you with plenty of noise, seating and very little light. (and yes, I feel like an old man saying that as a complaint)

We had a very sweet waitress who had great knowledge of the various beers we sampled. Some were not what I was looking for, but most were very delicious. I would love to go back and have a bite to eat sometime soon.

My favorite weeknight Philly haunt!!! 
Where to start... I've had makeout sessions here, jumped out the window, nearly killed myself going down the steps to the wc, danced to the jukebox, fallen asleep in the back and of course... drunk and merry.
