It's a typical Philly row-home-turned-irish-style-pub. There's a great fireplace in the back I've never seen lit, and around it are huge, heavy wooden bench seating around 4 massive tables. It's good for a big group. Smaller tables up front and more seating upstairs for proper dining. 

In the front part of the bar are two side windowledges which are perfect to perch on. Forewarning, ledge is about 7 feet from the ground, so if you jump out of them, don't do it in high heels. 

Good beer list though it seems to lack local brews. I'm not much of a beer drinker so it doesn't matter. They carry Pimm's!! The bartenders are fun. (Ask for Eileen by singing or screaming "COME ON EILEEN!!!" She loves that.)

Try the filet and goat cheese sliders. So delicious!!! Food here is much nicer than typical bar fare. The mac and cheese is freshly baked with a good sharp cheddar, there's goat cheese on more than just the sliders, the lamb shank looked delicious though I haven't had it. 

I wish they had outdoor seating. It was such a beautiful spring night the other night which is how i discovered prime window-ledge seating.

Decent shellac manicure - nothing special though. Disappointed with the time it took got them to get me into a seat. They had me sitting in the back room - walking back and forth past me - and no one said a word.

WORTH TRAVELING TO....GREAT SERVICE AND REASONABLE PRICES
I have used Glantzman Subaru since 2001 when we bought our first Subaru legacy.  When it died (age 10) we bought another, a Forester.  The salemen are (surprisingly) honest and the price is reasonable.  What stands out to me about this dealer (after almost 15 years) is the consistency of the service department.  They actually communicate with each other.  The 3 guys who work there are professional pleasant and friendly.

Okay! This is my last for Landry's! I tried, I really did. See after the icky experience on my first review and the monthly delay on a mgr contacting me, I decided to be fair and see if I could leave the restaurant satisfied...on my terms. See when the district mgr finally called me he offered to set up a "VIP service" dinner, that all I had to do was call the mgr and make a reservation...I declined. It would be a fake set up just to make me happy, no thank you. 

Sooo...the bf was craving fish...and I had a hankering for oysters, he mentioned Landry's. We figured hey its 3 blocks down lets go. His first time and my last chance that I was giving...

We walked in, no hostess. She was standing in the middle of the dining room. She saw us...it was not even halfway filled...she took her sweet time to come over, grabbed menus and just asked if it was 2 of us. No 
problem. We were seated. Our server was Emma or Emily. I dont recall, she was as sweet as can be BUT didn't know anything when I asked about oysters. I ordered them anyway against my better judgement...they tasted fishy. Not fresh!!!! I doused them in cocktail sauce. The salad 
with the house dressing was delicious...of course had to request the garlic bread, hands down top 5 best. I ordered crabcakes and he did a sirloin with  a salmon fillet. The plates came out and she made a big emphasis on the plates being hot...they were. But my first bite was lukewarm at best. WHY THE HELL IS THE PLATE HOTTER THAN THE FOOD? my bf's was the same way. His steak was dry, salmon was undercooked and salty
 as hell. Emily asked how everything was and i answered ok. She asked if i wanted a manager, i assured her it wasnt her but no. I have this thing about sending food back. 

We left tipsy tho! The captain's punch was divine as always. However at the end of the day I can't  come here for salad, bread and drinks. The food isnt fresh and clearly reheated. Its overpriced for the crap u get. I really tried. And for it being the bf first time too, he gave it 2 stars.

Great course for the price. I can't find a place where I can pay $20 for a round of golf with a cart and still play a good course. I don't have the kind of money to pay $50 for a round at a course that gets on me if my foursome doesn't get done in 3 hours. If your a regular, you know what I mean by that. I enjoy it plus $12 for a six pack of beer!!!

Best mattress buying experience I have ever had. In fact one of the best customer experiences I have ever had. I came in to the store around 12:15 in the afternoon and was welcomed by Chad. Chad was able to get me a great deal on a great mattress. The best part was I was in a hurry, I would have been sleeping on the floor that night as I had just moved into town that morning and had an apartment rented but no furniture. Chad not only got it delivered that day but the mattress was delivered and set up within 90 minutes from the time I walked into the store. Highly Highly Highly recommend the store, ask for Chad!

And now, by popular demand (and by popular demand I mean my new Yelp friend Nancy P asked), the St. Louis establishment that offers the best fried egg sandwich is....(you should now hear a drum roll somewhere.  I know you already know since it's at the top of the review however, for dramatic effect, pretend you don't know and that you hear drums, please)..... 

SODA FOUNTAIN SQUARE!!  
For the record you should have heard trumpets blaring just then...  

This is a review based solely on their fried egg sandwich.  So, in all the fried egg sandwich joints in all the restaurants in St. Lou, why did I have to pick this one?

Let's start with the bread - Manna from heaven.  Not because the bread is especially unique or freshly baked (it might be - I have no idea).  I appreciate their bread because I am asked which kind of bread I would like.  That doesn't usually happen with a fried egg sandwich. Restaurants rarely do this. They falsely assume that "Wonder" will do.

We're going to move past the egg - it's not difficult to fry an egg and I can't say I know a restaurant that does this badly.  I do a poor job of it, personally, but short order cooks and chefs alike seem to have it down.

Let's address the cheese.  Not only is there cheese on the sandwich at the Soda Fountain Square, but you get to...wait for it..choose your cheese!  AND, Havarti is on the list!

I'm not saying I'm a die hard Havarti fan, but when cheese is an option, the Kraft Single Slice seems to be a favorite of restauranteurs who serve my favorite breakfast entree. So a little gourmet cheese is a surprising delight.

With all of that said, the Soda Fountain Square gets my five stars in honor of their fried egg sandwiches.

Awesome pizza. Awesome staff, they took their time to explain what they have in the menu. Very fast and calls your name before you actually settle on the seat. Nice clean place and have enough space for groups. Would def visit again!

LOVE THIS PIE. Homemade sauce is BOSS. They shred their own cheese, and they make their own dough. In a world of sysco products I feel comfort knowing that NYP still takes the time to make things from scratch. LOCAL GEM!!!!! & they have a huge TV.

Great place for drinks (I've never had food here). It's a nice and quaint place that's perfect for drinks with a small group. There is plenty of table space, great beers on tap, and wonderful service. It's a dark and quiet ambiance...perfect for conversation.

The juices are good. I would skip the rest. Very erratic, I've tried everything (burritos,salads) and it's never the same as the time before.  It's almost like they are winging it each time they make something.  Not cheap by any stretch and anything added is extra.  No hot sauce out but they have some they make which is nasty. Consistently. The people who work there are generally rude and seem irritated to be there. And there are always a lot of people working. I really want to like this place as I am often in the area for business and would love a quick place for something different.

This is becoming our new late night delicious spot. I am giving the food 5 stars and the overall 4 stars. It can be so loud that it's hard to have a conversation. Also not a great spot for Fri/Sat unless you like to be wedged up on top of others and you also happen to have ear plugs on your person. Servers are really friendly and service is quick. Love the hidden patio for a late night in the cool breeze and a good beer. A variety of local and import beers (and a cider) on draft and a drink special every day. 

I'm usually ordering from the late night menu, which includes the apps and pizzas. The spinach and artichoke dip with pita chips is the best I have ever had. Super creamy and full of cheesy goodness. Oh and there are some veggies in it, probably spinach and artichokes, whatever. The wings are phenomenal! Super meaty and the sauce is perfection. The garlic cheese fries aka crack fries are addictive! Olive tapenade = yummy in my tummy, My hands down fav pizza is the Robert Browning. Meats, banana peppers, cheese, covered in spring mix and italian dressing. When you feel compelled to eat a salad, but you really want pizza. I have 2 words Flippin Delicious!

We went to Thai House based on the previous reviews and we were not disappointed. This place is great. We had chicken satay, their special Thai House fried rice with prawns, and and Larb Gai. All were excellent!  And they were not timid with the spice-- when they say hot, they mean it ( so many restaurants disappointingly  wimp out thinking Americans like things milder). The portions were generous and priced VERY reasonably.  The service was attentive, the staff friendly, and the owners charmingly gracious. We loved it here.  If we lived here we'd be regulars, if we ever come to the area  again we will be sure to come back to Thai House for another great meal.

Ten Thousand Villages is nestled in the heart of the Media shopping district and offers a unique selection of affordable gifts for family and friends. Or buy something for yourself, you deserve it!

Ten Thousand Villages is a non-for-profit retailer. Yep, you read that right. It pays fair-trade prices for artisan products from the developing world (no mass produced lead-tainted things from a gritty factory in China here). 

So shopping here is a win-win in the best sense.

(I don't have any connection to Ten Thousand Villages, except as a customer that likes their wares and social philosophy and happens to have visited multiple locations- so if reviews of different locations bug you, PM me, don't flag.)
Love the Naam salad and the Panang curry!!! Coconut soup is also amazing. One of my favorite spots in west philly.

I come here for breakfast alot - the egg & scrapple melted with cheese on a croissant is sooo delicious, and only $3.75. 

However, for as many times as I've been in here, I've now been triggered to write a review.  I actually bought a sandwhich for lunch (usually I have salad and its "ok"), but my chicken sandwhich on croissant was quite dissappointing.  For $8, I got COLD chicken, on an UN-toasted croissant, and the cheese wasn't even melted.  I was expecting a warm grilled chicken on a toasted warm croissant and that is not the case.  If the chicken is going to be served COLD, then it should say so on the menu!!  Like everyone knows cobb salad has cold chicken -- but a "oven roasted chicken" sandwhich as its quoted on the menu should be warm.

Soups are OK, I sampled a few and they were OK.  Not bad, but not good enough to make me buy some.  I tried the veggie, potato leek, and some kind of lentil curry soup.  

I will not spend my lunch money here.  Only breakfast.  

On another note, the staff is always friendly and the atmosphere with new booths, tables, and upstairs seating is really nice.
We bought a Lexus at this place a couple of years ago. The price was good. They were pretty professional from payment process to paperwork.

I came in towards the end of the lunch rush. It was great to people watch all of the locals. I tried their Ellen salad and it was heaven. Its an arugula salad with scallops, salmon and shrimp with a dijon vinaigrette. Simple salad, but when you are using great quality it really makes the difference. I have yet to find something similar in LA. I guess there is only 1 Ellen salad.

NEVER AGAIN. 

EW. 

The food here was awful, the waiters acted like they had much better things to do and the clientele made me feel like I was eating in Penn's cafeteria. I didn't go to Penn for a reason, folks. 

Salmon Tartare: There was no salmon, I'm pretty sure. It was mushy tomatoes and olives in a ring mold with balsamic vinegar from the Christmas Tree Shop drizzled on top.

Striped Bass: First of all, Im pretty sure it was flounder. Second of all, there was no goat cheese as promised. Third of all, it tasted like it had been sitting under a heat lamp all day.

Do yourselves a favor...Go to the rite aid around the corner and buy $140 worth of beef jerkey and cheese balls. It will be a better meal.

xo

Wow. I have NEVER been to a business where the customer service was so terrible. First when I ordered the cupcakes I asked if they did a strawberry shortcake kind of cupcake ( this was for my sisters bday and she celiac and pregnant) cause that's what my sister loves and the girl said yes. I asked if the cupcake would have real strawberries in it and on top of it and she said yes! So I ordered them. I picked up the cupcakes 2 days later and as I walked in to get my cupcakes there were 3 people standing behind the counter talking and NO ONE acknowledged me. I had to say something to get someone to help me. I get the cupcakes and they look ok.. I figured the strawberries were on top as well the inside like the girl said but I didn't see any on top. Ok so I leave and when it's time to serve the cupcakes after dinner, we cut the cupcakes in half for everyone to try and just as I thought NO strawberries. Then everyone takes a bite and spits the cupcakes out all at the same time. It was crazy. The cupcakes tasted HORRIBLE!!!! I couldn't believe it. 
So I tried to call and speak to a manager and she wasn't there. The employee had no clue when the mgr would come in. So I called for 4 days straight and still no mgr was around to help me. They didn't even know her last name or any other way to contact her. I was furious. This place is terrible. When I saw the bad reviews I still took a chance to try them out. Well I guess I should of went with the reviews. I will NEVER COME BACK TO THIS PLACE AGAIN. I even have pics to show how terrible the cupcakes were. Terrible. Disgusted.
Heard the food was great but I personally just love their ice cream :). A little on the pricey side but with the view you get of the fountain center, it's all well worth it.
This place has the best sandwiches, great beer selection and also live blues music Thursday evening and Saturday afternoon. Enough said

What can I tell you something about this restaurant?  The place is CHAMP!  Service is very good.  I ordered prawns in spicy sauce in small pan twice (earlier in the afternoon and again evening) and someone in my group ordered thin onion rings.. they are soo delicious and yummy.  My tasting buds are craving for that sensuality food.  When I visit NOLA, I must go to that place again..have more prawns and onion rings to eat!
Best burger and fries. Very tasty. Yum. Also try the cheesesteak,excellent.  Support our local restaurant's.

I really enjoyed the Buttermilk pancakes here. We came in on a weekday morning and we didn't have a wait. While the food is good, not sure if I would wait in a line around the block like it normally is on the weekend. Coffee could use improvement. Service was excellent.
Everything you could want in an outdoor upscale mall and more!! Love shopping here and there are so many restaurants to choose from whatever your taste!

Yes, only two stars and the food is actually very good. The bad is the same as the other reviewers here: they seem to skimp or ration food and serve dishes with very little "there" there. Just like other reviewers we had the experience of ordering the yummy Salume plate with two types of sliced meat, a potted pork, mustard and another spreadable meat and only two slices of bread!! Only two! When we asked for just one slice of bread to eat the spreads, we were told: No. The chef says you can buy a whole plate of bread, but you cannot have one slice. What???  

This negative experience colored our meal. We let it go of course, and enjoyed our meal but afterwards when discussing our experience the stupid bread thing is what came up. Very short sighted Ava. 

Also, our mussel pasta dish may have had 3 to 5 mussels on a large bowl of noodles. The beet salad was beet in name only. After dinner we all thought the others ate the beets. I doubt we had but 2 pieces. At 7:20 they had run out of all fish. They must have been short on bread too because that was as rare and valuable as diamonds. Too bad. 

The atmosphere wonderful, the food tasty,  and the service pretty good for a new restaurant, but It seems like the management is high on a new restaurant buzz, the bread-stingy chef seems arrogant and is forgetting that the novelty will soon wear off and they will need to earn repeat business. The food is good, but not exceptional in a town with great food. For the best pasta in town try La Terrazza in Ybor City. Five stars here on yelp, a fraction of the price and the cute little Italian owner will give you all the bread you want to sop up the delicious sauce.

Ava management: if you read this please know that I'm rooting for you. I want you to succeed and fulfill your promise and potential. The food is yummy but you have work to do on customer experience. Mine is only one voice of many here trying to tell you the same thing. This is tough love. 

Diners: when you make a reservation demand extra bread or hang up. They will get the message.

Small place, usually a line, always packed.  Somehow the three times I've been there I get right in, get my order which comes out quickly and I always seem to find a seat.

My favorite has to be the Italian beef.  I've told people it's the third best ever so as not to insult certain mother-in-laws.

Love the crushed ice, fountain coke & kettle chips. 

Overall excellent experience every time.

Okay food, lovely service. The roti canai was amazing! Nice and soft with a nice crisp. The curry was the perf amount of spicy. The soya milk with grass jelly tasted a bit watered down and was brown instead of the expected milky white. Ordered fried pearl noodles and replaced it with flat noodles but the sauce was too strong for my taste. The service was great though, our waitress was super friendly and adorable.
Great experience from estimate to completed job. I look forward to working with Rob again in the future! Great product, free shop at home service, expert installation. Thank you!

I was a repeat customer for as long as they have been open, fantastic work, the problem now they are saying they do not do mens clothes, I have lots of work for them but they turn me down because I am male, that is discriminatory and I will not refer them any more business


                                                            Sincerely, Mr F

Cool place. Totally hipster. Food was good, service was excellent price reasonable. You can get vegan and gluten free but they have traditional American healthy food too. And free WiFi.

I will be back and I definitely recommend DeLuxe for breakfast. Only minor distraction: no omelets, but that's only me. This place is really good.

I am so confused by this place.

First off, at the relatively young age of 26, I feel like a total Grandma in here! It's full of kids, and by that I mean the 21 year olds who are trying out bars and clubs for the first time. Most seem even younger than that, and these kids have just not learned bar etiquette yet. You will be stepped on, rammed into, and touched by more sweaty people than you thought possible. The space is small and cramped, so I started to feel quite faint from the heat. If there's one way I would describe this place, it would be amateur; seriously seasoned drinkers and dancers need not even bother. There's also an abundance of extremely annoying bachelorette parties here, with every other song ending in a shout out to a pack of young girls who are clearly binge drinking their way to the hospital. 

Anyway, the music isn't bad. The performers are clearly talented and have a good energy that should not be wasted here. Think an even more depressing Piano Man scenario than the actual song. Speaking of Billy Joel, somebody requested actually Italian Restaurant and the band actually played it. Even though it's one of my favorites, really? Playing Italian Restaurant at a dance club? I was shocked when most of the crowd started singing along and seemed to dig it. I guess people can surprise you sometimes. And I guess that the kids these days like piano bars.

Aside from the piano aspect (which is a welcome change in the club scene), this place is a dump. Their drink menu and prices leave a lot to be desired. All the people clamoring for the never ending supply of Jell-O shots kind of grossed me out. The dancing flat out sucks, and most people just sway in a drunken stupor. Leave this stuff for the amateurs, a better time can be had elsewhere.

Good food the locatio. Isn't the best......but its the best thing I can get next to going into philly to get golden krust. The service is a bit cold.........but the jerk is muuuuuuuch hotter!!!!! 

All in all its a nice place to pick up a quick bite......of some down home jamican food!!!! Lol

Wish  people who are in the business of selling burgers  would have a great deal more pride in their respective companies and individuals. Teller in drive tru apparently is not happy  about working nights and in some need of attitude adjustment. Was not helpful in the slightest. Came around drive-thru for a 2nd order and she doesn't acknowledges that the only vehicle  is there waiting to get food . Sat in front of the prompter so long vehicle  #2 pulled up ,waited for a few minutes and drove off angrily

True artistry in a diverse array of coffee and tea based beverages. But for those who are looking to go clean with no caffeine they have infused waters and other creative beverages
If you sit at the small red table out front and face south and look 180° you might think you're in California for a moment with the mid century modern buildings around you and the West Coast vibe the shop gives off

I decided to follow the yelp for lunch while visiting Indianapolis. And boy it was great. I had Jambalaya and it was very flavorful. The staffs were super friendly. I didn't have cash and they offered to feed me first before going to ATM across the street.  I'll bring some friends later, with cash, of course.

Four of us had lunch at the Des Peres location. Loved the patio area, although too cold yet. Excellent, friendly service!  Food - needs some work. French fries are terrible (and I love good fries!)'. Two had the fish sandwich. Two of the three pieces were mushy and inedible. Also, there was far more bun than fish. With a little work in the kitchen, this will be a nice addition to the area

Great espresso and amazing tea selection. Perfect for both coffee and tea lovers. Espresso was bold yet smooth. With delicious chocolate notes. They carried White2tea as well as a few others. The tea list was very extensive with a fantastic selection of everything from herbal to puerh.

Ordered delivery from here for the first time today. Normally, I would never review a place based on just their delivery service, but I felt compelled to based on the kindness extended to me today. I am at home, sick, and all I wanted was a bowl of homemade soup. Unfortunately for me, I'm not a cook and in any case, wasn't feeling up to making anything or leaving the house at all. Upon browsing through Yelp, I found the menu for Frank's and saw that they offered a variety of soups. Pleased, I called to place an order but feared nowhere would deliver just soup, so I ordered fries too. When I placed my order, I was informed by the very nice lady who took my order that there is a minimum order amount of $10 for deliveries. She asked if I wanted to order a soda to reach the minimum and I told her I didn't need a drink but asked if there was anything else small I could order. She told me that it was okay and my amount was close enough (it was around $9), and to feel better. (Guess she could tell I was sick over the phone.) The delivery driver was there less than 20 minutes later with my order plus an order of garlic knots from the lady who took my order! I thought that was so nice of her to go out of her way to send me something extra to make my day a little better. So if that lady reads this, thank you!!! Also, the chicken tortellini soup is delicious--the perfect cure for the common cold!

This place is dirty, don't look up at the nasty ac vents, the floor is gross. The food wad bad. I had the pork sandwich and there was a bunch of hard pieces that I had to spit out. My husband's ribs were cold and overdone. It was hot, ac sucked. We won't be going back.

As a foodie, every once in a while you stumble upon a culinary gem- sometimes, off the beaten path. I am no stranger to ethnic food, however, there are not many options within and around Indy for the more exotic types of cuisine such as African food. 

The first type of African food I discovered, was Nigerian, back around the Y2K hype at the transition into the 21st century. I vividly recall eating very tasty greens (sautéed in onions and tomato sauce with meat), and chicken and goat, and very tasty and colorful rice and other starchy based dishes such as Fufu and Amala. As a lover of spice and exotic food, I indulged in all the spices, herbs and unique favors I'd been missing for almost a decade when I by chance learned of Beautful Shades (aka Naira Land). 

The owner and chef, David, is very friendly and eager to answer any question you may have regarding the unfamiliar to many, typical Nigerian dishes. I ate the Efo (mildly spicy greens sautéed in tomato sauce with beef and fish and herbs), lightly fried chicken with no batter added to it, and beans (served with a delicious sauce on top) and Dodo (lightly fried plantains). The price of such very tasty food is very affordable. Besides some main dishes and specials, you can create your own meal by ordering side items plus meat. The meal that I usually create cost around $9.37 including tax but excluding a drink. 

Oh, and regarding the interior: the restaurant is simple, yet clean and not too long or wide. There's enough room for about a party of under 50 in the main restaurant area. There are two wall mounted flat screens and a sink to wash your hands before you indulge in some of the finger food based meals like Fufu (pounded yam) or Amala ( a similar yet wheat based starchy pounded substance upon which sauces with meat are served). 

So, if you like ethnic food and you've never had African food before, this is the perfect place for you to discover some of the best West African food you can find in Indy! Be bold and adventurous, and add a new restaurant to your list of ethnic food gems.

Mr. B's is by far my favorite restaurant in this city with too many choices.  I can't believe this was my first check in and haven't written a review yet seeing as that I have been going there for special occasions and when I feel like treating myself to an amazing causal but upscale meal for years. Let's get down to it, this place is the most consistant I have ever experienced which is one reason I love it so much.  Not only is the food consistant, but the service is always above and beyond amazing.  I have never had a server who was a boring person with no personality. Whomever it is that waits on my table when I go is always super happy and excited to be your server. They have conversations, they of course ask where you are from, because being from New Orleans is so abnormal when dining in the French Quarter, they make jokes, they are just down right entertaining.

Now on to the food and drinks.  I'll go by my most recent visit which was just a few days ago. We ordered a bottle of wine which was in my opinion a pretty reasonable $34 for a place of this quality.  Now of course I ordered Duck Spring Rolls. This is is a must do for me every time, and they are always perfect. They are a bit of Asian flavor with goat cheese, shitake, spinach and duck inside. Yummm! I also ordered the heirloom tomatoes and fresh mozzerella salad, which isn't always on the menu. I was really happy I got that salad, it was so refreshing and pretty to look at too, darn I should have taken a picture! Then for my entree I ordered the scallops, which is actually an appetizer, and has two jumbo sea scallops that are buttery delicious perfection, and they are accompanied by watercress and shaved parmigiano - reggiano. The best scallops ever!!! I had a bite of my dad's enormous pork chop, it was amazing, my brother's Osso Bucco, it was amazing, my mom's veal picatta, amazing, my son's very special birthday chicken tenders, amazing!!! Dessert: bread pudding of course, in my opinion the best other than my mom's recipe. If you are reading my review and you aren't from New Orleans looking for an amazing dinner, take it from this born and raised NOLA girl, you must go to Mr. B's!!! You will be very happy you did!

I am very disappointed . It is because they treated me unfairly. A couple weeks ago,  I went there for the first time. I liked the food, so I told my friend to try this restaurant. Tonight, I went there again and I saw that my friends were there (They were located in two different tables). When I came into the restaurant, they were almost done. While I was enjoying my food with my family, they had finished. Before they left, the waitress gave them one big box full of clementines for free (It was given as a New Year's gift.) Also, my other friends (at the other table) received a free big box of clementines. My table and one of the other tables had paid the bill, the only table that got the free stuff was the other table and I did not receive anything. I saw that they still had many boxes of clementines. 
I won't go back there to spend my money.

I'm trying to reply to the Manager's comment on my review. I'm unsure how to respond directly, so I'll leave it here in the hopes it will be seen. 
Yes, this was the Frankford Avenue location, just south of Shelmire. And the woman who groomed my puppy was Hope (I have a very good memory for names)

Wow! Great calzone! This place should have a "passport" program - I want to try each one. Meat me in St Louie had creamy moscarpone with the usual pizza stuff: sausage, pepperoni, mozzarella and a meat sauce (on the side of course). When they came out we thought "gee, we could have split one". However none of us stopped eating till they were gone. Waiting for an Apple pie dessert calzone. Employees are all cool and seem happy to be working here: I saw two dancing to the music playing in the background. 

If your on the Southside of St Louis you gotta try this place. About 1/2 mile from SLU. I'll be back.

Our daughter and family moved from Seattle to Sacramento and had a terrible experience. They weren't sure they would ever see their belonging again.  That was until they were put in touch with Rose Olsen from Olsen and Fielding Mayflower. Immediately, the moving van with their items showed up.  We decided to follow them to Sacramento and didn't think twice about which company to use.  Rose Olsen was held our hand throughout the entire move.  We managed to fill 13 units making this a large move.  We had wonderful movers in Seattle, and the same in Sacramento.  All the while, Rose was helping us out, answering questions and offering encouragement in addition to providing a skilled and experienced staff.  If you want a trouble free experience, Olsen and Fielding Mayflower are the people to call - ask for Rose!

I bought a month membership in the low $19.99 bed. It didn't give me a tan at all, so don't waste your money. All of the workers were very rude (with exception to 1 girl who is new and was nice). Customer service skills are lacking... When you walk in the TV is cranked up and they make you feel like your a bother!

The salad bar has gone down hill!!!  Only 4 salad dressings---1 in the bottle from the shelf.  Dirty salad bar and dining tables.  No forks.  1 salt shaker, no pepper.
I generally shop here so I can get a great lunch.
Guess not!

And, I hope the kid cleaning the sneeze guards didn't spray cleaner on the lettuces!

My review is on the incredible customer service of Dan.  I had my hair done approx. a month ago and unfortunately was not a good fit with the stylist I had, although he was quite nice.  Dan has gone out of his way to make this right for me and save a customer.  I can't thank you enough Dan for your commitment to excellent service, it seems rare these days.  I look forward to a second visit with your salon soon.  
THANKS AGAIN.

Shelley

Disappointing and seriously overpriced.

Surprised to find so many good reviews of this place. Maybe I ordered the wrong thing. I ate here the Thursday before the Super Bowl, and I was excited about it. My husband and I ordered the daily special: A steak sandwich with chips and sauce. Couldn't have been more disappointed in it.

I thought the sandwich would be a toasty, flavorful pressed sandwich, and it wasn't. Just a paper-thin slice of steak on a plain bun topped with spring mix salad out of a bag and slices of onion. Served with maybe 10 packaged tortilla chips and a tiny cup of bland sauce. 

We were finished in about 5 minutes and it cost $19. Ended up costing a lot more because we promptly went back to Super Bowl Village and bought two giant pretzels for $10. Sigh.

The Tim Drum Asian Cafe is not what I expected.  It's a eclectic combination of asian street foods from Japan, China, Thailand, India, and Korea.  Much like its street food counterparts....it's loud inside the dining room, and certainly appears to be a hodgepodge of disorganization.  During our visit we watched merrily as servers, cooks, and cashiers bumped into each other and scurried all around....

I tried the Teriaki Chicken bowl, my girlfriend had Tin Drum Chicken curry, and we started with a pot sticker app.

The dishes were affordable and tasty, I don't think the atmosphere is recommended for "date night" although for lunch this would be perfect....and definitely something different than what is available in Oldsmar.  It was odd that the curry came with more than twice the chicken as the teriyaki....they seem to be inconsistent on portion control here.

I hope they can streamline this restaurant to run properly....they appear to still be working that out.  The staff was very friendly, I'll be back and update this review soon.

Had an awesome experience with Dave recently when he worked on a small tattoo for me and one a bit bigger for a friend. He took his time, made us feel comfortable with jokes but was 100% professional. He didn't just tell us what would work and wouldn't work, but explained why and didn't seem annoyed while doing it.

Minus one star because I found their emailing system a little odd - when i first called for an appointment I was told to email a gmail address, I did, but there was no confirmation of receipt or anything really. Just felt a bit odd to send your personal art of ideas into the abyss with no acknowledgement.

If you have a hankering for some fierce antique loving this is where you should go.  I was really hoping it would be more like the world's largest thrift store but it's got reallly authentic craaazy old international antiques.  Like actual antiques as in well over a hundred years old and in amazing condition.  I am not sure what asian villiage they raided to get all this stuff but they are selling it for very reasonable prices...still out of my range but hey.  Tables, benches, dressers and chairs are the most abundant here from china and thereabout to india.   Some american pieces were in the front room.  This wooden furniture is absolutely pristine shape I couldn't believe it and soooo much supposedly 90,000 sq ft of store on two floors.  Also rugophiles would be in heaven here a gigantic floor for ancient rugs or every sort and style is upstairs.  Next to the 'modern' super discount room with a bunch of ikea cheap style couches and chairs for around $100 or less.  This place is amazing just to see but I need a job before I can actually shop here.   You know to furnish my apartment in the style of 19th century chinese school houses.

What a fun treat!  I was skeptical due to some of the initial reviews but am so glad we tried it!  We've been two times now and I really like this place.  First, I'm a sucker for details.  Down to the chopsticks, the loud music, the dishes, the friendly staff... Someone with a vision is behind this place.  Then the food . It's not straight Japanese, it's not Spanish tapas - but maybe a rough hybrid of the 2?  
My 'make or break' is always flavors and care in preparation.  Home run on both here.  It's a fun quest trying something new because the food here really isn't like anywhere else in town.  

Tip - ask the staff about the dishes/ingredients!

My cons:  
1.  there were literally 2 bites of chicken in the Ramen.  And it was $14. We were splitting so I let my partner have both as I like mushrooms.  He said the flavor was amazing.  I think there should be more.....
2.  It's expensive 
3.  The sun is really bright and on a busy early night you might be seated with a beam of sun in your face (maybe more blinds?)

I used to love coming to this place when I was a student at U of A.  Recently, I decided to take an out of state visitor there. The pizza was not at ALL how I remembered.  Either we caught the place on an off-night or the management has really taken a poor turn.  At the ordering area, the food obviously did not look fresh; it appeared to have been sitting there for many hours unrefrigerated before our arrival.  I hesitated but ordered a veggie pizza for myself and he ordered a hawaiian pizza.  It took nearly 20 minutes for our food to arrive, even though there were very few people in the restaurant.  When our food was finally "ready" it was cold and soggy (even though the pizza had ostensibly been warmed up).  It was the worst pizza I have ever had from anywhere in town.  Total disappointment.  I won't be returning.  Go to Frog next door instead.

I got to go food for my hubby and I. Granted I live a good 35 minutes from here but I travel for good food. The fact that we didn't dine in I'm inclined to give them another shot. The lady who took our order was really nice. Unfortunately for the amount of time it took for her to come out with our food, It would appear that the food would've been piping hot. Nope. I checked the bag before we left the place and it was warm at best. So of course once I got home it was cold. My little soft shell crab po boy was meh. Not anything special. Take out always get treated different from dine in unfortunately. Hopefully if we go back maybe our dine in experience will be a lot better.

Was excited to try this new lunch spot in the Cool Springs area. From the start, the decor is just......strange. It is kinda modern and kinda something else all mixed together randomly. The menu is limited with very little descriptions, which is not good for a picky person like me. The waitress seemed very disturbed when I asked questions about what things were. The bread is good, but I would like a little something more than plain ole olive oil to dip it in, so we added pepper. The soup my husband got was great and that is where the great food ended. The sandwiches and salad was just okay. I can do a WAY better chicken paninni  at home, or at work - the chicken was so dry I asked for marinara to dip it in, that didn't even work. Overall, I am turned off and will not be back. Brixx and Cararrabas are closer and much much better.

Absolutely the best environment for a child to learn water safety and develop a love for swimming. The teachers, the office staff, the class sizes, and the curricula create the ideal equation for success.  There is nothing that compares to seeing the love and attention that are shown to your child and knowing that not only are they doing something good for their bodies, but their hearts, minds, and self-esteem.

This is a great place to grab a drink and quick bite to eat! Their bartenders are super knowledgeable, which is helpful with some of their more interesting liquors and cocktails. I asked the bartender to make me something winter-y and it was delicious and beautiful! Plus the hummus is to die for.

Great food. They have weekly special - must try. I have tried pretty much everything  on their menu and I love everything. The staff is great. Bubs holes are great, if you like donuts. If you come on Sunday, make sure and try their belinis.
Food and service very good. Only complaint is that the children's portion is tiny! (at least the lo mein is!) good for a5 or 6 year old not pre-teens!

Tangerine STILL receives five stars from me......

I have returned to Tangerine twice since my initial review back in January and am still tickled pink with their staff's professionalism, the quality of the work that they do (makeup, hair, facials and product knowledge) and plan to return as often as possible.

Beautiful location - full of modern artwork. There is seating at the bar, nice couches along the sides, and wonderful outdoor seating. There is an instant relaxing atmosphere here, where you just want to sit back, sip your beverage, and take in the beauty. The menu is extensive, and the bartenders will create something off-menu of course. The prices are steep, but these are drinks you slowly sip while enjoying great company, therefore the price is worth it. I would gladly return - and recommend Plat to others!

One of the worst experiences of my life. Horrible from beginning to end. After waiting over 30 minutes for my meal I told the waitress to take it off the bill and bring me the check. I can't comment on the quality of the food cause I never got it and 3 different waitresses couldn't find it. Stay away

I try so much to like this place. I even had my wedding here.  We definitely spend enough money here to have our rooms comped..... But time after time we always end up with a smoking room and of course   there are no other rooms available because it's such a busy Tuesday night.... Lol.  What a bunch of crap. What is the purpose of specifying a late check in and non smoking if stupid hotel doesn't even honor any of those requests?  This place forces you to get lung cancer.... How disgusting is that.  This is so unfortunate.

The food flavors are good but I had the chicken leg and it was very dry and tough. Not sure how you can dry out dark meat that much but it was done. The staff are very nice and I can only hope things improve with the food. The chili even though full of grease is very good and was the highlight of this place. I will go back to try other things and hope they improve!

Had a massage through groupon. My initial experience was terrible, and the worst massage of my life, but then I emailed the staff there and they're going to try to fit me in on another day. Hopefully this time will be better than the last!
Wir haben zwar für einen Montag 25 min warten müssen, das spricht ja schon für Crabby Bill's und wir würden auch nicht enttäuscht dies hier ist wirklich sehr gut und alles frisch!

The menu is smaller than it appears. I felt like I almost had to order the wings and the bibimbap. 

And I did. And it was great. 

But for some reason, not many venture far from those items. Or that's what it seems like, judging by the items coming out of the kitchen and the prior reviews. 

I would go if you are in the area, and if you have a need for twice fried wings and bibimbap in a stone pot.
My friends and I had dinner here last weekend and as always, it was phenomenal! Service was great as was the food! Definitely can't wait to go back!

Go here as an alternative to Terrain!

I tried Farmer's Road for the first time this week. The apple sandwich was delicious as was the wrap my friend had. The meals all came with sweet potato chips (a huge portion) and delicious fountain soda (try the Italian lemon.) The prices are ridiculously good for the quality of the food. The atmosphere was rustic, sort of like Terrain in the same neighborhood. We sat inside for a quick meal and will definitely be back.

I've wanted to come here for awhile, and last night I finally got the chance. Leaving another event downtown and relaxing there was a Pacers game going on, we figured Pearl Street would be worth checking out. Somewhat hidden on Pearl Street - which is really an alley - this place was really quiet for having a game going on a block and a half away. 

We sat ourselves at a table and our server came over right away.. Which I expected seeing how there was only one other table with people at it. Drink specials for a Wednesday night was $2 well drinks, so I went with a vodka cranberry. Well drinks are hit or miss, I had a vodka cranberry and something in it was way too sweet. Another person had a Joanna B (Jameson and Ginger Ale) and thought the same thing.

Food was good.. service was good up until we were ready for our checks.. then we had to track our server down. I'd be up for checking this place out again though, if nothing else but for the immediate seating on game nights.

Yum so refreshing and yummy 
I had pineapple cherry it was great not overly sweet perfect amount and only $2.00 can't go wrong! Hope to visit again

Fried tofu was amazing - but everything else was way too salty! I had to gulp down at least two cups of water throughout lunch. We tried to redeem the 10% of $40 check in deal when our total came out to be $39.34 and the lady waitress insisted that we bought something else!
I've been going to Frosty Boy since the 1970's. Best ice cream around. Burgers are good, fries are great, onion chips... On and on and on. You can't miss with Frosty Boy in New Palestine.

My rating is based on overall experience. Our server was very polite however was outnumbered by tables as the service was VERY slow. I am a very picky eater and decided to have the soup of the day with a Cesar salad and add chicken. 

The soup was delicious! It was warm, very tasty and perfect size. 

About 10 minutes before dinner was served the waiter told me that the chef would not add chicken to my salad. Honestly, for the couple hundred that was paid for our total meal, they could have thrown on a darn chicken breast!

My dad had lamb shank and loved it. 
My grandmother had mussels but some were served closed.
My brother in law had the ribeye but there was a lot of fat on his piece. 

The service was slow slow slow.
Saturday night at 9pm and the staff is overwhelmed and the food is average.  For the price it was not a value.  Try someplace else
Excellent burgers and delicious waffle fries! I recommend the sweet potato fries. The service was great, and the food came out fast!

Went to opening day today and WOW! This place is definitely something that's been missing in this area. Even though the place was super busy it didn't take long to order a beer and food came out fast. The place looks great and on a warm summer night it'll be awesome to relax outside with the fire pits, huge Jenga and cornhole. This place is first and foremost a BAR. So expect it to be loud, crowded and fun. My only problem is that parking is scarce. Otherwise this place will be a hot spot in the exton area I'm sure.

I am writing after my worst experience with Woodbury Nissan for the second time with in a year. Both times my van had to stay with them for days and still come back with the same problem and time worst than when I brought for service. No one has any answers. No at the dealership want owe to the responsibilities. They put my families life in jeopardy twice by saying the problem is fixed it was never fixed.
Seriously kicked my butt.  Great bikes and instructors. Soul Cycle might have some competition.

Eating here is a must if you either live in Santa Barbara or are in for a visit.

Came here recently and it was worth every penny. It was easily the best meal I have ever had. We each ordered different things and loved it. The service was great, and our server was very pleasant. 

When I come back to Santa Barbara, I will definitely make it a point to come back.

I loved how fresh, delicious, and inexpensive my burger and fries were. I ordered a avocado as an extra on my burger and it was fantastic. The chocolate milkshake we got was good, but nothing special.

Ooh, I kind of love this place. I've only been there once so I can only vouch for the bartender we had but it was a great time. It was pretty empty when we walked in, got some cheap beers and shots and checked the place out. The bartender ended up telling us about some crazy random string of incidents that had happened about 5 minutes before we walked in. I won't bore with the details, but it was a hilarious story and I was not surprised at all to hear that these sort of things happen at the Saint. 

Great jukebox with Screeching Weasel and tons of other stuff I haven't listened to in about ten years. Photo booth, centipede/milipede, table seating, comfortable bar to sit at, lots of cool crap to look at on the walls. Will definitely go back.

We had 3 different dishes-omelette, frittata, snd an eggs Benedict, all really good.  Great decor, great server, but the espresso was not so good , the prices a little high.  Will definitely go again.  Try the strawberry orange juice, fresh and refreshing.
Excellent happy hour with tasty, well priced apps and beer. The only downside is the noise level. Once the place fills up you will be yelling to hear the person you're sitting next to.

Thank you Bondurant Plumbing for going the extra mile to get a warranty enforced for our indirect water heater.  They installed the new tank and came back the next day when there was a problem with the new tank calling for heat.  Everything now is working and we have lots of hot water again.... Thanks to the techs and this company....

Let me start with saying I am originally from Texas! We know bbq like none other...especially brisket!  While the ribs and pull pork sandwich were decent, the brisket is what I base my reviews on when it comes to a smokehouse.  The owner is super nice and informative!  I wouldn't mind coming back for ribs and pull pork.  It's decent compared to many others I have seen around here.  The place is really clean and I love the choices of sauces available.  It's more on the vinegar and Tabasco side of the sauce scales.  I like my sauces thicker and use of Sriracha can achieve the spiciness without the tart taste.   

When it comes to brisket, the smoke flavor profile seemed to be lacking.  I like to see the smoke ring that a smokehouse should have on their meats.  Brisket should be able to hold its own flavor without dousing an obscene amount of sauce on it to bring out flavors.  The brisket was a bit tough which tells me it needs more time @ lower temps.  

Bc this place is new, I would love to try it again in a few months to see improvements! I always encourage everyone to support their local joints! I don't discourage anyone from coming to try this place!

Simply great food.. likely best kept secret in Tampa / Clearwater..

Host / owner was funny and really attentive..

If you are in the area, try it.. you won't regret it..
My first time there. Food was amazing. I had the smash and stack burger.  Fried pickles. Service was great. Had the homemade ice cream will definitely be back !!

Lecture classes are hit and miss depending on the instructors style. This was a read along scribble on the board type class. A lot of reviews rave about Julio being a wonderful instructor- I didn't have him. I had another guy who didn't seem very much like he wanted to be there. 7 day intensive wasn't right for me and I wasn't allowed to switch to online unless I paid another $249. So I suggest you get Julio or take it online somewhere else. They're twice as expensive as other programs and half as caring.

This restaurant is very cute and cozy. It's located in a strip mall near Southgate and easy to miss. The food is reasonably priced and their salmon sashimi is great - very fresh! Hard to find sashimi in this city that isn't partially frozen...

This Bully's location great food with a great attitude it is one of my favorite places to go when I'm out on the motorcycle they always have a specialty beer on tap which you can get a sample of. outside of special events it is kid friendly during the day and early evening
It is very cool experience and the food is great I definitely recommend it and would gladly come back

One of my family's favorite restaurants. Food is delicious and consistent, the large dining area split into different sections gives an intimate feeling while also reducing waits, and the service is fairly decent.

My family usually comes here for the prime rib. Everyone really loves how tender and juicy it is and it is definitely cooked to order; if you want it medium rare, it'll be just that, which is awesome. Besides the prime rib, I've also had the filet mignon and even ventured out to try their Greek cuisine such as the Mousaka which reminded me of lasagna but with eggplant and a cream sauce instead. It was delicious and I plan on getting it again the next time I can escape the peer pressure of my family to order the prime rib. Literally every time we eat here, the waiters don't have to remember much since its just prime rib, prime rib, prime rib...It really is that good!

Spiro's Chesterfield also has an awesome early dinner special, their version of a happy hour sans drink specials, which gives you several entree options along with soup or salad, sides, and dessert for a price that is less than an entree only during regular hours! I really like the avgolemono soup which is a chicken broth with rice and an added lemon zest. It really helps prime your appetite for the rest of the food to come. I've noticed that the early bird dinner is usually skewed towards the older age crowd, but really if you can get here between 5-6:30pm (earlier on the weekends I think), it is completely worth it.

The owner is also really friendly and he often comes around to chat with us during the meal. It is always nice when owners take the time to get to know their clients, it improves the atmosphere that much more. My only gripe with the place is that the service can be iffy sometimes, I guess with a bigger party there is always extra stress on the staff, but at a fine dining establishment like Spiro's, we would expect good service consistently. Otherwise, come here! You won't be disappointed.
Really fresh oysters - 1 doz for $17.  Very fresh and the shucker pointed out how the color of the shell indicate the quality of oyster.  These were so good we each ate  a dozen!

This location provides a steady stream of small and sundry items I need to fix up my house, and to build fun things with and for my children.

Staff is solid and reasonable, with an uncanny knack for knowing where things are hidden.

By the time I'm done fixing everything at my new location, I suspect my house will be approximately 11% from this Home Depot.

This used to be a great place.  When I moved to Forty Acres years ago, I was thrilled to have great Italian food so close to me.  The veal, the gnocci, everything was out of this world.  Now the food is not that good.  Pizza has declined in quality over the last couple years.  Calamari is always soggy.  The pasta and sauces are just so-so.  

Now for the reason I will NEVER return.  I placed a phone order.  I was told twenty minutes.  I went to pick it up and got there 25 minutes after my call.  I had to wait another 15 minutes.  The restaurant was not that busy.  The man who rung me up and barely spoke English hovered over me while I signed my slip, to the point that I was uncomfortable.  When he saw the tip line had a zero on it, he huffed very loudly and gave me a dirty look like he wanted to fight or something.  If I was classless like him, I might have been upset and lost sleep over it.  But knowing I will never, ever return to this horrible place actually just made it quite funny.  And when I got my food home, it was again just bland and boring.  

I do not recommend this place at all anymore.  A year ago, I might have.  Two years ago I always did.  Now I recommend you avoid the average food and horrible, horrible service and lack of basic human manners and respect at all cost.

While looking around for restaurants for a company get together, I stumbled upon the Watermark. Before we spent a lot of money, we wanted to come and try the restaurant. From start to finish it was an exceptional experience. 
We were able to eat some of the items on the fixed menu since it isn't that much different than the regular one. 
First course was a salad which had candied pecans, feta cheese, and a vinaigrette. I'm not normally a fan of pecans, but I ate them all in this salad. 
Second course was soup. I had the butternut squash bisque and my colleagues had the shrimp & corn chowder (I couldn't since it wasn't gluten free). I thought mine was excellent and my coworkers felt the same. 
Thirdly they brought out their famous grits souflee. It had bacons and I'm told it was good as well.
The entrees we had were the salmon, filet, and goat cheese stuff chicken. We all three shared them and while they were all amazing, I felt like the salmon was my favorite. 
They also brought me some cornbread (gluten free) and I took the leftovers home.
Creme brûlée, pecan pie, and a chocolate cake were the desserts. I could only have the creme brûlée but it was quite good!
Scott was our main server and was so attentive, but there were quite a few who would come and bring all our food at one time. It was really 5 star service the entire evening. 
We were working with Trish, who does the special events planning. She was incredibly friendly, accommodating, and helpful with me not being able to eat gluten. 
While it is pricy, there are many restaurants in Nashville that you could easily spend the same amount at and not get the same quality service. 
I HIGHLY recommend the food, the service, and oh the atmosphere! Luckily, it was a perfect evening and we were able to sit on the patio which overlooks the gulch. It is hard to beat this restaurant and I will definitely be back.

Caters to all the tastes(Spicy, mildly Spicy to Non Spicy). Different lunch and Dinner menus. I tried the Del Rey Chicken Burrito which was very juicy with very fine and flavorful sauces used. I found the rice and Black Beans here to be better than rest of the mexican places I have been to. Must try.

DO NOT judge this book by its cover.

The Mexican at Taco Suave is by far the best I've had in PA. If you're a cheese lover, like me, order the nachos. Basically a heaping pile of delicious cheese and refried beans over amazing (probably homemade) chips. The tacos are fantastic, authentic and perfect. Don't miss the carnitas or carne asada.

As a newbie to the area, the whole time I was eating, I kept thinking "this is what i'll be craving after a night out..." I then read almost exactly the same comment in the review below mine. Good quality Mexican food is hard to find, and this is it, for sure.

Half price sushi was probably one of my favorite things to dine on when working downtown..in love with spice tuna, for some reason theirs never really did much for my taste buds, nevertheless the food is good whether your sitting at the sushi bar or doing it up getting a steak and fried rice at the group tables. Manager is friendly, staff is attentive. Just busy as hell on certain nights, but worth the wait.

not once have i gone to honey's for a weekend brunch and not incurred a wait of at least 30 minutes to upwards of an hour. on occasion i have been so hungry [and/or hungover] that even a 5 minute wait seemed impossible, thereby leading me to nearby alternatives north 3rd or the abbaye. both are good...but neither hold a candle to the deliciousness that is honey's.

today was one of those days where we were willing to wait the 45 minutes while our stomachs rumbled in anticipation of the meal to come. we passed the time by people watching and contemplating whether to go breakfast or lunch (seeing as it was 2pm), all the while growing more & more eager as other 2-tops being called had tired of the wait and left, making us that much closer to Next.
 
within moments of sitting down, we were handed menus and asked if we wanted coffee - yes, please! since enjoying the enfrijoladas so much on my last visit, i was set on ordering them again. this time instead of getting it made with tofu, i went for the vegan sausage. equally as delish. as if that wasn't enough food, i added a latke + [homemade] applesauce on the side for a mere $2.50. 

my boyfriend went the lunch route and ordered the brisket sandwich, topped with melted cheese & sauteed spinach, served with a side of horseradish sauce & fries. this led to me eating fries for the 3rd time this week (that's typically how many times i eat them in a month!) as i simply could not resist dipping them in the tangy horseradish sauce.

there are so many veg-friendly options at honey's that i sorta kick myself for getting the same one twice, but i fully intend to eat here enough to try everything [meatless] on the menu.


[ random aside:  i had parked on 3rd street, just north of poplar, which as i later learned is a popular spot for birds to gather on the telephone poles. when we returned to the car, it looked like it had gone to war with the entire winged population of philadelphia....and lost. this required a quick detour to the nearest car wash (11th & spring garden - thanks, GPS!) where, $16 later, it was as if my car had never been the crap-magnet that it was. all in all, the meal was still well worth it! ]
Another New Orleans breakfast spot well worth hitting while you're in town. Fried Oyster Eggs Benedict was amazing. I will be returning  at least one more time before we leave :)

Food was decent tex-mex and the bean dip was good. My partner and I both got the chimichanga. He got the ultimate margarita and I got the house margarita. Both were strong but the house didn't taste great. Fountain in the middle of the room is sweet but overall decor is lacking.

Food was good but for an 8pm reservation we were given our table 840pm. What's even better is that we got a 6 seater for an 8 people table. It's gets better, the hostess told us that she can't ask a 2 seater table next to us to leave so we should hover around them to pressure them to leave!! Expect a long wait, bad service from the hostess and good food. Food worth 4 stars.

Shrimp and grits hold a very close place in my heart, due to my step mom! Compliments to the chef! It definitely have hers a run for her money. Justin was our server, and he did an amazing job. Friendly and welcoming! Don't pass this place up! Amazing!!!!

Went to Farmhaus last night for dinner with the parents.  Don't sleep on this place!  The menu is inventive and has its heart in the right place.  Oh, and everything tasted great, as well.

It's a new-menu-daily-depending-on-what's-fresh kind place, which I think should be more common in StL.  Glad to see they're rocking it over at Farmhaus.

For drinks:  the wine list was apt;  Missouri craft brews were definitely present on the beer list; and my mom had a rhubarb cocktail, which was delicious and not cloyingly sweet.  

For eats:  we had the sweet potato "nachos"... these were my least favorite thing, though they were still tasty.  There were not enough toppings to be evenly distributed on the chips, so most chips I ate were just chip + sauce.  I really liked the turkey tasso serv, but I ended up eating it more on its own because the size of the cuts weren't accustomed to staying on the chips.  

Everything else was splendid.  We had the "breakfast", which may have been my favorite thing.  The syrup was delicious and the pork belly was some of the best I've had.  Also had the nairagi, which was quite tasty, as well as the duck which was done to perfection and served with delicious greens.  

All in all, it was a great dining experience.  And I thought the portions/pricing were totally fair and not too expensive.  But then, my dad did pick up the bill, lucky me!

Regrettably I booked my stay at this hotel due to the reviews. Upon arriving and checking into my room I had a completely different experience. The hallways reek of cigarette smoke, the room was in need of repairs and a good cleaning and there were dead bugs in my room. Very disappointing.

Only been here a couple times, but very pleased with our service so far! They got a red stain out of my wife's white coat a few months back and I recently took in an outfit to be dry cleaned for an event. They have same day service (drop off by 10am, done by 5pm) on most items and prices aren't bad - cost us about $3 for a button-up shirt (cleaned and starched,) $7.25 for one pair of pants, and $5 for a tie. They have a drive-thru where you can pick up your items, which was really convenient. Everyone I talked to was very courteous. Only issue I had was that I would've liked to know about how much it would cost before I picked it up - I could have asked but it didn't dawn on me until later. We'll definitely use Milto again for any of our cleaning needs.

I came here when this place was "hot and new," but apparently never got around to writing my review!
Even after being open for only a few weeks and with a line of customers out the door, Raijin Ramen has quick, speedy service. While I felt a little rushed eating my ramen, since they clearly wanted to turn over my table to get more customers inside, the service itself was still attentive and not overbearing.
Their vegetarian ramen was surprisingly different than the vegetarian miso broths I'm used to having at ramen shops, and was a nice change of pace. The bowl itself included some unusual and not-so-traditional ramen add-ons, like thinly sliced zucchini, but it still tasted good.
I would prefer for Raijin to have a miso vegetarian broth, since that is my preference, but I think it's nice that they have a vegetarian option at all, since many ramen places do not.
Seeing as how it's Tucson and ramen doesn't really exist here, Raijin's got a monopoly on the ramen market in town, and that's probably how they can get away with their prices. In the Bay Area where I live, this wouldn't fly because there are so many other ramen options to choose from. However, next time I'm in Tucson and craving ramen, I will gladly pay their rather high prices!

I am highly disappointed at my experience here today. 

After visiting Nox last week, I had such a great experience that I changed a reservation from Tavolino to here, because I think it would be a more contemporary type of dining experience. I regret having changed locations, and wished this whole experience could've been avoided. 

*management reached out within a day in good gesture to make things right and I appreciate that.

We needed a last minute reservation with 3 pets and these guys were so accommodating. They bent over backwards yo help us. The room was great new and clean. We will use Residence Inn as much as we can in the future.
SLOW EST BARTENDER EVER. Took 15 plus minutes each time, all night, at half capacity bar. Horrible

Good price for food, good food, good service!!!! $5.29/lb of crawfish, $8 for a dozen of oysters. Came here for late dinner at 930pm & there was still a line outside. Sat at the bar instead of a table with husband & got in within 5 minutes. Will definitely come back here if we happen to come backe to NOLA.

This is the absolute worst property management company I have ever rented from and I plan to contact the owner of the property I rent to advise him how bad they are!  Do not rent here if you like your home maintained and certainly don't hire them as managers for your property.  Things will fall apart which most people who own rentals want to be sure maintenance is taken care of because it's a huge investment.

From trying to get into the payment portal to pay rent and not having anyone return my calls  to a huge piece of corrugated metal I reported was going to fly off in the wind, potentially killing someone, I had to fix it myself because they never came out even after 4 calls and a maintenance report entered online.  

Do not rent from them, seriously!

We were just walking around and saw the lights inside that caught our attention.  We decided to have a drink and check it out.  The ambiance and server were excellent!! He recommended drinks, took the time to explain ingredients on the menu that I wasn't familiar with.  He made sure we enjoyed our drinks and checked up on us often.  Great service can make any experience memorable, and our server did that for us!!!

I didn't find this clinic as dirty as some reviews stated, but maybe I'm lucky. It does look a bit old, but I can't say it affects the service somehow, not in my opinion, at least. 

We got a quick appointment for my cat. She had a watering eye. The person on the phone and receptionist were nice. The assistant was attentive. Dr. Littlejohn performed pretty thorough general check-up and found that my cat had an infection on her eye. We got antibiotic to treat it. The pricing was fair, in my opinion. We paid for the check-up + medication $72. 

In general, the visit was as short as they could make it, the exam was thorough, the general service was nice, and they are close to where I live.
No complaints.

This place is as massive as it looks.  No bells and whistles. Just simple, clean and very well laid out - making most items really easy to find. Meaning I can get in and out in a hurry. 

You certainly don't have a lack of options - in fact - even for someone very knowledgeable in the alcoholic beverage department - it can be overwhelming!! Good thing they have a super friendly staff willing to help! 

I am a weekly customer - there to pick up some red wine. I have found they carry what is the most amazing 10 dollar Lambrusco EVER. 

The only small complaint I have is that the workers are very good at "up selling".  I should have known to stick to the Lambrusco I always get considering every time I go there are only one or two bottles left on the shelf. But I asked about any other possibility and the guy working eagerly told me about a bottle that is twice the price - saying it is the "owners favorite" and that is why they keep it in stock! I thought - well then it has to be good!  Yea - not true. I'll go back to my original. 

None the less - this is a great spot. East to get to. Plenty of parking and friendly staff.

If you want some great margaritas & reasonably priced tacos, this is the place! My friends & I love going here on Thursdays for Dollar Taco Night! The environment is really fun, laid back and the perfect summer hangout for happy hour or dinner. I have been a couple of times already this summer and plan to be there every Thursday if I can! Definitely recommend this place :)

Terra Malia Designs just designed the florals for our Sonoma wedding over labor day. Terra was intimately involved with our planning process. She listened intently and asked great questions to understand the feeling we wanted to create for our special day. The floral arrangements she created were absolutely beautiful and beyond we had imagined. I highly recommend Terra for weddings and special event designs. Thank you TMD!

My darling & I stumbled upon this intriguing new spot last night on our way to dinner in the bywater. We popped in for a quick drink and found the place packed on what we found out was opening night. We grabbed our drinks at the bar and chatted with a group of friends who were waiting on their dinner. I perused the menu and while it is limited, it offer an assortment of fresh, local dishes. Everything coming out of the kitchen looked and smelled delicious. The space is small, dimly lit and modern (reminded me a bit of Bar Tonique - which I love). We'll surely be back for dinner or brunch soon at which point I hope to give the place 5 stars.  Check their website for hours.

I already left a review I just wanted to add, my massage therapist was ginger.  She alleviated my long term back pain.  I don't know what she did, she really helped my back!!!  Thank you ginger I may fly up from Vegas to get another massage if my pain comes back.

Last minute decision--quick reservation via Yelp. Seated immediately upon arrival. Our waitress, Emma, was great--friendly and helpful. The food (Pescado de la Casa--Sea Bass tonight and Chile Relleno) was delicious. The horchata was perfect--refreshing with just the right amount of cinnamon. Loved the fresh chips and salsa. We will definitely return.

Had the Bello Bistro (a big mushroom sandwich). Loved the mashed roasted arugula, great touch for a veggie sandwich. 

The price is very reasonable. The "healthy" drinks better be as healthy as they are disgusting, because they are THAT disgusting. 

Service is fast and friendly. Ingredients tasted pretty fresh.

My girlfriend did like the healthy drinks though, because she's weird and actually likes the taste of kale. "The lemon and agave makes the kale taste not too overwhelming."

I made an appointment for a tune up. Today I was scheduled for service from 12-4 pm. 3:40pm I called and asked if I was still scheduled. The gentleman who answered was nice and sent me to the dispatch person. She said "I called you earlier today to let you know we were running late due to a broken truck" Well they never called. I wont use them again and I'm glad they never came out as I dont like to be lied to. Remember most people never compliment so Im sure they have many happy customers. Im not one of them, my time was wasted.

This place was delicious for brunch and looking forward to going for dinner. Although it's now hard to walk away from that stuffed French toast 

Sabrina's is super cute inside and energy is high. Servers and staff were all friendly and inviting. BYOB so you know I'm there!! I was torn between the huevos rancheros and stuffed French toast and went with that. French toast made with challah bread and filled with sweet cream cheese in the middle, with some banana slices and drenched in syrup. Could've totally shared it because it was monstrous. Ended up taking half back home with me. 

I'm not sure if they take reservations but they do call ahead seating so that works out. Can't wait to go back and try some other stuff on the menu!!

When I go to Reno, this is probably one of my favorite places to stay. Strange enough I haven't actually eaten here only because we are usually  on the strip during meal time. But the Peppermill has pretty decent rooms. Some are amazingly updated and super clean. They are all about generous comps and have nice pools. The only thing I don't like about the hotel is it isn't pet friendly. Unfortunately, I have a little pooch that I like to bring along with me sometimes. If that's the case, I'll stay at Atlantis but this place is better then some of the other junky hotels in the area.
Got the Lumberjack breakfast. It was a nice place not that packed, looked like a pub. Waiters were nice and there's beer and yoga

Pretty much what I was expecting. We stayed a weeknight. The room was clean with decent modern accomodations. The bed was comfortable. It was relatively quiet in the hotel. Easy to connect the network. The staff we encountered were friendly and helpful.

This is a great little diner. It's clean, friendly, convenient to get to, lots of parking and they make some great food! Sometimes I take just my kids and sometimes we meet up with large groups and it's a great experience either way. Definitely a must try if you like the diner experience!

Nice little place.  Breakfasts are always consistent and the staff is friendly.  Sure beats a chain restaurant. Particularly good breakfast sausage and coffee.  Expect it will be replaced by a chain store since mall management feels that is a better fit for the area.  It will be a shame
Awesome non-greasy pizza that is made with real Mozzarella and a delightful sauce,  our "go to" place for pizza,  cheese steaks or a nice sit down dinner,  they have it all!!
Beautiful building, friendly staff & volunteers, good shows. A sometimes overlooked (at least by me) treasure located in the heart of downtown.

We had dinner there on January 14th.  The Beet Salad was okay .....just okay. The portion was small for the price, and it looked as though it had been prepared earlier, perhaps wrapped in plastic wrap, and then unwrapped to be served...everything was sort of smashed together on the plate.  My friends steak was ordered Medium and served Med Rare and floating in butter. The fries were lukewarm. Service was pleasant and friendly and beverages were kept full.

Then we had breakfast on January 16th and 17th.  The staff were all smiling and friendly ....they seemed to want to help....but there also seemed to be a big gap in organization. On both mornings, the buffet ran out of plates and food. When the food was replenished, the portions put out were small ...even though the restaurant and the bar were packed with people. If you weren't standing at the buffet, waiting for more food to come out ....then by the time you got from your table to the buffet and waited in line ....the food was gone again.  On both mornings.....I ate my toast, scrambled eggs, and bacon at differing times because if there were eggs...there was no bacon, if there was bacon there were no eggs.....and the loaf of bread was over 30 minutes in appearing.  

There was also something else we encountered.  The tables had napkins, forks, and knifes .....but no spoons.  Coffee was offered to us on both mornings....and we asked for cream and Splenda ...which were quickly provided.  And when we said 'there are no spoons'....the waitress on each morning said 'yes, we don't roll them in the napkins anymore because people are stealing them'....so then we smiled and said ...'well can we have spoons please?' .... spoons never arrived, so we used our knives.  Now ....if you, as a waitress, know there are no spoons on the table, and you also know your customer wants cream and sweetener for their coffee.......wouldn't you bring a spoon when you deliver the cream?  

It was clean and the staff IS friendly ...they just need some good old fashioned direction.
I was impressed by the cleanliness. The staff was friendly and my needs were met from start to finish of the trip. Would suggest as wonderful location in old Philly

The establishment is very appealing by sight and cleanliness. Unfortunately the food is not. We ordered an omelette and an egg salad sandwich and neither was even mediocre. The food had no favor. The waitress didn't have much of a personality and the hostess was on the phone our entire transaction upon leaving. We will be finding another diner to eat at because having a pretty, and clean restaurant isn't the only important aspect of food service.

What? 5 Stars? If Geoff getting soft in his reviews?

Not at all, but this is deserved!

I was blown away by the staff, the freshness the cleanliness and more.
