This is quite a niche place. Lots of vegan and gluten free stuff. I've been here multiple times but it seems like they don't change their menu often. I tend to go for vegetarian options so I've had their curried cauliflower a lot. We always tend to order the same options - chicken satay, grilled peppers, and the wings. They give so many peppers it's insane. I don't think we have ever finished a whole bowl between 3 folks. I've gotten their lettuce wraps twice but the second time felt like I ordered a completely different dish. It was like a waldorf chicken salad, when I expected it to be savory. That's the only reason I'm giving it 3 stars. 

Also, one time our waitress said she was going to bring some popcorn for us but she never came back with popcorn :(

One of my favorite stores for home goods. Love this location the most as it used to be the iconic Urban Outfitters years ago. Got to pick up a few gifts for some friends and some stuff for myself. Love the product and the service. They wrapped up all my gifts which gives me extra time to enjoy the holidays and less time wrapping.
This place failed to move me.  Everything was just OK.  Our server was nice, the food was pretty good, the outdoor patio was alright, but nothing wowed me.  I want to be wowed damn it.

The food is cheap, but the breakfast was yummy! the bacon is extremly salty beware. LOL...there is an odd sign up sheet that you have to sign in on when you first enter befor they seat you. The hostes/ waitress not friendly at all. not rude either, just gruff, as if she doesnt enjoy her job and she's pissed that she had to get up that morning. Its a cute small little place.
would i go back ? yes....but only if the service got better and wasnt treated as if just another dollar going into their register.
The family and I are visiting and decided to stop in for lunch. The staff was nice and the place was clean. The food was ok but a bit over priced for what you get.

The husband and I both got our wedding garb altered here.  Lee is a sweet fella and he's been in the business for a long time.   While I was there, a guy came in from a few hours up north talking about how he couldn't wait until he came back to SB so he could get some suits altered by Lee since the tailors aren't as great where he's living now.  Something similar happened when my husband went in.   He makes people happy enough to keep coming back for more.  That's always a good sign.

What you really want to know is if he's any good, and based on the work he did on my dress and Mr.'s suit, I'd say he does fantastic work!  I have a few other articles of clothing that have been cast away to the deep, dark, scary corners of my closet that I'd like to have him resurrect.

The chicken here is amazing!  The last time I ad authentic Peruvian rotisserie chicken was at malecon in NY. The skin is crispy and flavorful and the meat juicy. I ordered a whole chicken meaning to save half but...  Oh well, it'll be time to hit the gym. After my sat gorge fest at a NY style deli of course but I digress. Anyhow great food and friendly people. I'll definitely be back because I love my meat.

My family are eating dinner at Old Country Buffet by Oxford Valley Mall as I write this. We usually come for breakfast which is always good. So we decided to come for dinner. A huge mistake. I struggle to find edible food. The honey ham is way too salty. The roast beef is dry and cold and there isn't any au jus sauce even though there's a sign for it. The orange chicken and chicken tenders are so hard I was afraid of breaking my teeth. The spaghetti is overcooked. Spaghetti sauce is watery. They have brown gravy which lid incredibly oily and looks gross. So tried dessert. Bread pudding which is usually good is hard and cold. The quality of the food has gone downhill. I told my husband we should have gone to Pizza Hut.
What a find!!! While visiting our relatives we came here to eat breakfast. Our meals were outstanding. Generous portions, friendly staff and low prices. I will definitely return!!

First visit this morning with my youngest. We sat outside. Coffee was hot, fresh. My son got the kid's scrambled eggs & bacon. It came with an enormous amount of food - small pancake, 2 strips of bacon, eggs, home fries. I got the breakfast sandwich - like an Egg McMuffin on steroids...delicious. Friendly service, good prices, good diner breakfast!

Bring an appetite.....
The sandwiches are huge! Great quality and a fun shop all around. There are over a hundred different sodas there! Very neat place. Did i mention - the sandwiches are GREAT! Perfect place for a quick bite!

We arrived on a Monday morning at 10.50am so only just in time for breakfast that finishes at 11.  Never the less we were welcomed and seated and asked to be expedient with ordering. We ordered the crab desire which is a crab cake with a poached egg inside - very, very, nice - But it was a bit cold , could have been warmer.
Came on a bed of spinach surrounded by a chunky tomato something ( which might have been herby tinned tomatoes warmed through) 
Cafe du Monde coffee which is always nice so all in all a good meal just could have been hotter. 
Would go again and probably for dinner.
My grandfather went there to see Dr. Panelli for hearing aids he was very helpfull and knowledgeable! I will refer more family and friends to his practice. Thank you for everything! !!!!!
We got the baked lasagna,  which was delivered cold, and the veal marsala which was nothing but maybe some veal and a brown gravy! Very disappointed!  Wont order from there again!

Service was slow which is understandable since its new but the vodka was horrible. Only thing they had to offer was vodka since they ran out of everything in Thursday. No biggie; ordered a mule. Read the Yelp reviews as I waited and everyone said the vodka tastes like dirt. But I figured you can't mess up a mule and the vodka can't be that bad.... I was wrong. They didn't even use ginger beer... Simple syrup and Scweeps was used instead of ginger beer and the vodka...well Yelp reviews were right. Tastes like dirt. Hopefully they will get everything worked out in the next couple of months.

I have been here several times. I tend to always get the Tennessean. I also ask for extra Jack Daniel glaze cause that's how I roll. 

The sides were average as best....could use some improvement. Fries and tater tots were very average. The home chips had a weird seasoning to it. I suspect it tastes better when you're drunk.

The beer selection was great. Homer Simpson would approve, come to think, he only drinks Duff beer (which they don't carry). 

Milkshakes were good, very thick, like they would clog your intestines. Not literally speaking of course, I'm still here 3 days later.

They have gluten free bun, which is great if you have a gluten allergy, like my wife. She said the bun was one of the better ones she's tried.

I've been eager to try this restaurant once I learned that Nina Compton opened her own place. The restaurant was beautiful with a nice vibe. It was really loud the night we were there and realize that this is attributed to it being in the lobby of a hotel where patrons came in and out to have drinks at the bar. 

We first were given biscuits which were so amazing! I wanted to continue snacking on them all night. We had the conch croquettes and pig ear to start. They both had amazing flavors, especially the pig ear which was an explosion of savory flavors. I wasn't too pleased with the textures of either though. Next we had the hamachi and the "eat your vegetables" which for that day was Brussels sprouts with crunchy chicken skin. The hamachi was surprisingly refreshing with a crazy burst of flavor in such a small bite. This was my favorite dish of the night. The Brussels sprouts were overwhelmingly salty because of the amount of ranch dressing on it. It could have been better with less dressing. For our entree we had the curry goat gnocchi and lobster pasta. These were both phenomenal! The gnocchi was a richer dish and the lobster pasta a lot lighter. Great flavors.

If I could give no star, I would. Go to any other store but this one.  TWICE I was told I would get a replacement for my tablet that wouldn't turn on. No new one arrived, just an empty box delivered for sending in the broken tablet.  A week later, same tablet  returned saying "no problem found."  Product was badly scratched on the back side. Ok, it worked.  But for how long?  And they scratched it.   Went back and signed in.  Waited 25 minutes for my turn when a man walked in with a broken screen on his device and TWO guys started to help him.  When I objected that I was there first, I was just blown off.  Had to INSIST that I be helped next.  The employee guy agreed that I should get a new device and took my mailing address.  He said I would get the new one first, then send in the old one.  Another empty box for returning my tablet was sent -- TO THE WRONG ADDRESS.  Third trip into the store, I was told another empty box would be sent and I would have to mail in my tablet...and maybe would get a reconditioned one back.  These guys don't know how their own system for returns works.  And they are rude.

Went there for famous donuts and fried chickens. The donuts were nice and hot but the fried chickens were too salty. The employees were friendly with high energy level. Please tone down on the salt during marination.
I love pizza mizza' buy one get one deal at night. They have quite a few options to choose from but I would have to say that the carnivore combo is the best by far.
I've always experienced great service at this Discount Tires. Yesterday Aaron was especially helpful.

I will start by saying this food would be really good--it clearly is good quality. I ordered takeout and it was just so cold that it made the meal unejoyable.
Whenever I order takeout, I make sure to get there 5 minutes early in order to prevent taking home cold food. Because I'm not eating it right away, I want to at least take it home immediately. When I arrived it wasn't ready yet, which was fine. I waited and waited and my pickup time came and went. I waited some more and others' orders kept getting called out to be picked-up. Finally, I went to the register and asked them to check on my food. The bartender reached behind him and grabbed a bag that had been sitting there for at least 15 minutes and said "oh it must have just came up!" Now i was taking home food that had already sat around when I had gotten there early to prevent just that. 

I was very disappointed by this. I would suggest if you are going to eat there, don't do take-out. Dine in for sure.

Decent. I had the "Feeling Good" burger and fry for $15 w/ water. 

The burger was good and initially reminded me of Wendy's but with a better grade of beef and a bigger serving per patty. 

The fries were good but I could've used a few more (portion wise). I hate getting halfway through a burger and running out of fries, that should only happen on to go orders (cause what else do you eat on the ride home)

I was kind of disappointed when I asked for the regular burger ($10) with fried egg,and I was suggested the "Feeling Good" burger ($13), although I didnt want bacon. She (a shift leader I'm assuming) said just remove the bacon (she shoulda just removed a dollar or two right?). Obviously, the items are either too pricey a la carte, or they have no way of charging you for a single fried egg. Left me feeling just a little cheated. 

Otherwise, service was hella friendly and the cook cool as a fan.

As a downtown lunch option, I would come back if I REALLY wanted a decent burger in walking distance. I cant name a better burger between here to the Municipal

I'm a  student and UCSB  and have noticed that this place was here when new owners took over last year. The menu has a lot of creative dishes that I still want to try. The 2 sushi plates that I have tried are Superb. The cashier is a student. She was nice and helpful. The place was very clean. The decorations and atmosphere were calming. Definitely returning soon.

I was excited to try but was very disappointed. Beef schwarma was very dry and so old to the point it was curling up from being so dried out. Chicken schwarma was just shredded boiled chicken breast which was also dry. Falafel was also dry and dense and not fried fresh.  Hummus may be  house made but too acidic and not smooth. Everything was coated with tahini in an attempt to cure the dryness but it didn't help.  I also ordered a side of baba ganousch which was meh with too much acid and no smokey flavor and you get a tiny container for 5 bucks. Really the Only edible thing in the platter was the salad. 

I am usually not picky and will generally eat and like anything. But I could barely eat the food I ordered. I would say that the generic schwarma carts all around the city are better and they are by no means good. Maybe they were having an off day because I can't believe that everyone who gave this place great reviews ate the same food I ate today. The staff did seem a bit confused back there. Did something recently change?  For now I would say save your money and eat pretty much anywhere else.

The parking is terrible at Kabuki. They only have 2 stalls behind the Garneau building. But they apparently have a few more in the residential further west. You have to check their website for the exact location of their stalls or pick up one of their brochures at the restaurant.

Once you manage parking and go inside, the restaurant is quite unique in terms of their decor. It's quite simplistic but there is a giant cherry blossom tree in the center decorated with lights, which create a romantic atmosphere for the place. The walls are painted a greenish-yellow with green bamboo accents.

And, of course, we care about the food. For friends who love eel, Kabuki boasts a huge selection of unagi dishes on their menu. Typically restaurants only offer the one and only unagi roll, but this restaurant offers a great variety. What attracted me most to the menu was a couple of flaming rolls. What was disappointing about the rolls was the rice was not rolled tight enough or was the wrong type of rice used(?) but it has that s

What we ordered:

- Flaming unagi roll (forgot the actual name) - It wasn't exactly flaming. They put the roll in a handmade tinfoil box and made it flame underneath the roll. The flame was for decor purposes and enhanced the roll in no way, which was a little disappointing for me, but still beautiful to look at.

- Dragon eye roll - Ahh, the Mikado-made famous dragon eye variation. The sauce was not bad, but comparing to Mikado's original sauce, it tastes nothing like it. What made this stand out for me was they mixed fake crab meat (pollock) in with the rice. It's hard to notice, but if you stop to look at your food carefully, you will notice the flaky addition. Very nice touch to make the roll unique.

- Sockeye salmon sashimi - A rare but classy addition to a few Japanese restaurants in Edmonton. This is the second place where I found this on the menu. At $16 ($4 more than regular salmon sashimi here), it's quite an expensive indulgence. But the sockeye salmon was VERY lean. The texture seemed a bit weird for me...almost flaky like cooked salmon. I haven't had too much experience with raw sockeye salmon, so I can't say whether this is the correct texture or not. But it definitely differs from my other experiences.

The service was good. Since this is quite a new restaurant, I think they just need more time to work it out, but definitely A+ for trying. We ordered tea, but instead of giving us a pot, like they did with the table of 4, we had to wait for the waiter to come by to get more tea...a slight inconvenience. I assume our waiter is the boss as he was super polite and always smiling. What impressed me the most was he bows every time he comes to our table and tells us to enjoy our food quite often. It was to the point where I thought he was starting to go hunchback from doing it too much. But definitely A+ on the Japanese mannerism. In fact, he caught me spying at his parking sheet on the wall and rushed to give me a brochure (for the parking spots) and told me about the website. Needs improvement in some areas, but great service still.

All in all, I would be willing to try this place out again some time in the later future.

Cannot comment on service because if I am going to sit down somewhere it wouldn't be in a pizza place. With that being said, food is incredible. You can tell they use fresh ingredients and cheese steaks are the best in Delco. Good quality food, fast delivery and reasonably priced. Their pizza is not on my favorites list but everything else i have was dynamite.

Well, I don't understand how we could order, the table next to us orders 3 minutes later, they get their food and are half done when we finally get ours (their order looked similar to ours, but there were 3 of them). Oh wait, we get ours, and it's cold! It was good, but would have been VERY good if it was at lead warm. I would have complained, but was with company and they weren't paying. I'd think twice about going there again

My First spot and favorite place to go for drinks before I start my night life.
 Must try their St. Germaine drink! Its the best!. 
If you plan to go for dinner, try to go early before 8pm maybe. Their food are great!!. 
But after 8, Tables are empty with many 'reserve' signs on it nor can they take any orders because their kitchen will be closed.
After 8pm I usually sat at their bar or their open window for my drinks so its not so bad.

This salon is an  Aveda Lifestyle Salons/Spas.  These are flagship Aveda salons and spas with a passion for service and commitment to our philosophy of connecting beauty, wellness and care for the environment. They offer Aveda Signature Services as well as the full range of Aveda products. Expect to be greeted, offered a beverage (the tea is yummy),  receive a complimentary sensory ritual and get a killer head massage.
Pricey, yes! But if you are Mrs. Thurston Howell the Third it doesn't matter!

This place is so amazing. Don't let the long wait phase you one bit. There's an efficient coffee bar where you can have drinks (including a scrumptious Bloody Mary complete with a mini charcuterie stick) and pastries while you wait. I'm convinced that you could close your eyes and point at anything on the menu and be 100% satisfied. There is nowhere else in Indianapolis to even consider going for brunch if Milktooth is open. My advice is to come with an open mind and allow yourself to be extra indulgent!

Claims to have the best bloody mary in the city. Don't believe it.
It just mix, vodka and a few pickled green beans and a lemon.
pathetic.

My 2004 Honda CRV stalled out on Lincoln Drive thankfully restarted and i took it took it to Martin that morning...after i got the car back the check engine light came on again...brought it back the following Monday morning.........The building also lost power that morning so the shop was running on backup power supply. Mark took my car in right away and fixed the 2nd problem on it right away....I was very thankful they took my car in right away those two times......and had the shuttle to take me to work...that's a huge lifesaver. Im not a fan of dealerships but when they take your car with no power in their building and fix it before 10am- im a fan.

This place is great. Staff is really friendly and supportive, machines and overall the cleanest gym I have been to in New Orleans. Love the circuit area for an overall timed workout when I run in before work.  Not one of those places [eople come to show off.  Especially like the treadmills with TV's.  I can watch my news shows before work as well.  Locker rooms couldn't  be nicer.  Color choices make you feel comfortable and not antiseptic.

The bar itself is beautiful.

We looked at a menu..
Can we try the wheel of happenstance?
- We don't have it.
Can we try the gummis?
- I don't have those in.
May I buy a postcard to send?
- We don't do that anymore.

So one entire side of the menu was void, admittedly the part that brought us in. The bartender was less than engaged. We wont be back and this place honestly couldn't care any less.
I have been in many Rodizio's restaurants around the world, including tops in Brasil. Boizao is on my top list. The lamb chops are superb... Job well done!!!

What's my favorite food?  BARBECUE!  What's my favorite sound to listen to while eating my favorite food?  VROOM VROOOOOOM!

That's right, ladies and gents, this backwoods gem is straight out of Easy Rider... you half expect to turn and see Dennis Hopper and Peter Fonda eating at the table next to you.  Not Jack Nicholson, unfortunately... although he's all of our favorite character, George Hanson was beaten to death in his sleeping bag.  Ah, and so went the leftist movement.

Anyways, back to the review.  You drive up the highway past Santa Barbara, and wind up a beautiful hill and into the wine country.  Turn off on an easy to miss left turn, and then go right down into a heavily-wooded canyon.  

Cold Spring Tavern originated as a coach stop in the mid-1800s, and the buildings all (at least) appear to be original.  Water damaged wood structures with the clear evidence of termite infestation.  Now it's a hot spot for motorcycle riders (both the original gangsta freebird riders and also the rich dudes with a bike or the crotch rockets), old guys with really sweet cars, and also the everyday Joe who just wants some damn good barbecue.

If you go on a day that isn't Sunday, you will have the option of a variety of reasonably-priced sandwiches, ribs, chicken, and pork.  Sunday afternoon is really the time to go, however.  A MASSIVE Samoan guy manning a barbecue, and piling huge sandwiches full of beautifully cooked tri-tip.  The barbecue sauce has a little kick and is delicious.  Even the horseradish (of which I am not usually a fan) is a perfect compliment to this sandwich.  Get two of them, trust me, and for $6 or so a pop this is a deal that can't be beat.  Sloppy, tender meat, perfectly complimentary sauces, and fresh rolls that are other-worldly.

And then sit around, gorge yourself, have a few drinks and enjoy the live music.

This is a place where you go to be yourself... no one is judging you, because everyone is there for one reason and one reason only... great food and a unique atmosphere.

If you're going for dinner, make sure to bring a full wallet, because the prices escalate quickly.  Gone are the rib and tri-tip deals.  Arriving are the interesting dishes (rabbit, duck, venison, etc.) with prices to match.  I haven't eaten dinner, but I have looked at the menu, and it looks like a very special spot... I will be going, and I will add to this review when I do.

I can't say enough good things about this place.  It is one of my favorite restaurants anywhere.  I have driven up the coast from LA (about a 1 1/2 hour trip) just for lunch.  5 stars without any hesitation.

Reservation for six people on a Saturday (no problems there). I love bourbon so I was excited. 
The good: the food was very good (tavern ham with 151 sauce was excellent, jerk bbq wings were some of the best I've ever had, crab deviled eggs were very good, and the mac and cheese was good as well). 
The okay: no flights for the bourbon or whiskey (they need to look at DRY 85 in Annapolis) and the beer selection was a bit limited as far as top notch craft beers. For that matter, most of the bourbons were ones you can get locally. For a whiskey bar, I want spirits I've never heard of. 

We will definitely be going back though!!

I've been to Bailey's Range 3 times in the last 4 months. That may not sound like a lot...but I also live in Las Vegas. I found out about Bailey's Range on Yelp as I was looking for a good selection of local beers at a place that would be open between lunch and dinner. The local beer selection is excellent and the staff who work the bar seem to know quite a bit about the beer. Of my three visits, two of them included the best service I've received in St. Louis.

I have had 3 different burgers for  each of my three trips. The most recent was a Big Popper, which is my favorite. I've also had Dave's Chop House and The Carolina. After my three different burgers I will believe that they do not serve a bad one. The fries are also a favorite, as well as having some of the best fried pickles I've ever eaten. I am still dreaming about them. 

I have also sampled a couple of the lemonade cocktails which are both strong and refreshing. 

I will most definitely be back to Bailey's Range on my next visit to St. Louis.

Since going paleo it's hard to find something that doesn't taste like cardboard to satisfy my pizza cravings. The gluten free pizza here is the best I've found and they even personalize it any way I want including no cheese and extra sauce. It's my new fav!

Ordered the trout sandwich and didn't really know what to expect. It ended up being one of the best sandwiches I've ever had in my life. So good that I'm writing a Yelp review about it, which is not typical for me. Absolutely delicious. Also ordered The Butcher (cocktail) which was very good as well. Highly recommend.

A restaurant has to have a 'hook' these days, and one of Bailey's is the dairy/cow/rustic farm theme, right down to the milk can lights and assortment of old windows over the central community table in the bar area. The first floor is open to the second floor, lending itself to increased noise level, which it was the night we were there. Burger joints seem to be the "in" thing and this is a burger joint, but definitely an upscale one, both in their offerings and their prices. 

Another 'hook' is the option to have your burger made from a variety of sources: bison, lamb, beef, pork, chicken or veggie. All cooked to order and on your choice of bun. Some of their condiments were unfamiliar to our group (sriracho mayo, rooster sauce). All in all, an interesting concept. Our burgers were good, but we all agreed they didn't make it on our "best ever" list. And $11-$12 for a burger is pretty steep in my world - you're obviously paying for the concept & cutesy atmosphere rather than a well-executed burger. And when you add in drinks and dessert, it ends up being a pretty pricey night out, especially with a family.

Service was so-so. The hostesses seemed pre-occupied with their own conversation. Our server was friendly and answered all our questions about the menu, but she was pretty much MIA after she took our order. We didn't order dessert, and after reading other reviews, sounds like we missed out on the one thing Bailey's does exceptionally well.

We're here once a week, for the beer/food/company and the great happy hour deals.  

The 2 for 1 pizza happy hour special is IMO the best deal in town if you're looking to have dinner a bit early or lunch a bit late.   Pizza selection is a bit limited, however the ones we've tried have all been delicious.  They're putting in a new pizza oven, so I hope the pizza's are going to get even better.

Excellent burgers as well, top class Blue Burger and BBQ Burger.  The happy hour 'Gregs Messy BBQ Burger' is IMO the perfect dinner, sized right  enough to fill without stuffing yourself silly.

My wife enjoys the asada taco's, it's a shame they're not on the happy hour menu.

The beer is good as well, put some money into a machine and they are typically generous with the comps.   I think due to the limited space there is not much interesting beer, usually one handle with something different but it can take a while to cycle through and get a new beer so the selection doesn't change much.

Bartenders are friendly and always seem willing to go the extra mile.
Michelle is......Michelle. She is disorganized, a total mess as is the place. But she has a good heart and does a good job and is inexpensive. That's all I really care about.

So I am not a real fan of Japanese Steakhouses such as these because I am not a fan of pasta and rice; however, I went to try this one. Now I haven't been to a restaurant like this in over 10 years, so I don't quite remember the set up etc. This was my first time going to a Kobe so I thought this would be different than what I did remember from my last visit to Benihana's. Ok, let's get into the review. 

First Impressions/Appearance:  So when you walk in, the restaurant is very dry and doesn't give you anything to awe at. There is no real pop of red or anything to make this restaurant stand out from any other typical restaurant. The tables are very dark in color, which I typically don't mind but again it was very dry and dull. They seat you at 10 to a table which again I didn't mind, but it is very close and a bit uncomfortable when you're trying to enjoy dinner. 

Customer Service: I am big on customer service and theirs was on point. Their customer service was great. We were seated immediately and the wait staff was great and attentive. Our drinks were filled and they cleared our soup and salad bowls in time so we had more space at the small tables. At the end of our meal, there was another lady that came out to box up our left overs which she did in front of us so that gets an extra star from me. 

The Dinner Show:  our chef was very entertaining. He did all of the tricks, the 'egg roll', flipping the egg in his hat and flipping the shrimp tail in his shirt pocket. That was cool and so was the volcano and making the fire shoot out and up. He cracked jokes and made fun of all the latest commercials playing on the radio. He cooked the vegetables with such precision and made the noodles and rice with so much action. I don't remember noodles and rice being that entertaining, but he made them a real show. His knife techniques were astonishing and the cut of the meat and chicken all the same size. 

The Food:  the soup was ok and full of flavor. It was served hot which was good on a cold night. The salad was fresh and the ginger dressing was delicious, I really could have used more salad. The vegetables were cooked first. We had onions, zucchini, carrots, broccoli, and green beans. I think they were undercooked but I think most people like their veggies a bit more crispy. The onions were very pungent and could have been cooked a little longer along with the carrots and beans. Next came the noodles. Now as o stated earlier, I am not a pasta fan but I do cook it for my family. These noodles were under seasoned and overlooked. They could have used some salt and pepper and should have been a little less than al dente. That way, it can finish cooking on the grill. The rice was next, and it was not cooked, so when the chef went to fry it, it didn't steam enough, so we ended up with hard rice that was greasy and had no flavor. Lastly were the meats. The meat had good flavor and it was cooked well. I had the chicken and steak and both were prepared how I liked. The steak also came with potatoes, which surprisingly were pretty good. 

Rating: So why 3 stars? Simply put, the food could have been better and the establishment could have been nicer. I can spend the same amount and maybe a few dollars more on more food and much better food. I know the idea is a dinner and a show, but I think they need to work on their food more since they have the show down. I don't think I will be going back but glad I decided to give it a try since I have never been and now I have a platform to let others know what to expect.

It's not hard to land really good Greek food in Tarpon Springs.  And this place is always at the top of our list.  The Gyro is the best.  The sampler plate is always perfect with plenty to take home.  The Sangrias are good (although sometimes not heavy enough).  My love is the Grouper a la Hellas.  What is already an excellent fish, they know how to do just right.  We always stop at the bakery after dinner for take-home deserts.  Service...always consistent, never had a bad experience.  Everyone from our 5 year old to out-of-town guests fall in love with the place.

I really like this neighborhood place a lot! The decor is bright, welcoming, and really adorable. I love that they now have outside seating as well. Every time I have gone there the staff and service is very good. The only thing they need to bring on is happy hour though! The cocktail and wine list is excellent and would be even more so once they bring a HH into the mix!
Our party of 6 each order something different. We are all pleased with our entrees and look forward to a return visit.

OK its Superbowl Sunday at 4:57 p.m. when I realize I am out of propane.  I had some great looking Prime Ribeye's that badly needed a good grill'n.   I called Snyder's to see what time they closed.  When the guy said they were closing in 3 minutes, and I asked if he knew somewhere else I could get a tank filled.  He said he didn't but if I could get over there in the next 10 minutes, he'd wait around for me.  I am sure he had his own Superbowl party to go to, but he stuck around.  Above and beyond.  Thanks Snyder's.

1, the one bedroom apartment has 950 SQ for 1160$ 

2, The deadline at the first of every month and it will effect your credit by being late, if you don't have it by the 5th they will turn to the court

3,Not advised at the summer their AC doesn't stay cool
Oh man, coushined foot rests at the bar!!!! Whoa! Yes! Good service, prompt attention and great environment. Love the concept as well. Thanks!!!
My mother and I shared the fresh tuna salad sandwich with fries. The fries were amazing! And the tuna salad was the best I've ever had. I like canned albacore tuna, and this topped it ten times!!!
Simply Amazing! Everything was spot on, from the bread and butter to the last bite of the French toast dessert. Will return and try the tasting menu.  Farmhaus is a must try and must return!

This place was big and had a rustic interior. It was busy but the service was pretty fast. The donuts were huge and the flavors were pretty clever. The texture is between cakey and light like a regular donut. The cold brew was dark and delicious.

3-Stars for being good, BUT over priced. Unless you are  a senior, then you get a good deal, and it is well worth it.  

Usually the place is either empty or near empty in the morning.  And it's most often seniors who are there. It really is a nice place. We also really think that it is usually really empty because it is really over priced.  I mean there are often more staff than customers in the morning/afternoon because they have prices that keep people away.

Seriously omelet, toast, and coffee is near $15, and with wife it's near $30. 
I would like to give the place a better review as we like it there. However we also feel stupid for spending that much on eggs and toast.

We  only go there when our parents are visiting as the senior deal is a good deal for  them.
I've past this place a number of times and glad I stopped. I got the chicken Pad Tai to go, it was great. Nice portion well presented and a container of red pepper to make it as hot as I wanted.

I feel compelled to give Smoothie King five stars...the service is quick, they don't spend a lot of time upselling me and never mess up my order.  Granted, they're not creating nepal, but still, I can (and do) appreciate people who can follow directions.  This location has a great staff and they can work through a crowd pretty quickly, which is why it's my preferred location.
Plain and simple, I need to move to Indy.  The brewery is perfect in every way; I cannot wait to be back.  As a Statistician, the name is too great not to love.

A friend took me to lunch here while I was in town visiting recently. They do have gluten free bread so ordered a Choose Two, with a McAlister's Club and their vegetarian chili (which I was told was GF). Really enjoyed both. The manager even came out to see how we were doing and when I mentioned I wished we had one of these in Phoenix, she proceeded to tell me that apparently we do! In fact there are two locations and she went to find out where they are and came back to tell me. What service and then some! Looking forward to my next visit to a location near me.

This is the only deli within walking distance of my office. They have a pretty big menu of most deli style sandwiches. They also sell sodas and chips. The only thing that's hard for me is, there never seems to be a go to person to order your food. Sometimes you're placing an order to a short person over their 5' tall reach in cooler, which is strange. Other times you order at the register, other times the guy in the back wake over and asks you. I really am not sure about that, I hope they can figure out the organization because it gets awkward for customers when several people are in there standing around at lunch time.

Food: great fries, all sandwiches are oversized. Soul food Friday is a thing here, but I have no idea how it compares.

This place is two for two with me!

I went once for lunch and had their specialty Farmhouse Burger - a burger with an egg on top, and their specialty mustard on the side. It was a surprisingly excellent burger. Very juicy and full of flavor. Service on this particular visit was extremely slow, and with all the televisions showing college football plus the music blaring, the place was pretty loud.

My second visit I met a friend for happy hour.  Much lower volume level this visit, and the server was much more efficient.  Great deals for happy hour - I went with the lemon drop martini, on special for $6.  All the appetizers are discounted for happy hour also, so my friend and I ordered a smorgasbord of items.  

Duck wings are mentioned in every review, and they were great - nice and crispy, with a bit of a bite from the sauce. I also loved the drunken meatballs - they too were in a spicy sauce, and cooked perfectly. The big surprise of the night was the Kobe Brick Pizza - thin crust, loaded with wagyu beef, cheese, caramelized onions, roasted tomatoes, bacon and arugula, it had a fabulous flavor - I would definitely order this again. 

The only appetizer I didn't love was their version of the Seven Layer Dip: white bean purée, harissa, yogurt, oven roasted tomatoes, smashed avocados, smoked cheddar & chopped olives served with grilled naan.  Even with all those ingredients, it just did not have much flavor.  It was still good, but not great.

I will definitely be back to explore their drink and food menus further, and to take advantage of their excellent happy hour.

I got the baked chicken...or should I say chicken jerky. This measly piece of breast meat was so overcooked the edges were turning translucent. I could barely chew through it to swallow. They were out of EVERYTHING when we arrived, which made me assume my food would be tasty. The black eyed peas tasted like they were just boiled. Had something weird looking in it maybe bacon, but absolutely no flavor. Cabbage was the same, just boiled. Not exactly sure why we had to wait 20 minutes for food that they popped in the microwave. I'm assuming at one point over the years they served cornbread, well no longer. My bf got fried fish and chicken; it all tasted like flour. The mac and cheese was super dry and burnt, and tasted like boiled noodles nothing else. Sweet potatoes are definitely from a can, probably why they taste so good in comparison to everything else. We only went here because we had a free gift card. STILL wound up spending like 20 bucks. Wasn't worth the drive we made half way across the city. And having to listen to the cook curse and complain about working there made those 20 minutes seem even less fruitful. Definitely won't be back.

Yea.. So this place is terrible. I don't know when they became "famous", but it tastes like it was a long time ago. Floating objects in our drinks. Some in the original drink brought out and in the one they replaced it with. Along with lipstick on the brim of the other glass. The food was meh. Crab soup and buffalo shrimp for starters and garlic crabs for the main course. Oh and they're kind of expensive. Don't waste your money.

Stopped by for dinner.  Great place, good vibes, clean with great service with reasonable prices (for Santa Barbara).  Tried the Cobb salad and the rainbow trout.  Both were excellent!  The cob salad was chopped, so I had all the delicious fresh ingredients in every bite.  Nice crispy bacon!! Yum!!  Even if your not a salad water, this dish will not disappoint.  Trout was very tasty.  Grilled, perfectly deboned, moist and flavorful.

Finally got to try this place this weekend and boy was it an experience. 7 courses. all in a big vat in the middle of the table eating with your hands. It was a blast. Definitely go with a big group and bring some wine as it's a byo. The phyllo wrapped chicken was probably my favorite. There's belly dancing (only on the weekends apparently) which made it one of the best evenings in a long time. You get a big towel napkin because of how sloppy you get and they wash you down with rose water. It is simply just a wonderful place I will be sure to return.

Based on the exceptional reviews, my wife and I decided to try this restaurant.  The staff was very friendly and we  felt like were family.  We order two salads and four sushi rolls.  We were also given soup and edamame.  The salads were very good.  While the rolls were very good, our sushi restaurant in Las Vegas is much more flavorful.  However, we would visit this restaurant again on our next visit to Tucson.

It's been family run since 1989.  That's a lot of time to perfect breakfast food.  This is no frills or fluffyness breakfasts.  It's down home pancakes, waffles, omelets and the almighty... Dutch Baby!  This thing alone is what makes this spot where I go for breakfasts.  It takes some time to cook; so grab an appetizer of breakfast potatoes or an english muffin.  Both are great.
Had lunch here because it was right next to where we parked. Thin crust pizza was really good. Their home made Italian  sausage was delicious!
Live music and delicious sandwiches on a sunday morning. I love blues city deli. It has a great friendly atmosphere, and the sandwiches here are the besssst

I wish I could give more than 5 stars!
It was our first time here and I can guarantee it won't be our last. 
Since moving from out of state, we've been searching for a burger & fries (with ranch) and haven't found anything comparable--until tonight!
Service was great- our waitress made sure drinks were refilled and the food met our expectations. 
The burger was HUGE and came to the table exactly as ordered. And the fries & ranch-- hit the spot.  
The cost of this fantastic meal was super reasonable- $10 for burger and fries.  Just wish I would have taken a pic to go along with the review.  Next time!
Thanks Bully's for such a great overall experience.
How can you not love this place; "leather" electric recliners, pretty much the same price as AMC or Regal, they serve alcohol and there are no kids/tweens!!!

We have a Yorkie we rescued and it was important to us that he be treated well.  When we first took him in he was frightened, shaking almost uncontrollably.  The staf was wonderful with him..and he was much better when we picked him up.  We have taken him here a few times in the last five months and I must say, each time he is doing so much better, although he still plays the guilt card when we take him in.  But he is obviously happy when we pick him up and  He even kisses his groomer, Heather, goodbye!  His cut is fabulous and the appointment times are within a day, if not the same day.  We cut him pretty short when we take him camping and the staff had wonderful suggestions should he get pine sap in his fur.... which he did.. and the peanut butter on it worked great!!  I have not been disappointed yet.  Whether it is a typical puppy cut or the short cut, it is always just what we asked for.
 
I would highly recommend them, and so does our little guy, Scooter!

Stumbled upon this place when I was walking around the neighborhood. Very small but lovely. I think it's a fun "supplemental gift option" especially for your Philly friends who are leaving. If you're like me and you've come here for school, you've had a lot of good friends stay for a while and then up and leave me for residencies, fellowships, new jobs... So sad, but so nice to give them something to remember Philly by. I purchased this canvas where a local philly artist had painted different neighborhood logos-- like they had a Pennsport/Queen Village one that had Federal Donuts, Royal Tavern, Tatooed Mom's, etc... Very cute. They have lots of totes, philly-themed onesies, jewelry etc... A fun find!

We have been there twice and will not return. The Good: both times service was great. Surprising their sides are really good. The Bad: tiny portions, very dry meat, over salty ribs and all of their sauces are super watery. Not a good sign for BBQ place without great meat and sauces. If they guys want to survive they need to change their portions, address the super dry meat, over salted ribs and come up with better sauces.

Tried a couple varieties of the stromboli - the supreme and sausage & mushroom - both were outstanding.  But, what really stood out was the crust.  It was thick, chewy, buttery, salty and garlicy - in short, it was good.  

This place doesn't skimp on the fillings - which were fresh and well-seasoned.  The prices aren't too bad either.

We were pleased and satisfied with the amazing level of service at Ed Morse Cadillac. They addressed each concern with respect and affirmation; skills that other dealerships could benefit from. Our vehicle was returned in impeccable quality with all issues corrected, and it was returned on time when originally quoted to be returned to us. The rental was wonderful and a true joy to drive. Of course, that too was a Cadillac. In customer service along, every penny was well spent. And the quality of product does not need my words to enhance it. In short, thank you for treating us and our vehicle with respect and care. You are doing a wonderful job, keep it up!

Don't believe the bad reviews. Everything was delicious. Went with my Groupon and now I'm stuffed as heck. Highly recommend either the shrimp or scallops. Certainly pricey but you get a ton of tasty food. Also you should upgrade to the fried rice.

Let me begin by saying I had high expectations of this place because some foodie friends recommended it. First, they don't take reservations, so be prepared to wait. And wait. And wait. We decided to go there later, thinking we'd avoid a long wait. Wrong! Got there at 8:00 on a Friday night, put our name in, and was told it would be a 45 to 60-minute wait. If you have to wait, make sure you go on a nice evening so you can stand outside...the "bar" is more like a walkway/pass through to the dining room. If you can't sit at a table or belly up to the bar, be prepared to be elbowed, stepped on and bumped into every 2 seconds.

When we were finally seated 75 minutes later, our bubbly waitress, Ashley, was at our table in just a few minutes. As she tried to share the evening's specials, half of the table couldn't hear because the noise level is DEAFENING!!!!

Appetizers: We started with appetizers...smokey shrimp with grits and cole slaw, and flatbread with herbed goat cheese. I found the shrimp/grits appetizer tasty, while the flatbread was, well, flat. Just goat cheese spread on some plain bread.

The entrees: being a pescatarian, there weren't many choices for me...trout or the striped bass special. I opted for the trout. While it was quite tasty and cooked properly, it was heavy on the salt. And I am not a fan of salty dishes. Others ordered the pork chop, the ribeye and the bass special. Everyone's comments: it's okay. Just okay.

The desserts: I am a dessert person. Anything with sugar. Period. But, after perusing the menu, nothing really appealed to me. Which says alot because...did I mention I'm a dessert person? Those that ordered dessert ate their dessert quietly. Draw your own conclusions.

Lesson learned: go to a new restaurant with no expectations, just in case.

I have been to this place twice once being on Valentines Day. The first time waited almost 2 hours to be seated but was totally worth it. We had the oyster shooters, abalone, cioppino, shrimp scampi, and the steamed clams and mussels in wine broth. Everything was killer our plates were left spotless. We were even drinking the wine broth from the clams and mussels from how good it was. On Valentines Day obviously it was very packed so we ended up going to the side and ordering to go to sit on the benches on the pier. We ordered oyster shooters, steamed clams and mussels and rock crab. The shooters and clams were to die for yet again. The crab got me it tasted so fresh and even came with soup(clam chowder) and a salad. I had not had fresh crab like that in quite some time. Our order was ready very quickly. I will definitely be going to eat here whenever I need my seafood fix.

I have never had my hair done here so I am writing based on my spa experience only. I have had several massages and facials here and have found them all to be wonderfully relaxing. Aveda products are wonderful and they will ask you some brief questions about your skin before your facial so they use the correct products on you. They have a store in the front if you wish to purchae products. They will often have a special where you will receive a 50 minute spa session if you purchase $60 worth of face products.

Pretty solid place. The burgers are good, though not quite as craveable as Shake shack, and sometimes cooked a little more than I like - medium means I should see pink. You can get an egg on them though which obviously makes anything awesome. Even though the burgers aren't top tier ; this place makes up for it with comfy seating, super friendly staff and all around good vibes. And the milkshakes are awesome. And beer.

PHOTOS UPLOADED 

Ethiopian food virgins no more! Such a delicious cuisine. Prepare to eat with your hands. You can request a fork if you are not feeling adventurous. Some entrees are spicy but can be requested as mild. 

PROS: 

~ You will be greeted by a woman with such an infectious smile. 

~ Modern and relaxed ambiance. 

~ Exciting cuisine. So many to try. 

~ They accept American Express. 

~ Locally owned by a mother and daughter team. 

~ Plenty of parking. 

~ Clean restroom. 

Description Taken from Their Online Menu 

~ Beg Tibs ...............................$12.75 
Fresh lamb sautéed with purified herbal butter seasoned with onions, green pepper, tomato spices and fresh rosemary. 

Zilzil Tibs.................................$12.89 
Long strips of tender beef sautéed lightly in purified herbal butter; seasoned with onion and fresh rosemary 

CONS: 

~ It can be difficult to find as it is in an industrial area. 

~ Service can be a bit slow; however, the food is worth it. 

NOTE TO PARENTS: 

~ No diaper changing table in the women's restroom.

~ You can request a small portion of split peas for your little one as baby food.  My son happen to love Ethiopian food but it was offered to us.

First time here in a long time. Thought we'd give it a shot. Server was pleasant but service was slow. I had the meatball parmigiana with pasta in white sauce. My plate was by far the best thing at the table. My wife had the roast beef sandwich with mash potatoes. It was ok but a bland and not much to talk about. My daughters kids cheeseburger meal with fries was good she said. Overall with the service and food we got gave us the agreed upon rating above.

How many Peco Energy lineman does it take to turn on a lightbulb?.... 

This is the year 2009 and yesterday a huge tree fell across a main, two lane road and knocked down power lines. Eighteen and 1/2 hours later, we finally had our power restored. 

From 4AM to 10:30PM I watched as Peco trucks traveled down the road, along with firetrucks and police cars. The road was totally blocked, for most of the day. 

This is what ultimately irked me... Asplundh arrived shortly after 4AM, with trucks for removing this huge tree and two flatbed trucks with new poles. 

The Channel 6 news crews were there and the police stayed on the scene to direct traffic turn around. Peco workers were spotted having breakfast at the local eateries and or just sitting in their trucks in the nearby shopping centers. 

From what I have witnessed, this is atypical of Peco, Verizon and Comcast, to sit in their trucks and eat hero's and drink coffee. When will you be my hero guys? 

The Channel 6 news trucks came, Peco flew down the road to the scene. Later when the helicopters starting pouring in around 5PM and 6PM, the Peco workers again flew down the road to the power outage site. 

Now, I know I do not have all the reasons as to why they were not at the scene to restore power, but I do know, as sure as I am typing this Asplundh did their job, early on and left and the news was right on top of this story. 

Peco is the major electric and gas power providers in the Philadelphia and surrounding areas. Their generation and transmission charges have gone through the roof. We pay, we can't bitch, because they are the major game in town. 

I was off from work and did paperwork by candle light, okay this is cool and I know how they felt in Colonial times, all I needed was a quill pen and ink. I could not cook, do laundry or vacuum. It was a dismal day with the rain pouring down, my sump pump, dehumidifier and laundry pump not being able to assist me, so my basement flooded. 

I am hoping the food in both of my refrigerators and freezers is good. 

But, eighteen and one half hours, with no power, TV, computer and Yelp in this day and age, because a tree fell, is inexcusable.

An amazing experience for my mother.  From the first time I called to make the appointment and arriving at the office was great.  Everyone was so pleasant and friendly.  My mom's appointment was at 10:30 and at exactly 10:30 she was called back to see the dentist.  This is a beautiful and stat of the art facility, this office is phenomenal.  The dentist and staff are wonderful.

Still no whip cream machine like most of the other places so therefore I don't come here anymore.

Some locations are not as clean as others

The anticipation mounted for the grand opening of Nordstrom. I missed the Big TA-DA but I did make my way down that wing of the mall while doing a bit of light shopping.
Large pillars, bright lights, friendly sales people, and Carrie Bradshaw's' shoe closet met me as I walked in. This company knows the way to any woman's heart ; Choos' and Blaniks just to name a few... ohhhh in another world with out student loans I would have done some major damage just in that first room alone. 
My mission was a hat for p2p but I had no such luck. The fragrance wall just outside beauty bar row also caught my eye. Ill have to return for a Nordstrom only day and while im there have lunch at the upstairs restaurant.

Oh I'll be back
Good food! Decent indian flavor. Service can be better, a lot of times short of staff.
The capirinhas are soooo good. My fave cocktail! Especially passion fruit. :) The chicharrones rock, and I've never had bad food here.

This huge outdoor mall was a great find while on a brief getaway to Reno. I giddily shopped Pottery Barn, Orvis, and Dillard's and was majorly surprised by how nice all the employees were (hey, I'm from California)..Nor did any of the employees' demeanors change when we stepped out of stores without any purchases. It was nice to leisurely walk and shop, but some places are driving distance away, since it is just a large strip of shops. Also, missing were small food shops while the actual restaurants were stand-alones not connected to the strip. Still, if back in this area, I would definitely come back. The Dillard's here was a tad nicer than the Macy's west chains, and had pretty sweet deals.

After many years of intending and wanting to join my sister in N.O. for Jazz Fest, my wife and I finally did it!  We just returned from a five night stay.  My sister has attended the festival for many years and typically stays at another hotel in the French Quarter.  When we tried to make a reservation there several months ago, they were booked.  My sister then recommended the Hotel Provincial since it was close to where she was staying and also had recommended it to friends in the past.  That was fortunate for us.

The location was perfect.  Walking distance to all sorts of cool places in the French Quarter including Bourbon St., Central Grocery, Cafe du Monde and the French Market.  

As soon as we arrived we were greeted by a friendly staff at the door who immediately assisted us with our bags and then brought them to our room once we checked in.  They had someone posted at this position (doorman, if you will) at all times during the day and evening and the two or three different staff we saw throughout our stay were always helpful whether we needed directions, a picture taken, or with calling a taxi.

Our room was very quaint and clean (no sign of any ghosts).  We did not ask for housekeeping each day, but when we did, the room was ready for us when we returned each night.  There is free wifi which worked well.  This is an older hotel in the French Quarter and definitely not a "cookie cutter" Hyatt or Sheraton type place so you won't find such things as a "business center", but you will find a nice courtyard and a pool (we didn't use the pool) as well as a pretty cool bar.

It did tend to get a little loud at night.  Maybe it had something to do with our room overlooking Chartres St.  Also, there was some sort of domestic issue at the room next to us on one of the nights and the police were called.  But I think that could happen anywhere; especially in a town where there are more bars than Starbucks. 

We will definitely be headed back to N.O. as soon as we can and will stay at the Hotel Provincial.

Avoid this place like the plague. They are a bunch of cocky witches trying to pretend they are a swanky NYC bar.  My friends paid the bouncer $100 to let them in since there was a ridiculous line.  The bouncer took the money and said to give him 5 minutes.  15 minutes later, he disappeared.  We spoke with the manager, Monica who was outside the entire time with the bouncer and she said "none of our bouncers will ever take money" then she said "there is no one here who looks like that" after we explained the bouncer who took the money.  Clearly he worked there since she was speaking with him a mere 20 minutes earlier.  We would have been totally fine waiting in line if they told us so, and NOT taken $100 from us.  

Inside was a mad house with overpriced drinks we had to wait 30 minutes for.  That was my first and last time at this so called establishment.  They are low class and money grubbing a holes.

Yes!  Finally a great Chicago deep dish pizza in Nashville!  Made our first visit here today and already cant wait to take friends. The pizza was delicious, with the crisp, flaky crust that you'd expect.  The sauce had that little bit of sweet taste that I'm used to having on a Chicago pizza.  Also, the risotto balls were delicious.  We didnt order the pretzels this trip but got to see them.  If they taste jalf as good as they look theyll be great too.  Service was very friendly too.  Get there now, youll be glad you did.

Worst Chinese/Asian food ever. Ordered appetizers and entrees together and entrees were on the table within 3 minutes after ordering but no sign of appetizers. Well I can live with that if the quality of food is good. We ordered two fried tofu dishes and believe it that tofu was definitely refried from a pre-fried tofu as it was filled with oil which explains why they were out in 3 minutes. Any of the vegetables in any of the dishes including lo-mein weren't fresh. There was no flavor to any of the dishes, no spices, not even salted properly. The only thing we could taste was oil, oil and oil. One of the person from our party did get sick right after we left the restaurant.

Try at your own risk.

I wish I had this place at home! Amazing. I couldn't decide and wanted one of everything. I ended up getting the pork belly slider, waffle fries and a cinnamon roll. They torched the cinnamon roll to Carmelize and it was unreal! Everything was so good. I would definitely go back to try the donut sandwiches and some of the other delicious flavor a of donuts they had. Don't miss! They also have great coffee!

Consistently good burger, beer, sandwich and individual pizza place in the heart of the Main Line, near Villanova University.

Don't expect anything too fancy, but always count on something dependable and good-tasting.

If you're reading this update in isolation (not in the sense that you're in solitary confinement, but in the sense that you're not reading it along with my Penang update), I recommend you go to phillymonica.yelp.com.

Now, as part of my morning goals for the day, I promised I wouldn't drink or eat carbs, but would instead opt for a salad and go to the gym.

While I did go to the gym, I failed to "not drink." At lunch, I downed 2 margaritas (one with Canton Ginger Liqueur instead of tequila) and a Canton-bourbon-'arita. They were all so delicious I couldn't help but allow one to follow the other. 

I did order a taco salad though. Great food, but unsuccessful day, folks. Better luck tomorrow.

We were lucky.  Our waiter, Mark, enjoys food as much as we do.  His recommendations were right on the mark.

We started with 2 glasses of red wine and the Mr. George's Onion Rings $5.  What a surprise and treat.  We are not fried onions eaters but this plate was cooked to perfection.  The batter on thin, delicate and very flavorful.  Onion cooked just enough without being soft.

Cindy's main course was the Chili Butter Baked Escovar Fish Baked with Compound Chili Butter $18.95.  Perfectly cooked - very moist with lost of flavor.

My dish was a Pork Shank serviced with a delicious sauce around $21.  The meal was excellent even though the pork was a little dry due to being slightly over cooked.

The 3 items were our waiter's favorites so I can't recommend anything else on the menu.  Overall a nice experience.
Everything here is amazing. I've been a customer for 13 years. It's my go-to for amazing deserts and other items. Do yourself a favor. Go. Now.
I loved the Honolulu roll. Some of the best sushi in Tampa! Fairly priced and cute atmosphere

Interesting St. Louis tradition. Have many St. Louis friends who have told me about it  before I ever tried it. But I'm from Milwaukee which lays claim to being the original custard location (Leon's , of TV's "Happy Days" series) and where it's a much bigger thing than it is in St. Louis. However, Drewes has tried the trendy "Dairy Queen" mixtures, not only with success, but with some really nice variations. I love sour cherries and even in Wisconsin, all you get is Bing cherries in custard. Drewes' Sour cherry and hot fudge is a great experiment. Next time, however, I want to try it just plain to make a comparison with Milwaukee.
the food and the service are outstanding, the best smoked fish ive ever eaten and huge portions

This is one of my favorites in Armature Works! The sangria, the Cuban, and the guava pastry empanada is AMAZING! Probably my favorite in all of Tampa! Not too mention, they just won best Cuban Sandwich at the Cuban Sandwich Festival! Hemingway's is a fantastic addition to Armature! It won't disappoint guys! This place is delicious! #byefelicia
Indoor and outdoor seating. Very casual. My husband and son had pizza. I had the Greek salad. Food was great. Salad was served in cardboard box..so that part not so appealing.

Haven't been here for a couple of years but I hope the reviews about bad service are a fluke because we are planning to come for dinner this week. Attention management: Thete is no excuse for bad service! A server does realize bad service equals bad tip, no?

Still the best-no matter how many other sushi places my friends insist upon, they don't come close to Jazmine! 

I wish they were open Sundays but I realize even perfection needs a day off : )

Awesome beer, awesome staff, awesome atmosphere.

I first stopped into Bier Brewery two days ago after learning of them on Beer Advocate. I was fortunate enough to show up when they weren't too busy and was able to chat with Ben and Jerry, two personable and engaging staff behind the bar, and a few other friendly customers. Bier's line-up tends to be on the less bitter side, which makes me extremely happy. Of the seven or eight beers I tasted, most ranged from 10-20 IBUs (International Bittering Units scale, a measurement of a beer's bitterness, with 0 as the lowest possible). Only one rated at 50 or above, and even that tasted delicious!

When I visited a couple days ago, I picked up a growler of Weizengoot, my favorite of the seven. It had an enticing deep-orange hue and looked simply fantastic. The first sip tasted faintly like Blue Moon, but the finish felt closer to Hoegaarden -- an excellent combination, yet still wonderfully unique. Since I had to share, the growler lasted less than an hour! I stopped into Bier again this afternoon -- Sunday growler sales in Indiana are a beautiful thing! -- but was mildly disappointed to discover  that Bier had already sold out of the Goot. Blast! 

Instead, I chose my second favorite -- Chamomille Wheat. Another delicious wheat beer, somehow light-tasting yet full-bodied? Yes, please. The growler is now nearly empty... and I didn't have to share this time!

While the prices ($12-14 for a fill) are just a touch high (I'm spoiled by $6-9 fills), they're well worth it for such fantastic beer -- and for supporting such a great, up-and-coming small business. They're such relative newcomers, their beer is only sold on the premises -- you can't buy it in any bars or stores, but I imagine that will quickly change once word gets out and they're able to ramp up production.

In short, I can't wait to go back to Bier. Next time, I'll be bringing two or three growlers with me!
Second time I've been here and they're closed during business their stated business hours.  Going to have to find a new place for consistency.

Great customer service and easy parking, what else can you ask for? Ohh and the food was pretty darn good! Easy going atmosphere, maybe I'm generous because the girly friend was with me, but it was a very pleasurable experience!

Great restaurant!! We were pleasantly surprised how nice it was inside. The patio bar is really nice. Food is outstanding! One of the bartenders recommended the Tuna Poke. It was so good! I got the twin lobster tails. Again, really good. I highly recommend it!! I do suggest you make reservations or you will wait awhile!

Where do I start?

First, I was reminded of an old Seinfeld episode when my "reservation" for a specific room was not honored because the hotel was sold-out.  Never mind we paid for the room in advance.  And to top it off the young lady checking us in made me feel as if the hotel's lack of availability for the room type we reserved was my fault.  Candidly, I was too tired to argue with her as we had spent nine hours driving and I should have asked some questions so this is partly my fault - obviously the young lady at the front desk did a great job of making me feel like the was my fault.

I will tell you this...Nick, the young man who helped us with our car and initial greeting outside was fantastic.  We had three experiences with him and he was amazingly helpful.  Perhaps Nick the Valet should be giving training to those in the front office and at the front desk relative to customer service.

As Jerry Seinfeld said, "...you know how to take the reservation, you just don't know how to "hold" the reservation, and that's really the most important part of the reservation, the holding."

My favorite surprise outing in NoLa. 

What's not to love about this place?  Everything, EVERYTHING, was sublime. 

The food was all delicious, the indoor and outdoor spaces were bohemian and magical, the wine selection was out of this world and the music- wow. We got a great sampling of all the goodness New Orleans has to offer. 

It's about 14 minutes from the French Quarter by car, but it is worth taking an uber or taxi out there. 

It gets busy, so have patience. It's so worth it!

First time here and it was great ! Our server was a little quiet but he was still very attentive and respectful. The food here was really good ! Totally fell in love with the salmon fish and chips !!! I've never had such a thing before and I will definitely be craving this when I head back to California. The atmosphere was chill as well. Bathrooms were pretty clean and the room was nice. I like this place.

I took our annual managers meeting there for dinner there Tuesday night.  We had reservations for the group and Spiro's was nice enough to stay open through a significant snowfall.  

We (group of 15) were pretty much the only people in the place.  SO, we got plenty of attention and service was speedy.   Everyone seemed to like the entrees.

I had the fish special which was a sea bass prepared Greek style.   It was very tasty. as well as the spinach and potatoes that were included.

I went to the Waffle House and I had a great experience. The food is prepared for u in front of your eyes. Each dishes that I have tried always has a homestyle feel to it. From that, the cleanliness is ok and the bathroom needs improvement.

I eat here a lot and the pho is pretty good and I do highly recommend the summer rolls with the peanut sauce.  It is fresh rice paper with veggies and rice noodles and not the fried version that some restaurants serve.  For beginners I would recommend the pho steak and then venture into the other meats from there or the bun or rice dish with beef.  Gosh I am getting hungry talking about it... Yes the shopping plaza next door is convenient for all kinds Asian groceries and it is at a very good price to!

Outstanding dining experience!  The service is beyond exceptional, the atmosphere is perfect, and the food is incredible.  Mr. Ronnie West made our "early Mother's Day" dinner very special.  I would highly recommend you request Mr. West if you plan to dine here.  Absolutely, the best restaurant in Metairie.

To clarify, I did not mean to imply (nor did I say) that the restaurant had no French influence or dishes.  The menu is fine, it's mainly the bread that I hope will be improved.  To me, good French baguette has a crusty, brown exterior, and an airy interior.  What I found at Ghinis, as typical in the US, was pale, without a significantly crusty exterior, and a uniform interior without the characteristic air pockets. There's really a big difference.

Rarely, and I mean rarely do I ever make a review about a "fast food restaurant". But this is needed to heed warning to my fellow Yelpers. This is the second time I've been to this KFC and the last time I attempt to give them business. One the first occasion they told me my meal would take about 20 mins to complete and all I ordered was a 8 piece with 2 sides? No courtesy offered no alternatives asked. But today tops the cake, I ordered 2 Famous Bowls, after them telling me their brand new loaded bowl which is the main reason I came they didn't have, so I settled for normal bowls. But was told they would take about 15 mins which kinda took me by HUGE surprise. And in the process of me thinking wether to wait or not the gentleman behind the mic says "well is you waiting or not??" I just pulled off, never will be back.

We used their drop off laundry service. $1 per pound. They did ok but up charge for anything other than clothes.  For example they charged $1.25 for pillow cases (seriously).  They don't use any fresheners so your clothes end up smelling a little musty.

Had a great experience here in this lovely and clean salon today. Someone recommended it to me and I'm so glad they did. I had a great pedicure with a massage and the person who did it was excellent and also a great resource for restaurants in NOLA.  The owners couldn't have been nicer and I enjoyed talking with them about us both having a French Bulldog as a pet!  I would highly recommend this place!

My husband and I have wanted to try this place since we heard about it opening! We LOVE St. Elmo's and Harry & Izzy's. And I would say I was underwhelmed by Burger Study. Don't get me wrong, the food was good. But it wasn't outstanding like I find the food at their other restaurants. We started with the beer cheese tot appetizer which was my favorite part of the meal. Our friend got the BLT salad which was also very good. We all ordered the homecoming burger which was okay. Also, the fries are not very good. I would definitely get the tater tots. We will be back but I don't think this will be a regular for us!

Came for dinner tonight. We were quickly seated and the chips and salsa are very good. We ordered and I feel the food came promptly. I had a chimichanga with carnitas, my husband had the steak burrito, and my mom had the nachos. All the food was at best a 5/10. It wasn't bad, but just nothing to write home about. The meat in each item had very little flavor. The rice was bland and the beans were basic. The service was pleasant but slow. I can't say I'd make the trip to come again.
Best place I've used to do laundry in SB. Can be crowded at times inside and in parking lot, but great pricing and convenient location, near downtown.
The cashew chicken (substitute tofu for the chicken) is to die for. I love eating here! Not a fan on the salad with the lemongrass, though. But the other dish is so good it doesn't even matter.

Me and my boyfriend went there Saturday for my birthday just to try something new and it was ok. I believe it was the day of the festival so there was a lot of outside seating and they used disposable plates and cutlery. My appetizer was delicious. I had ordered the Texas Shrimp which consisted of 6shrimp in a spicy butter sauce that came with dipping bread. The shrimp could have been seasoned but the sauce with bread is delicious. I didn't enjoy my beef tacos . It was more of steal which tasted like vinegar . I'll give it another chance in a week or two. The service was great. Didn't receive salsa and chips however.

I recently got to try this place out for their weekend Brunch.  The day we were here was their inaugural Stereo Sunday Brunch, which had a dj spinning live music as everyone partook in their usual weekend brunch activities.  The overall ambiance and crowd was pretty decent and the food offerings were not bad either.  I indulged in a Northern Bird sandwich, which was a grilled chicken breast topped with a pesto type sauce and cheese on a bun with lettuce, tomato, and onion.  I added bacon to mine to make it one of a kind.  The fries that accompanied my sandwich were cooked and seasoned perfectly.  My only gripe with the whole experience was that our server was a bit sparse and I'm not sure if it was due to the crowd of people filling the place or if she was just slow in her duties.  She asked if I needed a refill on my drink at the end of the meal after she had already cleared our groups plates.  One more thing is that the parking situation should be figured out beforehand, the owner/manager asked me to wait as we were leaving when I asked if they validate parking as they had run out of validation slips and had to send someone to Skyhouse to get more.  Overall, a great experience and I'll be back when back down in the Channelside area.

This was our favorite place while we were living in Delaware.  It has been almost 3 years since we left DE.  When we visited recently we went here for lunch.  I was craving for their fried fish and was glad to get one! My daughter loves chicken adobo.  We ordered fish sinigang.  It was a great lunch.

Iyanna Roberts was our waitress and she was fantastic.  Yaya was very knowledgeable in reference to the food and drink menu.  Yaya anticipated our every need.  She checked on us continuously throughout our meal.  She kept our drinks topped off.  I look forward to having Iyanna as our waitress again.  Iyanna is a valuable asset to the Landry's team.

Took my car in for service and the staff was professional and friendly. They called me later that afternoon to tell me the job was done & I could pick my vehicle up. They were quick which meant a lot to me.

Legit review because it's based on multiple visits/experiences - one of the best restaurants in the Tampa Bay Area, hands down. Fantastic food, high quality, perfection in balance. The spectrum of what's on the menu could only be summarized in multiple pages. Take it from a food snob - B&M is top notch!

The cook is so fun he comes out to explain the desserts and the different things. He makes the dressings, most the meats, soups, and the desserts by himself. The gooey butter cake is my favorite! This is a must try!!!

I wish this restaurant was closer to my house.  Overall, I'd say Upland is the best local brewery.  The food and service are very good here as well.  The pretzel appetizer leaves a bit to be desired.  The nachos and the fish tacos are both very good.

Try a pint of Champagne Velvet while you're there.  Thank me later. 

$2 pints on Sundays.  And if you want the place to yourself then go on a Sunday night when the Colts have a prime time game.

This place as a local feel to it. Food is legit. I ordered the flautas, chile relleno, and the tacos. Prices are cheap, food is pretty authentic. It definitely compares to food that I've had in Mexico. Unfortunately, they ran out of chicken when I was there so I didn't get a chance to try it. The place is worth checking out.

This place is definitely what Freret Street needed. A place to get a sweet treat after dinner! The owner was super nice and cheerful. I couldn't decide which flavor to get so I got two! I got a scoop of Vanilla Toffee and a scoop of Coffee. Both were super yummy. I love that it's all made there. You can for sure tell it's homemade. I love that it was fresh and sweet but not overly so. We will absolutely be back!

Coming from someone who finds asylums creepy, this got me!  There are 4 attractions of which I did 3--the house, the dungeon, and the tunnel.  The tunnel was by far the scariest.  If you go into it with an open mind then yes, you will be startled if not scared by attractions, but most of all it was just FUN.  Everything is set up very well and the employees are GREAT--they WILL grab you and follow you and get in your face, so don't go if you can't handle that.  Very intricate and detailed and exciting.  Only thing is you will most likely come back bruised from bumping into everything--some parts are very dark!  

Make sure you get the VIP pass--it's worth the money as you can skip the huge lines.  The only reason I didn't give this 5 stars is just because I didn't leave petrified--you still know they're actors once the general scare is over so it's not like you're going to run screaming from the building (although I've heard some people still have!).

This was my first time in an official "running store" and I came to PHILADELPHIA RUNNER based off of a friend's recommendation. I informed the sales associate ( his name is Ross) that I was fairly new to running and he kindly walked me through the assessment for selecting an appropriate running shoe (your arch sitting down & standing up, ...etc).
