I didn't feel pressured to buy anything I didn't need since Ross was straightforward with me. Even though I liked the first pair that I tried on he took the time to show me several brands that were a fit for me. The store has a decent selection of shoes although their prices are above average. I purchased a pair of Nike's that same day and I am very happy with them.

Was in town for a concert at Lincoln Financial.  The traffic out was horrendous we were directed out of our way through South Philly....Thank God for that!  Without that little frustration, we would've never stumbled upon this place!  Open late, nice seating outside...and the food was incredible.  Had a cheesesteak whiz with onions.  Simply great! Along with some cheese fries and a cherry coke...honestly, doesn't get much better than that.  Great place, so happy we ran into it!
Love this place!  Friendly, great food, and great prices!  Always specials going on too! Down home genuine place! Kid friendly too.

we have been at this chilis many times over the years. We did  boycott  it a few years ago due to our shitty waitress making us wait over twenty minutes to come and see what we wanted. We actually ended up walking out of Chilis..So we decided to give it any other try and we were happy with food and service till last night. We ordered well done hamburgers and they came out raw!!!!. So we had to wait another 25 minutes for our meal due to their mistake and we had to pay the full bill which was B.S. We feel they should of given us a break on the bill for their mistake and us having to wait another 25 minutes before we got to eat.. We again are boycotting this place and will probably not be returning..Our server was Monica and she did a good job.... Your cooks need to read before they just assumed we wanted raw burgers.........................

My wife and I went there on memorial day weekend to the Acme oyster bar to experience the taste of New Orleans oysters as they were highly recommended by  friends who would been inprior when I tried to order a dozen charbroiled oysters I was told that there was no one available to shuck oysters. Are you kidding me Memorial weekend and nobody available to shuck oysters Also the bartender was a complete beoutch. Totally unfriendly. I rated it one star because nothing worse was available. Want oysters DONT go to Harrahs Acme Oyster Bar. POOR

I went here for The Bounce with a girlfriend during the Summer. I overall liked the atmosphere and the music selection (Albeit Tuesday I'm in Love being more my scene...) aside from the stage-five clinger I met on the dancefloor and rude hipsters. Definitely took advantage of that 2 hour open bar.

Great customer service, they were very friendly from the moment I walked in. Quick to go order. I had the Alfredo which was really good with extra mushrooms and the Parmesan chicken. Had plenty of meat and veggies and the small was enough to fill me up before work. My only disappointment is with the chocolate chunk cookie, I didn't realize it was oatmeal. Oatmeal is okay but it's not the same as a real chocolate cookie. I wish it was labeled on the cookies oatmeal choco chunk.
The food served here is disgusting and greasy.  The Roast Pork Lo Mein was loaded with noodles and barely any pork.  The food itself was way too salty.  I will not be back here again.

My Thai ice cream WAS DELICIOUS BUT may I point out how bad of a customer service I received that Sunday I went. No customers were in there. The employee DID NOT GREET my husband and I, as if we interrupted his time from his phone. I had asked a question and he replied with a attitude as if I was annoying him. I asked because it was my first time having Thai style ice cream. Then as he handed me my ice cream I said thank you, he didn't reply or even looked up at me. So RUDE, I def regret tipping him. Will NEVER return to establishment. What sucked was we don't even live in Philly but still went since I was craving for Thai style ice cream.

I loved this restaurant, yall! I lived in Hong Kong for two years and this restaurant is a welcomed throwback to those glory years in Hong Kong. The vegetables and produce are all fresh and the cooking is authentic. I look forward to becoming a regular and getting to know the owners a bit better. Had MaPo Tofu which is an extremely Chinese dish and thought it was delicious. Sichuan chicken was great and so was the Moo Goo Gai Pan.

IHOP is the place to go for a family bunch 
There pancakes are a special recipe. There eggs and bacon make the pancakes even better! For the grown ups you have a sissy mix of red peppers, potatoes, bacon, and a toasted piece of bread 

Go with your family to ihop!!!

I just love Skyline Chili. Granted, I always get the worst Heartburn ever after, but it is so worth it! I love the Coney Bowl which is simply their chili with hotdogs and cheese in it. Their five ways are always delicious. The seating is very "no fuss." You pick a spot and they come over to you. The food comes out quick as the chili is already made.

I can't say enough how awesome Shift Insurance was!

Let's face it, shopping for auto insurance isn't easy, nor is it cheap. Most of the time, you have to suck it up and ask for help, and reliable help on top of that, to make sure that all of your basic needs are covered. 

All it took was one phone call, I didn't expect it to be that quick and so easy. I was helped by Raphael. He really listened to what I had to say and basically set out a plan that worked best for me. Great customer service, hands down. 

I made up my mind after speaking to Raphael because he knew what he was talking about. I wasn't dealing with someone who just googled "insurance" and blurted out nonsense to me. He explained it to me in a way that I could understand --- AND maybe, just maybe, it totally helped that I was quoted the lowest price too!

All around, it was a relieving and friendly experience. Everything was covered. No pun intended. Just give them a call. Like, now.

Great wine bar!  They have an awesome cheese, beer and wine menu.  Service was fantastic and intimate ambiance.  Our waitress was super helpful in suggesting things to try.  The Russian River beer = killer.  We nibbled on creamy goat cheese while sipping glasses of crisp white wine.  Nice little Saturday.
It was ok. Not worth $10 for adults and $3 for kids. Some of the statues were falling apart. They were all behind glass windows. Definately just a one time visit for me.

I recently made reservations for a night out with a friend. I haven't stopped raving since! As R2L is on the 37th floor, our table gave us the absolute most breathtaking view of the city. The drinks were awesome, the food was phenomenal and the service was beyond outstanding. 

The atmosphere was chic, and the attentiveness of the staff was seriously refreshing. A girls night out dinner like that left me feeling completely satisfied and so, so full. I'd recommend it to just about anyone.

I came here a little after my birthday to take advantage of their 50% off one item birthday promo. Although I was a few days late, the sales associate on the phone gracefully stated they will still allow me to use my birthday discount. I came in later that day and a different lady assisted me in finding a necklace. She seemed to be in a slightly irritated mood but was definitely putting effort into helping me find something.  I worked retail for about 5 years so I have reservations about harshly judging a place/person based on a 5 minute interaction, but in efforts to provide full-disclosure of my experience, there was definitely a sense of some snootiness in the store, which is my ultimate retail pet peeve. The store was also organized in an appealing, but disorienting manner as like things are not displayed together so if I liked a style I had to go around each part of the store to find different color options; they pretty much have every style in every color except for certain exclusive styles from the new collection. This made the experience a little overwhelming and definitely makes you rely on the employees for guidance. Overall, it was a good experience and i love my necklace! Can't beat half off:).
My personal favorite restaurant. Nice atmosphere and the staff are kind and resemble intelligent human beings as well. They have a little store in the restaurant too if youre a bumpkin.

Not sure what I can say about this place that hasn't already been said in a few hundred 5 star reviews so I'll just tell two stories:

1.  My first visit to Fed Nuts was last year.  I was talking to one of the owners outside who is a friend of mine.  I was hungry and chicken sounded perfect.  I walked in and ordered a spicy chicken from the super awesome Blake F.... this is how it went down

I pushed open the screen door and my senses were overloaded in fried goodness. My life seemed rather dull and lusterless before inhaling the medley of donuts and chicken.  A familiar face was at the counter and beaming her winning smile.  

"Hey buddy, good to see you!" I said.
"Hey there, welcome!" she replied.
I could barely contain my hunger at this point. If I wouldn't look insane for licking the sweet air, I would have.
"Can I get the spicy chicken?" I said.  God knows I love everything spicy and fortunately, luck was on my side.
"You bet, 1 spicy" she commanded.

I paid and waited for my chicken.  As I was admiring the simple establishment that has nailed the adage, "Do a few things VERY well instead of a lot of things crappily," an old timer walked up and adjusted his worn cover.  He ordered chicken but his fortune was not as mine.

"Sorry, we just ran out, he got the last one."  
The seasoned Philadelphian turned to me with a mired glare that said "you gotta be shittin me."  I really wondered if he would wait idly in on a wooden stool and leap for the box of chicken as it offered to me, only to run out the door with a super villain cackle.  Didn't happen though, he left with a donut and I ate the chicken.

2. I ran an experiment where I brought them in to work and let a bunch of people try them.  Invariably, every person would take a bite and say, "This is like the best donut I've ever had."

Cons:  The biggest disappointment was the service.  Although I initially loved the decor and feel of the space, this quickly dissipated due to the mediocre service.  The waiter wasn't as polished as I'd have expected, could have been in an Applebees or any other average chain.  It was a slow Monday night, all the more reason I was baffled by the service.  No explanation of the menu layout or small plate style of dishes. When asked for guidance on how many dishes we should start out with for a group of our size, we were given an ambivalent answer. Also took forever to get our check at the end of the meal. 


Pros: Upon first entering, felt very welcomed by the colorful glass decor and natural light (the walls were head to toe windows).  The corned beef sliders were excellent.  Ceviche lettuce wraps were also very good.

Dined al fresco this Sunday afternoon. Our server greeted us and we were given a dinner menu at 2pm. Not what we were looking for, but we went with it. We started with the spaghetti squash soup which was outstanding, and a burger and a pasta dish for our main entree. Both entrees were very good, though very overpriced. Our server, Sofia, was very accommodating and checked on us throughout the meal. Nice place, but I was expecting just a little bit more.

This review is for their happy hour. Three dollar draft beer that includes Dragoon IPA is awesome.  The food is going to have good ingredients and flavor. The happy hour apps are inexpensive and small.  

Service was ok. 

There was a foul odor pretty much the whole time.

And my pita bread was old and very tough. Sorry,  that is unacceptable for a place with pita in the name.

Great service. I came here for the first time for a grooming visit for my maltipoo. Vicki did a wonderful job. She really listened to me and took out pictures to make sure it was the cut I wanted. Everyone was super nice and my dog looks great. Glad I found them.

Excellent beer selection, You can find almost any type of beer that you fancy, However, it is a little bit pricey, If you can find a beer somewhere else, there is a good chance it will be much cheaper. 

Every time I go there, I become overwhelmed by the selection and will end up spending a lot of money on beer (No regret)

Laura has been doing my hair for years. I've tried other stylists in times when I couldn't make an appointment but I've always come back to Laura. She has created a custom cut and color for me and I always get compliments on it everywhere. She KNOWS hair and cuts very well and will give her honest and professional opinion when it comes to a different style. Whenever I ask about a particular style she will let me know how to look my best.

She runs a great, inviting business. Recently she has redecorated the salon and give nit a much more open and inviting feel. 

Prices are very reasonable for the amazing service and finished look. She also sells Aveda make up and skin products.

The Homewood Suites across the street doesn't have a full restaurant, but luckily, the Hilton Garden Inn across the street does, and they've worked it out so that Homewood guests can order room service from Coast. I took advantage the one night that the Homewood didn't have free dinner, and I'm glad I did.

It took me a while to decide what to order, because several of the menu items looked amazing. I eventually decided on a salad and a half pizza. Yes, they sell half pizzas, which is the best idea ever. More pizza places should do this. Mostly so I don't order a whole one and ending up eating the entire thing. But that's beside the point.

I had the house salad, described on the menu as iced greens, roasted peppers, pine nuts, red onion, smoked bacon and sweet pepper vinaigrette. The iced greens were very heavy on the dandelion greens, which I can't stand. So that made me a little sad. But everything else about the salad was excellent. The pepper vinaigrette was perfect - similar to a catalina or french dressing but a little thicker and a little sweeter. The pine nuts just added a little something different. I would have loved to have had more greens - if I get the chance to order it again, I may ask for it on spinach instead.

The half pizza was probably about a 10 or 12 inch pizza - not big slices, but not tiny. The crust was crisp, and the sauce was very tasty. All in all, a mighty tasty pizza, but nothing super special or different about it. It was pretty much what I was hoping for.

Apparently the entire menu is that good - I got back one night and there were a few cops hanging out that apparently come into the Homewood and order dinner from Coast on a regular basis. Definitely better food than I've experienced in the past in hotels of a Hilton Garden Inn type - more along the lines of what I would have expected at a regular Hilton. And that's a good thing, as far as I'm concerned.

Enjoyed a wonderful lunch on the patio with a great glass of Prosecco.
Tantalizing menu selection. I liked the wood grilled tuna and vegetables, which were excellent, although the salad was just so-so. I would have paid extra for a fresh, farmers market herb salad. My husband liked his open faced roast beef melt. 
The waitress was a little prissy, but the host and busser were friendly. So, all-in-all we will definitely return.
Who doesn't like Ted Drewes? If you visit STL, then this is a must-have treat.
This was the best coffee around the French Quarter that I could find.  A nice place to sit to take a break from the crowds.
Very good food and plenty of it. The bathroom is clean and hot water is sink which means to me it is sanitary. Value is very high, lamb is the best I have had in years!

Came here on a Saturday night with my girlfriend for dinner. Made reservations but still had to wait about 10 minutes before we were seated. The place is pretty small and was very chilly. BYOB was nice. Ordered the duck fries for an appetizer and they were great. For an entree I got the general tso's wings. The sauce was delicious but the wings were just alright. Would have preferred them a little crispier. Got strawberry cheesecake for dessert and my girlfriend and I both agreed it was the best we've ever had. Service was prompt and friendly.

We enjoyed the boba tea, which seemed to have met the industry standard. The banh mi was also pretty tasty.  What we enjoyed most about this particular restaurant were the service and the setting.  We will probably return in the near future.

Batter'd & Fried was the way we went. Nice casual atmosphere, friendly staff.  Our first time, we decided to try the favorite icon's suggested on the menu. My favorite was the fried scallops. Other guest in our group enjoyed Chef Andy's Fish & Chips, & Seattle Fish & Chips. The fried oysters were good but once again I experience sand in a few of my bites. The French fries were not good, but the Onion rings were very good!!. We wanted to try the Boston Cream pie but they ran out. We will have to return to try the Sushi. When in East Nashville would suggest you check out this family friendly spot. Parking can be a challenge but worth the experience.

A completely ordinary breakfast and an outrageously long wait, That's what you get at the famous PP.

A good breakfast, tasty and well prepared. But NOT special by any means. What you end up waiting an hour for is the name, and the reputation. You can get as good or better breakfast at lots of places in town without the outrageous wait standing out on the street. 

Pancakes were 100% average. Been eating flapjacks for over 50 years, and these are pretty ordinary.

Servers were very friendly, and the atmosphere is fun. A good family place if your family doesn't mind standing in the street for an hour waiting to be seated.

This so far is my favorite place to eat seafood and/or sushi in East Nashville.  It's cool to find a Boston themed place that serves amazing fish and chips as well as great sushi.  I don't think I've ever encountered anything quite like it.  

I love their fried pickled jalapenos, but they're a lot on the taste buds so be wary if spicy isn't your thing.  Their coconut shrimp and fried oyster  sandwich are some of my favorites.  They have some unique sushi rolls that are surprisingly delicious, which is one thing you wouldn't automatically think would be found in a fried seafood joint.  

They have an outdoor patio which is always a plus, but they're parking lot is teeny tiny and sometimes you have to walk a bit to get there.  The one thing I find lacking about this place is their draft beer selection.  I wish they had more to choose from the best thing really is Sam Adams, which although fitting is not always the beverage I'm craving.  Their cocktails also tend to be on the pricey side, so if you're a liquor drinker on a budget prepare to limit your intake.

I called 3 weeks before my membership renewal to add my son.  No problem, she said.  Card on the way, she said.  Now it is 3 days after I paid my membership, including adding my son....NO card.  I called yesterday, I'll email a temp card, she said.....NO email.  Wow.  I'm sure glad the dispatcher works better than customer service (with no customer service).

Not family friendly at all. Went to Grace and Pats tonight, at 5:00, with my 16 mo old son, but we were told upon arrival that they had no high chairs or booster seats and no plans to get any. For a pizza place in east passyunk, a neighborhood full of families, this was simply unacceptable. We won't be back to a business that does not welcome family dining.
Great service! They were quick, friendly, and thoroughly explained everything while installing our infant car seat.

So great - I almost gave 5* but the prawns were so big I was uncertain of how to eat them without making a mess.  Beautiful space and service - although TV(s) were showing NFL football playoffs.  Affected the ambiance a tad.  Go Nina Go!

I don't need to eat Gluten free. But I'm always up for sweets. So yesterday, I popped in (because it's right next to the Wine and Spirit's Store, HELLO!!) 
It's a very small bakery. But good things come in small packages (seriously, don't believe the hype about the bigger the better!). I tried the peanut butter delight. OMG. It tastes just like a Tastykake Candycake. It was sooo good, I told the cashier in the wine store about it (he knew and agreed). 
I also tried the crème filled cake donut. OMG. It tasted just like a powered donut with rich cream filling. So good! The kiffles (strawberry, raspberry, apricot) were just ok for me. I do like the kiffles at Wegman's a bit better. 
Now, remember, I am not 'gluten' free - but for me, the doughnut and peanut butter delights were superior and/or just as good as ANY I've had. 
I'm excited to go back and try everything else! 
They had samples out (which is what made me buy the peanut butter delight). I don't know if they do regularly, but it never hurts to pop in a see. 
I work in a commercial bakery and Happy Mixer's are at times, less expensive than the store I work for. Some things are more (cookies are 16.95 a pound, at my place they are 10.99 - but Kiffles are 15.99 per pound). 
For homemade and being a "specialty" (ie: Gluten Free) - I think these prices are actually cheap (but please don't raise them!) If this shop was in say...Chestnut Hill, you can bet the 2.95 dollar muffins would be 5.00. 
Don't let the "Gluten Free" stop you from considering a visit to this "sweet" bakery! 
Love it!!!
Went to this place every day when I was in Nashville for the week. Love this place! The staff was so nice and helpful. Smoothies and food always satisfied my healthy cravings :)

Fabulous ambiance 
Fabulous food 
Fabulous service w Matt
Scallop dish really terrific and worth the drive there. The steak frite was better than it could be anywhere else. 
This restaurant was excellent

I really enjoy this place, time after time. It's chill and relaxed, the drinks are delicious, and the bartenders are talented. I love the couches and funky seats. They create a communal environment for a decently large group of 5-6. The menu rotates enough that you get to try a variety of drinks. And they're never so crazy busy and crowded that you feel like you're at one of those other places that I just won't mention. :) A great place for drinks with a date or a group of friends. Can't say enough good things about this place!

I'll cut to the chase: In Riva may be one of the best restaurants in Philly that you've never heard of. I must have gone past it tens of times while driving down Kelly Drive, but I never thought to look up at the kind of nondescript, set-back building and realize it was actually a restaurant. We only tried In Riva after my brother-in-law raved about it, so we thought we'd give it a try with another couple. It was one of the best dinners out we had a long time.

In Riva's website says it specializes in Neopolitan-style wood-fired pizza and antipasti, which isn't entirely accurate because all their courses are equally delicious. I can't remember exactly what we ordered but it included some salumi and formaggi, pea soup, pork ribs, charred octopus, a trio of pastas and a mushroom and zucchini pizza. Everything was delectable. My favorite was the agnolotti with pea, shallot and truffle. It was the best pasta I've had in Philly (my favorite pasta is at L'Artusi in NY), though I hear Vetri's pasta is amazing. 

What makes In Riva so wonderful is that it is so unassuming. It has a casual, dark wood, industrial-feel interior that doesn't ring of pretense, yet the food rivals any of the best-known, heralded nouveau cuisine restaurants in Philly. In fact, the two meals I've had at In Riva have knocked the socks off the past two meals I had at Amada, which used to be my favorite Philly restaurant.

I just noticed Andrew B's negative review and understand that he thinks In Riva may be overpriced. I think because In Riva looks so casual, one would expect the price point to also be casual. I agree the pasta serving size could be bigger. I paid $11 for the agnolotti dish that I ate in a few bites and could have easily downed another order. But, truth be told, we shouldn't eat that much. The price reflects the quality, not quantity, of food.

Philadelphia Magazine recently published the top 50 restaurants in Philly issue, and I eagerly looked for In Riva's name to be listed. Not this year, but hopefully next. It's not to be missed.
A must if you are in or near St. Pete Beach.  I am a frequent visitor and love the food and coffees here.   An unexpected delight in a 'strip mall'.

There has been many times I have received tickets because different meters do not accept coins on Girard Ave. But one occurrence really made me wonder what is the purpose of PPA when the city does not receive revenues from PPA? I came out and saw a PPA person writing a ticket for my car. Looked at the meter and it had 38 mins still left. I asked the PPA guy why I was getting a ticket; he said "oh, my bat?" Had I not come out and checked on how much time I had left the ticket would not be fight-able. He removed the ticket after he clearly saw the time still left in the meter.

Meters in this area is always broken, takes a coin here and there or full. When contacting PPA or flagging down a PPA agent they state move your car. Phone operators will not give you back a quarter or fifty cents but rather give you a quick ticket for broken meters.

PPA or the city needs to offer 2 hour free parking to revitalize the 2600 -2900 blocks of Girard Ave. This area is clearly a poorer area with many struggling business to make ends meat. If Fairmount ave can offer free 2 hour parking, Girard ave should be able to offer the same.

Convenient walk from my hotel near the arch. I had dinner at the bar and great conversation with employees, bartenders and customers. 
I ordered the beef taco salad. It was yummy! Just make sure you have a healthy appetite or sharing it because this salad was huge!
Great service, great food. 
The next time I visit St. Louis I will pop in for a bite to eat with friendly folks!

A group of Yelpers and I were all appalled at the level of service we received at this establishment. From the start this hovel of mediocrity fell on its face by not seating us at all; the hostess was not even at the door. We seated ourselves. Once we were in, the bar-tending waitress, who seemed to be running the show upstairs, took our drink orders, all the while giving off the aura of disdain and employment-regret that could sear hair off.

We had to wait around for over 30 min for someone to take our actual orders and after I took it upon myself to express to the waitress that were getting antsy. The forceful OK and stare I got back did tick me off but I decided I wouldn't make a huge deal of it. I gave her a well-timed "Alright, [pause] Thank You" until she broke eye contact and went back to our table. Not a pleasant experience. Even after all of this, someone was sent to "confirm" our orders 10 min later.

When we finally received the food it didn't impress me terribly. The Fish and Chips plate was plentiful but the fish itself was somewhat greasy and bland. However, the Humus platter was huge and pretty darn tasty (but nothing that can't be found elsewhere). Decent prices though.

The dcor of this place was as mediocre as was everything else about it. Wooden booths and low lighting define this place, as well as ever other pub everywhere else; the only distinction being the occasional framed picture of a sheep.

(I must admit I did not get to see much of the lower floor and dined upstairs)

The upstairs had large windows that may open to take in some night air - but they were closed when we were there. 
My advice, if you're in the neighborhood go to Monk's just around the corner. Price point may differ but hell, so does quality!
This place is cute as can be and very historic but the food was awful. I did not experience fresh or quality food and neither did my lunch companion.

Their lunch special really is a good value. For $10 today I was served a very nice salad, fried fish, rice & beans, hush puppies and and ice tea. I've easily spent more than that any other day of the week for a worse lunch. 

I'm not sure... but I think if you come at lunch, you eat the lunch plate... you don't get a choice of anything else. Or at least the server didn't offer anything else. 

The space has been redone but is still a little dilapidated. The ceiling was all warped. I don't know why this bothered me but I couldn't stop looking at it. And our table was wobbly. I hate that. Freaking annoying. 

The food was good... I really liked the salad. The fish was average. Nothing special. The hush puppies tasted homemade... like something grandma would have cooked. Beans and rice were good. I liked that the beans had big chunks of ham in it. The tea was weird. It tasted like it had tobacco in it. Tea shouldn't make me feel like I need to brush my teeth. 

I'm glad I visited. Huge props for good, well prepared food at $10. And I was in and out at lunchtime within 40 minutes.  I'll be back to try other items.

Came here for the first time tonight. 

Beer is amazing. I was super impressed with their selection and we ended up having the Enhanced Psychic Damage and the Half The Gentlemen as well. 

I was super excited for all the vegetarian and vegan options they had! We had the mushroom appetizer which was DELICIOUS and I had the banh mi wrap. The wrap is gigantic (as in two people could split it!) and it was very tasty. I would like to see a little more tofu on it next time but overall it was delicious. My husband had the fish tacos and he thought they were great. Comes with two and no side (so if you're hungry order a side--or eat the rest of someone's banh mi wrap :)) 

We were told it'd be 45 mins for a table for two (Saturday at 7:00) but was only 15 mins and that was a nice surprise. 

Highly recommend!! I can't wait to try he Brew Café!

We discovered this Laotian restaurant through yelp while visiting our family so we decided to give it a try. The look of the restaurant from outside was deceiving where we almost left after we arrived because of the location, parking situation, and my fear of not being used to the type of surroundings. When we walked in we were surprised by how warm, cozy, clean, filled with customers, and we were greeted and seated promptly. It didn't take long for us to get our food and the food was very $reasonable. We ordered the sticky rice, chicken larb, papaya salad, beef jerky, stick rice mango dessert and all we delicious. We enjoyed all but probably will not order the sticky rice mango dessert again for $8 although we didn't mind paying for it considering the cost of how much it would have taken for them to make it but it was just a little too watering for us. We would definitely do it again next time we visit Philadelphia since we don't have any Laotian restaurants in Tampa area. I would highly recommend this place for anyone who likes to try authentic Laotian food that cannot be found from Thai restaurants. This was the first Laotian restaurant we have ever been to and we truly enjoyed the Laotian unique food experience! 
p.s BYOB is a plus..

I actually thought the food was good. The grouper sandwich came on a pretzel roll. It was a really cool combination of flavors.

The portions were small - which I like so I don't over eat. But I did think it was over priced for the amount of food you got.

The service was good - and they have a great drink selection.
Pancakes were great. The syrup is especially good. Seemed to have a hint of rum flavor. Yum. The orange walnut pancakes were also very good.

Great location on Santa Claus Lane, with easy off/on to CA 101. Prices are a bit higher than most because of the location, but the portions were plenty. Homemade meatballs, sauces and salad dressings hit the spot when looking for an easy place to grab a bite of good Italian fare. Sisters that run the restaurant are very nice, warm and inviting. No frills, just good food!

I went for dinner last night with family. We were seated promptly but it took over 5 minutes for our waitress to say hi and take our drink order. She always seemed in a hurry to talk to us. The place seemed understaffed. I ordered the filet mignon. It was cooked perfectly (medium was actually pink). The sides were unassuming. A side of broccoli that I didn't think was seasoned in any way. And some crispy overcooked potato wedges (slightly spicy). Presentation was poor and it looked like any amateur could have done that. I give it the three stars based on the meat alone, otherwise would have been lower.
Always great food and service.  One of my favs
Fabulous food, delicious and creative.  One of the best restaurants in Indianapolis.  I had the special, Fanesca, a creamy EcuadorIan stew with cod.  Mouth-wateringly delicious!

Can we be serious for a moment?
The Greek pizza this place whips up is the bomb.com.  I've never had a pizza that wasn't homemade taste so good.  I love the fact that I can watch them put it together, and I also love that I can ask for more feta if I want it, (and who doesn't?!)  Kudo's to Papa Murphy's for preparing my delicious din-din to cook at my convenience.

Had a great time with my group at Margaritaville! Fun for everyone - drinks and food to serve all tastes and ages. Thank you so much Valerie for your amazing service and tips. Yum! 

Edit: 
We were told they let lunch goers into the Friday show but this is not true. Just a heads up before you plan to dine before the show... better to just wait in line and dine upstairs at 2 when they open it up

I had high hopes for Bub's but was very disappointed. I run by it most weekends on the Monon Trail and it always smells delicious. I was told by my dining mates I shouldn't be surprised by the prices because it's in Carmel, but I was. It's way overpriced, and everything is ala' cart. I think a an omelet can at least come with some toast or something included.

That being said, the elk sausage is delicious, as are their pancakes. The omelet seemed a bit buttery or greasy (I could see the oil dripping from whatever the lubricant was) which made it tasty, but a lot less healthy. The pancakes were thick and textured and delicious, though overpriced. I'm sure it had some whole wheat in it. 

But when I spend $15 on an omelet, coffee, and a single pancake, I feel gypped. I'd go to the Original Pancake House every time over this place.

So I go to this cafe a lot and I gotta say that lately I've been really disappointed with their kale salad. I usually get the same thing (pesto grilled cheese). It's a go-to for me. And I always get a side of the kale salad but the last 4 times, it's been prepared differently and it always looks like it should've been thrown out four days ago. The grilled cheese is always on point but I'm gonna have to switch to a different side because I'm convinced this kale salad is not being taken care of.

I don't generally leave reviews. But I'm quite unhappy about this place. Our group of fourteen consisted of three children: 3, 5 and 7. When we received the check, they had charged full price for the 7 year old and 16 for each of the children.  I would highly recommend this change. I do not believe any child 7 years of age is capable of eating like an adult. 

Besides that, the food was mediocre for the price. The meat for the BBQ was bland.

Great food.. Sushi is good, fave dessert here is the double crem brûlée. Ambiance nice for a date night.  Negatives.. It can be tight depending where you're seated. And if don't make a reservation, be sure to plan for a long wait time.

All I can say is.......wow! I came here because my friend told me how good the tacos were and I finally dived in and gave it a try. We pulled up and I was shocked of how small the building was. I am always looking for some type of seating or outdoor seating but this is a grab a taco and leave type of establishment. 

We walked in and immediately I knew 2 people in there lol. I was thinking oh this food must be good!!! I ordered the chicken, shrimp, and steak taco and when I say it was good... honey..... it was good lol! The tacos were seasoned well and the meat was tender. It was just perfect! 

Be careful with the sauces they throw in the bag. It is super spicy and I am not a fan of that. I love the limes and cucumbers that they give us with the tacos too. Very fresh and yummy! 

The quesadilla was EXCELLENT! Def will be back.
Been there twice within two days my nails come off then my daughter just went there last  month and hers came off with in a week and it was a waste of money

Many people told me it was a must to visit El Camino Real, and I have to agree that the food is pretty amazing.

We opted to get the all-you-can eat chips and salsa, which costs $1 per person.  (I think this should just be free as most Mexican places do.)  The chips came with a chunky red pico de gallo and a salsa verde, both were tasty.  I also had a pina colada BF opted for a beer from the draft selection.  My cocktail was well-spiked and I got a nice buzz from it, but didn't overwhelm the yummy pineapple and coconut.

I ordered the Smoked chicken burrito which had bacon, plantains and chipotle crema.  BF got the shrimp, smoked garlic/onion, crispy chicken skin & jalapeno burrito.  Our server asked if we wanted them as a platter with rice and beans.  FOR FIVE DOLLARS EXTRA.  For real??  Are these magic beans???  No thanks.  The plate came with a shredded red cabbage and radish salad which was untouched on both of our plates.  How bout leave off that cabbage nonsense and just give us rice and beans?  The burrito was not your typical gargantuan size, (ala Cantina or most Mexican spots) but instead two thinner burritos... more like rolled tacos.  This was nice for sharing, we each got to try one half and were pretty full.  I actually enjoyed the shrimp one better, the crispy chicken skin was a nice complement to the smoky flavors.  A tad spicy for this spice-wuss but I went for it anyway because the flavors were so nice.

Service was great, I'll probably be back again.  I also want to try the barbecue selections.

The Baring address is out-of-date -- they are now at Sparks BL and Los Altos.

There's a trick that I learned when I was doing TV news "secret reviews" . . .my first visit, I go looking a bit scruffy (in this case, after a day working on my experimental airplane), tell them I'm only drinking water (no ups, no extras) and give them the chance to charge me more than they might have for the meal.  Here, I found a 2-enchilada combination plate which interested me, then flipped over to add a taco from the a la carte menu.

The waiter seemed more than willing to let me pay too much, but only after telling me that I could save a couple of bucks by ordering the tamale / enchilada / taco combination, and he would have them give me two enchiladas.  My water glass was never empty, but he didn't smother me with service the way waitstaff will if they are trying to get you to buy dessert, etc.  One star for the service.

The restaurant was clean, comfortable, and not overly noisy.  One star.

The food was . . .okay.  There was nothing to stand out one way or the other.  It arrived on a plate too hot to touch -- just as hot food should -- and there was no sign of skimping.  The taste was good, texture good, the price was right (I ate alone for about 11 bucks).  Two stars.

All in all, if I'm hungry for Mexican food when I'm in this area, I'm likely to stop in here, but I'm not going to pass by anywhere else that I know to get here.
Excellent Cuban sandwiches! Owner works the  punter and is very friendly. Totally authentic food, would be a return customer if I lived nearby.

Taco Tuesdays is my jam! The line type serving is a lot o like chipotle, but the tacos are better. I believe I got the tacos with all of the dressings on top. Highly recommend if you want to get a quick bite to eat downtown. There isn't a lot of seating when it gets super busy, however if you come at a non peak time you won't have any issues. 

Unlike a few other taco shops you can take a handful of chips from a heated machine, which is a nice touch. Choose your own salsa and refill your own drinks. You can also get beer here which is a nice touch when you're having a quick taco any day of the week. 

The atmosphere is pretty much expected for a taco place, and the price is great for what you get. I've only been here once, but recommend if you're in the area and need a quick bite to eat.
I was disappointed with the cheesesteak; the meat was quite bland and dry. Besides the cheesesteak, they do have a wide selection of other food items- which I will try in the future

Pretty much everything I look for in a place that services my car:  fast, friendly, inexpensive & honest...not necessarily in that order.  $30 for an oil change, and I was in and out in 30 minutes on the dot (& I was a walk-in).  A little heads-up:  they keep their prices so low, that if you must pay by card, they will charge you the 3% that the bank charges them for using the card.  If you can pay cash, you will save the 3%.

I jokingly call this place Oh So Mediocre - but really it is pretty good.  The Korean lady who runs the place is very, very nice and always asks about my daughter.  The hot & cold food bar is fairly clean with a wide variety of choices, some of which are actually healthy.  (Be careful - many of the hot foods are loaded with oil/fat).

If you really want something good here, though - skip the "pig bar" and head to the back for a fresh grilled turkey burger.  You'll have to be prepared to wait several long minutes - but it is worth it.  Cheap and tasty - not at all dry.  I got my T-burger with Ketchup, tomato and lettuce.  3.75.

What a deal.
Oh So Good.

Worst sushi. Worst service. Oh and they wouldn't take into consideration one of my family members disorders!!! They wouldn't let him take home his food which he only took 5 bites of and was charged the all you can eat price. Ridiculous won't be going back.
It is the world's largest children's museum. But I wouldn't say it's just for children. Everyone can have fun there. Lots to do, and lots of fun.

I went to eat at this so called great diner the food was disgusting plus we ordered takeout food it was all wrong the order plus I complained and they told me well what u want me to do very rude workers I will never go to eat there again u will not get a vote from me for 2018 worst place to eat tell ur workers to treat there customers with dignity and respect worst 2018 diner

After 13 back surgeries in this hospital I've gotten to know the nursing team pretty well. On an 8 year journey at this point it's fair to say I've returned for far too many procedures for my back but i just love them so much I'll keep coming back again and again. The nurses on the surgery floor, used to be 2 more it's 3, are top notch. My friends on the 5th floor short procedure unit are wonderful as well. 

I think i get some pity bcuz I'm a frequent flyer but they always make sure I'm comfortable, warm enough, and have everything i need before they sneak me away and stick me with needles! Mercy in the procedure room is always ready with some fun back and forth banter. 

It makes me sad when the familiar faces of the old staff is moved to different departments but there is always joy in meeting new nurses to the floor and tormenting them with I'll be back :) But there is always the chance i run into an oldie but goodie nurse in the hallways like Leslie. She was and I'm sure still is the best, from pre-op to SPU.

And the other half of the time i have to go to Voorhees but they have a wonderful staff over there too.

I stopped in here after reading multiple reviews about how great it was. My dad was in the mood for chicken and I remembered this place, so I headed over.

I was here on a Sunday afternoon and the place was packed. I'm talking line out the door, people inside waiting on their order packed. I took this as a good sign, so I hopped in line and got ready to order at the window. I got the 14 piece chicken combo which comes with fries and a salad. It was a little over $10 which was perfect because there's a $10 minimum on cards. After you order they give you a number and you sit and wait. On this day the wait was about 15 minutes, because of the crowd, but that wasn't a problem. When my number was called I got my food and I was on my way.

The chicken itself is tasty and really generous. There was an even mix of wings and legs and I enjoyed it. The fries weren't anything spectacular and the salad was just lettuce, so next time I might skip the combo and get the 14 piece for $8 deal. While Golden Wings isn't on the level of Popeyes, you can't beat the price and the food is enjoyable. I'll be back.

Loved this restaurant.  Looking for local amazing flavors. Started off with cocktails which were unique. Had the French 8132. Great. Appetizers had butternut squash panzanella salad with burrata, Louisiana crab, 
And tuna. 3 delicious choices.  For dinner had the pork belly with Vietnamese noodles, steak frites and pan-fried snapper. You can't go wrong with any of these choices.  Staff was incredible and if you can't tell we had a wonderful evening!

Well for starters, I enjoyed breakfast there for the first time! Clean! Inside, outside, & the restrooms were clean. I like the decor, it was like a tropical scenery. For breakfast had shrimp and grits, with a waffle. I had the seafood omelette, with 2 pancakes. It was like homemade pancakes. The sweet tea and orange juice were so good. The service was quick and hot! Our food and service was awesome! I gave it 4 stars bc the shrimp and eggs just don't go together. To me those 2 things are not compatible. But I would recommend this place for breakfast. Now I would like to come here when it's warm outside & for dinner. There is outside seating, with a pond view.

I can't say enough about this place the food is phenomenal! Paulie is from Chicago the best hot dogs and Italian beefs in Tampa! Don't judge a book by its cover at this place doesn't look like much from the outside but you won't get better true Chicago food anywhere else in Tampa. Paulie the owner treats you like family from the very first visit.

If you're in Reno you must eat at Roundabout Grill. My husband and I went for a weekday breakfast and we loved it. Chef Walt knows what he is doing!  We had excellent service from Kelly. She is very attentive and kind!  We ordered the Apricot Granola Pancakes and Colin's Scramble. Pancakes came with butter, syrup, and fresh strawberry purée. Plus we both had Lattes. Overall this exceeded our expectations by a long shot. We were told about their weekend brunch - sounds fabulous. Go to the Roundabout Grill!!!!

Absolutely fabulous!!! You can't go wrong with anything on the menu. 

Our dinner party of 8 arrived Tuesday night for dinner. We we're greeted immediately by the owners. While our online reservation wasn't received they quickly assembled tables to accommodate our party.  The decor is elegant and the ambiance was superb. The reggae inspired music playing in the background really set the mood. From the moment we walked it we began to relax following a very long work day.

I can't say enough about the owners. They were so attentive, pleasant, warm and welcoming. All the food is prepared fresh and they communicate the preparation time of the various entrees ahead of time. 

Now for the food....AMAZING! The mango salsa was great. I had the islands of Caribbean. It was so delicious. I had goat for the very first time, it was so tender and flavorful. The jerk chicken is on point! Everyone was extremely pleased with their dinner. So pleased that a sampling of dessert was a must. We shared the chocolate cake, rum cake, cheesecake, and coconut cake. All were oh so good, though the rum cake was my absolute favorite.   

I highly recommend. Next time I'm in Tampa I will be back.

This little gem is tucked away in Legends Park on Bourbon Street. It's completely passed over by partygoers, and truly a great place to catch your breath. The full bar has reasonable prices, and the pastries are excellent!

A word about the Beignets:

Yes, they are better than Cafe Du Monde's. Bigger, for starters, and more doughy. They deliver them to your table hot and let you enjoy them while listening to live jazz in the courtyard amidst string lights. The only drawback? The tables are gridded, so you will get powdered sugar everywhere! In the future, I will pass on Cafe Du Monde and only go here!

the staff is incredibly attentive.. almost ninja like.. I'd be drinking my water.. and put the glass down.. almost immediately it was refilled.. like out of the blue.. They were just very nice..

The tableside guac was delish.. I love how you can decide how much of certain items or if at all would be put... fresh guacamole holds a special place in my heart, especially when accompanied by house made chips. 

I also ordered the fundido.. it was delicious.. very flavorful.. 
My friend got the sopa azteca, and the chicken and rice she liked the soup, although she did complain that because the cheese was cubed, she couldn't taste it in every bite. Despite that she enjoyed it. She ordered the chicken and rice and really enjoyed everything except the lime mayo.. 

With such fresh ingredients, it's hard to go wrong.
Not a half bad neighborhood bar. The patio was pretty nice, drinks were just alright though. Tables were hard to come by.

Enjoyed my small cup of soup of the day: Italian wedding soup which I paired with the small pear and blue cheese salad.  The salad had lots of blue cheese, pears were crunchy and not overly ripe, and candied walnuts for more texture ( and taste). Wonderful salad and so reasonable.  We sat outside admiring the greens.

Firehouse Sub's is a chain, so this location is much like every other store. Place your order at the counter, pay, and wait for your sandwich to be made and your name called out. While waiting you can grab a seat at a table and get your beverage, there is a Coca-Cola Freestyle machine here so can customize your soda to fit your personality. 

The food here is pretty good, a step up from Subway. The sandwiches are served on steamed bread. I usually prefer the Smokehouse Beef & Cheddar Brisket, its more than enough to fill even the biggest of appetites, if not you can always get a larger sandwich. Prices are reasonable, and service is usually pretty good. Good food, fast service, decent location, and plenty of seating make Firehouse Subs a great place for a quick bite to eat.

I saw Dr. Chang, and after many years of believing I had a bee sting allergy I was surprised and relieved to find out that this was not true. She painlessly identified what I was actually allergic to instead. Her staff is friendly and attentive, and Dr. Chang is far and away the smartest, most thorough physician I've known.

Indian Walk has been wonderful to our beloved dog. Their online pharmacy service is extremely convenient, and we have been treated with love and care at every visit. We recently had to put our dog on arthritis medication. Although I was very resistant to medicating him, the staff patiently explained the risks and benefits, and long term treatment options. As a result, he is acting like a puppy again!

Terrible service. Check in was delayed by 2 hours. Took an hour to get the car out of valet after being told it would be 15 mins. Missed most of a dinner date with friends because of it. Rooms are outdated for the price and we were in the "nice" area. Normally when traveling for pleasure I like to stay at a W or Westin. This was of lesser quality for a higher price than the hamptons I stay in for work. Really wish I would have stayed at the days inn across the street because I could have had the same experience (or better) for less money.
The coffee was very watery-didn't taste like coffee at all. 5 bucks went down the trash. I'm a big coffee person so that was a big disappointment for me because i've read all these good reviews.

We discovered this place a couple of months ago.  We have not found anything on the menu that we do not like.  This is the best breakfast place we have found. Great sandwiches for lunch and the dinners are just as good.  Great home cooking food and the service is just as good.   We have had nothing but great experiences here that this is about the only place we will go.

Came here with my mom and brother before I caught my plane back to Denver. The service was excellent, she gave us great recommendations for the wine and food abd it was a perfect last meal before I left.

The service and convenience of this hospital was amazing.  I brought my cat in around 8:00pm because he just stopped using his back legs, once there they immediately took him back to do a physical and got a history from me.  After they examined him they explained things that could be causing the pain and leg dragging and the outcomes were not good.  They were very compassionate about the well-being of my cat and also gave me all the information they could about what it could be and what options I had.  When I was told about the option of putting him to sleep because it was something fatal, I began to cry and they were very comforting.  They gave me time to think about what I wanted to do, in which I decided to take him home to spend more time with him, I was given medicine to help ease his pain.  I was looking to pay A LOT of money because it was an emergency room, but was very shocked to find out it was extremely reasonable.  I highly recommend this place to anyone who needs it.  The staff there was professional and compassionate.

I visited the restaurant during a conference on a lunch break. The food was not good. It wasn't properly seasoned and tasted bland. The wait to order was short but I had to wait about 25 minutes for three chicken tacos. The meal came with tortilla chips which were very stale. The cooks wore no gloves and were constantly wiping their foreheads that were filled with sweat then touching the food. Gross! I'm giving this restaurant one star only because the decor was cute for a bar. It also seems like they have something going on every day of the week. The staff was friendly.  I wouldn't recommend this restaurant and definitely wouldn't bring children here.

WARNING: SERIOUS SEXISM. This review is for an experience that my mom, a professional women in her early sixties, had with Faouzi at the National Car Rental counter in Indianapolis this week, Tuesday, March 14th. Due to impending snow and cancelled flights she was trying to rent a car to drive from Indianapolis to St Louis, Missouri. She was going counter to counter trying to hire a car and when she got to National she was told by the employee working that they didn't have any cars. She turned to keep walking and was less than ten feet away when a man approached the counter and was told they did have a car. My Mom turned back and asked about it as she had just been told they didn't have any. Then man behind the counter, his name tag read Faouzi, responded that he told her no because it was an Escalade and it cost $100 a day to rent. Let's talk about how horrible that is: he's made the assumption that 1. she isn't competent enough to drive an SUV and 2. she couldn't afford a $100 a day car rental but the MAN that approached the counter after her could do both of those things, or at the very least, deserved the right to make the decision for himself and she didn't. My mom asked for the man's card as she was going to call National herself and he handed her a business card with the name Mike Massaro, which did not match his name tag. Sorry Mike, he threw you under the bus. 

Completely disgusting behavior. If that is the type of people that National hires, I know I won't be renting from them ever again.

In Tria We Trust. I have yet to be disappointed with any dish or beverage here. Always fresh and full of flavor - highly recommend the bruschetta: Pistachio Herbed Ricotta with Lavender Honey (though may work best as a dessert rather than appetizer).

Staff is extremely knowledgeable, ask any and all questions - better yet, tell them what you're looking for and take them up on their suggestions!

I ordered the Italian hoagie and old bay fries with cheese wiz sauce on the side.  The food was very good!  The staff was extremely pleasant when I called to place my order and the delivery man was also very nice.  I will definitely order from here again.

Leigh Anne was absolutely wonderful! She offered so many different choices for the cake. She listened to all that I wanted and made it happen. The result was breath taking and I am so happy I chose her to make my wedding cake. She also offered a gluten/dairy free option for my mother in law and everyone who had the gluten/dairy free chocolate cupcakes absolutely loved them! We had three options for our cake flavors, a coconut flavor, a strawberry flavor, and for the top we have another strawberry flavor that my husband and I will enjoy on our 1st year anniversary. The design of the cake was absolutely stunning, took my breath away when I laid eyes on it! The taste and flavors were so good! Melt in your mouth, moist, fluffy, pure deliciousness! Everything from the experience to the actual product was just absolutely amazing! And Leigh Anne took my order in the last minute! My "friend" was originally suppose to make my cake but backed out last minute and Leigh Anne was my Wonder Woman, swept in and saved the day! I really cannot say enough good things about my experience with Delicious Designs. You can't beat the flavor and design, and at a very reasonable price for brides on a budget! I recommend you look no further, Delicious Designs is the place where your cake dreams become a reality! Thank you Leigh Anne!!

Truly a pleasant experience. I live in Tampa but had some time to kill while my friend was having an elective surgery.  Thanks to my fellow yelpers I tried this place and it was amazing! Aaron did my shall a manicure and design on my toes. Very affordable and they truly are nice people!

I purchased my 2011 Toyota Highlander new on April 1, 2011 from Beck Toyota.  Knew the exact vehicle and color I wanted and had even had another dealership do a "search" for me.  Found my vehicle at a dealership down in KY.
Cannot say enough good things about Beck Toyota.  Had known for years I would be buying a Highlander and assumed I would buy from Butler Toyota on the north side as we live closest to that dealership.  When the time came to purchase, Butler had the highest price and would NOT negotiate!  My husband does negotiations for his work and even went in and spoke with the sales manager.  Nope!  He was told they "don't have to negotiate".  I feel they get enough north side/Carmel business that they are not that hungry for the sale.
When I called Beck Toyota the salesperson person gave me the best price - over the phone! - of anyone, and I had checked all local dealerships and even some out of town/out of state.  Butler wanted just under $1000. more for the same exact vehicle!  Definitely worth the 30-minute drive from Castleton/Fishers to Greenwood!  Would definitely recommend Beck Toyota to anyone looking for a Toyota!

This Party City is no different than any of the others ones I've been in around the country.  It's located across from the mall in Clearwater. It's clean, well organized and easy to find. They have a good selection of all things party and celebration. 

The staff is friendly and helpful! There is a full wall behind the register of all things helium related. There are balloons I've never seen any other place. They will fill them for you and if they deflate before your event they will refill it for free. 

At Halloween the right side of the store and most of the isles are all things related to the holiday. If the costume you want is not available they will order it right there for you. If you see something online and not in the store they will ship it, no extra charge. 

There is a full party candy isle with baggies available for party favors. They have wedding, school, sports, and many other themes available in the store at all times! 

Go check it out!!

I came here for lunch before movie time.  Had a Sparks sweet tea. Quite yummy. Food was very good. I had the brisket sandwich with crispy onions on a brioche bun. With sweet potato fries on side. Best fries I've ever had! Not greasy and had a nice crunch.  Tried all their sauces and liked CBQ original best. But all were good. Will be bringing my family here next week. I was told they try to source as much of their food locally as possible.

Excellent customer service.
Attention to detail
Clean
Worth the price 
Cash is better since there is a surcharge for credit cards
On-time service

Last night we walked here for dinner.  It was a nice night so we sat outside to people watch while enjoying the food of El Camino. The margarita was so good, I could have had another 1 or 2.  We had the unlimited chips/salsa, the veggie wings and pig wings as appetizers, which really could make a meal in itself. Onto the entrees, I had the bbq sampler;  short rib, pork shoulder and pork belly and my friend has the "ole gringo" burrito. I did try the homemade sauces that I read about on yelp, but it would have been nice for the server to explain the sauces.  Service was ok and prices are reasonable. Worth checking out.

Discovered this place during a quick stop in Philly and was very glad I did!  I really appreciated the variety of options here. I went in expecting to be able to get some fresh carrots and was able to walk away with some cooked veggies from the hot food bar at the cafe there. 

When I interacted with the staff there they were fairly friendly though no one asked me if I needed any help or was looking for anything in particular. 

This is a great spot to grab some groceries or get a bite to eat.  Definitely recommended if you prefer vegetables and healthy meal options over cheesesteaks!

What a awesome experience this was. We got there on a Tuesday at about 1:30 and it was crowded there was a wait for a table ( about 30 minutes ) while we were waiting we walked along the water and watched boats and fish jumping out of the water so it went fast. There is also a tiki bar. We had a choice of indoor or outdoor seating we went with the outdoor and was very happy with our choice. We ordered coconut shrimp as a appetizer in my 40 something years of life I have never had shrimp that good. My husband had wings with a dry rub I'm not much for wings but they were good. I had a fried chicken wrap it has lettuce, tomato, Swiss cheese, bacon and avocado it was awesome!!! All the staff was friendly and helpful. We will definitely be returning very soon. Worth the wait!!

We went for the lunchtime all you can eat sushi (which is $18, 12-4 I think, including weekends, I believe, but call to confirm this).  There's a really wide variety of choices, which includes about 15 of the special rolls.  I'm no connoisseur, but I enjoyed all the rolls we got, especially the special rolls.  They were definitely NOT overloaded with rice when we were there.  The $18 is well worth it if you go there with a moderate appetite.

Just tried to go there ordered my food at 8:05 2 platters she told me 25min so I said OK..walked in at 8:35 she ignored me and after handing out 3 orders and .. Ohh upon arrival already had 4 customers waiting for over 20min she finally said how can I help you..... So I told her I called ahead and then she said ohh well its another 20more min so I'm like you know what ... You were stank and service was disgusting.. I won't be coming back left without anything....HIGHLY DISSATISFIED?..!!
Their happy hour is the best!! Til 7 which is great for someone who works a little later. They have the best salsa.
Have waited 25 minutes for my order on numerous occasions. Store is busy, but less so than other locations. Staff is unfriendly and unapologetic.

We were really excited that this place has moved closer to us because I've had a couple of people tell me they were good. I'll deal with those people later. We got 24 wings and will be throwing away 20. The flavors are so bland and they are not at all crispy or cooked well. We got 4 flavors...tried one of each and are so disappointed. The "famous" fries were terrible. Bland and soggy.

I've lived in the area for over 17 years and have never used Just Cruisin. Not for any other reason than I didn't think about them. But today that changes!! My daughter bottomed out her car thus popping off the driver side of her front bumper. We were fearful this was going to cost her hundreds of dollars because she was going to have to take it back to the dealer (she's only had the car a couple months) to be repaired. Then she remembered Just Cruisin and called them. She went there on a Friday at 3 pm and had her car back in an hour and were beyond reasonable! On top of all that she had left her wallet on her car seat next to her purse. When I took her back her wallet was in her purse zipped up. These guys are life savers and I definitely recommend them!!

This is a totally mixed review and here's why~ I have been to the Original Oteri's and had great things but recently went to the newer bakery near Franklin Mills, NE Philly and it was horrible! I ordered cookies, which were just average, and 2 cupcakes. The cupcakes were so hard and stale that they did not crumbel but instead broke in chunks. I have never seen icing so hard, the jimmies on the cupcakes were a faded color, old and stale:( I was very excited to have an original Philly bakery around and then this. After this I went to buy pies for Thanksgiving, they were ok but packaged so poorly (just wrapped in a clear cling wrap type of wrap) that they were ruined by the time I got them home. I also bought a slice of Italian Cream Cake, it was actually pretty good. While there the first time I did notice an Oteri's delviery truck making their delivery I assume from another where they bake everything? I hope this is not how they are going to be because I would really like to go back and get some more goodies!!

Quirky, cute, homey friendly and good coffee / tea!  What more could you want in a local place.  They aim to please and have many regulars.  They have a limited selection of muffins and quiche which I did not try.  The tea is loose leaf and brewed when ordered.  They have a "bar" set up with stools, a sitting area with couches and chairs and outdoor seating.  If you drink in they give you a mug, no mugs match they are eclectic and vary in size - it is part of what makes the place fun.  They have art work all over the walls and quotes that will have you inspired or laughing.  Some of my colleagues had the Elvis which was a coffee roasted with banana and peanut flavorings.  They have every milk/non-milk option.  The prices are decent too.  They are also pet friendly.  I have already told 3 friends they should check it out and now all of you.  Enjoy!
Excellent customer service. Glen was a nice as could be. He was very informative and Helpful. The storage facility seems secure and safe.

I was terrified to bring my dog to a groomer, but with nothing but a stand up shower at home, I had very few choices.
I have a rescued 50lb pit mix who is generally very well-behaved, but usually only if I'm around. He gets very skittish around people he doesn't know and is very prone to wrestlemania when around other dogs. He often forgets his own size. In addition, he hates water. As in, will not leave the doorway for a walk if its raining. Hates. Water.
I dropped him off on a weekday right before work and sat at work dreading the phone call from the staff to come pick him up. When it came time to collect him I was pleasantly surprised by the Suds and Swagger's staff's reaction. They went on and on about how easy (he has very short hair, so I'd imagine that's not too much trouble) and calm (my dog?) he was!
I could not be happier to have eliminated the dreaded bathtime from my dog's routine here at home! If Suds and Swagger keeps this up, he'll be getting bathed every two days!

If you haven't had gelato, I first have to wonder where you've been for the past 6 years, and then I have to tell you about Frost.

If you have jumped on the Italian answer to ice cream bus, welcome and let's go to Frost.

Lots of flavors--around 25--are just the first option available. Then, one flavor, 2, or 3? What size? Chocolate lover, it's here. Fruit-a-holic? No problem. Wanna go to Italy with the flavor, too? Easy.

I don't think it's possible to leave Frost without a smile on your face and a happy belly...if you do, well, you're not like anyone I know.


Lemoncello, Strawberries and Champagne, Mocha, White Chocolate Cream, Margarita...these are just some of the flavors avaiable in May 2010. A mixture or a single selection, either way, you're set for about $4 for a medium size. And once you get the hang of your favorites, try a shake or freeze!

I haven't explored a lot of the sushi places in the city, but I've been to a few and this is hands down the best sushi place I've come across. They have an all-you-can-eat menu, which doesn't serve the creme de la creme of their offerings on this menu, but I've never been disappointed. If you want good sushi in the city, I would seek this place out.

This UHAUL location is as good as it gets. I am writing this review after working with a separate UHAUL location in Charlotte, NC which has provided extremely dissatisfactory service. I now have come to the realization how great the Kingshighway location really was. 

I rented a 15 foot truck in November for my move back to CLT. The customer service was impeccable over the phone and in person. When we arrived at our designated pick-up time, the vehicle was ready to go and a friendly male staff member walked us around the truck explaining how it all worked, looking at previous damage (there was very little) and had even warmed up the cab for us. The truck had just gotten new tires and had less than 30,000 miles on it!

I would recommend this location to anyone who is looking for moving services in STL!

I love the local ingredients and unique menu at Maynard's. If you are looking for something extra special I highly recommend requesting a chef's table here. I took my husband for his 30th birthday, named the price and specified a focus on sous vide cooking. We were delighted by a five course meal with wine pairings (non alcoholic Bellini pairings for me as I was pregnant) and all were excellent. Chef Addam came out to explain each course personally. The only slight hiccup in the evening was when my husband spilled his fourth glass of wine on me and started inviting everyone to come to our home for dinner :)

Ordered the papas "bowl"--potatoes are the only vegetarian option--and received a box with an inch of white rice on the bottom, topped with a handful of shredded iceberg lettuce, a tablespoon of chopped tomatoes, a tablespoon of corn, and about a half cup of seasoned potato cubes. For $7.50. Ridiculously overpriced for the quality of ingredients, flavorless without heaps of "'not avacado' guacamole" [sic] (salsa verde).

Sorry. Never again. For what it's worth, not a fan of the boxing chic either, but would have gotten past it if the food was any good.

Ok I have rented from Hertz here a number of times...and never felt compelled to leave a review. Tonight, is the exception. When I walked out of the airport with my luggage after a three hour delay, the Hertz bus was there. The air conditioning was pumping (thank goodness) and the driver was delightful! When I got to the rental center, I had my pick of cars and chose a clean SUV. As I pulled out to show ID a very nice guy checked me out, showed me some features I didn't know about and gave me a bottle of water! Great experience!

I got a yelp email and it said that this place has some of the best wings in town. So we ventured over and it was true! We loved their wings so much. Pizza was just ok but it's worth going just to get the wings! Their sauce is soooo yummy! The wings are smaller but I like that. It weirds me out when wings are these huge, unnatural giant things. These are the perfect size and flavor. Go get the three pound portion and share with a friend!
This my favorite Mexican place in St. Louis ! Lunch Vippys style is awesome as well as the burrito  California, the grease salsa and chips are yummy too!

Its baffling how Rusty's became the most prolific pizza joint in this town.  Its national chain quality pizza at a premium price.  The boring looking salad bar reminded me of Pizza Hut.  The uniformly round sausage kibbles reminded me of those rectangular "oh so tasty" school cafeteria pizza.  I came here for the first time in 4 years because it was the last day of Youth Soccer.  The place was completely kid friendly, like Chuck e Cheese, Pizza Hut, and Little Caesar all roll into one.  I have kids and even I think its too kid friendly, maybe that how they compete with super cheap Costco pizza across the street and better American style pizza places scattered around town.

You would think the "hospitality" suite would be more hospitable. If only I was here to throw a raging party--but I'm not. I arrived at 11pm off a flight, get told despite having a reservation the only room left is the hospitality suite, I get upstairs and there is not even a bed ready for me. I call housekeeping and they come quickly to move a love seat and stone/metal coffee table in order to pull down the Murphy bed. Was I expected to do this on my own? Meanwhile, I pull all the towels out and create a walking bridge throughout the room so I can stop wondering what all the carpet stains might be from. Gross. I spent the next 30 mins scrubbing the bathroom floor to see if any stains would come up from the flooring--no luck...more towels. There are no lights next to the bed--because let's be honest, no one should sleep in this room--and so of course I bruised my shin trying to get from the light switch to the bed. I guess I should be grateful I got a room given 3 other late night arrivals with reservations got moved off property. This is just disgusting though. Disappointing Marriott.

Hands down the best sushi around! The rolls are creative and fun, the fish is fresh, and there are so many different options. There are many other menu options, but I can't stray from the delicious sushi!

This is my go to for fresh, fast and healthy!  I've never had anything from Freshii that I didn't like and I've tried pretty much everything that has a vegetarian option. It is a little expensive, but worth the extra couple of dollars to eat healthy. Whatever you do, get the goji (peanut butter coconut) balls. Amazing.
The door man is absolute tool. He claimed that i was being rude and disruptive when I was getting my friend an uber.  Didnt let me come back in.
I just received  terrible uber eats order from here. They sent me the wrong pizza, uncooked wings, and a FLAT 2 liter of Pepsi. Do not order from here. I  WANT MY MONEY BACK.

The most stupid supermarket that takes advantage of its proximity to center city and its monopoly as a full-fledged market in order to sell overpriced and expired foods. Pretty much every single thing is over priced while still being of terrible quality, since its been sitting on the shelf for too long.

Bought canned peppers and used it once and a week later it was bad. 

I've been guilty of running in here when in dire need of something but I try to avoid it as much as possible.

All their food is incredible and fresh, but the hot roast beef is Literally the best sandwich Ive ever had. I've been going there for years but just discovered it and had to create a Yelp account just to let the world know. It's otherworldly good. You're missing out big time if you do not make Abruzzis a regular destination!
Amazing hotel in downtown!  Brand new, with very friendly staff.  Great location and amenities.

Rons is awesome. Food is great. Beer selection is awesome. Bartenders are always friendly. Bar is an older scene though. My only complaint are the shitty crinkle cut french fries. They're the worst french fries around. Everything else is awesome.

We had two thin crust pizzas - they were both very good. The garlic bread is an interesting and tasty variation on the traditional.

Interesting art adds to the ambiance.

We stumbled upon this place while wandering around on Labor Day. It was the sign out front that got me, promising a Louisiana style brunch. Being that my boyfriend just moved here from Louisiana, I knew we had to check it out. When we walked in I was a little skeptical that they would have good food, as it has a dive bar feel. And that isn't necessarily brunch friendly. My expectations were more than exceeded. I ordered the bananas foster French toast and a side of praline bacon, as promised on the sign. He was excited to order fried green tomatoes and boudin with hash browns and eggs, a taste of home. We sampled some of each other's food and agreed everything was amazing! I'm not a huge sweets for breakfast person but the French toast was some of the best I had!!! And the praline bacon was like candied bacon. So good. And then I topped off brunch with a beer brewed with chai tea. That's a breakfast beer right? If you are in town come check it out. Great beer list and even better food!!

Really great place! Sweet Thai decor inside and outside patio space with Thai inspired tea house seating. The waiter Mitch was great and it was an all together good experience.

This was a forst for my 15 yr old stepson so he, my husband and I shared 3 lunch specials so he could try some different dishes. We had Pad Thai (chick), Pad See Iew (beef)and Red Curry (chick). Each special came with soup (best Tom Yum ever) or salad, egg rolls, wonton crisps and rice. 

I would absolutely go back and also recommend this place.
The staff is not friendly and the fish spread is ok, but it is certainly not the best in town like they advertise. Overall, we were disappointed with our experience.

I've been exploring han's dynasty and here are my preliminary rankings (1 is best)

1. Exton
2. Old City
3. Manayunk
4. University City

Coming in at the bottom of the list, this location has a hip ambiance with a nice bar that saves it from 1 star. The dry pot was swimming in soup (more like a wet pot) and other dishes had execution issues as well.
Fabulous food, professional and friendly staff, fun music, hip ambiance.  I keep coming back for more!

Customer service is terrible, I don't think they clean the theaters in-between viewings and the lines are always outrageously long for tickets and snacks because they are understaffed. The main attraction is the upgrade they did to the seats in each theater. The seats alone aren't worth it. There are other theaters in the area that are much better.

This chain is normally one of our favorites. Last night for our anniversary dinner- not so much.
Service (Benjamin) was totally lacking. Almost awkward to be honest, Cheese steak egg rolls (our favorites) were overcooked and extra greasy,.   Waited for drink refills for a long time.
