Went 3 other people and we all ate each other's food because everyone wanted to try it all. Chicken parm - awesome. Lobster ravioli - awesome. Steak - awesome. Fish dish - awesome. 

And it's BYOB which makes its extra great. 

I'd suggest this to anyone in the area!!! 

Call ahead though, because it gets packed and you need a reservation to get a table on a busy night!

Yesterday- 2/4/15- we were in Indianapolis on business and decided to go to Joe's Crab Shack for lunch.  Our first clue was that we were the only people in the place at 2PM..figuring we missed the lunch crowd, we sat down and ordered our meals.  The 2nd clue was that our table was wobbling back and forth.  Asked the server about it and the neighboring tables also were uneven.   Our food came out and it was sloppy placed on the plates- I had the shrimp platter.  The french fries were cold and covered in salt, the shrimp were greasy.  My husband had a piece of fish and potato dish.  Food was not hot but he ate it.....about 3 hours later he  did not feel well and the next few hours were spent in the hotel bathroom.  Now we remember why we never go to the Joe's in Schaumburg IL, near our house.   We should have gone to another restaurant down the road, but thought we would give them a chance.  Never again. When we left the restaurant, another couple had just been seated.  I hope their experience was better than ours.

Ok the BBQ shrimp here is the best I've ever had!!! Our bartender was phenomenal and truly made the whole experience for us. He gave us bibs and we ate with the BBQ shrimp with our hands -- there really is no other better way to eat them!!! They are finger lickin' good! I can't wait to come back here and try more of their menu items.
I was so impressed with this salon. Friendly service and exceptionally detailed work were the highlights. Best spot I've been to in St. Louis! If you're needing a mani/pedi, this is the place to go!

Three stars is not great. Hibachi should be easy, but this place suffers from mediocre service and food. Sushi was ok but still the highlight of the meal. Hibachi was kinda yuch. They put a nasty teriyaki sauce on everything. It's too heavy. They put it on my lobster, which helped hide the fact that it wasn't fresh. 
The choices on Sam Ridley pkwy aren't great and I had high hopes that this place could be added to my list of options, but alas, no.

Disgusting. Pillows were stained with big yellow puddles of slobber, (not mine) and stunk horribly. The stains were in plain sight as the pillow cases were tattered and didn't completely encase the yuck. I used rolled towels as  my pillow. Planned to stay there for 3 nights, left as soon as the sun came up. So gross... Bad odors, bathroom nasty. ..hair on the bathroom floor, also not mine

Unremarkable. Food was good, but it took a long time. When I asked for a beer taste, the waiter told me it was going to take awhile because the bar staff was super busy. I thought, this is a beer restaurant, surely a beer taste isn't too tough.  The atmosphere was dull. The wait staff seemed unhappy. Don't think we will go back.

I've lived in Nashville my entire life, and I've noticed that this place seems to be a staple for a lot of newcomers and tourists, but I'm not entirely sure why. I couldn't have helped but notice the insanely long lines wrapping around the building, so one day I decided to try it myself. 
I was not impressed with the food here at all. It's your average breakfast food, and honestly, the quality is about the same as something you'd get at iHop. While there is a wide variety of different pancakes to choose from, I still wouldn't say that this makes the restaurant worth it. If you're looking for a good breakfast restaurant, save yourself the time and choose somewhere else. 
However, if you're wanting to try to popular restaurants in Nashville but don't care too much in terms of quality for the price, then this is the place for you.

I love this place.  That's all.  If you can't tell by the other reviews I'm not sure mine will help you, but here it goes.  Icecream=excellent
Staff=friendly and quite possibly faster that jimmy johns
Try a delicious blizzard!!

It took several calls to Jason Martinez, who works in the tire department, to get through and make an appointment for 4 new General tires.  The transaction was set up by my father, so they may not have connected me to the service as I use a different last name.  Hopefully, the service will happen tomorrow at 1:30pm with no glitches.  Their shop is near King's Buffet, and the Savers/JoAnn fabric and Harbor Freight shopping center (as well as being near the Atlantis and Burlington Coat Factory) so I can do some shopping while I wait the approximate 2 hours for the tires to be installed.

The building where Iris Restaurant is located could easily be mistaken for an apartments but the menu posted outside the window makes its presence known. The interior, while painted the same colors as the outside of the building, is a classy upscale but not stuffy atmosphere. Whether you're looking to wine and dine, cozy up on a first date or celebrate a romantic special occasion this restaurant is the place.

Our waitperson was a true professional and my trusted advisor throughout the evening. He interjected his opinion and made suggestions which is something a lot of waiters don't do but that I find welcoming. His suggested cocktail for the evening was either the Prickle or The Count. I ended up choosing The Count and I couldn't be happier with the choice. It wasn't what I would typically order but it was a exemplary choice and a well crafted cocktail.

I was so please with my first cocktail and curious about what our waitperson said was his favorite cocktail that I ordered the Prickle. This is a gin based drink and I don't drink gin. You could obviously taste the gin in the drink but its subtle sweetness and refreshing coolness made me like it.

Iris's menu is small with about 10 main choices but most of the dishes sounded so good I was having trouble choosing just one. I offered up my choice and out of my picks, our waitperson recommend the Duck Confit. The skin was perfectly crispy and the meat was moist beyond belief. Combine that with the corn and the sweetness of the peaches and you have a delectable dish.

My boyfriend ordered his usual steak in the form their Steak Frites. It was very tender and tasty. The foie gras-marrow butter was a brilliant touch and put this dish it over the top. The fries were incredible too, I reckon a Belgium would eat these fries and give them his/her stamp of approval.

We finished off the meal with the Chocolate Soufflé Pistachio Cake. It was rich, chocolaty yumminess but if I am not mistaken, this was not a soufflé (unless it was a fallen one) and more like a flourless cake. I liked it anyways and the nuts added some texture to the dessert.

Iris was flawless, I can't wait to come again!
I absolutely love Finley's! For starter we love the spinach dip. The corn beef and cabbage is like good ol' home cooking, smothered chicken is also amazing. Always had great service and atmosphere!
This place is delicious!!!! From the Shrimp to the Buffalo Chicken Strips :).. The atmosphere is perfect as well. I would encourage you to try it.

Ate lunch on a busy Friday and had just a couple minute wait to be seated . The place was packed but service was quick and accurate.  The wife and I both had some healthy low calorie meals.  Much better than my last visit and more of  what I  expected of the restaurant after eating at several across the country.
The blackened catfish with shrimp creole sauce is amazing!

So I do a lot of conventions Orlando Las Vegas Nashville seems to be the theme however I checked into the Nashville Gaylord and can't even get a charge by my bed however I did fix it by changing the lamp from the desk to the one by my bed that has an outlet how hard is that this is not a huge Convention it's a little smaller than the ones that I usually go to. Stayed in a lot better rooms at the same exact price you have to give a discount for the ones that are not accommodated yet or remodeled
4 screens of first run double features.  Digital protection looks great! Open 6 days a week in summer including Sunday.
Excellent food and price ^_^ .... The place is all but coZy .... Waiter was nice ....I would definitely come back again

I took a friend there for her birthday. She is a huge fan of Indian food. I was not, just couldn't get past the smell. We wanted to go somewhere we've never been and decided a trip to downtown would fit the bill. Let me just say, I am now a fan of Indian food. The restaurant is bright and clean. As a newbie to Indian cuisine this was the best place to start. The staff was very friendly and did a great job explaining all the foods to me. The food was very fresh with lots of flavor. I've been back several times and will return very soon. I just wish they were open on the weekends.

I heard about Mellow Mushroom from an article citing the best pizza places in each of the fifty states, and Georgia's Mellow Mushroom in Atlanta made the list, specifically the Holy Shittake pizza.  Seeing that they had a location near our mosque, we went there to try it out.

There was a ten minute wait, but busy nights happen, nothing you can do about that.  Once seated, we placed our order and waited ... and waited ... and waited.  I'm pretty patient when it comes to restaurants but I was just starting to wonder if we had truly been abandoned when finally our pizza came.

It was very good, but very greasy.  We were to take some home for leftovers but my husband went all out and ate his half (with added bell peppers) right there.  Apart from the greasiness I was also quite impressed by the pizza.  After we boxed my leftovers, we ordered the Key Lime Pie.  Someone from the kitchen, perhaps the manager or the head chef/cook/whathaveyou - or maybe even just another employee - brought out our pie to us, apologized for the wait on the pizza, and gave us the pie free of charge!  Yay.

Unfortunately, the pie was nothing spectacular.  Having lived in Florida for a little over two years, I've had the pleasure of trying quite a few key lime pies and while Mellow Mushroom is known for their pizzas it is NOT known for its key lime pie and for good reason.  But, it was free, so no complaints.  Next time, we might try their brownie sundae, I saw one go past us and it did look tempting.

So, four stars on account of greasy pizza and a somewhat inattentive waitress but super nice chef/manager that gave us desert on the house.
Very good. Happy hour $.50 oysters are where it's at. Great cocktails. Delicious desserts. Always a fav place to stop while in New Orleans.

I like it, I love it, I want some more of it.  This is a great new trend that will hopefully be sweeping the nation.  Quick, affordable sushi to go.

I was staying at a buddy's place and used my trusty yelp app to try and find some brunch.  This definitely wasn't brunch, but when I saw the name, I knew I had to give it a shot.

I liked the idea of making my own, but just needed to try what they recommended first.  The original seemed like the way to go.  Large chunks of tuna, crab as well as some other toppings.  I went with the poke sauce as that seemed like the obvious choice with the tuna.  All wrapped up with rice and soy paper.  Super easy to eat, reasonably priced and made quickly to order.  Its a win win for everybody and I seriously hope I start seeing similar places in other areas of the country.

One of the most charming and unique hotels I've ever stayed in, a converted train station and historic, but not over the top. The rooms reminded me of a boutique hotel feel. Staff was terrific and close by everything we wanted to see. 

Historic atmosphere, modern amenities. Win/win.

I forgot to write my review from my stay a few months back but this is probably the best hotel & casino in Reno! The one thing that stands out is the sportsbook area if you are a sports bettor this is the place to go!

burgers are great, so great that I can never get myself to try the other sandwiches on their menu.  get any combo of the burger you want, the meat is the best part.  and if your debating the thousand island on the village burger, its worth trying...good combination I would have never thought of.
the duck fries are average compared to other places, but they become excellent with the beer cheese sauce.
this place has limited seating so a wait is to be expected.  but they will text you when your table is up, so just plan on another activity for 30 to 90 minutes while your table is ready.

Thank you yelp! We came in on for Sunday brunch and requested something we've seen on YELP! They were more than happy to replicate the dish. We also ordered raw oysters and crab benedict. The main star dish was the Roasted jalapeno cheese grits with yard egg topped with a crispy fried soft shell crab. Yes, it was very rich in favor. The egg yolk oozing with perfection & you can taste the jalapeno like you just bit into a fresh one.

This place is great for younger kids. I would not bring anyone over 8 yrs old because it's geared more to younger kids. There is a lot to see and do. There are different stations the kids can play in and keep them entertained for hours. This place is affordable.

Here for the CMA festival with family and this was next to our hotel so we have it a try. Glad we stopped in!  Everything we had was excellent and staff was very friendly. I guess it's only been open three weeks as that was what the manager (owner?) said when he stopped by to ensure we had a great meal. You know how at nice restaurants today the manager always stops by and sometimes it feel forced? This was not like that in the least. He felt genuine and it was a nice finish to an excellent meal. We only had tapas and con pan, but everything was excellent. I asked my wife about the review on the crispy rice with the paella that was low and she reminded me in Spain when we had it....it was the same so we did not consider that review when we decided to try this out. Highly recommended from a family of foodies.
Fantastic service, above average food, outstanding whisky selection, and the best old fashions I've had in Philadelphia.

WOW!!!  My wife said she didn't want anything fancy , I burger would be fine.  This place undeniably has the best burgers We have ever eaten!  Add some seasoned fries with a variety of unique dipping sauces.  Lastly I got the bourbon and bacon milkshake which was amazing!   This is now a must do whenever return to St. Louis!

Amazing place with amazing flowers and gifts. Went today to get flowers for anniversary  .... Got a great tropical arrangement that was both beautiful and unique. Before I could leave I spotted a incredibly graceful wooden vase with silk flowers that would be perfect for our dinning room table, I couldn't leave without it.

They also carry Caldwell-Massey products and quite good chocolates. They counter person was low key but very helpful, including carrying my purchases to the car. 

Mayfield Florist was a real find ... I'll be buying more flowers, all  at this great shop.
Called ahead for seat in of 10. Show up on time and they split the 10 of us between opposite tables and we can't communicate with the party we came with. Really?

I absolutely LOVE this place. Yes, this one in particular!! The customer service is wonderful! Theres one lady there who seems to hate her job and she makes it clear that she doesn't like working there and she makes it clear the way she slaps together your food and gives you little to no meat even when you offer to pay more for extra you still get nothing. Which is why im giving it 4 stars instead of 5. But aside from her, this place is amazing. I am always in there with my girlfriend every friday we get queso burritos! If i see her in there i go to like burger king or something. Nothing can compare to qdoba though. We need more of these! POPULATE THE EARTH LIKE MCDONALDS!!!!!! Lol
Great service, very accommodating!! Love it!! Strongly recommend the Danny if you like hot... if you like hot hot asl for some of the special sauces from hell's gate roll! Nice heat!!!

Tuscany towers are the shit..... Great food sweet casino and sports book room! Got to try the sushi place there and the steakhouse is pimping too! Then enjoy a nice cigar and a cold beer around the fire pits outside the club!!!!!!
This used to be a beautiful romantic place. Now its filled with country western video screens. Ugh. The staff is very nice.

Checked out this place for the first time last week. Location is cool, I love NoLibs.
 
You start of with a bowl of rice or salad and add on. TIP: you can pick between 3 and 5 scoops, of fish, not rice (serving of rice stays the same). I got a mix of octopus, salmon and tuna. It was okay, way too much sauce and it took away from the entire bowl. TIP: a little goes a long way, stick to minimal toppings and ask for less sauce. The food itself was overwhelmingly soaked in soy sauce and it kind of ruined my first poke experience.

Service was fine, the glass wall makes it hard to communicate with the employees so make sure to speak a little louder. They guy who rang me up kept calling me mamma, which made me very uncomfortable. I don't think I will be going back. I'll wait until my honeymoon to Hawaii in 2090.

LES CREPES SOMMES MAGNIFIQUES! Oh quelle surprise qu'on avait d'apprendre  que la femme qu'on a adoree depuis longtemps est la maitresse de cette restaurant. On ne peut pas croire que c'est la meme personne qu'on a connu, mais on avait ete tres content apres on eu manger. Et on a manger encore et encore.  

Alors, voila...vous allez ici aussi et vous mangerez les crepes magnifiques aussi. 

Essayez le lait avec du menthe. C'est tres délicieux.

Peut etre le service est un peu lent, mais c'est la vie en la cuisine française.

I'm a fan. They offer some nice designer burgers as well as a build your own option, and of course a variety of toppings and sides like fries. You can go for a plain burger or prime organic grassfed beef. You place your order at the counter and then they call your name when it's ready. 

I chose a buffalo blue burger off their specialty menu. You're asked how you want your burger cooked, which usually makes me nervous. If an establishment asks for temp preference, they had better nail it. Lucky for me, my burger came out perfectly medium and my fellow diners were also pleased with their orders. 

The first thing that impressed me about the burger was the SLAB of blue cheese sitting atop the sizeable, mouthwatering patty and the nice drizzle of buffalo sauce encompassing everything. No blue cheese crumbles here - this cheese chunk was like a deck of cards in size! No complaints from me about this burger!

I snuck a few fries from my friends - truffle fries were nice and light and crispy. Sweet potato fries were also good. 

The only downside of this place is the cluttered and small seating area. We went during lunch rush on a Friday so this is to be expected in any center city spots, but the large wooden high tops and stools were laid out in a really inefficient patten. It was like a game of Jenga to try to work yourself into a seat (which luckily we found). 

Burgers are around $9. Price with a drink and fries was about $15.

Verdict: I would definitely return.

An excellent hotel, certainly stylish. Not cheap yet a good value for the money. Love the art everywhere, from lobby to halls to rooms. Staff is helpful and friendly. Best hotel shower I've taken with water faucet on ceiling and well lit shower (something most hotel showers/baths don't have is good lighting). Good bed and pillows. Convenient plug-ins around room. Plenty of outdoor space in restaurant and bar. Free and good wi-fi signal everywhere. I'd stay here again and will look for other Dolce brand hotels when traveling. Their slogan matches the experience: "Hotel Reinterpreted."

H&I is a great place with a wide ranging menu that is sure to satisfy any patron.  The  homage to St. Elmo's is well done in the replication of the world class shrimp cocktail and well executed steaks.  However Harry & Izzy's takes it a step beyond with a broader menu selection that allows you to try pizza, sandwiches, and more all well executed and sure to satisfy.  I would recommend this as a must try for visitors and larger parties as it is sure to meet everyone's needs and expectations.

If you are in the neighborhood, this is worth checking out. The wait is first come, first serve so expect to wait at peak brunch times. I will say they do move quickly so the wait isn't as bad as you would think. That being said, i only think the food was average. You will likely find better and more unique brunch spots in the city.

The best thing at this Olive Garden was the service. Outstanding! The 3 course meal deal was great and satisfying. The salad and breadsticks were yummy. Loved the offer of complimentary wine when we arrived. Overall, great experience and would return.

Came here to support a local band, Island Avenue, and have some BBQ. The BBQ here is outstanding. Started with the 'smoked bologna' which is off-the-chain,AGT. Then , brisket and spare ribs with garlic red potatoes with cornbread pudding. Mmmmmmm mmmmmmm gooooood! The smoke near perfect with an outstanding rub. 
All this listening to some great music. The is a great place and it is only a Sunday night! Will try another night soon.

I love the variety of sandwiches they have here. I like that they also deliver and they don't take long on their deliveries which was pretty convenient for me being a college student and being hungry at night. There prices aren't the best prices ever but I was able to get a discount for being a Tapingo Club Member which helped a lot because I bought each sandwich for about $3 each which I am happy about. Overall their sandwiches are good and I do recommend eating or ordering from here if you do want a sandwich that is good.

I have two old Saeco machines - an 1990's vintage Vienna Deluxe (Silver), and a 2003 Magic Comfort +.  The Vienna Deluxe's doser stopped registering coffee and would grind up all my beans.  So I unpacked my Magic Comfort + and after a couple of espressos it lost its home position and jammed the brew group.  So I now had two nonfunctional machines!  

I contacted Saeco Parts (Parts Guru) for replacement gears for the Magic Comfort  + along with a couple of micro-switches.   Edward, referred me to the Parts Guru website for troubleshooting and repair information as well as giving me some advice as to what to look for when repairing the unit.  He also suggested that my old Vienna Deluxe could probably be saved with some maintenance as well.  I found Parts Guru's instructions on how to clean up the doser and it solved the problem. Yea!  

Additionally, the parts I ordered for the Magic Comfort  + arrived, promptly, were less expensive than the parts I could buy locally, and with the additional troubleshooting and testing materials found on their web site, allowed me to repair it also.  Double Yea!  

Finally, I definitely will be purchasing their suggested maintenance kits to keep my machines working for years to come.  I highly recommend these people.

This is my favorite brewery in Saint Louis. It has two levels plus a small outside seating area. Their beer is sublime! 4 Hands brews a boatload of IPA's, terrific stouts, and so, so much more. Food at the downstairs bar, has previously been Mexican and now rotates with the Bailey restaurant family in town. Skeeball and two projectors that they air blues/cards games on up top. Their beer really is phenomenal if you savor hops and they have Crowlers to go. Parking lot out back and also street parking. Right off of I-44/55 about a half mile from Soulard, as well as the South entrance of Busch Stadium. Serves wine and liquor as well as beer. They bottle/can and distribute as well; however, plenty of specialty releases in-house only which is always terrific to be a party to. Quite probably much a must-see for beer lovers visiting STL.

We came here about 5:30pm on a Saturday. We had purchased a groupon when it was High Sierra brewing and had checked with them and confirmed they would honor it. This is an expansion of a brewery from Portland Oregon.

They were having a BBQ buffet for $10 to benefit fallen officers. Our Groupon was for a beer taster flight, an appetizer and two entrees. The place was pretty busy and most tables and the bar area we're fully seated. It was not like that the last time we came in. We were initially seated at a table in the bar area but a server came by and said they had a booth open and she was less busy than the area we were initially seated.

My wife ordered the club sandwich and I ordered The Brewery style French dip. Our appetizer, beer tasters, and entrees were delivered in a timely fashion. Everything looked and tasted delicious.

The food was good, the beer was good, and the service was awesome. It was a good experience and we will be back to try something else.

This Pathmark is just bad for produce, meats & seafood. Really bad. Go elsewhere, please.

If you need the basic staples for your pantry & you live in the neighborhood & you don't drive, work it out as best you can.

Absolutely great customer service and the interior decor is very chic, true to it's name. As a vegetarian with a vegan partner, we are always pleased with the wide variety of food and drink options. Personally, I enjoy the popovers and absolutely love the mayan lattes (which are available in soy and almond varieties). I often find myself spending the morning/afternoon working and enjoying some dishes here with my GF.

I'm torn. I was obsessed with this place when it first opened. Their portion sizes have gone down dramatically whether it be the French fries as the side or the toppings on a burger. However, the quality is top notch. Their burgers are creative and delicious. The beer options are plentiful and always changing. The bar has large TVs if you're wanting to watch the game or nice tables if you're wanting a night out with the family.

5 stars simply does not do this place justice. My fiance and I had dinner here tonight before we went to see Jerry Seinfeld at the Arlington Theater. We got there before our 5pm reservation without realizing it was still happy hour. We began by ordering a dozen oysters and 2 oyster shooters. The oyster shooter was unbelievable. The most delicious oyster shooter I have ever had in my life. It had Parmesan cheese on top which I had never had before, atop some sort of a spicy cocktail sauce, with 2 oysters including the liquid inside. I was amazed. We ordered two more. Then we went ahead and got the calamari.. and let me say, HOLY CRAP! Again, another pleasant surprise. Drizzle it with lemon and you're good to go. We then ordered the margherita pizza with extra cheese. Perfection. I had to cut myself off there, but my fiance ordered one final thing. The plate that topped off the evening, the white truffle shrimp pasta. I had a bite, and if I wasn't so full from the food we already had I would've absolutely ordered my own. The staff was so friendly. Our server was Riley, and she went above and beyond to wait on us. It was slower because of how early it was.. but I'm sure if it was busy, she would have been just as attentive! I told one of the staff it was my fiance's birthday, so at the end of the meal they brought him over complimentary salted caramel flavored scoop of ice cream with a candle in it which was garnished with mint. A nice touch. This place is classy, fresh, casual and elegant all in one. I am so happy to only live 40 minutes away from here.. as I will definitely be coming back for the oyster shooters during happy hour, and look forward to trying one of the salads and other delicious looking menu options.

I got the Newks special salad and it was delicious. I would order this salad again next time. This restaurant is very clean and the staff is great. I normally order a tea which I do love but went with water this time. But I'm sure the tea was great.

I just had to file a Paypal dispute after getting an order confirmation email but no indication that order shipped. No order received at all. I tried to call but no answer. Emailed...no response. Order placed on June 8th and amount was charged. Hopefully they will respond to the dispute so I dont have to file a claim. I wish I would have read the reviews. There are a lot of recent bad ones. I can see why they are suspect. I will try to post an update on how things go in the future with my order. Such poor communication and bad business. I am a first time and last time customer. But they probably dont care...obviously.

I go in there all the time. The guys are really helpful and do everything they can to get you what you need. When you get a new phone, they go through everything in the contract with you. To be completely honest, I've seen people come in complaining they didn't know about something in the contract, and that no one told them about it. Usually, they aren't paying attention either 1. They are too excited, playing with their new phones or 2. They don't care cuz they think they know all there is to know. So that's their own fault. There are times when they can't do as much, because they are a 3rd party, so they send you to the corporate store.  But other than that, the store is excellent! Clean, well maintenanced, and very organized. If they don't have what you want in the store, they will either go pick one up from a different store or order one online. They really do everything they can to get you taken care of.

A hipster's paradise! The Lay's potato chips were definitely a miss and the pretzel bun was good but totally unrealistic to think you should eat it like a sandwich... It was way too big. We sat outside, which was nice and I got a French pressed coffee. It was great!

You will never find acai bowl like this, I've tried many different kinds to try and fill my void of not being able to have backyard bowl and only getting one when I visit Santa Barbara and nothing compare or comes even close to theirs! They do it the best and the staff is always so friendly!

Overall experience was good. Went here after going to a few other bars. Loved the basketball shooting game they have as well as the outdoor fire pit. The outdoor dining makes me feel like I'm in my own backyard and I absolutely love it.

I was so excited to try out the Peanut Butter Bacon burger and I was not disappointed! It was just what I wanted with the sweet and salty with the burger. My only complaint about the burger is that I asked for medium and it was well-done when it came out, but it was still good. I am jealous of my husband since he ordered the potato salad and I ordered the Mac and cheese (which is good), but that potato salad!! It was so creamy and to die for and I only had one bite! So get the Peanut Butter burger and potato salad and you'll love it.

Worst experience I have ever had with a property management group.  Was looking for a hone to rent in Boise area and was treated horribly.  They wouldn't return calls and when they did they were rude and short over the phone.  I had set up times through their system to view homes and nothing gave me suggested times, just repeated responses that my time needed to be rescheduled.  Finally I had set up to view a unit and the wrong key was in the box.  They then missed two subsequent showings.  It just not worth working with them.  Its hard enough to find a rental without this group wasting valuable time.

Great atmosphere and really well done brick over pizza. The dough was perfect and the toppings were delicious.  I also tried the beef tar tar. It was very tasty and high quality. I wish they had more specials for drinks though. Will return.

You know that website, This is Why You're Fat? I think Five Guys is probably the original culprit. Their burgers are pretty much pure meaty perfection on a lightly butter-toasted bun, and the fries are greasy heaven in your mouth. Throw the diet out the window when you walk in the door, and prepare to work out something serious the next morning, because you're here to enjoy yourself tonight.

I find that it's best to go later at night instead of lunch, when it's usually always bananas. It's great for a last-minute take out dinner. Being a girl, and making a purely vain effort to drop a few pounds and maybe salvage my cholesterol in the process, I get the Little Cheeseburger, which is usually plenty for me, and I am not a small gal. My BF is not a small fella, and he get the Little Bacon Cheeseburger. One of these days, I'm going to skip lunch and get the Bacon Cheese Dog. He prefers the Cajun fries, and I like the Plain, and usually just a Regular is enough for two people.

This is what I like most about Five Guys: it's extremely cost-effective. You can share most of what you order and save both calories and dough. Also, um, it's the best burger I've ever had. Believe the hype, y'all.

I will gladly pay $5 for two smallish scoops of gelato. However, what I had here was not gelato. Too icy and airy. Gelato is creamy and dense.

My semantic quibble could have been redeemed by flavor. Unfortunately, there wasn't much. Actually, the pistachio was completely flavorless. The sesame seed had a nice nuttiness, but wasn't nearly sweet enough to classify it as a great sesame seed dessert. 

The space itself has a nice ambiance and plenty of seating including an outdoor patio that is probably great for people watching. I would gladly meet friends here for coffee (assuming Capogiro doesn't miss the mark there too). But even if someone else was buying, I wouldn't partake of the gelato again. Too disappointing.

I will say I was worried when I first checked in.  The "lobby" was more of a hallway and the common areas were pretty shabby.  The front desk person was friendly.  The room itself was fantastic!  Updated flooring and bedding.  An ideal spot for travelers with pets especially.
The duck fries are a must but one hair in my Mac and cheese and well to the " do not go list " it has become

I don't frequent Dunedin very often so instead of Dunkin Donuts, I decide to support the local businesses.  Well, I will never go back here again. The lady working was rude, and had zero customer service skills. She treated me as if I was a burden to her.  The bagels were just ok. I managed to spend  $15 on 3 bagels and cream cheese,  don't ask me how.  Back to Dunkin Donuts it is!!
Just one piece of advice. Your spicy food is so delicious so turn down the temperature!!

What a great place to have some good Mexican food. The menu is authentic. And the prices are reasonable. 
They have the hard to find items like mole and menudo. 
There is plenty of room and tables inside with seating available outside,  too.

I wasn't overly impressed. The som tum mango was alright, but the garlic chicken that a few people mentioned liking was dry and flavorless. The panang beef was tasty, but nothing to write home about. Also, the sticky rice with mango seemed a bit underdone.

I absolutely love going here for all my nail needs.  Prices are great, hospitality is even better. They do such a great job. I've been going there for years, I've brought my mother and daughter here as well.

Came in after a terrible experience with another salon dyeing my hair and Leslie fixed it perfectly! She is amazing with color and knows exactly how to keep your hair healthy while giving you the color that you want. Highly recommend her!!

I had no intention on stopping at the NFM today, but decided to...only to check for honey crisp apples in the produce area. I was hungry, and surprisingly, this place wasn't packed today! I had never eaten middle eastern food before, so I went for it. There were a lot of choices, but I ordered the King's Vegetarian Platter. I am by no means a vegetarian, but it came with a little bit of everything; falafel, hummus, baba ganoug, tabouli salad, stuffed grape leaves, pita, and a lemonade/tea. It came to $10.06, which wasn't a bad deal. My plate was loaded. I felt like a total noob for ordering things that I had NO idea what they were. When I sat at a table, I Googled what baba ganoug and tabouli salad were. Hell, I wasn't even sure what all was in a falafel!
The food was decent. I probably wouldn't go out of my way to order certain things on my plate again, but I still enjoyed it. My pita was on the stale side, but I still ate it. The stuffed grape leaves were yummy. The falafel....oh the falafel...it was amazing. I'm happy that my first falafel experience was a good one. Now I feel the need to try falafel everywhere. Not that I know what a perfectly cooked falafel tastes like, but to me, this was cooked perfectly. I will definitely come back for these themselves and to try some kebabs.

Four stars for product.  ZERO STARS FOR THE RUDEST MOST ARROGANT, OBNOXIOUS 'CUSTOMER SERVICE'.  I should have walked out of there ... but I didn't and I am still kicking myself.

Pralines are good.  Good texture, good bite quality, I would go slightly less on the sugar and more on the flavour.  But good product nonetheless.

This is a review of the Ramble Pizza food truck when it's been at the Mt. Airy Weavers Way Co-op location on Fridays. A great addition to the neighborhood. Happily, they sell pizza by the slice. I've only tried the mushroom pizza and plain cheese pizzas. Cheeses were very good, and some of you might prefer an even thinner crust "Roman" style, so this was pizza in the thicker end of the Roman style spectrum. Nevertheless excellent - what is better than a pizza right out of the oven? I had some concerns about how they'd turn out a pizza from an oven in a food truck, but was very pleased with the results. Owner-run and operated, and they are really friendly, nice people.

Tonight was our first visit here. Paid $70 each person for VIP tickets plus $10 for parking. Got through all 5 attractions in less than 1 1/2 hrs. It was nice skipping the lines cause I would have been pissed if I waited hours for these attractions. 
I'm easily scared but this place didn't do it for me. The interactive ones aren't really interactive. Just light touches on your arms and guiding you different directions than your group. At one point it started down pouring raining and instead of people walking through the attraction they stood there and held up the rest of people. The guests were more scared of the rain. We had to push through people to get through which messed up the scares. 
I wanted to get scared and that's not what I got. I guess I'm still on the look out for an actual scary experience.

This location is great because it's so centrally located, historical, and extremely charming.   The food was fabulous and the service was also excellent. I'd recommend this place to anyone visiting New Orleans.

I'm a new fan of the Local Taco.  I've tried both locations, Brentwood and in Nashville. Along with the great variety of tacos, sauces, and enchiladas; my husband and I love the laid back atmosphere and the Lohitos of course!  

The ingredients are fresh and you never have to wait long for your food.  There are no frills about this restaurant, so don't expect frilly service.  That's not necessarily bad thing.  Just expect good tacos for cheap like the budget.  

One recommendation before you venture:  The Murphy Road location has limited parking in the front and back of the building, so be ready to do some parking spot hunting and/or stalking.
The staff is the friendliest I have ever met. She bought me a petit which was so kind of her. They were delicious. So was the king cake and the doberge cake we got also!!

I have been to this store a handful of times, and each time I've come away with at least something, and something I felt I was getting either for a steal or for a good deal.  I go thrifting often and it's true that the standard prices are higher than normal thrift prices.  However, because everything of the same category is priced pretty much the same way (sweaters one price, shirts another, jackets, suits, shoes, etc.), lots of the stuff is very overpriced.  This is true of shirts and coats especially.  On the other hand, that means that some of the nicer stuff is really underpriced for what it is.  That, for me, is where to find great value.  If you know what to look for, you can get a steal.  Most of it, however, is either junk or overpriced or both.  Sales staff is polite but quiet, not in-your-face.  Not super-helpful, but pleasant to deal with and nice to look at (always well dressed).

Bottom-line: takes luck, patience, or both, but there are deals to be had.  Majority of stuff is too pricey for what it is, though.

If you are looking for a random spot to find random stuff this it the place for you.

Everything is in impressive order and is all priced.  Unfortunately things are often over priced and the owner will not be talked down.

One of my favorite Korean restaurants in the area.  I have a friend that has to go once a week to get his Soondubu (soft tofu soup) fix on.

The place is famous for its soon dubu, and soon dubu is one of my favorite Korean dishes that does not involve meat. They give you alot of choices for what to put in the stew, I almost always get everything which is: Tofu, Beef, Shrimp, Clam, Oyster.  The stew is very very hot when it comes out and you have to put the raw egg in when it first comes out. The taste is indescribable because it is good.   They give you a choice of how spicy you want it, I always get the very spicy.  The side dishes (ban chan) is always good and they give you alot.  Also if you want a appetizer I would recommend the BBQ squid which is marinated in gochujang (korean chili paste) it gives it a sweet and spicy kick and also the hae mool pajun (seafood korean pancake).  I also love at the end how you can put the tea into your rice bowl and get a the crispy rice since the rice is served in a hot clay pot.  

Just writing this review has made me hungry and wanting me to go back to eat their soon dubu.  I would recommend this place to anyone.

Hands down the best donuts I've ever had. I came home to visit from Atlanta and went 3 times in 2 days. I had too many different donuts to name them all, but every one of them were freaking fantastic. This is a must visit place!

Amazing coffee...

but the service sucks! on several occasions, the baristas have just been overly pretentious to the point of being rude! to me, and several other customers. when i asked about wifi, one barista scoffed and said "please, we don't do that here." he laughed, looked at the other barista and said, "she just asked about wifi." the other barista then laughed. WTF?! this is a collegetown is it not?! my boyfriend also told me that the baristas made a sweet old man feel embarrassed about asking for sweetener instead of sugar. they're just a tag team of awful - the one who wears the hat and the vest, and the one with an accent. 

i feel weird saying that i'd rather go to the starbucks less than a block away, over la colombe. even studying at the starbucks (with sofachairs!) is way, way more comfortable than at la colombe. The coffee is definitely expensive, but it is quite good. I can't give this place 4 or 5 stars because the service is just that obnoxious.

I've been here a few times and this is only for the emergency visits.  The first few times for my older son, I have to say that patient care was good. But the last time when I brought my infant in, I wasn't very happy. He had an allergic reaction and was brought in via an ambulance.  They checked vitals and everything and had me strip him down to his diaper.  I was there for a good 5 hours and I wasn't once offered a gown for my infant.  He slept most of the time but he ended up having a fever after a few hours.  Also while he was sleeping I noticed that his lips had turned blue so I had to get the doctor in.  That's when they noticed that his pulse ox wasn't on his little toe.  Thank god he was still okay and he eventually got all his color back. They couldn't figure out what was wrong that his lips were blue.  That experience that day was a big disappointment to me.  Especially since it's the go to hospital for emergencies with kids.

My experience at Edgehill is totally different than the earlier reviews from several years ago. I have a feeling a remodel happened or something or there's just some crankiness in the air. 

The inside of this cafe is comfortable, kind of industrial looking, and a good place to get a latte and tap away on your laptop. I haven't tried them- but they do offer gluten free brownies, cookies, and muffins, which I appreciate.

I like to sit outside in the afternoon, read the paper, and pretend that a certain fake-ass Mexican restaurant isn't mere meters away from me.

Came to Reno for 1 night and a friend suggested to try this place. The building was big and beautiful. I felt like I was at a winery instead.  
There were options to sit outside or inside. We sat inside bc it was slightly hot that day. 
I rated it a 3 because of the food and drinks. We ordered the chicken sandwich which turned out to be tender and juicy. Loved the avocado touch. The side was fries that came with house made ketchup which I loved. You can taste some chunks from the tomatoes. I ordered a Mango IPA which was super smooth compared to regular IPA's. 
What's different here is that the bartender is your server so if the bar is busy, it takes longer for them to come to your table for orders. We didn't know and waited longer than usual before ordering. A friend went up to the bar to order but the bartender had already came to the table. Food came out fast though. 
They served craft beers, cocktails, wine, and hard liquor as this is a distillery too. Wished they sold their crafts in cans though.

Mirko is heaven on earth. My husband and I wanted REAL food last night instead of the junk we usually settle for at chain restaurants. I suggested Mirko because we have lived in Donelson/Hermitage for 3 years and I still haven't tried it! I have fond childhood memories of a local Italian restaurant in Memphis that had a dish with seafood-filled shells covered in Alfredo and baked cheese. That restaurant closed and I have never found anything as good. Mirko is BETTER. I ordered the seafood ravioli with Alfredo and wow. I think I complimented it in between every bite. The ravioli was rich, plentiful, and perfectly cooked. The filling was incredible and I felt like I was eating a luxury meal. The Alfredo sauce was simple and to die for. Absolute perfection. Keep in mind we got takeout! I'm sure eating there is even better! My husband got the Bolognese sauce and I was thankful that he did because I almost ordered the same. We sampled each other's meals and his was just as amazing as mine. Many times you feel like you wasted money when you order pasta at other restaurants. This stuff cannot be replicated at home! It is so so so good. I am so pleased to have found authentic Italian food that blows my childhood Italian restaurant out of the water! I can't wait to eat here again!

Waited 45 minutes before they even offered to take our order. This was after we'd told our waiter we were ready to order and he said he'd "be right back" and then disappeared for twenty minutes. We spoke to the manager who gave us our two beers for free as well as a $10 credit. So - it's probably a nice place, but they've gotta work on training their staff. A lot.

Really great ice cream parlor! Friendly service, delicious treats! Restroom need to be checked regularly though, and the cleanliness of the parlor wasn't to a T but the quality of the ice cream was delicious! Cookies and cream ice cream is gone ! :)

One word to describe this place - AWFUL. I ordered take out from here a few weeks ago. It was a Sunday night, around 7 o'clock. They told me to pick it up in 30 minutes (I ordered a grilled chicken sandwich with lettuce and tomato and Maria's sandwich which consists of prosciutto, mozzarella, and tomato). I thought 30 minutes was a little excessive but figured they were probably busy with dinner service. So I arrive to pick up my food about 35-40 minutes later. Not one car in the parking lot, not one person in the restaurant area and I'm told my food is STILL not ready. I ended up waiting an additional 15 minutes for a piece of grilled chicken and a COLD sandwich. The grilled chicken should not take too long on the grill and the other sandwich didn't even require cooking!! The girl at the front desk was not apologetic at all. The cook came out 3 times to talk/flirt with the girls at the front desk. All around it was very unprofessional. 

So I get home to try my sandwich and was not pleased at all. The grilled chicken sandwich was literally a piece of flavorless chicken served on a hamburger bun. Yes, a hamburger bun. The other sandwich was not for me but I had to try it. Again, flavorless. I will not be going back here ever again. For the record, this was probably my 3rd or 4th time ordering from here only due to the fact that it's right down the street from me, and every time I've had to wait a long time for food and/or the food was not good. I've eaten at the other location in Conshohocken before and have been pleased but this location is horrible. Save your time and order elsewhere.

Finally went to Spasso after being told to by a friend repeatedly.  Went there on a Wednesday night (Dining Under The Stars) in Media.  Service was very fast and waiter was extremely knowledgeable, knew all the ins and outs of the specials, almost as if he cooked them.  Food was delicious, fast and hot, and just the right amount.  Slightly more expensive than your average Italian restaurant but it was worth it.  Will only take reservations for parties of 8 or more.

Wow, really bad gumbo. My partner started with the seafood version, but the seafood tasted old and there was no other flavor to it other than the roux coming through. A very kind waiter exchanged it for the ya-ya, but this too was flavorless! Even the andouille had no flavor whatsoever!  Just more roux taste. We had to abandon it. 
Their famed BBQ shrimp were ok ... flavorful spices mixed into otherwise pure melted butter, how could that be so bad?
Get out of the Quarter and go eat for real.

After reading some of the reviews and a bit of word of mouth I have to stay I'm a bit underwhelmed with Albasha. The food was good, but not great.  I had a falafel sandwich, hummus, and a typical side salad. The falafel themselves were pretty good although slightly overdone. The hummus was solid. The restaurant was clean and looked recently redone. Waitstaff was courteous and helpful.

Overall solid but not exceptional. I might go again because it's closer than Mona's.

The office and staff are so nice! Dr. Cherry is knowledgable, informative, accommodating, caring, and even gentle for me being a 1st timer to chiropractic care. After just 3 weeks of adjustments, I'm doing significantly better! Coming from a career in the medical field, I have to say I am pleasantly pleased with the results and look forward to ongoing care at Cherry Chiropractic! Thanks again Dr. Cherry!

I do not miss this shop every time I'm in Nashville. I love this joint, and while I miss the feel of the old location, the hip, sleek, coolness remains. I especially love the art work of one of the owners--the collage art. She's amazing. I suppose I could be wrong, but this feels like one of the places that sets the tone bar for the cool zone in Nashville. Gimme gimme more, gimme more...

Delicious donuts. Management was helpful in taking an advance order for a large quantity of donuts for our event. Having used Dunkin Donuts the previous year, we will stick with Donut King from now on.

Outstanding public course. From the pro shop to the cart staff to the snack bar, the staff is always pleasant. I don't know how many times we heard "thanks for coming to Prairie View". The course is always in great condition especially considering it's a public facility. Great layout. The back nine is especially beautiful. Reasonably priced for this quality. For price, condition and layout, probably the best around.

Recently purchased a Sonata from this dealership. Have never had such a good experience at a auto dealership. The staff was professional, courteous,  knowledgeable and patient, especially Jonathan Palmisano the salesman, Robert Marjaram the sales manager, and Jordan Harvey the finance manager, and Mike O'Rourke, who helped us leaning the features of the vehicle. I highly recommend this dealership for those in the market for a Hyundai vehicle.
What's to stay absolutely yummy. Best breakfast find yet! Biscuits with honey butter and homemade jams and jells. Just for starters! The rest of my meal just got better.

The best shrimp and grits we had during our stay (not surprising as most of the pics on here are of that meal!) and all round quality food with a home cooked feel.... unlike some of the bigger brunch places in the city. Felt slightly healthier and more organic, green, etc than other places we visited too. The juices helped with our recovery from the night before and was refreshing to see granola, fruit and yoghurt on the menu as a lighter option :)
It's extremely tiny and packed.. and very loud!!! The service was pretty good.. The food was okay, but not anything special! It's BYOB, so that is a plus.

Walked into this hidden gem, my burger was amazing and the service was wonderful. Kristian behind the bar, simply livens up the place and makes you want to stay and have an extra drink. Give it a try, you will enjoy their tasty burgers.... Southwest burger, Woodstock burger and Avocado Burger were all packed with great flavor and cooked to perfection!

I ordered from Toppers - 2 pizzas. One was the Buffalo Chicken and one was the Loaded Tot-zza on 3/23/17. I was so looking forward to the tot-zza pizza and sorely disappointed, other than only ordering bacon on half, there were no variations on the order. However, the pizza arrived with NO chives, NO nacho cheese on top and was only luke warm. It can be warmed, but no nacho cheese and no chives??? Come on! We called to advise them, and the manager said he would send another one then (nice) or a coupon. Well, I had to go to a meeting, so we opted for the coupon. It is 3/31 & a wonderful, dreary day for a TOT pizza. Not sure why it takes so long for a coupon to arrive. We still don't have it. The ladies I shared this pizza with start a diet April 1 and the management won't allow me to have another pizza on the house. Is there no way to keep my name and number and address to ensure I don't get 2 free pizzas? Seems like quite poor customer service. I paid $45.58 for 2 pizzas, delivery and tip. Seems like there could be a better way.

Well thanks to the Kardashians (as well as anyone that has been here) this was on our radar as one of our main stops while we were in New Orleans. We caught it at the perfect time there was plenty of tables and we got those warm, delicious, powdery doughnuts very quickly with a great cup of Café a late. This would be our first stop in New Orleans.

Don't understand why this place has so many stars. I got the simple burger I believe and my boyfriend had the burger with the bacon (forgot the name) but both of us are now sick throwing up our meal. After coming ill after our meal I decided to come onto here to see how the ratings was and it seems some other people have also gotten sick here too. I personally would give it 0 stars. I did not enjoy my meal due to the rudeness I have encountered since the minute I stepped foot into that establishment, it just made my dinner with my boyfriend pretty bad due to neither of us wanting to be there from the attitudes we were receiving from the the hostess and our waitress. Won't be returning and I would recommend for you not to even check this place out. Go to five guys or any other burger establishment and save yourself some money and possibly a very rough trip to the bathroom!

I like this mall but they need to start carrying men's shoes in lower sizes. My feet are finna fall off cuz I had to walk around the mall for 4 hours just tryna find a pair for my queer AF  girlfriend.

This place gives you really big portions for the price. I got the regular plate with chicken kabob, gyros, salad, rice, and hummus. It was so delicious; I was raving about it as my bf and I ate and I'm pretty sure he was ready to leave me because I kept talking. Ha!!!

The employees/servers are super friendly. They won't mind if you don't know what some of the items on the menu are. In fact, they act perfectly happy to answer any questions

The wait time is a bit longer than most, but the food is worth it. I'd recommend not going here if you're in a hurry tho. Or to order ahead of time.

This is definitely going to be my go to spot if I'm not craving anything when going to IV.

Excellent service. We were a large group and our waiter went above and beyond to ensure a great meal.
I had the tortilla soup and it was excellent, the small pieces of avocado made it quite nice.
The red  chili shredded beef was a hit as well as the taquitos!
In a previous visit I had the posole' it's a bit more of a stew here but quite good.
The fact that they limit the free chips to 1 bowl is kinda of sketchy, no Mexican restaurant I have ever been to has ever charged for a refill of chips, So there's that as a negative.  .
But overall the food is good and the service is great!

Would give Ted Drewes 6 stars is possible. It truly lives up to its ranking as 'World's Best Ice Cream.' I took my sister here when she was visiting me in St. Louis, and she was at a loss of words of how to describe it. It's different than any other ice cream or custard I have tasted - it is soft and light while still being thick and creamy, and the mix-ins are high quality and work together well. 

Ted Drewes is a must for anyone in St. Louis, even if you are just driving through.

Went there for lunch before they moved locations and myself and husband were pretty impressed.  Just think about how excited we were to hear that they were now open for breakfast at their new location! 

We visited there on a Sunday morning for breakfast.  Husband isn't home that much due to work so we wanted to enjoy a sit down breakfast together before running our errands for the day and thought we would try out the new breakfast menu (Belgian waffle with side of bacon for me and Disco Ball for my husband).  Walked in to no line at all and placed our order at the counter.  Went around to pay, grab our fruit tea, and took a seat.  We looked around and noticed what appeared to be a couple people (I'm assuming at this point) ordered food after their group did.  Didn't really think anything of it.  After approx. 20 mins, my name is called. They put my Belgian waffle down (no sign of side of bacon) and tell us that my husband's meal is right behind them.  My husband didn't want my food to get cold so told me to go ahead without him.  I ate my ENTIRE waffle and he still didn't have his food.  Plates were slowly making their way from the kitchen to the other people's tables. My husband still waiting for his.  I finally go to the counter and ask about his plate.  They hand me a plate that was sitting on the counter and says "Breakfast takes longer to cook."  Ummmmmmmmm....ok..  They didn't seem apologetic in the slightest even though I told them that I've already finished my breakfast.  I took his plate to him and went back up for my side of bacon.  He literally finished his food before my side of bacon was brought to the table.  His food was cold and the look of the meat on his plate was questionable.  The quiche was pretty good though!

Needless to say, our planned nice sit down breakfast together turned out to be far from our expectations which included a price tag of $30.  If you go for breakfast and plan to eat TOGETHER...you may want to take a snack to eat while others in your party enjoy their plates one by one.

We were visiting the town of West Chester for a College visit and found this very nice nice restaurant while were were there.

Upon our arrival an hour after it had opened for dinner, the bar was packed (on a Friday). The hostess asked if we had a reservation which we did not, but she did find seating in the back of the restaurant (highly recommend making a reservation). The air vents were prevalent which resulted in us asking for a change of seating due to the "climate". Some people even covered the air vents with a menu! They were very accommodating and found us a better table in the front of the restaurant.

We ordered, as appetizers, mussels and clams oreganato. The entrees included Chicken Parmagiana, Fusilli Bolognese, and Braised Short Ribs Ravioli. 

Appetizers
Mussels - Frenchman's Cove style mussels in a Fra Diablo sauce. They were very good. The sauce was outstanding. There was also an Italian hot pepper at the bottom of the dish; a pleasant surprise.

Clams Oreganato - My son, who has never had clams before, loved this. Though we thought it was going to be some kind of stuffed shell, it was much closer to a sautéed clams dish in another outstanding sauce.

Entrees
Fusilli Bolognese - Pasta was homemade. Just the right amount of meat was in the sauce. I was very well pleased with it.

Chicken Parmagiana - Chicken was pounded out very thin (scallopini style) and had just the right amount of cheese, rather than the overwhelming amount I typically encounter.

Braised Short Ribs Ravioli - Raviolis contained not just plenty of short rib but also a surprise of mozzarella. This was sautéed with vegetables, such as mushrooms, peppers, etc. In the third a final outstanding sauce.

Dessert
Cannoli - Freshly filled. Enough said.

Overall, it is a very small eating area that filled up very quickly. Wait staff was attentive, but clearly trying to turn over tables due to the lack of seating (so expect to eat and go). There is an open pizza area in the front of the restaurant where they are cooking and I did observe an employee eating in the cooking area. The food was great with plenty of homemade ingredients. The sauces stole the show.

What a very pleasant first visit! I was in the area for an extended period of time (I am stationed in Fort Lauderdale normally) and Yelp'ed Craft beers. This place appeared on my search.

Off the beaten path of Main Street in Safety Harbor's downtown area, I arrived with a family member on a weekday night. It was trivia night, and the place was pretty crowded.

I had an IPA, which has been my go-to beer choice recently. The folks behind the bar were very helpful, and the local patrons friendly. One gentleman in particular bought us a round, which was kind. We privately joked that this would never happen in Fort Lauderdale. I have always theorized that the Gulf side of Florida is friendlier than South Florida for reasons like this. 

This place is large in size and has an outdoor portion. The beer is terrific. Good atmosphere, too. I love Craft beer!
I could leave it at the have Salvadorian pupusas, but the staff was also super friendly as well!
This place has gone downhill in cleanliness. Who wants to do their was in a dirty place?? Owner needs to get on this.

Terrible experience. Waited over an hour for our food when the restaurant was empty then waited an additional 45 minutes to get the check. We asked them to split our check four ways (like it says on the menu) and gave a written breakdown of each check. The waitress came back with one large check after we gave her a breakdown of the bill TWICE. Then she proceed to complain about having to divide the checks. We asked for itemized copies several times and never got them. Good food but terrible experience

This place was a super surprise for me, and I love it when a restaurant exceeds your expectations!

My wife and I were running around on Saturday, and both became extremely hungry.  We just wanted quick Mexican food, and I had thought that this location was once a chain-fast-food place that we liked.  Well, when we got there, we saw the "Nato's Mexican Food" sign, and we just went for it.  We'll, we were not disappointed.

I ordered a taco and enchilada lunch combination, and my wife requested a chicken burrito.  Now, for all we knew, this could just be Americanized Mexican Food, but we were pleasantly surprised to have what felt like authentic Mexican family food.  As I watched the cook in the back, in my mind I said, "His name must be Nato, and his wife is running the front counter".  They were a cute couple, (and in the story in my mind) running the family business.  

The flavors of the sauces and the spices were delicious.  The beef in the taco was seasoned wonderfully, and all the veggies tasted fresh.  My wife's burrito had a unique flavor.  It was huge, and stuffed with more chicken than I thought was possible in one tortilla.  The place was clean, the service was great, as the folks there were super friendly.  To add to the atmosphere, European soccer was playing on the TV, and I got to see one guy get pushed over and he slipped and fell on the grass, and cried and screamed like a baby for about 20 minutes before he finally got back up and into the game. (Actually, I love the game of soccer, but I always laugh at the drama.. ) For a quick, cheap, lunch, it was just great.



[  There are 10 kinds of people in the world.  Those who understand binary, and those who do not.  ]

Had a wonderful time at the Peppermill Hotel Casino this past weekend. Went for a convention being held there. Had a small issue with our room but Mike at the front desk took care of it right away! The buffet is incredible to say the least and the hotel and casino were beautiful. We did not have a chance to use the pool or spa services but look forward to trying them out next time.

The economy rooms are o.k. but for a few dollars more, I suggest upgrading to the newer rooms.

Thank you Mike for taking such great care of us.
These tacos .. people.. we ordered the shrimp tacos, the chronic sandwich and a side of pork belly. We can't wait to go back.

Thought I'd update ... installed the control board myself ... not too difficult. The job took me about 2 hours ... one to map the wiring, 30 min to gather confidence, 30 min to wire. If I were a contractor, I would guess about one hour needed with travel time. I'm sticking with the my original impression about the contractor's quote.

really good, fresh, latin-influenced cocktails.

thought the service could have been better. Food was good, but overpriced. My date got the carnitas tacos...they needed a little sauce or kick.

(3.75 Stars) Unique name, not so unique food. Fresh and healthy are the first two words that come to mind when I think of their food. This food truck strictly does sandwich wraps. The natural flavors of the ingredients are on the forefront and not over-powered or masked by heavy sauces. My friend got one of the vegan wraps "Primo Vegetarian". It has sauteed Veggies, mixed Greens, cous cous, Daiya vegan cheese, and "Zoink" sauce. I tried "The Scallywag" which has seared scallops, snow Peas, mushrooms, cous cous, parmesan cheese, and lemon champagne sauce. All of the ingredients were cooked well, super fresh, and the light champagne sauce brought everything together.

While everything was fresh, it took waaaaaaay too long to get the food... much longer than a wrap should take. On the plus side - the food is good and healthy as opposed to a lot of food trucks where you feel like you need to add an extra couple hours on the treadmill the next day. HOWEVER, is it worth the wait? I personally don't think so because it's not a new concept, it's not mind-blowingly delicious and it's not difficult to prepare. I overheard so much chatter from others while waiting for the food about how it takes so long and it really shouldn't because of what it is. Though they're in a that special category of healthy eating that tastes good, if they don't improve customer satisfaction with speed and in creativity to excite the taste buds, it will be difficult for them to survive in the Tampa Food Truck scene that is constantly growing with new and unique food. Overall, this review is more of a knock against the service, not the food. While I don't have any real complaints about the food, I don't have anything emphatically positive either.

My friend and I came in quick to do our nails. We are visiting family from New York and New Jersey where it can be pretty pricey with no pay off. The ladies here did a great job and were very sweet to us. I LOVE how my nails turned out. Can't stop looking at them. We will definitely come again whenever we are back in the area!

Reservation was booked online a month before my trip. All emails and communication between me and the business said everything was set up, paid for and taken care of. Arrive in St. Louis at 5am take the shuttle to their location (which was a 20 minute wait for a shuttle) gets there and the lady behind the desk was rude. Had no idea of my reservation. Put a huge hold on my credit card tried to up sell me for all these extras. Caused my card to decline and then tells me because it declined her she couldn't run it again. I had to go to another rental car company because of this. Not only was this my first time in St. Louis, not knowing where I was or how to get anywhere else the lady sent me walking up the street to Avis...... not professional and not helpful at all.

I didn't think this place was anything special. And in my opinion it's a little expensive (good thing I had a groupon).
Their california rolls are $6....which is pretty expensive for a california roll is you ask me. I should be able to make a meal out of two california rolls and still be under $10. So I didn't order one. Decided to go big or go home instead (their fancy roll prices are more along the lines of what i'd be willing to pay).
Got a caterpillar roll ($11) and a snow roll($10.50). They are average sized rolls. The caterpillar roll kind of tasted like nothing. And the snow roll barely had any crab on top. C'mon guys. If I'm paying 10.50 for a crab-based roll I'm expecting to have the amount of crab on top of it actually cover the rice.
I also got the spicy tuna salad appetizer (I think that's what its called...don't remember the exact name). I think it was the most flavorful, delicious part of the meal. But for almost $9 you get a lot of salad and not very much tuna. The tuna is very good though.
I got a complementary miso soup and salad. Miso soup was good....but I'm not sure how you can mess up miso soup. And the salad was just a salad. They were free and tasted like one would expect them to taste, so no complaints there.
Drink-wise, I saw they had a hemingway daiquiri on the menu and this is only the 2nd place I've seen that actually knows what that is! So I had to order it ($7) because it also happens to be my favorite drink thanks to TGI Friday's deliciously fruity/slightly bitter hemingway daiquiri. Maybe I was spoiled by TGI....but I don't like tasting the alcohol in my mixed drinks and I like my hemingway to be fruitier than it is bitter. I definitely tasted the alcohol in this one...and the bitterness. So I was really disappointed.
Service was also average. Things got cleared off relatively quickly. The server was pleasant. The thing that irked me was that I was eating by myself (so had nothing to eat nor anyone with whom to chitchat) and I waited around for a while until my server brought me my check and then some more until she picked up my credit card to take my money. When I ask for a check and have no food left in front of me I'm ready to go home and don't want to be sitting around for 10 more minutes. She wasn't awful, but I've had better.
All in all....in my opinion their simple roll prices are on the high end, fancy roll prices are average, their fancy rolls are average or skimpy, size of rolls is average, spicy tuna salad is delicious but skimpy, hemingway daiquiri is not what i was expecting at all, and service is average. Everything is kind of average...so they get a 3.

Ok, this place is multifaceted. It is a great spot for spring breakers (day or night)...as well as regular beach-going people, or tourists looking for a good breakfast, lunch or dinner.

I've been for spring break, and if thats when you go.. be prepared for crowds, lots of good live music on the beachbar.  They have a nice nightclub 'The Wave' that gets packed late at night. Only bad thing, it boots everyone out at 1:30am. Perfect timing for after-hours in our hotel I guess!

They have a nice indoor restaurant as well..with a large buffet. On the weekends that prices are higher (but you get more)..like wafffles, etc.
I've had the lunch and breakfast buffets during the week (cheaper) as well as the wknd, and loved both. This restaurant turns into a nice bar at night, with a dance area as well. Good spot. 

We have a place in the area, and never miss coming to Shephards. Go during the day for ppl watching, and nighttime for drinks and dancing. Clearwater needs more of these!
Very fast, price was a bit high but I guess that'll teach me a lesson on losing my rental keys. The locksmith was a very nice guy.

How can it be that this place is around 2 years old, peeps here on yelp mentioning their name in other reviews, yet not having a review of their own? A little strange, to say the least. Well, here's their 1st review and from a Californian nonetheless, strange, right? 

An ambitious restaurant in a business-park zoned area made it a strange find. Upon entering however you're presented with a sleek, modern interior worthy of a romantic date. Curved, deep maroon walls flow throughout the space making the seating arrangement interesting. A far eastern touch is present as the larger tables had a marble lazy susan to spin your dishes to be served family style, nice looking but very cumbersome to spin. Metal chain mail see- through 
curtains separate the larger tables and is actually effective in providing a sense of separation from other diners. 

The service is western style with personable servers who pays attention to detail with wine service, verbal specials announcements and a comfy warm towel service at the end of the meal. The food is primarily Americanized Chinese food presented in a more stylish manner, real similar to PF Changs, only it taste more authentic. There is also a separate sushi bar area which can get quite busy but sushi can be ordered from the tables in the dining room. So an upscale Chinese restaurant, that serves up legit sushi to order, a full bar and respectable wine list with effective service, did I already say that Jazmine is one ambitious restaurant. The good thing is that they actually pull it off, definitely restaurant people in this independently owned restaurant, a gem of a find. 

5 of us ordered family style which started with a small nigiri selection from the sushi bar which included maguro (yellowfin tuna), saba (cured mackerel) and shiro maguro (albacore). All were very legit and priced properly and served with a little modern flair with flecked scallions on the saba and a dot of sriacha on the albacore. We also ordered shrimp siu mai which were large, juicy and delicious and probably one of the best I've had, and I'm from the Bay Area where dim sum joints are plentiful. So the mixture of Japanese sushi and Chinese dumplings as appetizers were an absolute treat, especially with our Columbia Valley Gewurtztraminer, now where else can one start a meal that way? Not many places in my experiences. 

Chinese entrees we shared were: 

Ginger Scallion Beef ($14)Properly textured beef with present ginger and scallion flavors, good rendition. 

Braised Tofu with Black Mushrooms and Vegetables ($12)Okay with the tofu being deep fried then braised. I may have preferred it not fried. Presented in a claypot which was nice. 

Szechuan Snapper ($14) Fillet of Pacific Snapper in a thickish spicy brown sauce. Fish was just ok but drowning in the gloopy sauce. A bad pick in my opinion. 

XO Dried Sauted String Beans ($12) Very properly executed with a little ground pork and garlic, shriveled yet firm beans with just enough sauce to get absorbed into the beans but not pool on the bottom of the dish. 

With some steamed white rice this proved to be a perfect amount for 5 hungry adults. Even though we were all satisfied with the meal thus far we still decided to indulge in a sampling of some dessert with some tea. I mean we were trying to set the tone for the up and coming new year, so bring it on. 

A Coconut Dream Cake was well...dreamy. Very moist layered white cake with a soft coconut cream between the layers was perfect with hot tea. 

A cheesecake which was described as a cherry cheesecake gave me an image of cherries being in the cake but on arrival it was just basic New York cheesecake with that traditional cherry filling topping. Though a decent rendition it was just too ordinary for me. 

A huge dinner for 5 with wine came out to about $130, which is definitely not a bad way to sample a multitude of dishes from different cultures in an upscale setting. To say the least, I'll be back here to celebrate if ever I wanna celebrate up here in Reno. Jazmine is a good find.
Love the brick oven pizza. Always nice to sit outside in the warmer months on their patio.

If you're going to eat at a conveyor belt sushi place, go during peak hours so that the offerings are fresher and more diverse. If you wait until after the peak, you'll end up seeing the same 30 dishes spinning around. 

Mondays at Yo! Are blue plate days, where everything on the belt is $3.50. This can be a great deal if you want to sample a lot of items. 

The sushi is passable. If I hadn't been around International Plaza with a hankering for sushi, I wouldn't have come here. Nothing was bad, but nothing was especially remarkable. 

I tried their ramen, and the tempura was good, but the broth was missing something. It felt too light, yet was quite salty. 

Service was excellent.

Long wait but great staff!  They just roll with the crowds.  I'm not necessarily a pancake lover so I'm definitely not their target market.  Lots of variety in pancakes!  Hashbrowns were okay, nice and crispy but need salt and pepper.  I had the sweet potato pancakes, very good and recommended with the cinnamon syrup.  Had a bite of the santa fe pancakes.  A bit weird for me, didn't love the sweet/savory combo.
I have had a couple more meals since writing my initial review and they were definitely improved, but they still need to make the overall experience better.

I read the reviews on Yelp and decided to check out Bricks of Ybor for myself. 

Nice atmosphere and hip music playing in the background. I sat at the bar and watched the flat screen televisions (they were playing the History Channel on one TV. & "Shaun of the Dead" on another TV.). 

Good beer on tap (I tried the IPA -- it was good) and a small menu specializing in appetizers, salads & sandwiches. I ordered the hummus plate and the iceberg wedge salad -- both were delicious. The blue cheese dressing on the salad was particularly scrumptious. 

For one beer and an app and a salad, my bill came to just under $25 before tip -- kinda expensive (considering they no longer serve the "salmon spread" on the hummus plate -- should that really be priced at $10, still?).
