The Greek salad was ok but they didn't even have Greek dressing. You can do way better than this place... Trust me!

best most authentic indian food in town.  unless you want to nyc!  this place beats all.  love the deconstructed samosas.  the mango lassi and kulfi is soooo good.  try the rotli as well.  it comes with some of the dishes.  i love it!

You can always find good deals at Marshall's. Their customer service is good, but nothing to write home about. Merchandise is normally clean and organized. They recently update their cash registers, making it easier and more efficient for check outs,

The Gaslight Theatre is one of those places I'd been told that I "HAD to try" ever since we moved to Tucson. It's just that dinner theater + audience participation + parody shows didn't sound all that appealing to me. I imagined a corny type of production where I'd sit dreading not to be called up on stage or something. 
It was sooooooo much fun! A group I knew was going and some last minute tickets became available. They called me up and asked, so I figured I'd finally give it a try. The place itself is kind of small. Expect to be a bit crowded, but it adds to the audience participation effect. The show we caught was The Three Musketeers. The whole family can enjoy this kind of show! The actors' ad-lib was hilarious and quite enjoyable to me as well as my kids who thought it was silly. 
The food is OK, but we didn't go there for a fine dining experience. We had some fries, some drinks and ice cream. They bring out popcorn and then they bring out popcorn and then they bring out popcorn. You get the picture. Overall, it was great fun for the whole family. We were told the next show will be a Phantom of the Opera parody, so now I'm looking forward to that!

Tried this place out after looking for somewhere that makes good philly cheesesteak. It was not the best it was just ok. It didn't quite cut it. Also tried there baffalo chicken and it was kind of nasty . I was really looking foward to eating them but it had a weird taste to it. Will not return .

Vinny , Tony, Lindsay , Anne, Mark ... in fact everyone at Heavenly Nails do excellent work and everyone makes you feel special!  Great people who do a fabulous job!!!   I Would not  go anywhere else! Thank you!!!

Went with a large group last night and got to try a little bit of everything.  I personally ordered four tacos and was impressed with both the quality and quantity of food for the price.  I think we actually lucked out that it was so busy on a Friday night, it gave us a chance to hang out at the bar and try some cool cocktails.  

High Points:
Great street taco options
Unique and very fresh cocktails
Fantastic guacamole
Attentive and knowledgeable wait staff

I'm always on the lookout for a good pizza place and since we were headed to the Eskimos/Riders game, it seemed like the perfect opportunity to check this place out! 

When we arrived it was PACKED, but thankfully we didn't have to wait (at all). The restaurant is quite large and there were a lot of Saskatchewan Roughrider fans (myself included) enjoying a meal before the game.

I ordered a coffee and we got a large 3 meat pizza. Unfortunately with it being so busy, my coffee cup sat empty for awhile. The pizza arrive in a reasonable amount of time, fresh from the oven & piping hot. 

The pizza was very good, no complaints! I loved the chewy crust with the crispy/cheese edge. There were a decent amount of toppings, tasty sauce and lots of cheese. Perfect.

Our waitress was extremely busy, but took the time to compliment my Rider jersey and apologized for being so busy. She was very sweet and was clearly busting her ass to trying to do a good job. 

While we were waiting for our food I saw a lot of delicious food coming from the kitchen. The steak & shrimp looked delish! We definitely plan on returning to try a few other items on the menu!

After a day on the road we really didn't feel like going out of the hotel for a bite and drink so we tried this place.  Dark and small, but with comfy couches and chairs and different sizes of tables to fit whatever mood you're in.  Friendly bartender and servers, but the bartender was our server and as the place got busier she didn't tell the other servers to check on us so wait time was a bit long.  The drinks were good and strong, a little pricey, but understood as it's in a hotel.  Were good about us taking our drinks to our room when we were ready.  The menu is small, but it was tasty and filling.  I wouldn't hesitate to come back the next time I'm in town.

Philadelphia has decent tacos but these tacos won me over and created and new level of possible taco yumminess in Philly. 
All of the margaritas were good, but my favorite there so far is the prickly pear margarita. It tastes VERY good paired with certain tacos. 

My favorite taco: Shrimp taco, i could eat so many.

my favorite parts about going here that makes this food place stands far above the rest
- their desire to please the customer: beer while you wait in line? now thats what the customer wants
- choices for people who love authentic tacos but also choices for people in your group who are picky eaters 
- margaritas are delicious
- you do not have to carry your food to you table 
- quick and easy because it takes out the time waiting for a server to come and take your order
- adult friendly
- family friendly

people say the tacos are tiny portions but seriously i ate two and was stuffed. My boyfriend who is obviously larger than I am ate three and was full so i find that incorrect because it was the perfect amount for us. I recently brought my sister here who used to live in Philly to Buena Onda and she was so happy to find a place to go with her friends and boyfriend when she visit. 

The staff is also incredibly nice. thats refreshing because i have been to places with great food but the staff wasnt friendly so it made me and my party never go back. staff really does contribute to the customers overall experience. 

I waited a couple visits to rate this place. Overall this is my rating.

I love this place

Visited August 2015

I will try to give a synopsis of an amazingly over-the-top Italian Dining Event that I recently "experienced" at Mangia (Mohn'-zjuh). Chef, owner - Nick Pellegrino.

Wow, first, go hungry, but not so much so that you will faint; hint, if you hit the movies the afternoon of the same evening you'll hit Mangia, eating popcorn or other movie snacks is not a good plan.... Second, drink lots of water all thru the day of your evening date at Mangia, you'll be so glad you did, more on that later!) Third, definitely review the menu before you go ("like" them on fb), yes, you'll begin to salivate in anticipation - AND... it will help you know what kinds of wines to bring as it is BYOB (if you are stumped here, then take a copy of the menu to your local wine geek). Fourth, once you are there, seated and getting excited about this evening of homemade Italian dining, don't fill up on the bread. (They'll tell you that, and do listen to your server!) Fifth, prepare yourself for a long, loud, fun, food-fest filled with music, singing, dancing, and an intermission! You'll need it, we all did, at almost 75 people,  the place was almost entirely filled to their seating max. Further, if you go on a Friday evening (seating doesn't happen until 8:00), tell your sitter you'll be home late, as in 'close to midnight late', this is a full-tilt, multi-course event. And everyone gets to eat a little or a lot of everything on the menu. So, you do get serious bang for your $45 bucks/person (plus tax & tip, plus $5/bottle of wine as their corkerage fee, very reasonable - do be sure your server knows how to open the wines, tho, not kidding; ours struggled, for various reasons, but at least we did get bottle opened, finally).  

When you arrive, you're welcomed by Nick, Chef & Owner, then directed to your table. You'll notice that the table is fully set w/all dishes, glasses, etc. (a tip to Mangia, please use black napkins, the white is all over the black slacks! -eek!), for the wine, smart choice - small glasses juice glasses! nice touch! The servers bring and explain every dish, one was even brought to our table by Chef Nick! Here's the thing, this food service doesn't happen fast but gradually throughout the evening. The food unfolds, you eat, drink, talk, over & over, course after course. Word to the wise: take your time, don't over stuff, it isn't worth it. If you taste something and it's just "okay" take a few more bites then stop..something else will wow you even more!

At one point, about mid-event & before the main courses were served, Chef Nick took to the microphone to welcome all & explain we would take a short break, right then. This was a smart move, we were all getting kinda full by then - so more dancing and singing ensued (to the Italian and oldies selection, a great mix, many sung by Italian artists, of course, from Dean Martin to Frank Valli) playing thru the sound system. At this point in the evening, Mangia officially becomes a very loud place...imagine we could be heard all the way to Hillsboro Road!

Pointers to Mangia - please get some whole pepper grinders to have at the ready when requested, 'twould be so the nice touch. I was rather surprised when I asked for one to find that none were present. Also, no salt & shakers on any table, at all, learned later that typical Italian meals do not require such ergo they're not on table & it could be an insult to ask for same (oops!!)...not needed by & large, using some of the freshly grated Pecorino helped...but....read on - to Mangia:, please salt the pasta water for the shells (used with the short rib bolognese), it really needs it, also shells were watery and had not even a hint of EVOO...(the meat sauce wasn't flavorful, which was sad...I kept trying to find it, the flavor that is. Possibly the beef had not been salted prior to cooking?) The pasta with the citrus cream sauce was amazing, divine, I could eat that again right now. The orange zest (right?) was a fabulous touch! The other best dish was the rosemary lemon chicken, very tasty! The freshly made-that-morning-sausage with fennel was rich and moist, if a bit too fennel-y.

Oh yeah, why drink a lot of water all that day? Because you will likely be sipping a lot of wine that evening...even if sipping water, too, that eve, you will be glad to be so well  hydrated in advance of your Italian dining, sipping & singing event!

All in all, the crowning touch was the wee brown bag given to us as we departed, holding xxx sugar and two, fresh, hot Italian "dough-nuts", or Zeppole. The plan: shake 'em in the sugar and enjoy, which I did, both of them..oh my so very good...as in melt-in-your-mouth (the watermelon granita served prior to these sweet goodies was refreshing, but too sweet!)

Yes, go to Mangia, IF you can get in! I was really fortunate to get a place for myself and my pal...we both agreed we would enjoy going again (when they change their menu) with a small group of friends and fellow foodies!

Enjoyed dinner on the back patio after a sunset viewing on the pier a couple blocks away. 

Ordered the Mega Mary for an app, and my wife and I split it. Granted, it wasn't the right time for it, but we just had to try it. Glad we did, they make their own mix and topped it with a strip of bacon, a pickled string bean, and two bleu cheese stuffed olives. Their cocktail selections were great. In fact, they had an entire page for just martinis. 

Ordered the local ravioli with chicken and the filet with kale and sweet potatoes for our mains. Got the chowder which was great, not the creamiest but I'm okay with that. The mains were very tasty and rather large...probably too large for one person. The steak was cooked to perfection. 

As if we weren't stuffed enough, we had to order another cocktail for dessert, can't remember the name but it had vanilla ice cream and tasted like a milk shake. 

The wait staff was attentive and friendly as well. You can't lose of you choose this place in Dunedin.

While technically I live in walking distance to this new frozen yogurt spot, it requires me to cross Gravois on foot and then avoid the panhandlers that greet all visitors to Soulard at Midwest Petroleum.  I have a four year old so I put the kiddo in the car and drove 4 blocks. I forgot it was Saturday night and almost changed my mind when travelling all of one block down Russel into the island  I had already been cut off by a golf cart driven by a native and then dealt with all those Honda Accords from the county unloading their passengers in the bike lane in front of McGurks.  When we got to the shop there was no parking so I went off roading in that big elevated lot right next door(I don't know if you are supposed to park there, but we did).

Lots of people outside enjoying their purchases, good sign.  Get inside and it is really nicely done.  Tropical decor of course, a wall of machines and a nice little topping bar area.  8 unique flavors, root beer float, key lime pie, cheesecake, acai berry, cake, that is all I can remember.  We got root beer float and key lime pie.  I added some coconut and then my daughter teed off on the topping bar.  Cherries, sprinkles, chocolate chips, all I could see were mounting ounces to be added to our bill.  I blacked out.  I somehow managed to get our two selections to the weigh station/cash register.  $5.50, what a deal! I immediately came to and we happily ate our dessert outside(which was delicious). 

A happy addition to the island I spend a lot of time on!

Delicious roast beef sandwich and glass of Pinot Grigio. If you like extra sharp provolone or even if you are open to trying it or you enjoy sharp provolone or even provolone- GET THE SANDWICH WOTH EXTRA SHARP PROVOLONE!!! It's delicious and you won't regret. Some couple got us all free drinks (apparently they give free drinks out when they come here because we did not know them and the bartender confirmed we didn't know them and that they just but free drinks). Anyways delicious food. The cheese is perfection. And the bartender (who has an uncanny resemblance to a Breaking Bad character - if you have seen the show go check it out ) was very nice. Since I believe in 20% tip minimum I put another $10 tip down (slyly) on top of the $14 left for the $77 dollar check - for multiple beers, one glass of wine, sodas and 6 roast beef sandwiches - 4 with extra sharp provolone cheese. Try it on a weeknight (Monday) between 8pm and 9 pm - that's when I went and service and food was quick and exceptional ... And I was in a bad, pissed off mood so that says a lot :)

The concept here is awesome.  I love how many people this event brings together throughout Philadelphia, and I loved even more that it came to my hood (Fairmount, yo).  

The wide variety of food trucks serving up treats can satisfy any palate, however the trucks I wanted to go to the most had lines that were borderline ridiculous.  Not sure what the fix for this would be... perhaps I need to show up 10 minutes before opening to secure a good spot in line? 

Anywho... The live bands were great and created a perfect summer kick-off ambiance (the 80+ degree weather didn't hurt either), and it was really awesome to see so many Philadelphians (Fairmounters and Non-Fairmounters alike) congregated in one place to celebrate Philly's finest food trucks.

The location was great for Fairmount too, since if you were sick of waiting in the beer line you could very easily pop into the local Wine & Spirits shop for a juicebox of wine, or pop into one of the restaurants for a drink.

Alas--my only complaint is that the lines were out of control.  Somehow my friends and I managed to go home hungry from the food fair, but that's probably due to our impatience.

OK, went for brunch yesterday. Good but needs some improvement: The biscuits are amazing and buttery, but slightly underdone. Sausage in the grits was overcooked so the texture was hard. Hashbrowns looked awesome, but found the insides to be oxidized and undercooked. The over medium eggs were just shy of over hard. 

All that being said: the grits themselves were beautifully creamy and delicious. The burger was as good as during a previous dinner service. Crawfish omelette was rated "excellent" by fellow diners. Coffee is also really good!

Service is awesome! Hayden and Tim are super cool and attentive!

So, after hearing much about Hendricks BBQ, my wife and I decided to try it out tonight.  We were seated very quickly, and then were largely ignored for 10 minutes.  After seeing another table get seated and have their order taken immediately, I decided to talk to the management.  I talked to the manager on duty, and he told us that he was sorry that we were ignored and wanted to make it right.  Right then, the bartender, Nick, said he'd be happy to serve us right now if we wanted.  We said sure, let's give it one more shot.  We placed our order and the food came out piping hot and delicious, very quickly.  the chef, Marc, also came out to make sure that we were taken care of.  I told them all that I understand glitches with employees, and that they totally made up for it in the long run, both with the service we ultimately received, and the quality of food. The only reason this isn't a 5 star review is due to the initial problem.  We do plan on going back often, and giving them another chance to make this a 5 star review.  I want to thank them all, including the manager on duty, whose name unfortunately escapes me at the moment.  Thanks again, gentlemen!  it was fantastic!

Are trip didn't start well when walking in and a lady was returning a pizza. She claimed It was the worst pizza she ever had. (she wasn't far off)! It was editable at best, the fries where cold, and no taste to them at all. I had got a calzone which was full of ricotta and pineapple but not mozzarella. The pineapple taste like the can it came in and the marinara sauce on the side was uneatable. I would never go there again.

Veronika, her daughter, her husband and the rest of the staff @ Brummis are wondeful, as is every one of the 10-12 menu items I have sampled @ the place.  Go.

eh

We had lunch here last week and really enjoyed it. Service was quite friendly and the items we ordered had great flavor and high quality. We sat outside and enjoyed the shade the building offers during lunch hours. They'll validate your parking too so take advantage of the garage for sure!

Oh...and not sure I totally want to share this tip, LOL...they sell Vincent Van Doughnuts here.

Visited the orchid show with my 2 year old and it was a great time! wish there were more golf carts to transport us with small children from the museum to the greenhouse. We went on a first Thursday = free admission! some of the Lilly house is being renovated until May, so we didn't get to go upstairs and the pop up shop with the Orchids was double the price of Home Depot ones (which I purchased from Home Depot when I left lol) Can't wait until the Beer Garden opens at the end of this month!

Easily the worst Wingstop I've ever been to. Slow slow slow slow, workers on phones or joking and laughing with each other instead of working. Place needs serious help. Some guy walked in that knew the worker and they grabbed my wings and gave Em to him without thinking I'd notice. Absolute joke.

If I'm being totally honest I can't properly articulate how meaningful an establishment Blues City Deli is. Many might argue that the past fifty or so years have not been kind to the city of St. Louis, but just in the past decade (coincidentally the same amount of time Vince Valenza's BCD has been open) there's been a notable change in this city, and Blues City Deli has come to represent this transformation using everyone's favorite medium: sensational sandwiches. 

Star 1: How were the service and atmosphere?

While I hear there are often (and rightfully so) lines out the door at Blues City Deli, I strolled in with a buddy on a Saturday afternoon and was blown away right from the get go. Maybe thirty or forty people were seated, sandwiches in hand, watching and listening to live Blues fill the room and spill out onto the street. The atmosphere was vibrant, the crowd was into it, the band was into it, and the whole experience lit up the whole block. In other news, I ordered the Aporkalypse Pretzelwich that I'd scoped on instagram, grabbed my Fitz's root beer, and awaited the glory while basking in the culture of a city. Star Granted. 

Star 2: How were the portions relative to the cost?

I'd be lying if I told you I remembered the exact price of my pretzelwich, but honestly who cares. The sandwiches at BCD are all priced comparably, and they're priced fairly given what are generous portions. My sandwich was a beast, and I left satisfied without a hole in my wallet. Star Granted. 

Stars 3 and 4: How was the food?

I could probably just list the ingredients of my sandwich (shaved pork, bacon, cheese, optional pickles, and a not at all optional sauce on a pretzel roll) and have you in a fit of hunger, but I'll add some commentary in saying that the sandwich was brilliant in just about every way. 

To top that off, all of the other sandwiches around me looked equally tasty as did the cookies and other treats. Well done. Dual Stars Granted. 

Star 5: Would you eat here every day if you could?

Our lives are stitched together with snapshots both cultural and culinary, and you can get both at Blues City Deli. Star Granted.

Three of us had dinner here before the Philly pops concert. I am being generous giving them 3 stars.  I had a glass of wine for 12 bucks. We all shared a potato pancake appetizer. It was delicious but since we had no forks we had to wait forever for the waitress to notice. Actually, one of the managers helped us.  I had the meatlloaf platter. The meatloaf was good, but the gravy was reall really sweet. My dining partners had a turkey club and the other had a cheeseburger. There was nothing special about the food and the service was poor. They just too busy. With only one glass of wine the check was 70.00. We could have had the same dinner at Oregon diner for half the price.
Carnitas tacos were good, chips and salsa were cheap (delicious too), nice atmosphere. I'd recommend it to my friends and colleagues.

A group of us (eight people) were looking for a place to have lunch on a rainy Saturday afternoon.  We were a bit worried about getting in somewhere - so we decided on Spinners since they took reservations!  We were seated right away.  It's take a full hour to make it all the way around - and it took a few in our group a bit to get used to it.  The food and service were great - and the view was fantastic!  I would definitely recommend!
Great place.  We drove away after seeing line out the door, but came back it was worth the wait!!!

Excellent food, excellent service! What an amazing staff. We came in during Mardi gras at happy on the parade route. The resturant was sooooo busy, they had every excuse to drop the ball but instead Amili (sp) and Jamie made us feel so special. They treated us like kings and queens. They made my 80 year old, old man feel special for his 1st Mardi Gras. Hats of the ownership and leadership of this super AWESOME resturant, your commitment to quality and service excellence is refreshing. Shout out to the most amazing bar staff in all of NOLA, you guys are awesome. Definitely, the highlight of the trip. We'll be back.
Scratch made food. Fresh ideas on traditional meals. Friendly staff and reasonably priced . Nice stop!
Simple and yummy breakfast. Really liked the variety of fresh squeezed juices and smoothies. The crab cake benedict was good and really liked the aioli; just wish the crab cakes were bigger.

I never really liked this place. The music was mediocre, the crowd was a bit creepy, and the drinks were overpriced. Plus, the bathroom sink that was shared between the men's and women's room was really unappealing. 

As the closest club to where I lived I accepted that this is where I might occasionally end up, until tonight. Even though I don't have to pay a cover, gracing this place with my beautiful face is more than it deserves. 

Mainly I'm upset because I knew tonight was one of those nights I would end up at Mandarin because it was the closest club. I called ahead to make sure all the guys were dressed up to par : no hats, tennis shoes, cargo shorts, baggy tees, or flip flops. All my guy friends amped up their outfits with polos, shorts without side pockets and nicer shoes. The definition of tennis shoes is a bit ambiguous, but they chose nice clean lace up shoes. At the door the two boys I entered with were still turned away. I went up without them and saw boys in outfits identical to theirs as well as plenty of flip flops. Without the friends I came with to serve as buffers from all the creeps there, I quickly left.

 I really hope I don't have to deal with going to Mandarin again. There are plenty of other crappy clubs with slightly better music and nicer bouncers  I rather give my money to (even if I can get in free here).

I came here earlier this year before I discovered YELP, I just had forgot the name of the restaurant. I just had to warn you all not to come here. The restaurant is small, the decor abysmal, the food burnt, flavorless and nasty. Oh yeah, it was in the summer and no AC, it was hot and humid inside. I am so ashamed I even came here. Will never be back again and will never in a million years recommend this restaurant to anyone..... Zero stars

I have eaten Thai food throughout the U.S.
THIS PLACE IS GOOD! And authentic prior to this place a Thai Restaurant in Seattle Washington was the gold standard now we use this restaurant as the benchmark. 

I live in Miami but when we visit Tampa this is a must. You must try all of there items most people just try Pad Thai and your really missing out ALL GOOD.

Absolutely horrible food for the money. You can go to Kona Grill or Yardhouse and have good food for the same price. This place charges to much for low quality food. I posted it on my facebook and everyone agreed and wont go back. The menu has little variety and whats up with the pasta section how about normal pasta and if you are going to do a fondue you don't do two greens you add a green and maybe like an apple or a meat with the bread not broccoli and barely cooked Brussel sprouts and the cheese was gritty. To bad cause it has nice curb appeal and nice inside but thats all that is nice.

I've been going to this salon since I moved to Goleta about a year and a half ago.  Somehow I ended up with Nicole who has been somewhat nice, but often unavailable. Recently, I needed a quick color appt. for an event.  Nicole was on vacation so I ended up with Amanda. My hair looked nice, but two hours later bloody scabs started popping up all over my scalp. The back of my ears and hairline were on fire.  I waited a few days and then called the salon.  I left a message for Nicole for suggestions. Five days later, she hasn't called me back.  I paid $180 for this misery.  Two weeks later I'm still itching like crazy.  Calling the dermatologist Monday.  I will never go back to this salon.

This is now my go-to place for Lebanese food. This is how all food should be done - authentic with fresh ingredients. A big 'Thank You' to the owners and chef of Shishkabib House for being the gold standard! 
Don't let the simple name of this fine restaurant fool you. The only other time I've had Mediterranean food this good was when I was overseas.

We had an extra long wait since the buzzer the host gave us was apparently broken.  But we did find some good mojitos at the bar with some nice live music provided by a girl and her guitar. 

Once seated, we noticed that much of the seafood was fried.  however, the food and service were both good.

I had dinner here on Saturday night with a girlfriend. Our meals were amazing! I had the salmon special - came with mango salsa, coconut risotto, and veggies. She had a steak.

I cannot rave enough about my meal. Salmon was tender and delicious (if a touch under-cooked). I get that some people order "medium" salmon, but I would prefer if it was cooked all the way through. That may be a personal preference though. Risotto and veggies were the best I've had.

My only issue was the ambiance / decor. This could be a high-end restaurant if they modernized it. It was nearly empty on a Saturday at 7pm, and I'm sure the look of the place is part of the problem. Your food and beverages are good enough for five stars! Renovate the interior and modernize the feel, and you'll have a gold mine! :)

This was my favorite pizza place to go, till today! I called in advance to place my order like I always do. When I came for pick up, they tell told me they didn't have my order? Manager Stevie tells me they can place the order and I have wait 25-30 mins for a pie. Hell no!!!! I called in advance so I wouldn't have to wait and someone there never placed my order! I am a very dissatisfied customer and I didn't like how this situation was handled.

Dirty, worn, nasty hotel run by staff that doesn't care at all about the guests. No valet, luggage carts were broken, the pool was cloudy & had trash in it. In the room, the trim was beat up, the fridge was falling out of the cabinet, the bathroom door was rusty. The furniture had stains & they only left 2 towels at a time. The elevators were slow, then finally broke Sunday at dinner time. Staff scattered when confronted with guests that needed help. Stay somewhere else!

I went into the shop as a walk-in on Friday, June 2. The receptionist scheduled me for a 5:15 appointment with Clarissa. I knew I wanted to cut about 10 inches of hair off, but was unsure at the time what I wanted other than for the end result to be shoulder length. Clarissa was EXTREMELY enthusiastic and helpful - she explained to me what looks would work best for my hair type/texture. She suggested a forward angled cut which kept the length I wanted in front while still allowing the amount I wanted off. She also threw in some trendy layers all while walking me through every step and telling me about the products she used. After the cut and a short photo shoot, all of the other stylists were so friendly and complimentary.  I am very happy with how my hair turned out as well as with the atmosphere in the shop. I will definitely be back to see Clarissa!

I went here after the North East Shopping Center UPS Store gave me routine horrible service/attitudes. The women and man here were very nice, service was fast and they did not try to 'shaft' me. 5*'s.

I've bumped up to 5 stars after having a great lunch from there yesterday. The samosas were great and the saag paneer was the best I ever had! Chicken tikka masala- excellent. A lot of times I find chicken in an Indian buffet sub- par but this is good quality, well prepared moist white meat.Cauliflower-potato curry was excellent. I love the food here, always fresh and tasty. Don't forget to ask for hot sauce; it's extremely flavorful without being too hot.Skip the naan. I had a Trader Joes paratha with it instead!

I love this place, sure sometimes you wait a while, but I find the customer service unparalleled.  I'm a restaurant manager and I wish half of my employees were as passionate and knowledgeable as the emoloyees at FreedomSmokeUSA. I worked with Kyle at both the Orange Grove and Catalina locations and he is always a joy! He greats me with a smile, never tries to rush me out and never tries to sell me accessories I dont need. The personal experience he provides is rare in employees these days. Keep up the good work!
Wow! Driving from San Luis Obispo to Orange County and needed some good tacos. Yelp reviews were positive so we stopped and loved this place. Everything was very very good. Recommend the Cubano!

Do not eat here. First of all, it took them about 3 weeks to fix their drink machine. Secondly, my coworkers and I got sick from eating here all on separate occasions. I feel like the employees there were not trained well too. They cant really make a good sandwich. I opened mine up and the meat fell everywhere. Maybe consider some better training and a quality of food check up. I generally like subway but this one has made me sick on multiple occasions.

If you love coffee, &/or local shops, this is THE shop for you. Not only is Brigitte amazing, the coffee and desserts are equally amazing. They will treat you with kindness like you've known everyone for years. This isn't just a coffee shop, its a small community of loyal customers that is inviting to anyone who loves conversation, or a nice 'hello' every day. 

There is a daily brew offered every morning, and they can make ANY drink you can think of. Starb*cks has nothing on this shop. The coffee from No Name Java will change your coffee drinking life. You will gain knowledge not only on coffee, but on other local products as well. They sell great raw honey from Negley & Sons, as well as fresh tea.

If you love locally owned businesses as much as your coffee this is the place for you. Support local, not corporate. Brew D Licious treats you like family and it's a great experience every time you walk in.

A far cry from my hometown of Boston, Citizens Bank Park is big, new -  and of course full of beer and food.  I'm pretty sure that equals happiness.

Since moving to the Philly area in '03, I cannot deny my newfound love for this team of underdogs. And every game I have attended, which must be a half dozen or so, I've always had a good time.  From tailgating in the parking lot with creepy old dudes and high school students to harassing any Mets fan in sight, one can be entertained by the crowd alone.  With lots of cheap tickets and game specials, what's not to love?

I'm a product of passionate sports cities - Chicago and Boston.  I'm happy my latest home of Philadelphia proves to be the same and MORE.

This place was highly rated on Foursquare for 'regular' food so wasn't sure what I was getting myself into when looking for vegan food. Boy as I surprised! All options were clearly marked and there were plenty of items to choose from.  To top it off my meal was delicious.  Would highly recommend!
Amazing Turkish coffee! I never knew straight black coffee (no cream) could be so tasty. Secret family recipe, straight from Turkey.

Finally checked this place out on a date and now I'm wondering why it took me so long!

Beautiful lights, a "big city" feel, great view, excellent cocktails, and complimentary popcorn flavored with truffle oil and sea salt? Sign me up. 

We visited on a weekend night so it was a bit crowded, but the service was excellent. I was able to successfully order one of my favorite old fashioned cocktails off menu with good results. Great spot for a nice drink downtown!
Friendly staff and good pizza. Alex took his time to make the perfect gluten-free pizza!

Made a reservation at least one week in advance. Check. Received reservation confirmation. Check. Credit card charged. Check. All appeared to be going according to plan...

Until check-in, that is. Upon arrival, at approximately 10:00pm on Saturday evening, my girlfriend and I were not-so-promptly informed that the hotel had been "over-sold" and that we were being sent to another hotel. No directions were provided, and no manager was on-site to explain why this was happening.

Interesting note - we were further advised that "non-preferred" guest reservations can be cancelled at any time, in the case that a "preferred" guest makes a conflicting reservation. 

Message received, Marriott. My non-preferred business and I will no longer patronize your lackluster institution. Good luck catering to your "preferred" clientele.

P.S.: I wish that there was an option to give a negative number of stars.

Ordered 2 coffees and a muffin. Got one coffee and the muffin 20 minutes before the second coffee. Watched people who came in after me get drinks while I continued to wait for the second coffee.  How do you give half an order to someone and then make them wait for the rest while the first one gets cold?  This is not the first time this has happened.

They always do a great job on my vehicle. The wifi is nice too. But the hard sell tactics up front are a little off putting. Bubbles should re-assess how they market their services. Overall I am happy with the service they provide.
We are from Phoenix and tried the Fish Tacos here and they are very very good!  Alot of Fish for the money. Better than Rubio's which we like alot as well.

I have had good food and one decent service experience here, but it's been a long time since either of those things have happened here.  We arrived here at 5:00pm on a Sunday and ordered 2 appetizers and a salad.  After inquiring about the long wait, our server seemed unconcerned and told us they were busy.  It took 50 minutes for our food to come out, with no apology.  My meal was cold.  I informed the manager of our long wait and cold food, and although she offered to comp my meal, she did not offer any other solutions or see if I wanted anything else.  It's a shame because we like this place and would like to continue to support our neighborhood restaurant.

I got the Chicken Tikka Marsala, It was brilliantly plated and  although I couldn't  finish it I took if home and I ate it as a midnight snack.  My friend got the antipasta platter. I tried the Baba Gnoush and it was the best I have ever had. Great place, with awsome art all around the walls and the open kitchen is pretty neat.
The food is mediocre. Nothing special. The outdoor seating is nice when it's not cold.
From Cali to NYC this place has the best bagels and lox you have ever tasted. Just over a mile from the French Quarter, worth the walk two mornings in the cold. Mouth waters just thinking about it.

Really not that good. Ate here with my sister for brunch today and was really underwhelmed. We both ordered omelettes that were overdone (hers contained maybe a crumble of feta at most).  Our toast came out with no butter, which we had to ask for unfortunately. Jones is also pretty pricey for what you get. Four dollars for poor quality drip coffee is absurd.  Can't say I'd recommend this place for brunch at least.

A friend and I were craving savory curries and delectable mango sticky rice so we grabbed a few bottles of vino and situated ourselves at Vientiane Cafe. The space is small, but clean and comfortable. The wait staff was extremely courteous and prompt with our orders and didn't try to charge us extra for uncorking. I got the yellow curry (which is Massaman to me) and my friend got the green. Both were generously portioned and colorful. I would have liked by curry a tad less runny, but it tasted quite good and had the right touch of sweetness. 

Needless to say, my friend and I ended up consuming a great deal of wine and lost track of time. We noticed the staff was closing, but they were really polite about it. They didn't say anything to us or passive aggressively thump around tidying up, they just waited patiently for our oblivious drunk selves to schlep our stuff and leave. I would definitely come here again because of the excellent service.

The staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was very large and clean and the beds were very comfortable. We had dogs with us and there was not a lot of room to walk them. The hotel is right next to the freeway so it was a big noisy too but I would still recommend this hotel.

Gelateria Del Leone is definitely an STL gem.  They make the absolute best latte in all of STL. Period.  You can enjoy this latte in their cozy cafe space or outdoor patio -- never too busy or too loud!  Just enough ambient background noise to get your work done or enjoy a leisurely morning or afternoon.  Let's not forget to review their gelato, which is excellent.  While they don't have a million flavors, their gelato is always creamy and delicious.  Not to mention you can get two flavors, even if you only get their small sized cup!  Staff is professional and friendly, taking time to explain their products to you and whip you up whatever delight you choose.  Love this place.

I'll keep this short. 

I hate shrimp. This place made me crave crawdads. It must be Cajun magic.

Surprisingly, Cafe Envie was one of the best meals I had while in New Orleans. Cheap, hearty, and delicious, my egg, biscuit, sausage, and hashbrown breakfast was mind-blowingly good.

Biscuit was buttery, hashbrowns were salty and scrumptious, and the eggs were scrambled to perfection. Cut the biscuit in half and turn it into a breakfast sandwich!

Oh and the cafe itself is quite cute and spacious with tons of tables outside and indoors overlooking the street. Order your food at the counter and have it delivered to your table within 5-10 mins

I was only just there yesterday and am already craving this breakfast. BADLY. I may be returning to New Orleans just to have this breakfast again..

Thank you for making all my southern breakfast dreams come true, Cafe Envie.

Food is awesome
Location is perfect
Service is impeccable
What makes this place awful is they allow cigar smokers
We complained and server told is, too bad
Just had a spa pedicure with Vicki. She squeezed me in right away. It was excellent and tailored for my needs. My feet look so pretty now.

I had the usual problem: my Samsung had blown it's caps and was cycling endlessly.  I called Caden TV, Luan came out the next day and had the problem fixed within the hour.
Very competent and polite and the price was reasonable.  I would call them again..

I'll start by saying that the beer selection is great and the bar staff is wonderful every time we go there.
Tonight we decided to go for dinner and to try their food for the first time. My fiance's dinner (pasta) was excellent. I ordered a "toasted" sandwich that came out with soggy, mushy bread that was burnt black on the edges. The ham and brie inside were also overcooked and burnt black on the edges. I was very hungry and don't like to complain, so I picked the less-burnt ham and cheese out of the middle and left the rest on my plate as I nibbled on my fiance's dinner (there was plenty for both of us). I wasn't going to say anything- but the bartender noticed how awful it looked, apologized and took it to the manager. The manager refused to offer us any sort of compensation for the meal- even though it was their own staff who noticed how terrible it was.The bar staff apologized profusely and took care of us in the end, but not thanks to the management or chef who made the sandwich.
I will continue to go to Jacksons for the friendly staff and excellent craft beer selection. I highly doubt that I will ever return for the food or to be treated with such terrible customer service.

We came here originally to try the frozen yogurt from the self-service area or the boba tea but we were intrigued with the rolled ice cream so we got that instead. 

We ordered the Cake Walk flavor (strawberry + cheesecake) and received an unexpected amount of ice cream for $7. It contained 3 large rolls that was filling for 2 people. It comes with whipped cream and the choice to add more toppings. 

They even have an area for VR gaming that we tried out. My boyfriend tried a couple games and so did I but warning the VR headset has a smell in it probably from the accumulation of people's head and face sweat! We had never played any VR games before and was lost most of the time but the younger boy behind the counter was shouting out tips and instructions which was nice :)

We will be back to try the boba tea and self-service frozen yogurt!

Always fresh!! Great vibes. I willing pay the 3$ toll to go over the Burlington Bristol just to eat at this place. I have never had a bad experience and I imagine I never will. Keep up the great work!!

Being kind in the review as it appears management who passed our table more than once totally avoided us.  Yes the view is the only good thing.   Ice tea old and nasty.  Fish so greasy oil could not have been hot enough.  Coating was hard greasy and gross on the fish.   Others who came after us served long before us.   Save your money and eat somewhere else
The service was polite,  the food came in a great portion and very delucious. Our waitress was wonderful. One of my go to places

My boyfriend was looking for diamond earrings as a gift for me and had visited two other jewelers in the area before we came here. We loved that everyone at Gossage was family and was so kind and not pushy. They only showed us bigger sizes when we asked to see them, rather than trying to push us to a higher price point. Then, their prices were so much better than the other jewelers we visited! We bought the earrings on the spot and I love them. They also offered to replace a missing back on a pair of gold earrings, when I mentioned it.  
I'll absolutely bring my other jewelry here and recommend them to friends.
DONT GO IF MONEY IS AN OBJECT. BUT if it's not thus place is great. Excellent fish tasty veggies and home made ice cream with chocolate sauce. Drinks any size shape or color.  Repeat often.

I love this stadium.

Coming from London, I'm not a huge baseball fan... yet. I am really into a lot of other sports, and always love a live game. Baseball is no exception.

I find fans of the Phils to be very knowledgeable and passionate. Of course this year as World Champs they have a lot to cheer, but the new stadium has great character and there's a buzz about the place.

Views are great from all over, I love that you can walk all the way around the ground (not something that is typical of most English venues), facilities are great and prices aren't too dear (which is good considering there are about 80 home games a year!!)

Going to a game is a lot better than watching on TV, so even if you're not an avid follower, go and check out just how massive Ryan Howard is and how short J-Roll is in the flesh.

For the non foodies, sure go ahead. For foodies, skip

The whisky is severely overpriced, go to any nearby bar for a $10 Laphroaig rather than$20 here. The cocktails were meh. Not the best I've had by far.

The burger was once my favorite, now it pales in comparison to the best burger in the city, namely hickory lane. 

The food otherwise, was technically fine but for the price it pales in comparison to the better places in the city

Everyone is nice and helpful. But if you're a foodie, you can do better. If not go ahead and enjoy it!

I want to root for this place - it's cute and the guy who helped me was super nice. But alas, my smoothie was just not very good. It had lime in it and they threw the entire lime in so I kept getting bits of peel in my mouth that I wanted to spit out. Yuck! I've seen other places peel a lemon or lime before juicing it. There were other things I disliked about the texture (too many oats!). Overall it just didn't taste very good - it was just bland and not worth the $8 or so I paid for it. I'll give them another chance but I'm not sure this place is going to make it. :(
Ted Drewes totally ROCKS! I love their cookies and cream frozen custard!

My 1st visit was GREAT! and now I am a regular picker upper! Man this is just good. I come 1-2 a week now. I ask for grilled chicken tacos vs. shredded, on 1 would do the job but I also get 1 fish taco, its really good too, then 1 beef taco and its simply great, while i wait I get 1 margarita. Salsa is fresh every time  & service has been great also..and try the shrimp soup its Top Shelf. So far so great

It's my second time drinking at this location. Always a great place to be if you prefer to enjoy a nice dark ambience. Servers and bartenders know their concoction(S), it's not overly crowded like most places. I highly recommend this bar :).

Grey Salt is a collaboration between Seminole Hard Rock Tampa and celebrity chef Marc Murphy. I recently ate there as part of a VIP group and i must say overall i was impressed. The food is very good although a bit pricey. I had the Roasted Chicken and it was delicious it takes three days to cook.

The appetizers are good we ate a margherita flat bread and a lamb flat bread. side dishes were good although broccoli rabe was very bitter.

Overall a great dining experience, wait staff, hostesses, and bartenders all very polite and knowledgeable about menu.

Soft Opening on the  9th of November and i believe grand openiong on the 19th.

LOCATED IN THE SEMINOLE HARD ROCK HOTEL & CASINO IN TAMPA, FLORIDA, GREY SALT BRINGS A NEW LEVEL OF DINING AND AESTHETIC TO A WORLD-RENOWNED GAMING CENTER, A BREATH OF FRESH AIR, THIS MEDITERRANEAN INSPIRED EATERY FROM CELEBRATED CHEF MARC MURPHY, IS BOTH OASIS FROM, AND GATEWAY TO, THE EXCITEMENT OF THE FLOOR.

I went to a nail salon near the area and asked the ladies for some fast food recommendations. They immediately told me that Butters had great soul food. I was hungry and in the neighborhood so I thought I would give it a try. Man, I was surprised that a take-out like this existed in the neighborhood. I've lived in the neighborhood for two years but I didn't even know about this place! I had fried chicken dark meat (2 drumsticks and one thigh) with two sides, greens and rice with gravy) which came to $10.80. The wait was long (35m) for one entree with only several people around but it was worth it. They seem to make things per order. The best part was that the chicken was pipin' hot and crispy. The batter was good- could use some more seasoning or honey but good. The collards were good as well- simple, just the way I like it. When I got home, I added some red pepper for some spiciness. The rice with gravy was nothing special. Overall, I'm glad a takeout such as this is around the neighborhood and I will be ordering again when I crave fried chicken. The staff was friendly too. This time I'm calling beforehand though.

Met some friends here while in town. Started off at the bar where the bartender made me an amazing watermelon cocktail ... Could have had those all night, but I needed to be in bed by 10, so I stopped at two. Dinner was a mixed bag - and I was conflicted over the the short ribs dish - the short ribs were awesome, tender, juicy and tasty, but the hominey it came with was bland (I know it's hominey but still ...) and had an odd texture, but the grilled squash was excellent ---- my dish was part hot food, part cold. The setting is super cool, hip, etc., but loud so hard to hear your dining companions sometimes. Service was excellent - attentive but not overbearing. Had a great time so, I'd come again.

The food was really good. The staff was very friendly and we enjoyed our dinner. While we were there, we observed that they have a really good to go service! If your looking for somewhere new, you should give it a try.

I tried this gem a couple months ago. Their menu is small but satisfying. There is something for everyone. I am on a diet and the owner actually made me a delicious salad that wasn't on the menu to cater to my needs. The prices are reasonable and I'd definitely recommend this place.
Loved this place. Cheesey and meaty is as good as it gets! I hope to return to Nashville again!
the only things i love on their menu are the tuna tacos and fried pickles.. thats it. oh and a tecate with a shot of tequila for only 5 bucks? sure!
Oaklelys never disappoints!  The entire evening was outstanding from excellent service to impeccably prepared dishes.  We've been here several times and Oakleys remains my favorite in Indy.

Inconsistent...WE were so excited to try this lovely, atmospheric restaurant.  The setting and our waiter were wonderful BUT our food (overall) batted about 50%.  The hamburger was terrific; one dish with pork tenderloin was great ...but the "Ways and Means" dish was not good ...and the fries (served with the hamburger) were cold.  The cheese plate appetizer was disappointing...old grapes and very little fruit...(way too skimpy)...  The bread pudding was very good...the custard was cold-refrigerated... and only fair.  Gosh ... this restaurant COULD be great!!!  But...we were disappointed....

Cant say how much i love shopping here. Staff are always very nice and the prices are always great too. My son even loves to go shopping here with me. Although its mostly because the treats he gets while were there.

Was excited to check out the Children's Museum with 5 and 6 year olds, but was sadly disappointed. Almost the entire first floor is dedicated to a waterway play which had potential but nothing seemed to be working while we were there. Water did not flow which in effect made a majority of the exhibit pointless. Other parts of it just weren't functioning such as water spray buttons.The second floor was smaller than expected, we were done in 1 hour. Kids liked the paper airplane launcher, the hockey game, and the fire truck the most. While the prices aren't as high as other major cities, the experience wasn't as great either.

All the positive reviews about this place are spot on.  This isnt a fancy restaurant,  it is more like a fast food restaurant on steroids.  The employees are welcoming and the guy behind the counter is absolutely entertaining.  

Despite being across from Busch Gardens, it isn't in the greatest neighborhood.  I say this only because this lends itself to a steady stream of interesting characters stopping in to eat and to pick up take out.

The menu has a lot of food choices and we chose to share the gyro, a greek salad, and chicken schwarma.  Everything we ordered was nothing short of spectacular.  The prices are also very reasonable. 

I will defintely be back for the food and the service.   If you haven't been to this place,  do yourself a favor and give it a try.

Stopped in for brunch because Day By Day didn't take plastic and when a friend offers to pick up the tab and needs to use plastic you just find a place that takes plastic. 

Slate was that place. 

Now we didn't go for the full-on hair-o-the dog brunch, although the bar looked amply stocked with top shelf items. Instead we just ordered food and coffee. 

The eggs florentine looked good. The other order was just a straight-up eggs benedict. However, the hollandaise sauce was a litte thin. Runny yolk thin. Spinach was a bit salty for my taste. 

Service was good, coffee was good, ambience good. Solid 3 stars.

Awesome rooms

I usually stay across the street at the Residence Inn, but they were booked so this was my second pick.  I was very suprised that the rooms were this nice. The lay out was spacious, the bed was very comfy, and the room seemed very clean.

The front desk people were nice and courteous. And the selection at the snack market was decent. Very quite location right next to downtown so you wont be disturbed trying to sleep, but your still seconds away from the downtown fun.

Ill always stay here when i travel to Boise

Stopped here after a cold day at Busch Gardens for one last Mexican meal before heading back up North to NY. Probably the best tacos I've ever had. The chips and salsa were amazing, too. Definitely recommend.

First time here - it was a great experience. Donuts were fresh and delicious. Tony, the owner is very friendly! Other staff weren't as enthusiastic but weren't rude either. I'll definitely be going back. Especially with any out of town guests.

Came here a couple months ago after finding out our favorite Mexican place closed down. Ordered a burrito, some tacos, kid's quesadilla, and some gauc n chips.

Burrito is seriously overpriced for what you get.  Flavor is about average, but you're essentially paying $9 for a taco bell burrito with a side of rice and beans. I'm totally ok with taco bell style burritos, but they shouldn't cost more than a a few bucks.  Tacos were mediocre and also overpriced.  Gauc n chips were ok because I'm pretty sure it's impossible to mess up gauc.

I don't know if this is accurate, but it felt like the cooks in the back have no culinary education or skill.  The food felt like what you'd make in high school before you learned how to actually cook well.  Maybe they are a bunch of high schoolers and no one is actually quality controlling the dishes, I really can only guess.

Suffice it to say we won't be coming back.

Ordered the spring roll and pho combo. 

Spring roll was pretty good. Ingredients was fresh.

Pho combo was very good.

Very good pho broth. Hard chewy noodles (this is a good thing) with rare steak on top.

I've cheated on my first true love for banh mi in St. Pete. And basically just across the street. I got suckered to check it out with a group of friends because Danny V. had already paid a visit and raved. Not bad. The grilled pork banh mi hasn't supplanted my top banh mi place but it's serviceable. What's really cool about seasons is that they offer a seemingly wide array of menu items that's clearly on display. Points for that. Not to mention... have you ever had shaved ice? Neither have I. So I'll have to give it a shot one day. After all, I did score that living social deal for $20 worth of food. Who wants to join me?

How may dive liquor stores mix one hell of a Bloody Mary? This is our first stop when we head to the quarter.

Vieux Carre' Wine and Spirits is totally unpretentious, not overpriced whatsoever, and you might walk past it without even giving it a second look. Once you know though that you can walk in and get the best Bloody ever in a to-go cup, you'll remember it.

Such great customer service. I've been to many bike shops looking for my first bike but none had made me feel comfortable with a big purchase except for Bike Sport. When I came in the first time, Andrew spent maybe 30 to 35 minutes explaining the different bikes to me and not selling them. He listened to what I wanted out of my first bike and made recommendations. Ultimately we decided on one, which I just came to pick up. Another maybe 40 minutes going over everything that I need to know by it being my first bike. Kevin even took me out to the parking lot and watched me ride to make sure I was OK. They go above and beyond to make sure that not only you receive great customer service but also to make sure you have a great riding experience. I look forward to joining the community and coming back fotr all of my biking needs. 

Happy 1st time bike rider:):)

The staff was super friendly and generous with my family... Whenever there was a problem with the machine in more than compensated with my kids really happy, and they were super nice with the food, and even gave my kids a little extra points to help them get a surprise with their tickets! Staff came by to let me know the schedule, and quickly made fresh ice tea when I ran out. Definitely going to come back here, more than happy to spend my weekly kiddo entertainment budget at this place.

After hitting all the local haunts in the Soho area for food options, I finally decided to give this healthy "fast food" place a try. I only use the term "fast food" because the food orders come out in a quick and timely manner, I say it devoid of any indication that the food isn't tasty of high quality because I very much so believe it is and like the name says, FRESH. Housed in a strip of other eateries and stores, there is parking lining the retail complex which is in close proximity to the storefront. 

The premise at So Fresh is that you choose a salad, a wrap, or a bowl from the menu. The menu descriptions serve as a base and then you add your protein, hormone and antibiotic free chicken and organic tofu are included in the price with hormone free beef and ahi tuna with a small up charge. Any bowl has the potential of zucchini "noodles" to be added on (I believe $1 for half or $2 for full bowl) or avocado for a nominal charge. 

My particular favorite here is the superfood bowl which I have gotten with both seared Ahi tuna and organic tofu, both of which are delicious. I enjoy that the restaurant keeps bottles of Sriracha for patrons and I fee or really compliments the meal. There are fountain drinks available and they sell gluten free (I think) oatmeal cookies for a sweet treat. The staff is always friendly and helpful and able to answer any question you may have and works to give you a quality product efficiently. I have never waited for more than 5-10 minutes for my meal so I would advise coming here if you want good, wholesome healthy food and are in a rush, as long as it's convenient to you. There is also another location off Fowler which is their original location. I will be sure to return again and again. I really enjoy their flavorful options and inventive creations. 

The interior, although not large is comfortable and has nice decor appropriate for the restaurant. I can attest that the restroom that they have was clean when I used it to wash my hands. Overall, a really great place and I look forward to my next meal from there.

It takes a lot for me to be impressed by great service, and even more to write a review, but I have never been so impressed with a restaurant.  This staff was the most polite and generous I've ever experienced.  They surprised us throughout the night with little unexpected treats and the food was amazing!!  I recommend this restaurant with the highest praise!

My favorite Indian Food in all of Tucson. Tried a couple of other place's this is the place to me deliver's the most tasty authentic Indian Food. I highly recommend this to anyone who wants to eat good Indian food in Tucson! :)

Benefitting from the limited options available in Bala, La Collina is the epitome of a traditional Italian restaurant.  Uninspired menu of things like chicken Parmesan, and tortellini soup.  The waiters, while pleasant, were all very old and slow,  I'll be back, but only because its the only real option for a business lunch in the neighborhood.
Garlic and cheese grits were creamy and went so well with the pork! Pork was unadorned but tasted great

I just completed a review of this restaurant, but it is under "El Dorado Tortilla Factory."

In a nutshell, this place is the real deal:  truly authentic truck stop Mexican food, you know, the kind that locals in central Mexico may prefer and probably snowbirds from Chicago would not. You can happily avoid the typical gringo/Mexican chimichangas, fajitas, burros, taco salads and hamburger tacos you find at most Tucson restaurants. Instead you can get machaca, pozole, menudo, huevos con nopalitos, picadillo, chilaquiles and other not-smothered-with-lettuce-and-kraft-cheese food. It may not be healthy, but for sure tastes good and is real Mexican food. Call it ethnic comfort food.

Lunch buffet was very tasty with lots of choices, under $8 per humanoid including drinks. Compare that to a boring taco combo plate for over $10 and $2 more for an iced tea at most Tucson "Mexican" restaurants. 

Service was quite good. We were the only gringos eating there, and the servers (yes, several of them) stopped by to see if we were happy with our food.

Great hotel! Customer service was excellent and the decor was beautiful! This is my second time in a Kimpton Hotel and I would highly recommend it if there's one in your city. Second one with no pool though...

this is for the takeout window only.  which by the way appears to be the back door into obtaining some of the most delicious chowder this side of the mississippi, without waiting in a gadawful line for the resto. I never order clam chowder in CA, and I'm so glad I did -- creamy, rich but not gloopy chock full of tender clam. the oysters were fresh and juicy, even more delicious slurped on the pier by the water. just wish that the service window guy was a leetle bit happier with his job/life, and that there was some covered seating.

so I dropped in to this store since it was the same company as you would find in Hong Kong. Thought it might have the same delicious pastries you would find in Hong Kong. Although you did find your egg tarts and sweet buns, they weren't as ... how would you call it... fresh. They didn't have the same "zest" as you would find at the little stores along the alley ways of Hong Kong.They do have egg tarts which will satisfy your craving but doesn't leave you as tickled as you would hope. They don't take credit cards by the way and there's a lot of construction going on around them so it looks like they're closed.
Best Country Fried Steak I have ever had bar none. Pleasant enough hole in the wall restaurant with excellent food. It boggles the mind why anyone would patronize the Waffle House next door.

The place is cute enough.... I guess. The tables are a little too close together for my taste, but I guess that doesn't matter because the place was empty!!! So then, please tell me WHY, with so much space in the place, our waitress crammed  other patrons at the 3 tables closest to ME??  That's a serious pet peeve of mine. I like to BREATHE, and I honestly felt suffocated.

Their crepes fall into 5 different categories :Les Bourgeoises (rich and light taste),  "Les Classiques (traditional taste), Les Savoureuses , ( seafood delight ), Les Tentantes (very creative mix), and Les Rebelle (Revolutionary, delicious taste,  Pizza Crêpes). Then,of course, you have the brunch menu and the sweet crepes.

I ordered  the Chatelet" off the brunch menu. It's a savory crepe with scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, swiss cheese with boiled sautéed potatoes for $13.00. I thought it might taste better w/ onions, so I asked for them, and I was right. It was DELICIOUS! My potatos were just ok.

My bf ordered a sweet crepe with banana, strawberry and nutella. he wasn't impressed. He thought it was too "crispy." We both ordered black tea to drink, but they did have a variety of loose teas to choose from as well.

Overall, I'd say, the place is far too overpriced, because it simply doesn't have the ambience to charge so much money. They're also pretty stingy on the portions.

We will returm, but RELUCTANTLY!  lol

For drinkers: decent beer selection; good tequila variety.

I was worried about the recent overhaul with the menu - I suspect ownership has changed, but I am not positive.

There was no need to worry, however. In fact, I believe that the taco quality has increased, especially with respect to the tortillas. 

The Korean BBQ is their staple and if you're there for tacos, get it. It has a great flavor with soft meat. I also had the Southern Fried and though the sauce was delicious. The tortillas are flour, which is one reason it drops to 3 stars for me (I believe heartily in corn tortillas), but I thought they were prepped nicely.

I couldn't justifiably rate it four stars or above for one main reason: your tacos are not made-to-order. Our orders came out within 2 minutes of ordering them. It is impossible to make fresh ingredients or freshly fry a chicken tender for a taco and deliver the tacos at this rate. In order to get 4 or 5 stars, from me, I think the food needs to be made right after I order it. That being said, don't let this fact deter you from stopping by and satiating your taco craving.
The place is dark and noisy. Service is good but at Montecito pace, i.e. slow. The Greek omelette was totally bland due to lack of any seasoning. Potatoes tasted old but the bacon was good.

Absolutely loved this place! Quaint welcoming feel to it, colorful wall murals, and friendly staff were nice complements to the delicious food. I love shrimp and grits, so I ordered their BBQ shrimp and grits, which was delicious and generous enough size, since grits are heavier. There re plenty of yummy options on the menu, which made decision making difficult! Their Moscow Mule was good, as was the bloody mary. My friend had the crab cake Benedict, with which he was very happy. Would come back to this place for sure. Expect a wait, but if you are patient, you won't regret it.

I went to HandleBar on the suggestion from a friend. It was so much better than what I was expecting. The food was great- I had the Lightening BoLT sandwich - it's a BLT with caramelized onions. My only tip was to not go there before 9pm.

Staff was so friendly.  Ordered the classic and grilled pork and it was amazing and fresh.  The bubble drinks was also very tasty and not watered down - soft bobas for the win . Will definitely come back.

I actually use to work here years ago.....for three weeks. It's a horrible place. The owner doesn't care about anything at all and I don't think the Manager ever took a shower and always smelled of BO all the time. There is a lot more about this place that I'm not gonna get into all I'm going to say is keep driving another 5 minutes down the road to DD.

What an incredible restaurant. The waiting staff seemed incredibly professional and the food was out of this world. The bar has some really creative drinks like an egg and bacon martini - which is made with frozen orange juice and candied bacon. It was really cool. Food-wise, the mushroom bisque is nirvana and the yukon gold flatbread is heavenly. It has truffles on it and it rocked my world.

To start with, easy access, easy parking, clean and bright. Very friendly staff. 
Arrived on a Wednesday just after noon. Shortly after the ordering line was long. Looked like a few regulars including a deaf or mute man right behind us. Very obvious he and the owner/manager have become friends as he gestured for his order. 

I ordered the zee-food platter. Definitely not same day wild caught specimen (pretty sure all are farmed raised products from thousands of miles away). But you should know that already. Their preparation keep the freshest taste possible. Did I mention that this was a huge load of food? No one single person should clean off the entire plate.
Felafel was scrumptious. The "small order" of six came with flat bread and fixings. Can easily make a meal out of it. 
Wife got the gyro. Again, one person probably shouldn't finish it in one sitting. 

Went back 2 days later. This time I knew not to over-order. Me, wife, and 8 year old shared salad with grilled chicken, beef kebab platter, and child wanted the plain flatbread (81 cents, hot and fresh!) which she gobbled up almost the whole thing as-is. "Small" order of salad was huge. I saw someone with a large order, and the bowl was the size of a wok. I laughed at her. Definitely enough of well-seasoned breast to fill up. Beef kebab was wonderful. Lots of big chunks of meat with plenty of seasoned white rice and chop-chop, their mix of diced cucumber, tomato, onion, and parsley. 

Go eat at Zeko's. You will not be disappointed. Just remember that your eyes will be bigger than your stomach.

I had a chocolate milkshake and the soup of the day (a spicy kale and sausage soup). Great prices, great service and absolutely delicious. The milkshake was easy to drink, but not too watery. Not overwhelmingly sweet. Even in 10 degree weather with snow, it was perfect.

Love this buffet every time I  am in Marana.  The food is not fancy, but it is tasty, fresh, and worth the modest price.  The staff is friendly and welcoming.  Make sure to try the Mongolian BBQ!  This buffet is very family feiendly.

I just got back from Chucks and had to login to write a review. I was optimistic going in because Chuck is from Texas and from his social media posts and menu, I got the sense that his food would be solid. Unfortunately, I couldn't have been more wrong. 

I ordered the two meat platter - brisket, pulled pork, mac salad and potato salad along with an order of original wings and the only thing remotely good about the entire order was the jalapeno cornbread. The brisket and pork with both extremely bland with absolutely no smoke ring or smoke flavor. In fact they tasted boiled. I can't understand how this could be if that meat was in fact inside a smoker. 

The two sides were both bland as well. I looked hard and couldn't see any spices in either of them. I then moved on to the original wings. Again, the meat was bland with no seasoning and what tasted like a bottled BBQ sauce. No smoke/grill flavor whatsoever.  

I'm at a complete loss for how a BBQ place with a pitmaster from Texas could serve up food like this.

I used to visit this place almost every time I visit friends/family in STL.  It's good and is not really any different than STL Bread Co (Panera's), just a local small business (as STL Bread Co once was).  I'll echo the generally bad and slow service comments from other Yelper's.  The manager gave me a disgusted face and retort when I asked if they offered any organic breads, menu items, or even coffee.  

The nice local atmosphere earned the 3 star rating.

Great pizza, salads, and amazing desserts. Also very good entrees. Quick and really nice service. Very reasonable prices. My number one choice for pizza.  Try the Christopher Columbus if you like lots of fresh veggies. The carrot cake and cannolis are sooo delicious. Better in the main dining room than in the larger room.

After bowling, the Hubba Hubby and I, along with another couple, needed to nourish our bodies so we were looking for a restaurant on the west end.

We ended up at Chilis as the first three restaurants we tried all had waits. But there was a lot of availability at Chilis. 

After pursuing the menu we decided on two for $30 promo that they had on which came with an appetizer and two entrees. The artichoke dip was great - cheesy and flavourful. And the chips that came with it were so tasty. But they were so thin that you couldn't scoop the dip. After finally tracking down our server, he dropped off some cutlery and we were good to go. 

It was a very long time before the mains came out; too long. And it tasted like thy had been sitting a while. I had fajitas with pork. Unfortunately the pork was super dry and it came with very few toppings. And only three small tortillas. I'm sure I could have requested more, if I could have waved down the waiter. But if he had come, I would have used that opportunity to ask (probably for the third or fourth time) for another glass of water. 

Overall we were disappointed. The service was slow and inattentive, my main was overcooked and I felt that I didn't have enough fixings/tortillas to enjoy my fajitas. But happiness was achieved in the appetizer. Enough so that I would go back for it again. There was just something lovely about those chips!

I am a big pizza fan.  I love the amount of toppings and they don't skimp on the ingredients.  I also love how the sauce is not overpowerful or too dry.  I like how the pizza has a chewy texture for a thin crust.  This is one of the best places to eat at.  The only drawback is the salad bar.  The iceberg lettuce doesn't appear too fresh, but who comes here for salad anyway?
Nice spot. Affordable. Great Yelp check in deal--20% off. Too much sizzle, not enough steak. A little weak on the steamed milk. London Fog was missing something. But can I complain for just $1.60?

This place is FANTASTIC!! Family owned. Local food. Great service and a really cool/modern ambiance. I forgot I was just getting a quick dinner in Tampa. The sides are amazing. The meats are super moist, tender, and flavorful. They also have dessert! The seating is super cool - communal seating but a very family feel. 

Hands down one of the best bbq joints I've ever been to, and I've done a cross-country bbq tour. We made the mistake of driving by so many times. Boy did we miss out!

Can't wait to come back here... The menu was fascinating and what an array of mimosas! Service was just superb and very cool artsy vibe atmosphere although a little noisy - not the best acoustics I had the sweet potato hash which was one of the healthier items on the menu ... A friend had the special which look like acfrrnch dip and fries and I really wanted to take some of hers... Another had the French toast with berries and it looked incredible .  I wish  they offered more gluten free pastries and breads and also some cappuccino or lattes. I look forward to going for breakfast or brunch

It's never packed here but the service is always slow. I've never seen a worker crack a smile and the vibe is just ... dry. 

I only come here because it's the only fried chicken place in goleta and it's decent. Biscuits are always dry and the chicken never seems to be warm enough, but It gets my fried chicken cravings satisfied. If there were any other KFCs or even a Popeyes, I wouldn't even bother with this place.
Incredibly beautiful and delicious pastries. Best Napoleon in town and great sandwiches.

Stop right there, thank you very much, I need some chicken with big flavor and crunch. 

Follow these steps: 

Drive to Sassafras.
Sit down.
Order the fried chicken IMMEDIATELY (cooked to order, takes at least 30 minutes)
Order some apps.
Wait patiently for amazing fried chicken.
Control your salivary glands when it lands on your table.
You will want to pick it up with your hands. DON'T...unless you like 3rd degree burns.
Finish whatever the hell came to your table first while it cools.
It's cool. Snag a piece with your fork. Plate it. 
Breathe it in.
Sink your teeth into the juiciest, flavorful and crunchiest fried chicken you will ever have the pleasure of eating.
Go home and cry because your meal is over.

This place is amazing! I've been to the one in Nashville and in Smyrna and both are great! I always start with the crab rangoons, as I could live off those, and I get one of curries for my main dish. Service is great but even if it wasn't I would still eat here!

The breakfast culture club changed my life, super tasty coffee, snacks and treats. Absolutely love their attention to detail, design, and their customer service is top notch!

They serve different kinds of specialty roasts including a delicious Avocado Toast.

They carry a revolving selection of coffee roasters, Coava is their current (based in Portland). There are great work-spaces, plenty of outlets, and a couch area to relax and read.

Pros: diverse menu, great atmosphere
Cons: bad parking (not enough spots during busy times), slow service, presumptuous bartends

Stopped in here on a slow Saturday afternoon.  We came in around 2 pm to find more of the lunch crowd had left and there were just a few people having drinks around the bar.  We decided to seat ourselves in the bar area and look over the menu.

Something that turned me off immediately was when I ordered a beer (a sour) the bartender gave me the "you're a girl and definitely won't like this face" and suggested I try something else. Strike one.  I had the beer and enjoyed it, and did not appreciate someone telling me I "might like something else more".  

Their menu looked excellent.  There was something for everyone from your weird vegan cousin to your mom who thinks Applebee's is the epitome of fine dining.  Everyone is going to find something they liked.  I had a delicious sandwhich with some hearty steak fries and my better half enjoyed buffalo chili.  One thing I did not enjoy was paying a huge markup for Taste of Philly Pretzels with a side of some not-so-yummy pimento cheese dip.  I'll pass on that next time, and wouldn't recommend this app.

All in all it was a nice place to have a late lunch and enjoy some brews.  The seating in the bar area isn't very comfy (no backs on the chairs, just stools) so don't sit there if you're planning to stay a while.

 Also, make sure you ask for your check well before you need to leave.  It honestly took over 15 minutes from the time we told the server we were ready to leave to get our check and have our card run.  That is too long to wait for something like that, especially when the place is only moderately  busy.
