So I am on vacation and decide that my hair is grossly out of whack, probably a month overdue for a good cut.  Go to Yelp, see if I can find a highly rated nearby location for a last minute appointment, and find Salon Ya Ya.  

The first Salon Ya Ya I called apologetically referred me to their second store.  It was with trepidation that I made that second call.  At first it seemed I'd be shut out, nothing available, but David worked hard to fit me in and set me up with Candace.  He told me I would need at least an hour for the personal level of service they give.  Actually my ADD side was glad for the warning, because he was right. 

In a nutshell:
- comfortable and sophisticated vibe
- solid line of professional products and interesting treats (jewelry, make-up)
- comfy chairs at the wash basins
- bright but not blinding colors and lighting
- clean
- genuinely happy people (is that a Nashville thing?) work to serve you
- cuts and services priced based on the experience of the professional

Candace spent time but more importantly gave her full attention to the state of my hair, the shape of the cut and my face and the whole shibang.  She explained what she was doing and why as she went along.  The result was perfect according to my criteria: no one noticed I'd had 2.5 inches taken off!
We stumbled in here randomly to grab lunch and were blown away with the food. Everything we got was excellent - from the first bite to the last it was great!
Vinnie is the best!!! By far the best bar in New Orleans!! Fast service and great burgers. The gimlet and Mary Pickford were delicious.

Went for BRUNCH, which was delicious. 3 stars for the food, 3 1/2 stars because you get to make your own bloody mary! My dreams came true! I didn't have to hope that they would spice the rim with old bay, or include baby gherkins on a toothpick, I got to CHOOSE!! Genius move, Jones. 

The brunch items all come with TATER TOTS! Way to make me so ecstatic during a brutal hangover. 

The LATKES are addicting. Give me a good latke with some delicious applesauce and a little creme fraiche, and I'll give you a kiss and a good bootyshake. (Those latkes go straight to my booty)

The omelette was definitely solid, though our friend's huevos rancheros were looking pretty tempting. It took everything I had not to reach across the table and grab a bite. 

Jones has a great diner feel, without being a gross greasy diner. I highly recommend, and I'll definitely go back.

Han Dynasty has some of the most delicious food I've had in Chester County. Apparently it's very authentic but they also have an Americanized menu. The only complaint I have is the customer service. Expect a longer than normal wait, possibly non attentive waiters and waitresses and maybe getting your food in the incorrect order. If you can if you can let those things slide you will be treated to a delicious meal.

I had high hopes for this one, because it would have been convenient, but I won't be going back. I will say that the prices are decent and the place is pretty cool, but the quality is less than good. Got home and noticed that the haircut was lopsided...

I walk into the store to buy a bottle of water and it was this Asia lady in their she was discriminating against me she told me the bottles of water in her store was warm and I told her it's fine I would still like to buy a bottle water and then she told me her store closed. After she told me her store was closed I decided to walk out the store. once I left out I noticed she allowed this white woman to walk into her store so I confronted about her store being closed and then she had the audacity to tell me that was her friend so I told her that's wrong cause this white woman randomly walked without even speaking a word to you and you telling me your closed that's straight up wrong ,unfair, and mess up and I walked away.  A little after that situation I have walked past the store again and noticed another person inside the store which was an Asian man. Sad to say this but discrimination still exist and I am a young productive black male and this really made me feel sad and unimportant to not be able to buy a bottle water based on my race.

We googled places you should eat when visiting Philadelphia and Jones came up.  We went here Saturday around 12/1 pm and they were very busy so we sat at the bar and our bartender was very attentive.  

We ordered chicken and waffles and french toast which were amazing.  The chicken was SUCCULENT hands down the best chicken I have ever had with chicken and waffles.  It was soo good that it was unbelievable.  The French Toast was good but I was seriously blown away by the chicken

Stayed there for a conference.


I used to travel for business -- 75+ nights a year on the road -- and I don't know that I've ever stayed at a hotel with better customer service than this one. Every single member of the staff was insanely helpful, and bent over backwards to make sure my stay was awesome and that the conference went off without a hitch. 

Location is great. Rooms are nice size and well appointed. Amenities are lovely. But it's the awesome staff that makes this hotel top notch.

This is the second time my husband and I have come to Josef's - expressly to get an assortment of cookies - so I can't speak on behalf of the meals they serve.

Just before the holidays, we came in to get a dozen cookies. Since they were just for my husband and I, I thought even 12 cookies was extravagant. There was only one gal behind the cash register helping a short line of customers. The service was VERY slow. When our turn came, I mentioned that I wanted just an assortment of cookies. Immediately, the gal tried to HARD SELL me on the pre-made-up platters of cookies that were heaped on a large table in the entrance area. I kept saying "NO, that's too many!" But she just wouldn't listen, and kept telling me that this assortment was ready to go. 

When I *finally* got her to listen to me - the customer - I told her I wanted just one cookie from each line in the top two shelves of the display cabinet. Over and over and over and over I had to repeat this ridiculously simply request. Even my hubs was wondering if the gal understood English? She kept asking what we wanted, and then 15 min into putting some of the cookies into a box, I said, "So what have we got here?" And she said, I've got 5 cookies - what else did you want? Seriously, it was like some kind of skit on SNL. How difficult is it to grab ONE each of SIX different cookies on TWO shelves? We got the cookies and I have to admit: they were DELICIOUS! I think cookies (and probably cakes & pastries) baked at the holidays are bound to be good and fresh because of the turnover.

Flash forward to yesterday. We returned with a sweet tooth to get just six cookies for us. One gal behind the counter was on the phone as we approached the cash register. She remained on the phone a couple of minutes (with no greeting whatsoever), then hung up and disappeared in back. Um. OK. Anyone HOME? After waiting 5 minutes, a different gal came out to take our order. This time, we got the cookies we asked for and went home to try them. HORRIBLE! 

We took a bite from 4 of our 6 cookies purchased, and found they tasted like rock hard sawdust. I am not kidding. I bake cookies myself, and I know that when you bake them fresh - DAILY - they should be moist and tender. Yes, they look pretty all dolled up in frosting and daubs of jam, but the flavor is absolutely flat - not a hint of butter or sugar in them. I guess they use lard? I also suspect that the cookies stored under the hot lights of the display case are not only dried out beyond repair, but were probably baked a good week ago. I broke a Cary cookie in half and it just shattered like glass! The cookie was dry as a biscotti, and tasted like some kind of stale dog biscuit. 

These cookies are an insult to Josef (if he is even alive and cares what is baked and sold in his store). We will not be returning to Josef's again for ANY dessert of any kind ever. I was so mad about these stale biscuit cookies I chucked them all in the garbage. Money down the drain. 

You may as well get a small cookie or two at Whole Foods, or even a small box of infinitely fresher cookies at Trader Joe's! Josef's so-called Vienna Bakery is a total Fakery.

The pho was tasty although considerably less tasty than that of Pho Nouveau downtown. My biggest problem was that they would only sell bottled water. After having put my last dollar and change in the tip jar I had to run another transaction to get a bottle of water with my meal for $1. I guess I just felt nickel and dimed :/

I know they don't have to, but I would sure appreciate it if they would provide the common service of water with my meal. I like my pho spicy!

Good food, polite and attentive servers and bartenders. Plenty of screens to enjoy a game. The place is clean. I do not like the bathroom stalls. The bathroom is clean, I just think they need to modify the stalls. The parking is not very good luckily a friend drove us. Overall, not to shabby. I will definitely go back and then I just read a post and saw pictures of roaches in a persons food. Yeah, "Good Food" ewwwwww yeah right.

If Harry & Izzy's is a indicator of how could St. Elmo's can be, then I can't wait to eat there this year!!  I have only been for lunch their, but our service has always been spot on.  The Shrimp Cocktail is, of course, worth the hype.  Steak sliders?  Yes Please!  House starter salad!  Oh, gawd!  I do love dining her during one of my many trips downtown for lunch dining.  I thank god everyday for my job downtown because I have the opportunity to dine at great restaurants like Harry & Izzy's.

Been a long time since Ive dined at Smilies, but on a recent visit back home we accompanied my great aunt there for her 90th Bday.  She said the gumbo was too spicy--but hey, shes 90, so that doesnt count. My husband got the seafood platter, and as usual, gives me the fried soft shell crab, which I happily devoured. I got the fried eggplant topped with shrimp and crab. Eggplant pcs were so thin that I almost couldnt see it thru the fried crust , but the cream sauce and fresh seafood on top made up for that. Seafood platter disappeared next to me, and I didnt hear any complaints around our table of 10. Prices were a little high, if it were up to me, I would eat at a more low key type place, but for the occasion, it was just fine, as I thought it would be. I would go back, as I have for years.

Elmers great.  Cookie dessert, oh my.  Friendly bartenders who are often airing their woes behind the bar.  
Burgers were good.   
I would visit again, just not first choice.

I love this place!  Came in for a great beer and found it!  If you venture beyond the bathrooms in the back you will find the coffee and food spot.  Smells like awesome coffee, bread and butter aka heaven.  I got a macchiato and loved it.  Great place and I recommend you check it out!
This place was packed when I first walked in so I decided to order to go. The food is legit. I really enjoy it. Authentic and satisfying.

I have been visiting The Spine Shop and Dr Vince Grande for several years now. As a Realtor, I am getting in and out of my car many times a day, and often end up doing something goofy to my back. Walking new construction is always a challenge... And I rely on Dr. Grande to help me correct my "missteps".  He always listens intently so that he understands the issue and applies his skills brilliantly.  I have had many chiropractors over the years, but none as skillful as Dr Grande.  IMHO, It is the smartest $20.00 you can spend on wellness care.
Cute! Love the place. Finger food and tea was great- service maybe could have improved when coming to reservations but we had a good time!
Great pizza place with a nice outdoor seating area. Thin crust, flavorful toppings and great salads.

Best restaurant in Edmonton. I ate here every other week for the 3 or 4 years we lived there. Relatively small servings as Asian restaurants go, but a lot more bang for your buck. They pile on the meat and quality veggies rather than bulking you up on cheap veggies like onions and bean sprouts. And the service is fantastic! Polite, prompt and unobtrusive. A perfect dining experience every time.

Favourite items on the menu: 

Soup: Tom Kha - perfect, just the way it should be. So spicy it makes you hiccup. Tender, melt in your mouth chicken. Good as either single-serve or a larger serving for the whole table.

Appetizer: Deep fried tofu - best sauce ever. Sweet, gooey, peanut sauce with just a hint of spice. Ask for a second serving of sauce if you can as you and your dining companions will be fighting over it. I'm not ashamed to admit that I licked the sauce bowl every time.

Main dishes:
Coconut rice - sweet, sticky goodness. Get there early as they sometimes sell out of this!
Baby bok choy and shitake mushrooms - a good, safe bet that everyone will enjoy. Flavourful but not spicy-hot and something I've never seen on another menu.
Pad chan - like pad thai but sweeter and slightly spicier. 3 perfectly cooked shrimp on a bed of delicious noodles.

We also sampled a variety of meat dishes over the years. All were good. Never ordered anything here we didn't like to be honest. Can't remember the names of any particular dishes and their menu isn't online.

The desserts were also quite nice, but you might want to avoid the tamarind candies that come with the bill. I've never met anyone that liked those and it's not a taste you want to have left in your mouth after an otherwise sensational meal. If a restaurant's only flaw is their choice of after-dinner-mint, that's a fine restaurant by my standards!

This store has many beautiful things.  In fact, both my engagement ring and wedding ring were purchased here.  My husband and I discussed blood diamonds pretty early in our relationship so it was clear that I would not have the typical diamond ring (nor would I want one because it is not my taste anyway).  As our relationship became more serious I would drop hints about what I really did like when we were in an antique shop or walking by Richard Kenneth Jewelers.  My engagement ring is a deco sapphire dinner ring and it is the perfect ring for me.  My wedding band is a white gold, multifaceted band with intricate detailing around the edge.  Gorgeous and simple.

My husband did buy me a pair of earrings here once that I didn't care for.  They were clip ons.  When he gave them to me I told him that I would never wear them because they were so uncomfortable.  My sweet husband took them back and got them converted to posts, but they were still really heavy and don't hang right because the post is in a weird spot.  Apparently the owner told him not to make them into posts, but didn't explain that it wouldn't work.  I wish he had just exchanged them instead.  

Overall, I think the owner is a bit odd, with a goofy sense of humor, but not a bad guy and he has beautiful jewelry that you can't find anywhere else.  I have also bought gifts for my mother here.  I wish I could afford more the beautiful things in this store.

Fabulous food - longish wait on weekends (no wonder!). Only thing lacking is comfortable seating. Seafood is ultra fresh and delicious - servers very knowledgeable and quick once you do get seated. Oysters any style and Uni shooters delicious. You will leave full and happy! And how about that ocean view near sunset!
Do not eat here. Overpriced and the food is disgusting. $4 for a glass of iced tea. Chicken wings were nasty,  no flavor.  I think they were boiled.

This is a great little restaurant in an ideal location.  If you are staying in Sandy Key, you won't find a better brunch option.  The lines can be long, but the service and the food is very good.  If the line is an issue, they offer carry out.  The bananas foster was excellent.  We also tried their tuna salad sandwich.  It is made from fresh salmon and is very tasty.  Definitely worth a visit.

Loved the food here! They give you plenty, so you get a good bang for your buck. I tried the mango sticky rice for the first time ever and fell in love. That is probably my favorite dessert, unfortunately I was just passing through. Anyway, me and my dad both would recommend trying this restaurant.

Delicious sandwiches! It was our first time there and were hesitant on some of the stuff they put in the sandwich but it is a good place to eat. It was cheap, fast, and had great customer service! The cookies are a must, only 50 cents, honestly they exceeded my expectations. It's a very casual place, good for kids, enjoyed our meal there.

I should have researched more before we went.  It's great for 5 and under.  

Bathrooms were clean.  My biggest pet peeve are toilets that give you a shower when you flush them.  Usually I have the door open and ready to run but this was an atomic, I mean, automatic flush.  

The staff was hit or miss.  Most tried to help.  

I feel it was overpriced for what it had to offer.  Don't expect to spend the entire day there.  You can leave and come back, which did break up the day but that still had us leaving at 2pm.  

Location is prime.  We ended up at Buddy Brew, which made me happy.

The one consistent thing about IHOP is the breakfast menu. Always good no matter which IHOP you eat at. I had a nice little fun plate with 5 silver dollar pancakes, Nutella, banana slices and 3 juicy and sweet strawberries and my husband had a Nutella crepe plate. Very good! Service although very sweet, extremely slow for an almost empty house. One thing I learned working for IHOP myself, is accuracy and QUICK service. Service is too slow for an IHOP and attentive waitress????? Where is she? Hello!!!!!!.........Thus my three star rating.

Erin is the dopest bartender working here, she'll make your drinking experience here incredible. She gives awesome beer recommendations and knows how to make customers feel like they're  regulars within minutes of meeting them.

Decor, rustic fabulous..service, just enough, flavors restrained but perfect...white sangria much stronger than I was expecting at noon (that is not really a complaint)..Jano's was eating right next to us, if its good enough for him, its good enough for me...lunch set us back 50 dollars so don't come here for a quick cheep lunch....It was a lovely experience though and what is that worth?

I'm a foodie from the Carolina's, so I have a high standard for certain foods, shrimp and grits in this case. I was wowed, shrimp and grits did not disappoint. Simply amazing. Sat at the bar and chatted with their professional oyster schuker while enjoying a fantastic meal.

What a great place for a midnight snack! I really do mean that seeing as how we ordered everything at 11:55 at night here on vacation in the heart of New Orleans. 

We ordered the meat lovers pizza, a meatball sandwich and the artichoke sandwich. I swear when I say, each were better than the other! Then, you changed your mind over and over. In the end, we really couldn't decide on which dish was better. 

Anyway, we think the stars of their show was their bread and pizza crusts! So delicious! Oh, and their portions are enormous! [the bread! God! the bread! so warm, so moist, so crispy and absolutely delicious!]

In the end, not one person complained AND everyone went out of their way to double wrap their leftovers so they could finish it on the long road home to Albuquerque. Yup. The serving sizes really are that big!

Came Friday with the lovely Eva H and dragged the boyfriend over the next evening.  Both times, I ordered one of the delectable cheese platters and was far from disappointed.   The warm figs with Gorgonzola and prosciutto were  divine.  All three whites I've tried there were excellent and complemented the cheeses perfectly.  Impeccable service, classy but unpretentious atmosphere, and very reasonable prices to boot.  My only regret is that I stayed at the Alexander Inn across the street several times prior to moving to Philly, and not once did I have the sense to visit Tria.

After using Roto-Rooter before, I had no problem calling them again. The first plumber explained the problem- My wash machine was putting out all of the lint from the wash and it was backing up my drain. To prevent this I needed to get a lint catcher. I didnt so it backed up again. So I called Roto-Rooter. I wish I never had this time because the technician lied. First of all he cleared the pipe within 10 minutes of the service call. Then proceeded to say that I had a cracked pipe and that caused the problem. He lied. He never even mentioned the washer machine like the first plumber did and took the time to explain.   But this second plumber took the time to tell me and write up a proposal to replace the pipe that would cost me $5900! He conveniently mentioned that they had "financing".
He also wrote on my receipt that if any thing went wrong, that I can not even get the 30 day warranty because of a "cracked pipe". He also said I had roots in the way. And some kind of broken screen. Yet the drain was cleared. He said it will back up again and when I said when, he said he did not know but to replace the pipe "ASAP" He neglected to tell me that I just need a WASHER MACHINE LINT TRAP. That was the back up. I found this out upon second inspection. 
He charged me $405.00 and I mentioned the $40.00 off coupon and it came to $365.00 which I KNOW was overpriced.
He was such a liar that if something else does go wrong, my husband and I are prepared to get a lawyer involved. We are suspicious that he wrote that we cant have the guarantee  AFTER he cleared the pipe and I rejected his offer to replace the pipe for $5900.  He should have said that BEFORE so that we could have had a choice to use the service or not.

Staff was pretty friendly. 

The food area was a bit of a mess. 

The pinto bean looked like bean paste. Not refried bean. But bean paste. Very unappetizing. 

The portions were once again very small. 

Ordered a burrito and it ultimately looked like a frozen burrito you would get from a truck stop. 

Hopefully after 2/8/2016 something will be done to get portions consistent as well as do something with the bean paste. 

Certainly not my favorite chipotle. 

I miss the days when going to chipotle was satisfying.

I was not sure what I needed as far as landscaping, but Mark talked with me about it and we agreed on a plan for my house. They planted a Natchez Crepe Myrtle in the front and a Japanese miniature maple in the back. They also planted Carolina Jessamine vines along my fence. It turned out great and the trees and vines are beautiful. They also aerated and fertilized the front yard and it has been the greenest ever.

It seemed like a lucky coincidence that a grilled cheese sandwich craving would hit on the same night the Say Cheese Truck was making an appearance at the South Street Night Market.  Unfortunately, the sandwich that I got after my long wait did little more than quiet the craving.

I was psyched to see that the "grown up grilled cheese" listed on the menu board featured Taleggio, arugula and jalapeno-peach jelly.  Sadly, as I reached the truck a staff member erased the Taleggio and wrote in a fairly generic substitution of Monterey Jack in its place.  The event was packed and we were there on the late side, so I don't fault them too much for running out of the Taleggio.  However, they kept charging the same price for the sandwich!  WTH?

Whatever - I had waited that long; I was getting my grilled cheese.  I had high expectations, and what I received was underwhelming.  There was a meager ratio of ingredients to bread; the bread was hard and dry; the cheese was not melted the whole way through; and it seemed like they salted the outside of the sandwich.  There were a few bites in the very middle that actually had a reasonable amount of cheese, arugula and jelly that made me realize what the sandwich could have been.  For a place that calls itself the "Say Cheese" truck, my grilled cheese should have been more than just "acceptable".

Curiously my husband went with the non-grilled cheese option, a roast beef po'boy, and got a really great, substantial sandwich.  It was $2 more than the grilled cheese, but that $2 got him a LOT more food.  His sandwich added a star to the review all by itself.

I might give Say Cheese another try - especially if I encounter them outside of the mob scene of a night market.  Maybe keeping up with the crowd was part of the problem...

I stayed there for a convention with about 200 others and had a pretty seamless experience. Self-check in and out is the way to go - super easy and very fast. The rooms were nice and updated, although the formerly-smoking rooms smelled musty and stale (thank goodness mine was in a never-been-smoked-in building. 

The catered meals were good and the service attentive. I did grab a bite at Cafe Milano and was rather disappointed in the bland food and super slow service (even for water refills). I heard the other fine dining restaurants were completely different, so I'll give them the benefit of the doubt. 

I enjoyed a massage at the spa and was very impressed. Their massage tables even gently rumble with the music in the room. If you take in a spa treatment, budget an afternoon of time and enjoy the pools and amenities that come with it. I had a tight window and had to decline. 

The only heads-up: a $13.40-something per day "resort fee" added to the bill for everyone staying at the hotel. Not a bankbreaker, but confusing.

If I'm back in Reno without a couch to crash on, I'll definitely head to the Peppermill.
Sushi was just okay.  The spicy tuna roll was not spicy and the rice on the rolls was very dry.  We got the calamari appetizer and it was cold and chewy.  Ugh!
Always a pleasure to stop in while waiting for the bus or simply walking around downtown on a day off.
Small town feel. Great service and the food is very good.  Excellent diner style 24 hr spot! And there's a drive thru

Best experience I've EVER had at a restaurant. Couldn't have chosen a better place to go for my eighteenth birthday. When the host called this morning to confirm our reservation, my friend told her it was my birthday, and as soon as I walked into the restaurant I was immediately greeted by everyone inside. The hosts and servers were the kindest people I've ever met and very professional about their jobs. Most of the service was silent, which I loved, but our server also was so easy to talk to. I am so sad that I don't remember his name, because he was very very knowledgeable about the menu and amazing at his job. For an appetizer we started with the kale and quinoa salad, which was absolutely delicious. He recommended I try the mushroom/ricotta stuffed pasta special, which was amazing as well. For sides we had the brussels sprouts and artichoke hearts, and for dessert, the chocolate mousse cake. Amazing way to spend my birthday. I would highly recommend this restaurant, as I can easily say it was the best food I've ever had.

When asked if bartenders are RAMP certified (a requirement of my wedding venue) - I received this email from Sara : 

"RAMP is a silly online / multiple choice class about alcohol service that insurance companies make restaurant owners have their staff to complete in order to lower their insurance costs. Maybe 1 out of 50 venues still request it these days. It's a very dated requirement and a bit of a scam in my humble opinion.

Please confirm exactly what the venue needs from us before we move forward, this guideline makes me a bit nervous that we will be approved.

Thank you,
Sara"

I am not a picky person. I wouldn't normally even bother with leaving a one star review. But this place is just plain awful. Everything you have read in other reviews is true--no exagerations. The first thing we noticed was the cigarette smell on the second floor. We called down to the front desk to let them know about it and that we weren't smoking here so we wouldn't be charged extra for it. They offered to move us but I doubt it would have been better.

The floor was sticky. Honestly, there was a spot in front of the dresser in room 202 where my foot stuck so badly I had to use a lot of force to remove it. Stains on the carpet everywhere. Just plain gross.

And does it have to be? We own a shampooer. Don't hotels have shampooers? The only excuse is that the owners and staff just don't care.

Except for Pam at the front desk. We liked Pam. Pam at the front desk was very nice. If she knows what's good for her she'll be looking for other employment soon. She's too good to stay here.
Lester's at Clayton and Baxter has closed permanently as of 3 Nov 2014.

I have liked my last 2 stops with these guys. The coffee is good like my old coffee shop and the staff is friendly. They offer suggestions. I really  like this place. The one i went to was in suburban station.

I placed a delivery order at 6:44 and was told it would arrive through grub hub between 7:30 and 7:40. After they did not get there in the time frame, I called and they said it was out for delivery and would be there momentarily. Grub hub then updated the delivery time two more times delaying it further both times! It arrived at 8:11. The food was gross - nothing was even warm, let alone hot. It was soggy, not crispy and it all tasted bland- like no taste and over cooked. Order from somewhere else.

Bumping this up to 3 and a reluctant 1/2  because I do come here on a regular basis for my Thai fix. The owners/staff are nice, but the food needs to deliver.

Again, I am plagued by the lack of meat! 20% more meat and I might be singing the praises of this establishment.

Time will tell.

Pulled pork sandwich on Texas toast was as good as any I've ever had and better than a lot. Coleslaw was fantastic, seemed to be fresh made. The ribs were fall off the bone tender. All sides were good except baked beans--need more meat scraps in them. Texas toast was perfect. Waitress's were friendly and service was fast. We'll be going back and taking family and friends.
Enjoyed a nice Sunday brunch with a tall caramel latte.  Jalapeno cheddar bacon grits where on point.

Dan is definitely THE person you want helping you with a home purchase. He's absolutely the best to work with and I cannot recommend him more. I recently moved to St. Louis from California in December of 2016 with intent on buying a home. Being new to the area and never having purchased a home before, I had no idea where to start. Fortunately, I was steered in Dan's direction from all the positive reviews on Yelp and boy am I super glad! What could have been a very stressful, daunting, and grueling process was in actuality very low stress, encouraging, and streamlined. 

Dan was honest and looked out for my best interest. I truly felt like he listened to what I wanted in a home. He sent me listings to review that matched closely with my needs. If we saw homes in person that I thought I would love but he saw concerns with he voiced it right away and would recommend continuing the search instead of allowing me to pursue a house that wouldn't be in my best interest even though that could have meant a quicker sale. I'm so grateful for that as I could've easily been steered in a direction that may have not been the best due to my limited knowledge/experience. As a buyer, you can wholeheartedly trust that Dan has your best interest at heart.

Furthermore, he's VERY organized and works ridiculously hard to get you the house of your dreams. Dan communicated everything regarding the offer and contract in real time. He wasted no time in communicating important details to me regarding the purchase of my home which made the process much smoother and eased a lot of my anxiety. He was also available to answer any questions that I had in a more than timely matter. For example, Dan was able to get us under contract with my house because of just how amazingly on the ball he is with things. My house had multiple offers at the time so we had some stiff competition and little time to spare. He worked quickly and it's thanks to his speed and efficiency that I managed to get the winning bid! Even after getting under contract, he continued to make the process a breeze with updated timelines and keeping me on track with all the steps all the way through closing. 

I go could on and on about how wonderful he's been in the whole process, but that'd pretty much turn into and essay and no body has time to read that. Just do yourself a favor and save yourself a headache. Contact Dan and get the house that you've been looking for!
Roast pork sandwich with broccoli rabe and provolone. Extremely good and would definitely suggest.

If I could rate this place any less I would. My fiancée and I decided to order through the Chili's To-Go option on their website. We showed up at the appropriate time that was designated for us, and absolutely nobody paid attention to us. No one greeted us, but instead decided to converse amongst themselves laughing and joking around. We waited for 20 minutes with a waitress who continually walking passed us without a second glance so we left. I would recommend going to any other chili's except this one if you want a good experience.

Swanky. I was here last week for a corporate outing for a friends company. We had at 6:40 tee time and as we arrived there was a fog coming off of the rolling hills. I felt like I was at St. Andrews for a second! This course is WIDE OPEN. If you can't hit the fairways here, you need to hit the driving range. The course has some pretty intimidating hazards, like sand traps you need literal stairs to get down into. Theres a snack shop after the 9th hole and a beverage cart driving around the course so you're never at a loss for a drink or snack. 

I DID get a snooty little vibe from the crew though. We were given basically an itinerary that told us what times we should be at certain holes to make sure our pace was fast enough. We were playing a scramble, and were only slightly ahead of schedule, so I can tell you with 100% certainty that if we were all playing our own balls we would be way behind what theyre version of "on pace" would be. 

Other than that, the fairways were very well maintained, the greens were immaculate and the place was just clean and professional. 

I will be back.
Great place to eat. Loved the broccoli casserole .  The sandwiches were amazing .   Fun place, great service and amazing food.

Decent snowball joint where you can drive through for your chill fix.  They are heavy on the syrup pour and the sizes are large and cheap.  The ice consistency just wasn't my cup of tea and it seemed more like a snow cone instead of a snowball but that might have been due to the very heavy syrup pour.

With the diversity we have here, it's about time for something like the Boise International Market to make its debut! I've been in three times since its opening, and each visit gives me a hand full more reasons to return. Khave's coffees and teas are just outstanding, Joyful Tea is an absolute gem, and the Ethiopian and Eritrean food restaurant (I'm sorry I can't remember the name at the mo!), is just awesome. I can't wait for the rest of the shops to open, I just have to try them all! Excellent food and drink aside, the ethic behind the market is just what we need. This is genuinely a community institution with quite a bit to offer our city and I can't wait to see how it grows!

Good food, great prices and esspecally awesome portions. The ambiance of good ol fashion is in the air and the staff is friendly with just the perfect amount of feistiness. I really do recommend this place if you want to walk away full and happy.

One of my favorite breakfast spots because it's within walking distance from my home, the food is consistently delicious, the service is excellent, and you never have to worry about waiting longer than 25 minutes for quality food. I have introduced several of my city friends and they all fell in love. It's nice to have a restaurant like this in Crestwood!

Excellent pizza, especially if you are not in the mood for chain pizza.  Great hole in the wall place.  Delivery is quick and friendly.  A bit pricey, but well worth it.  Best pizza I've had since moving here from CA.  Highly recommend.

My husband's recently purchased truck began acting up, the cause couldn't be found. Someone where he worked recommended Sincere, so husband took truck there to have the problem diagnosed. They were quite busy, he had to leave the truck there overnite, no problems regarding vehicle break-ins or vandalism. When problem was diagnosed, the owner took his time to clearly explain the issues, & recommended that out of the possibilities, 1 or 2 sensors were usually responsible for the problem & to try replacing them 1st before he went deeper. Husband purchased both sensors elsewhere, did the repairs himself, & thanks to Sincere's diagnostics, truck is now running like a well oiled piece of machinery. We appreciate the extra time the owner gave us. We'd go back. Please note that we did not have them do any actual repairs so I can't attest to the quality of repair work, but I HAVE noticed they do quite a lot of business, so that speaks volumes too.  Might I also mention that the waiting room is very clean, has some beautiful plants, & a reasonably priced candy machine! Thank you, Sincere!

Happy fish, take some notes. The ceviche at Cuenelli's is amazing! The fish is cut into small pieces, little to no membrane on the fish, and the ceviche is flavorful and it is refreshing. Every bite allowed my tastebuds to go on a new adventure, from spicy to zesty to tangy. The onions and the accompaniments to the ceviche were also amazing and fresh. The fried yuca was crispy and although lacking in flavor, it was delicious when it was dunked into the juice of the ceviche. The service was attentive and the ceviche came out in ten minutes. Unlike a lot of Latin American restaurants, the exterior and the interior had a clean and modern look. Overall, the best Peruvian restaurant in Tampa!

Had to wait a few min to be seated. Sat on the patio. Large menu with very reasonable prices. Best tuna melt I've ever had. Friendly service. Very much like a classic luncheonette. Fantastic view of the water!
I went inside for a couple minutes and I couldn't stay due to the awful smell ;/ yuckkkkkkkk my clothes, skin and hair were smelling like fries!!! If you don't mind the stench go for it! ;)

Would not return. Grilled pork was like warm. Obviously microwaved. Sent it back. Microwaved it again. Got it back hot. But it was one of the toughest, dryest cuts of pork I have ever had. Terrible. They also gave us chicken instead of beef for our other dish. The only thai iced tea they offer is in a can. It was clean and the furnishings were up to date. That's the reason for two stars. But they seriously need to rethink food and service quality if they are going to stay in business.

I love Jones most for their baked mac & cheese and tomato soup/grilled cheese combo. Their take on American food is spot-on. 

My only complaint- it's a little steep for frequent lunches and I've only been to dinner a couple of times because of the high prices, but the food is always great, the service is great, and the atmosphere is great, so at least you're not wasting your money! 

Special Note: If you can get a seat by the fireplace, it's even better! If you can't get a table, the bar is usually available.

Special Treat: Sometimes it's nice to walk here from a neighboring restaurant and just get dessert- they are sooo goood!!
Well the food was good...and then a mouse scurried by our table. Better on the floor than in the food but oddly enough we were still presented with a bill. Come on Han Dynasty!

Love the onion pakoras and the chicken 65 appetizers!  The dosas are quite good and the Chana batura is a must try!!  The kothu porotta dish is really spicy (beware) ,  but not the typical that I have tried. 
Service is decent, I have never had a bad experience here. 

My go-to south-indian veggie food spot in the area!

I don't know, kids.. I'm just not feelin' the Chang.  

I went with three other people, and all of our food was mediocre... Like, I've had better Chinese takeout!  But at least with Chinese takeout, there are no delusions of grandeur (stupid sauce mixing at the table.. Puh-lease!  Macaroni Grill called, they want their shtick back...!) like 500 sharing plates on your table, Chang's this, Chang's that.  Get over yourself, P.F!

Anyway, we were there for like 500 hours bc every course was so drawn out and Chang-ed up (yeah, I've made it into a verb)... and so every one of our meals was luke warm when it arrived.  I'm like, umm aren't you cooking in a wok?  How is my food cold?  

Anyway - there were a couple things I did like.  The stir fried spinach with garlic was delish, and cooked really nicely, the tea selections were above average, and the "Great wall of Chocolate" dessert was a hit at our table :)

But overall...  I won't ever Chang again.

Mmmm mmmmm....   I initially went there and had a BLT and the bread was so tasty and fresh.  I had been looking for a more authentic tasting pizza and this place filled void. Needless to say, I eventually ordered two pies and OMG!!! The dough is just about as gourmet as you could get and the sauce has a sweetness to it that will keep you coming back for more.

I frequently shop at Nordstrom and decided to try the Nordstrom Grill for the first time today.  It's a great place for lunch, a little on the pricey side but the food was very good.  We were seated immediately (which is very rare at noon in Green Hills) and the service was great.  

I had the Chicken Paillard salad and my friend had the Crispy Chicken sandwich.  Both dishes were very tasty and priced around $13.  Nordstrom Grill is a great alternative to the Cheesecake Factory which is always busy and loud.  Prices are similar and the food is a little better in my opinion.

Terrible service and dirty tables. The 20-something year old girl behind the counter definitely acted like she had better things to do than to be working behind the counter during our visit. She needed continued prompts to get our order correctly and then neglected to make our smoothies (we had to remind her when 15 minutes had gone by and we still haven't received them). The tables were all dirty and we had to ask her if she could clean one for us. The coffee station was filthy. Our sandwiches were pretty good, but I'm not sure if we will be back. Customer service and satisfaction is not a priority here.
The server is attentive. The food is decent. However compare with the other choices nearby, their buffet has less option.

Bailey's Range is definitely among a list of my favorite places to bring friends or relatives visiting from out of town. I love the quirky interior, the extensive menu and of course the fun, boozy shakes. What I haven't loved (consistently) is the service. It's so hit or miss. Sometimes it's on, sometimes we're waiting 30 minutes for someone just to come to the table and greet us after we're seated. We're usually pretty laid back and/or not in a rush because we're catching up with friends or something and it doesn't really matter but, if I had to nit-pick SOMETHING, that would be it. That said, I did just have to call to have a receipt emailed to me (for work purposes/expenses) and they were incredibly helpful. So see, it's just hard to pick on them that much. 

As far as the food goes, I love the Buffalo Chicken sandwich - super juicy, has yet to be dry like chicken can sometimes be in patty form. The "Aw Jam" was pretty great too! We love trying new sauces with our fries (pro-tip: they're all good!) and the milkshake with the rumchata in it is seriously to die for. SO. GOOD.

Think I found my new spot in town.  Ish is the man if you're looking to get groomed up!  I came here to clean up before an interview for my grad program, and the barbers here proved great at doing just that.

Honest service at a fair price. My immediate family has entrusted Reno Vulc for years. We decided to call and get a quote for a 90,000 mile service on a Subaru Impreza after hearing an outrageous price from the Subaru dealership. 
The only reason I didn't give 5 stars is because they forgot to change a blinker bulb I had asked to be done. I noticed once I was a block away then turned around to ask if they'd charged me. When I returned they offered to do it for free, but I had somewhere to be.
This gesture is not one you'd receive at other locations. I will definitely be back.

I was excited to try this place after the Yelp reviews, came by with the fam for Sunday brunch, the hostess did not offer good service at all, 20 minute wait even though a real tables were empty .... This place always has reservations so better call ahead. 
The ambience is great, not very family friendly though. No kids menu and for all you parents and babysitters, the restroom does not have a diaper changing table. They'll recommend a few things on the menu for kids. There were a few other families with toddlers with the same issues. Although the Yelp page says it's good for kids it's really not.
The waitress offered was sweet, we got the soup (3/5), arancino (4.5/5 but small portion), huevos rancheros (4/5 but greasy), veggie melt (3/5 bred was greasy and the onions were too sweet it was off putting) and the kettle chips (very nice thin cut but a bit too greasy).
Overall service was slow but friendly. The savory dishes seemed a bit too greasy but the menu is well though of, very creative dishes. The sweet dishes/desserts are a real treat and worth it.
Would I come back? Yes, only to try out the dinner menu or a holiday special brunch but not with kids.

Tons of really cool stuff, but very pricey.  I saw a lot of great mid century decor, but it was all priced way higher than other antique malls I've been to around the Nashville area.   If you don't mind paying an arm and a leg, there are some really cool things to see.

So glad to have an affordable but beautiful massage spa in Rittenhouse.

Walnut Street is a busy street so I expects a certain amount of street noise or noise from the yoga/barre studio above BUT I am happy to say I didn't hear a thing (and I know for a fact there was class in progress at the time of my massage).

I loved the personal touch of being able to select your own aromatherapy scent as well as type of  music. And it was so nice to get a little chocolate truffle and moist towelette to go (to help with off any excess oil) along with a glass of water.

The studio itself is very beautiful...very warm and inviting. The temperature of the room was perfect and the lighting was perfect. Oh and I also liked that my therapist covered my eyes when it was time for me to lay on my back (that way I wasn't disturbed by any lighting). 

The massage itself (by Emily) was fantastic. I left feeling rejuvenated and very relaxed.

All in all, every little detail was carefully thought out to give you an amazing experience.

Party of 6 early on a Saturday night, 5pm, or first time in Reno.  Venue looks very promising from the outside, with outdoor seating and an upscale appeal. We were seated immediately, but as soon as we turned the corner from the hostess station, the place was a turnoff. A bit too loudly playing music, but the mostly twenties crowd seemed not to mind it

Our table surface reeked of sour dishrags, very off-putting.  We ordered drinks, took a while, the sangria looked like a blush wine and did not taste like sangria.

Our waitress was pleasant but detached, no interest in boosting our experience or displaying a personality, the smile and pleasantries seemed forced.  We ordered 2 appetizers: onion rings and nachos.  They were served pretty quickly but we were not provided with plates, which made for a messier experience than it should have.  Curiously, the check noted "no plates" for the apps and we were perplexed by this. 

The entrees were just okay. Nobody was thrilled but it was all edible.  The burrito came with chips and salsa, according to the menu, but no salsa was served. When questioned,  the waitress said the salsa was inside the burrito.  Oh, okay a pile of chips but nothing to dip them in.  We asked for boxes for leftovers which were provided, but no bag for carrying them.

All told, we had enough to eat but once we left we had to laugh because we had ALL wanted to leave when we were seated but nobody spoke up. Generally disappointed, in large part because we all liked the outside look of the venue but the experience didn't deliver.

The food/price  is pretty decent. The service on the other hand is ridiculous. I have been in 3 times, and each time I find myself completely annoyed by the immature "playing" that goes on with the entire staff. It's obnoxious, and definitely not someplace to come to enjoy a nice dinner. There are less childish activities at Chuck E. Cheese. Twice now, I have received food before receiving my drink because no one is here to "work." This place will not last.

My favorite dish here is the two way salad with the Curry Chicken and Grape Chicken salads.  I came here today for lunch and noticed the size of the scoops changed from the medium scoop to a MINI scoop.  It was barely a nibble of each of the chicken salads.  I left hungry and had to order more food to go.  Quit being cheap and go back to the medium scoop.  I feel ripped off.

Honestly came here with the folks and was taken away by the Nostalgia.

So glas I got to come in and see all the Forrest Gump references. Also i got a shrimp platter to kind of get a feel for the place.

They were surprisingly really well done. This place is like the swiss chalet of all things shrimp.

We dont have one in Toronto- so it was great to try out!

The gift shop was nice as well.

This restaurant is right off Watson, but offers other entry ways from side roads. There is also a drive through. 

You order at the counter, they call your name to get your food (like a bread co). Seating is limited so be ok with sharing a big table with strangers. There are two double seat tables and a table for parties that are 3 people or more. 

I've been twice and have enjoyed my food every time. The bacon is ultra thick and crispy, and the gravy is so good, and has a lot of flavor but isn't over salted. The iced coffee is great, and has coffee Ice so you don't get watered down coffee. I have asked for one refill at both visits and have gotten them. 

I have a very "spirited" son and he loves this place. There are crayons, as well as an open kitchen to watch. He also loves peeking in the bakery window and seeing what the back of the house is doing.
I loved eating here but they appear to be closed. Tried to eat there today and couldn't.

For a handsfree car wash, this has to be one of the best car wash! It's a little bit pricey but you get the best bang for your buck. The buffer leaves your car shining like new, and the tire cleaning option really cleans the rim and rubber part of your tires. You want regret spending $16 on a good car wash that lasts you about a week or so. 

They provide you with drying towels in case there are water spots left on your vehicle, which I never had to do; or if you want to clean the inside of your car using your own car cleaning products.

The food and service is great. A suggestion for improvement: there should be a drink menu, it's uncomfortable to ask bar tenders about the margarita and wine choices and their prices. Help us out, have a menu!

I love sweets and cinnamon rolls but I was very disappointed with this place. The rolls are large but dry and the icing is overly sweet and you can crunch on the sugar granules. I tried a plain and one with various toppings and they were pretty disgusting.

My dad has a few feral cats in his backyard that he's grown accustomed to having now that his granddaughters come over and like to watch them play around. He called Pet Community Center and they provided him with traps and showed him how to use them in order to trap them and bring them in to the center to get them spayed, neutered and rabies shot. I picked them back up and the cats didn't seem like they skipped a beat. It's a very new and clean facility and I'd suggest anyone who needs any assistance with their pet to go there and make a donation as well. Great Place!!!

N and I went for dinner with a couple who are from Texas, and they grudgingly admitted that the BBQ was pretty authentic. This pleased me, as it was also tasty. 

Between the four of us we sampled the short rib, the sausage, the brisket, and the enchiladas. Our house vegetarian was thrilled with the cheese enchiladas, and we carnivores enjoyed all the meats, although the short rib was definitely best. Sandwiches were under $10 and came with a side of fries. Good fries, but not outstanding. In Philly your fries have to be something special to stand out.

The night's big winner was the endless chips and salsa. I don't know for sure, but I suspect they make their own chips. In any case, the chips were fried crisp and dusted with cayenne. The green tomatillo salsa was good and the red chipotle salsa was fantastic; both were pleasantly spicy, but not mouth burningly so. As advertised, every time a bowl was empty the waitress offered to refill it. The Texans were miffed that there was a charge for chips and sals at all, but even they had to admit that the $2,50 was well spent.

Although El Camino Real is vegetarian friendly, there are almost no actual vegetables to be had. But the meat is so good it's hard to care.
Wow, just wow. Had them swap out my battery and this is what I saw when I noticed rattling under the hood. Bolt is snapped. Battery is clean but everything else is a mess

been a few times.  brisket has improved in s tpa over what I use to get at Carrollwood restaurant much more lean. sides consistently good  although may vary slightly in taste and consistency between visits.  parking can be a bitch like newhere in s tpa. depends on time of visit

Crazy Sushi is by far my new favorite sushi restaurant in the Rittenhouse area! The rave reviews from other members were spot on! I went last night and received a free edamame with my yelp check in. As our main course we ordered the Odessa Roll, The AK 47 (daily special) and the Kk Roll. All of the rolls were delicious and the presentation was excellent! The overall decor the restaurant is very modern and not as dull as it may seem from the outside. The service was just ok but I'm looking past any flaws in that because the sushi was just too good! I will definitely be back!

I have been to this Starbucks multiple times and everytime the same thing happens, they make drinks out of the ordered in which they were received. This last time was my absolute final straw with this location. The woman behind me had order 5 drinks and had gotten all of them before me, as well as the 3 people behind me. When I asked if my order had made it through because the people behind me had gotten their orders, the man behind the counter said oh yes it is right here is is coming up. Well, 3 more orders later, again from people who order after me, I finally received my iced coffee. And it only took 20 minutes to get. I would definitely advise anyone to purchase from a nearby Starbucks rather than this one.

Very nice lil farm stand. Reasonable prices. They habe some morunusual items like white eggplant and cactus fruit. They also hve a grest variety of honeys. With honeycomb, bee pollen, etc. Some jams, corn relish, hot sauces. But the fruit is the big draw. Avocados (Florida and Haas),  various apples, pluots, etc. Deals for stuff that's going off in the back ($1 a basket). Nice people.

Quick review/thoughts- The Zombie lab escape room was very fun, and challenging. it took full advantage of the theme and showed a great deal of creativity and really showed a eye for details. 

long review/thoughts

going to Fox In A Box, was only my second attempt at doing an escape room, so i am still a little new to the concept. however i can say i left extremely impressed with what i was given. upon entering, when my party and I showed up, everyone working there was pleasant. they made sure we understood both the room we where going into and the general escape room idea. before entering the room, we were shown a short video, that both explained the concept of the room, and made the whole thing more immersive.

the room its self was truly a sight to see. they had clearly done a great deal of time and effort to create a fun but kinda unsettling atmosphere. the room provided many challenges and required some out of the box thinking, and did stump my party more then once. however the challenges never felt unnecessary difficult, and the hints given were spot on to helping us. 

if you are looking for an escape room, or for something fun and exciting for a  small group of people, i highly suggest trying this place out.

Gosh, I feel like giving Villagio zero stars based on my experience this evening, but that wouldn't be fair as I have been there many times and most weren't as bad as tonight.

Villagio is a very comfortable place to watch a movie because of the reclining chairs. The food is OK. Nothing special. If we get anything, it's a simple pizza and a beer or two. A 17% tip is added to each bill, whether you've received good service or not.

Unfortunately, the last two times I have been the service has been just awful. Tonight, while purchasing my ticket at the front desk I was told to order my food/drink in the theater  ... but I never managed to do that. I tried to get the attention of a waiter. No luck. The only person who came by my seat apparently couldn't help because she told me, "I'm a server. I can't take your order." OK - please help find someone who can! The next time this same person came by my seat trying to give me a pizza that I didn't order, I asked her again if she could help me and I got the same "No, I'm just a server." answer. She said she had asked a waiter to come, but alas... no waiter. When the movie finally started, I just figured she'd probably done me a favor. Saved me $$ and a mandatory 17% tip for nonexistent service. The movie was great and the chair was comfy, so it wasn't all bad.

Now, yes, I could have gone to the bar and placed an order myself when I finally got tired of waiting for that nowhere-to-be-seen waiter, but that brings me to the previous time I was at Villagio. We were a group of four, sitting at the bar and waiting for the movie to start. There were at least 3 employees at the back of the bar, yapping away and pretending to do shots (seriously, they were pretending to do shots!). Oh, and they also completely ignored us as we sat watching them, very amused. Finally, a female bartender (who had been busting her butt helping all of the customers at the bar by herself while these guys messed around) came over and we actually joked about how it was kind of ridiculous to have 4 people behind the bar and yet no one interested in helping the customer. Apparently a lot of people at Villagio have a job. One job. And are completely unable to assist with anything else. Either that, or the majority just aren't that interested in providing customer service. I think it's the latter.

Sigh. I really like Villagio because of the seats, but I am getting frustrated with the poor service.

This is the best rib spot in the city.  It's no surprise, that the people are lining up to get these ribs. Best quality ribs, very tender, a lot of meat, the sauces are delicious. Everything about this place rocks. Drive through is very efficient, with all the traffic they have, it runs very quickly and smoothly.  The service is always top notch. I highly recommend king rib.

This is the best boba tea I've found in Tucson. They're quick and cheap. We always get the taro tea, which is delicious and purple! Unfortunately the boba aren't as flavorful as Quickly, which is a chain in many major cities. But that's not enough to keep me away!
I had lunch here last week and it was great! Service was good and I really loved my grilled Chicken and turnip greens! My son had the chili and loved it!

ok-no previous reviewer. There is a Jacuzzi was 5 steps aways from a king sized bed. With mirrors on the walls and ceiling with running strobe lighting weaving through it. The hotel is conveniently located to RNO Airport with shuttle service. Was just there on business, amenities are bare minimal. however the event room we booked was a refurbish of a High Roller loft/suite. Beautiful view of the city and pool. 
Downstairs at the cafe-order The Boss and bring fear it's HUGE. The same owners of the Rio of Las Vegas, so bring your shades there are some mighty brght colors here. The newly renovated parts were nice, there's even a bar/club my fellow colleagues and I popped into. Refreshing, it was "industry night", we're software industry people...nonetheless they welcomed us at no charge. Despite the pocket protectors and polo shirts.  
Pass the cheese, this place rocks :)

This truck is something to experience. The portions are massive for $10 and the food is cooked with heart. I really enjoyed his chicken. Only downside is the wait. If there are about 8 people in line ahead of you, expect about a 35-45min wait. Something to experience in Philly for sure!

After reading so many positive reviews on Yelp, I just had to check this place out.

Upon walking in, I could tell that Mood Cafe was unique. The man behind the counter just about welcomed us with open arms, asking us if we'd been there before, if we knew what chaat was, etc.

My friends and I looked at each other, then placed our orders of chaat and lassi. What is chaat? To this day, I still have no idea. It's a colorful mixture of spicy meat, vegetables, crispy pieces, yogurt, almonds, chickpeas, potatoes, dried fruit, and about six different sauces. Never in my life have I experienced so many flavors and textures in a single dish. Fortunately, the mixture is both delicious and satisfying. The spices deliver just the right kick to pair perfectly with a sweet, cool lassi. I'll be back to try the other chaats. In the end, what really sets Mood Cafe apart is the exceptional service. The man behind the counter is friendly and loves to share his crazy concoctions with people whether they are first-timers or longtime customers. Heck, some of Starr's restaurant staff could learn a thing or two.

Mood Cafe is a neighborhood gem. So if you're craving something daring, give it a shot!

I have been here a few times but this was the best, I should probably mention that Tuesday is 3 dollar pint night. I had the sidekick supreme and the people next to me recommended the spicy ranch ( house made) for dipping, amazing,try it

My trip to Pub and Kitchen was an unplanned lunch after some hanging in Rittenhouse Square on a perfect fall afternoon.  

Outdoor seating was a must.  

I was looking at a menu and it was rather small and read in an unimpressive way.  

The waiter sold me on a burger which was their special on this day, the meat came blended from a high end butcher in NYC.  Supposedly he had never until now let this blend of meat out of the city.  Pub and Kitchen had exclusivity to this meat which peaked my interest in what can a "high end butcher" from nyc do that I haven't seen before with a burger.  

The burger came with caramelized onions on a bun.  The meat lived up to the height of exclusive beef.  Although I don't plan on spending 18$ for a burger again anytime soon.  My tastebuds were more then satisfied.  I will describe this meal as I would when I describe the eating experience of any of my favorite foods... when the burger was gone, I was a little bit sad.

DISGUSTING!!! I ordered out last night: Sweet/Sour Chicken, Chicken Fried Rice and Egg Rolls. The egg rolls had some weird meat, wasn't pork, I can tell you that. Needless to say, they didn't taste very good, and this was the best part of the order. The chicken fried rice was steamed rice, not fried, still white not even browned. The chicken was rough and not looking too good. The sweet/sour chicken was horrible. The chicken pieces were thin little strips with way too much batter. It was all fried batter and very little chicken. This is the type of chicken I would expect to get at a KFC. This is the first time I ordered food and threw it all out. I can't believe people eat here. I am new to STL and if anyone can let me know where to go for good Chinese food, I would greatly appreciate it.

AMAZING service!!! We wanted to express our gratitude and appreciation especially to Bert. He was great help to us being our first time and then to find out he's the director. He runs this place beyond what you would normally expect from a fast food joint. He made this place a happy environment. All staff was very happy to help and even came around to fill our drinks. We weren't only blown away at the service but the food is amazing!! Definitely our new favorite place! Even has a kid jungle gym for the kids
Thank you again, 
Joshua and Ashlee
This place is so cute! It's insanely busy on weekends, but for good reason. The food is awesome. The servers are really nice. Great breakfast foods.

The Epcot of Liquor!! Eh...not quite. More like the Walmart. 

So I don't mind that you can actually find some hidden gems on their deeply discounted sale rack. And I can't argue with a $1.00 bottle of white wine to keep around for nasty red wine spills during get-togethers (instant stain remover). However, you can spend hours looking for one damn bottle as they just stack boxes at random. Their staff really isn't helpful in find or suggesting liquor. I've had several staff members look at me like I had three eyeballs when I've asked for common wine brands or varieties. 

Beer selection here varies constantly and isn't great to start with. You can buy plenty of standard beers there, but their craft brews are few and far between. Their beer isn't really consistent. ACTUALLY, nothing here is consistent. Their selection is constantly changing (which wouldn't be a problem if they weren't constantly running out of some pretty basic wines and beers). Their times aren't consistent (Sometimes they stay open til 10; sometimes they close 15-30 minutes early). Their staff isn't consistent (Sometimes, they're at least nice, even if they can't help me find what I'm looking for. Buttt sometimes, I swear the fact that some poor soul is waiting in their checkout line is a fate worse than death for their cashiers).

When they are open and actually carry what I'm looking for, I can look past the rude staff to pick up a few bottles or cases for my home bar at a pretty great price before popping back to the Puritanical land of PA liquor/beer separation.

I held back from giving one star because we didn't get a chance to eat. I'm feeling nicer today than I did last night. Yes. It was a very busy night. Here is how the events went down at the door:

No special greeting like, "Have you ever been here?", just the words "two of you". 

Yes. the two of us. How long is the wait?

"35 minutes"... nothing like, "We're happy you're hear...you see how great the response is...we're doing our best sir to get everyone seated as fast as possible...but it might be 35 minutes or so". Just a flat... "35 minutes" the 7 second answer is way better than the 1 second. 

Ok. How long is it taking to get food out after we've been seated?

"about 45 minutes"..... I wasn't asked what I was thinking of ordering. Just an assumption.

May I see a menu?

Another assumption... "We stop taking preorders at 4 pm...blah, blah". I wanted to see the menue to assess what might take less time to serve. I KNOW deep dish takes more time. I was open to trying something else. 

Ok. I'm not willing to wait an hour & fifteen minutes just to get my meal. 

All I heard was.... "sorrreeee"...

I go out to eat for the experience..... the food is only part of that. Make me feel WELCOMED and not like "oh no. here are more people". After parking blocks away, it was an unsatisfactory walk back to the car. We went somewhere else & it too was on a wait. But we were welcomed nicely, invited to have a drink, sit outside, to review a menu, & once we were sat, the service was divine.  Sooorrreee 312. I'm not eager to head back.

Well i guess its a good thing, there isn't a lot of competition on the mainline for vietnamese food because if there were - they would be in trouble. 

After reading the reviews, we decided to give this place a try. I grew up eating vietnamese food - so I know good, bad, and fair. SO far we ordered the beef and pork vermicelli. What can I say - super bland, barely any veggies - too many noodles. I don't have much incentive to go back. You can always tell if a vietnamese place is good by their vermicelli and their Pho Broth. But after this, I don't think i want to try it - I'll just make the drive to Upper Darby or the city. However it is a cute place.

This is the second time we have eaten here. Both times the food was excellent, from the fresh, warm chips w/ both salsa and bean dip to the delicious chimichanga. They would've gotten 5 stars except for they sat us in the bar. Usually that would be fine, but today we felt like we were in the employees break room. The LOUD bartender (Leo) wouldn't shut up and the waitress was only a little better than okay. At times there were as many as 5 or 6 employees standing around-even climbing up onto one of the booths right next to us putting up Christmas decorations. That didn't change the fact that this is the best Mexican food we have found in NOLA. Just wish they would pay attention to details-$34 for lunch leads me to expect a little more professionalism.

I was in on a Wednesday evening during a pacers playoff game, it was packed, loud and fun. Ate dinner at the bar, beer selection is overwhelming, but I guess that is the purpose!   Food was awesome, hangover burger and fresh cut fries, fries are not something dumped out of a bag into a deep fryer like most joints of this nature. The wings are good but hard to eat, they are literally the entire chicken wing, honey bourbon sauce was great!  I'll be back soon.

Good burgers. We don't have Whataburger in California, so I decided to try one here. Was not disappointed. Good to try a different chain for once. Something different I noticed is that while I'm eating, the employees would regularly come ask for a refill or present to you any napkins or ketchup that you need. Good customer service!

How is this place not packed? All. The. Time. ??? Definitely best burger in The Quarter. I'm assuming best in New Orleans. Maybe the best ever. In the history of always. Go here. Enjoy the food. Keep it open for when I come back.

This is the tastiest ramen in Tucson. The broth is rich and filling. The egg preparation is the only thing lacking in this soup..overcooked, cold, and plopped in as afterthought, not seasoned. Chashu is very yummy. Way better than Oban. Karage-don is also very good. The service is busy but friendly. Go for weekday lunch to avoid the lines at this new and popular spot. I'll be back many times.

Super friendly and helpful staff, and be prepared to get dirty as you're provided a bib, gloves and scissors to tackle the hot delicious bags of seafood that come out. You can choose the type of cooking broth, spice level and order seafood by the pound. We rounded out our seafood boil with corn, sausage (small amount of thinly sliced garlic sausage) and potato, seafood rice (a decent amount of shrimp and scallops in buttery rich rice) and crispy calamari. If you prefer not to have a mountain of seafood carnage on your table, you can ask for a bucket to toss it in.. almost everything is composted, so you can feel good getting messy and filling up on seafood! Only downside is this place is smaaaaaall, so they dont take reservations.. try to pop in during an odd time and you may luck out and get a table without waiting for hours.

A great place for fresh food and a neat little bakery. Breakfast is fantastic, the signature dish "eggs provencale" is great. Very fresh and satisfying. 

The earlier the better, highly recommend you check them out!

Great burgers. I always mean to try the cheesesteak, but can't break away from the Charlie Brown, which I've been ordering since Spot was a cart on Drexel's campus.

It can get crowded in there, but that's what happens when you're serving what is in the running for best burger in the city.

Don't sleep on their specials either - the corn dogs were great!

Came here for my birthday dinner after a local on the beach recommended the place. So glad we did! The coconut shrimp appetizer was delicious. I got the crab cakes and my husband got the steak. We both loved our dishes and left super stuffed. Don't forget the complimentary rolls! Service was nice and quick for a Saturday night.

This place is alright.  They don't have many bakery goods and I did try the ube cake to go.  It looks delicious but taste like a regular cake, I barely tasted the ubeness.  I got the "taho", I guess I'm used to the clear very soft tapioca balls in the Philippines and not the chewy black ones but the main flaw with the taho was the texture of the tofu.  It's like lightly firm tofu when it should be buttery soft, silken tofu.  Where it just breaks apart when you slurp it like soup.  That's how I've always had it when I was in the Philippines of when my mom buys me some in Hawaii Chinatown.  The syrup was on point though.
My family has been going to Rick's for years.  He is friendly and gets the job done correctly and efficiently every time! I can't say enough about how good of a mechanic he is.
Best kept secret Italian in the area. Fabulous home-made pastas and excellent service.

My favorite pastry spot in the RTM.  Biscotti is amazing, they serve La Colombe Coffee and they never run out.

Short and sweet.

Hands down this is my favorite nail salon in Nashville. Rose, John and the rest of the staff are very friendly and their service is outstanding. They originally opened further down West End (where the Homewood Suites is) and I am SO GLAD they re-opened. Their new location is convenient and their prices are fair. I highly recommend!!!

I was happy to use the Tampa Coast Bike Share system! This is a great way for tourists to see the City and residents another way to travel the roads.

My wife and I live in Channelside, so we wanted to bike and walk around to get a feel for the different areas since we moved in. Granted we were mostly close to downtown, which is where most of the stations are.

It is very convenient to have this! It's much easier than renting a bike for the day, since then you have to rent a lock as well.

It seems like stations are reasonably close together in the downtown area. As others have stated, it would be helpful to have stations visible from popular streets and it would be helpful to have stations well marked.

We tried to go to one station that we never found. We were on the right corner, but the station must have been hidden.

Overall i think this is great for all types of people who want to get out and see the city!!!

So I ordered flowers from Pennypack Flowers for a friend & when they arrived they were the wrong color & vase.  I called to ask if there was a mix-up & was told that they simply ran out so they sent this instead... Are you kidding me?  I asked why i wasn't notified to see if i was ok with the changes the incredibly rude manager, Lisa, told me she was too busy to deal with me because she had 3 weddings & a funeral.  I was stunned & she finally, & impolitely, said she could send new flowers on Monday but... here's where it gets good... she would have to send the driver back today to pic up the incorrect flowers.  What???!!!  Take them back from my friend?  Are you high??  (Didn't actually say that but should have).  So she again informed me that she was too busy & crudely & abruptly hung up.
So I went to the shop after work where she was even ruder & told me I had a bad attitude!  Gee... I wonder why?
Anyway... Got nowhere because she obviously doesn't give a damn about an $75 flower order.  
So please... Do not use Pennypack Flowers unless you want to be treated badly when they send the wrong flowers.  I only wish I could give them minus stars... They don't even deserve 1.
Could contend for the best thin in STL if they would give you an option to have something other than that awful provel cheese.  Won't come back.

I was recommended to try this place out (particularly the cheese curds!) by my hairdresser. Really happy that my hubby and I gave it a try!

We were fortunately able to enjoy a flight of beer and a couple appetizers outside one beautiful night on their outdoor eating patio. They have a ton of different craft beers on draft and I love the fact that they offer flights- my hubby and I's favorite thing to get when at a restaurant/bar type of place. We like to talk and compare the different ones we order and then we rank our top fave to least fave. It makes for a fun date!

The Cheese Curds were very yummy! Definitely loved the dipping sauce that came with- it is kinda runny, so you may get some drips on your shirt. We also ordered the Blue Cheese Chips which were equally just as good. The service was great- would definitely go back again!

Boy do I love this place! I started going here before it got popular but it is still amazing and worth the wait. Great beer and wine selection, the food is perfect (light fair like sandwiches and salads, cheese, and bruschetta - which you must try!). Great to hang out on Sunday as well - check out Sunday school!!
Great little sushi joint! The sushi is so fresh. I highly recommend the Ocean and Bronze Pebble!
This restaurant failed to proceed my order 2 times at took 15 minutes to make my food.
Honest, fair, reasonable, prompt. Highly recommend. Yelp reviews helped us choose this company. Thank you

I had KungPow shrimp for lunch here, it had just right among of hot spice in my meal, and it is very good portion for just $6. Also I got a choice of soul hot soup or egg drop soup as a starter. It's not a fince place but it is worm and clean. Food come out pertty quick. I will come back again to try their dinner sometime in the future.
Oh, they have a pertty good selection of Chinese vegetarian food.

I love this little place. High points: awesome drink specials and awesome food. Decent service, can be hit or miss sometimes. A great place to go with friends to kick off the rest of the night. Their late night menu is great too.
Very good sushi spot, tucked away in a small strip mall. Gyoza and the Spider roll were top notch.  Enjoyed it thoroughly.  Staff was very friendly.  Fyi, this is a byob place.

I got my hair cut here once.  I actually did like the cut/style even though the salon was a bit dilapidated.  I have called and tried to get back in, but they don't answer their phone.  I have left three messages to call me back.  So frustrating.  I do not even want to go back now. Not professional.
AWESOMENESS!!!    great  authentic Szechuan food... friendly service certainly one of my favorites. Twice cooked pork, Cumin lamb,  yum......Chengdu classics all good also..

We haven't been by here in some years but the TriCity shopping center is awaiting demolition and renovation. We were instantly greeted and seated.  We ordered the cheese dip(queso blanco).
