This is my go-to neighborhood spot.  I LOVE that it's BYOB and the servers are always very laid-back and nice. It's almost like going to a friends for lunch/dinner. I recommend the thanksgiving dinner special if they offer it. Their mac-n-cheese is very yummy too. I've also had their teriyaki salmon dish with soba noddles and it was amazing (more gourmet than I anticipated from this place!)

ON TAKE OUT
Fast, consistent, and so easy to order through Seamless Web. A great option when you don't feel like cooking and want to avoid delivery fees. I've ordered a wrap and a burger 

ON THEIR BAKE GOODS/ICE CREAM
Probably the best Peanut Butter Pie I've ever had. Period, nuf said.
Their Apple Pie is huge and so comforting served warm with vanilla ice cream.
They offer a large variety of ice cream and I've never tried any flavors that didn't hit the spot.

I really enjoy this place for lunch.  They have very limited seating, which is kind of annoying since I have to walk a bit of a ways to get here from work, just to turn around and get back to my desk to eat.  Although, I will say that the few tables they have here is better than the center city location, they only have a few stools and a long table against a wall.

I really like to make my own creation, I usually get the salmon with various veggies such as the papaya, jicama, carrots, etc.

I also like either the spicy mayo or the peanut sauce as my sauce.  The only reason I have not trued the other sauces, is because there is no description of them to be found and the restaurant is usually pretty busy when I am there, so I feel like I am holding people up if I ask. The staff usually wants to get you order quickly and get to the next customer.

I also enjoy either the fried shallots or garlic as my crunch.

I do which there were more meat/fish options.  I would love to have more sushi quality fish in my sushirtto.  It is kind of disappointing when the only non-fried fish option and there are no real sushi fish options either since everything is cooked. However, even though I wish there were more options as stated above, I do always enjoy the salmon.

I love Willensky's and came here often. Until I had carbon monoxide issues and spent over $100 on alarms. 
   I bought three alarms and put them up.  When the gas company came over to double check the furnace, they checked the alarms - all of them were from 2008.  Carbon monoxide alarms are only good for 4-5 years, they said. 
    I'd already opened them and they were working, so they wouldn't let me bring them back.  
    So if you're buying something that doesn't expire - like a hammer or a key - you're fine. But be careful of paint, oil or anything else that might break down over time.

This was our first time at Gusto's and we were very pleased.  Our waiter, Tim, was terrific.  He was attentive, got all of our order correct, and paid attention to all the details. 

My husband had the stuffed mushrooms and loved them. I had the beet salad.  Just the right amount of dressing. Basically a spinach salad with beets, orange sections, walnuts and goat cheese. Delicious.  For my entree I had the sea bass special that was served on vegetable rice. I love the rice!  Almost had a risotto texture that was great. The sea bass was perfectly cooked but a bit bland. 

For dessert we shared spumoni. I also had a cappuccino. 
All in all the atmosphere, the food, and the service were great. It was fairly quiet as it was a midweek night.  I would recommend this restaurant for a nice dinner at it with friends or a date night.

Sometimes it's 9:30 pm in East Nashville and you still want to go to a nice place for wine and maybe a snack....welcome to Butcher & Bee! 

Keeping doors open past 10 PM on a holiday Sunday, we three took full advantage of a nice reasonably priced wine list and a great mezzo list. Selecting four for $16 our taste buds were well satisfied along with a nice rose'. Greeted by the proprietor and cared for by an attentive and pleasantly quirky waitress, we'll be back to try a full meal.

(Prices @ B&B are at the higher end, but we are on vacation and doing a bit of splurging.)

I had so much fun here! I was in NOLA for a bachelorette party (what else right??) and we were walking down Bourbon after the drag show we watched for a fun place to drink and dance. The music coming out of this place was fun so we knew this had to be one of our spots that night. 

We walked into the Cupid shuffle. Not a lot of people knew the steps but people were trying! 

Great cover band inside. Did a really good job of having different genres, old and new. Really diverse crowd. There are a lot of shot girls going around, but I didn't try any (I try not to have my drinks have sugar in it since my old age is showing with my hangovers the next morning!) 
Prices for a vodka soda was decent (about 7$.) 

I would come here for a chill and fun time. You'll drink and dance the night away. Everyone was having fun here. Check it out!
Great place to rent a car!! The whole staff makes it a quick and pleasant experience. Best value on rentals!

Truly authentic and amaaaazzzing Thai food!  We've eaten here dozens of times, often for large family gatherings with at least 10 of us.  Service is always attentively top-notch.  Food is fresh, perfectly seasoned, and consistently awesome.  Lunch specials include an appetizer, soup or salad, and entree - all for right around $10 - and we all leave feeling like we got a bargain!  Love this place!

Really enjoyed our breakfast at Two Chicks. I had the Under the Sea omelette and it was delicious. If you enjoy seafood and Brie this is the choice for you! Creamy grits were amazing and the mimosa was delicious as well. Prices were very reasonable. Would definitely visit again

Great breakfast! Service was top notch! 
The portions were HUGE! if you want a great breakfast stop in... good coffee too
Food is great. they tend to be busy on weekends and delivery takes slightly longer than most places. If you don't mind the wait the food is worth it.

I really like Ethiopian food and was excited to eat here when visiting Indianapolis.  Their food was good and similar in price to other Ethiopian restaurants that I've experienced, and the staff was very kind.  Unfortunately, service was VERY poor.  We came in around 3:00 on a Saturday so it wasn't very busy, but it took a really long time to order and then to get our bill.  Also, they only provided one roll of Injera per person and while they did replenish it, we were completely out for almost 15 minutes before we received more.  Our water glasses were consistently empty for 10-15 minutes (even when asking for refills) as well.  If I return to Indianapolis, I'll probably try a different Ethiopian restaurant.  It took almost 2 hours for our party of 5 to have lunch and pay which is just too long.
4 stars for the late night tasty hot dogs. I might feel different about the place if I was sober but I'll stand by my review at 1 am!

Really great people. They really care about you and your tattoo and seems as excited about it as you are. Went it for a consultation - I forgot the guy I met with's name but he was really lovely and made sure he had every detail about my tattoo. Made me feel really good about getting it done here.

Good pedicure but the lady is NOT friendly at all! I feel like an inconvenience.  I've been here several times previously to this time and it has been better but with this experience - I will be looking for another Nail Salon.

Uhaul moving help is a scam! I placed my order only to be told by the movers hours later they were not available. I went to the site and immediately canceled the order. It's been over a week and no refund. It was difficult to contact them and once I did I was told that once my funds are available in some account they have for me, I can then request a refund. This is absurd. I have to spend so much time just to get my money back for a service they can't provide? Horrible operation and customer service. This is for the mover help only. I've been to the uhaul location here in Hendersonville and the people were nice and helpful. I wrongly assumed their moving help would be the same. Save your money and hire a mover directly! 0 stars for moving help, scam!

I love this place! Chicken pad thai is awesome and very generous portion. Prices are reasonable. Staff is very friendly and easy going. I keep wanting to try other dishes, but it is so hard to not get my pad thai.

We were able to walk to Marti's from our hotel, although the street it's on is under construction so it's not the prettiest view.  You enter through a side door, directly into the bar, which is small with a few tables.  It's pretty in the light but pretty dark when the sun sets.  The bathrooms divide the bar and main dining room, and the main dining room only holds 12 tables, making it a very intimate setting, which we loved.  We were celebrating our wedding anniversary and I made the res over OpenTable, asking for a quiet table if possible... not knowing that every table was quiet :)  Our waiter (whom I'm ashamed to say I don't remember his name) was great, very attentive and great with suggestions.  They had a Yelp check-in offer of a free glass of Cava, which I took advantage of, and my husband got a mojito on the recommendation of our waiter.  We brought our own bottle of wine, and the corkage fee was $20.

We split an order of pommes frites, husband got 6 roasted gulf oysters, we split the arugula salad, and for entrees, had the duck confit and the flat iron steak. The fries came with housemade ketchup and mayo, the oysters were apparently very delicious, I can't get over the cheese that was on the arugula salad (idiazabel, I MUST find this cheese), the steak was cooked perfectly medium and the salsa verde was delicious), and the duck was good, but had some very hard crunchy parts that I feel should have been fork-tender and were not.  

We had the "dreamsicle" creme brulee and the caramel pots de creme for dessert... the pots de creme paired SOO well with the bold Cab we had. Chocolate + wine = can't go wrong.  

They did say they were working on enlarging the restaurant to include the upstairs and add a balcony, which, being across from Armstrong park, would be wonderful on nice evenings listening to jazz in the park.  Hope it comes to fruition soon!

The total bill was around $150 and we weren't rushed but weren't ignored, either.  It was a wonderful dinner and I wouldn't hesitate to go back next time we're in town!!
Great local shop for fishing tackle. Not a hunter but it seemsthey Carry alot of that too
Updating my review to 1 star because they initially reached out to say that they would contact me to make it right and they never did. I still haven't been back and I certainly don't plan on it now.

It is with great sadness and concern that report that my business partner, Brian Cain,​ and I, as well as all of the attendees of our event, HexFest​, have been discriminated against by the Steamboat Natchez​ for our religion of Witchcraft which itself is recognized as a legal religion in the United States of America (see the following law memorandum at http://www.paganmade.com/temple/download/ckhtlawmem.pdf for details on this). We are writing this from the isle of Anglesey in Wales, where we are on our honeymoon and having to rearrange the most important moments of our life to deal with this discriminatory event. 

On the morning of August 7th, the coordinator of our event, Ty Siddiqui and I spoke on the phone with Deidra Edwards, Director of Sales for the Steamboat Natches, which is itself owned by your Grey Line NOLA affiliate. Ty and I were informed by Ms. Edwards that the owner of the boat had just found out about our Riverboat Ritual conducted by a Voodoo Priestess and featuring drummers and that he was canceling it for "religious reasons." The website describing it been up for over a year and we had explained everything that was going to be going on to Deidra on the phone and even referred to components such as drumming and voodoo in emails back and forth, none of which she expressed concern over because we had already discussed this by phone. Moreover, the Voodoo Priestess in question, national television personality "Bloody Mary," has been hired by Grey Line NOLA for numerous events on the boat through the years and, according to Mary, even our shop has supplied services for Mary in helping to entertain guests on the boat. In spite of all of this, Deidra Edwards informed Ty and me by phone that the owner wanted nothing with Witches or Voodoo for "religions reasons." In addition to this being incredibly discriminatory, it also put us in a precarious position given that this was two weeks before the event. 

Thankfully, we are now at the Creole Queen and Deidra did help with that so perhaps she feels some shame at the actions of the owner of her company. However, after she and the owner met with their lawyer, Deidra has revised the reason we were being cancelled, never having admitted in writing to the "religious reasons" she spoke of to Ty Siddiqui and I on the phone, but rather is now stating that they are canceling the contract because we violated it by having a drumming​ on the boat that they were unapproved and by selling tickets to "non-members" of our organization, both prohibited by their contract. However, I had addressed the membership piece of the contract by phone and Deidra had said that said that this didn't apply to us since we were a public event and not a membership organization to begin with. I also have emails back and forth referring to the drummers on the boat and to the Voodoo priestess and blessing she was doing and never once did Deidra act surprised by this, presumably because we had already discussed it by phone. Deidra Edwards knew all along that this was an event that sold to the public and that we were having drummers and a Voodoo priestess and that the event was for Witches. If she had an issue with the drummers or the public event, both of which they knew about, why wait until two weeks before the event to cancel? This is appalling. I realize she kept the owner out of the loop but he should have at least had the good grace to treat us as a customer and allow us to have our event at least for this year so we would have time to plan for next year's event in June, where we would happily rather go to the Creole Queen than be somewhere we are not wanted.

I have worked in tourism for thirteen years. I sat on the Board of Directors for the official office of tourism of Salem, Massachusetts. I have been an ambassador for tourism in both cities with appearances on Showtime, The Wall Street Journal, TLC, BBC, The New York Times, The Travel Channel (multiple times), and more. To treat us this way at the last minute, causing us to incur numerous costs such as flyer reprinting, several staff members allocated to calling attendees and presenters to make sure they know the location of the other riverboat, which is also much further away from the hotel we are at. There's a good chance we would have changed hotels if we knew we were going to be at the Creole Queen. 

Perhaps most disappointing about this is that it has put is in a compromising position with our guests, who now have to walk a mile from the hotel or rely on cabs that there may not be enough of in order to reach the new location which is 3/4 of a mile further away. We take our relationship with our guests seriously and we believe that the Steamboat Natchez and Grey Line Tours NOLA should take their customer relationships seriously as well. It is deeply distressing to think that they could treat this so cavalierly.

I have finally found somewhere comfortable to get my hair done. 
This is a great place to get a relaxing haircut with top notch quality. 
After 4 months in Nashville area I have finally found Sarah at 18/8 she's does great men's cuts  with an eye for the details. 
Very quality haircut and I will be going there often for mine.

Called to make an appointment and the women who answered was very friendly. From the moment my friend and I walked in, everyone was friendly and efficient. They did a great job and were accommodating. They made sure water temperature was fine and the chairs were comfortable. Everything was clean and the background music was nice. $65 for gel manicure and regular pedicure. I will definitely be going back. Best experience I've had in SB.
Best ahi tuna bowl ever! I could eat it every day ! Son had fish kids meal. Husband had snapper dinner.  So good!

Big portions.
Too thick a batter ( I know some people like that. My grams did when she still had the good dentures.).
Hardest onion rings ever.
Decent fish
Really slow service
OOOOLD fashioned place.

When you walk in, you are not sure what's going on because their front portion is really dark and unusual. I thought I was walking into a bar at first.
The manager told me that Guy Fieri stuck his head in when he was in town...looked at how dark the front was, and went over to The Joint across the street. I can believe that.

This is not the place to go if you want modern New Orleans fried seafood. This is where you go if you want to pretend you are back in the 50s when McCarthyism was great and breading was more important than what it covered (Just think of deep fried mushrooms or shrimp from drive-ins).
Yeah. That old fashioned. Personally, I prefer to taste the seafood now.

This place caught me totally off guard! Suffice it to say the surroundings do not come anywhere close to representing the quality of the pizza. If you like deep dish and cheese you need to visit this place, but go early!

If your making a weekend trip, get up early!! Its worth it and the line gets crazy long! Hashbrowns are money in the bank, and the four of us got different types on pancakes and they were all delicious!

The first day, we drive by at around 10am, and the line was around the block.......So we came back the next morning (Sun) at 7am, and walked right in. By the time we left, there was a line building up.

Def worth the trip!

Almost didn't go here because the reviews were pretty mixed, but I love pizza and had a Groupon coupon so thought I'd take some friends.  The pizza was excellent, and the "Spring Salad" and pizza sticks were really good.  Atmosphere is why I give this 3 stars.  Service, except for the very nice blonde cashier, was terrible.  True story:  You order at the cash reg, so don't go here if you want someone to take your order.  They will serve you the food -- that's the funny part.  When the very hairy/bearded cook delivered our pizza (I began searching for hairs immediately), we realized we did not have any forks.  Asked him for some, and he hesitated and then said, "you can get them at the counter," and walked away.  I guess he realized how incredibly rude that was, so he did bring back some very nice plastic ware (everything is plastic), but that sets the tone for the overall "attention to detail and Service" mindset.  I also had serious concern for the cleanliness of the place --- it just "felt" dirty.  All that said, the pizza was excellent -- next time I'll do carry-out."

Service is suuuuuper slow with not many patrons. Restaurant is filthy, layers and layers of dust on air returns and HVAC pipes on ceiling. The Cuban does NOT have pulled pork on it. Fried fish tastes like stove top stuffing...sage in a fish sandwich? We should've looked at reviews before choosing. Find another spot!

The meal took quite a while to get. We ordered a pizza and calzone which were both pretty burnt after they finally came out. 

However, without having to ask the manager saw we were unsatisfied with our meal and addressed the situation. He got us a completely new meal, that was delicious. I have been out here quite a few times and I would say that when done right the calzone is the best thing on the menu. The small is easily large enough for 2 people. 

To make the expierence even better, the manager also brought us complementary cheese cake. Overall the meal worked out, and the food was fantastic. Very friendly staff.

Coming from NYC, good pizza is hard to come by or maybe we just have a different taste bud for it. But, East Coast has pretty good pizza that satisfies our standards. We get our pizza solely from there and when we have visitors from NY that want pizza, we bring them there.

Try this place...you will LOVE IT!!!!  Such friendly owners and extremely attentive and concerned that the food is to your liking...which is was.  Excellent dining experience.  The Pan Fried Gyoza was delicious.  We also ordered the Yaki Udon Stir Fry with chicken with the side of Miso.  And the Chirashi Zushi Bowl with Salad.  DELICIOUS!!!  All of it...we had never had Yaki Udon...the noodles and stir fried ingredients were flavorful and the chicken was tender.  The extra side of Super White Tuna Sushi was fresh and a generous portion.  A must visit.

Well it was Girl Scout cookie inspired beer day and they did not disappoint. I got the mint chocolate stout and s'mores stout in a bottle, while they lasted. I proceeded to get myself a 12 oz Chocolate peanut butter porter, that I loved. It was $7.
The place was densely populated for the unveiling of the aforementioned Girl Scout beer. I stayed at the bar and chatted up a random customer till my porter ran out. 
I like the layout of the bar and the beer was amazing. Do yourself a favor and swing on by for a cold one.

The best thing about Lime Fresh is that they have Mellow Yellow in their soda machines.  Seriously, amazing! 

Unfortunately the food wasn't nearly as good as the Mellow Yellow.  I paid $7.50 for chips and queso and a soda.  Ridiculous!  I figured it was worth the splurge if the queso was good.  Unfortunately not.  It tasted like they melted a can of Velveeta and added a jar of salsa to it.  And the chips - no flavor except a crunchy, slightly stale taste.  I also tried the pineapple salsa.  Publix and Target both have great store brands that were MUCH better than the one at Lime Fresh.  

If the prices were lower (closer to Taco Bell's prices), I MIGHT be back.  I'd prefer to spend a few bucks less eating fresher, healthier, yummier food from Chipotle!

I strongly believe that this place could create world peace. There is just no way you can be angry while eating one of these sandwiches. For me life just seems a little happier, things a bit more "right" with the world that is creating such culinary delights. All of the ingredients are fresh and they have such an interesting menu of great sandwich combinations. The service is friendly and very efficient. I honestly don't remember how much I paid for my meal because after one bite, it just didn't matter. Seriously, if you care about yourself, at all, walk, run, bike, ride, or drive to Blues City Deli today. You won't be sorry.

Not 5 stars but pretty good. 
I took off one star for the price and the line (lol). 
I tried another yogurt spot and it was not as good. All of the fruit at the other place was not fresh. Here it appears that all the toppings are fresh. I guess that is why the prices are high and the lines are long. I love the coconut with pineapples and strawberries. It tastes like a tropical drink.

MEGU BAIT AND SWITCH PRICES. 

If I could give it 0 stars I would.  

I am a bit thrifty but we did some research about where to eat hibachi without killing the bank account.  We love Yokohama but figured we would try a less expensive alternative. 

The menu prices ranged from 16.95 for
Chicken to around 18.95 for other selections like steak.   Plus they offered a $15 coupon on their website.     Needless to say when we get there he's is a laminated piece of paper with all prices at
Least $6 more entree.  

I brought it quietly to the managers attention and inquired.  I was told I had an old website and the manager showed me the new website on my phone and I said I understood.  I quickly looked at the new website and the prices were still much lower on the menu.   I showed the manager and she abruptly told me that those prices are for takeout.   Who orders takeout hibachi with soup, salad and rice anyway?  I quickly looked at the website again and there was actually a second tab for the regular hibachi menu vs. a tab for takeout and surprise......  prices were still more then 20% less than the plastic laminated bait and switch menu.  

Now  she said it's all about the presentation at the restaurant ( that is what tips are for) and was still very rude.  I sat back down and when my family realized that the restaurant was fraudulent they chose to leave and go elsewhere.   I offered to pay for my son's coke and we left.  The "customer is always right" is surely not followed at Megu.   

I think I would have just told a party that they would honor the menu prices rather than lose customers.  

We went to Yokohama and if I could give them 6 stars I would.   This place and owner don't deserve business.

We've been here for 10 minutes and the waitress has walked past twice with no acknowledgment.....the place is dead, btw.  Oh wait, we just asked for service and she had to go wipe down a table next to us first...... yay, we finally ordered beer 13 minutes later
Good food. My son loves the lamb. Owner super friendly and visited our table. Very clean. Lots of seating. We enjoyed it.
This thrift store is huge! The furniture is often well priced and there is a wide selection of clothes, dishes, books, decor, kids toys, movies...etc.
Great place for entertainment and very good food. Their service is very good as well. The only thing is beware of the additional entertainment charges they add which is steep. Make reservations.
Very clean, the staff was on the ball. We did have to wait 20 minutes to check in, but the front desk staff went beyond expected.
My favorite place to get a beer, salad and pizza. Our recent trip was great, and our server Jessica  was very pleasant and attentive. We will be back soon!
Love this location.  Great Customer service and fresh food.  Love being able to find new items to try and appreciate the sample and ideas provided each time I visit.  Tight parking, but worth it.

The Studio: Very upbeat, love the design, the two separate studios (Barre) and (Spin) are roomy and provide plenty of personal space. The mirrors help coordinate you with everyone else

The Workout: Inspiring. I took the SoulRide led by Shoshana (owner), The woman is a FORCE. She runs, dances, and coaches the entire class. Before starting she came to every bike and either introduced herself, asked how return riders were doing, or offered little adjustments. I've been cycling for years and that kind of personal care is not common. She leads by example and positivity that was much appreciated while trying to coordinate pushups while simultaneously running up a hill. The class is 45 minutes long and you will sweat like no other. Be prepared with water and multiple towels.

The Feeling: When I was warming up there was a small moment before class where Shoshana placed the name of a particularly amazing rider on one of the bikes. Her name is Jen and has been special enough for her bike to be reserved. It was touching. I'm a serial FlyWheel attendee and do appreciate a reserved bike. But to ride so much as to have your own special care, that was really special. I don't know if I would have held it together as well as Jen did.

Ultimately I left Soulbeat very tired, but very inspired. Thank you Soulbeat, I'll be back.

Since having moved away from this late-night treasure, I've experienced what I can only describe as homesickness.

When I first moved to the city-
twenty years old and saturated in cheap, stolen alcohol-
every other late-night drunk I encountered recommended this place to me in such a whimsical tone that I knew I had to try it.
I remember coming to this place as a last-resort, when all other places had long-since closed down, wanting nothing more than to soak up all the excess that rumbled in my stomach with a butter-drenched pancake and some leaky bacon.
And that's exactly what I got.
There's literally no proper way to describe what it feels like to be sitting in a dimly-lit diner at 4am, chugging water to avoid the inevitable pain of daylight, only to look up and see an old-fashioned waitress bring you three plates of American-portioned breakfast food balanced on her arms.
Surrounded by sweaty, still-plastered friends and plowing into a plate-sized omelette with hashbrowns drenched in cholula hot sauce. Washing it all down with a poorly-churned chocloate milkshake with spray-can whipped cream and a candied cherry on top, before biking home to your over-inhabited Seminole Heights home and passing out, full-clothed, and potentially surrounded by a friend or two that couldn't quite make the ride home without passing out in a water drain.
Those are the nights I remember having here. 

And I doubt it's the intent of the diner to appeal to these sorts of crowds-
reckless twenty-somethings that have $20 in their bank accounts, riding their fixed-gears from hospitality night at Resevoir-
but it's the image I've formed in my head of them in the years since I first walked in, and the memory I carry with me now that I belong to a different city.
It's a vibe that can't be re-created, and that I miss quite a lot now that I'm a fully-sanctioned adult.

Cheap, large portions, diner quality, great service, wonderful location.
I miss this place a lot.

Saw all the reviews here so wanted to try them out.   Not to mention they were downstairs from my hotel. 

Everything was good. Food had slot of flavor, servers were fast and easy going. 

Price is good for the environment.
Service is very friendly. Food totally perfect. I ordered clam and chowder. Shrimp and scallop pasta, shrimp Louie and 3 plb of Steam crab . Price is acceptable.!!
A very pleasant family-run place with a few distinctive dishes (grilled asparagus, spicy chirashi, etc.)

Loved my first experience here! Rachel, blonde one (I believe there is two) was so nice and accomdating! I had a coupon and it was honored so I'm a very happy camper.  I enjoy their tea tree products usage! Go for the triple play haircut, the wash and face towel are amazing. The massage is a handheld massager that is ok,  but not worth the extra cash. 

If I will definitely be back!

Edit: I forgot to mention however that my wait time was about 35 minutes, not the worse I've had, but not preferable at all. So 4 stars definitely

Great little sushi place, especially for a novice. The rolls were great and the menu was informative enough that I felt comfortable with the ingredients. 

The service was amazing. They brought us multiple styles of glasses for our 3 types of alcohol and were cheerful about it.

$3 movies! Yes please.

True, they are few month old films, some even already out on DVD. For $3 though, that is cheaper than a visit to Blockbuster.

The theatre itself is out of date compared to the the rest in town but it has a charm which I love. Never busy either, a plus!

We went here for our 10th anniversary dinner. It is a gorgeous space, each room unique and equally charming. So the setting is a 10. Service is understated and very professional as you would expect in a fine dining restaurant, and timing of their appearances at each step of our experience was perfect.

We got Gorgonzola Cheesecake, house salad, Shrimp and Grits, Sauteed Salmon on pea succotash with zesty onion rings, flourless choc cake, and trio of sorbets. Every single bite of every single thing was heavenly. The gorgonzola cheesecake is one of the best things I ever put in my mouth. The salmon was also absolute perfection with a very interesting bed of the succotash that was extremely flavorful. It was one of those dishes where the chef rightfully probably wants you to get a bit of each of the elements in each bite - extraordinary. Husband was very pleased with his shrimp/grits as well.

It made for a wonderful dinner all around: atmosphere, food, and service were perfect.

On an extended weekend trip, we made 3 stops here, we sat at the bar and had great service from the bar staff.  

The Chargrilled Oysters are some of the best I have tasted and the bread that is served with helps them stand out from the competition. 

Another standout dish was the Shrimp Ya Ya, which has a great blend of spice and flavor.  

Make sure to order a Bloody Mary with their house infused vodka too.

A great local find, the food is as  close to authentic Thai that you are going to find. The Tom Kha soup is incredible, the Pad Thai is the best I have found in the area and the Coconut rice with Mango is spot on..  You need to request spicer food if you like it but a must try.   The outside seating is great too

Mildly charming building; the food however is bad and overpriced.The baked artichokes were greasy and my pasta tasted of cardboard. The salad was nice but over dressed. Portions are very big, perhaps that's why it has good reviews.

*This review is for the Sunday brunch only*

Any Brunch snob knows delicious melt in your mouth waffles are a must. These waffles were so dry, they practically disintegrated.  The same for the biscuits. Dry and nasty. Thankfully the sausage gravy was delicious and saved the biscuits from being almost inedible.

While the omelets were delicious along with a few other things, there was not very many options and definitely not worth the $25.

Gratuity was included with my bill beforehand which I didn't like because my server was missing 75% of the time. 

The resort is nice and I enjoyed the man on stage playing piano while we dined but the brunch could of been better.

I really, REALLY love this place (for lunch, not for dinner). Not that their dinner service isn't great, it's just that I almost *always* go here for lucnh. The service is always great, as is the food. I always opt for the veggie burger (which is not vegan, FYI) and it never disappoints. Add a glass of sparkling and you have yourself a nice little lunch with great service. Love this neighborhood gem.

This is by far one of the best hot dog places on the west coast I've been and my wife and have been everywhere---from Seattle to San Diego. The creativity of the different types of dogs, will tempt you to destroy your diet plan and visit this place multiple times until you've conquered every single one! Oh and I dare you, I double dog dare you (nice, right!), to try the fried pickles....

Great place lots of cool stores that are pretty moderatly priced, has a high class strip mall kinda feel. But make sure you don't go when its raining cause their is no roof and no awnings, so your pretty much boned in the rain.

Great food and atmosphere - the homemade tortillas were on point and fajita chicken and beef were seasoned well and really tender. There was a musician who dedicated songs to us too! We'll be back soon or we'll get delivery from Waitr  :)

I've been going to Pina's for a lot of years now. It continues to offer good food at reasonable prices. In the past two years (since my last review), I've had nothing but good experiences. The waitresses are efficient and the guys behind the counter are always friendly. I'm a huge fan of their cheesesteaks -- the meat is tender, juicy, chopped as I prefer and flavorful. The salads are well prepared and huge. I very much like spaghetti with clams in white sauce. Their garlic bread is to die for!  Calzones are large, cheap and very good, especially with spinach with black olives (my favorite concoction. Pina's isn't a destination dining spot, but if you're driving down Ridge Pike from Montgomery County to/from Roxborough, it's the best place to stop for a casual meal (in my humble opinion and based on 40+ years in the area.)

Being a major Top Chef fan, I really wanted to fall in love.  With this place.  This is an expensive restaurant and the food was creative, so upon sitting down, you really do expect the best Philadelphia has to offer.  I could go into detail about what I ate, but it wouldn't change my overall impression.  There were two major things that led to my 3 star rating.

The odor.  I was put off by the overwhelming pork/bacon/sausage smell.  I realize these items are on the menu, but so too are they at 99% of restaurants, and most places don't have that overwhelming odor.

The crowded tables.  We were seated literally one foot away from the next couple.  They were on their first date.  It sounded like they met online  It was impossible to ignore all the first date things they were talking about - past boyfriends/girlfriends, how rudely they were treated by said past boyfriend/girlfriend, how past boyfriend/girlfriend begged them to come back, etc. etc. etc.  This really interfered with my husband and me having a normal conversation because newbie daters were right in our faces.  I told my husband "Tell me I'll never have to be out there again."

Not impressed at all. All the sides tasted like they have been sitting there for days. The brisket was 50% fat and the ribs were dry. $36 for ribs and 3 sides. Absolute waste of money...just utter crap
Very accommodating and nice. The food was delicious and the restaurant was packed on a Friday night. This is a BYOB and we can't wait to go back and try more on the menu.

Yikes. They totally ruined the sweet, dark, decadent, wonderful Pravda I used to know. We brought an out of town friend here, forgetting that this spot had changed hands, and were really disappointed. Most of the decor that gave the place its unique ambiance is gone, the great soundtrack is gone, the bartenders we used to know and love are gone. Their once-stellar absinthe selection is mostly gone. I guess there is food there or something, but we didn't stay long enough to try it. 
This place is now just another bland, catering-to-tourists spot, and I'm really upset about it.

This is the best nail spa in Saint Louis. I moved to Saint Louis from Long Island two years back. I tried one or two salons in the area before I found these guys and I am so glad that I found them. BTW I am a very very picky person when it comes to nail salons for multiple reasons. 
number 1 reason being hygiene- this place is always so clean. They open a fresh pack of tools each time for each individual which according to me is top of the  list. 
number 2 reason being they do such a wonderful work. I mean each person at this place is so  good at what they do.
number 3 reason - I could rank this number 1 as well - these people are so polite and so nice. For me getting a mani pedi is like relaxing and winding down so being around happy and sweet faces makes it even more relaxing. 
number 4 - their prices are pretty reasonable too. Even if they were not, I would still go only here in Sanit louis.

Thanks for the great service guys.

Trying the chai.   Best ever even compared to the places in Santa Cruz!  The chai is the closest to what I've had in India.  No additional ingredients needed.  Looking forward to the sausage burrito!  Yeah.

In the middle of Jackson square, this beautiful converted home had the most amazing menu. True southern cuisine that melts in your mouth. Crawfish and goat cheese crepes were not too heavy and paired perfectly with my mimosa. Grilled tenderloin salad with the most amazing dressing and fried chick peas for the right amount of crunch. Highly recommend !  Great service to top it all off.

One of the top restaurants  in Tucson very nice atmosphere perfect for the special occasion with nice table settings as well.  The menu is excellent French but not over the top so that it limits dishes most Americans would enjoy.  We had something of everything in our two visits during the last several weeks. I love their pepper steak done as it would be in Paris with a rich and very flavorful green peppercorn sauce over a wonderful steak each complemented the other.  Others had fish which was excellent along with escargot, scalloped potato's, soufflés.  The second visit was a group of a 11 which they handled well the combination of wine, cocktails and food with good friends made it a really great visit.   The waiting staff is somewhat young and perhaps somewhat inexperience but very gracious so demonstrating a little patients is a good investment.

This was a great buying experience. I started dealing with Kelly Sullivan online after going into many dealerships. Too many others played games and wanted to get me into cars they wanted to sell, not what I wanted to buy. 

After emailing back and forth with Kelly, I felt comfortable going in and making an offer on my Tucson. The sales process could not have been more comfortable. I felt I received a great deal on the vehicle I wanted and Kelly could not have been nicer (not to mention she came in on her day off to help me). 

To my surprise, the finance and insurance portion of the sale with Rick went pretty smooth as well. 

Kelly took the time to go over the car with us, show us all the options and made sure we knew how everything worked.  

Everyone else we came across that worked there was very nice as well. Overall it was a great experience and I would definitely buy from Kelly and Mungenast Hyundai again.

SUCH a nice guy, and really delicious lassi (although it makes you SUPER full after awhile)! The owner is incredibly friendly and nice, and let us try a ton of different samples, including his precious rose-flavored stuff. A little bit far from center city and campus.

Tangelo's customer for 20 years! Delicious food, great portions and awesome people. My favorites include the mojo chicken sandwich and fresh roasted turkey daily. 
In addition, they've started an excellent brunch. My go-to's are the the Jamaican custard French toast with butter rum sauce and huevos espinacas (omelette with Parmesan and spinach). Not to mention they are super DOG FRIENDLY, always proving dog treats. 

Tangelo's never disappoints. Recommend to anyone in and around Gulfport!

We have frequented Blue Moon Pizza for many years and have noticed the quality has gone way down from what it used to be. The last two times we have found the pizza leaves a lot to be desired. Last night we had our usual pizza "to go" and it was way over done. The crust was burned in some spots and tasted like burned toast. The shrimp was tough and dried out. The cook was too busy flirting with one of the female workers and chatting with another and wasn't paying close attention to what was in the oven. Will not be returning to Blue Moon, but now we need to find another local pizza place with quality pizza. Will check the reviews on Yelp to find a new one to try.

From the outside, and at first glance inside, this looked like it wasn't going to be much.  Hole-in-the-wall-ish from outside, and inside the one steam-table shut down, dimly lit with old decor, standard-looking red-green menu, backlit pictures behind the counter, and grandma baby-sitting two of the owners' small kids in the dining area.

I was pleasantly surprised to find at least three Thai dishes on the dinner-combo menu, so I ordered the Pad Thai.  The rest of the menu looked pretty standard. Though they do have fried chicken wings and buffalo wings in the appetizers section, and 5 kinds of duck under the "Thai and Fusion Cuisins"(sic).

The young 20-something lady behind the counter spoke with a heavy Chinese accent, but she both understood and communicated very well. She wrote up my order and ran my credit card while taking another order over the phone like an old pro, and kitchen staff were bringing delivery and to-go orders up to the counter.

There was a constant stream of to-go orders, people calling in, and people picking up. This is one popular place! And when a few orders were ready to be run out, one of the guys from the kitchen took them out for delivery. 

Buffet, $3.99, is for lunch only, but you can also order off the menu for lunch.

To-go/delivery are served in standard clam-shells and pint/quart paper containers.  Minimum $10 for delivery in limited area. Dine-in meals are served on a solid plate with stainless steel utensils.  Soft drinks are from a soda machine behind the counter, served in a plastic tumbler, but the cashier regularly checked to see if I wanted a refill.

My Pad Thai came with both shrimp and chicken.  I liked it.  Not the best I've had, but pretty darn good. Especially considering the staff is not Thai.

Fax # is 780-8383.

Located in between K-Mart and Marsh.

Open later than most.  Hours: Mon-Thur: 10:30am - 10pm. Fri/Sat: 10:30am - 11pm. Sun: Noon - 10pm.

This was a pleasant surpise. Much better than what you'd expect at first glance.

This was the best cheesesteak I've had in awhile. The bread was fresh as well and the cheese fries were on point. I would come back again. I've had cheese steaks from other places and this knocks it out the park compared to them.

I don't understand all the reviews for this place. I've been twice, just to make sure the first time wasn't an off day for them, and because I live nearby and want to support local places, but I've yet to try anything from their menu that didn't have dry, chewy meat in it. You can get much better for the price elsewhere in Nashville. The decor is typical modern discomfort, most notably with tall metal chairs that are hell on earth for a short person to get in and out of. Service was friendly enough, but the food is what's important and so far it's lacking.
Food was alright, service was horrible. Still waiting for our check back 20 minutes after giving our waiter my card.
The store smelled like baked cookies and the staff was friendly and helpful. What they sell is a bit overpriced, but they do home cooking ware right.
Carne seca burrito....mmmmmmmmmm oh so yummy!

This place has gone downhill. On a recent Thursday night visit there were four customers and five employees in the restaurant. It took them 18 minutes to make three burgers and two orders of fries. I spent those 18 minutes examining the dozens of used napkins and bits of French fries that littered the tables and floor. No one cleaned anything up or wiped down a single dirty table in those 18 minutes. The restaurant is hot, the equipment is loud, and the tables and chairs are worn out. Two of the three burgers were not as ordered. The average length of the French fries was 3/4 of an inch. Can't wait to try the new ramen place in the same shopping center. They'll probably start strong, just like EB did when they first opened.

Great getaway spot for a few days - it is awesome opening up the suite and being right on the beach. Bathroom looks like it was newly renovated and was amazing. We stayed in the "suite" but there are no dressers or even cabinets for clothing. No silverware, cups or glasses. Plenty of chairs on the beach for all guests and also grills. Make sure you don't accidentally take a wash cloth home, they do have a sign saying things are for sale and you will be charged. Rooms are kept clean. Overall it is a basic spot to stay on the beach for a few days, but there's nothing wrong with that, just don't expect entertainment here, just relaxation.

Our party of 6 arrived on a busy Sunday afternoon so there was a wait to be seated and a longer wait to get our food.  We were hungry so any wait seemed too long.

The food was good and the Margarita Pizza was very good fresh and made for really good leftovers.  

The quality food saved the day.
Very fun experience. Drinks are unique and very tasty. Very boozy which is THE BEST. Atmosphere is great. I can't wait to go in the summer time and sit outside. It is a hidden gem in Indy.

Came here for a conference. The room was clean and the bathroom was nice. I originally booked a king bed on orbitz and gotten two full size instead but I was too tired too change at that time. The down stairs hall was large and beautiful and the dinning area too. Gotten the chicken sandwitch which was cooked perfectly and the fries too. but the lobster salad was soso ( the lobster was frozen and defrosted from the deep freeze) the wings were a little cold but the flavor was good. It's really close to the mall maybe even walking distance. This is a great place to stay for a seminar or conference but not so mux for a vacation. It was kind of noisey in the am with the door opening and closing and last night with people walking and talking from the hallway. The rooms are clean no bugs were seen and the view wasn't too bad... The staff however could be a little friendlier, they weren't unpleasent or rude they just didn't smile. The only disappointment I had was the pool was closed by 9 so the front desk stated.. I would of like to enjoy a nice soak in the jacuzzi before bed

BBQ Shrimp!! Wow!  It was truly amazingly delicious!  ! It's was described to us as the best in the city and I believe it.  The lamb chops with mint pesto sauce were awesome, and the gumbo was perfectly spiced and flavorful! The cheesecake and white chocolate brownie were decadent and delicious.  The wait staff was exceptional!  We will be back!!!!!

This "steak" house had no NY Strip. They over peppered the Cesar salad and the mashed potatoes.  The ribeye was like a cheap sirloin.  The expensive lobster was way too salty to enjoy. Service was a nice guy but amateur. Will never go back too many other establishments to enjoy.

I was a member of LA Fitness before moving and this was the only gym close to me. When I first went there to check it out, I was heavily pressured to join and the monthly rates are expensive!  They also make you pay extra if you cancel your membership within 1 year. They had limited equipment and didn't have most of the features I liked that LA fitness offered.

Where to start?  Nice local watering hole where the drinks aren't expensive. Dark inside,well stocked bar,good pool table. Rest rooms were clean.The food is great if you like oysters,crawfish,shrimp,'gator,all fix any way you want,raw,grilled,boiled,on french bread. Great daily specials too!!!
My lady and I had the grilled oysters and an oyster PoBoy,delicious and priced fairly.
If you're into karaoke then this is the place for you at almost any night. 
Me,I'd like a live band or DJ that played the oldies at least once in awhile.
All in all a nice place to meet and sit and have an adult beverage while eating some great local food. Didn't see any tourists!! Mixed age group. Dress code was what ever!
I will go back just to chill out and eat but will say adios when the croakyokey starts.
We had an amazing time Saturday night.  Returned tonight, by myself, and was told they won't seat a party of one.  I appreciate the space is small, but am beyond disappointed.

I went for lunch during the week (Wednesday) with my friend Peter. I was really excited to try this Cypriot food. He got the spanakopita, and I got ground lamb with pine nuts on flatbread (I think it was called lacham azeen). Both came with a few mouthfuls of a side salad.  The food was tasty & hot, came out quickly, and the portions were perfect for lunch.

Service was decent, the waiter was very practiced and tried to be funny. I would have preferred he had been ]better about keeping the water glasses full instead of disappearing outside every few minutes He was, however, very solicitous and offered recommendations.

The decor is nice, the walls are painted white, the touches of blue and the ambient light give it a very Mediterranean feel, which I suppose is what they're going for!

This place is a bit expensive for "fast food" and the portions aren't too generous, but if you're in a hurry and you're walking home from a night class, this may be your best bet (it's open most weeknights until 11 P.M.)  Lunch items aren't served until 11 A.M. - if you go any earlier you're stuck with bagels (I believe they're called "squagels" by virtue of the fact that they're squarish and not circular) and other items I don't really consider to be "real" food.  I tried the jalapeno and cheddar squagel on two occasions - I ordered cream cheese with it and it was fairly tasty to my sleep-deprived, 7 A.M., slightly off-game taste buds.

The Asian chicken salad was acceptable and the piece of bread it came with was fairly good and added value to the meal.  The chain also offers a 1/2-salad, 1/2-sandwich combo which is a convenient (though obvious) idea. I usually get the Tuscan pesto chicken since it's the least offensive and least messy of the sandwiches I've ordered here (the chicken tinga sandwich is a bit messier - the guacamole and stringy chicken bits tend to spill out of the sandwich when you bite into it) and I order a salad with it.  I've never gotten a soup here.  

The coffee is acceptable if not memorable.  The brownies and cookies don't exactly taste homemade, but if the mood strikes you, they're available.    Going back to the sandwiches - order them raw (not toasted) since the toasted bread is crunchy and hard.  Also, the Tuscan pesto chicken tastes better without melted cheese.  The latter ruins an otherwise quasi-healthy meal.  I've never gotten the carrots with a sandwich, but I've opted for the pepper-flavored kettle chips.  Raw carrots don't particularly appeal to me.  For beverages, I do recommend their lemonades (mojito lemonade or raspberry lemonade) albeit they're full of empty calories.  

Service: B-
Taste: B-

Este sitio para mí es el mejor restaurante japonés de Santa barbara, tienen una promoción todos los días a mitad de precios algunos rolls. También él servicio es bastante bueno, y los Rolls también. También tienen una zona a parte donde tienes a tu chef personal y puedes pedir arroz, vegetales,camarones,etc y el chef te los cocina en una plancha enfrente tuyo.

I was pretty excited to try La Colombe after my friend told me it was featured on the Travel Channel. Upon walking in, I instantly liked the feel of it. There was the smell of good coffee, warm and inviting decor, cute mugs for people enjoying their coffee in the shop, and cool art hanging on the walls. There was even a fancy water station with not only options of room temperature or cold water, but sparkling water too! 

There was no menu so I went with my go-to order of an americano. It had a great bold flavor. I liked that when they handed it to me it was presented with a saucer and spoon to add my cream/sugar right at the counter. My friends got lattes which were equally flavorful with a good amount of creaminess. I was only in Philly for a few days but visited La Colombe 3 times that's how much I liked it!

This place is a little hard to peg. As a dyed in the wool Surrey's guy, I like that they make a few nervous nudges towards the "crunchier" side of breakfast (the morning glory muffin was exquisite). However, there is also an undercurrant of "hey, we could franchise this operation" and I suspect a few items were squezzed out of a tube from SYSCO. The counter service was friendly but erratic and distracted and the breakfast burrito was a solid "good", no better. The Tulane student & Riverbend neighborhood denizens seemed right pleased.

The drinks are expensive, but they are unique and delicious. The fact that they give you a little bag of truffle popcorn kind of makes up for the bill. Comfy seating, great bartenders, and nice decor. I could spend an entire evening here if I wouldn't go broke doing so.

Yum! My husband and I got the cheesy garlic bread as an app and we devoured it in less than a minute. We even had a legitimate argument over the last piece. Crispy crust and great flavor.  He got a plain cheese personal pie and I got the Hawaiian.  The ham had a strange texture that I didn't enjoy but the pizza itself was delish. Nice outdoor seating.  The waitress seemed frazzled even though there weren't many people there. We loved it and will be back.

The young lady working Saturday night on 7/3/16 was very arrogant, condescending and too busy talking to the regular patrons.  I had to wait twenty minutes in a very slow bar to wait for another order for myself and my girlfriend.  When I asked for another drink for my girlfriend, she immediately copped an attitude.  Wrong answer.  There's too many bars in Tampa that'll treat their patrons with respect.  You're better off buying a six-pack and taking it home without the patronizing attitude.
Yummy Shrimp & Grits! Buffalo feathers are delicious! The ambiance is fun and upbeat! Would recommend it!!

Express Scripts is only the tip of the iceberg when it comes to what the future of government regulated health care is going to be like. I've been trying to get a prescription for 4 weeks and have had nothing but the big 'run-around'...Express Scripts says they are waiting for the doctor's office to verify...the doctor's office says they've called Express Scripts and so on. 
This is a pathetic excuse for a 'Health Care' organization making it perfectly clear their only interest is making money from not filling your prescriptions.

This is one of the only places in Seminole Heights to eat where you get good food and excellent service. A staple for area residents it is nice to get consistent quality at a reasonable price. Lotsa TPD eat there and its nice at late hours to see those uniforms.

Food was good, drinks poured right, atmosphere is cool, service was fast and friendly. Fortunately we didn't get one of the "man bun" servers! Lmao! Visiting from California and we have enough of those snowflakes there, I was hoping Nashville was Man Bun Snowflake free.  Other than that I'd recommend this place and I'll probably be back!

It wasn't great but it wasn't bad. The food was good. I had a ham and cheese griller so you really can't mess that up. My mom had a club and my sister had a wrap. The wrap had honey mustard even though my sister said "no honey mustard". But I don't know if I can blame the cook or the waitress. 

Our waitress wasn't the greatest. She was a little slow and when we asked her what the soup of the day was she forgot to come back and tell us. When she did remember she couldn't remember what the soup was. Today it was cream or something, maybe crab or maybe corn and something vegetable. I'm not kidding that is what she said. Now as I am allergic to seafood they are very different soups! 

The prices there are pretty reasonable. For the three of us it was about 30 bucks. I will admit I have been there for breakfast and that was much better.
I probably can't say anything that hasn't been said.  My advice is to plan ahead and do the Brewmaster's Tour.  It is well worth the money, but you need to plan in advance and reserve a spot.

This place gets busy, it is a tourist destination as it is on the wharf (I also went during Memorial Day weekend so go figure). This was the first time that my partner and I ate here and we did not where to go and what to do. We were like standing inside until we asked a server how we order and he told us that there was a window on the side of the building. If you want to eat inside, you might have to wait for a while but if you want to sit outside, there are benches on both sides of the restaurants. Depending on how busy it is, you might have to share with other people which is great and fine! 

We ordered a cioppino and I imagined that it was going to be a small serving but when we got it, it was huge! It fed me and my partner. We meant to just get a snack because we were going to go to the public market but I ended up getting really full. I did not try anything else so I can't vouch for anything else but this cioppino was AMAZING!

As for parking, you can park on the wharf which I was amazed at because most wharfs or even piers that I have been to are usually only for pedestrian traffic. And parking is free for first 90 minutes (that's what I remember). Don't try to find parking at the very end, look for parking as you driving by because my partner and I were able to find parking easily but we saw a lot of people at the end trying to park at the very last parking lot.
A quiet place to have a cup of nitro cold brew while doing work or reading a book. The atmosphere is a lot nicer than the chain coffee spots in Newtown, and at a comparable price.

Been here several times for meetings and had breakfast.   Good Diner breakfasts.

Had dinner at a buffet for another meeting.  Typical Diner food with super service.

Wepa!!!! Given that there aren't that many Dominican people in Philly I was shocked to find this restaurant and wow...as we Dominicans say...que hartura de perros!!! (Meaning we ate like beasts). Better than most places in the NYC/NJ area to be honest. The ropa vieja is a must try and the prices are Amazing. The owner was super welcoming and I just loved everything about it. I will definitely come back when in town.

We are avid sushi lovers and I love fruit on top of sushi. It may sound weird but trust me, it's delicious! This place has a huge variety of rolls at reasonable prices. It's in a great location and can get pretty crowded on a weekend night.

The steamed veggies instead of pasta with the salmon on it is really good here.  It's a great way to avoid carbo loading.  Great prices on decent bottled wines-- raumbauer
Chard for 33 bucks and Just Cab for 30 bucks is nice price at a restaurant Duckhorn's Decoy on 25 bucks.  The one thing that I don't like is no local beers on tap. The beer selection is weak for craft beer geeks.  We would come more often if they at least had Icky on tap. Everyone has Icky. Meatball appetizers are tasty and the wings are nice and spicy.
Salads are big and filling-- dressing on the side though as it comes drenched. 
Oh and the mud pie! - huge and delicious--Oreo cookie crust and coffee ice cream.
 Big enough for a crowd

Cute little shop with unique ice cream flavours. Their cones are huge, so don't fill up in dinner before stopping by. 

I swirled the pandan and watermelon together in a charcoal cone. They had enough flavour that the taste was distinguishable, but it was mild enough that someone new to Asian flavours won't be overwhelmed.

It's definitely worth a try. I will come back another time to try different flavours.

We are (were) annual summer visitors that come to Indianapolis expressly for the IMA. Until this year the IMA had free admission, $5.00 parking and an excellent cafe. It still has a lovely encyclopedic collection of art from Neolithic times up to the mid 20th century, in the mid-western American art museum style. Lots of marble, excellent 19th century pieces including all the stars, Van Gogh, Monet, Renoir etc. and a noteworthy collection of early 20th century American art featuring memorable works by Georgia O'keefe and Edward Hopper, among others. The grounds are attractive with nice gardens and an excellent cafe, which we always ate at to support the museum. This year things changed. I gave IMA three dollar signs because their new entrance fee of $18.00 per person makes this one of the most expensive, and therefore inaccessible, art museums in the country. The operation of the cafe has been outsourced to a catering company, adding the costs of a profit hungry middle-man to both the museum and the patron. When the museum was free we paid a small fee to see an astonishing exhibition of Ai Weiwei's art, fresh from the Smithsonian and on its way to Los Angeles which I will always remember. Now you must pay more than it costs to visit the LACMA in CA  and only slightly more than the Met to see a solid permanent collection (Cincinnati [Free], Cleveland [Free] and Detroit [$12.50] are better, Toledo [Free] is equal) featuring special exhibitions one might expect to find in the Evansville town hall. We will miss IMA.

I've said it many times; one day this place is going to be a local legend in St. Louis.  The Ted Drewes of sandwiches, if you will - only without the overrated part..  All Blues City is missing from qualifying for the "legend" status is time.  It's still relatively new in that sense, but it doesn't make it any less special.

First, up front is the food.  For years I was loyal to Mom's Deli in South City.  No longer.  Blues City has the best sandwiches in St. Louis.  The best of that bunch, I believe is the Benton Park Poor Boy.  Ham, Turkey, Roast beef, pickles, onions, peperoncini with a roasted red pepper sauce.  Wow.  And the portions - huge.

The environment is one of a kind for a deli - anywhere.  Show up on a Saturday afternoon and you'll be treated to live, local blues while you wait in line.  That might be my only *tiny* grumble, which is although the line is always fast  the space is so small that the music can really blast you in there.  But that's all part of the charm as well.  The walls of the place are covered with framed local blues photos and signage and I always seem to spot something I haven't seen before.

Staff is always friendly, and that comes from the top.  The owner, Vince always seems to be there and will greet you with a smile every time.  He's the kind of guy you like to see do well, and he appears to be sitting on a gold mine right now.

Germantown Pub was the sports bar I landed in to watch the Superbowl. They had a limited menu but the full bar. So I chose the wings and fries, which were delivered by a polite and friendly waitress. The hot wings were indeed "hot" but actually had some flavor instead of just tasting like "fire." Meaty and cooked properly, these were quite good. The fries were a little mushy though.

Two-for-one beer specials was a nice touch, so I enjoyed my two Blue Moons each with a big wedge of orange in them.

The sound quality was pretty poor. Too loud, a speaker that sounded blown and they were slightly out of sync. Still, there were eight or more TVs with the game on and lots of cheering.

I'd return to Germantown for a game but maybe not THE game.
I got a french pedi. It was terrible. The whites were so big and uneven. My nails were square with corners. I had them fixed at another salon. Wont be going back to them.

The more and more I go to gastropubs, the less and less impressed I am by them. I don't know if the schtick is just getting old, or if people are doing a worse job, or what, but c'mon people, ENTERTAIN ME!!!

Pub and Kitchen strikes me as a fairly run of the mill entry into the gastropub arena. Very nice interior rehab job? Check. Pretty awesome selection of beers? Check. Couple fancy, gourmet-ish items on the menu? Check. Yawn. The thing missing was something to separate this place from the crowd. Why would I go here instead of any other place just like this? Jonny Brendas has whiskey donuts. The Tap Room has tacos of the day. The Royal has one of the better burgers around, not to mention innovative uses of pork that surprise me every time (mmmm, pulled-pork nachos with beer cheese sauce ... I digress.) This place had ... 18 dollar fish and chips. 18 bucks??? Seriously? For fish and chips? Maybe you should've saved some money on the fancy interior so you could serve some food for a reasonable price. Listen up Pub and Kitchen (and you too, Devils Den!): If I wanna spend 40 dollars on dinner, I'm not going to a gastropub, not when there are better dinners to be had for $40 (pick your BYOB) or much cheaper gastropubs with the same food! I don't get the 20 dollar entree movement in these places, it really makes no sense.

One other irk: our waiter was nice, but he had to have come to our table like 45 times during the course of the meal. Body language my friend, it will tell you all you need to know, like when we are done with our menus (see: putting down menu), when I need another drink (see: drink close to or completely empty). This ain't rocket science homey. (UPDATE: As I read through all the other reviews, bad service is a recurring theme.)

if you live near Pub and Kitchen, or are in the area, hit it up, it'll be a fine dinner. But I don't think it's worth traveling very far at all to go to this place.

The atmosphere is a cool vibe, staff is always friendly and the food is very good. Favourite thing on the menu would be a brunch pirate Poutine with side of bacon but can't go wrong with any of their options.

If you are not familiar with TJ Maxx, they sell high end and designer items at a discount.  Usually it is a pretty decent discount, although they can be a bit steep.  I have a special affinity for the health and beauty aids section as I love the higher end shampoos and soaps.  

The lotions and bubble baths are occasionally more than you would pay for them at Macy's and Dillard's so watch out. 
 
There is a modicum of organization at TJ Maxx but just barely. Most of the time, I just wander around the store looking through all sizes and departments as there is something about this place that prevents things from remaining in the proper sections. 

I have to fight the urge to reorganize everything. 

If you are interested there is a 30 day layaway.  There are lots of things you can't put on layaway there so don't load up a whole buggy thinking you are about to put housewares and such on layaway. They will not let you. 

The employees all seem miserable. Even the manager has the "Get out while you still can" look. The computer voice at the registers directing you to a specific register are a little weird. "Register 4 is now available, Please proceed to register 4."  

I'm always tired when I leave here, like I have fought a battle and lost.

I have returned to this restaurant over and over because their salsa is the best in town. But ... the service is really bad and, if you ask them to bring more salsa ( they bring small bowls when you are first seated) it is NEVER brought out quickly and the staff is almost reluctant to do it. The last two times I ate there (tonight and about 2 weeks ago) my water and soda were not re-filled until I got up to get a server.  Both times we were there close to closing time, they weren't busy, but were very inattentive.   And, tonight, the man who was cleaning tables was seen picking his nose twice as he stood near the windows in the guest area. I am not sure what is happening here, but I hope they figure it out soon.

You would think that because I live in the Mission district of San Francisco, I could take a break from having a burrito, right? No way, and the Paradise Cafe proves my point. Great little breakfast place in downtown SB with a little dish I just couldn't pass up, the Huevos Venezuela. It's basically a fancy way of saying 'breakfast burrito' with eggs, black beans, peppers, cheese and salsa on the side served with potatoes. Easily the best way I've ever had eggs prepared.

I really like this place. I've only ever been here for lunch so I can't comment on the dinner service. They will make any sushi for you if you want to try something off the menu. I tend to ask for different combinations of vegetables & cream cheese in my sushi. The only downside is they tend to be busy so if you're in a time crunch it can be an issue. I suggest ordering 2 or 3 rolls at a time or you may find yourself there for well over an hour as they make the sushi specially for you when you order it. Just don't order too much because they will charge you for uneaten pieces. Oh & as far as the rest of the food goes, it's standard fare. This is definitely more a place for someone who wants sushi specifically.

Amazing calzones.  Our kids ordered plain - one cheese and one pepperoni.  My husband and I actually preferred the simple ones over our more creative ones (can't remember the exact names).  Portions are huge - we stopped before heading back to Chicago and nibbled on our leftovers on the drive home.  Kids didn't ask once to stop for anything - they had their delicious leftovers.

Best darn Mexican food in STL period.  Love love love the Guadalajara special and shrimp chimichanga.  Spend a birthday here and wear the big sombrero.  Tip...the monster margarita is big enough to split.  For authentic Mexican it's hard to beat this UCity treasure!

Two elks is the best on mountain lunch restaurant at Vail. Great timberframe building with 50 foot ceilings and a great atmosphere. The food is fresh and they turn out a lot of it. Lunch runs the gamut from big salads to pasta dishes to a grlll for hamburgers and chicken sandwiches to baked potatos and a Mexican station for burritos.

Its pricey as you should expect but they do offer the $9.95 daily sandwich, fry & drink meal though which helps. Located at the top of the mountain, Two Elks is Vail's nicest on mountain lunch restaurant and sitting outside overlooking the back bowls and Blue Sky Basin on a sunny day is paradise.
5 tacos and nachos missing tomatoes and sour cream. Must have ran out of food. Not good.

I ordered the Pima Melt Sandwich is my SO ordered the Unforgettable sandwich. I thought my food was fine but a bit too salty. I've eaten at the Baggins downtown location plenty of times and never had so much salt in a sandwich. My SO also thought his was extremely salty and he even had stomach problems afterwards that I will not go into details for the sake of grossing other people out. 

The service was pretty quick, but it could have been quicker if the drink machine was not located RIGHT next to the cashier in a corner. There was a line when I arrived and it was extremely difficult to access the drink machine with the huge line blocking access and limiting the space around the drink machine. 

I highly recommend forming a line to the side by using arrows on the ground or somehow signifying to customers to form a line in the opposite direction instead of a straight line close to the drink machine. 

I don't think I'll go back to this Baggins even though it's located so close to me.

Usually solid, but just got the most lifeless biryani I've had. White rice and chicken...disappointing.

Reached out and offered replacement. Very gracious.

I went last weekend looking for a car and stopped by my old stomping grounds. One salesman was polite and friendly. The prices aren't too bad on some of the used cars. I left with a good impression of the place.

Not bad, but not out of this world. City Limits is a popular breakfast spot in Bellevue with a roomy interior, outdoor seating, a large array of coffees, and friendly employees.

The extensive menu offers a number of options and specializes in the banini (various panini-style sandwiches framed by a "b"agel). On paper, the Huevos Rancheros banini seems like the winner, with pepper jack cheese, egg and bacon, and my favorite condiment on the planet, jalapeño cream cheese, all between an everything bagel. But there wasn't that spicy kick I had hoped for, reasonably flavorful but not the heat I anticipated. The bagel was blander than most I've eaten, which really surprised me because it's hard to mess up an everything bagel.

The Southern Banini was better, with egg, bacon, and cheddar cheese, but the most significant difference was the flavorful sausage offsetting the blandness of the sesame seed bagel. Would I eat here again? Sure, if I were meeting someone for breakfast. But I wouldn't go two blocks out of my way to eat here. Quite frankly, when I'm in the Bellevue Station strip mall, I'm heading straight for legendary Pizza Perfect!

This is beautiful little Parisian dessert shop. Very intimate. The charcuterie board was underwhelming and not enough baguette for two. Definitely not worth $25. Also ordered a brownie for $5.25. Again overpriced. You're paying to say you visited. That's all. Friend ordered the quiche and thoroughly enjoyed it. The free champagne with check in was a great addition. Great spot for an after dinner dessert/drink with a friend. Cute vintage cuterly,stemware,furnishings
We love La Cabaña! Service is very quick and the employees are friendly. The food is great. The queso and chicken quesadilla are my favorites. The facility is clean as well.

Not bad, but not great either. It's totally affordable, but the staff is not at all attentive. They were more concerned about conversing amongst themselves than checking us in. After swiping my my card, I stood there for a minute before the girl at the register broke away from her conversation long enough to say "oh did you want your receipt?" 

The place is relatively clean, and I appreciate that there were places my little one could play without being trampled by the older kids, while my older one could run off and do her thing without being stuck with the babies. Only a few times did I see them ask big kids to get out of the little person area. Also, there was only one staff member who addressed the fact that there were children not wearing socks. This is one of the main rules, and should be more closely monitored as it is just downright gross and unhygienic. Oh, and clean the bathrooms. They were in desperate need of attention.

Overall, though, I'm not really there to interact with the staff, and my kids enjoyed it  immensely. Not a bad deal for the price.

Normally we love this place but I ordered the meatloaf and after a few bites I noticed the it was uncooked in the center.  Asked the waiter if any pork was in the recipe and he checked and yes there was pork.  I asked to have it heated to proper temperature and it came back undercooked again.  They took it off my bill but I had to go home and make a sandwich .

Kampai is hands-down the best place to get sushi in St. Louis. I've been to many sushi places around town, and none of them can even hold a candle to Kampai. 

The atmosphere is peaceful, almost Zen-like, and it's never uncomfortably crowded. In fact, most of the times I've been there, it has been pretty quiet, which I feel enhances the overall experience. 

The servers are always friendly and attentive, and the complimentary (and scrumptious!) Miso soup and Garden salad are a welcome addition to your main course, which will undoubtedly be some of the freshest, most delicious sushi you have ever eaten. 

The quality of the sushi itself is something that deserves the highest praise. Although the Crunch Roll is my favorite, and very well done, I try to get something new each time I visit, and I am never disappointed. The sushi is always extremely tasty, totally filling, and completely satisfying. 

As far as alcohol is concerned, the small selection of sake that they do have is delicious and fairly priced, just like everything else on the menu, and they seem to have a pretty good selection of Japanese beers, as well.

 For dessert, they have several tantalizing options to choose from, and you will not be disappointed with any of them. The fried green tea ice cream is particularly delectable.

So, to make a long story short, if you think you've had the best sushi that St. Louis has to offer, give Kampai a try, and see how it compares. You'll be pleased at what you discover.

They were fabulous.They confirmed several times prior to their arrival.Asked me questions about the type of carpets and stains I had before coming.They did ask me to sign a waiver that certain stains may not be removed and there may be some bleeding of the dyes,which did not happen.I felt very comfortable to have them in my house alone.Friendly,efficient moved all my furniture.Did a fabulous job on my area rugs.Look brand new.Very fairly priced.Highly recommend!

Since I had moved to this area in 2005, I had yet to find a take out Chinese restaurant that I could consistently go to. After many years of being disappointed and then finally giving up, a coworker recommended Super China. This is bar none THE BEST take out in this area.

This place is the worst! Cold fries I'm pretty sure we're cooked yesterday. Smushed flat as a pancake grilled cheese. Didn't give me a pickle. Took like 20 minutes to drive through and there was ONE car ordering when I pulled up.
