There are 3 sauces to choose from all kept hot and serve yourself.  Try the brisket, ribs, ham and the sweet BBQ sauce.

This place is good meaning it will get pretty busy at lunch time and if you're getting the order to go order online.

A favourite of my family for the last 7-8 years, every time we are back in town we make this one of our must visits. My personal menu usually includes the moussaka main course with a sampler platter of tadziki, taramasa and feta dips. My wife always opts for the spanakopita, my daughter goes Italian and my son always goes for the tried and tested chicken bites and fries. So what I'm saying is they can cater for my whole family and the good is plentiful, great tasting and very good value for the money. As a plus the owner is always friendly and welcoming just to make the meal that bit more special. For family meals or even larger groups this is a great choice!

I have been in sales all my life. The term, "Car Salesman" always carries a very familiar and often negative connotation. I can happily say that Momenul has broken that view in my eyes. He was warm, friendly, and very engaging. I met him first about a year ago when I thought I might need a car. His level of professionalism is the reason I convinced my wife to see him and the Hyundai Santa Fe. When we arrived, I sought out Momenul to work with yet again. My wife was very pleased with his demeanor and actually ended up buying the Tucson based on Momenul's recommendation and the features of the car. Six months later, I needed to purchase a vehicle. There was no question as to where and whom I would seek. We now drive two Hyundai Tucson's and are very pleased with both of them. Thanks for your spectacular level of professionalism and courtesy Momenul!!

This is the first place we opted to eat seafood in Santa Barbara, and it was not too shabby. We walked to the restaurant from our hotel, which was a bonus. Taking in the atmosphere of the wharf on a chilly night certainly got us into the Santa Barbara mood. Even once we arrived, the small bar style dining and aroma of the day's catch inside the place was in line with the image one conjures up when thinking of fresh seafood.

After a very brief wait, we got a seat looking directly at the kitchen, and let me tell you, the staff have this operation down to a science. They are moving people in and out of the restaurant at record speed, all without sacrificing service. Our waiter was friendly and helpful, and we never once felt rushed. In fact, this was a highlight for us. Even when selecting our beverages, he let us sample beer and made recommendations on wine. 

We ordered all of our food at once, as we'd had a chance to peruse the menu and take a few tips from Yelp. We ordered a glutenfest including a cup of clam chowder, a half dozen oysters, some coconut shrimp and the shrimp and scallop linguine.

The clam chowder arrived first, and it was a bit bland. I really wanted to like it since the weather was ideal and they add bacon in every batch (!), but it was lacking something. Adding the oyster crackers helped, but I would recommend skipping this. If you are in a soup mood, maybe try the soup of the day. They had a bisque, and that might have been a better option. 

The oysters arrived next, and that was the biggest letdown for me. I am an oyster junkie - I've been known to eat four dozen in one sitting. I'm also an oyster purist, meaning I add only a tiny bit of lemon before eating them so they maintain their sea flavor. The presentation was sloppy - just ice on a plate, which was melting and wet our eating area, a measly slice of lemon and lime, cocktail sauce and a little horseradish. The oysters themselves just weren't that good, and for the first time in my life, I left two on the plate when it went back.

The coconut shrimp and linguine arrived together, and they were both quite good. You know how sometimes when you get coconut shrimp, they seem to be lacking coconut? These babies were loaded with it and were large in size to boot. I think I bit into the tail on every shrimp I ate on account of the batter being so delicious. The onion ring garnish was also amazing. Maybe it's just the fact that I don't eat gluten often, but the batter on everything was outstanding.

The linguine was pretty good as the seafood was tender and the noodles were just past al dente. The sauce was a little too white winey for me, but my boyfriend loved it. Maybe it felt like too much because I was already drinking a glass of Sauvignon Blanc.

All in all, I think this was a three and a half star dining experience. Admittedly, the biggest disappointment was likely my own elevated expectations. Yelp reviews caused me to believe that the food would be spectacular, and I'd say it was just good. Seeing the aquariums of crab was also sad as they were overcrowded and all trying to escape. Maybe I've just seen Finding Nemo too many times, but I couldn't watch them. Watching the chef, however, was fun, and the shellfish coming off the grill looked delicious. It's possible that we just didn't order the right thing, so we will likely go back once more during our stay to try their specials and the lobster tacos.

Great customer service hardly a wait and great place clean great staff!
Took our insurance from out of state all good 
Easy to find

It's a tire place...so they sell tires.  BUT, they also do alignment and all kinds of other stuff light head lights and other lights.  Got some good help from Brain and then got a free ride to work after I got my car all checked in and headed off to work.  Can't really complain about anything; I'd love to pay less for the tires, but they throw in a lot of extras that make it a little less painful, and their costs are comparable with other locations I checked.  See their page for details: http://www.gotodobbs.com.

Glad I am not the only one to experience his bad moods that he takes out on customers. Hence the variety of good and bad reviews, if you catch him on a good day, it's good customer service, if not...
Quality of work is inconsistent. Did a good job re-soling my husband's boots although we had to bring them back to be re-glued (no charge). I brought a pair of boots and two pair of platform wedge sandals in for new heels on all three. Boot heels perfect, sandal heels okay. He left sawdust all over my the black fabric sandals. $45.00 for heels on three pairs. I am used to picking up leather shoes and being surprised they are polished, but not at this store. Minimal effort.

Super friendly staff. Really clean inside and alot of unique teas to try. They use the actual taro root in their drinks so beware that their taro drinks are pulpy, but I enjoyed the flavor. The souffle cake was also nice and light.

The worst Double Tree we've ever stayed (and we stayed in this brand a lot).
Unwelcoming front desk.
 Dark, dated, gloomy, old and exhausted interior/exterior everywhere: starting from rooms, halls, lobby, the building itself and finishing with the quality of the linens, bath towels and the quality of the housekeeping. The only thing that got them to 2** rating is quite a good quality of the breakfast, and the nice gentleman we dealt with at check out.
Absolutely no-no for future reservations.
Truly outstanding in every way.  Staff knows everything about their products.  Helpful, unpretentious, and good wine pairing food.

I wound up eating here because every other spot in the area had a line out the door and I was starving.  Perhaps that should have been a hint.  There were only a handful of customers so I was seated quickly and service was prompt.  The food was edible, but not good.  My omelette was completely unseasoned and adding my own salt and pepper didn't improve the taste.  There was no side of fruit or hashbrowns to create a more filling meal, just stale white bread toast.  First of all, who still eats white bread and if that's the only option why would anyone want it stale?  Given the portion size and lack of flavor the price was too high.

By far the best sushi in south Tampa! Especially the bronze pebble and I like that they offer all types and forms of sushi, making it a very well rounded menu. Plus, the urban ambiance gives the joint a nice modern twist. Great for lunch or dinner.
no complaints.. good service, nice bartenders.. manager even came around to check on the customers...I've never had any issues here..

While staying in NOLA,hopped over for lunch and it was crowded. As you enter you see the open kitchen and know how well the food is prepared. Loved it at once. We ordered pad thai and it was really good. The spring rolls were good too. 
Came back for dinner and the crowd was a little less than lunch time. We ordered a lobster dish and it came out okay, but the fried eggplant was just awesome. Heard they are opening another branch nearby soon.

Easily my favorite go-to place!  They always have a solid beer selection and the music is way better than what other bars in the area are playing.  Great place to go to for bruch, especially hungover because it's pretty dark in there and it goes until 4pm.  Friendly staff, which is always a plus.

So everyone raved about the burgers here - had to check it out. Not bad - tough to eat because they were so damn big (height wise). Tasted great but that wasn't what was cool about the place. It was the space - really comfortable, neighborhoodish style. And the dude who wait on my was pretty friendly in his own hipster way. I'd go again if others wanted to but I wouldn't go out of my way.

I love this place! The music is ALWAYS good. Always! I love it because they do different theme nights daily so it's always something unique. Drinks and cover are always reasonably priced. Kind of dive-ish. 2 floors (2 different DJ's). Security is great. Only con - they're cash only! They could have more of my money if they accepted credit cards, haha. Since they are cash only, the bartenders (there are 3 bars) are quick, friendly, and attentive.

Go!

What an amazing, fun, cool, beautiful hotel. Best staff, great rooms, quiet, great location, amazing bar with a great band! People that complained in other reviews about not enough coffee cups, or lights are to dim need to stay at the best western! This is New Orleans, not Sunday school! STAY HERE!!!!!

Great quality coffee, cool decor, and a hipstery atmosphere. I've only stopped in to grab a cup to go, but it would be a great place to meet a friend and chat, or chill out with a book. I'm not a coffee expert, but no matter what I order on the menu I feel like I'm on my way to becoming a coffee snob.

Been here a few times and everytime I leave happy and satisfied!

The owner is a friendly man who really seems to care whether I enjoyed my food or not. 

I love their chana masala, because it has just enough heat and is filled with yummy spices. Their lamb tikka masala is good too, no stinginess on the lamb! What I really really like (and sometimes they dont have it- maybe sold out?) is the Alu Paratha. Its soo deliciously savory with the thin potato stuffing. 

Whenver the food comes out I always think its not enough but end up so happily stuffed! This is by far the best/most authentic (not that Ive ever been to india/pakistan) indian food in st louis! LIke other reviewers have said, good food, good price, good service!

I love Mood Café. So many juice and lassi choices. Like others here, I heart the carrot juice. The chaats are so flavorful and perfectly filling. You can't go wrong with anything you order. Hassan, the owner, will help you select an item or tailor one to suit your taste. The friends I've introduced to Mood have thanked me for it. What a treat on Baltimore Ave!

Indiana City Brewing is one of my favorites in Indy! I love that they always have a light beer on tap, that is hard to find these days with everyone enjoying dark beers or IPA's. I only wish they had more to the space like games, music or something. But overall love coming here!

Visiting from LA thought it would be nice to pick up some pastries for friends. Showed up at 6:03. Plenty of people were in the cafe and the lady at the door wouldn't let me in. I asked very politely if I could just grab some pastries which I received a reply of no I can't let you in. Pretty lame for a 6:00 close to say no to a patron at 6:03. There was no one else behind me either not like it would have kept a crowd coming in

I've always had a good experience with the West Chester location. The weekend mornings are a better time to go since it's not crowded. Customer service was good as long as you're only there for an oil change. I don't recommend any of the add-ons they offer. They will likely try to sell you new wiper blades or a new air filter (even though modern economy cars have lifetime air filters). Just say no to all the other crap they try to sell you, and you should be out of there in less than twenty minutes.
This is the closest Vietnamese restaurant around my area. Pho is great for the price. The rice dishes are also great. I love there Thai tea, very tasty and sweet.

I walked in with my wife and kid after a morning birthday party my kid had across the street. Seating was a little congested but I can understand due to the location. We ordered Chicken Biryani, Chicken Makhni and Naan. The food was good and the spice level was as we wanted (we eat less spice). They had some special going on so for a discount on the check. Overall it's got good food and will definitely go back again.
This place has got to be seen!!! So cute and  more importantly -the people are genuine. It feels like home and you can  feel the love there.  I'll be there everyday this week! Love from Chicago!

A regular staple for evening dining in chain-riddled North county! Warm quaint atmosphere & great service - perfect for a date or even adult family dinner. Cajun carbonara is very tasty, as is the grilled portobello - very generous cuts of meat & fish! All in all tasty fresh food & a great atmosphere in the heart of old town Florissant!

I went to the soft opening out this restaurant and have returned many times afterwards because I was so impressed during my first dining experience here. The food is consistently amazing, the service is perfect, and the wine list is interesting as well. They excel in their small plates though, do try their appetizers along with your entree! The pasta is made in house and their sauces are complimentary and flavorful.

One word- YUM!!
The mango lassi was delicious. So were the appetizers, the dinners, the roti, and the naan. All fresh, the right level of spice as ordered and all hot! The plate with the kabob was sizzling!
Meun Fan is one of my favorite Thai restaurants in Santa Barbara! It's great quality, authentic and not too expensive. Get the pad see ew or pad Thai; also love the eggplant dish. Service was okay

This place has a great vibe . This 3 store brick building was build in 1910 to serve as a railway headquarters. Pretty impressive . Inside you can find crafted beers (Voyager is my all the time favorite there) and delicious food . I tend to choose the same when I visit this place.  My choices are : The Depot burger which is a tasty burger especially if you are hungry.( Last time we had to share it. ), grilled broussell sprouts  ( I even didn't know I can possibly like them ), and of course sweet potato fries . (they  always go great with anything) . I would recommend to try their mustard. 
If you are visiting Reno , this would be the place to check out. If you live in Reno then it would be good to know that their Happy hours Monday - Sunday 3-6 pm.
Another interesting fact to know . They do delicious courses of meal and drinks for happy NY celebration.

Went to dinner last night and noticed the chicken was undercooked, red and raw after eating a few bites.  Manager gave our party two $10 dollar vouchers for our next visit and took off the app.  I don't think this did justice.  We ordered the chicken and waffle sliders.  No one enjoyed their entrees.  The vouchers will be going towards a beer sampler if and when we go back next time.

I really love German Bistro.  It has a great local restaurant feel!  Prices may seem high for dinner service upon first glance, but given the free beer and wine, indulge and it more than pays for itself!

I found this little Gem of a place over a year ago via Groupon and they NEVER disappoint. The reception area always welcomes you with a smile and warmth. They know who you are and are so accommodating. The entire staff is FABULOUS!! I absolutely LOVE Nikki (masseuse) her attention to details and her personal little touches... Would be very hard not to appreciate her and what she offers... Michelle (masseuse) is also another BEST with the Hot Stones.. Wow you have NOT lived until you have had a Hot Stone Massage.. It's a must try.. 
Overall the staff, location and treatments are great and if you ever have a problem or issue ask to speak to a Manager and they work with you... 3 Thumbs up as far as I am concern.

Attended the USP Graduation at the Liacouras Center. Intimate venue. Good sight lines. Parking garage is across the street. Stiff a pretty rough part of town, but definite gentrification can be seen since our last visit to the Temple area more than 10 years ago.

Yo the croissants here are banging. Probably the best in Philly. Great coffee and solid spot to get some work done. They also accept credit card, and it's such a clean and modern looking bakery. Everyone here is so friendly. A real gem right here.
Awesome hole in the wall , food was banging,  service friendly ! Lot of good reviews from neighborhood locals , so had to try it out . The Stoner Burrito is the real deal yo.

I went to the Tracey UYE S.P.S. Extravaganza.  Where were you?  I ordered the "special" St Paul Sandwich.  I was guessing this was the best way to go.  It was okay.  Pretty much what I expected.  The mayo was a little weird. Hot mayo grosses me out. 

I think I've made this sandwich late at night after way too many vodkas.  You go to the Philco (fridge) and start grabbing and frying.  You bring it all together with about 3 eggs, throw it on bread and there you go.  I like it on toast.  Not exactly the same but similar.

Hao had the hook-up since she speaks Mandarin, they had a little food conver with the owner. I know she seemed pretty happy with her food. Cherie, girl you had enough food for 2 days, your so little too. Darn you.  That  tofu dish you ordered looked good.

  I meet a new Yelper friend Tonii, if she puts the east side "like" event together I'll go.  Venice Ill doesn't scare me.

It is a cute, and colorful small restaurant.  Next time I'm jonesing for a Vess peach or cream, I know where to go.  The owners were very nice and they busted a move to get that food to the table.  We did take up the whole middle of the restaurant.  I give them 5 stars for their service

I've been to Ralph three times over the past few years, and I don't think I'll be going back again.  Bottom line: this place is overpriced.  Case in point in the tomato and mozzarella appetizer.  It's $9.75.  I understand that appetizers and desserts are the place to mark-up prices, and that's fine. These people run a business to make money.  However, I cannot respect a restaurant that gouges its customers.  This particular appetizer is one tomato cut up (prob cost them 50 cents), a few small mozzarella balls, and then a drizzle of balsamic vinaigrette.  A dish that costs them $2-$3 to make should not be priced at $9.75.  Similarly, a bottle of beer, Stella, cost $7.  Furthermore, the menu prices on their website are out of date and misleading.  Another case in point: the veal saltimbocca.  On the website, it's listed as $23.  In the restaurant, however, its $25.  This is one of my favorite dishes because of the prosciutto that is traditionally supposed to cover the veal cutlet.  At Ralph's, there were three tiny bites of prosciutto.  I honestly don't think I was even given one full slice, let alone enough to cover the veal.  

I think Ralph's offers traditional Italian food in a great atmosphere.  However, in a city like Philadelphia where Italian restaurants are a dime a dozen, Ralph's has to do much more to make it worth your while.  The food isn't bad, but it's not great either.  On top of serving lackluster food, they have the nerve to charge an arm and a leg for it.  I can think of at least two other Italian restaurants in the city where the food is better AND cheaper.  Ralph's is the perfect example of a once-great restaurant that is now resting on its laurels and relying on name only.  Try it out if you must, but don't expect to be wowed.
Excellent coffee, great ambience, and friendly staff.  Oh and did I mention... the macaroon was absolutely to-die-for?  Great way to spend a weekend morning.

I can't say enough good things about this place!!!! I'm from Mass and my bf is from the Tampa area so I originally booked an appt in Ybor city  (YBCT) during our vacation....but after some mis-communication or non communication (ugh)  it didn't happen so we decided to roll down to St. Pete....I quickly yelped the best place to get a tattoo and this place popped up. 

I wanted a really pretty blue-ish peony tattoo on my right wrist and originally I honestly wanted a girl to do it to add a bit of a feminine touch but I got Brian (Bower) and he was nothing but wonderful! He quickly sketched it out and it was slightly bigger than I originally thought in my head, but after he placed it, I was super excited and happy and decided to just leave it the way it was drawn! He also quoted a really reasonable price which I was happy to pay! Brian was also very professional and invited me back to his space so that I could see that all the needles were new!

Not only was Brian super helpful and patient, but he made sure both me and my bf were comfortable, made small talk, and did exceptional work. He started out by saying he was really happy that was his first tattoo of the day since he really enjoyed doing bright and colorful flowers! I knew that was a good sign! :)

He also answered all my questions on the shading and color choices and he went out of his way to match the colors I had in the reference photo on my phone. He went over and beyond the time with all the details and shading, outline, etc.... both me and my bf (also an artist) loved the tattoo!!!!  He loves his art and his passion really shows!
This Bostonian highly recommends Foolish Pride and thanks Brian for a kickass tattoo!!! I adore it!
This grocery store is great! Perfect size for the broad ripple neighborhood. There are organic options, and the workers are very friendly.

Not sure about their steak and cheese as I was visiting early AM catching a flight.  Ordered a bacon and egg sandwich on a roll and coffee. Coffee was good which gets the one star. The sandwich came with cheese which I had asked to exclude but had to take it as I was rushing for a flight. The bacon was nearly raw like it just came out of the package. It ruined the entire sandwich and in the trash it went.

Seorak exceeded my expectations. The portions were perfect, food was well cooked and plated but what I loved most was the service. I really appreciated the manager coming to our table to ask how the food and drinks were (highly recommend the cucumber geisha).

Their staff is knowledgeable and as much as I love coming for a bottle to have out back, it's a few dollars cheaper to get a bottle and go home. I love going in the spring or fall but it gets super crowded.

Very good casual launch experience from start to finish.  Ordering was fast on a touch screen kiosk, and my food was ready within 5mins.  Seating area was clean and there was wifi and there were outlets available if I wanted one.

Just had a delicious lunch of their "mixtas": my selection was the brussel sprouts, camote (Mexican purée of sweet potatoes) and steak. Everything was delicious, service was very good, decor is high quality and they were playing great Latin music. I recommend.

O Sole Mio is a great addition to the neighborhood! We were welcomed by the friendliest owner who accommodated us with high chairs for the kids and cold waters on the hot day. Not a ton of seating options, but it worked perfectly for us to park our stroller right next to the outdoor tables. They also brought us a basket of bread just to help keep our kids occupied. We ordered the Caprese salad, buffalo margarita pizza, and the pesto pizza. They were so good and IMO better than some of the "trendier" options close by. I am rooting for this place to do well bc we will definitely be back!

This is such a hidden gem of a breakfast/brunch spot in Doylestown. Cross Keys Diner is pretty good too on Swamp Road, but is always mobbed. Back to the 50s is just as good, but it is so much easier to find a seat, especially on weekends. Their menu features traditional breakfast/brunch fare, but their specials on the chalkboard every day are the real reason to go. There is always an excellent variety of savory and sweet options (typically between 5-7 a day). The specials are just a shade on the pricey side, but I'll be honest, we've never had a bad one. Their inventive creme cheese stuffed French toasts with fruit compotes are amazing. Their pancakes, crepes, waffles and omelets are original and quite tasty. Last but certainly not least, the staff is super friendly, very responsive and makes the visit all the more enjoyable. Highly recommended. We'll definitely be back.
Great food , very tasty , Service is sometimes slow but over all clean place , halal food . Highly recommended
Pizza is amazing!!! Great byo place that's kid friendly!!! We had their meatball pizza and Neapolitan dessert. I even got my parents a gift certificate here for Christmas!

My visit to Nook was quite pleasant. The service was super, but the food was just okay. I had high hopes for this diner, but I was let down by the quality of the food. I got the paleo pizza and the crust was very dry and didn't hold its shape. The flavor was good, but I probably would not get this a second time. Overall, I enjoyed the experience, but I wasn't a fan of the paleo food.

Free tour...which is pretty sweet. My husband and I are not Bud fans...but still like hearing the history of the Anheiser-Busch families. 

Wear decent walking shoes as it is a 60 minute tour that consists of mainly walking. It was pretty warm today when we went on the tour. Some of the buildings did have A/C, but I was looking forward to being done. Free beer at the end of the tour which is great if you like the Bud brands. soda for the kids...which was luke-warm and a tad flat. 

Worth stopping by if you have time to kill in STL. One that I would probably not go to all the time.

BTW...if your GPS is unable to locate the actual location...here is the physical address of the brewery: 1127 Pestallozi St. & Lynch St, St Louis, Missouri.

I've been to this location and cherry hill and they are both awesome. But what I love is their crunchy shrimp sushi. I usually let my friend order for me cause I never know what to get but its good anytime he orders it. I usually have my food rather quickly and always a comfortable setting. I absolutely love those soda machines because of the wide variety of sodas and juices that you can customize.

My wife and I dropped in tonight for dinner. I prefer the authentic menu items and my wife prefers the Americanized  menu.  Both choices  are good. In general the food is very good.  The downside is that the service really sucks. The staff is running around in a near chaos state. There is no organization. If the service was better we would  return more often.

Sociale very well might be my new favorite Italian spot in Tampa! HUGE portions, super quick turnaround after you order, and quality wine (the $7 Sangiovese was great!) The build your own pasta lets you get a little creative, and the mix-and-match meatball platter is a stand-out that I haven't seen on any other menu. Highly recommend!

My girlfriend & I had lunch at Yai Yai's where we were very happy with the preparation, presentation, & amount of food we were served. The generous servings were absolutely delicious. The food is very reasonably priced. I will go back for more & highly recommend this wonderful restaurant.

Best authentic Japanese cuisine and sushi place in St. Petersburg.  While the fish is fresh and the sushi rolls ranging from reliable and unique,  what sets this place apart from the rest of the gang is the authentic Japanese appetizers.  You must have the barbecue squid and the tuna tataki is to die for.  Not too far away from Tyrone Square Mall

The atmosphere is nice and casual. The service was friendly. However, I was unimpressed with the food. The dishes we tried had a strong tomato base and it just made the flavors weird. The beef itself was nice and tender. The rice had stale grains mixed throughout. My bf didn't enjoy the fried plantains or his coffee all that much. We skipped dessert.

This place is so cute...of course, everything in Montecito seems to be. Inside and out, it's just adorable. The quaintness translates to a bit of crowding, though. I felt like they had maybe one too many tables crammed in there, fortunately we were dining late, and it wasn't too suffocating. 

Upon looking at the menu, I was astonished at some of the prices. $17 for an enchilada and taco? We were celebrating, so I just went with it. We ordered the halibut ceviche, and I went with the aforementioned combo. Holy cow...amazing ceviche. I loved it. Then, the food came. So good...and huge! I went into dinner pretty ravenous, thinking I would devour everything, but I managed to only eat about half. My favorite part was how fresh the tomatoes were...I love tomatoes. 

For dessert we went with the espresso martini, which was a perfect combination of the chocolate and coffee tastes I crave after meals. 

One of my favorite parts was when they boxed up our food they put it in plastic containers instead of Styrofoam. Everything was kept sealed very well, and it was quite tasty reheated. 

I was pleased with the service and the whole experience actually. I would certainly return...well, when I start working again so I can afford it.

My hidden little sushi gem! Is it fancy? No. Is it hip? Not really. But the sushi at this quaint establishment is on point!! People always flock to Subzero and Drunken Fish down the road or even Tani in Clayton...which is great, I love all those places too!!! But the best sushi in St. Louis is right here people and very reasonably priced. Go show Kampai some love...you won't be sorry!

Definitely a no-frills place, but that's perfectly OK sometimes.  I had never been here before but my husband has been raving about it for years, so off we (finally) went.  

I would describe the burger as tasting like a Five Guys burger, only not as greasy and less expensive.  So in other words, totally worth it.  We both got fries but the portions on the fries are huge so we could have easily split one....lesson learned for next time.  Even though its nothing fancy, it is very clean which I appreciated.  All in all, its a great place.  I'll definitely be back.

I would have to agree with the very first review by BH.  I came to Nashville for a school interview and decided to lodge with La Quinta anyways.  I've lodged at various other La Quinta places and if ever I have to come back for something important and need a good nights rest, I won't be staying at this particular La Quinta.  However, amenities that I needed for my interview were readily available: blow dryer, iron and board, free Wi-Fi, soap, shampoo, free continental breakfast, and free parking.  Because of the hotels location near the train tracks, I could not sleep because of the trains screeching brakes, which went from midnight until 2am in the morning. Mind you I had to get up at 6am to attend an interview at 7:45am.  Throughout the night I used my pillows to filter out the sounds and it might have done the trick but then again I am not too sure if I slept at all or just closed my hopes hoping to fall asleep.  The location is not really close by to anything other than restaurants.   I had paid $66 for a one night stay, but when compared to other places I've stayed at the same price, I have had better experiences.

Went for dinner with a group from work. Most horrible experience I have had in a restaurant in a very long time. 
The waiter was slow, smart mouthed, rude, and when he did come to the table he was pushy! Slamming down our plates and glasses! Why in the world would a waiter tell the customer 'thanks for not getting food on the menu!' WHAT! It's a paper menu, one of our party spilled something on one, big deal it's a restaurant for petes sake! Laminate them then! 
Then in top of that the Salmon fish and chips were tasteless and greasy! 
Overall not a good first impression at all! The only reason for the 2 stars is the manager sent over a new waiter to finish after we complained.

The Love is a perfect example of what two people can do. Aimee Olexy of Talula's Garden fame and Stephen Starr pair up to bring us this amazing new edition to the regions culinary scene. 

The decor is minimal yet cozy highlighted by the arched brickwork in the ceiling. The cocktails are lovingly prepared. I highly recommend the $20.00 Manhattan. A custom made over proofed rye made specifically for The Love is the standout ingredient in this perfect Manhattan. 

The food, not surprisingly, is well executed and was absolutely delicious. I enjoyed every bite of my Farmers Salad, Roasted Brussels Sprouts, and my Acorn Squash with red sauce and burrata. We finished off the evening with the Chocolate Slice and the Cookie Plate which paired very well with my glass of vintage port. I loved The Love!

Fantastic little restaurant on the edge of the Quarter near the French Market and the Old U.S. Mint.  It's clearly related to Saint Lawrence (on the other side of the Quarter) but this is more of a casual restaurant than bar and the food & service initially appear to be better (or at least more consistent) here.  On a recent weeknight visit everyone in my group absolutely loved their food - deviled eggs, red beans & rice, char-grilled oysters, fried green tomato & shrimp po-boy, and gnocchi.  Wow, some of the best traditional NOLA food you'll find in town plus they've got some additional items & twists.

Service was great (admittedly on a slow night), and while prices may seem a tad high initially you'll also find that the portions are huge and everything appears to be cooked in-house from scratch.  Plus you can get a real daiquiri including the signature Pimms Cup from Saint Lawrence and they donate $1 from every daiquiri plus some of the restaurant proceeds to The Roots of Music (Saint Cecilia is apparently the patron saint of musicians).  They've also got discounted oysters and drinks during happy hour from 4-7pm and they're apparently open long hours from 9am to Midnight daily.

This will definitely be a go-to place when I'm going to Frenchmen Street (where there's not much exciting in terms of restaurants) or the Old U.S. Mint for festivals.  Or when I have folks in town who want real New Orleans food including some of the best red beans in town.  Bravo!!

I really, really love HWK. It's one of my very favorite places. Every meal I've had there has been wonderful, the $30 bottles of wine are so smart, the service is great...the entire restaurant makes me happy.

I most recently went this past weekend for lunch. My husband was in a burger mood, and as he started googling "best burger in STL," I reminded him that he's already had the best burger that St. Louis can possibly offer. So, off we were again to HWK.

Once we got there, I flip-flopped a million times on my order (and our waiter very patiently put up with me) before I finally decided on the burger as well. We were going to try the panisse frites to start, and because my husband ordered the "fries," the waiter was really kind in explaining what they were and setting expectations so he wasn't disappointed. We were excited to try the panisse, but after a few minutes, our waiter told us they weren't happy with the way they were setting/molding, and surprised us with a huge and wonderful cheese plate.

The burger, yet again, earned it's rightful place in our household as "best burger in STL." It's so delicious and filling, I didn't need to eat the rest of the day. I can't wait to try No Menu Mondays...I've really enjoyed dinners there, so going on a Monday night is definitely next on the list.

So far I've visited Fat Ham twice; the first time I visited, I was completely blown away.. the second time... well. you will see.

The first time I visited:
- ricotta spread was perfectly smooth and smoky 
- oyster sliders were highlight of the meal-- juicy oysters fried with spicy & crunch batter
- pulled pork was a meh
- charred cabbage was a huge surprise... VERY GOOD
- hot chicken was crispy and spicy..  and actually, too spicy for me. Potato salad was too salty.
- pecan pie.. oh.. pecan pie... 

My first experience was so good that I just had to go back, which I did few days ago. 

Unfortunately, the oyster slider had too much batter (where is my oyster?) and hot chicken was GODDAMN hot. Ricotta and pecan pie were good, though. 

I might give Fat Ham another try, when their menu is updated.

Today is day one on the trip and we are heading out. Everything seems to be going along nicely but I am highly disappointed in how their drink package is set up. I am 22 years old and sharing a room with my grandma who is 75 years old. They will not allow me to purchase the drink package if my grandma doesn't because we are sharing a room. I understand this policy so people can't share drinks and I believe it is a good policy. But are you kidding me!!! She will drink a glass of wine a day and she will pay for it! I now have to suffer this trip and possibly spend way more money than I would originally because I can't purchase the drink package! I am not happy at all with the customer service about this situation. Not one person has been kind about trying to figure it out. Hopefully the rest of this cruise goes better than the beginning.

Back again, this time on vacation having moved back to NYC from Tampa. One of the many great losses in the transition back has been a place like Basimo's. In the realm of gourmet coffee houses and $15 juices and smoothies that NYC is, nothing hangs with Basimo's $8 wonders. 

Keep it up family-run business.

Our waitress was very kind. I had the chicken tortilla soup which was my favorite thing. Tasted very homemade and healthy. Real ingredients. My taco salad I didn't like at all. The lettuce was weird, kinda old maybe?
We ordered the guacamole sampler that was good, very unique flavors. 
My husband said he loved his tacos, and the dessert we ordered was plantain foster (like bananas foster) homemade Carmel sauce was fantastic. I would like to go back just to try a burrito because the people next to us order these massive beautiful looking burritos. I wouldn't order a salad there again but the hot food is good. Other thing that made me sad was they don't serve ground beef. They only have sliced or shredded meat. So not tradition ground taco meat etc. I would go back to try a burrito though. They looked killer.

Cake Bake is like stepping into the tea party you pictured in your head when you were a little girl. It is everything you wanted in your imagination, even when you made your little brother get dressed up and have "tea" with you at high noon!This place is so amazingly elegant you will never want to leave.

Okay now that I got all that off my chest--let's review this place! I had tea and raspberry cake. Both the tea(which had enough tea for a couple cups) and the cake were full of flavor. The cake had glitter in the frosting. Glitter people! How cute??! 

The whole shop is beautifully decorated and they have so many amazing choices for sweets. If you have a little girl or babysit a little girl, please take her! She will love it! I will love it! Take me! Haha. 

In all seriousness you can tell the owners wanted this place to thrive. Their hard work on the desserts, tea, coffee, location, and decoration have set this place apart from any dessert place in Indy. Well done Cake Bake!

Loved the atmosphere. Sitting with all the doors opens listening to the activities in Jackson Square. Be prepared to not have a decent conversation, because it's so loud you can't hear yourself think. The food is good, would go again, but nothing that I would go out of my way for. Prices are decent for the Quarter.

3 1/2 STARS

Wanted a local place for brunch on a Sunday morning while we visited with friends. The 2 of us followed all the rave reviews and arrived before a big push followed in after us. Waited about 10 minutes for our name to be called and was greeted with a huge smile. It so happened that we were sat at a table big enough for 5 and offered the rest of the table up for a community seating if they needed it.

Coffee was good. The wait for food was reasonable since they cook to order. My husband was looking forward to one of their signature dishes, Hobo Hash served with biscuit and sausage gravy on the side. I ordered the corned beef hash, over medium eggs and corn muffin. It comes with hash browns or grits...I got both. I was asked if I wanted onions or cheese in my hash browns. I said yes to onions. Was also offered cheese on my grits. I declined.

The waitstaff all worked very well together, each one either seating customers, bringing out food for any table and refilling coffee.

My husbands Hobo Hash was not as interesting as he had thought it would be...eggs...omlette style, filled with hash browns, cheese, peppers and onions and even now, as I write this, neither of us can remember if there was any meat in it. He added hot sauce to see it it would help but only half of it was eaten.  The gravy was bland in flavor except for pepper and he felt that the biscuit was slightly underdone. 

My hash, traditional canned (which I do confess to loving), was crispy on both sides and piping hot. My eggs were cooked perfectly. The hash browns were some of the best I have ever had!  DELISH!! Grits were grits and the corn muffin was a deliciously, light version which I enjoyed with butter and honey.

If in the area, I would like to come back and check out their lunch offerings.
Just took the wife and kids to this restaurant for the first time good authentic Texas barbeque great big beans awesome pulled pork!!!

The congenial service and attention from the owner to the bus boy make this restaurant special.  No effort was spared to make us happy, even to the extent of preparing a dish gratis in response to my inquiry.  The food was quite good and measured up to the best of the local Indian restaurants.  Everything was obviously made fresh, making the wait a bit on the longer side, but worth it.  We were even given an extra container of rice to accompany our "doggie bag".  Warning to the uninitiated, "medium" spice was on the hot side.  We had a great experience and will definitely be coming back again.

I go here every time I am visiting. I usually sit at the bar and the bartenders usually working are very friendly. Happy hour has some great deals! The hot cauliflower is my favorite but everything else I have tried is also great!!

These are not your average Taco Bell, Moe's, Qdoba, and dare I say it Chipotle (sheesh I really love Chipotle) tacos. 

Took a suggestion from a respected fellow Yelper, Christian S., and tried this place. Well let's just say I only got 3 tacos and boy did I want more. I already knew what I wanted before I got there. Online menus serve a purpose people, if nothing else it helps you narrow down your choices and if you're like me, it pretty much helps you walk into a new place looking like a pro. Back to the matter at hand, I ordered 3 shrimp tacos, fish of the day was perch, no thank you. And Mahi Mahi, is a little too strong for my subtle fish palate. So 2 glazed shrimp tacos and 1 fried shrimp taco it was for me. Took it to go. First I definitely appreciate the care they place in their to go containers. They serve their tacos on these taco triangle thingamajigs in the restaurant which help the tacos to stand up. Well lo and behold they have a cardboard version of it for the take out tacos. Major points for that, they seriously take tacos serious... So I ordered my tacos and a drink and I waited. A girl at the bar who was eating told me to place my number in the holder. That's how they identify you. It was appreciated but probably not needed only because the restaurant wasn't busy and when the lady bought my tacos out she called me by name. But the hospitality was gracious. 

Got to my car cause I had somewhere to be, opened the box of tacos and one side of the cardboard taco holder had flattened and my fried shrimp taco was all over the place. No biggie I just put the taco together. First bite, the glazed tequila lime, or whatever shrimp taco. It was good, two nice sized juicy, sweet, perfectly cooked shrimp in the taco. I was in love. I had been searching for a great shrimp taco and I think I found it. I had one at El Camino a few weeks ago and it was abysmal, lacked flavor and totally disappointed my taste buds. Not this taco at Buena, was fabulous! The chipotle crema was really tasty and had a nice zing. Now I love hot sauce and was about to put some on mine but I'm glad I didn't because the crema provides just enough bite. Now onto the fried shrimp taco. Batter beware, really good breading and batter on these shrimp. Kind of tempura style so the shrimp aren't buried in the breading. It was a smidge salty but I am really averse to any salt at this point in my life so don't take that as a cautionary measure from me. 

I forgot to mention that they have Boylan's soda on fountain tap. Umm yesss because this is my favorite soda ever, well that and Frank's and Dr. Browns, but these sodas are so yummy it was nice to see it somewhere as a fountain drink as opposed to the big box soda dealers...

My side notes and suggestions: They should increase the size of the soda cup. It's small for the $3 they charge, even if it's Boylan's. If you're hungry order more than 3. If it's your first time order 3, then order more if you like them because you will be hungry. I forgot to order the corn with mine so that may have helped stave off my lingering hunger after I ate my tacos. Finally, they have a rewards program. Really nice to have for a non chain establishment. 

Finally, I expected these tacos to be good. I mean come on, it's from Jose Garces who had like the best taco truck, Guapos Tacos, in the city for a while. Plus pretty much everything he, Stephen Starr, and Michael Solomonov seem to touch or open in this city you can pretty much guarantee a good meal. 

Went on a Wednesday night and it wasn't crowded. Municipal parking lot right across from the restaurant if you struggle finding street parking.

Very good uptake on fast, casual dining.

It's never easy giving your daughter's hand in marriage, but when that day comes, you want it to be special. I have no doubt that my daughter had the most beautiful day possible by having her wedding at The Bluffs On Broadway. This was an amazing setting on the bluffs of the Mississippi River. The view of the river was striking and there was beauty everywhere you looked in the gardens surrounding the house. The house itself is unbelievable and has the perfect layout for guests to mingle, dance, eat, and celebrate. The lower level and patios were alive with music and dancing while the upper level and decks provided an area to eat with more intimate settings for friends and relatives to catch up and visit. The food was incredible too. My guests went on and on about how delicious it was and how accommodating the entire staff was. Mark and his staff had a solution for every mistake we had made in planning or lack of planning. They made what could have been a very stressful day with a wedding party of 20, families that hadn't met, and difficult relatives into a joyous event. I am so thankful for all they did. It was above and beyond anything I've ever experienced....

I've had their pizza by the slice a few times.  It's about as good as it gets around here for NY style pizza.  I work downtown, and this is probably the best pizza option there is downtown for a reasonably priced lunch.

I've also had their Reuben and it was quite tasty.  The thousand Island slaw was spicy, which was unexpected, but I love spicy food, so this worked out great for me.  

I will be back often to work through the rest of the menu.

Edit - 1/17/14 Came back for a slice and this time tried their Hot Italian Beef.

Pizza - outstanding as usual.

Hot Italian Beef.  The menu says it has a spicy Giardinara.  This Giardinara is not spicy at all.  Tastes like they left out the spice completely and just brined some vegetables.  The Reuben I had here last time had more spice than this.  The meat used on this sandwich is terrible.  It is a very low quality rubbery beef.  I've had dozens of Italian Beef sandwiches.  This one is not good at all.

Went on date here a couple weeks ago. It's decent, laid out in a way that no one is overlapping each other. You have to have a membership to play and it's 4 bucks per person to play after membership...which kinda makes it a little....odd. you're paying for the membership AND THEN paying to play the same day. Smoking is allowed inside, and food is prepped and made inside the tiny cafeteria. Alcohol is also served. My only issue is the parking....finding fuscos wasn't the easiest challenge because it was dark and it's not well lit. Be very careful driving there.
Always looking for flavorful vegetarian food. Great selection. Really nice staff. Clean atmosphere. Good  prices, nice portion size. I will return
Great food, even better atmosphere. Make sure you get a nice coast-side table outside.

We just had a wonderful stay at the Eagle Inn last week. Stayed in the deluxe queen room. It was wonderful! Large fireplace, patio with lots of seating, beautifully decorated and very clean. 
The Spanish style architecture really set the mood. Love the carved wooden doors and terra cotta tiling.
Breakfast (included) is prepared fresh according to your order. Choices were eggs, meat, fruit, bagels, yogurt, granola, waffles.
Location is wonderful, very close to the beach and marina, but on a quiet side street.
Staff are friendly and very accommodating. We are anxious to return and try one of the casitas.

Not bad for a Mexican joint in Tennessee!! Fajitas were a'plenty, salsa was tangy and the chips were crispy. Only downside-seating isn't comfortable and beans were super, super salty. Other than that, it was pretty good!

Came here for dinner with a Groupon. The place was empty but it seems like they have a steady take out service. The service was good and the food was good. Big portions and the raita was great. The garlic naan could have used more garlic since it tasted and smelled like plain naan. We'll probably be back to try out other dishes.

Update: I came back with a friend to try their Wednesday night buffet and was pleasantly surprised. There was lamb, chicken and beef proteins, naan, all of the chutneys, vegetable simosas, byrani and dessert was golub juman and fruit. I was hesitant but for $14 a person this was great. I have been to other Indian buffets and they all failed hence my hesitation. My friend also agreed it was a great place to come back to on a Wednesday.

I was looking forward to this place.  After eating there I will be in no hurry to return for the food.  

Pros:
- very good beer selection.  Many drafts and bottled beers.  
- cool atmosphere 
- 5 minutes from my house

Cons:
- service: we found 2 seats at the bar to bypass the wait.  it was very busy but the bartender was not very attentive and he was either drunk , high or both
- food: seriously I've eaten better Mexican food at Chili's.  I couldn't agree more with Wanda's assessment of the salsa.  It was awful.  Ro-tel is much better than what we ate.  The burrito was ok, too much rice.  My wife liked her quasadilla but I wasn't impressed.  The nachos were decent.  Also the appetizer selection was lacking - only about 5 appetiZers on the menu.  

This place is racking up now because the Mexican bar/grill concept is novel for the area.  It's also a good place to drink.  But based on the food and service I will not be going back.
Interesting spot. Great decor. Delicious drinks. Appetizers were very good. Hummus, cheese board were delicious.

Loved Mo's! My boyfriend made reservations here for my birthday. As soon as we walked in, they greeted me with happy birthday and seated us with a special happy birthday Stacy menu! It was so cool! All the food was amazingly delish! And they brought me the most incredible chocolate cake!
Only been here once and the steaks are great! The restaurant has an interesting layout and a rather small second floor! Be sure to look nice if you're coming in for a bit to eat!

I have been going to this bar since my college years and its only gotten better. Jeremy is an outstanding manager, professional, fun and welcoming. This bar has a very relaxed atmosphere, and depending on what time of the day you go, you'll find all sorts of awesome crowds. It is one of the few bars left around here that have indoor smoking, but there is outside seating option as well. 

Overall, this is not a typical "college bar". Almost all nights are 21+, the music is well rounded, the bar tenders are mature and professional. In fact, the only thing that makes this place "college friendly" are their amazing drink specials and the option to play fun college games. And... that its right across from UT. But seriously, who doesn't like drink specials and some entertainment!! ;)

If you're in NOLA and want great food outside of the French Quarter, stop by Morrow's. I highly recommend the BiBimBap. The prices are great. Extremely friendly staff. The drinks are !! The location is small, but the food packs BIG flavor! The owner/proprietor, Larry Morrow, is Nawlins native and he's all about serving his community. I suggest getting there early, as they're known to have a line. Just know, it'll be well worth the wait!!

I used to live in Bryn Mawr and loved insomnia! I would get my cookies warm and a cup full of ice cream, yum! Unfortunately here in west chester I got cold cookies and my fiancé visibly got more ice cream than me. Three stars because the cookies are delicious but wished they were warm and delivery didn't take 1 hr and 1/2.

I came here on a Monday afternoon with my friend and we sat at the bar. WOB is your typical chain restaurant, however I was very surprised by how delicious and reasonably priced my lunch was. We both ordered the 8.99 buffalo chicken sandwich which comes with your choice of side, I chose mac & cheese. Wow all I can say is I was blown away by how good the Mac was. It arrived a small dish topped with toasted bread crumb coating. The mac and cheese had a kick to it as well. The buffalo chicken sandwich was delicious and crispy!although I was really hoping for some blue cheese to dip into it. 

Unfortunately yards PYNK was tapped, so I ordered both sangrias and a cider.
The red sangria was nothing spectacular. However if you like sweeter sangria, I HIGHLY recommend the white peach sangria. Ugh it was so good I wish I ordered that twice instead of the red.

All in all, my friend and I had a great meal. The bartenders were all very attentive and super cool with me sampling out beer.

If you like beer and good bar food I recommend.

If you like people watching, enjoy a great patio and enjoy half price bottles of wine on Sunday after 3; then this is your place.

The food is good, but I honestly can't say spectacular.  I am not a big fan of meatloaf but would recommend the barbecue meatloaf here.  I also love the Torrado's and for starters the sesame barbecue chicken is deli-sh.

Parking in Hillsboro village; well it is what it is.  Your options are street parking or in the evenings take advantage of the post office or church parking.  It is very noisy on the street with all the ambulances and fire trucks that usually go by.

The wait staff while a little peculiar on occasion do a great job keeping up with the flow of traffic; although there socialization skills could be refined!

I would highly recommend this place based on just one item that we had a few months back - the puri/halwa with chholey!!! This is a northern style dish from the Indo-Pak area (the joint is Pakistani-owned). Those who are not familiar with this style of halwa might find it greasy with ghee/oil. But hey! That is how it is made! That chholey tempers the sweetness of the Halwa. We loved it. Also, we had a great chat with the male owner (I think, he is the owner) who used to play first division cricket in Pakistan!!! We had a nostalgic chat about the great Indo-Pak matches of the 1980s and the early 1990s. Ohhh! I gave 4 stars because of the ambience. But again, we actually like it because we find it cozy :).
Great place. Very very good staff and amazing sandwiches. Would definitely come here again and would suggest anyone in St. Louis to support the local business.

It is an absolute must I get my Latin fix while in my home town. I have been coming here for years and I can always count on them to fix my cravings. Although I couldn't get my normal Cuban sandwich (I no longer eat meat) I was able to enjoy the famous black beans and rice with a hand rolled authentic devil crab!

I have had several experiences with the SB Airbus and am happy to say that I have been completely satisfied.  From Dodger Games on the 4th of July to Mother's Day at the Magic Castle, I give five stars!  Super friendly staff, and Joe is our favorite driver with all his great stories!!  What a great locally owned private company!

+ dog friendly
+ consistent good service
+ all the beers!
+ discount on beer when train stops (choo choo)
+ cool atmosphere and good for groups
+ their party room is well organized, same cool atmosphere but away from the main area to enjoy large parties. (I had a better time here for my rehearsal dinner than I did the actual wedding...)

- only negative is the food is nothing to write home about ( C at best)

This place has been around for as long as I can remember, and I still stop by often due to the very good prices and nice selection.

Its your "normal" produce selection, but the prices are often much lower than what you will find at a grocery store. On the flipside much of the stock is in a "eat it today or tomorrow" state, but depending on your shopping habits that isn't a bad thing. They also have their own sauces and dressings (the salad dressings are great), and the owner and his son are always friendly. Gotta love the vintage Rocky posters and pinups that are randomly strewn about too.

Worth stopping by, especially since it is right next to Pudge's.
Kids talking and being disruptive during the whole movie; staff refused to do anything about it.

I may be partial to this particular Dobbs because a family member works here, but I have never had anything but decent service.

Their staff has always been great to work with.  They usually do their best to fit you in if you're a walk-in or if you call ahead, they'll do their best to work around you.

They do need to improve on how their warranties work and how they relay that things need to be done to your vehicle.

All in all, however, this is my go-to Dobbs and I most likely will not change to another.

Last year, they recently increased the toll from $4 to $5 for Passenger vehicles entering Pennsylvania.  And while there are discounts for frequent commuters ($6 credit to an E-ZPass tag for crossing 18 times in a calendar month) and senior discounts program, it's tough to shallow the increase knowing that there is a toll surplus.  That mismanagement by the Delaware River Port Authority and their fear of a lowered bond rating motivated the increase.  And this is while the DRPA executives and their families and friends were able to cross the bridge for free.

I gave an extra star since this 85 year old steel suspension bridge is still impressive to look at when light up at night.

Great time! One thing we didn't like was having to eat the second we got on the boat..do NOT get first seating. Food was ok...white chocolate bread pudding was GREAT! As you cruise the river a narration is broadcast by one of the captains, which was very informative. A great way to spend a couple of hours in NOLA!
Went for first time yesterday and will go back for certain. Had the bucatini carbonara small plate and it was best I've ever eaten! And a great mojito!! Friendly efficient staff. Loved it all.
You guys. I have wanted to try one of these sandwiches since I was pregnant in 2009. It was so worth the wait. I loved every single bite, I would have posted a pic but I inhaled it too fast.
Great store I'm going this weekend! Great deals great selection and better prices than the "other" thrift stores

Seasons is one of the better Vietnamese cafes in the St. Pete area. They have an extensive menu for a small cafe. You can get full rice plates, noodle bowls, banh mi sandwiches, and desserts. You order at the cashier, pay, and choose a seat to where your food will be delivered to you. All their foods are fresh and made to order. I've been here a few times, and the employees are all very friendly and accommodating.

I enjoy their banh mi sandwiches. I usually get the special, which has cold cut meats (pork roll, head cheese, and jambon) with the pickled veggies. I also got Brian's Special, which has grilled pork and egg. I love both sandwiches, and they are always made fresh right at the counter. You can also customize to your taste (for instance, I skip the jalapeño).

Seasons also has a desserts menu with something for everyone! They have shaved ice, bubble tea and slushies, coffee, and regular teas. You can get different toppings on the bing soo, like crushed Oreos, gummies, nuts, and various other candies. They cook their boba just right; they're not too chewy (I'm very picky about my boba). I ordered their Thai iced coffee and liked it. They put a lot of condensed milk in it, which is nice that they don't skimp, but it made it too sweet for my taste. Next time, I will ask for less, but it was a delicious drink regardless.

The inside of the restaurant is somewhat small; the tables get filled easily during peak meal hours because there's only about 10 tables inside. You can also take your food to go. 

If you're looking for a quick bite or a full sit-down meal, Seasons Cafe has great choices for Vietnamese street food.

This place is my favorite sushi location in the... wait for it... COUNTRY!!!

I was visiting a friend in Nashville and she suggested we come here for good sushi. Boy was she right! 

The location is kind of unassuming and its certainly nothing fancy inside, just darn delicious food.

I still dream of the ginger dressing on the salad and can't wait to make my way back here to enjoy that and any number of their yummy rolls. Samurai will be my first stop when I'm back in Tennessee.

Loved the location right at Jackson Square. Quick service and we were out of here in 45 minutes. Shrimp Etoufee, Cajun combo, and Creole combo were all delicious. Jambalaya was the favorite of the table! Drinks were also fair priced and the cocktails were delicious! The only con was we couldn't split the check between two couples, but enjoyed it for a quick meal as we explored the city.

This restaurant has fantastic wings that are large and meaty, great pizza and a lot of other excellent food.  The employees are very friendly and helpful.  Not a huge selection of beer but the food more than makes up for it!

My coworkers and I were on our way to Five Guys at lunch when we remembered that this place had just opened, so we rerouted and queued up in its slightly out the door line. The line around 12:15 was considerable, it probably took 15 to 20 minutes before we exited with our food (to go). So how was it? My experience was slightly tainted by an order mixup... when I got back to my office I found that although I ordered The 500 burger, I was missing lettuce and tomato. The bacon, however present, was pretty chewy; I'd prefer it much crispier. The burger itself was cooked to order and the combination of burger, brioche, roll, and cheddar really came together nicely. I inhaled it. I also accompanied this small wonder with the truffle fries. They were delicious, the truffle taste came through in every bite, but they were incredibly salty. For the rest of the day I staggered back and forth to the water cooler to quench my thirst, like a man walking through a desert that also has a water cooler in it. This place has some potential and I'd definitely try it again, but I'm not sure if I'd eat here any more than once a month. For those looking for a miniature version of the fabled Rouge burger, there is one distinction: The Rouge burger is topped with divine gruyère cheese while the 500 burger is only available with swiss, provolone, cheddar, or American. Other than that, the burger is pretty much the same, except about 1/4 the size or less. Brioche buns are key!

If you can get an egg on it... get an egg on it.
I've never had a bad thing here. When the Fishtown one opens I will be promptly gaining 100 lbs. 
The Super Gogeta of noodles - power level 2,500,000,000 - The Ultimate Fusion

Can't ask for a better cheap breakfast. I go here all the time when I want good and cheap food. Its filling, it taste great, and the service is quick. Definitely worth a shot. (Standard diner food - do not go in expecting any frills)

Simply...the best frozen custard anywhere.
Plenty of selections.  Reasonable prices.  Quick line movement.  Unbelievably good custard.
Enough said.

Best Burger in Santa Barbara. I'm a huge gourmet burger fan and for that alone I give it 5 stars. Some of their other dishes are hit or miss but they cook a mean filet mignon and their chicken salad is also quite tasty.

Every thing was heavy and overly salted. I had only one night in phily and regret wasting my time and money here. Octopus probably was the worst ku treated! Soaked in oil and salt! I can not recommend this restaurant!

The fish was nicely cut and very fresh. The pieces we had were good sized, unlike some of the other reviews. That gets it 4 stars! Sushi chefs are personable. Nice clean place. Some new rolls here that I haven't seen other places. The only down side is the dessert options for AYCE. I prefer a piece of fresh fruit( orange) that is commonly served other places. The only options here are fried bananas and ice cream.
Authentic French bakery with totally amazing Pastries and pretty awesome sandwiches/ croissants too.

Came in late for some ALL day breakfast, 
The waitress was very sweet and gave us great service. (Didn't catch her name, but she finished her shift at 11 and transferred us to her manager) 

We ordered waffles and chicken and a donut sandwich (check out the pictures) and holy shit! Sooooooo good.
Super disappointed we found out about this place on the last night. 

Will definitely come back, so much we gotta try!
Great place for aQuick bite.select all your own pizza toppings and they brick oven your pizza in less than 10 mins! Great tasting crust too. Nice selection of toppings, sauce and cheeses.

This is a great BYOB in a super cute neighborhood. The food was amazing: rich, fresh, and creative. The only reason they didn't get a 5 from me is because the server disappeared when we wanted our check. Other than that, it was great. The hostess let us know where we could pick up some booze (just a block or two from the restaurant) which was awesome. Definitely going back!

The food here is delicious. However, I spent $12 for a sandwich and side and it took over 30 minutes to order and receive my food.  They had 4 kids working the entire place. While eating my food, I overheard several other customers complain about how they are always short staffed. One lady never even received her sandwich-she had to go up and ask multiple times about it, then finally ask for a refund. Good food, but service is definitely lacking

I'm surprised this place is getting a lot of good reviews.  Went for the first time on Sunday night and waited 2 HOURS to get our two deep dish pizzas.  Our table of 6 got there about 8pm, and finally got pizza around 10pm.  The waitress seemed apologetic and so did some other random older lady that came by to check up on us.  But, if your customers are waiting 2 hours for pizza, how about throw em a bone and put some cheese bread or something on the table?  Maybe take a little off the tab?  Nope.  They gave a receipt/coupon for half off a pizza on our next visit.... but guess what, I'm not coming back.   Not unless I'm desperate.  

As for the actual pizza:  it was good.  Being a Chicagoan though, I'd put this somewhere between Giordano's and Connie's, with Giordano's winning.   I'm a Lou Malnati's girl, so nothing beats that of course.  But if we're talking Nashville, save yourself some grief and go to Desano's - better pizza, less wait.  

And btw, what's with the bland decor of this place.  Sucks that this place is supposed to be representative of my hometown.

We cannot day enough great things about our experience at Loa. We sat at the bar and were treated like royalty by Adam (I hope I remembered his name correctly). We tried several fabulous cocktails and met interesting people to talk and pass the time with. I cannot wait to go back!

Paradice Shave Ice was beyond wonderful.  It was the first time we used them for a 13 year old bday party. They were timely, friendly and their product is beyond wonderful.  I so very much recommend them for your next event!!! Their homemade syrups can't be beat and their set up is great looking too.  I could go on and on.

Congratulations to owner Vernon Gibson on making Delaware's top 40 under 40.  Completely well deserved!  This business is great, I'll be contacting them again shortly for another move we probably have coming up next year.

After planning to meet friends for brunch in Indy, we decided on Milktooth. The restaurant is smaller and they have many community tables. We got there just at the right time for a Saturday, 10:30 am. Didn't have to wait for a table. The menu is unique, but for those brunchers who just enjoy simple eggs, toast, and bacon they'll make it. I ordered a Dutch baby with apples and the mocha. The coffee was a good, solid coffee. I was underwhelmed by the Dutch baby. It was good, but not great. Without the apples on top, the 'pancake' itself was very bland. I didn't taste any extra seasoning. I also felt that the $13 for the Dutch baby was a little high. Having made a Dutch baby myself and knowing the ingredients and how easy it is to make, I didn't feel like the $13 was warranted. 
Our service was good and the atmosphere was unique. The place gets very busy around 11, so be sure to plan ahead. It was a neat brunch place and would be a great place to visit when the weather gets nicer as they have outdoor seating. Parking is limited in the parking lot, but there was a lot of free parking on the street.

Such an adorable little gem!  I absolutely loved the intense pink décor and glitter - I felt so girly and fancy being here - no joke!  Ordered wine and cake (the Hummingbird) while celebrating for my sister's birthday, and it did not disappoint!  We had a great time, and I'm already begging to go back!

I found this place while driving to work. It was my first haircut in the city and I'm extremely happy. The woman who cut my hair was "Ta Rey" and not only did she do a great job but she was engaging and happy to have a conversation with someone new. Billie and Shaina (I spelled her name wrong, sorry!) where super friendly and happy to converse with a new client. They are all knowledgeable, friendly, and professional.

Brisket burger was outstanding on a slow Monday night. Kingshighway being closed can't be helping business, so make a special trip.

Next time going to try the lobster beignets and fried chicken.

This review is based on the deli side only. The pastry side is delicious 5 stars.  Great pies and donuts. Ok back to my review.   I got a hoagie today. Yes eat gud makes hoagies now.  The price was reasonable.  $4.99 for a 6 inch hoagie with a small side salad. I got potato salad which was tasty. The roll was stale which wasn't like eat gud since their bread is usually fresh and they were sold out of French baguettes. I got londonport roast beef which was tasty but was lacking in quantity.  They weigh out their meat to only 3oz of meat for 1 meat per sandwich.  They use boars head meat which I prefer but for some reason  the majority of sandwich shops in Hamilton don't carry. So all in all good tasting meat but not enough of it.  Hopefully on my next visit they get rid of their weighing out policy and provide more meat. Also I hope they have a fresher roll selection for hoagies.

Great spot for breakfast in the gulch.  They always have a long wait on the weekends, not sure about during the week.  I got lucky and found 2 spots at the bar and started off with 2 "not so Bloody Mary ", we loved them.  They are made with Clamato juice some other wonderful ingredients.  Then we had the avocado toast and chicken biscuit.  They also have a full menu of wonderful fresh juices. Everything was amazing and a great start for a long day of drinking on broadway.  
Be prepare to wait at most breakfast spots
In the gulch.

Excellent service. Justine was wonderful very knowledgeable about the food. Gabe her preferences which we took her up on most of them. The hot chicken was awesome. Spicy, fried goodness. Bar had good beer and lots of good whiskeys.   Gave us a nice card and signed menus for our anniversary date.  Very cool.  We will be back
Been here countless times and i always leave satisfied...great curry dishes and great apps!!

Ordered a meatball parm hero to go, very good! Bread was amazing and toasted to perfection. Sauce was excellent. Could've used some more cheese. 

They were nice over the phone, had my order ready 15 mins after the call. Very nice when picking up as well. I'll be back!
I live in Bradenton, Fl and let me tell you this place is well worth the short drive over the skyway!!!!  I had the flautas and they were amazing!  I will be coming back often!

I love paradise, but this is the worst location. The place is filthy,the employees clearly don't want to work and take forever all while giving you attitude, they're somehow low or out of every ingredient, the whole salad that I ordered was the size of a half (the casher even had to ask if it was actually a whole). I could go on, but just avoid this place. The Paradise at Hamilton Town Center is so much better it's like they're not even the same chain.

I ordered the taiwan trio, a spring roll, and the peking noodles. The trio came with marinated tofu, pig ears and seaweed. the highlights were definitely the tofu and seaweed. the tofu had a fantastic savory marinade and was nice and firm. the seaweed was cut into ribbons and had an almost pasta like texture with a great salty briny flavor. I like pig ears but these were boring, and had nothing in the way of seasoning at all. I love the way Nan Zhou does pig ears, sliced super thin, marinated in sesame oil and chili, and served with pickled carrot and daikon. the peking noodles were a total home run however. a big bowl of noodles with a ground meat (pork I'm guessing) chili and tofu sauce. the noodles had a decent texture but were a little soft for my liking, however the meat sauce blew me away. it was filled with diced chilis which packed just enough heat to wake up your tastebuds but not destroy which is a good thing because there were so many of them that if they had been hot this dish would have been a nuclear bomb in your mouth. They were just right and cooked so they were still nice and crunchy and the flavor came through brilliantly in the sauce, which had a rich sweet gingery zing. This dish felt like a chinese version of spaghetti with meat sauce. Total comfort food. There was a good amount of sauce left over when I was finished with my noodles and I did not stop till my bowl was clean. The restaurant itself was nice and clean with friendly and fairly attentive staff, and even the americanized dishes looked well prepared and were not over priced. I will be returning soon, seriously I am thinking about those peking noodles right now.

I pretty much tried all the food in the menu. My favorite is the chicken parmigiana and chicken Marsala. This is old school place the waiter still writes the check. The food quality is so great and you can taste the fresh pasta.

I would never use a different company than this for pest control. Definitely the best in SB hands down. Honest , knowledgeable and caring. Tony is a special kind of guy who cares about people and really wants to help you out. Thank you Tony! You are so appreciated!!!!

At one point in time, The Foodery was the ONLY place to go for mixed six-packs of good quality craft beer. The times, however, have changed rapidly. The Foodery has not!

This Foodery still hasn't decided whether it wants to be a bodega or a bottle shop, which in a store that small means that there's not a lot of room to walk around. Once you get more than 5 people in the store, you're literally pressed up against each other as you try to open the fridge doors. If you go before 4pm, you'll have room to shop, but the staff the works during the day don't know shit about beer, including one woman who doesn't drink beer at all. The night time staff is more on the ball.

There are literally dozens of other bottle shops now that have better selection and lower prices (Beer Heaven, Beer Love, the Bottle Shop, Pennsport Beer Boutique, the Beer Peddlers, etc.), so it's not worth it to pay the extra $5-$10 per bottle unless you're really, really lazy. It's especially galling when you consider that they own their own beer distributor, Global, but are still overcharging you.

Really late on this review. Amy was a godsend. I knew practically nothing about buying a home and Amy walked my through every step graciously. And, very importantly, her awareness and logic helped tremendously. Highly recommended!

A LOT OF FOOD!! A bit on the pricey side, but I guess it was worth it for all you get. I will advise when you get the bag, it does have a lot of grease in the bag. I had to take my food out and dab it on the napkin before I ate it. Unfortunately it doesn't come in a matter in which you can take it home unless you want to take home half grease and half food. Good experience but will not go back for a second visit.
Place was great, Tried two menu items and both tasted great. I think I had the Banana fosters french toast. Cant' remember what my wife had.

Tonight we went to the Shlafly brewery for supper. I had a salad called Green and Grain with ranch grilled chicken.  I am very pleased with my choice a full plate nicely arranged and the quianno was a great addition to the salad.
Food is typical for Chinese delivery. The delivery however... Estimated wait time was 45 minutes. I received my order via GrubHub after a remarkably disappointing HOUR AND A HALF WAIT.
