We've lived in this area for 15 years and never made it here for some reason. A Birthday Pak arrived in the mail and offered a discount so we figured we'd finally give it a try.  We arrived during Happy Hour and had 1/2 price drinks and a french fry with cheese app. My wife was more of a fan than I. I thought the fries were a bit on the dark side. We were seated in the main dining room just off the bar area and the live music was still quite loud. We both enjoyed the house chips when most other restaurants that we'd been to offered these they would be poor. These had a nice taste with a dipping sauce that made them even better.  My wife had the crab cakes and liked them. I had the filet with the mashed potatoes and it was done exactly as requested and was a solid piece of meat with no waste and had very good flavor. We could see that other patrons had ordered sandwiches and they looked fairly large. We will plan on coming back and the next time we will stop for lunch.

Under new management and service sucks.  Never got our food.  The waitress did not pay attention to the fact we sat for 45 minutes without our food.  She kept saying it would be right out.  She never checked on it.  We walked out.

Excellent service.  The drinks were delivered very quickly.  The menu was refreshingly different including conch fritters (decent).

We hit the place about 4:45pm and there were excellent drink specials, honored at the table as well as the bar.

We were with the kids and their meals were served quickly.

Just walk up and order then go around and wait for your number. Small menu but some authentic Italian choices. We opted for a small bestia. The spicy sausage went really well with the arugula but overall it was just ok. The bites where I got the sausage, cheese and arugula it was really good but on the small pizza it was not a lot. The bread was pretty tasty and I really liked the oven baked flavors. The whole armature works is very loud but the pizza was pretty good. We sat at their counter and watched them make the pizza.  A cool experience.

We refer to Khyber as our Cheers.  There's always a friendly familiar face to greet us, and they know our names!  The food is consistently great, the servers/bartenders are always knowledgeable of the menu (which there are different daily specials) and how to pair the best libation with your meal.   I am a beer drinker and I'm confident that there are few other establishments in Philly that can rival the Khyber's beer selection. Which changes weekly btw. 

My only challenge is that I always ask my server to surprise me with a beer of their choice so I never remember what I had the time before. The only parameters I request is the abv i.e. 7% or below.  Which often times 80% of the beer selection is well over 7%.  Generally when we go back, the options have changed but are always good. I wouldn't recommend going in looking for a Miller Light Draft.  They're proud beer connoisseurs and they may laugh but suggest a great local, light beer.  

As for food, love the Bayona's duck sandwich.  I've had the actual duck sandwich at Bayona's in New Orleans and Khyber's is a pretty solid rendition.  The fried green tomatoes, crawfish etouffee, honey habanero chicken wings, bbq pulled pork sandwich the boudin and eggs for brunch are a few other favorites.  And for any of you veggie/vegan folks, I was told the chef was vegan for a few years so there are usually non-animal options on the menu.  

As for cons...the only negative feedback I can give is when we walk into the bar or restaurant and it's so damn busy there's no room for us.  I'd like to think we have seats with our names on them and are bummed when reminded that we aren't the only Philly patrons who frequent the Khyber.
HUGE calzones. Amazing salads. Lots of beer options. Plenty of seating. On street parking. Friendly staff. Had the Five-O calzone and it was great. The sauce was sweet and delish!
BEST Fish tacos in the area! I really love this place and come here often.  You cant beat the prices either!

Love, love, love TFA!!  Have shopped at rhis fun store for years and I am thrilled that they have moved to such a convenient new location!! They new store looks great! The staff is always friendly and helpful but they never pester you while you are gawking at all of the crazy treasures of yesteryear .... welcome to the neighborhood TFA!
Excellent food and service at reasonable prices. All four of us had delicious meals and everything was perfect. The shrimp bisque is exceptional. Nice venue and decor.

Recently moved from Chicago to Indy & have been in search for a decent "rib joint"...there aren't many BBQ spots to choose from & the ones I tried (which shall remain nameless) totally missed the mark. I drive up & down Binford everyday as a part of my commute to work & was always curious as to what they had to offer. 
I stopped in last night because I'd been jonesin for some tips. Hardly ever do I see anyone in there & wondered if I had set myself up for disappoinment. Well LO & BEHOLD!!!! I found a WINNER!!! 
Sauce was awesome, meat was smoky & tender, and the price was right! Great job Black Diamond BBQ! You just won me over : )

Very cool eating sushi in the form of a burrito! I had the spicy tuna tartare with white rice, cucumber, and carrot. Everything was fresh and tasty. I'd definitely come back again when I have the extra money since this place is a little on the expensive side.

I needed to simplify this review.  I stayed here for a conference, and here are my observations:
Room:  The shower was like standing in front of the water sprinkler at my high school football field.  It was actually quite painful.
Conference rooms:  Gross!  That's the only way I can accurately describe the feeling of our group towards the conference room we used.  It smelled of cigarettes and musk.  It could have something to do with the fabric on the walls, perhaps they retain odors, but it was just.....gross.
Floor Plan is confusing, and there don't seen to be any windows other than in the rooms and you get turned around very easily.  The lounge seems to be on the other side of the resort than the casino, and the lobby is.....honestly, I don't know where the lobby was.
Check out:  No desk help, and only one self kiosk.

Have been very happy that Lloyd's has finally found their place! We had high hopes for it when it first opened, and finally they are exactly what he had hoped they would become... one of our favorite neighborhood hang out spots. The staff are welcoming and friendly, always at the ready to make recommendations. Perfect spot for drinks or grabbing a bite to eat. Eclectic menu with delicious offerings - deep fried devil eggs, duck sliders, and their cheese board are a few of our favorites. Check them out!

I come to town regularly and pick a hotel close by to eat here. While an odd little spot in a business building, taking the time to find it is worthwhile, whether to enjoy the patio, stroll the vegetable garden out front, or simply to indulge in the delicious food. I would vouch for the crispy Brussels sprouts (share this dish with friends-its huge), the delicate trout, the meaty halibut and the zesty watermelon salad. 

But hands down, the carpaccio is the most memorable dish I have had and was simply outstanding. Each wafer thin slice of beef was buttery and tender, accompanied by earthy mushrooms, tangy sour cream and a nutty biscuit. 

The service is consistently warm and helpful, parking is plentiful and there has always been space at the bar for a single business traveler. I will continue to come back and keep working my way through the menu.

Horrible rip off. If it seems to good to be true it probably is. Charged me for 4 days even though I returned it after 2 days. And charged me for an ENTIRE tank of gas even though I only used 1/4. The workers were nice but they have to be to work for this scam!! Call other rental car companies. Do not use PAYLESS!
Terrific hidden gem in Dunedin. Love the lavender vanilla latte!  Who knew!?!  And the Italian Cookie gelato is off the charts. Worth finding.

The Hemingway Cuban was to die for and the yucca fries with garlic aioli were better than any French fry I've ever had. Can't wait to go back and try the Cuban Salchipapa and Tres Leches cake. Service was good.

The food is fine and the drink menu is better.
Lots of filler in the burritos - rice and beans.

Now...I just saw one of the kitchen workers use the bathroom and walk immediately back to the kitchen without washing his hands. 

Enjoy the E. coli burrito! I hear it'll run right through you!
What an amazing little bar... unique interior with knowledgeable staff... craft cocktails at their finest... in the edge district, so the prices are much more reasonable than further downtown...

Easily the best in Reno.  Jaime is our casino hostess and she rocks.  The sports book is outstanding and takes great care of their customers especially Fannie, Emmett, Scott and Leah.  Rebecca is the best cocktail waitress in the whole place.  Makes our Saturdays off the charts for the GMC.  My wife loves the Spa and we dine at all of the restaurants and the newly revamped deli.  Chinese is our favorite, however the Saturday morning buffet is a must for me.  The gym is state of the art and yes I use it every Saturday when I am there.  Fun, safe, modern nad full of amenities, Reno's best.

This is one of the nicest casinos in Reno with a recent remodel done well.   The only real complaint I have about this place is it is like a maze and you have to do a lot of walking to get anywhere.   If you need a power scooter you will find you have to do a lot of turning and maneuvering to get around.

Another great spot for breakfast!  No frills, quick in and out service, cheap prices.  Very hospitable wait staff, they seem to know several of the regulars and makes you feel at home.  I should've went back for lunch, but sooooo many other places to eat... Go if you can, for any meal.

My family and I enjoyed a nice dinner at Pan D'olive. It was our first visit and we will be back. The food was very good and so was the service. The portions are not large - more than enough for me but my husband could have used a bit more of the delicious chicken breast. One person in our party had the chicken tortellini and it was wonderful. My daughter and I split a wedge salad and I was impressed by the fact that the kitchen staff split it for us so that each of us had a tasty portion nicely presented. Prices are reasonable and that includes the wine.

We went to the Bridgestone Arena for the first time for the Womens Basketball Final Four Championship. We actually loved the experience. People couldn't have been nicer. All the employees were so very helpful, friendly and efficient in the job they were doing.
I realized I had lost my camera about 5 minutes after entering the premises. We immediately went to the information counter to find out what I needed to do. My camera was already sitting on the lost and found shelf! Unbelievablel!There was an  estimated 17,000 people in the arena at that time. Some one found my camera and immediately turned it in. Could hardly believe this happened in barely 10 minutes. Grateful.
I love Nashville. 
UCONN ROCKS.....

Overall a well done place imo. Food has been good both times. Atmosphere is trendy and has all the usual offerings these types of places thrive on. Craft beers and specialty diet standard options etc. 

Basically if you have a millennial with a beard  and love selfies on Instagram this is your heaven on earth.

This is a fantastic little joint in downtown Reno.  Reese (sp), a now local Kiwi bartender is totally awesomesauce.  They have dj's in a little booth overlooking the top floor bar and pool tables and jukebox downstairs.  Have a 'Bees Knees' when you go.  You won't be disappointed.  Also, Reese got a hold of some of the last kegs of a New Zealand beer called Steinlager left i the country.  Get one (or 5) of those also.  Great spot to kick it.

I was so impressed with the Service, the food and the atmosphere. This place is awesome. I recommend The Cider Factory to anyone who wants great service and food.  Made us feel very special. I ordered the New York steak, it was cooked to perfection.  I will definitely return. Mick

Everyone loves it here. I clearly am not everyone. Which is sad, because I had really been wanting to try it, so I made a res for brunch on opentable, and despite planning ahead, it still took 20 min to get us a table. Once seated, our waitress took forever to come over, and I'm pretty sure she never heard the expression "service with a smile" as she had a dour frown the whole time she negligently "served" us. We got egg dishes that were clearly fresh and could have been outstanding, but lacking spice (and love). When we asked for toast, she told us there was no bread. Like the bread that came with our eggs. There was none. So I guess the bread we had was a mirage. Perhaps it was just a bad day. But I'd have to be strongly persuaded to ever go back. NOTE: This is the worst review I've ever given (I generally only Yelp if I love something), so it's not as though I like to pan places--I went here with high hopes--but it disappointed me on all fronts so I'll stick to Silk City or Farmacia for furture brunches.

Just recently stayed at the hotel. 

The staff was rude, inconsiderate and non-caring. The restaurants were always closed for private events and it was not an enjoyable stay. 

Not Impressed at all!
I had the tuna sandwich seared! Fabulous sandwich to say the least. Friendly staff and very clean cafe. I would recommend this place for lunch!!
Enjoyed the service...cute and helpful wait staff. The food was very good...ordered mostly apps. Glad we dropped in...would come back.

Love this place. A go-to favorite of ours. Very intimate so get there early on weekends since they don't take reservations. 

Food is delicious and quite reasonably priced. Love the Greek salad (no greens) and citrus avocado salad to start off. Spinach pie is great. The escarole pasta is a garlic lover's dream. Shrimp PilPil is usually a favorite of people. Grilled veggies, beets, etc all great sides for your meal. 
They always have good fish specials to check out. 
Never get tired of this place and we're never disappointed.
Have been there countless times. Love their beer and the atmosphere, but have never gotten good service. Not a single time. Not even decent service, pretty rude mostly.

Minima is incredible. The owners, Eugenie and Michael take the time to educate you about all of their furniture, and everything they sell is really unique and special. 

If James Bond lived in Philadelphia, he would definitely shop here.

Found it on their website, wrote $3 off for reward card holder, nothing mentioned it's only for gold & above members, coz the list separated the gold & above members promotions from the others, so when I got here, there was no discount for normal members, tried to make it clear, just no explain to me. It's ok for until now, coz just $6 diff. Later, waiters were unfriendly, always made angry face, I can understand how busy they were, but how hard to make a smiley face? Went to lot of buffet, didn't feel like here. For this price, I rather wanna go to Flavors, which is next door, in SL.

This place used to be great. I really liked the instructors and they taught great classes. Now the best instructors have moved on. 

Plus, classes get cancelled in the middle of the day. 2 of the last 3 that I've tried to go to have been cancelled. I showed up and no teacher was there. 

I'm going to use up my punch pass and find somewhere else

Sweet server good food.  The oysters were a bit over cooked but yummy didn't need a drop of butter to enjoy. The crab cakes were heavy on crab light on filler.  We had both buffaloes  and coconut shrimp they were big but not tough.  The fried fish sandwich was enormous. All in all good seafood dinner. Slightly pricey considering the atmosphere but yummy.

I've heard so many good things about Termini Bros Bakery.    

I arrived at the perfect time so I was able to take my time and choose the perfect dessert.

Decided to go with a mini carrot cake ($5).  The staff was friendly and even gave me a fork and napkin to go..

The cake was fresh and perfect to split with hubby.

Will I be back? Yup!  Can't wait to try something else.

Hidden in a charming Reno neighborhood, the Coffeebar is a must try if you enjoy a nice cup of coffee. The coffee menu is simple, yet display a variety of options for everyone.  They have a full kitchen so all the food and pastries are freshly served. I enjoy drinking an iced Americano with a splash of cream. Their lemon bar is by far the best I've ever had.

Allegro is falling off. I haven't been to this place in a year, and last weekend I was reminded by why. The pizza was not good to me. It was just blah. Went to go and wash my hands and the bathroom was filthy. I mean filthy. We decided to sit outside, hoping we'd get away from the chatter, but no. 

Two college kids followed us to these other tables and were busy running their mouths about people walking about and obviously going to parties. I know that we were outside but I don't want to hear your conversation. Annoying. Plus the tables hadn't been cleaned in like all day. 

I will not be returning for a long time.

Oh, yeah, I DID not like the pizza.

Our family of 6 had a great dinner here the other night.  so good in fact that we asked for the head chef to come to our table, so we could thank him personally.  The wine selection was good, we ordered Pino - new zeland while the server brought out fresh bread with two types of oils that are made fresh.  3 of the folks at our table ordered the burger- they said it wad very good....but the 3 other dishes were amazing.  I had the New York strip- grilled to perfection - 10oz.  Another dish was the lamb wellington , and the 3rd was the lamb stroganoff - WOW!!   serverd over the noodes and on the bone. This was truely the best lamb and stroganoff combinatoin I've ever tasted.  The entire table tried it, and agreed.   All food is fresh and they purhcase from farms they know.
a+

Terrible vibe. There was no hostess for about 5 minutes. Our waiter was definitely on some anxiety-inducing drugs. There was no drink menu despite this being supposedly known for its nectar margaritas. We weren't offered water while we waited for a meal. The one alcoholic drink we did get was sugary sweet despite asking for less sweet. The kombucha was bad. Our appetizer didn't come in the first few minutes and the whole place felt so anxious and uncomfortable that we dropped a $20 on the table and left.

I didn't become a regular here until recently, but I've definitely paid attention to the gripes of Yelp and the neighborhood message board.  I can't say what they were like when they first opened, but they have a fantastic selection of stuff for what I'm looking for right now.  I work at a bank up the street, and the entire branch has gone on a lunch diet.  Every day they give me money, I walk down, browse, and return with armfuls of semi-healthy and totally satisfying goodies.  Moz-avocado sandwich... hummus and pita chips... Greek yogurt... trail mixes... random pretzel selection... stuff that is delicious enough to keep us from caving in and ordering pizza or Chinese.  Oh, and chapstick and cigarettes.  The employees are all so friendly too.  I adore this place.

Had dinner here on a gorgeous night -- we had to take advantage of the weather and sit outside. We were told it would be a 45 minute wait for a table, so we had a few drinks at the bar. $7 cocktails? This New Yorker needs to travel -- who am I kidding? -- anywhere to get her affordable liquor fix! I ordered the mint julep but really didn't like it... the bartender swapped it out for the strawberry sangria for FREE! Spreading the love in Philly :) The sangria was MUCH tastier... I had been craving mussels all day and so was thrilled to see them on the dinner menu. Big mistake - these mussels were in a hefeweizen broth. The flavor was awful. The color of the broth was murky and make me frightened to dip my bread. And once I mustered up the courage, it didn't even taste good! Soooo very disappointing meal. My friends were perfectly satisfied with their own selections, so I'm just going to chalk it up to poor selection on my part. But if the word "pub" is in the name of your restaurant, shouldn't you do a good job with mussels? Three stars for the cheap and tasty alcohol :)

If I could give it a zero star I would. Wish I could also tell you how the food was. But after sitting at TWO tables and getting no service for 20 minutes, we had to leave. Shitty people. Shitty service.

WOOT WOOT 
This place rocks!!
You can sit outside and enjoy a coffee, tea, or any beverage of choice.
They also have fresh pastries and breakfast sandwiches made daily. 
The best chai tea latte I have ever had. The sausage egg and chees on an English muffin is delicious as well. 
GO! you wont be disappointed

cheers,

Overall: Grassfed Missouri raised cow with homemade patties! Can you ask for more?

Ambience: This place is located in a busy corner of downtown STL. Parking is street only, just like most places in downtown. When you come inside, you'll notice, this restaurant is pretty big. You almost never need a reservation but it is good to have one for larger parties. The crowd is here everything from families to college friends to tourists.

Food: The place offers Missouri raised grass fed beef. So you know you're getting good stuff. If you're not into beef, their chicken burgers are also really good. I will say though their vegetarian patties aren't as flavorful. I have been to very few burger places that can do a good veggie patty. After all, this is a burger joint. We hope you didn't come here for veggie patty. We asked for ketchup and they had a house made version. I'll say, I'm not a fan of it. It tastes like puree than ketchup. The sauces on burgers could use some inspiration. They have the basics such as siracha, mayo, mustard, bbq... But if you really want to set your burger apart, step up your game on the sauce!

Drinks: They have a pretty nice bar with TVs, if you're looking for a place to eat by yourself. With that said their spiked shakes are pretty awesome. If you haven't, you should try their normal shakes and ice cream too!

Service: It was pretty busy when we came here, yet the service was fast. Our server cared for what we wanted and checked up on us a few times.

Price: $12-$14 for a burger with no sides is alright. You could throw fries with it and charge extra for other sides such as sweet potato fries or onion rings. Still can't complain.
Go for the buffalo cauliflower! What better combination could you ask for?! The drinks also are delicious. The space is large and draws a mix after work - a great place for happy hour.

I was trying to put my finger on what  type of place this is and came up with this: JD's is a worn out older local's bar.  They have their place in the Indian Beach area just not for food.  There's the 65+ group dancing on the back deck with 60s music and cheap drinks, fine.  But if you are coming here for food best to spend your bucks elsewhere.   I winced when one of our party ordered steak, either his knife was to old and dull or the meat like rawhide.  Forget the fried food, its bland and tasteless unless its coated in tarter sauce.  Either the severs were new and didn't know that hamburger Wednesdays ended last week or with attitude.  Skip this one for food, and bring the ear plugs.

A somewhat strange assortment of seating choices greet you at the door.
As you seem to walk right from the street to the dining area.   Staff is super friendly, service is quick and responsive.   The larger sushi platters looked more like art then dinner.   Pho was very good too.   We'll certainly return

Jee Whizz! The steak and cheese was AWSOME. Now I must say this was my first. I do a lot of traveling and hear about how awesome an authentic Philly cheese steak sandwich is. When I asked some locals about where to get a good cheese steak they mentioned a couple of places, when one of the individuals said its all about the cheese and meat you need to go to Armadore pizza. 

Once I sank my teeth into it,  I must say the flavor was superb. The aroma emitting from the sack while driving back to hotel was mind blowing & mouth watering. Even in the elevator up to my room, people were commenting how good it smelled. Asking where did I get it from. 

The staff was super, very helpful. As this was my first cheese steak. the guy taking the order asks what do you want on it. Like I would know after all this was my first. He asked you like onion etc. Anyway he was polite helpful and sandwich was AWSOME, 

The fries were tasty. I was instructed to request the extra crispy fries. again this was new to me.  i guess i will now order my fries extra crispy. There were  a chit load of them in the bag.

Super friendly staff, fast service and GREAT food. I got the goat stew which was flavorful, as well as a big meal. My coworkers got the chicken mofongo and pork ribs, which were also delicious, and the desserts were also phenomenal - we got the flan and tres leches cake. Would definitely recommend. I didn't know it was BYOB going in, or else I would have brought something.

MUST MUST visit when in NOLA. I came here because of great reviews and it definitely lived up to the hype and even surpassed my expectations.

The banana foster French toast was literally heaven on earth. Everything about this dish is perfection. 

Shrimp and grits. Wow also divine. The shrimp was fresh and so perfectly seasoned. I don't even like grits.

Perfect combination of sweet and savory dishes. I could not get enough of both and really have considered booking a ticket just to come back here. Will definitely be back when I visit NOLA again!!

This is by far my favorite shrimp po-boy around town. I haven't ventured into the hot case yet but a lot of the regulars go for it. The ladies running the place are super sweet. Good neighborhood joint.

The tasting menu at Vetri was an experience I will never forget. Every plate that was put in front of me was executed perfectly and was delicious. The fresh tortellini with a generous shaving of white truffles was borderline sexual. Spinach gnocchi with brown butter, Russian salad, smoked Canada goose stuffed endive, sweet onion crepe w/ truffle fondue, boar ragu, apple fed lamb, and pistachio flan were all memorably awesome.

Overall, it was a four and a half hour dining experience that was worth every penny. 

Be sure to get a reservation, go hungry, and buckle up for the meal of your life.

I love this place. Arrived tonight to be expertly guided through the menu (oyster selection) by our fantastic server. Had an incredible rye spiced Manhattan. Okay, maybe 3. 

Fried chicken sandwich new to the menu and fantastic. Expertly fried, juicy and flavored with buttermilk. Loved it. Worth the diversion from our usual burger. Which is the city's best. 

Food is excellent. Drinks are excellent. Service is excellent.

This is supposed to be the In-N-Out of the Midwest, meh...
I think I was just expecting a lot more since In-N-Out is what I had always heard as the comparison, but that doesn't even come close to true. As a Bi-Coastal resident of both Cali and Indy I am privileged to eaten at both places many times for many years, and Five guys, although a step up from McDonalds/Wendy's, is nothing more than just an average fast food burger joint. The fries are not anything worth writing home about, and the peanuts are kinda weird. I have been to this location many times and I have always had great service (that's what the 3 stars are for), and the food is fine, it just ain't no In-N-Out. But this is a good location for sure, they are clean, friendly, and fast!

I went there with a group of people and everyone enjoyed their meal.  The service was friendly and the décor is festive.  If you like Cajun/creole food, I think you should give Acadia a try.  You'll love it.

Love this place!  The service is outstanding , they prepare the guac right in front of you so you know it's fresh, feels like authentic Mexican food. The decor is beautiful, and the ambiance... They even gave us this Mexican voodoo dolls (you put them under your pillow me all your worries will be gone ) while I have yet to confirm the Mexican doll works, I have Mexican family and they would approve of this  restaurant ... I certainly do. Thank you!
The cheese steak was delicious. I love the crispy crunch of the bread, then it was soft on the inside.

Best regular pizza I've had in the local area. Overall, it's alright. People love their wings, I personally think their wings are decent. Their  options for both alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, however, far exceed any other establishment for miles.
Amazing hike an view of the sunset. So peaceful, great place to mediate. A must see.
I love this Wawa! It's always clean, and everybody is no nice (especially Rich from the deli).

If you like burgers this place is pretty good. I had high expectations for the burger, though, and was left without any real wow factor. The truffle fries were really good, so I would recommend those. The seating is also family style, so be prepared to get cozy with your neighbors!

Check my reviews. Usually don't do bad ones but this place sucks. Don't spend $25 for a sandwich, small wine and terrible service. 

Atrium Lounge and their grumpy employees make for an awful way to finish your time in New Orleans. Whatever mood you were in when you get here, they'll do their best to ruin it. 

Wish I could put less than 1 star cuz they don't even deserve that much. 

Sadly the entire airport isn't much better. Someone just walked by and told his friend this is by far the worst airport. Gotta say, it's hard to argue against that assessment. 

Awful. Hate that my flight is delayed 2 hrs. Get me out of here!!!

Five thousand stars!!! We are so impressed with this complex, and especially the staff- specifically Juliette. What a wonderful, warm, and professional individual. She made us feel so welcome and was so informative- no surprises! The tour was actually enjoyable. We felt absolutely no pressure. The grounds are the best I've seen and the amenities alone are well worth the $$. This place is the gold standard from value to property to staff. What a wonderful breath of fresh air.

We had a washer and dryer that we needed moved to the second floor of our trinity after the delivery company refused. Sultans of Schlep surveyed the situation, considered all possibilities, and ended up being able to go directly up the stairs with it. Quick, clean and friendly job. After moving out our old washer and dryer, they even alerted us that we we need some electrical work done to get our new units hooked up.

Definately a hole in the wall bar in south Tampa, a nice change up from the yuppie bars down the street. Bartender makes you get pitcher from the freezer. Great place to get a couple pitchers in you before you brave the collared shirts in soho

As a tower resident I've always been a big fan of the neighborhood and all that Tower has to offer with fun restaurants, the piazza and unique shops. However, I'll try not be to biased with my opinion of this place.  

Obviously, this club was meant to entice the hip, young, affluent clientele of Philadelphia but having this club in NoLibs (where you are literally blocks from Girard Ave) was not the smartest idea.  I can't be sure the success of this place but a source tells me that it is having issues filling up their membership.  It's not surprising when you are charging $1000 for only using this space for 3 months out of the year. Last time I checked, I thought we were still in a down economy especially with gas prices still so high. The $1000 just gets you into the club; that doesn't mean that the cabanas are included in that price.  That is still an additional cost of some odd hundred dollars.

There is a restaurant within the same building which looks nice but I have not had the opportunity to try the food and taste of food better be good because you have a few staple places in this neighborhood such as PYT and Dos Segundos and Standard Tap that if the food isn't good it won't do well (ie Swift Half, Vino)

I know that as a Tower resident I have access to the club till June 15 but during the weekdays. I was under the assumption that Memorial Day was a weekday but they denied me access.  How are you supposed to gain more clientele when you deny them access?  Not so epic fail, but fail nonetheless.

I'm not a big IHOP fan, however, we did stop in and eat to get the 2 for $10. You can't beat two omelets (certain ones) with two sides for $10. 
Service was good as he kept our drinks filled and met all our needs (and then some so my man said - from the way the server kept looking at me and making sure my needs were met, LOL)
Atmosphere was nice, thank goodness it wasn't crowded. 

All in all, it was a nice experience.

I've been to many boba houses all over the country and all over the world. This does not do true boba any justice. Authentic Taiwanese boba is the way to go. The drinks were okay. We ordered 6 , some weren't that great. The cleanliness wasn't the best. From a far it looks decent. However, as I was observing I noticed a lot of downsides. I didn't like it, compared to all of the other places that I've been to.
Awesome neighborhood brewery.  All of there beers are great. They do need to improve on the appetizers they offer.  Just not much to choose from.  Hopefully they will offer lunch or dinner options.

My wife and I came in shortly after the new ownership took over and while I was pleased at how much cleaner it looked, felt, and smelled... I was really bummed that they took out half the taps and made that remaining selection pretty lame. It didn't help that the one beer I actually wanted they were out of. They also increased the prices of the 'schooner' fills (to the point where it wasn't even a tiny bit of a deal) and reduced the options of what you could put in them. Service was fairly slow, but not as slow as many of these other reviews have indicated.

I'm a beer-lover who strives to always try different things, so a diverse and changing selection is essential to me. I was already really taken aback by the significant reduction in choices, but then to rename the place as a Tap Room? What a slap in the face.

With HopCat across the street, The Pint Room just a hop over in Carmel, and TwentyTap a few blocks south in SoBro, I have literally no reason to ever go back. Additionally, The Sinking Ship only has 8 taps, but they are expertly managed and always have great things. Flat Water has a similarly small number of taps, but their food is anything but basic bar food.

I'm not really sure who the Village Tap Room is trying to appeal to, despite their claimed demographic of "an older crowd."

Our family of four went on a Groupon as we all were pleasantly surprised.  Their chicken tikka and basmati rice was so fragrant and delicious.  The waitress was unfriendly and very slow.  We had to ask her for every small thing like water, more water, the check etc.  There was only one other family in a booth while we were there.  It would be nice if she smiled and was more attentive but that just was not the case or I'd give it five stars.

We stayed at the Holiday Inn right next to North 30th and decided to head there for dinner after a long day at Busch Gardens.  Great sports bar, very clean, lots of TVs showing all different sporting events.  Staff was very friendly and we had nice quick service.  Food was good and we were all very happy.We hung around for a bit after finishing our meal and had a few drinks, which were well made and much needed after dealing with our kids at the theme park all day!!! We had our own liquor in our hotel room , however we enjoyed the setting here and did not want to go back to our room just yet, so it was nice to sit and enjoy our drinks without feeling rushed to leave. Will definitely eat here again the next time we are in Tampa.

A friend and I frequent the Take-Out area often during the week! The service, which is always Judy, is fantastic! She has a great personality and is always quick to take our order and get our lunch out to us.  We never try anything other than the pizza which we love!

I had the pleasure of dining at Home Wine Kitchen twice in one week! The first being brunch with Erin and Tim G, and the second being a ladies night out with Stephanie S and other Twitter friends who I begged to let me join. Ha! 

First, the brunch experience. Make reservations. We didn't because it was a spur of the moment decision, and so we sat at the high tops, which aren't so bad if you're tall, but for someone short whose legs don't touch the floor it's not that comfy. Lesson learned for next time. I had a mimosa, which was refreshing, though maybe a little tart for my taste. Then I had the crepes. OMG. They were unbelievable. The best I've ever had, hands down. Stuffed with marscapone and covered in fresh fruit (raspberries, strawberries and cherries), they were really filling. I couldn't finish them. Perfect amount of sweetness but not over the top. They had several vegetarian options for brunch. The price was good, befitting of the portion and quality of ingredients. I will definitely be back for this.

For dinner, we made reservations so no problem there. They can accommodate groups, even though they are small (take note, Farmhaus!!). We had 6 people and there was another group of 7-8 when we were there too.

The menu changes every week, so be sure to check it out if you have dietary restrictions. We made reservations in advance and with me being vegetarian and another dining partner being vegan, we had no problem. Lots of veggies and they can also do some things without meat if you ask.

I ordered the roasted veggie salad first. It was brussels sprouts and something else that I didn't know what it was, but was good, in an herbed butter sauce, served warm. YUM! I only wish it had more brussels sprouts - LOVE them! Then I ordered polenta with vegetables for my entree. Again, yummy! The polenta was the perfect consistency and tasted great with the veggies (asparagus, summer squash, zucchini) and was drizzled with this absolutely delicious red pepper saffron sauce that I wanted to lick off of my plate. My only complaint about the dish was that it was really small for $18.

We had two bottles of wine between the group. I am a wine idiot so I can't say much about them, though one thing that makes it unique is that no matter which wine you order, it's $8 a glass and $30 a bottle. Definitely a good deal for the bottle if you have enough people or want to get a buzz!

Wait staff was very efficient both time and nice too, and Josh, one of the owners, was very visible, which I like. Cassy, the chef, came out during dinner and talked to several tables. I like the small, family type atmosphere, and seeing the chef and owner involved and caring for their patrons is a huge plus in my book.

Both times, it was really hot. I mentioned this to Josh, the owner, and he said that they have had the AC people come out but it's working fine. Must just be the space. 

I'll be back for sure, though on a cooler day!
Great service and friendly staff. Highly mediocre food. Calamari undercooked and doughy. Spaghetti bolognese tasted like chef boyardi world there. needs improvement

Right now I am a disappointed with Swill. My BNI group meets there every Tuesday morning and we try to give them as much business as we can. I met with a client after my meeting and needed to use their free wireless service for a presentation. I went up and asked the cashier what the passcode was and she said "Ill give it to you if you buy a drink." I replied back that I was in the middle of a meeting and would be getting a drink and snack a little later. She again stated that I should buy something now and then I could have the passcode. I was blown away! I had to cut the meeting short because I couldn't get on to the internet and walked out. Luckily the client was understanding. I sent an email to the owner and after a month still haven't heard anything. I'm surprised. I do my best to support the local businesses of Reno but this incident has really got me thinking if Starbucks is the way to go with their no hassle free wireless...

I really enjoy eating here every time that I come. The food is always good, the quality and freshness consistent. The people are hit or miss when it comes to friendliness, but they are prompt and efficient. 

This particular visit, my fiancé and I ordered labneh and kibbeh for an appetizer. For our meals, he ordered the kufta kabob plate with hummus and salad and I ordered the chicken shwarma plate with rice and hummus. The amounts of food you get here are always huge and I never leave without taking home leftovers. Everything was delicious, especially the kibbeh and the meats. My favorite thing on the menu, and what I usually get, is the Meat and Tomato Stew, with rice and hummus. I look forward to my next visit!
We ordered one of everything. Chicken and waffles won! The gravy is ridiculously awesome!

We wanted to like the Flamenkuchen, but just didn't.  Those big pieces of ham/bacon with all that fat was just too much.  And we encountered the most arrogant server, Kenneth, that we have ever had.  After the first course, we decided to cut our loss and not stay for anything else.  We expected so much more from a Besh restaurant.

I've been a couple of times and I had been so excited to try it before they opened. The food is really good with decent prices. TRY THE APPLE LANDSLIDE, it is fantastic! My only complaint was I asked for no tomatoes on my sandwich, was told there was no tomatoes on my sandwich and when I got home, guess what, there was tomatoes on my sandwich. It happens.
Angel  provided excellent service. She made my first visit special. The food and bear were excellent. Deducted one star because of the cost. Prices are a bit "high"

This place could be seriously addictive and it's more expensive than Starbucks. After seeing a few Yelp buddies check in I bookmarked this place as a must try next visit. 

I did not know what to order and I had no idea that placing an order and receiving the order would take as long as it did, but it was worth the wait. 

If you are a fan of the the Berry Chantilly Cake at Whole Foods or any other store in the area, the Chantilly cake snoball is a must try! The concept of cheesecake, fresh strawberries, fresh blueberries AND condensed milk in a snoball is simply ingenious. It was very rich but absolutely wonderful. 

March 2016----My new favorite is the Strawberry Lemonade. It is a lemonade sno-ball with a lots of freshly cut strawberries throughout.  

Nicely done.

Tasty, tasty, tasty! 

For a fast food option, they're relatively healthy. The pulled pork was delicious and moist. The black beans were delightful, but the salad was over dressed. I'll come back when I get the chance, since it's on the way to work, but now I know it's a great choice for protien.
Best Cuban food I've had, hands down. They even said the man who prepared it was new, but you'd never tell! Perfect.

Review is for the bar only, have not had the food yet.  We love the Fox and Hound!  It is a great place to stop for a relaxing evening or to have a drink after dinner or going out.  Nathan is awesome and everyone was having a great time. Ask him to do a card trick for you.

Visited three times in the past few months and every experience has been great and a lot of fun.  There seems to always be a lively and fun crowd, the employees enjoy working there and make it a great experience.  They have a nice selection of drinks and beers.

It is a terrific place to relax and enjoy the atmosphere. We will be back soon!

We found Desire four years ago and enjoyed it. We have returned every year on our visits. However this time it was disappointing. We were seated immediately on Friday night at 7:30pm. The Char-Oysters, my husband looks forward to all year, were half the size they normally are and he was extremely disappointed. He felt he paid $19 for just some butter and garlic. Also the Char-oysters arrived 10 minutes later than everyone else's meal. 
The Seafood platter $32 was small in quantity. 
The catfish was lacking in flavor. The service was fair at best. 

We will look for a new favorite in the area.
Yum !!!!! The scones are to die for and the Mexico coffee is delicious !! Th staff is awesome and so willing to share the knowledge with you ...

Another great dinner.  My wife had the salmon entree --- DELICIOUS.  Really good served over a bed of sauted garlic spinach.  I had the traditional lamb gyro.  The presentation was a little different than I am used to but was fantastic. Different in that usually, I can fold these and eat them kind of like a fajita or taco.  This just had too much stuff on it to do that.  Wonderful mix of flavors and eating with a fork and knife was just fine. :-)

We shared a baklava for dessert and it was excellent.  Presentation is very nice with some sliced strawberry, toasted walnuts, whipped cream and an orange slice.  The additional flavors enhanced the baklava and was a nice touch.

Went here early afternoon on a Sunday and it was packed, which was not surprising for a place I've heard good things about. Waited a little bit, which was fine, then was seated and got our drinks promptly. I'm not a big pancake fan so I got one of the omelettes, with a side of bacon. The bacon was $5 but well worth it, and the omelette was around $11 but was huge. Overall good flavor and fresh ingredients. A little more than what I wanted to pay but a good Sunday brunch nonetheless.

This is my home away from home. I have business meetings in Boise 2-3 times a month and travel with my family often. The staff is great here and they always treat my my wife and son with courtesy and respect. Seriously, from the mainetenance guy, all the way up to the manager on shift. I am not sure if all Hampton Inns are this good, but I always book here when I know I will be in Boise. Free breakfast is a bonus as well. Pool water is a little cold, but the hot tub works great!

I know the area really well, but they even teach me a thing or two when I need a good recomendation for a business or service. 

Most importantly, they are sincerely helpful, not patronizing. They deal with many business travelers and families alike, so they really do cater to you without coming off as fake.

Top shelf experience, for food especially but also atmosphere. Raw oysters,  crab meat au gratin, and rabbit & liver pate (all with  exquisite crostini) made superb appetizers. At our table were served delicious and perfectly cooked mussels, a magnificent medium rare ribeye (and was glad to have taken the waiter's suggestion to choose only the pat of butter for the topping; this was an excellent cut and well cooked), and well received shrimp and grits. The cocktails, sides, and wine were up to the task as well.

Great atmosphere and style. Ladies running the cafe are delightful. I live a couple blocks away, and the location is convenient for conventioneers and warehouse district residents. 

The menu offers creative and healthful options including juices and smoothies. My egg white turkey & veggie omelet was good. The café breakfast is a familiar and solid breakfast. 

I used to prefer the Community Coffee from the café across the hall from Two Chicks, but now the coffee served at Two Chicks - which also is a local brew- is my fav.

If you want one on one therapy with therapists who really want you to succeed then come here!! I know some other therapy places write a program and allow you to be independent once you're familiar with the exercises and will periodically check on you but not here. I wish I could have stayed longer but I it wasn't necessary

We are local and try to eat at local places regularly on the weekends. This post is more for the owners than for patrons because nowadays service is more the exception than the rule at most restaurants.  My son and I had breakfast here on a Saturday morning and the food was your standard run of the mill food; nothing exceptional, but if you like bacon, eggs, biscuits and gravy then it's ok. Now the coffee was absolutely nothing to write home about. During our time there two of the girls were 15 feet from us at the bar talking away and we're completely oblivious to the fact that we were signalling for attention to order. Once we finally got our order in I forgot to add the blueberries to the kids plate and finally got one of the girls attention to add them. When we got the bill I noticed the blueberries were more expensive than were indicated on the kids menu and when I asked about it one of the oblivious ones stated that I ordered them as a side vice with the kids meal. You can see where this is going, and she didn't budge to fix the price.  So, if you are good going to a place where the food is just ok and the coffee is not and you have to deal with substandard to nonservice then this is your place!

By far the best value in Philly (in my opinion).  The burgers are as good as it gets. The fries are always perfect. And you have all the Scotch and Whiskey you can handle. Oh yeah, the staff is always super friendly.

Solid, if not mind-blowing barbecue, but there are some sleepers on this menu. The cornbread is really, really good, as are the potato salad and coleslaw. I also really like their wings. They're just spicy enough.

As for things not taste bud-related, I think they could've figured out a better way to take food orders. If it's crowded, you'll be in line for a while. On a nice day, the garage doors are open, and I think that'd make it a great place for beer and barbecue after work.

Nashville isn't in short supply for good barbecue places, but the location of Edley's is a huge plus when compared to getting better barbecue at Jack's on Trinity or going all the way to Nolensville.

This is my new favorite go to with my friends! They have a wide variety of food choices to choose from besides just pizza, but if you love pizza you're set! I usually start off with spinach and artichoke dip, and it's probably some of the best I've ever had. It's perfectly spicy and just amazing. I could go there just for the dip! They have a huge selection of pizzas and thus far I haven't had the same one twice . I haven't been disappointed yet and can't wait to go back to find something new to try. I recommend trying here at least once and then you'll be hooked!
Service average. Food average. Atmosphere average. Meh describes my whole experience.

This location is compete trash! I have given  them MORE chances then they deserve! EVERY time I go there, they mess up my order, forget my order. And if you need a stir stick or napkin good luck. Because once they give you for drink they ignore you
The burger with sweet potato fries are the best in town and the lattes are always picture worthy!!!
Beer selection...great. View...wonderful. Shrimp po' boy...huge and tasty! Can't really find fault with anything. Need to come back at sunset.

I shop Target whenever possible for toiletry, household and even food items. I love the bright clean layout of the store and most items are easy to find. I also think it is great that they feature products from small businesses as a way to help the little guy out-Go Tarjay!

 On my last visit with my mom she was unable to find the bath powder. Four associates attempted to help us but in the end we left without it and my mom muttering the awful W word (((shudder))). You would think employees would be able to punch a product into an electronic inventory and see exactly where it should be; instead the emps scoured the shelves and walked the aisles. While the system fails I give service an A. 

PS. IF someone finds out where they are hiding the bath powder let me know (I will score major mom points!!). thanks :)

Another local coffee shop, hooray! Since moving downtown about a year ago, I've been on a mission to try all of the small business coffee shops that Indy has to offer. I had heard good things about Henry's on Yelp and was on leisurely walk one Saturday morning and thought I would pop in for a latte. Super friendly staff, in fact I had an espresso connection with my barista. We bonded over our middles names and and it was quite spectacular. I ordered a medium latte without any syrup, it's easier to detect the roast and intensity of the bean this way. The cafe has a casual laid back feel with a slew of regulars. I didn't try anything on the menu besides the coffee, but they do have options if you're feeling peckish. Free wifi and outgoing staff with a solid coffee menu to delight the senses.

p.s. they have outdoor seating with a great view

First time here, got bagelicious sandwich. Bagel was delicious and filling! Drink was a small iced coffee, and boy is it strong and TASTY. Really pleased with my experience here. There's a lovely seating area in the back of the shop. Don't be fooled that it looks small from the front, go in and check out their large menu of items. Monica was behind the counter and she was so sweet. I will be back!

Best place in town on Saturday mornings for freshest and best produce and flowers, specialty items and people watching. As you would expect, the organic stuff is more costly than your local chain supermarket. That said, please be sure to ask whether the produce is pesticide free because organic here does not always mean free of pesticides (ie. grapes all are doused with sulfides and not a problem if done early in the growth cycle). Street musicians, artisans and colorful locals people the place. Some great food samples are often available as well. Try different farmer's wares, and return often to your favorite stalls on Saturdays. Other days also have the market in different locations, but the festive Saturday is my fav!
Service was good. But food way too salty! Pork porterhouse was over cooked. Mashed potatoes were the worst I ever had! Like a brownish spackle. Too salty!

I had been to Pagoda a few times with only great things to say about the food (particularly the cold sesame noodle and lo mein). I hadn't been there in over a year and thought I'd check some recent reviews to see how how they are doing...wow was I sad to read that the place has utterly went downhill. I didn't want to believe that so we went for the lunch time special to give it another go. 

Well folks...the reviews don't lie. 

Very sad in there now - we were the only people in there on a Friday during lunch. The walls inside are falling apart and the seating was duct taped in places. Eek! The cold sesame noodle was dry with no sesame in sight, tasted a few days old and was very unappetizing looking. I thought I saw mold on a noodle but I cant confirm if it was or not - either way I didnt eat it. The entrees came out hot but nothing to write home about - they changed their noodles for the lo mein which was one of the reasons we go there. The sauces were flavorless. Thank god we got the cheaper lunch special because no way in hell does this place deserve to charge regular menu prices for sub par food. We won't be coming back to our once favorite lunch spot anymore and that makes me sad!
Excelente servicio y comida; cachapas, tequeños, arepas. Finalmente un restaurant Venezolano en Edmonton. Muchos éxitos!

This may seem like a standard American burger joint, but they actually have taken pains to create a thoughtful and surprising menu. 

There are options ranging from middle eastern to Mediterranean to Indian to new American and I had a sampling of them all. Everything had a distinct flavor profile, regardless of whether I liked it, and the burger was one of the best I've had in Nashville. Oh, and for dessert you can roast your own marshmallows at the table. 

Service wasn't the greatest, but not terrible as other reviews have noted and overall this is a spot I'd recommend.

I had a veggie burger with tempeh and it blew my mind. Though the patty wasn't anything to write home about the tempeh was delicious. The menu was great (not a thing on there I wouldn't order) and I look forward to going back to try everything on it. My only complaints are that it's tough to find a spot to sit and there's no bathroom to wash your hands.

Best meal we had in NOLA. Just go with no preconceptions and you should have a fab experience. Order what they're most famous for; it's for a reason. Only dropped a star because the shrimp n grits was not equal to my bananas fosters (but only by a smidge). All in all, a great dining experience; they run the cafe like pros and I would definitely go again and really recommend it.
Great doctors and CNP's .  This is the best I have seen in  a while.   No complaints except getting scripts refiled.  It take at least a week.

We came for breakfast and everything was excellent. They even made my son a special Mickey Mouse pancake which was great. The breakfast meats were especially delicious. I would have given them 5 stars but the service was a bit slow and they didn't seem that busy. I will definitely be going back soon!

This is my new favorite hideaway in the Grove....well not exactly new, but I am learning to adore and appreciate this fine little place more and more.  The best part about this place is that it caters to cyclists aka bikers of the human powered variety.  

The venue is sweet....I have always been a fan since it was previously the Church Key and then Bar 5.  The Handle Bar gave this venue an ambiance overhaul by adding colorful murals and old school bikes to the mix.  They have a great selection of liquor and beer and feature local craft breweries on tap - Civil Life, Perennial, Urban Chestnut, Four Hands, etc.  They also rotate their selections somewhat frequently, which is nice.  Happy Hour offers the ability to sample a delicious pint at very little cost.

I love the layout, the food, the beer, the staff, and the ambiance of the Handle Bar.  Don't assume that this is a hipster headquarters....the crowd that gather here is extremely eclectic and can vary depending on the time of day and whatever happens to be going on at the HB that evening.  They often feature crazy live music and DJs as well as interesting events that cater to everyone - not just cyclists.  They just recently expanded their hours to include Sundays and earlier hours during the week for lunch, which is FANTASTIC!

I have yet to really dive into their food menu but can say that everything that has passed under my nose looks fantastic.  The best part is that Tatyana (the mastermind and owner) focuses on healthy ingredients and healthy nontraditional pub food. It offers a nice twist and added variety that you simply do not see at your everyday pub/bar that does offer food.  There is the traditional pizza, of course should you feel more comfortable with something you know.  

It is simply a fun place to relax and hang without the madness you have at most of the other Grove venues.

Great neighborhood restaurant!! The staff are amazingly friendly and helpful. I started off with some Mint, Ginger Ice Tea cocktail that was delicious. We had some of the crawfish and seafood beignets that were ridiculously delicious and like nothing I've ever had. For dinner I had the blackberry and jalapeño ribs and would recommend trying this also. To finish off the food bonanza we had an 8 layer cake with thin mints inside. This is definitely worth the trip outside of the French Quarter and everyone should try it.

I can't even remember  how  many years I have been eating at Ranch House. It doesn't matter if it's  breakfast or lunch, it is always good down home food.
Plenty to fill you up & at a price you certainly  can't  complain about.
Yes I am a sucker for diners, also love Mom's  Place & Pop & Son's. 
Back to Ranch House, they usually have daily specials & remember it is an indie!  Breakfast is always relaxing and bountiful. Lunch has the usual fare with open faced sammies, burgers, hot plates & more...something for everyone. They do aim to please, I often make minor adjustments to my meal & have never had any complaints about it.
The servers, most have worked here for years. Food consistency  is good & my plate is usually clean...all good signs.
Yup, it looks like a throwback to the 70's, but if they updated it, they would be killing most of it's  character  & charm.
What's a girl to do? Just like the restaurant,  what you see is what you get.

We did the Independence Mall tour with Rich.  Mostly becuse we had to leave town in a few hours and the other tours we checked were booked or started too late.  Couldn't have been more pleased.
Rich was pleasant, funny, friendly and very knowledgable.  We asked a lot of questions, and he had a lot of answers. The few things he wasn't sure about, he let us know.  I also liked that he pointed out the "history" that might not have really happened.  The tour started right near Independence Hall and sort of circled the area.  Lots about Benjamin Franklin, of course, but lots of other Philadelphia and US history too.   We left feeling like we know the city quite a bit better.  Thanks.

I came here on a whim after taking my dog to Schukyll River dog park.  I'd been wanting to check this place out for a while, as I'd heard they were very dog-friendly here and were even developing a special menu for dogs.  I asked the hostess if the dog menu was out yet - it wasn't, but after checking, the hostess said the chef would be able to whip something up for her.  

This alone made me want to come back, as I like to patronize places that welcome dogs, but the food was SO good  I was by myself (exept for my dog) so didn't order an appetizer, but I got the burger, which came with parmesan fries and a garlic aioli.  The burger was the best I've ever had - great quality meat, uicy & perfectly seasoned, and it came with mushrooms on it, which I normally don't like on a burger, but they were phenomenal on this burger.  You can also order it with a quail egg on top, which I think I'll try the next time I get the burger.  The fries were delicious, thin & cripsy, and I could've eaten the aioli with a spoon, it was so good.  My dog's meal (chicken & rice, with an egg on top) came out after I was almost finished, but hey, she's a dog, and she didn't mind getting tidbits of the burger while waiting.  I'd forgotten I wanted to try the truffle popcorn, so I asked for a little container to go, and they accommodated. I tried some when I got home; at first I didn't think I liked it, seemed a bit sour or something.  But the next day I tried it again and couldn't stop eating it, so apparently I liked it.  
 
Service was a little slow; I kept having to ask someone to get my waitress, but I didn't really mind as I was resting up from the long walk, and she was very friendly.  Can't wait to come back again and try the other food (although I just might weaken and get the burger again!), but I'll probably wait a few weeks, when hopefully the dog menu is out.

Cracker Barrel rarely disappoints. Wish there was one on Long Island. Went with a party of 4 and ordered the special cinnamon French toast special. It was as good as advertised. The wait for a table was a bit long but the food was fast and the waitress attentive.

I do not shop at this store on a regular basis; however, today, I was there to buy some toys for Marigold since she is rambunctious and runs around a lot. I used to go to this store more frequently than I do now, and it's still like a superstore for pet owners; you can get just about anything that you might need for you dog or cat, but it's not just dogs and cats. You can buy supplies and food for hamsters, gerbils and fish. 

I'll be back, but not really soon because I don't need a lot of pet stuff at the moment for the cat.

We were a party of 4 and initially the waiter did not write down our order which made me nervous. Although, he came out with our order and everything was correct. Food was great! You can defiantly taste all the spices in the etuoffee!  prices are not bad either! Good place for dinner.

Great service. Treated well. Great quality. I got a gel manicure 3 weeks ago and I just got my first chip. Had to take it off bc my nails grew out and that's the only reason. Also, I work in healthcare and am constantly washing my hands and using antibacterial soap and it still lasted this long. Highly recommend!!
Nice to have an awesome local coffee shop. Their Peruvian (must buy a bag) is my favorite.

STAY AWAY!!!! This is my first time writing a review about a business but my experience was so bad I have to share.  My iPhone 6s would not allow me to download or delete apps. It didn't bother me too much but while I was shopping I figured I would ask for some advice.  They told me they could fix it;however, I MIGHT loose my pictures. I said whatever that's fine let's give it a try.  He tries to fix it for about 30 minutes then comes back and says it cannot be fixed and now my phone is absolutely done and won't turn back on. And it will be $300 for a new 6s. Long story short I got the price down to $150 for a 6s. But, honestly I shouldn't have had to pay anything. I went in with a phone completely capable of making calls and texts and somehow got stuck with a phone that wouldn't even turn on. Not to mention I lost all of my contacts and pictures. NEVER AGAIN. They were not sympathetic at all. They just said my case was "one in 10,000." Well if I was 1 in 10,000 the billion dollar company should have handed me over a cheaper if not free phone.

Strolled to Mr. B's  for an 11:30 lunch reservation.  Thought it was a very nice restaurant and  I had awesome service.  I am a messy eater to begin with, so I was worried about ordering the BBQ shrimp, but this was my reason for visiting the place so I had to suck it up and do it.  I started with a blood orange margarita, for $3.  Gotta like those lunch time specials! 

Then I ordered the Gumbo Ya Ya ($7).  I am no expert on gumbo at all.  In fact, the only time I've had it is at Emeril's in Miami.  I didn't think much of it honestly.  BUT, today, my mind was changed forever.  This gumbo was so delicious.  So flavourful with layers!  So good!  That andouille, chicken and broth was too good for words.   I know that if I lived here, this is one thing I'd order each time I came here. 

Then onto the BBQ shrimp ($18).  I was outfitted with a bib, and that was a good thing as I had many splatters on it by the time I was finished.  My server gave me a little lesson...hold the tail side to the left with my left hand.  Unwrap the shell, but don't worry about the feet til after.  Ewwww, those things are feet?  I never knew that before today!  With my long fingernails, this was a little work, but so worth it.  First  picture is how it looked when it was served, and then next picutre is the reward after I got the shell off!  The BBQ sauce was just insanely good.  Butter, worster sauce, lemon, garlic, etc. etc.  It would be fun to bathe in it.  Thank goodness there was french bread to dip it in, which was the next best thing...

Loved this place!

Dinner, live music, while on one of the last steam driven paddle boats that exist in the world. Sure why not. The food was pretty good, and so was the live band. While on the boat, they take you for a ride up the Mississippi River,  while the band plays, about half way up. The food is served including a dessert. It was well worth it.

After hearing about FTS from some friends, we had to check it out. As we currently have two train enthusiasts in our midst, this was a home run!

Entering, you're greeted by a HUGE train set with all sorts of trains to play with. Naturally, our three year old gravitated towards the 3 engines another boy was playing with rather than the 50+ currently not in use. After a discussion about the importance of appropriate social conduct and the need for personal space, we proceeded to play for the next few hours on one of the four huge train tables. 

The walls are covered with just about any popular train toy your little, or you kiddo's little, heart may desire and is great place to stock up on birthday and Christmas gifts if the little ones are into this sort of things. Plenty of engines, tracks, cars as well as tons of books, puzzles and games made it a great spot to see what's available currently and get ideas of later in the year. 

Great place to come and spend a few hours on a rainy or nice day. Very nice folks running the place as well. Don't feel like standing? They've even got a bunch of seating for the adults while the little squirts run off some energy! A great place to check out for any and all train enthusiasts!

I love it out here. Such a relaxed, charming brewery with awesome outdoor patio and really fun indoor spaces. They have food now (mostly hot sandwiches), with lots of local sourcing. The beer is all consistently tasty, too, with some interesting brew styles and flavors. Could easily spend a whole lazy weekend afternoon here with friends. 

Only complaint: no flights.

I have never written a bad review before. I just stopped by for a cup of coffee and a desert.  I ordered strawberry pie.  There were 2 half strawberries,  quite old and burried in gobs of creamy stuff. It was really not a strawberry pie but something way more unhealthy, too sweet and rich. 
I told the waitress (for the very first time in my life complaining in a restaurant - and I am 65) that it was not satisfactory. She said I could have another desert. I declined. Then she gave me a bill for the whole thing -even though I had not eaten it. I don't think that my message got to the cook or owner.

Started our 7 mile bike trip to Lamberville from here.  Free parking and bathrooms at the far end of the lot.  We sat down by the river after our ride and planned our next stop for the evening.  This was a nice park and perhaps a return visit is in order to explore more.

I always get my prints done at this fedex....but today when I called, the girl I had to talk to was absolutely amazing and got my prints done when I emailed her my documents. I did not notice the time when I went to pick up my prints knowing that they close at 6pm on Saturdays. I was on my way at 5:50pm so I figured I would give them a courtesy call and let them know I was on my way. Well the male that answered the phone said sorry but I lock the door at 6pm so if u are not here by that time I cannot let you in past 6pm. So I said ok that's fine I understand company policy, I hope I make it. I literally pulled up at 5:57pm as he was locking the door. I ran up to the door, but since it was locked he just pointed at his clock inside and said no it's 6pm. I was trying to tell them the actual time was before 6pm and all I needed to do was run in and grab my prints! 
He was just smiling and laughing and pointing at his stupid clock, which I'm sure if he looked at his cell phone it would have said 5:57pm! 

I have worked in customer service for 15years! Seriously where has the real customer service gone!

The interior is really cool. It does not appear to be a busy place -- Delicia is definitely more hopping -- and their dinner menu is a severely abbreviated version of their lunch menu, so definitely go for lunch instead of dinner. Nice selection of tacos, salads and sandwiches.

Food was great. As a vegetarian I was thrilled to have multiple unique options for an entree. I ended up getting the vegan sausage with mac n' cheese and loved it. Overall was pretty loud in there but it was also late on a satu

One of the things I love about this place? They are always getting in new games that I can try out. That being said it never gets boring playing the same games over and over. My boyfriend and I are there almost every weekend and the staff is always available to answer any and all questions we may have whether it be showing us how to play a game or just something simple like a rule not making sense. The other thing I love is that they are willing to play games with you or find you people willing to do so if you don't have enough players. Also it's conveniently located to all kinds of yummy food that they let you eat (or drink!) in shop.

Customer service is number one. Made us feel very welcome and not pushy on sale. Patient and aimed at pleasing us AND they did. Emmanuel was one of the best auto salesmen I have met and we enjoyed working with and talking to him. Even though it took most of the day because the vehicle just came off the truck, we were treated with respect and apology after apology for it taking so long. I have bought about 50 cars in my lifetime and this was the best experience.

Are you kidding? Who is reviewing these restaurants? I seriously feel decieved. I ordered the generals chicken and my daughter had the seseme chicken. We both took a few bites and left. I LOVE to eat, and I rarely will leave a restuarant but the food, service, and ambiance was horrible. Don't waist your time people.

The lovely wife and I were Living the Dream!

1. We were on our way to a new place my fellow Yelpers were raving about.
2. Cambodian was a new ethnicity for us. Very exciting!
3. It was BYOB which we always appreciate.
4. On our first pass we snagged a parking spot less than a block away. Very lucky in this crowded part of South Philly.
5. We walked in to this tiny cozy place at 3 PM on a Sunday and snagged a table right away.

Everything was going so well it was time for a bump in the road. The first thing our very pleasant waiter did was list the seven items, that's right seven items, which they were out of.  This included all the skewers and several other dishes. The carnivore in me was completely ready for those beautiful sticks of meat and I was to be denied.

It turns out that they were slammed on Friday and Saturday and this was the result. Also, it's happened before. LESSON LEARNED- Sunday afternoon maybe great for snagging a table but bad for availability of menu items!

So with limited choices available we picked PRAH-HOK KAHTEEH ($8) as our appetizer. It was delicious and a perfect way to begin our meal. Some folks may think that dipping raw vegetables into a meat sauce is a little odd but trust me, it works.

For our meal we decided to split two dishes. The first was PLEAH SACH-KHOE. This was delicious marinated beef with kaffir lime and lemongrass. It was so good it was beyond five stars for both of us.

We also devoured a CHICKEN CURRY STEW that was incredible. The texture and layers of flavor in the broth brought smiles to both of our faces.

The wife and I both love this place and we'll be back but not on a Sunday afternoon.  We understand it's tiny and family run but seven items off the small menu was a big disappointment.  However the food was so incredibly good that I'm awarding four stars.

First of all, I will add the disclaimer that I was going to dinner with my boyfriend's parents for the first time when we went here so I was not doing my usual fine-tooth-comb of the facilities and services offered.... as I was, well, let's just say more than a little nervous! 

They had a great selection of red wines, and French reds and Napa reds are pretty much my favorites hands down and they had a lot of good ones. The Bordeaux and their house Cabernet are both delicious. 

We all got different appetizers so we could try different things. I had never really had French food. 

It was here that I realized I had never had a properly cooked scallop. I had spent my entire life boycotting scallops because they were gross rubbery balls of wasted calorie intake. Blegh! Who wants to eat something with the texture of an inedible gummy bear!? Not this girl. However, Provencal served us four perfectly cooked scallops in a delicious creamy butter sauce. I dipped my bread in the remaining butter sauce (I know, I know the chef was probably like "For real????! Oh I see my bread alone wasn't good enough for her!") but the truth is the butter sauce was just that delicious and renewed appreciation for properly cooked scallops.

I got the roasted red pepper bisque - absolutely delicious - it was on a prixe fixe menu for that night. Amazing. 

For the main entree I got the steak and frites. The steak was probably the best steak I have ever had... I couldn't finish it all, and it reheated beautiful and it was excellent "brunch" the next day. 

The dessert, that I can't remember the name of, was also delicious. I told you I was distracted... and a little nervous considering the context of the meal... LOOK! Just eat there, OK? I promise it's delicious.

Love this truck and hit it a few times a month.

I'll pile on with the praise that everything they sell is great.  I normally get the spicy chicken and add potstickers for a buck then add some sriracha but I've tried them all.

I also gave the cucumber kimchi a try and it's also great.

If you see the KBop truck don't think twice, you won't be disappointed.

I love Cedar Park Cafe! I usually come by here after church, and it's a friendly restaurant with great brunch foods.  Last time I went, I got chicken and waffles and it was delicious and filling. Over the last few years, I have been able to taste everything on the menu, and I have not come across any dishes that were disappointing. 

The waitresses are extremely kind, and it is a welcoming environment. 

The only inconvenient part of eating at Cedar Park is that there is always a long line.

Extremely disappointed at this place over the weekend. They offered summer drinks as part of their specials but they were out of the Raspberry. Then we ordered a Pina Colada instead, but they didn't have the mix for that either. We each ordered the prime rib and got mashed potatoes with it. When I tried to send mine back for a baked potato I was told that they don't serve baked potatoes on Sunday. I also wanted creamed horseradish and was informed that they might possibly be out of that as well, so I asked for sour cream to mix with the straight horseradish. By this time the bartender (subbing as a waitress) was becoming visibly agitated with my persistent requests.  I was planning to order 2 additional prime rib dinners to take home to my husband and son-in-law, but I wasn't about to give this place any more money for their poor choices and now an attitude from a food server.  So I phoned in my order to the Outback Steakhouse where (for the same money) we got our choice of potatoes, AND choice of vegetable, AND we also got warm baked bread.

OK it's a Home Depot.  The address is technically Clifton Heights but everyone knows it as the Upper Darby HD. Even the PA announcements from the staff reference Upper Darby.

This HD is a big one.  It helps if you are a regular because it takes some time to get the lay of the land.  It has more live plants than many HDs so gardeners find it particularly nice.  

They do a fine job here.  I know that if I visit there is a very good chance I'm going to find what I need.

We went here for a quick dinner, and we were pleasantly surprised.  We've eaten many times at the Top Deck restaurant, but this was the first time we tried the Steak and Pasta House.  The place is very nice and clean, and we were greeted right away by our server, Diana.  She was very friendly.
