I've been coming to this store for months without a problem. Today was the last time I stepped into this location. I thought Walmart was the worst, this just might top the worst customer service in my life. Today, the cashier asked for my ID to pay with a target gift card!! Then she asks me if I want to apply for a credit card?, I replied "did you not hear? I'm paying with a Target gift card not by credit." She called a manager who was as stubborn as her. Told her she can stock all the items back. I don't need an attitude because you're not getting a bonus for signing me up. What kind of dumb S.H.I.T is this? Avoid this store, shop online!

This was a good clean property.   Awesome views of the mountains and dessert.  The room was totally up to date and even had a gas grill on the patio so I could grill some steaks.   I will be back to visit. 

On a side note the only negative is that if you are going South of Tucson this may not be the best place as it is on the north side of the city.  This means you waste a little bit of time going through the city and if you hit the traffic wrong you could waste quite a bit of time in gridlock.

I was visiting my parents in Tucson when my dog was bit by another dog at the park. My lab had his ear torn at the tip, and there was no way I could stop the bleeding. I called VCA Animal Hospital, and even though their computer system had been shut down for half an hour during the day, which would set anyone behind, they still managed to get my dog in in a timely manner. Even though it was a little bit of a wait, and there were many pets in need of immediate medical attention on this particular day, they still treated my dog as a high priority patient. I had to leave my dog for a few hours, but Samantha, at the front desk, was extremely caring and made sure to let me know that I could call for anything, even if I simply wanted to check on my baby. Dr.Ray and Dr.Olsen did an amazing job communicating everything that was happening with my lab, and I appreciated the way they took care of him.  Overall, it was a successful end to our awful day thanks to VCA Animal Hospital.

Simply delicious...

On a recent trip, my cousin who grew up eating their water ice and recently returned to the area suggested  (insisted?) we stop at Italiano's after dinner at Nick's (for a roast pork sandwich).  I think it was the first time I've had water ice since I moved away in 2007. The medium lemon water ice was as I remembered it, delicious.  And yes I got rind in each order--Yum!

We had a second serving on the way to the airport.  What a fun start and finish to a great trip to Philly.
Greek salad--freshest I have ever had. Service was great, and $10 pizza special was awesome. I will be back.
I had a taste for something fresh with a ton of flavor. I came to Pho Voorhees for my favorite dish 525 with the grilled shrimp on the side. Delicious and quick as always.

This place is the standard for excellent and consistent service. The staff is always welcoming and everyone always seems genuinely happy to be there. The selections are premium and there staff is always eager to assist you in finding the cigar you're looking for. The smoker's lounge in the back is comfortable. Obviously the Ashton Cigar Lounge above Holts is dynamite. This cigar shop is the elite of its kind, and a real gem of center city.  The buy-four-get-one-free deal is also awesome.

Ok...my last visit was way back in 2012 and I wasn't impressed. 

The coupon I received in the mail offering a free burrito lured me back. 

I'm still not impressed. I even got the hot salsa and still no flavor here. 

I guess I'll wait for their next crisis to return.
ouch!   this place is filthy dirty and the food is horrible!  service is avg.  the band sucked too!  crappy band with bad singers  and the bartender she was rude too!

Ordered from here before they moved to the new location, so maybe the food has also changed. Ordered delivery for a few co-workers. The wait was long. In fact, a prior attempt to order from here was cancelled because the delivery time was 2 hours...we didn't even get things that were cooked, so this was confusing.

I got a salad. It was fresh enough for a deli that probably specializes in sandwiches, but the dressing was awful.  It was thick and gritty with sugar. I actually had to add a few spoonfuls of water to thin it out and dissolve the sugar. I would have actually preferred bottled dressing at that point. 

Overall, no one was impressed. Prices are decent, but the food was just average.
Sooooo good! Came here with a handful of friends close to closing time. They were nice enough to let us in anyway. All of the good was amazing. Might go back tomorrow for the buffet.

I really wanted to like this place. It was cute and had a great vibe. The food was disappointing. We started with the Pi Bites appetizer, which was maybe the most bland thing I've ever paid $8 for. 

We got the thin crust pizza which had some interesting flavors, but nothing special. I think pizza is like sex- it's always good, sometimes amazing. This was ho hum at best. Try Dewey's instead. 

The music was very very good, but I think it was just a good XM channel.

I love the man who owns/is always at this store. He has the largest, whitest beard ever. He can chat you up about the weather, take your key, make a copy, give you your key x 2 back and finish the transaction in less than two minutes. 

He is helping me eradicate the horrible, and obviously traumatic, memories of the past when I would go to a lesser hardware store to get a key copied; those trips began with some snot-nosed kid and ended with me leaving in a huff after 10 long minutes.

I went to Luke with a friend for the happy hour and we had really good experience.  The decoration and the service both met my expectation. We tried raw oysters, fried oyster and red bean and rice on their daily special menu. All of them are good. I am surprised that their fried oysters are not too greasy. Overall it was a great experience and I will definitely visit again.
Talking to them was so difficult, they didn't know what I was talking about. All I needed was a cavity in a brick wall to install an intercom system.

Gosh...who would have expected this in downtown Granite City.  I love to try new restaurants and I usually drag either friends or family along.   Sometimes the outing is a great experience and sometime it is not so great.   I made a  reservation for Lascelles for Friday night 4/1 at 7 for the four of us (my spouse, brother and his wife).  We arrived to find the restaurant completely full.  They were however, able to seat us right away.  As we walked in we saw some friends (group of 12) who were also trying the restaurant for the first time. They had already finished their dinner and raved about the food.. We ordered two appetizers the brussels sprouts and the goat cheese.  Wow...I thought Cleveland Heath had the number on  brussels sprouts.  I have to say these were the absolute BEST brussels sprouts I have ever had.   They were deep fried and had pepper rings and fried union straws on the top.  The goat cheese appetizer was also very good.  The two males ordered the grouper dish (one with asparagus and one ordered the brussels sprouts as his side dish).  Both of them claimed the dish was excellent (and there was not one drop of food left on their plates).  The two gals ordered sandwiches.  My sister in law ordered the black and blue burger.  She liked it but wasn't fond of the buffalo sauce.  I ordered the portabella mushroom sandwich which came with a generous order of parmesan fries. It was one of the best I have ever had.  The portions are very generous and the prices are unbelievable.   We will definitely put this on our list of regular go to places.  Look out Edwardsville restaurant scene....this restaurant is now be one of my favorites in the Metro-east.  

The waitress was very attentive (although I did have to ask for a glass of water 2x) and a bit entertaining.   

The good thing is that they take reservations.  Many of the great places on the Illinois side of St. Louis do not take reservations and if you go on a Friday or Saturday night the wait is 1-2 hours.

Congratulations owners of Lascelles-you have quite a gem.  I wish you the very best and you bet I will be telling everyone within shouting distance about you.

The kids menu is up to age 10. I'd say the portion is right up to age 6ish. Except the grill cheese,  that is a whole sandwich.  The clam bake was a good value,  the ribs (appetizer) were a little too charred for my taste.  The portion size for adults was just right, but more on the small size. The short ribs is a little on the smaller size as well.  Ok value for the food.  Close to liberty bell and attractions which make its nice.
Driest reuben sandwich ever.  Meat cooked well but sandwich overall lacked moisture.  They ran out of mayo and the cole slaw they gave us just tasted like it was soaked in vinegar.  Yuck.

This was my second visit here.  My first visit went off without a hitch, not so much this time.  I drove down from Brooklyn to meet up with a girlfriend there.  We arrived around 5:15 pm and were told that they only do tastings from Noon-5 pm.  We were told that we could buy full glasses if we wanted too and that there would be live music shortly and pizza. The lady went on further to explain that it gets really busy and they do not have the staff or time to dedicate to a full tasting after 5 pm.  We told them that we didn't need the full breakdown and we know exactly what we wanted and they still said no.  Now the interesting thing is that a couple pulled up right before us and they were walking in while we were parking and we see that they are standing next to us doing a tasting.  So now I'm pissed because they clearly walked in and got a tasting but we are being told something different.  Fast forward, we got two glasses and took a seat.  We were there until about 6 pm and wouldn't you know it they were still doing tastings with other couples that were there as well as the couple that walked in before us.  I bought two bottles of the white Merlot just because I had been raving about it to a friend  and wanted them to taste it.  However I won't be going out of my way to return here again, customer service plays a huge role in where I spend my money at and they failed me here.  I realize they have a policy and but when you are blatantly ditching your policy for another couple but not for us I know it's bs.  In their defense I did not tell them that I came all the way down from Brooklyn, however I didn't feel the need to when I saw they were serving that other couple because they clearly had their minds made up.  Oh and from the time we walked in only 2 or 3 more people came in so it wasn't busy and there were about 5 people behind the counter and another handful of people coming in and out of the kitchen.  

I gave it 2 stars for the taste of the white Merlot only.  We also had the spumante secco (?) and I've had better tasting sparkling wine for a liquor store for half the price.  My girlfriend wanted to taste the spumante rose but they didn't have any more of it. 
This is worth a visit if you are going to pass it but other than that go to New Hope for the vineyards over there! Cheers!

Buddy Brew has to be one of my favorite coffee shops in the Tampa Bay Area. The staff are super friendly and are great at recommending drinks! I tried an iced shake cappuccino with soy milk. Yum!
For food, I usually get the avocado toast with an egg. It's incredible! BB has the best work environment and I know I can't go wrong when I choose it as a place to get stuff done.

Can I first just say: "who is the clown writing about "Kadels" for a business named "Abra Auto Body?" Hmmm, I wonder if his opinion is credible. He rear ended someone and blames everyone but himself. Granted, alzheimers makes us forgetful. Maybe he forgot he was responsible for the accident? Then he repeatedly calls Abra, Kadels? I'm all for accurate reviews but I don't like scumbags who make a yelp account, only to leave 1 bad review, for THE WRONG COMPANY. 

I am from Los Angeles. I was visiting. I visited 6 shops, including Petersons (way too long a wait), Mike Minegars (nice guy, but also too long a wait), and a couple others. Abra was professional from day 1....kept me in the loop the whole time....advising me of changes + parts + adjustments they needed approval for. Dave was my point person and he is a stand up dude.  My car - a 2015 Z06 -- is like my child. I spend a lot of time, thought, and energy into determining how best to fix her....I had a good feeling about Abra and I took a risk trusting them with the work. There is a slight color difference between one panel and the surrounding panels and I informed them of this. Like a true 5 star business, they were immediately willing to meet with me to discuss. Upon reviewing the work, they agreed with me and are now going the extra mile to fix the work....not because there is something bad with their prior work. SIMPLY BECAUSE THE WORK DID NOT SATISFY ME AND THEY WANT ALL CUSTOMERS TO BE SATISFIED AND HAPPY. 

Props to this business. They deserve every one of the five stars I am giving them. And to that jackal who left an unfounded, inaccurate review, I hope you will ignore it just as I did.
Very nice place, we enjoying that so much. It's allowed me who has just 19 years old to join in. Has so much fun, we will comeback tonight!
Great ice cream flavors! We got the coffee and the blackberry chip. It's also open late which is nice. Came here after a show right at 10:50 :)

I love the Bottleworks. 

My best friend and I went in today for a late lunch and had another tasty experience. 

The beer is fantastic, however, in my prego condition, I opted for the delicious, slightly flavored mango iced tea. Yum. 

We started off with some hummus. It's really good. I do wish they would load it up with more feta, onions and kalamata, but I am a gluttonous heathen. The crackers that accompany the hummus and pita have a little bit of a (curry?) kick to them. I am always sure to save the hummus for a to-go box; it's just as tasty two hours later.

My buddy had the Tuna Reuben. Don't get me wrong, I like tuna... but I'm not sure how I feel about it on a sandwich with a side of slaw. Buddy, however, loves the hell out of that funky combo. She claims it is a success every time.

I had the beer cheese soup.... it's goooood. And I also had the bottleworks salad and added chicken. It comes in some sort of vinaigrette, regrettably, such dressings lack enough calories to satisfy my gluttonous cravings so I opted for the sun-dried tomato ranch. It was tasty to say the least. 

On my boyfriend's behalf, I will say that the beer-brined chicken sandwich is far more superior than any regular joe chicken sandwich. It is a gift from God. Respect it.  It is moist and has a slight after taste of pale ale (?) plus it has bacon and cheese.... always a good combo.

Bison nachos are out of control humungo.

Pistachio ravioli are also freaking amazing... but it's a super small portion so load up on beer first... or a salad, whatev

And, come on people, everyone knows that bison is the driest meat on the planet. Order it medium, it always comes out well done.... that's just the way of the world. Lo siento.

Thought a little over priced. They had issues day we went. Couldn't get in beechwood aging section. Giving Bud Light Hat when I've been drinking Budweiser for 40yrs. For $35 should been given choice between Bud and Bud Light hat. Gave Bud Light hat away.

If I could give negative stars I would.  The manager is RUDE and accuses people of lying.  The employees are not properly trained and the District Manager will not call you back.  Do yourself a favor and spend your money elsewhere.

Best sushi I've had in NoLa! Sushi chefs are extremely talented and masters at their craft. Management and staff were extremely attentive and friendly. Try the infused sakes and salmon belly if you know what's good for you!

Went here last week with friends. The servers was ok, waiting time is too long. Didn't expect that it would take so much time for the food since theres not much people when were there. Nothing special and pricey.

I always enjoy dining at Bistro St. Tropez. The service is great, and the servers all seem to enjoy working there. The atmosphere is pleasant and relaxed. Usually I am able to get a table with a view of the Cira Center and the Schuylkill River. Admittedly, the location is a little "off the beaten path," but after dining, I like to stroll through the top floor of the Market Place Design Center and check out the crazy furniture. I think the location is part of the Bistro's charm.

I have ordered several different seafood entrees, and the fish is always cooked perfectly. The skatewing entree is amazing, and the Dorade (Sea bass) entree comes in as a runner-up for my favorite. The sauces and accompaniments are delicious and complex. I also devour the crusty dinner rolls with pesto sauce that the servers provide before the meal. 

I have been a patron of this restaurant for four years and will continue to bring friends there for a good meal.

I've moved to Massachusetts, but I come back to Philly often, so I keep coming back to Dr. Gilbert.  At the risk of sounding like I'm being paid for this, let me say that every person in Dr. Gilbert's office is friendly and professional. They all do great work, whether it is the hygienist, the dental assistant, the administrative staff who make appointments and process paperwork, or Dr. Gilbert himself.  Mari made my teeth look great and gave me some good advice to use between cleanings.  Dawn makes sense of even the most complicated of insurance processes and gets it done quickly.

There are TVs and headphones if you need distraction, and even free wifi (though I've never had to wait more than a moment in the waiting room).

Several of my co-workers now go to Dr. Gilbert on my recommendation, and they are all pleased with the results.
First time here have Bacon Cheeseburger & Sweet Potatoe Fries delicious nice snd fresh.Nice atmosphere for lunch

Recommended by the concierge of the Astor Crowne Plaza.  It was a Thursday night.  We ordered cocktails which took 15 minutes to arrive.  I ordered a Moscow mule which I'm assuming they just didn't know how to make it because it was green colored and had no ginger taste at all.  I then ordered the Frogs Leap Sauvignon Blanc which was practically undrinkable, my husband took a sip and actually shook his head to get it down.  I ordered the Blackened Red Fish which was the most expensive item on the menu and my husband assured me it wound be delicious: Wrong! It was undercooked, slimy and did not appear blackened just mild in spice.  It was actually kind of mushy.  I just couldn't eat it.  They were fairly accommodating, offering me something else, but at this point I was over it.  My husband found his items to be edible but not wonderful.  Sorry Muriel's, for the high end prices, this should be a lot better.  It is in the most touristy of locations so I should have known.  I would not go again.

Went for the Saturday lunch buffet. Beautifully set up, lots of dishes I had never tried before. Service was ok- water guys were obsessive as in most Indian places around here and very accommodating to our two small children. Food was excellent! Well worth the few extra minutes drive!

Since we were disappointed that we couldn't go to Santa Barbara to see the show that we went there for....well we decided to just walk around the area to look for a place to eat at. We found so many Mexican restaurants and typical American restaurants. As we were walking, the outside of the restaurant caught our eyes. We went in and was seated right away. We know thai food well and I think the servers (all are thai) know how much we love to eat. They even gave us special fish sauce to go with our order. We got the combo which comes with Tom Kha Kai with chicken OR house salad. Of course we picked the soup. Hahaha. We got beef panang which was just okay. We also got the the eggplant with basil leaves which was very good. Of course we had to get shrimp pad Thai too. Well, the eggplant order and pad Thai was gone in no time. The serving was actually a lot. Plus it comes with an egg roll and a few other things which I don't know what they are. We will definitely be back if we are in the area

I finally got to come and experience brunch here! Which is easier said than done. I've attempted to come before and the wait was around 1.5-2 hours. 
On Sunday we came around 1115 for a 45 minute wait which wasn't bad for a group of 5. 
It's two for ones for Sunday brunch and I tried the sangria and the blood orange mimosa. I preferred the sangria hands down!
For food I ordered the huevos rancheros which was pretty good. My gf ordered the Singapore stiryfry and the white trash hash and I liked her stir fry a lot!
I will be back for sure because I keep hearing how good the tavern burger is and I won't make the mistake of not ordering it next time! 
Awesome atmosphere with a brunch of tvs. Can be a little loud though.

Update: It's rare that I solicit attention for businesses, but one business I frequent is wildly deserving of attention. I have been a client of Lash Therapy Express Hair Bar and Spa since 2012, and if I had a dollar for every time someone has asked for a referral since then, I could retire. 

I don't wear much makeup, so having eyelash extensions that make me feel glamorous without having to do anything is a dream. They're unnoticeable and easy to maintain. As a cherry on the sundae, the owners Jayme and Jarad are the most kind, generous people you could find, and their marriage is the definition of GOALS. I bet that half of their business comes from "fixing" other lash places mistakes.  They train all technicians personally so you truly can't go wrong with whomever you book.

A quick trip to Lash Therapy is nothing short of therapeutic. Obviously I highly recommend them, and if you've ever considered such an indulgence, I can assure you won't be disappointed! Thanks Jayme and Jarad for all you do. You're loved!

Came to CBQ for drinks and an appetizer before enjoying a movie at our favorite theater. First of all, we thought that the place was closed. No one at the door and only one table with guests. The bartender noticed us standing there for 15 minutes and we sat at the bar.  We then noticed the new menu is void of our favorite items: bunt ends and okra! Only one type of ribs??? No St. Louis style ribs. Being half-Texan I know BBQ.  This place is not a BBQ restaurant.  That being said, the menu does not state that the place is a BBQ place, rather a "Bar & Que" because of the pool tables next door. Sorry CBQ, you just lost a customer and we will not be back!
Loved my food. The bread was definitely fresh. Service was sub par but a pleasant meal.

4 stars for being decent Greek food in the virtual Greek desert that is Center City Philly. Probably 3 stars for actual value and quality, but since I can't easily get to Queens for dinner, this will have to do, thus 4 stars for convenience. I recommend it for those in Center City looking for a Greek-fix. Best moderate-to-cheap Greek food I've had in Philly, not that there's a lot of competition.

Probably the best soondubu I've had in Philly and that's saying something, considering that there doesn't seem to be many good Korean places around my hometown unlike the DC Metro or Bay Area. Tofu comes to you in a stone pot and as for the quality, it is definitely probably the best I've had in Philly. Tofu is soft, soup is adequately flavored, and temperature of the soup is sufficient for all intents and purposes. The LA Galbi meat was also something that was ordered and I will say that the meat here is pretty good. Marinated well, not undercooked or overcooked, and pretty tasty. As there is a dearth of Korean places around Philly, prices here tend to be higher than what is normally expected so do keep that in mind were you to come here. Still, I would say it's worth a try at least.

Let me start out by saying I was initially terrified to try barre3 because I'm not a dancer. I assumed everyone was basically a ballet dancer in the class. I'm so glad I was wrong! This place is amazing!

The interior is light, inviting, and very well decorated with exposed brick - just as you would imagine an high class studio. 

The class that I took was lead by Holly who is the studio owner and I only have good things to say about her. She spoke with me prior to class to introduce herself and identify any problem areas. Throughout the class, she checked on me. The class was high energy and I definitely "felt the burn". The class focused on posture, abdominal control, and breathing. After seat work, leg work, and core work, I could definitely feel the workout! 

I felt such great energy from Holly and the atmosphere from the facility that I can't imagine not coming back!

I used to hate this location, but something has changed in the past year. I don't know if it's the management or the employees, but it's gotten better! Food is fresher, employees are nicer, tables are actually CLEAN. Happy to see this place improving! Will come back.
Yum yum yum. Authentic delicious Thai food, excellent service and nice outdoor eating space.

The food is ok~ 
It's honestly just a mediocre diner like everywhere else. I do enjoy the cheese sticks though. 
My server on the other hand was very sweet, polite and on top of her game. 
My order had originally came out cold and she was so sweet and patient about fixing it. I give it a 3 because of the food...

Han Dynasty is a different experience than your typical Chinese food restaurant. Most of their dishes have a 1-10 rating in hotness. They also have a selection of meat/, fish or veggie, but depending on the dish, the selection can be just one, or about five different options. It reminded me of a Mongolian grill, but your sitting down, not watching, there are more options, and it's not Mongolian.

The prices are a little high, considering how inexpensive good Chinese food can be. And, for someone not familiar, it's not so easy to know what many of these dishes taste like.

I ordered the 3 chicken. It was good, though the chicken was about as soft as chicken can be, almost doughy. And, it was not breaded! Weird, I know. Anyway, it tasted good, but lacked any veggies. A friend pointed out that since the set-up is family style, that it might work better if mixed with a veggie dish.

The hottest dish anyone got was a 5, and I am told that was pretty spicy. I can only imagine what a 10 is like. And no, I did not try the 5 dish. I'm just not balling like that.

We had dumplings and scallion pancakes as apps. They were both good.

In a nutshell, pretty cool place, but not worth it, and not nearly as special as they want it to be.

The tortilla soup had too much chicken. I know that may sound odd, but the chicken was a little dry and the shreds were a little too big, the broth was exceptional, I would drink a vat of that. 
The Quesadillas were stuffed, as in I wish I had bought one to split with my hubster. Wow, that was a lot of food. It was good. I picked a pork and steak, they tasted distinctly different. I like to add my own level of spice to things, so it was just right, there was good depth of flavor especially for the price point. 
The Mahi appetizer tacos were cute and tasted good. Next time we will order less though because we barely finished a quesadilla between the 2 of us.
This is an accessible establishment for both wheelchair or mobility scooter. You can easily enter, wait in line, order and pay.

Hands down one of my favorite places to sit and do work. Good coffee and friendly baristas, large space with plenty of tables and outdoor seating.  $3 bottomless coffee is worth it during finals week when you need a place to study all day! There's always great artwork and the atmosphere is just right.

The only place in Boise that does crepes that I know of.  

After traveling and having them at other places it's nice to know that we have this here in Boise.

We will definitely be back.

The place is clean and the server is nice and patient  the food is good too I ordered the chicken teriyaki bowl.. I don't like cabagge so I didn't eat it but that one comes in a separate plate so nothing to worry about.

AAA sent Crockett's towing when I broke down on the side of 275. They arrived 30 minutes sooner than AAA estimated. The driver was professional and friendly. I only have good things to say about their service and would recommend the company to friends.

I rarely go to Indian restaurants that don't have a buffet, so when I came here, I was excited to see what they would have.
I let a coworker pick out the menu items, because he has more experience in eating Indian foods and has been here before.
Everything was AMAZING (especially apparent because I all-caps this word).
When I saw each dish, my eyes were overwhelmed by how colorful and vibrant they looked.
When I tasted each dish, my tongue was overwhelmed by how delicious each dish was.
The garlic naan, was especially delicious too.
We got the spicy, and it was just the right amount.
Even though this place is 30 minutes away from where I live in Nashville, I will definitely be back for more.

A bit pricey, but that was to be expected with a bar in a hotel that's located downtown. The atmosphere was wonderful, especially on such a nice night. Our waitress Christina was rockin, and we couldn't have asked for a better waitress. The only thing I wish this place had was a fried potatoe. Please give me some greasy something!!

HIGHLY recommend this tour ! From a plethora of tours to choose from in New Orleans this is by far the BEST! Our tour guide, David Westbrook, is a local and a wealth of knowledge on the history of this great city. We walked at a leisurely pace while he chatted and told us about each restaurants cuisine and history. We had 5 tastings and were able to buy local drinks! David even provided a list of all the best restaurants for us to enjoy on our own with $ signs to indicate how expensive the menu would be. He gave us tips on local grocery stores to purchase supplies so we don't end up paying more at tourist shops! Thank you David for an Amazing time and wonderful memories!
I'm somewhat picky about my food and I frequent the place.  Good food, great prices, dedicated staff.  And! They use romaine lettuce, not iceberg.

Way unimpressed with this place. 

I ordered a sandwich that came with brisket, pulled pork and cheese. Too bad is was AMERICAN cheese. Such a sin. The meat was flavorless, the sweet potato fries were burnt beyond belief and the service and the service was pretty terrible, too. 

The corn bread, however, was delicious. 

Listen, if you want good BBQ within 15 minutes of Hickory Kitchen, go to Stockton Farmer's Market in Stockton, NJ and hit up the Ol' Tyme BBQ stand - you will think you have died and gone to heaven!
Terrific little place.  Great find for the area.  Very good food at very good prices and April the bartender made it even better. Looking forward to going back again soon.

well over-priced. 15% gratuity for 5 people ( family with 3 kids ). paid $200. $30 gratuity. We still had to go to tim horton's for donut coz we were still hungry. Most of their sushi has the same spicy taste and prawn tempura was a size of a shrimp. terrible...i would never go back there.
Food is excellent Atmosphere is great.  One downside there is usually a long wait when going during peak evening hours or on weekends but worth the wait if you have the time

I was at Jon's the day after Thanksgiving with my brother and his girlfriend. After wandering around Society Hill and South Street, we were tired and hungry and wanted to eat somewhere decent. I had seen this place a bunch of times and thought it might be worth checking out, since they claimed that famed Three Stooges member Larry Fine was born where there restaurant now stands. 

We sat outside on the patio and waited. And waited. And waited some more. Granted waiting 20 minutes for a simple hello at a restaurant, is not something I normally do. But we were starving and didn't feel like wandering around much. Nearly some thirty minutes after we sat down, we were finally acknowledged and asked what we would like to drink. The drinks then took nearly 15 more minutes to arrive, before we even got to place an order.

Our food took forever to come out from the kitchen. Our server wasn't all that personable or apologetic for the slowness. She even forgot my soup that I ordered. I can't recall everything we ordered, but my sandwich was nothing special, and not all that hot as I recall. My guess is that it sat under a heat lamp for a few minutes before arriving at the table.

It took over an hour to get seated, be greeted, get a drink, and then get our food. It was much longer than I normally have waited for lackluster service and average tasting food. I wanted to ask for a manager to complain, but didn't feel like waiting another hour to find one. What a shame, they have a great corner location, an interesting history with the Larry Fine angle, but they need better servers and better food quality.
One of our favorites! Been told multiple times that it's good to see "young people" enjoying the great food too!

Great service, fair pricing, excellent work!

Traveling through Reno we discovered some wiring difficulties with our hauling trailer. We went to another shop who were too busy and they recommended Reno Vulcanizing.
Scott and Clint fit us in that day and got us roadworthy as soon as possible, at a real reasonable cost.

This Walmart is awful. Employees are rude and not helpful. Sketchy place. Nice greeters though so that's a plus. 

New incident happened on 08/15/17 
I hate to be negative but many things happened at this Walmart for me yesterday that baffled me. For one an older gentlemen was out in the heat pulling carts...I immediately thought that was strange but walked in and low and behold there were no carts for the customers. Meanwhile, there were a few younger employees doing nothing. A woman and I chatted about how wrong that was and then we see the older man pulling the carts to their designated area, no employee helped him so we both stepped up to help pull them in. I start shopping and once I'm done I go to checkout. I had three different coupons and I got to use two of them but the Tamera (the cash register lady and what her name tag said) said I couldn't use my $1 off Alka Seltzer coupon because what I got wasn't on the coupon....it states ANY Alka Seltzer product 12 count or more. I got the Alka Seltzer day time cold and flu 20 count. I tell her it should count and it doesn't matter if what I get isn't on the coupon if it says "any alka Seltzer product" and she begins to argue with me. So I naturally argue back. She calls for a manager so the manager can explain to me what she just said even though I told her it wasn't necessary. Well, as we're waiting she begins to say she remembers me from a few days ago. I say well I haven't shopped here in about two weeks. She says no you came in about a few days ago about the same thing. I said no I didn't, I haven't been here in two weeks. So once again she starts arguing with me over when I had been there... anyway I tell her it's taking too long for a manager to get here and all these people are probably getting mad about waiting and she says, "it don't matter."  the manager gets there. They're all buddy buddy so I already know I'm not getting the dollar off. I keep telling them it's not a big deal but they made it a big deal. The "manager" says yeah if the picture of what you're getting isn't on the coupon you can't get the dollar off. I say that makes no sense. She leaves. Tamera (the cash register) says it's company policy. My boyfriends dad is a manager for a Walmart. I talked to him and he said it's not company policy and the way this was handled was unacceptable. I said thank you to Tamera after it was all done and she just stared at me. So, I called 1800walmart and complained. Some changes need to be made at this Walmart before I ever step foot in it again. It was only a dollar yet the whole thing escalated into an argument that could have easily been avoided. Below is a picture of the coupon they wouldn't let me use. Notice how it says "Any ONE Alka Seltzer product (12 count or larger)."

Great atmosphere if your looking for a nice place to get a good meal and watch a sporting event. I come here with coworkers for lunch fairly frequently, and get consistent service/meals. Not your average sports bar.
One of my very places in Philly. BYOB and you have to try the mango chicken. AMAZING gem in Philly.

Such a wonderful hotel!! We booked with a New Year's Eve deal and ended up with a two night stay for $325 and a $100 resort credit. I thought it was wonderful and although it was crowded it's definitely worth seeing during the holiday season.
There were a few cons: everything was overpriced, there are no microwaves (probably so you have to buy the food), and the shuttle drivers can be VERY rude (one of the guys requires that you tip even though it is a complimentary service & included in the resort fee and won't take you all the way to the destination). But overall it was a wonderful stay. 

I know a lot of people have questions about the parking, it's $29 a day to self park and $39 to valet park. I recommend parking in the 15 minute area to check in and then driving over to the Inn at Opryland to park. It's free, there are no hangtags or anything, and there is a shuttle from the inn to the resort that is free with a room key from either place. We did this and we didn't get towed or ticketed (we were there for 3 days & 2 nights) and we saved $90 in parking fees!

(I added a photo. Red is where we parked and green is where we stayed.)

Our visit to Bailey's Range was a bit of a disappointment.  It was our first dine in experience here, we were looking forward to it.  We had got an ice cream to go once previously and wanted to try dining in after we saw the cool atmosphere.  So on a luch break we tried a dine in.  We got sat right away even though they were slightly busy.  We got our order in right away.  We ordered the burgers well done which we regretted due to them being overdone and very dry.  However the flavor combinations of both burgers were quite tasty.  Our server was really slow and not because she was busy with other tables.  She just took extremely long to get anything we needed like more napkins, drink refills and our food.  She quickly picked up the bill to cash out our payment though.  She also was a bit rude in her service to us.  It was lunch time we were short on time so it felt too long of a visit, over one hour to get some burgers and fries.  We got our ice cream to go again as to get done on time.  On the plus side our servie at the ice cream station was very quick and super friendly.  We have agreed to try to dine in one more time before we give up on this place so hopefully it will be better.  Peace

Came in today and set a wait list reservation and they said it would be about 10-15 minutes. An hour later still no text back and brunch plans ruined...ended taking my girl to chipotle.  Disappointing experience.

Lilly's is my all time favorite Vietnamese restaurant in Nawlins, & I have been to all of them! It is very clean, the food is absolutely fresh & delicious, & Lilly is an absolute doll! 

The whole staff is sweet, attentive, & conscientious. The cooks are  awesome & will accommodate any dietary restriction with ease. In fact, it is the only Viet restaurant where vegetarians & vegans can eat safely & know that something they don't eat has not been sneaked into their food. If you say "No MSG!" you will get no MSG!

Now what to order? My order always starts with the Shrimp Spring Rolls, so fresh, & when smothered with their house-made Peanut Sauce, divine! I LOVE the Spicy Tofu served over the soft noodles & topped with steamed veggies. (They will add a whole pile of steamed veggies over anything for an extra $2!) You can taste the garlic, ginger, & peppers in it, & although hot & spicy, it will not set you on fire like some of their competitor's food. LOL!

Now keep in mind, that although Lilly's is a five-star Viet restaurant, it is not The Windsor Court or Commanders Palace, so don't expect that kind of service here. It is a small "Mom & No-Pop" venue. Some idiot woman gave them only three stars because, "The waitstaff kept asking if we wanted anything & did not observe our 'social cues' that we weren't ready to order!" 

Did this woman not know she was dealing with another culture? A culture who would not recognize her stupid Yuppie cues? I bet dollars to donuts they were trying in vain to move her along & get her cranky ass out of there. Only she did not recognize their polite Asian cues of "Hurry up & order bitch! We are trying to close up & go home!"

Getting that kind of attentive service in other restaurants would be the "impossible dream". Ha ha... too attentive... my God you moron! That being said, if you want delicious, authentic, fast, & cheap Vietnamese food, Lilly's is the place! See you there:)

Krispy Kreme - I think you are going to get a pretty consistent experience across the chain. Heck, I did not even know about the "HOT" sign -- that is a cool concept! It was also great to see a full selection of Halloween items for the holiday. Not, obviously, frequenting this kind of store I do not know how common this is for the holidays. The only thing I didn't get was the sign reading $1.29 each -- add 20 cents for each in an assorted dozen. Okay, you need to reach into different spots to gather the donuts to fill a box but charging more for buying more of anything just does not make sense. I didn't buy a dozen but I had to read the sign several times to make sure my vision was shifting the words around.

Earlier this week I got a tattoo by Jared. 
At first I wasn't sure what to think, but I've had a few friends recommend this shop, and I've been craving a new tattoo so I figured I'd try it out.
And I was not disappointed! Jared was fantastic, he does Script beautifully and is very friendly. 
Best decision I've made!

Giving it two stars because the food is actually pretty good, when you finally receive it. The service is slow and the food is way over priced. Don't waste your time calling ahead for a to go order, you will still wait for it.

Really cute local place for all your cooking and baking needs...

I took one cooking class here and signed up for 3 more... they're nice and helpful and provide everything for the class (as they should since the classes are not cheap!)

Also love their baking selection, ended up finding some random products that I haven't seen elsewhere, and it's moderately priced.
I always want to buy something or the other when I stop by!

Read the reviews and decided to try the restaurant.  The Double pork was excellent, the soup wontons were the best I tasted. So was the hot and sour soup, spicy and delicious.  The service is great and very accommodating .  We will be back.

Great omelets and Cuban sandwich. Fresh fruit and delicious coffee. They made my omelet with egg whites with no questions asked.  The atmosphere is crowded and hectic so if u are looking for a relaxing weekend breakfast/brunch this is not the place to go but if can handle the craziness,  the food is definitely worth it. Even though there is no waitstaff, the staff behind the counter and the bus boys were very nice, quick and attentive.
Red Sox Nation, New Orleans Chapter #1! Good times, through the tough times and thrillers. LET'S GEAUX RED SOX!!!

This little unassuming place does breakfast right. You get large tasty portions and service with a smile.  I ordered what I thought was a "small" mimosa and it came in a beer mug. The staff is friendly and attentive and it's a nice atmosphere for family and friends.  Casual and welcoming.

I too was expecting more, especially since I diligently researched all of the hotels in the French Quarter and read a lot of good reviews about Monteleone. But frankly, it was just mediocre for the price you pay. 

We stayed here for my boyfriend's 40th. Lobby is beautiful, but rooms are pretty small and bathrooms are out of date. Views aren't that great either. However, the rooms are very quiet, UNLESS of course the fire alarm goes off at 6:30am, as it did for us!!! And on the exact day of my BF's birthday! Needless to say, we had only been asleep for a few hours after enjoying a night on Bourbon street and WAM! It was so loud and wouldn't stop going off for an entire hour. There was some malfunction or something. 

Also, everyone raved about the Carousel Bar, but I have to say the service there is awful. The entire weekend, we tried to get a drink there and the bartenders never once looked up to serve us. We waited 15 minutes each time and NOTHING! Also, it's quite dizzying to sit while the bar spins around. I can only imagine how it feels drinking, but alas, I will never know, since I never got served a drink there...We ended up just getting drinks at the back bar, which is really nice. There's jazz and the bartenders back there understand customer service a bit better. 

Here are the remaining pros and cons...

Pros: Great area; old style hotel; charming; comfy beds

Cons: elevator sometimes doesn't work; crowded (especially during wedding season); staff isn't too hospitable; over priced; housekeeping forgot to clean our room and took 30 minutes to deliver a hair dryer

We LOVE this place. Go to if you're looking for a place to chill out, have draft beer, and awesome food. The service is great. Just overall a really good place to go. There's even an outdoor area. Sports are always on so that's a plus. One time a bartender made a funny joke and felt bad and poured us shots for free. Definitely a go to for anyone living in the area.

Good buffet for the price. We went during the week and spent $27 for 2 people (11.99 each). They had everything you could ask for! Waiters grabbing drink orders. Eggs, bacon, sausage, cinnamon rolls, cereal, fruit, bagels, and much more! They also have a made to order station for eggs which was a plus because their buffet style eggs were a little too runny for my boyfriend. Overall, would definitely recommend for breakfast!
Place is very solid...actually better than solid. On Monday and Tuesday free sake and all you can eat made to order sushi for $22.

I really wanted to like this restaurant! Alas, I don't think I'll return. Main reason: both my boyfriend and I felt hella sick a few hours after eating here. Not full-on food poisoning sick, but sick enough that regardless of whether my brisket sandwich and his pulled pork sandwich actually got us sick, we just have a bad association with this place.

But there are other reasons to two star this place, too: service on is slow even though it is not at all crowded. We waited at the hostess stand for three or so minutes before anyone sat us. The greeting is the first impression the restaurant gets to make, and not having a prompt and friendly greeting is a bad sign. Although the decor inside is great, when I went on a Saturday afternoon there were only three other pairs of people eating. In such a big open space, that kind of emptiness just looks bad! 

Prices were very reasonable, especially with the 15% Yelp check-in discount. The coleslaw--my favorite part of BBQ food--was really bland. The fries were meh. Our respective sandwiches were delicious while we ate them, but then our tummies were so unhappy later that day.

I love this place! I am new to kickboxing so I was nervous to check it out, but I decided to call to learn about the new year promotion they were running. I spoke with Gabe, one of the owners, and he was incredibly helpful! He took time to explain the promotion and answer my (many) questions. After speaking with Gabe I decided to go in that day for the trail class, and loved it so much that I signed up! All of the instructors are wonderful, welcoming, and make me feel comfortable. There is a great energy and it's a fantastic workout!

In short, this place would not come recommended from either of us. It is a sit down burger place that serves sub-par burgers. We're rating Bagger Dave's slightly above Working Man's Friend, but below Punch Burger, FIVE GUYS, and BRU Burger as far as Indy burgers joints go.

Really great pizza! I love that they have fresh Basil as a topping option. Get a large 5 topping carryout for only $11.99. The garlic twists are soft and flavorful and the accompanying marinara sauce is fresh and very tasty. And a great deal at $3.99 for 8. Highly recommend if you're in the Hermitage area and sick of the local pizza chains.

This is not nashville hot chicken.  Not even close.  So if you are thinking you are getting something like princes, hattie b's, etc. then don't eat here.

Nothing even close to nashville hot chicken- but in all fairness, maybe thats not what they are going for.

Seeing this is one of the only food trucks that serve eggs and AVOCADO on a roll.... I decided I need to try this food truck. Usually I see this as tacos-only type of place but they have truly changed. Awesome looking place. They don't always have fries or home fries but that's ok because I don't need starch lol. They have some good looking burritos and tacos too.

I am 100% Vietnamese and I approve 100%! Their vermicelli dish (particularly the beef and shrimp combo) is phenomenal! Also, the broken rice dishes are better than most Vietnamese restaurants in Philly. And as always, I always start out with the summer rolls! This place is authentic, fresh, affordable, and delectable!

The food here was nothing spectacular but I really enjoyed the ambiance. I went there on a Saturday night and we were literally the only group of people there. 

I tried three different dessert crepes, and they were all good. I would go back for brunch, but I probably wouldn't bring anyone visiting from out of town here.

THIS PLACE IS SO BEST! 
Friendly and Great Witnesses! 
Their foods are so deliciously! 
I see there's different experience from this place. 
But this place seem getting improved! 
I will keep going to there!

I had never been to a P.F. Chang's before. I was pleasantly surprised. It was nicer than i expected. Decorated nicely. I tried a little bit of what everyone else got and everything tastes very good. Nice menu selections. I didn't pay so I'm not sure how to gauge cost. But it did seem to be a tad high for a chain that isn't very unique. Our server was new she forgot some things and took forever to refill drinks. But she was fun, she'll do great once she has a few months under her belt:)

Our meal:
Apps: 1) Dumplings; 2) Cheeseburger bun; 3) Pork Belly bun
Entree: 1) Brisket Ramen; 2) Spicy Shrimp Ramen

The Pros:
- Egg: Cooked perfectly, runny in the middle. Just the way I like it!
- Noodles: I loved the chewy texture of the noodle in the Brisket Ramen and the al dente texture of the Spicy Shrimp Ramen. 
- Atmosphere: Cool and edgy. Good music playing in the background. Servers were very nice and friendly. 

The Cons:
- Noodle to Broth Ratio: Very disappointing. Both our ramen bowls needed more broth. I've tons of ramens in my lifetime. The one thing I always make sure I do is to make sure I have the right noodle to broth ratio.  
- Spice level: Both ramens claimed to be spicy, but I think Shin Ramen is spicier than these bowls.
Just a small town off the highway DD. They do a good job and i stop here at least once a month. Not much to say but they will always be a stop once i get into NJ!
Sam did an amazing job. It's the best haircut I have got and I am definitely going to recommend Sam to all my friends in STL. Keep up the good work and I'll be back!

It's really sad that this location is actually still open. I had my ubox to be shipped to this location. Whole moving was delayed becasue they could not be reached by shippers. Shippers ended up sitting with my box for few days in Edmonton simply becasue they can not contact this location to drop the box in the storage. I ended up asking shippers to send my box to different location where they at least receive their phone calls. 

Extremely frustrating experience and I really think this location should be closed if they can't even deal with phone calls..

Went here for our anniversary, first time for us.  I'd say it's pretty similar to Ruth's Chris maybe a little less formal.  Service was exceptional.  My only comment would be when you have a middle aged couple out for their anniversary dinner, don't seat them next to a table of multiple families with kids.  It was a little loud and distracting and I probably should have requested a different table but we have kids too so we understand.

For the appetizer we had the mushroom ravioli which was good but they only give you three of them and they are pretty small.  They bring bread too which was nice while we waited for our meals.  Our wine was the perfect temperature.  We both ordered the standard filet with sides of Flemings potatoes and asparagus.  The steak was cooked perfectly and was substantial if not slightly bland - we did not select any of their rubs or toppings although the wife did get Bearnaise which I think is a crime to put on a filet lol.  The asparagus was nothing unusual which is fine since we love it anyway, but the potatoes....woah.  Those were amazing.  We are going to try and copy cat that recipe for sure.  

Will I go back?  Eh.  For $200 plus tip there are better meals to be had.  Maybe I'd go there on a promotional night or something.
This is by far my favorite Thai restaurant...anywhere.  I really enjoy this place.  The staff are awesome, the food is fabulous, the decor is trendy/cool....go eat at Aroy Tahi!
The best pizza and good location! I recommend this place for sure

On a nice summer day in June, I took my sister-in-law and her two kids to the Children's Museum.  Our favorite part was the dinosaur exhibit where we experienced a thunderstorm and light show that took us back in time to a place where the world changed and the dinosaurs lived and became extinct. They have fantastic replicas of T-Rex and many other meat-eating reptiles.  

They also have a dinosaur dig for the kids - though I did think it was probably a bit germy and wished they had more sanitizing areas.

Along with that, we enjoyed the Fireworks of Glass exhibit and got to see the actual costumes from the latest Star Wars movie (though I though this exhibit was lackluster at best).

There is a little something for everyone and although we missed the King Tut show, I think it would have been well worth it.  A yearly pass is affordable with all the changing exhibits offered and I think when Max gets older, we will definitely partake so we can go anytime.  I definitely recommend it for adults and kids.  Very enjoyable and a nice gem for Indy to have!

I love La Cabaña! It is one of my family's and my favorite restaurants. It is always clean and the service is wonderful. The servers are friendly ("how is everything my friends?"--our server knows us because we come so often) and always attentive about checking to make sure we have enough drinks and chips. And speaking of the chips, they are delicious! Crunchy, large corn tortilla chips, perfect for scooping up yummy cilantro onion tomato salsa. 
It is often pretty busy, especially on Friday and Saturday nights, but they still always seem to be pretty fast and attentive. Tonight was packed but we got in and only had to wait a couple minutes before someone saw us to seat us. I had the #21 combo--a burrito, enchilada, rice and beans (a change from my usual #18 burrito, taco, rice and beans, which my dad had) and it was delicious! The burrito and enchilada, which are both about the same size and both filled with ground beef and diced onions, were cooked perfectly and very tasty. There wasn't a ton of seasoning on the actual tortillas but they still tasted good and I think it probably would have taken away from the flavor of the rest of the plate. The rice is very flavorful and cooked just right, with corn, peas and diced carrots throughout but not overpowering it. The beans are also very good. They have more of a mashed potato consistency but you still get some lumpiness from the actual beans and they melt cheese on top, which really adds to the flavor and texture. If you love good Mexican food I definitely recommend this place!
Same great pizza as all the other locations. Always found it interesting that they turned the old safe room, from when it used to be a bank, into a windowless party room.

We have stayed at Sandpiper lodge now about 10-15 times and can honestly say that we absolutely love their service. The rooms are nice and clean and the Manager Sean is so accomodating and courteous. The front desk staff there are all very professional and friendly as well. We've reccommended this place to all our friends who visit SB and will always stay there whenever we are in town.

Located on Upper State St within walking distance to restaurants which is great after a long drive. 

Great Customer Service and Big, Clean Rooms! The rooms are equipped with Flat screen TV's and free WiFi. Pool and Sauna a plus!

I have to admit, the negative (and at times very passionate... not in a good way) reviews of this place almost kept me from even checking it out.  Being out here on business from Denver, CO and working long hours on a new project, I was desperately seeking a good... no, make that great craft beer... and this place delivered.  Happy I dropped in.

I'm not sure of the service standards in this area (by reading the other reviews, they must be pretty high), but I thought they were ok... Not great, not horrible, but they got the job done.  The fact that they are a beer/sports bar, I was very happy with the service speed/level.  I came here 2 of the 4 nights I was in town... And I will head back if duty calls in the future.  

With that said, let's visit the food and beer side of things...  Great selection of beer (on tap, didn't even look at bottles/cans), 40 to 50, with everything from the basic grain water (Coors Lt, Millet Lt, Bud) to the legitimately might "knock you on your @$$" flavors (Alesmith/Green Flash/Mikkellen).  Just what I was looking.  The food was very good as well... Had a Chicken Cheesesteak the first night, and it was awesome (please refer to my "I'm from Denver, CO comment above, so I admit I'm no expert, but I thoroughly enjoyed it).  The second night I had the pizza, again, very much enjoyed it.  

Gave it 4 stars based on the fact that no, they are not the best beer and/or bar food place I have ever been in, but given the above... I give them a solid B+

VERY pushy. Went in with a group for a wedding the staff pressured most of the girls I was with into gel polish ($20 more). There was no posted price menu . They left many of us sitting with half complete manicures and pedicures for 10-15 minutes at a time. Extremely disappointed. And on top of everything they made up different prices for each person. Unless you want to blow serious money on a half assed job-Go somewhere else

The location.. lower Garden District... the cheap drinks.. the photo booth... the patio.. this place is a dive bar powerhouse. They serve 151 Rum... which fewer and fewer bars are doing.. the crowd is  "indie" and "artsy" types who are a little more trust fund than what you find in the marigny. Neighborhood can be a little sketch but there are usually a lot of people around.

I have eaten here several times, mostly for dessert.  You'll enjoy the fireplace in the middle.

They have bottomless drinks for brunch!

This place is amazing. We looked through the pictures on Yelp and saw the various chaats and lassis and we just wanted to try it out to see if the hype was real.  We walked through the door and looked up at the menu board and felt a bit overwhelmed. We knew what we wanted but the owner gave us a nice intro into the world of chaats and how he prepares them.  He made us feel welcome and comfortable and we really enjoyed the additional service he provided right off the bat.  Now let's get to the food!

Chicken Tikka Salad Chaat:  The chicken was absolutely delicious!  Fresh chicken with the same great tikka taste mixed in with salad greens, chickpeas, cranberries, juicy mango slices, and all of the chaat accessories as the base. It was well worth every penny and every bite just made you want to keep going. Many restaurants that offer chaat have a bland taste and sometimes its either too saucy or their isn't enough of the sauce to coat the chaat but this place had it just right.  I'd highly recommend the chicken tikka chaat or chicken tikka salad chaat for first timers.

Paneer Tikka Chaat:  Spicy, sweet, and tangy at the same time with every bite.  Cranberries with paneer were a great combo and the shredded paneer blended in well with the chaat mixture.   The mixture of sauces were perfect and the crispy chaat pieces were crunchy all the way through the meal.  No sogginess = more taste!

Now for the lassis:

As someone who is critical of lassis and find that most stores just make glorified smoothies with mounds of sugar, I found the lassis at Mood Cafe rather pleasing.  I ordered the blueberry and peach lassis and both were pleasing.  The blueberry was a bit more tasteful than the peach lassi and I'd highly recommend it for first timers.  The peach was a bit more difficult to taste but it was still a positive experience.  Both lassis had just enough salt and sugar and not overwhelming to a point where you'd feel like you've had enough.  

Final Conclusion:  The owner is a terrific person who really works hard to please his customers.  He's mastered the chaat world and anyone who wants to experience good chaat and have a positive experience, they should definitely stop by!
Don't waste your time.  My Vietnamese wife wont return nor will I.
Our go to place for pizza, wings, salad, cheesesteaks, etc. We keep trying other places but keep coming back to blue bell. Always delicious and always consistently great food.

I do not recommend. Walking in we were not greeted asked only "how many". The customer service was horrible. Forgot drink orders. Was mopping the floor 2 hrs prior to close all around all the people that were eating. My opinion  I don't like to eat and smell bleach all around me.  The food was OK but no one came to ask how anything was or follow up. I would not go back

I stayed here during Fat Tuesday. It is now known as Chateau Bourbon and is ran by Wyndham, I think. I am very pleased! The hotel was of a very good quality and the staff was excellent! I felt all of the staff went above and beyond to accomodate. There are two things I will saybad about the place. First, They have combined the Concierge and the Bell Service into one desk. This is not terrible but it keeps the belle hop rather busy and sometimes things just et confused. Second, Laundry...Ok we were there on Fat Tuesday come on! We eneded up with a red alcohol stain on my shirt and on my date's (if you could call her that-I wish Yelp had a place to review dates cause buddy this one was a doozy!) white jacket. I had to send these articles down through the Valet Laundry to be washed. They either got misplaced or forgotten or something. I do not know really who to blame for that but I was leaving to go to Mexico the next day and needed those clothes. Well what happened next brought this hotel to above and beyond status. In an effort to make the situation right, The hotel operator named Jacque' (jackie) found a late night cleaner had them comew and get the clothes and then using her personal time and car drove my clothes to me at the terminal so I would have them. That is the mark of a Hotel staff that cares! I will be back-when? I dont know, but that alone deserves some sort of reward for the staff. Good Job guys!

This place NEVER disappoints! The last time we were there was about a week and a half ago to celebrate one of our daughters birthdays and it was great! Our server, Joseph, was fabulous. He was knowledgeable, pleasant, and provided great service.
This is one of the few places I'll eat a crab cake in St. Louis, the steaks are always prepared perfectly, the bisque is yummy, the lobster mac and cheese is so good - we've never had anything we didn't like! I'm not a wine drinker, but the rest of my family always finds something they like and I'm very happy with their cocktail menu! 
The portions are generous and we usually leave with some leftovers.  
We're usually there for three hours or so. The timing of our courses is never rushed and the service is always attentive without being too much.
I highly recommend J Gilbert's!

I wish that there was an option to not give them any stars. 
This is a horrible cab company that should actually shut down.
Yes, shut down!

I'm thoroughly convinced that the operators who answer the phone are trained to lie.
Lie about times. Lie about locations. Just lie!

I called two hours ahead of time and was then told that a car was assigned to me. When I called to get the status, the woman said that the driver was lost and took it upon himself to cancel. Yes, people -- cancel! Did they bother to let me know, absolutely not!

The manager then calls in a very sheepish voice -- obviously a gimmick to keep me around, to let me know that he will assign a new car to come in ten minutes. The ten minutes passed, still no car. 

I should have known to not go with this company and like an idiot, I did. 
Never again Victory Cab. Your new name should be Defeated Waste of Time. You have inconvienced me and caused me great trouble when all you had to was just tell the truth. 

Please do not call this company for anything, not even the time because they obviously have no idea how to tell it. 

My advice, if you're in Philly and need a cab, just walk!

Eaten here several times.  I like this place because the staff is friendly and inside the restaurant is not exposed to the terminal. That makes it a little more relaxing. Basic midwest bar food but good. Tables are roomy

Just spent 15 minutes standing at the gun counter without being acknowledged even with when finished with their one customer. Headed elsewhere to make my purchases. 

Mirrors last time I tried to by shoes. No one to help even get them down after searching literally the whole store to find someone to even ask.
Delicious! Ordered asada taco and tortilla soup . One of the best tortilla soups I've had, fyi it has meat.

Delicious! I love going to ice cream shops that make their own product and get creative with it. The person working the counter was nice and helpful in allowing us to try many flavors since this was our first trip here.  I had the creole cream cheese and steen's molasses and oatmeal cookie flavors.  My sister had the black and gold special flavor and my mom also had the creole cream cheese.  All the flavors I tried were great though! Including the pumpkin praline. Should've got three scoops.
Good pizza and great delivery.  Right on time.  I liked the eggplant parm pizza a lot.  The pepperoni was OK.  I'll definitely order from there again.

Came in just a few minutes ago looking for some crafting supplies and a porcelain tile for the wife. Chris over in Lumber by the cutting station was EXTREMELY informative and helpful (and funny!) He definitely gave top notch customer service. Afterwards, Amber, one of the self check-out clerks, was awesome and friendly and had a smile on her face! I cannot remember the name of the other clerk she was with but she was the same! Highly recommend this location!

The service is great and the staff are very friendly, but I was very disappointed in the serving sizes of the adult beverages. Most beer bars restrict serving sizes around 11% ABV, but anything over 8% gets served in an 8oz glass at the price of a pint. Their bloody mary's are  phenomenal... All 6oz of them. Finally, I understand that people love their pets, but restaurants are not the place for your little yorkie in a basket that you continue to feed under the table. If you disagree, this is the place for you. A service animal is one thing and completely acceptable, but be considerate of other patrons; this isn't Petsmart.

Hell yeah. The chicken kebab and the rice that came with it were totally delicious.

My only issue was that the service was a bit slow. It seemed like waiters and waitresses were walking past us over and over throughout the whole meal.

This place was really great. I met up with some friends here and we were all pretty impressed. The beer list was extensive, it had anything you could possibly want. 

They also have pretty good food. We all shared a pulled pork sandwich, a catfish po boy, and collard greens and everything was outstanding. The atmosphere was very relaxed, friendly, and it wasn't too crowded. I fully intend on returning here very soon!

Ingrid is THE BEST. She earned her title as "Waxing Queen". To keep it simple, the appointments are super quick (I schedule mine during my lunch hour and get back to work with time left), Ingrid keeps you calm and generally I'm jabbering too much to even get surprised by the wax. She's a total professional and I refuse to go to anyone else!
Zack is a great bartender and the atmosphere is chill. We preferred Harry's to Rum Runner on the same property.

Limoncello is one of our favorite restaurants in the Borough which has become a great little town over the years with lots of choices for food and drink.  We were there for our anniversary and had a great experiences as always.  This place is the perfect mix of local, variety of ages, casual, friendly and very excellent food.  This night I had the chef's salmon special.  OMG.  Seriously!  It was absolutely the most delicious salmon I have ever had.  Can't really say what the spices were but along with the crab topping it all worked to make my taste buds explode.  No, really they did.  The lady had a chees board to start things off and loved it very much.  Talks about it all the time.

Gotta love a place that knows what you want before you even ask. This is especially clutch when you're only half awake in the morning trying to get your day started with a tasty brew of Black Gold ASAP. It's even more impressive when you come down for your afternoon brace and they're already making your Americano.

Combine that great service and good coffee with some tasty desserts like their brownies, coffee cakes, carrot cakes, and cookies from 4th Street Deli, you've got a regular coffee spot you can rely on during a long week at work.

Thanks Passero's!

AH, Mr Pasta! Nick from Sallies is still in there and kicki'. I haven't been back in Wilmington for years but this week is my penance and graciously Nick's ravioli and meatball ...the HOLY GRAIL! Food is consistent with what I remembered from high school years ago. This is true, old school italian food, priced reasonably and served with a smile! And it looks like Nick's grandson is in the kitchen, carrying on this great italian tradition!  You go, Nick!

Once I found out about this place and heard that they had cheesecake stuffed snowballs, I knew I had to try it. Sure enough, their snowballs are delicious! I've tried the sno-la favorite and the oreo cheesecake flavors and I would highly recommend both! They are a little bit pricier than most snowball places but it is definitely worth it

3.5/5 but definitely worth checking out.

Came here for the first time last week for happy hour so we got to try a couple of items on their menu for half the price which is great!

Parking is ample during dinner. I haven't been here for lunch but when I came here for happy hour around 5pm, they had the whole parking lot to themselves in the back! That's what had stopped me from coming here before because I didn't realize they had a parking lot.

If you're here for happy hour, get the following: brussel sprouts, manchego cheese, mussels, and their potato. They're all very good but the best was the manchego cheese. A lot of reviewers say to get the brussel sprouts which is good but after awhile, you kind of get sick of it. It's too sweet or too salty - or too much. 

In terms of their drinks during happy hour, their draft beer list is longer than other places! Also, their margarita is STRONG and delicious! I also had their red sangria and that was really good as well.

Not a bad place. I would come back for their drinks!

Cozy restaurant, it had that modern day hipster speakeasy feel. Prepare to wait if you come anytime after 6pm.

The hostess helped us snag a spot at the back counter which was really nice of her.

The pickled beets were fantastic and the veggie burger was fresh and delicious. Service was as prompt as can be expected in a busy place like this. Prices were fair. Ambiance and location are perfect. Would come back anytime I'm in town!

Typical diner fare. Layout similar to most of the Philly and south jersey diners. Menu options were nice.

Went with the Roast port sandwich with broccoli rabe. They brought it without long hots which just wasn't going to work for me. Luckily they were able to get some for me and I did really enjoy the sandwich.
Food was average but I found it to be overpriced for the food and level of service. We went on a Sunday afternoon over the summer. Maybe we will try again sometime in the future.

We have enjoyed many three-star meals here, often before boarding a train. But today, we struck out. With 45 minutes for our meal, we were quickly seated and placed our order. And then...nothing. Our server disappeared without a trace. Other diners were seated, ordered, were served, ate and left. For us...nothing. A runner came with our check after 40 minutes, but no food.

When our 45 minutes were up, we got up to leave. As we passed the kitchen, our server reappeared with a couple of entrees - not our full order - in styrofoam "to go" packaging. No explanation, no apology, and sadly, no repeat business from us.

The tradition of HORRIBLE cars continues at Hertz....lots of mile, not clean inside or out, and reeking of smoke......seems to be a trend with Hertz.

After arriving in STL you have to walk outside and wait for the bus. When I walked up to the stop the driver was having a smoke, and we had to wait for him to finish. It is a short ride to the facility (under 5 min) and as stated the car was horrible. 

Also, even though they were not busy and I am a gold club member, the car was parked far away.

Upon return on the shuttle you have to make a drop off/pick-up from SWA, then you go to main terminal. Leave at least 10 minutes once you leave their place.

The car was cheap, and so was the experience.

1 day rental - 20.48
taxes a bunch

Total - $29.04

When I flew into Philadelphia and found out that my plane was coming into terminal F I was excited because I had been wanting to try the airport version of my favorite cheesesteak place: Tony Luke's! 

I hurried down and found it in the main food court area next to Chipotle. There were already a few people in line, but it took no time for me to reach the register and place my order. (Traditional cheesesteak with whiz and onions.) I opted for the 9 inch and would have gotten bigger if they had it available. The wait for a cheesesteak was approximately 8 minutes which I was told at the register. No problem.

I sat down and opened my cheesesteak and the steam and delicious smell poured out of the cheese paper! I was a bit disappointed to find my roll had been charred on top, but I dove in. The sandwich was almost as delicious as I remember from downtown. The steak was well seasoned and wonderful! The whiz and onions were on point! I give the Luke's downtown a 5/5 and for now this one is a 4/5. The guy next to me did not have a charred roll so I'm sure it was an accident. I'll try again in a few days!

Great new find for us! Huge menu! Something for everyone and can adapt to all dietary accommodations. I ordered the GF oval (oval shaped pizza) which was great and wife ordered pasta dish which was also nicely prepared. Would definitely return as great neighborhood find with friends and family.

Super chill environment, great coffee, great food. I love the cortado and the avocado toast with poached egg. Yum, yum. Parking, is a nightmare -- wish they could figure it out. Wanted to take friends & fam here when visiting, which I did, but we had to park a couple blocks away which can be sketchy and plus it's so HOT! Maybe open up another Tampa location, Buddy Brew??

After having some bad experience at other local cleaners in Saint Pete, I found this small family owned dry cleaners. They took extreme care in dry cleaning my high pile white shag rug, my $500 dollar faux fur throws, suits, expensive dresses, and daily men's works shirts. I have since moved to NYC and the had my fur throws ruined, that seaside took such great care with. Really missing them right now :(.

Ox tail pho made for a great meal and the crepe appetizer was a hit with the table. My gf got the crab and garlic noodles, but they were out of crab so they upgraded to the lobster at no extra cost. Turned out the lobster was fantastic! Only down sides were the duck was dry and touch and the taps were not yet installed, the taps will be up and running soon. Hopefully the duck prep will improve or change to something else...

Just returned from a disappointing brunch at osteria. The steak and eggs dish was a fatty piece of steak hidden under eggs so every bite was chewy.  Very unsettling when spending $38 on breakfast steak.  There was four of us at brunch and not one of us loved our food.  I do not usually write reviews, but this was such a bad experience I felt it was necessary.  If you want a good brunch go to Redstone. I have dined with friends for lunch and the food was so so.

Haha what!? Can't I Yelp this.  Yes 4 star I'm a fan.  I was walking along Bourbon St and there were these girls up in the front inviting me in.  At the time I didn't fully understand the check-in feature on the Yelp app so I checked in for the humor of letting my friends know where I was and how my road trip was doing but of course it was a secret check-in and no one saw it. More of a 3 star place ain't nothing wrong with that.  It's close to all the bars just in case you Yelpers that's doing the YSB need any UYE ideas.

Burger Up is our favorite restaurant. My wife and I eat there probably more than any other restaurant. We've always been to the 12 South location, but after seeing a movie at the Carmike Thoroughbred, we decided to try the Cool Springs Burger Up. 

To preface, I want to say the service, decor, and even the food, was all good. But...it wasn't the same as the 12 South Burger Up. The aioli had a bit of a corn syrup taste, and the Woodstock my wife and I shared had a tinge of a sloppy joe like taste. None of these made the food bad, but the same items at the 12 South location tasted more refined overall of a higher quality. That being said, the Cool Springs locations features some menu items not found in 12 South. We enjoyed the fried green beans, and if I weren't full from popcorn and soda from the movies, I would've loved to have tried a milkshake. 

TL;DR: Great vibe and decor, but the food just wasn't the same as the original location.
