To ice the cake I was complimenting the owner Kim on the vegan pho and she is super personable. Heart and belly full! Highly recommend.

This place is not somewhere i frequent because of the wait and parking challenges.  However, every time i go there i enjoy the food tremendously.  I often bring out of town friends because of the unique and high quality food.  It never disappoints.

It's a nice, local, neighborhood joint. Acts a kind of a neighborhood hub. Good cookies which is key, good sandwich's and I am told the soup is good too although I have never had it. Breakfast or lunch, you're good either way.

Beautiful building! Restored historic train depot (with the safe in the men's restroom.) Beers are good and the food is gastropub fare. Service was excellent ! (Adequate parking in the back.) Started with four tasters which led to a full glass of their Belgian Dubbel. I paired it with a Rueben sandwich. Nice food and beer experience!

RKO is a fun, tiny, neighborhood comics & video store. They don't have a huge selection of comics, but they have a really nice breadth of things- and they're happy to order anything you would like that they're missing. All of the staff are extremely knowledgeable about comics, graphic novels, and the merchandise as well as stuff that RKO doesn't have in stock. 

Their movie selection is actually larger than their comic selection, or so it seems. And their pricing scheme is great- you pay by the night, not by the disc, which is fantastic if you're renting a TV season, for example. They're not really where you go for odd things, but if you live down here, it's fun and easy and a really good deal, and service with a smile!

The best part of RKO South, though, might have to be the artwork. They exhibit different artists, one at a time, and they're all local. They have openings for the different exhibits, where you can meet the artists, see the work, and have fun. Their choices so far have been slightly off-beat, and really interesting.

Got a great deal on the GMC 1/2 ton but their man who aligned my front end made a mess out my tires. I assumed they checked the front end alignment before I took possession of my 2011 GMC 1/2 ton, then again around 10 - 12000 i noticed the edges were wearing. They said it was out of warranty and had to pay $80. 7 to 10k later and the tires were wearing on the opposite side - they realigned it and at 26780 miles the inside edges are gone. I normally get 50k to 60k on a set of tires

805 ink artist Ken Knox created such bad vibe in the shop that he made me uncomfortable to the point that I did not even want to get a tattoo by him. He was condescending when I first presented him with a picture of my idea, when he drew it it didn't resemble the type of art I wanted and I showed a picture of what I was picturing. Bad customer service and bad attitude. I believe that getting a tattoo is 50% experience, 50% artwork. Both of which made me feel uncomfortable that I didn't agree with HIS art. The rest of he crew at 805 Ink(such as J.J.) was so cool and helpful when discussing what I wanted. Knox ruined the vibe of the whole experience.
Service was terrible, took about 20 minutes to get our drinks and another 40 for our food, which we ordered at the same time. Food was mediocre at best. Will never be coming back.

We came to Ricardo's on a Thursday evening and it was pretty quiet. The hostess seated us quickly but we figured that there would be problems pretty quickly when the waiter didn't come check in with us for about ten minutes. 
The food was good. Not incredible but good sized portions and tasty but the service was terrible. The entire night was plagued by the absence of our waiter and when he did come by, he was extremely aloof.

They have some tasty burgers! Their burger burrito abomination is actually really good as well! I would have loved if they had fries as well, but that would be a bit hard. I even got a free meal when they found out it was my birthday!

After reading the reviews and given my search for a new salon, I thought I'd give them a try.  I walked in for a mani and was immediately seated.  As one attendant begun to remove my polish another client entered.  My attendant was directed to that client.  Someone else came to complete my polish removal.  Then I sat...for 30 minutes awaiting my manicure as seven other people came in and were service promptly.   When the attendant came she apologized for the wait but in the middle of my polish left to set up an appointment.   For a basic manicure it took me 60 minutes.  Clearly this is not the place for walk ins and it's not my new nail salon.  The search will continue

Quiet and quant atmosphere with fresh cold beverages as well as a variety of coffees to eat with assorted pastries. Did not have any of the lunch items but plenty of vegetarian options along with the normal French brunch choices Cafe Simeon offers. Nice seating outside as well as inside. I sat in a comfortable fabric cushioned chair in the corner and observed the sweet waitress work tirelessly with a genuine smile on her face. Pastry was very light and airy with the perfect hazelnut stuffed inside. Very nice place to visit in St. Pete Beach.

This restaurant serves possibly the best crepe i've ever had.  The apple rum and chocolate crepe is so sweetly refined, and I haven't even tried the one with spinach which I hear is awesome.

This was my first and won't be my last visit to Ghini's.  I had the opportunity to try the Provencale Eggs which was a perfect meal for the morning.  Dressed in thyme and served with a delicious baguette, I felt so spoiled!  

As for the Baguette Bakery, I tried a few of the desserts- I am not too fond of the Princess.  The Parisbrest has a creme inside of it that is almost like ice cream.  The Almond truffle in which I split with a friend was a little bit of a let down, but was still good.

Come stop in for a warm meal, you won't be disappointed!

The mood café is a  cozy place on Baltimore avenue providing delectable tasty dishes and my favorite Lassies. There are over 50 different lassie favors. I visit the mood café several times a week every week. The owner Hassan is a remarkable gentleman that takes great pride in his business. He makes an awesome chatt and puts the same awesome love and effort into the next persons  order for a lassie or chatt dish. This place is very well know, the line that I run into on most visits speaks that truth for itself. Pina Colada, Guava Red Watermelon, Apple Banana, Honey, Peanut butter banana, Peaches & Cream and the list goes on, they are all delicious, delicious, delicious.  I am nowhere near done having all the lassies that are offered. The mood café offers awesome service from a very warm and personable owner and great lassies and chatt, I am so glad this place exit, I LOVE IT.

I went to Zorba's with moderate hopes, however I was extremely disappointed. Our waitress was awful. We waited 15 minutes after being seated to get our glasses of water and menus. She was very disrespectful over-all even when and after we ordered. When they brought out our wine glasses (BYOB) they gave us dirty glasses, it still had someones lipstick on it. When she put it down she said "Here this one is clean, it's just out" well I hope it's clean! 6 hours later I have actual food poisoning. I would never recommend this place, not even to someone I didn't like. It's poor service, unclean and food that will make you really ill.

Prices were OK, but I would rather pay a little more to get food (sandwiches) within an hour.  The food was sub-par.  I ordered their fish sandwich and, after an hour, I got a poor quality piece of fish that was still swimming (in grease).   I waited all that time and couldn't even eat my food.

Love love love TJs! They have so many yummy things you simply can't find anywhere else. On my last visit, my favorite buys were the Cowboy Caviar and as usual, the Charles Shaw wine. At $4 a bottle, you can't beat it! You can also buy sprouted Ezekiel bread here which is usually a hard find. Produce is pretty cheap here and the staff is always extremely helpful and friendly. They also have really pretty Calla Lillies for sale outside (my favorites)! I've never had a bad experience at TJs.

I needed to scan and email a copy of my son's diploma (it was too big for my scanner). Called FedEx and was told that while they don't email they could put it on a flash drive. I didn't have a flash drive so they said they could sell me one starting at $6.99. I was in a hurry so I asked how long it would take. I was told if it is just one item they could do it right away. Jumped in car and drove down only to be told by a lazy rude girl that it would take at least 30 mins. Of course the girl I spoke with just 5 mins earlier was on break. Spoke to manager who said he would have words with his employee. Big deal..and I'm really sure he did. If the girl had just told me it could take up to 30 mins. I would have been fine with that. I just really hate having my time wasted by inept people. I went across the street to the UPS store on Calle Real. They scanned and emailed it..bam..5 mins and $4.00 later the simple job was done. I will never go back to that FedEx again. I would rather drive further to the next location if I have to.
Cozy atmosphere. Great Happy Hour specials. Strong Margaritas and amazing tacos. Must try Guac and chips!

We decided to go here on a whim, when we couldn't decide where to eat one night and remembered this place had opened recently. Overall, we were not impressed. The menu is set up in a small plates style and they do not have any options besides the 4, 5, or 6 item choices. I would've rather had a significant portion of something really good, than small portions of 4 average dishes.
It's clear that the chef thinks he/she is a little more advanced than they actually are, dishes were more complicated than a lot of places but did not taste as good. We go out to eat at many nice restaurants and have absolutely no issue paying good money for good food, however $35 for the four selection menu was not worth it in quality or quantity. 
They did offer complimentary sangria or Victory beer (two types) which was nice as it is a byob restaurant. The desserts were great and the highlight of the meal, the rest of it was just OK. Service was great, definitely attentive and friendly.
They are also cash only, and while I understand some small businesses do this, when the MINIMUM price for two people to come eat is $75+tip, I think you need to be more accommodating as many people don't carry that much cash. 
With some menu changes to allow ordering of individual selections, and some simplifying of dishes, this place could do quite well.
Always a great experience, friendly folks, good for date night. Decent wine and beer prices.

This a great neighborhood spot with a wide variety of great food.  I really enjoy the specials, mainly because they change frequently and there are tons of them.  They often post the specials online via Twitter and Facebook.  If you go surrounding peak hours (I usually go at opening 11am or after 1pm for lunch) there's no problem getting seated right away.  They also have nice outdoor seating with fans that really isn't bad on a cloudy summer day (still a little too hot for a sunny one).

The staff is friendly and consistent.  Our waitress kind of flaked one day and didn't put in something we needed to go for someone at home and didn't even acknowledge that I should have had a salad with my entree (I forgot if it said it came with one on the menu so I thought maybe I was crazy, but the receipt said "no salad dressing" on it so she obviously saw it in the POS and let it go that she didn't bring it out).  Other than that, we've had great service. 

My favorites so far are probably the Huling's Chicken Club and their thick cut catfish-- it is always light and fluffy with a great batter.  I have yet to be back for brunch, but I am always trying new dishes so I'm sure I will have many many more favorites here.  Definitely try out this great Mid-City restaurant!

The worst hair cut of my life. Extremely nice staff though, but lets be realistic, we do not go to the salon to chat and be friendly. I am sorry, I don't want to be mean, but please learn from my experience. It's like going to super cuts and paying 4X the price.

Where do I start... The prices were outrageous! But I guess it's expected if you're on Canal. The fish had more skin and than meat. Too much batter... Fries tasted as if they were sitting under a heated all day. The chicken was average. Popeyes chicken has more season and quality chicken. The bartender was cool! We ordered 2 meals and 2 drinks.Let's just say it wasn't worth $45.00.

I was impressed. I was expecting another Whole Foods or Trader Joe's style store. Nope - much better!

It is a nice clean store with tons of fresh produce. They have lots of organic items, gluten-free items, a nice ethnic aisle, and the biggest variety of vegan products I've seen in any store.  Everything had great prices, and while there were some South American produce items, much of it was USA.  I got a fresh bunch of asparagus for $1.02, whereas the price in a conventional grocery store is usually $3.99 or higher!  Broccoli Crowns were $0.69/lb and were super fresh. 

They have a pretty good size meat selection including grass-fed beef and free-range chicken, and in the frozen meat section even had items like bison and elk. They had several fresh grab-and-go items ranging from chopped chicken breast and sliced turkey, to pre-made meals like roast beef, gravy and potatoes or chicken and pasta with a basil pesto sauce, salads and pre-made sandwiches. They had hot soup and tons of various breads. 

Many of their private-label items carried the Non-GMO Project Verified too. I'm sure I missed a lot, it was crowded so it was hard to be able to just stand and look at things closely.  

Parking is fairly easy (not a nightmare like at Trader Joes) as it sits in a large shopping center.  I definitely liked it better than TJs because of all of the fresh produce, and I think it even beats Whole Foods for variety.  It was easily the most popular section aside from the fresh-made sandwich counter.

My only complaint was the headache of getting some crushed ice to pack my cold items in for the long drive home. Whole Foods has a bin full of pre-made packages you can grab on the way out, but when I asked the cashier if they had any, she said I could buy some from the ice cooler. I mentioned WF gives it away for free and she said I could ask at the meat counter.  So after I paid, I had to go all the way back to the opposite side of the store where the meat counter had a huge line. I barged in at the sushi area and found someone to help me.  I hate barging in but I already had paid and had all these bags in my cart with cold items warming up quickly.

Now if only we could get more of these in the area!  We need something out in the East Tampa/Brandon area.  Sprouts, hear our plea!!!

Pure Design created the most beautiful bouquets for my August wedding, and on short notice! I called the shop a few days before a major holiday and less than two months before my wedding, and Michael was able to meet with me within 48 hours. After showing him a few photos from Pinterest, he was able to put together a look that was exactly what I was going for, and (most importantly) within my budget. I'm so pleased with how our bouquets turned out, and I would highly recommend Pure to other brides.
Fantastic Miso, great drinks, nice selection of Japanese beers, so very many excellent specialty rolls, and I adore the Yellowtail Collar (Hamachi Kama) so much that I often order two!

This place is not authentic Peruvian food and there is no space between the tables. It's a very small hole in the wall. The hostess is very rude and the food prices are redickulous.  I would not recommend this place.
Everything we ate here was splendid. The pastries were flaky and buttery! I honestly think 5 stars is an understatement. We loved it so much we had to come back for more!

I stayed here opening week for a conference and was very impressed with both the facilities as well as the staff here.

To say the staff was friendly and helpful would be an understatement.  Staff were just about everywhere to help you locate things whether it be the fitness center or conference room facilities.  At certain times during the day they'd actually walk around offering you mimosa's or champagne.  As an example, the first morning of my visit when I got off the elevator in the lobby there were no less than 5 staff members offering me a morning mimosa to start my day :)

The facilities are beautiful.  The beds are EXTREMELY comfortable and soft.  TVs are digitally delicious.  Hotel rooms have wifi available.

The hotel was both an Italian restaurant,  a sports bar (High Velocity) as well as a bar/lounge next to the lobby.

A small computing center is available in the lobby for folks to print out airport boarding passes.

The conference rooms here excellent:  large, comfortable and well stocked with A/V equipment and refreshments a plenty.  Conference food was well catered and delicious.  Absolutely no complaints here!

A full pool as well as fitness center (easily rivaling any local Y or 24-Hour Fitness in sheer amount of free weights, weight machines and cardio equipment) is also available on site.

Centrally located in the heart of downtown Indy you are also in walking distance to sporting venues (Victory Field, Conseco Fieldhouse, etc), cultural sites (State Museum, Art Museum, Historical Society, NCAA Musuem)  the Convention Center and many of Indy's other fine establishments.

The comfort of the facility and friendliness of the staff at the JW Marriott in Indianapolis will make your stay  in Indy a great one!

Refreshing classy joint in this area :) it's not cheap, but it also doesn't feel cheap. The French 75 (or something like that) is made SUPER well
& the whole vibe is a bit upscale & quiet. I thoroughly enjoyed this place, even though we didn't stay too long. It's a very welcome change to the French quarter madness!

Eh. They seemed to have a lot of cool stuff if you're willing to sort through the junk. What I didn't like is that they made me check my shopping bag (I had just purchased something at a nearby store) while I shopped. I get their reasoning for it (hello, thievery) but it was still a bit annoying. 

They had some cool antique map pages I was considering buying but did not. I like antique stores and overall this one was okay.
Happy Hour from 3-6pm. If you love oysters this is the place for that at 50 cents a piece with half off on selected alcoholic beverages.

Having never been to Buffalo Exchange, my friends and I headed straight here with a mission, to find a cute dress!

Luckily for all three of us, we hit the jackpot and found dresses we liked!

It took us a while to dig and sort through but it was a wonderful bonding experience, shopping and trying on clothes! One of the most girly things to do. I hardly get a chance to see them so it was a lot of fun just trying things on and getting opinions. The sales associates there were super nice and they were not pushy at all. 

We all walked away with an outfit or two or four from this place. This place is totally awesome! 

I also love the fact that if you don't take a bag to hold your clothes, you get a token to donate 5 cents to one of three charities. I fully approve of charity work and I approve of Buffalo Exchange in NOLA!

If you're looking for an astute, high-end tea place for loose-leaf tea, this is a well sought out crown jewel!! Having been a GM at Teavana at the Fashion Mall over 3 years ago, 'TeaBuds' falls in the heart of the light and nowhere short in comparison for much less! The ambience is superb, very quaint, with a delightful and very comprehendible tea wall with glass sample jars for visual appeal and aroma wofting!  They also have an assortment of samples for tasting! If you want an experience of an elite, loose-leaf tea company w/o the corporate conveyor belt-like sales pitches, then TeaBuds is the only place you want to go! They couldn't be in a more appropriate location and yet have access to the best sources available! Who says you can't 'Tea-off' in the winter?! Enjoy!!!!

FlavorDave

Located in a three story brick building at Fourth St., The Depot is a place to hangout with friends for drinks and food. They have a variety of beer they brew; pale ale, stout, saison, IPA, pilsner, just to name a few as well as a distillery for whiskeys.

Hands down, my favorite donuts in St.Louis!I'm never disappointed! They are open late enough on weekends to satisfy my late night craving! 
They have a great neon sign out front, pointing you in the right direction! Yes, you are at the right place! 
The lady behind the counter might not smile, but i don't feel unwelcome! 
There's a good variety of donuts, and the prices are low! 
Don't forget cash, there's a $10 minimum on cards! 
Go late night, you will most likely get a hot fresh donut! 
My favorites: 
chocolate cake with fudge icing- soft moist cake with more chocolate on top, you can't go wrong, and when its fresh, you get a slight crispness around the edge. 
Apple fritter- oh my goodness, if you can have this hot and fresh, it only adds to the apple cinnamon soft pillowy delight you are about to devour! 
BONUS, they have donut holes!!!
Now stop reading this, and GO!

I ended up here kind of by accident, or maybe it was divine intervention. It's a very quaint family owned & operated restaurant. Our waiter Christian was superb, his recommendations and hospitality was top notch. His father and the rest of the staff were great. We started with garlic bread brunette (which was a special order & it turned out perfectly). Then we had the seafood bisque which was very hearty and tasty. It was a perfect dip for our table bread. My friend had the meatball salad which looked good, I didn't try it because don't eat pork but he enjoyed it. For our entrees I had the salmon w: asparagus, I prefer a lil more seasoning, but it was ok. He had the filet topped with crab meat. The crab meat was delicious & his side of mashed potatoes and veggies were very tasty, well seasoned and everything was heated to perfection. They even made a Marsala sauce from scratch for my friend. This all def be added to our re-visit list!

As an out-of-towner who masquerades as a stodgy professional but secretly (even not-so-secretly) loves going to metal and indie rock shows, I was very happy when the tour bus made its "French Market" stop just across the street from Envie.  I was all like "Yay!  A real coffeehouse!"  Not that I don't love the cafe au lait at the Cafe Du Monde, it's just that those people who some jackass referred to as "gutter punks" (and their indoor counterparts, old activist hippies with ponytails reading free papers and writing in notebooks) are to me the signs of a GOOD LOCAL COFFEEHOUSE, a sight for my sore tourist-infested eyes.  

The counter girl was very cute and very nice and I immediately ordered a vegetarian panini (I'm not vegetarian, I just like veggie sammitches) and two of the huge cookies that weigh like a pound a piece.  They turned out to be underdone on the inside so if you like raw cookie dough you will love those.  My biggest problem with Envie was choosing an iced tea.  I was curious about the Blue Eyes but they also had my favorite, peach, so I went with that.  I may find myself walking 12 blocks back up there tomorrow morning at 8 am to try the Blue Eyes.  

Did I mention that it's in a gorgeous old bar with comfy booths, a beautifully tiled floor, big windows open to the outside, and My Morning Jacket was playing full blast?  And I didn't see one single person with their face in their laptop.  (Not that I would have minded, I have my face in my laptop enough.)  

No hataz here.  I like Envie.  Already recommended it to two of my friends who are visiting soon, because if I don't, it's highly likely they won't make it all the way past the French Market and Decatur to discover that it exists. So there ya go.

I find that neither the glowing reviews or the hardened pans of this place are not quite accurate.  I had Basil Spice last night and, while not the best Thai meal I've ever had, it was quite good.  

I always get a kick out Yelp reviews, citing either the BEST or the WORST of one thing that they've ever had.  I'm not much for hyberbole so I'll simply recommend Basil Spice as a good place to get a bite to eat.  It's simple, cheap and tasty.  The service is prompt and friendly as well.  

The spring rolls were very good, the dish that I had was very good.  My only complaint would be that I can't imagine how a place can have bad water in St. Louis.  The water had a metallic taste to it which I really don't get.  St. Louis is known as having the countries best tap water!  

Regardless.  Good solid place to eat.  Nothing special, but I'd go again.

I'm addicted to clothes! And the store are super chic and they have an amazing stuff the prices though are expensive so if you are student you can't really afford most of the things. 
Lovely store but pricy
Food looks beautiful but not a lot of taste. Good house Malbec $7.
Pretty good surf/Caribbean themed place.  Had the blackened fish tacos which were great.
Not very interesting or good. Everything we had ranged from disappointing to just okay.

Not worth all the hype !! Small portions .. Pasta dishes with no meat .. Small menu choices ... Very noisy very small place .. The only thing worth getting were the Cinnamon sugar Zeppoli dessert ! Wouldn't go back ! Try Il Fiore down the street !! U won't be disappointed !! Fab food !! Nice portions !!

COFFEE!  'Nough Said.  Glorious, smooth, kick your ass awake, creamy cafe con leche.  With a cinnamon sprinkle.  Luscious.  Cheaper and better than starbucks, ANYDAY.  Coffee.  Whatever the question, COFFEE is the answer.

Everything I got was delicious! Needed to get some soup after a long night and decided to come here. The braised need noodle soup was delicious! I loved their noodles. We also got the tofu and calamari, both were great as well!

Don't purchase clearomizers from them.

Wherever they get the clearomizers from, there is zero quality control.  6 out of 15 clearomizers that I've purchased from them were defective straight from the package.  At $6.50 a pop, it's not a huge issue to start with but it starts to add up fast when it happens every single order.  And they won't give you a refund!  

I told them about it the first time, simply thinking it was a bad batch or whatever, but every single order after that the same thing happened.   I asked if they would have staff inspect them prior to shipping, and was told (essentially) to go eff myself.  After my third order now with defective clearomizers, I've had enough.  I contacted them (thinking maybe they just weren't aware), and they don't care.  They'll keep on selling them, and couldn't give a crap about quality.

Also, give them a fake email address if you order anything!  Each order results in FIVE emails, plus a bunch of spam.

Bring any of this up and they'll ignore any constructive feedback and simply insist that they are awesome.  

Going elsewhere.

The food--chicken pho, beef/brisket pho, and some summer rolls--was solid, what might be expected from a four-star reviewed restaurant. The service was some of the worst I've ever experienced: we were seated after another couple walked in behind us, given dirty water glasses, and left unattended for the majority of our stay. We saw several tables around us stuck without food and/or receiving the wrong order multiple times. 

The waitstaff was more than incompetent they were rude at different points of service. (The hostess turned several groups of people away for both eat-in and takeout orders, one waiter told a friend not to eat there right in front of us, another couple of waiters discussed a table's food right in front of them as if they were not there). I've never felt so uncomfortable at a restaurant.

Came here on a Friday night.  There appears to be only one waitress, so service was extremely slow.  She was also kinda rude.  It took almost an hour to get our food.  Tasted very good though.  You can hear the gokarts next door.

Great happy hour special with margaritas. The food is more southwestern than Mexican, which surprised me the first time. The piggy wings are good and huge. An order could be a full meal. The signature sandwich with barbecue pork, Mac and cheese, and some other stuff came out soggy and somewhat wilted. Guacamole is adequate but nothing I'd ever crave.
There's nice outdoor picnic-style seating and a good atmosphere.
I'd recommend happy hour here or an afternoon drink, especially if you live in the neighborhood.

Food was good, service was ok. I wouldn't call it spectacular yet but this was only my first trip.

I had the Black & Blue burger because on a quick glance a few Yelpers had said it was good.  What is the point of having sauteed onions AND raw red onions on a burger? The red was overpowering and it was the only thing I could taste. Where was the blue cheese? Couldn't taste that either. Tater Tots as a side were a nice novelty instead of fries. They've got a great selection of beers and mild selection of decently priced scotch/whiskey. I had the apple crumble for dessert and it was good too. I guess I'm spoiled from the Caramel Apple Tartlets from Omaha Steaks though.

Major downside though and I'm not used to this because I'm not from Florida: the outdoor patio is for smoking CIGARS. My clothes stink and my throat hurts from being surrounded by stank sticks. Next time I'll dine inside and try something else.

Let me start off by saying that I love this place. We dropped by here yesterday.  I always get the Bibimap and they make a delicious one with brown rice.  Only complaint is the very small amount of meat they give you with it.   If they fix that then they will have the best Bibimap in the city in my books.
Great place with a huge fish tank. My son swam with the fishes. The restaurant was beautiful and the staff was professional and the food was fantastic.

The waitress was friendly and efficient. The home made potato chips were the best part of the meal. My margarita was lacking in flavor, but my friend said hers was good. My sandwich was a disappointment as there was a lack of flavor. The pork was large chunks, not pulled, and the brisket dry. The sausage didn't look like it had been grilled. Kept putting bbq sauce on for flavor and moisture. The outdoor fire pit had a  layer of cigarette butts, but no appearance of a recent fire. The saguaro rib ceiling lent to the southwest interior.  There are dining tables outdoors that looked inviting. The aroma of mesquite for the bbq was expected but not there. My friend's pork sandwich lacked flavor also. She mentioned that the ladies room needed attention also.

This is my first visit in their "new location" (it's been awhile). The front porch was a wonderful place for brunch. There wasn't a lot of room but it was enough that you didn't feel obligated to participate in your neighbors conversation. Unfortunately they were out of espresso (!) but the standard coffee was more than fine and the attentive server kept my cup full. I had Mama's eggs - because: avocado. It was a generous serving that I didn't even finish. The grilled chicken sandwich was also very large but was devoured quickly! The side of fruit was fresh and not the standard melon variety. The salmon salad has a large piece of salmon on top and the server had no problem with a few substitutions that were all taken care of when the salad was served. The server kept the ice tea and water glasses full. It was a reasonable price for an above average meal.

on our staycation at the beach decided to go here for our one nice dinner out. I had heard good things about it and was eager to try it.

Arrived at 7:00 on a Friday night and got a cozy table for two. The décor is Mediterranean , dimly lit and cozy. This night they had an excellent acoustic guitar player entertaining. 

We started with a cocktail, beer for him, tequila martini for me, while we perused the wine list. Ended up with a decent bottle of Santori Amarone ($85) which was quite good. 

Started with the pate platter which come out with two nice slices of pate and all the accoutrements.  ($9.00) I love pate and this did not disappoint.

We also tried the special tuna trio of the night, a smoked tuna spread on crostini, tuna sashimi and tuna crudo. All very good and fresh although the spread was just kind of a glammed up tuna salad. 

For dinner, after much debate, we went with the Paella for him and the Beef Shortribs for me. The Paella ($29) . we requested it to be crispy (as a true paella should be) and the chef obliged. Unfortunately it made the Paella so dry and overcooked it was not good at all. The shortribs, ($26) with a cabernet barbque sauce was very good. Served with a mini au gratin and fresh asparagus. The ribs were nice and tender 
, the sauce was almost bordering on overdone, almost but not quite. 

For dessert we ordered our fav limencello cake, it was good, but not as good as the craft in St Pete . Ended up at the bar for a couple glasses of Port to quell our dessert craving and get a chance to listen to the guitarist. 

While at the bar we were speaking of our dinners and before you knew it Chef Karim came out to speak with us, apologized for the Paella and told us next time we come in to ask for him personally so he can take care of us. 

You can tell he's a chef/owner that really cares about his clientel. He checked one very table and knew many patrons by their names.

I'll go back, and try his famous tangine or duck, after I ask for him personally!

Have been coming here for over 2 years.  Donuts are always fresh.  The staff is always courteous and friendly.  Today the young man waiting on me noticed I was an Iraq Vet.  In honor of my service he wanted to let me have my dozen of donuts at no cost.  I felt uncomfortable not paying anything so we worked out a deal instead.  I was very moved that this young man would take the time not only to recognize a Veteran but make such a generous offer.  I served 30 years in the United States Air Force.  God blessed and protected me those 30 years.  I have had the honor to serve with many not as fortunate as I.  Donut Drive - In thanks for making my day.  St Louis really does appreciate Veterans.
Great place to have breakfast! Enjoyed the seeded avocado on my plate with the frittata. Nice big cups of coffee. Great selection of food items. Can't wait to go back again.

Often times we go to particular places for one thing or the other, and I don't know about you....but customer service is EVERYTHING.  I understand you want to know about...IS THE FOOD GOOD BRUH...is it worth my drive....and TRUST ME when I get to that....you'll gas up and get there.  

As I was saying....CUSTOMER SERVICE IS EVERYTHING.  I scheduled a business meeting there at lunch not having been to this establishment and many people I know hadn't been to this place to give a heads-up so allow me to tell you....THE CUSTOMER SERVICE WAS NOTHING SHORT OF 5 STAR at LUNCH!   Both hosts were recent graduates of h.s., one on his way to SEMO.   They were well versed on the menu, the specials, the lay out, and you knew from the moment they opened their mouths to the moment you sat down after them having carried your tray, and retrieved your beverage of choice...THEY WERE HIRED TO SERVE YOU, and that they did with excellence and pride in what they did.   

I know....where is this place....and why haven't I heard about it.....well had it not been for my travel through the 170 corridor, and then catching a super late at night (early a.m.) advertisement I wouldn't have known about this SOUL FOOD GEM!  I know...there are a few spots that BOAST, but this isn't one that does, but once you GO, EAT, and ENJOY it will easily become your FAVORITE.   I didn't visit the restroom areas, but if it was anything like the front of house (clean as the dept of health....white glove military clean...) and the dining area.....I'd believe you if you said you could eat off the toilet seat it was that clean.  NOW ON TO THE FOOD:

The had some very tempting choices, and almost exhaustive (The WIDOWMAKER, SHRIMP PO'BOY and the TRIPLE  DECKER CLUB) were amongst the heavy hitters as far as sales go.   I personally wanted a good crispy tripe sandwich, but the manager (who hadn't tried it...) said I'd order from the table first if I were you.  Which was her way of encouraging me to order from the steam table that offered liver and onions, smother pork chops, fried chicken, smothered fried chicken, meatloaf as entrees, then followed by sides such as green beans, sweet potatoes, mashed potatoes, mac n cheese, cabbage, black eyed peas, and few other mentionables.   The WAY BACK WEDNESDAY special was an entree with two sides and I cautiously proceeded ahead.   I had the meatloaf, cabbage, and mac n cheese there were accompanied by cornbread muffin. 

MEATLOAF was more than enough, and I'd guess it was 5-6oz of a thick slice wonderfully tasty monolithic masterpiece of juicy, well seasoned beef with some green peppers, onions throughout.  It has house made tasty gravy over it that didn't over-power it, but complimented it.  I actually and eventually ended up mixing it ( the meatloaf and gravy with my mac n cheese).  Now I must tell you this meat loaf didn't have the traditional layer of baked on ketchup or tomato paste to top it....and honestly it didn't need it at all.  

MAC N CHEESE - This is look a mix of grandmas home made mac n cheese that was made by CHESTER CHEETAH.  Let me explain:  most home made macs have that baked crust that sometimes...often times....has areas of burns that we just chalk it up to the mac game, and it's still edible.  Other times home made macs are so cheesy that they are soupy and you'd have to bake them in a crematory before you get a crust.  This mac n cheese was a mix of golden yellow and orange deliciousness.  I'd err on the side of caution of one of the BEST if not THE BEST SOUL FOOD MACS in our area  ( I do have a favorite MAC...and it's from of all places a BBQ joint in the loop....UNTOUCHABLE) ...it paired well with my meatloaf and gravy for sure. 

FRIED CABBAGE:  Just like my grandmama or my momma, or I make....straight from the south.   It wasn't terribly overcooked but tender and flavorful.   A hint of salt, pepper, garlic...( I believe it even had some cayenne pepper flakes that gave it a nice kick) and possible in a light chicken stock broth.  Had I not been on this diet I would've had to take the corn bread (sweet I might add) and mix it up in my cabbage,unbuckle my belt, kick off my shoes....and call it a done deal!  

 My only negatives are be cognizant of your clientele with music volume.....you may want to turn it down 1-2 notches so they can enjoy your food, the establishment, and one another without having to talk over or louder than the background music, and  I wanted to speak to the owner (as well as my constituent did too) to simply behold the owner of this gem.  TRUST I WILL BE BACK, and will tell others of the wonderful experience we had.  We don't have a place like this in St. Charles County and if you're looking for, or considering a second location...I'd highly encourage you to head WEST ON 70, so we can bless you! Until then....I make it back I have a date with a CRISPY FRIED TRIPE SANDWICH.  

GOD BLESS YOU ALL, and thank you for your memorable service/experience.

We have been to BnF many times since my last review. It is our absolute favorite go to place. We love everything on the menu especially the sushi. YOU HAVE to try the fried cod and the Seafood Burger. Our favorites. Go. Just go.

Their lunch buffet is a great introduction to Indian food for those who have never had it or are afraid to try it. I've never liked Indian food in the past, but with the buffet I'm able to try a tiny bit of everything to see what I like. It's also a great price for what you're getting.
Yummm so fast and great service!!! prime rib/ribeye place to go for something yummi and FAST!!

Ummm, not so good.    I had the prime rib on Friday and it was medium-well done and I ordered rare.  My boyfriend said his barbecued pork, from the pork dinner, looked liked the cook staff pulled pork off of a pig as it ran through their kitchen -  unappetizing to look at but good.  Thanks to the reviewer who suggested trying a sample of all four sauces. We had the bloomin' onion which was very good, as were our side dishes.  

The place is stuffy, poorly air-conditioned, and the building is old.  The wait staff were friendly, helpful, and attentive.  The place was almost full so maybe I expect too much BUT I think the cut of meat you order should come how you order it AND be appetizing to look at as well.

And they don't even sell beer.  Barbecue without beer?  That's just wrong!

How can you not love this type of food? I wasn't sure about the location but I was wrong this place is great, clean and tons of food many different people will enjoy. Try them out on a weekday so you can enjoy the time.

Cold beer, great service... Good food.... Comfortable environment.....Was passing through Philadelphia on Amtrak.... Stopped into Slainte....Very happy....Nice staff, good prices....Safe location.....Bravo !

What a great unique place. My sister took me here and I loved it. The bites were inventive, the wine selection was great and the staff knowledgeable and helpful. If I still lived here I would be a regular.

Pulled in here around 1pm after a visit to the Brandywine museum. There were no cars in the parking lot and it looked dark inside. We were traveling on a long trip with our dogs, so I took the dogs out to use the bathroom while my boyfriend checked the hours on his phone. A car circled around me while I was walking the dogs around the empty parking lot, repeating multiple times that I needed to pick up after them, this was a public restaurant. I said we were there to eat but it looked closed, and of course I have bags for my dogs. The woman in the car said "no, we're open." I was so taken aback by the exchange that I got back in the car and we drove away. My boyfriend said he checked the hours online, and they weren't open until 4! The woman in the car, who worked at the restaurant, was accusatory and rude. We would have loved to dine here as it looked cute and cozy, but she ruined the experience for us, and for some reason lied about being open. I hope this was an isolated incident and not how they conduct business otherwise.

Nashville doesn't have a lot of international markets. 

I love diverse and ethnic food. My husband is Peruvian and in order to make his traditional dishes we need things like Aji Amarillo, Aji Panca or other classic Peruvian specialties. There is a lot you can find at this store - whether you need Chinese, Mexican, Asian, Japenese or anything in-between. Its a great store to pick  up canned or packaged products. 

With saying that, I would warn on the quality of meats or seafood. We typically get tripe at different stores, and the tripe there was frozen and yellow. I have seen packages of beef look extremely brown or fish smell. Even a lot of the shellfish is completely opened up or dead, which shows the conditions for keeping it fresh aren't up to standard.

I saw the Creole Creamery on the Food Network's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives and knew I had to try it whenever I visited New Orleans. It did not disappoint. It is as good as any ice cream I have tasted. It features some unique flavors. There are a couple of samplers, 4 mini scoops for $4.50 or 6 mini scoops for $6, so that you can try a few flavors. Despite the name, the mini scoops are regular size scoops. I tried the cookie monster, café au lait, lavender honey, and black and gold crunch. The café au lait and black and gold crunch are my favorites. The black and gold crunch honors the colors of the New Orleans Saints. It is comprised of French vanilla & chicory root w/ Oreos & chocolate chips. It is as delicious as it looks and sounds. Moreover, I saw the "Skyscraper" featured on the Food Network. In a tall glass, it contains cookies & cream, chocolate and vanilla layered with caramel, hot fudge and crushed oreos served with whipped cream, sprinkles, a cherry, and a wafer. It is very good and $7.50. I tried it on my second visit to the Creamery. Nevertheless, I recommend getting one of the mini scoop samplers and trying multiple unique flavors instead.

If you are visiting New Orleans and looking for recommendations, feel free to message me through Yelp and I can share my itinerary, which includes my Yelp reviews. The information for an electronic copy can also be found via my Yelp profile.

If you plan on visiting the St. Louis Cemetery No. 1, it is best to have a tour guide (I'm not for sure if you can enter the cemetery without one). Our guide was informative and knew a lot about the city's history. If you get a tour and guide, the cemetery will be a part of the tour. You will walk the city and explore some of its tales, history and folklore. The cemetery is some areas are in ruins. Also, there was a cemetery entry fee (either $1 or $2, I can't remember). You will need to replan via a tour company.

Wow! Tonight had the burger, beet platter, Brussels sprounts small plate. All incredible. Heidi was a fantastic waitress.
Update 4/1/18. Still 5 star brunch. Tryst 
is always amazing
Definitely exceeded my expectations. Great authentic Mexican food. The service was really good too.atmosphere is very fun

A little pricey for drinks and average for meals...but the Tilapia Reuben was to die for...not to mention the chicken wraps...we all traded meals to be able to sample everyone else's meals.......................Great Place....
Been going here twice a week for a year now - food is yummy yummy yummy, got to try the spicy tuna

YES! This has to be one of the better hotels in the area. CLEAN, nicely decorated with a bistro that serves Starbucks in the lobby, soft beds. No complimentary breakfast but I didn't even care. Cons: it was a bit noisy next to the freeway and wind ratting the windows (but blocked out with ear plugs). Also the lights in the room were all manual with no main light switch. But overall this place is definitely worth it for the money and good for a short term stay in the area.

I'm giving this place 5 stars because it's got the best shrimp and lobster tacos around.  Someone complained about the lack of seasoning and that is OK cuz the seafood is so fresh.  All I need on my shrimp taco is a little avocado and some lemon juice and it's good.  If you want to splurge  and they are in season try the lobster tacos.  I've never had anything but the tacos and chowder and it's great.  Sit inside at the bar or small dinning room or grab a bench outside right by the water and enjoy the view.  

Many other entree type items available, salads and beer on tap!

The food is delicious. They definitely have that down. As long as you understand that, when you eat there, you'll not only be eating with members of your party but also members of everyone else's party, you'll be happy. The service is pretty decent. The servers are well-educated about the product. The drinks seem a little over-priced, but I guess it's not your average burger joint. Overall it's a place that's worth a visit as long as you're patient.

A really very average Mexican strip mall restaurant.  On the plus side, it is bright and clean appearing and the wait staff is attentive.
Only problem is that they got my order complete wrong and I ended up with something I didn't order.  Not wanting to wait another 1/2 hour I went ahead and ate it.  OK food, not great but OK-maybe on par with Taco Bell or a little better.
Daughter did not finish her meal-said it was bearly eatable.
I would recommend that folks wanting Mexican in Brownsburg look elsewhere-there are a couple of place that are much better than this.

I took my bike here twice this month. They adjusted my breaks earlier this month. Today they gave me new skewers and fixed my flat! The one guy showed me how to properly lock my bike and gave me great suggestions. I hope everybody takes their bike here because everyone is friendly and gives the best customer service. Plus they have a shop dog and every time I come in it comes over and loves me. They fix things pretty quickly as well and have the best bicycle accessories. They are very inspiring and make me want to learn more.

Coming straight from Cecil Whittaker's I was worried about having enough room. Luckily the large s'more concrete just filled in the gaps nicely! Still jonesing for more of that wonder-substance! Pulling in, the place looked like a zoo, but the line was extremely fast. So don't be scared if that's what you see.

This place is great! This was my first time trying any of the Tired Hands brews and I have to say they make some damn good IPAs. The fermentaria is a great place to have lunch and I absolutely loved my burger. The service was great and our waiter was very knowledgable about the food as well as the beer. Parking is plentiful outside in a lot or on the street and this is just a fun, weird place to have great brews and great food!
Local sea food.   Local flavor.  Great grilled oysters   A little Funky and local. But that's the charm

Our first experience with Burger Study was definitely enough to bring us back again. We booked a table at 5:30 before the Billy Joel concert at Bankers Life, but then it took us an hour and a half to get downtown (Traffic! Ugh!) so we ran very late. We called around our reservation time and they assured us we'd still have a table. We arrived almost an hour late, and they managed to seat us on a very busy night within ten minutes. So, huge thanks for that!  The place was packed full, but our server was on the ball and our food arrived with plenty of time for us to walk the block to the venue.
Food wise, everything was delicious. Burgers and apps were tasty and fun. The bar menu was extensive, and my daughter loved her chocolate shake. :) 
Atmosphere-wise, I loved the library vibe. Classy and cool. 
We'll definitely be back, and hopefully on time next visit.

I love this tanning salon. I appreciate it even more after having first gone to the Planet Beach in Uptown on Tchoupitoulas. It's like night and day in terms of aesthetic, overall feel, and friendliness/competence of staff. This salon has a nice, serene vibe and is tastefully decorated, while the one on Tchoup is reminiscent of a low-rent Miami strip club.

I know one thing about Chef Oakley after eating here - he knows how to cook and run a restaurant.  This is my number one place for the north side of Indy.  The presentation and menu choices are interesting to say the least.  I received Oakley's Chef for a Day as a gift.  I don't think they make much $ off of this but Chef took time to explain to me a little about how he runs his business, cooking in general, and his approach to things.  Chef Oakley is very dedicated to his craft and shares his love of food with his customers.  I love the kitchen being open to the dining room - something you usually find in California.  I highly recommend Oakley's Bistro.

I am close to a five star on this one, but I've only had three meals there. The udon salad was a five star! It was great. The curry tofu wrap was a 4 star, and the curry tofu wrap as a salad over spinach was also a 3- surprise, right? Well the staff is amazing, and it's perfect for a quick lunch in the neighborhood.

 I've been to the downtown location, which is great, also, but this spot has much more seating. One downside was that there is no weather guarding for the door, and cold air was blasting in each time someone came in- we weren't sitting close to the door, so it must have been bad. Curtains would help. or make sure to keep your scarf on if you go in winter.

Great food.  Great service        
The choices are many and I have not had a bad roll. My all time favorite is the flower and they have the best mussels

Awesome flower shop I've ordered twice from here for my wife.  first time was our wedding anniversary and the guy I spoke with was helpful and stayed under my budget and the flowers were amazing huge vase large long full arraignment and not only did they have that wow factor but my wife was amazed at how long they lasted. Second buy was for her birthday and again wow factor helpful girl on the phone and stayed in my price range i feel like I can tell them what I want and am thinking and bam!  They do  it! " you always get me the best flowers babe"(wife)I will continue to buy from this business I highly recommend!
Thank you guys. -Andrew

Horrible!!!!!! if I could give zero stars or negative star I would. my wife & I walk in waited for 15 min than just left  we were not even acknowledged what so ever. A customer walked In right after us and was acknowledged and serviced. Never going back

Thank God for the RPO win or get a one-star plus I'll come down there and kick everybody's ass except the defense hey Eagles I haven't heard of anyone there in your organization using their money power and status in society talking to the White House #shut down I'm an honorably discharged Marine veteran get in there and do something thanks Super Bowl champs

We visited Farmhaus at 630 on a Thursday evening for my father's birthday.  We were among the first patrons for the evening, so it wasn't entirely necessary.  Considering the quality of the food that followed, and the relatively limited nature of seating in the dining room, I would definitely recommend a reservation.

Farmhaus is situated in a quiet neighborhood in South St. Louis (Lindenwood Park), something that contributes to its personal and informal feel.  It's dining room is cozy, with enough space for roughly 40-50 guests.  There are a few seats at the bar, and some outdoor seating seems available when weather permits, but the dining room felt like the right place to be.

Our waitress (I believe her name was Monica, although I could be mistaken) was very adept at explaining the menu and answering our questions.  The menu is not divided into specific sections, as the seasonality of the ingredients appears to drive the menu choices, but there were definitely dishes that better served as Tapas-style appetizers.  The wine and beer selection is excellent, although my first choice (the Four Hands Cuvee Ange was not available), so I settled for a glass of Riesling.  We ordered an appetizer and our entrees shortly thereafter.

The Ozark-mushroom salad, with Oyster (among others) mushrooms, pecans, goat cheese, and a bacon-citrus vinaigrette, was simply amazing.  The mushrooms were lightly seared and exploded with flavor, while the smoky-sweetness of the dressing, the acidity of the fresh goat cheese, and the texture of the pecans added to the overall balance very nicely.  Everyone agreed that we should have ordered at least one more of this salad, and that this was a true highlight of the meal.

Then our main courses arrived, and they were nothing less than top-notch.  I had the Seabass, while my mother had the bacon-wrapped meatloaf and my dad the dry-aged NY Strip.  The filet was cooked perfectly despite it's thickness and remained quite flavorful, and the mashed potatoes/sweet potatoes served with it were truly homestyle with a nice semi-sweetness.  The meatloaf had a nice acidity from the glaze and a pleasant saltiness throughout - although my mother found it somewhat too salty - with mashed potatoes and pearl onions on the side.  Truly, however, the Seabass was the best choice.  It came recommended by Monica as one of Chef Kevin WIllman's specialties.  and was served over mixed-white beans.  The texture was perfect, with a very nice flavor that accompanied the beans very well.  I could go on and on about it, but quite frankly, everyone agreed it was the best among great choices.

For desert, we agreed on the peanut butter cup dessert and the apple bake (tart?) with goat-cheese ice cream.  The peanut butter filling was light and didn't overwhelm the dark-chocolate shell it was situated in, and a sweet caramel glaze on the bottom brought a pleasant sweetness to the dish.  The apple dish (I wish I could remember what type it was) was very fresh.  The apples had a mild sweetness and firmness, with caramel and a lovely fresh goat cheese ice cream.

I really, really like Tangs. I like it better than the Jade Garden which is right next to my house. Granted, I keep things simple when I order. It's usually sweet and sour chicken, or General Tso's chicken, or Shrimp and Chicken in spicy thai sauce, or last but not least, Kung po chicken. It's always prepared fresh and it just tastes a little better than the rest out there. Every once in a while the breading on the s&s chicken gets soggy, but I can fogive them for it. The soups are excellent and the dumplings are also pretty darn good. The owner is a great guy who seems to care about the product he puts out. My fav when I need my chinese food fix!!

Over an hour wait for our party, we had made "reservations", which really don't mean anything as they don't reserve your table until you arrive and then they wait until almost enough space is available for your party to then seat you. We had an 18 month old with us, he eats at the table at restaurants, when that sat us they already had a family on one side of the table and stuck his high chair on the edge corner. We couldn't pull him closer than a foot away from the table and the hostess refused to allow us to move it so he could eat. We left before even putting in our food order as hungry as we were.
Amazing.  The food here is so good.  Highly recommended for brunch, and BYO!!!!!!!

We were taken here yet again last night.  Our English Mastiff was 12 years old, and for the last few months we have been discussing what to do with her when she passed.  I looked up pet cremation and it didn't seem that there were any in Tucson that would take a dog of her size.  We can't exactly flush a 150 pound dog down the toilet, and not even a little part of me wanted to dig a hole that size.  We decided we didn't know what we would do, but that we would just decide when the time came.

The time came last night.  We went outside to call our two dogs in for the night and only one came to the door.  We walked into the yard and found our poor Mastiff's body.  We called a friend to come over at 2 am to help us dig, when my husband had the brilliant idea to call this place and see if they could do anything with her remains for us.

We called, and before we gave our names or the dog's name, we explained that she had been there before.  The person on the other end said "Oh, I remember you!  Is this Tawny's dad?"  This person actually remembered our dog from when she was there months ago.  She told us they could cremate her and either keep or return the ashes to us, and to just drive around the back with her when we arrived.  The price for our ginormous dog to be cremated and have her ashes returned to us was $165.  This was much less than I was expecting to pay, based on my previous searches for this service and her size.

By this time my friend had arrived ready to dig, but instead the three of us wrapped her in a blanket, loaded her into the truck and drove over.  When we walked in, she asked about our cat and remembered his name also.  She commented on how good Tawny had looked last time she saw her, that she was a really good dog and how sad she was that Tawny had passed.  She also asked us if we wanted a clay imprint of Tawny's paw, free of charge, so we could have a little reminder of her.

She met us out back with a gurney and another blanket for her, she climbed into the bed of our truck to load her up, and very respectfully moved her and took her away.  There was no banging the dog around, and she did everything as gently as she could, considering the dog probably weighed more than she does. 

Southern Arizona Veterinary Specialty and Emergency Center has never stopped being a five star experience for me.  From the staff to the pricing to their willingness to help to the amount of turmoil they have helped our family avoid, I can honestly say these are great people who genuinely love animals and want to do everything they can for them.  I am so happy that I found this 24 hour clinic.

We sat outside and ordered the mussels, fried calamari, and coconut shrimp...everything was yummy...our waiter was extremely knowledgeable and prompt....food came out hot even though they were busy...

It kinda surprises me to see the bad reviews! I think I've had good luck (or some others have had bad luck :/), but I've gone here quite a few times over the years, and had really good experiences. The food isn't the best Viet food in the world (I mean, it's SB), but it's definitely one of the better places in town. And they had great late-night hours. Both of the servers working were super friendly, and regularly checking in to see if we had been helped, or how everything was (but didn't check in too much). They were also really great with recommendations. Also - get the sunset passion tea with rainbow jelly! Holy crap, that was delicious.
Always good, always fast, always friendly.  Once you've had it once you'll get cravings for it.  Just make sure you carry cash so you can satisfy those cravings.

Delicious dishes definitely aiming for the French cafe feel.  Plenty of healthy options to choose from as well as more decadent ones as well. If you are looking for some classic brunch alcoholic beverages they have options as well as a good selection of fancy coffee drinks.  Breads are fresh and closer to the European styles. Pleasant place for a leisurely morning with flavor.

Came here today and it wasn't busy at all, we sat right away. Had their famous crab fries and they were "meh". Had some garlicky clams in a white sauce which was pretty decent. We were warned that it was cook to order place and food would come out as such. Well we got out fries, and clams, then one entree: lemon pepper boneless wings - they were pretty good- ranch was amazing. 10 minutes later my burger is not out yet, waitress comes over shortly to explain they're "hand rolled" and that's why it could take a little longer. Um ok sure. Another 10-15 minutes go by, still no burger, no waitress in sight. Ok, now I'm getting pissed. My gf is done her food and I still haven't even got mine. Another 5 minutes go by and here comes the waitress to another table. I had to stop her like ummm, 30 minutes is entirely to long to wait for a burger and did you mean hand rolled like they put some meat in their hand and form it into a patty!? She says yes. I said okay well there's no excuse for it to take that long then. She said she would take it off the bill (no shit, I wouldn't pay for that)! We paid the check and left. She barley apologized and seemed like she really didn't give a shit.

Doesn't get any better than this!  

Guys need to keep their feet in good shape to wear flip flops. 

Nothing worse than bad looking toenails, and cracked feet when you have slaps on your feet!  

This is THE place for a regular guy to take care of his feet. Do it for yourself, your girl, and the general public that has to look at those ugly old dogs when you wear flip flops.

PREDATORY PRICING

I rented a storage unit from StorQuest in Dec, 2015. 6 months later, they raised their prices 10%!!!

I contacted the staff and, after a bit of a go-around, they agreed to reset my fee to the original amount. 

The following month, I discovered that they had raised their rates again. 

When I contacted their office, they "informed" me that they had decided only to waive the increase for 1 month. 

StorQuest is already the most expensive storage facility in Reno. Raising rates 10% every 6 months is predatory pricing. $82 for a 5X5? I think not!

Take your business someplace else, where you can obtain fair rates from a company that values loyal customers. Clearly, StorQuest thinks they can make more money squeezing their customers.

This place offers a budget priced, tasty (albeit a bit greasy) Tex Mex fare. There is complimentary salsa and pico de gallo to your heart's content. The food is good and served blazingly fast. It is often that I barely manage to pay, when my order is called. 
Eating a few soft tacos here is one of my guilty pleasures, especially that the place is just next door to my workplace. I enjoy the peppers and onions as an add-on.
Oh, their queso is really, really good. 
It is not a fine dining experience, but it does not aspire to be. The food is tasty, though not spectacular, but at this price it is difficult to beat.

This place is rightfully votes among the best doughnuts in New Orleans and recently I see them garnering national attention. Everything they do here is fun, creative and fresh. They worked very hard on social media campaign when they first opened and that was what sucked me into this Vortex of fried dough and mouthwatering combinations. They change daily so follow them on Instagram to see the special of the day.

I really like they have a deli with a very wide selection of ready to go meals and foods. As a business traveler, staying at a local hotel, this is very convenient for me. It's a good way to still eat healthy and at a low cost.

I noticed that this place had changed hands when getting my hair cut so came back to give it a try.  Unfortunately I have to give it a mixed review.  They tried real hard to make my daughters pizza including running to vons for more basil when they ran out.  

Unfortunately none of us felt that making a cheese pizza and adding sliced tomatoes and basil to a fully cooked cheese pizza qualifies as a Margherita Pizza.  I picked up a antipasto salad for the wife and it was a bed of lettuce with some pizza toppings piled on it and a tub of italian dressing.  It was unquestionably the worst antipasto salad she has ever had.  I had the chicken parmesan and I thought it was very nice.  The chicken was cooked properly, the sauce was flavorful and the pasta was good.

Every place has its good dishes and its not so good dishes and it seems we picked two of the latter.  We go this plaza several times a week for groceries so maybe I will get up the nerve to try it again to see if I can find another dish they do as well as their chicken parmesan and not one as bad as their antipasto salad.
Love this place!  Had a nail emergency and Ken hooked me up!  Amazing job!  Thank you!  I will be back!

Hello, this place has bugs! Like, not just one, but many... several... disgusting! You could see them crawling all over the buffet. I stuck to drinks after seeing that, waited for my friends to finish their food (which wasn't very spectacular either) and got the heck out!
If you order a breakfast sandwich get it on a croissant!!! Their croissants are huge and are absolutely the best!!! I wish I knew who their bakery is!

We ordered some food from Favela Chic via Uber Eats and got our food with no utensils, no salsa, no napkins....nada. Tried to call the number we looked up from Google and the phone number was not operational. Just a clear cut example of a business that gives Z3R0 F's about customer service or food prep in general.

Interesting store.  Wanted to buy a voodoo doll.  They only had a few.  They had lots of african tribal dollars.  Prices were high.  They had much merchandise to buy.  Also did 45 dollar tarot card readings for 30 minutes.
A bit pricey on the weekend.  The prime rib was good.  They have a good selection of family style buffet items.  The place is very clean and the service was good.

We've been here 4 times over the past few months. It's definitely officially now one of our go-to options when we're craving authentic Mexican (which is usually at least once a week). 

First of all, the service is phenomenal no matter which server you get. Very attentive and friendly! They start you off with chips (with retried beans) and two types of salsa (verde and a chipotle type) which are fresh and delicious. I, of course, cannot eat Mexican food without an order of guac and theirs is right on point on all levels (price, flavor, and quantity). I order it every single time. 

I order pork carnitas tacos almost everywhere and after trying at La China three times, I'll be sticking to something else from now on. The pork was extremely fatty and in big chunks instead of a bit more shredded like it's usually served at other establishments.  My husband swears by their chicken chilaquiles and I'm getting it next time myself. The chicken is very juicy, tender, and cooked perfectly. We rave about it!

The tamales aren't on the menu but are some of the best around and only $1. We used to be able to get them on weekdays but last time we went we were told they only have them on Saturdays and Sundays. Disappointing but I understand because they're a lot of work to make.

Absolutely love this place! The crab bisque soup was amazing. The service was spectacular. The manager even sent over champagne and shots and bread pudding for my birthday. Couldn't have asked for a better experience. Wish I could give this place 10 stars!

I thought it was a very good burger joint. Great fries and a really great, unique atmosphere. The service was very friend and on it! Bo, our server (awesome name) was extremely friendly. We will be back. Only complaint was the skimping on any extra sauces. The side of ranch and regular ketchup (they had their ketchup in a bottle on the table) came in a small cup. I had to ask for several of them to have a enough for my fries and burger. Other than that, fantastic place for burgers and fries!

I've been here a couple times, and the first time I came I thought the menu had so much variety, but after the first time I just couldn't really choose anything off the menu. I mean, I guess I shouldn't expect too much since it is just a sandwich shop, but I LOVE sandwiches! I tried their "hot" bbq sandwich which was a bit too salty, though I did like some of their cold menu items. But I could never finish because even though I got "small" it was just WAY too much. It comes with a LOT of meat. The food overall isn't bad tasting though. Their onion rings are amazing though. Pretty much every unhealthy thing on the menu is. Try to the cream cheese, avocado + everything else on it burger. You'll see what I'm talking about.

Was very pleased with our recent car buying experience. 

Our search began online, when we found a great deal on a great pre-owned Nissan. We coordinated with the lot to come see the car, and we were relieved the car we found online was the same car we arrived to see. (That's not always the case.)

A short time later, we drove that car home. No muss, no fuss. A great deal all around. Not only would I recommend Thoroughbred Nissan to others, but I'd go back for another vehicle when the time comes.

Fantastic job and courteous movers. I would recommend them to my friends & family. 

They showed up on time, went through the extras I might be interested in (extra insurance coverage if damages occur, carpet coverage, estimate including travel time, etc).

My girlfriend & I only needed our "big stuff" moved along w a few odds & ends. Tyler & Bobby were polite, respectful, professional, and worked well together. 

This wasn't a Big move, but I feel Two Men & a Truck did an excellent job. They wrapped all appliances & furniture to protect them. They strapped the furniture & all in to the box truck so it doesn't shift during transport. They always offered to move anything wherever we wanted even after we said one place & changed our minds. 

We did a lot of work preparing and moving smaller items, so we actually came in under estimate by $150. They charge you for transportation time & then every 15 minutes. Tyler & Bobby moved at a steady pace & did not dawdle. As Bobby was going back to the truck to get pliers for our washer, he asked if an item was to be moved. I replied yes, he commented theta he didn't want to return to the truck empty handed. 

Professional job fellas!

Two words: HILARIOUS TIME. I have never been to a place like this before, but it was definitely worth it. The cover charge was reasonable because all the music that was being played was live from very talented musicians and singers. They played today's latest hits to throwbacks from the 90s which was fun and different. I would definitely go back here because I had a good time and good laughs!

With a fast food restaurant you are getting the traditional food served at every other fast food restaurant. So reviews on Yelp are not meant necessarily to review the food, but the service. 

Every time I have ever been here, the wait has been atrocious. It is called "fast" food and yet I find myself waiting a long time. On more than one occasion I have left due to the speed. Also, that being said, if I am going to wait I would prefer the food to be freshly made, otherwise why did I wait? However this last time the food was cold, which is truly unfortunate. The reason I did not complain in person is two-fold. One, I was so hungry I couldn't fathom waiting for them to accurately make my food. Two, I actually fear restaurant confrontations as I am terrified the people will mess with my food. Maybe it is silly to be afraid of that, but I know it happens.

As a follow up, I had to come back and rant some more about Erik and his team.  We have had the need for four or five local pick ups and deliveries throughout our ordeal and MoveGreen has been there to help every step of the way.  These guys get customer service and know what it means to build relationships.  When I need something, it's an email or phone call away and I never feel like I'm being gouged or taken advantage of.  The pricing has been fair and we've been cut more than one break along the way.  I absolutely can't thank Movegreen enough.  Love this company and will be a customer for a long, long time.

Unbelievable fresh meat and seafood counter, olive bar and deli and impressive coffee bar, winery, cheeses and bakery. Opens early in the morning grab your coffee and then stay all day and shop and eat out back or bring your food to the beach make sure you have a cooler with lots of ice so you can shop and travel home with it!

I was here for 9days just a week ago with my husband & daughter. The stay was awesome! Our room was spotless we had everything we could need in the fully stocked kitchen (utensils, pots etc) breakfast buffet is out of this world GOOD! Even tired from the night before we made sure to come down for breakfast. The staff was courteous, helpful so sweet. I guess if I had one complaint it would be the pool 1. It's on the small side 2. It has to be cooler regulate it better turn off the self heating ( no need for that in July in Florida) they have an outdoor grill for the guests to use we had a bbq one night with friends. Miguel the front desk clerk cleaned it for us started it up. Very nice young man great very professional, courteous & welcoming. Can't say the same for the gentleman in the overnight shift didn't even catch his name. He wasn't courteous at all a bit rude. Overall we loved & enjoyed our stay we'd do it again. Also did Linsey twice while there machines worked well & soap was provided at front desk

Nice restaurant. Loved my server Shawn! The aquarium was pretty nice too. The food was ok but the sticker shock on the bill left a bitter taste. My mom and I had soup and salad. We shared an artichoke dip and she had a drink $85.00. I thought that was an expensive lunch for what we had.

Whenever I'm in Royersford and wanting sushi....there is no other option than Veekoo!
Besides, some of the best sushi had overall.
It's so flavorful and light. The rolls almost fall apart as you pick them up, bc they're so fresh.

Literally am enjoying my take-out now...and couldn't help but write a review!
Great, Great Spot!!!!

I'm a big fan of St Louis Bread Co, but the experience I had this morning was horrible. I stopped by the drive thru since l was on a tight schedule. With one person in front of me, it still took ten minutes to reach the window. I then was told the computer was down and being rebooted. Five minutes or so later, still nothing. Eventually another worker opens the window and says she's re-ringing the order but not charging me for the frozen mocha (I never ordered a frozen mocha). She finally found our sandwich, which I paid full price for. It was cold, hard, burnt, and made incorrectly... I didn't have time to complain since I was late and there were about 7 cars behind me by then. I'll never be going back to this location.

Spa Aria is my favorite getaway in New Orleans.  The staff is very attentive and really want to provide you with the best experience possible.  I've had a variety of massage types and I've also taken advantage of treating myself to a last minute facial.  

I always try to make room for a visit when I'm in town!
Their smoked brisket sandwich they have on special is possibly in the top 10 things I've ever eaten.

Came here for a birthday party last Friday and we had the whole 2nd floor to ourselves which was amazing! The music was AMAZING! Honestly, my favorite so far that I've heard in Philly. They were remixes of all the best classics, I was a huge fan and everyone was loving it on the dance floor. Drinks were cheap, bartenders were attentive but for some reason the speakers kept going in and out and for one second it would be kind of quiet and then the music would blare on. I was a huge fan and hope that more people have their birthdays here.

Roti canai (Indian pancake) is the best !! I could honestly eat this all the time
The Thai basil noodles was a lil greasy and kinda bland 
Tom yum soup is delicious 
Basil chicken was good but I've had better 
I definitely want to try other dishes 
Service was good surprisingly .. 
I'm so use to the lack of service in many other Asian restaurants
Decent service. Nice people. But overall, a mediocre spot. Food was fried, yes, but a bit bland. Nothing special.

I've been to this place twice in two days and each time I got one of their speciality latte drinks, and both were fantastic. It's also a very nice atmosphere and the people couldn't be much friendlier so I'm very thankful this coffee house opened up so close to my neighborhood. They have only been opened a few weeks but I have a feeling it's just going to get better and better the more they keep adding new items. I will definitely be back.

I'm following up on a previous review since I've been to this place at least a dozen times more so upping my rating to 5 stars. This place really is the perfect coffee place since they have added great new snacks, the speciality drink selections are fantastic, they always have different flavored house made free water and compared to the rest of Philly, the prices are very reasonable. . On top of that the people working there have always been very friendly and social plus I never have an issue getting quick parking.

Such a great addition to the mall. I feel like people are so fixed on Starbucks when quite honestly there are so many other establishments that have much better coffee! My favorite here has to be the flat white with soy milk but they also have fantastic light bite options.
