I was here for a business dinner and my boss had made reservations so as a party of 5 on a weeknight we were seated immediately.  Service was prompt and friendly.  There is a full bar and a wide selection of bourbons, I'm from Kentucky that is a thing.  

I had the pork chop special and split it with a table mate that was not an issue at all. The pork chop was cooked perfectly and well seasoned. The fried okra was yummy.  The fried green tomatoes were good, but could have used a little more seasoning in the coating.

Some members of the party ordered salads that never arrived but we taken off the bill.

The live music was great!

If I find myself in Downtown Franklin again, I will give this place another whirl.

We came here for dinner this evening and was absolutely delicious! Truly I was blown away. I ordered a fish special at market price and couldn't believe how yummy it was. Can't recall the name of the fish but it was in the grouper family. It tasted very identical to crab meat. 

I had my one year old daughter with and couldn't get her to eat anything, but she loved my fish! Service was friendly. Love it here, but it is pricey! $100+ for two people, however every penny was well spent.
The sales team definitely needs some customer service lessons. They were not willing at all to help me, and were a bit rude. The tux I rented was nice, however.

India Palace is awesome! The lunch buffet (which is all I've ever had), is excellent with fresh food, a lot of options, and delicious desserts. There is a coupon available online, too, for $1 off lunch buffet which makes the price not too bad for the amount of food that you get. I've never had to wait for a table, they always keep your water glass full, and being a vegetarian, there are tons of options... even more vegetarian options than things with meat in them!

I've only ordered from here twice thus far, and went to pick it up.  The first time, I ordered the sesame vegetarian "chicken;" the second, the General Tso's "chicken."  I always love finding places where they have mock meats instead of just tofu.  I really enjoyed both dishes, and they steam their broccoli to a good consistency.  All in all, it's not exceptional food, but the fact that they have a mock meat selection sold me.
Decent happy hour and lunch specials. I especially like their spicy tuna, as it's not super mayonnaisey. It's a great place to hang out for a bite in a chill place.

If you're a margarita drinker like me, then this is the spot for you! A little pricey, but totally worth it. I highly suggest brunch. Great seating, amazing menu, and a little live music outside to spice things up.

The guys who cleaned the inside of my car today were awesome!  I have a dog who sheds and they did an amazing job of cleaning the inside for $8.  They were very friendly, too - I'll definitely be back.

I've noticed this place on my way back into the city multiple times down Kelly and when a friend and I went on a nice mid day bike ride along the river looking for something for lunch what better oppurtunity to try it!!

The location is optimal. It's along Kelly right by the river but not too much traffic noise or congestion. The indoor setting was a bit dull and cold but the outdoor dining was perfect. Great views of the river and runners, especially perfect for people watching which I do quite enjoy.

We started with the tomato conserva and oh my goodness it was absolutely amazing. I'd recommend it as a started to anyone. It's a savory, full, salty, onion filled Italian salsa with perfectly toasty bread to spread it on. Then we worked on the kale borrata salad which was a perfect sharing size for 2. The dressing was light and lemony and the burrata  (creamy mozzarella) was to die for. I want to bathe in it!! 

We finished off with a basic Margarita pizza which ended up being my least favorite. The crust was chared abit too much for me and the pizza itself was very soft and smooshy. VERY difficult to use hands I had to eat it was a fork to keep it from falling apart. 

Overall the service was good, food came out quickly however they never refilled our water glasses and it was a pretty warm day out. I would definitely go back though for a nice lunch and go at some more of those salads.

I cannot say enough about this place!! It's the greatest thing to ever happen to northeast Philadelphia. There is nothing like it around!!! I am there at least once a week and have never been disappointed. The food is always fresh. The menu is creative and innovative. Whether you order off the menu or try one of their specials. You won't be disappointed. They treat my husband and I like family. The staff is so friendly. Johnny cakes Obrien always takes great care of us. If you haven't tried it yet. You should get there as soon as possible!!!

I've been coming here since the mid-1960s. Of course the canyon itself is extraordinary. What ruins the place now--as with many naturally beautiful places--is the human element. Namely the shuttles and their drivers. The peace and silence is shattered by belching diesel trams and even more, obnoxious drivers. They scream and yell to each other, are uninspired and surly, bottom of the barrel. Oh, and they chain-smoke cigarettes. So your first experience in the canyon will likely be like mine: covering my nose against the diesel fumes and drivers' cigarette smoke. I long for the days when the place had class, and you could get a breath full of clean desert scents and unpolluted air.

Quiet elegance, excellent cuisine (even by NOLA standards), prompt and attentive service.
This was the only restaurant we visited twice during our time here.

I should preface this by saying that I am a pizza snob, and living in Italy for quite some time has spoiled me. 

So when I heard I was being flewn into St. Louis for business meetings, I hopped on yelp to see if there was any legit wood-fired pizza joints worth checking out.  I came across "the good pie" and decided to put it on the list. 

Positives: Great ingredients, balanced pies. neopolitan style i.e. bubbly airy crust near the edges, with a thin charred bottom. Tasted like San marzano tomatoes,but i can't be sure. If you ever visit italy and taste true pizza, you will gain an appreciation for the char, without it, it's just not the same. 

Negatives: Limited menu, small space, no descriptions of beers on tap. I can understand the no substitutions/additions rule as most folks from Gli Stati Uniti try to jam as much toppings onto a pie as possible.  Also, basil is supposed to be put on the pie AFTER you bake it, or it burns. Oh yeah, and they have a really weak list of toppings.

Extremely pleased with Yolk. I was recommended to try it a couple of months ago, and never got around to it until recently. 

It's open til 3p most days, which is a hour longer than a lot of other breakfast/brunch restaurants in the area. This is a boon for me. 

The atmosphere was a lot better than expected. modern, clean, bright. Good amount of space, good sized tables and booths. 

I liked seeing the huge menu. Lots of options. I ended up with the El Torero Scrambler. It was good. I wished it had a little more chorizo in it, but I really can't complain. The scramble, fried potatoes and two pancakes was a lot of food for the 11.50 price tag. They have a steak and eggs on the menu that I'm definitely going to try next. (I have been searching for decent carne asada and eggs since moving back from San Diego, and have yet to find anywhere to get such a thing. perhaps this could fill that void)

The waitress was excellent - helpful and attentive. I also liked the pay at the counter setup - less waiting. 

Looking forward to going back.

EDIT: Since writing my review, I go to yolk often - every week or two. After all of my visits, there's one thing about this place that really stands out, and it's the quality of the staff. I've been trying a lot of other restaurants in the area and keep having terrible customer service experiences - mostly the wait staff don't seem like they know what they're doing. At yolk, the whole operation runs like a machine, and all of the staff are super on top of their game. It's one of the few places I've been that I know I can count on for a positive experience. 

Also, I've come to the personal conclusion that the all star combo is the best bang for the buck. It's my go to.
The restaurant was empty 7:30 Pm on a Tuesday night , less than half  full,  but a thirty minute wait.   We left as the tables were filthy and nobody looked happy.

Wow! I'm not usually a big fan of chain pastry shops, but Nothing Bundt Cakes, especially this location, definitely breaks the mold. ;-)

First off, when you walk into the store you are instantly hit with the delicious smell of freshly baked cake, but even better is the charming decorations and retail that line the walls and shelves of this store. The owners/operators have given this shop an amazing curb appeal.

Most importantly though is the taste of the cakes! Oh my god! The cinnamon swirl cake is beyond words, I wish I could describe it, but you just have to try it to understand. There are other great choices too and they are all topped with the signature cream cheese frosting, which is absolutely incredible. It is unlike any other cream cheese frosting I have ever had and there is a reason it is the only frosting that they have...there is no need for any other!!!

I highly recommend Bundt cakes for parties, work events, or just because! And if you just want a personal one after a bad day at work, a Bundtlet is the perfect remedy!

Cheers.

So happy we stayed here. It's conveniently and centrally located. Everything we did in Tampa was around 15 minutes away. The service was spectacular. We stayed in a bay view room which was very clean and very comfortable. The daily housekeeping was excellent and the in room dining was very delicious. Very highly recommend staying here if you're visiting Tampa Bay.

I agree with Dennis M.'s review, this is the place to go for crazy deals on clothing. Their clearance racks for women are always well stocked and decent. One can never go wrong especially for the price of the items.

Customer service is excellent - Always friendly and helpful. The staff  tries to greet everyone at the door and inform customers about current deals and discounts. Recently during the Black Friday weekend sale, a sales associate was even going around providing customers with bags for their purchases since everyone was getting their hands full. Also, if you are having a hard time looking for something specific, they can tell you exactly where you can find it, what it looks like, and provide you with other options.

I always leave happily with not only my purchase but with the level of service every time I shop here. Sign up for their email as well, it's definitely worth it.

Don't stay here if on business.  WiFi is horrid--ruined a workshop hosted in one of their meeting rooms.  The comforter on the bed was damp.  I asked for a dry one to be swapped while I ate dinner in the bar.  When I returned to my room it reeked of body odor.  The floor in the room is a toxic waste dump of stains on the carpet.  Good bed and pillows.  Polite staff.

Loved this place. The bartender told us that it was once a restaurant owned by New Orleans mob boss Carlo Marcello in the 1940's. Not sure if that was true, but it was a good story. This place serves Prohibition Era 1920's hand crafted cocktails. I stuck to a beer, not really into spirits, but my friend had a Sazerac, which she raved over. The bar is on the small size, but lavishly decorated for the era it celebrates. There is a huge beaded glass chandelier in the center of the room, fringed lamps and other Roaring 20's touches.  There are framed black and white mob figures hung around the bar. Carlo Marcello, Vito Genovese, and so forth. The bartender also showed us a leather bound book made by the bar chronicling the story of Prohibition and its repeal. That book was filled with wonderful photo's and history, but wasn't for sale.  The staff were friendly and I would go back again.

In regards to the museum, it was great.  In regards to one particular staff member...  She was horrible.  My family came to visit from Columbus.  We have a three year old and a 20 month old.  When we came in, we were politely informed by three separate people in the space of 60 seconds that our kiddie 2 seater wagon was not allowed in the museum.  In case we didn't hear it the first two times in the space of ten seconds.  Even though I was trying to get my kids unbundled and out of the wagon so I could get my husband to return it to the car.
That's fine.  I understand the concern.  But what got me was the woman who was standing 8 feet away from me as we were waiting for him to return complaining to the security guard in a very audible voice about how she couldn't understand WHY anyone would bring a wagon instead of a stroller.  And how she wanted to make sure we got rid of it.  And why kids would need a wagon anyway?  And on and on.  

Incredibly rude.  I followed the rules.  I put up no argument.  And you're still going to be snide?

 The museum is nice.  The kids area was nice.  The trains were cool. I sincerely hope they do well and spread understanding and better knowledge of Native American culture.   But I'm not coming back.

I'd say this was five stars except for the fact that the adjoining bar/ restaurant was ridiculous- the staff was so in the weeds it was a twenty minute wait at the bar on a Friday night.  On an up note, hotel staff and accommodations were absolutely perfect .

Being Salvadorian I was very excited to see another place making pupusas. The place is very small very easy to miss from the road. The inside is very small very typical for Salvadorian restaurants. The staff is nice but mostly only speak Spanish so make sure to have someone translate for you, if you only speak English. The menu is full so there's something for everyone. I've been to this place a few times and the last time really disappointed me. The pupusas are small and mostly filled with beans. This is a common trick to make more profit for less. The tamales were filled with rice, this is not typically found in tamales. I must say if they make changes and provide Quality food they'll get customers if they continue to cut corners people will stop coming. Good luck

Since Toppers is near my office, when we decided to order lunch in a few days ago, I decided to try a new pizza place. We settled on a thin crust veggie pizza, cheesy stix, and hot wings for three of us (plus extra to share). They delivered exactly at their estimated time. We all liked it - nothing too exciting, but definitely good. My one coworker found a few hairs on one of his slices that didn't appear to be any of ours, so that was kind of gross, but it happens, I suppose. Since everything else was otherwise good, I'd go back.
Sabrina's is fabulous! Great healthy food,  taste wonderful,  great atmosphere! Totally enjoyed eating there while on vacation in Reno.

Don't use this company! I went there to transfer a license plate from a car I had sold, to another car.  They charged $25, and gave me a new registration for my new car.  Then, when it was time to renew my registration, I didn't get a renewal notice from ADOT, and when I logged on the MVD web site, there was no record of my car.  I went back to the company to ask them to look into what was wrong, and they looked and said oh yes, they knew they had not entered the registration correctly, and then they corrected what they had done.  Then they asked me for $50.  I said, no, they should correct what I had already paid them to do.  After a little argument, this huge guy came out of the back room and said OUT!  OUT!  GET OUT!  I thought he was going to bust a gut,  and I felt very threatened.  They undid the correction, and I had to go to the DMV to do what I had paid these people $25 to do.  Don't use these people, they are unprofessional,  incompetent and rude.  Physical threats have no place in a vehicle registration office.

I've gotten oil changes here a couple times because it's close to work, but every time, they tell me I need multiple repairs/maintenance done. Most recently, they said I needed a brake & steering fluid flush and that my rear shocks were so rusted, they could fall apart at any moment. I went to my regular shop for a 2nd opinion. They said the shocks/struts...looked fine, the brake fluid didn't look bad, but I could do the flush if I wanted, and they said MY CAR DOESN'T EVEN HAVE STEERING FLUID. This place is the worst. Never going back again.

No stars, actually negative stars! Victory has the worst custumer service ever! Horrible broke down cars and the rudest people working for them. I say take your money eles where. There are many great taxi services in Philadelphia. Don't choose Victory!

I almost wanted to not like this place.  Do you really need to sanitize tacos, Garces?  The best tacos I've had were always slightly grimy, simple, and cheap.  Maybe from a truck or a dingy shack or a place where they had to send out the kid who speaks English to take your order.

But Buena Onda did sanitize this experience...in a good way.  While the grime is absent the prices and simplicity remained.  $3 for a regular taco, $3.50 for seafood guys.  And they're really good.  Not great, but really good.  And they have cheap beers - all under $5.  Margaritas under $10.  Wines $7.  Friendly service.  A small, appropriately stocked bar.  Right next to a froyo place.  I mean...what's not to like?

This used to be my go to spot, but it's really gone downhill. Customer service is terrible. They are very slow and completely inept. They completely wrecked my nails when taking off my gel, then made me bleed and claimed it wasn't their fault. I will never come back here.

I had a previously good experience here and then came back with my parents and received dirty silverware and they gave me a mug that still had someone's fresh lipstick print on it. We all lost our appetite worrying about the cleanliness. The food was not too outstanding either. Their biscuits taste like I'm biting into a clump of flour.

My SO and I love exploring new trails and so it was no surprise when he suggested we try Los Padres NF. Once we arrive and got passed the gate, we were detoured by the signs of a previous campsite (I think they should just remove the signs to stop the extra stops). Once we got on the trail, it was angelic. The trail follows a stream of ponds or swimming holes. We were surprised at the number of people taking the break from the summer heat. But that's not why we came, so on we went. As we walked we found signs along the trails of balancing rocks - very zen-like and very comforting knowing you're on the right path. The terrain varies and every turn is breadth taking. Definitely going back.

Just finished eating@R2L for restaurant week.  This was one of the best restaurant week dining experiences I have had.  Three of my girl friends and I wanted a girls night out to celebrate life and enjoy catchup up with a good meal.  We had a reservation@6pm.  I requested a window seat, but knew it would be difficult without a three month reservation.  To our pleasant surprise my request was honored and we were seated at an awesome location over looking Philly as she sparkled like a city of gold. Service was spot on.  Our server (Jonathan) was very approachable and gave us recommendations for the drink menu as well as the dinner menu. He was patient and didn't rush us to make decisions even though it was a busy night for restaurant week.   I got the Old Cuban which was described as  a "mojito in a tuxedo". Def not the best cocktail I had.  I will def try something else next time I go.

Now to the menu. Everything we had tasted delicious.  For appetizers, my two friends had the mushroom barley soup. It was delicious, but a little tart from the red wine.  I had the smoked salmon appetizers and my other friend had the salad.  The presentation of the salmon was right on! I asked if the salmon was smoked in house and the waiter said yes, which sold me. The salad look amazing as well and my friend described the steak as good chewy bacon, but the Salmon was the winner.

For the entrees, we all had the filet and short rib duo.  The meat melted as it hit the fork.  No knife needed. The sauce that came with it was a perfect marriage with the baked and crispy potatoes.  Def way too much food as none of us could finish our plates.

Last came the dessert.  My two friends has the French toast with pear dessert.  It was decent, but nothing really exciting about it.  I had the coconut parfait.  There was tapioca topped with pineapple, a meringue, a short bread cookie, a french macaroon type cookie, and some kind of coconut sugar cookie.  It was delicious and very refreshing. My other friend had the milk chocolate hazelnut crunch bar.  That was such a delicious desert that was rich and light all at the same time.  We all sampled this dessert and wished we ordered it instead. The whole piece may have been too much for me, so I am happy with the coconut parfait, but a few bits of this dessert  was enough for us all to want to back and sample the regular menu in the future. 
Last came the lattes, which were very well done. 

Def a night to remember with a wonderful wait staff, an awesome view, great company, and a delicious meal.  Can't wait to go back again!!

The restaurant is handicapped friendly. Bless them.  

We love it here!  Breakfast is the best!  They have weekday specials.   The soup bowls are gigantic!  

One thing you should know:  The deli doesn't open for business until 8:00 a.m.   I keep forgetting and getting there too early.  It is one of the few non-Chinese restaurants open for Christmas.   Business was brisk, but well-managed on the holiday.

I typically do not like red lobster I don't think that their food is anything exceptional but my boyfriend wanted to go and so we went. When we got there they told us it would be about a 20 minute wait we got seated in five minutes ... So win!! But once we got seated it was just downhill from there! It was literally close to 15 minutes before our server even acknowledged that we were there and when she came to the table it was Oh hey didn't even see you guys in the corner . really?! Well you know what shame on you but,even more shame on your place of business because you should probably implement some sort of system where a table is seated and the server is notified! ( maybe have a manager walk around Like other places.... I seem to get much better service when managers are walking around checking on guests experiences) Then we got salads with our meal and it's like she disappeared into a vortex and it was like 10 minutes before she came back and only brought biscuits and said she'd be right back with the salads you were gone for 10 mins you should have brought both! .... And this vortex I'm assuming was there for most of the night because anytime she came to the table she was gone and there was these large increments of time ! It was close to am hour before we even got our food! What?! It's red lobster?!?! I don't understand!  Then she asked me if I wanted a box to take our stuff home I said yes she came back with the check  and no box ( our neighbors got a box)  then asked me of I wanted a box.... Well yes I DID, but no not now because who knows where you will disappear to this time.... We were there for an hour and a half!!! And not for a good reason! What an awful awful experience! I won't throw her name out there but BEWARE!

This is a beautiful space! 

I went for a private event so I'm not sure about pricing - but as far as a venue that offers amazing food and in a beautiful space. I loved it.

The Sweet Potato Casserole was incredible. Hope you like pecans!
Best breakfast of my life, without a doubt. Tennessee sugar cured ham. Amazing.

A clean store a good crew  and well prepared food  a little pricey compared to
Most fast food establishments but how can you resist the mashed potatoes and gravy  I usually choose the chicken bowl  all the essential vitamins and minerals a growing boy needs all in one bowl  lol

We had their pizza for a long time at the Rillito farmer's market and finally they have a brick and table place. This is hands down one of the best pizzas I have had and among the top 3 (Florence included). It is thin crust so it you are looking for Chicago style, you will be disappointed. Their caprese pizza with pine nuts is amazing. They have won international competitions and it shows.

You get what you pay for .. I expected it to be way worse according to the reviews .. You guys don't give this enough credit .. You want to spend pennies to get amazing food .. I ordered the chicken parm sandwich and it's actually good and the mozzarella sticks are decent ..

Good date night spot! Both my daughter and I had steaks and they were cooked as we had order and tasted very good. Our server was polite and did a good job. Overall food wise and environment was a good experience. 

I would like to say though I felt overcharged for my daughters meal which I was explained there would be a mark up on her meal for Mac and cheese as a side. $10 for a child's meal is a little much to me when I could go to Texas Roadhouse and get an adult size steak 6 oz for that same price with 2 sides. But for a treat every once in awhile it wasn't bad.
Not organized and a lot of price tags were wrong or on floor. 1star for finding the item I needed and 2nd star got it cheaper then priced.

Meh. I had a pork burrito that was quite unremarkable. It was mostly rice and beans with a slight smear of guacamole. The other ingredients - cheese, crema, pico de galo - were undetectable. I agree with others about price.  At $7.49 it is overpriced by $2. The optional green sauce is good and was needed to give the burrito some flavor.

I love love love their tacos! My parent don't stay too far from it so I try to get some whenever I am craving tacos, which is almost 3 days a week. It is cash only . I have not tried anything other than the tacos.

We came here to watch 3 Sunday football games at once... The Eagles, Pittsburgh and the Ravens.  We were shocked by how empty the place was.  We asked to have them change a TV so we could see the Ravens game, but they wouldn't do it, so our resident Baltimorian was a bit bummed.  I guess X-Finity has impacted their game-day traffic.  I was pleased that we sat right down though.... and that nobody chased force fed us our food, and chased us out of our booth.  We got to enjoy a full football game at a table, which had never happened to me at Chickies before.  We grazed, and ate good food and watched great football.  Bud light was $2, but i noticed that the glasses had false bottoms which was kind of annoying... i mean a pint is a pint is a pint... but they try to save a few ounces?  Really?  I love the crab fry salad.  As a vegetarian, that's my trusty stand-by here.  

I had a fine experience, but I guess i'm just bitter about being so grossly mistreated here before.  The staff isn't particularly warm and nice... but I think that's almost partof the charm of the place.  I'll be back... but my craving of crab fries isn't as strong as it used to be.

Service OK; crepes were bland, but acceptable.
The staff was observed exchanging unpleasantries, which is not a good sign.  Especially when only two tables were occupied and no stress situation was in effect.
Amazingly great food!!!  Neat funky and friendly neighborhood spot, with gray shrimp and grits, bananas foster French toast, croque madame...everything we ordered was SO great!!!
I got a pedicure for the first time today at Cured and this place is a 10/10 in my book. Shon, my nail tech did an amazing job and I will for sure be back soon. :)

Best pizza in seminole heights! During the week they have a great special 2 large 2 toppings for $11 !!! Wow !!! Pizza is def the best hubs and I have had anywhere near seminole heights. They do a weekday lunch buffet for $7.99 that's good as well. I pretty much stick to the pizza but my husband lives their grinders. The eggplant is his favorite. Only dislike would be that the restaraunt is dark and outdated so I get the pizza to go. 
Def worth you giving it a chance. My favorite is the Hawaiian!

Best Asian food I have found in the area in the past year! A little pricey for take-out, but you get what you pay for. Service and food are equally fantastic! Looking forward to dining in BYOB style! Highly recommend this place.

The food is OUTSTANDING! Service is patient and attentive, this place is a gem of Frenchmen St. On a Saturday night, if you wanna have a good time and eat deliciously, do yourself a favor and go here! I took my mom and sis and they loved it!!!

When you can choose your beverage, amazing cheeses and then leave it to the plating people to add olives, cornichons, candied pecans and chutneys...this is the place!  Combine an atmosphere of "find a table midst the like minded appreciative souls", music and your drink of choice and let the happiness commence!  You can extend the amazement with great starters such as more olives, a trio of butters, salads and entrees...all good and great!
Very good always very clean staff are always polite. The food is pretty average and tends to be a little bland but i think thats they're way of trying to be kid friendly.

I have dined here many times, probably never on a Tuesday. The food was Bland and thoughtless.  I have had the pasta and fagioli many times, and never been so disappointed...hope you try harder next time.
Good sushi, great customer service, nice atmosphere. 4 stars because the fish quality isn't as good as some of the other sushi spots in town.

Dolan's has been great recently. I can see some things have changed, service is much better, crowds are bigger, food has been consistently good from the kitchen. They have updated their happy hour and food specials, all great things! Servers and bartenders have been in much better spirits. I love coming here again. Stop in and try it out. Recommended: garlic parm wings, homemade chips with cayenne ranch, pulled pork when available, and burger with egg. Thanks for getting on the right track. 

Also, live music Fridays and Saturdays... Usually really good acts. Sometimes a lil loud, but I don't mind that too much.

-WARNING!  DO NOT USE!-
No stars would be the correct rating!  Horrible!  Slow!  You want damaged furniture call these guys!  You want to save some money on the move DO NOT use this company.  Horrible customer service.  Will never use this company ever again. HORRIBLE!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

For a person who loves Asian cuisine but doesn't eat seafood a good-to-me ramen/hot pot/miso is hard to find. This place delivered, and then some, with their fusion flavors and crafted menu! Caters to all crowds and the food was just superb. 

Rave review:
Staff - so friendly, so helpful 
Atmosphere - fun, hip 
Food - MOUTH-WATERING 
Other diners - chill 

One caveat; not good for groups.

New to Philly and glad to find such a great place like this! All great experiences from scheduling an appointment to the finished product. Great cuts, great convos. Excited to make this my new go to barber shop!

We were there the first week. The wait staff seemed to be still in the breaking in phase. For some reason the lights were up bright like we were in a high school cafeteria. Food was good. Fairly priced. I will likely try them again.
Had 1 cut here so far. A bit pricey $16 for men, but I got the full show and the asst mgr did a great job on the cut.

I visited the Lawrence, IN location last week and it was a waste of my time and money.  The facility was clean and the front desk nurse was nice. I signed in shortly after they opened and there was one other patient signed in on that day before me.  I was called back within 5 minutes so I had high hopes that it would be a quick visit.  The nurse took all of my vitals and didnt write a single one down.  He led me to a room and asked the reason for my visit.  I explained my symptoms (sinus infection).  He asked which pharmacy I prefer and if I have any allergies.  Still hasnt written anything down.  I answered and he left.  35 minutes later a doctor came in.  The doctor introduced himself and to me and my daughter, who was with me, and asked what he could do for her.  I said "actually I am the patient" his response was "oh sorry, I havent even looked at the schedule for today."  He asked me the same questions the nurse did (symptoms, allergies, etc) with a little more detail. The Dr actually wrote down my responses on a piece of scrap paper.  The doctor was knowledgeable.   Knowledgable to the point of stating several studies of OTC medications I have been using and how they are no better than placebos.  He did an exam and in the middle of it, another nurse came in to give the Dr results for another patient. I'm not sure why that couldn't wait another 5 minutes until he was finished.  The dr told me it seemed like a viral infection and there was nothing to be done until it has been 10 days. (He never asked me which day the cold began). By this point all I wanted was to be finished with this place and move on.  The Dr wrote down, on his scrap paper, a few OTC meds that studies show DO work and tore the paper to give me the meds.  I was extremely dissapointed with the consistent lack of professionalism.  I will not be back or recommend this facility.   Of the hour I was in the facility, I was seen by a nurse or Dr for about 8 minutes total. Waste of time and money!

2nd time I've made an appointment for an oil change at this place and was told it'd be an hour and a half once I got there...what's the purpose of an appointment?  This is not meant to be a smear on Pep Boys in general, just this particular store.  I've been to 2 other stores in this area which have been great and is also the reason why I gave these clowns a 2nd chance...shame on me as the saying goes.  There is a small local guy 3 blocks down the road where I get anything significant done on my car and he does oil changes as well, go there...PINELLAS TOTAL CAR CARE, I just did a review on him if you want to learn about that experience.

Best Mexican Food in Tucson and not just for the food truck category. Also would put their Sonoran Dog up against any in town as I believe theirs to be the BEST! I honestly can not find one critical thing to say and could rant on all the positives for days. Just TRUST ME, this is a MUST go to when in Tucson. I eat there at least 3 times a week and stop by with all of my out of town guests. You truly cant beat the prices or the food! The late night hours are convenient as well.

Went there with a Travel Zoo voucher which ended up being a good deal.  Place was empty on a Sunday evening.  Service was attentive. 

The wine selection was decent as was the beer list.  Nothing to write home about but acceptable.  We got the fried mozzarella appetizer which was good.  These were decent, but its pretty hard to mess up fried cheese. 

We got two pizzas.  Both of which were good.  Not outstanding but good. 

Bottom line: 

Our bill was $79 for appetizer, 2 pizzas, 3 glasses of wine, and 1 beer.  I paid $29 through Travel Zoo which covered everything but 1 glass of wine and the beer.  The place was decent, but I would not have been thrilled with the place if I had actually paid $79 for what I got.

I was absolutely delighted by my experience at this hotel last week! I traveled with my daughter for an unplanned night ch needed mother-daughter trip not knowing what to expect after buying this room on Expedia the day before. Much to our surprise this waterfront location was completely clean, well staffed, hospitable, and accommodating. All amenities are inclusive complete with a complimentary breakfast and daily wine & cheese hour. Rooms and parking were very close and easily accessible. No down side in our experience. I will absolutely make the this our go to spot for future trips! Even outside rentals came complimentary from the hotel.  Not always easy to find affordability, location, and top service in one location. Highly recommended!!

Absolutely the best Thai food. The staff is friendly and the restaurant is laid out nicely, with intimate tables and a warm ambiance. We have tried a new dish every time, but always with chicken and shrimp pad Thai as the second dish, as well as tom ka kai soup. The hot sake also completes every meal.

I stopped in here tonight regardless of all of the poor reviews. I was staying close to this restaurant and thought what the heck I'll try it out. When I arrived the restaurant was fairly empty. I proceeded to the bar and sat near a TV and the bartender. She quickly showed me the happy hour specials as well as the menu.

They had some awesome happy hour specials on their cocktails. A martini was $5.50 and a glass of wine was only three dollars. This is an excellent place to stop by for a happy hour with your friends and family.

I ended up ordering the ahi tuna and  it came out perfectly rare with a light sear on the outside.  The service was good and the food was excellent. I understand that there are a lot of negative reviews on this restaurant. But I can tell you firsthand that at least at the bar the service was good and the food was excellent.

If you are looking for a great happy hour menu and some good atmosphere I highly recommend stopping at this joint, sit at the bar and you will have a great experience.

such a nice hotel. The most incredible sheets we have ever slept in. Breakfast is delicious and its FREE. Movie rentals at the front desk, nice bathtub, walking distance to the beach, close to state street, quiet, relaxing... amazing. We will be back :)

The best burger place I've ever been to.  Great variety of burgers, both in meat choice (including elk and DUCK, yes, duck), and in toppings.  You can order from a variety of burger/topping combos or build your own (I think build-your-own is better).  The onion rings are excellent.  The waiters are friendly. The burgers are great, and are all from grass-fed meat.  The booze is organic.  Best of both worlds - burger bar and environmentally friendly foods. They  have other things too, like salad and chicken, but I cannot imagine why anyone would get something other than a burger! Except, of course, the "Duck Duck Gouda".  Don't ask, just get it. Ambiance is casual - music is a BIT loud but at least it's good music.

Best meal of the year. Split the trip through Puerto Rico plate with my wife, both mofongos with carne frita, ropa vieja, and pastelon de amarillos (my favorite). Could not have been more satisfied with the food or the service. I'm pretty stingy with my stars, but this gets 5 without hesitation. Truly excellent.

Exceptional service, although the wait was rather long it ensured me that they took the extra time to throughly inspect the vehicle and found I had a bolt in my rear drivers side tire. I will be returning in the future. Walter is the best! He kept me up to speed with where they were at with my car and made sure everything was taken care of.
Good food, reasonable prices. Had Street Tacos  Wings & Fries. Lynn had Buffalo Blue Burger  All Good and Tasty. Come here a few times a year. Not a bad place to eat.

Def recommend this upbeat modern restaurant. Room fills up quickly so it is a must "make reservations" kind of establishment. Not only is the bar amazing but the kitchen staff work in a line of 6 or 7 (unlike I have ever seen) to put out this amazing and well thought out product. The ambiance is modern yet exuberant. My girlfriend and I had 4 courses and drinks. We probably spent over 2 hours there and watched 5 tables turn before we left. The staff is just like clientele base (young/modern, diverse, informative, and excited) while making you feel very welcome at the same time. Chef Sbraga is showing a great example of how to run a restaurant and how to keep consistency. He's made a great name for our school #jwu

Well, we have been to BJ's twice now, so here is what we think.

The good:
BJ's has a very broad menu selection with a menu that is twenty pages long.

The bad:
BJ's has a very broad menu selection with a menu that is twenty pages long.

BJ's is one of those restaurants that cannot decide if it is a steakhouse, a brew house, an Italian restaurant, a pizza parlor, a rib joint, or a burger place. As is so frequently the case with restaurants that try to do so many things, it ends up not doing any of them very well. The servers seem to have a lot of trouble answering questions, because there is such a massive amount to remember. Frequently they have to pass such tough questions as "can I get that with mushrooms" on to the kitchen manager, who appears to be in a black hole from which your server may never return.

On to the food. First visit we had salmon, which had a very nice flavor but was a bit over cooked. This time we first ordered calamari as an appetizer,which was nicely battered and fried with good marinara and horseradish dipping sauces. We then both ordered the rib eyes, each medium rare. The cooking was fine. The quality of the meat was terrible. We have been around a good while, and these were the toughest, most gristly rib eyes we have ever eaten, or at least tried to eat. When we arrived home, Rex the amazing wonder dog ended up eating most of them. He thought they were great. Then again, he eats cat litter.

Grandson had a burger and fries, which he gave his 8 year old's thumbs up to. If the ketchup on his face was any measure, both must have been good.

Beer selection was wide but not more than the average brew house.

So all in all, a great big mediocre for BJ's. If you are in the area of the Outlet Mall In Wesley Chapel, there are numerous other places to choose from. Think about them. Think about them hard.

This place is definitely worth the wait. 

Sometimes there's a line, sometimes you get a table right away, but EVERYtime you get an incredible meal and lite on your wallet. I love Hainanese Chicken and the chicken stock rice it comes with so I have to order this dish every time. For appetizer, you really have to try the satay skewers... I can drink the peanut dipping sauce til' I OD on it. hahaha 

Then there's the Malaysian style spareribs. It's not for everyone I'd say, but if you're ok with nibbling on small pieces of spareribs, this dish is definitely one to try. It's marinated in a red fermented tofu and that's where it gets the red coloring. Yum! The mango chicken there is also very good if you're not the adventurous type. 

Too bad I never have any room for desert, but I'm sure it's delicious!

I can't say enough about their beer.  It is so good and fun that it changes often.  The food here is also amazing.  Can't go wrong with the tacos, but the burger is the way I'll go from now on.  Their candied bacon and whiskey dills take it to another level.  Love this pace!

Amazing homemade chocolates and brand name candy. Candy is overpriced, but it still is delicious. They have every kind of chocolate bar in existence, along with all other candies. Wonderful fudge selections, great variety of little chocolate truffles. The store is filled and packed with wonderful, splendid candy.

Love this place! The wings are awesome...you gotta try the fried chicken at least once, it's crispy and yummy. 

The service is great, they are very attentive. We stopped going on the "other" Joe Bob's because the service was awful but this location is great. Check it out.

The Red Piano is a cool hang out spot if you want to just hang out and have a couple of drinks. My colleagues and I decided to try this out since it seemed like a cool place. Being told there was a dress code from the hostess the security said it would be okay for us to come in since we did not know.

In the middle of the restaurant was a red piano where they play the songs the customer requests, which is pretty cool because they add their own little style to each song. 

Down to the food, I ordered the crab mac n cheese which made me feel sick right after. The taste was not there, it was too salty and something about it did not taste right. However, for starters we ordered the meatballs, which okay nothing that would make me want more. The service was okay, our waitress was slow and it took a while for us to get our drinks as well as appetizers.

The first time I came here, it was interesting because it was new to me; the second visit not so much. Decent spices aren't a surprise as it is a P.F.Chang company. The problem here is that there isn't a lot of meat with the order, you tend to run out of meat before you finish your rice or noodles. Spicy sauce is also limited and does not cover (flavor) all the rice or noodles. So not bad but not great either. Consistency between preparations is also hit or miss, at the same lunch visit my daughter's meal hardly had any vegetables and they were all thinly sliced, mine had huge pieces of vegetables all were thickly sliced.

Upon entering the place I notice the somewhat dim lighting and dark colored chairs and tables. I found this to be a very nice choice with the majority of light being the natural lighting from outside. Very cool animal photos cover the nice earthy tones on the walls. The coffee was very good and obviously came from quality beans and roasting. Then I had the pumpkin muffin, which is pretty good. Not quite as good as the high quality, fresh out of the oven, homemade bake goods I am used to, but good for a store in a strip mall. As usual I had to check the potty out and the facilities were very clean as well as the state of the cafe itself. Clean is always good in this book! The service was prompt and friendly for the most part. The girl that waited on me seemed a tad bit condescending, but she probably fits right in with the apparent snobbish clientele in this joint. So no real loss of star for that. The only real flaw I experienced in this place was the God awful music that was playing. They really should consult someone, or me for that matter, to help them establish playlists to kind of satisfy a bigger array of customers. The music in here is so, so bad!! It's actually driven me to the point where I am gonna just down the rest of this coffee like it's an 8 am glass of whiskey and get on up outta here!!!

I just made my first official trip into The Khyber since its recent culinary and style rebirth, and it will not be my last.  The place is full of character, delicious southern-style food with fun twists, a great (though not exhaustive) beer selection, and knowledgeable down-to-earth staff.  You know what it is not full of?  Itself!  Always a refreshing bonus.

The meal in question was a Thursday, late-night, post-movie nosh with my husband after we had been turned away from a neighbor establishment that had randomly closed their kitchen early that night.  I was a little bit nervous, as husband has a somewhat limited (but expanding) palette, but we were hungry and thirsty and he was up for an adventure.  A summer weeknight in the city had the place pretty slow (~ 1/2 full bar, and just a few occupied tables), and we grabbed seats at the bar to keep an eye on the Phillies game.  The music was loud, but energetically rather than overbearingly so.  I was able to have a conversation with my immediate neighbor without shouting.

I had a difficult time deciding on food, as the menu was large and diverse, and there were also many specials available.  The overall influence was southern comfort food, but fancied up just enough to keep the comfort interesting.  I went with a great spinach salad with grilled shrimp, sauteed mushrooms and spiced walnuts topped with a simply delightful cane sugar balsamic vinaigrette, while my husband devoured a BBQ brisket sandwich with perfectly cooked shoestring (non-battered) fries.  I helped offset my nice healthy salad by succumbing to the temptation of a red velvet cupcake, which was only very good (rather than outstanding), but satisfied my sweet tooth nonetheless.

The bartenders were very cool about letting one sample a draft before committing to a pint (or half pint if you desire!), which is a nice touch.  When I requested a sample of a particular IPA (after finishing a pint of another), the young lady brought me a sample of the one I requested along with an additional IPA that she thought was even better.  She was right, and I appreciated her confidence in providing the recommendation.

My only regret is that I waited so long to actually try out the new Khyber after hearing the raves it was getting.  I am looking forward to many happy returns to explore their menu and see what fun new beers I can discover.

Not the best Chinese food I've ever had but not the worst either.  This place is alright.  I love the fried donuts they have for a dollar.  They are so delicious and come out piping hot!  I also enjoy their crab ragoons and hot and sour soup.  The fried rice left much to be desired.

Came here for brunch. I got the skillet de la casa and my wife the Dominican breakfast. Both were outstanding! The Bloody Mary was perfectly spiced and the cafe olla was one of the best coffee drinks we've had in a long time! Will definitely come back the next time we visit Indy.

The Posada Lodge is an old property. Probably built around 1980. Each unit is small. Attached to the lodge is a restaurant (cantina) featuring finger food and a large variety of tequila mixed drinks. The property has potential. Unfortunately the property has been neglected. It is rundown. Furniture, fixtures, walls the bathroom all need to be updated and revitalized. That said would I stay again on this property?  Yes if for a night. No if I was looking for a holiday destination.

I was fortunate to go here with work (they are quite pricey). However, this was a dining experience worth repeating. We were seated in a private room downstairs, but we hit up the bar area first. From there, we had a great view of the outdoor seating -- honestly, every place looked like it would a good experience. 

For our private room, we were seated with the wine, which was cool to see the selection. The service was fantastic -- only one of us had been there before, so he explained how the menu worked (everything is single service size) and made recommendations. We had a vegetarian with us and the only item they could order from the app menu (Tomato soup) and the entree menu Fried Green Tomatoes (as an entree). We also called ahead and asked if they could accommodate vegan (they said yes), but he ended up not attending. 

The food was excellent. I had the tuna for an appetizer -- delicious -- and the duck cooked two ways for an entree -- both ways were good. I ordered the blueberry crisp and port wine for dessert. Everyone else enjoyed their meal as well. 

Bottom Line: The location, service and food were a magnificent combination.

Can't do a fade to save their life. Walked in and gave very specific instructions to Sam on what I want and how to do it. Came out with the worst haircut I have ever received. Extremely disappointed and won't be going back

Real thieves!! Went for an inspection and they told me I needed front brakes and an oil change for my 2008 Nissan rogue which totaled $400. Both had recently been done. I also own a bmw and oil change and brakes don't don't cost $400. Amazingly coincidental is the fact that after I say I don't want them doing the work, my spark plugs all foul out and my truck won't start, costing me a day of work. I call to explain the situation to the receptionist and she tells me to call the state police. No thanks, I'll just call my lawyer! Crooks

Went here for lunch after a funeral service. It was not a happy day but the salmon salad was delicious. The atmosphere is nice and the staff are friendly. I also like that its so close to my house. Perfect for  date night

Let me tell you about this Red Lobster... they do a great job!


I ordered the lobster Maine with steak- this option gives you a choice of the filet mignon or Strip. I went with the strip . This meal comes with a salad. I ordered the caesar... and Mojitos.

My steak (medium...slightly more to the medium rare) was cooked perfectly! Very juicy. My lobster tail was delicious. The Caesar was very good as well. This meal will run you about $40, not including the mojitos.


The only reason this review receives 4 instead of 5 stars is due to my drinks, and the server. The drink wasn't terrible, but for the price they really skimped on the additives, which of course impacts taste. I love mojitos, and was disappointed by the scattered pieces of the single leaf of mint inside. 

I do not have the serve name for this review... however... a tall, tanned complexioned gentleman. My server responded and served, but was very standoffish and slightly abrupt in general. I observed him at other tables, this was his approach for all guests . He may need to be in the back doing something that does not involve customer interaction- like dishes 


... but for that steak... I will be back  just not during his shift

I'm from Spring Hill Florida. While driving home from sand key the kids wanted pizza so we saw the recommendation on yelp and we went....LEGIT!!! my chicken parm sub... top 3 I've ever had... garlic knots... killed everyone's in my area!! I was so surprised and happy! I asked the cook if he was from New York and to my shock he told me he was Albanian! Coming from an Italian I'm telling you that this restaurant is putting out better italian food than 97% of what I've sampled in the greater Tampa Bay area. Kudos to you Mr. Albanian... you're doing it better than most "Authentic" Italians! Oh and they were all smiles and very friendly! A++

This was my first time at Bernie's. My mom and I decided unexpectedly to go to brunch. We arrived shortly after they opened and were seated right away. Our server was nice and poured us water shortly after we were seated. She was also prompt in taking our drink order and then grabbing our drinks as well. My mom and I had ordered mimosas (which were pretty good) and coffee (which was not as strong as I usually like but probably on par for most coffee drinkers). Our server also took our order promptly as well. 

Then the downside was the wait for the food. It was definitely longer than normal. 

But once the food did arrive, it was really good. The breakfast potatoes were sooo yum and I enjoyed the French toast and bacon as well. I had ordered the Big Guy and everything turned out good. 

I really enjoyed the aesthetic of the place. The seats were super comfortable and there was a lot of great lighting. I'm not sure how the ambiance would be at night but I definitely enjoyed it for brunch! Will definitely be back to try the place again.

Ok, I've let over a month go by so I could write this free of emotion. I did my wedding block at hotel MONACO. The hotel itself is beautiful, which is why I didn't give it 1 star. Customer service was god awful. Between the many rooms booked, drinks and food purchased, my friends, family and I collectively spent 30k $ at this hotel, which for Philly is as expensive as it gets. When you spend this much, I expect to have nothing but the best customer service. Sadly I received the opposite. My correspondent at the hotel gave us a tour and said we were free to use the stratus as our after party location. However; when my guests arrived they were told they needed to pay 20$ cover each to get in. So I guess the 30k wasn't enough. When my husband and I went in (we booked the suite for 600$ a night) the bouncer started screaming at us for "trying to sneak in," pointing his finger about an inch from my eye ball. I told him who my correspondent was for the block and he said the stratus had nothing to do with my block, despite me being told the exact opposite. I went down to complain and the manager apologized. However at this point half my guests left because they were afraid of said bouncer. I was informed that he was fired as a result but doesn't change that the after party was ruined. I asked for some fort of comp/refund and all they could do was refund me 75$. Really, that's worse than nothing given what we spent on the block. The second issue was that all my guests missed my shuttle to our venue because driver was instructed to go to another street by hotel but hotel failed to inform any of my guests who were all waiting where we were told by the hotel to have them wait. When I called the hotel later to complain about this a manager named Christie said "let me stop you right there, we have nothing to do with hotel blocks. That's like expecting an ER surgeon to know how an emergency department works." Oh man was that the wrong analogy, as I'm an emergency medicine physician. I informed her that a TRAUMA surgeon certainly knows how an ED is run, that we operate in teams. Emergency physicians actually work integrally with trauma. Clearly the concept of working as a team with the various departments in a foreign concept to this hotel. I took insult to this comparison as she clearly was using this completely incorrect analogy complemented with major attitude as a tool to make her dissatisfied customer feel stupid. Too bad I'm a doctor and she's not. (As a side note, I normally never tell people I'm a doc or ask to be called Doctor as I find it to be pretentious.) I called management to complain but they told me there was nothing they could do as they already gave me the very generous 75$ discount already. Very disappointed. I've stayed in hotels all over the world and have never received such poor customer service in my life. They were acting like they were doing me a favor by letting me have my block there and give them 30k$. I've been treated better at hostels in developing countries. Seriously they don't deserve to have 5 stars despite the beautiful finishings and great location. Pretty sure 5 stars is supposed to imply nothing but the best customer service.
Visited again. Fantastic. French onion soup the best. Steak sandwich with mild horse radish and Gorgonzola cheese out of this world. A bit pricey but good grub.

The one and only sushi place to get your sushi fix in IV. I've been here a handful of times when I've been too lazy to go to Sushi Ahi at the Marketplace. It's never crazy busy and you get your order within 15 min if there's no one else around which seems a bit much, but I have enough patience to wait.
I'm not THAT adventurous when it comes to sushi, but I have to say their california rolls are pretty good.The cost of the sushi itself is a bit pricey for the quality, and sometimes quantity, that you get. I mean I got 2 mini hand rolls for 4 dollars when I could have gotten 2 large hand rolls for 6 dollars at the Marketplace. 
Bottom line: a good place to go when you are attacked by that sushi craving.

We got this once a few months ago for take out. I was pregnant at the time and craving some Chinese. Hubby was near here and wanted to give it a shot. We haven't eaten Chinese from anywhere else since then. 

90% of the time we get it as carry out and eat at home, but we've never had an incorrect order and it's always tasted fresh. We have dined in on occasion and service was always very prompt and attentive. 

I will say the to-go portions are larger than when you dine in. Also the kids sweet and sour chicken is large enough for both of my children to share.

It is by far our favorite weekly treat.

Chicken lettuce wraps and brown rice!
Bourbon chicken. 
Sweet and sour chicken with white rice!! 
All get a big thumbs up!!!

Massimo treats you like family and the food is delicious. He really cares about the community and is always reaching out seeing who he can help in our area. The restaurant is wonderful and a lot of it has to do with the people running it. Just awesome owners and great staff!

We wer at the Ipod, but et was Ihap! Oh ma gawsh et was good experence pare!

When I see da menyou, et was delicious bat expenseeb! So I expect it was many amount
I order da creoe internationel passport. Omg I taught I had to pay extra to leeb  in Edmonton!  Ay puta... jeez naman
Oke so when I pay the ten peeptee cent comboh I receeb da food . I expecting two eeklog many, bat they gabe me  Scrambled egg! I ded not order dat! Pak kabayo shet. And they r so paken cheap they use one egg to make da scramble! !! U tenk I am estupid!? Da proportion waz nat gewd!! I pay tew por price ob wan!!! Cheao oak naman!!

I well neber cum bak! I well only go to haps!!

I came in today not really knowing what I wanted. I asked so many questions and Kevin answered ALL of them and even gave me samples. I had mentioned a tea I tried a long time ago that I really liked and can't find anymore. He knew exactly what I was talking about.  He suggested brown rice green tea-milk tea with grass jelly. It's soooo good!!!! My only regret is not getting a large. I'm very impressed with Kevin's knowledge of teas, so much so I just had to write a review!!! Thank you again Kevin

I have been eating Brodo a lot recently and felt the need to give them a review. I do not think I have eaten anything I did not like. Their breakfast sandwiches are delicious and don't taste like fast food. Their soups are always great and their salads are always fresh. I hope this place lasts!
i dont often choose chains, but this place was pretty good. good service!

This is a beautiful p!ace. The parking is a nightmare, however. We spent the better part of an hour attempting to park. The parking lot is very small for such a desirable location.
If you do find parking, it is $10 unless you have a  national park annual pass which makes it free. 
The canyon is beautiful but IMHO it is not as pretty as the Saguaro National Park and is not as entertaining as the Arizona-Sonora Desert.  Museum

Okay the chicken wings are the stars. The other item in the menu don't stand out as much. You can find any of there other dishes at any Asian themed restaurant around town. 

Service, is limited so don't expect much dedication from your waiter. This isn't specific to the wait staff but the lack of one.  

You will enjoy a your meal in a relaxed environment.

Great place in the heart of downtown Saint Louis, right near the Arch.  Although known for their steaks, I got the port chops, which were moist, juicy, and super delicious.  There was two chops, and they were large.  Yum!  The staff was friendly, and our waiter was attentive.  Parking downtown was a bit of a bear, but what I didn't realize is they have a few parking spaces right next to the restaurant.  I'll be back!

We took our dog Stella here for the board and train service. We were moving from an Acre yard in the country of Monticello, IN to and apartment in the Carmel area. Ryan was a fantastic resource and they helped make the transition super easy! My dog was struggling with leash aggression and anxiety toward other dogs. Alpha K9 U was super patient with her and got her socialized with other dogs. Ryan was super great at explaining why Stella had those behaviors and gave us tools to help get her back on track. We have had her home for two days and she is a completely different dog! We are super excited to start her in the 6 week class! Thanks so much Alpha K9 U!

A nice and necessary museum.  I am grateful that Philadelphia has a plethora of attractions going back to a defining point in American history.  There is a lot that happened here, it is a pleasant experience.  If you are looking for a museum that has a lot of buttons and flashing lights, go to the Franklin Institute, this is not that type of museum.  If you are looking to stand in an historic place and soak in some information on the founding of this country, you have arrived.

Burgers were terrific: high quality beef, not greasy, delicious soft buns. The whiskey glaze on the one I ordered was perfect. Sacrilege to some, but I ordered mine well done and it was cooked through without being a hockey puck. Also, shakes were great.

I love everything about this place! The owners are very gracious hosts who regularly come out and check on everyone. The sake and wine based drinks are wonderfully refreshing! The food is as fresh as it comes. They deliver to the local area which is excellent for those of us doing trivia at the various breweries (Try Thursday night music trivia at Caledonia). Price is right, service is great,
I was extremely pleased with the staff, store, and my sales person. Absolutely great experience. I will go out of my way to do all my Best Buy shopping at this location.
Warm and cozy locale. Wonderful dumplings, bibimbap. Great service. BYO.

This place is awesome!!! Found it on Yelp for a dinner stop with a group of high school band students on a trip. Wonderful personal service and wow is the food fantastic! Bread and pasta and olive oil were wonderful and do not leave without at least one cannoli!

We love the cameras, it really gives us piece of mind being able to see what is happening. The last time our dogs were there, one started to get sick. The staff immediately called us (multiple times because we didn't answer) and told us what was going on. They asked what we wanted the staff to do and kept us updated if anything got worse. We truly appreciated the effort to keep us informed and it really feels like Camp Bow Wow has my pets best interest in mind.  Anytime we need a place for our dogs to go whether its for a night or a week, we send them to Camp Bow Wow.

A friend and I tried Cate Zone for lunch.  It's quite a little place, which I like, and the food was delicious!  We had the clear noodles with sesame sauce for an appetizer--amazing!  The sauce was fantastic, and the mixture of veggies gave the whole dish some great crunch.  I had the brisket noodle bowl, as well.  The meat was a little on the fatty side for me, but the noodles, broth, and bok choy were great!  There were many other dishes on the menu that I'd love to try.  The service was also quick and polite.  Great place for Chinese food that is more authentic and way more delicious than take-out orange chicken.

I've only been here once, but I'm definitely going back. I had the backed chicken, mac and cheese ,and greens and I loved everything about it. 

The best thing is that this is such a great community project. And those youngsters are SO attentive. They want to make sure that you never run out of bread or whatever it is your drinking. 

Will be back!

Wow, I don't even know where to start. 

My husband and I have been there several times and every meal has been outstanding. I'd list my fav things, but it would just be me writing a list of everything on the menu. But two things we always, *always* get are the potatas bravas (I think they're deep fried and the aioli is top notch) and the chorizo with pears and manchego.

We've been to brunch and love the 2 for 1 mimosas. They have a few different flavors and each person can pick their own flavor. It's a fun way to be adventurous (please do try the strawberry flavor).

Order some paella, get some tapas while its being made, and enjoy a pitcher of sangria. You won't regret it.

I'm so glad to see a local theatre like this in the outskirts of Nashville! They have a TON of heart here and I'd way rather give my dollars over to locals who are fantastically talented than seeing a blah blah whatever on the big screen. Of course I love the big screen too, but this is a great way to not only be entertained but support your artist neighbor. 

The good:
* The actors/singers/dancers - all the talent. They are really really good. They were much better than I expected and there were even a few of them that I think could easily compete with the pros. 
* It's charming. There's lots of heart. 
* The parking lot is big, it's easy to park and walk right in. 
* their website is good and makes it easy to order tickets in advance. 

The bad:
*The sound system, "band" (aka keyboard) and mics. OUCH. I'm maybe more picky than your normal joe, but boy could they use an upgrade. 
* One bathroom. ONE. On the night I was there we were seeing SPAMalot with about 40 Senior Citizens. Intermission took an eternity. Not to mention the bathroom is up front by the stage - making it awkward and interrupting if you need to use it during the show. 
* Uncomfortable hotel conference chairs. And if you're not on the upper raised part, you might get a ruined view if the person in front of you is tall or has big hair. Whah whah. 


You should check it out and support this wonderful troupe. We paid $18 to see SPAMalot on a Thursday which I think was painfully overpriced - but alas, I do want to support this kind of venture. I think most shows are under $15 which would be more reasonable. So check it out and enjoy these TRULY talented folks!!

Tomo is my favorite sushi place Old City! This place ticks all of my boxes: great food, great service, and great ambience. It is so rare that you find a place that does all three things so well. The food is top notch! The sushi is fresh with complex flavor: the Tomo and Margarita rolls are not to be missed. The wait staff is attentive and warm which makes Tomo a place you want to come back to time after time. The design of the space is clean, modern, and hip without being off putting and the aquatic life murals on the walls are gorgeous. Tomo is a neighborhood sushi place with prices and food that can't be beat!
The Salvadoran tamales are excellent and the tortilla soup is the best I've ever had.

This is the dirtiest Saint Louis Bread / Panera I've visited. All the tables we attempted to sit on were dirty. They got the order wrong (which is becoming too common at several Panera's in the past couple of years)

We went for like an Happy Hour thing and eh, it was ok.  The drinks are unique, but super strong.  The food decent but over priced.  

This would be one of those places you see drunk frat guys but scaled up, instead there were drunk real estate agents, lawyers and the like being loud and obnoxious.  

It was ok but I don't think i will be going back, I thought the happy hour menu items were way over priced although the pork sliders were pretty good.

Chips and blue cheese not so good. 

The rest of the apps we had were dynamite.  Clean oysters, mussels were amazing (ask for bread). Everyone loved the lamb, fish and chips, and the salmon.

Wait staff was very attentive, but not over the top, in your face.

Love, love, love the new addition to Doylestown. 

A welcome new a addition to the many duds in the area.

The atmosphere of the restaurant is wonderful! The service has always been up to par when I dine here. The wait is acceptable for an average dinner time, so long as Nashville isn't hosting a special event. 

The drinks are delicious, but can be light on the alcohol at times. The food, although delicious, seems pricey for the portion size. I could get a larger burger at Cheddars or even Applebee's. It seems you pay more for the ambiance of the restaurant than you do the food.

This  place is great.  I first got used to Chipotle in 2005 down in the Washington DC area.  I am extremely pleased they have made up the 95 corridor.  Where they can, they also serve beer.  This is great made to order mexican food with a very simple menu.  Don't be scared if you haven't tried it yet.  Jump right in, you won't be disappointed.

Took an out of town friend here for brunch this weekend. We had excellent service (friendly and attentive waitstaff), good food (omelet was delicious and tater tots hit the spot), and tasty drinks (can't beat bottomless bellinis)! We had a relaxing meal and enjoyed the retro-feel decor in this restaurant. I am glad I made a reservation as it got quite crowded by the door with people waiting for tables by the time we left. Overall great experience. Will be back!

Owners are friendly and courteous. The prices are sooooo reasonable. I went in with an armful of items that had been piling up. All in all, I think we had some 15 pieces and the total came out to a bit over $50. That included a couple heavy sweaters and one white dress shirt that was so discoloured, we thought for sure it was a lost cause. When we got back our clothes, we couldn't even tell which white shirt had been so terrible, because they all looked brand new. Turnover time was 2 days. Would highly recommend.

We live close by and wanted to try the place.  But as others have mentioned, our dining experience was lackluster and the noise level was extreme.  The food and drinks were not worth the 45 minute wait.

The only thing we liked about the food was the presentation - at least it looked pretty.  I had the Cajun Chicken Pasta, and there was nothing Cajun or spicy about it.  Very disappointed.  My wife had the Seafood Mac & Cheese, which was mediocre and a bit too runny.

The pitcher of Margaritas was small and packed with ice.  We each got a least a typical glass's worth, but it was nothing special.

Our waitress was admittedly inexperienced.  However, her personality and lack of attentiveness didn't help her cause.  

Sadly, I see no reason to go back.

Decided to say screw my weekday diet and try this place. Clean inside and ample parking which is nice for a change. I ordered the 5 wings with chili garlic and the honey glazed donut that comes with. Now I think of myself as a reliable source for wing opinions since it's my favorite food and I eat them way too much. Besides the sauce, these are by far the best breaded wings I ever had. Perfectly cooked, fall right off the bone, super crispy, moist, tasty breading - everything you look for in a breaded wing. The chili garlic sauce is good but I wish they had old fashion buffalo style. The honey glazed donut was delicious but Duck Donuts in OBX still holds the throne in my book.

Conclusion - a tad pricey but I will be coming here often and most likely tossing them in my own sauce at home.

Just ordered a bunch of munchies and thoroughly enjoyed a whole cheese pizza just for me :)  Cheese is #1 on my top 5 foods list and you can't go wrong here, the pizza is smothered in the good stuff.  I was pleasantly surprised with the broccoli bites and the zucchini fries were tasty too.
There are a handful of good people here. It is a shame the rest of them are very rude and unprofessional. You wait forever on your meds and then sometimes then give you somebody else s stuff!
Try the fish spread.  But bring cash because that's all they accept.  Very blue collar down to earth environment.  Great place for a quick bite and a drink, but not so much for a full sit down meal.

i visit this tasty, 9 dollar soon doob spot every time i go home.  no, seriously. every.  time.  

best soon doob ive ever had (with the exception of my momma's, of course)!  and quick too!  they come in a variety of flavors (kimchi, beef, mushroom, etc) as well as varying degrees of spiciness.  the meal comes with great panchan, a raw egg (to be added into your soon doob mid-boil), and a stone pot of rice which is later turned into noo-rung-ji with warm boh-ree-cha (barley tea).

the waiters/waitresses are so cute in the traditional korean garb and pretty much leave you to your delicious tofu unless you need something, then you can either flag them down or push the button on the side of the table.  ive eaten and sat there talking with my fellow soon doob loving friend for hours before, and they dont mind.

ALSO: you can call in your order ahead of time, so that it's nice and piping hot right when you get there to eat.

Absolutely best experience ever! For years we used the big companies and sometimes we received good service and sometimes not. With Steve at Combat Pest Control you always get the same great service every time! And if there is ever an issue with unwanted critters in between visits, he is quick to take care of it.  Will never use anyone else again!

We went for the lunch buffet. It was wonderful. A  GREAT DEAL! 7.99 for salad, drink, pizza and pastas.  They all tasted amazing and it was a nice quiet atmosphere. Definitely recommend for lunch or dinner

Best cappuccino I've ever had and of course the gelato is amazing. I would have given it a 5 star but I had to wait a long time for the barista to set up the gelato station and he didn't seem to be in a hurry AT ALL, even seeing that I was waiting with a small child.

Beautiful!  Nature and Christmas decorations under a roof out of the cold.  Take your time strolling and enjoying this peaceful place or stop and have some food/drinks and pretend you are in a rain forest somewhere.  Make a wish with a coin in one of many coy ponds, or take a little boat tour even!  Highly recommended to get you into the holiday spirit and get some exercise at the same time :)  It was quite magical.
Stopped in over the 4th of July weekend. Greated and seated right away. Try the Kobe Sliders and Goose Island IPA. Lots of beer choices
This place is amazing and is really good to there customers and I'm very impressed with there service and sandy was super amazing with us I would recommend her for everyone
Outstanding ice cream!!!  We will walk for 2 miles to get some Mike's!  The smoothies are good and the shakes are outrageous.  A must do if you are in Nashville....WOW!

Tina, Tammy and Hannah are so sweet. I recommend any one of them! I've tried all nail salons in the area, and for the price, kindness and quality they're so worth it. I get gel manicures and they last for at least 2 weeks without chipping! They do a really great job with the tips of your nail to prevent chipping.
Poor quality of food even if the prices are low and small portions. I would not go back sorry

I only come here because it's close and cheap and we don't have a freaking Target! Okay, maybe if they had a Wal-mart I wouldn't complain so much, but NO we don't even have that! 

I only come here when I'm in desperate need of something I can't get at Albertsons. Just the smell when you walk in is enough to make me turn around and walk right out.

Can someone please build a Target now?

I went here for a post Comedy show late night meal. The menu was bar food of salads, sandwiches, burgers and appetizers. There are TV's in every direction with all sorts of sports playing. 

I unique feature of Trident Bar n Grill are the 100's of steins hanging over the bar. You can order a drink that comes with the pewter stein and take it home to customize it. Then bring it back and it will live at the bar for you to drink out of when you dine there. Pretty cool. 
It was a bit too loud and so the combination of fans cheering, TV's playing and it being a late night for me was making me wonder if my timing for coming was just off. We had good service and the food was OK. I told a friend I was headed over, and they highly recommended ordering the Maryland Crab cakes. So as soon as I sat down I saw the menu had changed and there were no crab cakes. Boo. Once you get excited about something and it's sort of taken away it was hard for my heart to move on.

My husband ordered peel and eat shrimp which he liked and I ordered their Cajun burger; a burger topped with slaw and cajun sausage. For a person who likes all things New Orleans, this one was not for me. I could see many tables filled with groups of students having a great time and there were guys hanging outside near their motorbikes having fun. So it certainly it filling a niche, it just wasn't my kind of place to dine.

This is the best coffee available in the USA. Having lived in Brazil for 6 years, I developed a taste for strong espresso style coffee.
