Gruyere, white wine, morel mushrooms and spinach (I think), with two poached eggs nestled all in a small cast iron skillet.  Our server was Dave and he couldn't have been nicer or taken better care of us.  He also let us know that not only was Eddie nice (our bartender form the night before) he was also an award winning mixologist.  I can see why!

Our last day, heading out of town, we stopped at Maynard's Market to pick up something to take home to my son, and seeing the already made sandwiches in the gourmet case, we decided to just have lunch there.  I had brie and turkey on ciabatta and he had some sort of amazing club with bacon, pickles and who knows what else.  It looked great.  We grabbed a great organic hard cider to split and some chips and salsa and we were in heaven. I am sorry I don't know the name of the girl who waited on us but again, so nice and friendly.  I know the Market is going to change somewhat in the near future but I hope not too much. 

We will definitely be back sooner rather than later!

(a side note - while there for brunch, a family came in with kids.  There are crayons and butcher paper on the table and plenty of good things to choose from but they left.   The server was more than gracious about all of it.  They looked more like the ihop type anyway and it was definitely their loss.  I wouldn't have hesitated to bring my kids there!)

I ordered the turbo medium and it was the best burger I had ever had in a while. it was juicy and the jalapeños gave it a good kick. I had sweet potato fries and it they were a great compliment. seating was nice and the tables were very clean. would go back in a heart beat. try them if you're into burgers and want to be happy

I was disappointed that The Commons chose Tim Horton's as the retail space for their ground floor in the first place; however, I have given the shop several tries. The coffee is good, the breakfast sandwiches are fairly tasty. The staff is usually perfectly pleasant. The problem I have is that I have yet to get a correct order. Every time I ask for NO cheese, they add cheese to the sandwich. Today topped the cake..I asked very clearly for bacon and egg on a bagel, NO cheese - what do I see once I'm at work? Sausage and egg on a bagel. Seriously, how hard is it to tell the difference? Since they've argued with me in the past - "it didn't say no cheese" - I see no point in wasting my time going back to point out their constant mistakes and only possibly getting a correct sandwich. My only choice at this point is to stop frequenting this establishment.
Quick, quiet and great sushi.  This is my neighborhood sushi restaurant and we've tried nearly all sushi restaurant in Reno and Sparks.

Ate here again this morning and omylicious!!!! Keep up the great cooking and service!!! Highly recommend this place as a matter of fact there were quite a few customers today that were new. They were definitely enjoying their delicious breakfast!

I've always loved Pizza Hut but man...this place should strictly advertise take out only! For the last 5 times I've ordered delivery though the app (to get the deals) and every freakin time I get a call from them saying there's either no delivery driver and that they can never keep one! Funny thing is that Dominos doesn't seem to EVER have that problem and they're getting my business at this point since this Pizza Hut can never get it together with deliveries.

The customer service here is TERRIBLE. The lady working the front acted irritated and ignored my questions about the menu. She was on her phone the entire time and never once looked at me in the eyes. I was severely irritated and wanted to leave but since this is the only Chinese place in IV I was stuck. Even if the food is good most likely will not be back. She offered absolutely no help, would not recommend her at all !!!

The Blue Duck describes itself as a relaxed tavern featuring classic and new American eats. OK, I can go with that. I stopped in on a Tuesday night to the new Maplewood location with my father and stepmother. We got there right around six and we were the only table but after a couple of minutes it started filling up. Thank goodness because I have a thing about being the only table in a restaurant. I never want to eat somewhere that no one else wants to eat but we were OK here. Our server was friendly and pleasant but not that well versed on the menu. My father was asking about the Chow Chow side and she was trying to describe the flavor to him and I blurted out that it's pickled vegetables and she said oh yes, pickled is correct, they're pickled. So we ordered the Falafel Balls (harrissa tahini, smoked green tomato jam, cilantro, grilled flatbread) appetizer for the table. The grind of the chickpeas was too fine and the falafel had little flavor. The pita bread had a nice char but was very thick and cut in tiny triangles. The harrissa tahini turned out to be incredibly spicy and we are a family that likes heat. My father ate so much of the sauce he was sucking on ice cubes to relieve the heat. He was worried he wasn't going to be able to eat his entree. He ordered the DLT, a duck sandwich, and subbed the side for a small salad. The salad was tiny and no big deal but the sandwich he really liked. He commented on how moist and flavorful the duck was. My stepmother ordered the Seared Trout. This dish was beautifully presented and quite good. There was a tower of fried brussels sprouts on top and a squash puree under the fish. It was all excellent. As soon as I read the Pastrami and Pimiento sandwich I knew I had to order that. I love pastrami and I love pimiento cheese. I got the Mac N Cheese side which was just fair. The sandwich was delicious. I was only able to eat half of it. It was messy but good. I'd order it again and again. They ordered the cookie plate for dessert but I couldn't eat any. I was too full. The macarons looked delicious. Maybe next time.

New owners and fresh stock along with my old favorite goodies. I LOVE this store and LOVE the new owners. They seem to care deeply about their products and boy, do they deliver.  I was shopping for a gift for a friend who buys everything she wants. What to do?  Adam spent time with me patiently asking the right questions before bringing me to a display in the store -- and THERE IT WAS!  The perfect gift. Adam and his partner Morgan are the best. I would highly recommend this marvelous store to anyone looking for something special. 
     If you've stayed away because of a negative experience, walk into the new store with new owners and new and exciting goodies for home and gifts.

AWFUL & GETTING WORSE.  We live nearby so we've wanted very badly to like this restaurant.  If you enjoy greasy food that all tastes similar, dash right over....otherwise find somewhere else to eat.  When this restaurant first opened, the food was decent and drinks were great.  Really fun vibe.  The vibe has remained, though food quality has slid.  During our last (fifth visit), the margaritas were rushed, overpowered by individual ingredients.  So much so that we had to request side ingredients and mix our own at the table.  Keep your expectations low if you venture over....

Jesus Christ, get the wings. Hot n honey sauce and a bit of bourbon on the side. Allow your tastebuds to sore. 
But for real- good wings. Nicely breaded & fried. Sauce was great. I kinda want to get a few more. Big menu, lots sounds good. Decent bar selection & service was solid.

Well I was trying to avoid reviewing chains but this restaurant went above my expectations so here it goes...

This location just opened Monday, it is in the parking lot area of the Plymouth Meeting Mall. So parking is not an issue at all. The restaurant has a chic look using dark woods for their tables & decor along with black napkins & chopsticks. The plating is nice and creative. All of the dishes we tried were very good. Not overly saucey or salty, but well seasoned. Probably the best Kung Pao chicken I have ever had. Their Chang's Spicy Chicken (their version of General Tso's) was also very good, could have been less sweet & more spicy but still very enjoyable. Their array of mini-desserts were very tempting so I will have to go back soon & sample some. I am excited that they have an outdoor seating area since the weather is getting nice and the food was good.

The best thing they have going for them is the freshest of their items, which is something that is hard to come by these day in the Chinese food industry. I find that  some of their items are really good while other are lacking in the taste department. However, overall its a descent restaurant and they are just starting out; they will get better with time and experience.

I just had the best car buying experience of my life and it's all thanks to Jonathan Plasky & the amazing team at Crown Honda!

Thanks to Jonathan's outstanding customer service skills, I will never buy another vehicle from anyone but Jonathan at Crown Honda. 

Jonathan is the nicest guy you'll ever meet! He's friendly, knowledgeable, professional, technical, and down to earth. He goes above and beyond to assure you have an exceptional car buying experience.

I was given a great deal on my Honda Pilot and couldn't be happier. 

Jonathan and the team will make you feel like family.

I can honestly say that this was actually the best customer service experience I have had anywhere, ever!

I highly recommend that you buy your next vehicle from Jonathan Plasky at Crown Honda. Call 1-866-202-4593 and ask for him. 

I promise you; You won't be disappointed.

I thought I had found the world's best chicken and waffles until I went here. What a great place in dt Nola! My friend took me to brunch and she had the omelet and I had a tough time choosing, but ultimately took the waitress's advice and I couldn't have been more pleased. The pepper jelly is so fresh, the chicken is so moist, the waffles are so fluffy, and whatever cinnamon-butter with which  they top the waffles is divine. We also had a dozen oysters on the half shell, so fresh and clean! I couldn't recommend this place more for a really nice brunch experience.

Since it's quite a hike from both home & work, I don't get to Russell's often. So when a business meeting necessitated me being just down Centerville Road, I was pretty darned excited. 
   Now everyone who knows me knows my affinity for BBQ. The real stuff -- no boil in bag or microwave to reheat prepackaged crap. No liquid smoke. No gas grill. Real, cooked over wood smoke preferably on the side of the road BBQ. 
   So after my meeting ended around 3;00, it was off to pick up dinner. 
   The lot was empty so I pulled right up front to read the menu attached to the front of the building. When Ed, the young man working the stand saw I was getting out of my truck with my crutches...well, quick as a flash he was at my door ready to answer questions and take my order. Feeling the love...
   The only disappointment was that they were sold out of ribs. Ed gave me a menu and advised me to call early so they could save some for me. Fair enough. 
   They only do brisket on Fridays so I was left with "enough pulled pork to do one sandwich", but plenty of chicken. 
   So i ordered one each of the Yardbird Specials -- a Leg Quarter with two (generous) sides for $9 -- one BBQ and one JERK. 
   Both chicken orders came "southern soul food" style -- wet on top of two slices of white bread. I'm cool with that, or just chicken in foil -- with good chicken, either works for me. And there was plenty to share with not just one but two of my kids. 
   While both chicken orders were a little overcooked, Russell's holds them in their juices which keeps the meat moist. Since I was eating, not grading for competition, it was all about the rich and savory flavors. 
   The BBQ was very tasty -- a sweet, tomato based sauce. My favorite kind. 
   The Jerk was unlike any I've had from any Jamaican chefs -- it was wetter and less spicy. While a little more heat would be expected, frankly it was so good that I didn't really waste time worrying about it. I would drive back for either -- or both of them. 
   As for the sides, the first highlight was the sweet potato. I asked what they meant by sweet potato. Ed said "you know. We cook a fresh sweet potato." Then he hastened to add "but we cut them up and stuff." 
   Well, by "and stuff", that means they mash it and smash it and sweeten it and season it. The end result could be wrapped in a flaky pastry and be better than any sweet potato pie I've ever tasted. Two thumbs up. 
   I was told honestly that the potato salad isn't homemade (that's a pretty big mistake, Russell), but that they. "doctor it up". Ok. But not as good as homemade. Boil the potatoes while your meat is cooking. It will be well worth the effort. Use red potatoes and you wouldn't even need to peel them. 
   Then the greens. Honestly, I've never been a big fan, but I keep trying. Ed promised theirs wouldn't be sandy and they weren't. Nor were they tough, and not too bitter. Can I add butter to collard greens? With butter and salt I may like them more, but I may just have to get comfortable with the idea that I may never fall in love with greens. 
   Friendly, helpful Ed gives Russell's a bonus point. Loss of points for not cooking enough product (it was 3 pm on a warm and sunny Spring day) and the few other challenges noted above. 
   Solid 4. 5 needs to be more perfect.  
   Russell's is very good, but could be great.

I was looking for a new stylist that could give me a great perm, I've been to several and yet to find my home. So I had some time and called last minute and they were able to squeeze me in within the hour. Carol was awesome. She understood my concerns, she definitely knew what she was doing and had a lot of yrs and experience under her belt. Very delightful to talk with. I had a great experience and will go back!  and yelps 20% was a great bonus!

This place is a little gem for Conshohocken.  It opens early for people like me who have to arrive at work at seven in the morning. The environment is calm and exactly as a coffee shop should be. The decor is so cute and they collect owls which are my favorite! The girls and guys that work there are always so nice and so welcoming

Ive been here a few times and generally always like the feel of the place.  It's a good neighborhood bar with character.

Tonight I was a bit amazed by the service, or lack of it.  I arrived with a buddy for drinks and dinner, and arrived hungry.  When we sat at the bar, the bartender, one of about 5 people behind the bar working, came over and finally took our order for a drink.  We finished our drinks and wondered if they'd ask about food.  Instead someone eventually asked if we wanted another drink.  I had to suggest they take our food order which they said "OK, you know what you want?"  So we ordered.  

The food was great.  The drinks were great.  It was a while between times of my first drink being empty and my 2nd drink offer.  We were surrounded by staff that ignored us, essentially.  They were friendly overall, don't get me wrong, but they couldve encouraged us to stay longer.  When we finally asked for the bill, I saw that my friends cocktail was covered by happy hour, though my beer wasnt, from the first round.  Happy hour, huh, no one mentioned it even.  I feel like a good staff wouldnt ignore you and they would let you know there's a happy hour offer.

It's OK, all was OK.  Just weird when staff is aloof... when it's less than busy in a place.  You'd expect they would be more attentive and sell more food/drink.  (shrug).

I very much like this concept. If they would do some small but effective changes, I would give them more stars. I love good shawarma. We tried chicken and beef shawarma. Unfortunately, the bread was not the best. A proper shawarma has to be rolled into fresh bread and it shouldn't be inserted into a pocket of a pita bread that is not really fresh. The meat was seasoned a bit too much and it was very disappointing that the beef came completely cold (they replaced it by lukewarm beef) while the chicken was quite warm. Why don't they cut the meat a la minute made to order? This works well at traditional shawarma places. We also had the lentil soup and the fries. Both were quite good. I am a big fan of quality over quantity but for the shawarma they could add a bit more meat. Overall a great idea but poorly executed. For such an easy dish they should try to match the original.

You gotta at least try this place. After being a vegetarian for many years, I slowly added meat back in my diet. A friend who lives nearby says you have to try "Chinks". One bite and there was no turning back. I am convinced this is the best cheesesteak you'll find in Philly. Fries are just average; but they do make great egg - creams, shakes & fountain sodas.Wacky Wednesdays you can get a large cheesesteak for $6.50

almost good as AT&T park where the SF Giants play......almost. 

the interior of the park is great.  wide variety of food options, lots of different beer options.  sat in the nosebleeds and had a perfectly great view of the field.  updated jumbotrons.  even the fans weren't as heckling as i thought they'd be seeing that my friends and i were in the opposing team's gear (go giants!).  zito was keeping us safe though bc he gave up 4 hits to the phillies in the 1st.

i do miss the view of the bay and no one could tell me what the "phillies" actually were.

For our 1 year anniversary my girlfriend scheduled me a classic facial at Rescue. It was my first facial anywhere, but something tells me that Rescue is at the top of it's game. We were greeted as soon as we exited the elevator and escorted to the lounge area. We were offered water or tea (I had the cucumber water. Yum!) 

We sat down and looked around and waited for my appointment. I was taken in pretty soon and my gf waited in the lounge area for me. I'm really bad with names. I believe Rachel was the person who did my facial? I hope that's right. She was wonderful. She assessed my face, I put on the robe and then she went right to work. The conversation was good and she told me a lot about my face and what it needs. It was very informative. My face also felt AMAZING afterwards. I felt like I was glowing and I had a huge confidence boost for the rest of the day. 

I didn't feel like any products were being pushed on me, which I appreciated. She did recommend one product that I bought that day (Lotion P50) and I'm excited to look into her other recommendations. 

I had a perfect experience here. I can't wait until Winter so I can get another one! (They recommend quarterly facials for my skin type.) 

I also got my eyebrows done while I was there and tinted. They look perfect! They really do look like I have naturally perfect eyebrows. They don't look overdone at all. I also have very fair brows and it is amazing what a difference it makes having them a little darker. 

So yes, this was my first spa experience, but I'm thrilled I had it at Rescue and I can't wait to go back. My girlfriend also gets an A+ from me for picking this place.

EDIT: I forgot to mention that she stayed in the lounge area for the hour I was getting my facial and she said the staff there was awesome to her. They offered for her to take a steam (she didn't though) and they consistently made sure she had a drink. She just relaxed and read magazines and said it was actually really nice and relaxing. I was worried about her being bored so that was lovely to hear.

Ordered from Uber eats. It was delivered HOT. All 5 Stars could go to the Macaroni and Cheese. It was that good! But I also have to give a shout out to the amazing Meatballs. Everything we ate here was pretty delicious! I'll be coming back for sure.

After going to this restaurant a few times and getting decent service and average food (Value for Money) I decided to take my friends for mid-week dinner.  Upon arrival we asked to be in the back patio which they accommodated.  It was a weekday so there were a lot of open tables and I noticed 5-6 staff congregating around the kitchen talking as we went to the back outdoor section. In most restaurants patrons are usually greeted by a server within a few minutes and given water and a drink order.  I actually made note of the time after about 5 minutes and then waited another 5-10 minutes just to have a waiter greet us and take our Wine order with water.  We waited another 10 minutes just to get water and an additional 5-7 minutes for our wine.  So, after arriving we did not have even water until almost 20- minutes after getting seated and 25 minutes for our first glass of wine. Keep in mind the restaurant was less then half full...on a Wednesday, all while staff were congregating at the kitchen watching.

Then, after waiting another 10 minutes we actually had to track down another waiter just to order our food!

When our dinner was served the Chicken Piccata was served very dry/overcooked.  My GF mentioned it to both the waiter and the manager on staff and they both appeared to act like it was no big deal, no offer to re-cook it or comp even a glass of wine,,offer a dessert, nothing.  If this was a normal restaurant that charged $15 -$20 for a simple Chicken Dinner I would still expect it to be prepared correctly or fixed but $26 for a simple Chicken Dish with mashed potatoes and some greens was quite high in cost IMO...but I understand the overhead in Montecito garners these prices...but really,, dry and tough,,no attempt to make it better.  

Two of us had empty wine glasses and once again had to track down the water for a refill.  

I liked this restaurant in the past and hate to grade it based on one dinner but the attitude of both the waiter and manager was unacceptable and almost like they were upset that we had to mention anything to them.

Doubt I will go and spend another $150 + tip for three people to have two glasses of wine each , two simple pasta dishes and one basic Chicken dish.

Very disappointing! We went to dinner early with our children to avoid the crowd and we won't be going back. First, they were out of kids menus, sprite, & straws. Did i mention the server was sloppy and not professional. When the food came out the chicken was raw in the middle on two of the four entrees ordered. The soup was ok and the cheese sticks were good, but the marinara was horrible and tasted bitter. I would hate to see how things are at a later dinner when they are busy.

(3.25) ~ pretty good overall food & service

MENU:
* S'mores Sundae = (3.25) pretty good frozen custard, although Wisconsin is still my gold standard;)

Best Latte in StL.  I have been trying to find good coffee since moving back and I finally found a great spot.  I didn't try anything else but ifs its half as good as their lattes, then I will be happy.

Went in for dinner, sat at the bar, good service. 

I had high expectations for the food based on reviews here. We started with the bacon grease popcorn - I really didn't think it was anything special, and I could still kind of taste it the next day. We ate  half the bag. We then had fried oysters, fried green tomatoes, and the Boudin Balls. Of these the only one i would order again is the oysters. The other items were kind of meh. Dinner for me was brisket with mac n cheese and beans on the side. The Brisket was good. I'm not going to call it great, I've had much better, but it was good. The mac n cheese and beans fall into the same category. Huge sides. I ate maybe 1/4 of them, maybe. My cohort had the pulled pork sandwich and declared it excellent. Am I glad to check this off the list? Yes. Do I wish I'd gone to Amada or Buddokan for dinner after drinks at Khbyer Pass Pub, you bet I do. 

great place for drinks - really, but i think i'll leave it at that. Maybe the oyster app.

My favorite Farmer's Market!

Amazing vendors - Baetje Farms (superb goat cheese), Salume Beddu, Whisk (their popsicles are both interesting/refreshing/delish), Double Star Farm, MO Grass Fed Beef, Companion....etc. 

Food Trucks! - A big fat Holy Crepe or I love love love The Big Cheese - making grilled sandies utilizing all the local ingredients, found at the market - how perfect is that?!

Free Yoga! - It's at 9 a.m., and the instructor is f-ing hilarious.

This place is just full of activities - yogis, foodies, kiddies, and in summer, usually some live music and/or a wedding happening at Piper Palm House. 

Best in St. Louis! -  says the yogi who loves fresh foods (is there any other way to get tomatoes and lettuces?)

Everything about this place is great! The ambiance, service, food, wine, location, and hours of operation are all wonderful. The food is delicious with generous portions; great selection as well. Service is super helpful. We had Jodi who was exceptional but everyone is great. The wine selection and cocktails are great. They don't even mark up the wine when purchasing by the bottle; very unusual for a restaurant! I love this place.

It's hard to get a day-of reservation, especially on the weekends. Fortunately if you are planning on dining alone or in a pair, it is easily to find seats at the bar where they have full menu service. 

The bar is a little understaffed, and with all of the drink orders coming in from the tables, there is a high possibility that you will overlooked. Still, I commend the bartender who was serving me for being as attentive as he possibly could (which was very little attention). 

I ordered the seafood gumbo and the braised pork belly from the appetizer menu. The gumbo was good, but not particularly outstanding. Compared to the other gumbos I'd had the past few days, I'd say that it would rank about average. The braised pork belly on the other hand was phenomenal. The smokiness and sweetness (from the glazed pears) of the pork went very well together. The lightly dressed baby spinach salad was a perfect complement to the appetizer. Very well done! I only wish I had a bigger piece of pork belly!!

I'd definitely recommend this restaurant for out-of-town visitors and for anyone you really, really want to impress. :)

Tonight was our first visit to JB Dawson's after several years of being in the area for Sesame Place and we loved it! Definitely recommend calling for reservations which I did just a couple of hours in advance and was thankful since everyone was starving. Our sever, Matt was excellent. The food was fresh and prepared well. First "sit down" dinner in a long time where everyone loved their food. Great cocktails, great food, great service and kid friendly as many previous reviews stated.

I can't really say enough good things about BK's northern location. If you want the prices and quality of a good taqueria, but want a nicer sit down atmosphere with table service, I don't think that you can find a better place.
BK's is famous for their Sonoran dogs now, but their other food is just as fantastic, if not better. I would submit that they have some of the best carne asada in town. Cheap too. Tacos run $1.50 (cheaper than Nico's even), and not just for the asada ones: their pastor meat is also fantastic and runs at the same price. Great tortillas and they come loaded with meat.
A favorite of mine is also the caramelo, usually the carne asada one (I think the pastor tastes funny with all that cheese). They have a small and large size, but only the small comes with the corn tortilla option. Personally, I like their corn tortillas better.
As far as the dogs go, they run $2.50 per and come with a nice grilled pepper. They have a condiment bar that includes two kinds of cheese, guacamole, red salsa, green salsa, cucumbers, avocado sauce, radishes, etc., etc. That alone should make this a higher-end place but, like I said, it's really very cheap.
The service is always really nice too. They'll take your order at your table, refill your waters, even pick up your check when you're done. The servers always do a good job.
Honestly, I haven't tried the majority of the items on the BK menu, just because I can't get past my standards. If I go, I have to get a hot dog and a carne asada taco or caramelo. If I don't get those, I'm always left with a "What if?" in my mind.
The only negative I'd give out is that their chicken sucks. Seriously. It's that fake, water-injected stuff. Why the other meats are so great and this one is so terrible I don't really understand, but you just need to stay away from the chicken options. Get at least a carne asada taco.
So if you've never been, you should go down. Probably now. They're good for lunch and dinner. They even have breakfast!

Cool little place off the beaten path. I stopped here for lunch after leaving one of my jobs, but didn't realize they stop serving lunch after 3pm. I was a little bummed out, it was only 3:30pm when I got there. But I drove out there so I stayed for a glass or wine, which all the wine on their list is local, I thought that was a nice touch. There are so many good wineries in the area. My server recommended a nice white wine, can't remember which one, but it was good. As I was sipping it and taking in all the oddities on the wall he asked if I would like a bowl of soup or some chili. I went with the chili! The wine and chili was an interesting combo! But I was so happy to be feed and be in this odd little place I didn't care!
Best VW and buggy place in Southern AZ if not the Southwest.  The staff are knowledgeable, friendly and professional.

Love this place!  Our first time in yesterday and it was delicious.  The staff is friendly and creative.  Francisco was an artist and made amazing and beautiful creations!  Thank you to all the staff and this will be one of our regular spots!

Had a wonderful time at this property; it's very new and chic.  We enjoyed the roof top bar; the bartender Derick made some great recommendations for us to try.  Also ate in the street level restaurant which was ok, just ok.  The bartender there wanted my credit card before she would give us a drink, very strange.  The concierge, I forgot his name, was excellent and recommend a great area Italian restaurant; Bistro Romano.  He also gave us some tips for hitting the historical sights which worked our very well.

This is the first time l have ever been to a Cracker Barrel. I went with my sister and her kids. The table I was seated at had ketchup on it. I didn't realize it until I put my arm down on the table. This was way before we got food or drinks. The floor behind me was filthy as well. Ketchup and left over food on the floor between our table and the table behind me. I never would have paid attention if it wasn't for my niece dropping her toy constantly on the floor. That's enough to be hesitant to stay. Then we get the food. The fried chicken and macaroni & cheese were the best part of the meal. My mash potatoes were barely like warm in the middle, & almost cold. Plus the mash potatoes and fried apples were bland. The gravy they used on the mash potatoes was really good also. Right after I left the restaurant, my sister pointed out a bunch of food stains on my back. Needless to say I was shocked. I just bought this shirt the precious day in NY at the Nintendo store. Now it's ruined. I washed it once and it still hasn't came out yet. I am not happy since I do live out of state on the west coast. It's not like I can go back easily and grab another. 
My only positive on this restaurant was the staff. The staff was very polite and offered us great service with 2 rambunctious 3 year olds. From the wait staff to the store staff everyone was polite. 
Despite my positive on the staff I don't want to go back their anymore. Even to the one and only restaurant that's open in my city. This place did not live up to its hype. Maybe it should focus more on the restaurant side rather then the store. The store despite the crowd was impeccable. Nothing out of place and a person to put it back as soon as it was moved. If the restaurant had that same attention to detail, it would improve it a great deal.

I really like Country Sweets.  I've gotten several cakes and cupcakes from there, and they were all delicious.  I also got the cakes for my twins' first birthday there - a large cake and two smaller smash cakes, and they decorated them beautifully.  I am a huge fan, and I'll be getting the cake for their second birthday from there soon, too.

Bowling for 2016 state tournament the place was very clean ...Great staff and Good Food
Will be back

I went to Tako to grab a quick solo bite before meeting my friend M for a Hunger Games viewing. (Awesome movie, btw.) The service was great and the place is really cute. The fountain in the front provided a nice soothing water white noise and awesome private rooms with sunken tables and seating areas where you have to take your shoes off. :)

I tried the Sweetheart Roll with spicy tuna and mango with tuna on top; the tuna roll and another roll that I don't remember the name of with shrimp tempura inside and tempura banana on top with a sweet sauce. I loved the sweetheart roll, especially the heart presentation. Too cute. The tuna was really fresh and tasty on both the sweetheart and the plain tuna roll. They weren't shy with the fish either! The banana/shrimp tempura roll was a little too sweet for me together so I ate the banana separately but I still enjoyed it.

I would definitely return to Tako if I happened to be in the area.
Beautiful space during the day, but expect to hear every drunk clown with the open air layout.  Hotel staff will make zero effort to remind people that some guests do actually sleep before 3 AM.

By far the best sushi we've ever had and we've dined at Michelin starred restaurants such as Sushi Ran in Sausilito when we lived there. The place is a hole in the wall in an anemic strip mall in Chalfont. Do not let this minor detail discourage you. The inside is sleek and beautiful.  The staff is friendly and attentive. It's a BYOB and two doors up, there is a wine store. We had oysyers, sashimi and 4 rolls. All amazing.  The himachi was an inch thick and about 3 oz. which is unheard of at shushi restaurants.  The Manhattan Monkey and Snow Mountain were our favorite rolls by far. The sushi chefs take their craft very seriously. We are going to try the sushi boat next time. It came with an ice sculpture! Wtf? What an excellent meal.
I really enjoy this thrift store - worth a visit. Ask for Mary - she's the BEST.

This casino was a joke. So let me get this right, $900 for two night stay during the middle of the week. $900 for a basic room.The high prices were definitely attract people to spend money at the casino. What a joke

Outside, this teashop looks very unassuming, but inside? Wow!
Cally's Teas has an excellent selection of teas that you've most likely never heard of (Ice wine tea anyone? The answer is YES PLEASE!). They're high quality and full of rich flavour. 
If you're looking to take your tea experience to the next level, I suggest you try some of their freshly bakes scones. They come served on a lovely platter with a side of fresh cream and jam. **drool**
The owner herself (Cally!) is usually in the shop, making sure you're enjoying your experience. She's incredibly friendly, approachable, and makes a genuine effort to get to know you. 
While tea and dessert at Cally's isn't super cheap (it's not super expensive either), you definitely get what you pay for; delectable teas and baked goods, knowledgeable and friendly staff who go above and beyond, and an overall great experience. 
To top it all off, Cally's Teas takes customer service to a whole new level. When I mentioned that I was lactose intolerant, I was quickly informed that they didn't have any lactose free options for me... BUT, I was told by Cally herself that on my next visit, I should call ahead before coming in, and the staff would make sure to have a lactose free option available and waiting for me. 
:O!!!!! Customer service like that is hard to find. 
Tell ya what Cally's Teas, I'll definitely be back... and I'm bringing everyone I know.

Really friendly staff and the inside decor is cool. I liked the old-school diner concept with mostly stool/bar seating. Our food was great and didn't take too long. This was my favorite breakfast while visiting in Nashville.
OMG Amazing  food and it's fresh definitely a hard place to pass without stopping in for some food

Pretty sure this place is brand spanking new, walking in you can smell the newer construction of it. It kind of has a retro decor look to it, but with a modern-day twist. Located literally right off of I 69, it's very convenient for those traveling through. It's in a newer section of Fishers, so it's not surrounded by very much business or housing. There's a brand new espresso bar right next-door and a plaza to put new businesses in that are not yet established.

The employees at the front desk were very friendly, courteous, and attentive. There's a continental breakfast offered here that had an assortment of your typical hotel continental breakfast. Waffles, scrambled eggs, sausage, cereal options, yogurt, fresh fruit, oatmeal, milk, and juices. Lots of seating available for breakfast! Fresh water with cucumbers and lemon was always available at the front desk as well. They also have a small snack shop by the front desk.

The rooms have a small coffee bar area, microwave, and refrigerator. The bathrooms are huge with gigantic walk in showers. There was not a bathtub in the King room. TV included cable and online options such as Netflix, Hulu, Amazon to access your accounts. Plenty of USB hubs on the desk and on the alarm clock by the bed. Beds were comfortable, linens were clean, and pillows were fluffy. There's a really nice fitness room and there's also a pool and hot tub.

The only con was the parking seem to be somewhat limited, although I was able to always find a spot. Hotel is not huge, only three floors.

Absolutely wonderful ice cream! The place is very small but has authentic homemade ice cream. The options include drinks, cones, and sundaes.  Last night the line to get in was down the street, they are so popular. 

 It is cute for families and the restrooms for customers are spacious. They only have one male and one female restroom but that is sufficient for the small ice cream parlor.  The only issue I see is the restaurant is that the restroom is large but does not have baby changing table. Odd since it is a family ice cream spot and they should accommodate families better.
This location is overpriced. The room was not even cleaned to my standards. The toilet still had pub hair on it from the last guest.

SB Adventure Co is amazing! I first posted this on tripadvisor, but I was so happy with the experience I thought I'd add it here, too:
I had always wanted to try kayaking, and SB Adventure Co. made it a really fun, safe, and exciting experience! The guides were attentive but laid back, and they made sure everyone felt stable and secure before heading out for adventure. I had a great time navigating around the harbor, checking out the pier, and playing kayaking games facilitated by the guides. In fact, I have kayaked every weekend since I first tried it with SB Adventure Co. I highly recommend trying out any activity offered by this company - in fact, I plan on doing the bicycle wine tour next!

I eat here every time I find myself in New Orleans. It has consistently been a favorite dining experience. Ambiance is comfortable with a slightly masculine feel. It's good for a date night or dinner with friends, but also perfect for a business occasion as well. My favorites: Mint Julep, Crab & Corn Bisque, Croque Madam w/ fries. Another notable is the sausage plate....but it is a comically large amount of meat...shareable.

Had brunch here recently and really enjoyed the food as well as the decor and friendly service.  Loved the shag carpeting and lodge feel.  I had the turkey sausage, Swiss and arugula omelette, hubby had spinach omelette. The turkey sausage was flavorful - hubby said it tasted like it was from his home state of Louisiana - spicy!  We noted that there were no salt and pepper shakers on the table, but the food didn't need the extra flavoring, it was very good.  The tator tots were amazing, and we also had some hot chocolate muffins with raspberry jam that were moist and delicious.  As it was a brunch and not breakfast menu, there were also items like Mac and cheese, turkey burger, etc, and I couldn't look (because I was stuffed) but there was also a dessert menu - which seemed strange at 10 am).
It was a lovely breakfast and I look forward to the opportunity to return.

What an eclectic hipster joint, right in the heart of Ybor. The restaurant name alone fits the atmosphere perfectly. The menu options are unique, what might sound like it wouldn't mesh on the palette ends up making you want seconds and if drinking enough-- thirds. This is a great place to have a drink and a scrumptious sandwich on a Sunday. I had the bird and pig, perfect combination of savory and sweet.

I'm only giving this 2 stars because the staff was friendly.  However, the food was mediocre, had to return silverware because food was still on it.  Ordered enchiladas and a taco combo.  Paid for the queso add on.  I received an enchilada with no enchilada sauce.  So, my cheese enchiladas were just a tortilla and cheese.  Taco was good but then again... it's just a taco.  Also ordered the Texas margarita which I was told was better tequila and stronger.  It was stronger yes but the cheapest tequila was used.  I had to put some sweet & low packets in it to take some of the horrible tequila taste out of it.  My fiance ordered a chicken enchilada and burrito and he could not tell which was which.  We stopped here on a whim on our way to a friend's party.  But, we will never go there again even if we are close by.

To keep this place running there has to be some changes. First of all the workers here have to be more friendly and understanding, instead lack of interest in what they do. There was a Time when I came to this store 5 minutes before they closed  but they were already closed. I drove 5 miles going about 60/mph average for that BPJ Ice Cream and they are not going to give it to me because they felt like going home early would make the owner more money :(

I received immediate attention when I walked in the door.  A lady asked me if I was there for a driver's license or for motor vehicle.  She waved me to the counter immediately when I said I needed a title.  She was quick, efficient, and friendly.

Just found, and tried the place last night on recommendation of a friend. We ordered pierogie and meatloaf potato skin appetizers, a burger and ciapino with rum and coke and a Blue Moon. Final tab was $45, fair price. My wife could not finish the burger. The appetizers were very good except they were probably frozen as the potato seemed a smidge mealy.  Still acceptable, my wife did not notice it. The burger was huge, a full 1/2 pound and a very fair price and very good. The ciapino was really Frutti Di Mare, seafood over linguine. Ciapino is a seafood " stew" but regardless, it was good. 
On the positive, We went at good time as the appetizers were reduced price, $5 and beer was discounted due to happy hour. The menu is varied with a "multicultural" type selection which made it interesting. All burgers were 1/2 pound and seemed to be well worth the price. Place is clean, comfortable, nice decor and was quiet but that could change during a sporting event.
Downside was, I wanted to order the home made gumbo but they were out. That is a major faux pas. However, due to our good experience, I will probably give them a "pass"this time.
It's a good local place, fair price, reasonable quality food. Probably a 3 1/2 Stars
Ordered the Uno, Italian sub and original wings.  All were delicious and by previous posts there was no issue with the employees.  Highly recommend.

Their facility is very nice. Didn't care for the flavor of their coffee. Went twice. Once too busy so left. Other time deserted. Wondering if Vanderbilt has classes on tu/thurs so they get crowded on these days and not m/wed/fri.

No stars, can't even get two plates. They just stack the slices on top of each other, even if there different kinds of pies.

One bite & had to spit it out. 
Worst $16.00 I ever spent, 2 slices & drink. 

TERRIBLE!!!!

This picture is in portrait mode on the iPhone 8+ so use your imagination the further you look back in the photo or just focus on what's in front of you.
Attached is a picture of my order, which is Chicken & Waffles with a side of Pimento Cheese Grits. In the back is a Pineapple Mimosa which was delicious and even further back is a Cranberry Mimosa. I would highly recommend this spot for anyone who wants to take a good nap after they dine. This food filled me up and I emptied my plate (the grits first, mimosa next, then the food). Bourbon and Branch offers a chill vibe and cozy seating, excellent staff, nice prices, and delicious mimosas. If you're looking for a good weekend brunch, this is your spot! 
P.s my social dm's were flooded with ?'s about where my food was from after I posted it.
Delicious organic burger, but a bit overpriced for the size. Sweet potato fries excellent, but also overpriced.  Service is good.

I have experienced better. When we arrived the place was reasonably packed and continued to fill up, which I think is usually a good sign. 
Except for getting us water every minute we wanted it and needed it....The service was mediocre, inexperienced and generally apathetic. When our food got there, the waiter/busboy asked for my friend to take the plate from her. 
Then there was the food, the pico de gallo salsa was pretty good and smokey. The margaritas were overly sweet. My friend and I shared the brisket sandwich and it was a big disappointment. The brisket was overly fatty and the fries were extremely salty. 
Skip the trip, go check out the other great Mexican places that the city and Northern Liberties has to offer.

My co-worker and I went here for lunch two weeks ago. Being in the hospitality industry, I try to support independents over chains. 

My cousin and son RAVED about the perogies at this place.  My cousin loves it so much, he even drives from Northwest of the city to this southside establishment for lunch!   To share his love of the perogies here, he buys the frozen products to share with his family.  How could I not try this place out?

Prices for their lunch combos are good. My co-worker and I thought there was a tad too much dough but not enough to nitpick over.  My kubasa was good store-bought tasting but he found his meatballs were a bit small for the value.  One disappointing factor is that bacon and onions were not available.  I happen to like my perogies with as much fat as possible.  Bacon and sour cream, please.

Service SUCKS.  Unfriendly isn't a strong enough term.  It was our first time there and we were just reading her menu to decide what was the best menu combo to get.  When the lady came from the back, she asked us what we wanted.  We advised her we just needed a little time as it was our first time there.  She stood there and after ten seconds snarked at us to place our order.  

When she was dishing up my co-worker's dish, she put a dollop of sour cream on his perogies without asking and when he said "Oh, no sour cream on mine, thanks." she said "oh, well...I'll just transfer it to her plate."  Well...how about asking a customer if they want sour cream with their perogies first next time?  That way there is no waste? Isn't that like asking if a customer wants cream or sugar with their coffee instead of prepping it to your own preference?  

Decor is odd.  Very much like a cafeteria feel.  Doesn't affect the rating as this location is casual dining with prices to match.

We will never come back.  Even if the food was FABULOUS (which it wasn't), we would never part with our money for this business' gain.  There are other perogy places that I will make an effort to try next time.

People need to understand that good food alone is not enough to be successful.  A smile and good customer service is free but reaps rewards.

First time visit on my "Random Bar Wednesday Evening Tour". Small place, good mixed drinks ( priced right ), and Jacob was attentive and engaging. All and all a great spot to get a drink. Next week Public House.

When I pulled up I thought what did I get myself into. The crowd with me was like what is this place... Then the doors open and the fun begins, the staff and nick was absolutely awesome. As I am
Typing this we have had 4 appetizers , salad, bread and pasta. Then danced the night away and now waiting in the next 5 items in the menu. A little outside of Nashville but well
Worth the drive. A true value for 50.00 and they let you take the left overs.

My friend and I have gone to this gym for a year because of the location. Machines are broken and it's weeks before they are fixed. That's if they even get fixed. Took away music channels and lots of the tvs don't work. Someone left a water bottle on the floor and 3 weeks later it was still there. Machines don't get wiped off and the trainers never tell new clients to do this. Plus unless you pay extra for a trainer they are  very unfriendly. Sent 2 emails about my concerns NEVER got an answer. Poor management if there even is any.

Fantastic.

Great service. Great food. My sister and I had out last meal in New Orleans at Luke. We had planned to have dinner and then head over to the French Quarter, but we ate so well at Luke that we took out happily stuffed selves back to the hotel to relax.

My sister had the Croque Madame which she loved and I had the Luke burger. The homemade fries are delicious! Our drinks from the bar were well made and the meal was topped off with a box of chocolates brought with the check.

If Luke were in my city, I think it'd be on my regular rotation.

For those of you who want to hold your wedding here, do your research.  This place has great food in an awesome, historic location at a decent price.  The rack of lamb is juicy and tender.  The venison stuffed mushrooms are simply awesome.  Eat the food, relax, and check out the mini jailhouse next door.  I'll be back.

I love this place! Best fitness center I have ever been a member of, and I have been a bit of a gym hopper. The workouts are the best. I never get bored. The staff is so friendly and encouraging. The coaches are spot on. The facility is clean and I feel safe during the workouts due to the fact that the equipment is top shelf and the coaches experienced. Try it out you will like love it. Oh PS, the other members are super friendly and always welcoming.

John did an excellent job cleaning my chimney and reworking the connection between my furnace and the chimney.  He is a true professional and I would highly recommend him for any work you may need performed on your fireplace or chimney.

Great time.  Rice and Manchego rocked.  Shredded pot tacos rocked.  Guac double rocked - very nice you can order to taste!!

House margaritas were disappointing.  Recommend upgrading or trying their specialty drinks!

Ann Becnel conducts  well disciplined and organized classes that begin and end on time. She communicates a lesson plan at the beginning of each week and all know what to expect. The small classes are managed with water breaks, sniff breaks and playtime. Based on positive reinforcement, it's fun for dogs and guardians.  Good Dog! Thanks Ann!
Great for food allergies! The manager came to take our order to ensure that the kitchen knew. She made specific suggestions, and we we're thrilled with our meals. Definitely will be back.
Great time at the St Patrick's festival !   If you didn't go, you should plan on it next year.  Also family atmosphere.

Perfect place to just rest your head after a long day in downtown Nashville.  
Not fancy but it has exceeded all my expectations

I've been going here for awhile and had 3 to 4 star experiences. Today though, they pissed me off. If I'd never been here, and I based this review off today alone, definitely a zero would be given if it were possible. I pull in and two cars are ahead of me. I tell the guy I want the wash and hand wax. As I pay him I tell him I'm gonna go across the street to Frenchy's, and I ask how long will it take. He says about 45 minutes. So I walk across the street and have lunch. When I walk back I notice my car is in the same spot in line, but there are two different cars in front of me. The guy waves me down and says I didn't give him the keys so they couldn't move it. They'd been having to drive around it. He says he went over to Frenchy's to find me but couldn't. Frenchy's isn't that big, and I was sitting at the bar, right in the middle of the place, and there were only three people at it. Plus I'm pretty recognizable at 6"5" 350 lbs. Now I'm willing to take some of the blame here. I did walk off with keys,  but if he'd asked me for them to begin with, I wouldn't have walked off with them. But now here's the part that pissed me off. Instead of just leaving my car in line where it was, they drove it around to the back of the line putting me seven cars back. Are you kidding me?!?! You're going to punish me or something for forgetting to leave my keys with you. I should have said something then, but I was a bit embarrassed for walking off with the keys in the first place, so I just waited. What was quoted to take approximately 45 minutes now took 2 and a half hours. I'm finding a new car wash.

I love this place ! Hands down best Thai food in Tampa fl! I know when I want Thai food this is the place to go! I recommend this place to anyone who wants good Thai ! Everything they make in here is so good and you can tell the chef loves cooking  very talented! Also the people here are very friendly! My husband and I love Thai 5 ! Great place to get a bite to eat in south Tampa fl ! This place should be on the best eats in south Tampa fl !

This is our favorite restaurant in St. Louis. Very authentic Spanish food. You know a spot is good when people from the country of origin say good things about it and dine there; all my Spanish friends love this spot. They have an awesome Happy Hour M-F from 5-7pm where you can get small bites of food for .25 cents each. I typically just order the whole Happy Hour menu. 

Eating tapas (not topless...dad) is a fun way to share food with others. Modestos has a wide variety of options for both hot and cold tapas and main dishes. Our favorite menu items are below:

Arroz Negro (black rice with lobster and calamari)
Paella Mixta (safron rice with a blend of goodness)
Paella del Mar (safron rice with seafood) 
Medallones de Res (bacon wrapped beef medallions) 
Trucha Ahumada (smoked trout, endive, and crispy chick peas)
Aceitunas a la Sevillana (Spanish olives)
Queso de Cabra al Horno (baked goat cheese with tomato sauce and mushrooms)
Datiles Rellones (bacon wrapped dates)
Spanish cheeses and cured meats
Bread Pudding (best we've ever had)

I could go on and on because we have NEVER had a bad dish here. This place gets an A+!

Eh. My wife and I went a couple years ago, didn't have the greatest meal or experience, and haven't been back since. There are better and worse burger places in Nashville. This place specifically makes you feel like you are sitting in a TINY box clustered right next to other folks with barely any elbow room. Not my cup of tea.
Lovely shop. Very nice service, they ordered me some white hyacinth from their supplier when I mentioned I couldn't find white this season. The bulbs were best so far.

Went in for a quick lunch.  I had the Cajun catfish. It was definitely under-cooked and seriously over salted but  it came with a side of  pretty decent Jambalaya with andouille sausage. I had a cookie milkshake before I left and it saved the whole meal.
If you are near the eastern Main Line, this is the best place to go for Thai food.  BYOB.

I can't stress enough NEVER GO TO ADVANCED URGENT CARE. 

Over a year after I was seen there, I received a bill.  I called my insurance company and they have no record of any claims being filed and they only accept claims within 365 days from the visit. 

I tried calling the number on the bill to straighten this out and it goes directly to "you've reached the automated voicemail box of Advanced Urgent Care. This mailbox is full. Please hang up." so you can't even talk to a person OR leave a message.

I worked with my insurance company and this is now taken care of, but I can't stress enough the stress I went through.

This ain't Dora the Explorer, I'm talking about some real Mexican cuisine, so if you're feeling scared, go back to Taco Bell. Large portions at small prices, with friendly staff and quick service, this is an excellent spot to chow down on some food from our neighbors to the south. Stop on by, you'll be glad you did.
YES. Went last Sat night . Long wait as expected but worth the wait. Fresh seafood. I had the cioppino, wife ordered a whole crab. Good service.  YUMMY!

This place never disappoints.  A small place and the parking lot is usually crowded, especially on Tuesday wing night or any time there is a big game on.  A local eatery with that hole-in-the-wall feel.  The wings are great and you can order all drums if you want.  A wide selection of sauces for even the more timid that still want a great wing.   Breaded mushrooms are available, but I've switched to the fries with ranch and bacon on top.  Awesome.  You want good food, cold beer, and that nice neighborhood feel?  This is the place.  Seating can fill up (especially on Tuesdays or when there is a Wildcat game on but they won't seat you until everyone in your party arrives.  You've been warned.

Great place for breakfast or brunch. The atmosphere was really nice and the staff were very friendly. The grilled cheese and tomato soup was fantastic. I am not a huge tomato soup fan, but their's is DELICIOUS!! Highly recommended if you are in Tucson.

Not-so-good:
Small capacity increases wait
Service during peak times is slow
Prices are slightly more expensive than considered reasonable

Good:
Food (I am a vegan) is FANTASTIC!  Been here three times and have never had a bad dish!
Service is friendly

In town for a rowdy wedding weekend!  O'malley's took care of multiple needs!  Saturday morning ... needed some "hair of the dog", and a good start on the day! All the NCAA football you could take and KILLER Bloody Maries!

I agree with reviewers who comment about how the place opens up in front, FUN!  No Frills, Killer Screens, Great Drinks!

The food may be good, don't know, never ate there. But I do know the staff sucks.  My son was a dishwasher there and was told he was doing a good job but he was constantly berated by the cook, calling him a "pussy shrimp fucker," among other words.  Who does that and why would management allow such behavior to continue?   My son didn't want to work in that environment.  Hostility in the work force should never be allowed.  Considering a lawsuit.

Whoa! Let's talk about amazing... Because it can be found at The Fountain on Locust. I was recently in St. Louis for a work trip. A coworker and I got in on Saturday night, and since we were somewhat unfamiliar with the area, we spent some time on Yelp, scoping out the nearby restaurants. My coworker needed to eat soft things because of some dental work, so I searched "soups" -- little did I know that search would change my taste buds forever! Yes, as others, I am referring to the dill pickle soup! Seeing those words (as a huge dill pickle fan) had me ready to go to this restaurant fairly close to our hotel (Courtyard Marriott). 

We arrived around 8 pm as a party of two and were seated within 5 minutes. (FYI-We parked on the street nearby; I'm not sure if there is a lot or not.)  We sat down with the massive menus and overwhelmed by the amazing-sounding choices. We both opted for an ice cream martini to start. It was a tough choice, but I had a Pomegranate Power (I hope that's the right name.), and she had the dreamsicle-esque one (Sorry I don't remember the names.). Both were divine! There are more drink options than you can handle between those ice cream martinis and specialty cocktails. 

Then it was time for food. I will say the food menu isn't nearly as large as the drink and dessert menus, but there are still many appetizing choices. Like the dill pickle soup! If you like dill pickles, you will truly be in love. I'm no chef, but this had me wanting to try to make it at home! (If I lived in the area, I'd just go to The Fountain daily, but alas!) I got a cup of it with a sandwich described as an "adult grilled cheese." I probably should have had a full bowl of the soup because it was so great, but the sandwich was very enjoyable as well; it was large and a unique blend of flavors.

Then it was time for dessert. What to choose? There was a display of chocolates sitting right beside me at the bar, but I opted for more ice cream! I love a sweet and salty mix, but I went for a pretzel cone with black cherry ice cream! Holy smokes. It was truly a pretzel as a cone. How cool! I love pretzels, and the ice cream was delicious as well. 

My coworker also enjoyed all of her choices, and we both appreciated the service. We were wearing University of Louisville gear, and two staffers (neither being our server) came and spoke to us about living there/their trips there. Essentially, they went out of their way to be friendly. Our server was also on top of everything and kept us (and our bellies) happy! 

As someone who always wants to try new things, especially when I'm traveling, I don't often say this... But I will DEFINITELY go back when I visit St. Louis again! Hopefully sooner rather than later, because The Fountain on Locust is THAT GOOD.

Some of you may think I'm being very generous but my dining experience was quit good. My waitress, Marcelle, was very quick and knowledgeable about the menu. My drink glass was never empty and I even changed my mind about my entrée and she had no problem with it. 
Our dinners were very tasty, I had the chicken pesto which is a seasonal item for them and it was some of the best pesto I've had in Nashville. Our last other entrée was the chicken Parmesan and while I thought the sauce was a little sweet it was served hot and tasted delicious. We don't come here very often because of the location and how hard it is to find parking but it was a nostalgia thing for me tonight. I just had to eat here because it had been so long since we had. They have improved since my last visit which left a fowl taste in my mouth and I believe I gave them a 1  rating. 
If your in town and want eat here eat the specials they tend to make them better than the staples.

Moved from Lancaster County to North Wilmington and the thing we were missing in our lineup was a good pho place. So happy to have found Oriental Pearl. The vermicelli surpassed anything I have had before. We tried the BBQ pork and the beef as well as both spring and summer rolls. We will be back for our fix. It is in the rotation now.

Tried this place during Endymion parade day! We needed to fuel up and got it to go to eat while camping out for Endymion. I got the grilled chicken ceaser salad and my fiancé got the Cochon de lait poboy with a side of fries. They were both very good. I feel as if we were over charged a bit. The poboy alone was 14$ that didn't include the fries. Other than that everything was good. Next time we will eat inside.

Went around 4 pm on Sunday. Nobody there. Service was top notch. 
Ordered stuffed burger and spouse had strip steak. 
First. I never order burgers at a restaurant but this is was an exception. I was impressed. It was delicious
Now on to the highlight. 
My spouse ordered the chicken and dumplings as a side. 
These are by far some of the best of have ever tried in my twenty years or driving a truck. Absolutely outstanding. 
When I come back and I will. I'll have nothing but chicken and dumplings. 
The end. 
Yelp also had a free appetizer and the potato skins were good too.

While I really wanted to like this (love Top Chef, live nearby), I have to say I just wasn't that impressed, especially for the money you spend.  The space for the restaurant is beautiful so I enjoyed the atmosphere but there was really nothing on the menu that either myself or my date really loved.  I had the shrimp bisque which was just...ok.  I had the octopus for the second course.  I did like this dish but it felt just a tad over salted.  For the last course, I had cauliflower, sweet potato fritter with a red sauce and some beets.  Again, this was just ok and felt very salty.  I wanted to be blown away by at least one dish and I just wasn't.  I should note that I don't eat meat however my dad did and he wasn't impressed either.  He has the sea bream, calamari and pork belly for the second course and the lamb for the 3rd course.  We both loved our desserts, chocolate peanut butter and a mini pumpkin pie!  Definitely my favorite part of the meal.  I also did the wine pairing which was a nice touch.  So as I always say, in a city with so many wonderful restaurants, this place just really doesn't compete for me.

Great place for a quick lunch. The burgers are quick, cooked true to order, and cheap. It's pretty small inside so it has sort of an intimate "mom and Pop" type feel. I'll definitely be back. The burgers are also pretty large.

I am a huge fan of the South Philly location but to say that this one is a disappointment, is an understatement. I've had the pork sandwich with Rabe and it was barely decent. The cheesesteak I had was in all honesty, the worst I have ever had. Steak Ums taste better and that is horrific. I thought mine was just bad but then I tasted my wife's and we won't be at this location again. I won't even get into how long it takes to make a cheesesteak.

Great pool, clean updated rooms.  Got a cabana by the pool and it was money well spent.  Not a huge fan of the overall layout,it didn't really flow to get from the pool to the room to the casino.  
Did I say great pool?  Several separate swimming areas, hot tub and a waterfall off the roof into the water.... nice.  Plus cabanas and after about 4 pm it's in the shade of the building.
Phenomenal customer service and staff.  Super nice!

We had a 5:00 reservation.  6 parties were seated before us that had arrived after us.  At 5:20 after asking multiple times, we were finally seated at a 4 top when we had 5 people.  We had requested an empty 6 top and they said no that's for 8 people.  So, we sat down. At 5:30, we were finally addressed by our server.  We did not receive our drinks until 5:45.  2 of the members of our party ordered salads.  They arrived after the meals arrived.  I ordered pesto pasta.  There was not one ounce of pesto on my dish.  I did not mention it because it was tasty and the spinach was amazing.  One member of our party ordered a shrimp dish.  It was cold.  We sent it back.  They said they would cook a new one.  Awhile later, his shrimp arrived and it was the same one just reheated.  The server assured him it was new and he pointed out the bite out of one of the shrimps.  They brought him a 3rd plate and it was also cold.  The server finally sent the manager over.  We were running late to head to the Fox.  He offered free dessert.  This was an absolutely absurd offer since one of our party had not even had dinner.  It should be noted that the 6 top that we requested wasn't seated until 6:17.  We could have been in and out by that time.   This experience reminded me why I NEVER go to chain restaurants.  I can assure you I will never return.

Buddy Brew is Tampa's best coffee shop and a local powerhouse in the coffee roasting community. Everywhere in town that serves coffee (or rather, cares about the coffee they serve) brews with beans from Buddy Brew.

The only problem with Buddy Brew is its popularity! The current space could use more parking and seats.

The clerk talked politely and acted rudely, but food was good.

I went there with 2 friends at 7pm on Saturday. I didn't make reservation, but there were not so much consumers waiting. In this restaurant, they have "reservation area" with booths and "non-reservation area" with a counter and small tables. The clerk led us to a very tiny table for 2 people though we were 3, then he left us there and had gone. He had unusual hospitality, but we got a another small table where we 3 could take seats at last.

We ordered two Prim Rib steaks and a roasted salmon, and a server asked us how we liked our steaks cooked. I think that their Prim Rib steak is very delicious and is better than that of Texas Loadhouse, because of not only the meat itself but also the 2 sauces.
However, anxiously, they didn't provide their bread for us. They have unusual hospitality and services.

I am going to try the restaurant again with reservation.

I'm not a local. I can't claim to understand custards or concretes, but I've been to Ted Drewes more than any other eatery since I moved to St Louis.
They sell tasty "ice cream" with fun toppings for cheap. Parking is plentiful, the folks are nice, and service is crazy fast. They take plastic.
What's not to love?
Amazing tacos. Best guacamole in town. What more do you want in life, folks? Call ahead to get tacos to go - super convenient. I swear they sprinkle unicorn dust on everything.

Delicious food and great service. We were there on a Sunday night so there was little crowd, but I know this place is going to be tough to get in to when the warmer weather hits!! Glad we got to try now. Had both of the house margaritas, both delicious. Yucca fries are a must. Chorizo empanadas were also great, as was the ceviche. We will be back.

i lurve the truffle fries.

the burger itself was moist (probably because i asked them to cook it medium rare).  although it was big, i couldn't stop eating it.  it was delicious...i don't remember exactly the experience because my mind was in heaven mode.

must try if you're around philly.
Done and done. Won't come back. Poor food. Poor service. Ridiculously expensive for what you get. Sorry..3 strikes, you are out.

Small, quaint restaurant that upon first time entering seems a bit awkward because of the table arrangement. But, let me assure you that the couple who own, cook and wait on you are the nicest people around. Not to mention, their food is fabulous!  I have been here many, many times. The couple know me by name now, and I order the veggie thai every time. Prices are reasonable and food is very spicy! A little annoying that I can't get a wi-fi signal, but hey, sometimes we all just need to unplug, right?

My partner loves a cheap diner breakfast, and Surrey's comes through straight gold.  You can substitute tofu for eggs in most dishes; I choose their Surrey's Egg Plate (Surrey's Sub-the-Egg Plate?). It's going to become a great vegetarian-vegan compromise spot for us, I'm sure.

It was almost fully occupied on a Monday morning but my food came out quickly. The plate was really brown in the best carb-tastic way...home fries (really nicely spiced!), rye toast, and a few thick slices of solid tofu. Solid in all ways- texturally (maybe they freeze it? It's definitely pressed), flavor (no hint of beans like tofu can have when it's thrown straight into the pan from the water-filled package), and amount (I felt a bit skimped at first but it was quite filling). I was glad I got a carrot-grapefruit-cucumber juice to go along with it for some color and nutrients :] it was a very fair deal for a large juice.

Service was friendly and prompt. I was sad to see that they served their breakfast with cheap Smuckers jelly; I really hoped they would have some sort of better option. Props to them for including clearly marked veg*n options and for a beautiful interior! I would give five stars no doubt if they added some sort of vegan sweet treat so I can come have an indulgent BYOChampagne brunch!

This buffet restored my faith in buffets. ( I hate buffets) polenta, creamy chicken, veggies, lasagna were really good! Desserts tasted fresh and great quality, food was all fresh and very flavorful! Service was awesome! Absolutely no complaints.

I used to order from this place when they had another location out in West Philly and now I'm so glad  I don't have to go as far anymore. Back then the food was amazing and it still is! 

Don't go here on a date trying to be all cute because you WILL make a little mess...as you should. The crab legs are perfectly cooked and were the  easiest crab legs I've ever had to open. The amount of flavor inside was mind bobbling, as were the Maryland crab cakes which were divine! The fried shrimp were hands down the best I've ever had!

Each entree is perfectly complimented by a potato, broccoli, and corn on the cob. All are equally well-seasoned and just as delicious as the protein.

I enjoyed my food thoroughly, gladly settled my [fairly reasonable] bill, and waddled to the car a happy girl!

Our first visit and we will be coming back. The sign says wine, dine, and recline.  I was shocked to walk into a huge full service bar. With plenty of seating. When you purchase your ticket they show you a seating chart so you can select your seats. When you go inside  huge comfy leather recliners await you. These chairs are the best, this is the five stars rating.  To be able to have the comfort of home but even better. You sit and adjust as needed throughout the film. A waitress comes to take your order. The servers are available until 15 mins before showtime. We ordered drinks and mozzarella sticks even though we weren't looking to eat the server was so sweet. The order came hot and crispy they were good not great. But there are plenty of great restaurants in the area - you will not go hungry. The place is not sparky and new but it's a great place to see a movie and have a drink. And who knows maybe we will have a full meal on one of our visits as this will be our go to movie house.
A lot of kids (teams) but the staff stayed friendly and clean. Our room was nice and the value was fabulous. For the price and the location, I would definitely go back!

Had a margherita Sicilian pie . The sauce and the crust were amazing. This is a huge pie, that filled up 4 people, 2 of whom can eat almost a whole thin crust pie. If you like Sicilian pizza, this place has about the best I've ever eaten. Service was great. Place is big, clean, and decorated nicely.

This place was pretty good, the decor inside is super simple but with an odd bar that has little jutted out sections which is neat. Other than that, and the large wooden bar, its simply tables and chairs and totally unassuming. It seems like the type of place that anyone can go to and feel comfortable at. 

I just stopped in for one beer and a snack, (I mostly just wanted to try the fried green beans everyone had been talking about) and I'm glad I did! I had pliny the elder on draught for 6 bucks, and it was worth every penny. There's a good reason it's in beer advocate's top 10 in the list of best beers. My boyfriend got the sierra nevada belgian trippel, it was good as well.

And yeah, the fried green beans were AMAZING. So good, I could eat 50 more plates of it. 

The staff were super friendly as well. 


The only thing that bothered me was so many things on the chalkboard that touted what draught and bottle selection they had, were misspelled... haha. Sierra Navada Belgian Tripple... it made me giggle, not a big deal though. Definitely didn't put a damper on the experience.

The hubby and I are from out of town and stopped by here for a quick lunch before we headed to the airport. The first thing that I noticed was the BEAUTIFUL patio with brightly colored flowers and lots of seating. How fun to come hang out with friends to eat, drink and watch the game??

The interior is very clean and well kept. We were greeted right away and sat immediately. Marianne was our server and she was super friendly and attentive. The manager, Theresa, even came by and chatted with us for a bit. The entire staff seems really pleasant. 

We ordered the steak quesadilla for an appetizer, adult grilled cheese and nachos. All of it was delicious! The steak quesadilla was a recommendation by our server and we were not disappointed. The black bean and corn salsa it came with was amazing. The adult grilled cheese had the perfect palatable balance with the Gouda cheese and apples combined with bacon on sourdough. The nachos are HUGE. Definitely recommend getting it to share! The pork carnitas added to it was really flavorful. I loved that there wasn't just topping on the first layer of chips but ingredients were spread all throughout the giant mound. 

All in all, we had a great experience. This seems like it would be such a great place to come hang out with friends and watch the game. There were lots of TVs with a variety of sports featured on it but it wasn't overwhelming like some places with TVs can feel. Theresa told us about their happy hour specials and we wish we lived closer! Great place and will be back when we come into town.

It was extremely crowded when we went, so we assumed it had to be good. We even called ahead and still had to wait for 15mins. Nonetheless, the food ended up being just mediocre if not less than. Everything was oversalted. Not sure what the hype was about. Maybe since most other restaurants in the area are chains.

I love Ralston Massage Center!  I've been going to Ralston Massage on a monthly basis for almost a year now and it has been an amazing healing experience.  I was in a bad car accident a couple years ago and have chronic neck/back issues along with hip joint degeneration.  All of which were very painful.  I have to say my posture has improved significantly and pain has reduced immensely.  The Center is beautiful, warm, peaceful, and very clean.  The Massage Therapists are friendly and professional, and provide excellent massage therapy. I would recommend Ralston Massage to everyone.

Hipster coffee houses do exist in NoLa!! 
As a pair of Seattlites, we were in on a great search of a non-Starbucks place that would deliver in atmosphere, wifi, and good coffee. All that above was found inside, along with the nicest barista I've meet! We were curious about the chicory roasted coffee, and she whipped us up a few cups to sample along with giving some of the best indie shopping spots nearby. 
Best thing yet, is they offer vegan pastries of all kinds. My vegan oatmeal cookie hit the spot along with a cold glass of Yerba Mata tea. There are all sorts of cool little fixtures inside and table lights to keep the atmosphere chill. And not to sound like a creeper, but the people watching is fantastic here while soaking up a soy latte.

I have had lunch at Cool Springs Brewery one day a week each of the last six weeks. Every week I order something different. I haven't been disappointed yet. The service and the atmosphere are great 
It's always a pleasant experience.
Every time I'm in Philly I make it my business to stop by HipCityVeg! Amazing food for vegans is hard to come by but I'm so happy they're here!
Their press boxes are amazing! I highly recommend the sakana tower, yellowtail habanero melt and the crunchy box! Delicious sushi and friendly service.
Had the Reuben and a Bass ale, was NOT disappointed. The sandwich was lean, plump, and sweet as butter. Service was efficient and the restroom is clean. Will be back!

Me and my boyfriend went there for lunch. 

1. Food : yummy and delicious.
