I love that we always get those crunchy stick things with duck sauce right away.  Don't know what they put in that duck sauce, but it rules. 

So, all in all. Dragon Garden is a family run establishment with smiling servers and great food.  It's more than affordable, generous portions and a fantastic atmosphere.  Not sure what else you could want in a Chinese Restaurant!  Well done!

Calie is the best! She's always so sweet and does my nails perfectly. She takes her time and goes above and beyond. Also her sister Tracy is really good! She's done my sisters nails and mine one time and they looked great! If you go there ask for either Calie or Tracy!

EDIT - Since my review of this restaurant on 5/28/2011, I've visited many times since and I still find the place to be outstanding in all areas. Just wanted to update that this is a must-visit place if you want to enjoy happy-hour......... HAPPY HOUR 7 DAYS A WEEK and the specials are thankfully always the same - beer, wine and martinis.  I wish other restaurants would do this - it would take the thought out of deciding where to go depending on what day of the week it is.

The Italian Affair, by far, is my most favorite place to dine with friends, family, or even by myself.  They feature outdoor and indoor seating, and a really nice bar inside.  Their outside patio is landscaped with a waterfall and fishpond.  The staff is awesome, the regulars are welcoming and friendly, and the prices are reasonable - it's one of the few fine dining establishments that offers sandwiches and "light fare" in the bar area - while offering a cuisine as simple or fancy as you prefer in the dining areas.  The portions served are very generous - the wine selection is incredible - this establishment is popular for a reason!  I highly recommend their French-Cut Pork Chop - this place really goes out of their way to make you feel as though you're at home.
Wait staff was very friendly but my buttermilk waffle was overcooked and didn't really have a flavor. Bacon was good.
I will always recommend Puckett's. Food is great. Beer selection is great and the atmosphere is great. The wait staff is always friendly and kind. The food is always hot.

My, the things I have missed since I left Nashville!

My cousin brought me here for lunch on Christmas Eve and the place was hopping. (Maybe because so many other restaurants were closed?) I took the signed photo of Ben Folds posing with the owner as an excellent omen of the meal to come. The interior is small but cozy. Though we had to squeeze past tables to get to our own, we had plenty of room at our table and I didn't feel like we'd been packed in like sardines.

The menu said their pad thai was nothing like the crappy, sticky, sweet American version, which I detest, so I figured I'd better give it a go. I ordered the tofu-only version in spicy form, and it delivered. I can't claim to really know Thai food, but this pad thai was fantastic in my book. It was spicy, perfectly fishy, and flavorful. And the noodles were cut to a perfect size, greatly facilitating the plate-to-mouth-with-chopsticks maneuver, something I'd always quietly wished for but never had received. I had to beg myself to save half the meal in anticipation of my family's Christmas feast, but had no large fooding events been on the horizon, I would have happily inhaled the entire plate. 

The place was extremely busy and it wasn't clear to me how many servers were on the floor, but ours was rather lackadaisical in his approach. He wasn't rude or anything, just infrequently present, and I had to grab my own to go box. That said, my water glass was never empty (filled by the man who I believe is the owner), and I'm sure any needs or concerns I couldn't address by myself would have been taken care of if asked.

Went here for dinner before and most recently brunch. So crowded both times so I'm so glad we had reservations! We had to wait a little bit but nothing significant and well worth it! We had a little guy at our table and they customized for us by just bringing out plain old scrambled eggs which I thought was so nice of them. The Fruity Pebbles French Toast was SO good and the peanut butter mousse stuffed waffles they had on special looked as amazing as they tasted! Definitely would recommend (making reservations) and going for a tasty place... And did I mention it's BYOB?!

I've visited this café once and will certainly be giving it a second try! My first experience was all positive. I came on crutches and the staff were super accommodating. They brought me what I ordered so I could sit down and held the door for me when I left. Upon arriving, I was delighted to find a clean café with a wide range of menu options that work for special dietary needs for a place that doesn't label themselves as strictly vegan, gluten free, etc. They had both soy and almond milk, vegan soft serve, and several other menu options that were vegan and/or gluten free. They also had a good menu in the way of coffee and other drinks and some nicer options for sandwiches, salads, and the like. I ordered a café au lait with almond milk and a plain bagel with Earth Balance. The au lait was tasty and not too pricey even with the almond milk. The bagel order came out a little bit differently than what I had ordered- I got an everything bagel with cream cheese. I'm not usually one to speak up about that kind of thing, having been on the other end of things at the café where I work, and my shyness coupled with all of the friendliness I had already experienced from the staff led me to let it go. To my surprise, though, the staff took notice themselves. Upon realizing, the girl who had taken my order was extremely apologetic and corrected the mistake right away! I felt generally very welcomed at Benna's West and will be returning soon (with my dog! Bonus points to Benna's for allowing friendly canines into their coffee shops).

We have been frequenting this place for many years but the experience we had this past week definitely will force me to NEVER eat here again. 

Typical Saturday night, parking lot was busy and inside was wall to wall people. Over the years I realized that while their sushi is great the service is pitiful. Waitresses work hard and are always friendly. However the hostesses are usually unfriendly and strike an attitude. I have confronted them a few times over the years but it never seemed to improved. Since there were only 2 of us they stuck us at a small table in the very back which was fine however we waited almost 20 minutes for someone to take our order. In matter of fact we had a bottle of wine with us and we almost got through a full glass before someone acknowledged us (I was able to get someone to open it for us).  

Sushi was good and we were offered desert but opted not to.  We were immediately presented the bill which we paid and figured we would finish the half glass of wine we each had before getting going. Seems harmless right??? WRONG!!!  Immediately after paying the bill the what seemed like a manager came over and asked us to leave because they had other people waiting for tables and they were busy.  I was pretty taken back by this and even the people sitting nearby who overhead the conversation seemed taken back by the comments.  I normally would throw a fit but I left. 

A few things to consider:

1. Sushi is way overpriced - so the fact that we spent good $$$ that night the least you could do is let me finish my wine.  You want to charge me NY prices in suburban Philadelphia - well act the part

2. If you had a problem with people sitting and sipping on their drinks then get a liquor license - it will easily alleviate your problem 

3. Yes the sushi is good but the service and attitude of the staff makes this place un-appetizing

4. Do yourself a favor and go into downtown Phila and find one of many great sushi places - Fat Salmon is one of my favorites 

5.  I know they have other locations in Montgomeryville and North Wales - not sure if their service is any better but if they are all owned by the same person this needs to be addressed 

To sum it up, I have never been asked to leave a restaurant in any circumstance so while the sushi is good I recommend that YOU SHOULD NOT EAT HERE!!

split an egg and hash brown dish(homefries were amazing) and the scone we got was amazing too although a little on the pricier side, the freshly baked raspberry scone couldn't be beat. also, the coffee and juices are fresh and delish just made for a delicious but kind of expensive bfast. wouldn't crave it or go back again if it wasn't on my way elsewhere.

I was working in Collegeville and couldn't leave work to get lunch, so I searched for some restaurants that delivered.  Very few restaurants offered lunch delivery, and Tony's menu looked decent.

I ordered an eggplant sandwich which came with a side of fries, garlic cheese bread, and a Greek salad. More food than I needed for lunch but there is a $15 minimum for delivery, and I planned to save the salad  and garlic bread for dinner.

The Greek salad was really good, all the ingredients were fresh and they didn't skimp on the feta.  The grape tomatoes were sweet and very flavorful. The salad came with a garlic knot and it was delicious.

I had expected garlic cheese bread to be just one piece but it was a whole loaf, sliced in half, with loads of garlic. Really tasty. 

The eggplant on the sandwich was very thin, and not much of it.  The bread was thick.  The ratio of filling to bread was off, definitely could have used more eggplant.  Some mayo or sauce would have helped as it was rather dry.

Delivery was very good, the driver was very friendly and he was right on time.

Jesse H - 2010 probably would be the year I visited (several times) and never returned. My team was sponsored by Village Pub, and when we brought a trophy in to celebrate, we got half assed thanks. I mean, we appreciated the tiny shirts you donated (we returned them all because they were made for hooters girls) and the replacements were xxl but I digress. Maybe my experience roots back to first opening, but your comment asking if I've really been or just saw pictures help reiterate why I won't be back. Also, I can't (or couldn't in 2010 apparently) park a Pathfinder safely in that lot.

Everything an emo man-child could ask for. Went for their recurring emo night, and it was heaven-sent. Seriously, tell all your friends, it's where you want to be, even if your heart is in Ohio. I will be going back until the day I die, because this place is my only one. I was always such a sucker for that. I've got a twenty dollar bill, which is good enough for almost unlimited pbr at a dime a dozen. $3 cover.  I'd walk across the United states, all alone, so I could see my breath.  Up the stairs is the station where the act becomes the art of growing up. I came out swinging from a south Philly basement, caked in stale beer and sweat under half-lit fluorescents.  And though you swear that you are true, I'd still pick my Barbary over you. Die young and save yourselves, folks.

What a disappointment!  I moved to the area, a year ago, and I've been wanting to try the multitude of pizzerias in and around here.  Well, this was my second place, and I can tell you don't waste your money.  I should have known when I walked into the place when there was not one person eating in there, nor picking up, and it was during rush hour.  When you order a "gourmet pizza" you expect to pay a little more, but you also expect to "get" a little more.  Not here!  My main complaint is the crust.  It's premade, frozen, or  a Boboli like you buy in the supermarket.  That in itself is a strict NoNo for a pizzeria.  I guess the pizza maker had carpal tunnel and couldn't knead or toss the dough?  And the sauce was so runny and watery that by the time I got it home, everything had shifted to the other side, and I was careful with transporting it.  All this for 17.00.  Never again!  The Main Street Grill Pizzeria is so far the best, but again, that's with only trying two places.  Good Luck!

Let me start out by saying that I loved my breakfast!  I had the crawfish omelet, and it was wonderful. Crawfish were fresh and hot.  Rest of the  meal was just average.  It was crowded and load. But, I guess that is a sign of good food. 
My problem was that you had to move the mop bucket out of the way to get to the cooler with the juices and milk.  ICK!!
Staff was very friendly.

My wife and I enjoyed good food and service in this quirky new pizza place.  I really liked the breadsticks and the Sidekicks Supreme pizza.  

  I was surprised to find street parking just around the corner at lunchtime on Saturday.  (Free is good!)  Anyway, we walked past two other restaurants/bars in the Action Bowl building and saw the sign/stand in front of the entrance.  (It still says Shelby in bold letters over the doorway.)  As we entered, we saw the sign to seat ourselves and our waitress noticed us and greeted us, echoing the sign to sit wherever we liked.  We chose a window seat so that we could see the fountains and people watch.

  Our waitress was over promptly and maintained good service throughout our lunch.  She kept busy doing prep work while not attending us and managed to deal with carryout orders as well.  I noticed another sign that they now have Uber Delivery available.

  While waiting for our food, I noticed they have pictures of sidekicks all around the restaurant. I recognized many of them. There is also a pinball game to help pass time.  A long bar is available for patrons to order one of the bottled beers or local brews (I think there were 8 on tap.)

 Our breadsticks came out first.  We ordered 4 sticks which came with two choices of dipping sauces.  (Breadsticks can be ordered in 2, 4, or 6 and there are six varieties of dipping sauces to choose from).  We ordered the marinara and the nacho cheese.  The nacho cheese comes with red peppers diced into the sauce.  Both sauces were tasty and the sticks were flatter than I have had elsewhere, but that was a good thing.  They seemed to have a little more crispness than most I've tried.

  Our pizza arrived and was very good!  This thin crust pie had plenty of mozzarella that stretched when I lifted each slice. The green peppers were cut large, but were cooked thoroughly, so that was a nice surprise.  Plenty of flavor.  The crust itself was crisp around the rim, but just a little soggy in the center which made it hard to pick up at first.  There was just a little grease from the pepperoni, but just enough to lick my fingers, not make a mess.  Overall, I would order this again and since there were 8 slices, I had to get a box for my leftovers.

  I haven't tried their salads or sandwiches yet, but based upon my experience, I would gladly bring friends here to eat and maybe grab a brew.

Review #341

p.s.  This is the third restaurant I have been to in this location.  It is quirky here on its own, but seeing the same basic layout with new decor just adds to the oddness of the experience.
Food and service is good. The chef, Sergio, great guy and had bright future of him. Hope to see him next time as the head chef!
Went in last night to try the new restaurant in Midtown ordered two appetizers and 2 entrees and everything was Top Shelf will definitely make this a weekly venture

Went with a group of six last night.  Tried 3 different pizzas.  The shitake pizza was amazing.  The Mediterranean pizza was okay; chicken was dry and pieces were too big.  The Meatlovers was very good.  Service was good.  One really bad thing; the music was so loud conversation was almost impossible.  There is NO reason to have the music up that loud!  Overall B+.

I'm at the point in my life that in Reno, Walmart makes me feel like I could be on Maury or Jerry Springer. Target just feels so much more upscale. The store is always clean and the lines aren't as bad as Walmart. I do feel like their grocery section needs work (it's not a Super Walmart I know) though, and a self check out would be great. I've noticed Walmart is always a bit cheaper than Target however, I'm in and out when I'm in Target versus the time spent in Walmart.

Went here with my fiancé we ordered a bottle of wine, two salads and they somehow managed to get one of the salads wrong. The bill somehow came out to $92 for this service? Would recommend for drinks and people watching on the street but never again for dinner.

Their mocha drinks are my favorite thing in the world. I drink them every few days to go with my schoolwork. It keeps me going and tastes delicious. The baristas are really cool. I will go here as long as they stay open.
Very good service.  Wanted to get a new haircut that was much shorter.  Frog, was a true professional, helped me find a business professional cut that suited me well!

I hate to write how disappointed I was tonight with our experience at Pagoda. When I used to live in Philly we'd go often. Then after I moved to NJ we would make the trip maybe once or twice a year to Philly and choose Pagoda for dinner. The owners recognized us and had fantastic service and food. (See previous review) 

We were in town for the auto show and had decided to return to Pagoda.  After a long day on our feet we were glad to sit down somewhere familiar.  We were seated immediately,  put in our order by a somewhat hurried waiter. A few minutes later the waiter came back and barked out "no more Peking duck". That was a disappointment on a Saturday evening not too late at night that one of their specialties was not available. We did have shrimp dumplings which were decent;  my garden vegetable udon noodle soup & his shrimp dumpling udon noodle soup which were as good as we remembered. We got the orange chicken not spicy as our shared entree which was average but nothing special. During this time we also heard a little girl crying loudly for 10 minutes until one of the owners I presume grabbed her hard by the arm yelling at her and taking her to another room to yell at her / hit her. It echoed through the restaurant. We did not want dessert. Left a 15% tip and while my husband was in the restroom I heard the waiter say to a girl behind the counter "extremely cheap"
Now I don't know if I heard correctly but that was pretty ballsy. Especially since we tried the Peking duck rolls which were microwaved rolls with warm lettuce and bits of duck. Basically inedible. They charged $6 which we didn't dispute. We have no problem tipping well but he did not earn more than 15% - especially given what he said. Oh well Pagoda you lose our business to the Peking Duck House in North Brunswick which is only 20 minutes from us. So many restaurant choices in Philly too and our loyalty is done.

Good (a.k.a. only) choice for frozen yogurt in Manayunk. The yogurt flavors are extensive and the topping bar has an overwhelming amount of fruits and candies to chose from. I also like the option of turning your creation into a smoothie. 

What I dislike about Whirled Peace is the layout... when it comes to FroYo people can be indecisive and want to taste-test or play around with the flavor combos. This makes it difficult for someone, ME, who is very decisive about her yogurt selection, have to wait around during the hemming and hawing, or cut around you to the toppings. Either way, the layout is a little annoying. Also, I find it a bit expensive. But it does hit the spot when you have a fro-yo craving.
Happy, Happy to find awesome Tres Leches Cake! Plus, an awesome bakery loaded with homemade pastries.  Reminds me of home. This California girl is elated that Nashville has a pandaderia!

Walked in one weekday afternoon with my boyfriend, hoping to check it out. The host (owner, perhaps) smiled and invited us to look around, which we did. After a look-see, we returned to the front, hoping to be seated. And then we stood there for over 10 minutes while employees looked at as and past us, ignoring us. We tried to get the attention of the owner, who was deeply engaged in a conversation with two young men (not customers). Finally, she turned to us and said charmingly, "I just have to finish telling them this story!" and turned her back to us, continuing to talk to the two young men.

So, we left. We'll never go back.

I don't only love sushi, I consider myself a pretty good judge of sushi. This place IS excellent sushi! 
I find that places this far outside of the city usually lack the originality and sometimes even the good ingredients that you need for a successful meal, especially for seafood dishes. there are plenty of good restaurants in Newtown or New Hope...but this is Bensalem..

Being my parents favorite restaurant then raved about it, and I, although trying to humor them by going, thought to myself, what do they know about good sushi? living in the city, I've become somewhat sushi-spoiled. to my greatest surprised this place was amazing!
large, but not unbearable menu, features a very nice selection of your typical Japanese restaurant dishes and a very nice selection of very original rolls. the fish is at it's freshest! and the best part, it's pretty inexpensive. it's not cheap, but compared to other places serving this selection it is way less.
Great place! I highly recommend if you're ever in the area!
Simply the best ice cream anywhere!! Make sure you try the Chocolate Amaretto Cheesecake

They fried up the fish we caught after a trip on the Super Queen Fishing Charter for $8. Came with French fries and cole slaw. Can't beat that. Drank a Dosarita, which is a pint glass of margarita with an upside down bottle of Dos Equis sitting in it. Interesting idea, but I didn't really like it. Didn't quite go together. But all in all, they cooked the fish I just caught for a fair price. Worth the visit.

I was here visiting and decided to eat here because I had good experiences earlier.  The last time I was in Exton nine months prior to this I decided to skip Aoki because it appeared to have changed ownership or something (the details are unclear in my memory) and wasn't very busy.
This visit made me wish I had not skipped it the last time.
My sushi was very good, and came out quite rapidly.  The green tea was noteable, while the miso soup was average. The waitress was very classy and attentive.
Aoki continues to be one of my favorite places in the area.

Greek food is my favorite cuisine to eat.....period! I have never tasted greek food like this! I loved everything from the broadini fish all the way down the menu to the eggplant entree! 

Most importantly I love the staff! If anybody was to get fired, I think it could hurt the business tremenedously. Everyone that works there is so personable and also genuine. Your business could be out of state but if the customer service is good, I will be there all the time. It's hard to find service like this and I am a lifetime member from now to this place!

Still love the place but I wish the wait staff would share the up charges for certain thing as a courtesy. I'm pretty observant about up charges and if I can't find it on the menu I'll ask. I do believe when someone requests something that would cost extra, it would be kind to say "that will be an additional $1.99 is that ok?"  

The bread is still to die for.
Solid Thai food.  Amazing Tom Kha soup and loved the shrimp with mixed vegetables.   And fantastic service.

I love shrimp and grits, but my entree completely missed the mark. The shrimp on top of the grits were the tiniest shrimp I've ever seen - they looked exactly like the bagged frozen grocery store shrimp used in salads. They were NOT fresh Gulf shrimp, nor were they as pictured here. We counted 27 of them. They were boiled, not grilled, pan-fried or sauteed. The tasso gravy was tasty, but there was so much of it that it completely overwhelmed the grits. Very disappointing.

What a lovely, unique spot for an Italian dinner! I came to Mangia with a group of fellow foodies and this was perfect for a large party! For $50.00 on the weekends you get a full 6 course experience complete with dancing (and its mandatory). They offer affordable wine and we settled into a lengthy dinner experience. 
Highlights: 
The focaccia with olive oil was the first item I tried and one of my favorites. It was perfect! I also loved the scallops, rigatoni with butternut squash, sage, and brown butter. I couldn't stop eating it! The herb crusted pork loin was a home run as well, and the cappuccinos with our donuts didn't disappoint either. I wasn't such a fan of the short rib pasta or the risotto cakes (very bland), but the good thing about this experience is it's family style, and you get to try a bit of everything and if you aren't a fan of one item, another heaping dish is right behind it for you try! 
The staff was absolutely incredible and fun, and you can tell that this isn't just a restaurant, it's a passion for them! I appreciated all the work they put into making our meal an experience.

The toughest thing about Blue Sage is ordering more than you can eat. We always take food home because it's too difficult to resist ordering what everyone next to us ordered. Some restaurants excel at presentation, and others, at taste. Blue Sage is one of the few that has both.

The first time we came here we were a bit unsure because it says "vegetarian" in the name, and we hadn't eaten at a vegetarian-only restaurant before. Believe me, by the time you open the menu and look at the tables around you, you'll forget that it's vegetarian. This place has become one of our favorites in the region, and we've even taken out-of-town visitors here just to show off the delicious food!

By the way, their Sunday brunch rocks! It's priced reasonably ($18), and tastes better than most other brunches we've had.

An absolutely wonderful place. The rice and kabobs are my favorite but its all very good.  The prices are good and if you save room, their desserts are amazing. My wife loves the hummus and I'm a fan of their salad with feta cheese. The only negative is that this shopping center has terrible parking. But I won't hold that against them. I will just think poorly of whichever idiot put 7 restaurants in a row right here.

Fantistic meal, entertaining bartender, knowledgeable and friendly service.  A high point was the wine list with reasonable prices that allowed us to enjoy high quality wine to further enhance a great experience.  This is a gem in the St. Louis area foodscape, and I highly recommend it for a nice evening with friends.

Best pet store.  They have amazing deals.  Great samples that Tyler helps you with to specifically treat your animals... Every tenth purchase is free.  Not kidding.  I tried this with the large bag cat food and he was pleased as punch to hand it over.  Super impressed.  One of those small business stores off the beaten path I like to support, over corporate stores.  Small town hospitality goes a long way in my book.  Love.
Great customer service!!! The whole elote that is prepared with everything (including the homemade sauce) is SO GOOD! My top raspado choices are El Niño and leche with strawberries & pecans.

Okay here is a cool spot for everyone. We came in for the Maine Lobster at $9.99. It's a special on Monday and Tuesday for a limited time. This place does not look like anything from the outside or inside. I do wish it had a little bit more atmosphere but we sat in the oyster bar area which had a Louisiana flare to it. Beers are ice cold just the way we like them. We also got the fish spread which I highly recommend. It even has a little spice to it so don't add the hot sauce until you taste it. It might be too much and we felt like it didn't even need any hot sauce. Lobster definitely worth the $10 and service was very friendly. My boyfriend got the lobster roll priced $22. I thought it was a little steep. I say it had too much butter it actually felt like it was soaked in butter and the bread was limp. I like it when the bread is gently toasted  and the lobster is brushed with butter . My boyfriend said you can never have too much butter. You decide.  We also saw the soup come out and I definitely want to try that next time. I even think you can make a meal out of the fish spread and the soup. Can't wait to come back with some friends.
Yum! This is a great spot for folks looking for good and flavorful pho (not the best pho, but def solid). Banh Mi was great as well! Truly a bang for your buck. Service is great!

At first glance, the display cases seemed a little barren on a Sunday afternoon, but I ordered a chocolate moussestachio cupcake -- and it was fantastic. The icing was rich and chocolately, and the cupcake itself was moist, dense, and also very chocolately. Inside was a pocket of delicate and delicious pistachio mousse. I rarely think a cupcake is worth $3.50, but this one definitely was (in fact, I thought that was a pretty reasonable price for a large gourmet cupcake in Bryn Mawr). My companion has a chocolate peanut butter cupcake and was also very happy with it. Definitely worth a trip.

I've left a previous post about cat before, who has since left EWC. My new wax lady is also great. But this review is on their receptionists.

I find them cold, rude, unwelcoming, and generally uninterested in anything I'm saying. Some of them are great, but it seems whenever I call into the store I'm greeted by the same girl who always makes it sound like I'm annoying her by asking a question. She actually has no warmth or friendliness at all when talking to you, and it actually pisses me of and makes me want to frequent a different wax salon. This is a service industry, so when you expect a certain kind of service and you're met with abrupt and rude service, it leaves a bad taste in your mouth. Once my package is over, I'm not sure I'll be buying another.

We came here with my BIL and his girlfriend when we stayed at their place. This is their favorite breakfast spot, and I can see why. It could have been a 5-star if we hadn't had to wait such a long time for our food. People who came in 10 minutes after we did got their food first! I don't normally eat my eggs scrambled, but they had these cream cheese eggs that sounded wonderful, so I couldn't resist. They were as good as they sounded! They also have homemade HUGE fluffy biscuits, and you can't go wrong putting their gravy over them. My home fries and coffee were also good. As far as the food goes, you cannot go wrong.
I will never eat hash browns or biscuits anywhere else... To die for. And brought me back to life after a rough night.

Great place to stop for Pho! The servers are very attentive as it is often pretty empty. The food is exactly what you would want when it comes to Pho, and the prices are very reasonable. I'd recommend getting the large pho for $1 more, as it easily becomes lunch or dinner for the next day. They have a full bar and TVs, should you want to go in and watch a football game and eat Pho.

My husband and I had a lovely date night here. We ordered a few tapas that were all good but not very memorable. We also shared the chicken paella. The paella was awesome filled with chicken, sausage, and veggies. We both very much enjoyed it. 

As for the not so positives, my margarita swirl was not good. I wasn't able to drink more than a few sips. Also, our waitress was a smart ass. Weeks later, I'm still not sure if she was rude or funny. I'll keep pondering that. 

I would definitely return for paella, but I may skip some of the other parts of the experience.

The food was really good.....once I eventually got it. I docked 2 stars because the setup of the place was horrible and only half the staff seem to know what they're doing.

I ordered and paid, then waited 15 - 20 minutes. When my coworker and 3 or 4 people after me got their food and I hadn't, I squeezed my way to the pick-up area and asked. They had no ticket with my name and said they must have given it to someone else, and asked the cooks to make my sandwich. Another 5-10 minutes pass and nothing (I had no idea how long their food takes to cook since I'd never been). I ask again and they'd somehow forgotten it and made it. They were nice about it and refunded my money but I wasn't the only ticket that got lost in the time I was there so it seems like service could be improved.

One of the workers who was responsible for packing the orders multiple times put food in a bag with no ticket to identify who it belonged to. She also, multiple times, packaged up an order, stapled the ticket with the name on it, then set it aside without calling it out for the person to pick up.  

I might go back before lunch rush but we will see.

Another mediocre Tampa Mexican joint. The state of Mexican food in Tampa Bay is just so so sad. If you eat here, the best thing was the carnitas tacos.

DEAR XTREME: If you are reading this review, PLEASE GET REAL AC. Your AC sucks and it's always 1,000 degrees in there.

Parking is also a problemo here.

I like Bank of America and their Clayton and Frontenac locations are great, but this one has an ATM that needs to be fixed. The first time I tried to withdraw money I couldn't get a receipt for my transaction and the second time it was malfunctioning altogether.

Loved his place. Service was excellent and the food was great! The portion sizes were big and you get what you pay for. I loved the Guiness beer soup and the avocado egg rolls. Hope to visit again soon!!

Coffee is solid, I got the drip brew. My wife and I tried five of their sliders. Tuna, BLT, Blackened Chicken, Burger, and Fried Chicken. All of them were amazing. The fries are just run-of-the-mill waffle fries, which means they're great,  but nothing to write home about. 

Can't comment on the donuts. They look amazing, but I don't eat sweets.
I walked in with no appointment and was seen right away by Sam. I got lots of compliments on the cut. Great haircut for the right price. Classy place, thanks!

Interior looks like a school cafeteria.

Lady taking orders was very hard to understand.  I asked for no sauce and received food bathed in sauce.

Fries had a lot of black/rotten spots on them.

Soup of the day was lentil, advertised to warm you up on a cold winter's day.  It was 90 degrees outside.

I left hungry.

My husband and I had an excellent dinner. There were many cream sauces on the menu which we don't care for but we were able to modify the sauce.  The only reason I don't give five stars is that the limoncello cake is a huge disappointment. It's not cake, it is a little fried thing.   Our waiter was prompt and friendly.

Fire the entire management and employee staff covering lunch and start over! It's a mess inside and drive-thru. Constantly long waiting times at both as employees go at whatever pace they feel like. Take your business to Wendy's in KS instead. They seem to have management better organized to lead a team through high peak traffic times.
Love this place. Mushroom soup is amazing ! We had the ahi tuna and meatloaf . Both were delicious.

Traveling to Tampa, my friend and I stopped in Ybor City and went into this lovely shop. I was drawn in by its name "Agora" because it means the marketplace in Greek and she and I had learned all about it in World Cultures! What a cool place! We went in to see lovely things from afar including baskets, jewelry and masks and many other things. The manager was kind and informative and had a vivacious personality. Just a delight!

We visited on April 9, 2015 around 8pm. Victor was our server and he was awesome. One of our friends had a food allergy and he was able to accommodate her so she could enjoy the meal with us. Emily was the bartender and she made us some fabulous drinks!. The food was excellent. Also, one of our friends left her wallet in the bathroom. The hostess found it and returned it promptly. When does that ever happen in a big city? Overall, a great dining experience.

As a neighbor I've been waiting on 312 for almost a year, walking by every couple weeks, peeking in the doors, getting excited when signs went up. My expectations were low... I wanted a casual place for a beer after 9 pm without driving... Not much to expect living in the most difficult neighborhood to buy real estate in Nashville... On my first visit 312 performed beyond expectation, with epic Chicago Style deep dish pizza, great beer, attentive staff, and a subtle but nice ambiance that balances a pizza place with a trendy neighborhood. I will be spending a lot of time here. Also, props to the owner who I've been chatting with on the Nextdoor app for coming to the table and chatting with us. It was worth the wait!
This could not be more fun!! Great value. Just excellent melodrama, fun troop of actors. We're going again in a minute!!!
Open until 7pm but this deli consistently runs out of bread in the afternoon. Last three times I've gone from a sandwich at 5pm I got the same sign: Out of Bread.

The review is for the restaurant not the food. The food is amazing and the quality is great. The restaurant is ok as far as cleanliness but it's COLD! OMG, it's soooo cold in here I'm shaking! It's always like this and if you are cold natured get take out! I am going to bring a thermometer next time but guessing 58ish in here. The soap dispenser in the restroom doesn't work unless you work for it, hope the employees have another place to wash hands......... Second time I've been here that the soap has been sketchy.
Had the chicken with verde sauce, it was terrific. Again, eat here, bring a parka! Would be four stars if it were comfortable in here but trying to eat with teeth chattering sucks!

Not coming here again just because it's incredibly awkward. I walked in for the first time and everyone stared at me. It was made known I was a newbie. There is only one table with an available outlet for a laptop charger and there's no way to connect to the wifi without going up and asking them how to do it. The chairs at the tables are uncomfortable - I can't sit here and work like I had planned. Ugh. Just such an awkward experience. I'll stick to Starbucks.

Super hipstery. Let's just get that out of the way. But when it comes to the burgers at this place, this is not a bad thing at all. If you're vegan, vegetarian, or gluten free, you're set! If you're a happy meat eater, you're also set! Go with the make-your-own burger option. You won't regret it. With a wide variety of classic and unusual options (elk burger with feta, anyone?), you're sure to find something you'll enjoy.

So I'll start with the positives... The place is super clean which in the french quarter is kinda hard to come by and I love the decor and all the old photos

I had the eggs Pontchartrain and split the french toast with my husband. Both were REALLY REALLY good.

The manager, Olga, was on top of her game and super pleasant. 

Now to the reason why I only gave 4 stars... Seems like they may be under staffed in the kitchen? Or maybe all the staff is new? I'm not sure. We sat upstairs but not on the patio but the waitress seemed overwhelmed with the tables outside and we were sitting for nearly 15-20 minutes before she came to the table. The manager got us our drinks and took our food order before the waitress ever made it to us even though she was told by the manager that she had another table. 

Our food didnt take extremely long, but longer than i feel like it should have and there were others who complained about the wait for food being like 35-40 minutes... I feel like its still a new place and still working out the kinks but my overall experience was good so if you can go knowing that and be understanding and patient, its definitely a place to put on your list to try. We will definitely be back

Big post office -  always a line, and seems like a union rule that only two counters are open even if there are a bunch of folks in line.   

Crazy busy today and when a third agent walked up to open a register "crazy-hair-slow talker" agent announced to all she was going to break and would see us all later.  Really??

Chips were greasy and not very good. Margaritas were a little watery. The crunchy tacos I had were good but the service and experience was so bad that I won't be returning.  Also parking is a nightmare which didn't help.

We went here last night - the atmosphere was great - cute decor makes you feel like you're in Italy! Our waitress was very nice, and the service was good. The food was very good, although the mozzarella sticks were more like mozzarella spring rolls. I don't recommend them. Salads are excellent and the pastas and meats were great, too. There was nothing we didn't like! Portions were really large though, so if would recommend splitting, skipping apps, or ordering an app as a meal!

Awesome place.  Burned 3 hours there on a Wednesday afternoon.  This place smells amazing inside from all the aroma from the crafty malts!  Beer is textbook Schlafly.  Go on a weekday and you're not going to get great service, as we sat outside and had to order beer at bar and pick up food at bar.  On that note, the outside bandshell with live music puts out some good vibes (esp. on a summer day).  And it was neat to see all the workers literally having meetings throughout the building.  Would have given 5 stars but the food was meh.  Nothing spectacular, but then again they specialize in beer and not food.  I think the menu went well with their pairings, its just that I've had better food at other brewpubs.  Will go back next time I'm in the area.

I am a fan! While this isn't gourmet pizza, it's still really good and delicious. The delivery service is awesome and fast. In addition to the pizza, the salad is really good. I would order from Zio over many other options in the city!

For all the hype I heard about PP, I just don't think it lived up to my expectations. We waited about 30 minutes on a Monday (which it seems like is on the shorter end) and I thought it was OK. Maybe I my expectations were too high or I ordered wrong. I actually got lunch- the turkey wrap, which I understand isn't their specailty but I also got a pancake on the side (nice you can do that) which was good and I also liked the warm syrup bottles on every table. They do have quite an extensive pancake menu.

It is a cozy restaurant and definitely a good place for breakfast, I was just expecting out of this world. As with most of the people in Nashville, the server was very friendly and even split our checks without asking. If you are in town for a short trip and the wait is 2 hours, I don't think it's necessarily worth the wait but is a good spot if you have time.
Cant say enough good things about it, prices are excellent for the quality of the food given

I have to say that I have stopped going to this Petsmart for grooming because of the staff.  Each time that I've walked into the grooming part of the store, either I am not acknowledged at all, or I am met by a blank stare until I say hello to someone. If these people are this unhappy, then they should probably find work elsewhere.  And even though my dog looks cute when they are finished, which is why I gave two stars, she almost always has scrapes and red places underneath her that look like she was burned by the clippers being too close, or too hot. Another reason I have stopped taking her there.
Wanted tacos near USF but was tired of Taco Bus. I got the Combo #1 with pollo tacos and it was good af. They loaded me up so it was well worth the price. Definitely coming back.

I have to give it up to Unique... I only held back one 1 star because we never got to the point that the proposed work needed to be done. 

I cannot recommend this company enough. I worked with Bob and Chris and they were both fantastic.  Bob came onsite twice to investigate my concerns and he came up with a reasonable solution to my problem. But as my condo is new construction, Bob recommended I reach out to the company that did my HVAC because the work was sub-par.  And after reaching out, the company agreed to fix the problem at no cost to me. 

So again, definitely consider Unique! Extremely professional and they really look out for their clients!!

OK here is the gig... been here about a dozen times and eaten about half those stops.  mostly I there for the adult beverages before UA football and basketball games. Will this time we went in today before the UofA vs Wazzu and I went with my buddy of mine and he told me about the Blue Plate special. 

Well when I hear Blue Plate special I'm thinking yes it's a blue hair dish what the heck is going on here right....?  Well I was unbelievably surprised that it was a creamy New England style clam chowder with chunks of clams in it that were absolutely huge and delicious.  So then I opted for adding the half of the BLT sandwich which we all know BLT is bacon lettuce tomato but they add avocado and cream cheese and holy s*** was it ridiculously awesome but it probably had to do with the 10 slices of bacon that were on it. 

How many times have you ever been to a place an order to BLT and there's two slices of witty/soggy horrible bacon on it ???

Well this wasn't the case it, was good solid slabs of bacon not real fatty and good portion of meat cooked perfectly....and it was absolutely killer...

I can't can't wait to go back for more belly of the pig and chunks of clams!

Was here when they first opened for a happy hour and only had the griddled corn cake which I remember being really yummy. But hadn't been back until last week when a friend suggested we meet here for dinner. Their guacamole is fresh and delicious. I like the corn chips better than the flour.
I got the Anaheim tacos that have shrimp and grilled Anaheim chilis. They were very tasty. I got them with a side of rice and beans which were pretty standard to most Mexican restaurants. Next time I think I'd try the Mexican beans that my friend got and liked. I tried a bite of her tostadita with sweet potato and pork which was delicious. 
This place is not your typical, gringo-fied Mexican restaurant. They have fresh takes on traditional dishes. I can't wait to go back and try something different next time!

I shopped Fair Wheel faithfully for years. Bought a mountain and road bike here over the years, knew some of the staff; I'd see guys like Bruce out on the road and say hi, things were great. Last month, I dropped in with an old gift certificate for $350. Long story, I'd bought it for an ex-girlfriend, we broke up, and I dropped it in a desk drawer and forgot about it. I bought it in 2010. I took it in hoping to cash it in; I've spent 4, 5 thousand over the years here, and they had the $350 already, so what's the problem? So I give it to the manager and ask him what we can do. After 10 minutes, he walks back out of the office and tells me they expire after a year. 
I call BS. If this were a firm policy, he would've known that straight away and not spent 10 minutes talking about it w the owner. I can only suspect that the owner or manager made the policy up on the spot. No apology, nothing. 
That's the kind of treatment I would accept from a major chain. That's one of the reasons I kept going back to Fair Wheel; buying parts I could've bought cheaper at Performance in order to keep supporting their business. 
I ate the $350; that's life. But you just lost a long-time customer and now, when someone needs a shop recommendation, I send them to Trek. Act like a major store and blow off loyal customers, get treated like one.

We did not expect to see a fist fight(6/9/2018) among staff members. What's more is we were surprised that they were not fired on the spot. 

The manager did find time to curse at them in front of customers, but no time to apologize to the customers who witnessed the fight. Pretty much pretended it didn't happen.

We will be avoiding this place in the future as frankly if there is that much strife spilling out of the kitchen when will they take it out on a customer.
Food is bent toward the spicy side, Netflix set on weird, and super awesome ladies behind the bar. Couldn't ask for much more. Viva la Pet Envy!!!!

This is one of the best places you will eat. Chef inspired entrees that are delicious.  I have been going here for years and everyone I take always rave about it. Huge portions and great service everytime.

I love this bar.  The atmosphere is fantastic.  It's great for conversation and has a sexy ambience.  Perfect for my occasion.  Service is acceptable, but the decor and music make up for any shortcomings.

This place is realy good (wine, food, specials) 
Thursdays is wine tasting and small plate special night check it out

We went on a Friday night, about 6:30 pm.  When we got there they told us there were no tables available, so we sat at the bar.  At that point every table was available, but there were reservations for them.  

This was our first trip back to Xochitl since they re-did the menu.  We had only been once and thought the food was pretty good, so we were expecting even better.

After a few house margaritas at the bar, the bartender gave us a heads up that happy hour was over in 1 minute if anyone wanted a refill.  We thought that was pretty nice of her.

The four of us split 2 apps, which was enough food to whet our appetites before the main course.  The girls got fish tacos, the boys got pulled pork tacos and everyone shared.  After dinner we shared the churros which were not as good as I remember, though still good.

After we paid the check, the bartender offered us a free round of tequila shots before heading out - a great end to a great meal.  We left with enough food (but not too much) and a nice buzz.  I would go there again in a second.

Waited 20 minutes to be seated it did not happen. Waiter / Hostess told us it just be a few minutes "twice" but did nothing to prepare a clean table or ask us if we would like to sit at the counter.
So we left, can't say how the food is and wont be finding out soon or going back I am sure!
Way way to expensive. I can seriously eat at the outback or roadhouse.

The Humane Society does a great job of trying to run things as smoothly and efficiently as possible making sure that all of their animals have a great home.  Before we adopted our beagle, my fiance and I had to go through a long adoption process.  However, I rather us go through that then just being adopted a dog without them even knowing if we would be good parents or not.

If you are looking to adopt, this is the place to go.  Everything is pretty clean and the smell isn't too terrible considering the amount of animals they have.  There were a ton of cats there needing home, a few other animals (bunnies, birds, etc.), and then there were the dogs.  While the dogs were overrun with pit bulls and chihuahuas, you can usually find a golden egg in there (unless, however, those are the types of dogs you are looking for).  We found our beagle in between two loud, barking pitbulls.  We almost didn't end up with her because I couldn't stand the barking and wanted to leave.  However, I'm glad that we didn't leave!

One thing is that it's hard to know anything about your animals because they are mostly stray animals (although a few were brought in by owners who just couldn't take care of them anymore).  This means you have to spend some time getting to know your animal, but the Humane Society does the best they can with the information they know.  They will also spay/neuter any animal that comes through the shelter and give them all of their shots in addition to testing their temperaments out with different situations.

Overall, I can't say enough good things about them!!!

So Gluten Friendly! Who knew. I have been allergic to wheat my whole like so I drive by anything that says bakery or pizza. Anyway, a friend insisted I go and to my delight I had one of the best breakfasts I have ever had. I had the AM Relleno. It was unbelievably good and beautifully presented. My husband had the Eggs in the Basket. I was stealing his roasted potatoes which were to die for. The service was impeccable. Our waitress knew everything about the dishes and talked about them with such enthusiasm. They have a mind blowing mimosa menu which was fun. I had the blueberry lemon mimosa and my husband had a prickly pear. So much better than your standard OJ and champagne. Beautiful atmosphere to take some one special. Unbelievable food. I can't wait to go again!

I had a CL deal to burn and ordered the Bistec ala Mexican (strip steak) last Thursday night.  The steak was nicely cooked and well seasoned, as were the sautéed onions and peppers. The black beans were good but nothing overly impressive.  The bartender I ordered with was helpful and friendly.  My issue was with the size of the entree.  As one of the priciest options on the menu the portion should be enough for a meal.  This was reminiscent of the scaled down sizes served to early-birds or as lunch.  It wouldn't have even filled a single tortilla.  The only sufficient portion was the big pile of rice.... go figure. Luckily I had a CL deal, otherwise I wouldn't been more upset.
Always a great time, fresh and fun pub food. Delicious Irish fare as well! Have a bit of everything as well as a private room for functions! Love this place!

Beer battered cornbread hit the spot. Fried green beans were amazing.  I had the chicken pot pie which was pretty good, though it was somewhat bland.  My friends had the burger and yellow tail, all of which they loved.

The service was awesome.  Prompt and friendly staff.  Ambiance was cool and not stuffy.
A bit on the pricier side, but portions are much more than what you get at similar priced restaurants. 

I can't wait to come back and try other dishes!!

Soooo I don't really have a penchant for beer drinking -- wino here, but when I do drink beer, I prefer local craft options.  theCityMoms did an event here in September and this was a perfect location!  I loved the mid-town accessibility and there is always plenty of parking.  It's cozy and intimate inside with an approachable bar, showing off the latest brews.  The staff was awesome and accommodating for the moms who needed to come in and warm up with a brew or a place to sit.  I had a blond wheat which I don't think is on their current rotating list but it was delicious.  I thought the price was on point as well and not too expensive.  They do growler fills and offer seasonal choices throughout the year.  Great place to meet up with friends new and old.  Making beer wishes and dreams come true - always something new to try.

In terms of Korean restaurants in the nearby area, Eden ranks as one of the better ones. I used to like Sammy Chon's BBQ (formerly Myung-Ga) but quality has declined and prices have increased since the name change. Be warned, if you're looking for expensive Korean BBQ, Eden does not serve that type of food. 

To me, the food tastes home-made and authentic. The owner is extremely nice and also really Korean. You can get by in English but it's Korean all the way. All of the customers that I have seen are Korean, which reaffirms my view that the food tastes and seems more authentic. 

I had the Sujebi (spicy noodles with seafood), which was a slight mistake because it was 80 degrees and nice outside. However, the noodles themselves had a great texture and were delicious! It came with a variety of seafood that was pretty fresh and a giant clam. I definitely look forward to eating it again when it's colder outside. 

I've also tried Nakji Dolsot w/ brown rice, which was good, but not great. The calamari was eh. They don't have it on the menu, but I would prefer a Bulgogi Dolsot or a Spicy Pork Dolsot. I'm pretty certain that they would make it for me if I asked though. 

Give this place a shot. It doesn't look that great on the outside or inside but the food and prices make this place worth it. It's a regular for when I want Korean.

Flew in from LA and had heard about this restaurant from friends that live in Philly and I finally tried it last night. It was the perfect Fall evening with the perfect fall menu of Roasted beets and a wonderful pheasant dish.  The food is remarkable and I was very impressed as was the service. Had the pleasure of meeting the owners and the evening was a 10.  Perfect restaurant, Excellent cuisine and nice ambiance in a beautiful part of the city. 
Will be back every time I come to Philly!

Despite the name this place doesn't come close to any of the NYC pizzerias I've tried. Of course not many cities have pies of the quality served in NYC-problem is they don't come close to the other top local places either. To be positive it's not bad pizza just nothing special. Somewhat disinterested service at the bar the one time I went even though the place was empty. I'll give it another at some point-maybe.

Visiting the st. Petes area from Michigan. This was the best steak my husband and I have ever had. I can't say enough good things about this restaurant! Service was amazing, salad that comes with the meal is amazing, food is amazing. I'd give more stars if I could.

Everyone we spoke to gushed about how great this place was. With an 8 year old to help us judge, I'd say it was very good but not at the level one would have you believe. 

The transformer's exhibit was lame, but everything else was top notch. A hands on science exhibit allowed my son to make his own cheese, and the rock climbing wall was more challenging that what you'd find at a street fair. The planetarium and historical kids displays were great, as was the Avatar section. The part on Eygpt was not only cheap and generic feeling , the recent protests and change in government made it feel out of place in a Children's museum.

The restaurant area had a vast array of food choices and the toy store was full of unique items.

We spent 7 hours there and glad we did so, yet I was left slightly disappointed in the end.
The best in Southern comfort food!  The fried chicken was the best I've ever had!  Definitely worth the wait time!

This is our favorite restaurant in St. Pete! Fantastic food! Great Happy hour deals! The only negative I've ever experienced is the service can be slow sometimes, but everything else is so fantastic that we hardly notice!

Boyfriend and I walked in to get pedicures and they were amazing! First off, there was no wait, which was great! We got the foot facial pedicure and OMG AMAZING! Did a neon pink gel polish on my toes, had 18 min massage, masques, extremely relaxing and luxurious service! Our feet look and feel FANTASTIC! I highly recommend this salon to anyone who is looking for a service in the area! Definitely will be returning here! Also, very clean and attractive decor! Loved it!

Fresh mussels and clams in their own broth with warm toasted bread.  So simple but so delicious. So good that I got a shirt from them.  The walk through window was busy too.  The seats were minimal and appropriate for this spot.  A true seafood shack.

My favorite bar in all of New Orleans... 

Neighborhood AF and with an awesome/well executed cocktail menu! Homey, divey and the bartenders really know their stuff. Rotating food pop ups outside for your late night drunchies.

I've always bemoaned the lack of good hot dog places nearby. No more. Hot Diggity has great dogs and fresh cut fries. I had the Saigon which is like a banh mi but with a hot dog instead of compressed pig's ears. Come to think of it that may not be all that much different. The greens on the Saigon were super crisp and fresh and the fries were awesome. They could use less salt though.

A few suggestions:

1) They have dogs from all over the world but no Philly dog?
2) When you walk in the first thing you see is the posting for the Bronx Bomber. Now I'm from New York originally but I'd rather not see a dog named for the NY Yankees right when I walk into the place, in Philly.
3) The menu drawings for each item are cool but you can't see the ones in the back. Hopefully they'll add a menu on the wall to the left to look at if you are in line.
4) They put aluminum foil on the grill to cook the dogs. Heresy! I grew up near the original Nathan's. One of the reasons Nathan's hot dogs taste so good is that the grill gets seasoned with all the dogs cooking all day. I know the foil thing is cleaner but seriously, if I was that interested in cleanliness why would I be eating hot dogs in the first place?

Overall though this is my new go to place. Service is friendly and food is great. Good ambience. I hope they don't ruin it with a TV like so many other places have.

I like everything about this place but the food.  Owner is nice and polite, menu has quite a few options but the taste of their food is something which doesn't appeal to me.
I have tried alot of their food every time I thought of giving it another chance but I sadly to have say that I did not find anything tasty.

Smallest parking lot ever! Long line, 20 minute wait so not horrible! Food was quick and hot! Portion was generous but didn't have the presentation of some other Ramen restaurants in town. Oyster balls are a pass, potstickers we're flavorable. Service was slow on drink refills even though reminded at least twice. All in all good but not a must return.

My wife and I have been going to New Orleans once a year or so for the past few years, spending most of our time seeking out the best restaurants (and music) that we can find.  Bacchanal is our favorite, it's usually the first place we have dinner every trip.

It's a small but well stocked wine store in front.  You select your wine (very reasonable prices), pay for it at the counter and then head out back to the patio.  The patio is beautiful and relaxed. 
 There's a stage at one end, jazz starts at 7:30.  Pick up your wine glasses out of the dishwasher racks that are stacked outside the entrance and find a table.

Head to the kitchen door, look at the menu and choose your dishes.  Give them your order and head back to your table, they'll bring you your food when it's ready.  We've never been disappointed with anything we've ordered there.
This is the best fast food place ever. Food is always great and it's always fast no matter how many people are in line. The whole staff is pleasant as well. Kudos to Lee's.

Maybe one of the more interesting businesses in one of the strangest strip malls Ive ever seen. Walking in it looks like a fast food place. Milk tea on one side and food on the other. THere are lcd screens above that highlight both generic and Taiwanese specific fare. If not for a friend's rec, we wouldnt have known what to go for or that this place existed. Got the stinky tofu, Taiwanese sausage, beef tendon in chili oil, pork belly bun and green onion pancakes. The pancakes were under cooked but the tofu, tendon and sausage were good. Pork bun was ok. Service is what you'd expect and they were efficient but not too talkative. I guess for Reno this is pretty good.

It would be nice if just once a Walmart was actually stocked.  I have yet to go into any Walmart and walk out with everything I need. And what's up with the geriatric security force patrolling the front doors?  Most shoppers are not thieves!  Make shoppers feel welcome not like they're an inconvenience. Wake up Walmart.
Amazing, It just sucks that it's always so crowded, but it's because they are awesome!  If they don't have something you like, then you got problems.

They have the best burger in Philly.  The ambience strikes a delicate balance between fancy and casual:  It's the kind of place where someone in jorts can sit beside someone in a suit, and neither will feel out of place.  The burgers are thick and cooked to order, with a slew of high-quality toppings.  The drink selection is solid, especially in the realm of whiskey.  It's a little on the pricey side, but I keep coming back because the quality, service, and ambience are worth it.

I learned about See Spot Eat from my doggie daycare (Bark-O-Lounge). I love this place! 

These guys have some great treats for your furry friend. We bought a birthday cake for our dog from this place and it was adorable. It was shaped like a bone and had his name on it. My Bunk The Pug loves their treats. Some of his favorites are: macaroons, doggie pizza, the martini glasses, PUP-CAKES, and of course, the cakes! 

Sometimes, we also like to handpick different flavored biscuits for him. These are freshly baked and Bunk loves them. They're quite big so for a 17 pounder like mine, you might want to break them down into smaller pieces. 

I also love the samples that they always have available for your puppies- big and small. 

The store has a great environment and the decorations are adorable. 

We adore our pug and any chance to make him feel more special is appreciated by us. See Spot Eat makes that possible. 

They also sometimes run events to support the dog charities in the neighborhood. 

I am very glad to support this local business. 

TIP: Call them ahead of time to get cakes made to your specifications because on the day of, they can only give you cakes with a bone shape. That's what we are doing for this year!

The 3 rolls for $10.25 is a great deal. I got it for take out, the staff was friendly and quickly prepared the rolls. It was a lot of food for the price, and I'm glad that the deal is all day rather than just the lunch crowd. I ordered the lobster roll (similar to spicy salmon without the spicy), spicy tuna, and an alaskian roll (salman, cucumber, avocado). All were good, especially the price. I would definitely and probably will go back soon.
Loved the atmosphere, lobster roll was delicious, service was good. The PEI oysters were microscopic, so we weren't charged for them. The food is pricey but I would back again.

This place is amazing!! So welcoming on arrival.

Went here last night with my fiancé. We got 1/4 chicken and 1/4 pork, both are served with the tastiest potatoes I've ever had. We also ordered the half cauliflower and half carrots, both amazing. Everything was so good and there was so much of it! Our server was fantastic. She was helpful with the menu and explained all the food when it came out.

Without a doubt the best meal I've had in Edmonton. I cannot wait to return!

awesome carne asada burritos! when el guero canelo is too far to drive, Nico's is the next best thing.  Carne asada buritos, carne asada and egg burritos, and carne asada fries (ask for well done) are the beez kneez. Haven't tried much else on the menu, when it works, why fix it?! Only downside is only 1 24 hour location that I know of (ft. lowell and cambell i think).  really good salsa if you like chile rojo.
One of my favorite in New Orleans! My favorite dish is mr. B's barbecued shrimp. Very big gulf shrimp w really rich bbq butter sauce. It is really yummy but a bit messy to eat.

I was blown away by the service provided at Spaz Beverage. I was immediately greeted as I entered the building. A gentleman helped me select the beverage that I needed. Carried it to the register as well as my car. Every single employee was smiling. I have used this example in many pep talks that I have had with my team when I am trying to describe the type of service I expect from my team. 
Just a great experience.
Stopped in with my mom and boyfriend on a whim. I had the street fries with asada, plus a taco with al pastor. Everything was delicious! Can't wait to come back!

I have never in my life been soon impressed with an establishment.  There is so much love put into this family run, non-chain restaurant.  The food was awesome and the portions large enough I brought some home to enjoy tomorrow.  I had the mashed potatoes and cornbread for my sides and devoured them.  The owner was manning the front tonight which was so nice.  He really knew his product and took pride in his recipes and his sauces.  I appreciated the unlimited refills....even though I didn't make it through the first lemonade.  I recommend everyone pop in here at least once and let their magic work on you!

Stopped in Pizzeria Vetri late on Sunday night. Found parking easy on the street. The place is in a very nice store front and is simple, hip and clean. They have some outdoor seating, but we chose indoors.The waitress service was very good. They have a nice selection of rotating beers.  We ordered the following:

Quattro formaggi pizza - gorgonzola, mozzarella, smoked provolone, fontina

Salsiccia - fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, mozzarella

Arugula salad- coal roasted potatoes, pesto, taggiasca olives

The pizza was great, probably the best I have had in awhile. The crust is light and fluffy with just a touch of wood fried burn. The toppings are just right and tasted very fresh and were not oily.  I really liked Pizzeria Vetri and I will be back to try some other menu items and desserts.

AMAZING first place we tried after days of horrible food in Florida!!! Gator burger was amazing!! The flavor was delicious. My hubby ordered the burger with the grilled cheese and that was exactly what we imagined cheesy gooey goodness!!! The hot dog was also a weaner...get it lol winner!!! The staff didn't fall short of the food.  Great service easy going atmosphere. Cold AC. Flat screens everywhere. Great experience. I'll definitely be back next time I visit!!!

Great technicians, knowledgeable, prompt, they stay in touch. They don't charge you for anything more than they quote and will give you options. In my case they waived the service fee and I bought a maintenance service plan that covers both my plumbing and HVAC at a reasonable price. I'm happy! Definitely recommend

Today was my first visit and I am less than impressed.  I liked what I saw on the breakfast menu but opted for a lunch item instead - chicken cordon blu.  The wait was average for take out but the person behind the counter seemed new and overwhelmed with the small amount of business (me waiting to pay, and order she just took and already forgot, and a phone call that she took part of the order from and then told to hold).   My chicken sandwich was not made the way it was described in the menu which made it not a CCB.  It was served with a side of what I can only guess was the last remaining breakfast potatoes.  Not only where they not what I was expecting to receive with a lunch meal (ordered at 11am), but they were way overlooked, some burnt, and completely cold.  In addition, most of the pieces of potatoes were just small fragments of what used to be much larger pieces resulting in more of what could be described as potato crumble. Burnt potato crumble.  Burnt cold potato crumble.  All of this came to almost $10 with tax.  Had I not ordered this meal as take out and left the area it would have definitely been sent back. My first experience there left me feeling less than satisfied and ripped off.

Okay, I read there was a big problem with the service times. 

It took nearly 45 minutes for my wife and I to get our food. We didn't even order anything complicated. The people sitting next to us were also frustrated. 

My wife and I were excited to try it. The place was packed. There was a sign that said "best breakfast in Tucson" in the front window. 

Our server also looked very frustrated. She barely came by to check on us and ask if we needed anything or wanted a refill because she probably seemed embarrassed. 

The food was brought out and at least it was hot. The food was good, but not great. I brought the wait time up to the woman at the counter and she just said "yeah, it gets like that." She gave us a 10% discount though. 

Would I come back here? Nah. Would I recommend? No.

I love going to the Fair because I didn't get to do so when I was growing up. It is very pricy because of the admission, tickets, and food but a fun treat for a family! Unfortunately, there are too many people in the evening time so lines for rides are super long! I didn't go on any rides this year but I did get some good food. The chicken-on-a-stick is delicious! Perfectly cooked and flavorful. The ribs, though a lot, are dried and not as flavorful. I also had a funnel cake and deep fried reese's cup. Delicious food!

This is my mom's favorite restaurant and bar in Reno.  It's a perfect place to go and watch any game.  The service is prompt and the waitresses never leave you with an empty glass.  Typical bar food, so don't go here if you're on a diet!  Everything I've ordered from wings to a burger was good....but the atmosphere is what makes this a great place to watch a game!

Reserved a car for my boss' business trip. I reserved well in advance a mid-size car which was the same price as economy with the bigger name places. When my boss arrived, they said that the car was "not available". He was forced to pay for an upgrade. He also said the counter person was very aggressive trying to sell him on other stuff. Not worth the hassle!

Hours keep getting moved back. Now closing at 1 or 2 pm!!!

Possibly losing business? Closing? I hope not, as his Crepes are delicious and he's a friendly guy (just get past that initial Eastern European abruptness at first). 

Sad to see its not open for an early afternoon meal or cup of coffee anymore.

We arrived in Philly for the first time ever bleary eyed and a little bewildered. Fortunately the closest place to our airbnb was Honey's which was very fortuitous as it is the best brunch I've had to date this year. Which is really saying a lot as I live in New York which is definitely not short on options. We were accomadated immediately  on both days (yes we came back on Sunday!). Our servers were enthusiastic, friendly and very, very helpful. There are a bounty of vegetarian options which is unfortunately not the case in most places. The food was delicious, reasonably priced and the eggs were free range. If we lived closer we'd definitely come back all the time! I'd highly recommend it.

This Diner is worth seeing. It is a very attractive building. Service and food were great. I would definitely go again if I were in the area. If you are at Camden County Community College this place is not far away.

As a brooklynite I was very skeptical that I might find decent tacos in Indianapolis, but this place is pretty legit.  The space itself felt real, wasn't trying too hard to be cool.  Staff was friendly (except the annoying cook who was really loud and seemed as though he really needed/wanted attention), beer list was thorough, tequila/mezcal list was equally as impressive and the tacos were close to outstanding.
Minus half star for the "look at me, I'm a cook who sings and makes fun of the customers" guy in the kitchen.
Minus the second half for cheese in one of my tacos, it was not in the description and I'm not very tolerant I lactose.
Probably would have given them 4 anyway, 5 stars for tacos is no easy task, but these guys were close.  If they were in New York i may have given them three stars because the competition is stiffer but i a grading on a curve here...
I ended up eating there two nights in a row.  Even with a two mile walk from my hotel downtown.
I will go back, I am in Indy two or three times a year for work/races.  It really was quite good and where the hell else am I going to go in Indianapolis???

It's on account of the 1 1/2 hr long wait at Jacques-Imo's that we ended up getting appetizers at Squeal. 

I really liked the feel of this place. They had Abita Amber on tap, and it was nice and cold. Yay!

We ordered wings, onion rings, roasted corn cheese grits, and a casserole-like dish with pulled pork, cheese, and I-can't-remember-what else. 

The onion rings ROCKED. You get a ton of 'em for like $4. I am a BIG fan of that! The wings were really good too. You can get either pepper sauce or bbq sauce, and we went with the bbq ones. The grits were tasty, too. I didn't love the pulled pork dish - just not my gig. But it was hot, flavorful.... just not my taste. 

Service was friendly, if a little slow. Overall, though, it had a great feel and would definitely go back.
Three of five within my family got sick from eating here today. Chicken was the common ingredient. One was classic chicken quesadilla and two chicken freso. We will not eat here again.

Hit surreys at off hours. It closes at 3pm and has a good lunch menu. Come on a weekday do avoid the crush. I took this approach today and I have to say its a quite improved appearance. You can actually absorb the quaint decor and the wait staff is in a much better mood. The prices are quite reasonable. Fresh ingredients and my side recommendation- the potato salad. Check it out when things aren't so hectic and bring cash, you will leave happy.

I've had Whitts several times over the years and it is always good. They offer pork and turkey barbecue, ribs, and baked potatoes. Sides are potato salad, baked beans, slaw and chips. All sides are good, although not the best I've ever had. I pretty much only like the slaw on the sandwich and would not eat it by itself. It is definitely a vinegar based slaw and has no mayonnaise/dressing or carrots like you find in some slaws. On Wednesdays they have a family pack special which includes a pound of pork barbecue, a pint of a side item, and a pack of buns for $9.99. Not bad considering we can make 4 meals out of it. This particular location is to-go only. They are closed on Sundays and close at 8pm nightly so plan accordingly.
This is a great place to find foods of Taiwan in Reno.   It is great that is near casino.  Food is tasty both to my Taiwanese wife and her Caucasian husband

Wow, this place was delicious! Everything we ordered was fresh and flavorful. It's also a BYOB and is very inexpensive. . . . we ordered two grilled meat sticks, a salad, and two main dishes and the whole meal came to $26 before tip. The service was very friendly thought a bit slow. We learned from our waiter that this is his family's first restaurant (the cooks are his mother and grandmother!) so perhaps the service will improve over time. Even if it doesn't, the food at Khymer Kitchen is well worth the wait.

OK campground. Sites are tight but it's Nashville. Staff definitely needs a course in customer relations. Spent three nights at TR. As I was packing to leave I was told by an employee that I owed for a night. I replied that I had paid for three nights and had stayed for three nights. No she said " You owe for a night". She was very assertive. Before leaving I found my receipt and stopped in at the office to confirm that nothing was owing. When I showed the same employee my receipt she simply stated " oh yes I did some research and you do not owe anything". No apology, no explanation. Will I return here. Not a chance. KOA is two minutes away.

Lovely spot and the veggies omelette is the perfect breakfast for me. Was in the fortunate position I was staying one block away (at the equally brilliant victorian house on Magazine 1455: see airbnb), but it's worth a little trip.

I'm giving them four stars because they are fast, efficient, give a good haircut, and have a convenient location.  That being said, the $22 haircut is a bit steep.  Also, I had a weird experience with the Saturday barber (apparently he cuts on Friday and Saturday only).  The entire cut was done with my back to the mirror.  It is comforting to be able to watch what my barber is doing to my hair, so to go through the 20 minute cut without seeing it, especially as it was my first time there, was disconcerting.

I drove a long distance to see if the cheese steaks were that good or just hype. The shop is in a mixture of businesses and homes so I had to park a block away. It was a nice day so no issue.
