Never fixed it properly, leaks like a sieve to this day. Also, check the reviews on the type of roofing they try to sell you. For very little more we were able to upgrade to much better product. They buy a certain type of roofing in bulk so they make more money off of it. Don't let them fast talk you into a lower-quality product. Very satisfied with roof and guttering only.

I've been hearing this place was great, and have to admit that I was disappointed. 

The food just ok. I ordered a frozen strawberry pina colada margarita and it was WAY too sweet, and my friend said her margarita on the rocks was just fair. 

The dinning room is really large, and it seems like a good place for families since it was pretty loud, had huge menu and prices were reasonable. 

As much as I hate to admit I like a chain rest better than independently owned restaurant...I'd go to Chevy's over this place. Not bad, just not inspiring either.

Khyber Pass is one of those  places that's great for taking guests from out of town. The good is tasty and excellent quality, and it has that unique, hole-in-the-wall feel. The menu is diverse without being overwhelming, and there's something for everyone regardless of dietary restrictions.

Service can be hit or miss here (we had a really rude waitress once and could not for the life of us figure out what we did, since she acted like we were bothering her from the very beginning), but it's usually good. Service at the bar has always been excellent. The ambiance created by the dim lighting and colorful, Christmas-type lights is very nice, but it can be very loud between the music and the conversation going on around you.

I highly recommend the Khyber Burger and the fried chicken po boy. The sweet potato fries are delicious, and I think the cole slaw is the best I've ever had (and if not, it's definitely top three). As an appetizer, definitely the bacon grease popcorn - yum! This is not the place to go if you're watching your weight, but it sure is tasty!

Very good food.  I get the Moo-shoo something everytime I go and it's always a treat.  They are also heavy handed with their drinks so the pina colada (though and odd choice of drink with chinese food) will make for a more enjoyable evening.

There is a fish dish that you have to call ahead to order or wait a long time--which seems weird to me, but I wouldn't get it anyway.

I stayed here for 5 days and have to say Union League is an impressive looking French Renaissance-styled building. I've always admired the UL every time I walk pass it. 

Union League is members only private club. they have a strict dress code policy. Jeans, sneakers, t-shirts, etc are not permitted on the 1st and 2nd floors. Men are required to wear jackets in the dining rooms. Whenever I walked in and out of the hotel in my jeans, I definitely felt self-conscious. Also, there just weren't many young people at this place.

The room is spacious with a King sized bed. but its a shame that they don't have a bathtub! But i liked the plush bath robes that they provided. For some reason i wasn't able to detect the WiFi so I had to plug in the LAN cable.

In addition to the continental breakfast fare, the  breakfast has an omelet and waffle station. The chef is a sweet man. Each morning he'd brighten up my day by giving me generous compliments and making me a very delicious salmon omelet. In general, the staff here seemed to appreciate seeing a young woman in  a precinct thats predominantly white professional male.

The winner for me is their snack bar, which is replenished 24 hours. There's a big bowl of roasted mixed nuts (no peanut), What Thins, pretzels, fresh fruits, yogurt, fruit juices and hot drinks. Very convenient when I'm experiencing the munchies. and I love my almonds, hazel, brazil, cashew and walnuts.

The gym's pretty decent. They have LifeFitness cardio machines: 4 treadmills, 3 ellipticals, 4 stairmasters. There is also a selection of weights machines, not extensive but good enough for a hotel gym. There's also the free weights section as well as the stretching section with Swiss balls in assorted sizes. The trainers are very friendly and always ready to assist. I love how they have available headphones for you to borrow so you can watch CNN while using the Elliptical. The locker room has a sauna and a massage room. And I really appreciate the available t-shirts, shorts and socks for me to change into. Very handy since I forgot my gym clothes. And they have toiletries available too so you don't have to bring your own. Even curling iron and hair spray and spray deodorant.

Expect everything to be very old world formal. Snooty? Yes.

1. Mold on the Shower Curtain.  
Asked the front desk to replace it.  ...was told they would replace it immediately, so I went on with my day/evening exploring Reno.   Returned to the room very late in the evening only to find the same moldy shower curtain.  Asked again the next morning for a replacement and it was finally done.  This simple request should not have ever required me to ask twice.

2. WiFi constantly disconnected.  
At first I attributed this to being on the top floor, but later I tried to connect in the lobby and found the same level of uselessness with the WiFi.  Luckily my Verizon service would connect allowing me to get some work done... no thanks to Marriott.

2. Ripped/Torn Couch Cushion.  
Honestly, This didn't even bother me too much except that they didn't even try to conceal or hide the problem which would only have taken the effort of flipping the cushion over.  

3. Inexplicable Interior Design by a random 10 year old.
Someone decided a good place to hang "artwork" would be behind the TV despite there being ample wall space with no obstruction.  Again...maybe not a big deal, but it reflects a general lack of basic effort on the part of the hotel to appear marginally comfortable and/or attractive to it's guests.

Road warrior here....on the road for 3 weeks at a time in a city, so doing laundry while traveling is normal for me.   Stayed at the Grove, they don't have a coin operated laundry for guests, so I come to Jiffy Clean when I'm in town.   Spotlessly clean (believe me, I've seen some grungy laundromats in this country.)   The machines are wiped down often, clean inside and out, the floors and folding counters are clean, and the attendant is constantly working the room.   The soap dispenser and change machine is in the far room around the corner.   I love the credit card reader on all of the machines.   Good assortment of top and front loaders and cheap (25 cent) dryers.  Top loader will take only 29 minutes for a cycle on the warm water setting.   And the Korean restaurant next door is great for a meal while doing laundry!

My husband and I had dinner at Chase recently and while the atmosphere was interesting the rest of it was a let down.  The service was not very good, though I must admit the server seemed to be aware of the fact that everything was slow and seemed to feel badly about it.  The food was only mediocre and my husband got very sick from eating it.

It's come to my attention that yelpers tend to be overly enthusiastic about a location or overy critical. This seems to be one of those situations. 

Revolucion has some great stuff going on. The ambiance is spectacular, just the right amount of divey with exceptionally well thought out decor. Many people have given shout outs to the Luche Libra decor but I'm going with the dia de los muertos artwork. It's all works very well together and gives the diner/drinker something to enjoy while they are there. The service was very prompt, which I appreciate, especially when dining alone. They took great care of me despite being hidden behind the beer tower in the only empty seat I could find upon my arrival.

The beer selection is pretty great, I went with the Two Brothers tap, a beer I had never sampled before, I was very happy with the choice, it was a great beer. They have a small but good selection of local and craft brews to suit any appetite. 

As for the food it was probably the more forgettable part of my experience. I enjoyed the food, to be sure, but admittedly the other Yelpers set my expectations a bit too high  on this one. The hot chipotle  salsa was good, but did not blow me away and ditto the veggie tacos. The fresh made tortillas were a high point and but the veggie filling was just ok. I did leave just full enough off of just the two tacos, the portion is perfect for a meal without being too heavy. 

All in all the experience was good, they great service and awesome atmosphere covered for the foods lack of wow. I look forward to going back for the fish tacos and some more offerings from the kitchen. 

You absolutely should check this place out!

Thank you to Jim and team for a nice tour. So happy to learn about your service to our community.  Your staff has been so incredible in your support of Heroes In Recovery and The Next Door.  I'm so impressed with how friendly the staff has been.  Your ECT room was impressive.

My husband and I took friends for dinner over the Christmas holiday.  They were in from out of town and craved good food. Our server was amazing - she knew everything about the food and the bar.  We were extremely impressed!  I ordered the Amish Chicken - phenomenal.  Friends ordered the ribeye and cornmeal encrusted Missouri trout - impressed.  Didn't know what to think about the trout from reading the menu since I think of fishing for trout in a local river... however, i was blown away.  Their broccoli was AMAZING.  Seriously, come home and cook it for us, please. We ordered the mac n' cheese to share - it was flavorful and we would totally order it again, however, part of the dish was so salty we couldn't eat it.  We think it may have been the breadcrumb topping.  In any event, it was delicious. We are always happy when we leave The Block.  Also, Amy (owner, manager, etc.) was there and it was great to see her - keep up the hard work - The Block is yummy!

Always love to visit this hidden gem when in Nashville. It's a great choice for BBQ in Brentwood. 
Pretty small but tasty !!

We enjoyed eating downstairs in the open area lakeside with a light breeze and lovely views. Everything and everyone working here is still relatively or brand new, so there are some glitches to be overcome. Friendly, affordable and comfortable - enjoy Felix's open air.
All the furniture I saw were all way over priced  and I am certain I saw many of the same things on Craigslist being given away for free. Also isn't it illegal to sell used mattresses?

This is the best classic Italian pizza in central Bucks County.
Crust is thin and fresh.  Dough is made here.  This means that it is more tender, develops a better crunch and smells  like fresh bread.
There is no other way to make a really good pizza.
Toppings are varied and plentiful.  Also meat balls are very good tender and flavorful, rolls are fresh;  sauce is for real.  
Paninnis are well made and grilled just right.
Slices or whole pies are available.  Honest teas,  Boylan sodas and fountain drinks are for sale as well.
We go out of the way for this pizza.  It is worth it.

Food was decent - 

Bloody Mary - one of the worst bloodies I had during my time in NOLA. Might be me, but it was very horseradish-y and not at all spicy. tasted like cocktail sauce with vodka. I would pass on this if I were you

Eggs Dauphine - they overcooked the eggs (hard yolks) and the pork was really fatty - but it was still delicious. Would eat again.

Chicken and Waffles - sweet potato waffle tasted pretty bland/normal.  They didn't give us any syrup, maybe on purpose since it's served with a savory sauce but you can't eat this thing without it bc it's REAL dry.

Guatemalan - good. plantains are a nice touch but the rest is nothing to write home about: eggs, beans, tortilla. 


Service was okay - poor. Our waitress didn't stop by our table unless we intentionally flagged her down which we had to do to get silverware, coffee refills, syrup for pancakes, and hot sauce....so that was frustrating. 

Overall it might be a little overpriced for the quality of food and service. However still not a horrible option.

Don't place a delivery order from here, or actually any location. You'll get the pleasure of speaking with an employee who sounds miserable. I have placed a delivery order twice and never again will that happen. The first order I placed was a pepperoni pizza. Sounds simple right? But when the girl on the other end asked me what toppings I wanted I simply said pepperoni, obviously because cheese comes with your pizza unless otherwise stated. When my pizza arrived I had a pizza with pizza sauce and pepperoni. She had actually taken me literally. 
The next time I ordered delivery I ordered a pepperoni with 2 extra toppings. When I asked the SAME girl if cheese came on the pizza she answered annoyed "Ya, it's standard" .. Yeah I know. Rustys is crap when it comes to customer service.

Our family enjoys Chickfila, no matter the location.  Always consistent good food and friendly service.  Jalen was exceptionally helpful today!  We appreciate his patience with mutiple kids trying to order....service with a smile and extra helpful!

Service A+
Food A+
Atmosphere A+

A friend recommended this new establishment and after a disaster of a meal at downtown kitchen yesterday I was really hoping this place would be somewhat better, and it was! The staff was very friendly, very attentive without being overbearing. The food came out with perfect timing. I just felt like I was being taken care of by everyone at the restaurant with just the right amount of attention. 

The atmosphere was fantastic. The restaurant had a very modern but upscale décor. The interior actually doesn't sit too many people, which is fine it gives clients a very intimate experience with the restaurant, whereas the patio area was very lively and colorful. 

The food. I had originally wanted to try the mussels but since it was happy hour I decided to give the braised beef tacos a try and the first bite was simply perfection, I had a headache from a long day of work but I think that bite made it go away! The entrees are well made, and desserts few but the burnt caramel custard was done just right. 

price: very fair. It came out to be less than I anticipated I definitely think it was worth every penny unlike some other places where good money is shelled out for very little in return. 

highly recommended. I'm hoping this level of service and quality of food would remain as it becomes more popular.
Very classy joint!  Make sure u use the valet and park in the wine & spirits parking lot!  Just a hop-skip and a jump to get to the Kup from there!  Dressy-formal attire!  Have fun!

I am very picky with my pizza and wings. This place exceeded all my expectations. Love their fluffy crust and their wings are so good. The sauces have great flavor. It's far from my side of town but I will not mind the drive because it's worth it  please open one downtown or around the Tucson Spectrum area .

Love a Black Thorn spicy Chicago SOB ... Seriously delicious. Do call ahead because it takes an hour and 15 minutes... eat your pizza there because it is now smoke free (thank you ban!!!!) Tasty pizza, pinball, cold beer and great bathroom reading!

I made an appointment online at the last minute and the process was quick and easy. I ended up having my hair cut by Cameron, and she did a fantastic job! Not only did she explain to me how certain hairstyles would work for my hair texture, she even took the time explaining how to style my hair with the new cut. On top of all of that, Cameron was incredibly personable and we talked the entire time. She made me feel comfortable right away. It was an amazing experience and I absolutely loved the haircut I walked out with. Highly recommend Cameron and this salon because they were so professional and easy to work with.

Love this little hidden gem. Local little "upscale" dive bar owned and operated by the kindest of individuals. Live bands on weekends, catered Sunday football viewing parties. And the drinks are so affordable. You have to go visit Jamie and Patti, so sweet and always attentive to your needs - tell them Diana sent you ;)

Came to NOLA for a conference and stumbled in to the Howling Wolf. Friendly Staff (ask for Erica...she's the best) with an excellent selection of craft beers. This is definitely a place that I will visit again. The Howling Wolf has subdued lighting and an overall laid back jazy New Orleans feeling. A must visit.

Ordered from here while at work and I wanted to try something new. Whew! This food was so delicious, those onion rings are to DIE for, my coworker literally kept my receipt after I shared my onion rings with her, and she immediately started telling others about it at her second job!! Well done Bareburger. Next time I'll come sit in rather than having it delivered.
Awesome place, love the southwest chicken, add some spot sauce to it and it's perfect

Beautiful indoor/outdoor café. Had the privilege of sitting on the second tier above the restaurant. We had a sight of Bourbon Street and the sweet soulful sounds of classic jazz.  Their beignets are better then the popular touristy competitor. This place is an oasis and adds charm to the notorious Bourbon Street. Sadly,the shrimp po boy was a let down. It was obviously not fresh, and better shrimp can be found at a local Popeyes.

Okay so I subleased May-July 2017. It started as $450 but they told us it wasn't available to renew at this price because they were renovating the whole apartment to they're most premium package so it would jump to $650... which isn't necessarily an issue here although I wish it could've been communicated a little bit better however Micah did her best clarify a lot for me which was really nice. I would consider living here again.
Hands down worst service of any restaurant I've been to in STL. Food was decent, but service was enough to never return.

Fabulous Salon! It is very warm and inviting  and all the girls are just fabulous. Connie is truly an amazing stylist who is a miracle worker! I got baylage and cut and have never been more happier with my hair. If you want to feel like the most beautiful girl in the world go see Connie.

Fantastic burgers. Was very impressed with the awesomeness they give the classic burger. As well, got the tater tot fondue for appetizer and it was heavenly. Definitely will be visiting again!! Great atmosphere and good food.

My review will be a tad bit one sided because my first visit was on a whim for the turducken croissant specialty. However, I will be returning for more treats. 

Beautiful shop. The decor and the display cases are all arranged with loving care and definitely bump up the atmosphere to a sophisticated level. 

My fellow foodies and I stood outside in the cold anticipating the open sign and did our best not to drool once the door opened. The smell wafting through the air is enough to cause a riot but we all behaved ourselves and queued up for the turducken experience. Standing in line taunted us all with the other glorious treats, sweet and savory, which were on display, but I resisted. 
The staff was so friendly and helpful and quickly moved through the crowd which had gathered. 

The turducken croissant.  Okay I know sometimes you wait in line for a "specialty" because it is part of the experience and try not to be let down on the actual item. The turducken croissant is special. A perfectly soft and flaky croissant stuffed with a turkey/duck/dressing/cranberry mixture you can dip in a side of gravy. Dear lord it was decadent. I will be back next year.

We came here for a quick brunch before heading back to Chicago. It has a very chill vibe, and filled with southern hipsters. We came for breakfast and got the Eskimo sister and the vieja tacos, and Mexican mochas. The food and drinks were excellent! Love the fresh foods, mixture of different flavors like jalapeño cilantro hummus and goat cheese. Sorry we do not live here to come more often. Will definitely come again when back in Nashville!

I went here for my boyfriend's birthday and our further anniversaries. I do not regret a thing at all! Although we had reservations, we still had to wait a couple of minutes. The servers are super kind and I always feel bad for them when they have to sing happy birthday songs or do that one dance routine when a certain song plays because they look soooo tired. Anyways, we ordered the raspberry lemonade and oh so gooddd! We got the boneless wings as an appetizer and we did get the sampler with a few of the other appetizers as well. We did not like those cheesy potatoes at all. The cheese was too thick and had turned to stone when it came to us. The jalapeno poppers are hooootttt but soo gooooddd. I forgot to mention the AMAZING bread rolls!!! Take advantage of it while you can!  The steaks were perfectly cooked and tasted wonderful. The green beans side tastes watery and not worth it unless you dump it in your mashed potatoes like I did. Nonetheless, will come back again!!
Same great Kung Pao with attentive service in a pleasant, upscale but casual atmosphere.
Not sure what the negative reviews are about. The ambiance and view are amazing, service is fantastic and food is delicious!

What a great find! Happened on this place while visiting Tampa because we figured there would be good eats near a mall, and my son wanted Mexican. I'm not a big fan of the usual Americanized fare, but reluctantly agreed to try this rather than its better known neighbors. All I can say is that everything was perfect! The food was fresh and delicious and prepared beautifully. The table-side guac is prepared to your taste. Our server Andrea helped us with our choices and was attentive throughout the meal. Manager Andres checked on us and gave us a quick history of the place. As we left we told strangers walking past how good it was and convinced them to try it... It's not in my hometown so I don't have to keep it a secret!

Sunday morning we were treated to a post wedding brunch at Herbie's.  We arrived right at 10 and were quickly ushered into the reserved room.

The first thing I noticed about Herbie's was the vibe of the interior.  Pretty cool old wrap around bar that looked pretty nice.  It looked like a pretty cool place to grab a drink and it looked like they had some good beers on tap...but I digress.

The area that was reserved was very nice and accommodated our group perfectly.  

I went with the cast iron fritata which was great.  It was loaded with ham, onions, Cheddar cheese and roasted red peppers.  It also came with potatoes and toast.  It was a great dish.

However, my better half got the morning flat bread and it was amazing.  Eggs, cheese, spinach and tomatoes covered the flatbread from edge to edge.  Really awesome.

All in all, it was a great experience.  They were a little light on the wait staff but not horrible.

We were visiting IN from IL. My wife & daughter are vegan but I'm not. I tried their County Style dish with a lemonade. A great meal. Very pleasant staff. Awesome energy & experience. If we're ever back in IN we will make it a point to add Three Carrots to our agenda.

I'd like to add many more stars to my rating.

This is my ABSOLUTE FAVORITE wine bar in St Louis City OR county!!!
There's nothing else that comes close to the charm and atmosphere of this fabulous find in South City.  The building is over 100 years old.

Djiana, the owner, is very knowledgable about wines and foods and can always recommend a wine that suits both my husband and I. She's never been wrong.

The Balkan Platter and Stuffed Dates are my favorite appetizers as well as all of the Flatbreads. 
Djiana is always creating new appetizers and foods that immediately become a hit with her customers.

We happen to stumble in here after our long night on our last night visiting New Orleans , this was for the memorial day wknd.
were able to relax watch the drunken people ride the bull & just have a lil more fun before calling it a night.
Another decent place on bourbon street to chill in , a lil different cause of the bull u can certainly enjoy yourself here.

Just went there and it was frustrating, a staff full of cuban old ladies thinking the store is theirs, they priced checked two items i had with price tags!!  -making me think im a thief or something SMH!

I've definitely had better Tapas. I went with a group of 3 and we tried about 10 dishes. The mussels were served cold (which they did warn you about), but this seemed to result in a complete loss of flavor. The lamb skewers were excellent, but everything else was rather bland. Combine this with so-so service and it was an overall mediocre experience.

This is not the best Chinese food around as a matter of fact the best around is only one block away but I give this awesome place 5 stars anyway. Why you ask? Well I'll tell you the best around is pick up only and is cash only. When I have that magic double formula at my disposal I go straight to number 5 (locals will know) however when that criteria is not met, when I need delivery or I need to use a credit card I need a place that is up to the task of serving awesome Chinese food. Enter Pearl of the East. Its been my standby for years but a car smashed through the window a couple years ago and I forgot all about this place. Well I ordered tonight. Its as good as I remember and as I type this I'm thinking I might even like the garlic sauce better then number 5. Add the fact that they were not cheap with a random assortment of sauce packets and gave a whopping 8 fortune cookies with my order (which included a free quart of won ton soup for meeting a certain dollar spent threshhold). I am glad they are back and I will most certainly return and recommend them although I may not be totally ready to break up with number 5

The food is always hot and enjoyable to eat. Delivery is on point. Only things you have to order $15 dollars for them to order the food to you. but most likely you will enjoy the food my favorite is general tso and plain fried rice.

We love the Peppermill.   I can't say we have made any money while I can say we drank it all and then some!   The service here while you play is outstanding.   If your into gambling you will not be disappointed!

I've been coming here for about four years and in that time have acquired two pairs of jeans, a T-shirt, and a bandana.  I am highly impressed with the denim, in particular.  It wears well, holds its shape, and has thoughtful design details (such as the inside edge of the fly being trimmed and tacked down so it doesn't make a weird bunched up mess you have to remember to fix every time you zip your pants).  The staff has been on point in recommending the right denim to me after asking what my needs were.  As others have said, it's feast or famine when you come in: either the staff will be your BFFs or you will feel invisible.  I don't take that kind of stuff personally and don't care to analyze whether it's intentional vs not caring enough to do the job well.  All to say, if you need some help you aren't getting, ask and you will receive.  On inventory issues:  Sometimes it's frustrating when the perfect pair is sold out for months, but given that this is a startup, I guess it's to be expected.  They have some great flash sales, so sign up for their emails.  Another great way to save if their retail price point is too high is to look in consignment stores around Nashville.  I always see a few pairs of I+W when I'm thrifting.

3.5 stars. First the good news: the food here is amazing. Succulent pork, flavorful bisque, to-die-for jalapeño grits. John Besh knows his flavor profiles. But really, everything else about the restaurant was downhill from there. The oysters were tasty, but inadequately shucked. We had TWO servers, but still felt like we weren't paid adequate attention to. Getting our drinks, placing our order, and trying to pay took longer than we liked. The ambiance is confusing.  Are you fine dining? Or a bar? Or an Applebee's? Why are there newspapers hanging down as dividers between the tables? Some couples were dressed up for dinner - jackets, dresses, and heels. Others had shorts and flip flops. And then there were the fellas at the bar with Tshirts and hunting camo baseball caps on. Maybe it's b/c the restaurant is attached to a hotel? The hostess at the door had this really loud, piercing laugh that she unleashed more than once during our meal.

Food this good shouldn't be taken as carry out - unfortunately, that is the only way we can see ourselves eating it again.

We had a wonderful wedding rehearsal dinner in the banquet room (It is a great space separate from the restaurant and BYOB) for about 75 people. Mario set the room up perfectly for the "Taste of Philly" buffet and the service was exceptional.  Now for the non-stop food -- Philly Cheesesteak, pizza, ziti, hoagies, veal parmigiana, salad and mini cannoli -- All fantastic. Everyone commented on how they truly enjoyed the evening and especially the food.  Thank you Mario for far exceeding our expectations and creating a very memorable night for our family, friends and the lovely couple.

I ordered a spaghetti with meatballs platter and it was so bland that it reminded me of hospital food. Sauce was brown, not red. Meatballs were frozen style. Just very bad for the price. So disappointing.

Nice spot.  Not too crowded at lunch time.  Got the chicken tinga tacos with red spicy sauce.  Pretty solid tacos.  Would like to see an expanded menu with grilled chicken and steak as choices of protein.
Service was excellent and food was authentic as you can get!! Lived in Thailand for 4 months and this food was just as good as you can get there!! Highly recommend!!!

Love, love, LOVE their pizza! Best crust ever and nice employees. I am always satisfied - I tried Doughocracy last night and I regret that. Service and friendly employees go a long way! So does quality pizza. :)
I love this blimpie ! Staff is always friendly and they all make a damn good sandwich! Theres a blimpie closer to where I live but I drive the few extra miles to go here!

I liked Fired Up BBQ just ok. Don't get me wrong; I'm a carnivore. I love me my meat. But I just can't seem to get into southern barbeque. I think it's the kind of bbq sauce? I haven't given up yet though!

I think my experience with this place might also be skewed due to arriving about half an hour before closing, so there was less variety for the meats and sides. None of the sides we tried were outstanding (mac and cheese, spanish rice, southwestern corn, potato salad). For meats we had ribs and brisket. Huge portions so decent bang for your buck. The ribs were tender and falling of the bone (unfortunately I like my ribs to have a little bit of chew) with a smoky sauce, which was ok but not for me. The brisket was excellent, with a good balance of fat and meat, cooked so that it shredded easily under my fork. They don't have fried chicken which kind of surprised me - isn't that a hallmark of southern food? I could be wrong.

The place is kind of in a strange location, and it's got more of a fast food feel to it rather than sit-down restaurant, by virtue of ordering at the front, getting a plastic tray, and having the meats and sides ready-made behind the counter. Overall, if you're in the area or love barbeque, it's probably worth checking out, but for me, once was enough.

Amazing atmosphere. The friendliest staff I've seen by far. All are willing to help. The team work is amazing! The food is delicious! A bit pricey, but you get what you pay for. :) Love coming here when I'm craving seafood and lazy to cook.

Came here for lunch this afternoon..  We started with the house-smoked salmon, which was delightful.  Dining companion had the short rib sandwich with horseradish cream and watercress.  She definitely won the entree contest.  The horseradish was the perfect balance to the rich short rib, watercress was fresh and crunchy, bread was,if not fresh baked, delivered from someone who knows what they're doing.  Served with purple potato chips and house-made pickle (which was also awesome.

I had the skirt steak with ratatouille and semolina cake.  Can't remember the description of the dish perfectly now, but I assume they must have said something about sauce.  Sauce.  So much sauce.  I'm sure it wasn't just straight up A-1 or whatever, but it wasn't much of an improvement on that sort of generic steak-sauce-y taste.  And there was way too much of it.  

On the plus side.. this is a new place.  Apparently the lunch menu just started next week or something.  If the short rib sandwich is any indication, there's definitely some potential here.  The bar menu is also supposed to start soon, and there were a few dishes there that sound like they'll be contenders.  Crispy maitake mushrooms in particular...  Also, service was good, bartender was informed about the menu and attentive.

Great service and great tacos. Family ran jumpoff!
Got tacos, tortas, chips, burritos, queso. Was a huge take out order. Went smooth!
Sweet potato pancakes are my favorite! Service is always friendly. So many options of pancakes to choose from!

Chatham Tap is perfect for any occasion. The laid back atmosphere is comfortable for a working lunch, happy hour or dinner out. Stopped by today with a group of 5 and had awesome service and a delicious Southwest Cesar Salad, can't wait to get back and have it again!

WORST SERVICE EVER. and i mean ever. 

After someone took my food by accident, I asked them to make another one for me (and I waited ANOTHER 5 minutes). They misunderstood and didn't add chicken to the pizza I ordered. So the employee rolled his eyes at me and gave me this look. 
So after 15 minutes of waiting...I got my food.

I have never been treated this way at ANY fast food place even. No one apologized. 

Now I go out of my way NOT to go to Cosi. They don't care about their customers. They just make the money. But hey...students need food...so they go to Cosi.

Is it too much to ask for employees to be respectful?

My all time favorite brunch place! The food is always outstanding and the service can't be beat. I've been here at all hours of the day, and night, and I've never had a bad visit. I've even been in with a rather large group for a birthday brunch and they were wonderful. I don't eat meat but I can say that my carnivorous friends are always happy as well.

Steamboats are legendary as are the Dukes of Dixieland, and on the Natchez river cruises, you get to enjoy both!  The Dukes have been famous for over 50 years with their traditional dixieland jazz music.  And steamboats were at the heart of the growth of our nation through the 19th century.  If you are in New Orleans in the Summer, I recommend the evening dinner cruise.  If it is any other season, the afternoon lunch cruise would be better due to the loss of sunlight in the evening.  (You would end up photographing white pin-pricks from scattered lights in a sea of darkness.)  On the other hand, the Dukes of Dixieland play on every cruise, so you can't go wrong no matter which cruise you choose.  The meals are served buffet-style, and it is "all you can eat".  The extra 10 or 12  bucks for lunch is definitely worthwhile.  The most popular item for "seconds" (and "thirds") was the bread pudding with bourbon sauce.  An extra $25 for dinner?  I dunno ... the food is good, but not great.  A lunch cruise is the best value IMHO, but a sunset cruise with the city lights just turning on is a photographer's dream ("golden time").

I hadn't been here in a few years, but really used to enjoy their crispy  thin crust pizza.  So, I ordered one to go last night. Got it home and it was so soggy that you literally needed a spoon to eat it. So much for their crispy, thin crust and the toppings were very sparse.
   I ended up throwing it away... waste of $20.  .

I had eaten once at Blake's in New Mexico and it was pretty good so I was excited when the Tucson location opened. Severely disappointed. I was there on a recent Saturday in the drive though and waited not only for at least 10 minutes for the one car ahead of me to receive what looked like just a sauce packet, but personally for my own food for about 10 minutes. No one even came to the window until they collected my money and handed me the subpar chile cheeseburger combo. The burger was drenched in mustard and the patty tasted fresh off the hockey rink. It was semi cold and soggy rendering anything possibly positive, the cheese and the chilis, just a mess. The fries were ok, nothing special, and nothing about this experience would ever make me want to come back. I should have left while waiting forever in the drive-through as I contemplated multiple times.

I am a guy who has almost no experience with yoga. A friend told me about a special "guy's night" event that Green Locus was having in support of men's health issues. The price sounded reasonable and the special event came with a voucher for a beer at the World of Beer next door! 
The studio is tucked away on the second level of a very clean and safe commercial plaza located in the Westchase residential area. Depending on when you come, it might take a few more minutes than usual to find a parking spot, but even the overflow parking is a short walk to the studio.
Once arriving at the studio, I found a a few people waiting in the reception area where a friendly employee was quick to greet me and have me sign in for the class. There were drinks and equipment available for purchase, but nothing was pushed on me for a sale.
Since I'm inexperienced with yoga, I was hoping that I wouldn't feel overwhelmed. The yoga instructor was very welcoming and questioned our group about our level of experience. For almost every exercise she demonstrated, she offered alternative methods to perform the exercise to suit the student's abilities. I never felt overwhelmed, but I was definitely challenged! I did know that yoga could be such a workout! Fortunately, the class I attended balanced the exhausting workout with a very relaxing, meditative cool down.
The instructor definitely opened my eyes to the benefits of yoga and I look forward to returning!

I truly do not think it will ever get old going to the Children's Museum. I have always enjoyed this place when I get to go. We went when I was younger for field trips, and having lived up north, the long 2+ hours on a bus was worth it the minute we got there! And as an adult, I love going just the same to see everything they have displayed or attractions being featured since both are usually always a promised good time for kids and adults alike! Since I do not have children, I get invited to go with friends who do have children or family (I am a big kid at times when in places like this or maybe even the zoo, it's all about fun and good times!) There is truly something for everyone there and no matter what age you are, it's always worth at least one trip in the summer or spring!

This very good supermarket in Lower Makefield lies in the supermarket hiearchy immediately above the band containing Giant, Acme, Superfresh, Genuardis and Stop and Shop but below the premium top line of Whole Foods, Wegmans and Whole Earth (all in the Princeton and Philadelphia areas).

So if you live in the Yardley/Makefields area and you dont want to drive 20 minutes for your groceries, this is as good as it gets. 

The poultry and meat sections contain organic and minimally process selections. The fish counter offerings are clearly labeled and almost always have wild-caught options.  The bakery is good and usually has samples for the kids (and adults).  

If you are watching your budget, you can do what many people do (myself included): go to the Giant in the next-door lot for the packaged, non-perishable items and then go to Mccaffrey's for the meat, fish, produce and items you cant get at Giant (such as specialty condiments). 

Unlike most other grocery stores, this store's hot bar and salad bar are very good. The lunch room upstairs has plenty of tables and overlooks the store.

My few gripes: 
1. The produce guys act like undertakers and seem unaware that putting multiple stocking carts in the narrow produce aisles is a HUGE &^*@ing obstacle for us shoppers. I especially hate it when they have one barge in front of the parsely/lettuce section and another by the avocados/garlic area, which makes getting something from the area in between impossible.

2. The dimwit and preppy teens who work here are the worst baggers and tellers. The alterna-teens who work at Giant are much better (but still cannot bag well)  There are errors on about 25% of my checkouts.

3. Why oh why did they change the bakery bread selections? And why cant they ever stock a good, crusty, large semolina flatloaf?

Nice cozy Mexican restaurant with food which tastes great always goes for a 5-star rating for me.. The hosts were really friendly and patient.. The food tastes awesome.. My personal favorite would be the tortas and tazan... Keep up the good work guys!!!!

This place is no-frills, cash-only, and does not mess around with portion sizes. I got a small pho with beef balls, rare beef, tripe, and other meats (#1), some hot tea, and some fried egg rolls with a friend of mine. We each had PLENTY of leftovers and each paid less than 10 bucks. Broth was tasty and there was tons of meat in it for the price. I have been here several times and plan on coming back. Not sure if it's my favorite of the Vietnamese places in town, but I'm also not sure I can pick a favorite.

I would have given 1 star, but the room (in the Tuscany tower) was very nice and the woman on the phone for room service was super nice. 

There were two problems during our 12-hour stay at the Peppermill which will keep me from ever going back.

First, we got in late (about 11pm), and after we finally got to the room, we were starving and looking for room service. There was no menu in the room, but room service said that they would send housekeeping up with one. 4 calls (to room service, the front desk, and housekeeping) and a full hour later, and extremely surly housekeeping lady dropped one off. WTF? I would have walked somewhere to get it myself if I'd known I was going to put her off so much. I think we got put on the s*** list by housekeeping, because before 8:30 the next morning (we were only there for one night), housekeeping woke us up to ask if they could clean the room. Never in my life has a hotel asked to clean the room the morning I'm checking out. Were they going to clean it and then clean it again after we left? Obviously not. Seemed instead like a little petty revenge for having to repeatedly request the damn menu.

Second, since I was awake, I asked the front desk if we could have a late checkout (at noon instead of 11) but was told that they didn't have any. It was a weekday, and not very crowded at all, so I'm not sure how that could possibly be the case. We timely checked out on the tv by 11, but It took us almost until 12 before we were out of the room, anyway, and no one came by to clean or anything, so not extending us the courtesy really made no difference whatsoever save to piss me off.

All in all, an unfortunately poor level of customer service that I will remember next time I find myself in Reno.

Miserable.   Server was painfully slow.   We asked for a sugared rim,  got a salted one.   Chicken enchiladas were overdone and crunchy.   Salsa is too smokey.   
Definitely not coming back.   
Still looking for a good Mexican restaurant.

Normally, it would take something akin to a plague to get me to make the trek to a county chain restaurant attached to a mall for a bite to eat. So, I'll man up and just say it - I really like J Gilberts.

I'll start with two pluses. The ambiance is pretty cool. Very dark and classy enough without being too formal. The fire wall is my favorite amenity. Adding to the ambiance is the service. I have always had outstanding, attentive service in both the bar and restaurant. It's always a plus when your server can discuss suggestions with you and give you informative feedback.

I have been to J Gilberts twice so far - once for dinner and once for happy hour.

DINNER:
It is true what other reviewers say. J Gilberts offers excellent value for the price. This is because, with many entrées, you get to choose two sides at no additional cost. They have about 10 sides to choose from, making it easy to get a potato and veggie for a well-rounded meal. I tried the 6 oz filet mignon, medium, with pablano au gratin potatoes and grilled asparagus. Everything was done to perfection. At $29 for all of that, it was a steal. We happened to be dining on a Sunday evening and also benefited from their Sunday wine special, where all bottles under $100 are 1/2 price. Dinner was a wonderful experience.

HAPPY HOUR:
Happy hour, although not cheap in general, is a good deal to try discounted J Gilberts items and does last 4-7 pm Mon-Fri. They offer a variety of appetizers, many of which are seafood (which I don't care for). My favorite was the filet sliders. Two tenderloin sliders with watercress, shallot jam, and blue cheese, accompanied by house-made chips. At $7 (down from $9.50), you can easily make a meal out of these.

The shining star of happy hour was their cocktails, though. They have some very unique and intriguing mixed drinks to try, so I skipped wine, and tried a few at the $6 happy hour price. My ultimate favorite was the lemon, basil manhattan. Tart, smooth and delicious - especially on a hot summer day. I also tried the French 75, which was served in an adorable champagne glass and certainly packed a punch.

Parking can be a bitch but, all in all, I'd recommend that you give J Gilberts a try. For all those city dwellers, it's worth the trip. You may be surprised that you'll be willing to make repeat visits to enjoy what this place has to offer.

Ordered delivery for lunch at work since I was starving, but not crazy enough to go out in this afwul heat and humidity. The food arrived in about 20-25 minutes so that was a great plus. Though, he didn't bring the food into the building and I had to meet him outside (ugh... that heat). Not a plus, but not at all the delivery guy's fault.

I ordered the Chicken Tikka Masala with basmati rice and the gulab jamun for dessert. The chicken was well-cooked, tender, and probably had decent flavor. I say "probably", because the whole thing was so incredibly watery. I think they didn't use any yogurt or corn starch. Still, not the worst I've had (that prize goes to Nanee's Kitchen at Reading Terminal). The chicken wasn't really that bad and I still had dessert to look forward to. Nope. Instead of the sweet, spongey goodness usually associated with gulab jamun, it was hard and a little gritty.

I could overlook the quality of the food if it was at least cheap, but it's not really that much cheaper than other places.

Definitely not a place to introduce someone to Indian cuisine if they've never had.

This is a review for the bakery. I have been ordering my kids birthday cakes from here for the past 2 years and Tonya is simply amazing at creating beautiful and delicious cakes! At every party I hear tons of compliments and comments about the taste and design of the cake. This grocery store is not super close to my house but I will continue to order my birthday cakes from here. Thank you Tonya for all your hard work!
Spicy crab soup was good, clam strips had a perfect crunchiness to them. Crab cakes as good as you want them to be.

While most of the reviews were good, I had almost the EXACT same unsatisfactory experience described by another yelper. With only 5 other people at the restaurant, aside from our party of 4, the food took an hour + to arrive, and our order only consisted of eggs, English muffins, and a bagel. After 45 minutes of waiting the staff told us that they were out of cream cheese, but would be delivered within the next 15 minutes. No thanks. Finally.... 3 of our 4 orders came out. Lukewarm. We were told the 4th order of a poached egg burned (?!) and would need to be redone. 10 minutes later...the poached egg arrived. After recommending to some passerby's that they consider an alternative place to eat if they are hungry, the cook came out to apologize for our wait and offered a smoothie, on the house. While it was a nice gesture, we didn't want to wait another 45 minutes.

I saw that the hours had been expanded so decided to stop in one afternoon. They've done a really great job remodeling the space; there's tons of seating and the decor is really cute. However, for the quality of the food, the price was really steep. 

The cheese fundido w/ chorizo was probably the best thing we ordered, it was gooey and had lots of veggies; but it was not worth $10. 

I also have a hard time paying $4/$5 dollars for a single taco unless they are just great... and these were not. Although the tacos were hefty and filled well, the lack of salt and lack of salsa selection left me unsatisfied. Just not worth $5. My boyfriend was also very underwhelmed with his selection of tacos, although he mentioned he liked the Idaho taco the best. 

They did have a good local beer selection. you could tell the tortillas were fresh, and the workers at the counter were really nice.

Bottom line: If you're going to gentrify tacos, they need to have a lot more flavor. This place has lots of potential, but the college crowd who lives in the area will not be interested in paying $15 for a set of bland tacos.

I agree with Jay I.   I have been to the Phily Diner several times with friends who live in the area and once by myself for an early breakfast.  The food was always mediocre, re-heated things straight off the Sysco truck.  That could be expected, but Jersey diners get such a good rep for high-volume, quality food that my expectations were higher.

The exterior of the place is clean and inviting, and the interior seems very clean.  Aside from the mediocre food, the worst part of the Phily Diner experience is the slow, rude service.  The staff are all glued to television monitors which were showing mindless 'reality' shows when I was there.  Even what should have been a quick, simple breakfast at the counter early one morning, when it was not crowded at all, took 45 minutes.

The prices are high for the quality of food and service.

Part of the diner is the Phil Diner Sports Bar - a strange concept.  It's a wannabe sports bar that is part of the diner.  Same rude service, but in the bar you are subjected to the inane behavior of the patrons. Who goes to a diner to drink and hang out?  Adolescents in their mid-20s was my experience.  Angry losers mad at the world but not willing to do or say anything constructive.  Wait, is this review falling into that category? Well, I am not angry, and I will do something constructive - I will drive past the Phily Diner next time and save myself some, time, money and peace of mind.

Enjoy!

Housekeeping prevents another star. Admittedly, the other reviews are spot on but one would thing the hotel has gotten the memo and talked to the housekeepers. 

I stayed here a few nights during my last visit. I received a room that faced St. Joseph which is directly across the street from a popular night spot. I agree with one reviewer that says you need to be passed out to get a good night's rest. There is no way to sleep through the loud music that blasts on weekends until at least 6am. Geez!  To makes this worse, housekeeping knocked on my door at 8:30a on a Saturday. Really!!? I mean this is a late night city, in the heart of downtown. 8:30a? C'mon!! I told them to go away. At 10am, I received another knock. I answered and the housekeeper asked if I was ready for the room to be cleaned? I said no and she went away. 

Fast forward to another day, when I put the do not disturb sign outside. They did not knock but when I did leave the room at 12p and tool it off, I should have known that the housekeeper would not clean the room even though a cleaner was a few rooms down cleaning someone else's room. What is sad is I returned to the room and there was voicemail left a 2:30p from another hotel room saying your room was not cleaned because of the do not disturb sign. What sign? Just say you did not want to clean the room. 

The hotel rooms are really nice, very clean and are equipped with a microwave and refrigerator. The free breakfast was really nice, It included fruit, cereal, yogurt, juice, coffee and a few hot items. 

I would stay here again but the housekeeping needs retraining. It is unclear why they should continue to derail the experience of most guests.

Loved it. Had the roasted cauliflower,  ricotta gnocchi , and beef cheek. Amazing!  Each was better than the previous. For dessert,  the chocolate tarte. I wanted to take the dish home so I could keep licking it.

The place is sloppy.  A woman sits on a high stool and watches two servers walk their legs off to a room full of customers.  The food was ok. The price was ok but the service is terrible.  The table was wiped off and then left swimming in goo.  When we asked for to-go containers the woman on the stool said, " You already have two".

If you get it to go.  Then I guess you could say it's about a three star.

Terrible experience. Came for lunch on 2/12. Arrived at 12:30. Sat on the patio. Sat at about the same time as two other tables. Sat for about 5 minutes with the last party's dirty dishes on the table. Waitress finally removed the dirty dishes and brought two waters. Didn't come back for another 10 to 15 minutes to take our lunch order. Ordered the pretzel, Buffalo chicken sandwich and peel and eat shrimp (two of us). We now waited for about 15 minutes for the pretzel. An appetizer, waiting 15 minutes (and all it is was a frozen pretzel, not that hard). After receiving the pretzel and finishing it, waited another 20 minutes for our food. 20 minutes for a sandwich and a few shrimp (which literally requires placing them on a plate). About 4 tables that were sat around us at the same time or AFTER we did received their food before we did. I stopped the waitress who kept just walking by and asked what was taking so long. She so stupidly said, "I'll go check, not sure what's taking so long." Food still didn't come out for another 10 minutes. Peel and eat shrimp were fine. (They weren't for me). Chicken sandwich was disgusting. So much grease, it poured in my mouth the first (and only) bite. The batter was undercooked and just falling off the chicken. It was as if it was battered too much and just soaked in under temperature oil. Asked the waitress to send over the manager. This is a key point here. The manager acted dumber than the waitress. Literally seemed extremely unintelligent. Stuttering and mumbling, uhhh, ummm, not really sure. At one point he actually said, "uhhh, well it is a fried chicken sandwich." I mean really. This is your manager? This is your best guy on the floor? Shameful. After mumbling he said, "I'll take care of this for you" and walked away. Never to return. We sat there like idiots for the next 10 minutes without  the waitress or manager telling us we didn't have to pay. This was the worst restaurant experience I've had in recent memory. I will not return and I will not recommend anyone go here.

Chase's is a great hole in the wall. Very small menu, but everything is done correctly... especially the fries. The beer selection is excellent. Also, great selection of games to play while enjoying some adult beverages. No frills type of perfection.

This place is good, relatively cheap, unpretentious, and walking-distance from my apartment, so I visit pretty often. When we have guests from out of town this is usually one of the first restaurants we take them to. Recently we had a group of six or seven friends visit from San Francisco and we took them here the first night, and for the rest of the time they stayed with us they kept asking to go back!

Here are some of my favorite things from the menu:
1. Sweet potato and Andouille sausage hash (SERIOUSLY, you have to try this)
2. Curried edamame hummus
3. Lamb sliders
4. Baked summer squash and tomatoes in pesto

These are just the things I MUST order every time I'm there. Everything I've tried there has been good with only one exception (the baked goat cheese in tomato sauce needs some work). 

I have a couple of complaints, but I'm giving this place five stars to help boost its overall rating and make up for some of the stuffy, weirdly self-important reviews on here.
 
So, be warned about the following:
1. Consistently flaky hostess
2. That one hilariously stoned waiter who gets confused easily, but has still never gotten an order wrong
3. Inconsistent drinks. Sometimes watery, sometimes too sweet, sometimes awesome

Overall I love this place. They don't get everything right, but somehow I find their few shortcomings to be charming, especially after a couple of drinks. As a bonus, they handle large groups pretty well, which is great.
Had a great time at BR! Our server Reyna? was really nice and attentive. The salad with the grapes and pumpkin seeds was yummy. Good sized drinks for cheap, lovely patio.

This is my sports go-to. Being the partner of a - gasp - NY sports fan, we are constantly looking for those few Philly bars with Sunday Ticket or MLB Extra Innings. For the sake of the relationship. Well, Smith's doesn't disappoint. Rarely a problem finding a seat at the bar. Always with the drink specials during games. 

The food is usually very good. Above average bar food I would say. Love the boneless wings, love the pizzas, and even have been know to get adventurous on occasion with the fish tacos. I have been disappointed a few times but nothing consistent. Hit or miss specials during games.

Tons of TVs. Including the sneaky back room with the comfy chairs and dart board. I have watched a movie in this room, I hate to admit.

Me and a couple friends decided to venture north from our homes in Salt Lake City to see what awesome beer the good people of Idaho have to offer. We planned ahead and called a few breweries to see if we could get a tour and Mark at Sockeye responded!

You can tell these folks care about their craft. Spending time with four beer nerds from Utah was something they didn't have to do, but they did. And after the amazing tour of their facility, we grabbed some food in the restaurant. All of it was truly awesome. When we first walked into Sockeye it was clear they care about their craft. The employees and staff were friendly and every single one of them was super knowledgeable. 

I'd recommend their sour porter beer as well as the Sockeye IPA. Although, you can't really go wrong with any of their beer! Grab a sampler tray to try them all! 

Can't wait to go back. You rule, Sockeye!

Love. Love. Love this place.  No longer a secret in the middle of Kenner. This place has fresh, hot and amazingly delicious donuts with so many choices 24/7, not to mention awesome regular foods. The little Kastle burgers are the BOMB.  I mean where can you get smothered turkey necks, hot donuts and mini burgers.  YUMMMMMMM:)

Came here for my moms birthday. The staff bent over backwards to make sure we were comfortable and that we had everything we needed. The prices are reasonable and the food is absolutely delicious. We couldn't ask for better service or a better place to have a birthday dinner. Can't wait to come back!!

(November 17) I have been to Wings over Broadway a couple times. Recently, I have been dying to get back out to them and gorge on their wings. In my opinion, best wings there is in Tucson, although I haven't tried every wing place. Overall, the service is good, not excellent but just good. As much as I love this small community restaurant, I always get sick after eating there. It's not just sick and feeling off with a stomach ache, it is completely sick with food poisoning for a few days to a week long, sick. Although I love the food, I will not be returning due to getting sick all four times that I have been there. I don't know if it's just me, or if there are others who have got sick? Three stars because I loved this place and food is great, but I couldn't get over that I got food poisoning more then once here. It's very disappointing.
Great food! The red curry was excellent. Very large helpings for an affordable price.

I honestly don't think this yelp review will do this amazing meal justice but I will try!

We were visiting Philly on a Saturday night and pulled up Yelp to find a good italian spot. This place exceeded every expectation we had!

First, its BYOB (doesn't exist in VA) so we were already pumped and prepared with two bottles of red wine. We pulled up in an uber to this "off the beaten path" cute little restaurant close to 9pm. We were one of 3 tables and ended up closing the place down. 

They start you off with fresh hot peppers (spicy!) and fresh baked bread. 
I ordered the Amatricianna with the spicy sauce and my boy got the veal saltimboca. I literally cannot express how delicious both dishes were. 
We definitely would have ordered dessert - but I really wanted the Tiramisu - which wasn't a speical that evening. 

Did I mention all this great food cost only $42 bucks! We will definitely be back next time we are in Philly (basically planning a trip back just to eat here).

These are some pretty awesome mechanics. How often do you bring a car to get worked on and the mechanics tell you some of the things you asked them to do really aren't needed.

That never happens. You usually go some place and they come up with all sorts of mind spinning reasons to charge you more. NOT THIS PLACE.

They replaced my brakes, trans fluid, oil change and timing belts and took a look at the three or for other things I'd asked them to do, realized it the car really didn't need it done and didn't charge me a dime for the stuff that wasn't replaced even though they took the time to look into it.

Great, honest mechanics. A rare find.

I really enjoy going to see Shannon to have my nails done.  She does a great job and my nails always look great.  I used to just get the regular manicure, but recently decided to get the shellac manicure and was so glad I did.  A little extra cash, but I could do just about anything and my nails still look great for almost three weeks.  I am not very good to my hands and usually ruin nails quickly, so the fact that they still looked great after two and half weeks was super.  A co-worker even commented on them, so that made me feel happy.

We were here on a busy Saturday night so that could be why our experience was so sub-par. The service was slow, and the waitress got one of our orders wrong. We had to wait for cutlery when our food had been served and the food was just meh. And it was overpriced to boot.

They have excellent service. Lovely cashiers. Although, they do not dog ice cream. I took my dog in and they didn't even let her on with me. I took her through the drive thru and I asked for their best dog ice cream and they started being really rude. 0/10 IGN would not recommend no quick scoops.

Don't let the 3 stars fool you. This is a nice place to eat. The decor is that of any typical diner. The staff was so friendly and always checking in with you- it truly was the best service I have had in God knows how long. The salmon and chips were good, nice size pieces of fish and comes with 3 sides. I would definitely recommend this place if you are at the airport or need a place to eat in the area. Very affordable.

Had the grits with bacon and was perfect! Great outdoor seating in a cool section of Indianapolis. This spot came highly recommended and didn't disappoint. Also had a mocha which was excellent and unlike others not too sweet.
Mmmmm wings tasty morsels of deliciousness and the cheese & brown gravy fries extremely tasty, great prices friendly staff and a blast from the past family diner.

Food is really good BUT OVERPRICED!!
Ordered 4burgers w drinks...my bill w/tip
Was over $100.00?  Really $100.00 for 
4 burgers w drinks???Wow next time 
will go to burger shack just down 
the street!!
Steve

I normally don't really care for fast food type chains but tagged along with my bf and his friend for a quick lunch here one day. They ordered burritos and I made my own steak quesadilla. 

The burritos were massive. I had no complaints on my quesadilla. I liked that there were four different types of tortilla to choose from: white, wheat, cayenne and spinach. The girl working behind the register was also really nice. Personally, I prefer Chipotle if I were to eat Tex Mex type fast food because I feel their ingredients are more fresh and better quality... (Sorry, Izzo's fanatics).
The food and drinks were good, maybe even great, but being seated and waiting 30 minutes to get water or even a server is a bit off putting. Wouldn't recommend to friends.

We go here more than I'd like to admit. The food is consistently delicious, they have a great beer selection, and the staff is super friendly. The last time we went, my calzone lost the bottom crust while it was being made. They brought that one out, told us what happened, and said that they already had a new one in the oven and would box it up for us if we wanted. A free calzone! Any other place either wouldn't have told me that the bottom was missing, or would have reluctantly asked if we wanted another one made instead of taking the initiative to make the situation right. Fantastic customer service!
Great fried chicken and we went back a second time for the file gumbo and the fried fish. Service is attentive and fun. Not expensive.

The family and I stopped by this newly opened restaurant at Oaks on a Sat. at around 1pm.  Though it's peak lunch hour, it's rather quiet.  Despite that, almost everything is great!

Since the restaurant is new, the bath room is clean and in great shape, which a lot of restaurants around the neighborhood lack.

We chose the outdoor sitting.  The table and chars are in great shapes...  There's not single sight of bird dropping anywhere...one of the big No-No for outdoor dinning.

As for the food, we ordered from the 2 for $12 menu and got a  class Chicago pizza, vegi medley pasta and chicken parmesan.

The pizza was great...just like Uno used to make.  The crust was crispy, but not doughy.  The sauce is not too salty...however, the sausage is a bit gamy...this could be that they didn't put enough seasoning in the sausage.

The pastas were great.  The chicken in the chicken parm is thin and has a thin crispy parmesan crust.  The meat was cooked just right.

The wait staff does need more training about the common courtesy, but that would just icing on the cake!

My first visit to Cru Cellars was two years ago and that was the night I fell in love with a cheese, yes, a cheese.  Barely Buzzed, by the Beehive Cheese Co., is an espresso and lavender hand-rubbed cheese with subtle notes of butterscotch and caramel. Full-bodied with a smooth and creamy texture, Barely Buzzed will rock your world!  My dad lives about 20 minutes from the Beehive Cheese Co.(in Utah) and visits them often. He can't say enough amazing things about their wonderful staff and fabulous cheese. 

So now back to Cru Cellars. After my first visit, I knew I had discovered something special. I took a wine class a month later and learned so much from owner Jennifer, and I met some wonderful people. In the spring, their new food menu made its debut and has been wowing food and wine lovers all over Tampa. This past weekend I met a few friends and we enjoyed a nice selection of wines paired with cheese and a few of their innovative dishes. We had a fabulous time and I can't wait to go back. Cheers to Cru Cellars!
Doug gave me exactly what I asked for, I brought some pictures and he made it work.  My last haircut was horrifying and he fixed it!  I've already scheduled my next appointment.
Great local pizzeria! Fast and friendly staff. The menu has fun dishes with fair pricing. Eat in or take out both available. Also a BYOB! great neighborhood atmosphere.

Decent little spot to grab a quick bite. A bit overpriced, but their cookies are amazing! The juices aren't that great, I've tried several and they are all a bit "off". No need to try and be overly inventive with flavors. KISS - Keep It Simple Stupid. All in, a good place if you have no time for lunch and don't want fast food.
Traveling from Texas, saw the good reviews so came over. Great shop....had hubby all set, vaping and out the door in 5 minutes!!

This is absolutely, positively, hands down the best pizza in St Louis. I'd put it up against any place in the country, and I'm a Chicagoan. And before you judge... No, I'm not a touristy, "I went to Uno's and Giordanos and Gino's East so I know Chicago pizza" idiot... I've tried it all. Pequods, Stefanos, Lou Mals, Oven Grinder, those hidden gems in the burbs. I've lived there for 30 years and have tried hundreds of pizzas and this "Chicago style" at Black Thorn is as good as any I've ever had. 

We had a "supreme", pepperoni, sausage, mushroom, onion and green pepper. Chicago style. 

I don't know what kind of magic they do to this pizza in the 50-60 minutes it takes to prep and cook, but it is absolutely worth it. 

There are some complaints about how long the pizzas take.  Before you shoot your f*cking mouth off, go watch what they're doing... They're pulling dough, rolling it, tossing it, prepping it in the pan, loading it with all the delicious stuff you asked for and baking it. And I think they broil the top quickly at the end to give it a nice crisp top, and a great flavor.  Sit down, relax, have a beer and wait. It was worth it. 

The bar looks like it hasn't been touched since the 70s, which is awesome. I think if I had to gripe, I'd ask that they add a few seats... They seem sparse. 

Decent juke box, awesome atmosphere, small neighborhood joint. The Chicago Style here is among the best pizza I've ever had, whether you want to debate whether it's truly Chicago style or not. There's just no denying it's stellar.

This is the best hookah bar that I have found in Philadelphia. The only let down was that they didn't have my favorite flavor: rose. 

They do, however have great prices on hookahs, Turkish coffee, smoothies, hot tea mmm....

The service was great (we never went without a hot coal), the hookah equipment was clean and looked nice and the atmosphere is great.

I plan on going back.

The staff here was very patient with me my second day here when I repeatedly called every few hours or so to see if they had received my lost luggage.  They could have very easily gotten visibly annoyed by me.

This is your typical Comfort Inn.  The beds were OK, the AC worked wonderfully well in staving off the humid August heat  -- so well that I woke up freezing to turn the sucker down. 

The location in the Pyramids NW Indy area is convenient for business travelers or those wishing to be close to the 465, but not great for nightlife-seeking tourists.  I had wished I were downtown or in Broad Ripple for that.  Many chain restaurants and average sort of bars are within walking distance off Michigan or 86th Street (10 - 15 minute walk) and the hotel hosts an edible continental breakfast.

I tend to eat here about once a week. I love good sushi and SoHo is no exception. It's always fresh and the service is great. Never crowded and they have a happy hour where select rolls are discounted. And the wine, beer and sake is two for one. This is very close to home for me so it has become my go to sushi spot.

Went here on a Monday with couple of friends for some drinks and small meals all the while also looking for a new Monday spot. I ordered two appetizers and a glass of pomegranate juice. My total came to $25!!! Whoa! That's a little pricey for small plates. Wings, good! Crab cakes, good! Cornbread fritters, good! Shrimp tacos, MEH!!! The texture was good, however, a whole shrimp is placed in middle of a taco shell. It'll be so much better if they were at least chopped up so it spreads in the shell more. The coleslaw was bland, not much flavor to it. Overall, the shrimp tacos just didn't cut it for us. I will not be ordering it in the future. Our server was good, but there were couple of times when he was nowhere to be found when we needed something. Needless to say, this won't be a regular Monday spot ;)

My husband & I moved to Carp & we LOVE sushi so were super excited to have a sushi place just down the street, but much to our disappointment, this is the worst sushi we've ever had! So bad that we drive to Santa Barbara if we ever want sushi. Von's sushi even beats this place. Sorry for the bad review, but please replace this place with a good sushi restaurant soon!!

Hands down: my FAVORITE restaurant in Philadelphia. I love Jones for brunch, but would eat every meal here, if I had the chance. You must try the macaroni and cheese. The tomato soup and grilled cheese combo is great. If you are daring, try the chicken and waffles. This is comfort food at its finest. And the cocktails are great, too.

This place did the trick for our trip.  First time to NOLA, and this hotel is right in the mix - French Quarter bordering the Business District and just a block off of Bourbon.  We'd kind of had enough of the tourist party trap after the first day or two and found ourselves wishing that we had stayed elsewhere in the city.  Fortunately, street noise was muffled and we slept well in their wee beds, and the rest of the city is but a quick escape in any direction.  You'll get gouged for parking here, but I think that's true of pretty much any hotel in the area.  At least you don't have to wait on valet, and the in-and-out is very quick.  You could actually easily do without a car if you're staying within the city limits, but work took us outside of NOLA's walls where no buses dare tread, so for us it was a necessary evil.  A bit outdated, but clean enough, quiet enough (with the exception of the screaming kid next door on our last night), free wifi (slow), free pool (small), and complementary toiletries for those who ask (I always ask).  Oh, I did think it unprofessional that our hotel didn't notify us of a water advisory that was issued by the Sewerage and Water Board on our second-to-last day in town.  We overheard a waiter at a restaurant saying that the tap water wasn't safe to drink.  So that would have been great to know!  Otherwise, our stay was fine.
Gluten-free mixed berry scones were SO moist and delicious (a word I seldom use). My iced tea was also fantastic as was the service.

What a great place to visit!!! i wish we had places like that in Boston.. We were greeted and had a nice talk with the blond girl behind the counter ( nice to meet people who looves to travel as we are), she served us a GREAT green tea drink special and late. The place had only few spots left to seat (that popular it is @10am!) and the interior is something completely new and outstanding from all the cofee shops you could imagine.They even had a hammock swings, isn't it cool?! everything was delicious! Also, the guy behind the counter was making people feel great by smiling and being in the great mood!
The Peppermill is a one stop shop with all the goodies!  It's the best hotel in Reno!!!

This place is so amazing! I enjoy my time here. It makes me feel like a Good Old Southern Belle!!  The bartenders are really crafty and serious to their craft! The Chef is so amazing! He's so accommodating and he actually take his time and asks guest how everything is. When me and cousin came here we were treated like Royalty. We were also asked how the food and our drink was as well as gained the scoop on what the next best appetizers were. We really enjoyed out time here! I enjoyed the waiter that made sure we were having a great time. The staff is just amazing! Everything was so awesome! Definitely worth the Buzz!
EXCELLENT FOOD ( we had the scallops)! The service was terrible but the food was seriously delicious.

I went to Burger Up last night - I waited 30 minutes for a table and was sat at an extremely uncomfortable hightop table - we asked to move and we were graciously sat elsewhere. However, the tables are so close together that it is awkward.
After about ten minutes we were able to order drinks and they were out of most everything on their beer list. Then the waiter from the table we were originally sitting at starting yelling at the hostess that we were moved because now he wouldn't get a tip - this was right in front of us.
When we ordered we got a little something from every section of the menu - we are in the restaurant industry and wanted to try it all out!!
The scallop and foie gras app came out - and the scallops were cold and raw...not rare, RAW. We received a new app and the scallops tasted good and had a little of a sear on them, but the foie still had the vein in it and looked more steamed than seared. The she crab soup was tasteless outside of the paprika and parsley they garnished it with and the crab in the soup was dry and chewy.
We shared a caesar salad that was very good, and then we had the woodstock burger (benton's bacon, cabot white cheddar) and the shrimp po'boy which had to come on a hambruger bun bc they were out of the hogie rolls. the burger was good but the bun was too doughy, the poboy was mostly flavorless and the fries and onion rings these two came with were NOT good at all.
Dessert and coffee were a disaster everything came out ten minutes apart from each other and we ended up canceling our root beer float because it never came out and we finished everything else.

Other notes on the place - the waiters stood outside the front door in front of everyone with their aprons on smoking cigarettes - GROSS!
There was a lot of drama going on while we ate that covered everything from ppl stumbling around drunk to others walking out bc their waiter never came to the table and the owner chased them out of the restaurant begging them to please come back. It was a bizarre experience. I would NOT go back. And as for all the comments on whether or not this place is "hip" ......If hip is disorganized chaos and an amateur management mindset - then I prefer to never hang out in a "hip" establishment

Friendly staff, I was greeted when I walked in the door. I was a little confused as to where I needed to place my order. I ordered the drip and it was not too strong, nice condiment bar to add splash to my coffee. When I am in the area I will stop again and try the food. Check it out.

Went for lunch today with my Mum and my partner. Our server couldn't have been more friendly and prompt. All of of lunches were delicious (and huge, we all took half of our sandwiches home.) This place is not pretentious, serves great food, and the servers are fantastic. PS: the onion rings are absolutely terrific!

I love a good, informed bike shop that isn't too full of choices but still offers choices, that isn't pretentious but still provides expert service. I've purchased a new bicycle here and have had several bicycles tuned up. Genuine, family owned, local store with a long history of service.

Outstanding customer service. I ordered some parts for a restoration and when I was ready to install 2 months later I noticed a small dent on a hubcap. I asked what I could do and they said they would send a new one out right away. What a great feeling to be treated with respect and that my word was sufficient evidence.
