So, I set out to prove them wrong (lol). I did a comprehensive price comparison between The Oat (as we affectionately call it), Fresh Mkt, Publix & Trader Joe's.  I found that across the board (with only 3 or 4 exceptions) that Rollin Oats is not only cheaper, but sometimes substantially cheaper!!!!!! I compared identical item, brand & size to make sure I had an exact comparison.  There is nothing that they don't have that we need.  At first, I found myself still going to Publix every now and then but now that they have expanded the store size, I can find everything! They will also special order stuff for you, no problem. And then there's the extremely nice & helpful staff --- it feels like your neighborhood store from when you grew up.

This used to be one of my favorite thrift stores because it always had very unique, well taken care of items. I loved how much stuff that was always stocked on its shelves. I could spend hours in this place and still not be able to see everything, which made the thrill of the hunt very enjoyable. However, since they change management the shelves are much more sparse. The few items they do have are still nice quality.

This place hits the spot when it comes to wanting cheesy greasy food and their big daddy pizza is delicious.  The owner is always extremely friendly, but the staff isn't the greatest. Don't expect excellent service.  There's also no seating available so plan to eat outside or somewhere else.

I'm not sure why this restaurant is rated so highly.  The food was average. I ordered a gyro and it had once slice of a tomato and barely any Tzatziki sauce.  Everyone in my group had the same experience with their gyros.  Others in the group had average meals.  The best part of the meal was the salad.  Spend your money as you see fit but I've found better food elsewhere.

Aka Crappy's Pizza

My partner ordered a pizza by phone for pick-up. When we arrived to pick-up our pizza the staff was unenthused and less than stellar at giving good customer service. I went to the counter and the guy asked me what was my order, I said the name our pizza was under. Apparently, they don't use names on the order. (Remember my partner ordered so I didn't know they hadn't asked for one.) He asked what kind of pizza it was, and I told him I didn't know, that I was not the one who ordered it. He said "How could you not know what kind of pizza you ordered?!", with a condescending tone. I called my partner over and then at that time another man yelled from the kitchen was it a...? And he listed the ingredients on our pizza. My partner confirmed that it was and then we went to pay. They don't tell you over the phone that this is a cash only restaurant. So when I handed him my card he said, "Can you read the sign, it's cash only! We have an ATM." 

2014 and we don't accept credit cards? 

After getting our pizza we arrived back in the car and began to drive about a block when my partner, who was holing the box, began to feel his leg getting hot. The "Over Saturated Pizza" had so much sauce it was coming out of the box onto his lap and burning his skin! 

Once we cleaned the outside and inside of my car from pizza sauce pouring out of the corners of the pizza box, my partner changed his clothes from being covered in pizza sauce. We tried to sit down and enjoy it. However, the dough was just that...dough. There wasn't crust because it was that undercooked. The sauce was horrible and saturated the dough. 

So if you like Crappy Pizza with Crappy service...Cappy's is your place.

Oh it hurts me to dislike this place but I really really really really disliked Harry and Izzy's.

Went for an academic luncheon and had the "party room" that was maxed into its upstairs. When we walked in, there were at least 5 hosts/hostesses standing there--no greeting, nothing. Finally we approached them and was seated.

We were serviced by 2 waitresses who were in no way filled with personality. They were clearly upset they got our group, they barely smiled and honestly seemed like they wanted nothing to do with us!

For the food, I'm not a huge fan of horseradish, so the shrimp cocktail was a let down. Not only the sauce was not appetizing to me, but the shrimps alone were only appealing by size, but taste was barely mediocre. Had a chicken sandwich, bland...I mean, $20 and 2 hours later, I think I was just done with the place.

Service definitely stole the stars, but food didn't bother gaining any of them back. Sad.
We had a small problem with our room and Mel at the front desk made everything right. Thank you, Mel!

Food was excellent. Had egg-ceptional, omelete wife had spinach, bacon, portabella omelete with hollandaise sauce. Great coffee and breakfast potatoes wonderful. Excellent service. Can't wait to try something different next time. Highly recommend.

Outstanding cuisine, efficient service, exotic decor, reasonable prices.  Sansom Kabob offers food like your Afghani grandma would cook--everything fresh and homemade.  Unlike Indian food, Sansom Kabob's offerings are not unctuous, and the spices are subtle.  The eggplant is excellent, and the lentil and split pea soups are miraculous.  Our party of three consisted of meat-eaters and vegetarians.  We were all very happy.

Great meal, wife and I both and new York strip steaks which were very flavorful.  Ordered them medium and they both came out slightly under medium which is better than over. Sides were great, loved the wedge salad. Flour less chocolate cake was a great dessert. Only thing I would change is to increase the craft beer selection. I'm from Colorado where we are spoiled with choice when it comes to beer choices so I found their selection to be slim.

To begin, the atmosphere of this place is awesome! They have a ton of outdoor seating available and the lay out breaks the large restaurant into smaller sections to create a more intimate dining experience. I ordered the Summer Fizz cocktail while we waited 20 minutes for our table and it was very tasty but small for $10. We ordered the brussel sprouts as an appetizer and they were delicious! I love when brussel sprouts are slightly charred. I ordered the cheese empanadas and they were good but I wish I would've chosen one with meat. My boyfriend ordered the skirt steak and loved it. We will definitely be back to Livery!
Great sushi. Nice service. Long wait if it's a busy weekend. Store is a little small but oh well. The Sushi a little pricey but I assume most sushi is now a days. I would recommend this place.

Update:
I'm a fan of all their tacos. They are always generously stuffed with meat, however their  horchata (rice drink) is horrible. It tastes like water with some bland powder. Their horchata is not authentic at all. Would have been great with the tacos however they go great with a beer or coke. Delivery is generally fast and friendly. Some of the females answering the phone seem immature which make it difficult to place a phone order because they seem absent minded and laugh just about every other word because they can't pronounce items on the menu and don't even know their menu. It helped I had a menu and had to speak slowly to the lady and repeat it numerous times. It was annoying, but the food was worth it. Delivery is only $1 which is great. 

Ordered the beef tacos. There's no menu online so I asked what kind of tacos and if they came with any sides. The beef tacos are a fajita kind diced into nice small pieces but stuffed with a generous amount of meat. They don't come with any sides. That was the only good thing from this place. I ordered a side of rice and what I received was bland white rice. The chicken flautas would have been good if the chicken wasn't dry. They were stuffed with a generous amount of chicken too. The lady answering the phone and taking my order was completely rude. She said the tacos come with fries and they didn't. Looking at the menu they brought me they don't say that. At the end she just hung up on me. She was asinine and I could see why. Her job is too complex for her. I would go there again only for the tacos.

Not impressed by this Fairfield Inn. Staff was not friendly. Breakfast was not good- food was cold and non perishable items seemed old like they kept putting them out. Gym was tiny and limited. You could hear the freeway in your room at night and the light in their parking lot were so bright they shined right into your window. Won't be staying here again
Food that's worth the wait!!! I've lived in Nashville all my life and an invitation to the Pancake Pantry is never declined.  The service is great, the atmosphere is wonderful, and the food EPIC!!!

I have not yet gotten the chance to stay in the hotel but we were so impressed by the wonderful hospitality offered by the hotel. I came from New York City for a weekend visit to Philadelphia. We stayed one block away from the hotel and our building had a fire evacuation right after midnight last Saturday. We went to Double Tree hotel to see if we can stay for a little while till the fire alarm is cleared. We went into the hotel and explained our situation; the night shift manager and front desk staff were very warm-hearted and courteous. They generously offered us to sit in the lobby or at the bar. We were very touched by their compassion and hospitality offered to strangers. We spent about 15 minutes sitting comfortably in hotel lobby and we were widely impressed by the comfortableness, the cleanness, and the elegant design of the hotel, especially the staff member and the manager's kindness and sublime hospitality. We deeply believe that if we someday choose to stay in this hotel, we would have a great experience guaranteed by the high quality service reflected from the hotel manager and staff we met that night.

We were so looking forward to having breakfast here after seeing the commercial on TV and being told about it by others. Unfortunately our eggs we over cooked and had to be sent back. After waiting for over an hour for an order of eggs it really ruined our experience. I will give the management staff credit they did apologize and removed the order from our check. Will probably give this place another try. The staff really hustles out front.

One of the best restaurants in town, very unique twists on conventional kosher dishes. However, you will not find bacon nor cheese here everything is extremely good. I would recommend the Hillel burger.
Food is great and inexpensive!! The service is slow and minimal, so when you need something ask all at once because you will wait forever!!
The margaritas are excellent and the steak fajitas were the best I've had in awhile.  I recommend you make this one of your top considerations for a great Mexican experience.
Not sure why they have to have carcasses hanging in the back behind glass! That is really in poor taste! Vegan or not who wants /needs to see that!

As you walk into Wildflower Cafe, you feel as if you entered into somebody's home, the decoration feel homey and more like a grandmother style, you will be quickly greeted by an friendly hostess (perhaps she is the owner). Looking at the menu, we knew it was going to be hard to choose from the extensive choices, but looking at the food on the next table we realized that everything looked very good. I ordered the kale salad with the grilled chicken,kale never tasted  so good, it has a mild sweet flavor and it came with fresh fruit and wonderful multi grain bread, everything was delicious as well as a feast to the eyes with artistic colorful presentation.

I feel in love with this place i tried something new every week ...everything on the menu was perfect! I loved the staff that works at this restaurant everyone was professional and friendly.  Im truly sad i had to come back to Texas . I will miss this place!!

We just stayed at the Pere Marquette and were able to experience Bar Uncommon and Gin Fizz. I tried this drink at the suggestion of other posts. It was simply wonderful. Our only mistake was that we visited the bar on the last night of our trip. 

Chris and his wife were both working on this night. His enthusiasm for his profession is evident by the time and energy that he puts into each customer's request. The Pere Marquette is fortunate to have such a phenomenal mixologist.  We will definitely return and spend more time sitting and listening at the bar.

Apparently, Odunde, Inc does many things.  The only thing that I've experience is the Odunde festival, held in June on South Street near Grays Ferry.

Like many ethnic festivals, there were vendors selling trinkets.  but there were also lots of African and African-American themed products.  Lots of Caribbean and soul food for sale, and great entertainment.  There were capoeira, drumming circles, African dance, breakdancing, and even hip hop dance by some adorable girls from a local dance troupe.  Authors were on hand to sell their books.  There were hair stylists doing amazing things and beautiful clothing for sale.

I'm told Odunde hosts the biggest African American heritage festival in the US.  It was definitely packed with people.  

Check it out next June!  (As you can see by my photo, you don't have to be African American to have a great time at the festival!)

Give this place three chances. Today I just left the place again with nothing to eat, for some reason every time we get there, there is no chicken EVER! Their excuse? Our oven is not big enough. Their way to fix the problem? Eat our appetizers or anything else in the menu while you wait. My answer? Uhhhh... I came for chicken, because everything else in your menu, including your desserts I can cook at home. Maybe it's a good place for people that never had Peruvian food, or just trying something different, that can't have Peruvian food in a regular basis. But for a true Peruvian, don't even waste your time. Eat whatever you cook at home, and go try something different. Or it's even better go to Miami and eat La Granja :) 

Shame
On you
Cuenellis  !

Oh well

I had my fantasy football draft here.  The staff took great care of us.  Jessica was our server.  She absolutely rocked.  Paul Gellar was the manager on duty.  He was extremely nice and polite.  Paul even helped set up the room for my fantasy football draft.    The food was top notch.  Most of the guys in my league have never been to Twin Peaks.  They told me that they will become regulars because of the food and service.  I'm looking forward to visiting Twin Peaks again soon.

A nice little bar and restaurant. The mozzarella sticks were some of the best I had ever had and grouper sandwich was also very good. My wife had the fish tacos which she loved. They also have a great view up stairs to watch the sunset. Live music on the lower level might be too loud for some. The rum runners were also delicious. I would definitely go back.

I was there on a Sunday to watch some football. It's not that bad of a place, I mean the food isn't horrible...but the clientele is like straight out of a movie (or South Tampa). Guys wearing visors backwards and upside down with work boots on etc...

They do have a pretty cool fireplace outside which would be nice if there weren't so many mooks around it.

All-in-all...it's just average at best. Food leaves a lot to be desired. PLUS the menu is in the same font found on most of the shirts in the building - Old English Affliction/Ed Hardy font...

I heard so many great things about the restaurant. I got to go to this location and got a bowl with grilled chicken and the pepper teriyaki sauce and the sauce was just a lot, too peppery and salty.Maybe I'll ask next time to not overdo it with the sauce but it just didn't impress me. I was with a friend and she got the burrito with the Tuna and she also didn't like it as well.

There's two things I want in a barber: 1) to walk in and feel comfortable 2) attention to detail. As others have stated Mark is very polite but also "razor focused" while he's give you a shave. Aside from the aforementioned, the place competes pretty well in terms of price and perks (beer while you wait, good music) especially for the location. Although I can only speak to getting a shave and beard trim it appears the haircuts are also quality.
These places are very nice however if you choose to live here DO NOT use Micha. She is the absolute worst. Many problems on move in. We were outright lied to by this person. Very unprofessional.

"Authentic" bordering on stereotypical, but the food is good and people seemed to be regulars but everyone was greeted like an old friend. Our handsome waiter was either authentically from Italy or doing the best exaggerated Italian-waiter schtick I've ever seen. (He's Italian). 
The bread was ok, could have been better but at least they serve it hot. They bring a small place of (whatever the word for amuse bouche is in Italian I forget) which was just marinated vegetables - carrots, green beans with garlic, and grilled paper-thin yellow squash.
They were featuring a special dish of  Linquini Pescatore - linguini, clams, mussels, crabmeat, shrimp, calamari in red sauce. Everyone was ordering it, and everyone who came in (including us) was "sold" just by the look of it - and it was delicious. The calamari was tender, there was ample amounts of seafood and pasta and excellent red sauce.
We started with an arugula salad, which was dressed absolutely perfectly with lemon and oil. Couldn't resist dessert of "regular" (espresso) tiramisu (they also feature an amaretto flavor one).
The food is pricey (the special pasta was $38) but certainly enough for 2 to split, even with my big appetite. This is definitely the kind of place to bring a nice bottle of wine and spend a relaxing evening with a nice meal. We'll definitely be back to try many other things so I will update my review.

We absolutely love the Chesterfield location but because of the drive, we decided to do the St Charles Rock Road location. I will admit that today this place was fairly empty and service was prompt and pleasing. We thought for sure that it was not going to be a great experience looking at the parking lot as it seemed crowded, we walked right in and we seated immediately. Not sure why they closed the Florissant location as that one would have been ideal as we live closer to New Halls Ferry, but good job Bridgeton location!

Don't be fooled by the exterior of this place - it looks a little...meh...outside.  It's actually cute inside.  It has a lot of funiture, but has plenty of other baby essentials as well.  I got a high chair and a car seat from them.  The sales associate was quite friendly and VERY knowledgeable about all the products I was asking about.  The loaders...well, they weren't super nice, but they did their job.  Can't ask for much more than that.  

The thing I like most about this place is they PRICE MATCH.  If you see something on Amazon / Diapers.com for cheaper...they will match they price for you. 

Happy shopping!  Buying stuff for kids is so easy, and so fun.

Paid $20 for a fill. I've gone before for a full set by Minh and that lasted like two and a half weeks. This one an older woman did them and they are all very nice but nice doesn't equal quality. While they did stay extra long to do my nails because I got there twenty to close, they let me go without my nails even being fully painted and thus they were smudged badly. On top of that within three days I had two broken nails. Very disappointed. As a college student who works hard and I have rare little luxuries such as getting my nails done, and when I do spend my time and money to have them done, it is very irritating to have them break within days.

I ordered some takeout from here as it was the closest sushi spot and had the highest rating. Their specialty rolls are a bit pricey but they do have some standard priced fare at the end of the online menu.  The sushi was fresh and tasty. They didn't skimp on the wasabi or ginger and I didn't have to ask for chopsticks. 

Next time we will dine in as it looked intimate and a nice bar. I'm sure the is more noteworthy sushi in the area. They were our first try but not bad, not bad at all.

I owe all the credit for this one to the Yelp NOLA crew. I was staying at the Lafayette Hotel and wanted Mexican food without having to walk too far, saw this was nearby and stopped in. Its a small place, but I instantly felt welcomed by the waitstaff. We walked in just in time for Happy Hour so we took FULL advantage. I ordered the Margarita ($4) and my co-worker ordered the Mojito ($5) and then we decided to try the chips and with guac, salsa, and queso. DELICIOUS and very filling! As if that wasn't enough, we went in for round 2 with drinks (naturally, it's New Orleans and a Wednesday, why not?) and ordered the Pork and Sweet Potato Quesadillas to split. OH MY. One of the best quesadillas I've ever had. The succulent pork was a perfect complement to the sweetness of the potatoes and then add Manchego, one of my favorite cheeses, and a spicy smooth ancho chile sauce and you've got a winner!

If I'm in the Warehouse District any time soon, I'll be headed back to La Casita for sure! Next time I want to try their tacos...

We really enjoyed this place! The staff was extremely friendly and polite. What I also can appreciate is that it is family owned and operated. The food tasted authentic and home cooked. I will definitely come back again next time in the Reno area...

Maico is convenient for the "on way home" stop. I never eat any place new until I have checked the Pima county health department checks. They rated them excellent on almost all of their visits so I thought I would try it. I got a #5 (taco, enchilada, rice & beans) and a two carne asada taco plate. The meat was tender and plentiful. No grizzle at all like El Guero Canelo, always lots of it. The enchilada actually had cheese in it, which means it wasn't flat like most others. The enchilada sauce was smooth not tangy. The guacamole was fresh. The rice was good and the beans were just runny enough to mix the two together. Yum. I will definitely go back. The ambiance the others mentioned wasnt really bad. It was still very clean. Nice set up, location and prices. Better than the others around town. With my two top choices being Maico and Taqueria Juanitos just to show my taste.

This food is phenomenal!  Attended a party which served the most delicious ribs ever, catered by Beans bbq.  These ribs were melt in your mouth amazing with a wonderful sauce that I now crave.  The staff was friendly, the owner (Kristi) has an attention to detail unlike any other caterer.  She really cares that the food she delivers is the best quality and really wants it to be food you won't stop talking about!

If I wasn't so vain, this would place would make me obese. 

Their fruit offerings are just as strong as the savory. I love that place. Thanks to Shaun T and his workout vids I don't feel so guilty for giving in to Frost.

My husband and I had about 15 minutes to kill so we decided to go in and have a slice of pie & a drink.
It was slow inside so we figured we'd be in and out no problem, but we had to wait 20 minutes only to find out that one of the pies we ordered they did not have.  Waitress never took an actual drink order, but gave us both water.  Our quick stop to kill time turned into an hour.  And I didn't get my pie.

Had a craving for a burger and decided to try this place out since it's close to me, and it did not disappoint! Got the burger of the month and it was delicious along with some cheese fries and a beer. Everything here looked great and I will definitely be coming back to try more on the menu! Especially the milkshakes. The place itself is a small cute restaurant with an old feel to it and I would imagine its pretty busy on the weekends as there is not a lot of seating. Highly recommend!

We used Cajun Encounters for our New Orleans city tour and swamp tour. Butch, our city tour driver was awsome. Butch really knows the city. He gave us an amazing experience. Anthony was our swamp boat captain. We have never  had an adventure quite like that. Anthony got us literally up close and personal with the alligators. I am visually impaired and Anthony took the time to get close enough to the sights so that I could really enjoy them. We would use Cajun Encounters again in a heartbeat. We highly recommend them.

South Street's Night Market, 8/15/13 (see photos):

I've been traveling, so this was the first Night Market I've made since Chinatown last year.  Got there early, 6-ish, to try to beat the inevitable lines.  The traffic heading down Pine St was a disaster (whether due to South Street being closed, the Eagles game, or maybe it always is at rush hour).  I tried to park in that big indoor lot on Lombard between 2nd & 3rd, but it was full (did find one of the last spaces across the street, TG).

Getting to Night Market early is definitely a good plan, since after an hour the lines start to get really long for the best trucks.  But went with the flow and had a great time anyway.

Award for longest lines (too long to wait in): A tie between Cheu Noodle Bar (presumably for those killer wings), and the Surf and Turf Truck (lobster rolls).

Highlight of the night: Chatting with Marc Vetri as he sweated for his money at the Alla Spina tent (see photo).  Pretty good Sangria, Marc!

Also tried:

FOO TRUCK'S roast pork bahn mi crostini--perhaps the best thing all evening

FREECON FARMS' Crabby Granny cider--a nice big refreshing glass

LITTLE BABY'S ICE CREAM for peanut butter, maple, tarragon ice cream--Yum!

POI DOG SNACK SHOP for an authentic Hawaiian spam musubi (why Haiwaii consumes 80% of the world's SPAM supply!)

http://www.seriouseats.com/recipes/2008/04/tutorial-how-to-make-hawaiian-spam-musubi-sushi.html

STREET FOOD PHILLY...I can't remember what

SUPPER'S SCRATCH BISCUITS for a roast pork and pineapple salsa biscuit sandwith--great biscuit, but large and dry due to too little filling

TACO MONDO's Thai chicken taco--excellent

XOCHITL's margarita--pretty decent

About 1 1/2 hours to walk from Front to 9th street.  Definitely one of the "must dos" of the Philly food scene, but get a couple of beers to keep you company while you wait in line.

If you want to see what the vibe is like, the Inky's Dawn Fallik has a good video here:

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3gRp2a5g6ok

Things have changed here. Especially since the brains behind their establishment quit last year. They had a girl there that did all their booking, organizing - basically she ran the ship. She left and things went downhill quickly. 

The bottom line - there are bigger and better venues that have moved into Nashville. This place will also be a well known because they have been around for years. But if I were an artist, dj or anyone looking to book an event, this place wouldn't be on my radar.

The only thing great about this place is the fact its on the beach. The food was not great. My kids had some fish and chips, the wife had a chicken sandwich and i had a hamburger. Personally i thought my food was plain it was lacking the wow factor, in short this is how i would describe it frozen food plain. The wife and the kids did like their food, why because they were hungry

Don't waste your time at this place. We had a reservation, and wanted indoor seating. They said they only had hot outdoor seating available on the patio, and if we wanted indoor seating, we have to wait in line because we were surrendering our table reservation. They did cater to that request eventually after the hostess talk to the manager. We then sat inside and ordered some drinks, two of our four drinks came after 20 minutes. The third one after 30 minutes and the fourth one never made it. No one checked on us, and after waiting for 50 minutes for tacos, we ended up running our own food that was just sitting on the counter with no one delivering it. Unless you want a restaurant that ruins your night, don't go here.

first time going there on Tuesday for the Songbird Philly singing competition - very diverse crowd, very gay-friendly. we went upstairs where the bartenders were super friendly to everyone. ordered some late night chicken tacos for $2 each - simple, but they tasted relish & hit the spot for a bar bite. $5 Bacardi & $4 corona specials, plus cocktail list that was $7-$10. Great night at a chill & fun place!

This place has deteriorated so quickly .
When was initially opened as Flying Fish Crafthouse. It was so good. Creative, great menu with amazing staff
Then unfortunately seemed like for whatever reason the crowd wasn't coming.
Then after the rebranding it all went south.
Mediocre food. Went from spotless with cool vibe to kinda dirty and not well maintained 
So much promise. Just a shame.!!

Been enjoying delicious, hot pho at Saigon for more than 10 years, starting at their Lafayette Rd location.  Service is always friendly and efficient and food always reliable and reasonably priced.  One of our go-to restaurants for a quick, filling meal.  Banh-mi sandwiches, potstickers snd goi rolls always hit the spot.
This is the as good as any other  bbq I've had in Indianapolis.  Locally and family owned and operated.  A great business to support

The food wasn't terrible. I had the spinach and artichoke dip (delicious, they poured a hefty amount of olive oil on the bread which is always good.) My chicken was cooked perfectly, the pasta was sub par though, quite bland.  I would tell you how my dessert was, but my server thrusted the bill in my face before asking us if we wanted dessert. We did mention it before we ordered our food though. She seemed preoccupied talking to another table about her honeymoon at Yellowstone. Go for the food, expect bad service and a terrible old fashion.

Have been living in East Falls for a few months now and I've driven past In Riva more times then I can count. Finally got a chance to try it out for Happy Hour on a Friday. Never can complain about $3 Drafts and a nice selection of food. Very authentic, Italian menu. We got wood fire pizzas that were extremely well made and had great crust. Liked the ambience both indoor and outdoor.

Disclaimer: This is NOT a review for the restaurant and pool (i.e. Hollander Tap Room) which can be experienced by non hotel guests.  This is from the perspective of guests who actually stayed in the hotel. 

Forced to go with 2 stars because there is no 2.5 star option. The cons we experenced during our stay left me no choice. Just couldn't give the hotel a 3... Sorry Hollander. 

Pros: 
1) Hotel has character for days. 
2) Property and room seemed very clean & well kept. 
3) Great pool area with poolside service & outdoor bar.
4) A good restaurant (read con's for the exception). 
5) A GREAT coffee shop/bakery store... The cakes were crazy good! 
6) Free shuttle around the downtown area. 
7) Friendly & efficient service property wide. 

Cons: 
1) We had a first floor room with a queen bed in our room. Without exaggeration it was the WORST bed ever. It was absurdly hard, lumpy & generally miserable to lay on. More like a torture device than a place to relax & sleep. Considered throwing the sheets on the floor & sleeping there. Had hotel not been full we would have requested a different room (Not sure it would have mattered). After night 1 we even reviewed the early checkout policy on our reservation. If the booking not been non refundable we would have checked out. If you are looking for some blissful sleep on your trip, unfortunately you will have to look elsewhere. 

2)The bathroom was clean, but very small. At 6'3" I found it difficult to use the sink & move around in the space. 

3) Parking was an almost constant problem for our Thursday-Sunday stay. Busy restaurant, hotel sharing lot with property next door, many times no spots were available in the lot. 

4) Sat/Sun brunch/breakfast buffet left much to be desired. It lacked the large number of options you would expect from a quality all you can eat breakfast offering. Eggs seemed to be of the powdered variety, sausage was salty to the point of inedible and so on. Yes they have an omlet station, but it doesn't make up for the rest of the buffet. 

Property & staff were so pleasant I contemplated not leaving a negative review. Have traveled 30+ nights a year for a long time. Didn't expect Four Seasons, but not SUB Motel 6 quality either. After not sleeping for 3 nights I couldn't let the awful bed slide. Time for new beds Hollander.

Went here for the first time tonight and was not disappointed. Food is absolutely delicious and the service is great. Everyone here was so nice. The food was some of the best Indian food I've ever had. Can't wait to come back!

Manager Angela Vickers is absolutely TERRIBLE and RUDE.  What kind of manager turns to her employees and individually asks them OUT LOUD.."am I being rude?"!!  Furthermore when you complain to the Regional Supervisor Steve Mendrick he never returns your call.  AVIS is TERRIBLE!  Never going back!  BTW   try calling there customer service when you break down...You will be more successful picking up tooth picks with your ASS CHEEKS before getting someone on the phone...GOOD BYE AVIS!

First time in Philly and after debating whether to eat at Devon's or Rouge, we decided to take the underdog, aka Whiskey Village, and Boy are we glad we did.
Starters: 
The deviled eggs were just as good as the ones Mom makes for thanksgiving. wonderful presentation too. I actually didn't want to sip my water for fear of losing the taste in my mouth.
The fried pickles were delicious and crispy. not soggy at all. perfectly done.
Mains: 
The village burger was PERFECT. Juicy, thick, good temp. just Perfect. It's so hard to find a burger like this in New York.
The Pork Sammy was just as fine quality as your "Dino BBQ" or your Nyc BBQ scene. Fresh and we'll flavored pork that wasn't the least bit dry at all. Very well done.
Sides:
Duck fat fries with cheese sauce.......    YAAAAAAAAAAAAS!!!!!
Dessert:
Vanilla Bourbon shake had the perfect thickness to it, but you can still taste the Makers. Simply wonderful.
Alcohol:
The punch was as good as it sounded. No one flavor surpassed the other. a perfect balance.
The commodore had a nice kick with a citrusy flavor. Goes  hand on hand with the shake.
The overall selection of booze is as wide as the the bar itself. More whiskey choices than we've seen in a long time.
Staff: Kenny and Valerie were knowledgeable and attentive. Always checking on us and always there to service plates or answer questions. Fantastic bartenders on a busy Friday night.
Overall: Will come back again. If you're visiting The city of brotherly love, you CANNOT skip this little piece of wonderment. Excellent job Whiskey Village. Keep it up. We'll be back to check on you.

Love the chocolate stuffed chocolate with extra cream! They don't skimp on the juice and when we ask for a medium in a large cup, they ask no questions. (we do this so it doesn't have a cone top - one person picking up 5 snowballs is a task)
Staff is friendly and they have quick service.

My husband and I visited this place for the first time last weekend. I was in love with it the moment we entered. The restaurant is cozy and has a very classy decor. **Please make a reservation in advance** as this place fills up really fast. 

Our server was very helpful in suggesting dishes as we had no clue as to what we should order. 
Here's what we ordered :
1. Soup of the Day - a mushroom soup
2. Insalata Mista
3. Fusili Aristocratici
4. Salmone Al Limone E Capperi
5.Creme Brulee
6. Tiramisu

Everything listed up there was delicious. Do try their Tiramisu, I think it's the best I have ever tasted! 

The entire experience was very memorable. Each dish is carefully crafted. My taste buds definitely enjoyed the entire gastronomic delights!

You guys, I can't really describe how amazing both the food and owners of Yah Mon are. This review is so long overdue. We arrived a little late on the Saturday night before Valentine's Day. The place was busy with a big birthday group, and we didn't have reservations. We were initially told we could only order take-out, as they were swamped with the group and a server had called in sick for the night, but as we sat there deciding what to do (we were staying in an airbnb and didn't know where we could eat carry-out), the owner Janise came out from the kitchen and invited us to sit at a table. We chatted a bit and proceeded to enjoy an out of this world meal.

First, we ordered one of the meat pattys and were served both flavors due to it being the end of the evening. I'd highly recommend this as a way to start your meal if you're extra hungry (we were!). After much debate due to all of the great reviews for the brown stew, we ultimately ended up going with the caribbean chicken platter. Let me save you some time, this platter is amazing, but listen to what everyone is saying - JUST ORDER THE BROWN STEW! Seriously. The jerk chicken was moist and had complex levels of spice (you will need some water glass refills). The curry chicken was tasty and went well with the sides... but by far, the brown stew chicken was the stand out of the platter. My mouth is watering just thinking about it, and when I'm back in Tampa I will be here eating five portions of that brown stew. #noregrets

Our service was great, especially knowing they were understaffed for the evening and busy. When they brought out an amazing cake to the birthday crew, we knew we had to order dessert. While the bread pudding was tempting, we just had to go with the coconut cake. As a someone who does not consider myself a coconut fan, I had to eat my words this go around. This layered cake was light, fluffy, and full of real flavor. There was an impeccable balance between the frosting and cake with the entire presentation stealing the show (edible flowers and all). When Janise told us she had no real training as a chef, I honestly was not ready to believe her, but a more sincere individual you won't find in all of Tampa. She and her husband treated us like family while in their care for the evening. These two hard-working individuals are running a restaurant on top of their day-jobs and with the quality of their food, I hope it's not long before they can both make this their full-time focus.

Bui's is loved.  I like the egg and cheese sandwiches at different carts.  And this one is not significantly better than the rest.  But here is why they get everyone's loyalty: 
1. WEEKENDS - They are open on Saturday and Sunday. 
2. REMEMBER YOUR ORDER - I don't know how they do it, but they remember you.  I stopped going for several months and when I came back, they had it right. 
3. CONSISTENT FOOD - It is always good and they big roll is great when it is fresh. 

NOTE - For whatever reason, (hangovers?), they sell a lot of Gatorade with the egg and cheese.  Once I tried it, and it works.

This place is the best. Excellent food and an amazing cocktail menu. A place with a good bar menu is always a winner. Not to mention the great patio and lower patio with a fireplace. Winner winner chicken dinner.

Everything I've had here tastes fantastic and reasonably priced.  Beware the dessert bruschetta - it is so simple yet one bite will send you spiraling out of control in a fit of gluttony accompanied by a mild separation of body and soul.

Without going into all the gory details allow me to say that it has now been over five weeks since my first contact with Xfinity.  I have had the same promise  three times, and three canceled install appointments.  They are now willing to reschedule me for February 8th with the same assurances that I had three previous times.  Do yourself a favor and go to anywhere else or just update your library card.  Xfinity has the worst customer service department I have ever experienced.  They should not be allowed to operate wihout cable competition in all of their markets. Where are our political regulators at and why do they allow Xfinity to hold us hostage?

My boyfriend and I had a great experience working with ElementGQ for our kitchen countertops. Every step of the way was painless. Fair pricing with a large selection, and they even install in New Jersey. Yulia was a huge help from start to finish, between picking out my slab, to laying out pricing, to coming back to select precisely where I wanted my slab cut (and I'm super picky :-P) The installers worked quickly and the counter looks great! Would recommend. Everything is laid out very simply for you. Thanks again!

I've stayed here countless times when I travel to Nashville for business.  I like how it's not too far from all the action, but still convenient to the downtown area and right near the highway.  I also love visiting the Gulch neighborhood so this location is perfect for that.  The hotel is also usually on the more budget-friendly end of the cost spectrum, which is great. One of my favorite bars is located just behind the hotel so it's a bonus to be able to visit every time I stay there. It's also near some great restaurant options, including the famous Hattie B's hot chicken. Front desk staff are friendly- free cookie bars are usually available during check-in hours in front of the little store area and you get a free GooGoo chocolate bar and Nashville postcard in your room. (Another freebie is bottled Dasani water upon check-in, if you are a Starwood member.) Expensive but convenient valet and self parking- valets are always very fast and friendly, unlike many of the other Nashville hotels. There's also a free shuttle bus that runs regularly between the hotel and downtown locations, and anywhere else you like within the city.  The rooms are standard, but they are clean and fairly spacious...mini-fridge and Keurig coffee maker are available in the room.  The only negative is that the hotel rate doesn't include a free breakfast, but hey, you're in Nashville...head to the Gulch for Biscuit Love! The hotel was recently renovated as well so it's pretty nice and comfortable.  Definitely one of my top choices whenever I stay in Nashville.

I love the food here. I've had half the menu and haven't been disappointed yet (though they should get rid of the side salad).

Their seafood here is better than most restaurants I've eaten at in Mexico. It is easily one of the best Mexican seafood that I've had in Tucson. The prices are reasonable; I especially enjoy the three shrimp tacos for under $10.

Although other locations are not up to the same standard of service and cleanliness, this particular location is very clean and has good service. On April 24, I was served by Sergio. He was extremely nice and welcoming. He smiled and was polite when my wife asked him to take our picture.

I haven't received my glasses yet - I just went in for an exam and new frames today. But if they're right, and I am 99.9% sure they will be, I found the best eye doctor in the world in Dr. Tetrault. George, the manager, is also one of the very nicest people I've ever met. Like, really, really nice. To the point that I felt nervous speaking, lest I insult their delicate spirits. Dr. Tetrault was so patient and thorough - I feel like my last prescription was off, but not by much - so he went through some extra steps to determine how much my eyes have changed/how off the Rx was. Granted, it was only a little wrong, but now, if the glasses are perfect, I'll have better than 20/20. Frame selection a mite lacking but, I mean, how many eyeglass shapes are there? They do free adjustments and cleaning, like most optical shops I've been to, but they seem to do it with, um, glee?

They don't usually take reservations, but saved us a table for six for my wife's birthday.  We accidentally ended up there during their happy hour from 3 PM to 7 PM every day. It was a great atmosphere, and the food was very good. Wait staff was very attentive to our needs.
Summer roll was DELICIOUS!!! Also has the pot stickers and a pho bowl. Everything was fresh and amazing.
Stoped at this place passing through P. A. I must say it's a pretty cool place a definite college town sports bar. I tried the alligator tacos and I enjoyed them. Good vibes...

I have been going to gyms ever since I got out of college this is by far my favorite one.

I use it for some lifting, a place to do plyometrics and a training center to get ready for my races as running is my real passion. 

First up it is cheap. $29 bucks a month + the initiation and the random $50 fee they charge in October " to keep your monthly rate down" is not bad at all for the city.

The mornings are dead and I love it, I am there 3 or 4 days a week M-F and out by 9:30am.

The place is clean, i shower a lot here b4 work and I have yet to find something worse then what I would find in my own home...and I am a bit of a clean freak.

Members are cool, no huge gangs of weightlifters  taking over a bench for 2 hours and screaming with each set. Very diverse group of people....from yoga people to the MMA dudes to the spin people.

Employees are cool, usually helpful and at least say hey. Would like it a bit better if somebody was always at the smoothie stand so i did not need to hunt somebody down every time i wanted something.

All and all my experience the last few months has been good. I recommend at least giving it a weeks try...the sales guys are not pushy and chances are you will find a gym you like.

I feel like if Sheldon Cooper created a winter wonderland, this is just a small taste of what it would look like. 


Jingle Rails is a yearly holiday tradition where they create different landmarks from Indy to beyond that are easily recognized. There are 9 model trains that traverse their way through the different landscapes. 

Tips/Highlights:

+Tickets- You will need to purchase a ticket to the Eiteljorg Museum. This is considered an exhibit.

+Parking- Is free in the underground West street parking garage; however, make sure to get a validated ticket from the front desk.  As of Nov 2017- They are still working on maintenance in the garage, so is chunk of spaces blocked out.


+ Stroller Parking - Please be kind to other sand park you strollers prior to entry into the exhibit in the marked area. The space inside, while ample, I could see getting extremely tight with a bunch of people and kids running around enjoying the exhibit

+Guides/ Find the "Hidden" Items - Upon entry there are large cards that are geared towards kids that gives them fun information and tries to keep them engaged with the exhibit by spotting specific items in each section

+ The Displays - They are well crafted and you can tell the amount of time and attention to detail was extremely consuming.  The displays were but together using natural materials, so you will see a lot of wood. 

+ Noise - This may not be of concern to some; however, I could see certain kids, especially really young ones, possibly getting easily excited by the train noise and commotion of people taking photos possibly overwhelming. I would recommend going on a non-crowded day.

Hot dogs are very small but you get alot of cheese and a little bit of chili

Word of warning the onions are brutal!!!!!

Not sure where they get these I cook all the time and I've never tasted me that strong

Great crust, I'm going to play with toppings but the pizza was really tasty. As a former New Yorker pizza is in my blood. The coal firing makes the crust well done which I love, but for my first visit I'm pleased.

I feel they must be resting on some old laurels no one remembers they had.  That or people who grow up and never leave Delaware don't understand what real pizza should be.  Quite a few locals suggested trying it. 

After 3 tries, I don't think I'll be going back.  The pizza is sub-par, and attempting to get worse.  I feel they are abusing the great location they have by putting out this inferior product, and I think it's insulting pizza makers and lovers everywhere.  

Such a disappointment.  

This is by no means a judgement on the quality of the owners or people as humans, only on their ability to produce a pizza worth paying for, or eating.
Lunch was awesome. You've got to try the soft shell crab BLT. Geeeeezzzzeeee! Had to be sent from heaven.

I have been to Olive many times before - but not recently.  I went whenever I was home (fairly regularly for someone who has left the nest), but hadn't been for a while.  I was home for Thanksgiving and decided to go for a mani-pedi.  It was SO not good - they were rushed, my pedicure was seriously worse that what I can do to myself, and the polish didn't even last the few days.  The manicure was exactly the same way, but I had to go elsewhere to get my polish changed/fixed.  

She didn't cut my cuticles for either service, the massage lasted about a minute a leg, and I still have rough heels.  I mean really.  

It's a shame because the location is great and it's a cute place. Additional sadness because they used to give you a short back massage while you dried your nails.  

Another observation is that if they can't take you as a walk-in they should say so - they kept telling people "sure, 5 minutes" and the women would wait and wait and my service just got rushed faster when the walk-ins piled up.

Celebrated my Anniversary at Vetri's last night. Although we did not want the wine pairing, a nice bottle of wine was enjoyed. Going to Vetri's was a fabulous experience that I will remember forever. Thank you for the wonderful food, service and hospitality.

Awesome! Stayed here for 3 days and never had a problem. The staff are very friendly and will work with you to make your stay pleasurable. The breakfast was good but they had the same stuff every morning. My last morning there they were talking about making other food to switch things up. The rooms are very comfy. I've upload pictures of the studio suite i stayed in. I also took pics of the lobby and the kitchen area. Hope everyone enjoys their stay here like i did!

Too bad I cannot give it 0 stars!  Jessica is the most condescending customer service person I've ever encountered!  I tried to give her the benefit of the doubt the first time in person and then on the phone, but she is simply not a pleasant person to deal with!  The star is only because the gym is clean and spacious.  It is a pity there are people like her in the frontline of a business...shame!

Staff isn't very friendly inside they look very annoyed every time I've been inside, not very inviting to sit and relax and drink or eat, usually the drive through seems better to use at this location

I read the bad reviews and got worried - this was a off hours business dinner with co-workers, and I wasn't looking forward to a case of food poisoning.  I went over to CitySearch to see if the opinions were bad all around, and over there this place is raved about.

This place didn't match up to the wonderful relaxed, subdued atmosphere in Amura (Orlando).  I have never associated sushi with bad techno, but Ru San's doesn't let up.

We were a group of 6, and sure enough the service for large groups is indeed bad.  Watch your receipt too - they put the gratuity on it already, even though we all got seperate checks.  I asked for mine back and changed the total.  She wasn't THAT great..

The sushi was really unremarkable, and the wasabi pile was very small.  I will say that the seaweed salad was delicious, and at least twice the size of the one at Amura's, but serving it on a trifold paper towel as some kind of fancy presentation was really tacky.

I wouldn't go back just because of the terrible music.  It was all downhill from there.

Invited here by a friend I hadn't seen in years. 

Loved the ambience walking into a Muslim storefront - the greetings, the artwork, and the small of good food. 

I sat at a bistro table with my face glued to my phone as my friend took a call outside. A gentleman came over and left us two cups of tea. As a warm beverage isn't often free with purchase at most establishments, I was so very charmed. Gotta live hospitable cultures! 

I drank my tea... and my friends tea :) and waited for the lamb and rice dish he promised would make me fall in love. When they came out I saw how utterly huge the trays were. And all for $20! 

My friend and I sat and talked in my car for almost an hour before I made my way back up 95. When I reached some inexplicable traffic about 10 minutes out I took an opportunity to uncover my meal and dig in. 

The meat was tasty, the rice was flavorful and the veggies.... I can't even describe the combination of sweet and savory... soooo good. 

I'm not often in this area, and probably wouldn't return at that hour, but I would definitely come back  again.

This place is highly overrated. How can you serve something in lunch for $14 and not taste good at all. Just a wastage of time and money. I work on HORSHAM road so tried this, I recommended los sarapes on HORSHAM road as a better deal for lunch.

My favorite bar in nola! Second home status and definitely like Cheers in that everyone really does know your name! Love my pals peeps and love brining my pup to chill in this wonderful little nook of love!

Desire is always busy yet I've never had to wait more than 15 minutes for a table. The service can be a tad slow but the staff is very friendly and helpful. 

All of the food served is very good from the salads up to the entrees. The prices are very fair and the quality if quite good especially for a place located directly on Bourbon which is in NOLA tourist area. I recommend it :-)

Citizens Bank Park is a great stadium, there really isn't a bad seat in the place! 

They are vegetarian friendly! They had veggie dogs and veggie burgers. The beers are pricey, but what stadium has cheap beer? 

The stadium is clean and well maintained. No line for the ladies room...a major plus, I hate to miss an inning while waiting for the ladies room. 

If I lived in Philly, I'd be at more games. GO PHILS! 

Why not 5 stars? Well, I have been to Citi Field (IT WAS FOR  A PHILS GAME, I'm not a Mets fan!!!) and that my friends (even though it is the home to our rivals) is the best baseball stadium I've been to (including Yankee Stadium (old and new) and Fenway). I just can't get over that veggie dog at Citi Field, Citizens Bank Park is a close second.

Great music, great food, great bartenders, great location.... It's a pretty amazing place. The fish tacos are BOMB, the St.Germain cocktail is my favorite. I love the fact that they have outdoor seating which makes best for people watching. Must go if your visiting downtown St Pete aka the burg!!!
Love love love my lashes !! Absolutely love them !!!! Know more mascara ! I still have not tried the waxing yet. LOL Maybe.

The lunch special of the house salad and a small pizza is my go-to here! Great pizza, great prices, convenient location, friendly staff... It's one of my regular spots when I visit my childhood home from out-of-town!

Seems to be under new ownership. Waitress was friendly but continually voiced excuses as to why service was slow and orders were wrong.  Waited until she brought the meals ordered to inform us that they were out of sides.   Quite honestly, we probably would have gotten up and left at the time of order, if we had known the outcome was like this.  The fish was cooked well and crispy, non-greasy.  But that's probably the best I can say.  Atmosphere needs a little facelift as well.  Seems dingy and dirty.

Chickens and many other super home deco treats!  Lively displays snd loads to choose from.   I cant wait for Thanksgiving!  Pure joy!  This store has many many items to create the ambience I want to achieve for my gathering.

Good grief!  I need that table too!   

I particularly appreciated the mellow - yet attentive service and greetings.  

Will be back to choose final touches.

If you're in Historic Downtown Main Street, St. Charles, MO head south on the road or you might overlook this great BBQ restaurant.  It's been there for about a year and it's the first time I've been since I just did not see it.

Since I usually order pulled pork at any BBQ place, this was no exception.  It had the smoke flavor I love so much and I would have it again.  Two sides came with it so I chose sweet potato fries and cole slaw.
Small restaurant with big flavors. This was our last morning in New Orleans and Mena's didn't disappoint.
Beers were good. Got a sampler (I'm all about variety). Bartenders were very friendly. Got busy late.
Your phone number has a constant busy tone. I'm going to come in the shop and ask why.

Great atmosphere, dimly lit in the evenings, and the biscuits are literally to die for. 

If you are coming here to snack, then great! I honestly had to get something else to eat after leaving here. 

I asked our waitress about portion size, because hey, I don't mind several small plates, but I don't want to leave feeling hungry.

We ordered the half chicken, literally a kids portion, to be fair, it was tasty, but it certainly wasn't filling. We also ordered the spinach fondue, which was terribly plain and nothing like the waitress described. We paired it with Forefront Cabernet, which was great. I should have bought the bottle, we also ordered the sausage balls, can't remember the exact name, but they were great.

I may try their breakfast, because the biscuits were great, but I wouldn't dare come here if was hungry and wanting a filling meal.

Again, I had to buy a burger after leaving.

Tried the beef stew over rice which was nicely seasoned with a hint of star anise and five spice. 

The dinner special is OK. Got the greasy gluggy beef broccoli with rice and it came with a spring roll and crab rangoon. 

Roast duck with lovely. Crunchy outer skin and very meaty duck. Only thing missing was sauce for it. 

It's definitely a hit with the locals as it's the only Asian restaurant in the area and in front of the Peppermill Hotel. 

Very good value too.
Amazing healthy food that was fresh! First time i was in ther and I thought it was just a fast food place. The menue was intricate to read at first but it was all made to order. Great fresh food.

Besides being extremely inexpensive, this establishment doesn't really offer its niche...Mexican cuisine. They have a wide variety of menu items, but that shows me they don't have confidence in their Mexican cuisine. 

A big highlight of this place is that they give you free chips and salsa. The salsa wasn't homemade, which is something I was expecting from an "authentic Mexican restaurant." 

For an entré I ordered the chimichanga's. The plate was extremely sloppy and not uniformed, and I believe presentation is key. A highlight of the dish had to be the succulent shredded chicken. Will I give this place another shot? Probably not. But if you are looking for something affordable and half way decent then this is your best friend near the bars on Broadway.
Food delish, large menu, friendly service, huge portions. What else could you be looking for?

Alfredo is the man. He never forgets a face. so he greets u like he knows you, and i like that.. (not treated like a number at italian delight) i love the upside down pizza with pepperoni. Regular pizza is on point too.. the alfredos special hoagie is unbelievable.. even the regular ones.. (i ask for the norristown roll) and for the price u cant lose.. wings are probably #1 in broomall imho.. If this were boxing- Alfredos is the best lb for lb fighter around lol... best spot in broomall to order from everything is good..
great for Sunday brunch, enjoyed for dinner too.

So I read that this place was a hit or miss. I have to say all the reviews were right. For the most part, I had a positive experience. The hotel was clean, no bugs, and no screaming kids or babies.Happy hour was nice as always. I was surprised how small the pool was and the beautiful bay view from my bedroom. I think this could be a five star hotel with some polishing. We paid $160 a night, so the price was ok. Only regret ---Mimosas for breakfast would have been stellar! 


Here is a breakdown of my rating for Embassy Suites...



5 Stars

- Valet Service
- Front Desk
- Bartender
- Server
- Bay View
- Housekeeping
- Location / close to the casino and other attractions
- church service on second floor on Sunday
- cleanliness
- great Starbucks inside hotel
- peaceful in the morning
- trolley service



4 stars

- breakfast - not the best yet good

3 stars

- not enough snack variety during happy hour 
- signs for ice machine deceptive and we had to go to an odd numbered floor level for ice
- loud music blared from convention center nearby till 3 AM and we could hear it clearly from a very high level floor ( no fault of the hotel yet it made our sleep unpleasant)
- Internet not the best.
- hot coffee in the lobby was not available until breakfast

I'm surprised at how few people were in the restaurant. Seeing these reviews I thought it would be crowded so I made a reservation for a room. And while that was good there really was no need to. With that said, I think they really appreciated the reservation so do that! :D
I had the duck something salad and mango tango roll? Both were good, the duck was a little overly dressed, I think if I went back I would ask for either dressing on the side or just lightly dressed. But the dressing was uberly awesome, tangy with a strong hint of wasabi. LOVE IT! The mango tango roll was good but weird. In the 'romantic lighting' of the room I didn't really remember/realize that it would be mango on the outside and I thought, what a weird fish... But it still is a good roll. With that said, if you like the sweetness of mango, this is not the dish for you. 
My friend had the salmon sashimi roll or something like that and that was sweet and  tasty. 
If I was staying in the area, I think I would go there again. This really good restaurant seems oddly placed in Bensalem as I had never heard of Bensalem until yesterday but I"m glad Bensalem has a good japanese place! :)
Enjoy! Ittattakimaas~

Great place for a family to dine.  Where parents can have a beer after a long day and kids can play a game or two while waiting.

Food was excellant...pizza a must

The staff of friendly and props to a family business that is not a CHAIN in soco.

GO THERE ASAP
Found trips dinner on yelp app ... WOW best breakfast ever all 4 of us agreed  take it from me look no further

They Also Do Quality Repairs At Honest Prices!

Robert is a super awesome smog technician. He helped me recently with my newly acquired older Jeep that wouldn't pass smog check. Robert is always upbeat, positive, and a pleasure to do business with.

The brakes needed attention because it was pulling to the right when I braked hard so I took it in. Andy is a great 2G Mechanic. He noticed my brake fluid was very old and dark so he flushed the system and made the left caliper work again. The bill came to $35. Most shops would have just done a total brake job and charged me $600 to $800 or more. 

Andy took the time to explain everything and gave me a couple options. My brakes work fine now. I highly recommend Express Smog Check for smog checks AND repair work.

Nice work here. Simple menu, decent prices, and good food. The mahi mahi was flavorful, sweet and tangy. The carne was very moist and succulent. The pork? A little bland, in my view. Good enough service, too.

Santa Barbara local here & I gotta say, Pizza Mizza has delicious thin crust, Italian style pizza. My favorite is the B.B.T Bacon, Basil and Tomato pizza...Crumbled bacon, tomatoes, basil, mozzarella cheese, and gorgonzola with a rosemary white sauce...just thinking about it makes my mouth water! 

They have an amazing promo right now too, buy one large pizza get one free everyday from 8pm to close, great if you're having some friends/family over.

Divey place but so good! Reno does not have any real cultured full blown markets and grocery stores to obtain foods like roasted ducks and empress chicken or even barbequed pork handing on the glass window. This place is known for having their own ducks and making it themselves. 

Super delicious and meals are such a good deal.
I do not like the tomato beef pan fried noodle everytime I order it because it tends to be a hit or miss (too much sauce etc..)

Egg drop soup is delicious, their daikon cakes are great! Ducks are always meaty and fresh! And anything authentic is here as well. Divey place with a fairly huge chinese food smell to the place.

My kind of place to eat!

Located in an interesting spot of the city- west no libs?  East fairmount?  no clue.  but either way, we found it after stumbling upon it one day and it just happened to be cheat day so why not!  Of course we went only for the donuts (Maybe we'll try the other fare another day) but all in all a good experience.  The place looked clean and neat, simple (in a good way) and they were very quick to attend to us and answer any questions behind the counter.  I got the chocolate cake with glaze and my boyfriend got the original donut (right out of the fryer it seemed).  Price was average (obviously more than say DD) but when we bit into each donut we were surprised.  We never thought a donut could taste so real and good.  My choc cake donut was definitely exactly that- a cake-like donut.  It was delicious as long as you like choco cake.  My bf's donut was warm, sweet, soft and moist (though I HATE the word moist, I will use it just this once). 

YUM YUM YUM! Good job Fed Donuts!
The line was very long (waited 45 minutes on a Saturday morning at 9:45 am in July), but the food was fantastic. The pigs in a blanket with the cinnamon sauce they provide was amazing!

We got the hop on/off for 2 days. The first day we stayed on for an overview of the city with Brad and the young man on the trolley who plays in a band. They were both very knowledgeable and friendly.  The 2nd day we got to meet Starlene, who was also very nice knowledgeable and funny. We found the buses to be Timely  and easy to maneuver. If you have not been to Nashville before I would recommend a hop on/off tour.

When we got there they were all booked up but had a possible table opening up soon. We were seated just as the band started to play. It was a warm environment and although it was snug it was very comfortable. The food was great! Tapas style but definitely enough to share. We got a little carried away and had more than enough with 7 plates for the 4 of us. Our server was also a bartender. The Muse was my favorite cocktail. The band was great and it was never too loud. All in all it was a great experience. I will definitely be back next time I'm in town.

Had a great meal at the bar on a Thursday night. Drinks are very reasonably priced and tasted great. Bartender was very nice- but used her phone on the bar to look at a drink recipe while making the drink, which kind of took away from her authority on beverages. At least one ice cube would come flying out of the glass when she stirred. Every. Time. Not exaggerating at all, at least 8-9 times while we were sitting there we had to block ice cubes from hitting us. It became funny and we'd laugh when inevitably she would use the same amount of ice as last time or stir the same way every time. Might want to change your approach next time! But it was a great atmosphere and the food was great. French onion soup was very very port-y but I really enjoyed it. Tons of flavor and would order it again. Burger was great. Fries were the best. Highly recommend and will be coming back (maybe with protective eyewear for ice cubes).

I've been here and the burgers are okay. Not bad but for the same price you could go to Zinburger or Cheesecake Factory and get a better burger that isn't so greasy. The burgers are decent here though and the do have free peanuts.

This is a great locally owned and operated sporting goods store that focuses primarily on hunting and fishing.  They have a limited selection of clothing items and frequently offer great sales on Colombia fishing shirts.  If you need anything in the area of firearms or fishing equipment this place often has items that are difficult or impossible to find at other area stores.

A wonderful experience!!! Duke is amazing! Best shave I've ever had. I've gotten them all over the world, including Istanbul, a city of a long and great history of the art of the shave... A great experience!

I've eaten here a few times quite a few years ago and I thought it was OK to good, I absolutely loved the Indian pancakes.  But I just ate here yesterday and ordered "Wonton Mee dry with special sauce" (with soup on the side) and I also ordered Singapore noodles.  Both were just average or slightly below.  The soup from the Wonton Mee however WAS fantastic, very flavorful.  Specifically, the wantons were just ok, nothing special, they did have the soft type noodle dough rather than the old style Chinese restaurant wonton. The meat inside the wonton was not particularly tasty and the noodles were just coated with soy sauce as the "special sauce".  The leafy vegetables served with it were just steamed, not much taste.  The Singapore noodles were not as good as I had hoped.  They had some flavor, but still a bit bland and the noodles were overdone and a bit on the fall apart mushy side.  The wait staff were VERY nice and very accommodating.  The atmosphere was nice and generally had an up feeling.  Maybe this time I didn't get their better dishes.  Oh well, I might try again sometime.

I'm so glad that my friend who lives nearby Twisted Tail took me here! I will be back because I had a great experience. The service is friendly, the atmosphere is very warm and welcoming and the drink list and menu have something for everyone to enjoy. 

I was here on a Tuesday night and there was an autistic performance from Niki Sbaffoni and she was wonderful! The music really added to the southern flare of the place. 

Their mixed drink menu is amazing. Try the Kool Kat! It's made with fresh cucumbers and pear vodka. It's a perfect refreshing drink. I also ordered a cobb salad and it was delicious. It was in the appetizer section but it filled me up enough to be a full meal. The ranch dressing it was served with was a new recipe house-made and very tasty. 

Go here and you will def. want to go back too!

The New York style isn't really New York Style, it is better.  Perfect combination of crisp and chewy.

I like what they do with their beer options, for bottled beer, they have a beer fridege, and you pick what you want, and just tell the server.  **** awesome idea ****.

Our server was very good.  Accomodating, knowledgeable of the menu, and the right level of attentiveness and leaving us alone.

The booths off privacy with the high walls, but if you have a group, then long tables in the middle may be more suited.

Cheese bread was fantastic too.  Solid 4+*!  My wife would give this place a 5.0*, but this isn't the 1800's, she can get on Yelp and give her own rating now they women have suffrage as well.

This restaurant was simply ok. It got such rave reviews so perhaps my expectations were too high? Nonetheless everything about it was ok. Let me tell ya why...

The ambiance was nice. The decor was modern and unpretentious. Tables were spread far enough apart that you could enjoy a conversation without hearing your neighbor blab about her boyfriend's snoring or her irritating mother in law. They are also able to accommodate large groups comfortably. 

Food was pretty good...the problem? The portions were tiny. They were like designer little meals (with the matching price) in a setting that would be more fit for upscale burgers and such. My +1 had the duck and she was not feeling it. I had the brisket which was delish. Tiny but it tasted wonderful! For dessert we had peach cobbler, which was pretty good, and the lemon pie thingy. Our waiter raved about it so again I think I was expecting too much. It tasted like key lime pie. Pretty good but nothing over the top.

Service was spot on. Our waiter was friendly and for the most part attentive. I really liked that he paid special attention to food allergies. It's always a plus to walk out of the restaurant alive. 

All in all the was a decent experience. I would likely not return just because there are so many other wonderful places to try in the area. If you decide to check it out get the brisket, you won't be sorry.
Great ambience. Went there for lunch with family. Good service. Very limited menu. Food was good. We had ordered several salads and Tuna Burger.

Oh, my God, I love this event space!
I came here for the Bach Society's MagnifEvent dinner and silent auction.  Beautiful interior, plenty of space for mingling and circulating drinks & appetizers, nice setup of bidding items...

My only complaint is that during the performance by the Bach Society's young artists (soprano - alto - tenor - bass), the sound clarity was muddled toward the back of the room.  This was especially apparent during a comedic song where hearing the exact words was necessary.

Used to be pretty good, especially with delivery.  Sadly, they stopped delivering.  Called in several orders, to show up and wait inside for 15-20 minutes each time.  Quality of food has drooped off severely as well.

Food was pretty good. Went for lunch, not majorly crowded. They show you to a table but then ask you to order and pay at the counter and they will then deliver food to your table. Had to ask for silverware, napkins, salt and pepper. Prices are great for lunch. My major complaint was the amount of flies everywhere, even though we were seated inside. I spent the majority of my lunch time swatting flies away. I mentioned this to them on my way out but the lady made some comment about it just being the season. I understand that, but how come other restaurants don't have this problem? How about a fly trap?

(3.5) ~ good overall food & service.  Note: It's mainly for Take-Out, but there are a few tables inside.

MENU:
** Mango Lassi = (4) very good
** Lamb Vindaloo = (4) very good & spicy
* Onion Kulcha = (3.5) good
* Raita = (3.25) pretty good, but watery...
* Water(tap) = (3) ok, but needed to be filtered, to remove the chlorine taste, etc.
***Kulfi(dessert) = Next time....

This place is another pizza heaven. The calzones and the salads are plentiful and flavorful. I have been here twice and tired different things both times and the first experience was better then the second, not because of the atmosphere or workers there simply because for my palate I didn't make the best choice on calzone. I would highly recommend this place, not only do they have a cool place to enjoy mouthfuls of delight, they have an awesome selection of beers and sodas. Next time I'm going to make my own calzone and I am excited to go back! Don't worry about the large portions, if you have to take it home, it heats up very nicely, almost as tasty as straight from their oven. Also, try a different sauce with the calzones then you would expect. The queso and honey mustard dipping sauce are fantastic, adds to the experience and party in your mouth! Great place to take the entire family. Mmmm mmmm good!
Hundreds of Gel & Dip colors. I do Acrylics, one tec for that. Visually a busy place....
I LOVE this place. Yes, the service isn't the best but the food is so delicious that I don't care. I dream about their stuffed peppers and tomatoes. Plus you can't beat a BYOB.

We had gotten the spicy Nola bites, Crawfish cakes and the crab cakes and shrimp Alfredo...everything was amazing!!! The best crab cakes I've had so far....I know I will be craving the spicy Nola bites when I go back home. I definitely recommend this restaurant, the service was fast and friendly.

What can I say about this place but Ahhhhh!  Its very relaxing here, two pools, two hot tubs.  The rooms are very comfortable, huge soft beds with lots of pillow. Plus its within walking distance of lots of good places to go eat at.

For not being a "pizza place" their pizza is spot on. Notably the cajun pepperoni pizza. Knocks it out of the ballpark. And as the name implies, a great place to watch a game, especially in the fall for college football. While Nashville doesn't have an official Ohio State bar, there's always a nice little following of buckeyes gathered here for games which is another plus in my eyes!
Wow!  If Philadelphia and New Orleans had a child it would be named "Trainwreck".  Great sammich, great price, great service. Corn bread and gumbo is very good too.

The Quick: Fantastic hotel with incredible views of the water and an amazing restaurant (Oystercatchers) 

The Details: I had a great stay at the Hyatt. The rooms were pristine, the view was gorgeous, and the staff could not have been more accommodating. Everything was great for a business trip as well as for enjoying some time at the pool and beautiful weather. The restaurant Oystercatchers was phenomenal. I cannot say enough good things about the food and the staff. 

There's a fancy restaurant on the top floor as well. I did not eat there but I did enjoy a cocktail and the most amazing sunset. It's a great place to watch the sky turn rainbow colors. Overall a very nice experience at the Hyatt. 

The Damage: I honestly have no idea since it was a business trip, but considering how nice and luxurious the hotel was, I expect it is not cheap.

We ordered 2 speciality concretes (a frozen custard with mix-ins) - one was banana pudding themed and the other was a cherry chocolate pie.  Both were outstanding.  Delicious custard base with a healthy serving of delicious toppings.

Ordered 2 small sized specialty concretes, which was the perfect amount for us to share.

Service was friendly and quick.  You order and pick up at a window, only seating outside (this would also be easy to pick up and take to-go and enjoy at home).

I know gourmet burgers are all the rage right now, but Burger blows those other places out of the water.
With their fresh and local ingredients, awesome staff and beautiful decor, this place doesn't disappoint. The burgers and fries were all great, beer selection good, too, but you know what was surprisingly good here? Their salads.

Yes. I went to Burger up and got a salad, asked for them to substitute goat cheese instead of bleu on a spinach salad and I was on cloud 9. Don't worry, I got a side of truffle garlic parmesean fries, so I wasn't all good. The fries were equally delicious.

P.S. The bathroom was too cute.

Love this place! Just be prepared for a wait on a weekend night. From what I hear they don't take reservations, either.

I came here on a Saturday morning for brunch with my best friend because we saw a picture of the Drunken Monkey pancakes on instagram. The restaurant itself is adorable. The aesthetic feels cozy yet chic. We ordered the duck and sweet potato hash and this was definitely the star of the show (sorry, Drunken Monkey pancakes.) 

I would come back again, its conveniently located off of South Street. Service was fine, nothing to write home about but altogether a solid experience.

Little square cakes of happiness with cute bunnies, cherries, and fruit, and for 90 cents each.... Don't mind if I do!  I still can't believe the prices in here.  I was wondering what was wrong with the cake at first for that price, but it was surprisingly as delicious as it looked.  Everything in here just looks appetizing.  I like Asian bakeries because the cakes are not overly sweet as most ones are in American Bakeries.  

      I have tried the chocolate cake, and different versions of the vanilla cake here (bunny and cherry).  Both were fluffy, moist, simple, and slightly sweet.
