This place has come a long way. We got a suite overlooking the pool. It was fantastic. Huge paintings on the walls, separate shower with multiple shower heads, nice TV'S and great Casino action.

Staff is friendly and they just upgraded the poker room.

Who says the economy is suffering hasn't been here.

I can see why this only has 1 star. The store layout is nice but 8/10 employees clearly would rather not be there. Although my request was simple and I was served in a timely matter, the associate was brash and not friendly at all. There are better, more inviting Verizon retailers in the area. Drive the extra two miles to have a friendlier experience and you deserve it since Verizon prices are among the highest of any wireless provider.
Cute lil place with rad juices! Love the vegetable ones. I feel instantly healthier.
I love this place! Their shrimp soup is a thing of beauty, despite the fact that they use frozen veggies.
This place is disgusting! I wish i could give 0 stars. The customer service is horrible and the food did not make up for it! Do NOT come here!

My usual beer and pub food destination in Wayne was too busy so we trekked on to Ardmore as I've been wanting to try Tired Hands.  Heard about the high craftsmanship and unique styles there and had high expectations.  Arriving at the Fermentaria, we were greeted with a one-hour waiting time.  Having come this far, we decided to stick it out.  We headed to the bar and perused the beer list.  Finding that it is way heavily weighted toward pale ales and all kinds of fruity concoctions, we ordered a couple of the Tired Hands Saison.  Not bad, but definitely not what I've come to expect from a Belgian-style Saison.  Very sour on the finish, lacking subtlety.  Thinking that maybe I just don't have refined taste in their type of beers, I tried two other varieties.  Frankly, they all tasted remotely similar, as if they have limited range in their hops and brew styling.

We eventually got a seat at the bar tables, noticing that several dining tables had remained vacant the entire time we were waiting.  Ordered crispy pork belly buns (not bad but pricey for two small buns), and wife and I had crab and fish tacos respectively.  Tacos were savory, good blend of flavors and ample serving sizes.  Asked the server if they brewed anything along the lines of a brown ale, Belgian Dubbel or Trippel, stout, etc etc etc.  She recommended yet another what turned out to be yeasty, spicy, citrusy beer.

It seems many beer enthusiasts are crazy about this place and their brews. I've seen the great ratings on their beers, though I found that they are limited in their range. Maybe my beer palate is not as refined as I thought but I would take Victory's brew pub any time over this for variety, depth and less radical artisan haughtiness than this brewery.

This place is definitely a dive bar that caters to the younger college crowd. There is no table service- you place your order for any food or drinks at the bar. They seemed to have a pretty decent beer selection. In addition to what's on tap, they had a cooler full of craft beer options.

Our party ordered some lemon pepper and garlic Parmesan wings and sweet potato fries. Still being kinda full from our first stop, I only tried one of the lemon pepper wings. These wings would probably be the only reason I ever return. That was some good stuff. The menu says they slow smoke and then bake their wings. These were seasoned w/ what seemed to be  a dry rub and were very very good.

There are a few pool tables here, a dart board or two...was there a jukebox? The music selection was all over the place. I didn't venture from our table to look around...lol. Only saw the one bartender there. If you are looking for great wings, beer, and a dive bar atmosphere- this is your place.

Not impressed at all with my meal. I ordered the steak and it was very tough.  When the waitresses asked how our meal was after we were through and I said the same,  She said oh , that's a shame.  We won't be returning their anytime soon.

Horrible !!! I love to eat and very seldom complain about food but this place was just no good !!! Where do I start ? I'll start with the flies that wouldn't leave us alone. Fruit flies & regular flies.  I ordered mussels for my appetizer and when they came out I could smell a strong smell of fish. Anyone who knows about seafood knows that it shouldn't smell but I tasted it anyway and it was just down right disgusting. They served me old mussels. After sending them back the next appetizer I ordered was cold in the center.  And for dinner I had the lobster ravioli. The ravioli was just ok and supposably that's there main dish !! Not recommended at all !!! No surprise that we got reservations last minute.  The place was empty when we got there and when we left.

The first time I went to Slate, I swore never to go back.  The zucchini strand pasta I had there made me run the other way whenever anyone suggested going there for food.  That was 2009.  This is 2012 and I have broken my vow - three times already.  

Intending to walk in somewhere for brunch Mother's Day weekend, my family seriously miscalculated our chances of getting a table anywhere.  Constructively turned away from Day by Day, my dad ducked into Slate down the block.  No Dad! Don't do it, you don't know what you're asking for!  No wait for brunch? Damn.  Begrudgingly, I went in.  Hmm, the brunch menu looked surprisingly good, and affordable.  Interesting.  Still skeptical, I ordered a crab and bacon frittata and waited nervously.  The food took its time coming out (the place seemed very under-staffed), but I was shocked to find that the food was actually worth the wait.  My frittata was probably 9 inches in diameter and had plenty of good crab and bacon flavor.  It came with a nicely dressed side salad that barely squeezed itself on to the plate.  My parents wanted an order of eggs and sausage, which they don't have.  So the waitress had them order the two eggs and sides and the bangers and mash (you get both sausage and eggs).  Not exactly what my parents had in mind, but when it came out, it was more than enough food for 3 people and they actually loved it.  

Because of the great brunch experience, my fiance and I have gone back for dinner a couple times. The crab cake is big and meaty, enough for a very light dinner.  The mussels are delicious and brothy, with the bits of chorizo on top (also big enough for a light dinner).  Their salmon entree is perfectly cooked, crispy on the outside and cooked to order, accompanied by a decadently rich mash.  We also enjoyed their fish special one week, tilapia filet in a wine sauce topped with shrimp and scallops - lots of shrimp and scallops.  

My only criticism of this place is the wait.  It can take a little longer than other restaurants for the kitchen to churn out the food.  The waitress said they have a very small kitchen, so maybe it can't be remedied with more waitstaff.  We also weren't fans of the old fashioned that we ordered.  There was a lot of pummeled fruit in the glass, rye, and not much of anything else - not your typical old fashioned recipe.  But overall, I am a new convert when it comes to Slate.  Their food is reasonably priced, perfectly cooked, and delicious.  And the zucchini strand pasta is nowhere to be found.

We had went to a movie at the nearby Carmike Cinemas and decided to check out what was nearby... as beer fans we decided to give the new Cool Springs Brewery a try. Once inside, we headed for the bar (we'd been here once before when it was Guidos). It took awhile for us to get the bartender to come over to us... she was busy talking with a group of guys. Once we did get her attention, we'd ordered a beer, but one of the "guys" yelled something out to her and she left our beers where the tap was and went to talk to him... not great. 

Once we finally got our Fatback Amber's... they were pretty tasty. We were hungry for lunch and we drank our entire beer + 10 minutes before we could get the bartenders attention (and for the record... the only people in the bar were the 3-4 guys she was talking to and my husband and I... so it wasn't busy). We finally got a menu and I asked her to just wait a second because we wanted to order... we got the white pizza (something we'd had before when it was Guidos... and loved) and two more fatback amber's. 

About 20 minutes later we got our pizza.... and it wasn't what we'd remembered. The pizza was bland and didn't have nearly enough pesto or ricotta.

It took us another 15 minutes after we were done with our pizza and 2nd beers to get her attention and get our check. It was getting pretty annoying. 

We really did like their beer and the location/decor/vibe are all good... but the service and the pizza left a lot to be desired. I'd like to say we'll be back, but I'm not certain we will, and it makes me sad because they have a lot of potential to make it fantastic... but right now they're missing the mark.

This is the best gym in the area but I cannot give it 5 stars. The "workers" sit behind the desk and joke around and horse play. The only time they work is when Romeo who is the owner, is there. It is a hang out for the crew that works there and their friends. The weights are hardly ever racked,  and there is no enforcement of any rules. I don't mind the chalk on the floor, it is a gym, there should be chalk but members spill water or whatever on the floor and it will stay there for hours ( it happened tonight and I said something to they young guys that spilled the drink and they just looked at me).
The upside is the amount of equipment and weights they have. They even have a room that you can "CrossFit" in with a Rogue pull up rig and bumpers, but they are not a CrossFit affiliate nor do they claim to be. 
If you don't mind a few too many punks and people that don't follow gym etiquette, this gym is pretty good. 
I worked out here for a year and I did not renew my contract.

DELICIOUS!! This place is a neighborhood gem. The gorditas are awesome and at under $3 it is a steal. The staff are so friendly and service is pretty fast. Their menu is diverse and not your average Mexican restaurant offerings. My parents live down the street and we will definitely be going back each time we visit.

We had:
Fried Chicken livers with pepper jelly,
Side order of cornbread
Soup made with rice and green
Mac and Cheese
Gumbo File soup
Shrimp etouffe......

Everything was good to great.  We especially liked the chicken livers with pepper jelly. It is inexpensive and has a traditional style New Orleans dining room.

Four of us returned here for lunch.  We all found our meal orders to be tasty, reasonably priced, and well portioned.  However,  we didn't get the ordering process.  You must wait in line to place your order and pay.  It is a bit unwieldy.  The people taking your order are not particularly friendly. Yet we enjoyed our visit here because of the food quality, the atmosphere and our desire to support local businesses

They messed up our family's reservation. It's an hour drive one way from French Quarter. Long way to drive to find out they screwed up and couldn't accommodate us unless we wanted to spend several hours waiting for their schedule to open up. Disappointing as we were looking forward to it and had to skip.

Better than your average sandwich shop (i.e. Panera). They have a lot to choose from, and the ingredients seem more local/fresh. We went there on a Sunday afternoon and it was pretty crowded, so be prepared to wait for a seat or to order take-out. They have a range of foods, from soups/salads to sandwiches.. very much like Panera bread but I'm not too big of a fan of Panera. I give it a 3.5, since it's good, but not OMG ORGASMIC good. 

Best sandwich - Chucks 99!

I went here thinking that since it was in a nice area of town, I wouldn't have any problems but they used a chemical on my feet(without my permission) to remove callouses, which caused immediate redness and swelling and also cut into my skin on both sides of my foot. I'll never go here again. The picture is from three days after the pedicure.
I got the philly cheese steak with fried pickles.   Fried pickles were pretty meh, cheese steak was fine.   They messed up the order for the guy in front of me.

Snow was light and fluffy, and the creators behind the counter was more than generous with their syrups by dousing the ice with a second pouring of our chosen flavors.  We chose nectar cream and passionfruit.  Now here's the thing - I like my flavors pronounced and bold as much as the next person, but I was slightly disappointed with the somewhat artificial taste of the passionfruit syrup.  Comparing it to another place my husband and I tried on our first day here, this place's homemade grapefruit-basil syrup paired with their version of the nectar cream felt more light and refreshing; however because theirs did not have a second dousing of flavor, the syrup didn't get a chance to drizzle their way towards the bottom before we gobbled it up.  In the end ultimately, this place is clearly popular and you're not going to leave feeling un-refreshed.

The best tasting foods in town. The Étouffée was AMAZING. The Croque-Monsieur or Croque-Madame are to dine for. I definitely recommend giving Lüke a try if you haven't been there. You won't be disappointed.
Had the Texas Sunrise here. It was absolutely delicious & filling. Like eggs in your burger, you'll love it!
Was good, but not great.  I thought the gumbo was too salty for my taste.  Oysters were good.  Their Desire hot sauce wasn't bad either.

Some days this place is 5 star some days it's 3. I think one guy makes the pizza a little on the soggy side. But still not bad. We'll settle on four. The staff is friendly, delivery and pick up is always fast. The place seems clean, and they always have fresh slices.

Amazing selection of beer and you can experience it all for.... $$$$$

This place isn't cheap!  A random six pack of nice craft beers will cost you between $25-35.  Note, you can get a case of most beers for about $35-40.

The selection is 5/5 starts, but the store gets minus one star b/c there are no prices anywhere near where the beers are stocked (you have to sort through a yellow pages size beer guide to check prices, even for basic things like Yuengling lager).

If you want to treat yourself to some awesome beer and have the $$, definitely come here.  If you want cheaper beers, I goto Wegman's in Cherry Hill or the beer distributor on 11th and Washington area

Not a fan of thin crust but decided to be brave and try it.  It was good!  This was our first time and it was delivered.  It was easy, pizza was hot and tasty.  BUT...I ordered a salad and it was awesome!!  Delicious! Overall, a good experience. The next order was waaay different.  I ordered a salad again and the anticipation was great.  The salad was wilted, warm and not good at all.  My THIN pizza was cracker-like and cold and tasted old.  :(  Damn!
Thought this was outta biz?  Is it back?

SUPREME PIZZA I thought my other pizza place was good..... we drove all the way from Oro Valley to Midtown This family owned pizza it's worth the drive! A 14-inch pizza was an excellent choice three meats three veggies real meat in and vegetables, unbelievably good this is my new best pizza. Every bite I had was perfect. Not over sauced, perfect texture. A great place to go in the afternoon watch a game small seating with an open kitchen. We watched our pizza be made and baked  in the open  oven. a rustic Style Pizza that deserves a nine star.

We have had the hardest time with this office.  They only offer appointments from 9am to 3pm for visits, even though people work.  I get off at 4pm, but that's not good enough.  They state their hours are from 8am to 4:30pm, but that's clearly just what time someone may or may not pick up the phone.  You have to wait for a long time (almost your entire appointment time - I give it an hour), whereas I've been to plenty of doctors who can respect their patients time.  These do not.  The last appointment I had to wait for an hour, and the doctor saw us for maybe 10 minutes.  I don't mind efficiency, but when I wait for an hour to see a doctor, I'd like a tad more face-to-face interaction than "OK, looks good, next."  We will be leaving this practice shortly.

Went with some coworkers on lunch. Food almost took an hr so we had to get it to go. Waitress did not apologize for the long wait or ask if we were doing okay. I was a little disappointed in my portion size of potatoes. (That's just me being fat I guess) Everything was delicious though. I would eat here again if I had to but it wouldn't be my first choice only because I feel like it's a little overpriced for the amount you get and I'm cheap.

The beds are comfortable and the rooms are quite spacious for a smaller hotel/inn. They provide a mini fridge as well as a coffee machine in the room so that's always a plus, but why are there no porch lights for guests to avoid walking into the randomly placed iron chairs? We enjoyed our cracked tv screen until our gracious friendly clerk brought us a brand new replacement tv!!! 
Beware of the extra  $10 fee for each extra person beyond the standard 2. 
The bonuses are the complimentary continental breakfast that includes fresh local bakeries. Another highlight is that the location is close to everything.
Great place. We had excellent 4 star vegetarian chili, a turkey club and a Caesar salad. Service was good and we will definitely eat there again.

Ask for Christine.

Seriously. Just do it.

She's a little more expensive than most of the other stylists, but worth every penny. I visited her for the first time today, and I can honestly say that I've never had anyone cut my hair with such precision. She doesn't overlook a single detail. She takes her time, and she makes sure that it's just right before she lets you go. I didn't have to make a single request at the end when she asked me if I liked it, and I'm usually quite picky. It looks fantastic!

Christine is definitely going to be my regular stylist in New Orleans.

If you wandered in for a drink and stayed for some food, you'll do just fine. The calamari was particularly above average, and the ahi tuna nachos looked fantastic as they went by.

if you made a special trip to come here, you should maybe upgrade your Yelp skills. Service was well-meaning but not terrifically competent and the food was tasty, but about as interesting as you'd find at your average corporate hotel restaurant (though definitely better priced).

Okay, I'll first start off by saying that the other yelpers who complain about the parking lot and use it in their review are ridiculous! Giant didn't create the parking lot, the developers did and the township of Havertown approved it. If you don't like it, complain to them! 

Now, on to a REAL review about the GIANT, not the parking lot. 

I don't drink alcohol, so I can't say whether or not the Beer Garden is great to me, but I know that my fiance is a big fan, and since he's a beer snob of sorts, I'd say it's a good sign he's a fan! 

Now to the food! They have prepackaged meals that you just heat up at home! So simple and easy, especially for busy people or older people who can't cook or don't want to cook anymore. They also have a salad bar, olive bar, sushi bar, hot foods bar and I'm sure I'm missing something else! 

Their produce section is awesome, and I know from personal experience, my produce has lastly very long in the bottom of my fridge drawers. I have to say the fresh deli sides have been a hit or a miss; recently the potato salad tasted off and I returned it, only to find out that you get double your money back for bad deli sides! Winning! Of course, I'm sure I'm jerk will use this just to make money, and I sure hope this won't be the case, but you know people! 

The bakery donuts are to die for, but I'd kill for their Cannoli Cake. It's a big expensive, $13.00, but who cares when it's good enough to kill for? They have a great selection of health foods, (2 aisles), and the fresh meats are awesome. 

One of the best parts of shopping here, is when you use your rewards card you earn points to use towards money of of gas. Who WOULDN'T want that?!

Great pitchers of margaritas, food is alright. I wish the chips and salsa were better. I asked to pay the up charge for the spicy salsa and she brought me a bowl of green slimy looking sauce. Not too appetizing. The burritos were decent though.

Three stars for the pizza, four stars for the buffalo chicken wings.
The pizza was good. The toppings weren't the best. But the dough, sauce and cheese were nice. I got a regular combination and that isn't the specialty here. They're best with the Californicated pizzas I don't like.
The chicken wings were really good and that's what I get if I came back. Good meat flavor. Maybe some of the best quality chicken wings I've seen in the area. And the buffalo wings had a nice zing.

Is it weird of me to say that I have been here on numerous occasions and know only 2 items on the menu?  I can't get enough of the Crispy Hipcity Ranch and Groothie!  For being a meat eater, this is the best non-chicken, chicken sandwich I've ever had!  It's crispy, nicely seasoned, and the texture looks like chicken!  It's wild!  Love the peppercorn ranch that goes with it.  The Groothie is delicious!  It tastes like fruit, and not artificial fruit flavors.  It's grass green color might dissuade you, but just close your eyes, it's good!  It's healthy, it's fast, it's tasty, it's great!

Love this place. I come here every time I'm in town. Great guac, salsa, shrimp dishes and traditional Mexican food. Atmosphere is comfortable, just wish it was more crowded. Indy needs to support them more. They say the neighborhood is sketchy but I've never had any issues.

We checked out Modesto on a busy Saturday night... I had the family in tow and some of them were in rare form (read: having drank literally alllllll day and in serious need of a meal). We had about a 15 minute wait for a table, got seated, and got to the ordering. I really enjoyed everything we had... table favorites were the cauliflower, hummus, & pollo espanola, with the family raving about the beef skewers (I didn't partake in those). And of course we ended with the churros. You can never go wrong with that.

Our waitress was so great, she took the crazy comments from the buzzed members of the party lightly and with laughter. We even snagged a free plate of bacon-wrapped dates courtesy of my uncle flirting with the hostess. 

I don't think the prices are all that bad, but maybe that's because I'm used to Chicago tapas prices... these all seemed right on-par. In fact, I even commented how cheap our bill was... $80 for 5 people? And 3 of us had (delicious) sangria. That's not too shabby! I'll definitely be back next time I'm in STL.

It's very cheap but there's no air conditioning and the whole place is filled with mosquitoes. They also close between noon and three so you can't be at the hostel so that's the most inconvenient thing. It's also loud as hell because it's right next the train tracks so you're going to be woken up five or six times a night

worst sandwich I have ever had. after asking if they used fresh mushrooms ... nope, or even make the meatballs themselves.. again no I got a chicken parm sandwich which consisted of what seemed to be deep fried cardboard slathered in bland spaghetti sauce which did not even fill up the entire 14 inch roll. the roll wad cold and I could fit an entirely new sandwich inside mine it was so empty. I don't take it lightly saying the 'worst' but this truly takes the cake.

I will never go back and wouldn't even take a free sub if they offered 
stay away from this ghetto quiznos/subway hybrid
I am delighted to hear that Gary's carry 2 Degrees Bars!

My girlfriend and I went to Home this past Sunday for brunch.  The staff was very welcoming, and appreciative to have our business.  Inside the decor was very warm as I would expect for a place known for a great brunch.  Great barn wood walls and music was relaxing with the likes of John Mayer and Jack Johnson.  Although the menu was unique and exciting, the food was missing what I think breakfast should be based on, heart.  I had the Chicken and Waffles.  The waffles were luke warm and the chicken confit with gravy was difficult to look at and eat.  If you're going to put chicken and waffles on the menu, best to go with the standard fried chicken and change another aspect of the dish.  My girlfriend had the steak and eggs.  Was tasty but left our stomachs empty as the portion size was so small.  Also had glass bottles of soda which is cool if you only have 1, if you want a second it will cost you,.  Also did not have a cappuccino maker, but they said will have one soon.

I think this place has alot of potential, but needs work on brunch.

I really wanted to love this place.  The menu looked promising for a person with multiple food allergies.  The items that can be made gluten free, vegan, and vegetarian are clearly marked on the menu.  It was nice to have options to choose from. 

I settled on a few menu items and clearly stated that I wanted the gluten free, vegan versions of the dishes.

Gluten Free / Vegan Buffalo Cauliflower - because their buffalo sauce is dairy based, this dish is not buffalo at all.  The waitress said that the cauliflower would just come with the buffalo sauce and not the cheese.  I was fine with that.  When the dish arrived, it was just fried cauliflower, no sauce, no flavor.  The manager came and apologized for the mix up. The buffalo sauce had dairy.

Another downfall is that our party of 3 was seated in the bar area.  It was very loud and difficult to hold a proper dinner conversation. 

I had a couple of other dishes but I think there was cross contamination.  I left with major gastric distress.  I probably won't eat here again.

What a great experience.  Howard at Wagonwerx replaced the rear brakes on my 2010 Passat Komfort for far less than the dealer estimate. His work was accurate and professional. 

 I had no idea rear brakes on this car required an engineering degree, or that the "people's car" while fun to drive is so expensive to maintain.  Howard lowers the price of the fun.  

 If you are in the Northwest Philadelphia area, this specialist VW service alternative to the dealer is outstanding.  Keep it a secret, I can't imagine they need any more business.

CJ's in Lionville always have taken excellent care of me and my cars.  Staff is honest, friendly, helpful, easy to work with and overall makes every experience worth while.  Thank you for always being there.  Would definitely recommend them.

Probably the best liquor store in town.  I accidentally stumbled across this amazing store after going out for dinner one night and spent almost an hour inside.  They have a huge walk in fridge/cooler room with every craft beer/ale/specialty pretty much everything from pretty much everywhere you can imagine. In addition to that, their liquor selection is vast and diverse as well.  They have a generous selection of imported alcohol that I don't think I've seen anywhere else in Canada.  In addition to their amazingly vast selection of alcohol, they also have adorable cups, mixology gadgets and trinkets, and fun kitchen stuff.  Even though it's a little out of the way, everyone should come to Sherbrooke liquor to get their alcohol!! You won't be sorry you took the extra trip :)

Went for lunch. Had breakfast. Everything was done right. Service was great!  I would come back. I asked for home fries with onions and they were great!  Scrapple was deep fried, very crispy, and hot.
Love this place, the best choices and side dishes and deserts.  I love the smoked turkey.  The service is great

This place was the only place with a lot of stars and over 600 yelpers were on board stating it was good...

Unfortunately this place was simply okay. There is a sign in sheet by the door and the place is a small restaurant and maybe a five table seating outside, inside seemed crowded.

After standing there I noticed a side window and tables across the way, felt that we were hungry and really didn't want to wait.

Went with the shrimp and scallop pasta dish with linguine and it wasn't outstanding, it was okay. Also tried their clam chowder and the clams were non existing. 

My date tried their shrimp tacos (2) with some rice, she said they were okay, nothing great either.

Bill came out to $45 for just okay food. I for one don't mind spending on good food, but I truly felt this place was hype.

Oh well.
The Classic Roast Beef sandwich was excellent!! The baked Mac and cheese was ok and the Chai latte was low key! :/

Been here twice, always friendly, always great food.  Chicken Marsala was perfect!  We also had the shrimp and lobster ravioli in Alfredo sauce, which was amazing.  The price point is good for the beautiful meal we had both times.  A large party was sat right before us, and the owner took a round off our tab without us even asking.  We did have to wait a minute for our order, however, were there to enjoy our conversation not minding the wait at all.  

Keep up the good work!  
Cheers

My husband and I decided to try out this place since they recently opened and it's close to our home. This review is based on our "dine in" experience and we ordered stuffed mushrooms for our appetizer and a Stromboli each for our meal. 

I'll start with the PROS: The service was good and the Stromboli was tasty. The portion sizes are huge,  and two people could definitely split one Stromboli. They have a decent wine selection but the prices per glass are a bit high.

Now for the CONS: We both had only water to drink since my husband wanted a beer but their craft beer selection is limited to bottles of Yuengling or Sam Adams. The stuffed mushrooms were...interesting. They were stuffed with a Stove Top-esque type of actual stuffing and sitting on a plate of brown gravy. Also there was something unusually crunchy in the stuffing mix that occasionally I would bite down on. It was quite similar to that feeling when you eat an oyster and it feels like you're biting on a pebble or sand. We will not be ordering them again. As for the Stromboli it tasted good but had way too few toppings and too much cheese (and don't get me wrong, I'm a huge cheese lover) to the point that I had to pull much of it out. Also how much they charge for an extra added topping was a bit overpriced in my opinion. 

We will most likely give this place another try since it is so close to our house, but I think next time we'll stick to trying just their pizza and wings.

Who  doesn't love a Wawa!?!? Love this new location and large store.  The area is always bustling and I love the option for seating inside.  Crowds can be large, but the check out lines move quickly to facilitate a large
Number of people.  
Thrilled by this new location! I'll be a regular!

great neighborhood pub in Seminole Heights with excellent craft beer selection. food is unique and better then pub food but not excellent (perhaps some pub staples would be good). breakfast options are good but limited but it is great that they open in the morning for breakfast and lunch and have a semi-detached coffee shop/cafe. wish they did more shows in the side area with the small stage. comfortable place for a couple of beers and very glad it has established itself as a long term Seminole Heights establishment over the past 4 years.

Not bad food, ordered the country fried chicken, little disappointed that is came with brown gravy instead of country (white). was a little too much breading on the chicken as well. My wife had the spinach chicken pizza which was good as well but had a little too much oregano on it. Service was excellent though. We will return again and try some other items as it was a very nice evening there.
Great food, great service with a great price. Nice place for a casual meal. Been here a few times - food is always quick & delicious!

I love this place and go here regularly. The food is consistently delicious and fresh. The waiters are always friendly and nice! If your looking for good Thai food this is the place to go. My favorite is the chicken pad Thai.

Every time I come, the Hendricks staff fails to disappoint (which in retrospect, is a good problem to have)! 

Now I know you may be saying, "He's the Duke of Hendricks, he's obligated to say that." Well, let me just learn you something; if being the duke means you have the opportunity to eat some of the most epic BBQ of your life in a welcoming, laid back, kid friendly atmosphere, then hell...I'll be the Duke for life!

Come and join in the party. Treat your tastebuds to the greatness that is.....Hendrick's BBQ!

Well, in my first review I said we would return. And we did. It is still a dive, and the place is still packed. I am ugrading my rating because our breakfast was outstanding. Modest, but outstanding. My eggs tasted fresh. The hash browns were excellent, not the typical fried but more like baked. And the place is cheap. A real steal. I am not sure that it is a "palace," but if you want good food for a great price, it would be hard to do better than this place.

I had a great time at Charro Steak. The food was delicious and the service was excellent. Friendly staff and I really liked the look and feel to the place. I had the salmon dish and it had perfect touch of spice with a light sweet sauce. This is a great place to stop in for a drink at the bar, date night, or just to have an enjoyable evening meal. I'll definitely be back and look forward to bringing my family here.
Always order takeout sushi from here comes really fast very fresh always good and always polite drivers

I beleive this is my eighth year...and most mornings I am up and ready to jump out of bed  before my alarm rings at 5:15am.  My daily dose of platoon (between 3 - 6 mornings a week, 12 months a year) have kept me sane and fit from teenagers to college kids - and thru menopause. Love the workouts both the physical and mental part. Love the challange. Love the trainers. Love the friends I have made.

After reading the reviews My husband and I were excited to come for a nice italian meal. I have to admit it was very disappointing from the appetizer straight through to the meal. Will not be returning

When I started planning my wedding in New Orleans, finding the reception space was one of the easiest parts.  The fiance and I had been served one of the best meals of our lives at Luke's San Antonio location, so when I asked him what he thought about booking Luke New Orleans for our reception, it was an easy sell.

For your party or reception, Luke is extremely affordable, especially considering the other options in town.  They have two rooms available for rental--one is a private room that can be closed off, suitable for smaller groups, and a semiprivate wine room that's for larger parties.  Our reception will be in the wine room, and we were coincidentally seated nearby, so we could sneak a peek at what it was going to look like.  What did it take to secure our date?  Only a contract saying we would commit to a $1000 minimum, no deposit needed.  Sign me up!

When we signed the contract, I inquired about gluten-free options since the fiance is gluten-intolerant and was told the chef would accommodate all food allergies. Anyone who has an allergy as all-encompassing as gluten will give that statement some major side-eye.  But I'm skeptical no longer.  When we were seated, we asked our server about gluten-free options and he went back into the kitchen to talk to the chef.  "I'm sorry we don't have an actual gluten free menu," he told us when he came back, but he went through EVERY. SINGLE. ENTREE. on the dinner menu and told us if it was safe or how they could make it safe (grilling a fish fillet instead of dredging it in flour, for example).  For gluten-free folks and the people who love them, this is the equivalent of a unicorn sighting.  You are told more often than not you can just have a burger without the bun, or something equally deflating.  In fact, our server was so knowledgeable about gluten, he even joked about bring us a bread basket.

With the menu opened up to him, my fiance chose a dish of house-made bratwurst, pork shank, pork belly and sauerkraut, and I ordered the shrimp and grits.  His entree was a true mountain of meat, each component of it outstanding.  I don't even LIKE sauerkraut and I found myself stealing nibbles here and there.  And the shrimp and grits--ye gods.  I'd had it in San Antonio, so I knew it was good, but it was a pretty excellent reminder.  With bits of Andouille sausage sprinkled into the mix, the fiance and I agreed this one is DEFINITELY going on the wedding day menu. He remarked that usually due to cross-contamination he feels at least a little crummy after he eats at a restaurant, but that his meal at Luke left him without any--er, shall we say, inner turmoil.

Service was wonderful--the word that I keep coming up to describe it is "easy".  Not because it's simple, but because it felt so natural.  We truly felt taken care of during our meal, which is not an easy feat on a busy Friday night.

Speaking of which, if you're going on the weekend (and maybe even not) I would highly recommend reservations.  Running late after my bridal portraits and still needing to dress for dinner, I called Luke and asked if my 6:30 reservation could be moved to 7.  No can do, I was told.  I basically disrobed in a flurry, dressed, and we just short of ran to get there on time.  In fact, en route a passerby yelled at me "Slow down, little lady, you're in New Orleans!"  SORRY BUDDY CAN'T SLOW DOWN MUST GET SHRIMP AND GRITS.

With our stellar experience at Luke New Orleans, I'm looking forward to our reception even MORE now--if that's possible--and I'll update after our wedding day.

I enjoyed a nice lunch at Luke's during a recent visit to Louisiana. I ordered jumbo lump crab ravigote with toasted ciabatta  bread. The crab was excellent the only thing is it comes with a horse radish dressing mixed into the crab and it was very strong. If I went again I would not order it with the dressing although I'm not certain it can be extracted. The corn and crab fritters are a delightful taste of seafood, but crunchy enough to pass for a stand alone afternoon snack. The crispy brussels sprouts were fresh and in season and had great  texture to the meal.

We stopped in after shopping at Citrus Park Mall. We read the write up on TBO, and thought we would give it a try. We were seated right away, and the place was about half full. Getting our food took a long time, but I would rather have my food order correct and well prepared than having it fast. The wings were good, and you get about a dozen for $9. My husband ordered the BBQ hog heaven burger and thought it was good. I ordered the shrimp tacos with rice and beans, and was surprised how much food I got for $10. Flavor was good. My husband tried the Ballybrew beer, and he loved it. We will go back to try other items on the menu.

So disappointed.   Brought a friend from out of town there because I heard it was great..... horrible all the way around.   Cold air from floor vents  the Tom Kai, bland at best. The muscles small, over cooked and cold.  But worst they had me running for a bathroom an hour later.   Totally got sick from it.  :/  still sick from it.    Please do yourself a favor don't eat here.  Thai Phooket 1000 times better and half the price.
Very good pancakes and eggs! I knocked it a star because it was a breakfast place with bad coffee (burnt, flavorless). Can't have that.

They were nice enough to let us eat here even though the BFF and I were dressed way too casually for dinner. But then again, how do you turn away money paying customers?! Right?! Lol

Waited for 30-45 min to get seated because we didn't have reservations but as long as you're in before closing time they are able to still seat you. We've been wanting to try this place so we didn't mind the wait. 

For starters, we had the Truffled Garlic fries. It's served with a half head of freshly roasted garlic. Very good!

I had the Honey Ginger Pork chops! Wow! This dish is delish!! I'll remember this as a really amazing dish because it was so flavorful and there is so much meat to get you full! It's served with Jasmine rice so it reminded me of an Asian inspired dish which I love Asian food! 

My BFF had the bacon wrapped shrimp and grits! The only shrimp and grits I always compare everything to is from Dante's and Mr. B's is just as good, if not, better! The grits were very creamy. Once you've had really really good shrimp and grits, you tend to judge everyone else's harder and I can honestly say, the shrimp and grits here is outstanding!

For dessert, we shared the buttered pecan pie....and wow!!! This was awesome! I love how the pecans are chopped! It's served with French vanilla ice cream and it's making my mouth water just writing about it. Yum yum yum!! We asked a couple different waiters which dessert they preferred and they said pecan pie. Glad we took the advice. 

Mr. B's makes it to the top of my list!
Absolutely amazing. It's worth the wait! The size of the sandwich is huge, and it's very filling. I wish they had better hours, but besides that, I have zero complaints!

Can't understand the low rating, we thought this place was great. Stopped in after looking at property in the area. I had a bourbon and BLAT. My husband had tacos and a Stella. The beer was cold, the sweet potato fries were the best I've had, and the bartender, Mizael,  was both friendly and attentive. Five stars all the way.

The Phillies! Yipee!. I ahve just moved to Philadelphia and this is my second baseball season and I have spent more time in the ballpark than any other state I have lived in.

If you can get to the Hall Of Fame seats. Find them on Stubhub as they are for seaaon holders only but worth it.

You can get great dogs, bear, ice cream in baseball caps, and crab fries. 

Always a good time win or lose.

A friend and I ate here last night. Got there at 9pm and the place was pretty packed on a Monday no less. As soon as we sat down our server told us that there would be a 30 minute wait for a thin crust pizza and a 45 minute wait for deep dish. Ok, no problem. I've heard others complain about the wait time on pizzas, so I like that he set expectations from the start. I ordered a salad (the Wrigleyville romaine) and a glass of wine while my friend ordered a cocktail. The service was prompt, nice, not overly solicitous (which is fine by me). The salad was big. I made my friend split it with me. And, the lemon garlic dressing was very good. I would come back just for the salad (if I could throw some meat in there too). I am not a fan of deep dish pizza. It's just too much, too heavy for my taste. We ordered the Daley supreme thin crust pizza with pepperoni. It was done in 20-25 mins. And, it was really good. The crust was crispy. It was not greasy at all. And, it was covered in pepperoni (which I like). Not too much cheese and not too much sauce. As Goldilocks would say, it was just right. My only complaint was the pitiful wine list but I think they are more focused on their beer options. I'll give that a try next time. Will definitely be back.

I am not a member, but I need to go to TD to drop off a rent check once a month. The only problem I see is everytime I go there, no matter what time of the day it is (trust me...I went at 9 a.m. on a Saturday and there was still this problem) there is always a line of 7-10 people and ONE teller. I am not usually the person to complain about something like this, but I always happen to be waiting behind a person who takes 10 minutes to do whatever he/she has to do and my transaction only takes 30 seconds tops. Tellers are super friendly, I just wish they had more of them!
Good people great food love there turkey sandwich with cranberry definitely PDQ is in a league of their own in the fast food market

The food was great and our waiter was super friendly, but the hostess was a nightmare. We got a table for 4 but one of the members of our party was parking, so we were told we couldn't be seated until everyone was present. After explaining that the other member was parking and might just grab drinks we were told that "we can seat you but the person not here won't be able to order" and took their menu away. Very rude, very unprofessional. Definitely won't be back. We were thankful to the waiter for getting her some water and a add for our pitcher of mimosa!
Really wish they would bring the sweet potato fries back. Not sure why they rebranded in what seems to be for the worse...
Great food, but I'm not Cajun expert. What I was more impressed with was the excellent service. Very well trained staff. A little pricey, but that's the only negative thing I could say.

Jugs catered our company picnic (at work), and boy, do they have their stuff together! I pulled up at work to see a semi of full of food? Hell yes!
They ended up having a buffet line of fried biscuits and apple butter, pasta salad, cheesy potatoes and fried chicken- All under a nice tarped- in area. 

I almost passes on the pasta salad because pasta salad only ocassionally appeals to me. It's usually pretty bland (and when catered, it's usually more likely). I'm glad I didn't pass up on it. It was filled with so much flavor. It was sort of salty in a good way. Flavorful. Yum. 

The cheesy potatoes, or scalloped potatoes, rather, were a delicious alternative to mac n cheese. A lot of times, scalloped potatoes end up greasy, but these were nice and thick and really cheesy. 

And oh! The fried biscuits. Crsip on the outside, matched perfectly with the apple butter. 

Definitely a fan of Jugs for catering. Sometimes you just don't know what you're going to get. Catered food can be pretty bland, and Jugs was fun, full of flavor and great for teh occasion.

We waited in line for about an hour and it was worth the wait. We each got different sets of pancakes (sugar and spice) pancakes and sweet potato pancakes. We had it with cinnamon cream syrup. It was amazing, I would go back, though maybe at a less busy time.

Now I know why there is a line next door at Neyow's. The portions of shrimp in the "shrimp and grits" is inconsistent. The barbeque sauce in the "barbequed shrimp" was a waterry mess. The crab bisque and the gumbo were tasty. The atmosphere was just ok. Wish I had gone a second time to Neyow's instead.

I am here on work travel, and in 4 days I've been here 3 times!
I stopped in on a whim the first night and the food is out of this world. The owner recognized me my second time in and has been nothing but kind and gracious consistently every time I have gone in. I am very satisfied and would suggest this place to anyone. Too bad it's not close to home!!

Best italian food I've found in the area! A lot of it is made to order, and all of it is excellent. The fettuccine alfredo and white pizza are my favorite because they're super cheesy, but not overwhelmingly so. 

It's also BYOB, so go in, order some delicious, homemade italian food and enjoy a bottle or two of wine!

I just got my macbook there last Friday. I took the day off from work, saw that the store/mall opened at 10 a.m and figured I would be one of the first there.  WRONG!  I walked in at 10:20 and that place was busy!  There had to be at least 30 employees there and every one of them was with a customer.  The wait time board in front was showing the first open appointment at 1:30 p.m.  

But....I'm going to give you a tip that worked for me. 

Go to one of their computers.  Click on personal shopping assitant.  It showed that they had appointments open for 10:30 a.m. ( which at the time I was doing it was 10:26).  It instantly confirms.  I went right up to the front and let them know I had an appointment and they paired me up with Greg who helped me get my laptop. 

The service was great, the store was busy but that didn't stop many of the workers there from asking me if I needed any assitance.  I would go to this Apple store again in a heartbeat. 

Bonus:  Delaware's tax free shopping!!

I love this place. I came here for the second time last weekend and as far as seafood goes, it will never let me down.

The only reason I took off a star was because I listed my family's name down and they skipped over it. We came for lunch on a Saturday at 2:00pm and I had listed my name, then crossed the first one out since it was a bit messy, then wrote it again right next to it. After about 25 minutes of waiting, they call our names, say the table will be ready soon, and never call us again. We figure out that our name has already been crossed off. UGH! So, we had to list our name again and waited another 15 minutes. In total, we waited approximately 40 minutes -____-

Anyways, we had their oyster shooters, rock crab, lobster, lobster tacos, and calamari sandwich - all of which were very good. Very fresh! Very tasty! The lobster and crab also came with soup and salad beforehand. The clam chowder is amazing. It's so good. I don't know how they do it. Maybe it's something with the clams and fresh seafood. 

Overall, I love this place. I understand it was a misunderstanding that our names were crossed off the list, but still, if I didn't love this place, I wouldn't have waited that extra 15 minutes.

Super friendly staff, great gelato/pastries/drinks, plenty of space for whatever your coffee shop needs are. They have upstairs, downstairs, and patio seating. Upstairs is quiet and a good place to get some work done, downstairs and outside are better for socializing. The baristas are all very knowledgeable and willing to answer any questions or customize your order. I stop by here at least once a week to get coffee on my way to work, and I've never had an unpleasant experience.  This is probably my favorite coffeeshop in St Louis!
The food is out of this world. The sweet Italian sausage, the striped bass, the salmon. Delicious!  And Victoria is the best.waitress.ever. She took such great care of us. No one better.

This particular location of CVS is right on the corner of Napoleon and South Claiborne, near Ochsner Baptist Hospital.

Products: What you might typically find at any of these big box pharmacy chains---OTC medicines, Rx medicines, beauty products, supplements, photography accessories, snacks, etc. There are usually well-stocked, and their prices not unreasonable. 3 stars

Service: The management has definitely imparted the importance of the greeting when a customer enters the establishment. There's at least one cashier working at any time, but sometimes 2 during busier times, a security guard is almost always present, some pharmacy staff in the back, and they have "doc-in-a-box" service available for those requiring quick, non-emergency care. 3 stars

Facilities: A typical brick-and-mortar, flattop building you'd expect from this chain. There is ample private lot parking, and a drive through for the pharmacy. The major issue I've noted with the outside is the trashcan is not emptied often enough. Other than that, the exterior is quite nice. The inside is aisled, with the medical services in the rear. There is nothing really remarkable to say about the interior. It's usually tidy, though. 3 stars

Overall: This is a regular stop for me when I require a pharmacy. There is a Walgreen's across the street that's typically filled with all sorts of riffraff I try to avoid if I can. If you're in this area, go here instead. 3 stars

When this theater opened up, it was wonderful, nice and clean....it has gone downhill from there. It is cheaper to go to the Cheesecake Factory and order a Kobe beef cheeseburger than it is to get the chicken tenders and fries meal at this theater. Ticket prices are okay, but there are cheaper places out there to go.

The main reason why I will not come back here is how the management handles those who use their cell phones in the theaters. The situation had occurred when I wanted to see a movie on my birthday and during the previews before the disney movie, some lady had her cell phone on and bright, which is a major distraction. She had been asked by moviegoers around her to turn it off/put it away, but was not doing it. I got up to inform management of this and when someone finally came in, she was hostile to them and myself. They took her out of the theater for five minutes, to only let her in after some sob story about taking her kids to the theater, and instead of sitting where she had been, she decided to sit behind me and would nastily jangle her keys every so often during the movie itself. After the movie had let out, she left before my family did and waited outside of the theater, glaring nastily at us and followed us. We complained to management, they said there was nothing that they could do, and we asked if security could escort /us/ out to the car because that lady had been joined by a few large friends of hers that were also glaring at us.

When I go to the movies, I want to be safe, especially with those news stories of shootings going on. The management failed in a big way, and so did AMC when I complained to them about that theater. I have found a theater that I like much better that doesn't charge an arm, a leg, and two pints of blood to have a drink.

I haven't been here for a couple years but they have the best pupusas in the city. Get the mix kind and you can thank me later. The service here can be a bit slow, but I promise the food is worth the wait. Inside décor was kinda bleh back then but I heard they may have renovated more recently.

A safe place that has become an occasional comfort zone, Cheeseburger Paradise offers good fare of its namesake.  The festive tackiness aside, the food, service and experience can vary wildly.  There's no sure thing here except the ridiculous interior, which is fun when your experience is matching it.  
The slider option is usually safe as are most of the gourmet burgers, I've not gone off-lane and gotten a different meal than a burger so I can't comment on much more.  
Put on your best Hawaiian shirt (vomit) and enjoy!

Fool me once, shame on you.  Fool me FOUR TIMES, shame on me!

I don't know why we keep revisiting Land of Smile.  Wait.  I know.  It's ridiculously convenient.  It's clean.  It's friendly.

The food is just beyond mediocre.

That, and it's overpriced. 

Thai isn't that unique anymore and I guess I'm too used Thai places being along the same lines as Chinese takeout places to put up with such prices.  

After giving it a couple tries, we're more than willing to drive another 5 minutes to the next Thai place that we feel are more worth it.

BEST COFFEE  HOUSE IN CONSHOHOCKEN  BETTER THAN TRADE STONE !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! i love this place so much i pend about 30.00 a week on coffee and buy them all kinds of owl items to put in the coffee house I   love.  I plan on doubleing  my amount from 30 to 60 a week by visiting 2 times a day hope this place is there for the next 60 years!

This is by far the BEST moving company here in Nashville - without a doubt my FAVORITE that we have ever used! We have moved several times over the last few years and have used several different well-known companies. This past weekend we moved into our first home and at the request of a friend decided to go with Green Truck Moving Company. i had always been curious about them, but had not really heard many reviews, and while this is not often a deterrent for me, when it comes to moving, its stressful enough as it is so I admit that I do typically opt for those companies that I have heard more about. Well, after this move, I plan to make sure everyone I know hears about Green Truck Moving Co. and how GREAT they were to us.

They were fantastic, pleasant, and incredibly helpful to work with throughout every single step of the process. Starting with Crystal Pullen, who I spoke with each time I called to first get a quote, then to confirm that they were who we wanted to work with. She must have spent 45 minutes on the phone with me when I first called to get an estimate, and she remained patient, helpful, professional, but also just a lot of fun the whole time as she talked me through their policies and cost structures and then listened to me think out loud as I tried to remember what all we had and what all we actually needed them to move versus what we would move ourselves. She did not get pushy or impatient at any point and even helped me out when I couldn't figure out how to best "name" or describe some of the things on our list. Plus she did all that knowing that I was still planning on calling other companies to get their quotes as well! I know "that's her job", but that was a significant investment of time and energy on her part for a not-sure thing, plus when I spoke to people at the other companies I ended up calling, not one of them was even half as helpful or pleasant to speak with, and I spent a fraction of the time on the phone with them.

Then, when it came to our moving day, we actually got a notification call 24hrs before our scheduled move (which I can tell you, is not always as sure a thing as some companies will tell you). Plus, on the morning of the move, the guys that we going to actually move us called (like Crystal said they would) 30min before getting to our house! Again, I know all this is pretty standard policy stuff, but again, on more than one occasion, especially regarding the 30-min "heads-up" call, if this comes at all it is often when they are turning on to your street. Now, I am admittedly an overly anxious mover, so this "heads-up" window is EXTREMELY helpful and appreciated!

The company sent three men (Barry, Joseph Russell, and William Davis) to take care of our move and I cant stress enough AWESOME these guys were! All three of them worked incredibly hard and efficiently. The apartment we were moving out of was a small second story attic apt and the only access in/out was an outside staircase with like 20 stairs and only a small patio at the top to turn around once you came out of the house - not ideal. But these guys weren't phased. They were all very polite, 100% respectful of our things and our home, and much like Crystal, they were each really pleasant to work and interact with. Another thing that they did, which I was seriously impressed by and grateful for was that anytime there was something that they weren't sure about OR that they felt WE might be confused or concerned about, they ALWAYS took a second to check with us to ask or to let us know what they were doing or planning to do to make sure we were okay with it. They didn't do anything as far as wrapping or moving things without making sure we were 100% comfortable with how they were doing things and how our things were being handled (which I can honestly say that I have NEVER experienced, certainly not to that extent, from any other movers). They also constantly made sure that they were being respectful of our time and we never felt at any point like any one of the guys was not putting in 100%. In the end, they finished under the estimated time! They took great care of our things-nothing was scuffed, scratched, or dinged. They didn't damage any walls or door jams and they made sure to be extra careful on the wood floors at our new house. Barry, Joseph, and William ALL did an EXCELLENT job! I hope they get the credit and recognition they absolutely deserve!

The Green Truck Moving Co. did an excellent job and the help we received from Crystal and all the hard work that Barry, Joseph, and William put in was worth taking a minute to mention and share. We hope not to move again any time soon, BUT if we do, we will absolutely go with Green Truck Moving Co. again, without a second thought! I also 100% intend to recommend Green Truck Movers to anyone we know or hear about who is moving and share our about our experience with them! Thanks again!

The service was excellent and friendly, starting with the host -- in jeans on a Saturday night, which I preferred to some of the over-dressed stuffiness elsewhere in the FQ -- and I'm guessing from another review that he is the owner. The food was just ok. I had the rabbit, which was reasonable but nothing special. The most striking thing about it was that carrot appeared in three forms: diced in the stew, carrots among the baby veg side, and a pickled raw carrot unnecessary garnish. And, seriously, baby veg? I expected classic Creole, and didn't need to know that the chef cut his teeth in the 1970s or whenever those were popular. If you're looking for a restaurant with no wait at 8pm on a Saturday, this is an option, but you might prefer to look for a better one.

Requested a quote gave my timeline for the work, Ricardo showed up walked the property, didn't measure.  Told me to contact him closer to the date I required my work.  I reached out several times by text and call with no response.  Finally received a response with a per square price based on incorrect square footage.  I corrected him on this and asked him to provide me the quote in writing factoring in the retaining wall and planter I needed around my new pool.  Received a text back saying he will provide a written quote.  No dice.  Several weeks past.  I am now requesting additional quotes.  We will see how that goes.  Shame because this is a 14-15k job
Service was pretty good in the bar for a busy Friday, the BLT with avocado was really good and we liked the beer too

Horrible experience. Waited over 30 minutes and paid $14 for one crab po-boy that was basically bread and a poor excuse for garnish. Would recommend staying away from this place at all cost . Save your money and eat better next door at other vendors.

Pros: the eggs Benedict was amazing and so was the French toast. I would recommend them both highly. The service was pretty good! 
Cons: the hostess looked like she hated her life, the air conditioning was very bad, the sausage was nasty. 
Overall, I would definitely recommend this place based on the food!!

This place has one of the highest yelp reviews on Frenchman's street and now we know why! There is live jazz inside the restaurant and just brings the ambience all together and the host outside of the restaurant is very, very, very, organized. The wait is a little long but not too long that you are starving. The cocktail drinks are delicious, I ended up getting this creamy cocktail drink with mint inside and it was like a high class white Russian drink (which is my favorite cocktails). The food is amazing! The details of each plate that's coupled with vegetable or a certain sauce that you would never think would go together tastes amazing! Among our many tiny plates we got, we got the scallops and they were delicious. Everything else there is good! The only thing that could be improved was the service, but I am not kidding, it Is such a high volume restaurant, I'm surprised we even got sat. Come listen to the jazz!

Every single thing i have tried had been delicious! Great place to get your ice cream fix!  
Totally totally homemade and creamy!

Best Chinese food in Mooresville... Oh wait, it's the ONLY Chinese food in Mooresville. Regardless, I've been to too many Chinese buffets and they are not all the same. Dong's has a good variety of dishes with lots of veggie options. Good salad bar and lots of desserts. They also have a full menu available. I've liked everything I've tried here. They have some of the best grilled chicken skewers I've ever had and the steamed dumplings are excellent, too.

Read some of the negative reviews but know this.. the employees are rotating students and it's a Drexel operation not some private business with an owner. That said, it offers the food I love.. like fresh combinations, simple ingredients, healthy choices, and favs like tofu and seitan. I find every time I go there to be incredibly flavorful. Some chef at Drexel must be vegetarian bc it's very spot on flavor wise. I dunno, I can't really complain when before there were limited vegetarian foods to choose from. To be honest, initially they had some kinks to work out but I feel they responded to those. I notice the website menu does not match the store menu so don't rely on that unless they have a date on it or something.

Bait and switch! I have spent lots of time in piano bars all over the county, so I was really excited when I saw "the red piano" bar open on state street.  I took my girl and group of friends there with high hopes and we were all very disappointed in the fact that they have no piano. I mean they have a grand piano that hangs from the sign. After taking one step into the place I could hear without even seeing it that it was a cheap digital piano. Also I could see they spared no expense on the decor. I've been to really shabby establishments compared to this place that had real pianos (most have 2). I feel no self respecting piano bar should have a digital piano, and if they do it should at least be a high end one. We all left immediately feeling cheated. I guess if you just want to go to a bar this place would be ok. But if you are a musician, or just a music fan you will be frustrated and disappointed as we were. I will not go back to this fake piano bar.

Scallion pancakes were quite good. Pork chop soup had great flavor and crunch. We also opted for one of the Indonesian curries, which had a nice mix of flavors. Courteous staff. When we asked for our leftovers to be packed to go, we didn't specify that the rice needed to be packed as well, and ended up with curry sans rice as leftovers. Worth trying once, not sure that this will go into my regular rotation.

Good variety of flavors!

Me and my wife went here and it was our first time. The frozen yogurt was good and there were some cool different flavors to try out. We were surprised how tasty it the frozen yogurt was and at how reasonable the price was. We will definitely go back to this place again.

This place is horribly organized-- the system sucks. I arrived and tried to sit at a table while waiting for a group of people to arrive. A server told that I couldn't do that and that you had to order your food at the cashier first. So that already makes the system awkward. My friends arrived, and asked the hostess if we could sit at a table. She said yes, so we did, only to have the server come try to make us leave the table. We ordered right away to try to appease them. The employee at the cashier was either just really unpleasant, which may have been because we "broke the rules" because the new hostess condoned us sitting down, but nonetheless, the whole thing was unprofessional. This aspect already was making the experience negative, although we wanted to like it. It was cool to watch the milkshakes being made as we waited in line, but to be honest, I couldn't help but notice that was place was kind of messy and dirty. Our table was sticky, and as we went to the washrooms, I noticed that the floors were slick and greasy, especially by the kitchen. It seemed unsafe. The bathrooms were dirty and awkward. One of the restrooms has a pocket door and somehow of my friends got walked in on, as she was using the space because the door didn't lock properly. As for the food, sides are not included with the burgers, so it's pretty expensive. Then the fries arrived first, way before the burgers. The burgers were decent enough when they arrived, but not overly special. The shakes were what everyone was excited about-- they look amazing. I didn't personally order one, but the few people that did noted that the toppings were good, but that the milkshake itself was relatively flavourless. We wanted to like this place, but the service wasn't great, which was frustrating because you have to tip upfront. The food was just okay and it was relatively expensive. For one person to have a burger, fries and a milkshake, it's like $30. Overall, the restaurant was quite dirty, especially for only being open less than a month. Unfortunately, I won't return.
Its okay for a chain.  Not a first choice but tolerable for company lunch meetings.

I was craving a salad, but I wanted a specific kind of salad.  A friend recommended we try Marathon.  I saw the menu and found a few salads that looked good.  Then, when we sat down, they handed us the "control freak" menu.  There are a few categories (burgers, salads, etc.).  In the salad section, there is a list of greens, veggies, and various ingredients/toppings/cheeses.  I was able to design the very salad I wanted: mixed greens, grilled veggies, feta cheese.  It was fabulous!  

I went back another day for a hearty, yummy burger.  The fries were fresh-cut potatoes.  

Marathon might become one of my favorite spots in Philly.  I'm a sucker for fresh, well-prepared food.  It need not be fancy.

Amazing food and good value for what you pay for. Very decent amount of food, I have leftovers for both of my two visits here. The dolsot bibimbap is really good. Perfect ambience for conversations, it's not too loud and the music is on point. Definitely will come back to try more dishes!

Visited New Hope on beautiful summer day. We walked past the restaurant it's going to be pretty busy. We were sat right away. Service was great. Quality of food was spectacular. The ahi tuna was so fresh and delicious really enjoyed the pineapple salsa that came with it. My husband ordered the halibut special and it also was tasty. The only disappointment was that the Moscow Mule drink was not served in proper glassware.  I did also think it was a bit pricey in comparison to the quantity of food served.  Would come back !

If you want great service without snobbery Nordstrom is the place to go!  I've gone here for everything from lingerie to shoes and everything in between.  Love their beauty department where they often have Nordstrom exclusives.  Lots of different product lines to choose from and they happily throw in lots of samples with your purchase.   Got my Sperry's here on sale 40% off and the saleswoman who helped me didn't treat me any less than someone buying Jimmy Choo.  PJ Salvage jammies on the 3rd floor!  Ladies and gents at the E-bar are lots of fun and the coffee is delicious.  Good food at the cafe as well.  Five stars all around!

I have been going here for a few years to get an oil change.  They generally try to upsell me on repairs, but I stick with just the oil change and take my car elsewhere should it be needed.  I recently took my vehicle in for a routine oil change as normal and when I got the car back, I was told I needed my tie rods replaced within the next month or so.  They also quoted me nearly $1000 for that and an alignment for the repair.  To his credit, the person who rung me up did tell me that was on the high side.  I left feeling unsafe in my car and seriously considering buying another vehicle as my car is already on the older side.  After some research and recommendations from friends, I decided to take my car to another repair shop who quoted me less than half of what Midas did for the same repair and an additional service at my request.  After I dropped my car off at the chosen repair shop, I got a call from the owner asking me why I thought my tie rods needed to be replaced.  He said they were not bad at all and that I didn't need an alignment, I only needed to have my tires rotated.  Here's the thing, I knew I was being up sold at Midas for repairs, but I had no idea it was so egregious.  I will not be bringing my car back here for any service as I do not feel I can trust them.

Went here for lunch a few days ago.. Wanted something different than the usual terminal fare so I gave Beck's a try. I wish I didn't . I ordered the Trainwreck and red beans and rice. Let's start with the good, the beans and rice were pretty good. Smoky and creamy with nicely cooked
 Beans. Lots of meat inclined to give the beans richness. A very good side dish. The sandwich was not so good . The sandwich has about 1000 ingredients so this next part is gonna sound stupid, it honestly tasted like nothing. It really had no flavor to speak of. Just very soggy
And greasy with too much onion. I think I might have ordered wrong . Not sure if I'd give this place another try , there are too many better options at the terminal for my
Money .

Awesome atmosphere and staff - true local people.  You can't get food with more soul than this for breakfast anywhere.  Shrimp grillades - unreal.  Garlic, huge shrimp, grits, tomatoes. 'nuff said.  Jambalaya omelette, shut your mouth.  2 kinds of sausage and huge shrimp.

I had a mixed experience here:

Donut: hubs and I agreed that this was one of the best donuts we have ever had. So soft. So good.

Everything bagel with jalapeño salsa cream cheese: the cream cheese was really tasty, not too spicy, and a generous amount. My bagel was a little tough but was generously coated

Iced coffee : it did the trick but wasn't special

One area they can really improve on is the ordering system. They should calls names or order numbers. Calling only what was ordered led to much confusion on the shop
Good boba and milk teas.  My wife loves their beef stew,
Great value! Very pleasant place to go. They remodeled about 3 months ago. Consistently give great massages.

From the tamales to the margaritas, the food was amazing. Andy was awesome providing some first timers with amazing recommendations. He knew the menu from memory and even offered some churros and a worry wort thingy. Awesome restaurant!

This is a local massage-only center.  I've been to the center about 6 times in the last three years.  Some of their massages are way more affordable than other places in the city.

Starting with the PROS:
Affordability (however they have raised prices on their shorter massages, but their longer and combo massages are a good deal)

Flexibility of hours and ease of getting an appointment (you can call and always get an appointment same day) - great for walk-ins.  The quality of the massages are pretty much on par with others I've received at other places in the city.

Variety - you can get any kind of combo package that includes deep tissue, swedish, hot stone, foot reflexology - or one that includes only one of them or all of them.

Ending with the CONS:
If you're not a local it might be hard to find, it's above the Penn Herb store on the 2nd floor, entrance is on Green Street -

Just a warning, this place is not super modern-y spa - It's basic.  The ambience isn't the most calming or serene... it's got a bit of a hippy- trippy - eclectic vibe with crazy wall colors.  The space and rooms are pretty dated - bare-bones... The place could stand to get a few renovations.

The place as it reads is a Center and NOT a spa, so don't expect bathrobes or slippers, or hair ties.  The massage rooms and sheets are clean, but also, clearly old  (the sheets on all my visits had clearly been washed and used alot, they were pilled).

The rooms could also stand to be just a little bit darker and a little less noisy... because of its location, it is to be expected you'll hear traffic noise here and there (and depending on when you're getting your massage)

If you're looking to get a lot of massages and are worried about cost, this place is definitely for you.  If you could care less about decor and ambience and prefer a basic, no-frills experience - this place is also for you.

Had the lamb palau. It was extremely bland, not like the ones I've had in Afghanistan. I tried to add salt in the flavor, but it didn't help. I also ordered the garlic naan and I couldn't taste the garlic at all. I probably wouldn't go back

There is no other way to say it: Odie is fantastic.  It is so difficult to find a mechanic you can trust, and you can really trust Odie: he doesn't upsell, he won't swindle, he'll tell you the truth and perform the work well and at a reasonable price.  A real stand-up guy: I cannot recommend him enough.

When I moved to New Orleans finding a new nail salon was one of my top priorities. I had been going to the same nail tech for many, many years so I was worried I would have to try out a few places to find the right person. That kind of trust isn't easy to come by so I was a little worried about finding a new salon.

I booked a mani pedi on a Sunay afternoon with Emily. She was fantastic, very fun and talkative!! I've come back to Buff regularly for my mani pedis and a couple of blow outs too. When Emily wasn't working one day I booked my appointments with Whitney and she was also awesome. She was very particular and I really like that, she took her time and made sure everything was just perfect. On NYE I had a blow out by Jessie and she's awesome and a total sweetheart. I was a little worried about getting my hair done in the afternoon since it was going to be a long day but I had nothing to worry about. Even with the rain outside most of the day, my hair still looked fantastic and held up all night!

I love Buff! The staff are terrific and friendly and want you to enjoy your treatments to the fullest. The space is beautiful, clean and modern without being too cold. Happy to call Buff home :-)

TCM has been such a wonderful find!  My neighbor recommended it to me when I was pregnant and I am so glad that she did.  After giving birth to my first baby, I knew I needed to get out and meet new moms.  The New Moms Group was FABULOUS!  The space is so warm and inviting- you walk through the front door and forget you are off of a busy street in Oakland.  It can be so overwhelming as a first time mom to navigate everything from leaving the house, nursing, sleep!, tummy time, baby sign language etc.  I felt that each time I arrived at TCB I was greeted with open arms regardless of my current state or appearance.  They always had coffee brewing and comfy chairs waiting for everyone.  No question, no concern was off limits and I always felt comfortable sharing all my personal struggles.  Once my son was a bit older and I was cleared to workout I also took the Yoga Series.  Not only was there a wonderful yoga instructor, but also Renee (a TCB employee) always there ready and willing to hold your baby if he/she started fussing during class.  There were many times babies would cry or need to eat and there was no judgement.  Everyone was supportive of the effort made to get out and do something for ourselves and helped make the experience as wonderful as possible.  I couldnt imagine my first 3 months as a new mom without TCB. Now that my son is 6 months old I am looking forward to the "older baby" seminars and workshops- sign, starting solids, etc.

I didn't eat here but just stopped in for some drinks.  Nice outdoor area that is perfect for people watching on south street.  the beer list is shockingly good for a place that doesn't have a real reputation in the craft beer community.  

The service was a little subpar.  I think we may have actually had a barback/bus boy as our server which wasn't a big deal given that we just wanted a drink and a place to sit outside for a while.  Since its on South St. it is going to get a mixed crowd but that's part of the appeal.  

I don't think i'd go in the winter and sit inside but when the weather is nice and you want to check out the happenings on south st. its a good place to sit outside and grab a drink.

A perennial favorite that any visitor to STL should place on their do not miss list.  We go to Ted Drewes several times a year and have never been disapppointed.
