This is the best frozen custard in the state - and maybe the country.  Although it may seem boring, the basic hot fudge sundae is my favorite.  My wife and daughter are Turtles all the way.  I would say no matter what you order you will love it.

Don't miss it and make the extra drive if you want the most delicious creamy treat.

Dragged my hubby here since I've never been on a real steamboat.  We did the evening dinner cruise and it was great!  Captain gave us a tour  around  the engine room and also learned a lot about the "real"  steamed powered boat versus other.  It is truly impressive and historical to see. Dinner is buffet style, I thought it was good (we're from Vegas.... enough said ) , the pork loin stood out the most to us ;)  definitely would recommend taking a cruise on the Natchez!

I've lived with in walking distance of this mall off and on since 2008 and the changes they've made are not for the better. They got rid of the ice rink and the movie theatre and have added a Golds Gym, a Home Depot and now a Wal-Mart (which replaced Zellers). I don't like the Home Depot being here because if you have to walk from Wal-Mart to the mall you're forced outside and at times you almost have to walk on the road because they are delivery trucks at the Home Depot moving items. It's the oddest place to stick a Home Depot imo.

Like others have said there isn't much reason to come here. There's a used music/ movie store and no book store at all so that cuts out a lot of people right there. Here's what the mall looks like on an average day. Morning: Old people. Lunch: High School kids and old people leaving. Evening: Mixed bag of kids and 30 something's trying to figure out why they're there. It's the mall of 'newly weds and nearly deads'... as they say. If you want to shop just take the extra 15 minutes and go to WEM.

I highly recommended the burger or a Stromboli, both of which are huge. Great curly steak fries too. Service is usually a little slow but a comfortable atmosphere and some table games. Prices are very reasonable and a relatively wide variety of items on the menu. As a local, it's one of the usual places we go when we go out s opposed to the chain restaurants near the mall.

i do not mind paying "high dollar" for top notch food, but almost 60.00 for what I had received, NEVER AGAIN!!!!!  The cake slices were so small, they didn't even stand up in the box. They were also dry. If a shop is going to have teenagers work there, they need to know how to cut a slice of cake.  One cookie for almost 4.00!  REALLY?  The search is still on for a great slice of cake!!!

Ended up having dinner here last Friday. Didn't think we could get a table without making a reservation, but fortunately they were not that busy that evening. Talk about food presentation, as the wife put it 'too pretty to eat". I was a bit skeptical at first after seeing the menu listing dishes with way too many ingredients. But it turned out great for the most part. Started with 3 small appetizers, shrimp corn dog, deviled eggs, and some fruit warp in bacon. They were all ok but the deviled eggs stood out quite well. They mixed the yolk I think with some pesto which made it green and gave it a different flavor to your typical deviled eggs. The wifey had the veggie plate which according to her is excellent while I had the short ribs. The ribs were tender and flavorful and the roasted veggies and mash potato made excellent sides. But my favorite part of my entree was the potato chip tube filled with mash potato, that was just awesome. They could put that in their menu as appetizer and I'd order it. Didn't care much for the other sauces and oils and dressing on my plate, the meat and veggies by themselves were good. For dessert, we chose the cheesecake in a jar. It's no junior's cheesecake but its still good and the ice cream on the side was quite tasty and the plate presentation was quite clever. Overall, it was an excellent dining experience, service was excellent, food taste great, food presentation was excellent, and price was pretty reasonable.
Not much to say other than its the BEST. PIZZA. YOU. WILL. EVER. HAVE. That brick oven sends it over the top! Awesome music selection too!

Needed an old Takemine repaired after some fret damage...Thanks Jeff for doing a great job with my AE--you turned the job around in less than a couple of hours with an honest and professional up front--will certainly bring business back to you guys for sure! You guys rock Corner Music!
Love the studio, love the class, the entrance from the garbage alley is a deal breaker
Michelle is the greatest person ever. Ask for her. Michelle make that youtube channel. Thanks for making our trip enjoyable.

Awesome shakes, at least the one I had.  Lots of beers on tap.  Tasty burgers, although I felt that they were smaller than I was expecting, given normal restaurant fare.  The two we tried were both excellent, and I think the [many] other choices are likely to be the same.  Additionally, it is not the most clear thing, but no sides are included with your burger, so we ordered a couple of appetizers, as I thought that was what I was reading on the menu.  I approved of the fried pickles, but I was less impressed with the loaded fries and pretzels; loaded fries would have been better served with a description of their load, I wasn't expecting pulled pork (and it was quite substantial chunks as well), which I felt took away from the dish, and the pretzels were pretzel "puffs" and not quite my style, definitely not a traditional pub pretzel appetizer.  As mentioned, fried pickles get a plus from me, they were done disc style and came with a nice dipping sauce.  Finally, the aesthetic is... 70s/80s kitchen with quaint jar glasses and flower containers (at least in the second floor).  I found the faux kitsch annoying, but maybe it will click with you.  Not enough to ruin the experience, but enough to draw a snide comment or two.  Finally, the restrooms, at least in the first floor, have the sink outside of the actual room with the commode, which I found pretty unsanitary.  At least the dirty hands travel time wasn't too far, but how many people will just not wash or touch something? Yuck!

Really digging this plaza that they're building around Miniso - lots of Asian goodness next to each other and plenty of parking.

Miniso is a cute, bright store that was established in Japan, but the majority of its products are Chinese. (If you look them up, they're actually described as a "Chinese low-cost retailer" headquartered in China) There are lots of things to look at - think similar to an Asian dollar store. You'll likely find lots of cute things from purses/make up to stationery and kitchenware. Pricing is ok - I saw things between $3 and $20 ish (for some of the lamps and headphones.)

It's fun to walk around, and prices are a bit cheaper than a similar, bigger store in WEM.

This place might serve the BEST Indian food I have ever had in America! We had the Bollywood dosa, railway cutlet, idli vada sambar n utthapam! Everything we tried exceeded our expectations by tenfolds. The flavors were so authentic that it reminds you of food in India. The place is small and quaint... very much a hole in the wall place. Will definitely return to try more amazing dishes!!!!!!

Off the charts! Superior flavors, hearty portion sizes, creative menu, hip vibe. Allergen indicators on menu would be my only suggestion! Erin, our waitress, was visibly annoyed both times I've visited for having to field my inquiries (celiac, not lifestyle choice). But the warmth and hospitality of the owner and other staff more than made up for her! Amazing addition to Boise and we love that it's off the beaten path.

I wanted to get the bbq shrimp, but they come fully dressed, and i'm not a fan of having to work for my meal, so didnt go that route. Glad I didnt, especially since my friend got them and he had to wear a bib, sucka! had the shrimp and grits instead and they were the best ever. 

the atmosphere is a little too stuffy yet has a bit of a diner feel...so thats not my fave, but i'd go back for the shrimp for sure!

So so amazed with this place! Jenna does such a good job with the açai sorbet base under all of the toppings. I got my bowl, took a half hour car ride in 80 degree heat and it didn't melt! The granola had a sweet brown sugar note in it which made it even more yummy. Definitely going back and recommending to all of my friends!

Service was mediocre. Not at all impressive. Drinks were weak. Food was ok. Not exactly the best place for food in NOLA when there are so many other options around. And it's on Burboun Street which sucks. Burboun Street smells like piss and puke. It's disgusting. I would not go back to this spot.

yesss sirrr -- the best place to stay in Santa Barbara period!  If you've stayed at Four Seasons in Charlestown, Nevis or Four Season Maui, Hawaii or W hotel, San Francisco or St. Francis, San Francisco or Venetian, Las Vegas this place dominates it. 

a mini fridge, cable tv, mirrors in every wall of the room (including the bathroom), and complimentary wireless internet -- enough said.  lock it up!

I won a meal for two to India House on the radio. Cool! India House refused to honor their agreement. Not cool! So, we didn't eat there. I would say no meal + rude owner = no taste = negative review, n'est-ce pas? It is interesting to note that Bucatini, two doors up, was packed. How many guests do you suppose were in India House. Not one! Zero. Zilch. Completely empty. Not having any customers at all on a warm, busy Wednesday evening is another type of review in itself. So if you'd like some curry, perhaps you'd best stroll across State Street to Himalaya.

Not 24/7. Found that out the hard way at 3a.m.

Can't wait to try it when it's open.

Hopefully the ice cream machine works too.
I loved the Benton Park sandwich as well as the "daddy-Combo-o"! They were both amazing. I was lucky enough to eat both since my boyfriend and I split each sandwich. Go try this place!

This place surprised me. I wasn't expecting to like it so much. I've never had thin cat fish, it was so good! And the hush puppies were so delicious! The people there were so friendly and you get free ice cream cones! They put a lot of cheese on the cheese burgers, which is amazing. I really feel you get your money's worth here. We came here two times on our vacation.
Such a great local place! Never get tired of going here. Never too long of a wait, food is sooo good. Cuban sandwich is my favorite!

I went here in June (hottest day of the summer) for my boyfriend's birthday  with no reservations.  We were coming down from NYC and initially were going to go somewhere else.  Well the rental car fell through and we lucked out with finding this place.  From the train station it was maybe a 10 minute walk. to the location.  Clean and VERY professional but welcoming us as newcomers and first time shooters.  We took the class and what impressed me what that another guy was sitting in the class and they asked him if he had been drinking and he said no, he was just tired from his trip.  Nope sorry guy...they asked him to come back tomorrow in the nicest way and told him that they can't even offer him the class if he wasn't alert or feeling well.  I was astounded and relieved that they choose safety of not just the guy but of us as well rather than just make a sale on a lesson or range time.

I learned how to hold a gun and while I was nervous, our trainer Mike was awesome!  He took time explaining safety and how to shoot to me over and over again.  When I finally hit the range and by the time my second shot went off I was completely confident and moved from a 9mm to an AK-47!  Now the bigger the gun the bigger the kick back and it is really hard to hit your target especially if you are new to shooting but I got 2 bulls eye and I was happy.  They showed us guns and explained them all and since we took 2 lessons and brought extra ammo the owner was nice enough to throw in the rental of the AK-47 in free.

The only negative thing I can say about them was they recommended Pat's or Gino's for Philly cheese steaks and they both sucked!

I will recommend on a separate note to bring a change of clothes and wet wipes which we did.  It was super hot that day and after sweating and all that gun powder on us we hit the bathroom and cleaned up.  Made a huge difference.

We were craving good Italian and happened to be walking past here. Outside was cute and so was the inside (if you like dark, rusticky Italian style) and it was PACKED. Must be good right? No it wasn't even decent. First, our waitress took forever to bring our drinks and consistently kept us waiting as she flirted with the old man two tables over. The bread they bring tastes like the garlic bread you buy at the grocery store from the frozen section and heat up. We ordered the Chicken with Stuffed Shells and Shrimp Mediterranean. The chicken was inedible because it was so dry. The shrimp Mediterranean had an OKAY sauce (you could probably make better at home) but the shrimp was also inedible. It tasted like it had been simply boiled for WAY too long (super firm) and just thrown in without any kind of saute or seasoning. These meals were awful... Especially considering they were $14 and $13!!! And the portions were TINY TINY, not that we wanted more. We both ate the pasta portions and left the chicken and shrimp on the plate, but our server didn't notice. We will never be coming back. Please don't even bother you'd be better off going to Olive Garden for better food 100x and better prices/portions. ( I don't normally write bad reviews but this was by far the most disappointing "Italian" place I've ever been to)

BBQ shrimp, two nights in a row.  Yes, it's that good.  The pork belly fig/spinach appetizer is amazing.  Our first night, we walked in at 9:30pm and were surprised that they were no longer seating at tables, as they close at 10pm.  We were served at the bar, where it was gracially explained, most fine dining restaurants in the FQ close by 10pm.  The reason is legitimate as "nothing good walks in after 10pm".  If you were hungry and wanted their shrimp, you shoulda gotten there by 6.  I couldn't agree more.  Lots of drinking happening in the FQ, and we were just grateful that they seated and served us at the bar.  Came back the next day for a proper sit down dinner and we were not dissappointed.

I had been wanting to come here for some time now..after having such a nice experience at their old location ('A Peace of Sole' near 4th and South). The hubby and I finally made it out on a Saturday nite and found the restaurant to be busy but not crowded. It was warm for the end of winter (75 degrees that day) and the windows were opened to allow a slight breeze to blow. It was lovely. 

We started with the seafood salad and it was a very "healthy" serving. That, along with the delish buttered, garlic and oldbay rolls they serve could have been a meal by itself..Tri color rotini pasta, shrimp and imitation crab, celery and seasonings mixed with a creamy parmesan dressing. Lemme tell ya, it was the bee's knees!

Then onto dinner...I was undecided between the fried whiting and the stuffed turkey chops (spinach, cheese, roasted red peppers, mushroom gravy) so I convinced the dude to order the turkey chops so I could sample both..Yeah, greedy I know- so what!

We couldn't have been happier with the meal. Both came accompanied by two sides: corn, roasted potatoes, sauteed broccoli, orange rice. I think you could get mac-n-cheese or collards for an additional cost but we didn't order either this time. I was on the fence about ordering the cherry iced tea but it was on point. 

The meal came to about $40 - not too shabby, eh? With our $25 Restaurant.com gift certificate, we only had to pay $15 + tip, right??? WRONG! Little did we know that they no longer accepted Restaurant.com gift certs and when we explained this to our server, she pointed to a sign that was 8 1/2 x 11 (Landscape view) on a podium in the corner that read "We no longer accept Restaurant.com coupons". Are you serious?? I came here to eat not read little posters so I surely didn't notice that throughout the entire dinner. The hubby didn't either because the big screen TV's were blasting the NCAA game and he barely paid ME any attention, so the sign didn't stand a chance!

Al in all, the server gave us a 20% discount on the bill (not a lot of help when you expect to pay $15). That was the best she could do but you'd best believe that I contacted Restaurant.com as soon as I got home and got a replacement  cert. According to Sole II Soul, they cancelled their contract with Restaurant.com but the website continues to sell their certificates.. So BUYER BEWARE!!

All in all, I had a good time. Yeah, I left with the figurative "bad taste in my mouth". Even though they could've had better signage or more notice before we ordered AND devoured such a delicious, savory meal that we were actually going to have to pay for it - the service, food and atmosphere couldn't be beat. I'll be back!

I've been going to La Colombe forever, so this review is long overdue.  I got to know all of the baristas there because I spent nearly every day there, working on my grad thesis.  They're pretty awesome because they usually know what I'm going to have before I get to the front of the line.

Their coffee is outstanding and somewhat addictive, to the point that if I'm out of town I refuse to drink coffee.  It has a really rich flavor, and they brew it to perfection.  As someone noted earlier, their lattes can be on the lukewarm side, so if you like things piping hot, tell them to make it "extra hot" and they're more than happy to oblige.

Although people find their lack of menu intimidating, the baristas are more than happy to tell you what they have available.  Basically, it's anything coffee-related, but don't ask for flavors or crazy milk.  They don't have it.  They have bittersweet molten chocolate that they use to make hot cocoa and mochas-- yum!  They usually have a great selection of pastries and goodies-- try the tarts or a croissant; they are all really delicious.

One of the drawbacks of the place is that they don't have wifi or a ton of electrical outlets for computers.  That is a blessing in disguise for me, because I get very distracted by procrastinating on the web, so I purposely go there to work because I know I'll sit there and write rather than checking my email every few minutes.  It's not conducive for everyone's style of working, however.

I've been here more than ten times over the course of my time in Tucson as an undergrad - and it's been consistently phenomenal. The food is great and the atmosphere is always friendly. 

Granted it's not a 5-star restaurant - but it's less pretentious and better than that. If nothing else, the service is impeccable. The pasta is generally cooked to perfection and the Caruso's special sauce is OFF THE HOOK. Sitting outside is a must, as long as it's warm enough in Tucson :-)

Order the "Caruso's Special" with meat sauce and you won't regret it.
Plenty of space by the bar to wait for our table. Great service and friendly staff. Food was very good. Although my 1 1 1 appetizer was room temp. Still I'll be back!
Excellent tacos.  I had three: marinated pork, chicken, and chorizo.  All great.  Will definitely return.

Slightly disappointed. The bacon used on my grilled cheese looked to be the precooked bacon you buy in the packs at the grocery. The Mac & cheese was cool at best not hot. Ordered cheese fries and barely enough to share. Sandwiches were good. Might come back to try a signature one. I had the big cheesy, my daughter an original and my husband had a crawgator. We did take home leftover sandwiches bc they are big!
Sushi Minato is AMAZING! I haven't had a roll I didn't like there. My friends and I have pretty much stopped going any place else! Wonderful!

This place is amazing, we walked in at 630 on a Friday night with decent weather, and none of the pro sports teams in town. Somehow snagged a table. The staff hostile was polite, and said give me a minute and I'll get you seated. She did just that. 

The ambiance is amazing, beautiful place, nice decorated with a modern feel. Comfortable seating. Good lighting.

Waiter(Brian) was awesome, he knew the drinks, he knew the menu.

Thw drinks came quickly, and were perfectly made. ( it was busy)

Sushi....was....amazing...
It came quickly, was plated nicely, and the fish was beatifilly cut, and tasted like it was swimming this morning.

We had quite the feast sampling several of the menu options. Sushi, sashimi, rolls, blah blah blah. It's great 
You won't regret coming here.

I do recommend getting a reservation, we lucked out.

It's not cheap, but you should already know that by the $$$$ on the main Paige for reviews....very worth it by any standard.

Berwyn Veterinary Center provides excellent and affordable service for your pets, new and old!  My boyfriend and I just adopted a juvenile cat from the SPCA, and we were required to take the cat for an initial visit and shots.  We were able to schedule a complimentary appointment (thank you!!!) within 7 days, and it was very accessible from our place near Paoli.  

Upon arriving, I was greeted by two friendly staff persons and an office cat.  The staff members made sure there was a clear room for our kitten, the other provided us with the appropriate paperwork.  Upon completion, Dr. Whipple (what a name-- almost as good as Doolittle!) gave a quick, thorough examination and provided us with some resources as new pet owners.  After two shots and some good advice, the total bill was about $50.  

We were very happy with the accessibility of the office, the office's ability to accommodate us on short notice (though more time slots would have been nicer), and the very friendly staff.

Note: This is a review of the Barnes-Jewish Hospital South cafeteria. I have heard the North cafeteria is not nearly as good, but I can't say from first-hand experience. 

Hospitals are notorious for their lack of culinary delights, but this one actually does fairly well. We have been eating 2-3 meals a day here this week and still aren't considering going out for food. The offerings run the gamut from "LivingWell" dishes such as honey mustard chicken and tilapia almondine to fresh salads (salad bar and pre-prepared) to comfort foods like mac & cheese and meatballs. There are a variety of Italian offerings every day, plus sushi, sandwiches, and a grill with hamburger/chicken sandwich/grilled cheese type items with fries and onions rings. The Exhibition area has really interesting restaurant-quality dishes during the week, like a great vindaloo sweet potato and rice dish, so make sure to check that out. I also highly recommend the corn muffins, as they are the best I've ever had -- sweet without being too sweet and without losing that essential "corniness." And the slush machine beats any convenience store Slurpee, hands down. 

I would say that the prices are reasonable. They aren't dirt cheap, but they are fair given the relatively high quality and the convenience. I would, however, recommend you buy any bottled water in the vending machines across the hall because it's 39 cents cheaper there. Overall the Barnes South cafeteria offers a nearby place to enjoy a quick meal in a clean dining room. Nobody wants to spend their time waiting around in a hospital, but it's nice that there's a good place to relax, refuel, and enjoy some creature comforts if you have to be there.
Awesome place; very hospitable hosts. A must visit.

I can find myself here at least once a week even in the summer for their soft tofu or soondubu. I brought my boyfriend here for his first soondubu, and he's now hooked. They have a scale on how spicy you like your tofu to be (1-nonspicy to 5-very spicy), and the portions are generous. I'm always walking out of the door with a full and satisfied tummy. 
After ordering they serve you five side dishes, that compliment the meal perfectly. Instead of trying to flag your server down, there is a button on the table that you ring if you need them. They also bring you a pitcher of water or tea--depending on which on you have--so you don't have to constantly ask for refills. Although I never tried the Korean pancake yet, I always want to order it because it looks so yummy, and its huge. 
Parking is available on the side (where the door is), and on the street, even arriving around peak dinner time on a Saturday, parking was not a problem.
This is my favorite Korean restaurant in Philly, and I HIGHLY recommend it.

Absolutly horrible experience. Took my husbands pickup truck there (it was close to home)and they scraped the paint off from around the windshield. I took it back when I got it home and saw it, he paid the body shop next door to fix that. Then when the 1st good rain came it leaked so bad that the floor was flooded. Took it back again he put some sealant on. Leaked again as badly the next rain. Took it back about 3 more times and he could not repair it correctly, Over 2 years later and the truck has to be parked on a slope to keep the water out every time it rains. This is NOT customer service!

Cool, welcoming atmosphere with nice-feeling wooden interior. Quality coffee, king cakes (complete with plastic babies!), and "slightly more than snack" food. Great for plopping down for a solid cup of coffee or light meal.
This man saved my life.  Seriously.   I've been HIV+ for 20+ years and despite it all he's kept me going.  Please give Mark a chance, he'll change your life!

We were looking for somewhere new to eat this evening and I happened to remember seeing the sign for this place opening last week. We used to enjoy the restaurant that was in this building before (Five & Diner) so decided to give this new restaurant a try.

Little, well nothing, has changed about the interior of the place. It's still 1950's kitsch diner although the name and menu would be more appropriate to something country or rustic. I'm not sure if the owners just didn't have the money or time to makeover the decor but it certainly is a mismatch. They've even kept the 1950's and early 1960's jukebox pop music which seems strange. 

We decided to order from their  all day breakfast menu. Michael chose an omelet with potatoes and English muffin while I chose the Buttermilk hoecakes (although they are actually pancakes) with a side of bacon. 

The food was mediocre. Michael's omelet was barely warm and the cheese he asked for had just been melted over the top then allowed to sit so long it had firmed up again and congealed. Yes, service was slow and undoubtedly that part of the order was sitting in the window. His potatoes were OK although nothing particularly noteworthy. 

On my end the pancakes were a bit bland. Since I am currently dieting I decided to forgo the syrup and just use a little butter. While they were not inedible by any means they just didn't seem to be quite worth the hefty $6.95 price tag for three pancakes alone. The bacon, however, was tasty and high quality and prepared just as I had ordered it. 

The people seem genuinely friendly for the most part. Our server was a very nice older lady although I don't think waiting tables is really the career for her. While pleasant, she was rather inefficient and prone to forgetting simple things. It's also rude of a server to stand over the patron while they are filling out the charge slip and calculating the tip. 

This is one of those restaurants that seems just on the edge. With a little more attention to the food, some makeover in the decor, and a bit more efficiency in the front of the house and the kitchen it could succeed. However, without those things I'm not sure of the longevity of this business. Normally, in our neighborhood a new opening means a fairly full house for at least a few weeks. When we were there only three other tables were in use and half the dining room was closed. 

We'll probably try it again in a month or so (if they're still open) to see if they've made any changes or progress.

Great people, super fast service & the food is amazing! 
Homemade potato-bacon soup and homemade bread on a stellar sandwich. 
This cafe is in the heart of Historic Downtown Plant City and the setting is pure delight. 
Genuinely the best lunch I've had in a very long time. 
If you choose this place, you won't be sorry, I guarantee.  
Can you tell I enjoyed it?! Go there!

What a great stadium!  The seats are great, even the cheaper ones, and the place is just beautiful.  Super place to root, root, root for the Phillies.  Parts of CBP remind me of the boardwalk, with all the food stands and merch vendors.  What fun!  Clean, pretty (real grass, ivy, flowers!)--a place that's fun to go to whether the Phillies win or lose--though it's obviously better when they win.

We ate dinner here- it was pretty empty when we arrived but was packed by the time we left (we eat early with the two small kids). It was quite a walk from our hotel, but worth it. The building in general and restaurant decor is a bit old/dated, as were the wait staff uniforms/dress code. It is small, but cozy, no complaints. We ordered: fried chicken with red beans/rice/mac'n'cheese, crowder peas/okra/rice with smoked sausage, and crawfish etouffee. The boys loved the chicken, but to the adults it was borderline too salty. The crawfish etouffee was excellent- at the top other list of what we've had to date (and that includes multiple iterations of this dish). The crowder peas and okra were great by themselves and with the smoked sausage which was awesome. My mouth is watering just thinking about it again. The kids' mac and cheese was also great ( although stingy small portion) - they put some kind of a crumb on it which is nice. Cornbread was crumbly and came with ample butter - a definite must. The wait staff were nice, good service. All in all a solid meal. I saw another table order the bread pudding and it looked good- would definitely give it a try on a second visit.

Great everything, greeting, service, attention to detail. Sound system is zoned so when I asked to have music turned down so I could participate in conversation it was no problem.  Finally smart sound!  Still noisy but manageable.

Everything is awesome here, I just wish I could take this place back to CT with me!  Donuts are the best I have ever eaten and I have been to all the country's best.  Today was the 4th, so I had their special donuts, but every donut is a crowd pleaser.

Bub's Cafe is a great place for breakfast or lunch. It's in walking distance and I go there frequently. However, I have been very disappointed with the host/hostess stand people my last two visits. I have put my name in on the wait list to sit outside to only have people working the host/hostess stand take people to a table when they initially walk up to put their name on the wait list instead of seating the people that were there first. Staff needs to look at their wait list and work it appropriately!!!!  If you don't watch host/hostess stand people you may not get seated!!!

Service was impeccable.  Wine list was great, but more importantly, fairly priced. It goes without saying that I got a fillet mignon. It was cooked perfectly and all of the side dishes were done very well. We ordered seared ahi tuna as an appetizer and it was one of the best pieces of fish I've had in a long time.  Pricey, but with it!

I pick Edley's over any BBQ place in Nashville. No it's not like Kansas and no it's not like Texas but it's to me the best Nashville offers on the BBQ side. Even though ribs ribs ribs the brisket is everything. A tips:  the brisket usually sells out after the 12 noon rush.
Sooo good. Food is awesome and really friendly people there. Garlic bread is great. mushroom etouffe is sooo good!!!

I'm speechless so I'll keep my review short and sweet...

Service, Food, Décor all amazing... My server was attentive and outgoing.  I ordered the Pork shank which was finger licking good; tender and seasoned to perfection.  If you enjoy phenomanel food, this is your place..

wanted to love this place as it is near our house. the food was overpriced with a $3 price tag on a ham biscuit. if it was amazing I would have no problem with the price, but it was a pre-made biscuit just slightly larger then a silver dollar with very small scrawny piece of ham and microwaved. At $5 I had a butternut squash/bacon egg pie (slice of Quiche) which was also on the small side but tasted good. In all I am sure this would be a good alternate coffee stop, but would not recommend if you are looking for food with that coffee.

If you judge this "music venue" by the bathrooms, music, and food--it is as clean as a whistle!  (It is NOT a restaurant!) I gave this place 5 stars because  1) the doorman accommodates you in any way, shape, or form. 2) the bar is long and can adequately serve lots of patrons simultaneously! , like 50+ easily (3) the music is very unique -- (like a zydeco style "buffalo soldier" rendition), and if there is a cover 100% of the money goes directly to the musicians 4) there is a BBQ place inside ON-SITE called blue oak BBQ.  

We had all these double and triple meat BBQ platters, but the ultimate was the "BBQ shrimp taco on a corn tortilla with shreds of pulled pork".   It was MY idea to get the $8 "appetizer", while my wife looked at me like I had just been left released from the mental institution.  I think I went to go wash my hands, as the two appetizers sat in the plate untouched being that my wife gave me a clear "you're going to eat that AND a BBQ platter!!!" Look, I just got back to eat that appetizer. When my wife exclaimed "that was really good". We should have just gotten 10 taco appetizers.  As the bbq portions were kinda small, and even though the BBQ was good, it was frequently cooked (down) with bel-peppers, onions, and tobacco.  Which made much of it as spicy. And reason/star #5) there is an outdoor attached hall with patio chairs, and music piped in through a set of Bose weatherproof speakers, so you don't skip a beat and smoke a cigarette and have some nice conversation.  The cool part is you don't really have the wind blowing inside every few minutes.

Bring you friends here from out-of-town and 
(use the streetcar for nostalgia and lack of DUI's), I promise you won't be disappointed.  You'll be the insider of ALL New Orleans...

Go ahead and be the celebrity host ambassador for the night.  You won't regret it!!!

Drive the short distance from downtown to the Englewood area for a great cup of coffee (or latte for me)! Bonus, they have almond milk for the non-dairy drinkers. Can't wait to come back and try a Cuban or Media Noche sandwich for lunch or one of the bagel breakfast sandwiches!
They really do have the best breakfast sandwich!! Everything is delicious and the staff is very friendly and helpful. This is the perfect place for a nice lunch date.

Went to Gusto last night after a two year gap to see if things had improved. Food was actually quite tasty and service was good. We had Ceasar salad, tasty but slightly wilted, pasta bolognese and eggplant parmigiana. The pasta was a pleasant surprise and the eggplant was tasty with a crispy crust. Overall a good experience, but wish they could do something to improve the dining ambience relative to the prices. They charge about 30% higher than the place appears it should. Personally I am ok with the prices but don't like the vibe.

I got my first piece at Golden Eagle in April. I am so happy with it! While this was my first piece here, it was my 2nd by Jason Bradshaw, who I met when he tattooed a block from my house in Isla Vista at Kustom Ink. 

Jason is my favorite and I am trust him so much I drove 600 miles round trip to have him do this piece! He has a way with figuring out when I mean when I am using all the wrong terms and coming up with something way better than anything I imagined. I believe his favorite styles to do are Japanese and Traditional. 

The staff was really nice, one guy even did a bunch of video for me! There is also some nice local color, like this retarded guy that hangs out at the shop! Bonus! I had such a great time I had to have Jason stop tattooing while I shook with laughter on the table a couple times.

The do piercing and have a pretty decent selection of jewelry, too. 

Cash only folks, they do have an atm and don't forget to tip your artist well. 

Check out the videos from my last piece on YouTube! 

http://www.youtube.com/user/MollyLovesUTube

If you want local!!!! Amazing night with great service and a menu that speaks for it self! I really recommend asking for a wine suggestion, Myles will not steer you wrong, nor will any thing from the kitchen! Great food, great drink, great people, means great night! Thank you Farmhaus!!!

Really a lovely place, very solid.  Great atmosphere down near Jackson Square with exposed brick. Service is attentive and helpful.  Menu is classic/traditional New Orleans cuisine.  We went for lunch and I had the Satsuma salad which was tasty and the etouffe which was flavorful.  I didn't think the food was spectacular hence the 3 star rating but a great overall place for lunch in that area.

We didn't go, but the bar in the back was really cozy and looked like a classy place for a cocktail or beverage.

If you have never been to a John Besh restaurant, there is no easier way to be introduced than to spend an early evening at Luke's rightfully acclaimed happy hour. I have eaten my share of oysters (and part of yours) in my day, and a significant percentage of them have been consumed in Louisiana, which is only notable because I've never lived there. If you like your oysters plump, briny, ice cold, well-cleaned and grit free, this is the place to go. It's even better during Happy Hour because they are only $.75 each! I have eaten my way around NO twice last year, and these are my unchallenged winners for best oysters on both visits, even though I ate at several traditional oyster houses each time. If that were not enough, they also offer fried oysters for $1 each during HH, and they are the best I have ever eaten, any time, anywhere. We eventually tried most of the items on the HH menu, and they all exceeded expectations. The specialty cocktails are outstanding, even at full price, but they are a cocktail connoisseur's best value in a city known for impeccable cocktails.

If you are like me you want great service to make it a truly great dining experience. Nicholas was our waiter, and he gave that perfect blend of friendly service and attention to detail that makes a meal into a perfect evening. He's worth asking for.

Just as good as the big events for half the price. It is quite a bit out there unless you live in north Tampa. It took us about an hour and half to get there from Pinellas county. However it isn't much different if you go to Hall O Scream or Orlando with I-4 traffic. From the parking lot it reminded me of a future type mad max tent city. With flames shooting over top the structures and all the yelling and music. Parking was a little tight for a truck as they try to squeeze in every inch. The houses were well built. I really enjoyed the Prison. The interactive aspect was fun. If you dare they give you a glow necklace that lets the performers know you are willing to participate. They will get a little pushy and separate you from your group . It's becomes a maze and the experience is all that much more fun. I recommend purchasing the fast passes. For a few dollars more it was well worth it. Even on a Wednesday night the lines were quite long. An with the long drive back it was nice to be able to do all the houses and enjoy the midway. Still arriving back home at a reasonable hour . Being a school night.  If you are tired of the price of the theme parks give it a try. I found it just as enjoyable with a small town feel.

I ride regularly and this was the best trail ride experience i have had in the area.  The staff was amazing and the horses well cared for and loved.  Went on a trail ride and loved every minute of it.  I highly recommend it for any level rider. Great treat for your children. I will be back.

Well, when I got there they were closed for lunch, and I just missed it by 10 minutes. I had walked 2 miles to get there but I didn't realize they closed after lunch. The manager told me that I could go to the bar because they had a limited menu there. So, I went to the bar top where I was ignored for about 5 minutes, the 2 bartenders didn't even make eye contact with me or even let me know that they would be with me in a minute. There was only 4 other people at the bar at the time. I was going to order the BBQ shrimp because I have heard rave reviews about them, but when I asked if they de-vein the shrimp the bartender told me know. Well, as I have mentioned before, this is really culinary 101 here folks, how many times have you heard a chef like Gordon Ramsay or Bobby Flay etc. tell people to de-vein those things because no one wants to eat their poop tract!! The bartender asked me if I liked crab cakes and I smiled and told hime that I loved them and that I was a bit of a connoisseur about them. Well, he told me that they had the best in town and that I wouldn't be disappointed. Well, he couldn't have been more wrong! Although they had a good amount of crab in them, they were one note and quite tasteless, I was really disappointed to say the least. I walked all that way for nothing.......guess maybe I might go back and try something else on the menu, I don't know yet.

LOVE this place! Very knowledgeable, professional, accommodating and fair. I had a loose aquamarine that I needed a setting for, and Noman knew exactly how to make it look fantastic. The jeweler did a phenomenal job setting the stone, and it turned out beautiful! I'm very happy with the whole experience!  If you're looking for something unique, or want to put your own personal touches on a piece this is the place to go.

First timer here. I am in town for a conference and decided to get my hairs cut. Checked yelp and decided on this place. I called to make an appointment and was able to get in that day. I was greeted as i walked in and offered an adult beverage of my choice. I chose an amber ale. Sat down for a few minutes as i was a bit early for my appointment. Eric was my barber and he called me and we began.  He sat me down in the chair and asked me what i was looking to be done with my hair. After that it was hot towel and shampoo time. Then back to the chair for the cut. Then back to the basin for a final rinse. Then back to the chair for the final styling and tips to maintain the cut. Eric was informative and very easy to talk to. Thanks again. If i am ever back in Nashville i will definitely go here again.

I have been here a few times over the years, their food is good, especially the matzoh ball soup.  The last time, however, I was extremely disappointed in my server. I order latkas and he asked if I wanted potato or veggie, I didn't know they had veggie so I asked which one he liked better; "Neither really, I don't eat deep fried foods, it all tastes gross."
Well, not only was I feeling like he was judging me, I was a server for years and I would never, ever, ever describe something on the menu as "gross" and they have quite a few deep fried foods. Clearly the establishment doesn't care how their employees present the restaurant to the public.

It seems lots of Yelpers have had problems with service here. I never have (Yes the waiter forgot our waters and we had to remind him, plus the busboy was a little too eager to clear our plates, but I wasn't in a hurry and it didn't bother me much) but I guess if you're in a rush or looking for an upscale, accomodating place, then you don't want to go here. 

Still, I LOVE taking people to this restaurant. They have such a HUGE selection of all kinds of asian foods (chinese, japanese, thai, noodles) that it's hard for someone not to find something to like. Also, the prices are awesome... comparable to the suburbs. And the food has always been delicious (by Chinese restaurant standards, nothing gourmet) - so it doesn't seem that the quantity has deterred the quality. 

Plus it's in a great location off the street, so its rarely filled up and it's close to the Ritz theatres, Old City, and all the historical areas of the city. 

I would definitely recommend this place if you're entertaining friends, entertaining picky eaters, entertaining people who don't want to overspend, or just having your own Chinese/Japanese/Thai takeout cravings but would rather sit somewhere.
Delicious food and excellent service! I tried their Pelua which is an arepa with shredded beef and cheese... You won't be disappointed!
Love the beef and snow pea. Delicious crab ragoon. Quick and friendly service. Close and convenient
Food was really good and the staff was great! LOVED the live performer tonight! So talented!! Definitely coming back

The facility was clean and I enjoyed working out here while I was in town for a few months. I would like to acknowledge Brittany for being an exceptional manager and doing the right thing! She went above and beyond to help rectify an important situation and deserves credit for having good business sense and treating customers fairly and appropriately. If she continues in this manner I have no doubt that she will excel in business. Planet Fitness and/or any other company should take note of her ability to do the right thing and treat clients appropriately!

I get breakfast and bagels from here just about every weekend. I love their everything bagels, best j e had in philly. Their pancakes are good, both special but hit the spot. Corn muffins are quite tasty and their blueberry muffins are good too, just a bit sweet for me. Service is always very good.

Visiting from Washington, DC and struggled to find good coffee on the beach. This place is it! Food is also fresh, tasty, and many options available for vegetarians and non-vegetarians alike. Service is friendly. Just wish we'd found it a little earlier in our trip (but we still came twice!)

I originally discovered So Fresh on Uber eats.  for months I refused to download the app (I know myself and I wanted to stay away from temptation).But I was at work and extremely hungry. I try my best to eat healthy and stay on track with a healthier lifestyle. I was absolutely addicted to So Fresh after my fist order. The food is always fresh and delicious the workers are extremely friendly. They give you a huge portion size (I usually get the salmon bowl) which is plenty! I wish there was one in Clearwater! But I'm sure I'll be back AGAIN this week.

Loved the vibe and music and the service was great. I ordered the salmon and it was excellent.  However, my boyfriend ordered the Noble Pig pizza and it was very soggy. Besides that, it was a great experience and we'd come back.

This is tied with In-n-out for my favorite burger of all time. I get the Village burger with Jasper Hill cheddar and a fried egg (over medium).  Tip: cut your burger in half and set the other half of the burger cut-side down on the plate while you eat the first half.  This will keep the bun from getting soggy from all the wonderful juices that will inevitably leak from the patty. 

Pairs well with the Fish House Punch or the local bottled root beer. 

I can't recommend the duck fat fries b/c they are simply too inconsistent. Sometimes they taste like they were cooked inside a duck (awesome) and sometimes they just taste like normal Five Guys fries (meh).  I also don't recommend the short ribs fries bc it's overkill when you're about to have an amazing VW burger.

This place is exactly as advertised: unique, healthy and delicious! 

I had the backyard bowl and this thing was epic! You get your week's worth of antioxidants in one mouthful!

It seems a little pricey on first look, but when you take into acct the ingredients and the amount you get (you can make two meals out of the large), the price is on par!

Parking is a bit of a pain, but this place is well worth the effort. 

I just wish they had a BYB in Austin!

PHF does a fine job serving the small community of Carpinteria and providing healthy, eco-friendly staples like bulk foods, vegetarian protein options (they stock Upton's Naturals - we've requested Field Roast loaves but are still waiting for them), and local & organic produce. 

PHF is also a great find for vacationers and visitors if they really do want to find the best smoothie on the Central Coast. Our family favorite is the Yo Blue. We also love that we can bring our own to-go ware for smoothies and the staff gladly obliges our request. 

We also go there to grind our own peanut butter and buy local pistachios as great gifts for hard-to-shop-for dads. Best of all is the friendly customer service. Now, if they were only open on Sundays...

This was my go-to salon when I was living in Nashville, and I miss Danielle so so much. It's a Redken salon and they do a great job of explaining their products and techniques. The products are pricey but I'm a total fan now! Seriously, all the girls are amazing, but when in doubt- Danielle! Cut, color, style, men's, anything!!!

In town from NYC to pick up my best friend's wedding dress from a nearby salon, we yelped for a local spot for lunch and decided to give #WAG a try. The whole menu looked so tasty it was hard to make a choice! We started with the hummus and pita. Serving was beyond generous, pita was nice and soft. I had the mama's breakfast sandwich, my friend ordered the avocado toast, and Mac and cheese for my 4 year old. Avocado toast looked great but was gone by the time I even finished cutting around the massive chicken breast hanging over the biscuit on my sandwich. The sandwich itself was amazing even if the serving size was absurd. The kids Mac and cheese was straight up boxed Kraft. I'm a mom, I know what I'm looking at! Sweet potato fries and waffle fries were good. If we lived nearby, we'd be regulars. They could do better with kid options though.

I stopped at the 7th Sun Brewery for a beer, and was enjoying it outside when I caught a whiff of BBQ. I discovered the delicious smells were coming from Eli's BBQ, just up the road, so I changed dinner plans and went to Eli's. Eli's is nothing fancy, just an old-time BBQ shop. There ARE a few picnic tables under the shade trees, but it's mostly carry out. The food is all BBQ, smoked in house...or rather in the big smoker in the yard.
Smoked pork, ribs, chicken, and a few sides is all that's on the menu, but it's all good. NOTE: They are only open TWO days a week, on Friday and Saturday afternoons, and they DO run out of food, so get there early to avoid disappointment!

"Woohoo! As good as it gets!"

I've been hearing good things about this place for awhile so I decided to take the trip down to check it out for myself, and I was NOT disappointed. I just use yelp for its goods and never write reviews myself but this place was THAT good that I opened up an account to make sure everyone knows how great this place is!

All the specialty rolls (Passyunk, Tuna Canopy, and Caterpillar) were all AMAZING and filling. My party and I decided to do family style, so we order a Hot Entrees and YOU MUST try the ribs. We didn't even have to ask for a knife because the meat was that tender and it literally melted in my mouth. 

I believe our waiter JOE was taking care of all the tables in the place,  along with the hostess but I never felt like I was waiting around for his service. His recommendations were on point, especially the LYCHEE CREME BRULE, which was the perfect end to our meal.

Looking for another reason to treat myself out, so I can go back! :)

This was a nice facility, the coaches and members were very welcoming. Zack was very attentive to everyone in the class and made sure everyone was on the same page as well as performing movements in a safe and correct manner. A great place for CrossFit! I was really satisfied with this gym. Thank you CrossFit Regulus!

We've eaten Thai food all over the world, including Thailand.  This place is fabulous!  The prices are right, the food is incredible and the service is excellent.  They add a flair of 'Mom and Pop" to everything.  I thought my taste buds were up to the 'Thai Hot' and they very politely schooled me to go for slightly less spicy, which I truly appreciated.  My birthday is this week and this is my first choice for birthday dinners.  Enjoy!
Still one of my favorite places in town. I am loving their current tea selection. Jasmine key lime. This place is a must.

Jaco is great! Everything I've tried there has always been excellent, including the juice! The staff is very friendly. I've never had a bad experience here. I introduce to all my friends and they all love it too!

Food is always amazing. Portions are large so bring your "A" game. Great farm fresh homestyle food Breakfast served all day.

Service is very accommodating and friendly. 

Tend to have long waits for weekend brunch but it is always worth it.

Cash only. ATM inside.

Decided to have lunch here after picking up dinner at Lazzaroli's.
Sat at the sidewalk tables as it was a beautiful sunny day.
Got a 12" thin crust w pep, onion, garlic and some sweet tea.
Between the hostess and the server they were engaging and friendly.  they boosted the experience from 4 to 5 stars.
The pizza was perfect, there is just no other description for it.  I'm not normally a big fan off thin crust, but just wasn't feeling like a heavy deep dish, so I tried it.  I've never had a thin crust this good.  It was cooked to perfection.  Wasn't burnt or under cooked.  It was just right with a great flavor and texture, and wasn't loaded with grease.  From the sauce, cheese, pep, onion and garlic; they all came together with a wonderful taste that made it hard not to eat the whole thing.
If I didn't love trying new places, I'd be back here every day...
Great Dealership ! No pressure sales and extremely accommodating. Adam is the man!! Service guys Theo and Bill are great too!!

Just ordered delivery from here for the first time; super impressed. Completely enjoyed talking to the lady who took my order! Chicken parmesan sub was amazing, and I will definitely be ordering again.

After I was introduced to Bevmo in LA, I started coming here whenever I was at home in SB. The staff are really nice and they even offer beer tastings on friday for a $1. It is cool because you can try 6 different kinds of beers and I have actually decided on getting a six pack of the one I had liked the most during those tastings. The selection is decent depending on what you are looking for. I will definitely be back. Thanks Bevmo!

I love this place, it makes me think of home and the italian market in south philly! There are great meats, pasta, wine, cheese, coffee, just about everything this italian needs. We even got some HI-larious shirts that say something like "body by gabagool". 

I will say it's PACKED in there, hopefully we'll think of going earlier in our trip and NOT on a weekend so we can enjoy it a bit more. Oddly, in philly, the italian market has amazing deals on meat, cheese, and veggies, it seems over priced here, but fine by me, i can have a little home on vacation!

My Husband and I had High Expectations of Old Standard Chicken. I assumed if you have a limited menu, you will prepare these Dishes Well.  Please train your waitress, Iced Tea needs Ice (this includes Refills) their restaurant was Out of Lemons.  There was No Sugar, Sweetener, Salt or Pepper on the Tables. All of the Above Issues are the Managements Fault. We wanted Mashed Potatoes but they were Out of this Item also, we were here at 11:30am and we were One of Two tables seated. So it is Not like they're so busy they ran out.  The 1/2 Chicken arrived and was Burnt, way overcooked, Chicken Breast was boneless and had Grill Marks on it under the Fried Breaded Chicken Skin. What's up with this? Did you buy Pre-grilled chicken and then Fry it??? Chicken Needs More Flavor, a Brine would really help plus a more seasoned Flour for the Breading.
I really wanted to Love this Place, But...........Too Many Amateur Mistakes

So glad we finally made it to Brixx's!  We started off with the hummus appetizer which featured three types hummus.  For our enter we enjoyed their Rustico and wood fired veggie pizzas. Very flavorful.  It took our children a little time to get use to this style of pizza but they eventually acquired a taste.  Friendly staff and contemporary atmosphere.

This is the neighborhood sandwich shop you've always dreamed of.  From BBQ & muffaletta to deli staples like the reuben & BLT, they knock each one out of the park.  No matter your taste, they have you covered.

Pros:
- Local Beer
- Local Soda
- Al Fresco dining
- Great staff
- Solid house-made sauces
- Balanced meat / filling / bread ratios
- Live blues Thursday nights!

Cons:
- Seating can be problematic around lunchtime
- Generally only open for lunch (other than Thursdays)

We just moved to the neighborhood and everyone we've taken there has given the BCD a solid 5 stars.  Do yourself a favor.

WORST MCDONALDS EVER!! Wait times in drive thru are up to 15 sometimes 20 Minutes Iv been short changed 3 times now by the same older Philippine lady that receives payments at first window. And then when you call her out on it she just stares at the screen and pretends to be sorry I'm under the influence that this is her scam. Also could explain the long wait times. My kid doesn't like mustard on his burger and the other one doesn't like lettuce I ask for this every time and have received maybe once correct outta the dozen times Iv been. I live in the area so I enjoy my coffee before work 15 min for an incorrect coffee order gets old fast. I will be traveling to the Weber greens McDonald's from now on. I only gave them one star because it wouldn't let me give zero.
Amazing food!!!!  Everything from the chutneys, palak paneer, Channa masala, and tandoori player... it's all unreal!
This is my favorite coffee shop, so cute and great atmosphere. I'd definitely recommend you check this place out. The lavender latte is amazing by the way.

I have eaten at Sylvia's three times and I have been disappointed every time. I remeber my mom maaking salmon croquettes when I was a kid, so I was excited to see them on the menu at Sylvia's. But these were dried clumps of bread filler with a hint of fishy tasting salmon, and a side of  some sort of okra slime.
 The second time I ate there I decided to go in a different direction, so I ordered the ribs. These were worse than the salmon croquettes.  The ribs were huge and plentiful but they were really tough and fatty,  and slathered ina a sweet but odd tasting bbq sauce. I ate one and brought the rest home to my dog who gave them a five star rating. 
 So the third time I had tilapia, it, was better than the salmon or the ribs but still very mediocre.  
Why do I keep going back to a place that I don't like? Well I do some work there occasionally, contract work not an employee,  and they are nice enough to feed me. Unfortunately everything I have tried has been pretty bad.  I will be working there again soon and I will continue to try different items until I find something decent. I can't recommend this place, I eat for free and have yet to like anything enough to even finish a meal. I would not waste my money at Sylvia's.

I just ordered the Bison Burger with a gluten-free bun for dinner tonight and it was so delicious! The grass fed burgers at Burger Up are the best I have tried in Middle Tennessee. Highly recommend :)

Not impressed. Ordered our food and 40 minutes later we received it. It was breakfast so very simple eggs and pancakes. Ice bucket to help yourself was a huge block of ice. At least have fresh ice so we are not pounding on it. Another customer walked in and wanted a pumpkin latte as it was "available" on their board but it really wasn't because they didn't have the pumpkin yet.  Overall just not impressed.

What a lovely surprise it was to find Basimo Beach Cafe today!  They serve local, organic, and delicious food and drinks.  The owners are so very friendly, welcoming, and willing to answer any questions you have.  I felt like I was at a friend's house while they cooked for me!  A friend and I had the good fortune to enjoy the Coconut Supreme smoothie and the Veggie Burger and we loved both!  The smoothie began with a REAL coconut, it used the water and meat . . . can't get any fresher than that.  They really know how to combine healthy ingredients to make food bursting with flavor.   I appreciate that the menu lists every ingredient so you know exactly what you're getting but the owners were more than happy to assist me in figuring out which items were vegan.  The Veggie Burger was amazing.  I guess I was expecting yet another from-frozen Boca burger (gross) and this was nothing of the sort.  This burger was made fresh while we waited and was topped with all kinds of delicious fresh veggies and avocado.  The toasted bread was also vegan and so yummy.  The burger came with organic corn chips and some purple cabbage and tahini dip that was such a nice combination.  Some other customers ordered the Basimo Sunrise smoothie and the owner let us try it and it was very good as well.   

Yes, it is a little pricey but you have to consider that you are getting organic and non-gmo foods that are REAL foods!  And the food is made from scratch with care.  If you eat gluten free, they can help you with that as well. Everything about this place appeals to me and I will definitely be back.
The food here is super awesome. Fried tomato blt is the best thing ever lol. Also Jamie is the best server ever. Sweet and nice! Thank y ou!

A great St Louis tradition. I go every few months, and every time it is a consistent experience. There are a lot of people, you sit outside or in your car to enjoy the treat, and the treat is tasty. My usual poison is the big apple. Basically a slice of apple pie mixed in with vanilla custard. Its one heck of a treat. The most recent visit I had a cindermint concrete. Its was great! I may be more adventuresome next time and try something new. I've never had a bad combo here.

A colleague and I were in town on business and stayed at the attached hotel.  We stopped in here on two occasions during our stay.  The first experience was great.  We wanted a quick appetizer before meeting friends.  The BBQ nachos were delicious.  A decent-sized portion. Not too large and enough "stuff" to make your tastebuds happy. I also tried their in-house beer.  It was pretty good.  I was surprised.  Our bartender, Kevin, was very friendly.  Turns out he's also a damn fine musician too!  

Now, our second experience was quite the letdown.  We popped in for lunch.  I tried the fried bologna sandwich.  I was intrigued by something new.  I shouldn't have been.  It was a bit too fried for me and on plain old bread.  I opted for American cheese, which looked plastic-y and didn't cover the entire sandwich.  I felt slightly ill afterward, perhaps from the grease?  My colleague had the brisket sandwich.  She said the flavor was okay but that it was super fatty.  She also didn't feel great afterward.  

So, maybe stop in for an appetizer and music, but then head out?  I was disappointed that lunch wasn't as positive of an experience as lunch. Whomp whomp.
Great bar on the divey side.  Drinks are cheap and atmosphere is chill for happy hour.

I've only had takeout that hubby picked up.  My first order was curry goat, cabbage, rice and peas.  It also came with bread.  It didn't taste like coco bread, but had a sweet taste and was very soft and fresh.

The portion was large (I ate for 2.5 meals out of it).  It tasted fresh and it reheated well a few days later.  

Ordered another takeout of oxtails, peas and rice, callalo, beef patty, and patty coco bread.  Will update this review after that meal.

I see bad reviews, but so far I've been very satisfied and looking forward to today's meal.

A delightful italian restaurant. Very casual, but delicious food that goes from typical Italian-american offerings (like Chicken Parm) to more inventive and delicious riffs with a New Orleans influence (try the Veal Montalbano... you won't be disappointed).

Definitely recommend it if you're looking for a good Italian option in NOLA.

I lived in Chicago for 30 years. All over the Chicago metropolitan area, really...south side, north side, downtown and even out in the suburbs. Hell - my first paying job was selling newspapers at the corner of Randolph and Michigan in the early 80s. That said, the dog I got at this place only shared two characteristics with the hundreds (if not thousands) that I ate when I lived in the 312: steamed bun and bright green pickle relish. The similarities end there. 

Dog itself was alright but lacked the garlicky flavor typical of a real Chicago dog. Not sure what brand they're using but it certainly isn't coming out of the plant that shall remain nameless but is located just down the street from the Board of Education. If you've been there you won't mistake that product for what these guys are serving. The bun was wrong, too. No poppy seeds and not quite as tall as it should be to hold the ingredients in. 

I will probably make it back as I work pretty close by these days but I'll have to dig deeper into the menu to see if the beef or the pizza puff bring back the memories the way I was expecting. 

Yes, the woman at the counter was rude and short with me. No, that isn't "Chicago ambiance."

Great place !! My first time so the guy behind the counter made it very simple to order, with me just telling him what foods I like ...the chow mein  noodles are fine like angel hair, so it's definitely different but I would recommend this place to anyone ...not very expensive either 20$ for 2 large meals

Good baked goods but very rude staff! I always try and make a trip to the bakery when I am in town from TX. There are just some things you can't get in Austin. But after the rude service I received today I do not think I will be returning. I will give my business to Haydel's and Baum's Fine Pastries (it's worth the trip to BR).

Had a great meal tonight at this establishment. We started with the potato skins which were amazing! I then had the veal tortellini which was very good. My only complaint was for 36 dollars they did not give you very much. My boyfriend enjoyed his meal as well and we would definetly return!

I had never had mead, so this was a first! Very cool place. The couches were great for our group of 5 to lounge and enjoy. The decor was very eclectic.

We ordered the tasting flight - 3 meads and 3 ciders for $5. Again - this $5 taster flights in Indy are just top notch. I loved about 4 of the drinks total, the others were a bit sweet for my tasting but it was fun!

There are board games you can play. We got one out but never got around to playing because of our convo. I like that there isn't an actual huge, solid bar, just a casual metal bar with singular supports. It made it feel more homey. And they don't charge you until you leave, so it was nice to just keep ordering as we chatted and not worry about paying every single time. We also tried the Goose meat and cheese plate - delicious. 

I bought two of the ciders, one being the whisky barrel-aged cider that was no longer available on tap. That is the main reason I was told to come here was to try this cider, but it's season. So I bought a bottle but have not tried it yet! 

I thought the partnerships they do with other local business was really cool. One night you can enjoy meads and massages, they also do yoga and other some other events. Such a fun way to bring community members in.

Overall I loved it!

P.S. I wouldn't suggest bringing kids, but one guy must have been on babysitting duty because he had four munchkins with him. He asked about the juice boxes in the cooler and they were free! I thought that was pretty neat.
Great ice cream with a wonderful assortment of flavors.  Anytime I visit downtown Nashville, a stop here is almost a requirement.

really great breakfast - huge variety, very flexible, deliver on the food.  excellent grits - they're made with cream cheese and are creamy but not as heavy as you might imagine.  best mushroom gravy I have ever had - with homemade biscuits, blew my mind.  good granola, too.  would be my go-to brunch spot if I lived here.
This place is a solid 5. Staff was great and attentive, food is perfectly amazing no rush between apps and entrees no matter how busy it was. Great experiance
Excellent for lunch. Have the pecan pie!  Excellent service with lots attention to detail. Waiter was also helpful in recommendations.
Omg go and try everything, the biscuits will make you slap your momma!!!!! Thank me later!
Fourth time at Luke. Wonderful oysters on half shell! I had shrimp and grits and it was sensational....well seasoned. Great noisy atmosphere. Wonderful wait staff.

It was so difficult deciding what to order here. I was in the mood for a skanky chai latte, but the skinny bitch latte just had that calorie conscious ring to it.

After a bit of thought I decided, skanky it shall be!

This has got to be one of my favorite places in Tampa. I had never really put a pulse on "hipster" in Tampa, but I found the closest thing to it at Bricks. Plenty of space to lounge here with a nice offering that ranged from caffeinated beverages to brews and snacks.

I would have never typically thought to throw bacon on a peanut butter and banana sandwich and then drizzle with honey, but I'm glad someone did.
The Elvis sandwich is a hunka, hunka, burning yum!

I would give this place five stars all day, except for the fact that service is slow. Like, dial-up slow. Like larvae to butterfly metamorphosis slow. So slow in fact that on a pretty *slow* afternoon, it would take 20 minutes just to get an iced chai even though you have a clear view of queue and activity of the servers. So slow that from time of check request to actually receiving it, was about another 20 minutes.

While the laid back atmosphere is one of the things that makes this place so cool, it's also the incredibly laid back service that could put a damper on things if you're in a rush.
Waiting staffs r great but raw oysters r dirty n torn. We order the seafood stuff mushrooms n it is dry n salty. The 2 lbs lobster was actually 1 1/4 pound.
Great place.  Not a ton to it, just a noodle bar done right with innovation and little pomp.  Price is right, food is delicious, service is great.  Broccoli and brisket noodles are musts.

DELICIOUS LUNCH !!!!

Worth a try--their lunch specials include a LARGE variety of pasta dishes with soup or salad.

Cream Brule cheesecake is superb!

Very very good homemade Italian food.
I'm a first timer and was excited to stop in here for lunch today. The nuggets and sweet potato fries were overly greasy and soggy. I will not be back.
Terrible service, one of the worst Bloody Mary's I have ever had, and one of the saddest BLTs I have ever seen. Just over all bad experience. Will never go back.

some reviewers need to think before they speak and get over the idea of their self importance when posting reviews. that being said...it isn't a difficult concept to review a bar & grill comparably to similar establishments.  in doing so, keith's has great bar food!  wings rock, nachos are amazing, reuben sandwich is awesome, fried clams have great flavor and are crispy, crab & cheese soup is excellent, for great service ask for emily!!
Amazing Spot, Hidden Gem, Great Food, Amazing Service & Memorable For Sure!

I stayed here last month with 3 other buddies while on a motorcycle trip.  The hotel was very clean and the front desk staff was very pleasant.  The decor of the hotel was very modern, but nicely laid out.  

The room was top notch with some trendy furniture and plenty of space for four dudes with motorcycle luggage on a 14 day trip.  Having the 2 queen beds was nice, because most hotels within walking distance of Bourbon Street give you doubles.  Noise was never a concern and the AC worked flawlessly.

I did have an issue with one of the bell hops mishandling my (expensive) motorcycle saddle back, but to my surprise, the hotel covered it's replacement cost with no questions asked.  It isn't often customer service woos me, but this goes a long way and reflects admirably on The Saint's management.  I'd highly recommend this hotel and would stay here again.

I was very pleased with the convenience of scheduling an appointment.  She uses all organic products and charges alot  less than others in the area!  I don't understand, but I am not complaining.  The color looked so natural.  I am hooked.
The color looked great and I had several people ask if I had gone on vacation.  When I told them it was a spray tan, they complimented how natural it looked.

Absolutely delicious! I was led here through a random video ad on facebook, and I am so glad I followed the breadcrumbs (pun intended) to this macaroni spot. There is so much variety, that you could come once and then come again and again, even though everything is macaroni and cheese. I went with the cheesesteak mac because I was in Philly and was not disappointed in any way! The service is friendly and very willing to give advice and recommendations for the best options for you. Whatever you do don't skip getting their signature crumble, it is definitely the perfect topping, I wish I could have taken a cup home for my own mac and cheese. Now, the macaroni and cheese base is PRETTY good, if you make a strong baked mac and cheese this might not compete on purely base alone but once they make their combo magic you have what has earned this place a solid four stars. Limited seating so more of a quick eat, if that matters, but, if you are in Philly definitely stop in!

My GF and I decided to get dinner here on a whim because we were hungry, and well, it was open. We were both distinctly underwhelmed with the food and the service. Our waiter took our order, but never came back to check on us until it was time to pay. The place was definitely kid friendly, which is fine, but it was downright raucous and noisy. My dinner was a squid ink pasta with scallops and shrimp, and the pasta was mostly stuck together (although the sauce was nice), and there were two small shrimp and two small scallops - all for 19 bucks. Next time we'll keep on walking.

If you really want to watch sports they do have TVs...but who watches sports without the Internet to stay up to date of all the games. Really....its 2014 and you don't offer Wifi....thumbs down on no Wifi
Antipasto salad is enormous but tasty.   Pizza very good and pretty light.  Good service and nice pizzeria.

Would give a negative star if I could. Haven't had a good bar experience in about 4 attempts. Slow is an understatement. If they have more than 1 bartender working that's a good night. They should train all of the staff to at least pour a beer. Last but certainly not least... the entire building smells like a toilet. It's like they are trying their hardest to fail. From the day they opened its been terrible.
Comfortable hotel located in the heart of downtown Philly. Hotel was clean, staff were eager to help. I would stay here again.

Beware!!!! New ownership!!! Not same place at all!! I am so dissapointed in food amd service.  Really bad for as great as it used to be. Too many great restaurants to even bother with this place.  Cold uncooked hashbrowns kitchen yelling at everyone and not good food.

WOAW!!  My brother brought me here to eat since he knows how much I LOVE Vietnamese food ! And we have tried every one of them in town but this is BY FAR the most delicious one yet. We had to drink Thia ice tea which was sweet and refreshing ,unlike saigons that taste like sand in water . We also had spring rolls as an appetizer . The service was amazing , the gentleman there was very nice and professional. When they brought the food to the table we couldn't wait to try it . I have the pho Combo with meatballs, beef and chicken . Which I have to say the broth was SOO flavorful and delicious . And my brother had rice noodles with beef . We both kept switching plates to get a taste of both since they were both so delicious. I would recommend this place to anyone who LOVES Vietnamese food as much as I do . I have nothing bad to say about this place :)

What a place!  There's really nothing like it in the Tampa Bay area.  Where else can you get a $5 muffaletta?!?!  Wash it down with a Chinotto, finish off your meal with a cannoli or two, grab a pre-made pizza for dinner that night and it's a wrap!

went for breakfast on a monday.  20 minute wait but bypassed that by sitting at the bar.  Great menu.  Biscuits were great.  Had biscuit egg/bacon and cheese and fried chicken/egg/cheese biscuit.  Coffee was great.  Nice environment

Ted Drewes is a must-visit for locals and tourists alike.  It never disappoints.  The occasional long lines are worth it.  On summer days and nights, it's nice to relax eating your custard while sitting on your car in the parking lot.  Our personal favorites are the chocolate malt and the "All Shook Up", but there are constantly new specials to try, so I try not to get hooked on just one thing.  In short, this place lives up to the hype, but if you're a St Louis transplant like I am, just be careful - after Ted Drewes, regular ice cream will never satisfy you again.

Love this place.  The old train depot transformed into a brew house...yes pls!  Good beers, good bourbon, fun atmosphere, outdoor seating (even with the interesting walkers on 4th street).  

P.S.  some people take themselves way to serious as yelp reviewers...see below.  If you want good comfort food done well and a great selection of beer and spirits...check them out.

Quick, delicious and fresh. This was my first trip, so I didn't know what to expect, but I knew it better be good since walk to get there was so long. Lol
Anywho, all the ingredients are right there at your disposal,     And fresh! The prices are great, build your own any toppings for $7.95, that's a steal. And the staff was extra friendly, helpful and quick!!!!!

Man oh Man.

This is by far my favorite generic center city deli.  First off, they have some really innovative sandwich constructions.  A personal fave of mine is the Brian, which combines turkey (tastes freshly roasted), muenster, sauteed garlicky greens and pears (!?!) on some griddled bread.  I also like the option of getting my chicken or tuna salad made with fat free mayo.  

All sandwiches come with a side.  The asian pasta salad? gross.  But the whole wheat pasta with eggplant and sun dried tomatoes? A little cup of heaven.  

Occasional mistakes due to quick service are understandable, but the source for the lack of a 5th star.

Also, bagel chips while you wait (lines are long but move fast) and prices are somehow always below what's quoted on the board.  I don't really understand their discounting, but I'm not complaining...

They have a pretty big selection and more than just sandwiches.  While not the most interesting lunch, in the wasteland between 16th and 21st on Market, this is a gem.

What a huge disappointment. Note, we did not stay there but since we were traveling through Nashville on St. Patrick's day, I thought I would take my wife there for dinner and to watch the NCAA bracket announcements.
