I had heard and read that there was a great sports bar in the hotel. Drove over, found out we had to PAY $20 JUST TO PARK. 
So, came that far so figured what the H.
Wandering around the hotel took quite awhile to find Fusio? We asked several employees and it seemed like we kept getting incorrect answers.
Finally found it, and guess it was closed. A Sports bar closed on the day the NCAA's were announced?  And Jack Daniels was closed.
We ended up eating at the Irish Pub where the food was just so so and expensive for what we got.
I came, I saw, I won't return.

What a find! The best pork chop I have ever eaten. Our server Michael was excellent, the food delicious and the setting relaxed but classy. The menu was creative ad varied enough to please any palate.  Just a great dinner from beginning to end. Check it out

Pros:  The food is really good.  The burgers are tender and juicy and the chili is amazing.  The taste of the food alone will bring you back for more.  

Cons:  Both times I have ordered from there, it has taken forever.  The first time it took over 30 minutes and the second time I ordered I asked them how long it would take BEFORE I placed my order.  They said 15 minutes as they were finishing up a catering order.  I ordered at 11:55 and thought that they were slow the first time so I gave them a bit of extra time.  I arrived at 12:30(ish) and while the entire restaurant was empty, they had not started on my order.  I didn't walk out the door with my food until 12:55pm and not a soul walked in nor did the phone ring with any orders.  

If you order buffalo wings, make sure  you ask for them mild as you might wind up with the scorcer (like we did) and they were too spicy to eat!  The haystack the first time I had them were amazing.  The second time they were very doughy and heavy with oil.  A small fry is really really small as well.

I also ordered a small chili and it was a tiny 4oz portion.  I didn't expect it to be that small, but I will order again because the flavor was on point.  

So, if you want great food, just make sure you have plenty of time and are not in a hurry!

Quirky place with really good ramen! Got the miso ramen which was excellent.  Every component of the dish blended well together but was also good when eaten individually.

I went right before the dinner rush (~4pm).  Perfect timing if you want to avoid the dinner crowds.

"Weird" decor. Good music.
I love this place. The food and coffee are excellent. On the weekends, expect a bit of a line but as a local, It's great and I would highly recommend their "Build your own" hashes.

This place was kind of hard to find.  The signage from the road wasn't fantastic and it's location is tucked in the back corner of the first building in the shopping center.  When you walk in, however, you're presented with a nicely decorated, well lit (sunlight) indian restaurant with a buffet waiting for you.

Having never been to India, I am unable to comment on the authenticity of the dishes presented.  What I can say was that I really enjoyed the preparations.  Everything I tasted had flavor and it seemed cooked very well.  Even dishes that are the american staples tasted better here than I've had at other places.

On my plate there was palak paneer (very delicious), a samosa, some sort of vegetable ball in a curry sauce and, of course, the ubiquitous chicken tikka masala.  I liked it all.  The masala, which I'm not normally a fan of had a surprising amount of flavor.  The palak paneer still had some of its green characteristic and had a little tang to it.  Nothing was very spicy here, and that doesn't surprise me since it's a buffet.

Service was fine, not thrilling but it got the job done.  At $10 for the lunch buffet I felt like it was well worth it.  My co-workers, who normally aren't adventurous at all even liked it.  I'll be back.

I have been to many grooming salons for my Shih Tzu and Labradoodle but Kristi's has by far been the best. My dogs stand great for them because the care she takes. I drive 1 1/2 hours each way. My dogs come show looking like show dogs. Thank you for your attention to detail for this picky mama!

Expanded menu, little janky, and family run.  However, amazing chicken kebabs!!  Hands down, probably the best mediterranean chicken I have eaten in many years.  Excellent and unique seasoned rice with a pre-meal spiced soup that was delicious.

The menu is much larger than last year.  However, stick with the chicken...for reals.

It is better than any other med-food I have had in Boise with the exception of 1 Mazzah dish.
Visiting Indianapolis with a friend and we thought we should check out the Cuban food scene. The turkey Cuban was awesome! Service was great. I will definitely try and get back.

This is probably the best Hughes Fuel & Car wash, wash bay has 15 stalls which means virtually no waiting to wash your vehicle. Always clean with great staff.
Now its open 24hrs which for night shift folk like me is huge, saves me big time on my weekly car wash and can go to bed earlier on Saturdays. Go check it out yourself, you'll see where my praises are founded from.
I love this Chick-fil-A, have never once had a problem and I lived right around the corner for over a year. It is busy but we just used the app and never had a wait. Great food, great service!

One of my favorites in town!

I've tried almost everything on the menu... and love it alllllll! 
These are my favorite dishes:

*Starters 
Shrimp and Pork Rolls
Pork Belly Tacos
STICKY CHICKEN WINGS

*Soups
Wonton Soup
Pho Brisket add Meatballs
Tofu & Tomato Pho

*Entrees
Lemongrass Chicken and Fried Rice (it comes with white rice so you'd have to sub it)
Seasoned Noodles & Chicken (Pho Ga Co)
Mint Moon Crepe (Banh Xeo)
Chicken and Waffles

*Dessert 
Pandan Waffle with a Scoop of Red Bean Ice Cream

*Drinks 
Lychee Mule ------ something new and I LOVEEE it!

This sounds like a lot, but I promise you won't be disappointed! 
For starters, I picked my three favorite but if I had to pick one, it'd be the sticky chicken wings! You must try how amazing it taste - fresh crispy fried chicken drizzled with this sweet teriyaki glaze and spicy mayo (sometimes I like to sriracha for another dimension of favor). 

For soups, you can't go wrong with pho - especially to cure a hangover! I first had the tofu and tomato pho during lent season and didn't expect to like it, but I did. The broth in both has really good favor so you can tell they put some love in their pho! 

For entrees, the most popular and my favorite is the Lemongrass Chicken - flavor, flavor, flavor! Most of the time sub the white rice for brown rice, but sometimes I treat myself and sub it for their deluxe fried rice! The Seasoned Noodles & Chicken is my go-to as well. It's basically the reverse of a chicken pho! You get a small bowl of broth on the side, so you can sip it in between eat bite. The bowl of noodles and sliced chicken is topped with lettuce and fried shallots/onion. There's a small sauce on the side (of soy sauce/sesame) that you can mix in your bowl to your likings. 

For dessert, pandan waffle and red bean ice cream! If you don't like red bean, don't knock it til' you try it! The green tea ice cream taste just as good. Warm waffles and ice cream, mMm. You can't beat that. 

For drinks, they have CHAMANGO smoothie! It's soooo good - you get: the tamarid candy straw, cubes of frozen mango, and apricot syrupy goodness! 

My experiences here have always been great. The food is delicious and made with some mad love. Sometimes they are super busy so be patient because the food is worth it! I heard they're adding some new items to the menu and I can't wait to try them. Highly Recommended!!

Well what else would one expect from a MALL Starbucks except for mall employees - not Starbucks quality employees. 

Aside from watching four other people get their drink before my own, they made my first drink correctly; however, they literally threw my straw at me and my second drink was made wrong. Vegan and dairy free mean hmmm I don't know maybe NO MILK. Is it that hard of a concept? 

The size of the smoothie that I received after they finally remade the drink was smaller than the first - therefore I over paid for my drink which really pisses me off seeing as I paid $10 for two smoothies. 

Never again! I don't recommend anyone getting a drink in the place. Horrible.

Chris came out the next day and cleared some nuisance trees off my lot exactly as we discussed. He also took the time to give me some extra tips and advice for planning our landscaping in the future. Easy to work with and a fair price.

The best sandwiches in the area
 Best prices  great people Larry & josh always so nice 
Must try the roast beef

I have to revise my review after finding many bones and pieces of inedible meat in the meat/veg combo plate I took home. I usually get the vegetarian dishes with friends, so this was the first time I'd tried their meat. I don't know if it's the norm for them to have bits of bone and inedible fat/gristle, but it made me very sad. I've had the meat dishes from other Ethiopian places around the country and this is the first time I've encountered this.

I can't even tell you how much I love Delicia. I've been a number of times now, and each visit has been superb. Their food is always to die for, whether it's the vegetarian potato tacos or the empanadas. They also have the best margarita I've had in Indianapolis yet. Service was also A+. What more could you ask for?

Very creative decor. Nice staff. Big selection
of things to eat and drink.

We ordered peel and eat shrimp cold for an appetizer.  We were served hot shrimp, no biggie.  But we told the server and said it was no biggie. The manager brought us another order of shrimp cold.  I had the East Coast Platter and my husband had the build your boil with sausage and shrimp.  Everything was fabulous!  Then we got the check and the shrimp was taken off!  We were perfectly fine eating the shrimp hot, but they went above and beyond.
Club Cal Neva steakhouse has some of the best food offerings for great prices. The prime rib is great for the price!

Got the Yelp Deal!

Ernie gave a very informative tour of some New Orleans history along the way to the cemetery. You also stop for a bathroom break half way through the tour.

I gave up eating meat but I get cravings for burgers. I'm so happy I found the  black bean burger. It's so good, chargrilled and you can add any toppings as you would for the beef burgers.
I've had it 3 times and have not been disappointed. It's a pretty big burger and with fries on the side it's a great lunch for about $8.

This is by far the worst Days Inn I have ever stayed at.   The heater in the room wasn't working, but we didn't notice until late at night.  We ended up staying over another day due to a reservation mix-up with the airline and requested that the heater be repaired.  We returned later that afternoon and not only had the heater not been repaired, no one had even come into the room to make up the beds. 1/4 of the room was flooded.  I asked for a refund and said we would find another room.  The night manager said he wasn't authorized to do that.  I asked  him to call the manager and he said he couldn't.  Despite the fact the entire building appeared vacant, we were moved to a room on the farthest  side of the building and upstairs. Turns out the heater wasn't working in there either and we were provided with a small room heater.  I asked that the manager contact me - he never did.  I called corporate to complain and received a call back a week later saying there was no record of us staying in Missoula, Montana - what??????  Told her we were in Reno and never heard from them again.  I will never stay in any Days Inn again if I can avoid it.

The food and service was fine.  But I didn't have that much of a memorable experience that makes me want to keep going back - but I would go back its just not on my mind to go there.  The waitress we had was nice and the food came quick.  My meal was good - classic diner food.

I went to Thai Country Cafe on a Saturday night around 7pm. It wasn't especially busy that evening so we were able to get seated right away. 

The food was alright. We were starving so we order the Crab Rangoon as an appetizer and it was delicious.

We order the Red Curry with Chicken and Pad See something with Chicken (#43...can't remember the name of the dish and they don't have their menu posted online!).

The staff was friendly but never asked how spicy we wanted the Red Curry prepared, which is something you usually expect from a Thai place (scale from 1 to 5). And the Red Curry wasn't prepared that spicy to begin with...additionally there was no basil in the Red Curry dish, which is something that traditionally comes with the dish AND was stated on the menu. So that was a bit of a disappointment.

Next time I'm craving Thai, I'll probably explore another restaurant in STL, but this place isn't necessarily black-listed from my future dining options.

This farmers' market packs a lot of stuff into a relatively small area. And it's a popular place on Saturday mornings. So be prepared to be a little squished, bumped, elbowed, etc. But, I still like going. I'm not a weekly patron, but they have enough good stuff to lure me there early in the morning a few times each summer.

The fresh produce is a given, but some of my other faves include:
- Farm Fresh Cupcakes
- The Big Cheese
- Companion Bakery
- Queen's Cuisine
- Black Bear Bakery

Obviously, I gravitate towards the baked goods. :)

They also have grass-fed beef (a couple different vendors, I think). I usually get there around 9:00 and nothing seems picked over. But I would still recommend getting there kind of early.
Pool hall, bar, cocktail lounge, restaurant, sushi bar, dance club, and concert venue.  This place is always entertaining in some form.

H&W Produce is worth checking out if you are looking for a place to buy inexpensive fruits and vegetables. I stumbled upon this store by chance, and now it is on my "go-to" list of places whenever I am on the South side of Edmonton.
There are always lots of seasonal fruits and vegetables in stock. Here you will find your regular and familiar produce, as well as occasional exotic fruits and veggies. Some are locally grown, while others are imported from BC and the US. Shelves are never empty and are always restocked with new produce because the turnover is so high. The majority of fruits and vegetables are fresh and crispy, although they seem to go bad a lot faster than fruits and vegetables bought at, let's say, Save On, which may be due to the fact that they are all natural and not coated with paraffin. Not all fruits and veggies are fresh, though. Sometimes there are somewhat old, stale looking products on the shelves.
The store gets extremely busy on the weekends, so in order to have the best shopping experience, some as early in the day as possible, or better yet, stop by during the week.

I never realized how close I am to this amazing spot!

I wandered in one morning and discovered what I've been missing. Cheap, tasty bagel sandwiches; good coffee & lots of tables. (If you're going to eat in check that there's a spot open before you pay, because I was lucky to find a table!)

Good, quiet & calm atmosphere for studying/reading and everyone I encountered seemed friendly!

I will definitely be back!

Nothing fancy but it does have some delicious Vietnamese food.  My son loves it here especially the shrimp rockets and shrimp & pork noodle soup.  The beef pho is yummy.  Perfect on a cold day too!  Great service - quick and attentive but they aren't obnoxious about it.  Love coming here.

The food was very good. I got the "street" style fish tacos and they were delicious. My brother got a steak burrito and was unimpressed. 
My biggest issue was the customer service. The first person in the assembly line seemed annoyed and was short with us. The cashier didn't even ask us if we wanted a drink. I thought that was strange. 
They let you have complimentary chips and salsa which is awesome but half of there salsa choices were empty. 
Overall the food was good but I don't think I'll be coming back.

I came here with my mom and two of our good friends. We were lucky enough to get a great seat right in front of the live band. We ordered dinner - bread & butter (a must), asparagus, and bacon wrapped dates. All were delicious! Everyone on the staff is incredibly helpful, laid back, and down to earth. We didn't like one of the bottles of wine we had purchased so I took it back in and was accompanied by Anthony through their wine selection to find something I liked. He voided our previous order in place of our new purchase! 

I later went upstairs to order MORE food and ended up ordering more cocktails. Lucy provided friendly, efficient service. 

My first time in New Orleans has been made so much more magical because of this place and the people working there.

The first time I ever stepped foot into Smiling Elephant I wasn't to impressed. It was very small inside and not a lot of room to wait to be seated. We waited for about 10 minutes and it took maybe 15 minutes to get our food. After the first bite, I was sold!!!!! The food was delicious. I couldn't believe it. Goes to how you cannot judge a book by its cover. If your looking for a small community type of restaurant the Smiling Elephant is the place to be!

The significant other and I love to visit Pub and Kitchen multiple times per year. It's our go to spot near Rittenhouse during a weekend day to grab a bite to eat and wash it down with a nice beer on tap. I saw some people complain about the pricing, but I think it's pretty reasonable when compared to other places in the city. Love the ambiance (particularly the string lighting) and the service.

Franklin Flea is a great flea market making a fantastic use of an empty building in Phily. At 8th & Market, the location is beyond central and easily accessible via public transport.

Inside the vendors are diverse, selling anything from handmade jewelry to antique maps to vintage clothing. Not to mention the Elixr coffee, Luke's Lobster roles and other great food options.

I'm so happy to have something fun to do this winter on the weekends. Absolutely worth a visit - thanks to all who had a part in putting this together!

A fabulous find after a long drive north from Florida. It's located in the 4-Point Sheraton hotel, Food was delicious and made fresh. I actually mentioned to the waitress how I had wished it was Saturday so I could order their Saturday special Pot Pie. She told she could check with the kitchen and if they had all the ingredients, they could  make me a Pot Pie. And so they did, absolutely fabulous. Farm to table food is not an exaggeration! Add some live music and happy hour wine and I was feeling happy, happy. Not to mention I got the last room available and the hotel and staff all around simply the best. Made the trip worth it!

I've been here maybe a dozen times?  It's a pretty gothy-feeling bar, that's for sure!  Very dimly lit maroon-colored with random Russian-esque art haphazardly hung about and small cutesy little courtyard in the back. 
You can get your absinthe fix here (although yeck, the stuff is foul!) or just stick to your regular spirits and beer.  I think they have all sorts of vodka here - that's their shtick?  That and their absinthe.  I vodka, hate absinthe - do you get what I'm trying to say here?

Anyway, the bartenders are typically quite friendly, the drinks really vary in alcohol potency, but I stick to the basics here.  I don't think they have specialty cocktails to the best of my knowledge.

I love sitting up against to the booth seating to the left and just observing the people ebbing and flowing from Pravda - usually younger hipster kids, pseudo-goth people, and sometimes older people set up shop here with their books and laptops (there are classic books available on the shelves here, should you feel a moment of bold literacy). 

There's free wifi here, which is good as my phone signal usually blows in here.  

I would say that it's never gotten REALLY crowded in here, so it's a perfect pre-gaming or post-gaming site.
The food was reasonably priced, and the service was fast and knowledgeable about the menu. I really liked the Pho and would recommend this as the best Pho in Santa Barbara.
Sadly, 'feine went downhill fast.  At first it was such an adorable, pleasant cafe but now it seems like they don't care about the customer's experience.

What a pleasant surprise. After a lunch at Couchon Butcher, I didn't think I'd find any better food in New Orleans, but this place blew my mind. I had the shrimp, the pork belly, and something with raw red snapper. All were absolutely delicious, with lots of nuance in the flavors and textures. The staff were also great, and seemed to be really enjoying their jobs (I'm unsure as to their flavor and texture...maybe next time). Highly recommended!

This is my FAVORITE place to eat. The breakfast, lunch, and dinner choices are amazing. The past 7 years I have been enjoying this place's atmosphere and food. The owner/chef uses the local farmer's seasonal produce in his meal selections.

The atmosphere is fun and the service was decent, but the food was awful. I ordered the tuna burger which is supposed to be served seared. It was way over cooked and served on a super soggy roll. Yuck. The fries were limp and undercooked.  The hot potato chips we ordered as our appetizer were good but didn't have enough topping. Not sure I would come back. Much better burgers and bar food to be found.
Gorgeous place, great music and good wine. Was in New Orleans for a wedding and my coworker had recommended this place. So glad I went because the wine was good and the music was great!

The experience at Rent Max was phenomenal,great customer service, wonderful establishment, very very friendly.I had my three boys with me  and they were all over the place, instead of Steve the owner saying anything about it they were enter acting with them and it made me fill so calm like he understood there language it was such a relief.And the lady next to him was like a in house baby sitter she was very helpful with the boys not aggressive at all they even gave me a ride after I dropped the car off and the driver was phenomenal as well I give them all 100% stars thank you for the experience with Rent Max.

Came in to an almost empty restaurant. Tucked in location off of bay to bay. Lit bit of outdoor seating. Inside seating felt chipotle-esk. Not your typical sushi spot. If you crave the typical asian atmosphere this is not your place. Our server was not Asian. Open kitchen visible for patrons. I had green tea, edamame salad, miso soup, and a rose cave roll. Edamame salad was okay.. I prefer the hot edamame with salt. The rose cave roll was okay as well. Nothing to rave about. I probably will not be back but mostly because I like the typical Asian decor service experience.

I've eaten here a couple of times now.  I like the pizza--it's not the best pizza I've had but the best I've found in Santa Barbara so far.  The closest resemblance to thing crust New York Style pizza that I've tried here. Toppings are good, and the biggest plus for me is that it isn't as LOADED with salt as other pies I've had here.  I like to taste other flavors in my food, even my pizza, thanks!  All in all a good place to go out for pizza.

As for ambiance I'm generally not a fan of TVs in restaurants unless its a sports bar, I find them distracting--so if it's date night I'd go somewhere else.

No complaints so far about wait staff or service.
Great place. Recommend highly if in the area.  They take day of reservations as well as call-in same day.   Parking a challenge, but usually available in front.
Worst winghouse wings I've ever had. I don't ordinarily complain about food but these wings tasted worse than Walmart chicken.  Horrible. I wouldn't return and definitely won't recommend this place.

Stopped here for a quick lunch during the week while in area for work. Service was prompt and the food was tasty. I will say it was slightly more expensive then the Vietnamese I am used to getting in the city and I was disappointed to not find the usual condiments on the table to spice up my meal. That being said, the menu was clear and I ate the whole plate.

There is nothing hot or ready about this place. I walked in hoping just maybe there would be a supreme ready to go. Not even cheese or pepperoni were ready even though it says 4-8pm everyday and it was Friday around 6pm. It is the closest to where I live. That is the ONLY reason I stop in here rarely and they said it would be 10min wait. I went and bought a frozen pizza and made it at home instead this time.

I've always loved mellow mushroom. this place was no exception. very consistent across their restaurants.

tried the potato pizza, wouldn't try again but wasn't bad. got the pretzels with marinara, always love those. great to share.

drinks were good, had some apple pie cocktail and some other refreshing cocktail, both great. 

we also sat on the patio which was nice and relaxing. apparently upstairs they have karaoke sometimes?

even though there are a lot of good pizza places in town and this place is a chain, would rate this high up with the other ones and would choose this place just as often.

Amazing place!!! Went a couple of times for lunch, it's fast (except once during lunch hour where you I couldn't find a seat!!) Food was great and fairly inexpensive :0 Great vegetarian choices!! Will def become a regular at this place!

One of the top tier spa's in Reno. When I stayed at other suites in the area, they were trash compared to this gem. The Tuscany rooms cannot be beat! Courteous staff and no 2 hrs waiting in line to check in

Ted Drewes is a St. Louis staple. I didn't even know what frozen custard was until I moved here. I hadn't even heard of it. I tried it, liked it, and went on my merry little way. My dad eats it @ least twice a week, and usually it's his lunch. I mean he is obsessed. I don't find it that good. It has a funky after taste. I do love their banana splits tho. They do need to make some choc. custard b/c vanilla mixed w/ choc. syrup just doesn't cut it.  The service is fantastic so don't freak out when you see a line a mile long... before you know it you're at the front. Prices are reasonable. I don't hate it, but I don't think everyone has to like it. It's an edible frozen treat and sometimes does actually hit the spot.

I've seen so many 4 and 5 star reviews, so I had to try it out. I went at opening, on a Sunday morning.  The service was pleasant enough, no issues there. I ordered walnut pancakes, and two eggs. The pancakes where not light and airy, very dense and heavy, all most under cooked, flavor was OK.  Eggs, just egg's.  My nephew, ordered egg's sausage, and potatoes, he said everything was bland, potatoes a little under-cooked, no flavor.  Maybe it was a bad morning?  I don't think I'll be back.

Thursdays during Lent are my burgers days so I decided to stop in to grab a cheeseburger and coffee milkshake.  The burger was just okay: 2 thin, kinda dry patties and 2 cheese slices.  I was kinda surprised at the size since they claim to be better than Five Guys.  Well, um...not quite.  The housemade chips were the saving grace; they were fresh, thick-cut, and crispy.  Much better than your Lay's or Herr's.  My milkshake was just okay; it was decent but didn't really stand out.  I actually would have much rather gone to Baskin a few blocks down.  So, in summation: come here for the chips, and get your burger and shakes elsewhere.

We were exploring the neighborhood of Fashion Mall @ Keystone to find a good restaurant and Joe's came up. We've seen the commercial many times but yesterday was our first visit. It's not crowded at all. Their seafood seems fresh and tastes good. Definitely order crab legs! Wife had the crawfish but the portion is pretty small.
Place looks like a speak easy from outside. I went on trivia night, it was fun, didn't try the food.
Yum. I've tried about 3 different things from this place now over the last few months. I'll be back. Green bowl is delicious and has great balance.

To skip the glitter and hearts and overall massive crowds that are Valentines day, Prohibition was my pick of the night for a calm meal. Not only was the setting ideal for kicking back and relaxing, but it was delicious to boot. My favorite was the special appetizer (think fried provolone with goat cheese and caramelized onions) and my boy's burger (egg, Gorgonzola, m.rare) was also tasty. I had a hankering for comfort food, so I went with the mac&cheese, which, was nothing special, but hit the spot. 

Service was great..beer options were plentiful...yeah, I'll come back.
Excellent! Delicious food.  Everyone made the birthday boy feel very special! Will be returning first chance I get!

The food was interesting and delicious but the server was quite condescending. He also said that their computer could not separate our order from that of our dining companions so we had to make a guess and divide it by percentage. I found that difficult to believe when most other restaurants have no such trouble. Also we were on the second floor which was less noisy than the first floor but the floor vibrated horribly anytime someone walked by. Since it was a busy Saturday night the shaking was pretty much continual. Not sure whether we'll give it another try.

I rolled into this operation late in the evening before closing and loved the concept.  As someone mentioned before, it's like a 7-11 for urbanites with taste and disposable income.  I think it's what Whole Foods would offer if they operated a bodega chain.  Great bottled beer selection and they offer hot foods and beers on tap.  The outdoor seating area is a great place to buy a bottle and drink it on premise.  The only place within blocks of it which offers quality food staples too.

Went here the other night for the first time and was pleasantly surprised! The menu was so unique and I can't wait to try more of the entrees when I return. :) 

I had the Margarita Pizza and it was fantastic! It wasn't greasy or sloppy, but perfectly crunchy with a nice balanced flavor and cheese perfectly cooked. 

They also have some amazing gelato that we had the pleasure of tasting. Although, I'd prefer if they had an option to order a smaller amount of the gelato. They only offer it in one size and it's far too much for me, one scoop is plenty!

Overall, I highly recommend!

Ate here for the first time today and it will be my last. Ordered a full order of ribs (slab) with two sides (French fries and corn). Total was $29.11!!! That's the most I've ever paid for ribs ANYWHERE including Rendezvous and Corky's in Memphis and any of the amazing places in KC. 

The ribs tasted good but were ridiculously fatty. I asked for the sauce on the side and was given 1 tiny cup about the size of half a Jell-O shot. The tiny order of fries had pepper sprinkled on them (WTF?) and I also ordered corn which I thought would be corn on the cob but nooooo. It was disgusting frozen corn that you'd get with your lunch in grade school. No bread or Texas toast or anything else to accompany the meal. 

When I walked in to pick it up the place had no one else in it but cussing bikers. There is no way I will be back. Not unless every other BBQ place in St. Louis closed and they're the last dump standing.

Cool little place that I popped into based off of recommendations, and was more than satisfied.  It'll be hard to find hazelnut coffee porters that are better than here.  If you visit the area and intend to visit Cigar City then you definitely need to visit here too.
Every visit to Tipplings is always an incredible experience!  I love everything from the drinks to the ambience.

Oh my lord. This is food of the heavens. First they start off with warm baguette and butter. You shouldn't fill up on this because there's so much amazing food here but seriously who can turn away fresh bread? I think I ate like 3 baguettes. 

My sister and I split the shrimp and grits for lunch (which is a really good idea, they give you two separate skillets which are ample portions for no extra charge). My waitress described the shrimp and grits as a food "that goes straight to the soul". And boy was she right. I have eaten shrimp and grits many a times, but this dish was a spiritual experience. The grits was equally cheesy and creamy- a consistency I didn't know was possible. Every time I would bring my fork to my mouth a fat string of cheese would follow. This is the life people. The tomato sauce was so flavorful and spicy. This is probably the best thing I've eaten in the world, and I've eaten a lot of things.
This place was recommended by locals to me. Definitely a must-go restaurant if you like sea-type meals. The service was excellent the shrimp plate is exceptional!

We saw Jessi at one of the most derelict events I've ever been to. I only say this because I've been to a few and My husbeast and I were the only people who weren't vendors at the Glorifying Women's Expo, that Say's something. 

I'd seen Jessi and her Product on Monday at the Moonlight Bazzar at Red Rockstar Bar, but since I don't like hot things, I had avoided her. HOWEVER.. This time I had the Husbeast. and he is an avid consumer of all things HOT and spicy.  This was a good match. Jessi was awesome. She allowed him to sample each sauce, telling him about the components behind them and even offered some to me. Sharing with  me a brownie bite that was decadent and made with her blueberry ginger sauce. 

In the end, we liked them So much that we bought all 6 flavors. Yes, You read that right all six bottles now have homes in my kitchen. We will certainly be new customers as long as she's making these delicious condiments.

Great experience. I stayed here for 2 weeks on business. I was greeted every time that I came in the front door. My room was kept clean and tidy. They have a really great gym for being a hotel, it had everything that someone could possibly want including free water and variety of work out equipment. I needed to stay an additional 2 weeks than what I booked for and that location was sold out for the 2 additional weeks that I needed. Molly at the front desk made some calls for me and ended up booking me at another Hampton Inn that was located in Nampa. This was really going above and beyond to make sure that her customer was happy. I really couldn't see myself staying anywhere else if staying in Boise.

We used Colors of Spring for our landscaping, and they did a wonderful job.  I always wanted landscaping that was a combination of colors and would transition from spring-summer-fall, and Colors of Spring helped me achieve that.  Tom came to our house, reviewed the space, talked with us, and came up with a beautiful design with mixtures of shapes, colors, sizes, and seasonal blooms.  I am excited to see the seasonal transitions and what it will look like as the plants mature. They tore out all of the old, expanded/prepped our beds, laid edgers, sodded some areas, and fixed a retaining wall-- they even fixed a gutter that wasn't dumping into our yard and replanted some bulbs I saved.  It was a little slow going at first due to the weather, but they worked hard and finished it.  I had SEVERAL recommendations to use Colors of Spring, and after my initial consult, I didn't feel like i needed to get additional bids.  The quote was itemized, and the price was what I was expecting.  Landscaping isn't cheap, but I feel like Colors of Sping is very reasonable-- plus they guarantee the plants for a year.  I would definitely recommend them to friends and family for landscaping.

my first time going to a NOLA market; it was alright. was there for mardi gras, so my senses were in overdrive. king cake was OK, in comparison to others.

had an ok variety of stuff, but the liquor selection - they should put a sign that the good stuff is up front!

reasonable prices, good customer service. 

would return, if (WHEN) I move to NOLA.

While we were in Santa Barbara we stopped off at a few wineries, wine bars and wine tasting rooms. Ya it was a lot of wine. Just saying.
One of which was Deep Sea Tasting Room. It's located on the pier on the upper floor of one of the buildings which provides a really nice view from the pier. I didn't catch the stores on the first floor but I believe they were souvenirs-esque... or not but anyway they were on the left side as you walked onto the pier.
We walked around the building, on up the stairs and straight up to the bar. Well that's pretty much the natural flow of this spot which is nice because you can get started on the tastings without delay. There's a patio/deck you can sit at to enjoy the view while you also enjoy your selections. We sampled a couple flights and we were enlightened on the regions the wine came from along with a brief background on "wine-ology". Not so much the scientific aspect but more so snippets of history on the travel of how the wine ended up in our glasses. There were a couple very delicious Pinot Noirs that I enjoyed.
Afterward, we took our new found enlightenment to a couple of the other nearby wineries as recommended by the folks at Deep Sea which turned out to add to a really great experience.
Cant wait to come back to Santa Barbara and stop back into Deep Sea to sit a bit longer. Maybe I'll make it a regular thing.

Wow this place is good! It's quaint, tasty, and well priced! They have a great selection of good food for all diet types I.E.: vegan, vegetarian, meat eaters, and pesketarian. They have something for everyone and trust me it will taste good. I really enjoyed their Pho

lloyd is a little gem of a bar--the atmosphere is chill (with new outdoor seating for summer), the brussels sprouts side dish might be my favorite food in the entire universe, and there's a variety of cocktails, beers, as well as (most importantly) a wide range of whiskies. whiskey and brussels sprouts within walking distance of home? yes please!

Flat out wonderful. Everything we ordered was tasty, beautifully arranged, and fresh. My husband had the fried chicken and really liked it. It was tender, juicy, freshly fried, and served over a delicious bed of black eyed peas and rice. It was a tad spicy, but totally delicious! The corn was by far the best ever! It was absolutely perfect. Tender, flavorful, and dusted with cotija cheese. I had the flatbread which was also good, but I'd probably go with another choice the next time we dine here. The side of cornbread was a lovely addition to the fried chicken. Warm, cake-like, and drizzled with fresh honey. If that's not enough to entice you, let me mention the pecan pie we had for dessert. Nothing compares! Although the meal was a little more on the expensive side, every bite felt worth it. Sit outside to avoid the rowdy indoor bar area, or if you're into that, it seemed liked a good scene. Must try it!

Chef hutch is just amazing. It's like having your personal chef. Best food, best personality. Wish him all the best :)

Jacky has been the best bar tender and Monica and Amanda at the front desk. Both always has the biggest smile and warm hugs. 

I look forward to seeing them every week :)

Large restaurant with a good amount of people seated inside when I walked in. Being alone, I just sat at the front (bar style area). Ordered the pho dac biet ($8.50) and the mango boba ($3.50). The mango boba was tall and skinny. Mango taste was definitely there, but there was so much sugar and I could taste powder. The boba itself was like biting into a stiff snow ball, rather than chewy. The pho featured a flavorful broth with a lot of LEAN meat, which is hard to find in most restaurants. Soft, slippery noodles here compared to stiff in another places. They gave me as much basil as I planned to use. Overall, good pho, but skip the drink.

The only reason I gave one star is to actually be able to leave a review.  Rude staff.  Chairs are broken and taped with duct tape.  They act like massage chair recently quit functioning.  The girl said that it worked but the power light didn't even turn on.   Water in pedicure sink was cold.  It's like they do not want to invest in new equipment nor their customers.  Not even sure why this place is even in operation.

I would NOT stay here. We booked this place for my sister's bachelorette party based on location which was good. However, we had money stolen out of our hotel room. Apparently this hotel refuses to take any responsibility for the actions of the people they are hiring as they refused to do anything about it except file a report with some insurance company. If the hotel had just reduced my hotel bill by the $100 dollars that was stolen, I would not be here writing this terrible review. That is a tiny drop in the bucket to a large hotel, but to us, that is a lot of money. Also, since I am here, I will go ahead and tell you that the hotel rooms smell like mildew. Also the elevators are slow, not air conditioned, and there aren't enough of them. By the time we would actually get an elevator on our floor, it would be full. The key card reader to our hotel room rarely worked which then exacerbated the problem with the elevators when I had to keep going to the lobby to get someone to come let us into our room. Bottom line, I am sure you can find somewhere better to stay.

Need to step up the service of the wait staff. Absolutely poor wait staff service our last two trips. May be in the training or possibly brand new hires but it leaves a really bad taste in your mouth. Promised a coffee refill 4X then when it's brought it's regular not decaf. I took it anyway instead of continuing to wait

Overall, very good and worth visiting. Sort of a nondescript little restaurant on a corner full of locals. The muffaleta (on poboy bread) was totally delicious, if not traditionally served. Their oyster poboys were run-of-the-mill New Orleans great. In other words, not 'special' but up to par with top quality oyster sandwiches everywhere. The gumbo was a little watery and average. Definitely worth stopping in for a bite if you're nearby. The inside is full of picnic-like tables. Comfortable and casual, and the sandwiches are fairly priced.

This was the best restaurant we expeienced in New Orleans! The food was delicious and super fast, the servings were generous, but the best part of the restaurant was our waiter.

TJ was super polite and friendly and he was amazingly attentive. He not only kept our drinks refilled, he even did the same for a side order of sauce that one of our party requested. We literally never waited more than a few minutes for any request and that was only for the particular requests we made. Most of the time he took care of things before we asked. 

We only wish there were more TJs waiting tables in NOLA.

I love this store. Everyone who works here is professional, polite, and most of all extremely knowledgeable. I have a rambunctious German Shepard and the grooming department takes extra steps to ensure his comfort and safety. Brian is our guy! We have been very pleased every time we take our dog to him for grooming and he takes the time to bond with your dog. 
We also take training classes here and we could not be happier. Nick is such an incredible teacher, who is extremely knowledgable, patient, and so passionate about his doggy students. He takes the time to answer any questions and address any concerns we may have about that lesson, or about our dogs behavior in general. His advice is always well thought out and his experience really shows. We couldn't ask for a better person to help us with our dog and we are very glad we found Nick.

I've eaten at several P. F. Changs locations and this one is by far my least favorite. Lack luster service. Not to mention the apple in my salad still had the sticker on it. With KOP only 15 minutes away and several other restaurants near you would think that they would attempt to be more attentive to their patrons.

The best biscuits I think I have ever had in my life! And I grew up on Bob Evan's biscuits, so that's saying a lot. The eggs I had were baked with andouille sausage, onions, peppers, and cheddar, and tasted absolutely wonderful as well.

Happy hour from 3-6pm is the bomb! Oysters, fried oysters, and beer. What more could I ask for? How about great service from Richie Rich and the staff? If you can ask for his service area, do so. He makes the meal so entertaining. This restaurant is just outside of the French Quarter, but the 10 minute walk is so worth it.

This place is wonderful!! I had rescued a big rottweiler pitbull mix (90lb) that was not treated very well. They staff and doctors are patient and go slow do to his fear and they  have been able to treat him with no problem. We also have a 90lb Akita malumunt mix that they saved her life when she was ran over by a car all the laser therapy and herbals helped her to walk again sooner than later. We love this place

While in town and reading all the good reviews we decided to try this place out. We stopped in around lunch time, it was not busy so we were able to sit at the pizza bar and watch them cook. Now just to forwarn anyone we are not big fans of Neapolitan pizza just because it's hard to find a place that really knows how to cook it. It's always very burned and very soft amd wet in the middle. The staff was great, very friendly and the menu had great meat and veggie options. 

Today we started with their meatball and rotolo (pizza dough, mortadella, ricotta and pistachio pesto) appetizer. The meatballs were very tender, had great flavor and the sauce had great flavor. The rotolo was a nice treat it had a crispy exterior, soft interior filled with tasty mortadella and creamy ricotta and the pistachio pesto was a nice compliment. Next we tried their shaved cauliflower salad. The greens were fresh it just a bit to tart of a dressing maybe to much vinegar. Next we tried their Tonno Pizza (Sicilian tuna, onion, mozzarella and parmigiano). The toppings were very tasty, the dough had great chew and texture and the sauce was sweet and tangy. Next we tried their Pastinaca Pizza (roasted parsnip, charred brussel sprouts, brown butter parsnip sauce, mozz, parm and lemon zest. The flavor combination was outstanding very different but a great veggie option. While the dough had great flavor and texture it was very burned and very soggy in the middle. 

I would have to say if your a fan of Neapolitan pizza this would be a great place to check out. The menu is very nice and plenty of options for everyone.

My husband and I went there this morning for breakfast . soon after we parked our car and was up on the sidewalk a lady said to us " have a seat anywhere you like " . Very eager for us to sit . There was a sign of the breakfast specials and a breakfast menu that was brought to us . The menu was one sided single menu with few options . I ordered the Pumpkin pancake special with eggs and sausage . My husband ordered the 2 eggs with toast which came with potatoes. As we sat we noticed that the restaurant next door , ( it was so close that I thought it was all one place) there was a line of people waiting to sit over there . I should have known that was a clear clue to get in line over there . The breakfast arrived to the table next to us ,  2 eggs , toast and sliced tomatos . The toast was a 1/2 inch thick by 4 inch x 1 inch wide piece of bread toasted . I swear , it was literally 2 bites of toast . Now our breakfast arrives , I had ordered my eggs scrambled with cheese . The pumpkin pancakes with about 4 inch round and just ok, sort of doughy .. my eggs were the fake eggs with barely any cheese . The sausage was 2 brown and serve links , I recognise the stuff as I buy it .  My husbands eggs were real , he had them cooked over medium . His potatoes were served room temp... and very small portion . I looked to be about 1/3 of a cup if that . His toast was the same as served at the table next to us . 1/2 inch thick , 4 inch long by 1 inch wide . Literally 2 bites of toast .  No butter on it so my husband asked for butter and jelly , she brought the butter which was a few cut chunks of butter cut off a stick of butter  and the jelly was a pepper jelly . She said that is the ONLY jelly that they have . I fully see why there was a line waiting NEXT door . We also had 2 cups of coffee .... our breakfast cost $18 . I was waiting for our server to ask how our breakfast was ... no one asked how we liked it . Its not that it was any one thing that was just not right , the whole experience as a whole was just wrong .

PLEASE NOTE THAT IF YOU LOOK ON THEIR WEB SITE THERE IS NOT AN EMAIL ONLY A PHONE NUMBER .
This is our goto neighborhood pizza journey. I am a thin crust pizza lover and I order mine 'well done'. I recommend eating in so pizza is crisp. Calzones are great too.

The people who gave Imogene and Willie a paltry 1-Star rating are either completely ignorant or completely out of their minds; perhaps they are both. Everything about this classic American small business is authentic. They are taking pristine swaths of American-produced selvedge White Oak Cone denim and turning it into perfectly crafted and meticulously tailored jeans. 

To the man who commented about not finding anything he "couldn't find at Sears 20 years ago..." please educate yourself before you write such an unfounded, and, quite frankly, idiotic review. The jeans you bought at Sears 20 years ago are likely in a landfill somewhere, ripped to shreds after 25 wears. Imogene and Willie uses premium denim produced in one of the country's oldest denim manufactories. It is HAND SEWN by some of the most recognized stitchers in the industry. More importantly, they are using American products to create a purely American product made by Americans in America. If you want a cheapo pair of duds, head down to Sears and drop 12 dollars on a pair of jeans made in China that will last you about three weeks.

I have not been to the shop, nor do I own a pair of I+W jeans, but I deeply respect what they are doing. It is incredibly difficult to break into the premium denim industry, but these guys are caving out quite a niche for themselves. Everyone I have spoken to who owns a pair of I+W's agrees that they make an awesome pair of slacks. They swear by the quality and see their jeans as an heirloom that will last forever. You CANNOT, I repeat, CANNOT, find anything like Imogene and Willie at Sears, Urban Outfitters, American Apparel, or even J Crew. To suggest such a thing is downright insulting. 

Unfortunately, the last time I was in Nashville was 4 or 5 years ago, and Imogene and Willie were not in the area at that time. I am, however, going to be in Tennessee in a few weeks and will be making a point to drop by their shop. Although I am currently breaking in a pair of Tellasons, I+W will receive my patronage as soon as I am in the market for a new pair of raws!!! Keep up the good work, and don't let the negative ratings get you down. Those people have no idea what they are talking about.
Love the staff here!   Both sides (diner and bar) are good although they are two entirely different restaurant atmospheres.    We go here on a regular basis and always have a good time.
It's good but overpriced.  Don't expect to get cooled off though. Its 90 degrees outside and probably 78 in here.

Food was really good. I got a bacon blue cheese burger. It was a fantastic burger. Perfectly cooked, the blue cheese was awesome. The beer wasn't the coldest but it was good. That's why the 4 stars. Would definitely go back

If you're a fan of spending too much money on overhyped coffee, don't go here. This place has a fun, relaxed atmosphere, cheap but delicious coffee, and $2 books for all your James Patterson needs. Hit it up for fair prices, fair baristas, and fair grinds.
Amazing food and great quality. So much variety. My favorite place to come when I visit Tampa!
Place is small and service can be slow. But still excellent pho and beef stew soup. The sandwiches aint bad either.
Adorable small place with indoor and outdoor seating. Food was good with good portion. Service was top notch. Always had full glasses of water.

We came in last Saturday for dinner. The food was delicious, The owner was very  gracious, and our server Ed, was the best waiter we've ever had at any restaurant over the past 25 years.  Anyone who likes great BYOB Italian food, should definitely try Fellini Cafe in Newtown Square!

I ordered takeout: the combo special (jerk BBQ chicken and curry chicken) w/ rice and peas and cabbage along with festivals (2/$1) and man was i blown away by how good the food was. 

Definitely will be going there again. Though parking is a real pain though.

One of the best steaks I've ever had. Got the creamed spinach for an appetizer, the Double Cut Filet Mignon, and Morton's hot chocolate cake, which oozes godiva chocolate and has Haagendaaz ice cream on the side. It gave me multiple foodgasms :). This place is pretty pricy, but if you want one of the best steaks out there, this is the place to check out!

I am going to join the cacophony of joyful voices praising this place.  

I used to enjoy the services of Brie and Mary when they worked elsewhere.  Brie has been styling my hair since she was working through school and I've trusted her for years. I followed her to Apsara and I'm so glad I did.

They are SO BUSY... and yet, I've never had to wait more than a week for an appointment.  They are SO TALENTED! They actually listen to what you want, and you can trust their opinions.  They will tell you what they think, and all of the time, they're right.  It's a laid back atmosphere, but a beautiful clean salon with good music and really enjoyable people.  I have recruited many, many people to go to this VERY reasonably priced salon.  The great thing is - if you recruit 3 people, you get a free haircut!!

They don't want money or fame. They want you to look, honestly, the very best you can.  If you are paying through the nose for a sub-awesome haircut, think again.  Give some truly talented women your hard-earned money!  And they will make you GORGEOUS.
Great food and amazing service. One of the best place in NOLA. Really enjoyed the shrimp BBQ!
Great breakfast and the friendliness of the staff was spectacular. Thanks !  it. We always make this quaint location one of our many stops when we visit The French  Quarter!

Best Mex in the Tampa Bay area; best tacos in the TB area, with FRESH MADE TORTILLAS that melt in your mouth. Now don't go there expecting much in the way of ambiance. There is none. It's outdoor dining, in the heat, among the flies, it's a hole in the middle of nowhere. 

But if you care about REAL Mexican food, you will go there and thank me.

If you don't care about REAL Mexican food, you will go to Taco Bus like all the other morons.

I've lived here for 2 years and I love it! The office was very helpful when I came in and Jennifer is one of the friendliest people. If you ever need anything they are here to help. The grounds are kept clean and I see someone outside every day around 7am picking up after the ground. I don't see my neighbors too often. Most people are young professionals; families; nurses working at Christiana hospital. 

There is a gym, pool, jacuzzi, tennis courts. Mailboxes are right outside each unit. You have your own washer and dryer and balcony. The heat and AC work very well. Clean apartments with good management. Off Route 7, 273, and I-95.

If there is ever a problem just call the office. They will leave notes at your door for complaints (i.e. if people are being noisy or not picking up after their animals). They did an excellent job cleaning up the snow during the two 20" snow storms we had this winter.

Downsides - around holiday season there is a lot of traffic as people get last minute gifts at the mall. In the mornings it's easier to drive down to the 273 exit to get on 95 because of congestion.

NEVER AGAIN. Delivery driver never called tonight, just texted. NEVER ONCE CALLED. Then stood there for 7 minutes, still never calling. Until he finally decided to pound on my window so violently I thought a neighbor's house was on fire. I had zero appetite after your 9:30pm Friday delivery guy literally scared it out of me. Also, my coleslaw looked and tasted a lot like potato salad.
Best BBQ around. My favorite spot to eat in Gallatin! Huge portions at a great price. Be aware that they don't take credit cards.

We went on the bike/wine tour through the San Ynez Valley and it was really wonderful.  The trip was organized very well, the wineries we stopped at were fantastic, and the bike ride was pretty easy and relaxing and lots of fun.  The scenery is really wonderful and I can't think of a better way to see the valley then on a bike.  I highly recommend this trip! Only thing I would change is adding one more bike riding segment!

Holla to what is surely the best donut shop in south city. It may not be the most convenient location for everyone, but yum, these things are delicious!

They offer a variety of danish, cinnamon treats, and regular glazed and chocolate. They also offer cake and yeast types of donuts. I've never had a bad experience here, and the donuts have always been fresh, affordable, and super tasty. I'd spend more time raving about them, but I feel that most other yelpers have said it all already.

The only thing I wish they had was seating!

Oh, Nox... I love thee so much. Let me count the ways....


Went here for a late dinner on Thursday night around 9pm. The place was lively and the service was on point. We both ordered the Salmon entree which Roy recommend cooked at medium. It was such a splendid decision. It was perfect!! We both commented on how the brussel sprouts were still vibrant green and they weren't the usual bland or the typical "brussel sprouts with bacon" path. They had a hint of wassabi and were paired with butternut squash. It was so warm, spicy and inviting. I'm a small eater and usually end up with a box to go but this time I licked this plate clean. 

We ran into friends there and pushed tables together. The staff was very accommodating and remembered our names even when we first walked in. Amazing service. Will be back... probably weekly at this rate. Roy + Matt and everyone are awesome!

 Sunday Funday here I come.... mezcal + tamarindo candy is due for trying still.....

Great food, but slow service. 

We walked in and seated right away, ordered drinks and food immediately. But then waited just about an hour for our main food to come out. 

Such a shame becuase the food is so great! We would come more often over lunch if it didn't take so long.

Very good BBQ.  Have tried a few things off the menu and find everything consistently good.  Not the best BBQ I've ever had but hey I'm from Texas!

Probably the best in the area for table service BBQ.

Seriously love this place. I suffer from pretty chronic plantar fasciitis and am always in the need for relief. I stumbled across this place by accident but it was definitely a match made in heaven. I've been back 3 times and it is consistently good. The foot massage is very affordable and you will not be disappointed.

First off I would give this restaurant a 3 1/2 star for the food. But the service was amazing so this is based on my overall experience. I got the Pad See Ew with beef. The flavors of the dish were good but the beef was overlooked and dry. The establishment is family owned and the sisters were all nice and hospitable. Great for kids.
Our new neighborhood bar/restaurant! The drinks are cold, and the portions are huge. Their Spinach Chicken Salad is big enough for two, and we love their homemade dressing.

The "Honey Cristo" IS as good as it gets- well deserving of all five stars...don't forget the side of crispy bacon or a "shot" of syrup.  Very reasonably priced, BYOB, and options for my vegetarian friends. The only downside is always having a wait...thats a sign about the food!
Small portions. Staff aren't very  friendly. Overpriced. Food quality very poor. Try getting refills
Darling!! Haven't been here in years but went for breakfast with my hubby. Amazing food and very nice staff. The blueberry muffin was to die for. Can't wait to go back next time I'm in town.

Lucky to get one star. Only reason for 1 star was that the beer was cold. The bar staff did not pay attention to anybody at the bar. Came in hoping to get a bite to eat but after ordering a beer the bartender disappeared and never came back. You guys lost a couple of great customers. We travel all over and when we find a new area we pick out our favorite bar and spend a lot of money there. This will not be the place.
I bought a new IPhone from them three weeks ago, and today it didn't work.  Even though it was under warranty, they refused to replace it and told me to go to an Apple store.

Went to this place based on online reviews and was not disappointed. The staff are very warm and helpful if you need help deciding what you want to eat. The chicken dumplings were average. But the whole snapper in spicy Thai curry was amazing. The portions are good and the taste was great. This is a beer and wine place with limited options but the food will keep you busy. It's a nice casual dining option in the heart of Chinatown.

It really wasnt worth the wait for me. Personally, I would rather have Little Chicagos. They have buffalo chicken on the menu but you have 2 options, dry rub, which I didn't care for because it was sweet and sriracha, which I don't like at all. No hot or mild options. We were told that it would be 45min for the deep dish. The first round of chicken came out probably about 15min before the pizza so that sucked. Our waiter wasn't that attentive. It wasn't busy. I've never been to a restaurant where the entire staff sits at a table and converse and prep and chill while they're waiting on their customers food to get ready. It was...different, but like I said, it wasn't busy. The pizza was...ok for me. Compared to where I always go, this place comes in second and it's just not worth the wait.

Before I start I should probably tell you I'm from Jersey and pretty partial to diners. Hollywood Grill is a pretty good diner and has gotten better since they've expanded a bit. The breakfast portions are pretty large is pretty good. The service is great, but the waitstaff seems to be put through their paces when it's busy and may forget a thing or two with your order... a couple times, so just make sure you check.
These guys were awesome! Great rates, polite and efficient... They made my move easy and I highly recommend them.
Did both the bank and the zombie room and both of them were great. First time doing an escape room and had a lot of fun! Definitely recommend going

This company installed a saltwater system for us and said they knew how to maintain it. We had the same guy for months, and he wasn't great but seemed to do an ok job, then he got injured and his homes were divvied up between the other employees. All we ever saw them do was check the chemicals-nothing else, because they were too busy to take the time to do full maintenance.

We ended up developing a black mold problem that another company (Sparkle and Shine) is now fixing for us; not only that, S&S clearly knows waaaay more about proper maintenance of saltwater systems than Bluepoint. We found out the cell is supposed to be cleaned once a year, which BP never did and didn't tell us about. There are other things they did wrong or didn't do at all (maybe don't even know about?)

Don't even bother with them if you have a saltwater system - and maybe a regular chlorine system, I can't speak to that but I have to wonder if they're just as clueless on proper maintenance of those as well.

I find it surprising so many are complaining about their experience with the hostess(es).  Unfortunately, my experience began and ended with the hostess.  I arrived at 7:15 and was quoted a 20 minute wait for our party of 2.  That's fine.  I gave her my phone number, and she sent me a text confirming I was on a Wait List.  I sat in the waiting area by the downstairs bathrooms.  A few other larger parties were sat before us, but then, after waiting 25 minutes, 2 other parties of 2 who both arrived after us, who didn't have reservations were sat before us.  The hostess approaches me assuring a table will be ready in a few more minutes.  I ask why were they sat before us, and she explains that they only arrived a little bit after us.  Okay?  First come, first serve, right?  Maybe both parties tipped her to get bumped ahead?  Doubt it at this place.  So, we step outside to get some air, and another 20 minutes goes by.  At this point, it's 8pm on a Sunday, and I left.  Still never received that text message confirming if my table was ready.  

I just can't imagine whoever pays the bills around there is happy losing customers to their experiences with a hostess.  I don't see myself going back.

This is great hotel in center of New Orleans, within walking distance of the French Quater.  There is free breakfast and dinner(not the greatest food, but is there for free if for convenience or don't want to eat out), free wifi, great staff, good room service. This is not an elite or super nice place(this is no Roosevelt Hotel), but they take care of you and you have everything you need to enjoy your trip-which is why I am giving five stars.  The hotel is right next to the street cars and five or six blocks from the French Quarter. My wife and I walked all over French Quarter and the Drury put us in a great place to do so. Highly recommended.

This place was fine for one night.  There was a bed and shower.  Not worth the money, but everything in SB is way overpriced.  I did get pissed off when "security" said we were being too loud when all we were doing was laughing (and drinking some Goose), but I guess the sound traveled because our window was open?  Ridiculous.

Basically delicious. All the time. 

The consistency of the quality is always great. I've been here probably like 20+ times. The meat is all organic and so is the produce. It's hard to find hormone free good quality food out at a restaurant. Versus buying at the store and cooking at home. 

Basically love this place. Tasty. And casual.

Had the spinach pocket. 

It was more like eating cardboard. 

I tossed it in the trash after 2 bites.


Waste of $ 6.39.

AVOID this place.

I know the menu just changed to Mexican today so I am way ahead of the game here and perhaps that's unfair, but OE Market SHOULD NOT serve Mexican food.

There was a ton of hype leading up to the Market Goes Mexican release and yes, I was excited. But when you really think about it, the Mexican vibe does not go with Oxford Exchange. They were blaring Latin music and have added all sorts of pinatas and Our Lady of Guadalupe candles around the place to make it all Mexican.

You can choose your protein, choose your vehicle (aka tortilla or whatever else you want) and then choose three toppings. They do not ask you if you want it for there or to go, so I'm just assuming they make everything to go.

I ordered the spicy pork belly taco with ancho sauce, pico de gallo and blistered shishito peppers. I waited for a little bit to get my taco but it was sort of busy so I didn't really mind. There is basically no space to sit in the place and the guys in front of me had taken up the ENTIRE row so I had to eat outside. No big deal. 

When I got the taco, I was actually really disappointed. You'll see the picture and notice there is basically no pico de gallo on the taco at all. The pork belly wasn't even spicy and was mediocre at best. It had no flavor. The pepper? Meh. The ancho sauce was all over the place and although it tasted good, it was basically the only thing on the taco that I liked.

This is not OE's specialty whatsoever. The food at their regular restaurant is actually pretty good and I quite liked the sandwich aspect of the market because it truly felt like a market. Their juices are actually pretty good -- their almond milk is a good blend and is made fresh. 

The market also has some refrigerated items to take home which looked pretty appetizing. 

But on the whole, this new menu change is a recipe for disaster. OE will get people going there with the hype, but they won't keep them because these tacos are not good. Head to Green Lemon on South Howard for better quality tacos packed full of flavor. Or go to Miguel's. Or anywhere else.


I will go back and try more tacos, unwillingly, but solely for the sake of Yelp.

I honestly believe that CSB makes the best beer compared to any other brewery in Nashville.  Their Pecker Wrecker (IPA) and Toasted Coconut Porters are my favorite, but all of their beers are great, and I have never been let down.  I feel like this place is special because it is hard to find one venue with great beer and great food.  Their salads, sandwiches, pizza, and fish n chips are great and always fresh.  One of my most favorite places to go and service is always great!

A new food obsession.
I had never heard of a sushi burrito until I saw someone's excited post that sushi burritos were  here! Although sushi wrapped in a tortilla sounded kinda awful, so many good reviews persuaded me to try it. Silly me, it's not a tortilla, it's wrapped in that flat seaweed used in so much sushi. Too bad, I'm not crazy about seaweed either, but they also offer a sesame rice wrap as well. Bingo! I tried the Salmon with cucumber instead of corn. Loved, loved. All the goodies blended together well and the poke sauce added a little heat. I had a passion fruit/lychee bubble thingy as a yummy dessert. The staff was so helpful with explanations and recommendations. They seemed sincerely interested in giving me a quality experience. They also offer a nice selection of Vietnamese dishes which I will try on future visits, if I can keep from ordering a sushi burrito.
I can only comment on the rum raisin, but I was underwhelmed. The consistency was very thin, and the raisins had an unpleasant, chemical flavor. I was unable to finish a small.
Another dinner with customers another success!!! The steak and scallops were amazing and our waiter was wonderful!

I was SO excited to go to the Philly Diner, since the continental breakfast offered by the Ramada did not excite me whatsoever (sorry guys!).  The food was not the issue; however, there was really only one waitress who was scrambling to serve everyone, and not only that, it took FOREVER for the food to come, and the few other  face painters I was there with and I were worried we'd be late for our first class.  That aside, I really enjoyed my stuffed french toast, and would come back to try the oreo cheesecake pancakes, but next time, I'll try the University City location (*hoping it has the same menu!*)

First off the friendly and helpful crew epitomized what customer service should be like.
The restaurant was clean and the food was outstanding, and green Chile a New Mexican would be proud of.  Well done Blake's!  #LOVEaLOTA

So how does one get a 5 Star review for a New-Car Dealership? It is as much about what they do as it is about what they don't do. 

* Be polite and constently accommodating - not pushy and aggressive, 
* honor any and all advertized specials (even if the buyer doesn't know about them
* don't hide spiffs & specials so the salesman & dealership can make more profit, 
* always be pacient let the shopper shop (finding the right car takes time) - don't try to "steer" us to the car your manager offered you extra commission on if you can sell it.

Sport Chrysler Jeep Dodge Ram did everything right. From greeting to finding to negotiating.

Buyers understand clearly - it is the salesman's job along with the manager to ge the best price - they are not being rude or underhanded or any other nasty term people say about car salesmen - it is their job. IT'S YOUR job to go in well informed, having done your home work.

My wife and I researched 4x4 cars and knew we wanted a Jeep chrokee (with certin extras) - we then researched dealers and began the waiting game (waiting for advertised deals) - Columbus day arrived and Sport offered "your bluebook value trade + up to an extra $5,000. Our car was worth 4K we decided ahead of time "getting 8K is glory, but $7k was a must" then we knew we should be able to get 2 to 3K off the sticker - and if we can do that we would buy and off we went to Sport Jeep(norristown pa).  Having a plan in advance is important and it must be reasonable, in advance!

Martin was our salesmen, awesom guy did everything right - it took us 3 test rides (about an hour) and about 25 minutes negotiating for a (2015 Jeep Chrokee Latituid 4X4 3.5L V6, 17" wheels, winter pakage(heated seats/steering wheel, custom floor mats), automatic open and close liftgate, power driver seat, and all full size touch screen extras. We saved $10,833.00 off the sticker - more then we hoped(6,900. was our trade), the paperwork took 30 minutes.

We love the car, we love Sport Jeep, we love our price. Now did I work hard to get the good price, you're darn right I did, was there a bit of showmanship and drama, yup for-sure, and did they try at first to get a much higher price(?) big time yes, but that's their job, doing that does NOT make them scammers, in any way, it is their job to earn a profit. Getting mad at a dealer for earning a living is immature - I've read the bad reviews about Sport - I find the level of insult in lou of real reporting as proof of the reviewers naiveté about how dealerships work.

Do your homework in advance, know your numbers before you go in - how much you can afford, monthly, downpayment and/or trade value. Research the sales ads and specials, call on the phone first, ask, "are you having any unadvertised incentives?" You can find out about financing on the phone too. Ours dropped to 2.4%(ur credit score will cause %s to change). If you do these things, stay professional (a little drama is def ok) you will get a great deal from Sport Jeep just like we did :0) LOVE these guys at Sport, LOVE my Jeep! 2 humbs-up

Very cool historic little restaurant (as they called it from the old days tavern).  Small room in an old building, you can envision yourself as a stagecoach driver from back in the day as you eat the barbecue meals at this little outpost.

A unique experience compared to the places you see these days.  Also, the food is surprisingly better than you'd expect it to be.

Great place for visitors and historic buffs to check out and wasn't crowded!

If you are looking to stretch your dollar and get the most amount of decent quality food and live near the colleges; look no further. The food is good but defiantly not worth going out of your way to come here. If you don't have a choice and have to get something in the area then this might be a good option.

Two years in a row me and a group of friends have attended the 18th floor ballroom New Years Eve party. This year's part was not so great and compare to last year it made me really wish I could have relived my 2009/2010 NYE night. 

Either way this hotel is always very accommodating. the employees are friendly, the rooms are clean and it's never any trouble using valet or coat check. 

I would recommend this for locals or visitors, great location right near the Arch!

Mediocre.  
We had a taste of a few things.  Thought we couldn't go wrong with having 4 stars.  
Queso and chips: Fine,  chips were stale. 
Tacos al pastor: Chicken didn't have flavor,  and was chewy. Tortillas were great though.  
Tortas al pastor: meh. 
Chicken quesadilla: More not so great chicken.  
The wait staff is lacking. Lacking knowledge, table manners, work ethic.... 
We wont be coming back. Ever.  Even if it were the last place on earth to get a Taco. It got 2 stars solely on the tortillas.

OK, so I'm going to start with the feature you will see last - the "Letters to God" wall.  Inside the restaurant one of the walls is covered with what look like to be children's letters.  It is on the wall for at least 6 months, and possibly longer - it took me some digging to figure out what they were.  Apparently they are for this movie called "Letters to God" (Which came out in April).  It has just horrific reviews, and obviously none of the letters from Chicago Taste made it in. Sorry kids, the Pony Express missed it's stop :)

So the food... they serve Gyros, Dogs, Tacos, and other quick greasy food items.  I'll mention the standouts:

- Chicago Style Hot-Dog - great!  It has a pickle, peppers, tomatoes, and hot peppers.  You can request kraut.  It's just great.
- Polish - large polish sausage + onions on a hoagie.  Also excellent.
- Gyro - They have two types, the traditional and the chicken.  Don't get the chicken.  Excellent street-food type gyro.

The standout amongst the standout: *Gyro Platter*.  They advertise this thing as a "mound of meat" and "feeds 3 people", and man they do not lie.  This is an easy 2-3 artery clogging meals for me, and a great value.  The regular gyro meal comes with a portion for 1, and costs $7something, the platter is $10.51 and is easily 3x the size.  You can share it  between 2-3 people.

The atmosphere is sort of what you would expect from a Chicago grab and go place... kind of dingy, eat on a wrapping paper type situation.  There are a few tables around to eat in, and over lunch a constant stream of people getting take-out.

My only gripe is that (aside from the gyro platter) the place needs to be cheaper, but on the other hand there is not a similar type of eatery nearby, and their business seems good, so they are probably not going to drop their prices.

If you like the standouts I listed above, definitely go visit.

Here is the deal.  I live close by this place and love the food here.  When I feel like a hot Thai dish to go I usually come here and chill at the counter or take out.  I have also been here with my lady to eat as well.  Meun Fan Thai, (most will call it Mesa Thai, cause its on the mesa, has nothing to do with the old restaurant Mesa Thai) is a small mom and pop or I should say mom and daughter run restaurant, with great service and smiles.  The Beef Salad is one of my favorites and the curries are all pretty tasty.  This is  great place to come and keep it low key and cheap.  Very local place and we seam to love the new owners that have brought wonderful fresh Thai food back to the Mesa.

Classy, clean, lively atmosphere. Food was delicious. My 8oz filet was cooked perfectly and tasted on par with Bern's. Expensive dishes but worth it. Very crowded on weekend nights. My only complaint is that the tables are so close, the place feels cramped.

Not a whole lot to say here. The food is fantastic. I haven't tried anything that I wouldn't devour again. Brisket, pulled pork, smoked wings...yes please on all! All the employees are extremely friendly, service is fast, and this is the best Texas style bbq you will get in the Tampa Bay area. If you want good bbq, this is your place. Maybe next time I won't eat so much of the smoked meat that I can actually try one of the dessert offerings...

Stopped in here after we couldn't get poboys from killer's. We got the "taste of Louisiana" three plate consisting of gumbo and rice, crawfish etouffe, and jambalaya. We look got the shrimp poboy.
