I sent it back for a Pacifico. (which seemed to be the only redeeming quality). 
We ordered Steak Nachos and got cold chicken nachos.
I wont be back.
Me and my fiancé had the greatest time at the peppermill in Reno. The whole experience was great can't wait until next time

Seated upstairs next to the AC unit our table and chairs vibrated through dinner.. we order Margarita's that were 12.00 and straight sweet and sour mix, not even a buzz off a 12.00 drink.  I don't know when it became acceptable for Mexican restaurants to serve nachos without adding real cheese. Our nachos were served with watered-down queso watered-down sour cream no guacamole even though the waitress told us it came with guacamole, the only positive was that they did add a generous serving if meat with the nachos and the waitress was very nice. Other than that I'd go somewhere else.

So I've only had the tacos and flan here. I had 3 different types of tacos - carne asada, pollo, and fish. I garnished them with a healthy smattering of the "salsa" and it was super hot!! Maybe it was made with an habanero pepper? For my gringa taste buds, it was spicy. I'm not familiar enough with traditional Mexican food to know the difference between hot sauce and salsa or if there is a difference. I'm pretty open to spicy heat in my food, but this takes it to a Whole. Notha. Level. Think numb mouth and no ability to taste bites 2, 3, 4, etc.... The tortillas were amazing - I had both corn and flour. And the flan was tasty if you're a fan of flan. Don't know if it's fair to give a review because I feel like I need to give it another shot. But for now, I stand at an optimistic 3 solid stars with a possible boost in the future. Definitely try this place out! I feel like it's a hidden gem. But beware the salsa!!

The best al pastor tacos I have ever had. They cut the meat right in front of you and give you plenty of it for each taco. The burrito bowl is also delicious. Everything is well cooked and it's the most filling option. We picked up and enjoyed it with some homemade margaritas. Perfect date night in!
Food was very good and fresh. Extra charge for taziki sauce. The gyros were excellent. The kids meal were not the best. Best part is the bakery. Completely filled with a fun atmosphere

Charming, LITTLE spot with a divey atmosphere that seemed appealing to both the local & tourist crowds.  The staff was attentive and warm, the coffee was some of the best I've had in while (Starbucks who?) and both my mom (who was definitely skeptical) and I cleaned our plates!

What can i say. Other than consistently fresh and tasty food regardless of which store you visit. Personal favorite is the the Cuban Panini. Super yummy.  Love the bountiful outdoor seating at this particular restaurant.

if I could eat their tacos al pastor every day I would! love the pineapple addition to those tacos. My boyfriend can't get enough of the BRC, taco al pastor and chroizo tacos. 

All in all a perfect bite for lunch!
Shrimp and grits.  Everytime. We love Surrey's so much we went here right before we got engaged, b/c it's our special place.  Hellz yeah!!!!

Food is okay, for mass-produced, commissary-prepared ingredients that are cooked and/or assembled on site, as it is in most large, corporate establishments like this one. Nothing is particularly good, and nothing is particularly bad. 

I imagine the decision where to go vs Chipotle, Qdoba, Moe's, and Blue Coast largely comes down to price and/or convenience. For me, these four in the area are pretty much interchangeable otherwise, besides little things like one's chips are slightly better, etc. This location does have a Coca-Cola Freestyle machine, FWIW.

Qdoba has recently started to offer all add-ons for no additional charge -- even guacamole. It will be interesting to see if and how this new wrinkle may change the level of business -- I've never seen this location in any danger of being even half full.
Best pralines in NOLA! Also their tortures are amazing. Get your gifts for family/friends back home here and not the overpriced trinket shops. Delicious!

Tre Lune is fantastic Italian restaurant in the heart of Montecito. Their food is very good, and their staff is very friendly. Everything I've eaten here is fantastic -- from the soup to the salads to the pastas to the burger. Stop in if you're in town. You won't regret it.

TRY THE: Tre Lune Burger
Best Mexican food in St. Charles!

The food is excellent, no matter what you order. The wine is overpriced. The service is good except we had to ask for the bread and ask for my dessert. 

The problem is  they have 2 types of menus...an a la carte and a 3 course inclusive menu...My wife ordered the lamb a la carte and I ordered the ribs as part of the three course menu that also included Hors d'oeuvre (I  ordered the  fried green  tomatoes) and dessert. (Bread pudding)...All delicious! 

When the bill came I was charged extra for the fgt even though it was not on the a la carte menu?  It was corrected as per my request. When the bill arrived again I noticed the tip was included??? I normally add a tip...Glad I did a double take...While great food..check your bill!

So I will say that a few of the things I have had from here have been really good.  However, my friend who loves this bakery was celebrating a birthday and I ordered his cake from here.  I had it flat on the floor of my car and live only a short distance from the bakery - before I left the bakery it looked great - when I got home and opened the box the whole top layer of the cake had cracked in half.  When I called the bakery they offered no assistance in fixing this problem other than to pay for another cake. I am not sure why this would happen but when I spend a lot of money on a cake it would be nice if it looked presentable. :(  So - I would say that while their baked goods may taste yummy if you are looking for reliable customer service - go somewhere else!

What a nice restaurant! Inside was a little noisy, but we opted to dine outdoors and couldn't have chosen a better evening for it. The bruschetta we started our meal with was decent, but the salad special really outshone it. We also ordered the lobster risotto, which I recommend 100% (though it is very rich). The veal was good too, but the risotto the favorite. Altogether, the food and wine list speak to an expensive, fine dining establishment, but the prices were exceedingly fair and the service very down-to-earth (almost to a fault). A very cute neighborhood restaurant on the whole, and a place to which I anticipate returning soon.
Amazing food -- super flavorful. Highly recommend the chicken platter and the chicken patties. Owners are great (and very hardworking!).  A must-stop place if you're in the Tampa area.

Not worth the wait, the drink i ordered was watered down probably from the chopped ice that was in the drink. When seated we were served four waters we don't know why. Decor was excellent, floors need work and the tables were very bland. When the food came it looked decent, way to much chocolate on the pancakes and hash browns were mediocre. Food was only decent shoneys would have been better.

I haven't been to this restaurant in about 6 months, but I told the manager I was going to tell people about my experience so I'm keeping my promise. I had been to Brady's several times prior and didn't really have any problem except for it seeming a bit expensive for what you get (a bag of potato chips with your sandwich) and the seating accommodations (picnic tables). I had a Buy One Get One Free coupon, so I decided to treat my daughters to dinner. When the time came to pay, I handed over my coupon which still had several months before expiring. The server told me that they don't accept the coupon anymore. I asked to speak to the owner and he came over but seemed very uninterested in anything I was saying. I asked how they could refuse to take a coupon that they had put out (it was from the Entertainment Book, so technically I had paid for the coupon) and he just told me something about a dispute he was having with the publishers of the coupon book. He also said that there was a sign on the door stating that they don't take the coupon, but we had not seen the sign because the waiter opened the door for us as we entered and stood in front of it. The owner refused to give any other type of discount or compensation. I told him I thought it was a "Bait and Switch" and that I would be telling others about the experience and he just shrugged and walked away. Don't patronize establishments where the owners treat the customers like pests! There are lots of better BBQ places around.
This place has most everything I need for Asian cooking. Great prices on fresh fruit and veg. Just be selective to get fresh stuff.

Crab Night... What a joke! 
We were looking forward to an all you could eat crab night all summer, so much for the excitement. I have been in the restaurant business for over 15 years and this was by far my worst dining experience EVER.  The crabs were over cooked mush, not only were they terrible after picking thru the mess of 2 plates we were told, sorry there are no more crabs... We will be happy to take $6 off your check. Was this joke... After speaking with the waitress we were told that was all she was allowed to do. Than spoke with the manager and the only thing worse than the crabs was his arrogance and who gives a damn attitude. 
The entire experience was AWFUL... Don't waste your money!!!
Our new favorite BBQ place in the St Louis area. Awesome bbq pork steak and ribs. Get the pork steak, you wont regret it. tasty, tender fall of the bones. Portions are huge. Very reasonable pricing.

Ok, yes, the ribs are good.  My reason for the lousy rating was the mis-information in their advertising announcing something to the effect that the Rib Cook-off features "the largest arts and crafts show in Nevada."  Really??  We must have missed that because all we saw were row after row of booths selling tons of cheesy commercial merchandise.  I mean how many toe ring booths do we need?  Hey Nugget, how about next year a little more truth in advertising, or at least have your people attend a REAL craft show so you know what one is supposed to look like.

My husband and I went on a Friday night around 9 for our first visit. I like the atmosphere and feel the location of the restaurant is perfect for a BBQ joint since there isn't much like it in the Belmont/12th/Green Hills area. Other than the appearance of the place, not much else impressed me. We ordered fried pickles as an appetizer and they were waaay too greasy to even eat, and this comes from someone who is not afraid of a little grease here & there. When we ordered they were out of turkey, brisket and some other meat so I couldn't try the nachos like I'd wanted. I ordered a chicken sandwich which came with coleslaw on the bun. The coleslaw was delicious but couldn't hide the ever-so-intense dryness of the chicken. We went outside to eat and the tables hadn't been cleared, we had to ask a staff member to do it for us. The staff was kind and friendly enough and the side dishes as well as the pork my boy had were all good but nothing to write home about. I can think of 3 superior BBQ restaurants in Nashville that I'd prefer to spend my $ at. I may give them another shot but I just wouldn't try chicken again. Maybe next time they won't be out of brisket.

I was at the barbary the other evening for a DJing event with some friends that started at 10 and went until 2. The location is almost hidden in northern liberties, my ride got lost multiple times and couldn't find its location. The men at the door were quick and barely checked my ID so I rushed in to the bar. There was an open bar deal for 10 dollars for an hour so I did that. Started with vodka cranberry and it was a very weird drink. The vodka was not present in the drink and the cranberry juice was so watered down it seemed like it was soaking with ice and just melting into a semi cranberry semi water liquid. The beer selection was decent with the PBR being the only choice I was okay with drinking for the night. The environment was very grungy and dark and difficult to get around. I think another event I would have enjoyed it but this event had a lot of drunk stumblers kinda making it difficult to locate the bathroom and stairs to the upstairs.

Awesome!  I can't add much more to that one word review other then to say that I went here any more then I do Shubee would be able to take me as a dependent on his tax return!  Great food, generous portions, reasonable prices!

Not that great. Went here for dinner with my husband recently. He had the duck, I had the grilled salmon. Both were sadly overcooked. The duck was tough and the salmon was so dry that the only way I could swallow it was with a gulp of water. I'm giving 3 stars because we had gone on a previous occasion and everything was good.

Horrible, horrible check-in experience. Checked in on a Friday, and after spending a half-hour in the long line, was told that no rooms were ready, despite it being past check-in time. I told them that we had a convention to go to, and couldn't leave all of our expensive stuff in the car, and they just shrugged their shoulders. Jackasses. So, we go to the convention, come back 3 hours later and attempt to check in yet again. Once more, after a 30 minute wait in the ridiculously long "Soviet Union type line for toilet paper", we were told that no rooms were available.  The people behind the counter could care less, and were totally unmotivated to offer any service or recompense. When we finally did get a room, it was very nice, but did not make up for their just awful customer no-service. A letter sent to them, informing them of the crappy experience went totally unanswered. They clearly do not give a crap about customer service. I'll never stay at the Peppermill again.
Great little  diner with bug city feel. I've had omelets and burgers here that were very good and inexpensive. Very busy for weekend breakfast but service is fast

Overpriced and average food. 

The lobster chowder tastes like flower blended with salt and a little tiny bit of lobster meat. They charged $8.99 for that. Lobster was good but it doesn't worth of $21. They put way too much mayonnaise on the sandwich. Fish and chips tastes okay. They charge for $18. In overall the food was like 3 star. But because of the price I give 1 star.  Disappointed and waste of money.

I will concur with the other reviews regarding poor service. The lady who took our order was ok but the lady who made our burritos was extremely rude to my wife and also had soap suds all over her forearm and thankfully it didn't touch our burrito. This is the closest qdoba to our home but next time will go somewhere else

We literally visited this place the week it opened several years ago. The same relatives were in town that went with us the first time.. They wanted to go back, so we did. 

The parking is always a bit confusing and they were paving their lot, so we parked on the street. 

The place is amazing looking, I just wish the food was at the same level as the decor. I really feel like they nailed the faux blues bar/bbq feel here.. It is a bit over the top, but I do like it. 

So right off the bat, I see they have a pastrami sandwich. Done.. 

There were 6 people in our party.. So I ordered. No Pastrami. None.. SO... On to a pulled pork sandwich, which I knew better, but I just wanted to eat and leave. 

Everyone else ordered. It took quite some time for our food to come out. It was a dying off lunch crowd, and was defiantly not packed. Not thrilled about that. 

Our food came. I kid you not, I put so much seasoned salt and BBQ sauce on the pulled pork sandwich that it should have overpowered it. I COULD NOT get any flavor out of it. I think it was the bun. But all the same, it was VERY bland. 

The ribs were good (another member of our party ordered) but a bit tough. 

Someone ordered a Caesar salad, and man it looked weak. The grilled cheese sandwich for the kids was barely toasted. It was pale...Cheese was good, but bread was too much and not toasted. 

Here's the bottom line to me. If you really don't care about the overall taste of the food, and want some room and a slightly loud environment to hang out in.. This is the place. 

If you are a foodie and want the best. DO NOT go here. It's OK.. That's it.. OK... Go to Sugarfire or Lil Mickey's.
Tex-Mex food. If your looking for a good Margarita and some Tex-Mex appetizers give Don Pablos a try. Unlimited warm nacho chips and sausa. Great Service.

Of course you'll never NEED anything you'll find here, but I guarantee there will be plenty of things you'll WANT before you make it out the door.  I could spend a year's worth of paychecks outfitting an apartment, but what's the fun in that when they get new things in on a regular basis?  My favorite part is the kitchen area.  I see things that were used daily by my grandmother but lost over time.  

I'm amazed at the quality of the furniture, especially when you find something in pristine condition, and you'll pay for that quality here.  Nothing is cheap, but nothing is too expensive either.  It's a great place to wander around on a Saturday afternoon, and the staff are very helpful, polite, and knowledgeable.

My recommendation?  If you see something you like, don't hesitate to buy it, because it won't be there the next time you come back.  I can't tell you how many times I've kicked myself for not getting that rare find!!

I only came here for drinks while walking around the city on a nice Friday night, but the ambiance was amazing.  Great city views, fancy crowd, great cocktails and more.  I am only rating 3 stars for now since I did not try the food, however would definitely go back.  Would be perfect for a romantic dinner, or a private party in the back room.  Drinks were quite pricey though.

Hands down, without a doubt, THE best place to get a beignet in the French Quarter (maybe in all of Louisiana).  

Beignets cooked to perfection, Live Jazz in their courtyard and quick easy service, unlike that other place near the French Market! 

My kids actually got up and dressed in less than 15 minutes (one being a teenage girl if that tells you anything) when I said if they hurried, we would go to Cafe Beignet before leaving the French Quarter.

Hmm.. Definitely one of those places that doesn't live up to the decor. I was expecting so much more and was dying to try this place. We had a vanilla/vanilla cupcake and a vanilla/raspberry cupcake. They both just seemed "meh". I have to say the icing is fit for a wedding cake with fondant and shouldn't be on a cupcake because it is just too overpowering and too rich. The cake itself also seemed old tasting. I'm not going to go get another one. However, I would return again and again to Ramona Susan's. Their cupcakes have always been on point and I find myself craving another one or would go get their butter cake before returning to Cake life. We also tried the salted caramel brownie and it was totally stale. So disappointing!
The food was amazing and the service was perfect! Sandy was the best! Next time I'm in Tampa I will definitely visit again!

These guys are absolutely amazing. Being on a budget and a fun and reliable import that was in my price range proved to be a challenge. I stopped by Southampton to look at several cars. I told Collin the make and model I was seeking and no more than a week later he called with the perfect vehicle for me. I'm happy to say that it's been an amazing experience and anything that's come up has been handled promptly and professionally. I highly recommend Southampton Imports. Collin iand his team are the best

I love this place. It's part of the effort to make downtown Granite City look less like a trash heap and more like a place people like to live and hang out. It's family run and they do a great job taking care of people when you come in. You can usually find a quality special.

Salads and wings are awesome, and pizza is on point too. This is a great place to kick off an evening out, especially when it's located right across from the movie theater. Good job guys!

We stayed with kids  for one night.

Right across the beach and close to state street it is a nice location. Room is clean and well furnished. not too roomy but still comfortable. View from patio is very nice.

service was fine, complimentary breakfast  was okay, as well complimentary wine/cheese in evening.

I recommend this place for families.

Wow our 1st visit and we had a great time!    Had a groupon that included a lesson, bow rental and hour of range time for 2 for $40.  Took my 8 year old daughter and she loved it.  The instructor took her time explaining everything and gave us some great tips.  She also checked with us frequently and was always there to assist if we needed.   I would definitely recommend Wasting Arrows for a fun family activity.   Also would be great for individuals and couples.

This is my favorite place to get froyo in my area!

Menchies staff is always super polite, helpful, and welcoming. I have seen them deal with some disgruntled customers before- everyone who works there is very professional and helpful despite who they are serving.

The shop itself is family friendly, bright, clean, and has outdoor and indoor seating. Its a happy go lucky place to visit!

The froyo is priced by weight, and it comes in a variety of flavors. Ask for a little sample cup and you can try any of the flavors before you get them! They also have waffle cone options, and sell pre packaged froyo as well as froyo cakes. The toppings bar has pretty much anything you could imagine- including my favorites: boba & mochi!
Anyone who feels like driving 15 min over the bridge it is a great restaurant i go with my family all the time .Food is great atmosphere is great, fun place.

The only reason, and may I say it's irrelevant of the actual experience... Is why I'm not giving this place 5 stars is because the place is a little dated, and lacks modern decor. Other than that... I LOVED the experience! The drinks were great; the food was great; the service was great; the chairs were ridiculously comfortable; the screen play of the movie was as and their other theater. I'm going to be so bummed ever going back to a regular movie theater! The prices are a bit more for a regular ticket (around $12) but totally worth the comfort! I highly recommend everyone try this at least once!

If I could give a minus, I would. My husband and I ate there, and we both felt sick, after eating only a few bites. His fish and my scallops were old, smelly, and incredibly salty. He was a shrimp boat  captain so he knows his seafood. He said his redfish belonged in the garbage can, not on the dinner plate. We should have asked for a refund, but, frankly, we were so sick, we just wanted to go home. This place should be seriously examined by the health department.

It's the second day of that dreadful experience and I am sick and so is my husband. There is a good reason why you must pay for this food in advance: No one would pay for it after just a bite.

I love the Bywater but this place is a blight. After this place is examined by the health department - and I sure hope it's soon - it will definitely be closed down. 

According to a 2012 article by former T-P restaurant critic Brett Anderson, who is possibly this city's best critic ever, the city shut down Bacchanal in August of that year. It should be closed again - and never allowed to reopen. Obviously, it was shut down for a reason and obviously the changes made so that it could reopen were temporary.

The problem with reviews on Yelp and other places, such as Amazon, is that friends of the establishment can "stuff" the ballot box. I have no agenda other than to warn people about this awful, unclean, health hazard. Go to Elizabeths, go to South Park, Satsuma, Maurepas Cafe, Pizza Delicious - well, you get the idea.

As you can tell, I go out to restaurants a lot, focusing on this wonderful, vibrant area of our city. It is because I love this area so much that I am repeating my warning: Don't go here.

I have not written this negative review because the food didn't taste good, I have written it because the food was bad, as in rotten, spoiled.  And remember, it wasn't just my dish, it was my husband's dish as well.
I popped in last minute for a quick bite! The spring rolls were delicious,  and they do this thing where they make Tacos out of bao bun stuff. so yummy.  super clean,  great decor too. I'll be back!

We eat at Baguette Deli once a month, which is more than we eat at any other establishment. We go for the noodle bowls - they are delicious! Just the right combination of ingredients. I advise you to use the lime and tear the basil into the soup before mixing in all the sauces - they really add a great depth of flavor. 5 stars for the noodles!

4 stars overall because they don't put very much meat in their sandwiches, which are otherwise delicious, and their egg rolls had this weird rubber-like thing in it... maybe an overcooked mushroom? I pulled one out and it looked and tasted like rubber. The bread they use is amazingly crispy on the outside, but only a fine layer - not like hard like many other places. I prefer more meat and mustard, which they also skimped on.

If they have biegnets, get one for the road - they are really yummy!

The absolute best place to go in West Philly! Hassan will make your day by welcoming you to his home! He will ensure you are happy with every choice of lassie or chaat, and always entertain you with something special. Hassan is a gem here in West Philly and I always look forward to being here. Let him suggest new Flavors and things if you're adventurous - hell always make sure you're happy with his creation. :)

Awesome service.  Tremendously professional and personable.  Dr. Biscardi did a fantastic job with my wife, my daughter, and myself.

I highly recommend Dr. Biscardi.
Delivery driver didn't bring entire delivery, said he would go back to store to grab it and didn't return. Store refused to refund money!

Having returned to El Camino Real twice in the last month for dinner, a few conclusions can be made since my last review over a year ago. First of all, it has exploded with popularity. Dinner service, even at 5pm, is extremely popular. It has become a trendy place to see and be seen in the uber-chic neighborhood of Northern Liberties. 

The second observation is directly tied to the first- the outstanding food. No wonder El Camino has drawn rave reviews and grown exponentially since my first taste; the food is magnificent. Without a touch of pretense, the menu reflects both Tex Mex and authentic Mexican cuisine. It is extensive and has options for both the picky and adventurous, the carnivore and vegetarian, the glutton and the lush. 

May I point out that the Fried Pickle Chips are heaven-sent? I sometimes catch myself daydreaming about them at nite. The crisp vinegary crunch of the pickles, the savory, molten hot breading, and of course, the spicy, smooth, simply decadent chipolte mayo dip served on the side makes my mouth water. The flavors explode in your mouth in a WOOSH of satisfaction. The Fried Pickle Chips at El Camino Real are my favorite appetizer in Philadelphia. 

I won't wax poetic about the rest of the menu, but just know that it is nearly equal to the said satisfaction of the Pickle Chips. Just to name a few, I love the Texas cheesesteak, the pork bellies, the chili and the enchiladas.  

Furthermore, El Camino distinguishes itself in decor as well. It isn't overly oozing faux authenticity the way that the Cantina begs to (for real, you use flour tortillas, so let's not pretend this is actually South of the Border, ok??) and yet still satisfies the exotic taste inherent to Tex-Mex. The servers are great, it is not overly loud, and oh yeah, the brunch is amazing too. 

Looking for a good Tex-Mex joint in Philly that will satisfy your Mexican craving? El Camino Real is the place to go.

This place is amazing!  Joseph, the owner, and all the staff are very friendly and welcoming!  I came there for my birthday with some friends and Joseph totally took care of us!  We've been coming back almost every weekend since then because it's just so good!  Food is delicious, coffee is so yummy!  We were there again yesterday and I tried the Turkish coffee for the first time - SO SO good!  I love this place, definitely a must when visiting Clearwater!

Highly recommend Lockwood Chiropractic's. First, my husband went in an attempt to resolve an serious 28 year slow growing non-invasive bladder cancer issue.  Dr. Sharon Whalen recommended several plant based supplements to possibly treat the chemo/radiation damage he received and perhaps treat the cancer itself.  It has been one month and thanks to Dr. Whalen's knowledge of chiropractic medicine, his pain/bleeding distress from the chemo/radiation has ceased thus far (supplements his urologist did not even begin to suggest). 
I also went for a massage from Dr. Alanna McNelly ...it was WONDERFUL.  She went to great lengths to understand the cause of my muscle fatigue. I was quite sensitive, and, she suggested a japanese technique that greatly relieved my sensitivity which relieved my pain!! Felt like a new person...don't know why I didn't address this before.
Beautiful office facility and honest, friendly staff and physicians.

Great Cuban food. Good breakfast sandwiches, Steak sandwiches, and Cafe. Cafe could be hotter, but not big issue. For lunch they have hot bar with Moro(rice with black beans), roast pork, baked chicken, and chicharrons(fried pork). Very Busy early mornings and during lunch hours.

If you don't already love Jazz, the magic of this place will turn you into a believer. The venue is dark and intimate (true to the old school style of jazz venues). The only advice you need to get the maximum experience from this show is to line up early to get a really good seat in the front because there is limited seating via benches and the rest is standing room. The Preservation Hall really takes you back in time with outstanding performances/jazz improvisation. This place is a must-do if you're ever in New Orleans otherwise, you ain't doing NAWLINS the right way.
Excellent service and etoufee was awesome . Also the crawfish soup was good as well. Riggidy Row is coming !
I've been here over a dozen times. The ice cream is ok, I really don't get the hoop-la over ice cream. And to be honest, I hate places that only accept cash.

This is the best restaurant in St. Louis.  I stumbled across it for lunch a few weeks ago and had the best grilled cheese - greens, mushrooms, and just a whiff of truffle oil.  Best restaurant based on just a grilled cheese? What sold me on it was the "No Menu Monday" dinner.  You answer a few questions for the chef including your allergies and major dislikes and she does the rest for an individualized 3 course meal.  The three of us just couldn't get enough. While the poached salmon was exquisite and the steak and chicken dishes phenomenal, it was the scallops that stole the show.  Plus, the 3 course meal is worth far far more than the $30 charge.

Matt C was awesome to work with for my first tattoo. He took my verbal ideas (and horribly drawn ideas) and put them to paper for an awesome concept. I'll definitely be back to visit him to finish out my half sleeve - highly recommend him. 
The rest of the staff was extremely friendly, too. I wouldn't go anywhere else!

I've been in Santa Barbara for 5 years and have never had a better auto repair experience. I primarily worked with Bert Linau on multiple occasions for repairs to my Audi.
He and the entire staff were thorough, courteous and knowledgable. I would definitely recommend this shop to anyone needing auto repairs in the area.
Thanks guys!

I love this place! Today was actually the first time I ever tried their pizza(got a free slice for their "pizza appreciation day"). Pretty good for a local pizza place! I typically get their sandwiches and hoagies. My boyfriend loves their cheesesteaks. All have been so good and fresh. They get them ready quickly and the staff are always so friendly. Definitely recommend this place!! Hope to finally see a mom & pop pizza shop make it in this location.

This grub is spot-on if you're in the mood for Cuban food, it is cafeteria style so you pick what looks good to you. Quick service and reasonable prices. Friendliness of staff could use a bit of work but overall I feel welcome here.Big fan of their yucca and yellow rice, definitely worth stopping by if you want a quick and satisfying lunch.
This place is awesome. Clean! Friendly. They have fruit cups and water for guests aka customers. New clean equipment. Parking is minimal and not open on Sundays. Mani pedi cost 34 bucks!

Joy was such a pleasure to work with when altering my gown. She is very professional and truly cares about making the fit perfect. I had a gown that was 12 sizes too big and I was very concerned if it would even look the same after taking out so much fabric. Joy made it fit like a glove! She made a tedious process effortless (for me anyway) and really came through. Pricing was extremely fair and I would highly recommend her services. Thanks again Joy!  :)

Drove by this sandwich shop a couple of days ago, on the way to another place for lunch. Saw their sign proclaiming they have the #1 Cuban. #1 in what way? Most sold? Most expensive? I live in an area that has pretty much ZERO Cuban sandwiches (the best I've found is 100 miles away, in Indianapolis, but made by a Cuban ex-pat and it is the real deal. Miami style.) I know plenty of places in Tampa to get an authentic Tampa-style Cuban (there is a difference!), and I usually hit several every time I'm in the area. Needless to say I was skeptical.

We had been to a baseball game so we were close, so why not check out Larry's? Giant subs made using quality ingredients - nothing wrong with that. We ordered 12" subs, one Cuban and one cheesesteak, and we split them so each had a sample of the other. Cheesesteak was decent - tasty enough but definitely light on the meat. Might give it three stars alone.

The Cuban was made properly for a Tampa-style sandwich. The bread was from a local Cuban bakery. I think they toasted it dry so it wasn't quite as good as I'm used to, but it was OK. The problem was the amount of ingredients. I think there was one slice of everything, except maybe the salami, which was in one layer only. I am used to these sandwiches being well-stuffed, so I was definitely disappointed. (There is another Cuban shop literally not one block away that would blow this place away, plus they have great black bean soup. We should have gone there. Within a half mile, I can think of two or three other places that are all way better.)  The damage: over $20 for two sandwiches and two medium fountain drinks.

So, #1 Cuban? I think not.

Some additional comments added 27 April:

After re-reading my review, as well as several other accurate ones, I think I may see the problem. Larry's claims "Just voted #1 Cuban Sub in Tampa". Is there really any place in Tampa that refers to their Cuban Sandwich as a CUBAN SUB? I can't think of any, not even Publix! So, they could very well have been voted #1 as they claim. By whom? Their employees? 

One of the local newspapers has done a bracket-type pizza competition in the past. Perhaps they could do one for Cuban "subs". My guess is Larry's doesn't even get out of the first round.

We haven't been out for Sushi in years! We loved that they had hibachi for the kids and Sushi for the adults! They are sushi artists and the plates come me out with such amazing presentation! They have really creative rolls that are super tasty. The hibachi chef was great and did a great job interacting with the table and our waitress made sure we got a good taste of the menu!

Had a great lunch here today. Errands ran long today and every restaurant we kept going to was closed and just by chance we stumbled upon this place. The wait staff was very friendly and the food is home made and you can tell. I had a pizza and it was great. Some people have complained about the wait times but you have to understand it's home made food not frozen and pulled from a fridge and warmed up. The bread is made fresh daily and had we not been so full we would have tried the home made banana cream pie. If you want some good pizza or pasta give it a try. It's just a great little place for reasonably priced meal. I will definitely go back.
Very nice rooms.  Not a great place to book weddings.  No hotel bar and they will generally shut down any post wedding party at 1 am.   Lame.

Great coffee shop, great selection of great pastries, a third the price of Starbucks. My new favorite place to study. There's not a ton of outdoor seating, but there are about three small tables that stay dry even when it's raining, and they're just the right size for doing homework at. I'd give it five stars except (1) the staff could be a little friendlier and more helpful and (2) it's pretty dim inside if you're trying to work. Parking in this neighborhood is tough in general, and if you go anytime around Jazz Fest don't bother to take your car, but it's fine if you don't mind walking a block or two.

Went to this restaurant on recommendations for lunch on a Wednesday by family. We were seated immediately, which was great... received our water and iced teas quickly, which was also great. Everything else went downhill from there very quickly. I have a very serious allergy to avocados wich end in anaphylactic shock, which I mention immediately upon arrival to any restaurant. So far I never had any issues about restaurant kitchens dealing with this until yesterday. The waitress advised me that they would NOT be able to produce avocado free sushi for me in their establishment. The cooks would NOT clean the surface  properly  to ensure that no avocado would make contact with my food. Slightly shocked about the nastyness of the dirty surface they prepare their sushi on. I also did not receive any salad since they chop the greens on the same surface as the fish... hopefully a food inspector will read this!! GROSS, stay away if you have any allergies or a sensitive stomach...
Great food and staff. Wandered in looking for good food quickly and got everything we wanted. Will definitely be back.

Get ready to have some stale food with sad faces. The food served is of poor quality and seem like it was not freshly cooked. The host  was also not welcoming . I wont suggest going to the place. Worst Indian food I ever had

This was my second restaurant week stop this go-around and tbh I was v disappointed. It was a true bummer!

So, my qualms were mainly the food - for starters it was four courses. The first course was an antipasto board and let me tell you, it was a sad excuse for an antipasto board. I was looking forward to it most, but it turned out to be dry and bland. There were little cheese balls and olives and I don't even know what else. I can't remember because it was so forgettable. 

Second, I got the verde salad and it was eh. It didn't have enough avocado and it was also way too bitter. I was so excited for the pasta I ordered, but was again...sorely disappointed. The servings were small and it was extremely garlicky. For dessert I got the "chocolate cake." It came out and my friend said, "is this cake for ants." It was a tiny little circle brownie that you can get pre-packaged at Costco. 

I would totally understand if this spot had small portions cus the food was decadent and luxurious, but it wasn't at all.  It was nothing special or tasty. 

I did like the aesthetic, although casual, it was also modern and chic. It was located, however, in a weird spot attached to a We Work on 24th and Walnut. 

In all, I probs won't be back and 24 has gotta step up their restaurant week game!

Venue: clean, large, with indoor and outdoor seating. Plenty of room for large and small groups. Even areas with a pretty romantic vibe.

Service: horrendous. Our server literally hated her life or her job. She came out to "greet" us and already was annoyed that she was about to serve 13 people who would've tipped her more than 20% had she showed some enjoyment out of her job. She only got 20% because of that reason. She was miserable, we don't even know why, we paid with 1 card, we all ordered all at once. We only asked for additional beers, it was the easiest table to serve. I just can't imagine why she is working in the service industry when she clearly does not enjoy it. Hurts the company and restaurant. Nonetheless, this is about the food more than the service. Just had to mention it though.

Prices: over the top pricey. Drinks to food, small portions, barely any alcohol in the mixed drinks. Just poor choice in costs when it comes to such poor qualities. Although the pizzas were enjoyed by everyone around the table, but the other ancillary dishes were subpar, the poutine, not with poutine cheese. The wings were bland.

Beers: pricey, but again, had plenty of selection so everyone eventually found their top choice. $2 tiny tiny flights. There are many other breweries in the area that have better pricing and beer selection.

I will say we ended up sitting outside in the humidity even though there were 3 large tables inside that had no one sitting at them. They refused to let us sit there, by the time we left, 2 of those tables were still empty and remained open. I don't understand their thinking behind refusing us. We were a mix of all ethnicities and everyone was dressed well, so I don't know how they judged us to stick us outside rather than let us opt for the inside table.

Unfortunately, it was such a poor experience, will not be back. Hope for future customers to beware and proceed with caution. Happy eating and drinking!

This place is clean, the food is yummy and the service is friendly, prompt and attentive. They had some pretty amazing drink specials as well as food specials for happy hour. A huge, very open bar allows you to see the whole room from wherever you're sitting. The bartender and food server were both extremely pleasant and friendly. (Just an FYI that the food and the drinks are rung up separately. There is a bill for each one.)They both waited and kept checking on us before we were ready to give them an order. My French martinis were perfectly made and my burger was cooked the way I asked. Will definitely be back!
paid 40 dollars and its still dirty inside out. complained to manager didnt do anything. save your money and time

I'm not vegetarian, which is why this wouldn't be my first choice for Indian. What I've had was very tasty though! Try the kofta! The food is decent, and offered mild or spicy. The Korma and Paneer Tikka Masala are on point!! The samosas are great as well. The location is convenient and prices are lower than most Indian Restaurants I've been to. It's  authentic and the portions are large. I highly recommend for vegan or vegetarian people!

Brunch at this place is the best!  Salmon scramble was so good as were all of the accompanying items.  Also tried the blueberry marscapone stuffed french toast, which was just as good!  It wasn't too sweet, great flavor.  I will be back here often!

Have been seeing Jenn for my hair cuts for a few years now, she's the best.  Always funny and talkative and does a great cut/blow out.  I recently started coloring my hair (out of necessity, thanks grey hair) with Erika and she's been just as great as Jenn.  I wasn't totally feelin' the first color we tried, so when I went back today to get it re-done, I told her my concerns, what I thought I wanted, she mixed it up and voila!  I love it!!  I don't like having to sit in the salon for a long time, but as we got to talking, she painted me up, I sat for 30 minutes and I was done.  OH!  Almost forgot (almost) the best part.  Thanh shampooed me and honestly, I wanted to take her out for a drink after.  She's a magician with the scalp massage.  Only criticism for the salon is that (although I had to reschedule from last weekend) I called to make an appointment with Erika and Jenn on the same day and apparently they have a call center who makes their appointments.  I was told my appointment was set for Saturday at 10:30 -- and it was, but not with Jenn.  I had to get a haircut with another stylist (her name was Lorraine and she was sweet, but not Jenn)!!  Overall, my transition into more regular hair maintenance has been an easy and painless process thanks to Adolf.

Service was great. Food was even better! I ordered the Chicken Chorizo Etouffee and enjoyed every bite. Once you walk inside it goes from Broadripple, Indiana to New Orleans, Louisiana. Not my first time here and, definitely, will not be my last. 

P.S. Make sure you get the extra bread!

They do what they say they do...and really well.

Plus! You can get their house-made granola (it's not cheap but oh, it's so worth it) and it makes you feel better about mowing down on gelato!

Comfy seating - a nice post-date spot.
Great comfort food, good service, and reasonable prices. Never had a bad meal here.
Depending on what you order can be $$ but the food is awesome. It's not a fancy place and it's a busy place but it is soo worth it!

I was here the other day, nice south philly gem. 
Very old school, luncheonette style. 
Got the six pack of dogs, we mixed it up. 
The works (mustard, greek sauce and onions) 
Texas Tommy (wiz and bacon) 
the Texan (hash brown, onions and peppers) 

They're served on club rolls, just enough to fill you up.
Decent prices, quality stuff.

BAD Business!  If I could give negative stars, I would!... When I moved they shut off my ATM/CREDIT CARD while I was away on business because I called in a request for a new ATM card.  I was stuck in another city using only my company credit card.... 
The manager was not helpful or understanding of my situation when I called from New York to see what happened and said there was little they could do.  
BAD BAD BAD business!   If your looking for that home town bank, great, go here; but if that is the case, I am doubting that you have a pc or Internet access.

I say they have a solid pizza, based on getting slices there twice. Large, thin/foldable, with the right amount of cheese/sauce and a crust you'll want to finish. The second time I walked in about 5-10 minutes after closing, but they still were down to sell whatever slices they had, so they seem like decent folk. Getting a pie should only be better, which I hope to do soon. They're a block away from Main st., so if you're in the area for the evening, they're quite accessible.

Edit: After having ordered a couple pies from them, as expected they were great. I have to say, the pies are smaller than expected, particularly given the largeness of their individual slices. I'd dock them a point for their pies being smaller than what I'd expect for a typical pie, and a bit pricier too ($16). Oh well :\  If you overlook that though, you're in for a delicious treat. For myself personally, they were the tastiest NY style pizzas I've had in Philly thus far. Cheese, sauce and crust were all on point (I was really surprised by the crust...it's hard to find crust this tasty around here). I have to mention that they do this strange swirly thing with the sacuce/cheese, so that they're next to each other, and not layered on top of  one other (it's kind of like a margarita pie, except in a swirl instead of in splotches). Don't worry about that, the texture and tastes is just fine when you take a big bite into it. 

Anyhow, TL;DR  if you're in the Manayunk/Roxborough area, I highly recommend making them your go-to pizza place.
Best sushi in town!!!! Do yourself a favor and sit at the sushi bar with Jared or Tuan.. super creative and talented chefs. Drinks are delicious and food is exceptional. Great experience all around!!
Love this place!! I come regularly for massage at Stone Temple Massage (Rick Teliga) and to get my haircut from Jen Marino! Everyone is so friendly and professional!!

Came to this place after seeing the reviews. The staff is nice and the place is clean, and the other customers seemed to like it. 
I'm not happy with my haircut. It's hard to mess up military styles (and I've never seen anyone have trouble with them), but after 50 minutes of the guy trying just to make the cut even on both sides I decided to leave. My hair is cut to 2 different lengths on opposite sides of my head and is completely shaven shorter than both sides all the way up the back of my head. 
By the way, their prices have gone up since the earlier reviews. They charged me $30 for something I have to go have someone else fix. That's right: $30 for their simplest haircut. I would have been willing to revisit this place on the chance that I just got a poor barber or he was having a bad day, but I don't know how this place can justify charging so much for so little quality.
Edit: the manager called me after I complained about the experience and made a generous offer to try to earn my business back. I'm not interested in returning for now but I've added another star because I appreciate the professional gesture.

I used to dine at Albasha weekly in Baton Rouge. When I found out they were also in Metairie, I made my fiancée abandon our old middle eastern favorites. Albasha is all we eat now! It's worth the drive. Typically do take out. Love the big mezze platter of everything . Or the combo chicken schwarmA and gyros is my favorite !
We love Albasha!

Dinner was very enjoyable!  Nice service despite being busy. Had the broiled oysters, bistro tender. Everything was wonderful but the only reason I didn't give it 5 stars was everything needed a little salt lol!  The creme brûlée was definitely 5 star and be sure to experiment with the wide varieties of after-dinner coffees with a kick! :)
Such great food and bartender Joe is awesome!!!   Must is their She Crab Bisque. Makes you glow

I have dined at some of the finest restaurants in the world.  LaCampagnola is one of my favorites.  It can be a local bar or a fine restaurant.  The food has a consistent high quality and the staff cares.
The sushi is delicious and they always have great service.  We like going here because it's never over crowded like a lot of sushi restaurants near state street.  Try the spicy edamame!

My mom always told me I'd die if I went to breweries - she was almost right today. I came into the Barrio Brewery and sat in the one chair with a broken leg (they must keep it for the posers). After recovering from the fall, I enjoyed an excellent IPA and, even better, a white IPA.

The pizza is great. Brusell sprouts on a pizza is where it's at.  Their online ordering is awful.  Tonight was the 4th time I've ordered and every time has been a hassle. The first 2 times, they called to go over the entire order due to issues with their website. The 3rd time they didn't get our order at all, when we called an hour later, they ran out of what we wanted and then delivered what they had on hand plus they still charged us!  Tonight we ordered and called to make sure they received it, they didn't. The website also doesn't mention they don't take credit cards online so you have to call them anyway.  They need to take online ordering off their website and fire whoever designed it for them.  Try the pizza but don't bother with the stress of ordering online!

Awesome cupcakes. Employees are great too. Butterfinger is my favorite, with resees and Twix coming in as a close second and third. Prices are fair considering the quality of these cupcakes. We go back any time we have a sweet tooth

the crawfish sidney was tasty and the jambalaya's flavor was perfectly balanced, but there were a couple things that made our experience less than stellar. first, the service was ssslllooowww. we waited 15 minutes to get water and a drink order in, then another 40 for our food. the waiter tried to tell my husband that elysian was a local beer (it is not), and then served him one even after he requested something else. our food had obviously been sitting around bc the top layer of my sidney had begun to firm and my husband was displeased with the fact that he literally got one piece of chicken and one piece of sausage in his jambalaya. furthermore, the shrimp in the jambalaya had not been deveined. we won't ever go back.

I recently dined here twice so I felt compelled to update my 2011 review. I have to say, the 12 inch cheesesteak that I got here was one of the best that I've had. My wife ordered a pizza, which was also very good and we split an order of large fries. The meal was excellent and the price was very good! As an update, I can say that I shall return!

It's been a long while since I have been to a salon, but I must say, Tangerine AVEDA Lifestyle Salon impressed me. First off, the salon was very clean and well decorated; it contributed to the overall relaxing atmosphere. Food and drinks were offered when I arrived and while I was waiting for my hair to get done.

Cindy Bough worked with me, and she does wonders. Not only was she affable, but she was very down to earth and pleasant to talk to/work with. I learned more about her as a person, as well as the hair treatment/style I was getting (I got a balayage for the first time). She was gentle on my hair, and seemed genuinely interested in getting to know me and making sure that I got want I wanted out of the visit. I would definitely recommend the salon, and most importantly Cindy, to anyone interested in getting their hair colored. I am very pleased with the experience, and I hope to see her again in a couple of months. I highly recommend Cindy to anyone getting their hair colored!!!!!

*Also, I apologize if I didn't seem as excited as I actually was inside - it was getting late, the salon was already getting closed, and I had a long day at work and studying. Thank you so much again Cindy - it was a wonderful visit.

Yay! I'm a fan, but not of their prices and cramped space.  We opted to get ramen for dinner in the city.  This was our first time venturing for ramen.  I hopped onto yelp and decided to head over here.  I remember reading about this place on foobooz before so i was curious.  Plus it seemed more fun than the other ramen places.  It was almost a perfect night.  We got parking right across the street and seated immediately at the bar.  Sad to say i kept on bumming elbows with the woman next to me.  I wish there was a bit more elbow room.  Note to the owners: elbow room is a necessity when eating noodles!  Just try eating with your elbows tucked in, not so fun eh?!?  Also, i would have to minus points for the bartender.  He served me a flight of the sake (one was soju).  However, he did not shake the sake.  It was a nigori, i mean how could he not know.  Sad to say i just let it go, usually i would have mentioned something but it was just a shot.  Okay i've vented.

We ordered the mung bean and the chicken bun.  Both were delicious and the bun was not of the white dough kind that was expected.  This one was more of the brown flakey kind.  Nevertheless it was good and i would order it again.  They did forget to bring out the special cheeseburger bun that the bf ordered.  Next was the garlic flavored wings.  The carnivorous bf devoured it.  I had the smoked fish ribs.  This has got to be one of the best thing i ever ate.  It was a paku which is a cousin of the piranha.  The dish was very flavorful. The skin was crispy and perfect.  It was definitely a party in my mouth.  We ordered the pork and miso cod ramen.  The cod was cooked perfectly with a little crispness.  The noodles were cooked al dente, it was great.  The broth was mediocre, i'm trying to remember it but there was really nothing memorable about it.  The bf finished his bowl completely.  

Yikes! we got the bill and for 2 people it was about 86 with tip.  What a pricey ramen experience!

It was our first time to Tarpon Springs and we had just taken a Sponge-Diving boat tour.  We were looking for lunch and stopped here.  The menu had a great selection of typical Greek dishes.

The food was excellent.  The spanakopita was flaky, cheesy & delicious!  The waiter was generous with ice tea re-fills. It was a perfect lunch.

We followed this later in the day by stopping back at their bakery and trying out some of their selections of Greek pastries.  My favorite was the Greek Cannoli... loaded with more flaky phyllo dough!

Went with a voucher and am now a regular.  As I can actually afford this place on my own.  Sure, at other places I might get more pampering, but I'd rather pay less, stick to business, get my face glowing, do extractions, etc.. No, I don't get a fancy robe & slippers or flavored water.  Whatever.  Everything is clean and professional and I'm treated with the right products for ME and no pressure to buy anything. So less fu fu but the facial itself is AWESOME!

Village Inn is exactly what it advertises to be. A bit nicer than a dinner.
Good for them, good old American food.
Breakfast, brunch, lunch, dinner or coffee and conversation, it can't be beat.
Staff is okay, not overly friendly,  but usually alert, get orders correct and ready for refills.
Unless it is a busy time, they literally don't mind if you stay for hours.
Great place to meet someone for the fi rst time. Great after a night out on the town. Food is usually consistent, some items better than others.
One thing I love is they listen to their customers. Hence the vip or is it vib menu selections, they are great, separately they would be a fortune. Here your choices from super healthy to cholesterol city are all laid out for you.
Most of the salads and sandwiches are good or better. Most burgers very good. Breakfast skillets, omlets, waffles, and even, whole wheat pancakes. .. all very good.  I have not had many dinner entrees, so won't address them.
By gourmet standards they aren't very good, but they are great for what they are & we have a place for them in our lives.
I love the carafe of coffee on the table and the sugar free syrup, because they listen to their customer. 
A sign of a great reastaurant is the ability to meet your customers needs!

Good local brewery with some interesting brews. Recommend you sample before buy - some are a little strange and might not appeal to usual preferences. Staff of very helpful so it's not a problem. Great atmosphere and plenty of TVs. 

Sheep Tease New Zealand IPA is really good with imported hops. Not so for Nice Rack Mango IPA - even the staff recommend blending it with their other IPA if you are looking for more traditional IPA flavor. 

Parking is limited since this place is popular and located in strip center. Happy hour is 4-7 PM.
Great beer! Go here for the beer. The food is secondary to the fantastic beer. Don't get me wrong, the food and service were great as well.

I've read some of the other reviews that mention having to wait which I did not have to do. I'm going to preface this with wow, what a great restaurant / great experience. I had dinner on Wednesday evening with a group of four. From the skewer menu we ordered the Grilled Squid, the Chicken Gizzard skewers, and the Beef Tendon & Brisket. All of these proteins were perfectly cooked and spiced. The portions were extremely generous. My favorite of the three was the squid with the beef being #2. For entrees we ordered Chicken with Mushroom in Chicken Soup, Crisp Sautéed Pork, Salt Pepper Calamari, Szechwan Spicy Shrimp, and the Special Cumin Calamari fried rice. For me the standouts here were the Salt Pepper Calamari and the Special Cumin Calamari Fried Rice. Are you seeing a trend here? Yes, I love squid. These were both amazing though. The Salt Pepper Calamari was perfectly cooked. It was crispy, salty, and had sliced garlic in the dish. The fried rice was perfectly spiced with cumin. The rice was fluffy. The squid in it was not the least bit rubbery. I would order both of these dishes again and again. This is probably going to be my new favorite Chinese Restaurant! I'm going to need to work my way through this menu.

This is My first time  at the Peppermill 

Let's start  from the most disappointed  and most important facts , THE ROOM 

It was like entering  to a horror house filled with surprises,

We entered the room 3 steps into it and i was NOT able to breath fresh air ,instead  we were berthing this extremely  strong odor killer  of some sort  (i am not a allergy type of guy )  but this was strong  smell , maybe try to hide something ??? keep reading  more surprises to come ...
at this point  i was not concerned , i just turn the ac on and let  it air out, right .

5 steps later  i noticed a plastic bag with personal property from previews guest !!!!we thought  ok its all good.. lets put that aside and call maintenance to have it remove .

Getting bored? here comes the best part!

we need to put the cherry on top of the cake !

It was  painful.. i saw another phone  (yes they have 2 phones) i ran across the room to try to make a phone call  to demand  a different room. and so they did .

The Grand suite turned out a Horror suite

No happy happy ending , sorry

This is a divey bar that is not very far at all from the convention center.  We went there to have a mid afternoon lunch, and the pulled pork sandwich was excellent.  Was quiet and so fairly fast service.  A small amount of outdoor seating.  Good beer choices.

Smelled great from outside and sure looked very vibrant and interesting on the inside.  We had the buffet on Sunday.  Didn't see much staff and being past our hunger point we thought best option.  The food was bland.  I kept trying to like each dish...I sampled many and was constantly disappointed.  The naan was hot and okay.  Restaurant has a little area in the back where you can shop.  Loved the natural light and decor.  Unless something changes I wouldn't go back.

We discovered this little treasure accidentally 
The food here is to DIE for 
Totally  home cooking style 
The food here is better than what we are in Cambodia 
We had the cabbage salad , chicken with pumpkin sautéed , lemon grass spur soup 
Thank you to grandma Paula , Auntie Dyna Mother Sophia, Brother Jordan

Went there on opening night! The place is beautiful! Everything was excellent from the presentation and taste to the service and delicious desserts! They have to have the best tequila menu in the city! Can't wait to go back!

Unfriendly waiter, bare minimum service who couldn't even smile. He made us feel guilty for eating as much sushi as possible after paying for all you can eat.  "Will that be all?" We'll tell you when we're finished . 

2 stars because Sushi is decent.

This place has quickly become our regular spot. The ricotta cheese, rosemary potatoes, and beets salad are just delightful!!

Aside from being a little too salty... Everything is good. The ambiance, the service, the charm.... :)
Really, really good sandwiches, great prices, decent portions...just lacks adequate seating for a busy day.

The location is five star, the service four stars and the food was two at best. Clam chowder was okay but the bread bowl was stale and tough. We also had a crab salad sandwich and it was just okay. 

Pack a lunch and just eat at the pier.

Really 2.5 stars.  Arrived shortly before 1 on a Saturday to an empty hostess station and not a server in sight.  There were three tables with customers so not busy.  We waited a few minutes and the bartender saw us and seated us in the bar.  She was fairly friendly.  As stated in other reviews the chips are not complementary.  I had a craving for nachos as my meal anyway so I didn't care.  The bartender recommended the buffalo chicken nachos so that is what I ordered.  You do not want the nachos.  The tortilla chips are too thick, under salted and boring.  The toppings were quite good.  Hubby ordered the restaurant's equivalent of a pulled pork sandwich and fries.  Sad fries... too greasy so they lack crispness.  The sandwich he found to be just ok.  The pork in my opinion had great flavor.  We were underwhelmed and in a town with lots of Mexican food we will not be back.
Excellent food, excellent service. A little busy and small, but it's cozy. I would recommend checking this place out.

Firehouse subs puts all other sub shops to shame.  Their customer service is outstanding.  Everyone is really friendly.  The food is good.  I haven't had a bad experience yet.  I really like the soda machine.  It's fun to experiment with different flavors and brands.
I love chipotle . They're very quick and I like that u can show them what u want on your food. I always get the burrito bowl. There food is always excellent and the workers are very friendly .

i really wanted to like this place. I got the Philly style one. it was soggy and super buttery for some reason. maybe it was the mustardy mayo sauce that was on it. pretty bland. I ended up picking through the other half after eating the first and just ended up throwing away half of it. I'll have to try the Komchi version next time...if I go back.

This was a horrible breakfast and diner area. Took very long to serve and extremely unpleasant service. Disgusting women at the register and very rude. Way too overpriced and definitely not worth to sit and relax either. Do not go here.

There's the part of your life before you've had a sticky bun here, and then the rest of it where you're telling the world how incredible this place is. The sticky buns are off the charts delicious. The service is fast and highly efficient. Only good things come from Fritz's.

We tried Cafe Ponte based on a recommendation, and the reviews. The food and service exceeded my expectations! My husband and I like different qualities in our servers, but ours impressed both of us. To the point my husband actually wanted to leave a nicer tip! Kudos to the service because that doesn't happen too often! The Steve McQueen cocktail impressed me more than a standard cocktail. Amazing bread choices. Unique beet salad that I'd eat every day if I could but even I'd say this one is strictly for foodies. I'm all about a good steak and my hubby's NY was tasty, but I had hands down the best Sea Bass I've had in years. The only other close second would have been at Oyster Catchers and even there's wasn't this good from recent memory. Can't wait to go back to Cafe Ponte!!!

My mom ordered my sons cake here for his 4th birthday. It was a beautiful cake and the flavor we got was "chocolate truffle" We were very happy with the results. The cake was so moist and the frosting was gentle enough to eat every bite that was on your plate. I'm so used to going to parties and the store bought cake being so sweet that my teeth actually hurt so i end up scraping the frosting to the side of the plate. In this case, it's completely opposite.

Highly recommend the best barber shop in Tennessee. 

They welcomed a large group of friends who came to support a very brave woman shaving her head in preparation for her chemo treatments. It was an emotional moment for everybody, and I do not think we could have been at a better place for it. 

A special thanks to Eric Miller. Attentive and focused on his work while having at least ten people standing right behind him and 70 more pairs of eyes watching him on the live stream.

Worst pho I've had in a while.  The tendon is harder than plastic.  They need to take that crash of the menu, if they don't know how to cook it.  It's an offense to be served it.  The pho is also overly oily.  The flashy ads on the front of the store are a facade hides that this place is rather bad.
Zero benefit to ordering ahead. You still have to wait in line with everyone else when you get there and my drinks weren't even made.
I'm a big fan of dives but this was just dirty looking.  I didn't even want to touch the doors to enter.   Everything had a nasty layer of greasy scum.  Food was good though.

Delicious experience here at Harry's! I ordered the chicken sandwich, which included sauteed spinach, roasted red pepper, pesto and mozzarella on a extremely fresh bun. This sandwich was accompanied by sweet potato friend and kale slaw. What a combo!! I will be back to try the tacos. Thanks for the great experience Harry.

Amazing. Fried Oyster salad, crawfish bisque. I'll be dreaming about that salad!! Great service. We walked in with a 9 month old and 4 year old. Were nervous but were seated in the back. Kids behaved, dinner was amazing... wish we would have ordered more off the menu!

Too expensive...$265.00 for 3 nights? I understand that this is a busy weekend for holloween...but this isn't the beach or a resort on a fancy island...your in the middle of nowhere...i been coming here for the same weekend for the last 5yrs this is my last...i would rather spend my money going to a five star rated campground like castaways in ocean city md...every year i see less and less local people coming here...
Yay!!! I love this place! There are so many more delicious options than any coffee place in town! The staff is easy going and put a special touch on everything.

I can't say enough good things about this place. The name is misleading: it's New Orleans style cuisine, and it's superb. We had the fried shrimp po boy and the jambalaya special. Make sure you get the bacon popcorn to snack on while sampling their wide selection of beers. My go-to place in all of Philadelphia.

Very nice spot with a balcony overlooking the main street.  Really nice ambiance inside and outside.  Wine variety quite extensive - I had thought it would have been more local stuff but it is really a broad variety with many wines from CA as well as beer from the West coast.  The cheese platter was a nice accompaniment and much needed after a flight of tastings...

Tried the flight of wines (2 whites and 3 reds) and also a beer and a glass of wine.  The flight was a nice balance and ranged from the viognier to the shiraz.  All were reasonable and the ladies behind the bar were very helpful and accommodating, helping us to choose some wines by the glass and also some beers. 

Great spot and great service.  Will be back.

Puckett's is delightful. My family and I went to Puckett's in downtown Franklin on the last night of our vacation to Nashville. Our party of 5 was seated after about 30 minutes (it was a weeknight). The live music was loud enough to enjoy and sing along, but not so loud that we couldn't have a conversation. Our server was attentive and very helpful. 

The food was delicious. Please get the chicken & waffles. I don't want you to experience the lifelong regret you'll experience if you order something else.  My husband said the catfish was good, and my mother-in-law thought the chicken fried chicken was delicious. My daughter took five bites of her grilled cheese sandwich, which is high praise as she usually refuses to try new foods of any kind. 

We would definitely return! If you are in Franklin, it should definitely be on your list.

This place looks the part and the service was good. We came here for a casual Saturday brunch, while the atmosphere was good the food was decidedly average. After finishing my steak and eggs, which was drowned in an overly-salty sauce, all I could think of water water...

I've been back again and the fish was worth the trip. 

Lynn mentioned about the Onion Rings and I am sorry to hear they were processed.  A place like this should be slicing and dipping their own.

Come on Guys, throw an onion on that sushi counter and get busy.

Our waitress was very knowledgeable about Gluten Free menu items (I have Celiac Disease, so GF is not an option for me), and the blackened shrimp I ordered were really great.  This restaurant is right next to Jackson Square, so it is a bit of a tourist trap, but so is most of the Quarter!

Food is always great here. I've had one really bad experience here with the Daniel guy here, he's a very unfriendly guy and should not be working here. But the server Sofia is definitely the most friendliest server there. She's always smiling and talking to you making you feel comfortable, so always ask for Sofia.

We came here with really high expectations after reading all the rave reviews here, but were surprisingly disappointed by the food. We got the biscuit with goat sausage gravy to start, and the cobia and seafood pirlou as our main dishes, along with a glass of wine each (Malbec/Moscato). The cobia was well made, but the portion was legitimately just way to small to ever suffice as a meal. The pirlou was bland, and the peas ended up masking the taste of any other part of the dish. The presentation of the pirlou was definitely rather boring, and didn't do it any favors. The calamari was way too salty, and especially at the prices they charge here, we expected much much better.

The wines were good I guess.

Me and my friend came to this buffet cause everybody spoke so while about it. We came for brunch and it was not to our liking. The food looked good but was not good. I thought the prime rib steak was ok but that was about it. I want to try the seafood buffet but after having the brunch i am very skeptical after having the brunch.

I am not from around here, but I had a fabulous experience here. The owner was so kind and generous and the food was dare I say it, better than chipotle! I had the burrito with pork and it was so flavorful and the waitresses were more than helpful with getting me extra cheese when I asked. My friends got the chili soup and a sandwich (I forgot which type) and they stuffed themselves silly. The food is prepared fresh before every service and the salsas are made every day. Everything is delicious and the restaurant was beautiful!

I have been to Garden Bakery numerous time to enjoy the delicious assortment of baked goods, but never had an actual meal here. That changed yesterday when I headed upstairs to have lunch.

We were seated by a very friendly waitress. Looking at the overwhelming menu - pages and  pages with dense lists of soups, snacks, entrees, beverages, rice dishes, congees, barbecue, rice dishes, and just about anything else you can think of, it took us quite a while to decide upon what we would have.

When we finally did, we decided to stick with the tried and true - he had lemon chicken while I had Szechuan beef on rice.

The lemon chicken was a large potion, cut up with covered in a lemon sauce that was not too sweet. The chicken was a little on the chewy side and overcooked in some spots, but overall it was crispy and delicious. 

A word to describe my meal is: mountain. For $9 I had a huge pile of white steamed rice covered in crispy beef shreds and vegetables. I would have labelled the meal ginger beef, as the sauce had a mild and pleasant ginger taste, while Szechuan beef tends to be spicier. That aside, it was wonderful. The sauce enhanced the rice and there was no way I was going to be able to finish the entire meal. Fortunately, I was eating with someone who has a never-ending appetite, so little went to waste (although I am sure for both of us much of it went to waist).

Afterwards, we strolled through the downstairs bakery area and picked out a few items. I enjoyed some sweet buns, caked slices, bean cakes, and other treats for several days after.

Prices in the restaurant are very reasonable. Individual dishes are no more than around $12 at the most, with a variety of snack dishes and smaller items that are very inexpensive. Garden Bakery would be a great place to go with a group to share a wide variety of food.

You really need to sit on the floor near one of the corner pillars to really get a view of how beautiful this place is. I'm from Philadelphia and in my 24 going on 50 years of living, I didn't realize until I finally stopped and took a seat, what I was missing. 

It is so easy to quickly pass through this place on any given day running to a Septa or Amtrak train, but seriously folks, take my word for it, as a fan of ancient Greek architecture, I was blown away. Why was I sitting on the floor? My one pet peeve about this place, the lack of functioning outlets in good spaces. So after finding one at pillar 10, taking my place on the floor with my plugged in phone, I decided to take a break from electronics and look around. Looking up from the ground is so much better than I expected. I mean, really, the huge faux Corinthian columns and the coffered ceiling are gorgeous. 

Space wise, it does not have the overall complexity of Penn Station or the nastiness of Newark. It is a clean and efficient station. It offers tasty (but sometimes a bit steep price wise) restaurants and coffee shops for the weary traveler and nearby worker. 

You can take Septa regional rail from the station and across the street catch the Bolt Bus or Megabus out of town, and Septa El Subway Line to West Philly or Downtown/Frankford. 

The only other reason this place doesn't get 5 stars is because their car rental system and service sucks hard.

Erroneously called More than just ice cream simply because the menu covers more than desserts is a little unfair because the only thing they do well is ice cream and desserts.

I've had the food here and was pretty unhappy, so were all of my friends. Everything felt a bit stale and also a little flavorless. It's our own fault for not knowing that no one comes here for dinner.

Luckily, the desserts and ice cream concoctions make up for it pretty well. I've had cupcakes, shakes, ice cream, brownies, etc, you name it and all have been awesome. Nothing is fake-sweet here, everything is super sugary and delicious and that's the reason I keep coming back.

Word of advice to everyone else-- stick with the desserts. They may serve more than just ice cream but that doesn't mean you should order it.
Love this BYO Pho place. So glad it's getting cold again, just to have an excuse to go out for Pho here. Prices are very reasonable and the food is delicious.

Great tasting and looks pretty healthy. The wife loves it here, that also scores points. I got the wild strawberry milkshake, it was thick, just the right amount of sweetness, and true to taste. Nice job.

Read reviews prior to going saying to be there early. Arrived at 7 am. Parking lot around back- have to get a ticket to put on dash but was free on Saturday morning when we went. Got a table as soon as we walked in. The place was already getting pretty busy. By 7:25, there was a line out of the door. I got buttermilk pancakes- AMAZING. They literally melt in your mouth. Some of the best pancakes I've ever eaten. Our waitress seemed really unhappy, never cracked a smile. My boyfriend and I both got scrambled eggs. His was perfect, mine was really runny. When we left, the line had managed to snake out the door, down the sidewalk, and around the corner of the building. Would definitely recommend coming here.

Sad, very sad!  What happened to charm it was b4?
The place is cold, noisy, and so sterile. Not a place I want to visit again.

Great pizza used to be hard to find. Until Now. I just had a margarita pizza. Light crispy crust, flavorful tomato sauce, delicious cheese. LOVED IT. I can't wait to get another one. So excited that I know where to get a great pizza.
This place is the bomb. Their food is always AMAZING. Very quiet in the restaurant, and everyone is really nice.

Today was special.
