Now that none of the original techs are here and they chew through writers due to corporate decisions &policies  this store is terrible. I will no longer be spending my hard earned money here. I went to the dealer instead and spent $330 and was out under 2hrs and they washed the car for me. The oil change was only $60 but I had them do a few other things since I was here and leaving for the poconos for the weekend. So Pepboys lost more than an oil change by screwing around with their pricing.

This is my favorite ice cream shop around. I don't really like those chain froyo places that seem to be all the rave now. The ice cream here is delicious and they have many flavors. I love the birthday cake batter flavor! The only thing is that they only accept cash, which I never carry so I always have to go to an ATM or get cash back before we go here.

So,  second time there.  First time was about 2 months ago and we didn't stay as they had a hour and a half wait to be seated.   This time we did.  So when going need to be aware of time and day going it will matter on how busy they are. 

Our server was nice even if we did keep her coming back a few times to see if we were ready.  Their having an awesome menu and us being so hungry we couldn't make up or minds was not a good combo.  In the end we settled on The Triple (smoked cheddar, boneless short ribs, double smoked bacon and horseradish slaw) and the Bison (ground Buffalo,  apple bacon chutney,  blue cheese,  red onion and baby frisee).  

To go along with all this wonderful food they have is their HUGE selection of craft brews.  If you are not sure what you want or only want a little they offer sample sizes of 4 ounces for $2.  This way I was able to have an amazing stout and try something new that our server suggested.  It paired with my meal really well,  just like she said it would.  Not one I would normally get,  or would get again add it's not the kind I like,  but it did go well together.

We were all incredibly impressed by the menu. The food was delicious. The menu is flexible enough for anyone. The staff was spectacular and made it a memorable meal. Thanks to them for being so welcoming!! I loved starting the meal with a shot of olive oil. Truly impressive restaurant.
The food here is great I'm definitely going back. The menu has bison burgers. And they have bacon shakes (oh yeah!!!)

Very good food and service.
Got the Big Fish and it is BIg....tasty too!
Nice prices too....the view of the water is
Really nice. Situated on Johns Pass boardwalk with loads of shopping , deep sea fishing, dolphin sighting tours.  What a neat place, make sure you stop!

We had a delayed flight for 4 hours so we decided to eat here. Their pizza was really good and their lasagna was really good as well. The service was kind of slow, but then again, there was only one waiter and it was packed. The space is kind of tight as well. We would probably eat here again if we were ever back in the area.

If I could give zero stars I would. This is THE worst run Starbucks in the chain. Takes forever to get through the drive through. Painfully slow and rude barristas. If they didn't have a contract with the shopping center they would be out of business because any other coffee shop would put them out of business in a heartbeat. The two 5 star reviews on this store have to be fake reviews from employees because everyone who lives here knows this location stinks!

Naf Naf Grille did not disappoint! The food was amazing and I highly recommend ordering online. If this is your first time dabbling in this type of food I would suggest getting the garlic sauce with your order and trying some of the other items on the side. Falafel was great, hummus was one of the best I've ever had and the pita is out of this world!

I like this place a lot! Far better than some of the other Mexican places in Springfield. I love the tamales, I've had a few flavors and they don't disappoint, but my favorite is pork with green sauce. My husband had nachos with some kind of beef. THAT was delicious. They also have Mexican Coke in bottles, which is a favorite treat of mine. The flan was good. Not the best I've had, but still satisfying. I wish they had horchata! The atmosphere is nice, very casual. I would go for lunch not a romantic date. The menu is pretty large and I'm excited to keep trying new things.

Never been in the area before this time.  I liked the falafel and baklava from Bitar's.  Overall the food was reasonably priced.  The atmosphere is not conducive for a sit down restaurant, but definitely great for take out.  I would go there if again if in the area.
Absolutely delicious, we came from Washington D.C. and tried it. If you're in Philly, you should definitely grab a bite and don't forget the cheez fries!

Decided to go here for breakfast yesterday. Overall it was a good experience. My only, and I guess it's most important, complaint would be the food. I ordered the creamed chip beef and got a side of scrapple. The chipped beef was very VERY bland. Had no taste whatsoever.  I've made better at home from the frozen packages you get at the grocery store. The scrapple was fine, but a little pricy for the portion. 
For what it's worth, my gf enjoyed her meal. I forget it's name, but it was an open faced sandwich with some sauce on top. 

I'm not sure if it's worth the trip to just get okay food when there are better breakfast spots closer.

This place is awful with customer service. Upon arriving for a 3 day conference, there was a long line that wrapped around to check in.  We stood in line and there were women with clipboards, but I don't know what they were trying to do.  They couldn't offer any assistance and it seemed as if they were just wandering around the lobby.  I get to the front of the line and one of them asks me if I'd like to go to another line.  Why would I want to do that when I've reached the front?  Also, when I got to the front of the line, there were three open check-in stations right in front of me with no one manning them. They only had a few people checking us in when there was a long line and clearly they had the capacity to add staff to this area.  The prices are ridiculous.  My club sandwich and diet coke was $30.  If you want wine, prepare to spend $12-14 per glass. This place is also very large and confusing to navigate.  It's worse at night because it gets dark inside and there is NO ONE around to help you.  All the storefronts are closed and there is literally not one soul that you could ask for directions.  They claim to be a high-end, more fancy hotel, but this place is the pits.  I wouldn't return nor would I recommend it. I recommend staying downtown where you are close to good food and other amenities.

Amazing food!!!! But even better service by Brit and everyone (including the chef who made my daughter a special meal so she'd eat  - and didn't charge us for that part of the order!). 

The # of vegetarian choices were incredible! Seriously! We had:
Plantains, cauliflower (A+), corn on the cob (A+), yucca fries, corn empanadas (A+) and cheese empanadas.

A must visit if you're in indie.

I think this is one of the most overrated places in University City. Their gelato simply isn't good enough to justify the very high prices they charge. It wasn't bad in any way, but was not spectacular either. I think it is over $5 for a small, which wasn't very much gelato.

So love this place. I look forward to opening day each year.  Arrive early because the wait gets long. Even with that it's still worth it. The view is wonderful and the food is good. A must try is the mac and cheese, it is delicious.

We stayed at this hotel for Vanderbilt graduation, and found it to be appalling.  Looks like a social services room, with no shower door, mildew along sink back, and a bad odor throughout.  We had expected so much better, considering the price.  Would never stay here again, esp. with so many nicer options in Nashville.  My husband says it probably began as a holiday inn and got bought out and is going on reputation.  Stay away!!!
This place is great. I ordered the pouting to go and took it home. The time inside reminded me of a great business. the food was perfect as was everything.

My wife and I were looking for a local bakery while we were in New Olreans and thanks to the power of technology we were able to find this cute bakery with in walking distance of the Blake Hotel where we were staying for the week.  The walk down to Bittersweet Confections, was a nice one...too bad the rain made us rush a little.  

But now to the meat and potatoes of this review.  When I think of a cupcakery, this is the quintessential idea of what it should look like.  It had a warm inviting feel that made you want to sit down and chat with friends for hours.  It doesn't have that stale feel like a big chain bakery.  Excited that we found a place like this, we ordered way more than we should have...but there was so much good stuff how could you not!  We did 2 cupcakes, I had the breakfast bowl, my wife had the vegetarian Quiche, and I also had a cup of their Bittersweet Mocha.  The food was amazing!  It was a much better option to eat here than some of the tourist places that had constant lines in them.  

 - The breakfast bowl was a hearty mix of a biscuit, grits, egg, cheese, and bacon.  
 - The quiche was a light fluffy consistency with big chunks of veggies.  
 - The bittersweet mocha was not exactly my style of coffee, so I added a little caramel and it was fantastic.
 - German chocolate cupcake and salted caramel cupcake both had a nice texture and flavor, but my wife and I both preferred the German Chocolate over the Caramel.

At first I thought the prices were a little high, but in retrospect it was under most of the meals we had in the area and we walked out much happier because we weren't fighting for a place to sit.  I would definitely go back.

The fish hoagie is amazing. I wasn't even mad when they messed up my order. I asked for fried onions and mayo only. But they made it their way. It was great both times I've had it. I also tasted my daughter's wing platter with Mac and cheese and string beans. I don't eat Mac and cheese but the string beans were bomb. The kid loved it all so I'd say the Mac was good.

I dropped in for a few classes here when I was in town for work. The facility is big and the trainers were very knowledgeable and encouraging. The first class I felt a little weird and almost nobody, except the trainers, introduced themselves to me. I come from a very close-knit box that has a super welcoming community. The second and third classes had more people who were welcoming and made me feel comfortable. Could just be because the box is so big that many members don't know one another? Either way the programming and staff was great!

i'm not sure if this is the best mediteranian in the city..definately the best around. Delivery is superfast and the food is tasty if youre fimiliar with middle eastern food. I would stick with the 
middle eastern type of food like falafel , lamb ,beef shwarma etc. If youre looking for inexpensive and close to authentic this place will deliver right to your door. Give it a try , I too was skeptical before order for first time. enjoy!

Called an Order In and I repeated it twice drove 15 miles home to find its completely wrong. The lady stapled the bag all across the top so I couldn't see inside to check my order. Food was not what I ordered at all but I thought oh well I'll eat it. Bad choice! I threw it away and made my own food at home. Best to stay away if I could give a zero I would. Then on top of all that the lady was RUDE!

Do not pass this place up, it was amazing. I carry out twice a week and dine in at least once every two weeks awesome sushi..price good.... phenomenal service... oh and if you are in to hibachi it's second to done

Being from NY I am particular about my fast delivery Pizza/Italian food! I have to say that I am very impressed!!! We ordered a pepperoni pizza, 50 wings, a cheesesteak, and chicken cutlet parmigiana! Nothing was remotely bad, they must have a trained chef that owns this place! What great food, service and cost! Bravo La Cucina of Conshohocken! You have a few fans from a different area of the country! In particular you have me, and it is hard to impress this foodie!

Loved it! Best breakfast potatoes and coffee in town! Today we went for Mother's Day - a little wait but well worth it! Got the eggs Benedict with regular bacon - sooooo delicious yummy comfort food! Kids pancakes are Mickey Mouse head shape - fun!

I don't get the hype at all. Place looks like a college hang out. It's dirty, uncomfortable, chaotic, freezing cold. Food was "fine" but certainly not anything to get excited about. Coffee was decent, but far from the best I've ever had. Maybe I'm missing something.
This is a nice bread co., the parking is a little bit crowded if you're around lunch . But it's great, its bread co

Just picked up some takeout from Asian Chef.  Food was delicious.  We had the shrimp egg rolls, penang chicken and the thai basil chicken.  Plenty of spice and good portions.  We will definitely be going back. Staff were also very friendly.
Had breakfast there last week. What a treat. Best breakfast I have had in a long time. The service was unmatched. I definitely will eat there again.

Had take out--ordered the pan seared chicken. It was very rubbery, hard, dry.  The sides were so so.  My husband had salmon with crab hash that was so so.  Quality definatlely going down.  Its a shame because we have a huge gift card here from their black Friday half price sale.

i'm not sure how i never knew about this spot before but it's best sushi place i've honestly ever been. the place itself is stunning, the beverage selection is massive, the food and its presentation is 100% ! glad i only live 3 blocks away!!
The wife and I went down to buy a new bed and ended up spending a whole lot of money it was because of Thomas who is a great person and his customer service was out of this world thank you very much.

Oh my! I can here as it was the highest rated for brunch. Yelp did not do me wrong. I had the Baja omelet with the grits and I was oh so happy with my choice. The grits we're probably some of the best I ever had and the omelet was perfect. The pecan coffee was a perfect partner and the orange juice was amazingly fresh. 

The only reason I didn't give it give stars is bc the girl at the counter was not too welcoming and seemed a little irritated when I didn't know the routine of ordering at the counter and then picking a seat, but the guys who delivered my food to the table and came and took my plate we're really nice. This place is a definite must.

Some of my neighbors had been to this restaurant but I had not so I was happy to go in a large group so I could try a lot of dishes.  W shared the dumplings, spring rolls and papaya salad.  All very good as appetizers.  I thought the papaya salad was especially wonderful.  All eight people had different main dishes and I didn't try them all.  Mine was seafood massaman curry which was phenomenal and people kept grabbing some of the sauce for left over rice.  The salmon chewchee was very nicely cooked with a nice sauce but The vegetables on the side were very plain.  The Thai basil dishes were very popular and the chef modulated the spices according to each person's desire.  My husband had duck chew chee which is one of his favorites and he said it was extremely good.  Everyone came away full and happy.  This is a tiny restaurant but nice staff and the food was definitely a notch above usual Thai restaurants.

Great place for lunch or brunch. Their green juices were delicious and very healthy. I had their omelet and their veggie sandwich. Both were delicious. Went there twice during my trip to New Orleans. Great break from eating unhealthy food which often happens when you are on vacation.

This is by far the worse furniture store I have purchased from. They say they can deliver but then they can't. We called and spoke to them about getting an item replaced that was damaged during delivery and it took 3 days and about 10 phone calls to finally get someone to tell us that it was going to be two weeks to get the rest of our sectional. They put a line in their contract that states they will replace at their discretion. That's how they get away with ridiculous delivery schedule. We asked to cancel order so we can buy the furniture that we needed to host a party, they said no problem we will call you to schedule pickup. Guess what , 2 days later they tell us that they gave us false information. They will not pick up or refund us because that is their policy. Ashley furniture could have told us this before we purchased other furniture. I have never dealt with a company with so many excuses and poor guest response team and managers that don't know their own policies. If you want better service shop elsewhere. #dontbuyashleyfurniture #badcustomerservice

This place was fantastic. I discovered it by accident when I walked past. The lady stepped out the door when I was reading the menu and handed me a paper one. She stood there very patiently answering all my questions about the difference between Chinese food and Taiwanese. (the answer: since Taiwan was occupied by Japan for a while, there is quite a bit of Japanese influence in the food.)
Hubby and I went  back for dinner a couple days later. Yum! The service was great, the food was fresh and fantastic. The options were varied. I was very impressed.
I would definitely recommend the Zha Jiang (basically Taiwanese spaghetti).

A great little tapas restaurant. You have to try the hangar steak and lamb, they were my favorites. The flat breads are great too. 

This place is great for a normal weekend date night. They also run great specials through the week.

Disappointing. We asked the bar tender if we could get fried oysters, which are not on the menu, he said no problem. We asked how many, he said 4 per order so we asked for two orders. When the oysters came out there we only six not eight. They were nothing but breading. We couldn't even find the oysters in two of the lumps of fried breading. We ate two and sent the remaining dough back. They did not charge us for the order.

My family loved it here.  Food was great. Our waitress was sweet.  The hostess could have smiled but oh well.  It was clean, well decorated, and the view awesome!   I posted a pic of it. We will definitely go back.  And if your worried about the calories there's a track around the pond you see from the patio that you can work them off on.

I came in not sure if I was going to find what I was looking for or be able to finance because of my credit. Carlos Lima was very friendly, helpful and made the whole experience so easy not to mention stress free. He worked with me and kept me in my budget. Now I am loving my new Sonata:-) Thank you so much Carlos and the rest of the staff!!!

I stopped here for a hot second to kill some time waiting for my mom and overall I enjoyed it.  I had a nice cup of tea and was able to enjoy being outside for one of the last nice days of fall.  They have a fair amount of outdoor seating, which is nice and the inside looked pretty cozy too.  No complaints here.

What a hidden little gem. I'm not a coffee drinker but I wanted somewhere to sit and relax and maybe read a book.I walked in to a beautiful house turned coffeeshop. The barista there was very friendly and she suggested the house specialty coffee drink. it was very delicious and I'm even craving it right now. 

The decor of this place is very vintage chic and a unique place from your average Starbucks.  I will return again.

Luckily, and unexpectedly, Ralph's has valet parking available for the evening. We pull up and race to the entrance, just as the rain seems to be getting heavier. A small outdoor "foyer" guards the front door, New York style, which leads into a small, cozy dining room thronged with seated diners. Old-time photographs line the walls, proving that celebrities ranging from Teddy Roosevelt to Frank Sinatra have visited (and evidently loved) Ralph's. Faded patterned wallpaper looks like it belongs in your grandparents' Victorian mansion. Ornate ceiling tiles gleam overhead. The place oozes traditional, old-school vibes, and I fully expect to see men in pinstripe suits with one hand tucked in the breast pocket at all times.

MB chats with the host, who seats us promptly at a four-top near the entrance. The occasional blast of cold nighttime air hits us when other patrons enter (it is a virtual downpour now) but it gets warmer as the night wears on. Our server is friendly, gruff, and full of good humor. He takes our drink order (Yuengling for me), then rattles off the specials for the evening with lightning-round precision. Everyone opts to start with some kind of appetizer, but I'm still reeling from our stint at Mac's. I need a reprieve from meat (if only momentary). The "spring salad" sounds good, so I go with that: spicy arugula; sliced rings of red onion (which I shuffle off to the side); quartered, juicy Roma tomatoes; chunks of tangy gorgonzola; tart balsamic dressing. All that freshness does wonders, clearing my taste buds for more traditional Italian fare.

I'm ready for pasta now, and I'm a sucker for good gnocchi. This place looks like there may be a little old lady somewhere in back--grandma, let's say--hand crafting each seashell-like piece. Seems like a safe bet. I'm back on the carnivore train again, so I get the tomato meat sauce. The bowl arrives nearly overflowing with bright red sauce covering the pale gnocchi. There are green bits of herb in there, but not overwhelming. I try a nibble. Good, but not great. The gnocchi wavers from being slightly undercooked to perfectly cooked (it may have finished cooking under the sauce, so that's forgivable). It's a solid, if plain, dish with no real diversion from textbook Italian cuisine. A standby, if you will. It is satisfying, though. I do my best to eat most of it before setting aside my fork. The house chianti washes it down nicely. Again, no bells and whistles with the wine either.

While the rest of the table decides to end with coffee and cannoli, I'm good with just some espresso to fill in the cracks. (That's a good thing; no one else seems that impressed with the cannoli.) In the end, a one-time visit to Ralph's seems sufficient to get the gist. Solid food with little flair, adhering to time-honored recipes. The rain has stopped finally, and we're able to depart without getting soaked. Time to sleep...but not with the fishes.

Don't take my word for it. See what my better half has to say on our site (linked in my profile).

I live in NW, like to pick up sandwiches when we go hiking. Second visit here. 3 young ladies with very poor customer service working. Was the same at our first visit, plus they got our order all wrong then. Think I'll drive the further distance to Deli Town where both the customer service and sandwiches are consistently excellent. They also need to clean the filter in their soda machine.

Great place, great guys; they really take their time and make sure that you are taken care of.  They only have 3 chairs (4th guy left a couple months ago), so don't bother with a walk-in unless you are willing to wait 2+ hours until they hire a new guy.  They say that it'll only be 1-1.5 hours, but unless you get lucky, it'll be 2.  They do take appointments, so I'll be doing that next time, for sure.

If they can give me consistently good haircuts a couple more times, I'll be bumping to 5 stars.

Cash only, as more barber shops are.
Best pizza around, the wings are also a must try. It's always crowded but the wait is usually only 5-10 min.

Been here multiple times over the last 2 years.
Seems as if tofu isn't quite as good as it was when I started coming here.  Not sure if it's actually changed, or our tasting of it.

Everyone here is so nice. We got their pudding and a little cupcake once which were both delicious. We also got a large (20 people) custom buttercream birthday cake for our baby's 1st birthday and couldn't have been more pleased. The cake was fun and beautiful and soooooo yummy. I ate it for breakfast, lunch, and dinner for several days. They're so easy to work with. I never had to stress about the cake. We also bought separate cake toppers from Amazon and the bakery incorporated them so nicely into the cake. We will see them for our next bday cake!

Great food, prices, and service, with a nice atmosphere to boot.  Too bad I don't live in Philly

The four of us had the home made roti (yum!), satay chicken and beef (not my fav, but I'm not a big satay fan either), Indian mee goreng (good, but I think I was trying to order the hokkien char mee), ginger duck noodles (a hit with everyone), and the sizzling seafood combo with black pepper.  We also ordered some coconut rice.

For drinks we had the rambutan, lychee, ABC, and tea.  Can't speak for the rambutan and lychee, but ABC was very good.  Need to find a place in LA that serves it because I will definitely be craving it.

Overall, everything was good and our bill came out to about $55 after tax.  Worth another visit if I'm ever in Philly again.

This is the 2nd time I've been here. The first time I got the southwest BBQ chicken pizza which was really good. The second time I got the Caprice & it was just okay. The servers are wonderful here; they're all very friendly! I love the pizza crust; it's crispy & chewy. Give this place a try, you'll like it!

I will agree that the service can be hit or miss - especially if they are swamped - but what restaurant/bar doesn't have that on occasion?   If you are out on the patio on a Saturday night - expect to wait.  I don't find giving a bad rating to an establishment simply because you had poor service.  That is merely one component and while it is an important one - it doesn't mean you need to give the place a 1 star overall. 

The number of beers they have on tap is just insane.  A wonderful variety of just about anything you can think of and some, you wouldn't even consider (peanut butter porter?!) but should!   They are cold and most of the time, you get a fresh pint glass. Bartenders are very knowledgeable about the beers on tap and will you let you sample if you are undecided.  Note: There is a separate beer list for the indoor bar compared to the outdoor bar.  If you want something from one of the other bars, you will need to go get it yourself! :)

We've gone as a couple and we've met friends for dinner so we've sampled a large variety of the food.  Sandwiches, cheesesteaks, wings. homemade soup, salads.  Really good stuff.  We've also had the entree specials (a risotto and chicken dish respectively) and these were equally good, sizable portions with great flavor.

This is just a great place and I don't think you will be disappointed.

I had a good time at The Bricks of Ybor.  The service is really spot on and the quality of the food's pretty good.  I had the pulled pork sandwich.  It was pretty good.  Nothing memorable but what makes this place a four star place are the happy hour beer prices and the interesting art inside.

I loved the star wars art throughout this place and particularly loved the berpo and ern2d2 painting.

Friendly, fun crowd that looks like they're coming to a John Waters costume party.

Dr. Biscardi is truly wonderful and amazing. I have terrible eyes and had ongoing problems with my contacts (5+ years and multiple doctors) until I went to her. She discovered I was in the wrong shaped lens for my eyes and got me in the right ones-- and after years of discomfort and poor vision I was finally able to see again and feel comfortable in contacts! On top of that, she really cares about her patients and goes above and beyond for them. She fit me in on a fully booked day because I had an issue I wanted her to take a look at. She is careful, attentive, and kind. I could not give a higher recommendation.

This brewery was awesome. It is incredibly large with plenty of picnic tables and games. Bunch of friendly folks too! Their beer selection is good. Based on the banners that were hung, they've won some awards too.

I got Blueberry Lemon Gose which I think was a special they had at the moment. That and the Lime-Cucumber Gose both had the tart flavor I was craving. Ugh this place was so good.

I was so happy to find this place when I moved here a year ago! The food is exceptional and fresh the people and service is outstanding.  They keep improving on what they have, they've expanded the facility, added brunch and music wonderful!  The bakery is fabulous including the gluten free amazing options.  

I've brought several people here who now love it as I do! 

Thank you Cottage Cafe/Crumb de la Crumb for being so good at what you do serving healthy options with great people and offering decadent deserts!!

My brother and sister-in-law came out to visit from California for a long weekend. We were looking for something low-key to do on Sunday. This fit the bill - it's perfect for first-time visitors. We did the Sunday Brunch cruise and sat at the table right by the bar and the band. It was nice to listen to the band while we ate. We sat outside the rest of the cruise, listened to the tour guide and took photos. Lovely Sunday afternoon.

If you are ever visiting Tucson, you should not miss this gem!  Thank you Ted DeGrazia for leaving this beautiful treasure to the community and for visitors around the world.  The gallery only recently started charging admission, but it's only $8.00 for adults and children under 12 are free. Be sure to see the grounds where you can view the humble home he built and lived in on the property.  The area is absolutely gorgeous.

After traveling heavily for work for many years, the longest wait I ever had was here at Hertz in STL.  They had my reservation in the system and had the car size available.  However, none were clean.  Instead of doing an upgrade like every other rental company I've gone with, they had me wait.  For 20 minutes, when there were no other customers being serviced, I waited.  and waited.  I asked about the delay and they said it was just about finished.  It wasn't.  This is the last time I use Hertz in STL.

Pig supreme, pig utopia. I love TaTa's pork leg entree so much that it makes me audibly oink.

I used to think "ehh, pork is okay but it's not my favorite." The #7 dish at TaTa completely altered my stance. If every pig tasted like this, I wouldn't ever need any other type of meat. The depth of flavor, the tenderness, the salty richness, it's a complete experience. The accompanying rice and plantains are a perfect compliment. (Oh, and the Cuban sandwich here is probably the best version I've ever had ...and that's factoring in Yelp-acclaimed versions in Puerto Rico and Miami.)

Celebrate pig. Eat #7 at TaTa and be pork-revolutionized.

Our tour guide was Michael and he was amazing! He was enthusiastic and very kind. He made it a point to make sure everyone could hear and see him during presentation time. He taught us so much about New Orleans' history, it was really interesting to hear all the stories. Meeting the Voodoo Bone lady at the end of the night was a like a cherry on top of an ice cream sundae. She was very sweet and we were able to see the inside of her shop!

Great Mexican street cart food. Sonoran hot dogs, tacos, caramelos, quesadillas, al pastor etc... Can't go wrong with this place. Everything is great, and decent prices. This is nothing fancy, just to the point. Their sauces aren't the best and consistency is an issue, otherwise, they would get five stars.

This fast food place is highly overrated unless you love really really love greasy and tasteless fried chicken. This was the first time Id been to a Chick Filet.
I waited in the long line (not a problem if the food is good), and my food came out super fast, too fast. It had apparently been sitting under a food lamp for quite sometime. Took a few bites of my chicken, then found the manager and handed him my tray back, told him the food was disgusting , and with no response from him, I just left still hungry.
My daughter convinced me it was just a fluke and asked me to try it again. I went through the drive through and I have to say they have a very similar operation to ordering (like In-n-Out) when they are busy. Very nice. However, it was still crappy food. They do have a very nice ice tea. 
Definitely will not return.
I love this little Italian gem in Lafayette Square.  The atmosphere is so quaint and inviting.  They have a great menu and I've never had a bad glass of wine there.  Yum.

I was in Tuscon for work for a couple days. I was craving pasta. I knew Claim Jumper served pasta so I went on in. The waitress was nice, the server, the host.. Everything was cool. That is, until I ate the pasta I ordered. I got the black tie pasta.

Bruh... This pasta was sooo overcooked! It was the bow tie pasta. They weren't bow ties anymore. They were blankets!!! They were so overcooked and soft that the middle of the pasta had detached. It was just a bunch of blanket pastas. 

Waitress walked on by and asked, "how's your food".. I said "Its good" because she was nice and I didn't wanna be a headache. (I should've said something lol. I'm paying for this)

Anyways, I finished my food because I was starving like hell. Won't be going back tho

This motel is nothing to write home about...it was quite , clean , and up to date...great place to pick up a hooker,or some decent black tar heroin...at least thats what i was told by a guy named lil creepy who was staying there to...at night the driveway was turned into an active crime scene by the sheriffs but the real crime was the jacuzzi being closed for repairs...all and all, id stay there again,but only if i had to..

We landed in nashville from dallas at about 7 pm, we WERE STARVING! My girlfriend LOVES everything country, so we made a reservation. We arrived, were seated, not greeted for a few, but whatever. Ordered an appetizer fried green tomatoes YUM !!

Then the entrees, we ordered fried chicken and 3 sides, the sides were great, but the chicken was OFF, my wing was not noticeable but i took 1 bite of the thigh and it was like SOUR METAL. Mt girlfriends smelled sour, neither of us touched it. I pulled the waiter and let him know quietly, in case other guests ordered it and there was something wrong. His reply was "ill tell the manager", ok, good idea bro. Then came back and said "would you like something different", no thanks. Then came back and said "would you like to talk to the manager", well, you would think the manager would want to talk to me. Never seen them. Then i asked for the check, guess what the restaurant didnt have a problem with ??? Charging me full price for both entrees of spoiled chicken !!!

On top of that, i had left a note for the manager at the table because he was too coward to talk to us, i emailed the hotel chain that owns the restaurant, got an email reply back "well i hope we can do better in the future", NAH, DONT WORRY ABOUT ME BEING A GUEST IN THE FUTURE.

This was 3 chances to right the COMPLETELY WRONG situation. I am a restaurant operator, i prefer to fix every thing wrong in my restaurant myself and make sure noone leaves hungry nor unhappy, but this company would rather charge full price (check was $49.34 for 2 people) for food that was inedible, spoiled, and people who dont care about what they serve or how, just take the money.

Take what you will from my review,  ill never give this company another dime.

Came here before a Tampa Bay Lightning hockey game and my fiance and I had a house margarita on the rocks, comes in one size 18oz and was delicious. He had the pork tacos with the puffy shell tacos and I had the nachos both filled us up. Awesome service and a beautiful patio.

Always a fun and interesting  place that offers the unusual combination of creative cocktails, great food and decadent deserts. 
We come here often.
Came for lobster bisque had to settle for shrimp bisque instead.   rob loves Dungeness crab   Santa Barbara is beautiful!  My checkin here are sure tallying up.  Enjoy    Highly recommend.

I love their Turkey Burgers, Turkey Chili, Garden Salads etc. The owner works behind the register daily. They fax menus to your job and if you live/work in the CBD area, they will deliver. I think this place is well needed in New Orleans, it should be well deserved and frequented if we want to keep it open.

This is a great place for vegans, vegetarians, pescetarians, flexetarians etc etc etc

While visiting Tampa, I got a hankering for BBQ. Thanks yo Yelp, I found this little jewel and instantly fell in love. From the street, this place looks like a home. The owner and a worker were sitting on the porch chatting as I walked up. I go in and sit down...striking up a conversation that made me feel like I was sitting at home talking to my grandfather and uncle.
The food was AMAZING!!! Down home cooking that was truly satisfying. I will NEVER go back to Tampa without stopping by this spot...even if I don't eat (which is highly unlikely), just to say "hey, how y'all doin'?!"
Very good falafel, fries,and baba ghanoush.  Not very good shawarma though, it was light on meat and a little dry.  Quick and efficient service.

We found a cock reach in the bathroom and trash had not been emptied. We asked for other room and they showed us two others, one that had ceiling flakes all over the bathroom counter and floor, and the other with a nasty stench. The lady showing the room said that they flakes were from the room being painted recently and didn't offer to clean it and expected to stay there. Supposedly it is under new management and they're renovating soon but I wouldn't stay there until they do. They would not offer a refund for the one night we had checked in to so we will definitely be calling corporate to complain.

Just got take out from here yesterday, and everything was on point! The sushi is really excellent (ask for spicy mayo on the side), and their entrees are also very good and unique. This is definitely my spot for Japanese cuisine in Chinatown.

Don't have to be a Flyers fan at all to realize we need them in the NHL playoffs every year. Always an interesting team and for some reason every since Ron Hextall left the 1st time have not been able to solve their goaltending woes. 

Great fans if a bit stuck on the whole Broad Street Bullies era. I know you won back then with very good teams but, honestly, I think the '80s teams were better but they were stuck facing the Oilers dynasty in '85 and '87.

GREAT PANCAKES! It would be 5 stars if I rated solely on pancakes. My sons french toast was soggy but he didn't seem to mind.  Not the most kid friendly (no kid menu) so I had to get my 4 year old an adult sized meal. And even though we were only one of 3 tables there, early in the morning, I felt hurried (my kids were behaving nicely and no, we didn't make or leave a big mess). The waiter actually started to take my sons plate away while he still had half the food on it, was chewing, and had his fork in his hand. But give it a try (really those pancakes).

I wish I could give it more stars, but it just doesn't measure up. The food is bar food, not bad, but not great. The service depends on the visit, I have been a few times, sometimes its great sometimes it just plain sucks. 

The food looks so much better when reading the menu, my mouth waters, when it shows up, there is no pride, or time to make it look nice, and the taste that was described is lack luster.

The location is odd, not in the best part of town, Tucson doesn't have many best areas, but its in a odd location for me. I don't feel safe after dark walking to my car.

The drinks on the other hand are great, which is why I gave it 3 stars. From beer to spirits I would go here for that. The bartenders are great, and knowledgable.

My mom and I, both life-long drug store make-up users, decided to go for a make-up consult on a Friday afternoon when she was visiting, and it was a lot of fun! We were both interested in getting some tips on foundation and make-up application ( I rarely, if ever actually wear make-up and my mom wears very little ) and we were pleasantly surprised by the service.

It took a while to flag down a sales associate (even midday on Friday), but once we did, we were helped by Sue Bostani, who was very honest and not at all pushy. I was concerned that if I had my make-up done, the person helping me would try to sell me a bunch of different things that I didn't really need, but Sue was very sensitive to the fact that my mom and I are minimalists, which we really appreciated. The store was busy, and I'm sure she was as well, but she took time out with us and didn't rush our service. She sold us both on some awesome foundation and made my mom feel like a million bucks, which was the highlight for me. Would definitely go back sometime (probably on a weekday to avoid the crowds), and would recommend Sue! She was great!

Two visits at the Oro Valley location and two very big disappointments.  Today I visit to do water walking.  There were bugs all over in the pool room.  On the walls, pool side walls, pool deck and in the water.  Left the pool after two laps and asked to speak with a manager.  Told at the front desk she was on lunch and there was no one else to talk to.  The young man said they knew about the bugs, that customers have been complaining all day.  He said the exterminator was coming either today or tomorrow.  I asked why did they not put up a sign or close the pool and received no response.  Very bad experience!

While visiting in St. Louis, my daughter and son-in-law wanted to take me to Sage. It is their favorite restaurant and was on the "must do" list while I was there. I was not disappointed! 

We arrived a little early for our reservation and opted to sit at the bar and have a beer prior to sitting down to dinner. The bar tender was very friendly. The beer selection was excellent and priced reasonably. 

We were seated for our reservation on time. We chose to sit at the outdoor patio since the weather was cool by St. Louis standards. The outdoor patio was pleasant. The surroundings were quiet. One wouldn't know that they were in the middle of the city across from the brewery. 

We had the calamari and pot stickers for appetizers. The calamari is to die for! It is filleted and cooked in a seasoned butter sauce. It was very tender. This is the calamari that all others will be judged by henceforth. The pot stickers were good also, if not just a little salty for my tastes. 

I had a cheese and sun dried tomato stuffed chicken breast served over angel hair pasta for my main entree. It was excellent! I don't think I have ever had chicken breast quite so good. My daughter had the fillet Mignon and was very satisfied with it. My son-in-law had the fish special and was impressed as well. As a matter of fact he recommended it to the diners at the next table when they were wondering about it. 

For desert we tried the desert shots. They were just right after the scrumptious meal. I had the pecan pie shot and it was 3 bites of pure bliss! 

Sage is on my list of "must-do's" and I'll be back when I'm back in St. Louis the next time. I can't wait for my wife to try it!

IMA comes with a bit of a sticker shock for a single day admission. On its face, it seems expensive as it is right up there with some museums in Chicago. The catch there is other museums charge for specific exhibits but once you're in the IMA, you're good to go.

If you go at least twice a year, you should just spring for the $75 membership. You also get discounts for special events and a few other benefits as well.

IMA is a beautiful facility and have really done a lot to modernize over the past few years. In addition to the current Audubon exhibit, the IMA also has mini golf and a beer garden. You can explore the nearby greenhouse while drinking beer or wine. Or enjoy a King David's hot dog or some great iced coffee. And considering you're at a museum, the prices aren't marked up too much.

I'm glad I'm a member and will likely renew next year.

Awesome Saturday lunch here. My party was seated with no wait. Even on the touristy part of town, the restaurant was very clean and the service was friendly and prompt. Food (3 po-boys) came out super hot and quickly. The dressed shrimp poboy was delicious. The onion rings were a little greasy but still good. YUM. Fun decor and bar, too

We had great service, the grouper was really good and very fresh.  Wasn't crazy about the potatoes. It's very casual,  you get served on wood seafood plates, hasn't been updated since they took over from last place.  It was an older crowd there. They had  live band on Friday. A little overpriced but good food.  Key west martini was amazing.

I truely enjoyed my large poke bowl with 3 scoops of tuna, a scoop of shrimp, and a scoop of octopus.  the ponzu and seaweed salad gave it the right level of salt.  The brown rice was great.

If you haven't had poke before, this is a great place to start.  you can choose what you and don't want.

HORRIBLE! JUST AWFUL!!!!!!! WORST FILL I HAVE EVER HAD!!!! do not go here. not only are they over priced, $26 for a fill before tip (charged me $5 to cut them??? WHAT!) they look HORRIBLE!!!! they are grainy and jagged and uneven. I am so disappointed with this salon. I will NEVER go back.

I had never been inside the IMA before this week. SHAME, I know. How had I not yet explored this incredible place practically in my own backyard??

It was a beautiful fall afternoon so I decided, what the heck, let's go explore. I was on the hunt for a free annual membership using my handy dandy student ID - students attending Butler, CTS, IUPUI, Marian, Martin, and UIndy all get a free membership for a year. Crazy, right?! All you have to do is go to guest services inside the main entrance and fill out an application. Your official membership card comes in the mail a few weeks later.

Parking was easy (and free!) to find in the paved surface lot off the 38th Street entrance. There is also a parking garage. 

Before I even went inside, I strolled around the front lawn area and marveled at the gorgeous flowers and landscaping. Wooden benches beneath shaded trees? Check. Big beautiful fountain? Check. The requisite visit to the iconic Robert Indiana LOVE sign? Done. It's worth it alone just to go there and sit on a peaceful sunny afternoon! 

The inside though? IT'S SO BIG. Goodness gracious, it goes on forever. Three floors of gallery space that wind and weave to more rooms. You're like "there can't be more..." but there is, and then you're lost. But fear not, ask for a map at guest services or ask one of the friendly workers in the rooms. I had no idea the IMA had such an expansive collection - and everything from artistic paintings to ancient relics and fashion pieces. Something for everyone with any interest!

I also just really loved the modern vibe - high ceilings, bright, spacious. The escalators and elevators make it very accessible for all visitors.

I was impressed with how many staff members were spread in the gallery areas. They didn't bother me, but one kind fellow noticed I had stopped to ponder a crisp, photograph-like painting and informed me that Napoleon's brother used to own it. So cool! They are there to enhance the experience and answer questions but not bug you. 

According to the website and brochure, photography is allowed, but not for commercial use. I didn't take many photos because I thought it wasn't allowed and that's why the staffers were there - to watch us like hawks and snatch my camera. Guess not!

Don't forget the Lilly Gardens (need a membership to explore there), the IMA Cafe, and 100 Acres (which is free and open dawn to dusk - take entrance off of 38th Street). 

You can spend an hour here or a whole day here - it really depends on what you get out of the experience. There's a handy guide at guest services called "I have an hour" with recommendations on what to see to make the most of your visit!

TL;DR do yourself a favor and check out this state of the art museum in Indy!

The greatest restaurant, locally owned, chain, and or both, that I've ever been to, period. And I've found the same quality from California to Chicago to Indianapolis to Cleveland.

It's a nation-wide chain that doesn't give out its franchise tag or secret recipes lightly, so every single one of them is top quality. It's perfect for breakfast or brunch, especially since they're not open for dinner.

If you're hungry and love breakfast food, this place is heaven! Ginormous dutch pancake (one huge, fluffy, custardy pastry) smothered in apple/cinnamon/sugar/syrup goodness and dubbed the Apple Pancake is my hands down favorite dish to order from any restaurant anywhere in the country.

But don't let that shy you away from the omelettes.

I believe they include some pancake batter and bake these monsters, because they're light, fluffy, volumous and oh so tasty. Never, ever burnt or rubbery, and they contain simple goodness (my favorite being the corned beef hash and cheddar cheese!)

You will not be disappointed, my friend. Oh no, you will not be disappointed.

Ben was amazing!!! His customer service and technical insight diagnosed and fixed our a/c in minutes.  This was after a Progressive Air Systems tech cam out earlier in the week and told us the unit was working as it was supposed to.

Ben called us late on Saturday night to schedule our Sunday appointment, came out on Sunday and quickly tested and figured out the issued, and by Monday afternoon Ben fixed the issue and we had a/c again.

Thank you Ben - he's the only tech we'll work with at Progressive!!
WAG is a classic spot and is much beloved in Jenkintown (my hometown).  Their tomato soup is awesome as are their breakfast items.  I'm just sad they are no longer open for dinner.

My husband and I went to this Thai restaurant, Siam Elephant  for lunch or dinner several times whenever we went to visit our friends in Carpinteria. Very nice and lovely atmosphere inside and outside seats.  It is close to the beach. Foods are so delicious as we expected. Love their Shrimp Pad Thai, Spicy Seafood Fried noodle, Spicy Seafood Soup, Asparagus and Avocado salad.  Prices are reasonable. Good customer services.  Owners and staff are very nice and friendly.  If you happen to be in this area, we highly recommended.  We will definitely go back to this restaurant again.
This is the slowest drive through I have ever been in my entire life not sure how this survives why people continue to come back here

Stopped in for lunch today with 2 other friends. This was the first time any of us have been to this restaurant and we found it by accident, it was the only restaurant open for lunch on Monday. Boy we sure were glad we found us and it's going to be a new favorite. I had the Punkys house salad with blue cheese dressing and it was wonderful. It came in a large wooden bowlwith a lot of toppings. My only complaint would be the wooden bowl had some chips around the edges. And probably should've been thrown away. My one friend had the grilled cheese sandwich which was made with Bree, fried green tomatoes, and bacon. We all three loved this sandwich, unbelievable. The best grilled cheese I have ever had. Our other friend ordered the Cobb salad with a side of spicy waffle fries. He also really enjoyed his meal. We really enjoyed eating here, the atmosphere is super cool, my only suggestion would be to turn the music down a bit. We were there on a business lunch and the song crazy bitch came on. The song was blaring and it was not bleeped for the inappropriate words. So if not for the wooden bowl having chips around the edges and the loud somewhat vulgar music this would be five stars.

Came here during vacation, outside of El Salvador, these pupusas are among the best I've had. The pupusas are gluten free, The green Salsa adds a nice quick of spice to the curtido and house salsa. The price is quite reasonable and the cute Salvadorian girl was extremely helpful. #imaddicted can't wait to be back and refresh my pallet

Stopped in again not too long ago and as always the food was superb! Only thing that was a downer for me was that my last few visits they were out of the chicken wings again. Sometimes you know you have a craving and headed there to fill it but was just unfortunate they were out. Still love the restaurant and the staff but hoping my next visit they have the chicken wings I have been waiting to have! Hopefully see you soon.
We had Katsu Don and Sushi and Sashimi combo. The Don was salty and the fried chicken was so wet. Fish was not fresh. Not deserve 4 stars at all.

BEST CHILI EVER!!!! If you like old west style restaurants then you must stop by. The drive is a little far because this place is in the middle of the mountains, the drive is worth it's, very scenic and enjoyable. The restaurant itself is very small, and you might have to wait depending on how much people they have. the place is so nice that we didn't mind waiting, we sat outside on  a bench enjoying nature. Going to this restaurant is an experience like no other.

This is now one of my favorite restaurants! We ordered the spicy beef & noodle soup and dry pepper style fish - both were awesome! The complimentary tea was also delicious. I'd recommend ordering family style (we went during lunch time) as the portions are pretty big.

I thought that the person that seated us was a little rude - he was more interested in chatting with a group than welcoming us and was pretty dismissive of us (this is the only reason for it being a 4 star instead of a 5). Our waiter was wonderful though and gave us all the time and information we wanted. The service was also quick.

Very good lunch. Had the meatloaf which was very good. Nice touch of spice and moist 
The waitress was terrific would definitely recommend

I'm here right now and this is my hell. Worst drink in history. I mean...this margarita is  straight lime soda with a hint of urine. If I'm ever diagnosed with cancer it will be because of this place and it's awful bartenders. Most of this comment may sound like a joke but this place used to be wonderful before (I'm assuming here) it's owners changed because when this was Lola's it was dark and mysterious, hip and fun. Now it looks and smells like an old dirty motel in Vegas. It sucks guys. Plus it overcharged us for drinks.

Remedy has got easily the best Chai Latte in Edmonton, hands-down. A great atmosphere here with plenty of seating for groups of all sizes, this is a great place to come with a whole pile of friends, or your laptop to get some work done.

They have a terrific selection of indian food. I haven't tried a ton of it, but I remember really enjoying a veggie samosa.

But seriously, if you do nothing else, try the Chai. Authentic and delicious, one of the gems of Edmonton
Love this place. Ice cream is so creamy. The workers are so helpful. They didn't have my kind(french vanilla), but the worker suggested something close and it became my new favorite(forgot the name).

Woohoo, this place is killing it! Amazing bun with lots of HUGE shrimp, perfect dressing, fresh lovely veg. Shrimp salad (with perfect, fresh strawberries!) was amazing too. Great fresh coconut juice. Super fast and friendly ervice. Lovely, clean atmosphere. A perfect Magazine St. stopover.

When I went to New Orleans this was my single favorite attraction. I know it's odd, but I love cemetaries - especially old ones. It started when I was a kid... Seeing which headstones were the oldest was something I loved to do. It poured down rain as we got close to St. Louis Cemetary #1 and by the end of the tour boyfriend and I were soaked (with an umbrella) but I couldn't have been happier. I really enjoyed the tour and the stories about the cemetery itself (imagine dead bodies floating around town) and stories of those who were laid to rest there. (And, Nicholas Cage, who has his pyramid that doesn't at all belong). Anyhow, it was fantastic. Definitely do this tour if your into cemetaries it history. And get your two free drinks before you leave the bar

I mean, how can you NOT like chipotle? 

Located at Parkside Mall, this chipotle is like any other.....consistent, quick and efficient and very friendly employees. 

Even on a busy lunch day, the line moves really quickly. 

My go to is the veggie bowl topped with guacamole.  Wonderful, not terrible for you, and filling.
It may be the best in STL, but there is much better Q 313 miles NE in Chicago. Try Smoque BBQ the next time you travel to the Windy City.

I recently found out that it's pronounced "E-lings", but if you say "L-ings" or "Las Positas Park" people will know what you are talking about. Technically this is a private park but that just means if you want to rent it out for an event you have to pay more. Otherwise it's a wonderful park with 2 baseball fields, 2 soccer fields a small outdoor theater that people like to have weddings at and even an RC Car race track. Spread out over a terraced hills this park is a great place to take the kids or play some frisbee. It even has a nice little trail at the top with some great views.

For dog owners they have off leash licenses that last for one calendar year and aren't too expensive. Go early though, I hear they sell out pretty quickly every year.

They also have an area to launch your paraglider from. I'm not sure if they rent them or not but it sure looks like fun. You can glide out over the wilcox property and hendry's beach for some great updrafts.

I love this place! I wish I lived in Philly so I could visit more often. They had a great selection of vintage/mid-century furniture at great prices. Someone else mentioned the prices could seem high but I personally thought they were super reasonable. I'd say it's worth a visit.

Beautiful road to drive on.  We started on this road  from Natchez, MS to get to close to Vicksburg. It was a nice windy road, nice for motorcycle ride. We wished we had our bikes. From Memphis to Nashville, we took this parkway again. The whole route was very scenic and enjoyable. It was one of the highlights of our trip.

I was very happy with the patient, nice woman who sold tickets & let me see where the seats would be that I purchased as she walked me into the venue to check it out. I bought tickets for my daughter & son-in-law & they loved the seating & how comfortable & roomy it was. They loved the pizza & the variety of beer they sold. The production was very good & they are looking forward to seeing more shows there. Great date night!!

Holy boba! Some great stuff in a cup!!! Gotta get that halo halo all the toppings were yummy and their flan is so tasty!!! Try the a chocolate-taro smoothie aka the "Johnny" or at least they should call it that cause I order it too much.

food as always is delicious- the hash brown casserole is my fave.  however, the women's bathroom was absolutely disgusting.  the floors were sticky, it had a strong urine smell, and the stalls were not very clean.  I definitely recommend the food, but prepare to hold it and not use their bathroom.

Opera on Monday nights is well worth thr trip! Fabulous dinner and great atmosphere been here a few times and have never been disappointed in the food or service. Extensive menu with the something for everyone and the portions are huge. I have to say its one of the best byob's I have been too I highly recommend trying it if you've never been!

I have been going to veekoo forever. The food is delicious and fresh the only problem is they get so crowded between takeout orders and people waiting to be sat that it's almost like waiting in a crowded subway car. They should expand the sushi bar so you can actually sit at it and expand the waiting area to make customers more comfortable. They have already remodeled once, it's time to do it again.

Always a line outside... Always. It's there thing. But line moved well enough. Friendly staff and great food. Ordered the cooks medley(skillet dish) very good and it comes with pancakes if you want. Had their sweet potato pancakes, soft and very flavorful didn't except anything less. Coffee wasn't bad but not incredible.
Great prompt service,  Chris the manager goes above and beyond to make sure work is done right. Very good service.

My wife and I traveled to Philadelphia from Houston to celebrate our 20th wedding anniversary.  Vetri Cucina helped make our anniversary meal very special.  We frequent a lot of tasting menu restaurants, and enjoy being led by the chef's selections - but sometimes you get a dish that doesn't quite fit with your dietary preferences (as opposed to allergies).  Vetri Cucina's system of allowing you to look at the 20 or so potential dishes for the night and to let the kitchen know which dishes you DO NOT and which dish might be a MUST HAVE allows the kitchen to create a tasting menu tailored just for you.  They also do not serve each person in your party the same menu.  This allowed my wife and I to basically share a 13 course tasting menu, instead of 6 or 7 courses.  Service was very informed and outstanding.  The restaurant itself is located in a renovated brownstone, so it has a very homey feel to it.

The tuna crudo and prosciutto dishes were my favorite antipasta courses.  The pastas were the real standout dishes.  My favorite was the Fetuccelle (cross between fettuccine and parpadelle) with porcini and blueberry.  The pasta was perfect and the sauce was an interesting combination of the earthiness of the mushrooms and the sweetness of the blueberry.  My wife enjoyed the malfadine with braised beef ragu.  Very meaty and very flavorful.  

For the "secondi" courses, we were served the porcelet and the veal dishes.  Both were very tasty, but at this point in the meal we were getting pretty full, and we wished we would had been served the seafood course (snapper) to lighten up the meal a bit.  Live and learn, it would have been easy to ask for that dish at the beginning of the meal.  The desserts were good, but at this point, we were really stuffed.  Great anniversary meal though.  I highly recommend Vetri Cucina for a tasting menu that is quite collaborative between chef and diner.

I love love love the food from here. It's always top-notch and the ghost sauce is amazing. The service is sometimes not 100% and there is limited parking. Other than that I would highly recommend this place to the BBQ connoisseur.

Service was fine and it's nice that it's a BYO but I was super disappointed with the sushi here. It all tasted like it had seen better days- even the spicy tuna which generally can hide sub par fish with the spicy sauce. There are much better BYO sushi places in Philly, I would for sure skip this one.
Try the wine and beer tour. After a few wine tasting you can get a little drowsy. Mixing thing up with a beer tasting really wakes you up.

Today me and my 4 friends went to cosi to enjoy the "make your own smores"...which we were very excited about. We ordered a big tray of smores for the 5 of us, and the person taking our order said he would bring our smores to our table upstairs. After a few minutes he came upstairs to serve us our smores. When he went to light the fire so that we could toast the marshmellows, he said lit the match, held it up, and said a ritual as his eyes rolled back. He said something along the lines of "Curse God for bringing fire to mankind" and then lit our tray for our food. It gave me and my girlfriends a very uneasy feeling, and we went to speak with the manager right away. The manager was really nice to us about the situation but she also wasn't surprised that it happened. However she did fully refund us and gave us 2 free entree passes. I just wanted to post this to the cosi Facebook page so it doesn't happen again. We also noticed at the end that he was handling the food without gloves and extra long nails.

Was trying to think of a good place to eat last night that was good, quick, low cost and nearby. Yats came to mind. Food is always tasty and Joe the owner is still there making sure the customers are satisfied. He was offering everyone in line a taste of the latest dishes. I just ordered the jambalaya as I knew from past experience that it would be a great choice. When I got my carry out, it felt like 2 pounds of food!
For 6.75 ( including tax) I thought it was a great deal. 
I actually couldn't finish it all and have dinner for tonight as well. (Don't tell joe that his food is under valued)
Another favorite is the chili cheese étouffée.

Went in with some trepidation given the gimmick of a spinning dining room and was pleasantly surprised. While I could still do without the moving floor I had an enjoyable meal. Our waitress Darlena was fantastic. The food was a bit over priced but pretty good. I had a jerk steak special which was very tasty. Friends had coconut crusted grouper which they very much enjoyed. The place is bit of a cheese fest but once you get past that you realize it's kinda fun.

I had high expectations from reviews, but was disappointed. They didn't have anything too interesting, my food was served barely luke warm and needed a lot of salt. However, the pancakes were pretty good and the servers were nice.

One of our go to spots for weekend work lunch location. They are usually not that busy around 11 on a Saturday. They always offer a fast, friendly service which is a big deal to me!

I usually go with their enchilada with chicken and I love it. It's flavorful and delicious. They also make their food quite fast so whenever I am starving, I usually will pick this place over others because I know I'll get my food quick. 

Aside from weekend work lunch, my colleagues and I have also been here for a happy hour.  They don't really have any specials as far as happy hour goes but their drinks were affordable enough. It was fairly busy in the afternoon with some families out dining as well as people out for some drinks after work. We went on a Friday night so I'm guessing that was also a factor.

Overall, this place is pretty nice and the service is fast which is important especially if you have to go back to work or have an appointment you need to keep.

Nice place. They seem to be going for Guiness world record for most Lassi and Chaat flavors. Not only that, the food is also good. the Chaat looks a little strange. I must admit I was apprehensive, but once I tried it it was quite good. I had the Kunna lamb Chaat and my wife had the Chicken Keema. We also had a Lychee Lassi and a Date Almond Lassi, along with a sample of one that had strawberry in it. Only downside is this place is a bit of a hole-in-the-wall with very little seating. Probably better for takeout, although we were able to get one of the three tables when we were there.

Pros: nice place, clean, quiet, authentic.nice and warm. Great specials. Extensive menu, with many options. Pork chop not to be missed!

Cons: little slow to get food out in the order it goes in. A little heavy on sauces, and having the entire order ready at the same time.

House wine is excellent. 

Reservations a must.

If you are expecting "American Italian" food,
This isn't for you.
This is the real deal from the wait staff that clearly understands Italian hospitality.

Ok so I love the fact that they have organic food that doesn't have chemicals but one they are overpriced. Two, I had a slice of pizza and broccoli rabe and they were both horrible. I went in there today to buy berries and I was looking at the containers to make sure I get a good one and the produce guy clearly got annoyed that I was moving them and basically took one from my hand. A small container is $6 or more so as a customer I have the right to make sure the berries are fresh. I'm going to find another organic store with better prices!

For a smoked meat house this placed rocked the Green Dragon Vegan sandwich (disclaimer: there is honey in the dressing) I popped in after a float session at Modern Gravity cause I was too relaxed to drive. 

The space is very rustic, trendy and in it's own right had an individual flare of a backyard picnic with white string lights, an old bike and white washed wood. Black marker words of inspiration, love and admiration towards the restaurant were scrawled in front of the kitchen. The unique charm of this establishment is the homemade perserves they offer for sale and in their dishes. They use local producers and bring things back to basics. They do add a sense of adventure with items like pickled daikon. 

The place closes at 3pm for high tea. But at 2:30 they still allowed me in. All of the staff were authentic and really warm to be around. 

I choose the Green Dragon veggie sandwich on rye with a side order of fries and a coffee. The coffee was rich and flavourful. The sandwich was kale and sprouts tossed with a honey vinegrette dressing layered with pickles and jalapeno hummus on rye. It was a brilliant sandwich with a compliment of sweet, sour, astrigent and bitter flavours. The fries were excellent. Deep fried shoe string coated in cayanne with home made Ketchup. It could have used a bit more salt. But that's just me. 

Overall it was an excellent lunch. I left feeling full, happy and relaxed. I really enjoyed all aspects of the restaurant.

This place rocked during the time they were at the house instead of the strip mall. It was the best in town for BBQ. I was there with my wife one night and the sausage, baby back ribs were cremated...it was so dark, dry and had the scent of burn gasoline. The next time I came it was great, then another time it was the same dry meat again. Hit or miss or what is the deal?

If you can fit it in your budget, request one of the balcony rooms on the 2nd floor.  Sometimes being above the crowded streets can be more fun.  The rooms are well appointed, but you are getting location.  This busy hotel's service suffers during Carnival or any of the festivals when crowds converge on the quarter.  This is the Big Easy, time moves in a different direction here.

I have to agree with majority of other Yelpers here - the quality of both the food & customer service are way off. I ordered a buffalo chicken wrap & sweet potato fries & the delivery man practically threw it onto my porch like a newspaper. The flour wrap was stiff & tasted kind of stale & the sweet potato fries were way undercooked. I have had their lasagna before & really liked it so maybe I'll stop in & try that to see if redemption is possible.

The place seems was popular based on the crowd  Saturday night.  I can only surmise there is a lack of good Mexican food in Indy because the food was only slightly better than what you would get in any strip mall Mexican place at half the price.  The decor was modern and well executed. The service was mediocre at best.   I will not return or recommend.

i really really liked the pho here. unlike some so-called pho places, they did not use heavy msg in their broth. they also give you hefty portions of meat and tendon...yum!!! also, the place was clean and the waiters were very attentive -- extra points for that.
Good food, cold beer, great people :-) Nice place to go in this area. The French Onion soup was amazing, everything our table got was fantastic, enjoy :-)
Not happy when my husband comes home with a latte for me and it's only 8oz in a 12oz cup and way overpriced! See the photo I posted!

I go there every Sunday all day spent over 1000$ i got kicked out the club because one guy of security don't like me. I will find is name and updated this post. It was my girl friend birthday you guy lost over 800$ good job. This guy called police on me i have never had anything to do with police on my life. I will never go there again.
Taylor Home Solutions did such a great job on my carpet and furniture. I would highly recommend their services. Thanks a bunch Jeff!

I love their Hawaiian pizza.  Good toppings, great crust.  I typically like deep dish, a close second would be this crust.  It's not thick but it's not thin.  It's somewhere in between and it's soft and delicious.  

Best quick lunch or takeout dinner.

I LOVED this place! Might just be my new favorite restaurant in Philly.  The food, the service, the ambiance -- all quaint, simple, and perfect.  I read some reviews about poor service but that wasn't my experience at all.  The waiter was extremely helpful and thorough -- and we were a tough crowd with lots of questions.  For an appetizer, we all ordered the dips, which included, among other things, the best babaganoush I've ever had.  For an entree, I ordered the stuffed vegetables which was stuffed cabbage with lentils, rice, and feta.  It was amazing! My fiance got the veal dish and also loved.  Our two other dining companions ordered the rabbit and the special of the day - a pork dish - and they were as equally impressed as us.  For dessert, we got the homemade ice cream - halavah and mint flavored.  Delicious! The chef was making rounds during dinner and we had a chance to tell him what an amazing dinner we enjoyed.  I will definitely be back -- very excited to try their brunch!

I am a seasoned traveler. I had to come to Wilmington for business, and decided to bring my family.  The hotel is clean and brand new (two weeks so far), so it seemed promising, but they have LOTS of things to figure out.  First, many bathrooms don't have bathtubs- which may be a problem if you have a family and a toddler.  When we arrived into the room, we couldn't find a directory of services  and when I called to reception to get one they seemed confused as to why a guest would possibly want to have a room service menu, information about the hotel, etc. In fact every time we called whoever picked up the phone sounded confused, as if we were randomly calling a stranger. We were excited that there was a swimming pool, but the water was absolutely freezing- we couldn't stay there for more than 5 minutes.  We ran, freezing, back to the room to discover that water in the shower was lukewarm at best- we never managed to get a hot shower in all our stay. Room service was chaotic: I was put on hold three times and each time I needed to start my order anew,  and both times we ordered the order came wrong --they blamed the reception desk (how is that  smart customer service?). Once they delivered the drinks again by mistake.  The whole thing started to be funny. Room service was very expensive for hotel standards. The restaurant serves tapas portions at the price of full plates (the idea is that you need to share and order three dishes per person, the waiter helpfully explained).  When we were leaving, the whole lobby had buckets everywhere: the ceiling was leaking from the swimming pool on top of it which is right on the second floor. Scary.  When we were finally asked at checkout how was our stay and we described what I just wrote, they seemed sympathetic but acted as if we were talking about a different hotel. They took our name saying someone would be in touch with us. I am still waiting.

I came here once for lunch with coworkers. Service was fast, which is good when you have to get back to work. 
Their lunch deal is really good. You get the choice of an appetizer/salad, soup, and an entree with generous portions for a great price! They also have a good vegetarian selection as well. I got the silver noodles. The dessert looked really good, too, but I was too full after finishing my meal. I scraped my plate clean and left very satisfied! The others I went with were just as happy.

We originally found this place on Yelp. We love this place. The all you can drink beer is a great deal and if you can't fill a pitcher, the owner will definitely call you out for it. ;) He has a great personality which really makes you feel like you a regular customer  the first time you walk in. The all you can eat snow crab on Tuesdays is one of the best deals. You won't go hungry and even the biggest eaters can fill themselves on crab and free beer. If you are looking for authentic seafood served unassumingly look no further than Monstah Lobstah.

We had take out last night. We had samosa, garlic naan, Baingan Bhartha, and Del Makhani. It was really really good! It took a while to get our order but the staff informed us ahead of time so it was not a surprise about 35min). The staff was very friendly and gave us a type of appetizer we "Free" due to the wait. How cool is that? We got our food and took it to our room and it was soooo good! I recommend this to everyone out there wanting to try Indian food. Great place, great service.

I am new to the area and go the dentist every six months.  I made an appointment for a cleaning and i got an evening appointment within a week (the only reason for one star). When I got there, the office smelled like fast food and the girl was on the phone arguing with a kid to do their homework and she acted like she didn't see me until she was done with her call.  Then the assistant took my xrays and started telling me she saw a deep cavity-which made me alittle nervous because I just saw my dentist about 7 months ago and i had been going to him for about 10 years and he never said anything...then the hygeinist comes in and uses this water instrument that hurt like hell-i have never had that instrument used before and she was done in about 10 minutes so there is NO way i had that much crap in there.  Then she found out who referred me and wanted nothing more to gossip about them.  After i didn't give her much about that, she started gossiping about someone else to the assistant who took my xrays.  Then the dentist comes in to check  me-and didn't use that metal pick thing to check my teeth- which was a first-and wanted to fill the gap between my front teeth.  I like my gap!  He also didn't say anything about the deep cavity the assistant saw-and when i asked him he said we would watch that.  (Watch it do what-get bigger?!)  Then i go back out to the front desk again-and the girl is back on the phone with the kid again!  So I waited and she wanted to make me an appointment to fill the gap and i told her i would call.   I left with sore gums, unsure if i had a cavity or not and alittle self conscience about my gap.  Wow.  Three words for this office   rushed, chaotic and unprofessional

I was in Tampa briefly from DC for work and saw this place highly rated so decided to try it. So glad I did! Not only was the food amazing the man behind he counter was hilarious. Both funny and friendly with great service before we even asked. 

I ordered a gyro with a Greek salad and fried mushrooms. I didn't expect for the sides to be large enough to be their own meals! All was delicious and the portions were huge. All in all, a great experience- very clean establishment, fast food with great flavor and service. Would definitely come here again or recommend to others in the Tampa area.

Take-outs from Nadia Thai were timely, hot and awesome... We had the shrimp and corn cakes, which were fifty cent size pieces of corn cake...
Spicy, and plenty of shrimp with each bite...
Next, pork with wild ginger sauce and vegetables...perfect for a cold night, served with rice...plenty for two, and He had the Won Ton and liked it so much...I can't comment, because I didn't have any...
We'll be back, and we consider it a 2 person take-out because of the location...parking in front is luck of the draw...parking next to florist after hours??? might be ok...
