If you are not in a hurry and don't mind waiting it will be worth it.  The staff here is so helpful and good at what they do.  The bartenders were some of the best I have seen and offer great feedback on the beer and wine choices of which there are good ones!  I also think for the amount of food you get the cost is quite reasonable.  I was amazed at how many people were getting their tomahawk cut for one!  That is one large steak!!

Top notch. The hot and sour soup was good, with some subtlety. The garlic sauce (I ordered chicken with garlic sauce) was the best I can remember eating, and the veggies with it were nice. I'm a tough customer and rarely wowed by Chinese food. The portions are a bit smaller than typical Chinese but I'll take quality over quantity all day , and I left full for $10.

The ladies at the desk are very friendly. I have never been here and waited leas than an hour. It's absolutely ridiculous the amount of time they have you waiting. I understand that things happen but every single time I wait for over an hour.

This place. So, you're going to look at most of these reviews and feel like this place must be pretty good. Which is exactly what we did when we found ourselves in Maplewood and hungry.

But. An $8 "vegetable" salad consisted of arugula and carrots (barely heated up and basically raw) with an über salty brown butter "dressing". And it was on a side salad plate. Not good.

We continued to the veal meatballs which were completely dried out and dense. They didn't even really taste like veal -- you expect a little gaminess with some sort of aggressive spice. We got nothing. The polenta on the plate and the sauce was pretty good though (and it's a lot of food, definitely shareable if the meatballs themselves were better).

Then, it was on to dessert. We love dessert. Especially panna cotta. And even more if it's chocolate. Which is what was advertised. What we got though? Some sort of watery, jello-y concoction ... I wish I would have taken video. It was so weird. Like it was made from a box with water instead of cream, or milk even. Tasteless and boring.

And damn, expensive to boot. I can't imagine a scenario where I would want to go back here -- unless I just wanted to sit down for a while with a glass of wine, cause it is a nice looking place with nice people working there and what appears to be a good, extensive wine list (we did not partake). Just, the food. Yikes.

TJ is amazing! I've gone twice and he's done 2 family pieces for me. My first was the Alzheimer's symbol with ENDALZ in script. He is a chill guy, keeps the conversation flowing and is kick ass at his job! My second piece by his was another family piece and sentimental to me. So lucky my roommate told me about TJ, because after 8 years of a tattoo idea I had, I sketched it up but needed the right artist to finish it off and put it on my body.  TJ is that lucky artist that will finally put that 8 year in the making idea on my shoulder after my wedding this summer! He is extremely talented!

Finally a good San Diego mexican "fast" food joint in town!!
It was a staple i missed living there over 20 years.
Half order of super nachos are awesome! Carne asada is plentiful and cant beat the sour cream and guac.
Carne Asada burritos will satisfy a HUGE appetite. 
Takes a bit longer to prepare your food....yea they dont warm it up but prepare to order so its way worth the wait.

To understand why I love this place, I first need to explain why I started looking into spinning in the first place. I used to run frequently as my primary form of exercise (on a treadmill). A few years ago, however, I was diagnosed with psoriatic arthritis in several of my joints, with my knees being particularly affected. The pain and discomfort forced me to stop running. Over the next few years, I gained a fair amount of weight because I felt as though exercise was now off-limits to me. Earlier this year, my new doctor recommended exercise again and suggested spinning because it is both high-cardio (which is good for weight loss) and low-impact (easy on the joints). I chose Body Cycle for two reasons - it offers a free class for newbies (which explains the ins and outs of spinning and the bikes) and it's very close to my job. It's a good bit cheaper than other studios, which I like. 

The other things I love about going here is that the instructors never, ever pressure you. They will make suggestions about gear and how fast you might want to go, but those are just that - suggestions. Especially for somebody like me with a condition, this is great - because I get to be in control of the experience and go at my own pace when I need to. The instructors are unfailing positive and upbeat. I try to go at least once a week, but my odd work schedule can sometimes make that tough, so I try to fit it in when I can (they offer early mornings, after work and noon classes, so this isn't hard). Going here has been great for me both physically and mentally. It's helping me get back into shape physically, and on a mental level, it's helped me realize that I can still be active and maintain exercising even with a condition. I'd recommend Body Cycle to anybody who is interested in spinning, but especially would to anybody who is recovering from injury or with a condition. If your doctor clears you, I'd say come here - the environment is outstanding and supportive, and you'll enjoy it very much.

Pretty neat for a courtyard. The rooms look more like Renaissance hotels, I was impressed by the cleanliness. Has a nice lobby with bar and starbucks with its full menu, not just coffee. Had got a suite for $179/night...not bad at all. It's walking distance to most of the touristy spots and music venues. Staff was super friendly. It is easiest to valet park, although there are several public parking lots around the hotel in addition to the hotel parking. 4 stars cuz the bathroom was nothing impressive.

This is a funky little place to eat. I've only had breakfast here, and it was typical greasy diner food. They are known for their milkshakes, but since I've never tried them I can't tell you how good or bad they are. Some might call the decor of this place charming, but I honestly don't know what to think of it. You'll just have to decide for yourself.

Chili's has become that restaurant that we only go to when we are super bored with the other late night restaurants AND enough time has passed to forget how awful they are. They may have a new decor and some new menu items, but this is still the same old crappy Chili's with the same problems:

1- rarely a hostess to greet you
2- mediocre to awful service that takes FOREVER
3- disappointing (sometimes disgusting) food (I have even been served moldy cheese at this location..eww)

Our most recent visit reaffirmed that we do not like Chili's and we will not be returning soon. We arrived a little before 9pm and there was not an employee in sight. Since we were hoping to make this a quicker visit, we seated ourselves at the bar area along with 90% of the people that were in the restaurant (I'm guessing there was not hostess for them either). 

We were asked for our drink orders rather quickly. We ordered our drinks and took a few minutes to decide on our dinner. You are supposed to be brought free chips and salsa in the bar area...never happened. To make matters worse, the two tables right in front of us both received their chips and salsa. I guess they just didn't like us?

After we ordered we waited...and waited...and waited. It took about 35 minutes for one mushroom swiss burger and a carnitas fajitas. When the food arrived the burger was smaller than normal (we have ordered this burger here before), overcooked and SUPER dry. On top of that, my Husband's fries were about 1/4 of the normal amount they serve. He literally had about 7 overcooked tiny fries on the plate. Pathetic. 

My fajitas were served with a huge amount of onions, green bell peppers (which were undercooked) and carnitas. Unfortunately, I was only given a few tiny tortillas. It also came with some ridiculous tree of condiments (guac, some sort of taco sauce, sour cream, cheese, tomatoes, green chilis with pickled onions and a few other things). The meat was BLAND. How do you even make carnitas bland? The meat naturally has so much flavor. I also had a HUGE piece of stringy fat. Disgusting. We both ate our entrees feeling more and more gross as we ate. We left feeling sick. We probably would have complained if there had been anyone around. 

After waiting for awhile and having our credit card on the table, we finally had our server come back and say "Ohh sorry, you pay with the Ziosk now" and show us how to pay. That would have been nice to know at the beginning. 

Needless to say, we will not be back anytime soon. We will stick with BJ's for late night meals.

Worst customer service ever!  Went in at 7:40pm, 20 min before their closing time. Immediately a woman rolled her eyes and asked if there was something we were looking for because they were closing in a few minutes. 2 more employees felt the need to follow us and ask if we needed assistance because they were closing. seriously!?! 20 min people! I wanted to go upstairs and would have likely made a purchase but felt rushed and like they didn't want my business. Will NOT be going back! I refuse to give my money and business to an establishment who treats customers like this!

Beautiful 360 views of Santa Barbara--for free :-)

Highlights:
- Views: after a short elevator ride, you can walk around the square and see views from each direction. Mountains and the mission on one end and the ocean on the other. Cool birdseye spot to check out the little city. 
- Free: not your typical big city spot where you have to pay $20+ 
- Nice sb style building 
- Just few blocks from action on State Street

Lowlights:
- Not much else there so more of a few minutes activity than a destination

Glad my local friends gave us this heads up.

Went here for game 7 where the Warriors pulled it off against the thunder. Olivia made beer drinking an act of tribute to the beer deity, citing viscosity and aromatic natures. I highly suggest going there and having her describe each and every beer in detail and then pair with menu. Have a ball!
Yats is always consistent, with very good Gumbo.  I just wish they had the Gumbo more often and had brown rice as an option.

My boyfriend and I had polar opposite experiences here, on the same visit together.  So I would give it one star, he would give it 5..... which averages to three.  

It was our first time trying this place.  Customer service was good - everyone says aloha!  Food came out quickly.

We started out with onion rings.  They were ok, but nothing special. 

I ordered a grilled cheese and it was yucky :(  I can't describe what the deal was, but I had my boyfriend check it out and he thinks it had a ton of butter on it, and that's what made it taste bad.  It smelled just like it tasted too - a weird dusty old taste. My boyfriend said it was like movie theater popcorn butter.  I couldn't finish it, each bite was just gross.  I figured my boyfriend would eat it for me or want to take it home for later since he eats ANYTHING - Old food, food that's been sitting out, anything.... he's like a garbage disposal - But even he thought it was nasty.  So that was a bummer.  I got fries with it, and they were alright.

But out of the onion rings, grilled cheese, and fries I really wasn't digging any of it, and don't want to go back to have more. 

My boyfriend got the Colby burger and he loved it.  He said it was the best burger he has ever had.  He ordered it with mushrooms, avocado, and bacon and it was huge.  He couldn't stop talking about what a great place this was and how great his food was.  

I mean he was REALLY in love with this place...  He is the type of guy who is super stingy with tips and hates to tip for any sort of service, even though I feel like especially at restaurants, it is expected.  But he said that he wanted to give our guy an EXTRA big tip!  I have never heard those words come out of his mouth before.  He is also the type who is very hard to please at restaurants... every little thing bugs him, he always says he never wants to return because of some crazy little thing.  But here he said that he WANTS to go back and that he had an awesome experience (for example, he liked how the server asked for permission before taking his plate away - told you he's a hard-ass!). 

So I'm really dreading going back, but I think we will be doing that soon.  I guess I should have figured that at a place called "cheeseburger" you should probably just order a cheeseburger instead of trying something that isn't the restaurant's forte.

Visited The Bricks this evening for dinner with a group of 6 and I think I can say we all enjoyed our experience  - I give it a solid 3-stars because I wasn't blown away by the food, ambiance or service but all were good if not a little above average. 

I started with an Old Fashioned which was sadly, quite watered down.  The table started with the Bricklayer Nachos which were good and a pretty decent size portion too.  For my dinner I had the Mediterranean Grilled Cheese - feta and mozzarella cheese, olive tapenade, baby spinach and portabello mushroom pressed in a piece of flatbread.  The first few bites were enjoyable but about a quarter of the way into it I realized how SALTY it was.  Unfortunately, it was a little one-note and better in concept than in execution in my opinion. 

Our waitress was pleasant and split the check 6-ways without us even having to ask, which I thought was really nice of her.  Atmosphere was unique but nothing worth coming back for.

Also, worth noting - The Bricks doesn't have its own parking lot so you'll have to find street parking (good luck), a paid parking lot lot or one of the local parking garages.
30+ beers on tap,  good variety menu, Nachos were great!  Tucked away but worth leaving the interstate for.  Lots of regulars, but we felt just as welcome!

I've been here a couple of times now and now convinced I'd rather get my sushi elsewhere. The atmosphere has a kind of dingy feel to it and the service was pretty bad. Most of their rolls have cream cheese or have fried components so kind of difficult to get a healthier option. The mussels were overlooked and the rolls we got were OK. However, I will say that some of the nigiri we got was pretty good and they have some good specials.

My hole away from home.  Though I'm not there very often, they remember my choice of beverage, and are already opening a beer as I walk through the door. It's as if  they instinctively know how much I hate visiting with my parents.  This place is like Cheers, though a little seedier. The fireplace isn't real, but there are four pool tables, several dart boards, and usually a free table for 6.  The Copper Top, or Topper Cop, as it's sometimes known, keeps it simple. Cheep beer on tap, good company, and a juke box blaring such artists as Kid Rock, Outkast, and Marilyn Manson.  If I'm in Tampa and it's after 9 on a weeknight, there's a good chance you'll find me here.

This review is for the restaurant and hotel together. Restaurant alone would get 5, hotel 3. First, the hotel. My girlfriend and I arrived by bike, and our host seemed a bit unwelcoming. We had read some not positive reviews about the hospitality there, so were prepared for a negative experience. Upon further experience though, we realized that our host is just an eccentric lady, and is actually super sweet. She met us in the parking lot to take our credit card so she could get us in our room asap, as she saw us arrive by bike, and assumed we were exhausted. Our room was not impressive (I don't recommend room 3), but we asked to move and were accommodated without drama. Room 2 was a huge improvement, with its 4 post bed and well arranged furniture. The hotel staff were very warm and friendly. Continental breakfast was more than enough to eat, and featured fresh croissants. Their grounds are lovely, and away from the hustle and bustle. One note for bikers; they have a sheltered bike rack (converted horse shelter), which is a huge plus. Now, the restaurant: to start, we were given 50% off our bottle of wine because we were hotel guests. The food was just plain amazing. I had the filet, my girlfriend the duck. We had sweetbreads as an appetizer. It was the best meal I've had since eating at Marigold (in West Philadelphia), which is considerably more expensive. Everything was prepared exquisitely. I can't understand the bad food reviews, except to say that no meat in any French restaurant should ever be ordered above medium, or prepare for disappointment. French meats should be consumed rare to raw. In all, we had a lovely weekend with lovely hosts, and would repeat the experience anytime.

Went for dinner on a Saturday night around 8pm. Place was a little packed. Southern melt was delicious; pork was perfectly cooked. Coleslaw was tasty. Amigos ordered the luah Kaluah pork and the peanut noodle salad. Both were delicious! Saw Sabrina delivering a lime tart....it looked soo good I had to have it. Oh thank goodness I did! Best lime tart I've ever had. I'll definitely go back!

Not impressed. I understand only having 4 treadmills when starting out, but this little place is jam packed around 5PM and there is nothing available. Then they take out an additional $25 on top of your membership every few months and take suggestions on a new piece of equipment although I'm not sure where they plan on putting all this stuff. I think it's overpriced as well. The staff is friendly and helpful. I would recommend going in the mornings as it is empty between 6-8.

This is easily the best cuban sandwich, pastelito and espresso i have ever had. the espresso shot is included with your meal, which is a nice touch and a nice caffeine postwould definitely recommend and will be back for more!
Great Mexican food close by! Guacamole is outstanding, and the meals we had tonight were very good. Did I mention the $2.99 margaritas?  Yum! Friendly staff, too!

More Cuban inspired than actual Cuban cuisine. Experienced stellar service. Had a few appetizers( yuca fries, conch fritters and jerk veggie fritters) and tried the micro brews. Everything delicious. All the sauces were really good too. A table favorite was the jerk sauce.  The black beans were a little bit al dente and bland but I grew up in Miami and am extremely biased. I LOVE the outdoor seating on this strip - full moon and ocean breeze. Very very groovy vibe.

Monday, April 30, 2012 - Noon - 

After nearly two years, council approved the sale of 1 W. State St by a 4-3 vote to restaurateur Claudio Sandolo. Sandolo also owns Spasso Italian Grill in Old City, Philadelphia.  The building at State and Jackson streets previous tenant was Brodeur's Restaurant who vacated in Nov. 2009.  Prior to that was The New Orleans Café.  This building's history includes the post office through the 1960's and use as the borough hall into the 1990s.
I previously dined here when Brodeur's occupied the space.  I enjoyed the outdoor patio situated along the wall. 
The inside of Spasso is clean, bright, with brick-colored paint.  I ate facing an opened  semicircle doorway leading to additional dining space. I viewed two fans revolving from the ceiling where typically the iconic paddled ceiling fan would rest. 

I ordered the escarole soup and pork sandwich.  While waiting, I was served delicious complimentary bread with a dish of roasted peppers (red and green), zucchini, artichokes, and onions.  The escarole soup with over-sized meatballs was good.  The pork sandwich had slivers of provolone - also good. 
Music gently filled the room from the 1960's.  The music genres switched reciprocally from Italian to light jazz.  An artist sampling include: Jerry Vale, Ray Charles, Bobby Darin, and Bobby Rydell. 

The service was quite good and accommodating.

Spasso Italian Grill in Media opened about two weeks ago.  I'm hoping they're here longer than the previous occupants.

I'm a bit surprised by the negative reviews so far.  Maybe things have changed?  I'll keep this short and to the point.
I went last week after realizing Jake's was closed, and still craving a burger.  I remembered that Zac's took over for 5 Guys, so I figured I'd give it a shot.  I had a standard bacon-cheeseburger with extra cheese; as well as an order of waffle fries.

The burger was good.  It wasn't Jakes/Five Guys, but it was close.  It was cooked properly, tasted good, and the bacon was cooked perfectly.  
The waffle fries were real good.  They were the seasoned kind, so less chick-fil-a and more arby's curly fry flavor.  

I didn't have a chance to try the milkshake, but will next time.

Here's the thing about Zac's.  The burgers aren't as good as Jake's, and the fries aren't as good as Five Guys.  The fries are good, the burgers are good; just not as good as the more known establishments.  Considering Jake's is closed and 5 Guys gone; this makes a fine and serviceable replacement.  

Go in with moderate expectations and I think you'll be pleased.  If you're going for the next Jake's or Five Guys; skip Zac's and go to Jake's or Five Guys.  If you're looking for a pretty good burger and/or pretty good fries; give Zac's a shot.  Don't believe all the negativity because it's not bad.  Form your own opinion, but just give it a fair shot.

I was starving and stopped off at moe's for some lunch. First time visitor to this chain. I had a chicken burrito bowl with black beans peppers cooked onions pico de gallo lettuce and cheese. Tasty. Liked the idea they included salsa and chips with any order. 

What's really cool is their coke freestyle machine. It makes 106 flavors. Nice concept.

The place is casual and fast. The ingredients tasted fresh and the price was reasonable.
These guys are KILLING IT with their salmon game! I'm staying at the Hotel Monaco and have had their salmon for dinner as well as salmon with a Cobb salad for lunch- both fantastic. Great food!

Since I had some free time today, I decided to take the Steamboat tour. It was reasonably priced. You could either choose to get the lunch included or not. Either way, the tour was nice. The narrator gave good information about the sights we were seeing and about the boat itself. The jazz band was pretty good and it was just an overall good time. I would definitely recommend anyone to do it and would soon again, myself.

The Brandy Alexander martini was amazing. It was so good I wanted to lick the glass. My veggie sandwich and the side salad with Brussel sprouts were delicious too! The service staff was very attentive from time we walked in the door. I will  definitely go back the next time I am in St Louis.
Tiffany does a beautiful job on my nails every time! She always double checks to make sure the shape, color and style is exactly how you want them.
Amazing pickle chips. Amazing veggie wings. Great margaritas (I love passion fruit). Probably my favorite restaurant in the city.

I love O'Charley's food, I really do. I used to work at a different location and everything is so tasty!

It seems, however, that every time I visit this location the service just disappoints me. Not so horrible I wouldn't return but I am just so let down...maybe I have too high of standards since I know how I used to serve there.

The last time I was there the manager looked as if he was about to scream and punch the wall. He looked so angry walking around and it was quite odd. Our server was pleasant...sometimes, she was busy, which I more than understand but when she was at the table she didn't really listen and it was so frustrating!  Near the end of the meal, the angry manger came over to see how our evening was and he seemed so calm and pleasant that after he left my mom and I just looked at each other and started giggling. What a 180 he just pulled, it was so odd.

As for the food the the last time I went, it was ok. Rolls were good but our appetizer was a disappointment. We got the chips with the queso sauce on them and it was super runny and just kinda made the chips soggy and barely stuck to it. We both got the Black N Bleu salad which was delicious as always except mine had a TON of bacon crumbles on it. Someone got a bit careless, overall though, it was still the good food I remember.

I will still return, I just hope someday I will have a good all around experience!
thank you guys for always fixing my lashes!! the service is always fast and inexpensive and the ladies are so kind and helpful!! thank you so much!

The first time I went here I was in college and my friend and I had this ridiculously hilarious obsession (it started as joke and just snowballed) about Chili's El Presidente margaritas. Neither of us are crazy about Chili's food (what is there to be crazy about) we only went there for the margaritas. 

Yes, that is kind of a weird thing to do, but they were so damn good. 

I think we went there twice to have their El Presidente margaritas then we decided that it might taste better if we could eliminate Chili's from the equation. 

Anyway, somehow my friend figured out what the ingredients were, either by asking the bartender or just watching one being made. It had, among other things, cointreau, which is not hard to find but it also had some kind of tequila I cannot remember the name of that was like the unicorn of tequilas. 

I kid you not my friend and I were calling liquor stores all over to see if they had this tequila that we needed because we wanted the recipe to be 100% exactly like what is served at the restaurant. 

We called and called and it seemed like the dream of an El Presidente margarita minus the whole being at Chilli's thing was slipping away. But we kept trying, damn it we knew someone would have it.

Guess where we found it? Dorignac's. 

Their alcohol selection is the bee's knees. I am pretty sure they have bottles of vodka the size of my vacuum cleaner. 

I have not done any regular grocery shopping here which makes me sound like a saucy boozehound. 

For me it comes down to what I need and convenience, this place is just a little far away for me to be doing general grocery shopping. I will, however, l take a look around their meat department and deli next time I am there. It is a really unique store and from what I have heard I imagine they stock a lot of high quality products.

Ricuras de Venezuela helped host an awesome event at MOCA for me.  They were great about coordinating before the event, and we had arrival, departure, and number of guests pinned down.  The guests all loved the food, Ricuras really helped make my event a success!

I placed an order for three kits back on April 14.  I got a note from the owner about 2 weeks later that they didn't have the stock yet, but would soon.  Now it is June 10, almost two months later, and they have not responded to any of follow up messages or picked up any of my phone calls (and I can't leave a message as the box is full).  The website remains functional so I don't believe they have gone out of business, but clearly there is something wrong.

I wish I could write a good review as I believe in supporting local businesses, but this is just not acceptable.

This place just lost a loyal customer! I Buy boots here at least every six months,the last pair I got hurt my feet and I tried to return them after wearing them for one hour,but they refused to do it even though there was no wear or tear on them! Not to mention how rude they are most times!!! Do yourself a favor and avoid this millers location!!!!!

The food here is good. It's solid and a healthy option that I would frequent more often if it wasn't for the very poor service. Now, I've never had a problem with someone taking my order...it's the wait. It's the fact that there's one person taking orders and making the salads while there is someone else behind the wall NOT stepping in to temporarily assist get the line under control. I waited 25 minutes for 2 salads. How is this "quick"? 

I've reached out on their website on more than one occasion and have never gotten a response. Poor management starts at the top.

The place makes you miserable... The only good thing about it is the music. The prices make no sense and the owner is always feeling the need to introduce himself to his customers and to bother them. My friends and I certainly couldn't enjoy our stay here.
Classy place without insane prices. Had their prime rib sandwich. Man, was that tender and tasty. Also had their shrimp cocktail. Wasabi.... Prepare to have your world rocked!

I love trying new drinks and the Underground is definitely a great place to try new beers.  There are 72 beers on tap and featured on their own menu.  All of the beers are sorted by score with a pretty decent description of what you're about to order.  That's one thing I definitely appreciate, as I love trying new beers but don't want to order a pint completely blind, I'd rather know if it's hoppy or not, a porter, etc. As for their food, I've never had an issue with their burgers or mains.  On this past visit there I had their pulled pork nachos ($19) and while they were good and had a great ratio of cheese to nacho, I found it was a little small for my liking - normally nachos are stacked!  The tray was a decent size but there was really only one layer of chips.  Good for sharing with one other person, but I think if we had gone in a group we would have needed more food.

Last night's service was great and our food came out reasonably fast.  The atmosphere is nice and cozy so it's great for date nights or catch up with friends.  I don't come here that often in the summer time as it's located in the basement - I'd rather hit up somewhere where I can drink while enjoying the sunshine :)

Stopped by for dessert after an afternoon of ice skating at the Blue Cross River Rink. The desserts weren't over appealing so I ordered blueberry pancakes with a side of bacon. Bacon was ok but the pancakes were just plain with cheap, canned blueberry pie filling on top. Ate the bacon and asked the waitress to take the pancakes off the bill, which she did. However after she dropped off the bill she asked about the pancakes and i said I had expected actual blueberries to be cooked IN the pancake. She repeated a sarcastic comment the cook had made about me expecting the blueberries in the pancakes, so a little rude. Two other people in our party ordered scrapple which was crispy on the outside but totally tasteless mush on the inside - awful. There were only a few tables of customers but the pancakes and scrapple took forever. To recap - Slow service, bad attitude, crappy food. If the owners were smart, they would overhaul their chefs/service. Any diner in the middle of so many hotels should be JUMPING at dinner time.

This was the worst manicure I have ever received. I am incredibly disappointed I paid money for what I could have at home, and I'm terrible at doing my own nails. My nails are not fully covered, the polish is uneven, and the ends of my nails were filed with a rough file and no fine file, leaving rough and uneven edges. Not only that, but the manicurist didn't even make each of my nails even. My left thumbnail is 2 different lengths, longer on the left side of the nail and shorter on the right side of the nail. I could maybe see there being different length nails between 2 hands or fingers, but not on the SAME nail. I'm very upset that I wasted time and money here.

Stopped in for a breakfast sandwich and was greeted by the same unhappy lady at the counter as last time. I asked for a breakfast sandwich and she forgot the mayonnaise again! How hard is it to remember for the 2 minutes it takes to make the egg? I was really looking forward to the cafe con leche but it tasted like they used water from the water hose. Overall pretty disappointing this morning.

I've eaten at The Drafting Room a couple dozen times and I can honestly say I have never had a bad meal. 

The cream of mushroom soup is literally the stuff of dreams. I've dreamt about it. The quesadillas are amazing with a really smokey flavor. I ask for the salsa on the side because it makes the tortillas soggy. 

Everything else on the menu--from the the cheeseburgers to the brisket-- is great. They also have great specials. 

I've had specials which maybe didn't hit the mark. On at least two occasions, after not completing the meal, the manager asked me if there was anything wrong. I explained that it was good, just not to my liking, and he immediately took it off the bill. The thought of asking for a refund never crossed my mind, but it was very appreciated. 

The service, food and beer list are amazing. I just wish they updated the decor a little, but if that means they have to close the restaurant for a period of time, please don't do it!
Will definitely do this again...the service was exceptional Jordan rocked it. The food was great. I recommend the dancing crab roll.

What luck!!

After a long-winded adventure looking for 2 Sisters (soul food restaurant)  we gave up and took a cab to Fauburg Marigny to catch a show later at the Snug Harbor.

Cab dropped us right in front of the Praline Connection, and we were hungry...

Here is what I gotta say up front: I HAD THE BEST SPAGHETTI & MEATBALLS EXPERIENCE  that night.

Who'da thunk to order spaghetti and meatballs, especially when you're visiting a soul food restaurant, in New Orleans. 

Somehow my heart told me to do it. And I was completely blown away, time-travelled back to my childhood days, when my mother made spaghetti meat sauce from scratch and my sisters and I would challenge each other in a spaghetti eating contest.

Suddenly I remembered how to make home-made pasta sauce again. Suddenly I remembered how good it was. I vowed never to buy bottled pasta sauce ever again.

The cornbread was delicious. The Zaire gumbo was delicious. Boyfriend had the stewed chicken, that was also delicious. But my spaghetti meatballs, they were magical!!

The pizza is always good. We loved almost everything about this location. The parking was a bit insane. Good food, beer and atmosphere. The hostess was a bit rude. Aside from that another win for FPP.

I never really cared for wings but then one day I had a great basket full one day and they were delicious. Sadly that was in Florida. Now I'm all about finding some good wings with delicious sauce. 
  
 The wing stop is not too bad, staff very very friendly. The wings were hot, fresh and crisp in all the right places.  the hot sauce was very plain, seemed outta the bottle, no butter or other spices added. It was ok though, the wings were good on there own. It's not like a sit down restaurant, you order at the counter. That's ok with me, it does save on the tip. Oh and the workers are fully dressed. ( I've noticed some wing places the girls wear really short shorts!)

it wasn't busy at all & yet it took forever to get our smokehouse burgers.. 1 was ordered with out onions & sure enough there they were.. waitress tried to say they were part of the sauce..NOT!!  also 1/3lb burger was paper thin & cooked to a crisp.. after cooking a 2nd burger without onions it was del to the table without the fries that had been ordered & del w 1st burger.. after a couple of bites each we had to get the ck & leave.. it was horrible.. never going there again.. 
   similar experience at  diff location yrs ago but figured it had gotten better with time.. I was wrong..

Love LOVE love this place. We've been here several time and could never go wrong. They always busy but its all worth it. Their rolled ice cream very different compare to other locations I've been too. Their toppings is perfect for your craving and unlimited too. The best thing we love to go is right across where there is a beach that you can enjoy your ice cream roll with a beautiful scenery.
We had an amazing sea bass and steak dinner with maybe the best service we have ever experienced.  Thank you!!  We'll be back and will recommend Earl's to other. Chuck and Regina

For the price you really can't ask too much more of Thailand Restaurant. My family went there and had the green curry chicken and shrimp, the chicken pad thai, and some meal that was just spicy enough to give me serious concerns about what havoc it might wreak on me come 12-24 hours from its consumption. It involved chicken. 

The owner came out during our meal and hugged my dad. At first I thought this was aggressively friendly service, but then I realized my father had been coming here to satisfy his every craving for Thai food for my entire life!

That fun fact aside, I found nothing to complain about with Thailand Restaurant's cuisine. They've been pouring peanut gravel down customers' throats for a long time, and their durability is a testament to the quality of the meal I ate. Sure, I never rolled my eyes back and thought I was back in Bangkok, but the entire meal cost something like $30.

***

REVISION STICKS.
SCREW THIS PLACE.

Stayed here while on a school related convention. Employees were nice. Breakfast was good. Rooms were nice and clean...though the beds were a little small. The pool was tiny but I'm not a fan of swimming while out of town anyway. 

free wi-fi is always a plus of course :) and the guest computer in the lobby was accessible to my needs to check school email when rolling up from the french quarter at 3am. :)

My fiancé and I have been taking our cars here for a couple years. We always receive professional, courteous, and efficient service and never feel like we're getting overcharged. I highly recommend the Mavis in Abington!

This latest visit to Brio was the opposite of my last visit. Last time I liked my food and the service was bad. This time my food was ok and the service was better. I had the Pasta Brio and I was surprised to find the noodles a bit mushy and not al dente. For bearing the restaurant's name, I thought this would be a better pasta dish. It was very one note and just didn't really do anything for me. 

The service this time was decent. We sat in the bar area as opposed to the dining room last time. The bar was faster. We had to remind the server of a couple things but she had a lot going on.

I'm a soon to be ex-Tulane student and during the last few years I've been trying to explore the New Orleans food culture to its fullest, by trying everything I could in my brief time. But most importantly, I wanted to find "my" restaurant, the one that I'll go back to many, many times, the one that never gets old. My search isn't over but Lüke nearly took that title.

I'll be straightforward, this was one of my favorite dining experiences in New Orleans so far, if not the best I've had during my time here. Maybe I was having a good day or something great occurred recently, but this meal hit home.

I went to Lüke my first time on a weekday night around 10, grabbed a seat at the bar, and began to look over the menu for a good 20 minutes, having a great deal of trouble deciding what I want to get. The mix between German, French, and American cuisine was almost overwhelming. 

After much deliberation, I almost went with the Canard Roti, but this night, when the classic rock kicked on the speakers, I decided on the Lüke burger (I don't know why the music matters but it did at the time). Once the burger arrived (very quickly), I did not realize what I was about to eat. This might have been the best burger I ever had. An over reaction? Maybe. But really, It was so damn good. I finished it in a few minutes hardly noticing a couple staring at me from 2 seats over, commenting on my "Man vs. Food 'blank stare'". Primal eating at its best. 

To wash it all down I enjoyed Lüke's own beer "Lüke Alt", which went perfectly with the burger. The French fries were great, the perfect amount, fresh and crispy.   

In short, I highly recommend this place to anyone who wants a great environment, great service, and delicious food. It could be a perfect spot for a casual date or for a night out to get some great food while downtown.

We stayed here this past weekend for a Philly-Cape May weekend with our 3 daughters and Japanese exchange student.  

The 2 bedroom, 2 bathrooms, living room, full size kitchen, 3 TV's, etc... and the DELICIOUS hot breakfast buffet in their roomy and spacious dining room made our overnight stay PERFECT!!  Would definitely recommend this location and would stay again if passing through!

We have always dined at the Media location, but we aren't a fan of the remodel, so we decided to try this location. When we arrived on a Sunday evening for dinner, the restaurant was empty. We didn't mind since that usually means excellent service. While the service wasn't horrible, it was lacking, especially considering the fact that we were the only table to wait on.

For our meal we had paneer tikka masala and lamb masala with sweet naan. The naan was amazing as always. Perfectly sweet and fluffy. The dishes were all well received. They did a decent job catering to our  level 5 spice, although it wasn't extremely spicy.

We also got honey balls and Indian ice cream for dessert. Both were very good.

I think I would return to this location and hope for better service. The good was delicious and the atmosphere was more cozy than the Media location. Even better was the coupon for checking in on Yelp!

I'm a fan.  I have sensitive skin and therefore am very picky about what I'm willing to put on my face.  I wish they carried Dermalogica, but more often than not I can get what I need at Sephora.  (I love one stop shopping) The staff generally has been friendly and helpful, but as with any retail situation, this can be spotty at times.  Sign up for their Insider card - after you accrue 100 points ($1 = 1point) you get free samples. My favorite freebies are lip gloss and mascara, but they usually have a few options so you can choose what you like.  The prices can be steep, but not much more so than anywhere else, and the free stuff makes me feel like I'm getting a deal.

Being part Jamaican, I grew up on spicy food.  Not in a BW3's, Man vs. Food, drink some pepper spray type of way, but actually incorporating hot peppers as an ingredient to enhance the flavor of the dish so that you feel something other than heat is missing when you don't add it.  Han Dynasty does this very, very well.  The food is flavroful and not just hot for the sake of being hot.  I wish they had brown rice, but this restaurant will definitely be in my regular rotation.

This is one of the best delis in St Louis, maybe even the entire midwest. The food portions (the amount of meat, cheese, toppings, etc) are huge. You definitely get your moneys worth. I have never been disappointed. They have live music on Thursdays and Saturdays. Its a great crowd. The staff is quick and polite. Vince is the owner and one of the sweetest men you will ever meet. But back to the food, the sandwiches are huge. I can barely finish it but I often do because it is just sooo good. I love the Benton Park and the Turkey Supreme. But my favorite is the Spicey Mike. The line can be long at times but its not a long wait at all. I would highly recommend this place. You wont regret it.

This is a beautiful space for hosting private events. There is a large room that is perfect for a cocktail hour before dinner. The dining room is large with giant beautiful windows that look over the water. The food was delicious. The bathrooms were spacious and clean. I highly recommend this place for private events.

The bar was pretty crowded for a Wednesday night, I'd venture to say even decently packed. The bar is long enough that there is plenty of room, enough room even for there to be three stools open for us to sit together. There are also a good amount of large booths against the wall as well as several high tops in the front and back. Plenty of seating. There is also a patio in the back if you feel like being outside, or like me, feel like smoking.

The bartender, Cliff, was very nice and welcoming, making you feel like this is a bar you had been coming to for years. I was drinking Bud Lights all night, but also sampled my friend's White Russian, which was very good.

Now let's get to the important part: the food. We all ordered food, and I was excited for my taste buds because this place boasts some of the best burgers in Nashville, all made with natural local beef. I ordered the Blue Cheese Burger (bacon, blue cheese crumbles, grilled onions) and waffle fries.

Food came out pretty quick, but let me tell you....it was worth it no matter how long we waited for it. It was truly the most amazing burger I have ever had in my life. The blue cheese crumbles were perfectly melted on the burger, it was juicy, the bacon was crisp...it was literally heaven on a bun. I'm not a huge fan of fries but the waffle fries were pretty run of the mill, made amazing by me drenching them in Tabasco sauce and then dipping them in the spinach dip that Chris had ordered, which was TO DIE FOR.

I went the following night, on a Thursday, when they have 2-4-1's starting at 4PM. Other notable specials are Happy Hours Mon-Fri 4PM-7PM ($1 off apps, liquor, wine and beer), $2 domestic drafts on Saturdays, and $2 drafts all day on Sunday. They also have trivia on Tuesday where you can win up to $50.

They have a brunch menu on the website, which looks AMAZING. Brunch is served Saturday & Sunday 10AM - 3PM and I'm really considering flying in next Friday evening to sample what must be a delicious treat in the AM.

I give Melrose a hearty 4 1/2 stars. One of my favorite bars that I've been to in Nashville. So if you're ever in town, I'd definitely suggest stopping by here, if not for the friendly staff and great atmosphere, then for the burgers. Holy crap.
Such a great spot to stop on our way to Ventura! Service and food was amazing and they are super pet friendly, upon arrival they brought a little treat over for our dog! We will defiantly return!
I always get the best service and home cooking - in Tampa this is THE SPOT for down home yummy-ness. Hands down!

Horrible food!! I ordered nachos with beef. The cheese was not real , it was the kind in a can that 711 stores put on their nachos, chips were cheap too, i threw it out , meat tastes funny. 
I paid $10 and what a waste of money, I will never ever go back to that place again.

When in doubt and you need a place to eat at on 21st Ave, just pick Jacksons.  Seriously, you won't regret it.  

First off, it wins with a huge patio.  This is ground zero for people watching on 21st.  You can watch all the people buzzing about, getting to work, shopping, etc.  There are big tables and smaller tables so all types of parties can be accommodated outside.  

The second win is the menu.  Pretty much everything in this place is unique and tastes pretty darn good.  I love the Verde dip as an appetizer.  It is great for a big group of people, but some of my favorite dishes are the Panni Sandwiches.  You can really never go wrong with a Cuban with loads of pork and crisp pickles.  So good!  They also do a brunch too, so anyplace that believes in breakfast on the weekend completely scores.

The beer, wine and mixed drinks list is amazing.  Jacksons is committed to some serious high gravity beers like BBC Bourbon Stout, Victory Garden Monkey and Abbey.  They do have the good old standards like Yazoo and Jackaloupe on tap too.  The wine list is big and they do feature a wine of the moment for only $6 a glass.  This changes alot.  Jacksons is pretty innovative with drinks.  My favorites is the Misery and Gin:  Gin, Pear Cider, and Ginger is pretty different, but oh so good.

Went here last Sunday for happy hour with some friends. They offer a selection of small appetizers for a good deal ranging from $1 pita and hummus to $4 for mussels (2 per order). I ordered the white peach sangria for $4 and thought it was delicious! The only down side was our server who was a bit slow with bringing out our order. It also took more than 15 min to get an extra side of pita bread. 

I love the eclectic and artsy atmosphere and will certainly be back.

Decent food, nice outdoor courtyard seating, live music was playing I'm not sure if it's every night but they did last Friday nite. The alcoholic drinks aren't all that bartender could do better. Unsure of the dress code most people we were dressy.

Delicious food! The hummus with pita is fantastic, we had the rack of lamb and the chicken skewers and both were cooked fantastically. If anything would like for the restaurant to have an online reservation system but would 100% recommend you check it out.

If I could rank this place with six stars, I would.  I had the Shrimp and Cochin au lait sandwich.  My wife had the Cajun Cuban.  Great sandwiches.  This is a very busy place, so don't be surprised if you have to wait.  Well worth it though.

I have always loved Chipotle, and have never had a problem at any of the locations. However, now I am apprehensive about going back. I stopped in the Evesham Township, NJ location last night to pick up dinner. I ordered a bowl with chicken. When I got home and proceeded to eat my dinner I was greatly disappointed. The rice was terrible! Most of it was hard and crunchy. I ended up throwing out the bowl and cooking something else for dinner.

I have been coming to TZ for almost three years! It continues to add a variety of classes and constantly adapts to challenge even the regulars. There are classes as early as 5am to fit anybody's schedule. I have taken classes at multiple gyms and this one has provided the best experience. There are classes that cater to everybody's fitness level and the instructors are approachable. The owners Scott and Leslie are always quick to respond to questions and concern via email. My favorite classes are boot camp and afterburn. If you are a fitness enthusiast, TZ is more than worth the money.

I've been wanting to try Apollo's for quite sometime. We've been in the area about 8 years and I always seem to forget about it. We stopped by this past Thursday for lunch.

We arrived around noon and it was dead! Just us and the waitress. The place is small and it's dated but in a good way. The server had been there since they started in the 70s. For a pizza place to survive that long and in the same family, they must be doing something right.

I went with a cheesesteak hoagie and the wife had their 10" pizza. They are supposedly known for their cheesesteaks and they advertise 1/2 pounders. I must say that i was pleasantly surprised, it was very good. The steak was juicy and the roll was extremely fresh. There was an ample amount of meat and the sandwich was seasoned as it should be. Next time I would get the roll toasted. The pizza was also good but different. I love the cheese to sauce ratio, I always prefer more cheese than sauce. The cheese blend is unique and adds a nice flavor, I think it's provolone and mozzarella. The crust was nice and crispy but a little thick for our liking. Overall it was a good reasonable lunch and we would return. Solid 4 stars.

Best place in STL to hang out, eat, and drink. There is always something unusal going on. The menu is awesome. Only place I know to get a sardine sandwich. And the beer is great although it does seem to have lost a bit in the last couple of years. Still, no place Id rather be!

Bennie (I think her name is Sarah) waited on us. WHAT A BALLER! she was so enthusiastic, she was attentive to every need we had and did so with a smile! Will definitely be back because of her! Five stars!

Got some lunch here. They have a menu that they don't put online. You get to pick three items and it's $20. I got the shrimp appetizer, romaine hearts salad and prime rib sandwich. It was all really good and a great value for $20. Not that fast of service but not too bad. I have been looking forward to this shrimp cocktail for years. I saw it on 'best thing I ever ate' and have heard about it elsewhere as well. It was so spicy! (Is that the word for that taste?) I mean I really like horseradish but whoa. I scraped it off each shrimp as much as I could to not feel terrible for a minute after each bite. I'm glad I tried it but I wouldn't get it again. The salad was great. Every aspect done wonderfully and good proportions and melding of flavors. The prime rib sandwich also came with a cup of chili that was very good.  The prime rib was unbelievable. It came with a dipping sauce but was better on it's own. A good deal for lunch at Harry and Izzy's.

Beautiful strip of oasis from the city.  Great for kids, especially those riding bikes, but a little spot with playground equipment would be nice.  (No need for anything fancy; just to create a little center where kids can naturally meet other kids.)  The lack of bathrooms is a serious downside, though.

Outstanding. This is the place to indulge in BBQ of all styles accompanied by a solid drink menu. The ribs are thick and juicy. The pulled pork is tender and flavorful. The baked Mac and cheese is delectable. The sweet potato fries are crunchy and not overloaded with salt. You have a choice of different BBQ sauces from states such as Kansas City and the Carolinas. Whether it is brunch, lunch, or dinner I highly recommend this place. In my book, it's a "do not miss". OH, and do not forget about the bacon greased popcorn, the ultimate drinking snack.

Okay, I have no idea what some of these people are talking about. They're probably just grumpy people in general. Oh well. This place is pretty delicious. I'm not kidding. Now, I haven't ordered every meal ever, obviously, but I've had a few different ones and a few of the same ones twice in a row. They have these potatoes that come with almost every plate I've had, I think. Wow! They're really really great. They're nothing special, no cheese, just seasoning, but they're great! I promise. My girlfriend is a vegetarian and the first time we went, she ordered some sort of veggie eggs benedict and I ordered some TexMex styled dish. We both had those potatoes I told you about, and my food was really good. But then I made the mistake of trying hers. Wow!!! That eggs benedict is the best best best most delicious plate I've had there. I'm not sure exactly what it's called but it's a vegetarian dish. Trust me. It's a great place. Sometimes the wait is 5-10 minutes on a Sunday morning or something. (My girlfriend didn't let me have any more after I tried hers. I had to order it for myself the next time we went.)
Fresh excellent food.  Shrimp cooked to perfection.   Vegetables fresh and crunchy.  Great Chinese food.  Extensive menu.

Just sat here for 9 minutes and watched 4 staff members stand around and no one came to my table. There were 4 others tables in restaurant and I guess 2 tables a person was too much to ask for. Was really hoping to eat great Italian tonight. Disappointed.

My wife and I were on vacation in Nashville and we love historical spots. Civil War battleground. Check!

So this was where the Battle of Franklin was fought 

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Franklin_(1864)

The Confederates screwed up and let 20,000 Union troops slip past them while they were asleep.  

The Union said to the Carter House home owner, "This is our headquarters now"

They dug in and the South attacked. The south had 7,500 casualties and the north had 2,500.

The house is still standing with its 1,500 bullet holes still in it.

Great tour and very interesting to hear the history. One of the Carter boys were actually killed during the battle at his own house.

Ok so let me just say that everything about Brick & Mortar is FABULOUS!! The atmosphere, service, food, and drink are AMAZING!! I HIGHLY recommend the grilled octopus, as well as the prosciutto and goat cheese flat bread with the fig spread... Total sweet and savory HEAVEN!! For a main course the The Fat Noodles and also the Short Ribs and and Fat Noodles are insane!! This restaurant is definitely a gastronomic event! LOVE IT!!

There are no bathtubs in any rooms except the executive suites, only narrow showers.  The food is expensive. Two eggs, two slices of toast, one cup of hash - $17.  Servers are way too patronizing.  Unless you have to stay here for a conference, like me, stay away. And this is only my first day. Had to call maintenance to repair a leaky toilet and to try and avert the smell of sewer gas in the bathroom. I will let you know if they corrected it.
Well, the operator lied to me. There are rooms with bathtubs. not sure which is worse, the lie, or a narrow shower!  In any case, my bathroom still stinks and the toilet still leaks. Maybe they will fix it after I leave.
Too bad they don't have "no stars" as a rating.  Understand that my comments are all related to the high price I am paying for the room. My expectations are as high as $200 or so.

Have tried Cheddars three times.  First time I ordered (over)baked potato (so overbaked, the peel was actually crusty and the potato inedible) and overcooked vegetables.  Second time I ordered fish tacos. The fish was so over-seasoned and salty I had to send it back. So I got and ate my lunch after everyone else had finished theirs. The third time, my companion had shepard's pie which was so salty she sent it back and refused to order anything else. My Philly cheesesteak sandwich (they brought out a club sandwich to begin with, which was wrong) was over-salted and was nothing more than some overly seasoned beef with a couple of cheese slices on top.  The kids' meals were very salty as well.  I had to clear our salad plates before the main meals came out because the waiter said he would be back for the plates, then disappeared.  There is no chef in the kitchen and all their food comes from a central warehouse. When it's prepared in the kitchen, they just add a lot of salt to it, evidently. This is just another underwhelming franchise type "restaurant" (and I use the word loosely) that serves bad food with lousy service.  Their gimmick is fatty frozen croissants that seem unlikely to have come into contact with any real butter.  You can taste the freaking margarine in the croissant.  I'm NOT planning to try again.

The food was good...the service was not.  Wouldn't come back based on this experience.
Food - shrimp and grits was recommended....my friend who had it said it was great.  Spinach salads...one with chicken and one with shrimp...did not disappoint.  I did send back my iced tea because it tasted old.
Service- sat down and immediately had bread and water....and then waited...and waited.  Server was hot and cold with her attitude.  She was not happy and pretty short with us about separating our checks.  We asked her about it when she brought the bill, and she said we should have asked her...but she never gave us a heads up about bringing the bill.   Also, at one point the manager was seating a table next to us.  Without asking or acknowledging us he whipped our empty chair away from the table and took it for the table he was seating.   One of my companions had an Injured leg and was resting her foot on the chair...she had JUST removed her foot from the chair.
Because of the service my friends were not interested in going back.

I love Socrates' Revenge! I am become a huge fan of pizzas without red sauce and Dewey's has awesome ones! I also love the salads. I have tried three different ones and each was great! We also tried Ryan's Inferno which was an awesome buffalo chicken pizza as well!

Walking distance from the KOA where we were staying. The breakfast was so delicious and the service was top notch. We ordered the biscuits and gravy and some breakfast croissant sandwiches. 

We had our dog so they let us eat on their grassy patch outside and brought our meal to us. So friendly. Would definitely recommend

Nice brunch spot. I was visiting from out of town so my friend suggested we went there. I was a little skeptical about them not having bottomless mimosas but I was wrong. They had a Bloody Mary bar and we paid $25 for a bottle and then got bottomless supply of juice which was perfect. Make it as strong as you want. Ha! The food was good too. I got an omelette, it was tasty. Will definitely go back if I visit again.
I came in with pretty high expectations about there pizza.   I do have to say that I'm pretty disappointed with it. The atmosphere was Great. Since, being from the Chicago area. My search continues..

favorite meal during my visit in philly. amazing old fashioned, food was super flavorful, staff was incredibly courteous. we came in around midnight and ordered a lot of food, I made a point to ask if the bar closed at 1 or if the kitchen closed at 1, and that brings me to Beth. 

Our waitress, Beth, was so accommodating and sweet. We wanted to hang out with her. She was so attentive but not in an obnoxious way, made sure we were taken care of completely. When I asked if the bar or kitchen closed at 1 she said "the kitchen, but I'll keep the bar open all night if you want!" 

Food was great. We got deviled eggs, beer hall pretzel, whipped brie toast, buffalo wings, and eggplant fries. All super flavorful. They were out of the draught of old fashions but Beth whipped me up something similar and delicious. 

The atmosphere was pretty, the lights and the fixtures were well thought out. Will be back next time I'm in town!

Went here for lunch in NOLA. It was quite good! The b-b-q shrimp were tasty (a little zippy for my taste, but my husband loved them). The gumbo rocked. The desserts were incredible (especially the molten lave cupcake). A strange atmosphere, it's hard to decide if it is casual or formal. Plus the waiters almost outnumbering the guests, but it made for good service! We would definitely go here again. Not the easiest place to park, though...

Our group of five stopped in for dinner before a local meeting.  We were seated immediately, and the restaurant was not very busy.  Our orders were taken promptly, and our food was delivered fairly quickly.  The food was quite good, and nobody had any complaints about their order.  The waitress was young, but seemed to know what she was doing.  The prices for the meals were very reasonable, and we left happy.  The only issue we encountered was during the paying of the bill.  If you want to split out individual meals, make sure you say so before they produce the final ticket.  They don't have an easy ability to do so after the fact.  We will definitely be back.

There are some places that just catch your attention.  Some places that you walk out saying,  I've got to come back.  I didn't have that feeling here. 

Two chicks is a nice little cafe offering a little more than standard fare. 

$7 for a breakfast sandwich without side, not even fruit, is steep. 

I got the barnyard.  Which seemed a bit too simple for my liking but they had me at herb cream cheese so I went with it, indeed it's simple.  The turkey is super thick sliced like country ham.  Wasnt expecting that and honestly could have been better had it been normal deli sliced.  I added tomato and it was a good addition.  It's just too plain.  It needs Arugula or something to perk it up.  Thick sliced turkey with a fried egg slapped on some bread is reminiscent of "what's in my fridge that I can make this morning because I'm too lazy to go to the store". Sounds harsh I know. .. I'm sorry,  well not really.  Honest feedback.  

I would not hesitate to come here if you're in the area but don't go out of your way to try this new establishment.  

I may have to return with a greater appetite for some shrimp and grits. 

The staff are sweet and service was quick even during a relatively busy time.  

I like the layout and appreciate the bar seating for single people like myself.

I left paying $14 and some change + tip, for a breakfast sandwich and a mimosa. I feel like I can get more bang for my buck elsewhere in this city.

Smiths is a cool hang out with a great selection of beer and a great atmosphere to chat with friends. The waitstaff is lovely. However, the food that we had was mediocre at best, which was disappointing because the food choices looked extremely appetizing. 

We had two orders of two different types of wings. We had the classic and an asian variety, both of which were undercooked and neither of which were particularly good. Then we had the cheesesteak spring rolls, which were okay. Lastly, we had the BBQ chicken flatbread. While it wasn't terrible, it could have been better. It was a lot larger than we had anticipated. 

We ended up staying all night drinking. As I said, it is a really cool and unique bar scene and if you are just looking to get cocktails, Smiths is a good spot.

I went to Pub and Kitchen a while ago, right after it opened, and I was so not impressed. The place was pretty dead, yet the bartender was still not attentive, and we had to tell him how to make a greyhound, which is a pretty classic cocktail as far as I am concerned. I did however enjoy the whitefish salad snacks at the bar. Anyway, recently I had been hearing a lot of positive things about the place, so I gave it another chance. 
I went for dinner on a Friday night, and there was a half-hour wait for a table, which really isn't bad. My friends and I got cherry bourbon cocktails from the bar, and they were very delicious. When it was time to be seated, it turned out that we had to close that tab before going to our table, which was time consuming and a little annoying.  When we looked at the menu, we were all starving and everything looked really appealing, especially all the vegetables on the side-dish menu. I ordered the English onion soup  (the menu didn't describe it but I asked and was told it is made with pork instead of beef, then topped with English cheddar instead of gruyere), and a side of braised carrots. One friend has gnocchi with squash and brussel sprouts with spinach with cranberries and walnuts, and the other had a cheese plate with mustard green beans. Everything was so good and terribly satisfying. Halfway through dinner I switched from bourbon to the Pub and Kitchen Anniversary Ale, and found that to be yummy as well. In addition to good food, nearly everyone in the place that night was really hot, and they were playing a great mix of music, including two of my favorites, Hot Chip and Phoenix. I really talked a lot of trash about how bad this place was when I went the first time and now I feel like I owe them an apology.

Terrific values, quality, innovative merchandise, and a fun shopping atmosphere.

We used to pay $11-15/lb for coffee, but Trader Joe's coffees now fill the bill half that or less.  The frozen entree items have been reliably good.   The Hearth Oven Seeded Multi-Grain breads and wide variety of other baked goods, Valrhona chocolate bars (a dollar cheaper here than there!), Sunflower Nut Butter, Joe's O's, and Chile-Lime Pistachio nuts are among our favorites.   

You won't find everything at a Trader Joe's but you won't shop anywhere else for what you do go to a TJ's for.   We have found a good variety of Organic, Natural, Sustainable food, health, cleaning & pet products.     We used to buy primarily at Whole Foods, but Trader Joe's is so much less that we have scaled back Whole Foods without suffering loss of quality.  

The produce is not a broad variety, so don't plan on getting it all here.  Also, this store cannot offer beer or wine, courtesy of the commonwealth of Pennsylvania, and it can get crowded, predictably on weekends and around any holiday, but the atmosphere is always fun, so don't let that stop you from going.

Can't say that I didn't have a good experience at this particular Cheddar's. I was in town for the 4th of July so that night around 10 p.m. we were looking for somewhere to dine and this restaurant was the only one open. I like that Cheddar's has good food, good portions and is reasonably priced. As long as they stay this way, they will always have my business.

At the suggestion of a friend, I tried Hollywood last year and have been coming for sunday brunch at least twice a month.  I usually get an egg white omelet with spinach, cheese and mushrooms. The veggies are fresh from Kennett, so it's a huge plus from traditional diners that use canned or frozen veggies.

My son has been bragging about this restaurant since visiting last summer during a band camp.  The first time I visited I ordered a macaroni and cheese with bacon slice and a veggie one with artichokes while my son ordered pepperoni.  On Wednesday, I ordered one with fresh mozzarella and tomatoes.  One slice is enough since they're so large.  At our last visit, we shared a brownie.  Each time we've sat in large bench seating. It's comfortable though it can be a bit loud.  Delicious pizza; will definitely visit, again.

Wow what a disappointing trip here.the restaurants are closed.there ls no band tonight when I made my resavation that said how entertaining this place is.it is dead nothing here,I wanted a refund greg the front desk manager was a rude person never stay here.

This was our first visit and won't be our last! We ordered an appetizer of queso with andouille sausage and it was good. I would've liked more cheese than the sausage, but I think that it was a personal preference. The chips were crisp and not stale and the salsa had the right amount of heat. I ordered the burrito Mexicana and it was delicious. It came with lettuce, sour cream and tomatoes and it was just the right portion. It was topped with a red sauce that mixed well with the sour cream. The menu was expansive. They especially offered many combinations, which is what my husband chose. He ordered a taco, enchilada, rice, and beans. He also finished everything. He got 2 margaritas and said that they tasted very good. 
The service was also good. We were seated and then greeted immediately, and he checked up on us frequently. 
I found the prices to be just a tad bit higher than other places, but didn't balk since the experience was a good one.

Woohooo we found this awesome park after multiple visits to NOLA.  We went unprepared to walk much though so will have to come back when we are better prepared.  Beautiful setting and no homeless like so many other places in Nola.  Right along the mighty Mississippi and beautifully landscaped.  My legs got an amazing working on the bridge crossover!

What a gem!  Great wines relaxed atmosphere. Very helpful staff.  Absolutely fresh delicious food. We had the dates! Pea hummus and risotto!  All delicious. We will go back. The doorman was sweet and talented

Cool bar.  Solid pizza.

Really?  Chicago-style?  I'd like to think this as Pizza Hut pan pizza on steroids, with loads of extra cheese and toppings.

Either way it's pretty delicious, but it's not something to trek down for.  It's definitely a cool spot to hang out after kickball or flag football and Tower Grove Park, though.

This place is right off the main tourist drag in Nashville. You know that whole area no one who lives in or near Nashville actually goes to unless there's an event? Yep. Swarms of people, overpriced food and drinks, loud music from wannabe country stars doing 90s cover songs. We were going to a concert at Bridgestone and wanted grub first but not bar food when we found this place which serves breakfast and sandwiches all day.
I'm a sucker for good chicken and waffles so I ordered that. Sun's version is unique in that they cover it all in sausage gravy which I've never seen done. The chicken was good, the waffle was delicious, and the gravy was pretty good. However I think the chicken and waffles would've been better with the gravy separate, maybe with a biscuit. It wasn't bad by any means, just that it kind of takes away from the chicken -waffle combo to overpower it with sausage gravy. My wife had chicken and fries and the fries were great- almost unsalted but very crisp and I'd much rather have to add salt then have something served too salty.
Other menu items like the patty melt and some of the desserts looks good but it is a relatively small menu. A few beers in bottles if you need a drink and off the main drag where bars litter the landscape it's a pretty safe bet that all day breakfast is a good racket to be in.
'50s music and a plethora of Sun record memorabilia are in abundance. Kind of a surprising theme for a place with prime Nashville real estate since sun records is a Memphis rather than a Nashville thing.
All in all great service, pretty good food, and a bit pricey for what it is but not devastatingly so.

Cheryl was absolutely fantastic in helping us with our Wedding cake... we had a destination wedding to New Orleans May 11th and it was a very small intimate wedding. Our cake was 2 tier almond cake with vanilla buttercream... Oh my word it was beautiful with the ruffle piping and it was the most delicious thing I had ever tasted. If I had to do it again the only thing I would do different is order a bigger cake so we could have had more to take home!

Third Friday's are just great. Music, food & drink making our Birthday gathering of 20 family and friends perfect. It's always eye candy with glass blowing& the glass on display.
Someone actually bumped a display and CRASH!

This is a double restaurant. During the day it seems to be a brunch place and in the evening they are brazillian steak house (a la fogo de chao but cheaper). I ordered the chilaquiles for breakfast and they were really good. They came with pancakes or toast (i got the pancakes because pancakes are awesome). The decor is rustic with wood everywhere. Our server was on top of things and made sure our needs were being met. I would definitely go back.

The food here is pretty good, but far from great. The highlight was the empanadas. They were very tasty. 

The puerco asado was decent, but dry. Parts of it seemed overcooked. The black beans that accompanied it were very tasty and combined with the pork added some much needed moistness. 

Overall, a good experience. Our server was very gracious and fairly attentive. There was one question about a menu item that took a couple of minutes to get an answer to, but she was knowledgeable about most of it.

How hard is it to pour liquid into a cup to the proper height of the cup. I took the lid off and the coffee instantly starting pouring out. Not little drops, but POURING out obviously overfilled and spilling in my truck, on my clothes. You don't want to leave room for cream and sugar, that's fine, DONT FILL IT TO THE RIM THINKING Nothing can happen. Last I check there's still gravity and pressure on earth so movement and grasping the cup will change the dynamics of the damn contents inside the cup people!

This is a must try!  It is a hidden gem.  The staff is friendly and the food is awesome.  Don't let the location intimidate you, the spot is too busy with customers to worry.  The fuss of the place goes into the food and not the decor.  I highly recommend giving it a try.  Do carry out if you dont want to stay and eat there.

Phenomenal! In every aspect, service, food, decor.

While visiting New Orleans on business I found Iris on Yelp and gave it a shot...boy am I SO happy I did.  

We started with the potato gnocchi...out of this world! If it was a full order, I would have ordered one to go! It was hands down the best Gnocchi I've ever had! Cooked perfectly, with an amazing garlicky Parmesan sauce with wilted kale...superb!

For the main course we ordered the beef short rib and chicken breast.  Both were awesome! 

Everything on the dessert sounded delish! I (sadly) gave up chocolate for lent so we decided on the Lemon bar pudding...excellent! 

The service was wonderful and the decor was so charming. 

If i'm ever back in New Orleans, this is a MUST!
Great steakhouse thats affordable. Service is always friendly and quick. There is really no way to be disappointed other than if you're a vegetarian.
Celebrated by daughter's 21st birthday here.  The pasta dishes were absolutely delish.  Prices are reasonable and it is bring your own bottle.

I try not to go to too many chains.. But I will literally be searching for this place everywhere I go now. I went for the baba ghanoush bowl, chicken Schwarma, and literally every topping they offered.. Plus the two hottest sauces of course. Everything went together so well. The sumac onions especially were crunchy (hopefully not poisonous), and flavorful. And all the slaws made me mucho happy. It's literally a Middle Eastern Chipotle, and I cannot wait to find the rest of them.

After a long day at work I called and made an appointment for that same night. By the description and price I was expecting a longer version of a pedicure massage but man was I wrong! It was practically a full body massage and everyone was so nice and inviting!!! I will keep going back!! Do yourself a favor and try them out asap!!

Pleasant way for me to spend time in the morning if I have room to kill before getting into work. A small coffee is $2.16 including tax and is strong and hot.

I like the set up with an ample area for people to customize their drinks with whatever milk preference they have.  Strong wifi - password info is located in the area with the straws and milk.

Plenty of tables for people to sit and relax. I love that they keep a dog bowl on the steps outside for our furry friends.

The Beauty Parlous is gorgeous! The decor alone is worth a visit, but their services will keep you there. I went for my first visit this week and will be back for sure. I've been meaning to go see Celine for ages, she does many of my friends hair and they all rave about her. I went in for a  trim and blowout and left feeling amazing! She suggested some great products that I can use at home. I'm pretty picky about product and LOVE that they carry Kevin Murphy which is cruelty free, awesome and the stuff I got (Hair Resort Spray) smells delicious!! The overall vibe of the salon is laid back and welcoming. The other clients in we're getting fun cuts and colours, which all looked awesome. It's clear the stylists here take pride in their work and it may inspire me to do something a bit more adventurous next time! Thanks Beauty Parlour Crew!

Although this location is small and could use to be expanded, I love it here. The staff is friendly and the store is always clean and organized. This is the closest TJ to me and I always make a point to stop here when I can. My only wish is that they would be able to carry alcohol!

I purchased a 2016 Nissan from Enterprise in August 2017.. About 4 months later I learned my windshield was not sealed. The manager gave me a hard time, but after the repair shop I took my car to told the manager to dig deeper, my windshield was fixed. 
On May 30, 2018, I was heading home on the interstate and the car just stopped running. I quick put my hazard lights on and got out of the car. It was 8 minutes after I got out that a driver smashed it. Why did that car just stopped running, I'll never know because it was totaled. 
Buyer beware! If purchasing from Enterprise, please do something I didn't do and that's get it check out completely by a certified mechanic. You see, I counted on their little warranty they offer. And also, if the sales person ask you more than three times to make the purchase, walk away, because then their trying to pressure you into buying. This was a good lesson for me, yet I'm glad I got out of that car when I did. Happy to be alive!
