The girl was unpleasant didn't take my order right and the driver was high or drunk. He asked me if he gave me the correct change. And the food was thrown together. I order here often and been a customer since I was a kid. I'm highly upset with this.

I remembered going to this museum as a kid, but WOW. Now that I've gone back, I think it has GROWN is that possible?!?! If you have kids, and you are in the area, you NEED to go. 
First things' first, if you do decide to go, you need to plan well. If you go at a time in which children are off school, you need to realize that it's going to be crowded, EXTREMELY crowded. If you can, you might consider trying to go when there's not going to be a ton of visitors. Next, look at your shoes. Is there a heel? Are those the most COMFORTABLE shoes that you own? If not, find your comfy shoes, and put them on because this place is NOTHING but walking, and a LOT of it. You might think that when you get to each section, you are just going to be able to stand and rest, but your kids will be pulling you in every direction "SEE MOM AND DAD! LOOK OVER HERE! Now LOOK OVER HERE! Come see this/that!" Get those comfy shoes on (you might even consider house slippers (I won't judge!). 
Park in the parking garage across the street. It's FREE. But I recommend that you park as close to the top as possible. Everyone wants to park near the entrance, but then you have a lot more to look for when you are backing out of a parking space. 
I will admit, I purchased a membership. It really is the best deal. Going twice would have cost more for us than a membership. After you purchase your tickets, GET READY! Because the fun is about to start. Be transported to amazing places like China, underwater excursions, and Ancient Egypt. Ancient China is a must see! Let them dig and take statues apart and put them back together! Ancient Egypt is full of puzzles and games. China is REALLY cool. Get on the plane, and take the trip, after that, have a seat while kids wait on your and bring you dishes from china. You might even find that there's someone there teaching Tai Chi! 
I will say that one of the most amazing experiences I've had there was meeting Ryan White's mom. There is a section of the museum that is about some really hard/sad/awful pieces of the past. You can learn about the holocaust through the eyes of Anne Frank. You can learn about segregation through the eyes of Ruby Bridges. Learn about AIDS and the response of a community through the eyes of Ryan White. His mother happened to be there one day when we went, and I must say that I don't think that I will EVER forget that. What I love about those exhibits is that they make it so that children can understand, but you also learn some things as an adult. In the case of Ryan White, we got to ask his mother questions. 
They also change exhibits periodically. They had a DocMcStuffins exhibit, they also had a Christmas exhibit, and a circus exhibit. You can pretty much touch everything there. Children are encouraged to climb and have fun. It's one of the few places where you don't have to say "DON'T TOUCH THAT!" They also have a carousel, don't shy away because of the line either, it moves pretty quickly.
There's also a very large cafeteria that has a lot of different kinds of food. You can get pizza, sandwiches, wraps etc. The downside to the cafeteria is the seating. It's mostly these really long tables. It's kind of nice if you have a group of people, but it's kind of annoying as well because you will be sitting right next to strangers. If you are into that, you may think it's great, but trust me, you've been surrounded by noise and strangers all day. At some point, you might just want some space. The cafeteria isn't really the best place to get that. Be prepared though, it's also expensive. There are a few things that I really wish could be changed. The first is staffing placement. They have an AMAZING staff. They are all really excited, they know exactly what they are talking about. The only thing is, there are TONS of kids, and a LOT of blindspots. There's a portion of the museum that is this mirrored maze. While each section of the museum has a main way in and out, there's no one there making sure that children don't leave without an adult. I took my kids to Chuck-E-Cheese, they stamped all of our hands with the same number and would NOT let us leave without checking the stamp. That place is TINY in comparison to this place. Not only that, but there's nothing stopping them from actually LEAVING the building without an adult. Of course you really need to keep an eye on your kids, but I see people all the time who have four or more kids who are REALLY struggling to keep up because there's so much around, and they are always looking for one kid or another.  If they stationed a staff member at each entrance, II think that would take a lot of stress/worry/anxiety off of the parents. Another thing: BATHROOMS. When you first walk in, on the first floor, , there are male and female bathrooms with lots of stalls. The rest of the place though has family restrooms, and they are pretty few and far between. You know kids....they tell you they have to go to the bathroom when they are about to burst.

CUTE.

Atmosphere: (A) Like walking into a fancy, retro diner.  Loved it!  Big stone stacked walls, shag carpets, cute as heck.

Food: (A) Comfort food with an extra kick of uniqueness.  I got the brie grilled cheese and my friend got the ALT (avocado, lettuce, tomatoes), mine was delicious and hers looked delicious :)  And I got the 1 Fish 2 Fish - its a blue concoction that tastes like hawaiian punch and comes with swedish fish!

Service: (A) Not sure how all the servers are but ours was just super awesome!  Friendly, attentive, felt like a friend was serving us.

Overall: (A) I loved it, good food, fun atmosphere, and great service gives this place a super thumbs up!

Enjoyed this place. It was rather chilly but got a table on the patio next to a heat lamp. They have a open concept bar, upstairs seating, and outdoor games to play as well.

Food was ok, not great, but prices were reasonable. 

Service was excellent.

The reason that this restaurant is getting 5 stars from me is the fact that I can't stop thinking about their broiled oysters- I'm not an Oyster connoisseur, (I'm an Iowa native and lifelong midwesterner- not places known for Oysters) however, we ate oysters in every form all week in NOLA and these were my favorites. Desire's broiled oysters sit atop large-grained rock salt, and melted garlic butter- YUM. My friend and I had just discovered The Chart Room and its awesomeness, and we consummed quite a few drinks there. It wasn't until about 9:45 that we realized that we were hungry and didn't quite make the kitchen closing of ACME Oyster Bar. 

Desire to the rescue! I was definitely wary of its Bourbon Street location (because really- nice restaurants are usually a little bit more out-of-the-way) but I called ahead and told them that we were staggering down the street- we started with those delicious oysters (skip the pre-packaged butter they give you for the bread and dunk your bread right into that butter/salt mix.....)  and I had the red beans and rice and she had a cold seafood salad. Those dishes were good, and the perfect meal to avoid a morning hangover. Service was very friendly, and they were kind to let us in right before closing. This place isn't terribly fancy, but it didn't need to be, either. It serves its purpose faithfully- good food, friendly service, reasonable prices. 

And I know that this is NOLA protocol, but they even let me bring my last drink from the Chart Room in with me. That's amazing. Still not used to being able to do that.

Anyway, Broiled Oysters. Get them. Right now.

Awesome awesome wine selection. I got to sample 3 different wines. And if you mention the coupon on this here Yelp, if you spend $25 you get a free bottle of wine! So I got 5 bottles of wine for $28!!!!

Such an awesome vibe and location. Great place to chill. Unfortunately, the service is awful. The gal working at the point of sale (short bangs but long brown hair) could not have been more cold or uninviting. Wow. Horrible first impression. We took our biz elsewhere...

I've got to hand it to HatM, they really came through. My fiance set up a birthday package for me that included a table. We got there...no table. The staff, including the manager, sprung into action. They were able to get us a table pronto and also took care of us the rest of the night.

Music was great, too. I really like this place and the great service will keep me coming back. Word to the wise...arrive EARLY. A few friends wanted to get in around 11 PM and the line was down to Fox and Hound. In December. Chilly.

Absolute terrible customer service at this hotel.  I cannot comment on the rooms, as they were not able to honor my PAID in-full in advance hotel reservation.  We used Priceline to reserve a room at this hotel and upon our arrival were told they were overbooked and unable to give us a room.  They said they would relocate us directly across the street at a Marriott; however, when we went across the street, we were told we were at the wrong hotel.  I confirmed three times with the Loews Hotel employee that the hotel was directly ACROSS THE STREET.  THe hotel they actually relocated us at, and finding it after walking around downtown Philly, was actually several blocks away.  The Loews offered no sort of compensation or transportation, and just said there was nothing they could do.  I contacted their customer service twice, and have not received a response back in almost a week, not even an acknowledgement of my e-mail.  

I contacted Priceline and they were able to resolve the issue.  Thankful for them, because obviously the Loews does not care.

5 stars and more! The sushi here is so unique and fresh tasting! We had the tiger roll and spider wig roll with soy paper and I was blown away! Nice service, cool atmosphere and cute rooms for large parties to sit on the floor! I loved the service, all the women here are super sweet! Food came out really fast too! It was so good we just ordered more! Statue of Liberty roll and fujiyama roll! Can't wait!!!
The coffee is OK and it's fun to get a shot of booze in it. I'm never really excited by what I drink here, but it's enjoyable when I'm relaxing in the Quarter.
THIS PLACE IS FANTASTIC! For those unfamiliar with Indian food, eat first ask questions later. Nothing is bad here.

My boss was stoked when this placed opened back up after renovations...We've had it several times in the last few weeks.

The 30% off "re-opening" special was a really good deal.  

Park has a nice selection of Chinese and American cuisine.  The actual salad bar is really fresh.  As long as you get here before 1pm, there's quite a variety -- any time after this they start removing pans and the selection is much more scant and sparse.

Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be able to go here anymore as the last several times there have been hair in my food which honestly makes me want to puke just thinking about it.  The first time I convinced myself it was one of my own hairs...Then the next time I convinced myself it was a cat hair.  I can't do it anymore.

*vomits everywhere*

AWESOME! I love breakfast and this is where you want to have it while in Nashville TN. Thank you AG for sharing your hometown spot! The wait in line was worth it and it moved fairly quick. The line is part of the appeal...they even have a painting of the restaurant with a line of people in it to go along with the whole experience. I had the sweet potato pancakes with eggs I think - the sweet potato pancakes were so damn good and I can't remember if I had eggs - but I think I did. Loved it!

Returned recently with my momma bear for lunch, and the experience was consistent with my first one. Amazing service and even better food. We opted for the marinated olives, tuna sandwich, and truffled mushroom sandwich, and everything was delicious and filling!

The restaurant confused us as we didn't know whether to wait to be seated or sit down so we just grabbed a table. The server was new but she did her best to answer our questions. Food was pretty average, not bad but not great. We didn't expect much from a hotel restaurant but it gets the job done.

We went here for brunch and prices were 20 dollars a head.  We used our comps and got our meal for almost free.  The selection is pretty good as there is a salad bar, roast beef and ham station with sausage.  They had a place to make pho as well.  Thr breakfast was okay and the lunch portion.  Like the fried chicken too.  Overall not too bad for the price.

Ordered a family meal to go... & first let me comment on how RUDE the guy was when we called in. You would think I was placing a to go order close to closing time. I get that's annoying and reason for an attitude. But I called around 6 he proceeded to say hold on hold on let me check to see if we can complete your order... come in to pick up my order and it is COLD af! And cold BBQ is not appealing at all. Not to mention our ribs were pretty crispy. Needless to say this business will not be seeing me or my money again!! Horrendous service.
Good variety of food and excellent taste.  Really happy with the service and timeliness.  High recommendations for here.  Try it once and leave wanting to come back again.
Nice clean vehicles.  Prompt, reliable service.  Excellent customer service.  Locally operated.  Better than Uber!  No surge pricing.

Been wanting to try this place, so we decided to go for lunch. 

We both ordered the farmers salad with carne asada which was VERY well put together. The meat used was some of the best and the walnuts were my favorite. I really enjoyed it and would recommend the small because it had me full! 

The chips and salsa we very tasty and well mixed. I am very picky when it comes to salsa (yes, I know it's a very simple mixture) but, a lot of places just can't get it right. It was very tasty but has no kick to it but the flavor was still very satisfying. 

The water was served at room temperature which was kinda gross to me.

The only reason I can't give the place all stars is because we were waiting a whole HOUR for a SALAD. Two of their SMALL farmers salad's took 1 WHOLE HOUR. The tea was only refilled once and sat on empty for most of the time. Our waiter only came once to take our order and that was it. We had to ask a busser for our waiter because it was taking so long. In the end we both enjoyed the salads and were given a discount which was greatly appreciated. I wanted so much to LOVE this place because of how beautiful the decor and how much I liked my salad but I just am still in shock it took an hour for a salad. 

maybe next time Penca, hopefully next time...
Jerk swordfish was awesome.  Brisket soup was A1 2. This is a great place not to miss. They have done a superb job delivering great food!!!!

This is my first time dining at this Village Inn and it'll be my last dining at Village Inn anywhere. It seems that every single location prides itself on being dirty and having poor service. No thank you!

I've been to this place since I was a child. The first owner did an amazing job and this restaurant was famous in the Korean community - everyone who loved soon dubu knew this place was their go-to. However, owners changed somewhere along the way and the quality of the soondubu went down drastically. The flavors changed, there was less tofu, less seafood in the haemul soon dubu, and the somethin flavor was off.

Last year I gave it another try on a cold day and I was pleasantly surprised that the restaurant was really good again! They put in the right amount of spice (4 out of 5), it was a bit sparse on the seafood again, but plenty of tofu. I went a few more times after that, and the last couple visits I noticed the quality go down again.

I just went again with my [Korean] parents and was so disappointed that I don't think I will be coming here again for awhile. My dad got the clam soon dubu (level 2 spice) and it was ALRIGHT but maybe because it wasn't spicy. My mom ordered the doenjang soon dubu and it was just salty. There was no flavor and no substance I thought I was tasting super concentrated ocean water with soft tofu. My mom couldn't take more than 2 spoons because of how ridiculously salty the was. I ordered the haemul soondubu as usual (level 4 spice), and the seafood was sparse masked by a ton of tofu while the flavor was also a little off. Also, due to kitchen renovations the rice was not served in dolsot (stone pots) which was a huge part of my soon dubu experience.

To top off the decrease in quality of the food, we asked [multiple times] for plastic containers to bring home the leftovers but was told that those containers were only for take out customers. Instead, we were given these small foam containers that were could easily get crushed. We asked for one more plastic bag just to pack our leftovers separately but they insisted on only one bag per customer even though there were 3 people with 3 separate orders. Clearly the economy is hitting them hard and the quality of food and customer service is sinking with it.
I really recommend this place. It's an awesome group activity. You definitely need some group work to escape! You will have fun there!

Tight spots but clean and friendly campground. People were friendly. Campground store was great! So close to everything. Shuttles come by and pick you up to take you downtown. Camping world next door. Comes in hand.
Best place to find every kind of beer in the city. From beer to Zambuca and everything in between the staff is very knowledgable and have great recommendations.

Went in for drinks at the bar and while didn't stay for a dinner in the dining room, we did order and share a few items off the menu.  Here are is my summary.The mushroom and artichoke flatbread had a great presentation and looked very appetizing however it did lack flavor and was a little bland.  The guacamole was fresh, flavorful and presented nicely.  You can order it with your own selection of ingredients, however, I went with the traditional.   My favorite was the tacos. Very flavorful and well done. Tender shredded pork finish fried to a crisp, served on corn tortillas with onions.   I would definitely go back for the tacos alone.  They were somewhat small so I did order a second helping.  The place does have all the right ingredients to be a local hot spot for modern Mexican.  The bar is very nice and the barman was extremely friendly and accommodating, although I do forget his name.  The margaritas were fabulous, they fresh squeeze the lime juice for each order, they were the best i've had outside of Mexico itself.  

I would certainly return again and recommend it to friends.

This is one of those Philly brunch places that you don't want any more people to know about--be prepared to wait! 

You can saunter across the street and down a block to the Random Tea Room and order some tea to go while you wait. Just tell the host/ess and they'll summon you via walkie talkie when you're table's ready.

All the food is local and delish. What' s good:

Juevos rancheros, three-egg omelette with tomato and goat cheese, potato latke with apple sauce ($2 extra). Also, the fresh OJ is delicious and worth the five bucks at least once.
Love 1/2 off sushi during the week, and the rolls are pretty tasty! Comfort food at an affordable price for sure.

Drove past restaurant 3x and wasn't sure due to dark exterior outside but then yelped it and it was bright and sunny inside and good reviews.  Decided to give it a try with 2 kids who were very undecided what they wanted and now we found a new place we love.  I had their chicken salad melt and it was perfect melt for me as I don't care for hot mayonnaise products and the side pasta salad was excellent.  The server was awesome and we sat at the counter so she gave my kids the extra of a homemade milkshake she made....it was great!!!

I found this place in Yelp, but almost didn't go because it was a food truck.  Good thing my daughter said eating from a food truck was on her bucket list and we stopped!  The food was excellent and the service was friendly and fast.  Three of us had a variety of tacos and one had the quesadilla.  The food was fresh and wonderful.  The salsas were amazing!

I honestly don't think I could ever go back. I feel bad and I bet they are hard working people, but the place just does not look clean and I do not trust the food. I threw most of my first and only meal I will ever get there because it grossed me out so much.

Chains like this should drive Pizzahutdominoslittleceasarspapajohnsetc right out of business.

The secret is to keep your eye on the name when you order.  Barro's Pizza.  Not Barro's Pasta.  The pasta is bland... you can beat their pasta sauce by using a can of crushed tomatoes and skipping the spices.  This is ok, though, because this is Barro's Pizza, and the pizza is solid!

I order thin crust, pepperoni and either sausage, onion, mushroom, or peppers, and the haven't missed yet.  Delicious every time!  I'd go as far as saying it's my second favorite in the area.  The cheesy bread sticks are good too.

It's also a nice place to eat in, and they can easily accommodate groups from the look of it.  Just tell your group to stick to the pizza and pizza-like bready things, and save the pasta for the 90yo grandma in the group who can't have anything with even a little spice.

Nice place, friendly morning staff and fresh coffee. Lots of choices on the menu. French toast with 1 egg and ham was good. Other plates looked good too. No crowd, food came out quickly, waiter kept my cup of coffee full. Also provided a glass of water.

The sales people at Nordstrom work on 100% commission, so I've heard. So, one would expect them to be incredibly helpful. I've found this to be the case here, most of the time. 

I ventured into Nordstrom recently, to find a pair of jeans that fit my pear-shaped proportions. I'm usually a size 4 up top, and a size 8 on the bottom, so I like to stick with skirts. A good fitting pair of jeans is usually quite elusive. 

I found a pair of CJ jeans that fit okay, not great, and brought them home to realize that the high waist was something I couldn't abide by. I was able to easily return them with a salesperson in the denim section, although this pair of jeans had been purchased in the "Individualist" section. I'm not sure what an "Individualist" is... is that a nicer name for a curvy girl? Anyway, returning the jeans was a breeze, and the girl at the counter later helped me by grabbing about 10 pairs of jeans and bringing me to a fitting room. She also let me know that Nordstrom does your hemming for FREE. This is key because I can spend quite a bit of money at the tailor so my pants don't drag on the ground. I found a pair of Paige jeans that I liked quite a bit and the tailor was called down to prep for the hemming. While I waited in the fitting room for the tailor, another sales associate came into the room and snickered at me, something to the effect of "well, those pants are kinda big, huh." In my head I answered "kinda bitchy, huh?", but I don't tend to say those things out loud. 

So, they lose a star for one of the sales associates being snobby, and they keep four stars for a nice sales girl helping me, and a very good tailor who was prompt and, better yet, free. Overall, the experience made me ready to go back and pick out another pair of Paige jeans.

This is my favorite Indian restaurant! The lunch buffet always has plenty of vegan options and the staff has always been very friendly and accommodating towards dietary restrictions! The portions for dinner are generous and the prices are extremely reasonable. I would highly recommend this place to anyone!

disappointing.

maybe i wouldn't have been disappointed if i hadn't been under the impression it was going to be more like a farmers market, not basically just a bunch of long lines to a bunch of lunch trucks. i got there late, thinking it goes until 10 and my friends inform me that if the food hasn't run out, then it'll be an hour wait for me. no thanks. 

it had a lot of potential to be cool, there was music and i saw a lot of people i knew. but there was nothing to do but stand in line or stand around.

meh.
I don't normally frequent 7elevens but being a few blocks from my house, we have grown fond of this store. Nice staff, quick service and quite a bit of selection. It is always packed for a reason!

Tucked away in Sherwood Park this is a hidden gem.  A small place with an interesting collection of beer and some surprises that are still in stock when they sell out at the larger bottle shops.  Owners will take very good care of you and it is definitely worth a stop if you are in the area.

The doorman was rude. I showed him my id and told him i was 24. He rejected me because it was a month before my 24th bday and he thought i was lying. He was clearly too drunk with illogical words. I explained to him a month did not make a difference. He assaulted me he was going to call the police and escorted me out. I was like okat i would try another place. 
The other hookar bar called 'hoohare' had way more nice servants.
Great little coffee joint. I've only been here once but it was nice and quiet inside and the layout was very nice. The employees seemed friendly as well.

The food isn't bad, but it isn't something to write home about. What else to you expect from an airport restaurant/bar? I had the hot wings, which were surprisingly decent, despite being overpriced. They also have a good bar with a decent selection of beers, which would be the only reason I go back there.

The servers are understanding of any circumstance, given that travel plans shift often and drastically.

I am reviewing the ER services.  This place is basically equivalent to a human ER with all the benefits and hassles that entails.   Yes the waiting room is a little cold and clinical, and billing and signatures on waivers  is the first item of business.  Yes they triage pets so that the most severe ones are seen first, and others are left waiting for hours.  In our case, we were triaged to be first, but we did hear another family talking about a 5-hour wait.   

HOWEVER, if an animal is in serious jeopardy, be assured it will get first-class service, even late on a Saturday night.  They have surgeons on call who are willing to stay up through the night if necessary to save someone's pet.  I am certain they saved my dog after his surgery was botched by another veterinarian.  

I would give them 5 stars for their medical miracles, but reduce their rating a tad owing to the high cost of treatment -- thousands of dollars for one surgery.

The Service was superb there was this rising star and the young man was on point! He was polite, observant, and very accommodating! For his third day and handling a large table with the young lady he should be at Cracker Barrel for a long time! 
The food was good I couldn't decide between fish or shrimp so I went with my staple catfish and it didn't disappoint! We had a large table of about 15 people and a whole lot of food!
Small diner with a nice staff. Food was very good and filling. Not a long wait which was good. They have gluten free bread! I will come back. Food portions are filling.

Great fries and rings, but you can only get your burger cooked well done "for health reasons!"  My friends, if you don't have more faith in your product then you have to nuke it to keep from getting the customers sick, your in the wrong business!

We stay at the koa several times a year.  Always a great time.  Pool is wonderful and they keep it heated!  Staff is friendly and helpful.  Lots of amenities.  A very quite and peaceful place to vacation.  And its minutes from the beach.  Love this place, we have made many happy memories here.

I was lucky enough to be gifted an oil change from Wildcat from a friend, and didnt go in with much expectation other than getting the basics. 
 These guys really do seem to be the rare, honest and experienced mechanics that you hope youll find when your car springs a leak.
They went above and beyond, were quick and very helpful. Didnt try to talk me into a bunch of extra crap, and all this was for an oil change that they had donated to a local charity, which my friend won and gave to me so it was all out of their pocket.
 Ive gone back with issues since then and will be dropping my car off again today for a long list of probs. Though its never a pleasure to deal with auto bills, these guys are top notch and I will recommend them until they prove otherwise.
They are easy to deal with, courteous and though they may not be the cheapest, they take good care of your car and do the work right. 
 So do yourself a favor, when your car is ailing, give these gents a call and get it rolling proper.

We have been patronizing this restaurant for about 8 months.  Have had good experiences until last 2 weekends.  This weekend we were told that it would take a while, which we understood but after waiting 50 minutes and noticing that people who arrived 20 minutes after us were serve before us we complained.  We were told that it was not their fault and never offered an apology.  We will never visit that store again.

We love Firehouse Subs and will go out of our way to avoid this location.  They are extremely rude and care nothing about customer service.

Came here with a Groupon, which was incredibly easy to redeem. The service was prompt and welcoming and was probably the highlight of my visit. 

My date and I ordered phyllo cigars, which came out piping hot and tasted pretty good. I ordered the lamb kofte and piyaz, which also tasted good but didn't wow me or seem worth what they were charging. My date got the seafood linguine, which did not taste like anything special.

I did really enjoy the complimentary olive bread!

Anyway,  the happy hour specials looked good. I would come back for those but otherwise wouldn't pay full price for a meal here.

The interior is very classy and high scale so formal attire doesn't look out of place which is good since I was here for a formal dinner for work. The wait staff was very attentive to our group and made sure that everyone's drink order was taken as they sat down. Dinner was served timely which can be difficult with a group of 14.

I had the Mississippi Rabbit which was incredibly good. The meat was very tender and the mashed potatoes where silky smooth. The gravy was good and even with the bacon the meal didn't taste too salty. 

Between the excellent wait staff and the incredible food this place was top notch.

Have been hankering for a good pad Thai and a friend took me to this restaurant.  Very pretty decor, thoughtful service, beautiful food presentation with rice even in heart shape on its own plate.  I food the noodles done well and shrimp plentiful- peanuts were ground very finely, so no 'crunch' looked for.  Extra bean sprouts and lime were provided upon request at no charge.  Plentiful food at a reasonable cost- I would return.
Two others in my party, with other dishes- everything mildly seasoned for less adventurous eaters.
Food rates 4 stars. Service gets 3. Chairs very uncomfortable. Large facility but customers sparse.

Best sandwich I've had in Reno/Sparks. It takes a minute for them to make your order, can be quite a few minutes if they're busy but it's well worth it. Has the kind of unique look about it you'd expect from a local institution such as this.  Try the signature Yellow Sub - can't go wrong!
The food was terrific and the speciality cocktails were a bit of fresh air in the midst of a hot day in Nashville.  A one of a kind with exceptional service.  A must for dinner.

First time here yesterday and we loved the donuts! We loved the build your own concept which is great because you get to try different combinations of the things you like! Here are my thoughts, something to consider when you go:

Pros:
1) Long line packed with people but the wait for the donuts weren't long considering the amount of people there.
2) When you get to the counter, you kinda already know what you want because they have order forms for you to fill out while waiting in line so the lines move pretty quickly. 
3) You can let them know if peanut allergies and they can accommodate
4) Donuts are made fresh constantly

Cons:
1) If you have a nut allergy, your choices are limited in what you can order. For example, you can't get the s'mores one (which is the one we wanted).
2) The order forms does not list all the specialty donuts that were available so you'll have to make that decision at the counter.
3) I wanted to order iced coffee, on the menu, but was told that they didn't have iced coffee. I would have to get a cup of ice and poor hot coffee over it. You can guess why this wouldn't work. 

All in all, we loved the donuts and had a pleasant experience with the kids. The pros do outweigh the cons for sure. The cons are more for FYI if you're a first timer like us.

Had to give it a 5 star review to level out all the one star reviews. If there wasn't so many one star reviews I woulda gave them a 4-star. The only sushi place in Isla Vista that I know of. They rolls are really good, they miso is super dank, and there staff is really friendly. Your order does take a lil time to make but they also deliver.

Okay, by now after reviewing more than a few Chipotles I realize I have a problem, that being said my enabler the Chipotle Corporation has been kind enough to finally open one in Reno! So now even when out of state for a weekend away I am still eating great food for lunch.

The best part Nevada folks don't know what it is yet, so the lines are short and quick the down side is the staff doesn't know what it is yet so they are a little slow and give about half the portions as the California sites I've been too. They're new... so it's okay. They will learn.
Clean! Bright! Super knowledgable and friendly staff! Great variety! Can't wait to come back and try everything else!

Placed an order for delivery through UberEats and for some reason the order was not delivered. Called the restaurant and the young lady who answered my call couldn't care less about the order. She told me my problem was with UberEats not them. I explained that it was their responsibility to make sure that the order was delivered. She rudely disagreed told me to go back to the app to get help. I tried nicely to explain that she was wrong. She wanted nothing to do with me and hung up. Needless to say I will be posting this unfortunate incident to every review site I can find. Reckless disregard for customers.

Loved it. Everything I want in a coffee shop. Good coffee and coffee eats. 
Plus, they have real writers. You know how I know? I can see them write their screenplays.

Moved into Mike's food shop in the back. When we arrived it was later in the evening so some of the food choices were not available, but we had a great pepperoni pizza and tempura with brown rice and a mango salad. The food was great and because the pizza wasn't ready when the other food was they offered free delivery so we wouldn't have to wait and the tempura get cold.

Staff is friendly and honest about time for preparation of food and availability. Food is fresh and they are taking donations for supporting a youth writing program and providing them food, so if you have some spare change or cash leave it as a donation.

If i could give this place no stars I would. Stay away from this horribly pretentious place. They do not honor your reservation time and they will happily humiliate customers and make them stand behind a curtain by the door. There is no bar no place to wait, and they could not care less about your comfort or discomfort. We had been warned it was 'pretentious' but never imagined showing up for our reservation, on time, and being made to wait 15 minutes behind a curtain (in a space about two feet by two feet). When we inquired they made it sound like it was our problem, they were not the least bit sorry for the inconvenience. Instead we found a terrific place a few blocks away called Fish. Don't bother with these morons and spend your money someplace they will treat you well. No food is worth being treated like that.
This is a nice quaint spot buffet style.  All items were good gumbo, shrimp creole, fried fish, fried chicken, vegetables, etc. but my favorite I have to say was the bread pudding.  Soooo Good.

This will be short and sweet.  The pizza was good.  The stromboli had pepperoni in it, which I did not order and subsequently did not eat.  The hubs said it was good.  Delivery legitimately took 2 hours.  2 hours!  No, it wasn't worth it.

By far the best Hibachi my boyfriend and I have had . Too bad we live out of the state because we would be there every weekend ! We ordered a tempura sushi role and had hibachi shrimp and steak dinner . The yum yum sauce and the ginger sauce for the salad was our favorite . Everything tasted fresh and superb ! I wish I could give this place 10 stars . The only recommendation I would have is to fix the place up a bit ,the bathrooms were not nice and there was ripped seats in the booths

Not bad but not great. A restaurant that wants to be more but the staff is just not inspired to deliver. Spotty service most of the time and food that can be awesome (like those skillet mussels) or average to bad, like most pasta dishes. Steaks are good but side dishes are blah. Best part is the Sinatra Bar, great atmosphere and unique in this area. Do not go if you want to hear the people at your table...

I've always been curious about Phonoluxe since reading a lot about how 'snooty' their employees were.  I've never had that experience since I've been, I'm not really sure how or why but a lot of people mentioned getting glares from the employees and other rudeness of that nature.  My visits have been perfectly lovely.  Sure they don't come up to you every 5 minutes asking if you need help but they also don't follow you around the store like you've got sticky fingers.  Personally I enjoy that.  I tend to spend a lot of time wandering around record stores and find it rather bothersome to have someone bugging me while I'm making serious decisions about what awesome musical item to purchase.  

Due to my roommates recent quest to find cassette tapes, I know for a fact they're the only place in town with any sort of selection.  That probably is not of interest to too many people but I find it pretty cool.  Their inventory overwhelms you as you walk through the door, the very definition of sensory overload.  The main room is crammed almost floor to ceiling with cds, various vinyl and cassettes.  New and used, local and favorites from current artists to classics in every genre, you name it they've got it.  The second, larger room is crammed mostly with vinyl but they also have dvds and a small selection of video games.  I spend at least an hour when I go and could easily spend longer but I end up having to leave in order to keep me from buying way more than my budget can afford.

They are located in a sketchier side of town on Nolensville Road off 440, so a visit out there can be a little bit of a trip but it's definitely worth the drive.

Farm and Fisherman is fabulous top to bottom. To start with, the space itself is very nice, particularly if you can snag a table by the window. Small and intimate; you do not feel that your fellow dinners are right on top of you. I think it has a romantic feel. 
Food is outstanding. We had the Bloody Beet salad ( a signature dish) and grilled  cauliflower salads to start. Very fresh and tasty as you would expect since it all comes from their own farm. Then split the mushrooms stuffed with home made pork sausage stuffing. Simply delicious. I then had the pork loin, which was cooked perfectly with tons of flavor. Em had the wild stripped bass, which was also excellent. Topped it off with two excellent desserts. 
It's BYOB so brought an excellent french white burgundy and a  Hirsch Pinot; both outstanding. 
Can't wait too return!!!

Dinner with subline. Let me begin by telling you that they have oysters at $.75 per oyster and grilled oyster is a dollar and a quarter per grilled oyster during happy hour. Indeed it is happy. Happy hour is between the hours of 3 to 6 PM. Lots of locals and tourists all knew to flock to this place because they really do have the best deal in town. We had ordered 24 oysters; that is two dozen oysters and it came out to $18. Naturally we also had to have other food to go with The delicious oysters. We had seafood gumbo and we also had some wonderful vegetables that were in season. The sauce for the vegetables was an herb infused butter that we ordered extra bread just so that we can mop in the wonderful sauce.

This seafood gumbo was pretty good. It wasn't the best we've ever had. But it was pretty good. I do like the fact that they put nice okra into it. As you already know I love vegetables and the sauce that went with the vegetables was absolutely delicious. We overstuffed ourselves with the oysters we honestly couldn't eat another bite. Even when they mentioned delicious choices for desserts, sadly we had to refuse them. Another day, another meal.

This is by far the worst food I've ever had. If one wants to find out how you can screw up plain lettuce, this would be the place. Their entrees are mostly preprepared Aramark catered dishes. Stay away.
Butch did an excellent job describing the city I was born in! I learned so much! Thanks!

Good food. Great service. I don't like a thick rub on my ribs and I felt like I was missing something with the nachos. (Good pulled pork nachos at Juans Flying Burrito) But, overall I would go back for other items.

If you go to Blarney on a Saturday night, here's what you can expect:

- to pay a cover.
- to see trashed undergrad girls in cocktail dresses and heels falling all over themselves and anyone who gets in their way.
- to pay in cash, as the credit card minimum is $20. 
- to hear terrible karaoke (this part is actually fun).

You shouldn't expect to:

-have space to move around in. It's pack from the front door into the back room.
-to have easy access to the bar. The first Saturday night I was here, I didn't even get a drink because I physically could not get to the bar. However, I am only 5 feet tall, so I couldn't muscle my way through a wall of frat bro.

Bottom line: this is a Penn undergrad bar, so if that's your scene, go for it. I personally don't like getting dolled up to go to a dive bar, so I take my t-shirt-and -jeans clad self to Drinkers' West, Blockley, or Cav's, all of which are way better, in my humble opinion.
it was fast to the point very kind people didnt waste my time or theres thanks

Pretty good ice cream (not soft serve) and a good selection.  Nice happy staff.  Reasonable prices and long hours.  Beach atmosphere, as it is right across the street from the public beach at Pass A Grille.   They have a few chairs out front, but nothing fancy.

Just getting around to writing this review.  We went on Valentines day.  It was real nice with the French atmosphere.  I liked the savory crepes better than the sweet.  We had the Gyro Crepe and the Asiago Crepe, both were delicious.  We didn't try the Nanza but we will go back for that, they are flatbreads on iIndain Nan bread they sound great.  Wee ended on the Crepe suzette.  The service was excellent.  We will go back.

We went for our anniversary. Wow!! Best steak we ever had! We had the ribeye with crabmeat and bearnaise. Perfectly cooked and seasoned! Service was impeccable, busy Saturday night but functioned like a machine! Anthony, our amazing server recommended we get different side dishes because they are large enough to share. He was spot on! We shared mushrooms and onion rings. I didn't care for the onion rings. I guess I thought they would be the thick rings. They were stringy. My husband enjoyed them. We also got the famous St. Elmo shrimp. Sooooo good! Building was beautiful, barhrooms were clean. Great time! Can't wait until we go again. I was to try the prime rib pizza.
Great addition to the mainline. Service and food were spot on. Great California wine selection too! Will be back

I've never eaten here, but the music is fanatic and I've always had excellent service from the bartenders.  Downstairs has a bar and a dance floor in front of the stage, and upstairs has a bar and is lofted with seats so its easy to see the band.

Cute little bakery that offer up some pretty good pastries, cookies, and cakes. Their German Chocolate cake and petit fours are my favorites! Their decorated sugar cookies are tasty, but wish they were a little softer. They have great selection of coffee and tea drinks, and a vast variety of lunch entrees. They are a bit pricey, but overall have some tasty treats :)

First I want to start with saying I've been here a couple times before because of their proximity to where I live. Prior to last week I never really had a bad experience here but I really prefer it because of its location and proximity to where I currently live. 

Last week I came in to get a pedicure the day before a beach vacation on the east coast of FL that I was leaving for. Everything is fine to start, but I could tell the nail tech was going a little hard with the pumice stone on my foot...nothing too crazy but I've never had anyone do that before.  Then she starts going at the side of my toe, which obviously is not a rough part of my foot and I screamed because it hurt really bad! Turns out, she sliced the side of my big toe open. When I point it out to her I can tell that it's bleeding because she starts dunking my foot in and out of the water. Then I see what it looks like and it's definitely not a tiny cut, it's pretty much a small gash and very painful so I get upset. My mom was there with me and of course she begins to worry because of all the stories you hear about nail salons having unclean utensils, getting infections, etc.

The tech then called the owner over, who cleaned it with antiseptic and put a bandaid on it. It still hurt but there wasn't much I could do about it at that point so I had them finish painting my toes so I could be on my way. The funniest part about it is that they still charged me $15 for the pedicure...I guess that slicing my toe open was included in that price. I should have refused to pay but I think at that time I was more worried about how this was going to affect my trip. 

I didn't get to go swimming in the ocean this weekend for fear of the cut getting infected. I also didn't do a lot of walking because the location of the cut made it painful to walk on. We were able to rent bikes which was helpful in salvaging the weekend...but that was also an additional cost that we didn't plan on spending. 

I won't be returning to this nail salon.

I went here for breakfast/brunch on a Sunday morning. Service was great and it wasn't packed. We had a group of 6 and they were able to seat us right away. The menu was small and didn't have a ton of options but they had the breakfast basics and everything was of the highest quality. With some picky eaters and 2 vegetarians in the group the limited menu still had something for everyone.  

I highly recommend the jalapeño grits. Not spicy but great flavor!

In town for business so I thought I would pick a nice hotel in the downtown area.  An old train station that has been restored and it is a beautiful hotel inside and out.  

Once you move past the lobby and into your room things are a little different.  My room was in what they call "the tower." It is part of the original train station structure. 

I was excited at first then I saw the view from my room and I'm basically looking onto the roof of the floor below me.  Not cool.

No wireless internet at all - paid or free.  Have to plug in to pay $12.95 for the internet.  With all the upgrades and modifications why stop short when it comes to wi-fi?  Nope, not cool.

The "mall" that is attached to the building is nothing short of a tourist trap. Also not cool.

If it were not for the fact that I got such a good rate with my company I would have not stayed here past the first night.

Two stars because I got free breakfast because of my Marriott status and because the roof didn't leak.

The bf and I have decided that this is our favorite place to go for Vietnamese food in Tucson.  You simply must try the Bahn Mi (#39?) with extra meat!  It's so good that it alone will keep me coming back to this restaurant for years.  The pho is excellent, and you have lots of beef combinations.  (The bf likes it with added crab meat.)  If you're a pho fan, you can't go wrong with this dish.  I like Bun, myself, and I'd say theirs was pretty good.  Go for the extra meat on it.  This time, we tried two of the frozen drinks with the bobo.  The coconut was great, and the bobo balls that you suck up through the straw sort of taste like pieces of soft gummy worms.  Kind of weird, but intriguingly good.  We also tried the avocado, and it's made with REAL avocado (the rest are made with flavored powder.)  It was tasty--kind of creamy, like pistachio ice cream. The Vietnamese coffee is great.  It's sweet, and it only comes in an iced version.  No complaints on a warm day like today.

This place is incredibly affordable.  They also have coupons.  A word of warning--if you are here with a Groupon, try not to go during the last few days that the coupon is valid.  It's a small restaurant, and the place got SLAMMED.  The kitchen couldn't keep up, and the customers could barely contain their irritation. People were impatient; it wasn't their fault--they tried as hard as they could to keep up.  We went with a Groupon early in the promotion, and it was lovely. Logan was our server, and he was great.  

Another caution--they do "to go" orders, but if you're looking at an online menu, it's probably not correct.  DON'T order by number, because the numbers on the current menu are all different.  This really messed up a lunch order from my workplace.  Again...our fault and not the restaurant's fault, although I wish they would take a few seconds and upload their menu to their FB page, or something.

THIS PLACE NEEDS A FOOD TRUCK.  NOW.  Those bahn mi sandwiches would make them a fortune.

Well i'm still searching for good bbq in nashville. After 7 seven years here, I'm getting a bit weary that I won't find some. I had the bbq pork sandwich, no bun and a side of fries. LOVED the fries but the bbq pork was just ok. My fiance had the Tuck special and i had a few bites. It was SO good! I do recommend it. Jackalope Rompo Red was on tap- thank goodness! I'm willing to give it another try maybe some BBQ nachos or the pork/brisket platter! Also, i heard trivia on Mondays is good. def gotta show up for that.

A cyclist bar in the Grove!? Hell yeah! I've been careful to say cyclist bar instead of biker bar, as the unfamiliar person might get a different impression of this place in the open-minded Grove area if called a biker bar :)

I first visited this place the day it opened because I was so excited about it, and I have been a patron ever since. It is always refreshing when a bar opens in this town that offers more than just the dreaded Anheuser-Busch assortment of flavorless beers, and the Handlebar does not disappoint. They have a large variety of libations from not only across the U.S. and the world, but many if not all local micro-brews are represented. And, their stock is always changing with new types and flavors.

The bartenders have almost always been quick at their duties and friendly, and are always knowledgeable about the beers they sell without seeming pretentious at all.  

The interior is a work of art, with murals on the walls, exposed brick, local artist's creations on the walls as well as bike inspired sculptures attached to them. The exterior is just as great, with a fantastic and large outdoor patio with a firepit and an outdoor bar. 

I can't say enough good things about this place. With the ambiance, biking ethos, service, diversity of great beers, and nightly entertainment ranging from trivia, dance parties, and Nintendo nights, the Handlebar makes a great destination... especially if you ride there on your bike.

This was our first stop in Nashville. The brunch drinks were 2 for 1 (probably because the average wait time on a sat morning is 2 hours). We waited at the bar and had some of the most delicious brunch cocktails! The white trash hash and red velvet waffle were well worth the 2 hour wait! When in Nashville this is a MUST!
Chicken kabob pita with a side rice hit the spot. They're always timely with having orders ready. Oh, and the hummus is really great. I'd also recommend picking up a smoothie.
Great sushi for a great price! Great if you are looking for a BYOB in Media.

Great 'watering hole' and a favorite for many locals!  Massive beer selection and they have the BEST Touch tunes juke box!  Huge selection of music that can make anybody happy.  Oh can't forget about the service, Nate and Connor are two of the best and always on top of sorting another round!!

My family, friends and I absolutely LOVE The Local Taco! They are very reasonably priced and have delicious menu items that don't make you feel guilty after indulging. A few of our favorite items are the fish and shrimp tacos, and of course the margaritas. The restaurant is full of character and we love looking at the unique paintings on the walls while chowing down on our food. Highly recommend The Local Taco for anyone looking for a fun place to enjoy delicious, reasonably priced dishes.

Step out of the ordinary and enjoy some extraordinary Italian food! 
This is not not the typical Italian. Katie's unique twist to her dishes knock those restaurants out of the park!

We tried the Pear Pizza and the Fig and Squash Pizza (without pancetta). Both were delicious. The table is centered with extra olive oil and chili oil, which you can add to enhance or spice up your meal.  

Always remember with better ingredients come elevated prices.  Expect to pay a little more for these fresher, healthier dishes. 

Katie's also delivers excellent service that is knowledgeable, quick and accurate.  We were not disappointed in the service.  They seated us quickly and served us efficiently. 

What stops this place from being a five? The prices did effect my rating.  While seafood and fresh ingredients are frequently listed on the menu, I have experience fresh, larger (in portion size ) meals, that were lower in price. My own personal bias, also effected the rating. Italian is not my favorite, so it is based primarily on my personal taste.  If this review were over Italian food, it would be a five.  
 
So next time you want to take an afternoon or evening and step out of the traditional St. Louis Italian, try Katie's Pizza.  You'll take your taste buds on an adventure!

Definition of a 3 star place. 

Been here a few times. I think this may have been our fourth trip here.  Every trip has been with wife and the kids.  5&2.. 

Food is your typical bar food.  All frozen sysco type prepared for foods in a heat and eat style. 

The zingers aren't bad.
The beer specials are good.  (Regular beer menu is pricey)

Tonight I opted for the special.  I had a ribeye cooked perfect medium rare.  For only $13.95 it was a steal. Tuesday's kids eat free.  And 5 bottle beer bucket was $8.  So we were spot on with price point.  The wife got a filet mignon. Which she said was delish.  

We ordered a mojito that was not passable or drinkable.  They took it off the tab. 

Service was nice. If I went off just tonight's experience I may go four stars.  But the previous food I got from here was all the aforementioned frozen heat n eats. 

Summation.. good food food drink. Stop by. 
No frills.   Clean bar..

The burgers here are okay. We came here because it had good reviews and was right across our hotel the Thompson. I've had better burgers at the same price and with larger portions, but it was satisfactory. My cousin who was with me though found a hair in her food. We didn't send it back because she was almost done eating it by the time she noticed. 

I liked their beer selection, and the waitress was cool and attentive. It was Saturday around 5 PM when we came, so the restaurant was pretty light on customers and we were seated right away outside.

Overall, a completely satisfactory experience. Nothing truly special, but wasn't awful either.

Service is terrible they charge you $3 per person to not have mushrooms even if you're allergic!! Manager rude! Has no respect for people. The restrooms smell as if they are never clean. Don't go here!!

A friend found out about V Vegaz and recommended it to me. I made an appointment with Jason and highly recommend him. I wasn't sure how to describe what I wanted to him, kind of the posh spice look but a bit more wispy and he nailed it. He understood my description, though it didn't completely make sense. 

The haircut looked good for a few weeks but started growing out. I was planning on making another appointment with Jason, but the only person who had an opening when I could go was Callie. She was great. I kind of let her do what she wanted. She ended up giving me a trim to even out my hair and bit and thinning it out with different scissors (Not sure what theyre called). It didn't take long but it looks great.

I love the decor and music, and everyone is laid back and friendly. They seem to enjoy what they do and get along with each other. 

This place is a must go, especially if you're stuck in a haircut rutt. 

Also - you can park on the street but there are usually open spots in the lot behind the Moonrise hotel, across the street.

Not a bad stay. I liked that it was apartment style, and it felt very homey, as opposed to a hotel stay. We got a 2 bedroom, 2 bathroom suite and fit 6 adults comfortably. It was the perfect size  suite and the kitchen had plenty of space for all our food and snacks.

For 2 nights out of the 5 nights we stayed, we got calls from the reception desk late at night calling about a noise complaint downstairs. I know my family, I know loud and we weren't being loud whatsoever, nor were the kiddos busy running around being rowdy. We were so surprised each time we got a call and started to think it was a joke because there was literally nothing going on in our room. 

Located in a quiet neighborhood, it felt very safe and I liked that.

I always try to go here after work because I always get an MVP and it relaxes me before I get home. Not much more expensive than a regular cut, but the shampoo, hot face towel, and shoulder massage are great! Ever since I got the first complimentary one, I've been hooked. Don't really care about the sports talk shows on TV, because they're just opinions, and everyone's got one. 

Been through numerous hair shops, including the chain chop shops, but it's the extras that keep me coming back. I'm in my late 50's so I'm glad to still have my hair on my head, so I never have a bad hair day. The stylists are friendly and they move people through quickly. If they offered free bottles of cold water to their customers, that would make it even better.

Little by little we are eating our way through all of the pizza joints in New Orleans. We chose Reginelli's based on the recommendation of a few trusted friends, native to the area.

The recommendation was to choose Reginelli's if we wanted thin crust pizza. Well, we wanted thin crust pizza so we picked up the phone and ordered takeout.

The pizza was ready pretty quickly and I'm happy to say that our friends were right. The thin crust pizza is out of this world. We appreciated the nontraditional options considering we really weren't in the mood for simple pepperoni. There are plenty of artisanal choices and can I say arugula is really good on pizza! Who would have thunk it?

We will definitely be eating more Reginelli's in the future!
A good basic italian place. Good flavor meat sauces and quality pasta. Huge portions and a good value.
Accompanied friends against my better judgment - big mistake.  Food poisoned!

Going to the backyard is a culinary experience.  Chef JJ brings the funk and the noise.  My wife and I had a blast during our Egg 101 class.  JJ is very passionate about cooking and you can tell he has so much fun with it.  Our evening was fill with laughter, entertainment, and great food all cooked on the Big Green Egg.  

Rebecca did a wonderful job as Hospitality Director.  She brought me many Sun Kings and that made me very happy.  Jenna took the time to show us specifically how to work pizza dough after we asked.  We learned a lot from her.  If you have not been here, you must go.  We already booked our next three reservations!  I can't wait to go cook something on my BGE now!
Caminada PoBoy is the best poboy in the world(although not traditional). Its a must have. Waiter Steven was great too. I cant wait to come back to nola

This restaurant has very good energy! First, the owner has very good sense of humor. Second, the food is so good. My husband never took left-over home unless it is super good, and he did this time even though we are on our road trip back to California. Third, we love the mango juice bottle! All in all, you can tell that it is a very decent family restaurant, offering good food and service.

Food is solid.  We do takeout a lot.  Used to be on point but for three times in a row they quote 20-25 mins and it ends up being 50 mins.  Orders are wrong and they are very confused.  Disappointing that it has gone form so good to so bad.
Love their rum runner! Come visit Alex and Arlene behind the bar, they're a great conversation!  Can't beat their sunsets and view of the dolphins!

I have to say that good food was not even a redeeming factor for the experience my husband and I had. We stopped by for a late breakfast and got simple sweet potato pancakes and eggs and sausage. Which tasted pretty darn good. What made the experience so poor was the inattentive waitress and the high price of the meal for the amount of food we got. The bill didn't seem to add up. Three hours later we both experienced stomach cramps and severe indigestion. Will not return.

We ordered room service from the Drury Inn from here. The Chinese chicken salad is delicious. It comes with both a peanut sauce and ginger dressing.
We ordered the spinach artichoke dip. The Parmesan crackers were awesome. They brought the dip cold and uncooked which I thought was weird. We microwaved it and it separated.  It was still really good but prob better if it wasn't separated and oily.
I'm sure we will dine in during our stay and try it again.

We decided to try out this place again. Not sure how it usually works if you are suppose to seat yourself or wait to be seated....so we just decided to wait for someone. Well, a couple of employees walked by and didn't acknowledge us. One girl holding a tray of food came to us and looked annoyed asked how many and got some menus and proceeded to walk us to a table without saying another word. There were only about 5 tables occupied. Food took foreverrrrrrr to come out. My husbands food was burnt and he eats just about anything and it was hard for him to eat. Also almost broke a tooth on the burnt bits of what was suppose to be prime rib. My sons food (he's 3) took the longest to come out. He got Mac n cheese and it came out after sliders and a prime rib sandwich. It was also scorching hot so we ended up having to pack it up cause it was just too hot to eat and we had already finished our food. Our waitress was super nice though. But it's obvious that there is no manager or anyone in charge...it's kinda like a free for all from the couple of times I've gone. I use to love Parrot Pete's when it first opened...completely not worth your time now. There are so many better options elsewhere.
Love this place! Friendly people, great atmosphere, great food and prices.  Mimosa flight? Yes, please! Everything prepared fresh to order. Best breakfast/brunch in Gulfport.

Expect to wait a long time for dinner - it is slow to cook from scratch.

That said, as long as you are expecting the wait, this is the best dinner in town, and the best Indian food I have had anywhere. The dinner dishes are always of a higher quality than the lunch versions, but the lunch buffet is pretty good.

I've been coming here for years, and have never had a bad dish or server. The owner is very friendly and always helpful. 

My favorite dish here is the Tikka Masala, with the Palak Paneer a close second. 

There is always a great selection of craft beer on tap, and they have a pretty good wine selection. It is a bit pricier than some Indian places, but pretty cheap for BoDo.
Seriously? $10 to park at a casino? They should be embarrassed. I can't believe they have started doing this. I will not be back.

I so desperately want this place to be 5 STARS.  Like, REALLY.  

Location: Awesome!  in Winthrop shopping center, adjacent to Publix on one side and Acropolis on the other.  It has cozy decor on the inside, you can place your TO GO order directly with the Hostess at the entrance, they have these homemade chips with this spicy dipping sauce, the bartenders are EXCELLENT, even when the place is busy.  It has the makings of a GREAT DINING EXPERIECE overall, but it just falls short.  Example:  I ordered a Moscow Mule (don't ever do that by the way.  EVER)  it had WAYYY too much ginger beer in it and it was just gross.  I forced myself to drink it.  I ordered a salad last night...it was mediocre.  HOW IS A SALAD MADE AVERAGELY?  Even the raspberry basalmic dressing!!!  HOW?  I actually got really bored while I was eating it and wondered what I was going to eat tomorrow.  (HAHAHHAA) Just underwhelming.   BUT...the Shrimp and Corn chowder is worthy of a quick at the table twerk and body roll episode.

The have a BLT with fried green tomato that is REALLY GOOD!! .  But guess what?  Their fries are average at best.  EATS!!!!!  I want you to WIN!!  I really do...but please bring a chef in to overhaul the menu or something.  They need something to take them to the 5 star level, I just don't know what it is.
I ordered the Rittenhouse roll and geisha roll on the special menu! I really enjoyed both. They were very fresh and flavorful. I also liked the environment.

Regardless what the other comments say, this was my first time visiting and it became my favorite place for bubble tea. The lady at the counter was pleasant and helpful, the bbt had really fantastic tapioca and the portions were plenty (for the yam fries). The place had a really welcoming environment, very clean and comfortable and best of all ot was quiet for the most part. Any other bubble tea place is often packed to the nuts but I found this one to be quite relaxing. Another plus is that it's beside Tropicka, a place that already has great ratings for it's food. Would definitely come again and wishing it the best of luck in future success.

This was the first chance I have had to use Dolan for service.  My 92 Miata's slave cylinder failed us a few days ago and fortunately we were within close proximity to Dolan. We rolled in and were immediately greeted by the Service Manager who brought us into Doug one of the Advisors on staff that day. Doug and I talked about the issue and he mentioned that he has a Tech that specializes in RX and MX Mazdas.  Dolan provided us a ride home and we waited for the call with the estimate. Doug qualified the estimate by saying that it will be on the high end and that he would rather be high and come down than to have to call back and give bad news. I gave him the go ahead to have the work done and asked about an oil change being done at the same time (if you have changed the oil in a Miata, you know it is a messy job). Doug called me back with a final price which included the oil change for significantly less than what even the original quote was. All in all a very good experience.  .

You probably won't get sick eating here, it's clean and staff was ok.  Food was applebees(ish). 

There is something that every one can get buy with-so it's safe. Not overwhelmingly good.

Not a bad hotel but a little disappointing when you compare this hyatt to the others we usually stay in, primarily San Francisco.  The rooms don't have much drawer/dresser space at all.  The plus to this hotel is location.  Came here for our annual summer baseball trip and hotel is located a block away from stadium.  Also very close to downtown.

It was a Tuesday morning when me & a friend were looking for a place to have his birthday lunch. Silk City was closed to our disappointment when a man walked by and said "aww yeh man they closed, ya'll ever eat at Honey's?" No we hadn't so we headed to Honey's Sit-N-Eat. I had heard about this place for years but never made to the trek over. They decor is great, the people are cool, really cute little homey knick-knacks, all around great vibe. I ordered eggs benedict & he ordered the chicken fingers. The eggs benedict was good but different. It had more of a citrusy taste to it which didn't sit well with my hung-over stomach. His chicken fingers were amazing though. They were breaded with all sorts of herbs & spices that put a great new twist on the traditional. The fries were equally delicious served with a chipotle mayo.
Great service! I'm really happy with how my nails turned out! The staff was professional and courteous.

New to the area and needed a 1-year service on my Tiguan. Jason matched the price of another local service center and I was in and out within the hour that they quoted me. WiFi is available and both a Taco Bell and Wendy's are next door in case you need a little munch. Everyone was very kind and helpful.

I love the food and the prices. The only complaint I have about Cheddars is the....clientele....they attract. Come in any night of the week and you'll find large groups of loud, obnoxious urban people that crowd the doorways and have absolutely no care for anyone but themselves. They let their children run around and carry on like they own the restaurant. Cheddars can't do anything about this, but it's definitely not a good place for a nice family dinner or a date night. After 2 bad experiences with the crowd who basically takes over the dining room, I only get my orders to go now.
Hey it's a great bar food place so if you are in a happy hour mood they got plenty of tvs and the Sunday Brunch was inexpensive, but ya get what you pay for.  Not bad just...eh ok.

Back in NOLA for an event and wanted to try a different brunch spot and Horn's popped up. This place is amazeballs!! I ordered the Jewish Coonass with a mimosa and my boyfriend ordered French toast, cheese grits and plantains. The Jewish Coonass comes with a hash brown cake with carrots and hot sauce,I believe, spinach, topped with two over medium eggs (how I like my eggs) and crawfish étouffée. All these different flavors made me happy! The mimosa was $5 and it wasn't the skinny glass either, it was a nice size. They give you a lot of food and I was unable to finish mine, so my bf finished it for me. 

The service was great as well. Our waitress continued to fill our water glasses and answered any questions we had. We got there around 11:30 and there weren't many ppl there, but shortly afterwards, it started to get packed with customers.

LOVE this place! Some of the best pizza and pasta I've ever had. The pizzas have fresh ingredients and an perfectly crispy thin crust. The pastas all have great flavor and there's usually a great special. The portions are large, I always get at least another meal off the leftovers. Also love the bruschetta every table gets as a free appetizer. I've been coming here for years and it never fails to disappoint.

Lauren is my girl!! I tell everyone I know about her, not kidding! She's the best. I only trust her with my hair now lol. I always have to see her after I get my hair done by anyone else, it has been this way for a few years now! hahaha. I cannot thank her enough though. I have had the best experience with Salon Fiber. I got my hair done and it wasn't what I asked for for, which is okay it happens... so I asked if Lauren could fix it and she did an amazingg job. I couldn't have asked for anything better!!

But I'm trying to go blonde for summer, and these roots girl... So the other day I called and made another appointment with her for any Friday in the future (per my request) but the only appt available with Lauren was a month from today... I took it anyways... But a month is a long time from now... So I I just called, and because of the snow day last week, Lauren is coming in on a Monday to make up for appointments that were missed because we got like 10+ inches... !!!! I even had an appointment that day, so it has been a process lol

Thank you to the front desk for being sooo friendly and accommodating! This salon has such a chill environment and the chicks there are really cool. Everyone is so nice. Can't wait to come in  If you're wondering what salon to check out next come here!

Craving Korean food and where to go in St Pete?! Sushi Zen is actually right around the corner from me so despite some of these reviews, I decided to check it out (The craving was too strong!).

The restaurant just stretches far back with booths lining the wall. We were greeted by a nice lady. There was a man behind the sushi counter making sushi. They were not rude in any way. Just friendly in an understated kind of way, which is fine with me. We ordered the fried dumplings, galbi, and dolsot bibimbap.

Fried dumplings- very tasty with the dipping sauce! Meat inside the dumplings had a nice gingery taste. Dumplings were fried perfectly and were not too greasy.

Galbi beef- marinated short ribs in their special sauce. The plate came out sizzling hot and smelled wonderful. I only had a bite. Not the best galbi I've ever had but it was good.

Bibimbap- DING DING DING! Winner! Most delicious meal of my week. Served in a hot stone bowl, the bowl was still sizzling as it came out. The rice on the bottom was all crunchy and smoky flavored- So so good! There was a variety of vegetables in there to include shitake mushrooms, cucumber, seaweed, and lettuce. The beef was seasoned perfectly. I was given the Korean chili paste/sauce on the side for it so I threw that in and mixed everything up and: total mouthgasm.

Did not try the sushi so I can't comment on that. But our service and food was good. Prices are kinda the same as other Korean restaurants in the area; not sure how portion sizes compare though. 

Will most definitely be back for more Korean food.

I love Livery. It's one of my favorite spots in Indy, mostly because of their rooftop patio, but their food is also awesome. The food is mainly appetizers and small plates, so it's not a place to go if you're starving, but the atmosphere is lovely and the menu has some unique (and, more often than not, delicious) items that are fun to try. It's a great spot for drinks and catching up, as it's a little quieter and cozier than similar places in the area. Highly recommend!
Great med food.  I would pass on the gyro, kinda dry.  Everything else is fair game.  Dolmas, hummus, salad, baklava = yum.

what happened? this was the supreme Sami stop.. now the bread is super dry, I have to ask for sprouts and the parm is non existant..the last two time I went in my order was not right. I can't anymore.. I'm sorry , the "crew" act as if the order is easy but I have to watch them and correct. you've lost me . I hope the best.
The food and service very good. Our party had a variety of dishes and everyone really enjoyed.  And the prices are reasonable.  A definite return visit is in store.

The restaurant is beautiful with an eclectic, seasonal menu filled with fresh local choices. We had fantastic service - Ashley was an amazing server from start to finish. She provided a wonderful overview of the menu and impeccable recommendations and we left extremely happy with our choices. We can't wait to try it again!

So gross!!! Planned to eat here, arrived before our party so we sat for a drink at the bar. Michelada was awesome and for that, the one star. But while we were contemplating the menu, a young girl behind the bar (long light brown hair in a pony tail) drop a chip bowl on the ground ( ewww!!!) proceeded to pick it up dip it into the chip bucket scoop up chips and place them into the chip "drawer". Then as I watched gave said chip bowl to another customer!!! Just ewww!!! So, needless to say I will never be back because of that. If you plan to go ... Please be aware of what is happening with your meal...

First I'll mention that this place is cash only.  They do have an ATM, and (too) many places in New Orleans are also cash only, but just keep that in mind.

We hit up this place for brunch on the way out of the city. It was about a mile away from our hotel on Canal St. away from the French Quarter on Magazine St., making it a reasonable walk, even with our luggage.

We started with the apple-pear-ginger juice and fresh squeezed limeade.  Both were excellent.  The apple-pear-ginger was somewhat thick and not completely smooth, which I absolutely loved, but I could see how others -- especially those in the pulp-free OJ crowd -- would not.  Three of us split the bananas foster French toast, biscuits with sausage gravy, shrimp and grits, and a cup of cheese grits (one in our group doesn't eat seafood).  All were quite good, but the French toast was rich enough that I don't think I could have eaten an entire plate of it.  The biscuits and gravy rank up there with some of the best I've had.  The grits were creamy and far from the instant stuff.

There were a number of items marked either vegetarian or vegan, which is a rarity in this city.

The service was good, but the attention to coffee refills might have been too aggressive.  Our table was decoupaged with mementos from a jazz festival in 1994, and the place had a relaxed, kitschy atmosphere.

I checked out EWC because I changed jobs and worked on the other side of the city from my normal waxer. I try to stay away from chains but I needed somewhere with flexible hours (and open on Sundays!)  Long story short I'm very happy with my decision. I received the 50% discount for first timers and even their full prices aren't that bad, $47 for a full Brazilian in the city is very cheap. They were professional, clean, and walked me through the whole process. I already made my second appointment!
Love the hand grenade and other drinks.  If you are in NOLA it's worth it to pay 16 for a liter and save on the shipping.  They even let you sample the drinks....
Excellent, fast service.  Lee is just the nicest man!  He let out 4 pairs of my husbands pants and they look great!!  Highly recommend Lee!  Price was reasonable too.

Normally I would give this place 4-5 stars however today was a different story.  I am a very understanding person.....I served at upscale restaurants for years but it was hard to overlook all the issues.  They were very busy and my friends and I were understanding that service would be a little slow.  The drinks and food took forever and each time something was brought to us something was incorrect.  Our server was very nice and apologized and corrected the mistake.  The food runner that brought drinks and food was very short and rude when we tried to explain the mistakes.
