Hudsons, please bring back Holy Puck beer for next years Oiler season!

Thank u Kayla at the customer service counter!!!!! she really made it her goal to find a 2 year old receipt that I tried to get from the slidell location with the associate that said she couldn't find on the first search

Fresh and unique; I can't figure out how they can keep everything so top quality in such a little shop.  My son brought my husband and me here for lunch for something different than our normal Trader Joe's salads when we're in Reno from out of town.  Between the 3 of us we had the Kale salad, the Cobb salad, and the Half Sand Combo with today's soup special, French Onion with croutons and cheese, and a Silk Roadie on Dutch crunch bread for the half sandwich.  The servings were huge (the soup looked small but was delicious and very filling), the bread was light and very fresh with a tasty curried chicken filling; the portions of everything in the Cobb salad were more than ample, especially the avocado.  For dessert we each had a scoop of very reasonably priced homemade ice cream, each flavor delicious (and we sampled several before deciding on our flavors of choice).  We'll definitely return here the next time we're in town.

Elliot is very knowledgeable and professional.  He is well known in the law community and went the extra mile to ensure there was no stone unturned in dealing with my case.  I highly recommend him to anyone that wants a top notch professional handling their case.
Great pizza, good beer, fantastic outdoor deck, lovely staff, dog dining area.... Can't fault this place. I'm now a regular.

I was not expecting such a uniquely extraordinary place. I went in, thinking maybe I'll buy something since I do like spicy as well as souvenirs from traveling. The prices were a bit high, but I expected as much from a shop catering to such a specific market.

There is a wall where you get to sample all the hot sauces, but we got bored/lazy since we had had a few drinks and itched to go to another bar. Before we left, however, we saw some sweets by the cash register and thought they looked interesting. We asked the owner to try it, and he got out some samples. Upon closer examination, he decided that the brownie was too old and didn't want to leave a bad taste in our mouths, so he gave us smores instead. WOW. This went above and beyond my expectations! I was so blown away by how spicy it was (I was expecting it to be weak, like most American food is). The textures were pleasant and varied, and it was not overwhelmingly sugary. We decided to take a chance on the brownie, which was SPICY AS HELL (my first time acquainted with the ghost pepper). You've been warned. 

Really really regret not getting the smores the first time around. Also really really regret not coming back for them after we had a few drinks and forgot. Doh!
Pie was good but the service was terrible. Don't come here for lunch because you'll be waiting for about 30 minutes or more waiting to be seated.

Just passing by and decided to stop in.  All the food looked good and decided to order the chicken and waffles which were very good and hit the spot.  Also, got a bourbon Bloody Mary - a first.  Not crazy about bourbon but somehow it worked.  The menu has a number of items that were appealing and one day I should be back.  Waitress was very nice, casual and friendly.

I am very happy we decide to try this place. The draft beer and wine list are great. It's not too big but has a wide variety of great options. For an appetizer we got the coconut shrimp which was delicious. The shrimp was larger than you get at most places so it was a great choice. For dinner I had the crab cakes. They were amazing! They paired so well with my Malbec wine. The crab cakes melted in your mouth. This sides were a little strange and not so great but the crab cakes made up for it. My boyfriend got the mahi mahi which was deliciously. The seasoning was perfect. We would definitely go back.

If you enjoy light lunches, and are concerned about food truck mishaps - you can depend on the Fishin Chicken Food Truck to be a safe choice.

I'm not one to make safe choices, though. The Fishin Chicken was near my workplace for lunch, so I ordered the jerk chicken taco. The taco I gave it 3-stars - it depends on what you want out of it. At the time, I wanted some real jerk Caribbean style. The jerk chicken wasn't truly authentic, and I've done had the real stuff. But, if you're an overall "safe eater" and want just a bit of flavor, you can cheat knowing you've cheated on the healthiest/cleanest version.

I'd still buy again from them. The service was great and they got orders out quick.

Delicious sandwiches and a variety of chips and soda to choose from. There's almost always a  line, but it moves fast (usually). I'm a big fan of the chicken shack ranch. They have (loud) live music sometimes, but I'm just here for the sandwiches.

Newer is always better, but not in this case.  

Not much has changed in over a 100 years of service at Ralph's, and that suits me just fine. Sure, it's got the prestige, the history, the classic neighborhood feel, all of which really complement the food & huge wine cellar very well.

Besides the suggesting the pastas, some notable orders I would recommend:

Meatballs - delicious traditional seasoning
Eggplant Parmesan
Calamari in red sauce
Mussels in white sauce

Five stars for italian fare, you ask?  Why yes, because the food is that good.  There's few italian spots that I really recommend, but Ralph's does it well and should be a must try for anyone willing to shell out a couple bucks more than you'd pay at a chain restaurant.

First time here and it will definitely not be my last! I ordered a small trigo nutty and it was delicious and very generously portioned. A small was perfect for one person and I'm sure a large would be a good size for two to share. So good :)

My husband and I spent our honeymoon in New Orleans and got a good deal on this hotel. The staff was AMAZING!  Carol Ann at the front desk made our first day there by sending a bottle of champagne to our room while we were out to dinner. Coming back to that was such a nice surprise.  The room was great. The bar is super cool. The only drawback is that it's right on Canal, which is a super junky street. That said, I'd recommend this hotel over and over again!
Cute place, got there too late to eat,the drinks were good though, they have fresh ingredients and crushed ice!only bar in ybor I've seen with fresh things and a wide selection of booze

Great environment, good assortments of beers, funky people, board games, chill vibes, Monday Game nights and random parties, outside patio, great coffee, try liquid heroin coffee, one of my favorite places in town

I had a terrible waitress here. She was very rude and inconsiderate and she made me feel very uncomfortable. I won't go back here if she will be working. I believe her name was Jackie.

- To clarify, I've never had another problem here. The rest of the staff is friendly and very professional. I have always loved karaoke Mondays. This particular night was just very off because of this waitress.

In Riva is conveniently located off of Kelly Drive near the falls bridge. We came here around 7pm for dinner and drinks. We heard they have a great happy hour but were too late this time. 
The food came out promptly and was delicious. We tried the margarita pizza, the edamame crab ravioli and the meatballs. All were great and sharing was a great choice so we could sample everything. We also has their signature drink the Riva Spritz which was really refreshing for a summer night. We sat at the bar which was really busy---they had one person making drinks for the bar and the entire restaurant.  Our server was very friendly despite being noticeably busy. Would definitely return to try more menu items.

Hubs and I enjoyed our 4 night stay at the charismatic Hollander.  Some thoughts:

The goods:

+ The staff is great. Everyone was friendly and helpful and I felt truly welcome my entire stay
+ The location is convenient. You are right near the highway but can also walk to downtown
+ The porch/lobby/bar/pool is funky and fun.  There are always people to socialize with and the decor is very interesting (check out the grand piano frame mounted to the wall)

The could use improvement:
+ Parking is shared with the hotel next door and often has you circling looking for spots/parking in sand. It's also one-way in and out, which can be a tad annoying depending on your navigation direction
+Sound proofing of the rooms to the hallway isn't very good, so people walking by your door talking will sound like they are in your room
+Shower temperature fluctuated on us the whole weekend going from nice and hot to slightly cool

The good out-weighed the bad for me if you're looking to stay at a place with some character!

Stopped in for a quick lube, as I was overdue during my recent travels.  Thought everything went well until I looked in my driveway and found gear oil running down out of the rear differential and onto the concrete.  Looks like the help forgot to tighten the plug.....  lube express is now off my list of places to get a quick oil change....  this one is still costing me....

Dolce is a new restaurant in the recently added shopping plaza near the Oaks theatre. We've been looking forward to trying it since we first saw the sign go up. 

Unfortunately, our visit was very mix. The decor is really nice. They had beautiful lighting, nice tile floors, and the Tuscan villa mural was very pretty. Then, they had naked statues that tacky-ed up the place a bit. 

We arrived before our friends and waited about 5 minutes before we even saw one staff member. When the hostess appeared, she did apologize for the wait but since we had 4 in our party, a table had to be cleared. In the meantime, our friends arrived and so did 3 other parties behind us. We waited about 10 minutes for our table. We joked that they were making it from scratch. 

Our service was good. Although, a bit under experienced, I asked what pasta came with my meal and he said "penne". It ended up being spaghetti noodles. 

Now to the food...The portions were huge and had a price tag to match. The salads were drenched with salad dressing. I ordered their chicken parmigiana and it was not good. I've had better at an Irish restaurant in Reading, Pa. That's saying a lot. 

Jeff ordered their homemade fettuccine Alfredo. The noodles were soft and tender. They really looked like those no yolk egg noodles in the grocery stores. The homemade noodles saved this review from being a one star. 

For four people, our bill was $85 which is a bit absurd for underwhelming food. I really hope they can up their game because it could be a nice BYOB.

Pros: 
Location
Waitress is friendly
Open windows face to the crowded street

Cons: 
Worst Coca-Cola I had 
Shrimps are not fresh
Sands in gumbo

Super nice hotel for the area.

All the amenities you'd need or want. The facility has a pool/hot tub.

It's newly remodeled, clean, and the staff is very friendly. 

Rooms are clean, beds are comfortable, bathrooms fresh.

Complimentary breakfast. Decent but not spectacular. One of the better breakfast I've had at a hotel though.

I'd highly recommend this Hilton if you're staying in the St. Louis area.

I'm a firm believer that any Italian restaurant that serves bread with oil and Parmesan cheese for the table is already onto a good start. The bread was seasoned and yummy. My boyfriend and I ordered a large pizza to split, half pepperoni/half cheese and it was delicious. We missed happy hour by thirty minutes (it ended at 6:30) but it was nice to sit outside and enjoy our Friday night. I'm eager to come back and try the pasta as well as soup. The service was good and the food was satisfying. I will definitely be coming back for dinner.
Love this place Clearwater beach is the best highly recommend coming to Pier 60 and enjoying your time sunsets are amazing

Best laundromat ever! Clean, good music, kids' area, bathrooms (clean and modern), delicious snacks, plenty of machines, friendly and helpful staff, and plenty of room to fold your clothes! Highly recommend!!

Eh. Tasty food but careless, amateur service. I've honestly never seen a wait staff not give a shit about service as I saw at my meal at Luke. Randomly distributing plates as they came our of the kitchen with no apparent thought to having apps out before entrees.  Literally they stacked the tiny table full of appetizers and entrees all at once with no acknowledgement seemingly that fine dining establishments don't do that. Saved only by tasty food.

Best Plumber in the area. I have used Mr. Ecker for over five years now and every time I get honest work at a fair price. Mr. Ecker does a lot of work on his own, so if you have to wait for a little bit, I would suggest waiting if you want whatever issue you have to be remedied correctly.

You would not know it from the outside but the atmosphere is great and the food was amazing.  I took my wife here for our anniversary.  We are new to the area and my wife being sicilian loves italian food.  when we pulled up my wife wasn't very impressed thinking where did I bring her on her anniversary but when we got inside she was delightfully impressed and when the food came she was estatic.  We both loved the food and the staff and we will be back.

Really fantastic place. The food is always good and the decor terrific. Coco Thai has gotten more popular over the last year - the word is out. Atmosphere is very lively on the weekends -  always lots of regulars there. As other reviewers note, the PA Wine & Spirits store is less than a block away so it's easy to grab the right wine.

Great place to get a quick gyro. Fast service, quality food, and pretty nice staff. Even with a pretty big line I always get my order quickly. 
I've never tried their food truck, but if it is as good as their shack I'll try it out for sure.

Coming from NY, I'm usually picky with my pizza, and when I first saw the thin pan pizza, I was skeptical. After trying it though, it's safe to say I'm a changed man. The pizza was absolutely delicious! Also, good authentic tasting gyro's and don't hesitate to grab a cannoli on the way out!
Cash only but you get what you expect from a small, local owned business. I'll continue to shop here. Fast, fresh, warm, all around good food for price
I couldn't pick between the almond peach petit four and the strawberry cheesecake - so I got a scoop of both!  So delicious! Very generous with letting you taste anything you want :)

Not much of an out to eat breakfast guy so my words may fall flat. Having said that, I do make it out for the most important meal of the day occasionally. It was the first month of living in Indiana that my wife and I decided to pawn the child off to a family member so we could scout the town. March was still cold and the mid-week morning was gray and we Yelp'd great breakfast joints. And so we landed here by way of the reviews and didn't regret it!  My experience at Milktooth found me sunshine in the form of the BEST pour over coffee I could recall. So good that I had to ask Phil how he did it. Phil was very kind and even provided some coaching for my own novice barista ways.
I could go on and on about the fantastic pancakes and rave about the ancient grain porridge, but you just have to experience it yourself. I recall telling my wife, and our server, that this might have been the best breakfast experience in my life. But then again, how would I know, I don't get out that much for breakfast? I just know.
Well done Milktooth.
Amazing service and quality of food. Staff knows how to treat their customers right. Highly suggest the pork chop entree.

This place proves that locals really give a shit about good food. It is always packed and for good reason. Really well conceived dishes, fresh ingredients and fantastic service. I live in Clearwater and happily hall my ass to St. Pete for this privilege. 

Docked them 1 star for forcing me to listen to some part-time musician struggling through Top 40 covers... but for this food I can deal.

HORRIBLE DOESN'T BEGIN TO COVER MY EXPERIENCE WITH THIS COMPANY!!! First I've had two managers hang up on me, we have had the company for THREE YEARS & have never been called after our siren goes off and I've had the company tell me its my fault. Beware of this company. horrible service

The steak here is phenomenal. I highly recommend the porterhouse for two. It's big enough to share with leftovers. The sides I could take or leave; they were mediocre at best, salads, spinach, potatoes, etc.

A classy dump or an upscale place that's seen better days and is fraying around the edges; take your pick. You know you're in trouble when you walk in and smell that stale disinfectant smell in the lobby that continues to your room.

Got stuck here as overflow from a conference at the Gaylord across the way. I probably shouldn't complain since it was only $99 a night. Then again, for that price you barely get a parking space around San Francisco. So I need to factor in the cost of living index...

Cons:
-- Musty disinfectant smell everywhere
-- Fitness center looks like they refurbished a broom closet. Hand full of machines (some in not top condition), no place to do sit ups on the floor, disinfectant wipes dispenser empty.
-- HVAC in rooms is the old noisy type with no thermostat, just heat or cool high or low.
-- Bathroom has like a 20W bulb with a noisy fan. Bath tub is a ceiling to floor pre-fab plastic number with old fixtures.
-- No food to be found except the attached Applebee's. At the very least, they could have had a complimentary coffee Thermos in the reception area. How I wished they had at least a kiosk selling espresso drinks and muffins.

Pros:
More like Not So Bads...
-- Single cup coffee maker in room made a decent cup of joe
-- Free broadband in rooms
-- Sleep Number bed (I don't quite get it but it was kinda cool to check it out)
-- Rooms rather spacious

Bottom line: if you need to stay near the Gaylord Convention Center and can't get into the Gaylord Hotel next door, go to the Hyatt Place down the road instead.
Food is not badd...service is good too

From my initial phone call to the national chain and a phone call from the local rep to the arrival time at my back door was 45 minutes. Best customer service I have ever received and I will use them from this point forward! They were absolutely awesome!

There are 3 different experiences in 3 different areas at Italian Affair...
- A nice restaurant (with piano on week-ends)
- A richly wooded bar with booths and drink specials (Happy Hour just til 6 - boo!)
- An outdoor patio w/heaters TVs & even a stream.

OK, it's one of my favorite restaurants.  I've watched it grow from a pizzarea to  this really nice place.  That just doesnt happen if your food isnt wonderful!  
Stuff I like about it: 
- The Italian family that runs it, friendly and oh that accent!!! 
- They will make you anything - I mix & match Cheese tortilini alfredo w/shrimp & crab - not on the menu but for about 23.00 ITt's SOOO Good.  
- The little hard rolls & dippy (I always have to remind myself not to over do it) but I ALWAYS have take home bread or not!

I've had parties here - one with 60 people and NO ONE wasnt happy with their food!

Very nice restaurant with awesome atmosphere and wonderful staff!!! The calzones were delicious and the sodas that they getting from a brewing company in Illinois were fabulous!! We got the meat me in at. Louie and the duke and loved them both! The staff was very attentive! Would definitely go back!

I came into the minute clinic with my 2 and 4 year old boys. We got in line at the kiosk in hopes of being seen.

While the kiosk seems convenient at first, the elderly man in line ahead of us took over thirty minutes to sign in. Multiple times I had to assist him, because there was nobody around to notice or offer any help. The system required him to enter an email address, and he didn't have one.

When it was finally our turn to sign in, we found that there was only one appointment left, and we needed three. The next appointment was for an hour and a half later. 

By this point, my boys were quite unhappy and loud. We decided to leave and find somewhere else .

I always wanted to check out one of these tours and after doing some searching on yelp! I decided to go with the Voodoo Bone Lady tour and although it was unfortunate i was unable to have the Voodoo lady her self as my tour guide I still had a great tour guide named Brian who kept an upbeat tone throughout the tour and was extremely knowledgeable. What I really enjoyed about the tour was they covered more topics than just ghosts. Brian covered everything from history, ghosts, hauntings, vampires, pirates and even zombies. Overall I was very pleased with the tour.

Cheu's has to be one of the top 5 meals I have ever eaten.  Everything about this place is amazing, from the food, to the service, to the signs in the bathroom.  If I didn't live 600+ miles away from here, I would be here at least 2-3 times per week.

My dining companion Liz and I set out on a mission to try as many items as we could in one meal.  We succeded. We ended up enjoying the nightly dumpling special (among the best I have ever had), the broccoli, the black garlic wings, all three of their buns (get the pork belly), the Boloanasian, and the brisket (complete with a matzo ball).  To top it off, they have daily, fresh pressed juice concoctions that you can easily throw a few shots into.

Each dish was just as amazing as the last. Of all of the great eateries in Philly, this one shot right to the top of the list.

We bought a 2013 Honda CRV at Crest Honda in December 2013. I took the car to Crest Service a few months later for regular maintenance and they offered to wash my car. Of course I was pleased to let them clean my car and thought it was such a nice perq!

The car is garage-kept so it took several months to notice that the roof was leaking from the antenna. Since that's the last time the car went through a mechanized car wash, I knew they had bent the antenna so I took it back fully expecting to be questioned and to have to argue my way up the chain to get the repair. The service tech did question me and we went together to the manager, who said or course they'd fix it and apologized.

Several months later, with the car out of warranty, we noticed the roof was still leaking and the stain on the headliner was hideous, so I took it back fully expecting, again, to have to argue to get the repair. The service tech questioned me and we went together to Chad, the service manager, who said of course they'd fix it and would have their detailers clean the liner. Great! 

I spent a few hours in the service waiting area. It's comfortably furnished with clean restrooms, a coffee bar and soft drinks available. They popped popcorn and even had hotdogs available at lunchtime. They also offered shuttle drop off and pick up service to anywhere in the downtown area. A few hours later, I was told they needed to order a part and could overnight it if I wanted to spend hours there the next day or could get it via regular mail if I wanted to come in the following week. I came in the next Monday prepared to wait several hours and was told quickly that a necessary bolt did not come with the part and that they would overnight it and I could come in the next day. I told them this did not make me happy and that I had quite a drive through Nashville traffic to get there. Immediately they offered to rent me a car and it was there within the half hour. I came the following afternoon and picked up my car. I also had them do an oil change and tire rotation which they comped me for the inconvenience.

When I got home, I remembered to check the staining on the headliner and it was not good. I called Crest Service and left a message. Chad called back at his first convenience and I will be taking the car back Monday to get the headliner replaced.

I am in the midst of a saga with Crest Honda Service. At every turn it could have been maddening, but Chad has stepped up at every opportunity to make things right. The purchase of the car was smooth and I have never seen a service department go to such lengths to work with a customer.

I fell in love with the curry tofu wrap, mediteranean salad and the banana whips instantly. Many of the menu items seem a bit heavier than what I would typically eat which is why I don't venture to far across the menu items but, what I did have, I raved about and went back many times for.

I get a banana whip every day on my way home from the gym (obsessed!) and it would be great if they were made a little quicker since, it can become pretty cramped in there to wait. The free water with fresh citrus slices definitely helps ease the wait time.

Run by amateurs! They need Robert or Chef Ramsey to teach these amateur how to run a restaurant! Not only I waited 30 minutes to get my order I waited another 30 to get my food and it was the wrong order! Waited another 15 for my family's food. We were seated after 738 and didn't leave til 945pm.  Granted we meet the co-owners daughter waiting for a table so I figured, food must be really good for even she has to wait for a table. Service was 1 star. Not even a refill of water? Our waiter need to go to real restaurant to see how real waiter wait. 
Now the food? If it arrived hot and not cold? If it arrived all at one time? If the staff worked as one instead of standing pretending to work? Maybe!

I was disappointed! Most of the reviews here noted service was so, so..they weren't lying! The food was good I have to say but so is Appleby's on a bad day.

This was one of the highlights of our trip to New Orleans. It is definitely worth the wait! They are only open from 8-11pm nightly. The line starts around 7-7:15 and the earlier you get in line, the better seat you get. The hall is tiny and seats very few people. They allow for standing room in the back, but it gets pretty crowded in there! We attended a night that the Preservation Hall Band played and it was such an experience! Every single person in the band showed amazing talent and a visit to NOLA would be incomplete with a stop here!

Over the top-jaw dropping-best food of your life. My sister, my best friend, and I all have birthdays within one week so we decided to come here for a birthday lunch. The menu was a little pricey so we all ordered appetizers for ourselves as a meal and each one was INSANELY delicious (duck springrolls, garlic truffle fries, gumbo yaya, and the AMAZING mushroom dish that i don't think they have anymore :-( ). When we told the waiter (SUPER sweet guy) that we were there for our birthdays, he brought each of us a complimentary birthday bread pudding which was also ridiculously good. We all couldn't stop talking about this restaurant and the food for days afterward so 10/10 would recommend.
The food, ambiance, and service here is great. We had the burger and fried oyster salad. There was enough to share between the both of us, with room for their absolutely delicious bread pudding!
One of the best cigar shops I've ever been in. The guys there are always willing to help you out. Huge selection.

I dropped in just to get my oil topped off. The staff was very nice and very quick with everything. They topped off my oil, windshield wiper fluid which I was completely out of, and filled my tires. All which was free of charge with their free top off service in between oil changes. 
I stopped by again the following week to see if they were able to fix my mirror. They still filled my tires and checked to see if anything needed to be topped off. The staff was extremely nice. I would choose to come here over the one in my home town over 45 minutes away.

I can ride my bike with no handlebars...but it turns out an actual bar is way cooler than that. Even though it was raining the whole time, we had a blast. It was great to be able to bring our own coolers and the hosts were phenomenal. This is definitely a great activity for anyone, at any fitness level, that loves drinking, fantastic people watching, and belting out some of their favorite songs with friends. Everyone let loose, and after a few beers, the bike turned in to somewhat of a moving karaoke stage for us to showcase our Spice Girl caliber talent to all of downtown Indy. 

I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for something a little different, especially if you are coming from out of town. It would be a great way to see all of downtown Indy and hit up some of great bars at the same time.

It's ok as a park. It's nicely positioned to be a shaded respite in a business area with hotels near and museums sort of walking distance. The Wednesday night free concert, while great musically, was way too crowded for any comfort or to try and eat there. Most of the people were busy drinking and trying to yell conversations and come on lines over the music. It's wall to wall shoulder to shoulder and most everyone seems to be smiling so they can call the series a success but its a good idea gone too popular. It happens. Best place to hear any of the music, if your into the band that night for free, is across the street on the steps or wall with other nice folks who dont need the noise and crowd.

I've always been adventurous where food is concerned. Growing up in a multicultural paradise allows you to try new things all of the time. My husband can be a little hesitant, so when I described this place to him I promised that this experience would be worthwhile. As the driver dropped us off, we began to worry that we were in the wrong place until we saw the sign. You must knock and wait for the doorman, who is an extremely kind man. Once there is available space, you are whisked into what almost feels like another world. The smells, and small intimate settings alone made me happy. We were taken to the top floor and placed in a dimly light room with two other parties. I was worried that this would be awkward or "too crowded," but everything turned out fine. I had mentioned to my husband that they only accepted cash, and that the meal is 25 per person. Upon seeing this price in reviews I wondered if we would be full after the meal. We were full by the third course! There are technically seven courses (but some would not count the dessert of fruits and baklava as a course). There are no utensils, but that didn't stop us from digging right in. I started to wonder if we would get a visit from the belly dancers that seemed to only exist downstairs, when suddenly we heard cheering from the next room and moments later she appeared in our doorway. From beginning to end this was an experience we will not forget. Thank you Marrakesh for an extremely memorable night.

Good food, not so great service. I stopped by to get a quick bite between my doctors' appointments. I ordered fried Manchego cheese and sauté mushroom. Both plates tastes good. The portions are good for the price. They also have 2 for 1 drinks special and happy hours from 4-6. I can't comment any on drinks. 
Move on to service, it's lacking. My server seems to be running around all over the restaurant, however he walked past my table a few times without asking me if everything was ok. I used to work as a server, so I'm not usually a tough critic on this department. I saw him checking on a table not far from me a couple time, a simple "is everything ok?", would have been suffice. I don't know if coupling the facts that my bill was small, and me being Asian cause him to just ignore me. I gave 20% tip anyway, it's what I usually do unless the service is extremely horrible.

GF and I stopped here for a bite for dinner. Waitress was friendly and informative and the food came out fast once we ordered. This is about all that made it 3 stars. 

I ordered the matzoh ball soup to start and it wasn't the best I've ever had. Very salty. For dinner I opted for the baked Mac and cheese appetizer for my entree and that also left much to be desired. It came out hot and bubbly but the taste just seemed.. Off. 

GF got the turkey club with avocado mayo. Nothing special - she said it pretty much tasted like a Turkey BLT and couldn't even taste the avocado.

Prices were fair for the city but we probably wouldn't be back for dinner - maybe it's just more of a breakfast/lunch place.

Below average pricey Thai restaurant with a full vegan menu.  

Visited on 12/2/17 at 5PM.  I must have passed by this place a hundred times and never noticed it which is ludicrous because the sign on the outside of the building is absolutely enormous and they have a unique round entryway around the front door. It sits in a small strip mall next to a consignment store and a laundromat.  

Inside it's rather un-inspiring with plain tables and clutter.  It is one of those sketchy looking places where you want to order "something safe" if ya know what I mean. We were seated very quickly and service was fast and friendly.  $41.57 got us a seafood entree, a chicken satay appetizer, and a kid's meal. 

I got the $7.95 chicken satay appetizer which came with four chicken skewers, a bowl of peanut sauce, and a bowl of cucumber salad.  The cucumber salad was fantastic...chock full of fresh jalapenos and onions and fresh cucumbers.  The peanut sauce was a little bland but a very generous portion.  The chicken skewers were yellow, hard, dry, flavorless, and barely room temperature.  I am certain that they were cooked either yesterday or earlier today and re-heated.  For the price, I'd expect some freshly cooked chicken.  

My son got the $9.95 kid's chicken pineapple fried rice which came with apple juice and a spring roll.  I do not like paying ten dollars for a kid's meal at any restaurant but I will say their portion was enormous.  They give 3-4 times more than any child can possibly eat.  It was the best thing I tried tonight...hot and fresh and well seasoned. I found it unusual that it was smothered with fried onions which I wouldn't think is very kid friendly.  My advice would be to cut the portion in half and lower that price and nix the onions.   Also the meal was supposed to come with a dessert which they never brought out. 

I watched in horror as my husband's dish arrived.  He had the $20.95 "seafood basil delight" which the menu said had shrimp, calamari, mussels, and scallops stir fried with basil and onions and an herbal sauce.  What arrived was a plate full of green peppers, onions, calamari, shrimp, and mussels.  The scallops were missing and the green peppers were not on the menu description.  This is not the sort of place where I would order something like this but my husband is a brave man.  He said he'd give it a "4 out of 10" and that it was hot but bland.  

The prices here do not match the quality of the food.  Serving old chicken is absolutely unforgivable.  I would not go back.

A last minute Friday night trip that did not disappoint! 

In an effort to avoid meat for Lent, my boyfriend and I went to Ralph's in search of some delicious seafood and pasta. Extra points for having Lent specials with veggie soups and crab meat pasta!

We started off with some fresh mozzarella and tomato which was great. My guy had the flounder francaise which he raved about for the rest of the weekend and a side of ravioli-delish! I opted for the manicotti. If you are a fan of cheese, do yourself a favor and order this- outstanding!

Unfortunately, we had no room for dessert. Only con I can think of is that the temperature of the place was on the warm side. That won't stop us from going back!
All my experiences at Corks n Crowns have been amazing. But today was horrible, even awkward because of the server. She ruined it for us!

I went and had a gel manicure here today with Emily Vo and she was awesome! She did an excellent job, really took her time and was very sweet. I must say it was one of the best manicures and gel polish jobs I've received. I would definitely go back!

Food was fantastic, but everything else needs improvement.  

I walked into this restaurant to half of the tables unoccupied but was told that the wait was 45 minutes unless I wanted to sit at the bar.  Seeing that I was dining alone, I opted for the bar.  

Sitting and looking around, it was clear that the tables were unoccupied because they were all a mess.  It quickly became evident that this restaurant was horribly understaffed as I watched a handful of people try to run the place.  They all seemed like they were running around without direction and without knowledge of what to do.  Surely having more staff would have allowed them to turn tables faster and reduce the wait time (and reduce the amount of people who walked out refusing to wait).  

I ordered Drunken Noodles and a Salad.  I would have also had Thai Iced Tea, but they pre-mix this beverage and my dairy allergy means I must replace the cream with water (it's still tasty, trust me).  The beverage I did have took forever to get to me.  So did the meal.  I asked where my salad was when my entree arrived.  By the time I had finished, I still didn't have a salad or even an answer on where it was so I just canceled it, paid, and left.  

Even at the bar, the bartender looked overworked and confused.  Simple requests by myself and other patrons at the bar took forever.  I never saw a refill on my beverage.  Additionally, a manager-looking-type trying to help behind the bar almost spilled a tray of drinks all over me from the other side of the bar.  Had I not been watching what she was doing and been able to jump up just at the right time, I would have left drenched.

The only thing that saved this experience from a 1-star review was how fantastic my entree was.  I can only hope that this restaurant can get its act together on every other front.

This is my favorite restaurant in st. Pete at the moment. The cocktails are creative and fantastic the food is wonderful. I've tried almost everything on the menu and am never disappointed. I highly recommend the steak tartare to start, the curry as the main and the espresso martini to drink.

So I really wanted this place to rock our world but alas, it falls short.  You're in the right ballpark, B.Good, but execution is where you need work.  

1st, I don't want to be rushed while reading your board to order our lunch.  You guys may know what's up there by heart, but we don't.  2nd, I'm glad the food came out quickly, but what the heck? I just spent $30 and am still way hungry!  3rd, The Buddha bowl concept is great with the local fresh produce, but a little more dressing and more than 2 tablespoons of quinoa please?

We're going to Chipotle for the main course I guess. 

Not returning-

I really enjoy this place, they're so hospitable and the food is legit! Thai hot is actually hot and I can dig it. My favorite is the t2 garlic sauce. If you want to enjoy a great atmosphere, good food and nice staffing; you find it here!

OMG !!! I'm so excited to find a professional eyelash extension salon in New Orleans . The staff was pleasant and very professional and timely . I'm happy to say this is the place to be for lashes ... booking my refill in now

Worst Jack in the box ever! I had ordered a Jack's Spicy Chicken sandwich with cheese and an order of tacos (2) & when I was given the food I asked the guy to confirm that the sandwich had cheese and he said "yes"! Then, when I got home to eat it, guess what -- no frickin' cheese!!!! Complete losers and the worst customer service ever!! I am definitely gonna complain first thing in the morning.

We had the chicken tikka masala, paneer masala, naan, samosa. We ordered medium spicy and it was perfect. It was that balance of your nose running a little but can still taste all the flavors . Feels really homemade and we can't wait to go back.

What a great experience. From the time I came in I felt the good atmosphere. They have crafty decorations and a well designed menu. It is an all around American establishment with top service. 

We had the wings for starters and WOAHH! Were they good. we ordered the East of Melrose flavored wings and they were better than any sweet and sour alternative. I also ordered the Mayday Velvet Hustle beer to go along with the wings and they were perfectly paired. The bold hops of the beer meshed well with the tangy souse of the wings.  I would recommend it to anyone! 

For my entree I had the Smashy Melt burger that comes with griddled mushrooms and onions and Swiss cheese. The onions add a  sweet flavor to the burger while the mushrooms make it extra tasty. I cannot say one negative thing about this place. I'm beyond pleased and will be telling everyone I know about it when they crave a burger. Burger republic has nothing on M.L. Rose.

As a local, this was family's favorite place to stay when they came to visit.  Now that I've finally stayed here, I can see why.

The location is fantastic.  You're right in the Quarter close enough to play tourist, but yet off the raucous mess that is Bourbon Street...if you want it, it's there, but you can safely avoid it if needed.  It's also very close to the CBD.

The rooms are also attractive and comfortable.  Decorated in Victorian-era style, they match the overall theme of the hotel.  Note that almost every property in the Quarter has smaller rooms than you might be accustomed to.  The service is some of the best I've had at a hotel, which you'll find out in your first 5 minutes at this place.

Fantastic meeting spaces if you're booking a business event, and above average buffet catering for them complete the picture.

And of course, this hotel has the famous Carousel Bar, which is probably the best hotel bar in the city.  I've been a longtime patron of that particular establishment.  It's a Classic.  Stop by even if you don't stay at the Monteleone.

I was surprised that this place had a decent selection of vegan options/substitutes. The vegan fried chicken po' boy was tasty. My friend ordered the vegan pulled pork (made out of seitan) and he wasn't a fan, but he loved the big ass biscuit. It's a very hipster vibe. I plan on coming back to try out other menu options.

I can't believe it's a chain. The brisket is amazing! Get there early as this is truly cooked fresh daily and they run out of brisket towards the end of the night. I like the 2 meat platter with the ribs as my second meat. Not a fan of the green beans as they use some sort of giant hybrid of beans I've never seen in a grocery before and they don't have collards. The mac & cheese is just ok. But hey, you're here for the meat anyways. Oh, did I mention free soft serve ice cream? That is, if you're not too full to have anything afterwards.

I am as guilty as the next person when it comes to stereotyping.  It can be mean, or occasionally funny, and I had some preconceived notions about Indian food.  Do you know that scene from National Lampoons Vegas Vacation when Chevy Chase is with Randy Quaid in the off strip casino and they go to the buffet and order the "yellow" and the "blue?"  That's kind of what I expected from Indian food.  That, and massive indigestion afterwards from eating buckets of curry.  Let me apologize now for my erroneous notions of Indian food.  This place was fantastic.

There isn't a bad thing to report.  Perhaps - perhaps - the portion size.  My dish only had about 5 or 6 pieces of chicken in it, so it wasn't terribly filling, even with the rice.  However, lets face it, I'm a pig and every now and then, I can eat a normal human size amount of food.

My last time at Indian food was probably as a teenager, 20 or so years ago.  I don't remember it, except it was somewhere on Long Island.  Therefore, I didn't know what to order.  Thankfully, my girlfriend thought of posting a message on a yelp forum asking for advice for "safe" options for first time Indian food eaters, and Nick S and others (you know who you are) provided some great suggestions.  I went with one of their suggestions, the Chicken Tikka Masala.  Normally, I like spicy food.  However, with my preconceived notions, I decided to go with a medium heat (5 out of 10).  Glad I did, because even at a 5, I was sweating at the end (in fairness, I would be sweating eating a snow cone in Alaska in February).  Regardless, it was delicious - served in a creamy tomato sauce that I want to put on all of my food for now on.  

We also had a plate of nan bread with some dipping sauces that was also very enjoyable.  The sauces had an interesting flavor - couldn't quite place all of the spices - but very good.

The inside of the restaurant is very ethnic - decorated pretty much like you would expect an Indian restaurant to be decorated.  Very cute.  The service was fantastic.  Waitstaff couldn't have been friendlier, and our server couldn't have been more helpful with the menu.

They have a lunch buffet 7 days a week where they serve almost their whole menu (according to our server), so that our next trip will probably be for that so we can sample other dishes and see what we like.  Until then, the aforementioned Nick told us about an Indian market in Tampa, and I am going to try to make me some Chicken Tikka Masala...I might add bacon.
The food is below average compared to many other Mexican restaurants in the area.  Based on feedback from the table next to ours and our table, the drinks were watered down.

I have tried this place a few times over the years and I have either been disappointed or found that it was just okay.  Not authentic.  Not enough flavor.  Sauces decent, but not good.  No wow dishes or anything memorable.  Not going back any time soon.

HipCity is a gem in University City. I have taken many self-titled carnivores there and they have been astounded by the Crispy Hip City Ranch. Apparently, it's that good. 
I like everything here, but my favorite has to be the Curry Tofu Wrap (can be made as a salad) or the Cheesesteak. But like I said, everything is amazing. 
Their delivery is also on point.
"A" on the fried okra. Done with cornmeal not some thick breading.  In general good food good service, they were not very busy when we stopped in for a late lunch

Eat here!  You will NOT be disappointed!  I have had the fish and chicken tacos.  Tacos are $1.75 each but taste like a million bucks.  It's cash only and there is a small bar inside or a few picnic tables outside.  The atmosphere is more like a takeout place.  It's a busy little place.  You might have to wait a few minutes because they cook everything to order.

Stopped in for a quick morning coffee before my flight out. I had the iced cappuccino which the sign says they are famous for and it was delish!
I did see a friend eating a huge ice cream cone from there the day before and it did look tasty. 
Would definitely stop if I went back!!

Walking by all weekend... there was a HUGE line.. be prepared to wait.

Not very impressed with menu flavors/ and the contemporary mix of ingredients.

The "snacks" are appetizer size.   The wait for a drink at the bar took at least 15 minutes---- either short staffed or just way too many ingredients in their cocktails.

The pig ear snack was drenched in salt. The croquettes were a bit bland.
Fortunately we had reservations for dinner elsewhere.

I just called for a quote on a part for my vehicle, and received horrible customer service. They were extremely rude and treated me like I was an idiot. I felt stupid after hanging up the phone and definitely won't be taking my car there. Canadian tire should hire nicer employees in their service department. Not impressed.
My husband and I enjoyed a FABULOUS meal at Cafe Ponte tonight...very delicous and innovative menu. Our meal was not cheap but totally worth it...loved the experience.

My stay ending June 6th was a "do-over" from my unfortunate stay in April. Assistant GM, Sylvia Amlaw went above and beyond to make my stay perfect. I stayed in a Bayview room with a beautiful view of the harbor as well as the bay. On Sunday, when the storm rolled in, I had a front row seat. I decided on room service and it was well worth the small up charge. As before, the food was excellent, the service was fast and the staff members were professional and friendly. Even when it rained while sitting at the Tiki Bar, I had a great time. Lunch at the Tiki bar was very good as were the bartenders. I chose a massage for my 25 minute spa treatment included in my all-inclusive package. I was already relaxed and after that, I was butter. I didn't get to use anything else in the spa, I was having too much fun at the outdoor pool. 

I would recommend the you take the time to do a little research before your stay. The place is huge and takes a little effort to know your way around. Take some time to wander around and check out all of the old pictures and read about its history.

About my stay in April, I didn't feel like it was fair to give a poor rating at that time. It wasn't due to anyone being rude to me, just a comedy of errors that all just happened to me all in one weekend. I always prefer to give a place the opportunity to make things right. From the Assistant GM, the manager on duty upon check in (Lee, I think), Greg, the bartender at the Tiki, the staff members who brought my room service- it was made right. Very right. It was just what I needed!
Easily the best burger I have ever had! The service was fast and you get great quality food. Best burger in Philly!

I'm always a little wary of restaurants located right in the French Quarter. Because it's SO touristy, restaurants don't always have to work very hard to produce truly quality food because most people don't know much better. Tourists are easy to please, I guess. 

Located right off Jackson Square, Cafe Pontalba is convenient to lots of sight-seeing spots, which might be the only perk it really has. My friend and I were wandering around, looking for an affordable dinner. (Quite a difficult feat in this part of town, ugh.) Cafe Pontalba's prices were reasonable, so we stopped in for dinner. In hindsight, I should have just fronted more money for a better meal but you can't always win.

I got the Crawfish Étouffée, thinking I couldn't leave NOLA without eating some étouffée! It was suuuuch a bummer. It was one of the blandest, most spice-less meals I've ever eaten. I was STARVING so I ate it, but I did not particularly enjoy it. My friend got a crawfish po-boy and we both agreed it was also very so-so.

This place has no official closing time. We stopped in at around 7:30 on a Tuesday night and it was almost empty. There were two other tables seated and a couple of people at the bar, though most of them seemed to be the restaurant's employees who must have already finished their shift. The bar had TVs with games on, so I guess it might be a nice place to catch a game, but I wouldn't choose it. Like I said though, it wasn't particularly late but you would have thought we stumbled in at midnight judging by how exhausted our waitress seemed. I waited tables for six years and I know how exhausting and tireless it is, so I do always try to be sympathetic, but she just wasn't particularly friendly or helpful. Our food came out really quickly, which was nice, but our waitress was not super attentive to our table. 

It's not that this place is bad, but there is nothing impressive about it. In a city with such incredible food options as New Orleans, there really isn't any excuse to eat just so-so food. If you want good cajun or creole food and a quality dining experience, I highly suggest you look elsewhere.

This location is always timely and gets our special orders right.  While I am eligible for delivery, I never have. Their soups are a bit too salty for my taste so I stick to the endless wrap selection.

We went here for brunch before the parades while visiting New Orleans Feb. 2014. We didn't have a reservation, but they did seat us. It is loud and was very cold. My husband decided to order the hamburger. It was a $16 hamburger, so he thought it should be spectacular. He said it was just okay. I decided on the steak. I ordered it medium. First time they brought it out, it could moo. I asked to have it recooked. When it was brought back, it was tough and flavorless. I have to say the fries were great and the weight staff was wonderful. But I would definitely not go back there.

Quality sports bar in the Marriott. There was a big convention/event type thing going on while I was there so only bar was available for walk-ins.

There are so many bartenders that you don't really get a chance to build a connection with any of them. This could have been because of how chaotic the event made the restaurant though.

I had the grilled chicken sandwich with a Caesar salad. Nothing special but not horrible. The food runner was probably the friendliest out of all the employees.

Overall, seemed better than most hotel sports bars but you end up paying more than you would for a regular sports bar down the road.

The food was decent, but everything was too sweet for my taste. The owner is pushy with giving you her business card, and changing your order to what she thinks you should have. they have minimal choices in beers, only a few of which you can't get elsewhere.

Bourbon flights are pricey but well worth it if you're a whiskey fan.  Spent a night with live music and a couple of friends going through about 4 different flights, and was not dissapointed.   Whiskey burned good, the band played well, and the general crowd was friendly and comfortable.  

Haven't been able to get to the game tables upstairs, having only gone on weekend nights, but this would make for a fine happy hour stop for those as well.
Enjoyed Sin Nite. Atmosphere great food good also. Recommend if you're coming from out of town and just wanted to chill. G

Decent value for sure. Salmon I had was a bit over cooked but all in all a decent experience. Good atmosphere and crowd. Didn't like how she took my credit card right at order and server after my initial server was a little caught up with a personal issue but I'd come back.

It was okay for strip mall quick-order Chinese.  Service was quick, the place was spotless.  I had the boneless space-rib combo with fried rice.  This is different than the BBQ rib combo (by about $4).  Entree was eh (too tough, too sweet) but roast pork fried rice was good.  If I return (here in town for business) I'd do that as a meal.  Area is a little sketchy.

This is a restaurant/bar that is part of the hotel. The menu is small and doesn't have a lot of options but they have an extensive drink menu. Personally, the food is significantly overpriced, especially the half chicken entree. However, the food was flavorful and delicious. I think this is a great place for anyone who doesn't mind spending money and wants to enjoy a good meal and drinks. 

The mussels were delicious and a good amount for the price. The fingerling potatoes were a little dry but still yummy. The waitress was very attentive.

Dough god tapas was great! Chili con carne was amazing! Just like home! Great ambiance! 

We also tried the chicken, fell a little flat ...completely redeemed by the dessert! 

Great to see an indigenous inspired / woman owned restaurant in the heart of downtown! 

We'll be back for sure!
Classic donuts done well and at a great price. Love how fluffy and light their dough is! We need one in Nampa!

Great downtown location next to the Arch. Nice, modern, spacious, comfortable rooms, ours had a view of the Arch made this AAA Four Diamond hotel a fairly pleasant stay. We scored a good deal on hotwire.com for around $90.00 (tax included). The downside is the lack of attention to detail. The coffee maker was filthy and had white growth in it. The tub was filled with dirty water and debris floating in it. The hotel sports bar is lively and has reasonable food and drink prices. On Sundays, the hotel sports bar has $5 build your own Bloody Mary! Yum, yum! Overnight valet is $26.00. Public parking is available--see hotel website for details.
THE BEST I'VE EVER HAD! The chicken, sauces, & sides were all delicious. The salad had a tasty cilantro dressing on it and the spicy red beans were on point!

The location is convenient and the room is really nice. Excellent decoration, remodeled, pristine. The continental breakfast is good enough for the rate: you can get muffins, scones, tea, fruits, juices, and other cold beverages from the reception and have breakfast on your room. Highly recommended!

We are locals and took the group ride from the Pedego Bike shop to the Biltmore along Cabrillo Blvd. The weather and scenery were absolutely beautiful, we caught the sunset on the way back to the shop.  Pat was very friendly and very helpful. There are plenty of bikes to choose from whether you prefer to ride solo or tandem. This is a fabulous way to explore Santa Barbara and all its beauty ...  and not to mention environmentally friendly!

For what a room costs, especially an atrium view room, I expect the cleaning to be better. The closet for hanging clothes, safe, ironing board etc has not been cleaned in a very long time. The shower drain was clogged so it took about 5 minutes after we were done showering that the water would be gone.

I'm going to have to disagree with the majority of past reviewers of this place. I love Imo's pizza: the ultra thin crust, the sweet tangy sauce, the large portions of toppings... I wish the nearest location wasn't an 8-hour drive from my house. The staff at this location were friendly. Our meal was served quickly despite it being busy (thanks to the double whammy of a baseball game and a hockey game going on). The facilities were clean. My only complaint is that you've got to go on a long trek tithe bathroom, which involves going through a swanky restaurant/bar and into the Hilton hotel next door.
Best BBQ around. Have tried a few things and they taste very good. I'd recommend this place for anyone looking for BBQ. I've never sat down and ate inside but their take out is quick and fair priced.

I have been a member at almost EVERY gym in SB. Golds (formerly Spectrum/Bay club) 24 hour fitness, Key to fitness, the list goes on, you get it. NONE of them come close th SBAC.

Amenities include a yoga room, CrossFit room, pilates room, aqua massage chairs, steam room, sauna, personal spa (in ladies room anyway- not sure about the mens)! 3 weight rooms (one outside over looking their pool & Los Padres mountains), Spin studio (out doors/4th floor) Earth bar (smoothies juices etc.) POOL, Jacuzzi, and to top it off... BEER AND WINE! HOORAY!

Their classes include multiple levels of yoga, Tai chi, boxing, spin, barre, (actually there are too many to count, just check their website) but my FAVORITES are lunch time lift & hip hop with Tamarr. So sooo fun. All of their teachers are incredible at what they do!

My other half is a yogi, as in yogi yogi we have a yoga room at our house. He is not a fan of gyms but after I got him to come as my guest (after 6 months) he loved it and joined the next day. Their yoga teachers are top notch, above core power which is THE SAME PRICE as the club. He also loves to swim laps, so the pool was an added bonus. 

The club is a bit pricier than most but for a reason. It is extremely clean and has amenities beyond what you could ask for. 

Extra bonuses include organic coffee, crushed ice, pool parties & invites to sunset cruises!

Simply the best! The nicest people, the best hairstylist in all of Philadelphia and beyond! Love everything about this place! Betty is truly gifted in haircoloring! Travis is beyond excellent in haircutting! David , A truly gifted hairstylist that has many talents beyond your imagination! He I can blow your hair dry better than anybody I've ever seen and I am really picky!Every body here has a talent that exceeds anybody's expectations! The best Karitin hair treatment one could ever wish for! I give this place a 10 out of 10 or better!

Great space, great location, friendly service, and unfortunately careless attention to keeping things separate on the grill to the point where my vegetarian tacos had stray pieces of meat in them.  Upsetting to the senses and the stomach.  If this is the standard level of care here, then vegetarians and people with food allergies should avoid this place.

This place is a gem! Look no further..

I just moved back to St. Louis after being in Manhattan for 3 years. While out running errands, I decided to get a mani on the way home. I Yelped and this place got great reviews so I decided to walk in. Immediately, I was greeted by a women in a beautiful pink suit who fit me in right away without an appointment (an appointment was recommended on Yelp). She took me over to the color selection bar and while I was set on getting a gel shellac mani, she told me the powder gel dip mani was much better in terms of quality and duration to last. I was open to trying so picked my color (the selection is unreal - they have EVERY color and more!) and sat down. She then offered me a beverage. The water she brought out had delicious freshly cut oranges in it. What a nice touch! 

My manicurist was Jan who was so nice and conversant. Her attention to detail was fantastic and she made sure I loved my nails, especially being the first time with the powder dip. Toward the end, the nice woman who greeted me coming in (I am guessing a manager) came over and sat down to make sure everything was to my liking and was quite pleasant to converse with as well. Once finished, I was in love with my nails - the best I've ever had. 

As I was paying, a gentleman seated by the counter asked to see me nails. I thought he was another customer or waiting for his wife but it turns out he was the owner! I told him of my fantastic experience and how well run his salon was. He was very customer centric and could tell he knew exactly how to run a successful business. That goes such a long way and hard to find (especially when you are used to NYC nail salons where customer service is nonexistent and it's all about the dollar.)

Also, this place is gorgeous, spacious and clean - by far the nicest salon I've been to. The Christmas decorations were top notch inside and out. 

I gave Bello 4 starts because it is definitely pricey. $42 (excluding tip) for a powder dip manicure. The most I've ever paid for a gel manicure in $25. But despite the price, the service and experience was the best I've ever had (and I've been to hundreds of nail salons in different cities!) I will be going back in a few weeks and look forward to trying a pedicure at some point!

If you don't mind paying top dollar to be completely pampered, this is your place!
OK store...Lots of tanks & dry goods, But lack in small cheap SPS coral frags. I also think the store is a little pricey.

Not so great. Husband tenderloin was decent. Wings were awful. No sauce just grease. Had to salt then to find flavor. All in all disappointing. Too bad it was our first trip and will likely be the last

If there's one thing that stands out at Citizens Bank park more than any other stadium or ballpark, it's that there's not a bad seat in the house.  The nosebleeds, the outfield, the club boxes, and the lower level all have their own perks that make each section special in it's own way.  The stadium just feels so open and every seat offers an incredible view of the magnificent baseball diamond and vibrant green grass.

The food could use some improvements, although every year they actually seem to be listening to ticket-holders because they are expanding their options little by little.  If you're from out of town, I'd definitely recommend stopping in left field.  Take a look around at Harry the K's, go upstairs to Scoreboard Porch to check out the view (my favorite in the whole stadium) and then on your way back down stop to get a Schmitter--Three slices of cheese, sliced steak, fried onions, grilled salami, tomatoes, and special sauce.

CBP has plenty of activities for kids too, I'm sure at some point anyone who's been there has been entertained by the best mascot in sports, The Phanatic.  Whether its coming out on his ATV getting the crowd riled up, or spilling popcorn all over a row of fans, he's always providing plenty of laughs for the crowd.

I went to Games 3,4,5 of the '08 WS and Game 4 of the 2009 WS against the Yankees, and these were some of the best memories of my short life. 

Go check out this stadium and make some of your own.

This place is downright horrible. The service was probably some of the worst I've ever received in my life.  My friends have posted on yelp before about our experience, but the owners of this low-life hookah joint deleted them to make themselves look better.
Don't go here, that's all I can say.  I'm not hard to please at restaurants and public places such as this, but when we were overcharged for no reason I do get upset.  The "waiter" refused to give us a receipt showing what exactly we were paying for which was completely unprofessional.  Even with the gratuity added on to our bill, we still paid an extra $20ish dollars for god knows what.  We were the only large group at the location since it was a Thursday night.  We continually ordered more hookahs and drinks so it was a slap in the face when they took hookahs aways from us before we were finished.  We even told them we weren't finished and they insisted the hookahs were empty when they weren't.  I would understand if they wanted us to leave because we were loud or obnoxious but we were talking at normal levels and weren't doing anything obnoxious.  I'll never be heading back to this place, that's for sure.

Every time I go here some girl is talking to her boys at the drive thru. Slowest and rudest DQ I have ever seen. When I got to the window my shake was watery and had been setting there. The little girl basically said take it or leave it. The manager seems to support this behavior.
Awesome bakery!!!! Had cookies made for my daughter. They delicious and fresh even after a week and half they were still fresh. The donuts are amazing!!! Very friendly staff and great prices!!!!

First of all I like this place. Been here three times before. But the starter of Arincini the middle was cold. I know restaurant's precook food. But really. Couldn't get it hot? Got a special here. Totally Average. Groupon this place as usual. 
Why have they stopped making fresh food to order? 
I hate a place that throws it at you, without a concern. Pre cooked food. God I'm pissed about this review.

The wife and I eat here every couple weeks. The freshly baked chips are always excellent, and they have the best queso dip. The Tacos Al Pastor is probably my favorite meal of any restaurant in Indy - it's delicious! However, the best part of La Cabana is the service. Everyone is always warm, friendly, and eager to serve. Great people!

Not sure why I haven't visited this place sooner. My husband and son had the chicken and beef rice platters and both enjoyed it. Our younger kids LOVED their chicken pho. The younger ones are harder to feed because they can be very picky so imagine my joy in seeing them finish their bowls plus ask for seconds! I ordered the shrimp wonton soup that came with egg noodles, bok choy, and pork. It was so good! The wonton dumplings are different than other places and it tasted really good. I also got our oldest kid a jasmine bubble tea with lychee flavor and the popping boba, which he really loved. Thank you and will look forward to coming back!
Edit: I reviewed this after a great dinner at home, wish I had known about the 10% off deal?
Lobster Mac &cheese was very good. I'm glad I had the half order, wow!
Great service! I had a coupon that was about 3-4 years old with no expiration date. They honored it with no problems or hassles. I could not believe it. Is customer service making a comeback? :D

Since I've posted the last review, I came here a few more times.  What can I say, I am obsessed with the food here, and my goal is to try every single dish in the menu.  Unfortunately I am a long way from reaching that goal as I tend to order the same dishes each time because I can't help myself, namely Prah-Hok Kateeh and Sah-Law Machue Yuin.  I have tried a few new dishes since my last review, see below:

Pan Fried Tilapia with Ginger Sauce - my new second favorite dish, after Prah-Hok Kateeh!  They gave you an option to either get a whole fish, two filets or one filet.  We opted for one filet so that we can order more dishes.  I definitely want to get a whole fish next time.  The fish was perfectly breaded and seasoned, it was crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside.  The star of the dish was the ginger sauce, it was perfection.  I love the different notes in the sauce, including sweet, sour and a hint of spiciness.  I would be happy with a bucket of this sauce and a bowl of rice.  

Nkahp-Ch'in - I've never had frog legs before (I know, bad Asian!), and was hesitate to try it, but the dish looked so delectable that I had to give it a try.  I think the frog legs being fried really helped, I mean everything taste good fried no?  It kind of tasted like chicken, but with less meat.  I liked the batter and the sauce that came with the dish, but I am not sure I would try this dish again. 

Pleak Sak-Koe - I saw that a lot of people on Yelp recommended this dish and decided to try it.  The dish is basically thinly sliced beef that comes with a side of lettuce and basil to eat as a wrap, kind of like Korean BBQ style.  I was not a big fan of the dish as the meat was a bit bland, a rarity as nearly all of the other dishes I've tried have been burst with flavor.  I think this would be a good dish for someone who is new to South Asian food and not used to all of the bold flavors.

The four of us polished off 8 dishes the last time we came here.  Despite a few misses, I still think this is one of my favorite restaurants of all time.  If only I can convince the family to move to NYC and open up the restaurant here.  The three hours round-trip commute is kind of killing me :)  I highly recommend you to give this place a try!!

Fantastic!  By far the best restaurant I've eaten at in Philly.  As far as atmosphere, the restaurant is small (maybe 15 tables) in a small row house.  The staff is as friendly as it gets.  Our servers kept checking in on us, but did not get to the point were it became annoying. 

We dined on a Friday night, so we got the grand tasting menu with the wine pairing (a $90 supplement).  They presented us with the options that were being made that night and asked if there was anything that we would or would not eat on the menu.  

The amuse were a great start:
-Beet Salad: Ok, although I'm not sure how it was an amuse.
-Tomato and Red Pepper Cold Soup: Fantastic.  I only wish I could get a large bowl with lump crab on top.  I could eat this everday.
-Corn Pudding:  Very Good.
-Squab Fritter:  Very good.  It was my wife's favorite amuse.
-Foie Pastrami on toast.  Simply amazing.  I love foie and I love pastrami.  They two combined could have not been any better.

We then had a variety of smaller dishes that were different for me and my wife (which is great, so we can try more of the options):

Highlights:
-Foie Pastrami
-Sweet Onion Crepe.  Best thing we ate that night.
-Spinach Gnocci.  A Vetri classic.  It is unfair to compare any other gnocchi to these.  Simply amazing.
-Wine.  All the wine was perfectly paired with each dish.  All from Italy.  A great bargain.  Definitely worth it.
-Desserts.  Chocolate Polenta cake and peach and blackberry upside down cake were amazing.

Lowlights:
-Sardine.  Probably my mistake for not taking this off the table.  I'm not a huge sardine fan.
-Porchetta stuffed with Cherries:  I just wasn't a fan.

Overall:  Definitely a great experience and a must eat in Philly.  Hands down the best Italian I've ever had (including Italy).

In response to another post below:
Contrary to what another poster said, I think the amount of food was perfect.  We walked out full, but not feeling gross.  The portion sizes here are much more realistic than Per Se.  Walking out of Per Se, I wanted to vomit due to the large quantity of rich, buttery food and large number of courses.  Also, I'm not sure how you can compare the two on price, since my bill at Per Se for two was over twice what I paid at Vetri.  I'm not saying this is better than Per Se, but I don't think you can compare the two. They are two different styles of food, atmosphere (I had to wear a tie at Per Se), price, etc.

I'm not sure if this is the right one because there's about three of them in the same location  but the one on New Orleans/Bourbon st is shit. They I.D'ed us at the door like EVERY place in NOLA and then the guy asked my friend what she wanted then he ignored her after her request. We all looked at each other and was confused because he came over to me then said may I help you and I said yes my friend just asked for a hand grenade he continue to ask me for my ID and I kinda just looked at him because the guy at the front just checked all of our IDs. As I started to take it out he points at one of his employees from outside and says come make HER her drink ( as he points and yells at my friend) keep in mind we just came outside so it's not like we were intoxicated or anything for him to refuse the service.  We just was really confused then he told another employee "show these girls were the other tropical island  is goodbye" show these girls where the other Tropical  Island is. Extremely rude and inappropriate even the other doorman apologized for what ever was happening and said don't mind him. What makes it even worse I'm pretty sure it was the Manger that was carrying on in such manner.

I'm giving this place two stars because the food is generally very good, but my experience today with the restaurant is terrible.  Our waitress is nice enough but could have taken both our food and drink orders at the same time.  I repeatedly saw other tables who were seated after us get their food before us.  We've been waiting for our food nearly half an hour at this point and our waitress hasn't come by in the last ten minutes to check on us or the progress of our food.  The restaurant can say that they're really busy or that the kitchen staff is just overwhelmed, but as a customer a 30+ minute ticket time is not ok.  I don't think I or my family will be back here again anytime soon.

I never order a burger at a restaurant, unless it's some place like Village Whiskey or PYT and the like. HOWEVER, I did last night.
Check it:
-arugula
-gruyere
-fried egg
-truffle oil
How  could you NOT order that burger? It was ridiculous. Messy, but worth it.

Other reasons Prohibition rules:
-good beer (obv)
-great music (if you're an avid reader of mine, you'll note that this is a recurring theme)
-somewhat close to my apt.

The end.

Took my grandson here today to sample Indian food. He loved the food, I've been here before and I'm always so pleased. Everyone is polite, helpful and efficient.  The very best place for Indian food !!!

We stayed here for almost a week for our honeymoon. We were very pleased with our stay. 

The staff was great. They accommodated any requests we had and made sure our room was cleaned even after leaving the room later in the afternoon. We received a number of really good lunch recommendations from the staff. 

The room itself was very nice. Recently renovated and very clean. Our room was fairly quiet. Our room faced the inside and was next to the smaller courtyard. The shower was very large for a hotel shower and included a huge sink. The room was very spacious. It included a flat screen tv, small refrigerator, and complimentary bottled water. The breakfast was better than many hotels, including sausage, bacon, grits, bagels, eggs, fruit, coffee, and juices. 

I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone wanting a nice hotel in the French quarter. It is far enough away from most of the noise without being too far away from the action.

This was a home run on our scorecard!   We came n for the weekend for the Cardinals vs Cubs game and were looking for a place to grab a quick bite before heading home to Chicago. After reading reviewed we figured we would try this place out, and we are so glad we didn't bench the idea!

We arrived on a Monday afternoon around 1230, and there was a line out the door wrapped around the building. We were hesitant at first, but figured by the time we found another place to eat, we would of wasted the same amount of time in line. Surprisingly the line moves quite quickly and we place our orders in no time. 

Seating inside was a bit crowded and it was way to hit and uncomfortable to eat outside so we took our sandwiches to go. I had the prez Reuben and my husband has the old school and we were more then pleased. There is an assortment of chips to choose from to go along with the sand which. 

I wish I had take a photo of my sandwich, but it was so appetizing I couldn't wait!!  

I definitely recommend stopping by-  it's worth it!

We tried Luke for dinner since we'd heard good things. My friends ordered the burger and the shrimp & grits. The burger was pretty good -- it was similar to fathers office in LA but the bun wasn't as crunchy/crispy and it didn't have blue cheese. The portions are huge! The shrimp were super juicy and the steak was also quite tasty but came out a bit rarer than I asked for. 

Our waiter was awesome -  very personable and friendly. I want to give this place 3.5 stars, because although the food was good, it wasn't a wonder to behold, which is what I had been expecting after all the hype.

Look, there are a few affordable yet refined dining experiences where this fat boy can enjoy and not feel left short changed. This is a rare and delicious exception.  The food is fat-tastic and the ambiance is perfect - great music and friendly service.  I went twice in three days!!  Need to say more???
They fixed a problem with one of my power windows quickly and cheaply and were able to give me a ride back to my apartment after I dropped my car off. I couldn't have asked for better service.
Had a great time tonight. Awesome entertainment.  The Souliz Band was rockin'. So much energy & working the crowd. Can't wait to see them again at The Hard Rock Tampa soon.
Where my family made groceries when I was coming up. A little more pricey than some, but worth it. If you're looking for something hard to find, they're the ones to try.

This was my second time visiting this location and I was more pleased this time than before. I ordered a Love it size half and half banana and cheesecake. I was surprised that they had banana ice cream as it's one of my favorite flavors. I'll be going back whenever the craving hits.
I am very picky and I love this salon. The atmosphere is chic and comfortable. The people who work here are always so nice and helpful. I always feel welcomed.

I had to go through the hassle of downloading the yelp app JUST to give this business an accurate review! This is the worst place I've ever been to! It was recommended by my sister in law and it was a terrible experience.  When I walked in the place looked awful, but I didn't have time to look up reviews and really look into a place so I told them I need a mani/pedi. They told me to pick a color and I explained I wanted gel (shellac) polish for my fingers. A lady pointed behind a desk and when I looked I  saw a nasty dirty swatch board with about 40 colors on it.
